name: Larry Page
current_role: Co-founder, board member and controlling shareholder, Alphabet Inc.; founder of AI-manufacturing startup Dynatomics
profile: Larry Page co-founded Google in 1998 with Sergey Brin while they were Stanford Ph.D. students, and co-invented the PageRank algorithm. He was Google CEO 1998–2001 and 2011–2015, then Alphabet CEO until stepping down in 2019. He remains an Alphabet director and controlling shareholder. More recently he founded Dynatomics, a Palo Alto startup using AI to optimise product manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Page is a clean-energy advocate: his Palo Alto home uses fuel cells and geothermal energy. He has also backed electric and flying-vehicle ventures such as Tesla (early investor), Kitty Hawk and Opener.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Michigan, Page was on the 1993 'Maize & Blue' solar car team. He built a working inkjet printer out of Lego bricks by reverse-engineering an ink cartridge. He also proposed replacing the campus bus system with a driverless personal rapid-transit monorail.
notes: Extremely private: no public social accounts, and he has largely avoided public appearances since 2019. press@google.com is Google's corporate press desk, not a route to him personally. The energy/solar-car and Dynatomics manufacturing angles are the most relevant hooks for this podcast.

name: Sergey Brin
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Alphabet Inc. (Google); hands-on contributor to Google's Gemini AI work
profile: Moscow-born computer scientist who emigrated to the US at six and co-founded Google with Larry Page in 1998 while both were Stanford PhD students. He stepped down as Alphabet president in 2019 but remains a director and controlling shareholder, and since 2023 has come out of retirement to work on Gemini AI at Google.
interesting_fact: He backs airship maker LTA Research; in Oct 2023 its 124-metre Pathfinder 1 became the largest airship since the Hindenburg to be cleared for flight testing. He has also given $2B+ to Parkinson's research.
deep_cut_fact: His 1997 Stanford resume lists a 1993 internship at Wolfram Research (makers of Mathematica), the summer after he graduated from the University of Maryland at 19 with high honors in math; he then went to Stanford on an NSF graduate fellowship.
notes: Extremely private; does few interviews and has no active personal social accounts. Only realistic route is Google/Alphabet press. Received National Medal of Science in Oct 2026 (per Wikipedia/AP). Avoid personal-life topics.

name: Mark Zuckerberg
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Meta Platforms (Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Threads)
profile: Mark Zuckerberg started Facebook at Harvard in 2004 at 19, took it public in 2012 and renamed it Meta in 2021; he owns roughly 13% of the company. Meta is now spending heavily on AI, including its Superintelligence Labs and multi-gigawatt AI data centers, alongside AR/VR glasses; with Priscilla Chan he has pledged 99% of his Meta stake to the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative.
interesting_fact: Zuckerberg and Priscilla Chan are spending billions through the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative/Biohub in an effort to help cure, prevent or manage all disease by the end of the century.
deep_cut_fact: Around age 11 he built 'ZuckNet' to link the computers in his family home with his father's dental office; in high school his Synapse Media Player, which used machine learning to learn listening habits, was featured on Slashdot in April 2003 and got a 3-out-of-5 review from PC Magazine.
notes: Extremely high-demand; outreach realistically goes through Meta communications (press@meta.com). AI data-center/energy build-out (e.g. Louisiana Hyperion campus, nuclear power deals) is the obvious podcast angle. Social accounts listed are his long-standing verified 'zuck' handles.

name: Sergey Jr Brin
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Alphabet (controlling shareholder); hands-on technical contributor to Google's Gemini AI models
profile: Sergey Brin co-founded Google with Larry Page in 1998 after they met at Stanford's computer science PhD program; Google IPO'd in 2004 and reorganized under Alphabet in 2015. He stepped down as Alphabet president in 2019 but returned to the office in 2023 and says he now works on Gemini 'pretty much every day.' His giving focuses on Parkinson's research (>$2B) and climate.
interesting_fact: At Google I/O in May 2025 Brin made a surprise appearance alongside DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis and said he is in the office 'pretty much every day now' working on Gemini, years after stepping back from management.
deep_cut_fact: His airship company LTA Research (founded 2015) built Pathfinder 1, a ~400-ft helium airship that won an FAA special airworthiness certificate in Sept 2023, and acquired the historic Goodyear Airdock in Akron, Ohio as its future manufacturing site.
notes: Very private, rarely does interviews outside Google events; no personal office contact published. Google press is a corporate route only. Name in dataset has stray 'Jr' (Forbes slug).

name: Michael Dell
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Dell Technologies; founder of DFO Management (family office)
profile: Founded Dell from his UT Austin dorm room in 1984; took it private with Silver Lake in 2013, bought EMC for $60B in 2016 and relisted in 2018. Dell is now a major AI-server supplier. Much of his fortune sits in family office DFO Management (hotels, credit); in 2025 he and his wife pledged $6.25B to seed savings accounts for 25M U.S. children.
interesting_fact: At 19 he was selling upgraded PCs out of his UT Austin dorm room, grossing about $80,000 by the end of his freshman year.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, at about 12, was in a Chinese restaurant in Houston: he started washing dishes, was 'promoted' to water boy, then assistant maitre d'; at 14 he worked at a stamp-and-coin store assessing gold and silver people brought in to sell.
notes: Very active on X (@MichaelDell) and talks often about AI infrastructure; best formal route is Dell Global PR (media relations). Strong fit for data-center/AI-factory topics.

name: Jen-Hsun Huang
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, Nvidia
profile: Taiwan-born engineer (Oregon State, Stanford MSEE) who worked at AMD and LSI Logic before co-founding Nvidia in 1993. He has run it ever since, steering it from PC graphics chips to CUDA and the GPUs that power AI data centers, making Nvidia one of the world's most valuable companies. Now pitches 'AI factories' and sovereign AI to governments and hyperscalers.
interesting_fact: Nvidia was conceived in a booth at a Denny's in San Jose in 1993; as a teenager Huang had worked at Denny's as a dishwasher, busboy and waiter.
deep_cut_fact: He was a serious junior table-tennis player: he scrubbed floors at Portland's Paddle Palace club to pay for tournaments, and at 15 finished third in junior doubles at the U.S. Open Table Tennis Championships.
notes: No personal social accounts; all requests route through Nvidia corporate communications. Extremely high-demand; frames everything around 'AI factories' and data-center power, a natural podcast fit. Name commonly given as Jensen Huang.

name: Warren Buffett
current_role: Chairman emeritus and director, Berkshire Hathaway (stepped down as CEO end-2025 and as chairman Sept 2026)
profile: The 'Oracle of Omaha' built Berkshire Hathaway from a failing textile mill into a ~$1T conglomerate (insurance, BNSF, Berkshire Hathaway Energy, big Apple/BofA/Occidental stakes). Greg Abel became CEO on Jan 1, 2026; in Sept 2026, at 96, Buffett became chairman emeritus as son Howard took the chair. He has given away ~$66B of stock since 2006.
interesting_fact: He filed his first tax return in 1944 at age 14, reporting $592.50 of income (mostly from a paper route) and deducting $35 for his bicycle and $10 for watch repair as business expenses; he paid $7 in tax.
deep_cut_fact: Terrified of public speaking, he signed up for a $100 Dale Carnegie course, stopped the check, then re-enrolled paying cash so he'd have to show up. His Columbia degree isn't on his office wall, but the Carnegie certificate (dated 1952) is.
notes: Berkshire has no press office/PR firm or published press email; Buffett historically answers by letter to his Omaha office (address on berkshirehathaway.com). X account is verified but essentially inactive. Now 96 and stepping back (chairman emeritus since Sept 2026) - podcast odds very low; Berkshire Hathaway Energy (Abel's former unit) is the energy angle.

name: Larry Ellison
current_role: Executive Chairman and Chief Technology Officer, Oracle Corporation
profile: Cofounded Oracle (as Software Development Laboratories) in 1977 and ran it as CEO for 37 years before becoming executive chairman/CTO in 2014; owns roughly 40% of the company. Oracle's AI cloud/data-center boom made him the second person ever worth $400B+ (Sept 2025). Also owns ~50% of Paramount Skydance, most of Lanai, and funds the Ellison Institute of Technology in Oxford.
interesting_fact: He never finished college and started out building databases for the CIA; the CIA project's codename at Ampex, 'Oracle', later became the company's name.
deep_cut_fact: He sailed as a crew member aboard the trimaran USA 17 in the deciding race of the 2010 America's Cup in Valencia; ESPN noted he and tactician John Kostecki were the only Americans on BMW Oracle's crew for the clincher.
notes: Press email is Oracle Corporate Communications (Deborah Hellinger), as listed on Oracle's Oct 2026 Investor Day release. Ellison rarely does outside interviews; Oracle earnings calls/Investor Day are where he speaks publicly. Strong data-center/AI-infrastructure fit (OCI, Stargate).

name: Steve Ballmer
current_role: Owner/Chairman, Los Angeles Clippers; co-founder, Ballmer Group (with Connie Ballmer); founder, USAFacts
profile: Ballmer joined Microsoft in 1980 as employee No. 30 and was CEO 2000–2014; he remains its largest individual shareholder. He bought the LA Clippers in 2014 for $2B and built the Intuit Dome. With Connie Ballmer he has given away $6.5B+; in July 2026 Ballmer Group spun out three regional 'MoveUp' philanthropies in Michigan, LA and Washington.
interesting_fact: He created USAFacts.org, a nonpartisan site where anyone can look up and understand where government money goes.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after Harvard was assistant product manager for Duncan Hines' Moist & Easy cakes and brownies at Procter & Gamble — his cubicle mate was future GE CEO Jeff Immelt. He also briefly tried writing screenplays in Hollywood before Stanford.
notes: No published personal/office email; Ballmer Group site lists no press email (it warns of fraudulent requests). USAFacts media inbox is the cleanest published route. Also known: scored higher than Gates on the Putnam exam and was Harvard football team manager (Wikipedia).

name: Amancio Ortega
current_role: Founder and ~59% owner of Inditex (Zara); runs family office Pontegadea; founder of Fundación Amancio Ortega
profile: Co-founder of Inditex and pioneer of fast fashion; he opened the first Zara in A Coruña in 1975 and owns ~60% of Inditex (Zara, Massimo Dutti, Pull&Bear; ~5,000 stores). He reinvests $400M+ a year in dividends via his family office Pontegadea into prime property and, increasingly, energy and infrastructure (Redeia, Enagás, Repsol renewables, PD Ports).
interesting_fact: Pontegadea has become a major energy-infrastructure investor: 5% of Spain's grid operator Redeia, 49% of Repsol's Delta wind farm (~€245M) and stakes in Repsol renewables, alongside a property portfolio leased to Apple, Amazon and Walmart.
deep_cut_fact: At 14, after his railway-worker father moved the family to A Coruña, he became a shop hand at local shirtmaker Gala, which still stands on the same downtown corner, and learned to make clothes by hand. His first company (1963) was Confecciones Goa, which made quilted bathrobes.
notes: Extremely private: he has given only a handful of interviews, and his Foundation states that he has no social media. The Foundation press office (prensa@faortega.org) is the only published channel tied to him; Inditex corporate press is a separate route. His philanthropy includes €300M+ for cancer equipment in Spanish hospitals and ~500 study-abroad scholarships a year.

name: Rob Walton
current_role: Founder, Rob Walton Foundation (conservation philanthropy); former Walmart chairman (1992-2015); member of the Denver Broncos Walton-Penner ownership group
profile: Samuel Robson 'Rob' Walton, eldest son of Walmart founder Sam Walton, joined Walmart in 1969, helped take it public in 1970 and chaired it from 1992 to 2015. He left the board in 2024. With other Walton heirs he owns roughly 45% of Walmart. He led the 2022 purchase of the Denver Broncos and now focuses on large-scale conservation through the Rob Walton Foundation.
interesting_fact: Walton, who holds a Columbia law degree, served as Walmart's general counsel and corporate secretary and helped prepare the company's 1970 IPO before becoming chairman.
deep_cut_fact: In Sept 2025 his foundation gave $115M, the largest gift in ASU's history, to create the Rob Walton School of Conservation Futures, launched during NY Climate Week. He was photographed studying coral with students in ASU's Walton Center for Planetary Health. His foundation is a founding member of the Africa Keystone Protected Area Partnership.
notes: Very private, with no public email or social accounts. His foundation site has no contact form. Possible routes: ASU news office (Walton School) or Conservation International / African Parks, where he has held board roles (CI executive-committee chair per older ASU releases). His focus now is conservation, mainly in Africa.

name: Jim Walton
current_role: Chairman, Arvest Bank Group (Bentonville, Arkansas); Walmart heir and major shareholder
profile: James Carr Walton (b. 1948) is the youngest son of Walmart founder Sam Walton. He chairs Arvest Bank Group, the family's roughly $28B-asset bank, and the newspaper company Community Publishers. He sat on Walmart's board from 2005 to 2016 before handing the seat to his son Steuart. With his siblings' families he owns about 45% of Walmart, and Forbes ranks him among the world's 15 richest people.
interesting_fact: Jim started his career in 1972 in Walmart's real-estate department, working on store-site deals. He moved to run the family holding company Walton Enterprises as president about four years later.
deep_cut_fact: At Bentonville High School (class of 1965) he was junior-class president, an all-state football player, and learned to fly a plane, like his father, who famously scouted store sites from the air.
notes: Very private and gives almost no interviews. Arvest's CEO since Nov 2025 is Matt Machen; Walton remains chairman of the parent Arvest Bank Group. media@arvest.com comes from Arvest's media-contact page (bot-protected, confirmed via search snippet). Large 2026 GOP political donor, so worth knowing before any political framing.

name: Jensen Huang
current_role: Co-founder, President and CEO, NVIDIA
profile: Taiwan-born engineer who cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and has run it since, taking it public in 1999. Nvidia's GPUs went from gaming to the backbone of AI data centers, pushing its market cap past $4 trillion in 2025; Huang owns roughly 3%. He has funded engineering centers at Stanford ($30M) and Oregon State ($50M).
interesting_fact: After arriving in the US, his aunt and uncle sent him to a rural Kentucky boarding school for troubled youth, mistaking it for a prep school; he cleaned the boys' bathroom daily. He later waited tables at Denny's, which he says cured his shyness.
deep_cut_fact: As a teen he was a nationally ranked table-tennis player: in a Jan 1978 letter to Sports Illustrated, Paddle Palace owner Lou Bochenski called him 'perhaps the most promising junior ever to play table tennis in the Northwest', noting he scrubbed the club's floors to pay for tournaments.
notes: Extremely high-demand; route via NVIDIA Corporate Communications. Does not run personal social accounts of note.

name: Alice Walton
current_role: Founder and board chair, Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art; founder, Alice L. Walton School of Medicine (Bentonville, Arkansas)
profile: Alice Walton, the only daughter of Walmart founder Sam Walton, derives her fortune from her Walmart stake but has devoted herself to art and philanthropy rather than the company board. She opened Crystal Bridges Museum of American Art in Bentonville in 2011 and in 2025 welcomed the first class of 48 students to her Alice L. Walton School of Medicine, focused on whole-health medicine.
interesting_fact: Her art collecting began at about age 10-11 when she bought a print of Picasso's 'Blue Nude' at her father's five-and-dime, paying roughly five weeks of allowance.
deep_cut_fact: She was the first chair of the Northwest Arkansas Council and put up $15M of initial funding for Northwest Arkansas Regional Airport (opened 1998), while her investment bank Llama Company underwrote a $79.5M bond; the terminal bears her name and she entered the Arkansas Aviation Hall of Fame in 2001.

public_contacts.value: news@alwmed.org (Alice L. Walton School of Medicine news contact)
Shore Fire Media (handles Crystal Bridges & the Momentary press)

notes: Very private; no personal social accounts. Best routes are via Crystal Bridges media office or the medical school. Early career: equity analyst, EF Hutton broker, Arvest investments head, founded Llama Company (1988-98).

name: Carlos Slim Helu
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with family) of América Móvil, Grupo Carso and Grupo Financiero Inbursa; founder of Fundación Carlos Slim
profile: Mexico's richest person, Slim built Grupo Carso from 1965 real-estate and bottling deals, then in 1990 won Telmex's privatisation with Southwestern Bell and France Telecom; it is now part of América Móvil, Latin America's largest mobile operator. His family also controls construction, mining, retail and financial businesses; sons now chair the main companies.
interesting_fact: As a boy his father gave him a 5-peso weekly allowance and required him to record every purchase in a ledger; before going into business he taught algebra at UNAM.
deep_cut_fact: While still an engineering student at UNAM he also taught Linear Programming there, being student and professor at the same time; and the name 'Carso' combines the first syllables of Carlos and his late wife Soumaya.
notes: IR email is América Móvil's Head of IR (published on May 2025 release); press conference transcripts on carlosslim.com. Data-center angle: Telmex/Triara data centers and AMX infrastructure. Slim gives occasional press conferences in Mexico City.

name: Bill Gates
current_role: Chair, Gates Foundation; founder of Breakthrough Energy and TerraPower; Microsoft co-founder
profile: Bill Gates co-founded Microsoft with Paul Allen in 1975 after dropping out of Harvard, and now focuses on giving away his fortune as sole chair of the Gates Foundation, which he has said will shut down within 20 years (announced May 2025). His Microsoft stake is now under 1%; he backs climate and energy ventures via Breakthrough Energy and nuclear company TerraPower.
interesting_fact: Gates has spent nearly two decades and more than $1 billion backing TerraPower, the nuclear company aiming to complete its first reactor (Natrium, in Wyoming) by 2030 — a direct link to the energy/data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: A Costa Rican hoverfly, Eristalis gatesi ('Bill Gates' flower fly'), was named after him in 1997 by entomologist Chris Thompson in recognition of his contributions to the PC revolution; a sister species was named for Paul Allen. Also: his first company, Traf-O-Data (1972, with Allen and Paul Gilbert), turned traffic-counter data into reports.
notes: Extremely high-demand guest. Gates Foundation newsroom asks media to email/phone with name, affiliation, questions and deadline. For energy angle, TerraPower and Breakthrough Energy press offices are more targeted routes. Gates has his own podcast ('Unconfuse Me').

name: S. Robson Walton
current_role: Principal owner, Denver Broncos (Walton-Penner group); former Walmart chairman (1992-2015)
profile: Rob Walton, eldest son of Walmart founder Sam Walton, served as Walmart's chairman from 1992 to 2015 and remains a major shareholder through the family's holdings. In 2022 his Walton-Penner group bought the NFL's Denver Broncos for a record $4.65B. He and wife Melani fund conservation and sustainability causes via the Rob and Melani Walton Foundation.
interesting_fact: The Walton-Penner purchase of the Denver Broncos for $4.65 billion in 2022 set the record at the time for the most expensive sale of a sports franchise.
deep_cut_fact: After a Columbia Law JD (1969) he practised at Tulsa law firm Conner & Winters, which represented Walmart, before joining Walmart as SVP in 1978; he also attended The College of Wooster and later became one of its trustees.
notes: Very private; no personal channels. His own Rob and Melani Walton Foundation (Bentonville) has no verified official contact found. Broncos front office or Walmart corporate communications are alternative institutional routes.

name: Bernard Arnault
current_role: Chairman & CEO, LVMH Moët Hennessy Louis Vuitton; chairman, Christian Dior SE; controls holding company Agache
profile: Bernard Arnault runs LVMH, the world's largest luxury group (~75 brands incl. Louis Vuitton, Dior, Sephora, Tiffany, bought in 2021 for $15.8B). He started by putting $15M from his father's construction firm into buying Boussac/Christian Dior in 1984. His Agache holding backs VC arm Aglaé Ventures and bought a majority of Paris FC in 2024; LVMH was lead sponsor of the Paris 2024 Olympics.
interesting_fact: An accomplished pianist (he took classical lessons as a child), Arnault reportedly wooed his wife, concert pianist Hélène Mercier, by playing Chopin; he and LVMH also gave €200M to restore Notre-Dame, which reopened in Dec 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Fresh out of École Polytechnique (1971) he joined his father's industrial construction firm Ferret-Savinel and in 1974 persuaded him to sell the construction arm and pivot to real estate, renaming it Ferinel; its property business later became part of what is now Nexity.
notes: No personal social accounts. Press inquiries go to LVMH External Relations (director Jean-Charles Tréhan, press@lvmh.com). Gatekept; podcast angle could tie to LVMH's energy/sustainability (LIFE 360) program or Aglaé Ventures tech investments.

name: Changpeng Zhao
current_role: Founder and major shareholder of Binance (stepped down as CEO in 2023); backs YZi Labs (ex-Binance Labs) and founded Giggle Academy
profile: Changpeng 'CZ' Zhao, a Chinese-Canadian engineer who built high-frequency trading systems, founded Binance in 2017 and still owns an estimated ~90%. He stepped down as CEO in a 2023 U.S. settlement and was pardoned in Oct 2025. He now focuses on YZi Labs investing and his free children's-education project, Giggle Academy.
interesting_fact: As a teenager in Vancouver he flipped burgers at McDonald's and worked overnight gas-station shifts to help support his family. He has said he plans to give away up to 99% of his wealth, and pledged all royalties from his self-published memoir to Giggle Academy.
deep_cut_fact: After McGill, CZ interned in Tokyo with a Tokyo Stock Exchange subcontractor writing order-matching software, then spent four years building futures trading software at Bloomberg Tradebook. He heard about Bitcoin in 2013 over a poker game with Bobby Lee and became the third team member at Blockchain.info.
notes: Very active on X (@cz_binance), which is the most direct public channel. Based in the UAE. In outreach, avoid his conviction and pardon; Giggle Academy (education) and the memoir are the friendliest hooks.

name: Francoise Bettencourt Meyers
current_role: Founder-President, Fondation Bettencourt Schueller; principal L'Oréal shareholder (L'Oréal director 1997-2025)
profile: Granddaughter of L'Oréal founder Eugène Schueller and daughter of Liliane Bettencourt; her family owns over a third of L'Oréal. She sat on its board 1997-2025 (son Jean-Victor succeeded her as vice chairman) and presides over the family foundation for science, arts and solidarity. In 2023 she became the first woman worth $100B+.
interesting_fact: She is a published biblical scholar: her multi-volume 'Les Trompettes de Jéricho: Regard sur la Bible' on Jewish-Catholic understanding (2008) won a Lauriers Verts prize in 2009, and she also wrote a genealogy of the Greek gods; royalties went to Médecins Sans Frontières.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010 she and husband Jean-Pierre Meyers championed the creation of the Fondation Pour l'Audition with three ENT surgeons; it became a recognised public-utility foundation in 2015 and backs hearing and deafness research. She is also a devoted pianist.
notes: Extremely private; almost never gives interviews. Avoid referencing the Bettencourt affair/trial. Foundation is the only realistic route. Piano detail from French Wikipedia (same page as interesting_fact).

name: Thomas Peterffy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Interactive Brokers Group (Nasdaq: IBKR)
profile: Hungarian-born pioneer of computerized trading who bought an AMEX seat in 1977, built market-maker Timber Hill and founded Interactive Brokers in 1993; he was CEO until 2019 and remains chairman and largest shareholder. He is one of America's largest landowners (560,000+ acres, mostly Florida) and lives in Palm Beach.
interesting_fact: After arriving in the US in 1965 with almost nothing, he saved $200,000 working as an engineer to buy a $36,000 seat on the American Stock Exchange, where he traded options; in high school in Hungary he sold contraband Juicy Fruit gum to classmates at a 500% markup.
deep_cut_fact: His first US job was as an architectural draftsman on highway projects for an engineering firm; when it bought its first computer he volunteered to program it - the start of his software career. He later shocked the AMEX floor by bringing handheld computers into the pit in the early 1980s.
notes: Gives frequent media interviews (Bloomberg, CNBC) via IBKR. Avid equestrian. Received Hungary's Order of Merit (2017); IBKR runs its Central European operations from Budapest. Politically outspoken - keep outreach business-focused. Also a 10%+ owner of Newsmax.

name: Michael Bloomberg
current_role: Founder and majority owner (~88%) of Bloomberg LP; founder of Bloomberg Philanthropies; UN Special Envoy on Climate Ambition and Solutions
profile: After being let go from Salomon Brothers in 1981, Bloomberg used his payout to found Bloomberg LP, whose terminal business now has ~$15B in annual revenue; he served three terms as NYC mayor (2002-2013) and ran for president in 2020. Now chiefly a philanthropist, he gave $3.7B in 2024 and $21B+ lifetime, focused on climate, public health, gun safety and education.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he pledged $1B to Johns Hopkins University, his alma mater, on top of the more than $3.5B he had already given the school.
deep_cut_fact: As a Johns Hopkins electrical-engineering student he built the costume for the university's Blue Jay mascot; as a boy in Medford, MA he became an Eagle Scout at 12 and was a licensed ham-radio operator who built his own radios and knew Morse code.

public_contacts.value: communications@bloomberg.org (Bloomberg Philanthropies, for members of the media)

notes: Family office is Willett Advisors. Energy/climate angle is strong (Beyond Coal/Beyond Carbon, UN climate envoy). Bloomberg Philanthropies also lists environment@bloomberg.org on the same contact page.

name: Mukesh Ambani
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Reliance Industries Ltd.
profile: Mukesh Ambani runs Reliance Industries (~$125B revenue), spanning oil-to-chemicals, Jio telecom (500M+ subscribers), retail, media and financial services, which he took over after the 2002 death of founder Dhirubhai Ambani. He is pushing Reliance into green energy (~$80B planned over a decade) and in 2026 announced a ~$110B, seven-year plan to build AI infrastructure across India.
interesting_fact: During the 2020 Covid lockdown he raised more than $20B by selling about a third of Jio to investors including Facebook and Google.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer from Mumbai's Institute of Chemical Technology, he left Stanford's MBA program in 1980 (Steve Ballmer was a classmate) when his father called him home; at 24 he was put in charge of building Reliance's Patalganga petrochemical plant.
notes: Press contact is Tushar Pania, Reliance Corporate Communications (named 'Key Contact' on RIL media releases). Very hard to reach directly; strong podcast angle is Jamnagar giga-complex, green energy and the AI data-center build-out.

name: Giancarlo Devasini
current_role: Chairman (and estimated ~45% owner) of Tether; CFO of crypto exchange Bitfinex
profile: Italian-born Devasini (b. 1964) trained as a doctor in Milan and briefly practised plastic surgery before moving into computer-parts distribution. He joined Bitfinex in 2012 and co-founded Tether, the largest stablecoin issuer (180B+ USDT), which made over $10B profit in 2025 mostly from Treasury yields. Tether now invests in bitcoin mining, AI/data centers and Juventus.
interesting_fact: He graduated in medicine from the University of Milan in 1990 and worked as a plastic surgeon for about two years before quitting medicine to start an electronics-import business.
deep_cut_fact: He has roots in Piedmont's Monferrato area (the local paper calls him 'il monferrino'), and Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino says Tether's stake in Juventus started because both he and Devasini are lifelong Juventus fans.
notes: Extremely private; almost never gives interviews - public face of Tether is CEO Paolo Ardoino, the realistic route for any podcast request. Energy/data-center angle: Tether's bitcoin-mining and AI compute investments (e.g. Northern Data). Avoid regulatory-history topics.

name: Julia Koch
current_role: Director, Koch, Inc.; president, David H. Koch Foundation; founder and chair, Julia Koch Family Foundation
profile: Julia Koch and her three children inherited a 42% stake in Koch, Inc. (formerly Koch Industries) when her husband David Koch died in 2019, making her one of the world's richest women. An Iowa native and former assistant to designer Adolfo, she now runs the family's philanthropy and has moved into sports: 15% of BSE Global (Nets, Liberty) in 2024 and 10% of the NFL's New York Giants in 2025.
interesting_fact: Before marrying David Koch she worked as fashion designer Adolfo's assistant, doing fittings for Nancy Reagan; in 1997 she co-chaired the Met Gala with Anna Wintour and Patrick McCarthy.
deep_cut_fact: NYU Langone has an endowed 'Julia Koch Associate Professorship of Orthopedic Surgery', held by Hip Center director Roy Davidovitch, a pioneer of muscle-sparing hip replacement; she also backs East Harlem's LSA Family Health Service, founded by the Little Sisters of the Assumption.
notes: Tends to avoid public attention, but her own site publishes media and general-inquiry emails (best first route: media@juliakoch.com). Grew up in Indianola, Iowa and Conway, Arkansas; University of Central Arkansas graduate.

name: Zhang Yiming
current_role: Co-founder and largest shareholder of ByteDance (stepped down as CEO 2021 and chairman Nov 2021); no formal executive title
profile: Born 1983 in Longyan, Fujian, Zhang founded ByteDance in 2012 in a four-bedroom Beijing apartment, building Toutiao, Douyin and TikTok on AI-driven recommendation. He left management in 2021 but reportedly keeps over 50% of voting rights. In 2026 TikTok's US business passed to an Oracle/Silver Lake-led consortium, while ByteDance's Doubao became China's top AI app; Fortune named him Asia's richest person (Sept 2026).
interesting_fact: Sequoia Capital initially turned him down; ByteDance's first backer was Susquehanna, and Sequoia came around to lead a $100M round in 2014. He was on Forbes China 30 Under 30 in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he became the fifth employee and first engineer at travel-search site Kuxun; after a short, stifling stint at Microsoft and the failed startup Fanfou, his first company was 99fang.com, a real-estate search business spun out of Kuxun in 2009.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews since 2021 and reportedly spends much time in Singapore focused on AI research. Only realistic route is ByteDance corporate communications. Wikipedia cites Fortune (Sept 2026) for the Asia's-richest claim.

name: Gautam Adani
current_role: Chairman, Adani Group (Ahmedabad; ports, airports, power, green energy, data centres)
profile: College dropout Gautam Adani founded a commodities trading firm in 1988 that grew into the Adani Group, India's largest port and airport operator with major power, cement and renewables interests. He aims to be the world's largest green-energy producer and in 2026 announced a $100B plan for green-powered AI data centres in India.
interesting_fact: Adani has said he wants to be the world's largest green-energy producer, committing up to $70B to renewables; the group is building a giant renewable-energy park at Khavda in Gujarat's Rann of Kutch.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he left Ahmedabad for Mumbai (c.1978) and worked as a diamond sorter at Mahendra Brothers before setting up his own diamond brokerage in Zaveri Bazaar; he has recounted that his first deal, with a Japanese buyer, earned him a Rs 10,000 commission.

public_contacts.value: roy.paul@adani.com (Roy Paul, Adani Group Corporate Communication)

notes: Highly relevant to energy/data-centre theme (AdaniConneX data-centre JV, $100B AI data-centre plan, Khavda renewables). Sensitive topics: Hindenburg report (2023) and US DOJ/SEC indictment (Nov 2024) - avoid in outreach. Corporate Communication (Roy Paul) is the standard media route.

name: Jeff Yass
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director, Susquehanna International Group (SIG), Bala Cynwyd, Pennsylvania
profile: Jeff Yass co-founded Susquehanna International Group in 1987, after a stint as a professional gambler and options trading on the Philadelphia Stock Exchange from 1981. SIG is now one of the world's largest options market makers and trading firms, with 3,000+ staff. Its venture arm made early bets on hundreds of private companies, most valuably TikTok parent ByteDance.
interesting_fact: For a college economics class at SUNY Binghamton, Yass wrote a paper titled 'An Econometric Analysis of Horse Racing,' later published in Gambling Times. SIG still trains its traders with poker, and its staff have won three World Series of Poker bracelets.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Janine fund the Yass Prize, billed as the 'Pulitzer for Education Innovation.' Run by the Center for Education Reform since 2021, it rewards entrepreneurial schools and education providers that meet its 'STOP' test: Sustainable, Transformational, Outstanding, Permissionless.

public_contacts.value: info@edreform.com (Center for Education Reform, which runs the Yass Prize)

notes: Very private: he rarely gives interviews and keeps no public social media. He is a major political donor, so expect PR caution. SIG's media inbox is the official route; the Yass Prize/edreform channel may suit an education or entrepreneurship angle.

name: Charles Koch
current_role: Chairman and Co-CEO, Koch, Inc. (Wichita, Kansas); founder, Stand Together
profile: Wichita-born MIT engineer (b. 1935) who has run Koch since 1967, turning his father's Oklahoma crude-gathering business into one of America's largest private companies (~$125B revenue; refining, chemicals, Georgia-Pacific, Molex, Guardian, etc.). He took on a co-CEO (Dave Robertson) in 2023 and moved $5B+ of nonvoting stock to nonprofits; he remains focused on Principle Based Management and Stand Together philanthropy.
interesting_fact: In 2026 he and son Chase released a leadership book, 'Becoming a Principle-Driven Leader', laying out 41 'Principles of Human Progress', paired with an AI learning tool - an evolution of the Market-Based Management framework he began forming in Wichita.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three MIT degrees - a B.S. in general engineering (1957) and master's degrees in nuclear (1958) and chemical engineering (1959) - and started his career as a consultant at Arthur D. Little before returning to Wichita in 1961 to join Rock Island Oil & Refining, which he renamed Koch Industries in 1967.
notes: Age ~91. Media inquiries go via Koch's 'Connect with Koch' page (general & media inquiries). Data-center angle: Koch businesses (Molex, Koch Engineered Solutions, Guardian, energy) are active in the AI/data-center supply chain. Degrees/birth from Koch's official bio: https://www.kochinc.com/leadership/charles-koch

name: Tadashi Yanai
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Fast Retailing Co. (parent of Uniqlo, GU and Theory)
profile: Japan's richest person. Yanai turned his father's small tailoring business in Ube, Yamaguchi into Fast Retailing, opening the first Uniqlo in Hiroshima in 1984. Uniqlo now has nearly 2,500 stores in 25 countries, and the group earned $2.8B net profit on $22B revenue in FY Aug 2025. He still runs the company and aims to overtake Inditex and H&M as the world's largest apparel retailer.
interesting_fact: The name Uniqlo began as 'Unique Clothing'. When the brand was registered in Hong Kong in 1988, the 'C' was reportedly misread as a 'Q', and Yanai liked the new spelling enough to adopt it across Japan.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Waseda in 1971, his first job was selling kitchenware and men's clothing at a JUSCO supermarket; he quit after about a year to join his father's shop. He later endowed the Yanai Initiative for Globalizing Japanese Humanities, a UCLA-Waseda partnership, with gifts of $2.5M (2014), $25M (2020) and $31M (2024).
notes: Fast Retailing does not publish a press email. Media requests go through its corporate PR department, and the IR pages are at https://www.fastretailing.com/eng/ir/. He received the Malcolm S. Forbes Lifetime Achievement Award in Oct 2025, and made English Fast Retailing's company language. He sat on SoftBank's board for 18 years until 2019.

name: Zhong Shanshan
current_role: Founder and chairman, Nongfu Spring (HKEX: 9633); controlling shareholder, Beijing Wantai Biological Pharmacy
profile: Hangzhou-born Zhong (b. 1954) left primary school during the Cultural Revolution, worked in construction and as a Zhejiang Daily journalist, then founded what became Nongfu Spring in 1996. It grew into China's top bottled water and packaged-beverage brand and listed in Hong Kong in 2020; he also controls vaccine/diagnostics maker Wantai. He is regularly ranked China's richest person.
interesting_fact: After Nongfu Spring's Sept 2020 IPO and Wantai's April 2020 listing, Zhong briefly became Asia's richest person, with Forbes putting him sixth in the world in Jan 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before bottled water, he quit his newspaper job in 1988 and moved to Hainan, where he sold mushrooms, prawns and turtles, then became a regional sales agent for rival Wahaha and sold health supplements (his first company, Yangshengtang).
notes: Extremely private ('lone wolf' in Chinese media); almost no interviews. Only route is via Nongfu Spring's corporate office/IR (company secretary listed in HKEX annual reports). Avoid the 2024 nationalist online attacks and his son's nationality as topics.

name: Germán Larrea Mota Velasco
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO of Grupo México; Chairman of Southern Copper Corp. (NYSE: SCCO)
profile: Mexico's second-richest person controls Grupo México, the country's largest miner and a top global copper producer with operations in Mexico, Peru and the U.S., plus the Ferromex rail network (GMéxico Transportes, spun off in 2017). He has run the group since 1994; record copper prices pushed Southern Copper to record profits in 2026. In 2025 he made an unsuccessful bid for Citi's Banamex.
interesting_fact: He breeds Thoroughbreds as St. George Stable; his mare Letruska became the first horse that had raced in Mexico to win a U.S. Grade I stakes, the 2021 Apple Blossom Handicap.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the family mining empire he was a publishing entrepreneur: in 1978 he founded Grupo Impresa, a printing and publishing company he chaired until it was sold in 1989.
notes: Famously reclusive (Bloomberg called him 'the reclusive $30 billion tycoon'); almost never gives interviews. Only realistic route is corporate (Southern Copper IR / Grupo México). Avoid the 2014 Sonora spill and Pasta de Conchos topics in outreach.

name: Dieter Schwarz
current_role: Owner (via Dieter Schwarz Foundation) and effective controller of Schwarz Group (Lidl, Kaufland, Schwarz Digits), Neckarsulm, Germany
profile: Long ranked Germany's richest person, Schwarz (b. 1939, Heilbronn) opened the first Lidl store in 1973 and took over his father's business in 1977, building Schwarz Group (Lidl, Kaufland) into Europe's largest retailer (>$200B revenue). His stake sits in the Dieter Schwarz Foundation; the group is expanding into cloud/AI via Schwarz Digits and STACKIT.
interesting_fact: Schwarz Group is becoming an AI data-center player: in Nov 2025 Schwarz Digits broke ground on an EUR 11bn data center in Lubbenau, on a former coal power plant site, to be run by its STACKIT cloud with up to ~100,000 GPUs.
deep_cut_fact: He avoided calling his stores 'Schwarz-Markt' (literally 'black market'); after spotting a newspaper article about painter and retired schoolteacher Ludwig Lidl, he bought the rights to the Lidl name from him for 1,000 German marks.
notes: Extremely private: no interviews, almost no photos or recordings. Interview extremely unlikely; any approach via Schwarz Group press office or the foundation (Bildungscampus Heilbronn). Data-center angle: Schwarz Digits/STACKIT and Heilbronn's AI park (IPAI) are better podcast entry points via their executives.

name: William H. III Gates
current_role: Chair, Gates Foundation; founder & chairman, TerraPower; founder, Breakthrough Energy; technical adviser to Microsoft
profile: Co-founded Microsoft in 1975. His wealth is now managed largely by Cascade Investment (10%+ stakes in Republic Services, Ecolab, etc.). Chairs the Gates Foundation, which he plans to wind down by 2045, and is a major energy investor through TerraPower (Natrium advanced nuclear) and Breakthrough Energy.
interesting_fact: Founded TerraPower in 2006; its Natrium sodium-cooled reactor with molten-salt storage in Kemmerer, Wyoming is one of the leading US advanced-nuclear projects - directly relevant to data-center power demand.
deep_cut_fact: As a Harvard student he co-authored a 1979 Discrete Mathematics paper with Christos Papadimitriou, 'Bounds for Sorting by Prefix Reversal' (the 'pancake problem'); its upper bound stood for almost 30 years until a UT Dallas team beat it in 2008.
notes: For an energy/data-center podcast, TerraPower press (press@terrapower.com) or Breakthrough Energy are the most relevant routes; Gates Foundation media line asks for name, outlet, questions and deadline. Extremely high-demand; expect gatekeeping.

name: Zeng Yuqun
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd (CATL); vice chairman, All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Robin Zeng (b. 1968, Ningde, Fujian) co-founded consumer-battery maker ATL in 1999, stayed on after TDK bought it in 2005, then spun out its EV-battery unit as CATL. CATL listed in Shenzhen in 2018 (Hong Kong 2025) and is the world's largest EV-battery maker, now pushing into grid energy storage, sodium-ion cells and battery swapping.
interesting_fact: He holds a PhD in condensed matter physics from the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences, earned in 2006 while already running ATL.
deep_cut_fact: Before batteries, the marine-engineering graduate of Shanghai Jiao Tong University started out at a state-owned shipbuilding company in Fujian, then spent about 10 years at an electronic-parts factory (SAE Magnetics, part of TDK) before co-founding ATL with two former colleagues.
notes: No published press/IR email found on catl.com in this pass (site has a Contact Us section). Best route is CATL's corporate communications via catl.com; English name Robin Zeng.

name: Liang Wenfeng
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeepSeek (Hangzhou); co-founder of quant hedge fund High-Flyer
profile: Liang Wenfeng (b. 1985) co-founded quant fund High-Flyer in 2015-16 with Zhejiang University classmates, using AI-driven trading to build one of China's largest quant firms and a large GPU cluster. He spun that compute into DeepSeek in 2023; its low-cost R1 model (2025) shook the AI industry. DeepSeek raised $7.4B in June 2026 at a $52B valuation.
interesting_fact: While still a student, DJI founder Frank Wang (Wang Tao) reportedly invited him to join DJI as a co-founder; he declined to pursue AI in financial markets. He met President Xi Jinping at a 2025 tech-entrepreneur symposium in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: His 2010 Zhejiang University master's thesis was on object tracking with low-cost pan-tilt-zoom (PTZ) cameras, supervised by Xiang Zhiyu; the work appeared as 'Algorithm of robust object tracking using PTZ camera' (Liang Wen-feng & Xiang Zhi-yu) in the Journal of Zhejiang University (Engineering Science), 2011.
notes: Extremely media-shy; DeepSeek has historically declined press requests and Liang has given only a couple of interviews (e.g. 36Kr/Waves, translated by ChinaTalk). service@deepseek.com is a general company contact, not a press desk. Company-level X account only; no personal social accounts.

name: Robin Zeng
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. (CATL); vice chairman, All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Zeng (曾毓群) co-founded ATL in 1999 making lithium-polymer batteries for gadgets; after TDK bought ATL in 2005 he spun its EV-battery unit out as CATL in 2011. CATL, based in his hometown Ningde, is the world's largest EV-battery maker (Shenzhen/HK-listed), supplies BMW, Geely and Tesla, and is expanding into grid storage.
interesting_fact: Early in his career he worked at a state-owned shipbuilding company in Fujian; he studied marine engineering at Shanghai Jiao Tong University before moving into electronics and batteries.
deep_cut_fact: He kept studying while building ATL: an MSc in electronics/information engineering from South China University of Technology (2001), then a PhD in physics from the Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (2006) - a battery tycoon with a physics doctorate.
notes: Rarely gives Western media interviews; no personal social accounts found. Best route is CATL IR/corporate communications. Strong fit for energy-storage and EV-battery topics; note US geopolitical sensitivity around CATL.

name: Andreas von Bechtolsheim
current_role: Founder and Chief Architect, Arista Networks (leads advanced AI, silicon and optics initiatives)
profile: German-born engineer who co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982 after building the original SUN workstation as a Stanford grad student. Wrote an early $100,000 check to Google, and in 2004 co-founded Arista Networks, now a key supplier of Ethernet switching for AI data centers; he owns a large stake and focuses on AI networking, silicon and optics.
interesting_fact: He built the original SUN (Stanford University Network) workstation as a grad student; Sun Microsystems was named after it. He has co-founded two other networking firms with David Cheriton (Granite Systems, sold to Cisco; Kealia, sold to Sun).
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in a Lake Constance village (~1973) he built an Intel 8080-based controller for a local CNC-machine maker, coding it in binary on a hex keypad with no assembler. Too young to be hired, he was paid a royalty per box sold, and soon out-earned his teacher father.
notes: No personal social accounts found; best route is Arista corporate communications (Amanda Jaramillo). He speaks at OFC/Optica events on AI optics, a good hook. Under a 2024 SEC settlement he cannot serve as a public-company officer/director for five years; avoid the topic. Jugend forscht national physics winner 1974.

name: Len Blavatnik
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Access Industries (owner of Warner Music Group stake, LyondellBasell, DAZN)
profile: Soviet-born US/UK investor who emigrated in 1978, studied at Columbia and Harvard Business School, and made an early fortune via TNK-BP (stake sold in 2013 for $7B). His Access Industries bought Warner Music in 2011 for $3.3B and holds stakes in LyondellBasell, DAZN, biotech and tech (incl. DigitalOcean). Has given/pledged over $1B, mostly to universities.
interesting_fact: He bought Damien Hirst's gilded woolly mammoth skeleton 'Gone (but) Not Forgotten' for $15M in 2014, and has produced Broadway shows including 'The Front Page' and 'Sunset Boulevard'.
deep_cut_fact: His first US job was as a computer programmer in the biostatistics department of Mount Sinai School of Medicine; the pay let him study computer science at Columbia part-time. He then worked at Arthur Andersen and Macy's, and applied only to Harvard Business School ('I was pretty naive').

notes: Rarely gives interviews; best route is Hawthorn Advisors (Access press agency). Blavatnik Family Foundation also linked from Access site. Data-center angle: Access holds a stake in DigitalOcean.

name: Henry Samueli
current_role: Cofounder and director, Broadcom Inc. (stepped down as chairman June 2026); owner of the NHL Anaheim Ducks; chairman, Samueli Foundation
profile: Electrical engineer and former UCLA professor who cofounded Broadcom with Henry Nicholas in 1991 in a Redondo Beach condo; Broadcom's broadband and networking chips (now central to AI data-center networking and custom AI accelerators) made him a billionaire. He stepped down as Broadcom chairman in June 2026 but remains a director, and focuses on the Ducks, Honda Center/OCVIBE and the Samueli Foundation.
interesting_fact: Son of Polish Holocaust survivors, he holds 75+ patents and won the Marconi Prize; he and his wife gave UC Irvine $200M in 2017, the largest gift in the school's history.
deep_cut_fact: In 7th grade he talked his teacher into letting him build a five-tube radio kit (a ninth-grade project) instead of a crystal set; decades later he tracked down the same kit, a Graymark 506B, on eBay and built it again.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Samueli Foundation (Corona del Mar, CA; info@samueli.org) is the most personal route; Broadcom corporate comms for chip/AI topics. IEEE Spectrum's 2025 Medal of Honor profile is a great prep read. Deep-cut source is IEEE (accessible).

name: Vagit Alekperov
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder of Lukoil (president 1993-2022; left the board in April 2022)
profile: Baku-born oilman who worked Siberian fields, became the USSR's youngest deputy oil and gas minister in 1990, then built Lukoil (1993) into Russia's largest private oil company. He resigned as president and director in April 2022 after UK/Australian sanctions but remains its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: In 1990, as Soviet deputy minister, he led the delegation to BP in the UK and took over the agenda, asking BP's executives to explain how a modern vertically integrated oil company should be set up - the template for Lukoil.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious coin collector: the International Numismatic Club museum, opened in 2015 in Moscow's restored 17th-century Yusupov-Zinoviev Chambers on his initiative, displays coins from his personal collection, including a Konstantin ruble and the first regular-mint gold chervonets of 1701.
notes: Sanctioned by UK, Canada, Australia and New Zealand since 2022; Lukoil itself was sanctioned by the US in 2025. Very private, gives few interviews. Only company press route is Lukoil media relations, and he no longer holds a formal role there. Check sanctions/legal considerations before any outreach.

name: Linda Stephens
current_role: Co-owner/heir of Endeavor Energy Resources stake (now merged into Diamondback Energy); not involved in day-to-day operations
profile: Linda (Nagy) Stephens is the widow of Autry Stephens, the Midland, Texas wildcatter who founded Permian Basin driller Endeavor Energy Resources and died in August 2024. Endeavor was sold to Diamondback Energy for about $26B (cash plus stock), closing September 2024; her fortune derives from that family stake. Daughter Lyndal Stephens Greth chairs the family's activities.
interesting_fact: Endeavor's founder held drilling rights to ~350,000 Permian acres for decades, rebuffing offers, before the 2024 $26B sale to Diamondback.
notes: Very private; almost no public profile of her own. Reporting says she is not involved in operations. Family philanthropy runs via the Stephens Greth Family Foundation (Midland, est. 2024, led by daughter Lyndal Stephens Greth), which funded UT Austin's Autry C. Stephens Engineering Discovery Building - likely the only institutional route. No published contact found.

name: Lyndal Stephens Greth
current_role: President and director, Stephens Greth Family Foundation (Midland, TX); former chair of Endeavor Energy Resources; major Diamondback Energy shareholder
profile: Daughter of Endeavor Energy Resources founder Autry Stephens; served on Endeavor's board from 2013, became vice chairman, then chair on his death in August 2024. She oversaw the close of Endeavor's ~$26B cash-and-stock sale to Diamondback Energy (Sept 2024), leaving the Stephens family as a large FANG holder. She now leads the ~$2B Stephens Greth Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: Endeavor, built by her father from 1979, was one of the largest private U.S. oil producers (~327,000 boe/day in 2024) before the $26B Diamondback deal; she took the chair when he died months before closing.
deep_cut_fact: Her Stephens Greth Foundation gave $8M to the SPCA of Texas's 'Care Unleashed' campaign ($5M for a new building, $3M for programs), and the SPCA's Dallas campus was renamed the Stephens Greth Foundation Campus; the foundation also funded UT Austin's Autry C. Stephens Engineering Discovery Building.
notes: Very private; no public interviews or social accounts found. Foundation (EIN 99-2739395, Midland TX) has no published website/email found. Best route is likely via the foundation's registered address or Diamondback Energy's corporate office.

name: Leonid Mikhelson
current_role: Chairman of the Management Board (CEO) and co-founder, PAO Novatek; major shareholder of petrochemical group Sibur
profile: Civil engineer who built Soviet gas pipelines, privatised his pipeline-construction trust in 1991 and grew it into Novatek, Russia's largest independent gas and LNG producer (Yamal LNG, Arctic LNG 2). He also holds just over 30% of Sibur and funds the V-A-C Foundation, which turned a power station opposite the Kremlin into the GES-2 art centre (opened 2021).
interesting_fact: He spent more than $470 million converting the GES-2 power plant across from the Kremlin, designed by Renzo Piano's studio, into a contemporary art space that opened in late 2021.
deep_cut_fact: As a young man he dreamed of being a pilot (rejected for poor eyesight), then nearly left to play volleyball professionally in Tashkent before a shoulder injury ended it; in 1991 he sold his Zhiguli car to buy a 15% stake in the newly privatised pipeline company Nova.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK government in 2022 (and named on the US CAATSA 'oligarch' list in 2018); Novatek's Arctic LNG 2 is under US sanctions. Outreach from a Western podcast may be legally/politically sensitive - check sanctions rules first. Only corporate channels are public.

name: Andy Von Bechtolsheim
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, Arista Networks (responsible for advanced AI, silicon and optics initiatives)
profile: German-born engineer (Andreas von Bechtolsheim) who co-founded Sun Microsystems in 1982, later Granite Systems (sold to Cisco) and Kealia, and co-founded Arista Networks, whose data-center switches power AI/cloud networks. Early angel investor in Google. Now Arista's chief architect focused on AI networking, silicon and optics (e.g. XPO liquid-cooled pluggable optics MSA, 2026).
interesting_fact: In September 1998 he wrote a $100,000 check to 'Google Inc.' before the company was even incorporated, prompting Page and Brin to formally set it up; the stake was worth at least $1B at the IPO.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he won Germany's national Jugend forscht competition in physics (1974) with an ultrasound device that precisely measured flows; at 16 he also designed an Intel 8008-based industrial controller for a local firm, programmed in binary, whose royalties helped fund his education.
notes: Press email is Arista Corporate Communications (Amanda Jaramillo) per 2026 releases. Speaks often at optics events (OFC, Optica, PIC Summit); strong fit for AI networking/optics. No personal socials found. Title moved from Chairman to Chief Architect after a 2024 SEC settlement - avoid the topic.

name: Emmanuel Besnier
current_role: Chairman (président du conseil de surveillance) and controlling shareholder, Groupe Lactalis
profile: Emmanuel Besnier runs and controls family-owned Lactalis, the world's largest dairy group (Président, Galbani, Siggi's, Stonyfield). It had €31B+ in 2025 revenue and owns 266+ plants in 51 countries. His grandfather André founded it in Laval in 1933. Emmanuel took over in 2000 after his father Michel's death and has since made more than 120 acquisitions. His siblings Jean-Michel and Marie hold the rest of the shares.
interesting_fact: Known as 'the invisible billionaire' and 'the Emperor of Cheese' for avoiding the press. On his first day in business, his family's founder collected 17 liters of milk and made 35 camemberts.
deep_cut_fact: Besnier grew up in Laval (Mayenne), where his grandfather André, a barrel-maker (tonnelier) by trade, started making camembert in 1933. Emmanuel studied at Paris's Institut Supérieur de Gestion (class of 1993), did his internships inside the family group, and was hired by his father as Lactalis development director in 1995.
notes: Extremely press-shy; he rarely gives interviews (a notable exception was Ouest-France, April 2024). There is no personal social presence. The only route is Lactalis corporate communications via the website's Médias / Contactez-nous section, in French.

name: Phil Knight
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman Emeritus, Nike, Inc.; philanthropist (Knight Foundation)
profile: University of Oregon miler who in 1964 put up $500 with his track coach Bill Bowerman to start Blue Ribbon Sports, importing Japanese running shoes, which became Nike. He retired as chairman in 2016 after 52 years; his family still owns ~21% of Nike, and he and wife Penny are among America's biggest donors (Oregon, Stanford, OHSU Knight Cancer Institute).
interesting_fact: He paid Portland State student Carolyn Davidson $35 to design the Swoosh, and early on sold Japanese running shoes from the trunk of his car.
deep_cut_fact: Nike's idea started as a Stanford MBA small-business class paper titled 'Can Japanese Sports Shoes Do to German Sports Shoes What Japanese Cameras Did to German Cameras?' While building the company he also worked as a CPA at Coopers & Lybrand and then Price Waterhouse.
notes: Born 1938; no indication of death as of Nov 2026. Very private, rarely gives interviews; memoir 'Shoe Dog' (2016) is the best talking-point source. Nike press/IR is a corporate route only; no published personal or foundation contact found.

name: Suleiman Kerimov
current_role: Member of Russia's Federation Council representing the Republic of Dagestan (since 2008); family fortune tied to gold miner Polyus
profile: Suleiman Kerimov, a Dagestan-born economist, built his fortune investing in distressed Russian assets and stakes in Gazprom, Sberbank and Uralkali, then rebuilt it after 2008 losses by buying into Polyus, Russia's largest gold producer. Family stakes in Polyus were later passed to his son and then to others amid US (2018), EU and UK (2022) sanctions; he remains a Russian senator.
interesting_fact: In January 2011 he bought Dagestan football club Anzhi Makhachkala, which signed Roberto Carlos and then Samuel Eto'o, making Eto'o the highest-paid footballer in the world at the time.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Dagestan State University in 1989 with a degree in financial accounting and economics, his first job was as an economist at the Eltav electrical plant in Makhachkala, which made transistors and semiconductors for TV makers; he rose to deputy director general there.
notes: Sanctioned by the US (2018), EU and UK (2022): any contact or business engagement raises legal/compliance issues; consult counsel before outreach. Very private, no published personal or press contacts found. Only formal channel would be his Federation Council office (council.gov.ru, not reachable from this environment).

name: Rupert Murdoch
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Fox Corporation and News Corp (stepped down as chairman Nov 2023)
profile: Australian-born (Melbourne, 1931) media mogul who inherited the small Adelaide paper The News at 21 and built a global empire spanning Fox News, The Wall Street Journal, The Times of London and the New York Post. He sold most of 21st Century Fox's entertainment assets to Disney for $71.3B in 2019 and stepped down as chairman of Fox and News Corp in 2023.
interesting_fact: His first major U.S. purchase was the New York Post in 1976, which he still owns.
deep_cut_fact: At Geelong Grammar he edited the student journal 'If Revived'; at Worcester College, Oxford he kept a bust of Lenin in his rooms, earning the nickname 'Red Rupert', and managed Cherwell's publisher. After his father's death he worked as a sub-editor at London's Daily Express.

mflorin@newscorp.com (Michael Florin, Investor Relations, News Corp)

name: Warren Edward Buffett
current_role: Director, Berkshire Hathaway (stepped down as CEO at end-2025 and as chairman in Sept 2026; Greg Abel is CEO, Howard Buffett chairman)
profile: The 'Oracle of Omaha' turned failing textile maker Berkshire Hathaway, which he took control of in the 1960s, into a conglomerate spanning insurance (GEICO), BNSF railroad, Berkshire Hathaway Energy and big stakes in Apple and others. He handed the CEO role to Greg Abel on Jan 1, 2026, gave up the chairmanship in Sept 2026, and continues giving most of his fortune away.
interesting_fact: As a high-school sophomore in 1945 he and a friend spent $25 on a used pinball machine for a barber shop; they soon had machines in three Omaha barber shops and sold the business in 1947 for $1,200.
deep_cut_fact: On his first income-tax return, in 1944 at age 13, he took a $35 deduction for the use of his bicycle and watch on his paper route.
notes: Age 96; notoriously does not use email and has no social accounts; Berkshire has no PR department. Only realistic route is a letter to Berkshire's Omaha office. Energy angle: Berkshire Hathaway Energy (utilities, PacifiCorp, MidAmerican). Also a lifelong ukulele player (Wikipedia).

name: Vladimir Lisin
current_role: Chairman and majority shareholder, NLMK Group (Novolipetsk Steel); owner of Port One (UCL Holding)
profile: Lisin (b. 1956, Ivanovo) went from coal-mine electrical fitter to steel-mill manager. He partnered with Trans World Group in the 1990s and emerged controlling NLMK, one of Russia's largest steelmakers. He also owns port operator Port One (Baltic and Black Sea) and sold railcar operator Freight One in 2023. Forbes put him at ~$25.5B in 2026.
interesting_fact: A keen sport shooter, he built one of Europe's largest shooting-range complexes at Lisya Nora near Moscow and was president of the International Shooting Sport Federation (ISSF) for four years until 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He is a working academic as well as an oligarch: he holds patents on metallurgical processes, has published 100+ articles and 15 monographs on metallurgy and economics, holds a PhD in metallurgical engineering (MISiS) and a doctorate in economics, and has been a professor at RANEPA.
notes: Russian steel oligarch with sanctions exposure: reported sanctioned by Australia, and listed by Canada in June 2025; not US/EU-sanctioned as of 2024 reporting. Check legal and reputational fit before outreach. No personal public channels. NLMK's press-office page shows info@ with a Cyrillic 'с', so retype the address rather than copy it.

name: John Tu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kingston Technology (Fountain Valley, California)
profile: Taiwan-raised, German-educated engineer John Tu co-founded Kingston Technology with David Sun in 1987, after the pair sold an earlier memory business and lost a fortune in the 1987 crash. Kingston is the world's largest independent maker of memory and storage products and Orange County's largest private company. Tu still runs it as CEO, from a cubicle on the sales floor.
interesting_fact: Kingston is named after one of Tu's favorite bands, the Kingston Trio. Tu, a drummer, leads his own local band, 'JT and California Dreamin''.
deep_cut_fact: Kingston traces back to a Taipei fortune teller. In Aug 1987 Tu insisted on a reading and was told he'd find a partner and start a company; Sun then heard the same. 'I paid the fortune teller, actually,' Tu joked. He once worked as a cook in his uncle's Chinese restaurant.

public_contacts.value: Kingston press contacts page (US HQ PR representative and regional contacts)

notes: Low profile; Tu and Sun rarely give interviews. PR@kingston.com came from a 2026 Kingston release's media contact (seen via search; Kingston's site blocks automated fetches). He gives through the John and Mary Tu Foundation (music education, Freedom Writers). Kingston's server memory and SSDs are a data-center hook.

name: David Sun
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Kingston Technology (Fountain Valley, California)
profile: Taiwan-born engineer David Sun co-founded Kingston Technology with John Tu in 1987, after the pair lost most of their first fortune (from memory firm Camintonn, sold to AST Research) in the 1987 crash. Kingston is the world's largest independent maker of memory and storage products. Sun still runs U.S. and Far East operations as COO, famously from a cubicle on the sales floor.
interesting_fact: Sun and Tu met in a basketball league in 1978. Kingston is named after Tu's favourite band, the Kingston Trio. In 2026 the private company is shipping 30.72TB Gen5 NVMe SSDs for data centers and has passed 100 million A400 SSDs shipped.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding companies, Sun emigrated from Taiwan in 1977 with an electrical engineering degree from Tatung Institute of Technology. He was chief engineer at Alpha Microsystems in Costa Mesa from 1978 to 1982. He is an avid golfer.
notes: Low-profile. Co-founder John Tu is the more public face. Route via Kingston's PR team (Kingston Digital PR Team, US HQ). Emails on the press-contacts page are masked/behind bot protection. The data-center SSD line is a good hook for the podcast.

name: Greg Brockman
current_role: Co-founder and President, OpenAI (also leads product strategy since May 2026, plus AI infrastructure)
profile: North Dakota-raised programmer who left Harvard/MIT to join Stripe, becoming its first CTO (grew it from 4 to 250 people). Co-founded OpenAI in 2015; his stake made him a multi-billionaire. In 2026 he took charge of OpenAI's unified product team (ChatGPT, Codex, API) alongside its compute/data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: Won a silver medal at the 2006 International Chemistry Olympiad and was the first North Dakotan Intel Science Talent Search finalist since 1973.
deep_cut_fact: His first-ever paid job was an acting gig: as a scrawny ninth grader he auditioned to be a marching tin-soldier extra in a Mannheim Steamroller Christmas concert in Grand Forks. After high school he took a gap year and wrote ~100 pages of a first-principles chemistry textbook, still unfinished on his site.
notes: Publishes his own email on his homepage (obfuscated as greg [at] gregbrockman [dot] com). Very active on X as @gdb. Strong fit for AI compute/data-center topics (oversees OpenAI infrastructure). 'substack' entry is actually his personal blog.

name: Lyu Xiangyang
current_role: Chairman, Youngy Investment Holding Group (融捷集团); Vice Chairman and non-executive director, BYD
profile: Lyu (Lu) Xiangyang, born 1962 in Wuwei, Anhui, is a cousin of BYD founder Wang Chuanfu and supplied about RMB 2.5m of the seed money that started BYD's battery business in 1995. That year he and his wife Zhang Changhong also founded Guangzhou-based Youngy, which grew from property investing into lithium mining and battery materials alongside his large BYD stake.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he bought the Jiajika spodumene deposit in Sichuan (described as Asia's largest) for about RMB 110m, years before the EV boom; reportedly he has never sold a BYD share since his founding investment.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an investor he began his career at a local branch of the People's Bank of China, then moved to Guangdong in the early 1990s to work with brokerages before founding Youngy.

public_contacts.value: IR@younergy.cn (Youngy Co., SZSE: 002192, board secretary Chen Xinhua)

notes: Also romanized Lu Xiangyang / Lü Xiangyang. Fortune shared with wife Zhang Changhong. Very low public profile; best formal route is via Youngy Co. (融捷股份) investor relations or BYD.

name: King Faud Bin Abdul Aziz Alsaud
profile: King Fahd bin Abdulaziz Al Saud (name misspelled 'Faud' in the source list) was King and Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia from 13 June 1982 until his death on 1 August 2005; Forbes listed him in 1997-1998.
notes: Deceased 1 August 2005 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fahd_of_Saudi_Arabia). Head-of-state wealth estimate, not an entrepreneur. Skip.

name: Lakshmi N Mittal
current_role: Executive Chairman, ArcelorMittal (since Feb 2021); Chairman, Aperam
profile: Lakshmi Mittal built Mittal Steel through acquisitions of struggling steelworks worldwide and merged it with Arcelor in 2006 to create ArcelorMittal, one of the world's largest steelmakers. He was CEO until 2021, when son Aditya became CEO and he became executive chairman; shareholders re-elected him to the board for three years in May 2026. Based in London.
interesting_fact: For ArcelorMittal's 20th anniversary in 2026 he delivered a video address at the Global Steel Dynamics Forum in New York and joined Aditya Mittal on a special episode of the company's 'Steel Talks' podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He funded the Mittal Champions Trust (co-founded 2005 with tennis star Mahesh Bhupathi), which backed about 40 Indian athletes with Olympic potential and supported shooter Abhinav Bindra's 2008 Beijing gold, India's first individual Olympic gold medal.
notes: Very senior, media-selective; route via ArcelorMittal Corporate Communications (London). Company has its own podcast (Steel Talks) and he appears on it. Energy angle: steel decarbonisation (XCarb, DRI/hydrogen). His father Mohanlal Mittal died Jan 2026 - avoid in outreach.

name: Christy Walton
current_role: Walmart heiress and philanthropist/investor (Cuna del Mar founder); no executive role
profile: Christy Walton, widow of Walmart heir John T. Walton (d. 2005), inherited a stake in the retailer and is among America's richest women. She lives privately in Jackson, Wyoming, supports environmental and sustainability causes, and in 2010 founded Cuna del Mar, a fund backing sustainable seafood/aquaculture. In 2025 she ran a NYT ad urging civil, nonpartisan discourse.
interesting_fact: In 2010 she established Cuna del Mar, an investment fund backing companies developing a sustainable supply of seafood.
deep_cut_fact: She set up Tenaja Productions to finance the film adaptation of Rudolfo Anaya's Chicano coming-of-age novel 'Bless Me, Ultima'; filming wrapped in Santa Fe, New Mexico in 2010.
notes: Very private (Forbes: 'leads a very private life in Jackson, Wyoming'). No published office/press contacts found; she has been a director of Teton Science Schools and a San Diego Natural History Museum board member.

name: Jack Ma
current_role: Co-founder of Alibaba Group; member of the Alibaba Partnership committee (per Caixin, June 2026); founder, Jack Ma Foundation
profile: Former English teacher Jack Ma (Ma Yun) co-founded Alibaba in Hangzhou in 1999 and built it into one of the world's largest e-commerce and cloud groups, stepping down as executive chairman in 2019. After years largely out of view he returned to China in 2023 and since 2025 has been visibly re-engaged at Alibaba, backing its AI and cloud push and e-commerce strategy; he remains a key shareholder.
interesting_fact: Ma owns a vineyard in France and is a martial-arts fan who sparred with Jet Li and others in the 2017 short film 'Gong Shou Dao'.
deep_cut_fact: In 1980, as a teenager guiding tourists in Hangzhou to practise English, he befriended Australian Ken Morley's family; Morley later hosted him in Newcastle, Australia, and in 2017 Ma funded the Ma & Morley Scholarship Program at the University of Newcastle (~A$26M), the university's largest-ever gift.
notes: Very low public profile since 2020; rarely gives interviews. Best formal route is the Jack Ma Foundation (focus: rural education, entrepreneurship, women's leadership) or Alibaba corporate communications. Strong AI/cloud data-center angle via Alibaba Cloud.

name: Stuart Hoegner
current_role: Retired as General Counsel of Tether and Bitfinex (Jan 2025); remains a major Tether shareholder (est. ~12%)
profile: Stuart Hoegner is a Canadian chartered accountant and lawyer who started at Ernst & Young and then ran Gaming Counsel, a boutique practice for online-gambling and crypto clients. He was general counsel of Tether and Bitfinex from 2014 until retiring in Jan 2025. His estimated ~12% of Tether, the largest stablecoin issuer (>$10B profit in 2025), makes him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Hoegner's path to crypto ran through online gaming: before Bitfinex he was director of compliance and deputy general counsel at online-poker software company Excapsa, and his law practice served internet-gaming clients.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 Hoegner edited 'The Law of Bitcoin', one of the first legal guides to bitcoin, covering the US, UK, Canada and Germany, with a foreword by Coin Center's Jerry Brito. At the time he was General Counsel to the Bitcoin Alliance of Canada.
notes: Very low profile since retiring; no current published contact found. His X bio read 'Former GC @Bitfinex @Tether_to' (per Protos), but the handle isn't confirmed. Retirement source: https://www.theblock.co/post/332986/tethers-general-counsel-retires-in-wake-of-mica-stablecoin-regulations-coming-into-effect. Tether press routes would go via tether.io.

name: Henry Cheng
current_role: Chairman, New World Development and Chow Tai Fook Jewellery Group; head of family holding Chow Tai Fook Enterprises
profile: Henry Cheng Kar-shun (b. 1946) succeeded his father Cheng Yu-tung atop the family empire, chairing Chow Tai Fook Jewellery (founded 1929) and developer New World Development. Since son Adrian stepped down as NWD CEO in 2024 (replaced by Eric Ma), he remains chairman, steering NWD through a deleveraging period.
interesting_fact: He paid $71M for a 59.6-carat pink diamond in 2017 and renamed it the CTF Pink Star in tribute to his father; he and his father are rare father-son recipients of Hong Kong's top honours (he got the Grand Bauhinia Medal in 2017).
deep_cut_fact: He studied in Canada at Western's Ivey Business School (HBA 1971, MBA 1972), joined New World straight after in 1972, later co-established the Cheng Yu Tung Management Institute with Ivey and leads the Ivey Asia advisory board; Western gave him an honorary LLD in 1997.
notes: Avoid NWD debt/succession topics. Very senior Hong Kong establishment figure; approach via NWD corporate communications. HKU also gave him an honorary DSocSc.

name: Chen Tianshi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Cambricon Technologies (SSE: 688256)
profile: Born 1985 in Nanchang, Chen entered USTC's gifted 'Special Class for the Young' as a teen and earned a CS PhD by 2010. After research at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, he co-founded AI-chip maker Cambricon in 2016 ('China's Nvidia'); its shares soared from 2024 on demand for domestic AI accelerators.
interesting_fact: Cambricon grew out of academic papers co-written by Chen and his elder brother Chen Yunji; both entered USTC's gifted-youth program and had CS doctorates by 24. The CAS Institute of Computing Technology still holds a minority stake.
deep_cut_fact: He was lead author of 'DianNao' (ASPLOS 2014), an early deep-learning accelerator paper reporting ~118x speedup and ~21x energy savings vs a SIMD CPU; his ICT homepage lists it as an ASPLOS'14 Best Paper Award winner, and it seeded Cambricon's chip line.
notes: No published IR/press email found on company site; investor contact is via Shanghai Stock Exchange (688256) disclosures. Media-shy; rarely gives interviews.

name: Prince Alwaleed Bin Talal Alsaud
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder, Kingdom Holding Company (Tadawul: 4280); Chairman, Alwaleed Philanthropies
profile: Saudi royal and global investor who built Kingdom Holding after graduating from Menlo College in 1979; holdings include Four Seasons, X/xAI, Snap, Rotana and Saudi real estate. PIF bought ~16.9% of Kingdom from him in 2022. Kingdom is principal investor in Jeddah Tower, which he said in July 2026 had reached 430 m and 107 floors, targeting completion in 2028.
interesting_fact: Energy angle: he personally held a stake in Bill Gates's clean-energy fund Breakthrough Energy Ventures, which Kingdom Holding bought from him in April 2026 for SR255m (~$68m), about 30% below its latest audited value. His biggest win remains the $800m Citicorp stake bought in 1991.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 he gave Georgetown University $20 million to create the Prince Alwaleed bin Talal Center for Muslim-Christian Understanding in the School of Foreign Service - then the second-largest gift in the school's history; in 2015 he pledged his entire $32bn fortune to philanthropy.
notes: Best routes: Kingdom Holding corporate communications or Alwaleed Philanthropies. He is famously media-friendly (often hosts journalists). Avoid the 2017 Ritz-Carlton detention topic. Georgetown gift detail also on Wikipedia (Washington Post 2005).

name: Gina Rinehart
current_role: Executive Chairman, Hancock Prospecting Pty Ltd (Perth)
profile: Australia's richest person, Rinehart took over her father Lang Hancock's financially strained Hancock Prospecting in 1992 and rebuilt it around the Roy Hill iron ore mine (shipping since 2015). She has diversified into rare earths, lithium (Azure Minerals with SQM, 2024), gas and cattle, where she is Australia's No.2 producer.
interesting_fact: Hancock Prospecting and its Georgina Hope Foundation have bankrolled Australian Olympic sport: a $10M four-year deal with Swimming Australia from 2012 (renewed, with naming rights to the national championships), plus support for lesser-known sports like synchronised swimming.
deep_cut_fact: A true Pilbara child: until age four she lived at Nunyerry, 60 km north of Wittenoom, before the family moved to Mulga Downs station; she later left an economics degree at the University of Sydney to learn the iron-ore business at her father's side.
