notes: Rarely gives interviews to outlets she considers unfriendly; communicates mostly via Hancock statements and speeches. Energy angle: gas investments and critical minerals (rare earths, lithium). Avoid family trust litigation topics.

name: Gennady Timchenko
current_role: Founder/owner, Volga Group (private investment firm); Chairman of the Board, Kontinental Hockey League (KHL); President, SKA Saint Petersburg
profile: Russian billionaire (born 1952, Leninakan/Gyumri) who co-founded oil trader Gunvor in 1997 and built Volga Group, which holds major stakes in gas producer Novatek and petrochemical group Sibur. A close Putin associate, he is sanctioned by the US (2014) and EU/UK (2022); he sold his Gunvor stake the day before US sanctions hit.
interesting_fact: In 1998 he co-founded the Yawara-Neva judo club in Saint Petersburg (with the Rotenberg brothers; Putin is honorary president), and he has chaired the KHL hockey league since 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer (Leningrad Mechanical Institute, 1976) and started in 1977 at the Izhorsky plant near Saint Petersburg, which built power generators; as a child he lived in East Germany (1959-65) and learned German.
notes: Sanctioned by US, EU and UK; outreach/interviews may raise legal/sanctions-compliance issues for the podcast. Contacts are for the Elena and Gennady Timchenko Foundation (Moscow), not him personally. Volga Group has no reachable public press contact found.

name: Ashok Parmanand Hinduja
current_role: Chairman, Hinduja Group of Companies (India); Chairman, IIHL (IndusInd Bank promoter); Executive Chairman, Hinduja National Power Corp.
profile: Ashok P. Hinduja ('AP') is the youngest son of Hinduja Group founder P.D. Hinduja and has run the group's India business since it re-entered India in the mid-1980s. Holdings span Ashok Leyland, IndusInd Bank (via IIHL), Gulf Oil, HGS, NXTDIGITAL and power. After brothers Srichand (2023) and Gopichand (Nov 2025) died, he and Prakash are the senior generation.
interesting_fact: He is Executive Chairman of Hinduja National Power Corporation, which runs a 1,040 MW thermal power plant, a natural energy-podcast angle.
deep_cut_fact: A Bombay University commerce graduate, he is Managing Trustee of the KPB Hinduja College of Commerce in Mumbai; the group's own bio lists his interests as art, architecture, cinema, television and creative media.
notes: Press contact is Diana Monteiro, VP Corporate Communications & Branding, Hinduja Group (Mumbai), as listed on the group's contact page. Family business has had succession/legal coverage; avoid. Energy angle: Hinduja National Power and Hinduja Renewables.

name: Robert J. Pera
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO of Ubiquiti Inc.; owner of the NBA's Memphis Grizzlies
profile: Robert Pera (b. 1978, St. Louis) was an Apple Wi-Fi test engineer who founded Ubiquiti in 2005 with ~$30,000 of savings and credit-card debt to build long-range, low-cost wireless gear for underserved areas. He took it public in 2011 (NYSE: UI), still owns the large majority, and has expanded into UniFi networking, cameras and switches. He bought the Memphis Grizzlies in 2012.
interesting_fact: The idea for Ubiquiti came at Apple: testing Wi-Fi gear for FCC compliance, he noticed transmit power was far below legal limits and reasoned that boosting it could carry signals dozens of miles; when his bosses ignored the idea he built prototypes at night in his apartment.
deep_cut_fact: At UC San Diego he graduated Phi Beta Kappa with a B.S. in electrical engineering AND a B.A. in Japanese language, then stayed for an EE master's; in high school he had already run his own computer networking/database services company for local businesses.
notes: Famously low-profile and engineering-focused; rarely does interviews (a 2013 LEADERS magazine interview is one). Communicates via his blog/social posts and Ubiquiti shareholder letters. High-school basketball player; deeply involved with the Grizzlies.

name: Nicola Forrest
current_role: Founder, Coaxial (Coaxial Foundation and Coaxial Ventures), Fremantle; co-founder and board member, Minderoo Foundation
profile: Nicola Forrest AO co-founded the Minderoo Foundation (2001) with Andrew Forrest, whose Fortescue Metals iron-ore fortune they built together, and co-owns investment firm Tattarang. After their 2023 separation she set up Coaxial; in Oct 2026 she gave over A$500M (cash plus Fortescue shares) to the Coaxial Foundation, which backs early learning, female founders and Indigenous families.
interesting_fact: Coaxial's first partnerships (Oct 2026) include backing up to 250 Australian female founders through VC firm Antler, plus Cape York Partnership and SNAICC; reported as the largest single philanthropic donation by a living person in Australia.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up on a sheep, cattle and wheat farm at Spicers Creek, NSW, attending a one-room, one-teacher school; before marrying she was a private cook and secretary in Sydney and the UK, and in the late 1980s cooked in a pub in Kynuna, outback Queensland.
notes: Best route is Coaxial (CEO Philippa Watson). Separated from Andrew Forrest in 2023; avoid the topic. Energy angle via Fortescue's green-energy pivot, though she is not operational there.

name: John Franklyn Mars
current_role: Retired chair, president & CEO of Mars, Inc.; Mars family co-owner (born 1935)
profile: Son of Forrest Mars Sr. and grandson of founder Frank C. Mars, John Mars (b. Oct 1935, Arlington, VA; Hotchkiss and Yale) co-led the family's privately held candy-to-petcare giant for decades as the third generation in charge. He remains one of the main family owners of Mars (M&M's, Snickers, Royal Canin, VCA, Banfield and, since 2025, Kellanova); Bloomberg put his fortune at ~$44.6B in 2025.
interesting_fact: Famously camera-shy: from 2010 to 2014 he was the highest-ranked person in the Forbes wealth rankings whose photograph the magazine could not obtain.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Adrienne (Mount Vernon's Vice Regent Emerita for Wyoming) pledged $10M to the endowment of George Washington's Mount Vernon; the estate's top job is now the 'John and Adrienne Mars President & CEO' position.

public_contacts.value: kelly.frailey@effem.com (Mars corporate press contact on 2026 Mars Impact Fund release)

notes: Extremely private; aged 91, lives in Wyoming per Forbes. No personal channels. Only route is Mars corporate communications (press contacts on Mars releases use effem.com addresses). Wikipedia still calls him chairman, but Mount Vernon (2021) calls him retired chair/president/CEO.

name: Chen Jianhua
current_role: Chairman, Hengli Group (恒力集团), Suzhou; also chairman of Hengli Heavy Industry (shipbuilding)
profile: Chen Jianhua (陈建华), born 1971 in Wujiang, Suzhou, left school at 13, traded waste silk, and in 1994 with his wife Fan Hongwei bought a near-bankrupt township weaving mill that became Hengli Group, now a Fortune Global 500 textiles-to-petrochemicals giant with a huge refinery on Dalian's Changxing Island. Since 2022 he has expanded into shipbuilding via Hengli Heavy Industry.
interesting_fact: In 2022 he paid 1.729B yuan for a Dalian shipyard once owned by Korea's STX that had sat idle for nine years through 10+ failed auctions; within about three years it became the world's largest single shipyard by orderbook.
deep_cut_fact: The mill he bought for 3.69M yuan in 1994 in his home town of Nanma had just 27 employees and 104 silk looms. During the Asian financial crisis he coined a now-famous maxim: companies can 'winter like a cat' (lie low, ready to pounce) but must never 'winter like a snake' (go dormant).
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Wife Fan Hongwei chairs listed Hengli Petrochemical, so investor-relations route goes via that company. Hurun 2026 ranks the couple 6th in China (302B yuan).

name: Ernest Garcia II
current_role: Owner and Chairman, DriveTime Automotive Group; largest shareholder of Carvana (NYSE: CVNA)
profile: Ernest Garcia II (b. 1957) built DriveTime, one of the biggest US used-car retailers and lenders to subprime buyers, out of a bankrupt rental franchise. His son Ernie Garcia III founded Carvana inside DriveTime and spun it out, IPO'ing it in 2017. Garcia II remains Carvana's largest shareholder, and its rebound has made him one of America's richest people.
interesting_fact: He is the son of a liquor-store owner who was for a time mayor of Gallup, New Mexico. He played on the University of Arizona golf team, then dropped out to become a stockbroker before moving into Phoenix real estate.
deep_cut_fact: In 1991 he bought Ugly Duckling, a bankrupt rent-a-car franchise, for under $1 million and merged it with his small finance company. He took it public on Nasdaq in 1996 under the ticker 'UGLY', then took it private in 2002 and renamed it DriveTime.
notes: Extremely low public profile: he gives almost no interviews and has no social media. Carvana's contacts reach the company, not him directly. His 1990 Lincoln Savings guilty plea is widely reported, so avoid it in outreach. His son, Carvana CEO Ernie Garcia III, is the more accessible family member for a podcast.

name: Susanne Klatten
current_role: Owner and deputy chair of the supervisory board, ALTANA AG; BMW supervisory board member; managing director of her investment firm SKion GmbH
profile: Germany's richest woman (b. 1962, Bad Homburg), daughter of Herbert and Johanna Quandt. She owns ~19% of BMW and 100% of specialty-chemicals group ALTANA, which she helped transform from her grandfather's pharma business; via SKion she invests in industrial tech (e.g. SGL Carbon, water tech) and backs startups through UnternehmerTUM.
interesting_fact: She founded UnternehmerTUM at the Technical University of Munich in 2002, now billed as Germany's leading centre for business creation and startups; TUM made her an Honorary Senator in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job (1981-83) was at the advertising agency Young & Rubicam in Frankfurt; she later did an MBA at IMD Lausanne specialising in advertising, worked at Dresdner Bank in London and McKinsey in Munich, and often worked under the name 'Susanne Kant'. Buckingham made her an honorary graduate in 2022.
notes: Famously private; rarely gives interviews. SKion GmbH (Bad Homburg) is her personal investment company - info@skion.de is the published Impressum address. Avoid personal/family topics. Energy angle: past large stake in wind-turbine maker Nordex; SGL Carbon (carbon/graphite).

name: Diane Hendricks
current_role: Co-founder and owner, ABC Supply Co. (Beloit, Wisconsin). Hendricks Holding says she stepped down as chairman of ABC Supply and Hendricks Holding in 2024; Forbes still calls her chair.
profile: Grew up one of nine sisters on a Wisconsin dairy farm and sold custom homes before co-founding ABC Supply with her roofer husband Ken in 1982. After his death in 2007 she led it to its two biggest deals (Bradco 2010, L&W Supply 2016). ABC is now North America's largest roofing distributor, with 900+ branches and $20.2B revenue in 2025. Forbes ranks her among America's richest self-made women.
interesting_fact: Her revitalisation of Beloit, Wisconsin, including whole rebuilt downtown blocks, a riverwalk, ABC Supply Stadium and the Ironworks campus, was the subject of the 2025 A&E series 'Betting on Beloit'.
deep_cut_fact: In 2001 she and Ken bought Beloit's abandoned 800,000 sq ft foundry, which for 150 years had built paper-making machines the size of football fields. They turned it into the Ironworks campus, which in 2016 gained Irontek, a startup coworking hub that has since expanded to Delafield, Wisconsin, and Boise, Idaho.

public_contacts.value: bvollmer@hiebing.com (Becca Vollmer, Hiebing - ABC Supply media contact)

notes: ABC Supply's media center lists agency contact Becca Vollmer (Hiebing) for interview requests. Hendricks Holding is the family holding company (merged with DMHE in 2025). She is a prominent Republican donor, so a podcast pitch about entrepreneurship and small-town revival would be the natural angle. Her role descriptions conflict between Forbes and the company site; check before addressing her as chairman.

name: Lei Jun
current_role: Co-founder, chairman and CEO, Xiaomi Corporation (HKEX: 1810); chairman, Kingsoft and Shunwei Capital
profile: Wuhan University computer-science graduate who joined Kingsoft as an engineer in 1992, became its CEO and took it public in 2007, and sold Joyo.com to Amazon in 2004. He co-founded Xiaomi in 2010, building it into a top-3 global smartphone maker, and in 2021 bet on EVs as his 'last major startup'; the Xiaomi SU7 and YU7 have become hit products.
interesting_fact: Lei's first big win was selling online retailer Joyo.com to Amazon in 2004 for $75 million; Joyo became Amazon China.
deep_cut_fact: His philanthropy began with a ¥140,000 gift to his alma mater Wuhan University in 1997; in 2023 he gave the university ¥1.3 billion, at the time the largest individual donation it had ever received.

public_contacts.value: xiaomi@hkstrategies.com (Hill & Knowlton, Xiaomi results-event press contact)

notes: Highly public and social-media active (Weibo, X, Douyin; viral 'Are you OK?' meme). Hill & Knowlton address seen via search index of ir.mi.com (page blocked to direct fetch) — re-verify before use. Also an NPC deputy since 2013.

name: Vicky Safra
current_role: Principal heir/shareholder of J. Safra Group (J. Safra Sarasin, Banco Safra, Safra National Bank of New York); heads the family's philanthropic foundation
profile: Greek-born widow of banker Joseph Safra (d. 2020), she and her children inherited the J. Safra Group banking empire; sons Jacob (Switzerland/NY, real estate) and David (Banco Safra, Brazil) run operations. The group completed buying a majority of Denmark's Saxo Bank in March 2026 and in July 2026 agreed to buy the rest. She lives mostly in Switzerland and keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: She is often called the richest Greek woman in the world, yet is almost unknown in Greece; she met Joseph Safra at 17 in São Paulo and they were together for some 50 years.
deep_cut_fact: Born Vicky Sarfati in Thessaloniki, she emigrated to Brazil with her family in the 1950s but kept her Greek citizenship, still speaks Greek and occasionally visits Greece.
notes: Extremely private; no interviews or social accounts. Media address is the bank group's, not hers. Avoid the family inheritance litigation (Alberto Safra) in outreach. Birthplace: most sources say Thessaloniki; one Wikipedia citation says Athens.

name: Jerry Jones
current_role: Owner, President & General Manager, Dallas Cowboys; controlling shareholder of Comstock Resources
profile: Co-captain of Arkansas's 1964 national-title team, Jones made his first fortune as an oil and gas wildcatter before buying the Dallas Cowboys for $150M in 1989 (now worth ~$13B, the NFL's most valuable team since 2018). He remains an active energy investor as controlling holder of Haynesville natural-gas producer Comstock Resources, plus Dallas real estate.
interesting_fact: Jones started working at age 9 as a customer greeter at his parents' grocery store, Pat's Supermarket, in North Little Rock.
deep_cut_fact: In 1971 he and his wife carved 400 acres out of their 5,500-acre Buena Vista Ranch in the Missouri Ozarks to open Buena Vista Animal Paradise, a drive-through exotic animal park that survives today as Wild Animal Safari in Strafford, Missouri.

public_contacts.value: rmills@comstockresources.com (Ron Mills, VP Finance & IR, Comstock Resources)

notes: Energy angle is strong: Comstock (Frisco, TX) is a major Haynesville gas producer; Jones has injected equity into it. Comstock IR email appears in its press releases (2022-2026); the release page was access-blocked to me, confirmed via search snippets. Cowboys media relations is the other route.

name: Forrest Mars, Jr.
current_role: Deceased (died July 26, 2016, Seattle, aged 84); former co-president of Mars Inc. (1975-1999)
notes: Died 26 July 2016 per Mars Inc. press release ('Forrest E. Mars, Jr., Businessman and Philanthropist, Passes Away at 84') https://www.mars.com/news-and-stories/press-releases/forrest-e-mars-jr and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forrest_Mars_Jr. His stake passed to his daughters (incl. Valerie Mars, also in this lane).

name: Henry Nicholas III
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Broadcom; founder of the Henry T. Nicholas, III Foundation and backer of Marsy's Law for All
profile: Electrical engineer (UCLA BS/MS/PhD) who worked at TRW and PairGain before cofounding fabless chipmaker Broadcom with Henry Samueli in 1991. He took it public in 1998 and stepped down as CEO in 2003; Broadcom's later merger with Avago drives his wealth. He now focuses on crime-victims' rights via Marsy's Law, named for his sister, and on education philanthropy.
interesting_fact: A music enthusiast, Nicholas has said his inspiration for Broadcom came from Pink Floyd lyrics; Broadcom itself was started in 1991 in a spare bedroom of his Redondo Beach home.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he co-founded the Nicholas Academic Centers with retired Orange County Superior Court Judge Jack K. Mandel to give academic support to under-resourced Santa Ana high schoolers; he has given $57.7M and the centers have graduated 2,070 students, nearly all going on to post-secondary education.

public_contacts.value: Ted Varipatis, Serra Public Affairs - ted@serrapublicaffairs.com (press contact listed for Marsy's Law campaign)

notes: Has had widely reported legal/drug issues (2008 indictment later dismissed; 2019 Las Vegas case) - avoid. Best route is via the Marsy's Law for All organisation / its PR firm; the press contact found is on the Maine campaign page. His PhD (UCLA) was awarded in 1998.

name: Andrey Melnichenko
current_role: Founder of EuroChem (fertilizers) and SUEK (coal); left both boards in March 2022 and stepped back as beneficiary after sanctions
profile: Belarus-born Russian industrialist who started with a campus currency-exchange booth, co-founded MDM Bank at 21 (1993), then built fertilizer giant EuroChem and coal/energy company SUEK through MDM Group. Sanctioned by EU/UK/US in 2022, which he disputes; his wife became trust beneficiary of the stakes. Holds UAE citizenship since 2021.
interesting_fact: His Philippe Starck-designed Sailing Yacht A, the world's largest sail-assisted yacht, was frozen by Italian authorities in Trieste in 2022; he also collects Impressionist art including Monet.
deep_cut_fact: Studied physics at Moscow State University. At 14 he was evacuated after Chernobyl; he later called that his 'freest and most interesting summer' and wrote in The Economist (2026) it taught him 'a complex system containing enormous amounts of energy does not forgive miscalculation or arrogance.'
notes: Sanctioned by EU, UK and US (2022) - check legal/compliance before any engagement. Best route is the Andrey Melnichenko Foundation media inbox (foundation also runs the Mendeleev Chemistry Olympiad support). Has written essays for The Economist on energy/civilisation, so is open to long-form media.

name: Wang Chuanfu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, BYD Company Ltd.
profile: Chemist-turned-entrepreneur born 1966 in Wuwei, Anhui, who founded BYD in Shenzhen in 1995 as a rechargeable-battery maker. BYD entered autos in 2003 and is now the world's largest plug-in/EV maker, also making batteries (FinDreams/Blade), buses, energy storage and electronics; Berkshire Hathaway was an early investor (2008).
interesting_fact: Before BYD, Wang was general manager of a Shenzhen battery venture set up in 1993 by his Beijing research institute; he left in 1995 to found BYD at 29 with a CN¥250,000 loan from his cousin Lu Xiangyang.
deep_cut_fact: BYD's very first employee card, issued in 1995, belongs to Wang himself, bearing employee number 00001. He studied metallurgical physical chemistry at Central South University (grad. 1987) and earned a master's at the Beijing Non-Ferrous Metal General Research Institute (now GRINM) in 1990.
notes: SEC insider match (Lion Group Holding LGHL chairman/CEO) appears to be a different person with a similar name; ignore it. BYD IR email db@byd.com is the board-secretary/IR mailbox listed on CNInfo (Shenzhen exchange). Wang rarely gives Western interviews.

name: Jason Chang CS
current_role: Chairman, ASE Technology Holding (Taiwan; world's largest chip packaging & testing group)
profile: Jason Chang Chien-sheng (b. 1944, Shanghai; family from Wenzhou) cofounded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his brother Richard and built it into the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, now ASE Technology Holding (NYSE: ASX), a key player in advanced packaging for AI chips. He holds Singapore citizenship.
interesting_fact: Educated at National Taiwan University (BS) and the Illinois Institute of Technology (MS) before building ASE; Hurun lists him under China but he is Taiwanese-Singaporean.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2015 he received a SEMI Award recognising his 'significant achievements in the development and commercialization of copper wire in the IC assembly process' - an industry-wide switch from gold to copper bonding wire that ASE pushed early.
notes: Aged 82 and low-profile; skipped the June 2025 AGM. Hurun lists country as China but he is Taiwan-based with Singapore citizenship. Best route is ASE corporate PR/IR. corp_comms@aseglobal.com also published on the contact page.

name: Vinod Shantilal Adani
current_role: Dubai-based investor; runs a family investment office; part of the Adani Group promoter group (no formal executive title)
profile: Born 1949 in Gujarat, Vinod Adani is the elder brother of Gautam Adani. He started a textile business in Mumbai, traded commodities from Singapore from 1989 and has lived in Dubai since 1994, where he runs a family investment office. He is a Cypriot citizen, and the Adani Group lists him as a member of its promoter group.
interesting_fact: The IIFL Wealth Hurun India Rich List 2022 named him the richest NRI (non-resident Indian) and the sixth-richest Indian overall.
deep_cut_fact: He started out on his own long before Dubai. In 1976 he founded a textile business, VR Textile, in Mumbai, then moved to Singapore in 1989 to trade commodities.
notes: Very private: he keeps a low profile and has no public website or social accounts. He is central to the 2023 Hindenburg allegations and earlier DRI probes, so outreach is sensitive. If attempted at all, the realistic route is the Adani Group corporate communications office. Net-worth figures vary widely by source.

name: Dang Yanbao
current_role: Chairman, Ningxia Baofeng Energy Group (Shanghai-listed coal-to-chemicals/olefins producer); controlling holder of Baofeng Energy Storage
profile: Born 1973, Dang worked in building materials, trading and investment before founding Baofeng Energy in Ningxia in 2005, turning coal into olefins and other chemicals. In 2025 Baofeng started a $6.7B Inner Mongolia olefins plant, lifting capacity to 5.2M t/yr; a sister firm began trial output at a 100GWh battery/storage plant in Yinchuan in 2024.
interesting_fact: Baofeng's Inner Mongolia coal-to-olefins complex, which started up in 2025 at a cost of about $6.7 billion, is among the largest olefins plants in the world, raising company capacity to 5.2 million tons a year.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Yanchi County, Ningxia, and in 2011 he and his wife set up the Ningxia Yanbao Charity Foundation for education and poverty relief; by 2021 it had financially helped about 256,700 young students (he gave RMB 302M to it in 2019).
notes: IR email is the board-secretary/securities affairs contact listed in Baofeng Energy's 2025 interim report summary (China Securities Journal). Chinese-language outreach recommended; low international media profile.

name: Philip Anschutz
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, The Anschutz Corporation (Denver); owner of Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG)
profile: Kansas-born Denver billionaire who built fortunes in oil (from 1960s Wyoming wildcatting), railroads (Southern Pacific), telecom (Qwest), real estate and entertainment. Through AEG he owns 70+ arenas/venues, the LA Kings and a Galaxy stake; his Power Company of Wyoming is developing the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre wind project with the TransWest Express transmission line.
interesting_fact: On 320,000 acres of his Wyoming ranch land he is building one of the world's biggest wind farms (Chokecherry and Sierra Madre, ~3 GW), paired with a transmission line to carry the power to the Southwest.
deep_cut_fact: His early oil career was saved by Hollywood: when his Wyoming well near Gillette caught fire in the late 1960s, he sold Universal Studios exclusive rights to film the blaze for its John Wayne/Red Adair movie 'Hellfighters' for $100,000, which paid Adair to put it out.

public_contacts.value: mroth@aegworldwide.com (Michael Roth, AEG VP Communications, per Jan 2025 release)

notes: Famously private; has given almost no interviews in decades. The Anschutz Corporation publishes no press contact; AEG communications is the only published route. Energy angle: Chokecherry/Sierra Madre wind + TransWest Express line. Kool-Aid stand anecdote (age 6) in Forbes bio.

name: Huang Shilin
current_role: Co-founder and ~9-10% shareholder of CATL (left vice-chair/board in Aug 2022); reported chairman of Contemporary Nebula Technology Energy (CNTE, Fujian)
profile: Huang Shilin (b. 1967) co-founded battery giant CATL with Robin Zeng and was its vice chairman until resigning in August 2022 to pursue solar-storage, charging and inspection businesses. He remains CATL's third-largest shareholder (~10% before a ~1% block sale in Nov 2025) and is linked to CNTE, a CATL-affiliated energy-storage/charging-station maker in Fuzhou.
interesting_fact: When he quit CATL in 2022, the company said he would explore solar, energy storage, charging and inspection businesses and might form 'strategic synergy' with CATL in future; CATL holds ~20% of CNTE, the storage/charging firm he chairs.
deep_cut_fact: He and CATL chairman Robin Zeng (Zeng Yuqun) were high-school classmates; a Hefei University of Technology graduate, Huang was R&D director at Dongguan ATL (Amperex) and Ningde ATL before co-founding CATL.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal accounts found. The listed email is CNTE's general company inbox (not personal). CATL's English contact page blocks scripted access; CATL IR via catl.com investor pages.

name: Harold Hamm
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Continental Resources (private since 2022); founder of the Hamm Institute for American Energy at Oklahoma State University
profile: Oklahoma sharecroppers' son who turned a water-hauling trucking business into Continental Resources, pioneering horizontal drilling and fracking in North Dakota's Bakken. He took Continental private in a 2022 buyout. Now focuses on energy policy and the Hamm Institute, which in 2026 got Google.org funding for research on reliable power for AI.
interesting_fact: Hamm was the 13th and youngest child of Oklahoma cotton sharecroppers. In 2012 Time named him one of the world's 100 most influential people, and he was Mitt Romney's energy adviser that year.
deep_cut_fact: Hamm started work at 16 at a gas station, then mucked out oil tanks at a refinery. He founded his first company, Shelly Dean Oil Co. (later Continental), in 1967, and went back to finish college at Phillips University in Enid only after he struck oil.
notes: Strong fit: the Hamm Institute now does research on powering AI/data centers. The press email (Kristin Thomas, Continental's SVP/Chief Communications Officer) comes from a 2018 release, so check it is still current. Politically prominent (major Trump fundraiser); 2026 reports linked him to an oil trade-association role and interest in a U.S. Senate seat.

name: Jason Chang
current_role: Chairman (and CEO per company releases), ASE Technology Holding Co. (TWSE: 3711, NYSE: ASX)
profile: Taiwan-born, Singapore-based co-founder of ASE, the world's largest outsourced semiconductor assembly and test (OSAT) provider, which he started with brother Richard in 1984. ASE (incl. SPIL and USI) is a key advanced-packaging/heterogeneous-integration supplier for AI chips. The brothers also invest in real estate developer Sino Horizon.
interesting_fact: He founded ASE in 1984 betting early that the rise of the fabless model would let Taiwan become a global IC manufacturing hub; the company lacked technology and resources in its early years but he kept investing heavily in advanced packaging R&D.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as an engineer: electronics engineering degree from National Taiwan University and an M.S. in industrial engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology; National Cheng Kung University gave him an honorary doctorate in July 2022 (ASE and NCKU have collaborated on packaging R&D since 2012).
notes: Low public profile; route via ASE corporate PR/IR. Avoid succession topics (his son Rutherford, a presumed successor, died recently).

name: Edwin Chen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Surge AI
profile: Edwin Chen founded Surge AI in 2020 to supply high-quality human data, RL environments and evals for training frontier AI models. Bootstrapped with no outside funding, Surge passed $1B+ revenue in 2024 with under ~100 staff (customers include Google and Anthropic); Chen owns an estimated ~75%. Earlier he was a data/research scientist at Twitter, Google and Facebook.
interesting_fact: At MIT, where he studied math, computer science and linguistics, Chen researched how to decode the Inca khipu, a 'language' recorded via knots tied in rope.
deep_cut_fact: As a Twitter data scientist in 2012, Chen mapped geotagged tweets to show where Americans say 'soda', 'pop' or 'coke' (soda on the coasts, pop in the Midwest, coke in the South); the post on his personal blog went viral via Bloomberg, Gizmodo and FlowingData.
notes: Does long-form podcasts (Lenny's Podcast Dec 2025, 20VC, No Priors) — receptive to podcast format. Strong views on AI benchmarks, RL environments and anti-'blitzscale' company building; press@surgehq.ai is the published press route.

name: Khalif bin zayed an Nahyas
profile: Listed name matches Sheikh Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the UAE and Ruler of Abu Dhabi (2004-2022), who died on 13 May 2022. Record skipped per instructions.
notes: Died 13 May 2022 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khalifa_bin_Zayed_Al_Nahyan). Caveat: the listed 'S B K Holdings' (SBK Holding) is the private holding company of his eldest son Sheikh Sultan bin Khalifa Al Nahyan (https://sbkholding.com), so the Hurun 2014 entry may conflate father and son. If the journalist wants the living SBK owner, research Sultan bin Khalifa separately.

name: Khalifa bin Zayed Al Nahyan
profile: Former President of the UAE and Ruler of Abu Dhabi (2004-2022). Died 13 May 2022, aged 73; succeeded by his half-brother Mohamed bin Zayed.
notes: Deceased 13 May 2022 (source: https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/uaes-long-ailing-leader-sheikh-khalifa-bin-zayed-has-died). Not a viable podcast guest.

name: Paolo Rocca
current_role: Chairman of Techint Group and Chairman of Tenaris (stepped down as Tenaris CEO in May 2026, succeeded by Gabriel Podskubka).
profile: Milan-born (1952) grandson of Techint founder Agostino Rocca, Paolo Rocca runs the Italo-Argentine Techint conglomerate (Tenaris seamless steel pipes for oil & gas, Ternium steel, engineering). As CEO from 2002 he merged mills in Argentina, Italy, Mexico and Japan into the NYSE-listed Tenaris brand. Wealth is shared with his brother Gianfelice Rocca.
interesting_fact: He took Tenaris through more than two decades as CEO, unifying acquired pipe mills across several countries under a single global brand listed in New York; in 2013 Columbia Business School gave him its Deming Cup for operational excellence.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business, in the late 1970s he settled on a remote farm in Chubut, Patagonia, raising sheep and living austerely; he also worked as an executive assistant at the World Bank before formally entering Techint in 1985.

public_contacts.value: Tenaris Media Relations team contact (via Media resources page)

notes: Input name was just 'Paolo' (Techint, shared with Gianfelice Mario Rocca) = Paolo Rocca. Low public profile; best route is Tenaris/Techint media relations. Was indicted in Argentina's 2018 'cuadernos' graft case — avoid in outreach.

name: Kwong Siu-hing
current_role: Largest shareholder (via family trust) of Sun Hung Kai Properties; former SHKP chairman (2008–2011)
profile: Kwong Siu-hing (鄺肖卿, b. 1929) is the widow of Kwok Tak-seng, who co-founded Sun Hung Kai Properties in 1958 and died in 1990. Through a family trust she controls the largest stake in SHKP, one of Hong Kong's biggest property developers, and she is long ranked Hong Kong's richest woman. She chaired SHKP from 2008 to 2011; her son Raymond Kwok is now chairman.
interesting_fact: She left Guangdong for Hong Kong in 1947 and married Kwok Tak-seng at 20. Sun Hung Kai, which he started with Fung King-hey and Lee Shau Kee in 1958, went public in 1972 and became one of Hong Kong's largest developers.
deep_cut_fact: Her ancestral home is Huashan town in Hua County (now Huadu District, Guangzhou). According to the SCMP, before becoming SHKP chairwoman at 78 in 2008 she 'had never sat on the board of a Hong Kong company'.
notes: She is about 96 and entirely private, with no public role or interviews; she is not a realistic podcast guest. Any approach would go through SHKP corporate communications. Avoid family-feud topics.

name: Jaime Gilinski Bacal
current_role: Head of the Gilinski Group (Banco GNB Sudameris, Grupo Nutresa control stake, Panama Pacifico real estate); listed as Grupo Nutresa chairman since 2024
profile: Colombian banker and developer (Georgia Tech industrial engineering, Harvard MBA, ex-Morgan Stanley M&A) who built a Latin American banking empire through acquisitions, including Banco Andino and GNB Sudameris. In 2021–24 he won control of food giant Grupo Nutresa after a long takeover battle, and co-develops Panama Pacifico on a former US Air Force base.
interesting_fact: In the 1990s he bought the Colombian assets of collapsed BCCI for a nominal sum, rebuilt them as Banco Andino, and sold it about four years later for a reported $70 million.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he spent nine years building consumer-products and snack-food businesses in South America; the family group still owns Yupi snacks. He sits on the International Advisory Board of Oxford's Blavatnik School of Government, and funds an HBS fellowship for Colombian and Panamanian MBA students.
notes: Lives primarily in Panama/London; private, rarely interviewed in English. No dedicated Gilinski Group press contact found. Nutresa control story is contentious in Colombia (rivalry with GEA) — avoid. Fellowship HBS detail from Wikipedia.

name: Enrique Razon Jr.
current_role: Chairman and President, International Container Terminal Services Inc. (ICTSI); chairman of Bloomberry Resorts (Solaire) and Prime Infrastructure Capital (Prime Infra)
profile: Ricky Razon turned the Manila port business his grandfather started in 1916 into ICTSI, a global terminal operator on five continents. He also built the Solaire casino resorts and, via Prime Infra, moved into utilities and energy: Manila Water, the Malampaya gas field, gas plants bought from the Lopez Group in 2025 and big solar-plus-battery projects.
interesting_fact: Razon left school at 17 to take a minimum-wage job in the family's cargo-loading business and worked his way up through the ranks.
deep_cut_fact: Associates describe him as a former junior golfer whose real handicap is closer to two than the six he claims; he set up the Philippine Golf Tour Foundation, and one of his favourite sports is kiteboarding.

public_contacts.value: https://ictsi.com/contact (routes General / Investor Relations / CSR inquiries)

notes: Rarely grants interviews. Energy angle is strong (Prime Infra: Malampaya gas, gas plants, MTerra Solar solar+storage). investor@ictsi.com and info@ictsi.com appear as routing addresses in ICTSI's contact form source; foundation@ictsi.com is for ICTSI Foundation/CSR.

name: Mikhail Fridman
current_role: Co-founder of Alfa Group; shareholder (no board role) in Luxembourg-based investment group LetterOne
profile: Lviv-born co-founder of Alfa Group (Alfa-Bank, Alfa-Eco) who made his fortune in banking, telecom and oil, including the TNK-BP venture sold for $14bn in 2013. Sanctioned after Russia's 2022 invasion of Ukraine, he stepped back from LetterOne, sold his Alfa-Bank stake in 2025 and has spent 2025-26 fighting EU sanctions and seeking compensation for frozen assets.
interesting_fact: He lived in Western Ukraine until he was 17 and has called Lviv, where his parents lived, his 'favorite city'; in 2011 he founded the Alfa Jazz Fest there.
deep_cut_fact: As a student at the Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys he washed windows and co-founded a student discotheque called 'Strawberry Fields', and organised students to queue for theatre tickets used to barter for scarce goods.
notes: Highly sensitive subject: sanctioned (UK; EU status contested/partly lifted in 2026 per reports), on Ukraine's wanted list, litigation against several states. No published personal/office contact found; he no longer has a formal LetterOne role. Reputational risk for outreach.

name: Murali Divi
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Divi's Laboratories Ltd (Hyderabad)
profile: Pharmaceutical scientist (PhD, Kakatiya University) who worked at US specialty-chemical firms before founding Divi's Research Centre in 1990, which became Divi's Laboratories, now one of the world's top three makers of active pharmaceutical ingredients, with ~90% of revenue from exports. Divi's is now investing in peptides, including GLP-1 ingredients.
interesting_fact: A fitness fanatic, he built a yoga center at Divi's headquarters in Hyderabad and spends weekends at his organic farm near the city.
deep_cut_fact: His first career step was as a trainee at Warner Hindustan in 1975; before starting Divi's he partnered with Dr. Kallam Anji Reddy (later Dr. Reddy's founder) to acquire Cheminor Drugs in 1984.
notes: Low-profile, rarely gives interviews. Company general inbox is the only published route.

name: George R. Roberts
current_role: Co-Executive Chairman and co-founder, KKR & Co. Inc. (Menlo Park/San Francisco)
profile: Houston-born George Roberts co-founded leveraged-buyout pioneer Kohlberg Kravis Roberts in 1976 with his cousin Henry Kravis and Jerome Kohlberg, after the trio's 'bootstrap' deals at Bear Stearns, where he made partner at 29. He and Kravis handed the CEO roles to Joe Bae and Scott Nuttall in 2021 and remain co-executive chairmen; KKR is now a major infrastructure and data-center investor.
interesting_fact: He founded and chairs REDF (Roberts Enterprise Development Fund), a pioneer of 'employment social enterprise' that funds businesses hiring people facing major barriers to work; he has also given $190M to Claremont McKenna ($50M in 2012, $140M in 2022).
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Culver Military Academy in Indiana in 1962 and the school named him its 'Man of the Year' in 1998; he still serves as a Culver trustee.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews (Kravis is the public face). Best route is KKR media relations. Data-center/energy angle: KKR is a big investor in digital infrastructure and energy transition.

name: Sarath Ratanavadi
current_role: Founder and CEO, Gulf Development PCL (Thailand)
profile: Thai engineer often called Thailand's 'energy king' and its richest person. He founded Gulf Electric in 1994 during power-sector liberalisation, grew Gulf Energy Development into a major IPP, took it public in 2017 and in 2025 merged it with telecom holding Intouch (AIS) to form Gulf Development, spanning power, telecom, data centers (JV with Singtel) and a Kasikornbank stake.
interesting_fact: Gulf Energy's 2017 IPO raised over 25 billion baht, Thailand's biggest IPO in a decade; Gulf later co-launched a crypto exchange in Thailand with Binance.
deep_cut_fact: A keen golfer and former managing director of the Thailand Golf Championship, he opened Stonehill, a 340+ acre private golf club outside Bangkok designed by architect Kyle Phillips, in 2022.
notes: Born 1965 Bangkok; Chulalongkorn civil engineering, USC MS engineering management. Data-center angle via Gulf's JV with Singtel (GSA). Avoid USC donation/admissions topic. Best route: Gulf corporate contact/IR.

name: Dhanin Chearavanont
current_role: Senior Chairman, Charoen Pokphand (CP) Group, Thailand
profile: Dhanin (b. 1939; Chinese name Xie Guomin) is the youngest son of CP founder Chia Ek Chor. Over 48 years as chairman/CEO he built Charoen Pokphand into a giant in feed and livestock, retail (7-Eleven Thailand, Lotus's) and telecom (True), with stakes in Ping An and CITIC. He handed over the chairman and CEO roles in 2017 and is now senior chairman.
interesting_fact: CP's True Corp has partnered with BlackRock on a $1B data-centre venture in Thailand and won one of three Thai digital-bank licences in 2025, an unusual pivot for a group built on chicken feed.
deep_cut_fact: In 1979, as China passed its first joint-venture law, CP brought $15M into the country and secured the No. '0001' Sino-foreign joint-venture business licences in Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Shantou, making it one of the very first foreign investors of the reform era.
notes: Aged 87 and a senior/honorary figure; the next generation now runs the group day to day. He studied at Shantou No.1 High School (1952) and has written a memoir (reviewed in English as 'Success Is Delighted for Only One Day'). For a data-centre angle, True Corp management may be more accessible. I found no published personal or press email.

name: Josh Kushner
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Thrive Capital; co-founder, Oscar Health
profile: Josh Kushner founded Thrive Capital in 2009 and built it into a top VC firm, with early or large bets on Instagram, Spotify, Stripe and OpenAI. Thrive closed its $10B+ tenth fund (Thrive X) in Feb 2026 and manages over $65B. He co-founded insurer Oscar Health, owns about 66% of Thrive, and in Aug 2026 agreed with Bob Iger to buy the LA Lakers for $12.5B.
interesting_fact: He announced Thrive X himself on X: more than $10B, split into $1B for early-stage and $9B for growth investments. That makes AI-heavy Thrive one of the largest single-fund venture managers.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup was Vostu. In the spring of his junior year at Harvard he pooled $10,000 with two graduate students, including future Oscar co-founder Mario Schlosser, to start it. It grew into Latin America's largest social-games developer, with 35M+ users on Orkut and Facebook.
notes: Private about personal matters but posts firm news on X. Thrive's site has no published press email. Highly relevant to AI/data-center theme (large OpenAI backer). Avoid family/political framing.

name: William Erbey
current_role: Chairman (and reported CEO), Altisource Asset Management Corp (AAMC), U.S. Virgin Islands
profile: William C. Erbey founded mortgage servicer Ocwen Financial (now Onity) in the late 1980s and built it and its spin-offs (Altisource, AAMC and others) into a multibillion-dollar group based in St. Croix, USVI. He left Ocwen in 2015. He now chairs AAMC, which is licensing patents for an EV efficiency control system.
interesting_fact: AAMC, Erbey's current vehicle, has pivoted from mortgage-related assets toward developing and licensing patents for a control system that aims to raise electric-vehicle efficiency.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Ocwen, Erbey studied economics at Allegheny College, earned an MBA with distinction from Harvard Business School, and worked in GE Capital and GE Mortgage Insurance.
notes: No longer on Forbes lists (former billionaire). Left Ocwen in Jan 2015 under a New York DFS settlement, and AAMC is in ongoing litigation with BlackRock/PIMCO, so handle carefully. AAMC press releases list Charles Frischer as contact. The EV control-system angle is the most podcast-relevant hook. The deep-cut source is a semi-promotional profile.

name: Peter Mallouk
current_role: President and CEO, Creative Planning (Overland Park, Kansas)
profile: Kansas City native Peter Mallouk (KU undergrad, MBA and law degrees) joined Creative Planning as an estate planner in 1998 and bought it in 2004 with under $100m in assets. He built it into one of the largest US RIAs, helped by deals for a Goldman Sachs wealth unit (2023) and SageView (2025), and bought a majority stake in Sporting Kansas City in 2025.
interesting_fact: He co-authored the #1 bestseller 'Unshakeable: Your Financial Freedom Playbook' (2017) with Tony Robbins, and hosts Creative Planning podcasts including 'Down the Middle' and 'Icons and Ideas'.
deep_cut_fact: Barron's ranked him No. 1 on its Top 100 Independent Financial Advisors list three years running (2013-2015), and in 2025 he was named Henry W. Bloch Kansas City Entrepreneur of the Year and inducted into the Bloch Entrepreneurship Hall of Fame.
notes: Forbes bio's '$700 million in assets' figure is clearly a typo (firm is in the hundreds of billions). Very media-friendly: regular on CNBC/Fox Business and hosts his own podcasts, so a podcast invitation is a natural fit.

name: Wang Tao
current_role: Founder & CEO, DJI (SZ DJI Technology), Shenzhen
profile: Wang Tao (Frank Wang, b. 1980, Hangzhou) built helicopter flight controllers in his HKUST dorm and founded DJI in Shenzhen in 2006, backed by his professor Li Zexiang. DJI grew from selling flight-control components to dominating the global consumer and commercial drone market, later expanding into gimbals, action cameras and e-bike/automotive systems.
interesting_fact: Rejected by MIT and Stanford, Wang got into HKUST; in early 2006 he posted his working flight-control system on a model-aircraft forum offering it for 50,000 yuan and was surprised buyers paid - the seed of DJI.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 Wang's HKUST team won third prize at the Asia-Pacific ABU Robocon contest; in 2019 he and mentor Li Zexiang jointly received the IEEE Robotics and Automation Award. His 2011 HKUST MPhil thesis was 'Control systems for autonomous helicopters'.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews. Regional PR inboxes also listed (pr.us@dji.com etc.). DJI is on US Commerce Entity List / Treasury lists - sensitive topic for a US podcast.

name: Ludwig Merckle
current_role: Head of the Merckle family group (Blaubeuren); ~28% shareholder and supervisory board member, Heidelberg Materials; supervisory board chair, Kässbohrer Geländefahrzeug AG
profile: Ludwig Merckle (b. 1965) leads the Merckle family holdings, which he took over in 2009 and restructured by refinancing debt and selling Ratiopharm and part of the Heidelberg stake. He owns about 28% of Heidelberg Materials, co-owns drug wholesaler Phoenix Pharma, owns PistenBully snowcat maker Kässbohrer and forestry firm Blauwald, and co-owns Zollern.
interesting_fact: He owns Kässbohrer, maker of the PistenBully snow groomers, and is co-owner of Zollern (bearings, gears, winches, motors); a naturalist by hobby, he also owns forestry company Blauwald.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Hamburg in 1965, he studied business informatics (Wirtschaftsinformatik) at the University of Mannheim. He has been named Family Entrepreneur of the Year twice (Handelsblatt 2011, INTES 2017) and received Baden-Württemberg's Economic Medal (Wirtschaftsmedaille) in 2022.
notes: Very private, rarely gives interviews. No published personal/office contact found. Energy/industrial angle: Heidelberg Materials' carbon-capture (CCS) cement projects. Avoid referencing father's death or 2008-09 debt crisis.

name: Edward Johnson IV
current_role: President, Pembroke Real Estate (FMR/Fidelity-affiliated global property investor)
profile: Edward 'Ned' Johnson IV is the grandson of Fidelity founder Edward Johnson II and brother of Fidelity CEO/chair Abigail Johnson, holding an estimated ~10% of parent FMR. He runs Pembroke, Fidelity's affiliated real-estate arm, overseeing development, operations and expansion of a portfolio spanning Boston, DC, San Francisco, London, Tokyo, Sydney and more.
interesting_fact: Pembroke spent about a decade transforming Boston's Seaport World Trade Center into Commonwealth Pier, a mixed-use harbor destination that now houses Fidelity offices and the Museum of American Finance.
deep_cut_fact: When construction on the Commonwealth Pier revitalisation (a 705,000 sq ft building on Massport land) began in October 2020, he called it the realisation of Pembroke's vision for a new Commonwealth Pier.
notes: Low-profile Fidelity heir; best route is via Pembroke's corporate contact page or Fidelity corporate communications.

name: Wang Wei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, S.F. Holding (SF Express), Shenzhen
profile: Wang Wei (王卫) founded SF Express in Shunde, Guangdong, in 1993 and built it into China's premium parcel carrier, relying on its own employees, aircraft fleet and vehicles rather than franchisees for same/next-day delivery. He took S.F. Holding public via a 2017 reverse merger in Shenzhen and added a Hong Kong listing in 2024; he remains chairman and majority owner.
interesting_fact: Unlike most Chinese couriers, SF runs its own airline, and Ezhou Huahu airport in Hubei - opened July 2022 and developed by SF Express with Hubei province - is touted as China's first cargo-focused airport and is SF Airlines' hub.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2016, after an SF courier was slapped by a driver in Beijing, Wang posted that if he didn't pursue it to the end he was 'no longer fit to be SF's president'; when S.F. Holding listed in Shenzhen in Feb 2017, that courier was invited to the bell-ringing ceremony.
notes: Famously media-shy; almost never gives interviews. Only route is via S.F. Holding IR/corporate communications (IR meeting request form available).

name: Laurene Powell Jobs
current_role: Founder & President, Emerson Collective; chair of The Atlantic; co-founder & chair, XQ Institute
profile: Laurene Powell Jobs inherited Apple and Disney shares from her late husband Steve Jobs and runs Emerson Collective, her impact-investing, philanthropy and advocacy firm focused on education, immigration, health and climate. She owns The Atlantic, holds a minority stake in Monumental Sports, and in Oct 2026 joined the boards of Skydance and Anonymous Content.
interesting_fact: In 2021 she launched the Waverley Street Foundation and committed $3 billion over a decade to climate-change groups, one of the largest private climate pledges.
deep_cut_fact: Before Stanford GSB she spent three years at Goldman Sachs as a fixed-income trading strategist. After her 1991 MBA she co-founded Terravera, a natural-foods company selling to Northern California retailers. In 1997 she co-founded College Track in East Palo Alto, years before Emerson Collective.
notes: Private, rarely gives interviews. Emerson Collective is the route; its climate work (Waverley Street Foundation) is the most relevant hook for an energy podcast.

name: Shahid Khan
current_role: Chairman & owner, Flex-N-Gate; owner, Jacksonville Jaguars (NFL) and Fulham FC; lead investor, All Elite Wrestling
profile: Pakistani-American engineer who came to the US at 16, bought his former employer Flex-N-Gate in 1980 and built it into a giant auto-parts supplier (~76 plants, 27,000+ staff). He owns the NFL's Jaguars (2012) and Fulham FC (2013), backs AEW wrestling with son Tony, and owns the Four Seasons Toronto, with a Jacksonville Four Seasons due Dec 2026.
interesting_fact: He arrived in the US at 16 with $500 and washed dishes at night while studying engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.
deep_cut_fact: He launched his first company, Bumper Works (1978), with a $50,000 SBA loan plus $16,000 of savings; by adopting Toyota's production system it became sole bumper supplier for Toyota pickups by 1987 - a case study in Womack & Jones's book 'Lean Thinking'.
notes: Goes by 'Shad'. Best routes are Flex-N-Gate corporate or Jaguars communications; no published personal email. Lean Thinking detail is from Wikipedia citing Womack & Jones (2003).

name: Ka-shing Li
current_role: Senior Advisor, CK Hutchison Holdings and CK Asset Holdings; Chairman, Li Ka Shing Foundation
profile: Sir Li Ka-shing (李嘉誠, b. 1928) left school at 15, founded a plastic-flower maker in 1950 and built Cheung Kong/Hutchison Whampoa into a global empire of ports, telecoms, retail, infrastructure and energy utilities. He retired as chairman in 2018 (son Victor Li succeeded) and is now senior advisor; Forbes ranked him 42nd in 2026 (~$47B).
interesting_fact: Through his venture firm Horizons Ventures he became an early backer of tech start-ups such as Spotify and Zoom (2015 Series C) - unusual for a property-and-ports tycoon then in his 80s.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 his Horizons Ventures backed Summly, the news-summarising app of 15-year-old Nick D'Aloisio, making him the world's youngest person to receive venture funding; Yahoo bought Summly in 2013. Li is also famously frugal, long wearing a cheap Citizen watch.
notes: Aged 98; rarely gives interviews now. Input name 'Ka-shing Li' = Li Ka-shing. Energy angle: CK group owns power utilities (Power Assets/HK Electric, CKI, UK Power Networks). Best route is the Li Ka Shing Foundation.

name: Uday Kotak
current_role: Founder and non-executive director, Kotak Mahindra Bank (stepped down as MD & CEO in Sept 2023)
profile: Mumbai financier who skipped the family cotton trade to start Kotak Capital Management Finance in 1985 with about Rs 30 lakh from family and friends, backed early by Anand Mahindra. It became Kotak Mahindra Bank in 2003, now a top Indian private lender. He stepped down as CEO in 2023, remains a director, and got the Padma Bhushan in 2026.
interesting_fact: The bank's Kotak811 digital-banking app is named after 8 November 2016, the night India's government withdrew 86% of rupee notes in circulation (demonetisation).
deep_cut_fact: His first deal came via a Jamnalal Bajaj (JBIMS) classmate who had joined Tata's Nelco: Kotak offered to discount Nelco's bills at 16%, cheaper than its banks, funded by friends and family lending to him at 12%, run from his family's office in the Navsari building in Mumbai's Fort area.
notes: Active on X with macro/policy commentary (savers-to-investors, India growth), which makes X a plausible route. Chaired IL&FS rescue board 2018-2022. Avoid RBI stake-dilution issues.

name: Anders Holch Povlsen
current_role: CEO & sole owner, BESTSELLER A/S; owner of Wildland Ltd (Scotland)
profile: Anders Holch Povlsen took over Bestseller, the Danish fashion group his parents founded with a single store in 1975, at age 28 and is now its sole owner (Jack&Jones, Only, Vero Moda among 11+ brands). He also holds major stakes in ASOS, online grocer Nemlig and Klarna, and is among Scotland's largest landowners through his rewilding company Wildland.
interesting_fact: He owns more than 1% of all the land in Scotland, plus a reserve in Romania's Carpathians set up to protect wolves, bears and lynx.
deep_cut_fact: His first Scottish purchase was the Glenfeshie estate in the Cairngorms (2006); he later bought land in the Borders specifically to trade with the Forestry Commission for 1,000 acres of woodland to add to it. Wildland frames the project as a 200-year vision for Highland restoration.
notes: Very private; rarely interviewed. Wildland's 'Marketing & Press' inbox is the most direct published route; Bestseller press goes via its Communication department (no email published). Avoid references to the family's 2019 personal tragedy. Sources differ on the first store town (Forbes: Ringkobing; Wikipedia: Brande).

name: Kenneth Thomson
profile: Kenneth Thomson, 2nd Baron Thomson of Fleet (1923-2006), Canadian chairman of the Thomson Corporation and art collector; died June 12, 2006 in Toronto. Skipped per instructions.
notes: Deceased (June 12, 2006) - source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kenneth_Thomson,_2nd_Baron_Thomson_of_Fleet. Fortune now held by the family via Woodbridge Co.; son David Thomson chairs Thomson Reuters.

name: Wang Wei
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, S.F. Holding (SF Express), Shenzhen
profile: Wang Wei (王卫, 'Dick Wang'), born 1970/71 in Shanghai and raised in Hong Kong from age 7, skipped university and in 1993 founded SF Express to rush samples between Shunde factories and Hong Kong buyers. It became China's premium courier with ~400,000 staff and its own cargo airline; SF Holding is listed in Shenzhen (2017) and Hong Kong (2024), and he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He started SF in a Mong Kok shop with about US$13,000 borrowed from his father, six drivers (himself among them) and a single van; he declined all media interviews until 2011.
deep_cut_fact: When a Beijing driver slapped an SF courier after a minor collision in April 2016, Wang publicly vowed to pursue the case, saying he would not deserve to be chairman if he let it pass; the driver was detained for 10 days. His father was a Russian-language translator for the Chinese Air Force.
notes: Famously media-shy. IR email is stated to be for investors only, so expect low response for media requests. Father detail source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wang_Wei_(SF_Express). Not to be confused with other Wang Weis (Tudou, Vizio).

name: Gerard Mulliez
current_role: Founder of Auchan and patriarch of the Mulliez family association (AFM); retired from executive roles (turned 95 in May 2026)
profile: Born in Roubaix in 1931 into the Phildar textile family, Gérard Mulliez opened the first Auchan in 1961 in a disused Phildar factory and built it into an international hypermarket group. He created the Association Familiale Mulliez, which funds family ventures including Decathlon, Leroy Merlin, Kiabi and Norauto. He left Auchan's supervisory board in 2006 and is now retired; his granddaughter published his biography in 2026.
interesting_fact: The Auchan name comes from the Roubaix 'Hauts-Champs' district where the first store opened, respelled so it would appear first in the phone directory. Early struggles led him to seek advice from Édouard Leclerc, who taught him that lower prices sell more.
deep_cut_fact: In retirement the hypermarket pioneer became passionate about permaculture, growing a vegetable garden in the park of the Château de la Fontaine in Croix; at 91 he told La Voix du Nord he thought he could live to 120.

public_contacts.value: https://www.auchan-retail.com/en/newsroom/ (Auchan Retail newsroom; HQ 200 rue de la Recherche, Villeneuve d'Ascq)

notes: Aged 95, retired and private; no personal channels. Only realistic route is Auchan corporate communications / the Mulliez family association. Biography: Margaux Mulliez, 'Gérard Mulliez: L'épopée du fondateur d'Auchan' (Grasset, 2026), a possible conversation hook.

name: Bradley S Jacob
current_role: Chairman and CEO, QXO, Inc. (building-products distribution); non-executive chairman of XPO
profile: Brad Jacobs (b. 1956, Providence) is a serial roll-up entrepreneur who founded United Waste Systems, United Rentals and XPO (later spinning off GXO and RXO). In 2024 he launched QXO with a $1B raise to consolidate building-products distribution, buying Beacon Roofing and others. In Nov 2026 he announced a ~$1B equity investment to launch his ninth company while staying QXO CEO.
interesting_fact: He has founded eight separate billion-dollar companies and has written two books on his playbook: 'How to Make a Few Billion Dollars' (2024) and the sequel 'How to Make a Few More Billion Dollars' (2025).
deep_cut_fact: He studied math and music at Bennington College and Brown before dropping out in 1976; his first company was Amerex Oil Associates, an oil brokerage he co-founded in 1979, and he often credits Philipp Brothers' Ludwig Jesselson as an influential mentor.
notes: Name in dataset 'Bradley S Jacob' = Brad Jacobs (Bradley S. Jacobs). Very media-friendly (books, podcasts, CNBC). Joe Checkler handles QXO media; same contact has appeared on releases since 2024.

name: George Kaiser
current_role: President/CEO and primary owner of GBK Corp (parent of Kaiser-Francis Oil); chairman and majority owner of BOK Financial; founder, George Kaiser Family Foundation
profile: Tulsa-born son of refugees from Nazi Germany who took over the small family oil prospector Kaiser-Francis Oil in 1969 and grew it into an international E&P firm. Bought Bank of Oklahoma out of federal receivership in 1991 (now BOK Financial, ~63% owned) and holds ~72% of LNG firm Excelerate Energy; his GKFF has paid out $2.5bn+, focused on Tulsa.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he opened The Gathering Place, a 66-acre Tulsa riverfront park that is the largest public park in the US built with private funds.
deep_cut_fact: His foundation, jointly with the University of Tulsa, acquired Bob Dylan's 6,000+ item archive in 2016 (reportedly $15-20m), after earlier buying the Woody Guthrie archive; both now anchor Tulsa's Brady Arts District (Bob Dylan Center, Woody Guthrie Center).
notes: Famously low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is GKFF media office. Also a good energy angle: Kaiser-Francis (gas) and Excelerate Energy (LNG regasification). Giving Pledge signer (2010).

name: Lu Xiangyang
current_role: Vice chairman, BYD Company; chairman of Youngy Group (融捷集团) and chairman/president of listed Youngy Co., Ltd. (002192.SZ)
profile: Born 1962 in Wuwei, Anhui, Lu worked at a local People's Bank of China branch before moving to Guangdong in the early 1990s. In 1995 he backed his cousin Wang Chuanfu's new battery firm BYD, now one of the world's largest EV makers, where he is vice chairman. He also runs his own Youngy (Rongjie) investment group, with lithium assets.
interesting_fact: His initial stake in BYD came from investing a few million renminbi in his cousin Wang Chuanfu's newly formed battery start-up in 1995; that stake is the source of most of his roughly $15bn fortune.
deep_cut_fact: Through Youngy Co. (融捷股份), which he chairs, Lu controls Rongda Lithium, holder of the mining right to the No. 134 spodumene vein at Jiajika in Kangding, Sichuan, one of China's largest hard-rock lithium deposits. In 2024 it agreed a project to add 350,000 t/yr of ore-processing capacity at the mine.
notes: Very low public profile and rarely gives interviews. socialmediaglobal@byd.com is the general contact email BYD publishes for its global HQ; PressEU@byd.com is BYD Europe's press contact. Youngy Co. investor-relations contacts are listed in its SZSE filings (002192). Sources disagree slightly on his initial BYD investment (RMB 2.5m vs 5m).

name: Ralph Lauren
current_role: Founder, Executive Chairman and Chief Creative Officer, Ralph Lauren Corporation (NYSE: RL)
profile: Born Ralph Lifshitz in the Bronx to Jewish immigrants, Lauren started selling his own ties in 1967 from a tiny office in the Empire State Building. That grew into the Polo/Ralph Lauren lifestyle empire. He stepped down as CEO in 2015 but remains executive chairman and chief creative officer, controlling about 85% of the voting power.
interesting_fact: He gave $10 million to help restore the original Star-Spangled Banner flag. In 2019 he became the first American designer to receive an honorary knighthood (KBE), presented by Prince Charles.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion, he served in the US Army (1962-64), worked briefly as a sales assistant at Brooks Brothers, then sold ties for Rivetz. As a car collector he has twice won Best of Show at the Pebble Beach Concours d'Elegance: in 1990 with a 1938 Bugatti Type 57SC Atlantic and in 1993 with a 1930 Mercedes-Benz SSK 'Count Trossi'.
notes: Aged 86, he rarely gives interviews and has no personal social accounts; the brand's Instagram (@ralphlauren) is corporate. Go through RL corporate communications. Cars and Americana are better hooks than energy or data centres.

name: Lui Yiu Tung
current_role: Chairman, Galaxy Entertainment Group (Macau) and Chairman, K. Wah International Holdings; chairs the family K. Wah Group
profile: Francis Lui Yiu Tung (吕耀东) is the eldest son of K. Wah founder Lui Che Woo (d. Nov 2024). He joined the group in 1979, became an executive director in 1987 and deputy chairman in 1997, and led Galaxy's push into Macau casino-resorts (Galaxy Macau, Broadway, StarWorld). He became chairman in December 2024.
interesting_fact: Asian Gaming magazine has named him the most influential person in its Asian Gaming Power 50 list nine times (as of 2025), and he was named 'Outstanding CEO' at the 2024 IAG Academy IR Awards.
deep_cut_fact: Before casinos he trained as an engineer: a B.S. in civil engineering and an M.S. in structural engineering from UC Berkeley. France made him an Officer of the Order of Arts and Letters in 2021, and he is an honorary citizen of Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Jiangmen.
notes: Hurun's English label 'Lui Yiu Tung' = Francis Lui. Chairman since Dec 2024 after his father's death (https://igamingbusiness.com/casino/francis-lui-replaces-late-father-as-galaxy-entertainment-chair/). Formal, CPPCC National Committee member; route via Galaxy IR/corporate communications.

name: Andrew Forrest
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Fortescue; chair of Minderoo Foundation; owner of Squadron Energy
profile: 'Twiggy' Forrest, a former stockbroker, founded Fortescue Metals Group in 2003 and built it into one of the world's largest iron ore miners. He is now steering it toward 'real zero' emissions, including a $2.8B deal (2024) for electric trucks and mining equipment. His private Squadron Energy bought CWP Renewables for about A$4B, and his Minderoo Foundation is one of Australia's largest philanthropies.
interesting_fact: He has pledged to decarbonise Fortescue's mining operations by 2030 without offsets, and committed A$750M to rebuilding Ukraine's energy and communications infrastructure. A natural fit for an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 he earned a PhD in marine science from the University of Western Australia (he is now an adjunct research fellow at its Oceans Institute). He also converted his 58m superyacht Pangaea into a Minderoo ocean-research vessel with on-board labs.
notes: Very media-accessible and keen to talk energy transition and green iron. Fortescue's press releases use the title 'Dr Andrew Forrest AO'. Fortescue has had heavy senior-executive turnover. He has a separation from Nicola Forrest (2023); avoid it in outreach.

name: Steven Anthony Ballmer
current_role: Owner, Los Angeles Clippers (NBA); co-founder, Ballmer Group (philanthropy) and founder, USAFacts
profile: Steve Ballmer joined Microsoft in 1980 as its 30th employee and first business manager, succeeding Bill Gates as CEO (2000-2014). Still among Microsoft's largest individual shareholders, he bought the LA Clippers in 2014 for $2B, built the Intuit Dome arena, and with his wife Connie funds economic-mobility work via Ballmer Group and nonpartisan government-data site USAFacts.
interesting_fact: He scored higher than his Harvard dorm-mate Bill Gates on the William Lowell Putnam Mathematical Competition, and graduated magna cum laude in applied math and economics in 1977.
deep_cut_fact: Before Microsoft he was an assistant product manager at Procter & Gamble for two years, sharing an office with future GE CEO Jeff Immelt, then briefly tried writing screenplays in Hollywood before enrolling at Stanford GSB, which he left in 1980 to join Gates.
notes: Input record has only old Forbes 1996-2000 data; today one of the 10 richest people (Microsoft stake). Media-friendly on data/government and sports-business topics; route via Ballmer Group/USAFacts or Clippers communications. Avoid the Clippers/Aspiration-Kawhi Leonard sponsorship controversy.

name: Philip F. Anschutz
current_role: Owner and chairman of The Anschutz Corporation (Denver); owner of Anschutz Entertainment Group (AEG)
profile: Kansas-born oilman (b. 1939) who parlayed his father's drilling business into a sprawling private empire: oil and gas, railroads (Southern Pacific), telecom (Qwest), Regal Cinemas, AEG (Crypto.com Arena, The O2, Coachella), the LA Kings, The Broadmoor and newspapers incl. the Washington Examiner. He co-founded MLS. His Power Company of Wyoming is building the Chokecherry and Sierra Madre wind complex.
interesting_fact: His Chokecherry and Sierra Madre project in Carbon County, Wyoming (up to 1,000 turbines, ~3,000 MW, est. $5B) was described by the BLM as the largest commercial wind facility proposed in the U.S., paired with the TransWest Express transmission line.
deep_cut_fact: At 28, after a Wyoming wildcat well caught fire in 1967, he struck a deal with Universal Studios, which was making the John Wayne film 'Hellfighters', to pay $100,000 for rights to film the blaze; that money plus acreage sales paid Red Adair to cap it.
notes: Famously press-shy; has given almost no interviews in decades. No published personal or office contact found; approaches would go via Anschutz Corp or AEG corporate communications. Forbes record here is old (1997-2000 lists) but he remains a billionaire. Wind/transmission project is a natural hook for an energy podcast.

name: Alwaleed Bin Talal Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
current_role: Founder, Chairman (and majority owner) of Kingdom Holding Company, Riyadh
profile: Saudi prince (b. 1955, Jeddah), grandson of King Abdulaziz and of Lebanon's first PM Riad Al Solh. He built Kingdom Holding from 1980 into a global investor, famous for rescuing Citicorp in 1991 and stakes in Four Seasons, Twitter/X, Disneyland Paris and hotels; he is now driving the Jeddah Tower (set to be the world's tallest) and KHC's Al Hilal club deal.
interesting_fact: In July 2026 he announced on a site visit that Jeddah Tower, of which Kingdom Holding is principal investor, had reached 430 m and 107 floors after construction restarted in Jan 2025; completion is targeted for 2028.
deep_cut_fact: He started Kingdom Establishment in 1980 out of a small four-room cabin in Riyadh with $30,000 from his father; when it ran out he got a $300,000 bank loan, and his first success came in 1982 partnering with a South Korean construction company.
notes: Active and public on X; gives TV interviews. Also funds Alwaleed Philanthropies (pledged $32B in 2015). Avoid the 2017 Ritz-Carlton detention topic. Company X: https://x.com/kingdom_khc.

name: Johann Rupert
current_role: Chairman, Compagnie Financiere Richemont; chairman of Remgro and Reinet Investments
profile: Stellenbosch-born son of Anton Rupert who founded Rand Merchant Bank in 1979, then in 1988 created Richemont, now owner of Cartier, Van Cleef & Arpels and Montblanc. He chairs Richemont and the family's investment vehicles Remgro (7% stake) and Reinet (26%), and is a conservationist and vocal opponent of fracking in the Karoo.
interesting_fact: Rupert has said his biggest regret was not buying half of Gucci when it was available for just $175 million.
deep_cut_fact: A former cricketer, he co-founded the Sports Science Institute of South Africa with Springbok Morne du Plessis and scientist Tim Noakes, and developed the Gary Player-designed Leopard Creek golf course; he began his career with two years at Chase Manhattan and three at Lazard Freres in New York.
notes: Described by the FT as reclusive; rarely gives interviews. Chairs Peace Parks Foundation (conservation) - a possible angle along with his anti-fracking stance in the Karoo. Best route: Richemont Press Office or Teneo.

name: Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud
current_role: King of Saudi Arabia and Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques (since January 2015)
profile: Salman bin Abdulaziz (born 1935) is King of Saudi Arabia; his listed wealth reflects royal/state oil-linked fortune rather than a business he built. He governed Riyadh province for nearly five decades before becoming defence minister, crown prince and, in 2015, king. Day-to-day government is now led by his son Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, who chairs the cabinet.
interesting_fact: Before taking the throne he served as Governor of Riyadh for roughly 48 years (1963-2011), overseeing its growth from a mid-sized town into a city of millions.
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen amateur historian: he long chaired Darah (the King Abdulaziz Foundation for Research and Archives), and his personal library is known for its rare manuscripts and books on Arabian history.
notes: Reigning head of state (aged ~90; hospital tests Jan 2026, still chairing cabinet per Aug 2026 reports). Not a realistic podcast guest; any approach would go via the Saudi Royal Court / embassy media offices. Wikipedia was rate-limited during research.

name: Jeffery Hildebrand
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Hilcorp Energy Company (Houston); Chairman, Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission (named 2023)
profile: Texas-born geologist/petroleum engineer (UT Austin BS 1981, MS 1985) who founded Hilcorp in 1989-90 after stints at Exxon and Dan A. Hughes Co. He built it into America's largest private oil producer by buying and revitalising mature fields, incl. BP's Alaska assets ($5.6B, 2020). Stepped down as CEO in 2018; remains executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In December 2015 Hilcorp gave each of its ~1,380 employees a $100,000 bonus after the staff hit a five-year goal of doubling the company's size.
deep_cut_fact: His alma mater's department is now the 'Hildebrand Department of Petroleum and Geosystems Engineering' at UT Austin, renamed in Nov 2017 after he and wife Mindy gave $25M; as a student he was in Pi Epsilon Tau, the petroleum engineering honor society.
notes: Very private, rarely gives interviews. Hilcorp's contact form has a dedicated Media option (asks for outlet and deadline). Also reachable in public capacity via Texas Parks & Wildlife Commission. Bio with board roles: https://krirm.tamuk.edu/jeff-hildebrand/

name: Sam McCandlish
current_role: Co-Founder and Chief Architect, Anthropic (CTO until Oct 2025)
profile: Theoretical physicist (Brandeis BS/MS, Stanford PhD under Eva Silverstein) who moved into AI at OpenAI, where he worked on scaling laws, then co-founded Anthropic in 2021. His wealth comes from his Anthropic stake. After serving as CTO, he became Chief Architect in Oct 2025, leading pretraining, large-scale model training, research productivity and RL infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He was lead author of OpenAI's 2018 paper 'An Empirical Model of Large-Batch Training' (with Jared Kaplan, Dario Amodei), which introduced the 'gradient noise scale' to predict how far training can be parallelised; he later co-authored the 2020 scaling-laws paper.
deep_cut_fact: His 2012 DOE Office of Science Graduate Fellowship profile (High Energy Theory, hometown Pittsburgh) notes he spent a summer at the Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics studying gravitational microlensing, and that outside physics he enjoys climbing trees and playing jazz piano.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Title change to Chief Architect confirmed by TechCrunch (Oct 2025) and Anthropic leadership page. Best route is via Anthropic press.

name: Tom Brown
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Compute Officer, Anthropic
profile: Co-founder of Anthropic (2021), where he runs compute, the infrastructure that trains and serves Claude. He was previously a research engineer at OpenAI and first author of the GPT-3 paper. Before AI he worked as an engineer at YC startups including MoPub and the group-dating app Grouper. His wealth comes from his Anthropic stake.
interesting_fact: He is the first-listed author of 'Language Models are Few-Shot Learners' (2020), the GPT-3 paper that kicked off the large-language-model era.
deep_cut_fact: His route into OpenAI went through Grouper: Greg Brockman was a regular Grouper user. Brown spent six months teaching himself ML (Coursera, Kaggle, a GPU bought with YC credits), then messaged Brockman: 'I got a B- in linear algebra... I'm happy to mop floors.'
notes: Chief Compute Officer title per July 2026 reporting (https://thenextweb.com/news/tom-blomfield-monzo-founder-anthropic-compute). He spoke openly about his career on YC's Lightcone podcast (Aug 2025) and answered Business Insider by email. No personal contact published; go through Anthropic press.

name: Christopher Olah
current_role: Cofounder and interpretability research lead, Anthropic
profile: Canadian AI researcher who cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI staff and leads its interpretability research (understanding the internals of neural networks). Previously at Google Brain and OpenAI; cofounded the Distill journal. His Anthropic stake (company valued at $380B in Feb 2026) makes him a billionaire despite never finishing college.
interesting_fact: Olah skipped college and became a Thiel Fellow in 2012 at 19; in 2020 he wrote a blog post to help others decide whether to follow a similar no-degree path.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI, he was a 3D-printing hacker: in early 2012 he started ImplicitCAD, an open-source programmatic CAD tool written entirely in Haskell (inspired by OpenSCAD) that exports STL and G-code for 3D printers.
notes: Research-focused, rarely does business press; most active via his blog and X (@ch402). Anthropic press route for formal requests.

name: Daniela Amodei
current_role: Co-founder and President, Anthropic
profile: Co-founded AI lab Anthropic (maker of the Claude models) in 2021 with her brother Dario and five other ex-OpenAI staff; as president she runs day-to-day operations. Earlier: a Pennsylvania congressional campaign and Rep. Matt Cartwright's office, an early hire at Stripe (2013), then OpenAI (2018-2020) as VP of safety and policy. Anthropic was privately valued at ~$965B in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Before tech she worked in politics on Matt Cartwright's successful 2012 Pennsylvania congressional campaign and then in his Washington office; she and Dario were both named to the 2023 Time100 AI list.
deep_cut_fact: She went to UC Santa Cruz on a classical flute scholarship and studied liberal arts and music, graduating in English literature, and at OpenAI she managed the team during GPT-2's development before moving into safety and policy.
notes: Anthropic press office (press@anthropic.com) is the standard route. Lowell High School (San Francisco) alumna. Note: this research was compiled by Claude, an Anthropic model; facts drawn from public sources only.

name: Jack Clark
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Public Benefit, Anthropic (leads the Anthropic Institute, since March 2026)
profile: British-born former tech journalist (The Register, Bloomberg) who became OpenAI's policy director in 2016 and co-founded Anthropic in 2021 with six ex-OpenAI researchers. His wealth comes from his Anthropic stake. He ran Anthropic's policy team until March 2026, when he became Head of Public Benefit leading the new Anthropic Institute; he still writes the Import AI newsletter.
interesting_fact: Clark was a founding member of Stanford's AI Index (2017-2024) and an inaugural member of the US National AI Advisory Committee (2021-2024); his Import AI newsletter is read by ~70,000 people each week.
