deep_cut_fact: Before AI policy he was a technical journalist covering distributed systems and quantum computers; in 2016 he told his Bloomberg editor Alistair Barr, on a bench overlooking SF Bay, he was quitting to join OpenAI - Barr told him it was a terrible idea. He also writes short science-fiction stories in Import AI.
notes: Very public and accessible via Import AI newsletter and X; podcast-friendly (frequent interviewee). Forbes bio's 'head of policy' title is outdated as of March 2026.

name: Jared Kaplan
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Science Officer, Anthropic (on leave as associate professor of physics, Johns Hopkins University)
profile: Theoretical physicist (Stanford BS, Harvard PhD under Nima Arkani-Hamed) who worked on quantum gravity and holography at Johns Hopkins from 2012, joined OpenAI in 2019 and cofounded Anthropic in 2021 with six other ex-OpenAI staff. Anthropic was valued at $380B in Feb 2026; Kaplan leads its science work and served as its Responsible Scaling Officer.
interesting_fact: Lead author of 'Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models' (2020), the paper showing LLM performance improves predictably with model size, data and compute; he also co-authored the GPT-3 paper. Named to the Time100 AI list in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the Illinois Mathematics and Science Academy (IMSA) in 2001, and in 2026 IMSA's Board of Trustees gave him its alumni Trailblazer Award. His 2009 Harvard PhD thesis was titled 'Aspects of holography'.
notes: Reach via Anthropic press team. Strong physics-to-AI story; scaling laws link directly to data-center/compute demand theme.

name: George Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder and Co-Executive Chairman, KKR & Co. Inc.
profile: George R. Roberts (b. 1943, Houston) co-founded KKR in 1976 with cousin Henry Kravis and Jerome Kohlberg after their Bear Stearns buyout work. KKR pioneered the leveraged buyout (RJR Nabisco, 1988), went public in 2010, and now has 250+ portfolio companies, including energy holdings like Crescent Energy. Roberts and Kravis became co-executive chairmen in 2021; he is based in the Bay Area.
interesting_fact: Roberts and his wife sit on the boards of the Fine Arts Museums of San Francisco and SFMOMA; his nonprofit REDF (now Redefine Alliance) invests in businesses that train and employ people facing barriers to work.
deep_cut_fact: Roberts graduated from Culver Military Academy in Indiana in 1962 and received its 'Man of the Year' award in 1998. He became a Bear Stearns partner at 29. He also founded REDF in 1997 (originally the Roberts Enterprise Development Fund), an early backer of employment social enterprises; he still chairs its board.
notes: Very low public profile and rarely gives interviews. Best route is KKR Media (media@kkr.com). Redefine Alliance (formerly REDF), which he chairs, offers a philanthropic angle. KKR has a large energy/infrastructure book (e.g. Crescent Energy), relevant to the podcast.

name: Dario Amodei
current_role: Cofounder & CEO, Anthropic PBC
profile: San Francisco-born physicist turned AI researcher who led research at OpenAI (GPT-2/GPT-3, co-inventor of RLHF) before cofounding Anthropic in 2021 with his sister Daniela and five other ex-OpenAI staff. Anthropic, maker of Claude, filed its S-1 for an IPO in Oct 2026 and launched its roadshow in Nov 2026.
interesting_fact: Writes long-form essays on AI's future on his personal site, notably 'Machines of Loving Grace' (2024) and 'The Adolescence of Technology'; he earned his Princeton biophysics PhD as a Hertz Fellow.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI he was a neuroscientist: his 2011 Princeton PhD thesis, 'Network-Scale Electrophysiology: Measuring and Understanding the Collective Behavior of Neural Circuits' (advisors Michael Berry and William Bialek), built devices to record neural circuits. He was also on the 2000 USA Physics Olympiad team.
notes: Anthropic is in its IPO roadshow (Nov 2026), so expect quiet-period limits on executive media. Has done many long-form podcasts (Lex Fridman, Dwarkesh, Ezra Klein, Cheeky Pint), listed on darioamodei.com. Physics Olympiad detail per Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dario_Amodei).

name: Li Shuirong
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group and Rongsheng Petrochemical (SZSE: 002493)
profile: Li Shuirong (b. 1956) built Hangzhou-based Rongsheng from a 1989 polyester cloth workshop into one of China's largest private petrochemical groups, spanning refining, chemicals, logistics and property. He chairs Rongsheng Petrochemical, whose Zhoushan refinery is a strategic partner of Saudi Aramco (which paid $3.4bn for 10% in 2023).
interesting_fact: Before going into business Li tried to make a living as a carpenter; in 2020 Rongsheng became the first private Chinese refiner granted government permission to export refined oil products.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, founded in 1989, was the Yinong Network Chemical Fiber Factory in Yinong town (Xiaoshan, Hangzhou), making polyester fibre cloth; he only moved upstream into petrochemicals as the polyester industry shifted.
notes: Emails are Rongsheng Petrochemical board secretary (Quan Weiying) and securities affairs rep, from the 2026 interim report. Son-in-law Xiang Jiongjiong is GM of the listed arm. Low media profile; Chinese-language approach advisable.

name: Barry Lin Bai-Li
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Quanta Computer (Taiwan)
profile: Shanghai-born (1949), Hong Kong-raised, NTU-trained electrical engineer Barry Lam (Lin Pai-li) co-founded calculator maker Kinpo in 1973, then founded Quanta Computer in 1988, building it into the world's largest notebook ODM. Quanta is now a major AI-server builder (incl. Nvidia GB200 racks for hyperscalers), which drove his fortune to the top of Taiwan's rich lists.
interesting_fact: He started Quanta in 1988 with colleague C.C. Leung on under US$900,000 of capital; it became a Fortune Global 500 company and the original design manufacturer of the One Laptop per Child XO-1.
deep_cut_fact: A major collector of Chinese painting and calligraphy, he owns more than 250 works by Zhang Daqian and sponsors the Zhang Daqian Museum in the artist's former home; he also built an art-and-technology museum into Quanta's HQ.
notes: Known as Barry Lam in English. Low-profile; route via Quanta corporate spokesperson/IR (TWSE: 2382). Quanta ESG reports reportedly list a CSR contact (qci.csr@quantatw.com) but I could not reverify the PDF. Also funds NTU's Barry Lam Hall (EECS).

name: Oeri Paul Sacher
profile: This 1996 Forbes entry ($13.1B, shared with the Hoffmann family) appears to be the Hoffmann-Oeri-Sacher Roche founding-family fortune headed by Paul Sacher (1906–1999). Sacher was the Swiss conductor and new-music patron who became Roche's main shareholder through his wife Maja Hoffmann. He died 26 May 1999 in Switzerland, aged 93.
notes: Deceased (Paul Sacher, d. 26 May 1999; NYT obituary https://www.nytimes.com/1999/05/27/arts/paul-sacher-is-dead-at-93-conductor-and-arts-patron.html ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Sacher). The name merges 'Oeri' (Roche heirs Vera Oeri-Hoffmann / Jakob Oeri line) with Sacher. Living Roche-family heirs (e.g. André Hoffmann, Maja Oeri) would be separate profiles.

name: Family Hoffman
current_role: Family entry (Hoffmann/Oeri heirs of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche); public face: André Hoffmann, Vice-Chairman of Roche Holding
profile: A 1996 Forbes family entry for the Swiss Hoffmann-Oeri clan (shared with Paul Sacher and the Oeris), heirs of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche. Through a pooled voting bloc the family holds ~9% of Roche capital but a majority of votes; André Hoffmann (b.1958) has sat on Roche's board since 1996 and is vice-chairman, alongside cousin-line member Jörg Duschmalé.
interesting_fact: André Hoffmann is also Co-Chair of the World Economic Forum's Board of Trustees and a leading voice on 'sustainable capitalism'; he received the WWF Duke of Edinburgh Conservation Medal in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: André grew up in France's Camargue wetlands at the Tour du Valat biological station founded in 1954 by his father Luc Hoffmann (a WWF co-founder); in 1983 he left its board to work as acting administrator of the research station, and he now presides over Fondation Tour du Valat and the MAVA Foundation.
notes: This is a family entry, not one person; profile uses André Hoffmann (Roche Vice-Chairman, term to 2027) as the representative since he is the family's public figure. Other branches: Oeri (e.g. Maja Oeri, Andreas Oeri) and the late Paul Sacher's heirs. Confirm which family member the journalist wants before outreach.

name: Joseph Christopher Reyes
current_role: Co-chairman, Reyes Holdings LLC (Rosemont, Illinois; beer, Coca-Cola bottling and Martin Brower foodservice distribution)
profile: Chris Reyes (born 1953) and brother Jude started Reyes Holdings in 1976 by buying a small Schlitz distributorship in Spartanburg, SC, with their father. Via 115+ acquisitions it became the largest US beer distributor, a big Coca-Cola bottler and (via Martin Brower) a key McDonald's supplier; Forbes ranked it the 6th-largest US private company in 2025.
interesting_fact: When the Reyes brothers bought the Spartanburg Schlitz distributorship in 1976, it had just 12 employees serving a single small market with a handful of brands; the company celebrated its 50th anniversary in February 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the global board of trustees of Ronald McDonald House Charities, a fitting role given Reyes's Martin Brower unit distributes to McDonald's restaurants worldwide.
notes: Private, low media profile; also a large political donor (bipartisan in Chicago, mostly Republican nationally), so expect a guarded comms team. RMHC trustee role per Wikipedia citing rmhc.org (2023); confirm still current before mentioning.

name: R. Budi Hartono
current_role: Co-owner and head of Djarum Group (clove cigarettes, Bank Central Asia stake, Polytron, Blibli/Global Digital Niaga, Como 1907)
profile: Robert Budi Hartono (b. 1941) and his brother inherited Djarum after a 1963 factory fire and built it into a clove-cigarette giant. Their biggest asset is control of Bank Central Asia, bought after the 1997-98 crisis. They also own Polytron (now making EVs), Blibli (IPO 2022), Jakarta property and Italian football club Como 1907.
interesting_fact: Their father Oei Wie Gwan bought a bankrupt cigarette company in 1950 and renamed it Djarum ('needle') after the needle of a gramophone.
deep_cut_fact: PB Djarum, Indonesia's famous badminton club, began on a court at the Djarum factory in Kudus where Budi Hartono encouraged employees to play; spotting young Liem Swie King's talent, he formalised the club, and 7 of the 8 players on Indonesia's 1984 Thomas Cup-winning team came from PB Djarum.
notes: Very private; no personal or family-office contact published. Note: the 2018 Asian Games bridge bronze medal belongs to his brother Michael, not Budi. Route via Djarum Group / Djarum Foundation corporate channels.

name: Dan Friedkin
current_role: Chairman & CEO, The Friedkin Group (Gulf States Toyota, Auberge Resorts, NEON, AS Roma, Everton FC)
profile: Dan Friedkin runs The Friedkin Group, built around Gulf States Toyota, the Houston distributor his father Thomas founded in 1969 that holds exclusive Toyota distribution rights in five states ($14.5B of sales in 2025). He has expanded into luxury hotels (Auberge), film (Oscar-winning studio NEON) and European football (AS Roma; Everton since 2024).
interesting_fact: His Friedkin Conservation Trust works to preserve more than 6 million acres in Tanzania, and he owns one of the largest collections of vintage military warplanes in the US.
deep_cut_fact: He won a Taurus World Stunt Award (Best Specialty Stunt) for 'Dunkirk', where he flew an authentic Spitfire through the aerial dogfight and landed it on the beach. He also founded the Air Force Heritage Flight Foundation and flies with the Horsemen P-51 team.
notes: Very private; rarely interviewed. friedkin.com's contact page is behind a bot wall, so no press email was confirmed. Warbirds/aviation and conservation are safe, warm openers; he has chaired Project Recover (WWII MIA search) since 2019.

name: David Reuben
current_role: Co-founder, Reuben Brothers (with brother Simon); trustee/patron of The Reuben Foundation
profile: Born 1938 in Bombay and raised in Islington, he started in scrap metal and metals trading, then with brother Simon built Reuben Brothers, a property, private-equity and credit empire (Millbank Tower, Arena Racing, London Oxford Airport, a Newcastle United stake). They built data-centre operator Global Switch and sold it in 2016-18 for ~$5.7B combined.
interesting_fact: The brothers were early data-centre investors: their carrier-neutral operator Global Switch was sold in two tranches (49% for ~$3B in 2016, 25% for $2.7B in 2018), one of the biggest data-centre exits of its time.
deep_cut_fact: The Reuben Foundation gave £80M to create Oxford's newest graduate college, Reuben College (originally 'Parks College'), whose research themes include climate change and artificial intelligence.

public_contacts.value: Charles Stewart-Smith (listed 'Media' contact for Reuben Brothers): charles.stewart-smith@hotmail.com

notes: Aged ~88 and very private. Younger Reuben Brothers executives now front new deals (e.g. LA's Century Plaza), so the Reuben Brothers media contact or the Foundation media email is the best route. Wikipedia covers 1990s Russian aluminium-era allegations; avoid that topic. The Sunday Times ranked the family Britain's second-richest in 2026 (£27.9B).

name: Simon Reuben
current_role: Co-founder and co-chairman, Reuben Brothers (with brother David Reuben); trustee/director, Reuben Foundation
profile: Mumbai-born, UK-raised Simon Reuben built a real estate, metals and investment fortune with his brother David. Simon started in carpet importing and property; the brothers' Transworld traded aluminum in Russia and Kazakhstan in the 1990s. Reuben Brothers now owns London property, hotels, racecourses, a stake in Newcastle United and data-center operator Global Switch.
interesting_fact: The brothers grew data-center operator Global Switch, selling 49% to a Chinese consortium in 2016 for nearly $3B and a further 25% in 2018 for $2.7B. That is a direct data-center link for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: The Reuben Foundation's £80M gift in June 2020 founded Reuben College, Oxford's first new college in 30 years. It started as 'Parks College' and was renamed for the family; part of the gift funds graduate scholarships.
notes: Extremely discreet and rarely gives interviews. Born c.1941-42. Day-to-day public face of the group is the next generation (e.g. Jamie Reuben). Best route is the Reuben Foundation or Reuben Brothers office. The foundation site blocked repeated automated fetches, so the contact-page form was not verified.

name: Wang Liping
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Hengli Hydraulic Co. (Shanghai-listed, Changzhou)
profile: Wang Liping (汪立平) founded Hengli in 1990 as a small township factory in Wujin, Changzhou. He built it into a global maker of hydraulic cylinders, pumps, valves and castings for Caterpillar, Kobelco and Sany, with plants in China, Germany, the US, Japan and Mexico (a 141,000 m² Mexico factory opened in 2025). Hengli is now pushing into linear actuators and screws for EVs and humanoid robots.
interesting_fact: Hengli opened a 141,000-square-meter factory in Mexico in 2025 to serve customers across the Americas. Its push into precision ball screws and linear drives targets the humanoid-robot supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: Wang reportedly started Hengli with just 50,000 yuan. Around 1996, during China's excavator boom, Hengli broke foreign makers' hold on excavator hydraulic cylinders, and in 2005 it developed high-pressure pumps priced at about half of imports.
notes: Sensitive: on 20 Mar 2026 Hengli disclosed that Wang had been detained (留置) and placed under investigation by the Jiangsu Provincial Supervisory Commission, reason undisclosed. On 13 Apr 2026 the company said he had resumed his chairman duties. Very low media profile. Only the company's general email (hengli@) was found.

name: Martin Lorentzon
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Spotify Technology S.A.
profile: Swedish entrepreneur Martin Lorentzon (b. 1969) co-founded affiliate-marketing network Tradedoubler, which he took public, and then co-founded Spotify with Daniel Ek in 2006, providing much of its early funding. Through Spotify's dual-class shares he holds a large economic stake and outsized voting control, and he remains on its board.
interesting_fact: He and Daniel Ek first bonded over their love of gangster films and get together once a year for a Godfather-trilogy marathon.
deep_cut_fact: As a pupil at Särlaskolan in Borås he told classmates he wanted to sell one matchbox to every person in China and become a billionaire; he later studied industrial economics at Chalmers, which gave him an honorary doctorate in 2015.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Since 2013 part of Prince Daniel's Fellowship, visiting Swedish schools to inspire young entrepreneurs; member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences (IVA). Best route via Spotify press office.

name: Brad Jacobs
current_role: Chairman & CEO, QXO, Inc. (building-products distribution, Greenwich CT)
profile: Serial consolidator who has founded eight billion-dollar companies: Amerex Oil, United Waste, United Rentals, XPO Logistics (later spun into GXO and RXO) and QXO. Since 2024 QXO has bought Beacon (~$11B), Kodiak Building Partners ($2.25B) and TopBuild (~$17B, July 2026); in Nov 2026 he said he will bet $1B on a ninth company in an unnamed industry.
interesting_fact: A trained classical pianist who studied math and music at Bennington and Brown before dropping out; he wrote 'How to Make a Few Billion Dollars' (2024) and a 2025 sequel, 'How to Make a Few More Billion Dollars'.
deep_cut_fact: His first company was Amerex Oil Associates, an oil brokerage he co-founded in 1979 at age 23 and sold in 1983; he then moved to London to start oil trader Hamilton Resources, and often credits Philipp Brothers' Ludwig Jesselson as a key mentor.
notes: Highly media-accessible (books, frequent podcast/TV appearances). Media contact Joe Checkler (QXO) on 2026 releases. Timely hook: Nov 2026 announcement of a ninth company (Hartford Business Journal, 2026-11-09).

name: Michael Sabel
current_role: CEO and Executive Co-Chairman, Venture Global (NYSE: VG), Arlington, Virginia
profile: Former investment banker (Friedman Billings Ramsey, Sandler O'Neil) who co-founded LNG exporter Venture Global with finance lawyer Bob Pender in 2013; together they own 80%+ of the company, which IPO'd in Jan 2025. Sole CEO since 2020, he is building a third Louisiana export plant (CP2) and the company made its Fortune 500 debut in 2026.
interesting_fact: Venture Global's edge was building LNG plants from small, factory-made modular liquefaction trains (with Baker Hughes) snapped together 'like Legos' — Sabel called shrinking the scale 'our Eureka moment'.
deep_cut_fact: Before LNG, Sabel and Pender tried in 2009 to develop a coal power plant in Sri Lanka; it didn't happen, and the LNG idea came while studying how Haiti could import small volumes of gas.
notes: Company is in high-profile arbitration disputes (BP won in Oct 2025); avoid that topic in outreach. Best route is Venture Global Public Affairs (press@). Frequent speaker at Gastech / LNG conferences.

name: Robert Pender
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Co-Chairman, Venture Global, Inc. (NYSE: VG)
profile: Bob Pender is a former Hogan Lovells project-finance partner who cofounded LNG exporter Venture Global with ex-banker Mike Sabel in 2013. The pair own more than 80% of the company, which IPO'd in January 2025 at a near-$60B valuation. Pender was co-CEO until 2020 and is now executive co-chairman.
interesting_fact: Before LNG, Pender spent 28 years as an energy finance lawyer and worked on more than $35 billion of energy, infrastructure and power projects, from cogeneration, biomass and geothermal to LNG and nuclear, including representing the Government of India and the People's Republic of China.
deep_cut_fact: Pro bono, he gave legal support to the Interim Haiti Recovery Commission and then served as a counselor to Haiti's Minister Delegate for Energy Security. He also helped the American Red Cross with South Asia tsunami relief and Accion with microfinance projects in Africa.
notes: Low public profile compared with co-chair Mike Sabel, who does most of the media. The best route is Venture Global's press office in Arlington, VA. He sits on the Memorial Sloan Kettering board of trustees.

name: Joshua Harris
current_role: Founder, 26North; Founder & Managing General Partner, Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment; Managing Partner, Washington Commanders
profile: Josh Harris co-founded Apollo Global Management in 1990 with Leon Black and Marc Rowan after Drexel Burnham Lambert, spending 30+ years building it into a leading alternatives manager. He left in 2022 to found multi-asset alternatives firm 26North. Through HBSE he controls the Philadelphia 76ers and New Jersey Devils, and he led the $6.05B purchase of the NFL's Washington Commanders in 2023.
interesting_fact: Beyond the big franchises, his HBSE platform owns esports team Dignitas, minor-league clubs (Delaware Blue Coats, Utica Comets), the Prudential Center arena and HBSEv, a venture fund investing in early-stage sports-tech startups.
deep_cut_fact: The son of an orthodontist and a former wrestler, Harris still competes in marathons and triathlons. At Apollo he led the landmark LyondellBasell investment, and he was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School after graduating summa cum laude from Wharton.
notes: Forbes bio is stale: he is no longer at Apollo (left 2022, founded 26North). Wrestler/triathlon detail is from Forbes profile facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/joshua-harris/). Harris Philanthropies (600 Madison Ave, NYC office) links his LinkedIn. Best media route: HBSE/26North communications.

name: Gerald Cavendish Grosvenor
current_role: Deceased (6th Duke of Westminster, died 9 August 2016)
profile: Gerald Grosvenor, 6th Duke of Westminster, headed the Grosvenor estate (Mayfair and Belgravia property) and was a Territorial Army major general. He died of a heart attack on 9 August 2016; the title and estate interests passed to his son Hugh Grosvenor, 7th Duke of Westminster.
notes: Died 9 Aug 2016 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Grosvenor,_6th_Duke_of_Westminster). For the Grosvenor fortune today, the relevant person is Hugh Grosvenor, 7th Duke of Westminster (Grosvenor Group).

name: Bill Marriott, Jr.
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Marriott International (retired as executive chairman/chairman in May 2022; son David Marriott is chairman)
profile: J.W. 'Bill' Marriott Jr. (b. 1932) joined his parents' Hot Shoppes restaurant business in 1956, pushed his debt-wary father to expand into hotels, and as CEO (1972-2012) built Marriott into the world's largest hotel company. He stepped back to chairman in 2012 and to chairman emeritus in 2022; he remains a major shareholder.
interesting_fact: Marriott grew out of an A&W root beer stand his parents opened in Washington, D.C. in 1927; he told the story in his 2013 book 'Without Reservations: How a Family Root Beer Stand Grew into a Global Hotel Company'.
deep_cut_fact: At 74 he became one of the first Fortune 500 CEOs to blog: 'Marriott on the Move' launched Jan 16, 2007 ('I believe in communicating with the customer, and the internet gives me a whole new way of doing that on a global scale'), and he kept it going for years after.
notes: Aged 94; his wife Donna died Dec 30, 2025 - be mindful of timing/tone. Requests best routed via Marriott Global Corporate Communications (press contact named in Marriott releases, 2026).

name: Pao Pui Yung
current_role: Co-holder of the Wheelock/Wharf family fortune with husband Peter Woo; no executive role found
profile: Bessie Pao Pui-yung (包陪容) is the second daughter of the late shipping magnate Sir Y.K. Pao. She married Peter Woo in 1973; he took over the Pao family's property empire (Wheelock and Wharf) after her father retired. Hurun listed the family's Wheelock fortune jointly under her and Peter Woo; son Douglas Woo now chairs Wheelock.
interesting_fact: Peter Woo met Bessie while working at Chase Manhattan Bank; Wikipedia notes she was the sister of the woman he was originally expected to marry. He joined Y.K. Pao's Worldwide Shipping Group in 1975, two years after the wedding.
notes: Extremely private; almost no independent public record of her own. No report of her death found, but no recent appearance either, hence alive=unknown. Any approach would go via Peter Woo / Wheelock & Co (privately held since 2020). Chinese Wikipedia (吳光正) confirms the 1973 marriage.

name: Ian Henrick Lundin
current_role: Lundin family member/beneficiary; former Chairman of Lundin Petroleum/Lundin Energy (until 2022). Holds no current listed-board seat per Lundin Group site.
profile: Swedish-Canadian (b. 1960), son of Lundin Group founder Adolf H. Lundin, based near Geneva. Ran International Petroleum Corp/Lundin Oil and chaired Lundin Petroleum (later Lundin Energy, sold to Aker BP in 2022). Family wealth is held via trusts/Nemesia S.à r.l., a major holder in Lundin Mining, Lundin Gold, IPC and others.
interesting_fact: The Lundin family controls a stable of separately listed resource companies (Lundin Mining, Lundin Gold, IPC, Orrön Energy, Lucara, etc.) through a family trust; Nemesia held ~20% of Lundin Mining in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he was a drilling engineer for Wintershall (BASF) on offshore fields in northern Greece, then joined International Petroleum Corp in 1984 as operations manager in Dubai; he holds a 1982 B.Sc. in Petroleum Engineering from the University of Tulsa.
notes: Sensitive: Ian Lundin is on trial in Stockholm for alleged complicity in war crimes in Sudan (1999-2003); hearings ended and a verdict is expected around Dec 2026. He denies wrongdoing. Very private; no personal channels. Hurun's $13B figure likely reflects the whole Lundin family trust (Nemesia).

name: Bessie Pao Pui Yung
current_role: Wheelock/Wharf family shareholder; wife of Peter Woo Kwong-ching (Wharf/Wheelock chairman emeritus) - no executive role found
profile: Bessie Pao Pui-yung (包佩容), or Bessie Woo, is the second daughter of shipping magnate Sir Y.K. Pao, who took control of Wheelock and Wharf in the 1980s. She married Peter Woo in 1973; he went on to run both firms, and their son Douglas Woo now leads them. Hurun listed her jointly with Peter Woo (2020-21).
interesting_fact: Her father Sir Y.K. Pao, once the world's biggest independent shipowner, built the fortune that passed into Wheelock and Wharf via her husband Peter Woo, whom she married in 1973.
deep_cut_fact: With Peter Woo she funded the cancer centre at Hong Kong's Prince of Wales Hospital, set up to combine cancer treatment, research and education under one roof (credited in a 1995 CUHK honorary-degree citation).
notes: Very private; little public record of her own. Hurun shared listing with Peter Woo. Any approach would go via Wheelock & Co / Wharf Holdings corporate offices. Alive status unconfirmed (no evidence of death found).

name: Haji Hassanal Bolkiah
current_role: Sultan and Yang Di-Pertuan of Brunei Darussalam; also Prime Minister, Defence, Finance and Foreign Minister
profile: Hassanal Bolkiah has been Sultan of Brunei since his father abdicated on 5 Oct 1967, making him one of the world's longest-reigning monarchs. His wealth derives from Brunei's oil and gas revenues, managed via the Brunei Investment Agency (BIA), the sovereign fund that also owns the Dorchester Collection hotels. He still heads state and government.
interesting_fact: Educated at Victoria Institution in Kuala Lumpur, he trained as an officer cadet at the Royal Military Academy Sandhurst (enrolled Jan 1966) before being called home to take the throne in 1967.
deep_cut_fact: He is a qualified pilot who flies his own aircraft: in March 2013 he personally piloted his Boeing 747 to Washington for his meeting with President Obama.
notes: Reigning head of state; Hurun ranks him via the Brunei Investment Agency (state wealth). Realistic route is the Prime Minister's Office (general inbox) or Brunei embassy press channels; a podcast booking is very unlikely.

name: Liu Jiehong
current_role: Director, Amer International Group (正威国际集团), Shenzhen (per public reports)
profile: Liu Jiehong (刘结红) is the wife of Wang Wenyin and a director of Amer International Group, the Shenzhen copper-cable and non-ferrous-metals conglomerate he founded in 1995, which once ranked in the Fortune Global 500. Hurun listed the couple's fortune at about US$13B in 2017-18; she has held executive roles at Amer affiliates in copper and tungsten.
interesting_fact: She is listed jointly with her husband on China's rich lists: New Fortune's 2023 500 Rich List ranked Wang Wenyin/Liu Jiehong 108th with RMB 32.3bn; Hurun also put her on its 2017 Self-Made Women list.
deep_cut_fact: A native of Qianshan in Anhui province, she studied political education at Chizhou University in Anhui before joining the family business.
notes: Very private; no public profile, interviews or official contact found. Amer group has faced debt litigation and court-ordered asset auctions since 2023-24 - not an obvious outreach target. Any approach would go via Amer International Group corporate channels (no published press email found; amer.com.cn did not load).

name: Richard Kinder
current_role: Executive Chairman and co-founder, Kinder Morgan, Inc.; Chairman, Kinder Foundation
profile: Missouri-born lawyer who rose to president/COO of Enron, left in 1996 and with college friend Bill Morgan bought Enron's liquids pipelines for ~$40M, building Kinder Morgan into one of North America's largest energy-infrastructure firms. CEO until 2015, now Executive Chairman and top shareholder; funds Houston parks, education and pediatric cancer via the Kinder Foundation.
interesting_fact: He takes a salary of $1 a year from Kinder Morgan; his wealth comes from being its largest shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Missouri BA/JD alumnus (and Sigma Nu), he funded Mizzou's Kinder Institute on Constitutional Democracy with $25M in 2015, later raising total giving to the institute to $60M. Houston's Kinder Land Bridge over Memorial Drive in Memorial Park (2023) is also named for him and Nancy.
notes: Kinder Foundation site says it cannot respond to every inquiry and has no published email. Best route for an energy podcast is via Kinder Morgan media relations. Age 82.

name: David Velez
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Nu Holdings (Nubank)
profile: Medellin-born, Costa Rica-raised Stanford engineer and MBA who worked at Morgan Stanley, General Atlantic and Sequoia before co-founding Nubank in Sao Paulo in 2013 with Cristina Junqueira and Edward Wible. Nubank listed on the NYSE as Nu Holdings in Dec 2021 and now serves 100M+ customers across Brazil, Mexico and Colombia.
interesting_fact: He started Nubank after seeing that five Brazilian banks controlled about 80% of the market while charging some of the world's highest fees; he was at Sequoia looking for Latin American companies to back and, finding none he liked, built one himself.
deep_cut_fact: His father, one of 11 entrepreneur siblings, ran a button factory in Costa Rica where David spent summers working and saving; he says nobody from his school in Costa Rica had ever gone to Stanford before him.
notes: He and his wife Mariel Reyes have pledged to give away most of their fortune (2021). Accessible via podcasts/interviews (e.g., Sequoia Crucible Moments). Best route likely Nu corporate communications or IR.

name: Brian Chesky
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ: ABNB)
profile: Brian Chesky co-founded Airbnb in 2008 with Joe Gebbia and Nathan Blecharczyk after renting air mattresses in their San Francisco apartment, and has led it as CEO through its 2020 IPO. He owns nearly 11% of the company. A RISD-trained industrial designer, he has pushed Airbnb toward a design-led, founder-mode style and has signed the Giving Pledge (2016).
interesting_fact: To pay off early debts, the founders sold $40-a-box 'Obama O's' and 'Cap'n McCain's' cereal around the 2008 Democratic Convention.
deep_cut_fact: After RISD he worked in Los Angeles as an industrial designer at 3DID, designing toys, guitars and medical equipment; at RISD he captained the hockey team and designed its unofficial mascot, 'Scrotie'.
notes: Very active on X (@bchesky) and a frequent podcast guest, so a podcast invite via Airbnb press is plausible. Born in Niskayuna, NY; son of two social workers.

name: Steven A. Cohen
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Point72 Asset Management; owner of the New York Mets
profile: Steve Cohen (b. 1956, Great Neck, NY) is a Wharton-trained trader who started SAC Capital in 1992 with $10M of his own money and later converted it into Point72, a ~$35B+ multi-strategy firm in Stamford, CT. He bought the New York Mets in 2020, is pursuing the Metropolitan Park casino/entertainment project next to Citi Field, and is a major art collector.
interesting_fact: Through the Steven & Alexandra Cohen Foundation he committed $275M in 2016 to create the Cohen Veterans Network, a national chain of mental-health clinics for veterans and their families.
deep_cut_fact: One of eight children of a garment-district dress maker and a piano teacher, he credits high-school poker with teaching him 'how to take risks' - and on his very first day as a junior options-arbitrage trader at Gruntal & Co. in 1978 he made an $8,000 profit.
notes: Active on X (mostly Mets talk) - one of the few accessible channels. Point72 press office handles media. Avoid SAC-era legal history. Energy/AI angle: Point72 runs a dedicated AI-focused fund (Turion).

name: Ivan Glasenberg
current_role: Retired CEO (2002-2021) and largest individual shareholder of Glencore, Baar, Switzerland
profile: Johannesburg-born, Swiss-based Ivan Glasenberg joined Marc Rich & Co. (later Glencore) in 1984 as a coal marketer, became CEO in 2002, took Glencore public in 2011 and engineered the 2013 Glencore-Xstrata merger. He retired in 2021 but remains Glencore's largest individual shareholder, and his fortune rests on that stake.
interesting_fact: A former South African junior race-walking champion, he race-walked competitively for both South Africa and Israel and still runs and swims daily.
deep_cut_fact: Before commodities he spent five years as a chartered accountant at Johannesburg firm Levitt Kirson (CA(SA)); he earned his MBA through USC's IBEAR program in 1983 and ran Glencore's Hong Kong and Beijing offices in 1989-90 before heading its coal department in 1991.
notes: Very private, no personal website or social accounts found. Since he no longer holds a Glencore role, Glencore's media office is not his channel. Energy angle: Glencore is one of the world's largest coal and transition-metals (copper, cobalt) producers.

name: George Kurtz
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, CrowdStrike Holdings (NASDAQ: CRWD)
profile: A Seton Hall accounting graduate and former CPA, Kurtz held security roles at Price Waterhouse and Ernst & Young, founded Foundstone (sold to McAfee in 2004) and became McAfee's worldwide CTO. In 2011 he co-founded CrowdStrike with Dmitri Alperovitch, took it public in 2019 and built it into a leading cloud cybersecurity platform (~$3.95B revenue FY2025), now pushing into AI security.
interesting_fact: He co-authored 'Hacking Exposed: Network Security Secrets & Solutions', which CrowdStrike bills as the best-selling security book of all time.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious endurance racer: he won the LMP2 Pro-Am class at the 2023 centenary 24 Hours of Le Mans on his first attempt, and won it again in 2026 in the No. 4 CrowdStrike by APR ORECA with Alex Quinn and Laurin Heinrich, after an LMP2 win at the 2026 Rolex 24.
notes: Very media-accessible and active on X and LinkedIn. Corporate comms media contact: Jake Schuster, press@crowdstrike.com. Racing (CrowdStrike Racing by APR; 2026 IMSA LMP2 title reported) is a warm icebreaker.

name: Henry Kravis
current_role: Co-Executive Chairman, KKR & Co. Inc.
profile: Henry Kravis co-founded KKR in 1976 with cousin George Roberts and Jerome Kohlberg, pioneering the leveraged buyout. He and Roberts handed the co-CEO roles to successors in 2021 and serve as co-executive chairs; KKR (public since 2010) manages $650B+ across PE, infrastructure, energy and credit. He is a major donor to Columbia Business School.
interesting_fact: In 1989 KKR orchestrated the $25 billion buyout of RJR Nabisco, the deal behind the bestseller 'Barbarians at the Gate.'
deep_cut_fact: Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma, the son of an oil-industry engineer, Kravis captained the Claremont Men's College golf team as a senior in 1967, finishing his last season with an undefeated conference record; CMC's Kravis Center and Kravis Leadership Institute bear his name.
notes: Best route is KKR global communications (media@kkr.com). Energy angle: father Raymond Kravis was a Tulsa petroleum engineer/consultant (Tulsa Historical Society); KKR is a big infrastructure/energy investor.

name: Antonia Ax:son Johnson
current_role: Principal owner and board member, Axel Johnson Group; Chair of Axel Johnson Holding; founder and board member, Axfoundation
profile: Antonia Ax:son Johnson (b. 1943) is the fourth-generation owner of Sweden's Axel Johnson group (founded 1873), which she led from 1982 before handing the chair to daughter Caroline Berg in 2015. The group spans grocery (50% of Axfood), industrial distribution and US-based Axel Johnson Inc. She remains principal owner and a sustainability philanthropist via Axfoundation.
interesting_fact: An avid equestrian and breeder, she founded and chairs Lövsta Stuteri, a stud farm whose horses have competed at the Olympics.
deep_cut_fact: She founded Axfoundation, which runs the Torsåker Farm food-innovation project and 'Future Food'/'Future Materials' programs; she holds honorary doctorates from the Swedish University of Agricultural Sciences (SLU), KTH Royal Institute of Technology and Middlebury College, and studied at Radcliffe as an exchange student in the early 1960s.

public_contacts.value: https://www.axfoundation.se/en/contact (Axfoundation team incl. Media Relations Manager)

notes: Age ~83; quoted in Axfoundation news in June 2026. Sustainability/food-system philanthropy is the best angle; Axel Johnson group includes energy-adjacent and industrial businesses. Contact via Axfoundation media relations or Axel Johnson AB.

name: Tobi Lutke
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shopify; director, Coinbase
profile: German-born Lütke learned to code by 12 and left school at 16 for a programming apprenticeship. After moving to Canada in 2003, he built his own e-commerce software for Snowdevil, an online snowboard shop. That became Shopify (2006), now used by millions of merchants. He owns ~6% and holds ~40% of votes via a founder share.
interesting_fact: He moved to Canada after meeting his future wife, an Ottawa native, on a snowboarding trip to Whistler. Snowboarding gave him both his home and his company.
deep_cut_fact: He was on the Ruby on Rails core team and wrote open-source libraries such as Active Merchant. His first computer, at age six, was a Schneider CPC. In 2025 he raced LMP2 prototypes in the IMSA SportsCar Championship for Era Motorsport, sharing the car with Rails creator David Heinemeier Hansson.
notes: Very active on X (@tobi), engaging with founders and posting about AI/engineering - best direct route. Frequent long-form podcast guest. Strong AI-adoption advocate (his 2025 'reflexive AI usage' internal memo went public).

name: Wang Xingxing
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and CTO, Unitree Robotics (Hangzhou)
profile: Ningbo-born roboticist (b. 1990) who founded Unitree in 2016 after two months at DJI, building low-cost quadruped 'robot dogs' and then humanoids (G1, H1) sold worldwide. Unitree raised $905M in an August 2026 IPO, becoming China's first listed humanoid-robot maker; it also sells GD01, a 3m+ piloted transformable mecha from $650,000.
interesting_fact: In January 2025 he sat in the front row at Xi Jinping's private-sector business symposium - the youngest person there - alongside the heads of China's biggest tech companies.
deep_cut_fact: As a first-year mechatronics student at Zhejiang Sci-Tech University he built his first small bipedal robot from about RMB 200 (~$30) of parts; his master's thesis robot at Shanghai University, the ~RMB 20,000 'XDog' (2015), won second prize at a Shanghai robot design contest and became Unitree's seed.
notes: Unitree lists no dedicated press email; 'Marketing: marketing@unitree.com' is the closest published media route. Since the 2026 IPO, an IR/board-secretary contact should also exist in exchange filings. XDog prize detail also in SCMP/Yahoo coverage (https://www.yahoo.com/news/meet-wang-xingxing-young-chinese-093000107.html).

name: James C. Kennedy
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Cox Enterprises; Chairman, James M. Cox Foundation
profile: Grandson of Cox founder James M. Cox. Joined the family company in 1972 and was chairman and CEO of Cox Enterprises from 1988, as it diversified into cable, autos (Cox Automotive) and media. Became chairman emeritus in 2022 when Alex Taylor succeeded him; still chairs the James M. Cox Foundation and champions sustainability.
interesting_fact: An avid conservationist, he chaired the Colorado Division of Wildlife Commission, was president of Wetlands America Trust (Ducks Unlimited), and in 2008 endowed a chair in waterfowl and wetlands conservation at Mississippi State University.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Cox in 1972 as a newspaper production assistant, then worked as reporter, copy editor and ad salesman. As president of Grand Junction Newspapers and publisher of the Grand Junction Daily Sentinel (from 1979), he worked the back shop as well as the newsroom floor and was nicknamed 'the New Kid'.
notes: Input lacked a source of wealth: it is a roughly 25% inherited stake in family-owned Cox Enterprises. Sustainability angle: he spoke at Fortune Brainstorm Green, and Cox runs a Cleantech Accelerator and Cox Conserves. Born 1947 in Honolulu; lives in Atlanta. He was inducted into the Technology Association of Georgia's Technology Hall of Fame in 2016.

name: Barry Lam
current_role: Founder and chairman, Quanta Computer (TWSE: 2382)
profile: Shanghai-born, Hong Kong-raised Barry Lam (林百里, b. 1949) studied electrical engineering at National Taiwan University, co-founded calculator maker Kinpo Electronics in 1973, then founded Quanta Computer in 1988 with C.C. Leung. Quanta became the world's largest notebook ODM and is now a leading AI-server maker for cloud giants including Meta and Google, a boom that made him Taiwan's richest person in 2023.
interesting_fact: He is one of Taiwan's foremost art patrons, owning 1,000+ works including more than 250 by Zhang Daqian, displayed in a museum of art and technology inside Quanta's headquarters; he also chairs the National Palace Museum advisory committee.
deep_cut_fact: Before Quanta he and NTU classmates (incl. Wen Shih-jen) left Sanai Electronics on 26 April 1973 to found Kinpo, which he built into the largest contract maker of handheld calculators; in 2003 he funded NTU's EE building 'Barry Lam Hall' (博理館) with an art gallery in its basement.
notes: Rarely gives interviews but appears at Computex/Quanta events; Quanta uses designated official spokespersons per its media relations policy (see ESG report). Strong fit for data-center/AI-server angle. Best route: Quanta corporate communications / IR via quantatw.com or MOPS filings.

name: Marijke Mars
current_role: Board member, Mars, Incorporated (fourth-generation family shareholder)
profile: One of four daughters of Forrest Mars Jr., she inherited roughly an 8% stake in Mars, Incorporated, the private candy and pet-care giant founded by her great-grandfather Frank Mars in 1911, when her father died in 2016. A Duke graduate, she has worked inside the Mars businesses and sits on the company's board. Mars closed its $35.9B acquisition of Kellanova in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Wikipedia gives her birthplace as Veghel in the Netherlands, home to one of the world's largest chocolate factories, which Mars built after scouting a continental European site in 1962.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Duke she started out as a regional manager at Kal Kan Foods, Mars's pet food company (later part of its petcare business), rather than in the candy side of the family firm.
notes: Very private; the Mars family rarely gives interviews. No personal channels found; any approach would have to go through Mars, Incorporated corporate communications. Veghel birthplace rests on a single Brabants Dagblad citation in Wikipedia.

name: Pamela Mars
current_role: Mars family ambassador to the Mars Petcare division; supervisory board member, Heineken N.V.
profile: Pamela Mars-Wright (b. 1960), a fourth-generation Mars heir and Vassar graduate, inherited ~8% of Mars, Inc. with her three sisters on Forrest Mars Jr.'s death in 2016. A company lifer since 1986, she chaired the Mars board in 2004-2008 and now represents the family in Mars Petcare (VCA, AniCura, Linnaeus); Mars closed its ~$36B Kellanova deal in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: She was appointed to the supervisory board of Dutch brewer Heineken in 2016, an unusual outside board seat for a member of the famously private Mars family.
deep_cut_fact: She started at Mars in 1986 as an operations supervisor, rose to plant director at a petcare factory and then manufacturing director of Mars Australia, before joining the board in 2001 and becoming chairman (2004-2008).
notes: Also known as Pamela Mars-Wright. Very private family; best route is Mars corporate communications. A 2015 mars.com piece quotes her: 'I want to leave a sustainable planet for my children' - sustainability is a natural hook. Mars media page was blocked (403) for me, so the specific email wasn't captured.

name: Valerie Mars
current_role: Board member, Ermenegildo Zegna NV, the Mars family office and Conservation International; recently retired SVP & Head of Corporate Development, Mars Inc.
profile: Fourth-generation Mars heir (b. 1959) who, like her three sisters, inherited ~8% of Mars when her father died in 2016. Joined Mars in 1992 and rose to SVP & head of corporate development (M&A, JVs, divestitures) before retiring; former director of Fiat Chrysler and Ahlstrom-Munksjo.
interesting_fact: She sits on the board of Conservation International (chairing its audit committee) and on Hakluyt's International Advisory Board, and leads projects preserving natural woodlands and shoreline as community spaces.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business she began her career at Manufacturers Hanover Trust and was a controller at boutique investment firm Whitman Heffernan Rhein; she also once sat on the board of NASDAQ-listed Celebrity Inc. Her motto on the Redefiners podcast: 'If you don't tell your story, somebody else will.'
notes: Forbes bio's 'VP corporate development' is outdated - Russell Reynolds (Oct 2025) says she recently retired. Mars family is famously private; no published personal/office contact found. Mars corporate media page (mars.com) blocks scripted access; route via Mars corporate communications or Conservation International. Rare podcast appearance: Russell Reynolds 'Redefiners' S5E12.

name: Pei Zhenhua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Tianhua New Energy (formerly TA&A Ultra Clean Technology, SZ:300390)
profile: Born 1959 in Yixing, Jiangsu, Pei founded Suzhou TA&A (cleanroom/antistatic products) in 1997, later pivoting it into lithium battery materials as Tianhua New Energy. Most of his fortune comes from an early stake in battery giant CATL held via Ningbo United Innovation; in 2025 he sold a 12.95% Tianhua stake to CATL, making it a major shareholder.
interesting_fact: In 2015 the Ningbo United Innovation partnership bought 15% of CATL's predecessor for RMB 89 million; Pei was its biggest LP (79.9%). A decade later it was selling CATL shares worth tens of billions of yuan.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur, Pei worked at the Jiangsu Textile Research Institute, first in its knitting research lab and then in its new-products business department, before founding TA&A in November 1997.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed. Best route is Tianhua New Energy's board secretary office (IR email from its 2026 interim report). Spouse Rong Jianfen is co-controller of Tianhua.

name: Carrie Perrodo
current_role: Owner (with family) of Perenco, the family-owned Anglo-French oil & gas producer; son François Perrodo is chairman
profile: Born Ka Yee Wong, a former top model who married Perenco founder Hubert Perrodo in 1974; she inherited the company when he died in a 2006 ski-touring accident. Perenco is one of the world's largest family-owned oil producers (Gabon, Cameroon, Peru, Vietnam, UK North Sea etc.). Son François chairs it; daughter Nathalie oversees the family's Bordeaux wine estates. She is reported to live in London.
interesting_fact: A 1970s top model, she met Hubert Perrodo while he was travelling the world in search of oil and gas; she also launched her own agency, Carrie's Models, which she later sold but which is still active in Singapore.
deep_cut_fact: Her Chinese name is 黃嘉兒; she was born in Hong Kong and moved to Singapore to pursue modelling before founding Carrie's Models. Her late husband Hubert was also a polo player and noted art collector.
notes: Extremely private; no personal public profile or social accounts. Forbes says 'native of Singapore' while Wikipedia says Hong Kong-born, moved to Singapore. Best route is via Perenco's PR agency Celicourt or pitching son François Perrodo (chairman).

name: Terrence Pegula
current_role: Owner, CEO & President, Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres (Pegula Sports & Entertainment); runs JKLM Energy, Pittsburgh
profile: Penn State petroleum & natural gas engineering grad who founded Appalachian driller East Resources in 1983 and sold its assets to Royal Dutch Shell in 2010 (~$4.7B). He then bought the Sabres (2011) and Bills (2014) with wife Kim, and still produces Pennsylvania gas through JKLM Energy, staffed largely by ex-East Resources people.
interesting_fact: The Pegulas' $102M gift to Penn State built Pegula Ice Arena and created Division I hockey there, helping trigger the formation of the Big Ten hockey conference.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Carbondale, PA (Scranton Prep '69), he entered Penn State as a math major; his first job was with Getty Oil in Victoria, Texas, and Felmont Oil brought him to Olean, NY in 1975. He started East Resources in 1983 with $7,500 borrowed from family and friends.
notes: Best route is probably via Pegula Sports & Entertainment / Bills communications, or JKLM Energy (his active gas company) for an energy angle. Family business office in Boca Raton, FL. Avoid Kim Pegula's health as a topic.

name: Randa Duncan Williams
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, Enterprise Products Partners (general partner) and Chairman of EPCO / Enterprise Products Company
profile: Daughter of Enterprise Products co-founder Dan Duncan (d. 2010); the only one of four sibling heirs active in the pipeline business, which runs 50,000+ miles of pipelines plus Gulf Coast processing and storage. Joined in 1994, was CEO 2001, and has been non-executive chairman since 2013; also owns Texas Monthly.
interesting_fact: Before joining the family business she practised law for about six years (from 1988) on toxic-tort and property-liability cases; in 2019 she bought Texas Monthly magazine.
deep_cut_fact: A Houston Museum of Natural Science trustee since 1995 and former board chair, she also served on the board of the Manned Space Flight Education Foundation (the nonprofit behind Space Center Houston).

public_contacts.value: rrainey@eprod.com (Rick Rainey, Media Relations, Enterprise Products; tel (713) 381-3635)

notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Enterprise media relations (Rick Rainey) or via Texas Monthly ownership. IR site blocks automated fetches; contact emails taken from 2026 press releases as indexed by search.

name: Dannine Avara
current_role: Private investor; co-heir to the Duncan family's controlling stake in Enterprise Products Partners
profile: Dannine Avara (nee Duncan, b. 1964) is one of four children of the late Dan Duncan, who co-founded Houston pipeline giant Enterprise Products in 1968 with $10,000 and a truck. She inherited her stake when he died in 2010; Enterprise now owns 50,000+ miles of gas, oil and petrochemical pipelines. She keeps a very low profile and lives in Houston.
interesting_fact: Her father built Enterprise Products from a $10,000, one-truck propane business in 1968 into one of the largest US midstream companies; he was once Houston's richest man.

public_contacts.value: rrainey@eprod.com (Rick Rainey, Media Relations, Enterprise Products)

notes: Very private; no public role, interviews or social accounts found. Sister Randa Duncan Williams is the only sibling on Enterprise's board and is the family's public face; company media relations is the only published route.

name: Milane Frantz
current_role: Investor; heir and shareholder in Enterprise Products Partners (Duncan family); director, Duncan Family Foundation
profile: Milane Duncan Frantz (b. 1970) is one of four children of Dan Duncan, who founded Houston pipeline giant Enterprise Products Partners in 1968 and took it public in 1998. She inherited a stake after his 2010 death but is not active in the business (sister Randa Duncan Williams is). She lives in Houston, sits on the Hermann Park Conservancy board and is a director of the Duncan Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: Because Dan Duncan died in 2010, the one year the US federal estate tax was temporarily repealed, his heirs became the first American billionaire heirs to pay no estate tax since it was enacted.
deep_cut_fact: She studied at the University of Houston, and her family's Duncan Family Foundation is credited as a leadership donor to Houston's Hermann Park Conservancy, whose board she sits on.
notes: Very private, low public profile; no personal channels found. Best indirect route may be via Enterprise Products Partners (Houston) or the Hermann Park Conservancy. Avoid mentioning her late husband.

name: Zhu Yiming
current_role: Chairman, GigaDevice Semiconductor (603986.SH / HK) and Chairman, ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT)
profile: Zhu Yiming founded GigaDevice in Silicon Valley in 2005 and moved it to Beijing, building a NOR-flash and MCU champion listed in Shanghai in 2016 (and Hong Kong in 2026). With the Hefei government he set up CXMT, now China's largest DRAM maker, which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on July 27, 2026, lifting his fortune above $10bn.
interesting_fact: CXMT is China's leading bid to compete with Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron in DRAM; Zhu stepped back from GigaDevice's CEO role to lead the Hefei memory project. He is credited with 50+ patents.
deep_cut_fact: Born 1972 in Funing County, Jiangsu, he studied physics at Tsinghua and moonlighted as a programmer for Zhongguancun firms. He went to Stony Brook for a physics PhD (where Nobel laureate C.N. Yang taught) but switched to an EE master's to pursue Silicon Valley.
notes: Low public profile in Western media; outreach best via GigaDevice board office / IR (Chinese-language). info@cxmt.com is CXMT's general corporate inbox, not a personal channel.

name: John C. Malone
current_role: Chairman Emeritus and strategic adviser, Liberty Media (since Jan 1, 2026); major shareholder across Liberty companies
profile: John Malone, the 'Cable Cowboy', ran Tele-Communications Inc. (TCI) from 1973 to 1996 and built it into a cable giant later sold to AT&T. He then assembled the Liberty empire: Liberty Media (Formula 1, Live Nation stake), Liberty Global, QVC Group, plus big stakes in Charter and Warner Bros. Discovery. He stepped down as chairman of Liberty Media and Liberty Global at the start of 2026 but remains a key shareholder and adviser.
interesting_fact: From 2011 to 2021 Malone was the largest private landowner in the United States, with about 2.2 million acres of ranches and forests.
deep_cut_fact: Malone started his career in 1963 at Bell Labs doing economic planning and R&D, then earned a Johns Hopkins Ph.D. in operations research. He gave $60M to his old high school, Hopkins School in New Haven, for new buildings. One of them, Heath Commons, is named after his favorite Hopkins teacher.

public_contacts.value: Liberty Media investor relations: Shane Kleinstein, 720-875-5432 (corporate IR line)

notes: He is 85. He still appears at Liberty's annual investor meeting (Q&A) and occasionally on CNBC, but has no social accounts. The Liberty Media corporate office (Englewood, Colorado) is the only route.

name: Robert Duggan
current_role: Executive Chairman and Co-CEO, Summit Therapeutics (Nasdaq: SMMT); director and largest individual shareholder of Pulse Biosciences
profile: Serial entrepreneur and investor (b.1944, Oakland) who ran surgical-robotics pioneer Computer Motion until its 2003 merger with Intuitive Surgical, then became a billionaire turning Pharmacyclics around; its cancer drug Imbruvica led to a $21B sale to AbbVie in 2015. Since 2020 he has led Summit Therapeutics, developing the oncology antibody ivonescimab.
interesting_fact: He has built companies across wildly different fields: Communication Machinery Corp was among the first companies to sell Ethernet node processors, and his government IT firm GTSI was an early e-commerce pioneer before he moved into surgical robots and cancer drugs.
deep_cut_fact: In 1976 he was a founding partner in Paradise Bakery & Café, whose fresh-baked cookies were distributed to McDonald's, KFC and Disney World; his very first business was mowing lawns as a teenager to pay for college.
notes: Gave UCSB a 2009 science commencement speech and credits a UCSB corporate-finance class/mentor Herbert Kay. Avoid religion (Scientology donor) and his son's death. Summit faces some 2026 financial/legal headlines; keep outreach on entrepreneurship.

name: Charlie Mills
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Medline Inc. (Northfield, Illinois; Nasdaq: MDLN)
profile: Charlie Mills is chairman of Medline, the medical-supplies maker and distributor his father Jim and uncle Jon founded in 1966 from family roots going back to 1910. He was CEO for 26 years (1997-2023), sold a majority stake to Blackstone, Carlyle and Hellman & Friedman in a 2021 buyout valuing Medline above $30B, and the family still owned about 18% when Medline IPO'd on Nasdaq in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Medline's December 2025 Nasdaq IPO ended its first trading day with a market cap above $55 billion, and Mills's extended family includes four other billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he spent two years as a sales rep at IBM; he then started at Medline in 1986 as a sales representative and worked through sales management and VP of marketing and manufacturing roles before becoming CEO. He holds a B.S. in engineering and an MBA from Cornell.

public_contacts.value: srubenstein@medline.com (Stacy Rubenstein, Senior Manager, Public Relations)

notes: Low public profile; best route is Medline PR. Company now run by non-family CEO Jim Boyle. Wikipedia and IR site differ on when he became chair (2018 vs 2023).

name: Daniel Tsai
current_role: Chairman, Fubon Group; Chairman of Taiwan Mobile, momo.com and Fubon Bank (Hong Kong); Director, Fubon Financial Holding
profile: Daniel M. Tsai (蔡明忠), a Georgetown LL.M. and NTU law graduate, joined his father's Fubon business in 1981 and with brother Richard built Fubon into Taiwan's largest corporate group (NT$14T+ assets), spanning banking, insurance, securities, Taiwan Mobile and e-commerce platform momo. He chaired Fubon Financial 2001-2018 and now chairs Fubon Group.
interesting_fact: Fubon invests over NT$500 million a year in Taiwanese pro basketball and baseball, and its Run For Green initiative has planted 100,000+ trees; Tsai himself has run the Wan Jin Shi Marathon as group chairman.
deep_cut_fact: He started university as a Tunghai business student who swept leaves as part of its labor-education programme, then transferred to NTU law on his father's advice; he now teaches EMBA classes at Tunghai as a chair professor, telling students 'If the mountain won't move, change the road.'
notes: Taiwan Mobile chairmanship relevant to telecom/data-center angle. Fubon PR inbox (pr@fubon.com) is the best published route.

name: Wang Weixiu
current_role: Honorary chairman and actual controller, Zhongji Innolight (中际旭创), Shandong, China (stepped down as chairman in 2023)
profile: Wang Weixiu (王伟修) spent two decades building a Longkou, Shandong maker of motor-winding equipment, listed in 2012 as Zhongji Equipment. In 2016 he bought optical-module maker Suzhou Innolight for RMB 2.8B and handed operations to its founder Liu Sheng; riding AI data-center demand, Zhongji Innolight became the world's No.1 optical-transceiver supplier and passed RMB 1 trillion market cap in 2026.
interesting_fact: At 66 he made the biggest bet of his career: in 2016 his small equipment maker paid RMB 2.8B for Suzhou Innolight, with Wang personally putting in RMB 284M; that asset grew past RMB 760B in market value by April 2026 as a key optical-module supplier to AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: His whole business began in 1987 when he put up RMB 230,000 to start the Longkou Zhenhua Electrical Special Equipment Factory, which made motor-winding machinery — the direct ancestor of today's Zhongji Innolight.
notes: Aged ~76, low profile, no English-language interviews found; son Wang Xiaodong is a director/EVP. Day-to-day leadership is chairman Liu Sheng. Very relevant to data centers (800G/1.6T optical transceivers for AI clusters). Contact is company-level only.

name: Brothers Kwok
current_role: Group entry (Forbes 1996) for the Kwok brothers of Sun Hung Kai Properties: Raymond Kwok is SHKP Chairman and MD; Walter Kwok died in 2018
profile: This 1996 Forbes listing covers Walter, Thomas and Raymond Kwok, sons of Sun Hung Kai Properties founder Kwok Tak-seng, who inherited and expanded Hong Kong's largest property developer. Walter died in Oct 2018. Raymond Kwok remains Chairman and Managing Director of SHKP (as of 2026) and also chairs SUNeVision, Hong Kong's largest data-centre operator.
interesting_fact: SHKP's tech arm SUNeVision (chaired by Raymond Kwok) is Hong Kong's largest carrier- and cloud-neutral data-centre provider, a direct link to the podcast's data-centre theme.
notes: Not one person, so I kept the entry minimal. Walter Kwok died on 20 Oct 2018. Thomas Kwok left SHKP leadership in 2014 and is best avoided as a contact. If the journalist wants one person, Raymond Kwok (SHKP and SUNeVision chairman) is the relevant, data-centre-linked figure and could be profiled separately.

name: Gayle Benson
current_role: Owner and CEO, New Orleans Saints (NFL) and New Orleans Pelicans (NBA)
profile: New Orleans native Gayle Benson, a former interior designer, married Saints/Pelicans owner Tom Benson in 2004 and inherited both teams when he died in March 2018. She runs them as owner and CEO, contributed $180M to the $560M Caesars Superdome overhaul, sits on NFL and NBA league committees and founded thoroughbred stable GMB Racing in 2014.
interesting_fact: She contributed $180M of the five-year, $560M Caesars Superdome transformation that debuted for the 2024 season and Super Bowl LIX. The Superdome has sold out on season tickets every year since 2006, with a 73,000+ waiting list.
deep_cut_fact: Under her, the Saints became the first and only NFL club granted marketing rights in France (2023), citing Louisiana's French ties. That led the NFL to pick the Saints for its first-ever regular-season game in Paris on Oct 25, 2026. She also co-chairs the NFL Legislative Committee (appointed 2025).

name: Ravi Jaipuria
current_role: Chairman, RJ Corp; Chairman, Varun Beverages Ltd (PepsiCo bottler) and promoter of Devyani International
profile: Ravi Kant Jaipuria (b. 1954), India's 'cola king', joined the family Coca-Cola bottling business in 1985 and switched to PepsiCo after a 1987 family split left him one plant. Varun Beverages is now one of PepsiCo's largest bottlers outside the U.S. His Devyani International (KFC, Pizza Hut) agreed in Jan 2026 to merge with Sapphire Foods.

deep_cut_fact: PepsiCo named Jaipuria its 'Bottler of the Year' in 1999, and he received the award from former U.S. President George H.W. Bush.

name: Magdalena Martullo-Blocher
current_role: CEO and Executive Vice Chair, EMS-Chemie Holding AG; Swiss National Councillor (SVP, Graubünden) and SVP vice president
profile: Magdalena Martullo-Blocher (b. 1969) has run Swiss polymers and specialty chemicals group EMS-Chemie since 2004, when her father Christoph Blocher joined the Federal Council and sold his stake to his four children. An HSG graduate formerly at Johnson & Johnson and Rivella, she has been an SVP National Councillor since 2015.

deep_cut_fact: In a 2026 SRF radio pairing with Schwinger king Christian Stucki (shoe size 51), she joked 'Ich lebe nicht auf so grossem Fuss' - she wears size 36 - and said her wealth keeps her grounded because it is really shares of labs and plants worldwide with practical problems to solve.

name: Scott Duncan
current_role: Private investor; heir and co-owner (with three sisters) of a controlling family stake in Enterprise Products Partners (Houston midstream pipelines)
profile: Scott Daniel Duncan (b. 1983) is the youngest child of Dan Duncan, co-founder of pipeline giant Enterprise Products Partners, who died in 2010. He inherited roughly a quarter of the family's stake (about $3.1bn at the time) and is described as a Houston-based private investor; his sister Randa Duncan Williams chairs Enterprise Products.
interesting_fact: Because the US federal estate tax lapsed for the single year 2010, the Duncan heirs received their father's multibillion-dollar estate with no estate tax - the first American billionaire estate to pass untaxed since the tax was enacted.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes lists his education as Houston Community College - unusually modest for one of America's youngest multibillionaires.
notes: Very private; holds no executive or board role at Enterprise Products and has no public social or press presence found. Family philanthropy (Dan L. Duncan Foundation) is led by sister Randa Duncan Williams. Any approach would likely have to go through the family/Enterprise Products corporate office; no published personal channel.

name: Ernest Garcia III
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, President & CEO, Carvana Co. (NYSE: CVNA), Tempe, Arizona
profile: Ernie Garcia III co-founded Carvana in 2012 (with Ryan Keeton and Ben Huston) as a DriveTime subsidiary to sell used cars online, famous for its multi-storey car 'vending machines'. Carvana IPO'd in 2017, survived a near-collapse in 2022-23 and is now posting record results (197k retail units in Q2 2026, +38% YoY) after a 5-for-1 stock split approved in March 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2018 Garcia gave $35 million of his own Carvana stock to employees to celebrate the company selling its 100,000th car.
deep_cut_fact: Before cars, Garcia earned a Stanford degree in Management Science & Engineering (2005) and started as an associate in the Principal Transactions Group at RBS Greenwich Capital; he joined his father's DriveTime in 2007, serving as treasurer and in quantitative analytics before founding Carvana.
notes: Contacts from Carvana 2026 release contact blocks (verified via search index; site blocks automated fetch). Carvana has faced short-seller reports and litigation - avoid in outreach. Father Ernest Garcia II is the largest shareholder.

name: James Goodnight
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SAS Institute (Cary, North Carolina), CEO since 1976
profile: Jim Goodnight co-founded analytics software firm SAS in 1976 with John Sall and NC State colleagues, spinning out a USDA-funded project to analyze agricultural data. CEO for 50 years, he has kept SAS private and reinvested heavily in R&D as it moved into AI and cloud (SAS Viya); long-discussed IPO plans keep slipping.
interesting_fact: Goodnight considered taking SAS public in 1999 at the dot-com peak but resisted and avoided the crash; SAS is famous for perks like on-site day care, a pharmacy and sports leagues, and has ranked No. 1 on Fortune's best-places-to-work list.
deep_cut_fact: Before SAS, he worked at a company building electronic equipment for the ground stations that communicated with Apollo space capsules; the high staff turnover he saw there shaped SAS's famously employee-friendly culture. As a kid he worked in his father's hardware store.
notes: Age 83 (b. Jan 1943). Route via SAS corporate communications/newsroom. Data/AI angle fits; SAS co-authored HBR piece 'Managing for Creativity' with Richard Florida.

name: Heinrich Deichmann
current_role: Chairman of the Management Board / head of Deichmann SE, Essen (family-owned footwear retailer)
profile: Heinrich Deichmann (b. 1962) runs Deichmann SE, Europe's largest shoe retailer, founded by his grandfather in Essen in 1913 and still wholly family-owned. He joined in 1989 and succeeded his father Heinz-Horst Deichmann as company head in 1999, expanding it across Europe and beyond. In 2026 former Müller CEO Günther Helm joined as managing director.
interesting_fact: Deichmann largely funds 'wortundtat', a Christian social-mission aid organisation he leads, whose largest programmes are in Tanzania.
deep_cut_fact: From 1984 he studied not only economics but also history, theology and philosophy at the University of Cologne before joining the family firm in 1989; Handelsblatt profiled how the Bible guides his leadership.
notes: Exact title varies (CEO / Chairman of Management Board / Verwaltungsratsvorsitzender) amid 2026 leadership changes. Route via central press mailbox.

name: Thomas Strungmann
current_role: Co-owner (with twin brother Andreas) of family office ATHOS, major shareholder of BioNTech
profile: Thomas Strüngmann (b. 1950), a business economist, and his identical twin Andreas, a physician, sold their father's Durachemie in 1986 and founded generics maker Hexal, selling it with Eon Labs to Novartis for $7.5B in 2005. They then put ~$180M of startup capital into BioNTech (2008), whose Covid-19 vaccine made them among Germany's richest; their ATHOS office invests in biotech.
interesting_fact: The twins endowed the Ernst Strüngmann Institute, a Frankfurt neuroscience institute set up with the Max Planck Society in 2008, with more than €200M, and in 2007 founded the Ernst Strüngmann Forum conference series - both named for their father.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a doctorate in economics (Dr. rer. pol.) with a dissertation on the prescribing behaviour of office-based doctors ('Das Verordnungsverhalten des niedergelassenen Arztes'), and was already selling his father's company's drugs while still a student.
notes: Extremely private; ATHOS family office (Munich/Holzkirchen area) has no published contact found. BioNTech press/IR is an indirect route; ATHOS executive Helmut Jeggle chairs BioNTech's supervisory board. ESI press email is for the institute the brothers fund, not for him personally.

name: Andreas Strungmann
current_role: Co-owner (with twin brother Thomas) of the Strüngmann family office ATHOS / Santo Holding, BioNTech's largest shareholder
profile: Andreas Strüngmann, a physician, and his identical twin Thomas founded generics maker Hexal in 1986 and sold it with Eon Labs to Novartis for $7.5B in 2005. Through their family office ATHOS they were BioNTech's founding backers in 2008 and became billionaires many times over when its mRNA COVID vaccine succeeded. They also own stakes in Formycon and other biotech firms.
interesting_fact: The twins put more than €200 million into the Ernst Strüngmann Institute, a private cognitive-neuroscience institute in Frankfurt run with the Max Planck Society and named after their father; they also founded the Ernst Strüngmann Forum (2007).
deep_cut_fact: Andreas did his medical clerkship in South Africa and stayed on there for a time as a doctor before joining the family business. Their father's small firm Durachemie launched Germany's first generic antibiotic in 1969; the twins joined it in 1979 and sold it for DM100M before founding Hexal.
notes: Born 16 Feb 1950, Mülheim an der Ruhr. Very private; the brothers rarely speak publicly and their family office has no public website. The family office is run by Helmut Jeggle (also BioNTech supervisory-board chair), the practical route for any approach.

name: Issam Al Zahid
current_role: Chairman, Alzahid Group of Companies / Al Zahid Group Holding, Al Khobar, Saudi Arabia (per Gulf Business; not confirmed on current group site)
profile: Sheikh Issam Alzahid heads the Alzahid Group, founded in 1951 as Alzahid Construction in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province. It grew from roads and bridges into mining, logistics, oil & gas, IT, medical, agriculture and solar, and runs as a family office in Al Khobar. Not the Jeddah-based Zahid Group. Little recent public info.
interesting_fact: Alzahid Construction was tapped in the 1950s to build Saudi Arabia's first coast guard stations, and by 1958 was building bridges, tunnels and flyovers that still form part of the kingdom's basic transport infrastructure.

name: Rajiv Singh
current_role: Chairman, DLF Limited (India's largest listed real-estate developer)
profile: Rajiv Singh, son of DLF chairman emeritus K.P. Singh, joined DLF's board in 1981 and became chairman in June 2020. He has led DLF's shift toward rented commercial offices and malls (DLF Cyber City, the DLF Cyber City Developers annuity arm) alongside luxury housing in Gurugram, where DLF essentially built the modern city.
interesting_fact: Per DLF, he grew the company's rental (annuity) business from INR 15.5 million in 2007 to INR 29,000 million in 2019, and DLF delivered over 10.4 million sq m of space after its 2007 IPO.

name: Morris Chang Chung-Mou
current_role: Founder and retired chairman, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC); retired 2018
profile: Chinese-born, US-educated engineer (Harvard, MIT, Stanford PhD) who spent 25 years at Texas Instruments, then led Taiwan's ITRI and in 1987 founded TSMC, the world's first dedicated chip foundry. His wealth comes from his TSMC stake. Retired in 2018; published the second volume of his autobiography in Nov 2024 and now rarely appears in public (age ~95).
interesting_fact: His 2024 memoir reveals he once asked Nvidia's Jensen Huang to become TSMC's CEO, and Huang turned him down.
deep_cut_fact: After failing MIT's doctoral qualifying exam twice, he left without a PhD; TI later sponsored him to Stanford, where he finished his PhD in about two years (1964) with a thesis on optical absorption and photoluminescence of doped GaAs.

Only route is via TSMC PR; interview very unlikely. MIT-qualifying-exam detail is from his own 1998 memoir via Wikipedia.

name: Hans-Adam II
current_role: Reigning Prince of Liechtenstein (head of state; day-to-day duties delegated to Hereditary Prince Alois since 2004); head of the princely family that owns LGT Group
profile: Born in Zurich in 1945, Hans-Adam II became Liechtenstein's sovereign in 1989 after serving as regent from 1984. A St. Gallen business graduate, he restructured the princely family's assets into a modern holding, including LGT, the private bank and asset manager wholly owned by the Princely House, plus forestry, agriculture and the Princely Collections of art.

current_role: Founder, Chairman & Executive Director, Sunac China Holdings (HKEX: 1918)
profile: Sun Hongbin (孙宏斌; Hurun spells 'Hongbing'), born 1963 in Shanxi, founded Tianjin-based developer Sunac in 2003 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2010; it became one of China's largest developers. name: Tilman J. Fertitta
current_role: U.S. Ambassador to Italy and San Marino (since May 2025); owner of Landry's, Golden Nugget and the Houston Rockets

He bought the Houston Rockets for $2.2B in 2017, starred in CNBC's 'Billion Dollar Buyer', became Wynn Resorts' top shareholder and in 2025 U.S. ambassador to Italy.

name: Mikhail Prokhorov
current_role: Owner, ONEXIM Group (private investment holding); Russian-Israeli investor

He owned the Brooklyn Nets 2010-2019, ran for Russian president in 2012, and took Israeli citizenship in 2022.

name: John Paulson
current_role: Founder & President, Paulson & Co. (now a family office); director of Bausch Health and Bausch + Lomb
profile: Queens-born NYU valedictorian and Harvard MBA (Baker Scholar) who worked at BCG and Bear Stearns before founding Paulson & Co. in 1994. His 2007 credit-default-swap bet against subprime mortgages made him a Wall Street legend; the firm converted to a family office in 2020. He now invests in holdings such as Bausch, gold/antimony miner Perpetua Resources (Idaho) and Puerto Rico real estate, and is a major philanthropist.

name: Jay Chaudhry
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Zscaler (Nasdaq: ZS)
profile: Jay Chaudhry grew up in a Himalayan village without electricity, came to the US in 1980 for graduate school in Cincinnati, and worked at IBM, NCR and Unisys before founding SecureIT in 1996 with his wife Jyoti's and his savings. After selling four security startups he founded cloud-security firm Zscaler in 2008 (IPO 2018), which he still leads as CEO.
