deep_cut_fact: In Nov 2024 he and Jyoti gave $4M to the University of Cincinnati to create the Chaudhry Family Scholarship Fund for first-generation, Pell-eligible students in UC's Gen-1 residential house; he holds UC engineering degrees ('82, '83) and an MBA ('86).
notes: Active public speaker (Zenith Live) and LinkedIn poster; frames Zscaler as AI/zero-trust security - relevant to data-center/AI security discussions. Lives in Nevada. Route via Zscaler PR (press@zscaler.com).

name: Sun Piaoyang
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Hengrui Pharmaceuticals (SSE: 600276; HKEX: 1276)
profile: Sun Piaoyang (孙飘扬, b. 1958, Jinhu, Jiangsu) joined state-run Lianyungang Pharmaceutical Factory as a technician in 1982 and became its head in 1990 at 32. He turned it into Hengrui, one of China's largest makers of oncology and anti-infection drugs and its leading innovative-drug developer. Hengrui listed in Shanghai in 2000 and added a $1.3B Hong Kong listing in 2025.
interesting_fact: Hengrui's ancestor, Lianyungang Pharmaceutical Factory (est. 1970), was a tiny plant making red and purple antiseptic tinctures, with book profits of only about RMB 80,000 when Sun was called back to rescue it. It is now one of Asia's most valuable drugmakers.
deep_cut_fact: A 1978-entry alumnus of China Pharmaceutical University (medicinal chemistry), Sun gave his alma mater RMB 150M in 2026: RMB 100M cash plus RMB 50M in Hengrui shares. It is the largest single alumnus gift in the university's history and arrived ahead of its 90th anniversary; he had first donated RMB 20M via Hengrui in 2016.
notes: Very low media profile, with almost no interviews. Contact via the board secretary's office (IR email), preferably in Chinese. Biographical details come from Chinese financial media; avoid discussing family members.

name: Robert F. Smith
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Vista Equity Partners; founder and president, Fund II Foundation
profile: Denver-born chemical engineer (b. 1962; Cornell, Columbia MBA) who worked at Goodyear, Air Products and Kraft, then in tech M&A at Goldman Sachs before founding Vista Equity Partners in 2000. Vista invests exclusively in enterprise software and manages ~$100B. He is a major philanthropist (Student Freedom Initiative for HBCU students, Morehouse 2019 debt pledge) and chairs Carnegie Hall.

name: German Khan
current_role: Co-founder, Alfa Group and LetterOne (resigned from LetterOne board March 2022 after EU/UK sanctions)
profile: Kyiv-born (1961) Russian-Israeli billionaire who co-founded commodities trader Alfa-Eco with college friends Mikhail Fridman and Alexei Kuzmichev in 1989, building Alfa Group. notes: Under EU/UK sanctions (2022) and based in Moscow; outreach from a Western podcast may raise sanctions/compliance issues. His personal site lists philanthropy (Babyn Yar memorial, European Jewish Fund, Genesis Philanthropy Group).

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Atlassian (Nasdaq: TEAM); owner of Grok Ventures and Sun Cable
profile: Cannon-Brookes co-founded Atlassian with Scott Farquhar in 2002 straight out of UNSW, funding it on credit cards and growing Jira/Confluence without a traditional sales force; he has been sole CEO since 2024. Through Grok Ventures he is one of Australia's biggest climate investors: he bought solar-and-cable export project Sun Cable in 2023, holds a stake in AGL Energy and pledged A$1.5B to climate by 2030.

notes: Very accessible and outspoken on energy transition; strong fit for energy/data-center podcast (Sun Cable, AGL, data-center power demand). Birthday 17 Nov (1979). Avoid the 2023 separation from his wife and the Forrest falling-out as topics.

name: David Shaw
current_role: Chief Scientist, D. E. Shaw Research; founder of D. E. Shaw & Co.
profile: Former Columbia computer-science professor who founded quant hedge fund D. E. Shaw & Co. in 1988 after running technology for Morgan Stanley's automated trading group; the firm manages over $70B and alumni include Jeff Bezos. Since 2001 he has focused full time on computational biochemistry at D. E. Shaw Research, building the Anton supercomputers for protein molecular-dynamics simulation.

deep_cut_fact: As a Columbia assistant professor in the early 1980s he led the NON-VON ('non-von Neumann') massively parallel supercomputer project, a tree of processing elements for fast database search; after his Stanford PhD he had also founded Stanford Systems Corporation.
notes: Rarely gives media interviews; a science/computing angle (Anton, custom silicon, HPC) is the best hook for a data-center podcast. D. E. Shaw Research general inquiries address is the most relevant channel.

current_role: Co-owner (with family) of PhosAgro; no formal board role since stepping down as deputy chairman in March 2022

name: Eike Batista
current_role: Founder/promoter of Brazil Renewable X (BRXe) 'supercana' ethanol/SAF venture; former chairman of EBX Group
profile: Brazilian entrepreneur (b. 1956) who built EBX Group (OGX oil, MPX energy, MMX mining, LLX/Porto do Açu, OSX) and was ranked world's 7th-richest in 2012 (~$35B) before the group collapsed in 2013. Since 2025 he has been promoting BRXe, a high-yield 'supercana' sugarcane project for ethanol and sustainable aviation fuel near Porto do Açu.
interesting_fact: Before oil, he made his first fortune in gold: from 1980-2000 he put into operation eight gold mines in Brazil and Canada plus a silver mine in Chile, becoming CEO of Montreal-listed TVX Gold at age 29.
deep_cut_fact: He is a former offshore powerboat champion: in 2006 he set the record for the 220-nautical-mile Santos-Rio de Janeiro course (3h01m47s) in his boat 'Spirit of Brazil'. As a student in Aachen he sold insurance door-to-door, which he credits as formative.
notes: Sensitive history: EBX collapse, 2017-19 corruption convictions/arrests, ongoing creditor litigation (2026). Avoid these in outreach. Brazilian press credits an Instagram @realeikebatista but not verified here; he historically used X/Twitter as his main channel. No published office/press email found.

name: Tsai Ming-kai
current_role: Chairman, MediaTek Inc. (Taiwan fabless chip designer)
profile: Taiwanese engineer (b. 1950) who spun MediaTek out of UMC's consumer/multimedia chip unit in 1997 and built it into one of the world's largest fabless chip designers (smartphone SoCs, Wi-Fi, TV chips). Still chairman, he is steering MediaTek into AI edge-to-cloud silicon, including data-center ASIC work.
interesting_fact: In 2023 he received the IEEE Robert N. Noyce Medal for contributions to the semiconductor industry, one of the field's top honours.
deep_cut_fact: Before UMC he spent seven years as an IC design manager at ITRI's Electronics Research & Service Organization (ERSO), the government lab that seeded Taiwan's chip industry; he holds an MSEE from the University of Cincinnati.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Route via MediaTek corporate PR (pr@mediatek.com appears on MediaTek press releases syndicated via PR Newswire/technode). Contact form has a 'Media & Public Relations' option.

name: Leonid Fedun
current_role: Private investor; co-founder and former vice president of Lukoil (retired 2022)
profile: Kyiv-born former Soviet army colonel and sociology lecturer who joined Vagit Alekperov in 1987 and helped build and privatize Lukoil, becoming vice president and holding a near-10% stake. Both he and Alekperov stepped down from Lukoil in 2022; he also sold his FC Spartak Moscow stake to Lukoil that year.
interesting_fact: As president and co-owner of FC Spartak Moscow he said he invested nearly $1 billion in the club and built its Lukoil-backed stadium (Otkritie/Lukoil Arena), which hosted 2018 World Cup matches; in 2021 he bid about GBP 400m for Wolverhampton Wanderers.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in the Baikonur cosmodrome town where his father was a military surgeon; earned a 1984 PhD on army morale and public opinion among servicemen, and met Alekperov after giving a Znanie society lecture in Kogalym in 1987.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contacts found. Retired from Lukoil in 2022 and widely labelled an oligarch; check Western sanctions status before any outreach. Lukoil corporate press office is the only institutional route but he no longer holds a role there.

name: Zhao Baoju
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner of ENN Group (with husband Wang Yusuo); no current listed-board role found
profile: Zhao Baoju co-founded ENN Group (Xinao) in Langfang, Hebei, with her husband Wang Yusuo; it grew from local gas distribution into one of China's largest private natural-gas and clean-energy groups (ENN Energy, ENN Natural Gas). She served as a non-executive director of ENN-group listed companies until about 2014 and remains a co-owner of the group's holding companies.

name: Mohammed Al Amoudi
current_role: Owner/chairman, MIDROC (MIDROC Investment Group Ethiopia and MIDROC international companies); former owner of Corral Petroleum Holdings (Preem)
profile: Ethiopian-born Saudi billionaire (b. 1946) who made his fortune in Saudi construction (MIDROC won the contract for Saudi Arabia's underground strategic oil storage in 1988) and then bought refineries in Sweden (Preem) and Morocco. He is Ethiopia's largest foreign investor; in 2025 he agreed to sell Corral Petroleum/Preem to Switzerland's VARO Energy (completion reported 2025-26).
interesting_fact: Through MIDROC he is Ethiopia's largest individual foreign investor, with interests spanning Ethiopia's only gold exporter (Lega Dembi mine), cement, steel, a tyre maker, agriculture and the Addis Ababa Sheraton; his companies employ 70,000+ people.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he donated 10 million birr (~US$500k) to the proposed Ethiopian National Coffee Museum in the Kaffa Zone, the birthplace of coffee; he also fully funded the King Abdullah Institute for Nanotechnology at King Saud University.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Was detained in Saudi Arabia's 2017-19 anti-corruption sweep (avoid in outreach). Preem sale to VARO Energy (VAROPreem) means he is no longer in Swedish refining. Best route is via MIDROC Investment Group PR in Addis Ababa.

name: Jeffrey Hildebrand
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman, Hilcorp Energy Company (also Harvest Midstream, JDH Capital); Chair, Texas Parks and Wildlife Commission
profile: Texas-born geologist/petroleum engineer (UT Austin BS '81, MS '85) who worked at Exxon before founding Houston-based Hilcorp in 1989, now the largest privately held US exploration & production company, built by buying and reworking underperforming mature fields. Stepped down as CEO in 2018; remains executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In December 2015 Hilcorp gave every one of its ~1,380 employees a $100,000 bonus after hitting a five-year goal to double production; the company was also on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For list 2013-2015.
deep_cut_fact: His $25M gift in 2017 led UT Austin to rename the department he graduated from the Hildebrand Department of Petroleum and Geosystems Engineering; he is also a donor behind Texas A&M's Hildebrand Equine Complex.
notes: Private, low-profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Hilcorp media form. Political donor/methane-regulation coverage (ProPublica 2026) is a sensitive topic. Appointed Chair of Texas Parks & Wildlife Commission Aug 2023.

name: Prajogo Pangestu
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Barito Pacific group (Chandra Asri, Barito Renewables Energy, Petrindo Jaya Kreasi)
profile: Indonesian tycoon, son of a rubber trader, who started in timber in the late 1970s and built Barito Pacific, which took control of petrochemical maker Chandra Asri in 2007. He has since listed coal miner Petrindo Jaya Kreasi and geothermal/renewables arm Barito Renewables Energy (2023), and in 2025 Chandra Daya Investasi.
interesting_fact: In 2022 his family office took control of geothermal producer Star Energy by buying a 33% stake from Thailand's BCPG for $440 million; Barito Renewables now houses one of the world's largest geothermal portfolios.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1944 in West Kalimantan to a Hakka family, he finished only junior high (SMP Nan Hua in Singkawang) and worked as an angkot (shared minibus) driver on the Singkawang-Pontianak route before a chance meeting with timber businessman Burhan Uray led him into the Djajanti timber group.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is Barito Pacific corporate secretary (Jakarta). Corpsec email is from a 2023 AGM notice; verify it is still current.

name: Karel Komarek
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, KKCG (owner of Allwyn, MND, Aricoma)
profile: Czech entrepreneur born in Hodonin in 1969 who began in 1992 trading industrial valves, moved into oil and gas (MND) and founded investment group KKCG in 1995. KKCG built Sazka into Allwyn, Europe's largest lottery operator (incl. UK National Lottery), and now invests in energy, IT, real estate and US methanol; he lives in Switzerland.
interesting_fact: Through KKCG's US Methanol, he opened a methanol plant in West Virginia in 2023; he also co-founded the Dvorak Prague music festival (2008) and supports the Kennedy Center's REACH expansion.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded 'More than Equal' with ex-F1 driver David Coulthard, a non-profit aiming to find and develop Formula 1's first female world champion; he also backs American Racing Challenger Team USA sailing with Ken Read.
notes: Energy angle: KKCG's MND (gas storage, flexibility) and US Methanol. Approach via KKCG communications team.

name: Charlie Ergen
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, EchoStar Corporation (Nasdaq: ECHO, formerly SATS; parent of DISH)
profile: Charlie Ergen co-founded EchoStar in 1980 selling satellite dishes in rural Colorado, then built DISH Network into a top US pay-TV provider. He later amassed a large hoard of wireless spectrum. In 2025 EchoStar agreed to sell spectrum to AT&T (~$23B) and SpaceX (~$17B+ in cash and SpaceX stock), totalling ~$42B and making EchoStar a SpaceX shareholder. Ergen controls EchoStar's voting power.
interesting_fact: Ergen grew up in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. His father, an Austrian-born nuclear physicist at Oak Ridge, is credited with coining the phrase 'China syndrome' for a reactor meltdown.
deep_cut_fact: After a Wake Forest MBA, Ergen was a financial analyst at Frito-Lay. He 'retired' in 1978 to play poker and blackjack professionally. In 1980 he, his future wife Candy and Jim DeFranco put $60,000 into two C-band antennas and sold satellite dishes from the back of a truck around Denver.
notes: He is famously frugal and blunt and speaks mainly on EchoStar earnings calls. The spectrum-to-satellite pivot and SpaceX stake are strong podcast hooks for energy and data-center connectivity. The IR site blocks automated access; get the latest media/IR contacts from current EchoStar press releases.

name: Michael G. Rubin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Fanatics (licensed sports merchandise, trading cards/collectibles, betting & gaming); co-chair, REFORM Alliance
profile: Philadelphia-born serial entrepreneur (b.1972) who went from teenage ski shops to closeout firm KPR Sports and e-commerce outsourcer GSI Commerce (sold to eBay in 2011, keeping Fanatics). He has built Fanatics into a global sports platform spanning merchandise, Topps trading cards, sportsbook, live events (Fanatics Fest) and media.
interesting_fact: Fanatics has partnership deals with more than 900 professional and collegiate leagues and teams; Rubin was formerly a part-owner of the Philadelphia 76ers and New Jersey Devils before selling in 2022 to focus on Fanatics.
deep_cut_fact: He started tuning skis in his parents' basement around age 12, and grew it to five ski shops before college. His next company, KPR Sports, was named after his parents' initials and hit $1M in sales in 1993, the year he turned 21.
notes: Very public and social-media active (X/Instagram), but handles not verified from an official page here. Co-founded REFORM Alliance (criminal-justice reform) with Meek Mill/Jay-Z. Fanatics Sportsbook press used Phil.PriceFry@betfanatics.com in a Mar 2026 release (betting unit only).

name: Nassef Sawiris
current_role: Executive Chairman, OCI Global (Euronext Amsterdam); co-owner and chairman of Aston Villa FC via V Sports (with Wes Edens); Adidas supervisory board
profile: Youngest son of Orascom founder Onsi Sawiris and often Egypt's richest person, he built Orascom Construction and OCI into a major builder and one of the world's largest nitrogen-fertilizer producers. After OCI sold most of its plants in 2024-25, he is combining OCI with Orascom Construction and holds stakes in Adidas, MSG Sports and Aston Villa.
interesting_fact: In July 2018 he and Wes Edens bought a 55% controlling stake in Aston Villa, then a cash-strapped second-tier club, for about £30m; under their V Sports group Villa returned to the Premier League and reached the Champions League.
deep_cut_fact: A 1982 University of Chicago economics graduate, he has sat on UChicago's Board of Trustees since 2013 and in 2019 pledged $24 million to the university to fund scholarships for Egyptian students and an executive-education program.

public_contacts.value: sarah.rajani@oci-global.com (Sarah Rajani, VP Investor Relations and Communications, OCI - investors & media)

notes: Energy/industrial angle: ammonia, hydrogen and fertilizer (OCI), construction of power and infrastructure (Orascom Construction). Wikipedia infobox calls him 'Chairman of Adidas', which appears wrong; he is a supervisory board member. Best route is OCI IR/communications.

name: Zhang Xuexin
current_role: Founder (retired), Xinfa Group, Chiping, Shandong; stepped back from chairman/CEO roles in April 2015
profile: Zhang Xuexin (b. 1947, Chiping, Shandong) turned the state-owned Chiping power plant (founded 1972) into Xinfa Group, an integrated power and aluminium empire covering bauxite, alumina, smelting and power stations, with ~RMB 290B revenue (2023). Xinfa is unlisted and issues no bonds. It is now expanding into polysilicon and solar aluminium.
interesting_fact: Using the power plant's idle generating capacity, Xinfa started a 10,000-tonne electrolytic aluminium line in 1998; within seven years (1998-2004) it went from zero to China's largest electrolytic aluminium producer, a classic captive-power energy play.
deep_cut_fact: He was among the very first employees of the Chiping county power plant in 1972 and rose to plant director in 1986; he was later named a National Model Worker. Asked about aluminium overcapacity in 2012, he retorted: 'Are cars in surplus? Appliances? Clothes? Is there any industry not in surplus?'
notes: Alive status presumed (still on Forbes 2026 list; no death report found). Extremely low-profile; rarely gives interviews and no published contact. Retired from management in 2015 and reportedly no longer holds shares directly. Strong fit for energy angle (captive coal power + aluminium) but approach via Xinfa Group corporate office only.

name: Low Tuck Kwong
current_role: Founder and President Director, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (Indonesia)
profile: Singapore-born 'coal king' (b. 1948) who moved to Indonesia in 1972 as a building contractor, bought his first coal mine in 1997 and built Bayan Resources into a producer of ~57m tonnes a year. He also controls Singapore renewables firm Metis Energy and backs SEAX Global, a subsea internet cable linking Singapore, Indonesia and Malaysia.
interesting_fact: An animal lover, he has sponsored a zoo with gibbons, sun bears, peacocks and orangutans; in 2019 he gave $7m to Dana Lestari ITB, the endowment fund of the Bandung Institute of Technology.
deep_cut_fact: In 2023 the Low Tuck Kwong Foundation gave S$127.6 million to education and healthcare causes, making it the largest private giver among all of Singapore's philanthropic organisations that year.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is Bayan's corporate secretary (Jenny Quantero is listed corporate secretary per 2026 news). SEAX Global / Metis Energy angle fits data-center + energy themes.

name: Mark Stevens
current_role: Managing Partner, S-Cubed Capital (family office, Menlo Park); Director, NVIDIA
profile: Silicon Valley VC who spent ~22 years at Sequoia Capital (1989-2012), leading its 1993 investment in Nvidia and taking part in bets on Google, Yahoo and YouTube. Earlier worked at Hughes Aircraft and Intel. Now invests via his family office S-Cubed Capital, sits on Nvidia's board and owns a minority stake in the Golden State Warriors.
interesting_fact: In May 2026 he and his wife Mary pledged $200M to USC to launch a universitywide AI initiative; USC renamed its computing school the USC Mark and Mary Stevens School of Computing and Artificial Intelligence.
deep_cut_fact: He turned down a full-time job offer at Hughes Aircraft after graduating USC to become a technical sales engineer at then little-known Intel ('I had an educated hunch that Intel's microprocessors would transform society'); he earned his USC master's via distance learning while working. He also says his first Sequoia recommendation failed.
notes: Private family office (S-Cubed Capital) with no published contact found. Strong angles: Nvidia origin story (led Sequoia's 1993 Nvidia investment) and his USC AI/computing philanthropy. Possible routes via USC Viterbi / Stevens Center communications. Forbes fact: first job at 16 was cook at Jack in the Box, Culver City.

name: Fredrik Lundberg
current_role: President & CEO, L E Lundbergföretagen AB (Stockholm); chairman of Industrivärden
profile: Fredrik Lundberg (b. 1951, Norrköping) took over in 1981 the construction firm his father founded in 1944 and built it into a listed holding company with property and big stakes in Holmen, Hufvudstaden, Industrivärden, Handelsbanken and Skanska. Via Industrivärden he influences a dozen of Sweden's largest companies; his daughters sit on the board.
interesting_fact: He was once a junior curling world champion, and in 1985 he moved his family to Switzerland to avoid punitive taxes before later returning to Sweden.
deep_cut_fact: He holds two degrees — a business degree from the Stockholm School of Economics and an M.Sc. in engineering (civilingenjör) from KTH — and was elected to the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences (IVA) in 1997; SSE also made him an honorary doctor in 1998.
notes: Low-key, rarely interviewed. Company main inbox and IR contact (EVP Claes Boustedt) are published. Energy/forestry angle: Holmen owns hydro and wind power assets in Sweden.

name: Philippe Laffont
current_role: Founder and Portfolio Manager/CEO, Coatue Management (New York)
profile: Belgian-born French-American 'Tiger Cub'. Laffont studied computer science at MIT, consulted at McKinsey, then joined Tiger Management before founding Coatue in 1999. Coatue (~$54B AUM per Forbes) invests in public and private tech (ByteDance, Snap, OpenAI), and he is a vocal AI bull whose top holdings include Nvidia, Broadcom, Meta and CoreWeave.
interesting_fact: Coatue is named after Coatue, a beach on Nantucket Island. Laffont has jokingly called himself a 'repressed mediocre computer scientist' and reportedly dreamed of working at Apple as a teenager.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tiger, after leaving McKinsey and working in Spain, he and his brother bought tech stocks in their spare time. He then moved to New York and took a job working for free at a small mutual fund to break into tech investing. His advice to graduates: do the obvious thing passionately and 'one thing completely off the beaten path.'
notes: Gives few interviews, but Coatue publishes widely read AI/tech market decks at its annual East Meets West (EMW) conference, a natural hook for an AI/data-centre podcast. Coatue has backed AI infrastructure (CoreWeave). Route via media@coatue.com.

name: Sulaiman Al Habib
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib Medical Services Group (HMG), Riyadh (Tadawul: 4013)
profile: Saudi pediatrician Dr. Sulaiman Al Habib founded HMG in 1995 and took it public on the Saudi Exchange in 2020; he owns about 40%. HMG runs hospitals, clinics, specialty centers (fertility, dermatology, obesity and more) and a pharmacy chain across Saudi Arabia, Dubai and Bahrain. Forbes Middle East ranked him No. 3 on its 2026 Richest Arabs list.

The deep-cut education detail is from Bloomberg's billionaire profile (seen via search, not re-fetched). Little energy/data-center link.

current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, EP Group / Energetický a průmyslový holding (EPH); chairman of Royal Mail parent IDS; chairman of AC Sparta Prague

EPH is Central Europe's largest energy group (gas transit, storage, power). He has since expanded into retail and logistics (Royal Mail/IDS, Metro, Casino, Le Monde stake, West Ham) and in 2025-26 struck a €5.1bn all-stock power JV with TotalEnergies.

He said he made his first million at 24.

name: Steven Rales
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Danaher Corporation; founder, Indian Paintbrush (film production)
profile: Steven M. Rales (b. 1951) co-founded Danaher with his brother Mitchell in 1984, after buying a REIT in 1983. Danaher became a roughly $24B-revenue life-sciences and diagnostics conglomerate, and he has chaired it ever since. He also founded Indian Paintbrush, Wes Anderson's longtime financier, owns The Criterion Collection and Janus Films, and holds about 20% of the NBA's Indiana Pacers.
interesting_fact: Danaher is named after a creek in Montana. Through Indian Paintbrush, Rales has earned three Academy Award nominations with Wes Anderson and won the Oscar for Best Live Action Short for 'The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar' (2023).
deep_cut_fact: In 1992 the Rales brothers bought the AM side of Washington's WGMS and turned the classical station into WTEM, the D.C. area's first full-time sports-talk radio station.
notes: Famously private; the Rales brothers rarely give interviews. Danaher IR is the only published corporate channel. Indian Paintbrush (film) or the Pacers could offer softer entry points. A major DePauw University donor (Peeler Art Center; Indian Paintbrush Foundation grants).

name: Carl Cook
current_role: CEO, Cook Group Inc.; president, Cook MyoSite; chair of Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology board of trustees
profile: Carl Cook (b. 1962), Indiana's richest person, has led Cook Group, the private Bloomington-based medical device maker his parents Bill and Gayle Cook founded in their apartment in 1963, since his father's death in 2011. A Purdue engineering graduate with a University of Iowa MBA, he also heads Cook MyoSite, which develops a cell therapy for urinary incontinence.
interesting_fact: Cook Group started in 1963 when his father Bill spent $1,500 on a soldering iron, a blowtorch and plastic tubing to make then-new cardiovascular catheters in the family's Bloomington apartment.
deep_cut_fact: After college he spent a year in France and Germany setting up computers for the family company, then worked in Cook's pacemaker division in Leechburg, Pennsylvania and its Winston-Salem plant; Rose-Hulman made him an honorary Doctor of Engineering in 2015 and board chair in 2023.
notes: Private, low-profile. Pete Yonkman is president of Cook Group/Cook Medical and Steve Ferguson board chair; Carl remains CEO. His mother Gayle Cook died in 2025 - avoid in outreach beyond respectful mention. Deep-cut details partly from Rose-Hulman: https://www.rhit.edu/news/2023/carl-cook-named-chair-of-board-of-trustees.html

name: Cui Wei
current_role: Chairman, Hengtong Optic-Electric (600487.SH); President, Hengtong Group
profile: Son of Hengtong Group founder Cui Genliang, with whom he shares a Hurun listing. Rose from non-executive director to group VP, became chairman of flagship Hengtong Optic-Electric in 2021. The father-son pair control five listed companies; the AI-driven demand for optical fibre pushed Hengtong Optic-Electric's market cap to ~RMB259bn in June 2026.
interesting_fact: Hengtong Optic-Electric's market value rose from ~RMB61bn at end-2025 to ~RMB259bn by 9 June 2026 as AI data-center demand for fibre surged; Hengtong is now planning to spin off its submarine-cable unit Hengtong Huahai.
deep_cut_fact: In his 2026 New Year message he closed with '行而不辍，未来可期' (keep going without stopping and the future is promising), and highlighted Hengtong deploying the first commercial hollow-core fibre line with China Unicom and joining China's first hollow-core-fibre data-center interconnect project.
notes: Wealth shared with father Cui Genliang (Hengtong founder). Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Hengtong Optic-Electric board office (IR email published in annual report summary; board secretary may have changed in 2026).

name: Xu Yangtian
current_role: Founder, CEO and controlling shareholder, SHEIN (Singapore-headquartered; listed in Hong Kong Sept 2026, ticker 0625.HK)
profile: Xu Yangtian (Chris/Sky Xu, b. ~1984, Shandong) is an SEO marketer who founded the business in Nanjing in 2008 as ZZKKO, sold wedding dresses cross-border, then rebuilt it as SheInside/SHEIN, a data-driven ultra-fast-fashion and marketplace giant. After failed New York and London attempts, SHEIN listed in Hong Kong in Sept 2026 at about a $27B valuation; Xu holds ~30%.

deep_cut_fact: SHEIN's original corporate name was ZZKKO (founded October 2008 in Nanjing), and its first big seller was wedding dresses for overseas buyers before it pivoted to womenswear as 'SheInside'.

name: Michal Strnad
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, Czechoslovak Group (CSG), Prague
profile: Michal Strnad (b. 1992) took ownership of Czechoslovak Group from his father in 2018, having joined in 2011 and become chairman in 2015. CSG makes ammunition, military and Tatra vehicles, and rail/aerospace products, and grew via buys like Spain's FMG and Italy's Fiocchi. He listed CSG on Euronext Amsterdam in Jan 2026, raising $4.5B.
interesting_fact: CSG's January 2026 Euronext Amsterdam IPO raised about $4.5 billion, one of the largest listings ever in the defense sector, and made Strnad Czechia's richest person.
deep_cut_fact: He became board chairman of the family group at just 23 (2015), after joining at 19 in 2011. Beyond defense, CSG owns traditional Czech watchmaker PRIM, and Strnad is a car and motorsport enthusiast.

name: John Morris
current_role: Founder & CEO, Bass Pro Shops (Bass Pro Group, incl. Cabela's, Big Cedar Lodge, White River Marine Group)
profile: Johnny Morris founded Bass Pro Shops in 1972 selling fishing tackle from the back of his father's liquor store in Springfield, Missouri, and built it into an ~$8B outdoor retailer, buying rival Cabela's for $5B in 2017. A prominent conservationist, he built the $300M Wonders of Wildlife museum and aquarium and owns Big Cedar Lodge in the Ozarks.
interesting_fact: At 22 he competed in the first national B.A.S.S. fishing tournament and placed 21st; for Bass Pro's 50th anniversary in 2022 the company pledged 10% of earnings to conservation.

notes: Goes by Johnny Morris. Private company; route via Bass Pro Communications. Strong conservation angle for outreach.

name: Wang Yusuo
current_role: Founder & Chairman, ENN Group; Chairman/executive director of ENN Energy Holdings (2688.HK)
profile: Hebei-born (1964) founder of ENN Group, one of China's largest private natural-gas distributors. He began in the 1980s selling LPG cylinders and stoves, won early gas-well and pipeline rights around Langfang, and listed ENN Energy in Hong Kong in 2001. ENN now spans city gas, LNG trading, integrated energy and a privately funded fusion programme.
interesting_fact: ENN privately funds a fusion programme: on 16 Apr 2025 its EXL-50U spherical torus reached a 1-mega-ampere plasma current with hydrogen-boron fuel, which ENN calls a world first; it targets demonstrating proton-boron power generation by 2035.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004, when ENN was a comfortable downstream gas seller, Wang pushed it upstream by posing the 'ENN Three Questions': if the majors move downstream, what will ENN sell in 10 years, what will its brand be in 20, and what will it do when its 30-year city-gas concessions expire? He also once waited outside a meeting from 3:30pm to 10pm to pitch an official for 5 minutes.

notes: Low-profile; rarely gives foreign media interviews. Best route is ENN Energy IR (Hong Kong) or ENN's fusion research institute, which runs the international proton-boron fusion symposium (ISPBF) - a natural podcast hook. Son Wang Zizheng is also on the ENN Energy board.

name: Jack Dangermond
current_role: Co-founder and President, Esri (Redlands, California)
profile: Jack Dangermond (b. 1945) and his wife Laura founded Esri in 1969 with $1,100 of savings to do land-use analysis; its ARC/INFO and later ArcGIS software made it the leader in geographic information systems with ~40% global market share. Still president of the privately held company, he is regarded as the godfather of digital mapping and has pledged $1B of free GIS software to US K-12 schools.
interesting_fact: In 2017 the Dangermonds gave $165M to The Nature Conservancy to preserve 24,000 acres of coastal ranch at Point Conception, California - now the Jack and Laura Dangermond Preserve. The couple still go to work together every morning.
deep_cut_fact: The son of Dutch immigrants who ran a plant nursery in Redlands (the same town where Esri is headquartered), he studied landscape architecture at Cal Poly Pomona; his work at Harvard's Laboratory for Computer Graphics and Spatial Analysis led directly to Esri's ARC/INFO.
notes: Accessible and evangelistic about GIS; speaks every year at the Esri User Conference (San Diego, July). Strong angle for an energy/data-center podcast: GIS for grid planning, siting and climate. Route via Esri media relations.

name: Keith Rupert Murdoch
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Fox Corporation and News Corp (since Nov 2023)
profile: Rupert Murdoch, born in Melbourne in 1931, turned the single Adelaide paper he inherited at 21 into a global empire spanning The Wall Street Journal, The Times, the New York Post, HarperCollins and Fox News. notes: Sanctioned by UK, EU, Canada, Australia and Switzerland: any engagement may carry legal/compliance issues, so check before outreach. No published personal or office contact found. Very private; rarely gives interviews.

name: Cho Jung-ho
current_role: Chairman, Meritz Financial Group (Seoul)
profile: Cho Jung-ho (b. 1958, Incheon) is the youngest of four sons of Hanjin Group/Korean Air founder Cho Choong-hoon. After Korean Air's European office and Hanil Securities, he ran Hanjin Investment & Securities from 1989 and in 2005 spun the financial affiliates out of Hanjin as Meritz, which has since grown into Korea's No. 2 financial holding company by market value.

name: Les Wexner
current_role: Co-founder and chair emeritus, Bath & Body Works, Inc.; chairman, The Wexner Foundation (Columbus/New Albany, Ohio)
profile: Les Wexner (born 1937, Dayton) opened The Limited in Columbus in 1963 with a $5,000 loan from his aunt and built L Brands, which owned Victoria's Secret (bought for $1M in 1982), Bath & Body Works and Abercrombie & Fitch, serving as CEO for over five decades. Attended OSU Wexner Medical Center board meeting Sept 2026 (https://wysu.org/ohio-news/2026-09-01/les-wexner-attends-ohio-state-medical-center-board-meeting-for-the-first-time-in-more-than-a-year).

profile: Eldest son of Unibanco founder and former ambassador Walther Moreira Salles (d. 2001), FGV-educated Fernando (80) is the richest of the four billionaire Moreira Salles brothers (Forbes Brasil 2026: R$50.3B, 5th in Brazil). Brother Walter Salles is the Oscar-winning director of 'Ainda Estou Aqui', a well-known family hook. Niobium/CBMM is a strong energy-storage angle.

name: Viktor Rashnikov
current_role: Chairman of the Board and majority owner, Magnitogorsk Iron & Steel Works (MMK), Russia
profile: Viktor Rashnikov (b. 1948, Magnitogorsk) joined MMK as a repair-shop fitter in 1967, rose to general director in 1997 and chairman in 2005, and built a near-total stake by buying shares on the market. Under him MMK doubled steel output and listed in London in 2007. He remains MMK chairman in 2026 amid a downturn in Russian steel.
interesting_fact: A passionate hockey fan, he has been president of KHL club Metallurg Magnitogorsk since 1999.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training (metal forming, Magnitogorsk Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, 1974), he earned a doctorate in Technical Sciences in 1998 and was named an Honored Professor of the Moscow Institute of Steel and Alloys in 2002.
notes: Sanctioned by the US, UK and EU since 2022 - check legal/compliance before any outreach or appearance. Very unlikely to engage with Western media; 2026 coverage shows him still MMK board chairman (e.g. PRIME, 1 Jun 2026).

name: Carl Bennet
current_role: Owner, Carl Bennet AB (Gothenburg), the controlling shareholder in Getinge, Arjo, Lifco and Elanders
profile: Swedish industrialist Baron Carl Bennet (b. 1951) and partner Rune Andersson bought medtech firm Getinge from Electrolux in 1989; Bennet was its CEO from 1989 to 1997. His investment company Carl Bennet AB now controls five Stockholm-listed groups, including Getinge, Arjo, Lifco and Elanders, with net asset value of about SEK 103bn at end-2025.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he re-listed Lifco at about 28 times the price he paid to take it private 14 years earlier. He has also pushed Sweden to adopt a German-style apprenticeship system to fight youth unemployment.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up on the Fjerrestadstorp manor in Skåne, in a noble family descended from Jakob Bennet, who came from Scotland in the 1600s. His career began in the finance department of the Kockums shipyard in Malmö. At Electrolux he ran the commercial-kitchen unit in Alingsås before the Getinge deal.
notes: Private, low-key Swedish investor who rarely gives interviews and has no social media. Approach via Carl Bennet AB's contact page or the IR teams of Getinge or Lifco. He is an honorary doctor at Luleå University of Technology and a member of the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences (IVA).

name: John Overdeck
current_role: Co-founder and co-chairman, Two Sigma (management committee member since 2025); chair, Institute for Advanced Study board; co-founder, Overdeck Family Foundation
profile: Maryland-raised math prodigy (Stanford BS math, MS statistics) who was an MD at D.E. Shaw and a VP at Amazon.com before co-founding Two Sigma with David Siegel in 2001. The data-driven quant firm manages ~$60B. He and Siegel moved from co-CEOs to co-chairmen in 2024; he rejoined the management committee in 2025. His foundation has given $450M+, mainly to education.
interesting_fact: He won a silver medal for the U.S. at the 1986 International Mathematical Olympiad in Poland at age 16.
deep_cut_fact: Long before quant fame he was an early Amazon.com vice president, and today he is acting chair of New York's National Museum of Mathematics (MoMath) as well as chair of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton - Einstein's old academic home.
notes: Very low public profile. news@overdeck.org is the Overdeck Family Foundation's published media address; Two Sigma's contact form has a 'Media Inquiry' option. Data angle: Two Sigma is a big data/compute user. Avoid personal/family topics.

name: David Siegel
current_role: Co-founder and Co-Chairman, Two Sigma; chair of Siegel Family Endowment
profile: Bronx-born computer scientist (Princeton, MIT PhD from the AI Lab) who worked at D.E. Shaw and Tudor before co-founding quant firm Two Sigma with John Overdeck in 2001. Two Sigma's data-driven hedge funds manage about $60B. In Sept 2024 the two stepped back from co-CEO to co-chairman roles. He funds tech-and-society work through Siegel Family Endowment and the Scratch Foundation.

name: Terry Pegula
current_role: Owner & President, Buffalo Bills (NFL) and Buffalo Sabres (NHL); owner of Pegula Sports and Entertainment and JKLM Energy
profile: Penn State petroleum & natural-gas engineer (b. 1951, Carbondale, PA) who founded East Resources in 1983, rode the Marcellus shale boom and sold its core assets to Shell for ~$4.7B in 2010 (plus Ohio/WV assets for $1.75B in 2014). His father drove a truck for a coal company; his grandparents came from Hanigovce, Slovakia.

name: Morris Chang
current_role: Founder and retired chairman (since 2018), Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC)

Retired as chairman in 2018; now in his mid-90s, he keeps a low profile (a rare public dinner with Jensen Huang in Jan 2026).

Moll) was on 'Optical absorption and photoluminescence of doped GaAs and (InxGa1-x)As'; earlier he had turned down a Ford Motor job offer in 1955 to join Sylvania's small semiconductor unit.
notes: Retired; age ~95, rarely appears publicly (reportedly using a wheelchair in Jan 2026). TSMC press office is the only realistic route; no personal social accounts. His two-volume autobiography (2024) is a good outreach hook.

name: Kelcy Warren

Dakota Access). He stepped down as CEO in 2020 and remains executive chairman; SEC Form 4 filings show him still buying ET units in 2026.

He gave $10M+ to build Klyde Warren Park, the 5-acre deck park over a Dallas freeway, named for his son.

He holds a 1978 civil-engineering degree from UT Arlington.

In 2022 he and a group of businessmen bought the Circuit de la Ribera in Guadassuar and turned it into the Aspar Circuit, now the base of the Aspar MotoGP-family team.

He became famous as a huge retail Tesla investor, later trimming his stake and moving into Treasuries.

SHI recently acted as lead integrator for a New Jersey AI supercomputer initiative (data-center angle). SHI press has used agency Gregory FCA; no current verified press email found.

name: James Clark
current_role: Private technology investor; co-founder of Silicon Graphics, Netscape and Healtheon/WebMD; 10%+ shareholder of Ibotta (NYSE: IBTA)
profile: Jim Clark, a former Stanford professor, co-founded Silicon Graphics (1982) and then Netscape (1994), whose 1995 IPO helped ignite the dot-com boom, followed by Healtheon/WebMD and myCFO. He has since multiplied his wealth through early stakes in Apple, Facebook, Twitter and Palantir and remains a large holder in Ibotta; he is also a keen sailor and backer of ocean causes.
interesting_fact: Clark was the key financial backer of 'The Cove', the Oscar-winning documentary about dolphin hunting in Japan, and keeps a ~30,000-bottle Burgundy collection he calls his 'liquid asset'.
deep_cut_fact: A high-school dropout who learned electronics in the Navy and earned credits at Tulane night school, he did his 1974 Utah PhD under computer-graphics pioneer Ivan Sutherland on '3-D design of free-form B-spline surfaces', then built the 'Geometry Engine' graphics accelerator with Stanford students in 1979, the basis of SGI.
notes: No published personal, office or press contact found; he has no active public social accounts. Possible routes: via Ibotta IR (as a major holder) or Stanford/computer-graphics community, but none is an official channel for him. Born 1944 (age 82).

name: Justin Sun
current_role: Founder, TRON blockchain (TRX); controls/advises exchanges HTX and Poloniex; owner of BitTorrent
profile: Justin Sun (b. 1990; Peking University BA, Penn MA) adopted Bitcoin early in 2012, worked for Ripple, then founded TRON in 2017; it is now a major stablecoin network. He also owns HTX, Poloniex and BitTorrent. He was Grenada's WTO ambassador (2021-23). The SEC's 2023 case over TRX/BTT settled in March 2026 for $10M, paid by an affiliate.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he won Blue Origin's $28M auction for the first paid seat on New Shepard but missed the flight due to a scheduling conflict; he finally flew to space in August 2025 aboard Blue Origin NS-34.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he joined the inaugural class of Jack Ma's Hupan University entrepreneurship school as its only member born in the 1990s, finishing the three-year programme in 2018 with a thesis on blockchain. Before TRON he launched Peiwo (2014), a social app that matched users via 10-second voice clips.
notes: Highly public and media-friendly; very active on X (@justinsuntron), which is the most direct route. Reputationally sensitive: ongoing regulatory and litigation coverage (SEC settlement, WLFI dispute, UK FCA action vs HTX) — journalist should do own diligence.

Wealth from oil (TNK-BP stake sold to Rosneft in 2013), Alfa-Bank, VimpelCom and X5 Retail.
