current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jiangxi Redboard Technology (红板科技, SSE: 603459), Ji'an, Jiangxi
profile: Ye Senran (叶森然), a PCB veteran of 40+ years, founded Redboard in 2005 and bet on HDI boards rather than crowded low-end circuit boards. It now has ~13% of the global phone-HDI market (Honor, OPPO, vivo), listed in Shanghai on 8 Apr 2026 raising 1.77bn yuan, and is moving into AI optical-module PCBs, IC substrates and servers.
interesting_fact: Redboard is riding the AI data-centre build-out: its MSAP process is one of the few able to mass-produce PCBs for 1.6T/3.2T high-speed optical modules. Ye says mid-2025 was the 'watershed' when optical modules abandoned the old subtractive process.
deep_cut_fact: Redboard has developed a 26-layer any-layer interconnect board, at the limit of civilian PCB processes. Ye plays it down as a small-batch job for a Korean customer, arguing that real core technology means holding >90% yield at scale, not making record samples.
notes: Very low public profile and no personal channels found. Redboard's IR contact (board secretary) should be in its SSE filings and annual report at sse.com.cn (code 603459); I could not confirm a published email. Strong fit for the AI-hardware supply-chain angle.

name: Pavel Tykac
current_role: Owner, Sev.en Global Investments / Sev.en Group (coal, power, steel, oil & gas; Prague)
profile: Czech investor who began as a computer distributor, co-founded takeover firm Motoinvest in 1992, then built Sev.en Energy (Czech coal mines, power plants, 50% of InterGen). Via Sev.en Global Investments he now buys ESG-shunned assets abroad: Celsa UK/Nordic steel, Texas oil and gas wells, a stake in Vietnam's Mong Duong 2 plant.
interesting_fact: His group openly runs a contrarian strategy of buying companies that institutional investors are dumping over ESG concerns, betting coal and heavy industry stay profitable longer than markets assume.
deep_cut_fact: He is a native of Čelákovice, a small town near Prague, and Forbes Czech names his real passion as football club SK Slavia Prague, which it lists among his holdings.
notes: Very low public profile and rarely gives interviews; CEO Alan Svoboda usually speaks for the group. Best route is the Sev.en GI media team (Veronika Diamantová; communications director Gabriela Sáričková Benešová). The site shows emails through JS anti-spam markup (decoded with the site's own script).

name: Piero Ferrari
current_role: Vice Chairman, Ferrari N.V. (since 1988); Chairman, HPE COXA; non-executive director, Ferretti Group
profile: Piero Ferrari, Enzo Ferrari's only surviving son, owns about 10% of Ferrari and has been vice chairman since 1988. He became a billionaire at Ferrari's 2015 NYSE listing. He worked in Ferrari's motorsport division from 1970 to 1988, founded Modena engineering firm HPE (now HPE COXA) in 1998 and chaired Piaggio Aerospace from 1999 to 2014.
interesting_fact: He supports Centro Dino Ferrari, a research center for muscular and neurodegenerative diseases that his father co-founded in memory of Piero's half-brother Dino.
deep_cut_fact: His first Ferrari job, in 1965, was on the production of the Dino 206 Competizione racing car. He later chaired Piaggio Aerospace (1999-2014) and holds honorary degrees in aerospace engineering (Naples Federico II, 2004) and mechanical engineering (Modena and Reggio Emilia, 2005).
notes: Age 80. Cavaliere del Lavoro (2004). Engineering angle: HPE COXA does advanced design/simulation and high-precision prototype manufacturing. Ferrari media/IR emails come from Ferrari N.V. press releases (seen via search). Possible route: HPE COXA in Modena.

name: Hasmukh Chudgar
current_role: Founder and patriarch, Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); trustee, Intas Welfare Trust. Operations run by his sons
profile: Hasmukh Chudgar, a pharmacist, founded Intas Pharmaceuticals in Ahmedabad in 1977; it was incorporated in 1985. Bootstrapped for decades without diluting equity, it became India's largest unlisted drugmaker, with about $3.5B revenue and Europe and India as its biggest markets. His sons Nimish, Binish and Urmish now run it. Recent moves include buying biosimilar Udenyca from Coherus for $558M in 2025.
interesting_fact: Intas makes Eleftha, an affordable biosimilar of Roche's breast-cancer drug Herceptin. Abu Dhabi Investment Authority bought a 3% stake in the still-private company from Temasek in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became an industrialist, Chudgar was a pharmacy professor. He started Intas by making medicines in a small facility in Gujarat and deliberately refused outside equity in the early years.
notes: Very low profile and elderly; no interviews found. Binish Chudgar (dealmaker, Accord/Actavis UK deal) and Urmish (biopharma) are the active public faces. The only published corporate inbox is Intas's general queries email.

name: Pauline MacMillan Keinath
current_role: Cargill heiress and believed largest individual shareholder; no executive role
profile: Pauline MacMillan Keinath (b. 1934) is a great-granddaughter of W.W. Cargill and believed to be Cargill's largest individual shareholder, with a roughly 9-13% stake inherited after her father's death in 1968. Her late brother Whitney MacMillan was the last family CEO (to 1995). She lives in St. Louis and keeps an extremely low profile.
interesting_fact: Cargill began in 1865 as a single grain warehouse at the end of an Iowa railroad line founded by her great-grandfather; in 2022 her stake made her the richest person in Missouri.

public_contacts.value: media@cargill.com (Cargill corporate media; not her personal office)

notes: Age 92 and extremely private; no public foundation, interviews or personal channels found. Cargill media office will not speak for individual family shareholders. Probably not a realistic podcast guest.

name: Chris Larsen
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Chairman, Ripple (San Francisco)
profile: Serial fintech founder: co-founded online mortgage lender E-Loan (1996), peer-to-peer lender Prosper (2005/06) and in 2012 Ripple, which builds blockchain payment, custody and stablecoin (RLUSD) infrastructure around the XRP Ledger. He handed the CEO role to Brad Garlinghouse in 2017 and remains executive chairman; most of his fortune is in XRP and Ripple equity.
interesting_fact: As CEO of E-Loan he made it the first company to give consumers their FICO credit scores for free, and in 2019 he and his foundation gave $25M, largely in XRP, to his alma mater San Francisco State.
deep_cut_fact: A San Francisco native whose father was a United Airlines aircraft mechanic at SFO, Larsen's first job after SF State was doing financial audits for Chevron in Brazil, Ecuador and Indonesia; SF State named him Alum of the Year in 2004.
notes: press@ripple.com appears on 2026 Ripple releases with rotating named contacts. Avoid the SEC litigation and political donations in outreach. Energy angle: XRP Ledger's low energy use vs proof-of-work is a theme he has campaigned on.

name: François-Henri Pinault
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Kering; President, Groupe Artémis (Pinault family holding); non-executive Chairman, Christie's (from May 2026)
profile: François-Henri Pinault took over his father's retail group PPR in 2005 and turned it into luxury group Kering (Gucci, Saint Laurent, Bottega Veneta) in 2013. Since 2003 he has led family holding Artémis (Château Latour, Christie's, Stade Rennais, majority of CAA since 2023). Luca de Meo is now Kering CEO; Pinault remains chairman.
interesting_fact: French President Macron mandated him to set up the Fashion Pact at the 2019 G7 summit, an initiative signed by 56 fashion companies committing to reduce their environmental impact.
deep_cut_fact: While a student at HEC Paris (class of 1985) he co-founded CRM software company Soft Computing with classmates and interned at Hewlett-Packard in Paris as a database-software developer; he then did military service at the French Consulate in Los Angeles studying the fashion and new-tech sectors.
notes: Input record lists UK/Sunday Times 'Fashion and Films' (shared with Salma Hayek) - this is FHP. Press contact is from Kering's 2026 press releases (Kering Press, Emilie Gargatte). For media/podcast angle, CAA and Christie's are also Artémis assets.

name: Salma Hayek
current_role: Actress and producer; founder of production company Ventanarosa
profile: Mexican-born actress-producer Salma Hayek Pinault (b. 1966, Coatzacoalcos) rose from Mexican telenovelas to Hollywood with Desperado and earned an Oscar nomination for Frida (2002), which she also produced. She founded Ventanarosa in 1999 and executive-produced Ugly Betty. Her UK Rich List wealth entry is shared with husband François-Henri Pinault, chairman of Kering.
interesting_fact: Her portrayal of Frida Kahlo in 'Frida' (2002), which she also produced, made her the first Mexican actress nominated for the Academy Award for Best Actress.
deep_cut_fact: She won a Daytime Emmy for directing the children's special 'The Maldonado Miracle' (2004), and her first feature as a producer, 'El Coronel No Tiene Quien Le Escriba' (1999), was Mexico's official Oscar submission.
notes: Wealth is via marriage to François-Henri Pinault (Kering/Artémis); a better podcast angle may be Pinault family. Professional inquiries normally go through her talent agency/publicist (not verified here).

name: Andrew Cherng
current_role: Co-founder, Co-Chairman and Co-CEO (with wife Peggy Cherng), Panda Restaurant Group (Panda Express, Panda Inn), Rosemead, California
profile: Born in Yangzhou in 1948, Andrew Cherng moved via Taiwan and Japan to the US, met Peggy at Baker University in Kansas and earned an applied-math master's at Missouri. He opened the sit-down Panda Inn in Pasadena with his chef father in 1973, then Panda Express in 1983; it now has ~2,600 outlets across the US, Canada, Mexico, the Gulf and Korea and remains family-owned.
interesting_fact: The Cherngs have given big sums through their family trust: $100M to City of Hope for integrative cancer care (2023), $30M to Caltech (2017) and $17M to St. Rose Dominican Hospital in Henderson, Nevada (2025), its largest gift ever.
deep_cut_fact: Panda Express exists because the developer of the Glendale Galleria had eaten at Cherng's Panda Inn and invited him to take a spot in the mall's new food court - the first Panda Express opened there in 1983. Cherng has said he prefers keeping the company closely held rather than going public.
notes: Approachable founder who speaks about immigrant entrepreneurship and Panda's 'Tao of Panda' culture. FINN Partners is Panda Express's brand PR agency (consumer releases 2025); a founder interview request may need routing to Panda Restaurant Group corporate communications in Rosemead.

name: Peggy Cherng
current_role: Co-founder, Co-Chair & Co-CEO, Panda Restaurant Group (Panda Express)
profile: Burmese-born engineer Peggy Cherng earned a PhD in electrical engineering and worked at McDonnell Douglas and 3M's Comtal before joining husband Andrew to open the first Panda Express in a Glendale mall in 1983. She brought sales and analytics systems to the business, which now has ~2,600 locations and ~$6.7B in sales.
interesting_fact: Her 1974 University of Missouri doctoral thesis was a pattern-recognition program that scanned digitized chest X-rays for signs of congenital heart disease, an early piece of computer-aided medical imaging.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Hong Kong (Clementi Secondary School, class of 1966), she met Andrew Cherng as a freshman at tiny Baker University in Baldwin City, Kansas, then transferred to Oregon State for applied maths. At McDonnell Douglas (1975-77) she coded battlefield simulators.
notes: No published press email found; Panda Restaurant Group's media centre is the route. The Cherngs give through Panda Cares and the Cherng Family Trust. Her engineering and data background is a good hook for a tech-focused podcast.

name: Jean Salata
current_role: Chair, EQT Group (elected May 2026); still chairs EQT's Asia private equity investment committees
profile: Chilean, Hong Kong-based (since 1989) investor who founded Baring Private Equity's Asia program in 1997 and led its 2000 buyout to form BPEA. EQT bought BPEA in 2022 for $1.7B cash plus 191M EQT shares; he ran EQT Private Capital Asia until he was elected chair of EQT Group in May 2026.
interesting_fact: He and wife Melanie gave Harvard $200M in 2022 to create the Salata Institute for Climate and Sustainability - even though, per Harvard Magazine, neither had any prior Harvard connection (he is a Wharton grad).
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was a Bain & Company consultant in Hong Kong, Sydney and Boston, then a director at AIG's Asian PE arm; he graduated magna cum laude in finance and economics from Wharton.
notes: Climate angle (Salata Institute, https://salatainstitute.harvard.edu) is a strong hook for an energy podcast; EQT is also a big data-center/infrastructure investor (e.g. EdgeConneX). Route via EQT press office.

name: Guo Jinshu
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Inner Mongolia Huineng Coal & Electricity Group (Ordos)
profile: Guo Jinshu (郭金树), a former head of the Ordos municipal coal bureau, founded Huineng in the early 1990s from restructured small coal mines. It grew into a private coal, coal-to-gas/LNG, coal chemicals and power group with >RMB100bn in assets; he is now pushing into solar, new materials and acquisitions (e.g. Asia-Potash stake, ST Xinchao bid).
interesting_fact: Huineng began as a company of 600+ laid-off coal workers who pooled their own money; Guo says those who didn't take buyouts all became shareholders. Its Ordos coal-to-natural-gas plant became a national demonstration project.
deep_cut_fact: Guo explains the name: 汇 'gather' + 能 meaning energy, power, talent and ability, and preaches four qualities for running a business: 定力, 控制力, 穿透力, 平衡力 (composure, control, penetration, balance). In his 70s (2023) he still targeted RMB250bn in assets by 2030.
notes: Input's SEC link (Luckin Coffee CEO) is a mismatch: Luckin's CEO is Guo Jinyi, a different person. Very low-profile private Chinese coal tycoon; no published personal contacts found. Company site reportedly huinenggroup.com (unreachable, unverified). 2025 Asia-Potash filings name him as Huineng's sole actual controller.

name: Lilianne Bettencourt
notes: Liliane Bettencourt, L'Oreal heiress and principal shareholder, died 21 September 2017 (aged 94). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liliane_Bettencourt . Fortune passed to daughter Francoise Bettencourt Meyers. Skipped rest per instructions.

name: Joe Ricketts
current_role: Founder of TD Ameritrade (retired from board 2011); founder of High Plains Bison and other ventures via his Hugo Enterprises; Ricketts family owns the Chicago Cubs
profile: Nebraska-born (1941) entrepreneur who left Dean Witter and in 1975 co-formed First Omaha Securities, the discount brokerage that became TD Ameritrade (bought by Schwab in 2020). His family bought the Chicago Cubs in 2009; since leaving the TD Ameritrade board in 2011 he has focused on High Plains Bison, Wyoming ranches and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: He wrote a 2019 memoir, 'The Harder You Work, the Luckier You Get', tracing his path from a modest-means student who worked as a janitor's assistant to founding one of America's first discount brokerages.
deep_cut_fact: Ameritrade began in 1975 when Ricketts and a few partners put in just $12,500 each to form First Omaha Securities; separately, the bison company he founded in 2004, High Plains Bison, is the official bison vendor at Wrigley Field, with some herds raised on his Wyoming ranch.
notes: Lives in Wyoming. Politically active major donor; a 2019 leak of his emails drew controversy, so keep outreach on entrepreneurship. Business office is Hugo Enterprises (Omaha). Old DNAinfo email is defunct (site shut 2017).

name: Massimiliana Landini Aleotti
current_role: Co-owner of Menarini Group (Florence), with the company run by the Aleotti family's next generation
profile: Massimiliana Landini Aleotti (born 1942, Lerici) inherited Menarini, Italy's largest drugmaker, with her family after husband Alberto Aleotti died in 2014. Alberto joined Menarini in 1964 and bought it in the early 1990s; it now has 17,000+ staff and ~EUR 4.9B revenue (2025). She keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: Menarini, which she co-owns, was founded in Naples in 1886 and moved to Florence in 1915; it is now Italy's largest pharmaceutical group, operating in 140+ countries.
notes: Described in Italian press as 'the silent heir'; essentially no public statements. Menarini press office (Valeria Speroni Cardi, pressoffice@menarini.com) is the only published route; the company's public faces are its chairman and vice chairman. Avoid the family's past tax litigation.

name: Neil Bluhm
current_role: Executive Chairman, Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI); managing principal, Walton Street Capital; Rush Street Gaming co-founder
profile: Chicago-born Neil Bluhm (b. 1938) was an accountant and Mayer Brown lawyer before co-founding JMB Realty in 1969. He later co-founded Walton Street Capital (1994), Rush Street Gaming (Rivers casinos) and online-betting firm Rush Street Interactive (BetRivers), public since 2020. He owns Chicago landmarks like 900 North Michigan and stakes in the Bulls and White Sox.
interesting_fact: He pledged $45M to Northwestern Medicine in 2022 to create the Bluhm Heart Hospital, building on his 2005 $10M gift that founded the Bluhm Cardiovascular Institute.
deep_cut_fact: Raised by a bookkeeper mother in a small apartment on Chicago's northwest side, he studied accounting at the University of Illinois and co-founded JMB Realty with Judd Malkin - his high-school friend and college roommate.

public_contacts.value: Lisa Johnson Communications - lisa@lisajohnsoncommunications.com (RSI media contact)

notes: Aged 88; still active as RSI executive chairman. Art patron (Art Institute of Chicago, Whitney trustee). Avoid political-donation topics. RSI's published PR contact is the most direct route.

name: Dirk Rossmann
current_role: Founder and owner, Dirk Rossmann GmbH (Burgwedel, Germany); operations led by son Raoul since 2021
profile: Hannover-born Dirk Rossmann (b. 1946), a trained druggist, opened Germany's first self-service drugstore in 1972 at age 25 and built Rossmann into the country's second-largest drugstore chain (~$13B revenue, stores across Central/Eastern Europe). He handed operations to son Raoul in 2021, writes bestselling novels and autobiography, and co-founded the German Foundation for World Population (DSW).
interesting_fact: He is a bestselling author: a 2018 autobiography and the climate thrillers 'The Ninth Arm of the Octopus' (2020) and 'The Wrath of the Octopus' (2021); in 2020 he sent the book 'We Are the Weather' to every Bundestag member and DAX/MDAX board.
deep_cut_fact: His first store opened on 17 March 1972 near Hannover's Lister Platz; opening day was so chaotic that the till held about 20,000 DM instead of the hoped-for 2,000-3,000 DM. The shop ran until 2010 and now bears a commemorative plaque. At 12 he was already earning money delivering drugstore goods.
notes: Press email is labelled 'ROSSMANN-Pressestelle'. He also holds ~20% of Hannover 96. Outspoken on climate and sustainability, a possible energy-themed hook. Company name is spelled Rossmann; family name Roßmann.

name: Andrei Guriev
current_role: Founder and major beneficial owner (via family trust) of PhosAgro; left PhosAgro board as deputy chairman in March 2022
profile: Andrey Grigoryevich Guryev (b. 1960, Lobnya) was a Komsomol official who joined Khodorkovsky's Menatep group in 1990, ran its Apatit phosphate subsidiary and took control of PhosAgro after Khodorkovsky's arrest. He built PhosAgro into one of the world's largest phosphate-fertilizer makers, served as a Murmansk senator (2002-2013) and was deputy board chairman until 2022; his son Andrey A. Guryev ran it as CEO 2013-2022.
interesting_fact: The family owns Witanhurst in Highgate, often described as London's largest private house after Buckingham Palace.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as a sports educator: he graduated in 1983 from Russia's State University of Physical Education, Sport, Youth and Tourism and is a judo master; he later earned an economics degree from the University of Greenwich (2003).
notes: CAUTION: sanctioned by the UK and New Zealand (2022) and Japan (2023); he and his son left PhosAgro's board in March 2022 after EU sanctions on the son (Interfax). Contacting or featuring him may raise legal/reputational issues; check sanctions rules first. Very private. PhosAgro contacts are corporate, not personal.

name: Charles R. Schwab
current_role: Founder and Co-Chairman of the Board, The Charles Schwab Corporation (NYSE: SCHW)
profile: Charles 'Chuck' Schwab (b. 1937, Sacramento) founded what became Charles Schwab & Co. in 1971 and pioneered discount brokerage after fixed commissions were abolished in 1975, building one of the largest US brokerages. He was CEO until 2008 (and again 2004-08), chairman 1986-2022 and has been co-chairman since 2022; Rick Wurster is CEO.
interesting_fact: In his youth he worked as an ice cream salesman, railroad switchman, oil-field roustabout and golf caddie, and captained the Santa Barbara High School golf team.
deep_cut_fact: Before his brokerage, in 1963 he and three partners launched an investment newsletter, 'Investment Indicator', which peaked at about 3,000 subscribers paying $84 a year.

public_contacts.value: Nicole.thorpe@schwab.com (Charles Schwab media relations, May 2026 release)

notes: Age 89. Dataset had no source of wealth; he is the founder of Charles Schwab Corp. Media contacts on Schwab releases vary by topic (Mayura Hooper handles corporate releases by phone). Long-time SFMOMA trustee and golf enthusiast.

name: Robert E. (ted) Turner
profile: Robert Edward 'Ted' Turner III, founder of CNN (1980) and Turner Broadcasting, died on 6 May 2026 at age 87, according to a release from Turner Enterprises reported by AP/CNN.
notes: Deceased (6 May 2026). Sources: Bloomberg Law and AP (e.g., https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/may/6/ted-turner-cnn-founder-brash-outspoken-television-pioneer-died-age-87/). Skipped further research per instructions.

name: Leonard N. Stern
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Hartz Group / Hartz Mountain Industries (New Jersey real estate)
profile: New York-born (1938) NYU graduate who took over his father's Hartz Mountain pet-supply business in 1959, built it into the dominant U.S. pet products firm, then diversified into real estate - Hartz Mountain Industries is now one of the largest private property owners in the NY/NJ region (industrial, office, residential). He sold the pet business in 2000 and earlier owned The Village Voice.
interesting_fact: NYU's business school is the Leonard N. Stern School of Business, renamed after his $30M gift in 1988; he added $50M for undergraduate scholarships in 2021. He also founded the nonprofit Homes for the Homeless in 1986.
deep_cut_fact: He launched Hartz's real estate arm by buying swampy New Jersey Meadowlands land at about $20,000 an acre; by 1987 Meadowlands land sold for ~$500,000 an acre, lifting his holdings there from ~$10M to over $1B as companies moved offices from Manhattan.
notes: Age 88; very private, rarely interviewed. Day-to-day real estate run by family members/executives; best route is Hartz Mountain Industries' corporate office via its website. Meadowlands/Secaucus industrial portfolio is relevant to logistics/data-center land. No published press email found (site JS-rendered).

name: Ray Lee Hunt
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Hunt Consolidated, Inc. (Dallas; oil & gas, LNG, real estate, investments)
profile: Son of wildcatter H.L. Hunt, Ray Hunt (b. 1943, SMU grad) took over Hunt Oil after his father's 1974 death and built Hunt Consolidated into a conglomerate spanning oil and gas, Peru LNG, power/infrastructure and real estate (Hunt Realty, Reunion in Dallas). Now chairman emeritus; son Hunter Hunt runs the energy and infrastructure businesses.
interesting_fact: Hunt Oil was one of the first companies to land an exploration deal in Iraq's Kurdistan region after the fall of Saddam Hussein (2007), and it holds stakes in Peru's natural gas fields and its gas liquefaction plant.
deep_cut_fact: Hunt and John Scovell were 20-somethings who 'didn't know rebar from structural steel' when they started the Reunion project in 1972; Hunt made Scovell president of Woodbine Development as its only employee, and at 32 refused even to read the $35M construction contract, trusting him. Reunion Tower opened April 15, 1978.
notes: Very private family company. Best route is Hunt Consolidated public affairs (media line (214) 978-8534 published on same page). Also trustee/director emeritus at SMU and George W. Bush Presidential Center; son Hunter Hunt is the operational lead for energy/infrastructure.

name: Daniel Ziff
current_role: Private investor (New York); formerly co-head of Ziff Brothers Investments (dissolved 2014)
profile: Youngest son of publishing magnate William Ziff Jr. Daniel (b. 1973, Columbia BA 1996) and his brothers Dirk and Robert inherited the Ziff Davis fortune when their father sold the business for $1.4B in 1994. They grew it through Ziff Brothers Investments, spanning hedge funds, equities, real estate and private equity. Since the firm closed in 2014 he has invested independently, reportedly alongside former employees.
interesting_fact: The family fortune comes from Ziff-Davis, founded in 1927, whose titles included Popular Aviation, PC Magazine and Car and Driver. Their father had hoped to pass the company on to his sons, but they chose to invest instead.
deep_cut_fact: The Ziff brothers gave seed money to hedge-fund manager Daniel Och in exchange for a 10% stake in Och-Ziff Capital Management (the 'Ziff' in the name), which went public in 2007.
notes: Very private: no public statements, social accounts or published office contact found. Philanthropy runs through small private family foundations (performing arts, conservation, NYC causes). No published route; an introduction through a mutual contact is likely the only practical path.

name: Dirk Ziff
current_role: Founder, Ziff Capital Partners (family office, New York); co-owner of the World Surf League via ZoSea
profile: Eldest son of Ziff-Davis publisher William Ziff Jr., Dirk Ziff (b. 1965; Columbia BA, Harvard MBA) and his brothers inherited the fortune after the 1994 $1.4B sale of Ziff-Davis and multiplied it via Ziff Brothers Investments, including seeding Och-Ziff. After ZBI wound down in 2014 he formed Ziff Capital Partners; he and wife Natasha give through Vere Initiatives (environment, journalism, democracy).
interesting_fact: In 2013 an investment vehicle he co-owned with Paul Speaker and Terry Hardy (ZoSea) bought the Association of Surfing Professionals, which became the World Surf League.
deep_cut_fact: The Natasha & Dirk Ziff Foundation's largest recorded grant, about $1.6M, went via WSL PURE (the surf league's ocean nonprofit) to a Columbia University ocean research program; the couple's giving now runs through Vere Initiatives, set up in 2022.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Possible routes: World Surf League communications or Vere Initiatives. Avoid the 2017 Weinstein Company board resignation and real-estate stories.

name: Robert Ziff
current_role: Private investor (co-founder of the former Ziff Brothers Investments); runs the Robert D. Ziff Foundation
profile: Youngest of the three Ziff brothers, heirs to the Ziff Davis publishing fortune (PC Magazine, Car and Driver) that their father William Jr. sold for $1.4B in 1994. The brothers grew it via Ziff Brothers Investments and its hedge funds until it wound down in 2014; they now reportedly invest with former employees. He gives through the New York-based Robert D. Ziff Foundation.
interesting_fact: He graduated magna cum laude from Harvard and ranked first in his class at Cornell Law School.
deep_cut_fact: In 1998 he gave $2 million to Harvard's men's ice hockey program, and Cornell Law School has a 'Robert D. Ziff Professor of Law' chair, first held by civil-procedure scholar Kevin Clermont.
notes: Very private; no interviews, social accounts or published contact found. Foundation (EIN 13-4083712) funds by invitation only and lists no public email. Brothers Dirk and Daniel are separate profiles.

name: Liu Qiangdong
current_role: Founder and Chairman, JD.com (Beijing)
profile: Richard Liu (b. 1973, Suqian) studied sociology at Renmin University, founded Jingdong in 1998 as a Zhongguancun electronics counter and moved online after SARS in 2003-04, building JD.com into China's largest retailer with its own logistics network. JD listed on Nasdaq in 2014; he became chairman-only in 2022 and focuses on long-term strategy.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he turned down an offer to sell JD.com for just RMB 18 million; in April 2024 JD debuted an AI digital avatar of him, 'procurement and sales manager Brother Dong', on a livestream.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after graduating was at Japanese health-products company Japan Life, where he worked as director for computers, director for business and logistics supervisor - experience before he started selling authorised magneto-optical products in Zhongguancun in June 1998, when counterfeits were rife.
notes: Known in English as Richard Liu; Hurun entry shared with spouse. Data-center angle: JD Cloud / JD Technology. Avoid the 2018 Minneapolis matter. Route via JD media team.

name: Zhang Zetian
current_role: Businesswoman and investor; associated with JD.com (formerly chief fashion adviser of its luxury business); Hurun lists her wealth jointly with JD founder Liu Qiangdong
profile: Nanjing-born (1993) businesswoman who went viral as a teen as 'Sister Milk Tea', studied at Tsinghua (exchange at Barnard) and later took a Cambridge MBA. Married JD.com founder Richard Liu in 2015; her Hurun fortune derives from the couple's JD holdings. Was fashion adviser to JD's luxury business; invests via her own company.
interesting_fact: New Fortune's 2017 China top-500 rich list made her the youngest woman on it, and she was widely described as China's youngest female billionaire.
deep_cut_fact: After her viral 2009 photo, she starred in a promotional video for the 2014 Nanjing Youth Olympics but resisted further celebrity, turning down a film role offered by director Zhang Yimou.
notes: Wealth on Hurun is shared with Liu Qiangdong (JD). She holds no confirmed current executive title at JD; current business role is unclear. Very little 2025-26 English coverage. Only corporate JD contacts available - not a personal route.

name: Sri Prakash Lohia
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Indorama Corporation
profile: Kolkata-born (1952) Indonesian billionaire who moved to Indonesia in 1973 with his father to start Indorama Synthetics (spun yarns, 1976). He built Indorama Corporation into a diversified petrochemicals, fertilizer, polyester and gloves group; his 2006 purchase of a Nigerian olefins plant became West Africa's largest petrochemical complex. Son Amit is vice chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he acquired a struggling integrated olefin plant in Nigeria and turned it into the largest petrochemical company in West Africa; Indorama marked its 50th anniversary (Golden Jubilee) in Dubai in late 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started buying a few old hand-coloured 'colour plate' books around 2008 as a hobby; it grew into one of the world's premier private collections of the genre (21,500+ images), which he had digitised and made freely viewable online so anyone, regardless of language, can enjoy the plates.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Brother-in-law of Lakshmi Mittal. Son Amit Lohia (vice chairman) is the more public face. Not to be confused with brother Aloke Lohia of Indorama Ventures (Thailand).

name: Li Yanhong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Baidu Inc.
profile: Li Yanhong (Robin Li) co-founded Baidu in 2000 with Eric Xu after search-engine stints at IDD/Dow Jones and Infoseek in the US. Baidu became China's dominant search engine; Li has since steered it into AI (ERNIE large models, AI cloud) and Apollo/Apollo Go autonomous driving.
interesting_fact: Before Baidu, Li built RankDex (1996), an early search engine that ranked pages by the links pointing to them, a link-analysis idea that predated Google's PageRank.
deep_cut_fact: Li is the named inventor on US patent 5,920,859, 'Hypertext Document Retrieval System and Method' (filed Feb 1997, issued July 1999), written while he was at IDD Information Services, a Dow Jones unit where he also worked on software for the online Wall Street Journal.
notes: Known in English as Robin Li. The listed SEC insider roles (Datadog CPO, Equinix director) belong to a different person, Yanbing Li; this is a name-match error, not Robin Li. Best route is via Baidu corporate/IR.

name: Cao Renxian
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sungrow Power Supply Co., Ltd. (300274.SZ)
profile: Cao Renxian (曹仁贤) grew up in a poor rural family, studied industrial automation at Hefei University of Technology and taught there before founding Sungrow in 1997. Sungrow became one of the world's largest makers of solar PV inverters and energy storage systems, selling into the Middle East, Southeast Asia, Europe and the U.S. He remains chairman of the Shenzhen-listed company.
interesting_fact: Sungrow, founded by a university lecturer in renewable-energy power electronics, grew into what it calls the world's leading inverter and energy storage system supplier, with over 269 GW of inverters installed worldwide by mid-2022.
deep_cut_fact: Cao launched Sungrow on 28 November 1997 in a humble rented house in Anhui at age 30, quitting his secure university teaching job while newly married, and funded it with about 80,000 yuan of his own savings plus money from friends and relatives.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is Sungrow corporate communications or IR (the IR email is the company's published investor contact). Deep-cut source for the rented-house date is Sungrow's 25th-anniversary release (aap.com.au link); the savings figure comes from Wikipedia.

name: Sudhir Mehta
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Torrent Group (Torrent Pharmaceuticals, Torrent Power), Ahmedabad
profile: Elder son of Torrent founder U.N. Mehta, Sudhir Mehta became group chairman in 1998 and built Torrent from a pharma firm (Trinity Laboratories) into a pharma-power-gas conglomerate. He handed the chair to brother Samir in the 2010s and stepped off the Torrent Pharma board in March 2024, remaining Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: He pushed Torrent Pharma into exports, entering Russia during its 1990s political turmoil; Torrent later built a strong presence in Europe, Russia and Brazil. Business Standard describes him as extremely media-shy, avoiding interviews and press briefings.
deep_cut_fact: When India opened power to private players in 1991, he began quietly buying shares of Ahmedabad Electricity Co. and Surat Electricity Co., taking majority stakes by the late 1990s - the origin of Torrent Power, which went on to build the 1,147.5 MW Sugen gas-fired plant.
notes: Very media-shy; largely retired from active business. Brother Samir Mehta is group chairman; approach via Torrent corporate/company secretary channels. Group energy arm (Torrent Power, Torrent Gas) is the podcast-relevant angle.

name: Samir Mehta
current_role: Chairman, Torrent Group; Executive Chairman, Torrent Pharmaceuticals (reappointed for 5 years from Apr 2025)
profile: Ahmedabad-based chairman of the Torrent Group (pharmaceuticals, power, and more), founded by his father U.N. Mehta. He succeeded his elder brother Sudhir as group chairman in 2014 and has grown Torrent Pharma into a global generics player in ~40 countries, while Torrent Power is a major Indian power utility/generator.
interesting_fact: In March 2025 the Torrent Group completed the purchase of a 67% majority stake in IPL cricket franchise Gujarat Titans from CVC-controlled Irelia, reportedly for about Rs 5,035 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Torrent, he serves as President of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance (IPA), the lobby group of India's largest research-based drugmakers, where his bio highlights his push for an employee-centric workplace promoting equality and fairness.
notes: Energy angle is Torrent Power (Ahmedabad/Surat utility, renewables, pumped storage). Low public profile; route via Torrent corporate communications/IR.

name: Michael Kadoorie
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, CLP Holdings; Non-executive Chairman, The Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels (Peninsula Hotels)
profile: Sir Michael Kadoorie (b. 1941) heads the Kadoorie family interests in Hong Kong: CLP Holdings, the power utility the family co-founded that serves ~80% of Hong Kong, and Hongkong and Shanghai Hotels, owner of The Peninsula hotels. Still chairing CLP in 2026, he opened its May 2026 AGM and is overseeing power investment for the Northern Metropolis.
interesting_fact: He is the scion of a Baghdadi-Jewish family whose grandfather Elly Kadoorie settled in Shanghai in 1880; he is also a keen photographer and classic-car collector (Bugatti Type 57, Hispano-Suiza J12, Lamborghini Miura).
deep_cut_fact: He is a helicopter pilot: Heliservices (HK) was founded in 1978 after he bought Hong Kong's first private helicopter. He still chairs it, and it flies from the Peninsula's rooftop helipad and washes power-line insulators for HK utilities.
notes: Very private, aged 85; no personal social media. CLP press office (named contact changes per release) or the HSH/Peninsula corporate office are the realistic routes. Aviation (Heliservices, Metrojet) is a good conversational hook.

name: Rinat Akhmetov
current_role: Founder and owner, System Capital Management (SCM) group (Metinvest, DTEK); president of FC Shakhtar Donetsk
profile: Ukraine's richest person and the son of a Donetsk coal miner. He built SCM by buying mining and steel assets during 1990s privatisation; it now holds steelmaker Metinvest and energy company DTEK, Ukraine's largest private power producer. His plants and substations have been heavily damaged in the war, but he has stayed in Ukraine and funds reconstruction and aid.
interesting_fact: Through SCM's 'Steel Front' initiative, his companies make fortifications and other defensive equipment for Ukraine's military, including protection for US-supplied Abrams tanks.
deep_cut_fact: His 'Heart of Azovstal' project began with a call to Azovstal commander Denys Prokopenko 15 minutes before the defenders left the plant. Prokopenko asked him to 'take care of my men', and Akhmetov launched the project in January 2023 with $25M for Mariupol defenders and families of fallen soldiers.
notes: Very private; speaks mainly through SCM press statements. SCM's communications director is Natalia Yemchenko (Kyiv Post). DTEK (energy arm) is the most relevant angle for an energy podcast. scm.com.ua and dtek.com sit behind bot protection, so their contact pages could not be verified. Avoid oligarch/politics framing.

name: Li Ping
current_role: Vice Chairman, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL)
profile: Li Ping (b. 1968) is vice chairman and co-controlling shareholder (with chairman Robin Zeng) of CATL, the world's largest EV battery maker, founded in 2011 and dual-listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong; he holds ~4.3% of the company. He previously worked at electrical engineering firms and holds a Fudan degree and a CEIBS MBA. CATL licenses tech to Ford's Michigan battery plant, completed June 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2025 Li and his wife Liao Mei donated 4.05 million CATL shares (about 1 billion yuan) to their alma mater Fudan University; the transfer was registered on July 10, 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Li studied polymers at Fudan (class of 1985), while his wife Liao Mei was a Fudan history major (class of 1986); their 1-billion-yuan gift funds Fudan's new Xue Min Institute of Advanced Studies.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews (some speeches at CATL events). The only route is CATL corporate (IR/media). Sources disagree on when he became vice chairman (2015 or 2017).

name: Oleg Deripaska
current_role: Founder, Basic Element; major shareholder of En+ Group (which controls Rusal)
profile: Russian industrialist who built Siberian Aluminium in the 1990s and merged it with Abramovich's assets in 2000 to form Rusal. Founder of Basic Element (metals, energy, construction, agriculture). Sanctioned by the US (2018), UK and EU; his En+/Rusal stake was cut to resolve US sanctions on the companies in 2019. In 2026 he is a vocal commentator on Russia's economy.
interesting_fact: Through his Volnoe Delo foundation he has funded the Phanagoria excavation since 2004, which made him Russia's single biggest donor to archaeology and Phanagoria the country's best-financed dig.
deep_cut_fact: He enrolled in physics at Moscow State University in 1985 and graduated with honours in 1993. Before that he served in the Soviet Strategic Missile Forces in Trans-Baikal from 1986 to 1989. Shrinking academic funding ended his plan to become a theoretical physicist, and he moved into metals trading.
notes: Sanctioned by the US, UK, EU, Canada and Australia, so check compliance and legal issues before any outreach. He posts on an official Telegram channel that the press quotes often, but I could not verify the exact handle. His official site deripaska.com and the Basic Element site basel.ru were unreachable from this environment.

name: Mikhail Gutseriev
current_role: Founder and main shareholder / chairman, Safmar Group (oil, coal, real estate, retail; Russia)
profile: Russian-Ingush billionaire (b. 1958, Akmolinsk) who ran Slavneft, then founded oil producer RussNeft in 2002; fled to London in 2007 amid tax charges and returned in 2010. Built Safmar Group (RussNeft, Russian Coal, Neftisa, A101 developer). Sanctioned by UK and EU in 2021 over ties to Lukashenko; in 2022 transferred assets to a relative.
interesting_fact: He owns Moscow's Hotel National, where Donald Trump stayed on his first Russia trip in 1987, owns radio stations incl. Radio Shanson, and writes song lyrics performed by well-known Russian singers.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil, he trained in 'Leather and Fur Technology' (Dzhambul Technological Institute, 1981) and worked as a process engineer in Grozny; in 2005 he funded the rebuilding of his old Grozny high school No. 23, destroyed in the First Chechen War.
notes: Contact is the SAFMAR Charitable Foundation (his foundation) site, which looks dated (c.2014). Subject to UK sanctions (EU sanctions litigated; EU General Court annulled some listings 2025-26). Reputational/legal sensitivity for any engagement.

name: Mike Brown
current_role: Owner and President, Cincinnati Bengals (NFL)
profile: Mike Brown (b. 1935) is the son of coaching legend Paul Brown. He helped his father found the Cincinnati Bengals in 1967–68, served as assistant GM, and took over as owner after Paul's death in 1991. The Brown family still runs the team, with daughter Katie Blackburn as executive VP. Forbes valued the Bengals at more than $5B in 2025.
interesting_fact: The Bengals reached Super Bowl LVI under Brown's ownership in the 2021 season. That run brought the franchise's first playoff win since 1990 and its first-ever road playoff win.
deep_cut_fact: Brown played quarterback at Dartmouth (class of 1957) and graduated from Harvard Law School in 1960. As a young man he had a summer job as a deck hand at Kinsman Marine Transit, hired by George Steinbrenner long before either of them owned a pro sports team.
notes: He is 91 and rarely gives interviews beyond team press events. Bengals media relations (bengals.com/news/media) is the professional route. He is a poor fit for an energy/data-center angle.

name: Daniel Nadler
current_role: Cofounder & CEO, OpenEvidence
profile: Canadian-born AI entrepreneur with a Harvard Ph.D. in economics. Cofounded Kensho (AI for financial analytics), sold to S&P Global for $550M in 2018. In 2022 cofounded OpenEvidence, an AI medical-search tool free for verified doctors and ad-supported; valued at ~$12B in early 2026, with Nadler owning nearly 60%.
interesting_fact: OpenEvidence has signed up more than 758,000 doctors and was adding ~55,000 per month; it is free for verified clinicians and earns money from advertising.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published poet: his debut collection 'Lacunae: 100 Imagined Ancient Love Poems' (Farrar, Straus and Giroux, 2016) presents short poems as imagined translations of lost ancient texts. He studied poetry at Harvard under Pulitzer winner Jorie Graham.
notes: contact@openevidence.com is the general company contact in the site footer, not a dedicated press line. Poetry is a good angle for outreach; Forbes notes his Ph.D. thesis was on credit-derivative pricing.

name: Bruce Cheng
current_role: Founder and Honorary Chairman, Delta Electronics (Taiwan); Chairman, Delta Electronics Foundation
profile: Electrical engineer (BSEE, National Cheng Kung University) who founded Delta Electronics in 1971 as a TV-parts maker and built it into the world's leading switching power-supply maker, now a major supplier of power and thermal management for AI data centres, EVs and automation. He stepped down as chairman in 2012; son Ping Cheng is chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Taiwanese media dubbed him Taiwan's first 'CEO — Chief Environmental Officer'; since 2006 Delta has built all its new offices and factories worldwide as green buildings, and in March 2026 he joined Amory Lovins on a Delta 55th-anniversary panel on energy and AI.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 the International Astronomical Union named asteroid 168126 'Chengbruce' in his honour for his environmental work. Before founding Delta he worked at TRW and at Air Asia Co.
notes: Born 1936; still active in Delta events in 2026. Excellent fit for energy/data-center podcast (Delta is a key AI-server power supplier). Chinese name 鄭崇華. Delta Electronics Foundation is the most natural route for an energy/sustainability conversation.

name: Jacques Servier
profile: Jacques Servier (1922-2014), French physician and founder of pharmaceutical group Laboratoires Servier, died on 16 April 2014 in Neuilly-sur-Seine, aged 92. Servier is now controlled by a foundation structure.
notes: Deceased (16 April 2014) per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Servier ; skipped remaining research. Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Khalaf Al Habtoor
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Al Habtoor Group (Dubai)
profile: Khalaf Ahmad Al Habtoor (b. 1949, Dubai) went to work at 14 and founded Al Habtoor Engineering in 1970. It became Al Habtoor Group: hotels (with Hilton and Marriott), car distribution (Mitsubishi, Bugatti), real estate, education and publishing. A prolific political columnist, in 2025 he agreed to invest in Syria, including a bus network.
interesting_fact: His 572-page autobiography (Motivate Publishing, 2012) won 'Best International Book on Business and Economics' at the 2013 Sharjah International Book Fair; in 2017 he opened an interactive 'Life Journey' exhibition about his own life.
deep_cut_fact: From 1994 to 1997 he was the only non-American member of the USO (United Services Organization) World Board of Governors; he has also served on the UAE Federal National Council and chaired the Commercial Bank of Dubai.
notes: Highly media-friendly; writes columns and gives interviews. His personal website contact form and X account are the best direct routes. Outspoken on Middle East politics — keep outreach to business/entrepreneurship.

name: JK Irving
profile: James K. (J.K.) Irving, longtime chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and eldest son of K.C. Irving, died June 21, 2024 in Saint John, New Brunswick, aged 96.
interesting_fact: He was the last surviving son of Irving Group founder K.C. Irving; his brother Arthur (Irving Oil) died about a month before him.
notes: Deceased (June 21, 2024). Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2024-06-21/james-k-irving-canadian-forestry-billionaire-dies-at-96 . His son Robert K. Irving, co-CEO of JDI, reportedly died May 2026; Jim (J.D.) Irving remains co-CEO.

name: Stephen M. Ross
current_role: Founder & non-executive chairman, Related Companies; owner, Miami Dolphins and Hard Rock Stadium; chairman, Related Ross
profile: Detroit-raised Stephen Ross founded Related Companies in 1972 and built it into a $60B+ real-estate empire whose signature project is Manhattan's Hudson Yards. Now non-executive chairman, he focuses on Related Ross, the Miami Dolphins and the Miami F1 Grand Prix. Related's data-center arm Related Digital (launched 2025) is building a $16B, 1GW+ Oracle/OpenAI AI campus in Saline Township, Michigan.
interesting_fact: He is among the University of Michigan's largest donors — its business school and athletic campus bear his name — and founded RISE (Ross Initiative in Sports for Equality) to use sports to fight racism.
deep_cut_fact: A former Coopers & Lybrand tax attorney, he started Related in 1972 living off a $10,000 loan from his mother, using his tax-law know-how to syndicate deals for subsidized affordable housing — and earned $150,000 in his first year. His law degrees were financed by a loan from his uncle Max Fisher.
notes: Age ~86. Related's published press inbox is the best route. Strong data-center angle via Related Digital (see https://www.related.com/press-releases/2026-04-24/related-digital-announces-financing-16-billion-oracle-data-center-project). Avoid: 2020 fundraiser backlash and 2022 NFL tampering suspension.

name: Mao Wenchao
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Xiaohongshu (RedNote), Shanghai
profile: Wuhan-born (1985) Mao Wenchao (Charlwin Mao) studied mechatronics at SJTU, worked at Bain and in PE, and took a Stanford MBA (2013) before co-founding Xiaohongshu with Miranda Qu that June. RedNote has 300M+ users and drew 'TikTok refugees' in Jan 2025, and Reuters reported in June 2026 that it hired Goldman and CICC for a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: The 'Little Red Book' name has no Mao Zedong reference, he says: it came from the red colours of Bain and Stanford. The product began in 2013 as downloadable PDF shopping guides for Chinese tourists, and the first app was called 'Hong Kong Shopping Guide'.
deep_cut_fact: Xiaohongshu uses in-house nicknames: Mao goes by 'Seiya' and co-founder Miranda Qu by 'Mulan'. Staff can bring dogs and cats to the office on Fridays. Before founding it he had travelled to 20+ countries, which inspired the overseas-shopping idea.
notes: Keeps a low public profile; co-founder Miranda Qu is more often the public face. No published press or IR email found. If the Hong Kong IPO proceeds, the prospectus will list IR contacts. Approach via Xiaohongshu's official account or corporate PR.

name: Joseph Liemandt
current_role: Principal of Alpha School / founder of 2 Hour Learning; founder of ESW Capital and Trilogy Software
profile: Joe Liemandt dropped out of Stanford to found Trilogy Software and was the youngest self-made member of the 1996 Forbes 400. His ESW Capital has bought 100+ software companies. He now leads Alpha School and its AI-driven '2 Hour Learning' model, reportedly funding its AI software with about $1B of his own money.
interesting_fact: After his Forbes-cover fame, he 'vanished from public life for 25 years' before re-emerging as Alpha School's principal. He aims to bring AI tutoring to a billion learners.
deep_cut_fact: On The Knowledge Project (2026) he discussed sleeping on the floor in Trilogy's early days and being mentored by GE's Jack Welch.

public_contacts.value: Alpha School media contact: Daphne Ortiz, 312.488.3472 (listed on Alpha School press releases)

notes: Long reclusive but since 2025 a regular podcast guest (Knowledge Project, Joe Lonsdale, Peter Attia, Masters of Scale), so podcast outreach about AI/education is plausible. MacKenzie Price is Alpha's main public face. Avoid the critical coverage of Alpha's results and ESW's labor model.

name: Ali Ghodsi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Databricks (San Francisco); adjunct professor, UC Berkeley
profile: Iranian-born Swedish-American computer scientist (b. 1978) whose family fled to Sweden after the 1979 revolution. A KTH PhD, he joined UC Berkeley's AMPLab in 2009 and helped start Apache Mesos and Apache Spark. In 2013 he co-founded Databricks with six Berkeley colleagues, became CEO in 2016, and led its turnaround into the 'data lakehouse'/AI platform, valued at $134B in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Ghodsi joined Databricks in 2013 as a part-time engineer and was a first-time CEO when tapped in 2016 amid revenue struggles. He then rebuilt the leadership and products, taking the company to a $134B private valuation.
deep_cut_fact: He co-invented 'Dominant Resource Fairness' (NSDI 2011, with Zaharia, Shenker, Stoica and others), a scheme for fairly sharing CPU and memory across cluster users that shaped scheduling in Hadoop YARN and Mesos. Earlier he co-founded Stockholm P2P startup Peerialism.
notes: Very accessible and a frequent podcast guest; a strong fit for the data-center/AI angle. Best route is Databricks press (press@databricks.com). He is active on X and LinkedIn, but no handle was verified from an official page in this pass. He learned to program on a broken Commodore 64 as a child (btw.media, secondary source).

name: Marian Ilitch
current_role: Chairman, Ilitch Holdings; owner of Little Caesars, Detroit Red Wings and MotorCity Casino Hotel
profile: Marian Ilitch (b. 1933, Dearborn) co-founded Little Caesars Pizza with her husband Mike in 1959 in Garden City, Michigan; after his 2017 death she became sole owner of the chain (5bn+ in systemwide sales), the Detroit Red Wings and MotorCity Casino, while son Chris runs Ilitch Holdings as CEO. In 2026 the family formed Ilitch Gaming to expand into casinos beyond Detroit.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Little Caesars she worked as a Delta Air Lines ticket agent; she met Mike Ilitch on a blind date, and in the early days had to stop him from giving away free pizzas.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Dearborn to Macedonian immigrants, she was honored when Michigan's governor proclaimed 'Marian Ilitch Day' on May 8, the anniversary of the 1959 opening of the first 'Little Caesars Pizza Treat', and the NHL called her 'the most impactful woman owner in the league'.
notes: In her 90s and rarely gives interviews; Chris Ilitch is the family's public face. No published media email found; route via Ilitch Companies communications (Ilitch News Hub). Ilitch family charities have given $250m+, incl. $40m to Wayne State (Mike Ilitch School of Business).

name: Alain Bouchard
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairman of the Board, Alimentation Couche-Tard (Circle K), Laval, Quebec
profile: Bouchard opened his first Couche-Tard convenience store in Quebec in 1980 and built it through serial acquisitions (Circle K 2003, Statoil Fuel & Retail 2012, CST Brands and Holiday 2017, TotalEnergies stations 2024) into a global chain of 17,000+ stores. He handed the CEO role to Brian Hannasch in 2014 (now Alex Miller) and remains executive chairman; he chaired the 2026 AGM.
interesting_fact: He got his start stocking shelves at his brother's franchised Perrette store and climbed the ladder at two chains before striking out on his own.
deep_cut_fact: Through the Sandra and Alain Bouchard Foundation (created 2012 with his wife Sandra Chartrand), he funded a $4M Sandra and Alain Bouchard Intellectual Disability Research Program at Montreal's Neurological Institute; the foundation also backs arts and culture.
notes: Francophone; media route via Couche-Tard Media Relations. Energy angle: Circle K is a major fuel retailer rolling out EV fast-charging. Avoid the failed Carrefour and Seven & i bids as hooks.

name: Cliff Obrecht
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Operating Officer, Canva (Sydney)
profile: Cliff Obrecht co-founded Canva in Sydney in 2013 with now-wife Melanie Perkins and Cameron Adams, after the pair built Fusion Books, an online school-yearbook business started in Perth in 2008 that became Australia's largest. As COO he runs operations at Canva, valued at $42B in Aug 2025 with ~240M monthly users. He and Perkins (~18% each) pledged most of their stake to the Canva Foundation.
interesting_fact: Obrecht proposed to cofounder Melanie Perkins in Cappadocia, Turkey, with a $30 engagement ring; the couple has pledged to give more than 80% of their Canva stake to charitable causes via the Canva Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: Of the Fusion Books days, run out of Perkins' mum's living room in Perth, he said: 'We had no idea we were a startup, we thought we were a small business.' He has also mentioned unplugging on adventurous trips, like riding horses in Mongolia and staying in tree houses in Laos.

public_contacts.value: Appeared on 20VC #971: 'How We Turned Our Yearbook Company to $40B Business'

notes: Canva's press address varies by release (press@canva.com in 2022-23, comms@canva.com in 2024-25); confirm on latest release. Obrecht does podcasts (20VC) - receptive to long-form interviews. Canva newsroom site blocks automated access.

name: Melanie Perkins
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Canva
profile: Perth-born Melanie Perkins co-founded Sydney-based design platform Canva in 2013 with Cliff Obrecht and Cameron Adams after early investor skepticism; it was valued at $42B in Aug 2025 and serves ~240M monthly users. She and Obrecht each own ~18% and have pledged most of their stake to the Canva Foundation.
interesting_fact: To win over kiteboarding-enthusiast VCs including angel investor Bill Tai, Perkins learned kitesurfing.
deep_cut_fact: Canva's precursor was Fusion Books (2007), which she and Obrecht built so schools could design yearbooks with an online drag-and-drop editor; it became a large Australian yearbook business and expanded to New Zealand and France.
notes: Canva press contact has shifted (press@canva.com in 2022-23 releases; comms@canva.com in 2024-25). She is active publicly via Canva events; check her verified LinkedIn/X before use.

name: Jeffrey Koo Jr
current_role: President, Baseball Federation of Asia; Executive VP, WBSC; chairman, CTBC Charity Foundation; major shareholder of CTBC Financial Holding
profile: Jeffrey Koo Jr. (辜仲諒) is a fourth-generation scion of Taiwan's Koo family and a major shareholder of CTBC Financial Holding, set up in 2002 by his late father Jeffrey Koo Sr. (banking, insurance, brokerage; ~27,000 staff). Formerly CTBC Financial's vice chairman and president, he now focuses on baseball: he led Taiwan's baseball association 2018-2026 and heads the Baseball Federation of Asia.
interesting_fact: A former baseball player, he was elected president of the Baseball Federation of Asia in 2022; his CTBC group owns the CTBC Brothers pro team.
deep_cut_fact: In his last task as chairman of the Chinese Taipei Baseball Association (Aug 2026), he flew to Shanghai to lobby WBSC president Riccardo Fraccari and won hosting rights for Taiwan's 2027 Premier12 preliminary round and a 2028 Olympic final qualifying tournament.
notes: Holds no executive role at CTBC Financial now; best approached via baseball (Baseball Federation of Asia / CTBC Brothers) or the CTBC Charity Foundation. He is a defendant in an ongoing Taiwan court case (first-instance sentence reported in 2026; travel needs court approval) - sensitive, avoid in outreach. Brothers Andre and Angelo Koo are also billionaires.

name: Steven A. Ballmer
current_role: Owner, LA Clippers; co-founder, Ballmer Group; founder, USAFacts
profile: Steve Ballmer joined Microsoft in 1980 as its first business manager and was CEO from 2000 to 2014; his retained Microsoft stake makes him one of the world's richest people. He owns the LA Clippers (bought in 2014; built the Intuit Dome), funds economic-mobility work through Ballmer Group, and created the government-data nonprofit USAFacts.
interesting_fact: Ballmer launched USAFacts in 2017 after wondering where government money actually goes; it is a nonprofit that turns federal, state and local spending and outcomes data into plain-English figures.
deep_cut_fact: Ballmer lived in Brussels from 1964 to 1967 (International School of Brussels), scored 800 on SAT maths, and at Harvard managed the football team and outscored dorm-mate Bill Gates on the Putnam maths competition. He then worked as an assistant product manager at Procter & Gamble.
notes: Input record is a 1997 Forbes entry with no source of wealth (Microsoft). USAFacts media email is the published press route to one of his organisations; the Clippers' PR office is the other. He has been publicly enthusiastic about AI and data, which is useful for a data-centre podcast.

name: Edward Johnson
profile: Edward C. 'Ned' Johnson III, longtime chairman/CEO of Fidelity Investments, died 23 March 2022 at his home in Florida, aged 91 (per Bloomberg / daughter Abigail Johnson).
notes: Deceased - skip. Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-03-24/edward-johnson-iii-fund-pioneer-who-led-fidelity-dies-at-91 (also https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Johnson_III). Identity inferred from Forbes 2001-07 finance listing at ~$7.5B; Fidelity is now led by daughter Abigail Johnson.

name: Gordon Earl Moore
notes: Gordon E. Moore, Intel co-founder and author of Moore's law, died 24 March 2023 in Hawaii (aged 94). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gordon_Moore . Legacy continues via the Gordon and Betty Moore Foundation. Skipped rest per instructions.

name: Leise Maersk McKinney Moller
current_role: Maersk family heir and shareholder; former board member of the A.P. Moller Foundation (1991-2016)
profile: Eldest daughter of Danish shipping magnate Maersk Mc-Kinney Moller (1913-2012), born 1941; her wealth derives from family stakes in A.P. Moller-Maersk. She sat on the controlling A.P. Moller Foundation board from 1991 to 2016, then handed her seat to her daughter Alette; sister Ane Maersk Mc-Kinney Uggla succeeded their father as chair.
interesting_fact: She joined the A.P. Moller Foundation board in 1991 under her father's chairmanship and stepped down in 2016 in an orderly generational handover to her daughter, part of the five-generation Maersk family stewardship model.
notes: Extremely private; no public statements found. Alive status not confirmed (born 1941; no death report found in 2025-26 searches). Last appeared on Hurun list 2018. Only realistic route is via A.P. Moller Holding; unlikely podcast guest.

name: Liu Mingzhong
current_role: Co-founder, Deputy Chairman & CEO, Nine Dragons Paper (Holdings) Ltd (HKEX: 2689)
profile: Liu Ming Chung (刘名中) co-founded Nine Dragons Paper with his wife, chairlady Zhang Yin (Cheung Yan), and has been deputy chairman and CEO since 2006, overseeing management, manufacturing technology, equipment procurement and HR. Nine Dragons turns recovered paper into containerboard and is Asia's largest paperboard producer.
interesting_fact: Nine Dragons' Dongguan facility runs 15 paper machines producing about 5.25 million tonnes a year, described as the world's largest concentrated paper mill.
deep_cut_fact: Before paper he trained as a dentist: he earned a bachelor's degree in Dental Surgery from the University of Santo Amaro (Sao Paulo, Brazil) in 1983. He is also an honorary citizen of Dongguan.
notes: Hurun listing is shared with wife Zhang Yin (Cheung Yan), the chairlady. Low media profile; the IR inbox published in the annual report is the best route.

name: Alexei Kuzmichov
current_role: Private investor; co-founder of Alfa Group and LetterOne (no longer on LetterOne's board after 2022 sanctions)
profile: Alexey Kuzmichev (Kuzmichov, b. 1962, Kirov) co-founded Alfa Group with Mikhail Fridman and German Khan, running its commodity-trading arm; Alfa's holdings included Alfa-Bank, VimpelCom, X5 and a half-share of TNK-BP, sold to Rosneft in 2013. He co-founded Luxembourg-based LetterOne. He has been sanctioned by the EU, UK, Canada, Australia (2022) and the US (OFAC SDN, 2023).

notes: CAUTION: on the US OFAC SDN list (Aug 2023) and sanctioned by EU/UK/Canada/Australia - check legal implications before any outreach or paid arrangement. No public contact channel. Not a recommended podcast target.

name: David Thomson
current_role: Chairman, Thomson Reuters; chairman, The Woodbridge Company (Thomson family holding) and The Globe and Mail
profile: David Thomson, 3rd Baron Thomson of Fleet (b. 1957, Toronto), heads the third generation of the Roy Thomson media dynasty. He chairs Thomson Reuters, controlled through the family's Woodbridge investment firm, and The Globe and Mail. Through his own real-estate firm Osmington he co-owns the NHL's Winnipeg Jets and Montreal Canadiens, and he is a major art collector.
interesting_fact: To establish independence from the family empire he founded real-estate firm Osmington, which owns Winnipeg's Canada Life Centre, is redeveloping retail at Toronto's Union Station and in 2023 brought Shake Shack to Canada.
deep_cut_fact: A Cambridge history graduate (Selwyn College, 1978), he started as a junior associate at Toronto brokerage McLeod Young Weir and, inside the family business, once managed The Bay department store at Cloverdale Mall in Etobicoke before becoming president of Zellers.
notes: Notably private; avoids interviews. info@osmington.com is the general inbox of his own real-estate company (not personal). Role confirmed on Thomson Reuters board page (2026).

name: Peter Thomson
current_role: Chairman, The Woodbridge Company (Thomson family holding); Director, Thomson Reuters; Chairman & Founder, Thomvest
profile: Peter J. Thomson (b. 1965, Toronto) is the younger son of Kenneth Thomson and grandson of press baron Roy Thomson. He co-chairs Woodbridge, which controls Thomson Reuters, and sits on its board. Separately he founded Thomvest in 1996, a venture firm and family investment office (San Francisco and Toronto, ~$750M AUM) investing on behalf of him and his family, including in AI such as Cohere.

public_contacts.value: https://www.thomvest.com/ (offices: 138 South Park St, San Francisco; Toronto)

notes: Private, low-profile heir; best route is via Thomvest (VC firm with public office numbers on its contact page, no email published). The AI/sovereign-compute investing angle (Cohere) fits a data-center podcast. Don't confuse with Peter Thomson the Australian golfer.

name: Taylor Thomson
current_role: Co-owner (with brothers David and Peter and four cousins) of The Woodbridge Company, the Thomson family holding company
profile: Taylor Thomson, daughter of the late Kenneth Thomson and granddaughter of Roy Thomson, is one of seven family owners of Woodbridge, the Toronto holding company that controls about two-thirds of Thomson Reuters plus The Globe and Mail; her share equals roughly 14% of the business. She keeps a very low public profile.

deep_cut_fact: In 2013 she and her brothers David and Peter gave $5M to Toronto's Royal Conservatory of Music to endow the Marilyn Thomson Early Childhood Education Centre, expanding music education for young children.

Probably not a fit for outreach; if needed, Thomson Reuters corporate communications is the only published route and would not speak for her.

name: Zeng Fangqin
current_role: Chairwoman and General Manager, Guangdong Lingyi iTech Manufacturing (领益智造; SZSE: 002600, HKEX: 1688)
profile: Zeng Fangqin (曾芳勤, b. 1965, Hong Kong citizen) left a multinational in 2006 to found Lingsheng Electronics, then Lingyi Technology in 2012. Lingyi makes precision components, modules, thermal parts and chargers for smartphones, PCs and wearables, supplying Apple and Huawei. It completed a backdoor listing in Shenzhen in 2018 and a Hong Kong dual listing in June 2026, and is pushing into AI-server hardware and humanoid-robot parts.

deep_cut_fact: Before electronics she was deputy general manager of the Shenzhen Ocean Fishing Company (深圳市远洋渔业公司), a deep-sea fishing firm. She later ran Guangdong Fuhai and was China regional GM of precision-machining firm 美时精密加工 before founding her own company in May 2006.
notes: Low media profile. Her Forbes bio says she began her career in Silicon Valley, but the company's official resume does not mention it. Best route is the IR mailbox or the board secretary (VP Guo Rui). Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Maria Angelicoussis
current_role: CEO and owner, Angelicoussis Group (Athens) - Maran Tankers, Maran Gas Maritime, Anangel Maritime
profile: Third-generation head of one of the world's largest private shipping groups (~158 vessels across crude tankers, LNG carriers and dry bulk), founded by her grandfather Antonis in 1947. Best route is via industry events where she speaks (e.g. LNG2026 / World LNG Summit speaker listings) or Maran Gas/Maran Tankers corporate offices in Athens. Energy angle: major LNG carrier owner (Maran Gas). Avoid family/health topics.

name: John Grayken
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Lone Star Funds (stepped down as CEO in 2024; Donald Quintin succeeded him)
profile: Raised in Cohasset, Massachusetts (Penn, Harvard MBA). After Morgan Stanley and Robert Bass's real-estate firm, he founded Lone Star Funds in 1995 and built it into a global distressed-asset investor that has raised about $95B across some 25 funds. He took Irish citizenship in 1999 and lives in London.

The Novo Banco sale price comes from a wiki mirror, so check it against the Lone Star/BPCE press release. The hockey detail comes from Forbes facts. Avoid tax-citizenship and the India police case.

name: Safra siblings (Jacob, David, Alberto Safra and Esther Safra Dayan)
current_role: Jacob: chairman/president, J. Safra Sarasin (Switzerland); David: heads Banco Safra (Brazil); Alberto: founder, ASA (Brazil/US); Esther: sold her Banco Safra stake to Jacob and David in 2025

Safra Sarasin, Safra National Bank of New York) and David runs Banco Safra in Brazil; with their mother Vicky they now control the bank. Alberto left in 2019 to found ASA, an investment and private bank, and has since exited the family group.

name: Edward Roski Jr
current_role: President and Chairman, Majestic Realty Co. (Los Angeles)
profile: Ed Roski Jr. (b. 1938) runs Majestic Realty, the industrial and business-park developer his father founded in 1948, with 80-90M+ sq ft of U.S. property incl. a 441-acre park on the former Bethlehem Steel site in Pennsylvania. He helped lead development of LA's Staples (now Crypto.com) Center and is a minority owner of the LA Kings and Lakers. Major USC donor.

Majestic's site blocked automated fetches, so no corporate email verified. Industrial/logistics land + power is a plausible data-center angle.

name: Elizabeth Uihlein
current_role: President and co-founder, Uline (Pleasant Prairie, Wisconsin)
profile: Liz Uihlein co-founded shipping- and industrial-supplies distributor Uline with her husband Dick in their basement in 1980, using start-up funds from his father. Uline now sells 40,000+ products via its huge catalog, with ~$11B revenue and 9,000+ staff, making it one of the largest private US companies; the couple are also among the biggest US conservative political donors.
interesting_fact: She personally writes letters in the front of Uline's catalogs, often posing provocative questions on topics such as whether America is in decline.
deep_cut_fact: Uline's very first product was the H-101 carton sizer; its success let the couple move from their basement into a first headquarters in Waukegan, Illinois, before the 200-acre Pleasant Prairie campus opened in 2010.
notes: Born Elizabeth Anne Hallberg (Winnetka, IL). Name is pronounced 'YOO-lyne', hence 'Uline'. Politically prominent; may be media-shy. No published press email found.

name: Richard Uihlein
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Uline (wife Liz Uihlein is CEO); chairman, Galectin Therapeutics
profile: Schlitz-brewing-dynasty descendant (b. 1945, Stanford alum) who with wife Liz started Uline in their basement in 1980; it is now North America's leading distributor of shipping, packaging and industrial supplies, with 10,000+ employees and an 890+ page catalog. He also chairs and finances biotech Galectin Therapeutics, and the couple are among the largest US political donors.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranks Uline among the 100 biggest private companies in the US; it grew from a basement start-up to $8B+ estimated revenue selling via a famously thick printed catalog.
deep_cut_fact: Uline's very first product was the H-101 carton sizer, a simple tool for cutting boxes down to size - and it is still sold in the catalog today.
notes: Uline's own site now lists Dick as Chairman and Liz as CEO (Forbes still says CEO). Couple rarely gives interviews; Liz writes catalog columns. Highly politically active - outreach may draw attention. No press email published.

name: Maximilian Viessmann
current_role: CEO & President, Viessmann Generations Group GmbH & Co. KG; board member, Carrier Global
profile: Fourth-generation heir (b. 1989) of the Viessmann heating dynasty. Ex-BCG consultant who joined in 2015 and became CEO; sold Viessmann Climate Solutions to Carrier for ~EUR 12bn (agreed 2023, closed Jan 2024) and joined Carrier's board. Now runs family investor Viessmann Generations Group (2026: AI push, FC Bayern stake).

name: Luo Jinhong
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder of EVE Energy (Huizhou); holds 50% of controlling shareholder Tibet EVE Holding (not a director/officer)
profile: Luo Jinhong (骆锦红) co-founded EVE Energy in 2001 with her husband, chairman Liu Jincheng, after both worked at Desay Energy in Huizhou. EVE grew from lithium primary cells into a top Chinese EV and energy-storage battery maker. The couple are joint actual controllers; Hurun 2025 put their joint wealth at RMB 52.5B.

deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding EVE she worked at three battery makers in Huizhou: Huizhou Bohui Battery, Times Battery and Desay Energy Technology; EVE's first entity (2001) was set up via relatives' nominee shareholding while Liu was still Desay's deputy GM.
notes: Very low public profile; she is not an executive and gives no interviews found. Husband Liu Jincheng is the public face (gives English-language interviews, e.g. electrive 2025). Route via EVE securities department (IR email).

name: Jayshree Ullal
current_role: Chairperson and CEO, Arista Networks; director, Snowflake

Arista now sells $9B+ a year of high-speed Ethernet switches, a core supplier to cloud and AI data-center buildouts; she owns roughly 2% of the stock.

notes: Press email is Arista corporate communications (Amanda Jaramillo) as listed on 2026 releases. No verified personal social accounts found. Frequently speaks about AI networking/back-end AI clusters; strong data-center fit.

profile: Widow of cork magnate Americo Amorim (d. 2017); she and her three daughters inherited his fortune and top Forbes Portugal's rich list (~EUR 5.8B, Jan 2026). name: Albert Avdolyan
current_role: Owner, A-Property (holding behind ELSI / Elga coal complex, Pacific Railway, Yakut Fuel & Energy Co.)

Through A-Property he bought the giant Elga coking-coal deposit in Yakutia (2020), merged coal assets into ELSI (2022), owns gas producer YATEC and is building the ~530 km private Pacific Railway to a Sea of Okhotsk port.

Russian company sites (elsi-group.ru) were unreachable from this environment so no press email was confirmed. Very low public profile.

name: Robert Bass
current_role: President, Keystone Group LP (Fort Worth family investment holding company); founder of the Oak Hill investment funds
profile: Fort Worth-born Yale (1971) and Stanford MBA (1974) investor, one of the four Bass brothers whose fortune traces to great-uncle Sid Richardson's oil. Built his own wealth through Keystone and the Oak Hill family of funds (Oak Hill Capital, Oak Hill Advisors), plus 1980s deals such as Taft Broadcasting and American Savings. It is almost certainly the filmmaker son, whose legal name is Walther/Walter Moreira Salles Júnior. Brothers Fernando, Pedro (Itaú chairman) and João are listed separately. He is a filmmaker rather than a business operator, so his fit for an energy/data-center podcast is limited.

name: Hans Michel Piech
current_role: Deputy Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Porsche Automobil Holding SE; supervisory board member of Volkswagen AG, Porsche AG and Audi AG
profile: Vienna-born (1942) lawyer and grandson of Ferdinand Porsche, and one of the leaders of the Piëch branch of the Porsche-Piëch family that controls Volkswagen via Porsche SE. He practised law in Vienna from 1977 to 2021 and has sat on the Porsche SE supervisory board since 1989 and on VW's since 2009.

notes: Very private; virtually no interviews. Only routes are Porsche SE communications/IR. Brother of the late Ferdinand Piëch; avoid family-dispute topics.

name: Andre Hoffmann
current_role: Vice-Chairman of Roche Holding (board since 1996, vice-chair since 2006); Chairman of Massellaz SA (family office) and President of Fondation Tour du Valat
profile: A descendant of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche, he represents the founding families' voting pool on Roche's board. After St. Gallen, M&A at James Capel, Nestlé and an INSEAD MBA, he joined the board in 1996; today he is a leading voice for nature-positive capitalism via WEF, the Capitals Coalition, Systemiq and INSEAD's Hoffmann Institute.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he published the book 'The New Nature of Business' (with Peter Vanham), arguing companies must account for natural and social capital, not just short-term profit; he launched it at a literary festival in his hometown of Morges.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1983-85) was acting administrator of the Tour du Valat biological research station in France's Camargue wetlands, founded by his conservationist father Luc Hoffmann; he also sits on the board of the Restaurant de l'Hôtel de Ville de Crissier, one of Switzerland's most celebrated restaurants.
notes: Unusually accessible for a billionaire: personal site lists office@massellaz.ch as the contact and he does book talks/podcasts. Strong sustainability/energy-transition angle (Systemiq board, Capitals Coalition). Wealth is shared across the Hoffmann/Oeri Roche heirs.

current_role: Presumed shareholder in WEG S.A. via the Werninghaus founding family (unconfirmed)
profile: Listed by Hurun (2015-2026) with ~US$7B from WEG, the Jaraguá do Sul, Brazil electric-motor and power-equipment maker founded in 1961 by Werner Voigt, Eggon João da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus (WEG = their initials).
