name: Andreas Oeri
current_role: Orthopedic surgeon in private practice, Basel; Roche founding-family shareholder (Roche board member 1996–2020)
profile: Dr. Andreas Oeri (b. 1949) is a member of the Hoffmann/Oeri founding family that, through a shareholder pool, controls the majority of Roche's voting shares — the source of his fortune. He sat on Roche's board for about 25 years as a representative of that pool, chairing its corporate governance and sustainability committee, and stepped down at the 2020 AGM.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a pharma billionaire, he kept a full medical career: a board-certified orthopedic surgeon (1988), he has run his own orthopedic practice in Basel since 1988, even while serving on Roche's board.
deep_cut_fact: Before private practice he trained at the surgical clinic of Kantonsspital Liestal, Basel's institute for physical medicine and the University of Basel surgical department, and was deputy senior physician at Basel University Orthopedic Hospital (1986–88).
notes: Very private; no public contacts beyond his medical practice listing (not included — it is a clinical practice, not a press channel). Roche media relations would be the only institutional route. Little connection to energy/data centers.

name: Catherine Oeri
current_role: Roche founding-family shareholder (member of the Hoffmann/Oeri voting pool); Basel philanthropist
profile: Catherine Oeri is a Basel-based descendant of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche (Oeri branch). She is a member of the family shareholder pool that controls ~45% of Roche's voting shares, alongside André Hoffmann, Andreas Oeri, Sabine Duschmalé-Oeri and the family's Stiftung Wolf. She keeps a private life centred on Basel cultural philanthropy.
interesting_fact: The Hoffmann-Oeri family pool still controls ~45% of Roche's voting shares, more than 125 years after the company's founding in Basel in 1896, one of Europe's longest-lasting family controls of a pharma giant.
deep_cut_fact: In 1998 she personally bought the 759-object Gerd-Wolfgang Essen Tibet collection for Basel's Museum der Kulturen, giving it a comprehensive overview of Tibetan Buddhist art; the museum previously owned only a few Tibetan objects. It was later shown as 'Tibet: Buddhas, Gods, Saints'.
notes: Very private, with no personal channels. Alive status is unconfirmed: Hurun still lists her (2026) and I found no death report, but a 2021 Museum der Kulturen report says she left its commission for reasons of age. Stiftung Wolf (Basel umbrella foundation of the Oeri family) is the closest route; its JavaScript-only site shows no email. Little energy/AI link.

name: Sabine Duschmale Oeri
current_role: Roche founding-family shareholder; member of the foundation board (Stiftungsrat) of the Paul Sacher Stiftung, Basel
profile: Sabine Duschmalé-Oeri is a member of the Hoffmann-Oeri family, whose shareholder pool controls the voting majority of Basel pharma group Roche. Hurun lists her wealth (about $7B) as coming from Roche. She keeps a very low profile; her known public role is on the board of Basel's Paul Sacher Stiftung, a music research foundation tied to the family.

deep_cut_fact: She is listed as 'Sabine Duschmalé' on the Paul Sacher Stiftung's foundation board in Basel, one of the world's leading archives for 20th-century music manuscripts.

Treat the identity as probable, not confirmed. No direct contact; a Roche-family route would go via Roche corporate communications. No energy/data-center link.

name: Vera Michalski Hoffmann
current_role: Publisher and head of Groupe Libella (Éditions Noir sur Blanc, etc.); founder and president of the Jan Michalski Foundation, Montricher, Switzerland
profile: Vera Michalski-Hoffmann (b. 1954, Basel) is an heir to the Hoffmann branch of the Roche pharmaceutical fortune. In 1986 she and her late husband Jan Michalski founded the Swiss publishing house Éditions Noir sur Blanc to bridge Eastern and Western European literature; it grew into the Libella publishing group. In 2004 she created the Jan Michalski Foundation for writing and literature in his memory.

deep_cut_fact: She graduated from Geneva's Graduate Institute of International Studies. With Jan Michalski, a Polish-born sociologist, she launched Éditions Noir sur Blanc in 1986 with the explicit aim of building 'literary bridges' between Eastern and Western Europe.
notes: Private, culture-focused Roche heir with no energy or tech involvement; best reached via the foundation's journalist contact (Aurélie Baudrier). Wealth figure comes from Hurun only.

current_role: Founder and President, LUMA Foundation (Zurich) and LUMA Arles
profile: Maja Hoffmann (b. 1956), a descendant of Roche founder Fritz Hoffmann-La Roche and heir to the family's Roche stake, is a former film student and documentary producer. She founded the LUMA Foundation in Zurich in 2004 and LUMA Arles in 2013, a creative campus with a Frank Gehry tower opened in 2021, and is a major contemporary-art patron.

notes: Strong environmental/sustainability angle via LUMA's materials-research lab (Atelier LUMA) and Camargue roots, though not an energy investor. Best route: LUMA press office or Finn Partners.

name: Rajan Bharti Mittal
current_role: Vice-Chairman & Managing Director, Bharti Enterprises; non-executive director, Bharti Airtel and Indus Towers
profile: Rajan Bharti Mittal (b. 1960) co-built Bharti Enterprises with brothers Sunil and Rakesh, starting with an import business in 1980; the group grew into Bharti Airtel, India's No. 2 telecom operator, plus Indus Towers, OneWeb stakes, insurance, real estate and food businesses. He oversees group strategy and external relations as vice-chairman.
interesting_fact: A former president of FICCI (India's top business chamber) and of ICC India (2013), he received the Horasis 'Indian Business Leader of the Year' award in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Italy's Comitato Leonardo gave him its 2011 Leonardo International Prize and made him an honorary member, crediting his FICCI presidency with relaunching Italy-India business ties through exchanges of business delegations between the two countries' employer associations.
notes: Lower profile than brother Sunil; best route is Bharti Enterprises corporate communications. Data-center angle: Airtel's Nxtra data-center arm and OneWeb satellite stake.

name: Rakesh Bharti Mittal
current_role: Vice Chairman, Bharti Enterprises; Chairman, FieldFresh Foods and Bharti AXA insurance ventures; board member, Indus Towers and Bharti Hexacom
profile: Rakesh Bharti Mittal is the youngest of the three brothers (with Sunil and Rajan) who built Bharti Enterprises from a 1980 import business into a group spanning Airtel telecom, agri-food (FieldFresh, a JV with Del Monte Pacific), insurance and realty. He moved off the Airtel board to Indus Towers and Bharti Hexacom, and is a major force in Bharti's education philanthropy.
interesting_fact: He served as President of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) for 2018-19, and is a founder and Distinguished Trustee of Plaksha University, a new tech university in Mohali, Punjab.
deep_cut_fact: His formal training is in engineering: a PG diploma in Electronics and Controls from YMCA Institute of Engineering. Early recognitions include the LMA Entrepreneur of the Year award in 1992 and an Institution of Engineers Engineering Excellence Award (2004); Newcastle University (UK) gave him an honorary Doctor of Civil Law.
notes: Best route is Bharti Enterprises corporate communications (New Delhi). Philanthropy focus on education (Bharti Airtel Foundation / Satya Bharti schools); featured in Bridgespan 'Remarkable Givers' videos.

name: Ina Ashwin Dani
current_role: Asian Paints promoter-family shareholder (Dani family); former non-executive director of Asian Paints and director of Hitech Corporation
profile: Ina Dani is the widow of Ashwin Dani (1944-2023), long-time non-executive chairman of Asian Paints, India's largest paint maker, which the Dani, Choksi and Vakil families co-founded in 1942. Her wealth stems from the Dani family's Asian Paints stake; son Malav Dani sits on the Asian Paints board. She previously served as a non-executive director of Asian Paints.
interesting_fact: Asian Paints, built by the Dani, Choksi and Vakil families, is India's largest homegrown paint company; her late husband Ashwin Dani, a polymer scientist, was its chairman and helped shape its R&D.
notes: Very private; little verified biography beyond family/board roles. Only route found is Asian Paints corporate/IR. Hurun profile details (education etc.) come from weak sources and were omitted.

name: Vijay Chauhan
current_role: Chairman, Parle Products Pvt Ltd (Mumbai), run with brothers/cousins Sharad and Raj Chauhan
profile: Vijay Kantilal Chauhan heads privately held Parle Products, maker of Parle-G, Monaco, KrackJack, Hide & Seek and Melody, alongside Sharad and Raj Chauhan; the third generation (e.g. Ajay and Arup Chauhan) serve as executive directors. Parle crossed $2B in sales in FY22 (₹17,223 crore revenue in FY23) and makes over a billion Parle-G packets a month.
interesting_fact: Parle-G was named the world's best-selling biscuit brand in a 2011 Nielsen report; it launched as 'Parle Gluco', and in 1947 Parle advertised its glucose biscuits as an Indian alternative to British biscuits.
deep_cut_fact: He is the son of Kantilal, one of founder Mohanlal Chauhan's five sons. Mohanlal, from Pardi near Valsad in Gujarat, first tried tailoring in Bombay before opening a bakery in Vile Parle in 1929 (hence 'Parle'); biscuits began in 1939 under a licence to supply the British Army.
notes: Very private; virtually no interviews by Vijay himself - the media-facing family members are executive directors Ajay and Arup Chauhan, and category head Mayank Shah often speaks for the company. Not to be confused with Parle Agro (Prakash Chauhan's family) or Parle Bisleri (Ramesh Chauhan).

name: Samuel C Swire
current_role: Executive Director, John Swire & Sons Ltd; Chairman of Swire Shipping and Swire Bulk; Chairman, Swire Charitable Trust and Swire Chinese Language Foundation
profile: Samuel Compton Swire (b. 1980), son of the late Sir Adrian Swire and brother of chairman Merlin Swire, belongs to the family behind the Swire Group (Swire Pacific, Swire Properties, Cathay Pacific). He joined the group in 2003 after Oxford, worked across Asia, and has sat on the John Swire & Sons board since 2015.
interesting_fact: As chairman of Swire Shipping and Swire Bulk since 2019, he oversees the group's original line of business, shipping, which dates back to the 19th-century China coast trade.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 John Swire & Sons funded a new national centre for learning and teaching Chinese at Oxford's Department of Education, with a newly endowed chair. Sam Swire, as chair of the Swire Chinese Language Foundation, called the study of Chinese 'both challenging and important'.
notes: Usually goes by 'Sam Swire'. info@scts.org.uk is the Swire Charitable Trust's (which he chairs) registered contact at Swire House, London. He also served on the Swire Pacific and Cathay Pacific boards from 2015 to 2023 and is a Historic England Foundation trustee. Low media profile.

name: Tsai Yang Hsiang-Hsun
current_role: Fubon family matriarch / shareholder; widow of Fubon founder Tsai Wan-tsai - no executive role found
profile: Tsai Yang Hsiang-hsun (蔡楊湘薰) is the widow of Fubon Group founder Tsai Wan-tsai (d. Oct 2014) and mother of Daniel Tsai (Fubon Group chairman) and Richard Tsai (Fubon Financial chairman). Hurun ranked her in 2015-16 on inherited Fubon holdings, later reorganised within the family in 2016. She keeps no public profile.
interesting_fact: After Tsai Wan-tsai's death in 2014, the Fubon empire passed to her sons in a 2016 reorganisation, with elder son Daniel becoming head of the family group.
notes: Very private; no personal bio, interviews or recent news found, and no confirmation of whether she is alive (no obituary found either). Not a realistic outreach target; any approach would go through Fubon Financial (see P00594, Richard Tsai). Family relationship inferred from Business Weekly/CW coverage (https://www.cw.com.tw/article/5064353).

name: Tom Perkins
notes: Tom Perkins, co-founder of venture firm Kleiner Perkins (KPCB), died 7 June 2016 (aged 84). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_Perkins_(businessman) . Skipped rest per instructions.

name: Tony Zhang
current_role: Tencent co-founder; lifetime honorary adviser to Tencent and honorary dean/lecturer of Tencent Academy (retired as CTO and executive director in 2014)
profile: Tony Zhang (Zhang Zhidong), born c.1971-72, was Pony Ma's classmate at Shenzhen University and earned a master's at South China University of Technology. One of Tencent's 'five founding tigers', he was CTO from 1998 to 2014, building the engineering and massive-scale systems behind QQ, and remains a major Tencent shareholder.
interesting_fact: In his 2014 farewell letter he said he and Pony Ma began as two IT engineers whose simple dream was to build an internet product many people would use while earning a living; Ma replied that they shared '4 years as university classmates and 16 years as startup partners'.
deep_cut_fact: Former Tencent engineers recall his motto 'elegant interface, ugly implementation' (ship the feature fast, refactor later), and his habit of sending handwritten cards and piles of virtual gifts to staff, whether celebrating, encouraging after a failure, or saying goodbye.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Since retirement he speaks occasionally on 'tech for good' (e.g., 2020 talk on Scratch coding for kids and prison tablet education). Do not confuse with Allen Zhang (WeChat creator). Tencent pages are JS-rendered; IR/press emails not extracted.

name: Ahmet Ahlatci
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Ahlatcı Holding (Çorum, Turkey)
profile: Ahmet Ahlatcı (born 1959, Çorum) opened a small jewelry shop in 1984 and built Ahlatcı Holding, Turkey's leading gold refiner/exporter (Ahlatcı Metal Refinery, Ahlatcı Kuyumculuk) with 7,000+ staff in 10 sectors. The group also spans energy (Enerya gas distribution, acquired 2021; solar plants), finance (Dünya Katılım Bank, securities, FX), health, real estate, automotive and mining.
interesting_fact: His group brought natural gas to Çorum for the first time in 2004 (CorumGaz), and now runs Enerya Energy plus solar plants in Turkey and a 35 MW solar build-out in Ukraine, a strong energy-podcast angle.
deep_cut_fact: The empire began in 1984 as a single small jewelry retail shop in Eğridere, Çorum; by 1988 it was making bracelets and in 2000 started producing wedding rings, before its refinery's bullion began trading on the Dubai Metal Exchange in 2017.
notes: Contacts are the holding's corporate ones (kurumsal = corporate inbox). Heads-up: Turkish media reported in Feb 2026 that prosecutors opened a money-laundering/smuggling probe with a travel ban; he denied it ('a mistake'). Check status before outreach.

name: Peter Czernin
current_role: 11th Baron Howard de Walden (head of the family owning the Howard de Walden Estate, Marylebone); co-founder & producer, Blueprint Pictures
profile: Peter Czernin (b. 1966) succeeded his mother Hazel as Baron Howard de Walden in 2024, heading the family that owns the Howard de Walden Estate - much of Marylebone, including Harley Street. Separately he is a film producer who co-founded Blueprint Pictures with Graham Broadbent (In Bruges, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel, The Banshees of Inisherin).
interesting_fact: He co-produced 'Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri', which won the BAFTA for Best Film and earned him an Academy Award nomination for Best Picture.
deep_cut_fact: He is also Count Czernin von und zu Chudenitz of the Bohemian Czernin family, and his English barony dates to 1597, created by Elizabeth I for Admiral Lord Thomas Howard; early producer credits are under the name 'Pete Czernin' (e.g. In Bruges).
notes: Wealth is the inherited Marylebone estate, run by professional management; his own career is film. Do not confuse with US media exec Peter Chernin. Blueprint Pictures is the most natural route.

name: Hugo Sigman
current_role: Founder, CEO and shareholder, Grupo Insud (Insud Pharma: Chemo, Exeltis, mAbxience), Madrid/Buenos Aires
profile: Argentine psychiatrist-turned-industrialist Hugo Sigman (b. 1944) co-founded drugmaker Chemo with his wife Silvia Gold in 1978, growing it into Grupo Insud: APIs and generics (Chemo), women's health (Exeltis) and biosimilars (mAbxience, 55% sold to Fresenius Kabi in 2022). The group also spans forestry, agriculture, a stake in Bioceres and film production.
interesting_fact: In 2020 his mAbxience plant in Garin, Buenos Aires was chosen by AstraZeneca to produce the active ingredient of the Oxford COVID-19 vaccine for Latin America; his film company K&S Films produced 'Wild Tales' (Relatos salvajes).
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a psychiatrist: a 1969 UBA medical graduate trained in Enrique Pichon-Riviere's school of social psychology, he founded and ran the psychiatric emergency unit at the Policlinico de Lanus, then worked in psychiatry at Barcelona's Hospital Clinic after moving to Spain in 1976.
notes: comunicacion@ is Insud Pharma's communications inbox (Madrid). He co-founded the Argentine Chamber of Biotechnology (2011). The 2021 vaccine-delay debate in Argentina is a sensitive topic.

name: Shi Jing
current_role: Indirect shareholder in Playtika (via Alpha Frontier) and the Giant group; daughter of Giant Network founder Shi Yuzhu; no confirmed executive title
profile: Shi Jing (史静) is the daughter of Shi Yuzhu, founder of Shanghai-based Giant Network. Playtika's 2021 IPO prospectus says she indirectly owned 31.95% of the Class A shares of Alpha Frontier, the Giant-controlled vehicle that bought Israeli social-casino game maker Playtika from Caesars in 2016; her father holds voting power over those shares. Chinese rich lists usually rank the father and daughter together.
interesting_fact: The Giant-controlled vehicle she holds a stake in bought Playtika, the Israeli maker of Slotomania and Bingo Blitz, from Caesars Interactive in 2016, then took it public in 2021; after the IPO, Alpha's UK subsidiary expected to keep about 77% of the shares.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: the SEC prospectus confirms a 'Jing Shi, Yuzhu Shi's daughter' with the Playtika/Alpha stake, which matches the input (Giant; Playtika 10% owner), but no official biography or public role was found. Very private; no published contacts. Any approach would go through Giant Network or Playtika investor relations. Keep outreach away from family matters. WebSearch quota ran out during this profile; research done via SEC and Toutiao.

name: Yang Zhiling
current_role: Founder and CEO, Moonshot AI (Beijing; maker of the Kimi chatbot and open-weight Kimi models)
profile: Yang Zhilin (b. 1992, Shantou) studied CS at Tsinghua and did a CMU PhD under Ruslan Salakhutdinov and William Cohen, co-authoring Transformer-XL and XLNet. After founding Recurrent AI, he co-founded Moonshot AI in 2023 with Tsinghua classmates; it raised ~$2B at a $20B+ valuation in May 2026 and has reportedly raised more since, ahead of a planned Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: A prog-rock devotee, he named Moonshot AI in honour of Pink Floyd's album The Dark Side of the Moon; a white piano reportedly stands prominently in the Beijing office.
deep_cut_fact: At Tsinghua he was the drummer in a campus band called Splay and organised music competitions; he won admission there after taking first prize in China's National Olympiad in Informatics.
notes: Name usually romanised Yang Zhilin (杨植麟). Keeps a low profile: rarely gives interviews and has no public personal social-media account (Caixin). Best route is Moonshot's global PR address; X handle is the company's, not his.

name: Philip Ng
current_role: Senior Advisor (retired as CEO in 2023), Far East Organization, Singapore; director of sister company Sino Group (Hong Kong)
profile: Philip Ng Chee Tat (黄志达, b. 1958) is a son of Ng Teng Fong, 'King of Orchard Road', who founded Far East Organization, Singapore's largest private property developer. He ran the Singapore business as CEO for decades while brother Robert runs Hong Kong's Sino Group; he retired as CEO in 2023 and is now Senior Advisor. Far East describes itself as a Christian enterprise.
interesting_fact: Far East Organization explicitly operates as a 'Christian enterprise' seeking to be 'a community of love and a workplace of grace'; Ng speaks publicly about how faith shapes his leadership, e.g. a 2026 INSEAD Family Business Club talk.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer: a first-class honours BSc in Civil Engineering from King's College London, then two master's degrees from MIT - one in geothermal engineering policy and one in urban planning.
notes: Private; Far East publishes only sales/leasing emails, no press email. His MIT geothermal-policy degree is a strong hook for an energy podcast. Has appeared at faith/family-business events (INSEAD), which may be the warmest route.

name: Alexandra Schoerghuber
current_role: Chair of the Foundation Board (Stiftungsrat) and Executive Board member, Schörghuber Stiftung & Co. Holding KG (Schörghuber Group), Munich
profile: Alexandra Schörghuber (née Stumpf, b. 1958, Frankfurt) took charge of Munich's family-owned Schörghuber Group after her husband Stefan died in 2008. The group owns real-estate developer Bayerische Hausbau, holds stakes in the Paulaner brewery group (with Heineken) and Arabella hotels (with Marriott), and farms salmon in Chile through Ventisqueros. Day-to-day management now sits with CEO Florian Schörghuber.
interesting_fact: Alongside the property and beer businesses, the group runs one of Chile's large salmon-farming operations (Productos del Mar Ventisqueros, Puerto Montt). Its private holdings have also included car parks and Bavarian ski lifts and cable cars.
deep_cut_fact: A pastor's daughter, she trained as a hotel management assistant and worked in hotels in Germany, Switzerland and Bermuda. She sits on FC Bayern Munich's administrative advisory board (deputy chair from 2016) and backed the 'Sternenhaus' for grieving children with Bayern star Thomas Müller.
notes: Very private and gives few interviews. Route requests through the group's Chief Communications Officer. CEO Florian Schörghuber runs operations day to day. Real estate, hospitality and brewing are better hooks than energy or data centres.

name: Jeremy Jacobs Sr
current_role: Chairman, Delaware North (Buffalo, NY); owner of the NHL's Boston Bruins
profile: Jeremy M. Jacobs (b. 1940) took over Delaware North - founded in Buffalo in 1915 by his father and uncles selling peanuts and popcorn - at 28 after his father's sudden death in 1968, growing it into a global hospitality, concessions, gaming and parks operator. He bought the Bruins in 1975 and was inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in 2017; his sons Jerry Jr., Lou and Charlie now serve as CEOs.
interesting_fact: He co-owns a Florida restaurant with Jack Nicklaus, with whom he shares a birthday, and pledged $30M to the University at Buffalo, which named its medical school (Jacobs School of Medicine and Biomedical Sciences) after him.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the NHL Board of Governors for nearly two decades (elected 2007, tenure completed in 2026) and chaired the University at Buffalo Council from 1998 to 2025; he is even in the Arkansas Sports Hall of Fame (2013).
notes: Press email is Delaware North's published corporate-communications contact (Glen White, Director, Corporate Communications; Sportservice/Patina media: CHRobert@delawarenorth.com). Age ~86; company day-to-day run by his sons. Company-own article 'Works for Peanuts' is a good outreach hook: https://media.delawarenorth.com/boston-bruins-owner-jeremy-jacobs-works-for-peanuts/

name: Liu Ke-Chen
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Advantech Co. (TWSE: 2395), Taipei
profile: K.C. Liu (劉克振) studied telecommunications engineering at National Chiao Tung University and was a sales engineer at Hewlett-Packard Taiwan. In 1983 he and two HP colleagues (Chaney Ho and Huang Yu-ming) co-founded Advantech. It is now the world's largest industrial-computer and industrial-IoT brand, with about 9,000 staff and subsidiaries in 21 countries. He is still chairman and is pushing the company into edge AI.
interesting_fact: On Advantech's 40th anniversary he said that, when the company was two years old, he told his co-founders they would never employ more than 100 people because they wanted to know every employee. 'I never thought it would be over 9000 people.'
deep_cut_fact: Asked about retirement at 69, Liu said: 'I will not retire. I have no plans to retire and go to Fiji. I find fishing boring.' He described generative AI as like 'fighting with a machine gun rather than a knife', and said 'the niche model is beautiful' of Advantech's business units.
notes: The input lists the country as China, but he is Taiwanese and Advantech is based in Taipei. Known for the 'Good-to-Great Three Circles' management philosophy and for founding the Advantech Foundation. He gives trade-press interviews, which makes industrial AI/edge computing and energy management good angles. The IR address is the company spokesperson / IR mailbox.

name: Kjeld Kirk Kristiansen
current_role: Third-generation co-owner of the LEGO Group via family holding KIRKBI A/S (former LEGO CEO 1979-2004; handed KIRKBI chair to son Thomas in 2023)
profile: Grandson of LEGO founder Ole Kirk Christiansen, Kjeld (b. 1947) ran the Billund toy company from 1979 to 2004, overseeing its global expansion, then helped steer its turnaround as owner. The family (via KIRKBI) owns 75% of LEGO, roughly half of Merlin Entertainments, and a growing climate/renewables investment arm (KIRKBI Climate), including offshore-wind stakes.
interesting_fact: The original Legoland, built in 1968 in his hometown of Billund, is made of over 20 million LEGO bricks; 'LEGO' comes from the Danish 'leg godt' ('play well').
deep_cut_fact: As a child he modelled on several LEGO boxes in the 1950s and 1960s; the 1949-55 plastic-brick box was the first LEGO packaging he appeared on, alongside his sisters.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed; KIRKBI communications is the gatekeeper. Energy angle: KIRKBI Climate invests in offshore wind and climate tech. Avoid topics about his children.

name: Ronald Wanek
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ashley Furniture Industries (Arcadia, Wisconsin)
profile: Minnesota farm-raised founder of Ashley, America's largest home furniture manufacturer and retailer. He launched Arcadia Furniture in 1970 with investors, a loan from his father and proceeds from selling his home, bought Chicago distributor Ashley Furniture in 1976 and merged the two. Son Todd has been CEO since 2002; Ron remains chairman, and the family office Third Lake Capital holds real estate.
interesting_fact: He grew up the son of a tenant farmer and did not have electricity at home until he was 9, or indoor plumbing until 12.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Arcadia Furniture he spent the first nine years of his career at Winona Industries making stereo and TV cabinets; his love of furniture came from watching his grandfather and great-uncle build rocking chairs (with bowed rockers) and boats in their garages as a hobby.
notes: Has done industry interviews (American Furniture Hall of Fame oral history; Furniture Today podcast, 2020). No personal or office contact published; approach via Ashley corporate communications. Born May 1941 in Winona, MN.

name: Evangelos Marinakis
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Capital Maritime & Trading Corp. (Capital Group, Piraeus); owner of Olympiacos FC and Nottingham Forest FC; owner of Alter Ego Media
profile: Greek shipowner who built Capital Group (tankers, containerships and, via 59%-owned NYSE-listed Capital Clean Energy Carriers, a large LNG-carrier fleet) from his family's shipping roots in Piraeus. He also owns Olympiacos, Nottingham Forest (promoted to the Premier League in 2022), a stake in Rio Ave, and media group Alter Ego Media, listed in Athens in 2025.
interesting_fact: He wrote the lyrics for 'Excitement', a 2021 song by Greek pop star Natassa Theodoridou, and won a Piraeus city council seat in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2025 his Capital Clean Energy Carriers became a founding member of the MIT Maritime Consortium with ABS, a collaboration researching nuclear propulsion and alternative fuels for commercial shipping.

public_contacts.value: Capital Link, Inc. (Nicolas Bornozis / Markella Kara) - ccec@capitallink.com

notes: Energy angle: LNG shipping and nuclear-propulsion research; also held ~6% of Terna Energy (2021). Brian Gallagher is EVP Investor Relations at Capital. Controversial public figure in Greece - keep outreach to shipping/energy topics.

name: Jim Davis
current_role: Chairman and owner, New Balance Athletics (Boston)
profile: Son of Greek immigrants (b. 1943) who bought tiny Boston shoemaker New Balance in 1972 and built it into a ~$6.5B-sales global brand that still makes shoes in New England. He is chairman, wife Anna is vice chair, and the family owns ~95%. Early investor in Major League Lacrosse and XL Fleet.
interesting_fact: New Balance's $500M Boston Landing development houses its HQ plus practice facilities for the Boston Bruins and Celtics; Davis was also an early investor (9%) in electrification company XL Fleet.
deep_cut_fact: Before buying New Balance he was a sales engineer at LFE Corporation in Waltham and marketing manager at Applied Geodata Systems (Techven Associates) in Cambridge; a biology/chemistry major at Middlebury, which later named the Davis Family Library for him.

public_contacts.value: miya.denison@newbalance.com (New Balance Global PR, per 2026 releases)

notes: Private, rarely interviewed; politically active donor in Boston races. Press contacts vary per release; Ketchum handles some NB PR. Origin story often told as buying NB on 1972 Boston Marathon day (single/weak sources - not used).

name: Zhu Hongmei
current_role: Co-actual controller of Shenghong Group / Eastern Shenghong (000301.SZ); director of controlling shareholder Jiangsu Shenghong Technology
profile: Zhu Hongmei (朱红梅) is the wife and business partner of Miao Hangen, founder of Suzhou-based Shenghong Group; the couple are joint actual controllers of Eastern Shenghong. Shenghong grew over ~30 years from printing and dyeing in Shengze, Wujiang into polyester fibre, refining and petrochemicals (Shenghong Petrochemical in Lianyungang) and new-energy materials. She holds no executive post at the listed company.
interesting_fact: The couple took Shenghong public via a 2018 backdoor listing into Wujiang state-owned 'Oriental Market' (renamed Eastern Shenghong), reported as the largest A-share asset restructuring of 2018 and a mixed-ownership reform test case.
notes: Very private; virtually no personal public profile or interviews. Husband Miao Hangen (chairman of Shenghong/Eastern Shenghong) is the public face; best route is Eastern Shenghong's securities/IR office in Shengze, Suzhou (board secretary Wang Jun). Hurun lists wealth jointly with Miao Hangen.

name: Tench Coxe
current_role: Director, NVIDIA (since 1993; audit and compensation committees); former Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures
profile: Venture capitalist who joined Sutter Hill Ventures in 1987 and was managing director 1989-2020, focused on IT investments. Sutter Hill backed Nvidia at its founding and Coxe has sat on Nvidia's board since 1993; his stake made him a billionaire as Nvidia became the AI-datacenter giant. Now Austin-based, he is a philanthropist and was an Artisan Partners director until 2025.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he and his wife Simone gave $100M, unrestricted, to launch UT Austin's new academic medical center (with an MD Anderson expansion) - one of the largest gifts in the university's history.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he was Director of Marketing and MIS at Digital Communication Associates; he holds an economics BA from Dartmouth and a Harvard MBA. In 2025 he also became a minority owner of MLS club Austin FC.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Austin FC ownership: https://austinfc.com/news/austin-fc-announces-additions-to-clubs-ownership-group. Best formal route is Nvidia corporate PR; Austin philanthropy (UT/Dell Med) is a friendly hook.

name: Mike Adenuga
current_role: Chairman, Globacom (Glo) and Conoil; founder of Conoil Producing
profile: Nigerian tycoon (b. 1953) who made his first million at 26 trading lace and distributing soft drinks, then built Conoil Producing (oil blocks in the Niger Delta) and Globacom, a top-three Nigerian mobile operator that also built the Glo-1 submarine cable to the UK. Also owns 74% of listed fuel marketer Conoil and a stake in Sterling Financial Holdings.
interesting_fact: He paid his way through an MBA at Pace University in New York by working as a taxi driver; his Glo-1 cable runs about 6,100 miles from Nigeria to the UK via Ghana and Portugal.
deep_cut_fact: He personally funded the new Alliance Française de Lagos 'Mike Adenuga Centre' at 9 Osborne Road, Ikoyi: Emmanuel Macron inaugurated its first phase in July 2018 and it fully opened in May 2019, with an auditorium, library, art gallery and outdoor amphitheatre.
notes: Famously media-shy; rarely gives interviews and speaks via Globacom statements. No personal social accounts found. Turned 73 in April 2026. NCC has required Globacom to appoint a separate CEO (2025), so leadership structure may change; route via Globacom corporate communications.

name: Wang Qingtao
current_role: Founder/Chairman, Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团, formerly Shandong Coking Group), Qingdao — group in court-ordered bankruptcy restructuring since 2023
profile: Shandong-born (1962, Zouping) coal and coking entrepreneur known as the 'coking king'. Built Shandong Tiexiong Energy Coal Chemical from 2003, co-founded Shandong's largest coal-chemical park with Shagang in 2007, then renamed his group Zhongrong Xinda in 2016 and pivoted into bank stakes and mining (incl. a Peru iron mine). The group entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2023.
interesting_fact: Ranked Shandong's richest person on the 2021 New Fortune 500 list (RMB 59.65B), and was vice-chairman of the China Coking Industry Association.
deep_cut_fact: To win steel magnate Shen Wenrong's (Shagang) backing, he visited him in Jiangsu more than a dozen times in three months, telling him: 'You build the biggest steel mill, I'll build the biggest coking plant.' Earlier he served in the army and worked at the Zouping materials bureau before quitting to trade coal.
notes: Group in bankruptcy restructuring (Zibo Intermediate Court, 2023) and he reportedly faces numerous consumption-restriction orders; sensitive subject, not a likely podcast guest. No published personal/office contacts found. Also credited with a patented coke-oven smoke/dust removal device (cnpp.cn/focus/30788.html).

name: Eric Lefkofsky
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Tempus AI, Inc. (Nasdaq: TEM); cofounder of Lightbank
profile: Serial Chicago entrepreneur who made his fortune cofounding Groupon (2008) with Andrew Mason and longtime partner Brad Keywell, after earlier ventures including Starbelly, InnerWorkings, Echo Global Logistics and MediaOcean. Since 2015 he has run Tempus, which applies AI and molecular data to cancer care; it IPO'd in 2024 at about $6B, his fourth IPO. He also cofounded VC firm Lightbank.
interesting_fact: After a girlfriend dumped him in college at Michigan, he started his first business selling carpets, which he estimates generated hundreds of thousands of dollars in sales.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published author and longtime teacher: his 2007 book 'Accelerated Disruption' (Easton Studio Press) is about how technology reshapes business, and he has taught entrepreneurship/disruptive business models at Kellogg, DePaul and Chicago Booth.
notes: Personal site lefkofsky.com links his X and LinkedIn. Tempus media route is media@tempus.com. Strong AI/data angle (multimodal foundation models, large genomic datasets). Avoid personal/family health topics.

name: Xu Xin
current_role: Non-independent director (since July 2024) and co-actual controller, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (300604.SZ)
profile: Xu Xin (徐昕, b. 1976) is co-actual controller, with chairman Zhao Yi (reported as her husband), of Hangzhou Changchuan Technology, a ChiNext-listed maker of chip test equipment (testers, handlers, AOI) founded 2008, listed 2017. She joined at founding as finance manager, later CFO and assistant GM; director since 2024.
interesting_fact: Changchuan has grown by buying foreign tool makers: Singapore AOI maker STI, the semiconductor division of Japan's SATO and Malaysia's test-equipment maker EXIS; it now employs about 4,500 people.
deep_cut_fact: Before Changchuan, she spent 1999-2005 as a sales clerk at Hangzhou Weili Trading; a Zhejiang Shuren University graduate, she joined Changchuan at its April 2008 founding as finance manager and ran its finances as CFO in 2015.
notes: Low public profile; husband Zhao Yi (ex-Silan Microelectronics production director, founder/chairman) is the public face. Best route is the company IR/board secretary office (secretary Shao Jingyang). Contacts are company-level, not personal.

name: Zhao Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hangzhou Changchuan Technology (CCTech, SZSE: 300604)
profile: Zhao Yi (b. 1976, Weiyuan, Neijiang, Sichuan) spent 1997-2007 at Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, rising to production director, then founded Changchuan Technology in 2008 to make chip test and handling equipment (testers, handlers, probers, AOI). CCTech listed in Shenzhen in 2017; AI-driven demand for memory/advanced-packaging test pushed its market cap to ~CNY180B, and it is now pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: CCTech was billed as China's first listed semiconductor test-equipment company (Shenzhen ChiNext IPO, April 2017, at CNY9.94/share); its value rose from ~CNY27.7B to ~CNY180B in about 18 months to 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He started CCTech in April 2008 with just CNY500,000 in seed capital, launched its first gravity-type test handler that same year, and its in-house analog tester CTA8200 in 2009. The name 'Changchuan' combines the hometowns of the two co-founders: Changxing (Zhejiang) and Sichuan.
notes: Described in Chinese press as low-profile; co-founder and wife Xu Xin is a director (Hurun lists the fortune jointly). Board secretary Shao Jingyang handles investor contact. Hometown-name detail is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hangzhou_Changchuan_Technology).

name: Rakesh Gangwal
current_role: Director, Southwest Airlines (chairman Nov 2024–Aug 2025); co-founder of InterGlobe Aviation (IndiGo)
profile: Kolkata-born, IIT Kanpur- and Wharton-educated airline veteran. Gangwal rose through United Airlines and Air France, ran US Airways as CEO and chairman (1998–2001) and then Worldspan. In 2006 he co-founded IndiGo with Rahul Bhatia, starting with one aircraft; it is now India's largest airline. He left IndiGo's board in 2022 and is selling down his stake. He joined Southwest's board in 2024 and still serves as a director after a stint as chairman.
interesting_fact: IndiGo started in 2006 with a single aircraft and grew into India's largest airline by market share. Gangwal's stake in it is the source of his multibillion-dollar fortune.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2022 Gangwal gave ₹100 crore to his alma mater IIT Kanpur to set up the Gangwal School of Medical Sciences and Technology, a planned medical school with a super-speciality hospital on campus. He also joined the school's advisory board. Earlier in his career he was a production and planning engineer at Philips India and a financial analyst at Ford.
notes: Low public profile; he is Miami-based. Avoid the IndiGo governance dispute with Bhatia. No personal social accounts were found. The IIT Kanpur medical school philanthropy is the warmest angle.

name: Ma Jianrong
current_role: Executive Chairman, Shenzhou International Group Holdings (HKEX: 2313), Ningbo
profile: Former mill worker who joined Ningbo's Shenzhou knitting venture in 1989, rose to general manager, gained family control of the company in 1997–2004 and has been executive chairman since its 2005 Hong Kong listing. Shenzhou is China's largest vertically integrated knitwear maker, supplying Nike, Adidas, Uniqlo and Puma from plants in China, Vietnam and Cambodia.
interesting_fact: Shenzhou has been dubbed the 'Foxconn of apparel': a contract manufacturer that, despite thin-margin OEM work, became the most valuable listed apparel company in China by market value.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shenzhou he worked in a cotton spinning mill and a knitwear factory; at Shenzhou his first role was manager of the weaving department. The company itself was set up by the Beilun district government with Shanghai No. 20 Knitting Factory, where his father was technical deputy director.

public_contacts.value: iPR Limited (investor and press relations adviser)

notes: Aged 61 per 2025 annual report (Apr 2026). Very low media profile; rarely interviewed. Chinese name 马建荣. Best route via company secretary email or iPR.

name: Pierre Landolt
current_role: Owner/operator of Fazenda Tamanduá (biodynamic farm, Patos, Paraíba, Brazil) and sole investor in AxialPar sustainable-agribusiness company; Sandoz family heir and former Sandoz/Novartis board member
profile: Pierre Landolt is a French-Swiss member of the Sandoz family whose great-grandfather founded the group that became Novartis and Syngenta. He served on the Sandoz and Novartis boards until about 70 and helped create Syngenta in the 2000 agribusiness merger; since 1977 he has run a ~3,000-hectare biodynamic farm in Brazil's semi-arid sertão, producing mangoes, honey, dairy, rice and melons.
interesting_fact: Although his family fortune helped found agrochemical giant Syngenta, his Fazenda Tamanduá uses no chemicals: it follows Rudolf Steiner's biodynamic method, and over half the land is set aside as reserves and wildlife corridors, including ~350 ha of private natural heritage reserve.
deep_cut_fact: He came to Brazil at 29 after a law degree and a year as a paratrooper in the French army, and first went to the Paraíba backlands with a Dutch agronomist looking for land to grow senna, because war between Pakistan and India had disrupted world supply of the plant.
notes: Age ~78 (77 in April 2025 AgFeed interview). Very private; no published personal/office contact found (farm and AxialPar sites returned errors). Agri-sustainability angle rather than energy. IMD has 2006 case studies on AxialPar.

name: Paul-Louis Halley
profile: French retail entrepreneur who co-founded Promodès in 1961 with his father and brother; it merged with Carrefour in 1999, leaving him its principal shareholder (~11%). He died on 6 December 2003 in a TBM 700 plane crash on approach to Oxford Airport.
notes: Deceased 6 Dec 2003 (plane crash near Oxford, UK). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul-Louis_Halley. Skip for outreach.

name: Landolt family
current_role: Swiss family; descendants of the Sandoz founders and long-standing major shareholders of Novartis (via the Sandoz Family Foundation / Sandoz Family Office)
profile: The Landolts are the heirs of the Sandoz chemical/pharma dynasty through Elisabeth Sandoz and Jacques Landolt; their fortune comes from Sandoz shares that became Novartis in the 1996 Sandoz–Ciba merger (historically ~3.6% of Novartis). Pierre Landolt (b. 1947) chaired the Sandoz Family Foundation for decades and sat on Novartis's board 2010–2018; the family also has hotel and watchmaking interests.
interesting_fact: In 1998 Pierre Landolt said the family had stayed loyal to a single stock for 110 years — Sandoz, later Novartis — and had no intention of selling it.
deep_cut_fact: Pierre Landolt splits his life between Switzerland and Brazil, where, shocked by poverty in the Nordeste, he built a model farm and founded a bank to finance agricultural projects (Le Temps interview, 1998).
notes: Family entry, not one individual; Pierre Landolt is the most public member. Very discreet; no published contacts found for the Sandoz Family Office/Foundation. Reports of governance turmoil at the foundation exist (finews) — avoid in outreach.

name: Frederik Paulson
current_role: Chairman emeritus / principal shareholder, Ferring Pharmaceuticals (Saint-Prex, Switzerland); explorer and philanthropist
profile: Frederik Paulsen (correct spelling; b. Stockholm 1950) is the son of Ferring founder Frederik Paulsen Sr. At Ferring since 1976, he led the reproductive-health and peptide drugmaker for decades; it passed €2.5B revenue in 2025. He has been Switzerland-based since 2003 and also invests in property and vineyards. Since Feb 2026 Jean-Frédéric Paulsen is Ferring's chair and CEO.
interesting_fact: A serious polar explorer, he is described as the first person to visit all eight of Earth's poles (completed winter 2013). In 2007 he dived 14,000+ ft in a MIR submersible to the seabed at the North Pole.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010 he and companion François Bernard made the first crossing of the Bering Strait from America to Russia in an ultralight aircraft. Academically, he holds a doctorate in demography from EHESS in Paris and studied chemistry in Kiel.

public_contacts.value: carine.julen@ferring.com (Senior Manager, Corporate Communications & Public Affairs)

notes: Hurun spells the name 'Paulson'. He was Russia's honorary consul in Lausanne (2009-22) and holds Russian state honours, so check fit. His philanthropy includes ~$40M to the Museum Kunst der Westküste and support for the South Georgia Heritage Trust and Bhutan's Royal Textile Academy. Polar exploration is the best hook.

name: James Cox Chambers
current_role: Board member, Communities In Schools; Cox Enterprises heir; self-described renewable-energy entrepreneur, biodynamic farmer and filmmaker
profile: Jim Cox Chambers is the son of Anne Cox Chambers (d. 2020) and grandson of Cox Enterprises founder James M. Cox. He inherited a large stake (~17% per LittleSis) in the family-owned media, cable and auto conglomerate but has no operating role. He has chaired Bard College's board (he is a 1981 alumnus) and been an Atlanta Hawks partner.
interesting_fact: His official bio calls him a 'renewable energy entrepreneur' and 'biodynamically trained farmer' whose life mission is 'an equitable, just, bounteously clean Mother Earth', an energy angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as 'essentially a hippy since adolescence', 'born and bred in the cradle of the Civil Rights Movement, Atlanta.' His mother Anne Cox Chambers, Carter's ambassador to Belgium, was a formative early supporter of Communities In Schools, whose board he now sits on.
notes: Very private, with no personal website or verified social accounts found. He is no longer listed on Bard's current trustee leadership page, so the Bard chair role is past. I could not confirm his current Hawks ownership status or the name of his renewable-energy venture. Possible route: Communities In Schools national office.

name: Marcos Galperin
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, MercadoLibre (stepped down as CEO in 2026 after 26 years)
profile: Argentine entrepreneur Marcos Galperin founded MercadoLibre in 1999 while finishing his Stanford MBA, after stints at oil company YPF and a JPMorgan internship. He built it into Latin America's dominant e-commerce and fintech (Mercado Pago) platform, operating in 18 countries and Nasdaq-listed since 2007. In 2026 he handed the CEO role to a successor and became executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Galperin comes from Argentine business royalty: his grandfather founded tannery Sadesa, now one of the country's largest leather makers. He also helped organise Argentina's first-ever presidential debate before the 2015 election.
deep_cut_fact: At Stanford GSB, finance professor Jack McDonald had him drive private-equity investor John Muse (Hicks Muse) to the airport. Galperin pitched MercadoLibre during the ride and won his first investor. In 2012 he gave $1.5M to name two spaces in the GSB's Knight Management Center.
notes: Lives in Uruguay. Very active on X, but the handle was not verified from an official page in this pass. MercadoLibre's media contact (Valeria Bazzi) is the published press route. Galperin is a vocal political commentator in Argentina.

name: Gao Dekang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Bosideng International Holdings (HKEX: 3998)
profile: Gao Dekang (b. 1952), from a family of tailors in Changshu, Jiangsu, started a village tailoring workshop with eight sewing machines in 1976, moved into OEM down jackets for Shanghai brands and launched his own Bosideng brand in the early 1990s. Bosideng is now China's leading down-apparel brand with thousands of stores, sold internationally, and Gao still chairs and runs it.
interesting_fact: In the early years he personally rode a Yongjiu bicycle some 100km each way between Changshu and Shanghai, before dawn, to pick up materials and deliver finished garments.
deep_cut_fact: The name Bosideng is a phonetic play on 'Boston': the jackets he first made under licence were branded 'Xiushideng' (echoing Houston), so when he registered his own brand in 1992 he picked a famously cold US city instead.
notes: Input lists him on 'Hurun Self-Made Women' - likely a data merge error (Gao Dekang is male; his wife Mei Dong is a director). He reportedly got the down-jacket idea after reading about a Chinese Everest expedition. Best route: Bosideng IR.

name: Dinara Kulibaeva
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Timur Kulibayev, via Almex Holding) of Halyk Bank, Kazakhstan; long-time head of the Nursultan Nazarbayev Educational Foundation (NNEF)
profile: Daughter of Kazakhstan's first president Nursultan Nazarbayev, Kulibaeva and her husband control Halyk Bank, Kazakhstan's largest bank, through Almex (about 62% at end-2025, after selling ~10% via London/Astana GDR placements). They also hold oil-services and former gold-mining interests and run a Halyk charity foundation (est. 2016, 120+ projects).
interesting_fact: A graduate of Moscow's Institute of Theater Arts (GITIS), she headed the president's education foundation, which supports Kazakh students with financial aid.
deep_cut_fact: NNEF (founded 1998) runs an education cluster including Miras International Schools in Almaty and Astana, Miras kindergartens, the Aryston lyceum and the International IT University (IITU); Miras Almaty earned 1.24bn tenge profit in 2025.
notes: Politically exposed person; very private, no published personal or office contact found. Forbes lists her as 'former' on the real-time list. Not an entrepreneur-operator; low fit for the podcast. Avoid politics/family in outreach.

name: Mohed Altrad
current_role: Founder and President, Altrad Group (Florensac/Montpellier, France); President, Montpellier Hérault Rugby
profile: Born into a nomadic Bedouin tribe in Syria and orphaned young, Mohed Altrad taught himself to read, earned a PhD in computer science in France and worked at Alcatel, Thomson and ADNOC. In 1985 he bought scaffolding firm Mefran, the seed of Altrad Group (~$5.8B revenue industrial services), now run by joint CEOs. He also owns Montpellier rugby club.
interesting_fact: He won EY's World Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2015, the first Frenchman to do so; Altrad Group's name has appeared on the jerseys of both the French national rugby team and the All Blacks.
deep_cut_fact: He is also a published novelist: his novel 'Badawi', about a Bedouin boy's journey, was recommended by French authorities for the national school curriculum. Before scaffolding, his first venture back in France was an IT business, after an engineering stint at Abu Dhabi's national oil company ADNOC.
notes: Personal site mohedaltrad.fr is linked from Altrad's official site. Energy angle: Altrad provides industrial services to nuclear, oil & gas and power plants. Avoid referencing his 2022 rugby-sponsorship conviction, tax disputes, or 2026 Montpellier mayoral politics.

name: Bill Haslam
current_role: Chairman and majority owner, Nashville Predators (NHL); former Governor of Tennessee (2011-2019)
profile: Bill Haslam was president of his family's Pilot Corporation (Pilot Flying J), which the Haslams sold to Berkshire Hathaway for $13.6B across 2017-2024. He was Knoxville mayor and two-term Tennessee governor (2011-19), championing tuition-free college. In 2025 he became majority owner of the Nashville Predators, later adding Nick Saban as a minority partner.
interesting_fact: With wife Crissy and the Predators Foundation he launched 'Smashville Schoolhouse', honoring Nashville public school teachers during the 2025-26 NHL season.
deep_cut_fact: After Emory he had planned to teach history and become a minister; he joined Pilot only to learn business before seminary, then stayed. After office he co-taught a Vanderbilt leadership course with historian Jon Meacham (2019).
notes: Public-facing and accessible (Bush Institute fellow, author of 'Faithful Presence' on faith in public life). No personal contact verified; route via Predators communications.

name: Michael Herz
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Wolfgang) of family holding maxingvest AG, which owns Tchibo and ~47% voting control of Beiersdorf (Nivea), Hamburg
profile: Michael Herz (b. 1943), third son of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz, became the largest shareholder after the 2003 family buyout of siblings Günter and Daniela. Through maxingvest the brothers own 100% of coffee and retail chain Tchibo (founded 1949) and control Beiersdorf, maker of Nivea and Eucerin. He is notably publicity-shy.
interesting_fact: His father Max Herz had the idea of shops where coffee could be both sipped and sold over the counter - a forerunner of the Starbucks model.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond coffee, he bought and turned around book wholesaler Libri and florist chain Blume 2000, and in 2003 his engagement helped prevent the break-up of Beiersdorf (Nivea) when it was up for sale.
notes: Famously press-shy ('der scheue Unternehmer'); essentially never gives interviews. Only route is maxingvest/Tchibo Corporate Communications in Hamburg.

name: Wolfgang Herz
current_role: General Manager, Participia Holding GmbH (Hamburg); supervisory board member at maxingvest, Tchibo and Beiersdorf
profile: Wolfgang Herz (b. 1950) and his brother Michael control maxingvest, the Hamburg family holding that owns 100% of coffee and retail chain Tchibo and a controlling stake in Nivea maker Beiersdorf. Their father Max co-founded Tchibo in 1949. Wolfgang has managed family companies since 1976, runs Participia Holding, and replaced Michael on Beiersdorf's supervisory board in 2020.
interesting_fact: Father Max Herz came up with the idea of shops where coffee could be both sipped and sold over the counter, a forerunner of the Starbucks model, which turned Tchibo into a German coffee institution.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond Tchibo and Beiersdorf, Herz chairs the supervisory boards of florist chain Blume2000 and TOPP Holding and is deputy chair of book wholesaler Libri. He has run Participia Holding in Hamburg since 1989.
notes: Extremely private; the Herz brothers almost never give interviews. presse@tchibo.de is Tchibo's corporate-communications address from a 2024 press release (could not re-open the PDF; it now returns 404). Beiersdorf re-proposed him for its supervisory board at the 2024 AGM.

name: Stephen Feinberg
current_role: 36th U.S. Deputy Secretary of Defense (sworn in 17 March 2025); co-founder of Cerberus Capital Management (on leave)
profile: Stephen Feinberg (b. 1960) co-founded Cerberus Capital Management in 1992, building a major distressed-debt and buyout firm whose biggest win was Albertsons. He chaired Trump's Intelligence Advisory Board in the first term and since March 2025 has been the Pentagon's No. 2, driving acquisition reform and equity stakes in strategic firms.
interesting_fact: Under Feinberg, the Pentagon has taken unprecedented equity stakes in private companies, notably in critical minerals - an unusual private-equity-style approach to defense industrial policy.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a steel salesman who moved the family from the Bronx to Spring Valley, NY, he captained the Princeton tennis team and joined ROTC, then started out as a trader at Drexel Burnham in 1982 before Gruntal & Co. and founding Cerberus.
notes: Famously media-shy, and a sitting senior government official - any request must go through Department of Defense/War public affairs and is unlikely to be granted while in office. Avoid the Freedom Group topic and confirmation-hearing conflict-of-interest coverage. Deep-cut source is Upstart Business Journal 2007 (cited by Wikipedia).

name: Shen Nanpeng
current_role: Founding and Managing Partner, HongShan (HSG, formerly Sequoia Capital China)
profile: Neil Shen (沈南鹏), ex-Citibank/Lehman/Deutsche Bank banker, co-founded Ctrip (now Trip.com) in 1999 and Home Inns in 2002, then built Sequoia China from 2005 into China's top VC, backing Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan, JD.com and Pinduoduo. The China arm spun out as independent HongShan in 2023; he topped the Forbes Midas List four times (2018-20, 2023).
interesting_fact: He topped the Forbes Midas List of the world's best-performing venture capitalists four times (2018, 2019, 2020 and 2023), and chairs the Yale School of Management board of advisors.
deep_cut_fact: A math prodigy at Shanghai No. 2 High School, he went to Columbia for a math PhD but quit after doubting he would make his mark as a mathematician - switching to Yale SOM (1992) and a Wall Street career instead.
notes: HongShan's published inbox is for funding pitches; no dedicated press email found. Based in Hong Kong; holds Singapore PR. Frequent speaker at Davos/Boao.

name: Andre Koo Chung-Li
current_role: Group President of Chailease Group (since 2003) and director of Chailease Holding (TWSE: 5871)
profile: Born 1967 in Taipei, Andre Koo is the third son of late CTBC patriarch Jeffrey Koo Sr.; schooled in Japan and a New York military academy, with BA and MBA from NYU Stern. He built Chailease, the family's leasing and consumer-finance group, into a Taiwan-listed lender across Asia, plus property and dining interests.
interesting_fact: When Forbes Taiwan published its 2020 rich list he was the youngest of Taiwan's 50 richest at 52, jumping from 28th to 16th as his fortune more than tripled.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong beef-noodle lover, he opened his own 'President's Beef Noodle' shop and personally shaped the menu, broth and side dishes; and because his whole family plays badminton, Chailease formed a badminton team and then built the Chailease Sunshine Badminton Hall.
notes: Wealth source listed as 'CTBC' but his own business is Chailease. Not to be confused with elder brother Jeffrey Koo Jr. (CTBC), whose legal case is unrelated. His wife chairs the Chailease Foundation. Private; little English-language media.

name: John Catsimatidis
current_role: Owner, Chairman and CEO, Red Apple Group (Gristedes/D'Agostino, United Refining, WABC radio); director, Turning Point Brands
profile: Greek-born (Nisyros, 1948), Harlem-raised grocer who dropped out of NYU to buy into the store he clerked at, opened the first Red Apple in 1971 and later bought Gristedes. In 1986 he acquired Pennsylvania refiner United Refining (Warren, PA), now the core of his energy holdings, alongside NYC real estate. Since 2020 he has owned WABC radio, where he hosts 'The Cats Roundtable'.
interesting_fact: He hosts a weekly political talk-radio show, The Cats Roundtable, and bought the station that airs it (WABC 770 AM) in 2020; he ran for NYC mayor as a Republican in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil he dabbled in aviation: he invested in charter carrier Capitol Air in 1984 and in 1992 launched his own charter airline, Capitol Air Express, which flew from 1993 to 1996 in the old Capitol Air livery. He studied electrical engineering at NYU (Brooklyn Tech '66) before quitting 8 credits short.

public_contacts.value: The Cats Roundtable (WABC 770 AM) - linked from his official site

notes: Very media-friendly; hosts his own radio show and does many interviews, so a guest-swap/radio angle may work. Red Apple Group HQ is 800 Third Ave, NYC (no published press email found). Wrote a memoir, 'How Far Do You Want to Go?' (listed on his site).

name: Bert Beveridge
current_role: Founder, Tito's Handmade Vodka (Fifth Generation Inc.), Austin, Texas
profile: Bert 'Tito' Beveridge, a geology/geophysics graduate who first worked in oil and gas, founded Tito's Vodka in Austin in 1997 with $90,000 borrowed on 19 credit cards. A 2001 World Spirits Competition win kick-started growth, and Tito's became one of America's best-selling spirits (est. 12M+ cases in 2024). The company says it donates net proceeds from its online store to nonprofits.
interesting_fact: Tito's first big break came when it beat 72 vodkas from around the world to win the 2001 World Spirits Competition in San Francisco.
deep_cut_fact: Tito's began as a hobby: he made infusions of cheap vodka as gifts using a pot still, then set up the Mockingbird Distillery, billed as Texas's first legal distillery, which produced just 1,000 cases in its first year (1997).
notes: Company (not personal) channels only; the contact page's structured data also lists marketing@titosvodka.com. Grew up in San Antonio playing polo and started in oil and gas, so an energy-to-entrepreneur angle works.

name: Doug Meijer
current_role: Co-chairman / board member, Meijer Inc. (Grand Rapids, Michigan)
profile: Doug Meijer (b. 1955), grandson of Dutch immigrant Hendrik Meijer who founded the Meijer grocery chain in 1934, co-owns the family business with brothers Hank and Mark. Doug and Hank were co-CEOs from 1990 to 2017; Meijer now runs ~500 Midwest supercenters with ~$22B revenue. He lives in Grand Rapids and gives via the Doug Meijer and Kendall Meijer foundation.
interesting_fact: Meijer's first 'Thrifty Acres' store on 28th Street in Grand Rapids (1962) combined grocery and department-store shopping under one 180,000 sq ft roof and is often considered the first hypermarket/supercenter in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 he gave $19.5 million to Michigan State University's College of Human Medicine to bring the world's most advanced medical imaging technology and cancer treatments to Michigan, via MSU's Grand Rapids research campus.

public_contacts.value: cara.lutz@meijer.com (Meijer communications, named on company press releases)

notes: Low public profile; brother Hank is the family's public spokesman (executive chairman, author of a Meijer history). Avoid personal health topics when referencing the MSU gift.

name: Hank Meijer
current_role: Executive chairman, Meijer Inc. (Grand Rapids, Michigan supercenter chain)
profile: Hank Meijer (b. 1952), grandson of Dutch immigrant founder Hendrik Meijer, co-owns the Meijer supercenter chain (~500 Midwest stores, ~$22B revenue) with brothers Doug and Mark. He was co-CEO from 1990 to 2017 and is now executive chairman; he is also a published historian and vice-chair of the Gerald R. Ford Presidential Foundation.
interesting_fact: Meijer pioneered one-stop 'supercenter' shopping (groceries plus general merchandise), the model later adopted by Walmart; the family's Frederik Meijer Gardens & Sculpture Park draws 700,000+ visitors a year.
deep_cut_fact: A 1973 University of Michigan literature graduate, he worked as a journalist until 1979 before joining the family firm, and is a serious biographer: 'Thrifty Years' (1984) on his grandfather and 'Arthur Vandenberg: The Man in the Middle of the American Century' (University of Chicago Press, 2017).
notes: Author angle (Vandenberg biography, C-SPAN appearances) is a natural podcast hook. Close friend of the Fords; trustee of the Kettering Foundation.

name: Mark Meijer
current_role: Co-owner and board member, Meijer Inc.; co-founder of Life EMS ambulance service (Grand Rapids, Michigan)
profile: Grandson of Dutch immigrant Hendrik Meijer, who started the Michigan grocery chain in 1934, Mark Meijer co-owns the family's ~500-store Midwest supercenter retailer (est. $22B revenue) with brothers Hank and Doug. He sits on the board but stays out of day-to-day operations, having built his own career in emergency medicine as co-founder of Life EMS in 1980.
interesting_fact: Instead of joining the family supermarket business he became a medic and co-founded Life EMS, now a large ambulance and EMS-training provider covering a 5,000-square-mile area around Grand Rapids.
deep_cut_fact: Life EMS began when medics Mark Meijer and Ken Morris rented a Grand Rapids office barely bigger than a walk-in closet; their 'dispatch center' was a card table with a phone and radio mic, and of their three vehicles only one was fully equipped and in service.
notes: Low public profile. The Meijer media hotline is the corporate route; Life EMS (1-888-LIFE-EMS, listed on its site) may be a warmer, more personal channel. The Life EMS founding story is a strong, positive icebreaker.

name: Miguel Krigsner
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, Grupo Boticário (Curitiba, Brazil)
profile: Miguel Krigsner, 76, born in La Paz to Jewish parents who fled Nazism, moved to Curitiba at 11, trained as a pharmacist-biochemist and opened compounding pharmacy O Boticario in 1977. Early franchising built Grupo Boticario (O Boticario, Eudora, Quem Disse Berenice?), with R$38.1B consumer sales in 2025; Forbes Brasil ranks him Brazil's 8th-richest.
interesting_fact: In 1990 he created the Fundação Grupo Boticário, one of Brazil's first private nature-conservation foundations, funded with about 1% of the group's net income; in 2011 he founded the Curitiba Holocaust Museum.
deep_cut_fact: Noticing most of his pharmacy customers were women, he began making personal-care products in the back of the shop on Rua Saldanha Marinho - face creams based on seaweed and collagen, mixed in a cake mixer.

public_contacts.value: Agência PROS (handles O Boticário brand press since 2021; no email published in results)

notes: Brother-in-law Artur Grynbaum is the long-time group executive. No published press email found (site blocks scraping); route via Grupo Boticário press office or Fundação Grupo Boticário. Conservation philanthropy is the warmest angle.

name: Baron Albert Frere
profile: Belgian financier Baron Albert Frère, founder of the Frère-Bourgeois holding and longtime controlling force behind Groupe Bruxelles Lambert (GBL), died on 3 December 2018 at age 92.
notes: Deceased (3 Dec 2018), per Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albert_Fr%C3%A8re); he dropped off Forbes/Hurun lists after 2018. His family's holdings (Frère-Bourgeois / GBL) continue under the next generation. Skipped further research per instructions.

name: Dietmar Hopp
current_role: SAP co-founder; owner/main backer of TSG 1899 Hoffenheim; founder, Dietmar Hopp Stiftung (foundation)
profile: Heidelberg-born (1940) telecom engineer who left IBM in 1972 with four colleagues (incl. Hasso Plattner, Klaus Tschira) to found SAP, serving as co-CEO 1988-98 and supervisory board chair to 2003. In 1995-96 he moved most of his SAP shares into the Dietmar Hopp Stiftung, which has given away around $1B for sport, medicine, education and social causes. He also invests in biotech (CureVac, via dievini).
interesting_fact: He bankrolled tiny village club TSG Hoffenheim from amateur leagues to the Bundesliga (2008) and spent ~EUR100M building the 30,000-seat Rhein-Neckar-Arena near Sinsheim.
deep_cut_fact: Hoffenheim is personal: he played for the club himself as a teenager, near his childhood home. Before SAP he studied telecommunications engineering in Karlsruhe (to 1966) and worked as a software developer/consultant at IBM.
notes: Age 86. Foundation email is the best published route. Has been the target of fan abuse campaigns - avoid that topic. Data/software angle: SAP origins, early real-time business software.

name: John Henry
current_role: Founder and Principal Owner, Fenway Sports Group (Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC, RFK Racing); owner and publisher, The Boston Globe
profile: John W. Henry (b. 1949, Quincy, Illinois) made his fortune in the 1980s with J.W. Henry & Co., a pioneering trend-following commodities fund. He then built a sports empire: he bought the Red Sox in 2002 (World Series titles in 2004, 2007, 2013 and 2018), Liverpool FC in 2010 (Champions League 2019) and The Boston Globe in 2013. Fenway Sports Group keeps expanding, including into golf's TGL.
interesting_fact: The son of soybean farmers, Henry learned hedging by trading corn and soybean futures. After a summer in Norway he devised the mechanical trend-following system that became the basis of J.W. Henry & Co.
deep_cut_fact: Henry never finished college, which he puts down to time spent performing and touring with two bands, Elysian Fields and Hillary. In 2024 Led Zeppelin's Jimmy Page presented him with the American Academy of Achievement's Golden Plate Award.

public_contacts.value: media@fenwaysportsgroup.com (FSG communications, Zineb Curran, EVP & CCO)

name: Albert Boehringer

interesting_fact: Boehringer Ingelheim began in 1885 as a small tartaric-acid factory with 28 employees that the elder Albert Boehringer bought in Nieder-Ingelheim; it is still headquartered there and fully family-owned 140 years later.

name: Christian Boehringer

current_role: Chairman of the Executive Committee, Boehringer Ingelheim Stiftung (honorary); entrepreneur and family shareholder in Boehringer Ingelheim
profile: Member of the Boehringer family that owns Boehringer Ingelheim, the world's largest private pharma company (founded 1885 by Albert Boehringer; ~53,000 staff, 130 markets).
