name: Trevor Rees-Jones
current_role: Founder, Chief Oil & Gas (Dallas); co-founder of The Rees-Jones Foundation
profile: Dallas oil-and-gas bankruptcy lawyer (Thompson & Knight) who switched to investing in wells in 1984 and founded Chief Oil & Gas in 1994. Chief was an early Barnett Shale and Marcellus driller; he sold Barnett assets to Devon in 2006 and Chief's Marcellus business to Chesapeake in 2022, and remains active in oil, gas and mining ventures plus large North Texas philanthropy.
interesting_fact: By 2005 Chief Oil & Gas was the second-largest producer in the Barnett Shale, having drilled more than 250 wells, and its 2006 Barnett sale to Devon and Crosstex brought roughly $2.6 billion in cash.
deep_cut_fact: He earned Eagle Scout with Troop 70 in 1966, and the Circle Ten Council's Trevor Rees-Jones Scout Camp is named after him; his foundation also funded the Rees-Jones Foundation Leadership Veranda at the Boy Scouts' Summit Bechtel Reserve.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews but did several with Hart Energy and D CEO. Foundation emails were taken from search snippets of the official contact page (site blocked direct fetch) - re-verify before use. Also a Dartmouth trustee (2010-14) and TCU trustee.

name: Lin Shu-hong
current_role: Co-founder and President (總裁) of Chang Chun Group, Taiwan petrochemicals (stepped down as chairman end-2013)
profile: Lin Shu-hong (林書鴻, also Suhon Lin, b. 1928) co-founded Chang Chun Group in 1949 with classmates Tseng Shin-yi and M.K. Liao on about $100. It grew into one of Asia's largest private petrochemical groups (resins, chemicals, electronic materials) with plants in Taiwan, China and SE Asia. Though he left the chairmanship in 2013, in his mid-90s he still toured plants weekly.
interesting_fact: Called 'the Edison of petrochemicals': in the early days he ran 5-6 experiments a day to perfect a plywood adhesive that won over 60+ Taiwanese plywood makers and was even sold to the US military. He was elected to ITRI's first class of Fellows (2012) and won a National S&T contribution award (2016).
deep_cut_fact: At 94 he still visited the Hsinchu, Miaoli, Mailiao, Changhua and Kaohsiung plants every week, read nightly before bed, and recommended Kazuo Inamori's book on work, which he had covered in sticky tabs and notes.
notes: Born 1 Aug 1928 (age ~98); Forbes 2026 still lists him and no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Famously low-profile; group is private with no press/IR desk found (website behind Cloudflare). Any approach would go via Chang Chun Group corporate office in Taipei.

name: Carlos Bulgheroni
current_role: Deceased (died 3 September 2016, aged 71, in the United States)
profile: Argentine oil and gas magnate who, with brother Alejandro, built Bridas (founded by their father) into Argentina's leading private energy group, later partnering with BP and CNOOC in Pan American Energy. He died of cancer in September 2016; Alejandro now leads the family business.
notes: Deceased: died 3 Sep 2016 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni ; https://www.pagina12.com.ar/diario/economia/2-308544-2016-09-04.html). Wealth was shared with brother Alejandro Bulgheroni (alive, chairman of Pan American Energy Group) - he would be the relevant outreach target instead.

name: Vladimir Kim
current_role: Major shareholder, KAZ Minerals (private copper miner, Kazakhstan/Kyrgyzstan); former chairman of Kazakhmys/KAZ Minerals
profile: Vladimir Kim joined Zhezkazgantsvetmet, later Kazakhmys, in 1995 and chaired Kazakhmys from 2005. It became the first Kazakh company listed in London. After the 2014 split he kept a big stake in copper producer KAZ Minerals, which he and Oleg Novachuk took private in 2021; it runs the Aktogay and Bozshakol mines. In 2025 he sold his majority stake in Kazakhmys Corp. to Nurlan Artykbaev.
interesting_fact: He is descended from Koreans whom Stalin deported to Kazakhstan, and for years he was ranked Kazakhstan's richest person.
deep_cut_fact: Kim was born on 29 October 1960 in the village of Slavyanka (now Myrzakent) in South Kazakhstan. He trained as an architect, graduating from the Almaty Architecture and Construction Institute in 1982, and holds a Candidate of Technical Sciences degree. After independence he did business internships in Germany, Switzerland and South Korea.
notes: Very private; he gives no interviews and has no social presence. Copper for electrification and data centers is a relevant angle. Approach only via KAZ Minerals corporate communications (head office now in Dubai). Politically connected, so avoid political topics.

name: Jeff Skoll
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Skoll Foundation; Chairman, Capricorn Investment Group (impact investing)
profile: Montreal-born, Toronto-raised electrical engineer and Stanford MBA who became eBay's first full-time hire and first president in 1996, leaving in 2001. He turned his eBay wealth into the Skoll Foundation (social entrepreneurship, Skoll World Forum) and Participant Media (An Inconvenient Truth, Spotlight), which he wound down in 2024, and invests via Capricorn.
interesting_fact: One of impact investing's earliest proponents: Capricorn Investment Group's early bets included Tesla, battery developer QuantumScape and air-taxi maker Joby Aviation; his Skoll Foundation and Fund have distributed some $1.3B since 1999.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Toronto he co-edited the engineering students' satirical newspaper The Toike Oike. After graduating he backpacked around the world, then started two Toronto businesses: IT consultancy Skoll Engineering and computer-rental firm Micros on the Move.
notes: Best route is Skoll Foundation press (press@skoll.org). Strong climate/energy angle via Capricorn clean-tech investments. $1.3B giving figure per Forbes profile.

name: Franz Viegener
current_role: Co-Chair of the Viega Shareholders' Committee, Viega Group (Attendorn, Germany); board member, Viega Foundation
profile: Fifth-generation member of the family that owns Viega, the Attendorn-based maker of press-fitting piping, plumbing and HVAC installation systems (~5,500 staff; sites in Germany, the US and India). He co-chairs the shareholders' committee with cousin Anna Viegener while non-family executives run operations, and is involved in the Viega Foundation's clean-water work.
interesting_fact: Viega began in winter 1899 when founder Franz Anselm Viegener started making beer taps in his own farm shed for neighbouring breweries and pubs in the Sauerland town of Attendorn, before switching to water-pipe installation materials.
deep_cut_fact: At the June 2026 opening of Viega's sixth German plant, in former Michelin tyre-works warehouses in Kirkel, Saarland, he said: 'We operate globally... That said, Germany is and will continue to be a key production base for us,' citing the region's concentration of skilled metalworkers.
notes: Very private family-business owner; minimal personal press. Route via Viega Corporate Communication. Building-tech/water angle rather than energy, though HVAC/heat-pump installation is adjacent.

name: Thomas Kaeser
current_role: Owner and CEO (managing partner), Kaeser Kompressoren SE, Coburg, Germany
profile: Thomas Kaeser (b. 1953, Coburg) joined the family firm founded by his grandfather in 1919, became managing partner in 1985 and has led it since 2009 with his wife Tina-Maria Vlantoussi-Kaeser. As sole owner he built Kaeser into a global compressed-air and vacuum systems maker with ~8,800 staff in 140 countries and 2024 sales above €1.7B.
interesting_fact: He pioneered 'compressed air as a service' in an industry that sold machines: under the Sigma Air Utility model Kaeser runs the customer's whole air supply and bills for air used, on the motto 'customers need compressed air, not necessarily a compressor.'
deep_cut_fact: After his Abitur at Coburg's Ernestinum Gymnasium he studied industrial engineering (Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen) at TU Karlsruhe before joining the family firm in 1979; he later received the Preis Deutscher Maschinenbau, with the laudator calling him 'an entrepreneur in the classic sense. Not a manager. An entrepreneur!'
notes: Private, family-owned; rare interviews (mostly trade press). Company press releases list press contact Daniela Koehler (Kaeser press office, corporate line +49 9561 640452) — https://www.pressebox.de/newsroom/kaeser-kompressoren-gmbh. Compressed air is a large industrial energy user, a natural energy-efficiency angle.

name: Palmer Luckey
current_role: Founder, Anduril Industries (defense tech); founder, ModRetro
profile: Palmer Luckey built the Oculus Rift prototype as a teenager in his parents' Long Beach garage, founded Oculus VR in 2012 and sold it to Facebook in 2014 for ~$2B. After leaving Facebook in 2016 he founded Anduril in 2017, making autonomous drones, sensor towers and the Lattice AI software for the military (valued at $30.5B in June 2025). He also runs retro-gaming hardware maker ModRetro.
interesting_fact: He built more than 50 head-mounted display prototypes before the Rift, funding the work partly by repairing and reselling damaged iPhones (earning at least $36,000), and amassed a large collection of historic VR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: He majored in journalism at Cal State Long Beach and was Online Editor of the student newspaper, the Daily Forty-Niner; he also worked part-time at USC's ICT Mixed Reality Lab building low-cost VR for BRAVEMIND, an Army effort to treat veterans' PTSD.
notes: Very active and accessible on X; does many podcasts. Anduril media@ is the official press route. The journalism-major detail is a natural hook for a journalist. Energy/data-center angle is weak, but Anduril's Arsenal manufacturing campus (Ohio) is a big industrial build.

name: Penny Pritzker

name: Isaac Perlmutter
current_role: Private investor (former Chairman, Marvel Entertainment)
profile: Israeli-born investor 'Ike' Perlmutter arrived in the US in the 1960s, built a closeout-goods business, co-owned Toy Biz and beat Carl Icahn for control of bankrupt Marvel in 1998. He revived it via superhero films (Iron Man, Spider-Man) and sold it to Disney in 2009 for $4B, serving as Marvel chairman until Disney let him go in 2023; he now invests privately from Palm Beach.
interesting_fact: The famously reclusive billionaire reportedly attended the 2008 'Iron Man' premiere disguised in glasses and a fake mustache; he is also a veteran of Israel's 1967 Six-Day War.

name: Russell Savage

profile: Born 1970 as Russ Weiner, he founded Rockstar energy drink in 2001 after Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar rejected the idea, funding it with a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito condo. He sold Rockstar to PepsiCo in 2020 for more than $4B and in 2025 took the surname Savage to honor his father, radio host Michael Savage.

deep_cut_fact: Before Rockstar, the San Diego State political-science grad ran for the California State Assembly in 1998 and won the Republican primary for the 6th district by just five votes (he lost the general election).
notes: No published personal or office contact found; Rockstar is now a PepsiCo brand, so company press channels will not reach him. Search under both 'Russ Weiner' and 'Russell Savage'. Politically active donor; keep outreach on entrepreneurship and the bootstrapped Rockstar story.

name: Claudio Del Vecchio
current_role: Private investor; 12.5% shareholder of Delfin (Del Vecchio family holding, owner of ~32% of EssilorLuxottica)
profile: Claudio Del Vecchio (born 1956), eldest son of Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio, moved to New York in 1982 to build Luxottica's US business and took it public on the NYSE in 1990. He later owned US retailers Casual Corner and Brooks Brothers (2001-2020). Since 2022 he holds 12.5% of Delfin (EssilorLuxottica, Generali, UniCredit).
interesting_fact: He led Luxottica's 1995 acquisition of LensCrafters, a key step in turning the Italian frame maker into the world's largest eyewear group.

notes: Based in the US; no published personal, office or press contact found and no executive role now. Avoid the Brooks Brothers bankruptcy and 2026 Delfin shareholder disputes. Not an energy/data-center fit.

name: Romesh T. Wadhwani
current_role: Founder & Chairman, SymphonyAI; Chairman, ConcertAI; founder, Wadhwani Foundation
profile: Born in Karachi in 1947 and raised in India, Wadhwani studied at IIT Bombay and got a PhD at Carnegie Mellon. He became a billionaire when i2 Technologies bought his Aspect Development for $9.3B in stock, later ran Symphony Technology Group, and in 2017 founded enterprise-AI firm SymphonyAI (~$1B invested); he left the CEO role in 2022 but remains chairman.
interesting_fact: With brother Sunil he founded the Wadhwani Institute for Artificial Intelligence in Mumbai (2018) to build AI for public good, committing over $30M; his Wadhwani Foundation also runs India's National Entrepreneurship Network across 500+ colleges.
deep_cut_fact: Before software riches, his first two ventures were Compu-Guard Corporation, a technology-enabled energy management company, and American Robot Corporation, which made software for computer-integrated manufacturing.
notes: Good fit for an energy/AI podcast given Compu-Guard energy-management roots and SymphonyAI. Padma Shri (2020); trustee of the Kennedy Center and CSIS. Wadhwani Foundation (wadhwanifoundation.org) is an alternate route.

name: Johnelle Hunt
current_role: Co-founder and largest individual shareholder (~19%), J.B. Hunt Transport Services; philanthropist (Fayetteville, Arkansas)
profile: Born Johnelle DeBusk in Heber Springs, Arkansas in 1932, she and her husband J.B. Hunt (d. 2006) sold their home in 1961 to start a rice-hull business in Stuttgart, then launched trucking firm J.B. Hunt Transport in 1969. She served as credit manager, secretary-treasurer and corporate secretary as it grew into one of America's largest freight companies (~$12B sales). Now 94, she focuses on philanthropy, including a $100M pledge to the University of Arkansas (2024).
interesting_fact: She was one of the 11 inaugural inductees of the Arkansas Women's Hall of Fame (2015), and the Women's Foundation of Arkansas named her 2012 Woman of the Year.
deep_cut_fact: The original 1961 J.B. Hunt Company in Stuttgart, Arkansas sold and hauled rice hulls for poultry litter, using a hull-compressing machine J.B. invented. Johnelle and J.B. recorded a 2006 oral history for the University of Arkansas Pryor Center, with clips like 'Finding a Good Press' and 'From a Sled to a Jet'.
notes: Aged 94 and private; no personal channels. Corporate press form is the only published route; a philanthropy angle (University of Arkansas, Ozark Highlands Center) would land better. The Pryor Center oral history has rich first-person material.

name: Peter Kellogg
current_role: Chairman and controlling owner, IAT Insurance Group (privately held specialty P&C insurer and reinsurer, Raleigh NC)
profile: Peter R. Kellogg (b. 1942) joined his father's NYSE specialist firm Spear, Leeds & Kellogg in 1967, led it from the 1980s to become the first specialist handling over 10% of NYSE stocks, and sold it to Goldman Sachs in 2000 for about $6.5B. He then built family-owned IAT Insurance Group, serving as CEO until 2014-15 and remaining chairman.
interesting_fact: He has given more than $4 million to the U.S. ski and snowboarding teams.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 he and his wife, through their foundation, bought the John F. Peto Studio Museum in Island Heights, New Jersey - the home studio of the 19th-century trompe-l'oeil painter - to save it from demolition, spent about $2M restoring it, and later handed it to the museum's own board.
notes: Age 84; very private. IAT's CEO is Bill Cunningham; IAT press releases list no media contact. Avoid older NASD/AMEX matters (complaint dismissed in 2004). Philanthropy runs via the Peter R. & Cynthia K. Kellogg Foundation.

name: Alex Behring
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, 3G Capital (New York); board member, Restaurant Brands International
profile: Rio-born Alexandre Behring (b. 1967) trained under Jorge Paulo Lemann at GP Investments, then co-founded 3G Capital in 2004 with Lemann, Telles and Sicupira. 3G engineered Burger King's buyout and its 2014 merger with Tim Hortons (RBI), as well as Heinz/Kraft Heinz (exited 2024). It bought 75% of Hunter Douglas in 2021 and Skechers for ~$9.4B in 2025.
interesting_fact: He played water polo at national level in Brazil from the juniors through college. He is also a free diver and spearfisher who once held a world record for mahi-mahi.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineer by training (PUC-Rio), he co-founded a tech firm, Modus OSI Technologies, in 1989, working between Florida and São Paulo. In 1998 he became founding CEO of the privatised Brazilian freight railroad América Latina Logística (ALL), before 3G.
notes: Very private and rarely gives interviews; 3G as a firm is famously press-shy. The only published channel is 3G's general inbox. Hooks: his engineering and railroad-CEO past (infrastructure/logistics) and Harvard Business School (Baker Scholar, Board of Dean's Advisors).

name: Clemente Del Vecchio
current_role: Shareholder (~12.5%+) of Delfin, the Luxembourg holding company of the Del Vecchio family (EssilorLuxottica, Generali, MPS, UniCredit, Covivio)
profile: Youngest of Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio's six children (b. 2004), he inherited a 12.5% stake in family holding Delfin when his father died in June 2022, becoming the world's youngest billionaire on Forbes' 2023 list at 18. Delfin's main asset is a ~30% stake in EssilorLuxottica, plus stakes in Generali, UniCredit, MPS and Covivio. In 2026 he became Delfin's largest single shareholder after buying a small extra block.
interesting_fact: Forbes ranked him the world's youngest billionaire in 2023, aged 18, with a fortune of about $3.5bn - all from his one-eighth share of Delfin.
notes: Very private young heir with no public role, website or social accounts found; no published contact. Italian press reports he set up a personal vehicle to hold his Delfin stake. Delfin succession/shareholder disputes are ongoing - avoid. Little relevance to energy/data-center themes. Source on 2026 'first shareholder': https://iusletter.com/oggi-sulla-stampa/delfin-clemente-del-vecchio-primo-azionista/

name: Luca Del Vecchio
current_role: Private investor; controls Lufin, his Luxembourg personal holding company (est. July 2024)
profile: Fifth child of Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio (d. 2022). He inherited 12.5% of Delfin (EssilorLuxottica, Generali, UniCredit, MPS). In April 2026 he and his sister Paola agreed to transfer their combined 25% to their brother Leonardo Maria for about EUR 10B. He now runs Lufin, his Luxembourg holding company.
interesting_fact: MF-Milano Finanza reported in 2026 that he moved his residence from London to Luxembourg. His holding company Lufin, still small in its 2025 accounts, is being prepared to manage the billions from the Delfin share transfer, due by September 2026.
notes: Very private young heir with no public statements or official accounts. Lufin is a newly built investment vehicle and may become an active investor once the Delfin proceeds arrive (late 2026). Source on the transfer: https://www.quotidiano.net/economia/svolta-sulle-quote-delfin-sciolto-il-nodo-delleredita-jrz7iico. Avoid inheritance-dispute topics in outreach. No published contact route.

name: Marisa Del Vecchio
current_role: Heads the Museo dell'Ottica (Museum of Optics) in Agordo; 12.5% shareholder of Delfin, the Del Vecchio family holding company
profile: Eldest child (b. 1958) of Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio (d. 2022) and his first wife Luciana Nervo. She inherited 12.5% of Luxembourg-based Delfin, which controls EssilorLuxottica and holds stakes in Generali, UniCredit, Monte dei Paschi and Covivio. She keeps a low profile, leading the optics museum in Agordo, the Dolomites town where Luxottica was founded in 1961.
interesting_fact: Agordo, where she runs the optics museum, remains Luxottica's historic base: EssilorLuxottica plans to produce smart glasses there, and in 2025 the plant's street was renamed Via Leonardo Del Vecchio 1 for her father's 90th birthday anniversary.
deep_cut_fact: The Museo dell'Ottica she leads, promoted by Luxottica, is housed in the 17th-century Palazzo Crotta-De Manzoni in Agordo, which Luxottica bought, and traces the history of eyewear.
notes: Very private heir, no public channels found. Avoid Delfin inheritance/governance disputes among the siblings. Poor podcast fit; possible route via the museum or Delfin.

name: Nicoletta Zampillo
current_role: Shareholder (12.5%) in Delfin S.à r.l., the Del Vecchio family holding company; no executive role
profile: Milan-based widow of Leonardo Del Vecchio, founder of Luxottica and late chairman of EssilorLuxottica (d. 2022). She inherited a 12.5% stake in Luxembourg holding company Delfin, which owns stakes in EssilorLuxottica, Generali, Monte dei Paschi, UniCredit and Covivio. She has publicly said she has nothing to do with running Luxottica.
interesting_fact: She reportedly met Del Vecchio through her father, one of Luxottica's first sales representatives in Milan; the couple married in 1997, divorced, and remarried in 2010.
notes: Private individual with no public business role; press coverage centres on the Del Vecchio estate, which should be avoided in outreach. No contacts found. Son Leonardo Maria Del Vecchio is the more public family member (not to be contacted via this profile).

name: Paola Del Vecchio
current_role: Shareholder (12.5%, held via a personal vehicle) of Delfin S.a r.l., the Del Vecchio family holding company
profile: Third child of Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio (d. 2022) and his first wife Luciana Nervo. She inherited a 12.5% stake in Luxembourg-based Delfin, which controls EssilorLuxottica (the world's largest eyewear group) and holds stakes in Generali, Monte dei Paschi/Mediobanca, UniCredit and Covivio. She holds no operating role and keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: Delfin, in which she owns one-eighth, is the controlling shareholder of EssilorLuxottica, maker of Ray-Ban and Oakley and partner on Meta's Ray-Ban smart glasses.
notes: Extremely private; no published contacts or interviews found. Recent Italian press centres on the Delfin succession/governance dispute among heirs - avoid that topic. Not a natural fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Rocco Basilico
current_role: Shareholder (12.5%) of Delfin, the Del Vecchio family holding; left EssilorLuxottica as Chief Wearables Officer effective Jan 2026 to pursue new projects
profile: Stepson of Luxottica founder Leonardo Del Vecchio, whose will made him an equal heir with 12.5% of Delfin (EssilorLuxottica, Generali, MPS, UniCredit stakes). Rose from Oliver Peoples CEO to Chief Wearables Officer, leading the Meta partnership behind Ray-Ban Stories and Ray-Ban Meta; left EssilorLuxottica in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: He was the executive who forged EssilorLuxottica's smart-glasses partnership with Meta, creating Ray-Ban Stories (2021) and its AI-enabled successor Ray-Ban Meta, one of the most successful AI wearables to date.
deep_cut_fact: Named CEO of Oliver Peoples at just 27 (2016) and to Forbes 30 Under 30 a year later; on Google Glass he said 'every product, even the earliest, was a step in the right direction, because we are all learning from what comes before us.'
notes: Departure from EssilorLuxottica (announced Dec 2025, effective Jan 2026) came amid Delfin inheritance discussions - avoid that topic. Next venture reportedly tech/wearables-related but unannounced. No published office or press contact found; he announces news via personal Instagram (handle not verified here).

name: Liu Hanyuan
current_role: Chairman, Tongwei Group; NPC deputy and vice chairman of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce
profile: Liu left a job at the Meishan county hydropower bureau in Sichuan to build a fish-feed business (founded 1986) that became Tongwei Group, a global leader in aquafeed. Tongwei later moved into polysilicon and solar cells, becoming one of the world's largest PV manufacturers. He is a prominent lawmaker-advocate for solar and renewable-energy policy.
interesting_fact: Tongwei ranks among the world's largest players in two unrelated industries at once: aquaculture feed and solar (polysilicon/cells). Liu regularly files NPC/CPPCC proposals pushing PV, e.g. solar to cut smog and tax cuts for the PV industry.
deep_cut_fact: In spring 1983, aged ~18, he pooled 200 yuan savings plus money from his parents selling two pigs (500 yuan total) to build a 64 m2 submerged fish cage in a Meishan canal; stocking 185 kg of carp yielded 1,390 kg by autumn, reportedly a Sichuan record for fish yield per unit area.
notes: ir_email is the published board-secretary (Yan Ke) contact of listed Tongwei Co. (600438) per its 2024 annual report summary; Tongwei's English site publishes many news items about Liu's policy proposals, a good angle for an energy podcast.

name: Gordon Getty
current_role: Composer and philanthropist (Gordon P. Getty Family Foundation); Getty Oil heir
profile: Son of oil tycoon J. Paul Getty, he led the 1984 sale of Getty Oil to Texaco for $10.1B and in 1985 split the family trust into separate trusts. Now in his 90s, he is a working classical composer (operas Plump Jack, Usher House, The Canterville Ghost, Goodbye, Mr. Chips) and a major San Francisco arts donor; he co-founded PlumpJack Winery with Gavin Newsom in 1995.
interesting_fact: He has given more than $450 million to his philanthropic foundation since 2008, and New Century Chamber Orchestra dedicated its entire 2025-26 season in his honor; he was one of ten inaugural inductees into Opera America's Opera Hall of Fame (2020).
deep_cut_fact: An English-literature graduate of the University of San Francisco and longtime poet, he writes his own librettos; his most-performed vocal work is The White Election (1981), a cycle setting 31 Emily Dickinson poems for soprano and piano, performed at Lincoln Center and the Hermitage Theatre.

public_contacts.value: Nancy Shear Arts Services - sheararts@gmail.com (PR/press for his music only)
mail@rorkmusic.com (Rork Music, his publisher; music inquiries only)

notes: Born 1933; very old and private on business matters. Only published routes are music-related (publisher Rork Music, PR via Nancy Shear Arts Services); his site says funding requests are discarded. An energy-angle pitch is a stretch; an arts/legacy framing fits better. Wikipedia notes 2026-released documents showing past Epstein correspondence - sensitive topic.

name: Li Min
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Rockchip Electronics Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603893), Fuzhou
profile: Li Min cofounded Rockchip in Fuzhou in 2001 with Huang Xu and remains chairman (reappointed general manager in Jan 2025). Rockchip designs SoCs for AIoT devices, tablets and edge-AI products and listed in Shanghai in 2020; Li holds roughly 37% of the company, the source of his fortune.
interesting_fact: Rockchip, a Fuzhou chip designer, counts Intel, Samsung and Google among its customers and focuses on intelligent IoT and edge-AI processors.
deep_cut_fact: In December 2025 he donated 175,000 Rockchip shares (worth roughly RMB 31M at the time) to the education foundation of his alma mater, Fuzhou No. 1 Middle School (福州一中), 'to give back to his alma mater'.
notes: Low media profile; English name in Chinese is 励民. Best route is via Rockchip's securities/IR department. Some unofficial sites say he was born 1965 and graduated Zhejiang University 1991 - not verified.

name: Steven Hao
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cognition (maker of the Devin AI software-engineering agent)
profile: MIT-trained competitive programmer and former early engineer at Scale AI who co-founded Cognition in late 2023 with Scott Wu and Walden Yan. Cognition's Devin autonomous coding agent (and its 2025 acquisition of Windsurf) drove rapid valuation jumps, making Hao a billionaire per Forbes.
interesting_fact: All three Cognition co-founders were International Olympiad in Informatics competitors; Forbes reported that the company's rapid growth made CTO Hao a billionaire within about two years of founding.
deep_cut_fact: At IOI 2014 in Taipei he placed 6th in the world for the United States, scoring perfect 100s on five of six problems (525/600) to win a gold medal.
notes: No published press email found; only company social accounts. CEO Scott Wu is the usual public face; Hao is the technical lead and appears at engineering conferences (e.g. GitNation speaker profile), a possible route.

name: Fan Hongwei
current_role: Chairman, Hengli Petrochemical Co. (SSE: 600346); Vice Chairman, Hengli Group
profile: Born 1967 in Wujiang, Suzhou, Fan co-founded what became Hengli Group with her husband Chen Jianhua, starting in textiles in 1994 and integrating upstream into polyester, PTA and a giant refinery-petrochemical complex on Changxing Island, Dalian. She chairs listed Hengli Petrochemical; Hengli Group posted 2024 revenue of RMB 871.5bn (Fortune Global 500 #81).
interesting_fact: Hengli's integrated 'from a drop of oil to a bolt of cloth' chain helped break foreign dominance of PX and PTA feedstocks in China; in July 2025 Fan was one of 100 private entrepreneurs given a national 'outstanding builder' award in Beijing.
deep_cut_fact: Hengli began in 1994 as the Wujiang Chemical Fiber Weaving Factory in Shengze, Suzhou, with just 27 employees; when Hengli Group was formally set up in 2003, Fan became its general manager running production and operations.
notes: hlzq@hengli.com is Hengli Petrochemical's board-office/investor mailbox (listed in 2025 and 2026 earnings-call notices); Chinese-language approach advisable. Very low international media profile.

name: Carlos
profile: Carlos Alberto Bulgheroni (1945-2016), Argentine co-owner (with brother Alejandro) of the family energy group Bridas, died on 3 September 2016. Record matched via source of wealth Bridas and shared_with Alejandro Bulgheroni.
notes: DECEASED 3 Sep 2016 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carlos_Bulgheroni). Name field is truncated ('Carlos'); country listed as Spain is wrong - he was Argentine. For Bridas/Pan American Energy, the living family principal is his brother Alejandro Bulgheroni.

name: Romesh Wadhwani
current_role: Founder & Chairman, SAIGroup (SymphonyAI, ConcertAI); Founder & Chairman, Wadhwani Foundation
profile: Born in Karachi in 1947 and educated at IIT Bombay and Carnegie Mellon (PhD), Wadhwani made his fortune founding Aspect Development and later ran software PE firm Symphony Technology Group. He now heads SAIGroup, which includes SymphonyAI (backed by his $1B commitment) and ConcertAI. His Wadhwani Foundation funds entrepreneurship and AI-for-good work in India.
interesting_fact: Aspect Development, which he founded in 1991, was acquired by i2 Technologies in 1999 for $9.3 billion in stock. In 2020 India awarded him the Padma Shri.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aspect, he spent a decade running two startups. One was American Robot Corporation, which made computer-integrated manufacturing software. The other was Compu-Guard Corporation, an early technology-enabled energy-management company.

public_contacts.value: Chris Gale (Gale Strategies), SymphonyAI media contact: Chris@GaleStrategies.com

notes: The Compu-Guard energy-management startup is a natural hook for an energy-focused podcast. He also sits on the boards of trustees of CSIS and the Kennedy Center. The best route is SymphonyAI's PR contact.

name: Zhenhua Yao
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Baoneng Group (Shenzhen)
profile: Yao Zhenhua (姚振华, b. 1970, Shantou, Guangdong) founded Shenzhen-based Baoneng Group in 1992. He grew it from agricultural trading and retail into a conglomerate spanning shopping malls, property, insurance (Foresea Life), healthcare and autos (Qoros). He became famous in 2015–16 for the hostile stake-building in China Vanke. He is no longer on Forbes' billionaire list; Baoneng has been working through heavy debts since 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2016 the Vanke share-buying campaign made Yao one of China's richest men; Hurun ranked him No. 4 with about RMB 115B. Chinese media nicknamed him one of the market's 'barbarians at the gate'.
deep_cut_fact: Yao graduated from South China University of Technology in 1992 with a double major in industrial management engineering and food engineering. He started out in the agricultural produce trade before founding Baoneng in Shenzhen that same year.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Baoneng faces extensive debt-enforcement cases, and he is barred from the insurance industry until 2027. Forbes lists him as 'former' billionaire, so his net worth is likely far below the listed figure. No published contact found.

name: Yao Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Baoneng Group (Shenzhen conglomerate: property, retail malls, insurance, autos)
profile: Shenzhen entrepreneur (b. ~1970) who grew Baoneng from a 1990s vegetable-supply business into a conglomerate spanning shopping malls, property, healthcare, Foresea Life insurance and Baoneng Motor. He became nationally known in 2015–16 when his insurer built a ~25% stake in China Vanke; Baoneng has been in financial distress since 2020.
interesting_fact: Baoneng began in 1992 under Shenzhen's 'Shopping Basket' food-supply programme as a vegetable wholesaling operation, which grew into one of the city's largest vegetable suppliers before becoming a mall and finance empire.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 Baoneng bought the Shenzhen car plant of Changan PSA (the Changan–Peugeot Citroën joint venture), renaming it Baoneng Motor as his entry into carmaking.
notes: Caution: Baoneng is a distressed group facing creditor lawsuits (e.g. Bank of Shanghai won a 2.58B-yuan appeal in July 2026 naming Yao personally); he was barred from China's insurance industry for 10 years in 2017. Not a good outreach target; no published press contact found.

name: Xu Dongbo
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with his father, founder-chairman Xu Gaoming) of Laopu Gold Co. (HKEX: 6181); no listed executive or board title
profile: Son of Xu Gaoming, who founded Beijing-based Laopu Gold in 2009 as a 'heritage gold' brand of handcrafted jewellery using traditional Chinese goldsmithing. He holds shares directly and 30% of family vehicle Hongqiao Jinji; the family controlled ~58-61% after the 2024 Hong Kong IPO, whose shares soared with record gold prices.
interesting_fact: Laopu Gold positions itself as China's top 'heritage gold' brand: its pieces replicate textures of ancient royal jewellery and use at least two traditional handmade gold-crafting techniques, earning it comparisons with Western luxury houses.

public_contacts.value: ir@lphj.com (Laopu Gold, for the attention of the Board)

notes: Almost no public profile; father Xu Gaoming is the public face and the likelier interviewee. May 2026: Xu Dongbo personally bought ~HK$166M of Laopu H shares after a steep share-price decline. Consumer/luxury, not an energy or data-center fit.

name: Paul Foster
current_role: Founder & CEO, Franklin Mountain Investments (El Paso, TX); former founder/chairman of Western Refining
profile: A Baylor-trained CPA who kept the books for small Southwest refineries, Foster took over bankrupt El Paso Refining with partners in 1992, built Western Refining and sold it to Tesoro in 2017 ($6.4B deal). Via Franklin Mountain Investments he holds 30+ businesses (real estate, restaurants, sports); in 2025 he sold Franklin Mountain Energy for about $2.5B.
interesting_fact: He is part owner of the El Paso Chihuahuas Triple-A baseball team (via MountainStar Sports Group) and in 2007 gave $50M to help create the Paul L. Foster School of Medicine at Texas Tech in El Paso.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Lovington, New Mexico (class of 1975), he earned an accounting degree from Baylor in 1979 and then started out working at the local refinery back in Lovington before moving to El Paso.
notes: Very relevant to energy angle: serves on the Dallas Fed Energy Advisory Council and was appointed by Gov. Abbott to the ERCOT board selection committee (https://gov.texas.gov/news/post/governor-abbott-appoints-foster-to-ercot-board-selection-committee). Best route is Franklin Mountain Investments' general inbox.

name: Sofia Högberg Schörling
current_role: Vice Chairman, Melker Schörling AB (Schörling AB); board member of Hexagon, Securitas and ASSA ABLOY
profile: Sofia Schörling Högberg (b. 1978, BSc Business Administration) is co-majority owner with her sister of Melker Schörling AB, the Stockholm holding company built by her late father, investor Melker Schörling. It holds large stakes in listed Hexagon, AAK, ASSA ABLOY, Hexpol and Securitas. She has sat on its board since 2006 and been vice chairman since 2016.
interesting_fact: Crown Princess Victoria of Sweden attended her 2005 wedding, accompanied by Daniel Westling, now Prince Daniel.
deep_cut_fact: She joined the board of security giant Securitas in 2005, aged about 27, a year before joining the family holding company's board. She also sits on the board of the Stockholm Chamber of Commerce.

public_contacts.value: info@schorlingab.se (Melker Schörling AB / Schörling AB general inbox)

notes: Low public profile; acts as board-level owner rather than operator. Holding company's general inbox is the only published route. Securitas has a data-center security business, a possible hook.

name: Russ Savage
current_role: Founder of Rockstar Energy (sold to PepsiCo 2020); private investor, largely in luxury real estate; based in Miami Beach
profile: Russ Savage (born Russell Weiner, 1970; renamed in 2025 to honor his father, radio host Michael Savage) launched Rockstar energy drink in 2001 with a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito condo after Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar passed on the idea. He sold Rockstar to PepsiCo in 2020 in a deal worth $4B+ and has since focused on investing, notably luxury Florida real estate.
interesting_fact: When the first Rockstar cans hit stores and bars, he promoted the brand by driving around San Francisco in an old limo painted with the Rockstar logo.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Rockstar he ran a yard-service business in his Northern California neighborhood at age 8 and worked the Wendy's drive-thru at 15; later, after a political-science degree at San Diego State, he worked as a travel consultant.
notes: No published personal, office or press contacts found; Rockstar is now owned by PepsiCo (Celsius holds US/Canada rights since 2025), so company press channels don't reach him. Travel-consultant detail is from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russell_Weiner). Avoid politics; he ran for CA Assembly in 1998.

name: Russ Weiner
current_role: Founder of Rockstar Energy (sold to PepsiCo in 2020); private investor
profile: Weiner founded Rockstar energy drink in 2001 after his boss, Skyy Vodka founder Maurice Kanbar, passed on the idea, funding it with a $50,000 mortgage on his Sausalito condo. He built it into a top US energy-drink brand and sold it to PepsiCo in 2020 for more than $4B. He now keeps a low profile as a private investor and political donor.
interesting_fact: When the first Rockstar cans hit stores, Weiner promoted them by driving around San Francisco in an old limo painted with the Rockstar logo. As a boy he ran a yard-service business at age 8.
deep_cut_fact: Before beverages he ran for the California State Assembly in 1998 as a Republican. He won the primary by just five votes and was endorsed by the president of the Oakland NAACP branch, then lost the general election to incumbent Kerry Mazzoni.
notes: No published personal, office or press contact found. Rockstar is now part of PepsiCo, so PepsiCo media relations would only cover the brand, not him. Low energy/AI link (energy drinks, not energy). He is also a political fundraiser, so check fit.

name: Thomas Straumann
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Medartis Holding AG; major shareholder (~17%) of Straumann Holding; owner, Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois, Basel
profile: Thomas Straumann is the grandson of Reinhard Straumann, who founded Straumann in 1954 as an alloy research firm. His father Fritz built its titanium dental-implant business. Thomas joined the board in 1990 and refocused the company purely on dental, making it the world's largest dental-implant maker. In 1997 he founded bone-fixation implant company Medartis, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: He owns a stable of show-jumping horses and Basel's landmark Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois.
deep_cut_fact: When his family bought the 'Drei Könige' hotel and the adjacent Blumenrain 2 building in 2004, he had it restored under heritage-preservation rules with Basel architect Christian Lang, reconstructing parts from the original plans. Herzog & de Meuron later led a 2023-25 renovation.

public_contacts.value: Grand Hotel Les Trois Rois corporate media page

notes: Low public profile; Basel-based. Best route is Medartis investor relations, since he chairs Medartis. Little link to energy/data-center themes; more of a medtech and hospitality story.

name: Cai Haoyu
current_role: Co-founder, Anuttacon (AI-native games studio); co-founder and major shareholder of miHoYo/HoYoverse (stepped down as chairman 2023)
profile: Cai Haoyu (蔡浩宇) co-founded Shanghai game developer miHoYo in 2012 with Shanghai Jiao Tong University classmates Liu Wei and Luo Yuhao. miHoYo made global hits Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail and Zenless Zone Zero. He handed the chairmanship to Liu in 2023 but kept a large stake, and co-founded Anuttacon, whose 2025 game Whispers from the Star centres on an AI companion called Stella.
interesting_fact: After visiting miHoYo's Shanghai headquarters in 2023, Apple CEO Tim Cook called the team 'phenomenal'.
deep_cut_fact: miHoYo began in January 2011 in dorm D32 at SJTU's Minhang campus. Its first release, FlyMe2theMoon (iOS, Sept 2011), was named after Evangelion's ending song. The 'H' in miHoYo comes from Cai Haoyu's name, and 'mi' was inspired by Hatsune Miku.
notes: Very private and rarely gives interviews. Anuttacon is the best entry point for an AI-and-games angle, but it publishes no press email (site only).

name: Charles Cadogan
current_role: Deceased (died 11 June 2023, aged 86); was 8th Earl Cadogan and head of Cadogan Estates (Chelsea, London)
profile: Charles Cadogan, 8th Earl Cadogan, whose family owns the Cadogan Estate of roughly 90+ acres in Chelsea and Knightsbridge, died at his Chelsea home on 11 June 2023. His son Edward Cadogan succeeded him as 9th Earl and head of the family's property interests.
notes: Deceased - died 11 June 2023 (sources: https://www.cadogan.co.uk/remembering-the-life-of-the-earl-cadogan , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charles_Cadogan,_8th_Earl_Cadogan). Hurun still listed him through 2025. Successor is Edward Cadogan, 9th Earl; Cadogan Estates is run by CEO Hugh Seaborn.

name: Charles De Ganahl And David H. Koch
current_role: Charles Koch: Chairman and co-CEO, Koch, Inc. (Wichita, KS). David Koch: deceased.
profile: Joint 1997-98 Forbes entry for brothers Charles de Ganahl Koch (b. 1935) and David H. Koch, co-owners of Koch Industries (now Koch, Inc.), the privately held energy, chemicals, materials and trading conglomerate with revenues above $125B. David died 23 Aug 2019; Charles has run the company since 1967 and became co-CEO alongside Dave Robertson in 2023.
interesting_fact: Charles Koch became chairman and CEO of the family company in 1967 and grew it into one of the largest private companies in the US.
notes: Combined entry of two people: David H. Koch died 23 Aug 2019 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Koch); Charles Koch is alive. Charles likely has his own record elsewhere in the dataset - dedupe. Kept minimal.

name: Henry T. Nicholas
current_role: Co-founder and former co-chairman/CEO of Broadcom; Chairman, Henry T. Nicholas III Foundation and Marsy's Law for All
profile: Henry T. Nicholas III (b. 1959), a UCLA electrical engineering PhD, co-founded Broadcom with Henry Samueli in 1991, took it public in 1998 and retired in 2003. He now focuses on his foundation (education, incl. Nicholas Academic Centers in Santa Ana) and victims' rights via Marsy's Law, named after his late sister.
interesting_fact: He and Samueli started Broadcom in the spare bedroom of Nicholas's Redondo Beach condo in 1991, each putting in $5,000 of their own money; his doctoral work underpinned the integrated circuits Broadcom sold.
deep_cut_fact: Before UCLA engineering, he attended the US Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs. He met Henry Samueli while working at TRW in Redondo Beach, then ran microelectronics at PairGain Technologies before the two founded Broadcom. His foundation opened the first Nicholas Academic Center (free tutoring/mentoring) in downtown Santa Ana in 2008.
notes: Input record dated (Forbes 2000). Low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Best route possibly via Marsy's Law for All (marsyslaw.us) or his foundation. Avoid his past legal cases (2008 indictment dismissed; 2018-19 Las Vegas drug case) and family tragedy beyond Marsy's Law context.

name: Hazel Czernin
current_role: Deceased (10th Baroness Howard de Walden; died 13 July 2024)
profile: Hazel Czernin, 10th Baroness Howard de Walden, was a principal family owner of the Howard de Walden Estate in Marylebone, London. She died at home on 13 July 2024, aged 88; her son Peter Czernin succeeded as 11th Baron Howard de Walden.
notes: Died 13 July 2024 (source: Howard de Walden Estate announcement https://www.hdwe.co.uk/news/item/2598-baroness-howard-de-walden). Successor: Peter Czernin (film producer), 11th Baron.

name: Bulat Utemuratov
current_role: Key investor behind Verny Capital (Almaty); main shareholder of ForteBank; President, Kazakhstan Tennis Federation; Vice President, International Tennis Federation; founder, Bulat Utemuratov Foundation
profile: Bulat Utemuratov (b. 1957, Guryev/Atyrau) is a Kazakh investor and former diplomat (ambassador to Switzerland, Security Council secretary) who co-founded ATF Bank, sold to UniCredit in 2007 for ~$2.2B, and led the 2012 sale of Kazzinc to Glencore. Via Verny Capital he holds ForteBank and telecom Kar-Tel; in 2025 he sold the Ritz-Carlton Vienna, RG Gold, Burger King Kazakhstan and Sky Mobile.
interesting_fact: As head of Kazakh tennis since 2007 he has personally donated about $250M; the country went from ~60 courts and a thousand registered players to 39 tennis centres and 391 courts, and Kazakhstan's Almaty Open was voted ATP 250 Tournament of the Year in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He didn't pick up a racquet until he was 40. When he took over the Kazakhstan Tennis Federation in 2007 he found a letter asking the ITF to suspend its membership because it couldn't pay its fees - his first act was to pay off the debts.
notes: Tennis is the warm entry point - he gives long interviews around the Almaty Open. His personal site has a news feed and links to his X account; Verny Capital is his investment vehicle (info@ is a general inbox). The Bulat Utemuratov Foundation (est. 2014) covers health, education, disaster relief and urban projects.

name: Peter Spuhler
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Stadler Rail AG; owner of PCS Holding (stepping down from Aebi Schmidt board in 2026 to become honorary chairman)
profile: Swiss industrialist Peter Spuhler bought Stadler, a small Thurgau rail-vehicle maker, in 1989 and built it into a global train manufacturer that he took public in 2019; he still holds about 42% and chairs it. Via PCS Holding he also owns stakes in Rieter, Autoneum and Nasdaq-listed Aebi Schmidt. He sat in the Swiss parliament (SVP) from 1999 to 2012.
interesting_fact: When Spuhler took over Stadler in 1989 it had just 18 employees and about CHF 4.5M in revenue. He financed the purchase with a ~CHF 5M loan from Thurgauer Kantonalbank and bet on the new GTW regional train.
deep_cut_fact: Spuhler was born in Seville, Spain, in 1959, grew up in Zurich, and as a young man started a career as an ice-hockey player with the Grasshopper Club Zürich before studying business at the University of St. Gallen.
notes: Gives interviews to Swiss business media fairly often. Philipp Brunner becomes Stadler CEO on 1 Jan 2027. He plans to settle his succession by his 70th birthday in 2029. Aebi Schmidt change: https://www.bilanz.ch/peter-spuhler-tritt-als-aebi-verwaltungsrat-zurueck-2026/7hx1llb

name: Lynda Resnick
current_role: Co-owner and Vice Chair, The Wonderful Company (Los Angeles)
profile: Former child actress who started an ad agency at 19, Lynda Resnick co-owns The Wonderful Company with husband Stewart - the top tree-nut grower and largest US citrus grower (Wonderful Pistachios, Halos, POM, FIJI Water, Teleflora). She led its brand marketing and now focuses on philanthropy; the couple have pledged over $2B.
interesting_fact: The Resnicks' $750M pledge to Caltech in 2019 for environmental-sustainability research was at the time the largest gift ever for climate/sustainability research and the second-largest to a US university.
deep_cut_fact: The Resnicks funded the Resnick Center for Herbert Bayer Studies on the Aspen Institute campus (opened 2022), the first permanent museum devoted to the Bauhaus artist; earlier, as Teleflora president, she won a Gold Effie for pairing flowers with a keepsake container, now an industry standard.

public_contacts.value: comments@wonderful.com (The Wonderful Company HQ general contact)

notes: Marketing-savvy and media-friendly (author of 'Rubies in the Orchard', 2009). Energy/climate hook: Caltech Resnick Sustainability Institute; also big water-use footprint in California (sensitive). Avoid Pentagon Papers and water-politics controversies. Teleflora Effie detail from Wikipedia citing Forbes.

name: Stewart Resnick
current_role: Chairman and President, The Wonderful Company (Los Angeles), co-owned with wife Lynda Resnick
profile: UCLA-trained lawyer who built a janitorial business, bought Teleflora and the Franklin Mint, then from 1978 amassed California Central Valley farmland. The Wonderful Company (Wonderful Pistachios & Almonds, Halos, POM Wonderful, FIJI Water, Teleflora, JUSTIN wines) makes him America's richest farmer; at 89 he remains chairman and a major philanthropist.
interesting_fact: Energy/climate angle: in 2019 he and Lynda pledged $750 million to Caltech for environmental sustainability research - the largest gift ever for sustainability research and the biggest in Caltech's history - funding the Resnick Sustainability Resource Center, a hub for energy research.
deep_cut_fact: His first business was a janitorial/building-services company he started while still at UCLA law school and sold in 1969 - the seed capital for everything that followed. He bought his first California farmland in 1978 as an inflation hedge.
notes: Approach via The Wonderful Company corporate PR. Lynda Resnick is the more public face of the couple. Recent gifts: $100M to UCLA Health (Feb 2026); UC Davis Resnick Center for Agricultural Innovation opened May 2026. Avoid water-rights/drought controversy and health details.

name: Märta Schörling Andreen
current_role: Vice Chairman, Melker Schörling AB; board member of Hexagon, AAK, Hexpol and Absolent Group
profile: Born 1984, younger daughter of Swedish investor Melker Schörling (d. 2023). She and sister Sofia Schörling Högberg are majority owners and vice chairmen of holding company Melker Schörling AB, which holds big stakes in Hexagon, AAK, ASSA ABLOY, Hexpol and Securitas; she represents it on several of those boards.
interesting_fact: She joined the board of Melker Schörling AB in 2010 at about 26 and has sat on the Hexpol board (audit and remuneration committees) since 2014, where she is listed with roughly 14.8M Class A and 70.8M Class B shares.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the big listed holdings, she also sits on the board of Absolent Group, a Swedish maker of industrial air-filtration systems for oil mist, smoke and dust, one of the smaller industrial bets in the Schörling portfolio.
notes: Very private; acts through board seats rather than media. Melker Schörling AB has been trimming stakes in Hexagon, Hexpol and AAK in 2026 (Realtid). Data-center angle: Hexagon (measurement/reality-capture tech).

name: John Sall
current_role: Founder & Chair, JMP Statistical Discovery; Co-Founder & Executive Vice President, SAS Institute
profile: John Sall co-founded analytics software firm SAS in 1976 with Jim Goodnight, Anthony Barr and Jane Helwig after graduate statistics study at NC State; SAS (Cary, NC) now has $3B+ revenue and 83,000+ customers. He created and still architects JMP, SAS's desktop statistical-discovery software. He and wife Ginger fund conservation, global health and science via the Sall Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: JMP, released in October 1989, originally stood for 'John's Macintosh Project'; he kept writing code for it for more than 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Rockford, Illinois, he has a bachelor's in history from Beloit College and went to grad school for economics (Northern Illinois) because he felt he graduated into a weak job market. He served on The Nature Conservancy's board 2002-2011.
notes: news@sas.com is SAS Corporate Communications' general inquiries address (Head of Communications: Pamela Meek). Technical founder who still codes; good data/analytics angle. Fellow of the ASA (1998) and AAAS (2015).

name: Andre Koo
current_role: Honorary Chairman and board member, Chailease Holding (TWSE: 5871), Taipei
profile: Andre J.L. Koo (辜仲立), a fourth-generation member of Taiwan's Koo family and son of 'Father of the Credit Card in Taiwan' Jeffrey Koo Sr., built Chailease into a 70+-company equipment-leasing group across Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia, leading its reengineering and fintech push. He is now honorary chairman; son Andre Jr. runs NY-based K8 Capital.
interesting_fact: Three generations of his family are NYU Stern alumni - his father (MBA '62), himself (MBA '94) and his son (BS '18); he chaired Stern's Board of Overseers and sponsors the Andre Koo Tech MBA program.
deep_cut_fact: Asked by NYU Stern about vacations, he admitted he couldn't remember his last real one, then pitched Taiwan as Asia's hidden gem: climb mountains in the morning, soak in hot springs in the afternoon, eat through the night markets by evening.
notes: Self-described connoisseur of wine and business jets (Forbes). NYU trustee - NYU network is a warm route. Chailease is active in renewable-energy (solar) leasing/financing in Taiwan, a possible energy hook.

name: Anthony von Mandl
current_role: Founder and chairman/proprietor, Mark Anthony Group (White Claw, Mike's Hard Lemonade) and Mission Hill Family Estate winery, Vancouver/Okanagan
profile: Vancouver entrepreneur Anthony von Mandl began importing wine at 22 in the 1970s, selling it from his car trunk, then created Mike's Hard Lemonade and White Claw Hard Seltzer through Mark Anthony Brands; the U.S. business made ~$3.6B revenue in 2025. He owns six Canadian wineries led by Mission Hill in B.C.'s Okanagan, plus Ireland's Glendalough Distillery, and is an Officer of the Order of Canada (2016).
interesting_fact: He bought a rundown Okanagan winery in 1981 and renamed it Mission Hill; with architect Tom Kundig (Olson Kundig's first winery project) he rebuilt it for about C$35M by 2002 around a 12-storey bell tower.
deep_cut_fact: Mission Hill's tower holds four bronze bells, each dedicated to a member of the von Mandl family, hand-cast by France's Paccard foundry, and is topped by a pelican weathervane from the family crest; the flagship wine Oculus is named after the single round window lighting the underground barrel cellar.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. No published press email found (markanthony.com blocked automated access); best route is likely via Mark Anthony Group corporate communications or Mission Hill.

name: Montri Jiaravanont
current_role: Honorary Chairman, Charoen Pokphand (C.P.) Group, Bangkok
profile: Montri Jiaravanont is an older brother of C.P. Group senior chairman Dhanin Chearavanont and one of the founding family's elder generation; C.P.'s current leadership page lists him as Honorary Chairman, alongside brothers Jaran (Honorary Chairman) and Sumet (Advisory Chairman). He was earlier executive director of listed C.P. Pokphand Co. Forbes lists him separately for a reported 12.63% stake in family assets (around $5.1B in 2022).
interesting_fact: C.P. Group spans seeds and agribusiness, food (CP Foods), retail (CP ALL, the 7-Eleven operator) and telecoms (True Corporation); Montri is one of four brothers who still hold titled roles at the top of the group.
notes: Forbes gives his age as 95; very private, with no personal channels. Alive status is inferred from C.P.'s current leadership page (Nov 2026), which still lists him; no death report found, but verify before outreach. Forbes profile last updated Apr 2022. Approach via C.P. Group PR.

name: Ratmir Timashev
current_role: Co-founder and backer, OH.io (Columbus, Ohio go-to-market venture fund); co-founder and former CEO of Veeam Software
profile: Ratmir Timashev (b. 1966, Ufa) studied at MIPT and Ohio State, then with Andrei Baronov founded Aelita Software (sold to Quest for $115M, 2004) and backup/data-management firm Veeam (2006; sold to Insight Partners for $5B in 2020). In 2026 he launched OH.io, aiming to invest $100M to bring 100 B2B SaaS/AI startups to Columbus, Ohio.
interesting_fact: He is Ohio State's major tech benefactor - about $150M, including a $110M gift in 2020 to create the Center for Software Innovation - and renounced his Russian citizenship in 2024 in opposition to the invasion of Ukraine.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, started in 1995 while still an OSU grad student with roommate Andrei Baronov, was an online store selling computer parts; the Windows NT admin tools they wrote on the side soon outsold the parts, which led to Aelita. As a Moscow PhD student he also fixed roofs and cleaned windows for extra money.
notes: Veeam (data backup/protection) and his Columbus startup-hub push make him a good fit for data-center/entrepreneurship themes. OH.io co-founder/CEO Jeff Schumann is the operational contact. No published press email found.

name: Kailashchandra Nuwal
current_role: Major shareholder and former Vice Chairman (to 2019), Solar Industries India Ltd (NSE: SOLARINDS), Nagpur
profile: Kailashchandra Nuwal's wealth comes from his stake in Solar Industries, the Nagpur explosives maker founded by his brother Satyanarayan Nuwal. Solar is India's leading industrial-explosives producer and a fast-growing defence supplier. He was vice chairman and a director until 2019 and is no longer in management.
interesting_fact: Solar Industries now earns the biggest share of its revenue from exports, followed by defence. Other customers include housing and infrastructure builders, non-coal miners and state-owned Coal India; the defence business has driven much of its recent value.

public_contacts.value: investor.relations@solargroup.com (company IR; he is not in management)

notes: Very low profile, with no public channels of his own. He is out of management and in a long-running shareholder/board dispute with the founding family, so the company IR route is unlikely to reach him and the dispute is a topic to avoid. We found no sourced positive deep-cut fact. Probably a low-priority target.

name: Torbjorn Tornqvist
current_role: Former co-founder and CEO of Gunvor Group (oil trader, since renamed Centalion); stepped down Dec 2025 in a management buyout; head of Artemis Racing sailing team
profile: Stockholm-born (1953), Geneva-based oil trader who co-founded Gunvor in 1997 and grew it into one of the world's largest independent energy traders. He bought out co-founder Gennady Timchenko's stake in 2014. In Dec 2025 he resigned as CEO and agreed to sell his ~86% stake to ~60 senior employees, partly vendor-financed; the firm has since rebranded as Centalion.
interesting_fact: He founded the Artemis Racing sailing team in 2006, which reached the Louis Vuitton Cup final in the 2013 America's Cup challenger series and helped bring Sweden back into the America's Cup.
deep_cut_fact: He came to competitive sailing late: he started crewing with Russell Coutts at the Swan Worlds, Coutts 'talked me into a TP52', and they won the MedCup and the championship in the same season, after only about three years of sailing. He still helms his own RC44 on the 44Cup circuit.
notes: No personal or office contacts published. He has left Gunvor/Centalion, so company press office is no longer a route to him. Artemis Racing (sailing) is the only active public affiliation. Avoid Russia/Timchenko/US Treasury topics; they are the context of his exit.

name: Ivan Tavrin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Kismet Capital Group (Moscow); co-owner of Avito
profile: Moscow-born (1976) MGIMO graduate who built regional TV/radio businesses (Regional Media Group, Media-1, later partly sold to Disney), ran MegaFon as CEO 2012-16, then founded Kismet Capital in 2016. Since 2022 he has bought Russian assets of exiting Western firms, notably classifieds giant Avito from Naspers for ~$2.4bn (selling 50% to Rosselkhozbank in 2025), plus Henkel's and Fleetcor's Russian businesses.
interesting_fact: While still a university student he started an advertising agency selling TV ads, then invested in regional TV and radio stations that were later acquired by The Walt Disney Company; he remained a shareholder in Disney Channel Russia until 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Through Kismet he took SPACs public on Nasdaq that raised more than $400M, and the first merged in August 2021 with Nexters, the developer of the mobile game 'Hero Wars'.
notes: IMPORTANT: Tavrin and Kismet Capital Group are under UK and US sanctions (per Wikipedia citing UK/US government lists) - check legal/compliance before any contact or podcast arrangement. No published contact pursued for that reason. Received Russia's Order of Friendship.

name: Gwendolyn Sontheim Meyer
current_role: Cargill heiress and show-jumping equestrian (Rancho Santa Fe, California); no operating role at Cargill
profile: A descendant of Cargill founder W.W. Cargill, through the MacMillan branch (her late mother was Marion MacMillan Pictet), who inherited an estimated 8% stake in Cargill. The family still owns about 90% of the company, which had $154B in 2025 sales. She spends most of her time on her Rancho Santa Fe farm training show-jumping horses and also sponsors dressage.
interesting_fact: She owns part of one of the world's largest private companies, a food, agriculture, financial and industrial group founded in Conover, Iowa, in 1865 by W.W. Cargill, the son of a Scottish sea captain.
deep_cut_fact: A competitive show jumper, she won the Prix Credit Suisse at the Geneva International Horse Show (CHI Geneva) in 2011.
notes: Very private; no public statements, accounts or office contact found. Forbes and Wikipedia disagree on whether W.W. Cargill is her great-grandfather or great-great-grandfather, so avoid stating the generation. Equestrian circles are the only visible public footprint. Not an obvious fit for an energy/data-center show.

name: Heinrich Otto Deichmann
current_role: Chairman of the board (Vorsitzender der Unternehmensleitung), Deichmann SE, Essen
profile: Grandson of founder Heinrich Deichmann, who opened a cobbler's shop in Essen in 1913, Heinrich Otto Deichmann (b. 1962) joined in 1989 and has led Deichmann since 1999, building it into Europe's largest shoe retailer (~4,700 stores in 34 countries, ~$9B sales). He owns about 80%; his son Samuel joined the management board in 2020.
interesting_fact: Deichmann pairs its retail empire with long-running faith-based philanthropy: the family's aid organisation wortundtat, founded in 1977 by his father after meeting leprosy patients in India, runs development projects in the world's poorest regions and is funded largely by the Deichmann foundation he now chairs.
deep_cut_fact: Alongside economics, he studied history, philosophy and theology before joining the family business in 1989; he openly speaks about his Christian faith shaping how he runs the company.
notes: Gives occasional interviews (e.g. Abendzeitung 'on God and shoes'); son Heinrich Samuel Deichmann is the more public next-gen voice (OMR podcast). Route via Deichmann corporate press office.

name: Euisun Chung
current_role: Executive Chair, Hyundai Motor Group
profile: Grandson of Hyundai founder Chung Ju-yung, he succeeded his father Mong-Koo Chung as chairman of Hyundai Motor Group in 2020. As Kia president (2005-09) he grew it faster than Hyundai Motor and pushed design-led management; he has since driven the group into EVs, hydrogen, robotics (Boston Dynamics) and U.S. manufacturing. Hyundai Motor India's 2024 IPO was India's largest ever.
interesting_fact: Before joining the family business he worked at the New York office of Japanese trading house Itochu, then joined auto-parts affiliate Hyundai Mobis in 1994.
deep_cut_fact: He has led the Korea Archery Association since 2005 (re-elected in Dec 2024 to a sixth term, through 2029) and is in his fifth term as president of World Archery Asia; he was at Les Invalides when Korea's women won their 10th straight Olympic team gold in Paris.
notes: Reachable only via Hyundai Motor Group corporate communications/newsroom (hyundai.com/worldwide/en/newsroom); no verified IR/press email captured. Hydrogen (HTWO), robotics and Georgia Metaplant are natural energy/tech hooks; archery is a warm personal topic.

name: Dan Snyder
current_role: Private investor (RedZone Capital); former owner of the NFL's Washington Commanders (sold 2023)
profile: College dropout (b. 1964) who co-founded marketing firm Snyder Communications with his sister in 1988, took it public in 1996 and sold it to Havas for $2.1B in stock in 2000. He bought Washington's NFL team for $750M in 1999 and sold it for a record $6.05B in 2023; via RedZone Capital he has held stakes in Six Flags, Johnny Rockets and Dick Clark Productions.
interesting_fact: In 1996, at 32, he became the youngest CEO of a NYSE-listed company; by 20 he had made $1M chartering jets to fly college students to spring break.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was at a B. Dalton bookstore in White Flint Mall; at 12 he had moved with his family to Henley-on-Thames near London for two years. He was later an executive producer on the 2008 Tom Cruise film 'Valkyrie'.
notes: No published personal or office contact found. Highly controversial tenure as NFL owner (workplace investigations) - avoid. Keeps a low profile since the 2023 sale.

name: Cho Tak Wong
current_role: Founder and former chairman (stepped down Oct 2025), Fuyao Glass Industry Group; founder of Heren Charitable Foundation and Fuyao University of Science and Technology
profile: Cho Tak Wong (Cao Dewang, b. 1946) founded Fuyao Glass in 1987 and built it into one of the world's largest auto-glass makers, with plants in China and the US (incl. the Ohio factory in 'American Factory'). Handed the chairmanship to his son in Oct 2025; now focused on philanthropy, notably Fuyao University of Science and Technology.
interesting_fact: His Heren Charitable Foundation pledged $1.6 billion in 2021 to build the Fuyao University of Science and Technology, which admitted its first 50 undergraduates in fall 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before Fuyao he started his own business at 16 peddling cut tobacco and also worked as a farmer, chef and fruit seller; in 2009 he won EY's World Entrepreneur of the Year, and Fuyao (1993) was the first company in its sector listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange.

name: Pyotr Aven
current_role: Co-founder/shareholder of LetterOne (L1) and Alfa Group; former chairman of Alfa-Bank (2011-2022); art collector based in Surrey, UK
profile: Moscow-born economist Pyotr (Petr) Aven was Russia's minister of foreign economic relations in 1992 before joining Alfa-Bank, which he ran as president (1994-2011) and chairman until 2022. With Mikhail Fridman and partners he co-owns Alfa Group and LetterOne. Sanctioned by the EU/UK in 2022, he stepped off LetterOne's board and now focuses on his art collection and writing.
interesting_fact: He owns what is described as the largest/best private collection of Russian art (Goncharova, Petrov-Vodkin, Chagall, Kandinsky), lent to Tate, the Royal Academy, MoMA and Fondation Louis Vuitton; in 2022 he bought a building in Riga for a planned private museum.
deep_cut_fact: His collecting began in childhood with stamps and toy cars; the first painting he bought was a 1920s still life by Pavel Kuznetsov. As a young economist he was seconded to IIASA in Laxenburg, Austria, and he has lectured at Moscow's Higher School of Economics since 2007.
notes: Under EU/UK/US sanctions since 2022 - check legal/editorial implications before any engagement. petraven.info describes itself as his website (email appears in its schema.org metadata); appears to be a reputation-style site, so treat accounts linked there with some caution. Books: 'The Age of Berezovsky', 'Gaidar's Revolution' (free at petr-aven-books.com).

name: Liu Debing
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director & Chairman, Knowledge Atlas Technology / Zhipu AI (Z.ai), HKEX: 2513
profile: Co-founder and chairman of Zhipu AI, the Beijing developer of the GLM large language models, spun out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab (AMiner) in 2019. He handles fundraising and business decisions. Zhipu listed in Hong Kong in January 2026, billed as the world's first listed LLM company, raising about $560M, and in 2026 changed its English short name to Z.AI.
interesting_fact: Speaking to Bloomberg TV on the day Zhipu listed, Liu said the AI price war would go global: if Zhipu can keep its prices at about one-seventh of its rivals', international customers will have to accept it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zhipu, Liu earned a computer science PhD at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, then worked at Technicolor's China research institute before joining Tsinghua as a senior engineer. He was one of Zhipu's six founders.

name: Cai Huabo
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Shenzhen Longsys Electronics (江波龙, SZSE: 301308)
profile: Cai Huabo (蔡华波, b. 1976, Jiujiang, Jiangxi) went to Shenzhen after high school. In 1999 he and his twin sister Cai Lijiang turned a tiny Huaqiangbei electronics-market stall into Longsys, now a major memory/storage maker (FORESEE, Lexar, Zilia). It bought the Lexar brand from Micron in 2017 and listed in Shenzhen in 2022. Riding the AI-driven memory boom, its 2025 revenue reached RMB 22.8B, including SSDs for AI servers and data centers. It is pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Longsys's growth was a 'snake swallows elephant' story: a company that began as a Huaqiangbei trading counter acquired the global premium flash brand Lexar from Micron in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Cai never went to university. His first job was selling resistors and capacitors at Huaqiangbei counters. The name 江波龙 combines 江 for their home province Jiangxi, 波 from Cai Huabo, and 龙 for the Year of the Dragon that he and his twin sister share.
notes: Forbes' bio text mistakenly names his twin sister Cai Lijiang (a minority co-shareholder) as chairman; the chairman is Cai Huabo. The AI-memory/data-center SSD angle is highly relevant. Route via the IR mailbox / board secretary; Chinese-language outreach is advisable.

name: Shen Bin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Shagang Group (Sha Steel), Zhangjiagang; actual controller of Jiangsu Shagang Co. (SZSE: 002075)
profile: Born 1979, the son of Shagang founder Shen Wenrong, he rose through Shagang Group as first deputy general manager and finance roles before becoming chairman; after his father died in June 2024 he inherited ~29% of the group and became controller of China's largest private steelmaker.
interesting_fact: Shagang is an unexpected data-centre player: it bought control of London-based Global Switch (carrier-neutral data centres in Europe and Asia-Pacific) from the Reuben Brothers in 2016–2019 and has repeatedly explored selling it.

current_role: Co-founder and President, Xiaohongshu (RedNote), Shanghai

It grew from an overseas-shopping guide into one of China's biggest lifestyle and search platforms, briefly drawing millions of US 'TikTok refugees' in January 2025.

He retired in June 2015; his wealth comes mainly from his MediaTek stake. No public role since retirement was found.
