deep_cut_fact: An engineer from National Chiao Tung University (communication engineering), he came out of NCTU's famed 'Lab 307' under Prof. Wu Chung-yu, one of the first master's cohorts in a lab that produced many of Taiwan's IC-design leaders.
notes: Very private, retired since 2015; no published personal/office contact found. Deep-cut fact taken from search-indexed text of GVM/NYCU pages (gvm.com.tw not fetchable here) - double-check before use. Alive status not confirmed but no death report found; still on 2026 Forbes real-time list.

name: Lutz Mario Helmig
current_role: Founder and majority owner, ATON GmbH (family investment holding: engineering incl. EDAG, mining, medical, aviation)
profile: Lutz Helmig (b. 1946) is a vascular surgeon turned entrepreneur. He co-founded the Asklepios hospital group in 1987, then built Helios Kliniken, which his family sold to Fresenius in 2005 for €1.5B. Through ATON (founded 2001) and Horus Finanzholding he invests in engineering (EDAG), mining, medical and aviation businesses.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he paid off the entire €2.1M debt of Grebenhain, the Hessian village he has lived in since 1977, on condition it balance its budget for the following three years.
deep_cut_fact: After the 2006 sale of airline dba (he had bought 25.1%) to Air Berlin, he gave every dba employee 195 Air Berlin shares worth over €3,000 as a farewell gift. He also co-founded Asklepios with lawyer Bernard große Broermann in 1987 before splitting off to build Helios.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed; wrote a 2013 book on health economics, 'Gesundheit und Freiheit'. ATON's general inbox is the published route. Aged ~80.

name: Li Hua
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Futu Holdings (Futubull / moomoo), Hong Kong/Shenzhen
profile: Leaf Hua Li (b. 1977, Hunan University CS 2000) was Tencent's 18th employee, an early QQ developer and a founder of Tencent Video. He founded Futu in 2012, funding it partly by selling Tencent shares; its Futubull and moomoo trading apps are Nasdaq-listed (FUTU). Barred from signing new mainland users since 2022, Futu is expanding in the US, Singapore, Malaysia, Japan and beyond.
interesting_fact: He is named on 20+ Chinese and international patent applications from his Tencent years, where he also headed the multimedia business and innovation center.
deep_cut_fact: Futu's origin story is a mooncake: his broker once brought him one as thanks for roughly HK$5M in commissions he had paid that year — the first gift since he became a client in 2004 — and the lopsided deal convinced him to build a low-cost broker.
notes: Goes by 'Leaf'. Company PR/IR inboxes are published. Avoid the 2022 mainland regulatory crackdown as a topic. Moderate data-center relevance (heavy trading-infrastructure user).

name: Murat Ulker
current_role: Board member, Yıldız Holding; Chairman of pladis and GODIVA Chocolatier (handed the Yıldız chair to Ali Ülker in Jan 2020)
profile: Murat Ülker, second-generation head of Turkey's Ülker family, joined Yıldız Holding in 1984, became CEO in 2000 and chairman in 2008. He turned the biscuit maker into a global snacks group: Godiva ($850M, 2007) and United Biscuits ($3.2B, 2014), merged into London-based pladis. He owns about 63% of Yıldız and still chairs pladis and Godiva.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he gave $24M to Harvard; a research facility focused on genetic diseases is named after his father, Sabri Ülker.
deep_cut_fact: He writes a weekly personal blog (in Turkish) on business, history and AI. Recent posts cover the AI agenda session he joined at the Fast Company CEO Summit (Oct 2026) and whether Jack Sparrow was really modelled on Ottoman corsair Yusuf Reis. He also travels to watch Turkey's national basketball team.

public_contacts.value: https://muratulker.com/iletisim/ (messages are read by his corporate communications unit)

notes: One of the more reachable people in this lane: he runs his own blog with a contact form, plus linked LinkedIn and Instagram. An interest in AI (Fast Company CEO Summit AI session) gives a podcast hook. The Yıldız Holding website blocked automated access, so I could not verify its corporate press email.

name: David MacNeil
current_role: Founder, owner and CEO, WeatherTech (MacNeil Automotive Products), Bolingbrook, Illinois
profile: David MacNeil founded WeatherTech in 1989 and still owns 100% of it. The US-made auto-accessories and home-goods brand had about $800M in 2025 revenue. Trump nominated him to the FTC in Jan 2026; he was never confirmed, and a Nov 2026 MLex report says he withdrew. His vintage car collection is worth over $400M.
interesting_fact: His car collection includes a 1963 Ferrari 250 GTO, bought in 2018 for an estimated $75M and among the most expensive cars in the world. He is also a certified airline transport pilot who has flown to 39 countries.
deep_cut_fact: He started WeatherTech in 1989 by taking a second mortgage on his home and working out of his house, frustrated that 1980s floor mats were 'just these thin cheap rubber floor mats' that 'didn't do what a floor mat is supposed to do.'
notes: Known for Made-in-USA advocacy and Super Bowl ads; a GOP donor. FTC status: nominated Jan 2026; MLex (4 Nov 2026) reports the nomination withdrawn in favor of Chris Mufarrige (single source; avoid as a topic). No published press email found, and WeatherTech's site blocks automated fetches.

name: N. Murray Edwards
current_role: Executive Chairman, Canadian Natural Resources Ltd.; owner, Edco Financial Holdings; chairman/co-owner, Calgary Sports & Entertainment Corp. (Calgary Flames)
profile: Regina-born lawyer-turned-financier who built his fortune backing and running Canadian energy companies, above all oil-sands giant Canadian Natural Resources (executive chairman), plus Ensign Energy, Magellan Aerospace and Imperial Metals. He also leads the Calgary Flames ownership group and owns Resorts of the Canadian Rockies. He moved his residency from Calgary to London in 2016.
interesting_fact: In high school Edwards worked four nights a week as a hockey referee; he also worked on a garbage crew and had a summer job at a beer factory with unlimited beer on breaks.
deep_cut_fact: A keen investor as a student, Edwards rang the bell on Oct 3, 2002 to launch the 'N. Murray Edwards MarketWatch' stock-ticker board he donated to his alma mater's business school in Saskatoon, years before it was renamed the Edwards School of Business (2007).

public_contacts.value: https://www.cnrl.com/contact (Canadian Natural contact page incl. Investor Relations link)

notes: Very low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is likely via Canadian Natural's investor relations or the Edwards School of Business (USask), where he sits on the Dean's Advisory Council. Lives primarily in London (UK) since 2016.

name: Jiang Rensheng
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder, Chongqing Zhifei Biological Products (Shenzhen-listed); controls Chongqing Genrix Biopharmaceutical (Shanghai-listed)
profile: Jiang Rensheng (蒋仁生, b. 1953, Guangxi), China's 'vaccine king', spent ~20 years in public epidemic prevention. He quit at about 46 to sell vaccines, and in 2002 bought a struggling Chongqing maker and renamed it Zhifei. Zhifei distributes Merck's HPV vaccine in China and partners with GSK; Jiang took Genrix public in 2023.
interesting_fact: Jiang is a classic late-blooming founder: he left a secure government job at about 46 to become a vaccine salesman in Chengdu, then started Zhifei in Chongqing at 49.
deep_cut_fact: At 17, with university exams suspended, he taught at his village school in Guangxi. He got into Guilin Medical College when the gaokao resumed in 1977. In Zhifei's cash-strapped early days he sold his own home and moved into the staff dormitory.
notes: Low international media profile; Chinese-language outreach recommended. His son Jiang Lingfeng is a Zhifei director and heir apparent. Zhifei's general office email is the only published channel; BD@zifibio.com is for business partnerships.

name: Todd Christopher
current_role: Founder of Vogue International (OGX, Maui Moisture); now a private investor based in Clearwater, Florida
profile: Todd Christopher, a high-school dropout and fourth-generation hairdresser, founded hair care company Vogue International in 1987, eventually building brands such as OGX and Maui Moisture. He sold a stake to Carlyle in 2014, and Johnson & Johnson bought the company for $3.3bn in 2016. He lives in Clearwater, Florida, and keeps a low public profile.
interesting_fact: Short on cash when he opened his first salon in his twenties, he slept in the salon to save money; he is one of very few high-school dropouts to make the Forbes 400.
deep_cut_fact: He got his start in hair care products in 1987 selling Pro-Vitamin hair-treatment capsules out of the trunk of his car, and has trademarked phrases such as 'Vitamin & Herbal Indulgence', 'Beach Bum Gear', 'Ego Trip' and 'Shampurity'.
notes: No current company role, official website or published contact channel found; Vogue International is now part of J&J's consumer spin-off Kenvue, which does not represent him. Common name - beware other Todd Christophers (e.g. a USC MBA/brewery co-founder is a different person). Very private.

name: B. Partha Saradhi Reddy
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Hetero Group (Hyderabad); Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha
profile: A synthetic organic chemist (PhD, Osmania University), Bandi Partha Saradhi Reddy founded Hetero in 1993 and built it into one of the world's largest generic makers of anti-retroviral drugs, with 200+ products across oncology, immunology and diabetes, sold in branded and unbranded form worldwide. He also serves in India's upper house of Parliament.
interesting_fact: Hetero's leadership page credits him with developing one of the first affordable APIs for anti-retroviral (HIV/AIDS) drugs, helping bring down treatment costs in developing countries.
deep_cut_fact: He began in 1979 as a research trainee under Dr. K. Anji Reddy at Uniloids, briefly worked at Standard Organics, and in 1984 joined Dr. Reddy's Laboratories to head research - one of DRL's very first employees - before leaving to found Hetero.
notes: Media inquiries via Hetero Corporate Communications. Also a sitting Rajya Sabha MP (politically exposed); avoid tax-raid and political topics. Low fit with energy/data-center theme.

name: Shen Guojun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, China Yintai Holdings (Yintai Group), Beijing
profile: Shen Guojun (沈国军), from a fishing family near Ningbo, left China Construction Bank to found China Yintai Investment in 1997; after the 1998 Asian crisis he turned an unsold building into Intime department stores (HK-listed 2007). Yintai spans retail, property, mining and investment. A Jack Ma ally, he helped found and chaired Cainiao Network.
interesting_fact: He was a founding leader of Alibaba's logistics arm Cainiao Network in 2013 (CEO at founding, then executive chairman), alongside friend Jack Ma.
deep_cut_fact: Yintai's lantern-shaped Beijing Yintai Centre tower (completed 2008) is such a landmark that Singaporean singer Stefanie Sun sang a song titled 'Yintai'. Shen earned a master's from Zhongnan University of Finance and Economics in 1986 and once said that even with nothing, 'my street-stall business would do better than others'.
notes: Cainiao fact source is a secondary blog; Cornell eCommons hosts a Shen Guojun interview (https://ecommons.cornell.edu/bitstream/handle/1813/41516/Shen_Guojun_interview_EN.pdf) that could not be downloaded. No published press contact found. Avoid references to wealth decline, asset sales and his parents' early deaths.

name: Lai Meisong
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, ZTO Express (NYSE: ZTO; HKEX: 2057)
profile: Lai Meisong, from Tonglu county in Zhejiang, worked in the timber trade before founding ZTO Express in 2002; it is now China's largest express delivery company by parcel volume. ZTO listed on the NYSE in 2016 and added a Hong Kong listing in 2020; Alibaba/Cainiao hold a minority stake. He is deputy chairman of the China Express Delivery Association.
interesting_fact: He was urged into the courier business by his classmate Chen Dejun, then head of rival STO Express, many of whose franchise operators were Lai's classmates and fellow Tonglu natives.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Tianjingling, Gewu township, which he called Tonglu's most remote mountain village; at 17 he worked in a factory and bought a loom (RMB 6,800) for contract weaving. Losing money on that work taught him to 'control his own destiny', which is why he founded ZTO himself rather than run a franchise point.
notes: Interviews mostly in Chinese media; route via ZTO IR.

name: Daniel D'Aniello
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman Emeritus, The Carlyle Group; chairman, Wolf Trap Foundation for the Performing Arts
profile: Daniel D'Aniello (b. 1946, Butler, Pennsylvania) co-founded private equity giant Carlyle in 1987 with William Conway Jr. and David Rubenstein after finance roles at TWA, PepsiCo and Marriott. He chaired Carlyle until 2018 and is now chairman emeritus; Carlyle manages ~$450B+. A Vietnam-era Navy veteran, he gave $20M to Syracuse's National Veterans Resource Center (2018).
interesting_fact: The only child of a single mother who worked four jobs for 25 years, he worked as a produce-market stock boy from age 9 through high school, went to Syracuse on scholarship (transportation economics) and was on its gymnastics team.
deep_cut_fact: After Syracuse he served as a Navy supply officer aboard the aircraft carrier USS Wasp (CVS-18) until 1971, and before Carlyle he was Marriott Corporation's VP of finance and development, valuing its mergers, acquisitions and divestitures.
notes: Lower-profile than co-founder David Rubenstein; strong veterans' causes angle (Syracuse D'Aniello Institute for Veterans and Military Families, NVRC). Media contact Brittany Bensaull appears on Carlyle's 2026 earnings releases (SEC 8-K exhibits).

name: Ben Chestnut
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Mailchimp (stepped back to an Intuit advisor role in 2022); now largely private
profile: Atlanta-raised Ben Chestnut started Mailchimp with Dan Kurzius in 2001 as a side project of their web-design agency and went full-time in 2007. They bootstrapped it with no outside capital to ~$800M in revenue before selling to Intuit in 2021 for $12B, each owning 50%. He moved to an advisor role in 2022 and has kept a low profile since.
interesting_fact: Mailchimp is one of the largest bootstrapped exits ever: the founders refused venture money for 20 years, then sold for $12B in cash and stock. Chestnut learned about small business from his mother, who ran a hair salon from the family kitchen in Georgia.
deep_cut_fact: Chestnut studied physics at the University of Georgia before switching to industrial design at Georgia Tech. After the sale he told Kleiner Perkins' Grit podcast it took nearly a year to stop checking email every morning; his advice to other exited founders is simply 'Just get a dog'.
notes: No published personal or office contact found; he rarely appears publicly beyond occasional founder podcasts (e.g. Grit, 2025). Avoid his 2022 departure circumstances as a topic. Physics/design detail: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Chestnut

name: Alexandre Behring
current_role: Co-Founder and Co-Managing Partner, 3G Capital (New York); director, Restaurant Brands International
profile: Rio-born engineer and HBS Baker Scholar (b. 1967) who trained under Jorge Paulo Lemann at GP Investments and ran railroad ALL as CEO before co-founding 3G Capital in 2004. He led the Burger King/Tim Hortons, Heinz and Kraft Heinz deals, and recently Hunter Douglas and the $9.4B Skechers buyout. Lives in Greenwich, CT.
interesting_fact: His family's Behring Foundation gave R$35M to PUC-Rio in Dec 2024 to create an Artificial Intelligence Institute - the largest private donation in the university's history - and funds Brazilian students' scholarships to MIT, Harvard and Carnegie Mellon.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he was a tech founder: in 1989, fresh from PUC-Rio engineering, he co-founded Modus OSI Technologies, a software company operating in Florida and São Paulo, and stayed a partner until 1993 before HBS and GP Investments.
notes: Goes by 'Alex Behring'. Low-key; rarely gives interviews. AI/engineering angle (PUC-Rio AI Institute, Behring Foundation computer-science focus) is the best hook for a tech podcast.

name: Stephan Schnabel
current_role: CEO (Chairman of the Executive Board), HELM AG, Hamburg
profile: Third-generation head of HELM AG, the Hamburg family-owned chemicals marketing and distribution group founded in 1900 (revenue ~US$6B, offices in 30+ countries, 100% family-owned). He joined in the 1990s as a salesman, ran the Turkish subsidiary and later the Crop Protection unit, and succeeded his father Dieter as CEO in 2020.
interesting_fact: HELM began in 1900 as a Hamburg import-export house 'for merchandise of every description'; his grandfather Hermann steered it into chemicals from 1950, and the family still holds 100% of the shares, having never felt the need to change that despite approaches from banks.
deep_cut_fact: He cut his teeth abroad: he was managing director of HELM's Turkish company until 2009, then at 36 took over the 'Chemical Solids' division - in a 2011 interview his father said that job was a test he first had to 'survive' before he could be considered as successor.
notes: Low public profile; gives occasional trade-press statements (CHEManager, CEO Magazine on sustainability/emissions). Reportedly also vice president of the Hamburg Chamber of Commerce (Handelskammer) since 2024 (theorg.com, unverified).

name: Pierre M. Omidyar
current_role: Founder of eBay (chairman 1998-2015); founder of The Omidyar Group / Omidyar Network (philanthropic investment) and publisher of Honolulu Civil Beat
profile: Paris-born (1967) Iranian-American engineer who wrote AuctionWeb over Labor Day weekend 1995 while at General Magic; it became eBay, public in 1998. With wife Pam he founded Omidyar Network in 2004 and now runs a family of philanthropic and impact-investing groups under The Omidyar Group, focused on responsible tech, democracy and journalism.
interesting_fact: The first item sold on AuctionWeb was a broken laser pointer; Omidyar was so surprised he contacted the buyer, who explained he collected broken laser pointers. His original eBay.com site also had a page about the Ebola virus.
deep_cut_fact: Fresh out of Tufts (CS, 1988) he worked at Apple subsidiary Claris on the team that upgraded MacDraw to MacDraw II, then in 1991 co-founded pen-computing startup Ink Development, which became eShop and was bought by Microsoft in 1996.
notes: Lives in Hawaii; posts on social media about tech ethics and democracy. The Omidyar Group says it does not accept business plans or personal requests, so frame outreach as a media/interview request.

name: Giovanni Agnelli
profile: Giovanni 'Gianni' Agnelli (12 March 1921 - 24 January 2003), 'L'Avvocato', was the principal shareholder and longtime head of Fiat; he died in Turin in 2003. Control of the family holdings passed to his grandson John Elkann.
notes: Deceased (died 24 January 2003; source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gianni_Agnelli). Forbes 1996-2000 listing with no company field matches Gianni Agnelli of Fiat. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Yoovidhya Family
current_role: Family owners of TCP Group (Krating Daeng) and ~51% of Red Bull GmbH; Saravoot Yoovidhya is TCP Group CEO
profile: The Thai Yoovidhya family descends from Chaleo Yoovidhya (d. 2012), a pharma salesman who founded T.C. Pharmaceutical in 1956, created the Krating Daeng energy drink and co-founded Red Bull with Dietrich Mateschitz in 1984. The family holds a majority of Red Bull GmbH; son Saravoot runs TCP Group, a Thai beverage multinational (Red Bull, Sponsor, Warrior).
interesting_fact: Chaleo personally formulated the original Krating Daeng drink and registered the trademark about 50 years ago; TCP opened the TCP Legacy Museum in 2024 to tell the story of how Kratingdaeng became Red Bull.
deep_cut_fact: TCP's first office (March 27, 1956) was a rented building in Rambuttri alley off Bangkok's Khaosan Road - long before it became a backpacker hub - where Chaleo sold medicines under the TC-MYCIN brand.
notes: This is a family entry, not one person. Most accessible member is CEO Saravoot Yoovidhya (TCP Group); sister Nucharee is a senior executive. TCP's sustainability report highlights rooftop solar investments - possible energy hook. Avoid unrelated family legal matters.

name: Saddam Hussein
profile: Deceased: Saddam Hussein, former President of Iraq (1979-2003), listed by Forbes in 1997-98 with an estimated $5B fortune. He was executed in Baghdad on 30 December 2006.
notes: Died 30 Dec 2006 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddam_Hussein). Head-of-state entry from old Forbes lists; not a candidate for outreach.

name: Samuel Zell
current_role: Deceased (died May 18, 2023); was founder & chairman of Equity Group Investments and Equity Residential
notes: Real-estate billionaire Sam Zell died May 18, 2023, per Equity Residential's 8-K that day naming him its Founder and Chairman of the Board of Trustees: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/906107/000119312523148424/d505438d8k.htm. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Mohamed Salim Bin Mahfouz
profile: Most likely Mohammed bin Salem bin Mahfouz, eldest son of Salem Ahmed bin Mahfouz, founder of Saudi Arabia's National Commercial Bank (NCB, now Saudi National Bank); he was NCB's CEO from 1992 and long chaired its executive committee. An Arab News tribute to the founder (c. 2013) states that Mohammed and his brother Khalid had both died.
notes: Only appears on Forbes 1996 list with no source of wealth. Death per Arab News tribute (https://www.arabnews.com/news/464418): 'Mohammed the eldest and Khaled... both of them died in the last few years'. The family stake in NCB was sold to the Saudi state by 2002. Not a viable outreach target.

name: Hansjorg Wyss
current_role: Chairman, Wyss Foundation; founder and former chairman/CEO of Synthes; co-owner of Chelsea FC
profile: Bern-born Hansjörg Wyss (b. 1935), an ETH Zurich civil engineer and Harvard MBA, founded Synthes USA in 1977 to sell AO bone-fixation plates and screws. He grew it into the global Synthes, which he sold to Johnson & Johnson in 2012 for $19.7B. A Giving Pledge signatory, he now concentrates on philanthropy, especially land conservation through the Wyss Foundation.
interesting_fact: He funded Harvard's Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering, and his Wyss Campaign for Nature pledged $1B+ to protect 30% of the planet by 2030. In 2024 he gave CHF 100M to the City of Bern, which made him an honorary citizen.
deep_cut_fact: While working in the steel industry in Brussels, he ran a side business selling airplanes. One of those sales introduced him to a surgeon who had co-founded Synthes, which led to his medical-device career. Earlier he worked as a textile-plant engineer and as a Chrysler project manager in Pakistan, Turkey and the Philippines.
notes: Aged 91 and very private; he rarely gives interviews. The foundation's contact form is the only published channel, and it warns about impersonators. Hooks: the conservation and land-protection work, the engineering background, and the Glenturret distillery he bought with Silvio Denz in 2019.

name: Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani
profile: Former Emir of Qatar (1995-2013), known as the 'Father Emir'; died 12 July 2026 aged 74, as announced by the Amiri Diwan.
notes: Deceased - death reported by AP and Qatari state media on 12 July 2026: https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/qatars-former-ruler-sheikh-hamad-bin-khalifa-al-134688542 . Forbes 1998 entry was for the then-ruling Emir. Remaining fields skipped per instructions.

name: Philippe Stern
current_role: Deceased (14 June 2026). Former president (1993-2009) and honorary president of Patek Philippe
profile: Philippe Stern (b. Geneva 1938) led the family-owned watchmaker Patek Philippe as president from 1993 to 2009, then handed over to his son Thierry. He died in June 2026, aged 87/88. Patek Philippe announced his death.
notes: DIED 14 June 2026. Sources: https://nationaljeweler.com/articles/15059-patek-philippe-s-visionary-leader-philippe-stern-dies-at-88 ; https://www.luxurytribune.com/en/patek-philippe-announces-the-passing-of-philippe-stern ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Stern_(businessman). The Hurun fortune now presumably sits with the Stern family (Thierry Stern is Patek president). Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Archie Aldis 'Red' Emmerson
current_role: Founder and owner, Sierra Pacific Industries (Anderson, California); sons George (president) and Mark (chairman) run day-to-day
profile: Born 1929 in Grand Ronde, Oregon, Red Emmerson went into the lumber business with his father in 1949 and built Sierra Pacific Industries (incorporated 1969) into the second-largest US lumber producer. The family owns ~2.4M acres of forestland in California, Oregon and Washington and was America's largest private landowner until 2026; SPI also makes windows and doors and runs biomass cogeneration plants at its mills.
interesting_fact: Per the Land Report 100, the Emmersons held the title of America's largest private landowner (2.33M acres in 2021) until Stan Kroenke overtook them in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In 1948, aged 19, he arrived in Arcata, California and set out to work every job in the sawmill to learn the business; decades later Timber Processing magazine named him its 2019 Person of the Year.
notes: Surname is spelled Emmerson (input has 'Emerson'). Aged ~97, very private; sons George and Mark are the practical contacts. Energy angle: SPI operates wood-biomass power plants at its sawmills. Avoid wildfire litigation topics.

name: Russell Weiner
current_role: Founder of Rockstar Energy; private investor (now known as Russ Savage), ~4.7% shareholder and activist at Celsius Holdings
profile: Founded Rockstar energy drink in 2001, reportedly financing it with a mortgage on his Sausalito condo, and built it into a top-3 U.S. energy drink before selling to PepsiCo in 2020 for ~$3.85B. He legally changed his name to Russ Savage in 2025, and in Aug 2026 disclosed a ~$300M stake in Celsius Holdings (which now owns Rockstar's North American rights) while campaigning to become its CEO.
interesting_fact: His 2026 activist push targets Celsius, the company that now controls the North American rights to Rockstar, the brand he created; Celsius shares jumped ~12% on news of his stake.
deep_cut_fact: A San Diego State political-science graduate who once worked as a travel consultant, he ran for the California State Assembly in 1998 and won the Republican primary for the 6th district by just five votes.
notes: Search under both names: Russell Weiner and Russ Savage (legal name since 2025, per MarketScale/CNBC reporting). Son of radio host Michael Savage. Lives in Miami Beach. No published personal contact found; the Celsius campaign may generate an official campaign website/press contact worth checking later.

name: Ingrid Flick
current_role: Owner of Ingrid Flick Holding / Flick Family Office (Austria); chair of the board of trustees, Friedrich Flick Förderungsstiftung (Düsseldorf)
profile: Born Ingrid Ragger in 1959 in Carinthia, a carpenter's daughter, she met industrialist Friedrich Karl Flick in 1981 while a hotel receptionist on the Arlberg and married him in 1990. On his death in 2006 she became main heir to the Flick fortune (built on Daimler-Benz and industrial stakes), which she manages via her own holding and family office.
interesting_fact: Since 2006 she has chaired the Friedrich Flick Förderungsstiftung, founded in 1963, which funds young talent in science, technology and research as well as education, youth, disability support and culture.
deep_cut_fact: In early 2020 she became an entrepreneur in aquaculture, founding 'White Panther Gebirgsgarnelen' in Styria - an indoor 'mountain shrimp' farm producing ~60 t a year without antibiotics or hormones, among Europe's largest indoor shrimp farms. She is also an honorary citizen of Rottenmann and a children's-book author.
notes: Input lists country as United States, but she is Austrian (based in Carinthia/Styria). Very private. Avoid the family-history and 2008 grave-robbery topics. No published contact found; possible route via White Panther Produktion GmbH or the foundation.

name: Issac Perlmutter
current_role: Private investor; former chairman of Marvel Entertainment (until Disney eliminated the role in March 2023)
profile: Israeli-born (1942) investor who arrived in New York with little, built a closeout-merchandise business (Odd Lot Trading), then gained control of Toy Biz and Marvel in its 1990s bankruptcy restructuring. He led Marvel through its film boom and its $4B sale to Disney in 2009, becoming one of Disney's largest individual shareholders, and ran Marvel Entertainment until 2023.
interesting_fact: Famously reclusive, he long took pride in never having given an interview - breaking that streak only in 2023 with the Wall Street Journal after leaving Disney.
deep_cut_fact: After serving in the IDF during the 1967 Six-Day War and emigrating to New York, one of his first ways of earning money was standing outside Brooklyn's Jewish cemeteries, using his Hebrew to lead funeral prayers for tips. He and wife Laura later gave $50M to found NYU Langone's Perlmutter Cancer Center.
notes: Name is usually spelled Isaac 'Ike' Perlmutter. Extremely private; no published personal, office or PR contact found. Philanthropy route: NYU Langone Perlmutter Cancer Center. Politically connected (Trump ally) - expect no reply to cold outreach.

name: James
profile: Most likely James K. 'J.K.' Irving, chairman of J.D. Irving Ltd. and brother of Arthur Irving (Irving Oil), with whom the Hurun 2014 entry is shared. He died on 21 June 2024, aged 96, in Saint John, New Brunswick. Record skipped per instructions.
notes: Entry gives only the first name 'James' (Irving Group, shared with Arthur Irving), so identity is inferred. J.K. Irving died 21 June 2024 (https://www.cbc.ca/1.7243426); Arthur Irving died in May 2024. If the entry meant J.K.'s son James D. 'Jim' Irving (co-CEO of J.D. Irving Ltd.), he is alive and would need separate research.

name: Alejandro Bulgheroni
current_role: Chairman, Pan American Energy Group (Argentina); owner of Bulgheroni family wine estates incl. Bodega Garzón (Uruguay)
profile: Argentine industrial engineer (b. 1943, Rufino) who joined his father's Bridas Corp. in 1965 and ran it with brother Carlos from 1985; sold 50% to CNOOC and in 2017 merged with BP's Argentine assets to form Pan American Energy Group, Argentina's largest private integrated energy firm. Lives in Uruguay; owns 10+ wineries worldwide and a large dairy complex.
interesting_fact: In 1992 he secured some of the first gas exploration concessions Turkmenistan granted to a foreign energy company. His Garzón wine club membership reportedly costs $200,000.
deep_cut_fact: His wine empire began as an energy idea: in 2006 he stood on a windy Uruguayan hilltop scouting a wind-farm site, advisers suggested vines instead, and when told quality would take 6-8 years he quipped, 'How old do you think I am?' (Wine Spectator, 2018).
notes: The PAE email is the company's general 'otras consultas' inbox, not a press desk. Son Marcos Bulgheroni is PAE Group CEO. The wine/energy angle (wind farm turned vineyard) is a natural hook.

name: Li Chunan
current_role: Chairman of Dalian Linton NC Machine Co. (Linton Technologies, BSE: 835368); cofounder and major shareholder of Longi Green Energy.
profile: Li Chunan (b. 1968, Nanyang, Henan) cofounded Longi Green Energy, one of the world's largest solar wafer and module makers, with Lanzhou University classmates Li Zhenguo and Zhong Baoshen. He also chairs Dalian-based Linton, which makes crystal-growing, wafer-slicing and other equipment for the solar and semiconductor industries.
interesting_fact: Longi's three cofounders were college friends from undergraduate days at Lanzhou University; Li studied in its physics department (entered 1986) and serves as a trustee of the Lanzhou University Education Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he was an inventor of magnetic separation gear: he holds a 1997 Chinese utility-model patent for a 'suspended permanent-magnet iron remover' (ZL97233990.6) and a 2010 invention patent for a circulating-oil-cooled electromagnetic iron remover, from his Fushun magnet-electric company days (cofounded 1993).
notes: IR email is the Linton board office contact (named staffer Jin Yao, tel 0411-62638881) published in an Aug 2025 shareholder-meeting notice. Deep-cut source is a user-contributed Chinese bio page (patent numbers are checkable on CNIPA). Avoid: 2024 CSRC Liaoning fine for insider-info leak.

name: April Goh
current_role: Fellow, Columbia University China Center for Social Policy (New York); Nippon Paint heir
profile: April Goh is a granddaughter of the late Singapore paints tycoon Goh Cheng Liang (d. August 2025), who partnered with Japan's Nippon Paint in 1962. In a 2025 transfer, six grandchildren received a combined 55% stake in Nippon Paint Holdings; she got the largest share, about US$3.4B, reportedly partly held for siblings. Voting control stays with her uncle Goh Hup Jin. She works in social policy, not the family business.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather broke with Asian convention by skipping a generation: he passed the bulk of his Nippon Paint fortune straight to his six grandchildren, making all of them billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: She formerly worked in finance and is now a fellow at Columbia University's China Center for Social Policy, focusing on gender-based violence. She was among the Goh family members who visited the patriarch's ancestral village in the Teochew region of Guangdong for a Chinese TV programme.
notes: A private, non-operating heir who declined to comment to Bloomberg; there are no business role or public channels. She is a poor fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast; recommend skipping or approaching only via academic channels if relevant.

name: Andrei Bokarev
current_role: Co-owner/partner in Iskander Makhmudov's holdings (UMMC, Transmashholding, Kuzbassrazrezugol, Ust-Luga Oil); stepped down from Transmashholding posts in April 2022
profile: Russian businessman and long-time partner of Iskander Makhmudov who ran Krutrade (coal exports for Kuzbassrazrezugol) and then chaired/led Transmashholding, Russia's largest rolling-stock and metro-car maker, until 2022. He co-owns stakes in Ural Mining Metallurgical Company and half of the Ust-Luga oil terminal.
interesting_fact: Transmashholding builds most of Russia's locomotives and Moscow metro trains; UMMC, in which he is a partner, spent $100M building the Shayba ice arena for the Sochi 2014 Olympics and handed it to the state afterwards.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (Apr 2022), Australia, EU and US Treasury (Sept 2023); left Transmashholding roles due to sanctions. Not suitable for outreach; any contact could raise sanctions-compliance issues. No published contacts. Alive per 2025 sanctions-list updates.

name: Timur Kulibaev
current_role: Private investor; owner of Joint Resources holding and (with wife Dinara) majority shareholder of Halyk Bank; former chairman of KazEnergy (2005-2023) and Samruk-Kazyna
profile: Son-in-law of Kazakhstan's first president Nursultan Nazarbayev, he built a fortune in banking, telecoms, gold and oil and gas: sold Kar-Tel (2004) and Altynalmas Gold (2014) and, with his wife, controls Halyk Bank. Dubbed the 'oil prince', he sat on Gazprom's board 2011-22 and led KazEnergy until 2023; he has kept a low profile since 2022.
interesting_fact: He headed the Kazakhstan Boxing Federation from 2009 to 2024; in that period Kazakh boxers won gold, silver and bronze medals at both the 2012 London and 2016 Rio Olympics.
deep_cut_fact: After studying national economic planning at Moscow State University (1988), his first job was junior research assistant at the economics research institute of the Kazakh SSR's State Planning Committee; his 1999 PhD thesis was on enterprise management mechanisms in market conditions, using the oil industry as the example.
notes: Politically exposed person; extensive critical press (FT pipeline-contract reporting, offshore structures). Very private since 2022, no published personal or office contact found; Halyk Bank IR is the only corporate channel and does not represent him personally. Energy angle (Kazakh oil & gas) is strong but access is unlikely.

name: Igor Kesaev
current_role: Owner and President, Mercury Group (Megapolis tobacco distribution; retail)
profile: Igor Kesaev (b. 1966, Vladikavkaz; MGIMO graduate) founded Mercury in 1991 as a food and alcohol importer. Its Megapolis arm, co-founded with Sergei Katsiev, distributes ~70% of Russia's cigarettes; Philip Morris and JTI bought 40% of it in 2013 for $1.5B. In 2019 he merged his Dixy supermarkets with the Krasnoe & Beloe alcohol chain.
interesting_fact: He enjoys heli-skiing and mountain climbing.
notes: Sanctioned by the EU, UK (2022), Canada and the US (May 2023); Cyprus revoked his passport in 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Igor_Kesaev). Contacting or featuring him carries legal/reputational risk; recommend excluding from outreach. No published contacts collected.

name: Miguel Fluxa Rossello
current_role: Chairman and owner, Grupo Iberostar (Palma de Mallorca)
profile: Miquel/Miguel Fluxà Rosselló (b. 1938, Inca, Mallorca) is the third-generation heir of a Mallorcan shoemaking family who in 1986 opened the first Iberostar hotels and built the group into a global resort chain (~100 hotels). In 2006 he sold its tour-operator and travel-agency arms to Carlyle for $950M to focus on hotels. Daughters Sabina (vice chair & CEO) and Gloria (vice chair & CSO) now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: The family business dates to 1877, when his grandfather Antonio Fluxà set up a shoe workshop in Inca that within a decade had 11 workshops and five leather factories; his brother Lorenzo later founded the Camper shoe brand.
deep_cut_fact: After his father died in 1993, he led Iberostar's first international opening, in the Dominican Republic. He received the Gold Medal of the Balearic Islands in 2014 and in 2026 was named Mallorcadiario's 'Personaje del año' and awarded the Balearic College of Economists' Gold Medal.
notes: Age 88; low media profile. Iberostar's 'Wave of Change' ocean/coral program (led by daughter Gloria) is the group's signature sustainability story. 2026 awards: https://www.mallorcadiario.com/miguel-fluxa-personaje-mallorcadiario-2026 and https://www.mallorcadiario.com/miguel-fluxa-recibira-medalla-oro-colegio-economistas-baleares.

name: Francois Graff
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Graff (Graff Diamonds), London
profile: CEO of Graff, the London jewellery house his father Laurence founded in 1960. He joined around 1986 and learned every division before running the vertically integrated firm, which sources, cuts and sets record stones (e.g. the 302.37ct Lesedi La Rona) and sells through ~60 boutiques. The Sunday Times counts the Graffs among Britain's richest.
interesting_fact: His favourite pieces are the 'Eternal Twins': two near-identical 50.23-carat D-flawless emerald-cut diamonds cut from a single 270-carat rough. 'I don't think we will ever repeat that in the history of our company,' he says.
deep_cut_fact: He tells of a 3.5ct blue diamond his father first admired on a client's hand, thinking it a zircon, and bought. Graff has sold it three times and it always comes back: 'It has an affinity for this company and doesn't want to leave.' He has never cut a diamond himself.
notes: Interviews are rare ('nearly as rare as acquiring one of Graff's diamonds'). Best route is Graff's PR/press enquiry option on the official contact form. Little energy/AI link, though Graff's vertically integrated sourcing and cutting operations (including in Africa) could be a supply-chain angle.

name: Pierre Chen Tai-Ming
current_role: Founder and Chairman, YAGEO Group (Taiwan, TWSE: 2327)
profile: Pierre Chen (Chen Tai-Ming) founded passive-component maker Yageo in Taipei in 1977. Through acquisitions such as KEMET and Pulse, it became one of the world's largest makers of resistors, capacitors and magnetics, components found in servers, EVs and data-center hardware. He also runs the YAGEO Foundation, which holds one of Asia's top contemporary-art collections.
interesting_fact: A mega-collector, he told Artnet in 2019 he owned seven Picassos, two Francis Bacons and ten Gerhard Richters. His YAGEO Foundation, set up in 1999, lent works to Tate's 'Capturing the Moment' and opened an art center in Taipei.
deep_cut_fact: He bought his first artworks in 1976, a year before founding Yageo. He has long planned a private museum in the Yangmingshan mountains outside Taipei.

public_contacts.value: IR@yageo.com (spokesperson Thomas Chang, Global Finance Senior Director)

notes: Hurun lists his country as China, but he is Taiwanese (Taipei). Also a renowned wine collector (Sotheby's 'Pierre Chen: An Epicurean Odyssey' sale). Data-center angle: Yageo/KEMET components are core to AI server power delivery. Best route: Yageo IR/spokesperson, or the YAGEO Foundation for art-related outreach.

name: Nikolai Buinov
current_role: Co-founder, chairman of the board and majority shareholder, Irkutsk Oil Company (INK)
profile: Krasnoyarsk-born (1967) founder of Irkutsk Oil Company, Russia's largest independent private oil producer. He started in timber, co-founded fuel supplier Bodaibo Energy with his father in 1995, bought his first oil licence in 1997, and in 2022 bought back Goldman Sachs' stake in INK. INK is now moving into petrochemicals with its Irkutsk Polymer Plant near Ust-Kut.
interesting_fact: In 2025 INK began launching the Irkutsk Polymer Plant near Ust-Kut, the first polymer plant in Eastern Siberia and the company's largest investment project.
deep_cut_fact: A transport-university graduate (St Petersburg, 1990), he financed the restoration of the historic Wawelberg Bank building on Nevsky Prospekt, a long-stalled St Petersburg project completed in 2021 and now operating as a hotel.
notes: Low public profile, based in Irkutsk. Best route is likely INK's press service via irkutskoil.ru (site unreachable from here, so no contact verified). Russian energy company; check sanctions exposure before outreach.

name: Rodger Riney
current_role: Founder of Scottrade (sold to TD Ameritrade 2017); philanthropist via the Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation (St. Louis); MMRF board member
profile: Rodger O. Riney (b. 1945) co-founded discount broker Scottrade in Scottsdale in 1980, after 1975 brokerage deregulation. He grew it in St. Louis to 3 million accounts and $170B in assets and sold it to TD Ameritrade for $4B in 2017. Since then he has given hundreds of millions to medical research, especially on blood cancers and neurodegenerative disease.
interesting_fact: After Scottrade launched online trading in 1996, its trade volume grew 15% a month, compounded, for 39 straight months. Fortune repeatedly named Scottrade one of its '100 Best Companies to Work For'.
deep_cut_fact: His grandparents got him into investing by giving him 10 shares of stock as a boy. He studied civil engineering (BS) and earned an MBA at the University of Missouri, and interned at Edward Jones before turning down an engineering job for a lower-paid role at a Missouri investment firm.
notes: Retired and private; no published personal, office or foundation contact found (rineyfoundation.org belongs to a different Riney family foundation). Possible routes are his Multiple Myeloma Research Foundation board role (themmrf.org) or Washington University in St. Louis, a major gift recipient.

name: Hu Baifan
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang NHU Co. (新和成, SZSE: 002001)
profile: Hu Baifan taught chemistry at a rural school before founding a school-run factory in Xinchang, Zhejiang in 1988 with money borrowed from fellow teachers. It grew into Zhejiang NHU, one of the world's largest makers of vitamins A and E, plus methionine, flavors and fragrances and new materials. He is chairman; his younger brother Hu Baishan is vice chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: NHU started as a school-run venture recycling waste alcohol in a rented workshop with borrowed money, no plant, workers or technology; it made a RMB 100k profit in its first year.
deep_cut_fact: While buying waste alcohol from a drug plant, a workshop director told him some pharma products sold for RMB 100k-2m a ton; that pushed him into high-value chemistry, and in 1991 his team developed ethoxymethylene, a norfloxacin intermediate, replacing imports - NHU's first national key new product.
notes: Low international media profile. Best route: NHU board office / IR (+86 575 86017157 is the company line in its sustainability report).

name: Austen Cargill II
current_role: Cargill family heir/shareholder and Montana rancher (retired Cargill vice president; former Cargill board member)
profile: Austen S. Cargill II (b. 1951) is a great-grandson of W.W. Cargill, founder of the grain business in 1865; the family still owns ~90% of Cargill ($154B revenue). Trained as an aquatic biologist (PhD, Oregon State), he worked at Cargill as a marine biologist, joined its board in 1995, retired as a VP in 2001 and now ranches in Montana.
interesting_fact: Before becoming a Cargill executive he earned a PhD and worked as a marine biologist for the company - unusual for an heir to the largest private US company.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of a 1985 Freshwater Biology paper, 'The role of lipids as feeding stimulants for shredding aquatic insects', co-written with stream ecologist Kenneth W. Cummins.
notes: Very private Cargill heir with no public office or published contact; lives in Montana (Paradise Valley/Livingston area). Not an operator; low fit unless discussing agriculture. No contact route found beyond Cargill corporate media relations (not specific to him).

name: James Cargill II
current_role: Cargill family shareholder/heir (no executive role at Cargill identified)
profile: James R. Cargill II (b. 1949) is a great-grandson of W.W. Cargill, who founded Cargill in 1865 as a single grain warehouse on an Iowa railroad line. He is one of ~21 billionaire heirs of the family that still owns ~90% of Cargill, America's largest private company ($154B 2025 sales), and lives a private life in Wisconsin.
interesting_fact: The Cargill-MacMillan family still owns roughly 90% of Cargill and collects an estimated 18% of net profits as dividends each year.
deep_cut_fact: Through the James R. Cargill II Trust he has owned stock in SolarAttic, a company that uses solar energy to heat swimming pools. He has also served on the board of trustees of the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum and on the board of CU Boulder's Center of the American West.
notes: Very private; no published contact. Not involved in Cargill management, so Cargill corporate press is not a route to him. Avoid any references to his wife Kathy Cargill's widely covered local disputes or his late first wife.

name: Marianne Liebmann
current_role: Cargill family shareholder (no executive role found)
profile: Marianne Cargill Liebmann (b. 1953) is a great-granddaughter of W.W. Cargill, who founded Cargill as a single Iowa grain warehouse in 1865, and one of ~21 billionaire heirs of the family that owns about 90% of America's largest private company. A Montana State University graduate, she lives in Bozeman, Montana; siblings include Austen S. Cargill II and James R. Cargill II.
interesting_fact: The Cargill-MacMillan family collects an estimated 18% of Cargill's net profits as dividends each year; Cargill had $154B in 2025 sales.
notes: Extremely private Cargill heir; Forbes calls the Cargill billionaires 'secretive'. No published personal, foundation or office contacts found.

name: Donald Sterling
current_role: Los Angeles real-estate investor/landlord (apartments on the Westside and in Koreatown, Beverly Hills Plaza Hotel); former owner of the LA Clippers (1981-2014)
profile: Chicago-born Donald Sterling (né Tokowitz, b. 1934) was a divorce and personal-injury lawyer before building a fortune buying run-down apartment buildings across Los Angeles. He bought the then-San Diego Clippers for $12.5M in 1981; after his 2014 lifetime NBA ban over recorded racist remarks, the team was sold for $2B. He still holds a large LA property portfolio.
interesting_fact: His $12.5M purchase of the Clippers in 1981 turned into a $2B sale to Steve Ballmer in 2014 - at the time a record price for an NBA team.
deep_cut_fact: At Theodore Roosevelt High School in Boyle Heights he was on the gymnastics team and class president (class of 1952); his first real-estate deal, made while practising law in the 1960s, was a 26-unit apartment building in Beverly Hills.
notes: Highly controversial (2014 NBA lifetime ban; past DOJ housing-discrimination suit) - reputational risk for any podcast guest booking. No published office or press contact found. Aged 92.

name: Jeffrey S. Skoll
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Skoll Foundation; Chairman, Capricorn Investment Group
profile: Jeff Skoll was eBay's first president and first full-time employee (1996), and his eBay stock made him a billionaire. He now backs social entrepreneurs through the Skoll Foundation and Skoll World Forum and invests through Capricorn Investment Group. His film studio Participant made Spotlight and An Inconvenient Truth.
interesting_fact: Participant's films earned 11 Oscar nominations in 2006 alone, and Spotlight won Best Picture in 2016. He also produced Al Gore's climate documentary An Inconvenient Truth, a useful hook for an energy-focused show.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Toronto, Skoll co-edited the engineering students' satirical paper The Toike Oike and paid his way by pumping gas in North York. Before Stanford he founded two Toronto firms, IT consultancy Skoll Engineering and computer-rental company Micros on the Move.
notes: Input lists him under a 1999 Forbes entry with no source of wealth (eBay). Capricorn Investment Group is a notable clean-energy and climate-tech investor (an early Tesla backer), which suits an energy podcast. Skoll Foundation press (press@skoll.org) is the best route.

name: Laurence A. And Preston R. Tisch
profile: Joint Forbes entry (1997-98) for brothers Laurence A. Tisch (d. 15 Nov 2003, aged 80) and Preston Robert 'Bob' Tisch (d. 15 Nov 2005, aged 79), co-founders of Loews Corporation. Both are deceased.
notes: Both deceased - skip. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laurence_Tisch and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preston_Robert_Tisch. Their heirs (e.g. James Tisch at Loews, Jonathan Tisch, Steve Tisch of the NY Giants) would be separate profiles.

name: Jim C. Walton
current_role: Chairman, Arvest Bank; chairman, Community Publishers Inc.; Walmart heir (Walmart board 2005-2016)
profile: Youngest son of Walmart founder Sam Walton, born 1948 in Newport, Arkansas. He joined Walmart in 1972 on real-estate deals, ran family holding Walton Enterprises from 1975, built and led family-owned Arvest Bank (now chairman) and chairs newspaper group CPI. Forbes ranked him about the world's 12th-richest person in early 2026.
interesting_fact: He replaced his late brother John on Walmart's board in 2005; together with his siblings he pledged about $2B to the Walton Family Foundation in 2008-2013.
deep_cut_fact: At Bentonville High School (class of 1965) he was junior class president, an all-state football player and learned to fly a plane; his first Walmart job in 1972 was in the real-estate side, scouting deals for new stores.
notes: Input record was a stale 1996 Forbes entry; he is now among the world's richest. Very private, rarely interviewed. Best route is via Arvest or Walton Enterprises. Avoid political-donation topics.

name: Austen S. Cargill II
current_role: Cargill family shareholder and rancher (Montana); joined Cargill's board in 1995 (current board status unconfirmed)
profile: Austen Stowell Cargill II (born 1951) is a great-grandson of W.W. Cargill, founder of Cargill, the world's largest privately held agribusiness, and his fortune comes from his family stake. Trained as a scientist (BS/MS University of Minnesota, PhD Oregon State), he joined Cargill as a marine biologist, became a director in 1995 and later ranched in Montana's Paradise Valley.
interesting_fact: In 2001 he bought the North Ranch in Montana's Paradise Valley near Antelope Butte, formerly owned by the Church Universal and Triumphant.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published aquatic ecologist: lead author of 'The role of lipids as feeding stimulants for shredding aquatic insects' (Freshwater Biology, 1985) with stream ecologist Kenneth Cummins.
notes: Extremely private Cargill heir; no published personal or office contact. Only route would be Cargill corporate media relations, which is unlikely to forward. Alive per Wikipedia/Wikidata (no death recorded); current Cargill board role not confirmed.

name: Charles Bartlett Johnson
current_role: Retired former CEO/chairman of Franklin Resources (Franklin Templeton); largest shareholder of the San Francisco Giants
profile: Charles B. Johnson (b. 1933, Montclair NJ) became CEO of his father's small mutual-fund firm Franklin Resources in 1957 at age 24, took it public in 1971 and bought Templeton in 1992, building Franklin Templeton into a global asset manager. He stepped down as chairman in 2013; son Greg and daughter Jenny later led the firm. He owns about 26% of the San Francisco Giants.
interesting_fact: His $250M gift to Yale in 2013 to build two new residential colleges (one named Benjamin Franklin College) was the largest in Yale's history at the time.
deep_cut_fact: At Yale (class of 1954) he was a scholarship student who waited tables in the dining hall and played offensive guard on the football team; after ROTC he served as an Army lieutenant in Germany before joining Franklin.
notes: Aged 93 and retired; very unlikely podcast guest. No personal public contact; Franklin Templeton and the Giants are run by his children/others. Avoid political-donation controversies.

name: James R. Cargill II
current_role: Cargill family heir and shareholder in Cargill Inc. (no operating role)
profile: James Ray Cargill II (b. 1949) is a great-grandson of William Wallace Cargill, founder of Minneapolis-based Cargill, the world's largest privately held food and agriculture company. His fortune comes from his inherited stake in Cargill; he keeps a low profile in Birchwood, Wisconsin and supports arts and museum institutions.
interesting_fact: He has served on the Board of Trustees of the Smithsonian's National Air and Space Museum and on the board of the Center of the American West at the University of Colorado Boulder.
deep_cut_fact: Through the James R. Cargill II Trust he was a shareholder in SolarAttic, a small company making systems that use attic solar heat to warm swimming pools (listed in its 1998 stockholder meeting minutes).
notes: One of the 'secretive Cargill billionaires'; no public contact channels, website or social accounts found. Donor to the Walker Art Center and Minneapolis Institute of Art. Information is thin, so keep outreach generic.

Cargill II and James R. Cargill II. Forbes puts her net worth at ~$4.8B (Nov 2026).

name: Robin Li
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Baidu, Inc. (Nasdaq: BIDU; HKEX: 9888); Chairman of iQIYI
profile: Robin Li (李彦宏, b. 1968, Yangquan, Shanxi) studied at Peking University and SUNY Buffalo, worked at Dow Jones' IDD and Infoseek, and co-founded Baidu in 2000; it became China's dominant search engine. He has repositioned Baidu around AI: the ERNIE large models and chatbot, Apollo Go robotaxis, AI Cloud infrastructure (growing ~50-80% a year in 2026) and Kunlunxin AI chips.
interesting_fact: While at Dow Jones' IDD Information Services in 1996 he created RankDex, a link-based site-scoring algorithm for search ranking; Larry Page's later PageRank patent references Li's work, and RankDex became the basis of Baidu's search engine.
deep_cut_fact: He named Baidu ('a hundred times') after the last line of Song-dynasty poet Xin Qiji's 'Green Jade Table in the Lantern Festival': 'Having searched hundreds of times in the crowd, suddenly turning back, she is there in the dimmest candlelight' (众里寻他千百度).
notes: Highly relevant to AI/data-centre themes (Kunlunxin chips, AI Cloud). Baidu IR contact email appears at the end of quarterly results releases (IR site was not reachable from this session to confirm the exact address). Hurun 2026 also lists him among unicorn founders (likely Kunlunxin).

name: Fernand Huts
current_role: Chairman and owner, Katoen Natie (KN Holding, Luxembourg/Antwerp); controlling owner of waste-to-energy group Indaver
profile: Antwerp-born Fernand Huts (b. 1950) joined Katoen Natie, then a cotton-warehousing firm of about 100 staff where his father was a partner, in 1981. He gradually bought out the 19 other partners and built it into a global logistics group of 350+ companies and ~20,000 people. Katoen Natie bought waste-processing and energy-recovery group Indaver in 2015. He served in Belgium's parliament (VLD) from 1995 to 1999.
interesting_fact: A major collector, he once paid more than €5 million for a Tyrannosaurus rex skeleton. He also collects archaeological textiles and Flemish art, shown at Katoen Natie's Antwerp HQ and through his Phoebus Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: His first company, Het Veldboerke, sold organically grown vegetables and fruit long before organic was mainstream. As Trends' 1987 'Manager of the Year', he said his managers should not read management books but go out for beers. He is also an occasional DJ.
notes: Outspoken and colourful in Flemish media and fairly accessible via Katoen Natie's general inbox. The energy angle is Indaver, a waste-to-energy and industrial-waste treatment company. Port logistics and Antwerp's petrochemical cluster are also good hooks.

name: C. Dean Metropoulos
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Metropoulos & Co. (Greenwich, CT); minority investor (~5%) in the NFL's New England Patriots
profile: Greek-born (Tripoli, 1946) turnaround investor who emigrated to Massachusetts at 10, studied at Babson (BS, MBA), and has done 70+ 'buy-build' food and consumer deals - Chef Boyardee/International Home Foods, Pinnacle, Vlasic, Bumble Bee, Ghirardelli, Pabst. With Apollo he revived Twinkies maker Hostess (2013), later sold to J.M. Smucker for $5.6B (2023). In 2026 he bought a 5% stake in the Patriots.
interesting_fact: He is best known for saving Twinkies: he and Apollo bought Hostess out of liquidation in 2013 for ~$410M, relaunched the brand and later took it public; Smucker bought it a decade later for $5.6B.
deep_cut_fact: At 25 he moved to Geneva as financial director for GTE International's Europe, Middle East and Africa operations, then returned to the U.S. as the company's youngest-ever controller; his first business was a summer landscaping company he started in 11th grade.
notes: Age ~80. His firm's site publishes info@metropoulos.com. First US acquisition (1981) was Stella Foods, a Vermont cheese company (his wife's home state), later sold for $375M. Little energy/data-center link, though the firm once owned a dry-bulk shipping business (Solar Marine).

name: Georg Nemetschek
current_role: Founder, majority shareholder and Honorary Chairman of the Supervisory Board (since May 2022), Nemetschek SE
profile: Born in 1934, Georg Nemetschek founded a structural-engineering office in Munich in 1963 that was one of the first to use software for finite-element slab calculations. He built it into the Nemetschek Group (Allplan, Graphisoft, Vectorworks, Bluebeam, Maxon), an MDAX-listed AEC software maker with about EUR 1B revenue. He still holds voting control and funds AI-in-construction research through his foundations.
interesting_fact: He funds the TUM Georg Nemetschek Institute 'Artificial Intelligence for the Built World' at the Technical University of Munich, which made him an Honorary Senator in 2024. He was also a Munich University of Applied Sciences professor and dean (1971-1996).
deep_cut_fact: As a TUM civil-engineering student he was fascinated by PERM, the vacuum-tube computer built by professors Piloty and Sauer, which led him to invest in software in the 1960s before PCs existed. He received the Konrad Zuse Medal in 1997 and was inducted into Computerwoche's IT Hall of Fame in 2014.
notes: Aged about 92. No death notice was found as of Nov 2026. The Forbes bio's 'deputy chairman' title is outdated: he has been honorary chairman since 2022. Nemetschek's news-media page lists press and IR contacts, but the addresses could not be extracted here. The TUM GNI institute is a strong AI/data angle.

name: Nithin Kamath
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Zerodha (Bengaluru); co-founder, Rainmatter and True Beacon
profile: Nithin Kamath co-founded discount broker Zerodha with brother Nikhil in 2010; bootstrapped and profitable, it became one of India's largest brokerages by active clients, popularising zero-brokerage equity investing. Through Rainmatter he backs fintech startups and climate/health ventures, and he is one of India's most active founder voices on X.
interesting_fact: 'Zerodha' fuses 'zero' with the Sanskrit 'rodha' (barrier); the company never raised outside capital, unusual among Indian fintech unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: He began trading at 17 managing his father's account, and from 2001 to 2004 worked night shifts as a senior tele-sales associate at a call centre so he could trade the markets by day.

current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Medpace Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: MEDP), Cincinnati

name: Otto Toto Sugiri

Richardson and father Perry Bass in the late 1960s, growing a ~$50m company into a multibillion-dollar investment group. Now a low-profile private investor and arts philanthropist.

notes: A natural fit for an energy/AI podcast: C3 started as C3 Energy, serving utilities, and he wrote the book 'Digital Transformation' (2019). He stepped back from the CEO role in 2025 for health reasons and returned in May 2026; don't raise health in outreach. He also founded the Montana Meth Project and the Siebel Scholars programme.

profile: Laurence Graff OBE (b. 1938, Stepney, London) left school at 14 for a jewellery apprenticeship in Hatton Garden. He founded Graff Diamonds in 1960 and built it into a vertically integrated top-end diamond jeweller with 60+ stores, serving clients from the Sultan of Brunei to Hollywood. By 1962 he already had two shops, including his first in Hatton Garden, where he had started out scrubbing toilets as an apprentice.

current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Monumental Sports & Entertainment (Capitals, Wizards, Mystics, Capital One Arena); partner, Revolution Growth

He sold Redgate Communications to AOL in 1994, spent ~14 years as an AOL senior executive, then bought the Capitals (1999) and Wizards (2010) and built Monumental, now rebuilding Capital One Arena in downtown DC.

profile: Mississippi-born petroleum geologist (MSU 1958) who founded GeoSouthern Energy in 1981 and became a billionaire when it sold its early Eagle Ford acreage to Devon for $6B in 2013. I especially want to help students that have the desire to work but don't have the funds.' He also owns the Eagleford Restaurant in Cuero, Texas, near his ranch.

Woeste & Co. before chairing both Henkel's Supervisory Board and Shareholders' Committee from 1990 to 2009, handing over to Simone Bagel-Trah. His wealth comes from the family's controlling stake in Henkel (Persil, Schwarzkopf, Loctite).
