current_role: Co-founder, executive director and Chief Innovation Officer, WiseTech Global (Sydney); stepped down as executive chair July 2026
profile: Sydney-born Richard White co-founded logistics software firm WiseTech Global (originally Eagle Developments) with Maree Isaacs in 1994; its CargoWise platform automates freight forwarding and customs for 17,000+ customers in 193 countries. CEO for 30 years until October 2024, he later returned as executive chair, gave up the chair to Raelene Murphy in July 2026 and stays on as chief innovation officer.
interesting_fact: A former musician, refrigeration engineer and computer wholesaler, White has repaired guitars for top Australian rock bands such as AC/DC and The Angels.
deep_cut_fact: Before software he played in a band called Jade and ran a guitar-repair business named Rock Repairs; he taught himself electronics and programming while building lighting systems for bands. As a youth he washed dishes at his grandparents' wedding-reception business in Sydney's Bexley.
notes: Sensitive: subject of 2024-26 personal and governance controversies (misconduct allegations he denies, a 2025 AFP raid over insider-trading claims) that led to board changes; expect PR gatekeeping. Chair change source: https://www.fool.com.au/2026/07/07/wisetech-shares-surge-10-as-richard-white-steps-back-from-chair-role/

name: Kevin David Lehmann
current_role: 50% owner of dm-drogerie markt (Karlsruhe); no operational role
profile: Born September 2002, Kevin David Lehmann owns half of dm-drogerie markt, Germany's top-selling drugstore chain (63,600+ employees, ~$14B+ revenue). His father Günther, of the Pfannkuch grocery family, invested in founder Götz Werner's dm in the 1970s and quietly transferred his 50% stake to Kevin when he was a teenager, with a trustee managing it until he came of age. Neither is involved in running dm; Forbes estimates his fortune at ~$4.9B (2026).
interesting_fact: He was the world's youngest billionaire on Forbes' list (debuting at 18 in 2021) and held that title until 2022.

public_contacts.value: presse@dm.de (dm press office; spokesperson Jan-Henrik Mende)

notes: Almost nothing public about him personally; he has no known public role, interviews or social accounts. dm's press office handles company matters only and is unlikely to broker contact with a passive shareholder. Low-priority target for outreach.

name: Hans Peter Wild
current_role: Owner and Chairman of the Board, Capri Sun Group Holding (Zug, Switzerland) - back in operational control since Sept 2026; owner/chairman of rugby club Stade Français Paris
profile: Hans-Peter Wild (b. 1941, Heidelberg) joined his father's flavour company Rudolf Wild in 1974 and built two global businesses, WILD Flavors and Capri-Sun. He sold WILD Flavors (with KKR) to ADM in 2014 for about $3B but kept Capri-Sun and pouch-machinery maker Indag. In Sept 2026, aged 85, he dismissed CEO Roland Weening and resumed running Capri-Sun himself while remaining chairman.
interesting_fact: His biggest marketing coup was signing Muhammad Ali, then at his boxing peak, as Capri-Sun's advertising ambassador in 1979, helping turn the German pouch drink into a global brand sold in 100+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he donated $16.5M to the Marine Corps Scholarship Foundation in recognition of the US military's role in WWII and the liberation of Germany from the Nazis. A trained lawyer, he studied at the Sorbonne and Cambridge and wrote his Mannheim PhD on 'The market-dominating company under French law'.

public_contacts.value: caprisun@golin.com (Golin, Capri-Sun media contact on 2023 release - may be outdated)

notes: Also owns Salzburg hotels Goldener Hirsch and Schloss Moenchstein, and is a 10%+ holder in ADC Therapeutics via his Zug family office (Wild Group Management). Recent CEO dismissal (Sept 2026) is a sensitive topic. Golin contact dates from 2023.

name: Wu Yajun
current_role: Co-founder and controlling shareholder, Longfor Group Holdings (HKEX: 960); stepped down as chairman in Nov 2022
profile: Chongqing-born Wu Yajun (吴亚军, b. 1964) worked as an engineer and then a journalist before entering property in the early 1990s. She co-founded what became Longfor in 1993-95 and built it into one of China's largest and most conservatively financed private developers. She handed the chair to Chen Xuping in 2022 to 'institutionalise' the company and remains its main shareholder.
interesting_fact: As a journalist in Chongqing she interviewed more than 200 local entrepreneurs in about five years. That front-row view of business inspired her to quit and start her own company around age 30.
deep_cut_fact: She graduated in 1984 from Northwestern Polytechnical University's School of Marine Engineering with a degree in torpedo thermal-power plant design (鱼雷热动力装置设计). Her first job was as a technician at Chongqing's Qianwei Instrument Factory, long before she went into property.
notes: Has kept a very low profile since stepping down in 2022; no personal social channels. Longfor's IR site is the only official channel, and we found no verified published IR/press email. Chinese-language outreach is advisable. The torpedo-engineering background is a memorable hook.

name: Cheng Cheung Ling
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairwoman and Executive Director, Sino Biopharmaceutical Ltd (SBP Group, HKEX: 1177)
profile: Cheng Cheung Ling (郑翔玲, b. 1964) is a co-founder of Hong Kong-listed Sino Biopharmaceutical, one of China's largest drugmakers (Chia Tai Tianqing, Beijing Tide, etc.), where she is vice chair and on the executive committee. Her husband Tse Ping is a co-founder and their daughter Theresa Tse chairs the group, which is pushing into innovative drugs and international partnerships.
interesting_fact: Sino Biopharm's flagship Chia Tai Tianqing grew into one of China's leading makers of liver-disease and oncology drugs; the group has pivoted from generics to innovative medicines and global licensing deals.
deep_cut_fact: She is a trained clinical physician (临床医师) as well as holding an MBA from Peking University's Guanghua School of Management - a medical background unusual among China's pharma billionaires.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed. pr@sbpgroup.com is labelled 媒体垂询 (media inquiries), info@ is the company mailbox. Little energy/data-center link; best framed as entrepreneurship/pharma.

name: Harsh Mariwala
current_role: Chairman and Founder, Marico Ltd; Founder, ASCENT Foundation
profile: Joined the family's Bombay Oil Industries in 1971, started its consumer business in 1975 and spun it out as Marico (Parachute, Saffola), now selling in 59 countries. He also founded Kaya clinics, the Marico Innovation Foundation and the ASCENT Foundation, a peer network of 1,000+ entrepreneurs.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he published 'Harsh Realities', co-written with Ram Charan, about building Marico without an MBA or a 'fancy degree'. Marico's early breakthroughs included moving Parachute coconut oil from metal tins to plastic bottles and smaller packs.
deep_cut_fact: The family name began as a nickname: his grandfather Vallabhdas Vasanji moved from Kutch to Bombay in 1862 and traded pepper, known in Gujarati as 'mari', so he became known as 'Mariwala'.
notes: Very accessible and entrepreneurship-focused: an active poster on X (@hcmariwala, widely quoted by Business Today; confirm verification) and an EY Entrepreneur of the Year juror. The ASCENT Foundation is a natural angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. He also funds mental health through the Mariwala Health Initiative.

name: Sol Daurella
current_role: Chairman, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (Nasdaq/LSE: CCEP); independent director, Banco Santander
profile: Barcelona-born (1966) Sol Daurella Comadrán is the third generation of the family that won Spain's first Coca-Cola bottling licence in 1951 (Cobega). She ran Coca-Cola Iberian Partners and since 2016 has chaired CCEP, the world's largest Coke bottler by revenue (~$22B, 31 markets), in which she owns about 7%. She also sits on Santander's board.
interesting_fact: She serves as Honorary Consul for Iceland in Barcelona, alongside chairing the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler and sitting on the board of Spain's largest bank.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family Coca-Cola business in 1992 she began her career at strategy consultancy Mac Group; her grandfather Santiago Daurella Rull was a salted-cod importer before the family moved into bottling. She holds a business degree and MBA from ESADE.
notes: Low-profile, rarely interviewed. Route via CCEP corporate communications. Avoid the recent death of her husband Carles Vilarrubí and family topics.

name: James Duff
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Duff Capital Investors (Mississippi)
profile: With brother Tom, Jim Duff co-owns Duff Capital Investors, a holding company of 20+ businesses (~$6B revenue) incl. Southern Tire Mart, now the largest U.S. truck-tire dealer and retreader, trucking firms (KLLM, Frozen Food Express), car dealerships and DeepWell Energy Services. They bought back their father's tire business in 2003. The two are Mississippi's only billionaires.
interesting_fact: The brothers gave $26M toward Ole Miss's 202,000 sq ft STEM building, the largest academic project in the university's history, now the Jim and Thomas Duff Center for Science and Technology Innovation.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Columbia, Mississippi, Jim studied business at Utah Valley University; in 2017 the brothers created the Ernest R. Duff Flagship Constellation Fund at Ole Miss to honor their father, a 1955 UM law graduate who started the family tire business in 1973.
notes: Low national profile but visible locally via philanthropy (Southern Miss Duff Athletic Center, MSU autism center). DCI owns DeepWell Energy Services (oilfield), a possible energy angle. Avoid the 2016 plot against his brother noted by Forbes.

name: Chey Tae-won
current_role: Chairman, SK Group (SK Inc.); Chairman, Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry
profile: Has chaired SK Group since 1998. SK is one of Korea's largest conglomerates, spanning energy and refining (SK Innovation), telecom (SK Telecom) and memory chips (SK Hynix, a key HBM supplier for AI data centers). He has pushed SK hard into AI, batteries and clean energy, and has chaired the Korea Chamber of Commerce and Industry since 2021.
interesting_fact: He has championed 'social value' as a business metric. Under his 'Double Bottom Line' initiative (2018), SK companies measure and report their social impact in monetary terms alongside profit.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a physics degree from Korea University, completed the economics PhD program at the University of Chicago, co-authored a 2019 Stanford business case on SK's Double Bottom Line, and has twice been elected President of the Korea Handball Federation.
notes: Sources disagree on the Chicago degree. SK's site says he holds a PhD; other bios say he completed the PhD program. Avoid his 2013 conviction and his divorce case. Given SK Hynix (HBM) and SK's energy businesses, he fits both the data-center and energy themes. Best route is SK's US media team; KCCI is an alternative.

name: John Bicket
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Samsara Inc. (NYSE: IOT), San Francisco
profile: MIT-trained computer scientist who co-founded cloud-networking company Meraki with Sanjit Biswas (and Hans Robertson) in 2006, selling it to Cisco for $1.2B in 2012. In 2015 the pair co-founded Samsara, a 'connected operations' IoT and AI platform for fleets, construction and industrial firms, now with ~$1.9B ARR (FY2026) and 20,000+ customers.
interesting_fact: Samsara ended fiscal 2026 with $1.89B in annual recurring revenue, up 30% year over year, approaching $2B ARR by mid-2026.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT CSAIL grad student he was lead author on the 2005 Roofnet paper, 'Architecture and Evaluation of an Unplanned 802.11b Mesh Network' - a 37-node rooftop Wi-Fi mesh across ~4 sq km of Cambridge, MA that became the basis of Meraki.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder (Biswas is the public face/CEO). Samsara serves energy, utilities and construction fleets - relevant to data-center build-out supply chains. Route via Samsara media team.

name: Moshe Kantor
current_role: Major shareholder of Acron Group (Russian fertilizer producer); former president of the European Jewish Congress (2007-2022)
profile: Viatcheslav Moshe Kantor (b. 1953, Moscow), a Russian-British businessman, built his fortune as the principal shareholder of Acron, one of Russia's largest mineral-fertilizer producers. Long prominent in Jewish communal life, he led the European Jewish Congress for 15 years and chaired the World Holocaust Forum Foundation. EU sanctions imposed in 2022 were lifted in March 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he founded and became president of the International Luxembourg Forum on Preventing Nuclear Catastrophe, an NGO of leading nuclear non-proliferation experts.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as an aerospace engineer, he earned a diploma (1976) and a PhD (1981) from the Moscow Aviation Institute; he is also a serious art collector who founded Moscow's Museum of Avant-Garde Mastery (MAGMA) in 2001 and was made an honorary member of the Russian Academy of Arts in 2018.
notes: Removed from EU sanctions list in March 2025 (https://www.juedische-allgemeine.de/juedische-welt/frueherer-ejc-chef-kantor-von-eu-sanktionsliste-gestrichen) but was also sanctioned by the UK in 2022 - check current UK/other status before engaging. Personal site moshekantor.com was unreachable. Also known as Viatcheslav Kantor.

name: Liu Jincheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, EVE Energy (亿纬锂能, Shenzhen-listed 300014), Huizhou
profile: Hubei-born battery engineer (PhD) who studied electrochemistry at Wuhan University and founded EVE Energy around 2000-01. EVE makes consumer, EV (incl. BMW Neue Klasse cylindrical cells) and storage batteries, ranked No. 2 in energy-storage cell shipments in 2025, and now pitches itself as an 'energy base for the AI world'.
interesting_fact: At EVE's 25th anniversary he recalled that China's smart-meter procurement rules once explicitly banned domestic batteries; EVE ran hundreds of battery-explosion tests to break the import monopoly. His motto: 'Lithium battery, I love you' is 'a lifelong mission, not a slogan'.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as the first engineer in China to do lithium-battery safety research, some 40 years ago; EVE also funds a named 'EVE Energy Chair Professor' at his alma mater Wuhan University.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is EVE's board office / IR (board secretary Jiang Min per company IR page). Chinese-language outreach advisable. Company says it was founded 2001 (Forbes says 2000).

name: Ray Davis
current_role: Managing Partner, Majority Owner and Board Chairman, Texas Rangers; Chairman & CEO, Avatar Investments L.P.
profile: Born 1941 in Overton, Texas, Davis co-founded pipeline giant Energy Transfer with Kelcy Warren in the mid-1990s and was co-CEO until retiring in 2007 (left the board 2022). He now runs family investment firm Avatar Investments in Dallas and is managing partner of the Texas Rangers, which his group bought in 2010 and which won the 2023 World Series.
interesting_fact: Under his ownership the Rangers won the first World Series title in the franchise's 63-year history (2023) and opened the $1.25B retractable-roof Globe Life Field in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He received the Navy SEAL Foundation's 'Fire in the Gut' Award in 2024 and the BENS Eisenhower Award in 2017; his listed interests are ranching, bird hunting and reading.
notes: Famously press-shy ('doesn't grant interviews'; called his 2015 Dallas Morning News interview possibly his last). Best route is via Texas Rangers communications. Energy Transfer roots make him relevant to the energy angle.

name: Francois Perrodo
current_role: Chairman, Perenco (Franco-British independent oil & gas producer)
profile: French businessman (b. 1977, Singapore) who chairs Perenco, the oil and gas company founded by his late father Hubert, which specialises in extending the life of mature fields the majors have left. The family (with mother Carrie) also owns Bordeaux wine estates such as Chateau Labegorce and is diversifying via its London family office BNF Capital and PE firm Perwyn.
interesting_fact: A serious amateur endurance racer and car collector: he races for AF Corse at Le Mans/ELMS and owns a Ferrari 250 GTO (bought in 2016 for ~$56.4m) plus several McLaren F1s and the only privately owned Toyota TS020 Le Mans car.
deep_cut_fact: He read physics at St Peter's College, Oxford, where he captained the University polo team in 1999, then earned an engineering degree from the French petroleum school IFP School (2002) and an INSEAD MBA in Singapore, his birthplace.
notes: Private; best route is Perenco's media agency Celicourt. His Instagram (fanchracing) covers cars/racing - motorsport is a good rapport hook. Note: Sunday Times entry is shared with mother Carrie Perrodo.

name: Americo Amorim
profile: Américo Amorim (1934-2017), Portugal's richest man at his death, built the family cork business Corticeira Amorim into the world's largest cork producer and held energy (Galp) and banking interests. He died on 13 July 2017. His daughter Paula Amorim now leads the family's interests.
notes: Deceased 13 July 2017 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Am%C3%A9rico_Amorim ; AP via https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/americo-amorim-thought-portugals-richest-man-dies-48614152). Energy-related successor is Paula Amorim (Galp chair).

name: Zhang Hong
current_role: Co-owner, with her husband Lin Jianhua (chairman), of Hangzhou First Applied Material Co. (Fu Si Te, SSE: 603806)
profile: Zhang Hong appears on the Hurun lists jointly with her husband Lin Jianhua as the couple behind Hangzhou First Applied Material (福斯特). The company was founded in 2003 and is the world's largest maker of EVA encapsulant film for solar modules. Lin is chairman and controlling shareholder; Zhang has no public executive role at the company.
interesting_fact: First Applied Material was the lead drafter of China's national standards for EVA and co-extruded encapsulant film used in solar modules (GB/T 29848, GB/T 45939).
notes: Very private, with no individual public profile; Hurun lists the wealth as '林建华、张虹夫妇' (2022 list, No. 83). Outreach would go to the company's securities department (fst-zqb@firstpvm.com). Her husband Lin Jianhua is the public face.

name: Saban Cemil Kazanci
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Kazancı Holding; Chairman, Aksa Energy and Aksa Electricity
profile: Istanbul-born (1961) son of Ali Metin Kazancı, he started in the family's generator-making business and drove its growth into Aksa Energy (1997) and the broader Kazancı Holding (generators, power, gas and electricity distribution). Aksa Energy now runs gas and renewable plants in Turkey, Central Asia and Africa, and is widely ranked Turkey's richest person.
interesting_fact: Aksa Energy is the largest Turkish investor in Uzbekistan's power sector (1,220 MW after the 430 MW Talimercan plant) and is building out Africa, incl. an 825 MW Takoradi plant in Ghana.
deep_cut_fact: He has been awarded Uzbekistan's Order of Friendship (Dustlik), recognising Aksa's power-plant investments there.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Aksa Energy corporate communications (the press_email is listed as Corporate Communications) or Kazancı Holding general contact. Aksa IR site: https://www.aksainvestorrelations.com/investor-relations/contact.

name: Chen Weiliang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, MetaX Integrated Circuits (Shanghai) Co. (SSE STAR: 688802)
profile: Chen Weiliang is a GPU engineer who spent over a decade at AMD in China, latterly leading GPU/GPGPU SoC design, before co-founding MetaX with ex-AMD colleagues Peng Li and Yang Jian in Shanghai in September 2020. MetaX builds GPGPUs for AI training and inference; its December 2025 STAR Market IPO raised ~$593m and shares jumped ~700% on debut, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: MetaX shares soared roughly 693% on their December 2025 Shanghai debut, one of the biggest first-day pops of China's AI-chip IPO wave, turning the ex-AMD engineer into a billionaire overnight.
deep_cut_fact: MetaX was founded on 14 September 2020 and in 2024 alone filed more than 210 patent applications, with over 120 granted, 97% of them invention patents.
notes: Business@ is the company's general business inbox (not personal). Reports differ on AMD tenure (13-15 years). Data-center/AI angle: domestic Nvidia alternative under US export controls.

name: Todd Wanek
current_role: President & CEO, Ashley Furniture Industries (Arcadia, Wisconsin)
profile: Son of founder Ron Wanek, Todd Wanek has been CEO of Ashley Furniture since 2002, after running its Taiwan factory for five years and becoming COO in 1996. Ashley is the world's largest home furnishings manufacturer and North America's largest furniture store brand; his father remains chairman.
interesting_fact: As a teen and college student he worked odd jobs at Ashley, including on the production line and shipping furniture, and after college spent five years living in Asia managing the company's Taiwan factory.
deep_cut_fact: He was named a 2026 Tampa Bay Father of the Year by the National Father's Day Council (June 2026 luncheon benefiting Big Brothers Big Sisters). Ashley's Hope to Dream program, which he describes as starting to help local kids who needed a mattress, passed 200,000 donated beds.

public_contacts.value: Sharon Okaah, Flytevu - sharon.okaah@flytevu.com (campaign media contact on Ashley press release)

notes: Best route is Ashley corporate PR (publicrelations@ashleyfurniture.com). Hope to Dream bed-donation program is a good warm hook. Flytevu contact appears campaign-specific.

name: Mark Pears
current_role: Chief Executive, William Pears Group (since 1984); Chairman, Talisman Global Asset Management; trustee, Pears Foundation
profile: London property billionaire who has run the family's privately held William Pears Group, founded in 1952 by his grandfather Bernard and father Clive, since his father's death in 1984 when he was 21. He runs it with brothers Trevor and David; together they co-founded Pears Foundation (1992), one of the UK's largest family foundations.
interesting_fact: Appointed CBE in 2014 'for services to Business and to Charity'; he has been a trustee of the British Museum and the homelessness charity St Mungo's.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he co-founded Telereal, which became the UK's largest property outsourcing company, managing estates for British Telecom, the DWP, the DVLA and Royal Mail assets.
notes: Low public profile; family business is private. Foundation is invitation-only and asks not to receive funding requests; general foundation inbox is the only published route found.

name: Weili Dai
current_role: Co-founder & Board Director, Silicon Box (Singapore chiplet packaging); co-founder of Marvell Technology
profile: Shanghai-born, UC Berkeley CS grad Weili Dai co-founded Marvell Technology with Sehat Sutardja in 1995 and served as its president until 2016. Based in Las Vegas, she now invests in tech and real estate and has co-founded several startups, including AI firm MeetKai (2018) and Silicon Box (2021), which runs a ~$2B chiplet-packaging fab in Singapore aimed at AI customers.
interesting_fact: She is often described as the only woman co-founder of a major semiconductor company, and is reportedly the first woman to give the commencement address at UC Berkeley's engineering school, where Sutardja Dai Hall (home of CITRIS) bears her name.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Shanghai, before emigrating to the US at 17, Dai played semi-professional basketball.
notes: Also linked to DreamBig Semiconductor (co-founder/chair title reported) and inherited a stake in Alphawave (acquired by Qualcomm). Her husband and co-founder Sehat Sutardja died in 2024; treat sensitively. Avoid Marvell 2016 exit topic.

name: Pansy Ho
current_role: Group Executive Chairman and Managing Director, Shun Tak Holdings; co-chairperson, MGM China Holdings
profile: Daughter of the late Macau gaming magnate Stanley Ho, Pansy Ho runs Shun Tak Holdings (property, hotels and the Hong Kong-Macau TurboJET ferries) and holds stakes in MGM China and SJM Holdings. She made more than $1.5bn from MGM China's 2011 IPO and is now a prominent global tourism advocate, serving as a UN Tourism Ambassador.
interesting_fact: She dabbled in Hong Kong show business as an actress in the 1980s and helped promote her sister Josie Ho's acting and singing career.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 she founded the Global Tourism Economy Research Centre, which organises the annual Global Tourism Economy Forum in Macau; she was named a UNWTO Tourism Ambassador in 2018 and became the first official PATA Foundation Ambassador.
notes: Shun Tak has issued a statement warning about false AI-generated content about the group online, so check sources carefully. Her sister Maisy Ho, an executive director, died in April 2026; avoid that topic. Tourism (GTEF, UN Tourism) is the most natural hook. Shun Tak's site blocked scraping, so no email was verified.

name: Angela Bennett
current_role: Head of Wright Prospecting; principal of AMB Holdings (family investment company), Perth
profile: Australian iron-ore heiress whose wealth comes from Wright Prospecting's share of the Rio Tinto royalty negotiated by her father Peter Wright with Lang Hancock. She took over Wright Prospecting with her brother Michael after their father's 1985 death; in Dec 2025 sold a 15% stake in the Rhodes Ridge project to Mitsui in a ~$2B deal. Son Todd runs AMB Holdings.
interesting_fact: Her wealth stems from a royalty on every tonne of iron ore Rio Tinto mines in parts of Western Australia, negotiated decades ago by her father and Lang Hancock (father of Gina Rinehart).
deep_cut_fact: Ruah's 11-storey Perth shelter for homeless women and children is named the Angela Wright Bennett Centre after her donation; her foundation also gave $250,000 to autism research at the Kids Research Institute in 2015.
notes: Described as reclusive and rarely seen in public; no personal/public channels found. Angela Wright Bennett Foundation (program director David MacKenzie) funds climate/nature work; best route likely via AMB Holdings / foundation. Avoid the Rinehart litigation and family disputes in outreach.

name: Antti Herlin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, KONE Corporation (Helsinki)
profile: Finland's richest person and fourth-generation controlling owner of elevator/escalator maker KONE, which his great-grandfather invested in in 1924. He was KONE CEO 1996-2006 and has chaired the board since 2003. In April 2026 KONE agreed to combine with TK Elevator; Herlin is to remain chairman with over 50% of KONE's voting rights.
interesting_fact: KONE tests its elevators underground: in 2017 it expanded its Tytyri test facility to 350 m (1,150 ft) deep inside a working limestone mine in Lohja, Finland.
deep_cut_fact: Herlin owns a farm in Kirkkonummi, his birthplace west of Helsinki, where he raises Hereford and Aberdeen Angus beef cattle.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is KONE Global Head of Media Relations (Gia Forsman-Härkönen). KONE-TKE combination announced Apr 2026 (https://www.tkelevator.com/global-en/newsroom/press-releases/kone-and-tke-to-combine-creating-a-world-class-company-in-the-elevator-and-escalator-industry-197696.html) is a timely hook.

name: Anne Beaufour
current_role: Board member of Ipsen (representing family holding Highrock S.à r.l.); director of family holding Mayroy
profile: Granddaughter of Dr. Henri Beaufour, founder of the labs that became French pharma group Ipsen. After her father Albert died in 2000 she and brother Henri controlled ~52-57% of Ipsen via Luxembourg holdings (Mayroy, Highrock, Beech Tree). Switzerland-based; Henri died in Nov 2025, his stake passing to a foundation.
interesting_fact: Ipsen traces back to the Beaufour laboratories founded in 1929 by her grandfather; she holds a geology degree from the University of Paris-Sud (Orsay).
notes: Extremely private; declines comment via Ipsen spokesperson. Brother Henri Beaufour died 28 Nov 2025 - avoid as an outreach topic. Best route is Ipsen corporate communications.

name: Adarsh Hiremath
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Mercor (San Francisco)
profile: Co-founded Mercor in 2023 with high-school debate partners Brendan Foody and Surya Midha after dropping out of Harvard (CS) as a sophomore. Mercor recruits domain experts who train and evaluate models for the big AI labs; a $10B valuation in Oct 2025 made the three, then 22, the youngest self-made billionaires. He leads Mercor's technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: Mercor's annualized revenue went from $100M in March 2025 to $500M by September 2025, and the three cofounders each own roughly 22% of the company.
deep_cut_fact: At Bellarmine College Preparatory in San Jose he was one of the school's top debaters and a debate-team captain; even after leaving for Harvard, he and his cofounders came back to volunteer as Bellarmine debate coaches.
notes: No published press email found (support@mercor.com is a contractor support line only). CEO Brendan Foody is the usual public face; Hiremath has appeared on a Felicis fireside podcast. Avoid the March 2026 data-breach topic.

name: Brendan Foody
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mercor (San Francisco)
profile: In 2023 Brendan Foody cofounded Mercor with two Bellarmine high school friends, Adarsh Hiremath and Surya Midha. The company supplies expert contractors who help the big AI labs train and evaluate their models. A $10B valuation in October 2025 made the three of them the world's youngest self-made billionaires at 22. Mercor reported $500M in annualized revenue in September 2025.
interesting_fact: Foody and his cofounders were Thiel Fellows, and he left Georgetown to build Mercor. Mercor grew from about $100M in annualized revenue in March 2025 to $500M by September 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His first business was an 8th-grade donut stand. He bought Safeway donuts at $5 a dozen and sold them at his middle school for $2 each. When a rival started selling Chuck's donuts, he cut his price to $1 to run them out. After the principal banned the stand, he moved it about 20 feet off campus. He told the story on 20VC.
notes: He does a lot of podcasts (20VC, Conversations with Tyler) and would likely be receptive to a podcast invite. Mercor's site lists only a support@ inbox, with no press email. I could not confirm his personal X handle from an official source, so reach him via LinkedIn/X DM or Mercor's press page.

name: Surya Midha
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mercor (stepped back from COO role Oct 2025)
profile: San Jose-raised son of immigrants from New Delhi; left Georgetown's School of Foreign Service in 2023 to co-found Mercor with high-school friends Brendan Foody and Adarsh Hiremath. Mercor pays domain experts to train frontier AI models; its 2025-26 rounds ($10B then ~$20B valuation) made the trio the youngest self-made billionaires. Thiel Fellow (2024).
interesting_fact: Forbes named Midha, Foody and Hiremath (all 22) the world's youngest self-made billionaires in late 2025, younger than Zuckerberg was on his list debut; Midha is the youngest of the three.
deep_cut_fact: With partner Adarsh Hiremath he was on the first team ever to win all three national policy-debate titles (TOC, NDCA, NSDA), and was top speaker at TOC and NDCA; he was Bellarmine salutatorian (2021) and later interned for Eswar Prasad at Brookings. Lists F1, tea and Halloween as loves.
notes: Unusually accessible: publishes his personal Gmail on his own site (obfuscated as 'suryamidha [at] gmail [dot] com'). Good AI/data-labor angle for the podcast. Company X: @mercor.

name: Reimann family
current_role: Family owners of JAB Holding Company (Luxembourg-based investment vehicle; stakes in Keurig Dr Pepper, Coty, Peet's, Krispy Kreme, Panera etc.)
profile: German family descended from chemist Ludwig Reimann, who joined Johann Adam Benckiser's chemicals firm in the 1820s and married into the founding family. Albert Reimann Jr. expanded into consumer goods; the business became Reckitt Benckiser, and four of his adopted children own most of JAB, run by professional partners.
interesting_fact: JAB takes its name from the initials of Johann Adam Benckiser, the founder of the 19th-century chemicals firm the family inherited.
notes: Family entry listed only on Forbes 1996-2000, so it's unclear which members are meant. Very private family; JAB says it is run by professional partners. Best route is JAB's corporate contact form. Avoid the Nazi-era history unless relevant.

name: Ronald Owen Perelman
current_role: Chairman & CEO, MacAndrews & Forbes Incorporated (New York); Chairman of Carnegie Hall since 2015
profile: Wharton-trained financier who built MacAndrews & Forbes, his wholly owned holding company, through leveraged buyouts from 1978 on, most famously Revlon; holdings have included Deluxe/Vericast, SIGA Technologies and Scientific Games. Since 2020 he has sold assets and the firm reportedly now operates more like a family office.
interesting_fact: He has been chairman of Carnegie Hall since May 2015 and gave $75 million toward the performing arts center at the World Trade Center site, which bears his name.
deep_cut_fact: His first big deal came in 1961 as a Wharton freshman: with his father he bought Philadelphia's Esslinger Brewery for $800,000 and sold it three years later for a $1 million profit. By age 11 he was regularly sitting in on his father's Belmont Iron Works board meetings.
notes: Net worth fell sharply since 2018 peak; avoid wealth/litigation topics. Best route is MacAndrews & Forbes contact form. Carnegie Hall connection is a warm, positive angle.

profile: Taiwanese real estate developer, founder of Union Bank of Taiwan and of the Liberty Times newspaper group (incl. Taipei Times). Died 28 Nov 2015 in Taipei, aged 76.

name: Ernesto And Fabio Bertarelli
current_role: Ernesto Bertarelli: head of B-FLEXION (formerly Waypoint Capital), Geneva; co-chair, Bertarelli Foundation
profile: 1997 Forbes entry for father and son behind Swiss biotech Serono. Fabio Bertarelli died in 1998; son Ernesto (b. 1965) ran Serono from 1996, shifted it to biotech and sold it to Merck KGaA in 2007 for $13.3bn. He now invests the family fortune via B-FLEXION and co-chairs the Bertarelli Foundation with sister Dona.
interesting_fact: Ernesto founded sailing team Alinghi, which won the America's Cup in 2003 on its first attempt, bringing the Cup to Europe for the first time; he was the team's only Swiss national, serving as navigator.
deep_cut_fact: The name Alinghi comes from the Bertarelli family boats that raced around Porto Santo Stefano and Porto Ercole on Monte Argentario, where Ernesto spent his youth sailing.

Best route is probably B-FLEXION in Geneva or the Bertarelli Foundation, whose marine-conservation work has protected over 3m km2 of ocean since 2010.

name: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck Bros.
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Rainer) of the family stake in retailer Metro AG, held via the Meridian Stiftung structure
profile: Michael Schmidt-Ruthenbeck (b. 1942) and his brother Rainer are sons of Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck, who co-founded the German cash-and-carry wholesaler Metro in 1963/64. The family has held a large minority stake in Metro AG (about 16% around 2011), controlled through the Meridian Foundation vehicle, and is based in Duisburg. deep_cut_fact: The Karl Schmidt family of Duisburg merchants founded Stiftung Mercator in 1996 and named it after the cartographer Gerhard Mercator, who lived in Duisburg for decades; it is now one of Germany's largest private foundations, with a climate-resilient-society programme.
notes: Very private family; no personal web/social presence found. No death reported, but no recent public appearance found either (born 1942). The only institutional route is the family's Stiftung Mercator (Essen), which is not a personal office. Forbes entry dates from 1997.

profile: Entry appears to be a truncated 'Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck' (Germany, listed jointly with brother Michael). name: Thomas M Siebel
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, C3.ai (CEO until Sept 2025)
profile: Tom Siebel, an Oracle sales executive in the 1980s, founded CRM pioneer Siebel Systems in 1993 and sold it to Oracle for ~$5.8B in 2006. He founded enterprise-AI software firm C3.ai (originally C3 Energy, focused on smart-grid analytics), was CEO 2011-2025 and handed the CEO role to Stephen Ehikian in Sept 2025, remaining executive chairman.
interesting_fact: C3.ai began life in 2009 as C3 Energy, building analytics for utilities and the power grid -- a direct tie-in to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 his Thomas and Stacey Siebel Foundation started the Montana Meth Project, a graphic teen-prevention ad campaign; he testified about it to the U.S. Senate Finance Committee in Sept 2007, and Montana teen meth use reportedly fell 63% over four years.
notes: Stepped back from CEO role in 2025; still executive chairman. Siebel Energy Institute and Siebel Scholars are relevant to energy/data themes. Best route is via C3.ai PR.

name: William R. Berkley Jr
current_role: President & CEO (and, since June 2026, Chairman) of W. R. Berkley Corporation
profile: W. Robert Berkley Jr. is the son of William R. Berkley, who founded commercial insurer W. R. Berkley Corp. in 1967 with $2,500 while studying for his Harvard MBA. The son joined the company in 1997, became President & CEO in 2015 (per Wikipedia), and was named chairman after his father died in June 2026.

Robert Berkley Jr. IR contact per company releases: Karen A. Horvath, VP External Financial Communications, (203) 629-3000 (corporate line); no published email found.

name: Johan H. Andresen
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Ferd AS (Oslo)
profile: Fifth-generation head of the Andresen family business (Tiedemanns tobacco, bought 1849), which he renamed Ferd in 2001 and turned into a Nordic investment group (Elopak, Aibel, Swix, real estate, funds). CEO 1998-2012, chairman since 2012; in 2007 he passed most shares to daughters Katharina and Alexandra, and in Dec 2023 said his A-shares will go to a Ferd Foundation.

In 2009 he founded Ferd Social Entrepreneurs, and he helped launch the Norwegian Microfinance Initiative (2008). He has also chaired the Council on Ethics for Norway's Government Pension Fund Global.

name: Rodger O. Riney
current_role: Founder of Scottrade (sold to TD Ameritrade 2017); trustee, Paula and Rodger Riney Foundation; family office Lightchain Capital (St. Louis)
profile: Riney founded Scottsdale Securities in Scottsdale, Arizona in 1980 after brokerage commissions were deregulated, moved it to St. Louis and built it into discount broker Scottrade, sold to TD Ameritrade in 2017. He now focuses on philanthropy via his foundation and investing via family office Lightchain.
interesting_fact: After Scottrade launched online trading in 1996, its trade volume grew about 15% per month, compounded, for 39 straight months.
deep_cut_fact: His grandparents got him into the stock market by giving him 10 shares of a stock; he went on to earn a civil engineering degree and an MBA at the University of Missouri and interned at Edward Jones.

name: J.B. Pritzker
current_role: Governor of Illinois (re-elected to a third term on Nov 3, 2026)
profile: Hyatt hotel-fortune heir who co-founded Pritzker Group (private equity/venture) with brother Anthony and ran it until 2017. Elected Illinois governor in 2018, re-elected 2022 and won a rare third term in Nov 2026, beating Darren Bailey again; widely discussed as a possible 2028 presidential candidate.
interesting_fact: He is the first Democrat elected to three terms as Illinois governor and the first governor of either party to win a third term since Jim Thompson in the 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Before politics he founded 1871 (2012), the Merchandise Mart startup incubator run by the Chicagoland Entrepreneurial Center and named for the rebuilding after the 1871 Chicago Fire; it was later ranked the world's top private business incubator (UBI Global, 2019).

name: Julia Thiele-Schuerhoff
current_role: Member of the Supervisory Board, Knorr-Bremse AG; Chair of the Executive Board, Knorr-Bremse Global Care e.V.
profile: German lawyer and heiress of Heinz Hermann Thiele (d. 2021), who built rail/truck braking maker Knorr-Bremse and held stakes in Vossloh and Lufthansa. She has sat on Knorr-Bremse's supervisory board since 2016 and leads the company-affiliated charity Knorr-Bremse Global Care.
interesting_fact: She cofounded Knorr-Bremse Global Care in 2005 after the Indian Ocean tsunami; it funds partner projects worldwide in education, emergency relief and water/sanitation/hygiene.

notes: The Thiele family has long avoided publicity. The best route is Knorr-Bremse corporate communications (those contacts are for journalists only), or via Knorr-Bremse Global Care.

name: Phillip T. (Terry) Ragon
current_role: Founder, CEO and sole owner, InterSystems Corporation (Cambridge, MA)
profile: Terry Ragon, an MIT physics graduate, founded data-platform software company InterSystems in 1978; it still is wholly owned by him and has around $1B in annual sales, serving hospitals, banks and government health systems. With his wife Susan he funds the Ragon Institute of MGH, MIT and Harvard, endowed with a $200M gift in 2019, which works on HIV and other vaccines.
interesting_fact: After a 2009 trip to South Africa where they saw the toll of AIDS, Terry and Susan Ragon set up the Ragon Institute to pursue an HIV vaccine; they joined the Giving Pledge in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first programming job at Meditech, an early electronic medical records company, after admitting in the interview, 'I really don't know much about computers... But I play guitar.' There he learned MUMPS, the hospital programming language InterSystems was later built on.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews (the 2024 Forbes piece was described as a rare one). Best route is InterSystems PR. The Ragon Institute (ragoninstitute.org) is another angle.

name: Chao Chung-Hsin
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Jentech Precision Industrial Co., Ltd. (Taiwan, TPEx: 3653)
profile: Chao Chung-Hsin (also romanised Tsung-Hsin Chao) founded Jentech Precision with his younger brother Yung-Tsang in 1987 after learning mold-making on factory floors. Jentech grew from molds into heat spreaders, vapor-chamber lids and liquid-cooling modules for chips and AI servers, which drove its stock and his fortune; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: A high school dropout, he picked up industrial molding techniques by working in factories and started his own module business in 1978; Jentech's lids and liquid cooling now sit inside AI-server supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: His first company (1978) made molds for car audio systems, then a fast-growing Taiwanese sector; he studied at Hsin Chuang Senior High School and has been named one of Harvard Business Review's Top 100 Taiwan business leaders.
notes: Low-profile Taiwanese industrialist; little English-language press. Name appears as Chao Chung-Hsin (company site/Forbes) and Tsung-Hsin Chao (exchange filings). Best route is Jentech IR. Strong data-center angle (AI chip thermal management).

name: N.R. Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; principal of family office Catamaran Ventures
profile: Co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues and Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha; CEO 1981-2002, chairman to 2011, briefly returned 2013-14. Still a minority Infosys shareholder; his family office Catamaran (est. ~2009) invests in startups and, increasingly, manufacturing, AI and data-centre-related opportunities.
interesting_fact: He says being arrested and expelled in 1974 at a border town near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border while hitchhiking through Europe turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and wrote a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first company, Softronics, folded after about 18 months before he joined Patni Computer Systems.
notes: Family office Catamaran (run by ex-Infosys CFO MD Ranganath and president Deepak Padaki) publishes an office address in Bengaluru but no email; Catamaran's 2025 thesis includes AI, data centres and precision manufacturing - relevant hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Frequently gives interviews/speeches in India.

name: Tu Huilong
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Haiya Group (Shenzhen) and Hong Kong Haiya Investment Ltd
profile: Tu Huilong (涂辉龙) heads Shenzhen-based Haiya Group, a private conglomerate in commercial real estate, shopping malls/department stores, urban complexes, cultural tourism, finance and hotels, with 42 subsidiaries and 38,000+ staff. A Hong Kong JP and long-serving CPPCC National Committee member (11th-14th).
interesting_fact: His flagship Haiya Mega Mall in Bao'an was western Shenzhen's first large commercial complex (~300,000 sqm, opened 2013) and hosted the world's first Burberry new-concept store.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2020 Two Sessions he proposed amending China's Property Law so residential, commercial and industrial land-use rights renew automatically, and pushed for Shenzhen-Zhongshan integration across the Pearl River Estuary.

name: Yuan Jiangtao
current_role: Co-founder, Director and General Manager, Shenzhen JLC Technology Group (JLC/JLCPCB, SZSE: 001232)
profile: Jiangxi-born (Duchang, Jiujiang) electronics engineer who in 2006 founded the predecessor of JLC, pioneering cheap, fast PCB prototyping for small orders; he added the LCSC components marketplace in 2012 and merged with the Ding brothers' volume-PCB business in 2021. JLC listed on the Shenzhen main board in Aug 2026; he is its largest shareholder (~35%).

notes: Chairman is Ding Hui; Yuan is GM. Nanchang University junior-college (dazhuan) graduate in mechatronics, 2000. JLC is known globally as JLCPCB/LCSC/EasyEDA, which is a good hook for data-center hardware. IR email is from the 2026 interim report summary.

name: Jeffrey Cheah

profile: Malaysian tycoon who in 1974 left a job as an accountant at an auto assembly plant to buy a near-mined-out tin-mining company, then turned the land into Sunway City. Sunway now spans property, healthcare (Sunway Healthcare IPO'd in March 2026), construction, education and more; his children Sarena, Adrian and Evan work in the group.

Sunway hosts annual media nights and is press-friendly; energy/infrastructure angle via Sunway's autonomous transport and electric aviation plans (Oct 2026).

name: Ursula Bechtolsheimer-Kipp
current_role: Chairwoman (board president), Tschuggen Hotel Group / Tschuggen Collection (since 2016; current status not reconfirmed)
profile: Heiress (b. 1951), only daughter of Massa department-store founder Karl-Heinz Kipp, whose property was leased to Metro. She inherited much of his fortune in 2017 and since 2016 chairs the family's Swiss luxury hotel group (Tschuggen Grand, Valsana, Carlton St. Moritz, Eden Roc Ascona). current_role: Founder and president, Bohemian Foundation (Fort Collins, Colorado)
profile: Granddaughter of Stryker Corp. founder Homer Stryker; her fortune comes from inherited Stryker stock. Based in Fort Collins, she founded the Bohemian Foundation in 2001 (music, community, global and civic programs), has given ~$225M to charity, redevelops downtown Fort Collins real estate and is a major Democratic donor.

name: Roger Samuelsson
current_role: Founder and majority owner (~68%), SHL Medical (Zug, Switzerland)
profile: Swedish entrepreneur who moved to Taiwan in 1988 and in 1989 co-founded SHL Group (now SHL Medical) with Martin Jelf; it grew into the world's largest maker of autoinjectors, supplying Novo Nordisk, Amgen, Pfizer and others. EQT holds roughly a third of the company. He also owns the 414-ft yacht Octopus, formerly Paul Allen's.
interesting_fact: He owns Octopus, the 414-foot explorer megayacht originally built for Microsoft cofounder Paul Allen.
deep_cut_fact: As a young amateur boxer, Samuelsson first visited Taiwan in 1983 out of curiosity to see where his boxing equipment was made; with a Swedish mechanical engineering degree he later returned to source merchandise for European importers before starting SHL.
notes: Press-shy; Forbes reports he declined multiple interview requests. Best route is SHL Medical communications (Carl Gillblad listed as media contact in releases).

name: John Caudwell
current_role: Investor and philanthropist; founder/chair of Caudwell Children and Caudwell LymeCo (ex-founder of Phones 4u)
profile: Stoke-raised entrepreneur who started wholesaling mobile phones with brother Brian in 1987, built Singlepoint (sold to Vodafone 2003) and Phones 4u, the UK's largest independent phone retailer, and sold out in 2006 and 2011. Now invests in property, fashion and other businesses and runs his charities; Giving Pledge signatory since 2013.

deep_cut_fact: Before phones he was an engineering apprentice-turned-foreman at Michelin, earning an HNC in mechanical engineering while running a corner shop and a mail-order clothing business for motorcyclists on the side; he later owned the F1 powerboat team Caudwell Racing (2012-14).
notes: Media-friendly, frequent interviewee (podcasts, speaker agencies). Best route is via Caudwell Children PR or his Caudwell office (caudwell.com). Keen long-distance cyclist; avoid Lyme-disease controversy angle.

current_role: Private investor; controlling shareholder of Aegean Baltic Bank and majority owner of PAOK BC (via Alpha Sports Group); ex-head of copper at Glencore
profile: Greek-British 'Telis' Mistakidis spent ~25 years at Marc Rich & Co./Glencore after six years trading metals at Cargill, rising to run Glencore's global copper business until 2018; the 2011 IPO made him a billionaire. He now invests in Greek banking (Piraeus, Aegean Baltic Bank), shipping (Union Maritime), real estate and sport.

profile: Second son of shipping magnate C.Y. Tung and younger brother of Hong Kong's first chief executive Tung Chee-hwa. name: Reed Hastings
current_role: Co-founder of Netflix (left board in 2026 after serving as chairman); majority owner of Powder Mountain ski resort, Utah
profile: Co-founded Netflix in 1997 after selling his first company, Pure Software, and turned it from DVD-by-mail into the dominant streaming service. Stepped down as co-CEO in 2023, became executive chairman, and in April 2026 said he would leave Netflix's board. Now focused on Powder Mountain (bought control in 2023) and education philanthropy; lifetime giving above $2bn.
interesting_fact: Before college he deferred Bowdoin for a year to keep selling Rainbow vacuum cleaners door to door, a summer job he said he liked; he then taught math in the Peace Corps in Swaziland.
deep_cut_fact: He has put more than $100m of his own capital into Powder Mountain, Utah, and in 2026 announced a further $157m for its private Powder Haven area, adding two new lifts for the 2026-27 season. The resort also has an outdoor art museum.
notes: Leaving Netflix's board as of summer 2026, so Powder Mountain is the likelier route. The Netflix newsroom lists only regional press contacts, so none is a direct line to him. Ties to the podcast topics: education philanthropy and real estate/resort development.

name: Schmidt-Ruthenbeck family
current_role: Founding family of Metro AG (Michael b.1942 and Rainer b.1941 Schmidt-Ruthenbeck); assets now largely held via the charitable Meridian Foundation
profile: Duisburg family behind wholesaler Metro, co-founded in 1963-64 by Wilhelm Schmidt-Ruthenbeck and his brother Ernst Schmidt; grandfather Karl Schmidt founded a Duisburg trading firm in 1923. Brothers Michael and Rainer held ~16% of Metro. In 2017 the Karl Schmidt family completed moving its business assets into the charitable Meridian Foundation, which funds Stiftung Mercator.
interesting_fact: The family transferred its entrepreneurial assets to charitable status: since 2017 the Meridian Foundation is sole shareholder of Stiftung Mercator GmbH (Essen) and funds it and Stiftung Mercator Switzerland.
deep_cut_fact: The family's foundation (registered 1996) is named after Duisburg cartographer Gerhard Mercator (1512-1594), whose maps and globes were prized in the Age of Discovery - a nod to the family's Duisburg roots.
notes: Listed as a family (Forbes 1996-2000). Individuals are Michael and Rainer Schmidt-Ruthenbeck (Wikipedia; alive per Wikipedia, ages ~84-85, not independently confirmed). Very private; only institutional route is Stiftung Mercator / Meridian Foundation. Family had a public rift in 2006 - avoid.

name: Irving, James, Arthur
notes: Family entry for K.C. Irving's sons (Irving Oil / J.D. Irving, New Brunswick). All three brothers have died: John E. 'Jack' Irving in 2010, Arthur Irving on May 13, 2024 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Irving), and James K. Irving on June 21, 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Irving).

name: John
profile: John E. 'Jack' Irving, youngest son of Irving Oil founder K.C. Irving (Forbes listed him jointly with brothers James and Arthur). Died July 21, 2010 in Saint John, New Brunswick, aged 78.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Irving; https://globalnews.ca/news/62776/n-b-business-magnate-jack-irving-dead-at-78/). Input name is only 'John'; identified via shared_with Irving brothers. Business interests passed to son John K.F. Irving.

name: H. Ross Perot, Sr.
profile: Founder of Electronic Data Systems (EDS) and Perot Systems; died July 9, 2019 in Dallas.
notes: Deceased (d. 2019-07-09), source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Perot. Son Ross Perot Jr. runs the family business (Perot Group/Hillwood).

name: T. Ananda Krishnan
notes: Died 28 November 2024 (aged 86). Malaysian tycoon, founder/chair of Usaha Tegas (Maxis, Astro). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ananda_Krishnan

name: Chen Shuhong
current_role: Director, Red Star Macalline Group; acting-in-concert shareholder with founder Che Jianxing
profile: Chen Shuhong is linked to Red Star Macalline, the Shanghai-based home-furnishing mall operator founded by Che Jianxing. Company filings list her as a board director and as a person acting in concert with Che and Red Star Holdings. Her own business profile is very thin in public sources.
interesting_fact: Red Star Macalline's announcements name Chen Shuhong, together with Che Jianxing, as an acting-in-concert party of controlling shareholder Red Star Holdings, and she sat on the company's fourth board of directors.
notes: An unverified report (ctol.digital) calls her Che Jianxing's wife and says she handled shareholder duties while he was detained; no authoritative source confirmed this. Very private, and the group is in a sensitive period, with shares frozen by courts in 2025. Any approach should go through the company.

name: Akira Mori
current_role: Chairman, Mori Trust Co., Ltd. and Mori Trust Holdings (reconfirmed in June 24, 2026 officer list)
profile: Born 1936 in Kyoto, son of Mori Building founder Taikichiro Mori. He split the family business with brother Minoru in 1999 and built Mori Trust into an owner of 100+ office buildings and hotels across Japan. Since 2016 his daughter Miwako Date is president/CEO, expanding overseas (e.g. ~50% of a Park Avenue tower for ~$700M in 2023).
interesting_fact: Mori Trust bought close to a 50% stake in a 45-story Park Avenue office tower in New York for about $700 million in 2023, part of a push to put ~20% of new investment overseas.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family real-estate business, he graduated from Keio University in 1960 and started his career at Yasuda Trust & Banking (now part of Mizuho Trust & Banking); he only formally joined Mori Building as an employee in 1972.
notes: Age ~90; day-to-day leadership is with daughter Miwako Date (President & CEO), who is the more realistic interview target. Mori Trust press releases go out via digitalpr.jp. Officer list: https://www.mori-trust.co.jp/assets/media/20260624_1.pdf

name: Hu Shuangmei
current_role: Co-founder and Vice President (per 2019 filing), GoerTek Inc. (SZSE: 002241)
profile: Hu Shuangmei co-founded GoerTek, the Weifang, Shandong acoustics/VR/AR components maker and major Apple/Meta supplier, in 2001 with her husband, chairman Jiang Bin. A Harbin Institute of Technology graduate, she has held management roles at the company and is listed as a vice president; her wealth is shared with Jiang Bin.
interesting_fact: She and Jiang Bin started GoerTek in 2001; the company grew from a microphone maker in Weifang into one of the world's largest makers of acoustic components and VR/AR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: A Harbin Institute of Technology graduate, she joined GoerTek in 2001 as manager of its marketing department and later led its operations leadership group before becoming vice president.
notes: Low public profile; husband Jiang Bin is the public face. Current (post-2025) title not re-verified. Route via GoerTek corporate contact.

name: Liang Zhaoxian
current_role: Chairman & President, Galanz Group (also chairman of Whirlpool China since 2021)
profile: Son of Galanz founder Liang Qingde, he joined the family firm in 1991 and took over as executive president in 2000, steering Galanz from a 1978 feather-products plant in Shunde/Foshan into one of the world's biggest microwave makers, then into air conditioners and small appliances. In 2021 Galanz took control of Whirlpool China, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: Galanz began in 1978 as a feather (duck down) products plant before pivoting to microwave ovens; it now makes roughly half of the world's microwaves.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Galanz he graduated from South China Institute of Technology (now SCUT) in 1987 and that same year founded his own international trading company in Hong Kong, Zhanbang Enterprise (展邦企业); he later took MBA courses in Hong Kong in 1990.
notes: Press email is Galanz Americas' Marketing/PR contact (US subsidiary), not the Foshan HQ. Whirlpool China (惠而浦中国, SSE 600983) is a listed vehicle with a board secretary/IR route. Title is reported variously as chairman/president/CEO.

name: Samvel Karapetyan
current_role: Founder/president, Tashir Group (Russia/Armenia); leader of Armenia's 'Strong Armenia' party
profile: Armenian-born developer who moved to Russia in the 1990s, ran Kaluga supplier Kalugaglavsnab (a Gazprom subcontractor) and founded Tashir Group in 1999 - shopping centers, Moscow construction, and Electric Networks of Armenia. In 2026 he was Strong Armenia's PM candidate while under house arrest in Armenia.
interesting_fact: Tashir Group owns Electric Networks of Armenia, the country's power distributor, and in 2021 he announced plans to invest about $600M in Armenia's energy sector.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer: he graduated from the mechanical engineering faculty of Yerevan Polytechnic Institute in 1986. Through the Tashir Charitable Foundation (2000) he paid ~$2M toward the Vardenis-Martakert highway in 2013.
notes: Politically exposed: detained mid-2025 in Armenia, then under house arrest during 2026 (charges disputed; extended July 2026 per ARKA). He said he would not return to Russia. Route via Tashir press service; outreach may be sensitive. Forbes says his hometown Kalinino was renamed Tashir.

name: Anna Katharina Viessmann
current_role: Non-executive board member, Viessmann family holding (Viessmann Generations Group)
profile: Fourth-generation heir of Viessmann, the heating/cooling maker founded by great-grandfather Johann Viessmann in 1917. The family sold the Climate Solutions (heat pump) business to Carrier in 2023 for EUR 12B; proceeds now sit in Viessmann Generations Group, led by her brother Max. She sits on the family holding's board as a non-executive member.
interesting_fact: When the Viessmann Family Holding was created in 2019, she joined its board as a non-executive member alongside father Martin Viessmann (president) and outside directors from Flick Gocke Schaumburg and Dr. Oetker.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's in International Cultural and Business Studies from the University of Passau and a master's in Corporate Management and Economics from Zeppelin University, Friedrichshafen.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Viessmann Generations Group communications. Energy angle: family sold its heat-pump business to Carrier. Deep-cut fact is only from Forbes facts (no more obscure sourced detail found).

name: Ronald McAulay
current_role: Private investor; Kadoorie-family shareholder in CLP Holdings (retired from CLP board 2016 and HKSH board 2017)
profile: Glasgow-educated Scottish chartered accountant who married into Hong Kong's Kadoorie family (wife Rita is Sir Michael Kadoorie's sister). He sat on the CLP Holdings board from 1968 and Hongkong & Shanghai Hotels (Peninsula) from 1972. His fortune derives mainly from a roughly 10% CLP stake held via family trusts.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of CLP, Hong Kong's largest power utility, in 1968 at age 32 and stayed nearly half a century until 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond power and hotels, McAulay was an Honorary Trustee of the Tate Foundation in London, the fundraising arm of the Tate galleries, per HKSH's 2015 annual report.
notes: About 90 years old and very private, with no public social media. No death reported; Forbes still listed him in 2026. Son Andrew McAulay chairs Kadoorie Farm and Botanic Garden. Any approach would go via Sir Elly Kadoorie & Sons (Kadoorie family office), but I found no published contact.

name: Joesley Batista
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of J&F (holding company of JBS); slated chairman of J&F board after 2026 reorganization
profile: Joesley Batista and brother Wesley control J&F, the family holding behind JBS, one of the world's largest meat processors, which grew from father Jose Batista Sobrinho's butcher shop in Anapolis. He led JBS's international expansion (Swift 2007). In 2026 J&F was reorganized to fold in Eldorado, LHG Mining and Flora, with Joesley as chair.
interesting_fact: The empire began in 1953 as 'Casa de Carnes Mineira', a small butcher shop opened by his father 'Ze Mineiro' in Anapolis, Goias; today the brothers' J&F spans meat, pulp, mining, cosmetics, banking (PicPay) and energy.
deep_cut_fact: His father brought him into the family business at 16, when he was put in charge of a slaughterhouse with about 130 employees (J&F's own bio says his first role was manager at Flora Cosmeticos).

public_contacts.value: FSB Comunicacao (JBS Brasil corporate press): jbs@fsb.com.br

notes: Controversial past (2017 plea deal/bribery case, $3.2bn leniency fine); avoid in outreach. Route via J&F/JBS corporate press. Note: sources disagree on his first job (slaughterhouse manager vs. Flora manager).

name: Miao Hangen
current_role: Chairman & general manager, Jiangsu Eastern Shenghong (000301.SZ); chairman of parent Shenghong Group
profile: Born 1965 in Shenghong village, Wujiang (Suzhou), Miao rose from a village silk-mill job to run the Shenghong sand-washing/dyeing works founded in 1992, then built Shenghong Group into a textiles-to-petrochemicals giant. Eastern Shenghong now spans polyester fibres, a large Lianyungang refining/petrochemical complex and new materials; the group broke ground on a $4.2bn energy-storage battery plant in 2023.
interesting_fact: Eastern Shenghong has issued global depositary receipts listed in Switzerland (SIX Swiss Exchange), giving a Suzhou textile-born company a European capital-markets listing.
deep_cut_fact: After failing the gaokao in the early 1980s he joined the village silk factory for 30 yuan a month, working as accountant and storekeeper; at 27 he was made head of the new Shenghong sand-washing plant, whose early hit was a 'palm-print' (手掌花) fabric effect.
notes: Wife Zhu Hongmei is co-owner per Hurun. IR email is from the 2026 annual report summary (board secretary Wang Jun). Low international media profile; approach via IR/board secretary office, ideally in Chinese.

name: Kwak Dong-shin
current_role: Chairman & CEO and largest shareholder, Hanmi Semiconductor (promoted to chairman Dec 2024)
profile: Son of Hanmi founder Kwak Noh-kwon (an ex-Motorola Korea engineer), he joined the Incheon chip-packaging equipment maker in 1998 and has run it since 2007. He spearheaded its thermal-compression (TC) bonders, now the leading tool for stacking HBM memory for Nvidia AI GPUs, and supplies SK hynix, Micron and others. Also holds a stake in HPSP.
interesting_fact: He has argued publicly that Hanmi's TC bonders are sufficient for HBM4 and HBM5, pushing back on the industry shift to hybrid bonding (which he says costs over 2x as much per unit); Nvidia's Blackwell is built using Hanmi TC bonders.
deep_cut_fact: Hanmi's bet on HBM-style stacking long predates the AI boom: its 'TSV Dual Stacking TC Bonder' won Korea's IR52 Jang Young-sil Award back in 2017. On the day he was named chairman (Dec 16, 2024) he personally unveiled the new 'TC Bonder Griffin Super Bonding Head'.
notes: No published press/IR email found on Hanmi's English site (has an IR&PR section, mostly Korean). Gives media remarks at Computex and SEMICON; a trade-show booth or Korean press channel is the likeliest route. Name also romanized Gwak Dong-shin.

name: Ron Mannix
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Coril Holdings Ltd. (Calgary family asset manager); ownership passed to sons Stephen and Michael Mannix from 2016
profile: Third-generation heir of Calgary's Mannix construction/energy dynasty (founded 1898). With brother Fred he ran the Mancal/Loram group (Manalta Coal, Pembina Pipeline) and sold most energy assets for over C$2bn in 1997; Ron then founded Coril Holdings (rail equipment, real estate, health investments) and is a major Alberta arts and children's-development philanthropist.
interesting_fact: The Mannix family firms helped build the St. Lawrence Seaway, the Trans-Canada Highway, Toronto and Montreal subways and the Cold War DEW Line radar stations; Ron joined Manalta Coal in 1973 and was its president by 1974.
deep_cut_fact: A keen music patron, he founded the National Music Centre Foundation (Calgary's Studio Bell) and formerly chaired the Cantos Music Foundation and the Calgary International Organ Festival and Competition; he also founded the Norlien Foundation.
notes: Born 1948; very private. Hurun's 'Mancal' label belongs more to brother Fred Mannix (Mancal Group); Ron's vehicle is Coril. No longer listed on Coril's board (2026), sons run it. No death record found; most recent bio is JA Southern Alberta Hall of Fame (2021).

name: Victor Gradin
profile: Bahian economist and businessman who joined the Odebrecht group in 1974 at founder Norberto Odebrecht's invitation; his family became Odebrecht's second-largest shareholder (~20%). Died 26 May 2019 in Salvador, aged 86.
interesting_fact: Before joining Odebrecht he served as Bahia's state secretary of economic development (1963-1967) under governor Lomanto Junior.
notes: Deceased 26 May 2019 (sources: https://www.novacana.com/noticias/morre-86-anos-victor-gradin-empresario-grupo-odebrecht-270519 ; bnews.com.br obituary). Family's Odebrecht stake was later sold back to the Odebrechts after a long dispute. Not a podcast candidate.

name: Divyank Turakhia
current_role: Dubai-based tech entrepreneur and investor; founder and former CEO of Media.net, co-founder of Directi
profile: Mumbai-born programmer who co-founded web-hosting/domain group Directi with brother Bhavin in 1998 at age 16, then built contextual-ad network Media.net, sold in 2016 to a Chinese consortium for $900M, one of the largest ad-tech deals ever. Now based largely in Dubai, he invests and builds new ventures.
interesting_fact: He was named India's youngest billionaire three years running (2016-2018) and the youngest self-made Gulf billionaire in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started coding at age eight; a 2021 interview with domain investor Mike Mann was titled 'From Wing Walking to Billion-Dollar Exits', and Entrepreneur India profiled his passion for flying planes and scuba diving.
notes: Low public profile; no verified personal social accounts or published office email found. Some web profiles about him are aggregator/AI-written; current title unverified. Don't confuse with brother Bhavin (Zeta, Flock).

name: Leopoldo Del Pino Y Calvo Sotelo
current_role: Private investor; major Ferrovial shareholder via his holding company Siemprelara (Ferrovial director 2010-2016)
profile: One of the children of Rafael del Pino y Moreno, who founded construction and infrastructure group Ferrovial in 1952; brother of Ferrovial chairman Rafael del Pino. He sat on Ferrovial's board from 2010 to early 2016 and has gradually sold down a stake that once exceeded 8%, investing through his vehicle Siemprelara and SICAVs.
interesting_fact: His Ferrovial shares came from the family holding Portman Baela, which distributed 40.82% of Ferrovial's capital directly to the siblings' individual vehicles, his being Siemprelara.
deep_cut_fact: Through Siemprelara he created and presides over the Fundación Estrella de los Mares, whose stated aims include promoting Spanish history, including its famous navigators.
notes: Very private; no personal site or social accounts found. MarketScreener lists him as a director of the Spanish parking association (Asociacion Espanola de Aparcamientos y Garajes). The foundation is the only possible route but no published contact was found.

name: Maria Del Pino Y Calvo Soleto
current_role: Non-Executive Director of Ferrovial N.V. and President of the Fundación Rafael del Pino
profile: María del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is the eldest child of Ferrovial founder Rafael del Pino y Moreno (d. 2008) and holds about 8.7% of Ferrovial through her company Menosmares, S.L. She has sat on Ferrovial's board since 2006; her brother Rafael is executive chairman. Since 2000 she has also led the family's Fundación Rafael del Pino.
interesting_fact: Her father personally named her president of the Fundación Rafael del Pino when he created it in 2000. Its mission is to train future leaders, and it has since funded hundreds of 'Becas de Excelencia' scholarships for Spanish graduates.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business she interned at the European Commission in Brussels, worked in the International Relations Secretariat of Spain's UCD party from 1979, and later volunteered with the development NGO Codespa until 2000. She studied economics at Universidad Complutense and holds an IESE PDD.
notes: The input spells her name 'Calvo Soleto'; the correct spelling is Calvo-Sotelo. She is very private and has reportedly given only one interview. The best route is through the Fundación Rafael del Pino (general info email), which runs economics and energy-policy events. She also sits on the Princess of Asturias Foundation's board of trustees.

name: Prem Watsa
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Fairfax Financial Holdings (Toronto)
profile: Hyderabad-born, IIT Madras-trained engineer who emigrated to Canada in 1972, earned an MBA at Western's Ivey school, worked at Confederation Life, and in 1985 took control of what became Fairfax Financial, a value-investing insurance and investment holding company often compared to Berkshire Hathaway. He still runs Fairfax, which reported $1.39B Q2 2026 net earnings.
interesting_fact: Often called 'Canada's Warren Buffett', he has led Fairfax since 1985 with a value-investing approach and still delivers the opening remarks at its annual meeting (the 41st was held in April 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He arrived in London, Ontario with just 8 rupees and paid his way through his Ivey MBA by selling air conditioners and furnaces; in 2017 he became Huron University College's first-ever Chancellor.

public_contacts.value: John Varnell, VP Corporate Development, Fairfax Financial (published contact on press releases; phone +1 416-367-4941)

notes: No personal social accounts. Fairfax press releases list John Varnell as the contact (phone only, no email published). Watsa writes a widely read annual shareholder letter, a good hook for outreach.

name: Sergey Katsiev
current_role: Co-owner and board member (former president, until 2015), Megapolis tobacco/FMCG distribution group, Russia
profile: Russian who founded tobacco distributor Megapolis in 1998 after running Igor Kesaev's Mercury Tobacco Corporation from 1993; the firms merged in 2006 to form Russia's largest tobacco distributor (Philip Morris and JTI took 20% each in 2013). He stepped down as president in 2015 but remains a shareholder; in 2022 he and partners bought Imperial Brands' Russian assets.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Katsiev and his partners bought the Russian business of British tobacco company Imperial Brands as Western firms exited Russia.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering business he studied at the Moscow Institute of International Relations (MGIMO) and, after the Soviet collapse, worked at a Russian government trade mission in the Netherlands.
notes: Extremely private; did not answer calls from Kommersant even when he stepped down (https://www.kommersant.ru/doc/2714727). No published personal or press contact found; Megapolis is part of Igor Kesaev's Mercury group. Russia-based tobacco business - consider sanctions/reputational context before outreach.

name: Mikheil Lomtadze
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman of the Management Board, Kaspi.kz
profile: Georgian-born Harvard MBA who joined Kaspi via private equity firm Baring Vostok, which invested in the Kazakh bank in 2006. As CEO he rebranded it Kaspi in 2011 and turned it into a super-app combining payments, marketplace and fintech; Kaspi listed in London (2020) and on Nasdaq (2024).
interesting_fact: Before Kaspi he was a partner at Baring Vostok, Russia's largest private equity fund; Kaspi's leadership team pointedly contained no career bankers when it pivoted to technology.
deep_cut_fact: While still a student in Tbilisi he founded his own audit and consulting firm, Georgia Consulting Group Audit (1995), which he later sold.

public_contacts.value: Fintech Leaders interview (Miguel Armaza) - prior podcast appearance

notes: Also spelled Mikhail Lomtadze. Does occasional long-form interviews (McKinsey, Fintech Leaders) - podcast-friendly. Best route: Kaspi IR.

name: Eric Duval
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Groupe Duval (Paris-area family real estate group; CEO is his daughter Pauline Boucon Duval)
profile: French entrepreneur who founded Groupe Duval in 1994 as a real estate developer. It grew into a family group of about 6,000 staff in 20 countries and roughly €1bn in revenue, spanning development, retail parks, Odalys tourist residences and golf. His children now run day-to-day operations, and the group is expanding in Africa and into energy-transition services.
interesting_fact: Groupe Duval bought Odalys in 2000, UGolf in 2009 and Bluegreen in 2022, which made it Europe's leading golf operator and the world's 5th largest.
deep_cut_fact: The group marked its 30th anniversary on 19 September 2024 at the Palais Brongniart (the old Paris stock exchange). Its plans include renewable energy and energy-transition services.
notes: Florian Silnicki is listed as Directeur de la Communication and Philippine Barneville as Responsable de la communication. The group's renewable-energy activities fit the podcast angle. Low personal media profile.

name: S Gopalakrishnan
current_role: Chairman, Axilor Ventures (Bengaluru seed fund/accelerator); co-founder of Infosys; Chair, IISc Council
profile: Senapathy 'Kris' Gopalakrishnan co-founded Infosys in 1981 and was its CEO/MD (2007-2011) and vice chairman (2011-2014). He now backs startups through Axilor Ventures and family investment arm Pratithi, and funds neuroscience and research through the Pratiksha Trust, while chairing IISc's Council and several Indian government innovation bodies.
interesting_fact: He gave Rs 2.25 billion to build the Centre for Brain Research at IISc, described as the largest individual gift the institute has received, and funds a cellular-level brain-mapping centre at IIT Madras.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a physicist, earning an M.Sc. in Physics (1977) before an M.Tech in Computer Science (1979) at IIT Madras, and his first job was as a software engineer at Patni Computer Systems in Mumbai in 1979, where he met the future Infosys founding team.
notes: Goes by 'Kris'. Very active public speaker on AI, deep tech and startups (CII, IISc); good podcast fit. Axilor's general inbox is the best published route; the Pratiksha Trust site lists no email.

name: NR Narayana Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of family investment firm Catamaran Ventures
profile: N.R. Narayana Murthy (b. 1946) co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues, seeded by Rs 10,000 from his wife Sudha Murty, and built it into one of India's largest IT services companies, serving as CEO and chairman. Often called the father of the Indian IT sector, he is now Chairman Emeritus and invests via Catamaran Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has said being arrested and expelled near the Yugoslav-Bulgarian border in 1974, while hitchhiking back from Europe, turned him from a 'confused leftist' into a 'compassionate capitalist'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed a BASIC interpreter for ECIL; his first startup, Softronics, folded after about a year and a half.
notes: Infosys press email reaches the company, not him directly; Catamaran Ventures (his family office, catamaranventures.com) may be a more direct route but no published email was verified. Gives frequent public lectures and interviews, often on work ethic and entrepreneurship.

name: Peter P Gassner
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Veeva Systems
profile: Software engineer who worked at IBM's Silicon Valley Lab, led PeopleTools at PeopleSoft and ran technology at Salesforce before co-founding Veeva Systems in 2007. Veeva builds cloud software for the life-sciences industry and went public in 2013; Gassner remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Under Gassner, Veeva became a public benefit corporation in 2021, which made it the first public company to convert to a PBC.
deep_cut_fact: Gassner grew up in Portland, Oregon, the son of Swiss immigrants (his father had a machine shop). He earned a computer science degree from Oregon State University in 1989, and his first internship was at IBM.
notes: Low public profile but gives occasional founder interviews (Sramana Mitra, SaaStr) on vertical SaaS. The PBC claim is from Wikipedia; check it before using. Best route is Veeva PR.

name: Vince McMahon
current_role: Founder of 14TH & I, a private sports, media and entertainment investment firm (Connecticut)
profile: Former WWE chairman and CEO. He bought his father's wrestling company in 1982 and built WWE into a global media business, which merged with UFC to form TKO in 2023. He resigned from TKO in January 2024 and in 2025 launched 14TH & I, named for the D.C. intersection where his father's Capitol Wrestling Corp. was based.
