interesting_fact: McMahon was behind the 1976 Muhammad Ali vs. Antonio Inoki match, years before he took over his father's promotion.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from East Carolina University in 1968 and working as a traveling salesman, he became a ring announcer in 1969. In 1971 he promoted his first card, in a small territory in Maine.
notes: Sensitive: he resigned from TKO in January 2024 amid a lawsuit alleging sexual misconduct, and in January 2025 he settled SEC charges over undisclosed payments (>$1.7m). Weigh reputational fit before any outreach. 14TH & I's site published no contact details; reported executives are Brad Blum (president) and David Spingarn (CIO), per https://wrestletalk.com/news/vince-mcmahon-new-company-wwe-exit-revealed/

name: Paul Georges Despature
current_role: Chairman of Edify (Despature family investment company); former chairman of Somfy's management board (1983-2014)
profile: Paul-Georges Despature is the patriarch of the French Despature family, which controls Somfy, the Cluses-based maker of motors and automation for blinds, shutters and gates. He ran Somfy as chairman of its management board from 1983 until the end of 2014, then moved to head the family investment arm Edify. His son Jean Guillaume Despature now chairs Somfy, which the family took private in 2022-23.
interesting_fact: The Despature family, which already owned the thermal-underwear brand Damart, bought Somfy in 1984 as a diversification into summer-season products; Somfy has since become a world leader in motorised blinds and the connected home.
deep_cut_fact: The name SOMFY is an acronym for 'Société d'Outillage et Mécanique du FaucignY', a 1969 spin-off of the Cluses precision-machining firm Carpano & Pons in the Arve valley, a region known for Swiss-watch part-making.

public_contacts.value: Agence Shan (Somfy press agency), 30 rue des Mathurins, 75008 Paris

notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Edify role per Somfy's December 2014 announcement (https://echanges.dila.gouv.fr/OPENDATA/AMF/ECO/2014/12/FCECO035465_20141222.pdf); check whether he still holds it. Somfy press route is the corporate one, not a personal office.

name: Raja Bagmane
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Bagmane Group (Bagmane Developers Pvt Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Bengaluru real-estate developer who founded Bagmane Group in 1996 and built it into one of the city's largest commercial/tech-park landlords (Bagmane Tech Park, Bagmane World Technology Center; ~30 mn sq ft operational). Blackstone took a minority stake in 2024, and the group sponsors Bagmane Prime Office REIT, which has listed in India. His sons Aditya and Shashank are directors.
interesting_fact: Bagmane Tech Park in C V Raman Nagar, launched in 2001, was one of Bengaluru's earliest IT parks; the group's portfolio is now hosted in a Blackstone-backed listed REIT.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. The published email is a general company enquiries inbox. A data-center/tech-park angle is relevant: Bagmane hosts big tech occupiers in Bengaluru. His sons may be easier to reach for a conversation.

name: Naveen Jindal
current_role: Chairman, Jindal Steel Ltd (formerly Jindal Steel & Power); BJP Member of Parliament (Lok Sabha) for Kurukshetra
profile: Naveen Jindal (b. 1970, Hisar), youngest son of O.P. Jindal, took over the group's Raigarh and Raipur steel operations in 1993 and built Jindal Steel & Power into a major steel, power and mining group. He is founding chancellor of O.P. Jindal Global University and, since 2024, a BJP MP; the group is now expanding Angul steel capacity and investing in nuclear and solar in Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: His 1990s court fight after hoisting the flag at his Raigarh factory led to the 2004 Supreme Court ruling that flying the Indian national flag on any day is part of citizens' freedom of expression.
deep_cut_fact: While earning his MBA at UT Dallas (1992) he served as Student Government VP then president and won Student Leader of the Year; the university's Naveen Jindal School of Management now bears his name. He is also a national-record skeet shooter in India.
notes: Highly public figure (industrialist + MP); active on X. Also captains the Jindal Panther polo team. Steer clear of the coal-block allocation case.

name: Nikolaus Knauf
current_role: Shareholder and longtime member/former chair of the shareholders' committee, Knauf Group (Iphofen, Germany)
profile: Born 1936, the eldest son of Knauf co-founder Alfons Knauf. From 1969 he co-ran the family plasterboard/building-materials group with cousin Baldwin Knauf, overseeing technology while it expanded across Europe, Russia and the CIS; he left management in 2008 for the shareholders' committee. Knauf remains fully family-owned (~EUR 15B sales).
interesting_fact: Knauf was founded in 1932 by brothers Alfons and Karl Knauf as a gypsum works in Perl on the Moselle before moving to Iphofen in Lower Franconia, where the family's Knauf-Museum (opened 1983) shows casts of great relief artworks.
deep_cut_fact: Within the cousin duo running Knauf, Nikolaus handled the technical side while Baldwin took administration; he has also served as a CSU councillor in the small municipality of Markt Einersheim near Iphofen and on the Kitzingen district council.

public_contacts.value: Gebr. Knauf KG, Corporate Communications, Iphofen (press-release contact)

notes: Aged ~90, very private, no personal channels. Was honorary consul of Russia in Nuremberg until March 2022 (Knauf's Russia business was a sensitive topic after 2022) -- avoid. Route via Knauf corporate communications.

name: GM Rao
current_role: Founder Chairman, GMR Group (infrastructure: airports, energy, highways, urban development)
profile: Grandhi Mallikarjuna Rao (b. 1950, Rajam, Andhra Pradesh) is a mechanical engineer who built GMR Group from a single jute mill bought in 1978 into one of India's largest infrastructure developers, running Delhi and Hyderabad airports plus energy and highway assets. He funded the move into power by selling his Vysya Bank stake; sons and family now run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He used the roughly Rs 3.4 billion from selling his entire ING Vysya Bank stake to fund GMR's entry into power and infrastructure; the group is also co-owner of IPL cricket team Delhi Capitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked as a shift engineer at a paper mill and then as a junior engineer in the Andhra Pradesh Public Works Department; he moved into commodities trading at his mother's insistence.
notes: Press email reported from GMR's media page (page returned 503 when re-checked; verify). Philanthropy via GMR Varalakshmi Foundation (est. 1991). Strong energy/infrastructure fit for the podcast.

name: Nirmal Kumar Minda
current_role: Chairman (Executive Chairman), UNO Minda Ltd; President of ASSOCHAM for 2025
profile: Second-generation head of UNO Minda (formerly Minda Industries), a Gurugram-based maker of auto switches, lighting, alloy wheels and EV components. He joined his father Shadilal's business in 1977 and ran it on his own after a 1996 split with his brother. He built it through Japanese and European joint ventures and moved from MD to Chairman in April 2025.
interesting_fact: The business goes back to 1958, when his father Shadilal Minda started importing ammeters from Japan. It moved to Delhi in 1962 to serve the tractor and motorcycle aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The group's first joint venture (1995) came from a quality push by Maruti. Minda asked the carmaker to help find a Japanese partner for switches, which led to Toyota-group supplier Tokai Rika. Separately, he and his wife Suman run Samarth-Jyoti, which operates two schools, a 100-bed hospital and 18 village centres.
notes: The Samarth-Jyoti detail comes from an India CSR profile (https://indiacsr.in/biography-nirmal-kumar-minda-president-assocham-2025/). EV components and ASSOCHAM policy work are possible podcast angles. Sources differ on his exact title (Chairman vs Chairman & MD).

name: Jonathan Burrell
current_role: CEO, Burrell Family Office; director of Garmin Ltd. (since 2018); president of the Burrell family charitable foundation
profile: Jonathan C. Burrell is the son of Garmin cofounder Gary Burrell (d. 2019), and his wealth comes from the family's Garmin stake. He formerly helped lead Garmin's engineering department, now runs the Burrell Family Office and sits on Garmin's board. He invests in financial, technology and clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on 35 issued and pending U.S. patents, many of them owned by Garmin.
deep_cut_fact: He has a BS in mechanical engineering from Wichita State University and was a hands-on Garmin engineering leader before joining the board. Garmin's 2018 proxy says he invests in clean-energy businesses, which ties in with the podcast's energy theme.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Garmin contacts are company-level; he is an independent director, not an executive.

name: Jacob Brunsborg
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Lars Larsen Group (owner of JYSK)
profile: Son of JYSK founder Lars Larsen; became chairman of Lars Larsen Group (JYSK, ILVA, Actona, investments) in June 2019 shortly before his father's death. Rose through JYSK as head of purchasing and brand director, then did business development, entrepreneurship and board work; now steers the group's strategy, including investments in securities, property and green energy.
interesting_fact: He carries his mother's surname rather than Larsen, and his father reportedly warned him against aiming for the JYSK CEO job, insisting management be chosen on merit while ownership stays in the family.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1993 as a trainee ('elev') in the JYSK store on Grenåvej in Aarhus, and did his military service with the Royal Danish Life Guards (Dronningens Livregiment).

public_contacts.value: Press contact: Communications Director Lise Brøndum Wemmelund via Lars Larsen Group press room

notes: Rarely gives interviews and says he is less outgoing than his father (lex.dk). Group invests in green energy, a possible hook. Approach via the group's Communications Director.

name: Mette Brunsborg
current_role: Board member, Lars Larsen Group A/S (owner of JYSK) and Lars Larsens JYSK Fond
profile: Daughter of JYSK founder Lars Larsen (d. 2019). She and her brother Jacob Brunsborg (chairman) control Lars Larsen Group, the Silkeborg holding company that owns the JYSK home-furnishings chain plus BOLIA, ILVA, SOFACOMPANY and other investments. She joined the family foundation's board in 2019, taking her mother Kris Brunsborg's seat.
interesting_fact: When she joined the board of Lars Larsens JYSK Fond in 2019, she took the seat of her mother, Kris Brunsborg. The foundation's first gift under the new board was DKK 1m to Børns Vilkår to help children whose parents have mental illness.
deep_cut_fact: Away from the boardroom she runs her own farm (driver sit eget landbrug), according to the Danish encyclopedia Lex.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Brother Jacob Brunsborg is the family's public face. In July 2026 Lars Larsen Group announced a new renewable-energy agreement, which could be an angle for an energy podcast. Best route is Lars Larsen Group press.

name: Maha Vajiralongkorn Phra Vajiraklaochaoyuhua
current_role: King of Thailand (Rama X), since 2016
profile: Vajiralongkorn is the reigning King of Thailand, the only son of King Bhumibol Adulyadej; he took the throne in 2016 and was crowned in 2019. Hurun counts his wealth through his holdings in Siam Commercial Bank, assets once managed by the Crown Property Bureau that he took into direct ownership after his accession.
interesting_fact: He is a graduate of Australia's Royal Military College, Duntroon, and qualified as both a military fast-jet pilot and a commercial airline pilot.
deep_cut_fact: He was once known as the 'Football Prince': he played forward and later centre-back at Chitralada School, Millfield School in Somerset and Duntroon. Since 1978 he has personally handed out degrees at Rajabhat University commencements every year, estimated at over 2.1 million degrees.
notes: Reigning monarch, not a realistic podcast guest. Thailand's strict lese-majeste laws make any outreach or commentary sensitive. The only channel is formal, via the Bureau of the Royal Household. No personal contacts are published.

name: An Sumei
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Lin Lairong) of Zhongxing Group (众兴集团), controlling shareholder of Dazhong Mining (SZSE: 001203)
profile: An Sumei and her husband Lin Lairong are the actual controllers of Zhongxing Group, which holds ~41% of Inner Mongolia-based Dazhong Mining, listed in Shenzhen in May 2021. Dazhong mines and processes iron ore (iron concentrate, pellets, sulphuric acid) and has been adding spodumene/lithium resources. She keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Hurun's 'Zhongxing' is 众兴集团 (Zhongxing Group), not telecom maker ZTE; filings list Lin Lairong and An Sumei as joint actual controllers of Dazhong Mining, whose product line now includes spodumene (lithium) ore alongside iron concentrate.
notes: Very private; virtually no English-language coverage. Best route is via Dazhong Mining's board secretary office (IR email from annual report). Company chairman is Niu Guofeng; lithium pivot could be a hook for an energy podcast.

name: Madhusudhan Agarwal
current_role: Co-owner/director, Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd (Delhi branch of the Haldiram's family)
profile: Madhusudan Agarwal and his brother Manohar Lal Agarwal, grandsons of founder Ganga Bishan 'Haldiram' Agarwal (sons of Moolchand), built the Delhi-based Haldiram's snacks business. After the 2022-25 merger of the Delhi and Nagpur packaged-snacks units into Haldiram Snacks Food, the Delhi brothers hold ~56%; Temasek bought a ~9% stake in 2025 at a ~$10bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a 1937 bhujia shop in Bikaner, Rajasthan; the merged company was valued at nearly US$10bn when Singapore's Temasek bought in in 2025.
notes: Family is famously interview-shy (Financial Express called the brothers 'elusive'). Most coverage focuses on Manohar Lal; very little on Madhusudan personally. Best route is via the company's corporate communications.

name: Brad Garlinghouse
current_role: CEO, Ripple (Ripple Labs)
profile: Kansas-born executive (b. 1971) who held senior roles at @Home, Dialpad, Yahoo (SVP running Homepage, Flickr, Mail, Messenger) and AOL, then ran Hightail (ex-YouSendIt). Joined Ripple as COO in 2015 and became CEO around end-2016; his wealth comes from Ripple equity and XRP. He continues to lead Ripple's global payments, custody and RLUSD stablecoin push.
interesting_fact: As a Yahoo SVP in 2006 he wrote the internal 'Peanut Butter Manifesto' memo, warning Yahoo was spreading itself too thin like peanut butter; it leaked to the Wall Street Journal and became a Silicon Valley strategy classic.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his interest in technology began growing up in Kansas when his dad brought home a Tandy TRS-80 computer.
notes: Very media-accessible, active on X (@bgarlinghouse) and frequent podcast guest. Best route is Ripple's press team form. Avoid the long SEC-litigation saga as a hook.

name: Dmitry Pumpansky
current_role: Former owner and chairman of TMK (Russian steel-pipe maker); left TMK's board and beneficial ownership in March 2022
profile: Russian industrialist (b. 1964, usually spelled Dmitry Pumpyansky), graduate of the Ural Polytechnic Institute. Started as a metals trader, ran pipe plants including Sinarsky, joined TMK in 2002 and by 2006 owned 100% of it, building one of the world's largest makers of oil-and-gas tubulars. Said to have exited TMK in 2022; reported living in Geneva.
interesting_fact: After co-buying TMK with Sergei Popov and Andrey Melnichenko, he bought both partners out in 2006 to become its sole owner.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 he earned a Doctor of Technical Sciences degree with a dissertation on steels, alloys and production technologies for next-generation OCTG and specialty pipes, adding to his earlier engineering candidate degree and economics doctorate.
notes: Name in input is a variant spelling of Pumpyansky. Sanctioned by UK (2022) and named on the US CAATSA list; EU sanctions annulled by the EU General Court on appeal. Outreach carries compliance/reputational risk; no published personal or office contact found.

name: Rajendrakumar Shivkisan Agrawal
current_role: Director, Haldiram Foods International (Nagpur Haldiram's) and related family companies; shareholder in merged Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd
profile: Member of the Nagpur branch of the Haldiram's snack-food family; Indian company registries list him as a director of Haldiram Foods International and some 27 related companies. The family's fortune jumped after the Delhi and Nagpur businesses merged in 2025 into Haldiram Snacks Food (Nagpur ~44%) and Temasek, Alpha Wave and IHC bought stakes at a reported ~$10B valuation.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal's bhujia shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur arm was built by Shivkisan Agrawal, who introduced kaju katli to Nagpur. Hurun named Rajendrakumar one of India's biggest wealth gainers in its 2026 Global Rich List.
notes: Almost no public profile, interviews or social accounts found. Sources don't state his exact relation to Nagpur founder-chairman Shivkisan Agrawal (the patronymic suggests he is a son; unverified). The only site email is customer support, so a better route is corporate PR at Haldiram Snacks Food.

name: Hu Bopan
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Zhejiang NHU Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002001)
profile: Hu Baifan (胡柏藩; listed here as 'Hu Bopan') founded NHU in Xinchang, Zhejiang, growing it from a school-run workshop into one of the world's largest producers of vitamins (A, E), animal-nutrition ingredients, flavors and fragrances and specialty materials. He has chaired the Shenzhen-listed company since 2005 and indirectly controls roughly 31% of it.
interesting_fact: NHU began as a business started to fund a rural middle school; its first product was recycled waste alcohol, which earned about RMB 100,000 profit in year one before Hu pivoted to high-value pharma intermediates.
deep_cut_fact: Hu was a newly graduated chemistry teacher at a rural middle school in 1988 when the principal asked him to start a business; with borrowed tens of thousands of yuan, no plant, workers or product, he built it, and in 1991 his team developed ethoxymethylene malonate (a norfloxacin intermediate), NHU's first national key new product.
notes: Name in source list is a romanization variant; standard spelling is Hu Baifan (胡柏藩). Low international media profile; Chinese-language outreach via NHU Securities Department is the most direct route. His brother Hu Baishan is vice chairman.

name: lin Wenjing
profile: Lin Wenjing (Sutanto Djuhar, 1928-2018), Fuqing-born Indonesian-Chinese co-founder of the Salim Group, returned to Fuqing in 1987 and founded Rongqiao Group in 1989; died 2 July 2018.
notes: Deceased (2 July 2018) per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sutanto_Djuhar. Rongqiao Group / Lin Wenjing Foundation now run by family; the Forbes listing may refer to heirs.

name: Allison McCain
current_role: Chairman, McCain Foods Ltd. (chair since 2004; no 2025-26 source found confirming he still holds the title)
profile: Allison D. McCain, nephew of McCain Foods co-founders Harrison and Wallace McCain, joined the Florenceville, N.B. frozen-potato giant in 1975 as an engineer, ran production in Australia and the UK, became deputy chairman in 1999 and chairman in 2004. His wealth is his family stake in privately held McCain Foods.
interesting_fact: As chair of UNB's 'Forging our Futures' campaign from 2003, he helped raise $107 million, then a record for Atlantic Canada; he later served as UNB's chancellor (named 2013) and chaired the Beaverbrook Art Gallery board.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineering graduate of UNB (1972), he worked at the New Brunswick Telephone Company before taking an engineering job at McCain's Florenceville plant in 1975 — the first of the family's next generation to join the firm.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. No death reports found (born c.1949). Best route is McCain Foods corporate communications. Only listed by Hurun 2014-2016.

name: Heinz- George Baus
current_role: Deceased (died 10 May 2016, aged 82)
profile: Founder of German DIY/home-improvement chain Bauhaus (first store Mannheim, 1960). Died 10 May 2016.
notes: Died 10 May 2016 per Wikipedia and DIY International obituary (https://diyinternational.com/content/news/2016/05/20/bauhaus-founder-heinz-georg-baus-passes-away.html; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz-Georg_Baus). Son Bernd Baus is a Bauhaus managing director.

name: Maurice Greenberg
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Starr Companies (C.V. Starr & Co.); sons Jeff and Scott Greenberg took over leadership in 2025
profile: Maurice 'Hank' Greenberg (b. 1925) ran AIG from 1968 to 2005, building it into one of the world's largest insurers, then led C.V. Starr & Co. (Starr Companies), a global insurance and investment group. In 2025 he handed leadership to his sons and he chaired The Starr Foundation until 2024; he remains active in US-China and medical philanthropy.
interesting_fact: A WWII veteran, he enlisted at 17, landed at Omaha Beach on D-Day and took part in the liberation of Dachau; he later served in Korea, and credits the GI Bill for his college education.
deep_cut_fact: In 1990 he became the first Chairman of Shanghai's International Business Leaders' Advisory Council, later served as Senior Economic Advisor to the Beijing municipal government, and was made an honorary citizen of Shanghai.

public_contacts.value: Prosek Partners (listed as Starr's PR adviser, Oct 2025 release)

notes: Aged 101; Hurun-listed wealth via Starr. Best route is Starr media office (media@starr.com). Starr Foundation does not accept unsolicited proposals.

name: Won-Woo Kim
current_role: President (사장) and head of Digital Strategy, NICE Holdings (largest shareholder of NICE Group), promoted in the 2026 executive reshuffle
profile: Kim Won-woo (김원우, b. ~1993) is the eldest son of NICE Group founder Kim Kwang-soo, who died in 2018 at 55; he inherited control at age 25 and is the largest shareholder of NICE Holdings, parent of Korea's leading credit bureau NICE Information Service. He has worked in the group's digital strategy unit, becoming executive director in Dec 2024 and president for 2026.
interesting_fact: He became controlling owner of one of Korea's biggest credit-information groups at just 25; day-to-day management has been run by professional CEO Choi Young while he built experience in digital strategy.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Korean-language press only. Best route is via NICE Holdings corporate communications.

name: Jacques Bouriez
current_role: Chairman (président), Louis Delhaize Group (Charleroi, Belgium); operations run by sons François and Pierre Bouriez
profile: Member of the Bouriez family that controls Belgian-French retailer Louis Delhaize Group (Cora hypermarkets, Match, Smatch, Delitraiteur). Brother of Cora founder Philippe Bouriez (d. 2014). Moved from CEO to chairman when his sons became joint managing directors. The group has since been unwinding: Cora France sold to Carrefour (2024), Belgian Cora stores closed by early 2026.
interesting_fact: Louis Delhaize Group traces its roots to 1875 in Charleroi; Jacques's brother Philippe Bouriez founded the Cora hypermarket chain, and the family held the group for decades as one of Europe's last big private grocers.
notes: Very private, elderly; no death reported in searches (only brother Philippe's, 2014: https://www.lsa-conso.fr/philippe-bouriez-mort-d-un-grand-nom-de-la-distribution-francaise,166753). Group is being dismantled (https://www.retaildetail.eu/news/food/dismantling-of-ldz-louis-delhaize-group-nears-completion/), so poor fit for podcast; any route would be via Louis Delhaize SA corporate office. Shares listing with Philippe Bouriez (deceased).

name: Uma Devi Prasad
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2025-26) as a holder of Aristo Pharmaceuticals wealth; no executive role found
profile: Hurun links her to Aristo Pharmaceuticals, the Mumbai-based drugmaker founded in 1971 by Mahendra Prasad, a seven-term Rajya Sabha MP who died in December 2021. Public records name an Uma Devi in disputes over his estate. I could not confirm her role at the company or any public profile.
notes: Very private, with almost no public profile. Her link to Aristo is tied up in ongoing estate litigation over Mahendra Prasad's assets, so this is a sensitive family matter: avoid. The only contact is the company's general email. Low priority.

name: Darshan Hiranandani
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman, Yotta Data Services and Nidar; CEO, Hiranandani Group and Nidar Group
profile: Son of Mumbai developer Niranjan Hiranandani, named successor to the real-estate group in 2019. He launched Yotta in 2019 as the group's data-center park business (Panvel/Navi Mumbai), now a sovereign AI cloud/GPU provider with NM1 (Mumbai), D1 (Greater Noida) and G1 (GIFT City) and reported IPO plans. He also founded LNG developer H-Energy.
interesting_fact: Yotta says its NM1 campus in Navi Mumbai is Asia's largest Tier IV Gold uptime-certified data center; Yotta has been empanelled under IndiaAI to supply GPU compute.
deep_cut_fact: Before data centers he went into energy: he founded H-Energy, which began developing India's first floating LNG terminal in 2017; the FSRU Hoegh Giant arrived at H-Energy's Jaigarh terminal in Maharashtra in April 2021, India's first FSRU.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/energy theme. Search results are flooded with SEO/reputation-management pages about him (hackmd, issuu, sites.google) - ignore those as sources. Yotta CEO is Sunil Gupta, who does most media. Avoid political topics (2023 Indian parliamentary 'cash-for-query' controversy) and the later Hoegh FSRU charter termination.

name: Frank Sobey
current_role: Director, Empire Company Limited (Sobeys parent); President, ECL Properties; founding partner, Creative Destruction Lab Atlantic
profile: Frank C. Sobey is a grandson of Sobeys founder Frank H. Sobey and a son of Bill Sobey. He spent 36 years at Empire Company, retiring as VP Real Estate in 2014, and chaired Crombie REIT and its predecessor until 2019. The Sobey family's fortune sits mainly in Empire/Sobeys, Canada's No. 2 grocer, and he remains an Empire director.
interesting_fact: He is a founding partner of CDL-Atlantic, the Atlantic Canada site of the Creative Destruction Lab startup program, and sits on the board of the Canada-U.S. Fulbright Program.
deep_cut_fact: When he stepped down as Crombie REIT chair in 2019, he had chaired it for 13 years and its predecessor Crombie Properties for eight, and said he had been 'connected in one way or another with Crombie' for 40 years.
notes: The founder Frank H. Sobey died in 1985, so Hurun's 'Frank Sobey' is most likely Frank C. Sobey, possibly standing in for the wider family's Empire stake. board@empireco.ca is Empire's published route to directors and goes through the corporate secretary. CDL-Atlantic offers an entrepreneurship hook.

name: Jacques
current_role: Former chairman / supervisory board president, Louis Delhaize Group (Belgium; now renamed LDz)
profile: Jacques Bouriez (identified via shared_with Philippe Bouriez and source Louis Delhaize) is a member of the Bouriez family that controls Belgian retailer Louis Delhaize, owner of the Cora and Match hypermarkets. He chaired/oversaw the group's supervisory board after his brother Philippe stepped back in 2009. The group sold Cora/Match France to Carrefour (2023-24) and Delitraiteur to Colruyt (2024).
interesting_fact: The family group, founded in 1875 in Charleroi, sold its French Cora and Match chains to Carrefour, closing in July 2024.
notes: Input gives only first name 'Jacques'; identity inferred as Jacques Bouriez. No recent public info; current status and age (likely 80s) unconfirmed. Next generation (Pierre and François Bouriez) runs the business. Very low public profile.

name: Xu Gaoming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and executive director, Laopu Gold Co., Ltd. (HKEX: 6181)
profile: Hunan-born (1964) founder of Laopu Gold, the 'Hermes of gold' luxury jeweler known for traditional Chinese 'heritage gold' craftsmanship, fixed pricing and a small number of palace-style stores. After a decade in government he started a souvenir/cultural-products business in 1995, launched Laopu in 2016 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2024; the stock's surge made him one of China's richest.
interesting_fact: Laopu runs only a few dozen stores, yet in H1 2025 each generated an average of ~459m yuan in sales; its Tmall flagship became the first gold jewelry brand to exceed 1bn yuan in the 618 festival.
deep_cut_fact: He started out around age 20 as a clerk at the fisheries bureau of Yueyang near Dongting Lake, and earned his degree in 1988 via a correspondence program with Huazhong Agricultural University. He has said the brand 'seeks to both preserve tradition and rebel against tradition'.
notes: No published personal/press email found; company IR contact details should be in Laopu Gold's HKEX annual report (hkexnews.hk, stock code 6181). Says he expects gold prices to keep rising; expanding abroad starting with Southeast Asia.

name: Neal Aronson
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Roark Capital Group (Atlanta)
profile: Neal Aronson (b. 1965) founded Atlanta private-equity firm Roark Capital in 2001 and remains its majority owner. Roark specialises in franchised brands and owns Subway, Arby's, Jimmy John's, Sonic, Dunkin' and Baskin-Robbins (via Inspire Brands), having done many of the restaurant industry's biggest deals of the past decade.
interesting_fact: Roark Capital is named after Howard Roark, the uncompromising architect-hero of Ayn Rand's The Fountainhead.
deep_cut_fact: Before Roark, he co-founded U.S. Franchise Systems in 1995 with his uncle Mike Leven (ex-Holiday Inn president), growing a 27-hotel regional chain (Microtel) into the 10th-largest US hotel franchisor with 1,100+ properties before selling to Hyatt's Pritzkers in 2000. He began his career in Drexel Burnham Lambert's corporate finance department.
notes: Low public profile; best route is Roark's media contact at Joele Frank. Franchise focus (restaurants, services) — not energy, but large real-asset/consumer deal-maker.

name: Prathap Reddy
current_role: Founder & (Executive) Chairman, Apollo Hospitals Group
profile: Cardiologist Prathap C. Reddy (b. 1933) came back to India from the US and in 1983 opened Apollo Hospitals in Chennai, India's first corporate hospital chain. Apollo now runs about 80 hospitals and more than 7,000 pharmacies. His four daughters run the business day to day, and he still speaks publicly as founder-chairman, for example at the International Health Dialogue in January 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Apollo Hospitals Group opened a hospital in Nairobi, Kenya, with Balmer Healthcare, offering 20 specialties. He received the Padma Bhushan (1991) and the Padma Vibhushan (2010).
deep_cut_fact: Before returning to India he did a fellowship at Massachusetts General Hospital and led research programmes at the Missouri State Chest Hospital. In 2012 Apollo opened the first 'Apollo Isha Vidya Rural School' in his home village of Aragonda, in Chittoor district.
notes: He is 93. His daughters (Preetha, Suneeta, Sangita, Shobana) run Apollo day to day, so the best route is Apollo Hospitals' corporate communications. An undated report said he had been hospitalised; treat his availability with care.

name: Arkady Volozh
current_role: Founder and CEO, Nebius Group N.V. (Nasdaq: NBIS), Amsterdam-based AI cloud/neocloud company
profile: Kazakhstan-born, Tel Aviv-based Volozh co-founded Yandex with Ilya Segalovich in 1997 and led it through its 2011 Nasdaq IPO. After Yandex sold its Russian assets in 2024 (~$5.4bn), he relaunched the remainder as Nebius, an AI-infrastructure cloud that has since signed deals with Microsoft (up to $19.4bn) and Meta (up to $27bn) and targets multi-gigawatt contracted power.
interesting_fact: Long before Yandex, he and Segalovich built search tools for patents, Russian classical literature and the Bible; in 1993 they built a search engine for 'non-structured information with Russian morphology'.
deep_cut_fact: He attended the Republican School of Physics and Mathematics in Almaty, studied applied maths at Moscow's Gubkin oil-and-gas university, worked at a state pipeline research institute, then started a small business importing PCs from Austria. In 2007 he set up the free Yandex School of Data Analysis.
notes: Highly relevant for data-center/AI-infra episode (Nebius is building multi-GW AI capacity, e.g. Finland, UK, US). He has appeared on Accel's podcast. Avoid leading with Russia/sanctions history; EU sanctions were lifted in 2024.

name: Ji Qi
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, H World Group (Nasdaq: HTHT; HKEX: 1179)
profile: Shanghai Jiao Tong University-educated serial entrepreneur who co-founded Ctrip (now Trip.com) in 1999 and Home Inns in 2002, then founded HanTing/China Lodging in 2005, now H World Group, which runs 13,000+ mostly budget and midscale hotels (Hi Inn, Ji Hotel, and others). He remains executive chairman; CEO Hui Jin runs day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Often described as the first Chinese entrepreneur to found three companies that each passed a $1B valuation and listed on Nasdaq: Ctrip/Trip.com, Home Inns and H World (formerly China Lodging/Huazhu).
deep_cut_fact: He wrote 'The Founder's Notes' (LID Publishing, 2020), a book of essays on applying Chinese philosophy and the pursuit of 'Truth, Goodness and Beauty' to company culture and management.
notes: Listed as Singapore resident. Company IR is the main published route; his book publisher (LID Publishing) is a possible secondary angle.

name: Sir Anwar Pervez
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Bestway Group (nephew Lord Zameer Choudrey is chairman)
profile: Rawalpindi-born Sir Anwar Pervez (b. 1935) moved to the UK in 1956, drove buses in Bradford, opened a London grocery and built Bestway into a cash-and-carry, pharmacy (Well), cement and banking (UBL) group employing ~47,000. He turned 90 in 2025 and is now Founder & Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: For his 90th birthday in June 2025 King Charles and Queen Camilla hosted him for tea in the Royal Box at Royal Ascot; Bestway also marked its 50th anniversary with an 800-guest event at the Royal Albert Hall.
deep_cut_fact: His first paid job was as a telephone operator for Pakistan's state telecom PTCL, earning 96 rupees a month, before he emigrated and worked double shifts as a Bradford bus conductor for about £16-18 a week.
notes: Aged 91; approach via Bestway Group head office (Park Royal, London). Founded Bestway Foundation in 1987.

name: Stephen Jarislowsky
profile: Stephen Jarislowsky, founder of Montreal money manager Jarislowsky Fraser (sold to Scotiabank in 2018) and noted philanthropist, died in October 2026 at age 101 (reported Oct 8-9, 2026).
notes: Deceased (October 2026, Montreal per reports). Sources: https://www.advisor.ca/industry-news/industry/canadian-investor-and-philanthropist-stephen-jarislowsky-dies-at-age-101/ ; https://www.lesoleil.com/affaires/2026/10/08/alerte-l-investisseur-stephen-jarislowsky-s-eteint-a-101-ans-34JJFWJYTBA5XMWSPSJM5EXA6E/

name: Chao Yung-Tsang
current_role: Co-founder & Vice Chairman, Jentech Precision Industrial Co. (TWSE: 3653), Taoyuan, Taiwan
profile: Co-founded Jentech Precision in 1987 with older brother and chairman Chung-Hsin Chao; early on he ran finance while Chung-Hsin ran R&D. Jentech grew from a tool-and-die shop into a key maker of heat spreaders, vapor-chamber and micro-channel lids and liquid-cooling parts for AI servers, EVs and chips. He oversees operations, finance and capacity planning.
interesting_fact: AI-chip cooling demand turned Jentech into one of Taiwan's highest-priced stocks: its shares broke through NT$5,000 in April 2026 as Nvidia-class processors adopted advanced lids such as micro-channel lids that build liquid coolant paths into the chip lid.
deep_cut_fact: Jentech's own board bio says he graduated from the Affiliated Senior High School of National Taiwan Normal University and showed 'a strong entrepreneurial spirit from an early age'; in the company's first years he ran finance while his brother handled R&D.
notes: Low public profile; brother Chung-Hsin Chao is chairman and the company's public face. Company form lets you pick a department. Jentech's ESG report also lists a sustainability-office email, but no press/IR email was found; the company's annual report names the general manager as spokesperson. Some hosts (jentech.com.tw, taipeitimes) blocked for WebFetch but reachable via curl.

name: Xia Zuoquan
current_role: Co-founder and non-executive director, BYD Co.; founder/chairman, Shenzhen Zhengxuan Investment
profile: One of BYD's three founders: an investor who put a few hundred thousand yuan into Wang Chuanfu's battery startup in 1995, served as executive director and VP running group operations 2001-2008, and remains a non-executive director holding ~2.8% of BYD. Since 2010 he has run his own VC firm, Zhengxuan Investment, backing robotics, aerospace, new energy and biotech companies.
interesting_fact: His 1995 investment of a few hundred thousand yuan in BYD returned more than 20,000x; he has sold BYD shares mainly to fund Zhengxuan's tech investments, including early, rescue-stage backing of robot maker UBTech.
deep_cut_fact: Xia, from Xiangyang in Hubei, first met Wang Chuanfu in November 1994; he didn't understand batteries, but the two talked for three days and two nights, going to bed at 4am each night, before he committed to invest in April 1995.
notes: Very low-profile; rarely gives interviews. db@byd.com is BYD's listed-company contact (board office) from its Shenzhen exchange profile. Zhengxuan Investment (正轩投资) would be the more personal route, but I found no published email for it.

name: Arthur James
notes: Likely a parsing artifact of the Forbes 2001-09 joint listing 'Arthur, James & John Irving' (Irving family, Canada). All are deceased: Arthur L. Irving d. 13 May 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Irving), James K. Irving d. 21 Jun 2024 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_K._Irving), John E. Irving d. 2010.

name: John Irving
current_role: Deceased (died July 21, 2010, Saint John, New Brunswick)
profile: John E. 'Jack' Irving (1932-2010), youngest son of K.C. Irving, co-owned the Irving Group with brothers J.K. and Arthur (listed jointly by Forbes 2001-2009). Died July 21, 2010 aged 78.
notes: Deceased - source: CBC News 'Industrialist Jack Irving dies at 78' (http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/new-brunswick/industrialist-jack-irving-dies-at-78-1.870034) and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_E._Irving. Irving Oil (the energy arm) is run by Arthur Irving's family; consider them instead.

name: Joan Tisch
profile: Died November 2, 2017 in Manhattan at age 90; widow of Preston Robert Tisch (Loews Corp. co-founder, NY Giants co-owner). Death announced by the New York Giants.
notes: Deceased (source: https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/joan-tisch-dead ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Tisch). Her stake passed to children Steve, Jonathan and Laurie Tisch. Remove from outreach list.

name: Robert McNair
current_role: Deceased (died 23 Nov 2018); was founder/owner of the NFL's Houston Texans
profile: Robert (Bob) McNair founded cogeneration firm Cogen Technologies in 1984, sold it to Enron in 1999, and used the proceeds to found the Houston Texans NFL franchise. He died on 23 November 2018; per instructions the rest of the profile is skipped.
notes: Died 23 Nov 2018 (Houston Chronicle obituary; Wikipedia 'Bob McNair'). Texans ownership passed to his widow and then to son Cal McNair (principal owner since 2024). Not a viable podcast guest.

name: Brijmohan Lall Munjal
profile: Founder of the Hero Group / Hero MotoCorp (motorcycles); died 1 November 2015 in New Delhi, aged 92.
notes: Deceased 1 Nov 2015 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brijmohan_Lall_Munjal ; https://www.autocarpro.in/news-national/hero-founder-brijmohan-lall-munjal-passes-away-9597). Son Pawan Munjal leads Hero MotoCorp.

name: Brenninkmeijer family
current_role: Family owners of COFRA Holding AG (Zug, Switzerland), parent of C&A, Bregal Investments and Sunrock; chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, with Florian Brenninkmeyer due to take over in April 2027
profile: This Dutch-German dynasty founded the C&A clothing chain in 1841 and owns it through the Swiss holding company COFRA, alongside private equity (Bregal), real estate and renewable energy investments. Around 2026 the group reported roughly €40bn under management and was handing control to the sixth generation, with Georg Wunderlin as its first non-family CEO.
interesting_fact: C&A takes its name from the initials of the founding brothers Clemens and August Brenninkmeyer, who opened their first textile shop in Sneek, Netherlands, in 1841. Six generations later the business is still entirely family-owned.
deep_cut_fact: Long before ESG became fashionable, Marcel Brenninkmeijer founded Good Energies in 2001 to run COFRA's renewables portfolio. It backed wind and solar developers and the Atlantic Wind Connection offshore transmission backbone, a strong energy hook.
notes: This is a family (hundreds of members), not an individual, and it is famously private. For an energy podcast, the best individual targets are probably COFRA chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, incoming chair Florian Brenninkmeyer, or the Sunrock solar business. Contact is through the COFRA newsroom; no email could be scraped. The family won the 2026 Kellogg Family Leadership Award.

name: Edward C. (Ned) Johnson
profile: Edward C. 'Ned' Johnson III, longtime chairman and CEO of Fidelity Investments, died on March 23, 2022 at age 91 at his home in Florida.
notes: Deceased March 23, 2022 (source: https://www.cnbc.com/2022/03/24/fidelity-investments-longtime-leader-edward-c-ned-johnson-iii-dies-at-91-.html). Fidelity is now led by his daughter Abigail Johnson; the family wealth is held by his heirs.

name: Abigail (Abigail P. Johnson)
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Fidelity Investments (Boston)
profile: Listed only as 'Abigail' sharing a 1997 Forbes entry with Edward C. (Ned) Johnson; this is almost certainly Abigail Johnson, Ned's daughter. She joined Fidelity full-time as an analyst in 1988 (after Hobart and William Smith and Harvard MBA), became CEO in 2014 and chairman in 2016, and runs the privately held, family-controlled asset manager today.
interesting_fact: An early Wall Street crypto champion: at Consensus 2017 she said she was 'still a believer' and revealed Fidelity had set up a small in-house bitcoin and ethereum mining operation; Fidelity Digital Assets followed in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Her first Fidelity job, straight out of high school in 1980, was answering phones in the customer-service department; she then majored in art history at Hobart and William Smith before Harvard Business School.
notes: Input record has only the first name 'Abigail' (Forbes 1997, shared with Ned Johnson); identification as Abigail Johnson is inferred, not confirmed by the source data. Publicity-shy; route via Fidelity corporate communications. Fidelity mining is a natural energy/data-center angle.

name: Alfred Lerner
profile: Deceased: Alfred Lerner (1933-2002), chairman of credit card giant MBNA and owner of the Cleveland Browns (1998-2002), died October 23, 2002 in Cleveland. Matches the 1996-2000 Forbes listing.
notes: Died 2002 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Lerner ; NYT obituary https://www.nytimes.com/2002/10/25/sports/alfred-lerner-69-banker-revived-cleveland-browns.html). Identity inferred from Forbes 1996-2000 US listing at ~$3.8B; no source_of_wealth given in input. Son Randy Lerner inherited the Browns.

name: Heinz-Georg Baus
profile: Founder of German DIY/home-improvement chain Bauhaus (founded 1960 in Mannheim). Died May 2016, aged 82.
interesting_fact: Died in May 2016 aged 82; Bauhaus was Germany's first DIY store chain, opened in Mannheim in 1960 on the American model.
notes: Deceased (May 2016) per DIY International and Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heinz-Georg_Baus). Not a candidate.

name: Sid Richardson Bass
current_role: Private investor and philanthropist, Fort Worth, Texas (head of the Bass family investment group since 1968)
profile: Fort Worth oil heir (grand-nephew of wildcatter Sid W. Richardson) who took control of the family business in 1968 and, per Vanity Fair, grew a ~$50M company into a ~$14B investment group. With his brothers he was Disney's largest shareholder from 1984 and is known for backing Michael Eisner's management. Yale 1965, Stanford MBA.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he and then-wife Mercedes Bass gave $25 million to the Metropolitan Opera, at the time the largest individual gift in the company's history.
deep_cut_fact: At just 28 he and his then-wife commissioned Paul Rudolph to design the Bass Residence in Fort Worth's Westover Hills, often called Rudolph's most ambitious residential project; it received the AIA Fort Worth chapter's 25 Year Honor Award in 2005.
notes: Very private; no published personal office email, website or social accounts found. Family office (Bass Enterprises, Fort Worth) does not publish contacts. Best route is likely a warm intro via Fort Worth civic/arts circles.

name: Mukesh Jagtiani
notes: Mukesh 'Micky' Jagtiani, founder and chairman of Dubai-based Landmark Group, died May 26, 2023 at age 70; his wife Renuka Jagtiani is chairwoman and CEO of the group. Source: https://www.arabianbusiness.com/culture-society/dubais-landmark-group-owner-micky-jagtiani-passes-away-at-age-70

name: Samwer Brothers
current_role: Oliver Samwer: CEO, Rocket Internet SE. Marc and Alexander Samwer: co-founders and investors (Rocket Internet / Global Founders Capital)
profile: Oliver, Marc and Alexander Samwer, from Cologne, sold their eBay-style auction site Alando to eBay in 1999 and later sold Jamba to VeriSign. They founded the Berlin incubator Rocket Internet in 2007, which built Zalando, Delivery Hero stakes, HelloFresh and others. Rocket went public in 2014 and was taken private in 2020. They now invest through Rocket and Global Founders Capital.
interesting_fact: Their first exit was Alando, a German auction site launched in 1999 and sold to eBay about 100 days later for roughly $43m. It became eBay Germany.
deep_cut_fact: Oliver Samwer's 1998 WHU diploma thesis, written with Max Finger, was published as the book 'America's Most Successful Startups'. It studied US startups, mainly in Silicon Valley and Massachusetts. He first visited Silicon Valley in 1995.
notes: This entry covers three brothers; Oliver is the public face and Rocket CEO. They are famously press-shy (Oliver once walked out of an interview). Rocket's general inbox is the only published route. Book record: https://stafforini.com/works/finger-1998-america-most-successful/

name: Prakash Parmanand Hinduja
current_role: Chairman, Hinduja Group (Europe); Chairman of the Advisory Board, Hinduja Bank (Switzerland)
profile: Prakash 'PP' Hinduja is the third of the four Hinduja brothers behind the Hinduja Group, a conglomerate whose interests span Ashok Leyland, IndusInd Bank, Gulf Oil, energy and media. He ran the group's European operations from Geneva and has been based in Monaco since 2008. After brother Gopichand's death in November 2025, he and Ashok are the surviving brothers of that generation.
interesting_fact: He and his brothers built the group, founded by their father P.D. Hinduja, into an international conglomerate with a footprint across about 38 countries and a 200,000-plus workforce.
deep_cut_fact: After university, PP began in the family business in Tehran, Iran, before moving to Geneva to take charge of the group's European operations. He also sits on the board of the Swiss-Indian Chamber of Commerce.
notes: Born 1945. Sensitive: in 2024 a Geneva court convicted Prakash and family members in a case over the treatment of domestic staff; check the current status before outreach. The group's Energy/Hinduja Renewables arm (multi-GW generation plans in India) fits the podcast's energy angle. Group contact page lists business-unit emails but none for him personally.

name: Srichand Parmanand Hinduja
current_role: Deceased (former chairman, Hinduja Group); died in London on 17 May 2023, aged 87
notes: Died 17 May 2023 (Al Jazeera; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S._P._Hinduja). His brother Gopichand P. Hinduja succeeded him as Hinduja Group chairman; any outreach should go to the group or the surviving family leaders.

name: Jose Batista Sobrinho
current_role: Founder of JBS S.A. (honorary patriarch; no operational role since the 1980s apart from a stint as interim CEO in 2017)
profile: 'Zé Mineiro' (b. 1933, Carmo do Rio Claro, Minas Gerais) opened a small butcher shop, Casa de Carnes Mineira, in Anápolis, Goiás, in 1953. It grew into JBS, named after his initials and now the world's largest meat processor, run by his sons Joesley and Wesley. In June 2025 he rang the NYSE opening bell for JBS's US listing.
interesting_fact: At around 91, he rang the opening bell at the New York Stock Exchange on 25 June 2025 when JBS began trading in New York, with his sons alongside him.
deep_cut_fact: His business first took off by selling beef to the construction companies building the new capital, Brasília, in the late 1950s. That was the springboard for what became JBS.
notes: He is in his 90s and has no public channels of his own. Any approach would go through JBS/J&F press. Hurun last listed him separately in 2014; the family wealth is mostly attributed to his sons.

name: Woody Johnson
current_role: Chairman and co-owner, New York Jets; partner and director, Crystal Palace FC
profile: Robert Wood 'Woody' Johnson IV is a great-grandson of Johnson & Johnson co-founder Robert Wood Johnson I, and his wealth stems from the J&J family fortune. He bought the New York Jets in 2000 for $635M, helped build MetLife Stadium, served as U.S. Ambassador to the UK (2017-2021) and is back as Jets chairman.
interesting_fact: As ambassador he led the U.S. Embassy London's move to its new headquarters at Nine Elms.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a pioneer backer of women's and girls' flag football from youth to international level, and has held civic roles with the Wildlife Conservation Society and the Peregrine Fund (a raptor-conservation group).
notes: No source_of_wealth in input; identity confirmed via Wikidata Q3569866 (Jets owner). Founded the Lupus Research Alliance. Best route via Jets communications.

name: Daniel S. Loeb
current_role: Founder and CEO, Third Point LLC (hedge fund / activist investor, New York)
profile: Dan Loeb founded Third Point in 1995 with about $3 million and built it into a major activist hedge fund managing roughly $24 billion at end-2025, known for pointed letters to boards (Yahoo, Sony, Nestle, Disney). Recent positions include SK Hynix, Siemens Energy, Vistra and Microsoft, giving him an AI/power angle.
interesting_fact: Third Point's top Q4 2025 contributors included SK Hynix and Siemens Energy, with power producer Vistra among its holdings: a direct bet on the AI data-center and energy buildout.
deep_cut_fact: At age 12 he started a skateboard company, making boards for his friends; he is a lifelong surfer who grew up near the beach in Southern California.
notes: No published press email on Third Point's site; ir@ is investor-focused. Third Point's quarterly investor letters are public and a good conversation hook.

name: Edward J. DeBartolo, Jr.
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeBartolo Holdings LLC (Tampa, FL)
profile: Son of mall pioneer Edward J. DeBartolo Sr. He joined the family's Edward J. DeBartolo Corp. in 1971 and led its 1996 merger with Simon Property Group. He owned the San Francisco 49ers from 1977 to 2000, a stretch that brought five Super Bowl titles. Since 2002 he has run DeBartolo Holdings, which covers real estate development, private equity investments, sports and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 2016 as a contributor. Steve Young credited his 'family approach', which treated players as partners, with changing how NFL owners run teams.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 he co-founded Brooks-DeBartolo Collegiate High School in Tampa with Hall of Fame linebacker Derrick Brooks. At the 2014 flag-football game that was Candlestick Park's last football event, Joe Montana threw him the final touchdown pass.
notes: No published email. DeBartolo Holdings lists a main office line, 813.908.8400, at its Tampa HQ (debartoloholdings.com contact section). Avoid his 1998 Edwin Edwards case and the 2020 pardon. Debartolo.com is a parked domain, not his.

name: Ivar Tollefsen
current_role: Chairman and co-CEO, Fredensborg AS (Oslo), owner of the European residential landlord Heimstaden
profile: Norwegian real-estate investor. At 14 he started a disco/DJ equipment rental business and used the earnings to build Fredensborg AS. Through Heimstaden it owns roughly 150,000 apartments across Europe. In 2017 Fredensborg bought Oslo's former U.S. embassy building, which now houses its hotel 'Ambassaden'.
interesting_fact: Besides building a property empire, he has led several polar expeditions and has raced in the Dakar Rally.
deep_cut_fact: He led the 13-man Norwegian expedition that left Cape Town on Christmas Eve 1993 for Queen Maud Land, Antarctica. In 1994 he, Robert Caspersen and Sjur Nesheim made the first ascent of the 'Wolf's Fang' (Ulvetanna) via an 11-day push up its northwest wall.
notes: Media-shy. Fredensborg's media inbox is the best route. He also wrote his own account of the Ulvetanna climb for the Alpine Journal (1997).

name: Jiang Nanchun (Jason Jiang)
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Focus Media (Shenzhen-listed 002027)
profile: Shanghai-based founder of Focus Media, China's largest elevator/building-lobby digital-screen advertising network. Took it public on Nasdaq in 2005, delisted in 2013 and relisted in Shenzhen via reverse takeover in 2016; he still runs the company and is a prominent voice on brand-building in China.
interesting_fact: Focus Media began in 2003 with an offbeat idea: selling ads on screens in office-building elevator lobbies, a format nobody then knew was worth anything.
deep_cut_fact: A Chinese literature graduate of East China Normal University, he wanted to be a poet; he credits student poetry for his business instincts: 'Writing poems requires you to connect and combine two seemingly irrelevant objects with a sharp imagination, which is also true in business.'
notes: Comfortable public speaker (NYU Shanghai, CKGSB alumnus events). Outreach likely needs to go via Focus Media IR/marketing in Chinese.

name: Wang Qicheng
current_role: Founder of the Hakim (Handing / 汉鼎) group; private investor based in Hangzhou
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur born in the 1980s, who shares the Hurun listing with Wu Yan. While at Zhejiang University he founded Handing (Hakim) Information Technology, a smart-city systems integrator that listed on ChiNext in 2012. In 2019 he passed control of the listed company (later Haixia Innovation) to Pingtan state capital, and he now invests his own money across a portfolio of roughly 100 startups.
interesting_fact: He was an early backer of US EV maker Fisker, investing in 2017 for a stake of about 10%, and of Aurora Mobile (极光), which listed on Nasdaq in 2018. In 2020 he was named one of China's top five angel investors, the only one born in the 1980s.
deep_cut_fact: He started his company straight out of Zhejiang University's business administration department in 2003. When it listed on ChiNext nine years later, the 31-year-old was reported to be the youngest controlling shareholder of any A-share company at the time.
notes: Sources are mostly promotional Chinese articles, so verify before quoting. No personal channels are published. Hurun lists him together with Wu Yan. He has little English-language presence.

name: Wu Yan
current_role: Co-owner with husband Wang Qicheng of the Hakim Unique (汉鼎宇佑) group's holdings; former controlling shareholder of Hakim Unique (300300.SZ, now 海峡创新)
profile: Hurun's Wu Yan (吴艳) is listed jointly with her husband Wang Qicheng, founder of Hangzhou-based Hakim Unique Group (汉鼎宇佑), a conglomerate with more than 150 companies. In 2019 she sold a 15% stake and control of listed Hakim Unique to state-linked Pingtan Chuangtou for RMB 1.05B. Wang now invests through platforms such as Qianshan Capital.
interesting_fact: The couple were ranked No. 5 on Hurun's 2019 list of self-made rich people born in the 1980s, with RMB 18B; Wang was once the youngest controlling shareholder of an A-share company, at 31.
notes: The input's SEC link (Microvast CEO) is a name collision. Microvast's CEO is Yang Wu, a different person, so ignore it. Wu Yan has almost no public profile of her own and the details are mostly about her husband. Identity is marked uncertain on the person level; the source of wealth ('Hakim' = 汉鼎宇佑) matches. No published contacts found.

name: Tony Chen Shih-Ching
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder, Largan Precision (TWSE: 3008); left the board in 2022
profile: Chen Shih-ching (陳世卿) co-founded Largan Precision in 1987 with Lin Yao-ying, running optical lens design and R&D as general manager; Largan became the leading maker of smartphone camera lenses (a key Apple supplier). He and Lin stepped off the board in 2022, handing over to Lin En-ping; Chen and his wife Chiang Tsui-ying remain large holders.
interesting_fact: Largan, the lens company he co-founded, is now moving into co-packaged optics (CPO) for data centres, sampling to a volume customer in 2026 with mass production targeted as early as mid-2027.
deep_cut_fact: A National Cheng Kung University mechanical-engineering grad and ex-Canon Taiwan engineer, he insisted every new Largan engineer, however skilled, spend at least a month in their first year crouching beside production machines.

public_contacts.value: precision@largan.com.tw (general company email shown on Largan homepage)

notes: Extremely private, no public social accounts. Born c.1949 (age 54 in 2003 per Business Today). No death reports found; still on Hurun 2026. Best route is via Largan Precision's IR/spokesperson office; CPO/data-centre optics is a natural podcast hook.

name: Chiang Tsui-Ying
current_role: Shareholder in Largan Precision (Taiwan) via the family of co-founder Tony Chen Shih-Ching; no public executive role found
profile: Chiang Tsui-Ying (蒋翠英/蔣翠英) appears on Hurun rich lists sharing a fortune with Tony Chen Shih-Ching, co-founder (1987, with Lin Yao-ying) and longtime technical lead of Largan Precision, the Taichung-based world leader in smartphone camera lenses. Her exact relationship and role could not be confirmed from public sources.
interesting_fact: Largan co-founder Chen Shih-Ching ran R&D because he was devoted to optical lens design; both founders left the board in 2022, with Chen's son Chen Chun-ming reported as taking a board seat.
notes: Essentially no public footprint under this name; Hurun lists the wealth as shared with Tony Chen Shih-Ching (likely family, unconfirmed). Only route is Largan corporate/IR. Treat as low-priority unless relationship is verified.

name: Nadir Godrej
current_role: Chairperson, Godrej Industries Group (Godrej Industries, Godrej Consumer Products, Godrej Properties, Godrej Agrovet)
profile: Mumbai industrialist (b. 1951), younger brother of Adi Godrej, trained as a chemical engineer (MIT, Stanford) with a Harvard MBA, who joined the family business four-plus decades ago. After the 2024 family split he chairs the Godrej Industries Group - four listed companies with ~$6.1bn revenue spanning consumer goods, chemicals, real estate and agri.
interesting_fact: A published poet, he often delivers business speeches entirely in verse; his first collection, 'Life and Other Poems', appeared in 1992 and he has done joint poetry readings with novelist Vikram Seth.
deep_cut_fact: He started at IIT Bombay but transferred after one year to MIT for chemical engineering; he speaks six languages including Russian and French, is known for a love of mathematics, and is a Chevalier of France's Legion of Honour.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: 'Business and Poetry with Nadir Godrej' on AND is the Future podcast

notes: Approachable and has done podcasts before (sustainability angle; Godrej is a WBCSD member). A poetic hook in an outreach note would land well. Route via Godrej Industries media desk.

name: Maurizio Billi
current_role: Controlling shareholder and chairman/president of Eurofarma (Brazilian pharma group)
profile: Son of Italian chemist Galliano Billi, who founded Eurofarma in 1972. Maurizio joined as a teenager, took over as president in 2000 and turned it into one of Brazil's largest drugmakers, expanding via acquisitions across Latin America (operations in 20+ countries, 12,600+ staff). Still leads the company and its strategy.
interesting_fact: An avid racer: his Eurofarma team has repeatedly won Stock Car Brasil titles, and in 2013 he himself won a race in the Porsche Master Cup Brasil.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in 1957, the same year his parents emigrated from Italy to South America, and at 19 (1976) started helping his father's small company, rotating through production, finance, purchasing and HR before becoming president in 2000.
notes: Described by Forbes Brasil as discreet. No published press email found; Eurofarma site blocks scraping. Sources differ on title (president vs chairman of the board); company 2024 report signs him as Presidente do Conselho.

name: Cameron Adams
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Canva
profile: Sydney-based designer-engineer who co-founded Canva in 2012 with Melanie Perkins and Cliff Obrecht and leads product, design and technical development. Before Canva he ran a design agency, spent four years at Google as the designer on Google Wave, and co-founded an email startup (Fluent) with other ex-Googlers. Canva was valued at $42B in 2025.
interesting_fact: He was the lone designer on Google Wave, working with Google Maps co-founders Lars and Jens Rasmussen; Lars Rasmussen later introduced him to Melanie Perkins, and he was recruited as an adviser before signing on as Canva's third co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Canva he blogged as 'The Man in Blue' and wrote about a 'resolution dependent layout' technique, a forerunner of responsive web design; he has written five books on web design, and he still publishes a year-end DJ mix of the best songs of each year on his site.
notes: Approachable and publicly invites contact on his site about startups, technology, design and speaking (the email address dates from 2018, so it may be stale). He does many podcasts (First Round, Lenny's). The LinkedIn handle comes from a mirrored post and is unverified.

name: Nick Caporella
current_role: Chairman and CEO, National Beverage Corp. (Nasdaq: FIZZ)
profile: Pennsylvania-born son of Italian immigrants who built a Florida site-preparation business, sold it to Burnup & Sims in 1972 and became that firm's CEO in 1976. In 1985 he founded National Beverage via the Shasta acquisition, adding LaCroix in 1996; he still runs the Fort Lauderdale company as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Forbes named him to its 2026 list of the 250 Greatest Self-Made Americans; he started in construction by putting $250, his entire savings, down on a $9,000 used dragline excavator.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Connellsville, PA, to a coal-miner father, he ran a bicycle-reconditioning business by age 11, later retired a millionaire at 30 after building a business in Puerto Rico, then within seven months started Caporella & Sons, named in honor of his father. He is a 1979 Horatio Alger Award recipient.
notes: Born c.1935, so he is in his early 90s and still CEO. Known for idiosyncratic, florid press releases written from the 'Office of the Chairman'; the company rarely does interviews. No published press email was found; the corporate-inquiry form is the official route.

name: Yu Renrong
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, OmniVision Group (formerly Will Semiconductor, Shanghai-listed)
profile: Ningbo-born Tsinghua electronic-engineering graduate (1990) who worked as an engineer at Inspur and in electronic-component distribution before founding chip designer Will Semiconductor in 2007. In 2019 it bought US image-sensor maker OmniVision for about $2.2bn, making it the world's No. 3 CMOS image-sensor supplier; he now also funds a new research university in Ningbo.
interesting_fact: In February 2025 he was the only semiconductor executive to speak at Xi Jinping's private-sector symposium, alongside Ren Zhengfei, Lei Jun and Wang Chuanfu; Will Semi shares hit the 10% daily limit the next day.
deep_cut_fact: His education foundation is co-building the Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo, in his hometown (CNY 10bn from his foundation vs CNY 16bn from the city); in Dec 2025 he gave another 30 million Will Semi shares (~2.5% of the company) to its foundation. Hurun named him China's most generous donor.
notes: Company now trades as OmniVision Group (豪威集团); IR email above is from 2025 earnings-call notices (securities investment dept). Board secretary listed as Ms Ren Bing. Chinese-language outreach likely more effective; the Eastern Institute of Technology, Ningbo is an alternate angle.

name: Otto Philipp Braun
current_role: Major family shareholder of B. Braun Melsungen AG (left the management board in Feb 2017)
profile: Sixth-generation member of the family behind B. Braun, the Melsungen medtech group that began as a pharmacy in 1839 and now makes infusion systems and surgical instruments. He ran B. Braun Brazil from 2008, then sat on the management board (Iberia/Latin America) for nine years until leaving by mutual agreement in 2017; he remains a large owner.
interesting_fact: He was the first sixth-generation family member to work in the company and serve on its board; his sister Anna Maria Braun is B. Braun's CEO.
deep_cut_fact: As MD of B. Braun Brazil (from 2008) he professionalised the Rio-based unit, introduced 'lean' processes, and oversaw a new fully automated medical-device plant in greater Rio, calling Brazil the group's 'launching hub' for Latin America (2012 interview).
notes: Very low public profile since 2017; no personal site or social accounts found. Only route is via B. Braun corporate communications (not a personal channel).

name: Spiro Latsis
current_role: Head of the Latsis family group; chairman of EFG Bank European Financial Group; president of the John S. Latsis Public Benefit Foundation's supervisory board
profile: Spiros J. Latsis (b. 1946) is the son of Greek shipping-and-oil tycoon John S. Latsis (d. 2003) and has led the family's Latsis Group since then. Holdings include EFG International (Swiss private banking), Lamda Development (Athens real estate), a stake in Helleniq Energy and the TALOS shipyard. He also funds the Latsis foundations in Athens and Geneva.
interesting_fact: He holds three LSE degrees: a BSc in economics (1968), an MSc in logic and scientific method (1970) and a PhD in philosophy (1974). He is also a trustee of the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.
deep_cut_fact: His PhD in philosophy at LSE was supervised by the famous philosopher of science Imre Lakatos, and he worked in the philosophy of economics before turning to the family business.
notes: Very private. The input Forbes bio appears to mix up names ('John and Margarita'); verify before quoting it. The foundation site warns about fraudulent emails that impersonate it. His Geneva family office (SETE SA) was named in a 2024 Swiss probe; per SETE he was not charged. Avoid this in outreach.

name: Daniel Mate
current_role: Retired former head of zinc/lead at Glencore (retired July 2020); private investor and Glencore shareholder
profile: Basque-born (San Sebastián) metals trader with economics and law degrees from Deusto. Joined Marc Rich & Co. in Madrid at 25, moved to Switzerland, took part in the 1994 management buyout that created Glencore and ran its zinc, copper and lead business until retiring in July 2020. Since then invests in Spanish real estate; lives in Switzerland.
interesting_fact: Through his property companies he bought Telefónica's former landmark Barcelona headquarters (Portal de l'Àngel/Fontanella), where Telefónica remains as a tenant.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Marc Rich & Co.'s Madrid office at age 25; after moving to the Swiss head office, Marc Rich himself took him on as a protégé. He also was a director of Asturiana de Zinc.
notes: Extremely low-profile (Forbes España notes even photos of him are hard to find). No published personal or office contacts found; Glencore media relations would not represent him post-retirement.

name: Sanjiv Goenka
current_role: Chairman, RP-Sanjiv Goenka (RPSG) Group, Kolkata
profile: Sanjiv Goenka chairs the ~$4.9bn-revenue RPSG Group, formed in 2011 when his father RP Goenka's empire was split between him and brother Harsh. Flagship is 127-year-old Kolkata power utility CESC, alongside PCBL, Spencer's, Too Yumm! and sports (Lucknow Super Giants, Mohun Bagan, Manchester Originals). In 2026 the group announced Rs 15,800 crore capex in West Bengal across energy and more.
interesting_fact: His older brother Harsh Goenka, who runs the separate RPG Enterprises, is also a billionaire; in 2025 Sanjiv bought 70% of English cricket team Manchester Originals.
deep_cut_fact: He has chaired IIT Kharagpur's Board of Governors since 2002, nominated for a fifth time in 2021, and was CII president in 2001-02 at about 40.
notes: Energy angle is strong (CESC power utility; son Shashwat, vice chairman, pushing renewables). The @RP_SanjivGoenka X link appears on the group homepage. CII term: https://cii.in/CII_Past_presidents.aspx

name: Mark Leonard
current_role: Founder of Constellation Software; former president (stepped down Sept 2025 for health reasons), left the board May 2026, now adviser on its Permanent Engaged Minority Shareholder (PEMS) strategy
profile: After an MBA from Western Ontario and ~11 years in venture capital, Leonard founded Toronto's Constellation Software in 1995; it has bought 850+ vertical-market software businesses and holds them permanently. He and family own ~7%. He resigned as president in Sept 2025 and did not stand for re-election to the board in May 2026, staying on as an adviser.
interesting_fact: Famously elusive: he has almost never spoken to the press, and before CSI he worked as a banker, valuator, mason, gravedigger, dog handler, bouncer, sapper and wind energy researcher (Globe and Mail via Forbes).
deep_cut_fact: Despite building a multibillion-dollar company, his reported compensation as president was a symbolic C$1 base salary with no bonus or stock awards.
notes: Extremely private; famously never gives interviews; stepped back for health reasons in 2025, so an interview request is unlikely to succeed. His annual President's letters (csisoftware.com) are the best way to show familiarity. Route via Constellation corporate.

name: Norbert Dentressangle
current_role: Founder; chairman/president of family holding Dentressangle (formerly Dentressangle Initiatives), Lyon - day-to-day co-chaired by his children
profile: Born 1954 in Annonay, he joined his parents' Rhone-valley trucking firm in 1974 and founded Norbert Dentressangle SA in 1979, building it into a European logistics leader (43,000 staff, $5.5B revenue) before selling to XPO Logistics for $3.53B in 2015. He now invests via the family holding in real estate and industry (e.g. Kiloutou), with a plan to deploy EUR 1B.
interesting_fact: He wrote 'Passion Rouge', a book about his entrepreneurial journey - the red refers to the group's iconic red trucks, long a familiar sight on European motorways.
deep_cut_fact: His breakthrough niche was the Saint-Vallier (Drome) to London run: in 1979 he set up a new company focused on that route, starting with about 40 tractors - which is why his red trucks became so familiar to British drivers.
notes: Low-profile; holding now led day-to-day by children Pierre-Henri and Marine Dentressangle (co-chairs). Born 9 July 1954 in Annonay (https://www.lyonmag.com/profil-personnalite-lyonnaise/301/norbert-dentressangle/25). Best route: holding's contact form.

name: Lawrence Stroll
current_role: Executive Chairman and controlling shareholder, Aston Martin Lagonda; owner of the Aston Martin Aramco F1 team
profile: Montreal-born fashion investor who, with Silas Chou, built Tommy Hilfiger and then Michael Kors into global brands and cashed out after Kors' 2011 IPO. Bought the Force India F1 team in 2018, led a 2020 rescue investment in Aston Martin, and now runs both the carmaker and its F1 team (with Adrian Newey on board).
interesting_fact: He collects vintage Ferraris and paid a then-record $27.5m for a 1967 Ferrari 275 GTB/4*S N.A.R.T. Spider in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He owned Quebec's historic Circuit Mont-Tremblant, a former Canadian Grand Prix venue, from 2000 until selling it in 2022. In 2021 he listed it for sale, then took it off the market.
notes: Gives few interviews. The best route is the Aston Martin corporate or F1 team press office (media.astonmartin.com).

name: Wang Junlin
current_role: Chairman, Sichuan Langjiu Group (Lang baijiu); his son Wang Bowei is general manager of Langjiu Co.
profile: Chairman of Sichuan Langjiu, maker of Lang-brand baijiu from Erlang town in Gulin, Sichuan, and a smaller rival to Kweichow Moutai. A former pharmaceutical turnaround manager, he acquired the loss-making state distiller via his Baoguang group in 2002 for about RMB 490m and built it into a multi-billion-dollar business. In 2026 he is still publicly leading dealer conferences and the brewing ceremonies.
interesting_fact: Langjiu says it has 20,000 employees and more than $2.8bn in annual sales; the Lang brand is named after Er Lang town in Sichuan, its place of origin.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Luzhou Medical College he practised traditional Chinese medicine for 10 years; in 1992 he took over the near-bankrupt state-run Luzhou pharmaceutical factory and returned it to profit within a year, the start of his Baoguang group.
notes: Input lists SEC insider role 'Baozun Inc. (BZUN) - Director' - this does not match the Langjiu chairman and is likely a name collision; not verified. Mostly Chinese-language media; son Wang Bowei is the public operating face. No published press email found. Avoid 2002 restructuring/IPO controversy.

name: Thomas James
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Raymond James Financial; co-founder of the James Museum of Western & Wildlife Art (St. Petersburg, FL)
profile: Son of Raymond James founder Robert James, Tom James built the firm into a national financial services group over 40+ years as CEO and then chairman. He stepped down as chairman in 2017 and retired from the board in Feb 2024. He now focuses on art: he and his wife Mary opened the James Museum in St. Petersburg in 2018.
interesting_fact: Tom and Mary James have collected 3,000+ works of American, Western and wildlife art since their student days. Part of the collection hangs in the James Museum and the rest at Raymond James headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: He began buying art in the 1960s while at Harvard and playing gigs with a rock band. After a 1980s ski week in Aspen he walked into a gallery planning to buy three or four paintings and left with eight. He calls himself 'artistically inept' and has never tried painting.
notes: Retired from Raymond James. The best warm route is probably the James Museum, which he founded and still identifies with; use its contact form with the 'Press' topic. Raymond James media relations handles corporate inquiries.

name: Danny Harris
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Alo Yoga / Color Image Apparel (Los Angeles)
profile: Danny Harris co-owns athleisure brand Alo Yoga with childhood friend Marco DeGeorge. The pair grew up in Los Gatos, CA, launched screen-printing wholesaler Color Image Apparel in 1992 (parent of blank-tee maker Bella+Canvas) and created Alo in 2007. Alo drove most of the group's ~$2B 2024 revenue and has 150+ stores worldwide.
interesting_fact: The name Alo stands for 'air, land, ocean'; the brand grew out of DeGeorge turning to yoga to recover from childhood back surgery, with Harris joining him.
deep_cut_fact: Before graduating high school, Harris and DeGeorge were already screen-printing shirts for a local business in Los Gatos, the side hustle that became Color Image Apparel.
notes: Very low personal media profile; Alo has an in-house PR team but no published press email (only customer-service addresses). Best route is via Alo corporate PR.

name: Reinold Geiger
current_role: Chairman and executive director, L'Occitane Group (Geneva-based)
profile: Austrian-born (Dornbirn, 1947) engineer and INSEAD MBA who began investing in Provence cosmetics maker L'Occitane in 1994 and built it into a group of brands (Elemis, Sol de Janeiro, Erborian etc.) in 100+ countries. He stepped down as CEO in 2021 and took the company private with Blackstone in 2024; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: L'Occitane was the first French company to list in Hong Kong (2010); Geiger then delisted it in 2024 with Blackstone. The group became a certified B Corp in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Son of a carpenter, he studied engineering at ETH Zurich; before L'Occitane he founded several small firms, including a tourism company in London, and in 1978 founded AMS Packaging in Paris, which made cosmetics packaging, later sold at a profit.
notes: Lives in Geneva. In a 2012 INSEAD interview he said he expected to be a hands-off investor in L'Occitane and 'just wanted to have no boss'. Best route: group communications.

name: Martua Sitorus
current_role: Co-founder, KPN Corp (formerly Gama Corp), Indonesia; co-founder of Wilmar International (left board 2018)
profile: Born in Pematangsiantar, North Sumatra, Martua Sitorus co-founded Wilmar International with Kuok Khoon Hong in 1991, growing it into one of the world's largest palm oil traders. He left Wilmar's board in 2018 and now runs KPN Corp with his brother Ganda, spanning palm plantations, property (Gama Land), cement (Cemindo Gemilang) and hospitals (Murni Sadar).
interesting_fact: A former economics student, he traded shrimp as a teenager before switching to palm oil; the name 'Gama' comes from the founders' first names, Ganda and Martua.
deep_cut_fact: His Medan hospital, Murni Teguh Memorial Hospital, is named after his mother, Murni Teguh, and was launched on the date 12/12/2012. His Gama group also built Jakarta's 64-storey Gama Tower, described as Indonesia's tallest building.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found (kpncorp.com is a parked domain). Possible routes: listed affiliates Cemindo Gemilang or Murni Sadar investor relations via IDX filings. Energy angle: palm oil/biodiesel, cement.

name: Catharina Claas-Muhlhauser
