current_role: Founder and chairman, Parker Foundation and Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy; executive chairman of Stability AI (since 2024)
profile: Napster co-founder (1999) and Facebook's first president at 24, the stake behind most of his fortune. He later backed Spotify (board until 2017), co-founded Plaxo, Causes, Airtime and Brigade, and launched the Parker Foundation in 2015 with $600m, including a $250m grant for the Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy. He became chairman of Stability AI in 2024.
interesting_fact: Parker, who has asthma and food allergies, founded the Sean N. Parker Center for Allergy & Asthma Research at Stanford in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: His father taught him to program on an Atari 800 when he was seven. In high school in Virginia he won the state computer science fair for building a web crawler and interned for Mark Pincus.
notes: No personal contact is published. The Parker Institute press email is an institutional route, not a direct one. His AI role (Stability AI chair) fits the podcast's data-center theme.

name: Leonard Schleifer
current_role: Co-founder, Board Co-Chair, President and CEO, Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: REGN)
profile: Leonard Schleifer was a young neurologist and assistant professor at Cornell when he founded Regeneron in 1988, recruiting George Yancopoulos as co-founder. He took it public in 1991 and still runs the Tarrytown, NY company, which has 12 FDA-approved medicines, including the blockbuster eye drug Eylea and Dupixent (with Sanofi). He owns about 2% of the stock.
interesting_fact: The company name means 'regenerating neurons', with 'gene' hidden in the middle; the idea was first sketched on a napkin.
deep_cut_fact: At the urging of his Queens high-school math teacher, Schleifer entered the 1970 Westinghouse Science Talent Search, the competition Regeneron itself now sponsors as the Regeneron Science Talent Search.
notes: Active public figure who speaks regularly on drug pricing and science-led management. The best route is Regeneron corporate communications. Press and IR names come from 2026 earnings releases; check the latest release for current contacts.

name: Alceu Elias Feldmann
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, Grupo Fertipar (Curitiba, Brazil)
profile: Santa Catarina-born agronomist (Federal University of Parana) who founded Fertipar in Paranagua, Parana, in 1980. He grew it into one of Brazil's largest fertilizer groups (~$3.9B revenue in 2021), a dozen-plus companies across Brazil's farm belts plus affiliated port terminal Fospar; he and his three children keep it private and he still runs it.
interesting_fact: Fertipar expanded region by region through separately branded companies: Fertigran (1984), Fertilizantes Piratini in Rio Grande do Sul (1985), then the Northeast in the 1990s, Fertipar Sudeste (1998) and Bandeirantes (2000).
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Fertipar he worked in sales at fertilizer maker Ultrafertil, travelling widely to talk with farm professionals; that region-by-region view of the sector became the basis for his own company.
notes: Very low profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is Fertipar's corporate contact page (HQ in Curitiba). Older son of the same name is a Stock Car Brasil driver. Birthplace reported inconsistently in Brazilian press (SC vs PR).

name: Geoffrey Kwok
current_role: Director, Empire Group Holdings (Hong Kong); Non-Executive Director, Sun Hung Kai Properties
profile: Eldest son of the late Walter Kwok (ex-chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties) and grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng. He studied economics at Yale, earned a Stanford MBA and worked as a Morgan Stanley investment banker. After his father died in 2018, he and his brother Jonathan took over Empire Group Holdings, which has invested over HK$29bn in property since 2010. He also joined the SHKP board.
interesting_fact: Empire Group's 'E' logomark is derived from Walter Kwok's own signature; the rest of the word 'Empire' is meant to be completed by the succeeding generation.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Walter & Wendy Kwok Family Foundation has donated to Hong Kong's Foodlink Foundation (hot meals, food waste from hotels) since 2011. Empire also runs a Kwok Scholars programme for tertiary students and opened Kimpton Tsim Sha Tsui in March 2026.
notes: Low profile. Empire Group is the more direct route, because SHKP press is controlled by the other branch of the family. Avoid the family-feud history.

name: Jonathan Kwok
current_role: Director, Empire Group Holdings (Hong Kong property developer)
profile: Younger son of the late Walter Kwok, former chairman of Sun Hung Kai Properties. After Walter's death in 2018, Jonathan and brother Geoffrey inherited his SHKP stake and took over Empire Group Holdings, the developer Walter founded; Jonathan leads its real estate investment, project development and asset management.
interesting_fact: He was ranked the world's sixth-youngest billionaire in 2020; he studied at Cornell's School of Hotel Administration and worked at CSI Properties and CMB International Securities before Empire.
deep_cut_fact: The 'E' in Empire Group's logo was handwritten by his father Walter, and Jonathan and his brother completed the remaining letters in tribute.
notes: Avoid the family feud/kidnapping history of his father. General company inbox is the only published route.

name: Chen Mingyong
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, OPPO (Guangdong Oppo Mobile Telecommunications)
profile: Chen Mingyong (Tony Chen, b. 1969, Wanyuan, Sichuan) studied at Zhejiang University, then followed Duan Yongping from Subor to BBK. He took over BBK's audio-visual business and the OPPO brand, launched OPPO's first phone in 2008, and built it into one of the world's top smartphone makers. He remains CEO and rarely gives interviews.
interesting_fact: He was one of six people who left Subor (Xiaobawang) with Duan Yongping in 1995 to start BBK, the group from which OPPO, vivo and OnePlus all descend.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Zhejiang University's information and electronic engineering department in 1992, he worked 1992-1995 at Zhongshan Subor (Xiaobawang) Electronics, the 'learning machine'/game-console maker, rising to assistant general manager.
notes: Very media-shy. press@oppo.com is the media contact in OPPO's Oct 2025 Find X9 global release (wire copy; could not re-load to verify). The SEC-insider tag 'UMC Vice President' in the input is likely a different person with the same romanized name; disregard.

name: Shi Jiazhang
current_role: Chairman, Chi Mei Corporation (since May 2026); also Director of the Chi Mei Museum and Chairman of Chi Mei Culture Foundation
profile: Hsu Chia-chang (許家彰), 62, is the only son of Chi Mei founder Shi Wen-long (許文龍). Chi Mei, based in Tainan, Taiwan, is the world's largest ABS resin maker. He has chaired Chi Mei's appliance arm (CHIMEI/新視代) since 2010 and joined the group board in 2013. In May 2026 he succeeded his father's cousin Hsu Chun-hua as chairman, pledging a shift from volume to high-spec medical, semiconductor and auto materials.
interesting_fact: On taking over, he summed up his strategy as moving Chi Mei 'from quantity to quality' and building a 'green value chain', in response to a glut of Chinese petrochemical capacity.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he was made to practise the violin every day by his father, who built the Chi Mei Museum's famous violin collection. He has called that childhood 'torment' a lifelong spiritual asset. He now directs the museum himself.

public_contacts.value: cmm@chimeimuseum.org (Chi Mei Museum, which he directs)

notes: The name in the input is a pinyin rendering; he is usually written Hsu Chia-chang (許家彰). Media-shy, he gave a rare interview to Mirror Media (鏡週刊) in mid-2026. Chi Mei's contact page is JavaScript-rendered, so no corporate press email was captured. Specialty materials for semiconductors are a possible podcast angle.

name: Chu Huafeng
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Easy Smart Group Holdings (HKEX: 2442) via Ever Genius International / Galaxy Equity Management, which he wholly owns
profile: Chu Huafeng (储华锋) is a Chinese investor. In December 2025 his vehicle Ever Genius bought 75% of Easy Smart Group, a Hong Kong passive-fire-protection subcontractor that had the largest market share there. The company says it is now looking to diversify into AI and communications, and its shares surged. The listing appears to be the source of his Hurun valuation. He was earlier an executive director of Shin Hwa World (2019-2020).
interesting_fact: Easy Smart's 2026 annual report says Galaxy Equity Management, wholly owned by Chu, controls Ever Genius. After 30 June 2026 Ever Genius sold 102M shares (25%) to Terminus Consumer Ltd, leaving it with about 39.6%.
notes: Very little public information; he is not on Easy Smart's board. MarketScreener lists him as a Hefei University of Technology graduate (unverified). Web search budget ran out mid-research, so the Chinese-language sources were not fully checked. Treat the billionaire valuation as volatile because it rests on a stock that surged on an AI pivot.

name: Isabella Seràgnoli
current_role: President (chair) and sole shareholder, Coesia S.p.A., Bologna
profile: Sole owner of Coesia, the Bologna packaging-machinery group that grew out of G.D (founded 1923, taken over by her father Enzo), whose cigarette-packing machines dominated the tobacco industry. She took over in 2002, renamed it Coesia in 2005 and diversified into many packaging sectors, while funding major Bologna philanthropy (MAST, hospices).
interesting_fact: She founded MAST (Manifattura di Arti, Sperimentazione e Tecnologia) in Bologna, a combined corporate-welfare and cultural centre known for its photography exhibitions on industry and work.
deep_cut_fact: Her family's hospice foundation funded and built 'L'Arca sull'albero', Bologna's paediatric palliative-care hospice opened in 2024, designed by Renzo Piano to sit suspended among trees in a purpose-planted wood.
notes: Very private; rarely interviewed. Best route is Coesia press office. Coesia's Corporate Governance page lists her as President with Alessandro Parimbelli as CEO.

name: Anthony Langley
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Langley Holdings plc (Bergen Engines, Piller Power Systems, Marelli Motori, Clarke Chapman)
profile: Tony Langley founded Langley Holdings in 1975, aged 20, from the remains of his grandfather's failed engineering firm. He started by selling mining equipment to the UK coal industry, then built a group of 90+ subsidiaries through acquisitions such as Clarke Chapman (2000) and Bergen Engines (2021), both bought from Rolls-Royce. He is now repositioning the group as a supplier of grid-free, behind-the-meter power for AI data centers.
interesting_fact: Bergen Engines won its first independent power order for a new US AI data center in 2025: gas engines of 11.2MW each for E-Finity Distributed Generation. In May 2026 it won more than 500MW of orders from Liberty Energy. Langley says the group 'is now principally a power equipment supplier.'
deep_cut_fact: His Gladiator team won the 2024 Rolex TP52 World Championship in Newport, RI, the first British-flagged team to take that title and his first world title as an owner. Langley called tactics after handing the helm to two-time world champion Guillermo Parada so he could learn from him.
notes: A highly relevant guest for a data-center/energy podcast. He has given trade-press interviews (Capacity, June 2026) and attends Datacloud Global Congress in Cannes with his sons. LinkedIn is the company page, not a personal profile.

name: Joe Lonsdale
current_role: Managing Partner, 8VC (Austin, TX); host of the American Optimist podcast
profile: Joe Lonsdale co-founded Palantir in 2004, then wealth-data platform Addepar (2009) and government software firm OpenGov, and started VC firm 8VC in 2015, which he moved to Austin in 2020. 8VC has about $6B in assets, with bets in defense tech, logistics and life sciences. He also founded the Cicero Institute policy think tank and co-founded the University of Austin.
interesting_fact: He began his career at Peter Thiel's hedge fund Clarium Capital straight out of Stanford, after interning at PayPal, and then helped build Palantir's first prototype in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Before Palantir, he was editor-in-chief of The Stanford Review in 2002–03. It is the student paper Peter Thiel co-founded in 1987, the link that led to his PayPal internship and Clarium job.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly: hosts his own podcast and posts a lot on X. Interested in energy and data-center policy. Best routes are press@8vc.com or X.

name: Zhang Hongchao
current_role: Founder and chairman, Mixue Group (HKEX: 2097)
profile: Founded Mixue Bingcheng from a shaved-ice stall in Zhengzhou in 1997 and grew it into a near-fully franchised chain of ultra-cheap bubble tea, lemonade, coffee (Lucky Cup) and ice cream with 50,000+ stores, more outlets than McDonald's. Mixue listed in Hong Kong in March 2025; his younger brother Zhang Hongfu is CEO.
interesting_fact: Mixue now has more locations worldwide than McDonald's, built on cones and drinks priced around 1-6 yuan, plus a vertically integrated supply chain and its 'Snow King' mascot and viral theme song.
deep_cut_fact: In June 1997, while a student in Zhengzhou (Henan University of Economics and Law), he opened his first shaved-ice stall with about 3,000 yuan borrowed from his grandmother, using a shaved-ice machine he built himself.
notes: Rarely gives interviews; Chinese-language media is the main channel. Best route is Mixue IR. Expanding overseas (Southeast Asia, US stores from 2025).

name: Zhang Hongfu
current_role: Co-chairman and executive director, Mixue Group (HKEX: 2097); stepped down as CEO in March 2026
profile: Zhang Hongfu co-founded Zhengzhou-based Mixue Bingcheng with elder brother Hongchao, joining in 2007 and serving as CEO from December 2017 to March 2026, when CFO Zhang Yuan took over. Mixue is a near-fully franchised, ultra-cheap bubble tea/ice cream chain with 50,000+ stores (incl. ~5,000 overseas), listed via a $444m Hong Kong IPO in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Mixue is the world's second-biggest freshly-made drinks seller by cups after Starbucks; the brothers are described as complementary, with Hongfu the outgoing marketing/branding mind and Hongchao the introverted operations and supply-chain lead.
deep_cut_fact: He left school in 2007 to join his brother's venture, which began in 1997 as a small cold-drink/shaved-ice stall in Zhengzhou.
notes: Mixue is HK-listed; IR site ir.mxbc.com. The 'Snow King' mascot and ultra-low-price franchise/supply-chain model are good podcast hooks. Hongfu was the brand/marketing face of the company.

name: Ramon Ang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, San Miguel Corporation; President and CEO, Top Frontier Investment Holdings
profile: Tondo-raised mechanical engineer (b. 1954) who rose from fixing and dealing used Japanese engines to running San Miguel, the Philippines' oldest conglomerate. He steered it from beer and food into power, fuel (Petron), cement and infrastructure - including the $15bn New Manila International Airport in Bulacan, the NAIA revamp and a $3.3bn LNG hub in Batangas.
interesting_fact: Per a widely told account, he met San Miguel chairman Danding Cojuangco at a car repair shop: when the mechanics couldn't diagnose Cojuangco's sports car, Ang identified the defect and was hired on the spot as his mechanic - the start of a decades-long partnership.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his mechanical engineering degree from Far Eastern University as a working student while helping in his father's auto repair shop on Jose Abad Santos Street in Tondo; FEU gave him an honorary doctorate in business engineering in 2018. He is also a former racing driver and vintage-car restorer.
notes: Highly relevant to energy (SMC Global Power, LNG, Petron) and infrastructure. Gives frequent press conferences in Manila. No dedicated press email published; SMC Corporate Affairs Office (main line +63 2 8632 3000) is the media route; IR email listed as fallback.

name: William Hockey
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Column N.A. (developer-focused nationally chartered bank); board member, Plaid
profile: Emory history/business grad who met Zach Perret as a junior Bain consultant and co-founded Plaid in 2012, the API layer connecting fintech apps to bank accounts. Left as CTO/president in 2019 and, with his wife Annie, bought a small California bank and relaunched it in 2022 as Column, a self-funded chartered bank powering fintechs such as Brex and Mercury.
interesting_fact: Rather than seek a de novo charter, he and Annie bought 94.1% of Chico-based Northern California National Bank for about $45 million in July 2021 and renamed it Column National Association that August.
deep_cut_fact: The bank he bought was a small community lender whose CEO Todd Lewis was kept on in a leadership role under the 2021 tender-offer terms, so Column's charter traces back to a Chico, California community bank.
notes: Low public profile; personal X/LinkedIn handle not verified. Column press inbox is the best route; engineering-heavy fintech/banking-infrastructure angle.

name: Patrice Motsepe
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, African Rainbow Minerals; President, Confederation of African Football (CAF, re-elected 2025)
profile: South African lawyer-turned-mining entrepreneur and the first Black African on the Forbes billionaires list (2008). He was the first Black partner at Bowman Gilfillan (1994), then bought marginal gold shafts in 1997 and built African Rainbow Minerals. He also founded African Rainbow Capital, has a stake in Sanlam, owns Mamelodi Sundowns and has led CAF since 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he became the first African to sign the Giving Pledge. His Mamelodi Sundowns have won the South African Premiership every season since 2017-18.
deep_cut_fact: His first business, Future Mining, was a contract-mining outfit that cleaned gold dust from inside the Vaal Reefs mine shafts, paying workers a low base salary plus a profit-sharing bonus. He learned business as a boy in his father's spaza shop, which served mine workers.
notes: ARM lists Betty Maloka (Senior Manager: Media Relations and Brand Management) as its media contact. Very high-profile and press-friendly; mining, energy and African-investment angles fit the podcast. He is the subject of 2026 speculation about a run for the ANC presidency.

name: Atul Ruia
current_role: Chairman, The Phoenix Mills Ltd (stepped down as managing director in Dec 2019)
profile: Third-generation scion of the Ruia textile family (Phoenix Mills founded 1905). The Wharton-educated Ruia turned the loss-making Lower Parel cotton mill into High Street Phoenix/Palladium, then built a national portfolio of 'Phoenix' and 'Palladium' malls, offices and hotels (St. Regis Mumbai, Courtyard Agra). He remains chairman of the listed company.
interesting_fact: He is not related to the Ruia family of the Essar Group, a frequent mix-up.
deep_cut_fact: The mill's redevelopment started with leisure, not shopping: in 1996 the compound opened what was billed as South Asia's largest 20-lane bowling concourse (Bowling Co., India's first bowling company and sports bar), years before the mall took shape.
notes: Low personal media profile; retired from executive duties at 48. Approach via Phoenix Mills corporate/secretarial office. Third-party sites list investorrelations@highstreetphoenix.com, but it is unverified on an official page and not included.

name: Cao Longxiang
current_role: Chairman, Hubei Jumpcan Pharmaceutical (600566.SH) and Jiangsu Jumpcan Holding Group; co-controlling shareholder with son Cao Fei
profile: Born in 1957, Cao built Jumpcan, a Taixing (Jiangsu)-based maker of western and traditional Chinese medicines, and reverse-merged it into Shanghai-listed Hubei Hongcheng in 2013. He chairs the company and Jumpcan Holding; since 2025 he and son Cao Fei jointly control about 563 million shares, and he was renominated to the 11th board in 2026.
interesting_fact: Jumpcan's best-known products are pediatric and consumer remedies such as Pudilan anti-inflammatory oral liquid and Xiaoer Chiqiao Qingre granules (children's fever granules).
deep_cut_fact: Before pharma he served in the Chinese military and managed a cement factory; he holds an EMBA and the professional title of senior economist, and once sat on the board of Jiangsu Taixing Rural Commercial Bank.
notes: Military/cement-factory detail is from Forbes bio; EMBA/senior economist/bank board from the 2026 AGM filing. Low international profile; route via company securities department (board secretary Cao Wei). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Howard Butt III
current_role: CEO and board member, H-E-B (since 2021); board member, H.E. Butt Foundation
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Howard Butt III succeeded his uncle as CEO of the family-owned Texas grocer in 2021. H-E-B has 455 stores in Texas and Mexico, about 160,000 employees and roughly $50 billion in sales. In 2025 he picked COO Roxanne Orsak as the company's first female president, starting in 2026.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity each year. The company was started in 1905 by his great-grandmother Florence Butt.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming CEO he ran H-E-B's Mexico division (as of 2016). His father, Howard E. Butt Jr., co-created the Laity Lodge retreat center in the Texas Hill Country in 1961.
notes: Keeps a low media profile. The news@heb.com address came from a search snippet of an H-E-B page that loads by JavaScript, so I could not confirm it directly; check before use. H-E-B says media inquiries go to regional Public Affairs offices.

name: Stephen Butt
current_role: President of Shareholder Relations and of the Central Market division, H-E-B; H-E-B board member
profile: Great-grandson of H-E-B founder Florence Butt and nephew of chairman Charles Butt, Stephen Butt is a member of the family that owns privately held Texas grocer H-E-B (Texas and Mexico, roughly $50bn revenue). Based in Dallas, he runs H-E-B's specialty-food Central Market format and shareholder relations and sits on the board.
interesting_fact: H-E-B gives 5% of pretax profits to charity. The first Central Market opened in Austin on 22 Jan 1994 despite advice that a store without Coke, Pepsi or Tide would fail.
deep_cut_fact: He recalls that in Central Market's second year, shoppers began carpooling from Houston and Dallas with big coolers, taking turns filling friends' shopping lists; by year three customers routinely drove 25 miles to shop there.
notes: Described by PaperCity as a 'low-key billionaire' who 'doesn't want press'. He did give Shelby Report and Dallas Morning News interviews tied to Central Market, so pitching around Central Market/food retail innovation works best via H-E-B public affairs. Note: H-E-B's CEO is not his brother (Forbes bio claim looks outdated/wrong); verify before citing.

name: Ren Yuanlin
current_role: Founder/honorary chairman, Yangzijiang Shipbuilding (son Ren Letian is executive chairman since 2020); controller of Shanshan Co. via investment platform
profile: Ren Yuanlin turned a failing state-owned Jiangyin yard into Yangzijiang Shipbuilding, one of China's largest and most profitable shipbuilders (SGX-listed). He handed the chair to son Ren Letian in 2020; in 2022 Yangzijiang Financial was spun off. In 2025 a Ren-led consortium took control of Ningbo Shanshan, the world's largest lithium-battery anode supplier, in a court-led restructuring.
interesting_fact: In late 2025 the shipping tycoon moved into EV batteries: his consortium paid about RMB 3.2bn for ~23% control of Shanshan, which holds roughly 21% of the global anode-material market, making Ren its actual controller.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the yard (then Jiangyin Shipbuilding Factory) in the 1970s as a young technician, ran its ship-body (hull) workshop, rose to factory supervisor and became chairman in 1997.
notes: Very private; no personal channels. Strong energy/battery angle via Shanshan. Separate entity Yangzijiang Maritime Development (public@yzjmaritime.com, per search result only) is not the shipbuilder. SGX filing on Shanshan: https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/J4HMJ4YW8Z36QGX3/2a2655ec83d9aa4d67ba46901f928072638151dc862fbdce983b03daa9c28c51

name: Mark Davis
current_role: Owner and managing general partner, Las Vegas Raiders (NFL); owner, Las Vegas Aces (WNBA)
profile: Son of Raiders legend Al Davis, Mark Davis spent his whole career inside the team, starting in the equipment room and team retail, and inherited control after his father's death in 2011. He moved the franchise from Oakland to Las Vegas in 2020 and Allegiant Stadium; the team is now valued at over $7bn (vs $761m in 2011). He bought the WNBA's Aces in 2021.
interesting_fact: While working in Raiders team retail he is said to have invented the muff-style hand warmer now used across the NFL.
deep_cut_fact: A Chico State alumnus, he long kept driving from Oakland back to Chico to see his favourite barber for his trademark bowl cut, and famously drove a 1997 Dodge Caravan with a VHS player.
notes: Approachable, unpretentious reputation but gives few long interviews (ESPN's Tim Keown profile is a rare one). Aces dynasty (WNBA titles) and Las Vegas stadium economics are natural podcast angles. Route via Raiders communications department.

name: Eduard Schleicher
current_role: Managing partner / co-managing director, SCHWENK Zement GmbH & Co. KG (Ulm); supervisory board member at PAUL HARTMANN AG and Wieland-Werke AG
profile: Fifth-generation member of the Schwenk family behind Ulm-based SCHWENK, a cement maker founded in 1847 that now also spans concrete, sand & gravel and concrete pumps, with ~4,500 staff across Germany and Central/Eastern Europe. Schleicher co-leads the group and drives its international expansion; he formerly sat on Heidelberg Materials' supervisory board.
interesting_fact: SCHWENK's Mergelstetten cement plant hosts catch4climate, a >EUR120M oxyfuel carbon-capture pilot run jointly with rivals Heidelberg Materials, Buzzi/Dyckerhoff and Vicat; it captured its first high-purity CO2 (as dry ice) in July 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal coverage. catch4climate CO2 capture is a strong energy/decarbonisation angle; route via SCHWENK corporate communications. Board roles per https://de.marketscreener.com/insider/EDUARD-SCHLEICHER-A09UUA/ (aggregator).

name: Ursula Hutter-Schleicher
current_role: Family shareholder in SCHWENK Zement (Ulm), per Forbes; no public operating role found
profile: Forbes says her fortune comes from SCHWENK, a family-owned Ulm building-materials group founded in 1847 that makes cement, concrete, sand and gravel and employs about 4,500 people. Her brother Eduard Schleicher, the fifth generation, runs the company. I found no public statements, interviews or a separate profile for her. She is not the late CSU politician Ursula Schleicher.
interesting_fact: SCHWENK is one of Germany's oldest family firms: Carl Schwenk founded it in Ulm in 1847, and the family has run it for five generations.
notes: Very private: only Forbes mentions her. The only route is the SCHWENK corporate contact (general company email), probably via the company's management, which her brother Eduard Schleicher leads. Cement links to the energy and decarbonisation angle.

name: Zhang Lei
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Hillhouse Investment (Hillhouse Capital)
profile: Henan-born investor who studied at Renmin University and Yale SOM (MBA 2002) and worked in Yale's Investments Office under David Swensen. He founded Hillhouse in 2005 with seed capital from Yale's endowment and built it into one of Asia's largest investment firms, with early stakes in Tencent, JD.com and BeiGene and buyouts such as Belle International.
interesting_fact: Hillhouse began in 2005 with a startup investment from Yale's endowment, after Zhang had worked under endowment pioneer David Swensen; he later set out his long-term philosophy in the 2020 book 'Value'.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010, less than 10 years after graduating, he pledged exactly $8,888,888 to Yale SOM for its new campus - reportedly the largest gift ever by a SOM graduate - choosing the number because eight signifies fortune in Chinese.
notes: Rarely does English-language podcasts; firm communications go through Hillhouse. Best route is the firm's published general contact.

name: Charles R. Bronfman
current_role: Retired co-chairman of Seagram; philanthropist (honoree of The Charles Bronfman Prize)
profile: Charles Bronfman, born 1931, is a son of Seagram founder Samuel Bronfman. He spent 50 years at Seagram, retiring as co-chairman in 2001, and owned the Montreal Expos from 1968 to 1991. He chaired the Andrea and Charles Bronfman Philanthropies for 30 years and co-founded Birthright Israel.
interesting_fact: He brought Major League Baseball to Canada as the founding principal owner of the Montreal Expos, the first MLB franchise outside the U.S., and owned the team for about 22 years.
deep_cut_fact: His CRB Foundation came up with the Heritage Minutes, the 60-second Canadian history shorts that first aired on CBC on 31 March 1991. He later co-founded Historica Canada, which still produces them.
notes: He is 95, so an interview may be difficult. There is no published personal or office email. The Charles Bronfman Prize (founded by his children) is the nearest official channel. His 2016 memoir 'Distilled' covers Seagram, the Expos and the Heritage Minutes and is a good hook.

name: David Rockefeller, Sr.
profile: Former Chase Manhattan chairman and Rockefeller family patriarch. Died March 20, 2017, aged 101.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Rockefeller).

name: Akira Mori
current_role: Chairman, Mori Trust Co., Ltd.; founder and chairman, MA Platform
profile: Kyoto-born (1936) Tokyo property developer, son of Mori Building founder Taikichiro Mori. He and brother Minoru inherited the family business in 1993 and split it in 1999; Akira built Mori Trust (Marunouchi Trust City, Tokyo Shiodome Building, Conrad Tokyo and ~30 hotels). In 2016 he handed the CEO role to his daughter Miwako Date and became chairman.
interesting_fact: Mori Trust helped create Japan's REIT market and listed Mori Trust Sogo REIT; the group also brought Conrad and Shangri-La hotels to Japan and turned around the historic Karuizawa Manpei Hotel.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent 12 years as a banker: after graduating in economics from Keio in 1960 he joined Yasuda Trust and Banking, only joining Mori Building in 1972; in 1973 he founded Mori Trust Hotels & Resorts.
notes: Input record listed only 'Akira' (shared with Minoru Mori, Forbes 1996-98); this is Akira Mori of Mori Trust. Age ~90; daughter Miwako Date runs day-to-day operations. Route via Mori Trust corporate contact.

name: Maersk Mc-kinney Moller
notes: Mærsk Mc-Kinney Møller, longtime head of A.P. Moller–Maersk, died 16 April 2012 (aged 98). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A6rsk_Mc-Kinney_M%C3%B8ller

name: Rosa Anna Magno Garavoglia
profile: Died 22 November 2016, as announced by Gruppo Campari. Her controlling stake, held through Alicros, passed to her son Luca Garavoglia, Campari's chairman.
notes: Deceased (2016); source is Campari's press release. For the Campari angle, approach her son Luca Garavoglia, chairman of Davide Campari-Milano.

name: Denis Defforey
profile: Co-founder of French hypermarket chain Carrefour (1959) and its CEO 1985-1990. Died 6 February 2006 aged 80.
notes: Deceased (d. 6 Feb 2006). Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Denis_Defforey (cites Le Monde obituary, 14 Feb 2006).

name: Richard Chang
current_role: Vice Chairman and President, ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. (Taiwan)
profile: Richard H.P. Chang co-founded Advanced Semiconductor Engineering (ASE) in Kaohsiung in 1984 with his elder brother Jason; it is now ASE Technology Holding, the world's largest provider of chip assembly, packaging and test services, a key beneficiary of advanced packaging demand for AI chips. He is vice chairman/president, and with Jason a main investor in developer Sino Horizon.
interesting_fact: In the early 1980s the Chang family was already successful in property, but Richard argued Taiwan's nascent electronics industry was the bigger long-term bet; their mother sold properties to cover ASE's losses in its first three years.
deep_cut_fact: He was ASE's founding President from March 1984 (when the first Kaohsiung plant started with about 200 people) until becoming Vice Chairman in 1999, and holds an industrial engineering degree from Chung Yuan Christian University in Taiwan.
notes: Taiwanese family but Forbes lists him under Hong Kong. Low public profile; brother Jason Chang (chairman) is the public face. Best route is ASE corporate PR. ASE is highly relevant to AI/data-center chip packaging (CoWoS-type capacity).

name: Hsieh Wen-Ta
current_role: Chairman, Hon. Precision Inc. (鴻勁精密, TWSE: 7769), Taichung, Taiwan
profile: Hsieh Wen-Ta (謝旼達) founded Hon. Precision's predecessor in 1999 to build IC test handlers; the company now holds about a third of that market and adds active thermal control and liquid-cooling plates, supplying TSMC, Nvidia and ASE. AI/HPC orders drive about 70% of sales. He took it public on the Taiwan Stock Exchange on Nov 27, 2025.
interesting_fact: Hon. Precision's Nov 2025 TWSE debut set Taiwan listing records: it opened at NT$1,495 (an all-time high listing price) and jumped NT$1,445 on its first day, briefly pushing its market cap near UMC's.
deep_cut_fact: A machine-design graduate of Taipei Institute of Technology (台北工專機械設計科), Hsieh came out of Taiwan's machine-tool trade. Commentator Hsieh Chin-ho noted he wears work clothes on the floor of his Taichung factory, tucked in a lane off Daya Road, so visitors may not realise he's the boss.
notes: Very low-profile engineer-founder; rarely interviewed. Hon Precision is unrelated to Hon Hai/Foxconn despite the name. The SEC insider roles listed (Amprius, Ambiq, Desktop Metal director) belong to a different person, Wen Hsieh (a US venture capitalist), not this Hsieh Wen-Ta. Route via company IR.

name: Zhang Shuangwang
current_role: Founder of Inner Mongolia Yitai Group; legal representative of Inner Mongolia Yitai Investment Co., the de facto controller of Yitai Coal (per 2022 annual report)
profile: Zhang Shuangwang (张双旺), born 1943 in Jungar Banner, Inner Mongolia, was a local government official before founding Yitai in 1988. Yitai grew into a large Ordos-based group spanning coal mining, coal railways and coal-to-liquids, controlling listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal (SSE B-shares/HKEX). He is recorded as responsible person of the group's holding company, Yitai Investment.
interesting_fact: Yitai Coal's ultimate controller, Inner Mongolia Yitai Investment Co., is itself owned by 2,315 individual shareholders rather than one family vehicle; Zhang Shuangwang is its legal representative.
deep_cut_fact: In March 1988 Zhang gave up his post as deputy head of the Ikh Ju League (now Ordos) township-enterprise office and led 21 surplus government staff out of the civil service to start Yitai; he was later named a National Model Worker (1995).
notes: Born 1943 (about 83). No death reports found and he is still on Hurun lists through 2026, but there is no recent public activity, so alive is marked unknown. Wealth is shared with Zhang Donghai, former Yitai Coal chairman. Very low public profile; the only route is Yitai Coal's board secretary/IR office. Current day-to-day chairman of Yitai Coal is Zhang Jingquan.

name: Zhang Donghai
current_role: Reported as president/director of Inner Mongolia Yitai Group; chaired listed Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal until late 2019 (current group title not confirmed by official source)
profile: Zhang Donghai is the son of Zhang Shuangwang, who founded Ordos-based coal producer Yitai Group in 1988. Donghai joined in 2001, became group general manager in 2004 and long chaired Inner Mongolia Yitai Coal, which expanded into railways and coal-to-liquids. Zhang Jingquan succeeded him as Yitai Coal chairman in Dec 2019; the family shares the fortune.
interesting_fact: Yitai began in 1988 when his father quit a government post and led 21 surplus civil servants to start the company; Yitai Coal later became China's first coal company listed via B shares and expanded into coal-to-liquid fuels.
deep_cut_fact: In 2001, during Yitai's hardest period, he resigned a division-level post in the Inner Mongolia regional government to join a Yitai subsidiary as general manager; cost controls in his first year alone added about RMB 12 million, and he launched the 'Yitai clean coal' brand with national research institutes.
notes: Low public profile; little recent English-language coverage. Fortune shared with father Zhang Shuangwang (Hurun). No verified published personal/office contact found; Yitai corporate websites did not load. Best route is likely Yitai Coal's company secretary/IR via HKEX or SSE filings.

name: Ding Hui
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder (~26%), Shenzhen JLC Technology Group (嘉立创, SZSE: 001232)
profile: Born 1979 in Xuzhou, Jiangsu, Ding Hui moved to Shenzhen at 17, rose from electronics-factory apprentice to supervisor, then founded PCB trader Zhongxinhua. He and his brother invested in Yuan Jiangtao's JLC from 2012 and merged their businesses in 2021; JLC (PCB prototyping, component e-commerce, EDA) listed on the Shenzhen main board on 4 Aug 2026 at a market cap above RMB100bn.
interesting_fact: JLC serves engineers' small-batch PCB orders at scale: over 21 million orders a year and 9.5m+ registered online users by end-2025; CATL subscribed as a strategic investor in its 2026 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he started out in a ~20 sq m rented room in an urban village on Shenzhen's outskirts selling electronics; he recalled having 'no money and no goods' and taking any customer that earned a few hundred yuan just to survive.
notes: Dataset lists industry as semiconductors; JLC is actually PCB/electronics manufacturing platform (hardware supply chain for AI/data-center prototyping). Very low media profile; route via board secretary office.

name: Ding Huixiang
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (26.25% pre-IPO), Shenzhen JLC Technology Group (嘉立创 / JLCPCB); listed as director and deputy GM in the prospectus (one report says he left those posts in April 2026)
profile: Ding Huixiang (b. 1982, Suining, Xuzhou, Jiangsu) is a co-founder of JLC, the PCB prototyping and electronics-components platform behind JLCPCB, LCSC and EasyEDA, with his elder brother Ding Hui and Yuan Jiangtao. JLC listed on the Shenzhen main board on 4 Aug 2026 at RMB 84.46/share and topped RMB 100bn market cap; 2025 revenue was RMB 10.2bn.
interesting_fact: All three JLC founders hold only junior-college (dazhuan) diplomas; the business grew from a shared counter less than one metre wide in Shenzhen's Huaqiangbei electronics market into a 100-billion-yuan listed company with ~9.6m registered engineer users.
deep_cut_fact: Before JLC, he joined his brother's PCB maker Zhongxinhua (founded 2004). In Dec 2012 he personally put RMB 600,000 into Yuan Jiangtao's then-small JLC for a 60% stake, later passing half to his brother; this deal merged the two founding lines.
notes: Low public profile; brother Ding Hui (chairman) and Yuan Jiangtao (GM) are the public faces. Reports conflict on whether he still holds director/VP posts after April 2026; check latest SZSE filings. Best route is JLC's board-secretary/IR office via its SZSE disclosures.

name: Ryan Smith
current_role: Co-founder and board member of Qualtrics; chairman of Smith Entertainment Group (owner of the Utah Jazz and Utah Mammoth)
profile: Utah tech billionaire who co-founded survey and experience-management software firm Qualtrics with his father and brother while at BYU. SAP bought it for $8B in 2019 and later spun it off, and Silver Lake took it private in 2023. He now runs Smith Entertainment Group, which owns the NBA's Utah Jazz and the NHL's Utah Mammoth, and remains a Qualtrics shareholder.
interesting_fact: He brought the NHL to Utah: in 2024 the league granted him an expansion franchise, and he paid $1.2B for the Arizona Coyotes' hockey assets. The team became the Utah Mammoth.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of BYU's Marriott School in his junior year to build Qualtrics. He went back and finished his degree in 2016, when he was already a billionaire CEO. Before that he served a two-year church mission in Mexico.
notes: In Feb 2026 Qualtrics named Jason Maynard CEO, with Jim Whitehurst as executive chairman. Older sources still call Smith executive chairman, so describe him as co-founder. He sold his stake in Real Salt Lake in 2025. X handle @RyanSmith belongs to a different person. For sports or media topics, the best route is probably SEG or Utah Jazz communications.

name: Michelle Zatlyn
current_role: Co-founder, President and Board Co-Chair, Cloudflare, Inc. (NYSE: NET); director, Atlassian
profile: Canadian-born Zatlyn co-founded internet infrastructure and security company Cloudflare in 2009 with Harvard Business School classmate Matthew Prince (and Lee Holloway). Cloudflare IPO'd in 2019 and hit $2.2B revenue in 2025; she owns ~2% and is president and board co-chair. Earlier: Google intern, Toshiba product manager, founding team of Achievers (I Love Rewards).
interesting_fact: She studied chemistry at McGill (BSc 2001) before her HBS MBA, and was named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 (2017) and C100's 2019 'Icon of Canadian Entrepreneurship'.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in Prince Albert, Saskatchewan, attending Ecole Holy Cross and Carlton Comprehensive High School, where she was captain of the basketball team; she has urged Saskatchewan entrepreneurs to 'lean in' to tech.
notes: Talks to media often about Cloudflare, AI crawler and bot policy, and internet infrastructure, so she is a good fit for the data-center and AI angle. The best route is Cloudflare press. Her X handle is not verified, so it is left out.

name: Alexandr Wang
current_role: Chief AI Officer, Meta Platforms (leads Meta Superintelligence Labs); board member, Scale AI
profile: Wang co-founded Scale AI in 2016 at age 19, after dropping out of MIT. Scale became the leading data-labelling and model-evaluation supplier to AI labs and the Pentagon. In June 2025 Meta bought 49% of Scale for $14.3B, and Wang left as CEO to become Meta's Chief AI Officer. Mid-2026 reporting still had him in that role, leading Meta's frontier-model (TBD Lab) work.
interesting_fact: He grew up in Los Alamos, New Mexico, the son of two Los Alamos National Laboratory physicists. As a teen he was a USACO finalist and made the 2014 US Physics Team, then took full-time engineering jobs at Addepar and Quora at 17.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2025 he co-wrote 'Superintelligence Strategy' with Dan Hendrycks and Eric Schmidt. The paper introduced 'Mutual Assured AI Malfunction' (MAIM), a deterrence idea modelled on nuclear MAD that explicitly covers the sabotage of rivals' datacenters.
notes: Very high-demand executive. The Meta communications/newsroom team is the likely route. His Superintelligence Strategy paper fits the podcast's data-center/energy angle.

name: Micree Zhan
current_role: Co-founder and controlling shareholder (CEO/legal representative since 2021), Bitmain Technologies, Beijing
profile: Chinese electronics engineer (b. 1979, Fujian) who co-founded Bitmain with Jihan Wu in 2013 and designed the ASIC chips behind its Antminer rigs, making it the largest bitcoin-mining hardware maker. Ousted in 2019, he regained control in a 2021 settlement, buying out Wu's camp for ~$600m. Late-2025 crypto-press reports of a fine/detention are unconfirmed.
interesting_fact: Forbes reports he first met cofounder Jihan Wu via a chance encounter on a Beijing street while working on a TV set-top-box startup; in 2018 Hurun named him the world's richest crypto entrepreneur.
deep_cut_fact: After a microelectronics master's at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Microelectronics (2004), he was an engineer at Tsinghua University's IT Research Institute, then ran DivaIP, a set-top-box startup, before Bitmain. He grew up in Minhou County, Fujian (Minhou No.1 High School).
notes: Very private; no personal channels found. Dec 2025 crypto-media rumors of regulatory fines/detention unverified - check status before outreach. Bitmain publishes only sales/supplier emails (sales.apac@bitmain.com) on its homepage, no press email.

name: Li Zhaoting
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Tunghsu Group (Dongxu Group); barred from China's securities markets for life
profile: Hebei-born (1965) engineer and former NPC deputy who built Tunghsu Group (Shijiazhuang) into a glass-substrate, optoelectronics, solar and EV conglomerate with three listed firms. After 2019–20 bond defaults, regulators found multiyear financial fraud, fined the group and Li personally and banned him from the market for life.
interesting_fact: Before founding Tunghsu he spent years at the Shijiazhuang Diesel Engine Factory after graduating in mechanical engineering in 1986, rising from technician to deputy general manager.
notes: Not recommended for outreach. Hebei regulators fined him personally about US$870M (reported) and imposed a lifetime market ban over the Tunghsu fraud. Caixin covered the auditor's record penalty in April 2026. No sign he has died, but there are no recent public appearances. No public contact routes found.

name: Li Qing
profile: Li Qing (李青) was listed by Hurun (2019-2021) jointly with Li Zhaoting, founder of Shijiazhuang-based Tunghsu Group (东旭集团), a maker of LCD glass substrates, optoelectronics and solar businesses. No public information about Li Qing's own role could be found; Hurun pairings like this usually denote a spouse or family member.
interesting_fact: Li Zhaoting founded Tunghsu's predecessor in 1997 after quitting a state job, taking 20-odd former subordinates and his wife's entire savings with him.
notes: Not a good outreach target: Tunghsu group has been in a prolonged debt crisis, and a Feb 2026 filing by Shanghai Challenge Textile (嘉麟杰) said Li Zhaoting had been detained by Shijiazhuang police (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2290214). Li Qing has no public profile; identity unconfirmed.

name: Yang Yafei
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Shenzhen DapuStor Microelectronics (大普微, SZSE ChiNext: 301666)
profile: Born 1979, BUPT-trained engineer with a PhD from the University of Rhode Island who spent years at Qualcomm before returning to China in 2016 to found DapuStor in Shenzhen, making enterprise SSD controller chips and SSDs for data centers. DapuStor listed on ChiNext in April 2026 as the board's first unprofitable IPO, surging ~350% on day one to a >RMB100bn market cap.
interesting_fact: DapuStor was the first loss-making company ever to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board (April 2026); its shares opened up nearly 350% and the market cap passed RMB 100 billion on day one.
deep_cut_fact: He studied industrial automation at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications (class of 1998), earned an EE PhD at the University of Rhode Island in 2008, then rose from senior to senior staff engineer at Qualcomm; he chose Longgang because Shenzhen is hardware's 'China Silicon Valley'.
notes: Strong data-center storage angle (enterprise SSDs/controllers for AI servers). IR email from 2025 annual report summary; IR phone 0755-89932506 also published there. Chinese-language outreach likely needed.

name: CC Leung
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Quanta Computer (Taiwan)
profile: C.C. (Chee-Chun) Leung (梁次震) co-founded Quanta Computer in 1988 with fellow NTU alumnus Barry Lam, after serving as a VP at Kinpo Electronics. Quanta became the world's largest contract notebook maker and is now a leading builder of AI servers and racks for hyperscalers. He remains vice chairman and comments on the AI server outlook.
interesting_fact: A physics graduate of National Taiwan University (unlike EE-trained co-founder Barry Lam), Leung gave NT$205 million to his alma mater to support basic research.
deep_cut_fact: National Taiwan University's Leung Center for Cosmology and Particle Astrophysics (LeCosPA), founded in 2007, was created with his donation; in July 2025 it became host of the new Max Planck-IAS-NTU Center for particle physics, cosmology and geometry.
notes: Low-profile; speaks to Taiwanese press mainly at Quanta AGMs/events. No published personal or IR email found; Quanta routes media via designated spokespersons (contact via quantatw.com). LeCosPA physics connection is a strong conversation opener.

name: Rajeev Juneja
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Mankind Pharma (New Delhi); President, PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (2025-26)
profile: Co-founded Mankind Pharma with elder brother Ramesh Juneja (company started 1991 with ~20 staff and INR 5M seed capital; incorporated 1995). Mankind sells affordable generics plus consumer brands (Manforce condoms, Prega News). He led its May 2023 IPO and the 2024 INR 13,630 crore acquisition of Bharat Serums and Vaccines.
interesting_fact: He and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart; Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
deep_cut_fact: He credits Mankind's growth to a 'startup culture' and the mantra of staying dynamic: 'In a fast-changing world, you cannot remain stationary... Every day is a new day.' He also said of the IPO: 'It makes you more responsible.'
notes: Also reachable via PHDCCI (industry chamber) in his presidency role. Company also lists investors@mankindpharma.com.

name: Daniel Pritzker
current_role: Musician/filmmaker; president and director, Jay Pritzker Foundation
profile: Son of Hyatt co-founder Jay Pritzker and one of the Chicago Pritzker family's billionaire heirs (Hyatt and family investments). Rather than run the business, he became a musician and filmmaker: he founded the band Sonia Dada and wrote and directed films on jazz pioneers, including Louis (2010) and Bolden (2019), which he self-funded over more than a decade.
interesting_fact: He bought Jerry Garcia's 'Wolf' guitar for $790,000 in 2002 and put it up for a 2017 charity auction. The sale raised $3.2 million for the Southern Poverty Law Center.
deep_cut_fact: He formed Sonia Dada in Chicago in 1990 after hearing three singers performing in a subway station. Their 1992 single 'You Don't Treat Me No Good' spent four weeks at No. 1 in Australia and was the third-best-selling single there in 1993.
notes: No personal social accounts or published email found. The Jay Pritzker Foundation (Tufts BA 1981, Northwestern JD 1986; the foundation funded the $10m Pritzker Challenge at Tufts) is invitation-only. The band site/Facebook (facebook.com/soniadadaband) is the only public channel tied to him.

name: Senapathy Gopalakrishnan
current_role: Chairman, Axilor Ventures (Bengaluru seed fund and accelerator); co-founder of Infosys
profile: Kris Gopalakrishnan co-founded Infosys in 1981 and served as its CEO and MD (2007-11) and vice chairman (2011-14). Since retiring he has chaired Axilor Ventures, which backs early-stage and deep-tech startups. He is one of India's biggest funders of brain research, at IISc and IIT Madras, and a frequent voice on AI and 'Unicorn 2.0' deep tech.
interesting_fact: He gave Rs 225 crore to set up IISc's Centre for Brain Research, the largest gift the institute had ever received from an individual. He also funded IIT Madras's Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre, which maps human brains at cellular resolution.
deep_cut_fact: Data-policy hook: he chaired the Indian government's (MeitY) expert committee on a Non-Personal Data Governance Framework and was the first chairperson of the Reserve Bank Innovation Hub. Trained as a physicist (M.Sc. Physics, IIT Madras, 1977), he began as a software engineer at Patni Computer Systems in 1979.
notes: Very accessible and a frequent speaker at CII, startup and AI events. He talks openly about AI's impact on IT services, so he is a strong fit for a data and AI podcast. Best route is through Axilor or CII; Itihaasa (itihaasa.com) is his IT-history project.

name: Matteo Danieli
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons (Milan); has served as VP of Product / former Chief Product Officer
profile: Italian engineer who co-founded Bending Spoons in 2013 with Luca Ferrari, Francesco Patarnello and Luca Querella after their note-taking startup Evertale failed. Largely bootstrapped until 2022, Bending Spoons buys apps with loyal users and overhauls them (Evernote, Meetup, WeTransfer, Eventbrite, Vimeo, AOL) and was valued at ~$11B in October 2025, Italy's most valuable startup.
interesting_fact: The four cofounders met while studying in Copenhagen; their first venture, Evertale, failed before they relaunched as Bending Spoons and later moved to Milan.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1984, he graduated with honours in Information Engineering from the University of Padua through the T.I.M.E. double-degree programme with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), where the Copenhagen connection began; he was Evertale's CTO.
notes: Lower-profile than CEO Luca Ferrari. Reportedly stepped down from the CPO role because he felt someone else could add more value, in line with the company's meritocracy culture (per a Sourcery interview summary, unverified). Has appeared on podcasts, so he may be open to one.

name: Yu Zhuyun
current_role: Chairman, Central New Energy Holding Group (HKEX: 1735) and Anhui Central Holding Group
profile: Zhejiang-born former soldier who worked at Comba Telecom in Hong Kong, sold his shares after Comba's 2003 IPO and founded Central Holding Group in Anhui in 2004. The group spans construction, real estate, logistics, wellness and, increasingly, solar module manufacturing, PV EPC, energy management and hydrogen/ammonia/methanol; he owns ~68% of HK-listed Central New Energy.
interesting_fact: His fortune was seeded by telecom, not property: he sold his stake in Comba Telecom after its 2003 Hong Kong listing and used the capital to start Central Holding Group in March 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Born in a village in Quzhou, Zhejiang, he served four years as a soldier in Anhui in the late 1980s and later returned to Anhui to found his group; in 2018 he committed 5 billion yuan to a healthcare and nursing complex in Qujiang district of his hometown.
notes: Strong energy angle (PV, hydrogen-ammonia-methanol). Low English-language profile; outreach likely needs Chinese. Contacts are listed-company secretary channels.

name: William Chisholm
current_role: Managing Partner, STG (Symphony Technology Group); Governor and principal owner, Boston Celtics
profile: Massachusetts-raised private equity investor who co-founded Symphony Technology Group with Romesh Wadhwani in 2002 and built it into STG, a software-focused PE firm in Menlo Park. In 2025 he led the group that bought the Boston Celtics for a record $6.1 billion, the highest price ever paid for a US sports team at the time.
interesting_fact: He was on Dartmouth varsity soccer teams that won Ivy League titles in 1988 and 1990, after captaining Brooks School in New England prep soccer.
deep_cut_fact: He left Dartmouth intending to become a teacher, but was drawn by the competitiveness of finance and began his career as an investment banker at PaineWebber before Bain & Co. and venture capital.

public_contacts.value: Prior podcast appearance: Celtics Talk - 'From fan to owner of the Boston Celtics: The Bill Chisholm interview'

notes: Basketballjournal URL slug may differ slightly; Boston Globe paywalled. Route via STG HQ general inbox or Celtics PR. Has done podcast interviews since the purchase.

name: Tung Chee Hwa
profile: Shipping heir (Orient Overseas/OOCL) and Hong Kong's first Chief Executive (1997-2005). He died on 8 September 2026, aged 89.
interesting_fact: He was Hong Kong's first post-colonial leader. In 2018 he and his brother sold the family's 68.7% stake in Orient Overseas to COSCO for about $4.3bn.
notes: Died 8 September 2026 (SCMP, AP, The Standard: https://www.thestandard.com.hk/news/article/342223/Hong-Kongs-first-chief-executive-Tung-Chee-hwa-dies-at-89). Not a candidate.

name: Hiroshi Mikitani
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Rakuten Group, Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Kobe-born ex-Industrial Bank of Japan banker (Harvard MBA 1993) who founded Rakuten in 1997 and built it into one of Japan's biggest e-commerce, fintech and telecom groups, including the 2020 launch of Rakuten Mobile. Through Rakuten he is also a 10%+ owner of satellite-to-phone company AST SpaceMobile.
interesting_fact: In 2010 he made English Rakuten's official internal language ('Englishnization'), later a Harvard Business Review case study. In 2011 he quit Keidanren after Fukushima, partly over its backing for continued reliance on nuclear power.
deep_cut_fact: Rakuten Ichiba went live on May 1, 1997 with just 13 shops and 6 employees, funded with $250,000 of the founders' own money. As a boy he lived in New Haven, Connecticut (1972-74) while his economist father taught at Yale.
notes: Nickname 'Mickey'. Strong podcast angles: Rakuten Mobile, AST SpaceMobile, his public position on energy policy after Fukushima. Avoid Rakuten's losses. Media enquiries go through the Rakuten press contact form.

name: Chan Tan Ching-fen
current_role: Matriarch and largest shareholder of Hang Lung Group (Hong Kong)
profile: Chan Tan Ching-fen is the widow of Hang Lung Group founder Chan Tseng-hsi (T.H. Chan, d. 1986) and controls the largest shareholding in the Hong Kong property developer. Her son Ronnie Chan ran Hang Lung until 2024, when grandson Adriel Chan became chair; son Gerald leads Morningside Group.
interesting_fact: Her father, Tan Hui-kuk, was a second cousin of Sun Yat-sen, founding father of the Republic of China, and provided Sun with financial support.
deep_cut_fact: Trained as a nurse, in the 1950s she gave cholera vaccinations to neighbourhood children in the family kitchen; her sons later named Harvard's T.H. Chan School of Public Health after her husband with a $350M gift in 2014.
notes: Alive status based on her live Forbes real-time listing (Nov 2026); age not published and she is very elderly and entirely private. Not a realistic podcast guest; family business-facing figures are Ronnie, Gerald and Adriel Chan. Web-search budget ran out during this lane, so status not separately verified.

name: Zhang Tao
current_role: Founder of Dianping; major shareholder of Meituan (no longer in management)
profile: Shanghai-born Zhang moved to the US in 1994, studied at DePauw University and spent three years in consulting before a Wharton MBA (2002). He returned to China in 2003 and founded restaurant-review site Dianping, which merged with Meituan in 2015. Meituan listed in Hong Kong in 2018, and his fortune comes from his stake in it.
interesting_fact: Dianping was founded in early 2003, two years before Yelp, and was one of the first companies funded by Sequoia China (2005).
deep_cut_fact: Before Wharton, Zhang studied at DePauw University, a small liberal-arts college in Indiana. In a 2009 interview he credited Dianping's early start in China to the country's food culture: 'Chinese people just love to eat.'
notes: Low profile since stepping back from Meituan management. Past interviews: Wharton Knowledge and the Sinica/China Project podcast (2018). The only published Meituan email is a complaints inbox (not useful), and no IR/press email was found. No personal channels found.

name: Choo Chong Ngen
current_role: Founder, Worldwide Hotels Group (Hotel 81 and other brands), Singapore
profile: Singapore hotelier who made his first money in textiles, then launched the Hotel 81 budget chain in Geylang in 1995. His private Worldwide Hotels group, run with daughter Carolyn since 2002, has about 41 hotels in Singapore and has expanded since 2017 into Australia, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea and Thailand. In 2024 it opened the world's largest Mercure (989 rooms) on Club Street.
interesting_fact: Choo dropped out of school and worked as a fishmonger to help support his family before going into textiles and then hotels.
deep_cut_fact: He named his first Hotel 81 (1995) after the unit number of his home at the time.
notes: Very low profile. Alive is inferred from his presence on Forbes real-time 2026. Daughter Carolyn Choo runs day-to-day operations, so the company's general channels are the realistic route. The deep-cut fact comes from Forbes's fact list, so he may already know it is public.

name: Lucio Tan
current_role: Founder and Chairman, LT Group Inc. (tobacco, spirits, beer, banking, property; parent links to Philippine Airlines)
profile: Born in China and raised in the Philippines, Lucio Tan co-founded Fortune Tobacco in 1966 and built it into LT Group, with interests in tobacco (PMFTC), Tanduay rum, Asia Brewery (1982), Philippine National Bank and property. He also controls flag carrier Philippine Airlines through PAL Holdings. In 2023 his grandson Lucio Tan III became president of LT Group and PAL Holdings.
interesting_fact: Before becoming a tycoon he worked as a janitor in a tobacco factory while studying chemical engineering at Far Eastern University, and was later promoted to tobacco 'cook' mixing blends.
deep_cut_fact: Tan says he went to school barefoot as a child; decades later he was expanding into nickel mining to ride the EV-battery-driven nickel boom.
notes: In his 90s (born 1933/34); day-to-day leadership is moving to grandson Lucio Tan III. Enjoys riding helicopters (Forbes). LT Group IR is named in PSE Edge disclosures (https://edge.pse.com.ph/downloadHtml.do?file_id=1987230), but no clean email was verified. Very limited personal media presence.

name: Satyanarayana Chava
current_role: Founder and CEO, Laurus Labs (Hyderabad)
profile: Organic chemist (PhD) who spent about a decade in pharma, at Ranbaxy and then at Matrix Labs, where he rose to COO. He founded Laurus Labs in Hyderabad in 2005 as an R&D firm. It now supplies APIs and formulations for HIV, cancer, asthma and diabetes drugs and has expanded into CDMO and biotech. He still spends about 25% of his time in the labs.
interesting_fact: He is a named co-inventor on about 145 patents granted to Laurus Labs, and in his spare time he enjoys cooking Indian food and sweets.
deep_cut_fact: As founder and first employee he never held 50% of Laurus Labs. In 2006, a year after founding, he set aside 5% of the company's equity for employee stock options.
notes: He won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2021 (Life Sciences & Healthcare category), and he serves on the USP board of trustees. I found no dedicated press email; the secretarial inbox is the published investor channel.

name: Shlomo Eliahu
current_role: Controlling shareholder and director, Migdal Insurance & Financial Holdings (stepped down as chair in 2022); chairman, Eliahu Insurance
profile: Born in Baghdad in 1936, Eliahu emigrated to Israel at 14 and grew up in a transit camp and south Tel Aviv. He opened an insurance agency in 1955, founded Eliahu Insurance (the first company licensed to sell insurance after statehood), was a Knesset member 1977-1981, and in 2012 bought control of Migdal, Israel's leading insurer, where he remains controlling holder.
interesting_fact: He served in the Knesset (Dash/Democratic Movement, then his own Ahva faction) and chaired the Knesset's capital-markets subcommittee before quitting politics in 1981.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he worked as a messenger boy at Migdal -- the insurer he bought control of in 2012. His first agency (1955) ran from the corner of a motorcycle-repair garage in Tel Aviv's Shapira neighborhood, and he signed up clients by bicycle while also promoting entertainment shows.
notes: Aged ~90; no death reported. Hanan Melcer replaced him as Migdal chair (2022, Globes). Quote from honorary-fellow citation: 'The hardships forged me. Wealth never spoke to me.' No personal contact channel found; route via Migdal corporate.

name: Segolene Gallienne
current_role: Head of Champagne Lenoble (Damery) since 2023; director of Christian Dior SE, Groupe Bruxelles Lambert, Power Corporation of Canada and Château Cheval Blanc
profile: Ségolène Frère-Gallienne is the daughter of the late Albert Frère, Belgium's richest industrialist, and co-heir to the Frère holding with stakes in GBL (run by her husband Ian Gallienne). After PR roles at Belgacom/Proximus and five years leading communications at Dior Fine Jewelry, she sits on several boards and since 2023 runs the family's Lenoble Champagne house.
interesting_fact: She sits on the board of Château Cheval Blanc, the Saint-Émilion first growth co-owned by the Frère family and Bernard Arnault, and has been a director of Christian Dior SE since about 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She has a long-standing passion for gemology, and at Lenoble she has personally joined the grape harvest to understand the terroir; she redesigned the house's HQ with Dior Maison creative director Cordelia de Castellane as a free-to-visit family home.
notes: Contacts are for Champagne Lenoble (the business she runs), not personal. Private family; GBL press office is an alternative route. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes beyond GBL holdings.

name: Maritsa Lazari
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Lazari Investments (London); trustee, Christos Lazari Foundation
profile: Born in Dora, Cyprus in 1943, she moved to London at 16 and married fellow Cypriot Christos (Chris) Lazari in 1965. In 1978 the couple put profits from his Drendie Girl fashion label into London property. Lazari Investments now owns over 3M sq ft, mostly West End offices plus the Brunswick Centre. Since Chris died in 2015 she has stayed on as a director alongside their three children.
interesting_fact: The fortune began with a high-street fashion label: Chris saved money from washing dishes and waiting tables to study fashion design, and Drendie Girl funded the move into property in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: The family's Christos Lazari Foundation, set up in 2017 with Maritsa as trustee, supports Cypriot, Greek Orthodox and medical causes. It gave £3.25m of investment property to the Cypriot children's charity Radiomarathon.
notes: Very private, with almost no interviews on record. The foundation's published email is the only route found. Lazari Investments has no verified official website (lazari.co.uk sits behind a bot wall and could not be confirmed). Her sons are also directors. Little obvious energy or data-center fit beyond London office property.

name: Zhu Mengyi
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Hopson Development Holdings (HKEX: 754) and Zhujiang (Pearl River) Investment Group. Longtime chairman; his current board title was not verified.
profile: Zhu Mengyi (朱孟依, Chu Mang Yee, b. 1959) is from Fengshun county, Guangdong. He founded Guangzhou-born developer Hopson Development in 1992, listed it in Hong Kong in 1998 and later moved its headquarters to Beijing. His Zhujiang Investment group also holds transport infrastructure, energy, education and technology assets. He served on China's CPPCC national committee.
interesting_fact: Hopson was once one of Guangdong's five biggest private developers. In October 2021, during the Evergrande crisis, it agreed to buy a 51% stake in Evergrande's property-management arm, but the deal was suspended.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from Koupu village in Liuhuang town, Fengshun county, a Hakka/Chaoshan area of eastern Guangdong. He built the Zhujiang Investment group alongside Hopson, and Chinese media have called it his 'invisible' wealth empire.
notes: Extremely private; he gives essentially no interviews. Hopson's IR site (hosted by irasia) did not expose a contact email, and the web search budget ran out before a published IR/press email could be found. Check Hopson's latest HKEX annual report for the current board (family members may now chair it).

name: Nikhil Kamath
current_role: Co-founder, Zerodha; founder of True Beacon and Gruhas; host of the 'WTF is' podcast
profile: Bengaluru entrepreneur who co-founded discount brokerage Zerodha with brother Nithin in 2010, disrupting Indian retail broking. Also runs zero-fee asset manager True Beacon, co-founded investment firm Gruhas (2021), and hosts the 'WTF is' podcast, whose guests have included PM Narendra Modi, Bill Gates and Elon Musk.
interesting_fact: In 2023 he became the youngest Indian signatory of the Giving Pledge, committing to give away at least half his wealth.
deep_cut_fact: A school dropout after 10th grade with no formal degree, he started out working in a call centre while trading equities on the side; in 2024 he launched WTFund, a non-dilutive grant fund for founders aged 25 and under.
notes: Fellow podcaster; peer-to-peer pitch (guest swap) is a natural angle. Very active on X/Instagram. Gruhas invests in climate tech. No published press email found.

name: Stephen Lansdown
current_role: Owner, Bristol Sport (Bristol City FC, Bristol Bears, Bristol Flyers); private investor based in Guernsey
profile: Bristol-born accountant (b. 1952) who co-founded Hargreaves Lansdown with Peter Hargreaves in 1981. It grew into the UK's largest retail investment platform. He left its board in 2012 and moved to Guernsey in 2010, and now concentrates on Bristol Sport and private and impact investments. He co-founded the sustainable PE firm Earth Capital in 2008; it closed in 2024.
interesting_fact: Trained as an accountant, he started Hargreaves Lansdown trading from a bedroom in 1981. He later sold Hargreaves Lansdown shares to help fund Bristol City's redevelopment of Ashton Gate, and rescued Bristol Rugby (now Bristol Bears) when it was close to going under.
deep_cut_fact: He was an early convert to sustainable investing. In 2019 he said he had narrowed his focus to four themes: food security, energy security, clean water and waste management. Earth Capital scored every deal on its own 'Earth Dividend' ESG scorecard, mapped to the UN SDGs.
notes: He received a CBE in 2017. His energy-security and sustainability investing is a natural podcast angle. Bristol Sport is the most direct published route.

name: Fabrizio Di Amato
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, MAIRE S.p.A. (Rome/Milan); Chairman, Maire Foundation
profile: Rome-born Di Amato started his business at 19 with three employees. Through acquisitions including Fiat Engineering (2004), Tecnimont (2005), Stamicarbon (2009) and KT (2010) he built MAIRE, now an energy-transition engineering and technology group with 9,800+ staff in 45 countries. He listed it in Milan in 2007, and in 2018 he founded NextChem, its sustainable-technology arm working on hydrogen, ammonia, SAF and circular chemistry.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he founded Federprogetti, the Italian Plant Engineering Federation, and chaired it until 2015. He was made a Cavaliere del Lavoro (Knight of Labour) in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: His degree is in Political Science from La Sapienza, yet the Politecnico di Milano later gave him an honorary degree in Chemical Engineering. His Maire Foundation preserves the group's historic engineering archives and trains 'humanist engineers' for the energy and digital transitions.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: MAIRE/NextChem work on hydrogen, ammonia, SAF and nuclear MoUs (e.g. Nuward). The group media relations contact named in releases is Tommaso Verani. The press-release contact block was confirmed via search snippet, not opened directly.

name: Frank Love
current_role: Co-CEO, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores (with brother Greg Love)
profile: Son of Tom and Judy Love, who started Love's in 1964 by leasing a gas station in Watonga, Oklahoma. Frank and Greg have been co-CEOs since 2014 of the Oklahoma City-based, family-owned chain, now 640+ truck stops and stores in 42 states with ~40,000 team members and an estimated $22B in sales.
interesting_fact: Love's is also an alternative-fuels player: in 2016 it bought Trillium, then the second-largest U.S. distributor of compressed natural gas, which became the base of its alternative-energy business.
notes: Low personal media profile; sister Jenny Love Meyer (Chief Culture Officer) is the family's usual public voice. Father Tom Love died 2023. Truck-stop fuel transition (CNG, RNG, hydrogen, EV charging) is the natural energy-podcast angle. Route via Love's media group.

name: Greg Love
current_role: Co-CEO (with brother Frank Love), Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores, Oklahoma City
profile: Greg Love is co-CEO of Love's, the family-owned truck-stop and convenience chain founded by his parents Tom and Judy Love in 1964, now 600+ locations in 42 states with ~$22bn in estimated sales. He began working at the company in high school and previously held roles including president/COO and VP of real estate. Founder Tom Love died in 2025.
interesting_fact: Love's is a sizable energy-transition player: its Trillium unit (bought 2016, renamed Love's Alternative Energy in 2025) runs 100+ CNG stations, hydrogen stations, EV charging and RNG supply.
deep_cut_fact: Love's opened its first hydrogen fueling station in 2018 at the Orange County Transportation Authority's Santa Ana bus facility, via its then-subsidiary Trillium CNG.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (truck fuel, CNG/RNG, hydrogen, EV charging). Low personal media profile; route via Love's media group. Aggregators say he holds a BA from Trinity University (unverified).

name: Jenny Love Meyer
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Culture Officer, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores
profile: Daughter of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Love's in 1964 with a $5,000 family loan; the Oklahoma City chain now has 600+ truck stops in 42 states and ~$22bn in sales, run by her brothers Frank and Greg as co-CEOs. She joined the company in 1991 and in 2019 became its first-ever Chief Culture Officer; her wealth stems from the family's ownership stake.
interesting_fact: She was the first person to hold the title of chief culture officer at Love's, created in November 2019, and has described culture as being like the water in an aquarium: always present, but it needs nourishing.
deep_cut_fact: She studied political science at Colorado College, began at Love's in 1991 in business and operational roles, and for years led the company's public/media relations, internal communications and charitable giving; she sits on the Greater Oklahoma City Chamber executive committee.
notes: Speaks at comms/HR conferences (Ragan, NACS), so open to culture/leadership conversations. Route via Love's media relations. Energy angle: truck-stop fueling and alternative fuels (verify Love's current EV/alt-fuel programs before using).

name: Laura Love
current_role: Co-owner (with siblings Greg, Frank and Jenny) of Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores; no public executive role found
profile: One of four children of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Love's in Oklahoma in 1964. The family-owned chain runs 600+ truck stops in 42 states (~$22B est. sales); brothers Greg and Frank are co-CEOs and sister Jenny Love Meyer is chief culture officer. Laura keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Love's began in 1964 when Tom and Judy Love started it with a $5,000 loan from Tom's parents; it remains wholly family-owned with 600+ locations in 42 states.
notes: Very private; no interviews, personal accounts or individual role found. Parents died 2023 (Tom) and 2024 (Judy) - avoid. A podcast pitch would more realistically go to the co-CEOs via the company media group.

name: Tim Cook
current_role: Executive Chairman, Apple (stepped down as CEO on Sept 1, 2026, succeeded by John Ternus); director, Nike
profile: Alabama-raised industrial engineer who joined Apple in 1998 from Compaq, after 12 years at IBM, to fix its supply chain. As COO he became Steve Jobs's successor and was CEO from 2011 to Aug 2026, taking Apple to record valuations. He is one of the few billionaires who made his fortune as a hired CEO. As executive chairman he now focuses partly on global policy engagement.
interesting_fact: He handed the CEO role to hardware chief John Ternus on Sept 1, 2026 after nearly 15 years. He came from humble roots (his father was a shipyard worker, his mother worked at a pharmacy) and was salutatorian of Robertsdale High School in 1978.
deep_cut_fact: To pay his way through Auburn's industrial-engineering program he did a co-op with Reynolds Aluminum, working in Richmond, Virginia every other quarter. Before Apple he was COO of the computer-reseller division of Intelligent Electronics.
notes: The press contact is Josh Rosenstock, named on Apple's Cook/Ternus transition release. Very hard to book; any request goes through Apple PR. The X handle @tim_cook is widely known, but I didn't confirm it on the leadership page. The Intelligent Electronics detail is sourced to Wikipedia/CNN Fast Facts.

name: Eugene Murtagh
current_role: Founder and President Emeritus, Kingspan Group plc (stepped down as chairman in 2021)
profile: Born in Kingscourt, Co. Cavan in 1942, Murtagh started out making agricultural trailers and engineering parts in the early 1960s, then built Kingspan into a global leader in insulated panels and building envelopes, with 200+ factories in roughly 80 countries. He was CEO until 2005 and chairman until 2021, and still owns about 15%.
interesting_fact: Kingspan began with him building agricultural trailers behind his family's bar, Murtagh's, in Kingscourt. The group's head office still sits in the same small Cavan town.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2011 local Q&A he said that before going it alone he worked for a company in Carrickmacross and went to England with them for a short while; by the time he came back he had decided to work for himself, at 21, starting in his father's backyard.

public_contacts.value: Murray Consultants (Pat Walsh), Tel +353 (0)1 4980300, Kingspan's listed press contact

notes: In his 80s and retired from the board; keeps a low profile in Kingscourt. His son Gene Murtagh is Kingspan CEO. Kingspan is highly relevant to data centers (it supplies data-center building envelopes and raised floors). Route through Kingspan's PR agency Murray. Avoid mentioning his late wife.

name: Sol Daurella i Comadrán
current_role: Chairman, Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP); executive chair of family holding Cobega
profile: Barcelona-born (1966) heir to the Daurella family, which became Spain's first Coca-Cola bottler in 1951. After strategy consulting at Mac Group she joined the Coca-Cola system in 1992, led Coca-Cola Iberian Partners, and has chaired CCEP, the world's largest Coca-Cola bottler by revenue, since its 2016 formation; the family holds its stake through Cobega.
interesting_fact: Her family's Cobega has been part of the Coca-Cola system since 1951, when it became the first Spanish Coca-Cola bottler; she has also sat on the boards of Banco Santander, Banco Sabadell, Acciona and Ebro Foods.
deep_cut_fact: She went to an English school in Montreux, Switzerland, holds a finance master's from UC Berkeley as well as an ESADE MBA, and has served as honorary consul general of Iceland in Barcelona.
notes: Very private, rarely interviewed. Iceland consulate role may be historical (Icelandic government now lists a different honorary consul). Route via CCEP media relations.
