name: Wang Yi
current_role: Listed by Hurun alongside Liang Qin as co-holder of the Yangjie Technology fortune; exact role at the company unconfirmed
profile: Hurun lists Wang Yi with Liang Qin as owners of the Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology (300373.SZ) fortune. Yangjie is a power-semiconductor maker that Liang Qin founded in 2000 and chairs. She is its sole disclosed actual controller, and its 2025 filings do not name Wang Yi, so his link to the company (likely family) is unverified.
interesting_fact: Yangjie Technology began in 2000 as a semiconductor brand-distribution business started by Liang Qin with about ten partners. It has since become a listed power-semiconductor (diodes, MOSFETs, SiC) manufacturer, a supplier to energy and EV-related markets.

public_contacts.value: zjb@21yangjie.com (Yangjie Technology, published in its 2024 ESG report; phone 0514-80889866)

notes: The name is ambiguous: 'Wang Yi' is also China's foreign minister, so do not confuse them. I could not confirm who this Wang Yi is. Yangjie's filings name only chairwoman Liang Qin as actual controller. Contact Yangjie via its published company email and confirm the relationship before any outreach.

name: Wang Yun‘an
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Guming Holdings (Good me / 古茗), HKEX: 1364
profile: Millennial founder (born mid-1980s) of Good me, a franchise bubble-tea chain he started in 2010 after graduating from Zhejiang Sci-Tech University. Focused on lower-tier Chinese towns and cities, it grew to roughly 10,000 stores; Guming listed in Hong Kong in Feb 2025, making him a billionaire. HQ Hangzhou.
interesting_fact: The first Good me shop opened in April 2010 in Daxi town, Wenling (Taizhou), Zhejiang, opened with a high-school friend; the name 古茗 means roughly 'old tea'. Big-city tea brands hadn't reached small towns yet, which was his opening.
deep_cut_fact: As a student he sold radios and quilts and helped classmates sign up for credit cards, building up hundreds of thousands of yuan; after graduating he lasted just two weeks as a car-dealership (4S store) salesman in Hangzhou before quitting to open his tea shop.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Company site lists a named media contact (媒体联系) and brand-partnership email; IR page at gumingnc.com/investors.

name: Jamie Dimon
current_role: Chairman & CEO, JPMorgan Chase
profile: Jamie Dimon has run JPMorgan Chase, the largest US bank by assets, as CEO since 2005-06 and chairman since 2006-07, after helping Sandy Weill build Citigroup and leading Bank One. His stake and pay make him one of few bank-CEO billionaires. In June 2026 JPMorgan named Doug Petno and Troy Rohrbaugh co-presidents; Dimon reportedly plans about three more years as CEO before becoming executive chairman.
interesting_fact: His Greek grandfather, a banker in Smyrna and Athens, changed the family name from Papademetriou to Dimon; his father and grandfather were both stockbrokers at Shearson.
deep_cut_fact: His break came from a college paper: at Tufts he wrote about Shearson's mergers, his mother sent it to Sandy Weill, and Weill hired him for a summer job doing budgets at Shearson.

public_contacts.value: Global Communications: Joe Evangelisti (no email listed); IR/HR media: michael.f.fusco@jpmchase.com

notes: Go through JPMorgan Global Communications. He publishes an annual shareholder letter, which is a good hook for outreach. Succession source: https://www.foxbusiness.com/business-leaders/jpmorgan-names-2-new-co-presidents-setting-up-race-succeed-jamie-dimon

name: Adam Kwok
current_role: Executive director, Sun Hung Kai Properties (since 2014); runs SHKP's South China property business
profile: Adam Kwok Kai-fai (郭基煇) is a grandson of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and son of former joint chairman Thomas Kwok. After a stint in investment banking he joined Hong Kong's largest developer in 2008, became an executive director in 2014 and has led its South China (mainland) property business since 2013, acting as project director on major residential and commercial schemes.
interesting_fact: He is part of one of Asia's richest property families: four of his cousins, his father, an uncle and his grandmother have all been billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: A keen cyclist, he donated HK$10 million to a Hong Kong Sports Institute / HKUST joint venture to develop more aerodynamic cycling equipment for Hong Kong riders.
notes: Also sits on HK government's Major Sports Events Committee and is a vice president of REDA. Avoid referencing his father's conviction. Route via SHKP corporate communications.

name: Gerald J. Ford
current_role: Chairman, Hilltop Holdings (NYSE: HTH); co-managing partner, Ford Financial Fund; director, Mechanics Bank
profile: Dallas lawyer-turned-banker (b. 1944, raised in Pampa, Texas; SMU grad) who has bought and turned around distressed banks since 1975. His biggest win was selling Golden State Bancorp (with Ronald Perelman) to Citigroup for ~$6B in 2002. He owns ~25% of Hilltop Holdings (PlainsCapital Bank, PrimeLending, HilltopSecurities) and controls California's Mechanics Bank via Ford Financial Fund.
interesting_fact: He gave his alma mater SMU $20M in 1997 for a new football stadium (Gerald J. Ford Stadium) and $15M in 2013 for a research center.
deep_cut_fact: Ford credits working as a teenager in an auto body shop alongside his dad in Pampa, Texas, with pushing him toward a better career - and he carried around Ayn Rand's 'Atlas Shrugged' in high school.

public_contacts.value: mdunn@hilltop.com (Matt Dunn, Hilltop Holdings investor relations)

notes: Not to be confused with the US president. Son Jeremy Ford is Hilltop CEO. Low media profile; IR contact is a corporate route, not personal.

name: D. Leopoldo Del Pino
current_role: Private investor and Ferrovial shareholder; former Ferrovial board member (until early 2016)
profile: Leopoldo del Pino y Calvo-Sotelo is a son of Rafael del Pino y Moreno, who founded Ferrovial in 1952, and inherited a stake in the infrastructure group. He sat on Ferrovial's board until early 2016 and has since gradually reduced his holding from over 8% to roughly 4%. His brother Rafael chairs Ferrovial. He invests privately, largely through SICAV vehicles.
interesting_fact: Ferrovial, the company his father founded in 1952, is now one of the world's largest infrastructure operators, with stakes in toll roads such as Toronto's 407 ETR and in Heathrow Airport.
notes: Very private, with no public role or published contact. He is not an executive at Ferrovial, so the company press office is not a real route to him. Press coverage centres on his SICAVs and stake sales. Low priority.

name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
current_role: Founder & Executive Chairperson, Biocon Ltd (Bengaluru)
profile: Trained master brewer who founded Biocon in 1978 and built it into one of India's largest biopharma firms, with one of Asia's largest insulin plants (Johor, Malaysia) and a biosimilars arm that bought Viatris' biosimilars business in 2022. In Dec 2025 Biocon agreed to buy out the rest of Biocon Biologics (valued at $5.5bn). Her philanthropy includes the Mazumdar Shaw Medical Center cancer-care model.
interesting_fact: She wanted to be a doctor but couldn't get into medical school; after qualifying as a master brewer in Australia she was told in India she wouldn't be hired as a brewer because it was 'a man's work', and started Biocon in 1978 in a rented garage with Rs 10,000.
deep_cut_fact: On 5 March 2015 her alma mater, Federation University Australia (formerly Ballarat College of Advanced Education, where she was the only woman in the 1974 brewing course), opened 'Mazumdar Drive' at its Mt Helen campus in her honour; she cut the ribbon herself.
notes: Very media-accessible and active on X (@kiranshaw); frequently speaks on Bengaluru infrastructure, biotech policy and women in science. Husband John Shaw died in 2022 - be sensitive. Avoid the 2022 CBI bribery case.

name: Luca Querella
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons S.p.A. (Nasdaq: BSP), Milan
profile: Luca Querella co-founded Bending Spoons, the Milan company that buys established apps and internet businesses (Evernote, WeTransfer, Eventbrite, Vimeo, AOL) and rebuilds them on its own tech. Bootstrapped until 2022, it listed on Nasdaq in July 2026 at about an $18B valuation, and the co-founders keep about 83% of the votes.
interesting_fact: Before Bending Spoons, the founders met while studying in Copenhagen and built a failed note-taking app called Evertale. A decade later Bending Spoons bought Evernote, the best-known note-taking app.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike his Padua-educated co-founders, Querella is the computer scientist of the group. He earned a computer science degree at the University of Turin and a computer engineering degree at the IT University of Copenhagen.
notes: Keeps a very low public profile. CEO Luca Ferrari does nearly all the interviews. The press office (Christy Keenan, press@bendingspoons.com) is the realistic route, and pitching a founders' conversation may land better than Querella alone. Some Italian sources say he joined the original Copenhagen trio slightly later.

name: Sergei Galitsky
current_role: Owner and president, FC Krasnodar (football club and academy); founder of Magnit
profile: Sergey Galitsky founded Magnit, one of Russia's largest grocery and cosmetics chains, after starting as a perfume/cosmetics wholesaler (Tander) in 1994; he opened the first store in 1998 and took it public in 2006. He sold almost all his stake to VTB in 2018 for $2.4B and now focuses on FC Krasnodar, its academy, a stadium, a 2,500-tree park and a family winery.
interesting_fact: An admirer of Walmart, he advertised his first Magnit store with the slogan 'Always Low Prices'; he later spent ~$460M on FC Krasnodar's stadium (nicknamed the 'Galiseum') and $70M on the adjacent park.
deep_cut_fact: A teenage chess talent, he became a candidate master within two years and won the Sochi championship; he made chess compulsory at the FC Krasnodar academy and in 2013 played a 4-hour simul vs 20 pupils, winning 16.5-3.5.

public_contacts.value: n.baiburin@fckrasnodar.ru (head of FC Krasnodar press service)

notes: Russia-based; check current sanctions/compliance status before outreach. Known as outspoken and relatively accessible to press in Russian media (e.g. Novaya Gazeta 2025 interview). Born Sergey Arutyunyan, 1967.

name: Liora Ofer
current_role: Chairperson, Ofer Investments and Melisron Ltd (TASE)
profile: Haifa-born (1953) real estate businesswoman who inherited Ofer Investments, cofounded in 1957 by her father Yuli and uncle Sammy Ofer. She has chaired Melisron since 2008, growing it into one of Israel's largest property companies (malls incl. Ramat Aviv Mall, office parks), and now owns 100% of Ofer Investments.
interesting_fact: She is one of only two female billionaires in Israel (the other being Shari Arison); under her chairmanship Melisron acquired 25 shopping malls from British Israel Investments.
deep_cut_fact: She began working alongside her father at Ofer Investments at age 20, and in 1995 became general manager of Coral Beach Eilat Ltd, the Red Sea hotel business, years before taking over Melisron.
notes: Private; rarely gives interviews. Best route is via Melisron's corporate/IR office (melisron.co.il; site was unreachable during research). Recognized as a donor to Reichman University (IDC Herzliya): https://runi.ac.il/en/about/runifriends/donor-recognition/liora-ofer

name: Gerry Harvey
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Harvey Norman Holdings (Australia)
profile: Gerry Harvey (b. 1939) co-founded Harvey Norman with Ian Norman in 1982 after their first chain, Norman Ross, was sold; it now sells furniture, electricals and bedding across Australia and 100+ overseas stores (NZ, Singapore, Malaysia, Slovenia, Ireland, UK). His wife Katie Page runs the business as CEO, while he remains executive chairman, a vocal media commentator and a major thoroughbred breeder.
interesting_fact: He owns Baramul Stud, has one of the world's largest thoroughbred portfolios (600+ horses) and co-owns the Magic Millions bloodstock auction.
deep_cut_fact: He started out selling vacuum cleaners and fridges door-to-door for Goodwins of Newtown, where he met Ian Norman; the pair opened their first Sydney store in 1961. He dropped out of university and has said: 'I always wanted to be a farmer.'
notes: Very media-accessible; frequently gives interviews to Australian business press and radio. No published press email found; company contact page or ASX company secretary are the routes.

name: Lin Jianhua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hangzhou First Applied Material (Shanghai: 603806)
profile: Co-founded Hangzhou First Applied Material in 2003 with his wife Zhang Hong after 12 years at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang. First became the world's largest supplier of solar-module encapsulant film (EVA/POE), with over half of the global market, plus backsheets; it has since expanded into electronic-circuit and battery materials.
interesting_fact: Before founding a solar-materials giant he spent 1982-1994 working at a state-owned fertilizer factory in Zhejiang Province.
deep_cut_fact: First did not start in solar: its early product was hot-melt adhesive web film for the textile industry, and moving into EVA solar film was what the company calls its first transformation, from textiles into new energy. It now supplies over 50% of the world's PV encapsulant film.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed, company communications usually come from the board secretary (Zhang Ying). Best route is the securities/IR department email; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jerry Yang
current_role: Founding Partner, AME Cloud Ventures (Yahoo co-founder; Stanford trustee, board chair 2021-2025)
profile: Taiwan-born Jerry Yang co-founded Yahoo with David Filo in 1994-95 while both were Stanford EE PhD students. He was Yahoo's CEO from 2007 to 2009 and left the company in 2012. His bet on Alibaba, a 40% stake in 2005, was one of the most lucrative in tech history. Through AME Cloud Ventures he backs data-driven startups such as Zoom, Wattpad and Evernote, and he chaired Stanford's board of trustees from 2021 to 2025.
interesting_fact: He collects ancient Chinese calligraphy, about 250 works from the Ming and Qing eras. In 2017 he and his wife Akiko Yamazaki gave $25M to San Francisco's Asian Art Museum, the largest gift in its history.
deep_cut_fact: His VC firm's name, AME (pronounced 'ah-meh'), means 'rain' in Japanese, a nod to cloud computing. He met his wife Akiko on a six-month Stanford exchange in Japan in 1992, and he says 'shoe' was the only English word he knew when he arrived in San Jose aged 10.
notes: No public email on the AME site. Best route is AME Cloud Ventures (Palo Alto) or a warm intro through Stanford or portfolio founders such as Eric Yuan of Zoom. AME's data and cloud focus fits the data-center theme.

name: Sam Altman
current_role: CEO, OpenAI
profile: Stanford dropout who founded Loopt (sold 2012 for $43M), ran Y Combinator as president 2014-2019, then became OpenAI CEO (briefly fired and rehired in 2023). He holds no OpenAI equity; his wealth comes from investments such as Stripe, Reddit and fusion company Helion. He stepped down as Oklo chair in April 2025 and as Helion chair in March 2026, citing AI-energy partnerships.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he put $375 million into fusion startup Helion Energy, his largest startup investment at the time; he had chaired Oklo (advanced fission) since 2015 and took it public via his SPAC, which makes him central to the AI-power story.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first computer, an Apple Macintosh, at age eight and learned to code and take its hardware apart.
notes: Extremely high-demand guest. Oklo stepdown: https://www.neimagazine.com/news/sam-altman-steps-down-as-oklo-chair/ ; Helion stake was scrutinised in the 2026 Musk v. OpenAI trial (https://www.geekwire.com/2026/openai-ceo-sam-altmans-stake-in-helion-energy-draws-scrutiny-in-musk-trial-and-on-capitol-hill/). No OpenAI press email is published first-party (third-party sites list press@openai.com, unverified). Best route is OpenAI comms or a warm intro.

name: Anton Osika
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lovable (Stockholm)
profile: Swedish engineer (b. 1990) who co-founded 'vibe coding' startup Lovable with CTO Fabian Hedin in 2023 after his open-source GPT-Engineer project went viral. Lovable launched in Nov 2024, hit $100M ARR in eight months and was valued at $13.3B in Aug 2026; Forbes estimates he owns ~24%. Earlier he was first employee at Sana Labs and co-founder/CTO of Depict.ai.
interesting_fact: Lovable reached $100M in annualized subscription revenue just eight months after launch - which Forbes calls the fastest-growing software startup in history; he and Hedin pledged 50% of exit proceeds to charity via Founders Pledge.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he was a physicist: he earned a physics BSc at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, then an MSc in engineering physics at KTH, and did research tied to the ATLAS experiment at CERN.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly; posts constantly on X and LinkedIn and does lots of podcasts/conference talks. Best route: press@lovable.dev or a DM on X. AI-software angle more than data centers/energy.

name: Fabian Hedin
current_role: Cofounder and Chief Technology Officer, Lovable (Stockholm)
profile: Swedish engineer who, after founding small startups (Tentium, TenFAST) and leading frontend at Depict.ai, was recruited by Anton Osika to cofound Lovable out of the open-source GPT Engineer project. Lovable's 'vibe coding' platform lets non-coders build apps by prompt; it hit $100M ARR eight months after its Nov 2024 launch and was valued at $13.3B in Aug 2026. He owns ~24%.
interesting_fact: Lovable reached $100M in annualized subscription revenue just eight months after launch, which Forbes calls the fastest-growing software startup in history; Hedin and Osika have pledged 50% of exit proceeds to charity.
deep_cut_fact: His path into building software started with running his own Minecraft servers in high school, a story he told on Notion's 'First Block' founder series; Lovable also dogfoods heavily, building its own internal tools (office CRM, ops software) in Lovable.
notes: Accessible, technical founder who does podcasts/conference talks (Notion First Block, Google Cloud Next, HumanX). Best route: Lovable press@ or via conference speaker circuits. Personal X/LinkedIn not verified here (web-search budget ran out).

name: Edward Bass
current_role: President, Fine Line, Inc. (Fort Worth private investment and venture capital firm); owner/developer of Sundance Square
profile: Fort Worth-born Bass brother (Yale 1967) whose share of the Sid Richardson oil inheritance grew through oil, pipelines and investments; the brothers sold their oil company to ExxonMobil in 2017 for $5.6B in stock. Best known for remaking downtown Fort Worth via Sundance Square, Bass Performance Hall and Dickies Arena, and for funding Biosphere 2; pledged $160M to Yale's Peabody Museum.
interesting_fact: In 1991 he spent about $150 million backing Biosphere 2 in Arizona, the sealed experimental ecosystem meant to show humans could live in enclosed habitats such as those in space.
deep_cut_fact: He won the 2007 Henry Hope Reed Award (given alongside Notre Dame's Driehaus Prize) for championing traditional architecture and urbanism; as chairman of Performing Arts Fort Worth he led the building of the Bass Performance Hall, which opened in 1998.
notes: Private; no published personal/office email found. Natural routes are via Fine Line, Inc. or Sundance Square (Fort Worth). Strong interest in architecture/urbanism and ecology (Biosphere 2); emeritus Yale Corporation trustee.

name: Scott Lin
current_role: Co-founder, Largan Precision; chairman of Mao Yu Memorial Co. (Maoyu), Largan's largest single corporate shareholder (no executive role at Largan)
profile: Scott Lin (Lin Yao-ying, b. 1933) co-founded Taichung-based Largan Precision with Tony Chen in 1987; it became the world's leading smartphone-lens maker and a major Apple supplier. Largan is now run by his sons; in 2020 he moved family shares into the locked holding company Maoyu. Forbes puts his fortune at about $3B.
interesting_fact: At 93, 16 years after handing over the reins, he still goes into Largan six days a week and closely follows its push into co-packaged optics (CPO) for AI data centres, studying AI alongside staff.
deep_cut_fact: An agricultural-chemistry graduate of National Chung Hsing University, he was a middle-school chemistry teacher and worked at Taiwan Sugar and a provincial ammonium-sulfate company before moving into optics; he started Largan at about 47 with no optics background.
notes: Chinese name 林耀英. Aged 93; very low profile, Chinese-language media only. 'office_email' is Largan's general company address. Outreach likely best via Largan IR or in Mandarin; CPO/data-centre optics angle is topical.

name: John Paul DeJoria
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, John Paul Mitchell Systems; co-founder of Patron Spirits (sold to Bacardi 2018); >10% holder of HighPeak Energy
profile: Born 1944 in Echo Park, LA, DeJoria sold encyclopedias and shampoo door-to-door and was at times homeless before co-founding John Paul Mitchell Systems with Paul Mitchell in 1980 on a $700 loan. He co-founded Patron in 1989 and sold it to Bacardi in 2018 ($5.1B deal). He now invests across ventures incl. West Texas oil producer HighPeak Energy (~12% stake) and runs a family foundation.
interesting_fact: Sea Shepherd-linked Captain Paul Watson Foundation named its first anti-whaling ship the 'John Paul DeJoria II' (2022); he also bought the former McDonald's HQ campus incl. Hamburger University for $40M in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the U.S. Navy at 17 straight out of high school and served on the aircraft carrier USS Hornet; in 2012 the U.S. Navy Memorial gave him its Lone Sailor Award, and he credited the Hornet with teaching him the people-management and teamwork skills he later used in business.
notes: Very public, media-friendly speaker (Shark Tank guest, documentaries, memoir). Energy angle: HighPeak Energy 13D holder plus past interests in solar and natural gas ventures. Foundation (JP's Peace, Love & Happiness) website/Instagram are the cleanest routes; no published personal or press email found. Avoid ROKiT bankruptcies as a topic.

name: Zhu Guodong
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (~7%) of Suzhou TFC Optical Communication (300394.SZ); no board or executive role since Nov 2023
profile: Zhu Guodong (朱国栋) is the technical co-founder of TFC Optical, set up in Suzhou in 2005 with Zou Zhinong and Ou Yang as a ceramic-ferrule maker (Zhu held 25%). TFC grew into a supplier of passive optical components and optical engines for AI data centers. Zhu was a director and VP until the 2023 board election and remains a top shareholder.
interesting_fact: TFC started with a single rice-grain-sized ceramic ferrule, a part then dominated by Japanese makers; the team produced roughly a million rejects before cracking nano-zirconia sintering and cut the price by nearly two-thirds versus imports.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, Zhu graduated from Tsinghua University in welding technology and equipment, holds Singapore permanent residency, and spent about 10 years at foreign firms, working as an engineer at Singapore's Sharikat Kian Tong Pte Ltd and Aston Air Control Pte Ltd before co-founding TFC.
notes: Very low profile; English sources almost nil. He is no longer an officer, so TFC's securities/IR office (zhengquan@tfcsz.com) is only an indirect route. Sold ~1.27% of TFC via inquiry transfer in Aug 2025. Chairman/face of TFC is Zou Zhinong.

name: Mário Araripe
current_role: Founder and majority owner, Casa dos Ventos (shares leadership with CEO Lucas Araripe)
profile: Ceará-born ITA-trained engineer who ran textile, real-estate and auto businesses (bought jeep maker Troller and sold it to Ford in 2006), then founded Casa dos Ventos in 2007, now Brazil's largest renewable developer (about a third of the country's operating wind farms). TotalEnergies owns 34% of its generation JV. The firm is now pivoting to powering data centers, incl. a large campus at Pecém.
interesting_fact: Casa dos Ventos calls data centers its main growth vector: it signed a ~US$500M renewable supply deal with Ascenty (Jan 2026) and is exclusive power supplier to a large data-center campus at the port of Pecém, Ceará, linked to ByteDance/TikTok.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Crato, Ceará, son of an engineer in Brazil's federal anti-drought works department; he trained as an aeronautical-mechanical engineer at ITA. The wind idea came from ITA classmate Odilon Camargo, who urged him to be first to map Brazil's wind potential; he then used the Troller sale cash to prospect the Northeast.
notes: Company accounts, not personal. Son Lucas Araripe is CEO and the public face for data-center strategy; Mário gives occasional interviews (Forbes Brasil, Diário do Nordeste). Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Contact form is commercially oriented; no published press email found.

name: Gao Guangrong
current_role: Chairman, Eoptolink Technology Inc. (新易盛, SZSE: 300502), Chengdu
profile: Sichuan-born (1969) optical-communications engineer who co-founded Eoptolink with five partners in 2008 and listed it on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2016. Eoptolink makes high-speed optical transceivers (400G/800G/1.6T) for AI clusters and cloud data centers and has boomed with AI build-outs, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Eoptolink, once focused on domestic telecom, only broke into overseas hyperscaler (e.g. Amazon) supply chains around 2019; with Innolight and TFC it is nicknamed one of China's 'Yi-Zhong-Tian' AI optical-module trio, and its market cap passed RMB 350B in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A technical-school graduate (industrial electrical automation, Chengdu Radio Machinery School), he joined the optical-communications branch of Leshan Radio Factory at 20 as a technician and stayed 10 years, then rotated through tech, purchasing, sales and management jobs before founding Eoptolink at 39.

public_contacts.value: daniel.wang@eoptolink.com (Wang Cheng, board secretary); vivi.wei@eoptolink.com (securities affairs rep)

notes: Low public profile; route via board secretary/IR. Note: CSRC issued an administrative penalty in Feb 2025 over his 2023 share sales (avoid in outreach). Strong data-center/AI angle.

name: Lisa Su
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, Advanced Micro Devices (AMD)
profile: Taiwan-born, Bronx Science- and MIT-trained (BS/MS/PhD EE) semiconductor engineer who worked at Texas Instruments, IBM and Freescale before joining AMD in 2012 and becoming CEO in 2014. She led one of tech's great turnarounds; her wealth comes from AMD stock. Now she is pushing AMD's Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs into AI data centers, including a 2025 compute partnership with OpenAI, against Nvidia.
interesting_fact: At IBM she played a key role in developing the 'recipe' to replace aluminum interconnects with copper on chips without contaminating them, a technology launched in 1998 that yielded chips up to ~20% faster.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT freshman her UROP job was 'pure grunt work' making two-inch wafers in Hank Smith's semiconductor lab in Building 39 for x-ray lithography research; that plus summer jobs at Analog Devices hooked her on semiconductors. Her PhD was among the earliest work on silicon-on-insulator (SOI).
notes: Extremely high-demand speaker; formal route is AMD Corporate Communications (corporate.pressinquiry@amd.com). Active on X (@LisaSu). Natural fit for AI data-center compute/power topics. Distant relative of Nvidia's Jensen Huang (often raised; she downplays it).

name: Alki David
current_role: Media/tech entrepreneur; founder of FilmOn and Hologram USA; shareholder in the Leventis-David group (Coca-Cola HBC)
profile: Lagos-born Cypriot-British heir to the Leventis-David trading family, whose holdings are tied to Coca-Cola HBC bottling. He founded internet-TV service FilmOn (2006), hologram-entertainment firm Hologram USA and other ventures, and acted in and directed independent films. No verified 2026 business activity found.
interesting_fact: He studied film at the Royal College of Art, acted in 'The Bank Job' (2008) and wrote/directed indie films such as 'Fishtales'.
deep_cut_fact: His father Andrew A. David joined the family's Leventis-David Group in Ghana in 1957 and managed a Coca-Cola bottling plant in Accra; in 1998 Alki co-founded London modelling agency Independent Models.
notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: multiple civil sexual-misconduct judgments since 2019 (incl. a reported $900M jury award in 2024) and other legal issues per Wikipedia; in 2021 he called earlier billionaire claims 'complete fiction'. Journalist should vet carefully before any outreach. No published contact route found.

name: the Leventis family
current_role: Family group: controlling shareholders (with the David family) of Coca-Cola HBC via Kar-Tess Holding; Leventis Group; A. G. Leventis Foundation (chaired by Anastasios Paul Leventis)
profile: Greek-Cypriot dynasty founded by Anastasios G. Leventis, whose West African trading house A. G. Leventis & Co. (1936) grew into a Nigerian/Ghanaian conglomerate. From the 1970s, Constantine Leventis expanded the family's soft-drinks business into Europe; the Hellenic Bottling Company merged with Coca-Cola Beverages to form Coca-Cola HBC, its main source of wealth today. Media assets come from relative Alki David.
interesting_fact: In the 1948 Accra riots, the most serious anti-colonial violence in post-war West Africa, the only large stores left unburned were those of A. G. Leventis & Co.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Anastasios G. Leventis was born in 1902 in the Cypriot mountain village of Lemythou, studied commerce in Bordeaux, and started out in 1920 as a manager for an Anglo-Hellenic firm in south-eastern Nigeria. In 2025 the family's foundation partnered with the Coca-Cola HBC Foundation on a EUR1m programme to restore fire-hit areas of Limassol.
notes: Multi-person family entry (Sunday Times 2020, shared with Alki David). For outreach, pick a specific member, e.g. Anastasios I. Leventis (Coca-Cola HBC non-exec director) or Anastasios P. Leventis (foundation chair). The CCHBC press office is the corporate route. Alive status is per-member, so it is left as 'unknown'.

name: Jason Murray
current_role: Co-Founder, CEO and Chairman, PACS Group, Inc. (NYSE: PACS)
profile: Jason Murray, a licensed nursing home administrator and former healthcare executive, co-founded PACS Group with Mark Hancock in 2013. Starting with two skilled nursing facilities, it has grown into a Utah-based post-acute care platform with about 387 facilities in 17 states. PACS listed on the NYSE in 2024; Murray owns roughly a third of the shares and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: PACS went from two skilled-nursing facilities in 2013 to a national post-acute care platform with nearly 400 facilities in about a decade, then listed on the NYSE in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He was named Ernst & Young's 2023 Mountain West Entrepreneur of the Year and was a finalist for EY's national award that year. He is a Fellow of the American College of Healthcare Executives (FACHE) and says he enjoys 'anything related to sports and athletics'.
notes: Route through Brooks Stevenson (corporate communications). PACS has faced short-seller and accounting scrutiny since 2024, so keep outreach focused on entrepreneurship and scaling. The web-search budget ran out at this point; facts come from the PACS IR site.

name: Richard Chandler
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Clermont Group (Singapore); founder, Chandler Foundation
profile: New Zealand-born investor who began investing in 1982, built Sovereign Global with his brother Christopher (a deep-value, emerging-markets investor), split assets in 2006 and founded Singapore-based Clermont Group. Clermont holds healthcare, financial services and aerospace assets, including India's SBFC, Vietnam's Hoan My hospitals and electric-aviation firm magniX; he also funds good-governance work.
interesting_fact: Clermont owns magniX, maker of electric powertrains and energy storage for aircraft, which won a $74M five-year NASA contract in 2021 for electrified aircraft propulsion research.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Matangi, New Zealand, the son of a beekeeper, he went on to found the Chandler Institute of Governance in Singapore (2019), which publishes the annual Chandler Good Government Index ranking 100+ countries.
notes: Private; no published email found. magniX (electric aviation) gives a natural energy-angle hook. Background sourced from Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Chandler_(businessman)

name: Alfred Gantner
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Partners Group (Baar-Zug, Switzerland); Chairman, Breitling SA (since Dec 2022)
profile: Swiss private-equity investor ('Fredy') who co-founded Partners Group in 1996 at age 28 with Goldman Sachs colleagues Marcel Erni and Urs Wietlisbach; he was CEO to 2005 and chairman 2005-2014. The firm listed in 2006 and manages $150bn+; he holds ~5%, chairs the founders' multi-family office PG3 and chairs Partners Group-owned watchmaker Breitling.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Partners Group banned staff from using the word 'deal', to push them to think like founders and long-term owners rather than short-term transaction investors.
deep_cut_fact: He started out with a banking apprenticeship at Cantrade Privatbank (a former UBS subsidiary) before his BYU MBA, and in 2002 helped with Swiss public relations for the Salt Lake City Winter Olympics.

public_contacts.value: Prosek Partners (Partners Group, Americas media): Pro-PartnersGroup@prosek.com

notes: Publicly outspoken on Swiss-EU relations (co-leads the Kompass/Europa business network), so open to media on policy topics. Partners Group invests heavily in infrastructure/energy platforms - possible podcast angle. Current PG board status per Wikipedia; verify against latest annual report.

name: Marcel Erni
current_role: Co-founder and large shareholder, Partners Group (Zug); long-time board member (verify current seat)
profile: Swiss financier who co-founded Partners Group in 1996 with Alfred Gantner and Urs Wietlisbach after stints at McKinsey and Goldman Sachs Zurich. The firm grew from a tiny Ikea-desk office into a global private-markets manager with $185bn+ AUM, listed since 2006; Erni holds ~5%. Chicago Booth MBA '91 and St. Gallen PhD.
interesting_fact: He has described Partners Group's start as 'no money, no clients, no clue'; the founders' original plan was just three partners, one or two deals a year, and time for skiing.
deep_cut_fact: At Chicago Booth he was in Merton Miller's finance class when Miller learned he had won the Nobel Prize, and he loves art: 'If you haven't seen the Seurat (A Sunday on La Grande Jatte) at the Art Institute, you haven't been to Chicago.'
notes: Lowest-profile of the three founders; Partners Group is a big infrastructure investor (incl. data centers/energy), good podcast angle. Could not confirm his 2025-26 board status (search budget exhausted).

name: Cristiano Crippa
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Technoprobe S.p.A. (Euronext Milan: TPRO), since 2017
profile: Cristiano Crippa co-founded Technoprobe with his father Giuseppe Crippa (an ex-SGS/STMicroelectronics manager, d. 2025), which makes probe cards that test microchips; it is now the world's No. 2 probe-card maker with ~2,700 staff. Technoprobe listed in Milan in 2022 and later joined the FTSE MIB; Cristiano owns about 18% and has chaired the board since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Technoprobe became the first company in Italy to open a COVID vaccination hub for the general public inside its premises: a 4,300 m2 space where 160,000 doses were given to local residents over six months.
deep_cut_fact: Technoprobe started in the garage and attic of the Crippa family home in Merate (Lecco), while his father was still working at SGS/ST; in 1997 it bought its first building in nearby Cernusco Lombardone and moved in with about 10 employees.
notes: Founding year differs by source (Forbes: 1989 with his father; company history: garage start 1993, incorporated 1996). Family-run, low media profile; press@technoprobe.com is the published route. Father Giuseppe died July 2025 - avoid leading with that.

name: Roberto Crippa
current_role: Vice President (and Vice Chairman of the Board), Technoprobe S.p.A.
profile: Roberto Crippa is the son of the late Giuseppe Crippa (d. 2025), who founded probe-card maker Technoprobe in his garage in 1989. Roberto joined in 2002, ran Italian operations and has been Vice President since 2013; Technoprobe, whose probe cards test chips before packaging (including for AI processors), listed on Euronext Milan in 2022 and Roberto owns about 18%.
interesting_fact: Technoprobe began in 1989 in Giuseppe Crippa's garage and attic while he was still working at STMicroelectronics; it became a global top probe-card supplier and made the founder a billionaire in his late 80s.
deep_cut_fact: A chemical engineer from Politecnico di Milano, he started in a technical product-development role and is author or co-author of numerous international patents; in 2018 he and brother Cristiano led the 100% acquisition of hydraulics-components engineer DA-TOR, starting a diversification into an Italian industrial hub.
notes: Forbes named him among Italy's top 100 managers in 2019. Gave a 2023 interview to Corriere della Sera's L'Economia (https://technoprobe.com/news-and-press/news-events-publications/leconomia-interview-with-roberto-crippa). Company is in Cernusco Lombardone (Lecco). info@ is a general company address.

name: Augusto Perfetti
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Giorgio) of Perfetti Van Melle, the Italian-Dutch confectionery group headquartered in Lainate (Italy) and Breda (Netherlands)
profile: Son of Ambrogio Perfetti, who started a chewing-gum business near Milan with brother Egidio in 1946. Augusto and Giorgio grew it, notably through the 2001 Van Melle merger, into Perfetti Van Melle: Mentos, Chupa Chups, Airheads, Brooklyn and Mondelez's former gum brands (Trident, Dentyne). Revenue is over $4.8bn. Professional managers run day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: He named his yacht and private jet after Mentos and Airheads, the company's best-selling brands. His father and uncle were inspired to start the business after seeing American WWII soldiers bring gum to Europe.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2026, for the company's 80th anniversary, Lainate named a square near the plant 'Largo Ambrogio ed Egidio Perfetti'. A giant replica of the first Brooklyn gum pack ('la gomma del ponte', launched 1956) was unveiled there.
notes: He keeps a very low public profile and I found no interviews. The company route goes through Perfetti Van Melle corporate communications (no press email is published; the contact page lists a data-protection address only). Corrado Bianchi is CEO of PVM Italia.

name: Kim Beom-su
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of Kakao Corp. (Seoul); left the chairmanship and board in 2022 (any 2026 executive role not confirmed)
profile: Also known as Brian Kim. He grew up poor in Seoul, studied engineering at Seoul National University, founded online gaming portal Hangame (merged with Naver to form NHN) and launched KakaoTalk in 2010, now on about 90% of Korean smartphones. Kakao expanded into payments, mobility, games and banking, and he backs startups through K Cube Ventures.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he became one of the first Korean signers of the Giving Pledge, committing more than half his wealth to charity. He paid his way through college as a private tutor, sometimes skipping meals to save money.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a developer for an online communication service at Samsung's IT services unit. Hangame, founded in 1998 with $184,000 from friends and family, started as an internet café business before becoming Korea's first online gaming portal. In 2006 he set up IWILAB, a Mountain View incubator for Korean founders.
notes: Avoid the 2024 SM Entertainment stock case (acquitted Oct 2025) and gambling allegations. No published personal channel found. Kakao's press room is the corporate media route; its media contact details load dynamically and were not captured. Web search budget ran out before his 2026 role could be checked.

name: Remo Ruffini
current_role: Executive Chairman, Moncler S.p.A. (since 1 April 2026, when Bartolomeo Rongone became CEO); controls holding company Double R
profile: Como-born Remo Ruffini (b. 1961) took over near-bankrupt Moncler in 2003 and turned it into a global luxury brand, listing it in Milan in 2013 and buying Stone Island for about EUR 1.15B in 2020. He owns roughly 15% via Double R and in 2026 moved from chairman-CEO to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Moncler's December 2013 IPO was one of Italy's largest in years; shares jumped 47% on the first afternoon, putting Ruffini on the Forbes billionaires list in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: At 23, after working in the U.S. for his father's company Gianfranco Ruffini Ltd, he went home to Como and founded his own label, New England, which he sold to the Stefanel Group 16 years later.
notes: Moncler Group site (press and IR contact pages) blocked automated access; press/IR contacts are listed there under Media / Investor Relations and on Moncler press releases. No verified personal social accounts found.

name: Mark Hancock
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chairman, PACS Group (NYSE: PACS); head of family office PV3 Investments
profile: Hancock co-founded Utah-based skilled-nursing operator PACS Group with Jason Murray in 2013. It grew from two facilities to more than 300 in 17 states and listed on the NYSE in 2024; he owns about 35%. He previously worked as an analyst at Ford, a director at a steel company and treasurer of a financial-services firm.
interesting_fact: In 2024 his family office PV3 Investments bought Utah carbon bike-component maker ENVE Composites from Amer Sports.
deep_cut_fact: Before buying ENVE, Hancock was a longtime customer and cycling enthusiast. ENVE's GM said he owns two custom ENVE road bikes and lives about 20 minutes from the Ogden factory, and called the deal 'an investment, not a private equity' play.
notes: Low media profile. Cycling and ENVE make a natural, friendly opening. Be aware that PACS has faced public accounting and short-seller scrutiny since late 2024.

name: Michael S. Smith
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Freeport LNG (Houston); director, Teledyne Technologies
profile: Made his first fortune with Basin Exploration, an E&P company he founded in Fort Collins in 1981 and sold to Stone Energy in 2001 for ~$428M. He founded Freeport LNG in 2002 as an import terminal, then flipped it to exports when shale arrived, raising $15B+ of debt to build three liquefaction trains in Freeport, Texas (~15 Mtpa). He still runs it and speaks publicly on U.S. LNG export economics.
interesting_fact: Freeport LNG was designed to import gas; when the shale boom hit he turned the strategy 180 degrees and built one of the largest U.S. LNG export terminals instead.
deep_cut_fact: Though he left CSU just shy of a chemistry degree, his 2016 $13M gift to Colorado State created 50 full-tuition business scholarships for the college's 50th anniversary and completed funding for the Michael Smith Natural Resources Building; he credited 'strong science and mathematics' at CSU for teaching him the oil business.
notes: Company is private. Freeport LNG press releases list media contact Heather Browne, Director Corporate Communications (phone 713-980-2888, office line), e.g. https://freeportlng.com/files/docs/FINAL-Restart-Press-Release-022123-2.pdf. Info@ email dates from a 2018 release. Speaks at CERAWeek/Milken - conference route possible.

name: Hubertus Benteler
current_role: Member of the supervisory board (former CEO), Benteler International AG, Salzburg
profile: Fourth-generation owner of Benteler International, which grew from Carl Benteler's 1876 ironware shop in Bielefeld into a roughly $9bn-revenue maker of automotive components, steel tubes and engineering equipment. He led the group from 1991, turning it into a global auto supplier, and moved to the supervisory board in 2017. Son Casper is expected to lead the family eventually.
interesting_fact: Benteler marks 150 years in 2026; the business began as a small ironware shop opened by Carl Benteler in Bielefeld, Germany, in 1876.
deep_cut_fact: Benteler's official timeline dates his era to 1991, when he took over management and remade the company into a global automotive partner. Its first Mexican plant opened in Puebla in 1992, and the Liberec (Czech) brownfield plant followed in 1995.
notes: Private family. Alive is inferred from Hurun Global 2026 and Forbes listings; no obituary was found. The press page loads its contacts dynamically, so no press email was captured. Corporate communications is the realistic route.

name: Eddie Zakay
current_role: Deputy Chairman, Topland Group (London); brother Sol Zakay is Founder & CEO
profile: Eddie Zakay and his brother Sol built Topland Group, a privately owned London property and investment group, starting in the UK in the 1980s/90s. Topland made its name with counter-cyclical bets and large sale-and-leaseback deals with Marks & Spencer, Tesco and Eroski, and sold its 26 Hallmark hotels in 2019. Today it runs a multi-billion-pound portfolio, a bridging-loan arm and a roughly GBP 0.8bn development pipeline.
interesting_fact: Between 2000 and 2010 Topland completed more than GBP 1.5 billion of sale-and-leasebacks with retailers including Marks & Spencer, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Aldi and Eroski.
deep_cut_fact: In the 2010s Topland moved beyond property into renewable-energy investing, and was an early aggregator of UK supported-living housing before selling the portfolio to long-term holders including Civitas.

public_contacts.value: 'Contact Eddie' form on Topland's People page

notes: Very private; no personal social accounts found. Topland's site has a dedicated per-person contact form for Eddie, which is the best published route. The renewable-energy angle could fit the podcast. Web search quota ran out here; facts come from the company site.

name: Sol Zakay
current_role: Founder and CEO, Topland Group (London)
profile: Israeli-born British property investor (b. 1952) who founded Topland Group with his brother Eddie in the early 1990s (incorporated 1991). Topland made its name on large sale-and-leaseback deals with M&S, Tesco, Sainsbury's, Aldi and Eroski (over £1.5bn in 2000-10). It then expanded into hotels (exited 2019), bridging finance and development, and now has a £0.8bn development pipeline.
interesting_fact: Topland describes itself as a pioneer of UK alternative real-estate lending. It was also an original aggregator of UK supported-living housing, building a portfolio before selling to long-term holders including Civitas.
deep_cut_fact: In the 2010s Topland moved beyond property into renewable-energy investment alongside its real-estate activities. That history fits the podcast's energy angle well.
notes: Very private, with no social accounts. The Topland website has a 'Contact Sol' form on the People page, which is the most direct published route. The company has a past legal dispute with the UK Ministry of Justice (2012); do not raise it.

name: Johan Johannson
current_role: Chairman (since 2022) and co-owner, NorgesGruppen ASA (Norway)
profile: Fifth-generation heir to a trading business founded in 1866 by an earlier Johan Johannson from Askim. With his father Knut Hartvig Johannson he controls about 75% of NorgesGruppen (Kiwi, Meny, Spar, Joker; ~40% of Norway's grocery market). A BI business graduate, he joined the family firm in 1995, ran retail, property and new ventures, and succeeded his father as chairman in 2022.
interesting_fact: The family business began in 1866 as a coffee importer/wholesaler (known for the Ali Kaffe brand) before evolving into Norway's largest grocery group.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent 1991-1995 as a consultant at Andersen Consulting (now Accenture); his uncle Torbjorn Johannson recruited him in 1995 to be the day-to-day driving force of holding company Joh. Johannson. He is also a certified retail worker (butikkfagarbeider).
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: he is now chairman (father stepped down 2022). Family keeps a low profile. Press emails are named NorgesGruppen communications staff listed in its NTB press room.

name: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi
current_role: Shareholder/heir in Diagnósticos da América SA (Dasa); no public executive role found
profile: Camilla de Godoy Bueno Grossi is the daughter of Edson de Godoy Bueno (d. 2017), who co-founded Brazilian health insurer Amil and sold most of it to UnitedHealth for $4.9 billion in 2012. She and her brother Pedro Bueno (Dasa's president) inherited large stakes in lab-diagnostics group Dasa. She keeps a very low public profile; listed as UK-resident.
interesting_fact: Her father Edson Bueno, Brazil's richest healthcare billionaire, sold Amil to UnitedHealth for $4.9 billion in 2012, the source of the family's fortune.
notes: Very private; no personal public presence found. Only route is via Dasa IR (company contact, not hers). Low fit for the podcast.

name: Prasert Prasarttong-Osoth
profile: Died 21 April 2026, aged 93. He was a former surgeon who co-founded Bangkok Dusit Medical Services in 1972 and founded Bangkok Airways. Son Puttipong now leads the airline and daughter Poramaporn is president of BDMS.
notes: Deceased (21 Apr 2026), per Khaosod English and Nation Thailand (https://www.nationthailand.com/news/general/40065318). Profile skipped as per the instructions. For BDMS or Bangkok Airways, contact the next generation instead.

name: Vildan Gulcelik
current_role: Shareholder in ENKA İnşaat ve Sanayi A.Ş. (Gülçelik/Tara founding families); no executive role found
profile: Vildan Gülçelik is one of more than a dozen family members who hold shares in ENKA, one of Turkey's largest construction and energy companies. Sarık Tara and his brother-in-law Şadi Gülçelik cofounded ENKA in 1957. Today it is Turkey's leading private electricity producer and also has real estate (including large Moscow office and retail holdings), tourism and trade businesses.
interesting_fact: For roughly 20 years ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. embassy and consular buildings, with projects from Algeria and Nepal to Equatorial Guinea, the Dominican Republic and the Netherlands.
notes: Passive family shareholder with no public profile; her exact relationship to cofounder Şadi Gülçelik and her current status could not be confirmed (Forbes now lists her profile as former). ENKA's only published contact is the general corporate inbox. The energy angle (ENKA's gas-fired power plants) would go better through ENKA management (CEO Agah Mehmet Tara).

name: Jonathan Harmsworth (4th Viscount Rothermere)
current_role: Chairman, Daily Mail and General Trust (DMGT)
profile: Fourth-generation Harmsworth to run the Daily Mail empire; became chairman of DMGT in 1998 on his father's death. Built MailOnline into one of the world's most-read news sites, took DMGT private in 2021 (~£1.6bn), and in Nov 2025 agreed a £500m deal to buy The Telegraph, which faced a UK public-interest/competition review from Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: DMGT owned energy-market data firm Genscape (bought 2006 for ~$130m) and sold it to Verisk/Wood Mackenzie in 2019 for $364m, a useful energy-data angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Educated at Gordonstoun in Scotland, he went to university in the US, studying history at Duke University, before joining the family's Associated Newspapers.
notes: Very private, rarely interviewed. Telegraph deal status after the 2026 regulatory review not confirmed here; check before outreach. Route via DMGT PR.

name: Susan Williams
current_role: Independent Director, W.W. Grainger (since 2020); President, Donald Slavik Family Foundation; Director, Mark IV Capital
profile: Susan Slavik Williams owns about 5% of industrial distributor W.W. Grainger and has sat on its board since April 2020, serving on the nominating and compensation committees. She has been a director of Newport Beach real-estate firm Mark IV Capital since 1989, and she leads the Donald Slavik Family Foundation, which focuses on wildlife and environmental education.
interesting_fact: As president of the Donald Slavik Family Foundation since 1995, she funds wildlife conservation in North America and Africa. She also sits on the board of the St. Louis Zoo.
deep_cut_fact: Before her board career she was a manager at Capgemini US. With her husband Felix she ran a custom home-electronics firm, The Screening Room, for about 10 years. She also founded Four Palms Ventures LLC.
notes: Low public profile. Grainger corporate communications or the investor-relations page is the only published route. The deep-cut details come from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener) plus Forbes; confirm them in Grainger's proxy before using.

name: Ted Turner
notes: Died May 6, 2026, aged 87 (AP). Source: https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2026/may/6/ted-turner-cnn-founder-brash-outspoken-television-pioneer-died-age-87/. Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Tatiana Casiraghi
current_role: Co-founder and creative director, Muzungu Sisters (ethical fashion brand); member of Monaco's princely family by marriage
profile: Born Tatiana Santo Domingo in New York in 1983, granddaughter of Colombian brewing magnate Julio Mario Santo Domingo; her wealth stems from the family's SABMiller stake (now AB InBev). Married Andrea Casiraghi of Monaco in 2013-14. In 2011 she co-launched Muzungu Sisters with Dana Alikhani, sourcing handmade garments from artisans at fair prices.
interesting_fact: She and co-founder Dana Alikhani met in London and started Muzungu Sisters in 2009 after travels together; the brand buys handmade clothing directly from artisans in countries such as Colombia, Morocco and India and sells it at fair prices. She speaks five languages.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion, she trained in photography (BFA in visual communications, photography concentration, 2005) and interned at Vanity Fair in New York; she cites Loulou de la Falaise as her style idol.
notes: Wealth estimates vary widely (Forbes later revised to well below $1B). Royal-adjacent and private; contact via Muzungu Sisters brand. Weak fit for energy/data-centre topic; entrepreneurship/ethical-sourcing angle only. Recent Hola interview (May 2026).

name: Girdharilal Bawri
current_role: Chairman and co-founder, Macleods Pharmaceuticals (Mumbai)
profile: Girdharilal Bawri co-founded Macleods Pharmaceuticals in 1986 with brothers Rajendra Agarwal and Banwarilal Bawri; the family had owned a pharmacy in Jaipur. Privately held Macleods began with anti-TB drugs and is now a top-10 Indian pharma firm selling generics (HIV, malaria, diabetes, cardio, respiratory) in 170+ countries. Brother and MD Rajendra Agarwal died in November 2025.
interesting_fact: The company is named after John Macleod, a Scottish doctor and author of medical textbooks; the three brothers and their families lived together in the same Mumbai building.
deep_cut_fact: Macleods built its business on first- and second-line tuberculosis medicines and became a key exporter of affordable TB drugs; its first R&D centre opened in Mumbai in 2000.
notes: No interviews found; very low media profile. Family recently lost co-founder Rajendra Agarwal (Nov 2025) — be sensitive in timing/tone. Route via Macleods corporate office (contact page is JS-rendered; check https://www.macleodspharma.com/contact-us in a browser).

name: Xie Zhikun
profile: Founder of Beijing-based Zhongzhi Enterprise Group (est. 1995), who started in timber and real estate before building a large wealth-management/shadow-banking business. He died of a heart attack in Beijing on 18 December 2021, aged 61.
notes: DECEASED 18 Dec 2021 (heart attack, Beijing) - sources: https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3160259/chinese-rags-riches-tycoon-xie-zhikun-dies-aged-61 ; https://yicaiglobal.com/news/20211220-03---shares-of-firms-controlled-by-china-zhongzhi-dive-on-founder-sudden-death . Zhongzhi later collapsed and entered liquidation (2023-24). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Bang Si-hyuk
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, HYBE Co. (formerly Big Hit Entertainment)
profile: Seoul National University aesthetics graduate and hit songwriter ('Hitman Bang') who co-founded JYP Entertainment's songwriting engine before launching Big Hit, home of BTS. HYBE's 2020 IPO made him a billionaire; it has since bought Ithaca Holdings and built a multi-label global group. He stepped down as CEO in 2021 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He signed RM, later BTS's leader, when RM was just 15, and co-wrote six songs on BTS's 2016 album 'Wings'.
deep_cut_fact: He debuted as a composer while still a student, winning the 1994 Yoo Jae-ha Music Contest; in 2022 SNU gave him an honorary business doctorate, the first awarded to an entertainment-industry figure.
notes: Ongoing criminal investigation over 2019-20 pre-IPO dealings (case referred to prosecutors Sept 2026; shares provisionally seized) - outreach timing/reputational sensitivity. No verified published press email found (press@hybecorp.com appears only in third-party docs, not used). Route via HYBE corporate communications.

name: Amy Goldman Fowler
current_role: Co-owner, Solil Management (Goldman family real estate); author, heirloom gardener and seed-conservation philanthropist
profile: Daughter of New York real estate investor Sol Goldman, she shares ownership of Solil Management (about 400 properties) equally with her siblings; her sister Jane runs it. She holds a Ph.D. in clinical psychology, grows heirloom vegetables on her Rhinebeck, NY farm, has written five books, and is a former board chair and now special adviser of Seed Savers Exchange.
interesting_fact: Her husband Cary Fowler helped create the Svalbard Global Seed Vault. Her books (The Melon, The Heirloom Tomato, The Compleat Squash, Heirloom Harvest) have won multiple American Horticultural Society Book of the Year awards.
deep_cut_fact: She also sculpts: 'Rare Forms' is her line of limited-edition bronze sculptures of heirloom produce from her Hudson Valley garden. Garden Conservancy president emeritus Gregory Long called her 'perhaps the world's premier vegetable gardener.'
notes: Her author website has a contact page and a media kit. The best hook is gardening, seed conservation and books rather than real estate. She publishes as 'Amy Goldman'.

name: Ravi Ruia
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Essar Group (senior family figure since brother Shashi's death in Nov 2024)
profile: Co-founded Essar with elder brother Shashi in 1969, growing it from a Chennai port construction contract into a conglomerate spanning steel, oil refining, power, ports and telecom. Essar bought the Stanlow refinery (Essar Oil UK, now EET Fuels) from Shell in 2011 and sold its Indian refiner to a Rosneft-led group for $12.9bn in 2017; it now pursues energy-transition projects at Stanlow.
interesting_fact: The name Essar comes from the brothers' initials, 'S' and 'R' (Shashi and Ravi); the group's first job was a 1969 contract worth about Rs 2.3 crore to build an outer breakwater for Chennai (Madras) Port.
deep_cut_fact: He is a mechanical engineer by training, a graduate of the College of Engineering, Guindy in Chennai - India's oldest engineering college (founded 1794) - and was singled out as one of its six most notable alumni when it turned 225 in 2018.
notes: Essar's corporate press contacts are on essar.com press releases (Essar Capital corporate affairs) and EET Fuels (Stanlow) releases, but those sites blocked automated fetching, so no email was verified. Forbes profile is joint with Shashi Ruia (died 2024). Best route: Essar corporate affairs office.

name: Douglas Perkins
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Specsavers Group (Guernsey)
profile: Llanelli-born optometrist (b. 1943), trained at Cardiff, where he met his wife and co-founder Dame Mary Perkins. They built and sold a 22-store West Country optician chain in 1980, then launched Specsavers in Guernsey in 1984; it is now the world's largest privately owned optical and audiology group, with 2,500+ stores in 11 countries. In 2023 they placed it in a family trust to keep it from private equity.
interesting_fact: Specsavers was started in 1984 on a table-tennis table in the couple's spare bedroom in Guernsey, and they still live in that house.
deep_cut_fact: The founders kept the table-tennis table they used as Specsavers' first desk; Dame Mary told the BBC at the 40th anniversary that 'you could still use it,' as they still have the bats and balls. Doug, a policeman's son from Llanelli, was made a CBE in 2025.
notes: Wealth is shared with wife Dame Mary Perkins (the Forbes/Hurun entry is joint). Modest and low-key; told the Guernsey Press 'this award isn't for me' on receiving his CBE. Best route is the Specsavers press office.

name: Walter Faria
current_role: Owner and controlling shareholder, Grupo Petrópolis (Itaipava, Crystal, Petra, Black Princess beers), Brazil
profile: Brazilian brewer (b. 1955, Pedranópolis, SP) who went from a cotton gin to Brazil's largest Schincariol distributor, then bought Cervejaria Petrópolis in 1998 at ~2% market share; by 2013 Itaipava made it Brazil's No. 2 brewer. The group also makes TNT energy drink - likely the source of the 'energy' tag, not the energy sector.
interesting_fact: Under Faria, Grupo Petrópolis grew from about 2% of Brazil's beer sales in 1998 to over 11% and the No. 2 national brand in 2013, largely through aggressive marketing and low prices.
deep_cut_fact: At 13, in the Macedônia district of Fernandópolis (SP), he sold eggs and piglets around town using a horse cart - a cart he kept as a keepsake. His savings then funded a coffee-processing business with a brother.

public_contacts.value: VCRP Brasil (press relations for Grupo Petrópolis, South/Southeast, appointed 2024)

notes: Very private, gives no interviews. Carries significant legal baggage (Lava Jato 2019 arrest; group filed for judicial recovery in 2023) - poor fit and sensitive; avoid these topics. Weak link to the energy theme (beverages only). Company site blocks automated access; press route is via the group's PR agencies.

name: Wonowidjojo family
current_role: Controlling family of PT Gudang Garam Tbk (kretek cigarettes); Susilo Wonowidjojo is president director
profile: Indonesian family behind Gudang Garam, the Kediri-based clove-cigarette (kretek) maker founded in 1958 by Surya Wonowidjojo and run since 1984 by his son Susilo. The family controls the listed company and has diversified into infrastructure, including the privately financed Dhoho airport and a toll road in Kediri.
interesting_fact: Gudang Garam's subsidiary PT Surya Dhoho Investama built Dhoho Airport in Kediri, inaugurated in October 2024 as Indonesia's first airport built without government budget (an unsolicited PPP).
deep_cut_fact: The Dhoho airport launched with a Citilink inaugural flight on 5 April 2024 and is operated by state operator Angkasa Pura I under a cooperation deal with Gudang Garam's Surya Dhoho Investama.
notes: Family entry, not one person; Susilo Wonowidjojo is the figurehead. Extremely private, essentially never gives interviews. A corporate-secretary email appears only on aggregator sites (not verified on the company site, which blocked access). Infrastructure (airport/toll road) is the natural podcast angle.

name: Gerard Louis-Dreyfus
notes: Deceased: Gérard (William) Louis-Dreyfus, Louis Dreyfus Energy Services chairman and Louis Dreyfus Group heir, died 16 September 2016. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G%C3%A9rard_Louis-Dreyfus

name: Ricardo Martin Bringas
current_role: CEO (Director General) and board member, Organización Soriana (Mexico)
profile: Member of the Martín Bringas family that controls Soriana, one of Mexico's largest supermarket chains (founded in Torreón). A 1982 Tec de Monterrey computer-systems graduate, he worked across commercial, credit, finance and systems roles before becoming director general on 4 Nov 1991, a post he has held for 30+ years.
interesting_fact: He has run Soriana as CEO since November 1991, one of the longest CEO tenures among Mexico's listed companies.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2025 Tec de Monterrey's Laguna campus gave him the Premio al Mérito EXATEC; accepting it he said 'success is a very subjective word' and advised young entrepreneurs to act with ethics, professionalism and 'mucho empuje' (lots of drive).
notes: Low media profile. IR email is from Soriana's BMV issuer profile and may be dated; confirm via Soriana's investor site.

name: Do Won Chang
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO, Forever 21 (no current role found)
profile: Korean-born Do Won Chang emigrated to Los Angeles in 1981 and in 1984 co-founded Forever 21 with his wife Jin Sook, growing it from one 900 sq ft store to roughly 800 stores worldwide. The family-owned chain filed for bankruptcy in 2019 and its assets were sold in 2020; Forbes no longer lists the Changs as billionaires. No public information found on his activities since.
interesting_fact: The couple started the first store, Fashion 21 in Highland Park, LA, with $11,000 in savings and reached $700,000 in first-year sales, then opened a new store roughly every six months.
deep_cut_fact: Carnegie Corporation of New York named him one of its 'Great Immigrants' in 2017. Forever 21 bags carried 'John 3:16' printed on the bottom, reflecting the founders' Christian faith.
notes: No longer a billionaire after the 2019 bankruptcy; Forbes/Hurun listings are stale (2011-2019). Very private, with no published contact channel. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source (born 1954; no death reported). Shares listing with wife Jin Sook Chang.

name: Jin Sook Chang
current_role: Co-founder and former chief merchandising officer of Forever 21 (no longer involved since the 2019-20 bankruptcy sale)
profile: Korean-born Jin Sook Chang emigrated to Los Angeles in 1981 with husband Do Won Chang; in 1984 they opened a 900 sq ft store, Fashion 21, in Highland Park and built it into Forever 21, a fast-fashion chain with ~600 stores and 30,000 staff by 2015, where she ran merchandising. The company went bankrupt in 2019 and was sold in 2020; she is no longer listed as a billionaire.
interesting_fact: The couple are devout Christians, which is why 'John 3:16' was printed on the bottom of every Forever 21 shopping bag.
deep_cut_fact: The empire began as a 900-square-foot shop called 'Fashion 21' in LA's Highland Park, opened in 1984 with just $11,000 in savings.
notes: No longer a billionaire (Forbes, July 2019) and no public activity found since 2020; very private. Avoid the bankruptcy as a topic. Profile is shared with husband Do Won Chang. No published contact channels.

name: Hanni Toosbuy Kasprzak
current_role: Chairman of the Board, ECCO Sko A/S and ECCO Holding (Bredebro, Denmark); board member, The Toosbuy Foundation
profile: Daughter of shoemaker Karl Toosbuy, who founded ECCO with Birte Toosbuy in Bredebro, Denmark, in 1963. She joined the company straight out of school, became board chair in June 1996 and took majority ownership in 1997. ECCO is one of the few big shoe brands that owns its value chain, from tanneries to stores; her son Andre Kasprzak sits on the board.
interesting_fact: ECCO is a vertically integrated shoemaker that owns its own tanneries and factories - unusual among global footwear brands - and has been controlled by one family from tiny Bredebro in southwest Denmark since 1963.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job after school was as an ECCO quality controller in India in 1978/79, before returning to headquarters in Bredebro to work across several departments.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed. Husband Dieter Kasprzak was long-time ECCO CEO. Avoid ECCO's Russia-operations controversy in outreach. Route via ECCO group press office.

name: Robert Defares
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman/CEO, IMC Trading (IMC Financial Markets), Amsterdam
profile: Rob Defares co-founded IMC with René Schelvis in 1989 as a partnership of market makers on the floor of the Amsterdam Equity Options Exchange. IMC is now a global proprietary trading and market-making firm with about 2,000 employees across 10 offices. Defares has led it as CEO and chairman, sole CEO since co-CEO Wiet Pot left the board in 2017.
interesting_fact: IMC began as two traders on the Amsterdam options floor, where orders were made by hand signals, and became one of the first firms to build its own automated trading systems.
deep_cut_fact: The firm's original name was 'International Marketmaker's Combination', which is what the letters IMC stand for.
notes: Very low public profile: almost no interviews. The route is via IMC's Amsterdam office. IMC's data-centre and low-latency infrastructure fits the podcast's data-center angle. His current title (CEO vs chairman) comes from secondary sources, so verify it.

name: Thomas Friedkin
notes: Thomas H. Friedkin, founder of Gulf States Toyota (Houston, 1969), died 14 March 2017 aged 81 (Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_H._Friedkin; Houston Chronicle 25 Mar 2017). Business now led by his son Dan Friedkin (The Friedkin Group, owner of AS Roma/Everton) - research him separately if relevant.

name: Garibaldi Thohir
current_role: Vice President Commissioner, PT Alamtri Resources Indonesia Tbk (formerly Adaro Energy; stepped down as President Director at the June 2025 AGM)
profile: Garibaldi 'Boy' Thohir, son of Astra co-founder Teddy Thohir and brother of Erick Thohir, led the 2005 takeover of coal miner Adaro and ran it for ~2 decades, steering it toward aluminium smelting, minerals and renewables (now AlamTri; coal spun off as AADI in 2024). He is also a tech investor (ex-Gojek commissioner).
interesting_fact: He served as president commissioner of Gojek after founder Nadiem Makarim joined the cabinet in 2019, and has said he advised Nadiem informally for years before Gojek scaled.
deep_cut_fact: Back from his US MBA, he wanted a $2,000-a-month job at Citibank, but his father refused and told him to be an entrepreneur. His first venture (1991) was a plan to build a rental office on a 3,000 m2 plot along the new Saharjo-Kuningan road in Jakarta; it stalled because land clearances required at least 1 hectare.
notes: Widely known as 'Boy Thohir'. corsec@ is AlamTri's corporate secretary (company office, not personal). Some data sites still list him as President Director - outdated since June 2025. Energy-transition angle: AlamTri is building an aluminium smelter and hydro/renewables in North Kalimantan.

name: Ronald Southern
notes: ATCO and Spruce Meadows founder Ron Southern died January 21, 2016, in Calgary, aged 85 (https://globalnews.ca/news/2469107/atco-founder-ron-southern-dies-at-85). His daughter Nancy Southern now leads ATCO.

name: Stephen D. Jr. And Riley P. Bechtel
current_role: Riley P. Bechtel: non-executive director (former chairman & CEO), Bechtel Corporation. Stephen D. Bechtel Jr.: deceased.
profile: Joint Forbes entry for father and son owners of Bechtel, the San Francisco engineering and construction giant. Stephen Jr. ran the firm 1960-1990 and died March 15, 2021 aged 95. Riley, his son and great-grandson of founder Warren Bechtel, was CEO 1990-2014 and chairman to 2017, then stayed on as a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Riley Bechtel first worked summers at the company starting in 1966, joined full-time in 1981 and was CEO by 1990, making him the fourth generation of the family to lead it.
notes: Mixed entry: Stephen D. Bechtel Jr. died 2021 (https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/retired-chairman-and-ceo-stephen-d-bechtel-jr-dies-at-95-301247806.html). Riley P. Bechtel alive per available sources; he stepped back as CEO in 2014 for health reasons. Very private family; Bechtel corporate media team is the only route.

notes: Deceased (d. 2013-03-23), source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boris_Berezovsky_(businessman)

name: Henry Lea Hillman
