notes: Deceased (2017); see University of Pittsburgh and Princeton Alumni Weekly memorials. The family office (The Hillman Company) and the Hillman Family Foundations continue.

name: Semahat Arsel
current_role: Chair, Vehbi Koç Foundation board & executive committee; board member, Koç Holding; chair, Divan Group
profile: Semahat Sevim Arsel (b. 1928, Ankara) is the eldest child of Koç Group founder Vehbi Koç and holds a stake in Koç Holding, Turkey's largest conglomerate (energy via Tüpraş, Aygaz, autos, appliances, banking). On Koç's board since 1964, she built its tourism/hospitality arm and leads the family's main foundation.
interesting_fact: Turkey's only postgraduate nursing education center, SANERC (founded 1992 at the American Hospital, Istanbul), is named after her; she has chaired the Vehbi Koç Foundation's Nursing Committee since its nursing fund began in 1974.
deep_cut_fact: In 1972 she took charge of renovating Istanbul's Divan Hotel in Elmadağ and went on to turn 'Divan' into a luxury hospitality brand; she also co-founded TUGEV, a foundation for tourism training, and lived in Germany in 1959-60, studying at the Goethe Institute.
notes: Aged 98 and very private; no personal public channels. Best route is via the Vehbi Koç Foundation or Koç Holding corporate communications. Koç's energy link (Tüpraş refining, Aygaz, Entek power) is the podcast angle.

name: Lukas Henrik Lundin
profile: Swedish-Canadian resource financier who chaired the Lundin Group of mining and energy companies for 25+ years (Lundin Mining, Lucara Diamond, Filo Mining, NGEx etc.); family holdings were held via the Nemesia trust vehicle. He died on 26 July 2022 in Geneva, aged 64, after a two-year battle with brain cancer.
notes: Deceased 26 July 2022 (sources: https://www.mining.com/?p=1096241 ; https://filomining.mediaroom.com/2022-07-27-Filo-Minings-Founder-and-Former-Chairman-Lukas-H-Lundin-Passes-Away). Sons Adam and Jack Lundin now lead Lundin Group companies; the Lundin family remains long-term shareholders.

name: Henrik Mads Clausen
current_role: Shareholder of Danfoss A/S (no public executive or board role found)
profile: Born 1953, one of five children of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen and Bitten Clausen. He is listed as a direct owner of Danfoss alongside Clausen Controls A/S and the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation (largest shareholder). Danfoss, based in Nordborg, Denmark, makes drives, cooling, heating and power solutions, including for data centers.
interesting_fact: Danfoss was founded by his father Mads Clausen in 1933 in a farmhouse attic on the island of Als; the company now leads in energy-efficient cooling, drives and heat pumps.

public_contacts.value: lars.lohff@danfoss.com (Lars Grubak Lohff, Head of Media Relations, Danfoss)

notes: Very private; no public role. Family is represented on the Danfoss board by third-generation Mads Clausen and Mads-Peter Clausen - better interview targets for an energy/data-center podcast. Approach via Danfoss media relations.

name: Arvindkumar Poddar
current_role: CEO & Managing Director (chairman & MD in earlier filings), Balkrishna Industries Ltd (BKT Tires), Mumbai
profile: Arvind Poddar controls and runs Balkrishna Industries (BKT), the Mumbai-listed maker of off-highway tyres for agriculture, mining and earthmoving. BKT opened its first off-highway tyre plant in Aurangabad in 1987 and sells mainly into replacement markets in Europe and North America. It held about 8% of the global off-the-road tyre segment in 2014 and supplies OEMs such as JCB, John Deere and CNH.
interesting_fact: Under Poddar, BKT became a major sports sponsor: the official tyre of Monster Jam since 2014 and title sponsor of Italy's Serie BKT and France's Ligue 2 BKT (extended to 2028). In October 2026 it announced a 50:50 joint venture with Pirelli to make Pirelli-branded premium tyres in India.
notes: Web search budget ran out at this point, so research came from Wikipedia and BKT's site only and no sourced deep-cut fact was found. BKT runs a registration-only Press Hub for journalists, which is the logical route. The investor-relations email is in stock-exchange filings but was not verified here.

name: Sandeep Pravinbhai Engineer
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Astral Limited (Ahmedabad)
profile: Sandeep Engineer is a first-generation entrepreneur and chemical engineer. He spent eight years in pharmaceutical bulk drugs before founding Astral Poly Technik in 1996, now Astral Ltd, a leading Indian maker of plastic pipes and building materials. He has since expanded into adhesives (Resinova, 2014), water tanks (Sarita, 2020) and paints (Gem Paints).
interesting_fact: In 1998 Astral launched CPVC piping in India for the first time. Plastic pipes were then barely accepted against metal, so Engineer spent years educating plumbers and builders to create the category Astral now leads.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a project engineer at a pharmaceuticals company, then became a distributor and later manufactured pharmaceutical remedies. He said he had been fascinated by polymers since his graduation days, which led to the pivot into piping. He also completed Harvard Business School's OPM programme.
notes: Self-made founder story with a strong entrepreneurship angle. His wife Jagruti Engineer is a whole-time director. Contact is through Astral corporate (info@) or company secretary or IR via the investors page.

name: Rafique Abdul Malik
current_role: Chairman, Metro Brands Limited (Mumbai)
profile: Indian footwear retailer who turned the single Colaba, Mumbai shoe store his father Malik Tejani acquired in 1955 into Metro Brands, one of India's largest and most profitable footwear chains (~800 stores) with Metro Shoes, Mochi and Walkway plus franchises for Crocs, FitFlop, Fila and Foot Locker. Metro Brands is listed; daughter Farah Malik Bhanji is MD and Nissan Joseph CEO.
interesting_fact: Metro started as one standalone shoe shop in Colaba, Mumbai, and over three generations grew into a 'Made in India' footwear house of brands with roughly 800 stores.
deep_cut_fact: He has been chairman since 19 January 1977, the month Metro Shoes was incorporated, giving him nearly five decades at the helm; the company bio also notes he is a Harvard alumnus.
notes: Low public profile; daughter and MD Farah Malik Bhanji is the usual public face. The company site has a Media section that may list a PR contact.

name: Cecilia Morel
current_role: Former First Lady of Chile (2010-14, 2018-22); heir to the Piñera family fortune (family investment group Bancard)
profile: Cecilia Morel Montes is the widow of former Chilean president and billionaire investor Sebastián Piñera (d. 2024), whose fortune came from introducing credit cards to Chile and stakes including LATAM Airlines; Hurun lists her as holder of the family wealth. A trained family and youth counsellor, she chaired social foundations such as Integra and PRODEMU as First Lady.
interesting_fact: She was at the San José mine site with the president throughout the October 2010 rescue of the 33 trapped Copiapó miners, famously moved to tears when the first miner surfaced.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989, with professionals from the Instituto Carlos Casanueva, she founded 'La Casa de la Juventud', running personal-development workshops for young people in Santiago's Conchalí district; the project later spun off the Women Embark Foundation.
notes: Not an entrepreneur in her own right; wealth is inherited from Sebastián Piñera (family vehicle Grupo Bancard). No published personal/office contact verified (search budget exhausted). Recently widowed (2024) - handle sensitively. Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast.

name: Jogi Hendra Atmadja
current_role: Founder and President Commissioner (chairman), PT Mayora Indah Tbk
profile: Jakarta-born (1946) University of Indonesia economics graduate who founded Mayora with his siblings in 1977, starting with a biscuit factory in Tangerang. Mayora now owns 50+ brands including Kopiko, Danisa, Beng-Beng, Torabika and Energen, runs 25 factories and exports to 100+ countries; son Andre Sukendra Atmadja is president director.
interesting_fact: Through its Kopiko brand, Mayora is often described as the world's largest coffee-candy maker; Kopiko is exported to more than 100 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mayora, he started his career as a banker at Bank Central Asia.
notes: Very low public profile, in his late 70s. Deep-cut fact cited via Wikipedia to a Jakarta Post article that was paywalled/403 for me - verify before use. Mayora's published consumer email (consumer@mayora.co.id) is consumer-care only, not a press route.

name: Zhou Guodi
current_role: Listed by Hurun (with Cao Longxiang) as a principal owner of Jumpcan Pharmaceutical (济川药业, SSE: 600566), Taixing, Jiangsu
profile: Hurun lists Zhou Guodi together with Cao Longxiang as owners of Jumpcan Pharmaceutical. Jumpcan is a Jiangsu drugmaker with 4,000+ staff, focused on respiratory, paediatric, digestive and women's health, including the Pudilan brand. It went from state-owned to private in 1998 and listed in Shanghai via a 2013 reverse listing. I couldn't independently verify her personal role.
interesting_fact: Jumpcan went from state-owned to private shareholding in 1998 and first entered China's top-100 pharmaceutical manufacturers in 2001. It has since struck licensing deals for innovative drugs (e.g. with I-Mab in 2021 and Akeso in 2025).
notes: My web search quota ran out at this point, so verification is limited to the company site. Neither the company site nor any source I could reach names her. Cao Longxiang is the better-known figure (understood to be her husband/co-owner, not verified here). jc@jumpcan.com is the general/customer-service address.

name: Douglas Hsu Hsu-Tung
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Far Eastern Group (Taipei); re-elected chairman of Asia Cement in 2026
profile: Douglas Tong Hsu (徐旭東) is the son of founder Yu-Ziang Hsu and heads Far Eastern Group, a Taiwanese conglomerate of about 250 companies and nine listed firms. Its businesses span petrochemicals and energy (including Chiahui Power), polyester, cement, telecom (Far EasTone), banking, retail (SOGO, Far Eastern Department Stores) and hotels. Son Jeff Hsu debuted as group Chief Innovation Officer at 2026 AGMs.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Far Eastern New Century became the world's third-largest polyester textile maker (2018), and the group's family foundations established leading private universities and a medical-centre hospital in Taiwan.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his BA and MA at the University of Notre Dame, where he is an Emeritus Trustee, followed by postgraduate study at Columbia. His Committee of 100 profile calls him an 'architecture devotee' and collector of modern art and sculpture who enjoys diving and swimming.
notes: No personal or press email published on the FEG site (the only email listed is a mall customer-service address, so it is excluded). Energy and telecom holdings make him a podcast fit; best route is via group corporate communications or Far EasTone/FENC investor relations. Member of the Committee of 100 since 2005.

name: Maria Dolores Mantegazza
current_role: Heir and shareholder of the Globus family of travel brands (Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways, Monograms; U.S. arm Group Voyagers); trustee, Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation
profile: Maria Dolores Mantegazza (b. 1956) is the daughter of Sergio Mantegazza (1927-2024), longtime owner-chairman of Lugano-based Globus, the escorted-tour group behind Globus, Cosmos, Avalon Waterways and Monograms. She appeared on Hurun's 2024 global list after inheriting a share of the family fortune on her father's death in February 2024.
interesting_fact: The Globus travel empire traces back to 1928, when her grandfather Antonio Mantegazza started out with a single gondola carrying tourists and goods on Lake Lugano.
deep_cut_fact: She is a trustee, with Fabio and Geo Mantegazza, of the Sergio Mantegazza Charitable Foundation in Canton Ticino, which supports arts, youth sports, education and medical charities.
notes: Extremely private; no interviews or public channels found. Alive status inferred from Hurun 2024 listing, not independently confirmed (web-search budget exhausted). Globus press pages blocked automated access; best route is the Globus/Group Voyagers corporate press office.

name: TS Kalyanaraman
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Kalyan Jewellers India Ltd
profile: Born in Thrissur, Kerala in 1947, Kalyanaraman came from a family textile business founded by his grandfather in 1909. He opened the first Kalyan Jewellers store in Thrissur in 1993 and built it into one of India's largest jewellery chains, with stores in India and the Gulf. The company listed in 2021. He also runs Kalyan Developers.
interesting_fact: He opened the first Kalyan Jewellers showroom in Thrissur on 18 April 1993, after two decades in the family's textile retail business, Kalyan Silks.
deep_cut_fact: He was named after his grandfather T. S. Kalyanarama Iyer, who started the family business in 1909. He began learning trade at age 12 by helping in his father's shop, and in 2023 he published an autobiography, 'The Golden Touch'.
notes: The age-12 detail is from Wikipedia (citing Bloomberg 2013). His autobiography is a good conversation hook. The company's general inbox is the only published email; the IR page lists no separate address.

name: Basudeo Narain Singh
current_role: Executive Chairman, Alkem Laboratories Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Co-founder of Alkem Laboratories, one of India's largest pharma companies (incorporated 1973, listed on BSE/NSE), which he built with his elder brother Samprada Singh. Samprada, the Chairman Emeritus, has died; Basudeo is now Executive Chairman, and the next generation (e.g. MD Sandeep Singh) sits on the board.
interesting_fact: Alkem's own founders' story compares the two brothers' partnership to the Ramayana: 'a tale of two determined brothers' from Bihar who built a company now employing over 23,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: After the Jehanabad district school in Bihar and a degree from Patna University, he had started work as a professor when his brother called him into the business. In the early years he personally delivered stock to stockists and distributors.
notes: Listed as Executive Chairman on Alkem's board page (checked Nov 2026). Low media profile. Corporate head-office and IR channels are the published routes.

name: Guo Jianjun
current_role: Former general manager of Inner Mongolia Huineng Group (汇能集团); left Huineng's management and shareholding in July 2025
profile: Guo Jianjun (郭建军) is the son of Guo Jinshu, who quit as head of the Ordos coal bureau in 2004 to found Huineng Group (coal, coal-to-gas/power, roads, property). As Huineng's GM he led its capital-markets push, including a stake in Asia-Potash International and an offer for ST Xinchao (oil & gas). Hurun listed him 2019-2024; a July 2025 filing says he exited Huineng.
interesting_fact: Hurun ranked him alone under Huineng (coal, roads & bridges, property, Ordos), at No. 224 in 2024 with RMB 22bn, while his father Guo Jinshu remains Huineng's chairman.
deep_cut_fact: In his first media interview he said Huineng would enter capital markets 'in a long-term, good-faith, professional way' and would not take over companies 'like a barbarian' (不会选择'野蛮人'的方式入主).
notes: Identity confirmed (Hurun API: 郭建军/Huineng/Ordos; Sohu Aug 2026). Prior pass confused him with father Guo Jinshu. Per an Asia-Potash filing (July 2025) he left Huineng management/ownership after being penalised for disclosure violations in the ST Xinchao bid, so avoid that topic. No published personal contacts; Huineng is the only org route.

name: Pritviraj Jindal
current_role: Chairperson (Non-Executive), Jindal SAW Ltd. (O.P. Jindal Group)
profile: Prithavi Raj (P.R.) Jindal is the eldest son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group. When the group was split among the four brothers, he took Jindal SAW, a leading maker of submerged-arc-welded line pipe for oil, gas and water, and the family cross-holdings give him stakes in JSW Steel and other group companies. His daughters Sminu Jindal (MD) and Shraddha (Joint MD) now help run Jindal SAW.
interesting_fact: Jindal SAW credits him with introducing SAW (submerged-arc-welded) pipe manufacturing in India more than four decades ago, helping make India one of the world's leading line-pipe makers.
deep_cut_fact: Besides steel pipes, he is listed as a director of Sonabheel Tea Limited, a tea company, among his other board seats.
notes: Company spells his name 'Prithavi Raj Jindal' (also P.R. Jindal). Listed under UAE by Hurun. Low personal media profile; route through Jindal SAW corporate office (New Delhi). Pipe and energy-infrastructure angle (oil and gas, water) fits the podcast.

name: Patrice Pichet
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (PDG), Groupe Pichet (Pessac, Gironde)
profile: Bordeaux-born (1959) property developer who started as a salesman for home-builder Maisons Phénix in 1983. He did his first property deal on a Bordeaux plot in 1988 and founded his own developer, Eurobat. Renamed Groupe Pichet in 2004, the family company now develops housing and commercial property across France, especially Île-de-France, and employs about 1,250-1,400 people.
interesting_fact: Groupe Pichet bought Château Les Carmes Haut-Brion (Pessac-Léognan) in 2010; it is the only Bordeaux château with an address inside the city of Bordeaux.
deep_cut_fact: He commissioned Philippe Starck (with architect Luc Arsène-Henry) to design a ship-shaped winery at Les Carmes Haut-Brion. Inaugurated in 2016 at a cost of about €10m, it was the first wine cellar of Starck's career.
notes: French-language outreach is advisable. The Groupe Pichet press office is the best route; the wine estate (les-carmes-haut-brion.com) is a softer conversational hook.

name: Bhushan Dua
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, T-Series (Super Cassettes Industries Pvt Ltd), Mumbai/Noida
profile: Bhushan Kumar Dua (b. 1977, Delhi), son of T-Series founder Gulshan Kumar, took charge of the music label as a teenager in 1997 with his uncle Krishan Kumar. He built T-Series into India's largest music label and a major Bollywood producer (Aashiqui 2, Hindi Medium, Animal, Bhool Bhulaiyaa franchise), and its YouTube channel became one of the world's most-subscribed.
interesting_fact: He is credited as producer on 100+ films since Tum Bin (2001); T-Series' Hindi Medium won him the Filmfare Award for Best Film.
notes: Listed as Bhushan Dua; publicly known as Bhushan Kumar. T-Series site says to contact exclusively via its contact page. Avoid father's 1997 murder and past allegations/tax probe. No sourced deep-cut fact found beyond widely known film credits.

name: Anand Suresh Deshpande
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Persistent Systems (Pune); stepped back from CEO role in 2019
profile: Anand Deshpande (IIT Kharagpur B.Tech; Indiana University PhD, 1989) founded Persistent Systems in Pune in 1990 with about Rs 2 lakh of own and borrowed money and built it into a listed global software/AI engineering firm (Q2 FY27 revenue $487.6M; 2026 takeover offer for Nagarro). Through the family's deAsra Foundation he supports small 'nano-entrepreneurs'.
interesting_fact: deAsra Foundation, named from his family's initials, has supported more than 750,000 nano-entrepreneurs with free help on registrations, finance and business setup.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Persistent he worked as a Member of Technical Staff at Hewlett-Packard Laboratories in Palo Alto (1989-1990), after a database-systems PhD at Indiana University, which later gave him its School of Informatics Career Achievement Award.
notes: Accessible, entrepreneurship-focused founder who speaks often at Indian tech/startup events; strong fit for an entrepreneurship podcast. deAsra (deasra.in) is another route.

name: Devi Prasad Shetty
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Narayana Health (Narayana Hrudayalaya Ltd), Bengaluru
profile: Cardiac surgeon from Karnataka, trained at Kasturba Medical College and Guy's Hospital, London. He founded Narayana Hrudayalaya in Bengaluru in 2001 and grew it into a listed hospital chain, including a facility in the Cayman Islands, built on assembly-line economies of scale. That model has pushed bypass surgery prices to a fraction of US costs, and his family holds a majority stake.
interesting_fact: The Wall Street Journal called him 'the Henry Ford of heart surgery'. His hospitals save money with tricks like cross-ventilation instead of air-conditioning, and their surgeons do 30-35 operations a day.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up the eighth of nine children in Kinnigoli village and chose heart surgery as a schoolboy after hearing of Christiaan Barnard's first heart transplant. In 1992 in Kolkata he performed India's first neonatal heart surgery, on a 21-day-old baby. He also co-designed Yeshasvini, Karnataka's low-cost farmers' health insurance scheme.
notes: Padma Shri (2004) and Padma Bhushan (2012). He speaks often about healthcare economics and frugal innovation, which suits an entrepreneurship podcast. No dedicated press email was found; investor relations is the best published route.

name: Hilmi Panigoro
current_role: President Director, PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (MedcoEnergi), Jakarta
profile: Bandung-born geologist and younger brother of Medco founder Arifin Panigoro. Joined Medco as a director in 1998 and has run or overseen it since (President Director 2001-08 and again from 2015). MedcoEnergi spans oil & gas across Southeast Asia, power (incl. geothermal/solar) and a stake in copper-gold miner Amman Mineral.
interesting_fact: Holds an ITB geological engineering degree (1981), Thunderbird MBA core program (1984) and an MSc from the Colorado School of Mines (1988); he has over four decades in oil and gas and leads a company that has set net-zero targets.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1981 as a wellsite geologist at Huffco/Vico Indonesia, rising to VP & Director of Business Process Reengineering before his brother invited him to join Medco as a director in 1998.
notes: Regular speaker at energy conferences (SPE, Singapore International Energy Week) and has given interviews on energy transition, so reachable via MedcoEnergi corporate communications/IR.

name: Mary Vy Ty
current_role: Adviser to the Board, GT Capital Holdings and Metrobank; Honorary Chairman, GT Foundation; Trustee, Metrobank Foundation
profile: Mary Vy Ty is the widow of Metrobank founder George S.K. Ty (d. 2018) and the matriarch of the Ty family. The family controls GT Capital, the Philippine conglomerate behind Metrobank, Toyota Motor Philippines, Federal Land and stakes in Metro Pacific and AXA Philippines. She was GT Capital's Treasurer from its 2007 incorporation and became a Board Adviser in 2014.
interesting_fact: GT Capital, which takes its name from George Ty, combines Metrobank with the Philippine Toyota franchise. It is one of the country's largest listed conglomerates, with interests in banking, cars, property, infrastructure and insurance.
deep_cut_fact: She has more than 50 years of experience in banking and general business, is a University of Santo Tomas graduate, and served as GT Capital's first Treasurer from its incorporation in 2007.
notes: Elderly (her GT Capital bio gives her age as 85) and private, with an advisory rather than executive role. For a business conversation, GT Capital/Metrobank management are the active leaders. The corporate inbox is the realistic route.

name: Maximilian Rudolph von Finck
current_role: Heir/investor in the von Finck family fortune; board member of family holding Clair (per Bilanz)
profile: Middle son (b. c.1969) of the late Bavarian banker-investor August von Finck Jr. (d. Nov 2021), whose fortune included a large SGS (testing/inspection) stake, mostly sold in 2020 ahead of an equal four-way inheritance. Naturalised Swiss (canton Schwyz); Bilanz reports he is mainly active as an entrepreneur in the USA, e.g. in the seed business.
interesting_fact: The family sold SGS shares worth about CHF 2.3bn in 2020, reportedly to split a holding too big to divide equally among August von Finck Jr.'s four children.
notes: Extremely private; almost no public profile and no published contact. Identity matched to the von Finck SGS fortune via Bilanz, but his own business activities are not documented. Hurun listing likely reflects inherited share of the family fortune. Not a realistic podcast target.

name: Diane Goldman
current_role: Co-owner, Solil Management (Goldman family real estate, New York); philanthropist
profile: Diane Goldman Kemper (b. 1946) is a daughter of New York real-estate investor Sol Goldman (d. 1987) and one of four siblings who co-own Solil Management. Solil holds roughly 400 mostly Manhattan properties, including the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building and part of the land under the World Trade Center. Her sister Jane runs day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Solil's portfolio includes the land under Olympic Tower and the Cartier Building, The Peninsula New York hotel, and about 17% of the land under the World Trade Center complex.
deep_cut_fact: She studied at C.W. Post College and the New York School of Interior Design, and once worked in the family company's residential leasing department. Columbia University has a 'Diane Goldman Kemper Family Professor of Epidemiology in Psychiatry' chair.
notes: Known publicly as Diane Goldman Kemper. The family is famously private (Forbes: 'doesn't want you to know who they are'), and there is ongoing family litigation over Solil, so avoid that topic. She has no published personal or office contact. The only published family entity address is the Lillian Goldman Charitable Trust (postal). Low relevance to an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Jami Gertz
current_role: Co-owner, Atlanta Hawks (with husband Tony Ressler); actress; philanthropist (Ressler-Gertz Foundation)
profile: Jami Gertz is the actress known for The Lost Boys, Less than Zero, Twister and the CBS sitcom Still Standing. Her listed fortune is shared with her husband Tony Ressler, co-founder of Ares Management. Their group bought majority control of the NBA's Atlanta Hawks in 2015 for about $730M, and the couple give through the Ressler-Gertz Foundation to education, Los Angeles and Jewish causes.
interesting_fact: She was discovered by Norman Lear in a nationwide talent search and reportedly turned down the role of Rachel Green on Friends during pre-production.
deep_cut_fact: Between acting jobs she worked in Paris as a scent designer for the fashion house Lanvin. She grew up in Glenview, Illinois, and graduated from Maine East High School.
notes: Private; rarely appears in public. Wealth is through Tony Ressler (Ares Management), who is the better entrepreneurship or podcast angle. No personal or foundation contact was published; the Atlanta Hawks communications office is the institutional route. Gertz is also a Melanoma Research Alliance board member.

name: Ratan Jindal
current_role: Chairman (and managing director), Jindal Stainless Ltd
profile: Son of O.P. Jindal, founder of the O.P. Jindal Group; brother of Sajjan (JSW), Prithviraj and Naveen Jindal. Ratan heads Jindal Stainless, India's largest stainless-steel producer and a major exporter, and in 2006 set up the group's Dubai (Jindal Stainless FZE) and London arms, which fits Hurun listing him under the UAE.
interesting_fact: He pitches Jindal Stainless as a front-runner in circular, scrap-based stainless production, writing that 'the world is quickly transitioning towards circularity in production processes' and committing to power growth with renewables.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006 he was put in charge of the group's global foray, heading newly formed subsidiaries in Dubai (Jindal Stainless FZE) and London as their CEO.

public_contacts.value: sonal.singh@jindalstainless.com (Jindal Stainless media contact; others listed on same page)

notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because Hurun tags his wealth as 'JSW Steel' (brother Sajjan's company) - he is the O.P. Jindal son who chairs Jindal Stainless; the family holdings are intertwined. Green/circular steel and renewable power are good podcast hooks.

name: Lachman Das Mittal
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus/Chairman, Sonalika Group (International Tractors Ltd), Hoshiarpur, Punjab
profile: Lachhman (Lakshman) Das Mittal, born 1931 in Hoshiarpur, spent decades at LIC (agent from 1955, retired as deputy zonal manager) before building Sonalika: threshers from 1970, then Sonalika tractors (International Tractors Ltd) from 1995-96, now one of India's largest tractor makers and a big exporter. Sons Amrit Sagar and Deepak Mittal run the business; he is often called India's oldest billionaire.
interesting_fact: He launched his tractor business around age 60 after retiring from LIC, making him one of the world's most striking late-start founders.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.A. in English and Urdu from Panjab University, and once quipped: 'Once I applied for dealership of Maruti Udyog but was rejected. Today, I give out dealerships.'
notes: Aged ~95; operational leadership is with sons Amrit Sagar Mittal (Vice Chairman) and Deepak Mittal (MD). For a podcast, the sons may be the realistic guests; Sonalika has a media room with interviews.

name: Gérard Déprez
current_role: Chairman (Président) and CEO, Loxam Group
profile: French executive who took over equipment-rental firm SAM in Brittany in 1986 and built it into Loxam, Europe's No.1 and the world's 4th-largest equipment rental company (~1,120 branches in 30 countries, ~€2.6bn revenue in 2024) through acquisitions such as Lavendon, Cramo Denmark and Finland's Ramirent (2019). He remains chairman, with Stéphane Hénon as managing director.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Loxam grew from a 1967 regional Breton rental outfit into a supplier of equipment for the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games.
deep_cut_fact: Before Loxam he was VP of finance at cement maker Ciments d'Origny (Holderbank group) from 1978-83 and a regional director at building-materials firm SOCIMAT; he is an EM Lyon graduate with law and accounting degrees, and chaired the European Rental Association 2005-2013.
notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews beyond trade press (KHL, Rental Management). Loxam press releases also route media via FTI Consulting (loxam@fticonsulting.com per search snippets; not verified on a current release). Possible angle: equipment rental for energy/data-center construction and Loxam's carbon trajectory.

name: David C Paul
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Globus Medical (NYSE: GMED)
profile: Mechanical engineer who left Synthes, where he was Director of Product Development, to found spine and musculoskeletal device maker Globus Medical in 2003. He was CEO until 2017, then executive chairman; he remains the largest stockholder after Globus' 2023 merger with NuVasive, and Keith Pfeil has been CEO since July 2025.
interesting_fact: He is named as an inventor on more than 300 patents and published patent applications.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he was a research engineer in biomaterials at Temple University. He earned a mechanical engineering degree from the University of Madras in India and a master's in computer-integrated mechanical engineering systems from Temple.

public_contacts.value: investors@globusmedical.com (Brian Kearns, SVP Corporate Development & IR)

notes: Engineer-founder; low media profile. Also sits on boards of Free Flow Medical and Cross Ventures LLC (real estate). Company IR is the published route.

name: Siew Khim Ng
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun as a billionaire whose wealth derives from Indoritel (Indonesia)
profile: Hurun Global Rich List (2023-2026) attributes about $3B to Siew Khim Ng via Indoritel Makmur Internasional (IDX: DNET), the listed parent of the Indomaret convenience-store chain and a holder of FiberStar. I found no public source that names her role or shareholding. DNET's disclosed major holders are Hannawell Group Ltd (~39%), Anthoni Salim (~25%) and PT Megah Eraraharja (~20%).
interesting_fact: Indomaret, which Indoritel controls, runs more than 21,900 convenience stores across 32 Indonesian provinces.
notes: Identity unresolved: the only web profiles named 'Siew Khim Ng' are unrelated executives at Malaysia's U Mobile and Singapore's Keong Hong. She may be the beneficial owner behind the offshore holder Hannawell Group, but that is unverified. Very private. If you approach her, go through Indoritel corporate secretary/IR.

name: Dana Azrieli
current_role: CEO, Azrieli Group (since March 2026; chairwoman 2014–2026); Chair, Azrieli Foundation (Israel)
profile: Montreal-born (1967) daughter of developer David Azrieli, educated at Swarthmore (BA) and Vermont Law School (JD). She took over Azrieli Group, Israel's largest listed real estate company (Azrieli Center towers, malls, offices, hotels, rentals), in 2014. She pushed it into data centers, buying Norway's Green Mountain in 2021 for about NIS 2.8bn, and became permanent CEO in 2026.
interesting_fact: Under her, Azrieli bought Green Mountain, whose flagship Stavanger data center is built inside a mountain in a former NATO ammunition store. She called data centers 'a significant new category of income-producing real estate.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2001 she produced 'One Step Ahead,' her father David Azrieli's memoirs of 1939–1950, published by Yad Vashem. In 2004 she founded the Azrieli Empowerment Program for at-risk middle-schoolers, run with Darca Schools.

public_contacts.value: Azrieli Group Investor Relations page (Head of IR: Ran Meir)

notes: Spelled 'Danna' officially. Very relevant guest for the data-center theme (Green Mountain in Norway and the UK, plus a stake in Compass Datacenters). TASE filings list a corporate secretary's email; not included because it is an individual staff address. Route via IR or the Azrieli Foundation.

name: Suman Kant Munjal
current_role: Chairman, Rockman Industries and Hero Electronix; non-executive director, Hero MotoCorp
profile: Son of Hero Group founder Brijmohan Lall Munjal and a member of the family that controls Hero MotoCorp, the world's largest two-wheeler maker by volume. He built Rockman into the world's largest maker of bicycle chains and hubs, then into auto components; he also chairs Hero Electronix (Tessolve Semiconductor) and sits on Hero Future Energies' board.
interesting_fact: Through Hero Electronix he chairs a tech arm whose holdings include chip-design/testing services firm Tessolve Semiconductor, while also sitting on the board of renewable developer Hero Future Energies.

name: Karthik Sarma
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, SRS Investment Management (New York); director, Avis Budget Group
profile: Indian-born hedge fund manager (IIT Madras, Princeton master's) who spent three years at McKinsey and five at Tiger Global before founding SRS Investment Management in 2006; it manages about $10bn. SRS is Avis Budget Group's largest shareholder (~43%), and Sarma has sat on Avis's board since May 2020.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he was one of eight hedge fund managers to personally earn over $1bn (about $2bn), mostly from Avis's roughly 5.5x share-price surge on talk of EV fleets.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he trained as an engineer at IIT Madras, then came to the US for a master's at Princeton, followed by three years as a McKinsey consultant.
notes: Very low public profile; SRS has no usable public website (srsinvest.com returned an error). Only published route found is via Avis Budget Group's media form, which reaches Avis rather than Sarma. Verify current Avis board status in latest proxy.

name: Wang Yun'an
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Guming Holdings (HKEX: 1364), operator of Good Me tea
profile: Born 1986, Wang co-founded Good Me (Guming) with college and high-school friends in 2010, opening a 30 sq m shop in Daxi, Wenling (Zhejiang). He franchised from 2011, focusing on lower-tier cities and building cold-chain supply before stores; Guming now has roughly 10,000 stores and listed in Hong Kong in Feb 2025.
interesting_fact: The first store opened on April 1, 2010 with about RMB 140,000; early daily sales were only RMB 300-500 and the partners debated quitting before it turned around.
deep_cut_fact: A materials-science graduate of Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, he made his first money in college selling quilts and radios, and he personally drew the site-selection and fit-out plans for Guming's first ~150 stores.
notes: Young (b. 1986), first-generation founder - good entrepreneurship story. The press email is listed as Guming's media contact (媒体联系) on its homepage. Briefly worked at a car 4S dealership in Hangzhou before starting Guming.

name: Don Levin
current_role: Owner of D.R.L. Enterprises / Republic Brands (rolling papers: OCB, JOB, E-Z Wider) and owner of the AHL's Chicago Wolves
profile: Chicago entrepreneur, son of a used-car salesman. He bought a head shop called Adams Apple, saw demand for rolling papers, and started a distribution business that became Republic Brands. In 2000 he bought OCB and JOB from Vincent Bolloré. His group now owns a paper mill and a rolling-paper factory, with about $600m in estimated annual revenue.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the Chicago Wolves hockey club on 24 January 1994 with Buddy Meyers and Grant Mulvey. The team has won two IHL Turner Cups (1998, 2000) and three AHL Calder Cups (2002, 2008, 2022).
deep_cut_fact: He had planned to follow his father into selling cars, until a friend talked him into buying a Chicago head shop named Adams Apple. Most customers came in for rolling papers, which led to his distribution business.
notes: Very low media profile apart from the Chicago Wolves. The Wolves' front office is probably the most approachable route; I couldn't read their site, so check chicagowolves.com for media relations. Republic's only published email is salesinfo@ (sales), so I didn't include it.

name: Lottie Tham
current_role: Private investor; major H&M shareholder (no operating role at H&M)
profile: Helga Liselott 'Lottie' Tham (née Persson, b. 1949) is the daughter of H&M founder Erling Persson and the sister of former chairman Stefan Persson, and holds over 5% of H&M. With her husband, financier Pieter Tham, she invests in real estate including hotels, commercial buildings and land. She deliberately keeps out of the public eye.
interesting_fact: Her father got the idea for H&M (founded 1947 as Hennes in Västerås) on a road trip through the US after seeing New York's department stores.
notes: Very private, with no public role, website, social media or published office contact. Little energy/tech relevance. Low-priority outreach target; any approach would need a warm introduction.

name: Hal Jackman
current_role: Patriarch / largest family shareholder of E-L Financial Corporation (Toronto); former Lieutenant Governor of Ontario
profile: Henry N.R. 'Hal' Jackman (b. 1932) expanded the insurance and investment empire built by his father Harry Jackman, chairing National Trust and Empire Life; the family controls TSX-listed E-L Financial, now run by his son Duncan. He was Ontario's 25th Lieutenant Governor (1991-97) and U of T chancellor (1997-2003). In 2025 he gave $80M to U of T law, renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
interesting_fact: His September 2025 $80 million gift was the largest ever to a Canadian law school, bringing his giving to U of T's law faculty to $100 million; the school was renamed the Henry N.R. Jackman Faculty of Law.
deep_cut_fact: While Lieutenant Governor in 1991, Jackman donated his historic collection of toy soldiers (over 650 figures) to the Royal Ontario Museum; he also served as honorary colonel of the Governor General's Horse Guards, a Toronto militia unit.
notes: Aged 94; no personal public channels. E-L Financial press releases name CFO Scott F. Ewert as the contact (published business line (416) 947-2578). Honorary-colonel detail from U of T/Victoria College sources: https://vic.utoronto.ca/henry-n-r-jackman-honoured-with-international-business-lnew-news-page

name: Glenn Dubin
current_role: Founder, Dubin & Co. (family office); co-founder, Engineers Gate; lead shareholder, Castleton Commodities International
profile: Dubin co-founded Highbridge Capital in 1992 and sold a majority stake to JPMorgan in 2004 for $1.3bn. He co-founded quant fund Engineers Gate and in 2012 led an investor group that bought energy trader Castleton Commodities. His family office, Dubin & Co., backs growth companies such as Brex and Scale AI.
interesting_fact: He is a founding board member of the Robin Hood Foundation. With his wife Eva, he funded the Dubin Breast Center at Mount Sinai, which opened in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Dubin and Highbridge co-founder Henry Swieca grew up a few blocks apart in Washington Heights. Highbridge, launched with $35m in 1992, is named after the 19th-century High Bridge aqueduct linking Washington Heights to the Bronx.
notes: His energy angle is Castleton Commodities (oil, gas and power trading and assets). Dubin & Co.'s site has no published email; it links his LinkedIn. He has appeared in Epstein-related press coverage, so expect him to be press-wary.

name: Rajiv Jain
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Chief Investment Officer, GQG Partners (Fort Lauderdale; ASX: GQG)
profile: India-born investor who came to the US in the early 1990s for an MBA at the University of Miami, joined Vontobel Asset Management in 1994 and became its co-CEO in 2014. In 2016 he co-founded GQG Partners with Tim Carver and listed it on the ASX in 2021; it now manages over US$150bn in long-only equities. He writes GQG's CIO Perspectives, which recently covered the AI investment cycle.
interesting_fact: In 2023, GQG invested about $1.9bn in four Adani Group companies, one of the most high-profile contrarian bets in emerging markets.
deep_cut_fact: Jain has backed Florida International University students since 2013, and GQG's community foundation funds FIU's First-Generation Scholarship for students pursuing STEM degrees as the first in their families to attend college.
notes: No published press email. GQG's published AI and semiconductor commentary (e.g. 'The Chips Are on the Table', Oct 2026; 'Always Evolving: Adapting as the AI cycle unfolds', Oct 2026) makes him a natural guest for the data-center and energy angle.

name: Jonathan Tisch
current_role: Executive Chairman, Loews Hotels; co-owner, board member and treasurer of the New York Giants; chairman of The Shed (NYC)
profile: Jonathan Tisch is the son of Bob Tisch, who co-founded Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence in 1946. Jonathan has led Loews Hotels since 1989 and was co-chairman of Loews Corp. until stepping back from its board at the end of 2024; he is now Executive Chairman of Loews Hotels. The family also owns 50% of the New York Giants, and he is a prominent civic philanthropist and chairman emeritus of the U.S. Travel Association.
interesting_fact: He hosts the interview programme 'Beyond the Boardroom with Jonathan Tisch' and has co-written three books, including 'Chocolates on the Pillow Aren't Enough: Reinventing the Customer Experience' (2007).
deep_cut_fact: In 1990, a year after becoming chairman of Loews Hotels, he launched the Loews Hotels 'Good Neighbor Policy' committing hotels to local community engagement. His $40M gift created the Tisch College of Civic Life at Tufts, his alma mater (class of 1976).
notes: Very media-friendly: a host and author himself, so a strong podcast candidate. Loews also owns natural-gas pipelines (Boardwalk), an energy angle. SEC data still lists him as a Loews director, but Wikipedia says he left the Loews Corp board on 31 Dec 2024; check before outreach.

name: Hayes Barnard
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, GoodLeap; Founder and Chairman, GivePower Foundation
profile: St. Louis-area native and former Oracle sales executive. He founded Paramount Equity Mortgage in 2003 and Paramount Solar in 2008, sold the solar unit to SolarCity, and was SolarCity's chief revenue officer. Back at his own firm, he turned it into Loanpal/GoodLeap, a point-of-sale platform that has financed over $26bn of solar and other green home upgrades and was valued at $12bn in 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he founded the nonprofit GivePower, which builds solar-powered clean water and energy systems, including solar desalination, for underserved communities worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He won a football scholarship to Central Missouri State but was injured as a freshman and transferred to Mizzou. On arriving in San Francisco in 1995 for the tech boom, his first jobs were staffing booths at trade shows.
notes: He is a strong fit for an energy podcast: residential solar finance, an ex-SolarCity executive, and GivePower solar water projects. He is publicly visible and does interviews; GoodLeap press is the best route.

name: Jian Yao
current_role: Shareholder, Shenzhen Mindray Bio-Medical Electronics (no known operating role)
profile: Per Forbes, Jian Yao is the ex-wife of Xu Hang, co-founder of Shenzhen medical-device maker Mindray (founded 1991), and obtained a minority stake in Mindray in 2020 after their divorce; that stake is the source of her fortune. No public role or activities found.
interesting_fact: Mindray, set up in Shenzhen in 1991, is one of China's largest medical-device makers; co-founder Xu Hang worked at Shenzhen Anke High-Tech (1987-1991), where he met fellow co-founders Li Xiting and Cheng Minghe.
notes: Wealth comes from a divorce settlement; she is a private individual with no public profile, so independent verification beyond Forbes was not possible. Not a good outreach target; avoid any reference to the divorce.

name: Safra Catz
current_role: Executive Vice Chair of the Board, Oracle Corporation (CEO 2014-Sept 2025); director, Paramount Skydance
profile: Israeli-born American executive who joined Oracle from investment bank DLJ in 1999 and rose to president, CFO and CEO (co-CEO with Mark Hurd from 2014, sole CEO from 2019). Her wealth is largely Oracle stock. In Sept 2025, amid Oracle's AI data-center build-out, she handed over to co-CEOs Clay Magouyrk and Mike Sicilia and became executive vice chair.
interesting_fact: She is credited with driving Oracle's $10.3bn hostile takeover of PeopleSoft in 2005, and in 2011 was the highest-paid woman among Fortune 1000 companies.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Holon, Israel, she moved to Brookline, Massachusetts at age six and graduated from Brookline High School; alongside running Oracle she has been a lecturer in accounting at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
notes: SEC insider data still lists her as CEO; she became Executive Vice Chair on 22 Sept 2025. Very press-shy; best route is Oracle corporate communications.

name: Sathien Sathientham
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman/Vice Chairman, Carabao Group PCL (Thailand) (title varies by source)
profile: Sathien Sathientham (formerly Sathien Setthasit) co-founded Carabao in 2002 with folk-rock star Aed Carabao (Yuenyong Opakul); Carabao Dang outsells Red Bull in Thailand and the group listed in 2014. He has since pushed into large-scale beer brewing, packaging and cans; his sons run Carabao and CJ Express.
interesting_fact: Carabao is title sponsor of the English Football League Cup (the 'Carabao Cup'), and its energy drink outsells Red Bull in Red Bull's birthplace, Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy drinks he started out in real estate, and in 1999 he had early success pairing house-brewed beer with Thai food at Tawandang German Brewery in Bangkok, where he has been a director since 1999.
notes: One sponsored Khaosod piece credits Supote Teerawatanachai as Tawandang's founder, so say 'Tawandang' carefully (he is at least a long-time director). Searches may need both surnames (Setthasit/Sathientham).

name: Stephen Deckoff
current_role: Founder and Managing Principal, Black Diamond Capital Management (also director and 10%+ holder of KVH Industries)
profile: Distressed-credit and private-equity investor who worked at Drexel Burnham Lambert, Chemical Securities, Bear Stearns and Kidder, Peabody (SVP) before founding Black Diamond in 1995. The firm now manages more than $11B across CLOs, distressed funds and control private equity, with holdings including Werner ladders and Polynt. He has lived in the US Virgin Islands since 2011, where the firm has an office.
interesting_fact: He is an avid skier and named Black Diamond Capital after the ski-slope rating for the hardest runs.
deep_cut_fact: He studied operations research, earning a B.S. from Cornell's engineering school, and has sat on the boards of an unusually varied set of portfolio companies, including Werner Ladder, SmarteCarte, Sun World, Bayou Steel and ION Media.
notes: No published email or press contact; the firm site lists only office addresses (Stamford CT, St. Thomas USVI, Mumbai). In 2023 he bought Little and Great St. James islands (formerly Epstein's) for a resort, which is widely covered but sensitive, so avoid it as an opener. Reported >$1.2M in USVI nonprofit donations (St. John Source). Industrial portfolio (steel, paper, chemicals) may suit the energy angle.

name: Lucy Peng
current_role: Alibaba cofounder and former Ant Group chief executive/chair; no current public executive role confirmed (left Ant's board in Aug 2020)
profile: Peng Lei (彭蕾), one of Alibaba's 18 founders, joined Jack Ma in 1999 after five years as a university lecturer. She built Alibaba's HR function and was its chief people officer for over a decade. She ran Alipay (2010-13), led Ant Financial and sat on Paytm's board. She was an Ant director until August 2020 and has kept a low profile since Ant's IPO was halted.
interesting_fact: She led Alipay from January 2010 to February 2013, when it became China's dominant payment gateway. In 2016 Ant Financial raised $4.5B, then the largest private fundraising ever for an internet company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alibaba she taught for five years at Zhejiang University of Finance and Economics. At Alibaba she created the 'mom and pop' management model, in which one manager ('mom') focused on teamwork and motivation and another ('pop') handled performance reviews.
notes: Very private since 2020; she has no personal website or social accounts. No published contact route was found, and Alibaba/Ant corporate channels are unlikely to forward requests. She spoke publicly at Stanford GSB's China 2.0 conference (2012). The web search budget ran out, so her current activities (e.g. any investing vehicle) were not verified.

name: The Lazari family
current_role: Owners of Lazari (Lazari Investments, Lazari Financial Holdings, Lazari Developments), Mayfair, London
profile: Family of the late Greek-Cypriot developer Chris (Christos) Lazari (d. 2015), who founded Lazari Investments in 1976. Widow Maritsa (co-founder) and children run a private group with 2.9m sq ft of prime London property and combined assets of over £4.1bn across eight London estates, including the West End and Euston Road.
interesting_fact: The group is now three businesses: the legacy property company, a property-finance lender and a development arm, with combined assets above £4.1bn.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Chris Lazari left Cyprus at 16 with just £20 aboard the MV Messapia, washed dishes and waited tables to study fashion design, and built the 'Drendie Girl' high-street clothing label before moving into property in 1978.
notes: Family entry: founder Chris Lazari died 2015; widow Maritsa (b. 1943) is alive per Wikipedia, and children are directors. Low-profile family; best route is FTI Consulting.

name: Katarina Martinson
current_role: Chair, Indutrade AB; board member, L E Lundbergföretagen AB and other Lundberg group companies
profile: Swedish businesswoman (b. 1981) who, with her sister Louise Lindh, owns about 15% stakes in the family investment company L E Lundbergföretagen. Founded by her grandfather in 1944 and led by her father Fredrik Lundberg, it holds stakes in Holmen, Handelsbanken, Sandvik, Skanska, Indutrade and others. She chairs industrial group Indutrade and invests privately in brands such as NN07 and Lyko.
interesting_fact: When she became chair of Indutrade, she was the youngest chair of any company listed on the Stockholm Stock Exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Norrköping, she grew up in Norrköping, Switzerland and Djursholm and is a Stockholm School of Economics graduate. In 2021 she was elected a member of IVA, the Royal Swedish Academy of Engineering Sciences.
notes: Fairly private. Lundbergs (whose holdings include Holmen, which owns forest and hydro/wind assets) and Indutrade are the routes. Her IVA membership suggests an interest in engineering and tech topics.

name: Qian Dongqi
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ecovacs Robotics (科沃斯, 603486.SH), Suzhou
profile: Qian Dongqi (b. 1958), a Nanjing University physics graduate with a master's in philosophy, worked in state-owned foreign trade before renting a village factory in Suzhou in 1998 to start Taiyikai Electric, an OEM vacuum maker. It became Ecovacs, one of China's largest robot-vacuum brands, and listed in Shanghai in 2018. The group also owns Tineco, the floor-cleaner brand run by his son David Qian.
interesting_fact: Before launching its own brands, the company made vacuums for other labels; by around 2006 this OEM business already brought in about RMB 1B a year.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for a robot vacuum reportedly came from a 1999/2000 news story about a robot soccer match, which made Qian wonder whether a robot could sweep floors. The company kept the name Taiyikai (泰怡凯) until 2011.
notes: The email is the general contact in the Ecovacs Group website's site config, not a named press office. For IR, use the SSE disclosures for 603486. The sources disagree on the year of the robot-soccer anecdote (1999 vs 2000). David Qian, chairman of Tineco, is the more media-facing family member.

name: Firoz Mistry
current_role: Non-executive director, Afcons Infrastructure (Shapoorji Pallonji Group) since Sept 2025
profile: Elder son of the late Cyrus Mistry, ex-chairman of Tata Sons, who died in a 2022 car crash; he inherited part of the family's ~18.4% Tata Sons stake. A Yale liberal-arts graduate (29 in 2025), he had worked on strategy, HR and governance projects at the Shapoorji Pallonji Group before joining the board of its listed engineering arm Afcons in his first operating-company directorship.
interesting_fact: His Afcons board seat (Sept 2025) marked the formal entry of the next Mistry generation into SP Group operating companies, joining cousin Pallon Mistry; Afcons builds tunnels, metros, bridges, ports and energy infrastructure in India and abroad.
deep_cut_fact: He studied liberal arts at Yale University rather than engineering or finance before joining the family's construction group.
notes: Very private, no known public social accounts; listed by Forbes as Ireland-resident (family holds Irish citizenship). Avoid the father's death and Tata boardroom disputes in outreach. Route via Afcons corporate communications.

name: Zahan Mistry
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Firoz) of the Cyrus Mistry branch's stake in Shapoorji Pallonji Group and Tata Sons; no confirmed executive title
profile: Zahan Mistry is the younger son of the late Cyrus Mistry (ex-Tata Sons chairman, d. 2022). He and brother Firoz inherited their father's share of the Mistry family's ~18.4% Tata Sons stake and of the Shapoorji Pallonji Group, which they reportedly co-own roughly 50/50 with uncle Shapoor Mistry's branch. The family holds Irish citizenship, hence Forbes lists him under Ireland.
interesting_fact: To reduce debt, the family's Shapoorji Pallonji Group listed its construction and engineering arm Afcons Infrastructure in a $646 million IPO in 2024.
notes: Very private; virtually no interviews. Reported to have formally joined SP Group with Firoz (neherald report, undated). Sources mention Yale alumnus (unverified). Avoid references to father's death or Tata boardroom dispute. Route via SP Group head office (Mumbai).

name: Marianna Latsis
current_role: Owner/head of Latsco (Latsco Shipping and Latsco Family Office), Greece
profile: Daughter of late Greek shipping tycoon John S. Latsis (b. 1953). After the 2019 family split she took shipping arm Latsco (~33 vessels incl. tankers, gas and LNG carriers) and in 2025 took control of Nasdaq-listed EuroHoldings. Her family office holds stakes in GEK Terna, Attiki Odos, Helleniq Energy and venture bets.
interesting_fact: Latsco's fleet is heavily energy-focused - product tankers, VLCCs, gas and LNG carriers - with dual-fuel Very Large Gas Carriers on order for 2026 delivery.
deep_cut_fact: She funded the 'Nikos Kourkoulos' oncology day-care units in Athens, Thessaloniki and Patras (named for her late husband, the actor), and in 2023 received the Evangelis Zappas Gold Medal from the Olympion and Bequests Committee for her philanthropy.
notes: Very private; essentially no interviews. Son Paris Kassidokostas-Latsis is the more public face of Latsco/EuroHoldings and may be a better route. Energy angle: LNG/LPG shipping, Helleniq Energy, GEK Terna infrastructure.

name: David Booth
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Dimensional Fund Advisors
profile: Lawrence, Kansas native who studied under Eugene Fama at Chicago, worked on one of the first index funds at Wells Fargo, then co-founded Dimensional with Rex Sinquefield in 1981 to turn academic research into low-cost systematic investing. Dimensional manages hundreds of billions; Booth is a Giving Pledge signer.
interesting_fact: He paid $4.3 million for James Naismith's original 1891 rules of basketball, now displayed at the University of Kansas; his 2008 $300M gift to the University of Chicago is the largest in its history (hence Chicago Booth).
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a house just down the street from KU's Allen Fieldhouse. After serving as Fama's teaching assistant he skipped academia, reasoning of Fama: 'He was smarter than I was and willing to work harder.'

public_contacts.value: Has appeared on podcasts e.g. Rational Reminder ep. 131 (guest, not his own show)

notes: Relatively accessible: has done long-form podcast interviews about the first index fund. Dimensional media relations is the published route.

name: J. Hyatt Brown
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Brown & Brown, Inc. (NYSE: BRO)
profile: Born in 1937 and raised in Daytona Beach, he became CEO in 1961 of the insurance agency his father co-founded in 1939 and grew it into Brown & Brown, one of the largest US insurance brokerages (2025 revenue above $5.9B). His son J. Powell Brown has been CEO since 2009; Hyatt remains chairman and owns about 12% of the company.
interesting_fact: He served in the Florida House from 1972 to 1980, including as Speaker (1978-80). The Cici and Hyatt Brown Museum in Daytona Beach, which he and his wife funded with $13M, holds the world's largest collection of Florida art.
deep_cut_fact: In 2018 he and his wife Cici gave Stetson University $18M, the largest gift in the school's history (he is a past chairman of Stetson's trustees). That same year they pledged $15M to rebuild Daytona Beach's Riverfront Park.

public_contacts.value: Brown & Brown PR: Jenny Goco, VP Public Relations & Communications (phone published in press releases; no email listed)

notes: He is 89. The best route is Brown & Brown corporate communications (Jenny Goco) or the Brown Museum / Museum of Arts and Sciences in Daytona Beach. He is also a director of Daytona International Speedway LLC.

name: Chen Kaixuan
current_role: Chairman, Liby Group (Guangzhou Liby Enterprise Group)
profile: Born in 1958 in Puning, Guangdong, Chen ran a small detergent business in his hometown before co-founding Liby with his brother Chen Kaichen in Guangzhou in 1994. Starting as an OEM brand with heavy TV and rural wall advertising, Liby grew into one of China's largest household-chemical makers (laundry powder, liquid detergent, soap, dish liquid), competing directly with P&G and Unilever.
interesting_fact: Liby began with outsourced (OEM) production and a 'countryside surrounds the cities' sales strategy; within about two years (by autumn 1996) sales passed RMB 200 million.
deep_cut_fact: Liby started with Chen, his brother and five staff in three rented offices on Lujing Road in Guangzhou, which doubled as bedrooms at night. In Chen's words they were 'bosses by day, sleeping on the floor by night' (白天做老板，晚上睡地板). His founding goal: 'make the best laundry powder in China.'
notes: Privately held, mainly Chinese-language media presence; no published press email found. Outreach would need to go through Liby corporate communications in Guangzhou, in Chinese.

name: Richard LeFrak
current_role: Chairman and CEO, LeFrak Organization (New York)
profile: Fourth-generation head of the LeFrak Organization, the family developer behind LeFrak City in Queens and the Newport waterfront in Jersey City. CEO since his father Sam's death in 2003, he has pushed into luxury and new markets such as the 184-acre SoLe Mia project in North Miami, alongside a broad investment portfolio, with sons Jamie and Harrison in the business.
interesting_fact: His holdings include LeFrak City, a 20-building, 5,000-unit complex in Queens, plus hundreds of acres from Manhattan to Newport, N.J., and he has invested in startups such as Affinity and storage firm MakeSpace.
deep_cut_fact: He started working for his father at 13 as a messenger boy 'doing the most menial things', spent summers working in the field, and joined full time in his first year at Columbia Law after graduating from Amherst (1967).
notes: Gives occasional trade-press interviews (The Real Deal, Bisnow). Longtime friend of Donald Trump. Route via LeFrak corporate (general info address).

name: Liang Xinjun
current_role: Principal of XIN Family, his Singapore single-family office (founded 2019); former vice chairman and CEO of Fosun International
profile: Liang Xinjun (b. 1968, Taizhou, Zhejiang) co-founded Fosun with Guo Guangchang in 1992. As vice chairman and CEO he helped build it into a conglomerate spanning steel, mining, tourism and pharmaceuticals. He resigned in 2017, cashed out his stakes and now invests from Singapore through XIN Family, including early-stage tech deals.
interesting_fact: He and Guo Guangchang were both young Fudan University staff when they started the business in 1992 that grew into Fosun, one of China's largest privately run conglomerates.
deep_cut_fact: He was Taizhou's top science scorer (理科状元) in the 1987 gaokao. He entered Fudan's highly selective genetic engineering department and won the top scholarship every year.
notes: Low profile since 2017; he cited health reasons for leaving Fosun, so avoid that topic. He has spoken at Milken Asia Summit, which could be a warm route. No published XIN Family email found.

name: Sylvan Adams
current_role: President, World Jewish Congress Israel (since 2025); owner of Iberville Developments; philanthropist
profile: Quebec City-born (1958) real-estate heir who ran and later became sole owner of Canada's Iberville Developments, founded by his father Marcel. Emigrated to Tel Aviv in 2015 and became one of Israel's best-known philanthropists (Giving Pledge), funding sport, medicine and education, including a $100m gift in 2025 to rebuild a missile-struck hospital. Stepped back from his cycling team in late 2025.
interesting_fact: He personally funded bringing the 2018 Giro d'Italia start to Israel, the first time any Grand Tour stage was held outside Europe, and built the Middle East's first indoor velodrome in Tel Aviv.
deep_cut_fact: He only took up cycling in his 40s, yet won a Masters world title in Manchester in 2017 and has been a multiple-time Masters world time-trial champion in his age category; he also donated $2m to redevelop the Bromont Velodrome in Quebec.
notes: High public profile in Israel; frequently interviewed by Jewish/Israeli and cycling media. No self-published email/socials verified; best route is via World Jewish Congress Israel or the Margaret and Sylvan Adams Family Foundation. Israel–Premier Tech controversy (renamed for 2026) is sensitive; avoid leading with it.

name: Glen Taylor
current_role: Chairman, Taylor Corp. (North Mankato, MN); owner of the Minneapolis Star Tribune
profile: Glen Taylor bought a wedding-invitation printer for $2m in 1975 (where he had worked through college) and built it into Taylor Corp., a printing and marketing firm with over $2bn in sales. He owned the Minnesota Timberwolves and Lynx from 1994 until the $1.5bn sale to Marc Lore and Alex Rodriguez closed in 2025. He still owns the Star Tribune and Midwest farmland, and is now giving farmland away to rural causes.
interesting_fact: Before he was a sports owner he was a politician: a Republican Minnesota state senator from 1981 to 1990, serving as Senate Minority Leader in the mid-1980s.
deep_cut_fact: Raised on a 150-acre farm near Comfrey, MN (corn, soybeans, flax, dairy cows), he set up the Taylor Family Farms Foundation in 2023 with ~$172m of farmland and added another $100m+ in Jan 2026. Farmers keep working the land and the rent funds rural grants in southern MN and northwest Iowa.
notes: Farm-upbringing source: https://www.startribune.com/from-farm-boy-to-billionaire-glen-taylor-steers-his-own-course/265057261. Timberwolves sale: https://www.fox9.com/news/timberwolves-sale-approved-nba-governors-june-2025. Taylor Family Farms Foundation may be a softer route for outreach.

name: Wang Jian
current_role: Co-founder and chairman, BGI Group (parent of Shenzhen-listed BGI Genomics, 300676.SZ)
profile: Wang Jian (汪建, b. 1954) trained in medicine in China, did postdoctoral research at the Universities of Texas and Iowa and was a research fellow at the University of Washington (1990-94). He co-founded BGI in 1999 to take on China's share of the Human Genome Project and built it into one of the world's largest genomics groups (sequencing, BGI Genomics, MGI Tech). He also co-founded iCarbonX.
interesting_fact: BGI was founded in 1999 to deliver China's 1% contribution to the international Human Genome Project, and grew into one of the world's largest genome-sequencing organisations.

notes: Outspoken, media-friendly in Chinese press; known for extreme-sport stunts (Everest, etc.) used to promote health data science. ir@bgi.com is BGI Genomics' listed IR address, not personal.

name: Zhou Zerong (Chau Chak Wing, 周泽荣)
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Kingold Group (Guangzhou)

No published direct contact found; Kingold site unreachable. Possible routes: Imperial Springs International Forum organisers or his university philanthropy offices.
