current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Asymchem Laboratories (凯莱英医药集团), Tianjin; listed in Shenzhen (2016) and Hong Kong (2021)
profile: Dr. Hao Hong (洪浩) holds a PhD in medicinal chemistry from the Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences and founded Asymchem in 1995. He built it into a leading CDMO making active ingredients for innovative drugs for global pharma, with more than 10,000 staff and R&D and manufacturing sites in China, the US and the UK. The company positions itself as a leader in green pharmaceutical technology.
interesting_fact: Asymchem, now a Tianjin-headquartered Chinese pharma-outsourcing leader, was founded in 1995 in North Carolina, USA.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Asymchem he was a postdoctoral researcher in medicinal chemistry at the University of Georgia, and he has published dozens of papers in the Journal of Organic Chemistry (JOC) and JACS.
notes: Input 'Casymchen' = Asymchem (凯莱英). He goes by 'Dr. Hao Hong' in English. The company also publishes securities@asymchem.com.cn for securities affairs. A scientist-entrepreneur, which may suit the entrepreneurship theme.

name: Li Xiangping
current_role: Party Secretary and Chairman of the Board, Shandong Dongming Petrochemical Group (山东东明石化集团)
profile: Li Xiangping heads Shandong Dongming Petrochemical, one of China's largest private 'teapot' refiners, based in Heze, Shandong. He took over a near-bankrupt small refinery and grew it into a group with about RMB 50bn in assets and 8,000+ staff. He has since pushed it from fuels into downstream chemicals. Li has also served as a delegate to the National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Under Li, Dongming built the 20 Mt/yr Rizhao-Dongming crude pipeline, listed its subsidiary Hengchang Chemical in Singapore, and became the first private refiner in China to obtain crude-oil import qualification. In 2022 Shandong named him a 'provincial industry-leading entrepreneur'.
deep_cut_fact: Li set up an in-house 'brain trust' of 12 of China's top chemical experts to advise the group. His motto for fuel quality: '油品如同食品、滴滴都是承诺' (fuel is like food, and every drop is a promise).
notes: No verified official website or published press/IR email was found (the group is privately held). Coverage is mostly Chinese-language local and state media. The best route is probably through Heze or Shandong business media, or the company's general channels if an official site can be confirmed.

name: Liu Xianbing
current_role: Listed by Hurun as the principal behind 'Kema Tech' (manufacturing); title not verified
profile: Chinese manufacturing entrepreneur (刘先兵) listed on the Hurun China (2024-26) and Hurun Global (2025-26) rich lists with about US$2.75bn, attributed to 'Kema Tech'. I could not verify the company's full name, his role or his biography from accessible public sources in this pass.
notes: Not researched in depth: the shared web-search budget ran out before this entry, and Wikipedia has no article on him or on 'Kema Tech'. Needs a follow-up pass with Chinese-language sources (Hurun detail page, exchange filings for the Kema entity) to confirm identity and find an IR contact.

name: Liu Tin-Ren
current_role: MediaTek co-founder and former vice president in charge of R&D (retired); shareholder
profile: Liu Tin-Ren (劉丁仁) was part of the founding team of MediaTek (聯發科技), the Hsinchu chip designer spun out of UMC in 1997, where he led R&D as vice president. Chairman Tsai Ming-kai has called Liu (R&D), Cho Jyh-Jer and Wei Chih-chan (marketing) the company's founding 'iron triangle'. He has since retired; Hurun ranks his MediaTek wealth at RMB 18.5bn (2026).
interesting_fact: In 2005 Taiwanese media ranked him No. 34 among Taiwan's 50 richest (NT$2.87bn), richer on paper than Tatung founder Lin Ting-sheng, as a showcase of salaried 'hundred-billion VPs' who got rich without founding their own firm.
deep_cut_fact: Tsai Ming-kai named Liu, who ran R&D, as one leg of MediaTek's early 'iron triangle' with Cho Jyh-Jer (employee No. 00001) and marketing head Wei Chih-chan, when the company started with just 35 people.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API 2026 (刘丁仁 / Liu Tin-Ren, 联发科技 Media Tek, Hsinchu) matches the early MediaTek VP named in Chinese press. Taiwanese, not mainland. Also NCTU-linked per Tsai's speeches (unverified). Retired and very low profile; MediaTek IR is only an indirect route.

name: He Yi
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO (since Dec 2025, with Richard Teng), Binance; head of YZi Labs (formerly Binance Labs)
profile: Yi He (born He Ying, 1986, rural Sichuan) co-founded crypto exchange Binance with Changpeng Zhao in 2017 after marketing roles at OKCoin and live-streaming firm Yixia. Long Binance's marketing and customer-service chief, she has run its venture arm Binance Labs (now YZi Labs, investing in Web3, AI and biotech) since 2022 and was named co-CEO on 3 Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Her co-CEO appointment was announced on stage at Binance Blockchain Week in Dubai as the exchange neared 300 million users.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto she trained in counselling psychology, taught for two years at a private arts college in Lijiang, and hosted travel TV programmes (Travel Satellite TV, Beijing TV) in 2012-2014; at OKCoin she ran a Times Square billboard campaign.
notes: Based in Dubai (UAE). Highly visible on social media, but I could not verify her personal X handle from an official page, so it is not listed. Avoid Zhao's legal case and personal relationship. Route via Binance press/communications.

name: Chen Guihua
current_role: Co-listed (with Wang Shuifu) as owner of Xizi United Holdings (Hangzhou); no public executive role found
profile: Hurun lists Chen Guihua jointly with Wang Shuifu, who founded Hangzhou Xizi Elevator Factory in 1981 and built it into Zhejiang Xizi United Holdings, spanning elevators (former Xizi Otis JV from 1997), boilers, parking systems and, since 2012, aerospace components. Her exact relationship and role could not be confirmed from public sources.
interesting_fact: Wang Shuifu founded Xizi's elevator factory in 1981 in Jianqiao, Hangzhou, when elevators were still a novelty in China, and formed a joint venture with Otis in 1997.
notes: Very little public information on Chen Guihua herself (likely Wang Shuifu's spouse per Hurun's pairing, unconfirmed). Any approach would go via Xizi United Holdings / Wang Shuifu. No published contact found.

name: Georgi Domuschiev
current_role: Co-owner (50%) of Advance Properties, Sofia; co-owner of Huvepharma and PFC Ludogorets Razgrad
profile: Georgi and his older brother Kiril went from selling locally made clothes and shoes in 1990s Bulgaria to buying privatised state companies. Their holding company, Advance Properties, now controls Huvepharma (a top-10 global animal-health firm with plants in the US and Europe), Navibulgar shipping, BMF Port Burgas, real estate and champion football club Ludogorets. The brothers sold Nova TV in 2021.
interesting_fact: With Kiril he became one of Bulgaria's first billionaires. Huvepharma accounted for about 77% of the brothers' fortune, according to Forbes in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: The brothers grew up in communist-era Sofia, where Georgi went to a French-language school (Kiril studied Spanish). Their father headed Sofia's electricity department and their mother was CFO of an energy company, a family background in power utilities.
notes: Georgi is the lower-profile brother; Kiril does most interviews and is the public face (owner of Ludogorets). Pitching both brothers together through Advance Properties is probably best. Their parents' power-sector careers fit the energy theme.

name: Kiril Domuschiev
current_role: Co-owner (with brother Georgi) of Advance Properties; President of Huvepharma; owner of PFC Ludogorets Razgrad
profile: Sofia-born industrialist (b. 1969). He and his brother started out selling shoes in the 1990s, then bought into privatized state companies. In 1999 he founded Huvepharma, which bought state vet-drug maker Biovet and grew into the world's sixth-largest animal-health company, with plants in several U.S. states. Through Advance Properties they also own Navibulgar (shipping), Port Burgas and real estate.
interesting_fact: After he began backing the small-town club Ludogorets Razgrad in 2010, it won promotion and then nine consecutive Bulgarian championships starting in 2011/12.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2019 the U.S. state of Nebraska made him an honorary citizen because he was the largest Bulgarian investor there; Huvepharma has plants in Nebraska, Missouri, North Carolina, Arkansas and Colorado. He went to Sofia's French-language Lamartine high school.
notes: Publicly visible in Bulgaria (football, employers' confederation CEIBG, which he chaired from 2014). The Advance Properties office inbox is the best route. EIB-funded Biovet plant expansion (EUR 100M, Juncker Plan) is an industrial angle.

name: Joseph Edelman
current_role: Founder, CEO and Portfolio Manager, Perceptive Advisors (New York)
profile: Biotech-focused hedge fund manager who founded Perceptive Advisors in July 1999 with $6m; it grew to about $10bn under management. A former sell-side biotech analyst (Prudential Securities) and Aries Fund manager at Paramount Capital, he also backed the ARYA biotech SPACs and sits on the New York Genome Center board.
interesting_fact: After a rough 2021-22, his flagship Perceptive Life Sciences fund returned about 83% in 2025 on biotech winners like Praxis Precision Medicines and Celcuity.
deep_cut_fact: A UC San Diego psychology graduate (magna cum laude, 1978) and son of a Columbia biochemist, he quit pharmacology grad school, moved to New York, and worked as assistant comptroller for the Actors' Equity Association to pay for his NYU Stern MBA.
notes: Low media profile; firm-level contact only. Fit with podcast is weaker (biotech, not energy/data centers).

name: Sjamsul Nursalim
current_role: Founder/controlling family shareholder, Giti Tire / Gajah Tunggal group (Singapore-based)
profile: Indonesian tycoon (b. 1942, Lampung), the son of a rubber seller, who built a fortune in tires, property, coal and retail. His Singapore-headquartered Giti Tire sells in more than 130 countries. The family also holds stakes in retailer Mitra Adiperkasa (Zara and others in Indonesia) and Singapore-listed Tuan Sing Holdings.
interesting_fact: Giti co-developed the tires on BYD's Yangwang U9 Xtreme hypercar, which set a world speed record for mass-produced cars in September 2025. Brand Finance ranked Giti among the world's 10 most valuable tire brands in 2026.
notes: In his 80s and believed to live in Singapore. No death reports were found, but he has no recent public appearances. He has a long, sensitive legal history in Indonesia (the BLBI bank-bailout case), so avoid it. Forbes now lists him as 'former'. Day-to-day leadership of the businesses has passed to the next generation. Not a realistic podcast guest. The Giti contacts are generic corporate inboxes.

name: Fernando Roig
current_role: President and majority owner, Villarreal CF; owner and president, Pamesa Cerámica; ~9% shareholder in Mercadona
profile: Fernando Roig Alfonso (b. 1947), brother of Mercadona chief Juan Roig, helped his siblings take over their parents' eight-store grocery in 1981 and keeps about 9% of Mercadona. He owns ceramic-tile maker Pamesa (Almazora, Castellón) and bought control of Villarreal CF in 1997–98 while it was in the Segunda División. He built it into a regular in European competition and La Liga.
interesting_fact: Roig bought Villarreal while it was a second-division club; under him it reached La Liga and played in the UEFA Cup and the Champions League. Spanish Wikipedia also says he has wind-energy interests through the company Renomar.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2017 Villarreal renamed its century-old El Madrigal ground 'Estadio de la Cerámica' in tribute to the local ceramics industry, the business behind Roig's Pamesa. Vila-real named him its 'Hijo Adoptivo' (adopted son) in 2006.
notes: No press email was found for Villarreal or Pamesa; the club contact page lists only ticketing, shop and GDPR addresses. His wind-energy holding Renomar (renomar.es) could be an energy angle, but its link to Roig is sourced only from Spanish Wikipedia.

name: Kei Hoi Pang
current_role: Founder and chairman, Logan Group (HKEX: 3380), Shenzhen-based property developer
profile: Kei Hoi Pang (纪海鹏) founded Logan in Shantou, Guangdong in 1996 (as Shantou Longguang Jian'an), moved its HQ to Shenzhen in 2003 with his brother, and listed it in Hong Kong in 2013. Logan grew into a major Greater Bay Area residential developer; since 2022 it has been working through offshore and onshore debt restructurings amid China's property downturn.
interesting_fact: Logan started in 1996 with urban-village redevelopment in Shantou and became known early for a fast-turnover development model, before relocating to Shenzhen and expanding across the Greater Bay Area.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Logan he traded medical equipment and building materials in Shantou; Logan's prospectus says his start-up capital came from personal savings built in earlier construction work.
notes: Very low public profile. Company in prolonged debt restructuring - sensitive; avoid in outreach. Daughter is also an executive director. A third-party site lists ir@logan.com.cn but it was not confirmed on an official page, so omitted.

name: Xue Hua
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Haid Group (SZSE: 002311), Guangzhou
profile: Xue Hua (薛华) founded Haid Group in the late 1990s, growing it into one of China's largest animal and aquaculture feed makers, also active in fry/seed breeding, animal health and farming, with ~20,000 staff and a fast-growing overseas business (Southeast Asia, Africa, Latin America). He studied aquaculture at Huazhong Agricultural University (1992).
interesting_fact: Haid is often cast as the main challenger to Tongwei in China's feed market, and has been expanding overseas into land-based shrimp and aquafeed projects.
deep_cut_fact: After a master's at Sun Yat-sen University researching fish and shrimp feed under fish-nutrition scholar Lin Ding, he worked at a Guangdong Academy of Agricultural Sciences tech company, then quit and raised about RMB 180,000 with classmates and colleagues to start Haid, initially making aquatic premix.
notes: Mostly covered in Chinese media; little English presence. Haid website was unreachable at time of research; IR contact should be in its Shenzhen exchange annual report. Founding year reported variously as 1995 or 1998.

name: Zhang Ning
current_role: Executive Director and Chairwoman, Red Avenue New Materials Group (彤程新材, Shanghai-listed)
profile: Shanghai-based Canadian citizen who founded Red Avenue Chemical in August 1999, initially distributing rubber additives to tire makers. Red Avenue became a leading tire-chemicals supplier and has pivoted into semiconductor materials such as photoresists; in 2026 it filed for a Hong Kong listing (A+H).
interesting_fact: Red Avenue is one of China's domestic photoresist makers - a strategic chip material long dominated by Japanese suppliers - after she steered the tire-additive business into electronic chemicals from 2020 onward.
deep_cut_fact: She studied biochemical engineering at Beijing Technology and Business University (enrolled 1993) and started the company at about 25, right after graduating; later she earned a doctorate in global financial business management from Arizona State University. In 2020 Red Avenue partnered with BASF to make compostable PBAT polyester.
notes: Rarely interviewed in English media. IR email published in 2025 earnings-call notices for investor questions; HKEX listing prospectus (2026) may list a PR contact. Semiconductor-materials angle relevant to data centers/chips.

name: Xu Jinfu
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangzhou Tinci Materials Technology (SZSE: 002709)
profile: Chemist (Hangzhou University/Zhejiang U. BSc; CAS Guangzhou master's in plant chemistry) who founded Tinci in 2000, first in personal-care chemicals, then from 2005 lithium-ion battery electrolytes, where it became a global leader. Tinci has ~20 sites across China, Europe and the US and is planning plants in Texas and Morocco.
interesting_fact: Tinci pivoted into lithium-battery electrolyte in 2005, long before the EV boom, and is now one of the world's largest suppliers of electrolyte to battery makers - a direct link to energy-storage and EV supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988, aged 24, he quit his 'iron rice bowl' research-institute job and with classmate Luo Qiuping co-founded Daoming Chemical, the company later known for the Blue Moon (蓝月亮) detergent brand; he entered Hangzhou University's chemistry department as a teenager.
notes: IDENTITY CAVEAT: input SEC insider link (Jinxin Technology, NAMI, CEO) is a different person - NAMI's CEO is ed-tech founder 'Jin Xu'. Tinci IR email not verified (search budget exhausted); use IR channel in Tinci's SZSE filings. Strong battery/energy-storage angle.

name: Ugo Gussalli Beretta
current_role: Board member, Beretta Holding (retired from executive roles in 2015; former chairman of Fabbrica d'Armi Pietro Beretta and president of Beretta USA)
profile: 14th-generation head of Beretta, the world's oldest firearms maker (founded 1526 in Gardone Val Trompia, Italy). He rose from general manager to CEO to chairman, then handed day-to-day control to his sons Pietro (Beretta Holding) and Franco (Fabbrica d'Armi Pietro Beretta). In 2026 he joined the family's 500th-anniversary celebrations.
interesting_fact: Beretta's first recorded deal was the sale of 185 arquebus barrels to the Republic of Venice in 1526. The company marked its 500th anniversary in 2026 with events attended by Italian PM Giorgia Meloni and a commemorative stamp.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership Beretta decided in 1977 to manufacture in the US, buying the former Firearms International factory in Accokeek, Maryland; the first US-made product was the M950 pistol. He was featured in American Rifleman's March 1980 article on the company.
notes: He is about 89, retired and private. Approach through Beretta Holding corporate communications or his sons; Pietro Gussalli Beretta is the public face. The contacts page is JavaScript-rendered and no email could be extracted.

name: Aneel Bhusri
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Workday, Inc. (returned as CEO in February 2026; executive chair 2024–2026)
profile: Born in 1966 in Pittsford, NY, Bhusri studied electrical engineering at Brown and earned an MBA at Stanford. He rose to vice chairman of PeopleSoft and became a Greylock partner. After Oracle's hostile takeover of PeopleSoft, he co-founded cloud HR and finance software firm Workday with Dave Duffield in 2005. He handed the CEO role to Carl Eschenbach in 2024, then retook it in February 2026 to lead Workday's AI push.
interesting_fact: He joined the Giving Pledge in 2018 and has been on the Forbes Midas List six times for his venture investing at Greylock, where he backed cloud and data-center infrastructure companies such as Pure Storage and Cloudera.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after Brown was as a corporate-finance analyst at Morgan Stanley. At Workday, he personally interviewed the company's first 500 employees to shape its culture, as he told Reid Hoffman on Masters of Scale.
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: he is CEO again as of Feb 2026, per CNBC. He has podcast experience (Masters of Scale). Route via Workday media relations. The deep-cut sourcing relies on Wikipedia because the Masters of Scale page blocked automated access.

name: Bent Wilhelmsen
current_role: Co-owner of Awilhelmsen AS, Oslo family investment company (major Royal Caribbean shareholder)
profile: Bent Christian Wilhelmsen is a son of Arne Wilhelmsen (d. 2020), who co-founded Royal Caribbean in 1968. He co-owns Awilhelmsen, the family investment group founded in 1939 by shipowner Anders Wilhelmsen, alongside his brother Arne Alexander (chairman) and Paweco Trusts; it spans industrial investments (incl. Royal Caribbean), real estate via Linstow, and financial assets.
interesting_fact: Awilhelmsen funds the Lise Wilhelmsen Art Award Programme, described as Norway's largest art award programme, supporting mid-career artists, plus the impact investor Wilstar.
notes: Forbes' 'Awas Holding' is actually Awilhelmsen AS (Aker Brygge, Oslo; CEO Arve Ree). Bent holds no board seat there and has essentially no public profile; brother Arne Alexander is the public face. Route via Awilhelmsen's office (published switchboard on contact page).

name: Peter Preben Wilhelmsen
current_role: Principal/co-owner, Awas Holding (parent of the Oslo family investment group Awilhelmsen), per Forbes
profile: Per Forbes, he is an heir of the Norwegian Wilhelmsen family that co-founded Royal Caribbean in 1968 and remains one of its largest shareholders. He co-owns the family business through Awas Holding, inherited after his father Arne Wilhelmsen died in 2020. The group invests in cruise, real estate (Linstow, active in Norway and the Baltics), offshore and financial assets.
interesting_fact: The family group (founded 1939 by shipowner Anders Wilhelmsen) financed its diversification with earnings from the tanker Wilstar, delivered in 1967. A year later it helped found Royal Caribbean.

public_contacts.value: https://www.awilhelmsen.no/contact (Awilhelmsen AS, Beddingen 8, Aker Brygge, Oslo; office tel +47 22 01 42 00)
post@linstow.no (Linstow, family real-estate company; general address)

notes: Very private; almost no public footprint beyond rich lists. Awilhelmsen's site names Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen as chairman and Arve Ree as CEO, and lists owners as Bent Christian Wilhelmsen, Arne Alexander Wilhelmsen and Paweco Trusts. Peter is not named, so his exact role is unverified. Best route is the Awilhelmsen office.

name: Tor Peterson
current_role: Former head of coal trading/marketing at Glencore (stepped down 2021); private investor and Glencore shareholder, based in Zug, Switzerland
profile: The only American among the Glencore IPO billionaires. After six years trading commodities at Phibro-Salomon in New York, he joined Glencore in 1992 and ran marketing for its coal division, becoming a billionaire via Glencore's 2011 London IPO. Left the role in 2021 in the post-Glasenberg leadership shake-up (succeeded by Ruan van Schalkwyk).
interesting_fact: He attended boarding school in Switzerland and Duke University, and still lives in Zug, Glencore's home canton.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a B.A. in political science and French from Duke in 1986, and served as a non-executive director of Xstrata from 2011 to 2013, before its merger with Glencore.
notes: Very private; virtually no interviews or public footprint since leaving Glencore. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Peter Unger
current_role: Private investor via Unger family office (Unger Capital Management), Weiden, Bavaria
profile: Peter Unger founded Auto-Teile-Unger (A.T.U.) in 1985 and built it into Germany's largest auto parts and repair chain. He sold 72% to Doughty Hanson in 2002 for $900m and the rest to KKR in 2004 for $360m (A.T.U. is now owned by France's Mobivia). He now invests through a Weiden-based family office in listed stocks, startups and German residential and commercial real estate, including thousands of Berlin apartments with Groth Gruppe.
interesting_fact: In Berlin he has bought or co-financed the construction of thousands of apartments with developer Groth Gruppe; his other bets include e-bike and sensor-tech startups.
deep_cut_fact: A.T.U. grew fast: after the 1985 start it opened a branch in Aschaffenburg in 1986 and its 100th branch, in Kulmbach, in 1992, seven years after founding.
notes: Very private. No published contact; family office is Unger Capital Management, Weiden (per altss.com profile, not an official site). Do not confuse with the NYU philosopher Peter Unger. Alive status not confirmed by a recent source, though he is still on Forbes real-time 2026.

name: Kalanithi Maran
current_role: Founder, executive chairman and managing director, Sun TV Network / Sun Group
profile: Son of former Union minister Murasoli Maran, he launched Sun TV in 1993 and built Sun Group into a south-Indian media giant: 37 channels reaching 140m+ households, newspapers, FM radio, DTH, Sun Pictures and a Hindi channel (Sun Neo, 2024). Sun also owns cricket franchises Sunrisers Hyderabad (IPL), Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SA20) and Sunrisers Leeds (The Hundred). He owned SpiceJet 2010-15.
interesting_fact: Sun Group's cricket empire spans three countries: Sunrisers Hyderabad in the IPL, Sunrisers Eastern Cape (SA20 champions) in South Africa and, since 2025, Sunrisers Leeds in England's The Hundred.
deep_cut_fact: After Don Bosco and Loyola College in Chennai, he went to the US for an MBA at the University of Scranton in Pennsylvania, where the abundance of TV channels (vs India's single state broadcaster) is said to have inspired Sun TV.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. tvinfo@sunnetwork.in is Sun TV's general company email from exchange filings (not a dedicated press address). Avoid the family share dispute and old telecom case.

name: Lachhman Das Mittal
current_role: Founder, Sonalika Group (International Tractors Ltd), Hoshiarpur, Punjab; operations run by his sons and grandsons
profile: Born 1931 in Punjab, a former LIC insurance officer who began making threshers in 1970 and scaled the business after retiring around age 60. Sonalika (International Tractors) is now India's third-largest tractor maker and a major exporter; Japan's Yanmar holds 30%. Often called India's oldest billionaire, he has handed operations to sons Amrit Sagar and Deepak Mittal and grandsons.
interesting_fact: Sonalika ('lines of gold' in Hindi) is named after a wheat seed variety that fuelled India's Green Revolution.
deep_cut_fact: In 1970, while still an LIC agent, he began building wheat threshers with the help of local blacksmiths in Hoshiarpur, Punjab - the seed of what became the Sonalika tractor empire.
notes: About 95 years old; no death reported in searches (Nov 2026). Spelled Lakshman Das Mittal on Wikipedia. Realistic podcast guests would be son Deepak Mittal or grandson Raman Mittal (exec directors). Route via Sonalika corporate.

name: Surender Saluja
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Premier Energies Ltd (NSE: PREMIERENE), Hyderabad
profile: Surender Pal Singh Saluja, a mechanical engineer (Karnatak University), founded Hyderabad-based Premier Energies in 1995, starting with solar lanterns and streetlights. It is now one of India's largest integrated solar cell and module makers; its 2024 IPO made him a billionaire. His son Chiranjeev Saluja is managing director.
interesting_fact: Premier makes solar cells, not just modules - rare in India, where most players import Chinese cells - and has benefited from India's domestic-content rules for solar.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, he set up Premier Deep Well Hand Pumps in 1981 to sell pumps for rural drinking water; he has called Premier's early solar days 'a one-man show', selling lanterns before assembling modules by hand.
notes: Name also spelled Surendar / Surender Pal Singh Saluja. Son Chiranjeev (MD) is the public face and does most interviews - likely the better podcast route.

name: Bom Kim
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Coupang, Inc. (NYSE: CPNG)
profile: Korean-American founder of Coupang, South Korea's dominant e-commerce company, known for Amazon-style rapid 'Rocket' delivery. A Harvard graduate and ex-BCG consultant, he founded Coupang in 2010 and listed it on the NYSE in 2021, then the biggest US listing by an Asian company since Alibaba. He runs the Delaware parent.
interesting_fact: He dropped out of Harvard Business School after about six months to start Coupang in 2010, shortly after selling his first company, Vintage Media.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004, a few years after graduating, he was planning a magazine for Harvard alumni and filed for trademark protection on the name '02138', Harvard's ZIP code. His memo said Harvard Magazine 'reads more like a collection of press releases and academic papers.'
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Coupang is under intense scrutiny in Korea after a large customer-data breach in late 2025, so expect a guarded PR team; lead with the logistics/automation angle. Route via press@coupang.com.

name: Elisabeth Mohn
current_role: Bertelsmann family matriarch: member of Bertelsmann Supervisory Board and BVG steering committee; President, Liz Mohn Foundation; heads Bertelsmann Stiftung's Liz Mohn Center
profile: Liz Mohn (b. 1941), widow of postwar Bertelsmann builder Reinhard Mohn, joined Bertelsmann as a young employee and became the family's leading figure, owning ~19% of the media group with her children (the Bertelsmann Stiftung owns the rest). In 2021 she handed the family-speaker role to son Christoph Mohn; she continues her civic work via the Liz Mohn Center and Liz Mohn Foundation.
interesting_fact: She founded the German Stroke Foundation (Stiftung Deutsche Schlaganfall-Hilfe) and has long promoted German-Jewish understanding, in part in response to Bertelsmann's Nazi-era publishing history.
deep_cut_fact: She founded the NEUE STIMMEN international opera singing competition in 1987 after conversations with Herbert von Karajan about the lack of support for young opera talent; its 20th edition was held in 2024.

public_contacts.value: info@bertelsmann.de (Bertelsmann SE general; Corporate Communications led by EVP Karin Schlautmann)

notes: Age 85; publicly active but rarely gives interviews. Best route is Bertelsmann Corporate Communications or the Liz Mohn Center at the Bertelsmann Stiftung. Avoid private-life angles (recent SWR podcast covers her relationship history) and family succession topics.

name: Bernard Lewis
notes: River Island founder Bernard Lewis died 28 February 2026, 18 days after his 100th birthday (https://www.jewishnews.co.uk/a-true-gentleman-who-quietly-led-from-the-front-tributes-paid-to-river-island-founder-bernard-lewis/). River Island is now led by his nephew Ben Lewis.

name: Farhad Moshiri
current_role: Private investor based in Monaco; former majority owner of Everton FC (sold to Dan Friedkin, Dec 2024) and former chairman of USM Holdings
profile: Iran-born, UCL-educated chartered certified accountant who worked at Ernst & Young and Deloitte before partnering with Alisher Usmanov in the early 1990s, gaining stakes in Metalloinvest (which he chaired 2006-13), MegaFon and USM. He sold his Arsenal stake in 2016 to buy into Everton, rose to 94% ownership, cut ties with Usmanov in March 2022 and sold Everton in December 2024.
interesting_fact: He swapped clubs in 2016: sold his Arsenal stake to Usmanov to fund buying Everton, where he backed the new Bramley-Moore Dock stadium project before selling the club to Dan Friedkin.
deep_cut_fact: Before the oligarch world he was a career auditor: Ernst & Young (1979-85), Pannell Kerr Forster (1985-87) and Deloitte & Touche (1987-92), leaving as a senior manager in Deloitte's audit division; he later ran Europe Steel (2000-08).
notes: Very private, Monaco-based; rarely interviewed. No published personal or office contact found. Historic links to Usmanov (sanctioned 2022) - he severed ties March 2022. Avoid Everton-era fan criticism topics.

name: Bernard Francis Saul II

name: Lin Ming-Cheng

name: Zhang Jianzhong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Moore Threads Technology (Shanghai STAR Market)
profile: Zhang (James Zhang), born 1966 in Nanjing, was Nvidia's global VP and China GM for about 14 years before founding GPU designer Moore Threads in Beijing in October 2020. It makes full-function GPUs and AI training clusters. Its Dec 2025 STAR Market IPO rose about 425% on day one, making his roughly 36% stake worth billions.

He was then a senior researcher at the national computer lab of the Automation Research and Design Institute of Metallurgical Industry (1990-92), followed by stints at HP China (from 1992) and Dell China (2001-06).

He sold the brand and its beauty business to Estée Lauder for $2.8bn in 2022 and stepped back fully at the end of 2023. He is now focused on film: after A Single Man and Nocturnal Animals, he is directing an adaptation of Anne Rice's Cry to Heaven, which began shooting in January 2026.
interesting_fact: He trained in interior architecture at Parsons rather than fashion. His Santa Fe ranch, Cerro Pelon, was designed by Japanese architect Tadao Ando.
deep_cut_fact: To land his first fashion job, he phoned designer Cathy Hardwick every day for a month. Asked his favourite European designers, he said 'Armani and Chanel', later admitting it was because she was wearing Armani. He worked as her design assistant for two years.
notes: No personal channels found; the Tom Ford brand accounts are now owned by Estée Lauder, not by him. The most realistic route is via his film company Fade to Black or his film publicists around the Cry to Heaven release. He is a weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Lirio Parisotto
current_role: Founder and chairman, Videolar-Innova (petrochemicals/plastics, Manaus); private equity investor
profile: Born in Nova Bassano, Rio Grande do Sul, and trained as a physician (Universidade de Caxias do Sul), Parisotto founded Videolar, a pioneer in Brazilian videocassette manufacturing, and reinvested its profits in dividend-paying Brazilian stocks (banks, power, mining, steel). Videolar later merged with Innova to make petrochemical products; he stepped back from day-to-day management in 2007.
interesting_fact: He has 11 siblings, holds a medical degree and also spent time in a monastery before turning to business.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Videolar reportedly came after he saw a videocassette in a New York store; and as a young man in 1971 he won a monograph contest run by Brazil's Army Ministry, putting the prize (worth about a VW Beetle) into his first stock-market investment.
notes: Sources differ on Videolar's founding year (1980 vs 1988). Sits on the board of Fundacao Amazonas Sustentavel (per MarketScreener). Low media profile; route via Videolar-Innova.

name: Thomas Kwok
current_role: Senior Director, Sun Hung Kai Real Estate Agency (subsidiary of Sun Hung Kai Properties), since 2020
profile: Thomas Kwok Ping-kwong is the second son of SHKP co-founder Kwok Tak-seng and, with brothers Raymond and Walter, inherited one of Hong Kong's largest developers in 1990. He was SHKP joint chairman until 2014; since 2020 he has been a senior director of the group's real estate agency arm, while his son Adam serves as an SHKP executive director.
interesting_fact: He and brother Raymond, both devout Christians, built the Noah's Ark theme park on Ma Wan island, Hong Kong, reflecting their evangelical faith.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a civil engineer (BSc, Imperial College London; MBA, London Business School), and in the 1990s set up a church in the 75th-floor pyramid atrium atop SHKP's Central Plaza tower.
notes: Sensitive history (2014 bribery conviction, released 2019); avoid in outreach. Approach via SHKP corporate communications. SHKP also runs data-centre business (SUNeVision/iAdvantage), a possible podcast angle.

name: Alexander Frolov
current_role: Investor; former CEO of Evraz (2007-2021) and still a major shareholder (~10%); no current executive role found
profile: A physicist (MIPT PhD) who left Moscow's Kurchatov Institute in 1994 to go into business. With partner Alexander Abramov he built the Evraz steel and coking-coal group, sold 40% of it to Roman Abramovich in 2006 for more than $3B, and was CEO from 2007 to 2021. He left the Evraz board in March 2022 and was sanctioned by the UK in November 2022. He also holds stakes in Norilsk Nickel, Yandex and Ivi.
interesting_fact: He started out as a research fellow at the I.V. Kurchatov Institute of Atomic Energy after earning a doctorate in physics and mathematics, an unusual path into steel and coal.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated with honours from the Department of Molecular and Chemical Physics at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (1987). He was also one of the sponsors of the restoration of the Valaam Spaso-Preobrazhensky Monastery on Lake Ladoga.
notes: Under UK sanctions since November 2022 (Russia-related); check legal and reputational exposure before any outreach. Very private, with no published personal or office contacts found. The Valaam fact comes from Forbes facts (https://www.forbes.com/profile/alexander-frolov/).

name: Yusuf Hamied
current_role: Non-executive Chairman, Cipla Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Cambridge-trained chemist (b. 1936, Vilnius; raised in Bombay). He took over Cipla, the generic drugmaker his father founded in 1935, and became famous for taking on Big Pharma with low-cost generics. He is now Cipla's non-executive chairman and a major benefactor of Cambridge University.
interesting_fact: In 2001 he electrified global health by offering a triple-drug AIDS cocktail for about $1 a day, a fraction of branded prices. The price later fell to around 20 cents a day.
deep_cut_fact: He studied chemistry at Christ's College, Cambridge, under Nobel laureate Alexander (Lord) Todd. Cambridge's oldest chemistry professorship, the 1702 Chair, is now the Yusuf Hamied 1702 Chair, and there is a 'Todd-Hamied' laboratory and seminar room in tribute to both men. He was elected FRS in 2019.
notes: Aged 90 and now only a non-executive chairman, though he still gives occasional interviews on drug access. Cipla's pages blocked automated access, so its published IR/media email could not be captured; check cipla.com/investors manually. Childhood friend of conductor Zubin Mehta.

name: K.C. Liu (Liu Ko-chen)
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Advantech (TWSE: 2395); becomes full-time Chairman on Jan 1, 2027 when Miller Chang takes over as CEO
profile: Co-founded Advantech in 1983 at 29 with two HP Taiwan colleagues and built it into the world's largest industrial PC maker (about 41% share), now pushing edge-AI and IoT platforms. In 2026 he announced succession: from 2027 he will focus on governance, long-term development and new business investments.
interesting_fact: An avid reader of management books, he shares titles such as Built to Last and Blue Ocean Strategy with Advantech staff.
deep_cut_fact: Before Advantech he was an R&D engineer and then a sales engineer in HP Taiwan's Instrument Department; in 2026 he noted he had spent 42 years building the company since co-founding it at 29.
notes: Strong fit: industrial edge-AI/IoT hardware used in energy and data-center infrastructure. Leadership transition on Jan 1, 2027 is a timely hook.

name: Zhao Weiguo
current_role: None. Former chairman of Tsinghua Unigroup; currently imprisoned in China
profile: A Tsinghua University alumnus who led chip conglomerate Tsinghua Unigroup and drove a major acquisition push in China's semiconductor industry in the 2010s. He lost control after Unigroup's 2021-22 restructuring, when his Jiankun group and Tsinghua Holdings exited. In May 2025 a Jilin court sentenced him to death with a two-year reprieve for embezzlement and related crimes.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: he is serving a suspended death sentence handed down at first instance on May 14, 2025 (https://www.caixinglobal.com/2025-05-15/former-tsinghua-unigroup-chairman-zhao-weiguo-receives-suspended-death-sentence-in-first-instance-for-embezzlement-of-particularly-huge-amounts-102319729.html). All his personal assets were ordered confiscated. Forbes lists him as 'former'.

name: Hans Georg Naeder
current_role: Chairman of the Board (Verwaltungsrat) / Chairman of the Management Board, Ottobock SE & Co. KGaA; majority owner via Näder Holding
profile: Hans Georg Näder (b. 1961, Duderstadt) is the third-generation head of Ottobock, the prosthetics and orthotics maker founded by his grandfather Otto Bock in 1919. He took over from his father in 1990 at age 28 and built it into a world leader with over 10,000 staff and 60 country branches. Ottobock listed in Frankfurt in October 2025; his family holding keeps roughly 80% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Ottobock has given on-site technical repair service at every Paralympic Games since Seoul 1988, became the IPC's first Worldwide Partner in 2005, and is signed on through Brisbane 2032.
deep_cut_fact: He has been an honorary professor at PFH Göttingen since 2005 and pushed for its new 'Orthobionik' (orthobionics) degree course. He has also been a guest professor at Capital Medical University in Beijing since 2009.
notes: Press contact is Merle Florstedt, Head of Corporate Communications, as named in Ottobock press releases. Avoid the pending VAT investigation over yacht purchases and the May 2026 short-seller report. He is a keen sailor (yacht Pink Gin won the 2007 Millennium Cup per Forbes), but no independent source was confirmed for that.

name: Hussain Binghatti Aljbori
current_role: Founder, Binghatti (Dubai real estate developer); son Muhammad Binghatti now chairs the company
profile: Emirati entrepreneur who founded Binghatti in Dubai in 2008, starting as a contractor before becoming a vertically integrated developer of distinctive residential towers. He owns 100% of the firm, which has launched branded towers with Mercedes-Benz, Bugatti and Jacob & Co and raised $500M in sukuk in 2024; day-to-day leadership has passed to his son Muhammad.
interesting_fact: Binghatti built the Bugatti- and Mercedes-Benz-branded residential towers in Dubai, among the first car-brand residences in the region, and became one of the UAE's biggest developers by launches.
deep_cut_fact: He named the company after his late father, Ghatti Bin Ghaeb, and holds a PhD in Industrial Technology and an MSc from the Cranfield Institute of Technology in the UK.
notes: Founder keeps a low profile; son Muhammad Binghatti is the public face and gives frequent interviews - likely the better route. Uses title 'Dr.' Name spellings vary (BinGhatti, Aljbouri).

name: Robert Friedland
current_role: Founder and Executive Co-Chairman, Ivanhoe Mines; Executive Chairman, Ivanhoe Electric (NYSE American: IE)
profile: Chicago-born, Singapore-based mining financier Robert Friedland built a fortune finding giant deposits: Voisey's Bay nickel (Canada), Oyu Tolgoi (Mongolia) and now the Kamoa-Kakula copper complex in the DRC (JV with Zijin), whose on-site smelter began producing copper anodes in January 2026. He also chairs Ivanhoe Electric (US copper exploration, Typhoon geophysics tech) and backs Ivanhoe Atlantic iron ore in Guinea/Liberia.
interesting_fact: He is an outspoken voice on electrification: he argues that the world's energy transition and AI/data-center build-out require vastly more copper than is being mined.
deep_cut_fact: At Reed College (political science, class of 1974) he was student body president, and he managed his uncle's apple orchard near McMinnville, Oregon (the 'All-One Farm') where his friend Steve Jobs tended trees, an experience credited with inspiring the name Apple.
notes: Excellent podcast fit (copper for electrification and data centers) and a famously talkative conference speaker. Interesting_fact is a paraphrase of his frequent public theme; verify a specific quote before using. Avoid Summitville/Jobs-era counterculture anecdotes.

name: Nilima Divi
current_role: Whole-Time Director (Commercial), Divi's Laboratories Ltd, Hyderabad
profile: Daughter of billionaire Murali Divi, founder of Divi's Laboratories, one of the world's largest makers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and a custom-synthesis partner to big pharma; she holds a minority stake. On the board as Director - Commercial, she oversees sourcing and procurement, capital projects, corporate finance and investor relations.
interesting_fact: Divi's Laboratories is among the world's top suppliers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and also does custom manufacturing for global pharma companies.
deep_cut_fact: She joined Divi's in July 2012 after building experience in material-requirement planning and procurement, and holds two master's degrees: international business from the Gitam Institute of Foreign Trade and international finance from the University of Glasgow.
notes: Low public profile; she heads investor relations herself, so IR channel reaches her function. Web search budget ran out mid-lane - role verified only via company site, no press interviews checked.

name: Zhixiang Zhang
current_role: Chairman, Beijing Jianlong Heavy Industry Group (Jianlong Group)
profile: Zhejiang-born (1967, Shangyu) chemical engineer who started in trading, then in 1999 bought the Zunhua steel plant and built Jianlong into one of China's largest privately controlled steelmakers, with interests in shipbuilding and mining. Jianlong ranked No. 53 among China's top 500 private companies in 2018.
interesting_fact: Nicknamed China's 'Magnate of Steel', he moved into steel in 1999 by acquiring the Zunhua Steel factory, which became the core of Jianlong.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated in chemical engineering from Zhejiang University of Technology in 1989 and in 1994 founded Zhongxiang Industry Corp. in Shaoxing, expanding it into 13 regions before turning to steel.
notes: Low international profile; no published press email found (site is JS-only). Off Forbes list since 2022. Steel decarbonisation is a possible podcast angle but not verified here (search budget exhausted).

name: Bret Taylor
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sierra (AI customer-service agents); Chairman of the board, OpenAI
profile: Stanford-trained engineer who led the team that co-created Google Maps, co-founded FriendFeed (sold to Facebook, where he became CTO), built Quip (sold to Salesforce, where he rose to co-CEO) and chaired Twitter's board through the Musk sale. Co-founded Sierra with Clay Bavor in 2023; a roughly 25% stake at a $10B valuation made him a billionaire, and he has chaired OpenAI since Nov 2023.
interesting_fact: Facebook's 'Like' button came from FriendFeed, the startup Taylor co-founded and sold to Facebook in 2009; in Dec 2025 he bought a ~1% minority stake in the San Francisco 49ers.
deep_cut_fact: Recounting Google's pre-Maps local search, Taylor noted that a search for 'coffee near Menlo Park' returned only Sun Microsystems pages, because Sun's Java-themed site was full of coffee puns. His follow-up, Google Local, was a formative near-miss that led to Google Maps.
notes: Very accessible publicly (frequent podcast guest). He lists his personal Gmail on his own homepage backchannel.org, which is the best direct route. Strong fit for AI/data-centre themes given his OpenAI chairmanship.

name: Clay Bavor
current_role: Cofounder, Sierra (AI customer-service agents), San Francisco
profile: Clay Bavor cofounded Sierra with Bret Taylor in 2023 after 18 years at Google, where he rose from associate product manager to VP running Google Labs and its AR/VR work (Cardboard, Daydream, ARCore, Lens, Project Starline). Sierra builds AI agents for customer service; a $350M round led by Greenoaks valued it at $10B.
interesting_fact: He and Bret Taylor were both hired into Google's associate product manager program by Marissa Mayer and stayed friends for ~20 years (incl. a 'monthly' poker game that met about twice a year) before founding Sierra.
deep_cut_fact: Sierra was hatched over a long lunch in December 2022, a week after ChatGPT launched. Though known as Google's 'AR/VR guy', Bavor says he had become obsessed with language models in Google Labs, the group that produced NotebookLM.
notes: No published press email for Sierra found; company X account and Bavor's own (lightly used) X account are the public routes. Frequent conference/podcast guest (Acquired, Slush 2025, AI Engineer), so podcast invitations are plausible.

name: Zhang Xin
current_role: Founder, Closer Media (film production/finance); CEO, Closer Properties / Closer Group family office (New York); co-founder of SOHO China (resigned 2022)
profile: Born in Beijing in 1965, she worked in Hong Kong factories as a teen, studied at Sussex and Cambridge, then worked at Barings and Goldman Sachs. In 1995 she co-founded SOHO China with husband Pan Shiyi. Now US-based, she invests in Manhattan trophy buildings and, since 2021, film via Closer Media.
interesting_fact: She won a special prize at the 2002 Venice Architecture Biennale as a patron for Commune by the Great Wall, a collection of villas by 12 Asian architects. In 2026 she was invited into the Executives Branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
deep_cut_fact: To pay her way in England as a student she worked in a traditional fish-and-chip shop run by a Chinese couple. Years later she made a cameo as a Chinese investor in Oliver Stone's 'Wall Street: Money Never Sleeps' (2010).
notes: Shares her fortune with her husband Pan Shiyi. She is a frequent speaker (WEF, Aspen trustee, MoMA trustee) and fairly media-friendly; film, architecture and US real estate are good hooks. No published email was found. My web-search budget ran out at this point, so contacts beyond her company sites were not checked.

name: John Jahr
profile: The 1999–2000 Forbes entry is John Jahr Jr. (1933–2006), Hamburg publisher, founding managing director of Gruner + Jahr and a member of its executive board from 1971 to 2000. He and his siblings held 25.1% of G+J via the Jahr holding. He died in Hamburg on 14 August 2006. His father, G+J co-founder John Jahr Sr., died in 1991.
notes: Deceased (14 Aug 2006, Hamburg), per German Wikipedia: https://de.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Jahr_junior . The entry most plausibly refers to John Jahr Jr.; if it meant the family or John Jahr Sr. (d. 1991), he is also deceased. Not a candidate for outreach.

name: Brenninkmeyer family
current_role: Owners of Cofra Holding AG (Zug), parent of C&A, Bregal Investments, Redevco and Anthos; chair Martijn Brenninkmeijer, to be succeeded by Florian Brenninkmeyer in April 2027
profile: Dutch-German family that founded fashion retailer C&A in 1841 in Sneek, the Netherlands. Its 100% family-owned holding Cofra has become a diversified investment group with about EUR 40 billion under management across private equity (Bregal), real estate (Redevco), asset management (Anthos), retail and clean energy, now moving from the fifth to the sixth generation.
interesting_fact: Cofra is moving leadership from the fifth to the sixth generation: CFO Florian Brenninkmeyer becomes board chair in April 2027, succeeding Martijn Brenninkmeijer (CEO from 2015, chair from 2018).

name: Joseph Lewis
current_role: Founder and principal investor, Tavistock Group (Bahamas-based private investment group)
profile: Assumed to be Joe Lewis (b. 1937), the East London-born currency trader and investor behind Tavistock Group, which holds 200+ companies in 15 countries (real estate such as Lake Nona and Albany, restaurants, life sciences, golf). name: Phillip Ruffin
current_role: Owner, Treasure Island (TI) and Circus Circus, Las Vegas; Ruffin Companies (Wichita)
profile: Wichita-raised Phil Ruffin built a fortune in Midwest convenience stores, then hotels, oil distribution and hand-truck manufacturing before moving into casinos. He bought the New Frontier (and ended a record strike), sold the site for about $1.2bn in 2007, then bought Treasure Island from MGM in 2009 (~$775m) and Circus Circus in 2019-20 ($825m). Forbes ranked him No. 972 in 2026 at about $4.3bn.
interesting_fact: In 1972 he pioneered self-serve gasoline in Kansas, building a chain of about 60 Midwest convenience stores whose cash funded his first hotel, a Wichita Marriott, in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: He was a state wrestling champion at Wichita North High School (class of 1953). One profile recalls that his father, who never went to a match, asked whether he was the one the newspaper was talking about. His family's surname was originally 'Rufan'.
notes: Aged about 90-91. Long-time Trump friend. Recent profile: https://thenevadaindependent.com/article/for-phil-ruffin-timing-is-everything. Has floated selling Circus Circus at ~$5bn (Forbes, Jan 2025). No dedicated press email found.

name: Carolus Nolet, Sr.
current_role: Chairman, Nolet Distillery (Schiedam, Netherlands); 10th-generation head of the family that co-owns Ketel One with Diageo
profile: Carolus Nolet Sr. (b. 1941) joined his family's 1691-founded Schiedam distillery in 1962 and took it over in 1979. After touring US bars from 1983 he created Ketel One, a pot-distilled premium vodka, landing its first US case sale in 1989; in 2009 Diageo bought 50% of Ketel One for $900m. He later launched NOLET'S gin and remains chairman, with sons Carl Jr. and Bob running the business.
interesting_fact: Ketel One is named after Distilleerketel #1, the coal-fired copper pot still at the Nolet distillery, a method normally used for jenever and whisky rather than vodka.
deep_cut_fact: Ketel One's first-ever case sale came in 1989 from Doug Biederbeck of Bix restaurant in San Francisco; Nolet's own after-dinner drink is a Vesper made with 50% Ketel One and 50% NOLET'S Silver gin, stirred over ice.
notes: In his mid-80s; sons Carl Jr. and Bob Nolet are the active executives and more accessible for interviews. Last on Forbes list 2015-17. Alive status assumed from lack of any obituary; not explicitly confirmed with a dated 2026 source.

profile: Sister of longtime Brose chief Michael Stoschek and co-owner of family-held Brose, the Coburg-based mechatronics auto supplier (door and seat systems, electric motors, e-bike drives) founded by Max Brose in 1908. Brose is owned 100% by the Stoschek and Volkmann family branches; she has no management role and almost no public profile.

Identity as Brose shareholder/sister of Michael Stoschek per Tharawat; no personal details or confirmation of current status found. notes: Deceased (source: https://www.myjewishlearning.com/2013/12/22/mourning-edgar-m-bronfman/). Forbes 2001-2009 entry assumed to be Edgar Sr. (son Edgar Jr. was not separately a Forbes billionaire then).

name: Ronald Burkle
current_role: Co-founder, President, Chairman and Managing Partner, The Yucaipa Companies; Executive Chairman, Soho House & Co
profile: Pomona-born (1952) investor who rose from bagging groceries at Stater Bros. to founding private-equity firm Yucaipa in 1986, rolling up supermarket chains (Fred Meyer, Ralphs, Food4Less, Dominick's). Yucaipa now invests across hospitality, sports, entertainment and logistics; he is executive chairman of Soho House and a co-owner/investor in pro sports teams.

name: Zadik Bino
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with family, via Bino Holdings) of FIBI Holdings / First International Bank of Israel
profile: Iraqi-born Israeli banker and investor (b. 1943/44). He exited Paz in 2016-17; the Bino family still controls FIBI Holdings, chaired by his son Gil.

name: Drew Houston
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO of Dropbox (transitioning to executive chairman after co-CEO Ashraf Alkarmi was named in May 2026); Meta board member
profile: Drew Houston co-founded Dropbox with MIT classmate Arash Ferdowsi in 2007 at age 24, took it public on Nasdaq in 2018 and remains its largest individual shareholder (20%+). In May 2026 Dropbox named Ashraf Alkarmi co-CEO; Houston is to move to executive chairman after a transition. He has sat on Meta's board since 2020.

deep_cut_fact: His first company, an online SAT-prep startup called 'The Accolade Group, LLC', was founded with Andrew Crick in a Chili's over onion strings when he was 21; while burned out on it he wrote a poker bot. His 2013 MIT commencement 'cheat sheet': a tennis ball, a circle and the number 30,000.

name: Wu Kai
current_role: Chief Scientist, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. (CATL); Academician, Chinese Academy of Engineering (elected 2025)

His CATL shareholding made him a billionaire. He now fronts CATL's technology roadmap, announcing sodium-ion mass production in 2026 and talking up lithium-air as a future direction.

notes: No personal channels found; route via CATL corporate communications. He speaks often at CATL Super Tech Day and academic forums (e.g., SJTU GIFT lecture Dec 2025, where he is a distinguished professor) - a speaking-event angle may work better than cold outreach. Name is common; identity matched via CATL/batteries.

name: Michael Polsky
current_role: Founder and CEO, Invenergy (Chicago)
profile: Kyiv-born thermal engineer who fled the USSR as a refugee, co-founded Indeck Energy while a Chicago Booth evening MBA student, then sold gas-plant developer SkyGen to Calpine for ~$450M (2000-01). He founded Invenergy in 2001, now a top US private clean-energy developer (~33 GW), and is pushing the Grain Belt Express transmission line.

deep_cut_fact: He arrived in the US with $500, four suitcases and no English, mailed his résumé to hundreds of companies he found in library directories, and won his first job, an engineering post at Bechtel, by communicating through math equations and sketches.
notes: Gives occasional long-form interviews (Brunswick Review, UChicago Big Brains podcast), so a strong podcast fit for energy and data-center power. Best route is Invenergy media relations. Avoid the divorce item in the Forbes bio.

current_role: Managing Partner and Co-Chairman, Silver Lake; director of Broadcom and Altera
profile: Ken Hao joined tech private-equity firm Silver Lake in 2000 after a decade as a managing director at Hambrecht & Quist, and rose to chairman (now co-chairman). name: Daniel Rocher
current_role: Major family shareholder of Groupe Rocher; founder of Daniel Jouvance (marine cosmetics)
profile: Daniel Rocher, son of Yves Rocher (founder of Groupe Rocher, 1959), founded the marine-ingredient skincare brand Daniel Jouvance in 1980; it later became part of the group. name: Bris Rocher
current_role: Chairman, Groupe Rocher (La Gacilly / Issy-les-Moulineaux, France)
profile: Grandson of Yves Rocher, he joined the family company at 16 without finishing his baccalaureate, trained at Arthur Andersen in the US, and became CEO at 31 after his grandfather's death in 2009. He bought back Sanofi's 19.3% stake in 2012, acquired US-based Arbonne in 2018, and in 2023 handed the CEO role to Jean-David Schwartz while staying chairman of the family-controlled group (Yves Rocher, Arbonne, Sabon, Dr Pierre Ricaud, Petit Bateau).
interesting_fact: He joined Yves Rocher at 16 without a baccalaureate after his father Didier died; his grandfather groomed him as successor and he became CEO at 31.

name: Kamal Ghaffarian
current_role: Founder and executive chairman of X-energy (XE), Intuitive Machines (LUNR), Axiom Space and Quantum Space
profile: Iranian-born serial entrepreneur who came to the US at 17 and co-founded SGT (1994), NASA's No. 2 engineering-services contractor, sold to KBR for $355m in 2018. He founded SMR developer X-energy (2009, now public) and co-founded Intuitive Machines, Axiom Space and Quantum Space.
interesting_fact: His Intuitive Machines lander Odysseus made the first US moon landing since 1972 (Feb 2024); X-energy is building Xe-100 small modular reactors for Dow's Texas plant and evaluating gigawatt-scale deployment with Talen Energy.
deep_cut_fact: At Capitol Technology University's May 2026 commencement (his alma mater: BS 1983, PhD 2022) he handed every graduate a gold envelope with $1,500, saying it was inspired by the family support he got after immigrating. Watching Apollo 11 on TV as a boy in Iran sparked his space passion.
notes: Energy + space angle suits the podcast (SMRs for industrial/data-center power). X-energy comms lead in 2026 releases: Robert McEntyre. info@ is his nonprofit Limitless Space Institute. In 2026 he co-founded the Fermi Explorer Mission and won Armenia's State Award for high tech.

name: Mike Repole
current_role: Majority owner/chairman, NOBULL; founder, Repole Stable; investor in the United Football League
profile: Queens-born son of Italian immigrants who co-founded Glaceau (Vitaminwater, Smartwater; sold to Coca-Cola for $4.1bn in 2007) and BodyArmor (sold to Coca-Cola for $5.6bn in 2021). He now owns a majority of athletic brand NOBULL (merged with Tom Brady's TB12 brands in 2024), invested in the UFL in 2025 and runs a major thoroughbred stable.
interesting_fact: Kobe Bryant invested about $5m for 10% of BodyArmor in 2014 and became its creative director; Coca-Cola later bought the whole company for $5.6bn.
deep_cut_fact: Between his two beverage exits he chaired snack maker Pirate's Booty from 2009, growing it about 300% in under five years before its $195m sale to B&G Foods in 2013; his racehorse Uncle Mo was 2010 American Champion Two-Year-Old.
notes: Highly media-friendly (co-starred in Barstool's 'Big Brain', frequent podcast guest) - strong podcast fit. Verified personal social handles not confirmed here (search budget exhausted); check his X/Instagram before use.

name: Brian Venturo
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV)
profile: Brian Venturo co-founded CoreWeave in 2017 with Michael Intrator and Brannin McBee; it began as an Ethereum mining operation and pivoted into a GPU cloud for AI. CoreWeave went public in 2025 at about a $23B valuation (he owns roughly 6%) and supplies compute to Microsoft, OpenAI and Meta. Earlier he was a portfolio manager at natural-gas-focused hedge fund Hudson Ridge Asset Management.
interesting_fact: CoreWeave started as a crypto miner: at its peak it ran about 50,000 Nvidia consumer gaming GPUs and was, per Venturo, the largest Ethereum miner in the world for around two and a half years before pivoting to AI cloud.
deep_cut_fact: The first mining rigs sat on the pool table in the founders' Manhattan office, then moved to a closet, and then, as Venturo joked, to 'the most cliche place possible' - his grandfather's garage in New Jersey. He also recalls 'literally pounding on the dinner table' to win Magnetar's first $100M check.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (energy-trading background, GPU/power infrastructure). Has done podcasts (Castle Island Ventures 'On the Brink' ep163 and EP.366), so is podcast-friendly. Best route: CoreWeave press team. No verified personal X handle found.

name: Riaz Valani
current_role: Investor; general partner at Global Asset Capital; longtime Juul Labs board member and major shareholder
profile: San Francisco-area investor who, through Global Asset Capital, was the first outside investor in Pax Labs/Juul, putting in a few million dollars for a stake of roughly 20%. Altria's 2018 $12.8bn deal for 35% of Juul reportedly brought him a ~$2.6bn pre-tax payout; he has remained a key Juul director and shareholder.

current_role: CEO, Baykar (Turkish UAV maker); TÜBİTAK board member; founder of the Türkiye Technology Team (T3) Foundation
profile: Istanbul-born (1978) industrial engineer who joined his father Özdemir's company Baykar after graduate study in the US. He worked on Turkey's first national UAV systems. As CEO he co-owns about 47.5% with brother Selçuk, and has turned Baykar into a major exporter (TB2, Akıncı, TB3) with $1.8bn exports in 2024.

name: Wesley Edens
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, New Fortress Energy (NASDAQ: NFE); cofounder of Fortress Investment Group; co-owner of the Milwaukee Bucks and Aston Villa
profile: Born in Helena, Montana (1961). He worked at Lehman and BlackRock before cofounding Fortress Investment Group in 1998 and became a billionaire when it went public in 2007. He founded LNG company New Fortress Energy in 2014. Through Fortress he built Brightline, the only private U.S. intercity passenger railroad (Miami-Orlando), and started Brightline West (Las Vegas-Southern California) in 2024.
interesting_fact: Brightline West is a roughly $12B, 260-mile line from Las Vegas to Rancho Cucamonga designed for speeds up to 200 mph. It is billed as the first true high-speed rail line in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: Brightline was inspired by Les Standiford's book 'Last Train to Paradise', about Henry Flagler's Florida railroad. In 2007 Fortress bought Flagler's original Florida East Coast line. As a teenager in Montana, Edens was a competitive skier.
notes: Strong energy/infrastructure fit (LNG terminals in Jamaica, Brazil and Puerto Rico; high-speed rail). Steer clear of NFE's recent financial stress. The NFE IR page blocked automated access, so check it manually for a named IR/press email.

name: Emad Al Muhaidib
current_role: Vice Chairman, Al Muhaidib Group (Dammam, Saudi Arabia)
profile: Co-owner (about 28%) and vice chairman of Al Muhaidib Group, the family conglomerate founded in 1943 by his father Abdulkadir as a food trader, later spanning building materials, real estate, infrastructure, consumer goods and finance, with stakes in at least 16 listed Saudi and Egyptian companies. He leads the group's development in Saudi Arabia's Western Province.
interesting_fact: Al Muhaidib Group started in 1943 when his father Abdulkadir traded food, before expanding into building materials and real estate; Emad and brothers Essam and Sulaiman took over after his death in 1996.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the family group he sits on the boards of Middle East Paper Company, Thabat Construction, Waste Collection and Recycling Co (WASCO) and United Feed, and is vice president of the Economic and Social Committee of the Emirate of Makkah Province.

It grew into one of Russia's largest drugmakers and state suppliers, and Mitsui bought 10% in 2017. In 2022 he stepped down as R-Pharm chairman and reportedly sold his R-Pharm assets. He chairs the business lobby Delovaya Rossiya.
interesting_fact: He started R-Pharm in 2001 with $40,000 in startup capital, half of which came from his mother. He had taken his first healthcare job in 1995, aged about 16.

name: Hiroshi Ishibashi
current_role: Chairman, Ishibashi Foundation; Director, Artizon Museum (Tokyo); Chairman, AXIS Inc.
profile: Hiroshi Ishibashi (石橋寛, b. 1946, Fukuoka) is a grandson of Bridgestone founder Shojiro Ishibashi and holds a small but valuable Bridgestone stake, with no executive role. He chairs the Ishibashi Foundation, which in 2020 rebuilt the Bridgestone Museum of Art and reopened it as the Artizon Museum in central Tokyo.

deep_cut_fact: He trained as a car and industrial designer at Art Center College of Design in Los Angeles from 1964, set up Bridgestone's in-house design department and corporate identity, and in 1981 founded AXIS, the Roppongi design hub and magazine, opening with a Sottsass show. He won the Red Dot 'Personality' award in 2023.
notes: Best route is via the Artizon Museum or Ishibashi Foundation press office; no press email was readable in the PDFs. The AXIS design-entrepreneur story is a good conversation angle.

name: John Stanton
current_role: Chairman and managing partner, Seattle Mariners; founder/chairman, Trilogy Equity Partners; director of Microsoft and Costco
profile: Wireless pioneer who was an early McCaw Cellular executive (COO/vice chairman), then founded Western Wireless in 1994, whose spin-off VoiceStream became T-Mobile USA after Deutsche Telekom bought it. He later built Trilogy International (Latin American and NZ carriers) and Trilogy Equity Partners, and has led the Mariners ownership group since 2016.
interesting_fact: He has helmed or co-led four of the top U.S. wireless operators, and lived in the Seattle area nearly all his life apart from university; in 2025 he was enshrined in the Little League Hall of Excellence.
deep_cut_fact: He got into wireless by volunteering in 1980, as a young Ernst & Whinney consultant in Tacoma, for a mobile-telecom regulatory docket nobody else wanted; one of the clients he recruited was Craig McCaw. Also: he didn't make his high-school baseball team.
notes: Accessible to Seattle tech media (GeekWire Startup Day speaker, podcast guest) - good precedent for a podcast ask. Route via Mariners communications or Trilogy Equity Partners. Whitman College '77, Harvard MBA '79.

name: Sheryl Sandberg
current_role: Founder, Lean In / Sandberg Goldberg Bernthal Family Foundation; co-founder, Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners; board member, Nscale (since March 2026)
profile: Former Meta/Facebook COO (2008-2022) and earlier Google VP of online sales, McKinsey consultant, World Bank economist and chief of staff to Treasury Secretary Larry Summers. She left Meta's board in 2024, invests via Sandberg Bernthal Venture Partners with husband Tom Bernthal, and in 2026 refocused Lean In on closing the AI gender gap.
interesting_fact: In March 2026 she joined the board of British AI data-center company Nscale alongside Nick Clegg and Susan Decker, as it raised a $2bn Series C at a $14.6bn valuation, Europe's largest Series C.
deep_cut_fact: She taught aerobics while at North Miami Beach High School in the 1980s, and at Harvard won the John H. Williams Prize as top graduating economics student and co-founded Women in Economics and Government.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center episode given the Nscale board seat. Lean In's press inbox explicitly handles speaking/media requests — best route. Personal social accounts exist (X/Instagram/LinkedIn) but not verified here. Avoid references to late husband Dave Goldberg.

name: Dennis Gillings
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Quintiles (now IQVIA); philanthropist and life-sciences investor (retired from IQVIA board 2018)
profile: London-born statistician (b. 1944) who moved to UNC Chapel Hill in 1971 to teach biostatistics and in 1982 founded Quintiles to make drug trials faster and more efficient. He took it public in 1994 and built it into the largest clinical-research organization; it merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form IQVIA. Knighted in 2020 for services to dementia and life-sciences research.
interesting_fact: UNC's school of public health - the UNC Gillings School of Global Public Health - is named after him and his first wife Joan, reflecting his roots as a former UNC biostatistics instructor.
deep_cut_fact: He is the son of a London fishmonger; he earned a BSc and PhD in mathematics at the University of Exeter (teaching there while doing his doctorate), and in 1998 endowed the Dennis Gillings Professorship of Health Management at Cambridge.
notes: No personal/family-office contact published that could be verified (web search budget exhausted mid-lane). Spouse Mireille Gillings runs HUYA Bioscience (San Diego) - possible indirect route via the Dennis and Mireille Gillings Foundation, but no official contact page verified. name: David Adelman

name: Alberto Bombassei
current_role: Chairman Emeritus and controlling shareholder (via family holding Nuova Fourb), Brembo; chairman 1993–2021
profile: Born in Vicenza in 1940 and raised in Bergamo, Bombassei joined his father Emilio's brake company Brembo in 1964 and ran it for decades (GM 1976, CEO 1984, chairman 1993–2021). notes: Now 86 and has passed his stake to his children, though he retains control. Approach via Brembo corporate communications or the Kilometro Rosso park. Formerly vice president of Confindustria; speaks openly to Italian press.

current_role: Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Trigano (former chairman of the management board)

current_role: Vice-chairman of the board, Dasa (Diagnósticos da América); stepped down as CEO in Feb 2025 (per reports)
profile: Son of Amil founder Edson de Godoy Bueno, whose sale of Amil to UnitedHealth in 2012 underpins the family fortune. current_role: Former co-owner of dm-drogerie markt; stake transferred to his son in 2016; reportedly moved to dm's supervisory board; managing director of Günther Lehmann GmbH & Co. KG, Karlsruhe (per marketscreener)
