interesting_fact: AIMA, founded in Tianjin in 1999, only moved into electric two-wheelers in 2004 and is now one of China's largest makers, competing head-to-head with Yadea.
notes: Common name - identity tied to AIMA chairman per Forbes. Little English-language biography; Chinese sources (stcn.com) were unreachable from this session and web search budget was exhausted, so no deep-cut fact. AIMA (battery/EV two-wheelers) fits the energy theme. Corporate IR route via SSE filings recommended.

name: Pavan Jain
current_role: Chairman, INOX Group and INOX Air Products (Delhi)
profile: IIT Delhi chemical engineer with 50+ years in industry. He built INOX Air Products from a single plant into India's largest industrial and medical gas maker, and diversified the group into refrigerant gases, cryogenic equipment (INOXCVA / Inox India, listed in 2023) and cinemas (INOX Leisure, merged into PVR INOX). Son Siddharth runs the businesses day to day; his brother Vivek leads the separate Inox GFL group.
interesting_fact: In 2023 he listed cryogenic tank maker Inox India, which debuted at a 44% premium to its IPO price. The same year INOX Leisure merged with PVR to form India's largest multiplex chain.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chemical engineer at IIT Delhi. As chairman of INOX Air Products he grew it from a single plant into one of India's leading industrial gas companies.
notes: Industrial gases and cryogenics (LNG/hydrogen tanks) fit the energy angle. The media-centre email is shown as 'punnet.gupta' in the page text, but the mailto link is puneet.gupta@inoxap.com. Son Siddharth Jain is the more media-active family member.

name: Herbert Allen Jr
current_role: Former president (now senior figure and controlling family member) of Allen & Company, New York; son Herbert Allen III has run the firm since 2002
profile: Joined his uncle Charles's boutique investment bank Allen & Co. straight out of Williams College in 1962 and became president in 1966 at 26. The firm bought control of Columbia Pictures in 1973 and sold it to Coca-Cola in 1982, giving him a long-time Coke board seat. It advised on major tech deals and IPOs and hosts the invitation-only Sun Valley conference.
interesting_fact: He launched the Allen & Co. Sun Valley Conference in 1982, the 'summer camp for billionaires' where media and tech leaders such as Bill Gates and Mark Zuckerberg have gathered. He is also the largest individual holder of Coca-Cola stock.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Irvington, New York, joined Allen & Co. the year he left Williams College (1962), and became its president at 26. In 1998 he gave $20 million back to Williams.
notes: Allen & Co. is famously discreet: no public website, press office or published email. Now based in Cody, Wyoming (per Wikipedia), aged about 86. Realistic route is a warm introduction via the Sun Valley network or Herbert Allen III.

name: Ioannis Papalekas
current_role: Founder and ~66% shareholder of YODA PLC (Cyprus Stock Exchange-listed investment group); based in Nicosia
profile: Greek investor Ioannis Papalekas (about 50) made his name developing commercial real estate in Romania, then founded Globalworth, listing it in London in 2013 and selling his 13.5% stake for $315M in 2020. He founded YODA in 2019 and listed it in Cyprus in 2022; it invests in shipping and energy, hospitality, healthcare, technology and Greek/Cypriot real estate.
interesting_fact: Before founding Globalworth, his Romanian commercial real-estate developments reportedly earned a 175% rate of return for him and his investors.
deep_cut_fact: YODA listed on the Cyprus Stock Exchange's Emerging Companies Market in 2022 at EUR 0.50 a share, and in 2023 began buying Nasdaq-listed shipping/energy stock CCEC.
notes: Low media profile. YODA's general inbox is the only published channel found; IR announcements at yoda.com.cy/investor-relations/announcements/. Shipping/energy holdings give a possible energy angle.

name: Zygmunt Solorz
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Polsat Plus Group (Cyfrowy Polsat) and power producer ZE PAK
profile: Born in Radom in 1956, Solorz left communist Poland in 1977 for West Germany, where he ran a transport business and imported used cars. He launched Polsat by satellite in 1992 and built it into Cyfrowy Polsat / Polsat Plus Group, spanning pay-TV, mobile (Plus), Netia broadband, finance and energy. Energy assets include ZE PAK and green-hydrogen and renewables projects.
interesting_fact: A licensed pilot, Solorz flies as a hobby and controls Jet Story, a private-jet charter firm in Central Europe.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 his lignite power producer ZE PAK began working with Korea Hydro & Nuclear Power on possible small modular reactors at the Pątnów power station site, part of the group's move from coal to nuclear and renewables.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (ZE PAK's coal-to-nuclear/renewables shift, hydrogen). He rarely gives interviews. A widely reported family succession dispute has been running since 2024. Formerly known as Solorz-Żak. The forbes_facts entry 'Jest Story' is a typo for Jet Story.

name: Yvonne Bauer
current_role: Owner and Chair of the Board, Bauer Media Group (Hamburg)
profile: Fifth-generation owner of Bauer Media Group, which grew from an 1875 printing shop into a European publishing, audio and outdoor-media group with hundreds of magazine titles (InTouch, Grazia) and over 400 websites and apps. She took control in 2010 from her father Heinz Bauer, receiving 85% of the company. She has since expanded into newspapers, notably buying Mitteldeutsche Zeitung in 2020.
interesting_fact: Bauer Media has been family-owned for five generations since its founding as a small printing company in 1875; today it spans publishing, audio (radio) and outdoor advertising.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business in 2005, she served an apprenticeship at Hamburg publishing house Hoffmann und Campe. Inside Bauer she then worked in the German advertising and sales departments before taking over in 2010.
notes: Very private and rarely gives interviews. The corporate press-enquiry route on bauermedia.com is the published channel. The deep-cut fact combines Forbes (apprenticeship) with Bauer's management page (sales and advertising roles).

name: Natacha Nikolajevic
current_role: Heir and shareholder, via the estate of Olivier Dassault, in the Dassault family holding (Groupe Industriel Marcel Dassault)
profile: Natacha Nikolajevic married Olivier Dassault, a French National Assembly member and grandson of Dassault Aviation founder Marcel Dassault, in 2009. After his death in a helicopter crash in 2021 she inherited his share of the Dassault family fortune, which spans Dassault Aviation, Dassault Systèmes, Le Figaro and vineyards.
interesting_fact: She met her late husband Olivier Dassault at an auction where they were bidding against each other for the same item.
notes: Very private: no public role, website or social accounts found. Marriage date (5 Feb 2009) per French Wikipedia (https://fr.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivier_Dassault). No direct outreach route found; any route would go through the Dassault family holding, which does not publish a personal contact. Web search quota ran out.

name: Serge Godin
current_role: Founder and co-chair of the board, CGI Inc. (daughter Julie Godin became executive chair in 2025)
profile: One of nine children from a Lac-Saint-Jean sawmill family. He studied computing and administration, then used $5,000 of savings to found CGI in Quebec City in 1976 at age 26. He was CEO until 2006 and grew CGI through 100+ acquisitions (including Bell Sygma in 1998) into a C$15bn-revenue global IT services and consulting firm. His family office, Distinction Capital, manages family capital and the Fondation Famille Godin.
interesting_fact: After his father's uninsured sawmill burned down, the young Godin worked at a convenience store after school and at a dry cleaner's on Saturdays to help pay the family's bills.
deep_cut_fact: He earned one of the first CEGEP diplomas in computer science ever awarded in Quebec, at the Collège de Jonquière. His family office, Distinction Capital, is based in Montreal's 1906 heritage William Alexander Molson house.
notes: French-language outreach is preferred. The family office email is the most direct published route; otherwise go through CGI media relations (cgi.com). CGI's IT services and data-center outsourcing fit the podcast's theme.

name: Todd Wagner
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Charity Network; CEO & co-founder, 2929 Entertainment; co-founder, FoodFight USA
profile: A Gary, Indiana native with a UVA law degree, Wagner co-founded streaming pioneer Broadcast.com with Mark Cuban and, as CEO, sold it to Yahoo for $5.7B in 1999, hedging his shares with put options before the dot-com crash. He co-owns 2929 Entertainment (Magnolia Pictures, Landmark Theatres history) and runs Charity Network (Charitybuzz, Prizeo).
interesting_fact: The Broadcast.com sale made about 300 of its employees millionaires; Wagner later had a cameo in 'Akeelah and the Bee' (2006), which he also produced.
deep_cut_fact: He owns the Dallas Flash, a Major League Pickleball team, and in 2023 co-founded FoodFight USA, a nonpartisan nonprofit; his foundation (since 2000) brought KIPP charter schools and After-School All-Stars to North Texas.
notes: Sold his Dallas Mavericks stake in Dec 2023. Kelley School of Business Distinguished Entrepreneur (1998). Streaming-media pioneer angle fits an entrepreneurship podcast; foundation inbox is the best published route.

name: Leslie Alexander
current_role: Private investor; former owner of the NBA's Houston Rockets (1993-2017)
profile: Leslie Alexander (b. 1943) dropped out of Brooklyn Law School to trade bonds on Wall Street, founded The Alexander Group in 1980 and profited from a stake in student-loan securitizer First Marblehead. He bought the Houston Rockets for $85M in 1993, won titles in 1994 and 1995, and sold the team to Tilman Fertitta for $2.2B in 2017. He now invests privately and funds animal-welfare causes.
interesting_fact: He paid $85 million for the Rockets in 1993 and sold for $2.2 billion in 2017; Forbes named him the NBA's best owner in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He also owned the WNBA's Houston Comets (1997-2007), which won the league's first four championships (1997-2000); and he tried to buy the NHL's Edmonton Oilers in 1998.
notes: Very private since selling the Rockets; no published office/foundation contact found. Philanthropy via Clutch City Foundation (Rockets era) and a horse sanctuary in Middleburg, VA named after his mother Evelyn. Weak fit for energy/data-center themes.

name: Kevin Systrom
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Instagram; co-founder of Artifact (acquired by Yahoo, 2024); no new operating company announced as of 2026
profile: Stanford management science and engineering grad (2006) who co-founded Instagram with Mike Krieger in 2010. Facebook bought it for $1B in 2012, and he ran it until 2018, when it had about 1B monthly users. He later backed and joined the board of the Cazoo SPAC, and in 2023 co-launched the AI news app Artifact, which Yahoo acquired in 2024.
interesting_fact: Instagram began as Burbn, a cluttered HTML5 check-in app. Systrom and Krieger cut it down to its photo-sharing feature, and Systrom personally developed the X-Pro II filter that is still on Instagram.
deep_cut_fact: At Stanford he turned down a recruiting pitch from Mark Zuckerberg and spent a term in Florence studying photography. As one of 12 Mayfield Fellows he interned at Odeo, the podcasting startup that became Twitter.
notes: His public social accounts (@kevin on Instagram and X) are the most direct route. He has done many podcasts and talks about product, AI and the Artifact shutdown, so he is a good fit for an entrepreneurship show. His listed site systrom.com did not resolve.

name: David Fong
current_role: Managing Director and Co-chairman, Hip Shing Hong Group (Hong Kong)
profile: David Fong runs Hip Shing Hong, one of Hong Kong's largest private real-estate investment groups, with residential, commercial and hospitality holdings. The group was founded in 1948 and chaired by his late father Fong Yun Wah until 2022; it is now co-chaired by David and his uncle.
interesting_fact: The family's fortune started with a sesame-seed-processing business before it moved into property. Its roots go back to 1927, when Fong Yun Wah came to Hong Kong from Guangdong with his father.
notes: Private, low-profile family company with no verified official website or published contact found. The web search budget ran out before a group site or any family foundation (the Fong Yun Wah name appears on Chinese university buildings) could be checked; verify that before using it.

name: Daniel Lubetzky
current_role: Founder of KIND Snacks; founder of family office Camino Partners; Shark Tank 'shark'; founder of Starts With Us
profile: Mexico City-born, Stanford Law-trained entrepreneur who founded KIND in 2004 and sold it to Mars (deal valuing it at ~$5bn in 2020); he sold his remaining stake in 2025. Now invests via Camino Partners (consumer health, longevity, CPG), is a main shark on Shark Tank, and runs bridge-building nonprofits such as Starts With Us and Builders.
interesting_fact: As a teen and student he bought watches wholesale and resold them at flea markets and mall kiosks, and wrote a 268-page Trinity University senior thesis on achieving Arab-Israeli peace through business ventures.
deep_cut_fact: His first peace-through-business venture began in 1992 when, as a fresh Stanford Law graduate on a fellowship in Israel, he fell for a sun-dried tomato spread and visited its maker, Yoel Benesh; PeaceWorks later sold it as 'Spraté' under the joke label 'Moshe Pupik & Ali Mishmunken's World Famous Sauces'.
notes: Very accessible: has his own podcast and a published media/speaking inbox (comms@lubetzky.org) - best route. Strong entrepreneurship fit.

name: Leng Youbin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, China Feihe Ltd. (HKEX: 6186); deputy to the National People's Congress
profile: Heilongjiang dairy entrepreneur who herded cows as a child and worked at a state-owned dairy farm for about a decade. He then took stakes in the farm and a dairy plant and built Feihe into one of China's largest infant-formula makers, with its own farms in northeast China. Feihe listed in Hong Kong in 2019.
interesting_fact: He earned his degree from Northeast Agricultural University by correspondence course in 1995 and later an EMBA from Peking University. At the 2025 Harvard China Forum he lectured on scientific cattle-raising.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself a 'second-generation builder of the Great Northern Wilderness (北大荒)'. When the property boom tempted Feihe to diversify into real estate, he refused: 'If we had done real estate then, there would be no Feihe deeply rooted in its core business.'
notes: Active NPC deputy who speaks publicly on black-soil protection and on making dairy ingredients domestically. Contact would go through Feihe's investor relations; no published email was retrievable. Weak fit for an energy podcast, except possibly agriculture and energy angles.

name: Rishad Naoroji
current_role: Founder, Raptor Research and Conservation Foundation (Mumbai); member, Governing Council, Bombay Natural History Society
profile: Rishad Naoroji (b. 1951) is a Godrej family member and cousin of Adi, Nadir and Jamshyd Godrej. His fortune comes from a one-fifth share of the family's assets, though he never worked in the business; after the 2024 split of the Godrej group, filings show he sold his stakes to his cousins. He is a raptor biologist, wildlife photographer and author.
interesting_fact: He wrote 'Birds of Prey of the Indian Subcontinent' (2006/07), described as the first species-by-species book on the region's raptors, covering all 69 resident and migrant species. A reviewer said it seemed about 25 years in the making.
deep_cut_fact: He has published field ornithology himself, for example 'Breeding of the Red-headed Falcon Falco chicquera in Saurashtra, Gujarat' in Forktail (2011). His own 1992 photo of a female Mountain Hawk-Eagle on its nest in Corbett Tiger Reserve appears in his book.
notes: Very low-profile and not a business figure. A conservation or birding angle is the only natural hook. No published contact was found; the Bombay Natural History Society (bnhs.org) is a possible institutional route.

name: Jiang Yintai
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Daimay Automotive Interior Co. (SSE: 603730)
profile: Jiang Yintai (姜银台, b. 1950) set up Daimay on Daishan island, Zhoushan, Zhejiang in 1982 and moved HQ to Shanghai in 2002; he and son Jiang Ming are actual controllers. Daimay is the world's No.1 sun-visor maker by share and also makes headrests, armrests and integrated headliner systems for GM, Ford, Tesla and others, with plants in Mexico, the US, France and Vietnam.
interesting_fact: Over 86% of Daimay's 2024 revenue came from outside China; in Nov 2025 the auto-parts maker set up a RMB100M robotics subsidiary, Shanghai Daimay Robot Technology.
deep_cut_fact: Before Daimay he ran the Zhejiang Daishan Foam General Factory (岱山泡沫总厂) as factory director; he was named an outstanding Zhejiang entrepreneur in 2011 and served as a Zhoushan People's Congress deputy.
notes: Low profile, Chinese-language only. Route via board secretary / IR office. Robotics pivot and North American manufacturing footprint are possible hooks.

name: Ajay Parekh
current_role: Non-Executive Vice Chairman, Pidilite Industries (Mumbai)
profile: Ajay Balvantray Parekh is the younger son of Balvant Parekh, who founded Pidilite in 1959; he has served on the board for decades and is now non-executive vice chairman, while brother Madhukar chairs the company. Pidilite is India's leading maker of adhesives, sealants, construction chemicals and art materials, and in 2020 bought Huntsman's Indian subsidiary for $290m.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's flagship white glue Fevicol became a household name in India through decades of witty, award-winning advertising.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Family-linked charities include the Pidilite Foundation and Balvant Parekh Centre for General Semantics (his personal role unclear). Route via Pidilite corporate/IR.

name: Liu Sheng
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director and President, Zhongji Innolight (Shenzhen 300308; Hong Kong listing 2026)
profile: Liu Sheng (刘圣), a Georgia Tech mechanical-engineering PhD, worked in Silicon Valley optical comms (Lucent, Pine Photonics, Opnext) before returning to found Suzhou InnoLight in 2008. Google-backed InnoLight was bought in 2016-17 by Shandong Zhongji, renamed Zhongji Innolight, now the world's largest optical-module supplier to AI data centers; he has chaired it since 2023.
interesting_fact: Per CIC figures in its Hong Kong listing, Zhongji Innolight has been the world's largest optical interconnect provider by revenue for five straight years since 2021, with 21.2% of the market in 2025; its 2026 HK IPO was billed as Hong Kong's biggest since Alibaba's in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Born July 1971 in Daying County, Suining (Sichuan), he entered Tsinghua as the county's top science scorer; his first US job after the Georgia Tech PhD was R&D engineer at Lucent, and in 2008 he came back with four other US-trained PhDs to start InnoLight in Suzhou Industrial Park.
notes: Highly relevant to the AI data-center theme (800G/1.6T optical transceivers for Nvidia/Google/Amazon/Meta-type buyers). Route via board-secretary office email (listed in the 2025 interim report summary).

name: Thomas Dundon
current_role: Chairman & managing partner, Dundon Capital Partners (Dallas); owner/CEO, Carolina Hurricanes (NHL) and Portland Trail Blazers (NBA); chairman, pickleball.com
profile: Dallas financier (b. 1971) who co-founded subprime auto lender Drive Financial, which became Santander Consumer USA; he exited in 2015 with about $700m. Through Dundon Capital Partners he invests in finance, healthcare and real estate, owns the NHL's Carolina Hurricanes, led the $4.2bn Trail Blazers purchase in 2025, and controls pickleball's PPA Tour/UPA.
interesting_fact: His Carolina Hurricanes won the 2026 Stanley Cup - the franchise's first Final appearance since 2006 - eight years after he bought control of the team.
deep_cut_fact: Raised partly in Atco, New Jersey, and Plano, Texas (his father managed pizzerias), his first venture after SMU was a Fort Worth burger restaurant, Izzy's, which closed within a year; he then learned auto lending working in financing at a Chevrolet used-car dealership. He also co-founded Dallas's Trinity Forest Golf Club.
notes: Outspoken and media-accessible (sports/pickleball press). Best routes: Carolina Hurricanes or Trail Blazers communications departments, or PPA Tour/pickleball.com media. Avoid AAF collapse and subprime-lending lawsuits as hooks. No published email verified (search budget exhausted mid-lane).

name: Zhang Jin
profile: Input merges two different people. Hurun lists 张静 (Zhang Jing) with Maoye (茂业) wealth shared with Huang Maoru, i.e. the Maoye department-store/property group family. The linked Forbes profile is a different person: Zhang Jin, chairman of Guangzhou-based Cedar Holdings (real estate, finance, auto sales), last updated 2021.
notes: Identity conflict: Chinese name 张静 + 'Maoye' + shared_with Huang Maoru points to the Maoye International family, but forbes_bio/forbes_profile_url describe Cedar Holdings' Zhang Jin (Forbes profile, not updated since Apr 2021). Resolve which person is intended before outreach; kept minimal per instructions.

name: Liying Chen
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Yunda Holding (Shenzhen-listed Yunda Express)
profile: Chen Liying (陈立英) co-founded Yunda Express, one of China's largest parcel-delivery companies, in Shanghai in 1999 with her husband Nie Tengyun, who chairs the group. Yunda went public via a reverse merger on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in December 2016; she owns about 21% and serves as vice chairman.
interesting_fact: She and her husband are both billionaires from the same company. Hurun listed her among its Self-Made Women (2017-2020), and she ranks among China's few self-made female logistics founders.
notes: Very low public profile and no English-language interviews found. The route would be Yunda Holding's board secretary/IR office, whose contact is in its Shenzhen exchange filings (not extracted here). She shares the fortune with her husband Nie Tengyun. No deep-cut fact was found; my web-search budget was exhausted.

name: Shaowu Huang
profile: Huang Shaowu (黄绍武), a Chinese investor on the Hurun China list since 2007; source listed as 'SinoPostgraduate' (likely a garbled translation of a company name). Identity could not be verified in this pass.
notes: Not verified: the shared web-search budget ran out, and Forbes, Baidu Baike and zh-Wikipedia direct fetches failed. 'SinoPostgraduate' looks like a mistranslation. One unverified hypothesis is Shenzhen 神州通 (Shenzhou Tong) Investment Group. Needs re-research before any outreach.

name: Huang Maoru
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Maoye International Holdings (0848.HK), Shenzhen
profile: Guangdong-born (c.1965) founder of the Maoye group, who started in Shenzhen property development in 1992 and moved into department stores in the late 1990s. Maoye International runs department stores and commercial real estate across China; Huang, through his holding companies, is the controlling shareholder and still leads strategy as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Before department stores he founded Maoye (Shenzhen) Real Estate Development in 1992 and Shenzhen Maoye (Group) in 1995, and he has over 30 years in department-store and commercial property.
deep_cut_fact: Maoye's retail business began with a single store, Dongmen Maoye in Shenzhen's Dongmen shopping district, opened in March 1997; Huang's hometown is Qianhu village in Huilai County, Jieyang (Chaoshan region).
notes: Known in Chinese media as an 'invisible tycoon'; very private, rarely interviewed. Son Huang Wei (Tony Huang) is non-executive director at Maoye International and runs Maoye Commercial. Route via HK-listed company IR.

name: Ding Liguo
current_role: Chairman, Delong Holdings / Delong Steel Group; chairman of Tianjin Xin Tiangang Steel Group; actual controller of gas utility Delong Huineng (SZ: 000593)
profile: Tangshan-born (1970) steel entrepreneur who started a rolling mill in 1992, took over a struggling Xingtai steel plant in 1999 (renamed Delong Steel) and built Delong into a private steel group that absorbed Tianjin's state-owned Tiangang in 2019. He also controls listed natural-gas distributor Delong Huineng. A former deputy to the 11th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Delong's working steel plant in Xingtai was rated a national 4A-level tourist attraction in 2020 - billed as Hebei's first operating steelworks to earn it - after the company retired old equipment and turned the space into parks and lawns, with RMB 3.55bn spent on environmental upgrades since 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Studied mechanical manufacturing at Hebei Institute of Technology (now North China University of Science and Technology) 1989-91, and founded his first company, Tangshan Changcheng Rolling Mill, in 1992 at about 22.
notes: IR email is the published board-secretary address of Delong Huineng (000593), his listed gas company - not Delong Steel directly. Deep-cut source (maigoo) is a Chinese bio aggregator, moderately reliable. Chinese-language outreach recommended; no personal social accounts found.

name: Liu Ling
current_role: Director and Administrative Affairs Director, Shenzhen Kstar Science & Technology (科士达, SZSE: 002518)
profile: Co-owner, alongside chairman/GM Liu Chengyu, of Kstar, a Shenzhen maker of UPS power systems, data-centre infrastructure (precision cooling, modular DC), PV inverters, energy storage and EV chargers, listed in Shenzhen since 2010. She joined the company in 1998 and has sat on its board since 2007; re-nominated in Nov 2025 for a term to 2028.
interesting_fact: Kstar grew out of a small company in Xiapu, Fujian (霞浦科士达) into a listed power-electronics group whose UPS and data-centre power products sit right at the energy/data-centre intersection, now expanding into energy storage.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she was a schoolteacher at Fujian's Xiapu No. 1 Middle School (福建霞浦一中); she later earned an EMBA from Peking University.
notes: Low public profile; Liu Chengyu (chairman) is the company's public face. Approach via the board secretary's office (stock@kstar.com.cn). Source for bio/email: Kstar 2025 annual report (Apr 2026).

name: Li Dongsheng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, TCL Technology Group / TCL Industries (chairman since 1996)
profile: Li Dongsheng (Tomson Li, b. 1957, Huizhou) joined TCL's predecessor TTK out of university in 1982, became chairman/CEO in 1996 and built TCL into a global electronics, display (TCL CSOT) and solar-wafer (TCL Zhonghuan) group. His wealth is mainly his TCL Technology stake; he is also an ACFIC vice chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2004 TCL formed a TV joint venture with France's Thomson and bought Alcatel's handset business. That year Fortune named him Asia's Businessman of the Year, Time/CNN listed him among the 25 most influential global business people, and France awarded him the Légion d'honneur.
deep_cut_fact: He studied radio technology at South China Institute of Technology (class of 1982) and began as a technician at TTK Home Appliances, the joint venture that became TCL. He has written two books: 'Blue Ocean Transformation: TCL and Me' (2009) and 'Xiang Sheng Er Sheng' (2017).

public_contacts.value: ir@tcl.com (TCL Technology board secretary office; tel 0755-3331 1666)

notes: Strong energy fit: TCL Zhonghuan is a major solar-wafer maker. He is a National People's Congress deputy. Wikipedia also has a different Li Dongsheng (a former public-security vice minister jailed in 2016), so do not confuse them. He posts on Sina Weibo.

name: Fang Junyun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Jiemei Electronic & Technology (洁美科技, SZSE: 002859)
profile: Fang Junyun (方隽云, b. 1964) founded and controls Jiemei (input's 'Jimei Technology'), an Anji/Hangzhou maker of paper and plastic carrier tapes, electronic tapes and release films used to package chip components. He holds ~53% directly and via holding company. Jiemei is also moving into battery materials: composite aluminium and copper current-collector foils.
interesting_fact: Jiemei now makes composite copper foil and carbon-coated composite aluminium foil for lithium batteries, extending a component-packaging business into EV and energy-storage materials.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Jiemei he was a department manager at China National Packaging Import & Export's Zhejiang branch. The company began in April 2001 as 'Anji Jiemei Paper Products' in an Anji County industrial park with just RMB 1.5m in registered capital.
notes: Input spelling 'Jimei Technology' = Jiemei (洁美科技). Low media profile; best route is the board secretary's office (IR email in annual report summary). Battery-materials angle is a good podcast hook.

name: Fang Jining
current_role: Listed by Hurun as linked to 'Jimei Technology' (electrical equipment), jointly with Fang Junyun; role not verified
profile: Hurun China and Global lists (2017-2026) include Fang Jining (方骥柠), jointly with Fang Junyun, with wealth from 'Jimei Technology' in electrical equipment (about $2.3bn). Five English and Chinese searches found no public profile, company page or news coverage confirming the company's legal name or Fang's role.
notes: Could not identify the operating company behind Hurun's 'Jimei Technology' label. Needs a Chinese business-registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) lookup of the shareholder name or the Hurun China list entry. Treat as unresearched.

name: Cheng Zhuo
current_role: Founder, chairwoman and executive director, Circuit Fabology Microelectronics Equipment (CFME, 芯碁微装; 688630.SS, Hong Kong dual listing 2026)
profile: Cheng Zhuo (程卓, b. May 1966) is the founder and controlling shareholder of Hefei-based CFME, a maker of maskless direct-write lithography equipment for PCBs and semiconductors/advanced packaging. She founded it in 2015 after handling the restructuring of lithography firm Hefei Xinshuo, listed it on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021 and passed a Hong Kong listing hearing in June 2026.
interesting_fact: She came to chip-equipment from finance and management, not engineering: she was drawn into the industry in 2013 when asked to help restructure Hefei Xinshuo's debts, briefly serving as its chair and finance director before founding CFME in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Her career began in August 1984 in management at state-owned Factory 9409 (Anhui General Machinery); after leaving in 1998 she founded businesses including Anhui Shengjia Auction Co. before moving into lithography. She studied mechanics at a technical school and Chinese literature at Anhui Radio & TV University.
notes: Low-profile; Chinese-language coverage only. Contact via CFME's board secretary / IR office (details in company filings on cninfo.com.cn). Lithography for AI-server PCBs/advanced packaging is a relevant data-center angle.

name: Lei Jian (雷健)
current_role: Director and Vice President, HKC Corporation (惠科股份, Shenzhen display-panel maker); member of board strategy committee
profile: Co-founding executive of HKC, the Shenzhen-based maker of LCD/Mini-LED display panels and smart-display terminals (revenue ~40B yuan in 2024) controlled by founder Wang Zhiyong. He joined as vice president when HKC was set up in December 2001 and, with Xu Qiang, holds Shenzhen Jinfeiyang, HKC's second-largest shareholder (~16%). His Hurun wealth reflects HKC's Shenzhen main-board IPO process.
interesting_fact: HKC is one of China's biggest panel makers, with large state-backed fabs in Mianyang, Chuzhou, Changsha and elsewhere; it showcased a 5K RGB Mini LED panel at ChinaJoy 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a teacher - first at the national meteorological administration's Nanchang Meteorological School, then at Buxin Middle School in Shenzhen's Luohu district - before joining HKC as vice president at its founding in December 2001.
notes: Very low profile; no personal media presence. Contact would be via HKC board secretary office (see HKC/001399 prospectus on cninfo: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-06-04/1225350393.PDF); HKC website not reachable from here.

name: Luo Yan
current_role: Vice Chairman, Hoshine Silicon Industry (603260.SH); General Manager of controlling shareholder Ningbo Hoshine Group
profile: Luo Yan (罗燚, born 1984) is the daughter of Hoshine founder and chairman Luo Liguo, and one of the company's three controlling owners with her father and brother. Hoshine is one of the world's largest producers of industrial silicon and silicones and has expanded into polysilicon for solar. She has been vice chairman since 2015 and runs the family holding company.
interesting_fact: When she first joined the rich lists in 2021, she was dubbed Zhejiang's richest woman, holding about 24.93% of the family holding company that controls Hoshine.
deep_cut_fact: She started at Hoshine in the marketing department in 2008, then served as Communist Party branch secretary and head of the board office (2011-2015) before becoming vice chairman in June 2015. She holds a master's degree.
notes: Strong energy angle: Hoshine makes silicon and polysilicon for the solar supply chain. Low media profile; the route is the board secretary's office via the IR email in the 2025 annual report.

name: Alexander Ponomarenko
current_role: Co-owner of Sheremetyevo airport holding (with Alexander Skorobogatko); stepped down as Sheremetyevo board chairman in 2022 after EU sanctions
profile: Russian businessman who, with long-time partner Alexander Skorobogatko, moved from a perfume factory and banking into sea ports, airport construction and real estate; in 2013 they and Arkady Rotenberg won the tender to develop state-owned Sheremetyevo, Russia's largest airport. He chaired Sheremetyevo's board from 2016 until 2022.
interesting_fact: He and partner Alexander Skorobogatko started out by setting up a small perfume factory in Ukraine before founding a bank in Moscow and moving into ports and airports.
notes: Sanctioned by the EU, UK and US since 2022 (EU court declined to lift sanctions). Not a suitable podcast/outreach target given sanctions exposure; no published contacts. Forbes facts include politically sensitive items (Black Sea 'Putin's Palace' purchase) - avoid.

name: Navin Engineer
current_role: Founder and co-owner (with wife Varsha), Chemidex Pharma, Egham, Surrey
profile: Kenya-born pharmacist Navin Engineer founded Chemidex with his wife Varsha in 1981, starting with one pharmacy in Chertsey. In 1999 they sold their 14 shops to Celesio for about £12m and turned Chemidex into a company that acquires and markets prescription drug brands. The couple appear on the Sunday Times Rich List.
interesting_fact: He was sent from Kenya to London in 1963 to live with an aunt, trained at the London School of Pharmacy, and grew a single Chertsey chemist's shop into a billionaire's pharmaceutical business.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after qualifying was as a Boots pharmacist, which he found 'a little bit like the civil service'. When a visiting area manager asked him for a cup of tea while he was busy dispensing prescriptions, he resigned the same day.
notes: Extremely private. Chemidex has no active public website and no published press or office contact; only a registered office on Companies House, which is not a personal contact. The Rich List entry is shared with his wife Varsha. Chemidex-linked firms have drawn press scrutiny over generic drug pricing, so avoid that in outreach.

name: Varsha Engineer
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner (with husband Navin Engineer), Chemidex Pharma, Egham, Surrey
profile: Varsha Engineer and her husband Navin co-founded Chemidex in 1981 as a single pharmacy in Chertsey, Surrey. They grew it to 14 pharmacies, sold them to Celesio in 1999 (~GBP 12M), and turned Chemidex into a specialty pharma company acquiring and licensing prescription brands from 2000. The Sunday Times Rich List 2025 put the couple at GBP 3.45B.
interesting_fact: Chemidex started as one Chertsey pharmacy in 1981; after selling the chain in 1999 it bought its first drug brand in 2000 and became a billion-pound brand-licensing business.
deep_cut_fact: Navin (her co-founder husband) quit his first pharmacist job at Boots the same day an area manager asked him for a cup of tea while he was busy dispensing - the spark that led the couple to open their own pharmacy.
notes: Extremely private couple; no website (chemidex.co.uk down), no press office or social accounts found. Only public route is the company's registered office per Companies House (Chemidex Pharma Ltd, 01676110). Listed jointly with Navin Engineer; deep-cut fact is about Navin.

name: Hu Haiyang
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Semight Instruments (Suzhou; Shanghai STAR Market: 688808)
profile: Hu Haiyang (b. 1973) cofounded Semight Instruments in 2017 after ~15 years at Agilent/Keysight in China, and chairs it. Semight makes optical-module and semiconductor test gear (BERTs, burn-in systems, source-measure units) riding AI data-center demand for 800G/1.6T optics; it listed on the STAR Market in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Semight is the world's second company to offer a full suite of core testing instruments for 1.6T optical modules, the high-speed links used inside AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Hu earned a PhD in optical engineering from the CAS Shanghai Institute of Optics and Fine Mechanics in 2001, then joined Agilent (later Keysight) as an application engineer, rising to lab director and senior technical consultant before founding Semight.
notes: Technical founder; highly relevant to the data-center/AI optics angle. IR is handled by the board secretary's office (ir@semight.com, as published in the April 2026 listing announcement).

name: Chen Zhiping
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Smoore International Holdings (HKEX: 6969), Shenzhen
profile: Hunan-born (1975) founder of Smoore, the world's largest maker of vaping hardware (FEELM atomization tech, Vaporesso brand), supplying Japan Tobacco, BAT and NJOY. He joined the Shenzhen startup as a minority shareholder in 2007, led it to a 2020 Hong Kong IPO and has diversified into medical inhalation and beauty devices.
interesting_fact: Smoore's 2020 Hong Kong IPO raised more than $900 million and made Chen China's first vaping billionaire; at the 2021 peak his fortune was reported near 99 billion yuan.
deep_cut_fact: A Tongji University marketing graduate, he began as a salesman at a Shanghai tech firm after graduating in 1997 and later was a sales manager at Fudan Guanghua Information Technology; his first entrepreneurial venture, trading coal, failed before he turned to e-cigarettes.
notes: Extremely low-profile, almost never gives interviews. Vaping is regulation-sensitive; frame outreach around manufacturing/tech (atomization, medical inhalation). Route via Smoore IR.

name: Phillipe Foriel-Destezet
profile: Philippe Foriel-Destezet, founder of French staffing firm Ecco (merged with Adia in 1996 to form Adecco), died June 27, 2021, aged 85.
notes: Deceased (June 2021). Source: https://www.hec.edu/en/news-room/philippe-foriel-deste-zet-committed-visionary-and-entrepreneur ; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Foriel-Destezet

name: Mikail Shishkhanov
current_role: No current major corporate role found; former main shareholder and board chairman of B&N Bank (Binbank)
profile: Russian financier (b. 1972, Grozny) who was majority owner (~59%) of B&N Bank (Binbank) and Rost Bank and co-owned real-estate developer INTECO, with interests linked to oil via the family Safmar group. Forbes put him at $2.3bn in 2016-17. The Bank of Russia took over Binbank in Sept 2017 and he has since left business rankings.
interesting_fact: Holds a doctorate in economics and a PhD in law and is an associate member of the Russian Academy of Natural Sciences; a graduate of Peoples' Friendship University (1995).
deep_cut_fact: Lists chess and boxing as his hobbies.
notes: No longer a billionaire: lost his banks in the 2017 state takeover and a Moscow Region court declared him bankrupt in July 2023. Avoid referencing wealth/losses. No published contact found. Likely not a fit for UHNW outreach.

name: Viktor Nusenkis
current_role: Co-owner and chairman, Energo concern (coal trading); founder of the Donetsksteel group
profile: Viktor Nusenkis, born 1954 in Donetsk, is a mining engineer who founded the Energo concern in 1992, which became the largest coal trader in Ukraine, Russia and Kazakhstan. In 2000 he formed Donetsksteel (Donetsk Metallurgical Plant, coke plants, mines) and later bought coal mines in Russia's Kemerovo region; he is now described as a Russian businessman.
interesting_fact: He built a coal-trading business, Energo, founded in 1992, into the largest coal trader across Ukraine, Russia and Kazakhstan, and later expanded into steel, coke and Kuzbass coal mines.
deep_cut_fact: A Donetsk Polytechnic graduate, he started underground: he worked at the Batova mine in Makiivka and went on to run the Zhdanivska mine before founding Energo. He also funded the Church of the Epiphany in Kozelsk, Russia.
notes: Extremely low profile; no official website or published contact found. Caution: in 2015 Ukraine's SBU opened a criminal case alleging his coke plants financed the so-called DNR (per LB.ua). No recent news found, so his current status is unverified. Probably not a suitable podcast target.

name: Vyacheslav Kantor
current_role: President, European Jewish Congress; major shareholder of Russian fertilizer producer Acron
profile: Russian-born investor and trained scientist (Viatcheslav Moshe Kantor) whose fortune comes from controlling fertilizer maker Acron. He has led the European Jewish Congress since 2007. He stepped back in 2022 after UK sanctions and was re-elected for a fifth term in 2025 after his EU delisting. He funds Holocaust-remembrance and community-security programmes.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he founded the World Holocaust Forum. Its 2020 edition at Yad Vashem, co-hosted by Kantor for the 75th anniversary of Auschwitz's liberation, drew nearly 50 heads of state: the largest diplomatic gathering ever held in Israel.
deep_cut_fact: He is the president of MAGMA, the Museum of Avant-Garde Mastery: a private Moscow museum founded in 2001 on his own collection of 20th-century art (Chagall, Soutine, El Lissitzky, Kabakov). Its first public showing was a 2009 exhibition in Geneva.
notes: Sanctions-sensitive: the UK has sanctioned him since 2022 over Acron. The EU and Switzerland delisted him in March 2025, and Poland then imposed national sanctions. Check compliance before engaging. Best route is the EJC office in Brussels; the EJC bio has the fullest account of his philanthropy.

name: Paul Desmarais Jr
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Power Corporation of Canada and Power Financial
profile: Paul Desmarais Jr. (b. 1954, Sudbury), eldest son of Power Corp builder Paul Desmarais Sr., joined Power in 1981, led the 1984 creation of Power Financial and was chairman and co-CEO of Power Corp 1996-2020. He remains chairman, overseeing a group spanning Great-West Lifeco, IGM, GBL and alternative-asset platforms Sagard and Power Sustainable. (Input name misspelled 'Demarais'.)
interesting_fact: Beyond finance he has sat on energy-industry boards: a director of GDF Suez (2008-2014) and of Total until 2017, and vice-chairman of Imerys (1998-2008).
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he started out at S.G. Warburg in London and Standard Brands in New York; and in 2014 he joined a True Patriot Love ski expedition to the North Magnetic Pole raising money for Canadian military families.

public_contacts.value: Stéphane Lemay, VP General Counsel & Secretary (Power Corp media contact), 514-286-7400

notes: Input spells name 'Demarais'; correct is Desmarais. Power Corp named James O'Sullivan CEO effective July 1, 2026 (Jeffrey Orr to vice-chair); Desmarais Jr. remains chairman. Data-center angle: May 2026 Power Corp release on a joint investment in a Sagard AI fund. Route via corporate media contact.

name: Jyoti Bansal
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Harness (AI software delivery platform); co-founder, Unusual Ventures and BIG Labs
profile: Grew up in a small Rajasthan town helping his father's farm-equipment business, studied computer science at IIT Delhi, and moved to Silicon Valley in 2000. Founded AppDynamics (2008), sold to Cisco for $3.7B in 2017 a day before its IPO; then founded Harness, which merged with his security startup Traceable in 2025 and was valued at $5.5B in a $240M Series E (Dec 2025).
interesting_fact: He says he fell in love with entrepreneurship after Bill Gates visited IIT Delhi while he was a student; he also waited about seven years on a work visa for a green card before he could start his own company.
deep_cut_fact: Before AppDynamics he led design and architecture for several products at Wily Technology, the Java performance-diagnostics pioneer later bought by Computer Associates for $375M, and earlier held senior engineering roles at Datasweep (bought by Rockwell Automation) and netLens.
notes: Very accessible founder-CEO; frequent podcast/conference speaker on DevOps, AI agents and immigration/green-card issues. Harness press team (press@harness.io) is the cleanest route.

name: B. Wayne Hughes Jr
current_role: Founder, American Commercial Equities (real estate); founder of Serving USA and the Hughes Charitable Foundation (Jackson, Wyoming)
profile: Son of Public Storage co-founder B. Wayne Hughes (d. 2021), he worked at Public Storage from 1983 for nearly two decades (VP acquisitions 1992-2002) and sat on its board until late 2020. In 2005 he launched American Commercial Equities, which owns property in Hawaii and California; he now focuses largely on philanthropy from Wyoming.
interesting_fact: His Hughes Charitable Foundation focuses on education, at-risk youth, and food and housing insecurity in his home state of Wyoming; he is a USC graduate.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Serving USA, which funds Christ-centered nonprofits serving prisoners, women in recovery and military veterans, including prison-ministry and urban ministry training partners such as TUMI.
notes: Private; philanthropy (prison re-entry, veterans, Wyoming) is the warmest hook. Not an obvious energy/data-center guest.

name: Manuel Villar
current_role: Chairman, Vista Land & Lifescapes and Villar Land Holdings; president of the Nacionalista Party
profile: Born in 1949 in Tondo, Manila, Manny Villar went from selling seafood with his mother to building the Philippines' largest homebuilder, Vista Land, now run by his son Paolo. He also controls mall operator Vistamalls, VistaREIT, AllHome, AllDay Marts and Premiere Island Power REIT, and is building the 3,500-hectare Villar City south of Manila. A former House speaker and Senate president.
interesting_fact: He started his business in 1975 delivering sand and gravel in Las Piñas with two reconditioned trucks. The firm later expanded into building and selling homes.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he was an accountant at SGV & Co. and then a financial analyst at the Private Development Corporation of the Philippines, where he sold World Bank loans. He holds a BBA (1970) and an MBA (1973) from UP Diliman.
notes: High public profile as a politician. Children Mark and Camille are senators; avoid. Premiere Island Power REIT (solar assets) is relevant to the energy theme. Vista Land and his own site blocked automated fetching, so no published press email was verified; Vista Land investor relations is the likely route. Named in Forbes Asia Heroes of Philanthropy 2024.

name: Bent Jensen
current_role: Owner and CEO, LINAK A/S (Nordborg, Denmark), per Forbes 2026
profile: Bent Jensen, a mechanical engineer, took over his grandfather's 1907 blacksmith business, Christian Jensen & Sons, in 1976. He reinvented it around the electric linear actuator, renaming it LINAK in 1984. The family-owned company now makes actuators for hospital beds, height-adjustable desks, furniture and industrial uses, with factories in Denmark, the US, China and Slovakia.
interesting_fact: LINAK is short for 'Lineær Aktuator'. The company kept a significant share of its production in Denmark by investing heavily in automation and robotics.
deep_cut_fact: In 1979, as a newly graduated engineer, he came up with the electric linear actuator while talking with a friend from his student days who had a disability and needed a way to adjust his wheelchair. That conversation is the origin of today's LINAK.

public_contacts.value: bsp@linak.com (Birgit Spek, PA to the CEO, press and media enquiries)

notes: Strong engineer-founder story with a manufacturing and automation angle. Conveniently, the published press contact is the CEO's PA.

name: Matthew Roszak
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Bloq (Chicago blockchain infrastructure company)
profile: Chicago-based venture capitalist (Lake Forest College, 1995) who worked in VC and as an entrepreneur in the 1990s-2000s, began building a crypto portfolio in 2012, and co-founded Bloq, which provides blockchain infrastructure, digital-asset custody consulting for banks and stablecoin transaction services.
interesting_fact: He co-led an initiative to give every member of the US Congress $50 worth of digital assets so lawmakers could experience crypto firsthand; some accepted.
notes: Bloq's website blocked automated access and web search budget ran out, so no verified contact or deep-cut fact. Bloq's own site or press page is the likely route. Avoid the 2006 SEC settlement (Blue Rhino) in outreach. Bloq's crypto/Bitcoin mining-adjacent infrastructure could tie into energy/data-center themes.

name: Ho Hung Anh
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Techcombank (Vietnam Technological and Commercial Joint Stock Bank)
profile: Hanoi-born (1970) businessman who, with long-time partner Nguyen Dang Quang, started out trading goods between Eastern Europe and Vietnam in the 1990s, then invested in Techcombank from 1995 and took control in 2006. Chairman since 2008, he co-controls Techcombank and Masan Group via Masan JSC; Techcom Securities and Masan Consumer both listed in Ho Chi Minh City in late 2025.
interesting_fact: Ho and fellow billionaire Nguyen Dang Quang met as students in the former Soviet Union and have been intertwined business partners ever since, jointly controlling both Masan Group and Techcombank.
deep_cut_fact: He was selected by Vietnam's Ministry of Defence to study radar engineering in Kyiv after a year at the Military Technical Academy; when the USSR collapsed he stayed and graduated in electrical engineering from Kyiv Polytechnic, then ran SANMEX and Masan Rus Trading in Russia (1994-2004).
notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Route via Techcombank IR/communications. No published press email retrieved from site.

name: Chen Jinxia
current_role: Controlling shareholder/chair of Hunan Yongjin Group (investment holding)
profile: Shanghai University of Finance & Economics graduate who inherited control of Hunan Yongjin Group, the investment group founded by her late husband, entrepreneur Wei Dong, in 2008. Yongjin holds stakes in drug makers and financial businesses; Forbes and Hurun have listed her as a billionaire since 2008-2010.
interesting_fact: Graduate of Shanghai University of Finance & Economics; has appeared on Hurun's self-made women list since 2017 despite inheriting the core business.
notes: Identity marked uncertain only because the input's SEC field ('Sea Ltd - CPO, Shopee') almost certainly belongs to a different person with a similar romanized name - do not use it. The Forbes billionaire is the Yongjin heir. Extremely private; husband's death is a sensitive topic - avoid. No published contact found; web search budget exhausted.

name: Leonard Abess
current_role: Head of ThinkLab Ventures (Miami real-estate finance and investments); University of Miami trustee
profile: Miami banker (born 1948, Wharton graduate) who became majority owner and chairman of City National Bank of Florida in 1984. The bank his father co-founded in 1946 had about $400m in assets then; he grew it to about $2.75bn and sold his 83% stake to Caja Madrid in 2008 for $927m. He now invests via ThinkLab Ventures, owns about 4,000 acres in Miami and Vermont (some growing limes), and holds a stake in Jersey Jack Pinball.
interesting_fact: He shared $60m of the sale proceeds with 399 current and 72 former employees. President Obama praised him in his February 2009 address to Congress, and Time named him to the 2009 Time 100.
deep_cut_fact: He started at City National Bank in its print shop. With his wife he founded a floating research station in the Brazilian Amazon, and in 2006 he gave $5m to create the University of Miami's Abess Center for Ecosystem Science and Policy.
notes: I found no published contact; thinklabventures.com is a parked domain. Possible routes are the University of Miami Abess Center (he chaired UM's board 2011-2014) or Jersey Jack Pinball. Low media profile since 2009.

name: Inder Jaisinghani
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Polycab India Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Mumbai entrepreneur who, with his brothers, grew the family's small electrical-goods shop in Lohar Chawl into Polycab India, the country's largest wires-and-cables maker. Polycab added fans, LED lighting, switches and switchgear from 2014, listed in 2019, and runs 28 plants exporting to 79 countries. The World Bank's IFC took a stake in 2008.
interesting_fact: Polycab grew from a trading firm started in 1986 into a listed manufacturer with 28 plants across India selling to 79 countries, supplying the cables behind India's power, infrastructure and data-centre build-out.
deep_cut_fact: Before Polycab became an industrial giant, the Jaisinghani brothers began their first wire-manufacturing experiments in a garage of about 100 square feet in Mumbai, while still running the family's electrical shop in Lohar Chawl.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit (power cables, grid and data-centre electrification). Low media profile. Polycab IR is the best published route. Deep-cut detail comes from YourStory (blocked to direct fetch) and was corroborated in search snippets from several Indian outlets, including DNA India.

name: Mika Anttonen
current_role: Founder, principal owner and Chairman of the Board, St1 (St1 Oy, formerly St1 Nordic Oy), Finland
profile: Finnish engineer who started as a crude-oil trader at Neste in the early 1990s, founded Greenergy Baltic in 1995 and renamed it St1 in 2005, building it into a Nordic fuel retailer and refiner (incl. Gothenburg refinery). He stepped back from operations to focus on strategy, using fossil-fuel profits to fund renewables: waste-based ethanol, wind, biogas, carbon sinks and deep geothermal.
interesting_fact: St1 drilled two wells roughly 6-7 km deep in Otaniemi, Espoo, to harvest geothermal heat for district heating, one of the deepest such projects in the world. He also plays hockey and is a New York Rangers fan.
deep_cut_fact: He has a Master's in engineering and likes to say 'I is a bad pronoun. We is much better.' He has argued that educating girls and women in developing nations would be the single most significant climate action (Aalto University interview, 2018).
notes: Press email is St1's published Communications Manager, Finland. Outspoken on climate policy (favours regulation, short-haul flight bans on rail routes); a natural podcast guest on energy transition from an oil-company owner's perspective. St1 Nordic renamed St1 Oy on 1 June 2026.

name: Wee Ee Lim
current_role: President & CEO, Haw Par Corporation (Tiger Balm); Chairman, UOL Group and Singapore Land Group; Director, United Overseas Bank
profile: Wee Ee Lim (64), son of late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw, joined Tiger Balm maker Haw Par in 1986 and has been its president and CEO since 2003. After his father's death he became chairman of property developer UOL Group (2024) and Singapore Land Group, and sits on UOB's board; his wealth includes his share of the family stakes inherited in 2025.
interesting_fact: He has run Haw Par, owner of the century-old Tiger Balm ointment brand, for over two decades, while also chairing two listed property groups and serving on the board of UOB, one of Singapore's three big banks.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics in the U.S. at Clark University in Worcester, Massachusetts (BA Economics), and joined Haw Par's board in 1994, nine years before becoming CEO.
notes: Low-key; rarely interviewed. He is also a director of the family's Wee Foundation. UOL site blocked automated access; UOL's corporate communications contact is listed on uol.com.sg.

name: Lin Lairong
current_role: Director and controlling shareholder (actual controller, with Lin's wife An Sumei), Dazhong Mining (Shenzhen: 001203); Chairman, Zhongxing Group
profile: Born in 1968, Lin founded Wuhai Zhongxing Coal in 1995 and in 1999 founded Dazhong Mining, an iron-ore miner and pellet producer based in Baotou, Inner Mongolia. He chaired Dazhong from 2009 to 2016, and it listed in Shenzhen in 2021. Dazhong is now pushing into lithium, with lepidolite and spodumene projects in Hunan and Sichuan and a planned lithium-metal battery-materials plant.
interesting_fact: His iron-ore company has pivoted into battery materials. It is developing lithium mines in Linwu, Hunan and Jiada, Sichuan and plans a 1bn-yuan lithium-metal plant for solid-state batteries.
deep_cut_fact: Lin's formal education was at a technical school, Shanxi Datong Coal School (1984-86). He started in coal at age 27 and was named one of Wuhai's 'Top 10 Outstanding Young Entrepreneurs'.
notes: Very low profile, and Chinese-language outreach will be needed. The current Dazhong chairman is Niu Guofeng, who may be the more accessible spokesperson. The lithium pivot is a good hook for an energy podcast.

name: Roberto Sallouti
current_role: CEO, Banco BTG Pactual; partner of BTG Pactual Holding (São Paulo)
profile: Roberto Balls Sallouti has been at BTG Pactual since 1994 and is now CEO of the bank and a partner in BTG Pactual Holding, Latin America's largest investment bank, which runs as a meritocratic partnership. His partnership stake made him a Forbes billionaire in 2026. He also founded BTG Investments LP.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Inteli (Instituto de Tecnologia e Liderança), a nonprofit technology and leadership college in São Paulo, with fellow BTG billionaire André Esteves.
deep_cut_fact: He was part of the group that created an endowment fund and a new governance model that rescued the São Paulo Museum of Art (MASP) from bankruptcy.
notes: New to the Forbes list in 2026. BTG's IR email is the published institutional route; Inteli is a softer route on the tech and education angle. BTG is active in energy and infrastructure in Brazil.

name: Pan Weiming
current_role: Chairman, Fullsun Group (construction and property development, Guangdong), per Forbes; current status not verified
profile: Pan Weiming (潘伟明) quit his post as a magistrate in Conghua, Guangdong in 1993 and started his first property company with his brother. He went on to chair Fullsun Group, whose main businesses are construction and property development. He dropped off the Forbes and Hurun lists after 2019-2020.
interesting_fact: He was a local government magistrate in Conghua (Guangzhou) before leaving public service in 1993 to become a property developer.
notes: Off the rich lists since 2020; current role and wealth unverified. Web search quota ran out before Chinese-language sources could be checked. No published contact found. Low priority.

name: Alfred West Jr
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, SEI Investments (retired as executive chairman and left the board 1 Jan 2026)
profile: Founded SEI (Simulated Environments Inc.) in 1968, beginning with a computer simulation to train bank loan officers. He took it public in 1981 and grew it into a fintech, investment-processing and asset-management firm that manages, advises or administers about $1.8-2.1 trillion. He was CEO for 54 years until 2022, then executive chairman, and became chairman emeritus in January 2026.
interesting_fact: He wanted to be a fighter pilot and studied aerospace engineering at Georgia Tech, but poor eyesight kept him from flying, so he took a Wharton MBA and launched SEI instead.
deep_cut_fact: SEI's first product was the industry's first computer-based commercial credit simulator. In the 1970s it pivoted to an automated trust-accounting system that became TRUST 3000, the platform behind its move into fintech.
notes: Recently retired (Dec 2025 announcement), so a 'founder's 57-year journey' angle is timely. The SEI media contact is the most practical route.

name: Li Rucheng
current_role: Founder, Youngor Group (Ningbo); stepped down as chairman of listed Youngor in May 2026, remaining an adviser
profile: Born 1951 in Shanghai with Ningbo roots, Li spent 15 years as a sent-down youth before joining Ningbo's small collective Qingchun garment workshop in 1981, becoming its chief in 1982. In 1990 he formed a joint venture with Macau's Nanguang that became Youngor, a leading Chinese menswear maker that expanded into property and finance. He handed over the chair in May 2026, saying he would 'pass the baton but not retire'.
interesting_fact: He has been a deputy to China's National People's Congress for Zhejiang since 2008.
deep_cut_fact: His first clothing brand at the tiny Qingchun workshop was 'Beilungang' (named after Ningbo's Beilun port); its success put the factory on a firm footing years before the Youngor name existed. He has often called himself a 'farmer' after his years in the countryside.
notes: Leadership passed to a family successor at the May 2026 AGM (per Beijing News, https://www.bjnews.com.cn/detail/1779526038169838.html). Aged 75; Chinese-language outreach via Youngor corporate is the only route found.

name: Valery Kogan
current_role: Former chairman of the supervisory board, Moscow Domodedovo Airport (no current role; airport nationalised in 2025)
profile: Valery Kogan was a co-owner and long-time supervisory-board chairman of Moscow's Domodedovo Airport alongside main owner Dmitry Kamenshchik. In 2025 a Russian court transferred the airport's holding company to the state, and in early 2026 it was sold to a Sheremetyevo subsidiary; he no longer appears on billionaire lists.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: subject of 2025 nationalisation proceedings, asset freezes and a Russian travel ban (zona.media 27 Oct 2025, https://zona.media/news/2025/10/27/airport). No public contact. Recommend skipping.

name: Noam Gottesman
current_role: Co-founder and Director (co-chairman) of Nomad Foods; CEO of TOMS Capital (family investment office)
profile: Columbia graduate (1986) and former Goldman Sachs London executive director. In 1995 he co-founded hedge fund GLG Partners, which listed in 2007 and was sold to Man Group for $1.6B in 2010. In 2014 he co-founded Nomad Foods (Birds Eye, Iglo, Findus), now Europe's largest frozen-food company. He invests through TOMS Capital and owns about 200 Burger King franchises.
interesting_fact: He invested in Eleven Madison Park in 2011, and six years later it was named the best restaurant in the world. He also backed Shuko, which New York Magazine voted the city's best sushi.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from a family of art collectors; his father Dov Gottesman was president of the Israel Museum. ARTnews ranks him among the world's top 200 collectors, with works by Bacon, Freud and Warhol, and he sits on the Tate Foundation board and is a Columbia University trustee.
notes: Low public profile, with few interviews. Best route is Nomad Foods media or IR, or through TOMS Capital (no verified website found). The restaurant and art interests make good warm hooks.

name: Ed Craven
current_role: Cofounder of Stake.com and Kick; director, Easygo group (Melbourne); majority investor in AI company Maincode
profile: Melbourne-born (1995) cofounder, with Bijan Tehrani, of Stake.com, believed to be the world's largest crypto casino, with $4.7B gross revenue in 2024. They began with the crypto dice game Primedice in 2013, launched Stake in 2017 and in 2022 started Kick, a streaming rival to Twitch that gives creators a 95/5 revenue split.
interesting_fact: Craven and Tehrani met online as teenagers playing RuneScape. The name 'Stake' comes from the game's controversial 'staking' mechanic.
deep_cut_fact: He is the majority backer of Melbourne-based Maincode, which aims to build a sovereign Australian large language model, often described as 'Australia's answer to OpenAI'. That makes him a quiet player in local AI compute.
notes: He livestreams his own gameplay on Kick, which is his most public channel. No published press email or verified personal social handle was confirmed before the search budget ran out. The Maincode/AI angle fits the data-center theme better than gambling.

name: Han Arming Hanafia
current_role: Co-founder and minority shareholder, PT DCI Indonesia Tbk (data centers)
profile: Han Arming Hanafia co-founded DCI Indonesia in 2011 with Otto Toto Sugiri and Marina Budiman. It is now one of Indonesia's largest data-center operators, and its stock has soared since listing. He holds a minority stake and sold his shares in listed ISP Indonet (Indointernet) in 2023.
interesting_fact: He is one of three co-founders (with Otto Toto Sugiri and Marina Budiman) whose 2011 bet on Indonesian data centers turned each of them into a billionaire.
notes: Extremely low public profile; found no interviews or bios. Alive status not confirmed by a dated source, but he still appears on the 2026 Forbes real-time list. The 'connect@' and 'corpsec@' addresses are DCI company contacts, not his own. DCI has warned publicly about scammers impersonating its directors and commissioners.

name: Manfredi Lefebvre d'Ovidio
current_role: President, Heritage Group (Monaco); Executive Chairman, Abercrombie & Kent Travel Group; Chair, World Travel & Tourism Council (since Sept 2025)
profile: Rome-born, Monaco-based travel magnate who ran his father's Silversea Cruises from 2001, grew it to 12 ships and sold it to Royal Caribbean in 2018-2020 for ~$1.25bn. Then bought 85% of Abercrombie & Kent (2019) and added Crystal Cruises, Cox & Kings and Ecoventura; also backed quantum-encryption firm Arqit and chairs the WTTC.
interesting_fact: Since January 2024 he has been the Sovereign Order of Malta's Ambassador at Large for Culture and Philanthropy and its Permanent Observer to UNESCO.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Silversea, in the 1980s he and his father, Professor Antonio Lefebvre d'Ovidio, bought Sitmar Cruises and built three cruise ships before selling the line to P&O Princess. He also studied law in Rome but left before taking his degree.

public_contacts.value: jtreacy@abercrombiekent.com (James Treacy, Global Communications Director, A&K)
JFawcett@abercrombiekent.com (Jean Fawcett, Senior Manager, Media Relations, A&K)

notes: Frequent conference speaker (WTTC, Skift Forum); approachable via A&K global communications. Arqit stake gives a tech angle.

name: Constantinos Martinos
current_role: Owner/principal, Thenamaris (Athens); the company is now run day to day by his son Nikolas
profile: Greek shipowner known as 'Dinos' (b. 1953, Glyfada). He co-founded Thenamaris in the early 1970s with his mother Athina, one of Greece's first female shipowners, and his brothers. After the brothers split off in 1990 and 1998 he kept Thenamaris, which now runs a fleet of about 90 tankers, bulkers, container ships and LNG carriers.
interesting_fact: He is a serious, low-profile art collector whose holdings include works by Picasso, Twombly, Basquiat and Warhol. Greek press dubbed him the 'invisible collector'.
deep_cut_fact: The Martinos family funded a new €10m building with 115 hospital beds at Asklipieio General Hospital in Voula, near Athens. In 2011 Lloyd's List ranked him No. 67 among the 100 most influential people in shipping.
notes: Very private. Son Nikolas Martinos runs Thenamaris, including an LNG-carrier arm (Thenamaris LNG), which could be an energy angle. The best route is Thenamaris corporate communications.

name: Luis Enrique Yarur Rey
current_role: Board member, Banco de Crédito e Inversiones (BCI), City National Bank of Florida and Empresas JY; Chairman, Empresas Jordan and MAS Analytics. He chaired BCI 1991–2024.
profile: A lawyer by training, Yarur joined family-founded BCI in 1975, served 11 years as general manager and chaired it from 1991 until stepping down on 31 Dec 2024; his son Ignacio succeeded him. Under him, BCI expanded into Florida with City National Bank (2015), TotalBank and Executive National Bank, and reportedly grew profits 58-fold. He pushed a decade-long digital transformation.
interesting_fact: In 1994 he and his brothers took control of BCI by buying a 34% stake from their uncle Jorge Yarur Banna's estate. BCI's 2015 purchase of City National Bank of Florida was the first acquisition of a US bank by a Chilean bank.
deep_cut_fact: Even after leaving the BCI chair he kept the chairmanship of MAS Analytics, a Chilean data-analytics and AI consultancy. He also sits on the boards of Fundación Enseña Chile (Teach for Chile) and Chile Mujeres.
notes: No longer BCI chairman (since Jan 2025); the Forbes bio is out of date. MAS Analytics (masanalytics.cl) is a data/AI angle for the podcast. No press email was found on BCI pages fetched by script.

name: Clayton Zekelman
current_role: Co-owner, Zekelman Industries; owner/president of Windsor ISP MNSi Telecom (Managed Network Systems) and Nexicom
profile: One of three brothers (with Barry and Alan) who split ownership of Zekelman Industries, one of North America's largest steel pipe and tube makers (Atlas Tube, Wheatland Tube), which they sold to Carlyle in 2006 and bought back in 2011. Clayton, a former Atlas Tube Canada VP, focuses on telecom: he runs Windsor fibre ISP MNSi and bought Central Ontario's Nexicom in 2016.
interesting_fact: Beyond steel, he built his own telecom business: MNSi, Windsor's local ISP since 1995, committed ~$35M to a 1 Gbps fibre network; 'We want to build our own networks so we're not forced to rely on the incumbent networks,' he told CBC.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he bought Nexicom, a Millbrook/Kawarthas, Ontario telecom that the Downs family had owned for 75 years, keeping it as a separate company rather than merging it into MNSi.
notes: Low profile; brother Barry is Zekelman Industries' public face (chairman/CEO). Clayton's ISP/fibre and network-operator background is a strong fit for a data-centre/infrastructure podcast. Zekelman family are notable donors to St. Clair College and University of Windsor.

name: Per Sandberg
current_role: Owner (with his three sons) of Sandberg Development, Malmö; major shareholder of Camurus (~30%) and sole owner of Aimpoint
profile: Per Gunnar Sandberg inherited and consolidated the holdings of his father, entrepreneur Gunnar Sandberg, buying out his siblings. His family investment company Sandberg Development (founded 1959, formerly GS Development) owns red-dot-sight leader Aimpoint and ~20 tech companies focused on water, safety and quality of life, plus a large stake in Lund-based opioid-dependency drug developer Camurus, whose value has soared.
interesting_fact: Sandberg Development grew from 3 portfolio companies (SEK 798m turnover) in 2015 to 19 companies and SEK 5.9bn turnover in 2025, run from 'Sandberg Valley', an innovation neighbourhood it built at Jägersro in Malmö.
deep_cut_fact: In 2025 Sandberg Development and Mellby Gård's FMG Circular Invest launched a Water Innovation Challenge; the winner, SWARD, makes an energy-efficient sensor for real-time groundwater monitoring. The group also made a multi-million donation to Gunilla Westergren-Thorsson's COPD research.

public_contacts.value: lina.robekk.olsen@sbdev.com (Chief Corporate Affairs Officer, published as '(a) SBDEV.COM')

notes: Described as a 'doldis' (keeps out of the limelight); declined an Affärsvärlden interview. CEO Stefan Persson is the public face. Water-tech focus could fit an energy/infrastructure episode.

name: Bill Malhotra
current_role: Founder and CEO, Claridge Homes (Ottawa)
profile: India-born civil engineer who moved to Canada in 1971 and was the City of Ottawa's chief structural engineer (1977-86) before founding Claridge Homes in 1986. Claridge has built 14,000+ homes, condos and rentals, including Ottawa's tallest tower, and is developing in South Florida.
interesting_fact: Claridge's 469-foot Claridge Icon tower is the tallest building in Ottawa.
deep_cut_fact: He named his company after The Claridges, a luxury hotel in New Delhi he used to visit as a child with his father; before going into development he spent nine years as the City of Ottawa's chief structural engineer.
notes: Private, family-run company (sons Neil and Shawn are minority owners); rarely gives national interviews. Route via Claridge Homes head office (505 Preston St, Ottawa; main line published on site). Engineer-turned-developer story fits an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Lin Huiying
current_role: Chairman and 49% owner, Biel Crystal Manufactory (Hong Kong)
profile: Lin Huiying (Cantonese: Lam Wai-ying, 林慧英) co-owns Biel Crystal with husband and founder Yeung Kin-man (51%). Biel makes smartphone cover glass for Apple and Samsung, employs ~90,000 and has filed twice for a Hong Kong IPO since 2021. Hurun ranks her among the richest self-made women.
interesting_fact: Biel Crystal makes the cover glass for smartphones from Apple and Samsung; Forbes reported the couple had Hong Kong's biggest wealth gain in 2021.
notes: Very private couple; no interviews or published press contact found (company site returned no content; web search budget exhausted). Route via Biel Crystal corporate office / IPO prospectus contacts on HKEX if needed.

name: Nicholas Pritzker II
current_role: Investor (Tao Capital); chairman, Libra Foundation; former chairman/CEO, Hyatt Development Corporation
profile: Nicholas J. Pritzker (b. 1945), of Chicago's Pritzker family, led Hyatt's hotel development for decades and sat on its board from 1980 to 2007. Now in Marin County, California, he has sold most of his Hyatt stock and invests via Tao Capital (early in Juul and Twist Bioscience) and in clean energy and criminal-justice causes.
interesting_fact: He co-founded and co-chairs Clean Energy Trust, which backs early-stage clean-energy startups in the Midwest, and was vice chairman of Conservation International.
deep_cut_fact: Before law school at the University of Chicago he studied at Reed College, Lake Forest College and the London Film School.
notes: He is 81 and private. The clean-energy angle (Clean Energy Trust) fits the podcast well. Wikipedia names him chairman of the Libra Foundation, but its site doesn't mention him. The Tao Capital site (taocap.com) is private, and taocapital.com is a different Asian firm, so don't use it. His Juul board seat is sensitive; avoid it.

name: Hans Jakob Limbach
current_role: Founder and owner, Limbach Gruppe (Limbach Verwaltungs SE), Heidelberg
profile: Physician and founder of the Limbach Group, Germany's largest owner-managed medical laboratory group. It grew from a single Heidelberg lab (MVZ Dr. Limbach und Kollegen, founded 1979) into a network of about 50 labs, largely through acquisitions of smaller independent labs since 2012. It has 6,000+ employees and roughly EUR 1.2bn in revenue (2020), and also runs food, water and environmental testing under Limbach Analytics.
interesting_fact: The group's revenue jumped to about EUR 1.2bn in 2020 on the back of COVID testing, making it one of Germany's largest diagnostics businesses while remaining family-owned.
notes: Very private; little personal coverage in English. No sourced deep-cut fact was found, because the web-search budget ran out. Alive status is inferred from his presence on Forbes real-time 2026. German-language outreach via the group's head office is recommended.

name: Pierre van der Mersch
current_role: Honorary President, Brederode SA (Euronext Brussels/Luxembourg-listed investment company); family is reference shareholder
profile: Belgian investor dubbed the 'Belgian Warren Buffett', who started as a bank clerk in 1958 and from 1970 built Brederode by taking control of end-of-life listed shell companies. Brederode now invests mainly in private equity funds plus listed equities; day-to-day management passed in 2026 to family member Dimitri van der Mersch and Nicolas-Louis Pinon.
interesting_fact: He built Brederode over more than 40 years by acquiring six end-of-life listed companies with unhappy shareholders and easily saleable assets, recycling them into long-term investments.
deep_cut_fact: Brederode's cornerstone, acquired in 1970, was Auximines (Compagnie Auxiliaire des Mines), an 1899 Brussels firm whose patented rechargeable dry battery powered Belgian coal miners' portable safety lamps until the mines closed.
notes: Of advanced age (career began 1958); honorary role only. Son-in-law Luigi Santambrogio stepped down as managing director in May 2026; Dimitri and Axel van der Mersch now on the board. Route via Brederode's company email. Exact family relation of Dimitri not verified.

name: Huang Shan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Fortune Trend Technology Co. (688318.SH, maker of TDX/Tongdaxin trading software)
profile: Huang Shan, a Wuhan University graduate (b. c.1962), has run the Tongdaxin (TDX) family of financial-software companies since the mid-1990s. He has chaired Shenzhen Fortune Trend since 2010. Its TDX market-data and trading terminal is used by most Chinese brokerages. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020 and his fortune comes from his controlling stake.
interesting_fact: Fortune Trend's Tongdaxin software is reported to be used by more than 90% of China's securities firms, so much of Chinese retail stock trading runs on a terminal his company built.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1995 as GM of Shenzhen Tongdaxin Communication Electronics, and he went on to run Tongdaxin entities in Wuhan, Shanghai and Beijing. In 2025 Fortune Trend's board approved a RMB 10 million donation to his alma mater, Wuhan University.
