name: Stephen Rubin
current_role: Chairman, Pentland Group (family-owned; brands incl. Speedo, Berghaus, Canterbury, ellesse; large stake in JD Sports Fashion)
profile: Robert Stephen Rubin CBE (b. Dec 1937) joined his immigrant parents' Liverpool Shoe Company after UCL law, became chairman in 1969 and built it (renamed Pentland in 1973) into a major UK sports-brand group. His legendary 1981 bet, $77,500 for 55% of Reebok USA, sold for ~$770m in 1991. Son Andy Rubin now leads the business day to day.
interesting_fact: Pentland paid $77,500 for 55% of Reebok USA in 1981; by 1983/84 Reebok was 70% of Pentland's turnover, and the stake was sold in 1991 for about $770m.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he planned to be a barrister (UCL law, 1958) and at 21 stood unsuccessfully as the Liberal Party candidate for Streatham in the 1959 general election.
notes: Aged ~88; very private. Pentland's contact form has a 'Media Enquiries' topic. Pentland funds the Pentland Centre for Sustainability in Business at Lancaster University (possible sustainability angle). Honour is now CBE (Forbes says OBE).

name: Cai Jianyong
current_role: Chairman and Executive Director (also General Manager/CEO), Lygend Resources & Technology (HKEX: 2245), Ningbo
profile: Cai Jianyong founded Ningbo-based Lygend in 2009 after nearly a decade in commodities trading, and built it into a nickel supplier spanning ore trading and smelting. With Indonesian partner Harita it runs HPAL and RKEF smelters on Obi Island that make battery-grade nickel for EVs. Lygend listed in Hong Kong in Nov 2022; 2025 revenue rose 37.7% to RMB 40.2bn.
interesting_fact: Lygend's Obi Island HPAL plant was among the first in Indonesia to ship EV-battery-grade nickel sulfate, and in Jan 2026 it formed a JV to build an HPAL slag-treatment plant on the island.
deep_cut_fact: A Shanghai Institute of Building Materials Industry graduate, he closed his ESG-report chairman's letter with the line that Lygend would use 'responsibility as our vessel and innovation as our paddle' to navigate the global tide of sustainable development.
notes: Strong energy/battery-materials angle (Indonesian nickel for EV batteries). Low personal media profile. 2025 results: https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0331/2026033104229.pdf

name: Sergei Studennikov
current_role: Founder of Krasnoye & Beloye (Red & White); co-owner (with wife, ~49%) of Mercury Retail Group (Krasnoye & Beloye, Bristol, Dixy)
profile: Born in 1967 in Stavropol Krai and raised in Chelyabinsk Oblast, Studennikov founded the SPS holding distributing vodka, beer and tobacco in the late 1980s/90s, then opened the first Krasnoye & Beloye store in Kopeysk in 2006. In 2019 he merged it with Bristol and Dixy (Kesaev/Katsiev) into Mercury Retail, Russia's largest alcohol retailer with ~15,000+ stores; its IPO was shelved in 2022.
interesting_fact: Krasnoye & Beloye grew from a single store in Kopeysk in 2006 to about 6,700 stores by 2018 and is now Russia's largest liquor retailer.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail, he graduated from the Satka mining and ceramics technical school and worked in that trade; in 1998 he opened a large tile store, and he also helped launch the Evrograd DIY chain and the Monetka grocery chain.
notes: Very private; gave a rare major interview to RBC in Nov 2024. Russia-based alcohol retailer: consider sanctions/reputational context before outreach. No published personal or office contacts found.

name: Catherine Phillips
current_role: Co-founder and co-funder (with husband John Phillips), Northpine Foundation (Canada); retired psychologist
profile: Toronto-area psychologist (EdD, C.Psych) who specialised in helping cancer patients manage stress, leading relaxation/support groups at Wellspring and the Healing Journey program. She and husband John Phillips were early Shopify investors (~2% combined; John was on Shopify's board 2010-2023). Since 2021 their Northpine Foundation has committed about C$290M to 300+ ventures for under-served Canadians.
interesting_fact: In a May 2026 founders' letter, she and John wrote that after donating $130M to 100+ ventures they 'were not as good as we hoped at investing impactfully' and re-tooled Northpine to measure 'social ROI' - cost per person moved from precarity to stable, taxpaying life.
deep_cut_fact: Before Shopify wealth, she was a health contributor to Chatelaine magazine and wrote 'Calm Your Mind and Warm Your Heart' (2011; 2013 edition subtitled real voices and techniques for cancer), drawn from 15+ years leading the Healing Journey program for people with cancer.
notes: Goes by Cathy. Low public profile; best route is the Northpine contact form (media-request category). Staff emails on the About page are for grantees - not appropriate for this outreach. Shopify/early-investor story is the entrepreneurship hook.

name: John Phillips
current_role: Angel investor; co-funder (with wife Cathy Phillips) of The Northpine Foundation; former Shopify director (2010-2023)
profile: A Toronto lawyer for 25 years (including as general counsel of Clearnet Communications), he became Shopify's first angel investor in 2007, one of the most lucrative angel bets in Canadian history. He served on Shopify's board from 2010 to 2023. He and Cathy now fund The Northpine Foundation, a venture-philanthropy vehicle focused on climate, refugees and people leaving prison.
interesting_fact: He heard about Shopify through a friend in 2007 and invested $250,000 at a $3m valuation. The stake (about 2% of Shopify) made the couple billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: The couple's philanthropy is channelled through Klister Credit Corp., their early-Shopify investment vehicle. Through Northpine it gave $20m to The Ottawa Hospital's Campaign to Create Tomorrow.
notes: Low-profile. The best route is The Northpine Foundation's contact form (CEO Aatif Baskanderi). Climate investing is a good hook for the energy angle.

name: Li Tan
current_role: Executive Director, Shenzhen Hepalink Pharmaceutical Group (SZSE: 002399; HKEX: 9989)
profile: Co-founder, with husband and chairman Li Li, of Shenzhen Hepalink, a leading global supplier of heparin sodium API and enoxaparin. A Sichuan University chemistry graduate (1987), she worked as an Anhui provincial official before joining her husband at heparin supplier Chongqing Tongda in 1992; Hepalink has since expanded into CDMO and biotech investments.
interesting_fact: Hepalink's May 2010 Shenzhen IPO was priced at RMB148 a share, then the highest IPO price in China's A-share market, briefly making Li Li and Li Tan mainland China's richest people.
deep_cut_fact: She studied chemistry at Sichuan University - the same school as her husband - graduating in July 1987, then spent five years as a government official in Anhui Province before entering the heparin business.
notes: Wealth shared with husband Li Li (chairman), who is the public face. Very low media profile. Deep-cut fact is from Forbes bio, so modest novelty.

name: Chen Ailian
current_role: Founder and Chairwoman, Wanfeng Auto Holding Group (also chairs Zhejiang Wanfeng Auto Wheel), Xinchang, Zhejiang
profile: Chen Ailian founded an aluminum-wheel factory in Shaoxing, Zhejiang, in 1994 that grew into Wanfeng Auto Holding Group, which supplies lightweight auto parts to BMW, Mercedes, GM, Ford, Toyota and others. She expanded into robotic welding (Paslin), magnesium parts (Meridian) and aviation. She is married to co-founder Wu Liangding.
interesting_fact: Wanfeng has moved from car wheels into flight: it owns light-aircraft maker Diamond Aircraft and in 2025 took over German eVTOL startup Volocopter, an unusually large air-mobility bet for an auto-parts founder.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Wanfeng she worked as a truck driver. In 2023 she was a torchbearer for the Hangzhou Asian Games, and Fortune ranked her No. 74 on its 2025 Most Powerful Women in Asia list.
notes: Romanized as 'Ailian Chen' or 'Ai Lian Chen'. No published press email was found, and wfjt.com was unreachable during research. A Mandarin approach via the board-secretary office of Zhejiang Wanfeng Auto Wheel (SZSE: 002085) is more realistic. She is a former NPC deputy and the group's party secretary.

name: Wu Liangding
current_role: Co-founder/controlling family shareholder, Wanfeng Auto Holding Group and Rifa (日发) group, Xinchang, Zhejiang
profile: Wu Liangding (吴良定) ran the Xinchang textile-equipment factory that in 1992 became Zhongbao Industrial, forerunner of Wanfeng Auto. He led the Rifa textile-machinery business (now Rifa Precision Machinery) while wife Chen Ailian built Wanfeng into Asia's largest aluminium-wheel maker, later adding magnesium alloys and Diamond Aircraft. The family controls listed Wanfeng Aowei, Rifa Precision and Changchun Jingkai; son Wu Jinhua is a senior executive.
interesting_fact: Wanfeng, the family's wheel business, bought Austria's Diamond Aircraft in 2016-17 and is pursuing electric aircraft and eVTOL certification.
deep_cut_fact: Wanfeng's first aluminium motorcycle wheel was reverse-engineered from the wheel of an imported Yamaha motorcycle that Wu had given his wife Chen Ailian; her team spent 3 months measuring and copying it in 1993-94.
notes: Very low profile; wife Chen Ailian is the family's public face. 'Alive' inferred from continued Hurun 2026 listing - no recent personal news found. Avoid share-pledge/divestment topics.

current_role: Non-executive director, Binjiang Service Group (HKEX: 3316) (appointed June 2022); ~1% shareholder of Hangzhou Binjiang Real Estate Group, acting in concert with his father
profile: Son and designated successor of Qi Jinxing, founder-chairman of Hangzhou Binjiang Real Estate Group (SZSE: 002244), a leading Hangzhou homebuilder; Hurun lists the fortune jointly. A former academic and fund manager, he joined the board of the group's listed property-services arm in 2022 and is a beneficiary of the family trust controlling it.

deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he was a lecturer at North Carolina State University in the US, then a macro strategist and fund manager at China Life Franklin Asset Management.

name: Weng Te-Kuei
current_role: Co-founder, President and Director, Hon. Precision, Inc. (TWSE: 7769), Taichung, Taiwan
profile: Weng Te-Kuei (翁德奎, 'Collin Weng') co-founded Hon. Precision in 1999 with chairman Alan Hsieh and Chang Chien Jung-Li, bringing test-house experience and running sales. Its thermally controlled test handlers are used to test high-power AI chips for TSMC, Nvidia and ASE. It listed on TWSE in Nov 2025, and he is president and often its spokesman.
interesting_fact: Hon Precision's breakthrough came in 2012, when it beat rivals to a test handler with an integrated temperature-control system that solved heat problems for high-wattage chips, the capability that later made it a key supplier for AI chip testing.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days Weng and his two co-founders took 24-hour shifts beside a customer's test machine for more than a month to debug it, and the team rented a house directly across from test house KYEC so engineers were always on call ('buy the equipment, get the engineers free').

The listed spokesperson is Chen Ke-hsin. ir@honprec.com is the company's published 'Public Relations Mailbox'. Taipei Times 2025 coverage quotes him as spokesman/VP.

name: Manoj Upadhyay
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Managing Director, ACME Solar Holdings Ltd (Gurugram)
profile: Manoj Kumar Upadhyay founded ACME in 2003 to make energy-management systems for mobile phone towers, then pivoted to solar in 2008. ACME Solar Holdings now develops and operates solar, wind, hybrid and storage projects across India; it listed in Nov 2024. He is also developing green energy (incl. green hydrogen/ammonia) projects in India, Oman and the U.S.
interesting_fact: ACME began with Rs 20 lakh of seed capital in 2003 and by 2009 was a Rs 2,000 crore company; he says ACME handled nearly 80% of Bharti Airtel's tower roll-out from 2003-2009.
deep_cut_fact: After selling his stake in his first venture, lightning-protection firm Adhunik Power Systems, for Rs 20 lakh, he designed ACME's Power Interface Unit for Bharti Airtel's diesel-plagued cell towers in 17 days - 12 of them without sleep - lifting tower uptime to ~97%.
notes: cs.acme@acme.in is the company-secretarial address listed against him as KMP in an exchange disclosure. Natural podcast fit (telecom energy -> solar/hybrid/storage). Another early anecdote: as a 19-year-old at Shahjahanpur Polytechnic he pitched a Meghalaya rain-capture hydro scheme that reached the UP chief secretary (powerline.net.in, 2016).

name: Sing-ai
current_role: Shareholder, Chang Chun Group (Taiwan petrochemicals/plastics); no public executive role found
profile: Tseng Sing-ai and sibling Tseng Cheng (listed jointly by Forbes) inherited stakes in private Chang Chun Group from their father Tseng Shin-yi (d. 2016), who co-founded it in 1949 with classmates M.K. Liao and Lin Shu-hong. Chang Chun is one of Asia's largest petrochemicals-and-plastics makers, with plants in Taiwan, China and Southeast Asia.

notes: Forbes profile https://www.forbes.com/profile/tseng-cheng-sing-ai/ (residence Taipei). Very private; no personal public presence or role found. Chinese-language sources name the co-founder as 鄭信義, so the family surname may be 鄭 rather than 曾. Only realistic route is via Chang Chun Group corporate office (ccp.com.tw).

name: Anurang Jain
current_role: Managing Director and majority owner, Endurance Technologies (Aurangabad/Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, India)
profile: Nephew of the late Rahul Bajaj, Anurang Jain founded Endurance Technologies in 1985 to supply aluminium castings to Bajaj Auto. Endurance now makes suspension, braking, transmission and casting parts for two- and three-wheelers in India and car parts in Europe, with 18 plants in India and 9 in Europe.
interesting_fact: His twin brother Tarang Jain runs a rival auto-components group, Varroc Engineering; their father Naresh Chandra chaired both companies until retiring in 2020.

name: Ramesh Jaisinghani
current_role: Promoter shareholder, Polycab India (not listed among current directors on Polycab's key-people page; his son Nikhil sits on the board)
profile: One of the Jaisinghani brothers behind Polycab India, the country's largest maker of wires and cables. His older brother Inder (now chairman and MD) started it as a trading firm in 1986. Polycab supplies power, solar and optical-fibre cables to the power, oil and gas and renewables industries, added fans, LEDs and switchgear in 2014, and listed in 2019. name: Andy Konwinski
current_role: Cofounder, Laude Ventures and Laude Institute; cofounder of Databricks and Perplexity
profile: Ohio-raised computer scientist (UW–Madison BS '07, UC Berkeley PhD) who co-created Apache Spark and Mesos at Berkeley's AMPLab, cofounded Databricks (2013) and Perplexity (2022). He now runs Laude Ventures, a $150M seed fund for researcher-founders, and the nonprofit Laude Institute, anchored by his $100M pledge. He also teaches a 'Research to Startups' PhD seminar at Berkeley.
interesting_fact: He funded and ran the K Prize (Konwinski Prize), a $1M competition for the first open-source AI to score 90% on a contamination-free version of SWE-Bench; at Laude he also co-created the Terminal Bench agent benchmark with Stanford's Ludwig Schmidt group.
deep_cut_fact: He got hooked on computers playing Pac-Man on an Apple IIe and writing BASIC as a kid, and grew up tinkering with cars with his dad and reverse-engineering walkie-talkies. UW–Madison named him a 2025 Luminary alumnus.
notes: Active writer and poster on AI benchmarks and agents. Most recent blog post (Jul 2026): 'Concentration of power in AI is a risk, not a solution'. hello@laude.org is the Laude Institute's general inbox. Forbes says he no longer holds active roles at Databricks or Perplexity.

name: Aravind Srinivas
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Perplexity AI
profile: Chennai-born Aravind Srinivas co-founded AI answer engine Perplexity in August 2022 with Denis Yarats, Johnny Ho and Andy Konwinski, after a Berkeley CS PhD under Pieter Abbeel and research stints at OpenAI and Google DeepMind. Perplexity was valued at ~$21B in early 2026, reported ~$450M ARR in March 2026, signed a $750M Azure deal with Microsoft, and he has said it plans to IPO in 2028.
interesting_fact: Perplexity is backed by Jeff Bezos, Yann LeCun and Google chief scientist Jeff Dean; in Jan 2026 it signed a 3-year, $750M deal to use Microsoft Azure while AWS remained its main cloud.
deep_cut_fact: Before Perplexity he was first author of BoTNet ('Bottleneck Transformers for Visual Recognition', 2021), co-written with Transformer co-inventor Ashish Vaswani, and of CURL (2020), a contrastive-learning method for RL from pixels with Pieter Abbeel.
notes: Very active and responsive on X (@AravSrinivas); DMs/replies there are the most realistic route. No published Perplexity press email found. CURL paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2004.04136

name: Denis Yarats
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Perplexity AI
profile: Belarus-born (Gomel, 1987) computer scientist who worked on Bing at Microsoft, as an ML engineer at Quora and as a research scientist at Meta's FAIR while doing an NYU PhD in reinforcement learning. notes: Code Jam finalist detail sourced via Forbes Russia (https://www.forbes.ru/svoi-biznes/526489-kak-belorus-s-partnerami-postroili-odin-iz-samyh-dorogih-startapov-v-mire-perplexity). No published Perplexity press email confirmed; reach via X or Perplexity comms team.

name: Guillermo Rauch

Devout Christian. Route via SMIC corporate communications.

name: Athanasios Martinos
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Eastern Mediterranean Maritime (Eastmed), Athens
profile: Greek shipowner Thanassis J. Martinos co-ran the family firm Thenamaris from 1968 to 1990, then split off and founded Eastmed in 1990-91. It now operates about 75-78 tankers, bulk carriers and container ships. He also owns a Cyprus-based real-estate firm with offices and shops in London and Geneva, and served as civil governor of Mount Athos from 2019 to 2023.
interesting_fact: He and his brothers Andreas and Constantinos together control the largest shipping fleet in Greece, the world's largest shipowning nation.
deep_cut_fact: A Greek Navy veteran, he insisted on serving as civil governor of the monastic republic of Mount Athos (2019-2023) without any pay. He is also an Archon of the Ecumenical Patriarchate.
notes: Appears at forums such as the Delphi Economic Forum (advisory committee). The route is Eastmed's media email. Shipping decarbonisation and fuels give an energy angle.

name: Kiat Chiaravanont
current_role: Shareholder (~5.76% per Forbes) in Charoen Pokphand (CP) Group holding company; no current executive role found
profile: Hong Kong-based member of Thailand's Chearavanont family: eldest son of Choncharoen Chearavanont (uncle of CP senior chairman Dhanin) and thus Dhanin's first cousin. His main asset is his stake in CP Group, the agribusiness, retail (CP All/7-Eleven Thailand) and telecom conglomerate. He dropped off Forbes' real-time list after 2022.
interesting_fact: Although he lives in Hong Kong rather than Thailand, his 5.76% stake in CP Group - the holding outfit for the Charoen Pokphand conglomerate run by his cousin Dhanin's family - is his biggest asset.
notes: Extremely private; almost no public record beyond Forbes. Identity marked uncertain only because no independent primary source on him was found and his current status (incl. alive) is unverified. Route, if any, would be via CP Group corporate communications.

name: Simon Nixon
current_role: Private investor (Simon Nixon family office); owner of SimonEscapes luxury villa rentals; co-founder of Moneysupermarket.com
profile: Simon Nixon co-founded price-comparison site Moneysupermarket in 1993, floated it in 2007 and sold his last shares in 2016. He has since backed dozens of startups, including Airbnb, Robinhood and Wise before their IPOs, and runs SimonEscapes, which rents out his luxury homes in places such as Malibu and Barbados. He is based in Jersey.
interesting_fact: He was an early private investor in Airbnb, Robinhood and Wise (TransferWise) before they went public, and has put more than £100m into startups since leaving Moneysupermarket.
deep_cut_fact: Moneysupermarket began in 1993, while Nixon was an accounting student at Nottingham, as 'Mortgage 2000', an offline service selling mortgage information to independent financial advisers. It became moneysupermarket.com in 1999.
notes: SimonEscapes is his own business, so its inbox is the closest published route, though it is a bookings address. He has given interviews to City AM and the Chester Chronicle and is relatively accessible for a billionaire. His startup investing (an angel-investor angle) is a natural podcast hook. Avoid the Jersey tax-move topic.

name: Randal J. Kirk
current_role: Executive chairman, Third Security LLC; executive chairman/director and 10%+ owner, Precigen (NASDAQ: PGEN)
profile: A former attorney from southwest Virginia, Kirk co-founded injectable drug and vaccine distributor General Injectables & Vaccines in 1983 with a Bland County pharmacist and sold it in 1998. Through Third Security he backed New River Pharmaceuticals (sold to Shire) and Intrexon/Precigen, whose bets included non-browning Arctic apples and AquAdvantage salmon. He stepped down as Precigen CEO in 2020 but remains chairman.
interesting_fact: He sold greeting cards door-to-door at age 9 and claims an 85% close rate; he was also an avid falconer on his Virginia farm.
deep_cut_fact: A Radford University alumnus (B.A. 1976, then UVA law), he gave Radford $1 million in 1999 to create an endowment, won its Outstanding Alumnus Award in 2005 and was named Virginia's Outstanding Industrialist of the Year in 2008.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Precigen's first approved therapy PAPZIMEOS (for recurrent respiratory papillomatosis) is a timely positive hook. Third Security (Radford, VA) manages family money.

name: Chad Richison
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Paycom Software (NYSE: PAYC), Oklahoma City
profile: Oklahoma-raised former ADP salesman who founded Paycom in 1998 as one of the first fully online payroll providers. He took it public on the NYSE in 2014 (S&P 500 since 2020), owns roughly 12%, and still runs the HR/payroll software company; he also founded the Green Shoe Foundation for mental-health counseling.
interesting_fact: A wrestler in high school and college, he placed at the Oklahoma state championships as a senior in his hometown of Tuttle.
deep_cut_fact: He launched Paycom at 27 by selling his Denver house and funding it with his cashed-in 401(k), 13 credit cards and a $225,000 SBA loan; he personally sold the first 400 clients, many seeing the internet for the first time: 'I would get on my hands and knees to unplug their fax.'

public_contacts.value: https://www.paycom.com/resources/podcasts/episode/future-hr-chad-richison-evolution-tech/ (Paycom HR Break Room podcast, has interviewed him)

notes: Strong Oklahoma City booster ('I could have started this company anywhere, but I chose Oklahoma City'). Best route: Paycom media relations.

name: Zheng Guangwen (郑广文)
current_role: Chairman, general manager and actual controller, Shenyang Fortune Precision Equipment Co. (富创精密, SSE STAR: 688409)
profile: Shenyang-based entrepreneur who controls Fortune Precision, China's leading maker of precision parts for semiconductor equipment (process/structural parts, modules, gas lines) supplying NAURA, AMEC and global tool makers. Founded 2008 and listed on the STAR Market in 2022; its 2024 revenue was RMB 3.04bn and it bought Germany's Compart Systems to broaden its platform.
interesting_fact: Fortune Precision is one of the few Chinese firms in the supply chains of top global chip-equipment makers; its shares rose roughly 450% in a year to 2026, lifting Zheng's stake to roughly RMB 7.9bn.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in the car-trading business and crossed into industrial manufacturing in 2003 by investing in Shenyang Advanced (沈阳先进), an affiliate of the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Shenyang Institute of Automation, before co-founding Fortune Precision in June 2008.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. Route via company securities dept (board secretary Liang Qianqian, tel 024-31692129 per filings). Caution: in Dec 2025 part of his holding company stake was frozen in connection with an investigation he was assisting (company said unrelated to operations). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Dan Wilks
current_role: Co-founder/co-owner, Wilks Brothers LLC (Cisco, Texas); founder and principal stockholder of ProFrac / PF Holdings (ACDC) via THRC Holdings
profile: Texas mason-turned-fracking billionaire. With brother Farris he founded Wilks Masonry (1995) and frac company Frac Tech (2002), selling their 70% stake in 2011 for $3.5B. Via Wilks Brothers they now control oilfield-services firm ProFrac (run by his son Matt), invest in oil, gas and data firms, and own 670,000+ acres across the West.
interesting_fact: The Wilks brothers are among America's largest private landowners (~672,000 acres in six western states) and reportedly spend about four months a year in Montana building homes on their ranches.

public_contacts.value: https://ir.pfholdingscorp.com/ (IR contact form incl. Press/Media option)
https://www.wilksbrothers.com/ (family office site; no contact listed)

notes: Very private; lives in Cisco, TX. Prominent conservative political/media donor (Daily Wire, PragerU) - sensitive context. ProFrac is now led by his son Matt Wilks (Exec Chairman, CEO from Aug 2026); best route is via ProFrac/PF Holdings IR.

name: Feridun Gecgel
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~80%), Astor Enerji A.S. (Borsa Istanbul: ASTOR); board member, Fenerbahce Futbol A.S.
profile: Born in Sanliurfa in 1970, Gecgel became an entrepreneur straight after high school, selling electrical materials through Ozguney Elektrik and making furniture, then bought transformer maker Astor in 2005 for about $3M. Astor is now Turkey's largest maker of transformers and switchgear, exporting to 90+ countries; its 2023 Istanbul IPO made him a billionaire, and it is expanding into US grid-equipment supply.
interesting_fact: He bought Astor for roughly $3 million in 2005; after its 2023 IPO the company's market value rose to about $4 billion (pre-IPO value ~$750M).
deep_cut_fact: A football executive as well as an industrialist: in 2026 he joined Aziz Yildirim's Fenerbahce leadership, and was named to the Fenerbahce Futbol A.S. board at its 23 July 2026 extraordinary general assembly (earlier he served on MKE Ankaragucu's board).
notes: Heads-up: on 26 Sep 2026 Istanbul prosecutors placed precautionary measures on his personal cash/securities in a fund investigation (the measure on Astor itself was lifted next day); he publicly said he was on a planned US business trip. Do due diligence before outreach. Contacts are company-level only; good grid/transformer-shortage angle.

name: Liang Qin
current_role: Chairwoman and legal representative, Yangzhou Yangjie Electronic Technology (300373.SZ)
profile: Liang Qin (梁勤) has run Yangjie since 2000 (chair since 2006). Yangjie is a vertically integrated power-semiconductor maker - diodes, MOSFETs, IGBT modules, SiC - for autos, AI, clean energy and 5G, listed in Shenzhen in 2014 with ~7,900 staff. She sits on the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce executive committee.
interesting_fact: Yangjie's business scope extends beyond chips into distributed solar: it is licensed to develop and build PV power projects and sell solar modules alongside its power semiconductors.
deep_cut_fact: She studied electronic instruments at Yangzhou Technician College (1986-89), then worked in the trade-union office of the Yangzhou Grand Hotel (1989-93) before earning an electrical-technology degree at Yangzhou University; she has been named a Jiangsu Province Model Worker.
notes: Contacts are company-level (board secretary's office, secretary Qin Nan). Active in Jiangsu business-federation and women-entrepreneur bodies; Chinese-language outreach advisable. Power semis/SiC angle fits energy and data-center topics.

name: Wu Yingming
current_role: Executive Director and President of Regional Management, CATL (Contemporary Amperex Technology); chairman of CATL's board of supervisors 2015-Dec 2025
profile: Wu Yingming (b. 1967) is a longtime CATL executive and shareholder whose fortune comes from his stake in the Ningde-based lithium-ion battery giant. He joined CATL in Dec 2015 as procurement & IT director, chaired its board of supervisors for a decade, and in Dec 2025 became an executive director overseeing subsidiary management and zero-carbon ecosystem business; he also runs several CATL JVs, e.g. CATL-SAIC Power Battery.
interesting_fact: Before CATL he was procurement and IT director (2006-2012) at Dongguan Amperex Technology (ATL), the consumer-battery maker from which CATL was spun off in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He is a software engineer by training: he earned a bachelor's in computer software from Northeast Institute of Technology (now Northeastern University) in July 1989, and his first CATL post combined procurement with IT. He is also general manager of CATL's JV with SAIC (Shidai SAIC Power Battery).
notes: Low public profile; route via CATL IR/press. Board change: nominated non-independent director 6 Dec 2025 when the supervisory board was restructured (https://tech.ifeng.com/c/8orI8gQ7OKQ). Forbes profile still lists him as supervisory-board chairman.

name: Teo Swee Ann
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Espressif Systems (Shanghai STAR Market: 688018)
profile: Singaporean EE (NUS master's, 2000) who worked at Bluetooth startup Transilica, then Marvell and Montage Technology, before founding Espressif in Shanghai in 2008. Espressif's low-cost ESP8266/ESP32 Wi-Fi and Bluetooth chips power vast numbers of IoT devices; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019 and he still runs it.
interesting_fact: Espressif's ESP8266, a cheap Wi-Fi microcontroller, has been described as 'legendary' in the maker world; he started the company wanting to automate analogue chip design and at one point ran it as a design consultancy before making his own chips.
deep_cut_fact: His maths teacher at The Chinese High School, Mr Chew Kim Liong, entered him untrained into a national maths competition where he placed seventh, earning advanced number-theory classes; Teo says Chew 'changed the trajectory of my life'. He also chose to minor in law at NUS despite expecting to do poorly in it.
notes: Engineer-founder who answers press by email/chat (per Schoolbag). Publishes 'CEO Messages' on Espressif's site. No dedicated press email found; IR email is the only Espressif-published address. Forbes bio empty in input.

name: Ron Corio
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Array Technologies (Nasdaq: ARRY); private investor in Albuquerque, New Mexico
profile: Founded solar-tracker maker Array Technologies in Albuquerque in 1989, moving from home trackers to the horizontal single-axis trackers now standard on utility-scale solar farms after a first 250 kW BP Solar project in 2001. He stepped down as CEO in 2018, sold his ~38% stake for about $1.2bn within six months of the Oct 2020 IPO, and left the board in 2022.
interesting_fact: Forbes calls him the 'Godfather of Solar' and New Mexico's first (and only) billionaire; he now prefers to stay out of the spotlight.
deep_cut_fact: In Array's early days he built a solar tracker that hung from Steve Fossett's balloon on his first round-the-world attempt (keeping a flexible PV array pointed at the sun as the balloon rotated), supplied 'artistic trackers' for Robin Williams' Napa Valley home, and made fold-out tracking power trailers for anti-poaching patrols in Africa.
notes: Very private; no personal site, social accounts or office contact found. Array Technologies IR/press would not represent him since he left the board in 2022. Home Power magazine praised his first home tracker in a 1991 'Things That Work' review - good rapport hook for an energy podcast.

name: Alex Birkenstock
current_role: Private investor; former co-owner of Birkenstock (exited his remaining stake after the October 2023 IPO). Lives in Tegernsee, Germany.
profile: One of Karl Birkenstock's three sons, Alex took joint control of the family shoemaker in 2002, running his own brands under a multi-brand setup. He and brother Christian bought out brother Stephan in 2013 and sold a majority to L Catterton and Bernard Arnault's Financiere Agache in 2021 (>$4.5B), keeping minority stakes; Alex sold out after the 2023 NYSE IPO.
interesting_fact: The Birkenstock line traces to 1774 records of shoemaker Johannes Birkenstock in Hesse; his father Karl's 1963 'Original Birkenstock Footbed Sandal' (later the 'Madrid') was initially a commercial flop.
deep_cut_fact: His father Karl created, in 1962, the first standardized, permanently installed anatomical insole, which made healthy footwear mass-producible; earlier generations had made individually fitted insoles, and great-grandfather Konrad trademarked 'Fussbett' in 1925.
notes: Very private since exiting the company; no published personal contact or current venture found (search budget exhausted). Birkenstock corporate PR no longer represents him.

name: Li Jianquan
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Winner Medical Co. (Shenzhen-listed, Sept 2020)
profile: Founder-chairman of Winner Medical, which began making cotton-based medical dressings in 1991. It now supplies wound care, surgical and PPE products to around 150,000 Chinese pharmacies, 5,000+ hospitals and 110+ countries. He also built the consumer brand Purcotton (cotton daily-care products), and the group listed on the Shenzhen exchange in September 2020.
interesting_fact: Besides Winner, Li has chaired the Medical Dressing Branch of the China Medical Insurance Chamber of Commerce, and Winner was named a top-10 Chinese medical-dressing enterprise for 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Li (who signs as 'JQ Li') built Winner around a three-part tenet: 'Quality priority over profit; Brand priority over speed; Social value priority over enterprise value.'
notes: Goes by 'JQ Li' in English. The only published contact is the company's general info inbox; no personal channels were found. Not an obvious fit for an energy/data-center theme.

name: Avram Glazer
current_role: Executive Co-Chairman, Manchester United; co-owner, Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Chairman of the Board, INNOVATE Corp. (NYSE: VATE)
profile: Avram 'Avie' Glazer, son of the late shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer, has co-chaired Manchester United with his brother Joel since the family's 2005 takeover. The siblings sold a quarter of their stake to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023. The family has owned the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers since 1995, and he chairs holding company INNOVATE Corp. He also owns the Desert Vipers cricket club in Dubai.
interesting_fact: From 1995 to 2009 he was chairman and CEO of Zapata Corporation, the oil company founded by George H.W. Bush. He also previously ran Omega Protein and Safety Components International, giving him an energy-industry angle beyond sports.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Rochester, NY, he was named Junior Achievement's Outstanding Young Businessman of the Year in 1978. After law school he also studied at Peking University and Fudan University in Shanghai. With his wife Jill he founded Glazer Hall, a performing-arts centre in Palm Beach, in 2025.

public_contacts.value: ir@innovatecorp.com (INNOVATE Corp., where he is chairman)

notes: Glazer ownership is controversial among Man Utd fans, so avoid that in outreach; the energy (Zapata) or INNOVATE infrastructure angle is a better fit. INNOVATE sold DBM Global to IES Holdings in Oct 2026. The Manchester United IR site exposed no scrapeable email.

name: Bryan Glazer
current_role: Co-chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (with brothers Joel and Edward); director, Manchester United
profile: Son of shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer (d. 2014), he and his five siblings own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers (bought for $192M in 1995, now worth ~$5.2B) and a controlling stake in Manchester United (bought 2005; a quarter of their stake sold to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023). He has helped run the Bucs since 1995, including the new stadium and brand redesign, and the team has won Super Bowls XXXVII and LV.
interesting_fact: Under Glazer ownership the Buccaneers won Super Bowl LV (2021), the first time a team played the Super Bowl in its own home stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He majored in broadcast communications at American University before earning a law degree at Whittier; in 2016 he gave $4M to convert Tampa's historic Fort Homer W. Hesterly Armory into the Bryan Glazer Family Jewish Community Center.

public_contacts.value: https://www.buccaneers.com/ (Tampa Bay Buccaneers; route via team communications)

notes: The Glazers rarely give interviews, especially about Manchester United, so avoid United fan-protest topics. Best route is the Buccaneers communications department. He was a key figure in the design of Raymond James Stadium and the Bucs' logo redesign.

name: Darcie Glazer Kassewitz
current_role: Owner, Tampa Bay Buccaneers; Chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers Foundation, Glazer Vision Foundation and Glazer Family Foundation
profile: Daughter of the late Malcolm Glazer and one of six siblings who own the NFL's Tampa Bay Buccaneers and a controlling stake in Manchester United (a quarter of which they sold to Jim Ratcliffe in 2023). She leads the family's philanthropy and the Bucs' community, fan and women-in-football programmes.
interesting_fact: She created 'She Is Football' in 2025, whose girls' flag football preseason classic is the largest such event in the US (130+ teams), and the Bucs' She Is Football Scholarship is the first academic scholarship by an NFL team for girls who play football.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 she launched the Buccaneers National Coaching Academy: from thousands of global applicants, 25 finalists got full scholarships and five advanced to work training camp and preseason with the Bucs' coaches and scouts. She also started the 'Women of Red' fan programme in 2015.
notes: Inherited wealth; not an entrepreneur in the podcast's sense. Route would be the Buccaneers communications/front office or the Glazer Family Foundation; no published direct email found.

name: Edward Glazer
current_role: Owner/Co-Chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers; co-owner and director, Manchester United
profile: One of six children of mall magnate Malcolm Glazer, who bought the Buccaneers in 1995 and Manchester United in 2005; the siblings jointly control both clubs. Entering his 32nd season with the Bucs, Edward is co-chairman involved in strategy and business operations, oversees real-estate acquisitions for First Allied Corp., and founded US Property Trust and US Auto Trust.
interesting_fact: He and his wife Shari funded Glazer Arena at his alma mater Ithaca College (class of '92), a 6,700-seat venue with a 200-meter six-lane indoor track that opened in fall 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Glazer Arena has become the largest sports and events venue for the Elmira-Corning-Ithaca region, hosting concerts, trade shows and graduations as well as the Bombers' indoor track team.

public_contacts.value: https://www.buccaneers.com/team/contact-us (Buccaneers front office, One Buccaneer Place, Tampa)

notes: Man Utd ownership is a sensitive topic with fans - keep outreach on Bucs/real estate/auto dealerships. Best route: Buccaneers front office/communications.

name: Joel Glazer
current_role: Co-Chairman, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (NFL) and Co-Chairman, Manchester United
profile: Rochester-born (1967) son of shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer. He helped his father buy the Buccaneers in 1995 ($192m; now worth about $5.2bn) and Manchester United in 2005. He co-chairs both clubs with his brothers. In 2023 the six siblings sold a quarter of their United stake to Jim Ratcliffe at a valuation of about $5.4bn.
interesting_fact: The Buccaneers won Super Bowl XXXVII (January 2003) and Super Bowl LV (2021) under the Glazers. With brother Bryan, Joel built local support for what became Raymond James Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the NFL's International Committee, which oversees the league's games abroad, and sits on its Finance, Media and Sports Betting committees. The Glazer Family Foundation gave $5m toward the Glazer Children's Museum in Tampa (opened 2010).
notes: He almost never gives interviews, especially to UK media. Manchester United ownership is a sensitive topic with fans, so avoid it. The best route is Buccaneers communications (media site above); I didn't find a published press email.

name: Kevin Glazer
current_role: Co-owner, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (listed as 'Owner'); Manchester United director/shareholder; runs Glazer Properties, the family real estate arm
profile: One of six children of the late shopping-mall magnate Malcolm Glazer, who bought the Buccaneers for $192M in 1995 and Manchester United for $1.4B in 2005. In 2023 the siblings sold about a quarter of their United stake to Jim Ratcliffe (valuing the club at $5.4B) and still own the Bucs. Kevin oversees Glazer Properties and has no day-to-day sports operating role.
interesting_fact: The family's NFL franchise, bought for $192M in 1995, is now valued at about $5.2B and won Super Bowls in 2003 and 2021.
notes: The most private of the Glazer siblings; brothers Joel, Bryan and Edward are the public faces. No personal or Glazer Properties contact published; the Buccaneers front-office page (https://www.buccaneers.com/team/front-office-roster/) lists him only as 'Owner'. Avoid Manchester United fan-protest topics. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Huang Jianjun
current_role: Director and General Manager, Suzhou Semight Instruments (联讯仪器, SSE STAR: 688808); one of its three joint actual controllers
profile: Huang Jianjun (黄建军, b. 1981) is GM of Semight Instruments, a Suzhou maker of optical-communication and semiconductor test equipment for 400G/800G/1.6T optical modules used in AI data centers. He holds ~7.2% directly and, with chairman Hu Haiyang and VP Yang Jian, controls ~55%. Semight listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 24 Apr 2026 and closed day one at ~RMB 82B market cap.
interesting_fact: Semight is described as the world's second company to offer a full suite of core test instruments for 1.6T optical modules; on its April 2026 IPO day the stock closed at RMB 799 vs an RMB 81.88 issue price.
deep_cut_fact: An optical-module insider before he tested them: after a 2006 optical-engineering master's at Beijing University of Technology he worked at O-Net and JDSU in Shenzhen, then spent nearly a decade (2008-2017) at Finisar's Shanghai unit, rising from senior engineer to engineering director, before joining Semight as GM in Jan 2018.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. IR contact is the board office (board secretary Liao Jin, securities rep Zhang Jinping; office line 0512-68780583 published in filings). Strong fit for AI data-center optics/1.6T interconnect topics.

name: Lawrence Ho
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Melco International Development and Melco Resorts & Entertainment (Nasdaq: MLCO); founder of family office Black Spade Capital
profile: Lawrence Ho, eldest living son of the late Stanley Ho, left investment banking in 2001 to take a 26% stake in Melco International and built Melco Resorts into a major integrated-resort operator: City of Dreams and Studio City in Macau, City of Dreams Manila and Europe's largest integrated resort, City of Dreams Mediterranean in Cyprus (2023). His Black Spade Capital invests in SPACs, tech and green energy.
interesting_fact: His Black Spade SPAC merged with Vietnamese EV maker VinFast in a $23 billion Nasdaq listing in 2023; Black Spade's remit also covers green energy and, reportedly, space-sector deals.
deep_cut_fact: Before casinos he began in September 1999 in Jardine Fleming's Asia derivatives group (then Citibank), and in 2003 Melco's Mocha Clubs pioneered café-style slot parlours in Macau.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who speaks at conferences; Black Spade Capital (family office, Hong Kong) is a second route for non-gaming topics such as green energy and SPACs. Toronto-educated (Upper Canada College, U of T BCom 1999).

name: Yu Minhong
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, New Oriental Education & Technology Group; Chairman, East Buy (live-commerce spin-off)
profile: A Peking University English teacher, Yu founded New Oriental in 1993, starting with TOEFL/GRE prep classes. It became China's largest private education company and listed on the NYSE in 2006. After China's 2021 tutoring crackdown he pivoted New Oriental's teachers into live-stream e-commerce through East Buy (Dongfang Zhenxuan), which became a breakout hit in 2022.
interesting_fact: Peter Chan's 2013 hit film 'American Dreams in China' was loosely based on Yu and his New Oriental co-founders Xu Xiaoping and Wang Qiang.
deep_cut_fact: A farmer's son from Jiangyin, Jiangsu, Yu failed the gaokao in 1978 and 1979, mostly because of his English scores. On his third try he got into Peking University in 1980, where he majored in English and later taught.
notes: A prolific public speaker and author with large Chinese social-media and video channels; he is very open to media in China. The IR and FTI contacts are New Oriental's published investor/media contacts. His entrepreneurship and pivot story is a strong podcast angle.

name: Niu Yishun
current_role: Listed by Hurun as the principal behind Hixih (华勤集团, Hixih Rubber Industry Group), Shandong; exact title not verified
profile: Hurun lists Niu Yishun (牛宜顺), jointly with Niu Teng, as the owner of Hixih. Hixih Rubber Industry Group was founded in 1989 and centers on high-end rubber: tires, engineering rubber and steel cord. It has expanded into power, new energy, metal products, property, capital operations and healthcare, and employs over 10,000 people.
interesting_fact: Hixih has formed joint ventures with Italy's Pirelli and Germany's Continental, and is a repeat entrant in China's Top 500 Enterprises.
notes: The company was matched via its 'Hixih' name, but the group site does not name Niu Yishun, so his role and the Niu Teng relationship are unverified (web search budget used up). Possible energy angle through the group's new-energy and power businesses. Very low international profile.

name: Niu Teng
profile: Listed by Hurun (China 2017-2026, Global 2018-2026) with Niu Yishun, with wealth attributed to 'Hixih' in auto components. The underlying company and Chinese name could not be confirmed with the available sources.
notes: Identity not confirmed: 'Hixih' looks like a Hurun romanisation, and hixih.com is a parked domain. Web search quota ran out before Chinese-language searches (e.g. 牛腾 牛奕顺 汽车零部件) could be run. Needs a follow-up pass.

name: Zhang Ronghua
current_role: Chairwoman of the board, Tianjin Rockcheck Xiangtai Investment Holding Group (Rockcheck Group / 荣程集团)
profile: Tangshan-born (1969) self-made steel entrepreneur who co-founded Rockcheck in Tangshan in 1989 and moved it to Tianjin in 2001. She has chaired it since 2014. The private group now spans Rockcheck Steel, commodities trading, digital tech, new energy and culture/health. She is a 14th National People's Congress deputy for Tianjin and a vice-chair of the Tianjin federation of industry and commerce.
interesting_fact: Rockcheck has set up a dedicated new-energy arm (荣程新能科技集团, Rockcheck New Energy Technology Group) as part of a 'hundred-year green Rockcheck' push, and its steel bars now carry green-product certifications.
deep_cut_fact: Rockcheck, which she co-founded, donated RMB 100 million to relief after the 2008 Wenchuan earthquake. That was one of the largest private donations at the time, from founders who had themselves come out of Tangshan, the city devastated by the 1976 earthquake.
notes: Mandarin-only route; the group site lists a switchboard but no email. Steel decarbonisation and the new-energy unit are a natural podcast hook. Her co-founder husband Zhang Xiangqing died in 2014; do not raise this.

name: Lan Chun
profile: Listed by Hurun (Global 2021-2026, China 2020-2026) with wealth from 'New Talent' (education, biotech, real estate, investments), shared with Yang Ying. Not independently verified.
notes: Not researched: the shared web-search budget ran out and Baidu Baike was blocked. Needs a follow-up pass to identify the company behind Hurun's 'New Talent' (Chinese name) and confirm identity.

name: Lv Shaolin
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Bozhon Precision Industry Technology (博众精工, SSE STAR: 688097), Suzhou
profile: Lv Shaolin (b. 1973) founded Bozhon Precision in Wujiang, Suzhou in 2006 and, with his wife/co-controller Cheng Caixia, controls the STAR-listed maker of factory automation equipment for consumer electronics (a key Apple supplier), new-energy/battery production and semiconductors. interesting_fact: He steered Marcegaglia's diversification beyond steel into tourism and renewable energy. From 2017 he promoted the relaunch of the Ilva steelworks through AM Investco, a joint venture with ArcelorMittal.
deep_cut_fact: He was named 'Stainless Steel Executive of the Year 2010' at the 9th Stainless & Special Steel Summit in Rome, and won Forbes Italia's CEO Italian Award 2024 in the Industry category.
notes: The Marcegaglia newsroom explicitly invites journalists to write to the newsroom address. Energy angle: the group's renewables/energy arm (a euroenergygroup contact appears on its site). Wikipedia flags his page for promotional tone, so the facts above come from that page and should be checked.

name: Rosely Schweizer
current_role: Shareholder (~12.5%) of Dr. August Oetker KG; former advisory board chair (until 2010)
profile: Born Rosely Oetker in Hamburg in 1940, eldest daughter of Rudolf-August Oetker, she studied economics in Innsbruck (1964), was a general partner and advisory board chair at sparkling-wine maker Henkell & Soehnlein, and chaired the Oetker parent company's advisory board from 2007 to 2010. She owns about 12.5% of the food, beverage and hotel group; her son Rudolf Louis Schweizer became board chairman in 2019.

name: Andrei Krivenko
current_role: Founder and controlling owner (~88%), VkusVill grocery chain, Russia
profile: Former CFO of seafood distributor Agama who opened dairy shop chain Izbenka in 2009, then from 2012 rebuilt it as VkusVill, a fresh, short-shelf-life private-label grocer. It grew to ~2,000 stores plus dark stores in 170+ Russian cities with about half of turnover online (329bn roubles in 2024); a planned 2022 Nasdaq/Moscow IPO was cancelled after Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

notes: Russia-based; consider sanctions/reputational context. Ownership: via AO 'Evolyutsionnaya tsel' -> Proekt Izbenka (86.05%) + 1.79% direct; Baring Vostok 12.16%. No published press email retrieved (vkusvill.ru unreachable from here). Shown as 'former' on Forbes real-time.

name: Ong Beng Seng
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, Hotel Properties Limited (SGX-listed); chairman of Singapore GP (F1 race promoter)
profile: Born 1946 in Teluk Anson, Perak, and raised in Singapore, Ong started in shipping insurance, joined trader Kuo International in 1975, then built Hotel Properties Ltd, which owns or holds stakes in Four Seasons, Hilton, Hard Rock and other hotels in Asia and Europe. With wife Christina (Como hotels, Club 21) they are among Singapore's most influential couples.
interesting_fact: As chairman of race promoter Singapore GP he is credited with bringing Formula One to Singapore; the inaugural 2008 Singapore Grand Prix was F1's first-ever night race.
deep_cut_fact: His career began at a firm insuring ships; he met his future wife Christina at Kuo International, the trading company founded by her father Peter Fu Yun Siak, which he joined in 1975.

interesting_fact: Prince Albert is also a racing driver. He won the ADAC GT Masters (German GT) championship in 2010 with Reiter Engineering and has competed in the European Rally Championship since 2016.

The patriarch died on 27 April 2002.

name: William F. Austin
current_role: Founder, principal owner and Chairman, Starkey Hearing Technologies (Eden Prairie, Minnesota)

He built Starkey into a privately held global hearing-technology firm with 5,000+ employees, now pushing AI-powered hearing aids, and co-founded the Starkey Hearing Foundation with his wife Tani.
interesting_fact: When Ronald Reagan was photographed wearing Starkey hearing aids in September 1983, Starkey's sales quadrupled within weeks; clients also included Mother Teresa, Walter Cronkite and Arnold Palmer.
deep_cut_fact: At 19 he enrolled at the University of Minnesota to become a doctor but left after a few weeks for hearing care, explaining: 'As a doctor, I could help maybe 20, 25 people a day.' His motto: 'We live through what we give.'
notes: Press email comes from an older Starkey release; may be dated. Founder is in his 80s; CEO Brandon Sawalich handles most public engagement. Medical-school quote is from Wikipedia; motto from the 2021 interview.

notes: Now 83 and no longer the operating CEO; Gerald Prinzhorn runs the group and Cord Prinzhorn was CEO from 2013. The group's energy-efficiency and paper-mill energy projects are the podcast angle. Johnson Jr. and holds an inherited stake in the privately held company, now led by her brother Fisk Johnson. current_role: Founder & Chairman, AOG (Addax & Oryx Group, owner of Oryx Energies); Founder, Fondation Gandur pour l'Art
profile: Grasse-born (1949) Swiss oil entrepreneur who founded the Addax & Oryx Group in 1987, built Addax Petroleum into a major Nigeria-focused producer and sold it to Sinopec in 2009 for about US$7.3bn. He then launched Toronto-listed Oryx Petroleum (Iraqi Kurdistan; left board after 2020 change of control) and now chairs AOG while focusing on his art foundation.

name: Zdenek Bakala

He built his fortune via coal miner OKD/New World Resources (exited 2016) and the BXR group, and now invests via Bakala Capital in real estate and media (Economia: Hospodářské noviny, Aktuálně.cz).

profile: Baghdad-born (1937) British-Iraqi businessman, London-based. His Khalili Collections comprise around 35,000 objects across eight collections, including one of the world's largest of Islamic art, Meiji Japanese art and kimono; he now focuses on cultural diplomacy through his foundation.
interesting_fact: His collections total about 35,000 objects; he was knighted in 2020, and in 2024 the Khalili Foundation became a founder member of the King's Commonwealth Fellowship Programme and partnered with UNESCO's Memory of the World programme.

profile: Peter Johan Mads Clausen (b. 1949; 'Clauson' in Hurun) is a son of Danfoss founder Mads Clausen and brother of longtime chairman Jørgen Mads Clausen. Danfoss (drives, heating/cooling, hydraulics, power electronics) is controlled by the Bitten & Mads Clausen Foundation and the family; his wealth is his stake.
interesting_fact: His father founded Danfoss in 1933 in Nordborg; the company later created Universe, a Danish science-themed attraction park opened in 2005 that includes a museum of how Mads Clausen lived and invented Danfoss.
notes: Very private; almost no public profile, and he is not on the foundation board (age limit 70; next-generation Mads Clausen and Mads-Peter Clausen sit there). Could not confirm alive status (search budget exhausted). For a Danfoss/data-center cooling angle, Danfoss leadership or the younger Clausens are better podcast targets.

name: Sue Ann Hamm
current_role: Founder and President, Arnall Family Foundation (Oklahoma City); now known as Sue Ann Arnall
profile: Economist and lawyer, formerly an executive at shale pioneer Continental Resources; her fortune stems from her 1988-2014 marriage to its founder Harold Hamm. As Sue Ann Arnall she created the Arnall Family Foundation in 2015, an Oklahoma funder of criminal-justice reform, youth justice and homelessness work.
interesting_fact: Her foundation runs Oklahoma County's 'Diversion Hub' and a Black Justice Fund, aiming to safely lower incarceration by funding services that keep people out of the criminal legal system.

public_contacts.value: https://www.arnallfamilyfoundation.org (Arnall Family Foundation; contact page at /contact)

notes: Uses the name Sue Ann Arnall. Avoid the high-profile divorce from Harold Hamm in outreach. Foundation states it does not accept unsolicited proposals; frame any approach as a media/interview request via its Marketing & Communications team. Has an oil-and-gas background (Continental Resources) relevant to the energy podcast.

name: Sue Walker
current_role: Principal beneficiary/owner in the Walker family's Walker Corporation (Sydney), after the death of her husband Lang Walker in 2024
profile: Suzanne 'Sue' Walker is the widow of Walker Corporation co-founder Lang Walker, who died on 27 Jan 2024 aged 78; Hurun has listed her since 2024. The private Sydney developer is behind Collins Square (Melbourne), Parramatta Square, Riverlea Park (Adelaide) and Senibong Cove in Malaysia.
interesting_fact: The Walker group owns Kokomo Private Island, a six-star resort that occupies an entire 57-hectare Fijian island. Its Riverlea Park (~12,000 homes) is the largest residential development in South Australia's history.
notes: The input says 'Walter Corp'; this is almost certainly Walker Corp. Wikipedia/ABC confirm Lang Walker's widow is Suzanne, but I couldn't confirm her formal role at the company. She is private and has no public profile. The best route is Walker Corporation media (media@walkercorp.com.au). Mention Lang Walker's death only with care.

name: Binish Hasmukh Chudgar
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad)
profile: Eldest son of Hasmukh Chudgar, the pharmacist who founded Intas in 1976–77. Binish and his brothers Nimish (vice chairman and MD) and Urmish (MD, a haematologist who built the biologics unit) grew it into one of India's largest privately held drugmakers, with 22 plants in India, the UK, Greece and Mexico and sales in 100+ countries via subsidiary Accord Healthcare. The family owns about 84%, alongside Temasek and ChrysCapital.
interesting_fact: Intas's biologics unit was certified EU-GMP compliant in April 2007 for its biosimilar filgrastim, the first Indian company to reach that milestone. Accord Healthcare has since become a major generics and biosimilars player in Europe.
notes: Very private family; minimal personal press coverage. No sourced personal deep-cut fact was found, because the web-search budget ran out. Wealth is shared with his brothers on rich lists. Approach via Intas corporate communications.

name: Ipec Kirac
current_role: Board member, Koç Holding; Chair, Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation, TEGV and Sirena Marine
profile: İpek Kıraç, granddaughter of Koç Group founder Vehbi Koç through her mother Suna Kıraç, holds a significant stake in Koç Holding, Turkey's largest conglomerate, and has sat on its board since 2016. A Brown biology graduate, she ran yacht builder Sirena Marine as CEO (2012-18) and now chairs it, while leading the family's education and culture philanthropy.
interesting_fact: In 2026 she became the first Turkish member of the Brookings Institution's International Advisory Council, the same year she completed a master's in public health at Brown.
deep_cut_fact: She founded 'Suna's Daughters', a girls' education initiative named for her mother, and chairs the SemtPati Foundation, an animal-welfare organisation; earlier, as Sirena Marine CEO, she made the yacht builder one of Turkey's top 500 exporters.
notes: Forbes spelling 'Ipec' = İpek Kıraç. Engaged in public life via foundations (TEGV is a reasonable route). Avoid ongoing family legal matters concerning her father İnan Kıraç.

name: Nimish Hasmukh Chudgar
current_role: Managing Director (reported as joint MD/CEO), Intas Pharmaceuticals Ltd, Ahmedabad
profile: Nimish Chudgar co-founded Intas Pharmaceuticals in 1985 with his father Hasmukh and brothers Binish and Urmish. Intas, owner of Accord Healthcare, has grown into a large generics and biosimilars exporter, with about two-thirds of revenue from abroad. Nimish leads manufacturing, technical operations and the domestic business.
interesting_fact: Intas's turnover rose from Rs 20 crore in 1999 to about Rs 7,500 crore by 2017. About 65% came from exports, through a footprint that includes a large UK plant in Barnstaple.
deep_cut_fact: Industry veteran Sanjiv Kaul, who met the Chudgar brothers while at Ranbaxy in the late 1990s, called Nimish 'the go-to guy' with 'great technical skills and the ability to set up world class infrastructure.' His brothers were 'the visionary' (Binish) and 'Mr Science' (Urmish).
notes: Very low media profile; brother Binish is usually the family's public face. Intas is privately held (backed in the past by Temasek/ChrysCapital), so there is no listed-company IR channel. Route through Intas corporate communications.

name: Urmish Hasmukh Chudgar
current_role: Joint Managing Director, Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); heads its biopharma/biosimilars business
profile: One of three sons of Intas founder Hasmukh Chudgar who run the privately held Ahmedabad drugmaker, a major generics and biosimilars supplier operating globally via Accord Healthcare and, in the US, Accord BioPharma. A Gujarat University-trained physician, Urmish built Intas's biotech arm, incorporated as Intas Biopharmaceuticals in 2006 and later merged back into Intas.
interesting_fact: Intas's US arm Accord BioPharma bought the UDENYCA (pegfilgrastim) franchise from Coherus in 2025, making Intas one of the world's largest pegfilgrastim suppliers, and targets 20 US biosimilar launches by 2030.
deep_cut_fact: He is a practising haemato-oncologist, described as 'the man behind the biotech initiatives at Intas'; he steered its biotech R&D subsidiary (Indus Biotherapeutics) and once told BioSpectrum, 'We plan to release one product every six months.'
notes: Low public profile; brother Binish Chudgar (chairman/MD) is usually the company spokesperson, so don't misattribute press quotes. Only a general corporate email is published; no dedicated press address found.

name: Gunther Lehner
current_role: Family owner and former CEO (1997-2021) of ALPLA Group, Hard, Austria; son Philipp Lehner is CEO since 2021
profile: Günther Lehner is the second-generation owner of ALPLA, the Vorarlberg plastic-packaging maker his father Alwin and uncle Helmuth founded in 1955. He took over management in 1997 and built ALPLA into one of the world's largest rigid-packaging makers (bottles, caps, preforms), with ~206 plants in 45 countries and €5.2bn sales in 2025. He handed the CEO role to son Philipp in 2021.
interesting_fact: ALPLA began in 1955 as a start-up in a laundry room (Waschküche) in Hard; in 1958 the brothers built the Alplamat, the first extrusion blow-moulding machine for plastic bottles.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1990s he pushed ALPLA into recycling, turning it into a 'system provider'. ALPLA has run PET recycling since taking majority control of Austria's PET Recycling Team in 2010 and now operates rPET/rHDPE plants in about 10 countries.

public_contacts.value: erik.nielsen@alpla.com (Erik Nielsen, Team Leader Corporate Communications, ALPLA)

notes: Low public profile; CEO Philipp Lehner is now the public face. No death reported, but no recent appearance confirmed either. FY2025 results: https://blog.alpla.com/en/press-release/newsroom/stable-financial-year-2025-alpla-achieves-turnover-eu52-billion

name: Brian Kim
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of Kakao; head of Kakao's Future Initiative Center (stepped back from frontline management)
profile: Kim Beom-soo ('Brian Kim', b. 1966) grew up poor, earned engineering degrees at Seoul National University, founded online-game portal Hangame in 1998 (merged into NHN/Naver) and in 2010 launched KakaoTalk, now Korea's dominant messenger. Kakao spans Kakao Pay, Kakao Bank, entertainment and mobility; he signed the Giving Pledge in 2021. Since 2026 he has re-emerged publicly, focused on Kakao's AI push.
interesting_fact: He grew up in poverty, paid his way through Seoul National University by private tutoring and sometimes skipped meals to save money, then built Kakao into one of Korea's biggest tech groups.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first company, online game portal Hangame, in 1998 with about $184,000 given to him by friends and family; it later merged with Naver to form NHN, where he became co-CEO.
notes: Hurun lists him under 'Kakao Pay Corp'. Acquitted at first instance (Oct 2025) in the SM Entertainment share case; prosecutors' appeal was pending at Seoul High Court as of mid-2026, so outreach timing is sensitive. Made first public appearance post-acquittal Jan 2026 at Kakao's AI campus. Route via Kakao corporate communications.

name: RG Chandramogan
current_role: Founder and Chairman & Managing Director, Hatsun Agro Product Ltd (Chennai)
profile: Tamil Nadu entrepreneur who started selling 'Arun' ice cream from a 250 sq ft rented unit in Royapuram, Chennai, in 1970 with Rs 13,000 from the sale of family land, often pushing the cart himself. He built Hatsun Agro Product into India's largest private-sector dairy (Arun Ice Creams, Arokya milk, Hatsun curd/paneer, Ibaco), sourcing directly from hundreds of thousands of farmers.
interesting_fact: He started Arun Ice Creams in 1970 with Rs 13,000 and four employees, producing up to 10,000 ice creams a day, and grew it into a dairy group worth roughly Rs 20,000 crore.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as an apprentice at a timber depot in Viluppuram, about 160 km from Chennai, earning Rs 65 a month for roughly a year - taking orders and doing manual labour - before he went into ice cream. He had attended a pre-university course at St Xavier's College, Palayamkottai.
notes: Classic self-made entrepreneurship story; has given interviews to Indian business media (e.g. Outlook Business 'Doughty Milkman', https://www.outlookbusiness.com/magazine/story/doughty-milkman-4559). Route via Hatsun corporate office (info@hap.in).

name: Dinesh Krishnaswamy
current_role: Co-founder, Infosys; President of the Board of Trustees, Infosys Science Foundation (Infosys Prize)
profile: K. Dinesh (Dinesh Krishnaswamy) is one of the seven engineers who co-founded Infosys with N.R. Narayana Murthy in 1981. At Infosys he headed quality, information systems and communication design, and chaired Infosys Technologies Australia, before leaving the board in 2011. He now focuses on philanthropy, including the Infosys Prize for science and research.
interesting_fact: As President of the Infosys Science Foundation's trustees, he helps award the annual Infosys Prize, which recognises Indian researchers in six categories, from engineering and computer science to the humanities.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he co-founded the Ashraya Hastha Trust, which works on animal welfare, health, education, livelihoods and the environment. It backed a cancer centre at Narayana Health and built a clinic in the Mysuru area.
notes: Low public profile among the Infosys co-founders. The likely route is the Infosys Science Foundation. Note Hurun spells his name 'Dinesh Krishnaswamy'; he is usually known as K. Dinesh.

name: Byron D. Trott
current_role: Founder, Chairman and co-CEO, BDT & MSD Partners (Chicago/New York merchant bank)
profile: Byron Trott spent 27 years at Goldman Sachs, rising to vice chairman of investment banking. In 2009 he founded BDT & Company to advise and invest alongside family and founder-led businesses. It merged with Michael Dell's MSD Partners in 2023 to form BDT & MSD, which he co-runs with Gregg Lemkau.
interesting_fact: Known as 'Warren Buffett's favorite banker', he had Buffett's public backing when he left Goldman in 2009 to start BDT. In 2026 the Museum of American Finance gave him its Whitehead Award for Distinguished Public Service and Financial Leadership.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in small-town Union, Missouri, he played varsity baseball and football at the University of Chicago and started at Goldman in 1982 as a stockbroker. In 2018 he and his wife Tina founded rootEd Alliance, which funds college and career counselors in rural high schools.
notes: Low-profile dealmaker who rarely does media. The rootEd Alliance (rural education) and his UChicago philanthropy (Trott Business Program) are warmer angles than deals. BDT & MSD focuses on family and founder-led businesses, which fits an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Narendrakumar Kalyanji Parekh
current_role: Promoter shareholder, Pidilite Industries (Fevicol maker); stepped down as non-executive vice-chairman in May 2023 and reported to have resigned from the board in Feb 2024
profile: N.K. Parekh is a member of the founding Parekh family of Mumbai-based Pidilite Industries, the adhesives and specialty-chemicals company behind Fevicol, M-Seal and Fevikwik, founded by Balvant Parekh. A former joint managing director, he served as non-executive vice-chairman until May 2023 and held ~5.4 crore Pidilite shares as of March 2024. His son Apurva N. Parekh is executive vice-chairman.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's Fevicol is one of India's best-known household brands, and the Parekh family built the company into the country's adhesives leader.
notes: Elderly and retired from the board (resignation as director announced 29 Feb 2024 per MarketScreener; FY23-24 governance report: https://annual-reports.pidilite.com/Annual-Report-2023-24/pdf/CORPORATE%20GOVERNANCE%20REPORT%2015-7-24.pdf). Alive status not confirmed (still on Hurun 2026 list). Very low public profile; best route via Pidilite corporate communications.

name: S.D. Shibulal
current_role: Infosys co-founder; Permanent Trustee, Shibulal Family Philanthropic Initiatives (SFPI); co-founder, Axilor Ventures
profile: One of Infosys' seven co-founders (1981) who rose to CEO and MD of Infosys (2011-2014). Since retiring he has focused on philanthropy with wife Kumari through SFPI and the Sarojini Damodaran Foundation, and on backing startups via accelerator Axilor Ventures, while the family holds Infosys shares and property investments.
interesting_fact: SFPI's Vidyadhan scholarship programme uses an 'Each One, Teach One' model where former scholars, once financially stable, sponsor another student; it aims to grow from 20,000+ scholarships in 10 states to 100,000 nationwide.
deep_cut_fact: The family's philanthropy began in 1998 by sponsoring the education of just two children from Shibulal's hometown school in Alappuzha, Kerala - the seed of the Vidyadhan programme.
notes: Quote: 'Education has the power to transform the overall health of underserved communities.' Kumari Shibulal is the public face of the foundation work. Route via SFPI / Sarojini Damodaran Foundation.

name: Thomas Kurian
current_role: CEO, Google Cloud (Alphabet), since January 2019
profile: Kerala-born, Princeton-trained engineer Thomas Kurian spent 22 years at Oracle, rising to president of product development over a ~35,000-person engineering org, which made him wealthy via Oracle equity. Since 2019 he has run Google Cloud, turning it into a profitable, fast-growing business at the centre of Google's AI infrastructure and data-center buildout.
interesting_fact: His identical twin George Kurian is CEO of NetApp; in 1996 the twins effectively swapped careers - George moved from Oracle to McKinsey while Thomas left McKinsey to join Oracle.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Pampady, Kottayam, he and his twin boarded at Jesuit-run St Joseph's Boys' High School in Bangalore; both got into IIT Madras but took the SAT there and won partial scholarships to Princeton, moving to the US at 17. He graduated summa cum laude in electrical engineering.
notes: Wealth listed by Hurun is attributed to Oracle; he now runs Google Cloud - highly relevant for a data-center/AI podcast. Route via Google Cloud press team. X handle @ThomasOrTK ('CEO of @GoogleCloud') confirmed only via an aggregator; he is also active on LinkedIn.

name: Mahabir Prasad Agarwal
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (advisory), Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (NSE: SHYAMMETL); stepped down as chairman in May 2025
profile: Kolkata-based first-generation steel entrepreneur and co-promoter of Shyam Metalics and Energy, an integrated maker of ferro alloys, steel, aluminium foil and captive power, listed in 2021. He chaired the company until May 2025, when he resigned citing his age. Brij Bhushan Agarwal became chairman and MD, and Mahabir Prasad Agarwal stayed on as chairman emeritus.
interesting_fact: When he stepped down as chairman in May 2025, Shyam Metalics kept him on as chairman emeritus in an advisory role rather than letting him retire outright.
notes: Elderly and retired from the chair, so a low public profile. The company's Head of IR is Pankaj Harlalka, per the Nov 2026 earnings-call transcript. Unverified social posts say he started as a steel trader around 1970 and opened a sponge-iron plant in Sambalpur in 1990; these are not used as facts. The current chairman and MD, Brij Bhushan Agarwal, is the more active spokesman.

name: Sandy Li
current_role: Likely co-founder, Trendy International Group (Guangzhou fashion group behind Ochirly) - unconfirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun (2014-2016) as sharing a fortune with Jack Xu from Trendy, the Guangzhou apparel group founded in 1999 (Ochirly, Five Plus, Trendiano). Sources name Xu's wife and co-founder as Li Shanhu (Shanhu Li); whether 'Sandy Li' is the same person could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Trendy International was the first Chinese apparel group to receive investment from LVMH's L Capital Asia (about $200m, 2012-13) and grew to roughly 3,000 stores in 290 Chinese cities.
notes: Identity ambiguous: the English name 'Sandy Li' does not appear in sources; likely refers to Li Shanhu (李珊瑚), co-founder with husband Jacky Xu (Xu Yu). Very low public profile; route would be via Trendy Group corporate channels.

name: Stefan Fuchs
current_role: CEO (Chairman of the Executive Board), FUCHS SE, Mannheim (contract extended to June 2029)
profile: Third-generation family leader of FUCHS (formerly Fuchs Petrolub), founded in 1931 in Mannheim and now the world's largest independent lubricants supplier with ~6,000 staff in 50+ countries. He joined in 1996, entered the Executive Board in 1999 and has been CEO since 2004; the board extended his contract in Oct 2025 to 2029. (Input name 'Stefan Fuch' is a misspelling.)
interesting_fact: FUCHS has grown from a 1931 Mannheim family business into the world's largest independent supplier of lubrication solutions, independent of the oil majors; Stefan Fuchs has run it for more than 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he spent two years as an auditing assistant at Wollert-Elmendorff Deutsche Industrie-Treuhand in Mannheim, then was posted (1997-99) to Fuchs Lubricants Co. in Harvey, Illinois, responsible for Argentina, Brazil and Mexico. He also sits on the supervisory board of machine-tool maker TRUMPF.
notes: Input name misspelled ('Stefan Fuch'). Press contact Tina Vogel (FUCHS SE Public Relations) per July 2026 release. Born 1968; Mannheim University business graduate.

name: Paolo Zegna
current_role: Non-executive director, Ermenegildo Zegna N.V.; vice-chairman of family holding Monterubello; chairman of Lanificio Ermenegildo Zegna e Figli
profile: Third-generation member of the Zegna family (born Turin 1956, economics degree from Geneva). He was co-CEO of the group in 1998-2006 and chairman from 2006 until the 2021 NYSE listing, and now sits on the board as a non-executive director. His cousin Gildo is executive chairman. He also chairs the historic Trivero wool mill.
interesting_fact: He served as president of Sistema Moda Italia, Italy's textile and apparel industry association. He has also been vice-president of the Altagamma Foundation and sits on the council of Euratex, the European textile association.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs Achill Land Pty Ltd, the company behind Zegna's 60%-owned Achill merino sheep farm east of Armidale, New South Wales. Zegna bought into the farm in 2014 to secure its own fine-wool supply. Sixth-generation grower Charlie Coventry kept the other 40%.
notes: The source of wealth matches (Zegna). No personal social accounts found. The best route is the group's corporate press office, which is run by Paola Durante, Chief of External Relations.

name: N R Narayan Murthy
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Infosys; founder of Catamaran Ventures (family investment firm)
profile: Born 1946 in Sidlaghatta, Karnataka, Murthy co-founded Infosys in 1981 with six colleagues and Rs 10,000 borrowed from his wife Sudha Murty. He was CEO 1981-2002 and later chairman, and pioneered the Global Delivery Model for IT outsourcing from India. Now chairman emeritus, he invests via Catamaran Ventures and speaks often on entrepreneurship and work culture.
interesting_fact: Time magazine and CNBC have called him the 'father of the Indian IT sector'; Fortune listed him among the 12 greatest entrepreneurs of our time, and he co-chaired the World Economic Forum in Davos in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: Before Infosys, as chief systems programmer at IIM Ahmedabad he worked on India's first time-sharing computer system and designed and implemented a BASIC interpreter for Electronics Corporation of India Ltd; his first startup, Softronics, folded after roughly a year and a half.
notes: Infosys press is a company route; he holds no executive role. Catamaran Ventures is his personal investment vehicle (no published email found). Father-in-law of Rishi Sunak. Frequent public speaker, so likely receptive to a founder-story podcast.

name: Sun Xiang
current_role: Reported president of Sinogiant Group (Xinhua United Metallurgical Holding Group), chaired by his father Sun Jimu
profile: Sun Xiang is linked to Sinogiant Group (新华联合冶金控股集团), a private Chinese iron and steel holding company founded by his father Sun Jimu, with steel complexes in Huanghua (Cangzhou) and Tangshan, Hebei. The family shared a Hurun listing (2011-2018). Little recent public information.
interesting_fact: Sinogiant was formed in 2004 as the holding entity for Sun Jimu's industrial interests; one profile says Sun Xiang was formerly a delegate to the Hebei Provincial People's Congress (single source).
notes: Only single-source confirmation of Sun Xiang's role; wealth shared with father Sun Jimu. Very low public profile, Chinese-language channels only. Not on lists since 2018.

name: Jim Chanos
current_role: Founder, Chanos & Company (formerly Kynikos Associates); closed outside-capital hedge funds end-2023, now advisory/commentary
profile: Greek-American short seller who founded Kynikos Associates in 1985 with $16M and became famous for shorting Enron before its 2001 collapse. He returned outside capital at end-2023 and now runs Chanos & Company in an advisory capacity while remaining a prominent market commentator, notably sceptical of AI/data-center accounting.
interesting_fact: He has been an outspoken critic of AI infrastructure economics, arguing on X that GPU depreciation lives at hyperscalers are too long and calling neoclouds like CoreWeave 'financial conduits, not technology companies' - directly relevant to a data-center podcast.
