profile: Third child of Gina Rinehart. With her siblings she is a beneficiary of a family trust that holds a large stake in Hancock Prospecting, the Pilbara iron-ore group. She has no public operating role in the business and keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She went to boarding school at Switzerland's Institut Le Rosey.
notes: Very private passive heiress with no operating role in mining, energy or data centres, so a poor fit for the podcast. Most of her press coverage concerns the family trust dispute; avoid it. A search found nothing recent. If approached at all, go through Hancock Prospecting media relations, though they represent the company rather than her.

name: Stephane Bonvin
current_role: Founder, CEO and director, Investis Holding SA (SIX: IREN), Zurich
profile: Stéphane Bonvin founded Investis in 1994 and built it into a Swiss residential landlord with 3,000+ apartments around Lake Geneva. He listed it on SIX in 2016 and still holds a large majority stake. He co-founded private equity firm Patrimonium in 2006/07, ran it until 2015 and sold his stake in 2022. Investis has since sold its real estate services segment to focus on owning property.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Patrimonium in 2006, ran it until 2015 and sold his stake in 2022 to focus on Investis. In a 2026 interview he set a target of CHF 100m in rental income.

public_contacts.value: laurence.bienz@investisgroup.com (Laurence Bienz, Head Investor & Media Relations, +41 58 201 72 42)

notes: Low public profile, with few interviews and no personal social accounts found. Best route is Investis media/IR. Investis is residential real estate only, so energy/data-centre relevance is limited.

name: Mehmet Sinan Tara (Tara family)
current_role: Head of the Tara family / ENKA group (Tara Holding largest ENKA shareholder); passed ENKA İnşaat board chair to son Agah Mehmet Tara in 2022
profile: Mehmet Sinan Tara is the son of ENKA co-founder Şarık Tara and the largest shareholder of ENKA İnşaat, the Istanbul-listed engineering, construction, power-generation and real-estate group (580 projects in 58 countries). He ran ENKA for decades before handing the listed company's chairmanship to his son Agah in 2022; ENKA now also operates data centers near Istanbul.
interesting_fact: ENKA has been the biggest builder of U.S. embassy and consular buildings over roughly the past 20 years, with projects from Algeria and Nepal to the Netherlands.
deep_cut_fact: The name ENKA comes from the first syllables of the Turkish words 'enişte' and 'kayınbirader' (brother-in-law), reflecting its 1957 founding by Şarık Tara and his brother-in-law Sadi Gülçelik.
notes: enka@enka.com is ENKA's general corporate address. Sources differ on whether Sinan took over in 1984 (Forbes US) or 1994 (Forbes Türkiye). Podcast angle: ENKA is Turkey's leading private power producer and runs EDS data centers (IST 01 Tuzla, IST 02 Gebze); son Agah Mehmet Tara is the operational leader and likelier guest.

name: Deng Weiming
current_role: Chairman and President, CNGR Advanced Material Co. (中伟股份; Shenzhen 300919 / HKEX-listed)
profile: Born 1968 in Shaoyang, Hunan, Deng founded the Zhongwei group in 1995 around coal chemicals and trading, pivoted to new energy by buying a lithium-battery precursor maker in 2013, and spun out CNGR in 2014 in Tongren, Guizhou. CNGR makes nickel/cobalt precursor materials for cathodes supplied to Tesla, LG Chem and CATL; it listed in Shenzhen in 2020 and Hong Kong in 2025.
interesting_fact: After its 2020 Shenzhen ChiNext listing, CNGR at one point became the second-most valuable listed company in Guizhou province, behind only Kweichow Moutai.
deep_cut_fact: Deng studied organic chemistry at Taiyuan University of Science and Technology and began his career as a technician at a state-owned coking plant in Shaodong, Hunan, before quitting to try property trading in Hainan during the early-1990s boom.
notes: Chinese-language outreach recommended. He and his wife Wu Xiaoge jointly control ~56% of CNGR. Early-career details come from a Chinese media summary (Touzijie, reposted on Bilibili) of the HK IPO prospectus.

name: Said Gutseriev
current_role: Russian-British investor; founder of Larnabel Ventures; shareholder in SFI holding (Europlan leasing, VSK insurance) - reportedly exited M.Video board in 2025
profile: Said Gutseriev (b. 1988, Moscow) is the son of oligarch Mikhail Gutseriev and was educated in the UK from age 8. After an analyst stint at Glencore he took board roles in family oil, refining and coal businesses from 2014, then built holdings in retailer M.Video and investment group SFI. Reports say he left M.Video's board in 2025 after signalling plans to sell.
interesting_fact: He holds an Oxford master's degree in geology and an MA in oil & gas management from the University of Plymouth.
deep_cut_fact: He started out (2012-2014) as an analyst in Glencore's London structured-financing department for oil projects, later moving to the trader's finance office.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (28 June 2022) and EU over his SFI directorship - check legal/sanctions implications before any outreach or featuring. No published personal contact or official social accounts found. M.Video ownership in flux in 2025 (interfax.ru/business/860507).

name: Massimo Moratti
current_role: Private investor; former chairman/CEO of Saras (Italian oil refiner) and former owner/president of Inter Milan
profile: Son of Angelo Moratti, who founded Sardinian refiner Saras in 1962, Massimo ran the company with brother Gian Marco and took it public in 2006. In 2024 the Moratti family sold about 35% of Saras to trader Vitol at EUR 1.75/share, triggering a takeover and delisting. He is best known for owning Inter Milan for ~two decades, selling his last shares in 2016.
interesting_fact: His Inter Milan tenure included five straight Serie A titles and the 2010 treble (Serie A, Coppa Italia and Champions League), plus that year's Club World Cup.
deep_cut_fact: As Inter president he conceived Inter Campus, the club's social project that since 1997 has used youth football to help children in need, starting in Recife, Brazil; it now reaches thousands of kids worldwide.
notes: Forbes bio is outdated: family sold its Saras control to Vitol (closed June 2024; Vitol press release https://www.vitol.com/members-of-the-moratti-family-enter-into-an-agreement-to-sell-approx-35-of-saras-to-vitol/). No personal channels; reachable mainly via Italian press/football world. Brother Gian Marco died 2018.

name: Grigory Berezkin
current_role: Owner and Chairman of the Board, ESN Group and RBC Group (Russian media holding)
profile: Moscow-born chemist-turned-investor Berezkin made his fortune in Russian oil and power: he arranged the sale of KomiTEK to Lukoil (~$600m+) and built Rusenergosbyt, an electricity trader supplying Gazprom, Russian Railways and Transneft, selling ~half to Enel in 2006. He later moved into media (Komsomolskaya Pravda, Metro Moscow) and has controlled RBC since 2017.
interesting_fact: In 2000-2003 his group ran Kolenergo, a power system operating largely above the Arctic Circle, building cross-border links to Finland and Norway that let it export electricity and trade on the Nord Pool exchange.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD in chemical sciences (1993) from Moscow State University, where he was a junior research fellow until 1994. He backs the International Chemistry Olympiad and in 2022 created the Viktor Berezkin Prize for young chromatography researchers, named for his chemist father.
notes: No published personal/office contact found; ESN Group site appears defunct. Route, if any, would be via RBC Group corporate office. He was on EU sanctions list Apr 2022-Sep 2023 (delisted); journalist should check current US/UK sanctions status before any engagement.

name: Arthur Mensch
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Mistral AI (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique graduate with an ML PhD (Paris-Saclay), ex-DeepMind Paris (early Gemini work), who co-founded Mistral AI in 2023. Mistral builds open-weight LLMs and raised $2bn at a $14bn valuation in Sept 2025; it is now building its own compute, including a debt-financed site near Paris and a 1 GW target by 2030.
interesting_fact: Mistral is turning into an infrastructure player: it borrowed $830m to build a 44 MW Nvidia GB300 data centre at Bruyeres-le-Chatel near Paris, targets 200 MW by end-2027 and 1 GW by 2030; Mensch has put the cost of a gigawatt of compute at about $50bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before LLMs he was a neuroimaging researcher: his PhD (Inria Parietal team, supervised by Bertrand Thirion) was 'Apprentissage de representations en imagerie fonctionnelle' - learning representations of human cognition from fMRI brain scans, including fast dictionary learning for massive matrix factorisation.
notes: Highly relevant for a data-centre/energy podcast (Mistral Compute, French nuclear power as AI advantage). press@mistral.ai is the official press/events route. X handle @arthurmensch is widely attributed to him but the profile page itself was not fetched directly.

name: Guillaume Lample
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Mistral AI (Paris)
profile: French AI researcher (École Polytechnique, CMU master's) who spent years at Meta's FAIR, co-authoring the original LLaMA paper. In April 2023 he co-founded Mistral AI with Arthur Mensch and Timothée Lacroix; it builds open-weight LLMs and raised ~$2B at a ~$14B valuation in Sept 2025. He leads its science work.
interesting_fact: Mistral's $113M raise in 2023, weeks after founding, was then Europe's largest-ever seed round.
deep_cut_fact: As a CMU student he co-built 'Arnold' with Devendra Chaplot, a deep-RL agent that played Doom from raw pixels; at the 2016 Visual Doom AI Competition it placed second in both tracks but had the fewest deaths and best kill-to-death ratio by a wide margin.
notes: Active on X and does tech podcasts (e.g. Latent Space-style episodes on Voxtral in 2026), so a good podcast candidate for AI/compute. Mistral is also building its own data-center capacity in France, a natural hook. Route via press@mistral.ai or X.

name: Timothy Dunn
current_role: CEO, CrownQuest Operating (Midland, Texas)
profile: Texas Tech chemical engineer (b. 1955) who worked at Exxon Production Research, ran oil-and-gas lending at First City National Bank and was CFO of Parker & Parsley before founding CrownQuest in 1996. Early Permian Basin leases made CrownRock, his venture with Lime Rock, a major producer; Occidental agreed to buy CrownRock for about $12B in Dec 2023. He is also one of Texas's largest conservative political donors.
interesting_fact: Some of Dunn's fortune came from acquiring cheap Permian Basin leases years before fracking made the oil there economical to extract; CrownQuest was Texas's eighth-largest oil producer in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: He played lead guitar in a rock band from high school through Texas Tech, says making Eagle Scout is the early achievement he is proudest of, and scrapped plans for law school to take a job at Exxon Production Research, which sent him to the Middle East three times.
notes: Politically prominent and frequently profiled critically by Texas media; keep outreach on energy/entrepreneurship. His own site directs people to his Yellow Balloons Bible-teaching podcast; the contact form is for that ministry. CrownQuest's website lists no contact email.

name: Timothée Lacroix
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Mistral AI (Paris)
profile: French AI researcher who spent years at Meta's FAIR lab in Paris (co-author of the original LLaMA paper) before co-founding Mistral AI in 2023 with Arthur Mensch and Guillaume Lample. As CTO he leads Mistral's technical work on open-weight models (Mistral 7B, Mixtral, Magistral, Voxtral) and its European compute build-out; Bloomberg reported the trio became France's first AI billionaires in 2025.
interesting_fact: He is a co-author of Meta's 2023 'LLaMA: Open and Efficient Foundation Language Models' paper, published months before he co-founded Mistral.
deep_cut_fact: Long before LLMs, he co-authored TorchCraft (2016), a library connecting the game StarCraft to machine-learning research, and later PyTorch-BigGraph (2019) and HyperTree Proof Search for neural theorem proving (2022); his ICML 2018 work was on tensor decomposition for knowledge-base completion.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Arthur Mensch; technical framing (inference efficiency, compute/data centers like Mistral Compute) likely to resonate. Route via Mistral press.

name: Christopher Cline
current_role: Deceased (died 4 July 2019); was founder of Foresight Energy / Cline Group coal operations
profile: Chris Cline was a West Virginia-born coal entrepreneur who built Illinois Basin coal producer Foresight Energy. He died on 4 July 2019 in a helicopter crash in the Bahamas; per instructions the rest of the profile is skipped.
notes: Died 4 July 2019 (Miami Herald; Wikipedia 'Chris Cline'). Not a viable podcast guest.

name: Sit Kwong Lam
current_role: Reportedly chairman of Shenzhen Brightoil Group and founder of Marine Online (Singapore); former chairman of HK-listed Brightoil Petroleum (left 2019) - current status unverified
profile: Hong Kong oil entrepreneur who founded Brightoil in 1993 and built Brightoil Petroleum into a HK-listed marine-fuel bunkering, oil-tanker and upstream oil & gas group, serving as chairman (and CEO 2008-2014). He left the board in 2019 and returned briefly as strategic adviser; Brightoil later spun up Marine Online, a maritime e-commerce platform.
interesting_fact: Brightoil was among the largest marine-fuel suppliers in Asian ports and launched Marine Online, an early one-stop e-commerce platform for shipowners and charterers to buy bunkers and services.
notes: Low priority: his billionaire status (Forbes 2011-2017, Hurun to 2018) ended after Brightoil's 2019 restructuring and a personal bankruptcy order; avoid referencing that. No published personal/office contacts found and no 2025-26 news located; alive status not confirmed.

name: David Chow
current_role: Macau businessman; co-founder and former co-chairman of Macau Legend Development (developer of Macau Fisherman's Wharf); no longer on its board
profile: Hong Kong-born (1950) Macau entrepreneur and former legislator (13 years, until 2009) who developed Macau Fisherman's Wharf, the themed waterfront complex opened 2005-06, and co-founded Macau Legend Development in 2006, which ran the Babylon and Pharaoh's Palace casinos under SJM's licence. He has since exited the board and cut his stake to a fraction of a percent.
interesting_fact: Fisherman's Wharf was built partly on reclaimed land (about 40% of its area) and once housed Macau's first roller coaster, inside an artificial volcano topped by a Potala Palace replica.
deep_cut_fact: Besides his gaming and tourism businesses, he has served as Honorary Consul of the Republic of Cape Verde to the Macau SAR.
notes: Full name Chow Kam Fai, David (周錦輝). Fortune largely eroded: GGRAsia reported in April 2025 he held only ~0.39% of Macau Legend after a debt settlement. Forbes listing is from 2014 only. No personal published contact found; outreach would have to go via Macau business channels.

name: Alexander Shchukin
profile: Kuzbass coal magnate and co-founder of the Sibuglemet coal holding (Kemerovo region, Russia); former Forbes-list billionaire. Died in Novokuznetsk in July 2021, aged 70.
notes: Deceased: Kommersant (20 Jul 2021) reports Sibuglemet co-founder Alexander Shchukin, a former Forbes-list member and coal magnate, died in Novokuznetsk aged 70 (https://kommersant.ru/doc/4909362). Identity match is by coal/Russia/Forbes-list profile; rest skipped per instructions.

name: Vladimir Melnichenko
current_role: Former co-owner of Sibuglemet (Kuzbass coking-coal holding, incl. OAO Mezhdurechye); no current public role found
profile: Russian coal businessman from Kemerovo (Kuzbass), one of the co-owners of coking-coal producer Sibuglemet with Anatoly Skurov, Valentin Bukhtoyarov and Alexander Shchukin. Kommersant calls him an ex-owner of Sibuglemet and of its Mezhdurechye mine. His only Forbes listing is 2011 (coal, about $1.8bn); his stake was reportedly sold around 2013-14.
interesting_fact: Sibuglemet, one of Russia's larger coking-coal suppliers from the Kuzbass basin, was held by four roughly equal partners; Kommersant photographed and named him as an ex-owner in 2014.
notes: Not Andrey Melnichenko (SUEK/EuroChem). Kommersant confirms a Vladimir Melnichenko as ex-Sibuglemet/Mezhdurechye owner, but no source ties that person to Forbes' 2011 entry, so identity stays 'uncertain'. Forbes.ru's 2011 list is JS-rendered and English/Russian searches found nothing more. He was named in a 2014 Kemerovo criminal case (avoid). No published contacts; not a realistic guest.

name: Valentin Bukhtoyarov
current_role: Former co-founder, shareholder and VP for finance/economics of Sibuglemet coal holding (Kuzbass); no current public role found
profile: Valentin Petrovich Bukhtoyarov (b. 1955, Kemerovo region) is a Kuzbass coal-mining engineer who in 1995 co-founded Sibuglemet, a coking-coal producer, with Anatoly Skurov, Anatoly Smolyaninov and Vladimir Melnichenko, later serving as its VP for finance. Forbes Russia ranked him #52 in 2011 at $1.8B; the founders sold the holding to Akhmet Palankoev in 2013 after a shareholder dispute.
interesting_fact: Ranked 52nd among Russia's 200 richest businessmen by Forbes in 2011 with an estimated $1.8B, from coking coal used in steelmaking.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from the Siberian Metallurgical Institute in 1978 he was assigned to the Kalinin mine of Prokopyevskugol and rose to become director of the Yesaulskaya mine before moving to Kuznetskugol as supply director in 1994.
notes: Very private; only on Forbes list in 2011. Sibuglemet was sold in 2013 and its successor is under US/Canadian sanctions (2022) - outreach to Russian coal interests may carry sanctions/compliance considerations. No death reported; alive status not confirmed. No published contacts found (sibuglemet.ru unreachable).

name: Mario Brescia Cafferata
current_role: Deceased (died 16 May 2013, Lima); was co-chairman of Grupo Breca and chairman of BBVA Continental
notes: Died May 2013. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Brescia_Cafferata ; https://www.mch.cl/fallece-empresario-peruano-mario-brescia-presidente-del-holding-breca-dueno-de-cemento-melon-y-pinturas-tricolor/ . Grupo Breca is now run by the next generation of the Brescia family.

name: Qin Hui
current_role: Former controlling shareholder of Stellar Megamedia / SMI Holdings Group (星美控股), a Chinese cinema chain; no confirmed current role
profile: Qin Hui (覃辉), a Chongqing-born businessman, built the Stellar (星美) cinema and media group, one of China's larger theatre circuits in the 2010s, listed in Hong Kong as SMI Holdings. His brother Qin Hong ran day-to-day operations. Forbes listed him at #1339 on its 2018 billionaires list (Media & Entertainment). The group fell into a debt and cash-flow crisis from late 2018.
interesting_fact: Stellar was among the earliest private cinema chains to expand nationwide after China's film-distribution reforms. In 2010 SMI agreed to buy 25 cinemas directly from Qin Hui for HK$55m.
notes: The Forbes profile (forbes.com/profile/qin-hui) links him to SMI Holdings Group; he is NOT the historian Qin Hui (秦晖). Recent coverage is mostly negative: a 2018 CSRC 5-year securities-market ban over the listed unit Shengleda, and Stellar's debt crisis. Last on the Forbes list in 2018. No reachable public contacts found. Low priority for outreach.

name: Arthur Demoulas
current_role: Major shareholder and former president & CEO (2008-2025) of DeMoulas Super Markets (Market Basket); no longer in management
profile: Arthur T. Demoulas (b. 1955), grandson of the Greek immigrants who opened DeMoulas Market in Lowell, Mass., in 1917, ran New England grocer Market Basket as CEO from 2008, growing sales from about $3bn to $4bn and staff from 14,000 to 25,000. He and his sisters control the company; the board removed him from management in 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2014, after the board fired him, Market Basket employees and customers staged weeks of walkouts and boycotts until he was reinstated and his side of the family bought out their cousins - a rare case of rank-and-file workers successfully campaigning for a CEO's return.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989, after the family board rejected his proposal to start a pharmacy division, he founded his own drugstore chain, Lee Drug, and sold its nine stores to Walgreens in 1990. In high school in Andover he played running back on the football team.
notes: Sensitive timing: suspended May 2025, fired Sept 2025; a Delaware court upheld the removal in April 2026 and he said he would not appeal - avoid this topic. Market Basket's corporate channels represent the board, not him; no personal/public channel found. Very private and press-averse. Web search budget ran out during this person.

name: Zhang Huiming
current_role: Co-holder, with Wen Yibo, of the Sound Group environmental business (Sound Environment / Sound Global); no public executive role found
profile: Hurun listed her jointly with Wen Yibo (about $1.8bn, 2014-2020). Wen Yibo founded the Sound water and waste-treatment group in 1993 and chairs HK-listed Sound Global. HK filings show Zhang Huiming holding Sound Global shares through a spouse-interest designation, which suggests she is Wen's wife, but no source confirms this.
interesting_fact: In a March 2019 disclosure, GuruFocus shows Zhang Huiming with a 'spouse interest' in about 774 million Sound Global (HKSE: 00967) shares.
notes: Very low public profile; I found nothing on her as an individual. Wen Yibo is the operating founder, so any outreach would realistically go through the Sound group. Fell off the Hurun lists after 2020.

name: Katherina Andresen
current_role: Board member and co-owner, Ferd (Andresen family investment company, Oslo)
profile: Katharina G. Andresen (born 1995, Oslo) is a sixth-generation member of Norway's Andresen family. In 2007 her father, Johan H. Andresen, transferred most of the family holding company Ferd to her and her sister Alexandra. Ferd invests in listed and private companies, real estate, impact investing and social entrepreneurs. She has sat on Ferd's board since 2023.
interesting_fact: In 2020 Forbes ranked her as the world's third-youngest billionaire. She and her sister own Ferd together with their father, as its fifth and sixth generations of family ownership.
deep_cut_fact: She has served as an advisor to Oslo Pride and is known as a supporter of LGBTQ+ rights. She has also competed as a dressage rider.
notes: Listed country 'Netherlands' is likely a data artefact; she is Norwegian (Oslo) and has reportedly also lived in London. Correct spelling is Katharina. She gives few interviews; the best route is Ferd's press office. Ferd's impact-investing and social-entrepreneur arms may be a natural podcast angle.

name: Phatanee Leksrisompong
current_role: Possibly Deputy Managing Director, Feed Technical/Academic Affairs, Charoen Pokphand Foods (CPF), as of 2020; unverified as the Hurun-listed person
profile: Hurun listed Phatanee Leksrisompong as a CP Group billionaire in 2018-2020, but no source found explains her stake or any link to the Chearavanont family. A CP veteran with this name (spelled Phatthanee) is a CPF deputy MD known as the group's first feed formulator. That person is likely, but not confirmed, to be the Hurun entry.
interesting_fact: A 2020 Thansettakij profile calls the CPF executive 'Khun Noi' the CP group's first feed formulator. It says she led development of iodine-enriched layer feed that raises egg iodine levels, and oversees about 900 staff.
deep_cut_fact: After a chemistry degree from Eastern Kentucky University, her first CP job was calculating feed formulas, at a time when the group brought in an analog computer (1975) for formula calculation.
notes: Identity is uncertain: confirm that the Hurun CP Group shareholder and the CPF feed executive are the same person before using the facts. She is not named among Dhanin Chearavanont's children. MarketScreener links her to CPF Poland. The contacts are CPF corporate addresses only.

name: Raj Kumar Hiranandani
current_role: Founder/owner, Royal Holdings (now presented as RK Global family office), Singapore
profile: Indian-origin Singapore property magnate who formed Royal Holdings in 2011 when the family's Royal Brothers property business was divided with his brother Asok Kumar Hiranandani (Royal Group). Holdings span hotels, offices, retail and medical property, including riverside hotels at Clarke Quay and Robertson Quay. His son Kishin RK runs the affiliated RB Capital.
interesting_fact: A 2014 Wealth-X ranking placed him second among Singapore's richest property tycoons (US$1.4bn), with his brother seventh.
notes: Very low profile; little recent coverage of him personally (no evidence of death found, but nothing recent either). Son Kishin RK (RB Capital CEO, profiled by Tatler/The Peak) is the public face of the family and the more likely interviewee. RB Capital site cross-links RoyalHoldings.com.sg and lists the family office contact.

name: Zhang Yue'e
current_role: Co-founder, Lepu Medical (乐普医疗, SZSE:300003); founder of PW Medtech (普华和顺); current title not confirmed
profile: Materials scientist who, with husband Pu Zhongjie, returned from the US in 1999 to co-found Lepu Medical, one of China's earliest makers of cardiovascular interventional devices (ChiNext listing 2009). She separately founded high-end device maker PW Medtech, listed in Hong Kong in 2013. The couple appeared on Hurun's 2022 global list with about 15bn yuan.
interesting_fact: The 'Lepu family' of companies keeps spinning off: structural-heart unit Xintai Medical was carved out of Lepu Medical for a Hong Kong listing.
deep_cut_fact: She and her husband share the same academic path: both graduated from Xi'an Jiaotong University and both later did graduate study at Florida International University in Miami before coming home to start Lepu.
notes: Wealth listed jointly with husband Pu Zhongjie (Lepu chairman). Very low personal profile; route via Lepu Medical board office/IR (contacts in SZSE filings). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Li Suwen
current_role: Unverified. Hurun lists her as co-holder, with Liu Xuebin, of wealth from 'Cinese' (property developer)
profile: Hurun listed Li Suwen (李素文) jointly with Liu Xuebin in 2018-2021, at about $1.8bn from the property developer 'Cinese'. A MarketScreener insider profile shows a Liu Xuebin (Xue Bin Liu) as chairman of Harvest Property Holdings who formerly chaired Dongguan Cinese Real Estate Development. That suggests a Dongguan developer, but I could not confirm Li Suwen's own role.
notes: Low-confidence identity. The only lead is https://www.zonebourse.com/insider/XUE-BIN-LIU-A0W0OE/ (Liu Xuebin, Dongguan Cinese / Harvest Property). She has been off the lists since 2021. Not an energy or data-centre fit.

name: Claire Bombardier
current_role: Bombardier founding-family shareholder (no executive role found)
profile: Claire Bombardier (Beaudoin) is a daughter of snowmobile inventor Joseph-Armand Bombardier. She married Laurent Beaudoin in 1959, and he ran Bombardier for decades, turning it into a rail and aerospace group. Their son Pierre Beaudoin is chairman of Bombardier. Her wealth comes from the family's stakes in Bombardier and BRP; Hurun listed her in 2014-2015.
interesting_fact: She married Laurent Beaudoin in 1959 while he was studying accounting at the University of Sherbrooke. He joined her father's company as comptroller in 1963 and became president in 1966, after the founder's death.
notes: Very private: no public statements, roles or contacts found, and I couldn't confirm whether she is alive (born c. late 1930s). The family's public faces are Pierre Beaudoin (Bombardier chair) and the J. Armand Bombardier Foundation / Musée de l'ingéniosité in Valcourt. Reaching her would mean going through the family, which the rules rule out, so low priority.

name: Farhad Akhmedov
current_role: Private investor; Chairman of AZNAR (Azerbaijani juice/agriculture company, per Wikipedia); former Northgas chairman
profile: Baku-born Russian-Azerbaijani businessman (b. 1955) who traded oil and gas equipment from London via Tansley Trading, then bought into Siberian gas producer Northgas in the 1990s and chaired it. He sold his remaining 49% to Novatek in 2012 for $1.375B, the core of his fortune; he was a Federation Council senator 2004-2009.
interesting_fact: In the early 1990s he helped bring Amoco and McDermott into talks that led to Azerbaijan's 1994 'Contract of the Century' with an international consortium to develop Caspian oil and gas.
deep_cut_fact: Rejected by MGIMO after Navy service, he took an extramural degree from the Moscow Veterinary Academy in 'Technology and Merchandising Process of Fur Products' (1983) and started out selling furs internationally from London. His juice company AZNAR is named after his father, Teymur.
notes: Spelled Farkhad Akhmedov in most English sources. Was on Hurun 2014-2018 only. Highly publicised divorce litigation and a 2023 leaked call criticising the Kremlin make him a sensitive subject; avoid those topics. No published contact found.

name: Janine Bombardier
current_role: Retired; former president of the Fondation J. Armand Bombardier (1978-2018); Bombardier founding-family shareholder
profile: Janine Bombardier is a daughter of Joseph-Armand Bombardier, inventor of the snowmobile and founder of Bombardier, and aunt of former Bombardier chairman Pierre Beaudoin. Her wealth stems from the family's controlling stake in Bombardier (and BRP); she led the family's philanthropic foundation in Valcourt, Quebec, for four decades before retiring in 2018.
interesting_fact: She co-founded the Fondation J. Armand Bombardier in 1965 with her mother Yvonne and sisters Claire and Huguette, one of the first francophone family foundations in Quebec.
deep_cut_fact: In 1978 she succeeded her mother as president of the foundation, which in 1981 passed $1M in cumulative donations; she and her sisters stepped down in 2018 after 53 years, handing the presidency to niece Nicole Beaudoin.
notes: Elderly, very private; last on Hurun list 2015. No death notice found but no recent public appearances either (alive status unconfirmed). Family foundation (now chaired by Nicole Beaudoin) is the only plausible route; museum general inbox info@museebombardier.com is published on museebombardier.com.

name: Sun Hengchao
current_role: Former chairman and controlling shareholder (~43.7%) of Baota Petrochemical Group, Ningxia; arrested 2018, no current business role confirmed
profile: Founder/chairman of privately owned Baota Petrochemical Group, a Ningxia-based refining and chemicals group, and once reported as the richest man in Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. The group defaulted on debts in 2018; he and his son were arrested, and in Aug 2020 a Yinchuan court tried him and the group on bill-fraud charges (RMB 28.5B in bills).
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: Baota collapsed in 2018 and he was arrested and tried (Aug 2020) on bill-fraud charges; verdict/current status not confirmed. Sources: https://www.caixinglobal.com/2018-11-20/baota-chief-and-son-arrested-after-defaults-101349426.html ; https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2020-08-25/1489119.html

name: Li Liangbin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ganfeng Lithium Group (SZSE: 002460, HKEX: 1772), Xinyu, Jiangxi
profile: Chemistry graduate (b. ~1967) who worked at the state-owned Jiangxi Lithium Factory's research institute before buying a small lithium plant in 1997 that became Ganfeng Lithium. Chairman since 2007, he has built Ganfeng into one of the world's largest lithium producers, supplying EV battery, energy-storage and chemical markets, with resources in Argentina, Mexico and Australia.
interesting_fact: He received a Bauhinia Cup Technology Innovation Award from Hong Kong Polytechnic University in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: In nine years at Jiangxi Lithium Factory he rose from technician to engineer, head of its research institute and manager of its lithium-bromide branch; he quit at 30 in 1997 after seeing Chile's SQM undercut ore-based lithium with brine extraction, and started with a single 10-tonne lithium-metal line.
notes: Media contact (Evan Sun) and IR (A-share info@, H-share and international IR - Samuel Pigott) published on Ganfeng site. Likely needs Chinese-language outreach.

name: Brannin McBee
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Development Officer, CoreWeave (NASDAQ: CRWV)
profile: Former energy/commodities proprietary trader who co-founded CoreWeave in 2017 with Michael Intrator and Brian Venturo; it began as a crypto-mining operation and pivoted into a GPU cloud for AI. CoreWeave IPO'd in 2025 (~$23B valuation) with Microsoft, Meta and OpenAI as key customers; McBee (~6% stake) leads business development, financing and strategic partnerships.
interesting_fact: In 2025 CoreWeave signed a ~$14B deal to supply Meta with AI computing power through 2031, on top of its large Microsoft and OpenAI contracts.
deep_cut_fact: Before CoreWeave he was a proprietary trader in North American natural gas and power markets (Windy Bay Power, 2013-2018; Active Power Investments, focused on natural gas, power and agriculture). He received the Research & Development Council of New Jersey's Science & Technology Medal (2026 Edison Patent Awards).
notes: Ideal fit for an energy + data-center podcast: power-market trading background and CoreWeave's power/data-center buildout; he regularly appears on financial media (Schwab Network, Bloomberg Odd Lots). Route via CoreWeave press team.

name: Zhang Chuanwei
current_role: Chairman & CEO (and Party secretary), Mingyang Smart Energy Group (明阳智能, SSE: 601615)
profile: Former Chongqing government official who went into business in the early 1990s, founding Mingyang Electric in Zhongshan (1993) and turning to wind power in 2006. Mingyang listed on the NYSE in 2010, went private in 2016 and relisted in Shanghai in 2019; it is now one of China's top offshore wind turbine makers, also active in solar, storage and hydrogen, and is pushing into Europe.
interesting_fact: After the UK reportedly blocked Mingyang's planned £1.5bn Scottish turbine factory in 2026, Zhang met Spanish PM Pedro Sánchez in Beijing and pivoted to finding a continental European factory site.
deep_cut_fact: Per Mingyang's IPO prospectus, Zhang worked 1984-88 as a secretary/section chief in the Chongqing municipal Party committee office and then at a Xinyang high-voltage switchgear plant before going south; media report he started Mingyang Electric in Zhongshan with ~10,000 yuan of borrowed money after Deng's 1992 southern tour.
notes: IR emails are for Board Secretary Wang Chengkui and securities representative Zheng Jieshan, from the 2025 annual report summary (also printed in China Securities Journal 29 Apr 2026). Zhang does appear at earnings calls and gives state-media interviews; English-language outreach best via IR/Board Secretary.

name: Radik Shaimiev
current_role: Co-owner of former TAIF Group shareholders' stake in Sibur (petrochemicals); rally driver with TAIF Motorsport
profile: Made his fortune as co-owner of TAIF Group, a Tatarstan holding company whose assets he and partners acquired in Russia's mid-1990s privatizations. In 2021 TAIF merged into petrochemical giant Sibur, giving TAIF's shareholders ~15% of Sibur. Son of Tatarstan's first president Mintimer Shaimiev; brother Airat is also a billionaire.
interesting_fact: An avid racer, he won a European autocross competition in 2003; TAIF also sponsored Rubin Kazan, Russian Premier League champions in 2008 and 2009.
deep_cut_fact: Still racing in 2026: in May he and co-driver Maxim Tsvetkov (TAIF Motorsport) won the Abrau-Dyurso stage of the Tatneft Russian Rally Cup near Novorossiysk by 49 seconds, on a vineyard track back on the calendar after 13 years.
notes: Very private; no personal or office contacts published. Russia-based petrochemical wealth; sanctions/compliance checks advisable before any outreach. Motorsport (TAIF Motorsport) is the friendliest angle.

name: Jeffrey Chih Lo
current_role: Major individual shareholder of Eoptolink Technology (300502.SZ / 3308.HK); former director (to 2020); reportedly president of TC Tek, Inc.
profile: US-based investor whose wealth comes from a long-held stake in Chengdu's Eoptolink, a top supplier of high-speed optical transceivers for AI data centres (customers reportedly include Google and Nvidia). He was a pre-IPO 5%+ holder and board member until 2020; Eoptolink's 2025 annual report lists 'LO JEFFREY CHIH' among its top shareholders with ~22.3m shares.
interesting_fact: Eoptolink took nearly a decade to grow from RMB 10bn to 50bn market cap, then went from 50bn to ~600bn in about a year on AI optical-module demand; its Thailand plant (first overseas base) opened in 2023 with phase two in 2025.
notes: Almost no public profile, interviews or social accounts; even nationality/background is only inferred from Forbes (US). At IPO he signed an undertaking not to seek control of Eoptolink (controllers are Gao Guangrong and Huang Xiaolei). Only realistic route is via Eoptolink IR. TC Tek role comes from MarketScreener, unverified.

name: Daniel Chiu
current_role: Chairman, Fortune Oil Limited; Chairman, Harrow International Management Services Ltd; Chairman, Federal Asia Co.
profile: Daniel Chiu Tat-jung (邱達強), Hong Kong, has chaired Fortune Oil, which runs oil and gas supply and clean-energy infrastructure in mainland China (incl. aviation-fuel and crude terminals) and holds a large stake in China Gas Holdings. He also founded the Harrow International Schools (Bangkok, Beijing, Hong Kong, Shanghai and more) and has been a billionaire since 2019.
interesting_fact: He brought the 450-year-old English school Harrow to Asia: he founded and still governs the Harrow International Schools in Bangkok, Beijing, Hong Kong and Shanghai, while running an oil and gas business.
deep_cut_fact: He is an Honorary Citizen of Maoming, Guangdong, where Fortune Oil operates the Maoming single-point mooring (SPM) offshore crude-oil terminal. He joined Fortune Oil's board in August 1993 and was its chief executive before becoming vice chairman in October 1994.
notes: Fortune Oil says info@fortune-oil.com is its only official email; it warns about impersonators. Fortune Oil delisted from London (now Fortune Oil Limited, Hong Kong office in Wan Chai). Harrow schools are a possible second route.

name: Sanjay Gajendra
current_role: Co-founder, President and COO, Astera Labs (NASDAQ: ALAB)
profile: Former general manager of Texas Instruments' High Speed Interface business who co-founded Astera Labs in 2017 with TI colleagues Jitendra Mohan and Casey Morrison. Astera makes PCIe/CXL retimers, smart fabric switches and memory controllers that connect GPUs and servers in AI data centers; it IPO'd on Nasdaq in March 2024, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Astera Labs was started in Gajendra's own garage; at the 2024 Nasdaq listing he said seeing the IPO 'in as little as a little over six years is humbling'. The three co-founders were named the United States winners in the EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year 2026 class.
deep_cut_fact: Before Astera he ran TI's High Speed Interface business (signal conditioning chips) and holds a master's in engineering management from the University of Colorado Boulder.
notes: Very on-topic for a data-center podcast; frequent conference speaker (OCP, Computex). Press route via Astera's media contact Peter Lo. EY award source: https://www.ey.com/en_gl/weoy/class-of-2026/united-states

name: Albert Shigaboutdinov
current_role: Shareholder of SIBUR Holding (ex-TAIF owners' stake); joined SIBUR's board after the 2021 merger (current seat not verified)
profile: Kazan-based businessman (b. 1952) who ran Tatarstan's TAIF Group as general director 1995-2019, building it around the Kazanorgsintez and Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical plants plus refining, power and telecoms. In 2021 TAIF merged into SIBUR, with TAIF shareholders receiving ~15% of the enlarged petrochemicals giant.
interesting_fact: He sat in Tatarstan's regional parliament (State Council) for five years until 2014 and won a Russian Government Prize in Science and Technology (2008).
deep_cut_fact: Trained as a radio-electronics engineer at the Kazan Aviation Institute (1976) and first worked as an engineer at design bureau SKB-5; from 1979-83 he was deputy director of the 'Narmonsky' state farm before moving into trade and, in 1991, foreign-trade firm NPO Kazan.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (Nov 2022), also Ukraine and New Zealand - compliance check advised before any outreach. Very private, Russian-language only public presence. Only corporate route is SIBUR press office; he has no personal channels.

name: Lin Fanlian
current_role: Founder, Party secretary and chairman, Order Group (Aode Group), Linyi, Shandong
profile: Lin Fanlian (b. 1961, Linyi) founded Order Group (Aode), a Shandong conglomerate built around city gas distribution and clean energy, with interests in urban operations, finance and real estate and reportedly 300+ subsidiaries. Born into a farming family, he left school and worked construction as a teen; he has been Linyi's richest person in recent rankings.
interesting_fact: From a teenage construction worker who dropped out of school, Lin built Order Group into one of China's larger private gas-distribution groups and topped the 2023 Linyi rich list at ~44bn yuan.
deep_cut_fact: Lin received the 7th 'Shandong Charity Award' (charity model) and was named a 'caring entrepreneur' by the China Charity Federation.
notes: Very private; no English-language media, no verified official website or published press contact found for Order Group. Bio details beyond Forbes come from Chinese ranking/aggregator sites (cnpp.cn, maigoo.com), so treat the charity-award detail as moderately sourced.

name: Jitendra Mohan
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and director, Astera Labs (Nasdaq: ALAB)
profile: Co-founded Astera Labs in 2017 with Sanjay Gajendra and Casey Morrison after the three worked together at Texas Instruments; the company makes PCIe/CXL retimers, smart fabric switches and other connectivity chips for AI data centers. Astera listed on Nasdaq in 2024, and Mohan's ~4% stake made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Before Astera, he ran Texas Instruments' High Speed Interface and Clocking businesses as general manager, the exact connectivity niche Astera now sells into AI racks.
deep_cut_fact: An IIT Bombay electrical engineering grad (B.Tech 1994) with a Stanford MS, he spent nearly 16 years (1996-2012) at National Semiconductor, rising through technical roles to Design Director before joining TI.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/AI theme. Best route is Astera Labs media relations (Peter Lo). Co-founders Sanjay Gajendra (COO) and Casey Morrison (CPO) are also podcast candidates.

name: Rustem Sulteev
current_role: Co-owner of former TAIF Group (Tatarstan); Sibur shareholder; owner of an oil refinery, filling-station chain and construction company
profile: Rustem Sulteev (born 1954, Kazan) became rich as co-owner of TAIF Group, a Tatarstan oil, gas and petrochemicals holding that acquired most of its assets during 1990s privatisation. In 2021 he and co-owner Albert Shigaboutdinov merged TAIF into Sibur, taking Sibur shares; he still owns a refinery, gas stations and a construction company.
interesting_fact: TAIF's 2021 merger with Sibur folded Tatarstan's biggest private petrochemical group into Russia's largest petrochemical company, leaving TAIF's owners as shareholders alongside Leonid Mikhelson and Gennady Timchenko.
deep_cut_fact: A 1976 Kazan Institute of Civil Engineering graduate, he started as a construction foreman, and in 1984 was deputy general director for building Kazan's second bakery plant, before moving to Centrogaz and then TAIF in 1995.
notes: Sanctioned by the EU (Dec 2023, per Forbes). No personal or published office contact found; TAIF no longer operates as an independent group after the Sibur merger. Low public profile; likely not reachable or suitable for outreach.

name: Tseng Cheng
current_role: Shareholder in Chang Chun Group (private Taiwanese petrochemicals and plastics group); no public executive title found
profile: Taipei-based heir, 64, who inherited his Chang Chun Group stake from his father Tseng Shin-yi (鄭信義, d. 2016). His father co-founded the group in 1949 with classmates M.K. Liao and Lin Shu-hong. The unlisted group is one of Asia's largest petrochemicals and plastics makers, with plants in Taiwan, China and Southeast Asia.
interesting_fact: Chang Chun began in 1949 when his father and two classmates from Taipei's technical college pooled NT$500 and a bicycle to make bakelite powder at night in his grandfather's iron works. The group still refuses to list on the stock market or borrow money.
notes: Extremely private family; his father reportedly never gave a media interview. No personal public presence found. Chang Chun's site (ccp.com.tw) blocked automated access, so no corporate contact was verified. Forbes spells the surname Tseng; the Chinese is 鄭. Forbes also lists him jointly as 'Tseng Cheng & Sing-ai'.

name: Mati Staniszewski
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, ElevenLabs
profile: Mateusz 'Mati' Staniszewski co-founded AI voice company ElevenLabs (Warsaw/London) in 2022 with high-school friend Piotr Dabkowski, quitting Palantir to do it. ElevenLabs makes text-to-speech, dubbing and voice-agent models; Forbes cited a $6.6B valuation (Oct 2025) and estimates his stake at ~15%. He acts as CEO and has said he still interviews every hire.
interesting_fact: The idea came from Polish TV: foreign films there are often 'dubbed' by a single monotone lektor reading every character's lines, and the founders wanted dubbing that preserved the original performances.
deep_cut_fact: He and Dabkowski met at high school in Warsaw and bonded over mathematics; he recalls that an early public demo of their model laughing is what brought ElevenLabs its first wave of users (Sequoia 'Training Data' podcast).
notes: Very media-accessible founder; appears on many podcasts (Sequoia Training Data, 20VC, Stanford CS153). Social handles taken from ElevenLabs' own About page structured data. Good fit for AI angle.

name: Piotr Dabkowski
current_role: Co-founder, ElevenLabs (leads research and engineering; often styled CTO)
profile: Gdansk-born, Warsaw-raised engineer who studied at Oxford (engineering) and Cambridge (MPhil), then worked on machine learning at Google. In 2022 he and high-school friend Mati Staniszewski quit their jobs to build ElevenLabs, the AI voice/audio company; he leads its model research (e.g. Eleven v3, v4). ElevenLabs raised $500M at an $11B valuation in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: He and Staniszewski met at Warsaw's Copernicus high school IB programme; before ElevenLabs their side projects included an app that detected your accent from a speech sample and a recommendation system based on people you trust.
deep_cut_fact: As a Cambridge MPhil student he co-authored with Yarin Gal 'Real Time Image Saliency for Black Box Classifiers' (arXiv May 2017, NeurIPS 2017), a fast masking model that shows which parts of an image any differentiable classifier relies on.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Mati Staniszewski, who does most interviews; research-focused. Route via ElevenLabs press. Based in Warsaw (per 2022 interview).

name: Gregory Bentley
current_role: Executive Chair, Bentley Systems (Nasdaq: BSY), Exton, Pennsylvania
profile: Greg Bentley joined Bentley Systems - the infrastructure-engineering software company (MicroStation, digital twins) founded by his brothers Barry and Keith in 1984 - in 1991 and was CEO from 2000 until July 2024, when Nicholas Cumins became the first non-family CEO. He now serves as executive chair; the family retains majority control of the ~$1.2-1.5bn-revenue company.
interesting_fact: After the Space Shuttle Challenger disaster in 1986, NASA used Bentley Systems software to build 3D models of the launch to help analyse what went wrong. Before their software ventures, the Bentley brothers sold Christmas trees for extra cash.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bentley, he founded a financial trading software firm that became part of SunGard Data Systems, and he sat on SunGard's S&P 500 board from 1991 to 2005. He is a Drexel University trustee and chairs the advisory board of its Pennoni Honors College. He calls Bentley's customers 'users', not customers, because of the ongoing relationship.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center/infrastructure podcast (digital twins of energy and infrastructure assets). The IR email is also the published route for contacting the board (investors.bentley.com/contact-the-board).

name: Zbigniew Juroszek
current_role: Founder, main shareholder and President of the Management Board, ATAL S.A. (Cieszyn, Poland)
profile: Polish entrepreneur from Cieszyn. He started Atal in 1990 supplying clothing makers, moved into property in the late 1990s and built his first homes in 2003. Atal is now a Warsaw-listed developer active in Poland's major cities. He also founded the bookmaker STS, now run by his son Mateusz.
interesting_fact: He founded STS (Star-Typ Sport), which grew into Poland's largest bookmaker with roughly half the country's betting market. The family became sole owners in 2012 when its British partner Stanleybet withdrew.
deep_cut_fact: His first business was supplying fabrics to clothing manufacturers, and the textile roots survive: the family still runs Atal Textil, a wholesale fabric trader, alongside the property empire.
notes: He gives occasional interviews to Polish business media (Forbes Polska, Biznesradar) and has been a listed speaker at the European Economic Congress in Katowice in 2025 and 2026. The best route is via ATAL investor relations. He tends to appear publicly together with his son Mateusz, CEO of STS.

name: Shigenobu Nagamori
current_role: Chairman, Nagamori Gakuen Educational Foundation (operator of Kyoto University of Advanced Science); fully retired from Nidec in Feb 2026
profile: Nagamori founded Nidec (Nippon Densan) in Kyoto in 1973 and built it into the world's largest maker of HDD and precision motors, growing it through dozens of acquisitions and later pushing into EV traction motors. He was president for 45 years. He left the Nidec board in December 2025 and gave up the chairman emeritus title in February 2026. He now focuses on Kyoto University of Advanced Science.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he took over a Kyoto university, renamed it Kyoto University of Advanced Science (KUAS), and built an English-taught engineering program to tackle Japan's shortage of motor and mechatronics engineers. Commentators called it the latest in his string of acquisitions.
deep_cut_fact: Nidec started on 23 July 1973 with ¥20m of capital and three co-founders. A month later Nagamori rented the first floor of a two-storey house by the Katsura River in Kyoto's Ukyo ward as the first 'Katsura Factory' to make small precision AC motors.
notes: He left Nidec completely in Feb 2026 amid an accounting scandal at a subsidiary (TSE 'special alert' designation); avoid that topic in outreach. KUAS is now the best route and the natural angle (engineering education, motors/EVs). The Nagamori Foundation (motor/actuator/generator research awards) is a separate body: https://www.nidec.com/en/nagamori-f/about/

name: Paul Lee
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Yunnan Energy New Material Co. (SEMCORP Group, 002812.SZ)
profile: Paul Xiaoming Lee, a US citizen and University of Massachusetts graduate, co-founded SEMCORP with his brother Li Xiaohua after both studied and worked in the US. Since 2019 it has been the world's largest maker of lithium-ion battery separator film, supplying CATL, LG, Panasonic, BYD and Samsung SDI, with plants in Hungary and Ohio. He chaired its April 2026 earnings call.
interesting_fact: In 2019 SEMCORP overtook Japan's Asahi Kasei to become the world's largest supplier of lithium-ion battery separator film by volume.
deep_cut_fact: Before batteries, the brothers' first business after returning to China in 1996 was printing cigarette labels and packaging in Yunnan; that packaging arm (BOPP films, liquid-carton paper) still exists alongside the separator business.
notes: Also known as Li Xiaoming / Paul Xiaoming Lee. IR email is from SEMCORP's April 2026 earnings-call notice (board secretary Bai Yunfei). Company's Hungary (Debrecen) plant was suspended by authorities in mid-2026 over environmental/safety violations; avoid in outreach. Ohio separator plant plans relevant to US energy storage.

name: Alessandro Rosano
current_role: Founder of HeyDude (sold to Crocs in 2022); Hong Kong-based entrepreneur
profile: Italian entrepreneur from Pistoia, near Florence, who founded comfort-shoe brand HeyDude and, with partner/U.S. distributor Daniele Guidi, sold it to Crocs for $2.5bn in 2022. HeyDude sales rose from $20M in 2018 to $581M in 2021, and the brand later passed $1bn in annual revenue under Crocs. He runs his businesses from Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Rosano built HeyDude with no outside investment and minimal marketing before selling it to Crocs for $2.5 billion.
deep_cut_fact: Before HeyDude he launched several brands, including WeWood, a wooden wristwatch line, and Baldo, wooden clogs with springs built into the heels.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal website or verified social accounts found. HeyDude press now runs through Crocs and would not represent him. Web search budget ran out before this person, so current ventures are unverified.

name: Alberto Cortina
current_role: Investor and major ACS shareholder; co-founder of the Fundación Alberto y Elena Cortina
profile: Madrid-born (1947) lawyer-turned-businessman. With his cousin Alberto Alcocer ('Los Albertos') he ran Construcciones y Contratas and built stakes in banking (Banco Zaragozano, sold to Barclays in 2003/04), ENCE and ACS. His fortune now rests mainly on his ACS stake, alongside other investments.
interesting_fact: He led the BDK financial group, which opened Banque de Dakar in Senegal in 2015. It is an unusual sub-Saharan banking venture for a Spanish construction-era tycoon.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012 he and his wife Elena Cué started a foundation that runs a social canteen, an 'Econosolidario' discount store and a 'comedor invisible' service delivering food to families' homes discreetly. It also sent food aid after the 2010 Haiti earthquake.
notes: He is 79 and keeps a low profile; the family foundation is the only published channel. Forbes facts mention the Panama Papers, so avoid that topic. ACS (Florentino Pérez) has big data-center and energy exposure, which could be a podcast angle.

name: Zhang Shilong
current_role: Chairman and general manager, SG Micro Corp (圣邦微电子, 300661.SZ / 3661.HK)
profile: Zhang Shilong (张世龙, b. 1966, Shanghai) is the US-returned PhD who founded and runs SG Micro, a leading Chinese analog-chip designer (power management and signal-chain ICs) based in Beijing. After stints at a railway design institute and Texas Instruments, he built SG Micro, listed it in Shenzhen in 2017 and took it to a Hong Kong dual listing in June 2026.
interesting_fact: At SG Micro's Hong Kong debut on 26 June 2026 (offer price HK$85.20), shares opened up about 23% and the company passed HK$70bn in market value; Zhang spoke at the ceremony about the listing as a step toward going global.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips he was an engineer at the Ministry of Railways' Professional Design Institute (铁道部专业设计院). He then worked as an engineer at Texas Instruments and ran Harbin SG Micro before founding the Beijing company.
notes: Identity confirmed: Hurun API (张世龙, 圣邦 SG Micro, Beijing, PhD, 2019-2026) plus company filings. Prior pass failed because Forbes' profile has no company name. Holds US permanent residency. Strong fit for an AI/data-center hardware angle (analog/power chips). Best route: SG Micro board secretary/IR.

name: Park Soon-jae
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and largest shareholder, Alteogen (Daejeon, South Korea); stepped down as CEO in December 2025
profile: Park (born 1954) founded Alteogen in Daejeon in 2008, after research at MIT and senior roles at LG Life Sciences and Hanwha's Dream Pharma. Alteogen's ALT-B4 'Hybrozyme' enzyme lets IV biologics be given as under-the-skin injections, and it is licensed to Merck for Keytruda (Keytruda SC). He was CEO from 2011 to December 2025 and now chairs the board, focusing on long-term strategy and next-generation pipeline.
interesting_fact: Alteogen's ALT-B4 enzyme is licensed by Merck for a subcutaneous version of the cancer drug Keytruda. When the deal was announced in 2024, Alteogen's shares jumped 25% in a day.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a PhD from Purdue and says he left big-company life to escape slow decision-making and develop drugs 'with my own hands'. To avoid relying only on VC money, he funded early Alteogen by making biosimilars and pioneered licence-plus-profit-share deals with Brazil's Cristalia (2011) and Kyowa Kirin (2012).
notes: jsjang@alteogen.com is the IR & Corporate Communications director (Junseok Jang), listed as the media contact in Alteogen's 2026 press releases. Jeon Tae-yeon has been CEO since December 2025. Interviews with Park are mostly in Korean.

name: Matthew Rabinowitz
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Chairman, Natera (NTRA); co-founder & chairman, MyOme
profile: Matthew Rabinowitz was born in Johannesburg and earned a Stanford PhD in electrical engineering. He co-founded Natera in 2004-05 after his sister's newborn died of a genetic condition, ran it as CEO until 2019, and took it public in 2015. He is now executive chairman of Natera and also chairs MyOme (whole-genome analysis) and Marble Therapeutics.
interesting_fact: He founded and chairs NatureEye, a drone-technology start-up that gives wildlife conservancies anti-poaching tools and new revenue models.
deep_cut_fact: Before genetics he worked on positioning. In 2000 he founded Rosum with GPS pioneers to fix location indoors using digital TV signals, co-authored a 2004 paper with GPS pioneer James Spilker, and won IEEE's 2006 Scott Helt Memorial Award. He also won South Africa's National Science Olympiad in 1990.
notes: Engineer turned founder with a strong technical story (GPS, then genomics). He told it on Sequoia's 'Crucible Moments' podcast (https://sequoiacap.com/podcast/crucible-moments-natera). Handle the family tragedy behind Natera with care.

name: Michael Heine
current_role: Co-founder and non-executive director, Netwealth Group (ASX:NWL)
profile: Born c.1949, Heine worked with his father Walter in commodities, international financing, mortgage lending and property, started a fund-management business in 1982, and in 1999 founded wealth platform Netwealth with brother Leslie. Netwealth listed in 2017 and now has about A$100bn in funds under administration. He stepped down as joint MD in 2022; son Matt is MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: His father Walter fled Nazi Germany, was shipped to Australia as an 'enemy alien' aboard HMT Dunera, and in 1946 founded Heine Brothers, the family business Michael joined straight out of high school.
deep_cut_fact: In 1993 the Heine brothers' Heine Management bought 120 Collins Street in Melbourne, then Australia's tallest building, for A$286m.

public_contacts.value: Between Meetings with Matt Heine, Ep 100: 'Crafting a 25-year overnight success' (guest appearance)

notes: Rarely gives interviews, but did a long-form podcast with his son on Netwealth's own show (2025), so he is podcast-friendly in the right context. Best route is via Netwealth company secretary / shareholder email or through son Matt Heine.

name: Patrick Hanrahan
current_role: Canon USA Professor of Computer Science and Electrical Engineering, Stanford University; Tableau co-founder
profile: Computer-graphics pioneer who co-founded data-visualization company Tableau in 2003 out of his Stanford research; Salesforce bought it in 2019 for $15.7bn. Earlier a founding Pixar employee and chief architect of the RenderMan Interface; he shared the 2019 ACM Turing Award with Ed Catmull and still teaches at Stanford.
interesting_fact: Won three Academy Awards for technical work (RenderMan in 1993, subsurface light scattering in 2004, physically based rendering in 2014) and is credited on Tin Toy and Toy Story.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Green Bay, Wisconsin, earned a B.S. in nuclear engineering at UW-Madison (1977) and a PhD in biophysics (1985); as a grad student he taught a new graphics course in 1981 whose early students included future visualization artist Donna Cox.
notes: Email is his Stanford faculty address published on his own homepage. Academic, approachable profile; strong fit for a data/data-center angle (GPUs, rendering, visualization). Turing Award news: https://news.stanford.edu/stories/2020/03/pat-hanrahan-wins-turing-award

name: Steve Lansdown
current_role: Owner of Bristol Sport (Bristol City FC, Bristol Bears rugby, Bristol Flyers basketball, Ashton Gate); co-founder of Hargreaves Lansdown
profile: Bristol-born accountant (b. 1952) who co-founded the investment platform Hargreaves Lansdown with Peter Hargreaves in 1981, starting from a bedroom. It grew into the UK's largest retail investment platform. He now lives in Guernsey and has put much of his fortune into Bristol sport through Bristol Sport, which owns Bristol City, Bristol Bears, Bristol Flyers and the Ashton Gate stadium.
interesting_fact: He is one of the longest-serving owners in English professional football, involved with Bristol City for over three decades. In 2025 he sold a majority of Bristol City Women to Mercury13 and kept a minority stake.
deep_cut_fact: He started funding Bristol rugby in the 2008-09 season, when the club looked close to going out of business. After moving to Ashton Gate and rebranding as Bristol Bears, the club won the 2019-20 European Challenge Cup, beating Toulon 32-19. He was made a CBE in 2017 for services to business and the community in Bristol.
notes: Lives in Guernsey. He rarely gives interviews, and his public presence runs through Bristol Sport and its clubs, so the best route is the Bristol Sport / Bristol City media office. I did not verify a specific address. In Aug 2026, Kaizen Gaming CEO George Daskalakis was reported to be in talks to buy a minority stake in Bristol City.

name: Jennifer Steinbrenner Swindal
current_role: General Partner and Vice Chairperson, New York Yankees
profile: Daughter of George Steinbrenner and one of four siblings who each inherited about a quarter of his estate in 2010. She is a Yankees general partner and vice chairperson. The family also holds stakes in YES Network, NYCFC, Legends Hospitality and AC Milan. Based in Tampa, she focuses on philanthropy, including running the New York Yankees Tampa Foundation.
interesting_fact: George Steinbrenner died in 2010, during a one-year repeal of the federal estate tax. That saved his four children an estimated $600 million.
deep_cut_fact: She was a Morehead Scholar at the University of North Carolina, where she majored in business. Her first job with the team was in the Yankees Public Affairs Department in 1984-85.

public_contacts.value: https://www.mlb.com/yankees/team/contact (New York Yankees official contact page)

notes: Her public activity is Tampa philanthropy: NY Yankees Tampa Foundation, Gold Shield Foundation, Boys & Girls Club of Tampa Bay and St. Joseph's Children's Hospital Foundation boards. Go through Yankees media relations or the Tampa foundation. She rarely gives interviews. Avoid the topic of her divorce.

name: Guilherme Benchimol
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, XP Inc. (Nasdaq: XP)
profile: Rio-born Guilherme Benchimol founded XP in 2001 in Porto Alegre with about R$10,000 after being fired from Bozano's brokerage Investshop, and built it into Brazil's largest independent investment platform, listed on Nasdaq in December 2019. He handed the CEO role to Thiago Maffra in 2021 and remains chairman, also backing financial education through the XP Institute.
interesting_fact: XP started in a single room in Porto Alegre's Moinhos de Vento neighbourhood; Benchimol said he would rather go broke than lose a job again.
deep_cut_fact: He was expected to follow his grandfather, father and several cousins into medicine in Rio's Zona Sul, but chose finance instead; after being fired he said 'all I wanted was to disappear from Rio de Janeiro' and took a job offer in Rio Grande do Sul.
notes: Publicly visible founder who gives interviews/podcasts (e.g., General Atlantic podcast). IR email is for investors; for media, XP's press office (assessoria de imprensa) is the better route. Alternate IR address relacoes.investidores@xpi.com.br appears in XP's Portuguese reports.

name: Li Xiaoming
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Hui Lyu Ecological Technology Groups Co., Ltd. (001267.SZ), Wuhan
profile: Li Xiaoming (李晓明, b. 1974) co-founded the landscaping business that became Wuhan-based Hui Lyu Ecological Technology, a Shenzhen-listed landscape and ecological-engineering firm. He is steering it into AI hardware: Hui Lyu owns 51% of optical-transceiver maker Wuhan Tri-light (钧恒科技), a supplier to Coherent, and in 2026 was seeking exchange approval to buy the other 49% for RMB 1.13bn.
interesting_fact: A landscaping company has effectively become an optical-module maker: Hui Lyu's exchange industry classification is now optoelectronic components, and target Tri-light's 2025 revenue nearly doubled to RMB 1.30bn on AI data-center demand.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business, Li worked at the main equipment depot of the PLA Navy's Zhoushan base, and he holds a senior engineer title in landscape greening (园林绿化高级工程师).
notes: Company email and website are from exchange-registered company data (Eastmoney F10). huilyu.cn did not load during research. Board secretary is Yan Qi. Status of the 49% Tri-light acquisition is pending regulatory review as of mid-2026; check SZSE filings.

name: Nan Cunhui
current_role: Founder and Chairman, CHINT Group (incl. Zhejiang Chint Electrics, SSE: 601877)
profile: Nan Cunhui co-founded a small switch factory in Liushi, Wenzhou in 1984 and in 1991 formed CHINT Group, now a major maker of low-voltage electrical, meters and power transmission equipment with a large solar/new-energy arm (Astronergy, Chint New Energy). He chairs the group and holds senior posts in the All-China and Zhejiang federations of industry and commerce.
interesting_fact: In 1984 he and a primary-school friend, Hu Chengzhong, opened a switch factory together; they later split amicably - Nan founded CHINT and Hu founded rival Delixi Electric.
deep_cut_fact: He became a shoe-repairer at 13 because of family hardship; he has said three years of mending shoes taught him the importance of honesty and quality. CHINT began as Qiujing Switch Factory: 8 people in 20 square metres, funded with 50,000 yuan.
notes: chintzqb@chint.com is Chint Electrics' (601877) securities/IR mailbox from its results-briefing notice. Strong energy angle: Chint spans grid equipment, PV modules and storage. Approach in Chinese via the group or Chint Electrics board office.

name: D.V. Manjunatha
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Emmvee Photovoltaic Power Ltd (Bengaluru; listed on NSE/BSE Nov 2025)
profile: Manjunatha Donthi Venkatarathnaiah founded the Emmvee Group in Bengaluru in 1992, first making solar water heaters (the 'Solarizer' brand), then moved into PV modules in 2007 and later cells. He took Emmvee Photovoltaic Power public in November 2025 and is planning a ~$625m expansion of module and cell capacity over two years.
interesting_fact: He has been in solar since 1992, long before India's solar boom; Emmvee began PV module production in 2007, and he has publicly argued for at least 40% basic customs duty on modules so Indian makers can compete with Chinese imports.
deep_cut_fact: Before PV, Emmvee's Solarizer solar water heater became, by the company's account, the largest such brand in India; he personally received the Sourya Urja Bhushan Award in 2015 and a Business Leadership Excellence Award at Suryacon 2020.
notes: Recently listed and expanding; likely receptive to energy/manufacturing podcast via PR (pr@emmvee.in). Secretarial matters: secretarial@emmvee.in per Sept 2026 AGM notice.

name: Cai Lihong
current_role: Co-founder and director, Jiangxi Jovo Energy (九丰能源, SSE: 605090); executive director & GM, Guangdong Jiufeng Investment Holding
profile: Cai Lihong (b. 1968) co-founded Jovo Energy, a Guangdong-based importer and distributor of LNG and LPG, with her husband, chairman Zhang Jianguo. Together they are its actual controllers; she holds ~9% directly. Listed in Shanghai in 2021, Jovo now runs clean energy, energy services and specialty gases, including rocket-propellant gases for China's commercial launch sites.
interesting_fact: Jovo is the core specialty-fuel supplier at Hainan's Wenchang commercial launch site, providing liquid hydrogen, oxygen, methane and helium. It supplied high-purity liquid methane for the Long March 10B launch on 10 July 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Per Jovo's annual report she holds an EMBA from Xiamen University and, outside Jovo, is executive director of Guangdong Haijianeng Low-Carbon Energy Technology and chair of Guangdong Guanghaiwan Energy Holding.
notes: Low media profile; husband Zhang Jianguo (chairman, PLA veteran) is the public face. Hurun lists the fortune jointly with him. Route via Jovo's board secretary office. Commercial space gases are a strong podcast hook.

name: Jiang Xueming
current_role: Chairman, Dosilicon Co., Ltd. (688110.SS, memory chips); chairman and general manager, Oriental Hengxin Capital Holding Group
profile: A Jiangsu entrepreneur from Taoyuan, Wujiang, who started in textiles: he converted a township garment mill into Wujiang Oriental Garment Group and in 2005 founded Oriental Hengxin. He moved into semiconductors in 2014 with Dosilicon, a Shanghai STAR-listed designer of NAND, NOR and DRAM memory chips. The group also controls Dongwu Cement (HK) and has energy and rare-earth interests.
interesting_fact: To speed up Dosilicon's memory-chip design he bought control of the Korean chipmaker Fidelix and moved part of its engineering team to China to work alongside Chinese engineers. He jokingly called it a new-era 'roundabout way to save the country'.
deep_cut_fact: From 1983 to 1986 he was director of the Wujiang yarn-dyed fabric mill. He still chairs the Taoyuan town chamber of commerce in his home town and gave RMB 2M to its Siyuan education fund, founded in 2022. His group also co-invested with Shanghai Electric in Pakistan's Thar Block-I coal power project.
notes: Wealth is shared with his daughter Jiang Yuzhou, Dosilicon's board secretary. The IR email is the board office address from Dosilicon's 2025 annual report (April 2026). Both semiconductor and energy angles (Thar coal project in Pakistan). In 2026 his vehicle Hanpeng Qichen was named investor in Zhang Xiaoquan's restructuring. The 2026 regulatory warning letter to Dosilicon is best avoided.

name: Jiang Yuzhou
current_role: Director, Vice President and Board Secretary, Dosilicon Co., Ltd. (东芯半导体, SSE STAR: 688110)
profile: Jiang Yuzhou (蒋雨舟, b. 1988) is a director, VP and board secretary of Shanghai-based Dosilicon, a fabless memory-chip designer (SLC NAND, NOR, DRAM and MCP). She and chairman Jiang Xueming are the company's joint actual controllers, and her Hurun wealth is shared with him. She joined Dosilicon in 2016 as marketing manager, became a director in 2020, and also sits on the boards of Korean affiliate Fidelix and Nemostech.
interesting_fact: She holds a master's degree from Woodbury University in the US. Before entering the chip business she ran Kookie LLC (2013-15) and was executive director of a Suzhou cultural tourism development company (2017-19).
deep_cut_fact: She started at Dosilicon in September 2016 as marketing department manager and rose to board secretary and director. She now presents the company's annual results to institutional investors herself.
notes: As board secretary she is the company's official investor and press contact. The contact@dosilicon.com address is listed under her name in the 2025 annual report summary, so it is a direct route. Hurun lists her wealth jointly with Jiang Xueming (her father and the chairman, per the filing).

name: Ge Haiquan
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Henan Shijia Photons Technology Co. (688313.SH)
profile: Founder, chairman and GM of Shijia Photons, a Hebi, Henan optical-chip maker listed on the STAR Market (he holds about 6.7%). It began in indoor optical cable and moved into optoelectronic chips in 2010. It now makes PLC splitter, AWG and DFB laser chips, with AI data-center demand driving growth since 2024.
interesting_fact: In 2024 revenue rose 42% to RMB 1.07B and net profit rose 234%, both driven by AI computing-power and datacom demand for its AWG chips used in data-center optical modules.
deep_cut_fact: Shijia grew out of a 2010 R&D tie-up with the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Semiconductors. A year later it was the first and only company in China able to mass-produce PLC optical splitter chips, and by 2015 those chips held over 50% of the global market. All of this was built from a small city in northern Henan.
notes: Low public profile in English-language media. The deep-cut fact is about his company rather than him personally. info@sjphotons.com is the company's general inbox. The board secretary/IR office on SSE filings is the formal route.

name: Wu Yuling
current_role: Director, Advanced Fiber Resources (Zhuhai) Ltd. (SZSE: 300620); director of Infinimax Assets Ltd. (holds ~15% of AFR)
profile: Macau-resident businesswoman (b. 1963) who was the controlling shareholder of Advanced Fiber Resources (光库科技), a Zhuhai maker of passive optical components, from 2002 until Feb 2021 and its chair 2007-2018. Control passed to state-owned Huafa Group in 2021; she remains a director and major holder via Infinimax as AFR rides demand for AI data-center optical interconnects.
interesting_fact: AFR, the company she backed for two decades, now sells thin-film lithium niobate modulators, fiber arrays and optical-circuit-switch parts for AI data-center interconnects (showcased at OFC 2026).
deep_cut_fact: Alongside optics, she has run Macau trading businesses for decades: director and legal representative of 联盈制服 (uniforms) since 1996, 迅盈行贸易 (trading) since 1998 and 联盈旗帜 (flags/banners) since 1999, per AFR's director disclosure.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal media presence. Best route is AFR investor relations / board secretary (Wu Wei per 2025 filings). Has Australian permanent residency per filing.

name: Clément Delangue
current_role: Cofounder & CEO, Hugging Face
profile: French entrepreneur (ESCP 2012) who declined a Google offer to join Paris vision startup Moodstocks, then cofounded Hugging Face in New York in 2016 with Julien Chaumond and Thomas Wolf. It began as a teen chatbot app and became the main open-source hub for AI models and datasets; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: In 2023 Hugging Face's open-source meetup in San Francisco drew about 5,000 people and was dubbed the 'Woodstock of AI'. The team called every llama farm in California to bring live llamas, a nod to Meta's LLaMA model.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in La Bassée in northern France, son of a lawnmower-shop owner. As a teen he and his brother sold hundreds of imported ATVs and motorbikes on eBay; at 16, adults in his father's shop wouldn't take him seriously selling tractors. 'The internet was creating new rules for me.'
notes: Very active and approachable on X and LinkedIn; often replies publicly. A strong fit for a podcast about open-source AI and the compute behind it.

name: Julien Chaumond
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Hugging Face (being acquired by Nvidia)
profile: French engineer Julien Chaumond co-founded Hugging Face in New York in 2016 with Clément Delangue and Thomas Wolf; it began as a chatbot app for teens before pivoting to the open-source hub hosting millions of AI models and datasets. Earlier he co-founded social-reading startup Glose. In Sept 2026 Nvidia agreed to buy Hugging Face for ~$12.9B, expected to close H1 2027.
interesting_fact: Hugging Face started as a 'playful chatbot for teens'; the founders realised the models powering the app were worth more than the app itself. Nvidia's Sept 2026 deal price was $12.93B.
deep_cut_fact: His own Hugging Face profile lists his personal AI hardware: two RTX 3090s, an Nvidia GB10 (DGX Spark-class) box, an AMD Ryzen AI Max+ 395 machine and an Apple M5 Max with 128GB as his primary rig.
notes: Very hands-on and active on X and the HF Hub (handle julien-c). Nvidia acquisition announced early Sept 2026 (https://www.advanced-television.com/2026/09/04/nvidia-acquires-hugging-face-for-12-9bn/); his post-close role not yet public. X handle widely attributed but verify the link on his HF profile.

name: Thomas Wolf
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Science Officer, Hugging Face
profile: French physicist-turned-patent-attorney who co-founded Hugging Face, the open-source AI hub. He created/advised the Transformers, Datasets, Diffusers, smolagents and LeRobot libraries, drove BigScience/BLOOM and FineWeb, and now leads Hugging Face's open robotics (Reachy Mini) and AI-for-science efforts.
interesting_fact: After a physics PhD he spent five years as a European patent attorney at Paris IP firm Cabinet Plasseraud (earning a law degree from Panthéon-Sorbonne) before teaching himself deep learning and co-founding Hugging Face.
deep_cut_fact: An Ecole Polytechnique graduate, he worked on laser-plasma interactions at Lawrence Berkeley Lab's BELLA Center, was accepted to an MIT PhD but instead did his PhD at Sorbonne/ESPCI on superconducting materials for France's DGA and Thales; he says most ML methods looked like 're-branded statistical physics'.
notes: Very accessible: publishes a contact email (written as 'thomaswolfcontact [at] gmail [dot] com') on his own site. Co-author of O'Reilly's 'Natural Language Processing with Transformers' and 'The Ultra-Scale Playbook' (GPU training at scale) - good data-center hook.

name: Huo Qinghua
current_role: Founder and chairman, China Kingho Energy Group (中国庆华能源集团) / Inner Mongolia Qinghua Group (last reported)
profile: Huo Qinghua (霍庆华) built China Kingho (Qinghua) Group, once called China's largest private coal miner, from a 1996 start in Alashan, Inner Mongolia, expanding into coal chemicals, logistics and overseas projects (assets RMB 68.6B in 2014). He was on Forbes' billionaire list 2013-2018, but the group struggled after the coal downturn.
interesting_fact: In 2011 Kingho announced plans to build a coal terminal at Mozambique's Beira port and upgrade the Sena railway to the Moatize coal mines, and had proposed a $19B coal development in Pakistan's Thar field.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a coal magnate he served in the army and then worked as a physician at the hospital of Ningxia's Shitanjing Mining Bureau, studying economic management at the Ningxia Coal Workers' University.
