notes: No recent (post-2018) news on him found; no death reports found. Per NBD (2018) the group fell into financial distress after 2013 with creditor lawsuits and court enforcement lists, so approach with care; likely not a current billionaire. No published personal/press contacts.

name: Zhao Yilan
current_role: Co-owner, with husband Zhou Qingzhi, of the Narada group (Shanghai Narada Group / Zhejiang Narada Power, 300068.SZ); no executive post at the listed company
profile: Zhao Yilan (赵亦斓, b. 1978), Hong Kong-based, is the wife of Zhou Qingzhi, founder of the Narada group (Narada Power: telecom/data-center batteries and energy storage, plus property and Narada hotels). Before Narada Power's 2010 IPO she held about 24.5% via Shanghai Yidu and Shanghai Narada Group, with voting control left to her husband. Hurun listed the couple from 2010 to 2022.
interesting_fact: She ranked No. 8 on Hurun's 2011 list of young self-made rich (RMB 8.5bn), one of the few women on that list, though Narada Power's prospectus said her shares were in practice controlled by her husband.
deep_cut_fact: She has a master's in education from the University of Washington. After returning to China she helped set up the Narada Foundation (南都公益基金会), one of China's best-known private grant-making foundations, and was a trustee from May 2007.
notes: Identity confirmed via Hurun API (周庆治、赵亦斓, 南都 Narada, couple; Zhao: female, Hong Kong, master's from Washington) and 360 Baike. She is not on the Narada Foundation's current board (https://www.naradafoundation.org/category/11), so treat the foundation email as an indirect route via Zhou Qingzhi's circle. Narada Power now trades as 'ST南都'; avoid the topic.

name: Ling Shisheng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou AllTest Biotech (杭州安旭生物科技股份有限公司, 'Assure Tech', SSE STAR: 688075)
profile: Ling Shisheng (凌世生, b. 1972), a Zhejiang University genetics graduate, founded Hangzhou-based point-of-care (POCT) rapid-diagnostics maker Assure Tech in 2008-09 with his wife and vice-chair Jiang Xueying. COVID-19 antigen test demand (over 90% of sales overseas) drove a STAR Market IPO in November 2021 and put the couple on the Hurun list in 2022.
interesting_fact: Before running her husband's company, co-owner and vice-chair Jiang Xueying spent nearly two decades as a court judge in Shengzhou and Hangzhou's Xihu District.
deep_cut_fact: A trained geneticist (MSc, Zhejiang University; senior engineer), he started as a researcher at Hangzhou University's School of Life Sciences (1996-97), then spent ten years as R&D director at ACON Biotech (Hangzhou) before founding his own diagnostics firm.
notes: Emails are those of the board secretary (Han Jun) and securities affairs representative (Yu Jun) as published in the 2025 annual report summary. Low English-language profile; outreach probably needs to be in Chinese. Wealth tied to pandemic-era testing boom.

name: Jiang Xueying
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Ling Shisheng) of Hangzhou AllTest Biotech (安旭生物, SSE STAR 688075)
profile: Jiang Xueying (姜学英) and her husband Ling Shisheng, the chairman and general manager, control Hangzhou AllTest Biotech, a maker of in-vitro diagnostics and rapid tests founded in 2008. Together they hold about 60%. Their wealth peaked on Hurun's 2022 lists during the Covid-19 testing boom.
interesting_fact: AllTest is an export-focused maker of rapid diagnostic tests (drugs of abuse, infectious disease, fertility and similar) and is listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. In filings, Jiang is named only as a shareholder, while her husband runs the company.
notes: Hurun's 'Assuro Tech' corresponds to 安旭生物 (AllTest); filings confirm she and Ling Shisheng are a married couple and the company's controllers. She keeps a low profile, with no executive title in recent filings. The email is the board-secretary IR contact from company filings.

name: Zhu Hai
current_role: Actual controller (largest shareholder) of Shenzhen Bioeasy Biotechnology (易瑞生物, SZSE 300942); founding chairman
profile: Zhu Hai (朱海), a PhD scientist born in 1973, founded Shenzhen Bioeasy, a maker of rapid food-safety tests that has expanded into point-of-care diagnostics. It listed on ChiNext in February 2021 with Sequoia China backing. He remains the controlling shareholder via Yirui (Hainan) Venture Capital.
interesting_fact: Bioeasy's 2021 listing was Sequoia China's first IPO in food-safety testing. At the IPO Zhu said his goal was to use the capital markets to build 'a world-class food safety company'.
notes: The 2026 interim report lists Xiao Zhaoli (肖昭理) as legal representative, so Zhu may no longer be chairman. Press (c.2021) says he was a deputy lab director at the Shenzhen inspection & quarantine food-testing centre before founding Bioeasy; this was not verified, so it is not used. Avoid personal topics.

name: Guo Dongze
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Antong' (China) - presumably linked to Antong Holdings, a Fujian-based container shipping/logistics group listed in Shanghai. Could not verify his current role or status from accessible sources.
notes: No Forbes profile page (404), no English/Chinese Wikipedia article, company site unreachable, Baidu blocked, and web search budget exhausted. Kept minimal; needs a follow-up pass before any outreach.

name: Yan Jinggang
current_role: Former controller of Shanghai Zhongji (中技) Group; current role unknown
profile: Shanghai businessman whose Zhongji group began in building materials (concrete piles) and built a network of listed-company holdings, the 'Zhongji system'. That network included *ST Fukong (formerly Fortune Holdings). Hurun listed him at about $1.7bn in 2015-2018, before the group ran into heavy debt and lawsuits.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he agreed to sell 100% of Zhongji Group to Zhongshang Yunnan Asset Management, but that deal was terminated in January 2019.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target. Since 2018 he has been under a securities-regulator (CSRC) investigation and his group faced more than RMB 5bn in litigation (China Securities Journal, June 2018). I found no recent public activity and no contacts.

name: Xiuli Hawken
current_role: Former chair of Harbin Renhe Public Facilities Co.; former director and minority shareholder of Reading FC (per corporate listings)
profile: Xiuli Hawken, also known as Dai Xiuli (戴秀丽), is a Chinese businesswoman. She is reported to be the sister and business partner of Dai Yongge, who founded the Renhe group, which developed underground shopping centres in northern China and controlled the HK-listed Renhe Commercial Holdings. She appeared on Hurun lists from 2009 to 2014 and became a minority owner of English club Reading FC in 2021.
interesting_fact: Renhe's business was built on shopping centres converted from air-raid shelters, which it operates in some 30 Chinese cities including Harbin, the Dai family's hometown.
notes: Mostly inactive publicly since the mid-2010s, with no public contact channel. The family's Reading FC ownership ended in 2025 amid EFL sanctions and financial controversy, so this is a sensitive area to avoid. Not a good podcast candidate. I could not independently confirm the Hawken/Dai Xiuli identity link beyond Wikipedia's Chinese-name rendering.

name: Li Zhaonan
profile: Hurun China listed Li Zhaonan (李兆楠) from 2006 to 2013, and Hurun Global in 2014, with wealth attributed to 'Hengde' in insurance. Searches in English and Chinese found no reliable source that identifies the company or the person.
notes: He has not appeared on any list since 2014. Identity is unresolved: the 'Hengde' company could not be matched to a known insurer or holding company. A Chinese corporate registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) would be needed to identify him. Low priority.

name: Ranjit Singh Boparan
current_role: Founder and co-owner (with wife Baljinder) of Boparan Holdings / 2 Sisters Food Group; also behind Boparan Private Office (restaurant and other investments)
profile: Input name 'Ranjith' refers to Ranjit Singh Boparan (b. 1966, Bilston), the West Midlands 'Chicken King'. He left school at 16, worked in a butcher's shop, and in 1993 founded 2 Sisters Food Group with a small bank loan, growing it by acquisition (incl. Northern Foods, 2011) into the UK's biggest poultry supplier, providing about a third of UK supermarket chicken. He returned to run the poultry division in 2019.
interesting_fact: 2 Sisters began as a small frozen-retail cutting and packing operation in West Bromwich and became, by turnover, the UK's largest food manufacturer, with 20,000+ staff.
deep_cut_fact: A colleague quoted in 2019 on why he came back to hands-on management: "He loves the day to day. He is not about the next yacht or next fast car, he likes his chicken."
notes: Identity: 'Ranjith' = Ranjit Singh Boparan; shared fortune with wife Baljinder (spelled 'Beljinder' in input). Sensitive: 2017 Guardian/ITV food-standards investigation; avoid family topics. 2sfg.com blocked automated fetch so no published press email verified; try 2sfg.com media/contact page manually. Low media profile.

name: Guy Laliberté
current_role: Founder, Lune Rouge (Montreal investment/creative firm); founder, One Drop Foundation
profile: Former street performer who co-founded Cirque du Soleil in 1984 and built it into a global entertainment giant; sold 90% to TPG/Fosun in 2015 and his last 10% to CDPQ in 2020. Now invests in arts, tech and entertainment through Lune Rouge, runs the One Drop water foundation, and hosts the Big Deal for One Drop charity poker event in Las Vegas.
interesting_fact: In 2009 he became the first Canadian private space traveller (Soyuz TMA-16), using the trip for a 'water awareness' webcast spanning 14 cities on five continents and the ISS.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cirque took off he hitchhiked around Europe at 18 playing accordion, learned fire-eating and stilt-walking, and once took a full-time job at a hydroelectric dam in Quebec, returning to street performing only when the dam workers went on strike.
notes: Hydro-dam job is a natural hook for an energy podcast. Lune Rouge is his personal investment vehicle and the best route. Avoid the 2019 Tahiti cannabis episode and space-trip tax case.

name: Mike Speiser
current_role: Managing Director, Sutter Hill Ventures; director of Snowflake and Workday
profile: Silicon Valley venture capitalist known for incubating companies in-house at Sutter Hill Ventures, which he joined in 2008 from Yahoo. He helped start Pure Storage, and he co-conceived Snowflake and was its founding CEO (2012-14); Snowflake's 2020 IPO made him a billionaire. He keeps incubating data and infrastructure startups (Sigma Computing, Observe, Clumio, Augment, Reve AI) and investing in companies such as Sila Nano.
interesting_fact: He says he spends about 80% of his time and resources on a single project at a time. By 2021 Sutter Hill had built five companies on top of Snowflake, starting with Lacework.
deep_cut_fact: Before he was a VC he was a founder: he co-founded Bix, a Sutter Hill-backed consumer startup that Yahoo bought in 2006. In 2008 he started assembling Pure Storage with John Colgrove and John Hayes.
notes: Very relevant to data centres: Snowflake, Pure Storage and Sila Nano (battery materials) cover data infrastructure, storage and energy. He gave a long-form interview on the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast (Aug 2025): https://www.goldmansachs.com/insights/goldman-sachs-exchanges/finding-the-right-problems-how-sutter-hill-ventures-mike-speiser-creates-great-companies . He keeps a low profile; the best route is via Sutter Hill Ventures, though I did not verify a published contact.

name: Evangelos Mytilineos
current_role: Chairman and CEO, METLEN Energy & Metals (Athens/London-listed)
profile: Greek industrialist (b. 1954, Athens) who in 1990 founded the modern Mytilineos group from his grandfather's 1908 metallurgy business, listed it in Athens in 1995, renamed it METLEN in 2024 and added a London listing in 2025. METLEN runs aluminium plants and bauxite mines, builds solar and storage projects worldwide and is Greece's largest independent electricity supplier.
interesting_fact: METLEN's roots go back to a metallurgy business founded in 1908 by his grandfather, also named Evangelos; he turned it into one of Greece's largest industrial and energy groups and moved its primary listing to London in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A Moraitis School alumnus, he holds an economics BSc from the University of Athens and an MSc from the London School of Economics; the University of Piraeus gave him an honorary doctorate in 2019, and his family hails from Koroni in the Peloponnese.
notes: No personal social media found. Route via METLEN media/contact-us page (info@metlen.com). Strong energy fit: solar/storage EPC, power supply and energy-intensive aluminium. Deep-cut fact is light (from Wikipedia); my web-search quota ran out before I could look further.

name: Nihat Ozdemir
current_role: Co-founder and director, Limak Holding (daughter Ebru Özdemir chairs the board); reported 2025 board chairman of ÇEİS (Turkish cement employers' association)
profile: Mechanical engineer, born 1950 in Diyarbakır, who co-founded Limak in 1976 with university friend Sezai Bacaksız. Limak builds and operates infrastructure: Istanbul Airport (consortium member), hydroelectric plants (a top-10 Turkish power producer), cement, tourism. Özdemir led the cement and energy side. He was Turkish Football Federation president 2019-2022, and Limak is now moving into data centres.
interesting_fact: Before going into business he spent four years on the engineering faculty at what is now Gazi University. For a short time he was assistant to Necmettin Erbakan, who later became prime minister.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to Ankara in 1967 to study mechanical engineering and earned a master's in industrial engineering from Ege University in 1975, a year before founding Limak. He was also Fenerbahçe's deputy president and press spokesman before heading the Turkish Football Federation.
notes: Strong podcast fit: hydro and energy assets plus a new data-centre push. Limak says it is evaluating sites in Türkiye and the Gulf (https://www.cnbce.com/teknoloji/limak-yonetim-kurulu-baskani-ebru-ozdemir-veri-merkezi-yatirimlari-icin-turkiye-ve-korfez-ulkelerini-degerlendiriyoruz-h23324). Daughter Ebru Özdemir, the chair, is the more media-facing family member. Best route is press@limak.com.

name: Alexander Knauf
current_role: Member of the Shareholders' Committee (Gesellschafterausschuss), Knauf Group, since 1 Jan 2026; previously spokesman of the managing partners
profile: Third-generation heir to Knauf, the Iphofen-based family building-materials group (plasterboard, insulation, cement boards; 35,000+ staff). A managing partner since 2012 and later spokesman of the managing partners, he moved to the shareholders' committee at the start of 2026 as part of a planned generational and governance overhaul.
interesting_fact: Knauf's original 1932 gypsum operation on the Moselle, in the border region of Luxembourg, Germany and France, remains the company's production nucleus; the family's Knauf Museum in a 1688 inn on Iphofen's market square houses a renowned relief-art collection.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he began his career with an apprenticeship (Banklehre) at Deutsche Bank.
notes: Leadership change source: https://www.baulinks.de/webplugin/2025/1233.php4. Press route: Gebr. Knauf KG Corporate Communications (head: Matthias Link since Feb 2025), per Knauf newsroom; no published press email found. knauf.com blocks automated fetches.

name: Farkhad Akhmedov
current_role: Private investor; chairman/shareholder of AZNAR (Azerbaijani natural-juice and agriculture company); former Russian senator
profile: Baku-born (1955) Azerbaijani-Russian businessman who started trading furs in London, founded Tansley Trading to supply equipment to Soviet gas producers, and built a stake in Siberian gas producer Northgas, selling his 49% to Novatek in 2012 for ~$1.4B. Sat in Russia's Federation Council 2004-2009. Now invests privately, incl. AZNAR juice and agriculture in Azerbaijan.
interesting_fact: He invested $55 million in a pomegranate juice factory in his native Azerbaijan, in the region where his father worked during the Soviet era.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil and gas, he served in the Soviet Navy (1975-77) as a senior sergeant and platoon commander, then earned a degree in the technology and merchandising of fur products from the Moscow Veterinary Academy (1983), the expertise behind his first business selling furs in London.
notes: Sensitive: under UK sanctions since April 2022 (EU lifted its sanctions in Sept 2023) and subject of a long, heavily covered divorce case; avoid both. He has also been the first ethnic Azerbaijani in Russia's upper house. No published personal/office contact found; web-search budget ran out before checking AZNAR's site.

name: Lu Feng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Wind Information Co., Ltd. (万得信息, Shanghai)
profile: Lu Feng (陆风) founded Wind Information in Shanghai in the 1990s (sources give 1994 or 1998) and built it into mainland China's dominant financial-data terminal, often described as China's answer to Bloomberg, used by brokers, fund houses, banks and QFIIs. He remains chairman and is a part-time vice chair of the Shanghai Federation of Industry and Commerce's 14th executive committee.
interesting_fact: Wind's terminal is the default data source cited across Chinese financial media, research reports and academic papers; investors in the company have included Hillhouse Capital (2015) and Xinhu Zhongbao (2018).
deep_cut_fact: In a rare 2021 keynote at Huatai Securities' fintech open day he recalled that in 2006 Wind adopted the slogan '金融就是数据' ('finance is data'), described a 'digital twin enterprise' goal, and promoted Wind's 'Shared by Wind' program to share its data and networks with startups.
notes: Very low-profile founder; rarely gives interviews. Name collides with a Peking University economist Lu Feng (born 1951) - different person. Wealth is financial data, not energy, despite the 'energy' focus tag. Route via Wind corporate office in Shanghai.

name: Deng Ke
current_role: Director and General Manager (CEO), YD Electronic Technology Co., Ltd. (奕东电子, SZSE: 301123), Dongguan
profile: Deng Ke (邓可, b. 1985) runs YD Electronic Technology, the Dongguan precision-components maker (FPC, connector components, LED backlight modules) founded in 1997 by his father, chairman Deng Yuquan. He has led the company as general manager since its 2019 restructuring ahead of its 2021 Shenzhen ChiNext listing; the family fortune is shared with his father.
interesting_fact: YD worked with Amphenol in 2007 to develop Amphenol's first SFP (optical-transceiver) component, taking it into high-speed connectors for data and telecom equipment; in 2013 it co-developed what it calls the industry's first FPC for EV battery management systems.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a master's at Imperial College London and, from 2009 (aged about 24), headed YD's then-new FPC (flexible printed circuit) business group - now one of its core businesses - before becoming general manager.
notes: 'YDET' in the source data = YD Electronic Technology (ydet.com). Father Deng Yuquan (b. 1959) is chairman and a former engineer at state-owned Factory 733. Optical-communications components link to the data-center theme. Low English-language media profile.

name: Zhu Mengqian
current_role: Co-holder (with her father, chairman Zhu Shuangquan) of a family stake in Hubei Dinglong Holding (300054.SZ); no listed board or executive role found
profile: Hurun's 2026 China Rich List adds Zhu Mengqian (b. 1991, Wuhan; master's degree) jointly with her father Zhu Shuangquan, chairman of Wuhan-based Dinglong, a maker of semiconductor CMP polishing pads/slurries, display materials and printing consumables. The Zhu brothers (Shuangquan and Shunquan) control Dinglong with ~14.5% each; she is not among its directors, executives or top-10 holders.
notes: Identity per Hurun 2026 listing (朱双全、朱梦茜, relation: father-daughter; source https://www.hurun.net/zh-CN/Rank/HsRankDetails?pagetype=rich). No public profile or own role found; any outreach would realistically go via Dinglong's company/IR email (as shown in exchange-filing data). Web search budget ran out before further research.

name: Jiang Ling
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Sling Intelligent Drive Group (斯菱智驱, formerly Zhejiang Sling Automobile Bearing; SZSE 301550)
profile: Jiang Ling (姜岭, born 1973) founded and, with his daughter Jiang Nan, controls Sling, an aftermarket auto-bearing maker in Xinchang, Zhejiang. After its 2023 ChiNext listing, the company moved into humanoid-robot joint parts such as harmonic reducers, and in 2026 it renamed itself 'Sling Intelligent Drive'.
interesting_fact: Sling built a dedicated R&D team in 2023 for humanoid and collaborative-robot joint components. By end-2024 it had its first harmonic-reducer production line running, a pivot from car bearings into robotics.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the very bottom of the industry: from August 1990, aged 17, he worked as a factory worker at the Zhejiang Xinchang Bearing General Factory for a decade. In 2000 he became general manager of Xinchang Sanhe Bearing, and he later built Sling.
notes: 'Jiang Nan' (shared_with) is his daughter and co-controller, per the filings. The robotics pivot makes this a good fit for an automation or hardware story. He keeps a low profile, so the best route is the company's securities office (stock@bbsbearing.com).

name: Han Huiru
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Qingdao East Steel Tower Stock Co. (东方铁塔, SZSE 002545)
profile: Han Huiru's fortune comes from Qingdao East Steel Tower, which started in 1982 as a village galvanising works in Jiaozhou, Shandong. It grew into a leading maker of TV and telecom towers, transmission-line pylons and power-plant steel structures, and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. In 2016 it acquired a potash miner with a 141 km² concession in Laos and now runs steel structures and potash fertiliser in parallel.
interesting_fact: The company built the 388m Henan TV Tower, billed as the world's tallest all-steel TV tower, and supplied the feed-support towers for China's FAST 500m radio telescope, which won a Luban Prize. It also built structures for China's first 1000kV ultra-high-voltage test line.
deep_cut_fact: The company began in 1982 as the 'Houhan Galvanising Plant' of Jiaolai Commune in Jiao County (胶县胶莱公社后韩镀锌厂). Its first tower job, in 1985, was a 35m microwave tower in Huang County.
notes: The company site publishes a securities/IR department line (0532-88056092) but no email. Han's current board title and age were not verified (search budget exhausted); family members may now run the company. Strong energy/grid angle: UHV transmission towers, power-plant steel, and potash in Laos. The Chinese name 韩汇如 and his/her founding role are from memory and unverified.

name: Liu Jingkang
current_role: Founder & CEO, Arashi Vision (Insta360), Shenzhen
profile: Liu Jingkang (J.K. Liu, ~35) founded 360-degree and action-camera maker Insta360 in Shenzhen in 2015 with classmates from Nanjing University's computer-science program. Backed by Qiming, IDG and Suning, it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2025 and now rivals DJI and GoPro, holding roughly 73% of the global 360-degree camera market.
interesting_fact: NASA used Insta360 Pro cameras to live-stream the InSight Mars landing from mission control in 2018 (a project that won an Emmy) and again for the Perseverance landing in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: His first product was not a camera but a smartphone live-streaming app; the idea for 360-degree video came from wanting to record and share the feeling of being at a music concert, which led to a phone accessory that turned a smartphone into a 360 camera.
notes: Young, product-focused founder; good entrepreneurship story but little energy/data-center angle. Insta360 has offices in Los Angeles, Tokyo and Berlin; route via company PR (press contact not machine-readable on the JS site). Web search budget was exhausted, so no personal social accounts verified.

name: Mao Geping
current_role: Chairman, Mao Geping Cosmetics Co. (HKEX: 1318), Hangzhou
profile: Chinese makeup artist turned beauty mogul. He trained in Chinese opera, became famous doing TV makeup, and founded his eponymous premium cosmetics brand in 2000. He listed the company in Hong Kong in December 2024, raising more than $300m. The brand competes with international prestige labels in China, and his wife and sisters sit on the board.
interesting_fact: He became famous in 1994 as head makeup artist on the TV series 'Wu Zetian', where his technique turned actress Liu Xiaoqing into the empress across decades of her life. He has won four China Makeup Awards.
deep_cut_fact: Before building the brand, he founded the Mao Geping Image Design Art School in Hangzhou in 1998. In 2008 he opened a large campus in the Hangzhou Fashion Hub, the city's only creative hub dedicated to fashion and cosmetology. The school trains makeup artists, and they feed his counter network.
notes: The IR email is from the 2024 annual report's corporate information page. He mainly speaks to Chinese media. Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast, but a good entrepreneurship story (opera student to HK-listed beauty brand).

name: Isabel dos Santos
current_role: Private investor (former chair of Sonangol, 2016-2017); reportedly based in Dubai
profile: Isabel dos Santos is the eldest daughter of Angola's late former president Jose Eduardo dos Santos. She built stakes in Angolan banking and telecoms (Unitel, BFA) and Portuguese companies such as NOS, and was once called Africa's richest woman. Since 2020 Angola and other states have pursued fraud and money-laundering cases and asset freezes against her, all of which she denies; Forbes dropped her from its billionaire list in 2021.
interesting_fact: Her father appointed her to head Sonangol, Angola's state oil company, in June 2016; the next president removed her in November 2017. She is nicknamed 'the princess' in Angola.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an electrical engineer at King's College London before going into business.
notes: HIGH REPUTATIONAL RISK: she faces an Interpol notice, a UK worldwide asset freeze (appeal rejected 2024), a Dutch court finding over Sonangol funds and ongoing Angolan charges (some dropped in November 2025). She denies wrongdoing. Recommend not approaching her for an entrepreneurship podcast. Reported Instagram handles are inconsistent, so none are listed. No longer a billionaire per Forbes.

name: Carson Brice
current_role: Major (10%+) shareholder, First Citizens BancShares (FCNCA); private individual, Raleigh, NC
profile: Carson Holding Brice is the youngest of the four sisters of Frank Holding Jr., chairman and CEO of Raleigh-based First Citizens Bank. With her siblings she owns about 20% of the bank and close to half the voting power, a stake from a family that has led the bank since 1935. SEC Form 4 filings show she is a passive holder who mostly makes gifts and trust transfers.
interesting_fact: The Holding family controls First Citizens, which acquired Silicon Valley Bank in 2023 and has since grown into a national bank on the Fortune 500.
notes: Very private and has almost no public profile beyond SEC filings. A UNC page says she is a UNC and UNC business school graduate (https://ie.unc.edu/people/f-bryan-brice-jr). The bank media address reaches the company, not her.

name: Yang Jian
current_role: Co-founder, director and deputy general manager, Semight Instruments (苏州联讯仪器, 688808.SH); one of its three actual controllers
profile: Yang Jian (杨建, b. 1980, Jinan) co-controls Suzhou-based Semight Instruments with Hu Haiyang and Huang Jianjun. Semight makes high-speed optical-communication and semiconductor test equipment; its customers include Innolight, Eoptolink and Lumentum, so it is tied to the AI data-center optics boom. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2026, opened up more than 800% and later traded above RMB 2,000 a share.
interesting_fact: Semight's STAR Market debut in April 2026 rose about 876% and briefly valued the company at RMB 82bn; by mid-2026 its shares topped RMB 2,000, making it the A-share 'stock king', and the three controllers' stakes were worth about RMB 55bn.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a 2006 communications-engineering master's from Huazhong University of Science & Technology, worked in technical support at Qingdao Lucent, then was a sales manager at Agilent/Keysight (2011-17), the test-instrument giant Semight now competes with, before joining Semight at its founding in March 2017.
notes: Input record looks merged: Forbes' 'yang-jian' profile (2020-22, real estate, Wenzhou) is a different person, likely Zhongliang Holdings' Yang Jian (杨剑). The 杨建 / optical-semiconductor-test identity matches Hurun 2026 (联讯仪器 Semight; Jinan-born; HUST master's). Strong fit for a data-center optics angle. Route via Semight IR.

name: Gretel Packer
current_role: Chair, Packer Family Foundation; private investor; arts philanthropist (Art Gallery of NSW, Sydney Theatre Company Foundation)
profile: Daughter of media mogul Kerry Packer and elder sister of James Packer, she became a billionaire after the family fortune was divided in 2015, giving her investments including a Crown Resorts stake. Famously low-profile, she drove the creation of the A$160m National Philanthropic Fund (2014) and chairs the Packer Family Foundation, focusing on arts, education and environmental science.
interesting_fact: She was one of five women donors credited with championing the Art Gallery of NSW's Sydney Modern expansion, and served as vice-president of the gallery's board of trustees.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2020 she and the Packer Family Foundation pledged A$240,000 to a philanthropist-backed rescue of Sydney's Carriageworks arts centre when it went into administration during COVID.
notes: Very private; no published personal, office or foundation contact found. Avoid family-settlement topics. Only plausible route is via arts institutions she serves (AGNSW, Sydney Theatre Company Foundation). Appointed AM (2020) per Wikipedia. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so contacts not exhaustively checked.

name: Liang Changlin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Dingdong Maicai (Dingdong Fresh); stepped down as CEO in 2026 after Meituan agreed to acquire the company
profile: Army veteran (12 years' service) turned serial entrepreneur in Shanghai's Zhangjiang: built video software, then mother-and-baby community Yaya.com (sold to TAL in 2016), then founded fresh-grocery e-commerce platform Dingdong Maicai in 2017, listing it on the NYSE in 2021. In 2026 Meituan agreed to buy Dingdong for about US$717m; Liang handed the CEO role to CFO Wang Song and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Named on China's 2020 national honour roll of veteran entrepreneurs ('全国退役军人创业光荣榜') for job creation.
deep_cut_fact: His first pot of gold came from a piece of software: shortly after leaving the army in 2002 he wrote 'Easy Video Joiner & Splitter', billed as the first video cut-and-join tool, and sold about 50,000 copies worldwide for roughly US$800,000.
notes: Meituan deal and CEO change per Jiemian (https://www.jiemian.com/article/14091669.html); IR mailbox may change once Dingdong is absorbed into Meituan. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Brandt Louie
current_role: Chairman and CEO, H.Y. Louie Co. Ltd. and London Drugs Ltd. (Vancouver)
profile: Fourth-generation head of the Louie family business, founded when his grandfather H.Y. Louie opened a Chinatown store in 1903. Brandt worked as a chartered accountant before joining in 1972 and has led the business since 1998. The Vancouver-based group runs the London Drugs chain and IGA grocery operations and is one of BC's largest private companies. He was SFU's chancellor for six years and was named to the Order of Canada in 2024.
interesting_fact: H.Y. Louie's first store, originally called the Kwong Chong Company, sold seed, fertilizer and wholesale groceries. The family has been in the Vancouver area since the 19th century.
deep_cut_fact: He is a keen fisherman who supports ocean conservation and works with First Nations on preserving fish stocks. In 2023 he spoke in the Senate Chamber in Ottawa about families affected by the 1923 Chinese Exclusion Act, and he was a major catalyst for a national strategy on anti-Asian racism.
notes: Honours include the Order of Canada (2024), the Order of BC and the BC Business Laureates. Former RBC board member. He is approachable through community and civic channels in Vancouver. Older London Drugs press releases list Hartley PR as the media agency, but those contacts date from 2013-15 and may be stale.

name: Harvey Jones
current_role: Managing Partner, Square Wave Ventures; NVIDIA director since 1993 (Nvidia's board page lists him as Chair of the Board, plus audit and nominating/governance committees)
profile: EDA pioneer: co-founded Daisy Systems in 1981 (president/CEO to 1987), then led Synopsys 1987-1998 as CEO and executive chairman, and co-founded processor-IP firm Tensilica in 1997 (chairman until Cadence bought it in 2013). An Nvidia director since its 1993 founding, he became a billionaire from his Nvidia stake and invests via Square Wave Ventures.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Nvidia's board since the company was founded in 1993, and is a billionaire almost entirely from director compensation and stock, owning about 0.03% of Nvidia.
deep_cut_fact: In high school he discovered a teletype link to a timesharing system, taught himself BASIC, and 'sold my chemistry homework to my classmates' - his first entrepreneurial exercise. He then nearly took an IBM job on Allegheny Airlines' reservations system before joining CAD firm Calma.
notes: Georgetown math/CS and MIT Sloan MS. Gave a 2009 Computer History Museum oral history (good prep material). No personal social accounts or published Square Wave contact found; Nvidia corporate PR is the formal route. Chair title taken from nvidia.com board page (not independently re-verified).

name: Fu Guangming
current_role: Chairman, Fujian Sunner Development Co. (SZSE: 002299), Guangze, Fujian
profile: Fu Guangming founded what became Sunner Group, China's largest white-feather broiler producer and a major chicken supplier to KFC and McDonald's in China. He started with a small hatchery in Guangze county, Fujian, in 1983. He still chairs listed Fujian Sunner Development, which now produces over 600 million broilers a year, and he shares the fortune with his wife and his daughter Fu Fenfang, a company director.
interesting_fact: Sunner grew from a single flock and about 10 staff into a vertically integrated poultry group that produces over 600 million white-feather broilers a year.
deep_cut_fact: In 1983, aged 30, he quit a secure job at the Guangze County People's Armed Forces Department and borrowed RMB 20,000 to open a chicken farm. He told Yicai the idea came from his childhood: with so many siblings, the family's chickens were saved for his mother after childbirth.

public_contacts.value: snljj@sunnercn.com (Board Secretary Liao Junjie, Fujian Sunner Development)

notes: Rarely talks to Western media, so expect to work in Chinese. Best route is the board secretary's office (IR). Daughter Fu Fenfang is involved in management. Podcast angle is limited apart from the entrepreneurship story.

name: Femi Otedola
current_role: Chairman and largest shareholder (~27.7% as of Aug 2026), First HoldCo Plc (parent of First Bank of Nigeria)
profile: Lagos businessman who built Zenon Petroleum into a dominant diesel supplier, later controlled Forte Oil and then Geregu Power, whose majority stake he sold in 2025 for about $750M. He has since redeployed capital into First HoldCo, steadily raising his stake toward a stated goal of over 51%, and published the memoir 'Making It Big' in 2025.
interesting_fact: At one point he was Nigeria's largest private ship owner; one of his vessels, a flat-bottomed 16,000-tonne bunker ship, was reported as the first of its kind in Africa.
deep_cut_fact: In his memoir he recalls that while he was in A-levels his father set up Impact Press, a printing company in Surulere, Lagos; he became fascinated with the machines, skipped Upper Sixth to join the business, and became its MD at about 25 before founding Centre Force in 1994.
notes: Best route: the official memoir site's contact form, which has 'Media Inquiry' and 'Speaking Engagement' options. Active on social media; news reports cite X @realFemiOtedola, but I did not verify it from an official page, and reports give conflicting Instagram handles. First HoldCo site was unreachable from here. His memoir 'Making It Big' (Aug 2025) is a natural outreach hook.

name: Wang Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Seazen Group (formerly Future Land Development, HK:1030) / Seazen Holdings (SH:601155); no current formal executive post found
profile: Wang Zhenhua founded the Shanghai-headquartered property developer now called Seazen Group (formerly Future Land Development, HK-listed) after entering property development in 1993, building it into one of China's large developers. He resigned his posts after his 2018 detention; the group is now chaired by Wang Xiaosong, and 2025 filings still describe Wang as controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: He earned an EMBA from Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business in July 2005.
notes: CAUTION: Wang was detained in 2018 and sentenced in June 2020 to 5 years in prison over the molestation of a 9-year-old girl (reported by Caixin). Not recommended as a podcast guest. Forbes bio (still calling him chairman) is outdated. Release date and current status not confirmed. Conviction source: https://www.caixinglobal.com/company-info/seazen-7712.html

name: Filippo Ghirelli
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Infracorp (infrastructure, energy, AI and space investment group); founder of family office Sophrance Global
profile: Monaco-based Italian engineer-entrepreneur (mid-40s). Built real estate businesses in Italy/North Africa, founded energy-efficiency firm Genera Group in 2009 (sold to SUSI Partners in 2024), and in 2023 bought a 25% stake in India's Nayara Energy refinery from Trafigura for $169M - the deal behind most of his ~$1.5B fortune. Infracorp (2024) targets airports, energy, data centres, AI and orbital modules.
interesting_fact: He bought Trafigura's 25% stake in Nayara Energy (India's second-largest refinery) for $169M, a 42% discount to Trafigura's 2017 price; Forbes estimates it is now worth at least $1.1B. Infracorp's plans include data centres in outer space.
deep_cut_fact: Right after graduating from college in Rome he left for Africa, starting his career as an engineer on infrastructure projects in Guinea and Mali.
notes: Strong fit for energy + data-center podcast (Infracorp plans ~600M in airports, data centres and space; AI lab 'Manthica'). Speaks publicly (Forbes interviews, SuperReturn Private Wealth speaker, appears on a Buzzsprout podcast). Nayara is EU-sanctioned due to Rosneft co-ownership - sensitive. Confirm sophrance.com is his Sophrance Global before using.

name: Steven Meisel
current_role: Managing member of Pencross Energy, LLC (Dallas), an early investor in Fermi America (Fermi Inc., Nasdaq: FRMI)
profile: Steven Meisel is a Dallas investor whose fortune comes from Fermi America, the Amarillo, Texas REIT co-founded by Rick Perry and Toby Neugebauer to build 'Project Matador', a gigawatt-scale private power and AI data-center campus. Through Pencross Energy he held 56.25m Fermi shares (9.41%) at the October 2025 IPO, making him a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list. He had sold down to about 4.5% by March 2026.
interesting_fact: Fermi's October 2025 Nasdaq debut ($682.5m raised at $21/share, up about 54% on day one) instantly minted several billionaires; Meisel's Pencross Energy was then a 9.41% holder of a company with no revenue yet, planning nuclear, gas and solar power for AI data centers.
notes: Not the fashion photographer Steven Meisel. Identity from SEC 13G filings (Pencross Energy LLC / Steven Meisel, Fermi Inc.) and Fermi's 2026 proxy contest filings, which describe him as a close associate of Griffin Perry. He is caught up in the 2026 Neugebauer-board fight and related petitions (avoid). Some outlets link him to 'FG1 Capital'; unverified. No published contacts.

name: Wang Kunxiao
current_role: Director (formerly vice chairman and chairman), Yantai Jereh Oilfield Services Group (002353.SZ)
profile: Wang Kunxiao (王坤晓, b. 1969) is a co-founder of Jereh Group, founded in Yantai in 1999 with Sun Weijie and others; Jereh grew from oilfield equipment trading into fracturing fleets, gas compression, oil and gas engineering, new energy and power. He was vice chairman then chairman of the listed Jereh Oilfield Services and remains a board director.
interesting_fact: Jereh now runs a dedicated 'Data Center & Power' segment and markets PowerVEGA, a power-generation product built for AI data centers ('No waiting, power for AI now'), launched at RE+ 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a teacher at the Yantai Gold Technical School - the same school where co-founder Sun Weijie worked - before becoming deputy GM of Yantai Gold Economic Development Co.; he later earned an EMBA from the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
notes: No longer chairman (current chairman Li Zhiyong; president Sun Weijie), so he is a lower-profile founder-director. Jereh's gas-turbine/data-center power push is a strong podcast hook; route via Jereh securities office (board secretary Qu Ning).

name: Somphote Ahunai
current_role: Founder and former CEO of Energy Absolute PCL (Thailand); resigned as director/executive effective July 2024
profile: Thai entrepreneur and former stockbroker/financier who founded Energy Absolute in 2006, turning a biodiesel plant into a SET-listed renewable group spanning solar and wind farms, a battery gigafactory (Amita) and electric buses/boats (Mine Mobility), earning it the nickname 'Tesla of Thailand'. He held roughly 30-40% of EA; he stepped down in 2024 and dropped off Forbes' list after 2024.
interesting_fact: Energy Absolute was dubbed the 'Tesla of Southeast Asia' as it expanded from renewables into EVs and a lithium-ion battery gigafactory in Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: He had planned to retire at 36 as a millionaire stockbroker, but was drawn into an unprofitable biodiesel factory his family had invested in; with an electrical-engineering background, he taught himself mechanical and chemical engineering from books and rebuilt the plant from scratch - the seed of EA. In 2020 he still wore a Uniqlo suit and rode the MRT.
notes: Sensitive: he and a deputy resigned from EA in July 2024 after Thailand's SEC filed a criminal complaint alleging fraud (see https://www.caproasia.com/?p=44424); approach with care and do not route via EA. MBA from Univ. of Pittsburgh (Katz), undergrad Chulalongkorn. No personal published contact found.

name: Neha Narkhede
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Oscilar (AI risk decisioning / fraud prevention); co-founder and former CTO of Confluent
profile: Pune-born engineer who, at LinkedIn, co-created Apache Kafka, the open-source streaming system now underpinning real-time data pipelines worldwide. In 2014 she co-founded Confluent to commercialize Kafka; it IPO'd in 2021 at ~$9.1B. Since 2021 she has run Oscilar, an AI-native risk and fraud-decisioning platform for fintechs and banks, and angel-invests in startups.
interesting_fact: She co-wrote the O'Reilly book 'Kafka: The Definitive Guide' (2017) with Gwen Shapira and Todd Palino, and Oscilar won a 2025 Banking Tech Award while she made Inc.'s 2025 Female Founders 500.
deep_cut_fact: Her fascination with computing began when her parents bought her a computer at age eight; after a BE from the University of Pune and an MS at Georgia Tech, her first job was at Oracle before she joined LinkedIn's Kafka team.
notes: Active public speaker (Money20/20, Fintech Meetup, Slush) and on X/LinkedIn - good podcast prospect for a data-infrastructure angle. Another Oscilar release routed media to an outside rep (Tim Granholm, Shallot). Input net worth is from 2022 Hurun; she dropped off Forbes' real-time list.

name: Sait-Salam Gutseriev
current_role: Russian businessman; co-owner of Gutseriev-family oil assets (took control of Neftisa and his brother Mikhail's RussNeft stake after 2021 EU sanctions on Mikhail); long-time head of PFC BIN
profile: Younger brother of Safmar founder Mikhail Gutseriev, born 1959 in Akmolinsk (now Astana). An oil engineer from Grozny, he ran the BIN industrial-financial company from 1993, sat on BIN bank and RussNeft boards, and served two terms in the State Duma (1999-2007). He became a key holder of the family's oil assets after Mikhail was sanctioned.
interesting_fact: He was a two-term State Duma deputy (1999-2007) and holds both a doctorate in economics (2003) and a candidate degree in law (2000).
deep_cut_fact: He started at the bottom of the oil-products business: in 1978 he was an operator at the Grozny oil distribution depot, becoming its workshop chief in 1983, after graduating from the Grozny Oil Institute in chemical-production machinery.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK in June 2022 - check sanctions rules before any outreach. Only on Forbes lists 2016-2017; no English Wikipedia page, very low public profile, no published personal or office contacts found. Web search budget ran out during this profile, so current holdings were not re-verified beyond Wikipedia.

name: Su Weizhong
current_role: Former co-founder and senior shareholder of CEFC China Energy (中国华信能源); former actual controller of Huaxin International (002018.SZ); no current public role found
profile: Su Weizhong (苏卫忠, b. Sept 1968) co-founded, with Ye Jianming, the Fujian trading business that grew into CEFC China Energy, a Shanghai oil-trading conglomerate that briefly ranked among China's biggest private firms (Hurun: 华信石油, oil & chemicals; Forbes 2016-18). He ran Shandong Huaxin and was actual controller of listed Huaxin International. CEFC collapsed in 2018.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Hurun ranked him No. 65 in China with RMB 26bn, at the height of CEFC's global oil-trading and acquisition spree.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he co-founded Fujian Huaxin Import & Export with Ye Jianming and Ye Xiangdong; Fujian Huaxin Holdings followed in 2005, the seed of what became CEFC China Energy.
notes: Identity confirmed via Hurun API (苏卫忠, 华信石油, Shanghai, 2015/2017) and Chinese press. CEFC collapsed in 2018 after Ye Jianming's detention; in 2019 Su was put on a court consumption-restriction list as Huaxin International's controller (Sina, Sept 2019). Sensitive; not a realistic podcast guest. No published contacts.

name: James Kim
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Amkor Technology (retired as Executive Chairman 31 Oct 2024); family remains a major AMKR holder
profile: James Joo-Jin Kim, eldest son of ANAM founder Hyang-Soo Kim, studied at Penn and taught at Villanova before founding Amkor Electronics in Philadelphia in 1968 to sell ANAM's chips in the US. Amkor became a top outsourced semiconductor packaging and test (OSAT) firm (IPO 1998) and now does advanced packaging for AI chips, incl. a new Arizona plant.
interesting_fact: Amkor (America + Korea) grew from a Philadelphia sales office for his father's ANAM, whose 1970 metal-can transistor shipments were Korea's first recorded semiconductor export. Kim also chaired retailer Electronics Boutique, sold to GameStop in 2005.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Amkor he taught at Villanova, which later gave him an honorary Doctor of Commercial Science (1990). A Penn alumnus (W'59, G'61, GR'63), he endowed Penn's James Joo-Jin Kim Center for Korean Studies and a Wharton professorship; he won the 1998 Semiconductor Industry Award as a pioneer of merchant packaging.
notes: Born c.1935-36 and retired from operating roles; no personal public channels found. Kim family trusts remain major AMKR holders. ir@amkor.com was reported in Amkor's Jan 2026 Investor Day release (Business Wire); not independently fetched here. Strong AI-chip advanced-packaging angle via Amkor.

name: Johnathan Oringer
current_role: Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Chairman, Shutterstock (NYSE: SSTK) - back as CEO since October 2026
profile: Programmer-photographer Jon Oringer founded Shutterstock in 2003 with his own savings and about 30,000 of his own photos, built it into a global stock-media marketplace and took it public in 2012, becoming known as New York's first tech billionaire. He was executive chairman from 2020; after the planned Getty Images merger was terminated in July 2026, he returned as CEO in October 2026.
interesting_fact: To seed Shutterstock he bought a Canon Rebel and shot about 100,000 photos himself in six months, launching with a culled set of 30,000 images, a 600 sq ft office and a $49/month unlimited-download subscription.
deep_cut_fact: As a Stony Brook student in the 1990s he wrote and sold thousands of copies of one of the web's first pop-up blockers and ran about ten one-person subscription software startups (personal firewalls, cookie blockers, trademark managers); he is also a certified commercial helicopter pilot.
notes: Very current: per the Nov 2026 proxy (DEF 14A) he became CEO and Chairman in October 2026 after the Getty Images merger agreement was terminated on July 7, 2026. Shutterstock's AI data-licensing business (selling training data to AI labs) is a natural podcast angle.

name: Xiao Chunming
current_role: Unclear. Possibly the founder of Guizhou Honglicheng (宏立城) Group, Guiyang, whose founder is reported as 肖春红 (Xiao Chunhong)
profile: Listed by Hurun (2012-2015) for Honglicheng real estate. Guizhou Honglicheng Group is the Guiyang developer behind the giant Huaguoyuan (花果园) complex, but Chinese media name its founder as 肖春红 (Xiao Chunhong), not 肖春明. This may be the same person under a variant name, though that could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Honglicheng's Huaguoyuan project in Guiyang was nicknamed 'China's No.1 mega-development' (中国第一神盘) for its enormous scale.
notes: Name mismatch: no source links '肖春明' to Honglicheng, while the reported founder is 肖春红, so verify identity before any outreach. Media since 2022 report that the group is under heavy financial strain (court enforcement actions and a troubled Indonesian new-town project, 美加达新城). He has been off the rich lists since 2015, making him a weak candidate. No published contacts found.

current_role: Shareholder, Harbin Gloria Pharmaceuticals (誉衡药业, SZSE 002437); current role unverified
profile: Bai Lihui's fortune is tied to Harbin Gloria Pharmaceuticals, a Heilongjiang-based drugmaker listed in Shenzhen. She is understood (unverified) to be a co-controlling shareholder alongside founder Zhu Jiman. No further details could be verified in this pass.
