deep_cut_fact: Shengrun's ties to US markets: through China Infrastructure Investment Corp, the family's toll-road business (Pingdingshan Pinglin Expressway) was listed on Nasdaq, and in 2011 a Shengrun subsidiary, Zhengzhou Simian Real Estate, was folded into the listed company via VIE agreements.
notes: Hurun romanises husband's name as Li Xipeng (李喜朋, not 李西鹏). Hurun data: Shengrun Holding, Zhengzhou, Henan; Shu b. 1965. Company site www.srkg.com.cn did not respond. No personal public channels found; any outreach would go via Li Xipeng / Shengrun Holding. Baidu/Sogou blocked automated access, so Chinese news coverage was only partly checked.

name: Cai Di'e
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2022-2024) jointly with Wang Mingwang as a source of Sunwoda wealth; personal role at Sunwoda not confirmed
profile: Appears on the Hurun Global list 2022-2024 together with Wang Mingwang, co-founder (with Wang Wei) of Shenzhen-based Sunwoda Electronic (SZSE: 300207), a major lithium-ion battery maker for phones/laptops, EVs and energy storage. Her own role and relationship to the company could not be confirmed from public sources checked.
interesting_fact: Sunwoda, the source of this fortune, was the world's largest supplier of batteries for smartphones, laptops and tablets by 2024 shipments, with a 34.3% share of mobile-phone batteries.
notes: Identity uncertain: could not find a public bio or Chinese name for Cai Di'e (web-search budget exhausted mid-lane). Any approach would go through Sunwoda corporate/IR; Wang Mingwang or chairman Wang Wei are the public faces. Energy-storage/EV battery fit is good.

name: Vladimir Shmunis
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, RingCentral (NYSE: RNG)
profile: Ukraine-born engineer (SF State BS/MS in computer science) who founded RingCentral in 1999 and built it into a cloud business-communications company with over $2B in revenue. After a brief stint as executive chairman in 2023 he returned as CEO in December 2023 and has pushed AI-focused products; supports Stanford cancer research and Tel Aviv University's Shmunis School of Biomedicine.
interesting_fact: UC Today dubbed him 'the godfather of UCaaS'; RingCentral has been a Gartner Magic Quadrant leader for UCaaS for 12 straight years, and he received the Ellis Island Honors Society Award in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before RingCentral he founded Ring Zero Systems, a pioneer of desktop business-communications software that shipped more than 25 million copies bundled by PC makers such as IBM, HP, Sony and Toshiba, and was later acquired by Motorola.
notes: Goes by 'Vlad'. Best route is RingCentral media relations (named PR contact on 2026 releases). Named inventor on several US patents.

name: Lin Jiangwei
current_role: Founder and largest individual shareholder (~13.4%), Suzhou Jolywood (Zhonglai) Photovoltaic New Materials (300393.SZ); no longer a director or executive
profile: Lin Jianwei (林建伟; listed as Lin Jiangwei) founded Jolywood (Zhonglai) in Suzhou, Jiangsu in 2008, building it into the world's top solar-backsheet maker and an early mass producer of n-type TOPCon cells. In Feb 2023 state-owned Zhejiang Energy's listed arm Zheneng Electric Power took control; he remains the largest individual holder alongside Zhang Yuzheng (~2.75%).
interesting_fact: Jolywood's FFC double-sided coated backsheet broke a foreign technology monopoly in China, and the company says it was No.1 globally in PV backsheet shipments four years running (2021-2024), with over 210 GW shipped cumulatively.
notes: Correct Chinese spelling is 林建伟 (Lin Jianwei). Not on Jolywood's current board (chairman Zhang Chengyu); company now controlled by Zhejiang SASAC via Zheneng. Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Alive status not independently confirmed (still listed as shareholder at 30 Sep 2026). Web search budget exhausted before deep-cut research.

name: Zhang Yuzheng
current_role: Co-founder of Suzhou Jolywood (Zhonglai) Photovoltaic (300393.SZ); no current board or management role found
profile: Zhang Yuzheng (张育政) co-founded the predecessor of Jolywood/Zhonglai, Suzhou Zhonglai Solar Materials Technology, in Changshu in March 2008. The company grew from PV backsheets into N-type TOPCon cells and modules and listed on ChiNext in Sept 2014. Hurun listed this wealth jointly (to 2022) with Lin Jianwei. Control has since passed to state-owned Zhejiang Zheneng Electric Power, and Lin waived his voting rights in 2026.
interesting_fact: Jolywood went from a 2008 backsheet start-up to a ChiNext listing in only six years (Sept 2014), then became an early mass producer of N-type bifacial cells before Zhejiang Energy took control.
deep_cut_fact: Company filings name her as one of just two founding investors (with Dai Enqi) of Suzhou Zhonglai Solar Materials Technology, registered in Changshu on 7 March 2008.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. The founding family no longer controls Jolywood (Zheneng Electric is now the controlling shareholder), so the company is not a route to Zhang. Last Hurun appearance was 2022; current wealth probably much lower. Avoid the change of control and losses as topics.

name: Zang Jianjun
current_role: Unknown; formerly Executive Chairman of SGX-listed CEFC International Ltd and a senior executive of the Huaxin/CEFC China Energy group
profile: Zang Jianjun (臧建军, b. ~1974) is a petrochemical-trading executive from the Huaxin/CEFC China Energy group (founder Ye Jianming). He ran Hua Xin Energy Holdings 2006-11, then became CEO (2012) and Executive Chairman (2013) of SGX-listed CEFC International. CEFC collapsed in 2018 and went bankrupt in 2020. His current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: He joined CEFC International's board in January 2012, became CEO in December 2012 and Executive Chairman in December 2013, handing the CEO role to ex-PetroChina finance manager Lu Dachuan in February 2015.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in Hebei trading: business manager at Hebei Baoding International Trading Co (1995-96), international trading manager at Hebei Lixiang Corp (1996-99), then chemical business unit GM and deputy GM at DaGang Petro Chemical (1999-2006) before Huaxin.
notes: Identity: Hurun 2015/2017 entries list 臧建军, b. 1974, Shanghai, company 华信石油 / Huaxin (oil & chemicals), which matches the CEFC (华信) group. The CEFC group collapsed after chairman Ye Jianming was detained in 2018 (see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CEFC_China_Energy). No current role, channels or contacts found. Approach with care given the group's history.

name: Lin Haifeng (林海峰)
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Risen Energy Co. (东方日升, SZSE: 300118)
profile: Born 1975, founder of Risen Energy, a Ningbo (Ninghai)-based solar manufacturer founded in 2002 that makes PV cells and modules and builds solar plants, with sales offices in Australia, India, the US and Japan; listed in Shenzhen in 2010. Chairman since at least 2021 and holds ~283M shares; the company is pushing heterojunction (HJT) modules.
interesting_fact: Risen set up a 'Global PV Research Institute' in Nov 2023 to drive integrated cell/module R&D, and its 2023 revenue reached about RMB 35.3bn with net profit up ~46%, helped by its heterojunction technology.
deep_cut_fact: His official company bio notes he holds an EMBA from Ningbo University and has been named one of Ningbo's 'Ten Outstanding Young People' and 'Ten Charity Stars', as well as a 'Changzhou Star Entrepreneur'.
notes: Low international profile; no personal accounts found. Board secretary is Zhou Yinning. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so profile relies on exchange-data and company pages. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Zhang Jinfang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Chipone Technology (Beijing) Co. (集创北方); since Jan 2026 also actual controller of Silicon-valley display-chip firm Analogix/硅数股份
profile: Born 1985 in Shuozhou, Shanxi; PhD in circuits and systems from Beijing Jiaotong University. Founded display-driver chip designer Chipone in 2008 while a first-year master's student; it became a ~RMB 31B unicorn backed by Xiaomi, vivo, Huawei Hubble and BOE, and is preparing a STAR Market IPO. In 2026 he took control of display-chip maker Analogix (硅数股份).
interesting_fact: Chipone's chips are behind the 16K wraparound LED display of the Las Vegas Sphere, and it holds over 45% of the global LED display-driver chip market.
deep_cut_fact: He started Chipone in 2008 with four classmates in a ~40 sqm rented room in Zhongguancun; within a year the five-person team shipped its first product, a phone-charger power-management chip, before moving into LED driver and touch chips.
notes: Young (b. 1985) chip founder; IPO-in-preparation context means company may limit his media. Best route: Chipone public affairs (pr@). Display-chip focus is more consumer electronics than data center.

name: Radik Shaimiev
current_role: Businessman, Kazan; one of the main shareholders of the TAIF group (Tatarstan petrochemicals, merged into SIBUR in 2021); long-time Tatneft board member
profile: Son of Tatarstan's first president Mintimer Shaimiev (listed spelling 'Shaimev'). Trained as a civil engineer, he joined Kazan investment firm TAIF in 1992; TAIF became the holding company for Tatarstan's big petrochemical, refining and power assets, and he has sat on Tatneft's board since 1998. Also an internationally ranked rally/autocross driver and was named president of FC Rubin Kazan in 2017.
interesting_fact: A Master of Sport (international class) in motorsport, he won the 2003 European Autocross Championship in the touring-car class, with his own brother Airat as main title rival, and still competes in classic rallies, including World Championship rounds.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as an architect-engineer: after Marine service in Vladivostok (1982-84) and graduating from the Kazan Civil Engineering Institute in 1989, he worked as an engineer in architectural-planning workshop No. 2 of the Kazgrazhdanproekt institute.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Sanctioned by Ukraine (Oct 2022) and Canada (June 2025), which makes outreach/booking legally and reputationally sensitive for a Western podcast. Only data point is Hurun 2014; TAIF has since been folded into SIBUR.

name: Zhang Liguo
current_role: Chairman, Harbin Fuerjia Technology Co. (敷尔佳, SZSE: 301371)
profile: Zhang Liguo (张立国, b. 1964), a licensed pharmacist and senior engineer, built Harbin-based Fuerjia into one of China's best-known 'medical-dressing' facial-mask and skincare brands, selling through professional and online channels. He took the company public in Shenzhen in August 2023, raising about $306m, and stepped back from the general-manager role in December 2023 while remaining chairman.
interesting_fact: Fuerjia built a 1-billion-yuan 'Northern Beauty Valley' (北方美谷) manufacturing and R&D base in Harbin New Area, moving in during April 2023 - a bet on making Harbin a cosmetics hub.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1986 as a pharmacist at the Heilongjiang Provincial Cadres' Sanatorium, then became production dispatcher and workshop technical director at Harbin Pharmaceutical Group's No. 5 pharmaceutical plant (1989-92) before going into business.
notes: Weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast; possible angle is consumer-brand entrepreneurship in northeast China. IR email from the 2026 half-year report summary. Outreach likely needs to be in Chinese.

name: Rao Wei
current_role: Chairman (and legal representative), Shenzhen New Industries Biomedical Engineering (Snibe, 新产业, SZSE 300832)
profile: Rao Wei (饶微) joined Snibe in 1997, aged 33, when it was an 18-person trading firm. He led its move into in-house chemiluminescence immunoassay analysers and reagents, and it is now China's leading domestic player in that field, listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He is a major holder but not the founder or controller.
interesting_fact: Snibe's chemiluminescence R&D, started in 2000, took about a decade to pay off. During that time Rao and another major shareholder gave up dividends to reinvest everything in R&D, and spent over 100 million yuan learning to make reagent raw materials in-house.
deep_cut_fact: The trigger was a setback: soon after he joined, a Swiss supplier pulled Snibe's distribution rights, which convinced him China needed its own core technology. The first lab was set up in a residential flat in Nanshan, Shenzhen. Today the campus is planted with slow-growing golden nanmu and huanghuali trees, a nod to his goal of a 'century-old company' benchmarked on Roche.
notes: A technology-first, 'self-reliance' story that suits an entrepreneurship podcast. He gave a long interview to China Securities Journal in 2023. The IR email comes from the 2020 annual report summary, so confirm it is still current. In 2012 he insisted that about 120 employees hold shares directly as individuals.

name: Michael Krasny
current_role: Founder (retired) of CDW; philanthropist via the Circle of Service Foundation
profile: A University of Illinois business graduate (1975), Krasny founded CDW (Computer Discount Warehouse) in the early 1980s after reselling PCs from home. He built it into a major IT reseller, took it public in 1993, and sold it to Madison Dearborn Partners in 2007 for $7.3bn. He has kept a low profile since and gives to Jewish causes and medical research through his Circle of Service Foundation.
interesting_fact: CDW began when Krasny, then 28 and out of work, placed a $3 classified ad in the Chicago Tribune to sell his own IBM PC. The demand he saw led him to start reselling computers.
deep_cut_fact: Before computers he sold Toyotas at his father's dealership in Arlington Heights, and he first sold PCs under the name 'MPK Computers' before renaming it CDW. Since 2009 he has run a woodworking hobby shop in Northbrook, Illinois, Custom Woodworking Design, which makes plaques and awards.
notes: Very private since 2007. No published foundation contact found. The woodworking shop is a public business but is not a sensible outreach route without his consent. Not to be confused with KQED radio host Michael Krasny.

name: Herbert Sy
current_role: Adviser to the board, SM Investments Corp.; director, SM Prime Holdings (Philippines)
profile: Second-youngest of the six children of the late SM founder Henry Sy Sr., who all hold posts in the conglomerate spanning retail, banking (BDO, China Bank), property, mining and hotels. Herbert is closely involved in the group's supermarket operations and sits on the SM Prime board. He holds a management degree from De La Salle University.
interesting_fact: In 2022 SM Investments agreed to buy Philippine Geothermal Production Co. in a $304m all-share deal to cut its carbon footprint, a notable energy move for a retail-and-property group.
notes: Low-profile Sy sibling who rarely gives interviews; the realistic route is SM Investments corporate communications/IR. The SM sites blocked automated access, so no contact was captured. The geothermal deal is the energy hook.

name: Ranga Raju Kanumuri
current_role: Chairman, Sai Life Sciences (Hyderabad; NSE/BSE-listed CRDMO)
profile: Dr. K. Ranga Raju, a pharmaceutical scientist turned entrepreneur, founded Sai Life Sciences in Hyderabad in 1999 as a medicinal-chemistry partner to US biotechs. It is now an integrated contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRDMO) with sites in India, the UK and the US. Sai Life listed in India in December 2024, raising about INR 30.4bn; his son Krishna Kanumuri is MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: He holds a Doctor of Pharmacy plus bachelor's and master's degrees from the Massachusetts College of Pharmacy in Boston, after a first pharmacy degree from the University of Mysore.
deep_cut_fact: Sai Life Sciences was originally founded in 1999 as 'Sai Dru Syn Laboratories'. It began as a small medicinal-chemistry services provider for US biotechs and was renamed later to reflect a broader life-sciences focus.
notes: Low personal profile; CEO Krishna Kanumuri is the company's public voice and may be the easier guest. Route requests via IR or general inquiries.

name: Mikhail Fedyaev
current_role: Co-owner and president of Siberian Business Union (SDS) holding, Kemerovo (coal, fertilizers, engineering, transport)
profile: Kemerovo businessman (b. 1962, Prokopyevsk) who started as a car-factory mechanic. With partner Vladimir Gridin he won control of the Chernigovets coal pit in 1999 and in 2004 formed Siberian Business Union (SDS), now spanning coal mining, fertilizers/chemicals, engineering, transport and construction in Kuzbass. He has been SDS president since 2007.
interesting_fact: He was elected chairman of a production-and-construction cooperative in 1989, one of the first Soviet-era private ventures, and in the 1990s ran the Kemerovo office of MirInvest, where he met his long-time partner Vladimir Gridin.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer in 'Automobiles and motor transport' at the Kuzbass Polytechnic Institute (1985), rose to deputy head of a truck column, and in 1996 was general director of Partner-Grundfos, a Kemerovo venture tied to the Danish pump maker, before going into coal.
notes: Sensitive: owner of the Listvyazhnaya mine where a 2021 methane explosion killed 51; he was arrested in 2021 and given a suspended sentence in 2025. No published personal or press contact found. Russian-language, regionally focused; likely a poor fit for outreach.

name: Gao Jifan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Trina Solar Co., Ltd. (SSE STAR: 688599), Changzhou
profile: Gao Jifan, a Changzhou native with chemistry degrees from Nanjing University and Jilin University, founded Trina Solar in 1997. Trina listed on the NYSE in 2006, went private in 2017 and relisted on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020; it is now one of the world's largest PV module makers and has expanded into energy storage, trackers and digital energy services, with plants in China, Vietnam and Thailand.
interesting_fact: Trina was named the first solar 'Industry Shaper' by the World Economic Forum in Davos, and was the first PV and energy-storage company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market.
deep_cut_fact: Trina says Gao was inspired to found the company by the Kyoto Protocol and the US 'Million Solar Roofs' initiative (both 1997); academically he is a physical chemist - MSc in physical chemistry from Jilin University (1988) after a Nanjing University chemistry BSc (1985).
notes: Frequent Davos/industry-forum speaker, so conference panels are a natural route. Son Gao Haichun became co-chairman in 2025 (succession under way). Could not verify a published press/IR email (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Tang Xiuguo
current_role: Director & President, Sany Group; rotating chair (alternating six-month terms with Xiang Wenbo since 2023)
profile: Tang Xiuguo is one of four co-founders, with Liang Wengen, Mao Zhongwu and Yuan Jinhua, of Sany Group, China's largest construction-machinery maker and among the biggest in the world. He has been president since 2002. When Liang retired in 2023, Sany moved to a rotating chair, with Tang and Xiang Wenbo alternating every six months as leader of daily operations.
interesting_fact: Sany started in 1986 as Lianyuan Welding Material Ltd in the town of Maotang, Hunan, with RMB 60,000 of capital. The four founders quit their jobs to start it, renamed it Sany in 1991 and moved to Changsha.
deep_cut_fact: He studied metallic materials at Central South University (bachelor's, 1983), which fits Sany's origins as a welding-materials factory before it moved into concrete pumps and excavators.
notes: Sany has a big energy business: listed subsidiary Sany Heavy Energy (wind turbines) and hydrogen and battery equipment, which makes it a strong energy-show angle. Only sales and service emails are published, with no press email. Rotating-chair source: https://www.yicaiglobal.com/news/2023051611-sanys-founding-chairman-retires-chinese-heavy-equipment-maker-to-adopt-rotating-chair-system

name: Igor Yakovlev
current_role: Founder and owner, Kari (Russian footwear, accessories and household-goods retail chain)
profile: Igor Nikolaevich Yakovlev (b. 1965, Makhachkala) founded the Eldorado consumer-electronics chain in 1994 and sold it to Czech group PPF in 2008–2011. In 2012 he founded Kari, now about 1,500 stores in 600+ cities across Russia, Belarus, Kazakhstan and Armenia. He also holds a stake in Kazakh electronics retailer Sulpak.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he returned to Forbes' global billionaires list 16 years after first dropping off it, this time on the back of Kari rather than Eldorado.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail he studied at the Dagestan Polytechnic Institute and the St Petersburg University of the Russian Interior Ministry, moving to Moscow in the 1990s where he launched Eldorado.
notes: Very low public profile; Kari website blocked automated fetch so no press email verified. Russia-based retail; check sanctions/compliance status before outreach. Forbes bio says he owned 50% of FC Anzhi Makhachkala in 2008–2011.

name: Thomas Bailey
profile: Deceased. Founder (1969) and long-time CEO of Denver mutual fund firm Janus. Forbes now marks his profile 'Deceased'; Wikipedia's infobox gives a death date of 30 Aug 2025 (unsourced).
notes: Forbes profile labelled Deceased (https://www.forbes.com/profile/thomas-bailey/); exact date per https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thomas_H._Bailey not independently confirmed. Skip.

name: Juan Maria Riberas Mera
current_role: Co-owner of Gestamp Automoción (with brother Francisco); widely reported as chairman of Gonvarri Industries (not re-verified this session)
profile: Known as Jon. He and his brother Francisco each own just over 25% of Gestamp, the listed Spanish auto-parts maker, through the family holding Acek. Their father Francisco Riberas Pampliega founded the steel processor Gonvarri in 1958, and the group diversified into auto parts in 1997. Jon trained in law and business and joined the company in junior management in 1992.
interesting_fact: Gonvarri started in 1958 as a small steel trading business founded by Francisco Riberas (1932-2010). Today it runs a Gonvarri Solar Steel unit making steel structures for solar plants, a link to the energy transition.
deep_cut_fact: Gonvarri's first site was Gonvarri Burgos (1958), followed by Hiasa in Asturias (1972) and Gonvarri Valencia (1978). The group's stated founding values are 'Honesty, Humility, Tenacity and Hard Work'.
notes: Good energy angle: Gonvarri Solar Steel makes solar mounting and tracker structures, and the family's Acek group also has renewables interests (not verified this session). info@gonvarri.com is Gonvarri's general corporate address, not a dedicated press line. He keeps a low public profile.

name: Wang Dong
current_role: Co-founder and Executive President, Moore Threads Technology (Beijing GPU maker; STAR Market 688795)
profile: Per Forbes, Wang Dong spent more than a decade as a sales director at Nvidia before co-founding Moore Threads in 2020 with former Nvidia China head Zhang Jianzhong. Moore Threads designs full-function GPUs for AI training/inference and graphics as a domestic Chinese alternative to Nvidia; it listed in Shanghai in December 2025, raising about $1.1B.
interesting_fact: Moore Threads' shares jumped about 468% on their Shanghai trading debut on 5 Dec 2025, with DeepSeek founder Liang Wenfeng's High-Flyer reported among institutional investors.
deep_cut_fact: At the July 2026 World AI Conference in Shanghai he argued the inference market has no 'universal chip' - only combinations of solutions - because inference scenarios are highly fragmented and no single company can monopolize them; he also noted Chinese frontier models' cost advantage.
notes: Common name; matched via Forbes URL (wang-dong-1 = Moore Threads cofounder, $1.4B on 2026 list). Input's 'Hurun China 2007-2021' entries predate Moore Threads (2020) and likely belong to another Wang Dong. Public speaker at WAIC - route via Moore Threads marketing (mkt@) or IR.

name: Vincent Lo
current_role: Chairman, Shui On Group and Shui On Land (HK: 272)
profile: Vincent Lo Hong-sui (born 1948, Hong Kong) founded the Shui On construction and building-materials group and its property arm Shui On Land. Shui On Land is best known for turning a run-down Shanghai neighbourhood into the Xintiandi shopping and entertainment district. He has chaired the HK Airport Authority (2014-15) and the HK Trade Development Council (2015-19), and is handing day-to-day leadership to his daughter Stephanie, vice chairman of Shui On Land.
interesting_fact: He was an early mover into mainland China: he began investing in Shanghai in 1984, building a hotel there with the Communist Youth League, long before Xintiandi made Shui On famous.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating (reportedly from the University of New South Wales), he started his first business with HK$100,000 borrowed from his father, property tycoon Lo Ying-shek, rather than joining the family firm Great Eagle. He received Hong Kong's highest honour, the Grand Bauhinia Medal, in 2017.
notes: Prominent HK establishment figure. Avoid the family trust feud and the Trump lawsuit. The best route is Shui On Land corporate communications or IR; the contact page is JS-rendered, so I couldn't extract an email. Shui On has low-carbon and urban-regeneration angles.

name: Dora Voigt de Assis
current_role: Shareholder of WEG S.A. (no board seat or executive role); architecture graduate (2020)
profile: Dora Voigt de Assis is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, Latin America's biggest electric-motor maker, an inheritance from her grandfather, co-founder Werner Ricardo Voigt. She holds no board or executive role at WEG and graduated with an architecture degree in 2020.
interesting_fact: WEG, founded in Jaraguá do Sul in 1961 by an electrician (Werner Voigt), an administrator and a mechanic, takes its name from the founders' first initials: Werner, Eggon and Geraldo.
deep_cut_fact: Her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt was the electrician of WEG's founding trio; the company started as 'Eletromotores Jaraguá' before adopting the WEG acronym. WEG now also makes generators, transformers and battery storage systems used in power grids.
notes: Very private, young heir with no public role; no published contact. WEG (chairman Décio da Silva) would be the more relevant energy-sector guest route, not her.

name: Cao Zheng
current_role: Major shareholder (wealth shared with chairman Cao Ji) of Zhejiang Hangke Technology (688006.SH); director and VP of the company until Dec 2021
profile: Cao Zheng (b. 1983) built his career inside Hangke, the Hangzhou maker of formation and grading equipment used in the back-end of lithium-ion battery production lines, rising from purchasing staff to director, deputy GM and head of sales. Hangke listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in July 2019; Hurun lists his fortune jointly with Cao Ji, Hangke's founder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Hangke was one of the first batch of companies to list on Shanghai's STAR Market (July 2019), and its post-processing equipment for EV battery cells is sold to major battery makers in China and abroad.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he spent 2005-2008 as an assistant engineer at STATS ChipPAC, the Singapore-based semiconductor packaging and test company; he holds Singapore permanent residency and a master's degree.
notes: No longer on Hangke's board (term ended Dec 2021), so current role is unclear; alive status not independently confirmed (no reports of death found, but web search budget ran out). The IR email is the company's board-secretary mailbox. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Li Chen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (founding-shareholder group with Li Zhen and Guoxuan Holding) of Gotion High-Tech (国轩高科, SZSE: 002074); holds ~1.57% directly and sits on boards of group-related companies
profile: Li Chen (李晨) is the son of Gotion High-Tech founder-chairman Li Zhen and, with him and Nanjing Guoxuan Holding, one of the company's acting-in-concert controlling shareholders. Hefei-based Gotion (formerly Anhui Guoxuan) makes LFP and other lithium-ion cells for EVs and grid energy storage, with Volkswagen China as a major strategic shareholder.
interesting_fact: Although Volkswagen (China) is a top shareholder, under its shareholder agreement VW irrevocably waives part of its voting rights so that its voting power stays at least 5 points below that of the founding shareholders - Guoxuan Holding, Li Zhen and Li Chen.
notes: Wealth listing is shared with father Li Zhen, the public face of Gotion; Li Chen keeps a low profile and his executive title (if any) is not confirmed in the 2026 interim report. Strong energy-storage fit, but the better interview target is likely Li Zhen. Contact via Gotion IR/board office.

name: Lu Weidong
current_role: Deputy General Manager, Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources Co. (鄂尔多斯, SSE: 600295 / 900936); previously a company director
profile: Lu Weidong is a long-serving senior executive of the Erdos group in Ordos, Inner Mongolia, whose listed arm Erdos Resources spans cashmere (the Erdos brand), coal, power and ferroalloy/chemicals. He sat on the listed company's board (still a director in mid-2025) and is listed as Deputy GM in the 2025 pay disclosure; Hurun ranks him for his group shareholding.
interesting_fact: The Erdos group combines one of China's best-known cashmere brands with an energy-and-metallurgy business (coal, power, silicon/ferroalloys) in Ordos, one of China's main coal regions.
notes: Role confirmed in Erdos Resources' Apr 2026 notice on executive pay (Lu Weidong, Deputy GM, 2025 pay RMB1.96M): https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604141821185338_1.pdf . Chairman is Wang Zhen. No personal channels; formal route would be the board secretary listed in Erdos Resources' annual report.

name: Huang Biliang
current_role: Co-founder, director & general manager, JoulWatt Technology (Hangzhou); co-controlling shareholder with chairman Zhou Xunwei
profile: Huang Biliang (b. 1971, Macau resident) earned BS/MS degrees at Tsinghua and a PhD at Virginia Tech, then spent 2001-2013 at Linear Technology as a design engineer and R&D center manager. He co-founded power-management chipmaker JoulWatt in Hangzhou in 2013 (GM since 2016); it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market and serves data-center/server power.
interesting_fact: Both JoulWatt founders, Huang and Zhou Xunwei, earned PhDs at Virginia Tech under power-electronics pioneer Fred C. Lee, and both later worked at Linear Technology before co-founding JoulWatt; Huang is the named inventor on 99 granted invention patents there.
deep_cut_fact: Per JoulWatt's IPO prospectus, he was the first to propose using coupled inductors to improve power modules' static and dynamic performance, an idea widely adopted by industry, with the work cited 2,000+ times; in 2015 his team was named a Zhejiang 'leading innovation and entrepreneurship team'.
notes: Technical founder, low media profile. Coupled-inductor/VRM power-delivery work is directly relevant to AI server power, a strong podcast angle. JoulWatt filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing in Jan 2026.

name: Keiko Erikawa
current_role: Director & Chairman Emeritus, Koei Tecmo Holdings; President & CEO, Koei Tecmo Corporate Finance; outside director, SoftBank Group
profile: Yokohama-born Tama Art University design graduate (b. 1949) who co-founded Koei in 1978 with husband Yoichi Erikawa, ran its finance, HR and deal-making, and served as president and chairman. A lifelong stock investor, she built Koei Tecmo's large securities portfolio and since 2025 heads the group's new finance subsidiary; she joined SoftBank Group's board in 2021.
interesting_fact: Koei became a game company because she gave her husband a personal computer for his 30th birthday in 1980; she also co-founded Koei using land she owned as loan collateral.
deep_cut_fact: She founded Koei's all-female 'Ruby Party' team and spent a decade hiring women programmers to launch 'Angelique' (1994), widely regarded as the first otome (games-for-women) title. In early-1980s distribution talks she held out for 55% wholesale pricing - Masayoshi Son's Japan SoftBank was the last holdout - and she affectionately calls him 'Son-chan'.
notes: She began investing in stocks as a high-schooler under her grandmother's guidance. She is also an honorary sommelier (Japan Sommelier Association, 2004). Her Erikawa Education Foundation (FOEE) funds scholarships for students from single-mother households. Outreach in Japanese via Koei Tecmo corporate channels.

name: Arthur Levine
current_role: Founding Partner and Co-Chairperson of the Executive Committee, Levine Leichtman Capital Partners (LLCP), Beverly Hills; co-owner of NWSL's San Diego Wave FC
profile: Arthur Levine co-founded Levine Leichtman Capital Partners in 1984 with his wife Lauren Leichtman, whom he married in 1979. Before that he invested in and was president of the radio syndicator Westwood One. LLCP is a middle-market 'structured private equity' firm that has raised about $14.8bn across 15 funds. Its exits include Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Wetzel's Pretzels and Nothing Bundt Cakes.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he and Leichtman bought the NWSL's San Diego Wave FC for about $113 million, then a record for a women's soccer club.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer and business manager, not a financier: he holds a J.D. from Columbia Law School, where he was a Harlan Fiske Stone Scholar, and an MBA from UCLA Anderson.
notes: His wife and co-founder Lauren Leichtman is the more public face, especially for the San Diego Wave, where she is the NWSL governor. The best route is LLCP's Beverly Hills main office or its media page. The Wave sale was announced in March 2024 (Loeb), and Forbes dates the purchase to October 2024.

name: Lauren Leichtman
current_role: Founding Partner and Co-Chairperson of the Executive Committee, Levine Leichtman Capital Partners (LLCP); co-owner of NWSL's San Diego Wave FC
profile: Leichtman co-founded Beverly Hills-based Levine Leichtman Capital Partners with her husband Arthur Levine in 1984. The middle-market private-equity firm, known for its 'structured private equity' approach, has raised about $16bn across 15 funds and invested in franchise brands such as Tropical Smoothie Cafe, Wetzel's Pretzels and Nothing Bundt Cakes. In 2024 the couple bought the San Diego Wave women's soccer club.
interesting_fact: In 2024 she and Levine agreed to buy NWSL's San Diego Wave FC from Ron Burkle for $113m (a $120m valuation), a league record at the time, two years after Burkle paid a ~$2m expansion fee.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity she was a securities lawyer, including in the Enforcement Division of the U.S. SEC. She holds a J.D. from Southwestern University School of Law and an LL.M. from Columbia Law School.
notes: main@LLCP.com is LLCP's Beverly Hills HQ general inbox. LLCP was named to Inc.'s 2024 Founder-Friendly Investors list, a natural hook for an entrepreneurship podcast. The Wave FC ownership is held through the Levine Leichtman family office.

name: Vitali Machitski
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Vimetco NV, owner of 84% of Romanian aluminium smelter Alro Slatina; developer of Moscow's Rostec-City complex
profile: Russian businessman who traded timber and oil in the 1990s, sold refinery assets to Yukos and others in the early 2000s, and took control of Romania's privatised Alro aluminium smelter in 2002 via Marco Industries, later Vimetco. Vimetco also held stakes in China's Zhongfu Industrial. His companies developed the Rostec-City business complex in Moscow.
interesting_fact: Alro, his main asset, is Romania's single largest electricity consumer, using about 8% of national power. In 2007 it was the largest primary aluminium producer in Central and Eastern Europe outside the CIS.
notes: Very private, with no published personal contacts. Forbes notes he is a friend of Rostec head Sergey Chemezov, so check sanctions exposure before any outreach. Alive status was not confirmed independently but he is on the 2026 Forbes real-time list. Energy angle: aluminium smelting and power intensity.

name: David Chen
current_role: Chief Product Officer, Shopee (Sea Ltd, NYSE: SE); Sea co-founder
profile: David Chen (45, Singapore; BSc, National University of Singapore) co-founded Sea in 2009 with Forrest Li and Gang Ye. Sea is the Singapore group behind Garena's hit mobile game Free Fire, e-commerce platform Shopee and the digital-finance arm Monee. He was previously Sea's COO and chief of staff and now runs product for Shopee.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Sea, Chen trained as a computer engineer and worked at PSA Corp, the Temasek-owned Singapore port operator.
notes: Low profile compared with Forrest Li. Forbes marks him as 'former' on the real-time list, so his net worth is near the $1bn threshold. Common name: make sure outreach targets the Sea/Shopee co-founder. Web-search quota ran out before deeper research.

name: Herriot Tabuteau
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Axsome Therapeutics (NASDAQ: AXSM), New York
profile: Herriot Tabuteau is a Haitian-born, Yale-trained physician who worked in healthcare investing, including as a partner at Healthco/S.A.C. Capital. He founded Axsome Therapeutics in 2012 to develop treatments for brain disorders and took it public in 2015; he owns about 15%. Axsome sells the depression drug Auvelity and the migraine drug Symbravo, and is advancing AXS-05 for Alzheimer's agitation. He is named inventor on more than 200 patents.
interesting_fact: He is named as inventor on more than 200 patents, covering potential medicines for depression, Alzheimer's agitation and narcolepsy. Forbes includes him among the world's Black billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: He emigrated from Haiti at nine, grew up on Manhattan's Upper East Side near Rockefeller University, and attended Xavier High School, a Jesuit school. He calls himself 'forever grateful to New York City's Catholic school system', credits his mother for his love of Motown, and names Citymeals and Success Academy as favorite charities.
notes: Business Insider has called him an 'elusive doctor'; he gives few interviews. His personal site has a contact page and a 'Call for Grants' section, which may be the best direct route. Avoid the S.A.C. Capital association.

name: Joe Kiani
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Willow Laboratories (Irvine, CA); CEO of Like Minded Labs (since July 2025)
profile: Iranian-born engineer (b. 1964, Shiraz) who founded Masimo in 1989 and, with Mohammed Diab, invented pulse oximetry that reads through motion and low perfusion, making Masimo the hospital leader. He left Masimo in Sept 2024 after a proxy fight (Danaher agreed to buy Masimo in Feb 2026) and now runs diabetes/metabolic-health startup Willow Labs and media-tech firm Like Minded Labs. He served on Biden's PCAST.
interesting_fact: He finished high school at 15 after arriving from Iran at nine speaking almost no English, and earned BS and MS degrees in electrical engineering from San Diego State by 22; he holds 500+ patents and patent applications.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988, while consulting for Newport Medical Electronics on a low-cost pulse oximeter, he discovered the motion-artifact problem and pitched a fix; when they declined, he returned all the pay they had given him in exchange for a release, then founded Masimo. His first engineering job was a 1984 co-op at Burroughs in Rancho Bernardo.

public_contacts.value: https://medium.com/@JoeKiani (Medium blog linked from his site)

notes: Founded the Patient Safety Movement Foundation (goal: zero preventable hospital deaths). Avoid Masimo proxy fight/litigation topics. joekiani.com looks like a personal/reputation site (also links Threads @joe.kiani) – treat as semi-official. Willow Labs general email is the best published route.

name: Li Zhigang
current_role: Chairman, Wuhan DR Laser Technology (帝尔激光, SZSE:300776)
profile: Founder-chairman of Wuhan DR Laser, a maker of laser processing equipment for solar cells (e.g. PERC/TOPCon/BC laser doping and grooving) that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2019. Customers include LONGi, Trina Solar, Tongwei and Canadian Solar.
interesting_fact: DR Laser's laser equipment is used by leading Chinese solar cell and panel makers including LONGi, Canadian Solar, Tongwei and Trina Solar.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (solar manufacturing equipment). dr@ is the company's general mailbox. The company works closely with Huazhong University of Science and Technology (site news, Feb 2026). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jassim Al-Kharafi
current_role: Deceased (died 21 May 2015)
profile: Kuwaiti businessman and politician (1940-2015) from the family behind the M.A. Kharafi & Sons conglomerate. He served five terms as Speaker of Kuwait's National Assembly (1999-2011, briefly again in 2012). He died on 21 May 2015.
interesting_fact: He served as Speaker for five terms, the most in Kuwait's history.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jassem_Al-Kharafi). The family wealth sits with the M.A. Kharafi & Sons group.

name: Li Baoyuan
current_role: Honorary Chairman and non-executive Director, Hebei Construction Group (HKEX: 1727); chairman, Hebei Baocang Expressway; GM, Qianbao Investment
profile: Li Baoyuan (李宝元) has spent over 50 years at Hebei Construction Group, a Baoding-based general contractor descended from 1950s state construction units. He rose from trainee to lead it, took it public in Hong Kong, and controls it through Qianbao Investment. He is now honorary chairman, chairs the Baoding-Cangzhou expressway company and leads the SME Committee of the China Construction Industry Association.
interesting_fact: Hebei Construction Group traces its roots to two central-ministry construction companies founded in 1952-53 (Ministry of Light Industry's Northeast Engineering Co. and the Textile Ministry's North China construction company).
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1970 as a trainee and budget planner at No. 1 Construction Engineering Company of Hebei Province. He worked his way up through the site teams, heading 'Team 2 of Division I' and then the '101 Engineering Team', before running the whole group.

public_contacts.value: hebjs.hk@pordahavas.com (Porda Havas International Finance Communications, media enquiries for Hebei Construction)

notes: Aged about 71+ and semi-retired (honorary chairman); his brother Li Baozhong is executive chairman. Chinese-language outreach is best. Moderate fit through construction and infrastructure.

name: Urs Schwarzenbach
current_role: Swiss financier and art collector; founder of Interexchange and owner of The Dolder Grand hotel, Zurich
profile: Urs Schwarzenbach (b. 1948, Thalwil) built Interexchange into Switzerland's largest foreign-exchange dealership and used the proceeds to amass property in the UK (including the Culham Court estate near Henley), Australian farmland and Zurich's Grand Hotel Dolder. Long a Berkshire resident, he has moved back to Küsnacht on Lake Zurich.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he outbid other foreign buyers to buy Culham Court, a 650-acre Thames-side estate, for £35m, then launched a 20-year garden plan including a maze of 20,000 mature yews.
deep_cut_fact: Despite the famous surname, he grew up in a modest working-class family as the son of a Thalwil print-shop owner, Ernst Schwarzenbach, and is only very distantly related to the Schwarzenbach silk-manufacturing dynasty.
notes: Sensitive: Swiss courts fined him CHF 6m over undeclared art imports and in 2022 the Federal Supreme Court ordered ~CHF 160m in back taxes (per Wikipedia). Very private; no published personal or office contact found. Any approach would likely go via The Dolder Grand's management.

name: Kim Sang-beom
current_role: Chairman, ISU Group (ISU Chemical, ISU Petasys, ISU Specialty Chemical), South Korea
profile: Chairman of ISU Group since 2000, succeeding his late father Kim Joon-sung (founder of Daegu Bank, ex-chairman of Samsung Electronics and Daewoo). He became a billionaire in 2025 as AI demand sent shares of ISU Petasys - a Daegu maker of high-layer printed circuit boards for AI servers and 800G switches used by Nvidia, Alphabet, Microsoft and Cisco - up more than 200%; he holds ~17% directly and indirectly.
interesting_fact: ISU Petasys's most advanced product is 40+-layer multilayer boards for AI network switches; JPMorgan analysts forecast that mix rising from 22% of networking sales in 2025 to 43% in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the family group he was a New York lawyer at Debevoise & Plimpton; he holds a JD and an MBA from the University of Michigan and a business degree from Seoul National University.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts found. Route would be via ISU Group / ISU Petasys corporate communications (Korean company sites not reachable from this environment, so no published email verified). Strong data-center/AI-hardware angle (PCBs for AI servers).

name: Wang Xinyang
current_role: Chairman, Gpixel Changchun Microelectronics (长光辰芯, HKEX: 3277)
profile: Wang Xinyang (王欣洋) chairs Gpixel, a Changchun-based fabless maker of high-performance CMOS image sensors for machine vision, scientific, medical and professional imaging, founded in 2012 with subsidiaries in Antwerp and Tokyo. Gpixel listed on the Hong Kong main board on 17 April 2026 (HK$39.88 offer price), which made him a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list.
interesting_fact: Gpixel's very first product, the GMAX3005, was at launch the world's highest-resolution CMOS image sensor (150 megapixels), and it later built the first back-illuminated scientific CMOS sensor, the GSENSE400BSI.

public_contacts.value: info@gpixel.com (general/media contact; media inquiry form on site)

notes: Forbes profile now 404s (dropped off list). Personal bio details not verified from a public source; web-search budget ran out during this lane. Gpixel Europe (Antwerp) handles English-language inquiries: info@gpixel.eu.

name: Cao Kanyu
current_role: Director and President (CEO since April 2023), CXMT Corporation / ChangXin Memory Technologies, Hefei
profile: PhD-trained chip engineer (born 1971) who worked at Philips Semiconductors in the U.S., founded two Beijing chip startups, then ran a NAND flash unit before joining CXMT in 2017. Rose through R&D to CEO/President of CXMT, China's leading DRAM maker and world No.4 by share, which raised about $8.6B in its July 2026 Shanghai STAR Market IPO.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 he publicly unveiled CXMT's progress on a 4F2 DRAM cell architecture at China's Integrated Chips and Chiplets conference, with next-gen DDR5 RDIMM products targeted for year-end.
deep_cut_fact: Before CXMT he was a serial founder: between 2005 and 2013 he set up Beijing Kuntian Kewei Microelectronics and Beijing Fandaxun Technology, then was GM of the NAND flash division at NoVoMem Inc. (2013-17), per CXMT's IPO prospectus.
notes: Chinese state-linked strategic chip company; executives rarely give Western media interviews. Route via board office / IR (board secretary Yuan Yuan). Company is subject to U.S. export-control scrutiny.

name: Daniel Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder, Co-CEO and Director, IREN Ltd (Nasdaq: IREN)
profile: Sydney-based co-founder, with brother Will, of IREN (formerly Iris Energy, founded 2018), which began as a renewable-powered bitcoin miner and now builds AI/HPC data centers, including a 2GW campus in Sweetwater, Texas. IREN signed a five-year, ~$9.7bn AI cloud contract with Microsoft in 2025. Before IREN, Daniel helped grow Palisade Investment Partners in infrastructure.
interesting_fact: The brothers deliberately sought 'stranded' renewable power: their first site was a data center beside a shut pulp mill in Canal Flats, British Columbia, using surplus hydro and rehiring local mill workers.
deep_cut_fact: Daniel first bought bitcoin in 2013 at about US$1,000 and sold at US$500 ('What nonsense is this?'), then joined the Ethereum presale. Scouting sites for Iris Energy, the brothers backpacked through Europe, Iceland and the US, and still laugh about a scuzzy windowless New York hostel.
notes: Wealth shared with brother/co-CEO William Roberts. Forbes AU says Daniel was co-owner of Palisade Investment Partners (helped grow it to ~$6bn infrastructure AUM) while Will was a Macquarie VP, slightly contradicting the Forbes profile that both worked at Macquarie. Highly relevant to energy/data-center podcast.

name: William Roberts
current_role: Co-Founder & Co-CEO, IREN Ltd (Nasdaq: IREN), Sydney
profile: Will Roberts and his older brother Daniel co-founded Iris Energy (renamed IREN in 2024), which listed on Nasdaq in November 2021 as a renewable-powered bitcoin miner and has pivoted to AI cloud/HPC data centers. IREN is building a 2GW, 1,800-acre campus in Sweetwater, Texas, and in 2025 signed a five-year, $9.7B AI cloud contract with Microsoft. Before IREN, Will was a vice president at Macquarie Group, where he co-founded its digital assets team.
interesting_fact: The brothers deliberately named the company Iris Energy rather than something like 'Iris Data' - they measure compute in gigawatts, not gigabytes - and IREN's sites span Texas, Oklahoma and British Columbia.
deep_cut_fact: Will and Daniel first bought bitcoin in 2013 at around US$1,000, sold at US$500 after it crashed ('What nonsense is this?'), then got into the Ethereum presale for next to nothing - years before founding Iris Energy.
notes: Shares Forbes profile with brother Daniel (the more public-facing co-CEO). Ideal podcast fit (bitcoin-to-AI-data-center pivot, 2GW Texas campus, Microsoft deal). Best route: IREN media@iren.com. Avoid referencing Daniel's 2023 health scare mentioned in Forbes AU.

name: Tang Jie
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist, Zhipu AI (Z.ai); Professor of Computer Science, Tsinghua University
profile: Tang Jie (唐杰) is a Tsinghua professor and an ACM, AAAI and IEEE Fellow. He co-founded Zhipu AI in 2019 out of his Knowledge Engineering Group and, as chief scientist, leads its GLM/ChatGLM large-language-model family. Zhipu went public in Hong Kong in January 2026, which made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: He invented AMiner.org, an academic search and social-network mining system he has built since 2006, which grew to over 30 million users in 220 countries and regions. It became Zhipu's technical foundation.
deep_cut_fact: As a grad student he interned in Microsoft Research Asia's NLC group (2004-05) and at IBM China Research Lab (2004). He was later a visiting scholar at Cornell with John Hopcroft and Jon Kleinberg. His research won the SIGKDD Test-of-Time (ten-year best paper) award.
notes: He is an accessible academic who publishes his own email and gives many keynotes in English. Forbes estimates of his net worth vary widely with Zhipu's share price. For data-center/AI topics, frame the pitch around open models (GLM) and AGI.

name: Yan Junjie
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, MiniMax Group (HKEX-listed Chinese foundation-model/AI company, Shanghai)
profile: Born 1989 in Xiayi County, Henan, Yan earned a PhD at the CAS Institute of Automation, did a Tsinghua postdoc in deep learning, then rose from intern (2015) to vice president at SenseTime. He left in 2021 to found MiniMax (LLMs, Hailuo video, Talkie, speech/music models); its January 2026 Hong Kong IPO made him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: In January 2026 he joined a symposium hosted by Premier Li Qiang, only the second founder of a Chinese foundation-model developer (after DeepSeek's Liang Wenfeng) to attend such a meeting.
deep_cut_fact: A devoted Dota 2 player, he goes by the alias 'IO' (a pun on input/output and the Dota wisp hero); watching OpenAI's bots beat top Dota players in 2019 pushed him from computer vision toward language models. As a PhD student he said his goal was to be a Java developer at IBM.
notes: MiniMax name comes from the minimax algorithm. Gave a Bloomberg Q&A in Jan 2026 (https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-01-08/minimax-founder-was-once-dismissed-as-a-fraud-by-big-tech-q-a), so open to English-language press. Gaming link: knows miHoYo CEO Cai Haoyu, an early backer.

name: Oleg Misevra
current_role: Controlling owner and chairman, East Mining Company (VGK / Vostochnaya Gornorudnaya Kompaniya), Sakhalin, Russia
profile: Former USSR/Russian Internal Troops officer who became a top manager and minority partner at MDM Group and president of SUEK (2002-04). In 2004 he bought SUEK's Sakhalin assets, building East Mining Company around the Solntsevsky open-pit coal mine and Shakhtersk port, now one of Russia's fastest-growing thermal coal exporters to Asia.
interesting_fact: He was named Russia's 'Exporter of the Year' in 2019 in the All-Russian People-2019 competition, as VGK ramped Sakhalin coal exports and expanded its Shakhtersk port.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 interview he explained that VGK was then Russia's only exporter of brown (lignite) coal, so its real competitor is Indonesia rather than Australia, and that the business is fully self-contained: 'We have everything of our own: the mine, the port, the conveyor line.'

public_contacts.value: https://www.eastmining.ru/en/ (East Mining Company; was unreachable from our network when checked)

notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or press contacts found. Russian coal exporter: sanctions/compliance considerations for any outreach. Interviews exist only in Russian regional/business media (EastRussia, PortNews).

name: Ji Wei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Wasion Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 3393), Changsha
profile: Ji Wei founded Wasion in Changsha in 2000 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2005 - the first Chinese energy-metering company listed overseas and Hunan's first overseas main-board listing. Wasion makes smart electricity/water/gas/heat meters, distribution equipment and energy-efficiency systems, with subsidiaries in Mexico, Brazil, Tanzania and Hungary; its unit Willfar listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
interesting_fact: Wasion was the first professional energy-metering and energy-efficiency group from China to list overseas (HKEX, Dec 2005), and has since won large smart-meter contracts in emerging markets across Latin America, Africa and Europe.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an energy-tech founder he was a trader: business manager at Hunan Province Minerals Import & Export Co. (1980-85) and import-export manager at Hunan International Economic Development Group (1985-89). He has received the 'Top Ten Educational Entrepreneur' award and the Chinese Red Cross Dedication Medal.
notes: The listed email is the shareholder-enquiry address for the attention of the Company Secretary (spelled 'enquires@' in the 2023 annual report). Wasion IR site: http://website.wasionholdings.wisdomir.com/. Ji is ~69; low international media profile.

name: Hitesh Doshi
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Waaree Energies Ltd (NSE: WAAREEENER); head of the Waaree Group, Mumbai
profile: Founder of the Waaree Group, which began in 1990 making thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers and moved into solar modules in 2007 with a 30 MW plant in Surat. Waaree Energies is now India's largest solar-panel maker by capacity and listed in Mumbai in October 2024 at a 70% premium. He is expanding into cells, US manufacturing and other clean-energy businesses.
interesting_fact: On listing day in October 2024, Waaree shares jumped about 56% after a $514M IPO, roughly doubling the Doshi family's fortune to about $5.2B, according to Bloomberg as reported by Fortune.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Tunki, a village in Maharashtra, Doshi moved about 600 km to attend Shri Chinai College of Commerce and Economics in Mumbai in 1985. He borrowed Rs 5,000 (about $60) from a relative to trade hardware, electronics and instrument gauges, which paid his college fees (he told the Economic Times in 2014).
notes: waaree@waaree.com is the company's general/customer-service inbox, not a personal or press address; no dedicated press or IR email was confirmed (the web-search budget ran out). The X account is the company's (@waareegroup). Strong fit for an energy podcast.

name: Zhu Shunquan
current_role: Director and General Manager, Hubei Dinglong Co. (鼎龙股份, SZSE: 300054), Wuhan; also director of Wuhan Zhongyuan Huadian since Dec 2025
profile: Co-founder (in 2000, with his elder brother, chairman Zhu Shuangquan) and co-controlling shareholder of Hubei Dinglong, which grew from printer-toner chemicals and consumables into one of China's leading semiconductor-materials makers: CMP polishing pads and slurries, wafer photoresists, display materials and advanced-packaging materials.
interesting_fact: Dinglong entered CMP polishing pads in 2012, a market long dominated by Dow and Cabot, and says it is now China's only supplier with full-process, self-controlled pad technology (including its own prepolymers and microspheres); CMP pad sales grew 52% to RMB 795M in 9M 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His motto for chips materials, from a Feb 2026 Securities Times interview: 'There is no overtaking on the curve in semiconductor materials - slowest is fastest' (慢就是快). Before Dinglong he was a department manager at China Hubei International Economic & Technical Cooperation Co. (1997-2000); he is a member of Hubei's 13th CPPCC.
notes: Career details (CPPCC, prior job) from company executive bio at https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/300054/company.html. Board secretary: Yang Pingcai. Gives occasional interviews to Chinese financial press (Securities Times).

name: Pankaj Doshi
current_role: Promoter-shareholder, Waaree Energies Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Pankaj Doshi is one of four Doshi brothers whose family controls Waaree Energies, India's largest solar-module maker by capacity. Waaree's October 2024 listing, which debuted ~70% above its IPO price, made him and his three brothers billionaires. He holds a minority stake; the company is run day-to-day by his brother Hitesh Doshi (chairman & MD).
interesting_fact: Waaree started in 1990 not in solar but as a maker of thermal and pressure gauges for industrial boilers before pivoting to become India's largest solar-panel manufacturer.
notes: Low public profile; not on Waaree Energies' board per company site. Brother Hitesh Doshi is the public face of Waaree, so outreach likely goes through the company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no deep-cut fact found.

name: Liu Shiqi
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hubei Wanrun New Energy Technology Co. (688275.SH)
profile: Liu Shiqi controls Hubei Wanrun New Energy, founded in December 2010 in Shiyan, Hubei. The company makes lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode materials and precursors for EV and energy-storage batteries. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in September 2022, and Liu still runs it as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Liu personally chairs Wanrun's board-level Sustainability Committee. The company has joined the CDP carbon-disclosure programme two years running, scoring B-, and is developing technology to recover lithium carbonate and iron phosphate from waste.
deep_cut_fact: Wanrun funds the 'Wanrun Class' (万润班) at Yunyang High School in Shiyan, the company's hometown: 40 students a year from low-income families get study and living stipends through all three years of high school.
notes: The input's SEC insider link (UMC Vice President) is a different person and does not match. Low public profile, with little personal biography online. The email is Wanrun's general ESG/company contact from its 2024 ESG report; outreach in Chinese is advisable.

name: Li Fei
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder and director (per 2024 filings), Hubei Wanrun New Energy Technology (SSE STAR: 688275)
profile: Li Fei (李菲) and her husband, chairman Liu Shiqi, founded and jointly control Hubei Wanrun New Energy, a top-three global lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode maker based in Shiyan, Hubei. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022, it supplies LFP for EV and energy-storage batteries.
interesting_fact: Wanrun grew revenue at a 324% CAGR from 2020 to 2022, reaching RMB 12.35bn in 2022, as LFP displaced other EV battery chemistries and lithium carbonate prices spiked.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wanrun, Li Fei worked at Dongfeng Motor and Shenzhen Zhonghuang Industrial; the founders' first firm, Wanrun Gongmao (2003), made iron-phosphate cathode precursors and got into the supply chain of US battery pioneer A123 before Wanrun New Energy was set up in 2010.
notes: Low public profile; husband Liu Shiqi is chairman and public face (re-elected chairman Dec 2025). Board secretary is Gao Wenjing. Unconfirmed whether Li Fei remained a director after the Dec 2025 board re-election. Best route: board office email.

name: David Humphreys
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, TAMKO Building Products (Joplin/Galena area, Missouri-Kansas)
profile: Grandson of TAMKO founder E.L. Craig, David C. Humphreys took over the roofing-shingle maker in 1994 after his father J.P. Humphreys died, expanding production; TAMKO is now the fourth-largest US shingle maker (~$1.2bn revenue in 2023). The family sold a 25% stake to Carlyle in 2019 and he and his sister's families own the rest.
interesting_fact: His grandfather E.L. Craig founded TAMKO in 1944 at age 69 in an old Joplin streetcar barn, after earlier ventures including a sausage business, a soup kitchen, a boxing gym and a frozen-custard shop; TAMKO's name comes from Texas, Arkansas, Missouri, Kansas and Oklahoma.
deep_cut_fact: TAMKO has run on W. Edwards Deming's continuous-improvement principles since his father saw a June 24, 1980 TV special introducing Deming's quality methods; and for a decade TAMKO has donated its company planes and fuel for veterans' 'Hero Flights'. Humphreys is also a rare-books and history enthusiast.
notes: Prominent Missouri political donor (libertarian-leaning; Forbes notes he has criticised Donald Trump) - politically sensitive, keep outreach business-focused. His mother Ethelmae Humphreys, TAMKO chairman emerita, died at 94. Media route: TAMKO communications team.

name: Sarah Humphreys Atkins
current_role: President, J.P. Humphreys Foundation; director, TAMKO Building Products; board member, Moving Picture Institute; trustee, Capital Research Center
profile: Heiress to the TAMKO roofing fortune and only granddaughter of founder E.L. Craig. TAMKO is the fourth-largest US shingle maker, with about $1.2bn in revenue in 2023. Carlyle bought 25% in 2019, and she and her brother David (CEO) split the rest with their families. She sits on TAMKO's board with her husband Paul Atkins, chairman of the SEC, and leads the family's J.P. Humphreys Foundation.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather E.L. Craig founded TAMKO in 1944 at the age of 69, in an old streetcar barn in Joplin, Missouri.
deep_cut_fact: She is a long-time builder of free-market nonprofits. She has served on the boards of the Foundation for Economic Education, Free to Choose Network, Atlas Network and The Future of Freedom Foundation, and now sits on the board of the Moving Picture Institute, which backs liberty-themed films.
notes: Very private, with no personal social media found. Her husband is the sitting SEC chairman, so expect sensitivity around any outreach that touches on markets or regulation. The TAMKO communications office is the company's media contact, not hers personally. The nonprofit boards (Capital Research Center, Moving Picture Institute) are an alternative route.

name: Tsao Ter-fung
current_role: Chairman, Standard Foods Corporation (佳格食品, Taiwan), as representative of Mu Te Investment; board term 2025-2028
profile: A food-engineering PhD, Tsao rose to R&D director at Quaker Oats in the US and returned to Taiwan in 1981 to run Quaker's local unit. When Quaker pulled out, he bought its Taiwan assets in 1986 and founded Standard Foods, a major maker of oats, oils and nutrition products. His son Arthur Tsao became CEO in 2019.
interesting_fact: Besides food, he holds tech-industry board seats: chairman of Domex Technology and Maven Optronics, a director role at Polytronics Technology, independent director at PlexBio and supervisor at Crosslink Semiconductor.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing his food-engineering PhD in 1974 he applied to more than 40 US jobs and Quaker was the only company to make him an offer. He went on to become the first and only Quaker employee to win the company's President's Award three times.
notes: spokesperson1@ is the official spokesperson inbox, held by CEO Arthur Tsao. The company site names his PhD school as Colorado State University on the founder page but University of Colorado on the board page. His tech holdings (optronics, semiconductors) could be a podcast hook.

name: Colette Kress
current_role: Interim CEO (since 12 Nov 2026) and EVP & Chief Financial Officer, NVIDIA.
profile: Kress joined Nvidia as CFO in 2013 after ~25 years in tech finance (Texas Instruments, 13 years at Microsoft, CFO of a Cisco division). She steered its finances as sales rose from $4.3bn to $215.9bn and it became the first $5tn company. On 12 Nov 2026 she was named interim CEO after Jensen Huang resigned, while remaining CFO.
interesting_fact: She joined Nvidia partly at the urging of her two young sons, avid gamers who knew the company from the chips in their favourite video games.
deep_cut_fact: Jensen Huang interviewed 22 candidates before hiring her; in her first week she asked how long he'd want her in the role and he answered, 'For as long as we shall live and death do us part.' She holds a finance B.Sc. from the University of Arizona and an MBA from SMU.
notes: Very timely: just became interim CEO amid Huang's sudden 12 Nov 2026 resignation (personal-conduct reports) - avoid that topic; expect heavy media demand. Best route is Nvidia corporate PR (press@nvidia.com). Q3 FY27 earnings 17 Nov 2026.

name: Lidiya Mikhailova
current_role: Co-owner (about 15%) of Cherkizovo Group, Russia's largest meat producer; her sons Evgeny (chairman) and Sergei (CEO) run it
profile: Ex-wife of Cherkizovo founder Igor Babaev. He built the Moscow Cherkizovsky meat plant into Cherkizovo Group, which listed in London and Moscow in 2006, and later passed his shares to their sons. She holds about 15% alongside sons Evgeny and Sergei Mikhailov (about 28% each). The group has over 20,000 employees and about $3.4bn in 2025 revenue.
interesting_fact: Cherkizovo became a major poultry and pork producer through acquisitions; after buying LISKO Broiler in 2014 its poultry capacity reached about 550,000 tonnes a year. It trades on the Moscow Exchange as GCHE.
notes: Passive shareholder with no public profile; Forbes lists her as 'former' (2024). The company site blocked automated access, so no IR contact was captured. Russian-sanctions context applies, and this is not a useful podcast guest.

name: Gerald Engström
current_role: Founder and major shareholder, Systemair (Nasdaq Stockholm: SYSR); chairman until 2025; private investor
profile: Gerald Engström founded Swedish ventilation maker Systemair in 1974 and was CEO until 2015, then chairman until 2025. Systemair now has about 90 companies in 51 countries and roughly 6,700 employees, and listed in October 2007. He also holds a portfolio of listed stocks worth over $1bn and owns businesses such as fashion retailer Indiska and RVM Systems.
interesting_fact: Systemair is increasingly a data-centre supplier. In August 2026 it won a SEK 60m order for Geniox Tera Fanwall cooling units for a new Finnish data centre whose waste heat will feed the local district-heating network.
deep_cut_fact: Systemair's very first product was an inline duct fan with circular connections that installs directly into the duct system, greatly simplifying installation. The company is still headquartered in the small Bergslagen town of Skinnskatteberg, where it is the largest employer and exports about 70% of the factory's output.
notes: A strong podcast fit (data-centre cooling, heat recovery, energy efficiency). Systemair's press releases list CEO Robert Larsson and CFO Anders Ulff as contacts, but their emails are obfuscated, so none are listed here. Engström's own investment company may be a better route than Systemair.

name: Bastian Nominacher
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, Celonis (Munich/New York)
profile: Bastian Nominacher co-founded Celonis in 2011 with Alexander Rinke and Martin Klenk, straight out of the Technical University of Munich. Celonis makes process-mining software that analyses companies' system data to find inefficiencies and is now pitched as a 'process intelligence' layer for enterprise AI. It was valued at $13bn in 2022, and Nominacher, co-CEO alongside Rinke, owns about 16%.
interesting_fact: Celonis reached a $1bn valuation in 2018 and $11bn in 2021, making it then Germany's and New York's most valuable startup. It was SAP's process-mining reseller partner from 2015.
deep_cut_fact: Celonis grew out of a student consulting gig. As members of Academy Consult, Munich's largest student consultancy, the three founders analysed internal IT service processes for broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk, the work that became the first Celonis product.
notes: Rinke is the more public face; Nominacher focuses on operations and finance. The Celonis newsroom lists only a general info@ address. A good AI-and-operations angle.

name: Xu Yuejuan
current_role: Supervisor, Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group (Hangzhou)
profile: Hangzhou-based shareholder and supervisor of Zhejiang Rongsheng Holding Group, the private parent of Shenzhen-listed Rongsheng Petrochemical (002493), one of China's largest refining, petrochemical and polyester-fibre groups. She is the sister-in-law of Rongsheng chairman and cofounder Li Shuirong; Forbes lists her wealth source as petro fibre.
interesting_fact: She has appeared on Forbes' billionaire rankings for years as one of the family shareholders behind Rongsheng, which grew from a 1989 Xiaoshan textile mill into a refining-to-polyester giant.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Only route is via Rongsheng Petrochemical's board secretary/IR (tel 0571-82520189 per 2025 annual report summary).

name: Ken Kendrick
current_role: Managing General Partner and principal owner, Arizona Diamondbacks (MLB)
profile: Born 1943 in Princeton, West Virginia, Kendrick started at IBM, then founded higher-education software maker Datatel (merged with SunGard Higher Education into Ellucian, sold to TPG for $3.5bn in 2015) and became principal investor in Texas-based Woodforest National Bank in 1989. A Diamondbacks owner since the 1995 expansion, he has run the club since 2004, including its 2023 World Series run.
interesting_fact: A lifelong collector, he owns the T206 Honus Wagner card once owned by Wayne Gretzky; it and other cards from his 'D-backs Collection' were displayed at the Baseball Hall of Fame, on whose board he has sat since 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He owns Bumble Bee Ranch in Arizona, which hosts western-lifestyle experiences for children's charities, as well as the Ironbridge Golf Club in Glenwood Springs, Colorado.
notes: Best route is the Diamondbacks communications office via the team's official contact page (no media email published there). Also chairs the Arizona Diamondbacks Foundation. Tech angle: founded Datatel/Ellucian; he was personally part of the 2021 investor group that bought Collectors (PSA).

name: Blair Hull
current_role: Founder, Hull Investments (family office) and Hull Tactical Asset Allocation, Chicago
profile: Former blackjack card counter turned options market maker who founded Chicago's Hull Trading Company in 1985, a pioneer of computer-driven trading, and sold it to Goldman Sachs in 1999 for $531m. Since then he has run his family office Hull Investments and quant ETF adviser Hull Tactical, and is a Democratic donor.
interesting_fact: In the 1970s he was one of the 'Big Players' on Al Francesco's blackjack card-counting team (chronicled in Ken Uston's 'The Big Player') and was inducted into the Blackjack Hall of Fame in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before trading he worked on a cannery line and taught high-school math and physics; after leaving blackjack with $25,000 he leased a seat on the Pacific Stock Exchange and built his own options-pricing model without knowing about Black-Scholes.
notes: Aged 84. Hull Investments mailbox is his family office. Avoid the 2004 Senate race divorce-records issue.

name: Tseng Sing-ai
current_role: Shareholder (inherited stake), Chang Chun Group, Taiwan; no public executive role found
profile: Taipei-based heiress who inherited her stake in Chang Chun Group from her father Tseng Shin-yi (d. 2016), who cofounded the company in 1949 with classmates M.K. Liao and Lin Shu-hong. Chang Chun is one of Asia's largest petrochemicals-and-plastics makers, with plants in Taiwan, mainland China and Southeast Asia. Forbes previously listed her jointly with her brother Tseng Cheng.
interesting_fact: Chang Chun Group was founded in 1949 by three classmates, including her father Tseng Shin-yi, and remains privately controlled by the three founding families (Liao, Lin, Tseng).
notes: Very private; no public profile, interviews or official accounts found. Any approach would have to go through Chang Chun Group corporate (ccp.com.tw, site blocked automated access). Forbes listed her jointly with sibling Tseng Cheng until recent years.

name: Zhou Wei family
current_role: Chairman, Winning Health Technology Group (卫宁健康, SZ:300253) as of Forbes' April 2021 profile; current status unverified
profile: Self-made Shanghai software entrepreneur who chairs Winning Health Technology Group, a supplier of IT systems to Chinese hospitals and health institutions (more than 6,000 clients). Demand for digital-health systems during COVID-19 pushed him onto the Forbes and Hurun billionaire lists in 2020-2021. He fell off them as the share price dropped.
interesting_fact: Winning Health's software supports more than 6,000 medical and health institutions in China, and the business got a boost from the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
notes: Forbes' profile was last updated April 2021, and he has not been on the lists since 2022. The search budget ran out and winning.com.cn was unreachable, so I could not confirm his current role. Check recent 300253 announcements before outreach. Healthcare IT is a weak fit for the podcast.

name: Henrik Fisker
current_role: Independent automotive designer and advisor (strategic advisory, board-level and special projects); founder of Fisker Inc. (Chapter 11 in June 2024)
profile: Danish-born car designer (b. 1963, ArtCenter Vevey 1989) who shaped the BMW Z8 and the Aston Martin DB9 and V8 Vantage, and did early design work on the Tesla Model S. He founded Fisker Automotive (Karma plug-in hybrid, 2011) and later Fisker Inc. (Ocean EV, SPAC listing in 2020), which filed for bankruptcy in 2024. He is no longer a billionaire and now takes selective design and brand advisory work.
interesting_fact: He styled the BMW Z8 roadster that James Bond drove in 'The World Is Not Enough'. The Fisker Karma, launched in 2011, was the first premium extended-range electric performance car to reach production.
deep_cut_fact: Besides road cars, he designed a race car for the Formula BMW open-wheel series. His own site says he is particularly interested in turning historic brand designs into iconic timepieces, along with motorsport heritage and F1.
notes: Very reachable: his site openly invites advisory and special-project contact. Avoid dwelling on the Fisker Inc. bankruptcy and the 2013 Fisker Automotive collapse. Design, EV and entrepreneurial-resilience angles suit the podcast. No longer on billionaire lists.

name: Wang Wenjian
current_role: Founder, honorary chairman and non-executive director, Sunny Optical Technology (Group) Co. (HKEX: 2382)
profile: Wang Wenjian (王文鉴, b. ~1947) founded what became Sunny Optical in Yuyao, Zhejiang, in 1984, serving as chairman and CEO before moving to non-executive director in 2012. Sunny is now a global leader in phone camera lenses and modules (1.32bn lenses shipped in 2024) and automotive/AR optics. His son Wang Tan Jiong became board chairman in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Sunny's largest shareholder is an employee trust (Sunny Group Overseas Employee Trust, ~35.5%) co-administered by Wang, a structure designed to avoid family control; the company pivoted to phone optics in 2000 when phones had no cameras of note.
deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he started the business as a small township optical-instrument factory in Yuyao with just eight high-school graduates and a RMB 60,000 loan; he has also been honorary president of the Yuyao Charity Federation (2003) and a guest professor at Zhejiang University (2005).
notes: Age ~78-79; low public profile. Board bio: https://www.irasia.com/listco/hk/sunnyoptical/onlinereport/2025/e_annual/47/ . Best route is Sunny IR office. Shares the Sunny fortune with co-founders such as Ye Liaoning (P07144).

name: Dasari Uday Kumar Reddy
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Tanla Platforms Ltd (Hyderabad)
profile: Uday Reddy founded Tanla in 1999 as an SMS-centre provider for telecom operators and listed it in 2006. Tanla is now a leading Indian CPaaS and enterprise-messaging company, with blockchain-based anti-spam (Trubloq) and anti-phishing (Wisely ATP) platforms. He first joined the Forbes billionaires list in 2022 after Tanla's shares more than doubled in 2021.
interesting_fact: The name 'Tanla' contains his wife's initials. He told LBS he has no family office and no passive investments, and reinvests everything in his own businesses.
deep_cut_fact: At 11 he sold sweets to his whole school. In the late 1980s he sold his only possession, his motorbike, to start a paging business in Hyderabad, camping outside a hardware maker's site in Singapore until he had mastered the technology. He charged per message rather than for hardware.
notes: Not the same person as YuppTV founder Uday Reddy; avoid YourStory or FPJ articles about that Uday Reddy. He did an MBA at Manchester Business School, where seeing UK text-messaging use inspired Tanla. Forbes also notes his first venture was real estate in 1993.

name: Huang Shih Tsai
current_role: Chairman, Great China International Group (大中华国际集团, Shenzhen); controller of HK-listed Great China Properties
profile: Huang Shih Tsai (黄世再), from Huilai, Guangdong, built Shenzhen-based Great China International Group, whose holdings include Shenzhen's Great China International Financial Center, a Hilton hotel and GC Square, plus interests in TV media, gold and jewellery trading and logistics. He revived the HK shell Bao Fu Group as Great China Properties; he dropped off Forbes' list after 2022.
interesting_fact: He is the eldest brother of Huang Mao Ru, chairman of department-store group Maoye, making them part of one of the best-known Chaoshan business families.
deep_cut_fact: He is an honorary citizen of Shantou and received the China Foundation for Poverty Alleviation's 2008 annual contribution award; he was also named one of Shenzhen's top ten real-estate contributors in 2009.
notes: Low international profile; Chinese-language outreach via Great China International Group corporate office would be the only route. Wikipedia notes he is also vice-chairman of the Macau-based satellite TV channel 中华卫视. Last on Forbes in 2022 (US$1.2bn).

name: Tang Zhuang
