current_role: Co-founder, Director, Deputy GM & CTO of Jiangsu Maxscend Microelectronics (SZSE: 300782); Chairman of Wuxi Xinzhuo Huguang Semiconductor
profile: Tang Zhuang (b. 1973) is a co-founder and CTO of Maxscend (卓胜微), a Wuxi-based maker of RF front-end chips (switches, LNAs, filters) for smartphones that listed in Shenzhen in 2019. He has led its shift from fabless to IDM via the 'Xinzhuo' fab project, with 6-inch SAW filter and 12-inch silicon-based lines now in volume production.
interesting_fact: Under his technical lead Maxscend built its own 6-inch SAW filter wafer line in just 14 months and by end-2024 had shipped over 100,000 6-inch and 20,000+ 12-inch wafers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied physics at Peking University and earned his MS/PhD in electrical engineering at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign; in his first-ever media interview (2025) he said of heterogeneous integration: 'we have waited for this opportunity for at least 10 years.'
notes: Input lists source as 'Guide Electrics', which does not match; the semiconductor billionaire Tang Zhuang on Forbes 2021/Hurun 2019-21 appears to be Maxscend's co-founder (Maxscend's founders made those lists), but the label mismatch is unresolved. Board secretary Liu Liqiong; IR mailbox info@maxscend.com.

name: Wu Daohong
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controlling shareholder, Shenwu Technology Group (神雾集团), Beijing; current role unclear
profile: Combustion engineer who did postdoctoral research at China University of Petroleum (1995) and founded Shenwu in 1996 to commercialise energy-saving industrial furnace and burner technology. Shenwu grew into a group with two listed arms (Shenwu Environmental, Shenwu Energy Saving) before a 2017-18 liquidity crisis.
interesting_fact: China Daily credits Wu with inventing a 'third-generation' combustion technology in 2001, behind Shenwu's high-efficiency regenerative burner, which it says cuts energy use by over 30% on average.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually hands-on for a billionaire, Wu is a named inventor on many Shenwu patents (e.g. CN104848220A on regenerative combustion devices for heating furnaces) and co-authored a 2015 Energy Procedia paper on double-preheating regenerative burners.
notes: Low priority and sensitive. The Shenwu group collapsed in a 2017-18 debt crisis (shares frozen, executives left). In Nov 2025 the Shenzhen Stock Exchange proposed a public reprimand of Shenwu Environmental and Wu over past violations (https://finance.eastmoney.com/news/1354,202511043554848524.html). Last on rich lists in 2018. No current public contact found.

name: Clayton Riddell
current_role: Deceased (died September 15, 2018, aged 81); was founder, president and CEO of Paramount Resources, Calgary
notes: Died Sept 15, 2018 (Globe and Mail obituary, Sept 25, 2018: https://www.theglobeandmail.com/business/article-clay-riddell-81-was-a-billionaire-and-philanthropist-who-thrived-in/ ; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clay_Riddell). Paramount Resources (Calgary) continues as a listed company if an energy-guest angle is wanted.

name: Daisy Igel
profile: Brazilian architect and heiress (born 1927), daughter of Ernesto Igel, who founded Ultragaz/Ultrapar. Reported to have died in 2019.
notes: Deceased. Wikipedia gives her death as 2019, citing a 2024 UNIFESP dissertation (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daisy_Igel). This fits her dropping off Forbes after 2018. I found no Brazilian obituary to confirm the exact date. Skipped.

name: Kenneth Adams, Jr.
profile: K.S. 'Bud' Adams Jr. (1923-2013), founder and chairman/CEO of Adams Resources & Energy and founding owner of the AFL's Houston Oilers (now NFL Tennessee Titans). Died October 21, 2013.
notes: Deceased 21 Oct 2013 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bud_Adams). Not a candidate for outreach; Titans now owned by his heirs.

name: Marguerite Harbert
profile: Died March 17, 2015 in Mountain Brook, Alabama, aged 91. She was Alabama's only billionaire, having inherited the fortune of her husband John M. Harbert III, founder of Harbert Corporation, in 1995.
notes: Deceased (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marguerite_Harbert ; Birmingham News obituary 'Marguerite Harbert, Alabama's only billionaire, dies at 91', al.com, March 19, 2015). Remove from outreach list. Her son Raymond J. Harbert runs Harbert Management Corp. if the family/firm is of interest.

name: Ural Rakhimov
current_role: No known current corporate role; former chairman of Bashneft (until 2009); reported to live in Austria
profile: Russian (Bashkir) businessman, b. 1961 in Ufa, son of ex-Bashkortostan president Murtaza Rakhimov. He headed the Bashkir oil complex (Bashneft and refineries), sold to AFK Sistema in 2005-2009. He left Russia after being charged in absentia in 2014; an Austrian court declined extradition in 2016.
interesting_fact: In March 2016 the Vienna Regional Criminal Court refused Russia's extradition request, citing political motives behind the case against him.
deep_cut_fact: A trained petroleum engineer: he graduated from Ufa State Petroleum Technological University in 1984, then earned an MSc at the French Petroleum Institute (IFP) and a second master's in the US; he briefly owned KHL hockey club Salavat Yulaev Ufa (2009-10).
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: wanted in Russia since 2014 on embezzlement/laundering charges (contested as political), living abroad (Austria) with no public presence or published contact. Alive status based on Wikipedia 'living people' and no death reports; not independently confirmed recently.

name: David Yakobashvili
current_role: President, Orion Heritage Co. (private Museum 'Collection', Moscow); founder of InOil (GreenBooster fuel additive)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1957) entrepreneur who cofounded Russian dairy-and-juice giant Wimm-Bill-Dann and chaired it 2001-2010; it sold to PepsiCo for ~$5.7B in 2010-11, netting him ~$600M for his ~10% stake. He later moved into energy: InOil's GreenBooster fuel additive, Bioenergy Corp, and African mineral trading.
interesting_fact: The 'Wimm-Bill-Dann' name was coined to sound like 'Wimbledon'; in 2002 the company became the first Russian food company to IPO on the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serious collector of self-playing musical instruments and automatons: his Moscow museum 'Collection' grew from his ~2000 purchase of Swedish collector Bill Lindwall's ~460 mechanical instruments and now holds over 20,000 items, including wax cylinders and perforated piano rolls.
notes: Holds Swedish citizenship per Wikipedia. Left RSPP board and AFK Sistema board in 2022. No personal press channel found; museum is the only organisation-published route. Energy angle: GreenBooster fuel additive and Bioenergy Corp.

name: Mokhzani Mahathir
current_role: President, Motorsports Association of Malaysia (MAM); owner of Kencana Capital Sdn Bhd
profile: Tan Sri Mokhzani Mahathir (b. 1961), son of ex-PM Mahathir, is a petroleum engineer who founded Kencana Petroleum. It merged with SapuraCrest in 2012 to form SapuraKencana (now Sapura Energy). He now invests via Kencana Capital and leads Malaysian motorsport as MAM president.
interesting_fact: He chaired Sepang International Circuit for over a decade. As MAM president he said in October 2026 that Sepang has the capability and experience to host Formula 1 again.
deep_cut_fact: He is a racer as well as an administrator. Driving a Porsche 911 GT3 RSR for Team Hong Leong-Kencana Racing with Sven Herberger and Lars Erik Nielsen, he won the 2007 Merdeka Millennium Endurance race (Sepang 12 Hours). He earned his engineering degree at the University of Tulsa.
notes: No published personal or office email found. The most likely official route is the Motorsports Association of Malaysia (mam.org.my; site is JS-rendered and no email could be extracted). He left all Opcom positions in 2019 and retired from politics (quit UMNO in 2008). Motorsport is the strongest rapport angle.

name: Zhou Wenyu
profile: Listed once (Forbes 2018) as a Chinese real-estate billionaire worth ~$1.2bn; no company, Chinese name or Forbes profile could be found to pin down which Zhou Wenyu this is.
notes: Ambiguous: no company or Chinese characters in source data and searches return no matching tycoon. Needs the company name (or Chinese name) before any outreach.

name: Yang Jianxin
current_role: Former chairman/actual controller of Global Top E-Commerce (KJT, 跨境通, SZSE 002640); executive director of Shanxi Baiyuan Trousers
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur who built Baiyuan Trousers (百圆裤业), a budget trousers retail chain listed in Shenzhen in 2011. In 2014 it bought Shenzhen cross-border e-tailer Huanqiu Yigou (Gearbest, Zaful) for RMB1bn and became KJT, briefly making Yang Shanxi's richest man. He sold control to a Guangzhou state fund in 2019; Huanqiu Yigou went into bankruptcy in 2021.
interesting_fact: The 2014 RMB1bn acquisition of Huanqiu Yigou turned a Taiyuan trousers retailer into one of China's first listed cross-border e-commerce players, and made Yang the richest person in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: Before cross-border e-commerce, his business was Baiyuan Trousers, a Shanxi chain of budget men's trousers stores, which he grew into a Shenzhen-listed company in 2011.
notes: Probably no longer a billionaire: 2025 Chinese media report he is under 5 court consumption-restriction orders (about RMB2.2bn enforced) and his shares are being judicially auctioned; he is also in a public dispute with Huanqiu Yigou founder Xu Jiadong. Not a good podcast target; no published personal contact found.

name: Chen Jianming
profile: Listed by Hurun (2007-2021) and Forbes (2018) as a property developer whose wealth comes from 'Guangda', shared with Chen Runguang. Several searches in English and Chinese (陈建铭 / 陈润广 / 光大) did not establish which 'Guangda' company this is; it is not the state-owned China Everbright (光大) Group.
notes: Identity not confirmed: Chen Jianming is a common name and Guangda (光大) is a common company name. Needs a lookup of the Hurun China Rich List entry (e.g. the 2019 list) to pin down the company and city before any outreach.

name: Jean-Charles Naouri
current_role: President of Euris SAS (holding company); former chairman-CEO of Groupe Casino until March 2024
profile: French financier who left the civil service in 1987 to found investment holding Euris, then bought Rallye (1991) and used a layered holding structure to control retailer Groupe Casino from 1992. CEO of Casino until a 2024 debt restructuring handed control to Daniel Kretinsky's consortium and wiped out most of his stake.
interesting_fact: As chief of staff to finance minister Pierre Bérégovoy (1982-86), he is credited with France's 1984-86 financial-market reforms, including creation of the MATIF futures market and MONEP options market.
deep_cut_fact: He won first prize in Latin and Greek at the Concours général aged 14, got his baccalauréat at 15, and placed first in the 1967 École normale supérieure entrance exam; he is honorary president of the Institut de l'ENS.
notes: Lost control of Casino in March 2024 (https://esmmagazine.com/retail/french-retailer-casino-changes-leadership-team-as-boss-naouris-era-ends-262309). French Wikipedia reports a Jan 2026 Paris court conviction for private corruption and spreading false information, so check this before any outreach. Very private, with no personal public channels. Forbes listing is from 2015 and he is likely no longer a billionaire.

name: Alan Auerbach
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and President, Puma Biotechnology (NASDAQ: PBYI)
profile: Biomedical engineer turned biotech analyst turned founder. He founded Cougar Biotechnology in 2003, whose prostate-cancer drug abiraterone (Zytiga) led to J&J's ~$1bn acquisition in 2009, then founded Puma Biotechnology in 2010, which commercialises the breast-cancer drug neratinib (Nerlynx).
interesting_fact: Cougar's lead drug abiraterone acetate, licensed in as an early-stage asset, was approved for metastatic prostate cancer in the US in April 2011 after J&J bought Cougar in 2009.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Cougar he was a biotech sell-side analyst (Wells Fargo Securities, Seidler Companies) and was ranked second in the NASDAQ/Starmine survey of analyst stock-picking performance in biotechnology; earlier he designed oncology clinical trials at Diagnostic Products Corp. He holds BS/MS degrees in biomedical engineering (Boston University, USC).
notes: Best route is via Puma IR (Mariann Ohanesian, Senior Director IR). Biotech focus, limited overlap with energy/data centers.

name: Carlos Fernández González
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO of Grupo Finaccess (Mexico/Spain); Honorary Chairman of AmRest (majority owner via Finaccess)
profile: Mexican businessman (b. 1966, Mexico City) who ran Grupo Modelo, maker of Corona, as CEO from 1997 and chairman from 2005 until its 2013 sale to AB InBev. He then built investment group Finaccess, which controls Europe-based restaurant operator AmRest (KFC, Pizza Hut, Burger King franchises) and holds stakes in Spanish firms such as Colonial and Prisa.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Grupo Modelo became one of the world's largest brewers before its 2013 sale to AB InBev; Finaccess later became AmRest's controlling shareholder (about two-thirds of the shares).
deep_cut_fact: An industrial engineer from Universidad Anáhuac, he also took a beer-brewing course at the University of California, Davis, before leading Modelo. He founded the Mexico chapter of Fundación Carolina and the Academia Mexicana de la Comunicación.
notes: Wikipedia education details are flagged as lacking citations; verify the UC Davis detail before using. He left the AmRest board in May 2023 (now honorary chairman); José Parés chairs AmRest. Finaccess is the more relevant route.

name: Cen Zhaoxiong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Times China Holdings (HKEX: 1233), Guangzhou
profile: Cen Zhaoxiong (岑钊雄, known in Hong Kong filings as Shum Chiu Hung) founded Guangzhou property developer Times China (formerly Times Property) and has chaired it since its 2008 Hong Kong listing. He remains chairman/CEO while the developer works through a debt restructuring; he is also an NPC deputy for Guangdong.
interesting_fact: He is a member of China's National People's Congress for Guangdong and President of the Guangdong Youth Entrepreneurs Association; he was named a 'Guangzhou Model Philanthropist' in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: His company co-founded the Guangdong Times Museum in 2003 with the Guangdong Museum of Art, and later commissioned Rem Koolhaas and Alain Fouraux to design its permanent space on top of a Times residential tower (opened 2010).
notes: Forbes 'Cen Zhaoxiong' = Mandarin pinyin of 岑钊雄; HKEX/company English name is Shum Chiu Hung. Times China is in debt restructuring; avoid the topic. No personal social accounts found; route via IR.

name: Li Yiping (李一萍)
current_role: No executive role found; spouse of Times China Holdings (HKEX:1233) founder/chairman Shum Chiu Hung (岑钊雄)
profile: Li Yiping appears on Hurun rich lists jointly with her husband Shum Chiu Hung, founder of Guangzhou developer Times China Holdings (listed in Hong Kong in 2013). HKEX filings describe her as his wife and a connected person who co-owned Guangzhou property used by the company. No public business profile of her own was found.
interesting_fact: Times China's 2013 HKEX disclosure records that the company occupied Guangzhou premises owned by Li Yiping and the Shum family's Times Development group, making her a 'connected person' of the listed company.
notes: Very private; wealth is via husband Shum Chiu Hung's Times China stake (Hurun lists them jointly). Hurun's 2018 'self-made women' listing suggests she was treated as co-founder, but no independent profile found. Any approach should go via Times China corporate channels; live status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Chizuko Matsui
current_role: Shareholder of Matsui Securities (former controlling shareholder); no executive role found
profile: Chizuko Matsui (松井千鶴子) was the largest and controlling shareholder of Tokyo online broker Matsui Securities, holding about 58% of voting rights (directly and indirectly) in 2015. In 2016-17 she transferred shares to Maruroku Ltd, the founding family's asset-management company, after which she ceased to be a major/controlling shareholder. Wealth is shared with longtime president Michio Matsui.
interesting_fact: Matsui Securities, founded in 1931 as a tiny brokerage, reinvented itself in the mid-1990s as one of Japan's first online brokers; in Nov 2026 Japan Post Bank agreed to buy shares from Maruroku and become its largest shareholder.
notes: Extremely private; no public profile, interviews or role beyond shareholder filings (JPX disclosures e.g. https://www2.jpx.co.jp/disc/86280/140120161104430973.pdf). Exact family relationship to Michio Matsui not confirmed in sources. Not a podcast-likely guest; any approach would be via Matsui Securities/Maruroku.

name: Michio Matsui
current_role: Advisor (former President & Representative Director, 1995-2020), Matsui Securities Co., Ltd.
profile: Michio Matsui (b. 1953, born Mutai) married into the Matsui family and ran Matsui Securities as president for 25 years (1995-2020). He turned a tiny Tokyo broker into a pioneer of Japanese online brokerage, entering internet trading in earnest in 1998. He handed the presidency to Akira Warita in June 2020 and now serves as an advisor.
interesting_fact: Before finance he spent 11 years at shipping line NYK (Nippon Yusen) after graduating from Hitotsubashi in 1976; he joined Matsui Securities in 1987 as a mid-career hire and became president just eight years later.
deep_cut_fact: As a Tokyo high-school student he hung out in jazz cafes, was friends with singer Tatsuro Yamashita, and was in the art club aiming for Tokyo University of the Arts until a teacher talked him out of it.

public_contacts.value: https://www.matsui.co.jp/company/history/essay/ (Matsui Securities page hosting his memoir as former president)

notes: Wealth shared with wife Chizuko Matsui (daughter of the previous president). Retired from management; best route is likely via Matsui Securities corporate office. Speaks/writes in Japanese.

name: Somsri Lumsam
profile: Listed by Hurun Global (2018-2024) at ~US$1.2bn with CP Group as source of wealth. Searches found no person of this exact spelling linked to CP Group (owned by the Chearavanont family); a 'Somsri Lamsam' appears on a 2023 Thai rich list without a stated business link.
notes: Identity unresolved: the name is likely a romanisation of Somsri Lamsam (Lamsam family is associated with Kasikornbank/Muang Thai, not CP Group), so the Hurun CP Group attribution may be an error. Verify in Thai-language sources before any outreach. Caproasia 2023 list: https://www.caproasia.com/2023/04/15/2023-top-20-richest-in-thailand/

name: Fan Meihua
current_role: Co-shareholder (with husband Yang Jianxin) in KJT / Global Top E-Commerce (跨境通, SZSE: 002640); no confirmed executive role
profile: Fan Meihua (樊梅花) is the wife and concert party of Yang Jianxin, founder of Shanxi-based Baiyuan Trousers, which became cross-border e-commerce group KJT (跨境通) after acquiring export e-retailers Globalegrow (环球易购) and Patozon. The couple were controlling holders; from 2019 they ceded voting control to a Guangzhou state-backed fund (unwound 2021) and sold down stakes. Little else is public.
interesting_fact: SZSE filings describe Yang Jianxin and Fan Meihua as legal spouses and formal 'persons acting in concert' who jointly controlled KJT until a 2019 voting-rights delegation to a Guangzhou Development District fund.
notes: Very private; no public profile found. Hurun listing (2016-2020) was via the couple's KJT stake, which has since shrunk sharply, so she is likely no longer a billionaire. Only route would be KJT board secretary (Wang Yuedi per 2025-26 IR records) via cninfo filings / ir.p5w.net.

name: Omid Kordestani
current_role: Chair of the Board, Pearson plc (since 2022); non-executive director, Klarna Group
profile: Tehran-born Iranian-American executive who ran Google's worldwide sales and business operations from 1999 to 2009 (and returned as Chief Business Officer 2014-15), building the wealth tied to his early Alphabet stock. He was later executive chairman of Twitter (2015-2020) and has chaired education company Pearson since 2022.
interesting_fact: Before Google he ran OEM sales and business development at Netscape; at Google he built the global sales organisation that turned search ads into the company's revenue engine. Time named him one of its 100 people who shape our world in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to San Jose after his father died in 1976, graduated from Buchser High School in Santa Clara (1980), studied electrical engineering at San Jose State and worked as an engineer at Hewlett-Packard before his 1991 Stanford MBA.
notes: Best route is via Pearson's corporate media team (corporate/financial media contacts listed on the IR contacts page; addresses obfuscated there). Co-founded the PARSA Community Foundation for the Iranian-American community. Pearson confirmed him as chair in a Sept 2026 board announcement.

name: Zheng Jianming
current_role: Chairman, Asia Pacific Resources Development Investment (APRD); former controlling backer of Shunfeng International Clean Energy (HK:1165, in liquidation since Nov 2025)
profile: Hong Kong-based tycoon (Cantonese name Cheng Kin Ming) who made his money in China/HK real estate, then from 2012 built a clean-energy portfolio through APRD: Shunfeng (which bought bankrupt Wuxi Suntech in 2013), Nobao geothermal, Lattice Power LEDs, GreenWheel EV and US battery maker Boston-Power. Shunfeng later ran into debt problems and entered liquidation in 2025.
interesting_fact: He bankrolled Shunfeng's 2013 rescue of Wuxi Suntech, once the world's largest solar-panel maker, after it went bankrupt.
deep_cut_fact: Long described as reclusive, he made a rare public debut on a 2014 US tour (a NYC solar-finance conference, then Goldman Sachs' EcoSummit), pledging 50 GW of clean energy in 10 years and saying geothermal firm Nobao would replace coal heating in Beijing and Tianjin.
notes: Very private, little coverage since about 2019. No reports of death found, but nothing recent confirms his status. Shunfeng (01165.HK) is in liquidation (shares suspended 19 Nov 2025) and its only contacts are the liquidators. He is a creditor (via APRDIL). No published personal or office contact found. Probably a low-yield outreach target.

name: Chung Mong Jin
current_role: Chairman (and CEO), KCC Corporation / KCC Group, South Korea
profile: Eldest son of KCC founder Chung Sang-young (youngest brother of Hyundai founder Chung Ju-yung), he has led KCC, Korea's leading paint, building-materials and silicone maker, since the 2000s. He steered KCC's 2019 consortium buyout of US silicones maker Momentive Performance Materials from Apollo (~$3bn) and in 2024 moved KCC to full ownership.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership KCC bought Momentive Performance Materials from Apollo in 2019 for about $3.1bn, turning a Korean paint company into one of the world's largest silicone producers; in 2024 it agreed to buy out partner SJL Partners for 100% ownership.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Best route is KCC corporate communications via the company website. Brother Chung Mong-ik is vice chairman.

name: Khaleefa Butti bin Omair Al-Muhairi
current_role: Emirati investor; former vice-chairman and major shareholder of NMC Health (resigned Feb 2020); listed as chairman of Travelex Holding
profile: Abu Dhabi businessman (name also spelled Khalifa Butti Omeir Bin Yousef) who, with partners, built a stake of roughly 40% in UAE hospital group NMC Health, partly by buying shares from founder B.R. Shetty in 2017. He was NMC vice-chairman until February 2020, when he resigned amid the company's collapse. His current activities are not well documented.
interesting_fact: He and partners held about 40% of NMC Health, once a FTSE 100 company, before he resigned as vice-chairman in February 2020.
notes: Sensitive: NMC Health collapsed in a 2020 accounting scandal and AGBI reports he later sought bankruptcy/restructuring via an Abu Dhabi court. Probably not a suitable podcast guest. I found no published contact channels.

name: Nilima Motaparti
current_role: Whole-Time Director (Commercial), Divi's Laboratories (listed on company site as Nilima Prasad Divi)
profile: Daughter of Divi's Laboratories founder Murali Divi and a major shareholder of the Hyderabad-based API maker. Joined officially in 2012 as Chief Controller (Commercial); now Whole-Time Director overseeing material sourcing and procurement, capital projects, corporate finance and investor relations.
interesting_fact: She has built Divi's sourcing strategy around a base of alternative suppliers and long-term procurement contracts to cut supply risk; she holds master's degrees in international business (GITAM) and international finance (University of Glasgow).
deep_cut_fact: She first worked at Divi's as a trainee around 1999 while still a graduate, learning finance under CFO L. Kishore Babu; she has quoted her father's advice that although the company is cash rich, 'we still need to spend and think like a small company.'
notes: Company now lists her as Nilima Prasad Divi. Low public profile; she personally oversees investor relations, so the IR route (cs@divislabs.com) is the most relevant.

name: Paul Salteri
current_role: Founder and Chairman, CAGES Foundation (Salteri family private ancillary fund); former Chairman, Tenix Group
profile: Eldest son of Transfield co-founder Carlo Salteri. Became joint MD of Transfield in 1989; after the 1995 family split he ran the Salteri side as Tenix (MD 1997-2007, then chairman), selling Tenix Defence to BAE Systems in 2008 and the remaining Tenix assets to Downer EDI in 2014. Now focused on philanthropy via the CAGES Foundation.
interesting_fact: Transfield, the company his father co-founded, won a A$6bn contract in 1989 to build ten Anzac-class frigates for Australia and New Zealand, becoming Australia's largest defence company; that business became Tenix Defence.
deep_cut_fact: With his wife Sandra he set up CAGES Foundation to support First Nations early-childhood services; after asking Indigenous communities why investment often fails ('because they don't trust us'), the foundation shifted to trust-based, less onerous grant-making.
notes: Low public profile; best route is CAGES Foundation (Sydney). Trained as an accountant (UNSW BCom 1971), joined Transfield 1978. Tenix itself no longer exists as an operating group.

name: Tony Jashanmal
current_role: Group President, Jashanmal Group (Dubai); member of the Executive Board
profile: Kuwait-born (1947) scion of the Jashanmal family, whose Gulf trading/retail group dates back more than a century and distributes and retails books, fashion, accessories, home and electronics brands across the GCC. He joined in 1971 and led diversification into print media, accessories and fashion, post-Gulf War rebuilding in Kuwait and JV entry into India; he still sits on the Executive Board.
interesting_fact: He holds a Diplom-Volkswirt (Master's in Economics) from Hamburg University in Germany, after schooling in India and high school in Villars, Switzerland.
deep_cut_fact: He personally played a key role in rebuilding the group's Kuwait operations after the 1990-91 Gulf War, and has long championed e-commerce at the century-old retailer ('We have embraced technology wholeheartedly at Jashanmal').
notes: Hurun listing ended 2019. Day-to-day leadership: Group CEO is Shuja Jashanmal per the leadership page; Tony is Group President. Contact form is the retail customer form; no published press email found.

name: Haruko Mikitani
current_role: Major individual shareholder of Rakuten Group; wife of Rakuten founder/CEO Hiroshi 'Mickey' Mikitani
profile: Haruko Mikitani (三谷晴子 as listed; 三木谷晴子) married Hiroshi Mikitani in 1993. Her wealth comes from a personal stake in Rakuten Group, the Japanese e-commerce, fintech and mobile conglomerate her husband founded in 1997; she has kept an almost entirely private profile.
interesting_fact: She is reported to hold roughly 5% of Rakuten in her own name, separate from her husband's direct stake and his Crimson Group holding vehicle (figures vary by source and date).
notes: Very private; no public role, interviews or accounts found. Early-Rakuten back-office role claimed only by a weak source (prabook), not verified. Any approach would realistically go through Rakuten Group corporate communications or the Mikitani family office (Crimson Group). Alive status not independently confirmed (no reports otherwise).

name: Hirokazu Sugiura
current_role: Founder and adviser (non-executive), Sugi Holdings; chairman of the council of the Sugiura Memorial Foundation
profile: Pharmacist Hirokazu Sugiura (b. 1950, Nishio, Aichi) founded Sugi Pharmacy in 1976 and built it into Sugi Holdings, one of Japan's largest drugstore/dispensing chains (~¥1 trillion revenue). He was president 1982-2009 and chairman until 2021, when his son Katsunori became president; he is now an adviser and focuses on the family's health foundation.
interesting_fact: The first Sugi Pharmacy was a 16-tsubo (about 53 m2) shop in Nishio, opened in December 1976 at the same time he married fellow Gifu Pharmaceutical University graduate Akiko, who became the company's co-founder and vice president.
deep_cut_fact: In 2016 he and Akiko built the 'Nishio Citizens' Genki Plaza', a health-promotion centre on the site of the very first Sugi Pharmacy store, and lent the building and land to the city free of charge (opened April 2017).
notes: Name in input is misspelled 'Sugiara'; correct romanization is Sugiura (杉浦広一). Low public profile; Japanese-language outreach via the Sugiura Memorial Foundation is the most plausible route. Cited his reading favorites: Tempu Nakamura and Peter Drucker.

name: Rosana Camargo De Arruda Botelho
current_role: Controlling shareholder (via family holdings incl. Participações Morro Vermelho) of Mover Participações, formerly Grupo Camargo Corrêa
profile: One of the three daughters of Sebastião Camargo, who founded Camargo Corrêa in Jaú, São Paulo in 1939. She and her sisters Renata and Regina inherited control after their mother Dirce died in 2013; the group, renamed Mover, is run by non-family professionals. Mover has been selling assets in 2025-26 (e.g. its Motiva stake to Bradesco BBI) to cut debt. Widow/partner of businessman-aviator Fernando de Arruda Botelho; about 76.
interesting_fact: The family's controlling holding, Morro Vermelho, is named after a farm in Jaú, Sebastião Camargo's hometown, and also gave its name to the group's executive aviation arm, Morro Vermelho Táxi Aéreo.
notes: Very private; no personal public channels. Her daughter Daniela Camargo Botelho de Abreu Pereira is the only family member on Mover's board (since 2024). Best route is Mover Participações corporate communications (moverpar.com.br, blocked to automated fetch). Name sometimes spelled 'Rossana'.

name: Yang Aihua
current_role: Founder and Executive Director, Autostreets Development Ltd (HKEX: 2443), Shanghai used-car auction platform
profile: Shanghai auto-retail entrepreneur who founded Baoxin Auto in 1999, built it into one of China's largest BMW dealer groups and listed it in Hong Kong in 2011. In late 2015 he sold control to China Grand Auto (now Grand Baoxin) and in 2014 founded Autostreets, a B2B used-car auction platform that listed in Hong Kong; he remains an executive director.
interesting_fact: Baoxin opened its first 4S store in Shanghai in 1999 as one of Audi's first authorized dealers in China, and in 2004 became one of BMW's first authorized dealers, later the world's largest BMW dealer group.
deep_cut_fact: Autostreets counts Cox Automotive, parent of US wholesale auction giant Manheim, as its second-largest shareholder, alongside Tencent and JD.com; by 2022 about 4,900 dealerships had sold used cars through the platform.
notes: Described in press as extremely low-profile and rarely interviewed. Best route is via Autostreets corporate channels (company site / HKEX filings). Autostreets chairman is Yang Hansong.

name: Anders Westermann
current_role: Co-owner (Westermann family) of WS Audiology via T&W Medical; former Executive Vice President of Widex
profile: Son of Widex co-founder Erik Westermann; with brother Søren and cousin Jan Tøpholm he ran Danish hearing-aid maker Widex as Executive VP. The Tøpholm and Westermann families merged Widex with Sivantos in 2019 to form WS Audiology, which they co-own with EQT via T&W Medical.
interesting_fact: Widex was founded in 1956 by Christian Tøpholm and Erik Westermann; their sons (Jan Tøpholm, Anders and Søren Westermann) later ran the company together as second-generation leaders.
notes: Very private; little recent public info. Identity of the Hurun-listed person inferred from family ownership; MarketScreener 'Anders Steen Westermann' (Widex director since 1980) may be the same person but unconfirmed. Best route likely via WS Audiology corporate communications.

name: Soren Westermann
current_role: Co-owner of WS Audiology (via Westermann family); long-time Widex A/S director and engineer

A DTU-trained engineer and long-serving Widex board member, he shares in the family stake in WS Audiology, formed when Widex merged with Sivantos in 2019 and still owned by the Tøpholm and Westermann families alongside EQT.

Relative Adam Westermann (grandson of co-founder) is WSA board vice-chair; family holding is T&W Medical. Alive status not confirmed (patent filings into the 2010s, no death reports found).

name: Weit Pot
current_role: Major shareholder and former co-CEO of IMC (trading firm); listed as co-CEO of IMC Asset Management BV
profile: Wiet (Wilhelmus) Pot, born 1957 in Eindhoven, is a Dutch financier. His wealth stems mainly from a large stake in IMC.

He is behind the 'Huis van Leyden' cultural restoration project at Pieterskerkhof/Rapenburg in Leiden.

name: Chen Yiy Fon
current_role: CEO and Executive Director, NagaCorp Ltd (HKEX: 3918), operator of NagaWorld casino resort in Phnom Penh
profile: Second son of NagaCorp founder Tan Sri Dr Chen Lip Keong (d. Dec 2023). A USC economics graduate, he joined NagaCorp's board in 2015, became CEO of operations in 2022 and group CEO from 10 Dec 2023, inheriting the largest single allocation (~8.3%) of NagaCorp shares. name: Chen Yiy Hwuan
current_role: Chief Executive Officer – Hotels, NagaCorp Ltd (appointed April 2022; latest status not confirmed)
profile: Son of the late NagaCorp founder Chen Lip Keong (d. Dec 2023), whose HK-listed company runs the NagaWorld casino-resort monopoly in Phnom Penh, Cambodia. His wealth comes from the family's NagaCorp stake. In April 2022 he was named CEO – Hotels as part of a succession reshuffle; his brother Chen Yiy Fon now leads the group.

name: Dipankar Chatterjee
current_role: Whole-time director (listed as chairman by some sources), Luxmi Tea Co. Pvt Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Son of Paresh Chandra Chatterjee, who founded Luxmi Tea in Kolkata in 1912 as a swadeshi venture. Dipankar took over the business in the 1980s and grew it into one of India's larger tea groups (Assam, Darjeeling, Tripura and African estates, incl. Makaibari, bought 2014). His son Rudra Chatterjee is now managing director.
interesting_fact: Luxmi Tea was founded in 1912 by his father as a protest against British colonial rule; today the group produces tea from ~25 estates in India and Africa and owns Darjeeling's famed Makaibari estate.
deep_cut_fact: After buying Assam's Narayanpur Tea Estate, he noticed its tea was popular with buyers from Rajasthan and created a 'Narayanpur Tea' sub-brand, described as probably the first Indian tea brand named after a region.
notes: Low public profile; son Rudra Chatterjee (MD) is the group's public face and a frequent speaker, likely the best route. Alive status not confirmed by recent news.

name: Kevin Guo
current_role: Chairman & President, Yunnan Botanee Bio-Technology Group (SZSE: 300957), parent of Winona skincare (if Kevin Guo = Guo Zhenyu)
profile: Botanee wealth on Hurun lists belongs to founder-chairman Guo Zhenyu (郭振宇), a former engineering/biomedical academic who returned to China in 2003 to run Dihon Pharmaceutical, then built Botanee around Winona, China's leading sensitive-skin skincare brand. Botanee listed in Shenzhen in March 2021; he is now expanding brands like Winona Baby and Aoxmed.

name: Lee Chou Sarn
current_role: No public executive role found; family linked to NagaCorp (Cambodia casino operator)
profile: Lee Chou Sarn is listed as the (first) wife of the late Tan Sri Chen Lip Keong, founder of Hong Kong-listed NagaCorp, which runs NagaWorld in Phnom Penh. name: Zhang Tianren
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Tianneng Power International (HKEX: 0819); chairman of Tianneng Group
profile: Zhang Tianren built Tianneng from a debt-laden battery workshop in Changxing, Zhejiang (1986) into China's largest lead-acid battery maker, powering the country's e-bike boom; it listed in Hong Kong in 2007 and its Tianneng Battery arm trades on Shanghai's STAR Market. He is now pushing Tianneng into lithium, sodium-ion and energy-storage batteries.
interesting_fact: Changxing county, Tianneng's home on Lake Tai, produces nearly half of China's lead-acid batteries, and Tianneng is the county's dominant player.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as an ordinary accountant who in 1986 took over a small, heavily indebted battery factory, then partnered with Fudan University to develop a new generation of electric-bike power batteries.
notes: Energy-storage angle: Tianneng says 60-80% of its lithium capacity targets storage. No current IR email found; website IR section is the route. Birth year varies across sources (c.1963).

name: Devendra Kumar Jain
current_role: Deceased (was Chairman and Director, Gujarat Fluorochemicals; founder of INOX Group)
notes: Died per Gujarat Fluorochemicals' BSE notice of 29 Dec 2025 (https://www.business-standard.com/markets/gujarat-fluorochemicals-ltd-share-price-74458/announcements/bse-exchange-50429750). INOX Group is now led by sons Pavan and Vivek Jain (Vivek is GFL MD).

name: Borris Rotenberg
current_role: Co-owner of SMP Bank and businessman; co-founder (with brother Arkady) of SGM (Stroygazmontazh) group; president of the Russian Judo Federation (per Wikipedia)
profile: Boris Romanovich Rotenberg (b. 1957, St Petersburg) built his fortune with brother Arkady through SMP Bank (founded 2001) and SGM, one of Russia's largest builders of gas pipelines and power lines for Gazprom; Arkady reportedly sold SGM in 2019. He is under US (since 2014), UK and EU sanctions.
interesting_fact: He is also a racing driver: he has competed in the European Le Mans Series, the 24 Hours of Daytona and Ferrari Challenge, and is linked to the BR Engineering Le Mans prototype constructor and SMP Racing.
deep_cut_fact: A Soviet judo competitor in his youth, he moved to Helsinki in 1992 to work as a professional judo coach for six years before returning to St Petersburg in 1998; he later became a naturalised Finnish citizen.
notes: Input spells 'Borris'; this is Boris Romanovich Rotenberg. He is sanctioned by the US, UK and EU — check legal/sanctions implications before any outreach. No published contacts. Only appeared on Hurun in 2014.

name: Edward W. Stack
current_role: Executive Chairman, DICK'S Sporting Goods, Inc. (since Feb 2021; CEO 1984-2021)
profile: Son of Dick Stack, who founded DICK'S as a Binghamton bait-and-tackle shop in 1948. Ed and his siblings bought the two-store business in the early 1980s; as CEO from 1984 he moved HQ to Pittsburgh (1994), took it public (2002) and built it into the largest US sporting-goods retailer. As executive chairman he now oversees merchandising and the Foot Locker integration.
interesting_fact: After the 2018 Parkland shooting he stopped DICK'S selling assault-style rifles and guns to under-21s, destroying about $5m of rifles in inventory, and later lobbied for stronger gun laws.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2026 Little League enshrined him in its Hall of Excellence; he played Little League in Binghamton, where his father helped grow the local program from four teams to 16.
notes: Planned to become a lawyer before joining the family business; wrote a 2019 memoir 'It's How We Play the Game'. Best route is DICK'S media relations.

name: Xiu Laigui
current_role: Founder and chairman, Xiuzheng Pharmaceutical Group (修正药业), Tonghua, Jilin
profile: Born 1955 in Tonghua, Jilin, Xiu studied law at Jilin University and spent about 20 years in the Tonghua public security system. In 1995 he took over a bankrupt local drug factory and built it into Xiuzheng Pharmaceutical, one of China's largest private pharma groups (2024 sales reportedly ~RMB67.7bn). He is often cited as Jilin's richest person.
interesting_fact: Xiuzheng began as a bankrupt Tonghua municipal pharmaceutical research institute factory that Xiu took over in 1995; it is now among China's biggest private drugmakers, with 2024 revenue reported around RMB67.7bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before pharma he was a policeman for roughly 20 years; his last post was head of the facilities brigade of the Tonghua traffic police detachment (交警支队设施大队大队长).
notes: Private company, Chinese-language media only; route via Xiuzheng corporate site. Note Xiuzheng animal-health units reported (Jul 2025) to be pursuing a Nasdaq listing via a listed company (CB Insights).

name: Ryuji Arai
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder, Bic Camera Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Founded Bic Camera, the Japanese electronics/appliance retail chain. It began in 1968 as a photo-processing shop in Takasaki, Gunma, became Bic Camera in 1978 (first store Ikebukuro), and listed in 2006. Revenue topped $6B in FY Aug 2025. He also holds stakes in Hit Communications and contact-lens maker Seed.
interesting_fact: Bic Camera owns a majority stake in the listed satellite TV network Nippon BS Broadcasting (BS11).
deep_cut_fact: Arai's first venture, started in his early twenties, was Takasaki DP Center, a film developing and printing shop in Gunma. Bic Camera grew out of that shop's camera-sales department, which was spun off as Bic Color in 1972.
notes: Very reclusive and gives no interviews (Bic Camera declined to make him available to Bloomberg in 2018). Best route is Bic Camera PR/IR via its IR site. An old 2009 address, kouhou@biccamera.com, is unverified and not included. He is an anti-nuclear advocate (1995 store banners against French nuclear tests): https://macaudailytimes.com.mo/?p=91929

name: Laurent Burelle
current_role: Chairman of the Board, OPmobility SE (formerly Plastic Omnium); CEO of family holding Burelle SA
profile: Son of Plastic Omnium founder Pierre Burelle, he joined the family group in the mid-1970s, ran it as CEO from 2001 to 2019 and refocused it on automotive exterior systems and fuel tanks. Now non-executive chairman of OPmobility (renamed 2024), where daughter Félicie Burelle became CEO after Laurent Favre left in Nov 2025. He led French business lobby Afep from 2017 to 2023.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Plastic Omnium was renamed OPmobility in 2024 and has invested in hydrogen mobility (tanks, fuel-cell systems) and electrification, which is relevant to an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the group's Langres plant around age 25 after initially planning to work for Alfa Laval, and at 28 moved to Spain to run the Valencia plant, becoming head of the Spanish subsidiary in 1980. He trained as a chemical engineer at ETH Zurich and MIT.
notes: Governance change Nov 2025: Félicie Burelle took over as CEO (https://www.opmobility.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/11/evolution-in-the-governance-of-opmobility-se-20251107-en.pdf). Best route is via OPmobility corporate communications. Wiki sources disagree on the exact chairmanship start date (2020 vs 2021).

name: Xie Yi
current_role: Chairman, CEO and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Tianmai Thermal Technology (SZSE: 301626)
profile: Xie Yi founded Suzhou Tianmai in 2007 with his wife Shen Fenghua; it makes thermal-management parts (heat pipes, vapor chambers, synthetic graphite films) for customers such as CATL, Huawei and Samsung. The company listed in Shenzhen in 2024 raising $87m; he directly owns ~40.8% and in 2026 the company was issuing convertible bonds to expand.
interesting_fact: He started his first job at 16 at a local factory making thermal-management products, the same niche he later built a billionaire-scale company in.

name: Qiao Zhiyong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~71%), Sichuan Qiaoyuan Gas Co., Ltd. (侨源股份, SZ:301286)
profile: Qiao Zhiyong chairs Sichuan Qiaoyuan Gas, a Dujiangyan/Chengdu-based supplier of high-purity oxygen, nitrogen and argon produced by air separation. Founded in 2002, it is the leading retail air-gas supplier in the Sichuan-Chongqing region and is expanding into specialty and electronic gases. It listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in 2022.
interesting_fact: In 2003 Qiaoyuan commissioned what the company says was China's first all-liquid air-separation gas production line, at its Dujiangyan base. Its 'Qiaoyuan' brand of oxygen, nitrogen and argon was later named a Sichuan Famous Brand Product by the provincial government.

name: Bhaskara Rao Bollineni
current_role: Founder & Chairman (Managing Director), KIMS Hospitals (Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd)
profile: Cardiothoracic surgeon who founded KIMS Hospitals in 2000, starting with a 200-bed hospital in his hometown of Nellore, Andhra Pradesh. KIMS is now a listed chain of about 25 hospitals with roughly 8,300 beds across five southern and western Indian states. His son Dr. Abhinay Bollineni is CEO, and he remains chairman and a practising surgeon.

deep_cut_fact: He earned his MBBS at Rangaraya Medical College, Kakinada (1981) and his MS at Madras Medical College (1984). Before founding KIMS he practised at Medwin Hospitals and Mahavir Trust Hospital in Hyderabad, and he played a key part in Andhra Pradesh's Rajiv Gandhi Aarogyasri health scheme for poorer families.
notes: cs@ belongs to the Company Secretary (investor contact); assistance@ is the general patient inbox. No published press or personal email found. His spelling is often 'Bhaskar Rao'.

name: Mary Alice Malone Jr
current_role: Founder & creative director, Malone Souliers; owner of Duo Boots; director, The Campbell's Company (since July 2025)
profile: Great-granddaughter of Campbell's Soup inventor John T. Dorrance; she and her sister inherited a combined ~18% Campbell's stake when their mother died in June 2025, and she took her mother's board seat. London-based, she trained as a shoemaker, founded luxury footwear label Malone Souliers in 2014 and revived UK brand Duo Boots in 2020.

name: Sir Dennis Gillings
current_role: Non-Executive Chair and Founder, GHO Capital (healthcare investment firm); retired IQVIA lead director (2018)
profile: British-born statistician (b. 1944, London) who co-founded Quintiles in Durham, NC, growing it from UNC biostatistics consulting into the world's largest clinical-research organisation; Quintiles merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form IQVIA. Now an investor/chair at London-based GHO Capital and a dementia-research advocate.
interesting_fact: In 2014 David Cameron appointed him World Dementia Envoy; he helped found and became first chairman of the World Dementia Council, and was knighted in 2020 for services to dementia and life-sciences research.
deep_cut_fact: Quintiles traces back to a single 1974 project: Hoechst hired the UNC biostatistics professor to analyse trial data for a new diabetes drug; his analysis showed which patients to exclude, letting Hoechst bring it to market. The company was only incorporated in 1982 with fellow professor Gary Koch.
notes: Lane name 'Sir Dennis' = Sir Dennis Gillings (wealth shared with wife Mireille Gillings, per Sunday Times). Son of a London fishmonger (Wikipedia). Best route likely via GHO Capital (ghocapital.com) — no published personal contact found.

name: Mireille Gillings
current_role: Founder, CEO & Executive Chair, HUYABIO International; Co-founder & Non-Executive Vice Chair, GHO Capital
profile: Montreal-born neurobiologist (PhD Radboud Nijmegen, postdocs at Bordeaux and Scripps) who founded San Diego-based HUYA Bioscience International in 2004 to in-license and develop novel drugs discovered in China. She co-founded London healthcare private-equity firm GHO Capital. Married to Sir Dennis Gillings, founder of Quintiles (now IQVIA), source of the shared family fortune.
interesting_fact: HUYABIO pioneered a model of bringing Chinese-discovered drug compounds to Western clinical trials; Fortune profiled her in 2010 as a China biotech pioneer.
deep_cut_fact: The company name HUYA combines the Chinese abbreviations for Shanghai (Hù) and Asia (Yà); before HUYA she was also a co-founder of MIR3, and she calls herself a 'serial entrepreneur'. She speaks French natively plus Mandarin.
notes: Styled Lady Mireille Gillings. Listed as UK on Sunday Times Rich List but based in San Diego. Healthcare/biotech focus; best route is HUYABIO contact form.

name: Richard Warke
current_role: Founder, Augusta Group of Companies; Executive Chairman, Titan Mining Corp.; Chairman, Solaris Resources
profile: Vancouver mining financier who founded the Augusta Group in 2005 and sold a string of discoveries: Ventana Gold (2011), Augusta Resource (Rosemont copper, 2014), Arizona Mining (zinc, to South32 for C$2.1B, 2018) and Augusta Gold (AngloGold, 2025). He now chairs Titan Mining, Highlander Silver and Solaris Resources.
interesting_fact: Beyond mining he holds sports stakes: he is a partner in Fenway Sports Group (Boston Red Sox, Liverpool FC) and, per Wikipedia, in the PGA Tour and the Boston Celtics.
deep_cut_fact: Energy-transition angle: his Titan Mining is positioning itself as an emerging US natural flake graphite supplier (a battery material) from its zinc mine in upstate New York; he also co-founded Equinox Gold in 2017.
notes: Low media profile; best route is via Titan Mining / Augusta Group IR in Vancouver. Graphite (battery supply chain) is a natural hook for an energy podcast.

name: Jeremy Allaire
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Circle Internet Group (NYSE: CRCL)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Allaire Corp. (ColdFusion; IPO 1999, sold to Macromedia) and Brightcove (online video, IPO 2012). Pivoted to crypto in 2013 co-founding Circle, issuer of the USDC stablecoin, and took it public in June 2025, the first IPO of a stablecoin issuer.
interesting_fact: He has now taken three companies public: Allaire Corp. (1999), Brightcove (2012) and Circle (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In 1994-96, fresh out of Macalester College (political science and philosophy), he worked with Noam Chomsky and his wife Carol to build the first comprehensive online archive of Chomsky's political writings.
notes: Very public and active on X (@jerallaire); regular podcast/conference guest on stablecoins and payments. Circle press office is the best route.

name: Kenji Kasahara
current_role: Founder, Director and Senior Corporate Officer, MIXI, Inc. (Tokyo)
profile: Kasahara founded Japanese social network Mixi in 2004 and took it public in 2006. After Mixi lost ground to rivals he stepped back from CEO (2013) and the company pivoted to mobile games (Monster Strike), sports and lifestyle apps. He holds roughly half of MIXI and remains a director; in 2026 he announced a gift of ~1.8bn yen of his shares to ~1,700 employees.
interesting_fact: In May 2026 he announced he would personally donate about 680,000 MIXI shares (~1.8 billion yen) to around 1,700 group employees and officers, calling it a tangible way to express gratitude.
deep_cut_fact: Before Mixi, he built the job-listings site Find Job! in 1997 at age 21 while a University of Tokyo student, founding eMercury two years later; in 2015 he launched FamilyAlbum (Mitene), a private family photo-sharing app.
notes: Low public profile; best route is MIXI corporate press inquiry form. CEO is Hiroki Kimura.

name: Rajju Shroff
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, UPL Ltd (since Dec 2022)
profile: Rajnikant 'Rajju' Shroff founded Mumbai-based UPL in 1969 to make red phosphorus and built it over 50+ years as chairman and MD into one of the world's largest crop-protection companies, especially after the $4.2bn Arysta LifeScience deal in 2018. He stepped down at 90 in Dec 2022; son Jai Shroff is now chairman and group CEO.
interesting_fact: UPL began in 1969 producing red phosphorus, which Shroff pioneered making in India. He was awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2021 and Mexico's Order of the Aztec Eagle in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: A Bombay University chemistry graduate from a Kutch entrepreneurial family, in 1957 he developed a new process for making mercury salts at a UK plant, and a British company paid him royalties for it, which was rare for an Indian chemist at the time.
notes: Now about 93 and retired to focus on social causes; UPL lists upl@uniphos.com for corporate-affairs enquiries. Son Jai Shroff (chairman/CEO) is the active public face.

name: Lady Green
current_role: Co-founder, Green & Mingarelli Design (Monaco); owner of Taveta, the former Arcadia Group parent
profile: Lady Tina Green (born Christina Stuart-Paine), wife of retailer Sir Philip Green, was the legal owner via Jersey-held Taveta of the Arcadia Group (Topshop, Dorothy Perkins, Burton), which entered administration in 2020. Monaco-based, she now runs a yacht and aircraft interior design firm with Pietro Mingarelli.
interesting_fact: Although Sir Philip Green ran Arcadia, the retail empire was legally owned by Tina Green through a Jersey company, Taveta, which held the family's shares.
deep_cut_fact: With partner Pietro Mingarelli she designed the Benetti superyacht Illusion V inside and out; her studio is known for building each yacht around a single theme (once an antique woodcarving found in a northern Thailand market) and for its 'hidden cupboards'.
notes: Very private, Monaco-resident. No published personal or office contact found. Her design firm (Green & Mingarelli Design) is the most plausible professional route but no verified site/email found.

name: Liu Qingfeng
current_role: Founder, chairman and president, iFLYTEK Co., Ltd. (Hefei, Shenzhen-listed 002230)
profile: Born 1973 in Tongcheng, Anhui, Liu founded iFLYTEK in 1999 as a second-year PhD student at USTC with a dozen classmates, raising seed funds from the university. iFLYTEK listed in Shenzhen in 2008 and became China's leading speech-recognition and AI company; Liu now drives its 'Spark' large-language-model push.
interesting_fact: He recalls iFLYTEK losing money for its first five years before becoming China's voice-recognition leader.
deep_cut_fact: He entered USTC as an undergraduate in 1990 and, as a doctoral student, developed China's first Mandarin speech-synthesis system (1998), the year before founding iFLYTEK.
notes: taojiang@iflytek.com belongs to board secretary Jiang Tao, as listed in iFLYTEK's English annual report. xunfei@iflytek.com is the company's general email. Liu often speaks at Boao Forum and other Chinese AI events, so the AI and compute-energy angle fits.

name: Shao Xiaofeng
current_role: Long-time Alibaba executive (EVP and chair of the Group Risk Management Committee per FY2025 report); left the Alibaba Partnership list in June 2026, current role unclear
profile: Shao Xiaofeng (often written 邵晓锋) joined Alibaba in 2005 from the Hangzhou police, became executive president of Alipay in 2008 and Alibaba's first chief risk officer in 2012, and later served as director at Alibaba Pictures. His fortune comes mainly from his stake in Ant Group. Alibaba's FY2026 annual report (June 2026) showed him leaving the partnership.
interesting_fact: Before joining Alibaba he was a criminal investigator: head of the first brigade of the Hangzhou Public Security Bureau's criminal investigation unit; Chinese media nicknamed him Alibaba's 'old detective' gatekeeper.
deep_cut_fact: Like all Alibaba partners he has a wuxia nickname (花名): his is 'Guo Jing' (郭靖), the righteous hero of Jin Yong's novels, and staff describe him as '侠骨柔情' (chivalrous yet tender).
notes: Name commonly spelled 邵晓锋 in Chinese press (input has 邵晓峰). Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Exit from Alibaba Partnership reported by IT Home, 21 Jun 2026 (https://www.ithome.com/0/966/730.htm). Any approach would go via Alibaba/Ant corporate PR.

name: Peng Yongdong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, KE Holdings (Beike), NYSE: BEKE / HKEX: 2423
profile: Stanley Peng Yongdong co-founded KE Holdings (Beike), China's largest housing transaction and services platform, which grew out of the Lianjia brokerage; he has been CEO since its 2018 relaunch and chairman after founder Zuo Hui's death in 2021. Holds an electrical engineering degree from Zhejiang University and an IMBA from Tsinghua.
interesting_fact: KE operates Lianjia, one of the world's largest real estate brokerages, and has expanded into home rentals and renovation.
deep_cut_fact: Before real estate he was a senior consultant at IBM (2006-2010), joining Lianjia from management consulting.
notes: A March 2025 trade report claimed he resigned as chairman, but KE's later 2025/2026 results releases still list him as Chairman and CEO. Route via KE investor relations.

name: Xu Rongmao
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Shimao Group Holdings (HKEX: 813); son Jason Hui Sai Tan has been chairman and president since 2024
profile: Xu Rongmao (Hui Wing Mau), born 1950 in Shishi, Fujian, built Shimao into one of China's big property developers, known for Shanghai riverside towers and hotels. He remains Shimao's controlling shareholder via Gemfair and Shiying Finance, but handed the chairmanship to his son in 2024 as the company worked through a debt restructuring.
interesting_fact: He earned a business master's degree by distance learning from the University of Adelaide.

notes: He keeps a very low profile. Shimao is in a debt restructuring, and per Mingtiandi (July 2026) the CSRC proposed disclosure fines on him and his son. Any outreach would go through Shimao IR/media relations. The deep-cut fact rests only on Wikipedia, whose early-life details are partly tagged 'citation needed'.

name: Zhou Qingzhi
current_role: Founder and chairman of Nandu (Narada) Group; actual controller of Zhejiang Narada Power Source (南都电源, SZSE: 300068)
profile: Wenzhou-born Zhou Qingzhi (周庆治) worked ~10 years in the Zhejiang provincial Party committee office before going into business in 1991, trading electronics and oil in Shenzhen, then Hangzhou property. His Nandu Group (1995) controls Narada Power, a Hangzhou battery maker now focused on lithium energy storage and recycling.

name: Song Weiping
current_role: Founder of Greentown China; controls Bluetown (Lancheng) town-development / construction-management business
profile: Song Weiping (b. 1957, Sheng County, Shaoxing) is a Hangzhou property developer who founded Greentown China with his wife Xia Yibo in 1994, building it into a premium developer in Zhejiang, Shanghai and Beijing. He resigned as Greentown co-chairman in 2019 to focus on Bluetown and 'ideal town' projects.
interesting_fact: He founded the Zhejiang Greentown football club (Hangzhou Greentown F.C.) and is a well-known football fan.
deep_cut_fact: A 1982 history graduate of Hangzhou University, he taught at a party school for five years, then worked as a secretary at a computer company in Zhuhai before returning to Hangzhou and founding Greentown with RMB150,000.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Xia Yibo. Current Bluetown title not confirmed for 2025-26. No personal published contacts; route would be via Greentown China or Bluetown corporate offices.

name: Xia Yibo
current_role: Non-executive director, Greentown Service Group (HKEX: 2869) (per market-data profiles; verify in latest annual report)
profile: Xia Yibo co-founded Hangzhou developer Greentown with her husband Song Weiping in 1994; it became one of China's best-known premium home builders (Greentown China, HKEX: 3900). The couple sold most of their Greentown China stake to China Communications Construction Group in 2014-15; her wealth now rests largely on a large holding in property-manager Greentown Service.
interesting_fact: Greentown was started in 1994 when Song Weiping, a former history teacher, returned to Hangzhou and founded the company together with Xia Yibo.
notes: Very private; almost no independent biography or interviews found. Wealth listed jointly with husband Song Weiping. No published personal/office contact; any approach would go through Greentown Service (Hangzhou) corporate channels.

name: Qiu Guogen
current_role: Founder, executive managing partner and chief investment officer, Shanghai Chongyang Investment (重阳投资)
profile: Zhejiang-born veteran of China's private securities fund industry. After an economics master's at Renmin University and a stint (1993-95) at an investment arm of the former Junan Securities, he began investing professionally in 1996 and founded Chongyang Investment in Shanghai in 2001, long one of China's largest private equity-securities funds. Ranks on Hurun lists jointly with wife Luo Yi (approx. RMB 7.5B in 2026).
interesting_fact: Chongyang was described around 2010 as China's largest private securities investment firm; its style is value investing aimed at 'all-weather' returns across market cycles.
deep_cut_fact: At a 2015 Hangzhou wealth-management forum he recalled that after university he interned for three months at the Zhejiang provincial branch of China Construction Bank in Hangzhou, and argued that 'risk and return are matched' (风险和收益是匹配的).
notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews. Route would be via Chongyang Investment's official website/office in Shanghai (no published press email found). Wealth shared with wife Luo Yi.

name: Luo Yi
current_role: Co-owner (about 22% of Chongyang Group per Tianyancha, as reported), Shanghai Chongyang Investment, with husband Qiu Guogen
profile: Luo Yi and her husband Qiu Guogen control Shanghai Chongyang Investment, one of China's oldest and largest private securities funds, founded in 2001 and known for long-term value investing. The couple appear jointly on the Hurun Global Rich List (RMB 7.5bn in 2026). Qiu runs investments; Luo keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Before founding Chongyang, the couple reportedly grew their wealth nearly 20-fold in the 1996-97 bull market by buying undervalued stocks such as Shenzhen Development Bank.
notes: Almost no public information about Luo Yi personally; she appears only as co-listed with Qiu Guogen. Approach via Chongyang Investment (Shanghai). Site is behind a qualified-investor gate; no published press email found.

name: Yen Chen Lilian
current_role: Chairwoman and Group CEO, Yulon Group (Yulon Motor), Taiwan
profile: Lilian Chen Yen (嚴陳莉蓮) is the widow of Yulon chairman Kenneth Yen (嚴凱泰), and took over leadership of Taiwan's Yulon automotive group after his death in 2018. She now steers its Nissan/Mitsubishi partnerships, EV contract manufacturing with Foxtron (Hon Hai), North American energy storage and the Yulon City mall in Xindian.
interesting_fact: In Dec 2025 Yulon sold its home-grown Luxgen brand to Foxtron (Hon Hai's EV JV) for NT$787.6m while keeping a ~43.8% stake in Foxtron.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she was a Taiwan women's national basketball player and captain of the Tai Yuen women's team; an alumna of Chinese Culture University's PE dept, she gave NT$10m in 2025 to fund scholarships and the men's basketball team there.
notes: Taiwanese, not mainland (Hurun lists 'China'). Email is Yulon Motor's spokesperson/company contact from exchange filings (spokesperson Cho Che-yu); verify on MOPS. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Long Daqiang
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (with wife Meng Liye), SolarSpace / Jiangsu Zhongrun Solar Technology (中润光能), Xuzhou
profile: Long Daqiang (龙大强, b. 1973) and his wife Meng Liye, both from Pei County, Jiangsu, moved from steel trading into solar in 2010, founding cell maker Zhongyu PV and then SolarSpace (中润光能). SolarSpace became the world's No.2 PV-cell maker by 2024 shipments (14.6% share) and in 2025 filed for a Hong Kong IPO, partly to fund a North Carolina cell plant.
interesting_fact: SolarSpace ranked second among global PV cell makers in 2024 with a 14.6% share and plans to use Hong Kong IPO proceeds to build a US cell factory in North Carolina (lease signed Jan 2025).
deep_cut_fact: A true grassroots story: after being laid off from Pei County's materials bureau in the 1990s, he started a steel business in the county building-materials market with 50,000 yuan of borrowed money, founding Peixian Tongda Building Materials in 2000 before meeting GCL and other solar firms through steel sales.
notes: Hurun 'Solar Space' = SolarSpace (中润光能/Zhongrun Guangneng), wealth shared with wife Meng Liye. Deep-cut story is from an eastmoney caifuhao (user-contributed) article citing online info; corroborate with the HKEX prospectus before use. No official company contact found online in this pass; check HKEX filing for IR details.

name: Meng Liye
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with husband Long Daqiang), Jiangsu SolarSpace (Zhongrun Guangneng, 中润光能)
profile: Born 1979 in Pei County, Jiangsu. With husband Long Daqiang she ran a steel-trading business, then entered solar (Zhongyu PV 2010, Zhongrun 2011). SolarSpace became a global top-5 solar-cell maker with a plant in Laos. The couple control ~50.6% of votes; after withdrawing a ChiNext IPO in 2024, it refiled for a Hong Kong listing in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: The couple had no solar background or advanced degrees. They learned about the industry from Jiangsu PV customers such as GCL while selling them steel, then grew SolarSpace into one of the world's largest cell producers.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering business she worked at the Pei County supply-and-marketing cooperative, then left to run the steel 'husband-and-wife shop'. In 2011 she co-founded Zhongrun Ltd, SolarSpace's predecessor, with a 70% direct stake.
notes: Hurun's 'Solar Space' is Jiangsu SolarSpace / 中润光能 (website solarspace.com, which did not render). No published personal or IR email was found; once the HK prospectus is live, check its IR contacts. Her husband Long Daqiang is the public face.

name: Wang Shirui
current_role: Founder & CEO, Medlinker (医联) Group; CEO of Future Doctor (未来医生) group
profile: Wang Shirui (王仕锐) founded Chengdu-based Medlinker in 2014 as a professional network for Chinese doctors, growing it into a unicorn backed by Tencent, Sequoia China and China Renaissance focused on internet hospitals and chronic-disease management. He also ran Tencent Trusted Doctors (later Future Doctor, merged into Medlinker) and now pushes the medical LLM MedGPT.
interesting_fact: Medlinker's MedGPT was billed as China's first medical large model approved to give diagnosis and treatment suggestions; Wang says most revenue comes from B2B clients for now.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a tech founder he trained as a dentist: he completed the 8-year combined bachelor/master/doctorate program at Sichuan University's West China School of Stomatology and was a research scholar at Harvard.
notes: Twice named to Fortune China 40 Under 40 (2016, 2018). Active in AI-in-medicine discussions (e.g. dialogue with Kevin Kelly). Chinese-language outreach via media@ is likely the best route.

name: Ye Delin
current_role: Chairman and President, New Pearl Group (新明珠集团), Foshan
profile: Ye Delin (叶德林, b. 1956, Foshan) built Guangdong's New Pearl Group into one of China's largest ceramic-tile makers. He ran the Mingzhu No.1 and No.2 factories from 1993, bought them out in 1998 and has chaired the group since. He and his wife Li Yao control ~88% of the company, which filed for a Shenzhen main-board IPO.
interesting_fact: He is a member of the executive committee of the All-China Federation of Industry and Commerce and vice-president of the China Building Materials Federation, and formerly chaired the Foshan Federation of Industry and Commerce for two terms.
deep_cut_fact: Before tiles, he spent 15 years (1975-1990) at the Nanzhuang hydropower station office, rising from worker to its director; he started work in 1974 as a laborer on the Nanzhuang commune construction team.
notes: IR email is from the 2023 IPO prospectus draft (board office handles disclosure/IR). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Li Yao
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Ye Delin) of New Pearl Group (Xinmingzhu), Foshan ceramic tiles maker
profile: Li Yao and her husband Ye Delin control New Pearl Group, a Foshan, Guangdong building-ceramics and tile maker founded in 1993 with production bases in Guangdong, Jiangxi and Chongqing. The couple jointly held about 86.67% of the company directly at end-2022. New Pearl's planned Shenzhen IPO has stalled since 2023.
interesting_fact: New Pearl is often described as a husband-and-wife company: Li Yao and Ye Delin directly held 86.67% of its equity at the end of 2022.
notes: Very private; husband Ye Delin (chairman/CEO, a former Nanzhuang town hydropower station head) is the public face. Approach via the company site. Avoid IPO/dividend controversies.

name: Xia Chongyao
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Ningbo Orient Wires & Cables Co. (东方电缆, SSE: 603606)
profile: Xia Chongyao (夏崇耀) controls Ningbo Orient Wires & Cables via Ningbo Orient Group; the company, founded in 1998 and listed in Shanghai in 2014, is one of China's leading makers of submarine power cables for offshore wind. He chairs the board and leads its push into deep-sea wind and overseas markets (UK subsidiary registered 2024).

deep_cut_fact: Orient Cable's umbilical cable is a national 'single champion' (单项冠军) product; Xia has framed it as replacing previously imported equipment for China's deep-sea oil and gas.
notes: Highly relevant to energy (offshore wind/HVDC subsea cables). IR email is from a 2022 company filing; verify current address in latest annual report. Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Wei Jinkun
current_role: Major shareholder (~19%) of Weaver Network Technology (泛微网络, SSE: 603039), maker of the e-cology OA platform
profile: Wei Jinkun (韦锦坤) is the second-largest shareholder of Shanghai-based Weaver Network, a collaboration/office-automation software firm founded in 2001 by Wei Lidong whose flagship product is e-cology; it listed in Shanghai in January 2017. His wealth comes from this stake. Little else is publicly documented about him.

notes: Matched via 'E-cology' = Weaver's flagship OA product; shareholder data from 10jqka (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/603039/holder.html). Relationship to founder Wei Lidong not confirmed. Very private; route would be via Weaver Network (weaver.com.cn) board secretary/IR.

name: Lou Xiaoqiang
current_role: Co-founder, President & COO of Pharmaron; CEO of Pharmaron Clinical
profile: Lou Xiaoqiang (Larry Lou) co-founded Beijing-based contract research/manufacturing group Pharmaron in 2004 with his brother Boliang Lou (chairman/CEO) and Zheng Bei. Pharmaron is listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong and serves global drugmakers with labs in China, the US and UK. He runs operations and the clinical services arm.
interesting_fact: Pharmaron grew from a Beijing chemistry lab founded in 2004 into a fully integrated R&D services platform with sites in China, the US and the UK, listed in both Shenzhen and Hong Kong.
deep_cut_fact: Before Pharmaron he was a tech entrepreneur: he founded and ran Beijing Biopass Technology, an information-security product company. He trained as a materials scientist (BS/MS, Beijing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics) and holds a CEIBS EMBA.

name: Zheng Bei
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Executive Vice President, Pharmaron Beijing (SZSE: 300759; HKEX: 3759)
profile: Zheng Bei (郑北) co-founded Pharmaron, a Beijing-based contract research, development and manufacturing organisation (CRO/CDMO), in 2004 with Boliang Lou and Larry Lou. She set up its administration, HR and accounting functions and leads its capacity build-out; her wealth comes from her Pharmaron stake, held jointly with Lou Xiaoqiang per Hurun.

name: Shen Bo
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Fenbushi Capital (Shanghai)
profile: Bo Shen co-founded Fenbushi Capital in 2015, one of Asia's earliest blockchain-focused VC firms (Vitalik Buterin was an early co-founder), and has been an early backer of Ethereum-ecosystem and Web3 projects. A Georgia Tech-trained engineer, he spent years in US and Chinese finance before moving into crypto, and was a co-founder of Invictus Innovations, the team behind BitShares.
