name: Ou Yaping
current_role: Non-executive director and co-founder, ZhongAn Online P&C Insurance; founder of Sinolink Worldwide
profile: Founded Hong Kong-listed Sinolink Worldwide (chairman 1997-2013), which built city-gas distributor Panva Gas and power business Enerchina. He then co-founded ZhongAn, China's first online-only insurer, with Alibaba's Jack Ma and Tencent's Pony Ma, chairing it until July 2023; his family remains ZhongAn's largest shareholder (~14.6%).
interesting_fact: He co-founded ZhongAn, China's first internet-only insurer, with Jack Ma (Alibaba) and Pony Ma (Tencent), and chaired it until resigning as chairman in July 2023 while staying on the board.
deep_cut_fact: An engineering-management graduate of Beijing Institute of Technology, he later became vice chairman of its board and a part-time professor there, per Sinolink's 2007 annual report.
notes: Energy angle: built Panva Gas (city gas) and Enerchina (power) via Sinolink. ZhongAn IR email comes from a reposted company press release; confirm on zhongan.com. No personal social accounts found.

name: Ouyang Yongyue
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shijiazhuang Shangtai Technology (SZ:001301)
profile: Born 1966, Ouyang is a carbon-materials engineer who built Shangtai Technology in Hebei into a major maker of graphite anode materials for lithium-ion batteries. He owns about 36.5% of the company, which listed in Shenzhen in 2022. H1 2026 revenue rose 33% to RMB 4.5bn.
interesting_fact: Shangtai runs an integrated anode model that does the power-hungry graphitization step in-house. In H1 2026 demand outran this integrated capacity, so it had to outsource some graphitization to keep up with orders.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Hunan University in 1988, Ouyang spent 12 years (1988-2000) as an engineer at the Shanghai Carbon Factory, then ran Shanghai Shangtai Carbon before building the anode business in Hebei.
notes: Low media profile. The published email is the board-secretary/IR contact from the company's 2026 interim report summary. He holds Australian permanent residency per filings.

name: Shi Mingda
current_role: Honorary chairman (and vice chairman) of Tongfu Microelectronics (002156.SZ); son Shi Lei is chairman & president
profile: Nanjing University physics graduate and engineer (b. 1945) who in 1990 took over the debt-ridden Nantong Transistor Factory and turned it into Tongfu Microelectronics, now the world's No.4 chip packaging & test group. Key steps: a 1997 JV with Fujitsu and the 2016 purchase of 85% of AMD's Suzhou and Penang test plants; today Tongfu packages most of AMD's chips and is expanding advanced packaging for AI/HPC.
interesting_fact: Over 80% of AMD's products are packaged and tested at the Tongfu-AMD joint venture; Shi says AMD credits Tongfu with a role in its historic overtaking of Intel, and half of the Suzhou plant's orders now come from non-AMD customers.
deep_cut_fact: The Nantong Transistor Factory he rescued stood on the original site of China's first normal school, founded by industrialist Zhang Jian, whom Shi cites as his inspiration; for his 80th birthday in 2025 he wrote a memoir essay titled 'A lifetime of microcircuits, a patriotic chip' (一生微电路，一颗报国'芯').
notes: Hurun lists wealth shared with son Shi Lei (current chairman). Strong AI/data-center angle via AMD advanced packaging. Gave a long interview to Shanghai Securities News in Feb 2026, so open to press; approach via board secretary office (Jiang Shu).

name: Shi Lei
current_role: Chairman & President, Tongfu Microelectronics (TFME, SZSE: 002156), since Jan 2024
profile: Son of Tongfu founder Shi Mingda (now honorary chairman), Shi Lei (b. 1972, Fudan PhD) ran parent Nantong Huada Microelectronics before joining Tongfu in 2008 as director/president, becoming vice chairman in 2018 and chairman in 2024. Tongfu is one of China's largest chip packaging & test (OSAT) firms and a key advanced-packaging partner of AMD.
interesting_fact: In 2016 Tongfu (then Nantong Fujitsu Microelectronics) bought 85% of AMD's assembly and test plants in Suzhou, China and Penang, Malaysia, moving ~1,700 AMD staff into the JV; it remains a core packaging partner for AMD CPUs/GPUs.
deep_cut_fact: Shi Lei holds a Fudan University doctorate, is a recognised State Council special-allowance expert, directs Jiangsu's key laboratory for IC advanced packaging and testing, and has served as rotating chairman of the national IC packaging & test industry innovation alliance.
notes: Hurun lists wealth shared with father Shi Mingda. Best route is via Tongfu's board-secretary office (tfme_stock@tfme.com; board secretary Jiang Shu). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Gai Lujiang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Shanghai Iluvatar CoreX Semiconductor (天数智芯; HKEX: 9903)
profile: A finance professional and investor representative appointed chairman and CEO of Iluvatar CoreX (founded 2015) after its 2022-23 management changes. Iluvatar designs general-purpose GPUs for AI training (Tiangai) and inference (Zhikai) as domestic alternatives in China. It listed in Hong Kong in January 2026 with a retail tranche oversubscribed more than 400 times.
interesting_fact: Iluvatar CoreX was the first Chinese general-purpose GPU (GPGPU) maker to gain HKEX listing approval; it debuted on 8 Jan 2026 and opened about 31% above its HK$144.6 issue price.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a Chinese GPU chief, Gai is not a chip engineer: he trained in finance and worked at BDO China, PwC and Deloitte before representing investors on Iluvatar's board and taking the top job in 2023.
notes: Name is romanised as both Gai Lujiang and Ge Lujiang (盖鲁江). Low personal profile; route via Iluvatar PR. Chinese sources say he studied at Central University of Finance and Economics, but this comes from a single third-party profile and is not verified.

name: Dai Weimin
current_role: Founder, Chairman, President and CEO, VeriSilicon Microelectronics (688521.SH), Shanghai
profile: Dai Weimin (Wayne Dai) earned his BS and PhD in EECS at UC Berkeley, taught computer engineering at UC Santa Cruz and founded chip-design-software firms Ultima and Celestry (bought by Cadence in 2002). He founded VeriSilicon in Shanghai in 2001, building it into a major custom-silicon and semiconductor-IP supplier listed on Shanghai's STAR Market.
interesting_fact: VeriSilicon is a 'silicon platform as a service' company: it licenses processor IP (GPU, NPU, video, display) and designs custom chips for other firms rather than selling chips under its own brand.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a chip entrepreneur he spent 17 years in academia at UC Santa Cruz (1988-2005), rising from tutor to full professor of computer engineering, and overlapped his professorship with founding Ultima (1995) and VeriSilicon (2001).
notes: Known in English as Wayne Dai (Wei-Ming Dai). Speaks frequently at industry events (e.g. on chiplets and AI chips), English-fluent - a plausible podcast guest; route via IR or company news enquiry.

name: Luo Weiwei
current_role: Founder, chairwoman and CEO, Innoscience (Suzhou) Technology (HKEX: 2577); also leads Micro LED startup Xingyue Semiconductor
profile: Dr. Weiwei Luo, China's 'Queen of Gallium Nitride', holds an applied-math PhD from Massey University (NZ) and spent ~15 years at a NASA-affiliated institute before founding Innoscience in 2015; it built China's first 8-inch GaN-on-silicon line and listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024. In 2022 she also founded Micro LED startup Xingyue Semiconductor.

notes: Highly relevant to data-center power (GaN for AI server PSUs, NVIDIA 800V DC). Speaks English; approach via Innoscience corporate channels.

name: Zhu Shuangquan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Hubei Dinglong Holding (鼎龙股份, 300054.SZ); also Chairman of Wuhan Zhongyuan Huadian (300018.SZ) since Dec 2025

Dinglong began in printing/imaging consumables and became a key Chinese supplier of semiconductor materials: CMP polishing pads and slurries, display materials, photoresists and advanced-packaging materials. name: Michael Tojner
current_role: Founder/CEO, Montana Tech Components and Global Equity Partners (Vienna); chairman of supervisory board, Montana Aerospace; major shareholder of Varta
profile: Austrian serial entrepreneur (b. 1966) who bought microbattery maker Varta in 2007 for ~$40m and floated it in 2017; his Montana Tech Components group also built Montana Aerospace and Aluflexpack (sold 2024). name: Manfred Gorvy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hanover Acceptances Limited (London)
profile: South African-born (1938) chartered accountant based in London who founded the private investment group Hanover Acceptances in 1974. The group focuses on real estate (Dorrington, African Realty Trust), agribusiness (Letaba citrus in South Africa) and venture capital (Fresh Capital); it formerly backed drinks bottler Refresco Gerber.

name: Sanjeev Shah
current_role: Chairman, Everest Food Products Pvt Ltd (Everest Spices), Mumbai
profile: Sanjeev Shah chairs Everest, the Mumbai spice brand his father Vadilal Shah registered in 1967 with three masalas sold from a 200 sq ft shop. He joined in 1981 and built the sales and distribution network; brother Rajiv joined in 1992. Everest calls itself India's largest maker of pure and blended spices, exports to 80+ countries and has added herb seasonings and ginger/garlic pastes since 2021.
interesting_fact: Everest's first three products in 1967 were Milk Masala, Garam Masala and Tea Masala; by 2005 it held about 30% of India's branded spice market.
deep_cut_fact: The year after Sanjeev joined to build distribution, Everest held its first dealer meet, 'Everest Ki Yadgaar Raat' (1982), and in 1983 launched its first TV ad on Doordarshan with producer Harish Bhimani.
notes: Private, low-profile family; very few interviews. Corporate contact form/customer-care email on the website is the only published route. Avoid the 2024 Singapore/Hong Kong ethylene oxide recall topic.

name: Stefania Triva
current_role: President & CEO and largest shareholder, Copan Italia S.p.A. (Brescia)
profile: CEO and ~48% owner of Copan, founded by her father Giorgio in 1979. Her late brother Daniele invented the flocked swab there in 2003, making Copan a world leader in diagnostic swabs and lab automation. She became CEO in 2014, led it through the Covid demand surge, and keeps it family-owned despite buyout offers.
interesting_fact: Flocked swabs made up more than 80% of Copan's $445M revenue in 2021. The Covid-19 testing boom made Triva a billionaire.
deep_cut_fact: In 2023 President Mattarella named her a Cavaliere del Lavoro (Knight of Labour) for the medical-devices industry. She started out as a teenager in the 1980s packing boxes at her father's company.
notes: info@copangroup.com is Copan's general address, published in a 2020 press statement signed by Triva. Copan is private and keeps a low profile; the best route is the corporate contacts page. Copan is now based in Brescia. The box-packing detail comes from a Forbes profile reprinted in Forbes Middle East ('Nose for Business', 2022).

name: Bruce Springsteen
current_role: Singer-songwriter; leader of the E Street Band (Land of Hope and Dreams American Tour, spring 2026)
profile: New Jersey rock musician who built a fortune over five decades of recording and touring with the E Street Band: more than 140 million albums sold, 20 Grammys, an Oscar and a special Tony. In 2021 he sold his recorded-music and publishing catalog to Sony for a reported ~$500M. He is still touring, with a 20-date US arena and stadium tour in spring 2026.
interesting_fact: He and the E Street Band came up playing Jersey Shore clubs, most famously Asbury Park's Stone Pony. His 2021 catalog sale to Sony was one of the largest ever for a single artist.
deep_cut_fact: His first known recording came in May 1966 with his teenage band the Castiles: a demo at Mr. Music in New Jersey, paid for by manager Tex Vinyard, of 'Baby I' and 'That's What You Get', co-written with George Theiss. 'Baby I' was finally released 50 years later on the 2016 album Chapter and Verse.

public_contacts.value: Shore Fire Media (Bruce Springsteen press page)

notes: Media requests go through his longtime publicist Shore Fire Media (Brooklyn). He rarely does business podcasts but did host the Renegades podcast with Barack Obama (Spotify, 2021). Sources disagree on where the 1966 demo was recorded (Toms River vs Bricktown).

name: Yu Lili
current_role: Director, Changsha Jingjia Microelectronics (SZSE: 300474); stepped down as vice chair in Aug 2024
profile: Yu Lili (b. 1968) is a co-founding shareholder and long-time leader of Jingjia Microelectronics, the Changsha company best known as one of China's first domestic GPU designers (JM-series chips), listed in Shenzhen in 2016. Her husband Zeng Wanhui is chairman; she remains a board director, and the company is now pushing into GPGPU and edge-AI SoC chips.
interesting_fact: Jingjia is one of China's pioneering home-grown GPU makers; in 2025 its subsidiary launched the CH37 edge-AI SoC rated at 64 TOPS (INT8), extending it from graphics into AI compute.
deep_cut_fact: Per Jingjia's 2025 annual report, she has a high-school education and from 1988 to 2006 worked as manager of a Guangzhou auto-parts trading business and then deputy office director at Beijing Xinshenjian Economic & Technology Development Co. before taking a leadership role in the group in 2006.
notes: Very private, non-executive director; no interviews found. Chairman Zeng Wanhui (her husband) is the company's public face. Jingjia's GPU/AI-chip work is relevant to data-center themes, but it has strong defence-sector ties. Chinese-language outreach via board secretary office.

name: Huh Jae-myung
current_role: Private investor; former CEO and largest shareholder of Iljin Materials (now Lotte Energy Materials); still holds stakes in Iljin Display and Iljin Steel
profile: Second son of Iljin Group founder Huh Jin-kyu. As CEO and 53.3% owner of Iljin Materials he built a leading maker of copper foil for EV batteries, then sold the stake to Lotte Chemical for 2.7 trillion won (agreed 2022, closed 2023). He then founded investment firm Company H, stepping down as its head in 2025.
interesting_fact: He sold his 53.3% stake in Iljin Materials, a world-leading maker of copper foil for EV batteries, to Lotte Chemical for about 2.7 trillion won (about $1.9bn). The deal closed in 2023 and the company was renamed Lotte Energy Materials.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Iljin in February 2023 he set up a private investment firm, Company H (an LLC), as its sole executive. In July 2024 it signed a strategic partnership with NH Investment & Securities to co-invest in acquisition and project-financing deals.
notes: Romanised as Heo Jae-myeong in some outlets. Very low public profile, and no published contacts found. Avoid family topics: reports mention little contact with his brother. Forbes lists him as a former billionaire.

name: Li Zhixiong
current_role: Director, Shenzhen Longsys Electronics (江波龙, SZSE ChiNext: 301308)
profile: Li Zhixiong (李志雄) is a long-time director and major shareholder of Shenzhen Longsys Electronics, a memory and storage maker he joined in 2004 after research stints. Longsys bought the Lexar brand from Micron in 2017 and listed on ChiNext in 2022; Li still held ~3.9% after share sales completed in June 2026.
interesting_fact: Lexar, the U.S. consumer storage brand Longsys acquired from Micron in 2017, became a global partner of the Argentina national football team.
notes: Low public profile; not the CEO (Chairman/CEO is Cai Huabo). Holding reduced to 3.9% per June 2026 filing (stockstar/10jqka). Best route: Longsys marketing/IR.

name: Kavita Singhania
current_role: Shareholder (~5%) in J.K. Cement Ltd; director of Express Infrastructure (Chennai real-estate developer)
profile: Kavita Yadupati Singhania holds a stake in listed J.K. Cement, run until his 2020 death by her husband Yadupati Singhania as chairman & MD. She briefly served as a non-executive director of J.K. Cement (2020-21) and is a director of Chennai developer Express Infrastructure; she has no operating role in the cement business.
interesting_fact: She is a granddaughter of newspaper baron Ramnath Goenka, founder of the Indian Express media group.
notes: Low public profile. Stake (~5.01% as of June 2023) and 2020-21 directorship per MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/KAVITA-Y-SINGHANIA-A0CFTB). Only route found is via J.K. Cement corporate/IR channels.

name: Michael Rees
current_role: Co-President and board member, Blue Owl Capital; Head of GP Strategic Capital platform
profile: Rees spent 2001-09 at Lehman Brothers (head of asset management strategy 2003-06), moved to Neuberger Berman in its 2009 management buyout as first COO of its alternatives unit, and founded Dyal Capital there, pioneering buying minority stakes in private equity firms. Dyal merged with Owl Rock in 2021 to form NYSE-listed Blue Owl, where he co-presides and runs GP Strategic Capital.
interesting_fact: Dyal/Blue Owl GP Strategic Capital has bought minority stakes in 60+ private equity firms and runs a sports fund with pieces of the NBA's Phoenix Suns, Sacramento Kings and Atlanta Hawks.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he holds a BS in mechanical engineering and a BA in political science from the University of Pittsburgh plus MIT master's degrees in mechanical engineering and technology policy; his family backs the Rees Chancellor Scholarship program at Pitt. He calls himself a proud Pittsburgh 'Yinzer'.
notes: Has done podcasts (Capital Allocators ep. 278, CAIS Live) and a PEI 'Off-duty' interview on how Dyal got its name and Guns N' Roses (https://www.privateequityinternational.com/off-duty-blue-owls-michael-rees-on-how-dyal-got-its-name-guns-n-roses-and-being-a-yinzer/, paywalled). Blue Owl is a major data-center financier, relevant to the podcast. Route via Blue Owl media.

name: Chen Wenping
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Sailvan Times Co., Ltd. (赛维时代, SZSE ChiNext: 301381)
profile: Chen Wenping (陈文平) founded Shenzhen-based Sailvan Times in 2012 as a cross-border e-commerce seller and built it into a brand incubator selling fashion and lifestyle products to overseas consumers via Amazon and other platforms. Sailvan listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in July 2023; Chen is the controlling shareholder with roughly 37% and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Sailvan describes itself as a technology-driven 'smart commerce platform' organised as a 'small front-end + big middle platform' structure, combining product design, brand incubation and supply-chain integration for global online shoppers.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal biography online in English. Country blank in input but he and the company are mainland China (Shenzhen). Route via Sailvan investor relations / board secretary.

name: Arvind Nithrakashyap
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Rubrik, Inc. (NYSE: RBRK)
profile: IIT Madras (1995) and UMass Amherst (MS 1997) computer scientist who spent years at Oracle, where he co-founded the Exadata database platform, then led real-time ad infrastructure at Rocket Fuel. In 2013/14 he co-founded data-security company Rubrik, which IPO'd in 2024; his stake makes him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: At Oracle he co-founded Exadata, now one of Oracle's flagship database/storage platforms, before leaving to co-found Rubrik.
deep_cut_fact: At Rocket Fuel he architected the real-time bidding engine, leading ~30 engineers on an ad platform handling 50 billion requests a day at 50-60 ms latency; IIT Madras later gave him its Distinguished Alumnus Award.
notes: Low-profile technical founder but does keynotes/panels; route via Rubrik PR (Meghan Fintland, Head of Global PR, listed on releases).

name: Gina Vecchiarelli
current_role: Co-heir and principal shareholder (with sister Terry Leprino) of Leprino Foods, Denver; no public executive role
profile: Daughter of James Leprino, who built his father's 1950 Denver cheese shop into the world's largest mozzarella maker (supplier to Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's). After his death in June 2025, she and her sister inherited a ~90% stake in the private company. She keeps a very low profile; her father said in 2016 she ran a program for Make-A-Wish.
interesting_fact: Leprino Foods makes more than 1 billion pounds of cheese a year; her father pioneered the technology to manufacture pizza mozzarella at industrial scale.

public_contacts.value: No email published; Leprino Corporate Communications media line 720-295-4815 (company press line)

notes: Very private, no public footprint found. Forbes says her husband Dan Vecchiarelli became chairman/CEO c.2023, but Leprino's own site names Lance FitzSimmons President & CEO (Oct 2024) and does not mention Vecchiarelli - verify before outreach. Only route is via Leprino corporate communications.

name: Terry Leprino
current_role: President, Leprino Foods Company Foundation; board director and co-owner, Leprino Foods (Denver)
profile: Terry Leprino and her sister Gina Vecchiarelli inherited about 90% of Denver-based Leprino Foods, the world's largest mozzarella maker (est. $3.6bn revenue; supplies Domino's, Pizza Hut, Papa John's), after their father James Leprino died in June 2025. She spent a decade as the company's marketing director, sits on its board and now leads the corporate foundation.
interesting_fact: Leprino Foods, founded by her grandfather in 1950, makes more than 1 billion pounds of cheese a year; her father pioneered the technology to make pizza cheese at industrial scale.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a bachelor's from Arizona State and a master's in biblical counseling from Colorado Christian University, where she has served as a trustee for over a decade. She also sits on the board of the Issachar Urban Leadership Center.
notes: Very private family business with no named PR contact. The media centre directs press to Corporate Communications by phone, and the contact form has a 'Media' option. The CCU trustee bio URL came up in search results but returned 404 when fetched directly.

name: Holger Timm
current_role: Chairman of the management board, Berliner Effektengesellschaft AG; CEO, Tradegate AG Wertpapierhandelsbank
profile: A Berlin stockbroker who founded Berliner Effektengesellschaft (BEG) in 1986 and remains its majority shareholder. BEG holds about 57% of Tradegate AG, which runs the Tradegate trading platform (launched 2000) and co-owns Tradegate BSX exchange with Deutsche Börse; BEG also holds a stake in Quirin Privatbank.
interesting_fact: Tradegate, launched in 2000 as one of the first electronic trading systems for German online brokers, became a full exchange (Tradegate BSX) co-owned with Deutsche Börse and is now a key venue for retail traders and neobrokers; Timm chairs its exchange council.
notes: Low media profile. BEG ownership ~56.6% of Tradegate per 2025 half-year report (Forbes' 88% figure refers to his stake in BEG). Generic company inboxes only.

name: Simón Pedro Barceló Vadell
current_role: Executive chairman and CEO, Barceló Group (Barceló Corporación Empresarial), Palma de Mallorca
profile: Born in Palma in 1966, he studied law at the University of the Balearic Islands and joined the family tourism group in 1993. He co-chaired it with his cousin Simón Barceló Tous from 2000 and now leads it alone after his cousin's age-limit retirement in 2025. The group, founded in 1931, runs 300+ hotels in about 30 countries plus the Ávoris travel business.
interesting_fact: Barceló started in 1931 as a bus/transport company in Mallorca and opened its first hotel only in 1962. Hosteltur named Simón Pedro Barceló its 2023 Tourism Personality of the Year, marking 30 years at the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he was a senator for the Partido Popular from 1989 to 1993, entering the Spanish Senate in his early twenties.
notes: He gives Spanish-media interviews fairly often (Hosteltur, Exceltur forums) and is a former president of the Exceltur tourism lobby. The best route is the group communications office.

name: Jin Xin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (~40%), Dajin Heavy Industry (SZ: 002487)
profile: Jin Xin founded the predecessor of Dajin Heavy Industry in 2001; it moved from building steel structures into power-boiler steelwork (2004) and wind towers (2007) and listed in Shenzhen in 2010 as China's first A-share wind tower/pile maker. Dajin is now a leading supplier of offshore wind monopiles to Europe and is expanding into heavy-lift shipping, marshalling ports and wind-farm development.
interesting_fact: Dajin was reported as the No.1 supplier of European offshore wind monopiles by sales, with share rising from 18.5% in 2024 to 29.1% in H1 2025, and the only Asia-Pacific supplier to deliver monopiles to Europe in batches.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 2001 at age 34 with three production lines he bought himself (H-beam, shot-blasting and colour-plate lines worth RMB 4.8m), backed by his former employer Panpan Group, which supplied RMB 8m of panels and exited a year later.
notes: Highly relevant for an energy podcast (offshore wind supply chain). Jin is non-executive chairman and keeps a low media profile; board secretary/VP Ge Xin handles investor communications. Company filed for a Hong Kong listing in Sept 2025.

name: Tang Ye
current_role: Chairman (since 2007) and CEO, Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) Electronic Technology (SSE STAR: 688188)
profile: Tang Ye co-founded Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) Electronic Technology in September 2007 in Shanghai's Zizhu high-tech zone, near Shanghai Jiao Tong University, where he earned a master's in engineering management. The company makes control systems and software for fiber laser cutting machines and listed on the STAR Market in August 2019; he remains its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: Friendess was one of China's first private companies developing fiber laser cutting control systems and now supplies control systems to more than 400 laser equipment makers.
notes: Low international profile; communicates in Chinese. Investor posts relaying a SJTU video interview say the five co-founders took tiny salaries early on and never raised outside capital, but this is unverified so it is not used as a fact.

name: Vadim Novinsky
current_role: Founder/beneficiary of Smart Holding Group (Ukraine; ownership contested after 2022 trust transfer); former Ukrainian MP; protodeacon of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church
profile: Novinsky was born in Russia in 1963, rose through Lukoil's North-West division in the 1990s, then bought Ukrainian metallurgy assets and co-founded Smart Holding in 2006, which holds a minority stake in Metinvest. He became a Ukrainian citizen in 2012 and was an MP from 2013 to 2022. He left Ukraine in 2023 and was reportedly granted Serbian citizenship in 2026.
interesting_fact: An active patron of the Ukrainian Orthodox Church, he was reportedly ordained a deacon by Metropolitan Onufriy in 2020 and serves as a protodeacon.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in aviation, not metals: he graduated in 1985 from the Leningrad Academy of Civil Aviation in engineering management systems.
notes: HIGH RISK, not recommended for outreach. He is under Ukrainian NSDC sanctions (Dec 2022/Jan 2023) and was charged in absentia with high treason in January 2025; he calls the charges politically motivated. He lives outside Ukraine (reportedly Serbian citizenship, 2026). Control of Smart Holding is disputed after the Justice Ministry cancelled the trust transfer. No published contact found.

name: Konstantin Nikolaev
current_role: Private investor; owner of La Madonnina winery (Bolgheri, Tuscany); former co-owner of Globaltrans/N-Trans and Global Ports
profile: Russian-born logistics entrepreneur (b. 1971, Dnipropetrovsk) who co-founded Severstaltrans in 1996 with Nikita Mishin, Andrei Filatov and Alexei Mordashov, later N-Trans, which grew into Globaltrans (Russia's largest private rail operator) and Global Ports. He sold out of the ports in 2017 and completed his exit from all Russian business in January 2024; the Tuscan winery is now his main focus.
interesting_fact: He is one of the co-founders of the Moscow School of Management Skolkovo, described as Russia's first business school; he also was an early investor in US-based American Ethane.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Moscow State University and wrote his thesis on Plato's Republic, then started his logistics career as a forwarding agent at Murmansk port coordinating ship loading.
notes: Sensitive profile: under Ukrainian sanctions (2023) and has had press coverage tied to US politics; avoid those topics. Citizen of Malta per Wikipedia. No published personal/office contact found; any approach would likely be via the La Madonnina winery or a lawyer/spokesperson.

name: Nikita Mishin
current_role: Founder, Dar Charitable Foundation for the Promotion of Education; private investor (former Globaltrans co-owner)
profile: Nikita Mishin (b. 1971) built his fortune in Russian freight logistics with partners Konstantin Nikolaev and Andrei Filatov, co-founding rail operator Globaltrans and port group Global Ports. He exited ports in 2017 and sold his Globaltrans stake around 2024; UK-based, he now devotes himself largely to education philanthropy through his Dar foundation.
interesting_fact: His Dar foundation opened Moscow's New School in 2017 with needs-blind admission and fees about half those of other private schools; it gets roughly 600 applicants for ~48 entry places a year.
deep_cut_fact: He studied philosophy at Moscow State University, earning a degree that qualified him to teach or research the subject, and has said: 'I was never absolutely happy being just an entrepreneur.' He reportedly still sits in on New School classes via Zoom.
notes: Best angle is education philanthropy (Dar / New School). Dar foundation is based in Moscow; he lives in the UK (dual UK citizenship since 2024 per Forbes). Wikipedia also notes Cypriot citizenship (2015).

name: Yang Ying
current_role: Largest shareholder (~34%) and co-controller of Xiamen Amoytop Biotech (特宝生物, SSE STAR 688278)
profile: Investor in Xiamen Amoytop Biotech, a Xiamen-based maker of recombinant protein and long-acting modified drugs (e.g. Pegbing peginterferon for hepatitis B, Yipeisheng). Forbes lists her as a director and says her husband Lan Chun was chairman; Sun Li is now chairman/GM. She holds about 33.9% (2025 Q1 report); Amoytop's 2025 revenue grew ~31% to RMB 3.7B with net profit ~RMB 1.04B.
interesting_fact: Amoytop, founded in the mid-1990s, has never seen its controlling holders (Yang Ying, Sun Li and concert party) sell a share since its 2020 STAR Market IPO, and they pledged not to reduce holdings for five years.
notes: Extremely low profile; no personal bio found online and she is not alive-confirmed by any recent personal news (still listed as top shareholder in 2025 filings). Common name - many unrelated academics named Yang Ying. Approach via Amoytop's company office/board secretary.

name: Lou Zhongfu
current_role: Co-founder and honorary chair, Guangsha Holding Group (Hangzhou); son Lou Ming is chairman
profile: Dongyang, Zhejiang native (b. 1954) who rose from construction worker to head the collective Dongyang construction company in 1984 and built it into Guangsha, a Hangzhou-based construction, real-estate and media conglomerate. He handed the chairmanship to his son Lou Ming; in 2021 Dongyang state capital took control of listed Zhejiang Guangsha.
interesting_fact: He joined Dongyang No. 3 Construction Company in 1973 as a worker and rose via materials-department head to general manager, the business that became Guangsha.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988 he was named a national 'collective construction entrepreneur of the new era', and in 1997 a national outstanding enterprise manager.
notes: Not a good outreach target: detained by CCDI in late 2014/2015 in connection with the Ling Jihua case and named in a 2022 bribery trial; no recent public appearances found (alive status not confirmed after 2022). Family lost control of listed Zhejiang Guangsha in 2021.

name: Clemens Toennies
current_role: Managing partner (Geschäftsführender Gesellschafter), Premium Food Group (formerly Tönnies Holding), Rheda-Wiedenbrück
profile: Trained butcher who co-founded Tönnies with brother Bernd in 1971 and built it into Germany's largest meat processor; he owns about 45%. Rebranded in 2025 as Premium Food Group (~€8bn revenue, ~22,000 staff) to diversify beyond meat, with son Max increasingly taking over management. He turned 70 in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Chaired the supervisory board of football club FC Schalke 04 from 2001 to 2020; the company HQ in Rheda-Wiedenbrück even has its own football pitch with heated turf.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he wanted to become a radio and TV mechanic rather than a butcher; he was just 15 when the company was registered with his brother and needed his parents' signature. His parents' shop processed only seven pigs a week.
notes: Press email is head of corporate communications as published in a June 2020 press release; may be outdated post-2025 rebrand. Avoid Schalke 2019-20 controversy topics. Born 27 May 1956, fifth of six children.

name: Daniel Hager
current_role: Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Hager Group (Hager SE); President of ZVEI (German Electro & Digital Industry Association) since May 2026
profile: Third-generation family owner of Hager Group, the Franco-German maker of electrical installation, energy-distribution and building-automation products (brands Hager, Berker, E3/DC; 13,000+ staff). He joined in 2003, was CEO from 2008 to Nov 2023, then became supervisory board chairman; in May 2026 he was elected ZVEI president with energy transition as a priority.
interesting_fact: Hager sees the firm as straddling two cultures: 'We are perceived as a French company in France and as a German company in Germany' — and sums up its strategy as 'The future is electric.'
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business in 2003 he worked outside it: first as a project manager at Eaton Electric, then at wind-farm developer Plambeck Neue Energien — an early renewables stint fitting today's E3/DC home-storage business.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (electrification, home batteries via E3/DC, ZVEI energy-transition agenda). Studied economics in Brussels and Paris. Press contacts listed on May 2026 Hager release.

name: Philip Hager
current_role: Family shareholder of Hager SE (Blieskastel, Germany) per Forbes; current board role not confirmed
profile: Forbes lists 'Philip & family Hager' as major shareholders of Hager SE, the family-owned German maker of electrical installation, energy-distribution and building-automation products (brands Hager, Berker, E3/DC; ~13,000 staff). The firm was founded in 1955 by Peter Hager and sons Oswald and Hermann.
interesting_fact: Hager Group owns E3/DC, a maker of home battery-storage and energy-management systems, linking the family firm to the energy-transition theme.
notes: Could not confirm which family member 'Philip/Philipp Hager' is: a Philip Hager appears on a 2016 Hager annual-report supervisory-board page, while recent reports name Peter Hager (son of co-founder Hermann) as shareholder/board member. Possible mix-up. Very private; route via Hager Group corporate communications.

name: family Hager
current_role: Hager family owns Hager Group (Hager SE), Blieskastel, Germany; Daniel Hager (3rd generation) chairs the Supervisory Board since Dec 2023; Philipp/Peter Hager are shareholders/board members
profile: The Hager family owns Hager Group, a Franco-German maker of electrical installation, energy distribution, cable management and building-automation products (brands Hager, Berker, E3/DC) with 3.5bn+ in revenue and 13,000+ staff. Daniel Hager was CEO 2008-2023 and handed operations to Sabine Busse, becoming Supervisory Board chairman.
interesting_fact: Hager Group owns E3/DC, a German home battery-storage maker, putting a 1950s-era electrical-fittings family firm squarely in the energy-transition business; the group runs twin hubs in Blieskastel (Germany) and Obernai (France).
deep_cut_fact: Besides chairing the supervisory board, Daniel Hager heads the Board of Trustees of the Peter und Luise Hager Foundation, the family's charitable foundation.
notes: Forbes lists this as 'Philip & family Hager'. Daniel Hager is the most public family member and has given interviews on Franco-German identity and family business (Tharawat magazine). Energy angle: E3/DC storage and energy-management business. Press contact Markus Goegele (Hager Group).

name: Robert Toennies
current_role: 50% shareholder, Tönnies Group (operating at holding level as Premium Food Group since Jan 2025), Rheda-Wiedenbrück
profile: Son of Tönnies co-founder Bernd Tönnies (d. 1994), Robert inherited a stake in Germany's largest meat processor, cofounded in 1971 by his father and uncle Clemens, and holds 50% of the group. The business, rebranded at holding level as Premium Food Group in 2025, has ~€8bn revenue and ~22,000 staff across meat, convenience, plant-based alternatives, pet food and logistics.
interesting_fact: From 1 January 2025 the Tönnies holding operates as the Premium Food Group, signalling a shift beyond meat into convenience, ingredients and plant-based alternatives; Robert was named among the shareholders backing the strategy.
notes: Very private; no personal accounts found. Group press office speaks mainly for the Clemens/Maximilian side; Robert has historically communicated via lawyers. Long-running family shareholder dispute is a sensitive topic — avoid. Group's energy/environmental management contact also listed on the same page.

name: Vitaly Orlov
current_role: CEO, co-founder and sole owner, Norebo Holding (Murmansk, Russia)
profile: Murmansk-born (1965) Orlov co-founded Norebo, Russia's largest vertically integrated seafood company, after starting in the late 1990s by supplying used trawlers to Russian fishermen in exchange for fish. Norebo has spent ~$600m buying fishing companies and catches ~400,000 tons of cod, haddock and pollock a year; since 2022 he has also bought shipyards and port terminals.
interesting_fact: He moved to Norway in 1996 and lived there until 2014, then gave up his Norwegian citizenship when he moved back to Murmansk.
deep_cut_fact: His English skills launched his career: after working in the fleet he joined the Sevryba fishing authority's export-contracts department, then in 1993 joined Swedish seafood exporter Scansea International's Murmansk office before moving to its Norway office in 1996.
notes: Sensitive: Norebo was sanctioned by the EU (May 2025) and Norway (July 2025); Orlov is suing Norway and The Barents Observer (defamation, London). Expect a guarded, lawyered response; contact via Norebo media office.

name: Richard Teets Jr
current_role: Co-founder and former director of Steel Dynamics (retired from board May 2026; retired as President/COO of Steel Operations 2016)
profile: Mechanical engineer Richard 'Dick' Teets left Nucor with Keith Busse and Mark Millett to co-found Fort Wayne-based Steel Dynamics in 1993, taking it public in 1996. He ran its steelmaking divisions as EVP and President/COO of Steel Operations until 2016, then served on the board until May 2026. He holds roughly 3% of the company.
interesting_fact: Steel Dynamics, which he co-founded in 1993 as an electric-arc-furnace mini-mill startup, became one of the largest US steel producers and metals recyclers.
deep_cut_fact: He began in the late 1970s as a mechanical engineer at J&L Steel and at Nucor supervised construction of the first thin-cast slab steel plant; he is a past AIST president, received AIME Honorary Membership (2017) and the SMA's Iverson-Selig Award, and helped set up AIST Foundation scholarships.
notes: Retired from all Steel Dynamics roles as of May 2026; company IR is only an indirect route. Active in AIST (Association for Iron & Steel Technology) circles.

name: Hugo Ribeiro
current_role: Controlling shareholder, Amaggi (Brazilian agribusiness group), alongside Blairo Maggi and Itamar Locks
profile: Hugo Ribeiro is the son-in-law of Lucia Maggi, who co-founded Amaggi with her late husband André Maggi. Amaggi is one of Brazil's largest soybean and grain producers and traders (farming, logistics, energy); Ribeiro is one of its controlling family shareholders with Blairo Maggi and Itamar Locks. He keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Ribeiro previously served as president of the board of an Amaggi-linked research institute dedicated to developing more sustainable soybean varieties (per Forbes).
notes: Very private; almost no press coverage under his own name. Amaggi also generates hydropower in Mato Grosso, a possible energy angle. Best route is Amaggi's communications office.

name: Anne Dinning
current_role: Managing Director and Executive Committee member, D. E. Shaw group
profile: Seattle-born computer scientist (UW BS, NYU Courant PhD) who joined D. E. Shaw in 1990 as a quant researcher building models for Japanese stocks, and has been on the executive committee running the firm day to day since 2002. Her stake in the quant giant underpins her fortune; she has given over $300M to her Corabelle Lumps Foundation and serves on the boards of Robin Hood and Math for America.
interesting_fact: When she joined D. E. Shaw in 1990 the firm reportedly had about 20 employees, working in a loft with unfinished ceilings and exposed pipes.
deep_cut_fact: Her UW senior thesis was a text editor designed for DeafBlind users, built with Prof. Richard Ladner; she later co-endowed (with husband Michael Wolf) a UW professorship named for Ladner.
notes: Low public profile but speaks on women in CS/STEM (Code.org board, MIT EECS advisory board). Best route is D. E. Shaw corporate communications or via her CS-education philanthropy.

name: Edwin Soeryadjaya
current_role: Co-founder and President Commissioner, PT Saratoga Investama Sedaya (also President Commissioner of Merdeka Copper Gold)
profile: Son of Astra founder William Soeryadjaya; USC business graduate who joined Astra in 1978 and led its restructuring and IPO. After the family lost Astra in the 1990s, he co-founded Saratoga with Sandiaga Uno (1997-98), building stakes in Adaro, Tower Bersama, Merdeka Copper Gold and ~40 firms. His son Michael now runs Saratoga.
interesting_fact: He was one of the consortium (with his father, Garibaldi Thohir, Sandiaga Uno and Teddy Rachmat) that bought into Adaro in 2005, now one of Indonesia's largest coal and energy groups; EY named him Indonesia Entrepreneur of the Year in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: His comeback after Astra started with a Rp15 million loan to bid for a PT Telkom operational-cooperation (KSO) tender, drawing on telecom experience from his Astra days; his firm became one of five winners. He also chairs the foundation behind Universitas Kristen Indonesia (UKI) in Jakarta.
notes: Born 1949; low public profile. The IR email comes from a broker's company-profile page (last updated 2023), not Saratoga's own site, so verify it. His exact current board title is per MarketScreener and secondary sources. Deep-cut detail is from a secondary Indonesian profile (Cermati). Avoid the Bank Summa backstory.

name: Xia Xinde
current_role: Chairman, Guangzhou Great Power Energy & Technology (鹏辉能源, SZ300438)
profile: Xia Xinde (夏信德, b. 1964), a Central South University materials graduate with a master's in electrochemistry, founded Guangzhou-based lithium battery maker Great Power Energy in 2001 and owns roughly half of it; he was president until 2021 and has been chairman since 2011. The company has pivoted strongly to energy-storage batteries and filed for a Hong Kong 'A+H' listing in January 2026.
interesting_fact: Great Power's energy-storage battery revenue reached RMB 4.84bn in the first three quarters of 2025, up from RMB 3.03bn a year earlier, as the company swung back to profit and filed to list in Hong Kong.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Great Power, Xia spent 1988-1994 as deputy director of the Guangzhou 555 Battery Research Institute, then ran Guangzhou Weili Power Supply Co. (1994-2001).
notes: Low-profile technical founder; route via Great Power's general inbox or IR/board secretary office (HK listing application filed 30 Jan 2026, status of debut not confirmed).

name: Rubens Ometto Silveira Mello
current_role: Chairman of the Board and controlling shareholder, Cosan S.A.; chairman of Raízen
profile: Born 1950 in Piracicaba, grandson of Italian immigrant sugar-mill owner Pedro Ometto, he joined the family business in 1986 and built Cosan into Brazil's largest sugar and ethanol producer, listing it in São Paulo (2005) and New York (2007), buying Esso Brazil's assets and forming Raízen with Shell in 2011. A 2025-26 deal with BTG Pactual and Perfin keeps him Cosan chairman until 2031.
interesting_fact: Raízen, the joint venture he formed by merging Cosan's sugar, ethanol and fuel assets with Shell's Brazilian business, became one of Brazil's largest energy companies by revenue (about US$45.5bn in the 2023/24 harvest year).
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the family mill business he trained as a mechanical production engineer at USP's Escola Politécnica, worked at Unibanco (1971-73), then became finance director of Grupo Votorantim in 1974 under his mentor Antônio Ermírio de Moraes.
notes: Cosan is restructuring/deleveraging (2025-26) and Raízen is under pressure - avoid as outreach angle. Chairmanship to 2031 per shareholder pact: https://fusoesaquisicoes.com/acontece-no-setor/rubens-ometto-assina-acordo-de-acionistas-com-btg-pactual-e-perfin-na-cosan/. Route via Cosan IR/corporate communications.

name: Zhong Peifeng
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Amlogic (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. (晶晨股份, SSE STAR: 688099)
profile: Zhong Peifeng (John Zhong, b. 1963, US citizen) is a Georgia Tech-trained electrical engineer who co-founded Amlogic in Silicon Valley in 1995 and moved its base to Shanghai's Zhangjiang in 2003. Amlogic designs SoCs for smart TVs, set-top boxes and AIoT devices; it listed on the STAR Market in 2019 and in late 2026 was pursuing a Hong Kong H-share listing.
interesting_fact: Amlogic is the 'hidden king' of set-top-box chips: roughly one in three smart set-top boxes and one in five smart TVs worldwide reportedly use its silicon.
deep_cut_fact: Amlogic's first products in the mid-1990s were self-developed VCD decoder chips, riding China's VCD boom; before founding it Zhong worked at North American firms including Nortel after his Georgia Tech EE master's. Amlogic was in the first batch of STAR Market listings in Aug 2019.
notes: Goes by John Zhong in English. Forbes lists residence Beijing, citizenship US; company is HQ'd in Shanghai. Low media profile; route via Amlogic IR / board secretary office (IR@amlogic.com from SSE announcements).

name: Li Guoqing
current_role: Supervisor (board of supervisors), Rongsheng Petrochemical (SZSE: 002493); shareholder of Rongsheng Holding
profile: One of the original founding shareholders of Rongsheng Petrochemical, the Hangzhou (Xiaoshan, Yinong town)-based group that grew from textiles and chemical fiber into polyester feedstocks and refining; Forbes lists him as a supervisor of the listed company. His brother Li Yongqing, a Rongsheng director, is also a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Rongsheng controls 51% of Zhejiang Petroleum & Chemical (ZPC), an 800,000 bpd integrated refinery-petrochemical complex; in 2023 Saudi Aramco paid about $3.4bn for 10% of Rongsheng and agreed to supply ZPC with 480,000 bpd of crude.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of seven founding promoters when Rongsheng Petrochemical was set up as a joint-stock company ahead of its 2010 Shenzhen IPO, holding 7.15 million shares (1.43%) alongside Li Shuirong and Li Yongqing.
notes: Name is ambiguous: not the Dangdang co-founder Li Guoqing. Very low public profile; no interviews found. IR emails are those of the board secretary (Quan Weiying) and securities affairs rep (Hu Yangyang) as published in Rongsheng's annual-report summary; Chinese-language outreach advised. Deep-cut fact from the 2010 IPO prospectus-era filing (search-summarised; verify).

name: Scott Smith
current_role: Co-founder of Qualtrics; Professor Emeritus of Marketing, BYU Marriott School of Business
profile: Scott M. Smith is a longtime BYU marketing-research professor who co-founded Provo, Utah-based Qualtrics in 2002 with sons Ryan and Jared Smith and Stuart Orgill, starting in his basement. Qualtrics was bought by SAP for $8B in 2018, spun out in a 2021 IPO and taken private by Silver Lake in 2023. He is now professor emeritus and lives in Provo.
interesting_fact: Qualtrics grew out of his academic work: as a BYU professor he wanted an online survey tool that could handle sophisticated research yet stay easy to use. In the early days he took no paycheck so the company could pay employees.
deep_cut_fact: Colleagues say he 'still pours his own cement'; he once spotted an employee's car with bald tires in the Qualtrics lot and paid for new ones. He calls his Qualtrics experience a 'magic pony ride' and left the company in 2014 to serve a mission in Hong Kong with his wife.
notes: Name is common: this is Scott M. Smith of Provo, Utah (Qualtrics). Low public profile; academic author (Basic Marketing Research). No personal channels found. Best route: Qualtrics press, or via BYU Marriott School. Not an energy/data-center figure, though Qualtrics is a cloud company.

name: Kazim Turker
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Türkerler Holding (Ankara)
profile: Ankara-based founder of Türkerler Holding, a group of ~137 companies in construction, real estate, energy and healthcare. Türkerler owns 534 MW of hydro, wind and geothermal plants plus an electricity distributor serving 828,000 subscribers, and built Ankara's Etlik City Hospital with Italy's Astaldi as a $1.3B public-private partnership.
interesting_fact: He started out at 19 running a small clothing store in Ankara before moving into construction; one of his first projects was the Police Moral Education Center in Istanbul.
deep_cut_fact: The 'Kazım Türker Art Gallery' bears his name: opened in January 2018 at Dokuz Eylül University's Faculty of Fine Arts in İzmir, created jointly with the university through Türkerler's Mahall Bomonti İzmir real-estate project. Türkerler also won a best geothermal project award at the 2018 ICCI Energy Awards.
notes: Strong energy angle (geothermal, hydro, wind, power distribution). Rarely gives English-language interviews; approach via Türkerler Holding head office in Ankara (Mahall Ankara).

name: Roy Chi Ping Chung
current_role: Co-founder and Non-executive Director, Techtronic Industries (TTI)
profile: Macau-born industrialist who co-founded Techtronic Industries with Horst Julius Pudwill in 1985; TTI makes Milwaukee, Ryobi and Hoover-brand cordless tools and floor care and is a Hang Seng Index constituent. He retired as group vice chairman in 2011 and now focuses on education and youth philanthropy via his Bright Future Charitable Foundation.
interesting_fact: Nicknamed Hong Kong's 'King of Power Tools', he became a billionaire in 2021 when TTI shares surged on pandemic DIY demand.
deep_cut_fact: He moved alone from Macau to Hong Kong at 16 and started as a warehouse keeper, rising to manager within 10 years; he has since taken university students hiking and even joined them on an overseas Trailwalker event.
notes: Holds GBS, BBS, JP honours; honorary doctorates/fellowships from several HK and UK universities. TTI IR also lists ir@ttihq.com. No personal channel found; foundation or university-donor networks may be warmer routes.

name: Danilo Iervolino
current_role: Entrepreneur/investor; controlling shareholder of BFC (AI) Media (publisher incl. Forbes Italia) and owner of US Salernitana (stepped down as club president Aug 2024)
profile: Born 1978 in Palma Campania, Iervolino founded online university UniPegaso in 2006 at 28 and grew it into Italy's largest, then sold parent Multiversity to CVC in 2021 for about $1.3bn. Since then he bought Salernitana football club and media group BFC Media (briefly also L'Espresso), and invests in Italian tech startups and VC, e.g. a 6.2% stake in Vertis SGR via his holding IDI Srl.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for an all-digital university after time in the US, where he became interested in dotcoms and online education, after developing online master's programmes at the University of Salerno.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a book on the digital economy: 'Now! Strategie per affrontare le nuove frontiere del web' (Mondadori, 2015).
notes: Best route is via BFC Media (his media company). No verified personal social accounts found. Background check: Italian Wikipedia reports a first-instance conviction (2019 case re Ministry of Labour hiring) - verify before approaching. Don't confuse with film producer Andrea Iervolino.

name: Zhang Jianguo
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Jiangxi JOVO Energy Co. (九丰能源, SSE: 605090)
profile: Zhang Jianguo (张建国, ~63, Guangzhou) chairs JOVO Energy, a natural-gas/LNG and LPG distributor founded in Zhuhai in 1990, which listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in May 2021. He and his wife Cai Lihong are the company's controlling shareholders; Forbes ranked 'Zhang Jianguo & family' #2052 on its 2026 billionaires list.
interesting_fact: JOVO's international partners include Malaysia's Petronas and Norway's Skaugen Group; the company grew from a 1990 Zhuhai gas trader into a listed LNG/LPG importer.
notes: Very common name - identity tied to Forbes profile zhang-jianguo-1 (JOVO Energy). Low media profile; board secretary listed as Huang Bo - IR channel is the best route. 'Forbes annual 2001-2025' in input likely merges other people of the same name.

name: Lai Miao
profile: Listed on the Hurun China and Global lists (2021-2026) with wealth from Ganten (景田), the Shenzhen bottled-water company behind the Baisuishan (百岁山) mineral-water brand, founded in 1992. Searches did not find public material naming 赖苗 or describing their role at Ganten.
interesting_fact: Ganten's Baisuishan leads China's natural mineral water category, and Hurun valued Ganten at RMB 26B in 2025, top-three among Chinese bottled-water companies.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or bios found. Their role (founder, co-owner or family shareholder) is unconfirmed. Ganten is private, so the only route is likely the company's corporate channels.

name: Li Weiping
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Leadshine Intelligent Control Co. (002979.SZ)
profile: MIT-trained robotics PhD (born 1962) who left academia in 1997 to found Leadshine in Shenzhen. The company makes stepper/servo motors, drives and motion controllers for factory automation and listed on the Shenzhen exchange in 2020. He is the controlling shareholder alongside his wife, director Shi Huimin, and still runs the company as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he was an associate professor at Washington State University (1991-94) and at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (1995-97).
deep_cut_fact: He is the 'Li' of 'Slotine & Li': he co-authored the classic textbook 'Applied Nonlinear Control' (1991) with MIT's Jean-Jacques Slotine, still a standard robotics/control text. He also wrote a Chinese book on motion-control system principles and applications.
notes: Chair of the 5th board, re-elected May 2023, and chaired board meetings through 2025. The textbook link (Slotine & Li) is a strong hook for a technical audience. The company is an automation/robotics play, adjacent to humanoid-robot supply chains.

name: Deepak Mehta
current_role: Chairman (long-time CMD), Deepak Nitrite Ltd and its subsidiary Deepak Phenolics
profile: Deepak C. Mehta, a University of Bombay science graduate, has spent ~45+ years at Deepak Nitrite, founded by his father Chimanlal Mehta in 1970. He turned it from a nitrite maker into a diversified chemicals group with ~100 products and India's leading phenol/acetone producer; son Maulik Mehta is now CEO. He is active in FICCI and ICC on chemical-park policy.
interesting_fact: He was named among EY Entrepreneur of the Year (India) 2020 winners; Deepak Nitrite is a leading producer of phenol and acetone in India with 700+ customers worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: Per EY, the idea for the big phenol/acetone plant (Deepak Phenolics) came while he was scouting acquisitions in Europe and noticed European firms wanting to buy into India for growth, which convinced him to build at scale at home instead.
notes: IR contact is Company Secretary Arvind Bajpai. Son Maulik Mehta (CEO) is more visible in media and may be an easier route; company is investing heavily in petrochemical capacity in Gujarat.

name: Joseph Baratta
current_role: Global Head of Private Equity, Blackstone; member of Blackstone's Board of Directors and Management Committee
profile: Joined Blackstone in 1998 and moved to London in 2001 to help build its European private equity business. He has run Blackstone's global private equity business since 2012, overseeing deals such as Medline, Ancestry and Merlin Entertainments. His wealth comes from carried interest and Blackstone equity. Earlier he worked at Morgan Stanley M&A, Tinicum and McCown De Leeuw.
interesting_fact: He is one of very few non-founder private equity executives to reach billionaire status; Forbes lists him for his Blackstone stake and carried interest.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up with modest means in Sacramento. He champions Blackstone's Career Pathways programme, which hires people from underserved communities into portfolio companies, and sits on the board of the youth-employment nonprofit Year Up. He is also a trustee of the Tate Foundation.
notes: Comfortable with media: he appeared on Masters in Business, the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast and Bloomberg TV. Approach through Blackstone press inquiries. The Sacramento detail comes from a Money & Wealth podcast page (bryantgroupventures.com/money-wealth-podcast-joe-baratta/).

name: Zhang Changhong
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (~33%), Shanghai DZH (formerly Great Wisdom, SSE: 601519); no longer chairman since 2016
profile: Zhang Changhong (张长虹, b. 1958, Chengdu) founded Shanghai DZH in 2000, building it into a leading Chinese provider of real-time market data and trading software that competes with Reuters and Bloomberg; it listed in Shanghai in 2011. He stepped down as chairman in 2016 but remains the controlling shareholder as DZH is merged into Xiangcai Co. via share swap.
interesting_fact: In the early 2000s he proposed a 'full circulation' plan to resolve China's split-share structure, letting non-tradable state and corporate shares gradually gain trading rights.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance, he earned a master's degree in philosophy at Northwestern Polytechnical University in Xi'an (1987) and taught at Nanjing Aeronautical School, a forerunner of Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics.
notes: Sensitive: CSRC fined him and banned him from securities markets in 2016 over DZH's 2013 accounts; detained in 2019 per Beijing News. Current DZH chairman/GM is Zhang Zhihong. Probably a poor podcast fit; only route is company IR.

name: Manny Stul
current_role: Co-owner of Moose Toys (Melbourne); former chairman/co-CEO — current formal title not confirmed (stepson Paul Solomon became Executive Chairman, Ronnie Frankowski CEO, Oct 2025)
profile: Born in a German refugee camp to Polish-Jewish Holocaust survivors, Stul grew up in Western Australia, built and listed giftware firm Skansen, then in 2000 took over struggling Moose Toys and grew sales ~7,000% on hits like Shopkins (1bn+ units sold) and Mighty Beanz. Moose remains Melbourne-headquartered and family-owned.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he became the first Australian to win EY World Entrepreneur of the Year, aged 67. During the pandemic logistics crunch he chartered an entire ship to bring Moose products from China.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of university and worked in construction to fund his first business, giftware company Skansen, founded in 1973 and publicly listed 20 years later for over A$15m. As a toddler he spent three years in the Northam migrant camp in Western Australia.
notes: Moose leadership reshuffle Oct 2025 (https://globaltoynews.com/2025/10/09/moose-names-frankowski-ceo-other-management-changes/). Wife Jacqui Tobias is a long-time Moose product lead. Northam camp detail from Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manny_Stul).

name: Jacques Merceron-Vicat
current_role: Honorary Chairman (Président d'honneur) and director, Vicat SA
profile: Born 1938, Jacques Merceron-Vicat is the patriarch of the family that controls Vicat, the listed French cement group founded in 1853 near Grenoble by Joseph Vicat, son of cement pioneer Louis Vicat. He led the group as chairman/CEO for decades before handing operations to son-in-law Guy Sidos (CEO 2008, chairman 2014); he remains honorary chairman with a board mandate running to 2030.
interesting_fact: The family's ancestor Louis Vicat discovered the principle of hydraulic binders in 1817 (the basis of modern cement), and Joseph and Louis Vicat built the world's first concrete bridge at Grenoble's Jardin des Plantes in 1855.
deep_cut_fact: When Guy Sidos became chairman in March 2014, the board named Jacques Merceron-Vicat honorary chairman; he had stepped back from operational control around age 70, passing the CEO role to his son-in-law in 2008, keeping the 170-year-old company under sixth-generation family control.
notes: Aged ~88, low public profile. Company now active in cement decarbonisation and alternative fuels (energy angle). Better podcast guest may be CEO Guy Sidos; approach via Vicat press office (named press officer as published in Vicat's July 2026 release).

name: Hiroyuki Inoue
current_role: Chairman (Director), Yamato Kogyo Co., Ltd. (TSE: 5444)
profile: Hiroyuki Inoue (井上浩行, b. 1945) is the son of Yamato Kogyo founder Asaji Inoue and spent his entire career at the Himeji electric-arc-furnace steelmaker, joining in 1969 and serving as president for about 36 years (1981-2017). He internationalised the company into the US, Thailand, Korea and the Middle East, and has been chairman since 2017 while remaining its largest shareholder (~12%).
interesting_fact: Yamato Kogyo makes rails and switches for Japan's Shinkansen bullet trains, and earns the majority of its sales overseas.
deep_cut_fact: In 1987, under his presidency, Yamato Kogyo formed a joint venture with US steelmaker Nucor, Nucor-Yamato Steel in Arkansas, taking the company into North American H-beam (structural steel) production; it later added JVs in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.
notes: Re-elected director at June 2025 AGM (94.4% approval). Electric-arc-furnace (low-carbon) steel is a possible energy angle. Japanese-language approach via corporate office recommended.

name: Yao Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, LUSTER LightTech (凌云光, SSE STAR: 688400)
profile: Yao Yi founded Beijing-based LUSTER LightTech in 2002; it makes configurable machine-vision systems, intelligent vision equipment and optical-communication/fiber-optic products and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market. He owns roughly 44% of the company and runs it as chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: LUSTER began supplying configurable vision systems to Apple in 2016 and became one of its preferred suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he earned bachelor's and master's degrees at Xidian University (1986, 1989) and a doctorate from Beijing Jiaotong University in 1994, eight years before founding LUSTER.
notes: Board secretary is Gu Baoxing (per 2025 annual report summary). Machine vision for AI/electronics manufacturing is the podcast angle. Education details come from one MarketScreener profile.

name: Xiong Haitao
current_role: Actual controller of Gaojin Technology Industry Group (largest shareholder of Dongcai Technology, Gaomeng New Materials, Yichang Technology); vice chair of Dongcai Technology
profile: Chinese businesswoman, formerly a Kingfa Sci. & Tech. director (1998-May 2024) and ex-wife of Kingfa founder Yuan Zhimin; still a Kingfa shareholder (~1.5%). Through Gaojin Group she controls three Shanghai/Shenzhen-listed materials companies.
interesting_fact: Via Gaojin Technology Industry Group she is the ultimate controller of three separate A-share companies: Dongcai Technology (insulation/film materials), Gaomeng New Materials (adhesives) and Yichang Technology.
notes: Sensitive: in Jan 2026 the three listed companies announced she had been placed under detention (liuzhi) and investigation by the Sichuan Supervisory Commission; she resigned from Yichang's board 26 Jan 2026. Not a suitable outreach target at present. Source: https://finance.eastmoney.com/a/202601273632524882.html

name: Jet Jie Li
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, J&T Global Express (HKEX: 1519)
profile: Li spent 15+ years at OPPO, leading its expansion into Indonesia and other Asian markets, then founded J&T Express in Jakarta in 2015. J&T became Southeast Asia's parcel-volume leader, entered China in 2020 (riding Pinduoduo's growth) and listed in Hong Kong in 2023; it now also operates in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Mexico, Brazil and Egypt.
interesting_fact: The 'J&T' name and brand were born in Indonesia, not China: Li launched it in Jakarta in June 2015 and only later took it back to China, now the group's largest market.
deep_cut_fact: OPPO's headquarters created the 'Jet Lee' award, named in his honour, to reward top salespeople across its global sales agencies. He holds a 1998 marketing degree from the University of Science and Technology Beijing and began at OPPO selling audiovisual products in 1999.
notes: Goes by 'Jet Lee' (李杰) in Indonesia. Rarely gives interviews; route via J&T IR/corporate communications.

name: Philippe Benacin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Interparfums SA (Paris); Vice Chairman and President, Inter Parfums, Inc. (Nasdaq: IPAR)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded fragrance maker Interparfums in 1982 with Jean Madar, right after business school (ESSEC, 1983), after learning in class how high fragrance-industry margins were. Listed on Nasdaq in 1988 at a ~$4m valuation, the group now makes licensed perfumes for brands such as Jimmy Choo, Montblanc, Coach, Lacoste and Moncler. Benacin runs the European business, about two thirds of sales.
interesting_fact: He told Journal du Luxe that he got into licensing 'largely by chance': the first licence came in 1990, and a 1993 Burberry licence became the springboard for growth. He was inducted into The Fragrance Foundation Hall of Fame in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Asked in a March 2026 interview what he is proudest of at Interparfums, he chose not a brand but its 'communauté d'esprit', the team's shared spirit. In the same interview he argued that Gen Z is very attached to niche perfume.

public_contacts.value: The Equity Group (Devin Sullivan), investor relations for Inter Parfums, Inc.

notes: Gives interviews to the French luxury and beauty trade press (Journal du Luxe, Premium Beauty News). For the French side, the Interparfums Finance contact page is the best route; the US IR agency is The Equity Group.

name: Igor Kudryashkin
current_role: Commercial director and co-owner, Ural Mining and Metallurgical Company (UMMC); executive board member, Svyatogor
profile: Long-time commercial director of Iskander Makhmudov's UMMC, a major Russian copper, zinc, coal and gold producer, who received a UMMC stake when the business was reorganised in 2013. His family also controls a majority of European Media Group, a large Russian radio-station network.
interesting_fact: Besides metals, Kudryashkin's family holds more than two-thirds of European Media Group, whose eight radio stations reach roughly 35 million listeners a week.
notes: UK-sanctioned since Feb 2024 (listed for his Svyatogor/UMMC role, updated Apr 2025; see opensanctions.org/entities/NK-TCxUTL6L7fKzsmG7XVhB22). Not a suitable outreach target; no published contacts found.

name: Warren Chen
current_role: Chairman, DynaColor Inc. (TPEx: 5489); cofounder and shareholder of Chroma ATE
profile: Warren Chen co-founded Chroma ATE (TWSE: 2360) in 1984 with other National Chiao Tung University alumni, including billionaire Leo Huang. Chroma makes automated test equipment for power electronics, EVs and semiconductors, and AI data-center power demand has lifted its shares. In 1991 he founded DynaColor, a Taipei maker of video-surveillance and machine-vision cameras, which he chairs.
interesting_fact: Forbes notes that Chroma's power-testing equipment is increasingly used worldwide as the AI boom drives up electricity demand, which makes him a direct fit for an energy and data-center podcast.
notes: Investing.com and StockAnalysis list a Warren Chen as DynaColor chairman/CEO. MarketScreener names the chairman 'Chun Sheng Chen' (an NCTU graduate), probably his formal name, but I could not confirm that link. He is low-profile, with almost no English press. DynaColor's contact page lists only sales emails; reach him via the company or through Chroma ATE.

name: Shintaro Yamada
current_role: Director, Representative Executive Officer and CEO, Mercari, Inc.
profile: Serial internet entrepreneur who founded Unoh (Movie Life, Photozou, Machitsuku!), sold it to Zynga in 2010, then founded Mercari in Feb 2013. Mercari became Japan's first unicorn and its dominant flea-market app, listed in 2018 (making him a billionaire), and expanded into Merpay, crypto (Mercoin) and the Kashima Antlers football club. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: As a Waseda University student he interned at a then little-known Rakuten and built its auction site (Rakuten Auction).
deep_cut_fact: In July 2021 he set up the YAMADA Shintaro D&I Foundation with ~3 billion yen of his own money; its flagship is a no-repayment scholarship for girls choosing STEM tracks in high school, now in its 6th cohort (2026). Before Mercari he spent about six months backpacking round the world in cheap hostels.
notes: Foundation donation figure: 30億円 = ~3 billion yen (Business Insider Japan https://www.businessinsider.jp/post-239830). World-trip hostels detail: Japan Times 2016 (https://japantimes.co.jp/news/2016/03/18/business/5-night-hostels-led-japans-first-1-billion-startup, paywalled). Best route: Mercari press form or the D&I foundation.

name: Kuan Kam Hon
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hartalega Holdings Bhd (Malaysia)
profile: High-school dropout who started in his father's KL home-building firm in 1969, founded label maker Timol Weaving in 1978, then pivoted into medical gloves in 1988 as Hartalega, now one of the world's largest nitrile glove makers. He acts as mentor and spokesman, leaving operations to his sons.
interesting_fact: In 2005 Hartalega launched the world's first lightweight nitrile glove (4.7g vs an industry norm of 6g+), a product most rivals doubted could work.
deep_cut_fact: The name Hartalega combines two Malay words meaning 'relief assets'; he converted his struggling woven-label and badge plant into a latex glove factory as demand rose in the early AIDS-epidemic years.
notes: Also known as Kwan Kam Onn; wealth shared with brother Kuan Kam Peng. Glove sector is cyclical; avoid wealth-decline framing. Route via Hartalega corporate/IR (Sepang, Selangor); no published IR email verified.

name: Christina Ong
current_role: Founder-owner, COMO Group (COMO Hotels and Resorts, COMO Shambhala, Club 21), Singapore
profile: Christina Ong, born in 1948 and the daughter of oil trader Peter Fu Yun Siak, opened luxury boutique Club 21 in Singapore in 1972 and built it into an international fashion retail group. She bought her first hotel, The Halkin in London, in 1991, created the COMO hotel and COMO Shambhala wellness brands, and took control of Mulberry in 2002. In 2026 COMO opened new properties on the French Riviera and in Bordeaux.
interesting_fact: She founded Club 21 at age 24 as a small boutique in Singapore's Tanglin Shopping Centre. The group grew to about 400 luxury fashion and lifestyle stores worldwide, and its holdings include iShop, reportedly Asia's biggest Apple distributor.
deep_cut_fact: She released a cookbook, 'COMO Simple', in 2025. She was also inducted into the Singapore Women's Hall of Fame (2014) and has chaired Singapore's National Parks Board.

public_contacts.value: louise.james@comohotels.com (Louise James, Global Director of PR, COMO Hotels and Resorts)

notes: Described as extremely private. The Forbes profile is a joint one with her husband Ong Beng Seng, who has his own legal matters in Singapore; keep outreach focused on her. COMO PR is the best route. Wellness, hospitality and Mulberry are the natural podcast angles.

name: Wang Minwen
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hangzhou Lion Electronics (Hangzhou Lion Microelectronics, SSE: 605358); chairman of Xianhe Holding
profile: Chinese executive (b. 1963) who chairs Hangzhou Lion Electronics, a maker of semiconductor silicon wafers, power-device chips and compound-semiconductor RF/optoelectronic chips, listed in Shanghai in 2020. He and four siblings also control specialty-paper maker Xianhe Co. via Zhejiang Xianhe Holding.
interesting_fact: Lion runs a wafer-to-chip platform spanning silicon wafers (via subsidiary Zhejiang Jinruihong), power semiconductors and GaAs/GaN-on-SiC chips, making it one of China's few vertically integrated silicon-wafer-plus-chip groups.
deep_cut_fact: Before semiconductors he spent ~two decades at Shanghai energy group Shenergy: joining Shenergy Co. in 1988 in its investment department and rising to board secretary and director, then running Shenergy Asset Management and serving as Shenergy Group VP (2005-07). He is also a trustee of Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.
notes: Low public profile; bio from company filings. Energy-industry background (Shenergy) is a natural podcast hook. Investor email published in Lion's site (investors section).

name: Sergey Kasyanenko
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Management Board, Orimi Group (Russia)
profile: Co-founder of Orimi, Russia's largest producer of tea and roasted coffee (brands Greenfield, TESS, Jardin, Princess Noori). Orimi started in 1994 as Orimi Trade, a wholesaler of flour, sugar and tea, then built its own packaging and coffee plants in Leningrad Region. Most of his fortune is cash from roughly $1.5bn of Orimi dividends.
interesting_fact: He holds a Ph.D. in physics and mathematics before becoming a tea and coffee magnate.
deep_cut_fact: Orimi's very first tea brand, launched at its founding in 1994, was 'Princess Kandy'; within two years Orimi Trade was one of Russia's six biggest tea importers. He and co-founder Alexander Evnevich personally opened Orimi's instant-coffee plant with the Leningrad Region governor.
notes: Very low public profile; little English-language coverage. Company press office is the only published route.

name: René Holeček
current_role: Majority shareholder and Vice-chairman of the Supervisory Board, Colt CZ Group SE (per company corporate-affairs page)
profile: René Holeček (b. 1966), a Czech engineer-turned-banker, invested in ailing Česká zbrojovka Uherský Brod in 2001, took control in 2014 and listed it in Prague in 2020. He turned it into Colt CZ Group, buying US icon Colt (2021) and ammunition maker Sellier & Bellot (2024), and has since added an Amsterdam listing.
interesting_fact: Before guns he was a banker in the early 1990s (senior roles at Komerční banka and Pragobanka) and helped privatize the giant Třinec ironworks with long-time partner Rudolf Ovčaří.
deep_cut_fact: Forbes Czech lists his 'obsession' as golf, and with partner Rudolf Ovčaří he invested heavily in building golf courses and leisure resorts. His Holeček Family Foundation (Nadace rodiny Holečkových) funds education, health, science, crisis intervention and culture.
notes: Extremely low media profile (Forbes CZ calls him the 'mysterious owner'); rarely gives interviews. Best route is Colt CZ media relations. Defence/ammunition manufacturing angle may fit energy/industrial episodes.

name: Myron Wentz
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, USANA Health Sciences; founder, Sanoviv Medical Institute (Rosarito, Mexico)
profile: Microbiologist (PhD, University of Utah) born 1940 in Napoleon, North Dakota. Founded Gull Laboratories (diagnostic tests) in 1974, then USANA Health Sciences in 1992, a NYSE-listed nutritional supplements/skincare MLM in which he still holds roughly 40%. Retired as USANA chairman in Dec 2019; spends most of his time at Sanoviv, the holistic medical centre he founded in 1998. Still gave a keynote at USANA Live 2025.
interesting_fact: He enjoys snorkeling and watching coral reef videos on YouTube; he renounced US citizenship in the mid-1990s and claims St. Kitts & Nevis citizenship.
deep_cut_fact: He started Gull Laboratories in 1974 as a one-person operation that developed a diagnostic test for Epstein-Barr virus; later gave $10M to his alma mater North Central College (Naperville, IL), helping fund the Wentz Concert Hall, and its science center bears his name.
notes: Lives mostly in Rosarito, Mexico (Sanoviv). Best route is via USANA corporate communications. Health/longevity angle (cellular nutrition) is his signature theme.

name: Hartley Rogers
current_role: Co-Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board, Hamilton Lane (Nasdaq: HLNE) (named co-CEO Oct 2026)
profile: Private-equity veteran who joined Hamilton Lane in 2003/04 after two decades at Morgan Stanley and Credit Suisse; owns a large stake (>13% per Forbes) in the private-markets firm, which listed on Nasdaq in 2017. In Oct 2026 he was named co-CEO alongside Juan Delgado-Moreira while remaining board chairman; Erik Hirsch became executive co-chairman.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Advisory Board of HarvardX (Harvard's online-learning initiative) and sits on the boards of the Institute of International Education and Bessemer Securities; previously on the Metropolitan Opera board.
deep_cut_fact: His father, Hartley Rogers Jr., was an MIT mathematics professor (1956-2009) and a founder of computability theory, author of the classic 'Theory of Recursive Functions and Effective Computability'; the MIT obituary lists son Hartley R. Rogers.
notes: Press contact Tia Wilson; IR John Oh (Hamilton Lane). Good finance/private-markets angle; firm has infrastructure & real-assets strategies relevant to energy/data centers.

name: Simone Maag de Moura Cunha
current_role: Shareholder (~3.5%) of Straumann Group; no public executive role found
profile: Per Forbes, she owns about 3.5% of Swiss dental-implant maker Straumann Group. She is the niece of billionaire Rudolf Maag (Straumann's second-largest shareholder, who built Stratec Medical and merged it with Synthes) and sister-in-law of Straumann chairman-family member Thomas Straumann.
interesting_fact: Her uncle Rudolf Maag bought Straumann's medical device division in 1990, took it public as Stratec Medical, then merged it with Synthes in 1999; that stake was later sold to Johnson & Johnson.
notes: Extremely private; no independent public profile, interviews or verified accounts found. Only route is via Straumann Group corporate communications, and she has no operating role there. Low priority.

name: Sir Roger
