current_role: Chair, Creative Folkestone; founder of the Roger De Haan Charitable Trust (former Saga chairman)
profile: Sir Roger De Haan (born 1948, Northampton) took over over-50s travel and insurance group Saga from his father Sidney in 1984 and ran it with brother Peter for some 20 years before selling it in a £1.35bn buyout in 2004. Since then he has focused on regenerating Folkestone, buying its harbour and funding arts charity Creative Folkestone and local education. Knighted 2014.
interesting_fact: In 2004, the same year he sold Saga, he bought Folkestone Harbour for £11m; his trust has put about £50m into acquiring and restoring nearly 90 buildings in the town's Creative Quarter.
deep_cut_fact: While running Saga he extended the brand into broadcasting, launching Saga-branded radio stations for older listeners alongside its holidays and financial services.
notes: Input name is truncated: this is Sir Roger De Haan (shared listing with brother Peter De Haan). Low media profile; best route is via his charitable trust's contact form or Creative Folkestone. Avoid political-donation topics.

name: Peter De Haan
current_role: Private investor and philanthropist; founder/director of Opus Trust companies and director of Bancroft Wines (per MarketScreener)
profile: Peter De Haan co-ran Folkestone-based Saga, the over-50s holidays and insurance group founded by his father Sidney, alongside brother Sir Roger for about two decades until its 2004 sale (~£1.35bn). He set up the Peter De Haan Charitable Trust in 1999 and has since focused on philanthropy and private businesses including Opus Trust and Bancroft Wines.
interesting_fact: The De Haan brothers have poured large sums into regenerating their home town of Folkestone, including its Creative Quarter, harbour and Seven Hills sports ground.
deep_cut_fact: An arts philanthropist, he launched IdeasTap in December 2008, a funding and opportunities network for young creatives whose founding partners included Old Vic New Voices, the National Youth Theatre and Polka Theatre.
notes: Low-profile; no published personal or office contact found. Peter De Haan Charitable Trust (no. 1077005) was removed from the Charity Commission register in Dec 2024; a Swiss 'Fondation Peter De Haan' (Lausanne) may be his current vehicle (unconfirmed). Avoid referencing IdeasTap's 2015 closure.

name: Nutchamai Thanombooncharoen
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Carabao Group PCL (SET: CBG), Thailand
profile: Co-founder and chairman of SET-listed Carabao Group, maker of Carabao Dang energy drink. She moved from her family's financial-services business into property with partner Sathien Sathientham, co-owned Tawandang German Brewery, and in 2002 co-launched Carabao with folk-rock singer Aed Carabao. She also has stakes in Tawandang Distillery (rice whisky) and expanded into beer brewing in 2023.
interesting_fact: Carabao was launched in 2002 with Yuenyong 'Aed Carabao' Opakul, frontman of Thailand's famous Carabao band; she was named to Fortune's 2024 Most Powerful Women Asia list.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy drinks she and Sathien ran Tawandang German Brewery, a Bangkok German-style brewpub (she has been on its board since 1998); she studied at Silpakorn University and did graduate study at Thammasat.
notes: Low-profile; partner Sathien Sathientham is the more public face. Carabao is also known globally for football sponsorship (Carabao Cup).

name: Zhou Liangzhang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hexing Electrical Co. (海兴电力, SSE: 603556), Hangzhou
profile: Zhou Liangzhang (周良璋, b. 1963) worked at the state-owned Hangzhou Instrument Factory before founding Hexing in 1992. Hexing makes smart meters, metering/AMI systems, distribution equipment and new-energy solutions for power utilities, selling to 80+ countries; overseas business brought in RMB 2.94bn of 2024 revenue, with plants in Europe, Latin America and Africa.
interesting_fact: Hexing earns about two-thirds of its revenue abroad, building localised smart-meter factories in Europe, Latin America and Africa — an unusually global footprint for a Chinese grid-equipment maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Hexing in 1992, Zhou was deputy head of the foreign-economic-relations office at the Hangzhou Instrument Factory and then general manager of Hangzhou Yida Industrial Instrument Manufacturing Co.
notes: Grid/smart-meter angle fits energy podcast. Board secretary (2024 report): Jin Yi. Chinese-language outreach via IR office recommended.

name: Huxiong Chen
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and President, Shanghai M&G Stationery Inc. (晨光股份, SSE: 603899)
profile: Chen Huxiong (陈湖雄, b. 1970, Shantou) started out selling imported stationery around China, became a China agent for Japanese and Korean brands, and launched the M&G own brand in Shanghai after the 1997 Asian financial crisis hit his suppliers. M&G grew into China's largest stationery maker via a vast school-side retail network. He co-owns it with his twin brother Chen Huwen (chairman) and sister.
interesting_fact: M&G was born out of the 1997 Asian financial crisis: when the Japanese and Korean stationery firms he distributed for went bust, he decided to build his own brand.
deep_cut_fact: He left school for work at 17 in 1987 as a toy-factory operator earning 50 yuan a month; as a travelling salesman he once stood for 54 hours on a green-skin train from Shijiazhuang to Chengdu. Selling to Xinhua Bookstores got him into stationery.
notes: Low-profile; few English interviews. Best route is M&G's board-secretary/IR office (ir@mg-pen.com, published in annual report summary).

name: Hongbin Sun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sunac China Holdings (HKEX: 1918), Tianjin/Beijing
profile: Sun Hongbin (b. 1963, Shanxi) worked at Legend (Lenovo) before founding Tianjin property agency-turned-developer Shunchi (Sunco) in 1994 and Sunac in 2003, which became one of China's largest developers and bought Wanda's theme-park and hotel assets in 2017. Since 2022 he has steered Sunac through an offshore/onshore debt restructuring and remains chairman in 2026; his stake has been diluted.
interesting_fact: In 2017 Sunac bought a portfolio of cultural-tourism projects and hotels from Wang Jianlin's Wanda Group, pushing a homebuilder into theme parks and hotels.
deep_cut_fact: Before property he trained as an engineer in the power sector: he graduated from the Wuhan Water Conservancy and Electric Power College (now part of Wuhan University) in 1981 and earned a Tsinghua master's in engineering in 1985.
notes: US citizen based in Tianjin. Sunac is in post-default restructuring; avoid financial-distress framing. No dedicated published IR email found on sunac.com.cn (ESG reports list esg@sunac.com.cn). Background includes a 1990s conviction—avoid in outreach.

name: Tsai Chi-jui
current_role: Co-founder and long-time group president (總裁) of Pou Chen Group, Taichung, Taiwan; daughter Tsai Pei-chun has been CEO since 2012
profile: Tsai Chi-jui (蔡其瑞) co-founded Pou Chen with his brothers in 1969, starting with rubber shoes and slipper processing; it became the world's largest branded athletic/casual footwear maker, producing 200M+ pairs a year for Nike, Adidas, Asics and New Balance (incl. via HK-listed Yue Yuen). Now in his 80s, he has largely handed operations to the next generation.
interesting_fact: Before footwear he was a primary-school fine-arts teacher; Business Today credited his artistic eye for Pou Chen's distinctive shoe-upper designs that won over sneaker brands, and noted Pou Chen made Nike's Air Jordan line.
deep_cut_fact: A Lukang native and Taichung Normal College graduate, classmates recalled he had a fine singing voice and single-handedly did every class art contest and wall poster; he reluctantly left teaching and opened a shoe-upper/slipper factory in 1969 with NT$150,000. In 2014 he was still wearing his trademark Nike sneakers with shirt and slacks.
notes: Described by Forbes as humble and intensely private; born c.1940 (68 in 2008). No recent public statements found; route via Pou Chen spokesperson's office. Alive status assumed from continued 2025-26 rich-list appearances; no death reports found.

name: Yuequn Tao
current_role: Chairman, Ovctek China (欧普康视, SZSE: 300595), Hefei
profile: Tao Yuequn (陶悦群) is a physicist-turned-entrepreneur who founded Ovctek in Hefei in 2001, building China's leading maker of orthokeratology (ortho-k) myopia-control contact lenses plus a chain of optometry clinics. He earned an engineering PhD in the US (Forbes says USC; China Daily says UCLA, 1994) and taught at Cal State before returning to China.
interesting_fact: Ovctek describes itself as China's first listed optometry-technology company and runs what it calls the world's largest R&D and production centre for orthokeratology lenses.
deep_cut_fact: He began in nuclear fusion research after a 1984 USTC/CAS master's (he recalls spending two years just getting one program to run); Ovctek started by chance when a friend in China asked him to find ortho-k lenses in the US.
notes: PhD school conflicts between sources (USC per Forbes, UCLA per China Daily/ifeng); avoid naming it. Approach via Ovctek board secretary/IR (listed on SZSE disclosures).

name: Xu Guangfu
current_role: Chairman, Daqo Group (since 1984); director of Daqo New Energy Corp. (NYSE: DQ), whose board he chaired 2007-Aug 2023
profile: Born 1942 in Yangzhong, Jiangsu, Xu joined the township enterprise Xinba General Company in the 1960s and turned it into Daqo Group, a major Chinese maker of electrical systems and equipment. Daqo spun out polysilicon producer Daqo New Energy (NYSE-listed); his son Xu Xiang now leads much of the business while Xu remains Daqo Group chairman.
interesting_fact: He was named a National Township and Village Entrepreneur by China's Ministry of Agriculture in 2001 and 2002 and a 'Pioneer in Electricity Industry' in 2012.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an agricultural technician at the Xinba farm-tech station; the township factory he later ran made grinding wheels and bakelite goods, and its breakthrough came in 1990 when it won a contract to supply electrical products to 17 venues of the Beijing Asian Games.
notes: In his early 80s; son Xu Xiang (co-listed) is the more active executive. Best route is Daqo New Energy IR (ir@daqo.com; full list at dqsolar.com/IR-Contacts). Deep-cut fact from a Chinese brand-profile site, moderate reliability.

name: Xu Xiang (徐翔)
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Daqo New Energy Corp. (NYSE: DQ); President, Daqo Group
profile: Son of Daqo Group founder Xu Guangfu, Xu Xiang runs the family's Jiangsu-based Daqo (大全) empire, which spans electrical equipment and solar-grade polysilicon. He has been a Daqo New Energy director since its 2007 founding, president of Daqo Group since 2006, and became CEO and chairman of the NYSE-listed polysilicon maker in August 2023.
interesting_fact: Daqo New Energy is one of the world's lowest-cost producers of high-purity polysilicon for solar panels, with 305,000 metric tons of nameplate capacity.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Daqo Group he was general manager of Jiangsu Changjiang Electric Co. (a Daqo electrical-equipment subsidiary) from 2000 to 2006, and earned his EMBA from Nanjing University in 2004; he holds directorships at 25 Daqo Group subsidiaries.
notes: Wealth shared with father Xu Guangfu (Daqo founder). Low English-language media profile; IR team is the practical route. Relevant to energy angle (polysilicon/solar supply chain; Daqo Group also makes power equipment).

name: Qian Ke
current_role: Chairman, General Manager & CEO, Tolerance Precision Manufacturing (Jiangsu) Co. (托伦斯, SZSE ChiNext: 301583); actual controller
profile: Qian Ke (钱珂, b. 1973; Chinese national with US permanent residency; software degree) ran US-based UFO Engineering, a maker of semiconductor vacuum chambers, before taking over its Shanghai affiliate Tolerance in 2015. He moved production to Qidong, Jiangsu, in 2017 and built it into a key chamber/precision-parts supplier to NAURA and AMEC. Tolerance listed on ChiNext in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Tolerance's ChiNext debut on 10 July 2026 opened up ~1,054% (intraday high +1,070%) from its ¥22.6 IPO price, briefly valuing the ~¥720m-revenue parts maker at nearly ¥50bn - one of the year's hottest A-share listings.
deep_cut_fact: Tolerance's core edge is multi-layer vacuum brazing: it can braze 7-layer semiconductor vacuum chambers in one piece (most domestic peers manage 3-4), a technique Qian brought over from his years running UFO Engineering in the US.
notes: Hurun's 'Tolerance' = 托伦斯精密制造（江苏）股份有限公司 (Qidong, Jiangsu). Newly listed; very little English coverage, no personal social presence found. No IR email located in sources I could open; IPO issuance announcement lists contact person Xu Hongyan, tel 0513-83393785 (https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2026-06/26/A14/zqA1426.pdf). Check the 2026 interim report on cninfo for the board-secretary email.

name: Gao Denghua
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder (with Xie Yun), Hubei Doti-Micro Technology (东田微, 301183.SZ)
profile: Chairman and legal representative of Doti-Micro, founded July 2009, which makes precision optical components: GPON filters, TO caps, WDM filters and optical-isolator assemblies for optical transceivers, plus camera optics. He and Xie Yun are the actual controllers. AI-driven optical-module demand lifted earnings in 2026 and put him on the Hurun China list for the first time.
interesting_fact: Doti-Micro guided H1 2026 net profit of RMB85-95m, up 68-87% year on year, as its optical-isolator and filter components for transceivers rode the AI data-center optics boom.
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in public sources. Contact would be via the company's board secretary (Li Guanghua, also CFO, per July 2026 IR record https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202607091826847628_1.pdf); no published IR email located from this session (cninfo unreachable).

name: Xie Yun
current_role: Director and General Manager, Hubei Doti-Micro Technology (东田微, 301183.SZ); co-controlling shareholder with husband Gao Denghua
profile: Xie Yun and her husband, chairman Gao Denghua, control Hubei Doti-Micro Technology (founded 2009, listed on ChiNext), which makes precision optical components for smartphone cameras and high-speed optical modules. She has been with the company since founding and is its general manager and a director (re-nominated July 2026).
interesting_fact: Doti-Micro runs an 'imaging optics + communication optics' twin strategy; with AI data-centre build-outs driving optical-module demand, 2025 revenue rose 46.9% to RMB 877m and net profit 80.2% to about RMB 101m.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal accounts found. Hurun lists her jointly with Gao Denghua. Route: company board-secretary office (secretary Li Guanghua). Some data providers list her as CEO/general manager since July 2009.

name: Yang Yuying
current_role: Vice Chairwoman and employee-representative director, Satellite Chemical Co. (formerly Zhejiang Satellite Petrochemical; Shenzhen 002648)
profile: Yang Yuying (杨玉英, b. 1961) is the elder sister of Satellite Chemical founder-chairman Yang Weidong and a shareholder of controlling holder Zhejiang Satellite Holding. The Jiaxing-based group grew from a small chemicals plant into a major Chinese maker of ethylene, acrylics and polymers; she is vice chairwoman and the company's Party secretary.
interesting_fact: Satellite Chemical cracks imported US ethane rather than naphtha: it locked in supply through a long-term deal with Energy Transfer and runs its own fleet of very large ethane carriers (VLECs), giving roughly 80% ethylene yield vs ~30% for naphtha cracking.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the boardroom she is a prominent volunteer organiser: executive president of the Jiaxing Volunteers Association and president of the Nanhu District Charity Volunteers Association, and a winner of the 6th Zhejiang Province Charity Award and a Jiaxing 'moral model' title.
notes: Company website is the corporate site, not hers. Low media profile; her charity/volunteer work is the warmest angle. Route via the board-secretary/IR mailbox listed in the 2025 annual report.

name: Pan Jian
current_role: Co-Chairman and Executive Director, Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. (CATL; SZ 300750 / HK 3750)
profile: Hong Kong permanent resident (b. 1976, University of Chicago master's); a CATL director since 2015, later vice chairman, and co-chairman since Dec 2024. His wealth comes from his CATL stake, and he is CATL's frequent international face, e.g. at Davos and the 2025 Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: At Davos 2025 he said China's industry no longer talks about 'EVs' but 'EIVs' - the I for 'intelligent' - crediting China's software engineers from the smartphone/internet boom for its edge over Western automakers.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming a battery executive he sat on the boards of non-battery companies including Shanghai M&G Stationery (the pen maker), Luye Pharma and French animal-health group Ceva Sante Animale.
notes: Speaks English and is CATL's main voice at global forums (Davos, WEF) - a realistic podcast guest via CATL IR/corporate communications. IR email from 2024 interim report; verify against latest filing.

name: Wu Xiaoge
current_role: Co-actual controller (~16% holder) of CNGR Advanced Material (中伟股份, SZSE: 300919 / HKEX); former director & VP (stepped down 2023)
profile: Chengdu-based co-founder of CNGR, a Hunan-headquartered maker of nickel/cobalt precursor cathode materials for EV batteries, alongside her husband, chairman Deng Weimin. CNGR listed in Shenzhen in 2020 and dual-listed in Hong Kong in 2025. She left the board in 2023 but remains a joint controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: CNGR has become one of the world's largest suppliers of ternary battery precursors and now also makes sodium-ion and solid-state-battery precursor materials, as well as precursors marketed for the 'low-altitude economy' (drones/eVTOL).
notes: Forbes lists her as 'formerly' on its real-time list (age 54, Tsinghua MBA). Very low public profile since leaving management; husband Deng Weimin is the public face. Route via CNGR IR mailbox.

name: Chen Yuantai
current_role: Secretary of the Communist Party committee, Contemporary Amperex Technology (CATL) - per Forbes; not independently confirmed
profile: Per Forbes, Chen Yuantai is party committee secretary at CATL, the Ningde, Fujian-based battery maker that is the world's largest EV-battery supplier, and his fortune stems from CATL shares. He holds no board seat and has almost no public footprint beyond Forbes's listing.
interesting_fact: CATL, whose stake underpins his fortune, is headquartered in Ningde, a once-remote Fujian city now dubbed a global lithium-battery powerhouse.
notes: English and Chinese searches found no independent confirmation of his role (he is not among CATL directors in the Dec 2024 board slate or named in the 2025 annual report summary). Treat as a very low-profile insider; the only published route is CATL's board-office/IR email.

name: Anna Margaret Smedvig
current_role: Vice Chair, Smedvig Family Office (Stavanger); formerly chairman of London-based Smedvig Capital
profile: Norwegian-born, London-based fourth-generation heir (b. 1983) to the Smedvig shipping and offshore-drilling fortune founded by great-grandfather Peder Smedvig in 1915; the family sold Smedvig ASA's rig business and redeployed into venture capital (Smedvig Capital, est. 1996), funds and Stavanger real estate. Sunday Times Rich List has valued her and father Peter at ~GBP 850m-1bn.
interesting_fact: Smedvig Capital, which she chaired from 2016, has invested over GBP 1bn in British and Nordic companies, pivoting an oil-services dynasty into tech venture investing.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over the family investment arm she worked at luxury stationer Smythson, consumer private-equity firm L Catterton and EC Hambro Rabben; she holds an MA in Psychology and Business from the University of Edinburgh and lists fashion, film, architecture and design as interests.
notes: Private; rarely gives interviews. Smedvig contact form has a 'Smedvig family office' department option, which is the most direct published route. The family also runs Peder Smedvigs Stipendiefond (since 1992) funding Norwegian students' study abroad - a possible warm angle.

name: Dou Zhenggang
current_role: Chairman and owner, Hangzhou Jinjiang Group (environmental energy, alumina/aluminium, non-ferrous metals, trade and logistics)
profile: Dou Zhenggang (钭正刚) started in textiles in Zhejiang in 1983 and built Hangzhou Jinjiang Group into a conglomerate spanning waste-to-energy, power, alumina/aluminium, non-ferrous metals and logistics. His family's China Jinjiang Environment became a leading waste-to-energy operator; the group now runs large alumina projects in China and Indonesia.
interesting_fact: His Hangzhou Jinjiang Group signed an MoU to supply alumina to Aluminium Bahrain (Alba), one of the world's largest smelters, and has built alumina refineries from Shanxi to West Kalimantan, Indonesia.
deep_cut_fact: The World Bank's IFC backed his early power business: it lent up to $20 million to China Green to consolidate Jinjiang's plants, including a 12 MW waste-to-energy plant in Yuhang, Hangzhou, burning municipal solid waste, and plants fired by bone coal and low-grade coal.
notes: Low public profile; no official group website or published contact found. A possible indirect route is via Zheneng Jinjiang Environment (SGX-listed, formerly China Jinjiang Environment) investor relations, but the Dou family's stake there has been reduced. Name sometimes romanised 'Tou Zhenggang'.

name: Sam Tarascio
current_role: Non-executive Founding Director, Salta Properties (from 1 Jan 2026)
profile: Sicilian-born (1944) Melbourne property developer who emigrated to Australia aged five. A former pharmaceutical salesman at Hoechst, he built a warehouse for the company in 1972 and founded Salta Properties, now one of Australia's largest private industrial/logistics property groups (also Westgate Logistics, since sold). His son Sam runs Salta; he owns Taralinga Estate olive grove.
interesting_fact: His Taralinga Estate olive oil on the Mornington Peninsula has won gold medals at the New York International Olive Oil Competition.
deep_cut_fact: Taralinga continues a family olive-pressing tradition started around 1930 by his grandfather Salvatore 'Turi' Tarascio in Vizzini, Sicily, his birthplace.
notes: Inducted into Property Council of Australia Hall of Fame. Low media profile; route via Salta Properties general inbox. Note his son (also Sam) is Salta MD - don't confuse the two.

name: Pan Shiyi
current_role: Co-founder and board member, SOHO China (stepped down as chairman in 2022)
profile: Born 1963 in Gansu, Pan co-founded SOHO China with his wife Zhang Xin in 1995 and built it into a leading developer of landmark commercial property in Beijing and Shanghai, listed in Hong Kong. In 2022 the couple left management (remaining on the board) to focus on the arts and philanthropy, and are now based mainly in the US.
interesting_fact: He had a film role: he starred as a lonely real-estate developer, 'Li Wenqing', in the 2006 romantic film Aspirin (阿司匹林).
deep_cut_fact: On 14 Nov 2019 (his 56th birthday) he announced on Weibo 'I'm going to learn Python', calling it the 'best-evolved' computer language. The post went viral in China's tech community.
notes: Once one of China's most-followed Weibo users; now low-profile and US-based. No current published office/press contact found (SOHO China site pages 404). Best route is probably via SOHO China's HKEX-listed company secretary/IR or via Zhang Xin's arts/philanthropy channels.

name: David Capobianco
current_role: CEO & Managing Partner, Five Point Infrastructure (formerly Five Point Energy); Chairman of LandBridge (NYSE: LB) and PowerBridge
profile: Founded Five Point Energy (now Five Point Infrastructure) in 2012 after co-founding Vulcan Capital's private equity group. Five Point built Permian water business WaterBridge and land platform LandBridge (IPO 2024, 270k+ acres). Its new PowerBridge unit is developing gigawatt-scale powered data-center campuses, including 2 GW in Reeves County, TX.
interesting_fact: He pitches the Permian Basin as a rival to Northern Virginia as a data-center hub, citing its land, cheap gas, fiber, and produced water for cooling. He has argued that nuclear power, possibly small modular reactors sited at data centers, is the only route to fully renewable data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vulcan he worked in Salomon Brothers' Energy Corporate Finance Group and on the investment teams of Harvest Partners and Greenhill Capital Partners. He later chaired Vulcan Energy Corp. (formerly Plains Resources) and chaired the compensation committee of Plains All American Pipeline. Duke BA, Harvard MBA.
notes: A strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast: he has spoken on the Cool Vector podcast/Substack and speaks publicly about the Permian, powered land and data centers. For media, go through Kekst CNC (LandBridge's PR firm) or the LandBridge IR address. The Kekst address appeared in older releases, so check that it is still current.

name: Alexander Dzhaparidze
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Eurasia Drilling Company; London-based investor (reported exit from all Russian assets in 2022)
profile: Russian-Georgian oilfield-services entrepreneur. He bought used seismic gear abroad in the 1990s, built PetroAlliance and sold it to Schlumberger. In 2004 he bought Lukoil's drilling arm for $130M and turned it into Eurasia Drilling, Russia's biggest onshore driller. Schlumberger's bids for EDC were blocked, and he reportedly exited Russian assets in 2022.
interesting_fact: He collects ancient daggers. In 2016 he bought a yacht and renamed it 'Here Comes the Sun' after the Beatles song.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Makhachkala, Dagestan in 1955, holds a Doctor of Science from Moscow's Gubkin oil and gas university, and early on ran MD SEIS, a seismic-survey joint venture.
notes: Very private, with no personal website or social accounts found. EDC's website (eurasiadrilling.com) no longer resolves. Forbes now lists him as a former billionaire (real-time 2023). Wikipedia mentions a 2015-16 UK SFO probe into his Soma Oil & Gas, closed in 2016 with no action. Avoid the topic.

name: Charles Zhengyao Lu
current_role: Co-founder of Cotti Coffee (founded 2022); former chairman of Luckin Coffee and Car Inc.
profile: Fujian-born serial entrepreneur who founded rental-car firm Car Inc. (2007, HK IPO 2014) and ride-hailing UCAR, and was the angel backer and chairman of Luckin Coffee (Nasdaq IPO 2019). After Luckin's 2020 accounting scandal he was removed as chairman. In 2022 he and Qian Zhiya started rival chain Cotti Coffee, reported at about 15,000 stores by 2025.
interesting_fact: Cotti Coffee, his comeback venture, grew to about 15,000 stores in 28 countries within three years of its October 2022 launch.
deep_cut_fact: Born in 1969 in Pingnan County, Fujian, he studied industrial electrical automation at the University of Science and Technology Beijing (1991) and spent two years as a civil servant in Shijiazhuang before quitting in 1993 to start a business in Beijing's Zhongguancun tech district.
notes: Sensitive: the 2020 Luckin fraud led to a US$180M SEC penalty, a Beijing court ordered him to repay about CNY1.9B (yicaiglobal.com), and a Dec 2025 report says he lost control of his Luckin shares. He is probably no longer a billionaire. Very low public profile, with no personal channels found.

name: Denis Frolov
current_role: Major shareholder/co-owner, Astra Group (MOEX: ASTR, Astra Linux); co-founder of Varton group
profile: Denis Frolov bought 80% of NPO RusBITech, developer of the Astra Linux operating system, in 2017; it became Astra Group, which IPO'd on the Moscow Exchange in 2023 and supplies software to the Russian state as Western vendors exited. He also co-founded lighting/electronics group Varton (mid-2000s), has stakes in Sistematika and Baikal Electronics, and dairy interests.
interesting_fact: After Astra's 2023 IPO he was reported as only the second Russian to become a dollar billionaire from software, after Eugene Kaspersky.
deep_cut_fact: A Higher School of Economics graduate, he spent about seven years at dairy maker Wimm-Bill-Dann, rising from investment analyst to development director, before moving into tech.
notes: Russia-based; Astra serves the Russian government and defence-linked customers, so check sanctions/compliance before any outreach. Very low public profile. Contacts come from 2023 press releases and may be outdated; astra.ru was not reachable from here.

name: Valery Kustov
current_role: Chairman of the board and main shareholder (~42%) of EFKO Group (Russia); under arrest in Moscow since July 2026
profile: Russian entrepreneur (b. 1961) who co-founded EFKO with partners in 1994 on the base of an essential-oils plant in Alekseyevka, Belgorod region. EFKO grew into one of Russia's largest food companies, with sunflower oil, mayonnaise, industrial fats and brands such as Sloboda, Altero and DeOlio, and in 2025 it bought Bunge's former Russian oilseed assets.
interesting_fact: EFKO started as a small perfume and essential-oil producer privatised in the 1990s and was repurposed to make sunflower oil and mayonnaise. Today it also works in biotech, including sweet proteins.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s he worked at the 'Deviz' electronics plant in Alekseyevka. He then founded the business on the town's 'Efirnoye' essential-oil plant together with colleagues, bringing over former Deviz staff.
notes: CAUTION: detained in Moscow on 30 July 2026 on large-scale fraud charges over a drone project ('Transport of the Future', spun off from EFKO), with a court-ordered arrest until at least 29 Sept 2026. Unsuitable for outreach at present. The RBC deep-cut source sits behind a paywall or login; the detail was seen via search snippet.

name: Christian Herz
current_role: Managing director and ~45% owner, Mayfair Vermögensverwaltung SE (Herz family office), Hamburg
profile: Grandson of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz and son of Günter Herz, who ran Tchibo for almost 35 years. After Günter and his sister Daniela were bought out of Tchibo in 2003 they built Hamburg family office Mayfair, whose investments have included Puma and DNV GL; Christian owns about 45% and helps steer investment decisions as a managing director.
interesting_fact: Mayfair was once a major Puma shareholder, selling its stake into PPR's 2007 takeover offer, and held 36.5% of ship-classification group DNV GL until selling back to the Det Norske Veritas Foundation in December 2017.
notes: Very private; no interviews, website or social accounts found for him or Mayfair. Avoid the Herz family disputes and Vapiano. Route would be via the family office's registered Hamburg office (no published email found).

name: Michaela Herz
current_role: Managing director and ~45% owner, Mayfair Vermögensverwaltungs SE (Herz family holding, Hamburg)
profile: Granddaughter of Tchibo co-founder Max Herz and daughter of Günter Herz, who ran Tchibo for ~35 years. After Günter and his sister sold their Tchibo stake in 2003 they founded Mayfair, a Hamburg family holding investing in companies, bonds and real estate; Michaela owns about 45% and helps steer investment decisions.
interesting_fact: Mayfair's first big deal was a 17% (later 27%) stake in Puma in 2004, sold to PPR at €330/share; it then bought Germanischer Lloyd for €575m, which expanded into oil & gas and renewable-energy services before merging into DNV GL in 2013 (stake sold 2017).
notes: Extremely private — almost no public footprint under her own name. Energy angle for the podcast: Mayfair's Germanischer Lloyd/DNV GL investment. Aunt Daniela Herz-Schnoeckel's branch has exited Mayfair (Forbes). Mayfair website did not load; no published contact found.

name: Anton Fedun
current_role: Hotel owner / managing director, The Ampersand Hotel (South Kensington) and Vintry & Mercer (City of London); Lukoil shareholder
profile: Anton Fedun's fortune stems from Lukoil, Russia's No. 2 oil producer, where his father Leonid Fedun was a long-time controlling shareholder and in 2018 transferred part of his stake to him. A dual Russian-UK citizen living in London, he runs his own boutique hotels: The Ampersand in South Kensington and Vintry & Mercer, a 92-room City hotel opened in 2019.
interesting_fact: He is hands-on in hospitality rather than oil: he is managing director of Vintry & Mercer, built on the City site where medieval Vintners unloaded wine and Mercers traded silks and textiles, hence the name.
deep_cut_fact: In an Oct 2020 Boutique Hotel News video interview he discussed repurposing Vintry & Mercer and The Ampersand during the pandemic, courting London's local market and designing distinctive concepts; Vintry & Mercer's design deliberately references its City neighbourhood's history.
notes: Private; no personal channels found. Best route is via the hotels (Ampersand / Vintry & Mercer, an SLH member). Russian oil-wealth links (Lukoil) mean sanctions sensitivity should be checked before outreach. SLH journal Q&A (journal.slh.com, post 7096) describes him as MD of Vintry & Mercer.

name: Judith Neilson
current_role: Founder and director, White Rabbit Gallery (Sydney); philanthropist and Platinum Asset Management shareholder
profile: Zimbabwe-born former graphic designer and Sydney philanthropist whose fortune stems from her stake in Platinum Asset Management, the global equities manager co-founded by her ex-husband Kerr Neilson (divorced 2015). She founded and solely funds the White Rabbit Gallery of post-2000 Chinese contemporary art, backed the Phoenix arts spaces in Chippendale, and set up the A$100M Judith Neilson Institute for Journalism and Ideas.
interesting_fact: White Rabbit holds one of the world's largest collections of 21st-century Chinese art; in 2024 she said it held work by around 800 artists and 'there were 4,000 pieces the last time I counted'. Her interest began on trips to Beijing in the late 1990s.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 she endowed a Chair of Architecture at UNSW to develop housing solutions for displaced people such as climate refugees and disaster or conflict victims, and in 2017 a Chair of Contemporary Art at UNSW. She was made a Member of the Order of Australia (AM) in 2016.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed. Note: neilson.org.au (contact@neilson.org.au) is the Neilson Foundation run by ex-husband Kerr Neilson, NOT her - do not use. Best route is via White Rabbit Gallery or the Judith Neilson Institute. Arts/journalism focus rather than energy.

name: Peter-Alexander Wacker
current_role: Chair of the Supervisory Board, Wacker Chemie AG (since 2008; re-elected 2023)
profile: Great-grandson of founder Alexander Wacker, he owns roughly 10% of Munich-based Wacker Chemie. After ten years at BMW he joined Wacker's board in 1993, became CEO when it went public in 2005, and moved to chair the supervisory board in 2008. Wacker is a major maker of silicones and of hyperpure polysilicon for solar cells and semiconductors.
interesting_fact: Energy/chips angle: Wacker began producing polysilicon, the base material for solar cells and semiconductors, at a new plant in Bradley County (Charleston), Tennessee, in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: He collects elephant figures from around the world because elephants symbolize strength to him, which is why his holding company is named Blue Elephant. He was also named Germany's family businessman of the year in 2006.

public_contacts.value: Manuela.Dollinger@wacker.com (Wacker Media Relations, as listed in company profile)

notes: Holds a doctorate (listed as Dr.). Polysilicon for solar and semiconductors is a strong energy/data-center hook. Approach via Wacker corporate communications in Munich.

name: KR Sridhar
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE)
profile: Tamil Nadu-born engineer (MS nuclear engineering, PhD mechanical engineering, UIUC) who directed the University of Arizona's Space Technologies Laboratory, building Mars oxygen-generation tech for NASA. After NASA shelved its Mars Surveyor 2001 lander he co-founded Ion America (2001), renamed Bloom Energy, whose solid-oxide fuel cells now supply on-site power to AI data centers; IPO 2018.
interesting_fact: Bloom has become an on-site 'bring your own power' supplier for AI data centers, including a 2025 collaboration with Oracle to deliver power to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure sites at the speed of AI build-outs.
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored the 1997 Solid State Ionics paper 'Oxygen production on Mars using solid oxide electrolysis' (with B.T. Vaniman): a zirconia cell splitting Martian CO2 into oxygen. Bloom's fuel cell is essentially that Mars device run in reverse. Fortune named him one of five young innovators in 2000.
notes: Highly on-topic for an energy/data-center podcast; Bloom actively promotes its data-center power story. Media contact on releases: Katja Gagen (press@bloomenergy.com). Also an independent director at C3.ai (per Wikipedia).

name: Wang Jianyi
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, Futong Group Co., Ltd. (Hangzhou); deputy to the 14th National People's Congress
profile: Wang Jianyi (王建沂, b. 1963, Fuyang, Zhejiang) left a post-office job in 1987 to make telephone wire, formally founded Hangzhou Futong Group in 1994 and pioneered optical-cable production in Zhejiang (JV with Japan's Showa Electric, 1995). Futong became a major maker of optical fibre, cable and fibre preforms. Since 2024 the group has faced debt problems and its listed unit was delisted.
interesting_fact: In 2000 he pledged to crack optical-fibre preform technology, then a foreign-held bottleneck in China's fibre industry; Futong went on to help set preform standards and in 2014 began building what it called the world's largest single integrated preform-fibre-cable plant in Jiashan.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1982) was at the Fuyang post and telecom bureau. At 24 he left that 'iron rice bowl' and started making iron-core telephone wire with a few workers in a sub-40 m2 workshop built from bamboo poles and oil felt.
notes: Futong Group has been in financial distress since 2024 (court cases, frozen equity, delisting of Futong Information; Wang reportedly placed under high-consumption restrictions), so approach with care. Official site futong.com.cn did not load. Former CPPCC member; senior figure in the Zhejiang federation of industry and commerce.

name: Wee Wei Ling
current_role: Executive Director (Sustainability Partnerships, Lifestyle & Asset), Pan Pacific Hotels Group; director, Kheng Leong and the Wee Foundation
profile: Eldest child of the late UOB patriarch Wee Cho Yaw. At UOL's Pan Pacific Hotels Group she oversees owned hotels, the St. Gregory spa and Si Chuan Dou Hua restaurant brands and the group's sustainability and community partnerships; she also sits on the family's Kheng Leong property firm and Wee Foundation boards.
interesting_fact: A champion of inclusive hiring, she has pushed companies to treat employing people with special needs as corporate strategy rather than charity, and chaired Project We Care, the People's Association's CEO network for corporate volunteerism, from 2011.
deep_cut_fact: She personally curated Pan Pacific's corporate art collection of local artists, published as the book 'Along the Journey', and co-founded the performing-arts charity Extra.Ordinary People with her cousin Wee Boo Kuan; she kept a Delia Prvacki ceramic bought in 1997 even after selling the hotel it was in.
notes: Gives lifestyle-press interviews (Peak, Prestige, Tatler, Sleeper) on sustainability and inclusive hiring; best route is Pan Pacific Hotels Group corporate communications (Singapore) via its Mynewsdesk newsroom.

name: Wee Wei Chi
current_role: Board member, Kheng Leong Co. (Wee family property and investment company), Singapore
profile: Younger daughter of the late Wee Cho Yaw (d. Feb 2024), longtime chairman of United Overseas Bank; her wealth stems from the family's UOB and related holdings. She sits on the board of Kheng Leong, the family's commercial property development and investment arm, and is married to David Eu of the Eu Yan Sang TCM family. Brother Wee Ee Cheong is UOB CEO.
interesting_fact: She studied fine arts, earning a bachelor's degree from Moravian University in Pennsylvania, an unusual path in a banking dynasty.
notes: Very private; no public contact or social accounts found. Forbes lists her as a former (dropped-off) billionaire. Any approach would likely need to go through the Wee family office / Kheng Leong, which publishes no contact for her.

name: Alexander Rinke
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Celonis (Munich/New York)
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded process-mining and 'process intelligence' software company Celonis in 2011 with fellow Munich students Bastian Nominacher and Martin Klenk. Celonis was valued at $13bn in 2022, and Rinke owns about 15%. As co-CEO he is now pitching Celonis as the data layer for enterprise AI, unveiling the Celonis Context Model in 2026.
interesting_fact: Celonis was bootstrapped at first because investors found process mining too hard to understand. To get past gatekeepers, the founders hand-wrote about 1,500 letters to CEOs, which helped land Siemens as a customer.
deep_cut_fact: Celonis began with a 2011 student-consultancy (Academy Consult) IT job at broadcaster Bayerischer Rundfunk. The trio wrote simple software to measure gaps between timestamps and showed on a few A4 printouts how processes taking up to five days could be cut to hours.
notes: Very media-accessible: he speaks at WEF Davos and Web Summit and appears on tech podcasts. Celonis PR (press@celonis.com) handles interview and meeting requests. His AI/data-infrastructure angle fits a data-centre podcast.

name: Azman Hashim
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, AmBank Group; Chairman, Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers
profile: Malaysian banker (born 1939) who bought the Arab-Malaysian Merchant Bank in 1982 and built it into AmBank Group (AMMB Holdings), chairing it until 2019 and retiring fully in 2022. He holds stakes in RCE Capital and Amcorp Properties and still chairs bodies including the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers and the Malaysia-Japan Economic Association.
interesting_fact: He summited Mount Kinabalu (4,095m) on 31 October 2023 at age 84, his second ascent after first climbing it at 71 in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He passed the Senior Cambridge exam with first-class marks at 15, then trained as a chartered accountant in Perth, Australia (1955-60) on a Colombo Plan scholarship; his grandmother came from Imabari in Japan's Ehime prefecture.
notes: Retired from AmBank; best route is via the Asian Institute of Chartered Bankers (aicb.org.my) or AmBank corporate communications. Received a Chartered Banker Institute (UK) lifetime achievement award in June 2025 (Bernama). No personal contact published.

name: Chandubhai Virani
current_role: Cofounder and chairman/managing director, Balaji Wafers Pvt. Ltd. (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: A farmer's son from Jamnagar district, Virani and his brothers moved to Rajkot in 1974 and worked at the Astron Cinema canteen. In 1982 they began making their own potato wafers, and Balaji grew into one of India's largest regional snack brands. The brothers became billionaires after selling a minority stake to General Atlantic in January 2026.
interesting_fact: For years he turned down stake offers from PepsiCo, General Mills and about 50 private-equity firms, saying he was there to run the company, not sell it. The 2026 General Atlantic minority deal was the family's first outside investment.
deep_cut_fact: At Astron Cinema he earned Rs 90 a month and repaired torn seats after night shows in exchange for a plate of chorafali. He started making wafers after 'changing suppliers three times'.
notes: His Vad plant (2003) ran about 5,000 kg of potatoes per hour, a record at the time. He gives interviews mostly in Gujarati/Hindi media. contact@balajiwafers.com is the company's general inbox.

name: Kanjibhai Virani
current_role: Co-founder, Balaji Wafers Pvt Ltd (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: Kanjibhai (Kanubhai) Virani co-founded Balaji Wafers with brothers Chandubhai and Bhikhubhai; the Rajkot firm grew from wafers sold at a cinema canteen into one of India's largest regional snack makers (chips, namkeen, noodles, confectionery). The family became billionaires after agreeing in Jan 2026 to sell a ~7% minority stake to General Atlantic; the next generation is increasingly running the business.
interesting_fact: The brothers began in 1974 selling wafers from the canteen of Astron Cinema in Rajkot, where they had done odd jobs; wafers were made at home until the first factory opened in 1989. Balaji is said to hold ~90% of Gujarat's chips market.
deep_cut_fact: Their first venture failed: their farmer father Popatbhai sold ancestral farmland to give the brothers Rs 20,000, which they put into farm equipment and lost, before turning to snacks.
notes: Kanjibhai is commonly listed as 'Kanubhai Virani'. Chandubhai Virani is the public face of the company; approach likely via the company. GA deal announced 22 Jan 2026 (https://www.generalatlantic.com/media-article/balaji-wafers-announces-strategic-investment-from-general-atlantic/).

name: Ellis Short
current_role: Founder, Kildare Partners (distressed European real estate private equity)
profile: American financier (b. 1960, Independence, Missouri) who became president of Dallas private equity firm Lone Star Funds and ran its Asian operations, then founded Kildare Partners in 2013 to buy distressed European property and non-performing loans. Owned Sunderland AFC 2008-2018.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he paid about GBP 23m for Skibo Castle in Scotland, the members-only club famous for hosting Madonna and Guy Ritchie's 2000 wedding.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he was an engineer: he earned a mechanical engineering degree from Missouri University of Science and Technology (then Missouri-Rolla) in 1983 and started his career at General Electric.
notes: Very private; rarely gives interviews. Only route found is Kildare Partners (offices in Dallas/Westlake TX, London, Dublin, Bermuda). Returned to the US from London in 2017.

name: Diane Briere de l'Isle
current_role: Chair, Moondance Foundation (Welsh grant-making charity, reg. 1139224)
profile: Diane Briere de l'Isle Engelhardt OBE is married to Henry Engelhardt, founder and former CEO of Cardiff-based car insurer Admiral Group; their fortune comes from Admiral shares after its 2004 LSE flotation. The couple set up the Moondance Foundation in 2010, funded by regularly donating Admiral shares. She chairs it, and it has given away well over £76m, mostly to causes in Wales.
interesting_fact: The Moondance Foundation is funded by gifts of the couple's Admiral shares. When the pandemic hit, she launched a Covid-19 Relief Fund, and the foundation later committed a further £10m to Welsh organisations.
deep_cut_fact: She and Henry Engelhardt received the First Minister's Special Award at the Welsh Government's St David Awards 2026.
notes: Wealth is shared with husband Henry Engelhardt; the Rich List entry is joint. I couldn't verify any formal Admiral role for her, so don't describe her as an Admiral co-founder. The foundation's published contact is the best route. Moondance Cancer Initiative is a related Welsh initiative.

name: James Cameron
current_role: Filmmaker (Lightstorm Entertainment); director of the Avatar franchise; National Geographic explorer and ocean-exploration advocate
profile: Canadian-born (now also New Zealand citizen, 2025) director of The Terminator, Titanic and the Avatar films, three of the four highest-grossing movies ever; his films have grossed roughly $9-10bn. Much of his wealth comes from Avatar profit participation. He developed his own 3D camera and performance-capture tech, and released Avatar: Fire and Ash in December 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he became the first person to make a solo dive to the bottom of the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep) in the Deepsea Challenger, a sub he helped develop; he also sold The Terminator script for $1 on condition he could direct it.
deep_cut_fact: After dropping out of Fullerton College he worked as a truck driver and high-school janitor, teaching himself special effects in the USC library; he financed his first short film, Xenogenesis (1978), by borrowing money from a consortium of dentists. A frog species, Pristimantis jamescameroni, is named after him.
notes: Lives in New Zealand. No personal social accounts or published personal contact found; approaches go via Lightstorm Entertainment or his talent agency/publicist. Strong energy/sustainability angle: plant-based food businesses, OceanX adviser, ocean exploration tech.

name: Jerry Seinfeld
current_role: Stand-up comedian, writer and producer; co-creator of 'Seinfeld'; touring comic
profile: Jerry Seinfeld (b. 1954, raised in Massapequa, NY) co-created and starred in NBC's 'Seinfeld' (1989-98) with Larry David; his billionaire fortune comes mainly from his share of the show's syndication and streaming revenue plus touring. He still tours stand-up and has made Netflix specials, 'Comedians in Cars Getting Coffee', 'Bee Movie' and the 2024 film 'Unfrosted'.
interesting_fact: A serious car collector with about 150 cars, mostly Porsches; the centerpiece has been Steve McQueen's Porsche 917 (chassis 022) driven in the 1971 film 'Le Mans'.
deep_cut_fact: At 16 he volunteered on Kibbutz Sa'ar in Israel; he later started at SUNY Oswego before transferring to Queens College (BA communications and theater, 1976), doing open-mic nights at Budd Friedman's Improv while still a student. He has practiced Transcendental Meditation since about 1972.
notes: Celebrity; outreach realistically via his talent representation/publicist rather than direct. Car collecting and his long-form interview podcast appearances are natural hooks; not an energy/data-center figure.

name: Weijian Shan
current_role: Executive Chairman and Co-Founder, PAG (Asia-focused alternative investment firm); independent director, Alibaba Group
profile: Beijing-born (1954) private equity investor who spent six years as a sent-down youth in the Gobi Desert before studying in the US (MBA USF, PhD UC Berkeley). After the World Bank, Wharton faculty and J.P. Morgan, he was TPG/Newbridge's top Asia dealmaker (incl. Korea First Bank), then built PAG from 2010 into a ~$50B+ AUM Asia alternatives firm. Author of three books; British Museum trustee.
interesting_fact: His 2019 memoir 'Out of the Gobi: My Story of China and America' recounts laboring in the Gobi during the Cultural Revolution; Janet Yellen was one of his Berkeley thesis advisors.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wall Street he was an assistant professor at the Wharton School for six years, where he founded the academic journal China Economic Review; he first came to Beijing's Institute of Foreign Trade in 1975 to study English.
notes: Very public: frequent op-ed writer (FT, NYT, Foreign Affairs) and conference speaker; books (Money Games, Money Machine) give a natural hook. ir@pag.com is investor-only; info@pag.com (Hong Kong HQ) is the general route.

name: Qiu Lingyun
current_role: Former board secretary of Smoore International (HKEX: 6969); not listed among senior management in the 2025 annual report
profile: Smoore early executive (male, b. c.1975) whose fortune came from his stake in Smoore International, the world's largest maker of vaping devices and components (clients include BAT, Japan Tobacco, NJOY), which listed in Hong Kong in July 2020. He was CFO of Smoore Shenzhen 2011-2016, then board secretary handling board matters and investor relations.
interesting_fact: Smoore's 2020 Hong Kong IPO briefly made several of its early managers billionaires; Qiu appeared on the Forbes list only in 2021, after the shares peaked.
deep_cut_fact: He studied industrial international commerce (engineering degree) at Shanghai University, graduating in 1999, and earned an executive MBA from CEIBS in 2015.
notes: Very low profile; appears to have left the Smoore management team (absent from 2025 annual report). Smoore's IR mailbox IR@smooreholdings.com exists but is the company's, not his. Vaping is a sensitive sector.

name: Andrew Brode
current_role: Non-Executive Director, RWS Holdings plc (interim Chair Jan–Oct 2026, succeeded by Patrick De Smedt)
profile: Chartered accountant who sold a family publishing business to Wolters Kluwer, bought legal journal Eclipse in 1990, and merged it with translation firm RWS in 1995, building RWS into a global AI-driven language and IP services group via acquisitions. Long-time RWS chairman and major shareholder; also a key backer/chair of Learning Technologies Group.
interesting_fact: Took over as interim chair of RWS when the chair left at end-2025, then handed over to ex-Microsoft EMEA chairman Patrick De Smedt in Oct 2026 while staying on the board.
deep_cut_fact: An Old Edwardian (left 1959), he funded half of King Edward's School Birmingham's £5m 2012 appeal and much of the school's new sports hall, named The Andrew Brode Sports Centre.
notes: Passionate mentor of young entrepreneurs (coached LTG's Jonathan Satchell, Cera's Mahiben Maruthappu) — good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Route via RWS company secretary or MHP.

name: Lance Gokongwei
current_role: President & CEO, JG Summit Holdings (also chairs key affiliates such as Cebu Pacific, Robinsons Land and Universal Robina)
profile: Only son of the late John Gokongwei Jr., Lance Gokongwei runs JG Summit, a Philippine conglomerate spanning Cebu Pacific airline, snack maker Universal Robina, Robinsons property and retail, banking, petrochemicals and stakes in power and telecom. A Penn graduate (finance and applied science, 1988), he is shifting the group from owner-operator to an active investor model.
interesting_fact: Cebu Pacific, the family's budget airline, has been in talks for an order of up to 150 new aircraft, among the largest in Philippine aviation history.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was management trainee at Universal Robina selling Jack 'n Jill snacks door to door to supermarkets and sari-sari stores, paid P2,000 a month and driving an old Datsun with a broken air-conditioner, as he told PLV graduates in 2019.
notes: Low-key, rarely gives interviews; corporate route via JG Summit IR/corporate communications. Group has power and data-related interests relevant to energy podcast.

name: Jason Gardner
current_role: Founder and board director, Marqeta (NASDAQ: MQ); director, Pagaya Technologies
profile: New Jersey-born Jason Gardner co-founded rent-payments startup PropertyBridge (sold to MoneyGram in 2007), then founded Marqeta in 2010, building a card-issuing API used by DoorDash, Square and others; it IPO'd in 2021. He handed the CEO role to Simon Khalaf in 2023 and stepped down as executive chairman in June 2024, remaining a director with roughly 40% voting power.
interesting_fact: As a teen he worked at a thrift store and sold T-shirts on trains to Grateful Dead concerts; in his 20s he worked as an assistant to Senator John McCain.
deep_cut_fact: His first company, Vertical Think, was an early Elance/Upwork-style marketplace matching web developers with small projects, which he called 'more a lifestyle business'. Marqeta's original idea was a debit card that could hold many merchant coupons such as Groupon deals.
