current_role: Founder of Yanbal International (Peruvian direct-sales cosmetics); handed CEO role to daughter Janine Belmont in 2011
profile: Fernando Belmont Anderson founded Yanbal in Lima in 1967 after joining his father's Botica Francesa, the Peruvian Helena Rubinstein franchisee, and deciding to make cosmetics locally and sell them direct. He and brother Eduardo (later Belcorp founder) split their interests in 1988; Fernando took Yanbal into Spain and much of Latin America. He stepped back at 70 in 2011.
interesting_fact: He and his brother Eduardo started out together in Yanbal, then split in 1988 and became direct competitors, each building a billion-dollar door-to-door cosmetics company (Yanbal and Belcorp).
deep_cut_fact: Yanbal's model came from a problem at his father's Helena Rubinstein franchise: imports were too pricey for Peruvians, so he studied leading beauty brands and adopted local manufacturing plus the 'party plan' of home sales gatherings. The Yanbal name was inspired by his daughter Janine.
notes: Forbes lists him as 'Juan Fernando'; usually known as Fernando Belmont. Born c.1941; no death report found but no recent public activity either. Very private; daughter Janine Belmont (Yanbal CEO) is the public face. Last on Forbes list 2014.

name: Mehmet Omer Koc
current_role: Chairman, Koç Holding (since Feb 2016); also chairs Tüpraş and Koç University's board of trustees
profile: Mehmet Ömer Koç (b. 1962, Ankara), second son of Rahmi Koç, is third-generation leader of Turkey's largest conglomerate, Koç Holding (energy/refining via Tüpraş, autos, appliances via Arçelik/Beko, banking). He joined the group in 1992, led its Energy Group, became vice chairman in 2008 and chairman in 2016 after his brother Mustafa's death.
interesting_fact: A major art patron, he founded the Istanbul contemporary art space Arter in 2010, sponsors the Istanbul Biennial and Turkey's Venice Biennale pavilion, and is reputed to hold one of the finest private collections of Ottoman objects and books; he also sits on the Bilderberg steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: Before his MBA at Columbia Business School (1989), he earned a BA in Ancient Greek from Columbia College (1985), and began his career at Kofisa Trading in Geneva before joining Koç Holding as a finance coordinator in 1992.

public_contacts.value: https://www.koc.com.tr/investor-relations (Koç Holding Investor Relations; contact via IR menu)

notes: Known for avoiding media; lives largely in London. Strong energy angle via Tüpraş (Turkey's largest refiner) and the group's former Energy Group, which he led. Route via Koç Holding corporate communications. Not to be confused with a younger Mehmet Ömer Koç on the board of Bilkom.

name: Nezih Barut
current_role: Chairman, Abdi İbrahim İlaç (Türkiye's largest pharmaceutical company)
profile: A 1976 Istanbul University pharmacy graduate, Barut joined Abdi İbrahim (founded 1912 as a pharmacy by Abdi İbrahim Barut) the same year and has run the family company since 1981, institutionalising and internationalising it into Türkiye's top drugmaker. He is a long-time chairman of the pharma manufacturers' association İEİS, invests in startups via Revo Capital, and is a Fenerbahçe board figure.
interesting_fact: He has led Abdi İbrahim for over four decades, having worked up through roles such as production manager and general manager after joining in 1976.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he became the first Turkish businessman awarded the Prince Henrik honorary medal by the Danish Export Association.
notes: Fluent English speaker per his İEİS CV. Also partner in Revo Capital (Turkish VC) and was named a Fenerbahçe vice president. Route via Abdi İbrahim corporate communications or İEİS.

name: Ki-Won Choi
current_role: Chair, SK Happiness Foundation (SK Group's social-innovation foundation); also runs the Wooran Foundation (arts)
profile: Choi (Chey) Ki-won is the younger sister of SK Group chairman Chey Tae-won and a shareholder in holding company SK Inc., the source of her wealth (SK spans energy via SK Innovation, chips via SK hynix, and telecoms). She chairs the SK Happiness Foundation, which develops and tests its own solutions to social problems, and is known as an active private investor.
interesting_fact: Under her chairmanship the SK Happiness Foundation shifted around 2019 from grant-making to building its own problem-solving models, e.g. a low-floor-bus boarding reservation app for wheelchair users and braille literacy tools for visually impaired children.
deep_cut_fact: She runs the Wooran Foundation, a culture-and-arts foundation in Seongsu-dong, Seoul, named after her late mother Park Gye-hee, former director of the Walkerhill Art Center.
notes: Romanised variously as Choi/Chey Ki-won/Gi-won. Very private; no interviews found. Energy link is indirect via SK Inc./SK Innovation. Route via SK Happiness Foundation.

name: Wang Bufeng
current_role: Founder/chairman, Shandong Runfeng (Realforce) Group, Jining, Shandong (solar PV manufacturing & power); current status not confirmed
profile: Wang Bufeng (王步峰) founded Runfeng (润峰, 'Real Force'/Realforce), a Jining, Shandong group that made solar cells and modules (Realforce Power) and developed PV power plants, and later moved into other energy businesses. Hurun listed him 2012-2019. No recent public information on his activities was found.
interesting_fact: In Jan 2010 Shandong Runfeng Group switched on a 1 MW solar plant in Weishan, Jining, billed as Shandong's first grid-connected PV plant and China's first solar plant invested in by a private company.
deep_cut_fact: As chairman of Realforce Power in 2011 he said the company had completed nearly 50 MW of projects across China since its very first 1 MW project in early 2009, including a 2.5 MW rooftop array at a Shandong institute of technology, one of China's largest rooftop systems then.
notes: Hurun data: 润峰 / Real Force, Jining, Shandong, 'new energy products manufacturing'. The source for the interesting fact is a blog repost of a 2010 news item, so treat it as secondary. Old company sites (realforcepower.com etc.) don't resolve. No current contacts found. Chinese registry and news sites (Baidu/Qichacha) were not reachable from this environment.

name: Amit Agarwal
current_role: Founder and CEO, Standard Template Labs (STLabs); director at Datadog and Vercel
profile: Datadog's longtime product chief: he joined as roughly employee no. 8 in 2012, was Chief Product Officer until 2022 and President until the end of 2024, then moved to Datadog's board. After a stint as a general partner at ICONIQ Growth he founded STLabs, an AI-native IT service-management startup in New York that launched in March 2026 with a $49M seed round led by ICONIQ and CRV.
interesting_fact: STLabs was the first company ICONIQ ever incubated and led a seed round for. ICONIQ had backed him at Datadog a decade earlier and described working with him again as 'Ten Years. Day Zero.'
deep_cut_fact: He was employee no. 8 at Datadog and stayed 13 years, through its growth from a developer tool to an enterprise standard. His new company's pitch is that IT should 'resolve, not route': AI agents fix requests instead of logging tickets.
notes: No longer Datadog president (left end of 2024; still a director, term to 2027). STLabs' contact form has a 'Press' topic and says a person replies within one business day, which is a good outreach route. He also joined Vercel's board in 2026. Strong fit for an AI/infra-software angle.

name: J Frederic Kerrest
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Vice Chairman of the Board, Okta, Inc.
profile: Frederic Kerrest co-founded identity-management company Okta with fellow Salesforce alumnus Todd McKinnon in 2009 and was its COO until November 2023. He oversaw strategy, corporate development, partnerships and Okta for Good, and remains vice chairman. Okta IPO'd in 2017. Before Okta he worked in sales and business development at Salesforce and in VC at Hummer Winblad.
interesting_fact: He wrote 'Zero to IPO', a Wall Street Journal bestseller that grew out of his 2019 podcast of the same name. Its 12 episodes each covered one step toward an IPO, from the idea to the first big screw-up.
deep_cut_fact: He started Okta in 2009 during the second semester of his final year at MIT Sloan (MBA '09). He launched the podcast because, over ten years, many entrepreneurs had phoned him asking for advice.
notes: An experienced podcast guest and host, so likely receptive. One profile says he founded the advisory firm Windproof Partners in 2025, but I could not verify it. His own X and LinkedIn accounts are not verified here.

name: Gary Burrell
profile: Co-founder of Garmin (with Min Kao, 1989) and avionics pioneer; died 12 June 2019 aged 81 at his home in Kansas.
notes: Deceased (June 12, 2019) per Garmin announcement: https://www.garmin.com.sg/news/press-release/garmin-announces-passing-co-founder-and-chairman-emeritus-gary-burrell/ . Name in source data misspelled 'Burrel'.

name: Rajesh Mehta
current_role: Promoter and executive chairman, Rajesh Exports Ltd (Bengaluru); barred from the securities market by SEBI since June 2026
profile: Born 1964 in Bengaluru, Mehta started trading silver jewellery, then in 1989 founded Rajesh Exports with brother Prashant in a 10-worker garage workshop. It grew into a huge gold refiner, manufacturer and retailer (Shubh Jewellers) and in 2015 bought Swiss refiner Valcambi for $400m. Since June 2026 SEBI has barred him over alleged revenue misstatement.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Rajesh Exports bought Valcambi of Balerna, Switzerland, described as the world's largest gold refiner, for about $400 million.
deep_cut_fact: He wanted to be a doctor. Instead he borrowed Rs 1,200 from his eldest brother Bipin, a bank employee, to start silver trading: he bought jewellery in Chennai and sold it to relatives in Rajkot.
notes: HIGH RISK: on 3 Jun 2026 SEBI barred Rajesh Exports and Mehta from the securities market over alleged misstatement of ~Rs15.15 lakh crore in revenue; confirmed 14 Oct 2026 (https://www.moneylife.in/article/sebi-confirms-interim-directions-on-rajesh-exports-retains-trading-ban-on-promoter-rajesh-mehta/81948.html). Mehta denies the allegations. Probably not a suitable guest right now.

name: Andreas E.Rihs
notes: Andy Rihs, co-founder and longtime CEO/chairman of Phonak/Sonova and backer of the BMC cycling team, died 18 April 2018 aged 75 (source: https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/cycling-supporter_swiss-entrepreneur-and-bmc-cycling-backer-andy-rihs-has-died/44058924).

name: Jacques Nickolet
current_role: Co-founder and Supervisory Board member, Altarea (Altarea Cogedim); owner of OAK Racing / Ligier Automotive
profile: Jacques Nicolet (correct spelling; born 1956 in Gigondas) was development director at Pierre & Vacances (1984-94) before co-founding French property developer Altarea with Alain Taravella in 1994. Altarea bought Cogedim in 2007 and became one of France's largest developers. He long chaired Altarea's supervisory board and now sits on it, while running a motorsport business.
interesting_fact: A gentleman racer, he has driven at the Le Mans 24 Hours about ten times since 2007, and in 2012 founded Onroak Automotive, the race-car maker now known as Ligier Automotive.
deep_cut_fact: He won the 2010 1000 km of Zhuhai in China as a driver. His team OAK Racing grew out of Saulnier Racing, rebadged in 2009 as OAK Racing Mazda Team France.
notes: The input spells him 'Nickolet'; the correct name is Jacques Nicolet. Altarea's governance page lists him as a supervisory board member. The Le Mans/Ligier motorsport angle is the most natural hook. The Hurun listing is from 2014-15 and his wealth is shared with Alain Taravella.

name: Chen Tian-Pu Brothers
profile: Listed on the Hurun Global Rich List 2014-2015 (~$1.1bn, real estate, 'Nanho'). English and Chinese searches (陈田柏/陳田柏, Nanho/南和) found no matching company or biography, so the family could not be identified.
notes: Unidentified; possibly a Taiwanese or Hong Kong property family with a romanisation mismatch. Not on any list since 2015. Need the original Hurun entry (company Chinese name) before further work. Not recommended as an outreach target.

name: Kartini Muljadi
profile: Indonesian judge-turned-notary and lawyer (founder of law firm Kartini Muljadi & Rekan) who built Tempo Scan Group, a pharmaceuticals and consumer-goods company. She died in Jakarta on 20 October 2025, aged 95.
notes: Deceased 20 Oct 2025 (source: https://www.thejakartapost.com/business/2025/10/21/tempo-scan-group-founder-kartini-muljadi-passes-away-at-95). The input lists her country as United States, but she was Indonesian.

name: Lin Yu-Chia
current_role: Deceased (reported to have died aged 100); founder of Taiwan Glass Industry Corp.
profile: Lin Yu-Chia (林玉嘉) founded Taiwan Glass Industry Corp. (台玻) in 1964 and handed control to sons Lin Pei-Feng (chairman) and Lin Pei-Shih in 2009. He was on Hurun lists in 2014-2015; an investor-community profile reports he died aged 100 (exact date not found).
notes: Death source is a non-news CMoney note (https://www.cmoney.tw/notes/note-detail.aspx?nid=173744); consistent with reports he turned 87 around 2002 (Business Today). Taiwan Glass is now run by son Lin Pei-Feng; not an outreach target.

name: Patrick Fung Yuk-bun (冯钰斌)
current_role: Executive Director, King Fook Holdings (HKEX:280); former Chairman of OCBC Wing Hang Bank (to 2022)
profile: Hong Kong banker who led family-controlled Wing Hang Bank for decades — joined 1976, director 1980, CEO 1992, chairman & CEO from 1996 — and steered its 2014 sale to Singapore's OCBC, staying on as chairman of OCBC Wing Hang until 2022. He now sits on the board of jeweller King Fook Holdings (chairs its ESG committee) and Miramar Hotel.
interesting_fact: He spent nearly 50 years with one bank: from joining Wing Hang in 1976 through its 2014 sale to OCBC and his chairmanship of the renamed OCBC Wing Hang Bank until 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond banking he has served as an adjunct professor at Hong Kong PolyU's School of Accounting and Finance and on the Board of Governors of the Hong Kong Philharmonic Society.

public_contacts.value: irenquiry@kingfook.com (King Fook Holdings IR, company he is a director of)

notes: Not to be confused with barrister Patrick Fung SC. Wealth largely from the OCBC sale of Wing Hang (2014). Executive vs non-executive status at King Fook differs between 2025 and 2026 annual reports. Roles from 2016 article may be dated.

name: Somchai Bencharongkul
profile: Listed once (Hurun Global 2015) with wealth from Total Access Communication (DTAC), the Thai mobile operator founded in 1989 by the Bencharongkul family and merged into True Corporation in 2023. No source found confirming a family member named Somchai; the well-documented DTAC founder is Boonchai Bencharongkul (b. 1954), eldest of four siblings who sold most of their DTAC shares in 2005.
notes: Identity unverified: Thai and English searches for 'Somchai/สมชาย Bencharongkul' found nothing; may be a Hurun mislabel for Boonchai (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boonchai_Bencharongkul) or a lesser-known sibling. Family vehicle is Benchachinda Holding. Recommend confirming before outreach.

name: Stanislaus Turnauer
current_role: Owner and Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Constantia Industries AG (Vienna)
profile: Born 1970, grandson of Constantia founder Herbert Turnauer and head of the discreet Turnauer family. He owns Vienna industrial holding Constantia Industries (~3,400 staff, ~EUR 758m sales), whose companies include Fundermax (wood panels) and Isovolta (electrical insulation). He moved from the management board to the supervisory board in 2017.
interesting_fact: Group company Isovolta makes electrical insulating materials, laminates and composites used by around 20 industries, including generator/machinery makers and aviation, from bases in Austria, the US, Mexico, China and India.

public_contacts.value: https://isovolta.com/ (Isovolta contact form, a Constantia Industries company)

notes: Described by trend. as a very discreet family (~EUR 1.25bn). No direct Constantia Industries contact found; CEO is Erlfried Taurer. Avoid political-donation (ILAG/Ibiza) topics. Insulation for generators/electrification is a possible energy hook.

name: Liu Guoben
current_role: Deceased (former founder and chairman, Camel Group, 601311.SH)
profile: Liu Guoben (刘国本), founder of Camel Group, the Hubei lead-acid battery maker, died of illness on 30 November 2022 at age 79. He had retired as chairman in 2019. In 2023 control of Camel passed to his widow, Sun Jie.
notes: Deceased. Source: STCN, 'former actual controller died a year ago, 60-year-old widow takes over Camel' (https://www.stcn.com/article/detail/1038209.html). Camel's current chairman is Liu Changlai.

name: Pedro Brescia Moreyra
current_role: Co-Chairman, Grupo Breca (Peru); Vice Chairman, Rímac Seguros
profile: Third-generation member (born 1971, son of Mario Brescia Cafferata) of the family behind Breca, Peru's largest conglomerate (Minsur tin/copper mining, TASA fishmeal, Rímac insurance, BBVA Perú stake, Melón cement, real estate). Formerly Breca's general manager, he now co-chairs the group with cousin Alex Fort Brescia and sits on many group boards.
interesting_fact: Breca's mining arm Minsur is one of the world's largest tin producers and, through Marcobre, runs the Mina Justa copper project; Pedro sits on both boards.
deep_cut_fact: A Universidad de Lima business graduate with a Kellogg MBA, he serves on the board of Aporta (Breca's social-impact platform) and is a director of the Instituto Peruano de Economía think tank.
notes: Do not confuse with his uncle Pedro Brescia Cafferata (1921-2014). Family is very private; route via Breca corporate communications. Energy/mining angle (Minsur, Marcobre) fits the podcast.

name: Huh Young-In
current_role: Chairman, SPC Group (Paris Baguette, Paris Croissant, BR Korea / Baskin-Robbins & Dunkin' Korea), Seoul
profile: Hur Young-in (b. 1949), second son of Samlip Food founder Hur Chang-sung, opened the Paris Croissant bakery in Seoul in 1986 and began franchising Paris Baguette in 1988, building SPC into Korea's largest bakery-food group with stores across Asia, the US and France. Sons Hur Jin-soo (vice chairman, Nov 2025) and Hur Hee-soo now run day-to-day; SPC is building a Texas bakery plant due 2027.
interesting_fact: France decorated him in 2010 and 2012 for helping make bread a staple of the South Korean diet; Paris Baguette now even operates bakeries in Paris.
deep_cut_fact: In 1981, already working in the family bakery business, he moved to the United States to formally study pastry and baking before launching Paris Croissant in 1986.
notes: Romanized variously as Hur/Huh/Heo Young-in. Has faced labour-related prosecution in 2024 (released on bail) and SPC had high-profile factory safety incidents - sensitive topics. No published press email found; route via SPC Group corporate communications.

name: Pan Xueping
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Jinsheng Industry (金昇实业) and Saurer Intelligent Technology (卓郎智能, SSE: 600545)
profile: Pan Xueping (潘雪平) founded Changzhou-based Jiangsu Jinsheng Industry in 2000. In 2013 Jinsheng bought Oerlikon's natural-fibre and textile-components businesses (deal value about CHF 650m) and revived the historic Swiss Saurer brand. Pan chairs Shanghai-listed Saurer Intelligent Technology and is vice-president of China's textile machinery and textile engineering associations.
interesting_fact: Jinsheng's 2013 purchase of Oerlikon's textile units brought back the 160-year-old Swiss Saurer name. Pan said the new Saurer would be run operationally from Wattwil, Switzerland and financially from Shanghai.
deep_cut_fact: A textile-machinery engineer by background, before founding Jinsheng he ran a spinning-ring (钢领) factory at Pacific Group's Shanghai textile-parts works, then led the Jintan Textile Machinery Plant and was CEO of a Swiss spinning group's front-end spinning division.
notes: Low public profile in English-language media. Name in Chinese: 潘雪平; Hurun's 'Jinsheng' is 金昇. Jinsheng also has large textile operations in Xinjiang (Litai Silk Road), a possibly sensitive topic. Best route is Saurer IR.

name: Sharad P Chauhan
current_role: Co-owner / member of the controlling Chauhan family, Parle Products (Mumbai)
profile: Member of the Chauhan family of Vile Parle, Mumbai, whose Parle Products (founded 1929 by Mohanlal Chauhan) makes Parle-G, Monaco, KrackJack, Melody and Kismi. After the family split, the biscuit and confectionery business passed to cousins including Vijay, Sharad and Raj Chauhan; the privately held company remains family-run, with the next generation (e.g. Arup Chauhan) on the board.
interesting_fact: Parle-G, the flagship of the family company, was named the world's best-selling biscuit brand in a 2011 Nielsen report.
notes: Very private family; almost no personal press coverage. Parle's contact page lists a general inbox (cs@parle.biz). Current health/role not verified (search budget exhausted); Arup Sharad Chauhan, a Parle director since 2002, appears to be from his branch of the family.

name: He Renbao
current_role: Co-founder, director and controlling shareholder (with wife Wang Yingmei), Zhejiang Yongtai Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002326)
profile: He Renbao co-founded Zhejiang Yongtai Technology in 1999 in Linhai, Taizhou, with his wife Wang Yingmei, who chairs it. MarketScreener lists him as founder and director and as CEO from 2007. Yongtai makes fluorinated intermediates for pharmaceuticals and crop protection, plus battery materials such as LiPF6 and LiFSI lithium salts, and has expanded into the EV supply chain.
interesting_fact: Yongtai was the first Shenzhen-listed company to issue GDRs on the London Stock Exchange.
notes: Fortune shared with his wife Wang Yingmei. MarketScreener lists a Kuang He as CEO since 2020, so his current executive title is unclear. He keeps a low profile, and I found no English interviews. zhengquan@ is the securities/investor-relations department inbox. The battery-materials angle (EV electrolyte salts) is relevant to energy.

name: Wang Yingmei
current_role: Chairwoman (since 2007) and General Manager (since Jul 2025), Zhejiang Yongtai Technology (SZ: 002326)
profile: Wang Yingmei is co-founder and, with He Renbao, joint actual controller of Zhejiang Yongtai Technology in Linhai/Taizhou, a fluorine-chemistry maker of pharmaceutical and crop-protection intermediates and new-energy materials such as lithium-battery electrolyte salts. She built the business from small local chemical plants in the 1990s and still runs it day to day.
interesting_fact: Yongtai describes itself as a fluorine-technology-centred maker of fluorinated pharma, crop-protection and new-energy (lithium battery) materials, with subsidiaries spanning electrolyte materials, fluorinated chips materials and lithium mining in Hainan.
deep_cut_fact: She started as a technician at Huangyan No.4 Chemical Plant (1987-92), then ran the Linhai Xingchen Chemical Plant (1992-97) and Linhai Yongli Fine Chemical Plant (1997-99) before founding Zhejiang Yongtai Chemical in 1999; she holds an EMBA and is a senior economist.
notes: Wealth shared with co-controller He Renbao. Very low media profile; board-secretary/securities office (zhengquan@) is the published route. Battery-materials angle is relevant to energy coverage.

name: Li Guiru
profile: Listed on Hurun China lists 2017-2023 (with Liu Aisen) with wealth attributed to 'Center International' (software & services). Could not identify the underlying company or confirm her role from public sources.
notes: Identity not confirmed: searches in English and Chinese (李桂茹, 刘爱森, 中心国际) found nothing. Lane's web-search budget ran out before further attempts; worth a re-check against the Hurun China list entry to find the company's Chinese name.

name: Ji Xuewen
current_role: Co-founder and major individual shareholder (7.53% as of Q1 2026) of Shenzhen Dynanonic (SZSE: 300769), a lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cathode material maker; no current executive role confirmed
profile: Ji Xuewen co-founded Dynanonic (德方纳米) in 2007 with a RMB500,000 capital contribution alongside two partners. The company became a major supplier of nano-scale LFP cathode material for EV and energy-storage batteries. He was its signing company head around 2020, holding about 20%; his stake has since fallen through transfers to 7.53% (Q1 2026), and Kong Lingyong now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: Dynanonic started in 2007 as a RMB500,000 limited company set up by Ji Xuewen, Yang Haiyan and Wang Yunshi, and grew into a leading supplier of LFP cathode material for China's EV and grid-storage boom.
notes: Very low public profile and no English-language bio found. His stake has fallen sharply (about 20% in 2020 to 7.53% in 2026), so he is likely no longer a billionaire; the Hurun listing was 2022-23 only. 'Alive' is marked unknown only because no personal coverage exists; he is still listed as a shareholder in 2026. Relevant to the energy-storage theme. The only route is company IR.

name: Jin Liguo
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Dongguan Yiheda Automation Co., Ltd. (怡合达, SZSE ChiNext: 301029)
profile: Jin Liguo (b. May 1973) founded Yiheda, a Dongguan-based one-stop supplier of standardized factory-automation components (a Chinese counterpart to Japan's Misumi) for non-standard automation equipment makers, including lithium-battery and electronics lines. He has run its predecessor since 1999 and has chaired the company since 2017; it listed on ChiNext in 2021.
interesting_fact: Yiheda's model is to standardize the thousands of small mechanical and electrical parts that custom automation-equipment builders need and sell them through a one-stop catalog, cutting design and procurement time for China's automation industry.
deep_cut_fact: With only a high-school education, he started as a technician at the Xingcheng Bearing Factory (1993-95), then worked as a salesman at a Shenyang aerospace special-equipment plant before taking over as general manager of Shenzhen Yiheda in 1999.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts. Board office (secretary Zhang Meiqi) is the published route. Customers include new-energy/battery equipment makers - relevant energy angle.

name: Ira Ehrenpreis
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, DBL Partners; independent director of Tesla and director of SpaceX (per Tesla IR and SEC insider filings)
profile: Ira Ehrenpreis is a Silicon Valley venture capitalist (since 1996) who led the energy-innovation practice at Technology Partners before co-founding impact-VC firm DBL Partners. An early Tesla and SpaceX backer and long-serving Tesla board member, his wealth derives largely from those stakes; he remains a prominent clean-energy investor and governance figure.
interesting_fact: He founded and chairs the World Energy Innovation Forum, which he staged inside Tesla's Fremont factory, with speakers such as Elon Musk, Lyndon Rive, Steven Chu and GE's Jeff Immelt.
deep_cut_fact: A UCLA Phi Beta Kappa/summa cum laude grad, he earned a joint JD/MBA at Stanford, where he was an associate editor of the Stanford Law Review; he was inducted into the International Green Industry Hall of Fame in 2014 and chaired the Silicon Valley Technology Innovation & Entrepreneurship Forum (2014-17).
notes: Strong fit for an energy/entrepreneurship podcast: clean-energy VC who runs the World Energy Innovation Forum. His DBL bio page publishes a direct work email. Tesla/SpaceX board seats make him media-cautious on those companies.

name: Rupen Ashwin Choksi
current_role: Managing Director, Resins and Plastics Ltd. (Choksi-family company, Mumbai); member of the Asian Paints promoter group
profile: Son of the late Ashwin Choksi, former non-executive chairman of Asian Paints, and grandson of co-founder Chimanlal Choksi. His wealth derives from the Choksi family's promoter stake in Asian Paints, India's largest paint maker; he is not on the Asian Paints board but runs family industrial businesses including Resins and Plastics Ltd. (director since 2007) and is a director of Pragati Chemicals.
interesting_fact: His grandfather Chimanlal Choksi was one of the four friends who co-founded Asian Paints in 1942; the Choksi, Dani and Vakil families still share promoter control.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews or social accounts found. Company-registry sites list him as MD of Resins and Plastics Ltd. Route via Asian Paints investor/secretarial office is indirect since he is not an Asian Paints director.

name: Kong Lingyong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Dynanonic Co. (SZSE: 300769), lithium-battery cathode materials
profile: Born 1978, a professor-level senior engineer and co-founder (2007) of Shenzhen Dynanonic, a leading maker of nano lithium iron phosphate (LFP), lithium manganese iron phosphate and lithium-supplement cathode materials for EV and energy-storage batteries. He is the company's core technology inventor and largest individual shareholder, and a deputy to the 14th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: He leads China's national nano energy-storage technology standards working group (SAC/TC279/WG7) and is an expert on ISO/IEC nanotechnology committees; Dynanonic now ships 4th-generation high-density LFP.
deep_cut_fact: Despite holding only a bachelor's degree, he is an external doctoral supervisor at Central South University and has won the China Patent Award and the title 'Guangdong Outstanding Inventor'.
notes: Strong fit for an energy-storage/battery-materials episode. Board secretary is He Yanyan (IR route). Likely needs Chinese-language outreach.

name: Hong Zhenhai
current_role: Founder and retired chairman of Eclat Textile (儒鴻, TWSE:1476), Taiwan; left the board June 2024
profile: Hung Chen-hai (洪鎮海) co-founded Eclat Textile in 1977 with NT$500,000 and built it into one of Asia's largest makers of stretch and functional fabrics and sportswear for brands like Nike. He retired in June 2024, handing the chair to Wang Shu-wen while his son became president.
interesting_fact: Known in Taiwan as the 'father of functional fabric'; Eclat reportedly never posted an annual loss in its 40+ years and became the textile sector's highest-priced stock.
deep_cut_fact: Born to a farming family in Miaoli, he started as an apprentice in a dyeing plant; after studying in Japan in the early 1980s he wove Taiwan's first roll of stretch knit fabric in 1983, and began co-developing fabrics with Nike two years later.
notes: Taiwanese (Hurun lists 'China'). Retired; publicly stated succession should be by merit not family ('傳賢不傳子'). Email is Eclat's company contact from exchange filings. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Bajrang Lal Kheruka

name: Barry Canton
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA), Boston

As CTO he leads Ginkgo's foundry technology strategy; the company went public via SPAC in 2021 and is now pushing autonomous labs and AI models trained on biological data.

name: Reshma Shetty
current_role: Co-founder, President and Board Director, Ginkgo Bioworks (NYSE: DNA); handed COO duties to others from 1 Jan 2026

name: Liu Jingyu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Fine Made Electronics Group (富满微, SZSE: 300671)
profile: Taiwan-born electronics engineer (b. 1964) who founded Shenzhen Fine Made Electronics in 2001 and has chaired it since 2014; it listed in Shenzhen in 2017. name: Mitchell Hashimoto
current_role: Cofounder, Superlogical (launched July 2026); creator of the Ghostty terminal; cofounder of HashiCorp
profile: LA-based developer who created Vagrant and cofounded HashiCorp (Terraform, Vault, Consul), serving ~4 years as CEO and ~5 as CTO before leaving in 2023; IBM later bought HashiCorp. His first successful side project became a passive-income business he sold to help self-fund HashiCorp, and he built IRCRelay with Jack Pearkes, who later cofounded Superlogical with him.
notes: Publishes his own email on his homepage and also lists Mastodon (hachyderm.io/@mitchellh) and GitHub. He blogs often about AI-assisted coding, Zig and open-source nonprofits, which are good conversation hooks.

Innoscience is the world's largest GaN-dedicated chipmaker (8-inch GaN-on-silicon; ~30% global GaN power-device share in 2024), listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024 and partnering with Nvidia on 800VDC power for AI data centers. notes: Very low public profile; the public face of Innoscience is chair Luo Weiwei (ex-NASA scientist). Role confirmed from Dec 2024 HKEX prospectus; current 2026 board status not re-verified (search budget exhausted). Strong AI data-center power (GaN/800VDC) angle.

name: Jin Xiaodong
current_role: Actual controller (controlling shareholder) of Anhui XDLK Microsystem (芯动联科, SSE STAR: 688582); not a current director or officer
profile: Jin Xiaodong (金晓冬) is the actual controller of XDLK, a Bengbu, Anhui maker of high-performance MEMS inertial sensors (gyroscopes, accelerometers) and pressure sensors. Founded in 2012, XDLK listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2023; he controls it via vehicles such as MEMSLink Corp. plus a ~1.3% direct stake.

name: Cao Ji
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Zhejiang Hangke Technology (688006.SS); also chairman of Hangke Instruments
profile: Hangzhou engineer who has spent 40+ years building reliability-testing equipment. Hangke began in 1984 testing electronic components, moved into lithium-battery back-end (formation/grading) equipment around 1998 and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019. In 2026 it took control of semiconductor-testing affiliate Hangke Instruments.

name: Jeanine Dick
current_role: Retired; former vice-chair of the supervisory board of Virbac (resigned Sept 2017); member of Virbac's controlling Dick family
profile: Widow of Pierre-Richard Dick, the veterinarian who founded Nice-based animal-health company Virbac in 1968. She was involved from the start, chaired Virbac's supervisory board after its 1992 restructuring, and stepped down as vice-chair in 2017 at 81. The family still controls Virbac; her daughter Marie-Helene Dick chairs the board.
interesting_fact: After Virbac adopted an executive/supervisory board structure in 1992, she became chairwoman of the supervisory board of the company her husband founded.
deep_cut_fact: When she retired from the board in 2017 she proposed her granddaughter Solene Madelpuech as her successor, passing the seat to the third generation.
notes: About 90 (81 in Sept 2017). No death report found, but status unconfirmed and she has been out of public life since 2017; dropped off Forbes lists after 2015 and 2020. Not a realistic podcast guest; the active family members are Marie-Helene Dick (chair) and Jean-Pierre Dick (sailor, former executive).

name: Peng Qian
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Wuhan Jingce Electronic Group (300567.SZ)
profile: Peng Qian, born 1974, founded Wuhan Jingce Electronic in 2006 at 32. It started in flat-panel display testing equipment and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2016. Jingce has since expanded into semiconductor metrology and new-energy (battery) testing equipment. Peng remains controlling shareholder, chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: Before founding Jingce he worked in market sales at Guangzhou ASPEC Environmental Instruments, an environmental testing equipment maker. He then built one of China's leading display-inspection equipment makers.

notes: Best route is via the company board secretary (董事会秘书 Liu Binghua, per 2026 IR activity records) or the Shenzhen exchange's 互动易 investor Q&A platform. The university/major detail was summarised by search from 36Kr and was not visible on the fetched page, so verify before use. Relevant to semiconductor/new-energy equipment themes.

name: Parakramsinh Jadeja
current_role: Chairman and Managing Director, Jyoti CNC Automation Ltd (Rajkot, Gujarat)
profile: First-generation engineer-entrepreneur (P.G. Jadeja) who entered the machine-tool business in 1989 with Jyoti Enterprises and built Jyoti CNC into one of India's largest CNC machine makers, with 140,000+ machines installed in 60+ countries for defence, aerospace and auto customers. He listed the company in January 2024, making him a billionaire, and owns French 5-axis specialist Huron Graffenstaden.

deep_cut_fact: Jadeja has described the company as 'A Temple of Technology', a vision written into the company history, and said it grew from a dream started in a small workshop. Jyoti says it made a 'tiny contribution' to the success of India's Mars Orbiter Mission.
notes: Also a director of the Indian Machine Tool Manufacturers' Association (IMTMA). Gives trade-press interviews (Machine Tools World, The Machinist), so manufacturing/industrial-automation angles are a natural fit. Spelled Prakramsinh/Parakram in some sources.

name: Cyrus Madon
current_role: Executive Vice Chair, Brookfield Asset Management; Executive Chair, Brookfield Private Equity
profile: Queen's University commerce grad and CPA who began in corporate finance and recovery at PwC, then joined Brookfield in 1998 as CFO of its real-estate brokerage. He built and ran Brookfield's private equity group (Brookfield Business Partners) for years and is now executive vice chair of the ~$1tn asset manager. He sits on the C.D. Howe Institute board.
interesting_fact: As head of Brookfield's private equity arm he led its first-ever nuclear investment: buying Westinghouse out of bankruptcy from Toshiba for $4.6bn in 2018, later sold to Brookfield Renewable and Cameco (2022-23).
deep_cut_fact: On selling Westinghouse to the Brookfield Renewable/Cameco consortium he said: "Westinghouse is an exceptionally well-run business today and has a great future." He first joined Brookfield in 1998 as CFO of its real-estate brokerage business, not an investing role.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast: Westinghouse nuclear deal, and Brookfield is a major renewables and AI-infrastructure investor. Low personal media profile; route via Brookfield North America press office.

name: Harry Klagsbrun
current_role: Long-time partner/senior executive at EQT (Stockholm); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Stockholm-based Swedish financier (~74) who joined private equity firm EQT in 2006. His fortune comes from his EQT AB shareholding, which soared after the firm's 2019 IPO. A Stockholm School of Economics graduate and Fulbright scholar at NYU, he began his career at Smith Barney. He joined the Securitas AB board in 2021 but no longer appears among its members.
interesting_fact: He became a billionaire through his stake in EQT, one of Europe's biggest private-equity firms, after its 2019 Stockholm listing. Forbes lists him as self-made.
deep_cut_fact: The son of a clothing designer, he studied economics at the Stockholm School of Economics. He then went to New York University as a Fulbright scholar for his MBA before starting at Smith Barney.
notes: Very private, with almost no media presence. His current EQT title (possibly a senior adviser or partner role) could not be verified because the web search budget ran out. No longer listed on the Securitas board (checked Nov 2026).

name: André Kasprzak
current_role: Co-owner and member of the Board of Directors, ECCO Sko A/S (Denmark)
profile: Third-generation co-owner of Danish shoemaker ECCO, founded in 1963 by his grandfather Karl Toosbuy; he owns the company with his mother Hanni and sister Anna. He joined ECCO's supervisory board in 2017 after his father Dieter stepped down as CEO, bringing e-commerce and digital experience.
interesting_fact: Before joining the board he served in the Danish military and played professional golf on the Nordic League (ECCO also makes a well-known golf shoe line).
deep_cut_fact: In early 2015 he worked at Scandinavian online fashion retailer Boozt, then helped build a new European e-commerce platform at KRM AG, ECCO's European retail arm; on joining the board he said 'ECCO has always been an essential part of my life.'
notes: Private family-owned company; route via ECCO group press office. Mother Hanni Toosbuy Kasprzak has been chair.

name: Anna Kasprzak
current_role: Co-owner of ECCO (Danish shoemaker) with mother Hanni and brother André; international dressage rider (recently competing as Anna Toosbuy Rasch)
profile: Granddaughter of ECCO founder Karl Toosbuy and daughter of owner Hanni Toosbuy Kasprzak and former CEO Dieter Kasprzak; she co-owns the family shoe company, which sells in ~90 countries through 2,200+ stores. She is best known as a Danish Olympic dressage rider and runs a private dressage barn in Haderslev.
interesting_fact: She rode for Denmark at the 2012 and 2016 Olympics, finishing 4th with the team in London 2012 and 14th individually in Rio 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before her senior career she won one silver and six bronze medals at European junior and young-rider championships, and finished 5th at the 2016 Dressage World Cup final.
notes: Recent equestrian coverage lists her as 'Anna Toosbuy Rasch' (per eurodressage, 2025) — use that name when searching results. Private on business matters; ECCO corporate communications is the likely route. No published personal contact found.

name: Caspar Callerström
current_role: Partner, EQT AB (Stockholm); Group deputy CEO & COO 2016-2022
profile: Stockholm School of Economics graduate who joined Swedish private-equity firm EQT in 1996 and became a partner in 2004. He headed EQT Equity in Stockholm (2007-13), sat on its Equity Partners Investment Committee, and was group deputy CEO and COO from 2016 to 2022, steering the firm through its 2019 IPO; his billionaire status comes from his EQT AB shareholding.
interesting_fact: He is one of the founding members of a group of financial elites backing Stockholm football club Djurgårdens IF; EQT's listing has minted about seven billionaires.
deep_cut_fact: Before group management he worked hands-on in portfolio companies, holding directorships at Thule (the roof-box/bike-rack maker), Scandic Hotels, Munksjö, Nederman, Sanitec and Dahl International.
notes: Low media profile. EQT is a large infrastructure/data-center investor (e.g., EdgeConneX), relevant to podcast. Route via EQT press office.

name: Xi Chao
current_role: Director and co-founder, Neway Valve (Suzhou) Co., Ltd. (纽威股份, SSE: 603699)
profile: Xi Chao (席超) co-founded Suzhou-based Neway Valve in 1997 with Wang Baoqing, Lu Bin and Cheng Zhangwen, and serves as a director. Neway grew into one of China's largest industrial valve makers, supplying upstream, midstream and downstream oil & gas, power, nuclear and new-energy projects, with sales hubs in the Netherlands, Italy, Singapore, the UAE and Nigeria. It listed in Shanghai in 2014.
interesting_fact: Neway has expanded abroad with a valve factory in Vietnam and regional subsidiaries in Europe (2011, Netherlands), Italy (2012, Milan valve cluster), Singapore (2013) and Lagos, Nigeria.
notes: Very low personal profile; little biographical information found. Web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so research here relied on the company site only. Strong energy-industry hook (oil & gas, nuclear, LNG/new-energy valves). Route via company board secretary.

name: George Feldstein
profile: Founder and chairman of Crestron Electronics, the AV and building-automation control company he started in 1969 in a room above a deli in New Jersey. Died 4 November 2014 (some sources say 5 Nov), aged 73; Crestron remains family-owned.
interesting_fact: He received both InfoComm's Adele de Berri Lifetime Achievement Award and CEDIA's Lifetime Achievement Award.
notes: Deceased (Nov 2014). Crestron is now run by his family; contact Crestron corporate communications if relevant.

He holds an EMBA and has worked in stationery manufacturing since 1997.

IR contact (board secretary email/phone) is published in M&G's SSE annual reports on sse.com.cn/cninfo - not extracted here. Web search budget ran out during this person, so research is thinner.

name: Kostyantin Zhevago
current_role: Major shareholder of Ferrexpo plc (former executive director, 2008-2019); owner of FC Vorskla Poltava
profile: Ukrainian businessman and former MP (1998-2019) whose fortune comes mainly from his stake in London-listed iron-ore pellet producer Ferrexpo, which runs mines in Poltava region. He stepped down as executive director in 2019. He faces several Ukrainian criminal cases and 2025 sanctions, all of which he denies, and lives outside Ukraine; France refused extradition in 2023.

deep_cut_fact: He was born in 1974 in Iultin, a remote Arctic mining settlement in Chukotka, and grew up in Dniprorudne in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region. He later earned a PhD in economics (2003) from Kyiv National Economic University.

He holds no executive role, and I found no published personal or office contact. Ferrexpo's IR represents the company, not him. Recommend skipping or handling with legal caution.

He stepped down as chairman in 2022 and remains a director and major shareholder. Sinnet is now building AI computing centers in Hainan and Inner Mongolia.

Horizon makes driving-assistance chips and software (Journey processors) used by VW, BYD, Hyundai and others, and listed in Hong Kong in Oct 2024 in that year's largest HK IPO.
interesting_fact: At Baidu (2012-15) he founded and led the Institute of Deep Learning, Baidu's autonomous-driving team and the PaddlePaddle deep-learning platform; earlier he directed NEC Labs America's media lab, a pioneer of convolutional neural networks.

notes: Strong fit for a tech/data-center podcast (AI chips, energy-efficient computing). Frequent conference speaker (WEF profile: https://weforum.org/people/yu-kai). IR email surfaced via search of the IR page (page is JS-rendered; not re-verified by direct fetch).

name: Jeffrey S. Raikes
current_role: Co-founder, Raikes Foundation; board member (Costco, Hudl); former CEO, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation
profile: Nebraska farm-raised Stanford engineer who joined Microsoft in 1981, drove Office's product strategy and rose to president of the Microsoft Business Division before retiring in 2008. He then ran the Gates Foundation as CEO (2008-2014) and now co-leads the Seattle-based Raikes Foundation with his wife, focused on youth, education and impact-driven philanthropy.

deep_cut_fact: Before Microsoft he was Apple's VisiCalc engineering manager in 1980; after 15 months Steve Ballmer recruited him to Microsoft as a product manager. He first learned to program in Pascal on a DEC System 20 at Stanford, where he had prepared for a career in USDA agricultural policy.
notes: Name in input is 'S. Raikes Jeffrey' = Jeffrey S. Raikes. Also namesake of the Jeffrey S. Raikes School of Computer Science and Management at University of Nebraska-Lincoln. Best route: Raikes Foundation press inbox.

It grew from phone battery packs into one of China's major lithium-ion battery makers, supplying consumer-electronics battery modules to Apple and Huawei and expanding into EV and energy-storage cells. He is still the controlling shareholder, and the company has filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing (filed July 2025, refiled Jan 2026).

current_role: Chairman and President, Weixing Group (伟星集团), Linhai, Zhejiang; director of Zhejiang Weixing New Building Materials (002372) and Weixing Co. (002003)
profile: Zhang Kapeng (b. January 1965, Linhai, Taizhou) leads Weixing Group, the controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Weixing New Building Materials (PPR/PE plastic piping) and Weixing Co., a leading Chinese maker of buttons and zippers. He became a billionaire when Gambol listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in August 2023; KKR is among its investors.
