The gambolpet.com site is the OEM/export arm (published email brand@gambolpet.com is a sales inbox). Web-search budget exhausted before a deep-cut fact could be sourced.

name: Arno Schodl
current_role: Co-founder and CTO/Technical Director, think-cell Software GmbH (Berlin)
profile: German computer scientist (PhD in computer graphics, Georgia Tech) who worked at Microsoft Research and McKinsey before co-founding think-cell with Markus Hannebauer in 2002. think-cell's PowerPoint charting add-in became the de facto standard for consultants and bankers; PE firm Cinven bought a majority stake in 2021, and the founders retain a ~30% stake. He oversees R&D, QA and customer care.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding think-cell he worked at both Microsoft Research and McKinsey & Company; the company describes think-cell as 'the de facto standard' for professional PowerPoint presentations.
deep_cut_fact: As a Georgia Tech PhD student he was lead author of 'Video Textures' (SIGGRAPH 2000, with Richard Szeliski, David Salesin and Irfan Essa), a widely cited paper on synthesising endless, non-repeating video from a short clip. He is also a regular C++ conference speaker on think-cell's open-source ranges library.
notes: Engineer-founder, more visible in the C++ developer community (CppCast, NDC TechTown, Meeting C++) than in business press. A technical/C++ angle is likely to land well. Name also spelled Schoedl.

name: Markus Hannebauer
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, think-cell Software GmbH (Berlin)
profile: Computer scientist with a TU Berlin PhD in artificial intelligence who, after working at Fraunhofer, co-founded think-cell with Arno Schödl in Berlin in 2002. Its PowerPoint charting add-on became a standard tool in consulting and finance with over one million users; PE firm Cinven bought a majority stake in 2021. He ran the company as CEO until March 2024 and now chairs the board.
interesting_fact: think-cell won the Berlin StartUp award in its very first year (2002) and two decades later passed one million users worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he published a Springer book (Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 2427), 'Autonomous Dynamic Reconfiguration in Multi-Agent Systems', introducing 'agent melting and splitting', with a case study on medical appointment scheduling.
notes: info@think-cell.com is the company's general contact, not personal. LinkedIn link taken from Indezine profile page (not independently verified as his). AI/software founder angle; relatively accessible to tech press historically.

name: Andrii Verevskyi
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and controlling shareholder (>95%), Kernel Holding S.A., Kyiv
profile: Born 1974 in Poltava, agronomist by training; founded a small grain-export trader in 1995 that became Kernel, Ukraine's largest sunflower-oil producer/exporter and a major grain and farming group. Took Kernel public in Warsaw in 2007, served in parliament 2002–2013, and has since bought out minorities to >95% and moved to delist.
interesting_fact: In 2012 Kernel alone accounted for about 12% of the world's sunflower-oil exports.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Kernel, he worked from 1993 to 1998 as deputy director of a regional state bread-products (khliboprodukty) enterprise; he later took a modern-economics course at Oxford (2000).
notes: Spelling varies (Verevskyi/Verevskyy/Verevskiy). Avoid the minority-shareholder delisting dispute as a topic. Gave an FT interview in 2024 on Ukraine reforms/EU, so occasionally speaks to international press.

name: Craig Newmark
current_role: Founder, Craigslist; founder of Craig Newmark Philanthropies
profile: Craig Newmark spent ~17 years at IBM and then worked at Charles Schwab in San Francisco, where in 1995 he started an email list of local events that became Craigslist. Now largely focused on philanthropy through Craig Newmark Philanthropies (founded 2015), funding trustworthy journalism, cybersecurity ('cyber civil defense'), veterans and military families, and women in tech; he joined the Giving Pledge in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Craigslist started out as an email newsletter about events in San Francisco; Newmark launched it from his flat while working as a Schwab systems/security consultant.
deep_cut_fact: He is a devoted bird lover (since the mid-80s in Detroit) and a champion of pigeons, which he calls 'the underdog... possibly our successor species'; he has been a top funder of SF pigeon rescue Palomacy since 2013.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly, active on social media (also craignewmark@mastodon.social). Journalism-funding focus makes him a natural podcast guest; cybersecurity/infrastructure angle is a hook.

name: Subba Rao Jasti
current_role: Family patriarch and shareholder, Suven Life Sciences (Hyderabad); no executive role
profile: Subba Rao Jasti (born c. 1926-27) is the patriarch of the Jasti family of Hyderabad and an early investor in Suven, founded by his son Venkateswarlu Jasti in 1989 and listed in 1995. Suven was demerged in 2020; in 2021 the family sold most of its Suven Pharmaceuticals stake to Advent International, and it retains Suven Life Sciences, a neuroscience drug developer.
interesting_fact: Suven Life Sciences, the family's remaining listed company, runs a CNS drug pipeline including masupirdine (SUVN-502) for neuropsychiatric symptoms in Alzheimer's disease.
notes: Nearly 100 years old; no death report found but alive status not confirmed. Not a practical podcast guest; family business is run by son Venkateswarlu Jasti (Suven Life Sciences).

name: Rodney Lewis
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Lewis Energy Group (San Antonio, Texas)
profile: Laredo-raised wildcatter (born 1954) who bought his first gas well in 1982 and launched Lewis Energy in 1983, building a large Eagle Ford shale position and becoming one of Texas' biggest private gas producers. In 2004 he became the first U.S. oilman contracted to drill for Pemex in Mexico. Still runs the privately held company; inducted into Hart Energy's Hall of Fame in 2023.
interesting_fact: He owns one of America's largest fleets of airworthy WWII fighters, including the P-38 'Glacier Girl' recovered from under a Greenland glacier, and founded the Lewis Air Legends collection in 2009; he has served on the National Air and Space Museum board.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BA in criminal justice from what is now Texas A&M International University in Laredo, paid $13,000 for his first well, and in 2014 received Webb County's 'Angel of Hope' award for providing Christmas gifts to needy children.
notes: Goes by Rod Lewis. Private company; general info@ inbox is the only published email. Warbird aviation (Lewis Air Legends) is a strong rapport topic. No 2026 personal news found; alive status based on current company leadership listings.

name: Jeffrey Soffer
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Fontainebleau Development (Miami)
profile: Son of Aventura, Florida developer Donald Soffer; ran family firm Turnberry Associates with sister Jackie for two decades before forming Fontainebleau Development in 2019. Owns the historic Fontainebleau Miami Beach (about $800m reinvested) and completed Fontainebleau Las Vegas, which opened in Dec 2023; also owns JW Marriott Turnberry and Big Easy Casino.
interesting_fact: Fontainebleau Las Vegas took nearly 20 years from land purchase to opening: Soffer halted it about three-quarters built after the 2008-09 crisis, then reacquired it in 2021 with Koch Real Estate Investments and finished it in late 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He calls philanthropy 'really personal' and focuses on cancer causes via the Bleau Cares platform (Susan G. Komen Miami, Sylvester Comprehensive Cancer Center, Miami Dolphins Cancer Challenge); his career advice: 'Stay curious.'
notes: Does occasional interviews (Leaders magazine, Walker & Dunlop webcast). Avoid family/personal-life topics. Data-center/energy angle is weak; hospitality and mega-project development is the hook.

name: Li Jun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Leyard Optoelectronic Co. (SZSE: 300296), Beijing
profile: Economist-turned-entrepreneur who founded Leyard in Beijing in 1995 and built it into a leading LED/large-format display group (ChiNext IPO 2012), expanding via the 2015 acquisition of Oregon's Planar Systems and Germany's eyevis (2018), and into VR/AI-driven display and 'metaverse' tech. He was re-elected chairman and named general manager in February 2026.
interesting_fact: Before business, Li earned an economics doctorate at Renmin University and taught at the Central University of Finance & Economics (1987-1991). Leyard screens lit the 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony and it supplied most of the giant LED floor for the 2022 Winter Olympics opening.
deep_cut_fact: For the 2008 Beijing Olympics opening ceremony Leyard made the displays that illuminated the Olympic Rings and a 1,300 m² 'Ground Bar' LED scroll tough enough to have cars driven across it.
notes: Profile assumes the Forbes 'Li Jun' (Leyard). The listed source of wealth 'Botheart' (Hurun unicorn record) could not be matched to Leyard and may belong to a different Li Jun (very common name) - identity marked uncertain for that reason. leyard2010@leyard.com is the board-secretary/IR mailbox (2026 filing).

name: Chen Gang
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy Co. (AIKO, SSE: 600732)
profile: Chen Gang founded Aiko Solar in 2009 (Guangdong Aiko Technology), a solar cell maker with plants in Foshan, Yiwu and Tianjin that sells globally. Aiko rose from a mid-sized player to the world's No.1 PERC cell shipper in 2018, listed via a backdoor deal with ST Xinmei in 2019, and now champions n-type back-contact (ABC) cells and modules. He continues to lead it through the industry's consolidation.
interesting_fact: Aiko went from outside China's top 10 cell makers to No.1 globally in PERC cell shipments in 2018; Chen chose a backdoor listing because 'in an industry reshuffle, time matters more than money.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2017, while ordinary mono cells were very profitable, he halted his own mono lines to bet on unproven tubular PERC tech, pre-agreeing with suppliers to convert the equipment back if it failed. His rule: 'If even the worst outcome isn't bad, you dare to do it' (最坏的结果都不坏，你就敢做了).
notes: Common name - matched via Aiko Solar. Gives interviews to Chinese press (People's Daily Energy, The Paper at SNEC 2025); likely needs Mandarin outreach. Co-owner listed: Ou Chunlian. No dedicated English IR email found; Chinese annual report may list a securities-affairs email.

name: Ou Chunlian
current_role: Co-holder (with Chen Gang) of the controlling family stake in Aiko Solar / Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy (爱旭股份, 600732.SH); no executive title found
profile: Hurun lists Ou Chunlian (欧春连) jointly with Chen Gang, founder, chairman and controller of Aiko Solar (爱旭股份), a leading Chinese maker of high-efficiency PV cells and modules. Chinese media say Chen Gang made the 2023 Hurun Global list 'with his wife', so she is probably his wife, but no public profile of her exists.
interesting_fact: Aiko was the first company to develop and mass-produce n-type ABC (all-back-contact) solar cells, which have no front-side electrodes. Chen Gang argues that the technology closest to the efficiency limit wins.
notes: No public information on Ou Chunlian herself. The realistic interviewee is Chen Gang (chairman, Aiko Solar), via company marketing/IR. A 2025 article says the SSE sent Aiko an inquiry letter about related-party transactions, so outreach may be sensitive.

name: Yao Junliang
current_role: Chairman of the board, Meijin Energy Group (controlling shareholder of Shanxi Meijin Energy, SZSE: 000723)
profile: Second-generation head of the Yao family's Shanxi coal-and-coke business, which began in 1981 under his father Yao Juhuo and grew into one of China's largest independent merchant coke and coal producers. Since 2017 he has pushed Meijin into hydrogen (production, storage, refuelling, fuel-cell vehicles), though coking still dominates revenue.
interesting_fact: Meijin's hydrogen push started in Guangdong: it helped create membrane-electrode maker Guangzhou Hongji Chuangneng, invested in fuel-cell firm Guohong Hydrogen, and in 2017 took control of Foshan Feichi (now Feichi Technology), a hydrogen fuel-cell bus and truck maker.
deep_cut_fact: The Yao family firm has its roots in 1981 Shanxi; in 1996 his father, then 65, gathered the family and said he was only a 'passing god of wealth' (guolu caishen) holding money that belonged to society before entrusting the business to the next generation.
notes: Listed arm Shanxi Meijin Energy (000723) is chaired by Yao Jinlong (CPPCC member); Chinese press calls Yao Junliang chairman of the Meijin group board. Company under financial strain in 2025-26 (rating cut, losses, pledged shares) - avoid wealth/debt topics. Hydrogen is the best hook; Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Xia Feng
current_role: Co-founder and non-executive Director (since Oct 2008), Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (SSE STAR: 688368); director, Changsha Zuxing New Materials
profile: Xia Feng (夏风, b. ~1968) co-founded Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (晶丰明源) in 2008 with chairman Hu Liqiang; the fabless analog/mixed-signal chip designer makes LED-lighting driver, power-management and motor-control ICs. He holds ~19.6M shares directly and more via a partnership. Hurun also links his wealth to image-sensor maker GalaxyCore (格科微).
interesting_fact: When Bright Power was set up in Oct 2008 with just RMB 2 million of registered capital, Xia Feng put up 47% of it (RMB 940,000), almost as much as founder-CEO Hu Liqiang's 48.2%.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips, he started as a technician and assistant engineer at the Zhuzhou Zhongnan Radio Factory in Hunan, then became deputy head of the Zhuzhou zinc-oxide surge-arrester factory and later a VP at Shenzhen Zuxing Industrial (2025 annual report bio).

public_contacts.value: IR@bpsemi.com (Bright Power Semiconductor investor relations / board office)

notes: Non-executive, low-profile investor-director; no interviews found. GalaxyCore link is from Hurun and was not confirmed in filings checked. Route via Bright Power IR; chairman Hu Liqiang is the company's public face.

name: Zhang Xiaohui
current_role: Probable match: non-independent director (since Jan 2024) of Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources Co. (SSE: 600295), the listed arm of Erdos Group
profile: Hurun China (2025-26) lists a Zhang Xiaohui with wealth from Erdos (cashmere, coal, real estate). The best-matching public figure is a 61-year-old Erdos Resources director who joined the company in 1987 and previously ran Erdos hotels in Ordos and Beijing and was president of Qipanjing Real Estate (Zhiye) Group. His ownership link to Hurun's figure is not confirmed.
interesting_fact: Erdos Group grew from a 1979 Inner Mongolia cashmere mill into China's 'cashmere king' and later diversified into coal, power, ferroalloys and chemicals; its listed arm Erdos Resources now spans cashmere apparel, energy, chemicals and metallurgy.
notes: Identity uncertain: could not find a source tying a Zhang Xiaohui to Hurun-scale Erdos ownership (founder Wang Linxiang is Erdos's long-time Hurun entry). Candidate bio from Eastmoney F10 data on 600295 (male, 61, director since 2024-01-02). Exchange disclosures list a company contact email, but it is a named staff mailbox, so it is omitted. Verify before outreach.

name: Ajay Puri
current_role: Executive Vice President, Worldwide Field Operations, NVIDIA (still listed with this title on an Aug 2026 SEC Form 4)
profile: Ajay 'Jay' Puri runs NVIDIA's global sales and field organisation, which sells the GPUs and systems behind the AI data-center boom. He joined NVIDIA in 2005 after 22 years at Sun Microsystems in sales, marketing and general management. His wealth comes from NVIDIA stock (about 0.02% stake), and he remains in the role as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Puri holds about 0.02% of NVIDIA, which in October 2025 became the first company ever worth $5 trillion. That was enough to make a sales executive a billionaire on Forbes' real-time list.
deep_cut_fact: Before his 22 years at Sun, Puri worked in product development at Texas Instruments and in consulting at Booz Allen. He holds electrical engineering degrees from the University of Minnesota (BS) and Caltech (MS) as well as a Harvard MBA, so he is an engineer by training, not a career salesman.
notes: Low public profile with no NVIDIA newsroom bio page, so requests are best routed through NVIDIA corporate communications. SEC filer CIK 0001347842 ('Puri Ajay K'). Forbes now marks him as 'former' on its real-time list.

name: Eddy Sugianto
current_role: President Commissioner, PT Prima Andalan Mandiri Tbk (IDX: MCOL, 'Mandiri Coal'); controlling shareholder of Mandiri Herindo Adiperkasa (Mandiri Services)
profile: Indonesian coal magnate behind the Mandiri group, whose PT Mandiri Intiperkasa mine in North Kalimantan sells coal under the 'Mandiri Coal' brand, with in-house mining contracting and barging units. He took Prima Andalan Mandiri public in 2021 and the coal-services arm in 2023; his family controls ~70% of MCOL. Brother Handy Glivirgo is president director.
interesting_fact: Detik dubbed him one of Indonesia's 'OKB' (new rich) when he debuted on Forbes' billionaire list with US$1.2B; Mandiri Coal hit record output of 9.02 million tonnes in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: The group's mine traces back to a 1994 Coal Contract of Work (No. 08/PK/PTBA-MI/1994) for a 50,000-ha area in North Kalimantan; after revisions cut it to 9,240 ha, production only began in 2004, a decade later. He has been president commissioner of PAM since 2005.
notes: Very low media profile; no personal accounts found. Best route is MCOL's corporate secretary. Commissioner-since-2005 detail from Detik.

name: Pedro Grendene Bartelle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Grendene S.A.; Chairman, Vulcabras
profile: Born 1950 in Farroupilha, Rio Grande do Sul, he and twin Alexandre founded Plástico Grendene in 1971 with a loan from their grandfather, making plastic covers for wine demijohns before moving into footwear in 1978. Grendene (Melissa, Ipanema, Rider) became the world's largest sandal maker; he holds ~14% and chairs Vulcabras, where he owns ~50%.
interesting_fact: He also built Nelore Grendene, started in the 1980s, one of Brazil's largest breeders of Nelore beef-cattle bulls.
deep_cut_fact: Grendene's first sandal, the 1979 Melissa Aranha, came about after Pedro noticed the strap sandals worn by fishermen on the French Riviera; Melissa later collaborated with Jean-Paul Gaultier and Thierry Mugler.
notes: Low public profile. Grendene's press is handled by CDN Comunicação (agency). Vulcabras (run by his son) is a separate listed company with its own IR.

name: Cao Yuhua
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, Wuxi Best Precision Machinery (贝斯特, SZSE ChiNext 300580)
profile: A Wuxi native born in 1954, Cao spent nearly 30 years at a Wuxi machine-tool factory before co-founding Wuxi Best in 1997. It makes precision auto-parts components (turbocharger parts), tooling, fixtures and intelligent equipment used in new-energy vehicles, industrial machinery and robots, and went public in Shenzhen in 2017. More than a third of revenue comes from overseas; his daughter Cao Yi is vice chairman.
interesting_fact: Wuxi Best started in 1997 with registered capital of just RMB500,000, split 50/50 between Cao and co-founder Pan Zhiyu. It is now a ChiNext-listed precision manufacturer worth about RMB8bn.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the Wuxi Machine Tool Factory as a 16-year-old shop-floor worker in 1970 and rose to head its non-standard design office. While there he spotted the chance to localise motorcycle-engine tooling fixtures, which became Best's first business.
notes: Also a Jiangsu Provincial Model Worker and Wuxi People's Congress deputy (per Sina). Chinese-language only; route via the company securities-affairs (IR) office. Angle: NEV and robotics component supply chain.

name: Yang Xuegang
current_role: Chairman, Executive Director & CEO, China Risun Group (1907.HK)
profile: Founded Xingtai Risun Coking in Hebei in 1995 and built it into China Risun Group (1907.HK), China's largest independent coke producer and a major coke-based chemicals maker. Risun is expanding into hydrogen, new energy and new materials. He has been chairman since 1996 and leads Hebei's coking industry association.
interesting_fact: Frost & Sullivan ranked Risun the world's largest independent coke producer and supplier by volume in 2020. Its production bases include Xingtai, Dingzhou, Laoting and Cangzhou.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a hydraulic engineer (Hebei Hydraulic College, 1985) and spent about 10 years at Handan's Dongwushi Reservoir Management Center, becoming deputy director in 1988. He still keeps a water link as a director of Beijing Automic, a water-conservancy IT firm.
notes: Relevant to the energy theme: Risun produces hydrogen from coke-oven gas and is pursuing new-energy materials. The best route is Risun IR. Bio details come from the 2025 annual report (published April 2026).

name: Sheela Gautam
profile: Founder of Sheela Foam (Sleepwell mattresses, founded 1971) and four-term BJP Lok Sabha MP for Aligarh (1991-2004). She died in New Delhi on 8 June 2019, aged 87. Her son Rahul Gautam runs Sheela Foam.
interesting_fact: She founded Sheela Foam in 1971 and also served four consecutive terms in parliament, from 1991 to 2004.
notes: Deceased (8 June 2019, per Wikipedia). For the company, contact Sheela Foam (sheelafoam.com), now run by son Rahul Gautam.

name: Patokh Chodiev
current_role: Co-founder and co-owner, Eurasian Resources Group (ERG); founder, International Chodiev Foundation
profile: Uzbek-born, Belgian-naturalised businessman who studied international law and Japanese at MGIMO and worked on Soviet-Japanese commercial relations in Tokyo. With Alexander Machkevich and Alijan Ibragimov ('The Trio') he built ENRC in Kazakhstan, floated it in London in 2007 and took it private in 2013; it is now ERG, a mining, smelting and energy group active in 14 countries.
interesting_fact: He speaks fluent Japanese and received Japan's Order of the Rising Sun in 2020 for developing Japan-Russia economic and cultural ties.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he acquired the Kubota Collection, 104 kimono by textile artist Itchiku Kubota made with the revived 'tsujigahana' dyeing technique, and his foundation has since toured it to Kazakhstan, Russia, Europe and North America, with key pieces shown at the Tokyo National Museum in 2020.
notes: Significant reputational and due-diligence considerations: ENRC/ERG has been the subject of long-running investigations, he appears in the Pandora/Panama Papers reporting, and he was involved in the Belgian 'Kazakhgate' affair. Review before featuring. Best route is the foundation (ICF), which is PR-active; ERG (erg.kz) has its own press office.

name: Roy Vagelos
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Merck (1985–1994) and longtime Chairman of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (1995–c.2024); philanthropist
profile: Physician-scientist (b. 1929) who moved from NIH and Washington University to Merck's research labs, then ran Merck as CEO and chairman until 1994. He chaired Regeneron for nearly 29 years from 1995 and co-founded Theravance. His fortune comes largely from Regeneron stock, and he and his wife Diana are major donors to Columbia, Penn and Barnard.
interesting_fact: As Merck's CEO he had the company give its river-blindness drug ivermectin (Mectizan) free to governments and patients. Over two decades the programme reached more than 55 million people.
deep_cut_fact: The son of Greek immigrants, he grew up during the Depression working in his family's small restaurant in Rahway, New Jersey, the town where Merck's labs were based. He left on a partial scholarship to Penn, where he earned a chemistry BA (Phi Beta Kappa, 1950).
notes: Aged 97 and living in New Jersey. Columbia's medical school is named the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, and the couple gave $400m to Columbia in 2024. No personal contact published; Regeneron or Columbia communications offices are the likely routes (pages blocked automated fetches).

name: Jean Madar
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Inter Parfums, Inc. (Nasdaq: IPAR), New York
profile: Jean Madar co-founded fragrance licensor Interparfums with ESSEC classmate Philippe Benacin after learning about the industry's high margins in business school; it listed on Nasdaq in 1988 at a ~$4M valuation and is now worth billions. As CEO since 1997 he runs the U.S. operations (brands such as Montblanc, Coach, Jimmy Choo licences sit across the group).
interesting_fact: Madar never wears fragrance himself, to keep his sense of smell clear.
deep_cut_fact: The company's original name, Jean Philippe Fragrances, was a contraction of the founders' first names, Jean and Philippe, and it started out selling inexpensive alternatives to pricier designer scents before moving upmarket.

public_contacts.value: dsullivan@theequitygroup.com (Devin Sullivan, The Equity Group - IR agency)

notes: Accessible public-company CEO who does investor calls; IR agency The Equity Group is the published route.

name: Zelimkhan Mutsoev
current_role: Deputy of the Russian State Duma (United Russia), serving his 6th convocation (8th Duma, elected 2021)
profile: Tbilisi-born (1959) Russian businessman-politician of Yazidi heritage. He moved to Moscow in the early 1990s, ran a foreign-trade association, became a co-owner of Pervouralsk New Pipe Plant in 1998 and later built holdings in fertilizers (Uralkali stake) and real estate, while serving in the Duma almost continuously since 1999.
interesting_fact: He was dropped from the Duma after the 2011 election but returned in 2012 when another United Russia deputy resigned and her mandate was transferred to him.
notes: CAUTION: sitting Russian Duma deputy — likely subject to Western sanctions applied to Duma members since 2022 (not verified in this pass; check OFAC/EU/UK lists before any contact). Wikipedia also records a 2008 dispute over a Kyiv hotel. Probably not a suitable podcast guest.

name: Chang Chung-Hsing
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Apex Dynamics (Taichung, Taiwan)
profile: Chang Chung-Hsing (張重興) founded Taichung-based Apex Dynamics in 1987 as a maker of robotic arms and built it into one of the world's largest suppliers of high-precision planetary gearboxes used in automation and machine tools. Apex listed on the Taiwan Stock Exchange in 2022, making him a billionaire on Forbes' 2025 list.
interesting_fact: Apex also owns the Millennium Vee Hotel Taichung, run with Singapore's Millennium Hotels & Resorts, one of the oldest international-brand hotels in central Taiwan.
notes: Low English-language profile. Company site was unreachable during research (503), and the web-search budget ran out, so no deep-cut fact or press contact was verified. Robotics/automation angle. Reach via Apex Dynamics IR (TWSE filings) once site is reachable.

name: Larry Silverstein
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Silverstein Properties (New York)
profile: Brooklyn-born developer (b. 1931) who co-founded Silverstein Properties with his father in 1957. He leased the World Trade Center in July 2001, seven weeks before 9/11, and spent two decades rebuilding 7, 4 and 3 WTC. The firm also owns LA's U.S. Bank Tower and downtown Manhattan's tallest residential tower, 30 Park Place.
interesting_fact: He usually held breakfast meetings at Windows on the World atop the North Tower, but on the morning of 9/11 his wife insisted he keep a medical appointment, which likely saved his life.
deep_cut_fact: Before real estate he was a music kid: he played piano, loved classical music and attended New York's High School of Music and Art; he met his wife Klara while working at a summer camp in college. Brooklyn Law School named him its 2026 Alumnus of the Year.

public_contacts.value: mgrace@Rubenstein.com (Rubenstein, listed as media contact on Silverstein news releases)

notes: Age 95; accessible to press historically (many interviews). Avoid dwelling on 9/11 insurance litigation. Company now run day-to-day by his son and CEO team; press office is responsive route.

name: Harshil Mathur
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Razorpay
profile: IIT Roorkee graduate who co-founded Razorpay with batchmate Shashank Kumar in 2014 (Y Combinator-backed), building India's largest payment gateway by volume. Razorpay, valued at $7.5bn, now spans payments, banking, payroll and POS and is preparing for an Indian IPO.
interesting_fact: He has said nearly 100 banks rejected Razorpay before one agreed to partner, an early hurdle he credits with shaping the company.
deep_cut_fact: Razorpay began in 2014 as a social crowdfunding project 'to enable people to fund and help others in distress'; struggling to integrate payments, he and Kumar pivoted to payments. Before that he was a wireline field engineer at Schlumberger.
notes: Media-friendly and active on X/podcasts. Razorpay newsroom contact page (dated ~2021) also names individual comms staff.

name: Shashank Kumar
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director, Razorpay (Bengaluru)
profile: IIT Roorkee B.Tech graduate who co-founded Razorpay with Harshil Mathur in 2014; it now runs India's largest payment gateway by transactions, serving 113 of India's top 125 unicorns, plus banking (RazorpayX), payroll and POS products. Privately held, it was last valued at about $7.5bn after raising $700m+ from investors including GIC and Mastercard.
interesting_fact: Razorpay has grown partly through acquisitions - eight to date, including a payroll-management business and a point-of-sale platform.
notes: Razorpay newsroom contact page also lists named corporate-communications staff. Fintech/infra founder - plausible podcast fit on payments/data infrastructure. Web search budget was exhausted before a sourced deep-cut fact could be found.

name: Stanley Tang
current_role: Co-founder and Head of DoorDash Labs, DoorDash (also a director)
profile: Hong Kong-raised (born 1992 in Sendai, Japan), Stanford computer-science graduate who co-founded DoorDash in 2013 with Tony Xu, Andy Fang and Evan Moore. He owns about 4% of the company, which listed on the NYSE in December 2020. He now runs DoorDash Labs, the company's autonomy and robotics unit, which launched the 'Dot' delivery robot in 2025.
interesting_fact: He led the 2025 unveiling of Dot, DoorDash's in-house autonomous delivery robot, which can travel on roads, bike lanes and sidewalks at up to 20 mph. DoorDash says it was tested over millions of simulated and real-world miles.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager in Hong Kong he wrote 'eMillions: Behind-the-Scenes Stories of 14 Internet Millionaires', interviewing online entrepreneurs from age 14. He expected the project to take three months; it took 15.
notes: Strong fit for a robotics, autonomy and AI angle. Go through DoorDash press (press@doordash.com) and mention DoorDash Labs/Dot. Some 2026 sources call him Chief Product Officer, so confirm his exact title.

name: Muneaki Masuda
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Culture Convenience Club (CCC), Japan
profile: Born 1951 in Hirakata, Osaka, he opened the first TSUTAYA store there in 1983 and founded Culture Convenience Club in 1985, building Japan's largest book, music and video rental/retail chain plus the T-Point (now V POINT) loyalty program. He took CCC private in 2011 and has been chairman since 2024, with Yasunori Takahashi as CEO.
interesting_fact: CCC created the T-Point loyalty card, which grew into one of Japan's largest points programs and merged with SMBC's V POINT in 2024; CCC also runs design-led bookstores such as Daikanyama T-Site.
deep_cut_fact: He named his first store, 'Tsutaya Shoten Hirakata' (1983), after 'Tsutaya', the trade name of his grandfather's family business; only later did he adopt the Edo-era publisher Tsutaya Juzaburo as a role model for TSUTAYA as a modern 'producer'.
notes: Best route is CCC's media-relations inquiry page. Japanese-language outreach likely more effective.

name: Fatma Tuba Yazici
current_role: CEO, Diler and Yazıcı Iron and Steel; principal shareholder, Diler Holding (Istanbul), as of the last Forbes update in 2018
profile: Fatma Tuba Yazıcı and her three sons became the largest shareholders of Diler Holding after her husband Recep Sami Yazıcı died in 2009. She became CEO of Diler and Yazıcı Iron and Steel, among Turkey's largest steel producers, and holds shares in listed Asil Steel. She sits on the Istanbul Chamber of Commerce's committee for iron-steel and hot-mill products.
interesting_fact: Forbes called her Turkey's only woman billionaire industrialist.

The Forbes profile was last updated in 2018, so her current status is unverified. Diler Holding's websites did not respond, and the web-search budget ran out. Outreach is unlikely to succeed; any approach would have to go through Diler Holding corporate.

name: Jenny Zhiya Qian
current_role: Co-founder, Cotti Coffee (库迪咖啡); founder and former CEO of Luckin Coffee
profile: Qian Zhiya (钱治亚) worked for over a decade alongside Lu Zhengyao in the CAR Inc./UCAR group, rising to UCAR COO, then founded Luckin Coffee in 2017 and took it public on Nasdaq in 2019. After leaving Luckin in 2020, she and Lu launched Cotti Coffee in 2022, which expanded rapidly to thousands of stores at home and abroad.
interesting_fact: Cotti Coffee, founded in 2022, reportedly reached about 5,000 outlets within its first couple of years, sparking a price war with Luckin and Starbucks in China.
deep_cut_fact: A 2018 profile noted she personally drinks around three to five cups of coffee a day.
notes: Sensitive: she was removed as Luckin CEO after its 2020 fabricated-sales scandal. Avoid in outreach. Very private; no personal channels found. Cotti's own site did not expose a contact address; best route is Cotti corporate PR.

name: Peter Green
profile: Manchester-born investor who married into the Mitchell family (Luscar coal, Alberta) and led the family business; family later held stakes in the Maybourne hotel group and bought Bermuda's Hamilton Princess in 2012. Died in Bermuda on 7 November 2024, aged 89.
notes: Deceased 7 Nov 2024 per Bermuda Government condolence https://www.gov.bm/news/premier-burt-peter-green-condolence and Royal Gazette https://royalgazette.com/general/news/article/20241114/bng-remembers-peter-green . Family interests (Hamilton Princess, Sugar Beach St Lucia) now associated with sons; identity matched via 'mining and inheritance' (Luscar) source of wealth.

name: Tan Yu Yeh
current_role: Founder and adviser, Mr D.I.Y. Group (Bursa Malaysia: MRDIY); stepped down as executive vice-chairman in April 2025
profile: Tan Yu Yeh, a University of Malaya physics graduate and former engineer and remisier, opened the first Mr D.I.Y. hardware store in Kuala Lumpur in 2005 with his brother Tan Yu Wei. It became a home-improvement chain of more than 4,000 stores across Asia and Europe, listed in 2020, and its Indonesian unit listed in December 2024. He became an adviser to the group in April 2025 and remains the controlling shareholder through Bee Family Ltd.
interesting_fact: He had no retail experience when he opened the first Mr D.I.Y. on Jalan Tuanku Abdul Rahman, KL, in July 2005. Two more outlets opened within the same year.
deep_cut_fact: Before retail, he graduated in physics from the University of Malaya (1996) and worked in engineering at hard-disk media maker Komag USA.
notes: Low-profile founder with no personal social accounts found. Best route is Mr D.I.Y. corporate/IR. Tatler notes his first career in engineering and as a remisier.

name: Dong Mingzhu
current_role: Chairwoman (and president per latest available sources) of Gree Electric Appliances, Zhuhai
profile: Dong Mingzhu (b. 1954, Nanjing) joined Gree's predecessor in 1990 at 36 as an air-conditioner saleswoman and rose to head of sales (1994), president (2001) and chairwoman (2012), making Gree one of the world's largest air-conditioner makers. She pushed Gree into solar, robotics and EVs (acquiring Yinlong in 2016) and is one of China's most famous executives.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her among the most powerful women in business internationally; Gree says most of its 44 'internationally leading' technologies relate to green energy, and 2023 was its most profitable year (about $4.1bn).
deep_cut_fact: Sent as a junior saleswoman to Anhui, one of China's poorer provinces, she alone produced about one-eighth of Gree's annual sales, which got her noticed by first GM Zhu Jianghong. Her 2006 memoir 'Regretless Pursuit' was turned into a CCTV television series.
notes: High-profile, outspoken; avoid her 2025 remarks on overseas returnees. Strong energy angle (solar air-conditioning, energy storage, Gree Altairnano/Yinlong EV batteries). Confirm her current president title before outreach.

name: Boris Titov
current_role: Russian Special Presidential Envoy for Relations with International Organizations on the Sustainable Development Goals (since 2024); owner of Abrau-Durso winery group
profile: Moscow-born (1960) MGIMO economist who co-founded oil/petrochemicals trader Solvalub (SVL Group) in 1991 and later bought the historic Abrau-Durso sparkling-wine house. Led the Business Russia lobby, served as Russia's first business ombudsman (2012-2024 per most sources), founded the Party of Growth, and ran for president in 2018 (0.76%). Since 2024 he is Putin's special envoy on SDGs.
interesting_fact: He ran in Russia's 2018 presidential election as the Party of Growth candidate, finishing sixth with 0.76% of the vote.
deep_cut_fact: In 1989 he headed the chemicals department of Urals, a Soviet-Dutch joint venture, and in 1991 he and partners set up Solvalub by buying a London-based solvents and lubricants firm they had worked with alongside Soviet oil exporter Soyuznefteexport.
notes: Sanctioned by the UK (incl. 2025 director-disqualification sanction re Abrau-Durso; listed on OpenSanctions). Russian state official. Outreach likely inappropriate/legally sensitive for a Western podcast; no personal contacts researched.

name: Xu Yingtong
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Sigenergy Technology (思格新能源, HKEX: 6656), Shanghai
profile: Xu Yingtong (许映童, 'Tony Xu', b. ~1974) spent 23 years at Huawei (joined Jan 1999), where he started and led its smart-PV/inverter business and later ran its Ascend AI computing unit. In May 2022 he founded Sigenergy in Shanghai, which makes AI-driven all-in-one solar-plus-storage systems (SigenStor) sold mainly overseas. It listed in Hong Kong in April 2026, making him a billionaire.
interesting_fact: Sigenergy went from founding (May 2022) to an HKEX listing (16 Apr 2026, ~HK$4.4bn raised) in under four years, billed as one of the fastest IPO paths for a Chinese company. Xu controls about 49% of the votes.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar, Xu was a wireless engineer at Huawei: PDT manager for wireless products, head of the wireless software platform and director of Huawei's Wireless Hangzhou Research Institute. Since May 2023 he has also been an independent director of PV giant Tongwei (600438.SH).
notes: Hurun 2026: 思格新能 / Sigenergy, Shanghai; lists a Fudan master's, while one report says Nanjing Univ. of Science & Technology, so education is unsettled. The press email is the 'Media Contact: Tracy Li' address in GlobeNewswire releases. He speaks at launches (SigenAgent AI energy agent, May 2026), a strong AI-plus-energy angle for the podcast.

name: Cho Hyun-beom
current_role: Chairman, Hankook & Company Group (holding company of Hankook Tire & Technology); stepped off the holding company's board in early 2026
profile: Grandson of Hankook founder Cho Hong-jai and younger son of ex-chairman Cho Yang-rai; joined Hankook Tire in 1998, rose through marketing and strategy, became CEO in 2018 and group chairman in 2021. He drove the Hanon Systems acquisition and US tire/battery expansion. After an embezzlement conviction he was paroled in mid-2026 and has begun returning to management.
interesting_fact: In 2025 he ordered that major group meetings attended by team leaders, cross-border communication and shared internal documents be conducted in English under an 'English as a Common Global Language' principle.
deep_cut_fact: Born 1972 in Haman, South Gyeongsang; he finished high school in the US and studied business at a Boston university before joining Hankook Tire's marketing side in 1998.
notes: Sensitive: convicted of embezzlement (2-year sentence, paroled ~July 2026); avoid legal and family topics. Status of formal chairman title should be rechecked. Route via Hankook corporate communications.

name: Rihanna
current_role: Singer; founder of Fenty Beauty (co-owned with LVMH) and co-owner of Savage X Fenty; founder of the Clara Lionel Foundation
profile: Robyn Rihanna Fenty, from Barbados (country field in input is wrong), became a global pop star after being discovered by Jay-Z as a teenager. Her billionaire status rests mainly on Fenty Beauty, co-owned with LVMH, plus a stake in lingerie brand Savage X Fenty. She headlined the 2023 Super Bowl halftime show and has been working on her first album since 2016's Anti.
interesting_fact: Barbados declared her a National Hero in 2021, after the government had named her an ambassador in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: At age 11 she joined Barbados's Cadet Corps, where her drill sergeant was future singer Shontelle; she also helped her father sell clothes at a street stall in Bridgetown.
notes: Input country 'Bosnia and Herzegovina' is a data error: she is Barbadian. Managed by Roc Nation; no published press email found for her personally. Very hard to reach for an entrepreneurship podcast; Fenty Beauty/LVMH comms or Roc Nation are the realistic routes.

name: Li Liufa
current_role: Chairman/controlling shareholder, Tianrui Group (Henan) - steel casting, cement, tourism, minerals
profile: Henan entrepreneur who left a state fertilizer-factory job in 1985 to co-found a small farmer-owned steel casting plant in Ruzhou, then built Tianrui Group through takeovers of struggling cement plants and a state machinery works. Tianrui spans cement (HK-listed China Tianrui Group Cement), casting, cultural tourism and minerals; he handed day-to-day control of the cement arm to the next generation in 2022.
interesting_fact: In 1993 his small Ruzhou steel-casting works took over the state-owned Henan Yuxi Coal Mine Machinery Plant, a deal Chinese press called a 'snake swallowing an elephant'; he was twice ranked Henan's richest person by New Fortune (2011, 2012).
deep_cut_fact: After starting as a temporary worker at Linru County No. 2 Fertilizer Plant in 1975, he was recommended in 1980 to study Chinese literature at Henan University; his first plant made motor housings for combustion engines, reportedly taking ~70% of the national market.
notes: Low profile, Chinese-language media only. Tianrui Cement shares have been suspended and 2025 results delayed (2024 forced share sale) - avoid. Best route: company channels / HKEX filings.

name: Lee Chae-yoon
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Leeno Industrial (KOSDAQ: 058470), Busan
profile: Lee Chae-yoon (b. 1950, Namhae County) founded Leeno Industrial in 1978, nine years after finishing technical high school in Busan. Leeno makes IC test sockets and 'Leeno Pin' probes that check chips for defects, for more than 1,000 customers including Nvidia, Samsung, SK Hynix and TSMC. AI-driven demand made him a billionaire in 2024; he owns about 35% of the company.
interesting_fact: The company name combines his surname with his wife's. Leeno was the first Korean maker of semiconductor test sockets and probes, which were entirely imported until the 1980s. 'Leeno Pin' is now the industry's generic word for test probes, with about 70% global share.
deep_cut_fact: A self-made engineer who kept studying: he finished Kwangsung (Kyeongsung) Engineering High School in 1969, founded Leeno in 1978, and earned his Dong-Eui University degree only in 1991, 13 years after starting the company. He later completed a KAIST executive programme.
notes: Low media profile; rarely gives interviews. Route via Leeno's general company email or contact page in Busan. Korean-language outreach is advisable. Forbes source: https://www.forbes.com/sites/johnkang/2024/03/14/founder-of-chip-testing-firm-rides-ai-boom-to-become-south-koreas-newest-billionaire/

name: Toby Neugebauer
current_role: Co-founder and largest shareholder of Fermi Inc. (FRMI); former CEO (left April 2026); co-owner of MLS club Austin FC
profile: West Texas-born energy investor (NYU BBA '93) who worked at Kidder Peabody, co-founded Windrock Energy (sold to Macquarie) and in 1998 co-founded Quantum Energy Partners, running five funds. In 2025 he co-founded Fermi America to build 'Project Matador', a multi-gigawatt private power grid and AI data-center campus near Amarillo, and took it public in Oct 2025.
interesting_fact: Fermi's Project Matador in the Texas Panhandle was pitched as one of the world's largest energy-and-data campuses, combining gas, nuclear, solar and grid power to serve hyperscale AI tenants.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy, his philanthropy has focused on family formation in US inner cities, and abroad he has worked with orphanages in China and helped build and maintain schools in Rwanda and Zambia.
notes: Sensitive timing: he left Fermi as CEO in April 2026, was removed from the board, and has been in a public proxy fight with the company (calling for a sale/special meeting). Avoid the dispute in outreach; his PR firm Collected Strategies issues his statements. Fermi IR is not a good route for him now.

name: Fang Xiaoling
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Maxio Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (STAR Market: 688449).
profile: Fang Xiaoling (b. 1963, US citizen) holds Zhejiang University BS/MS degrees and a University of Utah EE PhD. After co-founding Taiwanese fabless firm JMicron, she founded Maxio in Hangzhou in 2014; it designs SSD/data-storage controller chips and AIoT signal-processing chips, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in late 2024. She controls ~45% of Maxio.
interesting_fact: Surveillance giant Hikvision invested in Maxio in its third year and became its 2nd-largest shareholder (37% with a subsidiary pre-IPO); Maxio's controllers are mass-deployed at YMTC and Longsys.
deep_cut_fact: Before chips for storage, she was a principal engineer at Sonic Innovations, a Salt Lake City hearing-aid maker (then ranked world No. 7), from 1995-2001 right after her Utah PhD; she then cofounded JMicron and ran JMicron USA for 15 years.
notes: Low media profile; best route is Maxio IR (board secretary/CFO Qian Xiaofei). Data-center angle: enterprise SSD controllers.

name: Wan Lipeng
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2023) with wealth from 'CTI', shared with Wan Feng. CTI is likely Centre Testing International (华测检测, Shenzhen-listed 300012), whose chairman and controlling shareholder is Wan Feng, but no public source links the name 万里鹏 to the company.
notes: Could not verify identity or role; likely a family member of CTI chairman Wan Feng (not confirmed). Wan Feng, not Wan Lipeng, is the public face of CTI. Do not approach without confirmation.

name: Nan Cunfei
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2021) with wealth from Chint, the Wenzhou low-voltage electrical and solar group founded by Nan Cunhui. I could not confirm his exact role or relationship within the Chint group from accessible sources in this session.
notes: Research incomplete: web search budget ran out before this person. Not on the Chint leadership pages or Chinese Wikipedia. Off Hurun lists since 2021. Chint (electrical equipment, solar via Chint New Energy/Astronergy) is relevant to the energy angle; Nan Cunhui is the better-documented family member. Needs a follow-up search.

name: Li Xiaolai
current_role: Bitcoin investor and author; founder of Bitfund (BitFund.pe) and INBlockchain
profile: Former New Oriental English test-prep teacher (2001-08) who began buying bitcoin in 2011. He founded crypto VC Bitfund in 2013 and was dubbed 'China's richest bitcoin billionaire'. In 2018 he said he would stop investing in crypto projects; he now writes books such as 'The Self-Cultivation of Leeks' (韭菜的自我修养).
interesting_fact: In July 2017 he raised a $200M ICO in China, two months before Beijing banned ICOs. He has publicly disputed the 'richest bitcoin holder' label, writing that he knew others who held more.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he was a bestselling self-improvement author: his book on time management, 'Take Time As a Friend' (把时间当作朋友), predates his bitcoin fame. At New Oriental he received stock options in 2005, an episode he describes as the start of his investing.
notes: Active online and writes in public; his X account and personal site are the most direct routes, and he also lists a WeChat public account. Avoid referencing the 2018 leaked-audio controversy. Only appeared on Hurun in 2018, so his current wealth is unclear.

name: Luo Yungang
current_role: Unknown; Hurun listed him (2017-2018) under Baota Petrochemical (宝塔石化), Yinchuan, Ningxia
profile: Luo Yungang (罗运刚) is listed by Hurun China 2017 (RMB5300m) and 2018 (RMB7000m) with Baota Petrochemical Group (宝塔石化集团), a Yinchuan-based private refiner with ~200 fuel stations that also ran Yinchuan University (hence 'petrochemicals, education'). His exact role or stake could not be independently confirmed.
notes: Hurun 2017/2018: 罗运刚 / Bao Ta Petrochemical, Yinchuan; no birth year. Searched 罗运刚 + 宝塔石化 / 泰瑞智本. The 2015 SZSE filing of Baota Industry (000595) lists Baota Petrochemical's holders as Sun Hengchao 43.8%, 宁夏泰瑞智本 32.1%, 江苏汇金 18.46% and Sun Shulan 5.64%; he is not named, so any stake is probably indirect. Group hit a debt crisis in 2018. Baidu/Qichacha blocked.

name: Zhang Jiangbo
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Ningbo Peacebird Fashion Co. (603877.SH)
profile: Ningbo-based co-founder of Peacebird, the Chinese apparel group led by his brother, chairman Zhang Jiangping, which has more than 4,000 stores across China. He sits on the board and is listed with his brother as actual controller, holding about 21% of the shares directly after 2023-24 internal transfers from Peacebird Group.
interesting_fact: In 1996 the brothers borrowed RMB 20,000 (about $2,900) to set up a garment factory with just six sewing machines, the start of the Peacebird fashion empire.
notes: Very low profile and overshadowed by his brother Zhang Jiangping, who is the public face. Board listing from a March 2025 SSE board resolution (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-03-28/1222923540.PDF). He was not in the April 2026 related-director list, so check his current board status. The best route is Peacebird corporate/IR.

name: Hou Xiaodi
current_role: Founder and CEO, Bot Auto (Houston-based autonomous trucking company)
profile: Xiaodi Hou co-founded autonomous-trucking company TuSimple in 2015 and served as its CTO and then CEO, taking it public on Nasdaq in 2021 (the source of his Hurun listing). After leaving in 2022 he founded Bot Auto in Houston in 2023, which in 2025 ran what it called the first fully humanless commercial freight runs on Texas highways (Houston-Dallas, Houston-San Antonio).
interesting_fact: Bot Auto completed a commercial freight run with nobody in the cab and no remote driver; Hou framed it as 'a business, not a demonstration.'
deep_cut_fact: Before trucks he was a vision scientist: his 2014 Caltech PhD, advised by neuroscientist Christof Koch, modelled how humans pick out foreground objects and proposed 'Image Signature', an extremely fast algorithm for predicting where people's eyes land in an image.
notes: Open to media and very relevant (AI, autonomy, logistics). Ongoing litigation with TuSimple (now CreateAI) over IP and its liquidation; avoid as a topic. Hurun wealth figure dates from 2021 TuSimple valuation and is likely far lower now.

name: Li Lingyun
current_role: Vice Chairman, Do-Fluoride New Materials Co. (多氟多, SZSE: 002407), term to Dec 2028
profile: Chinese executive (b. January 1976, master's degree) at Do-Fluoride, a Jiaozuo, Henan-based maker of fluorine chemicals and lithium-battery materials such as lithium hexafluorophosphate electrolyte salt. Hurun lists her wealth jointly with founder Li Shijiang. She has been vice chairman since 2018 and was earlier the company's general manager.
interesting_fact: Do-Fluoride began as a cryolite maker for the aluminium industry. In February 2009 it developed its own crystalline lithium hexafluorophosphate (EV-battery electrolyte salt) technology, breaking a foreign monopoly, and it listed in Shenzhen in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She started out heading the foreign-trade section at the Jiaozuo Cryolite Plant, Do-Fluoride's predecessor, before becoming deputy GM and GM of Jiaozuo Do-Fluoride Chemical. She is a professor-level senior engineer and a member of China's Light Metal Metallurgy Committee.
notes: Wealth is shared with Li Shijiang (founder, chairman until 2025); Li Yunfeng became chairman in Dec 2025. Her family relationship to the founders is not confirmed in the sources checked, so don't assume it. She is a low-profile, Chinese-language executive. Bio comes from Sina Finance's exchange-filing data.

name: Lau Ngai Leung
current_role: Chairman, Chong Sai Enterprise Group (澳門創世企業集團), Macau; Macau deputy to China's National People's Congress
profile: Lau Ngai Leung (劉藝良; Portuguese romanisation Lao Ngai Leong) is a Macau real-estate businessman who chairs Chong Sai Enterprise Group and was ranked Macau's richest person on the 2021 Hurun China list. A five-term Macau NPC deputy and former Executive Council member, he is also a vice-chairman of the All-China Federation of Returned Overseas Chinese.
interesting_fact: He received an honorary Doctor of Social Sciences from the University of Macau in 2018 and is an 'Honorary Citizen of Chaozhou'.
deep_cut_fact: As an NPC deputy he pushed for the Standing Committee decision that let Macau exercise jurisdiction over the University of Macau's new Hengqin campus, and for longer Zhuhai-Macau border checkpoint hours.
notes: Search under 'Lao Ngai Leong' (Macau spelling). Politically prominent; no company website or published contact found. Latest-status confirmation for 2025-26 not found.

name: Wang Jingliang
current_role: Legal representative of Kunming Huachen Investment Co. (昆明华辰投资), a shareholder of Yunnan Energy New Material / SEMCORP (恩捷股份, 002812.SZ)
profile: Wang Jingliang (王敬良, b. 1963, Kunming) is a Kunming investor whose wealth comes from a stake in Yunnan Energy New Material (恩捷股份), the world's largest lithium-battery separator maker, controlled by the Paul Xiaoming Lee family. Hurun 2021 put his fortune at RMB6.5bn (6th richest in Yunnan). He reportedly heads Kunming Huachen Investment and the Huakun investment partnerships in Hainan and Zhuhai.
interesting_fact: Kunming Huachen Investment held 2.64% (23.4m shares) of Yunnan Energy New Material at end-2020, among its top-10 shareholders alongside the Lee family's vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: Huachen Investment was one of the original holders of Shanghai Energy (上海恩捷, SEMCORP's separator unit). In 2018 it swapped that stake for new shares when packaging maker Yunnan Chuangxin (创新股份) bought Shanghai Energy at RMB24.87/share, turning a cigarette-pack printer into a battery-materials giant.
notes: Hurun 2021: 王敬良, b. 1963-04, Kunming, company 恩捷股份 / Energy New Material ('packaging box production'). His link to 昆明华辰投资 (legal representative) comes from a secondary rich-list article (https://m.maigoo.com/top/399867.html), not a filing. His name does not appear in Enjie's 2020/2024 reports, which only name Huachen. Very private. No contacts found. Enjie IR would be the only institutional route.

name: Ye Liaoning
current_role: Co-founder and consultant, Sunny Optical Technology; chairman until 1 Nov 2025 (retired from the board citing retirement age)
profile: Ye Liaoning (叶辽宁, b. ~1965) joined the Yuyao Chengbei optical-instrument factory that became Sunny Optical in 1984 and is counted among the group's founders. He rose to deputy GM (1995), executive director (2007) and chairman, leading Sunny's growth into a global phone/auto camera-optics leader, then stepped down in Nov 2025 and stays on as a consultant.
interesting_fact: He stepped down as chairman effective 1 Nov 2025 ahead of reaching retirement age in early 2026, handing over to founder Wang Wenjian's son Wang Tan Jiong, and remains a consultant to the group.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the factory in 1984 as a teenager and earned his diploma part-time from Zhejiang Radio & TV University only in 1999; he received China's National May-First Labor Medal (2019) and the title National Model Worker (2020).
notes: Low international profile; now retired from the board. Only published route is Sunny's IR office. Fortune shared with Sunny co-founders (see Wang Wenjian, P05955).

name: Zhang Weijian (张维建)
current_role: Chairman, President & legal representative, Shuhua Sports Co. (SSE: 605299), Jinjiang/Quanzhou, Fujian; chairman of Shuhua Investment
profile: Fujian entrepreneur who has led Shuhua Sports, a fitness-equipment maker founded in 1996 in Jinjiang, as chairman since 2013 and took it public on the Shanghai main board in 2020. Shuhua (~2,500 staff) makes commercial and home gym equipment and was named a national sports-industry demonstration enterprise in 2017.
interesting_fact: Shuhua had two multi-year partnerships with the Chinese Olympic Committee (2013-16 and 2021-24), supplying training equipment and services to China's Olympic delegations.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the company he heads the Chidian Town Education Development Promotion Association in his home area of Jinjiang, Fujian, and previously chaired Shuhua's real-estate arm.
notes: Sources are Eastmoney F10 data drawn from exchange filings (Chinese). Low international profile; Chinese-language outreach via board secretary office (ir@shuhua.com). He sold some directly held shares in early 2026 (filings).

name: Hartono Kweefanus
current_role: Chairperson Emeritus and director, Monde Nissin Corporation (Philippines); chairman, PT Khong Guan Biscuit Indonesia
profile: Indonesian businessman whose late father co-founded Philippine food maker Monde Nissin (Lucky Me! noodles, SkyFlakes, Quorn meat substitutes) in 1979 with Betty Ang, his sister-in-law. A Monde director for 45 years and long its chairman, he is now Chairperson Emeritus, while also chairing Indonesia's PT Khong Guan Biscuit and other family companies. His wealth stems from his stake in Monde Nissin.
interesting_fact: Monde Nissin's June 2021 IPO raised $1.1 billion, at the time the Philippines' biggest ever; its Lucky Me! brand has been the country's most-chosen FMCG brand for a decade.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Industrial and Business Management at Nanyang University in Singapore, and besides Monde Nissin he chairs PT Khong Guan Biscuit Indonesia, the maker of the famous red Khong Guan biscuit tins.
notes: Very private; Kataline Darmono is now board chair and Henry Soesanto CEO. Food-manufacturing, not energy. Route via Monde Nissin IR. The 'red tin' descriptor of Khong Guan is general knowledge, not from the cited page.

name: Betty Ang
current_role: President and co-founder, Monde Nissin Corporation (PSE: MONDE)
profile: Betty T. Ang, an Assumption College business graduate, co-founded Monde Nissin in 1979 with her late father-in-law Hidajat Darmono and built it into the Philippines' leading biscuit and instant-noodle maker (Lucky Me!, SkyFlakes, Fita). Monde Nissin's June 2021 IPO raised 55.9 billion pesos, then the country's largest, and it owns UK meat-alternative brand Quorn.
interesting_fact: Forbes once called her 'one of Asia's most mysterious tycoons'; she rarely gives interviews despite running one of the Philippines' biggest food companies.
deep_cut_fact: Monde Nissin's 1991 launch of Lucky Me! Pancit Canton was the first dry stir-fry pouched noodle in the Philippine market and created a category worth over 10 billion pesos by 2020; the company's very first products in 1979 were Nissin Butter Coconut biscuits and Nissin Wafer.
notes: Extremely private; husband Hoediono Kweefanus is vice-chairman. Avoid Quorn impairment/losses topics. Route via Monde Nissin corporate communications.

name: Ivan Müller Botelho
current_role: Patriarch of the controlling Botelho family of Energisa S.A. and its long-time former chairman; he is not listed on the board elected in April 2026
profile: An electrical engineer (University of Miami) from Leopoldina, Minas Gerais, Ivan Botelho is the third generation of the family that has controlled Brazilian utility Energisa since 1905. He built it from a regional Cataguases utility into a group with nine state distribution companies, transmission and gas, serving more than 20 million customers. His sons Ricardo (CEO) and Maurício (CFO) now run it.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Energisa, the underdog bidder, won the 2013 creditors' vote for the bankrupt Grupo Rede over CPFL, a deal that changed the group's scale. In 2026, at 92, he published a memoir, 'A jornada da Energia para o futuro', based on his testimony to journalist Plínio Fraga.
deep_cut_fact: He started on the front line, in the lines and power plants. His memoir recalls installing Brazil's first photoelectric cell to switch street lighting on automatically, and a safety-glove demonstration that ended up shutting down power to the whole town. He was also an early backer of the Instituto Liberal think tank.
notes: He is about 92 (per JB, March 2026), so the realistic route is via Energisa IR or his sons; CEO Ricardo Botelho is the active public face. The new memoir (2026) is a natural hook for outreach. Confirm his current board status in Energisa's Formulário de Referência.

name: Huang Yi
current_role: Chairman and executive director, Zhongsheng Group Holdings (HKEX: 0881)
profile: Co-founded Zhongsheng Group with CEO Li Guoqiang in 1998 and built it into one of China's largest car-dealer networks, focused on luxury and mid-to-high-end brands such as Mercedes-Benz, Lexus, Porsche and Land Rover. He sets group strategy as chairman of the Hong Kong-listed company.
interesting_fact: Zhongsheng is one of China's largest national car dealerships, centred on luxury marques like Mercedes-Benz, Lexus and Porsche.
deep_cut_fact: After a 1983 economics degree from Xiamen University he spent 1984-94 at state-owned China Resources Machinery, importing cars and machinery, and was named an 'economist' by the trade ministry in 1990; in 1994 he joined Hong Kong's Huaji Auto and became a shareholder in 1996.
notes: Low public profile. Route via Zhongsheng investor relations (company site was unreachable from this environment, so no IR email verified). Not to be confused with Yunnan politician Huang Yi.

name: Andrea Della Valle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Tod's S.p.A. (Tod's, Hogan, Roger Vivier, Fay)
profile: Born 1965 in Sant'Elpidio a Mare in the Marche shoe district, Andrea and brother Diego control Tod's, the luxury shoe and leather-goods group grown from their grandfather's early-1900s workshop. In 2024 they took Tod's private with L Catterton and LVMH at a ~$1.5bn valuation. The brothers also hold stakes in Piaggio and RCS MediaGroup; Andrea chaired ACF Fiorentina 2004-09.
interesting_fact: Tod's group funded the restoration of Rome's Colosseum; Andrea also led Fiorentina's revival after its previous owner's bankruptcy and remained honorary president until the club was sold to Rocco Commisso in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: On 31 May 2024 the Marche mountain town of Arquata del Tronto, devastated by the 2016 earthquake, made him an honorary citizen 'for the social and civil commitment shown after the 2016 earthquake'.
notes: Brother Diego Della Valle is the public face of Tod's; Andrea is lower-profile. todsgroup.com blocked automated access, so press contact not extracted - check its Media/Contacts section manually. Web search budget exhausted at this point.

name: Ivan Streshinsky
current_role: Shareholder (~5%) in USM Holding; former CEO of USM (stepped down in 2022)
profile: Russian lawyer-turned-executive who worked for Alisher Usmanov from 2006, first as CEO of Gazmetall and from 2012 as head of USM Holding, the group behind Metalloinvest, MegaFon and AliExpress Russia. Usmanov gave him 3% of USM in 2014 and 2% more in 2021. He resigned as USM CEO in 2022 to avoid Western sanctions.
interesting_fact: Before joining Usmanov he provided legal support on corporate transactions for billionaire Vasily Anisimov.
deep_cut_fact: He created the rock band ISB, which released its first album, 'Runaway', in 2020.
notes: On the US OFAC SDN list (designated in 2023 under EO 14024). A US-based journalist should get legal advice before any dealings. I found no published personal or office contact; USM is not an appropriate route. Recommend skipping.

name: Max Turnauer
current_role: Deceased (died November 2020)
profile: Son of Constantia group founder Herbert Turnauer; inherited Constantia Industries (Fundermax, Isovolta) in the family split. Died in 2020 aged 90; his son Stanislaus Turnauer now chairs and owns the group.
notes: Death reported by Industriemagazin on 9 Nov 2020: https://industriemagazin.at/industrie/der-industrielle-max-turnauer-verstorben/ . Listing is stale; relevant living person is Stanislaus Turnauer (Constantia Industries).

name: Vladimir Melnikov
current_role: Founder, owner and chairman of the board, Gloria Jeans (Moscow)
profile: Melnikov founded the Gloria cooperative in Rostov-on-Don in 1988 and the Gloria Jeans retail company in 1997. The business also manufactured for Western brands such as Levi's and H&M. After Inditex, H&M and Uniqlo left Russia in 2022 it expanded rapidly into their vacated space and now runs 700+ stores in Russia, Belarus and Kazakhstan. HQ moved to Moscow in 2016.
interesting_fact: In 2022 he gave 1 million rubles to each employee who had worked at Gloria Jeans for at least 10 years.
deep_cut_fact: His 1988 Gloria cooperative in Rostov-on-Don became the first officially recognised jeans maker in the Soviet Union.
notes: Russia-based. Check sanctions and reputational considerations before outreach. The Gloria Jeans site renders via JavaScript, so I could not extract a press email. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Charles Beauduin
current_role: Chairman of Barco NV (since Sept 2024); CEO and owner of Vandewiele NV (since 1993)
profile: Belgian industrialist (b. 1959; law, KU Leuven; MBA, Harvard) from a former sugar-industry family. He took over Kortrijk-based textile-machinery maker Vandewiele in 1993 and built it into a ~4,000-person group in 14 countries (incl. Italy's Savio, bought 2021). Barco director since 2015, he was co-CEO 2021-2024 and is now chairman; he owns ~25% of Barco.
interesting_fact: Vandewiele invests about 10% of sales in R&D; Beauduin says its looms went from one motor per machine to 14,000 computer-controlled motors, with AI that lets machines learn to solve problems: 'We've become a technology company.'
deep_cut_fact: Vandewiele, started some 165 years ago as a loom builder, now lists energy efficiency (in its own plants and in the machines it ships) as its current focus, and a single modern loom can cost close to EUR 2 million.
notes: Chairmanship announced Jun 2024 (https://www.barco.com/en/about/press-releases/2024/charles-beauduin-becomes-chairman-of-barco). Known in Belgian press for his 'legendary optimism'. Barco data-center/visualisation and Vandewiele energy-efficiency angles fit the podcast.

name: Louis Bacon
current_role: Founder, Chairman and principal investment manager, Moore Capital Management; Founder and Chairman, The Moore Charitable Foundation
profile: North Carolina-born macro trader who profited in the 1987 crash and founded Moore Capital in 1989, becoming one of Wall Street's best-known macro managers. He returned outside capital in 2019 and now runs Moore mainly as a family/employee investment firm, while focusing heavily on land, water and wildlife conservation through the Moore Charitable Foundation (founded 1992).
interesting_fact: He named Moore Capital after his own middle name, and launched Moore Global Investments in 1990 with $25,000 inherited from his family.
deep_cut_fact: His Wall Street start came from a summer job: while working on a fishing boat on Long Island he met NYSE specialist Walter Frank, who gave him a clerking job at Walter N. Frank & Co. during his college summers. He later ran a floor 'runner' job at the New York Cotton Exchange.
notes: Energy angle: has written publicly against Drax biomass sourcing (Daily Mail op-ed linked from louisbacon.com) and on wildfire/forest health and offshore drilling. Ann Colley, Moore Capital's Director of Public Relations and Charitable Giving and Foundation Executive Director, is the published PR lead (https://www.moorecharitable.org/leadership/ann-colley/).

name: Joachim Ante
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, Unity Technologies; co-founder and backer of Underground Ventures (Copenhagen geothermal VC)
profile: German-born Joachim 'Joe' Ante co-founded Unity (originally Over the Edge Entertainment) in Copenhagen in 2004 with David Helgason and Nicholas Francis. He wrote much of the engine's core, and Unity became the engine behind games like Pokemon Go and Among Us; it listed on the NYSE in 2020. He is now a climate philanthropist and in 2024 co-founded Underground Ventures, a geothermal-only venture firm.
interesting_fact: Unity began as a failed game project: Ante and his cofounders realised the engine they had built was more valuable to other developers than their game. He began writing the engine's core as a teenager.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded Underground Ventures with Torsten Kolind (ex-YouNoodle), and his own money funds it: a $40m vehicle backing early-stage geothermal tech such as drilling, well casings, sensors and underground storage. Portfolio includes Hephae Energy and GA Drilling.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast because of the geothermal angle. Underground Ventures is the most natural route; Torsten Kolind runs investment and has appeared on energy podcasts (Low Carbon Solutions ep. 183). He is also a Founders Pledge member. I found no verified personal social accounts.

name: Bart van Malderen
current_role: Founder, CEO and chairman, Drylock Technologies (Zele, Belgium); chairman of VGP NV
profile: Bart Van Malderen (b. 1966, Merchtem) spent two decades building his father's diaper company Ontex into Europe's largest diaper and feminine-care maker before it was sold to Candover in 2002. After his non-compete ended he founded Drylock in 2012 to make ultra-thin, cellulose-free diapers; it now makes about a billion diapers a month. He also chairs logistics-property developer VGP and is the largest shareholder of German webshop Lillydoo.
interesting_fact: Drylock launched what it called the world's first compostable diaper in February 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded VGP, now a large European logistics-park developer, with Jan Van Geet, initially building semi-industrial property in the Czech Republic; he earned an MBA at EU Business School in Montreux and joined Ontex at 20, in 1986.
notes: VGP angle is relevant for an energy/data-center podcast (VGP develops logistics parks with large rooftop solar). No personal accounts found; Drylock or VGP corporate communications are the route.

name: Irvine Laidlaw, Lord Laidlaw
current_role: Chairman, Irvine Laidlaw Foundation (Laidlaw Foundation); private investor
profile: Irvine Laidlaw (b. 1942, Keith, Banffshire) built the Institute for International Research from a small US publisher bought in 1973 into the world's largest conference organiser, selling it in 2005 for about £768m; he also founded Abbey Business Centres. A former Conservative life peer (2004-2010), he now focuses on education philanthropy via the Laidlaw Foundation.
interesting_fact: A keen historic racer, he owned and raced a Le Mans-winning 1950s Jaguar and a 1962 Ferrari 250 GTO before stopping racing in 2013. Wikipedia also says he part-owns a $2.1bn wind-farm project.
deep_cut_fact: His £9m gift to the University of Leeds, where he studied economics in the 1960s, was its largest ever and funded the £26m Laidlaw Library (opened 2015). His Laidlaw Scholarships for undergraduate research and leadership now run at about 19 universities including Oxford, Cambridge, Columbia and EPFL.
notes: Contacts are for his foundation, not him personally. Possible energy angle via reported wind-farm investment (unverified detail). Left the House of Lords in 2010.

name: Xie Juhua
current_role: Director, largest shareholder (~27%) and co-actual controller, Nanjing King-Friend Biochemical Pharmaceutical (健友股份, SSE 603707)
profile: Born in 1951, Xie Juhua is the largest individual shareholder of Nanjing King-Friend, a heparin and injectable-drug maker founded in 2000 whose products include cardiovascular (anticoagulant) and anti-tumor drugs, sold in China and abroad. She, her son Tang Yongqun (chairman and general manager since 2008) and Ding Ying are the company's actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Before becoming a pharmaceutical entrepreneur and investor she worked as a physician, according to King-Friend's director profile.
notes: Low profile; son Tang Yongqun is the public face of the company. Best route is the company's investor-relations office in Nanjing.

name: Prachak Tangkaravakoon
current_role: Founder of TOA Paint (Thailand) PCL; stepped down as chairman in Feb 2024 for health reasons (no current executive role)
profile: Founder of TOA, Thailand's largest paint company (around half the decorative market) with plants across Southeast Asia. He grew a family hardware business into paint supplies in 1964 and opened the first paint factory in 1972; the company IPO'd in 2017 raising $360m. Operations are run by his children; son Jatuphat is CEO.
interesting_fact: The Tangkaravakoon family started by importing TOA paint from Japan before building their own Thai manufacturing; he co-founded the business with his wife Laor.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as a hardware store; he expanded into paint supplies in 1964 and opened the first TOA paint factory in 1972.
notes: Retired from board in 2024 citing health; outreach better directed to CEO Jatuphat Tangkaravakoon via TOA. directors@ is the board contact channel published in the 2025 sustainability report.

name: Baokun Bai
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, Guangdong KinLong Hardware Products (坚朗五金, SZSE:002791), Dongguan
profile: Bai Baokun (白宝鲲, b. 1970) founded KinLong in Dongguan in 2003 and built it into China's leading supplier of high-end door, window and curtain-wall hardware systems, listing it in Shenzhen in 2016. He remains controlling shareholder and leads the company as it expands into broader building-hardware supply.
interesting_fact: He has received a second-class National Science and Technology Progress Award and was named a 'meritorious figure' by the China Building Decoration Association.
deep_cut_fact: Besides hardware, he sits on the board of Ligao Foods (立高食品), a listed Guangzhou bakery-ingredients company; he is a trained engineer with a Peking University HSBC Business School EMBA.
notes: Low public profile; few interviews. Email is the board secretary's office (董事会办公室) per 2026 interim report. Chinese-language outreach advisable. Education details vary between sources (EMBA vs DBA).

name: Muhammed Aziz Khan
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Summit Group (Bangladesh); based in Singapore
profile: Bangladesh-born, Singapore-based Muhammed Aziz Khan (b. 1955, Dhaka IBA MBA) started out as a trader and founded Summit in 1985; it built Bangladesh's first independent power plant (Khulna, 1998) and its first private off-dock port, and now spans power, LNG, ports, fibre optics and real estate. Japan's JERA owns 22% of Summit Power International, run by his daughter Ayesha.
interesting_fact: He told Nikkei Asia Summit plans Bangladesh's first data centre using Summit Power's gas-fired capacity: 'Summit Group's next phase focuses on integrating energy and data, leveraging our LNG and fibre-optic expertise.'
deep_cut_fact: Singapore's Prime Minister's Office awarded him the Public Service Medal (COVID-19) for financially helping Bangladeshi workers in Singapore during the pandemic; he and his wife were also the first Bangladeshis named UNICEF International Council members.

public_contacts.value: enquiry@summitpowerinternational.com (Summit Power International, One Raffles Place, Singapore)

notes: Very good fit: energy + data-centre angle (gas-to-data-centre plan, fibre/LNG). Gives interviews to Bangladeshi press and Nikkei. Best route: Summit Power International Singapore enquiry form (press category).

name: Richard Yuengling Jr
current_role: Owner and CEO, D.G. Yuengling & Son (America's oldest brewery), Pottsville, Pennsylvania
profile: Dick Yuengling, fifth-generation owner of D.G. Yuengling & Son, bought out his father in 1985 and turned a struggling 137,000-barrel regional brewery into one of America's largest brewers (~2m barrels a year), largely on Yuengling Lager. His four daughters work in the business and are being primed to succeed him; in 2026 the brand is expanding into Wisconsin and Iowa.
interesting_fact: Yuengling, opened in Pottsville in 1829, survived Prohibition by making ice cream and near beer.
deep_cut_fact: He knew by age 10 he wanted to run the brewery and started working there part-time around 15; he admits that when Yuengling isn't on tap, he'll order a Sam Adams or Sierra Nevada. His brewing philosophy: 'We stay nuts and bolts — we make beer.'
notes: Down-to-earth, avoids publicity. Press contact is brewery media relations (Bethany Ingerick) per 2026 releases. Daughter Wendy Yuengling (Chief Administrative Officer) is the more public family spokesperson.

name: Gennady Kozovoy
current_role: Shareholder (~5.7%) of Evraz plc; former CEO and board member of Raspadskaya coal company (Mezhdurechensk, Kuzbass)
profile: Siberian coal executive who rose through Russia's Raspadskaya mine. In 1993 he was elected general director and, with partner Alexander Vagin, gained control of the company as workers' shares were bought up. Raspadskaya listed in 2006. In 2012 they sold control to Evraz for cash plus Evraz shares, his main asset today. He stepped down as CEO in July 2014.
interesting_fact: Kozovoy and Vagin turned Raspadskaya, once a 'people's enterprise' owned by its miners, into one of Russia's biggest coking-coal producers. They sold their stake to Evraz for about $202M plus roughly 11% of Evraz.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 36 years at Raspadskaya, starting as an electrician-fitter (elektroslesar) at the mine and rising to general director, as the company noted when he handed over the CEO role in 2014.
notes: Very private and gives virtually no press. Russia-based. Evraz was sanctioned by the UK in 2022 (Abramovich link) and is no longer LSE-traded, so outreach may be impractical. Patronymic Ivanovich. No published contact found.

name: Dani Reiss
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Canada Goose Holdings (NYSE/TSX: GOOS)
profile: Third-generation owner of Toronto outerwear brand Canada Goose, founded by his grandfather as Metro Sportswear in 1957.
