He was Russia's honorary consul in Nuremberg until March 2022; Knauf's Russia business was a source of controversy. Route via Knauf Group Corporate Communications (head Matthias Link).

name: Georg ("Heini Jr.") Thyssen-Bornemisza
profile: Georg Heinrich, Baron Thyssen-Bornemisza (b. 1950, Lugano), eldest son of industrialist and art collector Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza. He chaired TBG AG, the family investment arm that bought weather-data firms DTN and MeteoGroup, and founded the NOMIS Foundation. He died in Zürich on 30 September 2022.
notes: Deceased 30 Sep 2022 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Heinrich_Thyssen-Bornemisza). TBG AG and the NOMIS Foundation continue; the TBG/DTN weather-data angle could interest an energy podcast through other TBG executives.

name: Martha Stewart
current_role: Founder of the Martha Stewart brand (owned by Marquee Brands since 2019), media personality and author
profile: Martha Stewart turned a 1970s Westport, Connecticut catering business into Martha Stewart Living Omnimedia, the publishing, TV and merchandising empire that made her a billionaire on paper when it went public in 1999. The brand is now owned by Marquee Brands; she remains its face, with 100 books (Martha: The Cookbook, 2024), a 2024 Netflix documentary and NBC's 'Yes, Chef!' with José Andrés (2025).
interesting_fact: In 2023, at 81, she became the oldest woman ever to appear on the cover of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue.
deep_cut_fact: As a 10-year-old in Nutley, N.J., she babysat for New York Yankees Mickey Mantle, Yogi Berra and Gil McDougald and organised birthday parties for Mantle's four sons; she later worked as a Wall Street stockbroker from 1967 before starting her catering business.
notes: Forbes billionaire only in 2005; current net worth estimated far lower. Avoid 2004 conviction. Very accessible publicly but heavily agented; Marquee Brands (marqueebrands.com) handles brand partnerships. Her blog themarthablog.com is personal and frequently updated.

name: Robert (Bob) Oatley
current_role: Deceased (died 10 January 2016, aged 87); founder of Rosemount Estate winery, former owner of Hamilton Island and yacht Wild Oats XI
notes: Death confirmed via Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Oatley). Family (Oatley Family Holdings / Hamilton Island, Oatley Wines) continues the business.

name: Ramesh Chandra
current_role: Founder of Unitech Group (no current executive role found; Unitech has been under a government-appointed board since 2020)
profile: IIT Kharagpur-trained structural engineer who in 1972 co-founded United Technical Consultants, a Delhi soil-investigation firm that became Unitech, once India's second-largest listed real-estate developer. He moved into civil engineering (including projects in Libya) and then housing, with Forbes putting his fortune at over $11B at its 2007 peak; he was a billionaire through 2011.
interesting_fact: Unitech began in 1972 as a soil-testing consultancy started by five partners before becoming a property giant building in Gurgaon and the Middle East.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh, the son of a banker, he worked briefly at the Bridge and Roof Company in Kolkata after IIT Kharagpur, then went to the University of Southampton to study structural engineering before co-founding his soil-investigation firm with four friends.
notes: Born c.1939-41; alive status not confirmed (no death reported on Wikipedia). Heavily entangled in legal cases (company and family) since 2011; Unitech under government-appointed management. Low suitability for outreach; no published personal contact found.

name: Lloyd Dorfman
current_role: Founder of Travelex; Chair of the Royal Opera House; Vice President, King's Trust International
profile: Sir Lloyd Dorfman (b. 1952) started Travelex in 1976 as one London bureau de change and built the world's largest non-bank FX retailer, sold to Abu Dhabi owners in 2014. He then chaired co-working pioneer The Office Group (sold to Blackstone, 2017) and co-founded Doddle; today he is a leading arts and youth philanthropist.
interesting_fact: His £10 million gift to the National Theatre's redevelopment led to the Cottesloe being renamed the Dorfman Theatre in 2013; Travelex also pioneered the National's cheap-ticket season.
deep_cut_fact: He never went to university; after a year studying for the Bar at Lincoln's Inn he dropped out, and in 1986 won Travelex the landmark contract to be the first non-bank currency exchange at the newly opened Heathrow Terminal 4. His business motto: 'fire before you aim'.
notes: Writes occasional op-eds (City AM) and gives interviews to the Jewish press; approachable via his philanthropic roles (Royal Opera House, King's Trust International). Avoid Travelex's later 2020 collapse/ransomware topic. No direct published personal or office email found.

name: Nurzhan Subkhanberdin
current_role: Private investor; former founder and chairman of Kazkommertsbank (exited 2015)
profile: Almaty-born (1964) banker who graduated in political economy from Moscow State University in 1988 and founded Kazkommertsbank, for years one of Kazakhstan's largest banks. He sold his stake and left the board in 2015 and has since kept a low profile, with investment interests including Hong Kong-based Meridian Capital.
interesting_fact: In 2008 he and six other Kazakh businessmen put about $100m into opening Haileybury Almaty, the first British private school in Central Asia.
notes: Very private; no published contact found. Wikipedia covers controversies (political-influence commentary, Paradise Papers reporting on Meridian) which should be avoided in outreach. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nurzhan_Subkhanberdin

name: Ioan Niculae
current_role: Founder/owner, InterAgro group (agribusiness and fertilizers), Romania; owner of FC Astra Giurgiu
profile: Born 1954 in Buturugeni, Giurgiu County, Niculae traded chemical fertilizers in the 1980s, co-founded trader Interaction after 1990 and set up InterAgro in 1995, building one of Romania's largest grain and fertilizer groups (~50,000 ha farmed, large silo capacity). He also profited from stakes in insurer Asirom and the Astra Română refinery. Forbes listed him 2010-2015.
interesting_fact: In Forbes' 2010 list he was the third-richest Romanian, behind Dinu Patriciu and Ion Tiriac; his group farms roughly 50,000 hectares, making him one of Romania's largest grain growers.
deep_cut_fact: He has owned the football club Astra Giurgiu since 1996, and planted about 170 hectares of vineyards whose first harvest came in 2008.
notes: Caution: convicted in 2015 (illegal campaign financing, 2.5 years) and 2021 (InterAgro corruption case, 5 years); acquitted in another case in 2024 per Romanian Wikipedia. Wealth has likely fallen well below $1bn. Poor fit for outreach; no published contacts found.

name: Joyce Raley Teel
profile: Died 25 February 2022 at 91. She was the daughter of Raley's founder Thomas Raley and co-chaired the Sacramento-area Raley's supermarket chain with her husband Jim Teel for 24 years. Her son Michael Teel later ran the company as owner and chairman.
notes: Deceased (Feb 2022), per Progressive Grocer, ABC10 and KFBK: https://progressivegrocer.com/raleys-2nd-generation-owner-passes-away-91 and https://kfbk.iheart.com/content/2022-03-01-friends-and-family-mourn-passing-of-joyce-raley-teel. Skip.

name: Silvio Scaglia
current_role: Founder, SHS A.M. (quant asset manager, 2020); owner of Freedom Holding / Pacific Global Management (Elite World Group parent)
profile: Swiss-born Italian engineer and telecom entrepreneur who launched Omnitel (Italy's second mobile operator) as CEO in 1995, then founded e.Biscom/Fastweb in 1999, the world's first all-IP fibre-to-the-home operator, selling his 18.7% stake to Swisscom in 2007. He later bought Elite World modelling agencies (2011) and La Perla (2013), and in 2020 founded AI-driven asset manager SHS.
interesting_fact: Fastweb was the first company in the world to build a fully IP-based network and the first public consumer fibre-optic network; e.Biscom's 2000 IPO was the second most successful in Italian history, and Time named him among 2003's 'tech survivors'.
deep_cut_fact: Fresh out of Turin Polytechnic (electronic engineering, cum laude, 1983) his first job was at Aeritalia Spazio, where he worked on the Tethered Satellite project with NASA and Martin Marietta, before stints at Andersen Consulting, McKinsey and Piaggio.
notes: His 'Freedom Holding' (ex-Pacific Global Management) is unrelated to Nasdaq-listed Freedom Holding Corp (Timur Turlov). Ongoing high-profile litigation with ex-wife Julia Haart over Elite World since 2022; avoid. Acquitted in the Fastweb/Telecom Italia Sparkle case (2013, upheld 2017). No published contact found.

name: Mian Mohammad Mansha
current_role: Chairman, MCB Bank Ltd; head of the Nishat Group (Pakistan)
profile: Born in Chiniot, Punjab, and educated at Hendon College in London, Mansha built his family's cotton-ginning business into the Nishat Group. It spans Nishat Mills (textiles), MCB Bank (acquired in 1992 privatisation), cement, insurance, hotels and power generation. In 2010 Forbes listed him as Pakistan's first billionaire.
interesting_fact: Forbes listed him in 2010 as the first Pakistani on its billionaires list. His group also bought two power plants in the late 2000s, adding an energy angle to its textile and banking base.
deep_cut_fact: He went to school at Sacred Heart Convent in Faisalabad before studying at Hendon College, London. In 1979 he built the textile complex at Nishatabad near Faisalabad that became the group's industrial base.
notes: Received the Sitara-e-Imtiaz in 2004 and has sat on the Atlantic Council board. The MCB and Nishat websites blocked automated access, so I could not pull a published IR/press email. MCB's investor-relations page and annual report should list one. The web-search budget ran out before this profile.

name: Douglas Fregin
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Quantum Valley Investments (Waterloo, Ontario)
profile: Electrical engineer (University of Windsor) who co-founded Research In Motion (BlackBerry) in 1984 with his grade-school friend Mike Lazaridis, designing early circuit boards and serving as VP of operations until retiring in 2007. In 2013 the pair launched Quantum Valley Investments with $100m of their own money to commercialise quantum information science; he was an early $10m donor to the Perimeter Institute.
interesting_fact: RIM's first product, the 'Budgie', was shown by Fregin and Lazaridis at Fairview Park Mall in Kitchener in 1984; the start-up was helped by a $15,000 Ontario New Ventures loan in 1985.
deep_cut_fact: Long before BlackBerry, he shared a 1994 Technology & Engineering Emmy (with Eastman Kodak and the National Film Board of Canada) for developing a keycode reader; RIM's DigiSync film reader also earned an Academy technical achievement award.
notes: Known as 'the other RIM guy' (Canadian Business, 2005) - keeps a much lower profile than Lazaridis. Best route: Quantum Valley Investments contact form. Quantum/computing angle fits a data-center podcast.

name: Patrick Bowlen
profile: Longtime owner of the NFL's Denver Broncos (from 1984), winning three Super Bowls. Died June 13, 2019, aged 75; team later sold to the Walton-Penner group in 2022.
notes: Deceased 13 June 2019 per PBS NewsHour https://www.pbs.org/newshour/nation/denver-broncos-owner-pat-bowlen-dies-at-age-75

name: Shahid Balwa
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Valor Estate Ltd (formerly D B Realty), Mumbai; re-appointed for 3 years from Dec 2024
profile: Shahid Usman Balwa co-founded Mumbai developer D B Realty (DB Group) with Vinod Goenka. It listed in 2010, when Forbes counted him a billionaire, and was later renamed Valor Estate. He remains Vice Chairman & MD, and in 2025 the hospitality business (Goa hotel, Delhi Aerocity project) was demerged.
interesting_fact: In November 2025 CREDAI-MCHI, Mumbai's main developer body, named him convener of a new task force to smooth developers' dealings with the BMC on building approvals, FSI clearances and DCPR premium payments.
notes: Sensitive history: he was a defendant in the 2G spectrum case and was acquitted in 2017; don't raise it. The Forbes listing is from 2010 only, and his current net worth is likely lower. I found no sourced, positive deep-cut fact. Valor Estate IR is the route.

name: William Belo
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Wilcon Depot Inc. (PSE: WLCON), Philippines (re-elected officer June 2026)
profile: William T. Belo founded Wilcon in 1977 and built it into the Philippines' largest home-improvement and construction-supply retailer, with roughly 100 Wilcon Depot stores; it listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in 2017. He has handed day-to-day leadership to his daughter Lorraine Belo-Cincochan and remains chairman emeritus and on the advisory board.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited with helping millions of Filipinos build their homes; Tatler named him among 'Asia's Most Influential' (Philippines) in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Outside hardware retail he raises crocodiles: he owns two crocodile farms that sell skins to LVMH.
notes: Private, rarely interviewed; company IR (VP Investor Relations Mary Jean G. Alger per June 2026 filing) is the published route.

name: Richard Farmer
profile: Richard T. Farmer (Nov 22, 1934 - Aug 4, 2021), founder and long-time CEO/chairman of uniform company Cintas, died in 2021 aged 86.
notes: Deceased (August 2021) per Wikipedia; skipped further research. Legacy: Farmer School of Business at Miami University (Ohio).

name: Jiayin Xu
current_role: None - former chairman and founder of China Evergrande Group; serving a life sentence in China (sentenced Aug 2026)
profile: Xu Jiayin (Hui Ka Yan) founded Evergrande in Guangzhou in 1996 and built it into one of China's largest property developers; he was once Asia's richest person. After Evergrande's 2021 debt crisis and liquidation, he was detained in 2023, pleaded guilty in April 2026 to fraud, illegal deposit-taking and bribery, and was sentenced to life with all personal property confiscated.
notes: NOT a viable outreach target: imprisoned for life (Shenzhen court, 20 Aug 2026) and assets confiscated; no longer a billionaire. Rich-list entry is stale. Sources: https://www.wwno.org/npr-news/2026-08-20/chinese-court-sentences-founder-of-property-developer-evergrande-to-life-in-prison

name: Bruce Gordon
current_role: Owner of WIN Corporation (WIN Television) and Birketu Pty Ltd; retired from boards in Aug 2024 but remains Birketu's ultimate decision-maker
profile: Sydney-born (1929) media owner who went from vaudeville magician and theatre manager to 30 years as a Paramount Television programming/sales executive, then bought Wollongong's WIN TV from Rupert Murdoch in 1979 and built it into Australia's largest regional TV network. Through Birketu he is a major Nine Entertainment shareholder; WIN co-owns the St George Illawarra Dragons.
interesting_fact: He is one of nine living Australians to have appeared on every AFR Rich List since it began in 1984, and was made an Officer of the Order of Australia (AO) in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he juggled fruit to draw customers to his father's street-side fruit stall in Surry Hills, and he kept honing his magic act into his 20s, debuting on Sydney's Tivoli theatre circuit, where he got to know Rupert Murdoch and the Packers.
notes: Aged 97 and retired from boards; famously private. WIN TV contact page is regional/station-level, not personal. Low likelihood of participation.

name: Robert Galvin
profile: Robert W. Galvin, longtime CEO and chairman of Motorola (son of founder Paul Galvin), died on 11 October 2011 aged 89.
notes: Deceased 11 Oct 2011 in Chicago, aged 89. Source: https://phys.org/news/2011-10-longtime-motorola-ceo-robert-galvin.html ; https://news.nd.edu/news/in-memoriam-robert-w-galvin-former-notre-dame-fellow-and-trustee

name: Rosa Brescia Cafferata
current_role: Director of Grupo Breca entities (e.g. Minsur, Breca Banca); President of CPAL (Peruvian Center for Hearing, Language and Learning)
profile: Peruvian heiress (born c. 1926), daughter of Italian-born Fortunato Brescia Tassano and María Catalina Cafferata, whose surnames gave Grupo Breca its name. Breca spans mining (Minsur), banking, fishing (TASA), cement, real estate and more; she and her children hold about 30% of it. Her son Alex Fort Brescia co-chairs the group.
interesting_fact: The conglomerate's name 'Breca' is formed from her parents' surnames, BREscia and CAfferata.
notes: Would be about 100 years old; no death report found but not confirmed alive. Extremely private. Realistic podcast contact is the group's co-chairmen (Alex Fort Brescia, Pedro Brescia Moreyra) via Breca corporate communications; Minsur (tin/mining) gives an energy-transition angle.

name: Alexander Putilov
current_role: Co-owner, Eurasia Drilling Company (EDC), Russia's largest onshore/Caspian drilling contractor
profile: Alexander Putilov (b. 1952, Tyumen) is a Russian oil veteran who ran Urayneftegaz, then served as president of state oil company Rosneft (1993-1998) and later as BP/Amoco's special representative to Sidanko. In 2004 he became co-owner of the drilling company founded by Alexander Djaparidze (ex-LUKOIL Burenie), now Eurasia Drilling, which drills in Russia, the Caspian Sea and Iraq.
interesting_fact: He was appointed president of Rosneft in April 1993, the first years of the then state-owned oil company's post-Soviet existence, and led it until 1998.
deep_cut_fact: A former mechanic: after graduating from the Tyumen Industrial Institute in 1974 he started out as a fitter/repairman in the oil fields, then rose to deputy head of a plant shop and chief mechanic.
notes: Forbes lists him as a Russian citizen living in Moscow, age 74. Wikipedia (single-source stub) calls him Czech. His exact current EDC stake is unclear (reportedly 25-28% at various points). EDC's site eurasiadrilling.com was unreachable from here. No personal public channels. Given Russia sanctions and compliance issues, check before any outreach.

name: Benny Subianto
current_role: Deceased (died 4 January 2017); formerly Commissioner, PT Adaro Energy and founder of PT Persada Capital Investama
profile: Benny Subianto (Soebianto), an ITB-trained mechanical engineer, helped found United Tractors (Astra group), served as its president director, founded Persada Capital Investama in 2003 and was a co-owner and commissioner of coal miner Adaro Energy. He died in January 2017; his daughter Arini Subianto now leads the Persada group.
notes: Died January 2017 - Adaro announced his death (source: https://www.petromindo.com/news/article/adaro-commissioner-passes-away). Rest skipped per instructions. Family interests continue via daughter Arini Subianto (Persada Capital Investama; Adaro/AlamTri commissioner) if the journalist wants a successor contact.

name: Mehmet Sepil
current_role: Founder and former president of Genel Energy (retired Oct 2015); private investor and former Göztepe SK chairman/owner
profile: Turkish entrepreneur who moved from construction into oil, founding Genel in 2002 and signing the first production-sharing agreement in Iraqi Kurdistan (Taq Taq). He was CEO until Genel merged with Tony Hayward's London-listed Vallares in 2011, then president until retiring in 2015. He later owned İzmir football club Göztepe, selling a 70% stake to Sport Republic in 2022.
interesting_fact: The 2011 Genel-Vallares deal paired his Kurdistan assets with former BP CEO Tony Hayward's cash shell; Sepil called it 'a marriage between the asset and the money', and Hayward insisted on keeping the Turkish name Genel.
deep_cut_fact: He was already working in Iraqi Kurdistan with his own construction company in 2002 when Jalal Talabani, later Iraq's president, suggested he try the oil business, which led to the Taq Taq field.
notes: Appeared only on Forbes 2011; wealth largely from Genel shares (major insider sales ~2015). No longer an executive; low-profile. I found no published personal or office contact; Genel Energy's corporate site (genelenergy.com) could pass on a message. Also chaired Turkey's Club Association (Kulüpler Birliği) c. 2019.

name: Leslie Lampton
notes: Leslie B. Lampton Sr., founder of Ergon Inc. (Jackson/Flowood, Mississippi; began as Lampton Oil Company in 1954), died 17 April 2018 as Ergon's Chairman Emeritus. Source: https://ergon.com/updates/company-announcement-death-of-ergon-founder . Ergon remains Lampton-family owned; a successor-generation family member would be the relevant contact.

name: Jiang Yu
current_role: Co-owner (with father Jiang Yehua) of Chongqing Huayu Group (重庆华宇集团), real estate; no public executive title found
profile: Jiang Yu (蒋宇, b. ~1988) is the son of Jiang Yehua (蒋业华), founder of Chongqing Huayu Group, a property developer founded in the mid-1990s that has built 285+ projects in about 30 Chinese cities. Hurun lists father and son together as the Huayu family fortune. Jiang Yu keeps a very low public profile.
interesting_fact: Huayu went national from 2017 and, while most private developers retrenched in the property downturn, it hired outside executives and took over stalled Evergrande/Sunac projects; it then had three RMB10bn+ regional markets (Chongqing, Zhejiang, Jiangsu).
notes: IMPORTANT: the input's SEC match (Nano Nuclear Energy chairman 'Jay Jiang Yu') is a DIFFERENT person: 45 years old and New York-based per NNE's 2026 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1923891/000149315226034874/formdef14a.htm). Hurun's Jiang Yu was born 1988 and is listed with father Jiang Yehua (父子) under 华宇 / Huayu, Chongqing. No contacts found.

name: Apichet Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Assistant COO and Acting Chief Resource Management Officer, King Power Group (per The Nation, Dec 2025); Vice-Chairman, Leicester City FC
profile: Apichet Srivaddhanaprabha is a son of the late Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha, who built Thailand's King Power airport duty-free empire, and shares in the family fortune. He holds senior management roles at King Power and has sat on the board of Leicester City FC since the 2010s, becoming vice-chairman when his brother Aiyawatt ('Top') took over as chairman.
interesting_fact: In December 2025 he and his brother Aiyawatt played together on the Thai national polo team that won SEA Games gold, beating Brunei 7.5-0 in the 2-4 goal final.
deep_cut_fact: The Dec 2025 final, played at VS Sports Club & Siam Polo Park in Samut Prakan, gave Thailand its first-ever SEA Games polo gold; the sport only entered the Games in 2007 (Thai bronze) thanks to the Thailand Polo Association his father set up, and the brothers dedicated the win to him.
notes: Not the same person as brother Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha (King Power CEO, Leicester chairman), who is the family's public face. Apichet is private; no personal social accounts found. kingpower.com contact is a general/customer-service address; Leicester City club contact page is an alternative. Energy/data-centre link is weak.

name: Aroonroong Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Executive at King Power Group (Thailand); listed in 2019 company materials as assistant to the CFO - current title unverified
profile: Daughter of the late King Power founder Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha and part of the family that controls King Power, Thailand's dominant duty-free retailer, and Leicester City FC. She sits on the group's executive team alongside siblings Apichet and Voramas; her brother Aiyawatt is chairman and CEO. Hurun listed her as a billionaire 2019-2021.
interesting_fact: The family's King Power owns Leicester City, the 5000-1 outsiders who won the 2015-16 Premier League; she and her sister were reported to each hold about 5% of Asia Aviation, parent of Thai AirAsia.
notes: Low public profile; wealth is shared family wealth and King Power is retail, so the energy fit is weak. No published personal contacts; route would be King Power corporate communications. Avoid referencing her father's 2018 helicopter death.

name: Voramas Srivaddhanaprabha
current_role: Senior executive (reported as Group Vice Chairman / Chief Marketing Officer) at King Power International, Thailand
profile: Voramas Srivaddhanaprabha is the eldest daughter of the late King Power founder Vichai Srivaddhanaprabha and sister of chairman/CEO Aiyawatt. The family's wealth comes from King Power, Thailand's dominant airport duty-free retailer, plus holdings including Leicester City FC and OH Leuven. She sits on King Power's executive team overseeing commercial and marketing functions.
interesting_fact: She is reported as a minority shareholder of English football club Leicester City (about 10%), the club her father bought in 2010 and which won the 2015-16 Premier League as 5000-1 outsiders.
notes: Very private; no interviews or personal channels found. Exact current title varies across aggregator profiles. Retail (duty-free) wealth, not energy: weak fit for the podcast's energy focus. Route via King Power corporate contact.

name: Zeki Zorlu
current_role: Honorary Chair (board of management), Zorlu Holding; chairs various group textile, energy and property companies
profile: Born 1939 in Babadağ, Denizli, Zeki Zorlu co-founded Turkish conglomerate Zorlu Holding with his younger brother Ahmet Nazif Zorlu, growing a family weaving trade into a group spanning textiles, Vestel electronics, Zorlu Energy (geothermal, wind, hydro, gas) and property such as Zorlu Center. He founded Korteks in Bursa in 1976, the group's first manufacturing company.
interesting_fact: He and his brother were 'masterful weavers' by primary-school age, working the family's household loom in Babadağ that their parents ran day and night; their father's Yükselen company (1953) is the root of today's Zorlu Holding.
deep_cut_fact: Before manufacturing, he took the family weaving trade into commerce by running the first Zorlu store, opened in Trabzon on the Black Sea; HQ moved to Istanbul in 1970 and he launched Korteks yarn in Bursa in 1976.
notes: Aged ~87 and largely retired from day-to-day roles. His brother and co-founder Ahmet Nazif Zorlu reportedly died on 2 Nov 2026 - be sensitive with timing of outreach. Next generation (e.g. Olgun Zorlu) more active publicly. Energy angle: Zorlu Enerji is a major Turkish geothermal/renewables producer.

name: Alicia Fentener Van Vlissingen
current_role: Heir / family shareholder in SHV Holdings (Fentener van Vlissingen family); no public executive role found
profile: Member of the Dutch Fentener van Vlissingen family that owns SHV Holdings, one of the world's largest private trading groups (energy distribution/LPG, industrial services). Reported as a daughter of former SHV chairman and conservationist Paul Fentener van Vlissingen (d. 2006); Hurun listed her at ~$1B (2014-2020). No public biography, business role or interviews found.
interesting_fact: Her family's Letterewe estate on Loch Maree in north-west Scotland, bought in 1978, was the subject of the 1990s 'Letterewe Accord', a pioneering public-access agreement that predated Scotland's 2003 land reform.
notes: Extremely private heiress; only a passing Wikipedia mention (uncited) links her as Paul Fentener van Vlissingen's daughter. Not an operator - no podcast angle beyond SHV's energy business. Better SHV-family interlocutor would be Annemiek Fentener van Vlissingen (SHV supervisory board chair). Identity marked uncertain due to thin sourcing.

name: Lyu Yongxiang
profile: Hurun (2015-2020) lists 吕永祥 with wealth from 'Yongda' (manufacturing). The only matching public figure found is Lu Yongxiang, founder and former chairman of Jilin Yongda Group (electric meters/circuit breakers; SZSE 002622), who sold his 23.81% stake in 2015-16; the company was renamed Rongyu Group.
notes: Identity not confirmed: Jilin Yongda's size seems too small for a $1bn fortune, so Hurun's 'Yongda' may be a different firm. No current role or contact found.

name: Mahdi Al-Tajir
current_role: Owner, Highland Spring Group (Scottish bottled water); private investor in finance and property
profile: Mohammed Mahdi Al Tajir, born in Bahrain around 1932-33 and educated at Preston Grammar School, was a key adviser to Dubai's ruler and the first UAE ambassador to the UK (1971-1987). He made his fortune in Dubai's development era, and owns Highland Spring, the Blackford and Keir estates in Scotland, London's Sheraton Park Tower hotel and Mereworth Castle in Kent.
interesting_fact: He was the UAE's first ambassador to the UK, serving 16 years from the federation's founding in 1971, and was a thinly disguised character in Robin Moore's 1976 novel 'Dubai'.
deep_cut_fact: A serious silver collector, he paid a then-record auction price for silver in 1993: GBP2.27m at Christie's Monaco for a 1736 silver chandelier by Balthasar Friedrich Behrens.
notes: Now about 93; very private and avoids media. Still on Hurun Global 2026, but no confirmation he is alive. Wikipedia also covers old Dubai Aluminium court cases; avoid those. Highland Spring press office is the only published route. Unlikely guest.

name: Mahmud Kamani
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chair, Debenhams Group plc (formerly boohoo group)
profile: Manchester entrepreneur who co-founded online fashion retailer boohoo with Carol Kane in 2006 and floated it in 2014. The group grew to include PrettyLittleThing, Nasty Gal, Debenhams, Dorothy Perkins and Burton, and is now renamed Debenhams Group. In February 2026 he became executive vice chair and invested £8M in a £40M raise.
interesting_fact: His father Abdullah, a Gujarati-heritage Kenyan who moved to north-west England in the 1960s, started out selling handbags on a market stall. He then built a textile business supplying New Look and Primark, which became the springboard for boohoo.
deep_cut_fact: He supports Kibera Kids, a Nairobi-based non-profit, a link back to his family's years in Kenya. He was Entrepreneur of the Year at the 2013 English Asian Business Awards.
notes: The group is in a turnaround and there is ongoing shareholder pressure from Frasers Group, so outreach is best kept to his entrepreneurial story. Go through the in-house press office or its agencies (Threesixty, Sodali). Little energy/data-center relevance.

name: Manoj Menda
current_role: Co-founder and Chair, Supervisory Board, RMZ (Bengaluru)
profile: Co-founded RMZ Corp in 2002 with his father Arjun and brother Raj, after the brothers spent years learning real estate at K Raheja Corp. RMZ became one of India's largest private office-park owners, sold 12.8M sq ft of offices to Brookfield for $2B in 2020, and is now a real-estate, infrastructure and private-capital group that is expanding into data centres through RMZ Digital Infrastructure.
interesting_fact: In 2020 RMZ sold 18% of its office assets (12.8M sq ft plus the CoWrks co-working business) to a Brookfield fund for $2B; Menda called it the firm's 'most important milestone' and said it made RMZ debt-free.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding RMZ, he and brother Raj spent several years at the Raheja group, where their father Arjun Menda had been part of its South India business. In 2023 the brothers received the Sindhi Chamber of Commerce Bangalore's Excellence in Business Award.
notes: Strong fit for a data-centre podcast: RMZ has a Digital Infrastructure unit and has said it is diversifying into data centres (aug-2023 press release). He is also active in WEF, YPO and ULI. Best route is RMZ's Head of PR.

name: Nathaniel Charles Jacob Rothschild
profile: Jacob Rothschild, 4th Baron Rothschild, founder of RIT Capital Partners, died in London on 26 February 2024 aged 87.
notes: Deceased (26 Feb 2024; source ITV News). His title passed to his son Nathaniel, 5th Baron Rothschild. RIT Capital Partners continues as a listed investment trust.

name: Peter Harris
current_role: Founder of Bourne Leisure (Haven, Warner); his family trust owns Butlin's (bought back in 2022)
profile: British former accountant (b. 1934) who co-founded Bourne Leisure in 1964 with David Allen. It grew into the UK's largest holiday-park group (Haven, Butlin's, Warner Leisure Hotels). In 2021 he sold the majority to Blackstone in a deal valuing the business at about £3bn, keeping a minority stake. In 2022 the Harris Family Trust bought Butlin's back for about £300m.
interesting_fact: He and his partners built and sold the business twice: they floated Leisure Caravan Parks in 1972 and sold it to Rank for £20m in 1975, started again, then bought Rank's holiday arm, including Butlin's and Haven, for £700m in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: He found his way into holiday parks while working as an accountant, after auditing a caravan park; in 1964 he bought the Alberta caravan park in Whitstable, Kent. From 1977 he bought land at Tring, Hertfordshire, where racehorses were trained until 2004. He was inducted into the British Travel & Hospitality Hall of Fame in 2013.
notes: Aged about 92; Wikipedia lists no death, but recent status was not independently verified. Extremely private. Butlin's, owned by his family trust, is the most direct organisational route.

name: Raj Menda
current_role: Chair, Supervisory Board, RMZ Corp (Bengaluru)
profile: Raj Menda co-founded Bengaluru-based RMZ Corp with his family in the early 2000s and built it into one of India's largest developers and owners of Grade-A office parks, later selling large portfolios to Brookfield. Wholly family-owned, RMZ now spans real estate, infrastructure, private capital and RMZ Digital Infrastructure (data centres); Raj co-chairs its supervisory board with brother Manoj.
interesting_fact: He is a former chairman of YPO India and a past president of CREDAI (Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India).
deep_cut_fact: He was the first Indian to chair the jury of the Urban Land Institute's global Awards for Excellence.

public_contacts.value: akash.philip@rmz.com (Head of PR, RMZ - published media contact)

notes: Good data-center angle via RMZ Digital Infrastructure (MD Ryan D'Souza). Next-gen (Sidharth, Mihir Menda) now run day-to-day and give interviews; route via RMZ Head of PR.

name: Rishi Shah
current_role: None — former co-founder, chairman & CEO of Outcome Health (resigned 2018); sentenced in June 2024 to 7.5 years in prison for fraud
profile: Oak Brook, Illinois-born (1986) Northwestern dropout who co-founded ContextMedia (later Outcome Health) in 2006 to put health-education screens in doctors' waiting rooms; it hit a $5.6bn valuation in 2017. After a WSJ investigation he resigned, and in 2023 he was convicted of mail, wire and bank fraud and money laundering.
interesting_fact: Outcome Health's May 2017 round of 500m+ dollars led by Goldman Sachs, CapitalG and Pritzker Group valued it at $5.6bn, then the largest single round since Groupon's in 2011.

name: Robert Tsao Hsing-Cheng

notes: High reputational risk: convicted of fraud over Nikola statements (2022), pardoned 2025; SEC civil case dropped Sept 2025; past misconduct allegations (denied). Very media-active. The 2021-22 Hurun $1bn figure is stale. Route via SyberJet press.

It is now Australia's largest wholly family-owned red-meat processor, with five plants, 3,000+ staff and exports to 85+ countries. Day-to-day management has passed to the next generation.

current_role: Founder, Managing Director and CEO, IndiaMART InterMESH Ltd

name: Geoffrey Guy
current_role: Founder, The Guy Foundation Family Trust (quantum biology research charity, Dorset); former founder-chairman of GW Pharmaceuticals
profile: British physician-pharmacologist (b. 1954, Barts-trained) who co-founded GW Pharmaceuticals in 1998 and developed the first FDA-approved cannabis-derived medicine, Epidiolex (2018), plus Sativex for MS spasticity. Jazz Pharmaceuticals bought GW for US$7.2B in 2021, when he stepped down. He now funds and leads quantum-biology research in medicine through The Guy Foundation.

name: Stephen Fitzpatrick
current_role: Founder and majority shareholder of OVO Energy; founder and major shareholder of eVTOL maker Vertical Aerospace (NYSE: EVTL)

name: Vladimir Tenev
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Robinhood Markets; Executive Chairman, Harmonic (AI)
profile: Born in Varna, Bulgaria in 1987, Vlad Tenev moved to the US at five, studied math at Stanford and UCLA, and co-founded commission-free broker Robinhood with Baiju Bhatt in 2013; it IPO'd in 2021 and he became sole CEO in 2020. He is pushing Robinhood toward a 'financial superapp' with AI and crypto, and in 2023 co-founded Harmonic, a math-reasoning AI startup valued at $1.45B.
interesting_fact: His AI startup Harmonic builds 'Aristotle', which generates formally verified Lean proofs to curb AI hallucinations; it showed top-level performance at the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad.
deep_cut_fact: Before Robinhood he and Bhatt built high-frequency-trading software: first Celeris in New York (2010), abandoned within months for Chronos Research, which sold low-latency software to trading firms. He dropped a planned UCLA math PhD to do it, and later gave UCLA's 2019 math commencement keynote.
notes: Highly public and podcast-friendly (All-In Summit, TEDAI, TechCrunch Disrupt). Harmonic/AI and compute is a natural data-center hook. Avoid GameStop 2021 controversy as an opener.

name: Zhao Lin
current_role: Chairman, CEO and executive director, Nayuki Holdings (HKEX: 2150)
profile: Restaurant-industry veteran who co-founded premium tea-drinks chain Nayuki (Nai Xue de Cha) in Shenzhen in 2014 with his wife Peng Xin, whose online nickname 'Nai Xue' gave the brand its name. Nayuki listed in Hong Kong in 2021; he now chairs and runs the company as it shifts to smaller-format stores.
interesting_fact: The brand name comes from co-founder Peng Xin's online handle 'Nai Xue'; the couple registered the trademark in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2014 he and Peng Xin each put up 50,000 yuan to register Shenzhen Pindao Catering Management, Nayuki's original operating company, and pledged personal assets to borrow 8 million yuan for the first stores.
notes: Shares Hurun listing with wife Peng Xin. Route via Nayuki investor relations (IR site ir.naixue.com); no IR email verified.

name: Peng Xin
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director, Nayuki Holdings (HKEX: 2150), Shenzhen
profile: Peng Xin (彭心) co-founded premium tea-and-bakery chain Nayuki (奈雪的茶) in 2014 with her husband Zhao Lin, now chairman and CEO. Nayuki pioneered the high-end fresh-fruit tea plus European-style bread format in Chinese malls and listed in Hong Kong in 2021 as the first 'new-style tea' stock. Her Hurun ranking (2021-22) reflected the IPO; the shares have since fallen sharply.

deep_cut_fact: The brand name 'Nayuki' (奈雪) came from an online handle Peng Xin used.
notes: Executive director per Nayuki's board list (with Zhao Lin as chairman/CEO). Likely no longer a billionaire given Nayuki's share-price decline. Route via Nayuki IR.

name: Zhu Fuyun
current_role: Founder, Chairwoman and controlling shareholder (~34.6%), Yijiahe Technology (亿嘉和, SSE: 603666), Nanjing
profile: Zhu Fuyun (朱付云) founded Nanjing-based Yijiahe in April 1999 and has run it ever since. The company moved into robotics in 2014 and became a leading maker of inspection and live-line maintenance robots for China's power grid (substations, tunnels, distribution networks). It listed in Shanghai in 2018 and has expanded into surgical, cleaning and embodied/humanoid robots.
interesting_fact: Yijiahe delivered the first batch of State Grid outdoor intelligent inspection robots in 2014. In 2024 it completed what it calls the first use of embodied humanoid robots in high-risk energy scenarios.
deep_cut_fact: Yijiahe existed for 15 years before building robots: Zhu founded it in 1999, and it only entered robotics in 2014, when its first outdoor inspection robot won a product-testing prize at the China Electric Power Research Institute (CEPRI).

Low English-language profile. info@yijiahe.com is the board secretary/IR address in the 2025 annual report, and a new board secretary, Lin Feng, was appointed in Aug 2026.

The firm grew into one of Europe's largest hedge funds; he also co-founded and later chaired the charity Ark (Absolute Return for Kids).

name: Paul Marshall
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Marshall Wace; owner of The Spectator and UnHerd, co-owner of GB News

He has become a major UK media owner (UnHerd, GB News, The Spectator from 2024) and philanthropist, topping the 2024 Sunday Times Giving List.

name: Fred Mannix
current_role: Chairman/owner, The Mancal Group (Mancal Corporation), Calgary

After the family businesses were split with brother Ron (Coril Holdings), he built the private Mancal Group, active in oil and gas (Mancal Energy), coal, real estate, private capital and ranching; Steve Letwin is CEO.

He also completed National Defence College Course 32 as a civilian in 1979.
notes: Input lists 'Fred and Ron Mannix' jointly; this profile is Fred P. Mannix (Mancal). Brother Ron runs separate Coril Holdings. Very private family. Strong interest in military history, defence/foreign affairs (founder of Canadian Defence and Foreign Affairs Institute) and journalism, a good hook for a journalist. Not to be confused with son Fred Mannix Jr., the polo player.

name: Massimo Moratti
current_role: Former CEO of Saras (sold to Vitol in 2024) and former president/owner of FC Internazionale; private investor

He owned and presided over Inter Milan (1995-2013), winning the 2010 treble. The family sold its remaining 35% of Saras to Vitol in 2024, and he still gives interviews on Inter and Milan life.

interesting_fact: He was an early backer and board member of Indonesian super-app Gojek, and has served as an independent director of Toshiba.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the board of the Singapore American School Foundation, has served on the National University of Singapore's investment committee, and has been active with literacy charity Room to Read.
notes: Energy angle: as a Farallon partner he led the Aston Resources coal investment (Whitehaven Coal). No published press contact found for Tiga Investments; Grindr IR is the closest corporate route but he is not an executive there.

name: Farukbhai Gulambhai Patel
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, KP Group (KPI Green Energy, KP Energy, KP Green Engineering), Surat, Gujarat
profile: Dr. Faruk G. Patel founded KP Group in Surat in 1994 as a small logistics and construction venture and built it into a renewables conglomerate (solar, wind, hybrid, BESS, green hydrogen) with a 10.6+ GW portfolio. Listed arms include KPI Green Energy and KP Energy; his 'KP 3.0' plan targets 10 GW owned capacity, 10 GW EPC and 10 GWh storage.

notes: Very media-friendly: personal website, published biography book ('Urja No Ujaas'), Josh Talks and IIM Ahmedabad lectures. Best route: contact form on farukpatel.com or KP Group media (kpgroup.co/media-kit). Strong energy/storage fit.

name: Jonathan Grimm
current_role: Co-founder of Toast, Inc. (restaurant software, NYSE: TOST); former CTO of Toast and CTO of its philanthropic arm Toast.org
profile: MIT computer-science graduate and ex-Endeca engineer who co-founded Boston-based Toast with Aman Narang and Steve Fredette in 2011-12, serving as CTO as it grew into a leading cloud POS and payments platform for restaurants (IPO 2021). He remains a significant Class B shareholder and moved to Toast.org, the company's giving arm, in 2022.

deep_cut_fact: After stepping back from the CTO role he became CTO of Toast.org, which partners with No Kid Hungry, World Central Kitchen and the Restaurant Workers' Community Foundation and gave $1.25m in grants in 2022.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed. Current exact role at Toast unclear in 2026 (still an insider/Class B holder). Net worth estimates vary widely ($90m–$350m+ in public holdings); Hurun $1bn may be generous.

name: Mira Murati
current_role: Founder and CEO, Thinking Machines Lab
profile: Albanian-born engineer (Colby BA, Dartmouth BEng) who worked on Tesla's Model X and at Leap Motion before joining OpenAI in 2018, rising to CTO and briefly interim CEO in Nov 2023. Left in 2024 and launched Thinking Machines Lab in Feb 2025 with a record ~$2B seed round; its first product, Tinker, lets users fine-tune frontier models.
interesting_fact: Thinking Machines Lab's governance gives Murati a weighted, deciding board vote, an unusual degree of founder control for a lab that raised one of the largest seed rounds in history.
deep_cut_fact: Under her full name, Ermira Murati, she wrote 'Language & Coding Creativity' for the Spring 2022 issue of Daedalus (American Academy of Arts & Sciences), on how NLP engines like GPT-3 change how humans relate to machines.
notes: High-profile and media-selective. No published press email found for Thinking Machines; company X/LinkedIn are the official channels. Born in Vlore, Albania; Albania's government invested $10M in her lab.

name: Pradeep Garg
current_role: Chairman, Kundan Group (gold refining, bullion, minting, mining, Kundan Green Energy), India
profile: Dr. Pradeep Garg chairs the Kundan Group, which grew from a single enterprise founded in 1971 into a diversified group running what it calls India's largest private gold refinery, bullion trading, minting and mining. Its Kundan Green Energy arm has about 350 MW of commissioned hydro, solar and waste-to-energy capacity; Udit and Vidit Garg also sit on the board.

name: Shahril
current_role: Tan Sri Shahril Shamsuddin, key figure of the family-controlled Sapura Group (Malaysia); retired as President & Group CEO of Sapura Energy in March 2021
profile: Shahril Shamsuddin built Sapura Energy (formerly SapuraKencana, now renamed Vantris Energy) into one of Malaysia's largest offshore oil-and-gas service and drilling groups, and led the wider family conglomerate Sapura Group (energy, engineering, aviation, defence, property). He retired as Sapura Energy's group CEO in March 2021, handing over to Anuar Taib.
interesting_fact: Sapura was founded in 1975 by his father Abdul Kadir Shamsuddin with six staff in a one-room office (starting with telecoms firm Uniphone Works) and was named after Abdul Kadir's wife, Siti Sapura.

Avoid Sapura Energy's 2022-24 debt restructuring as a topic. No current published contact found (sapura.com.my pages returned 404). Alive: no report of death found, but not positively confirmed.

name: Peter Smedvig
current_role: Third-generation owner of the Smedvig family business (Smedvig Family Office, Stavanger/London); co-founder of Smedvig Capital (no longer on its listed team)
profile: Peter Thomas Smedvig (b. 1946, Stavanger) is the grandson of Peder Smedvig, who founded the family shipping business in 1915. He took Smedvig ASA into offshore drilling (listed Oslo 1990, NYSE 1996), exited shipping (1996) and drilling (2006), and built the Smedvig Family Office (~US$2.4bn AUM), now owned by the 4th generation.
interesting_fact: In 1996, the same year the family exited shipping, he and Johnny Hewett founded Smedvig Capital in London - one of the early family-office private-equity/venture arms; it still invests in founders via Smedvig Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in England before Wharton: a bachelor's from Newcastle University (1970) and an MBA from the Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania (1972).
notes: Now ~80 and appears retired from day-to-day roles; the family office says the 4th generation owns it, and the family's philanthropy runs through North Star (founded 2019). Best route is the Smedvig family office general inbox. 'Alive' based on Wikipedia/Wikidata listing him as living; no recent public appearances found.

name: Doron Kochavi
current_role: Lawyer, real-estate developer and Executive Director, Buchman Heyman Foundation (Tel Aviv)
profile: Tel Aviv-born (1951) lawyer from the Buchman business family who became one of the main developers of the Gush HaGadol area of north Tel Aviv, with 20+ buildings. He is a co-owner of the planned ~$1.5bn 'Beyond Towers' (with Tidhar) and the 'Hi Tower' residential tower on the Tel Aviv-Givatayim border.
interesting_fact: He co-founded the Tel Aviv-Los Angeles sister-city partnership in 1997 and has chaired its steering committee.
deep_cut_fact: His family's Buchman Heyman Foundation, set up by his grandmother in 1942, funds the Israel Philharmonic, Tel Aviv Museum of Art and Habima Theatre and gives annual grants to young artists and students.
notes: Billionaire status is doubtful: only source is Wikidata ($1bn); a Wikipedia mirror says ~$130m. Not to be confused with tech billionaire Mati Kochavi. No published contact found.

name: José Fanjul
current_role: Vice chairman and president, Flo-Sun / Florida Crystals (Fanjul Corp., parent of Domino Sugar and American Sugar Refining)
profile: José 'Pepe' Fanjul (born 1944, Havana) is the second of the Fanjul brothers, whose family left Cuba after 1959 and rebuilt a sugar business near Lake Okeechobee from 1960. Fanjul Corp. now spans Florida Crystals, Domino, C&H, Redpath, the former Tate & Lyle sugar businesses and a stake in Central Romana in the Dominican Republic. Educated at Villanova (BA) and NYU (MBA).
interesting_fact: Energy angle: from 1996 Flo-Sun ran a biomass cogeneration plant next to its Okeelanta sugar mill, burning cane fibre and wood waste to supply power via FPL. By 2006 it had grown into the largest biomass power plant in the US.
deep_cut_fact: He was longtime chairman of New Hope Charities, which serves rural western Palm Beach County; it honoured him at its 25th anniversary in 2013. He was inducted into the Florida Agricultural Hall of Fame in 2018.
notes: Highly political mega-donor, frequently criticised over sugar subsidies; very private. The Florida Crystals website blocks automated access, so no published press contact was confirmed. Corporate communications at Florida Crystals/ASR is the likely route. The biomass/renewable power operations are the best podcast angle.

name: Kenneth Gaw
current_role: Co-founder, President & Managing Principal, Gaw Capital Partners; Managing Director, Pioneer Global Group (Hong Kong)
profile: Hong Kong real-estate investor who co-founded Gaw Capital Partners with his siblings. The PE real-estate firm manages over US$33B across Asia and the US (hotels, offices, data centers). He also runs the family's listed Pioneer Global Group, founded by his late father Anthony Gaw, which he joined in 1994 after Goldman Sachs.
interesting_fact: He is a director of Thai hotel group Dusit Thani and was a director of China budget-hotel chain Home Inns. Capital Entrepreneur named him 'Outstanding Entrepreneur' in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Bangkok in 1970 and grew up in Hong Kong. He studied applied mathematics and economics at Brown University (1992) before starting at Goldman Sachs in New York.
notes: Good fit for the data-center theme: Gaw Capital has been an active investor in Asian data centers, though this was not verified in this pass. The Gaw Capital website blocked automated access, so no published press email was captured; check its contact page manually. The web search budget ran out before more could be done.

name: Joel Wiener
current_role: CEO, Pinnacle Group (New York City residential landlord)
profile: Brooklyn-born lawyer turned landlord (J.D., Brooklyn Law School, 1974). His family firm bought NYC buildings in the 1970s-80s; he began buying in the late 1980s, founded Wiener Realty in 1995 and built Pinnacle Group, which manages about 10,000 mostly rent-regulated apartments (around $2B of property) across four boroughs. Bloomberg put his net worth at $1B in 2017.
interesting_fact: Pinnacle's portfolio, financed largely by Praedium, includes a $500M purchase of about 3,000 apartments from Baruch Singer, making it one of NYC's largest rent-regulated landlords.
notes: Reputationally sensitive: Wikipedia documents many tenant lawsuits, AG/DA investigations, a 2006 $1M overcharge settlement and a 2022 AG admission. Low public profile, with no official personal channels found. Probably a poor fit for the podcast; source is Wikidata only.

name: Rob Sands
current_role: Director, Constellation Brands (NYSE: STZ); former CEO (2007-2019) and Executive/Non-Executive Chair (2019-2023)
profile: Robert Sands, second-generation leader of Constellation Brands (founded by his grandfather as a regional wine company), was CEO 2007-2019 and chair until 2023. With his brother Richard he turned it into an S&P 500 beverage-alcohol group (Corona, Modelo, Robert Mondavi) with $9bn+ revenue; he led the acquisition of the US rights to Grupo Modelo's Mexican beers and the build-out of its Mexican breweries. He remains a board director.
interesting_fact: As CEO he led the 2013 acquisition of the US business for Corona and Modelo and the build-out of Constellation's own Mexican brewing footprint, which made it the top US beer importer.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the business he was its lawyer: he served as Constellation's General Counsel from 1986 to 2000, overlapping with his rise to EVP and CEO of the international unit.
notes: Input had only a Wikidata ID (Q52004979); matches Robert Sands of Constellation Brands (director since 1990, age 67 in 2026 proxy). corpsecretary@ is the published route for contacting board members. Constellation is investing heavily in water/energy for its Mexican breweries, a possible energy angle.

name: Musa Halilu Ahmed
current_role: Chairman, TILT Group (Nigerian conglomerate: energy, construction, engineering, agriculture, technology)
profile: Nigerian businessman and former APC politician (b. 13 May 1976), also known as Musa Yola and by his traditional title, Dujima of Adamawa. He chairs TILT Group, a Nigeria-based conglomerate with interests in energy, construction, engineering, agriculture and technology, and holds board seats in real estate, supply-chain and venture companies.
interesting_fact: In March 2018 the Lamido of Adamawa conferred on him the title 'Dujima of Adamawa', an honour reserved for philanthropists noted for civic and charitable leadership. He also holds Nigeria's national honour OFR.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Gembu on the Mambila Plateau and schooled in Yola. He studied management at Kaduna Polytechnic (OND then HND, 2005) and added an ICT diploma from the National Institute of Technology during his NYSC service year.
notes: Only source of wealth on file is a Wikidata net-worth claim ($1bn), which is unverified and not on Forbes or Hurun lists. Wikipedia sourcing is mostly 2018 Nigerian press. No official TILT Group website or verified social accounts found. Exercise caution; his political history and Wikipedia categories hint at past controversies.

name: Clifford Illig
current_role: Principal owner, Sporting Kansas City (MLS); co-founder of Cerner Corp. (acquired by Oracle 2022)
profile: Kansas City native Cliff Illig co-founded health-IT company Cerner in 1979 with Arthur Andersen colleagues Neal Patterson and Paul Gorup, served as COO through 1998 and later vice chairman; Oracle bought Cerner for ~$28bn in 2022. Since 2006 he has led the ownership of Sporting KC, building Children's Mercy Park and a national soccer training centre; Forbes reported in Feb 2026 the family would sell a 71% stake to an existing partner.
interesting_fact: Illig, Patterson and a colleague conceived the idea for Cerner while studying for a CPA exam in a park; they took it public in 1986.
deep_cut_fact: When Lamar Hunt approached them about buying the Kansas City Wizards in 2006, Neal Patterson asked 'Are we going to do this?' and Illig replied, 'I don't think we have any choice.' He and Kathy Nelson were named the KC Chamber's 2025 Kansas Citians of the Year.
notes: Ownership change at Sporting KC reported Feb 2026 (Illig family selling majority; status of his title may change). Philanthropy spans entrepreneurship, life sciences and education in KC. Route via Sporting KC communications.

name: Khalid Abdul Rahman Saleh Al Rajhi
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Abdulrahman Saleh Al Rajhi & Partners Co.; Chairman, Saudi Cement Co.; board member, Bank Albilad
profile: Member of Saudi Arabia's Al Rajhi banking family who runs the family investment company Abdulrahman Saleh Al Rajhi & Partners (stocks, real estate and more). He holds ~8% of Islamic lender Bank Albilad (~$41bn assets), where he sits on the board, and ~6% of Saudi Cement Co., which he chairs.

notes: Profile based on Forbes bio; Saudi Cement and Bank Albilad websites were unreachable from this environment and web-search budget was exhausted, so roles not re-verified for 2026. Best route: Saudi Cement / Bank Albilad investor-relations channels.

name: Simon Xie

Before joining Jack Ma's founding team he earned an engineering degree from Shenyang University of Technology and did financial work at a state-run company. He appeared on Forbes billionaire lists 2015-2018.

name: Leyla Tara Suyabatmaz

profile: One of more than a dozen Tara family shareholders of ENKA, the Istanbul-listed construction and energy group cofounded in 1957 by Şarık Tara and Sadi Gülçelik. current_role: Shareholder, ENKA İnşaat ve Sanayi (per Forbes)
profile: Listed by Forbes as one of more than a dozen family members holding shares in ENKA, Turkey's leading private power producer and a major global contractor, founded in 1957 by Şarık Tara and his brother-in-law Sadi Gülçelik. No independent public information about her role or family branch was found.

name: Yaohai Wang
current_role: Chairman, Opple Lighting (欧普照明, SSE: 603515), Shanghai (per Forbes profile)
profile: Wang Yaohai co-founded Opple Lighting with his wife Ma Xiuhui in 1996 in Zhongshan, Guangdong, China's lighting-manufacturing hub. Opple grew into one of China's largest lighting brands, listed in Shanghai in 2016, and sells in 70+ countries through 150,000+ outlets, with factories in Wujiang and Zhongshan. Forbes now lists him as a former billionaire.

deep_cut_fact: Opple was the official lighting-solution provider for the China Pavilion at Expo 2020 Dubai and a strategic partner of the 2019 Beijing International Horticultural Expo.
notes: Wife Ma Xiuhui is also a co-founder/billionaire. Very low media profile. Current chairmanship and ownership not re-verified for 2025-26 (web search budget exhausted) - check Opple's latest SSE filings, which also publish the board-secretary IR email.

name: Robert Peugeot
current_role: Honorary Chairman, Peugeot Invest (since May 2025); Vice-Chairman and director, Stellantis
profile: A great-grandson of Robert I Peugeot, he spent around 25 years in operating roles at PSA Peugeot Citroën, including on its Executive Committee for innovation and quality (1998-2007). From 2002 he ran the family investment holding FFP/Peugeot Invest, which holds stakes in Stellantis, Forvia, Rothschild & Co and others. His son Édouard succeeded him as chairman in May 2025.

deep_cut_fact: Despite the family name, he started in 1974 as a worker and then team leader on the Sochaux assembly lines. As a Citroën methods engineer (1979-81) he helped robotise bodywork welding, and he later ran Peugeot-Talbot in Coventry, UK.

name: Amit Burman
current_role: Non-executive director, Dabur India (chairman until Aug 2022); investor in Lite Bite Foods
profile: Fifth-generation member of the Burman family that controls Dabur, the Ayurvedic and consumer-goods company founded in Kolkata in 1884. A Cambridge MBA, he led Dabur's move into processed foods and juices (Real) and was chairman until 2022; he now sits on the board and invests in private ventures such as restaurant operator Lite Bite Foods.

deep_cut_fact: He started at Dabur on the shop floor of its industrial engineering department, working on mechanization and packaging, before leading the company's foray into processed foods spanning cooking pastes to fruit juices.
notes: Best route is Dabur corporate communications or Lite Bite Foods. Deep-cut and interesting facts come from Forbes profile text supplied in the input.

name: Yifeng Zhou
current_role: Chairman/controlling shareholder, Hongda Xingye Group (鸿达兴业); former National People's Congress deputy
profile: Zhou Yifeng (周奕丰) built Guangzhou-based Hongda Xingye Group, whose interests include industrial chemicals (PVC/chlor-alkali), coal and PVC packaging. Its listed unit, Hongda Xingye (SZSE: 002002), was later flagged 'ST' and is now marked delisted on CNINFO. Forbes listed him in 2022 at about $1B.

name: Yi Feng (Feng Yi)
current_role: Director and Vice President (副总经理), Sangfor Technologies (SZ: 300454); one of three co-controlling founders
profile: Feng Yi (b. 1974) is one of the three ex-ZTE engineers (with He Chaoxi and Xiong Wu) who founded Shenzhen-based Sangfor Technologies in December 2000. Sangfor grew from VPN appliances into cybersecurity, hyper-converged infrastructure and cloud/data-center products, listing in Shenzhen in 2018; Feng has served as director and head of management engineering and is now director and VP.
interesting_fact: Sangfor is one of China's leading suppliers of hyper-converged infrastructure (HCI) used to build distributed cloud data centers, alongside its cybersecurity business.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the University of Science and Technology of China in 1998 with a double bachelor's in automatic control and economic management, and spent just two years doing R&D at ZTE before co-founding Sangfor in Dec 2000.
notes: Name order: Chinese name 冯毅 = Feng Yi (Forbes lists as 'Yi Feng'). Low public profile; data-center/HCI angle fits the podcast. Approach via Sangfor IR.

name: Wang Jinhua
current_role: Chairman, China Kings Resources Group (金石资源, SSE: 603505), Hangzhou
profile: Hangzhou-based founder-chairman (age ~63) of China Kings Resources, one of China's leading fluorite (fluorspar) miners and producers; fluorite is a key input for fluorochemicals including lithium-battery electrolyte salts and refrigerants. Self-made, Forbes lists him with a master's from China University of Mining and Technology and a bachelor's from University of Science and Technology Beijing.
interesting_fact: He is a mining-trained engineer by education (USTB bachelor's, CUMT master's) who built a business around fluorite mines, a mineral China treats as strategic.
notes: Forbes' bio text says 'Wang Junmin' but the profile is Wang Jinhua (王锦华), who is China Kings' chairman; likely a Forbes typo. Company website (chinakings.com) was unreachable during research and the web-search budget was exhausted, so no IR contact was verified; SSE filings for 603505 list the board secretary's contact. Energy angle: fluorite feeds battery-electrolyte (LiPF6) supply chains.

name: Gary Lauder
current_role: Managing Director, Lauder Partners LLC (Silicon Valley venture firm investing Lauder family capital)
profile: A grandson of Estée Lauder, Gary Lauder is not involved in the cosmetics company. He has been a venture capitalist since 1985, has backed more than 170 private companies through Lauder Partners, and is the largest investor in SoundThinking (formerly ShotSpotter). He is co-inventor of 17 patents and advocates publicly on patent policy and on transport decisions to ease traffic congestion.
interesting_fact: At TED2010 he proposed a new traffic sign, 'Take Turns', that is half stop sign and half yield sign. He released the design under a Creative Commons licence and says roundabouts are better where they are practical.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Laura co-created the Aspen Institute's Socrates Society, and he was in the inaugural class of Aspen's Henry Crown Fellowship. Before his own firm he worked in the 1980s at Aetna's venture arm, Jacobs & Ramo Technology Ventures and Wolfensohn Associates.

public_contacts.value: gary@lauderpartners.com. He publishes it as 'my first name @ this website's domain name' and says email is the best way to reach him, not social networks

notes: Very approachable: his site says he prefers email for cold contacts. Follow his published etiquette: send under your real name, use a descriptive subject line such as 'Introduction from [mutual friend]', and ping again after a week. He also lists a wireline office number on his site. Energy and infrastructure angles: patents, transportation and a heliostat patent (per Forbes).

name: Severin Hacker
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Duolingo (Nasdaq: DUOL), New York
profile: Swiss-born Severin Hacker (b. 1984) co-founded Duolingo in 2011 with Luis von Ahn, his Ph.D. advisor at Carnegie Mellon, and has been CTO since; Duolingo went public in 2021 and now teaches language, math and music to 100m+ monthly users. He also invests in startups via hacker.capital and runs the Severin Hacker Foundation.
interesting_fact: His CMU research on large-scale human computation earned him MIT Technology Review's TR35 honor in 2014; he taught himself to program around age 12 because he wanted to build his own video games.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Above Ground Coffee, a specialty coffee roaster, alongside his Duolingo role; growing up in a small town outside Zurich, his family was one of the few in the neighborhood with internet access.
notes: Best route: contact@severinhacker.com published on his own site. Childhood-internet detail is from C-Suite Quarterly (csq.com/?p=32479). Has appeared on podcasts (Swisspreneur ep. 252, Tim Ferriss), so receptive to podcast invites.

name: Ruth Parasol
current_role: Principal benefactor and trustee director, Parasol Foundation Trust (Gibraltar)
profile: Ruth Parasol (b. 1967, San Francisco), a lawyer by training, founded the business that became PartyGaming in 1997; after PartyPoker's launch it floated in London in 2005 at about $8.5bn and entered the FTSE 100. She sold her last shares in 2015 and, based mainly in Gibraltar, now focuses on philanthropy through the Parasol Foundation Trust.
interesting_fact: PartyGaming's 2005 float made it, per Wikipedia, the first female-founded and -led company admitted to the FTSE 100.
deep_cut_fact: Her Parasol Foundation funds a scholarship programme at Murray Edwards College, Cambridge, for talented female students to study astronomy, and gave $3.5m to create a women's breast cancer centre at Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center; the trust has given over £40m since 2004, focused on women in STEM and health.
notes: Private; best approach is via the Parasol Foundation (women in STEM / tech pioneer angle). Avoid PartyGaming legal history and earlier adult-industry businesses in outreach.

name: Anton Rabie
current_role: Co-Founder and Chair, Spin Master Corp. (TSX: TOY); co-founder and chairman, The Kale Fund
profile: Toronto entrepreneur who co-founded Spin Master in 1994 with childhood friends Ronnen Harary and Ben Varadi right after college, starting with $10,000 and the Chia-Pet-like 'Earth Buddy'. As co-CEO for 28 years he grew it into a ~$2B toy and entertainment company (PAW Patrol, Hatchimals, Bakugan, Rubik's, Toca Boca) with offices in 28+ countries; he now chairs the board and signed with VaynerSpeakers in June 2026.
interesting_fact: Rabie and Harary reportedly met at summer camp in Ontario aged 11; Spin Master bought the Rubik's Cube brand in 2021 for $50 million.
deep_cut_fact: He played a foundational role in more than 24 Spin Master acquisitions - including skateboard-toy brand Tech Deck, Cardinal Games, GUND plush and Rubik's Cube - and is co-founder and chairman of The Kale Fund.
notes: Very good podcast fit: actively on the speaking circuit (entrepreneurship, 'how great companies are built'). Route via VaynerSpeakers. Stepped back from co-CEO role; Christina Miller is now CEO.

name: Jose Llado Fernandez-Urrutia
profile: Founder (1960) of Spanish engineering contractor Técnicas Reunidas, former Spanish minister and ambassador to the US (1978-82). He died in February 2024 aged 89; his son Juan Lladó Arburúa leads the company.
notes: Deceased Feb 2024. Source: https://www.deia.eus/economia/2024/02/15/muere-empresario-exministro-jose-llado-7875619.html . For the podcast, Técnicas Reunidas (now CEO/Executive Chairman Juan Lladó) is active in power generation for data centers, a possible alternative guest.

public_contacts.value: cindy.cheng@appian.com (Sr. Director, Global Marketing Communications, listed as media contact)

name: Vlad Shmunis
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, RingCentral (NYSE: RNG); returned as CEO in Dec 2023 after a brief stint as executive chairman
profile: Russian-born founder who started RingCentral with Vlad Vendrow in 1999, bootstrapped with about $5,000, and built it into a UCaaS leader with $2B+ revenue (NYSE IPO 2013). name: Jiang Jinhua
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder of Flat Glass Group (601865.SH / 6865.HK), Jiaxing; long-time vice chair
profile: Jiang Jinhua (b. 1961) co-founded and co-controls Flat Glass Group with her husband, chairman Ruan Hongliang. It listed in Hong Kong in 2015 and in Shanghai in 2019. She holds an MBA from Arizona State University.

name: Daisuke Sasaki
current_role: Founder, Representative Director and CEO, freee K.K. (TSE: 4478), Tokyo
profile: Daisuke 'Dice' Sasaki (b. 1980, Tokyo) worked at Hakuhodo, CLSA Capital Partners, ALBERT (as CFO) and Google, where he led SMB marketing for Japan/APAC, before founding freee in 2012 with Ryu Yokoji. freee provides cloud accounting, HR and payroll software for Japanese small businesses under the mission 'Small business, as the main player of the world'.

He also wrote the book 'The way you use 3 months changes your life' (「3か月」の使い方で人生は変わる).

name: Ashok Boob

current_role: Founder, Russell AI Labs (AI/frontier-tech builder and investor, launched Oct 2025); founder and former CEO of Luminar Technologies

name: Lim Chai Hock
current_role: Director & Chief Operating Officer, PT Bayan Resources Tbk (Indonesia)
profile: Malaysian cofounder of the Bayan Group, one of Indonesia's largest coal producers, controlled by billionaire Low Tuck Kwong. name: Takanori Nakamura
current_role: Founder, Representative Director & President, RAKUS Co., Ltd. (TSE Prime: 3923), Tokyo

RAKUS grew into a leading Japanese SaaS company for SMB back-office work, best known for the Rakuraku Seisan expense-management cloud and email-marketing tools; Nakamura remains president and its largest shareholder.

name: Ray Irani
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Occidental Petroleum (1990-2011); reported as chairman/CEO of private investment firm Ray Investment, LLC

Irani Hall in 2007, and he was elected to the National Academy of Engineering in 2012 for work on particulate systems.

name: Kiki Barki
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, PT Harum Energy Tbk (IDX: HRUM); owner of private coal miner Tanito Harum
profile: Indonesian coal pioneer Kiki Barki (Ji Qihui) founded Tanito Harum in 1988 and Harum Energy in 1995, listing Harum in 2010. name: André Street

current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, FIRY Inc. (NYSE: FIRY; rebranded from Skillz Inc. in 2026)
