ASE, Nvidia and AMD; listed on TWSE in 2021, its shares surged with AI demand in 2026 and it is building a new plant in Renwu, Kaohsiung.
interesting_fact: WinWay started as a one-man company in Wang's Kaohsiung home with NT$2 million; it is now one of the world's top-five high-end logic IC test socket makers with ~1,200 staff, and its share price passed NT$10,000 in April 2026.
deep_cut_fact: A Chung Yuan University mechanical-engineering grad (not an EE), Wang says the test socket used when Motorola brought its first BGA-packaged chip to Fulgent was his invention. WinWay's break came in 2002 when ATI asked it to build 10 sockets in one week after a foreign supplier failed; he delivered on time.
notes: Romanized variously as Chia-Huang / Jiahuang Wang. The input's SEC insider link to Hilton Grand Vacations is a different Mark Wang (HGV CEO), not this person. Gives interviews to Taiwanese financial media (Mirror Media, Business Today, UDN).

name: Kenneth Tuchman
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, TTEC Holdings (Nasdaq: TTEC)
profile: California-born entrepreneur who founded TeleTech (now TTEC) in Los Angeles in 1982 and built it into a global customer-experience outsourcing firm; it moved to Denver in 1995 and IPO'd in 1996. He owns ~58% of TTEC; he proposed taking it private in 2024 but withdrew the bid in July 2025 citing market conditions.
interesting_fact: As a teenager he sold millions of puka shell necklaces to retailers, becoming one of the largest shell importers from the Philippines - where most of TTEC's international call centers are now located.
deep_cut_fact: TeleTech's breakthrough came after the 1984 AT&T breakup, when it was hired to monitor customer transitions - work that led to contracts with MCI and United Telecom (later Sprint). He and wife Debra co-founded the Tuchman Family Foundation in 1996, which runs 'Supplies For Success' school-supply drives.
notes: Take-private bid (2024) was withdrawn Aug 2025; TTEC remains public. Best route: TTEC media contact.

name: Sean Lie
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS)
profile: MIT-trained chip architect and one of Cerebras' five co-founders, who all came from SeaMicro (sold to AMD in 2012). As CTO since 2022 he leads the technology behind the Wafer-Scale Engine, a dinner-plate-sized AI chip, and Cerebras' inference cloud and data centers. Cerebras listed on Nasdaq in May 2026; his roughly 5.3M pre-IPO shares are the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: Cerebras' May 2026 IPO raised $5.55B at $185 a share, the largest U.S. tech IPO since 2019. The stock opened at $350, valuing the wafer-scale chipmaker at about $95B.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cerebras, Lie was a microprocessor architect on AMD's advanced architecture team (2004-08). At SeaMicro he was lead hardware architect of the IO-virtualization fabric ASIC that linked hundreds of tiny CPUs in its dense servers, and after AMD bought SeaMicro he was Chief Architect for Data Center Server Solutions.
notes: Core AI/data-center guest. He often gives technical talks (e.g. at Hot Chips) on the WSE architecture. The X and LinkedIn listed are Cerebras corporate accounts, not his. Media route is pr@cerebras.ai; the general inbox is info@cerebras.ai.

name: Fernando Trajano
current_role: Shareholder in Magazine Luiza (Magalu); no public executive role found
profile: Fernando Henrique Borges Trajano belongs to the family that controls Brazilian retailer Magazine Luiza (Magalu), founded in Franca (SP) in 1957. In 2018 his father, Onofre de Paula Trajano (the founder's brother), split his Magalu stake among Fernando and siblings Gisele and Ismael. Forbes Brasil 2026 puts the siblings' joint fortune at R$1.5bn.
interesting_fact: Magalu, often called 'the Amazon of Brazil', grew from a single gift shop in Franca into one of Brazil's largest retailers, and most of its sales now come through e-commerce.
notes: Very private passive heir; no interviews, social accounts or personal contacts found. The Forbes bio is partly wrong: Forbes Brasil says his father is Onofre de Paula Trajano (brother of founder Luiza Trajano Donato), not Luiza Helena Trajano. Age about 50 (Forbes Brasil 2026). Not an operating executive; Frederico Trajano is CEO.

name: Eduardo de Pontes
current_role: Founder & CEO, Teya (formerly SaltPay), London; cofounder and board member of StoneCo
profile: Rio de Janeiro-born serial payments entrepreneur who cofounded Brazil's StoneCo with Andre Street (Nasdaq IPO 2018, ~$1.5bn raised) and owns ~10% of it. Moved to Europe in 2018 and founded SaltPay (rebranded Teya in 2022), a London-based payments/software company for small merchants that bought Iceland's Borgun.
interesting_fact: Before Stone, he and Andre Street cofounded payments firm Braspag (sold to Grupo Silvio Santos), plus Netcredit, Blindado and price-comparison site Sieve, and set up Arpex Capital in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: At Stone's start he spotted Brazil's weak data networks and led building a card machine that used as little data as possible. His team-building advice: 'The first thirty people in the company must have the potential to be CEO' -- 'a team full of strikers concedes goals, a team full of goalkeepers never scores.'
notes: Described by peers as extremely averse to public appearances; rarely gives interviews. Lives in London. No published press email found for Teya (teya.com/press 404s); try Teya's corporate site/LinkedIn.

name: Zhang Desheng
current_role: Founder and chairman, Zhejiang Wanma Group (controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Wanma Co., SZSE: 002276)
profile: Zhang Desheng founded the Wanma group in Lin'an, Hangzhou, which makes power cables and polymer materials via Zhejiang Wanma (listed 2009) and also controlled Wanma Technology (SZSE: 300698) at its 2017 IPO. Before going into business in 1989 he was deputy head of a farm-machinery factory. Wanma has expanded into EV charging.
interesting_fact: Forbes added him to its billionaire ranks in 2015 on investor hopes for Wanma's electric-vehicle charging business, an energy angle relevant to the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his own business in 1989, Zhang was deputy head of a farm-machinery factory (per Forbes profile).
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Some sources say his daughter Zhang Bin chairs the group's tech arm, so check current chair in latest SZSE filings. Best route is via the company's board secretary/IR office. Do not confuse him with the Shaanxi politician of the same name.

name: Xia Shudong
current_role: Chairman & CEO and controlling shareholder, China TransInfo Technology (千方科技, SZ:002373)
profile: Xia Shudong (b. ~1972, Hubei) founded China TransInfo, a Shenzhen-listed provider of smart-transportation and intelligent-security systems for Chinese cities; Alibaba bought a 15% stake in 2019 for 3.6bn yuan. He still chairs the board and in 2025 launched TranXmart (千曙科技), an autonomous-freight trucking subsidiary.
interesting_fact: In 2025 TransInfo spun up TranXmart (千曙科技), an autonomous-driving freight unit whose stated goal is to build China's largest unmanned freight-capacity platform, using hub-to-hub routes tested in Sichuan/Chongqing and new-energy heavy trucks.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was an academic mapmaker: after studying at Chongqing University he earned a 2003 PhD in cartography & GIS at Peking University's Institute of Remote Sensing and GIS, and the company began as Beijing PKU ChinaFront (北大千方), a PKU-linked spin-out.
notes: Contact via TransInfo board-secretary office (securities@ctfo.com). Chongqing University detail per WEF profile (page blocks scraping; seen via search).

name: Huang Yimeng
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and CEO, XD Inc. (HKEX: 2400), Shanghai
profile: Huang Yimeng ('Dash' Huang) co-founded the P2P resource site VeryCD in 2003, then pivoted to games, chairing X.D. Network since 2011. XD (Hong Kong-listed since 2019) runs game development/publishing and TapTap, an ad-supported game download platform that bypasses Chinese app-store revenue cuts. He holds a large stake and still runs the company.
interesting_fact: XD's TapTap is ad-supported and free for players and publishers; Huang publicly argued (Bloomberg, 2021) that hardware makers' 50% app-store cuts should be viewed from an anti-monopoly standpoint, and his stake passed $1bn when XD shares jumped after the Huawei-Tencent app-store spat.
deep_cut_fact: XD's origin is VeryCD, a P2P resource-sharing website Huang founded with Kros Dai (Dai Yunjie, now XD President) in 2003; the same duo still lead XD more than two decades later.
notes: Known in Chinese internet circles as 'Dash'. Company IR email is best route; no personal verified accounts found.

name: Ke Guihua
current_role: Chairman and President, Keboda Technology Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603786), Shanghai
profile: Wenzhou-born Ke Guihua chairs Shanghai-listed Keboda Technology (founded 2003, formerly Shanghai Oubao Electric), a supplier of automotive electronics - lighting control, body/chassis electronics, energy management and central computing/ADAS domain controllers - to Mercedes-Benz, BMW, Audi and VW. Keboda has expanded abroad with plants in Japan and the Czech Republic.
interesting_fact: Keboda says it co-develops products with 30+ global car brands, runs tech centres in Germany, France and the US, and in June 2025 bought 100% of Czech company IMI; it is a national 'specialised and sophisticated little giant'.
deep_cut_fact: In his signed chairman's message on Keboda's site, Ke opens with the proverb 'natural selection, survival of the fittest' and says Keboda holds to 'first principles' as its business essence while partnering with top AI ecosystem players.
notes: Low public profile; little personal biography online in English. xingzhengbu@ is the company's administration-dept address. Keboda site has an aggressive WAF (may block automated access). Vice chairman Ke Binghua is also on the board.

name: Cao Jisheng
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Shandong Yisheng Livestock & Poultry Breeding Co. (002458.SZ)
profile: Cao Jisheng (b. 1960), an MBA and senior veterinarian from Yantai, Shandong, co-founded Yisheng with 33 others in 1997 and built it into China's major supplier of grandparent/parent-stock white-feather broiler breeders and breeding pigs; it listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He has chaired it since then and holds about 41% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Yisheng co-founded by Cao with 33 other people in 1997 in Yantai; it is now one of China's key suppliers of high-generation poultry breeding stock and was named a national pig core breeding farm.
deep_cut_fact: Cao is a qualified senior veterinarian (高级兽医师) and serves as president of the China Animal Agriculture Association's white-feather broiler branch and of the Shandong Animal Husbandry Association; he is also a deputy to the 14th Shandong Provincial People's Congress.
notes: Low international profile; best route is the board office (董事会办公室) IR email; Chinese-language outreach advised. Company email/website as listed in exchange-filing data (Eastmoney F10).

name: Tan Ruiqing
current_role: Major shareholder (approx. 6.8%) of Lomon Billions Group (SZSE: 002601); former vice chairman (left board April 2023)
profile: Tan Ruiqing is a co-founding shareholder and former vice chairman of Lomon Billions Group, one of the world's largest titanium dioxide pigment makers, which grew out of a state-owned sulfur mine business in Jiaozuo, Henan. He left the board at the April 2023 re-election but still held ~162m shares (6.81%) per an April 2026 filing.
interesting_fact: Lomon Billions grew out of a state-owned sulfur/brimstone mine business in Henan and became a leading global supplier of titanium dioxide pigment (the white in paint, plastics and paper).

name: Li Zhenjiang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, China Shineway Pharmaceutical Group (HKEX: 2877)
profile: Li Zhenjiang (b. c.1955) co-founded China Shineway Pharmaceutical, a Hebei-based maker of modern traditional Chinese medicine (injections, soft capsules, granules) listed in Hong Kong since 2004. He joined its predecessor in 1974, has led it since 1984, and still runs overall management and R&D.
interesting_fact: He served as a deputy to China's 10th, 11th and 12th National People's Congress and is vice-chairman of the PRC Chinese Medicine Association.
deep_cut_fact: He joined the factory that became Shineway in 1974, became its head in 1984, and was named an Outstanding Entrepreneur of the PRC Pharmaceutical Industry in 1994; he also holds a National May 1st (Wu Yi) Labour Award.
notes: Low media profile; no published email found in the annual report. Best route is via the company's HK office / company secretary listed on shineway.com.hk.

name: Li Wenbin
current_role: Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer, Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing Ltd (HKEX: 2314)
profile: Li Wenbin (Lee Man Bun, MH JP; also known as Edmond Lee) is the younger son of Lee & Man founder Lee Wan Keung Patrick and brother of chairman Raymond Lee Man Chun. He has run Hong Kong-listed Lee & Man Paper, one of China's largest containerboard/tissue makers, as CEO since about 2013-14, and his family holds a large stake.

name: Cheng Sanrong
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Kunshan Huguang Auto Harness Co. (沪光股份, SSE: 605333)
profile: Founded the forerunner of Huguang in Zhangpu town, Kunshan in 1988 at age 25, making wiring harnesses for excavators and bulldozers. Huguang became a Volkswagen A-grade supplier in 1999 and listed in Shanghai in 2020; it is now a leading Chinese auto wiring-harness maker with R&D in Germany, Korea, North America and a plant in Romania (2023).

Jifeng bought control of German seating supplier Grammer AG in 2019, turning it into a global auto-interior group now pushing into complete passenger-car seats.

profile: Guo Yiqun is the wife of Zhou Wen, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Shanghai PRET Composites, a Shanghai maker of modified plastics and composites (largely automotive-grade PP, ABS, PA, LCP). Her Hurun wealth is shared with Zhou Wen and derives from the family's PRET stake. She keeps no public profile of her own.

In 2021 he and his brother Chen Dong each received ~39.9% of parent Guangwei Group; since 2024 Chen Dong's votes are delegated to him, making him sole actual controller.
interesting_fact: Guangwei began as a fishing-tackle company using carbon composites in fishing rods, then pivoted into making China's own carbon fibre when foreign suppliers restricted products, technology and equipment.
deep_cut_fact: Under a March 6, 2024 concert-party agreement, his brother Chen Dong delegated all his Guangwei Group voting rights to Chen Liang, making him the listed company's sole actual controller (per the H1 2026 report).
notes: Low public profile; many unrelated people share the name 陈亮 (e.g. the CICC chairman), so don't mix them up. Best route is the company's board-secretary/IR contact. Deep-cut fact is corporate-governance detail rather than personal.

name: Li Zhijun
current_role: Co-founder and Vice Chairman, Double Medical Technology Inc. (大博医疗, SZSE: 002901); Chairman, Double Medical International Investment Co. (HK)
profile: 林志军 (romanised Lin Zhijun; listed here as 'Li') co-founded Xiamen-based orthopaedic implant maker Double Medical with his brother, chairman Lin Zhixiong, and has been vice chairman since 2004. The brothers jointly control the company; he directly holds ~19.5% (2025 annual report). Born Sept 1975, Chinese national with HK permanent residency.
interesting_fact: The company describes the founding duo as complementary: elder brother Lin Zhixiong is a former orthopaedic surgeon, while Lin Zhijun brought front-line medical-device sales and management experience.
deep_cut_fact: Before Double Medical, he ran Xiamen Inet Medical Devices (厦门伊耐特医疗器械) as executive director and GM from 1999 to 2008; since 2013 he has been president of the Xiamen Medical Device Association and is a council member of the Xiamen Double Medical Charity Foundation.
notes: Input name 'Li Zhijun' is a romanisation error: 林志军 = Lin Zhijun. Low public profile; best route is via company board secretary / IR email.

profile: Born 1962, a 1978-entry Tsinghua thermal-engineering graduate who worked as an Air Force engineering-design engineer (1983-92) before turning to investment. Beijing Huaqing OmniVision Technology) he backed Will Semi's 2019 acquisition of OmniVision image sensors; he runs Tsinghua-linked VC firms Qingkong Yinxing and Ginkgo Angel Investment Center.

profile: Raymond Lee Man Chun founded and chairs Lee & Man Paper, a Hong Kong-listed maker of containerboard, tissue and pulp with ~10,000 staff and mills in mainland China and Vietnam. A UBC engineering graduate, he is a CPPCC National Committee member, holds the Silver Bauhinia Star and is an INED of Beijing Enterprises Water.
interesting_fact: He was named a Hong Kong Young Industrialist (2002) and one of Hong Kong's Ten Outstanding Young Persons (2003), and is an honorary citizen of both Dongguan and Changshu, where Lee & Man runs major mills.

profile: Jiang Jinzhi (George Jiang) founded Greenwoods Asset Management in 2004; it grew into one of Asia's largest China-focused hedge fund managers (~US$20bn AUM in 2023) with offices in Shanghai, Hong Kong and Singapore. A long-term value investor, he has gradually stepped back from front-line management as newer portfolio managers took over.

notes: Very low public profile; rarely appears in media. Best route is via Greenwoods corporate site (JS-only, no published email found). Greenwoods Asset Management HK files SEC Form ADV (CRD 161898).

name: Wu Sin-Yang
current_role: Vice Chairman and President (General Manager), Shin Kong Mitsukoshi Department Store (新光三越, SKM), Taiwan
profile: Wu Sin-Yang (吳昕陽), of Taiwan's Shin Kong family, runs Shin Kong Mitsukoshi, Taiwan's largest department-store chain and a joint venture with Japan's Mitsukoshi. He became general manager in 2019, succeeding his brother Wu Hsin-ta, and later added vice chairman. He has pushed into outlets and transport-hub retail, winning the Taipei Main Station mall tender in 2026, and targets NT$100bn in sales.

deep_cut_fact: In 2021 he set SKM's three strategic engines as 'new businesses, new customers, new channels' (新事業、新顧客、新渠道), said more than ten expansion projects across Taiwan were under evaluation, and aimed to beat the company's NT$82bn annual sales record.

profile: Zhang Xiaolin (张晓琳) is the wife of Tan Ruiqing, longtime 5%+ shareholder and former vice-chairman of titanium-dioxide giant Lomon Billions (龙佰集团, 002601.SZ). The couple's wealth stems from their Lomon Billions stake, held directly and via Henan Yintai Investment, which Zhang co-owns. Exchange filings describe Henan Yinke International Chemical as jointly controlled by Tan and Zhang.
interesting_fact: Lomon Billions is one of the world's largest titanium dioxide producers; Tan Ruiqing's stake was about 8.3% in early 2026 before he sold ~1.35% of the company's shares via open-market trades in Feb-Mar 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal channels found. Identity confirmed via SZSE filings naming her as Tan Ruiqing's spouse (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2022-04-13/1212898666.PDF). Any approach would realistically go via Lomon Billions' board office / Tan Ruiqing. Alive status not explicitly confirmed, though she appears as a shareholder in a March 2026 filing.

name: Ho Tsz Wan
current_role: Substantial shareholder (via spouse) of Lee & Man Paper Manufacturing (HKEX: 2314); reported director of Lee & Man Construction Holdings
profile: Hong Kong-based wife of Lee Man Bun, CEO and executive director of containerboard maker Lee & Man Paper. Under Hong Kong's SFO she is deemed interested in the 1.30bn shares (30.35%) held by her husband, which is the basis of her Hurun listing shared with him; she is not an executive of the listed company herself.
interesting_fact: Lee & Man Paper's 2025 annual report lists her as a substantial shareholder deemed interested in 30.35% of the company through her husband Lee Man Bun, son of founder Lee Wan Keung.
notes: Private individual with essentially no public profile; aggregator profiles (MarketScreener) say she was a Lee & Man Paper manager 2007-2012, a USC graduate (2003) and INED of Unipact Entertainment, unverified. Better outreach target is husband Lee Man Bun via Lee & Man Paper.

name: Niejuan
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with husband Zhang Min) of Cofoe Medical Technology (可孚医疗, SZ:301087); stepped down as vice chair in Jan 2023
profile: Nie Juan (聂娟) co-founded the home-medical-device business that became Cofoe with her husband Zhang Min, starting with predecessor brand 'Haohushi' (好护士) in 2007. Cofoe (blood-pressure monitors, hearing aids, wheelchairs, consumables) listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2021; the couple jointly control it. She resigned as vice chair in January 2023 and is no longer an executive.
interesting_fact: Cofoe grew out of Zhang Min distributing blood-pressure monitors, wheelchairs and cupping devices before he finished junior college; at about 30 he created the Cofoe brand and moved from distribution into own-brand manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding the business, Nie Juan was a government employee: a clerk at the Yiyang Municipal Engineering Management Office (益阳市市政工程管理处) in Hunan.
notes: Low public profile; not an executive since 2023. Best route is Cofoe's board-secretary office (secretary Xue Xiaoqiao) via the IR email; husband Zhang Min is chairman/president.

name: Zhang Qin
current_role: Executive Director, Vice Chairman, Deputy General Manager and Board Secretary, SG Micro Corp (300661.SZ / 03661.HK)
profile: Zhang Qin co-founded SG Micro (圣邦微电子), a Beijing analog-chip designer started in January 2007 with chairman Zhang Shilong. It is China's No. 1 domestic analog IC company by revenue and No. 8 globally. Listed in Shenzhen (2017) and Hong Kong (2026), it is part-owned by her: she holds about 8% and belongs to the controlling group.
interesting_fact: SG Micro makes the signal-chain and power-management chips (amplifiers, converters, drivers) that sit in nearly every electronic system. 2025 revenue was about RMB 4.0bn, and Q1 2026 net profit roughly doubled year on year.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as an engineer: in July 1993 she earned an engineering bachelor's from the Beijing Institute of Light Industry (now Beijing Technology and Business University). She has been on SG Micro's board since its first month in January 2007 and has also been board secretary since 2012.
notes: As board secretary she oversees SG Micro's investor relations, so the IR email effectively reaches her office. Low personal media profile. Chairman/CEO Zhang Shilong is the public face of the company.

name: Li Xing
current_role: Chairman, Huanlejia Food Group Co., Ltd. (Shenzhen ChiNext: 300997)
profile: Li Xing (b. 1971) founded Huanlejia in Zhanjiang, Guangdong in 2001 and remains chairman and co-controlling shareholder. The company began with canned fruit, seafood and quail-egg tins, and from 2014 built its 'Huanlejia' raw-pressed coconut juice into its biggest product line. It listed on ChiNext in 2021.
interesting_fact: Huanlejia moved into plant-protein drinks in 2014 when its canned-food niche plateaued; its coconut juice became the company's largest revenue source, alongside fruit canning.
notes: Company bio: Chinese national with HK permanent residence, founded company 2001. Day-to-day leadership has passed to vice-chairman/president Li Zihao (from March 2025). The IR email is the board secretary's office; best route is via IR. No personal media presence found.

name: Gerald G Wong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Shanghai Cambridge Industries Group (CIG; SSE 603083 / HKEX 6166)
profile: Gerald G Wong (黄钢) founded CIG in 2005-06, a Shanghai maker of optical modules and broadband/wireless equipment; it listed in Shanghai in 2017 and added a Hong Kong listing. Demand for high-speed optical modules for AI data centers has driven CIG's recent growth. He has been chairman and CEO since 2011.
interesting_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, Wong spent 1984-2000 at AT&T Bell Labs and rose to vice president at Lucent Technologies. He has over 40 years in telecom.
deep_cut_fact: Before CIG, he co-founded Photon Bridge (光桥科技(中国)有限公司) in 2000. He holds both a bachelor's and a master's in electrical engineering and computer science from MIT, both conferred in June 1985.
notes: Relevant to the data-center angle because CIG makes 800G/1.6T optical modules. The best route is the IR email or the board secretary office (board secretary: Jin Zeqing). Wong is a US/MIT-trained engineer, so outreach in English should work.

name: Wang Haijun
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Atour Lifestyle Holdings (Nasdaq: ATAT)
profile: Wang Haijun (王海军) founded Atour, China's largest mid-to-upscale hotel chain, in 2012-13 after years at Home Inns, Jinjiang Inn and as EVP of China Lodging (now H World). Atour listed on Nasdaq in 2022 and pairs hotels with a fast-growing sleep-products retail business. He is a Yanshan University graduate with a CEIBS EMBA.
interesting_fact: Atour also runs a large retail arm selling the pillows, bedding and mattresses guests use in its hotels, a key growth driver alongside its hotel network.
deep_cut_fact: Atour is named after Yaduo (亚朵) village in Nujiang, Yunnan: after leaving Hanting in 2012 Wang travelled to Bhutan and Nepal, then found in Yaduo the same simple contentment and named the brand after it. He long used the nickname 耶律胤 (Yelü Yin), a nod to his reported Khitan ancestry.
notes: Hosts quarterly earnings calls in English/Chinese; IR via Christensen Advisory is the most practical route.

name: Shao Hongzhi
current_role: Chairman, CEO and actual controller, Nanjing Sunlord Electronics Corp. (商络电子, SZSE: 300975)
profile: Sha Hongzhi (沙宏志; listed by Hurun as 'Shao Hongzhi', company 'Sunlux') founded Nanjing Sunlord Electronics in August 1999 and is its legal representative and actual controller. Sunlord is one of China's leading domestic distributors of passive electronic components (60+ agency lines, 2,000+ customers); it listed on the Shenzhen ChiNext board in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Sunlord runs large bonded warehouse/logistics hubs in Nanjing, Shenzhen and Hong Kong with WMS and automatic labelling, plus subsidiaries in Singapore and Taiwan and offices in Thailand and Malaysia.
deep_cut_fact: Before its 2021 ChiNext IPO, Sunlord was first quoted on China's NEEQ 'New Third Board' in 2015; Sha holds an MBA from CEIBS.
notes: Correct Chinese name is 沙宏志 (Sha Hongzhi); Hurun's 'Sunlux' = Nanjing Sunlord Electronics (not Shenzhen Sunlord 002138). CEIBS MBA per MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/HONG-ZHI-SHA-A37YJ1/experience/). Best route: IR email / board secretary.

name: Jin Kun
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Shanghai Beite Technology Group (SSE: 603009)
profile: Jin Kun (靳坤) is the founder-chairman and controlling shareholder of Shanghai Beite Technology, an auto-parts maker founded in 2002 and listed in Shanghai in 2014. Beite makes steering-rack and shock-absorber piston rods, auto A/C compressors, precision parts and lightweight aluminium components. Wealth shared with Jin Xiaotang, his concert party in Beite filings.
interesting_fact: Beite's predecessor was Shanghai Beite Metal Products Co.; in 2024 Jin Kun's voting stake passively rose above 30% (triggering a takeover report) only because Beite cancelled shares returned under a performance-compensation agreement.
notes: Low public profile; no personal interviews found. Best route is Beite's board-secretary/IR mailbox (touzizhe@ = 'investor').

name: Jin Xiaotang
current_role: Director and General Manager, Shanghai Beite Technology Group (北特科技, SSE: 603009)
profile: Jin Xiaotang (靳晓堂) is the son of Beite founder and controlling shareholder Jin Kun, acts in concert with him, and holds ~8% of the Shanghai-listed auto-parts maker (steering rack bars, shock-absorber rods, A/C compressors, aluminium parts). He has been a director and general manager since January 2019; in 2025 the company renamed itself Shanghai Beite Technology Group.
interesting_fact: Beite is pivoting into humanoid robotics: in 2024 it set up Jiangsu Beite Robot Technology to make planetary roller screws, planning ~2.6m sets/yr in Kunshan plus a Thailand base, an RMB 1.85bn bet.
notes: Wealth shared with father Jin Kun (chairman, ~31.6%). Low public profile; route via company board secretary Liu Gongyou (IR email above). Role per 2024 acquisition report; check latest SSE filings to confirm GM title.

name: Jin Lianqin
current_role: Director and largest shareholder (~29.9%), Jiangsu Changqingshu New Materials Technology Co. (Changqing Technology, SSE: 603125)
profile: Jin Lianqin (金连琴), 59, is a director and co-controlling shareholder (with her husband, chairman Sun Qiuxin) of Zhenjiang-based Changqing Technology, a maker of specialty monomers and polymer additives that listed on the Shanghai main board in April 2023. She also heads Xinxin Oil Products and is GM of Zhenjiang Baoju Oil Additives.
interesting_fact: Changqing's predecessor was set up in June 2010 as a wholly foreign-owned enterprise held via a British nominee, Alan David Pow, on Sun Qiuxin's behalf to fit local investment-attraction policy; the nominee arrangement was unwound in Dec 2011.
deep_cut_fact: Before chemicals, she spent 13 years (1990-2003) as a clinical lab staffer in the testing department of the Danmian Group staff hospital, then worked in the lab of Danyang Yunyang People's Hospital until 2006.
notes: Hurun 'Changqing' = Changqing Technology (常青科技, 603125), not Changqing Agrochemical (002391). Low public profile; best route is the company securities office (board secretary).

name: Dai Tiantian
current_role: Director, Vice President and Technical Director of Software R&D, Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (688188.SH)
profile: Dai Tiantian (b. 1983) co-founded Shanghai Friendess (Bochu) in 2007 with four Shanghai Jiao Tong University classmates; it makes the dominant laser-cutting CNC control systems and software (CypCut, TubesT) in China. He chaired the company until 2018 and is now a director, VP and software R&D chief, holding about 14% as one of five joint controllers.
interesting_fact: Friendess began in 2007 as an SJTU student startup with registered capital of just RMB 200,000; it listed on the STAR Market in 2019 among the first batch of companies and became the leading supplier of laser-cutting control systems.
deep_cut_fact: Both his bachelor's (2004) and master's (2007) degrees are from Shanghai Jiao Tong University; at founding he put in RMB 60,000 of the RMB 200,000 capital, six times each co-founder's RMB 10,000, and he holds the Chinese 'senior systems analyst' qualification.
notes: Male (the Hurun name can be misread). Low public profile, technical founder; chairman Tang Ye is the public face. Best route is the company IR mailbox.

name: Zhou Yong
current_role: Founder (described as CTO/CEO in different sources), Linkerbot (灵心巧手), Beijing
profile: Zhou Yong (Alex Zhou) founded Linkerbot in 2023 to build low-cost, high-degree-of-freedom dexterous robotic hands (Linker Hand series) for humanoid robots and industry. Linkerbot claims >80% of the global high-DoF robotic-hand market by volume and was valued at ~US$3bn in an April 2026 round, with later reports of a ~$6bn raise.
interesting_fact: Before robotics he spent about a decade in global online communities; his previous company reached ~300 million users, less than 1% of them in China. He says: 'The hand is the last great hardware problem in robotics.'
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from the Youth Class (gifted-teen program) at Huazhong University of Science and Technology at age 14; he set out to build a hand that beats the UK Shadow Hand at a fraction of the price.
notes: Goes by Alex Zhou in English media (WIRED, Pandaily). Titles vary across sources (founder & CTO vs CEO). Very on-topic for a tech/hardware podcast; company is actively fundraising and media-facing.

name: Yi Weihua
current_role: Co-founder and controlling shareholder, WG Tech (Jiangxi WG Optoelectronic, 603773.SH); stepped down as chairman and director in March 2026
profile: Yi Weihua (易伟华) co-founded WG Tech (沃格光电) in Xinyu, Jiangxi in December 2009 with Zhang Fujia. It started in flat-panel display glass processing, listed on the Shanghai main board in 2018, and is now pivoting to glass circuit boards (GCP) for Mini LED and semiconductor packaging. He left the board in March 2026 'for personal reasons', and Zhang Chunjiao became chairman.
interesting_fact: Yi has a technical background, and since 2019 he has personally led WG Tech's R&D push into glass-substrate circuit boards (TGV/GCP) for Mini LED backlights and advanced chip packaging. That puts the company in the glass-core substrate race relevant to AI and data-center chips.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from university in 1996, Yi started as a technician in Shenzhen and rose to manager and trader. In 2006 he started his own touch-screen sales business before founding WG Tech. He has said he wanted to 'gather a group of young people with dreams, character and ability to come together to do things that are meaningful to society.'
notes: No longer chairman (resigned March 2026); Zhang Chunjiao (listed as sharing this wealth entry) is now chairman. In May 2026 the CSRC opened an investigation into a share-transfer disclosure, and he was fined in August 2026. Treat as sensitive and approach via company IR.

name: Zhang Chunjiao
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, WG Tech (JiangXi) Group Co., Ltd. (沃格光电, SSE: 603773)
profile: Zhang Chunjiao (张春姣, b. Dec 1972) is co-founder of WG Tech, a Xinyu, Jiangxi maker of optoelectronic glass and glass circuit plates founded in 2009 and listed in Shanghai in 2018. Her wealth (per Hurun) is shared with co-founder Yi Weihua, the former controlling shareholder. She became GM in Nov 2022 and chairman in March 2026 after Yi stepped down.
interesting_fact: WG Tech says it is one of very few companies globally with full-process capability for GCP (glass circuit plate) technology, now used for glass-core substrates for high-compute chip packaging, optical-module glass substrates and Mini/MicroLED displays — directly relevant to AI/data-center hardware.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the company she worked her way through WG Tech as assistant to the general manager, vice president, head of the marketing center and special assistant to the chairman; the company credits her with nearly 20 years in optoelectronic display and supply-chain management.
notes: Name in filings is 张春姣 (input lists 张春娇). Board secretary is Gong Qingyu (龚庆宇); route via board office/IR email. Glass-substrate packaging angle fits the data-center theme.

name: Wan Zhijian
current_role: Vice Chairman (from Oct 2026), director and deputy GM, Nanchang Sanrui Intelligent Technology (301696.SZ)
profile: Wan Zhijian (b. Feb 1979) is co-founder and ~18.7% shareholder of Nanchang Sanrui Intelligent Technology, a leading maker of electric propulsion systems (motors, ESCs, propellers) for drones and robot joints, also developing eVTOL power systems. He co-founded the firm in 2009 with his cousin, chairman Wu Min; it listed on ChiNext in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Sanrui sits on two Chinese policy themes at once - the low-altitude economy (drone power systems, ~49% of revenue from exports) and embodied-AI robotics via its CubeMars robot-joint brand launched in 2018; gross margin on main business was about 60% in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before drones, Wan spent a decade (July 1998 - June 2008) running an earth-and-stone haulage business, then joined his cousin's Nanchang Sanrui Technology as deputy GM in 2008. He studied rural economics at the Jiangxi Provincial Party School.
notes: Elected vice chairman of the 2nd board on 27 Oct 2026 (cninfo 1225629729). Bound by concert-action agreement with Wu Min (cousin, controller). No personal public profile; route via company IR.

name: Sun Yaozhi
current_role: Co-actual controller of the Wanxi group (Henan Wanxi Holdings / Zhongjing Wanxi Pharmaceutical, Zhongjing Food 300908.SZ); former chairman of Wanxi Pharmaceutical
profile: Sun Yaozhi (b. 1951, Neixiang, Henan; Zhengzhou University graduate) built Wanxi Pharmaceutical in Xixia county, Nanyang, into Zhongjing Wanxi, maker of Zhongjing Liuwei Dihuang pills. He and Zhu Xincheng are the actual controllers of listed Zhongjing Food (300908.SZ); day-to-day leadership has passed to Sun Feng, chairman of Wanxi Pharma since Oct 2017.
interesting_fact: He served as a deputy to China's National People's Congress for Henan, first elected in 2008 and again in 2013 (12th NPC).
deep_cut_fact: Zhongjing Food, controlled by Sun and Zhu Xincheng, is headquartered in Xixia, billed as China's 'hometown of shiitake mushrooms'; its flagship is Zhongjing shiitake-mushroom sauce and it calls itself a partner of China's space programme.
notes: Listed as actual controller in Zhongjing Food's H1 2026 report (Aug 2026), but no recent public appearances found; alive status not directly confirmed. Not on the board; best route is Zhongjing Food IR / board secretary Wang Fei.

name: Lu Xinchun
current_role: Chief Scientist, Hwatsing Technology (华海清科, SSE STAR: 688120); Chief Researcher, Dept. of Mechanical Engineering, Tsinghua University
profile: Tsinghua tribologist (b. 1966, Yantai) whose team began chemical-mechanical polishing (CMP) research in 2000 and spun it out in 2013 as Hwatsing, now China's No.1 domestic CMP and wafer-thinning equipment maker, listed on the STAR Market in 2022. He was chairman until 2025 and remains chief scientist guiding R&D.
interesting_fact: His team launched China's first 12-inch CMP tool with domestic IP and an integrated grinding-polishing thinning tool, key equipment for chipmaking and advanced packaging; he won a 2025 Ho Leung Ho Lee Science and Technology Innovation Prize.
deep_cut_fact: An academic first: he earned his bachelor's and master's at Jilin University of Technology (1988, 1991), a PhD at the CAS Institute of Metal Research (1994), and did his postdoc at Tsinghua's State Key Laboratory of Tribology, the field of nano-scale friction behind CMP.
notes: Academic-founder; stepped down as Hwatsing chairman in 2025 (Wang Tongqing is now chairman & GM) but remains chief scientist (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2273649). Routes: Hwatsing board office (secretary Chen Zhenyin) or Tsinghua Mechanical Engineering dept. Likely Chinese-language outreach needed.

name: Huang Zewei
current_role: Chairman, Shannon Semiconductor (香农芯创, SZSE: 300475); chairman of subsidiary 联合创泰 (Lianhe Chuangtai)
profile: Huang Zewei (b. May 1984) built 联合创泰, a Shenzhen distributor of SK hynix memory chips. He sold it to Julong (now 香农芯创/Shannon) in a ~RMB1.6bn 2021 deal and joined its board, became co-chairman in July 2021 and chairman on 30 Oct 2025. The group's main-business revenue was ~RMB35.2bn in 2025.
interesting_fact: His business sits right in the AI/data-centre supply chain: SK hynix is Lianhe Chuangtai's core supplier, and the company sells its data-storage memory to China's leading internet firms for cloud-computing storage.
deep_cut_fact: He sold 联合创泰 twice: first to 英唐智控, then in 2020 he and partners bought 100% back for RMB1.48bn, and in 2021 he sold it again, this time to the Julong/Shannon listed vehicle for about RMB1.6bn.
notes: Hurun lists the source as 'Shannon'/Retail; this is 香农芯创 (memory-chip distribution). Directly held 24.9m shares at end-2025, plus stakes through 深圳/无锡新联普 partnerships. Strong data-centre/memory angle. Best route is through the IR/board-secretary office (secretary 曾柏林).

name: Le Weiping
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Technology (Hengyunchang, STAR Market: 688785).
profile: Le Weiping (b. 1973) spent ~11 years at US plasma-power maker Advanced Energy in Shenzhen and Shanghai before founding CSL Vacuum (Hengyunchang) to localise plasma RF power systems for chip equipment. Its main customer is Piotech; the company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 28 Jan 2026. He controls ~73% of voting rights (wealth shared with Cao Li per Hurun).
interesting_fact: He quit a well-paid multinational job in 2013, when China's chip-equipment sector was nascent, and started CSL with five employees in an office under 100 square metres in Shenzhen's Bao'an district.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a technician/engineer at the telecom-equipment factory of the Taoyuan County Post & Telecom Bureau in Hunan; he joined Advanced Energy Shenzhen in 2003 as a test technician and rose to product-applications engineer and senior sales manager in Shanghai.
notes: Recent IPO (Jan 2026); low personal media profile. Board secretary Zhuang Lihua handles IR. Relationship to co-listed Cao Li not confirmed.

name: Cao Li
current_role: Major shareholder (back-office management), Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Science & Technology (恒运昌, STAR 688785)
profile: Co-owner, with chairman Le Weiping, of Shenzhen CSL Vacuum Science & Technology, which makes plasma RF power supplies and related core components for semiconductor process equipment. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 28 Jan 2026, which put the couple on the 2026 Hurun China list. Per IPO disclosures she handles back-office management rather than operations.
interesting_fact: CSL was started in Shenzhen's Bao'an district with just five staff after Le Weiping spent 11 years at US plasma-power firm Advanced Energy; it now aims to be a platform supplier of plasma-process core components for China's chip-tool makers.
notes: Non-public figure; Le Weiping (chairman/GM) is the company's public face and better outreach target. IR phone 0755-23596099 per 2025 annual report.

name: Green Chang-Lin
current_role: Chairman, MPI Corporation (旺矽科技, TWSE: 6223), Hsinchu, Taiwan
profile: Ko Chang-lin (葛長林; listed by Hurun as 'Green Chang-Lin') started out in semiconductor equipment distribution and built MPI Corporation, now described as the world's fourth-largest probe-card maker. AI-chip testing demand has pushed MPI to record results, sold-out capacity and ~6-month lead times.
interesting_fact: With AI-chip test demand outstripping capacity, MPI in 2026 began asking customers to pay before taking delivery, which he called a first for the probe-card industry.
deep_cut_fact: He also chairs Gordon Biersch Taiwan (吉比鮮釀). He won the brewpub franchise after a meeting in the US was postponed and he spent the evening tasting 10+ experimental beers with the brewer until midnight; the first Taipei outlet opened in 2008. He says it made him no money but 10+ years of happiness.
notes: Listed with country China (Hurun) but he is Taiwan-based. Strong AI/data-center supply chain angle (probe cards for AI ASIC/GPU testing). Mandarin-language media interviews are common; route via MPI IR.

name: Jones Chen
current_role: Chairman, Genius Electronic Optical Co. (GSEO, TWSE: 3406), Taichung, Taiwan
profile: Chen Tien-ching (陳天慶, 'Jones Chen') leads Genius Electronic Optical, a Taiwanese maker of precision plastic lenses for smartphone cameras (a major Apple supplier), founded 1990 and listed 2005. Under him GSEO is expanding into smart-glasses optics, humanoid-robot lenses and data-center optical interconnects / co-packaged optics.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2026 3M agreed to take a ~4.7% stake in GSEO via private placement and partner on 3M's Expanded Beam Optical (EBO) connectors for hyperscale AI data centers; GSEO plans staged mass production of co-packaged-optics parts in 2027-2028.
deep_cut_fact: In the mid-2000s he was GSEO's general manager under his elder brother Chen Tien-shu (then chairman); the two brothers quietly went to Xiamen to invest in and build the factories that became the company's main production base.
notes: Taiwanese (Hurun lists him under China). Speaks at GSEO earnings calls; little personal press. Strong data-center angle via CPO/optical interconnect pivot. IR contact is a named IR officer published on the company IR page. Deep-cut source (Global Views 2006) could not be fetched directly; verify before use.

name: Wu Zuyu
current_role: Founder and chairman, Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage Technology (海辰储能)
profile: Wu Zuyu (吴祖钰), born in the mid-1980s, holds an applied-chemistry BSc from Shandong Normal University and a chemical-engineering MSc from Fuzhou University. He was an engineer at CATL before founding Hithium in Xiamen on 27 Dec 2019. Within about six years Hithium became one of the world's top three makers of stationary storage batteries, passing 100 GWh of shipments, and it is pursuing a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: Hithium went from founding to roughly third in global energy-storage cell shipments in about five years. Hurun valued it at RMB 25bn in 2024, and it now sells 5 MWh containers and 8-hour long-duration storage systems in the US, Australia and Japan.
deep_cut_fact: As a CATL engineer he was first-named inventor on a run of energy-storage patents covering current collectors, electrode sheets and cells. One count puts it at 67 such patents between 2012 and 2018.
notes: Very low public profile; Hithium's prospectus is the main source on him. The press email comes from an older Hithium newsroom release and may be outdated. Avoid the topic of CATL in outreach: there are ongoing non-compete and unfair-competition disputes, which also delayed the HK IPO. The 67-patent count is from 36kr (https://www.36kr.com/p/2541517764011779).

name: Wei Jisheng
current_role: Chairman, Longkou Shengtong Group; major shareholder (27.7%) and long-time director of Senton Energy / Shengtong Energy (SZSE: 001331)
profile: Wei Jisheng (b. 1963) built a trucking business in Longkou, Shandong into Senton (Shengtong) Energy, an LNG trading and tank-truck logistics firm ranked 5th in China for both LNG trading and LNG transport in 2025, listed in Shenzhen. In 2026 his family sold control (~45% incl. tender offer) to Qiteng Robotics; he still held 27.73% at mid-2026.
interesting_fact: Senton Energy trucks LNG from CNOOC/Sinopec/PetroChina coastal terminals and inland liquefaction plants to customers nationwide; its LNG sales revenue grew 18.6% to about RMB 5.47bn in H1 2026 (per its filings), and control passed in June 2026 to a robotics company.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in December 1978, aged 15, as a staff member of the Huang County Transport Company's Longkou motor team, rising to team leader and then manager of Longkou No.3 Motor Transport Co. before founding Shengtong Transport in 1994.
notes: Low public profile; no interviews found. Since June 2026 the controlling shareholder is Qiteng Robotics (actual controller Zhu Dong); board was re-elected early in 2026, so check whether Wei remains a director. Route via company board office mailbox.

name: Zhang Yiling
current_role: Shareholder in the Erdos group (Inner Mongolia Erdos Investment Holding), per Hurun; specific executive role not confirmed
profile: Zhang Yiling (张奕龄, b. ~1980, Ordos; Cambridge master's per Hurun) is listed by Hurun China (2016-2022) under Erdos (鄂尔多斯), the Ordos group in cashmere, coal power, metallurgy and real estate. Hurun 2021: RMB7.8bn, 3rd richest in Ordos. Erdos Resources (600295.SH) is ultimately controlled by Inner Mongolia Erdos Investment Holding.
interesting_fact: The Erdos group grew from a 1979 cashmere factory into an industrial group spanning cashmere apparel (the ERDOS brand), resources and mineral exploration, and power and energy use.
notes: Hurun: 张奕龄, b. 1980, Ordos, 硕士 / 剑桥 (Cambridge); company 鄂尔多斯 / Erdos. Gender unconfirmed. Not named in the Erdos Resources 2025 annual report, so the stake is probably via the holding company. A MarketScreener 'Yi Ling Zhang' is linked to Erdos Investment Holding (page unreadable). SSE, cninfo, Lixinger and Baidu were blocked here.

name: Jacob DeWitte
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Oklo Inc. (NYSE: OKLO)
profile: Nuclear engineer (Univ. of Florida BS 2008; MIT SM/PhD) who worked at Sandia, Urenco USA, the Naval Nuclear Laboratory and GE (core design lead on the PRISM sodium fast reactor) before co-founding Oklo in 2013 with Caroline Cochran (COO). Oklo, developing small advanced fission 'powerhouses' aimed partly at data centers, listed in 2024 via a Sam Altman-backed SPAC.
interesting_fact: Oklo is named after the uranium deposits at Oklo, Gabon, where natural self-sustaining fission reactions occurred about two billion years ago; DeWitte also raised the first modern institutional VC-led financing of a fission company.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Albuquerque, he spent weekends with his dad getting donuts and visiting the National Nuclear Science Museum; his favourite exhibit was a simulated fuel pellet the size of a pencil eraser holding the energy of a ton of coal. He later talked his family into detouring to Arizona's nuclear plant on a Grand Canyon trip.
notes: Highly relevant (nuclear for data centers). Frequent conference speaker (CERAWeek etc.) and congressional witness; 2014 Forbes 30 Under 30 (Energy). Oklo's site lists investors@oklo.com as its single media/investor contact; company X is @oklo. UF 2021 Distinguished Early Career Alumni Award: https://mse.ufl.edu/jacob-dewitte-2021-distinguished-early-career-alumni-award/

name: Caroline Cochran
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Operating Officer and Director, Oklo Inc. (NYSE: OKLO)
profile: Co-founded advanced-fission company Oklo in 2013 with her husband, CEO Jacob DeWitte; she now also goes by Caroline DeWitte. Oklo went public in 2024 through a SPAC backed by Sam Altman. It is building 75 MW 'Aurora' fast-reactor powerhouses, the first in Idaho, aimed at AI data centers, including a 1.2 GW agreement with Meta in Ohio.
interesting_fact: Oklo is named after the Oklo uranium deposits in Gabon, where natural nuclear fission reactions ran on their own about two billion years ago.
deep_cut_fact: She started out as a climate-concerned nuclear skeptic. She holds a BA in economics and a BS in mechanical engineering from the University of Oklahoma, where she later helped set up a technology-commercialization program, and she is one of the youngest recipients of OU's Regents' Alumni Award.
notes: A strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast, and she does podcasts (Business for Good, 2026). She is a former member of DOE's Nuclear Energy Advisory Committee. Use the Cochran/DeWitte name variants. Oklo's head of communications is listed as the media@oklo.com contact.

name: Steve Ells
current_role: Founder and COO, Counter Service (NYC fast-casual sandwich chain, formerly Kernel); founder of Chipotle
profile: Founded Chipotle in Denver in 1993 at 26 and led it as CEO/co-CEO until 2017-18; left its board in 2020. His next venture, Kernel, began as a robot-assisted vegan concept and became Counter Service, a five-unit NYC sandwich brand (2026) with Peloton co-founder Tom Cortese as CEO, now preparing to expand beyond New York.
interesting_fact: He describes Kernel's pivot with self-deprecation: of the original vegan, robotics-heavy menu, 'I thought the food was delicious... And so did a few of my customers.' Cortese admits he first thought Ells was 'absolutely bonkers'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Chipotle he earned an art history degree at CU Boulder, graduated from the Culinary Institute of America (1990) and spent two years as a sous chef under Jeremiah Tower at Stars in San Francisco; the first Chipotle opened near the University of Denver campus.
notes: Listed as former Forbes billionaire (~$0.97B). Energy/data-center angle is weak; best angle is automation/robotics in restaurants and founder reinvention. Speaks at industry events (NRN CREATE 2026).

name: Gunkul Dhumrongpiyawut
current_role: Chairman of the Board (non-executive), Gunkul Engineering PCL (SET: GUNKUL), Bangkok
profile: Founded Gunkul Engineering in 1982 as a trader importing electrical equipment for Thai government agencies, opened its own factory in 1992 to replace imports, then pivoted to renewables in 2007. Gunkul now runs solar and wind projects in Thailand, Malaysia, Japan and Vietnam. His wife Sopacha leads management as executive committee chair; daughter Naruechon is COO.
interesting_fact: Gunkul transformed from an electrical-equipment importer (1982) to a domestic manufacturer (1992) to one of Thailand's renewable-energy producers (from 2007), with solar projects across four Asian countries.
deep_cut_fact: Though he built an engineering company, his degrees are honorary: an Honorary Doctor of Engineering from Rajamangala University of Technology Thanyaburi (2018) and an Honorary Doctor of Art from RMUT Phra Nakhon (2016). Forbes notes he enjoys gardening in his spare time.
notes: Age ~71. Day-to-day leadership is with wife Sopacha and daughter Naruechon; outreach via company IR (CFO/Head of IR Thitipong Techaratanayuenyong) or corporate communications. Gardening fact from Forbes profile https://www.forbes.com/profile/gunkul-dhumrongpiyawut/.

name: Jeffrey Henley
current_role: Executive Vice Chair of the Board, Oracle Corporation; Chair, Institute for Energy Efficiency, UC Santa Barbara
profile: Finance executive who joined Oracle as CFO in 1991 to lead its turnaround, served as CFO until 2004, chairman 2004-2014, and has been vice chair since 2014 (Oracle's site now says executive vice chair). His wealth comes from decades of Oracle stock. Earlier he was CFO of Saga Corp. (food service) and Pacific Holding Co., after finance roles at Memorex and Fairchild.
interesting_fact: He and wife Judy pledged $50m to UC Santa Barbara in 2012 to support its Institute for Energy Efficiency and College of Engineering - and he chairs that institute today, a natural hook for an energy/data-center conversation.
deep_cut_fact: Oracle recruited him in 1991 for his reputation as a turnaround CFO; he calls Oracle 'the biggest turnaround, financially, of anything I'd done before.' At UCSB ('66) he cut his teeth as treasurer of the SigEp chapter, and he advises: 'If you think you want to be a CFO, you can't wait until you're 30.'
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. UCSB Institute for Energy Efficiency (iee.ucsb.edu) is an alternative, warmer route given his chair role there. Forbes lists him as 'former' billionaire (~$965m).

name: Gang Chen
current_role: Chairman and founder, Shanghai Aiko Solar Energy (SSE: 600732)
profile: Chen Gang (陈刚) founded Aiko Solar in 2009 after 20 years in aluminium manufacturing. Aiko became a top PERC cell maker after a 2017 breakthrough and an IDG-backed expansion, listed via a 2019 backdoor deal, and now pushes ABC back-contact cells and modules from plants in Foshan, Yiwu and Tianjin. He holds roughly 15% of the company.
interesting_fact: Aiko says its cumulative cell and module shipments have passed 200GW, equal to about 300 billion kWh of clean power a year by its estimate.
deep_cut_fact: A Ganzhou, Jiangxi native, he graduated in 1991 from the Southern Institute of Metallurgy (now Jiangxi University of Science and Technology), moonlighted as a 'Sunday engineer' at a Foshan state firm, cofounded the Aoumei aluminium JV, then switched to solar at 40. His motto on risky R&D: 'If even the worst outcome isn't bad, you dare to do it.'
notes: marketing@aikosolar.com is the general marketing inbox (listed for Thailand/Germany offices), not a dedicated press desk. Chinese-language outreach advised. Has given interviews to People's Daily's China Energy News (2024).

name: Bindiben Binish Chudgar
current_role: Listed promoter/shareholder of Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); no public executive role found
profile: Bindi (Bindiben) Binish Chudgar is a member of the Chudgar family that controls Intas Pharmaceuticals, the Ahmedabad generics and biosimilars maker (Accord Healthcare in Europe/US) founded by Hasmukh Chudgar. She is named as a promoter in Intas's draft IPO prospectus and appeared on the Hurun India list in 2018-2019 via her stake. No public business profile found.
interesting_fact: Intas, through its Accord Healthcare arm, became one of the largest suppliers of generic medicines to the UK's NHS and a major biosimilars player.
notes: Very low public profile; relationship to Binish Chudgar (Vice Chairman/Joint MD of Intas) inferred from name only and not confirmed by a source. Best route is via Intas corporate / Binish Chudgar. Promoter listing: https://prod-mssip.morganstanley.com/content/dam/msdotcom/en/indiaofferdocuments/pdfs/Intas-Pharmaceuticals-Ltd-DRHP.pdf (per search snippet).

name: Marcus Evans
current_role: Founder and owner, Marcus Evans Group (business conferences, summits, corporate hospitality)
profile: London-born entrepreneur (b. 1963) who founded what became the Marcus Evans Group in 1983; it runs thousands of B2B conferences, exhibitions and summits in ~32 countries, plus hospitality (THG Sports Tours) and training (Linguarama). Owned Ipswich Town FC from 2007 until selling to a US consortium in April 2021.
interesting_fact: His TV arm, Marcus Evans Entertainment, brought in World Productions (producer of Line of Duty) in 2012 before ITV Studios took a majority stake in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started out at about 20 with Associated Promotions (1983), selling corporate hospitality when it was a new market; it became The Hospitality Group / THG Sports Tours, still part of his group.
notes: Famously publicity-shy; rarely gives interviews and historically communicated via his executives. Best route is through Marcus Evans Group corporate channels. Relevant angle: his group runs energy/infrastructure business summits.

name: The Duke of Bedford
current_role: 15th Duke of Bedford (Andrew Russell); owner of the Woburn Estate and Bedford Estates (Bloomsbury, London)
profile: Andrew Russell (b. 1962), Harrow- and Harvard-educated, took over running Woburn Abbey from his parents in 2001 and succeeded as 15th Duke in 2003. Family wealth rests on the Woburn Estate in Bedfordshire and the Bedford Estates in Bloomsbury plus a major art collection; Sunday Times 2024 put it at ~£801m. Woburn Abbey has been closed since 2019 for a multi-year restoration.
interesting_fact: Woburn Abbey was founded in 1145 as a Cistercian monastery and granted to Sir John Russell (later 1st Earl of Bedford) in Henry VIII's will in 1547; the restoration has conserved all 24 of the Abbey's Canaletto paintings.
deep_cut_fact: The Woburn restoration involved 14,000 metres of scaffolding and lifting and re-laying 200,000 linear metres of floorboards; the gardens follow Humphry Repton's 1804 Red Book and are described as the most fully realised example of Repton's work.
notes: Private hereditary landowner, gives few interviews. Best route is the Woburn Abbey marketing team; woburn.co.uk also lists a Press Office page. Not an entrepreneurship/energy figure per se.

name: Andrey Blokh
current_role: Private investor; major shareholder of Curaleaf Holdings (described by Curaleaf as a retired CPG entrepreneur, not active in the company)
profile: Blokh was briefly president of Russian oil company Sibneft in the late 1990s, then with a partner consolidated Russian dairy assets into Unimilk, which combined with Danone in 2010 to form Danone Unimilk. He later became an early, large investor in US cannabis operator Curaleaf (public 2018). He is a US citizen who also holds a Russian passport.
interesting_fact: His dairy roll-up Unimilk merged with French food giant Danone in 2010 to create Danone Unimilk, one of Russia's largest dairy businesses.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal or office contact published. Only route is indirect via Curaleaf (where he is a passive holder). Press coverage centres on Abramovich-linked loans to Curaleaf insiders; avoid in outreach. Stake size reported variously (~6% voting to ~21%).

name: Lee Sang-hoon
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and Chief Research Officer, ABL Bio (Kosdaq-listed, South Korea)
profile: Korean scientist-entrepreneur who founded bispecific-antibody developer ABL Bio in February 2016 and listed it on Kosdaq in 2018. A November 2025 tech-transfer deal with Eli Lilly worth up to $2.6B for its Grabody-B blood-brain-barrier platform sent shares soaring and made him a billionaire. He continues to lead R&D for oncology and neurodegeneration programs.
interesting_fact: ABL Bio was born after Hanwha Chemical decided to shut down the biotech division Lee headed; he spun out with colleagues and built ABL Bio, later landing a $2.6B Eli Lilly deal for its brain-shuttle antibody technology.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he trained as a teacher: his B.S. from Seoul National University is in Biology Education. He then earned a PhD at Ohio State, did postdocs at Harvard Medical School and Stanford, worked at Chiron, AstraZeneca, Genentech and Exelixis, and co-founded PharmAbcine before ABL Bio.
notes: Country in input is United States, but he is Korean and based in Seoul (ABL Bio HQ, Seongnam). Speaks at BIO International; member of Council of Korean Americans.

name: Ali Erdemoglu
current_role: Board chairman/deputy chairman of Merinos Halı and vice chairman of SASA Polyester (Erdemoğlu Holding); sources differ on current Merinos title
profile: Co-owner with brother İbrahim of Erdemoğlu Holding (Gaziantep), which grew from father Mehmet's two looms in 1970 into Merinos and Dinarsu carpets, among the world's largest carpet makers. In 2015 the brothers bought 51% of SASA Polyester for $102M and now own over 75%. SASA is expanding into petrochemicals, including a planned $25B Yumurtalık complex.
interesting_fact: He started in the carpet trade with his father right after primary school; SASA has a $935M licensing and technical-service agreement with Koch Industries' Invista.
deep_cut_fact: In 2014 he accepted first prize (large-company category) in Turkey's Industrial Energy Efficiency Awards at the 2nd National Energy Summit in Gaziantep. Merinos won for upgrading compressors and electric motors in its factories, a natural hook for an energy podcast.
notes: Both are general group inboxes (Erdemoğlu Holding, SASA). Brother İbrahim chairs the holding and is its more public face. Turkish-language outreach is likely more effective.

name: Cai Hao
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Arctech Solar Holding Co. (中信博, SSE STAR: 688408), Kunshan
profile: Cai Hao founded Arctech Solar in Kunshan in 2009 and built it into one of the world's top suppliers of single-axis solar trackers, fixed racking and BIPV systems. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020 and has 110+ GW installed globally. In 2026 he broke ground on a RMB 2bn+ 'global zero-carbon HQ' in Kunshan and is expanding into tracker-plus-storage microgrids.
interesting_fact: Arctech says it now ranks No. 2 globally by tracker market share. At the 2026 groundbreaking of its zero-carbon headquarters, Cai framed the strategy as 'tracking+' and 'green power+'.
deep_cut_fact: According to pv magazine's 10-year profile of Arctech, Cai got into solar after learning that PV projects depended heavily on steel for their racking structures at a time when China was promoting PV. The profile describes his management style as blending Western business methods with traditional Chinese philosophy.
notes: Low personal media profile, with little English-language coverage of him personally. The IR email is from a 2024 notice and may have changed. Arctech is active at Intersolar and SNEC, which could offer an in-person angle.

name: Hyuntae Kim
current_role: CEO (Corporate Management), Voronoi Inc. (Kosdaq: 310210), Incheon, South Korea
profile: Former securities-industry asset-management chief (eBest, Hanwha, KB Securities) who invested in and took over Voronoi, the precision-oncology biotech his younger brother Hyun-seok founded in 2015; he became CEO in 2016 and listed it on Kosdaq in 2022. Its AI-assisted platform produced cancer candidates VRN10 (HER2) and VRN11 (EGFR), both in Phase 1 since 2025.
interesting_fact: Voronoi's stock rose about 190% in 2025 on its AI-driven cancer pipeline, making Kim, who holds roughly 35%, one of South Korea's newest billionaires despite the company having minimal revenue.
deep_cut_fact: A finance man with no biotech background, he bet on his brother's startup in 2016 by buying 100,000 newly issued shares at 10,000 won each while Voronoi was still private; he holds business and MBA degrees from Seoul National University.
notes: Co-leads with R&D CEO Kim Dae-kwon; Hyuntae handles business side. Voronoi has a US subsidiary (Voronoi USA, President Jaeyoung Ahn) which may be an easier English-language route. IR@voronoi.io is the best published channel.

name: Wu Po Sum
current_role: Chairman & non-executive director, Central China Management Co. (HKEX: 9982); founder and director of Central China Real Estate (HKEX: 832)
profile: Wu Po Sum (Mandarin: Hu Baosen), b. ~1950 in Henan, founded Jianye/Central China Real Estate in Zhengzhou in 1992 after a decade in Hong Kong trade, building it into Henan's leading developer. He chairs asset-light spin-off Central China Management, holding 47.59% via Joy Bright Investments (end-2025), and controls insurer Central China New Life.
interesting_fact: Known as Henan's 'godfather of football': in 1994 he founded Henan Jianye FC, which kept the same name from the start of China's professional league until a 2021 rule change, and he vowed to fund Henan football 'until Jianye goes bankrupt'.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in English from Zhengzhou University in 1979, he joined the Henan branch of China Textiles Import & Export Corp., which sent him to Hong Kong in 1982 to set up a trading company - a decade of export work before he returned home to found Jianye.
notes: Usually reported in Chinese as Hu Baosen (胡葆森). Contacts are company IR (Central China Management), not personal. Group has been in debt restructuring since 2022-23; avoid the topic in outreach.

name: Meyer "Micky" Malka
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Ribbit Capital (Palo Alto); director of Robinhood Markets
profile: Venezuelan-born fintech investor who started and sold companies in Venezuela, co-founded Brazil's Banco Lemon (sold to Banco do Brasil) and mobile-payments firm Bling Nation/Lemon (sold to LifeLock, 2013), then founded Ribbit Capital in 2012. Ribbit was an early backer of Robinhood, Coinbase, Credit Karma and Nubank; Malka sits on Robinhood's board and Ribbit is a 10%+ holder of Root Inc.
interesting_fact: Ribbit's name comes from the sound a frog makes, meant to evoke 'leapfrogging' incumbent financial institutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he co-founded Heptagon Group, a brokerage serving Venezuelan and U.S. markets, and co-developed Patagon.com, later acquired by Banco Santander; he also co-founded Banco Bracce, a Brazilian lender to mid-sized companies.
notes: Holds an economics degree from Universidad Catolica Andres Bello (Caracas). Has appeared on the Founders podcast (David Senra) — a good sign he does long-form audio. Ribbit site lists no public email; best route likely via Ribbit or Robinhood corporate communications.

name: Wong Kwong Yu
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, GOME Retail Holdings (HKEX: 0493)
profile: Wong Kwong Yu (Huang Guangyu) founded GOME, which grew from a single Beijing stall into China's largest consumer-electronics retail chain and made him China's richest man in the mid-2000s. He was convicted in 2010 and paroled in 2020; since his release he has sought to revive GOME's retail and e-commerce business.
interesting_fact: Time named him China's richest man in 2005; he had started GOME as a teenager with his brother after moving to Beijing from Shantou.
deep_cut_fact: GOME's first outlet opened on 1 January 1987 in a rented ~100 sq m shop on Zhushikou Street near Qianmen in Beijing; the 'GOME' (Guomei, 'beautiful country') brand name was only adopted in 1993.
notes: Highly sensitive history (2010 conviction, parole 2020); GOME is financially distressed. A general address info@gome.com.hk appears only on third-party quote pages (etnet), not verified on company site. Born Zeng Junlie, 1969, Shantou.

name: Michael Mente
current_role: Co-founder, co-CEO and director, Revolve Group (NYSE: RVLV)
profile: Michael Mente co-founded Revolve with Mike Karanikolas in 2003 using about $50,000 of their savings; the LA-area online fashion retailer pioneered influencer marketing and went public in 2019. As co-CEO he oversees merchandising, brand and the customer experience, including owned brands and the Revolve Festival events.
interesting_fact: Neither founder had a fashion background — both came from a software startup (NextStrat). Mente: 'We don't have fashion backgrounds—we were in tech.' They were named 2015 EY Entrepreneurs of the Year (retail).
deep_cut_fact: Mente left USC's business program in 2000, a year early, to join enterprise-software firm NextStrat, where he met future co-founder Mike Karanikolas.
notes: IR contact listed in Revolve press releases (SVP IR Erik Randerson). Media contact in older releases was the agency Walker Drawas; not re-verified for 2026.

name: Boris Jordan
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Curaleaf Holdings (CEO since Aug 2024)
profile: Long Island-born son of Russian emigres who helped build Russia's post-Soviet capital markets in the 1990s (CSFB Moscow, co-founder of Renaissance Capital, Sputnik Group, ex-CEO of Gazprom Media). Back in the US, he invested in PalliaTech in 2014, which became Curaleaf, one of the largest US multi-state cannabis operators; he now runs it as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: In 1995 Businessweek profiled him as 'the man who made Moscow's market' for his role in launching Russia's stock market and voucher privatization while co-heading CSFB's Moscow operation in his mid-20s.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his NYU bachelor's degree in the niche field of Russian-American Economic Relations, and worked closely with Bruce Gardner of the Russian Center for Privatization in the early 1990s.
notes: Forbes bio says 'executive chairman'; 2026 SEC filings list him as Chairman and CEO. Curaleaf proposed redomiciling to Delaware in 2026.

name: Keiichi Shibahara
current_role: Representative Director and CEO, Amvis Holdings, Inc. (TSE Prime: 7071)
profile: Medical doctor turned immunology/molecular biology researcher who spent about 20 years in science before founding Amvis in 2013 (Kuwana, Mie) at age 48. Amvis runs 'Ishinkan' hospice-style nursing homes where nurses, not resident physicians, manage care for chronic and terminally ill patients; listed 2019, now on TSE Prime.
interesting_fact: The company name Amvis is coined from 'ambitious vision'. Its Ishinkan model relocated hospital beds into nurse-run facilities, starting with Ishinkan Nabari in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author (with Yasumasa Ishida, Yasutoshi Agata and Nobel laureate Tasuku Honjo) of the 1992 EMBO Journal paper that first described PD-1, the molecule behind today's immune checkpoint cancer drugs; his CEO message calls that his first research.
notes: No personal social accounts found. Best route is via Amvis corporate/IR. Graduated Tokai High School and Nagoya University School of Medicine; Kyoto University graduate studies (Honjo lab era).

name: Hamad Ali Al-Sagri
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, Leejam Sports Company (Fitness Time), Saudi Arabia
profile: Saudi entrepreneur (about 67) who cofounded Leejam Sports in 2008; it operates Fitness Time, the largest gym chain in Saudi Arabia/MENA, and listed on Tadawul in 2018. He holds roughly a 51-52% stake; 2024 revenue was about $400m. His holding company also invests in equities, private equity, real estate, manufacturing and oil refining.
interesting_fact: Leejam operates more than 130 swimming pools plus cycling studios, running tracks, basketball courts and football pitches; Investcorp bought a 25% stake in 2013 before the IPO.
notes: Low public profile in English-language media. Company also lists info@leejam.com.sa and investments@leejam.com.sa. His son chairs the board (do not approach via family). Forbes ME lists net worth ~$1.1bn (2025).

name: Roman Sokolov
current_role: Pre-IPO shareholder (~2%) of Eoptolink Technology (新易盛, 300502.SZ), Chengdu; no management role disclosed
profile: Roman Sokolov is a Russian-born, Chengdu-based shareholder of Eoptolink Technology, a top supplier of high-speed optical transceivers for AI data centers (customers reportedly include Google and Nvidia). He has held shares since before its 2016 Shenzhen IPO: 2.61% at end-2020, ~2.0% in 2024-2026. The AI optical-module boom made the stake worth roughly US$0.9-1bn (Forbes real-time).
interesting_fact: He is one of only a few non-founder individuals among Eoptolink's top-5 shareholders, alongside co-founders Gao Guangrong and Huang Xiaolei and Jeffrey Chih Lo. At IPO he signed the same undertakings on non-competition and related-party dealings as the founders and directors.
notes: Hurun 2025-2026: Roman Sokolov, born Russia, residence Chengdu; company 新易盛 / Eoptolink (Hurun 2026: RMB11.5bn). Forbes profile: self-made, married, Chengdu. Eoptolink filings list him as 'Sokolov Roman' / 'ROMAN SOKOLOV' but give no biography or role. His background (early investor? engineer? partner of a founder?) remains unknown. The IR email is the company's, not his. Strong data-center/AI angle for the podcast.

name: Ding Shui Po
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Xtep International Holdings (HKEX: 1368)
profile: Ding Shui Po founded Xtep in Fujian in 1999. It began as a manufacturer for international brands before building its own Xtep sportswear brand, and it now also runs Saucony and Merrell in China. He has more than 30 years in the sportswear industry and remains chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Xtep is a major Chinese running brand. Ding sits on the China Athletic Association's marathon committee (2015) and became a specially invited vice president of the association in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serial executive-education student: Peking U (2004), Tsinghua (2006), CKGSB (2011), CEIBS and Xiamen EMBA (2014), Harvard's Global CEO Program (2018), and CKGSB again in 2023. He was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year China in 2009.
notes: Best route is via Xtep investor relations / corporate communications (Hong Kong). Running/marathon angle could be a hook.

name: Roy Richardson
current_role: Life President, Richardson family business (Richardsons, West Midlands property)
profile: Roy Richardson (born c.1930) and his late twin Don founded a Black Country business in 1948, moving from used commercial vehicles into property; they turned the derelict Round Oak Steelworks site into the Merry Hill shopping centre in the 1980s. The family business, now run by his sons, invests in property; Roy is Life President.
interesting_fact: The twins bought 400 acres of the closed Round Oak Steelworks (shut 1982, an enterprise zone) and, inspired by US malls, built Merry Hill in eight phases by 1989, one of Europe's largest shopping centres.
deep_cut_fact: He and Don left school at 14 to work for their father selling used commercial vehicles, often post-war surplus, and did RAF national service together before starting in business in 1948. He was the first businessman made an Honorary Freeman of Sandwell (2018).
notes: Now in his 90s; day-to-day business is run by sons (Lee, Carl, Martyn). Twin Don died 2007. Sandwell freedom: https://www.expressandstar.com/business/standing-ovation-as-dr-roy-richardson-made-honorary-freeman-of-sandwell-with-video-6241724 ; alive status inferred from no death reports and 2025 Rich List coverage naming him head of family.

name: Rebecca Taub
current_role: Founder; Board Director and Senior Scientific & Medical Advisor (since April 2025), Madrigal Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: MDGL)
profile: Physician-scientist Rebecca 'Becky' Taub, M.D., taught genetics and medicine at the University of Pennsylvania, then led R&D at Bristol Myers Squibb and Roche (VP metabolic diseases) before co-founding Madrigal in 2011. As CEO, then CMO/President of R&D, she led development of Rezdiffra (resmetirom). In 2025 she stepped back to an advisor role and remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Under her leadership Madrigal developed Rezdiffra (resmetirom), the first FDA-approved medicine for MASH (fatty-liver disease with fibrosis); the company grew from fewer than 10 R&D staff in Conshohocken, PA to 500+ employees.
deep_cut_fact: At the University of Pennsylvania, where she taught genetics and medicine, she was one of the youngest women at that time to become a fully tenured professor.
notes: Wealth stems from MDGL stock. Goes by 'Becky'. Also reported as Industry Co-Chair of the Liver Forum (UC Berkeley) and a BriaCell Therapeutics director (unverified here). Route via Madrigal media team.

name: Zhu Yiwen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Hygeia Healthcare Holdings (HKEX: 6078)
profile: Zhu Yiwen, a neurosurgeon-turned-entrepreneur, founded Hygeia Healthcare in November 2009; it operates oncology-focused private hospitals and radiotherapy centres across China and listed in Hong Kong in 2020. He became chairman in 2021 and CEO, and he and concert parties have repeatedly added to their stake since listing.
interesting_fact: Hygeia's 2025 annual report says Zhu and parties acting in concert have never sold shares and have increased their holding 22 times since the IPO; he was named 'Wei Lan Award - Entrepreneur of the Year'.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Hygeia, Zhu directed the Gamma Knife Treatment Center at the Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University (1998-2004), then ran the tumour radiotherapy centre of the PLA's 455th Hospital until 2015. In 2025 he became vice chairman of a China Medical Foundation clinical-specialty expert committee.
notes: Hygeia has an active IR function (won New Fortune best-IR listing) - IR email is the best route. Healthcare rather than energy angle.

name: Gary E. Dickerson
current_role: President and CEO, Applied Materials (AMAT)
profile: Gary Dickerson has led Applied Materials, the world's largest semiconductor equipment maker, as CEO since 2013 after joining as president in 2012. He spent 18 years at KLA-Tencor (rising to president/COO) and seven years as CEO of Varian Semiconductor, which he sold to Applied for $4.9bn in 2011. His wealth is AMAT stock; Applied is now riding AI-driven chip demand.
interesting_fact: Under Dickerson Applied is investing up to $4bn in the EPIC Center in Silicon Valley, a collaborative R&D hub for chipmakers and universities; in Q3 FY2026 Applied posted record revenue of $9.12bn.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in manufacturing and engineering management at General Motors' Delco Electronics division and AT&T Technologies, after a B.S. in engineering management from the University of Missouri-Rolla; in 2024 Singapore awarded him its Public Service Star.
notes: Press releases list Ricky Gradwohl (editorial/media) and Mike Sullivan (financial community) as company contacts (phone only, no email found). Natural fit for a data-center/AI-chip episode; route via Applied corporate communications.

name: Sara Liu
current_role: Co-founder, Senior Vice President and Director, Super Micro Computer Inc. (Supermicro)
