profile: Sara Liu co-founded server and storage maker Supermicro with her husband, CEO Charles Liang, in San Jose in 1993; it went public in 2007 and is now a major supplier of AI/GPU server systems built around Nvidia chips for data centers. She remains a senior vice president and board director.
interesting_fact: Liu was Supermicro's treasurer from its founding in 1993 until 2019 and its chief administrative officer over the same period, effectively running the company's finances through its growth from startup to public AI-server giant.
deep_cut_fact: She holds a B.S. in accounting from Providence University in Taiwan, and also served as Supermicro's SVP of Operations from 2014 to early 2018.
notes: Very relevant to a data-center podcast but rarely gives interviews; husband Charles Liang is the public face. Route via Supermicro PR.

name: George Sakellaris
current_role: Founder, Chairman, President and CEO, Ameresco, Inc. (NYSE: AMRC), Framingham, MA
profile: Greek-born engineer George Sakellaris started at utility New England Electric System, ran energy-services firm Noresco (1989-2000), then founded Ameresco in 2000 and took it public in 2010. Ameresco develops energy-efficiency retrofits, renewable-gas, solar and battery-storage projects for governments, utilities and corporates, and he still runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: He was the first president of NAESCO, the National Association of Energy Service Companies, and helped advocate for the then-new energy-performance-contracting industry.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a small village outside Sparta, Greece, where a teacher told the math-gifted boy he must become either a teacher or an engineer; he chose engineering and came to the US to study EE at the University of Maine (Orono), later earning an MSEE and MBA at Northeastern.
notes: Ameresco media contact is Leila Dillon (news@ameresco.com); IR handled by AdvisIRy Partners (Eric Prouty). Received the Greek America Foundation's first Gabby Award (2009). Data-center angle: Ameresco does on-site power/microgrids.

name: Zhang Xuanning
current_role: Director (non-independent), Yonghui Superstores (SSE: 601933); former vice chairman
profile: Zhang Xuanning co-founded Fuzhou-based fresh-food chain Yonghui Superstores with his brother Zhang Xuansong and was long its vice chairman. In 2017-18 the brothers sold a 5% stake to Tencent. He was re-elected a director in Yonghui's March 2025 board overhaul, after Miniso founder Ye Guofu took a major stake.
interesting_fact: Yonghui pioneered Fuzhou's 'farmers' market to supermarket' (nong gai chao) model in 2001, the fresh-produce focus that drove its national expansion; in 2018 Tencent bought 5% of Yonghui from the brothers for about $648.6m.
deep_cut_fact: When Yonghui Supermarket Co. was registered in 2001, Zhang Xuanning put in RMB 400,000 of the RMB 1 million starting capital, alongside RMB 600,000 from his brother Zhang Xuansong.
notes: Very low public profile; the brothers ended their acting-in-concert agreement in 2018 over strategy differences (avoid in outreach). Route via Yonghui board office email.

name: Tung Ching Sai
current_role: Executive Director and CEO, Xinyi Glass Holdings (HKEX: 868); chairman of Xinyi Electric Storage; director at Xinyi Solar/Xinyi Energy
profile: Tung Ching Sai has been CEO of Hong Kong-listed Xinyi Glass, a maker of float, automotive and architectural glass whose customers include Ford, GM and VW, since 2004. He is the brother of vice-chairman Tung Ching Bor and brother-in-law of founder-chairman Lee Yin Yee; he also chairs the group's energy-storage arm.
interesting_fact: Beyond glass, he sits across the Xinyi group's clean-energy businesses (Xinyi Solar, Xinyi Energy) and chairs Xinyi Electric Storage, a natural fit for an energy-focused conversation.
deep_cut_fact: Xinyi Glass's own annual report styles him 'Tan Sri Datuk' Tung Ching Sai, i.e. he holds Malaysian honorific titles, unusual for a Hong Kong/mainland industrialist (Xinyi has major manufacturing in Malaysia).
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Route via Xinyi Glass company secretary / IR in Hong Kong. Energy angle: Xinyi Solar and Xinyi Electric Storage. Malaysian manufacturing link stated as general context, not individually verified.

name: Ke Yunfeng
current_role: Chairman, DaShenLin Pharmaceutical Group Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603233)
profile: Guangdong-born founder and chairman of DaShenLin, one of China's largest pharmacy chains. It opened its first store in 1999, listed in Shanghai in 2017, and now runs thousands of outlets with more than 23,000 employees. He controls the company with relatives Ke Jinlong and Ke Kangbao under a 2015 concert-party agreement and holds about 21% himself.
interesting_fact: DaShenLin opened its first store in 1999 and has grown to more than 4,000 pharmacies with over 23,000 employees.
deep_cut_fact: As a deputy to China's National People's Congress, he proposed at the 2020 'Two Sessions' that retail pharmacies be formally brought into the public-health emergency system, drawing on pharmacies' role during COVID-19.
notes: The IR email belongs to the board secretary (Peng Guangzhi) and is published in DaShenLin's periodic reports. Outreach would need to be in Chinese. Birth year (1967) and early career (Maoming audit bureau) come only from aggregator sites and are unverified.

name: Lu Shenglin
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong OPT Machine Vision Tech Co. (688686.SH), Dongguan (per third-party exec data; latest status unverified)
profile: Lu Shenglin, who holds a PhD in machinery manufacturing and automation, co-founded OPT in Dongguan in 2006 with his brother Lu Zhilin (now general manager). OPT makes machine-vision lighting, lenses, cameras and software for electronics and battery manufacturing and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He has been chairman and R&D director since May 2018.
interesting_fact: OPT has a global footprint unusual for a Chinese vision firm, with offices in Cupertino (California), Stuttgart, Tokyo, Penang, Bangkok and Vietnam.
notes: The Forbes bio says HQ is Wuxi, but the company's own site and filings put it in Dongguan, Guangdong. optmv@optmv.com is the company's general inbox (not IR-specific). Brothers Lu Shenglin and Lu Zhilin are joint actual controllers. Role source: https://www.lixinger.com/equity/company/detail/sh/688686/688686/senior-executive/shareholding-compensation

name: Lu Zhilin
current_role: Director and General Manager, Guangdong OPT Machine Vision Tech Co. (688686.SH)
profile: Lu Zhilin (卢治临, b. 1983) co-founded Dongguan-based OPT Machine Vision with his brother Lu Shenglin in 2006 and has run it as general manager; he was chairman 2016-2018. OPT makes light sources, lenses, cameras and vision software for factory automation (notably consumer-electronics and lithium-battery lines) and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding OPT he ran a small clothing shop, with only a junior-college (dazhuan) education.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded the business in 2006 as Dongguan OPT Automation Technology Co., Ltd. at about age 23, alongside his brother Dr. Lu Shenglin, who serves as chairman.
notes: Low public profile; company IR (board secretary Xu Xueliang) is the realistic route. Forbes bio spells name 'Luo Zhilin' in one line.

name: Liang Xiaolin
current_role: Shareholder of Dashenlin Pharmaceutical Group (SSE: 603233); wife of chairman Ke Yunfeng
profile: Liang Xiaolin is the wife of Ke Yunfeng, founder-chairman of Guangzhou-based Dashenlin (大参林), one of China's largest drugstore chains; Hurun lists the couple jointly. She holds about 9.8m Dashenlin shares directly; the family's wealth comes from the Ke brothers' controlling stake. No public executive role found for her.
interesting_fact: Dashenlin differentiates on ginseng and tonic herbal medicines ('参茸滋补') and runs 38 warehouses with an order-fill rate of 99% and error rate under 0.008%, per its 2024 annual report summary.
notes: Annual report confirms '梁小玲为柯云峰之妻'. Very low public profile; outreach should go through Dashenlin's board secretary/IR office (tel 020-81176091 published in same report).

name: Guo Junwei
profile: Guo Junwei (郭俊伟) is reported to be a brother of Kaisa Group founder Guo Yingcheng (Kwok Ying Shing); the Guo family co-founded the Shenzhen developer Kaisa in 1999. Reports say he transferred a 16.42% Kaisa stake held via the family trust to Guo Xiaoqun. He appeared on Hurun only 2009-2012; no current public role found.
interesting_fact: Kaisa, founded in Shenzhen in 1999 by the Guo brothers, grew into a Hong Kong-listed developer (HKEX: 1638) known for urban-renewal projects in Shenzhen.
notes: Very low public profile; little beyond family-trust shareholding reports. Kaisa has been in debt restructuring since 2021 (avoid as an angle). Not a good outreach target; any approach would have to go via Kaisa Group corporate channels.

name: Guo Yingzhi
current_role: Co-founder family member of Kaisa Group (Shenzhen); reported senior advisor to Kaisa since 2015 (current status unconfirmed)
profile: Guo Yingzhi (Kwok Ying Chi) is the younger brother of Kaisa Group founder Kwok Ying Shing; the Kwok brothers held Kaisa through a family trust. He was Kaisa vice-chairman and director 2009-2014, then a senior advisor, and served as chairman/CEO of NYSE-listed Shenzhen developer Nam Tai Property from Jan 2018 to Sept 2020.
interesting_fact: After leaving Kaisa's board he was put in charge of Nam Tai Property, a former electronics maker turned Shenzhen/Wuxi property developer in which Kaisa was the largest shareholder.
notes: Very low public profile; last on Hurun 2009-2012. No personal channels found. Kaisa has been in prolonged debt restructuring, so the company is a weak route. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source.

name: Deng Longjiang
current_role: Professor, UESTC School of Electronic Science and Engineering; CAE academician; actual controller of Chengdu Jiachi Electronic Technology (JC Technology, SSE STAR: 688708)
profile: Deng Longjiang (b. 1966, Anyue, Sichuan) is a UESTC materials scientist specialising in electromagnetic radiation-control (absorbing/shielding) materials. In 2008 he co-founded Chengdu Jiachi with fellow professors Xie Jianliang and Liang Difei to commercialise lab work; it listed on the STAR Market in Dec 2024. He stepped down as director/chief scientist in Feb 2024 but remains controller.
interesting_fact: Elected to the Chinese Academy of Engineering in 2021; his team's domestic high-permeability magnetic substrate for phone antennas, used by Huawei and Xiaomi, reportedly broke a foreign monopoly and cut material prices to about a tenth.
deep_cut_fact: In Nov 2026 he received Sichuan's 2025 Science and Technology Outstanding Contribution Award; a middle-school classmate recalled him as diligent and 'always the first one at school each day'. In July 2026 Jiachi's founders pledged 10 million shares to UESTC.
notes: Academic first, businessman second; company is defense-related (stealth/EM materials), so media access may be limited. Chairwoman Yao Yao runs the company day to day. Hurun lists the company as 'industrial coatings' (EM functional coatings).

name: Roger Federer
current_role: Retired tennis champion (20 Grand Slam singles titles); investor in On Holding; co-founder of Laver Cup/TEAM8; founder of the Federer Foundation
profile: Swiss tennis great who won 20 Grand Slam singles titles and more than $130m in prize money before retiring in 2022. His fortune came mostly from endorsements (Uniqlo's 10-year, $300m deal; Rolex; Mercedes) and an estimated ~3% stake in Swiss shoemaker On, which listed in 2021. He now focuses on investing, the Laver Cup with agent Tony Godsick's TEAM8, and his foundation.
interesting_fact: Federer was the world's highest-paid athlete in 2020, earning an estimated $106.3m pre-tax. Most of it came from endorsements, which at his peak brought in $100m a year off the court.
deep_cut_fact: Before winning a record 10 Swiss Indoors titles, Federer worked as a ball boy at the same Basel tournament in 1992-93. As champion he later threw a pizza party for the event's ball kids.

public_contacts.value: TEAM8 (his management company, co-founded with Tony Godsick): info@team8global.com
contact@federerfoundation.org (Federer Foundation; only for enquiries related to the foundation's work)

notes: Heavily managed. Media and business requests go through TEAM8 (Tony Godsick). The foundation states it accepts no unsolicited proposals or autograph requests. For an entrepreneurship angle, the On investment and TEAM8/Laver Cup are the natural hooks.

name: Morris S Young
current_role: Chairman (since Aug 2021) and CEO (since July 2009) of AXT, Inc. (Nasdaq: AXTI), Fremont, California
profile: Dr. Morris Young co-founded AXT in 1986. AXT makes indium phosphide, gallium arsenide and germanium substrate wafers, mostly in China via subsidiary Beijing Tongmei. He was president/CEO 1989-2004, returned as CEO in 2009 and became chairman in 2021. InP substrates for AI/data-center optical links have become AXT's key growth market.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2026 AXT's Beijing subsidiary Tongmei agreed a private equity raise of up to RMB 3.67bn (~US$545m) to expand indium phosphide substrate capacity, the material behind optical interconnects in AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding AXT, Young was a physicist at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (1985-89). He holds a B.S. in metallurgical engineering from National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan, an M.S. from Syracuse and a Ph.D. in metallurgy from Polytechnic University (now NYU Tandon).

public_contacts.value: Leslie Green, Green Communications Consulting, LLC - leslie@greencommunicationsllc.com (AXT investor relations)

notes: Highly relevant to the data-center theme because InP substrates go into AI optical transceivers. Best route is the IR agency (Leslie Green). The CFO line (510) 438-4700 is published in press releases.

name: Zhang Feng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang XCC Group (浙江五洲新春集团, SSE: 603667); controlling shareholder
profile: Zhang Feng (张峰, b. July 1963) built Xinchang-based XCC from a local bearing works into a listed maker of bearings, automotive components and precision parts with plants in Zhejiang, Anhui, Sichuan, Dalian and Mexico. XCC listed in Shanghai in 2016; he is controlling shareholder, chairman and GM, and the firm is now pushing into robot bearings and planetary roller screws for humanoid robots.
interesting_fact: XCC has moved into 'embodied-AI' hardware: its 2025 annual report lists planetary roller screws, ball screws and micro screws for humanoid robots alongside a full range of robot-specific bearings.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1981 as Communist Youth League secretary at the Xinchang Bearing General Factory, later served as deputy head of Xinchang's foreign-trade bureau (1992-98) before running Zhejiang Xinchun Bearing; he is vice chairman of the China Bearing Industry Association.
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via XCC filings (Forbes profile matches XCC). Route via board secretary Peng Yaohui's office (securities dept email above).

name: Jeffrey W Clarke
current_role: Vice Chairman and Chief Operating Officer, Dell Technologies
profile: Jeff Clarke is a Dell lifer who joined in 1987 and rose through engineering and product leadership to run Dell's day-to-day operations as Vice Chairman and COO. He leads the AI server push: in Q2 FY27 (reported Sept 2026) Dell booked a record $60.9B in AI server orders and exited with a ~$95B AI backlog. His wealth (~$950M) comes from Dell equity built over nearly four decades.
interesting_fact: In Dell's Q2 FY27 results he reported a record $60.9B of AI-server orders in a single quarter and a $95B backlog, making Dell one of the biggest builders of AI data-center infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Dell in 1987 as a quality engineer, after working as a reliability and product engineer at Motorola, and earned his electrical engineering degree in 1986 from UT San Antonio, where he serves on the College of Engineering advisory council.
notes: Frequent keynote speaker (Dell Technologies World) and blogger on Dell's site on AI infrastructure; good podcast fit for the data-center/AI theme. Route via Dell Media Relations.

name: Binaben Nimish Chudgar
current_role: Chudgar family shareholder in Intas Pharmaceuticals (Ahmedabad); no public executive role found
profile: Listed by Hurun India (2018-2019) as a wealth holder through Intas Pharmaceuticals, the Ahmedabad generics and biosimilars maker founded by Hasmukh Chudgar and run by his sons Binish, Nimish and Urmish. The name format indicates she is linked to Nimish Chudgar (Intas joint MD), but no public source describing her could be found.
interesting_fact: Intas, the family's company, is one of India's largest privately held drugmakers and owns UK/EU generics arm Accord Healthcare.
notes: Very private; no profile, interviews or roles found under 'Binaben'/'Bina' Chudgar. Relationship to Nimish Chudgar inferred only from name format - unverified. Only route is Intas corporate office (general queries).

name: Sun Hongjun
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Awinic Technology (艾为电子, SSE STAR: 688798)
profile: Sun Hongjun (age ~53, master's degree) founded Shanghai Awinic in 2008 and has run it since; the fabless designer of mixed-signal, audio amplifier, haptics, power-management and signal-chain chips listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in Aug 2021. Customers include Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo, Samsung, Microsoft, Meta, Amazon and Google; it is expanding into automotive, server and industrial chips.
interesting_fact: He spent five years (1997-2002) at Huawei as an engineer and technical deputy expert in its basic-business department before going into chip design; Awinic has since been named a national 'single champion' manufacturer in audio chips.
deep_cut_fact: Between Huawei and Awinic he was product director at Shanghai chip startup Qipai Microelectronics (启攀微电子) from 2002 to 2008, then left to found Awinic in 2008.
notes: Low media profile; securities/IR department (board secretary Yu Meiyi) is the formal route. Forbes listed him at $1.2B (Mar 2026).

name: Kimberly Jo Keywell
current_role: Philanthropist; Director of the Keywell Foundation. She files with the SEC as a >10% holder of Tempus AI (TEM) through Red Sky Ventures LLC.
profile: Kim Keywell is a Chicago-area philanthropist focused on underserved youth. SEC filings (Schedule 13G and Form 4, 2024-25) list Kimberly Jo Keywell and Red Sky Ventures LLC, with Chicago/Winnetka addresses, as a 10%+ owner of Tempus AI, the precision-medicine AI company co-founded by Eric Lefkofsky. Before philanthropy she spent 15 years as a money manager at a large international bank.
interesting_fact: Before turning to philanthropy, she spent 15 years managing individual corporate accounts and multiple mutual funds at a large international bank. She holds a BA from the University of Michigan and an MBA from Michigan State.
deep_cut_fact: Besides her board roles, she has volunteered as a CASA (Court Appointed Special Advocate) child advocate in Lake County, Illinois. She is vice chair of OneGoal, a college-persistence nonprofit, and has served on the boards of the Chicago Council on Global Affairs and the Jewish Women's Foundation of Metro Chicago.

public_contacts.value: media@tempus.com (Tempus AI newsroom; she is an investor, not an executive)

notes: Identity is likely but unconfirmed: SEC filer Kimberly Jo Keywell (Red Sky Ventures LLC, Chicago/Winnetka) matches Kim Keywell of the Keywell Foundation by name and location only. She is a private investor and philanthropist with no published contact. Best route is a warm intro via Chicago civic networks (Chicago Ideas, OneGoal).

name: Wang Shumin
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~36%) and actual controller of Beijing Bei Mo Gao Ke Friction Material (SZ:002985); chaired it until June 2025
profile: Wang Shumin (b. 1957) turned the Beijing Friction Material Factory, which she led from 2000, into Bei Mo Gao Ke (founded 2003), a maker of aircraft brake discs, brake-control systems, wheels and landing gear, listed in Shenzhen in 2020. She remains its controlling shareholder; Zhang Tianchuang succeeded her as chairman.
interesting_fact: Bei Mo Gao Ke was set up in 2003 with just RMB 3 million contributed by 31 key shareholders and core employees of the old state friction-material factory, including Wang.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering industry she worked in the construction-commission system of Beijing's Xicheng District; she has received a National May 1st Labour Medal and multiple science & technology awards for the company's braking technology.
notes: Low-profile; defence/aviation supplier. Board office (董办) email is the best route. Note: a different Wang Shumin (Shirley Wang) chairs Anji Microelectronics — not this person. Company switchboard 010-80725919 published on site.

name: Emre Tezmen
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder of Turkey's Tera group (Tera Yatırım Menkul Değerler, Tera Yatırım Bankası); reported in 2026 to have stepped down as chairman
profile: Turkish financier who trained in Brussels (ULB economics, VUB MBA) and worked in research and institutional sales from 1995 before founding Tera in 2005. He expanded via the Stok Menkul brokerage, factoring (2015) and portfolio management/IT (2020); Tera Yatırım listed on Borsa Istanbul in 2022 and its surge put him and his father on Forbes' 2026 billionaire list.
interesting_fact: The name 'Tera' comes from Terra, the Roman earth goddess symbolising fertility and prosperity; his office displays artefacts from ancient cultures, notably ancient Egypt.
deep_cut_fact: To start Tera in 2005 he sold his house and car, and later put all his savings into acquiring the brokerage Stok Menkul.
notes: Caution: Turkish media (Sept 2026) report he was detained and then arrested in an Istanbul prosecutor's investigation into Tera Portföy funds, with a travel ban; outreach is inadvisable for now. Sources: https://www.ntv.com.tr/ntvpara/emre-tezmen-gorevinden-ayrildi-1742392 . Tera websites were unreachable when checked.

name: Viscount Rothermere
current_role: Chairman, Daily Mail and General Trust (DMGT); Chairman, Imperial War Museum Foundation
profile: Jonathan Harmsworth, 4th Viscount Rothermere (b. 1967), is the fourth generation of the Harmsworth family to control DMGT, publisher of the Daily Mail, Mail on Sunday, Metro, the i and MailOnline. He became chairman on his father's death in 1998, took DMGT private in 2021-22, and in Nov 2025 agreed a ~GBP500m deal to buy the Telegraph, which drew a UK public-interest review in 2026.
interesting_fact: DMGT's 2022 delisting ended 90 years on the London Stock Exchange (since 1932); in Nov 2025 DMGT agreed to buy Telegraph Media Group from RedBird IMI at a GBP500m valuation, a deal the Culture Secretary referred for public-interest/competition review in Feb 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the Imperial War Museum Foundation, continuing a tradition set by his great-grandfather the 1st Viscount; the foundation, set up in 2009, raised funds for IWM London's GBP40m Foster + Partners-designed First World War Galleries, opened in 2014. Before succeeding, he studied history at Duke and ran the Evening Standard as MD in the early 1990s.

public_contacts.value: enquiries@dmgt.com (DMGT general enquiries, Northcliffe House, London)

notes: Rarely gives interviews; Telegraph deal status should be checked for latest regulatory outcome. Best route is DMGT corporate PR. Media-only background, little energy/data-centre angle beyond DMGT's past info businesses (e.g., Trepp, Landmark).

name: Marie-Hélène Peugeot-Roncoroni
current_role: Peugeot family shareholder; director and deputy CEO (directrice générale déléguée) of Établissements Peugeot Frères (family holding)
profile: Daughter of former Peugeot chairman Pierre Peugeot and a Sciences Po graduate, she began at an accounting firm before working in the family group in corporate finance, industrial relations and HR. She sat on PSA Peugeot Citroën's supervisory board (1999-2014, later vice-chair) and on Peugeot Invest's board until 2022; she holds her stake via EPF, which owns stakes in Stellantis, Forvia and Rothschild & Co.
interesting_fact: The Peugeot family started as a steel foundry in eastern France in 1810 and built its first steam-driven car in 1889; the company merged with Fiat Chrysler in 2021 to form Stellantis.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond the car business she has served on the board of ESSO (ExxonMobil's French subsidiary) and of cleaning/services group ONET, and sits on the board of trustees of the Institut Diderot think tank.
notes: Very private family shareholder with no personal public channels; best route is via Peugeot Invest / EPF. Exact current EPF title per aggregator profiles, not confirmed in an official filing.

name: James Peng
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Pony.ai (Nasdaq: PONY; also listed in Hong Kong)
profile: James Peng (Peng Jun) co-founded robotaxi company Pony.ai in late 2016 with fellow ex-Baidu engineer Tiancheng Lou, after 11 years at Google and Baidu, where he was chief architect of autonomous-driving R&D. Pony.ai listed on Nasdaq in Nov 2024 and later added a Hong Kong listing; it runs driverless robotaxi services in Chinese megacities such as Guangzhou, Beijing and Shenzhen and is mass-producing its Gen-7 robotaxis.
interesting_fact: Peng holds a Tsinghua undergraduate degree, an MS from the University at Buffalo and an engineering PhD from Stanford, and spent seven years at Google building back-end and front-end advertising systems before moving into self-driving.
deep_cut_fact: He was Baidu's first US-based AI hire: Baidu SVP Wang Jing invited him to start Baidu Research US, and he was promoted to chief architect for autonomous driving in 2015 before leaving at the end of 2016 to found Pony.ai.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center/AI podcast (autonomous driving compute). He speaks publicly fairly often (Fortune Mar 2026 interview). media@pony.ai appears in 2025 releases; recent releases list only ir@pony.ai. Fortune: https://fortune.com/2026/03/26/pony-ai-ceo-james-peng-china-robotaxi

name: Susumu Fujita
current_role: Representative Director & Chairman, CyberAgent, Inc. (since Dec 2025); also President of AbemaTV, Inc. and CEO of Zelvia (FC Machida Zelvia)
profile: Susumu Fujita (b. 1973, Sabae, Fukui) founded CyberAgent in 1998 as an internet-ad agency and took it public on TSE Mothers in 2000, aged 26. He built it into a media, ad-tech and games group including Cygames and the streaming service ABEMA. He handed the presidency to Takahiro Yamauchi in December 2025 and remains chairman and a minority shareholder.
interesting_fact: He is a top racehorse owner. His Forever Young became the first Japanese-bred and trained horse to win the Breeders' Cup Classic (2025) and the first to win back-to-back Saudi Cups (2026).
deep_cut_fact: Fujita is a serious mahjong player. He trained at Shoichi Sakurai's Jankikai as a student and once considered turning pro, and in December 2014 he won the Mahjong Saikyosen title, announcing it on his own blog. He later founded the M.League pro mahjong league.
notes: Very public founder: he writes the long-running blog 'Shibuya de hataraku shacho' and has authored about 10 books, including 'Confessions of a President Working in Shibuya' (2005). Good angles are AI/ad-tech and ABEMA. CyberAgent also runs its own LLM and AI research lab.

name: Nikhil Merchant
current_role: Managing Director, Swan Corp Ltd (formerly Swan Energy); Chairman & Managing Director, Swan Defence and Heavy Industries (ex-Pipavav/Reliance Naval shipyard)
profile: Took control of century-old textile firm Swan Mills in the early 1990s and built it into Swan Energy (now Swan Corp): LNG infrastructure, petrochemicals trading, textiles and realty. Swan won Anil Ambani's bankrupt Reliance Naval shipyard at Pipavav, relaunched as SDHI, which now has tanker and ammonia-fuelled carrier orders.
interesting_fact: Swan's Jafrabad LNG project in Gujarat was conceived as India's first jetty-moored FSRU (floating storage and regasification unit) terminal; Swan revived the Pipavav yard from ~350 to ~1,000 staff and tied up with Samsung Heavy Industries.
notes: Low media profile; SDHI director Vivek Merchant is the group's main media voice on the shipyard. Past press coverage (The Wire, 2018) centred on political allegations he denied; avoid. Company now named Swan Corp Limited.

name: Marciano Testa
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (chairman) of Agi / Agibank (NYSE: AGBK), Brazil
profile: Testa was born to a family of Italian immigrants in Rio Grande do Sul. In 1999, while still a college student, he started Agiplan as a credit distributor. It became a financeira in 2011 and a bank in 2016, when he bought Banco Gerador. Agibank serves underbanked Brazilians through a digital bank and in-person 'Smart Hubs'. It listed on the NYSE in February 2026, and he owns nearly two-thirds of it.
interesting_fact: He calls himself an 'empreendedor raiz' (grassroots entrepreneur). He began as a door-to-door 'vendedor pastinha' (briefcase salesman), selling credit to low-income people and retirees, and became a billionaire when Agibank listed on the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: He started working at 8 to help his family. He opened his first business at 16 and sold it at 19, and calls that his 'primeiro MBA da vida real' (first real-life MBA). On legacy, he said he would like to be remembered as 'uma pessoa que transformou a própria história' (a person who transformed his own story).
notes: Glauber Correa has been Agi's CEO since 2021, and Testa sits on the board. Forbes' bio calls Testa 'founder, chairman and CEO', so his exact current title should be checked against the F-1 or 20-F. Some reports say he lives in the US. Press releases have also listed the agency address agibank@fsb.com.br as a press contact.

name: Cai Rongjun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, OFILM Group (欧菲光, SZSE: 002456)
profile: Cai Rongjun (蔡荣军), born 1972 in rural Jieyang, Guangdong, founded Shenzhen O-film in 2002, a maker of camera modules, touch panels and optical components listed in Shenzhen in 2010. After losing Apple business in 2020, OFILM pivoted to Chinese smartphone makers and automotive optics/smart-car components; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: OFILM was once one of Apple's key camera-module and touch-panel suppliers; after Apple dropped it in 2020 the company rebuilt around Huawei and other Chinese phone brands and in-car camera/lidar modules.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Shantou University in 1995 he worked a few months at a Guangzhou telephone factory, then joined Kodak repairing equipment on a then-princely salary of 10,000+ yuan a month; he has said that if Kodak hadn't declined he might still be working there instead of founding OFILM.
notes: Board secretary Zhou Liang (周亮) is the formal IR contact. Cai earned a DBA from the University of Minnesota in 2024 (per company filings).

name: Shou Bonian
current_role: Retired co-founder of Greentown China (former CEO and executive vice chairman); no current executive role found
profile: Shou Bainian (寿柏年, b. 1954) co-founded Hangzhou developer Greentown with Song Weiping, joining in 1998 and serving as executive vice chairman and CEO through the 2006 HK listing and CCCG's 2015 entry. He stepped down as CEO in 2015 and in 2018 sold his entire 8.1% stake (~US$269m) and retired from the board.
interesting_fact: In January 2018 he sold all 174.5m Greentown shares at HK$12.08 each (about US$269m), ending a near-20-year partnership with co-founder Song Weiping.
deep_cut_fact: A history graduate of Hangzhou University (1982), he spent 16 years in government and state roles - Yin County government office, Ningbo municipal general office and China Huaneng's Zhejiang subsidiary - before joining Greentown in April 1998.
notes: Name usually romanized Shou Bainian. Retired and low-profile since 2018; held shares via Profitwise Limited. No published personal contact; Greentown IR is not his office. Alive status inferred from continued Hurun listing (2026) and no death reports.

name: Wu Dongcai
current_role: Founder of Jiangsu Yonggang Group (Zhangjiagang steel); long-time Party secretary of Yonglian village (served ~35 years from 1978)
profile: Wu Dongcai (吴栋材, b.1936, Zhangjiagang) was a 1950s army veteran sent in 1978 to lead impoverished Yonglian village. He started a series of small village factories, then in 1984 the Yonglian steel-rolling mill that grew into Yonggang Group – now under Yongzhuo Holdings, ~10m tonnes of steel a year – making Yonglian one of China's richest villages. Successor as village chief: Wu Huifang.
interesting_fact: Yonglian's sales reached RMB40.3bn in 2017, mainly from Yonggang steel; a sculpture at the village entrance commemorates Wu Dongcai.
deep_cut_fact: Before steel he started eight small village factories – a fish farm, furniture, precast cement slabs, terrazzo, bathtubs and jade processing – and the 1984 rolling mill was his ninth venture.
notes: Would be ~90 in 2026; no death report found, and zh.wikipedia still categorises him as living, but status unverified. Last on Hurun list 2013 – likely retired. A collective/village-owned business; no personal channel found. CCTV 2013 profile: https://www.12371.cn/2013/04/11/VIDE1365680760853291.shtml

profile: Su Zhuangqi (苏壮奇) is a member of the Su family that controls Lianmei Group and its Shenyang-based listed arm Lianmei Quantum (formerly Lianmei Holding), a clean district-heating and integrated energy utility that also runs high-speed-rail digital media advertising. name: Zhou Ming
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder & Chairman, MaxOne Semiconductor (强一半导体/强一股份, SSE STAR: 688809), Suzhou
profile: Zhou Ming (周明) has 20+ years in semiconductors and founded MaxOne Semiconductor in Suzhou in August 2015 to make probe cards for wafer testing, moving from cantilever to vertical and MEMS probe cards. Backed by Huawei's Hubble and others, MaxOne became the only Chinese firm in the global top 10 probe-card makers and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market on 30 Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: MaxOne rose to No.6 globally in probe cards in 2024 as the only Chinese supplier in the top 10; Huawei's investment arm Hubble holds about 6.4%.

current_role: Shareholder (~10.86%), MaxOne/Qiangyi Semiconductor (强一股份, STAR Market 688809); no management role
profile: Holds ~10.86% of Qiangyi Semiconductor (Suzhou), China's first listed probe-card maker (chip wafer testing), founded 2015 by Zhou Ming and listed on the STAR Market in Dec 2025. Her shares (~RMB 6B in July 2026) came via transfer from Zhou Ming. She holds no position, votes with him under a 10-year pact, and is locked up until end-2028.

notes: Sensitive: her stake comes from a July 2026 divorce share split with founder Zhou Ming, so do not reference it in outreach. Per the filing she has no company role and no public profile. Founder Zhou Ming is the more relevant podcast guest. Not a good outreach target.

name: Li Weicheng
current_role: Major shareholder (approx. 7-8%) of Raytron Technology (睿创微纳, SSE STAR: 688002); director until the Dec 2025 board re-election
profile: Li Weicheng (李维诚) is an early backer and one of the largest individual shareholders of Raytron Technology, a Yantai, Shandong maker of uncooled infrared thermal-imaging chips founded in 2009 by Ma Hong and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019 among its first batch. He held about 9.2% before selling part of his stake in 2025, and served as a director; he was not named to the board elected in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Raytron, in which he is a top shareholder, designs infrared, microwave and laser sensing chips used in thermal cameras, automotive driver-assist and AI devices; it was among the first 25 companies to list on the STAR Market in July 2019.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal biography found in filings searched. Filings name him and his wife Shi Yun (石筠) as acting-in-concert holders. Not an executive, so the company IR route is indirect. Hurun lists him for 2019-2026.

name: He Donghan
current_role: Unknown; Hurun listed him (2017-2018) under Baota Petrochemical (宝塔石化), Yinchuan, Ningxia
profile: He Donghan (何东翰) is listed by Hurun China 2017 (RMB5000m) and 2018 (RMB6500m) with Baota Petrochemical Group (宝塔石化集团), a Yinchuan-based private refiner with ~200 fuel stations that also ran Yinchuan University (hence 'petrochemicals, education'). name: Ye Huodong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Longyan Zhuoyue New Energy (SH STAR:688196)
profile: Fujian entrepreneur who founded Longyan Zhuoyue New Energy in 2001 to make biodiesel, plasticizers and glycerin from waste cooking oil ('gutter oil'). It listed on the STAR Market in 2019 and is China's biggest biodiesel producer and exporter, with about 500,000 t/yr capacity. Ye controls it with his family.
interesting_fact: Zhuoyue was China's first company to make biodiesel from waste oils at industrial scale. It is now the country's biggest biodiesel producer and exporter, with about 500,000 t/yr of biodiesel and 140,000 t/yr of bio-based materials capacity.
deep_cut_fact: Well before the STAR listing, he chaired China Biodiesel International in 2008 while it expanded a Xiamen plant to double output. He said then that the company was 'delighted to report strong progress' despite industry-wide headwinds.
notes: Low media profile. The IR email is the company's published investor contact (2025 interim report). Good fit for a SAF/biofuels episode.

name: Chen Longji
current_role: Chairman, Regal International / Lijia Industrial (Fujian) Group (利嘉实业(福建)集团); Hong Kong-based, oil exploration & trading interests
profile: Chen Longji (陈隆基, b. 1956, Fuqing, Fujian) built the Lijia (利嘉, 'Regal') group in property and commerce (e.g. Fuzhou's Dalijia City market) and controlled several Shanghai-listed shells, including Lijia (Shanghai)/Duolun and Zhenghe. Around 2013 he sold out of Zhenghe and moved into oil and gas exploration and oil trading. Hurun listed him with his wife Wang Huayu (2008-2021).
interesting_fact: In 2013 he sold control of Zhenghe Industrial for about RMB3.5bn and put around RMB2.4bn into oil and gas exploration and production, reorienting his group toward energy.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a doctor: chief physician and vice-president of the Fuqing Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine in Fujian. He later became a visiting professor at Fujian Agriculture and Forestry University and vice-president of the Fujian International Chamber of Commerce.
notes: Hurun API: 陈隆基, b. 1956, born Fuzhou, Fujian (Sina gives 籍贯 Shanghai), residence Hong Kong; with wife 王华玉 (relation 夫妇); company 利嘉国际 / Regal International, 'oil exploitation, oil trading' (2015-2021). Note: 2013 Chinese press covered disputes over his past listed-company dealings (Duolun/Zhenghe), so be careful. No contacts or current activity found.

profile: Wang Huayu (王华玉) is the wife of Fujian-born, Hong Kong-based entrepreneur Chen Longji. Hurun listed them jointly (2014-2021) for Regal International (利嘉国际), whose interests moved from property and listed-company stakes into oil and gas exploration and oil trading around 2013. name: Tian Xiuying
current_role: Major individual shareholder (third-largest, ~9% in Nov 2024) of Inner Mongolia Junzheng Energy & Chemical Group (君正集团, SSE: 601216); no executive role found
profile: Long-term passive investor in Junzheng Group, a Wuhai, Inner Mongolia-based energy-chemical company founded in 2003 (PVC, caustic soda, calcium carbide, chemical logistics). She had held the stock for about 17 years and owned 766 million shares (9.08%) when, aged 78, she filed in Nov 2024 to sell up to 3%. Appeared on the Hurun China list 2015-2021.

notes: Very private, elderly (about 80) shareholder with no public profile or interviews; probably a poor podcast fit. The company is run by Du Jiangtao (largest shareholder). Any approach would go through Junzheng's board secretary/IR office.

name: Jiiang Yuan
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, PNC Process Systems Co. (Zhichun Technology, 603690.SH), Shanghai
profile: Jiang Yuan (蒋渊) founded Shanghai-based PNC Process Systems (至纯科技) in 2000 as an ultra-high-purity gas and chemical systems integrator for chip fabs, and grew it into a 'process-equipment-materials' supplier making wet-process semiconductor tools and running bulk-gas plants. She holds about 21% of the company and still chairs it.
interesting_fact: In 2022 PNC brought online what it calls China's first fully domestically built bulk-gas supply plant for a 12-inch, 28nm wafer fab, breaking foreign suppliers' hold on semiconductor-grade bulk gas.
deep_cut_fact: She describes China's chip industry when she founded PNC as 'like a desert' and her strategy as tree-planting: deep technical roots, then nurturing an 'ecological forest' of partners. She also caps PNC's debt ratio in a deliberate 50-65% band.
notes: Input name is a typo of Jiang Yuan; 'PNC' = PNC Process Systems (至纯科技). One of few female founder-chairs in China's semiconductor equipment sector; gives occasional interviews to Chinese financial press (China Securities Journal, Nov 2025). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Chen Ning
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Shenzhen Intellifusion Technologies (SSE STAR: 688343)
profile: Semiconductor veteran Chen Ning founded Shenzhen Intellifusion in 2014 with a team of US-returned PhDs; it designs AI inference chips that run pre-trained models on new inputs, plus vision/edge AI products. He took it public on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023 and in April 2026 it filed for a dual listing in Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Intellifusion bets on inference rather than training: its chips execute already-trained AI models, a segment Chen argues will dominate compute demand as AI deploys at scale.
deep_cut_fact: A Handan, Hebei native, he graduated from Shanghai Jiao Tong University's School of Electronic Information and Electrical Engineering in 1997 and earned an EE PhD at Georgia Tech in 2006; in 2014 he received Guangdong's Youth May Fourth Medal.
notes: No personal or published press contact found; company site intellif.com. Deep-cut source is a user-contributed Chinese bio page; Georgia Tech 2006 PhD is corroborated by marketscreener insider profile.

name: Zhou Weijian

profile: Zhou Weijian (周伟建; listed as 'Zhou Wweijian') chairs Maydos, a Shunde, Foshan-based paint and coatings maker founded in 1997 that sells decorative, art and stone-effect paints, adhesives and boards through ~12,000 franchise stores. UK-educated (master's), he also holds many civic posts, including Guangdong CPPCC member and vice chair of the Guangdong Paint Industry Association.
interesting_fact: Maydos says it has ~12,000 branded stores, 50,000 sales outlets and sells into 112 countries and regions.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999, two years after founding, Maydos won the tender to supply the full renovation of Beijing's Great Hall of the People for the PRC's 50th anniversary; in 1998 NPC vice-chair Wang Guangying visited and wrote the factory's name calligraphy.
notes: Name in input misspelled (Wwei-); correct Chinese is 周伟建 (not 周伟健). Private company, no IR channel; only route is corporate contact page. Also director of Meidi real-estate entities.

profile: Lin Lin (林林, b. 1973) is an early SG Micro insider and significant shareholder (~23.7m shares directly) in the Beijing analog/mixed-signal chip designer founded and controlled by Zhang Shilong. He was deputy GM of the predecessor Harbin SG Micro and handled administration at the early company, and has sat on SG Micro's board since 2012.

notes: Very low profile: non-executive director with no public interviews found; the company face is founder/chairman Zhang Shilong. IR email is from the 2022 annual report summary (2023) - verify in latest report. Investor Q&A also via SZSE 'Hudongyi' platform.

name: Yang Lijuan
current_role: Senior executive at Haidilao International Holding (since Apr 2026), leading its 'Red Pomegranate' multi-brand incubation plan; previously CEO of Super Hi International (Jul 2024-Apr 2026)
profile: Co-founding employee of hot-pot chain Haidilao who started as a teenage server in the 1990s and rose to COO, then group CEO (2022-24), where she led the 'Woodpecker Plan' turnaround. She ran overseas arm Super Hi (Nasdaq/HKEX) from 2024 and returned to Haidilao in April 2026 to drive new-brand growth. Holds ~3.7% of Haidilao.
interesting_fact: As Haidilao CEO she led the 'Woodpecker Plan' from late 2021, closing ~300 underperforming stores; the company swung back to profit in 2022 and earned about RMB 4.5bn net profit in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: She joined Haidilao before age 20 as a front-line server on 160 yuan a month, earning the nickname 'the most amazing server' and being promoted roughly every six months; she later led the chain's first overseas openings in Singapore and the US (2012-13).
notes: Also romanized Yang Lijuan / June Yang; some Chinese media write 杨丽娟. Li Yu succeeded her as Super Hi CEO in April 2026. Route via Haidilao media/IR.

name: Ruan Hongxian
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Yixintang Pharmaceutical Group (一心堂, SZ:002727)
profile: Born 1966 in Mile, Yunnan, Ruan started trading medicinal herbs as a teenager, set up the Hongxiang herb-buying station in 1981, and founded the Yixintang drugstore chain (company formed 2000, first store 2001). Yixintang listed in Shenzhen in 2014 and now runs ~11,000 directly operated pharmacies across 10 provinces; with his daughters he controls ~31% of the company.
interesting_fact: Yixintang was the first directly operated drugstore chain to list on China's A-share market (Shenzhen, 2014); it has 11,000+ stores and 53m+ members. Ruan was also a torchbearer for the 2008 Beijing Olympics.
deep_cut_fact: His start: in 1980, on a trip from Mile to Kunming to sell sugarcane, he spotted a herb-buying notice, borrowed 40 kg of honeysuckle (jinyinhua) from his father, and made his first 100 yuan on the price gap; he says a childhood friend's death for lack of an 8-fen remedy drove him into medicine.
notes: Deep-cut source is a Chinese brand-profile aggregator (cnpp.cn) repeating the company's founding story; treat as company lore. Best route is the board secretary's office via the IR email (listed in the 2025 annual report summary, April 2026). Not an energy figure.

name: Candido Pinheiro Koren de Lima Junior
current_role: Board member, Hapvida Participações e Investimentos (Hapvida NotreDame Intermédica); coordinator of its Commercial Committee
profile: Younger son of Hapvida founder Candido Pinheiro, he was Hapvida's sales and relationship vice president from 2001 to 2021 and sits on the board of the Fortaleza-based health insurer/hospital group, which IPO'd in 2018 and merged with NotreDame Intermédica in 2022. Re-elected to the board in April 2026 (term to the 2028 AGM); also on the innovation, quality-of-care and finance committees.
interesting_fact: Hapvida, founded by his oncologist father in Fortaleza, combined with NotreDame Intermédica to create Brazil's largest health-plan operator; the Pinheiro family remains the controlling shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Business Administration at the State University of Ceará (UECE) and led Hapvida's sales and relationship function for two decades (2001-2021); he now coordinates the board's Commercial Committee.
notes: Low-profile family member; brother Jorge Pinheiro is the public face (CEO transitioning to chair, with CFO Luccas Adib named incoming CEO). Approach via Hapvida corporate channels.

name: Michael Kors
current_role: Honorary Chairman and Chief Creative Officer, Michael Kors (brand of Capri Holdings)
profile: New York-born fashion designer who launched his womenswear line in 1981 at Bergdorf Goodman and built it into a global accessible-luxury brand; the company IPO'd in 2011 and became Capri Holdings (also owner of Jimmy Choo). He was creative director of Celine (1997-2004) and a Project Runway judge, and still leads design for his namesake brand.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Watch Hunger Stop with the UN World Food Programme in 2013, funding school meals worldwide; he is also a longtime board member of NYC meals charity God's Love We Deliver.
deep_cut_fact: After dropping out of FIT after nine months, his first job was at Lothar's, a boutique on West 57th Street, where he went from salesman to designer and window dresser; Bergdorf Goodman's Dawn Mello spotted him while he was merchandising the windows, leading to his 1981 Bergdorf debut.
notes: Fashion figure rather than energy/tech; best route is Capri Holdings press office. Instagram @michaelkors is the brand account, not personal.

name: Jorge Pinheiro Koren de Lima
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Hapvida (Hapvida NotreDame Intermédica); stepped down as CEO in 2026 after ~25 years, succeeded by Luccas Adib
profile: Fortaleza-born physician (Federal University of Ceará), elder son of oncologist Candido Pinheiro, who founded Hapvida. He ran Hapvida as CEO from 2001, taking it public in 2018 and merging it with NotreDame Intermédica into one of Brazil's largest vertically integrated health insurers. In 2026 he handed the CEO role to CFO Luccas Adib and became board chairman.
interesting_fact: Hapvida's vertical model pairs health insurance with its own hospitals and clinics. At its 2018 IPO it had 47 hospitals and nearly 200 clinics, and the 2022 NotreDame Intermédica merger made it a national giant.
notes: CEO succession was announced Dec 2025 and took effect around Apr 30, 2026 (suno.com.br, brapi.dev). Sources differ on the founding year: Forbes says 1986, others say 1979 (Hospital Antônio Prudente, Fortaleza). Low public profile; IR form is the main route. No sourced personal deep-cut found.

name: Thomas Patterson
current_role: General Partner/managing member, Madrone Capital Partners (Denver); Director, StubHub Holdings (NYSE: STUB) since Sept 2025
profile: Thomas A. Patterson, 60, has been a general partner at Madrone Capital Partners since 2005, investing in founder/family-owned businesses, emerging-market middle-class plays and technology; earlier he was at Weston Presidio (1995-2004) and McKinsey. He joined StubHub's board at its September 2025 IPO and also sits on Castleton Commodities and Teya boards.

deep_cut_fact: A Harvard history graduate (AB, plus HBS MBA), he is active in environmental conservation and chairs the Stanford Natural Capital Alliance Advisory Council. He also sat on StoneCo's board 2018-2022, a Brazilian fintech, and on Castleton Commodities, an energy trader, which is relevant to an energy podcast.
notes: The ~$913M SEC-derived net worth is almost certainly Madrone fund holdings (Walton/Penner-linked vehicle), not his personal wealth, since he disclaims beneficial ownership. Madrone keeps a low profile and has no public contact found; StubHub IR is the only published route.

name: Zhou Yifeng
current_role: Chairwoman, Oriental Energy Co. Ltd. (东华能源, SZSE: 002221); director & GM, Fuji Investment (Group)
profile: Zhou Yifeng (b. July 1978) chairs Oriental Energy, a Nanjing-based LPG importer turned propane-dehydrogenation (PDH) and polypropylene producer with bases in Zhangjiagang, Ningbo and Maoming that also sells by-product hydrogen. She and her husband Wang Mingxiang are joint controlling shareholders (~20.5% and ~20.1%). She was re-elected chair in August 2025 for a term to 2028.

deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a petrochemicals chief, she originally graduated from Beijing University of Chinese Medicine before earning a master's from Nanjing University of Science and Technology.
