name: Zhang Jindong
current_role: Founder and honorary chairman, Suning.com (stepped down as chairman July 2021); chairman of private parent Suning Holdings Group
profile: Nanjing literature graduate (b. 1963, Tianchang, Anhui) who opened a single air-conditioner shop in Nanjing in December 1990 and built Suning into one of China's largest appliance and e-commerce retailers, later buying 70% of Inter Milan (2016). After a 2021 state-led bailout he became honorary chairman; reports in 2024 said he was again steering the retailer's turnaround.
interesting_fact: He started Suning on 26 Dec 1990 with 100,000 yuan of his own money, renting a 200 sq m storefront on Ninghai Road, Nanjing, that sold only air conditioners.
deep_cut_fact: Because the first shop opened in winter, he pushed the units' heating mode with the slogan 'Buy a heating air conditioner and have a cozy New Year' (买一台取暖空调，舒舒服服过个年). Before that he had worked at the Gulou District Industrial Company after studying Chinese at Nanjing Normal University (1984).
notes: Lost control of Suning.com in the 2021 bailout (Suning's finances and Inter Milan sale are sensitive; avoid). Contacts are Suning.com's securities/IR office, not personal. Brother Zhang Guiping (Suning Universal) is a separate billionaire.

name: Li Denghai
current_role: Founder and Honorary Chairman, Shandong Denghai Seeds (SZSE 002041); chairman since 2025 is Tang Shiwei
profile: Li Denghai, a farmer's son from Laizhou, Shandong, is known as the 'father of compact hybrid corn' in China. He founded Houdeng Agricultural Experiment Station in 1985 (China's first private corn-seed enterprise), which became Denghai Seeds, listed in Shenzhen in 2005. In his late 70s he remains active as founder/honorary chairman.
interesting_fact: He set China's summer-corn yield record seven times and the world record twice, including 1,402.86 kg per mu with 'Denghai Chaoshi No.1' in 2005; his compact hybrids once covered ~43% of China's corn acreage. He and Yuan Longping are dubbed 'Southern Yuan, Northern Li'.
deep_cut_fact: After junior high in 1966 he went back to farm in Houdeng Village; at 23 (1972) he became head of the village agricultural-science team, and from 1978 spent winters breeding in Sanya, Hainan to squeeze two generations a year out of his corn lines.
notes: Emails are the company's board-office (dmb) and general mailbox as listed in the 2025 annual report. Attended the Feb 2025 private-enterprise symposium in Beijing. Agriculture rather than energy/data centers; likely Chinese-language interview only.

name: Qin Long
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and controlling shareholder (~43%), Qingdao Sentury Tire Co. (SZSE: 002984)
profile: Qin Long founded Qingdao Sentury Tire in 2007, building it from a manual tire plant in Qingdao into a listed maker of passenger, motorsport and aircraft tires with factories in Qingdao, Thailand and elsewhere. Sentury listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2020; he directly and indirectly controls about 43% of the company.
interesting_fact: Sentury is one of the few Chinese firms making aircraft tires, alongside motorsport tires, and it pursued an overseas-factory strategy with a heavily automated plant in Rayong, Thailand.
deep_cut_fact: Qin was reportedly the only one in his management team backing a fully automated 'Dream Factory'; after automating Qingdao's green-tire handling (utilisation rose from 72% to 96.5%) he copied it to Thailand. Quote: 'I have orders and I will lose the customers if I cannot deliver the tires.'
notes: IR email belongs to the board secretary's office (board secretary Wang Qian). Chairman title last explicitly confirmed in 2025 filings; 2026 interim report lists him as legal representative and controller. Cimcorp source is a vendor case study.

name: Chen Yin
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Greenworks (Jiangsu) Co. (SZSE: 301260)
profile: Chen Yin founded Greenworks (Globe Tools) in Changzhou in 2002; it makes battery-powered lawn, garden and DIY tools sold under Greenworks and other brands, with factories in China, the U.S. and Vietnam. It listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in February 2023; Chen controls a majority stake and still runs the company as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Chen is an outspoken advocate of replacing gas-powered outdoor equipment with batteries, arguing operators spend about $4 on electricity for every $100 they would spend on fuel; Greenworks launched its first lithium-ion string trimmer in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Chen was named EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2016 China in the industrial products category. He studied engineering at Donghua University (formerly China Textile University) and earned an MBA at Warwick.
notes: IR email is from the 2024 interim report; the board secretary is now Li Yirui (per May 2026 earnings-call record). Chen gives occasional English-language trade-press interviews, so US Greenworks PR is a possible route.

name: Wang Yu
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Guangzhou Ruoyuchen Technology (Ruoyuchen, SZSE: 003010)
profile: Born 1985, Wang Yu co-founded Ruoyuchen in Guangzhou in 2011 with his wife Wang Wenhui; it began as a Tmall/e-commerce operations agency and listed on Shenzhen in 2020 as China's 'first e-commerce agency stock'. It has pivoted to its own brands (laundry brand Zhanjia, supplements Feicui/Nuoyibei) and has pursued a Hong Kong (A+H) listing.
interesting_fact: After Ruoyuchen's share price surged in 2025, he told an interviewer the rally left him unable to sleep ('睡不着了'); the founding couple control about 43% of the company.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2021 interview he described entrepreneurship as 'a technical craft and a prolonged battle' (创业是一门技术活，更是一个持久战) and said 'the most important asset of a startup is people.'
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via Ruoyuchen. Best route is the company board-secretary/IR office.

name: Wang Mingxiang
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of Oriental Energy Co. (东华能源, SZSE: 002221) via Mason Enterprise / Oriental Petroleum (Yangtze) / Unico Yangtze holding companies (director of those holdcos as of 2016 filing)
profile: Nanjing-based businessman (born 1962) who, with his wife Zhou Yifeng (chairwoman), is the actual controller of Oriental Energy, a Jiangsu-based LPG importer/trader and propane-dehydrogenation (PDH) polypropylene producer. Their wealth comes from holding companies with about 44% of the listed company combined. He is not an executive and keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: A 2016 exchange filing shows the couple restructuring their holding companies so that Wang went from 40% to 65% of Mason Enterprise, the vehicle that controls Oriental Energy; they file as 'persons acting in concert'.
notes: Hurun pairs him with Zhou Yifeng (his wife), Oriental Energy's chair. Practically no public profile and no recent news, so 'alive' is unconfirmed. Oriental Energy reported a large 2025 loss and was publicly reprimanded by the SZSE in 2026, so not an obvious outreach target. Only route is the listed company's IR mailbox.

name: Ding Shuibo
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Xtep International Holdings (HKEX: 1368)
profile: Ding Shui Po (丁水波), 55, from Chendai, Jinjiang (Fujian), started in shoemaking in 1987, grew an OEM sports-shoe export business, then founded the group behind the Xtep brand in 1999 and listed it in Hong Kong in 2008. Xtep is now a major Chinese running-focused sportswear group that also owns Saucony and Merrell rights in China.
interesting_fact: He has over 30 years in sportswear and has kept studying throughout: Peking, Tsinghua, CKGSB, CEIBS and Xiamen University EMBA programmes, plus Harvard's Global CEO Program in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Anta founder Ding Shizhong, his biggest Jinjiang rival, was his classmate: 'Ding Shizhong and I are of the same age; we were classmates and are really good friends,' he told the SCMP.
notes: Also romanised Ding Shui Po. Best route is Xtep media/IR. Xtep sponsors many Chinese marathons, which would be a natural podcast angle.

name: Li Yulong
profile: Listed with wealth source 'Jiutai'. Could not confirm which Jiutai entity this refers to (e.g. Jiutai Group/Jiutai Energy coal-to-chemicals group in Shandong/Inner Mongolia) or that Li Yulong controls it; available English officer listings for Jiutai entities name other chairmen.
notes: Identity unverified: English search found no source tying a Li Yulong to Jiutai; Chinese sources (Baidu Baike, Qichacha) were not reachable. Needs a Chinese-language check (李玉龙 + 久泰/九台) before any outreach.

name: Su Ruchun
current_role: Founder and chairman, Huabang Holding Group (华邦控股集团); stepped down as chairman of Huanong Property & Casualty Insurance in April 2025
profile: Su Ruchun (b. 1967) founded Huabang Holding Group, a private conglomerate in real estate, infrastructure and financial-sector investments. It is the largest shareholder (20%) of Huanong P&C Insurance, which he chaired from Sept 2015 until resigning for personal reasons in April 2025.
interesting_fact: He served on the 12th CPPCC National Committee (economic committee) and was vice chairman of the Gansu Federation of Industry and Commerce.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a postgraduate degree and is a nationally registered first-class constructor (一级建造师), a professional engineering qualification that is rare among tycoons.
notes: 2025 Chinese press reports say Huabang Holding is under heavy debt pressure, with share freezes and consumption restrictions on Su. Approach with care, as he is unlikely to be receptive now. No published contacts found. Not related to Huabang Health (002004.SZ).

name: Li Xinyu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Talkweb Information System (拓维信息, SZ:002261); also chairs Kaihong Zhigu (开鸿智谷)
profile: Li Xinyu founded Changsha-based Talkweb in 1996; it listed in Shenzhen in 2008 and grew from mobile value-added and education services into a full-stack Huawei-ecosystem partner (Kunpeng/Ascend servers, AI computing, OpenHarmony OS). He remains chairman and holds ~11.7% of the company.
interesting_fact: Talkweb is a core partner in Huawei's Ascend AI-compute ecosystem and participates in China's 'East Data, West Computing' data-center program, offering chips-to-servers-to-OS-to-apps solutions; in 2026 Li gave a keynote at the OpenAtom open-source ecosystem conference.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Talkweb he worked at the Hunan Provincial Electric Power Bureau, giving up that 'iron rice bowl' state job in 1996 to start the company in Changsha.
notes: Energy/data-center relevant (former power-bureau employee; AI compute and 'East Data West Computing'). Power-bureau detail is from a single eastmoney caifuhao article; not cross-checked elsewhere.

name: Zhao Guiqin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Runben Biotechnology Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603193), Guangzhou
profile: Guangzhou entrepreneur born in the 1970s who started Runben's predecessor, Xinxiang Trading, in 2006 as an OEM/white-label maker, then launched the Runben brand in 2010. Runben grew into a leading Chinese mosquito-repellent and baby-care brand sold mainly online, listing on the Shanghai main board in October 2023; he and his co-founder wife control most of the shares.
interesting_fact: Runben became the A-share market's 'first mosquito-repellent stock'; by 2022 it held ~16% of China's electric mosquito-liquid market and its baby-care line overtook repellents as its largest business. Hillhouse-linked JNRY VIII invested in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: When he launched the Runben own-brand in 2010, he opened a Tmall flagship direct store at the same time, betting on e-commerce years before rivals; Tmall, JD and Douyin later produced ~70% of sales.
notes: Described by 36Kr as very low-profile, rarely gives media interviews. Board office (security@runben.com) is the published channel.

name: Zhang Xingong
current_role: Chairman, founder and actual controller of Qingdao Huicheng Environmental Technology Group (惠城环保, SZ300779)
profile: Zhang Xingong (张新功, b. 1970) is a petrochemical engineer who founded Qingdao Huicheng in 2006, initially regenerating spent FCC refinery catalysts; it listed on ChiNext in 2019. Huicheng has since expanded into treating petroleum-coke gasification slag and chemical recycling of mixed waste plastics, and he also sits in the Qingdao Municipal People's Congress.
interesting_fact: Huicheng's self-developed 'one-step' CPDCC deep catalytic cracking process turns unsorted, low-value mixed waste plastics into chemical feedstocks with over 92% yield; the company says each tonne processed cuts 3-4 tonnes of CO2 versus the conventional lifecycle.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he was Communist Youth League secretary and deputy head of student affairs at Sinopec Changling Refinery's training centre (now Hunan Petrochemical Vocational Technology College), and is credentialed as an applied engineering research fellow.
notes: Technical founder with a sustainability/circular-economy story (waste catalysts, waste plastics) that fits an energy podcast. Company site publishes phone lines and an online message form but no email.

name: Xu Shuqing
current_role: No current public role found; former chairwoman of Guangxi Wuzhou Zhongheng Group (SSE: 600252), resigned Jan 2016
profile: Xu Shuqing built Guangxi Wuzhou Zhongheng Group, a Shanghai-listed pharmaceutical and real-estate company best known for its Xueshuantong (notoginseng-based) injection, and appeared on Hurun China 2010-2015. She resigned all posts in January 2016 and the family holding company's 20.52% controlling stake was transferred to state-owned Guangxi Investment Group.
interesting_fact: Zhongheng's control passed to Guangxi Investment Group, which bought the 20.52% stake for about RMB3.88bn (RMB5.44/share) in 2016.
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: per 2016 press she was detained in 2015 in a bribery probe before resigning, and no longer controls Zhongheng. Not on rich lists since 2015. No personal contact route found.

name: Bao Xiaojun
current_role: Chairman, President and core technical staff, Guangdong Naruida Technology (688522.SH, Zhuhai)
profile: Bao Xiaojun (XIAOJUN BAO, b. 1973, master's degree) founded Zhuhai Naruida in 2014 after engineering stints in North America, and built it into a maker of full-polarization active phased-array radars for weather detection and low-altitude/'low-slow-small' target surveillance. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market; his Hurun fortune is shared with Liu Suling.
interesting_fact: Naruida pairs phased-array with dual-polarization technology to make advanced radar cheap enough for civilian weather networks; its products won gold at the 10th and 11th World Radar Expo.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Naruida, Bao worked as an engineer at Raytheon in Canada (2006-2013) and then briefly at AMD (2013-2014), founding the company in May 2014.
notes: Technical founder with North American career (likely English-capable). Low-altitude economy/radar angle. Contact via IR email (board secretary 龚雪华).

name: Liu Suling
current_role: Director and Vice President, Guangdong Naruida Radar Technology Co. (SSE STAR: 688522); co-actual controller
profile: Liu Suling (Su Ling Liu), a Canadian citizen, co-founded phased-array weather-radar maker Naruida in Zhuhai in 2014 with her husband Bao Xiaojun; they jointly control it. Naruida makes X-band dual-polarization active phased-array radars for weather and rainfall monitoring and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023. She has been a director and VP since Dec 2020.
interesting_fact: Naruida reached 100m+ yuan revenue within about five years of founding and became the niche leader in phased-array weather radar; its radars are used for meteorology and flood/rainfall monitoring, with expansion into civil aviation, ocean monitoring and forest-fire detection.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding a radar company, Liu (who holds a master's degree) spent nine years doing statistics work in Canada, per Naruida's IPO prospectus; her co-founder husband was a Raytheon Canada engineer.
notes: Input lists industry as 'Defence' but Naruida is primarily civil weather/hydrology radar. Low public profile; route via board secretary Gong Xuehua / IR@naruida.com.

name: You Zhenhua
profile: Listed on the 2025 Hurun China Rich List with an estimated RMB ~6.5bn (USD ~910m) fortune attributed to 'Deep Source' (non-ferrous metals processing). Web searches in Chinese and English could not identify the underlying company or confirm this person's role.
notes: Could not identify the company behind 'Deep Source' (深源?) or find any public record of 游振华 as its controller; check the Hurun 2025 list entry directly for the Chinese company name before outreach.

name: Wang Wenhui
current_role: Director and co-controlling shareholder, Guangzhou Ruoyuchen Technology (SZSE: 003010)
profile: Wang Wenhui (b. 1985) co-founded Guangzhou e-commerce services firm Ruoyuchen in 2011 with her husband, chairman/CEO Wang Yu; together they control roughly 43%. Ruoyuchen began as a cross-border/online store operator for international brands and has pivoted to its own brands such as LYCOCELLE (home care) and FineNutri (supplements). She has been a director since 2017.
interesting_fact: Ruoyuchen's growth has shifted from running Tmall/JD stores for foreign brands to building its own consumer brands (LYCOCELLE laundry care, FineNutri, NuiBay).
deep_cut_fact: Ruoyuchen started in May 2011 with registered capital of just RMB 100,000: she and Wang Yu each put in RMB 50,000. She served as the company's supervisor until 2015 and is also listed as its senior adviser on employee career development.
notes: Hurun lists her jointly with husband Wang Yu, who is the public face (chairman). Best route is via Ruoyuchen's board secretary / IR. Not on-theme for energy/data centers.

name: Hu Weiwu
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Loongson Technology (龙芯中科, 688047.SH); chief scientist of Loongson CPU
profile: Chinese computer architect (b. 1968, Yongkang, Zhejiang) who led development of the Godson/Loongson CPUs at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Institute of Computing Technology, then became head of the commercialised Loongson Technology, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022. Loongson makes domestic general-purpose CPUs for PCs and servers.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Loongson moved off MIPS in 2021 to its own instruction-set architecture, LoongArch, aiming to make China's CPUs independent of foreign ISAs.
deep_cut_fact: He studied computer architecture under Xia Peisu, the 'mother of Chinese computing', after graduating from USTC in 1991; his PhD dissertation was among the first national 'Top 100 Excellent Doctoral Dissertations' in 1999, and he won the CCF Wang Xuan Award in 2018.
notes: Prominent state-linked tech figure (former NPC deputy, CPC congress delegate); Loongson is on US export-control lists - be mindful. Board secretary Li Xiaoyu handles IR. Country field blank in input; he is Chinese.

name: Jin Hong
current_role: Legal representative of Beijing Tiantong Xinyuan Technology (controlling shareholder of Loongson Technology, SSE: 688047); co-actual controller of Loongson with chairman Hu Weiwu
profile: Jin Hong (晋红) is, with Loongson founder-chairman Hu Weiwu, the disclosed actual controller of Loongson Technology, maker of China's home-grown Loongson CPUs. She runs the Tiantong holding vehicles through which management controls the company and is the largest investor (about 15%) in its Tiantong Xinyuan investment partnership; she has no operating title at Loongson itself.
interesting_fact: Loongson designs its own CPU instruction-set architecture, LoongArch, rather than licensing x86 or Arm, making it China's flagship effort at an independent general-purpose processor stack.
notes: Extremely private; no public interviews or biography found. Roles confirmed from Loongson's Aug 2025 equity-change report (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202508121726239773_1.pdf). Hu Weiwu is the public face and better podcast target; any approach should go via Loongson IR.

name: Venkatraman Viswanathan
current_role: Founder & Chairperson, Latent View Analytics (Chennai / San Jose)
profile: IIT Madras civil engineer and IIM Calcutta MBA who co-founded data-analytics firm LatentView in 2006 with his wife Pramad Jandhyala; CEO 2006-2014, then chairperson with professional CEOs. LatentView's Nov 2021 IPO raised Rs 600 crore and was subscribed 338x. In 2026 the board named ex-Wipro executive Sonal Ramrakhiani CEO (effective July 15, 2026).
interesting_fact: LatentView's November 2021 IPO was oversubscribed 338 times and listed at roughly a 160% premium to its issue price, a record subscription level for an Indian IPO at the time.
deep_cut_fact: An old LatentView corporate bio says that outside analytics he 'indulges his passion for technological gadgets' (then a Squeezebox wireless radio streaming music and news from around the world) and is a value investor in public markets. He received IIM Calcutta's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 2024.
notes: Goes by 'Venkat'. venkat@latentview.com is embedded in the board-of-directors listing on LatentView's corporate information page. He's a strong fit for a data/AI episode and writes for Forbes Technology Council and Entrepreneur.

name: Christopher Urmson
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Aurora Innovation (NASDAQ: AUR)
profile: Canadian roboticist Chris Urmson led CMU's DARPA Grand/Urban Challenge teams, then spent 2009-2016 at Google's self-driving project (later Waymo), becoming project lead and CTO. In 2017 he co-founded Aurora with Sterling Anderson and Drew Bagnell. Aurora launched commercial driverless trucking in Texas in 2025 and is targeting 30,000 driverless trucks by 2030.
interesting_fact: He was technical director of the Carnegie Mellon 'Boss' team that won the 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge. CMU vehicles also took 2nd and 3rd in the 2005 Grand Challenge.
deep_cut_fact: His 2005 CMU PhD thesis, 'Navigation Regimes for Off-Road Autonomy' (co-chaired by Red Whittaker), split off-road driving into efficiency-, stop- and swerve-limited regimes and cited planetary exploration and mine-mapping as low-speed cases.
notes: Born 1976 in Canada to English emigrant parents. Grew up in Trenton ON, Victoria BC, Winnipeg and Saskatoon. BSc in computer engineering, University of Manitoba, 1998. Highly relevant to tech/AI podcasts and a frequent public speaker; Aurora's press office is the best route.

name: Chris Ruddy
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Newsmax Inc. (NYSE: NMAX)
profile: Christopher Ruddy, a former investigative reporter at the New York Post and Pittsburgh Tribune-Review, founded Boca Raton-based Newsmax in 1998 and launched its cable channel in 2014, now among the largest US cable news networks. Newsmax listed on the NYSE in March 2025; Ruddy owns nearly a third of the shares.
interesting_fact: He started Newsmax in 1998 with a $25,000 investment from Mellon heir Richard Mellon Scaife; by 2024 the channel was the fourth-largest US news channel with ~30 million regular viewers.
deep_cut_fact: He turned down Columbia to join St. John's University's Honors Program (BA History, summa cum laude, 1987), later earned an MPP at the LSE, and as a student worked on the 'rapid response' team of Reagan's 1984 re-election campaign.
notes: High-profile media figure, accessible and frequently interviewed; route via Newsmax corporate/IR. He also speaks on energy/environment at EarthX (https://earthx.org/speaker/chris-ruddy/).

name: Robert Hagedorn
current_role: General partner, Hagedorn Partnership L.P. (10%+ owner of The Scotts Miracle-Gro Co.)
profile: Son of Miracle-Gro founder Horace Hagedorn and brother of Scotts Miracle-Gro chairman/CEO Jim Hagedorn. His wealth stems from the family's stake in Scotts Miracle-Gro, created when Miracle-Gro merged with Scotts in 1995; he is one of the general partners of the Hagedorn Partnership, which holds roughly a fifth of SMG.
interesting_fact: His father Horace co-founded Miracle-Gro in 1951 with horticulturist Otto Stern and built it through direct-response ads; the 1995 merger with Scotts made the Hagedorns the largest shareholders of America's biggest lawn-and-garden company.
notes: Private, non-executive family shareholder; listed as a Hagedorn Partnership GP in 2025-26 Form 4s (with Chris Hagedorn, Katherine Littlefield, Nathan Baxter, Hope Reeves). 2005 obituary placed him in the Seattle area (Pacific Northwest). Best route is Scotts Miracle-Gro corporate communications/IR (investor.scotts.com).

name: Susan Hagedorn
current_role: Nurse practitioner, professor emerita (University of Colorado nursing), documentary filmmaker and philanthropist; Hagedorn family >10% holder in ScottsMiracle-Gro
profile: Eldest daughter of Miracle-Gro co-founder Horace Hagedorn; the family kept a large stake in ScottsMiracle-Gro after the 1995 Scotts merger. She built a career as a nurse practitioner and nursing educator (UMass Amherst BSN '77, Boston College MS, Colorado doctorate) and has produced 20+ films on nursing and social justice.
interesting_fact: In 2021 she gave UMass Amherst's Elaine Marieb College of Nursing $2 million to create a diversity and inclusion program, and received the UMass Alumni Association's Revolutionary Spirit Award.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 she co-founded Nurstory with the founders of the digital-storytelling movement StoryCenter, a project using nurses' personal stories in nursing education. Her films include 'The Berrigans: Devout and Dangerous' and 'Island Nurse'.
notes: Wealth is passive (family ScottsMiracle-Gro stake); not involved in company management. Her Wikipedia article is flagged as possibly AI-generated, so treat it with care; the UMass page is the solid source. No published personal contact found; a possible route is via her film/Nurstory work or UMass nursing college. Not an energy/data-center fit.

name: Gregory Boyd Penner
current_role: Chairman of Walmart Inc.; controlling owner & CEO, Denver Broncos; founder/general partner, Madrone Capital Partners
profile: Greg Penner (b. 1969), son-in-law of Rob Walton, has chaired Walmart's board since 2015 after ~20 years in Walmart roles incl. CFO of Walmart Japan. He founded Menlo Park investment firm Madrone Capital, StubHub's largest shareholder at its 2025 IPO, and leads the Walton-Penner group that bought the Denver Broncos in 2022.
interesting_fact: He is an avid mountaineer and triathlete who has summited Everest, Denali, Vinson Massif, Ama Dablam and Kilimanjaro.
deep_cut_fact: Before Walmart he was a financial analyst at Goldman Sachs and a general partner of early-stage VC fund Peninsula Capital; at Walmart he started as a store employee before rising to CFO of Walmart Japan.
notes: Walmart press office only answers working journalists. Also in April 2026 he and wife bought a 40% minority stake in the Colorado Rockies (per Wikipedia). Madrone Capital is a possible route for investment-themed outreach.

name: Liu Xinrong
current_role: Founder, chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiahe Foods Industry Co. (Cograin; SSE: 605300)
profile: Suzhou-born Liu Xinrong founded Jiahe Foods in Wujiang in 2001 to make non-dairy creamer (plant-based fat powder), then dominated by foreign suppliers, and rode China's milk-tea boom to a 2021 Shanghai listing as the 'first creamer stock'. With his wife Tang Zhengqing he controls the company, which is now pivoting toward coffee.
interesting_fact: Jiahe built its own spray-drying production line in-house at founding; its first creamer product ran at full capacity from launch, and the company became known as China's 'king of creamer' supplying tea-drink chains.
deep_cut_fact: Liu trained in grain inspection at Jiangsu Jianghai Trade School, and after graduating at 18 worked as a counter clerk at the Songling grain station in Wujiang, then as a QC/R&D staffer in Suzhou and a technical supervisor at a dairy plant in Shantou.
notes: Shared fortune with wife Tang Zhengqing. Low media profile; route via board secretary office (board secretary Liu Xinren). Some filings misspell the email as ir@cogrian.cn.

name: Tang Zhengqing
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder (about 20% direct) of Jiahe Foods Industry (SSE: 605300; brand Cograin)
profile: Tang Zhengqing and her husband Liu Xinrong, Jiahe Foods' controlling shareholder and chairman, are the company's actual controllers. Jiahe, founded in 2001 in Wujiang, Suzhou, is a leading Chinese maker of non-dairy creamer for milk tea, coffee and baking, plus coffee and other solid beverages. It listed in Shanghai in 2021. She holds no executive role and keeps a low profile.
interesting_fact: Jiahe's 2025 interim report lists her as the company's second-largest shareholder, with 92.16m shares (20.28%) held directly, next to her husband's 28.39%.
notes: Very private. No interviews or biography found, and the public face of the company is Liu Xinrong. The best route is Jiahe's IR or board-secretary office. Hurun last listed her in 2023. Alive status was not independently confirmed, though she is named as a shareholder in 2025 filings.

name: Gu Yunkui
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2004-2016) as Gu Yunkui (顾云奎) of 'Jiangsu Yongding' (cable, real estate). Web searches in English and Chinese found no independent sources linking this name to a Yongding company. The best-known Jiangsu Yongding cable group (Yongding Co., SSE 600105) is publicly associated with the Mo family, not Gu.
notes: Identity could not be verified. The Hurun listing may be a transliteration or company-name error, and he has been off the list since 2016. Recommend deprioritising unless the journalist can confirm the person and company from the original Hurun entry.

name: Li Bogang
current_role: Founder and head of Chengdu Diao Group (成都地奥集团), pharmaceuticals (latest confirmed role as of 2014 reporting)
profile: Li Bogang (李伯刚) was a Chinese Academy of Sciences researcher who in 1988 left to commercialise his own research, founding Chengdu Diao Group around a steroidal-saponin herbal heart medicine (Diao Xinxuekang). By end-2013 the group had ~RMB5bn in assets and >RMB2bn annual output. He has not appeared on Hurun lists since 2013 and recent news on him is scarce.
interesting_fact: In March 2012 Diao Xinxuekang capsules were authorised in the EU (via the Netherlands), reported as the first Chinese therapeutic drug with Chinese IP to enter a developed-country mainstream market.
deep_cut_fact: He started Diao in 1988 with a RMB500,000 loan, renting a corner of the old library of the CAS Chengdu branch; his management motto is '聚财先聚人，聚人先聚心' (to gather wealth, first gather people; to gather people, first win hearts). (People's Daily, 4 Apr 2014, p.20)
notes: Private, unlisted group; little recent coverage, current role and status (incl. alive) could not be confirmed post-2014. Company site is a legacy Flash page with no published contact email.

name: Liu Peiying
current_role: No public role found; listed by Hurun China (2010-2014) jointly with China Dongxiang chairman Chen Yihong
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2010-2014 as a co-holder (with Chen Yihong) of the fortune derived from China Dongxiang (3818.HK), the Beijing sportswear group that holds the Kappa brand in mainland China and Macau. Her exact relationship to Chen Yihong is not confirmed in any source found, and she does not appear in recent HKEX disclosure-of-interest filings.
interesting_fact: China Dongxiang owns all rights to the Italian Kappa brand in mainland China, and in 2008 bought Japan's Phenix Co., which managed Kappa and Phenix in Japan, to push into ski and outdoor fashion.
notes: No public profile; 2026 HKEX circular names the Chen family group (Chen Yihong, daughter Chen Chen, her spouse, brother Chen Yiyong) but not Liu Peiying. Likely a family member of Chen Yihong (unconfirmed). Only route is China Dongxiang IR. Off Hurun list since 2014.

name: Zhu Shanyu
current_role: Founding shareholder and concert-party (yi zhi xing dong ren) shareholder of Zhejiang Weiming Environment Protection (SSE: 603568); executive role not confirmed
profile: A founding promoter of Wenzhou-based Weiming Environment Protection when it became a joint-stock company in 2005, and part of founder Xiang Guangming's controlling shareholder group (~69% in 2024). Weiming builds and runs waste-to-energy plants and has expanded into new-energy materials and Indonesia.
interesting_fact: Weiming grew out of a food-machinery/ice-cream-line workshop; in 1998 it took on a Wenzhou government challenge to develop domestic incineration tech, and its Dongzhuang waste-to-energy plant (385 t/day) connected to the grid in 2000.
notes: Essentially no public profile; appears only in shareholder filings (listed with Wang Suqin and Zhu Shanyin as concert parties of Xiang Guangming). Last on Hurun China 2022. Founder Xiang Guangming is the public face; approach via Weiming IR (board secretary Cheng Peng). Alive status not independently confirmed.

name: Zhang Jiancheng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, IKD Co., Ltd. (爱柯迪, SH:600933), Ningbo
profile: Zhang Jiancheng (b. 1959) founded Ningbo-based IKD in 2003; it makes precision aluminium die-cast parts for car powertrains, steering and EV systems and listed in Shanghai in 2017. He is chairman, GM and actual controller, and IKD has expanded with plants in Mexico and Malaysia.
interesting_fact: IKD, founded in 2003 and listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in November 2017, now runs overseas factories in Irapuato, Mexico and in Malaysia alongside its Ningbo HQ.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in 1975 in the tooling section of the Ningbo Tractor Factory, studied mechanical manufacturing at the factory's workers' college, rose to section chief and deputy GM, then was deputy GM of Ningbo Zhongce Auto & Tractor (1989-96) before founding IKD.
notes: Hands-on industrial founder; few media interviews. IR contact listed on investor page; HQ phone 0574-8756 2112 published.

name: Liu Junhui
current_role: Early/pre-IPO shareholder of Walvax Biotechnology (沃森生物, 300142.SZ); private investor
profile: Liu Junhui (刘俊辉) is one of the founding-era shareholders of Kunming-based vaccine maker Walvax Biotechnology, named alongside founder Li Yunchun in its 2010 IPO undertakings and described as its second-largest shareholder in 2015. Wife Huang Jing (黄静) is a co-shareholder (filings: http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2023-05-30/1216940545.PDF). Wealth likely well below the listed figure after sell-downs. Walvax IR is the only published route and is not a personal channel.

name: Zheng Rong
current_role: Chairwoman and controlling shareholder, Sichuan Yahua Industrial Group (SZSE: 002497)
profile: Born 1953, Zheng Rong (female) led the restructuring of the state-owned Ya'an Chemical Plant into Yahua, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010 and is now both a major civil-explosives maker and a lithium-salt producer for EV batteries. She has chaired the company since 2009 and is its largest shareholder (about 10.2% at end-2025).
interesting_fact: Yahua has grown from a 1952 explosives plant in Ya'an into one of China's notable lithium hydroxide suppliers for battery makers, a direct link to the energy-transition supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: She joined the Ya'an Chemical Plant in 1971 as a workshop worker and worked her way up through deputy chief accountant and deputy director to factory director before leading the 2001 privatization; she is a senior economist and a Sichuan Province Model Worker.
notes: Zheng Rong is a woman (aged 72 per 2025 report). Lithium angle fits energy podcast; route via board secretary office in Chengdu.

name: Zhao Min
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controlling shareholder of Xi'an Baode Automation (Bode Energy Equipment, ex-SZSE 300023)
profile: Zhao Min (赵敏, male), a senior engineer, founded Xi'an Baode Automation, which made electrical control and drive systems for oil and gas drilling rigs. He and his wife Xing Lianxian were the company's controlling shareholders. In 2021 he agreed to sell control; the stock was delisted from ChiNext in June 2022 after losses.
interesting_fact: Baode was one of the 28 companies in ChiNext's very first batch of listings on 30 October 2009 (code 300023), rising about 84% on debut day.
notes: Ambiguous common name (also a famous fictional character); this is 赵敏 of 宝德股份, husband of 邢连鲜 per company filings (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202202251549129098_1.pdf). Company delisted 2022 (https://www.bbtnews.com.cn/2022/0628/442616.shtml); no longer on rich lists. Alive status inferred from 2021-22 filings. No published contacts found.

name: Xing Lianxian
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Zhao Min) of Xi'an Baode Automation (西安宝德自动化, 300023.SZ), as of early 2022
profile: Xing Lianxian (邢连鲜, b. ~1958) and her husband Zhao Min (赵敏) are the founders/controlling shareholders of Xi'an Baode Automation, a ChiNext-listed maker of electrical control and automation equipment for oil and gas drilling rigs ('energy automation equipment'). Hurun listed the couple (2015-2017). In 2021 they held about 38% (her direct stake 4.19%) and planned to sell down and hand over control.
interesting_fact: In March 2021 Zhao Min and Xing Lianxian held 34.04% and 4.19% of Baode and announced a plan to sell 12-20% of the company, which would change its controller. In Feb 2022 they were still the controlling couple.
notes: Hurun API (2015/2017): 赵敏 (b. 1957) & 邢连鲜 (b. 1958), relation 夫妇, company 宝德股份 / Bode Energy Equipment, Xi'an, 'energy automation equipment manufacturing'. The stock was under *ST risk warning by 2022, so the current control and listing status after 2022 were not verified. No personal contacts. Private individual.

name: Zhang Buzhen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, YSB Inc. (药师帮, HKEX: 9885), Guangzhou
profile: Zhang Buzhen (张步镇) spent about 15 years at SouFun (搜房网, now Fang.com), rising to CTO and then VP in charge of web, technology, product and mobile. He then applied the internet-platform model to China's fragmented drug-distribution market, founding Guangzhou-based YSB, a B2B platform linking pharmaceutical wholesalers with grassroots pharmacies and clinics; it listed in Hong Kong in June 2023.
interesting_fact: YSB's platform aggregates long-tail demand from small pharmacies and clinics in lower-tier towns, letting a pharmacy that lacks a drug source it via the platform with delivery in 2-4 days instead of waiting on infrequent local distributor runs.
deep_cut_fact: Zhang was one of the core executives who grew up with SouFun: he served as the property portal's CTO before becoming the vice president running its website, technology, product and mobile operations, spending roughly 15 years there before starting YSB.
notes: No published IR/press email found in this pass; check the contact section of YSB's latest HKEX annual report (hkexnews.hk, stock 9885) for an IR email. Some secondary sources report he graduated in communications engineering in 1997 (Beijing Electronic Science and Technology Institute), unverified here.

name: Yang Hansong
current_role: Former president of Baoxin Auto Group (now Grand Baoxin Auto, HKEX: 1293); no current board role found
profile: Yang Hansong was president of Baoxin Auto Group, the Shanghai-based luxury-car (BMW and other premium brands) 4S dealership group founded in 1999 by chairman Yang Aihua. It listed in Hong Kong in December 2011, raising HK$4.1bn. In December 2015 Guanghui Auto bought a 53.58% controlling stake for about RMB 8.2bn, after which the Yang family ceded control.
interesting_fact: Baoxin's 2011 Hong Kong IPO raised about HK$4.1bn at HK$10.8 a share, making it one of the larger Chinese auto-dealer listings of its time.
notes: The listing (Hurun 2012) is shared with Yang Aihua and Yang Zehua. The family sold control to Guanghui in 2015, and the 2026 board of Grand Baoxin does not include any Yang. His current activities are unknown and he has a very low profile; I could not establish a route to reach him.

name: Yang Zehua
current_role: Former executive director and vice president, Baoxin Auto Group (now Grand Baoxin Auto Group, HKEX 1293); no current role found
profile: Yang Zehua (杨泽华) was a founding-family shareholder and executive director of Baoxin Auto Group, a BMW/luxury car dealer group based in Shanghai. It listed in Hong Kong in December 2011 in a HK$3.2bn IPO. At listing he held about 1.55bn shares; the controlling shareholder was Yang Aihua. China Grand Automotive bought control in 2015-16, and he stepped down as a director around 2016.
interesting_fact: Baoxin Auto's December 2011 Hong Kong IPO raised about HK$3.2 billion (US$414m), making it one of the larger Chinese car-dealer listings of that era.
notes: Very low public profile and last on the Hurun list in 2012. HKEX filings (e.g. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2012/0314/ltn20120314214.pdf) list him as an executive director with Yang Aihua and Yang Hansong. MarketScreener gives Beihang (undergraduate) and a Dalian University of Technology MBA, but that is unverified. The family link to Yang Aihua is not confirmed. No published contact; probably not a good outreach target.

name: Rostam Abdulrasul Aziz
current_role: Chairman, Taifa Group (Taifa Gas LPG); investor in MIC Tanzania (Tigo/Zantel) and majority owner of Nation Media Group
profile: Tanzanian businessman and former CCM MP for Igunga (1994-2011). Built wealth via a ~35% stake in Vodacom Tanzania (sold 2014-2019 for ~US$470m), Caspian contract mining, and Taifa Gas, East Africa's leading LPG supplier. With Axian he bought Millicom's Tanzanian telecoms, and in 2026 bought 54% of Nation Media Group from the Aga Khan network.

deep_cut_fact: As Igunga MP in 1996 he started a local health insurance scheme covering a family of four children for about TSh10,000 a year; ex-President Mkapa's memoir credits it as the inspiration for Tanzania's National Health Insurance Fund (2001).

name: Lawrence Jones
current_role: None – former founder/CEO of UKFast (left 2019); serving a 15-year prison sentence since Dec 2023
profile: Welsh-born Lawrence Jones co-founded Manchester web-hosting/cloud firm UKFast with wife Gail in 1999 and built it into a major UK hosting provider before stepping down in 2019; UKFast (later ANS) was sold to Inflexion. In December 2023 he was convicted of two rapes and a sexual assault and jailed for 15 years.
interesting_fact: UKFast was founded in September 1999 by Lawrence and Gail Jones and grew into one of the UK's best-known independent hosting/cloud providers.
notes: DO NOT approach: convicted in 2023 of rape and sexual assault, jailed 15 years (https://www.uktech.news/tech-hubs/north-west/manchester/ukfast-founder-sentenced-15-years-prison-20231204). Wealth listing shared with ex-wife Gail Jones. No deep-cut fact recorded deliberately.

name: Gail Jones
current_role: Former co-founder, managing director and acting CEO of UKFast (Manchester hosting/cloud provider); no current public operating role identified
profile: Gail Jones co-founded Manchester web-hosting firm UKFast in 1999 with her husband Lawrence Jones and grew it into one of the UK's largest independent hosting/cloud providers with its own data-centre campus (UKFast Campus, Trafford). She became MD in 2017 and led the firm after Lawrence stepped down in 2019; the family sold its remaining interest to Inflexion in 2020, and UKFast was merged into ANS.
interesting_fact: UKFast ran its own Manchester data-centre estate (MaNOC) and in 2017 split its leadership into two MD roles, with co-founder Gail Jones taking the managing director post to drive cloud growth.

Reported prior board roles at Tech Manchester and Manchester Foundation Trust Charity (unverified on primary sources). No published contact found.

name: May Makhzoumi
current_role: President, Makhzoumi Foundation (Lebanon); board member, Future Pipe Industries and other Future Group companies; Chairperson, Future Management Services Ltd (London)
profile: May Naamani Makhzoumi is a Lebanese-British philanthropist and businesswoman, wife of Future Pipe Industries founder Fouad Makhzoumi; the family fortune comes from FPI, a global maker of fibreglass pipe systems. She chairs London-based Future Management Services, sits on Future Group boards and has led the Makhzoumi Foundation (vocational training, micro-credit, healthcare) since 2000.

deep_cut_fact: She trained as a pharmacist (BSc Pharmacy, AUB, 1975) and worked as an out-patient pharmacist in Beirut and then at King Faisal's Hospital in Riyadh (1975-77) before joining the family business in London.
notes: Email is from her expert profile on LAU's 'Who Is She in Lebanon' directory (profiles are typically self-submitted); a second, malformed variant is also listed there. Husband Fouad Makhzoumi is a Lebanese MP; keep outreach non-political.

name: Lady de Rothschild
current_role: Chair/owner, E.L. Rothschild (holding company); Founder, Council for Inclusive Capitalism
profile: Lynn Forester de Rothschild (b. 1954, NJ) is a Columbia-trained lawyer turned telecom entrepreneur and investor who, with her late husband Sir Evelyn de Rothschild (d. 2022), built E.L. Rothschild, holding stakes in The Economist Group and other assets; SEC filings show her as a 10%+ owner of oil & gas producer PrimeEnergy Resources (PNRG). name: Chatchai Kaewbootta
current_role: CEO and Director, Srisawad Corporation PCL (SET: SAWAD), Thailand
profile: Chatchai Kaewbootta built Srisawad into one of Thailand's largest lenders against motorcycles, cars and homes (5,500+ branches, plus nano-finance). The son of a tractor distributor, he became a Honda motorcycle dealer, started the lending business in 1984, sold it to AIG in 2007 and re-entered the market under a new name in 2009. He dropped off Forbes' billionaire list after 2023.

deep_cut_fact: He earned his undergraduate degree from Sukhothai Thammathirat Open University, Thailand's distance-learning public university.

name: Dipender Saluja
current_role: Managing Director, Capricorn Investment Group; managing partner, Capricorn Technology Impact Fund; director of QuantumScape, Joby Aviation and Navitas Semiconductor
profile: Electrical engineer turned impact investor who joined Jeff Skoll's Palo Alto-based Capricorn Investment Group in 2007 and leads its energy/cleantech and IT investing. His early-stage board seats at solid-state battery maker QuantumScape, eVTOL maker Joby Aviation and GaN chipmaker Navitas account for his large SEC-reported holdings.
interesting_fact: Capricorn's portfolio under his team has included Tesla, SpaceX, Planet Labs, QuantumScape, Innovium and Saildrone, built on the thesis that investing profitably and driving sustainable change are compatible.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing he was chief of staff at chip-design software firm Cadence, and earlier worked at Data General, Honeywell, ROLM (IBM) and GF Energy Research; he also sits on the external advisory board of the University of Minnesota's Institute on the Environment (since 2021).
notes: Spoke at Aspen Ideas 2017 ('Why Investing in Good Companies Makes Economic Sense') and is a WEF contributor, so he is open to energy/impact-investing conversations. Route via Capricorn media inquiries.

name: Taku Toguchi
current_role: Founder, Representative Director, President & CEO, AI inside Inc. (TSE Growth: 4488)
profile: Japanese entrepreneur (b. 1984, Aichi) who has worked on AI R&D since 2004 and founded AI inside in 2015. Its DX Suite AI-OCR SaaS digitises paper documents; the company listed on TSE Mothers in 2019 and its shares soared with Japan's pandemic-era digitisation push. He still leads management and technology strategy.
interesting_fact: He holds multiple patents personally, including character recognition combining machine learning with image recognition and NLP, anonymised encrypted communication, and 'virtual personality' generation from anonymous data.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of university after one year to become an entrepreneur and, to fund his AI research, founded a string of companies (socialwave 2010, IQUE 2011, SPACEBOY 2012, thinkapartment 2013), including gourmet/restaurant-site businesses, before AI inside. His listed hobby is reading.
notes: Japanese name 渡久地択. English contact page currently 404s; Japanese contact form works. Fortune largely tied to AI inside share price, which has fallen well below 2020 peak.

name: Telis Mistakidis
current_role: Private investor (Zug-based): controlling shareholder of Aegean Baltic Bank, shipping investor, owner of PAOK BC via Alpha Sports Group
profile: Aristotelis 'Telis' Mistakidis is a Greek-British metals trader who joined Marc Rich & Co (later Glencore) in 1993 and ran its global copper business. He became a billionaire with Glencore's 2011 IPO, when he held about 6%, and left at the end of 2018. Since then he has invested in Greek banking (Piraeus Bank stake, control of Aegean Baltic Bank), shipping (Union Maritime) and real estate.
interesting_fact: In 2025 his Alpha Sports Group agreed to buy a majority stake in PAOK BC, the Thessaloniki basketball club. In May 2026 PAOK announced a new basketball training centre in Pylaia.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Rome in 1961, where his father, a marine biologist, worked for the United Nations. He graduated in economics from the LSE and spent six years trading non-ferrous metals at Cargill before joining Marc Rich & Co's zinc and lead desk in March 1993.
notes: Very private, with no personal public channels found. Avoid the topic of his 2018 Glencore exit (the Katanga Mining accounting case in Ontario). Possible routes are via Aegean Baltic Bank or PAOK BC. Forbes 2026 put his net worth at about US$4.2bn, well above the 2020 Sunday Times figure.

name: Fu Mingkang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Riyue Heavy Industry Co., Ltd. (日月股份, SSE: 603218)
profile: Fu Mingkang (傅明康, b. 1963), a Ningbo native, founded Riyue Heavy Industry with his wife Chen Jianmin and daughter Fu Linger. The company is a leading maker of heavy-section ductile-iron castings, especially hubs and bases for wind turbines, plus parts for plastics machinery. He started as a technician at a Ningbo elevator factory and still runs Riyue as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Riyue specialises in thick, large-section ductile-iron castings for heavy equipment, a core part of the wind-power supply chain, and runs what it calls a fully digitalised casting plant (the 'new Rixing' digital foundry) in Ningbo.
deep_cut_fact: Besides running Riyue, he is a vice president of the China Foundry Association's council, president of the Ningbo Safety Association, and a deputy to the 16th Ningbo Municipal People's Congress; he holds a senior economist title.
notes: Strong energy (wind-power) angle. Board secretary is Lu Jianbo (卢建波). Directly holds about 260.6M shares.

name: Rui Chen
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Bilibili Inc. (NASDAQ: BILI / HKEX: 9626)
profile: Chen Rui (b. 1978, Chengdu) spent years at Kingsoft (Kingsoft Antivirus engine, later GM of the antivirus unit), co-founded Kingsoft Network (now Cheetah Mobile), angel-invested in Bilibili in 2011 and became its chairman in 2014. His wealth comes from his Bilibili stake; he still leads the video community as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: He was an angel investor in Bilibili in 2011 when it was a small hobbyist site, advised it for years, and joined full-time as chairman after Cheetah Mobile's 2014 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he left Kingsoft to found 'Beike Anquan' (贝壳安全), described as China's first cloud-security vendor; Kingsoft bought it in 2010 and he returned as a co-founder of Kingsoft Network (Cheetah Mobile). He is a long-time ACG fan and was among Bilibili's first ~210,000 users.
notes: Has a public Weibo and Bilibili space (linked from zh.wikipedia). Joined Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Media & Communication as adjunct professor in Dec 2021. Best formal route: Bilibili IR/media contact.

name: Bai Houshan
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ningbo Ronbay New Energy Technology (SSE STAR: 688005); Chairman, Beijing Ronbay Holding
profile: Metallurgist (b. 1964, Xiantao, Hubei; Central South University and Northeastern University) who began at China's state mining-metallurgy institutes, founded cathode maker Beijing Easpring, then started again with Ronbay in the 2010s. Ronbay is a leading supplier of high-nickel cathode materials for EV lithium batteries, with plants in China and South Korea.
interesting_fact: He has founded two of China's leading lithium-battery cathode companies: Easpring (listed 2010) and later Ronbay, which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market and for a time outgrew his first company by market value.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial story began in 1992 leading a research group at the Beijing General Research Institute of Mining and Metallurgy that originally developed additives for electronic ceramics - it only began making lithium cobalt oxide in 2001, becoming Easpring.
notes: nbrb@ is the listed company's published contact alongside its investor hotline; ronbay@ronbaymat.cn is Beijing Ronbay Holding (his holding company). Be aware: in April 2026 the CSRC Ningbo bureau warned and fined him over a Ronbay contract disclosure.

name: He Zhonglin (何中林)
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Hubei RT-Hitech Advanced Materials Group (湖北融通高科先进材料集团)
profile: Hubei-born entrepreneur (b. 1968) who built Beijing RT-Hitech (security chips for smart utility meters), then in 2016 bought a lithium cathode business and moved it to his hometown Daye. Hubei RT-Hitech became an LFP cathode unicorn backed by automakers (FAW, SAIC, NIO, Xiaomi) and state funds; it began A-share IPO tutoring in 2022.
interesting_fact: RT-Hitech's revenue went from about RMB100M in 2020 to RMB1.04B in 2021, with He forecasting ~RMB11B for 2022. He predicted LFP would take over 95% of large-scale energy-storage batteries.
deep_cut_fact: Born to a rural family in Huangshi, he graduated in electrical automation in 1991 and was assigned to the Huangshi Crane Machinery Works. His first company (2002) nearly failed until Beijing's water and power utilities adopted its smart-meter chips, using over 14 million of them in 2005-2010.
notes: Chinese-language coverage only; no official website or published contact found. Relevant to the energy-storage/battery supply-chain angle. Note: Beijing RT-Hitech (chips) and Hubei RT-Hitech (cathode materials) are separate entities, both founded by He.

name: Li Baoping
current_role: Actual controller of Shaanxi Huanghe (Yellow River) Mining Group and its listed unit Shaanxi Heimao Coking Co. (SSE: 601015), Hancheng, Shaanxi
profile: Li Baoping (李保平) is the Hancheng, Shaanxi coal and coking entrepreneur behind Shaanxi Huanghe Mining Group, which holds ~45% of Shanghai-listed Shaanxi Heimao ('Black Cat') Coking. Heimao, founded 2003 and listed 2014, runs an integrated coal-coke-chemicals chain (coke, tar, benzene, methanol, ammonia, LNG, BDO) in Shaanxi and Inner Mongolia; Li formerly chaired it (to 2022).
interesting_fact: Heimao runs a 'coal-coke-chemicals' circular model, turning coke-oven gas and tar into methanol, synthetic ammonia, LNG and BDO rather than flaring by-products - giving a coal business a gas-and-chemicals angle.

name: Liu Jianguo
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Delijia Transmission Technology (Jiangsu) Co. (德力佳, SSE: 603092)
profile: Gearbox engineer (b. 1969, Shanghai Jiao Tong graduate) who spent ~20 years at Nanjing High Speed Gear / NGC, rising to chief engineer and GM. In 2017 he co-founded Delijia, which makes wind-turbine main gearboxes; it listed on the Shanghai main board in Nov 2025 and ranks among the top global suppliers, with Envision and Sany Renewable as key partners.
interesting_fact: Delijia went from founding (Jan 2017) to a Shanghai main-board IPO (Nov 7, 2025) in about eight years, becoming one of the world's top-three wind main-gearbox shippers by some broker estimates.
deep_cut_fact: When Delijia was set up in 2017 (with Sany Renewable Energy as a co-founding shareholder), part of Liu's capital contribution was his own non-patented wind-turbine gearbox design know-how, valued as intellectual-property capital.
notes: Highly relevant for an energy podcast (wind drivetrain supply chain). Low international media profile; route via company IR/board secretary office. Shares wealth listing with co-founder Kong Jinfeng.

name: Kong Jinfeng
current_role: Director, Vice General Manager and Board Secretary, Delijia Transmission (德力佳传动, SSE:603092), Wuxi
profile: Kong Jinfeng and her husband Liu Jianguo (chairman/CTO) are the controlling shareholders of Delijia, a wind-turbine main-gearbox maker founded in Wuxi in January 2017; together they control ~42% via Nanjing Chenrui, a Wuxi employee partnership and direct stakes. Delijia listed on the Shanghai main board on 7 Nov 2025; wind OEMs Sany Renewable Energy and Envision are 5%+ shareholders and key customers.

deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a billionaire co-founder, she personally serves as Delijia's board secretary, the officer named as the company's investor-relations contact in its 2025 listing announcement; she is also the managing partner of the Wuxi Detong staff shareholding partnership.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (wind-power drivetrain). Because she runs the board office, the IR email reaches her team directly. Her husband Liu Jianguo (chairman/CTO) gave a Shanghai Securities News interview at the IPO (paper.cnstock.com, 7 Nov 2025). Director term in the prospectus ran to June 2026; confirm she was re-appointed.

name: Li Xiaomin (李晓旻)
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Wintech Nano-Technology Services (胜科纳米(苏州)股份有限公司, SSE STAR: 688757)
profile: A Peking University microelectronics graduate with a master's in electrical engineering from NUS, Li worked as an R&D engineer at Singapore A*STAR's Institute of Microelectronics before founding a commercial third-party semiconductor failure-analysis lab in Singapore in 2004. He set up Wintech Nano in Suzhou in 2012; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market and serves chipmakers with FIB/TEM/SIMS analysis.
interesting_fact: Wintech Nano is a 'hospital for chips': it diagnoses semiconductor failures with tools such as focused ion beams, TEM and SIMS, and in 2026 launched an AI-driven closed-loop analysis system called iWUDI.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 2001-2004 as an R&D engineer at A*STAR's Institute of Microelectronics in Singapore, then founded his first independent failure-analysis lab there in 2004 at about age 29.
notes: Semiconductor-testing angle (relevant to data-center chip supply chain). Speaks to Chinese media as chairman; Singapore background so English outreach plausible.

name: Chen Kai
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Jiangsu Azure Corp (蔚蓝锂芯, 002245.SZ), Zhangjiagang; actual controller (~18.7%)
profile: Australian-national entrepreneur (b. March 1968, master's degree) who has run Zhangjiagang-based Azure (formerly Aucksun / 澳洋顺昌) since 2007. It grew from metal-sheet logistics into LED chips and, via subsidiary Tenpower (天鹏电源), cylindrical lithium cells for power tools and small power systems. H1 2025 revenue rose 21.6% to RMB 3.73bn and net profit nearly doubled.
interesting_fact: Tenpower is pushing cylindrical cells into data-centre BBU backup power, robots/robot dogs and eVTOLs; it opened a lithium-cell plant in Malaysia in April 2025 and launched a semi-solid 21700 cell rated above 350 Wh/kg.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2025 Tenpower and Taiwan's Molicel jointly launched the high-capacity 21700-M65A cylindrical cell, aimed at humanoid-robot makers' core pain point, unveiling it at The Battery Show Europe and Eurobike in Germany.

public_contacts.value: azure@azurecorp.com (board secretary Fang Hongliang / securities office)

name: Zhuang Chenchao
current_role: Founder of Banma Capital (斑马投资) and founder of data-driven convenience-store chain Bianlifeng (便利蜂), Beijing
profile: Shanghai-born (1976) Peking University electronics graduate who co-founded travel search site Qunar in 2005 and served as its CEO until it merged with Ctrip in 2015. He left in January 2016 to start investment firm Banma (Zebra) Capital and, later that year, Bianlifeng, an algorithm-run convenience-store chain. Also an early investor in Rong360 and Meilishuo.
interesting_fact: Bianlifeng was built around his 'mathematical thinking': store ordering, pricing and staffing are largely decided by algorithms rather than store managers.
deep_cut_fact: While still a PKU student he built a search engine, Souke (搜索客), in November 1997; in 1999 he co-founded sports site Sharkwhy (鲨威) as CTO with Fritz Demopoulos, then worked as a systems architect at the World Bank in Washington before reuniting with Demopoulos to found Qunar.
notes: Input 'Banma' refers to his Banma (Zebra) investment vehicle, not Alibaba's Banma auto-OS JV. Keeps a low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Search rate limits cut research short; current Bianlifeng role not re-verified for 2026.

name: Zhang Jujun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Qingdian Group (清电集团), parent of Qingdian Photovoltaic (Hefei)
profile: Zhang Jujun (张菊军), a North China Electric Power University engineering master's graduate, spent nearly 20 years in power-plant planning and design before founding Beijing-based Qingdian Group in 2016, starting with wind farms in Henan. He has since moved upstream into an integrated solar silicon chain (industrial silicon, polysilicon, wafers) in Hami, Xinjiang and Hefei via unicorn Qingdian Photovoltaic.
interesting_fact: Qingdian Photovoltaic raised a RMB1.5bn Series A in 2023 led by Hefei's state investor and Beijing Energy Group; its Hami 'three-silicon' park (industrial silicon, polysilicon, mono ingots) was billed as China's largest approved project of its kind, powered by the group's own plants.
deep_cut_fact: As an engineer at the state Northwest Electric Power Design Institute he worked on planning and design for China's first solar-thermal (CSP) power project and on China's first low-wind-speed plains wind farm. He is described as originator and earliest practitioner of China's 'plains wind power' theory.
notes: Private unlisted company; low-profile founder (aged 42 in 2023). Gave a long founder interview to STAR Market Daily/CLS in June 2023, so he is open to media. No official contact channel verified; company said it planned an IPO within 3-5 years of 2023.

name: Wang Peng
current_role: Party Secretary, Director and Deputy General Manager, Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources Co. (SH 600295); president of the China Ferroalloy Industry Association (10th term)
profile: The Wang Peng found at Erdos is a 54-year-old career executive of Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources (director since Dec 2019) who rose through its chemicals, power-and-metallurgy and ferroalloy units. Erdos is China's top cashmere brand and also runs coal, power and ferroalloy businesses. Link to the Hurun listing is not certain.
interesting_fact: Erdos began as the Yimeng cashmere factory and grew into one of the world's largest cashmere producers, while its industrial arm is a major ferroalloy and chemicals producer powered by Inner Mongolia coal.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the Erdos textile park's property-management company as head of its general affairs section before moving into the group's metallurgy, calcium-carbide and chlor-alkali chemical units; he now heads China's national ferroalloy industry association.

current_role: Executive Director and Chair of the Strategy & Investment Committee, ESWIN Computing (Beijing; HKEX-listed Oct 2026); controls ESWIN group via ESWIN Technology
profile: Founder of BOE Technology, which he built from the near-bankrupt Beijing Electron Tube Factory into the world's largest display-panel maker; often called the 'father of China's semiconductor display industry'. After leaving BOE's chair in 2019 he founded the ESWIN chip group; ESWIN Computing, a RISC-V chip designer, listed in Hong Kong in Oct 2026, his third IPO.
interesting_fact: In April 1993 he led employees of the loss-making Beijing Electron Tube Factory to raise just RMB 6.5 million themselves for a shareholding reform, creating the company that became BOE.
deep_cut_fact: He started as an accountant: a finance/accounting graduate of Hangzhou Dianzi University (b. 1957, Zhejiang), he joined Beijing Electron Tube Factory's finance department in 1982, was sent to Hong Kong for 3 months to study international finance, and became the factory's director at just 35 in 1992.
notes: Strong data-centre/AI angle (RISC-V AI compute chips). Chairman/CEO of ESWIN Computing is now Mi Peng (per TechNode, Sep 2026). Hurun lists wealth as 'Eswin'. Branding mailbox is the closest thing to a press contact.

current_role: Angel investor and founder of 创业工场 (Chuangye Gongchang); early Pop Mart shareholder
profile: Chinese angel investor who in August 2012 became Pop Mart's first institutional backer, putting in RMB 2M at a RMB 12.5M valuation. Reports say he still held 44M+ Pop Mart shares in 2025, and its rise made him a Hurun-listed rich lister (listed jointly with Mai Haoyun). He was also an early Chinese bitcoin evangelist and mentored OKX founder Xu Mingxing.

notes: Also romanised as Gang Mai / Michael Mai. He invested in Xu Mingxing's Docin.com and was involved in founding OKCoin (chaincatcher.com/en/article/2187116). No verified official site or social accounts found; he has appeared on the Xiaoyuzhou FM podcast (crypto.news, Jul 2025). Relationship to Mai Haoyun not established.

name: Wang Qian
current_role: Founder and CEO, X Square Robot (Zibianliang Jiqiren), Shenzhen
profile: Wang Qian, a Tsinghua and USC-trained robotics researcher, ran a quant fund in the US before closing it in 2023 to found X Square Robot in Shenzhen. The embodied-AI startup builds general-purpose robot foundation models (WALL-A, open-sourced WALL-OSS) and reached a valuation above US$2.8bn in 2026, with backers including Alibaba, ByteDance, Meituan and Xiaomi.
interesting_fact: He argues humanoid robots doing repetitive factory work are 'just a PR stunt' and that the field should focus on generalisation; X Square raised four consecutive rounds to pass a $2.8bn valuation by mid-2026.
deep_cut_fact: As a researcher he was among the early adopters of attention mechanisms in neural networks, publishing at the same 2014 conference as Google's early attention paper; after leaving robotics for finance he said 'I couldn't sleep for nights. I regretted not pursuing robotics full time.'
notes: Highly relevant to an AI/compute-themed podcast (embodied AI foundation models). No published personal net worth found; the list source is not Forbes. Pandaily attention-mechanism claim is from a paywalled profile (visible portion).

name: Chen Mei-chi
current_role: Founder and Chairperson, Chenbro Micom (TWSE: 8210), also Chief Sustainability Officer
profile: Taiwanese entrepreneur (NCCU graduate, NTU MBA per data aggregators) who founded Chenbro in 1983 as one of Asia's first PC-chassis makers, then pivoted it from commoditised PC cases to server and cloud/AI-server chassis. Chenbro's 2025 revenue reached about NT$22 billion; she remains chair after the 2026 board re-election, with a professional CEO running operations.
