name: Ke Kangbao
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of Dashenlin Pharmaceutical Group (603233.SH); long-time director and general manager
profile: Ke Kangbao (柯康保) co-founded Guangzhou-headquartered Dashenlin Pharmaceutical with brothers Ke Yunfeng (chairman) and Ke Jinlong; the three each held about a third. Dashenlin grew into one of China's largest pharmacy chains, with 10,000+ stores, and listed in Shanghai in 2017. He served for years as director and general manager.
interesting_fact: The brothers' first shop, the 'Shenrong Pharmacy' (参茸大药房), opened around 1993 in an open-air market on Hongqi North Road in Maoming with an investment of just over 10,000 yuan, pioneering membership cards and discount pricing.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 the three Ke brothers signed a formal 'acting-in-concert' agreement to make all major company decisions jointly, after holding near-identical 33.3% stakes since founding.
notes: Forbes bio says 'Deshenlin'; company is Dashenlin. SSE 2024 disciplinary document lists him as co-actual controller and 'then-director', so he may no longer sit on the board. Low profile; brother Ke Yunfeng is the public face. Route via company IR.

name: Ding Lieming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Betta Pharmaceuticals (SZSE: 300558), Hangzhou
profile: Medical researcher who spent about a decade studying and working in the US before returning to China in 2002 and founding Hangzhou-based Betta Pharmaceuticals, an oncology-drug maker. Betta's icotinib (Conmana), approved in 2011, was China's first home-grown small-molecule targeted cancer drug; he still leads the company as chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: The Lancet Oncology said icotinib 'has created the new era of China's R&D of anticancer drugs'; Ding priced it at roughly 60-70% of comparable imported drugs so more lung-cancer patients could afford it.
deep_cut_fact: He said he left the US because there he 'could not fulfill my dream to innovate and start my own business'; Betta started with only about 200,000 yuan of seed funding, and he set up a program giving free pills to patients still responding after six months on Conmana.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Ding Shizhe. Company contact email is general corporate (Tel +86-571-86130357 on same page). Founding year given as 2002 or 2003 depending on source.

name: Cai Xiaoru
current_role: Founder and major (>5%) shareholder, Fuzhou Tatwah Smartech Co. (达华智能, SZSE: 002512); former chairman
profile: Cai Xiaoru (蔡小如) founded Tatwah Smartech in Zhongshan, Guangdong, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010 as a contactless IC card/RFID-tag maker. He then grew it by acquisitions into IoT, fintech and satellite-communications businesses. Chen Rongsheng is now chairman; Cai remains a top-10 shareholder per the 2025 annual report.
interesting_fact: Under Cai, Tatwah went from a pure contactless smart-card/RFID manufacturer to a serial acquirer: it bought Xindongwang (2013), then a string of IoT and internet-finance companies from 2015, earning him the nickname 'M&A madman' in the Chinese press.
notes: The emails belong to the board secretary and securities representative, as published in the 2025 annual report summary; they are company channels, not Cai's. He no longer runs the company, which now trades as 'ST达华' (special treatment). Some of his shares were judicially auctioned in 2021, so avoid wealth/control topics. Low public profile.

name: Wang Bin
current_role: Founder, legal representative and CEO, Sichuan Shuyi Catering Management Co. (Shuyi Xianshaocao / 书亦烧仙草 tea chain), Chengdu
profile: Wang Bin (王斌) founded Chengdu-based tea-drink chain Shuyi Xianshaocao, which grew from one shop in 2007 to 5,200+ stores across 32 provinces plus 60+ overseas outlets. In 2022 it raised close to RMB1bn from investors including Tencent, Juewei and Qiaqia Food. In 2025 he set the slogan 'restart the business, dare to innovate' as the chain adjusts after years as China's No. 2 tea chain by scale.
interesting_fact: Shuyi's signature 'shaoxiancao' (grass-jelly) drink sold more than 200 million cups in its peak year and is still the chain's best-seller.
deep_cut_fact: The brand began in 2007 as a single shop called '85°Tea' before being renamed Shuyi Xianshaocao.
notes: Wang says he wants Shuyi to be 'the warmest and most valuable company, not the biggest' (Beijing News, Apr 2025) — a usable quote. No published press/IR email found; private company.

name: Cen Guojian
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Ningbo ZhongDa Leader Intelligent Transmission Co. (SZSE: 002896)
profile: Cen Guojian (b. 1968), a Cixi motor-industry veteran, built ZhongDa Leader from his 1998 machinery partnership into a listed maker of geared motors and precision reducers (planetary, RV and harmonic) used in industrial automation and robots. He and his wife Zhou Guoying are the actual controllers; he has been chairman since 2015 and again also GM since 2023.
interesting_fact: ZhongDa Leader says it is one of the few companies mass-producing all three precision-reducer types (planetary, RV and harmonic) and sells integrated reducer+servo+drive modules, putting it in the supply chain for industrial and humanoid robots.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his own business Cen worked at Ningbo Changjiang Motor Factory and Cixi Gexin Motor Factory, then ran Zhanyun Machinery as managing partner from 1998 to 2006 before forming ZhongDa in 2006.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Zhou Guoying. No personal media presence; route via board secretary (Wu Xujun) at the published company email. Robotics/reducer angle could be a hook.

name: Zhou Guoying
current_role: Co-actual controller and adviser, Ningbo Zhongda Leader Intelligent Transmission (SZSE: 002896); legal representative of controlling holder Ningbo Zhongda Lide Investment
profile: Zhou Guoying (b. 1970) co-controls Zhongda Leader with her husband Cen Guojian, its chairman and GM. The Cixi, Ningbo company makes precision reducers, small and special motors and drive units used in industrial robots, logistics automation and new-energy equipment. She was a director from 2006 until her term ended in August 2025, and she now serves as company adviser.
interesting_fact: The company she co-controls makes precision reducers, servo/small motors and drive units for industrial robots, intelligent logistics and new-energy equipment. She and her husband first appeared on Hurun's China Rich List in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zhongda existed, she was finance department manager at Zhanyun Machinery (1998 to July 2006), the predecessor workshop her husband ran as managing partner. She then served as a director of Zhongda from 2006.
notes: Low profile. The 2025 annual report lists her as company adviser and co-actual controller, so she is presumed alive. Board secretary Wu Xujun handles IR. Robotics and automation is a good podcast angle. Cen Guojian is the public face.

name: Yuan Wenjie
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller of Baotou Tianhe Magnetics Technology Co. (SSE: 603072)
profile: Yuan Wenjie (袁文杰) chairs Baotou Tianhe Magnetics, an Inner Mongolia maker of sintered NdFeB and SmCo rare-earth permanent magnets for EVs, wind turbines, efficient appliances and electronics. With his sons Yuan Bo and Yuan Yi, he controls about 70% of the company, which listed on the Shanghai main board in Jan 2025.
interesting_fact: Tianhe's revenue rose from RMB 1.15bn in 2020 to RMB 2.885bn in 2022 on demand for high-performance magnets for EV motors and wind power. The company is based in Baotou's rare-earth high-tech zone.
deep_cut_fact: According to the sponsor's IPO report, a technical team centred on Yuan Wenjie has been developing and producing sintered NdFeB magnets since 1993, nearly from the start of China's rare-earth permanent-magnet industry. The company itself was founded in 2008.
notes: Low media profile with no personal interviews found. He is relevant to the energy theme through magnets for wind turbines and EVs. Best route is the board secretary's office via the IR email. Not to be confused with a Dalian University of Technology professor of the same name.

name: Ding Shizhe
current_role: Director (employee-representative) and Assistant to the Chairman, Betta Pharmaceuticals (贝达药业, SZSE: 300558); GM of Qiyuan Bio (Hangzhou)
profile: Ding Shizhe (丁师哲, b. May 1991) is the son of Betta Pharmaceuticals founder Ding Lieming, maker of Conmana (icotinib), China's first home-grown small-molecule lung-cancer targeted drug; Hurun lists the family's stake jointly. A Saint Louis University graduate (biochemistry + economics), he joined Betta and rose through strategic partnerships to the board in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: He handles Betta's in-licensing and business development: he pushed through the MCLA-129 and ensartinib projects, struck partnerships with InventisBio and Agenus, and led Betta's equity investment in US cancer-drug developer Xcovery.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Saint Louis University in the US with a combined biochemistry-and-economics background, and served as executive deputy GM of 'Betta Dream Factory' (贝达梦工场), the company's incubator platform.
notes: Father-son relationship per media reports of company filings (https://m.jiemian.com/article/14889899.html). Wealth is family-held with Ding Lieming, who is the actual controller. Contact via Betta IR.

name: Lyu Gang
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical (002020.SZ; Hong Kong H-share listing filed Sept 2026)
profile: Born 1962, Lyu Gang has run Zhejiang Jingxin Pharmaceutical, a Xinchang-born drugmaker now based in Hangzhou, since its days as Zhejiang Xinchang Jingxin Pharma; he has been chairman since 2004 when it listed in Shenzhen. With his wife he controls ~36% of the company, which focuses on CNS and cardio/cerebrovascular drugs (2025 revenue RMB4.07bn) and is seeking a second listing in Hong Kong.
interesting_fact: Jingxin's only approved innovative drug is the insomnia treatment dimdazenil (Jingnuoning); it is also developing JX2201 for elevated lipoprotein(a), and is pursuing an HKEX dual listing with CITIC Securities as sole sponsor.
deep_cut_fact: His formal education started with a mechanical-engineering associate degree from Zhejiang Radio & TV University (1987); he later did Peking University Guanghua's EMBA (2000) and a China Pharmaceutical University pharmacy certificate (2004), and earned senior-economist title in Dec 2022.
notes: Board secretary Hong Yunfei (tel 0571-86575888) is the published IR route. Company is mid-way through a Hong Kong IPO (refiled Sept 2026), so may be in a quiet period.

name: Xu Xiaming
current_role: Unknown; no public record of a '许贤明' at Nanguo Real Estate. Likely refers to Xu Xiaoming (许晓明), former chairman/major shareholder of Langold Real Estate (南国置业, SZ:002305)
profile: No trace of '许贤明' linked to Nanguo found; the listing (shared with Xu Xiaoming) most likely refers to 许晓明, founder and former chairman and largest shareholder of Wuhan-based Langold Real Estate (南国置业). Filings show he was chairman with ~50% in 2012, left the board by 2019, and by 2020 was a >5% non-controlling shareholder selling down his stake.
notes: Name likely a Hurun transliteration/typo for 许晓明 (Xu Xiaoming); only appeared on Hurun 2012-2013. Sources: SZSE filings https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2012-07-20/c94d105d-83e6-4d98-beba-90ec9ad35368.PDF and https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-05-29/a97f950e-0eef-43c8-88af-5bd654594207.PDF. Low priority.

name: Christopher J Nassetta
current_role: President & CEO (and board chair) of Hilton Worldwide Holdings; director of CoStar Group
profile: Chris Nassetta was a real-estate executive (Bristol Group co-founder, then CEO of Host Hotels & Resorts) before becoming Hilton's CEO in 2007 under Blackstone ownership. He led Hilton through its 2013 IPO and 2017 spin-offs into an asset-light franchise giant; his wealth comes chiefly from Hilton stock. He also chairs industry groups such as the US Travel Association.
interesting_fact: He and Hilton's senior executives spend a week each year working hotel jobs such as housekeeping, engineering and front desk.
deep_cut_fact: His first hotel job, from summer 1980 at about 16, was in the engineering department of the Holiday Inn on Capitol Hill, mostly plunging toilets; he likes to say his career 'started in a toilet'.
notes: Highly visible CEO who does lots of media; Hilton corporate communications is the route. breakingnews@ is labelled for urgent media requests; general requests go via the contact page.

name: Charles Sirois
current_role: Chairman and Founder, Telesystem Ltd. (Montreal family holding); Chairman, NorthStar Earth & Space
profile: Charles Sirois (b. 1954, Chicoutimi, Quebec) is a Canadian telecom entrepreneur who built paging firm National Pagette into BCE Mobile, ran Teleglobe, and founded Microcell (Fido) and Telesystem International Wireless. He chaired CIBC 2009-2015 and co-founded the Coalition Avenir Quebec with Francois Legault in 2011. Today his family holding Telesystem invests in media (OnMobile, Zone3, Stingray), space (NorthStar) and cleantech (CVTCorp).
interesting_fact: In 1994 Telesystem and Ted Rogers co-founded Telesystem International Wireless, which expanded into eight countries on three continents; Telesystem also launched Fido (Microcell) in 1996, which passed 1 million subscribers within about four years of its 1997 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: His empire began in 1978 when, aged about 24, he bought out Setelco, a small paging-device business founded by his father in Chicoutimi; it became Telesystem. He also chairs and co-founded the McPeak-Sirois Group for Clinical Research in Breast Cancer, and chairs the board of Montreal engineering school ETS.
notes: Strong podcast fit: telecom/infrastructure builder, energy angle via Telesystem Energy (renewables, run by Denis M. Sirois) and CVTCorp efficient drivetrains, plus satellite data (NorthStar). Son Francois-Charles Sirois is now Telesystem President/CEO. Wikidata net worth (C$1.2bn, 2015) is dated. Team bio: https://telesystem.ca/about-us/team

name: Daniel Allen Gold
current_role: Founder and CEO, QVT Financial LP and QVT Family Office; director of Roivant Sciences and Okeanis Eco Tankers
profile: Hedge-fund manager who ran Deutsche Bank's proprietary trading group and spun it out as QVT Financial in 2003; QVT is a long-time backer of Roivant Sciences and Okeanis Eco Tankers, where he sits on the boards (Roivant compensation committee chair). His wealth reflects QVT's large Roivant stake and other public holdings.
interesting_fact: Before Deutsche Bank he worked at Daiwa Securities and Bear Stearns; he holds an A.B. in Physics from Harvard College.
deep_cut_fact: He was an original board member of rare-earths producer MP Materials when it went public in 2020, and has also sat on the boards of Awilco Drilling and energy-management firm Gridpoint, a natural energy/critical-minerals hook for the podcast.
notes: Low public profile; approach via QVT media contact. Board roles at MP Materials/Gridpoint per 2021 MP proxy; check current status before citing as present-tense.

name: Spencer Clinton
current_role: Refers to brothers Spencer McCarthy (Chairman & CEO) and Clinton McCarthy (co-founder/Managing Director) of Churchill Living (formerly Churchill Retirement Living), with their father John McCarthy
profile: The Rich List entry 'Spencer, Clinton and John McCarthy' covers the family behind Churchill Living, a privately owned UK retirement-housing developer founded in 1994 by brothers Spencer and Clinton McCarthy. Their father John McCarthy co-founded retirement-housing pioneer McCarthy & Stone in 1963. Churchill, renamed Churchill Living in 2024, manages 250+ retirement developments; Spencer is chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: The business began in 1994 as Emlor Homes building stone and thatched cottages in Hampshire, Dorset and Wiltshire; after the success of its first retirement scheme, Avon Lodge in Southbourne, it switched entirely to retirement apartments in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: The company's very first office was in Clinton McCarthy's garage in the New Forest; in 2016 it became the first retirement specialist to win WhatHouse? 'Housebuilder of the Year' (it had also won in 1998 as Emlor Homes).
notes: Input name 'Spencer Clinton' is a mangled list entry for the McCarthy family (Spencer, Clinton and father John McCarthy). John McCarthy's current status not checked. Family-owned, low-profile; best route is via Churchill Living's head office (Ringwood, Hampshire) contact page.

name: John McCarthy
current_role: Co-founder of McCarthy & Stone (left 2003); his family's wealth is now chiefly Churchill Living (Ringwood, Hampshire), run by sons Spencer and Clinton
profile: John McCarthy, a builder from New Milton, Hampshire, partnered with Bill Stone and in 1977 built their first retirement-housing development. McCarthy & Stone became the UK's largest developer of private retirement flats, floated in 1982 and was sold for £1.1bn in 2006. His sons founded Emlor Homes in 1994, now Churchill Living, a leading retirement-housing builder.
interesting_fact: McCarthy & Stone essentially created the UK's private retirement-flat market: from its first scheme in 1977 it reached around 2,600 unit sales a year by 1988.
deep_cut_fact: McCarthy described his 1977 'eureka moment' of building retirement flats for older buyers in his autobiography, 'Building a Billion'.
notes: The Rich List entry is shared with sons Clinton and Spencer McCarthy (Churchill Living). I could not confirm whether John McCarthy, now likely in his 80s, is still living; verify before outreach. Leasehold campaigners criticise his-era McCarthy & Stone lease terms, so avoid that topic. Spencer McCarthy (Churchill chairman) is the more active, reachable family member.

name: Fabricio Garcia
current_role: Vice President of Operations / Retail (physical stores and logistics), Magazine Luiza (B3: MGLU3); member of executive board
profile: Fabrício Bittar Garcia belongs to the founding family of Magazine Luiza (Magalu), the Brazilian retailer started in Franca in 1957. Forbes says he owned about 8% of the company in 2021, the year five family members joined its billionaires list. A career Magalu executive, he has run operations since 2020: physical stores, expansion, logistics and distribution. Since a 2025 reorganisation he runs 1P retail and logistics.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Garcia was one of five Trajano/Donato family members who joined the Forbes billionaires list together, after Magalu's e-commerce shift (about 69% of revenue) earned it the nickname 'the Amazon of Brazil'.
deep_cut_fact: Despite being family, he started at the bottom of the business. Garcia joined Magalu's commercial department in 1996 and worked up through purchasing roles, including a senior purchasing post in 2006-09, before becoming operations VP.
notes: Low public profile operating executive. His title comes from 2020-2025 reports (most recently a March 2025 restructuring), so check it on the IR site. Forbes calls him a grandson of founders Luiza Trajano Donato and Pelegrino Donato, but some sources say the founder had no children. Avoid stating the exact family relationship. Best route is Magalu IR or corporate communications.

name: Angeliki Frangou
current_role: Chairwoman and CEO, Navios Maritime Partners L.P. (NYSE: NMM); head of the Navios Group
profile: Greek shipowner born 1965 in Chios to a family of Kardamyla shipowners. After working as an analyst at Republic National Bank in New York, she started her own shipping business in 1990 and in 2005 took control of Navios Maritime Holdings via a SPAC; she now runs Navios Partners, a diversified dry-bulk, container and tanker owner.
interesting_fact: She acquired Navios in 2005 through a blank-check company (International Shipping Enterprises) that raised about $200m, an early use of a SPAC in shipping; Lloyd's List ranked her 29th in its 2025 list of shipping's 100 most influential people.
deep_cut_fact: She trained as a mechanical engineer (BS Fairleigh Dickinson, MS Columbia), was named the Connecticut Maritime Association's Commodore for 2011, and collects Greek, Byzantine and Chinese art and loves opera.
notes: Hosts Navios Partners quarterly earnings calls; speaks at Capital Link and Posidonia shipping forums, which may be a good outreach route.

name: Wang Donghai
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Bestsun Energy (Baichuan Energy, SSE: 600681); chairman, Baichuan Investment Group
profile: Wang Donghai (b. ~1965) is the founder and controlling shareholder of Bestsun Energy (Baichuan), a city-gas distributor based in Langfang, Hebei, with pipeline gas, LNG and gas-station operations around Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and in Hubei. He has built Baichuan's businesses since 1992 and remains chairman and general manager of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Bestsun is a family-controlled listed gas utility: Wang is the actual controller via Langfang Baichuan Asset Management, and he founded both an urban-construction developer and the gas company before taking it public.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent eight years (1984-1992) working at the Yongqing County Economic Commission in Hebei; he later served as a vice-chair of the Yongqing county CPPCC and a member of the Hebei provincial CPPCC.
notes: Bestsun Energy = Baichuan Energy (百川能源). Published board-office email (board secretary Li Simeng) is the best route. Little English-language coverage.

name: Gao Jianrong
current_role: Chairman / actual controller, Tibet Zhongyin Group (西藏中茵集团, 'Join In'), a Suzhou-based property and investment group
profile: Gao Jianrong (高建荣) controls the Zhongyin ('Join In') group with his wife Feng Feifei, who holds 40% of the group. Zhongyin built a Suzhou-area real estate business and around 2007-08 took over listed shell S*ST Tianhua, renamed Zhongyin Co. (600745), which in 2015-16 swapped out property assets for Wingtech's phone ODM business.
interesting_fact: The listed company Zhongyin took control of around 2008 (S*ST Tianhua, later Zhongyin Co.) is today Wingtech Technology, one of China's largest smartphone ODMs and owner of chipmaker Nexperia.
notes: Hurun 'Joinin' = 中茵 Zhongyin/Join In. Very low public profile; little biographical info online (ChinaVitae reportedly lists him as born 1963 in Zhejiang, but I could not open the page to verify). No published contacts found. 2012 filing showing the stake transfer to his wife: https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2012-02/29/A39/AGG0390229C.pdf

name: Feng Feifei
current_role: Director, Join.In Holdings Group (中茵控股, Shanghai) – per MarketScreener; linked to Tibet Join-In Group
profile: Feng Feifei (冯飞飞) is listed jointly with Gao Jianrong, whose Joinin (中茵) group controlled Shanghai-listed Zhongyin Co. (600745) and its Suzhou-area property business until it was reverse-merged into Wingtech Technology in 2016; Gao exited most of his stake in 2017. Feng appears as a director of Join.In Holdings Group and is linked to Tibet Join-In and Wingtech.
interesting_fact: The Joinin-controlled listed shell, Zhongyin Co. (600745), became Wingtech Technology through a 2016 backdoor listing; Gao Jianrong cut his stake from 15.65% to 2.29% in 2017.
notes: Relationship to Gao Jianrong not confirmed in sources found (do not assume spouse). Role details only from aggregator https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/FEI-FEI-FENG-A1FOL7/experience. Very private; no direct channel found.

name: Shao Xionghui
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Zhaomin New Material Technology (肇民科技, SZSE: 301000)
profile: Shao Xionghui (邵雄辉, b. 1976) controls Shanghai Zhaomin (Hurun English 'Hajime'), a ChiNext-listed maker of precision engineering-plastic parts for auto powertrain, thermal-management and appliance systems. He joined its Japanese-invested predecessor Zhaomin Precision Plastics in 2003, rose to general manager, took over the business in 2012 and has been chairman and GM since 2019; re-elected June 2025.
interesting_fact: He started out in tourism, not manufacturing: from 1996 to 2003 he worked in the Japan department of Hunan Huatian International Travel Service, rising to deputy head, before moving into the Japanese-founded plastics firm he would later own.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he spent seven years (1996-2003) at Hunan Huatian International Travel Service's Japan department, going from staff member to deputy department head; his Japan background carried into Zhaomin Precision Plastics (Shanghai), where he worked his way up from manufacturing-department head.
notes: Board secretary is Xiao Jun (肖俊). Low media profile; best route is the company securities office email. Holds ~18m shares directly plus ~90m via Shanghai Jizhao and other vehicles.

name: Chang Hao
current_role: Reported owner of Zhehou New Energy (哲厚新能源), Beijing (chemicals/new energy), per Hurun 2021; not independently confirmed
profile: Chang Hao (常浩) appears only on the Hurun China Rich List 2021 (RMB5.6bn, rank 1281) under Zhehou New Energy (哲厚新能源), Beijing, listed as chemicals / new energy. No company website, exchange filing or press coverage could be found to confirm the business or his role.
notes: Hurun 2021: 常浩, Beijing; company 哲厚新能源 / Zhehou New Energy, industry 化工; no birth year. Searched Chinese (哲厚新能源 常浩; 北京哲厚新能源科技开发 股东) and English and found nothing. Wealth may come from a listed-company stake held via Zhehou (unverified). Registry sites, Baidu and cninfo were blocked. A registry search for 哲厚 is the next step.

name: Jiang Yongzhong
current_role: Director (since 1997), Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (600460.SH); chairman and GM of subsidiary Hangzhou Mecarel Optoelectronics (美卡乐)
profile: Jiang Zhongyong (江忠永; Hurun: 江永忠) is one of seven co-founders and joint controllers of Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (founded 1997), an IDM chipmaker making power semiconductors, ICs and LEDs for autos and new energy. He has been a director since 1997 and runs Silan's LED unit.
interesting_fact: Silan is one of China's few privately founded IDM chipmakers, designing and fabricating its own power devices and ICs, and is controlled jointly by its seven founders alongside China's national 'Big Fund' as a major shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs Hangzhou Mecarel (美卡乐) Optoelectronics, Silan's LED-packaging subsidiary building a premium 'Mecarel' brand of high-reliability LED display pixel tubes; its revenue grew about 48% in 2024.
notes: Name discrepancy: Silan filings spell him 江忠永 (Jiang Zhongyong); Hurun's 江永忠 appears to be a transposition, since Silan has no co-founder named 江永忠. Very low media profile. IR email is the board secretary / securities affairs office published in the 2024 annual report.

name: Xu Limin
current_role: Vice Chairman and Director, Beijing Oriental Yuhong Waterproof Technology Co. (SZSE: 002271)
profile: Xu Limin (许利民), born 1966 and a Peking University graduate, is described in company filings as a principal co-founder of Oriental Yuhong, China's largest waterproofing-materials maker. He joined in 1998 and rose from vice GM to executive vice GM to vice chairman, a role he still holds; he owns roughly 72 million shares.
interesting_fact: Oriental Yuhong, founded in 1995 and listed in Shenzhen in 2008, has gone global: it set up a plant in Trinidad and Tobago with Lake Asphalt (2013) and broke ground on a factory and logistics centre in Prairie View, Texas in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond waterproofing, he has been executive director of a Beijing film and TV media company, Beijing Xingle Yinghua Film & Television Culture Media, since 2011, and was a director of environmental firm Beijing GeoEnviron (高能环境) from 2002 to 2009.
notes: Low media profile compared with chairman/founder Li Weiguo. Best route is the board secretary's office (stocks@yuhong.com.cn).

name: Zheng Shaobo
current_role: Director, Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics (600460.SH); director of affiliate Shiteng Technology
profile: Zheng Shaobo (郑少波) is one of seven co-founders of Hangzhou Silan Microelectronics, who act together as its controlling group under chairman Chen Xiangdong. Silan is a major Chinese maker of power semiconductors, analog ICs and MEMS, now expanding into silicon-carbide chips for EVs.
interesting_fact: Silan has moved fast into silicon carbide: it began building a SiC power-device line in 2022, passed 5,000 wafers a month by 2024, and is building an 8-inch SiC line in Xiamen planned for 720,000 wafers a year.
deep_cut_fact: Silan began in 1997 as Hangzhou Silan Electronics, founded by Zheng and six colleagues: Chen Xiangdong, Fan Weihong, Jiang Zhongyong, Luo Huabing, Song Weiquan and Chen Guohua. All seven are still named together as the company's controlling group almost three decades later.
notes: Low-profile engineer-founder; Chairman Chen Xiangdong is the public face. Approach through Silan's securities affairs office (IR email published in shareholder-meeting notices). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Liu Yongliang
current_role: Founder, Executive Director and Chairman, Canggang Railway Ltd (HKEX: 2169)
profile: Liu Yongliang (b. c.1967) founded Canggang Railway, a local freight railway operator in Hebei. Its Canggang line runs from Cangzhou to the Bohai New Area and Huanghua Port and links with the Shuohuang and Hanhuang lines to move mainly coal toward the coast. He has chaired the operating company since 2009 and took the group public in Hong Kong in October 2020. He controls about 40% through Jinghai BVI.
interesting_fact: Before railways, Liu invested in coal trading, industrial property and storage/transport. Canggang now describes itself as Hebei's leading local railway operator and connects the Beijing-Shanghai line to the Bohai New Area.
deep_cut_fact: His education was in military finance: he trained in financial management at the PLA Navy Logistics College in Tianjin (graduated 1991), later did postgraduate finance at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (1999), and attended Peking University's post-EMBA courses from 2012 to 2014.
notes: Hurun lists his country as blank; he is mainland Chinese (Hebei). The only published channel is the company's general contact mailbox (a 126.com address on the official website). He reduced his stake from about 48% to 40% in September 2025.

name: Chen Qiong
current_role: Director and Deputy General Manager, Sirio Pharma Co., Ltd. (仙乐健康, SZSE: 300791), Shantou
profile: Chen Qiong (b. 1966) and her husband Lin Peiqing are the actual controllers of Sirio Pharma, together holding ~46% of the Shantou-based contract maker of nutrition and health products. The firm began as a drug maker in the early 1990s and pivoted to nutraceuticals after 2000; it calls itself the world's No.2 gummy and softgel solutions provider, earns 60%+ of revenue abroad and filed for a Hong Kong listing in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Sirio ranks third globally in nutrition-and-health-food solutions by 2024 revenue, and is building a plant in Thailand (due 2027) with planned capacity of 2.4 billion gummies a year.
deep_cut_fact: A pharmacist by training (master's degree), she started as a formulation researcher at the research institute of the Tuobin pharmaceutical factory in Shantou, then was quality head at Shantou Meiji Pharmaceutical before co-running Sirio.
notes: Wealth shared with husband Lin Peiqing (chairman/GM), who is the public face of the company. IR email is the board secretary's office per the 2025 annual report. Low personal media profile.

name: Jared Isaacman
current_role: 15th Administrator of NASA (since Dec 18, 2025); largest shareholder of Shift4 Payments
profile: Isaacman founded what became Shift4 Payments at 16 in 1999 and took it public in 2020; he also co-founded Draken International. He commanded the SpaceX missions Inspiration4 (2021) and Polaris Dawn (2024). He left Shift4's board after the Senate confirmed him as NASA Administrator in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: He is a fighter-jet pilot (call sign 'Rook') who bought a Soviet MiG-29 from Paul Allen's estate. As commander of Polaris Dawn in 2024 he made the first commercial spacewalk.
deep_cut_fact: In 2009, on his second attempt, he set the record for flying around the world in a light jet: 61 hours, 51 minutes and 15 seconds, about 20 hours faster than the previous record. He also left high school at 16, earned a GED, and later got an online aeronautics degree from Embry-Riddle (2011).

public_contacts.value: george.a.alderman@nasa.gov (Deputy Press Secretary for NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman)

notes: He is a sitting US government official, so interview requests go through NASA's press office ('Leadership Interview Requests'). He is a strong fit for an energy/space podcast because of his push on nuclear propulsion and surface power.

name: Michael F. Petrie
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Merchants Bancorp (Nasdaq: MBIN), Carmel, Indiana; Chairman of Merchants Bank of Indiana
profile: Michael Petrie co-founded Merchants Capital Corp., a multifamily and healthcare mortgage lender, with Randall Rogers in August 1990. It grew into Merchants Bancorp, an Indiana bank holding company focused on multifamily and affordable-housing finance that listed on Nasdaq in 2017. He has been chairman and CEO since 2006, and his large insider stake underpins his wealth.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he chaired the Mortgage Bankers Association's Board of Directors in Washington, D.C., and he has more than 40 years in mortgage banking.
deep_cut_fact: An Indiana University lifer (BS and MBA in finance), he serves on the IU Varsity Club's National Board and the advisory board of IU's Center for Real Estate Studies. He is also a trustee of the Michael F. Petrie & Jody J. Petrie Foundation and a director of the Indianapolis Neighborhood Housing Partnership.
notes: Contacts are from the Feb 19, 2026 press release (investor contact Tami Durle, media contact Rebecca Marsh). Affordable-housing finance angle; quoted regularly in quarterly results.

name: Yang Longzhong
current_role: Early BYD executive and shareholder; former BYD Vice President (sales), resigned 2012; no current public role found
profile: Yang Longzhong (杨龙忠) joined BYD in February 1995, the month it was founded, as deputy GM and later became Vice President running sales and marketing. His wealth comes from his early BYD shareholding, which has kept him on the Hurun China Rich List as BYD grew into the world's top EV maker. He stepped down as VP in Sept 2012 and also served as a director of the BYD Charity Foundation.
interesting_fact: He was part of BYD's founding-era team: BYD started in Feb 1995 with about 20 staff making rechargeable batteries, and Yang was deputy general manager from that very month.
deep_cut_fact: A trained metallurgist: he studied metallurgical physical chemistry at Central South University of Technology (1983-87), then worked as an engineer at Jiangxi Copper's Dexing Copper Mine and at Shenzhen Bi Ge Battery before joining BYD.
notes: Very private; no public channels. Only route is via BYD corporate. Resignation as BYD VP effective 27 Sep 2012 (https://marketscreener.com/quote/stock/BYD-COMPANY-LIMITED-5640763/news/BYD-Company-Ltd-Announces-Resignation-of-Yang-Long-zhong-as-Vice-President-39254980). Alive inferred from continued Hurun listing through 2026.

name: Kenneth Duda
current_role: Co-founder, President and Chief Technology Officer, Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) (President role since Sept 2025)
profile: Ken Duda co-founded Arista Networks in 2004 with Andy Bechtolsheim and David Cheriton and is lead architect of its EOS network operating system; he was acting president 2005-2008 and CTO/SVP software engineering from 2011. Arista's high-speed Ethernet switches are core infrastructure in cloud and AI data centers. Holds three MIT engineering degrees and a Stanford CS PhD.
interesting_fact: He is a co-author of the IETF's VXLAN specification, the overlay standard widely used to build virtualised data-center networks.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first employee of Granite Systems (the Bechtolsheim/Cheriton gigabit startup bought by Cisco), led software for Cisco's Catalyst 4000 line, then was CTO of virtual world There.com, designing a real-time 3-D distributed system for thousands of simultaneous users.
notes: Engineer's engineer; writes on Arista's blog and speaks at networking events (ONUG). Press contact is Arista Corporate Communications (Amanda Jaramillo, published on releases). Very on-topic for AI data-center networking.

name: Jihan Wu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Bitdeer Technologies Group (NASDAQ: BTDR), Singapore
profile: Chongqing-born (1986) Singaporean entrepreneur who co-founded Bitmain with Micree Zhan in 2013, building the dominant bitcoin-mining chip maker, then left in 2021 with the Bitdeer spin-off; he also founded Matrixport (2019). Bitdeer now designs its own SEALMINER ASICs and is converting mining sites (e.g. 180 MW Tydal, Norway) into NVIDIA-based AI cloud data centers.
interesting_fact: Wu was the first to translate Satoshi Nakamoto's Bitcoin white paper into Chinese (late 2011). In 2022 Bitdeer bought Le Freeport, Singapore's high-security 'Fort Knox' art and valuables vault, for S$40m.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics and psychology at Peking University and worked as a PE financial analyst. In May 2011 he raised 100,000 yuan from family and friends to buy about 900 bitcoins, and with Chang Jia co-founded Babite (8btc), China's first bitcoin community site.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-center/AI angle: Bitdeer is pivoting crypto-mining power capacity to AI cloud (Norway, Malaysia up to 350 MW by Q1 2028, US sites) and sold its BTC treasury in 2026 to fund it. IR contact is Tesh Dahya (Head of IR); media contact Eunice Hwangbo (Director, Corporate Communications) per Bitdeer releases; verify latest release. Ir.bitdeer.com blocks scripted access.

name: Shi Pingxiang
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Guangdong Huate Gas Co., Ltd. (华特气体, SSE STAR: 688268)
profile: Shi Pingxiang (石平湘) founded Foshan-based Huate Gas, which grew from industrial gases into electronic specialty gases (e.g. high-purity fluorocarbons and lithography gases) for chip fabs. It supplies most of China's 8-inch-plus fabs and international chipmakers. He co-holds the stake with Shi Sihui, per Hurun.
interesting_fact: By end-2019 Huate held 101 patents, had helped draft 30 national standards and replaced imports in nearly 20 products such as high-purity hexafluoroethane and trifluoromethane.
deep_cut_fact: Shi worked as a farmer for eight years before becoming a civil servant. Remembering a CO2 gas well he had seen erupt in Sanshui while a farmer, he proposed tapping it so a Foshan container project could get carbon dioxide. He was then moved to a new CO2 research institute, his entry into the gas industry.
notes: Low public profile outside Chinese financial press. Best route is via the company's board secretary office (board secretary Wan Lingzhi per 2026 IR activity records) or SSE e-Interaction; found no published IR email in an accessible source. Hurun lists wealth shared with Shi Sihui.

name: Shi Sihui
current_role: Chairwoman and legal representative, Guangdong Huate Gas Co., Ltd. (688268.SH, STAR Market), Foshan
profile: Shi Sihui (石思慧, b. 1978) took over as chair of Huate Gas in June 2025, succeeding founder Shi Pingxiang, who stays on as vice chairman. She joined the family company in 2009 as assistant to the general manager and was later vice president and vice chair. Huate makes electronic specialty gases for chip and display fabs and is a domestic substitute for imported semiconductor gases.
interesting_fact: Huate says it supplies over 90% of China's 8-inch-and-above IC fabs and has entered the supply chains of Intel, Micron, TSMC, SK Hynix, Infineon and Samsung. It was the only gas company named to China's 'Top 10 Electronic Chemical Materials' list in four editions (2017-2023).
deep_cut_fact: At Huate's May 2026 earnings call, Shi said helium made up about 12% of 2025 revenue, cautioned investors that helium prices may fall back, and said the next growth push is silicon-based gases using disilane as the entry point.
notes: Wealth is shared with Huate founder Shi Pingxiang (b. 1948). zhengqb@ is the securities-affairs office email registered with the exchange; board secretary is Wan Lingzhi. The STCN source for the deep-cut fact could not be opened directly from this environment (it came via search), so double-check it before use.

name: Guo Wei
current_role: Chairman, Digital China Group (SZSE: 000034); also chairs Digital China Holdings (HKEX: 0861)
profile: Guo Wei joined Legend (Lenovo) in 1988 and became one of Liu Chuanzhi's key lieutenants. When Legend split in 2000, he took the distribution/IT-services business that became Digital China, while Yang Yuanqing kept the Lenovo PC brand. He still chairs Digital China, now a major IT distributor pushing into cloud, data-center and 'Shenzhou Kunpeng' server businesses.
interesting_fact: On May 12, 2000, Liu Chuanzhi split Legend in two at a rally, handing one banner to Guo Wei (Digital China) and the other to Yang Yuanqing (Lenovo).
deep_cut_fact: Fresh from a master's at the USTC graduate school in Beijing (1988, aged 25), he was talked into Legend by Liu Chuanzhi, made PR manager within months, and coined Legend's famous slogan 'If humanity lost Legend (imagination), what would the world be like?'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly executive with frequent public speeches on digital transformation and computing infrastructure; good data-center/AI angle. Approach via Digital China board secretary/IR mailbox.

name: Lou Tiancheng
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director & CTO, Pony AI Inc. (Nasdaq: PONY; HKEX dual listing Nov 2025)
profile: Lou Tiancheng ('ACRush') is a legendary competitive programmer (two-time Google Code Jam champion, long-time Topcoder leader) who worked on Google's self-driving project (later Waymo) and at Baidu before co-founding Pony.ai with James Peng in 2016. As CTO he leads Pony's L4 robotaxi technology.
interesting_fact: Pony.ai launched what it called China's first public robotaxi service in Nansha, Guangzhou on 2 Feb 2018 after a months-long sprint; Lou was said to work about 100 hours a week during that push.
deep_cut_fact: Invited as a guest speaker to the East Asian round of the Topcoder Open in Sept 2020, he gave his talk to 100+ young contestants and then, without telling anyone, entered the contest himself half an hour later.
notes: Engineer-first, gives occasional technical interviews (e.g. PonyWorld 2.0 with Autonomous Vehicle International). Quote: 'The only things truly in your control are focus and hard work.' Route via Pony.ai IR/comms.

name: Steve Sanghi
current_role: President, CEO and Chair of the Board, Microchip Technology (NASDAQ: MCHP); director of Intel and Impinj
profile: Indian-born engineer (b. 1955) who left Intel for Waferscale Integration, then joined near-bankrupt Microchip in 1990 and ran it as CEO 1991-2021, building it into a major microcontroller/analog maker. He returned as CEO in Nov 2024, was made permanent in July 2025 and is leading the turnaround; he joined Intel's board in Dec 2024.
interesting_fact: Northern Arizona University renamed its engineering college the Steve Sanghi College of Engineering in Oct 2024, and in 2026 named the Maria and Steve Sanghi College of Nursing.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a business-advice column for the Arizona Republic, collected as the book 'Ask Steve' (Oct 2024), after his 2023 memoir 'Up and to the Right'. He holds a 1975 electronics degree from Punjab Engineering College and an MS from UMass Amherst.

public_contacts.value: Investor relations: Sajid Daudi, Head of IR, (480) 792-7385 (no email published)

notes: Publicly engaged author/columnist; his books and the NAU colleges are good hooks. Microchip IR (Sajid Daudi) or corporate communications is the formal route. The ir_email entry is a phone line because no IR email is published.

name: Shao Jianxiong
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Hoymiles Power Electronics (688032.SH); executive director & GM, Hangkai Holding Group
profile: Shao Jianxiong (邵建雄) chairs Hangzhou-based Hoymiles, a leading maker of solar microinverters, storage and balcony-solar systems, which listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. He controls it through Hangkai Holding Group, the Hangzhou industrial group he has run since the 2000s; Hoymiles' technology was co-founded by Zhejiang University power-electronics researchers Yang Bo and Zhao Yi.
interesting_fact: Hoymiles was built by pairing an established Hangzhou industrial group (Shao's Hangkai) with Zhejiang University power-electronics academics; CEO Yang Bo was a ZJU postdoc/researcher until 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Shao has been a director/chairman of Hangkai enterprise management since Aug 2002 and Hangkai Group's executive director and GM since Sept 2007; he took Hoymiles' chair in Sept 2017 after a few months as executive director.
notes: Not the technical founder (that is CEO Yang Bo / CTO Zhao Yi) - frame outreach around Hangkai/Hoymiles ownership. Strong solar/energy-storage fit for podcast. Route via board office (董秘办).

name: Bo Shijiu
current_role: Founder, Executive Director & CEO, Changjiu Holdings (HKEX: 6959); Chairman, Beijing Changjiu Logistics (SSE: 603569)
profile: Automotive-logistics pioneer with 30+ years in the sector. He founded Changjiu Industrial in 1999 and has chaired Beijing Changjiu Logistics (car transport/supply-chain, Shanghai-listed 2016) since 2003; Changjiu Holdings, listed in Hong Kong in 2024, provides digital inventory-supervision services to auto dealers. Co-controls the group with his wife, chairwoman Li Guiping.
interesting_fact: He led Beijing Changjiu Logistics to a Shanghai Stock Exchange listing in August 2016 and later took a second business, Changjiu Holdings, public in Hong Kong in January 2024.
deep_cut_fact: His career began inside FAW: from 1993 to 2003 he headed First Automobile Works' Fada vehicle-delivery service department; he also earned a Jilin University business degree in 1997 while working and has been president of the CFLP China Automotive Logistics Association since 2010.
notes: Low international profile. Route via Changjiu Holdings / Beijing Changjiu Logistics IR (board secretary). Wealth shared with wife Li Guiping.

name: Wang Jun
current_role: Founder (and CEO per Wikipedia) of iCarbonX (碳云智能), Shenzhen/Zhuhai
profile: Genomics scientist (b. 1976) who in 1999, while a Peking University PhD student, founded BGI's bioinformatics group, later becoming BGI's CEO; his teams sequenced the first Asian genome, rice, SARS, the giant panda and the human gut microbiome. In 2015 he left BGI to found iCarbonX, an AI/multi-omics health company that now makes silicon-based biochips and works on drug discovery.
interesting_fact: iCarbonX raised over US$100m in its Series A within about six months of founding, valuing it near US$1bn; Wang described its goal as 'digitising life and longevity'. He presented iCarbonX at TED 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He was named in Nature's 10 (2012) and Fortune's 40 under 40 (2013), won the 2005 Lundbeck Talent Prize, and held an Ole Rømer professorship at the University of Copenhagen.
notes: Input lists Chinese name 王军, but the BGI/iCarbonX founder is 王俊; profile assumes the iCarbonX founder (matches source_of_wealth). Fits a data/AI angle. iCarbonX also lists bd@icarbonx.com for business enquiries. Could not confirm his current title in 2026.

name: Su Zengfu (苏增福)
current_role: Founder; chairman of Supor Group (苏泊尔集团, the family holding company, separate from SEB-controlled listed Zhejiang Supor) per last available profiles
profile: Born c.1940-41 in Yuhuan, Zhejiang, Su rose from supply clerk to director of a township pressure-cooker parts factory, then in 1994 co-founded cookware brand Supor with his son Su Xianze; it listed in Shenzhen in 2004 and became China's top pressure-cooker brand. The family sold control to France's Groupe SEB from 2006-2011 and Su moved into stainless faucets, pharma, ports, logistics and property.
interesting_fact: Supor was born of necessity: when Shenyang's 'Shuangxi' cooker maker revoked the trademark his factory had licensed (Dec 1994), the family registered their own brand; 'SUPER' was refused, so on the spot they changed one letter to 'SUPOR'.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he served eight years in the PLA Navy (enlisting in 1960 at 19), then worked as a supply-and-marketing clerk for a commune enterprise in Chenyu town; he was also a deputy to the 10th National People's Congress.
notes: Now about 85-86; no recent (2024-26) news found and no death report found, so alive status unverified. No published personal/office contact; family no longer tied to listed Supor (chaired by SEB's Thierry de La Tour d'Artaise). Son Su Xianze is the more public family member.

name: Chen Haibin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Dian Diagnostics Group (迪安诊断, SZSE: 300244), Hangzhou
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (b. 1969, CEIBS EMBA) who started a diagnostics business in 1996 and founded Dian in 2001; it listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2011 and grew into one of China's largest independent clinical laboratory networks, combining lab services with IVD product distribution. Chairman since 2019 (previously also GM); remains the controlling shareholder as of 2026.
interesting_fact: He attended Jack Ma's Hupan University (湖畔大学) entrepreneur program; Dian, which marks its 30th anniversary in 2026, frames its expansion around a 'bamboo forest' (竹林) strategy of interconnected businesses.
deep_cut_fact: Per his own shareholder letter, the business began in 1996 in a bare ~30 m2 office in Hangzhou; less than two years in, a national clean-up of the PCR testing market forced a pivot to independent medical laboratories - the 'products + services' model Dian is built on.
notes: Former Zhejiang CPPCC member; chairs the Zhejiang Health Industry Federation. IR/board secretary (Tao Jun) is the realistic route; Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Gao Lufeng
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Segway-Ninebot (九号公司, SSE STAR: 689009)
profile: Beihang University engineering graduate who co-founded Ninebot with fellow alumnus Wang Ye in 2012 to make self-balancing scooters. In 2015, backed by Xiaomi and Sequoia, Ninebot bought its former patent rival Segway outright. Segway-Ninebot listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020 and now sells e-scooters, e-mopeds, robot lawnmowers and service robots.
interesting_fact: Ninebot bought Segway in April 2015, while Segway had a patent complaint pending against it. Gao said of the old rival: 'It seemed like we were facing a competitor that was tough to beat.'
deep_cut_fact: His first venture with Wang Ye, started in 2003 as he graduated from Beihang, was a smart-toy project that sold 2,000+ units before failing over quality, manufacturing and cash-flow problems. In 2009 Wang phoned him to reunite, which led to their balance-scooter business.
notes: No published IR or press email found. IR filings name board secretary Xu Peng as the investor contact (via SSE e-interaction). Strong fit for an energy/EV-mobility episode.

name: Li Hong
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder, Guangzhou ZWSOFT Co. (中望软件, SSE STAR: 688083); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Li Hong (李红) is a co-founding shareholder of ZWSOFT, the Guangzhou maker of ZWCAD (2D, DWG-compatible) and ZW3D CAD software, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Records show her holding 19.5% alongside chairman/GM Du Yulin (68.5%) in 2010, and she was one of three promoters when the firm became a joint-stock company in Nov 2006.
interesting_fact: ZWSOFT is one of China's leading domestic industrial-design software makers, positioned as a home-grown alternative to Autodesk/Dassault CAD tools amid China's push for software self-sufficiency.
notes: Very common name; no public biography found. Hurun lists her with Du Yulin (chairman/GM), who is the public face. Personal relationship to Du not verified here. Route via ZWSOFT board secretary/IR (ir@zwsoft.com).

profile: Li Guiping and her husband Bo Shijiu (Changjiu chairman) jointly control the Changjiu group, which grew from Jilin into one of China's largest finished-vehicle logistics providers (Changjiu Logistics, listed in Shanghai) and an auto dealership business, Changjiu Holdings, listed in Hong Kong in January 2024.

notes: Very low public profile; husband Bo Shijiu is the public face (chairman, logistics-association roles). Best route is the company's board office mailbox. Little personal biographical info is published.

name: Wang Weiyao
current_role: Founder and chairman, Jiangsu World Group (Wode / 沃得集团), Danyang, Jiangsu
profile: Wang Weiyao (王伟耀, b. 1963, Danyang) founded World Group, a Danyang-based machinery conglomerate whose World Agricultural Machinery unit is one of China's largest makers of rice combine harvesters; it also makes forging presses (World Precision Machinery), construction and garden machinery, auto parts and develops property.
interesting_fact: He built World Group from a small textile-machinery accessories workshop founded in 1988 into a group with ~20,000 staff; its harvesters are sold across China and exported to dozens of countries.
deep_cut_fact: After finishing Picheng Middle School in 1982, his first venture was the Danyang Textile Machinery Accessories Factory (1988); he later added crankshaft, filter and kitchen-equipment plants before moving into combine harvesters in 1997. He holds an MBA from Nanjing University of Science and Technology and a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: Identity inferred from 'World' source-of-wealth label (no Forbes bio in input); Wang Weiyao of World (Wode) Group is the only strong match. Very private; Chinese-language outreach via group website contact page likely best.

name: Jiang Chun
current_role: Chairman, Anhui Truchum Advanced Materials & Technology (Chujiang New Materials, SZSE: 002171), Wuhu
profile: Jiang Chun (姜纯), born 1960 in Wuhu, has spent 40+ years in copper processing. He built Truchum (楚江新材) into a major maker of copper strip, wire and specialty alloys, later expanding into carbon-fiber composites and high-end equipment via acquisitions; he is the controlling shareholder and chairman.
interesting_fact: Jiang has used acquisitions as Truchum's main growth engine, steering a traditional copper-processing business into advanced materials such as carbon-fiber composites for aerospace.
deep_cut_fact: A metal-forming (压力加工) graduate of Jiangxi Institute of Metallurgy, Jiang joined the newly founded Wuhu Nonferrous Metal Rolling Mill in 1986 and became its director in 1991 at age 31, turning the near-bankrupt plant profitable.
notes: Board-office email listed in the 2024 annual report. Rarely gives interviews; Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Hu Gang
current_role: Chairman, Newland Technology Group; controlling shareholder of Newland Digital Technology (SZSE: 000997)
profile: Fuzhou-born engineer (b. 1958, Fuzhou University automatic control) who founded Fujian Start Computer in 1988, then left in 1994 to found Newland Group. Newland Digital makes payment terminals/POS, barcode and IoT scanning hardware and runs merchant payment services; Hu controls it via Newland Group.
interesting_fact: Before founding Newland he founded Fujian Start (实达) Computer in 1988, aged 29, and later served as its group president; he left in January 1994 to start Newland.
deep_cut_fact: As a young engineer in 1989-90 he led development of the STAR-500 and STAR-600 Chinese/Western-language computer terminals, the latter a national Torch Program project; in 1992 he was promoted to senior engineer out of the normal sequence (破格).
notes: Bio details from user-contributed profile site (maigoo) consistent with company filings; Newland Digital chairman role may be held by others - Hu is group chairman/actual controller.

current_role: Chairman, Solareast Holdings (日出东方, 603366.SS) and its controlling shareholder Sunrain Holding Group (太阳雨控股集团)
profile: Founder of the Sunrain (太阳雨) and Micoe (四季沐歌) brands. He built Solareast, based in Lianyungang, Jiangsu, from a small workshop into one of China's largest solar water-heater makers. It is listed in Shanghai, also owns the kitchen-appliance brand Sacon (帅康), and has been moving into air-source heat pumps and other low-carbon heating.
interesting_fact: His solar-thermal company grew from a small workshop in Lianyungang into a leader of China's solar water-heater industry, the world's largest. Its brands Sunrain and Micoe became household names.
deep_cut_fact: On 16 August 2023 he gave the welcome speech at the ground-breaking of Micoe's 'heat-pump zero-carbon laboratory building' at the group's Lianyungang HQ. It is a whole building dedicated to air-source heat-pump R&D, part of his push to move the solar-heater group into heat pumps.

Born 1964 and a Peking University Guanghua alumnus, per a brand-directory site I could not confirm. Low media profile. Good fit for the energy-transition / heat-pump angle.

profile: Zhao Kui (赵魁, b. 1960) is a long-serving vice chairman of Inner Mongolia's Erdos Group, the cashmere-to-coal, ferroalloy, chemicals and power conglomerate led by Wang Linxiang. Its listed arm, Erdos Resources (600295/900936), reported revenue of 25.7B yuan in 2025. Hurun ranked him among Inner Mongolia's richest: 7.8B yuan in 2021 and 6.1B yuan in 2023.

name: Deng Xueqin

profile: Deng Xueqin (邓学勤), born 1967 and a Shenzhen University graduate, worked in Shenzhen Bao'an's construction bureau before going into business. He built the Zhengzhong (正中) property and industrial-park group, then took control of Shandong Kexing. He has chaired Kexing Biopharm since 2019 and took it public on the STAR Market in 2020. It traces back to a 1989 Shenzhen venture set up to commercialise the work of academician Hou Yunde, the 'father of Chinese interferon'. That venture's vaccine arm became the separate Sinovac.

name: Peng Yijie
current_role: Senior Vice President and Chief Sustainability Officer, Ant Group (as of latest 2025 sources; 2026 status unconfirmed)
profile: Peng Yijie (Sabrina Peng, 彭翼捷) joined Alibaba in May 2000, was a VP overseeing its B2B marketplaces (2008-12) and founded the AliExpress product, then built Alipay's international business from 2012. Later Ant's CMO and head of social good/green development, she became Ant Group's first Chief Sustainability Officer in May 2022. Her wealth stems from Alibaba/Ant equity.
interesting_fact: She founded AliExpress as a product inside Alibaba, and when Alibaba's 27 partners were named in 2014 she was the youngest of them.
deep_cut_fact: Her Alibaba employee number was 152 – she joined in May 2000, when the company was barely a year old (AliExpress founding per https://fintechfestival.sg/speakers-archive-2023/1622-sabrina-yijie-peng).
notes: Speaks publicly on carbon neutrality / ESG (says Ant's data centres are its main Scope 3 emissions source) – good fit for energy/data-centre angle. Reach via Ant Group media relations; 2026 role and Alibaba-partner status unconfirmed.

name: Han Hongwei
current_role: Founder/controller of Hywin Wealth (海银财富) and chairman of China Guijiu Group (中国贵酒集团); reportedly in police custody since Sept 2024
profile: Han Hongwei (韩宏伟) built Shanghai-based Hywin Wealth, a third-party wealth manager whose holding company listed on Nasdaq, and China Guijiu Group, a baijiu business that controlled Shanghai-listed Yanshi/Shanghai Guijiu (600696), run by his son Han Xiao. In Sept 2024 Shanghai police opened an illegal-fundraising case against Hywin Wealth and took several suspects, including Han Xiao, into criminal custody; media reported Han Hongwei was among those taken.
interesting_fact: A self-described army veteran, he said in 2020 that he aimed to use Guijiu's 'military liquor' range to help 30,000 retired servicemen start their own businesses.
notes: NOT SUITABLE FOR OUTREACH: Hywin Wealth is under criminal investigation for illegal fundraising (~RMB 70bn of investor products halted); son Han Xiao detained; Shanghai Guijiu (600696) was ordered delisted in 2026. Reports say Han Hongwei was taken away by police in Sept 2024 (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2024-09-11/3554578.html). No contacts recorded.

name: Han Xiao
current_role: Actual controller (~55.9%) of Shanghai Jundao Liquor Enterprise Development (formerly Rock/Shanghai Guijiu, ex-SSE: 600696, now delisted); no longer chairman
profile: Han Xiao (韩啸), in his mid-30s, became the actual controller and chairman of Shanghai-listed Rock Holdings, which was turned into a baijiu company (Shanghai Guijiu, later Jundao Liquor). He is the son of Han Hongwei of China Guijiu Group; the family's wealth was also tied to wealth manager HY Win Wealth. The listed company has since been delisted.
interesting_fact: The listed shell he controlled has one of the longest name histories on the Shanghai market: Fujian Haosheng -> Lijia -> Duolun -> Pitupi (匹凸匹) -> Rock (岩石) -> Jundao Liquor, before being delisted.
notes: CAUTION: Sept 2024 reports said Han Xiao was placed under criminal compulsory measures amid a police probe into an affiliate over suspected illegal fundraising (https://news.ycwb.com/2024-09/12/content_52923365.htm); company delisted. Not a suitable outreach target; no published contact.

name: Ke Lei
current_role: Director and Assistant to the President, Keboda Technology Co., Ltd. (603786.SH)
profile: Ke Lei (b. 1985) is a director of Keboda Technology, a Shanghai-based auto-electronics maker (lighting and motor control, energy management, central computing and ADAS domain controllers) that listed in Shanghai in 2019. He is a nephew of the co-controlling founders Ke Guihua and Ke Binghua and acts in concert with them. He owns 25% of Keboda Holding (about 59% of the company) plus about 3% directly.
interesting_fact: Keboda, founded in 2003 by Wenzhou-born entrepreneur Ke Guihua, has moved from lighting control modules into central computing platforms and smart-driving domain controllers.
deep_cut_fact: He started in Keboda's infrastructure/construction department as a supervisor and also ran MRO purchasing. From 2018 he was deputy director of the procurement centre, then worked in the intelligent light-source centre before joining the board.
notes: Low profile, operations-focused next-generation family member. Chairman/president Ke Guihua is the company's public face. Contact through the board office email.

name: Lin Qibin
current_role: Director (founder, former chairman), Changchun Engley Automobile Industry Co. (英利汽车, SSE STAR: 688584)
profile: Lin Qibin (林启彬), a Taiwanese entrepreneur born in 1953, founded Changchun Engley, a maker of lightweight car-body structural and crash-management parts for premium carmakers. He was executive director/chairman from the company's founding until 2022 and now sits on the board, alongside running Changchun Hongyun Yunduan Technology and chairing holding vehicle Engley Industrial (Cayman).
interesting_fact: Engley supplies body and crash-safety parts to FAW-Volkswagen, Beijing Benz, Volvo Asia Pacific, BMW Brilliance, SAIC-VW, SAIC-GM, Geely and Hongqi, focusing on vehicle lightweighting.
deep_cut_fact: He is a graduate of Ta Hwa University of Science and Technology (大华科技大学) in Hsinchu, Taiwan, and built his auto-parts business in Changchun, home of FAW.
notes: Taiwan national, age 73 per 2025 annual report. Stepped back from chairman role in 2022; control now with the next generation of management. Very low media profile; IR email is the practical route.

name: Tao Chunfeng
current_role: Chairman, Ningbo Changhong Polymer Technology (长鸿高科, 605008.SH); founder and chairman, Keyuan Holding Group (科元控股)
profile: Tao Chunfeng (陶春风), from Shengzhou, Zhejiang, trained in petrochemicals and worked at Sinopec Zhenhai Refining before co-founding Ningbo Keyuan Plastic. His listed Changhong Polymer makes styrenic thermoplastic elastomers (TPES). In 2024 it began trial output at a 600,000-tonne transparent ABS/polymer project in Guangxi. He is a Zhejiang provincial people's deputy.
interesting_fact: He holds more than 95 invention and utility-model patents. After seeing farmers in Qingyang, Gansu struggle to clear plastic mulch film, he launched the 'Spring Forest Plan' (春林计划) with 1,000 mu of demonstration land for degradable mulch.
deep_cut_fact: In his first two years after graduating, at Sinopec's Zhenhai Refining & Chemical, he won more than 30 technical innovation and management awards. He also funds an education fund at Zhenhai High School's Shengzhou campus in his hometown.

public_contacts.value: bh@kygroup.ltd (board secretary Bai Hua, Changhong Polymer)

notes: The input lists 'Changhong' as the source of wealth; this is Ningbo Changhong Polymer (长鸿高科), not Sichuan Changhong Electric. His energy angle is petrochemical feedstocks and polymer materials.

name: Lan Huasheng
current_role: Chairman and general manager of Shenzhen Dasheng Agriculture Group (深圳市大生农业集团), per older filings; current role unverified
profile: Lan Huasheng (兰华升) controls Shenzhen Dasheng Agriculture Group, an agricultural commodities, fertilizer and agri-finance group. From June 2014 he chaired its Hong Kong-listed arm, Dasheng Agriculture Finance (01103.HK). Dasheng lost its controlling stake in mid-2018 after the CEFC China Energy (Huaxin) crisis hit the group, and the HK company was later delisted. He was on Hurun's lists from 2015 to 2019.
interesting_fact: Lan held 70% of Qianhai Dasheng, making him the de facto controller of Shenzhen Dasheng, the group that built an agriculture-plus-finance platform in Hong Kong in the mid-2010s.
notes: Dropped off rich lists after 2019. The listed vehicle is delisted and the group had financial difficulties after 2018, so his net worth figure is likely stale. No current public contact route found. Low priority.

name: Marianne Odfjell
current_role: Private investor; chair of Ask Invest AS and director of Odfjell Invest / Odfjell Capital (per insider-profile listings)
profile: Norwegian heiress (b. c.1970), London-based, who received ~30% of offshore driller Odfjell Drilling in 2007 when her father Abraham Odfjell passed his shares to her and her sister Helene (70%). She sat on Odfjell Drilling's board 2010-2013 and in 2013 announced plans to sell her stake for about $500m ahead of the company's Oslo listing; she now invests privately.
interesting_fact: In 2007, after the share transfer, she was Norway's fourth-richest woman while her sister Helene was the richest; the family fortune was originally built on Odfjell tankers before the move into offshore drilling.
notes: Very private; no public contact, website or social accounts found. Not currently an executive of Odfjell Drilling (sister Helene is the active family figure there). Role listings come from MarketScreener insider pages (could not be fetched to verify).

name: The Jatania brothers
current_role: Family investors (UK); Danny Jatania's Jatania Group invests in SMEs, public equities and commercial property
profile: Four London-based brothers (Mike, George, Vin, Danny) built Lornamead, an acquisition-led personal-care group (est. 1978) owning brands like Yardley and Harmony Hairspray; it joined Hong Kong's Fung group in Dec 2012. The family now invests via Jatania Group (Jersey) in SMEs, public equities and commercial property.
interesting_fact: Lornamead's strategy was to buy established, sometimes neglected brands; its best-known deal was acquiring the 18th-century British perfumer Yardley. Mike Jatania said Lornamead wanted to build a significant personal-care business through strategic acquisitions.
notes: This is a group entry for four brothers. Jatania Group's site describes it as founded by Danny Jatania and is the only official contact route found. The family is low-profile, and recent Sunday Times Rich Lists show their wealth as flat. Lornamead's sale date comes from lornamead.com.

name: Lu Yonghua
current_role: Actual controller (largest shareholder) of Jiangsu Linyang Energy; stepped down as chairman June 2025
profile: Lu Yonghua (陆永华) built Qidong-based Jiangsu Linyang Energy (SSE: 601222), founded in 1995 as a maker of smart electricity meters for State Grid and China Southern Power Grid. From 2015 he pushed it into solar plant development, PV modules and energy storage. He left the chair in June 2025 but still controls ~39% of the company.
interesting_fact: Under Lu, Linyang evolved from a smart-meter supplier into a solar-farm developer and energy-storage maker; in H1 2026 revenue rose 82% as it sold down PV plants in a shift to an asset-light model.
notes: Now semi-retired; Yin Biao is chairman since June 2025. The IR email is the company board secretary's office (Cui Dongxu), not personal. Chinese-language outreach advised. Forbes shares listing with Mao Caihong.

name: Mao Caihong
current_role: No public executive role found; linked to Jiangsu Linyang Energy (SSE: 601222) alongside controlling shareholder Lu Yonghua
profile: Hurun lists her wealth jointly with Lu Yonghua, chairman/GM and ultimate controller of Jiangsu Linyang Energy (Qidong, Jiangsu), a maker of smart meters, solar power plants and energy storage. Linyang's 2023 annual report names 'Lu Yonghua, Mao Caihong' as joint guarantors of company borrowings, confirming her connection to the company; no other public profile found.
interesting_fact: Linyang Energy is controlled via Qidong Huahong Electronics (90% owned by Lu Yonghua), which held 34.72% of the listed company at end-2023.
notes: Extremely low profile; nature of relationship to Lu Yonghua not stated in sources found (do not assume). Any outreach would go through Linyang's board office (dsh@linyang.com.cn, board secretary Cui Dongxu per 2023 annual report). Lu Yonghua was placed under a supervisory-commission detention in Feb 2021 (NBD report) - sensitive.

name: Liu Manshi
current_role: Founder, chairman and president of Manshi Group (满世投资集团 / Inner Mongolia Manshi Coal Group), Ordos, Inner Mongolia
profile: Liu Manshi (刘满世, b. 1949) is from Zhunge'er Banner, Ordos. He co-founded Manshi Group in the early 1990s; it runs 8 large coal mines producing 25m+ t/yr of low-ash, low-sulphur thermal coal, plus a coal-logistics network, mine-mouth power and overseas projects. Hurun ranked him 9th-richest in Ordos in 2021 (RMB4.1bn).
interesting_fact: The group carries his given name - 'Manshi' (满世) - and its vision slogan '誉满全球 盛世百年' ('fame across the world, a century of prosperity') works both characters in; it ranked 483rd among China's top 500 private firms in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Manshi took coal abroad under Belt and Road: a 55%-owned open-pit coal mine in Gunung Mas, Central Kalimantan, Indonesia (103.72 km2 concession, ~61.6m t first-phase reserves), with a washery, power plant and barge port, alongside a 2x660MW mine-mouth plant at its Guanzigou mine.
notes: Unlisted private group; no published office/press email or official site verified. Group says it has spent nearly RMB300m on poverty relief and education donations. Identity linked via company profile ('founded by entrepreneur Liu Manshi and others') and Hurun 2021 Ordos list (https://m.maigoo.com/top/420440.html).

name: Hu Liqiang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (STAR Market: 688368)
profile: Born 1976, Hu is a chip designer who worked at ON Semiconductor's Shanghai design center and China Resources Siwei before founding Bright Power Semiconductor in Shanghai in 2008. The fabless firm began with LED-lighting driver chips and now sells AC/DC, DC/DC, motor-control and HPC power chips; he is its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Bright Power has moved from LED lighting drivers into power-management chips for servers, base stations and high-performance computing, a domestic-substitution play in China's AI/data-center supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as an assistant engineer at the 704 Research Institute of China Shipbuilding Industry Corp (marine machinery and power systems) before he moved into IC design; he has been named a Shanghai 'Leading Talent' and won the 8th Shanghai Tech Entrepreneur Innovation Award.
notes: Low-profile engineer-founder; route via IR (board secretary Yang Biao). Chinese-language outreach advisable. Relevant angle: Chinese power-management chips for servers/HPC.

name: Liu Jieqian
current_role: Listed by Hurun as co-owner (with Hu Liqiang) of Shanghai Bright Power Semiconductor (晶丰明源, STAR 688368); exact current title not verified
profile: Liu Jieqian (刘洁茜) appears on Hurun China lists 2020-2026 sharing a fortune with Hu Liqiang, chairman and founder of Bright Power Semiconductor. Founded in Shanghai in 2008, Bright Power designs power-management and motor-control chips (AC/DC, DC/DC, LED drivers) and now sells multiphase controllers and fan/pump solutions for AI servers.
interesting_fact: Bright Power started as an LED-lighting driver-chip maker and shipped 7B+ chips in 2021; it now pitches 48V server fan and liquid-cooling pump solutions for AI servers and multiphase digital controllers for high-performance computing.
notes: Very low public profile; I couldn't confirm her role at the company from an official page (company site doesn't name her) and my web-search quota ran out. Hu Liqiang is the public face - route via the IR mailbox. Data-center angle: server power/cooling chips.

name: Ye Huaneng
current_role: Actual controller of Guangdong Baolihua New Energy (宝新能源, SZSE 000690) via parent Guangdong Baolihua Group, which he founded and controls (~90%)
profile: Ye Huaneng (叶华能), from Meixian, Guangdong, left his mountain village in 1972 at 20, made his first money in construction and founded Baolihua Group (1993). Its listed arm (IPO 1997) moved from building/property into power: coal-gangue CFB plants at Meixian Heshuyuan and the Lufeng Jiahu Bay clean-energy base, plus wind. Chairman of the listed company is now Zou Jinkai.
interesting_fact: Baolihua's businesses once ranged from power plants to a men's fashion label ('Shenlang'), a 20% stake in the Meizhou-Shantou expressway and the Yannanfei Tea Field resort in Meixian.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he farmed after high school and worked as a 'minban' (community-funded) teacher in his home village of Changjiao, an old revolutionary-base village in Meixian; he later invested RMB180m to build the Yannanfei Tea Field resort near home.
notes: Not an officer of the listed company; reach via its board-secretary office (Meixian HQ / Guangzhou office). Be aware: in Jan 2026 the Guangdong CSRC bureau fined him over undisclosed nominee holdings and share sales and SZSE publicly reprimanded him (per 2026 interim report) - avoid in outreach.

name: Xu Chen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, SmartSens Technology (思特威, SSE STAR: 688213)
profile: Xu Chen (徐辰, 'Dr. Richard Xu') is a CMOS image-sensor engineer (Tsinghua BEng; HKUST MPhil/PhD) who founded Shanghai-based SmartSens in 2011. The company has led security-camera image-sensor shipments for years and expanded into automotive, machine vision and smartphones; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2022.
interesting_fact: SmartSens says it has led the security/surveillance image-sensor market by share eight years running and holds 550+ granted patents; Xu was named a 2025 Forbes China Best CEO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2019 SmartSens became the first Chinese company in the image-sensor field selected for ISSCC (the 'chip Olympics'), presenting the opening paper of the conference's image-sensor session.
notes: Uses the English name Richard Xu. The published 'Marketing and Media' address is the company media/BD contact, not a personal one. Academic background is in CMOS image sensors and high-speed optical receivers.

name: Wen Zhenlin
current_role: Chairman, co-founder and co-controlling shareholder, Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor Technology (展芯股份, SZSE ChiNext 301707), Nanjing
profile: Wen Zhenlin (温振霖, b. 1981), a Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics power-electronics master's graduate, spent 2009-2018 as an engineer at CETC's 14th Research Institute, then co-founded X-chip in 2018. It designs high-reliability analog/power-management chips and micro-modules for defense/aerospace import substitution; it listed on ChiNext on 7 Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: X-chip's IPO (Aug 2026) sold 41.12m shares at RMB23.45, raising about RMB964m. Pre-IPO, Wen and co-founder Xu Ligang together controlled 54.77% of votes; Wen also held 7.35% directly.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding X-chip he designed power-supply systems for national key radar/weapons programmes at CETC's 14th Institute (the Nanjing radar institute); the prospectus credits that experience with the firm's 'self-defined forward design' approach rather than pin-for-pin copies of imported chips.
notes: Newly listed 2026; shares the Hurun entry with his wife Yu Zhengjing (the prospectus names her as his spouse and concert party). Co-controller Xu Ligang (徐立刚) is general manager. Best route is the company securities department (contact person Zhu Dawei) via ir@semitech.cc.

name: Yu Zhengjing
current_role: Head of the General Affairs and Marketing departments (core employee), Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor Technology (展芯股份, 301707); concert party of the controlling shareholders
profile: Yu Zhengjing (余正晶, b. 1985) is the wife of X-chip chairman Wen Zhenlin and, per the IPO prospectus, acting-in-concert party of co-controllers Wen and Xu Ligang. She works at the company as head of its general affairs and marketing departments. X-chip, founded in Nanjing in 2018, makes high-reliability analog/power chips for defense and listed on ChiNext in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: The Hurun 2026 entry is shared with her husband; X-chip raised about RMB964m in its August 2026 ChiNext IPO at RMB23.45 a share.
deep_cut_fact: She is listed among X-chip's 'core employees' in the IPO prospectus, running both its general-affairs (综合部) and marketing (市场部) departments, not just a passive family shareholder.
notes: Low public profile; almost no press. Approach via the company securities department / her husband.

name: Luo Xingshun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Suzhou UIGreen Micro&Nano Technologies (和林微纳, STAR Market 688661)
profile: Luo Xingshun (骆兴顺, b. 1974, Huai'an, Jiangsu) built the Suzhou precision-parts business that became UIGreen (est. 2012), maker of micro-precision MEMS parts and semiconductor chip-test probes (memory, AI, CPU/GPU) plus EV and medical parts. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; AI test demand put him on Hurun's 2026 list.
interesting_fact: UIGreen's micro-precision probes and parts are used in semiconductor chip testing for memory, AI and CPU/GPU chips, and the company has set up market teams in the US, Japan, Singapore and Southeast Asia.
deep_cut_fact: He came up through procurement, not engineering: purchasing manager at Knowles Electronics (Suzhou) 2004-06 and briefly purchasing director at Guangzhou audio maker Diffeni (广州市迪芬尼音响) in 2006, before running Helin Precision from 2007; he later did an EMBA at HKUST (2012-14).
notes: Hurun 'Harmonics' = 和林微纳 (UIGreen). Low profile, Chinese-language only. Contacts come from the company's exchange-registered profile (Eastmoney F10 data); IR email is the securities department. Board secretary is Zhao Chuan.

name: Lu Lin
current_role: Co-founder, director and core technical staff, Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (柏楚电子, 688188.SH)
