profile: Lu Lin (卢琳) is one of five Shanghai Jiao Tong University-linked co-founders of Friendess (2007), which makes CNC control systems and software for fibre-laser cutting machines and dominates China's low/mid-power segment. Listed on the STAR Market in 2019, it posted 2025 revenue of ~RMB2.2bn. He is one of the five acting-in-concert controlling shareholders (~11%).
interesting_fact: Friendess says it holds ~70%+ of China's low/mid-power laser-cutting control-system market and ~40% of the high-power segment; the five founders reportedly took only living stipends at first and never raised outside capital.
deep_cut_fact: Lu is listed among Friendess's 'core technical personnel' - the engineers credited with the company's core control-system technology - alongside co-founders Dai Tiantian, Wan Zhang and Xie Miao, not just as an investor.
notes: Low public profile engineer-founder; chairman Tang Ye is the company's public face. Market-share figure is company-stated (via investor note/recruiting material). Route via board secretary office.

name: Liu Jianbo
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Kunshan Dongwei Technology Co. (东威科技, SSE STAR: 688700)
profile: Self-made engineer (b. 1979) who founded Dongwei in 2005; the company makes vertical continuous plating (VCP) equipment for PCB makers and has expanded into electroplating tools for semiconductors, photovoltaics and composite copper current-collector films for batteries. Listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; he holds roughly a third of the shares.
interesting_fact: Dongwei's VCP lines displaced traditional gantry-style plating in PCB plants, and the company has pushed the same technology into new-energy uses such as PV cell metallization and composite copper foil for lithium batteries.
deep_cut_fact: With a technical secondary-school (zhongzhuan) education, he started at about 17 as a technician at Dongguan Youda PCB equipment factory (1996-2001), then ran a small Kunshan machinery service shop (2001-05) before founding Dongwei.
notes: Energy-relevant (PV/battery plating equipment). Company holds regular online earnings Q&A sessions; IR email is the published channel.

name: Fan Yi
current_role: Vice Chairman, General Manager (CEO) and legal representative, MLOptic Corp (茂莱光学, SSE STAR: 688502), Nanjing
profile: Fan Yi and his brother Fan Hao (chairman) are co-controllers of MLOptic, a Nanjing precision-optics maker founded in 1999; they control ~66% via Nanjing Maolai Holdings and direct stakes. The company grew from custom lenses and prisms into optical modules and inspection systems for semiconductors, life sciences, AR/VR and lidar, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023.
interesting_fact: MLOptic supplies lenses for China's domestic lithography machines (Shanghai Micro Electronics), microscope objectives to Israeli chip-inspection firm Camtek, inspection optics to KLA, and its space filters have flown on China's Ziyuan resource satellites.
notes: Low public profile; no personal bio or interviews found. Relevant to semiconductor/data-center supply chain (chip-inspection and lithography optics). Route via the board office IR email (2026 half-year report).

name: Fan Hao (范浩)
current_role: Chairman, Nanjing Mloptic Corp. (南京茂莱光学科技股份有限公司, SSE STAR: 688502)
profile: Born 1972, Fan Hao co-controls precision-optics maker Mloptic with Fan Yi (vice chairman & CEO); together they control ~66% of the company. Founded in Nanjing in 1999, Mloptic makes precision optical components, lenses and metrology systems for semiconductor lithography/inspection, life sciences, AR/VR, LiDAR and, increasingly, optical interconnect for AI data centers. He has been chairman since 2015.
interesting_fact: Mloptic now markets optics, optical assembly and metrology for AI data-center optical interconnects, alongside AR headset test systems and semiconductor-equipment optics - a direct link to the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family optics business he spent 1994-2001 as a business manager at Jiangsu foreign-trade company 江苏省对外经贸, did an MBA at CEIBS (2001-03), then worked as a project manager at SCHOTT's Shanghai precision-materials trading arm; he holds a doctorate from Durham University (UK).
notes: Wealth shared with Fan Yi (co-actual controller, CEO and legal representative). Strong data-center/photonics fit. Sources: 2025 annual report (cninfo) for bio and IR email.

name: Shan Weijun
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨, HKEX: 2589), Shanghai
profile: Co-founder, with his wife Zhou Rongrong, of Auntea Jenny, one of China's largest fresh-fruit tea chains with well over 6,000 mostly franchised stores. The couple left jobs at a foreign-invested company in Shandong in 2011 to start a business in Shanghai; the brand listed on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange main board on 8 May 2025.
interesting_fact: Auntea Jenny became the sixth mainland Chinese tea-drink company to list publicly when it debuted in Hong Kong in May 2025; it has since added a coffee sub-brand (沪咖) and a sub-10-yuan brand, Cha Pubu (茶瀑布), for lower-tier cities.
deep_cut_fact: The first Auntea Jenny store opened on 18 July 2013 at Shanghai's People's Square, originally selling Shanghai-style freshly boiled five-grain teas; its breakout hit was a purple 'blood glutinous rice' (血糯米) milk tea that pushed the store past RMB 400,000 in monthly sales.
notes: Fortune shared with wife Zhou Rongrong. No published IR/press email found; company secretaries per HKEX filings are Wang Juan and Yu Anne. Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Zhou Rongrong
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director, Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨, HKEX: 2589)
profile: Co-founded tea-drink chain Auntea Jenny (沪上阿姨) in 2013 with husband Shan Weijun; both left jobs at a U.S. Fortune 500 company. It started as a 25 m² shop on People's Square, Shanghai, selling purple-rice milk tea, grew to 9,000+ mostly franchised stores in lower-tier cities, and listed in Hong Kong in May 2025.
interesting_fact: The first shop sold 1,000+ cups on opening day in July 2013, with queues tens of metres long, and took over RMB 300,000 in its first month.
deep_cut_fact: The idea was hers. In 2013 she wandered into a Shanghai lane and saw a queue outside an unsigned milk-tea shop that cooked tea with blood glutinous rice. That inspired a 'Shanghai-style' milk tea, and the brand name ('Shanghai Auntie') honours the aunties who ran such lane shops.
notes: Aggregators list her as Executive Director plus Deputy CEO or Chief Product Officer (unverified); husband Shan Weijun is chairman and the main public voice. No published IR email found. Check HKEXnews filings for the company secretary contact. Originally from Shandong.

name: Zhou Guangyu
current_role: General Manager and Director, Beijing BDStar Navigation Co. (北斗星通, SZSE: 002151), appointed GM July 2026
profile: Zhou Guangyu (周光宇) is a director of BDStar Navigation, a leading Chinese maker of BeiDou/GNSS satellite-navigation chips, modules and positioning products, and the son of founder-chairman Zhou Ruxin, with whom he is an acting-in-concert controlling shareholder (about 51.4M shares). In July 2026 he succeeded his father as general manager.
interesting_fact: BDStar, founded by his father Zhou Ruxin, is named after China's BeiDou ('Big Dipper') satellite navigation system and is one of the core commercial players building chips and receivers for it.
notes: Low public profile; no personal biography (education/age) found in accessible sources. Father Zhou Ruxin (chairman) is the better-known figure. Board secretary is Pan Guoping (潘国平); route via company. Satellite navigation/PNT is tangentially relevant to energy/data-center infrastructure (timing).

name: Xiong Yonghong
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Anhui Sinomag Technology Co. (Longci Keji, SZSE: 300835)
profile: Co-founded the predecessor of Sinomag in Hefei in 1998 (renamed Anhui Longci/Sinomag in 2001), which grew into a top global maker of wet-pressed permanent-ferrite magnet tiles used in car, motorcycle, power-tool and appliance motors. Listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020; he debuted on the Hurun China list in 2026 as the company expands in Vietnam and into chip inductors.
interesting_fact: Sinomag has a manufacturing subsidiary in Vietnam (Vietnam Longci), and a 2026 share placement of up to 760m yuan is funding a second Vietnam phase adding 10,000 t of ferrite magnet-tile capacity, plus a chip-inductor project.
deep_cut_fact: He came from trade, not engineering: with a technical-secondary-school education, he worked as a business manager in the documents/storage department and then 'Export Department No. 8' of Anhui Import & Export (Group) Corp. before running magnet ventures and founding Sinomag.
notes: Hurun lists wealth source as 'Sinomag' (龙磁科技). Formal route is the company's board-secretary/IR office via SZSE cninfo disclosures; official site sinomag.com.cn did not load during research.

name: Wang Chuan
current_role: Xiaomi co-founder; no confirmed current executive role (stepped down from remaining Xiaomi subsidiary posts by July 2025)
profile: Wang Chuan founded KTV song-system maker Leishi (Thunderstone) and e-reader software firm Duokan, which Xiaomi absorbed in 2012, making him one of Xiaomi's eight co-founders. He led Xiaomi TV/smart-home businesses and became Xiaomi China president in late 2018, then gradually stepped back; in 2025 he left his last legal-representative roles at Xiaomi entities.
interesting_fact: Leishi, the KTV song-selection system he founded and controlled, once held about 40% of China's KTV-system market; running it gave him the appliance supply-chain experience he later brought to Xiaomi hardware.
deep_cut_fact: In the Kingsoft years Lei Jun asked him to become Kingsoft CEO; he declined, agreeing instead to be a nominal executive director who came in two days a week (reportedly often four). He is a self-described Apple fan who idolised Steve Jobs' minimalism.
notes: Very low-profile; even Leishi employees reportedly didn't recognise him. No published personal or office contact found; any approach would have to go via Xiaomi corporate communications. Search budget limited this entry.

name: Ming Zaiyuan (明再远)
current_role: Chairman, Xinjiang Xintai Natural Gas Co. (新天然气, SSE: 603393)
profile: Born 1963, Ming has chaired Xinjiang Xintai Natural Gas since 2013 and holds ~174M shares. Founded in 2000 and listed in Shanghai in 2016, the company grew from Xinjiang city-gas distribution into an integrated clean-energy group spanning coalbed methane, tight and shale gas, LNG, pipelines (Shanxi) and coal resources.
interesting_fact: Xintai runs three flagship projects: the Kashgar North conventional oil and gas block, the Santanghu coal-chemical project and an underground coal-to-gas (coal gasification) project, alongside unconventional gas in Shanxi.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy he spent four years in the army (1980-84), then 13 years in rural banking in Deyang, Sichuan (1985-98), rising from auditor to deputy president of the local Agricultural Bank branch and head of the credit-cooperative union; he is a certified economist.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts. Board secretary Liu Dong handles investor contact (exchange-registered email above). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Liu Qiang
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Ingenic Semiconductor (北京君正, SZSE: 300223; HKEX: 03223)
profile: Founder and chairman of Beijing-based fabless chip designer Ingenic, set up in 2005 on the founding team's own XBurst CPU design and listed on ChiNext in 2011. Ingenic makes SoCs for smart cameras, AIoT, wearables and education devices, bought US memory maker ISSI (SRAM/DRAM/NOR flash) in 2020, and added a Hong Kong listing in August 2026.
interesting_fact: Ingenic's JZ4770 processor powered the world's first Android 4.0 'Ice Cream Sandwich' tablet in 2011, built on Ingenic's home-grown XBurst MIPS-based CPU core.

public_contacts.value: https://irm.cninfo.com.cn/ircs/company/companyDetail?stockcode=300223&orgId=9900016187 (official investor Q&A platform, linked from Ingenic site)

notes: Very low public profile; common name (刘强) - make sure to reference Ingenic. Biographical detail not verified this pass (web-search budget exhausted); HK listing prospectus (2026) should contain his full bio. Memory (ISSI DRAM) is a modest data-center angle.

name: Li Shijiang
current_role: Director and actual controller of Do-Fluoride New Materials (SZSE: 002407); chairman of parent Jiaozuo Do-Fluoride Industrial Group
profile: Li Shijiang (b. 1950, Wen County, Henan) turned the state-owned Jiaozuo Cryolite Factory into Do-Fluoride (DFD), a leading maker of fluorine chemicals and of lithium hexafluorophosphate (LiPF6), the key salt in lithium-ion battery electrolyte. He chaired the listed company from 2007 until handing over the chair in Dec 2025; he remains a director and controls the parent group.
interesting_fact: In 2006 he went to Japan to buy LiPF6 production technology, was turned away, then assembled his own team, which spent about eight years cracking the process, making DFD one of the world's largest LiPF6 suppliers for EV batteries.
deep_cut_fact: Before chemicals he served five years in the PLA Second Artillery (1968-73), then rose through the Wen County fertilizer plant (equipment and technical sections, petrochemical plant director) and a paper mill; he also chairs the council of Henan Polytechnic University's New Materials Industry College.
notes: Age 76. Strong battery-supply-chain angle. Military-service detail is from Chinese media profiles; the annual report confirms the career path. Listed company chairmanship changed hands in Dec 2025.

name: Huang Haoyun
profile: Listed on the Hurun China 2026 list (黄浩云, 'Victory', electrical equipment, ~US$820m). Several Chinese and English searches found no company or filing linking this name to a 'Victory' business; the best-known Victory company (Victory Giant Technology, 胜宏科技, a PCB maker) is run by Chen Tao, and no link to Huang was found.
notes: Could not identify the person or company. Check the Hurun 2026 list entry for the full company name before doing any research or outreach.

name: Han Jinghua
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Jiayou International Logistics (SSE: 603871); chairman of Guizhou Jialong Mining
profile: Chinese logistics entrepreneur who built Jiayou International from a Beijing freight forwarder into a listed cross-border logistics and infrastructure operator. With partner Meng Lian he controls about 43% of the company, which focuses on China-Mongolia coal corridors and Central African (DRC/Zambia) mining logistics and border-port infrastructure.
interesting_fact: Jiayou is building and operating the Zambian side of the Sakania dry port and the Ndola-Mufulira road, linking it to the Kasumbalesa-Sakania copper-belt crossing, and handled materials for the second China-Mongolia cross-border railway at Ganqimaodu.
notes: Very low public profile; little personal biography beyond filings. Company is relevant to energy/mining supply chains (coal, copper).

name: Gao Jiyang
current_role: Founder & CEO, Galaxea AI (星海图, GALAXEA (Beijing) Artificial Intelligence Technology Co.)
profile: Gao Jiyang (高继扬) studied microelectronics at Tsinghua (2015) and earned a USC PhD in computer vision (2018), then was a tech lead at Waymo and an executive director at Momenta. He founded embodied-AI/robotics company Galaxea AI with Tsinghua's Hang Zhao; it builds general-purpose humanoid and wheeled-arm robots plus its own G0 foundation models, and became a unicorn.
interesting_fact: At the 2026 World Robot Conference Galaxea signed a three-year deal with JD.com and showed what it called the world's first robot-run 'forward warehouse' that takes online orders and picks/packs them autonomously.
deep_cut_fact: At Waymo he was co-first author of VectorNet (CVPR 2020), an influential method for encoding HD maps and agent motion for trajectory prediction, and of TNT (CoRL 2020) with his future Galaxea cofounder Hang Zhao.
notes: Personal email is self-published (written 'jiyanggao1203 at gmail dot com') on his academic homepage, which dates from his Momenta days, so may be less monitored. Robotics rather than data centers, but strong AI-infrastructure/foundation-model angle.

name: Zhao Zhenhong
current_role: Legal representative and shareholder, Guangzhou Zhijing Information Technology (致景科技; Baibu / Quanbu textile platforms)
profile: Zhao Zhenhong (赵振洪) heads Guangzhou-based Zhijing Technology (founded 2013, a Hurun unicorn). It runs Baibu, a B2B fabric-trading app, and Quanbu, a textile industrial-internet platform linking yarn, greige, dyeing and garment factories. Investors include Source Code Capital, Tiger Global, DST Global and CICC Capital.
interesting_fact: Zhijing pitches itself as building a 'textile brain'. It uses big data, cloud computing and IoT to digitise China's fragmented fabric supply chain, from raw materials to garment making.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or social accounts found. Business registration (via 36Kr) confirms him as legal representative and a shareholder; the founder title comes from Hurun's unicorn list. Best route is via the company.

name: Zhao Wenlin
current_role: Founder, Honorary Chairman & Chief Engineer, GCH Technology (Chenghe Technology, SSE STAR: 688625), Guangzhou
profile: Founded GCH Technology in 2002 and chaired it until Sept 2023; he remains honorary chairman and chief engineer and its largest shareholder (~35-41%). GCH makes polymer additives -- nucleating agents and synthetic hydrotalcite -- for petrochemical giants like Sinopec, PetroChina, Borealis and Borouge, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in June 2021.
interesting_fact: GCH's tetrahydrophthalic-anhydride metal-salt beta-crystal nucleating agent was an industry first, and its hydrotalcite was Sinopec's first domestic brand, substituting Japanese imports; it now plans high-frequency electronic materials in Dongguan.
deep_cut_fact: After handing the chairmanship to Tong Jiaqi in 2023, Zhao kept the title of Chief Engineer -- signalling the founder's focus on the chemistry rather than management.
notes: Chinese name 赵文林; company 呈和科技. Very low English-language profile. No verified IR/press email found (company site did not load); SSE disclosures list the board secretary's contact for investor relations.

name: Wang Jianchen
current_role: Founder, chairman and CEO, Shenzhen Edge Medical (精锋医疗, HKEX: 2675)
profile: Dr. Wang Jianchen co-founded Shenzhen Edge Medical in 2017 with Gao Yuanqian to build domestic minimally invasive surgical robots. Edge says it was the first company in China, and the second worldwide, to get approvals for multi-port, single-port and natural-orifice surgical robots. It listed in Hong Kong in January 2026 after raising about HK$1.2bn.
interesting_fact: Edge Medical is a Temasek-backed rival to Intuitive Surgical. Its multi-port robot holds a CE mark, and its Hong Kong IPO in January 2026 drew 15 cornerstone investors.
notes: Some sources say he holds a Tianjin University doctorate (with MIT joint training), but this is unverified. The best route is Edge Medical's IR team, whose contacts are in its HKEX prospectus or annual report. Fortune is shared with co-founder Gao Yuanqian.

name: Gao Yuanqian
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director, COO and CTO, Shenzhen Edge Medical (精锋医疗, HK:2675)
profile: Gao Yuanqian, a Tianjin University mechanical-engineering PhD, co-founded Shenzhen-based surgical-robot maker Edge Medical in May 2017 with her husband Wang Jianchen. Its MP1000 multi-port and SP1000 single-port laparoscopic robots are approved in China and CE-marked; the company listed in Hong Kong on 8 Jan 2026, with the couple holding ~49% pre-IPO.
interesting_fact: Edge Medical was registered on 4 May 2017 with just 100,000 yuan of capital; by its last pre-IPO round in Oct 2021 it was valued at about US$1.5bn, more than 230x its angel valuation. Shares rose 30%+ on IPO day in Jan 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Her PhD was a joint program between Tianjin University and the Surgical Navigation and Robotics Lab at Harvard Medical School (PhD awarded June 2017, a month after she co-founded Edge); her husband/co-founder did his joint program at MIT.
notes: Fortune shared with husband/co-founder Wang Jianchen (CEO). Contact form includes a 'media inquiry' category. Young (post-'85) founder; Hurun Global U40 2026.

name: Tan Bingwen
current_role: Director and major shareholder (~11%), Guangdong Shenling Environmental Systems (申菱环境, SZSE: 301018), Foshan
profile: Tan Bingwen is a long-standing shareholder and board director of Shenling Environment, a Shunde (Foshan) maker of specialty HVAC and thermal-management systems; chairman and controlling shareholder is Cui Yingqi. Shenling's data-services segment supplies liquid- and air-cooling (CDUs, manifolds, cold plates, precision air-con) to cloud and AI-compute data centres, plus energy-storage and grid cooling.
interesting_fact: Shenling began researching data-centre liquid cooling in 2011, built one of China's early commercial liquid-cooled micro-module data centres with China Mobile and Inspur, holds 72 liquid-cooling patents and was ranked No.1 CDU vendor in China's 2024 liquid-cooled data-centre market (CCID).
notes: Highly relevant to data-centre cooling topic. No personal bio found; he is a director, not chairman (2026 pay notice: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604261821589318_1.pdf). He filed to reduce holdings in late 2025. Chairman Cui Yingqi may be the better interview target; route via board secretary office.

name: Liu Guocai
current_role: Chairman, CEO and Executive Director, Migao Group Holdings Ltd. (HKEX: 9879)
profile: Liu Guocai founded Migao, one of China's largest potash (potassium chloride, sulphate and nitrate) fertilizer producers, with plants across China and operations in Malaysia. He listed the group in Hong Kong in March 2024 at HK$4.08/share (one of the larger HK IPOs that quarter) and remains controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Migao says it ranks among China's top 10 fertilizer companies and is building a logistics and warehousing centre in Tongjiang, Heilongjiang on the Russian border, plus an R&D centre in Chengdu.
deep_cut_fact: This is Liu's second listing: his earlier vehicle Migao Corporation traded on the Toronto Stock Exchange (ticker MGO) as a China specialty-potash producer until a going-private deal he was affiliated with closed in September 2016.
notes: Low personal media profile. IR email is the best route; Hong Kong office at Cheung Kong Center II. Fertilizer/mining angle rather than energy.

name: Chen Jianping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Jame Technology Corp. (300868.SZ)
profile: Chen Jianping (b. 1983) co-founded Shenzhen Jame Technology in 2009, a designer and maker of mobile-phone cases and protective accessories for major handset brands and its own brands. He has chaired it since 2013; Jame listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020. His Hurun fortune is shared with Yang Meihua.
interesting_fact: Chen made the Hurun China Under-40 self-made rich list in 2020, the year Jame went public, with only a technical secondary-school (zhongzhuan) education.
deep_cut_fact: Before Jame he was director and GM of Shenzhen Jiameng Technology and executive director of Shenzhen Shenghuohui Trading; at Jame itself he started as supervisor (2009-2013) before becoming chairman.
notes: Hurun U40 source is the input metadata (Hurun China U40 2020); education per company filing. Contact via IR (board secretary 周波).

name: Yang Meihua
current_role: Director, Shenzhen Jame Technology Corp. (JMT, SZSE ChiNext: 300868); co-founder and co-controlling shareholder
profile: Yang Meihua (b. 1982) co-founded Shenzhen-based Jame Technology, which designs and manufactures protective cases for smartphones, tablets and wearables for major device makers and its own brands; it listed on ChiNext in 2020. She and her husband, chairman Chen (Shen) Jianping, are the controlling shareholders; she previously served as deputy GM and is now a board director.
interesting_fact: Jame grew from a 2006 start into a listed maker of phone, tablet and wearable cases and watch straps, supplying global device makers, leading accessory brands and international retail chains.
deep_cut_fact: Per Jame's annual report, Yang was born in 1982 and co-founded the company with a vocational secondary-school (zhongzhuan) education, serving as deputy general manager before moving to the board.
notes: Partner's surname is written 谌 (Shen/Chen) Jianping in filings. Very low public profile; route via board secretary Zhou Bo (zb@jamepda.com per 2024 annual report) or ir@jamepda.com.

name: Bobby Sheng
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Bora Group; CEO, Bora Pharmaceuticals (TWSE: 6472)
profile: Bobby Sheng (b. 1972), a Taiwanese-American raised in California, left UC Berkeley economics at 22 to help run his father's Hoan Pharmaceuticals in Taiwan. He founded Bora in 2007 and grew it through about a dozen acquisitions of plants from Eisai, GSK, Impax/Amneal, Pfizer and others into Taiwan's largest drugmaker and a global CDMO.
interesting_fact: Bora's first factory was a Tainan plant bought from Japan's Eisai in 2013. It went on to buy sites from GSK (Canada), Impax/Amneal (Zhunan) and others, leading Taiwanese media to call Sheng's goal becoming 'the TSMC of pharma'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bora, Sheng co-founded Machi Entertainment, a digital-first Asian record label, with Taiwanese entertainer Jeff Huang and Korean producer Jay Chong. He also gives new recruits and investors copies of 'Who Moved My Cheese?' to encourage adapting to change.
notes: Based in Taiwan though listed under China by Hurun. Fluent English speaker, US-educated and gives keynotes (e.g. JPM Healthcare Conference 2024), so a strong podcast candidate. Machi Entertainment detail is from Wikipedia citing China Times (chinatimes.com/newspapers/20180307000250-260202).

name: Jason Chen
current_role: Chairman and President, Test Research, Inc. (TRI, TWSE: 3030), Taipei
profile: Jason Chen (Chen Chieh-yuan) co-founded Taipei-based Test Research Inc. (TRI) in 1989 with colleagues from RCA's test division. TRI grew from in-circuit testers into a one-stop supplier of PCB-assembly inspection gear (ICT, ATE, AOI/AXI, semiconductor test) used by Foxconn, ASUS, Quanta and others; it listed in Taiwan in 2002 and he still serves as chairman and president.
interesting_fact: TRI's AOI optical-inspection line took about five years and three project leaders before it sold anything; Chen cites it as proof that decisive commitment matters in equipment businesses.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in RCA's automatic-test department in Taiwan; when RCA pulled back he co-founded TRI and coded in a small apartment on Zhongshan North Road. Business Today called him the industry's 'software R&D king': his 518F DOS test software became an industry standard.
notes: Taiwanese (list says China). Company spokesperson is Lin Chiang-huai (long-time VP). TRI inspection equipment is used in AI-server/electronics manufacturing, a data-center supply-chain angle.

name: Chan Wing Hong
current_role: Chairman & Executive Director, Plover Bay Technologies (HKEX: 1523); Founder & CEO of Peplink
profile: Hong Kong engineer-entrepreneur (Alex Chan) who founded Peplink in 2006 to build bonded multi-WAN and cellular routers (SpeedFusion), later adding the Pepwave wireless line. He took the parent, Plover Bay, public in Hong Kong. In Feb 2026 Plover Bay announced a plan to spin off Peplink Holdings as a separate Nasdaq listing, expected to close by the end of 2026.
interesting_fact: Peplink filed its first US patent on WAN-bonding in 2009. The technology became SpeedFusion, now used to bond cellular and Starlink links for vehicles, ships and public-safety fleets.
deep_cut_fact: In a post on Peplink's own community forum he summed up the company plainly: 'Fundamentally, we are in the modem business.' He noted that its ~200 staff span Taiwan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Hong Kong, Lithuania, the UK and Canada, and that the founding team is still with the company.
notes: Known publicly as Alex Chan. He posts directly on forum.peplink.com, which could be a low-key route. The pending Peplink Nasdaq spinoff is a timely hook, and the connectivity/Starlink angle fits a data-center or infra episode. No published IR email found; the HKEX filings list the company secretary.

name: Wang Li
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (about 43.7% per third-party data) of Hubei Zhongyi Technology Co. (301150.SZ), Yunmeng, Hubei. No board title is confirmed.
profile: Wang Li is listed as controlling shareholder of Hubei Zhongyi Technology (founded 2007, ChiNext-listed), which makes electrolytic copper foil for lithium-ion battery anodes and electronic circuits at plants in Yunmeng and Anlu, Hubei. The chair, Wang Xiaoxia (born 1990), resigned in May 2026, and finance chief Cai Litao was elected chairman.
interesting_fact: Zhongyi is a battery-supply-chain play: its copper foil is the current-collector layer in lithium-ion cells for EVs and energy storage, and a new 10,000-tonne high-end circuit-foil line at Yunmeng reached full production in 2026.
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed: Wang Li appears as controlling shareholder on 10jqka, but no biography was found, and his relation to ex-chair Wang Xiaoxia is not stated in sources. Leadership change: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-05-30/1225339053.PDF. Best route is the board secretary contact in the company's annual report on cninfo.com.cn.

name: Li Jialin
current_role: Chairman and CEO, VSTECS Holdings Ltd. (HKEX: 856)
profile: Li Jialin (李佳林), a Tsinghua electrical-engineering graduate (BEng, MBA), co-founded VSTECS (伟仕佳杰) in 1991. The Hong Kong-listed group is one of Asia's largest IT and cloud distributors, serving China and Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Thailand, Singapore, Indonesia, Philippines) across consumer electronics, enterprise systems and cloud computing.
interesting_fact: VSTECS has moved from PC distribution into cloud, operating its own 'VPlus' cloud platform and enterprise/data-center systems distribution across Southeast Asia.
deep_cut_fact: He won a National Science and Technology Progress Award (third class) and is founding president of the Tsinghua PBCSF (Wudaokou) Hong Kong EMBA alumni group and permanent president of the Tsinghua Alumni Association of Hong Kong.
notes: Email is the published general contact for VSTECS Hong Kong HQ, not personal. Relevant to podcast via cloud/data-center equipment distribution in Asia. Tsinghua alumni network is a warm angle.

name: Wang Yuedan
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Ningbo Fujia Industrial Co. (Furja, SSE: 603219), Yuyao, Zhejiang
profile: Wang Yuedan is chairman and actual controller (about 70% directly and via Fujia Holdings) of Ningbo Fujia Industrial, founded in 2002 in Yuyao, Zhejiang. Furja is an ODM maker of vacuum cleaners, cordless/wet-dry floor cleaners, robot vacuums and brushless motors, listed in Shanghai in 2021 and now expanding into Vietnam.
interesting_fact: Furja has made vacuums for Shark since 2004 and became JS Global/SharkNinja's largest supplier in 2018; that customer has long accounted for over 80% of its revenue.
notes: Low personal media profile. Company email is the listed corporate address (board office tel 0574-62838000). Interesting angle: Chinese ODM behind a major US appliance brand; its business scope now includes energy storage, PV and EV battery-swap equipment.

name: Liu Haiyan
profile: Hurun lists Liu Haiyan (刘海燕) as the owner of Continental Hope (大陆希望集团), the Chengdu-based group with electrical-equipment/energy businesses. That group was founded by Liu Yongyan, eldest of the four Liu brothers who started Hope Group. I could not find a public source that sets out her role or relationship there.
interesting_fact: Continental Hope comes from the original Hope Group that the four Liu brothers (Liu Yongyan, Liu Yongxing, Chen Yuxin/Liu Yongmei, Liu Yonghao) started in the 1980s. Liu Yongyan took the high-tech branch, which holds many energy and power patents.
notes: Identity not verified: web searches only turn up unrelated people named Liu Haiyan, and nothing ties her to Continental Hope beyond the Hurun list (2013-2026). She is probably a family member of the Liu Yongyan branch; do not assume this. Extremely low profile; any approach would go via Continental Hope Group corporate channels.

name: Liao Jieyuan
current_role: Founder and chairman, WeDoctor Group (微医, Hangzhou); left the listing-entity board in Jan 2024 but still presented as chairman in 2026
profile: Liao Jieyuan (Jerry Liao) was an early co-founder of iFlytek (1999), then ran telecom venture China Green Line before founding online hospital-booking site Guahao.com in Hangzhou in 2010, renamed WeDoctor in 2015. Backed by Tencent, Hillhouse and Sequoia China, WeDoctor refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in 2025 as an AI healthcare provider; he speaks on AI health agents.
interesting_fact: He switched to healthcare after a nephew spent ~10 months across seven hospitals with two surgeries before a misdiagnosis was found; WeDoctor's first hospital hookup (Huashan Hospital) took six months.
deep_cut_fact: Right after graduating he worked at a forestry research institute before leaving the public sector, then in 1999 helped found iFlytek with Liu Qingfeng and others.
notes: Good fit for a tech/AI angle; frequent conference speaker (World Internet Conference 2026). Dubbed one of the 'Longyan three heroes' with Zhang Yiming and Wang Xing (pedaily). 2018 interview: https://www.asianscientist.com/2018/12/features/wedoctor-jerry-liao-ai-healthcare/

name: Chai Lin
current_role: Director and chief engineer, Chengdu Ultra Pure Applied Materials Co. (SZSE ChiNext: 301717)
profile: Chai Lin (b. 1971, Chengdu) is co-controller, with his younger brother and chairman Chai Jie, of Ultra Pure Applied Materials, a maker of specialty-coated components for semiconductor etching, lithography and deposition tools. He joined in 2008 and led the shift into chip-equipment coatings from 2009; the company listed on ChiNext on 11 Aug 2026 and soared over 600% on day one.
interesting_fact: Ultra Pure says it is one of the few Chinese suppliers of key coated parts for 5nm-and-below etching equipment, taking on Korea's KoMiCo and Japan's Tocalo; BYD is its fourth-largest shareholder and saw a ~15x paper gain at the IPO.
deep_cut_fact: A UESTC graduate, Chai Lin was an assistant engineer at UESTC's electronics experiment centre, an engineer at the Chengdu Precision Optics Engineering Research Center, and a senior engineer at Leybold Optics' Beijing office before joining his brother's company.
notes: Technical co-founder rather than the public face; brother Chai Jie (chairman/GM) is the main spokesperson. Hurun's 'sensors' label is loose: business is semiconductor-equipment coatings. No published IR email found yet (newly listed); check cninfo for 301717.

name: Chen Jiangyue
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Xu Buyun) of Buyang Group and Buyang International Holding (HKEX: 2457)
profile: Chen Jiangyue is the wife and business partner of Xu Buyun, who founded Yongkang, Zhejiang-based Buyang Group. The group started as a small foundry and grew into security doors (Buyang doors), vehicles, real estate, auto parts and logistics. The couple's aluminium-wheel arm, Buyang International, listed in Hong Kong in December 2022. She holds no board seat and keeps no public profile.
interesting_fact: Buyang's 'BYW' aluminium alloy wheel business sold more than one million wheels in 2020 to customers in over 50 countries. It began in 2005 by targeting the overseas aftermarket.
deep_cut_fact: The HK prospectus says she co-founded the wheel subsidiary Buyang Wheel with her husband in 2007. Before the IPO reorganisation she owned 30% of the wheel holding company to his 70%.
notes: Very private. Xu Buyun, chairman and non-executive director of Buyang International, is the public face, so the best route is through the company secretary or IR of HKEX: 2457. Her last Hurun appearance was 2021. No death reports found, but she was not confirmed alive.

name: Che Chengju
current_role: Second-largest shareholder (~4.3%) of Zibo Qixiang Tengda Chemical (002408.SZ); former chairman and later director/GM, no longer listed among current management
profile: Che Chengju (车成聚, b. 1950), a Qilu Petrochemical veteran, from 1998 built Qixiang into a Zibo C4-chemicals producer, listed in Shenzhen in 2010. After the parent group's restructuring, state-owned Shandong Energy took control (2022); he stepped down as chairman in 2023 and remains a major individual shareholder.
interesting_fact: After losing control to Shandong Energy, he pledged in Sept 2023 to buy RMB 100-120M of Qixiang shares on the open market and did so, lifting his stake to about 4.2-4.3%.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in December 1971 and rose to labour-section chief and deputy director of Qilu Petrochemical's rubber plant before running Qixiang; he has won a Sinopec Science and Technology Progress first prize and was named a Shandong Outstanding Entrepreneur in 2002, 2007 and 2021.
notes: Age ~76 and no longer in management (company now state-controlled under Shandong SASAC), so the IR email reaches the company, not him. Alive status inferred from 2026 shareholder filings that list him as holder. Very low international profile; Chinese-language only.

name: Deng Jieru
current_role: Actual controller and largest shareholder of Chengdu RML Technology (SZSE ChiNext: 301050); former executive (chairman is now Gui Jun)
profile: Deng Jieru (邓洁茹) is the ultimate controller of Chengdu RML Technology (雷电微力), a maker of millimetre-wave phased-array microsystems for radar, data links and satellite payloads, listed on ChiNext in Aug 2021. She holds ~19.3% directly plus more via a holding company, and no longer holds an executive role.
interesting_fact: RML's products include satellite-borne and airborne millimetre-wave phased-array microsystems. The company was added to the US Commerce Department's Entity List in Jan 2025 and said this would not materially affect operations.
deep_cut_fact: She controls RML partly through a holding company named 'Wuhan Integrated Circuit Industry Technology Research Institute' (武汉集成电路工业技术研究院), which she owns 94.22%, according to RML's 2024 annual report.
notes: Very private, with no interviews found. The company is defence-oriented and on the US Entity List, which is sensitive for a podcast. She is no longer an executive, so the only route is via the company IR email.

name: Li Jixi
current_role: Founder, Chairman and actual controller, Shanghai WPG Smart Water (上海威派格智慧水务, SSE: 603956)
profile: Li Jixi (李纪玺, b. Oct 1972) has been an entrepreneur since 2002 and built WPG, a Shanghai maker of secondary water-supply pumping equipment and smart-water software for utilities. With his wife Sun Hailing he controls the listed company; he directly holds ~38% (2025 annual report) and remains chairman, with a board term to Dec 2027.
interesting_fact: WPG is a 'smart water' (智慧水务) company: it pairs the pump stations that keep water pressure up in high-rise buildings with digital platforms for city water utilities, and partners with utilities through its subsidiary Shanghai Jieshi Information Technology.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture was Beijing Panda Hengsheng Machinery Equipment (北京熊猫恒盛机械设备), where he was executive director; he holds a CEIBS EMBA and was a member of the Jiading District (Shanghai) CPPCC from 2016 to 2021.
notes: Hurun 'WPG' = 威派格. Low media profile; route via securities affairs dept email.

name: Shen Hao
current_role: Actual controller of Hongyu Investment (now Shenzhen Hongyu Information Technology), a ~5% shareholder of Trina Solar (688599); controlling shareholder and executive director/GM of Jiangsu Huabo Industrial Group (Nanjing)
profile: Shen Hao (沈浩) is a Nanjing-based investor whose vehicle Hangzhou Hongyu Investment bought 6% of Trina Solar during its 2017 return from NYSE to China; Trina's 2020 STAR Market IPO and solar rally put him on the 2021 Hurun list. He also owns 90% of Jiangsu Huabo Industrial Group. Hongyu still held 5.08% of Trina in Oct 2024.
interesting_fact: Trina's 2020 prospectus names him as one of only three non-founder individuals indirectly holding 5%+ of Trina, alongside Zhang Yong (Rongqi) and Zhu Guangping (Qisheng); Hongyu nominated director Dou Yuming to Trina's board in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Huabo, the prospectus lists him as a director of Shanghai Yingxing Network Technology, Nanjing Laifuxing Communications and Nanjing Guoli Management Consulting, plus controller of supply-chain firm Jiangsu Fengyun (蜂云) and Nanjing Mifeng (Bee) Management Consulting.
notes: Very private financial investor, not a Trina executive; no press profile found. In Oct 2024 his vehicle (Shenzhen Hongyu, 5.08%) planned a block-trade sale of up to 0.5% of Trina but ended early after selling 0.08% (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202410081640203107_1.pdf). No personal/office contact published; Trina IR (IR@trinasolar.com) is not his channel.

name: Zhang Weiming
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Shengjian Technology (603324.SH; formerly Shengjian Environment, renamed Aug 2024)
profile: Co-founder (with Wang Zhe) and chairman of Shanghai-based Shengjian, which supplies process-exhaust-gas treatment systems to China's semiconductor and display fabs. It grew from making a single exhaust-duct product into a full system integrator, listed on the SSE main board in April 2021, and is now pushing upstream into semiconductor equipment and materials.
interesting_fact: Shengjian dominated the niche of fab exhaust ductwork before 2011, then rode BOE-led domestic display-panel build-outs into full waste-gas treatment systems; Zhang's motto is to 'take the hardest road' and build a 'hundred-year company'.
deep_cut_fact: In its start-up years Shengjian's stainless-steel coated exhaust duct won FM Approvals certification for cleanroom exhaust/smoke duct systems; Zhang compares the climb upmarket to mountaineering: 'the higher you go, the fewer companions, the more beautiful the view.'
notes: Re-elected chairman 2024. Highly relevant to semiconductor-fab infrastructure angle. IR route is the board office.

name: Wang Zhe
current_role: Co-actual controller and founding shareholder (~1.7% direct) of Shanghai Shengjian Technology (盛剑科技, SH:603324), alongside chairman Zhang Weiming
profile: Wang Zhe is, with chairman Zhang Weiming, the co-actual controller of Shanghai Shengjian, a Jiading-based 'green fab facilities' supplier that builds process-exhaust treatment, chemical supply/recycling systems, equipment and electronic chemicals for semiconductor and display fabs. The company listed in Shanghai in 2021; Wang keeps a low profile and holds no prominent executive post in disclosures found.
interesting_fact: Shengjian's core business is cleaning up exhaust gas and recycling chemicals inside chip and panel fabs, putting it squarely in the semiconductor supply chain that feeds AI/data-center demand.
deep_cut_fact: Wang was one of only three founding promoters (with Zhang Weiming and Kunsheng Management) when Shengjian converted into a joint-stock company in April 2018, having taken stakes in the predecessor firm in May 2017.
notes: Very private; virtually no public biography. Zhang Weiming (chairman, 59% holder) is the public face; best route is company IR email.

name: Guo Shaozeng
current_role: Former director of China Fortune Land Development (华夏幸福) and its parent Huaxia Holdings; previously vice chairman of Bank of Langfang (current role not found)
profile: Guo Shaozeng was a long-time senior lieutenant and shareholder of Wang Wenxue's China Fortune Land Development, the Hebei developer of 'industrial new towns' such as Gu'an. In 2016 he sat on the boards of Huaxia Holdings and CFLD, chaired CFLD Venture Capital and Rongtong Capital (Gu'an), and was vice chairman of Bank of Langfang. He resigned from the CFLD board around the end of 2018.
interesting_fact: CFLD's model of building and running whole 'industrial new towns' for local governments began in 2002 with an agreement to develop the Gu'an Industrial Park south of Beijing.
notes: Hurun-listed only in 2015–16. He is no longer at CFLD, which has since gone through a debt restructuring (now *ST), so the company IR route (IR@cfldcn.com) is not appropriate. Roles per 2016 filing: https://epaper.cs.com.cn/zgzqb/images/2016-12/02/B030/ZQBXP0301202C.pdf ; board resignation: https://m.winshang.com/news653624.html . Very low profile.

name: Fan Chi
current_role: Former Alibaba Group vice president (left May 2021); current role not publicly reported
profile: Fan Chi (范驰, Alibaba nickname 'Cheng Yaojin') spent 11 years at Alibaba from Dec 2010, building Alipay's quick-pay and mobile payments, then serving as CEO of Koubei (2015), president of Fliggy (2019) and head of OTT/sports at Alibaba Digital Media & Entertainment (2020). His wealth came from Alibaba/Ant equity; he left the group on 1 May 2021 and has kept a low profile since.
interesting_fact: In June 2015 he became CEO of Koubei, the local-services joint venture of Alibaba and Ant Financial, which later merged with Ele.me after Alibaba bought it in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: His longest stint at Alibaba was at Alipay, where he worked across 'kuaijie' express payment, wireless payment and the Alipay app, holding brand, marketing, operations and product roles before Koubei.
notes: No public post-2021 activity, personal website or social accounts found; only appeared on Hurun in 2017. Any approach would have to go through mutual Alibaba-alumni networks. Not verified whether he was a formal Alibaba Partnership member.

name: Lu Xianping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager (president), Shenzhen Chipscreen Biosciences (STAR Market: 688321)
profile: Xianping Lu, a U.S.-citizen scientist, did postdoctoral research at UC San Diego (1989-94), helped found Maxia Pharmaceuticals and Galderma Research, and headed research at Galderma's North American R&D center before returning to China. In 2001 he co-founded Chipscreen in Shenzhen, which developed chidamide (Epidaza), China's first original anti-cancer drug; he still chairs and runs it.
interesting_fact: Chipscreen's chidamide is described as China's first original anti-tumor new drug; Lu received Shenzhen's 2018 Science and Technology 'Mayor's Award'. Note: Chipscreen is a drug developer, not a chip company.
deep_cut_fact: In 2006, short of cash, Chipscreen out-licensed chidamide's patents abroad on a fee-plus-milestones-plus-royalty model - reported as the first time a Chinese original new drug's patent rights were licensed to the U.S. and other developed markets. In 2000 he and five young Chinese scholars decided to return to China to start it.
notes: Still chairman per Chipscreen's 2025 annual report (signed 30 Mar 2026). Career details from the 2024 annual report bio. Mis-tagged as data_center_ai - biotech, low relevance for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Oleksandr Yaroslavsky
current_role: President, Development Construction Holding (DCH), Kharkiv, Ukraine
profile: Kharkiv-based Ukrainian businessman, born 1959 in Mariupol, who made his fortune as co-owner of UkrSibbank (sold to BNP Paribas) and then built the DCH group, whose assets have included Kharkiv International Airport, Kharkiv Tractor Plant, FC Metalist and the Kharkiv Palace Hotel. He was a member of the Verkhovna Rada (2002-2006) and Forbes Ukraine ranked him among the country's ten richest in 2016.
interesting_fact: As president of FC Metalist Kharkiv (2005-2012) and owner of Kharkiv airport, he was central to Kharkiv's role as a Euro 2012 host city.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he trained as a food technologist at the Kharkiv academy of public nutrition, served three years in the Soviet army in Hungary, and earned a candidate of technical sciences degree from the Odesa technological institute in 1989.
notes: No working official DCH site or verified personal channels found (dch.com.ua unreachable). Wikipedia article is tagged for poor sourcing and records reputational controversies since 2022; journalist should vet carefully before outreach.

name: The Gibbon family
profile: Listed on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020 with property as source of wealth (approx. US$580m+). Could not identify which Gibbon family or which property company this refers to from Wikipedia, trade-press rich-list coverage or web search.
notes: Identity unresolved: no public coverage linking a 'Gibbon family' to a named UK property business found (searches only surfaced New Zealand's unrelated Gibbons family on the NBR list). Needs the Sunday Times Rich List 2020 print entry to identify the company before any outreach.

name: James Richard Belardi
current_role: Co-Founder, Executive Chairman & CIO, Athene; Founder, Chairman & CEO, Apollo Insurance Solutions Group; board member, Apollo Global Management
profile: Jim Belardi co-founded Athene in 2009 and was CEO until 2025, growing it into a retirement-services insurer with nearly $400bn in assets (merged into Apollo in 2022). Earlier he was President of SunAmerica Life and EVP/CIO of AIG Retirement Services. He is now Athene's executive chairman and CIO.
interesting_fact: Athene, which he built, is the annuity and insurance engine behind Apollo's 'retirement services' model. Its insurance balance sheet funds much of Apollo's private-credit origination.
deep_cut_fact: Belardi is an elite swimmer: he swam in the 1976 and 1980 US Olympic Trials and is a nine-time Masters Swimming world record holder. He also sits on the board of Southern California Aquatics and chairs the investment committee of Paulist Productions.
notes: Stanford BA (economics) and UCLA MBA. Apollo's people page: https://www.apollo.com/about-apollo/our-people/jim-belardi . The best route is Athene External Relations or Apollo media relations.

name: Cynthia Paul
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chief Investment Officer, Lynrock Lake LP; director of Yext, ON24 and Allot
profile: Cynthia L. Paul spent 2002-2017 as a portfolio manager at Soros Fund Management, covering corporate credit, convertibles and equities. In 2017-18 she founded Lynrock Lake, a value-oriented fund that invests across the capital structure of technology, media and telecom companies. It holds large stakes in Teradata, Yext and ON24 (about 17.5%), and she sits on the boards of several of these companies.
interesting_fact: She is an activist-style tech investor. Lynrock reached a 2026 cooperation agreement with Teradata, and Yext appointed her to its board in July 2026. She has over 24 years of investing in public enterprise software companies.
deep_cut_fact: She chaired the board of semiconductor company Conexant Systems from 2013 to 2017, while still at Soros. She began her career in 1994 as head of convertible research at J.P. Morgan, after graduating from Princeton.
notes: A private investor with no personal website, press office or published email found. Lynrock Lake's address appears in SEC 13D/13G filings on EDGAR. Approach would have to go through a warm introduction or the board/IR offices of Yext, ON24 or Allot. The data-center/enterprise software angle (Teradata) fits the podcast. A MarketScreener page mentioning a Cribl CFO of the same name is a different person.

name: Hua Yong
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Shunwang Technology (SZSE: 300113)
profile: Hua Yong (华勇) spent about a decade at the state-owned Hangzhou Telecommunication Bureau before co-founding Shunwang in July 2005 to make internet-cafe management software; it listed on ChiNext in 2010. After stepping back in 2022 he returned as chairman in 2023 and is repurposing Shunwang's internet-cafe network into a distributed edge-computing (GPU cloud) business.
interesting_fact: Shunwang now runs 330+ edge-computing node rooms serving ~820,000 terminals with ~53,000 'channels' of operable GPU compute (Q1 2026), renting cloud gaming/AI PCs to internet cafes - a direct edge data-center angle for the podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Shunwang's flagship product was '网维大师' (Wangwei Dashi), maintenance software for internet cafes; Hua has described his return and the pivot of that cafe network into edge-compute nodes as a 'second startup' (二次创业).
notes: Very relevant to data-center/edge compute theme. Board secretary Rong Songyi (戎颂怡) handles investor communications; Shunwang holds regular IR sessions recorded on cninfo.

name: Yoji Sato
current_role: Non-executive Director, Dynam Japan Holdings (HKEX: 6889); Chairman, Eurasia Foundation (from Asia)
profile: Yoji Sato (b. ~1946, Waseda commerce 1968) took over his father's pachinko business Sawa Shoji in 1970 aged 24 and built it into Dynam, Japan's largest pachinko hall operator, listing it in Hong Kong in 2012 as one of the first Japanese companies there. He moved from chairman/CEO to non-executive director in 2016; his vehicle SAC holds the controlling stake.
interesting_fact: Dynam listed on the Hong Kong exchange in 2012 because pachinko operators could not list in Tokyo; it was only the second Japanese issuer in Hong Kong after SBI Holdings.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking over the family firm he worked at supermarket chain Daiei because he was fascinated by the then-novel 'chain store theory', which he later applied to pachinko halls (suburban, low-cost formats, hiring new grads, forming a labour union).
notes: Age 80 per Dynam FY2025/26 annual report. Since 2009 he has chaired the One Asia / Eurasia Foundation (from Asia), which funds university courses on Asian community-building in many countries - a good warm angle. Foundation phone published on its site: +81-3-5615-5500.

name: Chen Wukui
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Chief Engineer, Shenzhen Topraysolar Co., Ltd (002218.SZ)
profile: Engineer-entrepreneur (b. 1958) who founded Shenzhen Topray Solar in 2002 and has chaired it since, building it into a maker of amorphous, mono- and multi-crystalline silicon solar cells, modules and solar applications. Topray listed in Shenzhen in February 2008; he remains chairman and chief engineer and was re-elected for the 2025-2028 board term.
interesting_fact: He led Topray's industrial park project, which was among China's first batch of national renewable-energy demonstration projects (Ministry of Construction), and the NDRC's 25MW amorphous-silicon PV industrialisation project.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he worked across an unusual mix of fields - chemicals, magnetic materials, rubber, machinery and electro-vacuum technology - and holds degrees in both mechanical manufacturing and international economics; he still carries the title of chief engineer at the company he chairs.
notes: Last on Hurun China list in 2021; the IR email is the published board-secretary mailbox (Gong Yanping). Chinese-language outreach advisable; no English-language profile or social accounts found.

name: Wu Yueming
current_role: Unconfirmed – listed by Hurun (2006-2010) as head of Fengli Group (steel trading)
profile: Hurun listed Wu Yueming (吴岳明) as the owner of Fengli Group, a steel-trading business. A Fengli Group headquartered in the Zhangjiagang (Jiangsu) bonded zone runs import-export trade, steel-pipe making, metals markets and scrap-steel trading, but no source found ties Wu to it by name.
notes: Could not confirm identity; possible company match https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-companies/company/fengligroupcompanylimited/ . Off rich lists since 2010. Kept minimal.

name: Wang Wenzhi
current_role: Chairman (last reported) of Elion Ecological Restoration Co. (亿利生态修复), part of Wang Wenbiao's Elion Resources Group; former director of Elion Energy / Elion Clean Energy (600277)
profile: Wang Wenzhi (王文治) is a long-time senior executive of Elion Resources Group, the Inner Mongolia chemicals, coal, pharma and desert-greening conglomerate founded by Wang Wenbiao, with whom Hurun co-listed him in 2008-2013. He sat on the board of listed Elion Energy (2011-14 and later) and went on to chair Elion's Beijing-based ecological-restoration arm.
interesting_fact: He chaired Elion Ecological Restoration (founded 2014, Beijing), the group's eco-restoration arm; Elion's Kubuqi Desert greening earned Wang Wenbiao UNEP's Champions of the Earth lifetime-achievement award (https://unep.org/championsofearth/es/node/229).
notes: Family tie to Wang Wenbiao is implied by the shared Hurun entry but not confirmed in any source we found. Avoid: a CSRC penalty decision on Elion Clean Energy handed him a 10-year market ban (Wang Wenbiao got a lifetime ban) - https://www.jiemian.com/article/7011562.html. Tried Elion annual reports (2020, 2023) and board-election notices for a bio; none found. No published contact.

name: Liu Shaosheng
current_role: Minority shareholder in the Yihua (宜华) group of Shantou, Guangdong; no current executive role found
profile: Liu Shaosheng (刘绍生) appeared on Hurun China lists 2005-2010 alongside Liu Shaoxi (刘绍喜), founder of the Shantou-based Yihua Group (wood furniture/flooring via Yihua Lifestyle, property, later healthcare). Exchange filings list him as a 7% shareholder of a Yihua holding entity in which Liu Shaoxi held 56%. Little else about him is public.
interesting_fact: Yihua began as a Chenghai township wood-products business and grew into one of China's biggest solid-wood furniture exporters, with group assets once reported at RMB 85bn.
notes: Not recommended: the Yihua group fell into a debt crisis from 2019; Yihua Lifestyle was delisted in 2021 and Liu Shaoxi was placed under CSRC investigation for alleged market manipulation (2023). Liu Shaosheng's relationship to Liu Shaoxi (likely brother, not confirmed) and current status are unverified. No public contacts.

name: Mo Haosong
profile: Mo Haosong (莫浩松) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2007-2013 with Mo Haotang, with wealth attributed to real-estate company 'Sangem'. No filings, company site or press coverage could be found to confirm the company's Chinese name, his role or current activities.
notes: Not identifiable from open sources: multiple Chinese and English searches for 莫浩松/莫浩棠 and 'Sangem' returned nothing relevant; company appears to be private. Last on Hurun in 2013. Would need the Chinese company name (or a Qichacha/registry lookup) to proceed.

name: Wu Zhongquan
profile: Hurun listed him from 2009 to 2013 as the owner of 'Jindu', a real estate business, most likely Hangzhou-based Jindu Real Estate Group (金都房产集团). He has been off the list since 2013. No current public source could be retrieved to confirm his role or the company's present status.
notes: Not verified. Searches and direct fetches turned up no usable source; the Jindu websites were unreachable or blocked. He dropped off Hurun after 2013, and the private developer may have shrunk. Low priority.

name: Liang Zhibin
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich List 2007-2021 (~US$810m) with wealth from 'Xin Shiji' (新世纪, 'New Century') in real estate and chemicals. Searches in English and Chinese found no public source tying Liang Zhibin (梁志斌) to a specific New Century group, so his company, location and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Private company owner with essentially no online footprint; many Chinese firms share the 'New Century' name. Not identifiable without Hurun's original entry (city/province). Off the Hurun list since 2021.

name: Sun Weimin
current_role: Vice chairman of Suning Holdings Group (per Suning Easybuy filings); chaired Suning.com's supervisory board 2023 to Dec 2025
profile: Sun Weimin (孙为民) is a longtime Suning executive. He joined Suning Appliance in 1998 as assistant to the general manager and rose to president and vice chairman, sharing in its growth into China's largest electronics retailer. He left the Suning.com board in 2021 and then chaired its supervisory board until the body was dissolved at the end of 2025.
interesting_fact: Before retail, he was an academic. He studied psychology at Beijing Normal University (1981–1988) to master's level, then taught at Nanjing University of Science and Technology for a decade.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Xinjiang in 1963. He made the jump from a university lecturer's post to Suning in 1998, starting as assistant to the general manager. In 2014 he wrote a piece arguing that physical stores should become consumer social spaces.
notes: He was last on Hurun in 2016, so his wealth is probably much reduced since Suning's troubles (don't mention). Low public profile; the route is via Suning IR. The 'current vice chairman of Suning Group' title comes from a resume aggregator and may be stale.

name: Yang Qiu
current_role: Unverified; linked by Hurun to 'Hengxing' (恒兴), real estate and investments
profile: Hurun China listed Yang Qiu (杨秋), together with Yang Zhenxin (杨振新), from 2008 to 2020 for a real-estate and investment business called Hengxing. I could not tie the name to a specific Hengxing entity: several unrelated companies share the name, including Xiamen Hengxing Group and Hengxing New Materials.
notes: Identity could not be confirmed and the name is very common. Need the Hurun profile's city or company detail to disambiguate. Off the list since 2020.

name: Xue Fangquan
current_role: Chairman, Chongqing Minsheng Energy Group (重庆民生能源集团) as of 2015 reporting; current status not re-verified
profile: Xue Fangquan, born in the mid-1950s in Zhengxing, Bishan (Chongqing), went from farmer to railway soldier, teacher and state-firm employee before founding Chongqing Minsheng Energy Group, a private group spanning piped natural gas, energy chemicals, plastic pipes, petrochemical logistics, city buses, property and hotels, with ~3,000 staff and assets over RMB1B.
interesting_fact: Despite his wealth he told Chongqing Morning Post in 2015 that he still lived in an ordinary high-rise flat he had moved into in 1999, saying he liked knowing his neighbours.
deep_cut_fact: A creature of habit from four years as a railway soldier in Hebei, he was up by 6am and in the office before 7:30, where he walked 6,000 steps around the company lobby to music every morning - aiming to have walked the equivalent of a lap of the Earth by age 80.
notes: Source is a 2015 profile; he dropped off Hurun after 2021 and is now around 70, so check he is still active. Told the reporter interviews were welcome any day before 8:30am - an approachable, early-rising type. No published contacts found.

name: Ding Yongqaing
current_role: Founder & CEO, Growatt New Energy (Shenzhen)
profile: Ding Yongqiang (丁永强; name misspelled 'Yongqaing' in source list) led a group of PV-industry veterans to found Growatt in Shenzhen in 2011. Growatt makes PV inverters, energy-storage systems and smart energy management, selling in 180+ countries with 60+ service offices, and says it is the world's No.1 residential inverter supplier.
interesting_fact: Growatt says it ranks No.1 globally in residential inverters and among the top four PV-inverter suppliers, with 4.2M+ users on its cloud monitoring platform.
deep_cut_fact: Internationally he goes by 'David Ding'; Growatt's English 'Our Story' page is signed 'David Ding, Growatt Founder and CEO' and frames the company's mission as 'to enable everyone to benefit from sustainable energy'.
notes: info@growatt.com is the published general/sales inbox (not personal). Address him as David Ding in English outreach. Distributed solar + storage is a direct fit for the energy podcast.

name: Wang Nianqiang
current_role: Executive director, BYD Electronic (International) Co. (HKEX: 285); long-time BYD senior executive
profile: Senior BYD executive listed by Hurun China (2021-2026) for wealth from BYD shares. He is an executive director of BYD Electronic, BYD's Shenzhen-based electronics manufacturing arm (handset parts and assembly, auto electronics, AI-server and data-center hardware), which is ~66% owned by BYD and had 2023 revenue of CN¥130B.
interesting_fact: BYD Electronic, which he helps run, employed about 150,000 people in 2023; parent BYD was founded in 1995 as a rechargeable-battery maker before becoming the world's largest plug-in EV producer.
notes: Very low public profile; limited English-language sourcing. Personal biography (age, BYD join date) could not be verified - BYD Electronic site unreachable from this environment and web-search budget was exhausted. Route would be via BYD Electronic investor relations (HKEX: 285). Alive status not specifically confirmed but no reports of death found.

name: Zheng Yongjun
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Semitronix Corporation (杭州广立微, SZSE ChiNext: 301095)
profile: Zheng Yongjun (郑勇军, b. 1971) leads Semitronix, a Hangzhou supplier of yield-focused EDA software, circuit IP and wafer-level electrical (WAT) test equipment used by chip fabs and designers. A Cornell PhD who worked at PDF Solutions and Xilinx, he joined Semitronix in 2007 while a Zhejiang University research fellow; it listed in Shenzhen in Aug 2022.
interesting_fact: Semitronix is one of China's few homegrown EDA vendors, specialising in chip-yield improvement software and fast electrical-test monitoring across advanced process nodes - a niche long dominated by US firms such as his former employer PDF Solutions.
deep_cut_fact: He is a chemical engineer by training: in 1994 he took a double bachelor's in chemical engineering and computer science at Tsinghua, then a Cornell PhD in chemical engineering (2000), before working as a senior engineer at PDF Solutions and a senior staff engineer at Xilinx.
notes: US-trained (Cornell, Silicon Valley) - likely comfortable with English-language outreach. Best route: Semitronix IR / board secretary Lu Chunlong.

name: Zhong Yu
current_role: Probably Vice Chairman and CEO, Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology Corp. (SZSE: 300724) - unverified match
profile: Hurun lists 'Zhong Yu' (钟玉) with company 'S.C' in semiconductor equipment. The most likely match is Yu Zhong, controlling shareholder and senior executive of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology, a maker of solar-cell/semiconductor wet-process and deposition equipment; the Chinese name given (钟玉) could not be confirmed in any source.
notes: Identity not confirmed: no source links the name 钟玉 to a Hurun-listed equipment firm; MarketScreener/Simply Wall St list a 'Zhong Yu' as CEO/Vice Chairman of Shenzhen S.C New Energy. Verify via the company's annual report before outreach. Company site was unreachable from here.

name: Sun Zhongwei
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shenzhen Hello Tech Energy Co. (Huabao Xinneng, Shenzhen-listed since 2022), maker of Jackery
profile: Shandong-born engineer who started in Shenzhen making power banks as an ODM, launched the Jackery brand in 2012 and pivoted the company in 2016 to portable power stations and folding solar panels, where it claims global No.1 share. Hello Tech listed in 2022 and is pushing into home solar/storage (XBC solar roof tiles); wealth shared with wife Wen Meichan.
interesting_fact: Over 90% of his team initially opposed abandoning power banks for portable power stations; Sun pushed ahead and launched the Explorer series, which the company bills as the world's first lithium portable power station, now sold in 50+ countries. Jackery's Solar Mars Bot made TIME's Best Inventions 2023.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000 he arrived in Shenzhen with just 700 yuan, the first university student from his village; a newspaper headline calling new energy one of the 21st century's most promising industries, read by a roadside in Huaqiangbei, made him vow to spend 50 years on lithium batteries.
notes: Also known as Zhuo Sun. marketing@jackery.com is Jackery's published 'PR & Influencer' contact (US site). Strong fit for energy/storage podcast; he has given long interviews to Chinese media. Wealth shared with Wen Meichan.

name: Wen Meichan
current_role: Vice Chairman & Deputy General Manager, Shenzhen Hello Tech Energy Co. (华宝新能, SZSE: 301327; Jackery brand)
profile: Wen Meichan (b. 1984) co-founded Shenzhen Hello Tech Energy, maker of Jackery portable power stations, home energy storage and solar panels, and with co-founder Sun Zhongwei (chairman/GM) is its joint actual controller (about 23.5% vs his 43%). She has been vice chairman and deputy GM since 2020; the company listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2022 and sells heavily into the US, Japan and Europe.
interesting_fact: Jackery helped create the 'portable power station' category for camping, outages and off-grid use; Hello Tech's H1 2025 revenue hit a record RMB 1.637B, up 43% year on year.
deep_cut_fact: She was the original registrant of Hello Tech: on 21 July 2011 she signed the articles founding Shenzhen Hello Tech Energy Co. with RMB 500,000 of registered capital, contributing 49%. Before that she spent 2003-2011, from about age 19, as a product manager at Shenzhen Wantuo Electronics.
notes: Low public profile; her partner Sun Zhongwei is the public face. Only published company email is sales@hello-tech.com (distributor inquiries) - not suitable for press. Securities-affairs (board secretary Zhang Tongzhen) contact is in Hello Tech's CNINFO annual report. Mandarin outreach recommended.

profile: Shao Jiancong (邵建聪) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2009-2012 together with relatives Shao Jianming and Shao Jianjia, with wealth attributed to 'Highsun Yongye Group' (mining and real estate). No public source could be found in this pass confirming the group's identity or his current role.

name: He Boquan
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Today Investment (今日投资) - angel investor
