profile: Chen Bo (陈波, b. 1971) built Ningxia Jiaze Renewables from Ningxia Jiaze Power Generation into a Shanghai-listed wind and solar power producer and has chaired every board since listing. Earlier he ran Beijing trading, auto-sales and aviation-services businesses. He now pitches Jiaze as an integrated new-energy power supplier and also heads Jinyuan Rongtai Investment Management (Ningxia).
interesting_fact: An energy entrepreneur directly relevant to the podcast: his company develops and operates wind and solar farms in Ningxia, northwest China, and in 2025 he described its shift toward an integrated new-energy power supplier (Shanghai Securities News interview).
deep_cut_fact: His first job was as a salesman at the Longkou Foreign Trade Company in Shandong; he later ran Beijing Yichuan Aviation Service Center before moving into wind power in Ningxia.
notes: Strong energy-podcast fit. Board secretary is now Wang Xiaoyi (appointed Feb 2026); IR email is the company's published disclosure mailbox. Many namesakes (academics) — make sure to specify Jiaze.

name: Yu Awu
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Mingpai Jewellery Co. (SZSE: 002574); chairman, Zhejiang Sun & Moon (Riyue) Jewelry Group
profile: Yu Awu (b. 1941), a senior economist from Shaoxing, built the Sun & Moon (Riyue) group from a local gold-jewellery factory into one of China's largest jewellery makers; its listed arm Mingpai Jewellery (gold, platinum, diamonds) is controlled by him and his son Yu Tuliang. The family group also spans property and finance, and Mingpai has diversified into PV solar-cell manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Mingpai Jewellery, best known for gold jewellery, launched a 20GW 'new-energy PV cell smart manufacturing' project through its subsidiary Zhejiang Riyue Solar Energy Technology, a notable jewellery-to-solar pivot relevant to an energy podcast.
deep_cut_fact: From 1987 to 1995 Yu ran the Zhejiang Laofengxiang Jewellery Factory as factory director, and chaired Shaoxing County Laofengxiang Jewellery Co. until 1999, before building his own Riyue group (founded 1995). Still chairman of Mingpai at about 85.
notes: Aged ~85; son Yu Tuliang is co-controller and likely the more practical contact. Group name in Chinese: 日月集团 / 浙江日月首饰集团. The solar unit has faced asset-impairment testing, so frame the PV angle neutrally.

name: Yuan Kaifei
profile: Hurun lists Yuan Kaifei (袁凯飞) under 'Newcentury Shipbuilding'. New Century Shipyard was a private yard in Jingjiang, Jiangsu, that formed a JV with a Singapore company in 2004; New Times Shipbuilding absorbed its assets in 2006. No source found confirming Yuan Kaifei's role at either company.
notes: Could not verify this person's role in English or Chinese searches; Baidu Baike is blocked. He was on Hurun China 2008-2021, with his last appearance in 2021. Check the Chinese company registry (qcc/tianyancha) for New Times / New Century Shipbuilding shareholders before any outreach. Background on the yard: https://www.lr.org/en/shipyards/china/new-times-shipbuilding-co-ltd/

name: Yu Tuliang
current_role: Vice chairman of Zhejiang Sun & Moon (Riyue) Jewelry Group; co-actual controller with his father Yu Awu of Zhejiang Ming Jewelry (SZSE: 002574)
profile: Yu Tuliang (虞兔良) and his father Yu Awu control Zhejiang Sun & Moon Jewelry Group, parent of listed gold-jewellery maker Zhejiang Ming Jewelry (明牌珠宝) in Shaoxing. He ran the business day to day as GM of the group (1995-2010) and as chairman and GM of Ming Jewelry (2009-2016). His father now chairs the listed company.
interesting_fact: Through Zhejiang Mingpai Industrial, the family's group holds 16.2% of Beijing Caishikou Department Store (Caibai, 605599), Beijing's famous gold and jewellery retailer, but has pledged not to take part in running it.
deep_cut_fact: He was chairman and general manager of Zhejiang Mingpai Industrial from 1999 to 2010, and from 2009 to 2016 chairman and GM of Ming Jewelry, which listed on the Shenzhen exchange in 2011.
notes: Hurun lists the wealth as shared with his father Yu Awu. Low media profile. The best route is the listed company's IR email. The business is jewellery and investments, with little overlap with energy or data-center topics.

name: Liu Zhengguo
current_role: Retired (Jan 2025) as Senior Vice President of Beijing OriginWater Technology (碧水源, SZSE: 300070); remains a shareholder
profile: Liu Zhenguo (刘振国, b. 1965; listed here as 'Zhengguo') is a water engineer who joined OriginWater in 2006 as director and GM alongside founder Wen Jianping, then served as vice chairman (2007-2019) as the membrane water-treatment firm grew into one of China's largest sewage/water-reuse companies. After state-owned China Chengxiang (CCCC) took control in 2019-20 he stayed on as VP/SVP until retiring in January 2025.
interesting_fact: OriginWater is known for membrane bioreactor (MBR) water-treatment and reuse technology used in large Chinese municipal plants; Liu briefly doubled as company president (Jun 2017-Feb 2018).
deep_cut_fact: Before business he spent ~20 years as a public water engineer: starting in 1987 at the Miyun County water bureau, then Beijing Water Authority, Beijing Water & Hydropower Technology Center, and deputy head of the Beijing Soil & Water Conservation Station (1999-2006); he is a senior engineer.
notes: Name in Chinese is 刘振国 (Liu Zhenguo). Retired from OriginWater Jan 2025 (2025 annual report); company IR is only an indirect route. Avoid topics around his share auctions/voting-right arrangements.

name: Liu Haibin
current_role: Major individual shareholder (~62m shares, among top-3 holders) of Shanghai Bairun Investment Holding Group (002568.SZ, RIO cocktails); no current executive role found
profile: Early partner of Bairun founder Liu Xiaodong. Bairun began in 1997 as a Shanghai flavours-and-fragrances maker; Liu Haibin held a large stake in it and about 24% of its spun-out alcopop unit Shanghai Bacchus (maker of RIO), which Bairun re-acquired via share issuance in 2015. He and his wife Ma Xiaohua remain top shareholders of the group, which dominates China's ready-to-drink cocktail market and is moving into whisky.
interesting_fact: RIO, the brand behind his fortune, held close to 90% of China's pre-mixed cocktail market by 2021; Bairun still runs its original flavours business under the Bairun name.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews found. 2025 annual report lists him as a top-10 holder (62.16m shares) and confirms he and Ma Xiaohua are spouses. Route only via Bairun board office.

name: Jiang Junping
current_role: Unknown — listed by Hurun (2006-2021) as behind 'Ballon' (investments, real estate); no public record found linking 姜俊平 to an identifiable company
profile: Hurun China Rich List entrant (2006-2021) with wealth attributed to 'Ballon' in investments and real estate. Searches in Chinese and English found no verifiable corporate filing, company website or press coverage tying 姜俊平 to a specific firm, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: Unresolved identity; 'Ballon' could be a Hurun romanisation of a private group name (e.g. 百隆/宝隆). Would need Hurun's Chinese list entry or business-registry lookup to resolve. Low priority.

name: Zhang Zemin
current_role: Co-actual controller (with Liang Huaiyu) of Guangdong Yowant Technology Group (遥望科技, SZSE: 002291), formerly St&Sat (星期六) shoes; no longer chairman
profile: Zhang Zemin (b. 1963) founded the Foshan women's-shoe brand St&Sat (星期六), which listed in Shenzhen in 2009; he was chairman and, until 2018, general manager. After St&Sat bought Hangzhou live-streaming agency Yowant, the company pivoted to influencer live-commerce and was renamed Yowant Technology. Yowant founder Xie Rudong is now chairman; Zhang and Liang Huaiyu remain actual controllers.
interesting_fact: He turned a women's-shoe maker into one of China's big live-streaming e-commerce MCN operators, which is why Hurun now classifies his wealth as 'e-commerce'.
deep_cut_fact: Before shoes he was a teacher at a school in Shenyang (1985). In 1992 he became Belle's exclusive general agent in Shenzhen, and in 1993 he started running the Fushan shoe factory in Nanhai (Foshan), the forerunner of St&Sat.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Liang Huaiyu. The deep-cut career details come from a user-submitted biography page (maigoo) that appears to mirror prospectus data; verify against the 2009 St&Sat prospectus before use. In 2022 he and Xie Rudong jointly urged employees to buy company shares.

name: Liang Huaiyu
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Zhang Zemin) of Yowant Technology (遥望科技, formerly ST&SAT/星期六, 002291.SZ) via LYONE Group Pte. Ltd.
profile: Liang Huaiyu (梁怀宇) and her husband Zhang Zemin built Foshan women's-shoe brand ST&SAT ('Saturday', 星期六), listed in Shenzhen in 2009. After buying livestream-commerce agency Yowant (遥望网络) in 2019 the company pivoted from shoes to influencer e-commerce and was renamed Yowant Technology. The couple control about 13.3% via LYONE Group (Singapore) and Yunnan Zhaolong.
interesting_fact: The 'Saturday' name dates to 1991, when Zhang Zemin opened roadside shoe stores as Belle's first mainland sales agent; after the partnership split he bought a Foshan shoe factory (1993) and opened the first own-brand 'Saturday' store in Shenyang in 1994.
notes: Liang is a low-profile co-owner; her husband Zhang Zemin is the public face. Control confirmed in Yowant 2026 interim report (LYONE Group 7.77% largest holder, couple 13.30% combined). Wealth likely far below Hurun's earlier figure given the stock's decline.

name: Zhang Wenrong
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich Lists 2007-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Yalong' (cable and real estate). Searches in English and Chinese found no reliable public source linking a 张文荣 to a Yalong (亚龙) cable/property group, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not identify the company (Yalong is unlisted / ambiguous). Needs the full company name or province to research further; likely a very low-profile private-company owner.

name: Xu Maogen
current_role: Listed by Hurun as head of Zhejiang Yuandong (Far East) Chemical Fiber (远东化纤), Shaoxing (unverified elsewhere)
profile: Per Hurun's database, Xu Maogen (徐茂根, b. 1954, Shaoxing, Zhejiang) built Shaoxing-based chemical-fibre maker Yuandong (远东化纤, unrelated to Taiwan's Far Eastern New Century); Hurun ranked him No.290 in 2013 with RMB6.2bn and listed him 2003-2015. We found no independent source on him or the firm.
notes: Hurun record: https://www.hurun.net/zh-CN/Rank/HsRankDetailsList?num=WHJ76EYU&search=%E5%BE%90%E8%8C%82%E6%A0%B9&offset=0&limit=20. Tried Chinese searches for 徐茂根 + 远东化纤/绍兴/柯桥/化纤 and the company's chairman; results only returned Taiwan's Far Eastern New Century or other Shaoxing fibre firms. Dropped off Hurun after 2015. No contact found; registry check (Qichacha) is the next step.

name: Shi Jianxiang
current_role: Former chairman of Shanghai Kuailu Investment Group (快鹿集团); resigned April 2016
profile: Shi Jianxiang (施建祥) built Shanghai-based Kuailu Group, a conglomerate spanning taxis, investment/financing platforms, film (it backed 'Ip Man 3') and Hong Kong-listed companies. The group collapsed in 2016 amid a repayment crisis; he left China, resigned as chairman, and Chinese authorities later charged him over illegal fundraising.
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: he is on China's 'Sky Net' list of 100 most-wanted fugitives (2018) and was reported arrested in the US in Oct 2021 at China's request (sources: https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2021-11-03/1978715.html, https://www.chinatimes.com/realtimenews/20211102000627-260407). Current status after 2021 unknown. No deep-cut or contact recorded.

name: Lin Congyin
current_role: Chairman, Joeone Co., Ltd. (九牧王, Shanghai: 601566); special vice-president, China National Garment Association
profile: Lin Congyin founded menswear brand Joeone in Jinjiang, Fujian in the mid-1980s, specialising in men's trousers, and earned the nickname 'king of Chinese trousers'. Joeone listed in Shanghai in 2011. He remains chairman and controlling shareholder, with the company also investing in other fashion brands.
interesting_fact: Joeone won exclusive mainland rights to 'Masha Wang' fabric and sold more than 4 million pairs of trousers between June 1995 and end-1996, passing 100m yuan in sales.
deep_cut_fact: In 1985, with just 200 yuan in his pocket, Lin went to Jiujiang in Jiangxi selling zippers. That is where he saw the opportunity in clothing retail. The next year he used his zipper savings plus 18,000 yuan borrowed to start a garment factory back in Jinjiang.
notes: Before founding Joeone he left a state grain-bureau job in 1984. Route via IR/board office.

name: Zhang Guanfu
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controlling shareholder of Guizhou Xinbang Pharmaceutical (信邦制药, SZSE 002390); left as chairman in August 2016
profile: Zhang Guanfu (张观福), a pharmacist by training, founded Guizhou Xinbang Pharmaceutical in Guiyang and ran it as chairman and general manager from 1995. He took it public in Shenzhen in 2010, and it grew into a drug maker plus hospital and pharma-distribution group. He stepped down as chairman in August 2016 and sold down his shares. No public role since has been found.
interesting_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, he was a government pharmacist-researcher. He worked at the Guizhou Provincial Institute of Traditional Chinese Medicine and the Guizhou Pharmaceutical Administration Bureau before founding Xinbang.
deep_cut_fact: He has a pharmacy degree from Guizhou Medical University and later took an MBA/EMBA at CEIBS (China Europe International Business School).
notes: Last on the Hurun list in 2021 and very low profile since leaving Xinbang in 2016. The SZSE filings on his share reductions (e.g. https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2016-07-12/080ea94f-c6d2-49a6-9154-e366833b5f2f.PDF) confirm he was the controlling shareholder. No personal contact was found, and the company IR is unlikely to forward messages now that he has left.

name: Chen Lifen
current_role: Former chairwoman and general manager, Jiangsu Sunshine Co. (SSE: 600220); long-time executive of Sunshine Group, Jiangyin (current role unclear)
profile: Chen Lifen (陈丽芬) grew up with Jiangyin's Sunshine Group, a fine worsted-wool fabric and suit maker, rising to chair listed Jiangsu Sunshine and steering its move into high-end fabrics, branding and later biomedical and environmental businesses. The parent Sunshine Group entered court-supervised restructuring in March 2025 and she has not appeared on Hurun lists since 2021.
interesting_fact: At its peak Sunshine produced on average 100,000 m of worsted fabric, 10,000 suits and 10,000 shirts a day, and was the first Jiangsu company to win the China Quality Award.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 Sunshine Group took on the international secretariat of ISO's textiles technical committee (ISO/TC38), the first Chinese firm to host an ISO technical committee secretariat; she has said 'Sunshine Group gave me a golden, sunny life' (是阳光集团给了我一个金色的阳光人生).
notes: Sunshine Group is in restructuring (2025) and the listed company has had regulatory issues; Lu Yu chaired Jiangsu Sunshine 2023-2025. Low-priority / sensitive outreach target; no personal or office contact found.

name: Zeng Liqing
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Decent Capital (德迅投资); Tencent co-founder and lifetime honorary adviser
profile: Zeng Liqing (曾李青, b. 1970, Guangzhou) co-founded Tencent in 1998 as the third founder alongside Pony Ma and Tony Zhang, serving as COO 1999-2007 and running sales and marketing. Since leaving operations he has been an active angel/VC investor through Decent Capital, backing consumer internet, gaming and hard-tech start-ups.
interesting_fact: Decent Capital was an early backer of robot maker Unitree, investing about RMB4.6m across two rounds in 2019; its remaining stake was later valued at roughly RMB1.9bn.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tencent he was an engineer at Shenzhen Telecom's data bureau and drove what is described as the first broadband-wired residential compound in Shenzhen (and China) in the mid-1990s; he met Pony Ma through Ma's sister, a colleague at the bureau.
notes: Xidian University alumnus (telecoms). Decent Capital site is JS-rendered; no published email found. Best route is via Decent Capital or Chinese VC/startup events. Avoid mentioning his early QVOD investment.

name: Zhang Zhiping
current_role: Chairman, co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (with wife Liu Cong), Guangdong Greenway Technology (博力威, SSE STAR 688345), Dongguan
profile: Zhang Zhiping (张志平, b. 1976, Changsha area, Hunan) co-founded Greenway in Dongguan in 2010 with his wife Liu Cong (vice-chairman). It makes lithium battery packs and cells for e-bikes and other light EVs, plus consumer and storage uses; listed on the STAR Market in June 2021. The couple control it directly and via Shenzhen Kunlun Dingtian and employee platforms.
interesting_fact: At its 2021 IPO Zhang directly held 26.5% and Liu 6.67%; Hurun first listed the couple in 2021 at RMB5bn.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a civil engineer (industrial & civil construction, Central South University) and started out in 1998 as a manager at Zhuzhou Smelter Group, then moved into batteries: Zhuzhou Lianhe power supplies, a factory manager for a Taiwanese battery maker, and GM of Shenzhen Naili Battery before founding his own firm.
notes: Hurun's 'Greenway' = 博力威. Hurun lists him jointly with wife Liu Cong (刘聪). Board secretary Wang Juan handles IR via dms@greenway-battery.com. Hurun profile: Hunan native, based in Dongguan.

name: Zhang Suyang
current_role: Founding Partner, Volcanics Venture (火山石投资), Shanghai
profile: Zhang Suyang (章苏阳) is one of China's first-generation venture capitalists: he joined IDG Capital around 1994 and led its early bets on Ctrip (1999, ~34x) and Home Inns (2003, ~57x). After retiring from IDG he founded Volcanics Venture in 2016, a boutique early-stage firm (>RMB3bn dual-currency) backing AI, robotics (Geek+, Fourier), chips and healthcare.
interesting_fact: He has said IDG was ready to invest about US$3m in Alibaba but Jack Ma took Goldman Sachs and SoftBank money instead – one of his acknowledged regrets; the eBay-China (EachNet) deal was decided in ~20 hours and signed in a teahouse.
deep_cut_fact: An electronics-engineering graduate (Shanghai University, 1982), he was deputy director of the Ministry of Posts' Shanghai 520 factory and worked at Shanghai Bell before VC; he loves live music (goes whenever a good band comes to town) and was once a keen photographer.
notes: Gives occasional long-form interviews (ChinaVenture, July 2026) on China VC history and AI cycles; good podcast fit (robotics, AI). Approach via Volcanics Venture; no published email found. Background details also in https://pitchhub.36kr.com/organization/1678213531595779.

name: Lam Shun Chiu
current_role: Chairman and CEO, C-MER Medical Holdings (formerly C-MER Eye Care Holdings, HKEX: 3309)
profile: Dr Dennis Lam Shun-chiu (林顺潮) is a Hong Kong ophthalmologist (HKU MBBS 1984) who chaired the Chinese University of Hong Kong's ophthalmology department 1998-2008, then founded C-MER in 2012. It listed in Hong Kong in 2018 and now runs about 70 eye and medical facilities across Hong Kong and mainland China (incl. Shenzhen C-MER Dennis Lam Eye Hospital). He is also a long-serving NPC deputy.
interesting_fact: In 2013 he operated on a six-year-old Shanxi boy whose eyes had been gouged out, a case that made his newly opened Shenzhen eye hospital nationally famous.
deep_cut_fact: His Project Vision Charitable Foundation (founded 2004) follows a 'teach people to fish' model: it has trained 160+ cataract surgeons, set up 32 'poverty-alleviation ophthalmic centres' in China and done 200,000+ cataract operations; APVRS even created a 'Dennis Lam Lecture' in his name in 2023.
notes: Known professionally as Dennis S.C. Lam. Very public figure in ophthalmology (Power List Hall of Fame); Hurun lists wealth jointly with Li Xiaoting. Approachable via C-MER corporate office or ophthalmology conferences (APAO/APVRS). No published IR email found.

name: Li Xiaoting
current_role: Vice Chairman and CEO (since June 2025), executive director, C-MER Medical Holdings (formerly C-MER Eye Care, HKEX: 3309)
profile: Li Xiaoting (李肖婷), 47, is co-controlling shareholder (with her husband, ophthalmologist Dr Dennis Lam Shun Chiu) of C-MER, a Hong Kong-listed eye-care and medical group operating clinics and hospitals in Hong Kong and mainland China. She ran its Hong Kong eye centre from 2012 and Shenzhen C-MER Hospital from 2013, and took over as vice chairman and CEO in June 2025.
interesting_fact: In a June 2025 board reshuffle, Dennis Lam stepped down and Li became vice chairman and CEO, while former Hong Kong health secretary Dr Ko Wing Man joined as independent non-executive director and vice chairman; C-MER returned to profit in FY2025 on revenue of about HK$1.95bn.
deep_cut_fact: She studied tourism management at Shenyang University (2001), took a postgraduate business diploma at Massey University in New Zealand (2004), and worked as project coordinator/executive officer at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (2005-2009) before entering eye care.
notes: Company (not personal) social accounts; no published IR email found in the 2025 annual report. Company secretary is Chan Wa Ping (via registered office, Central, Hong Kong). She is a Pingshan (Shenzhen) CPPCC member.

name: Feng Tao
current_role: Founder, Shanghai Yongxuan Venture Capital Management (NewMargin / Lianchuang Yongxuan); co-founding partner, BioTrack Capital (Boyuan) per investor databases
profile: Feng Tao is a veteran Shanghai venture capitalist. He founded NewMargin Ventures (Shanghai Lianchuang) in 1999, one of China's earliest domestic VC firms, which later operated as Lianchuang Yongxuan / Shanghai Yongxuan Venture Capital. By 2015 he said his group managed about RMB 20bn and had taken Beijing Yongxuan public on the New Third Board.
interesting_fact: NewMargin, founded in 1999, was among the first generation of homegrown Chinese VC firms. In 2015 Feng said his group had more than 50 exits via the New Third Board in a single half-year.
deep_cut_fact: At a 2015 industry forum he called the New Third Board China's 'real growth-enterprise board' (真正的创业板), arguing it was built for companies in their growth stage. He cited game developer Wuyou Interactive as a portfolio example.
notes: Common name; the Hurun listing (Yongxuan, investments) matches the Shanghai Yongxuan founder. His later BioTrack Capital role comes only from investor databases and is unconfirmed. No published personal contact; approach through the firm. Off Hurun since 2021.

name: Fan Baoqiang
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich List 2018-2021 (~US$780m) with real-estate wealth from 'Zhihui' (智汇). No public English or Chinese source was found linking Fan Baoqiang (范保强) to an identifiable Zhihui property company, so his business and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Not the same as Fan Xiulian (founder of Tibet Zhihui Mining, Shenyang) - no link between them found. Private developer with no online footprint; dropped off Hurun after 2021. Would need Hurun's original entry (city) to identify.

name: Jin Xianghua
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jinhong Gas Co. (金宏气体, SSE STAR 688106), Suzhou
profile: Jin Xianghua (金向华, b. 1977) has run Suzhou-based Jinhong Gas since it was set up in 1999 from a local liquid-oxygen plant with his mother Jin Jianping. It grew into a major private industrial and electronic specialty-gas supplier (incl. ultra-pure ammonia for chips) and listed on the STAR Market in 2020. He held ~20% after selling 3.42% to Jinan Qianyuanhui in 2026.
interesting_fact: He became legal representative of the newly formed Jinhong at 22, having already managed the Suzhou Liquid Oxygen Factory from age 21; he is also a vice-chairman of the China Industrial Gases Industry Association.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, at 18, was production supervisor at the Wuxian Refractory Materials Factory (1995-97). He won a 2014 Jiangsu Province Science & Technology Award (2nd class) and, per the prospectus, is executive director of an antiques company, Xinfu Guwan (鑫福古玩).
notes: Hands-on founder-CEO, also listed as a core technical staff member. Family concert party: mother Jin Jianping, uncle Zhu Genlin, wife (per 2026 interim report). Best route: board secretary Chen Ying via dongmi@ address.

name: Liu Cong
current_role: Founding shareholder, Guangdong Greenway Technology Co. (博力威, 688345.SH); executive role not confirmed
profile: Liu Cong is listed on Hurun China 2021 jointly with Zhang Zhiping, chairman of Guangdong Greenway Technology (博力威), a Dongguan lithium-battery maker founded in 2010 and STAR-listed in 2021. Registration records show Liu held about 6.7% in 2019. Greenway makes e-bike and light-EV batteries, energy storage and consumer-electronics packs.
interesting_fact: Greenway says it was the first A-share company whose core business is lithium batteries for light vehicles such as e-bikes. It launched e-bike batteries in 2011 and now also makes its own cells and home and portable energy storage.
notes: Very low public profile: no biography, board role or interviews found. The 6.7% stake comes from a 2019 registration snapshot (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678329178878981). The best route is the board-secretary office email (dms@) or chairman Zhang Zhiping. 'Liu Cong' is a common name, so confirm before outreach.

name: Zhou Ping
current_role: Chairman, EIT Environmental Development Group (玉禾田, SZSE: 300815), Shenzhen
profile: Zhou Ping (周平) built EIT/Yuhetian into one of China's largest private sanitation and environmental-services groups (street cleaning, waste collection, property cleaning, landscaping), listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He and his son Zhou Mengchen are the actual controllers. In 2025 the group opened a new Shenzhen HQ and pushed into robotics for autonomous sweeping.
interesting_fact: In June 2025 EIT launched Shenzhen Yushu Intelligent Robotics (RMB 50m capital) and a joint innovation centre with humanoid-robot maker AgiBot, targeting driverless street sweepers and smart sorting robots.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in 1981 as a textile-machinery repairman at the Harbin Textile Mill in Heilongjiang, studied business management at the Heilongjiang Textile Industry Institute, and spent the 1990s in Shenzhen's restaurant trade before building a sanitation empire.
notes: Source of wealth 'EIT' = EIT Environmental Development Group (玉禾田). Classed as 'utility' but the business is sanitation/city services, not power. Still chairman per Sept 2026 shareholder-meeting notice (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-09-14/1225563117.PDF). Board secretary: Zhang Weibin. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Zhou Mengchen
current_role: Co-actual controller (with Zhou Ping) of EIT Environmental Development Group (Yuhetian, SZSE: 300815); no executive title disclosed.
profile: Zhou Mengchen is one of the two actual controllers of EIT Environmental Development Group (Yuhetian), a Shenzhen-based urban sanitation and environmental services contractor listed on ChiNext in 2020. Together with chairman Zhou Ping she controls ~51% via holding company Tibet Tianzhirun Investment, which the two set up in 2014; she directly holds ~4.6%.
interesting_fact: EIT's controlling holding company, Tibet Tianzhirun Investment, was set up by Zhou Ping and Zhou Mengchen in January 2014; environmental-engineering group BGE (Beijing GeoEnviron) is an indirect shareholder of EIT, per its 2025 financial statements.
notes: 'EIT' in input = EIT Environmental Development Group (玉禾田). Almost no public profile for Zhou Mengchen; family relationship to Zhou Ping not stated in filings (not confirmed). Business is sanitation services, not energy/data centers. Route via board office email (dmb@eit-sz.com, board secretary Zhang Weibin).

name: Zhu Yuanzheng
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Wuxi NCE Power Co. (新洁能, SSE 605111)
profile: Founder and controlling shareholder of Wuxi NCE Power, a fabless power-semiconductor designer of MOSFETs and IGBTs used in power supplies, EVs, solar inverters and data-center power. He co-founded the company in 2013 (holding 51% at formation) and took it public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in September 2020.
interesting_fact: NCE Power was set up in Jan 2013 by Zhu together with Jiangsu Xinchao (JCET's former parent group) and his earlier vehicle Wuxi NCE Power Semiconductor, and listed less than eight years later.
notes: Low-profile; little personal biography online. Info@ncepower.com is listed as the board secretary's mailbox (tel 0510-85618058); data from a 2021 aggregator snapshot, so confirm in latest annual report.

name: Yang Yong
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and Chief Engineer, Cmsemicon / 中微半导体（深圳）股份有限公司 (SSE STAR: 688380)
profile: Shenzhen chip entrepreneur (b. ~1972, New Zealand citizen) who founded microcontroller designer 中微半导 (Cmsemicon) in 2001 after running Shenzhen Pute Integrated Circuit. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022 and filed for a Hong Kong listing in 2025; it is China's largest MCU vendor by 2024 shipments.
interesting_fact: Per Frost & Sullivan data in its Hong Kong prospectus, Cmsemicon ranked No.1 in China's MCU market by 2024 shipments (12.6% share) and No.3 by revenue; it is No.1 in smart-home-appliance MCUs.

interesting_fact: IDG Capital led a $60 million round in Circle, the US fintech behind the USDC stablecoin, to back its China expansion; Zhou is now listed in SEC insider filings as a ten-percent owner of the public Circle Internet Group.
deep_cut_fact: When IDG partners Zhang Zhen, Gao Xiang and Yue Bin left to start Gaorong Capital, Zhou helped rewrite their business plan, personally introduced Accel partners as LPs and invested as an LP himself. Gaorong closed a first fund of over $200M within three months.
notes: Very low public profile. In 2018 he and Xiong Xiaoge said they would stop taking part in investor rankings 'to leave the opportunity to young people'. The best route is IDG Capital's media email. The Circle/stablecoin and Chinese-VC angles are the hooks.

name: Feng Yonglin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Chongqing Baiya Sanitary Products Co. (003006.SZ)
profile: Feng Yonglin (b. 1963) built Chongqing Baiya, maker of the Free More (Ziyoudian) sanitary-pad brand. Baiya listed on the Shenzhen main board in 2020 as China's first A-share sanitary-napkin company. It grew from a Sichuan-Chongqing base into a national top-3 brand, with RMB 3.49bn in 2025 revenue.
interesting_fact: Baiya's Chongqing plant runs 30+ smart lines with capacity of 6.7 billion pads a year, and was named to MIIT's 2025 list of 5G factories.
deep_cut_fact: Before hygiene products, Feng was head of the enterprise-management office and later deputy factory director at the Chongqing Match Factory, then ran Chongqing Huasheng tissue-paper and Sishuang hygiene-products companies.
notes: Low media profile. baiya.db@baiya.cn appears to be the board office (dongban) inbox. Investor Q&A is also possible via irm.cninfo.com.cn.

name: Hong Weidong
current_role: Deceased (was chairman and general manager, Yusys Technologies 300674.SZ)
profile: Founder of Beijing-based fintech/banking-software company Yusys Technologies (宇信科技). Died on September 29, 2026; his wife and co-founder Wu Hong was elected chairman and general manager.
notes: Deceased 2026-09-29 per Yusys announcement (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-09-30/1225589731.PDF; https://news.10jqka.com.cn/20260930/c680419431.shtml). Successor: Wu Hong (吴红), co-founder and his widow.

name: Yan Ming
current_role: Non-executive director and controlling shareholder (~23.7%), JF SmartInvest Holdings (HKEX: 9636), Shanghai
profile: Yan Ming co-founded Shanghai-based Yintech Investment Holdings (Nasdaq-listed 2016) with Chen Wenbin and Chen Ningfeng, and the trio are controlling shareholders of JF SmartInvest (九方智投), an online investment-research/education and stock-advisory platform that listed in Hong Kong in 2023. He has been a non-executive director there since August 2021.
interesting_fact: In 2025 JF SmartInvest moved into licensed brokerage by acquiring Yintech Financial, owner of Hong Kong's Forthright Securities and Forthright Capital - effectively reuniting the founders' earlier Yintech business with the listed company.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, Yan spent 2003-2013 as general manager of Beijing Jinghua Times International Culture & Entertainment, and since 2018 he has chaired the Hong Kong Federation of Jiangxi Associations.
notes: Non-executive, low-profile. Holdings: Chen Wenbin 36.14%, Yan Ming 23.72%, Chen Ningfeng 21.10% (May 2025 HKEX circular). Deep-cut source is an aggregator (MarketScreener); verify before use. Education per company site: finance BA (Shanxi Univ. of Finance & Economics), EMBA (CKGSB).

name: Guo Li
current_role: Reported CFO / early partner, CDH Investments (鼎晖投资)
profile: Guo Li (郭力) appears on Hurun (2015-2021) as a CDH Investments shareholder. Aggregator profiles describe a Ms. Guo Li who joined CDH in its founding year (2002) and serves as CFO of CDH Investments Management (HK). She previously worked at Arthur Andersen (1997-2001), is a CPA and graduated from the Central University of Finance and Economics.
interesting_fact: CDH grew out of the direct-investment department of China International Capital Corp (CICC). It was spun out in 2002 by six founders led by Wu Shangzhi and Jiao Zhen, with GIC, China Investment Guarantee and Zurich Capital, and became one of China's largest PE firms.
notes: Identity only moderately confirmed: the CFO background comes from data aggregators (mergr.com, marketscreener), not an official CDH page. Very low profile. Any approach would go through CDH corporate channels (cdhfund.com).

name: Ji Yue
current_role: Partner, Sequoia Capital China (now HSG/HongShan), TMT investing; current title not confirmed in 2024-26 sources
profile: Ji Yue (计越) has been a venture investor in China since 1999, working at Walden International, Vertex Management and CIV before joining Sequoia Capital China as a TMT partner. He led or participated in deals including Dianping (Sequoia was its only Series A investor), Ele.me, Tuniu, Ganji, Douban, Noah Wealth and Maple Leaf Education, plus AI-era bets such as 4Paradigm and Sensors Data.
interesting_fact: Sequoia was Dianping's sole Series A investor — a bet Ji Yue was involved in that later became part of Meituan-Dianping.
deep_cut_fact: He said he would rather spend an hour trying a product as a 'novice user' than sit through an hour-long meeting he doesn't understand, and that investors should never be in the spotlight (36Kr Open Day, Shanghai, 2013).
notes: Self-described as preferring to stay out of the spotlight; no personal channels found. A 'Yue Ji' linked to Hongshan sits on GalaxyCore's board per aggregator data (unverified). Best route likely via HSG.

name: Ge Yaolun
current_role: Director and lifetime honorary chairman, Hailir Pesticides and Chemicals Group (SSE: 603639)
profile: Ge Yaolun (about 65) founded Qingdao-based Hailir, a crop-protection (pesticide) maker, after a career in Laixi's rural supply cooperatives and agri-input firms. He chaired the company through its Shanghai listing (SSE: 603639); his son Ge Jiacheng is now chairman and GM, and Ge, his wife Zhang Aiying and son jointly control the group.
interesting_fact: Hailir is a family-controlled pesticide group from Laixi, Qingdao; Ge stepped back to 'lifetime honorary chairman' and handed the chairmanship and CEO role to his son Ge Jiacheng, a former accountant at Alcatel-Lucent's Qingdao unit.
deep_cut_fact: Ge began as head of the fruit station at the Tangjiazhuang supply-and-marketing cooperative in Laixi, then deputy director of the Wangcheng co-op, and ran the fruit company of Qingdao Dongfang Peanut Group before moving into agrochemicals.
notes: Largely retired from operations; son Ge Jiacheng (chairman/GM) is the active leader. Outreach is better via the company board office.

name: Guo Peng
profile: Hurun lists Guo Peng (郭鹏) as the owner behind Puyang Iron and Steel, the private Hebei Puyang Iron & Steel (part of Hebei Puyang Industrial Group) in Yangyi Town, Wu'an, Handan. In 2020 it was named one of the five groups into which Wu'an planned to consolidate its 14 steelmakers. No public source found confirming his title.
interesting_fact: In Wu'an's 2020 consolidation plan, which merged 14 local steel companies into five groups, Puyang Iron and Steel was chosen as one of the five surviving group platforms.
notes: Could not confirm his role. Baidu and the company site (pygt.cn) were unreachable. His last Hurun appearance was 2021. The company is private and unlisted, so it has no IR channel. Verify through a Chinese corporate registry before outreach. Low-priority, very private.

name: Li Xianhua
current_role: Co-founder and director, JinkoSolar (晶科能源, SSE 688223) and JinkoSolar Holding (NYSE: JKS); director of Jinko Power (晶科科技)
profile: Born 1974; co-founded JinkoSolar in 2006 with brother Li Xiande and Chen Kangping, first to supply wafers to elder brother Li Xianshou's ReneSola. As first GM he ran production and quality; Jinko became the world's top module shipper. He remains a director and one of three founders jointly controlling ~55% via Jinko Investment.
interesting_fact: The Li brothers' 'iron triangle' (Li Xiande on strategy, Li Xianhua on manufacturing and process quality, Chen Kangping on finance) ran Jinko for ~20 years, taking it to NYSE in 2010 and STAR Market in 2022; a Jinko executive called Li Xianhua 'a technical expert, very professional in production management and quality control'.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he ran a car-repair business; in 2006 he and Li Xiande sold their own assets to register Desheng Solar and Jinko Energy, and before that he managed Yuhuan Sunshine Energy (2000-06), his elder brother's early solar firm.
notes: Hurun lists Chinese name as 李先华 but company filings use 李仙华 (same Jinko co-founder). Very low public profile, no personal channels; route via JinkoSolar IR/board office. Jinko Holding approved renaming to 'Jinko Holdings Limited' (Oct 2026). Avoid elder brother Li Xianshou topic.

name: Li Shilun
current_role: Director of Shaoxing Shangyu Jingsheng Investment (controlling shareholder of Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical, SZSE: 300316); retired Zhejiang University professor
profile: Li Shilun (李世伦), born 1962 and holding a PhD in engineering, spent 1988-2022 at Zhejiang University's School of Mechanical Engineering. He was part of the academic group behind Jingsheng M&E, which makes crystal-growth furnaces and equipment for solar and semiconductor silicon and SiC. His wealth comes from his stake in Jingsheng Investment, the controlling holding company.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng grew out of Zhejiang University's mechanical engineering school. Several founders and directors are ZJU professors, and it became one of China's main suppliers of monocrystalline silicon growth furnaces for the solar industry.
deep_cut_fact: He taught and did research at Zhejiang University's School of Mechanical Engineering for 34 years (Aug 1988-Jul 2022) before retiring. He was a Jingsheng director 2010-2015 and chaired its supervisory board from Dec 2019.
notes: Academic co-founder rather than an operator. He no longer appears among listed-company officers in the 2025 annual report, probably because China's 2024 Company Law changes led many firms to abolish supervisory boards. Highly relevant to the solar and semiconductor equipment theme. Route is via the company securities office.

name: Mao Quanlin
current_role: Director and Vice President, Zhejiang Jingsheng Mechanical & Electrical Co. (晶盛机电, SZSE: 300316)
profile: Mao Quanlin (毛全林, b. 1970) is a co-founding executive and shareholder of Jingsheng, the Shaoxing-based maker of crystal-growth furnaces and equipment for solar-grade silicon, semiconductors and silicon carbide. He has been a director and (senior) vice president since 2010, focused on production management; his wealth comes from Jingsheng shares held directly (~0.8%) and through the founders' holding vehicle.
interesting_fact: Jingsheng is a core supplier of the monocrystalline silicon furnaces behind China's solar boom and has expanded into SiC substrates and semiconductor equipment, directly relevant to energy and chip supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: His formal schooling stopped at junior middle school (初中), yet he rose on production-management experience to the board of a high-tech equipment maker and shares a Zhejiang Provincial Science & Technology Award (first prize).
notes: Not the controller (Cao Jianwei / Qiu Minxiu are). Low public profile; route via Jingsheng board office. Good fit for an energy-focused show (solar/SiC equipment).

name: Xiao Zhengqiang
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller, Luoyang Xinqianglian Slewing Bearing (300850.SZ, ChiNext)
profile: Born 1971 in Henan, Xiao Zhengqiang and his brother Xiao Gaoqiang (general manager) built Luoyang Xinqianglian into a maker of large slewing bearings, wind-turbine main-shaft bearings and tunnel-boring-machine bearings, supplying wind OEMs such as Mingyang and Envision. Listed on ChiNext in 2020; he has been chairman since 2016.
interesting_fact: Xinqianglian's growth came from localising large wind-turbine main-shaft bearings, long dominated by foreign suppliers, as Chinese wind OEMs pushed domestic sourcing.
deep_cut_fact: Before bearings, he spent 13 years (1992-2005) as deputy head then head of the expatriate camp of French contractor Dumez on Lot 3 of the Xiaolangdi Dam on the Yellow River, after starting as a purchasing supervisor for the Xiaolangdi services company in 1990. He has a high-school education.
notes: Strong fit for energy (wind) angle. Route via board secretary Kou Congmei's office.

name: Gao Qiang
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Deputy General Manager, Shanghai Haoyuan Chemexpress (皓元医药, SH:688131); co-actual controller with chairman Zheng Baofu
profile: Gao Qiang (b. 1973), a Hong Kong University chemistry PhD, co-founded Shanghai Haoyuan Chemexpress in 2006 with fellow HKU chemist Zheng Baofu. The company sells life-science research reagents (MedChemExpress brand) and provides APIs/intermediates and CDMO services; it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021. Gao serves as director and deputy GM.
interesting_fact: Haoyuan's catalogue of intermediates covers key building blocks for drugs such as ticagrelor, palbociclib and lenacapavir, while its reagent arm supplies labs worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a chemistry master's at Lanzhou University (1999) and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong (2004), worked as an HKU chemistry researcher until 2006, then founded the company within months of leaving academia.
notes: Scientist-founder, low media profile; chairman Zheng Baofu is the main public face. Hurun lists wealth shared with Liu Yan. IR phone 021-58338205 published.

name: Qiu Jiajun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guobang Pharma Ltd. (国邦医药, SSE: 605507), Xinchang, Zhejiang
profile: Qiu Jiajun (b. 1965), a China Pharmaceutical University graduate and senior engineer, worked at Zhejiang Xinchang Pharmaceutical Factory from 1988 to 1996 before founding Guobang in 1996 as a small county plant making feed additives and veterinary drugs. It grew into a global supplier of antibiotic APIs, intermediates and animal-health products and listed in Shanghai in August 2021, with Qiu still chairman.
interesting_fact: Guobang started in animal health because that market was less crowded, then moved into human APIs; it has ranked among China's top 100 pharmaceutical manufacturers for ten consecutive years (2016–2025).
deep_cut_fact: The company name comes from the phrase 立人立国，兴业兴邦 ('build people, build the nation; grow industry, strengthen the country'). Qiu likens routine products to home cooking and new drugs to fine dishes: you have to master the basics before you can innovate.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Chen Jingjing. Board secretary is 彭德光 (per cninfo). Best route is Guobang's investor-relations/securities office.

name: Chen Jingjing
current_role: Co-actual controller of Guobang Pharma (国邦医药, 605507.SH) with husband Qiu Jiajun; controls Xinchang Qingyu Investment Development
profile: Chen Jingjing (陈晶晶) and her husband, chairman Qiu Jiajun, are the actual controllers of Guobang Pharma, a Xinchang, Zhejiang-based maker of active pharmaceutical ingredients, veterinary APIs and chemical intermediates, listed in Shanghai in 2021. She holds no executive post; her stake is held largely through Xinchang Qingyu Investment Development, which she controls.
interesting_fact: Guobang is one of the world's largest suppliers of macrolide and quinolone antibiotic APIs and China's largest producer of intermediates such as sodium borohydride, selling to 117 countries; its subsidiary helped draft standards for the Chinese Veterinary Pharmacopoeia.
notes: Annual report lists her occupation as 'none' (no executive role); husband Qiu Jiajun is the public face and best contact route via Guobang IR. No interviews or personal channels found.

name: Quan Qiuhong
current_role: Chairwoman, controlling shareholder and founder, BGT Group (倍杰特, SZSE: 300774)
profile: Born 1970, Quan Qiuhong (female) founded Beijing BGT International Environmental Technology in 2004 after a decade in water-treatment sales and management in Zhengzhou; BGT listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext and specialises in industrial water treatment and zero-discharge reuse of high-salinity wastewater. The company has since expanded into salt-lake lithium extraction and mineral development.
interesting_fact: BGT's core technology recovers resources from high-salt industrial wastewater (e.g. from coal-chemical plants), and it has pivoted that know-how into salt-lake lithium extraction, an energy-transition angle.
deep_cut_fact: She started out in 1995 as the Central China sales agent for Peninsula (半岛) Water Treatment, then became deputy GM (Hong Kong side representative) of its Zhengzhou JV and ran Zhengzhou Dahe Water Treatment Equipment before founding BGT in 2004.
notes: Hurun's 'BGT' = 倍杰特 (identified via cninfo filings). Water/lithium angle relevant to energy and data-center cooling topics. Route via company board office.

name: Xia Jun
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Guangdong Create Century Intelligent Equipment Group (创世纪, SZ:300083)
profile: Xia Jun (夏军, b. 1975) has run Shenzhen Create Century Machinery, a maker of CNC machine tools such as drilling/tapping and machining centres used in electronics and auto-parts production, since 2005. The listed company Jinsheng Precision acquired Create Century around 2015-2016 and later refocused on it; Xia became the controlling figure and chairman, and the group was renamed Create Century. He co-holds his stake with Ling Hui.
interesting_fact: Listed company Jinsheng (劲胜), originally a phone-casing maker, bought Create Century to pivot into high-end CNC machine tools; it eventually shed the old business and took Create Century's name, with Xia taking control around 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Xia started out as a salesman (业务员) and later a manager at Zhuhai Beisute (珠海倍速特) enterprise group before becoming executive director and GM of Shenzhen Create Century Machinery in December 2005. He completed an EMBA programme at Tsinghua.
notes: Best route is the board-secretary office (secretary Wu Yongbing) via ir@szccm.com. 2026 press coverage includes a patent dispute and a CSRC Guangdong warning letter on disclosure; avoid those topics.

name: Ling Hui
current_role: Shareholder and person acting in concert with her husband Xia Jun, controller of Guangdong Create Century Intelligent Equipment Group (300083.SZ)
profile: Ling Hui is the wife and acting-in-concert party of Xia Jun, chairman and GM of Create Century (创世纪), a Shenzhen/Dongguan maker of CNC machine tools and drilling/tapping centres for 3C electronics and general industry. Her wealth (listed jointly with Xia Jun) comes from their stake in the company. She does not appear to hold an executive role.
interesting_fact: Create Century's CNC machining centres are widely used to make smartphone and laptop casings. Xia Jun began as a salesman at Zhuhai Beisuite before running Shenzhen Create Century Machinery from 2005.
notes: Private, non-executive; media coverage of her is limited to share-sale disclosures (e.g. 2024 reduction, per NBD https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2025-02-26/3767697.html). Better to approach Xia Jun via company IR.

name: Zhang Yingjiu
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (about 12.6% in 2025), Yangling Metron New Material (美畅股份, SZSE 300861); professor, School of Physics and Engineering, Zhengzhou University
profile: Zhang Yingjiu (张迎九, b. 1969) co-founded Yangling Metron in Shaanxi in 2015 with Wu Ying and others. Metron makes the electroplated diamond wire used to slice silicon wafers for solar panels and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2020. He was its second-largest shareholder, and his stake drove his Hurun ranking in 2020-21. He also left the company's board.
interesting_fact: Metron's diamond wire is an unglamorous but critical input to the solar boom. It is used to saw polysilicon ingots into the thin wafers in most of the world's PV panels.
deep_cut_fact: He is a serving physics professor at Zhengzhou University's School of Physics and Engineering. Metron's prospectus credits the 'Jia Haibo and Zhang Yingjiu team' with being first in the industry to launch multi-wire diamond-wire production equipment ('one machine, six wires'), which raised output per machine.
notes: A scientist-investor who gives almost no interviews. In 2025 he disclosed plans to sell part of his stake (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202505201676133954_1.pdf). Relevant to the energy/solar angle. Possible routes are the Metron board secretary office or his Zhengzhou University faculty page, but no published personal email was found.

name: Gao Junfang
current_role: None - former chairwoman of Changsheng Bio-technology (delisted); serving a life sentence
profile: Gao Junfang (高俊芳) was chairwoman of Changchun Changsheng Bio-technology, a vaccine maker at the centre of China's 2018 falsified rabies-vaccine scandal. The company was delisted and bankrupt; she was sentenced to life imprisonment by the Changchun Intermediate Court in Jan 2026, upheld on appeal by the Jilin High Court in Sept 2026.
notes: Not a viable outreach target: imprisoned (life sentence, final Sept 2026), fortune confiscated, company defunct. Recommend removing from the list.

name: Tang Xuejiao
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen Manst Technology (曼恩斯特, SZSE: 301325); co-holder with GM/founder Peng Jianlin (彭建林)
profile: Tang Xuejiao (唐雪姣) chairs Shenzhen Manst Technology, founded in 2014 with Peng Jianlin (GM/CEO, Central South University graduate). Manst makes high-precision slot-die coating heads and coating lines for lithium-ion battery electrodes, plus hydrogen electrolysis, energy storage and semiconductor coating equipment; it listed on ChiNext in 2022/23.
interesting_fact: Manst says its slot-die coating heads broke foreign makers' monopoly in lithium battery electrode coating; it is now a national 'little giant' and Guangdong manufacturing single-champion with 260+ patents, and has expanded into water-electrolysis hydrogen.
notes: Input name_chinese (彭建林) is actually the co-holder Peng Jianlin; Tang Xuejiao is chairman per MarketScreener/Simply Wall St (https://simplywall.st/stocks/cn/capital-goods/szse-301325/shenzhen-manst-technology-shares/management). Strong energy-storage/hydrogen angle. Brand-department email is the best published media route.

name: Peng Jianlin
current_role: Founder, Director and General Manager, Shenzhen Manst Technology (曼恩斯特, SZSE ChiNext: 301325); Tang Xuejiao (唐雪姣) is chair/legal representative
profile: Peng Jianlin (彭建林), a Central South University graduate, founded Shenzhen Manst Technology in 2014. Manst makes precision slot-die coating heads and coating systems used to coat lithium-battery electrodes, supplying CATL, BYD, ATL, LG Energy Solution, CALB and Gotion, and listed on ChiNext in May 2023. The Hurun entry is shared with Tang Xuejiao, Manst's chair.
interesting_fact: Manst is a national 'little giant' specialist whose coating dies sit inside the battery lines of CATL, BYD and LG Energy Solution – an upstream picks-and-shovels play on EV and grid-storage batteries.
notes: Input record mixes names: English name Peng Jianlin but Chinese name 唐雪姣 (Tang Xuejiao, listed as co-holder). Both are tied to Manst; Tang is legal rep per cninfo. Founder/GM claim from https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/JIAN-LIN-PENG-A3RJP9/. Battery/energy-storage angle fits the podcast.

name: Baljinder Boparan
current_role: Director, Boparan Holdings (parent of 2 Sisters Food Group); trustee, The Boparan Charitable Trust
profile: Baljinder Kaur Boparan co-founded 2 Sisters Food Group with her husband Ranjit Singh Boparan in 1993; the couple are the sole shareholders of Boparan Holdings, now one of the UK's biggest food manufacturers (poultry, ready meals, Fox's biscuits). She sits on the holding-company board and is closely involved in the family's children's charity.
interesting_fact: 2 Sisters started in 1993 as a small frozen-poultry cutting operation in the West Midlands and grew by acquisition (Northern Foods in 2011, Vion UK in 2013) into the UK's largest food company by turnover.
deep_cut_fact: As a trustee of The Boparan Charitable Trust she helps fund disadvantaged, disabled and terminally ill children up to age 18 across England and Wales; the trust (charity no. 1129992) runs fundraisers such as the 'Atlas Challenge' and takes individual grant applications.
notes: Very private; husband Ranjit is the public face. The trust email is for grant applications, so use the trust contact form or 2SFG corporate comms for a general approach.

name: Mark C Pigott
current_role: Executive Chairman, PACCAR Inc (Nasdaq: PCAR); Chairman of the DAF Trucks Supervisory Board
profile: Mark Pigott (born 1954) is the fourth generation of his family to lead PACCAR, the Bellevue, Washington maker of Kenworth, Peterbilt and DAF trucks. He joined in 1978, was chairman and CEO from 1997 to 2014 (a period of ~1,700% total shareholder return), and has been executive chairman since 2014; he also presides over the PACCAR Foundation.
interesting_fact: A committed Anglophile and bibliophile, he sits on the boards of the British Library Foundation and Royal Shakespeare Company America and has led capital-project philanthropy at St Paul's Cathedral, London.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three Stanford degrees earned over 22 years - a BS in industrial engineering (1976), an MS in business (1984) and, while running PACCAR, a BA in humanities (1998) - and in 2014 founded the annual Pigott Poetry Prize in Ireland.
notes: Press contact is Ken Hastings, PACCAR Public Affairs (named on every earnings release). Pigott keeps a low personal media profile; arts/literary philanthropy (British Library, poetry prize, Trinity College Dublin) is a good conversational angle.

name: John D. Cote
current_role: Director, GPGI, Inc. (formerly CompoSecure; NYSE: GPGI); Managing Partner and founder, SRM Equity Partners
profile: John D. Cote (b. c.1982) is a private-equity investor and the son of former Honeywell CEO David Cote. He has sat on the GPGI (ex-CompoSecure) board since Resolute Holdings took control in September 2024. GPGI combined with Husky Technologies in January 2026. As manager of Tungsten 2024 LLC, managing member of Resolute Compo Holdings, he is deemed a beneficial owner of about 17.8% of GPGI.
interesting_fact: GPGI, the renamed CompoSecure (a maker of premium metal payment cards), became a Resolute-managed industrial platform. In January 2026 it combined with injection-molding equipment maker Husky Technologies in a deal involving Platinum Equity.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was a J.P. Morgan investment banker from 2005 to 2011 in the Natural Resources coverage group. He founded SRM Equity Partners in 2013 and was CEO of Industrial Inspection & Analysis, a testing and analytical business, from 2015 to 2019; he remains its chairman.
notes: The SEC-derived net worth overstates his personal wealth: the 51.7m shares (17.8%) are held by Resolute Compo Holdings and are shared with Thomas Knott and the Resolute investors. Energy/industrial angle: his J.P. Morgan natural-resources background. Executive chairman David Cote (his father) is the public face.

name: Kusumben Hasmukh Chudgar
current_role: Shareholder and former non-executive director (board entry 2015), Intas Pharmaceuticals Ltd, Ahmedabad
profile: Kusumben Hasmukhbhai Chudgar is a member of the Chudgar family that founded and controls Intas Pharmaceuticals, India's largest unlisted drugmaker, started by pharmacist Hasmukh Chudgar in Gujarat in 1977. She has been listed as a non-executive director of Intas and appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2018-2019 (~US$756m) as an individual stakeholder.
interesting_fact: Intas grew from a small Gujarat drug-making unit (1977) into a global generics and biosimilars group without early equity dilution; its $764m purchase of Actavis UK turned it into a major European generics supplier (Accord Healthcare).
notes: Very private; no interviews or personal public profile found. Director listing per MarketScreener (https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/KUSUMBEN-HASMUKHBHAI-CHUDGAR-A1GFYC). Family is now run by Hasmukh Chudgar's sons (Urmish MD, Nimish co-MD, Binish). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source. Only general company contact available.

name: Zhu Yuguo
current_role: Founder of Shandong Changxing Group (山东长星集团), papermaking-machinery and wind-equipment maker (current title unverified)
profile: Zhu Yuguo (朱玉国) founded Shandong Changxing Group in 1986; it became China's largest maker of vacuum couch rolls, a key part of paper machines. Around 2006-08 he pushed into wind power, announcing a RMB5.5bn plan with Shaanxi University of Science & Technology to build 1-3MW turbines (1,000 sets/yr). Forbes China ranked him No.102 in 2006 (RMB5.71bn).
interesting_fact: He planned to both build and operate turbines - up to 100 x 50MW wind farms over 5-10 years - arguing that owning the whole chain could cut a wind farm's payback to about three years.
deep_cut_fact: His case for wind was blunt: coal will run out one day, so new energy is the long bet - he said this while still running one of China's top paper-machinery component businesses.
notes: Little coverage since ~2008; no recent news, filings or official website found for Changxing or Zhu. Unlisted. Tried Chinese searches (朱玉国 长星/真空伏辊/风电) - only the dialogue.earth (China Dialogue) feature confirms the link.

name: Zhou Jinming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Sino Geophysical Co., Ltd. (潜能恒信, SZSE: 300191), Beijing
profile: Zhou Jinming (周锦明, ~61) is a geophysicist who founded Sino Geophysical in 2003, now listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext. The company began in seismic data processing/interpretation services and now also holds oil & gas exploration and development rights, e.g. Bohai blocks 05/31 and 09/17, where it works with CNOOC. He remains controlling shareholder (~131.7m shares).
