current_role: Actual controller of Shanghai Hanbell Precise Machinery (SZSE: 002158) via Taiwan's Hanbell Investment Holding; chairman 1994-2011, director 2011-2020
profile: Liao Zhenan (廖哲男, Liao Che-nan), from Taiwan, founded the mainland arm of Hanbell, which makes screw and centrifugal compressors for refrigeration, HVAC, heat pumps and vacuum pumps. He chaired Shanghai Hanbell from 1994 to 2011 and was a director until 2020. He still controls it via Hanbell Investment Holding (Taiwan), which holds 23.12%.
interesting_fact: Hanbell's 2025 annual report calls it a core equipment supplier for liquid cooling in Chinese AI data centres (AIDC). It leads domestic production of oil-free magnetic-levitation centrifugal compressors (RTM series), a direct tie to an energy and data-centre podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired Shanghai Hanbell for 17 years (1994-2011), then served as a director until 2020; he controls it through a chain running from Hanbell Investment Holding (Taiwan) via BVI and Panamanian holding companies.
notes: Taiwanese national, listed under China by Hurun. No longer on the Shanghai Hanbell board; the Taiwan parent (Hanbell Precise Machinery, Taoyuan) may be a better route. Romanised name may appear as Liao Che-Nan.

name: Xu Ligang
current_role: Co-founder, co-controlling shareholder, Director & General Manager, Jiangsu X-chip Semiconductor (展芯股份, SZSE ChiNext: 301707), Nanjing
profile: Xu Ligang (徐立刚, mid-40s) holds a PhD in power electronics from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics and co-founded Nanjing-based X-chip in 2018 with fellow NUAA alumnus Wen Zhenlin. X-chip designs high-reliability analog power-management chips and DC/DC micro-modules; it listed on ChiNext on 7 Aug 2026 and surged ~360% on debut.
interesting_fact: X-chip's IPO priced at 23.45 yuan and opened 360% higher on day one (peaking near 129.90 yuan), making Xu and co-founder Wen Zhenlin newly minted chip billionaires in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding X-chip he worked as an engineer at Shenzhen Qingxuan Electronics and at Silergy's Hangzhou arm, then ran the Zhuzhou Zhanxin business unit; X-chip's leadership and independent directors are largely fellow NUAA power-electronics alumni.
notes: Hurun 'X-Chip' = 江苏展芯半导体 (Zhanxin). Chairman is co-founder Wen Zhenlin; Xu is GM. Company focuses on military/high-reliability power chips, so expect low media appetite. Route via IR email.

name: Xie Shuli
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shanghai YCT Electronics Group (Yachuang Dianzi, SZSE: 301099)
profile: Xie Shuli (b. 1972), a Tongji University chemistry graduate, built Shanghai YCT Electronics from a component trading firm (run as GM from 2001) into a listed authorised distributor of electronic components, largely for automotive customers, which now also designs its own analog and mixed-signal chips (power management, drivers, automotive CIS). He controls about 52% of the company.
interesting_fact: YCT has moved up the value chain from pure distribution into in-house chip design (power-management, signal-chain and mixed-signal SoCs), alongside distributing memory, MCUs and passives.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating in chemistry from Tongji University in 1996, his first job was as a sales manager at Shantou Ultrasonic printed-circuit-board company (1996-99), before he became a director of Hong Kong Taixin and later GM of Shanghai YCT.
notes: Hurun's 'YCL' appears to be YCT (Shanghai Yct Electronics, 雅创电子); name and Chinese characters match the chairman/controller. Board secretary/CFO: Fan Xiaolei. Web search budget ran out; bio from exchange-disclosed data.

name: Wu Hehong
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Xinrui' (China). Not researched: the lane's web-search quota ran out before this person was reached, and direct fetches of likely company sites returned nothing usable.
notes: Needs a follow-up pass. Search the Chinese name plus the company (Xinrui) on the exchange filings (SSE/SZSE/HKEXnews) to confirm identity, role and the company's IR email.

name: Wang Zhangxing
current_role: Chairman, Shanghai Jiashijia Holding (Group) Co. (per a dated profile; current status unverified)
profile: Wang Zhangxing, from Shaoxing, Zhejiang, started in construction contracting and in January 2001 founded Shanghai Jiashijia Holding. The private group centres on self-operated commercial property (building-materials and home-furnishing malls, department stores, hotels) and expanded into developments in Beijing, Zhengzhou, Chengdu and Urumqi in the mid-2000s.
interesting_fact: He was ranked in the Hurun Rich List top 50 in 2005, and has appeared on Hurun China lists from 2005 through 2026.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999 he bought a former pharmaceutical warehouse on Shanghai's Yishan Road for RMB 36m to build housing. When a tenant offered RMB 10m a year in rent, he turned it into the Jiashijia building-materials mall, which grew from 15,000 to 60,000 sq m.
notes: The list's 'City' source of wealth is assumed to refer to Jiashijia's mall/'city' business, so the match is probable but not certain. The profile dates from about 2005-06. He has been president of the Shaoxing Enterprises Association in Shanghai. No published contacts found; private group.

name: Wan Zhang
current_role: Co-founder and co-controlling shareholder (~11%), Shanghai Friendess Electronic Technology (Bochu, 688188.SH)
profile: Wan Zhang (万章) is one of five co-founders of Shanghai Friendess (柏楚电子), a spin-out of Shanghai Jiao Tong University founded in 2007 that dominates China's market for fiber-laser cutting CNC control systems. The company listed on the STAR Market in 2019; the five founders jointly control it, with Wan holding about 11%.
interesting_fact: Friendess began as a student startup next to Shanghai Jiao Tong University, backed by the Shanghai university-student entrepreneurship fund, and its laser-cutting controllers became the market leader in China.
deep_cut_fact: When the company was registered on 11 Sept 2007 with 200,000 yuan of capital (half pledged by SJTU's technology-transfer center), Wan Zhang and three of the co-founders each put in just 10,000 yuan.
notes: Very low profile; could not confirm his current executive title. Chairman/public face is Tang Ye. Route via company board secretary (Zhou Zhiyu).

name: Su Jianguo
current_role: Founder and actual controller, Jiangsu Leili Motor Co. (SZSE: 300660), Changzhou; son Su Da is general manager and legal representative
profile: Su Jianguo (b. c.1955) founded Changzhou-based Leili in 1993, when China's micro-motor industry was in its infancy, and built it into a major maker of motors for air conditioners and appliances (listed in Shenzhen 2017). Now run day-to-day by his son Su Da, Leili has diversified into EV motors, medical micro-motors (Dingzhi Technology) and robot components such as hollow-cup motors and dexterous hands.
interesting_fact: Before its 2017 IPO nearly 90% of Leili's revenue came from home-appliance motors; it has since opened a Vietnam plant (2019) and started mass-producing hollow-cup motors for robots in 2024, with a subsidiary (Zhongke Lingxi) building dexterous robot hands.
deep_cut_fact: Leili's first product was an air-conditioner motor, developed by an early technical team drawn largely from an established state-owned enterprise in Changzhou.
notes: Hurun pairs him with son Su Da, who now fronts the company and gives interviews (e.g. The Paper, July 2026) - Su Da is the better outreach target. A team-profile page (pitchhub.36kr.com) says Su started in 1979 as a salesman at Wujin No.3 Electronic Components Factory; verify against prospectus.

name: Su Da
current_role: General Manager, Jiangsu Leili Motor Co. (江苏雷利, SZSE: 300660)
profile: Su Da (苏达) runs Changzhou-based Jiangsu Leili Motor, the micro-motor maker his father Su Jianguo founded in 1993; its first product was an air-conditioner motor. He has steered Leili from ~90% home-appliance revenue (pre-2017 IPO) into EV motors, medical micro-motors (via Dingzhi Tech) and now robotics/embodied-AI components such as coreless motors and dexterous hands.
interesting_fact: Roughly one in three air conditioners and one in five washing machines worldwide uses a Leili motor. Its high-end motors now reach 100,000 rpm.
deep_cut_fact: Leili controls Anhui Zhongke Lingxi, a USTC-incubated dexterous-robot-hand maker. Su splits embodied-AI commercialisation into three tiers: service, then industrial/commercial, then elder care. He predicts service robots scale first and end up with an EV-like market structure (Paper, July 2026).
notes: Emails are for the board secretary (Yin Chenglong) and the securities representative, as published in Leili's reports. Su speaks to media ('Vibrant China' tour 2026), so he is relatively accessible. Good robotics/electrification angle. Listing shared with Su Jianguo.

name: Pu Yilong
current_role: Chairman and general manager, Jiangsu Longda Superalloy Co. (隆达股份, SSE STAR: 688231), Wuxi; also acting board secretary
profile: Pu Yilong (浦益龙, b. Feb 1961) turned a Wuxi copper-tube factory he ran from 1994 into Jiangsu Longda Superalloy, a STAR Market-listed maker of cast and wrought high-temperature alloys for aero-engines and gas turbines. He has been chairman/GM since 2004 and is a Jiangsu provincial people's congress deputy.
interesting_fact: Longda's superalloys go into aircraft engines and gas turbines — the same turbine supply chain now in demand for on-site data-center power generation.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in July 1978, aged 17, at the Houqiao construction company in Xishan, rising to engineering-team manager before taking over the Wuxi Longda copper-tube factory in 1994.
notes: Gas-turbine/superalloy angle fits an energy/data-center podcast. He is personally acting as board secretary (2026), so the IR mailbox may reach his office. Source is Longda's 2025 annual report.

name: Ou Xinhua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shanghai Prisemi Electronics (芯导科技, STAR Market: 688230)
profile: Engineer-founder who set up Shanghai Prisemi in Nov 2009, a fabless designer of power semiconductors (TVS/ESD protection devices, MOSFETs, Schottky diodes, power-management ICs) for consumer electronics, with Xiaomi among its major customers. He controlled 100% of the company before its 2021 STAR Market listing and was re-elected chairman in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: Prisemi was his first startup, and he kept 100% control of it right up to its STAR Market IPO filing, with no outside VC shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Prisemi he was an R&D engineer and project manager at Shanghai Guangyu Ruixin Microelectronics and then technical director at Suzhou Jingxun Technology.
notes: Low public profile with no interviews found. Prisemi does power and protection chips, mainly for phones and consumer devices, so the data-center link is indirect.

name: Jing Shiping
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Suzhou Hengmingda Electronic Technology Co. (SZSE: 002947)
profile: Jing Shiping (b. 1969) built Hengmingda from a Shenzhen packaging-printing shop into a Kunshan-based maker of precision flexible and metal structural parts for smartphones, tablets, laptops and VR/AR devices. He has chaired the listed company since 2017 and controls it with family members; it now also supplies metal structures for EV chargers, energy storage and PV inverters.
interesting_fact: Hengmingda has moved beyond consumer electronics into new energy, supplying precision metal structural parts for charging piles, battery-swap cabinets, home and C&I energy-storage systems and PV inverters to leading Chinese new-energy firms.
deep_cut_fact: Jing started out at Hong Kong's Dasheng company and the Hengmingda packaging & printing plant in Bao'an, Shenzhen, and ran Kunshan Hengmingda Packaging Materials from 1999 before pivoting the business into electronics components; he holds an MBA.
notes: Family-controlled (Jing Shiping, Jing Tianping, Jing Jingping, Xia Chen, Jing Jiang); Jing Tianping is legal rep/GM. Energy-storage component angle fits the podcast. Route via securities affairs office email.

name: Zhang Rongming
current_role: Founder, chairman and general manager, Aimer Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603511)
profile: Zhang Rongming founded Beijing lingerie group Aimer, one of China's leading premium intimate-apparel brands (Aimer, Aimer Men, Aimer Kids and others). He started in 1992-93 by taking over a failing Beijing garment factory. Aimer listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in 2021, and he remains controlling shareholder, chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Aimer's first bra, launched in 1993, sold for RMB49 when average monthly urban wages were around RMB190. From the start he aimed to match international brands on quality, and he borrowed RMB800k from friends because banks would not lend without collateral.
deep_cut_fact: He was a materials scientist teaching at the Beijing Steel and Iron Institute (now USTB) when he heard shape-memory alloy could be used in bras. In 1991 he developed a 'super-elastic memory-alloy bra underwire', which he used as his technology stake to take over Huamei Garment Factory.
notes: Gives occasional long-form interviews (36Kr, SCMP 2026 profile). The materials-science and 'hard tech for the softest product' story is a natural entrepreneurship hook. Route requests through Aimer's securities/IR office.

name: Xu Bing
current_role: General manager of Guangzhou Zhanxin Communication Technology; co-actual controller (with Huang Shaoxiong) of Beijing Compass Technology (SZSE ChiNext: 300803)
profile: Xu Bing (徐兵) and Huang Shaoxiong control Compass Technology (指南针) through holding company Guangzhou Zhanxin. Compass is a Beijing-based retail stock-analysis software and fintech firm that listed on ChiNext in 2019 and has since moved into brokerage (Mega/麦高 Securities) and fund management. Xu has run Guangzhou Zhanxin since 2010.
interesting_fact: Compass grew from selling stock-analysis software to retail investors into a licensed financial group by acquiring a securities brokerage and a fund manager, using a software customer base to build a broker.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, Xu served 1984-1997 in the Guangzhou Military Region Air Force logistics department, then worked 1997-2008 at Guangzhou Nanhu Golf Club (assistant GM, later director), according to Compass's annual report.
notes: Low profile and not an executive of the listed company. He holds a Hong Kong (non-permanent) resident ID. Not to be confused with SenseTime co-founder Xu Bing (徐冰). The route is via the Compass securities office.

name: Wang Zhongshan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, Mokingran Jewellery Group (梦金园黄金珠宝集团, HKEX: 2585)
profile: Wang Zhongshan (王忠善, aged ~62), founded Tianjin-based gold-jewellery maker and retailer Mokingran in 2000 after starting as an apprentice gemstone setter in the 1990s. The company listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024; he holds ~23.7% directly and, with his family, controls ~60%. Rising gold prices lifted the stake into Hurun's China list in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2018 he was named an official inheritor of Shandong Province intangible cultural heritage for gold-jewellery craftsmanship, and was honoured for 'outstanding contribution to the jewellery industry' on the 40th anniversary of reform and opening up.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Mokingran he worked as an apprentice doing gemstone inlay and processing in the 1990s, and in January 2013 was recognised as Weifang's 'First Folk Art Master' (首届民间工艺大师).
notes: Family business: wife is an executive director and son is general manager. Route via IR email in the 2025 annual report.

name: Qiao Yuhua
current_role: Actual controller and director, Inner Mongolia Shuangxin Environment-Friendly Material (001369.SZ, listed Dec 2025); chairman, Shuangxin Resources
profile: Born 1966, an accountant by training who rose from cement/iron plant bookkeeper in Qipanjing (Otog Banner, Ordos) to found the Shuangxin chemical group in 2000. Shuangxin turns calcium carbide into polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) and derivatives used in construction, paper, fibres, PVB film and water-soluble film; he controls ~62% of the voting rights of the SZSE-listed unit.
interesting_fact: Shuangxin listed on the Shenzhen main board in late 2025 and is using IPO funds to move downstream from PVA into PVB (laminated-glass interlayer) and VAE emulsion products.
deep_cut_fact: His first job (1986) was at the Qipanjing cement & iron plant; he then worked four years at the ICBC Qipanjing office in Otog Banner before returning to the plant as finance chief - he holds an accounting degree from the Central Institute of Finance and is a senior engineer.
notes: Energy-intensive coal-chemical business in Ordos (carbide, captive power) - relevant to energy angle. Low media profile; route via board office of Shuangxin Materials.

name: Li Yi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, 51WORLD (Beijing 51World Digital Twin Technology; HKEX-listed)
profile: Li Yi (Archer Li) founded 51WORLD in Beijing in 2015, evolving it from a VR startup into a digital-twin and simulation platform used for autonomous-driving testing, transport hubs, smart factories, water management and energy. Backed by Sky9 Capital from its Series A, 51WORLD listed on the HKEX main board; he now pitches it as a data engine for embodied AI and robotics.
interesting_fact: His stated goal is to build a 'Digital Twin Earth' - a complete virtual replica of the world - by 2030; 51WORLD's simulation platform serves nearly a hundred intelligent-driving customers.
deep_cut_fact: On investor Sky9 Capital's founder page he lists as his favorite quote: 'Pessimists are always right but optimists are more likely to succeed.'
notes: Goes by 'Archer Li' in English. aes@51aes.com is 51WORLD's published customer-service email (no dedicated press address found). Data-center/energy angle: digital twins for energy sites and factories; recent focus on robotics training data.

name: Chen Jifeng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Beijing Worldia Diamond Tools (沃尔德, SH:688028)
profile: Chen Jifeng (b. 1968), a USTC plasma-physics graduate and professor-level senior engineer, built Beijing Worldia into a maker of ultra-precision superhard (diamond/CBN) cutting tools, listed on the STAR Market in 2019. He controls about a third of the company and is pushing it into CVD diamond functional materials such as heat sinks, optical windows and acoustic parts.
interesting_fact: Worldia now sells CVD diamond heat-sink materials and diamond optical windows — diamond's extreme thermal conductivity makes it a candidate for cooling high-power chips, a theme relevant to AI/data-center hardware.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from USTC's Department of Modern Physics (plasma physics) he spent 1992-2000 as an engineer at the State Building Materials Bureau's Synthetic Crystals Research Institute, then ran Beijing Xiboer (2000-10) before building Worldia.
notes: Technical founder in a data-center-adjacent niche (diamond thermal materials) — good podcast angle. Co-actual controller listed as Yang Nuo. Company hotline 400-766-9898 published; board secretary is Chen Huanchao.

name: Yang Nuo
current_role: Individual shareholder (about 1%) of Beijing Worldia Diamond Tools Co., Ltd. (沃尔德, SSE STAR: 688028); Hurun lists her wealth jointly with chairman Chen Jifeng
profile: Hurun lists Yang Nuo with Chen Jifeng for Worldia, a Beijing-headquartered maker of ultra-precision diamond and superhard cutting tools listed on the STAR Market. Chen (b. 1968) is chairman, general manager and controlling shareholder with about 33.5%; Yang Nuo held about 0.98% as of March 2026. Their relationship is not stated in the filings found; she is likely a family member.
interesting_fact: Worldia started in 2006 as a small Beijing company with registered capital of just RMB 500,000 and grew into a listed specialist in ultra-precision and high-precision superhard cutting tools and superhard materials.
notes: Very low profile and no biography found; the shareholding is from https://quote.cfi.cn/gdtj/93382/688028.html . Chen Jifeng is the public face, and the company securities office (board secretary 陈焕超) is the only route.

name: Cai Baogui
current_role: Chairman, JL MAG Rare-Earth Co. (金力永磁, 300748.SZ / 6680.HK); co-actual controller
profile: Cai Baogui (蔡报贵, b. 1971) founded Ganzhou-based JL MAG Rare-Earth in 2008, building it into the world's No.1 producer of high-performance NdFeB permanent magnets by output and sales in 2024. Its magnets go into EV motors, inverter air-conditioners, wind turbines, robots and humanoid robotics; the company is listed in Shenzhen and Hong Kong and he remains chairman and co-controller.
interesting_fact: JL MAG became the world's largest rare-earth permanent magnet maker by production and sales in 2024; wind power and EVs are core markets, and it is expanding into humanoid-robot motors.
deep_cut_fact: A 1993 fine-chemicals graduate of Nanchang University, he first taught at the university (1993-94), then spent eight years as a production manager at a Dongguan plastics factory before running his own plastics-electronics plant; since 2008 he has also chaired Lide Wind Power (Jiangxi). He earned a Tsinghua EMBA in 2022.
notes: Strong energy fit: rare-earth magnets for wind turbines and EVs, plus his own wind-power company (Lide Wind Power). Chaired JL MAG board meetings through Aug 2026. Co-controllers with Li Xinnong and Hu Zhibin.

name: Ao Fengting
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Inner Mongolia Mengtai Group (coal, power, aluminium; Ordos)
profile: Inner Mongolia entrepreneur who founded Mengtai Group (formerly Ordos Mengtai Coal & Power), an integrated coal, power and aluminium producer in Ordos. He has been on the Hurun list every year since 2010 (9th in Inner Mongolia in 2024, RMB 5.3bn) and reportedly is a vice-president of the China Ethnic Trade Promotion Association.
interesting_fact: Mengtai follows the classic Inner Mongolia 'coal-power-aluminium' integration model, using its own mine-mouth coal power to run energy-intensive aluminium smelting.
notes: Very low profile with minimal public information; the biography above comes from a Hurun-derived list (maigoo.com/news/725273.html). I could not reach a company website or published contact. Identity is matched by name and company only.

name: Zhang Zhimin
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen T&S Communications (太辰光, SZSE: 300570)
profile: Born 1951, Zhang Zhimin has chaired Shenzhen-based T&S Communications since December 2000. T&S makes passive optical components, notably high-density MTP/MPO fibre connectors and fibre flex circuits used in hyperscale data centres, and its value has surged with AI computing build-outs; he shares the Hurun listing with his wife Cai Bo.
interesting_fact: T&S's high-density MTP/MPO fibre connectors are widely used in large data centres worldwide, making it a direct beneficiary of the AI data-center boom.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1984 as an interpreter and later head of sales at China-Japan (Shenzhen) Leasing, one of Shenzhen's early Sino-foreign ventures, before he ran Shenzhen Zhonghe Optical and moved into fibre optics.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center podcast (optical interconnect supplier). His board term ran to Sept 2026 per the 2025 annual report; confirm re-election.

name: Cai Bo
current_role: Board Secretary and Overseas Market Department Manager, Shenzhen T&S Communications (太辰光, SZ:300570)
profile: Cai Bo (蔡波, b. 1972) is a long-time executive and member of the controlling shareholder group of Shenzhen T&S Communications, a maker of passive optical interconnect components (ceramic ferrules, MT ferrules, high-density MPO connectivity) used in hyperscale and AI data centers and telecom networks. She joined in 2000 as overseas sales manager and has been board secretary since 2011; her wealth is shared with chairman Zhang Zhimin, her husband.
interesting_fact: T&S's high-density optical connectivity products sell globally into large data centers; its 2025 annual report ties growth to the AI compute build-out and new technologies such as silicon photonics and CPO, a direct link to the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: An English major, Cai taught at a school affiliated with China Zhenhua Group from 1992 to 2000 before joining T&S in December 2000 as its overseas sales manager, building the export business that now dominates its revenue.
notes: As board secretary she personally runs the IR channel, so zqb@china-tscom.com reaches her office directly. English-speaking; strong data-center/optical-interconnect angle.

name: Wen Hongfu
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and CTO, Guangdong Omat Advanced Materials Co., Ltd. (Shanghai STAR: 688530)
profile: Wen Hongfu (aged ~61) is the founder and co-controlling shareholder (with Fang Hong and Wen Ya) of Omat (欧莱新材), a maker of high-performance sputtering targets for flat-panel displays, integrated circuits and solar. Omat listed on the STAR Market in May 2024. He also runs its subsidiaries making high-purity metals and indium products.
interesting_fact: Omat's shares opened 176% above their 9.60-yuan offer price on their STAR Market debut on 9 May 2024. Sputtering targets are a key material in semiconductor and display fabs, a supply chain China has been trying to localise.
deep_cut_fact: Before he became an entrepreneur, Wen was a university teacher at Anhui Institute of Technology (formerly Huainan Mining Institute). He then worked at China National Metals & Minerals Import & Export's Shenzhen trading arm and was assistant GM of Guangdong Metallurgical Shenzhen Import & Export Co.
notes: The Hurun source name 'Omat' is Guangdong Omat Advanced Materials (欧莱新材). He is also the CTO, so the company is a semiconductor-materials angle that may suit the podcast.

name: Liang Meizhen
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (acting in concert with Yu Zhong and Zuo Guojun) of Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology (捷佳伟创, 300724.SZ)
profile: One of three actual controllers of S.C New Energy, a Shenzhen solar-equipment maker founded in 2003 that builds PECVD, diffusion, texturing/etching and automation tools for crystalline-silicon PV cell lines; it listed on ChiNext in 2018. She directly holds about 7% and controls about 11% of voting rights (incl. shares held by her son), per 2025 filings. No executive role found.
interesting_fact: 'SC' in the Hurun listing is S.C New Energy (捷佳伟创), one of China's main suppliers of solar-cell manufacturing equipment, whose PECVD tools deposit anti-reflective and passivation layers on PV cells.
notes: Identity inferred from Hurun 'SC' + green energy and confirmed by S.C New Energy filings naming 梁美珍 as co-actual controller. Appears to be a passive shareholder with no public profile; better interview targets are chairman Zuo Guojun or CEO Yu Zhong.

name: Hu Yuhang
current_role: Vice Chairman, 37 Interactive Entertainment (三七互娱, SZSE 002555); long-time President of 37 Games (R&D arm)
profile: Hu Yuhang (胡宇航, b. 1976) is a co-founder of 37 Interactive Entertainment, one of China's biggest mobile/web game publishers (titles such as 'Puzzles & Survival' and 'Douluo Dalu' games). He has run its R&D brand 37 Games since 2013. His stake rose to 7% in 2020, and he was re-elected to the board in 2025 as vice chairman.
interesting_fact: He is the developer-side co-founder, leading 37 Games' studios while the group grew into one of China's top game exporters. In 2019 he was named a 'Craftsman Spirit Figure of the Game Industry' (游戏行业匠心精神人物).
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Lanzhou University in China's northwest, far from 37's Guangzhou base, and later took an EMBA at Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (CKGSB).
notes: He is low profile in English-language media. In December 2025 regulators (CSRC/SZSE) penalised several 37 Interactive directors, including him, over a 2018 related-party disclosure (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202512051794542444_1.pdf); avoid that topic. Best route is 37 Interactive IR or the board secretary (Wang Sijie).

name: Hu Xinrong
current_role: Chairman, legal representative and core technical staff, Shenzhen Xinyichang Technology (Hoson, SSE STAR: 688383)
profile: Shenzhen engineer who co-founded Xinyichang with Song Changning in 2006; the two are its controlling shareholders. Starting with capacitor aging-test machines, the company became a leading Chinese maker of LED (incl. Mini LED) die bonders and expanded into semiconductor die-attach and lithium-battery equipment. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in April 2021.
interesting_fact: Xinyichang began in 2006 making aluminium electrolytic capacitor aging-test machines, then used that know-how to break into LED die bonders, and later developed six-head high-speed die bonders for Mini LED and chip-packaging die bonders for semiconductors.
deep_cut_fact: He worked his way up from the shop floor: a technician at Shenzhen Huachang Electronics, then technician and equipment supervisor at Shenzhen Datong, before running two small Bao'an workshops (Hengchang machining plant and Yichang electronics factory) that preceded Xinyichang.
notes: Hurun's 'Xinyichang' = 新益昌 (Hoson). Low media profile; route via board secretary Liu Xiaohuan's office (hoson@szhech.com, listed in 2024 interim report). Chinese-language outreach advised.

name: Hsin Chung-Herng
current_role: Chairman, Taiwan Union Technology Corp. (TUC, 台燿科技, TPEx: 6274)
profile: Hsin Chung-Herng (辛忠衡; the input's 辛忠卫 appears to be a typo) chairs Taiwan Union Technology, a Taiwanese maker of copper-clad laminates and prepregs for printed circuit boards. Demand for its high-speed, low-loss laminates in AI servers and data-center switches has driven a surge in its share price, putting him on the Hurun list in 2026.
interesting_fact: TUC began in 1974 as Taiwan Union Glass, an optical-glass maker, and only switched to copper-clad laminates in 1997; its 'ThunderClad' low-loss materials are now used in AI server and high-speed networking boards.
notes: Strong AI/data-center supply-chain angle. Very low public profile; no interviews found. Company spokesperson listed as Huang Wen-hsu (黄文旭) per TechNews company data (https://info.technews.tw/company/04226091-台燿科技股份有限公司); TUC held a 2026 AGM with director elections, so confirm chair post-AGM.

name: Cherry Wang
current_role: Formosa Plastics heir; long-time executive in the Chang Gung Memorial Hospital system (current title not confirmed)
profile: Cherry Wang (王瑞慧) is the third daughter of Formosa Plastics founder Wang Yung-ching. interesting_fact: Invus has no fund life or forced exit timetable: its capital comes solely from Artal, and the modest initial pool from 1985 has compounded to over $10bn even after distributing billions to Artal shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he trained as a food scientist: a BS in agricultural sciences and agricultural engineering from the American University of Beirut and an MS in Food Science and Technology from UC Davis (then a Stanford MBA). He chairs Action Against Hunger USA.

name: Gu Shaofeng
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Innovation Officer, FinVolution Group (信也科技, NYSE: FINV)
profile: Gu Shaofeng, a Shanghai Jiao Tong University graduate and ex-Microsoft technical lead, co-founded Paipaidai in 2007 — China's first online P2P lending platform — and was its CEO, CTO and strategy chief before it became FinVolution, a NYSE-listed fintech operating credit platforms in China, Indonesia and the Philippines. He has chaired the board since 2020 and is its largest shareholder.
interesting_fact: Paipaidai, which he co-founded with Zhang Jun and Hu Honghui, was China's first P2P lending platform and listed on the NYSE in 2017 before rebranding as FinVolution.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he founded Podlook (菠萝网, 2006), which grew to one of China's largest podcast aggregators with ~26,000 channels on under RMB100k of startup capital; he worked unpaid, saying 'many on this team don't take salaries — like me.' A natural hook for a podcast pitch.
notes: Podcast-founder background (Podlook) makes him an unusually good fit. IR contacts from a 2023 6-K exhibit; verify against latest earnings release. Official bio page: finvolution.gcs-web.com.

name: Gu Zhengqing
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology (世华科技, SSE STAR: 688093); stepped down as general manager in July 2026
profile: Gu Zhengqing, born in the 1980s, founded Suzhou Shihua in 2010 at age 27 to make functional composite materials (adhesive, conductive and shielding coatings on PET/PI films) for consumer electronics. Small customised parts won it a place in Apple's supply chain, and it listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020. He and his wife Kuai Lili control it through Yefuyou Investment.
interesting_fact: Shihua got into Apple's supply chain by taking the small, high-spec custom parts that larger foreign suppliers found too low-volume to bother with; it grew from one or two Apple parts to more than 100 certified ones.
deep_cut_fact: Shortly before Spring Festival, while driving home, he got the call that Shihua's material would go into the iPad. He dropped off his family and drove straight back to Suzhou without eating; the plant ran until New Year's Eve 2011 and restarted on the third day of the holiday. He calls this the company's 'first pot of gold'.
notes: Hurun calls the company 'Shihua' and lists him with his wife Kuai Lili. He says 'entrepreneurship is forced on you' (创业都是逼出来的), which suits a founder-story podcast. Board secretary per cninfo: 计毓雯. GM resignation reported at https://www.caiwennews.com/article/1527702.shtml

name: Kuai Lili
current_role: Director and co-actual controller (with husband Gu Zhengqing) of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology (世华科技, 688093.SH)
profile: Kuai Lili (蒯丽丽, b. 1985) is a director and, since 2026, one of only two actual controllers of Suzhou Shihua New Material Technology, a STAR Market-listed maker of functional electronic materials and high-performance optical films used in consumer electronics. She co-owns holding company Yefuyou Investment (40%) with her husband, chairman Gu Zhengqing (60%).
interesting_fact: In 2026 the founders' five-person concert-party agreement was dissolved, leaving Kuai Lili and Gu Zhengqing as Shihua's sole actual controllers; she appeared on Hurun's China Under-40 self-made list in 2021.
notes: Low public profile; husband Gu Zhengqing (chairman) is the public face. Spouse relationship and 40% Yefuyou stake per 2025 prospectus (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-08-29/1224607144.PDF). Shihua is a 'little giant' specialised SME; no personal channels found.

name: Ke Longtu
current_role: Shareholder (12.5% of Keboda Holdings) and party acting in concert with the controllers of Keboda Technology (科博达, SSE: 603786)
profile: Ke Longtu is the daughter of Keboda co-controller Ke Binghua and holds 12.5% of Keboda Holdings, the parent of Shanghai-listed automotive electronics maker Keboda Technology (lighting control, motor control and EV electronics for VW, Audi and others). notes: Next-generation family shareholder with no public profile; wealth shared with father Ke Binghua. Better outreach target is chairman Ke Guihua via Keboda's board office.

name: Li Guoping
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Jiangsu Tongli Tianqi Technology (同力天启, SH:605286; formerly Tongli Risheng 同力日升)
profile: Li Guoping (李国平) founded Danyang-based Tongli Risheng, a leading maker of elevator and escalator components (guide rails, structural parts) supplying global brands such as Schindler and Otis; it listed in Shanghai in 2021. He has since steered it into new energy by taking control of Beijing Tianqi Hongyuan, an energy-storage system integrator, and the company was renamed Tongli Tianqi.
interesting_fact: The elevator-parts company now builds containerised battery energy-storage systems: its Tianqi Hongyuan unit's team has worked on over 3 GWh of storage projects and was named a 2025 'best energy storage system integrator', a strong energy-podcast angle.
deep_cut_fact: Li began in 1980 as a machine operator and cashier at a rubber-thread factory in Daoshu, Danyang, then spent 1985-2001 at the Daoshu Shenyang elevator-decoration factory rising from salesman to sales chief, sales manager and deputy factory head before running his own firm, Danyang Risheng, from 2001.
notes: Self-made from the factory floor; very relevant pivot from elevators to grid-scale energy storage. Best route: board secretary Liu Liang via zqb@jstljx.com.

name: Yam Yu
current_role: Controlling shareholder (~59%) of International Business Settlement Holdings Ltd (HKEX: 0147) via his wholly owned Long Grand Limited
profile: Yam Yu (任宇) controls Hong Kong-listed International Business Settlement Holdings (formerly Chaoyue Group). He owns 12.89bn shares (55.79%) through BVI vehicle Long Grand Ltd, plus 750m shares bought directly in March 2026. IBS runs supercomputing servers for Bitcoin mining and cloud mining, and began IC-chip trading in December 2025.
interesting_fact: In November 2025, IBS bought 1 EH/s of cloud-mining hashrate for a year from a subsidiary of Nasdaq-listed Bitdeer, paying about US$15m in Bitcoin. It mined about 117.5 BTC in FY2026 and held 234 BTC at 31 March 2026.
notes: He is not a director; the board is led by executive directors Yuen Leong, Chan Siu Tat and Lou Ming. The company's published office line is +852 2549 9988 (Causeway Bay). Recent news reports a proposed HK$563m acquisition of an AI-chip business. The data-centre/compute and Bitcoin-mining angle fits the podcast. Little personal information is public.

name: Wang Yaolin
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, InventisBio (益方生物, SSE STAR 688382), Shanghai
profile: Yaolin Wang (王耀林, b. 1963), a US-trained pharmacologist, spent 18 years as a drug-discovery scientist at Schering-Plough and Merck. In 2015 he left to build InventisBio in Shanghai with other returnee PhDs. The company developed the targeted cancer drugs befotertinib (EGFR) and garsorasib (KRAS G12C), both out-licensed, and listed on the STAR Market in July 2022.
interesting_fact: InventisBio's KRAS G12C inhibitor garsorasib (格索雷塞) targets a cancer mutation long considered 'undruggable'. It reached approval in China, putting this ex-Merck lab scientist's startup among the few groups with a drug against that target.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his pharmacology PhD at SUNY Stony Brook and did postdoctoral research at Baylor College of Medicine in 1992-97. He then worked as a principal scientist at Schering-Plough (1997-2009) and Merck (2009-15), and only founded his company at 52.
notes: He is a US citizen with Chinese permanent residency and comfortable in English, having spent 20+ years in US pharma. Co-controllers are Jiang Yueheng (board secretary) and Dai Xing. Best route is ir@inventisbio.com. A 2019 Endpoints News article covers his decision to leave Merck (https://endpts.com/?p=60394).

name: Yan Deping
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Hefei Hengxin Life Science & Technology (恒鑫生活, SZSE ChiNext: 301501)
profile: Yan Deping (严德平) left a teaching job in 1997 to start a small commercial print shop in Hefei, then pivoted around 2000 into paper cups and later biodegradable (PLA) food-service ware. Hengxin now supplies cups and packaging to tea and coffee chains such as Luckin and Mixue, and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Hengxin is a national 'little giant' specialist in biodegradable tableware, with annual capacity of around 9 billion cups and containers serving China's booming tea-and-coffee chains.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 11 years as a teacher at Hefei Forestry Vocational & Technical School; at 34 he started 'Hengxin Printing' with second-hand presses, doing design, printing and sales himself, and the paper know-how led him into paper cups.
notes: Hurun lists the company as 'HXIN'. Co-founded with spouse Fan Yanru. Company holds online investor Q&A sessions (e.g. 15 May 2026).

name: Yu Lanjun
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (19.66%) of Tonghua Golden-Horse Pharmaceutical (通化金马, SZSE: 000766); deputy GM of Liaoning Lingyuan Gangda Group Industrial
profile: Yu Lanjun (于兰军), a Liaoning businessman, is deputy GM of Liaoning Lingyuan Gangda Group Industrial and runs Shenyang Jinhaoxin Trading and Shenyang Zhongtuan Technology. In 2022 he became the largest shareholder and actual controller of Jilin-based TCM drugmaker Tonghua Golden-Horse, where he holds 190m shares (19.66%); he holds no executive post there.
interesting_fact: He became Tonghua Golden-Horse's controller in 2022 when a Chengdu court awarded him 80m shares owed by the previous controller, Beijing Jinshang Alliance, which then formally agreed to his taking control.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews or biography found. Day-to-day leadership at Tonghua Golden-Horse is chairman/GM Zhang Yufu. Part of his stake is pledged. The IR email belongs to the company, not to him.

name: Tang Zhuolin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Dongfang Precision Science & Technology (SZSE: 002611), Foshan
profile: Tang Zhuolin (唐灼林, 'Victor Tang', b.1963) founded Dongfang Precision in Foshan in 1996, growing it from a workshop making printing/packaging machinery into a leading corrugated-box equipment maker, listed in 2011. He expanded via acquisitions (Italy's Fosber 2014, Baisheng marine engines, EDF, Tiruna, Agnati) and in 2025 sold the Fosber overseas corrugated-line business for ~€817m, pivoting to high-end smart equipment, outboard power and AI+robotics.
interesting_fact: The Fosber corrugated-line business he bought into in 2014 was sold in 2025 for a final consideration of about €817m, funding a pivot to robotics and marine power.
deep_cut_fact: Dongfang Precision started out in agricultural-product packaging printing before Tang moved it into corrugated-carton equipment, growing it from a 'small workshop' into a group, as he recounted at a 2024 Nanhai chairmen's salon marking nearly 30 years.
notes: Co-controller with brother Tang Zhuomian per 2011 IPO docs. Manufacturing/robotics pivot is a podcast angle.

name: Liu Peichao
current_role: Founder, Chairman and President, Shenzhen Dobot Corp (越疆科技, HKEX: 2432)
profile: Liu Peichao (刘培超), a Shandong University mechanical-engineering master's graduate, quit a job at the Chinese Academy of Sciences' Suzhou medical-engineering institute to build a desktop robot arm in 2014, founding Dobot in Shenzhen in 2015. Dobot became a leading collaborative-robot maker (desktop, industrial cobots, now humanoids), listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2024 and is pursuing a ChiNext A-share listing; he owns roughly half the company.
interesting_fact: Dobot started with a low-cost desktop robotic arm for makers and classrooms in 2014 and grew into one of the world's top collaborative-robot vendors by shipments, now also building humanoid robots.
deep_cut_fact: As a Shandong University freshman he won the campus phone-card sales agency; after being recommended for postgraduate study he led classmates in business-plan contests and worked weekends as an outdoor team-building coach. He left the CAS medical-engineering institute to start up without telling his family.
notes: Named a national 'Ten Thousand Talents' tech-entrepreneur leader (2019). Gives media interviews on robotics. Sensitive: in July 2026 co-founder/ex-COO Song Tao publicly disputed shareholdings ahead of the A-share IPO; avoid the topic.

name: Li Xinnong
current_role: Director and co-actual controller (~9.1%), JL MAG Rare-Earth Co. (SZSE: 300748; HKEX: 6680); Executive Director & GM, Hunan Boxun Investment Holding Group
profile: Li Xinnong (李忻农), born 1969, is a Beihang-trained materials engineer who co-controls Ganzhou-based JL MAG Rare-Earth with chairman Cai Baogui and Hu Zhibin. JL MAG is one of the world's largest makers of high-performance NdFeB permanent magnets used in EV motors, wind turbines and, increasingly, humanoid-robot motor rotors. He has been a director since 2008.
interesting_fact: JL MAG's product list now includes motor rotors for embodied/humanoid robots and rare-earth recycling, alongside the NdFeB magnets that go into EV traction motors and wind turbines.
deep_cut_fact: He studied metallic materials and heat treatment at Beihang University (BS 1991, MEng 1995) and his first post-graduate job was deputy chief engineer at Zhuhai Tiannian Bioengineering (1995-98) - a biotech detour before rare-earth magnets.
notes: Non-executive at JL MAG; very low media profile. Relevant to energy/EV/robotics supply-chain themes (rare-earth magnets).

profile: Southeast University-trained semiconductor engineer who founded Wuxi Chipown, a fabless designer of power-management ICs (AC-DC/DC-DC converters, gate drivers) for appliances, industrial and automotive uses. Chipown listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020; Zhang remains chairman and controlling shareholder.

name: Ou Yang (欧洋)
current_role: Co-founder, Director and General Manager, Suzhou TFC Optical Communication (天孚通信, SZSE: 300394) (GM since Jan 2018 per 2024 reporting)
profile: Co-founder (b. 1968) with husband Zou Zhinong and Zhu Guodong of TFC Optical Communication, a Suzhou maker of passive optical components and high-speed optical-engine packaging. TFC started in 2005 with zirconia ceramic sleeves, listed on ChiNext in 2015 and boomed on AI data-center demand for 800G/1.6T optics; she and Zou are the actual controllers.
interesting_fact: The name 'TFC' (天孚) comes from the English phrase 'Technology First'. TFC's first product, a rice-grain-sized ceramic ferrule sleeve, displaced Japanese imports such as Kyocera's in China's fiber-optic market.
deep_cut_fact: Every TFC production line entrance displays a plaque reading '如履薄冰' ('as if treading on thin ice'). Ou Yang says it reminds staff to treat even the tiniest component 'like a baby' because TFC ships hundreds of millions of ceramic sleeves a year.
notes: Wealth shared with husband Zou Zhinong (chairman). TFC filed for a Hong Kong H-share listing in late 2025. The ir_email is TFC's securities department (证券部). Strong data-center optics angle. Current GM title confirmed only through 2024 reporting.

name: Hsieh Juor-Ming
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, Voltronic Power Technology Corp. (旭隼科技, TWSE: 6409), Taipei
profile: Hsieh Juor-Ming (謝卓明, 'Alex Hsieh') founded Voltronic Power with five colleagues during the 2008 financial crisis and built it into the world's largest ODM maker of small/mid-size UPS units, also making solar inverters and DC EV chargers. Profitable every year except its first, it is one of Taiwan's few non-semiconductor 'thousand-dollar' stocks; he now targets large data-center UPS as AI drives demand.
interesting_fact: Voltronic is a classic high-mix, low-volume maker: ~20,000 complete UPS models on the books, shipping 4,000-6,000 different models a month, often only a few dozen units per order - yet it holds 20%+ of global UPS ODM share.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2025 CTEE interview he contrasted himself with Morris Chang's ideal CEO (80% strategy, 20% execution): 'I am not that ideal CEO - I spend 90% on details; details decide victory.' During the 2020-22 chip shortage he personally chaired the shortage meeting every day.
notes: Romanisations vary: Alex Hsieh / Hsieh Jour-Ming / Chuo-Ming Hsieh. Company spokesman listed as Chiehmin Wang (Financial Manager). Strong fit for a data-center power episode (UPS, BBU views, AI demand); he does give occasional Taiwanese press interviews.

profile: Shenmu (Yulin, Shaanxi) coal-chemical entrepreneur whose wealth comes from Beiyuan Chemical, a large PVC and caustic-soda producer built on local coal and power, co-owned with state-owned Shaanxi Coal. name: Li Abo
current_role: Director and Honorary Chairman, Yinchuan Weili Transmission Technology (Shenzhen ChiNext 300904)
profile: Li Abo (李阿波, b. 1955), a senior engineer from Ningxia, built Yinchuan Weili Reducer (founded 2003) into Weili Transmission, which makes precision gear reducers and yaw/pitch drives for wind turbines. He chaired the listed company and is now honorary chairman; Li Xiang, with whom Hurun lists the fortune, is chairman and president.
interesting_fact: Weili, a gear-reducer maker in Yinchuan, is building a planned RMB5bn wind-turbine gearbox ('speed-increaser') smart factory, billed as the only large wind-gearbox R&D and production base in western China.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong gearbox engineer, he started at the reducer research institute of Yinchuan Crane Factory, later headed the design office of the Ningxia Reducer Research Institute and served as deputy secretary-general of China's national gear-reducer industry association, before founding Weili and serving as its chief engineer.
notes: Country is blank in the input; he is Chinese (Ningxia). Hurun-listed only in 2023. Day-to-day leader is chairman/president Li Xiang. Route via the IR mailbox in the 2025 annual report.

name: Paul S. Levy
current_role: Founder and Managing Director, JLL Partners; Chairman, Builders FirstSource (BLDR); director, Loar Holdings and ContextLogic
profile: Paul S. Levy is a New York private-equity veteran who joined/co-founded JLL Partners (Joseph Littlejohn & Levy) in 1988 after working on restructurings at Drexel Burnham Lambert. JLL has committed ~$4.7bn across seven funds in middle-market buyouts; his wealth comes largely from stakes in portfolio companies such as building-products giant Builders FirstSource and aerospace-components maker Loar.

name: Philipp Schindler

profile: German executive (b. ~1971, Düsseldorf) who rose through Bertelsmann, CompuServe and AOL Germany before joining Google in Hamburg in 2005. He ran Northern & Central Europe, moved to Mountain View in 2012 to head global sales and operations, and since 2015 has been Chief Business Officer overseeing Google and YouTube sales, partnerships and customer support. His wealth comes from Alphabet stock.
