notes: Deceased 12 April 2017; sources: https://www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Chandra_Agarwal and https://www.deccanchronicle.com/nation/current-affairs/120417/dainik-bhaskar-group-chairman-ramesh-agrawal-passes-away.html . His sons Sudhir, Girish and Pawan Agarwal now run DB Corp.

name: Andrew Nisbet
current_role: Founder of Nisbets (catering equipment); Director, Key West Holdings (Nisbet family investment company); founder-trustee, The Nisbet Trust
profile: Andrew Nisbet (b. 1960, Bristol) founded Nisbets in 1983 and built it into Europe's largest catering-equipment distributor, headquartered in Avonmouth, Bristol. In 2024 he sold an 80% stake to Bunzl at a reported GBP500m valuation; the family now manages its interests and property via Key West Holdings and gives locally through The Nisbet Trust.
interesting_fact: Nisbets started in 1983 selling knives, chef's whites and textbooks to catering students; it launched a mail-order catalogue in 1987, moved into wholesale in 1990, and by 2023 made most of its sales online.
deep_cut_fact: He joined his father's regional catering-equipment firm, Peter Nisbet & Co., straight from school in 1978 before striking out on his own five years later; he later served as High Sheriff of Bristol (2012-13).

public_contacts.value: info@keywestholdings.co.uk (Key West Holdings, family investment office, Bristol)

notes: Nisbet Trust contact is for grant enquiries, so Key West Holdings is the more appropriate route. Wikipedia article carries a paid-editing warning; core facts (1983 founding, Bunzl 2024 deal, High Sheriff) are widely reported.

name: Xiong Xianzhong
profile: Appeared on Hurun China (2009-2021) and Hurun Global (2015-2018) lists with wealth attributed to 'Hongkelong' (retail and real estate). No reliable public source was found describing him or the company; Hongkelong may be the Jiangxi retailer 洪客隆, but this could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity unverified (private company; Baidu Baike blocked, web search returned nothing). A person of this name appears in 2025 Changyuan Group (600525) filings as a plaintiff in a securities case; not confirmed to be the same person and not used.

name: Ma Xingfa
current_role: Chairman, Tianma Holding Group (天马控股集团), Hangzhou (as of last filings found); former chairman and controller of Tianma Bearing Group (SZ:002122)
profile: Ma Xingfa (马兴法, b. Nov 1962) built Hangzhou-based Tianma Bearing into one of China's major bearing makers, including wind-turbine and special precision bearings and heavy CNC equipment (stake in Qiqihar heavy CNC maker Qizhong). He controlled the Shenzhen-listed company with his family until selling control around 2016-2017; the listed company has since changed hands and names (now ST Huizhou).
interesting_fact: Tianma positioned its wind-turbine and special precision bearings as high-end import substitutes, an early Chinese play on wind-power supply chains.
deep_cut_fact: Ma, a trained engineer, served as rotating chairman of the China Bearing Industry Association, was twice named a national 'township enterprise entrepreneur' (4th and 5th rounds) and was a Hangzhou model worker.
notes: No longer connected to the listed company (now ST Huizhou, dsh@hzitg.com - not a route to him). Off Hurun lists since 2017; current activities not found. Avoid the post-sale history of the listed company.

name: Zhang Songshan
current_role: Chairman, Huapont Life Sciences Co., Ltd. (Shenzhen: 002004)
profile: Zhang Songshan (b. 1961, PhD, senior engineer) co-founded Huapont's predecessor, Chongqing Huapont Biochemical Technology, in 1992 and has chaired the company since 2001. Huapont is a Chongqing-based dermatology-drug leader that has grown into a group spanning pharma, medical services, agrochemicals (Beijing Yingtai), new materials (Kaisheng) and tourism (Lijiang Yulong).
interesting_fact: Alongside pharmaceuticals, he chairs or sits on the boards of a string of tourism businesses, including Lijiang Jade Dragon Snow Mountain tourism development, Shaanxi Taibai Mountain Qinling Tourism and Hunan Liye tourism.
deep_cut_fact: Huapont began on 11 March 1992 as a tiny tech venture with just RMB 500,000 of registered capital. It was co-founded by the Chongqing High-Tech Venture Center, the Shapingba Nanfang Biochemical Institute and individuals including Zhang Songshan and Pan Mingxin.
notes: Huapont controls three A-share listcos (Kaisheng New Materials 301069, Yingtai 920819, Lijiang Tourism 002033). The route is via the board secretary/IR email.

name: Yang Weixin
current_role: Chairman and co-controlling shareholder (about 18.3%), Bros Eastern Co. (百隆东方, SSE 601339), Ningbo
profile: Yang Weixin (杨卫新) has chaired Bros Eastern since 2004, which he controls with his brother and vice chairman Yang Weiguo. Based in Ningbo, it is one of China's leading makers of 'colour-spun' (melange) cotton yarn, where fibres are dyed before spinning. He also served as general manager in 2015-2020 and 2024-2025.
interesting_fact: Bros Eastern moved early to Southeast Asia. Its Vietnam subsidiary now accounts for about 78% of the company's total capacity, which makes this Ningbo yarn group effectively a Vietnam-based manufacturer.
notes: A low-profile textile industrialist; no interviews or personal biography found. He also chairs Bros Group Ltd and family property companies in Ningbo. The energy-intensive spinning and dyeing operations in Vietnam could be a hook for the energy angle. The best route is the board secretary email.

name: Guo Xinping
current_role: Largest individual shareholder (22.21%) of Beijing UniStrong Science & Technology (合众思壮, SZSE: 002383); not the controlling shareholder since a Zhengzhou state-owned investor took control (c. 2019)
profile: A Guo Xinping (郭信平) founded Beijing UniStrong, a satellite-navigation (GPS/BeiDou) and high-precision positioning company that listed in Shenzhen in 2010, matching his Hurun appearances from 2010. Control later passed to a Zhengzhou Airport Economy Zone state entity; he still held 22.21% at end-2025.
interesting_fact: UniStrong was an early Chinese maker of handheld GPS receivers and later moved into BeiDou-based high-precision positioning for surveying, agriculture and mapping.
notes: Identity not fully confirmed: input lists source of wealth as 'Yibei' / financial software, but filings tie Guo Xinping to UniStrong (GNSS). His UniStrong shares are recorded as frozen (2025 annual report) - sensitive. Web-search budget ran out before this could be resolved.

name: Shen Jieliang
current_role: Former controlling shareholder of Kuangda Technology Group (旷达科技, SZSE: 002516), Changzhou; ceded control to Zhuzhou state capital (Zhuzhou Qichuang) in 2025-26, retaining ~18.6%
profile: Shen Jieliang (沈介良) is the founder and long-time controlling shareholder of Kuangda Technology, a Changzhou (Wujin), Jiangsu maker of automotive interior fabrics and seating textiles that also built a solar-power business. In 2025 he agreed to sell 28% of Kuangda to Zhuzhou Qichuang for about RMB2.22bn (RMB5.39/share), making Zhuzhou SASAC the actual controller; he keeps roughly 18.6% but waives voting rights.
interesting_fact: His 2025 deal handed control of a private Jiangsu auto-textile maker to the Zhuzhou (Hunan) municipal SASAC for about RMB2.22bn – a notable private-to-state transfer.
notes: Very low media profile. Company is now state-controlled, so Kuangda IR is not a reliable route to him personally. Check completion of share transfer in latest SZSE filings.

name: Du Jiangbo
current_role: Shareholder (30%) of Wuhai Junzheng Technology Industry Group, the No. 2 holder of Inner Mongolia Junzheng Energy & Chemical (601216.SH); long-time chairman of Junzheng's supervisory board (not on the board elected July 2026)
profile: Du Jiangbo (杜江波) is the elder brother of Junzheng founder and controller Du Jiangtao, often Inner Mongolia's richest man. Junzheng, based in Wuhai, runs coal mining, power, calcium carbide, PVC/caustic soda, ferrosilicon, coke, methanol and BDO, plus a chemical-logistics arm. Du Jiangbo's wealth comes from his stake in the family holding company and his supervisory role at the listed group.
interesting_fact: Junzheng is a vertically integrated 'coal-to-chemicals' play: it mines coal and limestone, generates its own power, and turns it into carbide, PVC and cement clinker from carbide slag, and also controls a chemical tanker fleet of ~1.1M dwt.
notes: Very low profile; almost no personal coverage. Not listed among Junzheng's 7th board or executives in its July 2026 announcement (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202607241827321470_1.pdf), so his supervisory-board role likely ended with China's 2026 governance changes. Best route via Junzheng Group corporate/IR.

name: An Huailve
current_role: Co-actual controller (~11.5%) and adviser, Guizhou Xinbang Pharmaceutical (SZSE: 002390); resigned as chairman in April 2022
profile: An Huailve (安怀略), born 1963, is a physician turned pharma entrepreneur who built Guizhou Kekai Pharmaceutical and became chairman and co-controller of Xinbang Pharmaceutical, a Guizhou group spanning hospitals/medical services, drug distribution and traditional Chinese medicine manufacturing. He stepped down as chairman in 2022; Xinbang is now chaired by his co-controller An Ji.
interesting_fact: Xinbang combines three businesses rarely held together - hospital operations, pharmaceutical distribution and TCM manufacturing (e.g. Yixinshu and Maixuekang capsules) - in one Guizhou-listed group.
deep_cut_fact: A Guizhou Medical University medical graduate and associate chief physician, he once headed the emergency/outpatient department at the university's affiliated hospital before running Guizhou Kekai Pharmaceutical.
notes: CAUTION: reports say in early 2025 Kaiyang County court accepted a bribery case involving Guizhou Kekai Pharmaceutical and An Huailve (https://m.thepaper.cn/detail/30286999); outcome not verified. Likely not a suitable outreach target.

name: Cai Tianzhen
current_role: Former founder-chairman of Titan Petrochemicals Group (泰山石化, HKEX 1192); no current role found
profile: Cai Tianzhen (蔡天真, Tsoi Tin Chun, b. c.1962), an oil trader, founded Hong Kong-listed Titan Petrochemicals in 2002 and controlled ~56% through Singapore-registered Titan Oil Pte. Titan ran oil tankers, bunkering and oil-storage logistics in Asia. He stepped down as chairman in July 2012, left the board in Feb 2013, and later sold control to Guangdong Zhenrong.
interesting_fact: By 2006 he had over 20 years in the oil business, meaning he started trading oil in his early twenties, in the mid-1980s.
deep_cut_fact: He held his Titan stake through Titan Oil Pte. Ltd., owned 95% by him and 5% by his wife, via an intermediate company aptly named Great Logistics Holdings, and chaired Titan from its May 2002 inception until July 2012.
notes: Out of the public eye since 2013. Avoid: Titan went through a debt restructuring and the HKEX Listing Committee later censured him as a former director. No published contact. Resignation source: https://en.portnews.ru/news/140198

name: Li Zhantong
current_role: Actual controller (approx. 70%) of Tianjin Datong Investment Group (天津大通投资集团); current activity unclear
profile: Li Zhantong (李占通) controls Tianjin Datong Investment Group, a Tianjin conglomerate spanning pharmaceuticals, gas, real estate, environmental services and media that once held about 20 companies, including control of listed Chase Sun Pharmaceutical (红日药业) and Sichuan Datong Gas (000593). In 2018-19 he sold down both stakes; Datong Gas passed to steel magnate Ding Liguo.
interesting_fact: Datong Group was founded in Tianjin by a team largely made up of former teachers from well-known Tianjin universities, and was seen as the leading 'Tianjin university-faction' investment house.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2005 Datong Group bought 55 million legal-person shares of Baoguang Pharmaceutical from Langjiu Group and others, became its largest shareholder and swapped in its gas business, a backdoor listing that created listed Datong Gas.
notes: Very little public information; no recent (post-2019) news found, so alive status and current role are unverified. Hurun last listed him in 2020. Has exited the gas business, so weak fit for an energy podcast. No official contact channel found.

name: Wang Wenliang
current_role: Chairman and executive director, Zhongyu Energy Holdings Ltd (formerly Zhongyu Gas, HKEX: 3633)
profile: Wang Wenliang (王文亮; input has 王文良), 55, has been executive director of Zhongyu since 2003 and chairs the Hong Kong-listed city-gas and energy distributor, controlled through his Hezhong Investment Holding. Over 30 years he has also invested in securities, internet services, building materials, property, energy and infrastructure.
interesting_fact: Before joining Zhongyu, Wang was briefly an executive director of China Gas Holdings (Jan-Jun 2003), one of China's biggest piped-gas distributors.
deep_cut_fact: Wang is deputy chairman of the fourth council of the China Foundation for Justice and Courage, which honours civilians who act bravely. He is a Hong Kong Justice of the Peace, did postgraduate finance at CASS's Graduate School (2001) and a Peking University EMBA (2019).
notes: Correct Chinese name per HKEX filings is 王文亮. Hurun lists wealth shared with Feng Haiyan. The company was renamed from Zhongyu Gas to Zhongyu Energy. Best route is company IR in Hong Kong (Shun Tak Centre).

name: Liu Han
profile: Liu Han (刘汉), founder and chairman of Sichuan-based Hanlong Group (mining, energy, chemicals, property), died in February 2015.
notes: Deceased: executed in China in February 2015 (Hanlong Group Wikipedia article, citing BBC/Reuters/SMH; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanlong_Group). Do not contact. Hanlong Group has been dissolved. Remove from outreach list.

name: Ma Yongsheng
current_role: Founder/chairman of Yunnan Haolong (Haolong) Group, Ludian County, Zhaotong (current status after 2021 not confirmed)
profile: Ma Yongsheng (马永升; not Sinopec's Ma Yongsheng 马永生) left a prosecutor's-office job in 1988 to revive a bankrupt cement plant, then in 1998 founded Ludian Haolong Industrial, growing it into a Yunnan group in lead-zinc mining, cement, hydropower and Kunming real estate. He was once called Yunnan's richest man and its top philanthropist; on Hurun lists 2008-2021 with Suo Fang.
interesting_fact: From 2005 Haolong built a string of small hydropower stations in Yunnan (Heishihe, Pudu River, Qingshui River, Guanhe) and won rights to Huangjiaoshu, the largest cascade on the Niulan River.
deep_cut_fact: In 1999, ignoring an official survey that said the Lehong deposit was unfit for large-scale mining, he led his team in winter to measure cliff profiles by tape, sometimes roped to trees on the summit, and proved large lead-zinc reserves. Earlier, as a 1988 graduate, he carried cement sacks alongside workers to revive the idle Dashuijing plant.
notes: Hurun spells the company 'Haolong' (昊龙). Little coverage after the 2010s; current role and well-being unverified. Fortune shared with Suo Fang. Do not confuse with Sinopec chairman Ma Yongsheng. No published contact found; regional Yunnan private group with minimal web presence.

name: Suo Fang
current_role: Second-largest shareholder (6.36%) of Yunnan Haolong Industrial Group (云南昊龙实业集团, Zhaotong); wife of group president Ma Yongsheng
profile: Suo Fang (锁芳) is the wife of Ma Yongsheng, founder of Yunnan Haolong (昊龙) Industrial Group, set up in 1998 in Zhaotong and focused on non-ferrous metal mining and processing, with utilities and property interests. Registry data cited by the press show Ma with 89.1% and Suo Fang 6.36%. She has acted as the family's public spokesperson in recent years.
interesting_fact: Hurun's 2009 list made Ma Yongsheng 'Yunnan's richest man' (RMB3bn), 11 years after founding the group; Haolong says it has paid RMB5.13bn in cumulative taxes and ranks among Yunnan's top 100 private firms.
notes: Hurun romanises the firm as 'Haolong' but the Chinese is 昊龙 (not 浩龙). Sensitive: Ma Yongsheng was detained in April 2022 and a 1990 assault case against him was reopened in 2023; Suo Fang has spoken to media about it. Avoid in outreach. No published contact found.

name: Ji Jing
profile: Hurun's 2018 list ranks Ji Jing (纪静, Yinchuan-based) No.902 with RMB4.5bn from Bao Ta Petrochemical (宝塔石化, Yinchuan; petrochemicals and education). Baota's actual controller in filings was Sun Hengchao (孙珩超); we found no public source naming 纪静 as owner, director or relative.
notes: Hurun record: https://www.hurun.net/zh-CN/Rank/HsRankDetailsList?num=DFW1O34E&search=%E7%BA%AA%E9%9D%99&offset=0&limit=20 . Tried: 纪静 + 宝塔石化/孙珩超/银川能源学院; Baota Industry (000595) 2016 annual report. Baota later collapsed (finance arm licence revoked). Unresolved.

name: Sun Jiangyan
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-21) with Wang Fuxiang as holding wealth through Shanghai Sinyang Semiconductor Materials (300236.SZ), a Songjiang-based maker of chip electroplating and cleaning chemicals and photoresists. Wang Fuxiang, the founder, held about 14% directly in 2025, and the company is now led by Wang Su. I found no public filing or profile describing Sun Jiangyan's role.
notes: Identity not confirmed: probably a family member or co-holder alongside founder Wang Fuxiang, but no source confirms it. The company IR email comes from the 2018 annual report summary (April 2019) and may be out of date. A better route is probably via Wang Fuxiang or chairman Wang Su. Low priority.

name: Shi Zongmei
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and head of the materials-control centre, Guangdong Lingxiao Pump Industry (凌霄泵业, 002884.SZ)
profile: Shi Zongmei (施宗梅) and her husband, chairman/GM Wang Haibo, are the controlling shareholders of Lingxiao Pump, a Yangchun, Guangdong maker of plastic and stainless-steel pumps listed in Shenzhen in 2017. She works inside the company running its materials-control centre (物控中心). Lingxiao supplies pumps for spas, pools, water parks and bathroom fittings worldwide.
interesting_fact: Lingxiao describes itself as a leading global supplier of pumps for bath and water-recreation equipment (spas, hot tubs, water parks), especially plastic bath pumps sold to well-known international bathroom brands.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a billionaire co-owner, she holds an operational job at the company - director of its materials-control (procurement/inventory) centre - rather than a board seat.
notes: Very low profile; husband Wang Haibo is the public face. Route via board secretary email (listed as LX7236@126.COM).

name: Feng Haiyan
current_role: Substantial shareholder (non-executive) of Zhongyu Energy Holdings Ltd. (HKEX: 3633, formerly Zhongyu Gas); co-owner of Hezhong Investment Holding
profile: Feng Haiyan (冯海燕) is the wife of Zhongyu Energy chairman Wang Wenliang, and Hurun lists them together. She owns 49% of Hezhong Investment Holding, the couple's vehicle; with Wang's direct holding, they control about 29% of Zhongyu. Zhongyu is a Hong Kong-listed city-gas distributor in mainland China, and China Gas Holdings is its other major holder. She holds no board or executive role.
interesting_fact: Under Hong Kong disclosure rules she holds 10.9M Zhongyu shares directly and is deemed interested in 800M shares (29.12%) through Hezhong and her husband's holdings.
notes: Private, passive shareholder with no public profile; Hurun listed her only in 2021, jointly with Wang Wenliang. For a podcast, Wang Wenliang (chairman since 2003) is the more natural guest. The company's Hong Kong office is at China Merchants Tower, Shun Tak Centre (from the annual report). Company secretary: Lui Siu Keung.

name: Yu Dehai
current_role: Co-actual controller of Kede Numerical Control (科德数控, SSE STAR: 688305) via Dalian Guangyang Science & Technology (光洋科技), its controlling shareholder
profile: Dalian industrialist behind Guangyang Science & Technology, the parent of Kede Numerical Control, one of China's leading makers of high-end five-axis CNC machine tools with in-house CNC systems, servo drives and motors. Kede listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2021; Yu Dehai and Yu Benhong are named together as controllers in its IPO commitments.
interesting_fact: Kede is one of the few Chinese companies to build both five-axis machining centres and their CNC control systems in-house, serving aerospace and power-generation turbine-blade machining, a field long dominated by Swiss/German suppliers.
notes: Very low public profile; Yu Benhong is Kede's chairman and day-to-day face. Web-search budget ran out, so Yu Dehai's personal bio and current status were not verified. Route via Kede board secretary/IR email.

name: Yu Benhong
current_role: Chairman, Kede Numerical Control (科德数控, SSE STAR:688305), Dalian; member of the 14th CPPCC National Committee
profile: Yu Benhong (b. ~1977) has chaired Kede CNC since 2015; the Dalian company makes five-axis CNC machine tools, high-end CNC systems and key components (servo drives, motors, spindles) aimed at replacing imports, serving aerospace/defence and civil markets. Wealth is shared with Yu Dehai, the founder of the Dalian Guangyang group from which Kede emerged.
interesting_fact: Kede is one of China's few makers of both five-axis machine tools and their own high-end CNC control systems, including blade-machining and blisk centres used for turbine parts.
deep_cut_fact: Before chairing Kede he ran Dalian Guangyang's international industrial-control technology-transfer centre for 16 years (2004-2020); in January 2023 he became a member of the 14th CPPCC National Committee.
notes: Hurun listing shared with Yu Dehai. Relevant to advanced manufacturing/turbine machining. IR email from the 2025 annual report.

name: Zhang Hebing (张和兵)
current_role: Co-founder, joint controlling shareholder and Special Assistant to the Chairman, Porton Pharma Solutions (博腾股份, SZSE: 300363); chairman & GM of Chongqing Juxin Investment
profile: Zhang is one of three co-founders and joint actual controllers (with chairman Ju Nianfeng and Tao Rong, under a joint-control agreement) of Chongqing-based Porton Pharma Solutions, a contract development and manufacturing organisation founded in 2005. Porton makes APIs and drug products for global pharma across small molecules, peptides/oligos, biologics and ADCs; he holds about 7.7%.
interesting_fact: Porton has grown from a 2005 Chongqing start-up into a global CDMO with 4,400+ staff, 1,500+ customers and about 6,000 delivered projects.
deep_cut_fact: Porton's three founders signed a formal joint-control agreement before the 2014 IPO and still act in concert; besides Porton, Zhang chairs the supervisory board of Runsheng Pharmaceutical and runs Chongqing Yixin Investment Management.
notes: Low public profile; chairman Ju Nianfeng is the spokesman. Facts from Porton 2025 annual report (cninfo) and company site. Web search budget exhausted, so personal background (education/early career) not researched.

name: Zhao Guanlong
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2020-2021 (赵关龙) with wealth from 'RongSheng', a chemical-fibre business. The specific company could not be pinned down in this pass; it should not be assumed to be Rongsheng Petrochemical (controlled by Li Shuirong).
notes: Identity unconfirmed: web search budget was exhausted and no Wikipedia/Baike entry was reachable. Needs a Chinese-language follow-up search (赵关龙 荣盛 化纤) before any outreach.

name: Zhao Jinrong
current_role: Linked by Hurun China (2020-2021) to Inovance Technology (汇川技术, SZSE: 300124); role not verified
notes: Inovance was founded in 2003 by Zhu Xingming and other ex-Huawei engineers (Wikipedia). Zhao is presumably an early co-founder or shareholder, but this is unconfirmed. Web search budget ran out before research. Identity and details are unverified; re-run in a later wave.

name: Chuo Yung-Tsai
current_role: Founder and Group President, HIWIN Technologies (上銀科技, TWSE: 2049), Taichung, Taiwan; also founder of HIWIN Mikrosystem
profile: Chuo Yung-Tsai (卓永財, b. 1942), from a Hsinchu tenant-farming family, was a Bank of Communications executive who turned around Taiwan's largest nut maker in 1983, bought ball-screw maker Ho Feng Precision, and in 1989 founded HIWIN, now the world's No. 2 ball-screw maker. His son Eric Chuo is chairman.
interesting_fact: HIWIN bought German ball-screw maker Holzer in 1993, just four years after founding, giving the Taiwanese company an early European manufacturing base; it is now the world's No. 2 ball-screw maker.
deep_cut_fact: He once posted on Yahoo! Kimo Knowledge+ under the alias '猛男一號' ('Macho Man No. 1'), chatting about the machinery industry and encouraging female students to study mechanical engineering. He also funded a library at Liujia Elementary School in memory of his elder brother.
notes: Accounting graduate of Tamkang University with a management master's from University of San Francisco; author of a book on foreign-exchange practice. Honorary chairman of Taiwan's machine tool & accessory builders' association. Best route is HIWIN corporate/IR.

name: Zuo Guojun
current_role: Chairman, Shenzhen S.C New Energy Technology Corp. (捷佳伟创, 300724.SZ)
profile: Co-controller and chairman (since November 2023) of S.C New Energy, a major Chinese maker of solar-cell production tools (PECVD, diffusion, wet-chemistry) that also supplies semiconductor wet-process equipment. He acts in concert with Yu Zhong and Liang Meizhen and held 7.5% directly in March 2026.
interesting_fact: S.C equipment underpins much of China's solar-cell manufacturing build-out. In March 2026 Zuo and fellow pre-IPO holders took part in an inquiry-based share transfer, when Zuo held 26.16M shares (7.51%).
notes: 'S.C' in the source data refers to S.C New Energy (捷佳伟创). Little personal biography is public. The board secretary is Tan Xiangping. Company site was unreachable from this environment.

name: Liu Daojun
current_role: No current public role found; former director (2004-2022) and co-founding shareholder of Jiangxi Zhengbang Technology (SZSE: 002157)
profile: Liu Daojun (legal name Liew Kenneth Thow Jiun; Canadian, b. 1972) was a founding promoter of Zhengbang Technology, the Jiangxi feed and hog-farming group controlled by Lin Yinsun, and a director from 2004 to 2022 (169.6m shares at end-2019). Zhengbang has since been restructured under new control; his current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: Though listed by Hurun as a Chinese billionaire, filings identify him as a Canadian citizen named Liew Kenneth Thow Jiun - unrelated to Zhengbang's controlling family, yet a founding promoter of the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before and alongside Zhengbang he chaired Jiangxi Zhengbang Industrial, Yunnan Guanglian Livestock & Poultry and Nanchang Guanglian Industrial, and took no pay from the listed company as a director.
notes: Left Zhengbang board in 2022; the company went through court restructuring in 2023 and is now controlled by the Twins Group - avoid that topic. No personal channels found. Very low profile.

name: Huang Bingliang
current_role: Co-actual controller (with Zhang Xiaocheng, 50/50 via Qingdao Kangdien Industrial) of Qingdao Vland Biotech (SSE 603739)
profile: Huang Bingliang co-controls Qingdao Vland Biotech, which makes industrial and feed enzymes, probiotics (microecological products) and animal-health products. Vland's management is drawn heavily from Shandong Liuhe Group, the feed giant that merged into New Hope Liuhe in 2011, which likely explains Hurun listing his wealth source as 'New Hope'; that link is inferred, not confirmed.
interesting_fact: Vland's enzymes and probiotics sell into feed, food, textiles and other industries, making it one of China's notable listed industrial-enzyme producers.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: the Hurun entry says 'New Hope'; the only filings match for this name is Vland's co-controller, whose company has deep Liuhe/New Hope Liuhe ties. Verify before outreach. Search budget exhausted.

name: Fang Pingzhang
notes: Could not identify the company behind the 'CDWI' label or confirm this person from filings, Wikidata or exchange databases; web search budget was exhausted mid-lane. Needs a follow-up search (e.g. Chinese name 方平章 + company).

name: Chen Cuiping
profile: Hurun China 2020 lists 陈翠琴 (romanized here as Chen Cuiping; the characters read Chen Cuiqin) with 'CDWI' (diving equipment and services), jointly with Fang Pingzhang. The company could not be identified. It is not China Dive (中潜股份, 300526), whose filings do not mention either name.
notes: Unidentified. Note the pinyin mismatch (琴 = qin). The web-search budget ran out, so check the Hurun 2020 entry for the full company name.

name: Deni Bazhaev
current_role: Heir/shareholder of the Bazhaev family's Alliance Group interests (no confirmed executive title)
profile: Russian heir born in 1996, son of Alliance Group founder Ziya Bazhaev, who died in a March 2000 plane crash. As a minor he held about 29.9% of the holding controlling Alliance Oil (2007); the family sold its 60% oil-and-gas stake to Eduard Khudainatov's Independent Oil Company (NNK) in 2014. His wealth derives from those family holdings.
interesting_fact: Alliance Oil was founded through the Bazhaev family's Alliance Group; by 2007 the stake held in his name (29.9%) matched that of his uncle Musa Bazhaev, making him one of the largest shareholders while still a child.
notes: Very private; no public role, interviews or contacts found. Alive status inferred from his ongoing Forbes listing and Wikidata (no death date). Approach only via Bazhaev family/Alliance Group offices if at all. Search budget was exhausted.

name: Jabbok Schlacks
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, EquipmentShare.com Inc (Nasdaq: EQPT), Columbia, Missouri
profile: Jabbok Schlacks co-founded EquipmentShare in 2015 with his brother Willy and three others, after the brothers ran construction and contracting businesses from their teens. The company grew from a peer-to-peer equipment marketplace into a national construction equipment rental, sales and telematics business with 448 locations, and raised about $747m in its January 2026 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare's T3 cloud platform tracks over 397,000 construction assets with telematics, GPS and keypads. In 2025 the company opened a $100m Technology and Development Center at its Columbia, Mo. headquarters.
deep_cut_fact: The company began as a weekend pitch: in October 2014 the brothers won Startup Weekend Columbia with a peer-to-peer equipment-sharing idea, then joined Y Combinator's Winter 2015 batch.
notes: Strong fit for the podcast: a Midwest founder story (YC alum, Columbia MO) in construction tech, with exposure to data-center construction demand. Personal social accounts not verified. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane, so press/IR emails were not extracted.

name: Abel Matutes
current_role: President, Grupo Empresas Matutes (owner of Palladium Hotel Group), Ibiza
profile: Ibiza-born (1941) businessman and former politician: mayor of Ibiza (1970-71), senator, MEP, European Commissioner (1986-94) and Spain's foreign minister (1996-2000). His family group, Grupo Empresas Matutes, owns Palladium Hotel Group (formerly Fiesta Hotel Group), behind Ushuaia Ibiza and Hard Rock Hotel Ibiza, with banking, real estate and energy interests.
interesting_fact: In 1993-94 he was the European Commissioner responsible for Transport, Energy and the Euratom Supply Agency under Jacques Delors -- a direct link to an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: While studying law and economics in Barcelona he played professional football for RCD Espanyol, and reportedly turned down an offer from FC Barcelona to pursue business instead.
notes: Aged 85; his son Abel Matutes Prats now runs much of the group day-to-day. Also taught public finance at the University of Barcelona. Palladium HQ contacts page: palladiumhotelgroup.com/en/contact/oficinas-centrales; no dedicated press email found.

name: Joan Molins Amat
current_role: Board member (re-elected June 2025), Molins (Cementos Molins); non-executive chairman 2017-2025
profile: Joan Molins Amat (b. 1942) is a Catalan businessman and member of the family that controls Barcelona-based cement and building-materials group Molins. He joined in 1967 and moved into management in 1971, was managing director/CEO and led expansion into Argentina, Mexico, Uruguay, Bangladesh, Tunisia and Colombia. He chaired the group from 2017 to mid-2025 and remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Over five decades he took a Catalan family cement firm international. Molins now operates cement businesses across Europe, Latin America, Asia and Africa.
deep_cut_fact: He was president of Barcelona's influential business forum Cercle d'Economia (1992-95), a board member of Repsol YPF (1994-2006) and of the Port of Barcelona (1979-98), and has chaired the Institut Cerdà since 2016. He was also a driving force behind the Institut de l'Empresa Familiar.
notes: Also spelled Juan Molins Amat. Now in his early 80s. Cement and decarbonisation (energy-intensive industry) is a relevant podcast angle. Molins has a press room on its site, and the Institut Cerdà is another possible route. Do not confuse the company with Molins PLC (UK machinery).

name: Willy Schlacks
current_role: Co-founder & President, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT), Columbia, Missouri
profile: Willy Schlacks and his brother Jabbok (CEO) founded EquipmentShare in 2015, after winning Startup Weekend in Columbia, Missouri with a peer-to-peer equipment-sharing idea and joining Y Combinator (W15). It grew into the 4th-largest US equipment-rental firm with 430+ locations and its T3 jobsite telematics platform, and IPO'd on Nasdaq in Jan 2026 raising ~$747m.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare runs a 'Megasites' unit that puts fully staffed, on-site rental yards on huge jobsites such as data centers, infrastructure and renewables projects, directly relevant to the data-center build-out.
deep_cut_fact: Before EquipmentShare the brothers ran construction and general-contracting businesses as teenagers; their first pitch (2014, Startup Weekend Columbia, MO) was a peer-to-peer marketplace for contractors to rent idle equipment to each other, which won the event.
notes: Strong data-center/energy angle (megasites, energy & utilities rentals, power solutions). Brother Jabbok is CEO and the more public face. Personal social accounts not verified (search budget exhausted).

name: Christopher R Gordon
current_role: Partner, Global Head of Private Equity and Global Head of Healthcare, Bain Capital (Boston); former Kestra Medical director (2021 to Sept 2025)
profile: Chris Gordon joined Bain Capital in 1997 after consulting at Bain & Company and now leads its global private equity and healthcare investing. He has sat on boards of HCA, Quintiles (IQVIA), Waystar, Surgery Partners, Stada and Kestra Medical (wearable defibrillators), which Bain controls via West Affum Holdings. The SEC-derived net worth likely reflects Bain-held Kestra shares attributed to him, not personal holdings.
interesting_fact: He has served on the boards of a who's-who of healthcare buyouts, including HCA, Quintiles Transnational (now IQVIA), Grupo NotreDame Intermedica and Cerevel Therapeutics.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Baker Scholar (top of class distinction) at Harvard Business School, graduated magna cum laude in economics from Harvard College, and is a founding Director of the Healthcare Private Equity Association.
notes: Net worth figure ($646M) is likely an artefact: Kestra proxy lists his address c/o Bain Capital and shows no personal beneficial ownership; the 10% stake belongs to Bain funds. He left Kestra's board Sept 2025 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1877184/000119312526320956/ck0001877184-20260727.htm). Member, Council on Foreign Relations.

name: Oleg Tinkov
current_role: Founder of Tinkoff Bank (now T-Bank); no current executive role - divested his stake in 2022
profile: Siberian-born Oleg Tinkov built and sold several consumer businesses (Petrosib electronics, Daria frozen foods, Tinkoff beer - sold to InBev in 2005) before founding branchless Tinkoff Bank in 2006, listed in London in 2013. After condemning the war in Ukraine he sold out in 2022, renounced Russian citizenship and is now a Cypriot citizen.
interesting_fact: Tinkov owned a UCI World Tour cycling team - Tinkoff-Saxo/Tinkoff, bought from Bjarne Riis in 2013 - and earlier ran the Tinkoff Restaurants and Tinkoff Credit Systems pro teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before business, Tinkov was a serious road cyclist from age 12 and earned the Soviet title 'Candidate for Master of Sports' in 1984; he started trading goods during cycling training camps in Central Asia, and later studied at the St Petersburg Mining Institute.
notes: Sensitive: UK-sanctioned (March 2022), designated a 'foreign agent' by Russia (2024), outspoken political critic; outreach could be politically delicate. Active on Instagram/X but handles not verified from an official source. No published office/press contact found.

name: Institut Fur Marktentscheidungen e.V. Nurnberg (NIM – Nuremberg Institute for Market Decisions)
current_role: Non-profit association; >10% shareholder of NIQ Global Intelligence plc (NYSE: NIQ). President: Ralf Klein-Bölting
profile: NIM is the Nuremberg non-profit association (e.V.) that founded GfK in 1934 and now conducts behavioural and market-decision research (incl. the long-running GfK/NIM Consumer Climate index). After NIQ (NielsenIQ) acquired GfK in 2023, NIM became a major NIQ shareholder, holding >10% after NIQ's 2025 IPO. Not a person.
interesting_fact: GfK was founded in 1934 by Nuremberg university lecturers including future German Economics Minister and Chancellor Ludwig Erhard, with the concept developed by Wilhelm Vershofen.
deep_cut_fact: NIM's executive board explicitly lists its role as a NielsenIQ shareholder among its duties, and a Members' Council of business leaders must approve decisions on that stake; NIM also publishes the NIM Marketing Intelligence Review and runs 'Voices of the Leaders of Tomorrow' studies.
notes: Institutional holder, not an individual: an interview would be with NIM's president (Ralf Klein-Bölting) or researchers (e.g. consumer-climate head Rolf Bürkl). 'alive' not applicable.

name: Chen Jiangtao
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and actual controller of Beijing Watertek Information Technology Co. (SZSE ChiNext: 300324); not on current board
profile: Chen Jiangtao founded Beijing Watertek Information Technology in 1997; the ChiNext-listed company does embedded-system testing, electronic-component screening, tax/finance information-security platforms and smart-city work. He remains its actual controller (~5.1% direct stake at end-2025), while Chen Weiqun has chaired the company since November 2020.
interesting_fact: Watertek's 2025 annual report says it is repositioning around AI computing-power infrastructure, AI industry applications and the 'low-altitude economy' (drones/eVTOL), which overlaps with the podcast's data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Watertek, Chen held about 8.98 million shares (1.16%) of payments company Lakala (300773) at end-2025, per Watertek's annual report.
notes: Shared-wealth partner in input is Liu Xiping (also a Watertek shareholder). Company reported a loss in 2025. Route via board secretary Cai Houfu / investor@watertek.com.

name: Tao Hongxia
current_role: Co-owner of Chongqing Jinke Investment Holding (Group), historical controlling shareholder of Jinke Property Group (SZSE: 000656)
profile: Tao Hongxia (陶虹遐) and Huang Hongyun co-own Chongqing Jinke Investment, which controlled Chongqing-based developer Jinke Property after a 2009-2011 reverse merger into the listed Chongqing Dongyuan. Her wealth came from that stake. Jinke later went through court-supervised restructuring, and its annual report now says it has no actual controller.
interesting_fact: Jinke Property entered the stock market through a 2009-2011 reverse merger into the listed Chongqing Dongyuan Industrial Development, with Jinke Investment as controlling shareholder.
notes: Not a public-facing executive; profile is tied to a co-owner and to Jinke's debt restructuring, so outreach is sensitive and likely unsuitable. Hurun data ends 2021, so current wealth is probably far lower. Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Huang Youlong
current_role: Private investor (Singapore national); no current listed-company executive role confirmed
profile: Huang Youlong (b. 1976, Shaodong, Hunan) is a Singapore-based investor who started in the cement trade in Guangdong and, from the 2010s, took stakes in Hong Kong-listed companies (e.g. Sunlon/Shunlong Holdings) and resource ventures, including Mongolian cement and energy. Hurun (2015-19) listed him jointly with actress Zhao Wei, his wife at the time.
interesting_fact: He grew up in a farming family in Longtang village, Shetianqiao town, Hunan, and made his first money in the Guangdong cement business.
notes: Not recommended as an outreach target: very private, and his public record is dominated by the 2018 CSRC penalty (5-year securities-market ban over the Wanjia Culture bid) and media scrutiny. He and Zhao Wei divorced in 2021. No published contact channel.

name: Zhao Wei
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Gold Ocean' (China). Not researched: the lane's web-search quota ran out before this person was reached, and direct fetches of likely company sites returned nothing usable.
notes: Needs a follow-up pass. Search the Chinese name plus the company (Gold Ocean) on the exchange filings (SSE/SZSE/HKEXnews) to confirm identity, role and the company's IR email.

name: Liu Dejian
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Executive Director, NetDragon Websoft Holdings (0777.HK)
profile: Dr. Liu Dejian (Dejian Liu) studied in the US (Kansas) and ran a biotech company there before returning to Fuzhou in 1999 to found NetDragon, maker of online games such as Eudemons/Conquer Online. He later built the 91 Wireless app store (sold to Baidu) and Edmodo/Promethean ed-tech. NetDragon is now repositioning as an 'AI company' around its Moyu AI agent platform.
interesting_fact: NetDragon appointed an AI-driven virtual humanoid, 'Tang Yu', as rotating CEO of its main subsidiary Fujian NetDragon Websoft in 2022, which it billed as a world first.
deep_cut_fact: Before NetDragon's games took off, he created the game portal 17173.com, which he sold to Sohu for about US$20.5 million. Most of the proceeds reportedly went to support his mother's research work.
notes: Good podcast fit on AI and education: he gave a keynote at a UN high-level expert meeting on AI and education in June 2025. Early-life details (Kansas, US software and biotech ventures): https://www.qianzhan.com/people/profile/27c6c1.html

name: He Keneng
profile: He Keneng (何克能) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2018 with wealth from 'Yimei' (real estate and chemicals), shared with Zhang Xiuyuan. The company and any current role could not be identified from public web sources.
notes: No matching public information found in English or Chinese searches; dropped off Hurun after 2018. Needs a Chinese registry check to identify 'Yimei' before any outreach.

name: Zhang Xiuyuan
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2018, jointly with He Keneng (likely spouse/partner), with wealth from 'Yimei', a private group in real estate and chemicals. The company's Chinese name and the individuals' roles could not be identified in accessible sources.
notes: Unresolved: searches for 张秀元 and 何克能 returned nothing relevant; Chinese engines (Baidu/Sogou) blocked here. Off the Hurun list since 2018. Check the original Hurun entry for the Chinese company name (e.g. 'Yimei' 怡美/伊美/益美) before outreach.

name: Yang Zhenhua
current_role: Founder and former chairman/actual controller, Shanghai New Culture Media Group (新文化, SZSE: 300336); no current role found
profile: Yang Zhenhua (杨震华) founded Shanghai New Culture Media (est. Dec 2004), a film/TV drama investment, production and distribution company that listed on ChiNext in 2012. Filings from 2020 call him the 'former actual controller' with ~10.5% of shares, and by 2024 the company had a different chairman.
interesting_fact: New Culture Media was one of the private TV-drama production houses that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board soon after it launched.
notes: Hurun listing (2014-2017) is shared with Yang Lu. He has given up control and has been cutting his stake (2022 reduction plan), and the company now trades with a modified ticker prefix. Low profile; no published contact.

name: Qi Xiuping
current_role: Listed by Hurun China (2017-2021) with wealth from medical company 'Tairui'; role not verified
profile: Qi Xiuping (祁秀萍) appeared on Hurun China lists 2017-2021 with wealth attributed to a medical business recorded as 'Tairui'. Chinese and English searches found no public profile, filing or press coverage confirming the company or her role.
notes: Could not identify the company. Note: Hunan-based Tairui Medical (oxygen equipment, est. 2007) is credited to founder Ye Zhaohui, so it may be a different 'Tairui'. Check Hurun's original entry or corporate registries before outreach. Off the list since 2021.

name: Li Jundong
current_role: Former executive director, Canvest Environmental Protection Group (HKEX: 1381, delisted June 2025); member, 14th National CPPCC
profile: Li Jundong, known in Hong Kong filings as Lai Chun Tung (黎俊東), co-built Dongguan-based Canvest Environmental, a waste-to-energy plant operator, with his wife and chairlady Loretta Lee (Li Yongyi) and cousin Lai Kin Man. He led Canvest subsidiaries from 2007 and was an executive director from 2014; the group was taken private by Grandblue (瀚蓝环境) in a roughly US$1bn deal completed in 2025.
interesting_fact: Canvest grew into one of southern China's major waste-to-energy operators, burning municipal waste to generate power, and was bought out in 2025 by Foshan-based Grandblue Environment via a Cayman scheme of arrangement.
deep_cut_fact: He studied public administration at City University of Hong Kong (higher diploma, 1997), later earned an EMBA from South China University of Technology and a DBA from France's IPAG Business School (2018); he has been a director of Dongguan Rural Commercial Bank since 2009.
notes: Waste-to-energy is a strong fit for an energy podcast. Canvest is no longer listed and now sits under Grandblue, so the old IR email may be dormant; wife Loretta Lee (chairlady) was the public face. Hurun pinyin 'Li Jundong' = HK spelling Lai Chun Tung.

name: Zhang Jianming
profile: Hurun lists Zhang Jianming (张建明) as a real-estate entrepreneur behind 'MinYoung'. The name is very common in China, and I could not identify the company's Chinese name or find a source confirming his role.
notes: Ambiguous common name, and the company could not be identified from 'MinYoung'. His last Hurun appearance was 2021. Get the Chinese company name from Hurun's list page before any further research or outreach.

name: Dong Junzi
current_role: No current listed-company role found; former director and vice president of Yunnan Botanee Bio-Technology Group (SZSE: 300957), resigned March 2023
profile: Dong Junzi (董俊姿) co-founded Botanee, maker of China's leading sensitive-skin brand Winona (薇诺娜). She joined in 2012, was director and VP from 2019, and led Winona's marketing and online business through the 2021 ChiNext IPO. She resigned all posts in March 2023 for personal reasons, and her current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: After the March 2021 IPO, Botanee briefly became the A-share cosmetics company with the largest market value, driven by Winona, which supplied about 90% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: On Winona's rise she told CBNData: 'You have to do N things right to get to where we are today, not just one thing right.' On going global: 'Brands have no borders.'
notes: She left Botanee in 2023 and no current organisation or published contact was found. Botanee's IR email (ir@botanee.com) is not a route to her. On the Hurun U40 list (2021).

name: Jin Liwei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Coco Healthcare Products (可靠股份, SZSE: 301009); controlling shareholder
profile: Jin Liwei (金利伟, b. Nov 1970) founded Hangzhou Qiaozi Paper in 2001, later renamed Hangzhou Coco Healthcare, a maker of disposable hygiene products best known for its own 'Coco/可靠' adult-incontinence brand plus baby diapers and OEM pet pads. Coco listed on ChiNext in 2021; he controls it directly and through Hangzhou Qiaozhi Investment.
interesting_fact: Coco targets China's ageing-population market: its own brand focuses on adult diapers, pull-ups and care pads, and it set up what it calls the industry's first Zhejiang provincial key enterprise research institute for adult-incontinence care products.
deep_cut_fact: Before hygiene products he ran a car-repair business: general manager of Lin'an Qiaozi Auto Repair Co. (1999-2006), and the 'Qiaozi' (侨资) name carried into his first paper company in 2001.
notes: Low media profile. Route via IR email. Hurun listing only in 2021 (post-IPO peak); current wealth likely lower.

name: Liang Wanyun
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2020-2021) as a wealth holder via Foshan Haitian Flavouring & Food (603288.SH / 3288.HK)
profile: Appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2020-2021 with a fortune tied to Haitian, China's largest soy-sauce and condiment maker, which was bought out by its employees in 2007 and whose shares are largely held via Guangdong Haitian Group. She does not appear among Haitian's top-10 shareholders in the 2020 or 2025 annual reports, and no public profile was found.
interesting_fact: Haitian traces its roots to a group of 17th-century Foshan sauce factories, was bought out from the Foshan government by its employees in 2007, and is the world's largest soy-sauce maker; it added a Hong Kong listing in 2025.
notes: Likely an indirect shareholder via Guangdong Haitian Group or a family member of a Haitian manager - unconfirmed. No public footprint; only route is Haitian board office.

name: Wu Minzhi
current_role: Long-time Alibaba executive (former Group SVP, Chief Customer Officer and B2B president; former Alibaba Partner); current title not confirmed
profile: Wu Minzhi (Sophie Wu) joined Alibaba.com in November 2000 as a salesperson and rose through regional sales GM and supplier-services VP to president of the B2B business group / wholesale marketplaces. From 2017 she was Alibaba Group's Chief Customer Officer and SVP, and an Alibaba Partner; she is not on the slimmed-down 2025 partner list and her current role is unclear.
interesting_fact: She came up through Alibaba's legendary 'China Gold Supplier' direct-sales force (the so-called 中供铁军), selling Gold Supplier and TrustPass memberships before eventually running the whole B2B business.
deep_cut_fact: After almost two decades at Alibaba she spoke at CEIBS (2018) as Alibaba Partner, Chief Customer Officer and Group SVP — a role created in 2017 to champion customer experience across all of Alibaba's businesses.
notes: Low public profile since ~2019; check Alibaba's latest annual report (20-F) for current status. Not to be confused with unrelated 'Min Zhi Wu' board members on MarketScreener. Route via Alibaba corporate IR/communications.

name: Chen Bangrui
current_role: Chairman and co-actual controller (with Xu Xiaohe), Zhejiang Tenchen Controls Co., Ltd. (天成自控, SSE: 603085)
profile: Chen Bangrui (b. 1963) controls Zhejiang Tenchen Controls with Xu Xiaohe. The company traces its seat-making roots to 1984 and listed in Shanghai in 2015 as a maker of construction-machinery, commercial-vehicle and farm-machinery seats. It has since moved into passenger-car seats (from 2016) and aircraft seating. Chen remains chairman; Chen Yun runs the business as general manager.
interesting_fact: Tenchen went from tractor and excavator seats into aviation by buying a UK aircraft-seat maker (Acro Aircraft Seating). It now holds Boeing and Airbus supplier qualifications and aims to become a top-three global aircraft-seat and cabin-interiors supplier.
notes: Hurun lists him jointly with Xu Xiaohe. Little personal biography is published. Board secretary 林武威 (per cninfo). Company swung to a small loss in 2024 despite revenue growth.

name: Xu Xiaohe
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Chen Bangrui) of Zhejiang Tiancheng Controls (天成自控, 603085.SH); 49% owner of holding company Tiancheng Ketou
profile: Xu Xiaohe (spelled 许筱荷 in company filings; Hurun lists 徐筱荷) and her husband, chairman Chen Bangrui, are the ultimate controllers of Tiancheng Controls, a Shanghai-listed seat maker for passenger cars (including NEVs), construction machinery and commercial vehicles, and commercial aircraft. She holds 49% of controlling shareholder Tiancheng Ketou; Chen holds 51%.
interesting_fact: Tiancheng supplies seats to Caterpillar, Sany and XCMG excavators, builds airline passenger seats for carriers such as Jet2, Air New Zealand, Saudia and Etihad, and is developing seats for eVTOL air taxis.
notes: Name discrepancy: filings use 许筱荷 (Xu, 'allow' character) as Chen Bangrui's spouse; same person as Hurun's 徐筱荷. No executive role or public profile found; husband is the public face. Filing also lists board secretary email wuwei.lin@tenchen.com, but irm@ is the designated IR address.

name: Yang Lu
current_role: Minority shareholder of Shanghai Qufeng International Trading (former controlling shareholder of Shanghai New Culture Media); no known executive role
profile: Yang Lu (female) appeared on the 2017 Hurun China list alongside Yang Zhenhua, founder and controller of Shanghai New Culture Media Group (300336.SZ), a film/TV and outdoor-advertising company. In 2017 she acquired 8.33% of Qufeng International, the company's controlling shareholder, with Yang Zhenhua holding 91.67%. New Culture was delisted from Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2023.
notes: Very low public profile; family relationship to Yang Zhenhua not stated in filings. The underlying listed company was delisted in 2023, so the Hurun wealth figure is likely stale. Shareholding source: New Culture 2017 annual report http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2018-04-23/1204679662.PDF

name: Liu Xiping
current_role: Shareholder and member of the controlling group of Beijing Watertek Information Technology (旋极信息, SZ:300324); wife of founder Chen Jiangtao
profile: Liu Xiping (刘希平) is the wife of Chen Jiangtao, the engineer who built Beijing Watertek, a ChiNext-listed provider of embedded-system testing, defence/aerospace electronics and tax-control IT products, listed in 2012. Her wealth (shared with Chen on Hurun 2019) comes from the couple's stake; she is a direct shareholder acting in concert with Chen rather than a company executive.
interesting_fact: Watertek's founder Chen Jiangtao (her husband) is an aerospace electronics engineer who worked at a PLA General Staff communications unit and the aerospace ministry's Third Academy before starting the business.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal bio published in filings. Only on Hurun 2019. Caution: the 2025 annual report shows the controlling shareholder's shares under pledge and judicial freeze, so wealth has likely fallen sharply; probably not a priority target. Web-search budget was exhausted mid-lane; research relied on cninfo filings.

name: Dan Craddock
current_role: Founder / Managing Director, Bramden Investments (Isle of Man family office of the DLA Group)
profile: Isle of Man-based Dan Craddock heads the DLA Group (IT consulting and software development) and in 2008 founded Bramden Investments as its private investment vehicle. Bramden backed litigation funder Vannin Capital, which Craddock chaired and which was later sold to Fortress. It also invests in finance, telecoms, tech, digital marketing and property.
interesting_fact: He appeared among the 25 richest people in UK tech in his late 30s, at an estimated £500m. Through Bramden he became an early large backer of third-party litigation funding via Vannin Capital, initially allocating about £25m a year.
notes: Very low public profile; the bramden.com site was inaccessible. Aggregator profiles (Crunchbase, MarketScreener) say he graduated from Loughborough University (1999), but this is unverified. Law Gazette covered the Vannin launch and sale: https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/news/funder-defies-litigation-market-uncertainty-with-vannin-acquisition/5101367.article

name: David Pearl
current_role: Founder and owner, Structadene Ltd / Pearl & Coutts (London property investment and agency)
profile: David Pearl (b. 1944, Luton) grew up in Stamford Hill and left school at 15. At 19 he founded Pearl & Coutts in 1965 as a letting agency, then bought properties at auction in Hackney and Islington. He later moved into Fitzrovia ('NoHo') and the West End through his holding company Structadene. The Sunday Times put his wealth at £456m in 2019. He is a vice president of Tottenham Hotspur.
interesting_fact: In 2007 he appeared on Channel 4's 'The Secret Millionaire', posing as a volunteer at Queen Alexandra Hospital in Portsmouth. He gave £50,000 to a volunteer and to stroke-rehabilitation and cancer-care groups.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he worked as a clothing packer and part-time casino croupier. One of his first properties came with an interest-free mortgage of £7 a week and he let it for £10. He is famously scruffy and once said he spent about £91 a year on clothes.
notes: An 'old school' operator who prefers handshake deals; low-key but has done TV. Born October 1944. The best route is a letter or call via Pearl & Coutts/Structadene head office in London. Companies House lists Structadene's directors if needed.

name: David Richwhite
current_role: Private investor; co-founder of Fay, Richwhite & Company (retired from active banking)
profile: New Zealand investment banker (b. 1948) who co-founded merchant bank Fay Richwhite with Sir Michael Fay in 1973. The firm advised on and co-invested in NZ privatisations (Bank of New Zealand, Telecom NZ, NZ Rail) and backed the consortium that formed UK rail-freight operator EWS. Based in Geneva 1998-2003, he now lives in London.
interesting_fact: With Michael Fay he bankrolled New Zealand's first three America's Cup challenges (1987, 1988 'Big Boat' KZ1, 1992), and they later gifted KZ1 to Auckland's maritime museum.
deep_cut_fact: In 1988 Fay and Richwhite took a team to San Francisco and won the One Ton Cup with the Bruce Farr-designed yacht 'Propaganda' (KZ 6161); he also co-owns Great Mercury Island off the Coromandel with Fay.
notes: Very private; no public office, website or social accounts found. Rail-freight and privatisation history may be a hook. Avoid the Winebox Inquiry topic.

name: Michael Cornish
current_role: Former chairman of Linpac (Louth, Lincolnshire packaging group); no current executive role found
profile: Michael (John) Cornish, b. c.1953, is the son of Evan Cornish, who founded Lincolnshire Packaging Co (later Linpac) in Louth in 1959. Michael became chairman in 1992 and led the family-controlled plastics/packaging, materials-handling and waste-container group; the family's stake was realised in the ~£860m sale to Montagu Private Equity in 2003. He was on Linpac Group's board until 2009.
interesting_fact: Linpac grew from a small Louth packaging business founded in 1959 into a multinational plastics-packaging group; the family sale netted Michael Cornish an estimated £203m.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Michael Cornish Charitable Trust (registered 2005), a Lincolnshire grant-maker supporting children's and local charities; it was wound down and removed from the register in January 2026.
notes: Very private; no public profile, website or social accounts found. Linpac board dates (2003-2009) per https://webb-site.com/dbpub/offsum.asp?p=62993. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source.

name: The Clarke family
profile: 'The Clarke family' appears on the Sunday Times Rich List as UK property investors (valued at about £500m in the 2016 property-investors table, with source of wealth simply 'Property'). The published lists give no company, region or founder name, so the family could not be identified with confidence.
notes: Ambiguous: candidates include the family of the late Sir Stanley Clarke (St Modwen Properties founder; son Simon Clarke was listed separately at ~£212m in a West Midlands list), but no source ties that family to this specific entry. Needs the full Sunday Times entry text to identify.

name: S Craig Lindner
current_role: Co-Chief Executive Officer and Director, American Financial Group (NYSE: AFG), Cincinnati
profile: S. Craig Lindner (71), son of AFG founder Carl Lindner Jr., has been Co-CEO of insurance holding company American Financial Group since January 2005 alongside his brother Carl H. Souche now pitches itself as 'AI application infrastructure for China's used-car industry': dealer-management SaaS (claimed ~90% share), OEM user-operation systems, a used-car B2B auction platform, inspection services and vehicle delivery.

name: Zhang Wendong
current_role: Founder and chairman, Edifier Technology Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002351)
profile: Beijing entrepreneur who founded audio maker Edifier in May 1996. Edifier went public in 2010, the first listed audio-speaker company in China, and now sells speakers and headphones in 70+ countries. Under his leadership Edifier bought Japanese electrostatic-headphone maker STAX (2011), invested in US planar-headphone maker Audeze (2016), and marked its 30th anniversary in 2026.
interesting_fact: Edifier acquired STAX, the storied Japanese maker of electrostatic 'earspeakers', in 2011, giving a Chinese speaker brand a foothold in the high-end audiophile market.
deep_cut_fact: Edifier's Airpulse hi-fi speaker brand was developed with veteran audio engineer Phil Jones, and its 2013 gaming sub-brand is called Hecate.
notes: Wikipedia gives the name as 'Wen Dong Zhang'. Role verification is thin because search quota ran out mid-lane; check his current title and the company's IR email in Edifier's latest SZSE annual report. Outreach would likely need to be in Chinese.

name: Zheng Tao
current_role: Chairman and core technical staff, Jiangsu Cnano Technology Co. (688116.SH). He stepped down as general manager in April 2026.
profile: Tao Zheng, a physicist trained in China and Canada, leads Cnano Technology in Zhenjiang, Jiangsu. Cnano is China's leading maker of carbon-nanotube conductive pastes, which raise conductivity and energy density in lithium-ion EV and storage batteries. It listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019. He holds about 7.6% of the company.
interesting_fact: Cnano is an energy-storage supply-chain company: its carbon-nanotube conductive agents go into lithium-ion cells for leading Chinese battery makers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cnano he was a research scientist at Bellcore/Telcordia (the former Bell Labs spin-off) and held management roles at Voltix Technology and A123 Systems, the MIT-born lithium-ion battery pioneer, including China-related work.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/battery podcast. Role change: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604291821744613_1.pdf. The career details come from a third-party (36kr) database, so confirm with the prospectus. No published email found; route via Cnano's board secretary or IR in the annual report on sse.com.cn.

name: Zhong Meihong
current_role: Director (audit committee member), Shenzhen Capchem Technology (300037.SZ); re-elected to 7th board Dec 2025
profile: Zhong Meihong (钟美红, b. 1967) is a chemical engineer and one of the six-person acting-in-concert controlling group of Capchem (新宙邦), a Shenzhen maker of lithium-battery electrolytes, capacitor chemicals and fluorochemicals. She was a director of the predecessor Shenzhen Capchem Chemical and rose to executive vice president before becoming a non-executive-style director in 2017. She holds about 6% of the company.
interesting_fact: Capchem is one of the world's leading suppliers of lithium-ion battery electrolyte, a key input for EVs and grid storage batteries.
deep_cut_fact: She graduated in chemical engineering from Xiangtan University in 1990 and began as production department head at Hunan Jinhai Chemical before joining Capchem's predecessor.
notes: Low public profile; chairman Qin Jiusan is the company spokesman. Energy-storage materials angle fits the podcast. Route via Capchem board secretary/IR.

name: Zhou Zhixu
current_role: Chairman (and core technical staff), 3PEAK Inc. / Sipu Microelectronics Technology (Suzhou), STAR Market 688536
profile: Zhou Zhixu (ZHIXU ZHOU, 周之栩), b. 1968 and a U.S. citizen, is an analog-chip engineer who co-founded Suzhou-based 3PEAK in 2008 after 13 years at Motorola/Freescale. 3PEAK designs signal-chain and power-management analog and mixed-signal ICs, listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020, and has no controlling shareholder. He moved from general manager to chairman and holds ~9.46M shares.
interesting_fact: 3PEAK reports no controlling shareholder and no actual controller, which is unusual for a Chinese chip company; its founders and engineers each hold minority stakes.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his BS, MS and PhD in electrical engineering all at Arizona State University. At Motorola/Freescale (1994-2007) he went from device and process R&D engineer to principal analog design engineer and senior member of the company's Science & Technology Advisory Board.
notes: Technical founder with a low media profile; English-speaking (U.S.-trained, U.S. citizen), which makes outreach easier. business@3peak.com is the company's general business inbox, not a press desk; the board secretary's office (Li Shuhuan) handles investor and media matters. Analog/power ICs are relevant to server power delivery.

deep_cut_fact: She and her husband set up Qingdao Shancheng (青岛善诚) together in Laoshan, Qingdao in August 2005 with RMB1m of capital, she putting in 40% and he 60%; his Liuhe culture motto was 'harmony, kindness, hard work, learning' (和、善、干、学).

name: Viktor Medvedchuk
current_role: Leader of the Moscow-based 'Another Ukraine' movement; former Ukrainian MP and Opposition Platform – For Life leader
profile: Ukrainian lawyer turned politician and businessman; head of President Kuchma's administration (2002-05) and later leader of the pro-Russian Opposition Platform – For Life. He was detained in Ukraine in 2022, handed to Russia in a September 2022 prisoner exchange, and has lived in Moscow since, facing multiple criminal cases in Ukraine.
interesting_fact: He was handed to Russia in the September 2022 prisoner exchange that also freed Azovstal defenders, and has lived in Moscow since, where he leads the 'Another Ukraine' movement.
notes: NOT a suitable podcast/outreach target: sanctioned politician facing treason and other charges in Ukraine (new suspicions 2026, pipeline-privatisation indictment March 2026). Wealth (Wikidata 2021) is largely frozen or seized. Recommend excluding.

name: Robert J Small
current_role: Managing Director, Berkshire Partners (leads its Stockbridge public-equity team); director of TransDigm Group since 2010 (reported Lead Independent Director)
profile: Rob Small joined Boston private-equity firm Berkshire Partners in 1992 after starting at Bain & Co., and has led its Stockbridge public-equity strategy since its 2007 founding. His deals include TransDigm, AmSafe, Hexcel, Electro-Motive Diesel, English Welsh & Scottish Railway and Party City; his TransDigm-linked holdings are valued around $600m+ in SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Berkshire's portfolio under his involvement spans rail and power-equipment assets such as Electro-Motive Diesel (locomotive engines) and the UK freight railway EWS, alongside aerospace supplier TransDigm.
deep_cut_fact: He has led Berkshire's Stockbridge team since its founding in 2007; he holds a B.A. from Yale and an MBA from Harvard Business School and began his career at Bain & Co.
notes: Low-profile investor; no personal social accounts found. Lead Independent Director title comes from third-party sites — verify in TransDigm's proxy. Best route is via Berkshire Partners (Boston).

name: Lawrence T. Kennedy Jr
current_role: Managing Partner and CEO, Westwood Management; director (and 10% owner), Biodesix Inc. (NASDAQ: BDSX)
profile: Lawrence 'Lair' T. Kennedy Jr. is a Cincinnati-based healthcare entrepreneur and investor. He co-founded healthcare staffing firm Health Carousel, serving as CFO and then chairman, and now runs Westwood Management, a private investment and wealth-management firm. He joined the board and audit committee of lung-diagnostics company Biodesix in January 2023 and is a 10%+ holder.
interesting_fact: Biodesix described him as bringing 20+ years of operating, corporate finance, company-creation and investment experience in healthcare; he also sits on the boards of Healthcare for Kids, HC Locum, Revolution 4.0 and Health Carousel.
deep_cut_fact: He goes by 'Lair' and holds a BA from Colgate University and an MBA from Duke's Fuqua School of Business; he co-founded Health Carousel, a healthcare staffing and workforce-solutions company.
notes: Low public profile; contacts above are Biodesix's media/IR contacts from the Dec 2022 release and may be outdated. Wealth figure derives from SEC insider (10%-owner) holdings. No personal accounts found.

name: Brandon Lutnick
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Cantor Fitzgerald, L.P.; Chairman/CEO of the Cantor Equity Partners SPACs; director of BGC Group and Newmark
profile: Brandon Lutnick, born around 1998, took over Cantor Fitzgerald in 2025 when his father Howard Lutnick became US Commerce Secretary and moved his Cantor ownership into trusts for his adult children. His reported wealth comes from the family's insider stakes in Newmark, BGC and related entities. He runs Cantor's SPAC platform, which has taken Twenty One Capital (bitcoin) and tokenisation firm Securitize public.
interesting_fact: As chairman/CEO of Cantor Equity Partners he fronted some of 2025's biggest crypto SPAC deals, including Twenty One Capital with Tether and SoftBank, and Securitize, a tokenisation platform valued at $1.25bn.
deep_cut_fact: He studied Symbolic Systems (Stanford's interdisciplinary CS, linguistics, philosophy and psychology programme) and began his career as a credit analyst at Oak Hill Advisors. He joined Cantor in 2022 in equity sales and trading.

public_contacts.value: erica.chase@cantor.com (Cantor media contact listed on Cantor Equity Partners releases)

notes: He speaks at crypto and fintech conferences (e.g. Consensus 2025), which is the best public entry point. Route requests through Cantor media relations. The input lists him as a 10% owner of Newmark, GCM Grosvenor and others through family/Cantor entities. Newmark (commercial real estate) has data-center exposure.

name: J. Jonathan Ayers
current_role: Director of FB Financial Corp. (NYSE: FBK) and FirstBank; CEO of Ayers Asset Management, Inc.; President of Ayers Real Estate Services, LLC
profile: Jon Ayers, 54, is the son of FirstBank founder Jim Ayers, who built a rural West Tennessee bank bought in 1984 into Nashville-based FB Financial. He began his career at FirstBank, has been on its board since 2000 and FBK's since 2017, and co-executes his late father's estate, which owns ~13.6% of FBK. He runs the family's investment office and a commercial real-estate firm.
interesting_fact: FirstBank grew from a small rural West Tennessee bank Jim Ayers bought in 1984 into FB Financial, an NYSE-listed bank holding company with about $17.1bn in assets and 91 branches (Q3 2026).
deep_cut_fact: Besides banking, he has held executive roles at two private tech companies, Group Data Services and Pro-Accura. In 2016 he formed Ayers Real Estate Services to invest in and manage commercial real estate. He chairs FirstBank's Trust Committee.
notes: Not to be confused with Jonathan W. Ayers, ex-IDEXX CEO. His 10%-owner status reflects the family estate. Low profile; FBK media or IR contacts are the formal route, though he isn't an executive. 1984 purchase source: https://www.knoxtntoday.com/firstbank-founder-has-died/

name: Robert Mionis
current_role: President, CEO and (since May 2026) Board Chair, Celestica Inc. (NYSE/TSX: CLS); Director, Textron Inc.
profile: Rob Mionis has run Toronto-based Celestica since August 2015, steering the former contract electronics manufacturer into what it now calls 'a global leader in data center infrastructure', supplying AI/cloud networking switches, servers and storage to hyperscalers. The AI-driven rerating of Celestica stock produced his wealth. He became board chair in May 2026 and joined Textron's board in March 2025.
interesting_fact: Under Mionis, Celestica has repositioned around hyperscale data-center hardware (e.g. high-speed networking switches); its March 2026 release describes the company as 'a global leader in data center infrastructure and advanced technology solutions'.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at General Electric, rose to VP of Integrated Supply Chain at Honeywell Aerospace, ran aircraft-engine MRO firm StandardAero as CEO (2006-13), then spent 2013-15 as an operating partner at private-equity firm Pamplona Capital before Celestica.
notes: Highly relevant for a data-center podcast. Route via Celestica Global Communications (media@celestica.com).

name: Saria Tseng
current_role: Executive Vice President, Strategic Corporate Development, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, Monolithic Power Systems (NASDAQ: MPWR)
profile: Long-time MPS executive who joined as General Counsel in 2004 and has also run strategic corporate development since 2009. Her wealth comes from MPS equity as the power-semiconductor maker boomed on AI data-center power demand (Q3 2026 revenue $1.2B, +63% YoY).
interesting_fact: She has been at MPS for over two decades, through its growth from a mid-cap analog chipmaker into a top supplier of power-management chips for AI servers and data centers.
deep_cut_fact: She is admitted to the bar in California, New York and the Republic of China (Taiwan), holds LLMs from UC Berkeley and Taipei's Chinese Culture University, and came to MPS from storage-networking startup MaXXan Systems after working at Gray Cary and Jones Day.
notes: Corporate officer, not a founder; low public profile. Wealth figure is from SEC insider holdings. Best route is MPS investor relations / corporate communications. MPS moved HQ to West Palm Beach, FL.

current_role: Deceased (died April 1, 2025, aged 81); was founder, executive chairman and majority owner of FB Financial / FirstBank (Nashville)
profile: Jim Ayers founded FirstBank by buying Farmers State Bank in Scotts Hill, Tennessee in 1984 and grew it into Tennessee's largest locally headquartered bank (NYSE: FBK, 2016). He died on April 1, 2025.
notes: Deceased April 2025 (sources: https://news.vumc.org/2025/04/03/vumc-mourns-the-passing-of-noted-businessman-and-philanthropist-jim-ayers/ , https://www.newschannel5.com/news/tennessee-businessman-firstbank-founder-jim-ayers-dies). Stake now held via estate/family entities; skip.

profile: Chen Dakui built Zhejiang Zhongcheng, founded in 2001 in Jiashan, Zhejiang and listed in Shenzhen, into a large maker of plastic packaging film and sheet (heat-shrink film). He held about 39% in 2020. In 2021 he agreed to sell about 25% to Changde Urban Development Group, which made the Changde government's SASAC the actual controller, and he has continued to sell down since.

name: Zhu Chongyun
current_role: Controlling owner (~98.5%) of Shenzhen Enqing Investment Development; co-owner of Marisfrolg (Shenzhen Mases Fashion) with husband Yao Jianhua
profile: Zhu Chongyun (朱崇恽, b. 1964) and her husband Yao Jianhua built Shenzhen high-end womenswear house Marisfrolg (玛丝菲尔) plus restaurant and property interests, and became some of China's best-known private A-share 'super investors'. Through Enqing Investment they hold stakes in listed firms such as Youngor (long-time), Fortior Tech, Bolong Technology and, from 2025, Ping An Bank (~RMB1bn position).

deep_cut_fact: Before fashion and investing she was an engineer: a Zhejiang University mechanical and electrical engineering graduate who worked at the Zhejiang Metallurgical Research Institute and then Shenzhen Changli Silk Products, where her husband also worked.

name: Liu Shui
current_role: Founder and former chairman/controller of Shenzhen Techand Ecology (now CECEP Techand, 300197.SZ); no current listed-company role
profile: Born 1969 in Meizhou, Guangdong, Liu Shui studied physical geography at Peking University, worked in turf/lawn-engineering firms, and in 2001 co-founded Techand Ecology, which grew into a major Chinese ecological restoration and landscaping contractor listed on ChiNext in 2011. Control later passed to state-owned China Energy Conservation and Environmental Protection Group (CECEP), and the company is now chaired by He Liang.
interesting_fact: He picked the company name Techand (铁汉, 'iron man') himself and coined its slogan 铮铮铁汉，顶天立地 ('an iron man, standing tall between heaven and earth').
deep_cut_fact: A Hakka from Meizhou who attended the city's Dongshan Middle School, he was named from a family phrase: his parents named their four children Liu Xi, Liu Shui, Liu Chang and Liu Qing after 溪水长情 ('streams flow with lasting affection').
notes: No longer controls the company. Per a May 2026 report the Shenzhen Stock Exchange barred him for three years from serving as a listed-company director over related-party fund occupation (https://caifuhao.eastmoney.com/news/20260507100153176423950); Hurun wealth figure is likely stale. Approach with caution.

name: Rao Luhua
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Shenzhen Clou Electronics (002121.SZ); no longer in control (Midea Group took control in 2023)
profile: Rao Luhua founded Clou Electronics in Shenzhen in 1996. It listed in 2007 and grew into a supplier of smart electricity meters and grid equipment and an early mover in grid-scale battery energy storage. After heavy losses in 2018-19, control passed to Shenzhen state capital and then, in 2023, to Midea Group.

current_role: Co-founder and Honorary Vice Chairman, Jointown Pharmaceutical Group (九州通, SSE 600998), Wuhan (not a director since 2020)

It grew into China's largest private pharmaceutical distributor and listed in Shanghai in 2010. He was vice chairman until 2020, when the founders left the board for honorary titles to make way for a new generation of management, and he remains a shareholder.

name: Zhu Baoliang
current_role: Head of Honglou Group (红楼集团, Hangzhou); with family/Honglou the controlling shareholder group of Lishang Guochao (丽尚国潮, SSE: 600738, formerly Lanzhou Minbai)
profile: Zhu Baoliang (朱宝良) built Hangzhou-based Honglou Group, which spans department stores and retail, real estate and investment. Through Honglou he acquired control of Lanzhou Minbai (now Lishang Guochao), a Lanzhou department-store operator, folding in Honglou retail assets in a 2017 restructuring.
