notes: Co-listed with Hong Yidan (spouse). Low public profile; web-search budget exhausted, so personal background was not researched further. 2025 annual report shows his directly held shares as frozen - sensitive.

name: Lin Hao
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller, Beijing VRV Software Corp. (北信源, SZSE: 300352; trading as 'ST信源' in 2026)
profile: Lin Hao (林皓) founded Beijing VRV Software in 1996 and took it public on ChiNext in 2012. VRV began with the 'VRV Virus Killer' antivirus, then became China's long-time market leader in endpoint/intranet security management, and since 2013 has built Linkdood (信源密信), a secure messaging platform used by government, defence units and SOEs. In 2026 he is pushing overseas expansion via Malaysia and AI+secure communications.
interesting_fact: He says he proposed the concept of 'intranet security' (内网安全) in 2003, about a decade before the industry caught on, and that he 'lays out one big thing every ten years'.
deep_cut_fact: VRV's first product, 'VRV病毒克星' (VRV Virus Killer), made it one of China's first-generation antivirus companies alongside Jiangmin; Lin describes his management style as a 'nail-man' (钉子人) spirit of digging deep in one field.
notes: Stock is under special treatment ('ST信源') in 2026 – avoid raising this. Gives media interviews on cybersecurity/secure comms (2023 finet, 2026 科创中国).

name: Zhang Xiaojun
current_role: Chairman & GM, Suzhou Zhengxin Xinye Holding Group; executive director of Suzhou Changfeng Electric and Yida Electric (Suzhou); director of 3PEAK (思瑞浦) 2012-Jan 2025
profile: Zhang Xiaojun (章晓军, b. 1965) is a Suzhou electrical-equipment entrepreneur (switchgear makers Changfeng Electric and Yida Electric) who backed analog-chip designer 3PEAK from its founding in 2012 and sat on its board until January 2025. 3PEAK listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020, which put him on the 2021 Hurun China list. He holds no shares directly, implying indirect ownership.
interesting_fact: 3PEAK, the analog/mixed-signal chip company he backed from day one, has grown to 3,200+ products sold to 8,000+ customers in 20+ countries, with 300+ automotive-grade chips in volume production.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in China's switchgear heartland: from 1992 to 1996 he was operating factory manager at the Yueqing Zhongya Switch Factory (Yueqing, Zhejiang) before moving to Suzhou and running Changfeng Electric from 1997.
notes: Low-profile investor, not a 3PEAK founder-operator; he left 3PEAK's board in Jan 2025, so 3PEAK IR is only an indirect route. No personal or holding-company contact found. 'Alive' marked unknown: no recent news found, though nothing indicates otherwise. Last Hurun appearance 2021.

name: Gao Yuankun
current_role: Chairman and president, Linuo Group (Jinan); actual controller and director of Shandong Linuo Pharmaceutical Packaging (301188.SZ)
profile: Gao Yuankun (高元坤, b. 1958) has led Jinan-based Linuo Group since 1997, building it into a conglomerate spanning solar thermal and PV, pharmaceutical glass packaging and pharmaceuticals. current_role: Co-founding shareholder and former director of Risen Energy (东方日升, SZSE 300118); no current role found

profile: This Sunday Times Rich List 2020 entry ('Lingerie, Property and Football', shared with Vanessa Gold) is the Gold family: Ann Summers executive chair Jacqueline Gold and her father David Gold (ex-West Ham co-chairman), garbled into 'Jacqueline David'. Jacqueline Gold died on 16 March 2023, aged 62; David Gold died in January 2023.
notes: Deceased (Jacqueline Gold d. 16 March 2023 per Wikipedia; David Gold d. Jan 2023). Surviving family member on the entry is Vanessa Gold (Ann Summers/Gold Group). Skip or re-target to Vanessa Gold.

name: Vanessa Gold
current_role: Chair, Ann Summers (since July 2023); chair and 25.1% shareholder, West Ham United (sole chair since June 2026)
profile: Born 1967, daughter of the late David Gold. She worked her way up the family's Gold Group (Ann Summers, Knickerbox, property, Gold Air) from her teens, becoming joint MD and later CEO of Ann Summers. After the deaths of her sister Jacqueline and her father in 2023 she became Ann Summers chair and West Ham joint chair. In 2026 she agreed a provisional sale of the family's 25.1% West Ham stake.
interesting_fact: In August 2026 she agreed in principle to sell the Gold family's 25.1% West Ham stake to a consortium led by Amanda Staveley and PCP Capital Partners for a reported ~£150m. This followed an earlier June deal with Daniel Křetínský's EP Group.
deep_cut_fact: She started at Ann Summers as a teenager and rose to joint managing director and CEO before becoming chair. She has worked alongside her family in the business for decades rather than joining from outside.
notes: Do not reference her sister's or father's deaths. Stake-sale figures come from a fan-analysis blog, so check them with club statements. No published personal contact; routes are the West Ham United club media office or Ann Summers corporate (Gold Group House, Whyteleafe). Listing is shared with the family (David, Jacqueline).

name: Richard Harpin
current_role: Founder, Growth Partner (investor in founder-led UK businesses); owner of Business Leader; HomeServe founder (chairman until 2025)
profile: Sir Richard Harpin co-founded HomeServe in 1993 with a reported £50,000, built it into a FTSE company that bought Checkatrade, and sold it to Brookfield for £4.1bn in 2023, staying chairman until 2025. He now backs founder-led brands via Growth Partner, owns Business Leader and wrote the 2025 bestseller 'How to Make a Billion in Nine Steps'.
interesting_fact: His childhood dream, sparked at age four watching a helicopter land behind a neighbour's wall, was to own one — he later learned to fly and bought a helicopter and a plane.
deep_cut_fact: Aged nine he performed children's magic shows as 'Riccardo, the famous magician of the North' for 50p a show, and at 12 ran a mail-order business selling handmade fishing lures from a shed at his family home in Northumberland.
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly: Sunday Times business columnist, author, mentor to founders — strong podcast candidate. Publisher is Little, Brown (Hachette) — book publicity team is another route.

name: Yadupati Singhania
current_role: Deceased (13 Aug 2020); formerly Chairman & Managing Director, JK Cement Ltd
profile: Yadupati Singhania, an IIT Kanpur graduate and long-time CMD of JK Cement (Kanpur), died in Singapore after a brief illness on 13 August 2020. JK Cement is now led by his son Madhav Krishna Singhania. Remaining fields skipped per instructions.
notes: Died 13 Aug 2020 (source: Construction World). For outreach on JK Cement, the current leadership is Madhav Krishna Singhania (CEO/Deputy MD).

name: Meher Pudumjee
current_role: Chairperson, Thermax Ltd (Pune; energy and environment engineering)
profile: Meher Pudumjee is the second-generation leader of Thermax, the Pune-based Indian maker of boilers, heating and cooling systems, waste-heat and renewable-energy equipment, and water and air-pollution solutions. She joined in 1990 as a trainee engineer, became vice chairperson in 2002 during the company's turnaround, and succeeded her mother Anu Aga as chairperson in October 2004. Under her, Thermax has pushed into clean energy.
interesting_fact: Business Standard named her 'CEO of the Year' in 2009 for growing Thermax while keeping its ethical standards. She credits her father Rohinton Aga's advice: 'play to express and not to impress.'
deep_cut_fact: A chemical-engineering postgraduate of Imperial College London, she was sent with her husband Pheroz in 1991, a year after joining as a trainee, to turn around Thermax's UK subsidiary. Outside work she loves Western classical music and sings in a Pune-based choir.
notes: A strong fit for an energy podcast, since Thermax works on industrial decarbonisation, renewables and green hydrogen. She speaks at forums such as UNCTAD's World Investment Forum. Approach through Thermax corporate communications or the company secretary (Sangeet Hunjan, per 2026 filings). Family wealth is shared with mother Anu Aga.

name: Satyanarayan Nandlal Nuwal
current_role: Chairman, Solar Industries India Ltd (Nagpur)
profile: Founder and chairman of Nagpur-based Solar Industries India, which grew from industrial explosives for mining into a technology-led explosives, initiating-systems and defence group serving 90+ countries. FY2025-26 revenue rose 30% to Rs 9,838 crore with PAT of Rs 1,737 crore; his son Manish Nuwal is MD & CEO.
interesting_fact: Solar's defence arm, Solar Industries and Aerospace, became the first private-sector company in India to dispatch Pinaka Enhanced Mark I rocket systems to the Indian Army.
deep_cut_fact: He received the Padma Shri from the President of India in 2026; at Solar's 31st AGM he said he accepted it 'on behalf of every member of the Solar family' (about 15,100 people).
notes: Commonly spelled Nuwal (input says 'Nuwa'). Hurun figure (2015-16, $588M) is badly stale; Solar's market value has grown many-fold since. Explosives/defence rather than energy, though mining-explosives tie in to energy/coal. Web search budget ran out; facts drawn from company AGM transcript.

name: Will Roseff
current_role: Director of bet365 Group Ltd (Stoke-on-Trent) since September 2001
profile: William Wolfe 'Will' Roseff, born 1951, is a long-serving board director and early backer of bet365, the Coates family's Stoke-on-Trent online betting company. His fortune reportedly rests on a minority bet365 stake (one source says ~6.7%). The Sunday Times Rich List put him at £579m (254th) in 2025 and ~£591m (239th) in 2026.
interesting_fact: He is the lowest-ranked of the gambling-industry names on the Sunday Times Rich List but one of only a handful of non-Coates individuals to have built a fortune on bet365.
deep_cut_fact: Companies House records show him appointed a director of bet365 Group on 25 September 2001, among its earliest board members in the year the online sportsbook launched. He remains an active director.
notes: Very private, with no interviews, social accounts or published personal contact found. bet365 publishes no press email; the only route is a formal letter to bet365 Group Ltd, Bet365 House, Media Way, Stoke-on-Trent ST1 5SZ (registered office per Companies House). Gambling is a sensitive topic for some podcast audiences. Some outlets spell his name 'Rosseff'.

name: CV Jacob
current_role: Deceased (died 31 Jan 2021); was founder-chairman of Synthite Group, Kolenchery, Kerala
profile: C.V. Jacob founded Synthite in 1972 after two decades in civil construction, building it into a major producer of spice oleoresins and natural extracts. He died at home near Kolenchery on 31 January 2021, aged 87-88. His son Dr Viju Jacob is managing director of Synthite Industries.
notes: Deceased (sources: https://www.onmanorama.com/news/kerala/2021/01/31/synthite-group-chairman-cv-jacob-dies.html ; https://www.thenewsminute.com/kerala/veteran-industrialist-and-synthite-group-founder-cv-jacob-passes-away-kochi-142524). The business is now run by MD Dr Viju Jacob; https://synthite.com is the company site if the family business is of interest.

name: Martin Hughes
current_role: Founder and CEO, Toscafund Asset Management (London)
profile: Martin Hughes is a 'Tiger cub' who founded London-based Toscafund in 2000 after running Julian Robertson's Tiger Management Europe. Known for concentrated, activist bets on UK companies and financials, Toscafund took TalkTalk private in a £1.1bn deal (2020), is a major investor in Circle Health, and its website now carries a recommended offer for Spire Healthcare.
interesting_fact: The Times nicknamed him 'the Rottweiler' for his combative activism, e.g. a long campaign to oust Speedy Hire's chairman over governance failings.
deep_cut_fact: He was a top-ranked UK banking analyst in the early 1990s and deputy chief executive of Credit Lyonnais Laing Securities; he began broking for Julian Robertson in 1988, years before Robertson invited him to set up and chair Tiger Management Europe.
notes: Toscafund site is gated behind a professional-investor disclaimer; no published press email found. Do not confuse with BBC presenter/other Martin Hughes (some aggregator bios mix them up). Healthcare (Circle, Spire) and telecom (TalkTalk) angles.

name: Richard Koch
current_role: Author and private investor (author of The 80/20 Principle)
profile: Richard Koch (b. 1950, London; Oxford and Wharton MBA) worked at BCG and was a Bain partner before co-founding L.E.K. Consulting in 1983. He left consulting at 39 to write and invest, backing or founding more than 20 companies including Filofax, Plymouth Gin, Belgo, Betfair, FanDuel and Auto1. He is best known for The 80/20 Principle (1997).
interesting_fact: The 80/20 Principle has sold more than a million copies in over 30 languages; his 'Star Principle' investment approach targets high-growth leaders of niche markets, an approach behind his early Betfair stake.
deep_cut_fact: In 2024 his Oxford college, Wadham, made him a Visiting Fellow. He also helped rescue Filofax from near-collapse before Betfair, and wrote the foreword to Perry Marshall's '80/20 Sales and Marketing'.
notes: Very accessible, media-friendly author who has done many podcasts (e.g. Tim Ferriss). His site lists an email hidden behind JavaScript (not captured), so use the site or LinkedIn/X. A good fit for an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Tim Kemp
current_role: Co-founder and owner, Firmdale Hotels / The Firmdale Group (London & New York boutique hotels)
profile: Tim Kemp co-founded Firmdale Hotels with his wife, designer Kit Kemp, opening Dorset Square in 1985; he is the property developer and 'number cruncher' while Kit leads design. Firmdale now runs boutique hotels in London (Ham Yard, The Soho, Haymarket, Covent Garden, Charlotte Street and others) and New York (Crosby Street, The Whitby), plus Grade A Soho office buildings.
interesting_fact: Like many boutique pioneers, the Kemps were turned down by 14 banks before securing funding for their first hotel, Dorset Square, in 1985; Firmdale later won the Queen's Award for Enterprise (2000).
deep_cut_fact: Before hotels, Tim was a property developer running student accommodation in West London; he met Kit in the 1970s when he was a client of architect Leszek Nowicki, whose office she worked in.
notes: Tim is far less public than Kit Kemp (who has her own site kitkemp.com and does most interviews); Firmdale PR is the realistic route. Contact page also lists a property-development department (pd@firmdale.com) relevant to his role.

name: Kit Kemp
current_role: Co-founder and Creative Director, Firmdale Hotels; founder, Kit Kemp Design Studio
profile: British interior designer (MBE) who co-founded Firmdale Hotels with husband Tim Kemp in 1985, starting with the Dorset Square Hotel; the group now runs eleven boutique luxury hotels in London and New York (e.g. Ham Yard, Crosby Street). She designs all the interiors and runs the Kit Kemp Design Studio, a homewares shop and product collaborations.
interesting_fact: She has no formal design training: before hotels she worked for an auctioneer, a Greek shipping company's office and then architect Leszek Nowicki, whose practice is where she met Tim Kemp.
deep_cut_fact: She champions Fine Cell Work, the charity founded by Lady Anne Tree in 1997 that trains prisoners in skilled needlework, commissioning prisoner-made pieces as part of her design collaborations; she has also written four design books, from A Living Space (2012) to Design Secrets (2021).
notes: Wealth shared with husband Tim Kemp. Hospitality/design focus; less obvious fit for energy/data-center themes but strong entrepreneur story.

name: Tom Chapman
current_role: Co-founder, ABASK (luxury craft and homeware e-commerce, London); angel investor via his family office, the Chapman Office
profile: Tom Chapman OBE (b. 1963, Wimbledon) co-founded MatchesFashion with his wife Ruth in 1987 as a single Wimbledon Village boutique, took it online in 2007 and sold it to Apax in 2017 for an estimated £400m. Since then he has been an early-stage investor through his family office and in 2022 co-founded ABASK with Nicolas Pickaerts, an online platform for artisan-made design objects.
interesting_fact: The Chapmans built one of the world's leading luxury e-commerce businesses from one small independent shop in Wimbledon Village; both were made OBEs in the 2020 New Year Honours for services to international fashion retail.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into fashion retail, Chapman trained in hotel and hospitality management (Harper's Bazaar, 2018).
notes: Best route is ABASK press office. He gives occasional angel-investor interviews (Sunday Times Q&A 2019). Avoid dwelling on Matches' 2024 administration under later owners. The Wikipedia article carries an 'undisclosed paid editing' tag; the hospitality-training detail cites Harper's Bazaar Australia (Feb 2018).

name: Ruth Chapman
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO/joint chair of MATCHESFASHION (exited; the business went into administration in 2024)
profile: Ruth Chapman OBE (b. 1961, Wirral) and her husband Tom opened a single boutique in Wimbledon in 1987. They grew it into the global luxury e-tailer MATCHESFASHION.COM, launching the website in 2007. They stepped back to joint chairs in 2015 and sold to Apax in 2017 in a deal valuing the company at over $1bn.
interesting_fact: After the 2007 website launch, which she has called a 'seismic moment', the business grew by up to 100% a year. It ended up selling 450+ brands to 176 countries, with 95% of sales online.
deep_cut_fact: Before Matches she worked at Jaeger, at Harrods and at a video production company. She met Tom at 21, and he persuaded her to leave her job to help run his fashion boutique. From 2013 to 2017 she sat on the British Fashion Council's NEWGEN panel scouting young designers.
notes: Appointed OBE in 2020 with Tom, and they won the 2017 Drapers Lifetime Achievement award. Tom co-founded the homeware platform Abask (2022), which may be a route to the couple. No personal published contact found.

name: Charlotte Townshend
current_role: Owner of the Ilchester Estates (Melbury House and the Abbotsbury estate, Dorset)
profile: The Hon. Charlotte Townshend is a daughter of the 9th Viscount Galway. Through her mother Theresa Fox-Strangways, heiress of the 7th Earl of Ilchester, she inherited the Ilchester/Strangways estates in Dorset, about 15,000 acres. They include Grade I-listed Melbury House, much of Abbotsbury village, part of Chesil Beach, the Abbotsbury Swannery and the Subtropical Gardens. Her wealth is landed inheritance.
interesting_fact: Her estate owns the Abbotsbury Swannery, which the Strangways family has held for 15 generations since the Dissolution. Probably set up by Benedictine monks in the 11th century and recorded since 1393, it is described as the only managed swannery in the world, with about 600 swans.
deep_cut_fact: Melbury House has been the Strangways family seat since about 1500. Its signature hexagonal tower with banks of tall arched windows was built by Sir Giles Strangways after 1546, using Ham stone from a quarry nine miles away.
notes: A private landowner with no personal public channels. The best route is a letter via the Ilchester Estates office in Dorset or the Abbotsbury tourism business. The estate's website (ilchesterestates.co.uk) was unreachable from this sandbox, so no published contact was verified. The web-search budget ran out before this person, so the profile relies on Wikipedia.

name: Tang Qiaolian
current_role: Unconfirmed – listed by Hurun (2007-2016) with 'Wuxin Yufu' (financial services)
profile: Hurun listed Tang Qiaolian (汤巧莲) with financial-services firm 'Wuxin Yufu'. Searches in Chinese and English found no matching company or biography, so identity and current status could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity not confirmed; off rich lists since 2016. Kept minimal.

name: Tian Tongbao
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun 2017-2018 under Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团)
profile: Hurun linked Tian Tongbao (田同宝, ~US$580m) to Zhongrong Xinda Group, the Qingdao-based coke and chemicals group (formerly Shandong Coking Group) controlled by Wang Qingtao. No Zhongrong Xinda filing found naming him as a shareholder or officer.
notes: Tried: web searches 田同宝 + 中融新大/Zhongrong Xinda; cninfo full-text search for 田同宝 (only hits: Laiwu Steel 2003-04 reports naming a 田同宝 as accounting supervisor - possibly a different person, no link proven); Zhongrong Xinda 2016 bond prospectus and 2015 annual report (directors and shareholders) - not listed. Group entered bankruptcy restructuring in 2023 (https://hao.cnyes.com/post/49387). Low priority.

name: Chen Zaixi
current_role: Founder/patriarch of the Dynavolt (猛狮) battery group; as of 2015, chairman & GM of Guangdong Dynavolt (Mengshi) Industrial Group. Current role unverified.
profile: Chen Zaixi (陈再喜, b. 1945) built a lead-acid battery business from Chenghai, Shantou, through the Humei battery factory and Guangdong Mengshi Industrial Group. His son Chen Lewu co-founded Guangdong Dynavolt Power Technology (猛狮科技, 002684.SZ) in 2001, and it listed in 2012. The company later moved into lithium batteries and new energy but ran into heavy debt and was delisted in 2022.
interesting_fact: Dynavolt pivoted from motorcycle and lead-acid batteries to lithium-ion. Around 2017-2019 it announced 6 GWh lithium-battery bases in Fujian and Hubei and a 5 GWh plant planned in Henan.
deep_cut_fact: He started work in 1962 in his home village brigade of Pumei, Chenghai. He moved through village-run handicraft, building-materials and plastics factories before working at the Chenghai Humei storage-battery factory, the seed of the family's battery empire.
notes: He would be about 81 now. I found no recent news and could not confirm whether he is alive. The listed company (猛狮科技) was delisted in 2022 after debt problems and an SZSE public reprimand, so the topic is sensitive. Family members (Chen Lewu) were the public faces. No published contacts were found.

name: Han Chang'an
current_role: Controlling shareholder (with his brother) of Shanxi Lubao Group, a coking/coal-chemicals conglomerate in Lucheng, Changzhi, Shanxi (title not confirmed)
profile: Shanxi coal-and-coke entrepreneur who, with his brother, controls Lubao Group, a long-standing member of China's top-500 private companies and parent of Lubao Coking; Chinese press describes him as Changzhi's richest man. He appeared on the Hurun China list 2006-2012.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Lubao Coking teamed up with Hebei's Puyang Steel in a consortium that won the RMB 14.9 billion bid for Jinliu Energy, the restructured owner of nine prime coking-coal mines formerly held by Lian Sheng Group in Liulin County.
notes: Very private; no official biography or published contact found (web-search budget ran out before a Lubao Group website could be located). The Jinliu acquisition later became a shareholder lawsuit - avoid. Alive status not explicitly confirmed; Jiemian reporting refers to him as a current controller.

name: Liu Yongyan
current_role: Founder/chairman, Continental Hope Group (大陆希望集团), Chengdu (current status not confirmed)
profile: Eldest of Sichuan's four Liu brothers (with Liu Yongxing, Liu Yongmei and Liu Yonghao), who started a quail farm in 1982 and built Hope Group, China's first state-approved private enterprise group, with him as board chairman. After the 1995 split he founded Continental Hope; last on Hurun's China list in 2012.
interesting_fact: In 1995 the four Liu brothers, with a combined RMB 600 million, topped the very first Forbes China rich list; they were No. 1 on both Forbes and Hurun China lists again in 2001.
deep_cut_fact: In 1982, after a bank refused them a RMB 1,000 loan, he and his three brothers sold their belongings to raise the 1,000 yuan to start the Yuxin breeding farm in Guji village, Xinjin county; by 1986 it was producing 150,000 quail a year.
notes: Very low profile and off the rich lists since 2012; could not confirm he is alive or still active (web search budget ran out before further checks). Continental Hope's current business, including the 'Energy' industry tag in the input, was not verified. No published contacts found.

name: Wang Hairong
current_role: Unknown; Hurun lists him as owner of 'Haixin' (海新), a petrochemicals business HQ'd in Yueyang, Hunan
profile: Hurun's 2016-2021 lists name Wang Hairong (王海荣, b. Oct 1969 in Golmud, Qinghai; residence Langfang, Hebei) as the owner of 'Haixin' (海新), a petrochemicals company based in Yueyang, Hunan (Langfang in 2018), worth ~RMB2.5-4bn. The operating company behind 'Haixin' could not be identified in filings or news.
notes: Hurun record (birth date, birthplace, HQ) via hurun.net list API. Tried: web searches for 王海荣 + 海新/海鑫/岳阳/石化/董事长/胡润; cninfo full-text (王海荣 + 石化/董事长/三聚环保); checked whether 'Haixin' = Beijing Haixin Energy (海新能科, ex-三聚环保, 300072) - no link found, and that firm is state-controlled. Likely an unlisted private refiner/trader; a company-registry lookup (gsxt.gov.cn) for 海新 entities in Yueyang would be the next step.

name: Zhu Shanyin
current_role: Vice Chairman, Zhejiang Weiming Environment Protection Co., Ltd. (伟明环保, SSE: 603568), Wenzhou
profile: Co-founder and one of the four actual controllers, under a concerted-action agreement, of Weiming Environment Protection, a Wenzhou-based builder and operator of municipal waste-to-energy incineration plants. He was a vice president from 2005 and a director from 2014 to 2023, and is now vice chairman. Weiming is also expanding into new-energy materials and equipment.
interesting_fact: Weiming is one of China's main private waste-to-energy operators. It burns municipal garbage to generate power and still wins new incineration-power project tenders in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: Zhu's career began in machinery, not garbage. He was deputy general manager of a light-industry machinery factory from 1985 to 1998, then executive deputy GM of an environmental engineering company (1999-2005) before joining Weiming's leadership.
notes: Chairman and president Xiang Guangming is the company's main public face. Zhu is a significant shareholder (about 54M shares directly as of mid-2026). The career details come from the director bios in the 2025 annual report, which are matched to names by table order; re-check before quoting. Outreach in Chinese via the IR/board-office email.

name: Zhang Huanong
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Shenzhen Center Power Tech Co. (雄韬股份, SZSE: 002733)
profile: Battery engineer who founded Shenzhen Center Power Tech ('Vision' brand) in 1994 and controls ~36% of it. The company makes sealed lead-acid batteries, lithium-ion and sodium-ion batteries and hydrogen fuel cells. He also chairs/serves in several battery industry associations; since 2025 day-to-day management sits with director/rotating CEO He Tianlong.
interesting_fact: He received Hong Kong's Bauhinia Entrepreneur award in 2002 and a European battery-industry contribution award in 2004; he is supervisory chairman of the China Industrial Association of Power Sources and a distinguished professor at Harbin Institute of Technology (Shenzhen).
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 1984 as a supervising engineer in the technical department of the state-owned Wuhan Factory No. 752, then was chief engineer at Shenzhen battery maker Lupton (律普敦) from 1991-94 before founding Center Power in November 1994.
notes: Co-holder Xu Kerong is a company director. Board secretary: Liu Gang. Company website unreachable during research and no press email verified; IR via SZSE annual report contact or cninfo interactive platform. Web search budget exhausted; bio from 10jqka executive profile.

name: Xu Kerong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with Zhang Huanong) of Shenzhen Center Power Tech Co. / Vision Group (雄韬股份, SZSE: 002733); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Xu Kerong appears on Hurun China lists 2015-2021 jointly with Zhang Huanong as owners of Shenzhen Center Power Tech (Vision), founded in 1994 in Shenzhen and listed in 2014. Vision makes lead-acid, LFP lithium, sodium and hydrogen fuel-cell batteries for UPS/data-center, telecom, motive-power and grid-storage uses, selling in 100+ countries.
interesting_fact: Vision claims to be the world No.1 in LFP lithium UPS batteries and the top exporter of valve-regulated lead-acid batteries for 10 straight years; in 2026 it launched an 800V HVDC architecture and battery backup units (BBU) aimed at AI data centers, and has supplied a large Malaysian AI data center four times.
deep_cut_fact: Vision was among the first Chinese companies to build lead-acid and lithium battery factories overseas (Vietnam plant 2007, Vietnam lithium plant 2018) and among the first listed companies to invest in hydrogen, launching its fuel-cell unit Hydrogen Xiong in 2014.
notes: Very low personal profile; Zhang Huanong (chairman) is the public face. Strong data-center angle (UPS/BBU/HVDC for AI data centers). Deep-cut fact is about the company she co-owns, not her personally. Outreach via company.

name: Zhao Guoguang
current_role: Vice Chairman and General Manager (CEO), Bestechnic (Shanghai) Co. (恒玄科技, 688608.SH)
profile: Zhao Guoguang (b. 1977), a former RDA Microelectronics operations VP, co-founded Bestechnic in 2015 with Liang Zhang. Bestechnic makes low-power Bluetooth/Wi-Fi SoCs for earbuds, smartwatches, smart glasses and smart-home devices and listed on the STAR Market in 2020. He has been GM since 2022 and holds about 10%.
interesting_fact: Bestechnic's chips sit inside earbuds and smart devices from Samsung, OPPO, Xiaomi, Honor and vivo, audio brands such as Harman, Anker, Edifier and Shokz, and internet firms including Alibaba, Baidu, ByteDance and Google.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bestechnic he spent years at RDA Microelectronics, rising from design manager to operations director and then VP of operations. He was Bestechnic's first executive director and general manager (June 2015 to January 2016) before the company took its current shape.
notes: Source is the Bestechnic 2024 annual report. Chairman is Liang Zhang; Zhao is No. 2 and runs operations. Low personal media profile. Board director Tang Xiaodong is the company's PR director and is the formal press route.

name: Sir Ron Dennis
current_role: Former founder, chairman and CEO of McLaren Group (left 2017); private investor and philanthropist
profile: Sir Ron Dennis (b. 1947, Woking) rose from F1 mechanic to run McLaren's Formula One team (1981-2009), winning seven constructors' titles with drivers such as Lauda, Prost, Senna, Hakkinen and Hamilton. He built McLaren Group and founded McLaren Automotive (F1, P1 supercars), and co-owned TAG Heuer, before selling out of McLaren in 2017. He was knighted for services to industry and charity.
interesting_fact: He founded McLaren Cars, which produced the McLaren F1 (1992) - for years the world's fastest production car - as well as the Mercedes SLR and P1 hybrid hypercar.
deep_cut_fact: After studying motor vehicle engineering at Guildford Technical College, he joined the Cooper F1 team at 18 (1966) as a mechanic for Jochen Rindt, followed Rindt to Brabham, and in 1971 co-founded his first team, Rondel Racing, with fellow mechanic Neil Trundle.
notes: No personal website or verified social accounts found; McLaren is no longer an appropriate route. Long-time trustee of baby charity Tommy's and former British Business Ambassador for advanced engineering - possible warm angles. Engineering/advanced-manufacturing focus suits the entrepreneurship theme.

name: Simon Fuller
current_role: Founder, XIX Entertainment (London/Los Angeles)
profile: British entertainment entrepreneur (b. 1960) who founded 19 Entertainment in 1985, managed the Spice Girls, Annie Lennox and David Beckham, and created the Idols format (Pop Idol, American Idol). He sold 19 to CKX in 2005 for $200m+ and launched XIX Entertainment in 2010, behind global pop group Now United; he also partners with Day One Music, whose artist Lola Young hit UK No. 1 in 2025.
interesting_fact: Billboard certified him in 2008 as the most successful British music manager of all time, and he has a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame (2011) - largely thanks to creating American Idol.
deep_cut_fact: His first job, in 1981, was at Chrysalis Music, where he signed Madonna's first hit 'Holiday' to the company; he grew up partly in Ghana, where his father was a headmaster, and attended school in Hastings.
notes: Social accounts are XIX company accounts, not personal. Best route: XIX Entertainment general inbox. Avoid personal-life topics (2025 divorce filing reported).

name: The Duke of Northumberland
current_role: 12th Duke of Northumberland (Ralph Percy); head of the Northumberland Estates
profile: Ralph Percy (b. 1956), Eton/Oxford-educated with a land-management degree from Reading, succeeded his brother as 12th Duke in 1995. Northumberland Estates manages ~100,000 acres and owns Alnwick Castle, Syon House (London) and Albury Park; Sunday Times 2024 estimated his wealth at £509m.
interesting_fact: He or the estate owns Alnwick, Warkworth and Prudhoe castles plus Syon House; Northumberland Estates has around 100 tenant farmers and directly manages 4,000 acres of forestry.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming Duke he spent seven years working in the Arundel Castle estate office, then returned north to manage the Alnwick estate for his elder brother, the 11th Duke.
notes: Energy angle: the estate began an ~£80k restoration of its 1889 River Aln hydroelectric scheme around 2010 (https://ghgenergy.blogspot.com/2011/03/landowners-fight-anglers-over.html?m=1, a secondary source) and has studied a heat network for Alnwick. Alnwick Castle also runs a podcast (podcast@alnwickcastle.com). Very private; go via the estate press office.

name: The Gordon family

interesting_fact: Transsion, the 'king of Africa' in phones (Tecno, itel, Infinix), passed its HKEX hearing in September 2026 and is reported to have listed in Hong Kong in October 2026 (02636.HK) at HK$35.30 a share, giving it an A+H dual listing.

notes: The input name is 张琦, but Transsion filings show director 张祺 (same pinyin). The Hurun start year of 2007 is also odd against his 2013 join date in filings, so confirm the match. investor@transsion.com is the board secretary's office contact in an April 2026 AGM notice.

name: Zhu Xiaokun
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Tiangong International Co. Ltd. (HKEX: 826); deputy to the National People's Congress
profile: Zhu Xiaokun (朱小坤) built Tiangong, based in Danyang, Jiangsu, into one of the world's largest makers of high-speed steel, die/mould steel and cutting tools. Tiangong International listed in Hong Kong in 2007, and its A-share unit Tiangong Co. is on Beijing's exchange. The group now makes titanium alloys and ultra-fine-grain bar stock for PCB micro-drills used in AI server boards.

deep_cut_fact: In 1984 he ran the Houxiang TV Antenna Factory in Danyang County, Tiangong's predecessor, and in 1987 converted it from TV antennas to high-speed-steel cutting tools. It began making its own high-speed steel in 1992. He studied economic management at Jiangsu Radio & TV University.

It took a stake in Qingshi Yongjun, a spin-out of Zhejiang University's invasive brain-computer-interface team that is building an AI-driven implant for treatment-resistant depression, and in January 2026 it was sole investor in an AI-medical startup.

name: Li Qinghuai
current_role: Non-executive Director, Xinyi Glass Holdings (HKEX: 0868)
profile: Li Qinghuai (李清怀; HK filings: LI Ching Wai, aged 68) is one of the founding shareholder group of Xinyi Glass, the auto, float and architectural glass maker started by Lee Yin Yee and fellow Fujian-born auto-parts traders. Xinyi Glass also owns a large stake in solar-glass maker Xinyi Solar.

name: Lu Youzhong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, YouYou Foods Co., Ltd. (有友食品, SSE: 603697), Chongqing
profile: Lu Youzhong (b. 1955) is a Chongqing native who quit a state job in 1992 at 37 to open restaurants. In 1997 he founded YouYou Foods around packaged pickled-chili chicken feet (泡椒凤爪). The company listed in Shanghai in 2019 as the 'first pickled chicken-feet stock'; he remains chairman, and his nephew Lu You is now general manager.
interesting_fact: He moved from restaurants into packaged snacks because pickled chicken feet were his restaurants' best-selling dish, after building up four restaurants in Chongqing and Chengdu in about three years.
deep_cut_fact: Early shipments swelled in their packaging and lost him money because he had no preservation technology; he worked with food experts at Southwest University and ran more than 100 experiments to fix the shelf-life problem. He calls chicken feet 'version 1.0', fish snacks '2.0' and pork back skin '3.0'.
notes: Low-profile Chongqing entrepreneur, about 71 years old. Contact via the company securities office (board secretary 谢雅玲 per cninfo). Not linked to energy or data centres.

name: Tan Guanghua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Hangzhou Raycloud Technology (光云科技, SSE STAR: 688365)

profile: Rome-born Riccardo Zacconi (b. 1967) co-founded King in London in 2003 and, as CEO, turned it into a mobile-gaming giant behind Candy Crush Saga. name: Mark Burnett
current_role: United States Special Envoy to the United Kingdom (since Jan 2025); co-founder, Lightworkers Media
profile: London-born TV producer who built a fortune from unscripted formats including Survivor, The Apprentice, Shark Tank and The Voice. notes: Currently a US government appointee (Special Envoy to the UK), so outreach likely goes via the US Embassy London press office or his production companies; no verified personal/official contact found. Net worth shared with wife Roma Downey.

name: The Ives family
current_role: Family owners of Rainham Steel Co. Ltd (Rainham, Essex) and associated property companies; founder Bill Ives died in 2017

The business has expanded into industrial and commercial property investment through two property companies.
interesting_fact: Rainham Steel's Scunthorpe hub was chosen for its closeness to the British Steel mills and the docks. It stocks over 100,000 tonnes of structural steel and runs its own fleet of about 50 HGVs.
deep_cut_fact: Founder Bill Ives was a former boxer. Promoter Frank Warren published a personal tribute to him after his death in 2017.

No family member is publicly named as a spokesperson, and the only published email is a general sales inbox. The holding entity is Ives Family Holdings Ltd (Companies House). Avoid Bill Ives's Wikipedia controversies in any outreach.

profile: Fan Jiangang built Changshu Fengfan Power Equipment in Jiangsu into a leading maker of power-transmission towers and steel structures for State Grid and China Southern Grid, later adding solar wafers. In 2024 he and his concert parties sold control to Tangshan's state-owned industrial holding group and in late 2025 agreed to sell their remaining 17.32% for about RMB 989M.

deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership SinoHytec co-launched the world's first fuel-cell tram in 2014 and China's first fuel-cell logistics vehicle in 2015, and in 2018 initiated the China Hydrogen Alliance; it joined the global Hydrogen Council in 2019.

profile: Jiang Tianwu (姜天武), born 1955, built Changsha-based Mendale (梦洁) into one of China's leading bedding and home-textile brands, which listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He is a vice president of the China Home Textile Association and remains chairman. Since a 2023-25 change in share structure, the company reports no controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: He is an honorary professor at Beijing Institute of Fashion Technology, an MBA adjunct supervisor at Hunan University's business school, and sits on the home-textile industry standards committee.
deep_cut_fact: He started on the shop floor as a machine repairman at the bedding factory of Changsha's Cotton & Local Products Company, then rose through general affairs and workshop director to factory director. He later became GM of Changsha Mendale Quilting Products.
notes: DATA WARNING: the input's SEC field (AvePoint CEO) belongs to a different person, AvePoint CEO Tianyi 'TJ' Jiang, wrongly merged by name; this profile covers the Hurun-listed Mendale founder. Mendale and Jiang have received regulatory reprimands (2022, 2025) over disclosure issues per the annual report. Textiles have no energy or data-center overlap.

name: Zhou Lianqi
current_role: Chairman of the Board (董事局主席), Fujian Septwolves Group; Director, Fujian Septwolves Industry Co. (七匹狼, SZSE: 002029)
profile: Zhou Lianqi (周连期) now goes by Zhou Yongwei (周永伟), aged 64. He and his brothers Zhou Shaoxiong and Zhou Shaoming founded and jointly control Septwolves, the Jinjiang (Fujian) menswear brand known for jackets and casual menswear. He was chairman of the listed company's 2nd board and now chairs the parent Septwolves Group, holding ~2.3% of the listed company directly.
interesting_fact: Septwolves is one of the best-known Jinjiang apparel brands. The three Zhou brothers are joint actual controllers through Fujian Septwolves Group, which Zhou Yongwei chairs.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion he was a banker: deputy director of Bank of China's Jinjing office under the Jinjiang branch. He later earned an EMBA from Xiamen University and is a certified economist (经济师).
notes: Former name confirmed in a Septwolves filing: 周永伟, 曾用名 周连期 (http://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2020-12-10/1208874824.PDF). In outreach, use the current name Zhou Yongwei. Route via the securities dept email.

name: Sun Weiqin
current_role: Major shareholder (about 13–15%) of Zhejiang Changsheng Sliding Bearings Co., Ltd. (长盛轴承, SZSE: 300718) and acting-in-concert party of the controlling shareholder
profile: Sun Weiqin is one of the controlling-family shareholders of Zhejiang Changsheng Sliding Bearings, a Jiashan, Zhejiang maker of self-lubricating sliding bearings founded in 1995 and listed on ChiNext. Company filings say she acts in concert with her father, chairman Sun Zhihua, and her husband Chu Chenjian, the company's general manager. She held 14.91% in 2024 and has since sold down part of it.
interesting_fact: Changsheng specialises in self-lubricating sliding bearings, a niche component used in automotive, construction machinery and industrial equipment.
interesting_fact_source: https://www.emis.cn/php/company-profile/CN/Zhejiang_Changsheng_Sliding_Bearings_CoLtd__浙江长盛滑动轴承股份有限公司__en_5107269.html
notes: Not an executive and keeps a low profile. The listed company contact (securities office) is the only route. Family relationships per company Q3 2025 report: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-10-28/1224744683.PDF

name: Shen Yanan
current_role: Founder, Habit 栖息地 AI smart-home brand (operating company 楠社科技 / Nanshe Technology); former co-founder & president of Li Auto
profile: Shen Yanan ('Kevin') was Li Auto's employee No. 2 and first co-founder, and he served as president from 2015 until he resigned at the start of 2023. Before that he was a Lenovo vice president running global supply chain. He then founded the AI smart-home brand Habit (栖息地), backed by Li Auto. It raised RMB 653m early on and a RMB 700m Series A in August 2026.
interesting_fact: Li Auto led the Pre-A round of his smart-home start-up, making it one of the first ventures by a former executive that the carmaker invested in directly. The August 2026 Series A of RMB 700m was reported as the largest home-furnishing industry financing in China's primary market in three years.
deep_cut_fact: Before Li Auto he was a Lenovo vice president responsible for global supply chain operations. He joined Li Xiang as president in November 2015, responsible for overall strategy, business development and supply chain management.
notes: He exited Li Auto's shareholder register (Beijing CHJ) in July 2023. The current venture is an AI/embodied-intelligence 'smart residence' business with a global HQ and R&D centre planned in Changzhou, so there is a possible energy and home-AI angle. No personal channels found; approach via Habit/栖息地 PR.

name: Wang Dayong
current_role: Executive Director and President, Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls (SZSE: 002050 / HKEX: 2050); director of parent Sanhua Holding Group
profile: Wang Dayong (王大勇, b.1969) is a career Sanhua executive who joined Sanhua Holding Group in 1992 and has been president of listed Sanhua Intelligent Controls since December 2012. Sanhua, based in Xinchang, Zhejiang, is the world's leading maker of refrigeration/HVAC control valves and a major supplier of EV thermal-management parts; it added a Hong Kong listing in 2025. His wealth comes from Sanhua shareholdings.
interesting_fact: Sanhua is a global leader in HVAC control components and EV thermal management – thermal management being increasingly relevant to data-centre liquid cooling.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Sanhua in December 1992 as head of the planning section and secretary to the general manager, then ran manufacturing and the refrigeration-valve division before rising to president – a 30+ year single-company career.
notes: Professional manager rather than founder (Sanhua founded by Zhang Daocai; chairman Zhang Yabo). Still listed as executive director in Aug 2026 HKEX announcement. Thermal management / cooling angle suits a data-centre podcast.

name: Zhang Shimin
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2012-2021) as owner of Yuantong (源通), a Wuhai, Inner Mongolia coal business; current role not verified
profile: Hurun records Zhang Shimin (张世民, b. c.1959 in Bayannur, based in Wuhai) as the owner of Yuantong, apparently Inner Mongolia Yuantong Coal Chemical Group (内蒙古源通煤化集团), whose Yuantong Changfu surface mine in Wuhai's Hainan District has 1.5m t/yr of coking-coal capacity. He appeared on Hurun China lists 2012-2021 (~RMB3bn) and Hurun Global 2014-2016.
notes: Hurun record (birthplace, Wuhai residence, company 源通) via hurun.net API. Tried: web searches 张世民 + 源通/乌海/煤焦/董事长/内蒙古源通煤化集团; cninfo full-text (no relevant hits). The Yuantong Coal Chemical Group link is inferred from company name and location (mine data: https://www.gem.wiki/Inner_Mongolia_Yuantong_Changfu_Surface_Mine); no source names him. Unlisted, no official site or contact found.

name: Li Xinhua
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Henan Lantian Gas Co. (SH: 605368) and Henan Lantian Group
profile: Born in Aug 1975, Li built Zhumadian-based Henan Lantian Group into a regional natural-gas business spanning long-distance pipelines (Yunan pipeline) and city gas distribution in southern Henan. He has chaired Lantian Group since 2006 and took Henan Lantian Gas public on the Shanghai Stock Exchange in Jan 2021. A senior economist with an EMBA, he was a deputy to the 12th National People's Congress.
interesting_fact: He became chairman of Lantian Group in 2006 at about 31, and controls the listed gas company through Lantian Investment and Lantian Group (together roughly half the shares).
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the gas business he worked at the Zhumadian Public Security Bureau, then became a business supervisor at a liquefied-gas company and general manager of the Yunan (southern Henan) gas pipeline company.
notes: Regional player; Chinese-language outreach via the listed company's securities affairs office is the only realistic route. 2026 filings note heavy share pledges by the controlling holders - be aware of financial pressure. NPC deputy detail from third-party bio (maigoo), not an official filing.

name: Zhang Yinrong
current_role: Former vice chairman, Inner Mongolia Erdos Resources (SSE 600295) and VP of Erdos Group (left May 2014); no current role found
profile: Zhang Yinrong (张银荣, b. c.1953) is a long-time Erdos Group executive who ran the group's power company, then served as vice chairman of listed Erdos (cashmere, power, ferroalloy smelting) and group VP from 2011 until May 2014. He held 18.46% of Erdos Investment Holding Group, the controlling holder, around 2014-15. By 2019 he was no longer a shareholder.
interesting_fact: In 2014 filings he was one of five individuals (with chairman Wang Linxiang) who together owned 100% of Erdos Investment Holding Group, the parent of the cashmere-to-ferrosilicon conglomerate; later filings say those five hold the stake on behalf of employees.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming vice chairman, he was general manager of the Erdos group's power company (电力公司), the arm behind its move from cashmere into electricity and metallurgy (per Erdos's 2013 annual report).
notes: Confirmed via Erdos (600295) filings: vice chairman 2011-14 and an 18.46% holder of the parent in 2014 (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2015-04-02/1200779862.PDF). No longer a parent shareholder by 2019. Hurun 2015: 张银荣 | 鄂尔多斯 | b.1954, Ordos native. The contacts are company board-secretary IR emails, not his. A different Zhang Yinrong was a director at 002544. Retired and private.

name: Zhu Hongtao
current_role: Employee-representative Director, Joyoung Co. (九阳股份, SZSE: 002242), part of the JS Global Lifestyle group; executive director of several Shanghai investment companies
profile: Zhu Hongtao (朱宏韬, born 1970) is a long-time member of the Joyoung team, the Hangzhou kitchen-appliance maker best known for household soymilk makers, which sits within JS Global Lifestyle (HK-listed, former parent of SharkNinja). He previously chaired Joyoung's supervisory board and is now an employee-representative director. He also runs several Shanghai holding and investment vehicles.
interesting_fact: Joyoung builds the 'space kitchen' for China's space station. It has held the task since 2014, and its food-heating and drinking-water equipment went up with the Tianhe core module in April 2021 and has run for more than 1,500 days.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA from Nanyang Technological University in Singapore, an unusual credential among the founding-era Joyoung executives.
notes: Low public profile, and Hurun attributes his wealth to his JS Global Life stake. The route is Joyoung's board secretary office. The space-kitchen story is a good hook. Web search budget was exhausted, so the profile comes from the FY2025 annual report.

name: Jiao Yun
current_role: Founder, actual controller and honorary chairman (since June 2026), Baotailong New Materials (SSE: 601011), Qitaihe, Heilongjiang
profile: Jiao Yun founded Baotailong, a Qitaihe, Heilongjiang coal-chemical company (coking coal, coke and derived new materials) that he co-established as a listed vehicle in 2003 and long chaired. In June 2026 the board named him honorary chairman, a non-director advisory role on strategy and industrial upgrading, as Jiao Qiang took over as chairman; he remains the actual controller.
interesting_fact: Baotailong's board describes Jiao as the founder who spent years 'deep in the coal-chemical industry' and notes he is a deputy to China's National People's Congress.
notes: Stepped back from the chair in June 2026. Company's published securities-office mailbox (board secretary Liu Xin) is the only public route found. Low media profile.

name: Wu Haijun
current_role: Chairman & president, Shenzhen Hasee Computer Co. (神舟电脑) and its parent Shenzhen New World Group (新天下集团), per most recent available bios
profile: Wu Haijun (吴海军, b. 1966, Rudong, Jiangsu) founded New World Group in Shenzhen in 1995, which grew into Hasee, the low-price PC and gaming-laptop maker that was China's No. 2 domestic computer brand by 2008. Hasee tried four times to list on ChiNext (2010-2013) without completing an IPO; the company remains private and still sells laptops and gaming PCs.
interesting_fact: Hasee became a household name in China in 2002 with its CCTV ad slogan '四千八百八，奔四扛回家' (take a Pentium 4 home for 4,880 yuan), a price-war move that undercut major brands.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his company, Wu was a schoolteacher in Rudong County (1984-88), then earned a master's degree in power engineering (动力工程) at Southeast University (1991-94) and briefly worked at AVIC's Shenzhen group in 1994.

public_contacts.value: http://www.hasee.com/about/contact (corporate contact page; HQ switchboard +86-755-36388585, general service@hasee.com)

notes: Very low international profile; no press/IR contact published (company is unlisted). Deep-cut bio comes from a user-edited Chinese bio site (maigoo) - double-check before use. Approach via Chinese-language letter to Hasee HQ. Current status not confirmed by 2025-26 sources.

name: Wang Weifeng
current_role: Former Chairman & GM of Jiangsu Zhongli Group (002309.SZ); no longer listed in its management after Xiamen C&D (建发股份) took control. Current role not found.
profile: Wang Weifeng (王伟峰), son of founder Wang Boxing, helped run Jiangsu Zhongli Group, a Changshu maker of specialty cables and solar (Tenghui PV) products; he was GM from 2019 and chairman from Aug 2022. Zhongli is now a subsidiary of state-linked Xiamen C&D, chaired by Zhuang Yu'an, and Wang no longer appears among its officers.
interesting_fact: Zhongli, founded in 1988, grew from communication/specialty cables into solar via its Tenghui (腾晖) PV subsidiary; it now sells cables to rail, marine, mining and new-energy markets in 80+ countries.
deep_cut_fact: He studied for his undergraduate degree at York University (Canada) and later earned an MBA from Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
notes: Family lost control of Zhongli in a restructuring (now controlled by Xiamen C&D, 600153.SH); avoid financial topics. No published personal contact found. Education detail from aggregator (MarketScreener); verify before use. Hurun pairs him with father Wang Boxing.

name: Wang Yonghui
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Xiangxue Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300147), Guangzhou
profile: Founded Guangzhou-based Xiangxue Pharmaceutical in 1997, a traditional Chinese medicine maker listed in Shenzhen; has served as chairman and general manager since 2010 per third-party data. Also listed as director of related entities such as Guangzhou Kunlun Investment.
interesting_fact: Founded Xiangxue Pharmaceutical in December 1997 and still runs it as chairman/GM.
notes: One aggregator lists Huang Weihua as chairman from 2019, conflicting with others; verify current title in latest CNINFO annual report. No public personal channels found; route via company board secretary (contact in annual report). Searches limited by budget.

name: Chen Shumei
current_role: Supervisor, Kunlun Investment (controlling holder of Guangzhou Xiangxue Pharmaceutical); former Xiangxue director (2010-2016)
profile: Chen Shumei (b. 1963) is listed by Hurun jointly with Xiangxue Pharmaceutical chairman Wang Yonghui. She sat on the board of Guangzhou Xiangxue Pharmaceutical (SZ:300147, modern TCM) from 2010 to 2016, after posts in Huangpu district foreign-trade bureau and as GM of Kunlun Technology; she is now a supervisor of Kunlun Investment.
interesting_fact: Before entering business she worked as an engineer at the Guangzhou Wanbao Group washing-machine factory, the same Wanbao group where Wang Yonghui was a technical-development head.
deep_cut_fact: Her official bio lists an early civil-service post as deputy section chief at the Guangzhou Huangpu District Foreign Economic & Trade Bureau before she ran Kunlun Technology.
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Xiangxue is currently ST-flagged and in pre-restructuring per 2026 filings, so approach via the company board office may be slow. Hurun last listed her 2020.

name: Huang Zhaochun
current_role: Listed with Huang Hongming as owner of Chuanghong (创鸿), a real-estate group, on the Hurun China list (2014-2015). Current role not verified.
profile: Huang Zhaochun (黄昭纯) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List in 2014-2015 with an estimated $470M, held jointly with Huang Hongming, from the property developer Chuanghong (创鸿). No English-language or accessible Chinese sources could be found to confirm the company's location, his current role or recent activity.
notes: Very low public profile and dropped off Hurun after 2015. Identity and company details are unverified (Baidu Baike was blocked from this environment). Not a strong podcast fit (real estate).

name: Shen Jiansheng
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Yinbang Clad Material Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300337), Wuxi
profile: Shen Jiansheng (沈健生) is co-controlling shareholder, with Shen Yulan, of Yinbang Clad Material, one of China's largest makers of aluminium clad plate, strip and foil for brazing. Its products go mainly into heat exchangers for cars and home appliances. The company listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2012, and he still runs it as chairman and GM; he sat on the board as recently as April 2026.
interesting_fact: Yinbang is among China's largest producers of aluminium brazing clad materials. These are the sheets inside car radiators and air-conditioner heat exchangers, a supply chain that also matters for thermal management in EVs and data centres.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2023 he led Yinbang to Aluminium Stewardship Initiative Performance Standard certification for its Wuxi plant, saying 'We are pleased to pass the ASI Performance Standard certification.' He framed it as a step toward green, low-carbon and digital management.

public_contacts.value: Investor Q&A via the Panorama (全景网) investor relations interactive platform, as stated in company notices; board secretary Gu Yiming handles investor communication

notes: Low public profile. The company website (yinbang.com) was access-restricted from here. The published IR email and phone are in the company's annual reports on cninfo.com.cn. Heat-exchanger materials give an angle into energy and data-centre cooling.

name: Shen Yulan
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder and actual controller (with father Shen Jiansheng) of Yinbang Clad Material Co. (SZSE: 300337); not a listed executive
profile: Shen Yulan (b. 1988) is the son of Yinbang founder/chairman Shen Jiansheng; father and son jointly control Wuxi-based Yinbang Clad Material, a maker of aluminium-alloy clad strip and foil for brazed heat exchangers (auto, HVAC, power). The pair held ~80% pre-IPO before the 2012 ChiNext listing; a May 2026 filing still names him a controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: Yinbang developed its own brazing aluminium-alloy clad plate/strip/foil in 2005, the core product behind its growth supplying heat-exchanger makers.
deep_cut_fact: He was listed first among the 45 individual founding promoters when Yinbang was converted into a joint-stock company on 8 Dec 2010, when he was about 22.
notes: Low public profile; father Shen Jiansheng is chairman and the public face. IR email is from the 2012 prospectus; confirm in the latest annual report. Best route is via the company securities office.

name: Su Tingbao
current_role: Chairman, Rongda Mining (Xinbaerhu Youqi, Hulunbuir); largest individual shareholder of Yunnan Chihong Zinc & Germanium (600497.SH)
profile: Born 1954, Inner Mongolia-based mining entrepreneur. Founded Rongda Mining in Dec 2001 (lead-zinc/non-ferrous exploration, mining and processing); in 2014 Chihong Zinc & Germanium bought his remaining 49% of Rongda for shares and cash, making him Chihong's largest individual shareholder. Has since gradually sold down part of that stake.
interesting_fact: The 2014 deal folded his privately built Rongda Mining into Chihong, one of the world's leading germanium producers, turning a private miner's stake into ~250m listed shares.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from university he worked as a fuel attendant at the Gaoqiao petrol station in Huludao, Liaoning, then in the Gaoqiao development zone's general office, before going into mining in the late 1990s.
notes: Very low-profile; Chinese-language sources only. Chihong is state-controlled (Chinalco/Yunnan Metallurgical), so its IR desk is not his office. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Wang Weibin
current_role: Founder, Suntrans Group (Beijing) (per a single third-party bio)
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2021) for Suntrans (real estate, arts). A Prabook profile says he founded Suntrans Group at 25 with RMB100,000, built businesses in biology, IT and Beijing real estate, and in 2000 formed Beijing Suntrans Tiandi Technological Development Corp. to make educational software. Little else is published in English or Chinese search results.
interesting_fact: Per Prabook, he invested RMB20m in 'Suntrans Intelligent Educational Software' covering junior and senior high-school maths, physics and chemistry.
notes: Very low public profile; only one third-party bio found (Prabook, unverified, page blocked to direct fetch). Chinese company name for Suntrans not confirmed. No published contacts found.

name: Hu Delin
profile: Hu Delin (胡德霖, Hurun lists as 胡德林) was founder, chairman and co-controlling shareholder of Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Academy (EETI, SZSE 300215), a high/low-voltage electrical equipment testing firm. He died on 3 May 2023 aged 72; the company announced it on 26 June 2023.
interesting_fact: He led the 1999 restructuring of the state-run Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Research Institute into a private company and took it public on ChiNext in May 2011.
notes: Deceased (May 2023, source: Sina Finance 2023-06-26). Son Hu Chun (胡醇, Hurun co-listee) is now controlling shareholder of EETI (300215.SZ).

name: Hu Chun
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Academy Co. (EETI, SZSE: 300215); no longer a director since June 2025
profile: Hu Chun (b. 1978) is the son of Hu Delin, who led the privatisation of the Suzhou Electrical Apparatus Science Research Institute (founded 1965, restructured 2000) into EETI, one of China's largest third-party testing labs for high/low-voltage electrical, wind, solar and EV-charging equipment. He was chairman in 2019-21 and 2022-23 and remains its controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: EETI runs national testing centres for electrical products, smart-grid switchgear and explosion-proof equipment, and is an accredited IECEx and IECEE-CB lab, making it a key gatekeeper for China's grid and renewable-equipment makers.
deep_cut_fact: Long before becoming chairman in November 2019, he served as a director and deputy general manager of the testing institute from 2002 to 2016. In July 2026 the company disclosed he had become a Canadian citizen.
notes: Company site is EETI (eeti.cn); the company is chaired by Yuan Lei since July 2025. Board governance disputes in 2022-23 between Hu Chun and his father Hu Delin were widely reported, so avoid that topic. No personal public channels found; route via company board secretary/IR (SZSE 300215).

name: Chen Wei
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shenzhen Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海); chairman of the Shenzhen Venture Capital Association
profile: Chen Wei (陈玮), a Xiamen University accounting PhD and former university lecturer, spent about seven years at Shenzhen Capital Group (rising to president) before founding Oriental Fortune Capital in 2006. The VC firm now manages close to RMB 40bn and has backed 600+ companies (e.g. Kunlun Tech, Jiuxian.com). He remains chairman and an active industry spokesman.
interesting_fact: When the 2008 crisis led LPs to cancel staged commitments, Oriental Fortune's first fund shrank from RMB 900m to under RMB 350m; Chen says he personally borrowed RMB 80m to keep the firm going.
deep_cut_fact: He came to venture capital by accident: in 1999, aged 35 and just back from a visiting-scholar stint in the Netherlands, he wanted to join the Shenzhen Stock Exchange, but the ChiNext board was delayed and hiring frozen, so he applied to Shenzhen Capital instead.
notes: Source of wealth 'Oriental Fortune' = Oriental Fortune Capital (东方富海), not Eastmoney (东方财富). Very public VC figure; frequent speaker at Chinese VC forums. No published press email found; the company website did not load from here. Best route: the firm's official channels.

name: Tang Guoqiang
current_role: Former chairman (2011-2013) of Shunfeng Photovoltaic International (HKEX: 1165, now Shunfeng International Clean Energy); no current role found
profile: Tang Guoqiang (汤国强, b. c.1957), from Liyang, Jiangsu, chaired Shunfeng Photovoltaic International when it listed in Hong Kong in July 2011. Through his company Peace Link he owned about 29.65% of the solar-cell maker. He left the chair in mid-2013, before the group's 2014 takeover of Wuxi Suntech, and has kept no public profile since. Hurun listed him once, in 2014.
interesting_fact: He came to solar late. His earlier jobs were running Liyang Economic Development Corp (metals wholesale, 1990-96), deputy GM of a Liyang fine-chemicals maker (1996-2003) and a director of a Zhenjiang property developer (2003-07). He joined Jiangsu Shunfeng PV's board only in April 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Per the company's 2011 annual report, his formal education ended with a high-school diploma from Jiangsu Province Liyang Middle School in 1977, the year China restored the national college entrance exam.
notes: Identity confirmed from Shunfeng PV's 2011 annual report on HKEX (chairman; 100% owner of Peace Link, which held 29.65%). MarketScreener shows his chairmanship ending 1 Jul 2013. No current activity or published contact found. Not the actor Tang Guoqiang. The '1977 college-exam' note is historical context, not a claim about him.

profile: Xu Qi (徐琦) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2010-2021 for Sunleader, an electronic-components business. A third-party data aggregator (MarketScreener) lists a Qi Xu as CEO of Shenzhen Sunleader Electronic Group (founded 1993), but no primary source was found to confirm details.
notes: Very low public profile; no official company website, interviews or contacts found. Not to be confused with Sunlord Electronics (顺络电子, 002138), a different company. Would need Chinese business registry (e.g. Qichacha) research to confirm.

name: Guo Hongsheng
current_role: Founder of Shenyang Blue Silver (SBS) Group / Blue Silver Industry Automation Equipment (SZSE: 300293); Managing Director & Group CEO, SBS Ecoclean Group (Germany)
profile: Shenyang-born (1962) engineer-entrepreneur who founded the SBS Group in 1996, building Shenyang Blue Silver Industry Automation Equipment (tyre/rubber-processing automation, digital factory systems) into a Shenzhen-listed company. In 2017 he bought Dürr AG's industrial cleaning & surface-processing business, now SBS Ecoclean, which he runs from Germany as Group CEO.
interesting_fact: A Chinese automation founder who personally runs a German Mittelstand engineering group: SBS took majority control of Dürr Ecoclean (founded 1956, Filderstadt) on 1 April 2017 and he has been its Group CEO since.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the SBS Group in 1996 under the motto "technology drives the future" - a line Ecoclean still prints in his official management bio.
notes: Name spellings vary (Guo Hongsheng / Hongsheng Guo / Hong Sheng Guo). Best route is probably via SBS Ecoclean in Germany (English-language corporate comms) rather than the Shenyang listed company. Industrial cleaning for EV/battery and hydrogen components could be a podcast angle.

name: Yao Xiaoqing
current_role: Founder and ~10% shareholder of Tianjin Chase Sun Pharmaceutical (300026.SZ); stepped down as chairman April 2024, no current company post
profile: Yao Xiaoqing (姚小青) founded Tianjin Chase Sun Pharmaceutical, a Shenzhen ChiNext-listed maker of traditional Chinese medicine injectables (notably Xuebijing) and formula granules. He led it as chairman for years; in 2024 he resigned all posts a year early as state-owned Chengdu Xingcheng Group took control, though he remained a ~10% holder.
interesting_fact: Chase Sun's control passed to Chengdu's state-owned Xingcheng Group; Yao resigned as chairman and legal representative on 1 April 2024, a year before his term ended, while keeping about 10.24% of the shares.
notes: Low public profile; no longer holds a role at Chase Sun. Any outreach would have to go via Chase Sun's board secretary/IR office (published in its exchange filings), which no longer represents him.
