name: Ye Jian
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2021 (with Ye Zhehua) with wealth from 'Kunlun' in real estate and investment (~US$470m). Searches could not tie this name to a specific Kunlun-branded company; there are several unrelated Kunlun groups (Kunlun Tech, Kunlun Energy, etc.).
notes: Identity not confirmed: the Kunlun entity behind this Hurun listing could not be identified; do not assume a link to Kunlun Tech or Kunlun Energy. No public contacts found.

name: Hu Zuliu
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Primavera Capital Group; non-executive chairman, Yum China
profile: Fred Hu Zuliu is a Harvard-trained economist who worked at the IMF, then became Goldman Sachs' Partner and Chairman of Greater China. In 2010 he founded Primavera Capital, an Asia growth-equity firm that backed Alibaba, Ant Group, ByteDance, Kuaishou, Xpeng and Yum China; he still runs it and chairs its investment committee.
interesting_fact: Primavera initiated or led investments in Alibaba, Cainiao, Ant Group, Yum China, ByteDance, Xpeng, Kuaishou and SenseTime; Hu also sits on the boards of UBS Group and ICBC.
deep_cut_fact: Before economics he trained as an engineer, earning a Master in Engineering Science at Tsinghua before his Harvard PhD; he is also a trustee of Princeton's Institute for Advanced Study and co-chairs The Nature Conservancy's Asia Pacific Council.
notes: Frequent speaker at WEF, Milken and HKU AsiaGlobal events; conference circuit is a natural route. Writes WEF agenda pieces.

name: Xu Jie
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Phoenix Healthcare Group (now China Resources Medical, HKEX: 1515); current role not publicly reported
profile: Xu Jie (徐捷) founded Phoenix Healthcare, which grew from private hospitals into China's largest private hospital group by beds and visits and listed in Hong Kong in 2013 as the 'first private-hospital stock'. In 2016 China Resources took control; her family vehicle SpeedKey exited and she stepped down as chair. No public role since.
interesting_fact: Phoenix Healthcare's 2013 Hong Kong IPO made it the first listed private-hospital operator from mainland China; it pioneered investing in and managing public and SOE-owned hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Per the 2013 IPO prospectus, she bought the Jilin City Trauma Hospital (吉林市创伤医院) in 1988 and personally served as its legal representative and hospital director until 1995, before investing in hospitals in Dalian and Wuxi and founding Beijing Phoenix in 2007 with RMB45m of her own capital.
notes: Very low public profile since the 2016 China Resources takeover; company contacts (China Resources Medical) no longer represent her. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Huang Mingsong
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (about 24.6%), CSG Smart Science & Technology (科大智能, 300222.SZ), Shanghai
profile: Huang Mingsong (黄明松), born 1971, holds a master's degree. He leads CSG Smart Science & Technology, founded in Shanghai in 2002 with links to the University of Science and Technology of China. Listed in 2011, it makes smart power-distribution automation, EV charging and energy management systems, industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics is a strategic investor.
interesting_fact: CSG Smart combines grid tech (distribution automation, EV energy management) with industrial robots and logistics automation; JD Logistics invested about RMB 618m as a strategic investor in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before scaling CSG Smart he ran a cluster of USTC-linked ventures, including Anhui Keda Luneng Technology and Anhui Keda Smart Grid Technology. He also sits on the board of the Shanghai Fuke Intelligent Robot Research Institute.
notes: 'CSG Smart' = 科大智能 (not China Southern Grid). A 2026 report says Wang Tingting succeeded him as president (CEO) ahead of a Hong Kong listing application; he remains chairman per the latest board filings we found. IR email is the board-secretary address from the Jan 2025 board-election notice.

name: Huang Ruohong
current_role: Executive Director and Chairman, Redco Properties Group (HKEX: 1622)
profile: Huang Ruohong (Wong Yeuk Hung, 黄若虹) founded Redco Properties, a Shenzhen-headquartered residential developer listed in Hong Kong, and is its controlling shareholder (about 40%). He has chaired the board since March 2017. The company, like many Chinese developers, has been working through a difficult property market.
interesting_fact: He became Redco's board chairman and an executive director in March 2017 in his capacity as controlling shareholder, after building the developer from its Fujian/Jiangxi roots into an HKEX-listed group.
deep_cut_fact: He holds the Hong Kong title of Justice of the Peace (JP), is a member of a national CPPCC committee and serves as vice chairman of the Hong Kong Federation of Fujian Associations.
notes: Known in HK filings as Wong Yeuk Hung. No published IR email found; check latest HKEX annual report for company secretary / IR contact. Avoid referencing the company's debt situation in outreach.

name: Mo Shuming
current_role: Co-founder (and long-time vice chairman) of Guangdong Mingcrown Group, Dongguan
profile: Dongguan-born entrepreneur who co-founded Guangdong Mingcrown Group (名冠集团) in 1994 with Mo Zhiming. The family conglomerate spans construction, real estate, steel/new materials (Huaguan), Xinhui Port logistics, hotels, schools and a golf club; it is now chaired by Mo Guanliang and ranks among Guangdong's top 500 companies.
interesting_fact: Mingcrown is pivoting into culture-tourism: in March 2026 it won Dongguan's first land auction of the year for RMB 730m to build the Mingcrown Oasis theme-park project, and signed a strategic deal with Tencent Cloud in April 2026.
notes: Very low public profile; the group site names him only as co-founder. A 2012 Xinhui district government page called him vice chairman of Mingcrown. Day-to-day leadership is now Mo Guanliang (chairman) and Mo Guanjing (president). Hurun listed him jointly with Yao Hesong. Best route is the group's corporate email.

name: Xia Hua
current_role: Chairwoman, Eve Group (依文集团), Beijing; founder of Eve China Handmade; vice chair, All-China Chamber of Commerce (ACFIC); NPC deputy
profile: Xia Hua (夏华) left a law lectureship at China University of Political Science and Law to found menswear company Eve (依文) in 1994, building it into a leading Chinese menswear brand. She now focuses on Eve China Handmade, which links rural ethnic-minority embroiderers in Guizhou, Yunnan and Sichuan with global fashion through digital pattern libraries and IP licensing.
interesting_fact: Her China Handmade platform works with more than 25,000 rural embroiderers; she cites a Miao artisan, 'Grandma Pan', whose family embroidery business earns over 1.8 million yuan a year.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Eve she quit her teaching post and became a shop-floor salesperson at a Xidan mall in Beijing, becoming its top seller within a month by studying which stores' bags shoppers carried. She later funded an 'Eve Distinguished Professor' fund at her alma mater CUPL (2003).
notes: High-profile public figure in China (NPC deputy, ACFIC vice chair, frequent Xinhua interviewee); best route is via Eve Group corporate office. Hurun listing 'Eve' = 依文.

name: Gong Sheng
current_role: Standing Executive Director and President, Jiangsu Shagang Group (Zhangjiagang)
profile: Gong Sheng is the long-serving president of Jiangsu Shagang Group, China's largest private steelmaker (about 40m tonnes of crude steel in 2023). He took over as president from founder Shen Wenrong in 2011, after serving as vice president, and holds a shareholding in the group. He still runs operations under chairman Shen Bin.
interesting_fact: He succeeded founder Shen Wenrong as Shagang's president in 2011 and has run day-to-day operations of China's biggest private steelmaker for more than a decade.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2026 he personally led a site visit to Shagang's Huaigang special-steel subsidiary, which reflects his hands-on, plant-floor management style.
notes: Low public profile, and there is almost no personal biography online. The best route is the Shagang Group board office (集团董事局 常委办公室) email. Listed arm: Jiangsu Shagang Co (002075.SZ).

name: Wan Jie
current_role: Chairman, Artron Art Group (雅昌文化集团), Shenzhen
profile: Beijing-born (1962) founder-chairman of Artron, set up in Shenzhen in 1993 as a high-end art printer. He expanded it into China's largest art-data and online art portal (artron.net) with bases in Beijing, Shanghai and Shenzhen. A long-time CPPCC National Committee member, he also served as a vice-president of the Palace Museum Academy.
interesting_fact: Artron grew from fine-art book printing into a digital art database business; in 2022 Wan used his CPPCC proposals to push metaverse and digital-culture infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: At the 2014 'Two Sessions' he proposed a national copyright-registration system for Chinese calligraphy and paintings to clean up forgery in the art market.

public_contacts.value: help@artron.net (general Artron portal helpdesk, not personal)

notes: Best route is via Artron Group corporate channels; little English-language coverage. Industry listed as Print but now primarily art data/culture.

name: Zhang Yaping
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Shanxi Donghui Energy Group (coal, coking, non-ferrous metals, new materials, cultural tourism)
profile: Shanxi entrepreneur Zhang Yaping (张亚平) started in coal trading and mine acquisitions, then founded Donghui in 2003. It was once China's largest stamp-charged coke producer and now has about 19bn yuan in assets. The group spans coal, non-ferrous metals, new materials and tourism, and holds 7.5% of Shanghai-listed Kexin Development.
interesting_fact: In 2013 Donghui paid A$160M for an Australian copper-gold miner, making it the first private Shanxi company to buy mines overseas. The group has since added Wutai Mountain tourism, a Marriott hotel, EV in-wheel motors and modern agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: Hurun's 2017 business-jet owners report listed him with an Embraer Legacy 650, then the only private jet owned by a Shanxi tycoon. He first built capital as a coal trader and by buying the Dengjiazhuang mine in Liulin county.
notes: Very private; no official group website or press contact found. In June 2026 Shanxi securities regulators fined Donghui's investment arm over undisclosed share buying in Kexin Development. Approach cautiously, in Chinese. Hurun's 'Donghui Coal Coking & Chemicals' (2010-12) now trades as Shanxi Donghui Energy Group.

name: Chen Jianxing
current_role: Shareholder associated with Wens Foodstuff Group (per Hurun listing); no current public role found
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016-2021) as sharing a Wens Foodstuff fortune with Wen Xiaoqiong, one of the Wen family members named as actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (Guangdong pig and poultry producer). No public filings or press found naming a 陈建兴 in a Wens director or executive role.
interesting_fact: Wens grew from a 'seven households, eight shares' rural partnership in 1983 into a company with thousands of employee-shareholders, after introducing an all-employee shareholding scheme in 1986.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from public sources; appears to be a passive family shareholder rather than an executive. Contact only via Wens corporate channels (website/IR). Very low public profile.

name: Wen Xiaoqiong
current_role: Member of the Wen family group named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group (SZSE: 300498); no executive role disclosed
profile: Wen Xiaoqiong (温小琼) is one of the Wen family members named as joint actual controllers of Wens Foodstuff Group, China's largest hog and broiler producer. Wens was founded by her father Wen Beiying (per press reports) in 1983. She was among the top pre-IPO individual shareholders and is a passive shareholder rather than a manager.
interesting_fact: Wens began in 1983 when Wen Beiying raised 8,000 yuan from seven village families in Xinxing, Guangdong to start a chicken farm; it became China's largest livestock company, listing in Shenzhen in 2015.
notes: Very private; no public profile. Listed among Wens actual controllers in the 2023 annual report. Only route is the Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn). Hurun listing was shared with Chen Jianxing (also a listed controller).

name: Wen Junsheng
current_role: One of the 10 actual controllers (Wen family concert group) of Wens Foodstuff Group (300498.SZ)
profile: Wen Junsheng (温均生) is a member of the founding Wen family behind Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig/poultry producer founded by his father Wen Beifen in 1983. He remains on the 10-person actual-controller group named under the family's renewed concert-party agreement (2025), per the company's 2026 interim report.
interesting_fact: Per Jiemian, he is Wen Beifen's eldest son and the father of Wen Jiaolong, the first third-generation family member added as an actual controller and to the Wens board.
notes: No personal profile/executive post found; low public profile. Approach via Wens board secretary office (dsh@wens.com.cn, tel published 0766-2292926). Alive status not explicitly confirmed, but listed as controller in Aug 2026 filing.

name: Liu Rongjiao
current_role: Member of the Wen family (actual controllers) of Wens Foodstuff Group, per company filings
profile: Hurun lists Liu Rongjiao (with Wen Junsheng) as a shareholder in Wens Foodstuff Group, China's large pig and chicken producer founded in Guangdong. Wens' 2024 interim report names a '刘容娇' (variant character) among the 10 people making up the Wen family / actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Wens' 2024 interim report defines its actual controller as the 'Wen family', a group of 10 individuals including 刘容娇, rather than a single founder.
notes: Hurun spelling 刘荣娇 vs filing 刘容娇 (likely same person, not confirmed). No public profile; passive family shareholder. Only route is Wens board-secretary office.

name: Yan Juran
current_role: Director, Wens Foodstuff Group Co. (SZSE: 300498); director, Guangdong Yuncheng Investment Holding
profile: Yan Juran (b. 1962) joined the predecessor of Wens Foodstuff, China's big Guangdong-based pig and poultry producer, in 1983 and rose through vice president, technical director and executive VP to president. He was president until around 2019/20 and remains a board director; he is one of the pre-IPO founding natural-person shareholders (2.80% in 2018).
interesting_fact: A Wens 'lifer': he joined the company's predecessor in 1983 with a high-school education and worked his way up to group president of one of China's largest livestock companies.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2005 he has been vice-chairman of the Beiying Charity Foundation of Xinxing County, Guangdong (广东省新兴县北英慈善基金会), Wens' hometown charity.
notes: Still listed as a Wens director in an Aug 2026 board resolution (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-08-31/1225537760.PDF). Low public profile; no personal channels found. dsh@ is the Wens board-secretary office email.

name: Sun Pengsheng
current_role: Chairman, Jiangsu Nhwa Pharmaceutical Co. (SZSE: 002262), 7th board
profile: Sun Pengsheng (b. 1958) is chairman and one of four co-controlling shareholders (acting in concert) of Jiangsu Nhwa Pharmaceutical, a Xuzhou-based maker of central nervous system drugs. He rose through Xuzhou state pharma factories and has led the Nhwa group since 1996; in April 2026 he bought 200,000 more Nhwa shares.
interesting_fact: He holds about 4.9% of Nhwa directly, and with three partners in a contractual acting-in-concert pact controls roughly 48% of the company directly and via Xuzhou Nhwa Investment.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 as a factory worker at Xuzhou No. 2 Pharmaceutical Factory, then from 1980 rose from technician to director at Xuzhou No. 3 Pharmaceutical Factory; he was once named one of Xuzhou's 'Top Ten Outstanding Youths' and is a CEIBS EMBA.
notes: Company general email published on the corporate site; also Jiangsu provincial People's Congress deputy. Route via company board secretary office.

name: Guo Yongfang
current_role: Founder and >5% shareholder (about 12.7%) of Guotou Intelligence (国投智能, formerly Meiya Pico, 300188.SZ)
profile: Founder of Xiamen Meiya Pico (founded September 1999), which grew into a leading Chinese electronic-data-forensics and cybersecurity company and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. In 2019 she and other shareholders sold stakes to state investor SDIC, which became the controlling shareholder; the company was renamed Guotou Intelligence in January 2024. She still held 109.56 million shares in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: The company she founded is described as China's leading electronic-data-forensics firm; in 2021 it extended its blockchain virtual-currency forensics to NFTs.
notes: Female founder, low public profile. Holding confirmed in Feb 2026 share-reduction notice (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202602101819860269_1.pdf), which says she is not a controlling shareholder. A same-name associate professor at Hebei University of Technology is a different person. IR email belongs to the company's board office.

name: Dai Wenjian
current_role: Founder of Huochebang (Truck Alliance, merged into Manbang/Full Truck Alliance); reported chairman of Guizhou Aishang Dafeiniu (cattle farming)
profile: Sichuan University finance graduate who was reportedly one of the partners in NVC Lighting (雷士照明) before starting a logistics business in 2005. He built Huochebang, a truck-cargo matching app launched in 2013, which merged with Yunmanman in Nov 2017 to form Manbang (Full Truck Alliance). He later moved into beef cattle farming (Dafeiniu).
interesting_fact: His first attempt at logistics matching - handing about 20,000 satellite navigation units to truckers - failed and lost over 30 million yuan before he pivoted to an app.
deep_cut_fact: Before the app, he ran 13 QQ chat groups of about 500 cargo owners and drivers each across provinces south of the Yangtze, then moved ~60% of those cargo owners onto his own platform.
notes: Sixth Tone romanizes his name as 'Dai Jianwen'. MarketScreener notes he resigned from the Full Truck Alliance board (date not seen). Current role at Dafeiniu sourced only from cnpp.cn profile (https://www.cnpp.cn/focus/231635.html). No published personal contacts found.

name: Gui Guojie
current_role: Possibly Director, China Real Estate Group Union Investment Co., Ltd. (unconfirmed match)
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2018-2021) with wealth from 'Zhongfang' (real estate). A MarketScreener/Zonebourse insider profile for 'Guo Jie Gui' lists him as a director of China Real Estate Group Union Investment Co., Ltd.; 'Zhongfang' (中房) plausibly abbreviates China Real Estate, but no source ties the two together.
notes: Very little public information; Chinese and English searches for 桂国杰 returned nothing substantive. Possible match: https://zonebourse.com/insider/GUO-JIE-GUI-A2CTYK/ . Verify via Chinese company registries before outreach.

name: Zhang Peike
current_role: Chairman and Acting General Manager, Sunshine Global Circuits Co., Ltd. (明阳电路, SZSE: 300739)
profile: Zhang Peike (张佩珂) chairs Sunshine Global Circuits, a Shenzhen PCB maker founded in 2001 (predecessor 深圳明阳电路科技有限公司) and listed on ChiNext in Feb 2018. Zhang is also its legal representative. The company makes PCBs for AI acceleration cards, servers, optical modules and communications backplanes, exporting to Europe, North America and SE Asia.
interesting_fact: Sunshine's PCB product lines now include boards for AI acceleration cards, heterogeneous computing servers and optical modules, a direct link to data-center hardware.
notes: Personal biography not found in sources read. Company has European arm (Sunshine PCB GmbH) and in 2023 acquired Vision Industries Malaysia (iconnect007). Best route is via the listed company's board secretary/IR.

name: Yan Shengjun
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, China Tianying Inc. (000035.SZ)
profile: Yan Shengjun (严圣军) built Tianying from Jiangsu into a listed environmental-energy group (China Tianying, Shenzhen-listed) focused on waste-to-energy incineration, sludge and food-waste treatment. Under him it has pivoted into new energy, licensing Energy Vault's technology to build a 25MW/100MWh gravity energy storage plant in Rudong, Jiangsu, connected to the grid in 2024.
interesting_fact: China Tianying's Rudong plant is billed as the world's first commercial-scale gravity battery: cranes lift composite blocks made partly from waste (soil, coal ash, fibreglass from retired wind blades) when power is cheap and lower them to generate power later.
deep_cut_fact: At the March 2022 groundbreaking Yan said the project would help Rudong become a Yangtze Delta 'zero-carbon industrial centre'; Tianying's deal with Rudong county also covers tidal-flat solar, offshore wind, hydrogen and a zero-carbon data centre.
notes: Strong energy/data-center fit (gravity storage, zero-carbon data centre plans). Low personal media profile; no personal channels found. Company site ctyi.com.cn was unreachable from here; route via China Tianying IR / board office. Hurun listed wealth jointly with Mao Hongju.

name: Mao Hongju
current_role: Director and Vice President, China Tianying Inc. (SZSE: 000035), Hai'an, Jiangsu; joint actual controller with husband Yan Shengjun
profile: Mao Hongju (b. 1968) and husband Yan Shengjun, the chairman, control China Tianying via two Nantong holding companies. Tianying grew from waste-to-energy and environmental services into a 2014 reverse-merger listing spanning wind, solar, green hydrogen/ammonia and gravity storage. She has been a director and VP since 2014.
interesting_fact: China Tianying is Energy Vault's partner on the 25 MW/100 MWh gravity energy storage system in Rudong, Jiangsu, next to a wind farm; it was connected to the State Grid in Dec 2023 and billed as the first commercial utility-scale non-pumped-hydro gravity storage plant.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike many founder-spouses listed as passive shareholders, she holds professional titles as a senior engineer and senior economist, and has served as Tianying's vice president since its 2014 listing (per her 2026 board nomination resume).
notes: Husband Yan Shengjun (chairman) is the public face. IR email is that of board secretary Lu Ping as published in the 2026 interim report (securities rep: zhangmma@cnty.cn). IR email is the reliable route.

name: Zhu Hanping
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hubei Sanfeng Intelligent Conveying Equipment (Sanfeng Intelligent, SZ:300276)
profile: Zhu Hanping founded Sanfeng Intelligent in 1999, a maker of intelligent conveying/automation equipment that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2011. He is the company's legal representative, chairman and holds roughly 40% of its shares.
interesting_fact: A 2019 Shanghai Securities News profile described him as having stuck with manufacturing for 20 years, saying that after earning some money working for others he wanted to build a Chinese industrial company.
notes: Alive status not explicitly confirmed; sources indicate he still controls the company as of 2026 data. Shares wealth with Zhu Zhe. Best route likely via company board secretary/IR of Sanfeng Intelligent (300276).

name: Li Yongkui
notes: Hurun China lists Li Yongkui (李永奎), source of wealth 'Strong', food & beverages. Searches in English and Chinese did not turn up the company or person, so identity is unconfirmed. Try a Chinese company registry check for the legal representative of a food company named Strong (斯壮/斯强?).

name: Filip Sedic
current_role: Founder and CEO / 'chief imagination officer', FOREO (Swedish beauty-tech brand)
profile: Bosnian-born Swedish inventor based in Hong Kong who founded beauty-tech brand FOREO in 2013 (LUNA, ISSA, UFO devices). Earlier he co-founded Lelo and the feminine-care brand Intimina. He still leads FOREO and its FAQ Swiss skincare line.
interesting_fact: FOREO's name stands for 'for everyone'; Sedic says 'We are probably the most copied brand in the world' and doesn't mind if copiers improve things.
deep_cut_fact: Before consumer products, he ran a digital marketing agency in Sweden in the 1990s and worked at Ericsson from 2000 to 2005.
notes: Press email is FOREO Sweden's Marketing & PR manager from a Cision release (Nordic market); may be regional. Sources variously title him CEO, Chief Innovation Officer or chief imagination officer.

name: Xue Junteng
current_role: Shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle Technology (罗莱生活, SZSE: 002293); held 7.79% after a March 2019 share sale
profile: Xue Junteng is a major individual shareholder of Luolai Lifestyle, China's large home-textile (bedding) maker, which is controlled by chairman Xue Weicheng. In March 2019 he agreed to sell 25.44 million shares (3.37%) to CA Fabric Investments and kept 58.78 million shares (7.79%). His exact family relationship to the Xue founders was not confirmed in the sources read.
interesting_fact: His 2019 stake sale went to CA Fabric Investments, bringing in an outside strategic investor at Luolai.
notes: No biography found. Listed with Xue Weibin as wealth-sharer, but no source found linking the two. Appears to be a passive shareholder, not an executive. Route via Luolai's IR office if needed.

name: Ge Hang
current_role: Founder and largest shareholder of B-Soft Co., Ltd. (创业慧康, SZ:300451), Hangzhou; previously chairman
profile: Ge Hang founded Hangzhou B-Soft (创业软件, later 创业慧康), a developer of hospital and healthcare information systems listed in Shenzhen. In November 2025 he agreed to transfer about 6.23% of B-Soft and delegate voting rights to Hangzhou Genghao, an investment platform of HK-listed IVD Medical, which would give the company an actual controller.
interesting_fact: In Nov 2025 Ge Hang, as B-Soft's largest shareholder, signed a share-transfer and voting-delegation deal with Hangzhou Genghao (set up by IVD Medical) at RMB5.18/share, a deal framed by media as a bet on 'AI + healthcare'.
deep_cut_fact: Crunchbase lists him as a 1984 bachelor's graduate of Zhejiang University's electrical engineering school; B-Soft was built around hospital information systems.
notes: Facts from search-result summaries of B-Soft exchange filings (pdf.dfcfw.com) and Crunchbase snippet; Baidu Baike blocked. MarketScreener links a 'Hang Ge' to First-Trust Fund Management, which may be a different person; not used. Best route: B-Soft board secretary / IR via company filings.

name: Ji Chunlin
current_role: Co-founder and vice chairman, Kuang-Chi (光启) group (title per Wikipedia; current title not re-verified)
profile: Ji Chunlin (季春霖) is one of five PhD graduates of Duke and Oxford who founded Kuang-Chi in Shenzhen in 2010, a metamaterials and advanced-technology group led by Liu Ruopeng. He is listed as a vice chairman co-leading Kuang-Chi's state-level metamaterial electromagnetic modulation laboratory.
interesting_fact: Kuang-Chi was founded by five PhD students fresh from Duke and Oxford (Liu Ruopeng, Lin Luan, Ji Chunlin, Zhang Yangyang, Zhao Zhiya), and the founders remained its senior executives; it hosts China's first state key laboratory for metamaterial technology.
notes: Limited individual coverage found; best route is via Kuang-Chi corporate channels. Kuang-Chi Group was added to the US Entity List in Dec 2020 (context for a podcast host).

name: Luan Lin
current_role: General Manager & Director, Kuang-Chi Technologies Co., Ltd. (光启技术), since Dec 2022
profile: Duke-trained (PhD 2010) metamaterials scientist and one of the five Duke/Oxford PhDs who returned with Liu Ruopeng in 2010 to found the Kuang-Chi Institute of Advanced Technology in Shenzhen, forerunner of listed Kuang-Chi Technologies. He has been vice president of the institute since 2010, previously led KuangChi Science, and now runs Kuang-Chi Technologies as GM.
interesting_fact: He was part of the Duke student circle around Liu Ruopeng, whose team published the first broadband metamaterial 'invisibility cloak' paper in Science before returning to China to found Kuang-Chi.
deep_cut_fact: He served as a non-executive director of Martin Aircraft Company, the New Zealand jetpack maker backed by Kuang-Chi, and sits on the board of Kuang-Chi Martin Jetpack; his degrees are from Shandong University (2001), Peking University (2004) and Duke (2010).
notes: Low personal profile; route via Kuang-Chi Technologies (Shenzhen, A-share listed). Career dates from MarketScreener/Zonebourse insider profile, which has some inconsistencies.
