name: Chen Chun-Lin
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Shanghai Medicilon Inc. (688202.SS)
profile: Chen Chunlin (陈春麟) earned a pharmacy master's from China Pharmaceutical University (1986) and a PhD in pharmacology/toxicology from Oklahoma State University (1994), worked in US drug metabolism research, then returned to China in early 2004 to found Medicilon, a Shanghai preclinical CRO now listed on the STAR Market.
interesting_fact: Medicilon says it has served 2,000+ biotech/pharma clients and helped about 580 innovative-drug INDs get cleared for clinical trials in China, the US, Australia and the EU.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Medicilon he specialised in pharmacokinetics and metabolism for cardiovascular, anti-HIV and anticancer drugs; he also chairs the biomedicine branch of the Western Returned Scholars Association in Shanghai and won a Shanghai Zhangjiang 'most passionate Pharma Valley person' award (2013).
notes: marketing@ address is the business-inquiry mailbox, not a dedicated press desk; IR mailbox is best for a formal approach. A 2008 PharmAsia News interview with him exists (scrip.citeline.com SC066729).

name: Dai Yunjie
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Director/President of XD Inc. (心动, HKEX: 2400); described as CEO of TapTap at TDW 2024
profile: Dai Yunjie (Kros Dai) co-founded P2P sharing site VeryCD with Huang Yimeng (Dash Huang) in 2003, then pivoted with him in 2010-11 into games, founding XD (Xindong). XD publishes and develops games and runs the TapTap game platform; Dai oversees daily operations, overseas business and product development.
interesting_fact: VeryCD, which Dai co-founded in 2003 and where he ran tech R&D and operations, ranked among the world's top 100 websites by traffic at its peak before pivoting in 2010 to found XD.
deep_cut_fact: At TapTap's TDW 2024 developer conference he said TapTap keeps ads to about 20% of homepage game exposure and that ~70% of the Android homepage is driven by user preferences; TapTap charges zero commission on mini-games.
notes: English name Kros Dai. Contact is company investor-relations site only; no published personal/press email found.

name: Guo Yanhong
notes: Searches (EN/CN, incl. 普阳钢铁 + 郭艳红) found no source linking a Guo Yanhong to Hebei Puyang Iron & Steel (Handan/Wu'an, Hebei); only an unrelated Dalian Univ. of Technology professor of the same name. Very low public profile; check corporate registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Hua Guichao
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Inventronics (Hangzhou), Inc. (SZSE: 300582)
profile: Hua Guichao (Dr. Gary Hua) is a power-electronics engineer (Zhejiang University BS/MS; Virginia Tech CPES PhD 1994) who founded Inventronics in 2007, now one of the largest makers of high-efficiency LED drivers; the company entered EV chargers in 2015. He also founded 4D Bios Corp.
interesting_fact: Before Inventronics he co-founded VPT Inc. (military/aerospace power) as VP of Engineering, and founded e-Power Co., later a wholly-owned affiliate of NASDAQ-listed Bel Fuse.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his PhD at Virginia Tech's Center for Power Electronics Systems (CPES) in 1994 and has published 60+ papers and received 80+ patents worldwide.
notes: Goes by 'Gary Hua' in English. Strong fit for energy/EV-charging angle. ISA profile notes a CCTV 2010 Economic Person of the Year nomination (https://isa-world.org/Index/show/catid/14/id/121.html). 2026 reports of share-sale plans unverified.

name: Li Jianbo
current_role: Chairman, controlling shareholder and actual controller, Luoyang Jalon Micro-Nano New Materials Co. (SSE STAR: 688357)
profile: Founder (1998) and chairman of Luoyang Jalon Micro-Nano New Materials, formerly Luoyang Jianlong Chemical, a maker of molecular-sieve adsorbents and catalysts for industrial gas separation, medical oxygen, energy/petrochemicals and environmental uses. He and Li Xiaohong are the company's actual controllers; in July 2026 he proposed a share buyback for employee incentives.
interesting_fact: Jalon makes molecular-sieve powders, molded and special sieves and activated alumina used in industrial gas separation, medical oxygen, energy/petrochemicals and renewable energy.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Jalon he spent over a decade (Nov 1987 to Jun 1998) as sales section chief at the Yanshi Donggu water-glass (sodium silicate) factory in Henan.
notes: Company also romanized as Jianlong/Jianlon. For IR contact, consult the company's SSE annual report (board secretary). Molecular sieves for oxygen/gas separation could be an energy-adjacent angle. Company profile lists Li Yicheng as vice chairman/president.

name: Li Xiaohong
current_role: Co-actual controller and shareholder (~6.72%), Luoyang Jalon Micro-nano New Materials Co. (688357.SH)
profile: Li Xiaohong is listed alongside chairman Li Jianbo as an ultimate controller of Luoyang Jalon Micro-nano New Materials, a Luoyang, Henan maker of molecular sieves and activated alumina founded in 1998 and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2019. Her wealth derives from that stake.
interesting_fact: Jalon Micro-nano, founded in 1998 as Luoyang Jianlong Chemical, makes molecular sieve powders and molded molecular sieves used in industrial gas separation and purification; it listed on the STAR Market in 2019.
notes: Controller listing (Li Jianbo 27.71%, Li Xiaohong 6.72%) per basic.10jqka.com.cn/688357/holder.html. Her own executive role and relationship to Li Jianbo not confirmed in sources read. Low public profile; route via company IR / chairman Li Jianbo.

name: Li Qian
current_role: Chairman, Beijing Sun-Novo Pharmaceutical Research Co., Ltd. (STAR Market: 688621)
profile: Li Qian (利虔) is chairman and largest shareholder (~38%) of Beijing Sun-Novo Pharmaceutical Research, a CRO providing preclinical and clinical drug R&D services, which he has chaired since 2009. He also chairs Beijing Baiao Pharmaceuticals and is founder/executive director of Jiangsu Langyan Life Technology. Sun-Novo reported 2025 revenue of about RMB 1.22bn.
interesting_fact: Sun-Novo describes itself as moving from a pure CRO 'service provider' toward an innovation-driven 'partner' with its own self-developed drugs; 2025 revenue rose 12.9% to RMB 1.218bn and net profit 10.5% to RMB 196m.
deep_cut_fact: Besides Sun-Novo, he founded Jiangsu Langyan Life Technology Holdings (exec director since Jan 2016) and has been a non-executive director of Eastenova (Chengdu) Biotechnology since 2025; he studied at Peking University Health Science Center.
notes: Personally hosts investor meetings (e.g. March 2026) alongside IR director Guo Xinchi (郭心驰) and board secretary Wei Liping (魏丽萍); IR route is via SSE E-Interaction / company IR hotline. Company site sun-novo.com was unreachable during research.

name: Liao Ronghua
current_role: Chairman (and general manager per 2022 annual report), Shanghai Queclink Wireless Solutions Co., Ltd. (300590.SZ); controlling shareholder
profile: Born January 1976, he holds an engineering master's degree. He worked at ZTE, SIM Technology and SIMCom from 2001 to 2009, then founded Queclink in Shanghai in June 2009. The company makes wireless IoT terminals for vehicle, asset and personal tracking, sells largely overseas, and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in 2017. He held about 29% of the shares as of May 2026.
interesting_fact: Queclink sells its trackers to North and South America, Europe, Africa and elsewhere through a global network that includes foreign sales staff stationed abroad, which makes it unusually export-oriented for a Chinese IoT hardware maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Queclink he spent 2001-2009 at ZTE, SIM Technology (Shanghai) and SIMCom Wireless (Shanghai). His co-founder and vice GM, Peng Wei, followed the same SIM Technology/SIMCom path and joined Queclink at its founding in June 2009.
notes: Also listed in English as Adam Liao or Rong Hua Liao. He chaired the April 2025 board meeting. IoT and telematics hardware angle. Low media profile, so the best route is the board secretary's office (stock@queclink.com).

name: Lin Changqing
current_role: Shareholder (family-related) of Shanghai Medicilon Inc. (688202.SH)
profile: Lin Changqing (林长青) appears on the 2021 Hurun China list via Medicilon, a Shanghai preclinical CRO. Shareholder disclosures describe him as a relative by marriage of Medicilon co-controller Chen Jinzhang (nephew-in-law) and of shareholder Chen Guoxing (brother-in-law). No further public profile found.
interesting_fact: Medicilon's actual controllers are founder Chun-Lin Chen and Chen Jinzhang (acting-in-concert agreement); several other shareholders, including Lin, are their relatives but not acting-in-concert parties.
notes: Very low public profile; relationship info from a search-result summary of Sohu shareholder disclosure (page could not be loaded directly). Contact is Medicilon's company marketing email, not personal.

name: Lin Zhibin
current_role: Chairman, Ruida Futures Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 002961)
profile: Lin Zhibin is chairman of Xiamen-based Ruida Futures, a futures brokerage incorporated in 1993 and the first futures company listed on the Shenzhen market. Together with Lin Hongbin and Lin Lifang he controls the company as an acting-in-concert party through Ruida Holdings, per the 2024 annual report.
interesting_fact: Ruida Futures was the first listed futures brokerage on the Shenzhen market and the first Fujian futures firm to win a financial-futures brokerage licence.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 he was named 'Best Helmsman of a Chinese Futures Company' (中国期货公司最佳掌舵人) at the 10th China Best Futures Operating Institutions awards.
notes: No personal channels found; reach via company IR (SZSE 002961) website. Personal biography (age, education) not found in accessible sources.

name: Lu Hongping
current_role: Major individual shareholder (~2.35% at end-2025) of GoodWe Technologies (688390.SH); controller of Kunshan-based precision-electronics firms
profile: Lu Hongping (卢红萍, b. 1969) is a passive top-10 shareholder of GoodWe, the Suzhou maker of solar inverters and energy-storage systems founded in 2010. Her stake came largely from husband Tu Haiwen, one of GoodWe's five founding shareholders, who transferred his 8.76m shares to her in 2018. She also controls precision-electronics and investment firms in Kunshan and Shenzhen.
interesting_fact: GoodWe was set up in November 2010 by five individuals including chairman Huang Min and Tu Haiwen (who put in 4m yuan for 20%), and grew into one of China's leading PV inverter and home energy-storage brands, listing on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond GoodWe, GoodWe's IPO prospectus lists her as actual controller of Kunshan Tianyaze Precision Electronics, Shenzhen Tianyaze Precision Electronics and Anhui Deying Electrical Technology, plus investment vehicles Kunshan Hanzetai and Kunshan Handing.
notes: Not an executive or director of GoodWe; a passive investor with no public profile. GoodWe chairman/CEO Huang Min is the more relevant guest for an energy podcast. She has been reducing her GoodWe stake (sold ~3.6m shares in 2025). Only route found is GoodWe IR.

name: Lu Xiaojian
current_role: Director and General Manager (CEO), Zhejiang Jiecang Linear Motion Technology (603583.SH)
profile: Lu Xiaojian (b. 1970) is a co-founder of Jiecang Linear Motion, a Zhejiang maker of linear actuators for height-adjustable desks, medical beds and smart furniture listed in Shanghai in 2018. He has run the company as general manager since 2010 and holds about 66 million shares.
interesting_fact: He is one of the principal drafters of China's light-industry standard QB/T4288-2012.
deep_cut_fact: He studied applied mathematics at Nanjing University of Science and Technology and spent a decade (1990-2000) as R&D manager at Nanjing Sikai Electronics before joining Jiecang's predecessor, Xinchang Jiecang Medical Equipment, in 2000.
notes: A 2026 Jiecang robotics-actuator brochure lists him as 'Lu Xiaojian (Su Jie), President & CEO, co-founder'. Company is also moving into robot actuators.

name: Luo Aiping
current_role: Chairman and President, Guangdong Fangyuan New Materials Group (formerly Guangdong Fangyuan Environment; SSE STAR: 688148)
profile: Luo Aiping (罗爱平) founded Fangyuan in Jiangmen, Guangdong in 2002. The company makes lithium-battery cathode precursors (NCA/NCM) plus nickel-battery materials and lithium salts, and was a major NCA precursor supplier to Panasonic. He holds roughly 19.8% of the listed company. He studied at Central South University.
interesting_fact: Fangyuan began bulk-supplying high-nickel NCA precursors to Panasonic in late 2017. In 2021, NCA precursors brought in 1.326bn yuan, about 64% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He completed his undergraduate (1987), master's (1989) and doctoral (1998) degrees at Central South University. Fangyuan later commercialised a lithium-extraction process it co-developed with that university.
notes: Energy-relevant: battery materials. In Feb 2025 the company set up Guangdong Fangyuan Xincai to make high-purity electronic chemicals for chipmaking. The lithium-process detail is from the company homepage. Co-listed Wu Fang is a director and VP of the company.

name: Wu Fang
current_role: Director, Guangdong Fangyuan New Materials (芳源股份, formerly Fangyuan Environment; SSE STAR 688148)
profile: Wu Fang (吴芳) is a director and major shareholder of Guangdong Fangyuan (688148), a Jiangmen-based battery-materials maker, and a concerted-action party of controlling shareholder and chairman Luo Aiping. Per the Q1 2026 report she held ~17.3m shares (3.40%).
interesting_fact: Company filings list Wu Fang as an acting-in-concert party with founder Luo Aiping, who was re-elected chairman of the 4th board in July 2025 while Wu Fang joined that board.
notes: Low public profile; facts from search-result summaries of company filings. Route via company board office / IR (Fangyuan, 688148). Hurun list shares wealth with Luo Aiping.

name: Ma Yongtao
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller of Guangdong Dongjian Technology (东箭科技, 300978.SZ); listed as chairman in 2023 filings
profile: Ma Yongtao (马永涛) is the controlling shareholder of Dongjian Technology, a Guangdong maker of automotive exterior parts, roof racks and vehicle protection systems that has expanded into outdoor gear and full-vehicle customization. 2023 filings show him holding ~25.3% directly plus stakes via Dongjian Huiying Investment.
interesting_fact: The company says its founder entered the car-modification industry in 1994, and in 2023 Ma bought more shares on market (823,500 shares).
notes: Hurun lists wealth shared with Liu Shaorong. A July 2026 report names Luo Jun as Dongjian chairman (and racing driver), so Ma may no longer be chairman; verify. Facts on holdings from 2023 company announcements (dongjian.cc PDFs) via search snippets.

name: Liu Shaorong
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2021) with Ma Yongtao for WINBO-Dongjian (Guangdong Dongjian / 东箭科技, auto components, SZ:300978). Searches confirmed Ma Yongtao as Dongjian's chairman and controlling shareholder, but found no source naming Liu Shaorong (刘少容) or her role.
notes: Could not verify identity; company site dongjian.cc PDFs blocked by WAF. Ma Yongtao is chairman/actual controller of Dongjian per a 2023 company announcement (per search summary). Likely a family co-holder; route via company IR.

name: Shen Jie
current_role: Largest shareholder (about 8.75%, about 10.7% with concert party Beijing Hongyu Rongji VC) of Jiangsu Nata Opto-electronic Material Co. (南大光电, SZSE: 300346)
profile: Shen Jie (沈洁) is a pre-IPO investor and the largest shareholder of Nata Opto-electronic, a Jiangsu maker of MO sources, electronic specialty gases (e.g. phosphine/arsine) and ArF photoresists for chipmakers. Nata has no controlling shareholder. She appears to be a passive investor rather than an executive.
interesting_fact: Nata, where she is the top shareholder, said its ArF photoresist was the first domestically made one to pass customer certification (tested on 50nm flash memory, 2020), challenging an import-dominated market.
notes: Very private; no interviews or bio found. Exchange filings (June 2026, https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202606291826547570_1.pdf) confirm her as Nata's largest 5%+ shareholder. Common name, so be careful with other 'Shen Jie's. The company website lists a general inbox, natainfo@natachem.com, which is a company contact, not hers.

name: Sun Taoyong
current_role: Founder, Chairman, Executive Director and CEO, Weimob Inc. (HKEX: 2013)
profile: Sun Taoyong founded Weimob, a Shanghai-based SaaS and digital-marketing company serving merchants (including on WeChat), listed in Hong Kong. He chairs the board and is CEO, overseeing group strategy, and also heads Weimob Development and Weimob International.
interesting_fact: He was named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia list in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He serves as a deputy to the 8th and 9th Baoshan District People's Congress in Shanghai.
notes: Best route is Weimob investor relations (IR page lists the address for investors, analysts and media).

name: Zhu Guangping
current_role: Private investor based in Shenzhen; actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, an early ~4.25% shareholder of Trina Solar (688599.SH)
profile: Zhu Guangping (朱广平) is a Shenzhen businessman-investor. Trina Solar's 2021 bond prospectus names him as actual controller of Dangtu Xinshi Emerging Industry Fund, which held about 4.25% of Trina after its 2020 STAR listing. That stake explains his single 2021 Hurun listing. Filings also link him to duty-free retail, Guowei Electronics, microfinance and food-import firms.
interesting_fact: His Trina stake came through a private fund, not a solar company. Trina's prospectus lists more than 20 firms he controlled or helped run, from China Duty Free joint ventures in Shenzhen, Zhuhai and Urumqi to Comvita Food (China), the mainland arm of the New Zealand manuka-honey brand.
deep_cut_fact: For years he was listed as the legal representative of Shenzhen China Duty Free Merchandise Co. and Zhuhai China Duty Free Merchandise Co., joint ventures in which state-owned China International Travel Service (now China Tourism Group Duty Free) held 30-50%.
notes: Resolved via cninfo filings. Not a Trina executive; a financial investor whose fund had held over 5% within the year before the 2021 prospectus. Focus Media 2025-26 deal documents show him as an indirect LP via Shenzhen Guangliwei Investment. Hurun 2021: 朱广平 | 天合光能 | RMB 3.0bn (residence given as Changzhou). Private; no contact published.

name: Luo Jianqiang
current_role: Chairman & GM of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical; chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical; majority LP of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (per 2015 filing)
profile: Luo Jianqiang (骆建强, b. 1965) is a Hangzhou chemicals entrepreneur and investor. He held 61.3% of Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (上海辰祥投资中心), which took 300 million shares (11.89%) in the 2014 court-led rescue of bankrupt Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori was relaunched under GCL as GCL System Integration (002506.SZ), which explains Hurun's 2015 solar listing.
interesting_fact: His vehicle was the second-biggest investor, after GCL, in the nine-member consortium that rescued Shanghai Chaori Solar. Chaori's March 2014 missed coupon was China's first onshore corporate bond default.
deep_cut_fact: His day job is chemicals, not solar: GCL System's 2015 filing lists him since 2012 as chairman and general manager of Zhejiang Xinghuo Chemical Co. and chairman of Zibo Zhongda Chemical Co. in Shandong.
notes: Resolved via cninfo: Hurun's 'Chenxiang' is 上海辰祥投资中心 (not 晨祥). Chaori default background: https://thediplomat.com/2014/03/its-official-chinas-chaori-defaulted. Other filings show a 骆建强 as a 2011 Joyson Electronics (600699) asset vendor and a shareholder of Haixing (603115); not confirmed as the same man. Private; no published contact.

name: Frank Hurst Lin
current_role: General Partner, DCM (venture capital); independent director of Vipshop; board/major holder positions in 51Talk and GigaCloud
profile: Hurst (Frank) Lin, 林欣禾, co-founded SINA (now Weibo) and served as its COO, then joined VC firm DCM as a general partner in 2006. His investments include Kuaishou, Vipshop, 58.com, GigaCloud (US IPO 2022), QuantaSing and 51Talk; he now focuses on AI and consumer-internet companies, splitting time between the US and Asia.
interesting_fact: SINA, which he co-founded and ran as COO, was the first venture-backed Chinese internet company to go public in the US; he oversaw its global business development and M&A.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in New York City, earned an engineering degree at Dartmouth, worked as an Ernst & Young management consultant in Silicon Valley, and co-founded SINA's predecessor SinaNet in 1995 after his Stanford MBA.
notes: Goes by Hurst Lin professionally (SEC filings: Frank Hurst Lin). Data-center/AI angle: DCM AI investing; GigaCloud is B2B e-commerce logistics. Best route via DCM or LinkedIn.

name: Vitaliy Khomutynnik
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Cascade Investment Fund (Ukraine); President, Ukrainian Golf Federation
profile: Ukrainian entrepreneur and former MP (Verkhovna Rada 2002-2019) from Makiivka who founded Cascade in the 1990s and built holdings in gas production (Ukrnaftoburinnya, JKX Oil & Gas), insurance and agriculture (Kernel stake, Cascade-Agro). Between 2020 and 2023 he exited oil, gas and farmland, and he now runs Cascade as an investor in VC funds, European tech and Kyiv real estate (Respublika Park mall).
interesting_fact: He has pivoted from gas to tech. Cascade sold its JKX Oil & Gas, Ukrnaftoburinnya, Kernel and Cascade-Agro stakes (2020-23) and now invests via Cascade Ventures in funds and startups such as Wefox, McMakler and Discord.
deep_cut_fact: In 2000, at age 24, he served as 'Minister of Fuel and Energy' in Ukraine's Youth Government, years before he owned gas-production assets. He later backed mobile-game startup Playco, which was valued at about $1bn in 2020.
notes: Former Party of Regions/Opposition Bloc MP, often described in the press as an oligarch. He was sanctioned by Russia in 2018 and reportedly lives abroad. I found no published contact for Cascade Investment Fund. cascadeventures.com looks like an unrelated company, so don't use it. Energy angle: a gas-to-venture pivot.

name: Shengwei (Sean) Da
current_role: Chairman & CEO, AMC Robotics Corp. (Nasdaq: AMCI; formerly AlphaVest Acquisition Corp.); Executive Chairman, Kami Vision
profile: Sean Da is a Tsinghua- and UC Davis-trained electrical engineer who ran YI Technology (Xiaomi-ecosystem action/security cameras) as chairman & CEO from 2014 to 2021, then became executive chairman of AI camera firm Kami Vision. He founded AMC Corp. in 2021 and took it public via a SPAC merger with AlphaVest, listing on Nasdaq as AMC Robotics (AMCI) in December 2025; his reported wealth is largely those insider holdings.
interesting_fact: AMC Robotics builds AI security robots, including the Kyro quadruped robot shown at CES and Tokyo Security Show 2026, and the NovaArm system now running in a live warehouse with Sunward Logistics.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a chip designer: a staff design engineer in Analog Devices' Power Management Group (2002-05), then CTO of Rock Semiconductor and engineering director at Intersil, after a PhD in electrical engineering at UC Davis.

public_contacts.value: AMCRoboticsIR@allianceadvisors.com (Alliance Advisors IR - investors and media contact)

notes: Paper wealth from a small-cap de-SPAC (AMCI); actual value volatile. Power-electronics background makes him a plausible fit for an energy/data-center angle. Best route: Alliance Advisors IR/media contact.

name: Alisa Moussaieff
current_role: CEO & Creative Director, Moussaieff Jewellers (London)
profile: Austrian-born Alisa Moussaieff heads Moussaieff Jewellers, the London high-jewellery house she built with her husband Shlomo Moussaieff (d. 2015), known for rare coloured diamonds. She runs it with her daughters, with salons in London, Geneva and Hong Kong, and is regarded as a doyenne of the coloured-diamond trade.
interesting_fact: She married Shlomo Moussaieff in Jerusalem in 1948, two weeks before he was taken captive for a year during the Arab-Israeli war; together they built a gem business and he amassed one of the largest private collections of Biblical-era antiquities (~60,000 artefacts).
deep_cut_fact: Jewellery historian Vivienne Becker traces the Moussaieff family's gem-dealing lineage roughly 800 years back to Bukhara, the Silk Road city of gem merchants; Becker called Alisa the 'matriarch' of the global diamond industry.
notes: Very private; seldom seeks publicity (per Phillips). Best route is the house's published press contact. She is likely in her 90s; no death report found, but confirm before outreach. Mother of Dorrit Moussaieff (former First Lady of Iceland).

name: Michael J. Angelakis
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Atairos (private investment firm he founded with Comcast backing)
profile: Former Comcast Vice Chairman & CFO (joined 2007 from Providence Equity; earlier CEO of State Cable TV and Aurora Telecom, banker at Manufacturers Hanover). Founded Atairos in 2015/16 to provide long-term strategic capital. Director at ExxonMobil, American Express (since Mar 2025), Clarivate, TriNet and Lucky Strike Entertainment.
interesting_fact: Named 'Best CFO in Media' on Institutional Investor's 2013 All-America Executive Team while Comcast CFO; also sits on the ExxonMobil board (energy angle for the podcast).
deep_cut_fact: Served on the national board of directors of Big Brothers Big Sisters of America, with which Comcast ran a mentoring initiative; a Babson College grad who spent years in London building Manufacturers Hanover's acquisition-finance business.
notes: Best route is Atairos media contact at FGS Global. Babson/London detail sourced from wict.org/littlesis bios as well.

name: Charles A Davis
current_role: Chairman and Co-CEO, Stone Point Capital; Chair of the Board, BETA Technologies (since Feb 2021); director, Progressive Corp.
profile: Chuck Davis spent 23 years at Goldman Sachs (head of investment banking services worldwide, general partner) and was vice chairman of Marsh & McLennan before founding Stone Point Capital in 1998, a financial-services-focused investor with $65bn+ AUM. He chairs Vermont electric-aircraft maker BETA Technologies and has been a Progressive director since 1996.
interesting_fact: He chairs BETA Technologies, the Vermont electric aircraft and charging-network company, and was previously chairman of The Hershey Company's board.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Vermont graduate, he served on the board of Vermont's Merchants Bancshares from 1985 to 2008 and is credited as chief architect of Stone Point's 'Elephant Process' investment philosophy.
notes: Strong fit for energy/aviation electrification angle via BETA. Also on AXIS Capital and Fibrolamellar Cancer Foundation boards (Stone Point bio).

name: Thomas E Gottwald
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, NewMarket Corporation (NYSE: NEU), Richmond, Virginia
profile: Thomas E. 'Teddy' Gottwald is third-generation leader of the Gottwald family's Richmond chemicals business. He joined Ethyl in 1984, became NewMarket president/CEO in 2004 and chairman in 2014, succeeding his father Bruce. NewMarket owns Afton Chemical (petroleum additives) and in 2025 bought Calca Solutions, a maker of aerospace/defense propellants.
interesting_fact: His grandfather Floyd D. Gottwald Sr. ran Albemarle Paper, which in 1962 bought the much larger Ethyl Gasoline company, a famous early leveraged deal. Ethyl later became NewMarket.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Virginia Military Institute graduate and a former rector of VMI's Board of Visitors. He also chairs VMI's Jackson-Hope Board of Overseers.
notes: Low-profile CEO. Best route is NewMarket Corporate Communications in Richmond. The Calca propellants deal and the additives business are natural energy-podcast angles.

name: Gert-Rudolf Flick
current_role: Private investor, art historian and collector; visiting professor in the history of art, University of Buckingham (as of 2019)
profile: Grandson of German industrialist Friedrich Flick, born 1943; holds a law doctorate from LMU Munich. Joined the Flick firm in 1971 and, with his siblings, sold his stake in 1975, the source of his wealth. Since then he has lived in London as an art historian, author and collector of Italian old masters and vedute.
interesting_fact: He was publisher of Apollo, the London fine-art magazine, in the 1990s, and kept a collection of early silver and Italian vedute, including a Canaletto of fireworks over Venice, at Park House, Kensington.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote 'Missing Masterpieces: Lost Works of Art 1450-1900' (2003), a study of lost artworks, and 'Masters & Pupils' (2008), which traces an 'apostolic succession' of teacher-pupil training through European art history.
notes: Very private; no published personal or office contacts found. Probably best reached through the University of Buckingham's art history department. Not in energy or data centres, so a weak fit for the podcast. I could not confirm recent activity, so 'alive' is set to unknown (no death report found). His family history is a sensitive topic.

name: Corinne Flick
current_role: Founder and head of the Convoco Foundation (think tank, Berlin/London/Salzburg); general partner of Vivil GmbH & Co. KG, Offenburg
profile: Dr Corinne Michaela Flick, a lawyer trained at LMU Munich (doctorate 1989), is married to Gert-Rudolf Flick of the Flick industrial dynasty and comes from the family behind Vivil confectionery. She founded the interdisciplinary think tank Convoco in 2004, runs its Salzburg forum, London/Berlin lectures, podcast and the Convoco Edition book series.
interesting_fact: Before founding Convoco she worked as a lawyer at Bertelsmann Buch AG in London and at Amazon.com in Munich; she has also been a general partner of Vivil (Offenburg) since 1998.
deep_cut_fact: The Jewish Museum Berlin gave her its Prize for Understanding and Tolerance (alongside Wolfgang Ischinger); the jury noted that every Convoco topic takes the German Basic Law as its reference point.
notes: Wealth is via the Flick family (husband Gert-Rudolf Flick) and Vivil. Very relevant fit: she hosts a think-tank podcast and her council includes energy-sector figures; approach via Convoco's general inbox.

name: Jonathan Hiscock
current_role: Founder, GSA Capital Partners LLP (London quant hedge fund)
profile: British quant hedge fund manager (b. 1974), Oxford maths graduate. Ran Deutsche Bank's Global Statistical Arbitrage prop-trading team, then spun it out in 2005 as GSA Capital with ~$500m and 15 colleagues. GSA now runs systematic strategies across all asset classes with a team of ~150 and repeated EuroHedge awards; Sunday Times put his wealth at £350m (2019).
interesting_fact: GSA's name literally comes from 'Global Statistical Arbitrage', the Deutsche Bank desk he ran; the Independent said he modelled the firm on idiosyncratic tech outfits like Google rather than traditional finance houses.
deep_cut_fact: When he spun GSA out of Deutsche Bank in Jan 2005, it launched with two funds and ~$500m under management; in 2021 the firm deliberately returned investor capital in its scalable 'alt beta' strategies to refocus on its core.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Pitch via GSA press enquiries; quant/compute angle (systematic trading infrastructure) could fit a data-center theme.

name: Sir Elton John
current_role: Singer-songwriter; founder, Elton John AIDS Foundation; co-owner of Rocket Entertainment
profile: English singer, pianist and composer (born Reginald Dwight, 1947) whose catalogue, touring and Rocket Entertainment business built his fortune. His Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour sold 6m+ tickets over 330 shows (2018-2023); he returned for Rock in Rio (Sept 2026) and two final Mexico City shows in October 2026. He is an EGOT winner and runs the Elton John AIDS Foundation.
interesting_fact: His Farewell Yellow Brick Road tour (2018-2023) sold over six million tickets across 330 shows, ending in Stockholm in July 2023, before he announced two extra 'farewell' shows in Mexico City for October 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At 15 he got his first paid gig as the pub pianist at the Northwood Hills Hotel near Pinner, playing Thursday to Sunday nights; he left Pinner County Grammar School just before his A-levels to pursue music.
notes: Musician rather than entrepreneur/energy figure; best route is the EJAF media office (foundation emails are for the foundation, not him personally) or Rocket Entertainment management.

name: Sir Philip Hulme
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder, Computacenter plc; philanthropist (founder, The Hadley Trust)
profile: Born 1948, Imperial College engineer and Harvard MBA who was a Boston Consulting Group VP before co-founding IT services group Computacenter with Harvard classmate Peter Ogden in 1981. He chaired it 1998-2001 after its LSE flotation and remains a large shareholder; also a substantial shareholder in Dealogic and a major philanthropist.
interesting_fact: After Computacenter's 1998 London flotation he gave much of his share-sale proceeds to charity, and was knighted in 2016 for services to technology and philanthropy.
deep_cut_fact: Before Computacenter he graduated with a first in engineering from Imperial College, went to Harvard Business School on a Harkness Fellowship, and became a Vice-President and Director of Boston Consulting Group in 1979.
notes: Low public profile; no personal channels found. Route likely via The Hadley Trust (his charitable trust) or Computacenter corporate communications (computacenter.com).

name: Charles Odell Schiff
current_role: Director, Cincinnati Financial Corp (CINF); EVP, secretary & treasurer, John J. & Thomas R. Schiff & Co. Inc.
profile: Charles O. 'Charlie' Schiff is a nonindependent director of Cincinnati Financial (since Aug 2020, investment committee) and an executive of John J. & Thomas R. Schiff & Co., the privately owned Cincinnati independent insurance agency bearing the names of CINF's founding-era Schiff family. His wealth reflects a large CINF stake (~1.1M+ shares).
interesting_fact: He joined the CINF board in 2020 as Thomas R. Schiff stepped down under the director age guideline; the company said he would give insight into how CINF serves its primary customer, the independent agent.
deep_cut_fact: A Fordham history graduate (magna cum laude), he has served on the boards of The Children's Theater of Cincinnati and The Cincinnati Observatory, among other local nonprofits.
notes: Low public profile; contacts are Cincinnati Financial corporate (2020 release, may have changed). Insurance industry, not energy-related.

name: Wen Kaifu
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Holitech Technology (合力泰, SZSE: 002217); no current executive role found
profile: Wen Kaifu built Holitech, a Shandong-based maker of touch screens, LCD modules and other display components for smartphones. In 2018 he handed control (via a voting-rights proxy and share transfers) to the state-owned Fujian Electronics & Information Group, which now controls the company.
interesting_fact: Holitech grew into one of China's larger suppliers of touch-display modules for smartphone brands before Fujian Electronics & Information Group took control around 2018.
notes: Not a good outreach target: in June 2026 Holitech disclosed a regulator's preliminary penalty notice naming the company and Wen Kaifu over 2017-2021 financial misreporting, and reports say he faces a lifetime securities-market ban and his shares are judicially frozen (news.10jqka.com.cn/20260901/c679501996.shtml). No personal public channels found.

name: Chai Huijing
profile: Chai Huijing (柴慧京) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2008 to 2018 with real-estate wealth tied to a company listed as 'Guodu' (国都). I could not find any public profile, company page or press coverage to confirm her role or what she is doing now.
notes: Very low public footprint; searches for the exact Chinese name returned nothing relevant. Not the Taiwanese general Chai Hui-chen (柴惠珍). Verify via Chinese corporate registries (Qichacha/Tianyancha) before outreach.

name: Li Qinfu
current_role: Former chairman and major shareholder of Jiulongshan / 九龙山 (SH600555, later renamed HNA Innovation 海航创新); current role unknown
profile: Li Qinfu (李勤夫) built the Jiulongshan (Nine Dragon Hill) resort and real-estate business, listed in Shanghai as 九龙山 (600555), and appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2001-2016. In 2011 he sold a 29.9% stake to HNA-affiliated companies; by 2016 HNA had taken board control and the company was renamed 海航创新. No recent public activity found.
interesting_fact: After selling a 29.9% stake to HNA units in March 2011 (reported value ~RMB1.69bn), he kept about 19% and remained chairman for several years, favouring a real-estate focus while HNA pushed for a tourism-plus-finance platform.
notes: Very low recent profile; most coverage is from 2012-2016 and concerns a control dispute with HNA, so avoid that topic. Country field blank in the input; nationality not confirmed. No published contacts found.

name: Zhang Xinming
current_role: Formerly chairman, Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group (山西金业煤焦化集团); no verified current role
profile: Zhang Xinming was chairman of Shanxi Jinye Coal Coking Group and was described as Shanxi's richest energy tycoon, appearing on Hurun China from 2005 to 2010. Reports since 2010 concern legal matters rather than business activity.
notes: Do not approach. Chinese media reported in Oct 2010 that he fled and was wanted by police (https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2010-10-26/400513.html); later reports cite organised-crime allegations. Off rich lists since 2010; current status unverified.

name: Zhang Tongsheng
current_role: Chairman & General Manager, C&U Co., Ltd. (人本股份) and controlling shareholder of C&U Group (人本集团), Wenzhou
profile: Wenzhou entrepreneur who co-founded the Wenzhou Bearing Factory in 1991 with three partners; it became C&U Group, China's largest bearing maker, plus the Renben (人本) supermarket and Shizu retail chains. He controls ~60.8% of the votes of C&U Co., which re-filed for a Shanghai main-board IPO in late 2025.
interesting_fact: C&U has ranked No.1 in China by bearing output and sales every year since 2013 and is described as the only Chinese company in the global top 10 bearing makers; it employs ~19,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: He started the bearing business at age 24 with a junior-middle-school education; the Wenzhou Bearing Factory was registered in July 1991 with RMB 4 million of capital, and he has led it as chairman ever since.
notes: Low public profile; little personal press. Route via C&U corporate office or the IPO sponsor/IR once listed. Bearings for wind turbines/EVs could be an energy angle.

name: Sun Guomin
current_role: Early shareholder of Zhejiang Netsun Co. (生意宝, 002095.SZ); no executive role found
profile: Listed by Hurun alongside Sun Deliang, founder and chairman of Hangzhou-based Netsun (China Chemical Network / 生意宝), a B2B e-commerce pioneer listed in Shenzhen in 2006. Exchange filings show a pre-IPO 5%+ holder named 孙国明 (Sun Guoming), possibly the same person as Hurun's 孙国民, who held 9.25% and sold down to 4.83% by 2014.
interesting_fact: Netsun says it was the first Chinese company to build and run an industry-specific B2B website (ChemNet / China Chemical Network); it listed in Shenzhen in late 2006.
notes: Identity unclear: Hurun's 孙国民 may be a rendering of filings' 孙国明, a passive pre-IPO holder (9.25%, cut to 4.83% by 2014). Their link to Sun Deliang is unconfirmed. The public face of the business is founder-chairman Sun Deliang. Not a good outreach target.

name: Zhou Jianhe
current_role: President, Junefield (Holdings) Ltd (Hong Kong); chairman, Prime Century Investments Ltd (per MarketScreener, undated)
profile: Hong Kong-based businessman (also styled Zhou Chu Jian He) behind Junefield Group, whose interests span Beijing property, hospitality and trade. Was chairman of HKEX-listed Junefield Department Store Group (stock 758), based at Beijing Junefield Plaza on Xuanwumen Wai Street. Appeared on Hurun China lists 2003-2005.
interesting_fact: His group developed Beijing Junefield Plaza on Xuanwumen Wai Street, the PRC base of his HK-listed department-store company in the mid-2000s.
notes: Low public profile; most info from 2005 HKEX filings and aggregator data. No official Junefield website or contacts found. Verify current role via HK Companies Registry.

name: Hong Jiangyou
current_role: Chairman and President, Honz Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (康芝药业, SZSE: 300086), re-elected Dec 2025
profile: Born 1964 in Puning, Guangdong; pharmacy graduate (Guangdong College of Pharmacy, 1988) who left a state pharmacist job in Shenzhen to found Hainan-based Honz Pharmaceutical, a children's-medicine maker listed on ChiNext. He controls ~20% of the company and was re-elected chairman for a three-year term in December 2025.
interesting_fact: He has pitched Honz around a single mission, 'children's great health' (儿童大健康), and has said he won't retire until it is complete; the firm specialises in paediatric drugs.
deep_cut_fact: A keen Go player since university, he chairs the Hainan Provincial Go Culture Promotion Association and says Go's opening stage shapes how he makes business decisions; Honz sponsored a children's Go training camp in Guangzhou.
notes: Also chairs the International Teochew (Chaozhou) Business Federation 21st council and the Hainan overseas-Chinese business federation. Company has been loss-making in 2024-25. Best route: the board secretary (Lin Dexin) through the IR email.

name: Li Shiyong
current_role: Associated with Shandong Ensign Industry (formerly Weifang Ensign), Changle, Weifang; current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for wealth from Ensign, a citric-acid and alcohol producer. Shandong Ensign Industry (named Weifang Ensign until 2020) is reported to be the world's largest citric-acid producer, with ~600,000 t/a capacity and an upgrade planned to 700,000 t/a. Recent annual reports list Li Jian as company head; Li Shiyong's current role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Shandong Ensign has been described as the world's largest citric acid producer, planning to lift capacity from 600,000 to 700,000 tonnes a year.
interesting_fact_source: https://www.cnchemicals.com/Press/91863-Shandong Ensign: Citric acid capacity expansion proposal and refined citric acid project completion.html
notes: Very low public profile; no biography found in English or Chinese web search, and Baidu Baike was not accessible. A 'Shiyong Li' appears as an inventor on Weifang Ensign patents (goodip.io). No published contact or company website found.

name: Luo Weidong
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Aurora Mobile Ltd (Nasdaq: JG), Shenzhen
profile: Luo Weidong (Chris Luo) co-founded Shenzhen-based Aurora Mobile (JPush / Jiguang) in 2011 and has been chairman and CEO since May 2012. The mobile developer-services and big-data company, backed by IDG, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs, listed on Nasdaq in 2018; his stake (~30%) is the source of his wealth.
interesting_fact: PolyU says Aurora Mobile was the first company of its kind to list on Nasdaq (2018); Luo holds an MPhil in computing from PolyU and won its Outstanding Alumni Award for entrepreneurial achievement in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: During COVID-19, Luo led a research team behind a data platform that PolyU credits with supporting epidemic-containment work in 334 Chinese cities. Before Aurora he was GM of Shenzhen Zhiwo Information Technology (2007-2010).

public_contacts.value: Christensen Advisory - Xiaoyan Su, Xiaoyan.Su@christensencomms.com (IR agency named in Aurora Mobile press releases)

notes: Goes by Chris Luo. Some IR pages list ir@aurora-mobile.com instead of ir@jiguang.cn (company rebranding of IR domain). Named 2025 Greater Bay Area Strategic Emerging Industry Youth Leader (Feb 2026 release).

name: Yang Zhen
current_role: Founder and (per 2024 reports) actual controller of Jiajia Food Group (加加食品, SZSE: 002650); no longer chairman
profile: Yang Zhen (杨振, b. 1962, Ningxiang, Hunan) founded Jiajia soy sauce in 1996 and took it public in 2012 as China's first listed soy-sauce maker, earning the nickname 'soy sauce king'. He later stepped back from management to focus on outside investments; a cousin, Yang Xudong, now chairs the company.
interesting_fact: In 2003 he spent RMB 48m, nearly all of Jiajia's profits from its first seven years, to win CCTV's prime-time 'ad king' slot for two months; revenue hit a record RMB 500m in 2004.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he trained at Yiyang Normal College and worked as a Chinese-language teacher. He is credited with inventing the built-in pull-ring soy-sauce bottle cap, and he founded Jiajia in 1996 after Hunan factories turned down his offer to sell the patent for RMB 500k.
notes: Sensitive. Since 2022, Yang and his holding company have repeatedly been listed as debt defaulters, and Jiajia has been ST-flagged over guarantees he arranged. Approach with care, if at all. No personal or office contact published. Go through the Jiajia Food board secretary listed in SZSE filings.

name: Chen Wenli
current_role: Former director and co-founder of HNA Group (left the board in March 2020); no current public role found
profile: Chen Wenli was one of the founders of Hainan-based HNA Group in 1993, alongside Chen Feng, Wang Jian and Adam Tan. He held an individual HNA stake (Hurun rich list 2017-2019) and sat on the board. He left the board in March 2020 when a Hainan government working group took control. HNA later went through court-led restructuring in 2021, which wiped out the founders' equity.
interesting_fact: He co-founded HNA, which grew from a provincial airline into a global conglomerate that held stakes in Hilton, Deutsche Bank and Swissport during a record overseas buying spree that ended in 2017.
notes: Very low profile and likely not a viable guest. His wealth was tied to HNA equity that was largely erased in the 2021 bankruptcy restructuring, and other HNA founders were detained in 2021. Source for his 2020 board exit: https://www.mingtiandi.com/?p=43164. No personal channels found.

name: Ye Jiahao
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2020) as founder/owner of Qixin Construction; current role not verified
profile: Ye Jiahao (叶家豪) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2020 with wealth attributed to 'Qixin Construction' (construction sector). Web searches in Chinese and English found no public coverage linking him to a specific company, so identity and current role could not be confirmed.
notes: Very low public profile; company name 'Qixin' may be a romanisation of 祺鑫/启鑫/奇信 etc. Verify via Chinese business registry (e.g. Qichacha) before outreach.

name: Chen Qiming
current_role: Shareholder associated with SF Express / SF Holding (002352.SZ); no executive title found
profile: Chen Qiming is one of nine SF Express-linked individuals on the 2020 Hurun Global/China Rich List, with an estimated RMB 3.1bn (rank 1,705). The listing implies an early or indirect stake in SF Holding, the delivery giant founded by Wang Wei. I found no published biography or SF board or management role.
interesting_fact: He was one of nine SF-linked people on the 2020 Hurun list, a year in which SF's rising share price added five new SF billionaires-by-yuan.
notes: He is not among SF Holding's directors, supervisors or senior management in the filings I checked. He is probably an early partner or indirect shareholder. Identity details are thin. The only route is via SF Holding IR, which may not forward.

name: Wang Jinglian
profile: Listed on the 2008 Hurun China Rich List with Jinsheng Group (copper). No reliable online source found linking the name 王景连 to a specific Jinsheng group or role, so identity could not be confirmed.
notes: Could not verify. A copper business called Shandong Jinsheng Nonferrous Group (Linyi) went through a court-supervised restructuring/settlement in 2022-23 (https://www.zhonglun.com/news/trade/15361.html), but no source names Wang Jinglian in connection with it. Treat as unverified; low priority.

name: He Qiqiang
current_role: Chairman, Guangdong Chant Group (Changqing Group, 002616.SZ), Zhongshan
profile: Co-founded Chant Group (长青集团) in Zhongshan in 1985 as a gas and heating appliance maker, listed it in Shenzhen in 2011, and from 2004 steered it into biomass combined heat-and-power and industrial-park district heating, where it ranks among China's largest operators. Still chairman; fortune shared with wife Guo Miaobo.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from gas stoves and heaters to burning crop and forestry residues instead of coal, and its installed biomass CHP capacity ranks among the largest of China's peers.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting his business in 1985 he was a factory workshop director earning about 100 yuan a month, and his early goal was simply to save 1 million yuan, since its ~5% interest would yield 4,000+ yuan a month (told at a 2023 Yabuli entrepreneurs' forum).
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (biomass CHP). Active in the Yabuli China Entrepreneurs Forum, which may be a warm route. IR email is the board secretary's office.

name: Guo Miaobo
current_role: Shareholder and acting-in-concert party of the controlling group of Guangdong Chant Group (SZSE: 002616); holds no position at the company
profile: Guo Miaobo (郭妙波) is the spouse of Chant Group chairman He Qiqiang and one of the parties acting in concert with the company's actual controllers (He Qiqiang and Mai Zhenghui), per the 2025 annual report. Chant, based in Zhongshan, Guangdong, started in gas appliances and has expanded into biomass and waste-to-energy power generation and industrial-park heat supply.
interesting_fact: Chant Group pivoted from making gas stoves and water heaters into environmental energy, operating agricultural-biomass power plants and waste-to-energy and heat-supply projects in China, a possible angle for an energy podcast.
notes: Private, non-executive; the 2025 annual report states she holds no post at Chant. Better interview target would be chairman He Qiqiang; route via the board secretary office (dmof@chantgroup.cn).

name: Xu Xizhong
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Hubei Sanxia New Building Materials (600293.SH); current post unknown
profile: Xu Xizhong (许锡忠) controlled Shanghai-listed float-glass maker Sanxia New Materials (三峡新材), together with his vehicle Hainan Zong Xuan Da Industrial Investment (海南宗宣达实业), and chaired its board; the company also owned mobile-phone distributor Shenzhen Hengbo. By 2025 the company was controlled by Dangyang City Investment and chaired by Xie Pule.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he chaired Sanxia New Materials while also chairing Shenzhen Weikangde Investment Group, Jiangxi Chaosheng Mining and Hainan Zong Xuan Da Industrial Investment, per the company's 2019 annual report.
deep_cut_fact: His career began as a department manager at a garment factory in Laowu township, Chaoyang county, Guangdong; he later ran a restaurant (Haomen Yeda Jiulou) in Puning as general manager before becoming chairman of Shenzhen Xinzhen Co.
notes: Hurun listing only 2017. He has since lost control of Sanxia New Materials (now state-controlled) and his shares were frozen in 2019 litigation; a Dec 2025 SSE regulatory warning named him as former chairman. Likely no longer UHNW and not a good outreach target; no published contact found.

name: Zhang Chunhua
current_role: Possibly Chairman, Shenzhen Langhua Investment Holding (朗华集团), a supply-chain services group (link to Hurun 'Brilliant' not confirmed)
profile: Hurun China (2016-17) lists 张春华 of 'Brilliant' in logistics. A Zhang Chunhua chairs Shenzhen Langhua Investment Holding, a supply-chain/logistics group he started after leaving his job in 2006, offering logistics, cross-border compliance and bonded warehousing; whether Langhua is Hurun's 'Brilliant' is unverified.
interesting_fact: Langhua launched Shenzhen's first China-Europe freight train, the 'Langhua Express' to Duisburg, in 2017 after over 600 days of planning (per a 2026 Tencent News profile of Zhang).
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Langhua, Zhang visited Hamburg and Hong Kong to study logistics and supply-chain finance after a meeting with a university supply-chain researcher; he calls his company 'industry's nanny' (工业的保姆).
notes: Identity uncertain: could not confirm that Hurun's 'Brilliant' = 朗华 (Langhua). Verify before outreach. Common name.

name: Xing Weimin
current_role: Vice Chairman and co-controlling shareholder, Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry Co. (SZSE: 002982)
profile: Xing Weimin (b. 1969) co-controls Hunan Xiangjia, a Shimen, Hunan poultry breeder, farmer and chilled-chicken processor, together with chairman Yu Ziwen under a 2012 concert-party agreement. He ran Baofeng poultry from 2001, alternated with Yu as chairman/GM of Shuangjia Nongmu 2003-2012, and has been Xiangjia vice chairman since Sept 2012; the company listed in Shenzhen in 2020.
interesting_fact: He and co-founder Yu Ziwen took turns as chairman and general manager of their predecessor company Shuangjia Nongmu for nearly a decade (2003-2012) before formalising joint control.
deep_cut_fact: Named a 2007 'National Rural Youth Entrepreneurship Leader' by the Communist Youth League Central Committee and Ministry of Agriculture, and also honoured as a 'National Model Agricultural Worker'.
notes: Company email is from the 2020 listing announcement (board secretary contact); may have changed. Search results (lixinger) indicate he is still vice chairman; the chairman is Yu Ziwen. Low media profile.

name: Xing Chengnan
current_role: Shareholder of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry Co. (SZSE: 002982); no executive role found
profile: Xing Chengnan is a shareholder of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry (chilled poultry/livestock, Shenzhen-listed since 2020), part of the controlling family alongside actual controller and vice-chairman Xing Weimin, with whom she shares the Hurun listing. Filings show she holds about 2.8 million shares and has delegated her voting rights to Xing Weimin.
interesting_fact: Xiangjia is jointly controlled by Yu Ziwen and Xing Weimin through an acting-in-concert pact, renewed on 28 April 2025 for another five years.
notes: Passive family shareholder (filings describe her as daughter of controller Xing Weimin); no public profile or contacts found. Any outreach should go via Xiangjia's board secretary office or to Xing Weimin/Yu Ziwen.

name: Yu Ziwen
current_role: Chairman and legal representative of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry (湘佳股份, 002982.SZ); stepped down as president in Sept 2026
profile: Hunan poultry entrepreneur who started out as an ordinary farmer raising chickens over 30 years ago and built Xiangjia into an integrated yellow-feathered broiler group (breeding, farming, slaughter, chilled meat, cold-chain, feed, organic fertilizer) based in Shimen county; listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He is a National People's Congress deputy and an actual controller of the company.
interesting_fact: In September 2026 he gave up the president title to focus on long-term strategy as chairman, handing day-to-day management to director and VP Zhao Kecheng; he holds about 45.08 million Xiangjia shares.
deep_cut_fact: Xiangjia's home base is Shimen county, Changde; it grew via a 'company + farmer' model to 700+ contract farmers by 2008 and is shifting to company-owned bases.
notes: Shared listing with Yu Weirong. As an NPC deputy he made proposals on edible-oil safety standards in March 2026 (reported by Securities Times, https://www.stcn.com/article/detail/3663830.html; not opened). Emails are from the 2024 annual report.

name: Yu Weirong
current_role: Shareholder and member of the controlling family of Hunan Xiangjia Animal Husbandry (湘佳股份, 002982.SZ); no executive title found
profile: Yu Weirong is the daughter of Yu Ziwen, chairman and co-controller of Xiangjia, a Hunan yellow-feather broiler chicken producer (breeding, slaughtering, chilled poultry, food processing) whose predecessor was founded in 2003 and which listed in Shenzhen in 2020. Her Hurun wealth derives from the family stake in Xiangjia.
interesting_fact: Xiangjia's main revenue comes from chilled poultry meat (about 59% of revenue in H1 2026); the founder started out as a Hunan farmer.
notes: Low public profile; appears in filings only as a shareholder (approx. 3.92m shares per Sept 2026 report) and controlling-family member alongside father Yu Ziwen (source: 2024 pledge notice https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202405151633170502_1.pdf). Best route is via Xiangjia's investor relations / board secretary office.

name: Vagif Aliyev
current_role: Owner, Mandarin Plaza (Kyiv commercial real estate developer)
profile: Ukrainian businessman (Vagif Akhmedovich Aliyev), born 1959 in Ashgabat. After 1990s barter trade in Turkmen gas, he founded developer Mandarin Plaza (2000) and co-founded KAN (2001); he owns shopping centres and residential complexes in Kyiv. Ranked 18th richest in Ukraine in 2019 (NV/Dragon Capital).
interesting_fact: The developer KAN, which he co-founded in 2001 with Krapivin and Nikonov, was named from the initials of the three partners' surnames; its first Kyiv project was the Mandarin Plaza mall on Bessarabka (2003).
deep_cut_fact: In the late 1980s he built a soft-drink (sparkling water) sales network in his home city of Ashgabat before moving to Ukraine; he later earned a degree from the Kherson Institute of Business and Law in 2005.
notes: Wikidata Q97165485 matches (ukwiki: Алієв Вагіф Ахмедович). Very low public profile; Ukrainian Wikipedia lists him as an RF consul in Chernihiv from 2007 and Ukrainian media mention a Russian passport, so handle carefully. No published personal contacts found.

name: Gregory B Maffei
current_role: Executive Chairman, QVC Group; Chairman of SiriusXM and Tripadvisor; President & CEO, Liberty TripAdvisor (former Liberty Media CEO 2005-2025)
profile: Greg Maffei ran Liberty Media and the Liberty family of companies (Formula One, SiriusXM, Atlanta Braves, Liberty Broadband/Charter stake) as president and CEO from 2005 until stepping down at end-2024, staying on as a senior adviser. Earlier he was Microsoft CFO (1997-99), chairman of Expedia, CEO of 360networks and briefly Oracle president/CFO.
interesting_fact: He was CFO of Microsoft (1997-1999) and later spent just four months as Oracle's president and CFO in 2005 before joining John Malone at Liberty Media.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School, served as president of the board of trustees of the Seattle Public Library, and was vice chair of Dartmouth College's Board of Trustees.
notes: Announced Nov 2024 he would step down as Liberty Media CEO at year-end; Derek Chang succeeded him Feb 2025. Sources differ on his exact 2026 board portfolio (some list Live Nation chair, Charter director) - verify via latest proxy filings. Route via Liberty/QVC Group investor relations. Telecom/cable background (360networks fiber, Charter) relevant to data-center angle.

name: Paul J Fribourg
current_role: Executive Chairman, Continental Grain Company (Conti); director of Loews, Estee Lauder and IFF
profile: Paul Fribourg is the sixth generation of his family to lead Continental Grain, the agribusiness and investment firm founded in Arlon, Belgium in 1813. He joined in 1976, ran European operations 1980-85, became chairman and CEO in 1997, and has recently transitioned to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: On stepping back as CEO he said: 'After 50 years and at age 72, it's time to turn things over to the next generation of leadership.'
deep_cut_fact: Before running the company he served as General Manager of Continental Grain's European operations from 1980 to 1985, after starting in merchandising roles in the US in 1976.
notes: Amherst College graduate; Council on Foreign Relations member. Wikipedia's 'CEO since 1976' is likely wrong (joined 1976, CEO from 1997).

name: Sir James Wates
current_role: Former chairman of Wates Group (2013-May 2023); member of the Wates family that owns the construction group
profile: Sir James Wates CBE is a fourth-generation member of the family behind Wates Group, the UK's large family-owned construction and property company. He joined in 1983 as a management trainee, joined the board in 1997 and chaired the group 2013-2023 before handing over to his cousin Tim Wates. He was knighted in 2019 for services to business and charity.
interesting_fact: He was knighted in the Queen's Birthday Honours 2019 for services to business and charity; he has also chaired the CBI Construction Council and the BRE Trust.
deep_cut_fact: He started working on Wates housing sites in 1975, aged 15, during summer holidays, and says of himself: 'I'm very much a builder... There's nothing like the smell of wet concrete. I just love it.' The firm traces back to his great-grandfather Edward Wates building a house in Purley in 1897.
notes: Stepped down as chairman at the AGM on 4 May 2023 (source: theconstructionindex.co.uk/news/view/wates-group-leadership-transfer); no current role found. No published personal or press contact found; the Wates website blocked automated fetches. Best route is likely via Wates Group corporate communications (wates.co.uk).

name: Mayank Singhal
current_role: Vice Chairperson and Managing Director, PI Industries Ltd (India)
profile: Son of PI Industries chairman emeritus Salil Singhal, he joined the agrochemicals/agri-sciences company in 1996, became Joint MD in 2004 and MD & CEO in 2009, and has been Vice Chairperson & MD since 2019. PI has partnered with 25+ global innovators and has expanded into pharma via PI Health Sciences.
interesting_fact: Named 'CEO of the Year' in the agriculture sector by Business Today; sits on the advisory board of Boston University's Institute for Global Sustainability.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond agrochemicals he sits on the board of Fratelli Wines, is a founding member of Brookings India and has been a YPO Delhi Chapter member since 2013.
notes: Engineering and management graduate from the UK (per PI site). Company general email info@piind.com also appears in its filings.

name: Anurag Dikshit
current_role: Philanthropist; founder and trustee of the Kusuma Trust (UK and Gibraltar)
profile: IIT Delhi computer-science graduate who co-founded PartyPoker.com in 1997 and wrote the betting software behind PartyGaming, which listed in London in 2005. He sold his remaining stake by January 2010 and has since focused on the Kusuma Trust, which funds education and children's organisations, mainly in India and Gibraltar.
interesting_fact: The Telegraph reported that in 2010 he and the Sainsbury family were Britain's biggest donors, each giving over GBP 100 million that year; by 2014 about GBP 172.4m had gone to the Kusuma Trust.
deep_cut_fact: Before PartyPoker he worked in the US as a systems analyst at CMC and as a consultant for WebSci and AT&T; he and his wife also set up the Kusuma Gallery at the V&A's Photography Centre. He grew up and went to school (De Nobili School) in Dhanbad.
notes: Low public profile; best route is via Kusuma Trust. Note 2008 US guilty plea (online gambling) and $300m forfeiture - avoid in outreach. Trust does not accept unsolicited funding applications.

name: Robin Faccenda
current_role: Chairman, Faccenda Group / owner of parent Hillesden Investments Ltd (per Wikipedia)
profile: Robin Faccenda (b. 1937) founded the poultry business that became Faccenda Foods in 1962, building it into the UK's second-largest chicken processor by 2008 via acquisitions such as Hinton Poultry, Perry Poultry and Webbs Country Foods. In 2018 Faccenda and Cargill combined their UK fresh poultry operations into the Avara Foods joint venture (6,000 staff).
interesting_fact: He was appointed OBE in the 2023 New Year Honours for services to the UK poultry industry and to education.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a National Diploma in Poultry from Harper Adams College in 1961 and later gave about £0.5m back to it; the Faccenda student centre opened in 2011 and Harper Adams made him a Fellow in 1992.
notes: Born 1937; no death notice found in brief search but alive status not positively confirmed (OBE Jan 2023 is latest dated item). No personal public channels found; route via Faccenda/Avara Foods corporate office. Not obviously relevant to energy/data-centre themes.

name: Paul A Friedman
current_role: Director, Madrigal Pharmaceuticals; Chair of the Board, Prelude Therapeutics
profile: Paul A. Friedman, M.D., was CEO of Madrigal Pharmaceuticals from July 2016 to September 2023 and remains on its board. Earlier he was CEO and director of Incyte (2001-2014) and held R&D leadership roles at DuPont Pharmaceuticals, DuPont-Merck and Merck Research Laboratories.
interesting_fact: He led Incyte as CEO from 2001 until retiring in 2014, then came back to run Madrigal for seven years.
deep_cut_fact: Before industry he was an Associate Professor of Medicine and Pharmacology at Harvard Medical School; he holds an A.B. in Biology from Princeton and an M.D. from Harvard.
notes: Best route is via Madrigal or Prelude Therapeutics corporate/IR channels.

name: John Pigott
current_role: Director, PACCAR Inc (since 2009); Partner, Beta Business Ventures LLC
profile: John M. Pigott is a member of the Pigott family that controls truck maker PACCAR (Kenworth, Peterbilt, DAF) and has sat on PACCAR's board since April 2009; his ~3.4M PACCAR shares underpin his wealth. He is a partner at Beta Business Ventures (formerly Beta Capital Group) and a director of ChemChamp North America.
interesting_fact: He is the brother of PACCAR Executive Chairman Mark Pigott; PACCAR cited his manufacturing and financial-services experience when naming him to the board in 2008.
notes: Low public profile; facts mostly from MarketScreener insider profile (Stanford undergrad, UCLA MBA, age ~62): https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/JOHN-PIGOTT-A0PHNK/. PACCAR press release page returned 403 to direct fetch; content seen via search snippet only. Best route is via PACCAR corporate office.

name: Susie Wolff
current_role: Managing Director, F1 Academy (since 1 March 2023)
profile: Scottish former racing driver (Formula Renault, DTM for Mercedes-Benz, Williams F1 test driver 2012-15). Team Principal and shareholder of Venturi Racing in Formula E from 2018, CEO from 2021, leaving in 2022. Since 2023 runs F1 Academy, the all-female series. Shares Rich List wealth with husband Toto Wolff.
interesting_fact: At the 2014 British Grand Prix she became the first woman to take part in a Formula 1 race weekend in 22 years.
deep_cut_fact: Born Suzanne Stoddart in Oban, where her parents ran a motorcycle dealership; she started karting at eight and was British Woman Kart Racing Driver of the Year in 1996-99. She left an international business degree at Edinburgh to turn pro, and the university later made her an Honorary Fellow (2013).
notes: Official site has a Contact page; also books speaking through agencies. Founded Dare To Be Different (2016) to promote women in motorsport.

name: Richard Marko
current_role: CEO, ESET (Bratislava-based cybersecurity company), since January 2011
profile: Slovak computer scientist who joined ESET during his university studies, co-authored the ESET NOD32 antivirus scanning engine, became CTO in 2008 and CEO in 2011. His wealth stems from his stake in ESET. In May 2026 he announced a EUR 40m investment in AI-powered cybersecurity at ESET World 2026 in Berlin, stressing European tech sovereignty.
interesting_fact: Under Marko, ESET said in 2026 it had scanned nearly 800,000 unique AI agent 'skills' since March 2026, flagging ~25,000 as suspicious and blocking 3,000+ as malicious; he argues cybersecurity 'cannot depend entirely on models controlled by Big Tech'.
deep_cut_fact: He began as chief software architect of ESET's scanning core and co-authored the NOD32 engine; per Starmus, in 2002 he developed an AI-based heuristic method that helped counter email-borne virus outbreaks, later extended into malware 'DNA' detection. He also sits on the board of the ESET Foundation (ESET Science Award).
notes: Rebecca Kiely is Director of Global PR and Communication (best global route); pr@eset.com is the North America press team. Repeatedly voted Slovakia's most respected CEO in PwC/Forbes surveys. Regular speaker (Starmus, GLOBSEC). Good AI/sovereignty angle.

name: Eric Melloul
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Oatly Group AB; independent lead director, The Vita Coco Company; Senior Advisor (ex-Managing Director), Verlinvest
profile: Consumer-goods investor who spent 2008-2024 as a Managing Director of Verlinvest, the Brussels-based de Mevius family investment firm, where he backed Vita Coco (board since ~2008-2010) and Oatly (board since Nov 2016; now chairman). Earlier at AB InBev and McKinsey. SEC-reported holdings relate to these board/insider positions.
interesting_fact: Told Foodinc in 2021 that Oatly was the first company in Verlinvest's food & beverage portfolio to go public, and that Verlinvest had pushed Oatly's management toward China, bringing in China Resources as a partner.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was Global Marketing VP and China Commercial Head at Anheuser-Busch InBev (2003-2008), and before that an Associate Partner at McKinsey & Company (1999-2003).
notes: Company bios differ on Verlinvest dates (Vita Coco page: MD Aug 2008-Feb 2024, now Senior Advisor; Oatly page: Senior Advisor Mar 2024-Jun 2025). Best route likely via Oatly/Vita Coco IR or Verlinvest. Investor bio pages blocked automated fetch; facts taken from search extracts of them.

name: Thomas J Wilson
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, The Allstate Corporation
profile: Thomas J. Wilson has led Allstate as president and CEO since 2007 and chairman since 2008, after serving as its CFO, head of Allstate Financial and president of Allstate Protection. Before joining Allstate from Sears in 1995 he worked in finance at Amoco and ran M&A at Dean Witter Reynolds. His wealth stems from Allstate equity.
interesting_fact: He is chairman of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce Foundation and a past chairman of the U.S. Chamber of Commerce board; he was also deputy chair of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.
deep_cut_fact: Born in St. Clair Shores, Michigan, he graduated from Lake Shore High School in 1975, and he co-founded the Get IN Chicago Foundation, focused on reducing youth violence.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Allstate national media team. Also involved in Chicago civic initiatives (P33, OneTen).

name: Maurice J Gallagher Jr
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Allegiant Travel Company (ALGT); filings list him as Executive Chairman
profile: Maury Gallagher, born 1950, was a principal of WestAir (sold to Mesa in 1992) and a founding investor/director of ValuJet (1993-97). As the major creditor of bankrupt Fresno-based Allegiant in 2000 he took control, moved it to Las Vegas and built its ultra-low-cost leisure model; CEO 2003-2022 and 2023-2024, chairman since 2006.
interesting_fact: He owns NASCAR's GMS Racing (Truck Series titles in 2016 and 2020) and became co-owner of the Cup team now called Legacy Motor Club, alongside Jimmie Johnson.
deep_cut_fact: Between ValuJet and Allegiant he founded telecom carrier Mpower Communications (IPO 1998); a UC Davis history BA (1971) with a Berkeley MBA, he gave $10M toward UC Davis's Maurice J. Gallagher Jr. Hall and gave its business-school commencement address in 2011.
notes: Retired as CEO Sept 2024 (Greg Anderson succeeded). Allegiant's own board page lists him as 'Chairman of the Board'. Media line +1 702-800-2020 per press releases.

name: Adam Clammer
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Cellebrite DI Ltd. (since Jan 2025); Founding Partner, True Wind Capital Management
profile: Adam H. Clammer is a technology private-equity investor. He joined KKR in 1995 and co-founded and led its Global Technology Group (2004-2013), then founded San Francisco-based True Wind Capital in 2015. True Wind's SPAC TWC Tech Holdings II merged with forensics firm Cellebrite in 2021; he has chaired Cellebrite's board since January 2025.
interesting_fact: At KKR his board seats included Avago Technologies, Eastman Kodak, Jazz Pharmaceuticals, Medcath and NXP; he launched True Wind nearly two years after stepping down as KKR's head of technology investing.
deep_cut_fact: Before KKR he worked in Morgan Stanley's M&A group in New York and Hong Kong (1992-1995); he holds a B.S. from UC Berkeley and an MBA from Harvard Business School, where he was a Baker Scholar. He also chairs LeadVenture.
notes: Best route is likely via True Wind Capital or Cellebrite IR. No personal channels verified.

name: Antonio del Valle Perochena
current_role: Lead Director, Byline Bancorp (director since 2013); Chairman, Kaluz S.A. and Grupo Financiero Ve por Más (BX+)
profile: Mexican businessman, son of Antonio del Valle Ruiz. Chairs family holding company Kaluz (controlling shareholder of Orbia Advance Corp.) and BX+ bank; Orbia board member since 2002. Has sat on Chicago-based Byline Bancorp's board since June 2013 and became Lead Director in Feb 2021; a ~25% holder via MBG Investors.
interesting_fact: Served four years as president of the Mexican Business Council (CMN), which groups about 60 of Mexico's most important companies, ending his term in 2023.

public_contacts.value: brennie@bylinebank.com (Brooks O. Rennie, Head of IR, Byline Bank - listed as investors/media contact)

notes: Sources conflict on Orbia chairmanship: Orbia's own governance page lists his brother Juan Pablo del Valle Perochena as Orbia chairman; Antonio chairs Kaluz. Role facts from Byline 2026 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001702750/000119312526162758/by-20260417.htm). Orbia (PVC/fluor/pipes) is relevant to energy/infrastructure.

name: Mohammed Galadari
current_role: London-based hotel/property investor; associated with Blackfriars Hotels Ltd (current title not confirmed)
profile: Mohammed (also spelled Mahomed) Galadari is a London-based developer from Dubai's Galadari family who appears on the Sunday Times Rich List under hotels and property. He bought the Crowne Plaza hotel in Blackfriars, London for £85m via his Blackfriars Hotels company.
interesting_fact: His UK debut was the ~£85m purchase of the Crowne Plaza at Blackfriars in the City of London; his Blackfriars Hotels company had £28.3m assets in 2013 (per Sunday Times Rich List data).
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. The Blackfriars hotel was later rebranded under Hyatt (Hyatt Regency London Blackfriars, 2023) per search results not directly read. Companies House officer list for Blackfriars Hotels Ltd (03504830) may help confirm current involvement.

name: Frank J Hanna Iii
current_role: CEO, Hanna Capital LLC (Atlanta); major shareholder of Atlanticus Holdings (ATLC)
profile: Atlanta entrepreneur, merchant banker and Catholic philanthropist. A former Troutman Sanders corporate attorney, he and brother David devised a methodology for valuing loan portfolios and built firms around it; David is chairman/CEO of Atlanticus, in which Frank holds a large stake. CEO of Hanna Capital since 2006, investing in technology and financial services.
interesting_fact: Through his Solidarity Association he acquired the Hanna Papyrus I (Bodmer Papyri XIV-XV, c.175-225 AD), containing the oldest known text of the Lord's Prayer, and presented it to Pope Benedict XVI in 2007; it is kept in the Vatican Library.
deep_cut_fact: Was a Foundation Fellow and Truman Scholar at the University of Georgia; in 2002 President George W. Bush named him co-chair of the President's Advisory Commission on Educational Excellence for Hispanic Americans. Author of 'What Your Money Means' (2008) and 'A Graduate's Guide to Life' (2017).
notes: Featured in PBS/Acton documentary 'The Call of the Entrepreneur'. Hanna Capital contact page invites inquiries consistent with its investment or philanthropic approach.
