name: Guo Huabin
current_role: Chairman, Jiangxi Yaosheng Industry and Trade Development Co., Ltd. (Yaosheng Tungsten), per Asian Metal Jan 2024
profile: Guo Huabin heads Jiangxi Yaosheng, a private Ganzhou-region tungsten group listed by Hurun under tungsten mining, tourism and hotels. Asian Metal describes the company as running a full tungsten chain from mining and beneficiation to smelting, powder and cemented carbide production and trading.
interesting_fact: Yaosheng's stated annual capacities include 3,000t tungsten concentrate, 9,000t APT, 6,000t tungsten oxide, 4,000t tungsten powder and 2,500t tungsten carbide powder.
deep_cut_fact: In a January 2024 meeting with Asian Metal he discussed problems in tin mine production and smelting, showing Yaosheng's interest beyond tungsten into tin.
notes: Titled President in June 2023 and Chairman in Jan 2024 Asian Metal visit reports. Very low public profile; no personal or press contacts found. Trade-press (Asian Metal) is the main English-language footprint.

name: Song Ziming
profile: Song Ziming was the second-largest shareholder of Kingfa Sci & Tech (600143.SH), the Guangzhou modified-plastics maker. At end-2010 he held about 167.7 million shares (12.01%), behind founder Yuan Zhimin. No current role was found in recent Kingfa disclosures.
interesting_fact: Kingfa's 2010 annual report lists him as its No. 2 shareholder, with 12.01% of the company.
notes: Low public profile. The shareholder link to Kingfa is confirmed, but his current role and any biography were not found. Kingfa's chairman is now Chen Pingxu.

name: Zheng Heping
current_role: Chairman, Delisi Group Co., Ltd. (Zhucheng, Shandong); Chairman, Zhucheng Tongluren Investment; Vice President, China Meat Association (per MarketScreener)
profile: Zheng Heping (郑和平) has chaired Delisi Group, a meat processor in Zhucheng, Shandong founded in 1986, since 1994. He chaired its listed arm, Shandong Delisi Food (SZSE: 002330), until March 2015. The group covers pig slaughtering, processed and canned meat, and prepared foods. MarketScreener lists his age as 75.
interesting_fact: Besides running Delisi, he is listed as a vice president of the China Meat Association, the national industry body for the meat sector.
notes: Roles come only from an aggregator (MarketScreener); not verified against primary filings. Baidu Baike was blocked. The listed company Shandong Delisi Food is now chaired by another Zheng family member (Zheng Qiankun per MarketScreener) and takes investor questions via ir.p5w.net. Hurun listings stopped in 2017. 'Alive' is unverified.

name: Jin Liangshun
current_role: Founder and former chairman, Jingong Group (精功集团), Shaoxing; group underwent bankruptcy reorganisation from 2019
profile: Jin Liangshun (金良顺) built Shaoxing's Jingong (精功) group from a warp-knitting machinery factory into a ~50bn-yuan conglomerate spanning steel structures, equipment, new materials, yellow wine (Kuaijishan), general aviation and big data, controlling several listed companies. After a 2019 liquidity crisis the group was reorganised and in 2022 control of its listed assets passed to Fang Chaoyang.
interesting_fact: He took yellow-wine brand Kuaijishan (会稽山) through restructuring and onto the Shanghai exchange in 2014, alongside Jingong Steel Structure and Jingong Technology.
deep_cut_fact: He started at 14 as a carpenter (木工) at the Shaoxing Warp Knitting Machinery factory in the 1960s, rising to workshop head and factory director; press dubbed him the 'little carpenter' (小木匠).
notes: Alive as of Dec 2022 article (aged 68); no later confirmation. Sensitive: group collapsed/bankruptcy restructuring 2019-2022 — avoid in outreach. No published contacts found.

name: Li Zaichun
current_role: Co-founder and former controlling shareholder of Sichuan Haite High-Tech (海特高新, 002023.SZ); son Li Biao is chairman
profile: Li Zaichun (李再春), a senior engineer who spent 30+ years at a military aviation factory, co-founded Sichuan Haite High-Tech with his son Li Biao in 1991. Haite grew into a leading private aircraft MRO, avionics-testing and component-repair group listed in Shenzhen; Li was its actual controller in 2009-2011 filings and later transferred shares to Li Biao.
interesting_fact: Haite started in 1991 with an investment of just 10,000 yuan, attached to a state unit, doing aviation test equipment and airborne electronic component repair.
deep_cut_fact: As early as 1983 he moonlighted as a 'Sunday engineer'; in 1986 he co-launched the private Chengdu New Technology Application Institute, developing domestic replacements for aircraft VHF antennas, filters and boards.
notes: Likely elderly and retired; no recent public role found. Son Li Biao (shared Hurun entry) is the company's public face. Alive status not confirmed either way.

name: Fu Shan
current_role: Managing Partner, Vivo Capital; Chairman, VISEN Pharmaceuticals (since 2025)
profile: Former Chinese government official (NDRC, State Economic and Trade Commission, State Council offices) who became Blackstone's Beijing chief representative in 2008 and a Senior Managing Director in its private equity group. Joined Vivo Capital in 2013 as Managing Partner and Co-CEO, later CEO of Greater China; now chairs VISEN Pharmaceuticals and sits on biotech boards.
interesting_fact: In a Nov 2025 interview he said Vivo debated 'people versus assets' for two years and decided to back assets, running NewCos whose job is 'to develop its pipeline as fast and cheaply as possible.'
deep_cut_fact: He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in History from Peking University, an unusual background for a biotech investor.
notes: Before Blackstone he was VP of Beijing Mainstreets Investment Group (per globalcustodian/privateequitywire reports of Blackstone's Beijing office). Also on Esco Lifesciences board since May 2021. Best route: Vivo Capital.

name: Luo Lin
current_role: Founder and chairman, Anton Oilfield Services Group (3337.HK)
profile: Petroleum engineer (Southwest Petroleum University; Tsinghua MBA, per MarketScreener) who left a secure job at state-owned CNPC in 1999 to found Anton Oilfield Services in the Tarim Basin. Anton grew into one of China's largest private oilfield-service firms, once dubbed 'China's Halliburton', and listed in Hong Kong in 2007. It now works for international clients in Iraq and elsewhere.
interesting_fact: Caixin reported that Anton was once dubbed 'China's Halliburton' and was a major player during the 'golden decade' of China's petroleum sector.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as an employee of state oil giant CNPC. In 1999 he gave up that 'iron rice bowl' job to start a private company selling services to CNPC itself, one of the first private entrants into China's state-dominated oilfield-services market.
notes: IR email from irasia.com (2015) and a 2011 company release; antonoil.com did not load, so currency is unverified. Hurun listing (2013-14) is old; his stake is now far smaller (~$90M per MarketScreener). Good oilfield-services angle; the 'China's Halliburton' line comes from a sector ups-and-downs piece, so keep framing positive.

profile: Ni Bingda (b. 1954) was a director of Shenzhen Sunlord Electronics, a Shenzhen-listed maker of chip inductors and passive electronic components, from Sept 2005 (per its 2019 annual report) until around Dec 2020. He is a director of Golden Success Investment, Sunlord's former controlling shareholder, which sold down its stake from 2016 to chairman Yuan Jinyu.
interesting_fact: Golden Success Investment, where Ni is a director, was Sunlord's original controlling shareholder; after it transferred 78 million shares to chairman Yuan Jinyu in 2016, Sunlord declared it had no controlling shareholder or actual controller.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. MarketScreener lists his Sunlord board tenure ending Dec 2020. Sunlord contact is company general/IR channel, he is no longer on its board. Alive status not confirmed by any source.

profile: An Mei (安梅) is a private shareholder of Ultrapower, a Beijing IT-operations and software company founded in 1998 and listed on ChiNext in 2009. Her stake (6.47% in 2016) came from a 2013 property-division agreement, and its voting rights were entrusted to chairman Wang Ning. She sold down in 2016-2018 and fell below 5% in June 2018. She has no known operating role.

name: Sun Jie
current_role: CEO and Director, Trip.com Group (Nasdaq: TCOM; HKEX: 9961)
profile: Jane Jie Sun (孙洁) is the CEO of Trip.com Group (formerly Ctrip), one of the world's largest online travel companies. She was an audit manager at KPMG in Silicon Valley and then head of SEC reporting at Applied Materials. She joined Ctrip as CFO in 2005, became COO in 2012 and has been CEO since November 2016. She is also a director of iQIYI.
interesting_fact: She spent her pre-Ctrip career in Silicon Valley. After five years as a KPMG audit manager there, she ran the SEC and external reporting division at chip-equipment maker Applied Materials from 1997 to 2005.
deep_cut_fact: She did her first two undergraduate years at Peking University before finishing at the University of Florida's Fisher School of Accounting with high honors (1992). In 2010, already a Ctrip executive, she went back to Peking University Law School for an LL.M.
notes: Known in English as Jane Sun. She is a high-profile CEO who speaks often at travel-industry forums (Skift, PATA), which makes conference organisers or Trip.com corporate comms a plausible route. Trip.com press releases now date from Singapore. Data-center angle: Trip.com is a large-scale tech platform.

name: Dmitriy Zaporozhets
current_role: GitLab co-founder; left his Engineering Fellow role in Nov 2021; describes himself as a software developer (no confirmed current executive role)
profile: Kharkiv-born engineer who wrote the first version of GitLab in October 2011 as an open-source, self-hostable GitHub alternative with Valery Sizov, then co-founded GitLab Inc. with Sid Sijbrandij (CTO, later Engineering Fellow). He rang the Nasdaq bell at the October 2021 IPO and stepped away a month later, having fulfilled his 10-year commitment.
interesting_fact: The GitLab name was an accident: he and Valery Sizov were hunting for a cheap short 'git' domain and found gitlabhq.com for sale for $12.
deep_cut_fact: He studied computer-aided diagnosis of motor vehicles at Kharkiv National Automobile and Highway University, hoping to design cars, and taught himself C by writing a clone of two levels of Mario for Windows.
notes: Low-key engineer, not a media personality; he publishes his own email on his personal site, so a direct, technical note is the best route. Spells his name Dmytro in recent profiles.

name: Deepak Babani
current_role: Managing Director, Satguru Holdings Ltd (Dubai real-estate developer); former Executive Vice Chairman/CEO, Eros Group (Dubai)
profile: Dubai-based Indian executive who spent ~43 years at Eros Group, the UAE electronics/consumer-tech distributor and retailer (a major Samsung distributor), rising to CEO and Executive Vice Chairman. Left at end-2021 and now develops residential property in Dubai via Satguru Holdings, starting with a G+14 tower in Al Furjan.
interesting_fact: He says he is not actually a shareholder of Eros despite the common assumption; he built the business as its long-time executive, including a Huawei partnership creating the 'IdeaHub' B2B device destination.
deep_cut_fact: He landed in the UAE in April 1978 aged 27, got his first job (assistant manager at Jumbo Electronics) via a walk-in interview at a starting salary of Dh2,000/month; his favourite book is 'Buffett: The Making of an American Capitalist'.
notes: Listing says 'Eros / Media & Entertainment' (Hurun India 2015), which could be confused with Eros International (Lulla family, films). This Deepak Babani is Eros Group Dubai (electronics); he has publicly said he is not an Eros shareholder, so the wealth attribution is uncertain. Featured in Entrepreneur ME 'The 100 NRIs 2026'.

name: Nick Leslau
current_role: Partner, Prestbury Capital Partners Ltd; chairman/CEO, Prestbury Investment Holdings (London)
profile: London commercial property investor (b. 1959, Cricklewood) who built Burford Holdings with Nigel Wray, then Prestbury Group, Max Property Group (sold to Blackstone 2014) and Secure Income REIT (Travelodge hotels, private hospitals, theme-park freeholds), which merged with LXI REIT in 2022. He now runs Prestbury Capital Partners with long-time partners Ben Walford and Sandy Gumm.
interesting_fact: Secure Income REIT, his long-income vehicle listed in 2014, owned 20 private hospitals and 55 Travelodge hotels before its 2022 merger with LXI REIT at a 16.5% average annual return.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of a German degree at Warwick to study quantity surveying, qualified as a chartered surveyor, and became CEO of Burford Estate & Property at just 23.
notes: Low media profile but gave an FT 'My money' interview (2015). Prestbury's general enquiries inbox is the published route.

name: Paul Day
current_role: Owner and head of Turners (Soham) Ltd, haulage, warehousing and property group, Newmarket, Suffolk
profile: Paul Edwin Day runs Turners (Soham), the family haulage and logistics business founded in 1930 by his grandfather Wallace Turner and great-uncle Frank. Under him it grew into one of the UK's largest privately owned hauliers (about 1,000 trucks, temperature-controlled warehousing, tankers) with a sizeable property portfolio, all headquartered on a 40-acre site in Newmarket.
interesting_fact: Turners' Newmarket HQ holds 500,000 sq ft of temperature-controlled storage for 80,000 pallets; in 2010 it bought container haulier Dart Distribution.
deep_cut_fact: He is a former national table tennis champion and England international; his parents built a table tennis facility in their grounds for him where the Soham team played home premier-division matches. He also chairs the Soham and District Sports Association charity.
notes: Very private family-business owner; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Turners (Soham) head office contact page. Name is common: confirmed via Turners website ('Wallace Turner's grandson, Paul Day') and Companies House (Paul Edwin Day).

name: Peter Dawson
profile: Most likely Peter Michael Dawson (1938-2024), executive chairman and owner of Dawsongroup, the UK truck/trailer/equipment rental group grown from his father Ted's one-lorry Leighton Buzzard haulage firm (1935). He launched Dawsonrentals in 1974. He died in 2024 after a short illness.
interesting_fact: In 1994 Commercial Motor reported he topped the Sunday Times list of richest truck-industry figures, owning 75% of Dawsongroup, then valued at £100m.
notes: Deceased (2024), source: https://dawsongroup.co.uk/peter-michael-dawson-1938-2024/ . Identity inferred from 'Transport' + UK Rich List; Dawsongroup is the only UK transport Peter Dawson with Rich List coverage found.

name: Sir Martyn Arbib
current_role: Founder of Perpetual (now Invesco); philanthropist via the Arbib Foundation
profile: Sir Martyn Arbib (b. 1939, Hendon) founded fund manager Perpetual in 1973 in a small office on Hart Street, Henley-on-Thames, and sold it to AMVESCAP in 2001 for over £1bn; it became Invesco Perpetual. He left Perpetual's board in 2015 and focuses on philanthropy through the Arbib Foundation (est. 1987), which sponsors schools in Slough including Langley Academy.
interesting_fact: He was knighted in 2003 for services to charity, especially education; his foundation sponsors academies in Slough including The Langley Academy.
deep_cut_fact: His 1994 backing of Henley's River and Rowing Museum was what allowed the founders to commission architect David Chipperfield for the building, which opened in 1998 (and later won a Royal Fine Art Commission Building of the Year award).
notes: Very private, now in his late 80s; no personal website or social accounts found. Alive status assumed (no death notice found). The River and Rowing Museum closed in September 2025, so avoid framing it as current. Best route is likely via the Arbib Foundation (registered charity) or Langley Academy.

name: Steve Parkin
current_role: Founder and former executive chairman of Clipper Logistics (sold to GXO in 2022); private investor through Knaresborough Investments
profile: Leeds entrepreneur who left school at 16 and founded Clipper Group in 1992. He built it into a listed e-commerce and retail logistics firm (LSE IPO 2014) serving retailers such as John Lewis. GXO Logistics bought Clipper for about £965m in 2022, netting Parkin over £100m in cash plus GXO shares. He now invests privately in Yorkshire businesses.
interesting_fact: Clipper began in 1992 with a single van delivering clothing to fashion stores. Thirty years later it sold for roughly £965m.
deep_cut_fact: In 2017 his private-equity vehicle Knaresborough Investments took a 25% stake in a small Leeds electric-heating business. He likened it to Clipper in its early days.
notes: Not to be confused with David Parkin (Yorkshire business journalist with a Substack). Clipper was a Leeds United sponsor and Parkin is a known Leeds fan. He is also reported to own racehorses, but I could not open a source to confirm it. No published personal or office contact found; Clipper is now part of GXO, so its press office is no longer relevant. Best route is probably Yorkshire business networks.

name: The Queen
profile: Queen Elizabeth II, UK head of state 1952-2022, listed on the Sunday Times Rich List 2020. She died on 8 September 2022 at Balmoral.
notes: Deceased 8 Sep 2022 (source: https://www.royal.uk/her-majesty-the-queen). Skip for outreach.

name: Howard S Jonas
current_role: Chairman, IDT Corp; Chairman, Genie Energy; Executive Chairman, CEO & President, Rafael Holdings; director, Zedge
profile: Bronx-born serial entrepreneur (b. 1956, Harvard '78) who founded IDT in 1990 as an international call-back service and spun off Genie Energy (retail energy/solar), Zedge, Rafael Holdings and Straight Path (sold to Verizon for $3.1B in 2017). He chairs the group and leads Rafael's pharma efforts.
interesting_fact: He sold Straight Path Communications, a long-struggling spectrum company spun out of IDT, to Verizon for $3.1 billion in 2017 after a bidding war over its 5G-suitable millimeter-wave licenses.
deep_cut_fact: Asked about his first job, he said he had little jobs at the Bronx Zoo and a butcher shop, but his first real 'business' was a hot dog stand he opened at 14 near a local hospital - the origin of his 1998 memoir 'On a Roll: From Hot Dog Buns to High-Tech Billions'.
notes: Author of 'On a Roll' (1998) and 'I'm Not the Boss, I Just Work Here' (2006); generally open to media. Genie Energy is the energy hook (retail power/gas, solar). IDT contact emails are general corporate inboxes.

name: Brian F. Sullivan
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, Celcuity Inc. (Nasdaq: CELC), Minneapolis
profile: Serial Minnesota med-tech founder: co-founded filtration firm Recovery Engineering (sold to P&G for $265M, 1999), then ran Sterilmed (sold to J&J for $330M, 2011). Co-founded Celcuity in 2012, took it public in 2017; in July 2026 the FDA approved its first drug, Revtorpyk (gedatolisib), for advanced HR+/HER2- breast cancer.
interesting_fact: Revtorpyk (approved July 14, 2026) is the first FDA-approved drug to inhibit all class I PI3K isoforms plus mTORC1/mTORC2; in Phase 3 VIKTORIA-1 the triplet gave 9.3 months median PFS vs 2.0 months for fulvestrant.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he built a water-filtration business (Recovery Engineering) that he took public and sold to Procter & Gamble; he holds 11 U.S. patents and graduated magna cum laude with distinction in economics from Harvard College.

public_contacts.value: Sam Brown LLC - Laura Morgan, lauramorgan@sambrown.com

notes: Sullivan lists himself as an investor contact in Celcuity press releases (published email). Biotech, not energy, but a strong serial-founder story. Not to be confused with Brian F. Sullivan of Entegris.

name: Dmitry Korzhev
current_role: Non-executive director and major shareholder, O'KEY Group S.A. (Russian grocery retailer, O'KEY hypermarkets / DA! discounters)
profile: St. Petersburg entrepreneur who, with long-time partner Dmitry Troitsky, built car dealer Mega-Avto, then juice maker Multon (sold to Coca-Cola in 2005), and in 2001 co-founded the O'KEY hypermarket chain, floated in London in 2010. He still sits on O'KEY's board and audit and remuneration committees.
interesting_fact: Multon, the juice business he co-founded in 1995 in a workshop of a former defence plant and grew into one of Russia's largest juice makers (Nico brand), was sold to Coca-Cola in 2005 for about $500m.
deep_cut_fact: He and partner Dmitry Troitsky are both graduates of St. Petersburg State Marine Technical University. Their first venture as young partners was Mega-Avto, selling cars from the Volga Automobile Plant (AvtoVAZ/Lada) in St. Petersburg.

public_contacts.value: Natalya.Belyavskaya@market-da.ru (Head of IR, O'KEY Group; tel +7 495 664-40-42)

notes: Input lists industry as 'fashion-retail', but Forbes's Korzhev is the O'KEY grocery co-founder (confirmed on O'KEY's board page). Very low media profile. The only published route is O'KEY's investor relations. Russian business: check sanctions and compliance before outreach.

name: Dmitry Troitsky
current_role: Co-owner and board director, O'KEY Group / DA Group (Russian grocery retail; re-elected to board May 2026)
profile: St Petersburg entrepreneur, Leningrad Shipbuilding Institute graduate, who with longtime partner Dmitry Korzhev co-founded juice maker Multon (sold to Coca-Cola) and in 2001 the O'KEY supermarket chain, listed in London in 2010. After O'KEY sold its hypermarkets in 2025 the group runs the DA! discounter and is being renamed DA Group.
interesting_fact: He and Korzhev built Multon juice plant from 1995 and sold it to Coca-Cola about ten years later for roughly $500m, funding the O'KEY supermarket chain.
deep_cut_fact: He and Korzhev began working together as students; their first venture was selling cars, which became Mega-Auto (1993), one of St Petersburg's largest car dealers.
notes: Low media profile; Russia-based, sanctions/compliance context worth checking before outreach. Board re-election: https://interfax.com/newsroom/top-stories/117810/ . Input lists 'fashion-retail' but he is grocery retail (O'KEY).

name: Prakash P Chhabria
current_role: Executive Chairman, Finolex Industries Ltd (PVC pipes, fittings and resin), Pune
profile: Son of Finolex Group founder Pralhad P. Chhabria (group founded 1958). He joined the Finolex Industries board in 1992 and became Executive Chairman in 2012, building it into one of India's leading PVC pipe brands with a backward-integrated resin plant near Ratnagiri. He also holds a stake in Finolex Cables, the group's original business.
interesting_fact: Finolex Industries is backward-integrated: it runs its own PVC resin plant near Ratnagiri (set up 1994) supplied through an open-sea jetty it operates for raw materials; he is also a director of Pawas Port Ltd.
deep_cut_fact: He studied international business at the University of Evansville in Indiana, USA, and in FY2021-22 received an honorary D.Litt. from Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth, Pune, for his contributions to society.
notes: Source_of_wealth says Finolex Cables, but his executive role is at Finolex Industries; Finolex Cables is run by another branch of the family, so avoid conflating them. CSR is via Mukul Madhav Foundation. marcom@ is the company marketing-communications address.

name: Dharam Pal Gulati
profile: Founder/owner and face of MDH spices; died 3 December 2020 in New Delhi aged 97 (post-COVID cardiac arrest).
notes: Deceased 3 Dec 2020 (sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharampal_Gulati, https://www.tribuneindia.com/news/nation/owner-of-mdh-masala-dies-at-97-179362). Business now run by son Rajiv Gulati.

name: Raman Gupta
current_role: Promoter/long-time director of Metenere group (Metenere Limited, Metenere (Global) Ltd), Delhi; MD role at Metenere Limited reportedly ceased Oct 2024
profile: Raman Gupta is the Delhi-based promoter of Metenere, a non-ferrous metals group producing lead, lead alloys and oxides, aluminium products and tin. He has been a director of Metenere Limited since its 1997 incorporation; registry aggregators indicate a board change/amalgamation in Oct 2024. Hurun India listed him in 2017-2018.
interesting_fact: Metenere describes itself as one of India's biggest lead producers and the only producer of pure tin in India.
notes: Very little public coverage; sources are company-registry aggregators (Tofler, Qorpiq). Company website metenere.com appears to be parked/for sale. No published contact found; any outreach would need a verified company channel.

name: Prateek Agarwal
current_role: Head of Strategic Sourcing and Planning, Macleods Pharmaceuticals; promoter-group shareholder (per 2022 DRHP)
profile: Prateek Agarwal is part of the Bawri/Agarwal family that founded Mumbai-based Macleods Pharmaceuticals, a large privately held generics maker known for affordable TB and HIV drugs. He joined the company in 2012, heads strategic sourcing and planning, and was named as a promoter selling shareholder in Macleods' 2022 IPO draft prospectus.
interesting_fact: Macleods, founded in 1989, became a pioneer in low-cost tuberculosis medicines supplied around the world.
deep_cut_fact: He has a bachelor's degree in pharmacy from the University of Mumbai. He has worked at Macleods since 1 August 2012 and is a pharmacist by training, not only a family shareholder.
notes: Low public profile. Son of Macleods chairman Banwarilal Bawri (Agarwal). Co-founder and MD Rajendra Agarwal reportedly died in Nov 2025. The IR email comes from the 2022 IPO draft; the IPO was not completed, so the address may be inactive.

name: Rohini Nilekani
current_role: Chairperson, Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies; co-founder and director, EkStep Foundation
profile: Mumbai-born former journalist and author whose wealth comes from early Infosys shares held with her husband, Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani. She founded the water NGO Arghyam (2001), co-founded Akshara Foundation and Pratham Books, and now runs Rohini Nilekani Philanthropies, which funds civil society, water, climate, biodiversity and youth causes. She also hosts the Grassroots Nation podcast.
interesting_fact: She set up Arghyam in 2001 with a personal endowment of about Rs 150 crore. She chaired it for 20 years before stepping down in 2021, and she is regularly ranked among India's most generous women philanthropists.
deep_cut_fact: She started her career in 1980 as a reporter at the now-defunct Bombay Magazine, after a degree in French literature from Elphinstone College. In 1998 Penguin published her medical-thriller novel 'Stillborn'. She also writes children's stories (the Sringeri series) for Pratham Books, which she co-founded in 2004.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly: she writes columns, gives talks and hosts her own podcast, so a podcaster pitch could suit her. The best route is the RNP contact email. The X/LinkedIn/Instagram accounts listed are the foundation's, not her personal ones. Her angle is philanthropy and civil society rather than energy or data centres.

name: Dinesh Kumar Goel
current_role: Founder Chairman & Chief Mentor, FIITJEE Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: D.K. Goel, an IIT Delhi mechanical engineering graduate, founded FIITJEE (Forum for IIT-JEE) in 1992, building it into one of India's largest coaching chains for IIT-JEE and science olympiads, with centres in India, Bahrain and Qatar. Since late 2024 the company has faced centre closures and regulatory investigations.
interesting_fact: FIITJEE's name is an acronym: 'Forum for Indian Institute of Technology - Joint Entrance Examination'; the company was incorporated as FIITJEE Limited in 1997, five years after Goel started it.
notes: Caution: in 2024-25 FIITJEE shut multiple centres; Delhi Police EOW cheating case and Enforcement Directorate raids (April 2025) over student fees, which Goel denies; also a 2024 leaked staff-meeting video. Reputational risk for a podcast guest.

name: Sudhir Valia
current_role: Former director of Sun Pharmaceutical Industries; retired from the board at the 2025 AGM. Private investor and businessman.
profile: Sudhir V. Valia is a Mumbai chartered accountant and the brother-in-law of Sun Pharma founder Dilip Shanghvi. He is part of Sun Pharma's promoter group and held about 0.6% of the company in 2025. He was whole-time director from 2005 to 2019, running finance, commercial, operations, projects and quality control, then served as a non-executive director until he chose not to seek re-election in 2025.
interesting_fact: As Sun Pharma's whole-time director from February 2005, he oversaw finance, operations, projects and quality control during the decade it grew into India's largest drugmaker. He also sat on the board of Taro Pharmaceutical (Israel) from 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a chartered accountant (B.Com, University of Mumbai) and built more than four decades of taxation and finance experience before becoming the finance architect behind his brother-in-law's pharma group.
notes: He left the Sun Pharma board at the 2025 AGM, so a Sun Pharma contact is a weak route. He has no public social media. In 2019 he moved to a non-executive role after whistleblower complaints about loans to firms linked to him, so avoid that topic. Keep any approach low-key.

name: Sushil Kumar Kalyanji Parekh
current_role: Promoter-family shareholder of Pidilite Industries; director of family holding companies (e.g., Pidichem, Pargro Investments)
profile: Younger brother of Pidilite founder Balvant Parekh and part of the promoter family that controls Pidilite Industries, maker of Fevicol, M-Seal and Dr. Fixit. He worked with Balvant in the family's early dye and chemicals trading and served as Pidilite's Vice Chairman from 1969 to 2014. He now holds directorships in family investment companies.
interesting_fact: Pidilite's Fevicol, launched in 1959, became so widespread that 'Fevicol' is effectively India's generic word for white glue.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Vice Chairman of Pidilite Industries for 45 years, from 1969 to 2014.
notes: Elderly and very low-profile. No death report found, but there are no recent public appearances, so his status is unconfirmed. Sources disagree on whether he co-founded Pidilite in 1959 or joined early. The Pidilite investor-relations inbox is a company channel, not his own; Narendrakumar and Apurva Parekh are the family's public faces.

name: Maroš Grund
current_role: Senior Research Fellow and Member of the Board, ESET (Bratislava)
profile: Slovak software engineer and co-owner of cybersecurity firm ESET, maker of NOD32 antivirus. He became a co-owner in 2005 alongside Richard Marko and co-authored ESET's new-generation detection engine; he stepped back from day-to-day management in 2011 but remains on the board as Senior Research Fellow.
interesting_fact: In 2016 he and fellow ESET shareholder Peter Kusý bought Bratislava's landmark Carlton Hotel building in a joint venture with developer Erik Mikurčík.
deep_cut_fact: ESET's own 30th-anniversary history credits him (with Richard Marko) as co-author of the new generation of ESET's detection engine, the core of its products.
notes: Low public profile; engineer rather than spokesperson. Best route is via ESET's newsroom/press team. Owners stepping back from daily management in 2011: https://www.virusbulletin.com/blog/2011/01/all-change-top-eset/

name: Colin T. Moran
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Abdiel Capital (Abdiel Capital Advisors, LP), New York
profile: Hedge fund manager who co-founded Abdiel Capital with Geoffrey Gentile in 2006 after stints at Goldman Sachs and as a partner at Chieftain Capital. Abdiel is a concentrated, long-term investor and long-time 10%+ holder of low-code software firm Appian (APPN); in 2025 it also took a ~12% stake in Rise Gold (RYES), which is reviving California's Idaho-Maryland gold mine.
interesting_fact: Abdiel has reported as a 10%+ owner of Appian for years, filing more than 40 amendments to its Schedule 13D on the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before running money he trained as a historian and lawyer: a summa cum laude B.A. in History and Economics from Duke, an MSt in Modern History from Oxford, and a law degree from Stanford Law School (Order of the Coif).
notes: Low-profile investor; no published personal or firm contact email found. Rise Gold stake per Form 3 (Oct 2025): https://www.secform4.com/filings/1424864/0001193125-25-261127.htm. Education details from MarketScreener aggregator; worth double-checking.

name: Sir Rocco Forte
current_role: Chairman, Rocco Forte Hotels (London-based luxury hotel group; 49% owned by Saudi PIF since 2024)
profile: Son of Lord (Charles) Forte, Rocco Forte became CEO of the Forte Group in 1992 but lost it to Granada's £3.87bn hostile bid in 1995. He started again in 1996 with Brown's (London) and The Balmoral (Edinburgh), building Rocco Forte Hotels with sister Olga Polizzi. In 2023-24 Saudi PIF bought 49% at a ~£1.4bn valuation to fund expansion.
interesting_fact: After losing his father's empire in one of Britain's most bitter takeovers, he rebuilt a luxury group from scratch; in 2001 the Forte trademark was returned to him, and he and Olga Polizzi won the Cateys 2026 International Outstanding Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: He read modern languages at Pembroke College, Oxford, where he won a blue for fencing, and qualified as a chartered accountant in 1969 before joining the family business; he is also UK patron of Les Clefs d'Or, the society of hotel concierges.
notes: Media-friendly and outspoken (Brexit, UK tax policy); gives interviews regularly. Company press page blocks automated access; use the press/media section of roccofortehotels.com for the current PR contact. Head office 70 Jermyn Street, London (company office).

name: Olga Polizzi
current_role: Deputy Chairman and Director of Design, Rocco Forte Hotels; owner of The Polizzi Collection (Hotel Tresanton, Hotel Endsleigh, The Star)
profile: Olga Polizzi CBE (b. 1946), daughter of Charles Forte, is a British hotelier and interior designer who co-founded Rocco Forte Hotels with her brother Sir Rocco Forte, where she is deputy chairman and design director. She also owns The Polizzi Collection: Hotel Tresanton in Cornwall (bought 1998), Hotel Endsleigh in Devon (2004) and The Star in Alfriston, Sussex.
interesting_fact: She joined the family business only after her first husband died, starting in Forte's design department where budgets were so tight 'we couldn't spend more than £8 on a metre of fabric'.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager she and Rocco worked at the airport making sandwiches, and she also worked in the Café Royal kitchens; a keen gardener, she opens her Sussex garden every year for the local hospice and hospital. She calls herself 'a complete Eeyore' next to her optimistic brother.

public_contacts.value: sophie@thepolizzicollection.com (Sophie Grounds, Director of Communications, The Polizzi Collection)

notes: Also a former Conservative Westminster councillor (Lancaster Gate). Mother of TV's 'Hotel Inspector' Alex Polizzi. Best route: Polizzi Collection comms director.

name: The Marquess of Salisbury
current_role: 7th Marquess of Salisbury (Robert Gascoyne-Cecil); owner of Hatfield House estate; chairman of the Constitution Reform Group
profile: Robert Gascoyne-Cecil (b. 1946), Eton and Oxford, was a merchant banker, MP for South Dorset (1979-87) and Leader of the House of Lords (1994-97). He succeeded as 7th Marquess in 2003; his wealth is the Hatfield House estate and art collection. He chairs the Constitution Reform Group and Reaction and is a Knight of the Garter (2019).
interesting_fact: Hatfield House, his family seat, was once home to Elizabeth I and was given to the Cecils by James I in exchange for the family's house Theobalds.
deep_cut_fact: In 2020 he published a book on Victorian war artist William Simpson and the Afghan Boundary Commission, the survey that nearly sparked war with Russia in 1885; he also wrote for The Spectator as 'Robert Salisbury'.
notes: Aged 80. Press email is for the Hatfield estate (Gascoyne). Retired from the Lords in 2017; stepped down as Chancellor of University of Hertfordshire Nov 2025.

name: Priya Paul
current_role: Chairperson & Executive Director, Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels Ltd (The Park Hotels)
profile: Kolkata-born hotelier (b. 1967) who leads Apeejay Surrendra Park Hotels, the hospitality arm of the family Apeejay Surrendra Group, operating The Park and Zone by The Park boutique hotels and Flurys. She succeeded her father Surrendra Paul as chair of the hospitality division in 1990; the company is now listed in India.
interesting_fact: Awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honour, in January 2012 for trade and industry.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Wellesley College she started at 21 as marketing manager of The Park New Delhi, working under her father, before taking over as chair in 1990.
notes: Listed company (NSE: PARKHOTELS); IR email is company's. She also sits on the boards of DLF Ltd and Apeejay Shipping per search results. Net worth source listed as 'Appejay Surender' = Apeejay Surrendra Group.

name: Wang Muqing
current_role: Founder and former chairman of China ZhengTong Auto Services (HKEX: 1728); no current role confirmed
profile: Wang Muqing founded China ZhengTong Auto Services, a luxury-car dealership group (Wuhan-based, HK-listed) and served as its chairman until September 2021, when Wang Mingcheng took over after state-owned Xiamen C&D/ITG interests moved in. Xiamen ITG later took majority, then over 90%, control (2025).
interesting_fact: He stepped down as ZhengTong chairman effective 9 September 2021 after more than two decades building the dealership group; the company has since been taken over by Xiamen state capital.
notes: Low public profile; no longer runs ZhengTong. Current activities and contacts not found. Hurun/Forbes listings date to 2019-2020.

name: Liu Yanguo
profile: Listed on Hurun China Rich List 2008-2013 (real estate/investments, company 'Ximeng'). No source found identifying the person or company.
notes: Three searches (Chinese name with Ximeng/熙盟/锡盟 variants, Hurun + real estate) returned nothing about this person. The company's Chinese name is unknown; 'Ximeng' could mean 锡盟 (Xilingol League, Inner Mongolia), but this is unverified. Dropped off the list after 2013.

name: Rong Xiuli
current_role: Chairman, Vanchip (Tianjin) Technology (唯捷创芯, 688153.SH, STAR Market) per 2022 report; founder of Beijing Tianyu Langtong (K-Touch phones)
profile: Engineer turned phone distributor who founded Beijing Tianyu Langtong in 2002 and built the K-Touch (天语) brand, which shipped ~21m handsets in 2008 and made her a Hurun IT-list member. As K-Touch faded in the smartphone era she shifted upstream: Vanchip, founded 2010, designs RF power amplifiers for Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo and Honor and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2022.
interesting_fact: Dubbed the 'godmother of shanzhai phones', she built K-Touch by combining MediaTek chips, BYD batteries and Foxconn assembly; in 2019 MediaTek invested in her chip firm Vanchip and dissolved its own PA unit.
deep_cut_fact: She entered Hunan University at 16 to study internal combustion engines and was first assigned to a tractor research institute to develop tractors, earning about 100 yuan a month, before leaving to sell phones.
notes: Chairman title from a 2022 article; not re-confirmed in 2025-26 filings. IR email from Vanchip's 2024 results-briefing notice; board secretary Zhao Yanping handled IR in Dec 2025. Very low media profile.

name: Chen Tieming
current_role: Chairman, Dazhou Holding Group Co. Ltd. (Xiamen); also Chairman, Great Wall International ACG Co., Ltd.
profile: Xiamen-based property and investment entrepreneur behind Dazhou (大洲) Group, listed on Hurun China in 2009-2012. MarketScreener lists him (as Tie Ming Chen, 63) as chairman of Dazhou Holding Group, Zhangzhou Dazhou Real Estate Development and Xiamen Binjiang Asset Management, and as chairman of Shenzhen-listed Great Wall International ACG since Dec 2020.
interesting_fact: Beyond real estate he chairs Great Wall International ACG, a listed animation/comics/games company, and previously sat on the supervisory board of Xiamen Bank (2017-2024 per bio).
notes: Match is by pinyin name plus Dazhou company name; the Chinese name 陈铁铭 is not shown on the MarketScreener page. notes: Unverifiable from this environment (Baidu Baike blocked, no Wikipedia page). Long Hurun tenure suggests an established regional developer, but treat identity as unconfirmed. Real estate is not a strong podcast fit.

name: Lin Kaiwen
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO (legal representative), Shanghai Kaiquan Pump (Group) Co., Ltd.
profile: Lin Kaiwen (林凯文) founded Shanghai Kaiquan Pump in the mid-1990s; it was registered in July 1996 and is headquartered in Jiading, Shanghai. It grew into one of China's largest private pump groups, designing and making pumps, water-supply equipment and pump control systems. He has been on Hurun's China rich list every year since 2006 and still leads the group.
interesting_fact: Kaiquan sells through its own direct-sales model and has been recognised as a 'National Enterprise Technology Centre', claiming more than 700 technology patents. Large pumps like its products run municipal water, power plants and cooling systems.
notes: Very low media profile; I found no interviews. The company site (kaiquan.com.cn) did not load from here. Note that kaiquan.com is a different, unrelated pump company. Pumps for power plants and cooling are a possible energy/data-centre angle. Data aggregators disagree on the founding year (1995 vs 1996).

name: Wang Chunming
current_role: Founder/controller of Sichuan Guodong Construction Group (Chengdu); former chairman of Guodong Construction (SSE: 600321, now Zhengyuan Co.)
profile: Wang Chunming built Chengdu-based Sichuan Guodong Construction Group and was legal representative and chairman of its listed arm, Sichuan Guodong Construction Co., which IPO'd in Shanghai in 2001. In 2016 Guodong Group agreed to sell control (about RMB 2.5bn at RMB 7/share) to Zhengyuan Real Estate (Fu Yanbin). Guodong Group and an affiliate still held ~22.9% in 2023 as second-largest holder.
interesting_fact: Guodong Construction's March 2001 Shanghai IPO sold 70m shares at RMB 12.28 each (about 28x earnings), lifting its share capital from 105.2m to 175.2m shares.
notes: Very low public profile and little personal coverage; no published personal or office contact found. Control sale source: https://stock.stockstar.com/SS2016101100001192.shtml; 2023 stake: https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2023-04/10/content_1746133.htm. Not an obvious podcast fit.

name: Dai Wei
current_role: Founder, ofo (defunct Beijing dockless bike-sharing company); since COVID has run small US ventures (Seattle power-bank rental; About Time Coffee, New York)
profile: Peking University graduate who co-founded ofo in 2014 with fellow PKU cycling-club members; it pioneered dockless smartphone bike-sharing, raised money from Didi, Xiaomi, Alibaba and DST and became a $1bn+ unicorn by 2017 before collapsing in 2018-19. He has since split time between China and the US, launching a power-bank rental startup in Seattle and the About Time Coffee chain in New York.
interesting_fact: The name 'ofo' was chosen because the word visually resembles a cyclist riding a bicycle; ofo grew from 2,000 bikes on the PKU campus in 2015 to a global unicorn in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: He spent a year as a volunteer teacher in Qinghai Province during his postgraduate studies; the 'ofo' name was reportedly born on 15 Feb 2014 while he was still teaching there. He met co-founders through a PKU Cycling Association outdoor trip.
notes: Sensitive history: ofo's collapse left large unrefunded user deposits and he was placed on China's debtor ('laolai') list; avoid in outreach. No published personal contact; US coffee venture largely wound down per 2023 reports. Was a WEF Young Global Leader-type profile; best route likely via mutual tech/VC contacts.

name: Mo Jianrong
current_role: Linked by Hurun to Boee Group (保亿集团), Hangzhou property developer; exact current title not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2012-2018) for Boee, i.e. Boee Group (保亿集团), a Hangzhou-based private developer founded on 16 Sept 1991 as Huarong home-appliance trading company in Taizhou that moved into real estate in the late 1990s. The group now spans property development, property management, trading and industrial investment. A third-party profile names a Mo Jianrong as chairman of its property-service arm.
interesting_fact: Boee began in 1991 as Zhejiang Huarong, a home-appliance trading firm, and switched to property; its first project, Boee Mingzhu in Taizhou (2001), made its name. Its property arm sent butlers to train in Europe for a 'platinum butler' service.
notes: Chairman's name on Boee's site is shown only as an image; a third-party site (altss.com) names founder Mo Jianhua as group chairman and Mo Jianrong as chairman of Zhejiang Boee Property Service - unverified. Group HQ: Boee Center, Qianjiang Century City, Hangzhou. Very private; Chinese-language media is the likely route.

name: Chen Yunqin
current_role: Deceased (founder of Ningbo David Medical Device Co., SZSE: 300314)
profile: Founder, controlling shareholder and one of the actual controllers of Ningbo David Medical Device (founded 1992). The company announced he died of illness on 20 September 2024, aged 82; he held about 21.12% of the company at the time.
notes: Died 20 Sept 2024 per company announcement filed with Shenzhen Stock Exchange: https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk03/finalpage/2024-09-23/15a7f1c9-2396-4e01-b537-99518cc845e2.PDF . Company is now led by Chen Zaihong (legal representative/chairman).

name: Liao Dinghai
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Guangzhou Hi-Target Navigation Tech Co. (SZSE 300177)
profile: Liao Dinghai (b. 1963), a naval hydrographic surveyor turned entrepreneur, founded Hi-Target (中海达), a Guangzhou maker of GNSS/BeiDou surveying, mapping and marine-survey equipment that listed on ChiNext in 2011. He has chaired it since 2009 and was re-elected for a three-year term in May 2024; son Liao Wen is a director and VP.
interesting_fact: He graduated from the Dalian Naval Academy's marine surveying department and spent nearly 20 years in the PLA Navy as a unit leader and senior engineer doing marine surveying before running Hi-Target.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2015 he and Hi-Target's executives have funded a RMB10m 'Hi-Target Love Fund' (中海达爱心基金) that supports employees and their families facing serious illness or accidents.
notes: Hurun co-listee Liao Wen is his son. Relevant to podcast via BeiDou/GNSS positioning tech. Contact via board secretary office.

name: Liao Wen
current_role: Pre-IPO shareholder of Hi-Target Navigation Tech (中海达, SZSE: 300177); no executive role found
profile: Liao Wen appears on the Hurun list jointly with Liao Dinghai, founder, chairman and controlling shareholder of Guangzhou-based Hi-Target, a maker of high-precision GNSS receivers, CORS stations, total stations, 3D laser scanners and drones. Liao Wen was named as a shareholder in Hi-Target's 2011 IPO lock-up undertakings; the exact relationship to Liao Dinghai is not stated in the filings found.
interesting_fact: Hi-Target, founded in Guangzhou in 1999, is one of China's main makers of BeiDou/GNSS high-precision surveying equipment.
notes: Low public profile; the wealth figure is shared with Liao Dinghai, the public face of the company. Any outreach is better aimed at Liao Dinghai via Hi-Target's board secretary/IR. Relationship between Liao Wen and Liao Dinghai not confirmed.

name: Qian Yunbao
current_role: Deceased (died 12 April 2017)
profile: Qian Yunbao (钱云宝) was the controlling shareholder of Hengbao Co. (恒宝股份, SZSE 002104), a smart-card maker in Danyang, Jiangsu, and chairman of Jiangsu Hengshen (carbon fibre). A June 2017 Shenzhen Stock Exchange disclosure records his death on 12 April 2017 and the transfer of his shareholdings by inheritance.
notes: Deceased. Source: Hengbao equity-change report filed with the SZSE, 23 June 2017 (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2017-06-23/2d9ddce9-51ba-4b87-b463-e675958b7fe0.PDF). Not an outreach candidate.

name: Shen Jieyong
current_role: Shareholder (~2.1%) of Nanfang Pump / CNP (SZ300145), acting in concert with Shen Jinhao
profile: Shen Jieyong (沈洁泳) shares the Hurun-listed fortune (2014-2021) with Shen Jinhao, founder of Hangzhou-based CNP / Nanfang Pump, a maker of stainless-steel multistage centrifugal pumps listed in Shenzhen (300145). Control was later sold to state-linked owners; Wuxi Municipal Public Utilities is now controlling shareholder. In 2025 the company dropped the name 中金环境 and returned to 南方泵业.
interesting_fact: The listed company was renamed back from 'Zhongjin Environment' to 'Nanfang Pump' (南方泵业) in 2025, keeping stock code 300145; Shen Jieyong still held about 40.97 million shares (2.13%) as of December 2025.
notes: Passive shareholder with no public profile; the active figure is Shen Jinhao (founder). info@cnppump.com is a general/sales inbox, not personal. Very private.

name: Shen Jinhao
current_role: Founder and former chairman (2005-2019) of Nanfang Pump / Nanfang Zhongjin Environment (SZSE: 300145); reported as chairman of Hangzhou Nanfang Haoyuan Pump Industry
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur behind CNP (Nanfang Pump), founded 1991 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in December 2010; it grew into one of China's leading stainless-steel multistage centrifugal pump makers and was renamed Nanfang Zhongjin Environment in 2016 as it expanded into environmental services. He chaired the listed company until 2019; family member Shen Jieyong shares the Hurun listing.
interesting_fact: CNP was among the first batch of companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext-era growth listings (listed 9 Dec 2010, code 300145) and later bought Texas pump maker Tigerflow Systems (2016).
notes: Very little personal coverage; current role after 2019 control change not confirmed from primary filings. Alive status not confirmed (no reports of death found). CNP is now run by a different CEO (Shen Haijun).

name: Huang Zongmin
current_role: Listed by Hurun as founder/owner of 'Sanhe' (auto repair & retail); could not verify the current role
profile: Hurun China listed Huang Zongmin (黄宗敏) from 2014 to 2021 with wealth from 'Sanhe', an auto repair and retail business. Searches in English and Chinese found no reliable public profile linking him to a specific Sanhe entity.
notes: Could not identify which 'Sanhe' (三和) company this is; Baidu Baike was blocked. Needs Chinese company-registry research (e.g. Qichacha) to pin down. No contacts found.

name: Hu Dong
current_role: Founder, Chairman, CEO and CFO, Ebang International Holdings (Nasdaq: EBON), Hangzhou
profile: Born 1973; founded Hangzhou-based Ebang, which started out making communications network access equipment and around 2014 pivoted into bitcoin-mining ASIC machines, listing on Nasdaq in 2020. Holds most of the voting power; Ebang has since expanded into crypto exchange, payments and mining businesses.
interesting_fact: Ebang began as a telecom network-equipment maker and only moved into blockchain/bitcoin-mining hardware around 2014, becoming one of China's big three miner makers.
deep_cut_fact: Before and while building Ebang he was a lecturer at Zhejiang University of Technology's College of Computer Science and Technology (where he earned an industrial automation degree in 1998); he also holds a Zhejiang University MBA and Tsinghua EMBA.
notes: Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (bitcoin-mining hardware, mining operations). Company was subject of a 2020 Hindenburg short report. IR contacts from 2023 releases; confirm on latest release.

name: Yao Hong
current_role: Founder of Weidai (微贷网), Hangzhou; current role/status unclear since the platform wound down in 2020-21
profile: Hangzhou entrepreneur (born c.1980) who founded Weidai in 2010, a P2P lender that pivoted to car-collateral loans in 2012 and listed on the NYSE in 2018. The platform exited online lending in 2020 and came under a Hangzhou police illegal-deposit-taking investigation; Weidai reported repaying all outstanding investor principal by mid-2021. No recent public information on him.
interesting_fact: He started his first business in 2001 at 21 with three friends and 5,000 yuan; he says he struggled to borrow 500 yuan for inventory and a classmate lent it on the 20th call. He framed Weidai as a lender for small entrepreneurs like his younger self.
notes: Sensitive: Weidai has been under police investigation since July 2020 (https://m.thepaper.cn/newsDetail_forward_17363197). Status unknown; Hurun listings ended 2019. Not a good outreach target; no public contacts found.

name: Ding Mingshan
current_role: Unknown (listed by Hurun China 2015-2019 as real-estate entrepreneur, company 'Wallink')
profile: Appears on the Hurun China Rich List (2015-2019) with real-estate wealth attributed to a company rendered 'Wallink'. Could not identify the company's Chinese name or confirm his current role from public web sources.
notes: Searches in English and Chinese (丁明山) returned no matching biography; Baidu Baike blocked. Identity unconfirmed - needs a Chinese registry check (e.g. 国家企业信用信息公示系统) to locate 'Wallink'.

name: Shen Haiyin
current_role: Founder and CEO, Zhiche Youxing Technology (智车优行, brand Singulato / 奇点汽车), Shanghai/Beijing; current status unclear
profile: Shen Haiyin (沈海寅) is an internet executive turned EV entrepreneur: a former VP at Kingsoft and Qihoo 360 and angel investor, he founded Zhiche Youxing in Oct 2014 to build smart EVs under the Singulato (奇点) brand, which raised at least seven rounds through 2020 and made him a Hurun unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: He decided to build cars after driving a Tesla in 2014: 'After experiencing a Tesla, I felt the auto industry was bound to change' (体验过特斯拉的车后，我就感觉汽车行业一定会变天).
deep_cut_fact: Not a total auto outsider: his first job after university was at Shanghai Delphi Automotive Air Conditioning, making car A/C components; in 2000 he moved to Japan and founded three companies there before ~15 years in China's internet industry.
notes: Singulato faced funding/wage-arrears problems and was reported heading toward bankruptcy around 2023 - avoid as a hook. No recent (2024-26) public activity found; no published contact.

name: Huang Jinlan
profile: Hurun China (2017-2021) linked Huang Jinlan (黄金兰) to Zuoyou (左右), the Shenzhen sofa and furniture maker. Public sources name Huang Huakun (黄华坤) as Zuoyou's founder and chairman, and no source found describes Huang Jinlan's role.
notes: Could not confirm this person's identity or role. The company's public face is founder/chairman Huang Huakun (https://house.huanqiu.com/article/45vap4zG0ww); outreach about Zuoyou should probably go through the company. Checking Chinese business registries for the shareholder list was outside the allowed tools.

name: Huang Tengxin
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Zuoyou (Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture / 左右沙发)
profile: Hurun China lists Huang Tengxin (黄腾新) as the wealth holder behind Zuoyou, a furniture business. Shenzhen Zuoyou Furniture (左右家私) is a sofa maker with about 4,000 staff and parks in Shenzhen, Huizhou, Anhui and Sichuan. Public sources name Huang Huakun (黄华坤) as its founder, who started making sofas in Shenzhen in 1986. No source found that links the name Huang Tengxin to the company.
interesting_fact: Zuoyou registered its brand in 1995 and opened China's first 'scenario-style' living-room furniture stores. In 2005 it signed former China women's volleyball head coach Chen Zhonghe as brand ambassador.
notes: Identity unresolved. Hurun's 'Huang Tengxin' may be a transliteration or listing error, or a relative or partner of founder Huang Huakun. Verify against Hurun's Chinese list before any outreach. Baidu and Sogou blocked automated lookups.

name: Shi Weixue
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2016-2021) as owner of 'Guowei' (real estate, investments); current role not verified
profile: Shi Weixue (史维学) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2016-2021 with wealth attributed to 'Guowei' in real estate and investments. Chinese and English web searches returned no coverage linking him to an identifiable company, so identity and current role are unconfirmed.
notes: Very low public profile; Baidu Baike blocked from this environment. Verify company (国伟?) via Chinese business registry before outreach.

name: Li Lei
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2018-19) and vice chairman of Qutoutiao Inc.; no current public role found
profile: Li Lei co-founded Qutoutiao, the Shanghai 'pay-to-read' news-aggregator app, with Eric Tan Sixiao. He served as CEO from August 2018, when it listed on Nasdaq, until May 2019, and then as vice chairman. He held about 7.6% of the company (15.6% of the votes) in 2022, before Qutoutiao was delisted in 2023.
interesting_fact: He led Qutoutiao through its September 2018 Nasdaq IPO, which came about two years after launch. The app grew fast by paying users in coins to read and share articles, aimed at lower-tier cities.
deep_cut_fact: He studied while building the business, earning an associate degree in law (2014) and a bachelor's in law (2017) from the Open University of China. Earlier he was director of advertising solutions at Shanda's ad subsidiary, Shanghai Shengyue (2010-13).
notes: Qutoutiao was delisted from Nasdaq in 2023, and I found no current company or personal contact. He is low-profile since stepping down as CEO in 2019. Don't confuse him with other people named Li Lei (e.g. former ByteDance AI Lab head Lei Li).

name: Wang Yanzhi
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Gaea Mobile / 盖娅互娱 (Beijing/Shenzhen game publisher); latest-role sources are older
profile: Chinese mobile-game publisher. After stints at Kunlun and other game firms he founded Lemeng Interactive in 2012, sold it to Zhongqing Longtu (Locojoy) in 2013 and built its publishing arm as COO. He then founded Gaea, a game publisher focused on overseas markets, in which he controls about 77%.
interesting_fact: As Longtu's COO he signed the hit mobile game 'Dota Legends' (刀塔传奇), which pushed Longtu into China's top-10 game publishers.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Lemeng Interactive (乐檬互动, founded 2012), was fully acquired by Zhongqing Longtu within about a year (May 2013), and its team became the core of Longtu's mobile publishing division.
notes: Gaea Mobile (盖娅互娱) is listed on China's NEEQ/BSE as 430181; company filings are the best source for an official contact. No personal social accounts found. Current status (2024+) not verified.

name: Xing Jiaxing
current_role: Founder and former chairman of La Chapelle (拉夏贝尔); no current executive role found (resigned Feb 2020)
profile: Born 1972 in Pucheng, Fujian, he moved to Shanghai in 1994, began as a clothing sales agent and launched the La Chapelle womenswear brand, aiming to build a 'Chinese Zara'; it became the only Chinese apparel company dual-listed in Shanghai and Hong Kong (A+H). He stepped down as chairman in 2020 and no longer controls the company.
interesting_fact: During the 2003 SARS outbreak he bet against the downturn and ramped up production; when shoppers returned, deep discounting made La Chapelle a nationally known brand.
deep_cut_fact: He learned his trade at a clothing-design training school for just six months, then worked at a Fuzhou garment firm sewing clothes, staffing the counter and delivering goods by bicycle before becoming a business supervisor. He later built a 1,000-mu cherry-orchard leisure farm (樱园) in his home village of Yangdun, Xianyang town.
notes: Sensitive: lost control of La Chapelle in 2020 after his shares were judicially auctioned, and the company later faced bankruptcy proceedings. Avoid these topics. No current public contact route found; hometown agritourism project may be his current focus.

name: Sun Feng
current_role: Founder, Chairman, General Manager and Board Secretary, Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic Co. (SSE: 603283)
profile: Sun Feng (孙丰, b. 1978) founded Secote in Suzhou in June 2007 and still runs it as chairman and GM. Secote makes automated assembly and inspection equipment for consumer electronics makers and has expanded into semiconductor wafer inspection equipment. He and co-controller Zeng Hui are the company's actual controllers.
interesting_fact: Unusually for a listed-company chairman, Sun Feng also personally serves as Secote's board secretary, the officer responsible for investor relations and disclosure.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote he started out as a test engineer at Kunshan KONE Elevator (昆山通力电梯), then ran a small automation equipment factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong development zone.
notes: Since he is also board secretary, the securities office email (zqb@secote.com) reaches his own office. Low English-language profile.

name: Zeng Hui
current_role: Co-founder and ~18.85% shareholder (one of the controlling shareholders) of Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic (603283.SH)
profile: Zeng Hui (曾慧, b. 1977) co-founded Suzhou Secote Precision Electronic in 2007 with Sun Feng; the Shanghai-listed company makes automated/intelligent manufacturing and inspection equipment for consumer-electronics makers. She served as general manager from 2015 and remains a top shareholder, directly holding 18.85% as of Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Secote's 36Kr company profile lists her as founder and general manager with a junior-college (dazhuan) education, building the company from a 2007 startup into a listed automation-equipment maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Secote she did sales work at Shanghai Liangrui Electronics (1999-2002) and then was deputy general manager of Yanling Automation Equipment Factory in Suzhou's Wuzhong Economic Development Zone (2002-2007).
notes: Feb 2026 SSE filing confirms her 18.85% stake (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-02-28/1224987773.PDF); an Aug 2025 company notice mentions her separately from directors/officers, so she may no longer hold an executive post. No published personal contact; route via Secote board office.

name: Wang Shouchun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shandong Xiantan Co. (仙坛股份, SZSE: 002746)
profile: Wang Shouchun (b. June 1962) founded Shandong Xiantan in Yantai in June 2001, building it into a listed integrated broiler-chicken producer; he and his wife Qu Lirong are the actual controllers. He still chairs the company, with filings in 2024-25 showing him chairing board meetings and proposing dividends.
interesting_fact: He and his wife together held 83.68% of Xiantan before its Shenzhen IPO, per the 2013 prospectus.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Xiantan in 2001 he ran a sole-proprietor business and contract farming; a Shandong Agricultural University economics-management graduate, he was named a 'Shandong Rural Star' and an outstanding figure of Muping district's 30 years of reform.
notes: IR email is from the 2013 IPO prospectus; check the latest annual report for the current one. Also vice-chair of the China Animal Agriculture Association's presidium (as of 2013).

name: Qu Lirong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (21.34%), Shandong Xiantan Group (SZSE: 002746); no executive post found
profile: Qu Lirong is one of the actual controllers of Shandong Xiantan Group, a Yantai-based white-feather broiler company spanning feed, breeding, hatching, farming, slaughter and chicken processing. She holds about 21.34% (183.6m shares) and acts in concert with her husband, controlling shareholder Wang Shouchun; Xiantan reported H1 2026 revenue of RMB 2.99bn.
interesting_fact: Xiantan says it has more than twenty years of experience in white-feather broiler farming and slaughter, running an integrated chain from feed mills to chicken processing.
notes: Hurun lists the company as 'Xian Tan'. Shareholder only, no public profile found; approach via husband/chairman Wang Shouchun or the board-secretary office email.

name: Hu Liping
current_role: Former director, vice president and board secretary of Inner Mongolia Yili Industrial Group (600887); current role not confirmed
profile: Hu Liping (b. 1970, Mongolian ethnicity) is a finance executive who spent his career at dairy giant Yili, serving as executive director and board secretary from 2005 and also chairing Yili Finance Co. His wealth comes from roughly 79 million Yili shares built up via the 2006 share reform, equity incentives and stock dividends. He resigned as board secretary in December 2018.
interesting_fact: At end-2017 he held 79.3 million Yili shares (about 1.31%, the 8th-largest holder), worth nearly RMB 2bn at the time he resigned in Dec 2018.
deep_cut_fact: A finance specialist by training, he started out as finance supervisor at a Yili mineral-water subsidiary, then ran the group's settlement centre and was assistant to the president before becoming board secretary.
notes: Has kept a low profile since leaving Yili's board-secretary post in 2018; no public contacts found.

name: Yuan Meng
profile: Listed on the 2020 Hurun China Rich List with RMB 2.9bn (rank 1,883) as one of nine people whose wealth comes from SF Holding (顺丰), the express-delivery group founded by Wang Wei. Role at SF not found.
interesting_fact: One of nine SF-linked people on the 2020 Hurun list, alongside founder Wang Wei.
notes: Low profile. No source found for Yuan Meng's role at SF (possibly an early partner/shareholder; unverified). SF's filings searched did not name this person.

name: Guo Xiangwen
current_role: Founder and former chairman/Party secretary of Shanxi Kangwei Group (Qinyuan County coal and coke); 65% sold to Yongtai Energy (600157.SH) in 2012; current role unverified
profile: Guo Xiangwen (郭向文) built Shanxi Kangwei Group from Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke, set up in 2000 with him as legal representative. In 2012 Yongtai Energy paid RMB 2.895bn for 65% of Kangwei (a RMB 1.5bn capital injection plus RMB 1.395bn for 31% from Guo and employee share funds). He then held Yongtai shares (about 70m in 2014), and still appeared in its top-10 holders in 2020.
interesting_fact: Kangwei was a rural collective turned private company. Until 2012 three employee share-fund associations, one with about 420 worker members, owned about 36% of the group alongside Guo.
deep_cut_fact: Kangwei began as the Nanshan coal mine in Baizi town, Qinyuan County. It was restructured in 2000 into Qinyuan Kangwei Coal & Coke with registered capital of only RMB 820,000. Twelve years later Yongtai valued the group at billions.
notes: Identity confirmed via Yongtai Energy filings on cninfo (2012 acquisition report; 2015 notice that Guo personally paid the 2014 profit-guarantee shortfall: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2015-06-24/1201186581.PDF). That payment is neutral but avoid it in outreach. Very local, low-profile Shanxi coal owner; no published contact. Kangwei is now a Yongtai subsidiary.

name: Tao Yishan
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Tangrenshen Group (唐人神, 002567.SZ)
profile: Hunan-born (Ningxiang, b. 1955) agribusiness executive who rose from grain-station worker to director of the Zhuzhou municipal feed factory, then chaired Xiangda Group before becoming chairman of Tangrenshen in 2000. Tangrenshen is a Zhuzhou-based feed, hog-farming and meat-products group listed in Shenzhen; he still chaired its board meetings in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: He was a deputy to China's 10th National People's Congress and has served as executive vice president of the China Feed Industry Association and vice president of the China Meat Association.
deep_cut_fact: His career began in 1972 at the Hetang district grain station in Zhuzhou, followed by a decade at the Zhuzhou municipal rice mill, before he ran the city feed factory (1985-1993).
notes: Current chairmanship confirmed by Aug 2026 board notice (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202608281828640649_1.pdf). Biographical details come from a user-uploaded profile on maigoo.com; treat as secondary. Route via Tangrenshen board secretary / IR.

name: Victor Cha Mao Ching (Victor Cha Mou Zing, 查懋成)
current_role: Executive Chairman and Managing Director, HKR International Ltd (board effective 9 Oct 2026)
profile: Hong Kong property executive and son of Dr. Cha Chi Ming. He joined HKR International's board in 1989, became managing director (2001), deputy chairman (2007) and chairman (2020); his background spans property development and textile manufacturing. He is also a non-executive director of Mingly Corporation.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Hong Kong Arts Festival and has chaired the HKTDC's Hong Kong-Japan Business Co-operation Committee.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Sloan Fellow at Stanford University (MBA) and was named a University Fellow of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University in 2010.
notes: Current title confirmed via report of HKRI board structure effective 9 Oct 2026: https://www.itiger.com/news/1130580564 . HKRI website (hkri.com) blocked automated access, so no published press/IR email captured; best route is HKRI corporate communications or the Hong Kong Arts Festival.

name: Guo Chenghui
profile: Listed on Hurun China (2020-2021) with wealth from 'Cathay' (biomedicine). Possibly linked to Cathay Biotech (凯赛生物, SSE STAR 688065, listed 2020), but no source read in this task connects 郭成辉 to that company; Cathay Biotech is described as founded by Dr. Xiucai Liu.
notes: Identity not confirmed; do not use without verifying via Cathay Biotech prospectus/shareholder list.

name: Kwok Siu Ming
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Sa Sa International Holdings (HKEX:178)
profile: Dr Simon Kwok Siu Ming co-founded Sa Sa with his wife Eleanor Kwok in 1978, starting from a 40 sq ft cosmetics counter in Causeway Bay. He built it into a major Asian beauty retail chain, listed in Hong Kong in 1997, and remains chairman and CEO per the 2025/26 annual report.
