The AI-unicorn Daniel Levy is a former OpenAI researcher (led its Optimization team) who co-founded Safe Superintelligence (SSI) with Ilya Sutskever and Daniel Gross in June 2024; SSI reached a $30B valuation in March 2025 and announced a long-term compute partnership with Nvidia in July 2026. The 'Football' / Sunday Times 2020 entry is ex-Tottenham Hotspur chairman Daniel Levy (b. 1962).
interesting_fact: SSI calls itself the 'world's first straight-shot SSI lab' with one product (a safe superintelligence) and no product cycles; it uses Google Cloud TPUs and, from 2026, a strategic Nvidia partnership.
deep_cut_fact: (SSI Levy) He did the French prepa at Lycee Louis-le-Grand, then Ecole Polytechnique (applied maths/CS), an MS at Stanford with Stefano Ermon and a PhD with John Duchi on optimization and privacy; in 2017 he interned at Google Brain with Jascha Sohl-Dickstein and Matt Hoffman.
notes: IDENTITY MERGE: Sunday Times 2020 'Football' wealth (GBP ~421M) belongs to Tottenham's Daniel Levy, while the Hurun AI-unicorn listing is SSI's Daniel Levy; the profile above covers the SSI one given the data-center/AI focus. SSI is very low-profile; comms@ssi.inc is the only published press route. The Stanford email is self-published but from his PhD days and may be stale.

name: Andrew T. Kaplan
current_role: Partner (Healthcare), Bain Capital Private Equity, Boston; Director, Kailera Therapeutics (KLRA)
profile: Andrew Kaplan is a Bain Capital healthcare partner (joined 2009, ex-Goldman Sachs banker) who joined the board of obesity-drug developer Kailera Therapeutics with its $600m Series B in Oct 2025. The SEC '10% owner' holdings attributed to him reflect Bain Capital fund stakes in Kailera, not necessarily personal wealth.
interesting_fact: Kailera was launched in 2024 with $400m to develop GLP-1/GIP obesity drugs in-licensed from China's Jiangsu Hengrui, which took a 19.9% stake; it later went public as KLRA.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded EngagedHealth, LLC, a post-hospitalization service for chronically ill, low-income patients aimed at cutting readmissions; he was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School and studied economics at Wharton.

public_contacts.value: Kailera media/IR: maura.gavaghan@kailera.com (Maura Gavaghan, VP Corp Comms & IR, as of Oct 2024)

notes: Net worth figure is an artifact of SEC Form 4 aggregation of Bain Capital fund holdings; he is a PE partner, not a founder billionaire. Middle initial 'T.' not confirmed on Bain's page; distinct from Andrew Gary Kaplan (another Bain director). Best route: Bain Capital media office.

name: Jiang Ning
profile: Could not identify which 'Xinwei' company or which Jiang Ning is meant; no source linking a Jiang Ning to Xinwei Group or Sunway Communication (信维通信) was found.
notes: Ambiguous identity; kept minimal. Needs manual check of Forbes source record.

name: Shi Zhengrong
current_role: Founder, Sunman Energy (上迈新能源, Shanghai), maker of ultra-light flexible solar modules; founder and former chairman/CEO of Suntech Power
profile: Shi Zhengrong (施正荣, b. 1963, Yangzhong, Jiangsu) earned a solar PhD at UNSW, became an Australian citizen and returned to Wuxi in 2001 to found Suntech Power; its 2005 NYSE listing briefly made him China's richest man and helped spark China's solar boom. After leaving Suntech in 2013 he built Sunman Energy, which makes ultra-light solar panels, and still speaks widely on PV.
interesting_fact: Academic Lan Xiaohuan argues Shi's overnight wealth after Suntech's 2005 NYSE IPO had a 'strong demonstration effect' that prompted local governments across China to pour money into solar - seeding the industry China now dominates.
deep_cut_fact: He did his doctorate at UNSW's School of Photovoltaic and Renewable Energy Engineering under Professor Martin Green, the 'father of photovoltaics'; in 2009 he was elected a Fellow of the Australian Academy of Technological Sciences and Engineering and won the Oslo Business for Peace Award.
notes: Great podcast fit (solar pioneer, Australia-China story) and historically media-friendly. Avoid Suntech's 2013 bankruptcy in outreach. No published email found (Sunman site is JS-only); route via Sunman's website contact page or conference organisers where he keynotes. Holds Australian citizenship.

name: Song Jiming
notes: Hurun China 2007-2016 (tire cords/chemicals, 'Xishui'). Could not identify the company; only unrelated shareholder-list mentions of 宋继明 found in CNINFO filings. Web-search budget ran out. No facts or contacts recorded.

name: Chen Luwen
current_role: Listed as owner of 'Jinguang' (steel and nickel-chromium alloy) on the Hurun China list (2009-2018). Current role not verified.
profile: Chen Luwen (陈陆文) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2009 to 2018, most recently at about $420M, with wealth from 'Jinguang', a steel and nickel-chromium alloy producer. Accessible sources could not confirm the company's full name, location or his current activities.
notes: No verifiable sources found (Baidu Baike blocked, no Wikipedia page). Specialty alloys could be a materials or energy-supply-chain angle, but confirm identity via Chinese business registries first.

name: Jin Ming
current_role: Former President of Suning Appliance / Suning Commerce Group (2010 to about 2015); current role not publicly known
profile: Jin Ming (金明) is a long-time Suning executive who joined founder Zhang Jindong's appliance retailer in 1993, became a director and shareholder, and in July 2010 replaced Sun Weimin as president. He was widely seen as a possible successor to Zhang. His wealth comes from his Suning shareholding; he was on the Hurun China list from 2007 to 2011.
interesting_fact: He spent his whole early career at Suning, joining straight out of university in 1993 when it was still a Nanjing air-conditioner retailer, and rose to president of what became one of China's largest electronics retailers.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Suning in 1993 straight after graduating, three years after Zhang Jindong founded it as a single air-conditioner shop in Nanjing, and in July 2010 succeeded Sun Weimin as company president.
notes: In January 2015 there were reports, which Suning disputed, that he had stepped down as president; I found nothing public about him since. No personal channels. Suning.com's IR office is the only institutional route, and he may no longer be connected to it. A common name, so double-check identity before any outreach.

name: Qiao Tianming
current_role: Former chairman of Sichuan Jiannanchun (JNC) Group, the Mianzhu baijiu maker; no active public role since c.2016
profile: Qiao Tianming spent more than 30 years at Jiannanchun, one of the 'Mao-Wu-Jian' baijiu brands. He became chairman in 2001 and led its 2003 restructuring from state ownership, which made him a major owner. He largely vanished from public view around 2016, and in 2023 a Leshan court convicted him in a case tied to that restructuring.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he announced the RMB 2bn Datang Guojiu eco-park to add 20,000+ tonnes of base-liquor capacity; it was only formally unveiled in 2022, a decade later.
notes: Not a viable podcast guest. He was reported missing from public view around 2016, and in 2023 the Leshan Intermediate Court sentenced him to 5 years for bribery and illegally dividing state assets, with a RMB 400m fine (per media reports). Some reports say his son Qiao Yu took on management. Source: https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2018-07-24/1238247.html and tmtpost.

name: He Yan
current_role: Controlling shareholder of Chengdu GoldTel (Guoteng) Electronics Group and, since Jan 2025, actual controller of Chengdu Zhenxin Technology (300101.SZ, BeiDou satellite-navigation chips)
profile: Chengdu-born (1961) computer engineer turned entrepreneur. Founded Chengdu Guoteng (GoldTel) Communications in 1995 and in 2003 Guoteng Microelectronics, forerunner of Zhenxin Technology, often called China's 'first BeiDou navigation stock'. After years of legal disputes over the parent group, courts confirmed her control and she was reinstated as Zhenxin's actual controller in Jan 2025.
interesting_fact: Her group built an early Chinese satellite-navigation chip business (BeiDou), with GoldTel spanning communications, power, tax/finance equipment, satellite comms and IC design.
deep_cut_fact: She studied computer science at Nanjing Institute of Technology (now Southeast University), started her career in 1983 at Dongfang Electric, and is an adjunct professor at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC).
notes: Highly sensitive: arrested in 2013-14 in connection with the Li Chuncheng corruption case and served prison time; long control fight with Zhenxin management continues. Not a recommended podcast target; no published contact found.

name: Wang Yangang
current_role: Former chairman and CEO, China Animal Healthcare Ltd (HKEX: 0940); no current public role found
profile: Controlling shareholder, chairman and CEO of China Animal Healthcare, a veterinary-vaccine and animal-drug maker (incl. Inner Mongolia Bigvet Bio-tech) that listed via Singapore in 2007 and moved to Hong Kong in 2010. Hurun listed him with Li Chunhua (2014-2016). He stepped down from all board roles in July 2017; the shares were suspended in 2015 and the listing cancelled in January 2020.
interesting_fact: China Animal Healthcare was one of the few Chinese veterinary-vaccine makers to list overseas, first via a 2007 reverse takeover in Singapore before transferring to the Hong Kong main board in 2010.
notes: Name also romanised Wang Yan Gang in HKEX filings. Company delisted (2020) after a long suspension, and he has kept no public profile since leaving in 2017; no published contacts. Probably a poor podcast target.

name: Li Chunhua
current_role: Former ultimate controlling shareholder, China Animal Healthcare Ltd (HKEX-listed; in provisional liquidation since 2019)
profile: HKEX filings name Madam Li Chunhua as the ultimate controlling party and a controlling shareholder of China Animal Healthcare, a Chinese veterinary drugs and vaccines maker; she is described as the spouse of former chairman and CEO Wang Yangang. The company's shares were suspended and provisional liquidators appointed in 2019, so her current business activity is unclear.
notes: Essentially no public profile; source: HKEX filings (e.g. https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2018/0517/ltn20180517013.pdf). Company in liquidation; Forbes wealth figure likely stale. Not a good outreach candidate.

name: Dou Qiling
current_role: Chairwoman and controlling shareholder, Guizhou Yibai Pharmaceutical Co. (SSE 600594)
profile: Dou Qiling (窦啟玲, b. 1960), a co-founder of Guizhou Yibai Pharmaceutical in Guiyang, has led the company as chair, vice-chair and general manager over the years; it makes traditional-Chinese-medicine and oncology drugs (e.g. Aidi injection). Her daughter Dou Yaqi is now vice-chair and general manager.
interesting_fact: She holds a doctorate in business administration and is one of the few women founder-chairs of a listed Chinese drugmaker; the family runs Yibai as a two-generation team.
notes: Pharma, not energy. Company has had several regulatory warnings (2019, 2024) - avoid in outreach. Contact via board secretary email.

name: Zhang Shiquan
current_role: Chairman and legal representative, Zhejiang Shibao Co. (浙江世宝, SZSE: 002703 / HKEX: 1057)
profile: Zhang Shiquan (b. c.1950) co-founded Zhejiang Shibao in Yiwu in 1993 and, with family members, controls it. Shibao designs and makes automotive steering gears and steering-system components, with subsidiaries such as Siping Steering Gear and Wuhu Sterling Steering Systems. He was CEO until December 2017 and remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Shibao is dual-listed in Hong Kong and Shenzhen and is one of China's main independent steering-system suppliers, now developing electric power steering for new-energy and intelligent vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Shibao's chief executive for over 24 years, from its founding in June 1993 until December 2017, before handing the CEO job on while staying chairman.
notes: Low media profile; the controlling group includes several Zhang family members. Best route is via the company's board secretary / IR (HKEX 1057 filings list company secretary contacts).

name: Sheng Faqiang
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman, Toread Holdings (探路者); no current executive role found
profile: Sheng Faqiang (盛发强) co-founded Beijing outdoor-gear brand Toread in 1999. In 2009 it listed on ChiNext, where it was called the 'first outdoor stock', and he served as chairman during its mid-2010s diversification. In 2021 the founders transferred control to an investor group led by chip-industry executive Li Ming, and Sheng stepped down as chairman.
interesting_fact: Toread was one of the first companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext growth board when it launched in 2009, and was dubbed China's 'first outdoor stock'.
deep_cut_fact: Before outdoor gear he was in printing: around 1993 he quit a state railway survey-and-design institute, worked as a salesman for a printing plant in Beihai, Guangxi, and then set up his own small printing company.
notes: Since 2021 Toread has been controlled by Li Ming's group, so the company website is no longer a direct route to Sheng. Low recent public profile; I found no personal channels.

name: Chen Fucheng
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller (43.82%) of Shanghai Songz Automobile Air Conditioning Co. (SZ002454); holds no executive post
profile: Hong Kong-resident Chen Fucheng (陈福成) is the actual controller of Songz (松芝股份), a Shanghai maker of bus and passenger-car air-conditioning and thermal-management systems founded in 1998 and listed in Shenzhen in 2010. He owns about 43.8% of the company; day-to-day leadership is with chairman Chen Huanxiong. He was on the Hurun China list 2010-2021.
interesting_fact: Songz is a leading supplier of large and mid-size bus air conditioners and has moved into battery thermal-management systems for new-energy buses and passenger cars.
notes: 2024 annual report lists him as a Hong Kong (China) natural person with 'no' principal occupation/position - a passive owner with no public profile. Route via the board secretary / securities affairs office (IR email). Alive inferred from his continued listing as shareholder in the April 2025 filings.

name: Gu Qingwei
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Beijing Dinghan Technology Group (鼎汉技术, SZSE: 300011)
profile: Born 1972, a Jiangxi University of Finance & Economics graduate who spent 1996-2002 in Huawei's finance organisation before founding Dinghan in 2002. Dinghan makes rail-transit power systems (signal, platform-door and traction power supplies, train electrical equipment) and was among the first ChiNext listings (2009). Guangzhou state investor GIIC's capital arm is now controlling shareholder; Gu remains chairman and a 5%+ holder.
interesting_fact: Dinghan carries code 300011 - it was in the very first batch of 28 companies to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in October 2009; it supplies power systems for metro and high-speed rail across China.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Dinghan he was a Huawei finance man for six years: section chief in finance management, CFO of Shandong Huawei, director of Huawei's Beijing financial shared-services centre and CFO of North Huawei. He holds EMBAs from both Peking and Tsinghua universities.
notes: Good energy/power-electronics angle (rail power supply). Board secretary office (ir@) is the formal route. Source is Dinghan 2024 annual report (bio section).

name: Xu Xianda
current_role: Deceased; was a controlling shareholder and actual controller of Guangdong Delian Group (002666.SZ, automotive fine chemicals)
profile: Xu Xianda (徐咸大) and his children Xu Tuanhua and Xu Qingfang were the controlling shareholders of Guangdong Delian Group, a Shenzhen-listed maker of automotive fluids and fine chemicals. A September 2024 company filing says he has died and his shares await inheritance.
notes: Deceased per Delian Group's Shenzhen exchange filing: https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk03/finalpage/2024-09-09/77909eab-e7f8-4ba9-9d40-9d4c142dbee8.PDF (the family relationship is in the 2016 filing: https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2016-03-28/9262a952-b6b2-4e19-81ad-213be012b88d.PDF). Exact date of death not found. The business is now run by his son Xu Tuanhua (chairman).

name: Chen Zhifeng
current_role: Chairman, Yema (Wild Horse) Group Co., Ltd., Urumqi, Xinjiang
profile: Xinjiang entrepreneur whose Yema Group grew from trade with Central Asia into finance, property and tourism (Hurun China 2008-2014). He is best known as the man who brought Akhal-Teke 'heavenly horses' from Central Asia to China in numbers, running a breeding and exhibition base in Urumqi (Xinjiang Paleo-ecology Park).
interesting_fact: Claims the world's largest herd of Akhal-Teke horses, more than 300, imported from Turkmenistan via Kazakhstan to his ranch in Urumqi.
deep_cut_fact: He bred the first Akhal-Teke foal born in China and founded the country's first Akhal-Teke exhibition base; at the 2016 Huanta Rally in Tacheng he had the horses pay tribute at the opening ceremony.
notes: Horse/Silk-Road angle is the best hook. No official Yema Group website or contacts found in this pass.

name: Fu Guoping
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List 2013-2017 (with Yang Xiaowei), with ~US$420m from 'Jinfu' (金富?) in electro-optic products. Searches could not identify the company or confirm the person.
notes: Identity not confirmed: no public record found linking 富国平 to a Jinfu electro-optics company. No contacts found.

name: Yang Xiaowei
current_role: Unknown; no current role at Jinfu Technology (300128) - its chairman is Gu Qing and control passed to a Taixing state body in 2019
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2013-2017) with wealth from Jinfu, matching Suzhou Jinfu Technology (formerly Suzhou Jinfu New Materials, Shenzhen ChiNext 300128), a maker of optical display films and precision die-cut parts. The company's actual controller changed in 2019 and is now a Taixing high-tech zone administration; Yang's present activities could not be confirmed.
notes: Linkage to Jinfu inferred from Hurun industry (electro-optic products) - not confirmed by a source naming Yang. Company has had regulatory issues post-2019 (under new control). Not a strong outreach target.

name: Yan Xiaoping
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder of Eppen Group (伊品集团), a major shareholder of Guangdong Xinghu Technology (星湖科技, SSE: 600866)
profile: Yan Xiaoping (闫晓平) is co-controller, with husband Tie Xiaorong, of Eppen Group, whose Ningxia Eppen Biotech became one of China's top bio-fermentation makers of MSG, lysine and other amino acids. In 2022 Xinghu Technology acquired 99.22% of Eppen Biotech for shares and cash, making Eppen Group a large Xinghu shareholder.
interesting_fact: Eppen Biotech describes itself as ranking among the top three companies in China's bio-fermentation industry (MSG, lysine, threonine and other amino acids, largely for food and animal feed).
notes: Very private; appears only in shareholding disclosures (e.g. 2024 equity-change report showing she and Tie Xiaorong each hold 28.30% of Eppen Group). Best institutional route would be Xinghu Technology's board office via its exchange filings; no personal/office contact published.

name: Ma Guoli
current_role: Legal representative and controller, Shanxi Chenggong (Success) Investment Group; chairman, Shanxi Chenggong General Aviation (NEEQ: 834916)
profile: Ma Guoli (马国利, b. Oct 1967) is a Changzhi, Shanxi entrepreneur; Hurun's 'Victory' is its rendering of his Chenggong ('Success') Group. He made his money in coal (Changzhi Liansheng Xizhang Coal, Xishan Coal) and built a 'one body, two wings' group: coal as the core, with Chenggong Auto (mini-trucks) and Chenggong General Aviation, which he still chairs, as the wings.
interesting_fact: Chenggong General Aviation, which he founded in 2010, says it was the first fixed-wing general-aviation company listed on China's NEEQ (2015). It flies cloud-seeding and emergency-rescue missions with a 16-aircraft fleet that includes Y-12s, King Airs and Airbus H225 heavy helicopters.
deep_cut_fact: Before coal, he served in the People's Armed Police Changzhi detachment (Oct 1985-Nov 1988), then ran Changzhi Dafa Industrial Co. as general manager from 1991, per his official biography in Chenggong Aviation's 2024 annual report.
notes: Hurun lists him as 马国利 | 成功集团 | 原煤、汽车、航空 (2010 list: https://finance.ifeng.com/money/special/hurun2010/20101012/2698001.shtml). The email is the Chenggong Aviation board office (board secretary Xu Huating). 'Alive: yes' because he signed the 2024 annual report in April 2025. An aviation and EV-truck angle could interest the podcast.

name: Zhang Chunlin
current_role: Founder and former chairman of SafBon Water Service (Shanghai); listed as CEO of Shanghai Yingsu Environment & Technology
profile: Zhang Chunlin (张春霖) founded Shanghai-based SafBon Water Service, a water-treatment engineering and equipment company listed in Shenzhen, and chaired it from 1999 to October 2021. In 2021 he sold a 9.91% stake (about CNY 340m) to Shandong Gaochuang Construction Investment Group, which took control, and he left the company in 2022.
interesting_fact: He sold a 9.91% SafBon stake to state-backed Shandong Gaochuang Construction Investment for about CNY 340m, completed 21 June 2021, handing control of the water-treatment firm he had built since 1999 to a state-linked investor.
deep_cut_fact: He has an MBA from Antai College of Economics & Management at Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
notes: Low profile since leaving SafBon. Career dates come from MarketScreener aggregator profiles. No published personal or office contact found.

name: Lin Xiuhao
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun against Heiniu Investment (黑牛投资)
profile: Hurun China (2017-2019) lists Lin Xiuhao (林秀浩) as the holder of 'Heiniu Investment' (黑牛 = Blackcow). The name points to Shantou's Black Cattle/Blackcow Food Co. (黑牛食品), a soy-milk and cereal maker whose listed shell was later renamed Visionox Technology, an OLED display maker. No source retrieved confirms Lin Xiuhao's own role.
interesting_fact: In July 2016 Black Cattle Food sold its whole food and beverage business (soy-milk powder, cereals, sesame paste, nut milks) for CNY 513m to Shenzhen Blackcow Capital Management, and the listed shell pivoted to tech. It is now Visionox, the OLED panel maker.
notes: Identity not verified. Chinese search engines (Baidu, Sogou) blocked automated access, and English sources only show Lin Xiuhai (possibly a relative) as a Blackcow/Visionox director. Confirm via Blackcow Food's pre-2018 annual reports on cninfo.com.cn before any outreach. Very private, with no personal channels.

name: Qiu Guang
current_role: Chairman & CEO and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Riland Industry Group (瑞凌股份, SZSE: 300154)
profile: Qiu Guang (邱光) founded Shenzhen Riland, a maker of inverter welding and cutting equipment sold under the Riland, Rilon, HiTronic and T&R brands. Riland listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in December 2010; Qiu remains chairman, CEO and actual controller, with the company now expanding into laser welding and robotic/intelligent welding systems.
interesting_fact: Riland was the first company in China's domestic inverter welding equipment industry to list on the A-share market (ChiNext, December 2010).
deep_cut_fact: Known in Western trade press as 'Simon Qiu', he signed a 2014 cooperation deal with German welding-robot maker CLOOS at the Beijing Essen Welding & Cutting fair, under which Riland produces machines in China under CLOOS quality control.
notes: Email is Riland's published marketing-department address (not a dedicated press/IR desk); the site also has an investor-relations section and online message form. Hurun lists wealth shared with Qi Xuexia.

name: Qi Xuexia
current_role: Director and Assistant to the President, Shenzhen Riland Industry Co. (瑞凌股份, 300154.SZ)
profile: Qi Xuexia (born 1975, master's degree) is a co-founder-generation director of Riland, a Shenzhen maker of inverter welding and cutting machines controlled by chairman and president Qiu Guang. Hurun lists the wealth jointly with Qiu. She was sales director of the predecessor company, Shenzhen Riland Industrial, and now also runs Riland International and several investment vehicles.
interesting_fact: Riland is one of China's leading inverter-welding-equipment brands, with a European subsidiary (Riland Europe) and recent units in intelligent welding and industrial investment.
deep_cut_fact: She started on the commercial side as sales director of Shenzhen Riland Industrial, before the 2010 ChiNext listing. She now also sits on the board of Shenzhen HIT (Harbin Institute of Technology) Sci-Tech Innovation Industry Development Co. and is a director of Shenzhen Hengte Gene.
notes: Wealth is shared with Qiu Guang (controller, chairman and president). Board secretary: Kong Liang; securities representative: Xiong Xiaoju. Both are reachable via the IR email. Very low media profile.

name: Guan Yanbin
current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder, Kuihua (Sunflower) Pharmaceutical; no executive role since 2019
profile: Heilongjiang entrepreneur who turned a failing county brick/plastics factory into a business, then in 1998 led 46 shareholders in buying the insolvent state-owned Wuchang Pharmaceutical, which became Kuihua (Sunflower) Pharmaceutical, a major OTC and children's medicine maker. He resigned as chairman in 2019; reports say he remains the controlling shareholder.
interesting_fact: In April 1998 he and 45 other individuals paid about RMB14.9m for Wuchang Pharmaceutical, which had been shut for nine months and was insolvent, and built it into a listed national brand.
deep_cut_fact: Early in China's reform era he voluntarily left a government office job to run a near-bankrupt small brick factory, switched it to plastic products, and in 1985 borrowed money to import equipment from Italy.
notes: IMPORTANT: In July 2020 a Daqing court convicted him of intentional homicide (case involving his ex-wife) and sentenced him to 11 years (https://finance.sina.cn/2020-07-17/detail-iivhvpwx5932813.d.html). He is likely in prison; not a suitable podcast guest. Kuihua is now run by other executives.

name: Lin Xinliang
current_role: Unknown; listed by Hurun China (2014-2018) as behind 'Kerui Steel Plate'
profile: Appears on the Hurun China Rich List 2014-2018 with wealth attributed to a steel-plate business, Kerui Steel Plate (科瑞钢板). Searches in Chinese (蔺新亮) and English found no public record of this person or company, so identity and current status could not be verified.
notes: Could not identify the company or person in public sources (possibly a private regional steel firm; name/company romanisation may differ). Dropped off Hurun after 2018. Not recommended as an outreach target without further local-language registry checks.

name: Zhang Guoxing
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2010-2013 with Zhang Guoping for 'Shenda' (soft plastics). This most likely refers to Jiangsu Shenda Group, a privately held BOPP/plastic film maker whose president is Zhang Guoping, but no source checked confirms Zhang Guoxing's role there.
interesting_fact: Jiangsu Shenda Group, a leading Chinese biaxially-oriented film producer, set up Yangzhou Boheng New Energy Materials to mass-produce current-collector base film for lithium batteries (per its machinery supplier Brückner).
notes: Identity unconfirmed; dropped off Hurun after 2013. Not related to Shanghai Shenda (600626, state-linked). If pursuing, the company's battery-film business (Zhang Guoping) is the more visible route.

name: Huang Jiadi
current_role: Chairman and President, Royal Group Co. (皇氏集团, formerly Huangshi Dairy; 002329.SZ), Nanning, Guangxi
profile: Huang Jiadi (黄嘉棣, b. 1962) is founder-chairman and controlling shareholder of Royal Group, a Guangxi dairy company built around buffalo milk that listed in Shenzhen in 2010. In July 2026 he agreed to sell ~5.8% to a Shenzhen green/low-carbon investment partnership, keeping ~20% and control.
interesting_fact: He has positioned the company around buffalo milk; in a Feb 2026 interview he cited a dairy-buffalo germplasm 'chip' breakthrough and the birth of a calf from embryos imported from Pakistan.
deep_cut_fact: A Guangxi University graduate and senior engineer, he started as an engineer at the Guangxi Architectural Comprehensive Design Institute and was development manager at the Shenzhen Shatoujiao Free Trade Zone development company before dairy; he is a three-term president of the Guangxi Dairy Association.
notes: Company has an agrivoltaics (农光互补) buffalo-farm project in Binyang county, which may interest an energy podcast. Company and he received regulatory warning letters over disclosure (2023-2024). Also president of the Shanghai Guangxi Chamber of Commerce and CKGSB Guangxi alumni association.

name: Gong Xuebin
current_role: Chairman, Longda Group (龙大集团), Laiyang, Shandong (per 2014 IPO documents; current status unverified)
profile: Gong Xuebin (b. 1937) built Longda Group in Laiyang, Shandong, from his post as head of the Laiyang brick and tile factory into a food conglomerate spanning vegetables, frozen foods and pork. With Gong Mingjie he was actual controller of Longda Meat Foodstuff (SZSE: 002726) at its 2014 IPO; that listed firm is now controlled by Lanrun Development.
interesting_fact: A two-time National People's Congress deputy (10th and 11th), he received China's National Model Worker title, the May Day Labour Medal and a lifetime achievement award from the Chinese meat industry.
deep_cut_fact: His early career was as Party secretary and factory director of the Laiyang Brick and Tile Factory before he led Longda; he also served as president of the Shandong Vegetable Association.
notes: Born 1937 (age ~89); no death report found but alive status unconfirmed. Listed Longda Meishi (ST龙大) is now controlled by Lanrun Development (chnfund.com report, 2026), so the Gong family's link is via private Longda Group.

name: Chen Mingjun
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder (56.79%), Thinkingdom Media Group / 新经典文化股份有限公司 (SSE: 603096)
profile: Chen Mingjun (age 57 per 2025 annual-report data) founded Beijing publisher Thinkingdom in 2002 with a four-person team. It became China's largest importer of Japanese books and published all of Gabriel Garcia Marquez's works in Chinese. He was re-elected chairman for 2026-2029 and holds 56.79% of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Starting with One Hundred Years of Solitude (new Chinese edition, 2011) and ending with the memoir Living to Tell the Tale in April 2016, Thinkingdom published all 17 of Gabriel Garcia Marquez's works in China.
deep_cut_fact: Thinkingdom started in 2002 with just four people, including Chen and Japanese PhD student Shizuko Saruwatari, whom he recruited from Peking University's Chinese department. notes: Sensitive: Venus Medtech shares have been suspended since Nov 23, 2023. Jiemian reported a complaint accusing him of diverting company funds, which he did not answer before publication. Approach with caution.

name: Jan Hruska
current_role: Co-founder of Sophos; Oxford-based angel investor; listed as a director of Virus Bulletin Ltd (aggregator data, not current-verified)
profile: Dr Jan Hruska co-founded the Oxford cybersecurity company Sophos with Peter Lammer in 1985. They started with encryption products and moved into anti-virus software in the late 1980s and 1990s. Apax bought a majority stake in 2010 for $830m. Thoma Bravo acquired Sophos in 2019-20 at an enterprise value of about $3.9bn, and the founders exited before that sale. He is now listed as an angel investor in Oxford.
interesting_fact: He and Lammer met in Oxford in the mid-1980s and started out in a semi-detached house in Kidlington with a grand piano and a German Shepherd. A Norwegian distributor's suggestion pushed them from encryption into anti-virus.
deep_cut_fact: Their first venture was not software but a portable computer, the AC-86. It used a Harris-made 8086-class chip and ran DOS 1. Only one prototype was built and it was never sold.
notes: Low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. In January 2009 he gave a talk at the Oxford Internet Institute on Sophos's origins (https://www.oii.ox.ac.uk/?p=23198). Sophos history: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sophos. Angel-investor listing: https://nordic9.com/companies/jan-hruska/.

name: Jason Bannister
current_role: Founder and executive chairman, Oak Furniture Land (UK furniture retailer)
profile: Jason Bannister founded Oak Furniture Land in 2004 with about £10,000 of imported Mexican pine he sold on eBay, becoming eBay UK's top retailer before launching the website (2007), an airfield showroom (2009) and a Cheltenham store (2010). He grew it into a ~100-store chain, never taking outside investors, and later moved from MD to executive chairman.
interesting_fact: Within four hours of his first eBay listings he had missed 80 phone calls; within two years he was eBay UK's largest retailer by turnover.
deep_cut_fact: His first taste of retail was a brief job at 15 in a golf club pro shop, followed by three years on the B&Q shop floor and about ten years at Walmsley Furniture; the £10,000 seed money had been saved for a house extension.
notes: Exec-chairman move reported by Retail Week (date not verified): https://www.retail-week.com/home-and-diy/oak-furniture-land-boss-becomes-chairman-amid-reshuffle/7028457.article. Route via Oak Furniture Land head office/press.

name: Miguel Matias Galuccio
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Vista Energy (NYSE/BMV: VIST); board director, SLB
profile: Argentine petroleum engineer (b. 1968, Paraná; ITBA 1994) who rose through Schlumberger's international ranks, then led state oil company YPF as chairman/CEO from its 2012 renationalization to 2016. In 2017 he founded Vista, the first NYSE-listed independent focused on Argentina's Vaca Muerta shale, which he still runs.
interesting_fact: He was tapped to run YPF on the day of its renationalization in May 2012, steering the push to develop Vaca Muerta, one of the world's largest shale plays, before leaving to found Vista and becoming an SLB board member.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond oil, he co-founded and chairs GridX, a Buenos Aires science-based incubator that creates and invests in biotech startups spanning health, food, agriculture, energy and materials.
notes: Well-known public figure in Argentina; Vista IR is the cleanest corporate route. GridX is a strong rapport angle beyond energy.

name: Erik B Nordstrom
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Nordstrom Inc. (privately held since May 2025)
profile: Erik Nordstrom, of the Seattle department-store family, has been sole CEO of Nordstrom since March 2020, after serving as co-president from 2015 and president of Nordstrom.com. He led the family's take-private with Mexico's El Puerto de Liverpool (family 50.1%/Liverpool 49.9%), announced Dec 2024; shares were delisted from the NYSE on 20 May 2025.
interesting_fact: The $6.25bn take-private was the family's second attempt; a 2018 buyout bid was rejected by the board.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 working in the stockroom of Nordstrom's Seattle flagship, and from 1979 sold shoes in the shoe department through high school and college; he holds a business degree from UW's Foster School.
notes: Company now private; press via Nordstrom PR.

name: Jack Hightower
current_role: Founder and former Chairman/CEO, HighPeak Energy (NASDAQ: HPK); retired 15 Sept 2025, remains a major shareholder
profile: Texas oilman with 50+ years in E&P who founded HighPeak Energy, a Midland Basin (Permian) producer formed in 2020 via his SPAC Pure Acquisition Corp. He serially built and sold E&P companies: Enertex (1991-94), Titan Exploration (1995), which became Pure Resources (taken in by Unocal in 2002), Celero Energy I and II, and Bluestem Energy. He retired as CEO/chairman in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: Pure Resources, which grew out of the Titan Exploration he founded in 1995, became the 11th-largest publicly traded independent E&P company in North America before Unocal bought out minority shareholders in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: A 1970 Texas Tech graduate (BBA degrees in Administrative Finance and in Money, Banking & Investments), he chaired both Pure Resources (until Unocal's 2002 buyout) and, 15 years later, Pure Acquisition Corp. (2017), the SPAC that took HighPeak public.
notes: Retired from HighPeak in Sept 2025 (CEO now Michael Hollis). No personal public channels found; company contact is the only published route and may not forward. Not to be confused with the late Texas congressman Jack Hightower (d. 2013).

name: Jay C. Horgen
current_role: President and Chief Executive Officer and board member, Affiliated Managers Group (NYSE: AMG)
profile: Jay Horgen runs AMG, the asset-management firm that takes stakes in independent investment firms (its 'Affiliates'). He joined in 2007 and led new investments, served as CFO from 2011 to 2019, then became President and CEO in 2019. Before AMG he spent 1993-2005 as an asset-management investment banker at Goldman Sachs and Merrill Lynch.
interesting_fact: He became AMG's CEO in 2019, after serving as its CFO from 2011 to 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining AMG in 2007 he founded his own private equity firm, Eastside Partners, and served as its Managing Director. He holds a Yale B.A. in Economics and Mathematics.
notes: Best route: AMG press office (pr@amg.com).

name: Manish Mahendra Choksi
current_role: Non-Executive Vice Chairman (Promoter), Asian Paints Ltd
profile: Manish Choksi (58), a member of the Choksi promoter family of Asian Paints - India's largest paint maker, founded in a Mumbai garage in 1942 by four friends including Chimanlal Choksi - joined the company in 1992 and rose through sales, supply chain, IT, chemicals, HR and international business. He became a non-executive director in 2018 and is now Vice Chairman.
interesting_fact: As President of International Business, IT, HR and Chemicals he led Asian Paints' digital transformation and its entry into home improvement, and was instrumental in restructuring its joint ventures with US coatings giant PPG Industries.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MBA and a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the University of Houston; a recognised IT leader, he has served on the advisory boards of IBM and SAP and is an active angel investor.
notes: Data said 'Chemicals/Petrochemicals'; his wealth is from Asian Paints (paints/coatings). Angel investor and IT/digital background make him a decent podcast fit. Route via Asian Paints investor relations / company secretary.

name: Wu Jianlong
current_role: Actual controller of Zhejiang Sunflower Great Health (300111.SZ, formerly Zhejiang Sunflower Light Energy / 'Sunowe'); chairman of Zhejiang Longhua New Century Real Estate
profile: Wu Jianlong (吴建龙, b. 1967, Shaoxing) founded Zhejiang Sunflower Light Energy (向日葵, brand Sunowe), a solar-cell and module maker he chaired when it listed on ChiNext in 2010. In 2019-20 the company sold its PV assets and bought his Beide Pharmaceutical, becoming Sunflower Great Health. He remains actual controller; Wu Shaoqin is now the legal representative.
interesting_fact: Rather than ride out the solar shakeout, he turned his listed solar company into a pharmaceutical business. The PV unit went to his private Shaoxing Sunflower Investment, and the listed company took over Zhejiang Beide Pharma, which he had already chaired since at least 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he worked for the Huashe town government in Shaoxing County. He later earned an EMBA from Zhongnan University of Economics and Law and was a Shaoxing County people's congress deputy (2010 annual report bio).
notes: Hurun 2021: 吴建龙 | 向日葵光能 | b.1967 Shaoxing | RMB 2.6bn. 'Sunowe' is Sunflower's English brand/domain, not a separate firm. The IR email belongs to board secretary Li Lan (published in the annual report). 'Alive: yes': he is named as actual controller in the 2025 annual report and in a Sept 2026 share-pledge release. He holds Hong Kong residency. Not the Taiwanese basketball coach.

name: Weng Nandao
profile: Weng Nandao (翁南道) appeared on the Hurun China list from 2008 to 2010 with wealth attributed to Yigao Group (亿高集团), in IT and property. He has not been listed since 2010. I could not verify his current status or role before the web search budget ran out.
notes: Off Hurun since 2010 and has no listed-company footprint I could check, so this needs a follow-up Chinese-language search. Not researched further.

name: Wang Hua
profile: Wang Hua (王华) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List 2005-2013 with wealth attributed to 'Jinsheng' (金升), a furniture business. The name is extremely common and no verifiable source linking a Wang Hua to a furniture company called Jinsheng was found.
notes: Identity unresolved; Hurun listing lapsed after 2013. Needs company full name/city from the original Hurun entry or a corporate-registry check.

name: Huo Dongling
current_role: Chairman & Executive Director, Comba Telecom Systems Holdings (2342.HK)
profile: Huo Dongling (霍东龄, known in HK as Tony Fok Tung Ling, aged 69) co-founded Guangzhou-based Comba Telecom in 1997 after years trading telecom equipment; it became a major global supplier of base-station antennas, wireless access and DAS/indoor-coverage systems for mobile operators. He still chairs the board and leads group strategy.
interesting_fact: He was named Hong Kong CEO of the Year at the CNBC Asia Business Leader Awards 2006.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as a technical engineer (1982-87) at the Guangdong Post & Telecom Bureau's Microwave Telecommunications Main Station, and graduated in microwave communications from the Beijing Institute of Posts and Telecommunications in 1986.
notes: Hurun pairs him with Chen Jingna. Uses the English name Fok Tung Ling in HKEX filings. Telecom-infrastructure angle (5G/Open RAN) fits a data/energy-infrastructure podcast. No published IR email found on the site; HKEX annual reports list company secretary contacts.

name: Yang Wenjiang
current_role: Founder, Chairman & General Manager, Guangzhou KingTeller Technology Co., Ltd. (御银股份, SZSE: 002177)
profile: Founded KingTeller, a Guangzhou maker of ATMs and financial self-service equipment, and is its controlling shareholder (~13.7% direct stake); resumed chairman/GM role in July 2023.
interesting_fact: Founder and controlling shareholder of one of China's domestic ATM makers.
notes: No public personal channels found; route via company board secretary.

name: Liang Yaohui
current_role: None (former chairman, Oasis/Aoweisi Group, Dongguan; imprisoned)
profile: Dongguan-born (1967) businessman who chaired the Oasis (Aoweisi) Group, owner of Dongguan's Prince Hotel and Zhongyuan Petroleum, and was a National People's Congress deputy; Hurun put his wealth at about RMB 2bn in 2008. He was removed as NPC deputy in 2014 and sentenced to life imprisonment in 2017.
notes: NOT a suitable outreach target: convicted in 2017 (life sentence) in the Dongguan Prince Hotel case; source zh.wikipedia.org/wiki/梁耀辉. Hurun listing (2007-2013) predates this. Recommend dropping from the list.

name: Li Lianjie (Jet Li)
current_role: Martial-arts film star; founder of the One Foundation (Shenzhen One Foundation charity)
profile: Li Lianjie (Jet Li, b. 1963, Beijing), a five-time Chinese national wushu champion, became an international film star (Once Upon a Time in China, Hero, Fearless). Hurun listed him with wife Nina Li Chi for investments/entertainment. He founded the One Foundation in 2007, co-founded Taiji Zen with Jack Ma, and is a Singapore citizen.
interesting_fact: He founded the One Foundation in 2007 after nearly dying in the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami in the Maldives; in 2011 it became China's first private charitable fundraising foundation.
deep_cut_fact: His new book distils ten insights from his career and his 32-year Buddhist practice; at 11 he was a member of the 1974 Chinese national wushu team that toured the United States.
notes: Identity inferred from Hurun pairing with 'Li Zhi' (Nina Li Chi) and investments/entertainment; Hurun's 'Yuandong' label could not be matched to a company. Facebook/YouTube/TikTok also linked from jetli.world. Book tour suggests a publisher publicity route.

name: Li Chengwen
current_role: Listed as owner of Fato (low-voltage electrical equipment) on the Hurun China list (2007-2014). Likely Huatong (FATO) Group of Wenzhou, Zhejiang, but his current role is not verified.
profile: Li Chengwen (李成文) appeared on the Hurun China Rich List from 2007 to 2014 with wealth from Fato, a low-voltage electrical equipment maker. A company called Huatong (FATO) Group, founded in 1987 in Wenzhou, makes low-voltage apparatus, distribution boxes and voltage regulators. No source directly links him to that firm or describes his current activities.
interesting_fact: FATO comes from the Wenzhou/Yueqing low-voltage electrical cluster that also produced Chint and Delixi. Directory listings say FATO makes more than 2,000 types of low-voltage electrical apparatus.
notes: Not to be confused with Li Chengwen (b. 1955), the Chinese diplomat and former ambassador to Saudi Arabia. Off the Hurun list since 2014. The identity link to FATO is unconfirmed. Grid and electrical-equipment angle if confirmed.

name: Xu Baojin
current_role: Chairman and president of Jinhui Holding Group (金晖控股集团, Shaoxing), per 2015 filings; former vice chairman of Weiming Biomedical
profile: Xu Baojin (徐宝金, b. July 1960, Shaoxing) built Jinhui Holding Group, a Shaoxing private group in chemical fibre, property and investment; he owned 90% of it in 2015. Through Jinhui he invested in companies including Juneyao Airlines and Weiming Biomedical, where he was vice chairman when Weiming was injected into Wanchang Technology (002581) in 2015. Hurun listed him in 2009-10.
interesting_fact: His Jinhui Holding appeared among the pre-IPO investors disclosed in Shanghai budget carrier Juneyao Airlines' 2015 IPO documents. Those documents list Xu as Jinhui's 90% owner, chairman and president.
deep_cut_fact: He came out of Shaoxing's textile boom: a business-management graduate of Hangzhou Commercial College, he was general manager of the Shaoxing County Chemical Fibre Company from 1991 to 1995 before building Jinhui.
notes: Hurun 2009/2010 (hurun.net): 徐宝金 | 金晖控股集团 | chemical fibre, property, investment | b.1960, Shaoxing. Identity confirmed via Wanchang Technology's 2015 restructuring report and Juneyao's IPO appendix. In 2017 his Shaoxing Jinhui Yueshang partnership filed a stake-reduction report on Weiming (002581). No company website or contact found; private.

name: He Qinghua
profile: Hurun China (2007 to 2020) lists He Qinghua (何清华) with real-estate wealth from 'Dijing' (likely 帝景, a property developer). I could not identify the company or person; note that a different He Qinghua founded Sunward Intelligent Equipment (construction machinery).
notes: Unresolved: the web search quota ran out before research. Do not confuse him with He Qinghua of Sunward (山河智能), a Central South University professor, who is a different person. Needs a follow-up search.

name: Chen Desong
current_role: Former chairman and actual controller of Chunghsin Technology Group (Zhongxin Keji, SSE: 603996), Taizhou, Zhejiang; no longer controller
profile: Chen Desong co-founded Chunghsin Technology in Taizhou, Zhejiang (2007, with Jiang Zhenhui), an electronics ODM making flat-panel TVs, notebooks, tablets and phones that listed in Shanghai in 2015. He was chairman and legal representative, but the group's parent, Chunghsin Industry Group, later went into bankruptcy liquidation, and regulators named him the 'former actual controller' in 2023.
interesting_fact: Chunghsin grew from a 2007 Taizhou start-up into a Shanghai-listed contract manufacturer of TVs, notebooks, tablets and phones within about eight years.
notes: Not recommended for outreach. A 2023 filing says the CSRC warned and fined former controllers Chen Desong and Jiang Zhenhui RMB 1.6m each and imposed 10-year securities-market bans over undisclosed related-party fund occupation (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202311171611365228_1.pdf). The parent group was ordered into bankruptcy liquidation (2021). Wealth figure is likely obsolete.

name: Yang Zewen
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Nanfang Ventilator / Nanfeng Co. (300004.SZ), Foshan; family sold down below 5% in Dec 2022
profile: Nanhai (Foshan) native who in 1988, aged 42, founded a school-run factory making building fans that became Nanfang Ventilator, a leading maker of ventilation systems for metros and nuclear power plants. The Yang family took full ownership by 2005 and listed it among the first 28 ChiNext stocks in 2009 (code 300004). In Dec 2022 he and son Yang Zijiang sold 32m shares, exiting as 5%+ holders.
interesting_fact: Nanfang Ventilator was ticker 300004, one of the inaugural batch of companies on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in Oct 2009; its pivot to subway and nuclear-plant ventilation came in 1998 at the urging of his then 27-year-old son, a Xi'an Jiaotong nuclear graduate.
deep_cut_fact: At IPO time he drew a chairman's salary of just RMB 150,000 a year, and the family had lent the company RMB 18.58m that was converted into equity in 2005; he let his sons front the 2009 IPO roadshow while he stayed out of view.
notes: Born c.1946; alive as of the Dec 2022 share-transfer filing (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202212211581267520_1.pdf). Very private family that rarely gives interviews; company now under new control (Li Jie), so its IR is not his channel.

name: Zheng Songxing
current_role: Linked by Hurun to 'CSC' (real estate); not confirmed
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2014-2021) for CSC (real estate), with Zheng Jiawen. Searches did not identify the company's full Chinese name or any public profile of Zheng Songxing (郑松兴).
notes: Could not identify which 'CSC' this is. Research was cut short when the shared web-search budget ran out; worth a follow-up in Chinese sources (e.g. Hurun list pages, Qichacha for 郑松兴).

name: Song Qi
current_role: Co-founder and director, Renrenle Commercial Group (SZSE: 002336); director of regional Renrenle subsidiaries
profile: Ms. Song Qi co-founded Shenzhen supermarket chain Renrenle (Ren Ren Le) in 1996 and served as its vice chairman and vice president; by 2008 it ran about 100 hypermarkets and community supermarkets in 23 Chinese cities with revenue above CNY 6 billion, and listed in Shenzhen in 2010. After years of losses, a 2025 report said the chain was preparing to exit the A-share market.
interesting_fact: Renrenle was once Shenzhen's flagship home-grown retailer, competing head-on with Walmart and Carrefour in southern China.
notes: Low public profile; bio from MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/QI-SONG-A10QG0/), which says she founded Renrenle in 1996 (other sources credit He Jinming as founder). Company is shrinking/delisting, so wealth figure may be stale. No personal channels found.

name: Lu Tingxiu
current_role: Founder of China Electric Equipment Group (CEEG, Nanjing transformer maker) and co-founder/former chairman-CEO of China Sunergy (ex-NASDAQ: CSUN); current role unverified
profile: Lu Tingxiu (陆廷秀, b. 1960, Zhenjiang, Jiangsu) built CEEG (中电电气) from 1991 into a major power-transformer maker. In 2004 he co-founded solar-cell maker China Sunergy in Nanjing, which listed on NASDAQ in May 2007. He chaired CSUN from 2007 and returned as its CEO in September 2014, retiring from CEEG executive posts. Hurun listed him from 2012 to 2017.
interesting_fact: China Sunergy's CTO from its 2004 founding was Dr. Jianhua Zhao, formerly an associate professor at UNSW's Centre of Excellence for Advanced Silicon Photovoltaics, the lab known for record-efficiency silicon cells. That makes it an early Chinese solar firm with direct UNSW lineage.
deep_cut_fact: Per CSUN's 2014 20-F, he was general manager of CEEG's predecessor, Jiangsu CEEG Electrical Equipment Manufacturing, from 1991 to 2003. In 2005 he won the China Entrepreneur Confederation's China Excellent Entrepreneur award and was named one of Jiangsu's Top Ten Distinguished Youth Entrepreneurs.
notes: Hurun (Sina 2012 list): 陆廷秀 | 中电电气 | 江苏南京 | 变压器、光伏 | b.1960, Zhenjiang. Identity confirmed via SEC 20-F filings (CIK 1396247). CSUN later ran into financial difficulty and was delisted, so avoid that topic. CEEG website (ceeg.cn) did not resolve from here; no published personal or office contact found.

name: Chen Jingna
current_role: Substantial shareholder (spousal/deemed interest), Comba Telecom Systems Holdings (HKEX 2342); no executive role found
profile: Chen Jingna (陳靜娜) is the wife of Fok Tung Ling (Huo Dongling), co-founder and chairman of Comba Telecom, a Guangzhou/Hong Kong maker of wireless base-station antennas, RF and mobile-network infrastructure. Under the SFO she is deemed interested in his Comba shares, which is the basis of her Hurun listing.
interesting_fact: Comba Telecom's annual report lists her as a substantial shareholder solely through spousal interest in Fok Tung Ling's holding (via Prime Choice Investments).
notes: Very private; no public role or interviews found. Better podcast target is husband Fok Tung Ling (Comba chairman); route via Comba IR. Alive status not confirmed (still listed in 2020 annual report).

name: Liu Tie
current_role: Probably Liu Yi (刘轶), co-founder and former vice chairman of CCS Supply Chain Management (瑞茂通, 600180.SH, Zhengzhou) and a concert-party holder with controller Wan Yongxing
profile: Hurun's 2014 entry: 刘铁, b.1972, Zhengzhou, Ruimaotong (瑞茂通), coal supply chain, RMB 2.4bn. No 刘铁 appears in Ruimaotong's filings. Its co-founder and vice chairman Liu Yi (刘轶) was 41 in 2013 and is Zhengzhou-based, so 刘铁 is probably a misprint. Liu Yi ran Henan Hechang Property from 2007 and co-founded the Zhongrui group, which took Ruimaotong public via a 2012 backdoor listing.
interesting_fact: The coal supply-chain company listed on the stock market through an unlikely shell. Ruimaotong (600180) began life as Shandong Jiufa Edible Fungus Co., a mushroom producer listed in 1998, before the Zhongrui group of Wan Yongxing and Liu Yi took it over in 2012.
notes: Hurun 2014 (hurun.net): 刘铁 | 瑞茂通 | 煤炭供应链管理 | b.1972 | Zhengzhou. The match to 刘轶 rests on company, age and city; the characters differ. Caution: Ruimaotong is now *ST, and 2026 notices show the controlling holders' shares (Liu Yi included) frozen and bank litigation naming him. Not recommended for outreach.

name: Shen Renxing
profile: Listed on Hurun China (2011-2016), jointly with Shen Bin, with wealth attributed to 'Huaji' in paper machinery. Searches in Chinese and English found no public profile confirming the company or his current role.
notes: Could not identify the company 'Huaji' or any public record of Shen Renxing (沈仁兴); he dropped off the Hurun list after 2016. A Chinese business registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) lookup would be needed to confirm identity. Not recommended for outreach without more info.

name: Zhang Yichen
current_role: Chairman and CEO, CITIC Capital; Chairman, Trustar Capital; Chairman of McDonald's China master franchise
profile: Zhang Yichen (张懿宸), born 1963 and an MIT graduate, started on Wall Street in 1987 and worked at Bank of Tokyo and Merrill Lynch before joining CITIC Pacific in 2000. He founded CITIC Capital in 2002 and built it into a major China-focused alternative investment firm whose deals include McDonald's China, Alibaba, SF Express and Focus Media. He also chairs Harbin Pharmaceutical and GNC and sits on the HKEX board.
interesting_fact: Through CITIC Capital and Trustar he chairs McDonald's master franchise business in mainland China and Hong Kong, as well as the US supplement chain GNC.
deep_cut_fact: His first Wall Street job, in 1987, was at Greenwich Capital Markets. He later headed proprietary trading at Bank of Tokyo in New York. In a 2014 interview he recommended Charles Duhigg's 'The Power of Habit' and called China's anti-corruption drive 'a colossal exercise in changing habits.'
notes: CITIC Capital's media page directs press enquiries to Corporate Relations (Director: Cindy Tam) at info@citiccapital.com. He is a regular speaker at WEF, Milken and Boao forums, which are good warm contexts for an approach.

name: Li Yuzheng
current_role: Controlling shareholder (53.72%) and co-actual controller of Jinyi Film & Television / Jinyi Cinemas (SZ002905), Guangzhou
profile: Li Yuzhen (李玉珍; input romanisation 'Li Yuzheng') controls Guangzhou-based Jinyi Cinemas (金逸影视), one of China's larger cinema chains, listed in Shenzhen in 2017, alongside co-controller Li Genchang. She holds about 53.7% directly and appeared on the Hurun China list 2012-2020 (cinemas and real estate). The company elected Qiu Xianbang as new chairman in June 2026.
interesting_fact: In June 2026 Jinyi's board turned over: Li Xiaowen stepped down as chairman after about 16 years in the role (remaining a director) and Qiu Xianbang was elected chairman; Li Yuzhen remains the majority owner.
notes: Correct Chinese name per filings is 李玉珍 (Li Yuzhen). She holds no listed executive post and keeps a very low profile; best route is the company's securities/IR office.

name: Teng Daochun
current_role: Controller of the Tianyu group (Xuzhou Tianyu Investment / Jiangsu Tianyu Energy Technology Group), Xuzhou, Jiangsu; coking coal, ferroalloys, power and heat
profile: Teng Daochun (滕道春, b. Jan 1970) is a Xuzhou industrialist who controlled Xuzhou Tianyu Investment (77.67% in 2006). Its businesses span coke, pig iron, molybdenum alloys and coal washing, later grouped as Tianyu Energy. In 2006 Tianyu joined Shougang in restructuring S*ST Shengfang (000620). In 2017 HKEX-listed 1187 proposed buying his power-and-heat business. Hurun listed him 2012-2019.
interesting_fact: In 2006 his Tianyu Investment joined state steel giant Shougang in a restructuring of Shenzhen-listed S*ST Shengfang (000620), a rare private-plus-SOE tie-up for a Xuzhou family firm.
deep_cut_fact: He became a factory boss young. Per a 2006 filing, he was GM of Xuzhou Tai'an Co. at 20 (1990-92) and then director of Xuzhou No. 2 Ferroalloy Plant for a decade (1992-2002), before running the Huanyu molybdenum and coking businesses.
notes: Hurun 2019 (hurun.net): 滕道春 | 天裕能源 | 焦煤 | Xuzhou | family wealth RMB 2.8bn. 'Tianue' = 天裕. HKEX 1187 resumption-proposal update (Feb 2017) naming him: https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2017-02-28/1203117765.PDF. Low public profile; no published contact found.

name: Jiang Yong
current_role: Director (since 2007) and co-controlling shareholder of Guizhou Bailing Group Pharmaceutical (贵州百灵, SZSE: 002424); former VP (2007-2021)
profile: Born 1968, Jiang Yong is the brother and concert party of Bailing founder Jiang Wei; together they control Guizhou Bailing, an Anshun-based maker of Miao ethnic-minority traditional medicines. He was previously deputy director of the Anshun Pharmaceutical Factory and VP of several Bailing companies, overseeing sales.
interesting_fact: Bailing specialises in Miao (Hmong) ethnic medicine from Guizhou - a niche of Chinese traditional pharmacy rooted in the province's minority communities.
notes: CAUTION: In 2026 the CSRC found Bailing's 2019-2023 annual reports misstated; Jiang Yong (as director/VP) was warned and fined RMB 2M and Jiang Wei resigned as chairman (March 2026). Not a suitable or easy outreach target; poor podcast fit. Company now trades as ST Bailing.

name: Zhang Guangfu
profile: Listed on Hurun China (2010-2016) as owner of steelmaker 'Guangfu' (~US$400m). profile: Hurun China 2021 listed Tan Qing (谭庆) with wealth from 'Dahao', a manufacturing business, possibly Beijing Dahao Technology (大豪科技, sewing and embroidery machine control systems). The link is unconfirmed.

name: Wang Xuehai
current_role: Former chairman/director, Humanwell Healthcare (人福医药); a principal of Wuhan Dangdai Technology Industries Group (current role unconfirmed)
profile: Wuhan entrepreneur associated with Wuhan Dangdai Technology Industries Group, a conglomerate in pharmaceuticals, real estate, education and travel whose flagship was Shanghai-listed Humanwell Healthcare, which he chaired. Dangdai lost control of Humanwell in 2025 when China Merchants' life-science arm reorganised its board, ending 32 years of Dangdai control.
interesting_fact: Humanwell, which he chaired, grew into one of China's leading anaesthesia/analgesia drug makers under Dangdai's 32-year control before China Merchants took over in 2025.
notes: Sensitive: Dangdai group has been in financial distress and he was named in regulatory penalties (SSE 2023, Hubei CSRC Dec 2025) over related-party fund occupation at Humanwell; avoid referencing. Humanwell IR (board secretary) is the only corporate route, but he is no longer in control.

name: Wu Yinhe
current_role: Non-executive Director, Xinyi Glass Holdings (HKEX: 0868); Executive Director, Xinyi Electric Storage Holdings (HKEX GEM: 8328)
profile: One of the early shareholder-directors of Xinyi Glass, which was founded in 1988 and is now a Hang Seng Index constituent making float, automotive and low-e architectural glass. Known in Hong Kong filings as NG Ngan Ho (aged 61 in the 2025 annual report), he joined the group in 2003, ran finance and purchasing at the Dongguan complex, and holds his shares through Linkall Investment Ltd.
interesting_fact: Xinyi Glass says it has about 14% of global float-glass capacity, more than 25% of the global automotive replacement-glass market and 25% of the global low-e energy-efficient glass market.
deep_cut_fact: Besides glass, he is an executive director of Xinyi Electric Storage, the group's listed energy-storage and EV-battery-related arm, which is relevant to an energy-focused podcast.
notes: Matching 吴银河 to 'NG Ngan Ho' rests on the Cantonese romanisation plus the Xinyi Glass/Hurun 2021 link; the Chinese name was not machine-readable in the annual report PDF. Low profile; route via Xinyi IR.

name: Yan Binsheng
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and controlling shareholder (~56%), Ganyuan Foods Co., Ltd. (甘源食品, SZSE 002991), Pingxiang, Jiangxi
profile: Yan Binsheng (b. 1975) built Ganyuan Foods, a Jiangxi-based snack maker known for green peas, sunflower kernels, broad beans and mixed nuts. After working at several Guangdong snack companies he joined Pingxiang Ganyuan as marketing director in 2006, became chairman in 2012 and chairman/GM in 2015; the company listed in Shenzhen in 2020. He holds about 56% of the shares.
interesting_fact: Ganyuan's core products are humble pantry snacks - green peas, sunflower seed kernels, broad beans and mixed nuts - sold nationally from a factory park in Pingxiang, Jiangxi.
deep_cut_fact: He came up through sales: before Ganyuan he worked at Guangdong Qibao Yiding Food and other Foshan/Shunde snack firms, and joined Pingxiang Ganyuan in 2006 as marketing director before rising to chairman in 2012.
notes: Board secretary is Zhang Ting (per 10jqka); IR email should be in the company's annual report on cninfo.com.cn (not verified here). Site lists only a sales/franchise mailbox. Snack-food founder - tangential to energy/data-centre themes.

name: Yan Hua
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Farben Information Technology (法本信息, SZSE: 300925); controlling shareholder (~28%)
profile: Yan Hua (严华, b. 1977) controls and runs Farben Information Technology, a Shenzhen software outsourcing and digital-transformation services firm founded in 2006 that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in December 2020. He also chairs the affiliated Shenzhen Farben Electronics and Shanghai Farben Electronic Technology.
interesting_fact: Farben provides software R&D, testing and digital-transformation engineering services, largely as an outsourced development partner to large tech and financial clients; Yan holds about 105.5 million shares (28.13%).
deep_cut_fact: Before building Farben, Yan started out in sales - he was sales director at Shenzhen Kairong Industrial (深圳市凯荣实业) - and later completed a doctorate while running the company.
notes: Low media profile. Board secretary is Wu Chao (吴超); IR channel via SZSE filings/Hudongyi is the formal route. No published email found on the company site.

name: Yang Huanming
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, BGI Group (Shenzhen); academician, Chinese Academy of Sciences
profile: Yang Huanming (杨焕明, b. 1952, near Wenzhou) is a geneticist who co-founded the Beijing Genomics Institute (BGI) in 1999 and led China's part of the international Human Genome Project. BGI later moved to Shenzhen and became a commercial genomics group whose listed arm, BGI Genomics, is the basis of his wealth. He is a member of the CAS, the Leopoldina and the US National Academy of Sciences.
interesting_fact: His BGI team's draft sequence of the indica rice genome was the cover story of Science on 5 April 2002, an early sign that China had become a genome-sequencing power.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he was the only Chinese appointee to the international research panel of President Obama's Presidential Commission for the Study of Bioethical Issues, which examined the 1940s Guatemala syphilis experiments. He earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen's Institute of Medical Genetics.
notes: Scientist-founder who often speaks at conferences (e.g. ICG). A conference keynote may be an easier route than cold email. He is a well-known advocate of open genomic data, a strong podcast angle.

name: Yang Jiuhong
current_role: Controlling shareholder and co-actual controller, Changzhou Aohong Electronics (SSE: 605058); administrative director of subsidiary Haihong Electronics (per 2020 prospectus)
profile: Yang Jiuhong (b. 1950), from Changzhou, Jiangsu, owned about 58.8% of Aohong Electronics, a printed-circuit-board maker, before its 2020 Shanghai IPO. She controls it jointly with her son-in-law Chen Dinghong, the chairman and general manager. She is not a board member; she is listed as administrative director of the Haihong Electronics subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Aohong is a family-run PCB maker: the 2020 prospectus shows founder Yang Jiuhong and Chairman Chen Dinghong jointly controlling about 93% of shares before the IPO. Under a 2019 supplementary agreement, Chen's decision prevails if the two disagree.
notes: Very private, older controlling shareholder with no media presence. Chairman Chen Dinghong is the public face and the more realistic interview target. Contacts are company-level, from the 2020 prospectus.

name: Yao Zhongliang
current_role: Party Secretary, Chairman and President, Baixiang Food Co., Ltd. (白象食品), Henan; deputy to the 14th National People's Congress
profile: Yao Zhongliang (姚忠良), born 1962 in Pingyu, Henan, left the army in 1983 for local grain bureaus and in 1996 became general manager of the Baixiang instant-noodle factory, turning it into one of China's leading domestic noodle brands. He still runs the company as chairman and president and is an NPC deputy and vice chair of the Henan Federation of Industry and Commerce.
interesting_fact: About one-third of Baixiang's employees are people with disabilities; when this was reported during the 2022 Beijing Winter Paralympics, consumers bought its noodles en masse in support and the brand went viral.
deep_cut_fact: Before noodles, Yao was a soldier who, after leaving the military in 1983, worked his way up through a county and then a regional grain bureau; he was named a National Model Worker in 2010 and carried the torch for the 2023 Chengdu Universiade.
notes: Low personal media profile despite brand fame; company refers to disabled staff as 'self-improvement staff'. Route via Baixiang corporate office (Zhengzhou).

name: Yu Guoxu
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Hengsheng Energy (恒盛能源, SSE 605580), Longyou, Zhejiang; chairman of Zhejiang Xurong New Materials
profile: Born 1958; a Zhejiang builder-turned-energy entrepreneur who controls Hengsheng Energy, a combined heat-and-power (cogeneration) utility supplying steam, hot water and electricity to industrial parks in Longyou, plus waste-to-energy via subsidiary Hengxin Power. Hengsheng listed in Shanghai in 2021; it has since diversified into CVD lab-grown diamond through subsidiary Zhejiang Huamao Technology.
interesting_fact: His cogeneration company has moved into CVD-grown synthetic diamond (single- and poly-crystal) via Huamao Technology, and in H1 2026 sold 150,000 tonnes of carbon allowances on China's national emissions-trading market.
deep_cut_fact: He came up through construction, not power: project manager at Lanxi City Construction (1988-97), GM of Lanxi Longma Building Materials, then chairman of Zhejiang Qinglongshan Building Materials, before running technical upgrades ('技改办主任') at Hengxin Power and Hengsheng from 2008.

public_contacts.value: hsny@hs-energy.com.cn (Hengsheng Energy board secretary Jin Hai)

notes: Very low profile, regional; no personal channels. Route via board secretary. Company is family-controlled (do not reference family members).

name: Yu Xindong
current_role: Chairman, TKD Science and Technology Co. (泰晶科技, 603738.SH), Suizhou, Hubei
profile: Yu Xindong is founder and chairman of TKD Science and Technology, a Hubei-based maker of quartz crystal resonators and oscillators (frequency-control components) used in phones, IoT, automotive and communications gear. He ran the predecessor Shenzhen Taijing Industrial from 2004, has chaired TKD since 2005 and took it public in Shanghai in 2016. He is also a council member of the China Electronic Components Association's piezoelectric crystal branch.
interesting_fact: TKD is one of China's leading domestic suppliers of tuning-fork and SMD quartz crystals, a component category long dominated by Japanese makers. Its industrial park is in Suizhou, Hubei.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of the main drafters of China's national electronics industry standard for tuning-fork quartz crystal units (SJ/T10015-2013, 10kHz-200kHz test methods). He also earned a PhD in management science and engineering from Wuhan University of Technology in 2017, three decades after graduating from its mechanical department in 1988.
notes: Hurun's 'Tkd' is TKD Science and Technology (泰晶科技). He also holds a Tsinghua MBA (2007). Securities representative: Zhu Liuyan. The company board-office email is the best route.

name: Zhang Banghui
current_role: Founder, controlling shareholder and Chairman, Tianbang Food (天邦食品, SZ: 002124); president role reportedly ended April 2026
profile: Born 1963, a former fisheries research assistant who became deputy GM at a Wuxi animal-nutrition company and then general manager of Yuyao Tianbang. He built Tianbang (Tech-Bank) from aquafeed into one of China's larger hog producers and pork processors. After heavy debt in the pork-cycle downturn, the company went through a court-led debt restructuring in 2024.
interesting_fact: In a 2024 interview he predicted the end of China's famous 'pig cycle' as small farmers exit: 'From now on there will be no pig cycle; whoever is cost-competitive will survive.'
deep_cut_fact: Before going into business he was a research assistant at the Freshwater Fisheries Research Center of the Chinese Academy of Fishery Sciences in Wuxi; Tianbang's roots are in aquaculture feed.
notes: Hurun 'Tech-bank' = Tianbang (天邦). Company had debt restructuring in 2024 (ST status), so wealth likely much reduced; approach sensitively. Contact via company IR/board secretary listed in SZSE filings.

name: Zhang Bei
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jinghui Electric (Shenzhen) Co. (since June 1992); co-actual controller and ~24.5% shareholder of Shenzhen Crastal Technology / Buydeem (300824.SZ)
profile: Shenzhen small-appliance entrepreneur who has run Jinghui Electric (晶辉电器), an appliance manufacturer, since 1992. Together with George Mohan Zhang (Buydeem's chairman/GM) he controls about 52.5% of Shenzhen Crastal Technology, which owns the Buydeem (北鼎) premium kitchen-appliance brand known for kettles and health pots and listed in Shenzhen in 2020.
interesting_fact: Crastal started as an OEM appliance maker and built its own consumer brand, Buydeem, now a recognisable premium kettle and kitchenware label in China.
notes: Low public profile; the public face of the company is George Mohan Zhang. Best route is Buydeem's board-secretary IR email. Role details from Buydeem 2025 annual report (section on actual controllers).

name: George Mohan Zhang
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Shenzhen Crastal Technology Co. (Buydeem, 北鼎股份, SZSE: 300824)
profile: George Mohan Zhang (张默涵, b. 1982, Canadian national) has run Shenzhen Crastal Technology as chairman and GM since 2003. The company began as an OEM/ODM maker of small kitchen appliances and built its own premium brand, BUYDEEM, selling health kettles, steam ovens, water dispensers and toasters. He and Zhang Bei are the actual controllers; it listed in Shenzhen in 2020.
interesting_fact: He took the helm of the company in 2003 at about 21, and turned a contract manufacturer into a design-led consumer brand (BUYDEEM) sold in China and overseas.
deep_cut_fact: He studied mathematics and computing science (BSc) at Simon Fraser University in Vancouver and earned a master's in industrial engineering at UC Berkeley, as did his deputy GM Fang Zhen.
notes: English-speaking, North America-educated founder of a consumer brand, so a possible fit for an entrepreneurship episode. Route via the company's board office (buydeem@crastal.com).

name: Zhang Chongyu
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Jinyu Bio-Technology Co. (生物股份, 600201.SH), Hohhot, Inner Mongolia
profile: Zhang Chongyu (张翀宇, b. 1954) has led Jinyu Bio-Technology, a Hohhot-based maker of veterinary biological products, since 1993, as chairman and president until 2019 and chairman since. Hurun lists the fortune jointly with Zhang Jing, the company's vice-chairman and president.
interesting_fact: He has chaired the same company for more than 30 years (since March 1993) and has received the national May Day Labour Medal and National Model Worker honours.
deep_cut_fact: Before vaccines he spent 1976-1993 at Hohhot Metal Materials Company, rising from business-section chief to general manager; he holds a postgraduate degree and is a senior economist.
notes: Company 2024 annual report confirms him as chairman/party secretary since 2019 (chairman since 1993). Company describes its business as R&D, production and sale of veterinary biologics.

name: Zhang Chongshun
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Jiangsu Xinri E-Vehicle Co. (新日股份, SSE: 603787)
profile: Zhang Chongshun (b. 1969, Wenzhou) built a fortune supplying hardware and motorcycle parts in Haikou before founding Xinri electric bicycles in 1999, positioning it as a premium brand. Xinri listed in Shanghai in April 2017 as the first listed e-bike maker in China; he and his wife Chen Yuying control it.
interesting_fact: Xinri was an official vehicle supplier for the 2008 Beijing Olympics, the year its output passed 2 million e-bikes, and in 2017 it became the e-bike industry's first A-share listing.
deep_cut_fact: After failing the high-school entrance exam in 1985 he apprenticed in his father's hardware trade; in 1989, aged 20, he went to Haikou and supplied motorcycle parts to Sundiro, and even learned southern-style kung fu and staff fighting there. Motto: '实业实业，就是要实实在在、兢兢业业'.
notes: Key early tech came from a CAS Institute of Physics affiliate (motor/battery tech) in 1998 per the same profile. EV/battery angle fits an energy podcast.

name: Chen Yuying
current_role: Director and major shareholder, Jiangsu Xinri E-Vehicle Co. (SSE: 603787)
profile: Chen Yuying is a board director and individual shareholder of Wuxi-based Xinri E-Vehicle, the electric-bicycle maker founded by her husband, chairman Zhang Chongshun; together with his vehicle Anji Zhunlai they act in concert as controlling shareholders. Xinri listed in Shanghai in April 2017, the first electric two-wheeler maker on China's A-share market.
interesting_fact: Xinri was the first electric-bicycle company to list on China's A-share market (2017); its market value at one point passed RMB 6bn.
notes: Still a Xinri director per April 2026 board announcements. Low personal profile; company founder/public face is chairman Zhang Chongshun. Best route is the board office email.

name: Lin Lan
current_role: Chairman (since May 2025), general manager and legal representative of Fujian Chase Science (创识科技, 300941.SZ)
profile: Born 1973, a long-time Chase Science executive who rose through its systems-integration, network-security and financial-products divisions, served as board secretary and deputy GM, then became general manager and, in May 2025, chairman of the Fuzhou-based fintech/payments software firm. She is a co-actual controller with Zhang Gengsheng.
