name: Zhang Kaiyi
current_role: Early executive and shareholder of Sangfor Technologies (深信服, 300454.SZ); Vice President as of 2017 (current title not confirmed)
profile: Long-time Sangfor executive and significant shareholder (about 2.58% per Q1 2020 report) of the Shenzhen cybersecurity and cloud-infrastructure company founded in 2000 by He Zhaoxi (River He) and Xiong Wu. As a VP he was a public spokesman for Sangfor's 2017 push into hyperconverged infrastructure and cloud.
interesting_fact: In a 2017 interview he said Sangfor put 50% of its 2016 R&D budget into hyperconverged infrastructure and cloud products - a big bet for a company then known for security gear.
notes: Not named among Sangfor's actual controllers (He Zhaoxi, Xiong Wu, Feng Yi). Shareholding from 2020 Q1 report (https://disc.static.szse.cn/download/disc/disk02/finalpage/2020-04-25/3ee4f90b-4557-4fc9-ac14-d5bd08a1edc4.PDF). Data-center/cloud angle relevant to podcast.

name: Zhao Jian
current_role: Former major (passive) shareholder of Ligao Foods (立高食品); not involved in management
profile: Founding-era shareholder of Guangzhou food company Ligao Foods (立高食品), whose predecessor was founded in 2000 and run by Peng Yuhui, Zhao Songtao and Peng Yongcheng. After the April 2021 listing he held 10.14% as third-largest shareholder; from 2022 he sold down for about RMB 1.185bn, holding 1.14% by May 2023 and planning a near-complete exit.
interesting_fact: Although a shareholder since the company's founding, he never took part in running it; he invested on the strength of Peng Yongcheng's team's cream R&D and production expertise.
notes: Per the company (via TMTPost, 2023) he has settled overseas with no plan to return and is liquidating his domestic holdings. Very private; no public contacts. Weak podcast fit.

name: Zhao Shanqi
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Jiangsu Macmic Science & Technology Co. (SSE STAR: 688711), Changzhou
profile: Power-semiconductor engineer (PhD) who founded Macmic in Changzhou in August 2006 and remains its chairman, GM and largest individual shareholder (~14-18%). Macmic designs and makes IGBT and FRED power chips and modules for EVs, wind/solar/storage and industrial drives, and is now expanding into AI data-center power (GaN chips, UPS and server power).
interesting_fact: In Sept 2026 he said Macmic's GaN 650V 30mΩ chip had passed certification with AI data-center power-supply customers and it is working with a leading North American power-equipment company on UPS, server-power and solid-state-transformer (SST) products.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Macmic he was deputy chief engineer at the Beijing Power Electronics Center (to 1994), then a postdoc (1994-95) and visiting associate professor (1995-96) at INSA de Lyon in France.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center angle (power semiconductors for AIDC). Jilin University graduate per profiles. No published IR email captured; Macmic's securities office is reachable via SSE e-interaction (sns.sseinfo.com) and the company website. Chinese name 赵善麒.

name: Zhao Songtao
current_role: Vice Chairman and co-actual controller, Ligao Foods Co., Ltd. (立高食品, SZSE 300973)
profile: Zhao Songtao (赵松涛) is one of three related co-controllers of Ligao Foods, a Guangzhou maker of frozen baked goods and baking ingredients (creams, fats, fruit fillings, sauces) founded in 2000 and listed on ChiNext in 2021. With Peng Yuhui and Peng Yongcheng he held about 46.6% around listing; the three renewed their concert-party agreement in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Ligao supplies frozen baked goods and baking creams to bakeries, supermarkets, restaurants and new-retail channels, a B2B 'behind the bakery' business.
notes: Controller status per Jiemian (https://m.jiemian.com/article/6011270.html). Search-tool summary of 2026 filings says he is vice chairman; not read directly. Low public profile; route via board secretary (Wang Shijia, per stockanalysis).

profile: Zhao Yuling (赵玉岭) is one of the individual co-owners of Beijing Dahao Technology, a Shanghai-listed maker of control systems for sewing and embroidery machinery, majority-owned by state-owned Beijing Yiqing Holdings. As of 30 Sept 2026 he held about 73.5 million shares (6.58%).
notes: Lane spelling 'Yulling' should be Yuling. Not chairman (Hu Xiongguang elected chairman July 2026). Shareholding source: https://quote.cfi.cn/gdtj/19782/603025.html. Very low public profile.

profile: Zhong Xuanxuan (钟䁢䁢) is an elder sister of Nongfu Spring founder Zhong Shanshan. Nongfu Spring's 2020 Hong Kong IPO prospectus lists her as a shareholder and associate of Zhong Shanshan. She bought shares with personal funds in 2007-2008 and became a public shareholder when the company listed in September 2020.

name: Guo Jingsong
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Sotech Smarter Equipment (松德智慧装备, SZSE 300173, now Funeng Oriental Equipment Technology); current role not found
profile: Born 1962, an engineer by training, Guo Jingsong (郭景松) founded Zhongshan Debao Packaging Machinery in 1997, which became Sotech, a maker of gravure printing machines and later intelligent automated manufacturing equipment; he chaired it from 2000 (listed company from 2007). Foshan Public Utilities Holding took a stake in 2019 and the company was later renamed Funeng Oriental.
interesting_fact: He won a first-class Guangdong Provincial Science and Technology award and in March 2017 was named a 'Zhongshan Science and Technology Innovation Leader'; he was also vice-chairman of the gravure printing branch of the China Printing Technology Association.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career (1983-1992) as an engineer at the Ministry of Geology and Mineral Resources' Hengyang Exploration Machinery Plant, then was deputy director of Shunde Debao Packaging Machinery Factory before founding his own company in 1997.
notes: Bio from Sotech's 2018 annual report. The listed company (now Funeng Oriental, sec@fnorient.com) is controlled by Foshan Public Utilities; he appears in its 2025 report only as a party to earlier performance commitments, so company channels may not reach him.

profile: Listed by Hurun China (2015-2017) with wealth from 'Sotech Smarter' (manufacturing), shared with Guo Jingsong. No source linking 张晓玲 or Guo Jingsong to a company of that name was found; the name is very common.
notes: Identity unresolved; the company's Chinese name could not be identified. No contact found.

name: Liu Guoyao
current_role: Chairman, Nanjing Sciyon Wisdom Technology Group (科远智慧, SZ:002380)
profile: Liu Guoyao (b. 1962), a former Southeast University power-engineering lecturer, co-founded Nanjing Sciyon (科远), an industrial automation and smart-plant technology company listed in Shenzhen in 2010, where he is chairman and a co-controlling shareholder (~61m shares). He was re-elected chairman in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: He started as a teacher in Southeast University's power engineering department (thermal control) and head of the instrument lab at its vibration engineering institute; he later won a Jiangsu Science and Technology first prize (2017).
deep_cut_fact: He holds a master's in engineering from Southeast University and a Tsinghua SEM EMBA, is an honorary trustee of Southeast University and an off-campus PhD supervisor there, and in 2020 was named a 'caring ambassador' for Jiangning district's youth dream fund.
notes: Hurun 'Keyuan' = 科远 (Sciyon), Nanjing; identified via Lixinger controlling-holder listing and Sina Finance bio. Relevant to energy angle (thermal control/power-plant automation background). Board secretary: Zhao Wenqing (per Sina). Company site sciyon.com could not be fetched.

name: Shi Xugang
current_role: Shareholder (former controlling shareholder and chairman), Hangzhou Zhongwei Electronics (中威电子, 300270.SZ); current board role not confirmed
profile: Shi Xugang (石旭刚) was controlling shareholder, actual controller and chairman of Hangzhou Zhongwei Electronics (OB Telecom Electronics), a Hangzhou video-surveillance/communications company. He stepped down as general manager in 2021 but remained chairman; later he sold down shares and, around late 2025, waived voting rights on his 7.90% stake as control passed to Fu Yingbo.
interesting_fact: After a change of control, he committed to waive voting rights on his 7.90% stake and not seek control of the company he had controlled.
notes: No personal bio found. Chairman-in-2021 per https://www.nbd.com.cn/articles/2021-08-27/1893140.html. Low profile; route via company board secretary.

name: Chen Hankang

profile: Chen Hankang (陈汉康, b. 1961), from Chun'an county, Zhejiang, was the actual controller of Kangsheng, a Chun'an-based maker of refrigeration tubing and parts for appliances that later moved into new-energy commercial vehicles and liquid-cooling products. He held ~7.5% directly in 2022 alongside his vehicle Zhejiang Runcheng Holding; control of Kangsheng has since passed to other holders.
interesting_fact: Kangsheng, registered in Chun'an's Pingshan industrial park near Qiandao Lake, became a supplier of refrigerant pipelines for fridges and air-conditioners before diversifying into EV commercial vehicles.
notes: Current controlling shareholders of Kangsheng are other entities (Changzhou Xingruo etc.); 2019-21 filings show pledged-share litigation and court-ordered share disposals (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk02/finalpage/2019-09-18/391054ec-c700-424c-881b-c07aa748f2d1.PDF). Hurun wealth (2015-17) shared with Zhou Zhen is stale; poor outreach target.

profile: Listed on Hurun 2015-2017 alongside Chen Hankang for wealth from Kangsheng, the Zhejiang maker of tubular products (refrigeration pipes) listed in Shenzhen. A 2022 SZSE disclosure shows her owning 30% of, and serving as manager of, an entity in which Chen Hankang holds 70%. No other public biography was found.
notes: Very low profile. The source is SZSE filing https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk03/finalpage/2022-09-22/ace8775b-1608-4541-8900-d6550e8a6a0c.PDF. Her relationship to Chen Hankang is not stated in the sources read. The Hurun-era wealth is likely stale.

name: Pan Jiangen
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and Chief Scientist, Hangzhou Everfine Photo-E-Info Co. (远方信息, formerly 远方光电; SZSE: 300306)
profile: Pan Jiangen (born 1965), a professor-level senior engineer trained in optoelectronic measurement at Zhejiang University, founded Hangzhou Everfine Instruments in 1994 and Everfine Photo-E-Info in 2003, which makes optical/photoelectric test and measurement instruments. He directly and indirectly controls about 48.65% of the listed company and was reappointed GM in Sept 2025.
interesting_fact: He is both chairman and 'chief scientist' of the company he founded, and directly and indirectly controls 48.65% of it (Sept 2025 filing).
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he stayed on at Zhejiang University in 1989 to do research and teaching after graduating in optoelectronic measurement technology and instrument engineering, then founded Hangzhou Everfine Instruments in 1994.

name: Meng Xin
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Pan Jiangen) of Hangzhou Everfine Photo-E-Info Co. (300306.SZ, now short name 远方信息); current executive title not confirmed
profile: 孟欣 (b. 1966) and her husband Pan Jiangen controlled about 81.5% of Everfine, a Hangzhou maker of photometric/optical testing instruments, at its 2012 ChiNext IPO; Pan remains chairman, GM and chief scientist. name: Cheng Shangnan

current_role: Founder and controlling shareholder (~42%, acting in concert with chairman Shi Yimin) of Hangzhou Innover Technology (先锋电子, SZSE: 002767)
profile: Shi Zhengmin (石政民, b. 1946) founded Hangzhou Innover Technology, a smart gas-meter and 'smart gas' solutions maker set up in 1991 and listed in Shenzhen in June 2015. profile: Known as 'Duolong' and 'Taobao's first programmer', Cai joined Alibaba in 2000 after a biology master's at Hangzhou University, was one of three engineers who built Taobao in about a month in 2003, and became an Alibaba partner in 2014. profile: Cao Zhengguo chairs Jiangsu Zhengdan Chemical, a Zhenjiang maker of specialty fine chemicals founded in 2007 and listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext in April 2017. Its main products are trimellitic anhydride (TMA) and the plasticiser trioctyl trimellitate (TOTM). With Shen Xingxiu he is an actual controller, indirectly controlling about 33.5%.
interesting_fact: Zhengdan's core products are trimellitic anhydride (TMA) and trioctyl trimellitate (TOTM), a heat-resistant plasticiser. The company calls itself a maker of 'environmental new materials' and specialty fine chemicals.

current_role: Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, Bloom Energy Corp. (NYSE: BE), since January 2016

name: Terry Smith
current_role: Founder and CEO, Fundsmith LLP (London)

In 2010 he founded Fundsmith, whose buy-good-companies-and-do-nothing equity fund is one of the UK's largest (about £24bn under management). He is often called 'the English Warren Buffett'.
interesting_fact: His 1992 book 'Accounting for Growth', which exposed creative accounting at FTSE 100 firms, got him fired and sued by UBS Phillips & Drew. The row sent the book to No. 1, displacing Stephen Hawking's 'A Brief History of Time'.
deep_cut_fact: A military-history enthusiast, he led the campaign that put a statue of Battle of Britain commander Sir Keith Park in London. He was made a Member of the New Zealand Order of Merit (2012) for services to NZ-UK relations. He also cycles competitively and practises Muay Thai.

name: John W Allison
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Home BancShares Inc. (NYSE: HOMB, parent of Centennial Bank), Conway, Arkansas; handed CEO role to J. Stephen Tipton in 2026

Allison (79) is an Arkansas banker who co-founded Home BancShares in 1998 and built it, largely through acquisitions, into a ~$24bn-asset bank holding company operating Centennial Bank in Arkansas, Florida, Texas, Tennessee, Alabama and New York City. deep_cut_fact: Long before Home BancShares, he became chairman of First National Bank of Conway in 1983 and chaired the executive committee of First Commercial Corp., then Arkansas's largest bank holding company (~$7.3bn assets), until its 1998 sale to Regions.

profile: Jin Weidong (金卫东, b. 1963), a veterinary-science graduate of Shenyang Agricultural University with a master's from the former PLA Veterinary University, co-founded Wellhope in 1995. It grew into a major Chinese animal-feed, poultry and pork group (revenue ~RMB35.8bn in 2025), partly partnered with Dutch feed group De Heus. notes: Company is now named Wellhope Foods (禾丰食品股份有限公司). Board includes a De Heus representative (Jacobus Johannes de Heus). Fairly public-facing as a regional business leader.

deep_cut_fact: In 2014 Huantai struck a deal with US firm SunEdison, which agreed to supply polysilicon for Huantai's wafers as part of a partnership to build up to 1.7GW of solar projects in China.

name: Todd G. Schwartz

OppFi went public via SPAC in July 2021 and he returned as CEO in 2022; he is the largest stockholder and a partner at Schwartz Capital Group and Strand Equity.

name: Andy Jassy

profile: Grew up in Scarsdale, NY; Harvard AB and MBA. Joined Amazon in 1997 as a marketing manager, was Jeff Bezos's first technical adviser, conceived AWS with Bezos in 2003 and led it from its 57-person original team; succeeded Bezos as Amazon CEO in July 2021.
interesting_fact: Minority owner of the NHL's Seattle Kraken (joined the ownership group in 2018) and chairs the board of Rainier Prep charter school in Seattle.

notes: Highly relevant (AWS / data centers). Best route is Amazon corporate communications.

name: Steven T Mnuchin
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Liberty Strategic Capital; Director, Satellogic Inc. (SATL)

After 2020 he launched private-equity firm Liberty Strategic Capital, which holds large stakes in Lionsgate Studios, Starz and earth-observation satellite firm Satellogic.
interesting_fact: His Dune Entertainment co-financed blockbusters including Avatar and the X-Men films for Fox, and as RatPac-Dune backed Warner Bros. titles like Mad Max: Fury Road and American Sniper; he was an executive producer on The Lego Movie and Wonder Woman.
deep_cut_fact: At Yale (economics, 1985) he was publisher of the Yale Daily News, and he trained at Salomon Brothers while still a student before joining Goldman in 1985.

Firm website returned 503 during research; no press email found. Space/satellite data angle fits data-center theme. High-profile political figure; expect gatekeeping.

name: Jeff Radke

profile: Reinsurance veteran who co-founded Accelerant in 2018, which runs the Accelerant Risk Exchange, a data-driven platform connecting specialty insurance underwriters (MGAs) with risk-capital providers; it listed in New York in 2025. In August 2026 Accelerant agreed to be taken private by Thoma Bravo at $20.25/share (EV over $4bn), expected to close in H1 2027.

name: Andrew Page
current_role: Executive Chairman, Alfa Financial Software Holdings plc (LSE: ALFA)

Alfa makes Alfa Systems, a cloud platform for auto and equipment asset finance. It floated in London in May 2017, when Page was expected to sell shares worth over £180m. He still controls a large stake via CHP Software and Consulting Holdings.
interesting_fact: Alfa's May 2017 IPO at 325p was billed as London's largest float of that year, and the company joined the FTSE 250 that September.
deep_cut_fact: Page co-founded the business as CHP Consulting in 1990 with Justin Cooper and Ian Hargrave. It won its first customer in 1992 and only took the Alfa name, after its core product, in November 2016.
notes: Dec 2025 RNS lists Andrew Page, Executive Chairman, as an enquiries contact via Alfa (+44 (0)20 7588 1800). In May 2024 his holding company CHP sold ~4.9% of Alfa. His appearance on the 2020 Sunday Times list was not independently verified, but the software-wealth match is strong. Low media profile.

profile: Baijnath Choudhary founded Kolkata-based Anmol Industries, a maker of biscuits, cookies and cakes that traces its origins to 1994 and a first plant at Dankuni, West Bengal. It now runs seven plants in UP, Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha. In Sept 2026 it filed for a Rs 1,800 crore IPO, entirely an offer for sale by the Baijnath Choudhary & Family Trust.
interesting_fact: As of March 2026 Anmol had capacity of about 361,000 tonnes a year of biscuits and cookies; family packs alone brought Rs 485.5 crore of FY2026 product sales.

Himadri began as a coal-tar pitch maker and has grown into specialty carbon black, naphthalene derivatives and lithium-ion battery materials. The company is now run by Chairman/MD/CEO Anurag Choudhary.

name: Narendra Bansal
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Intex Technologies (India) Ltd
profile: Born in 1963 in Hanumangarh, Rajasthan, Narendra Bansal traded audio/video cassettes and then floppy disks and PC components in Delhi before founding International Impex (1994) and Intex Technologies (1996), which grew into a major Indian maker of mobile phones, consumer durables and IT accessories. He also owned IPL franchise Gujarat Lions.

profile: Son of founder Satyanarayan Nuwal; joined the family explosives business in the mid-1990s when it began manufacturing, and has been MD & CEO since ~2012. He has steered Solar from bulk/packaged explosives for mining into defence: propellants, warheads, ammunition, 'Nagastra' loitering munitions and counter-drone systems, with a large new defence/aerospace hub in Nagpur.
interesting_fact: Solar supplies 'Nagastra' loitering-munition drones to the Indian Army, and PM Modi inaugurated its loitering-munition test range in Nagpur in March 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A qualified chartered accountant, he says Solar's defence breakthrough was multi-mode hand grenades co-developed with DRDO over nearly three years, which he calls a watershed for private-sector defence in India; asked if 'playing with fire' is fun, he laughed.
notes: Hurun net-worth figure is from 2019 and well out of date; the Nuwal family is now multi-billionaire as Solar's market cap soared on defence orders. Strong energy/defence-manufacturing angle. Chartered-accountant credential per company website.

profile: Gu Shaoming founded Shenzhen Bauing Construction Group, a building-decoration and fit-out contractor that reverse-merged into listed Chenglin (成霖股份) in 2013. name: Yu Jianmo
current_role: Major shareholder (approx. 11.6% in 2023) of Dalian Meijimu Education Technology (*ST美吉, SZSE: 002621); former chairman, left board March 2017
profile: Yu Jianmo (俞建模) was the long-time chairman and a core shareholder of SZSE-listed 002621, originally Dalian Sanlei (plastic-pipe machinery), which later pivoted into early-childhood education by acquiring the China operator of the US My Gym children's fitness brand and was renamed Meijimu (美吉姆). interesting_fact: The company he led reinvented itself from industrial machinery into children's education, taking over the China franchise of the US kids' gym brand My Gym.
notes: No longer in management; low public profile. Hurun lists wealth shared with Yu Yang. Company is now *ST (risk warning) status. Sanlei-machinery background is from memory of company history, verify in SZSE filings.

name: Yu Yang
current_role: Shareholder of Dalian My Gym Education Technology (formerly Dalian Sanlei Machinery, 002621.SZ, now delisted); no current executive role found
profile: Yu Yang is a founding promoter of Dalian Sanlei Machinery, a maker of plastic-pipe extrusion machinery that listed on the Shenzhen exchange in 2011. He co-founded it with Yu Jianmo, with whom Hurun lists the wealth jointly. In 2016-17 the pair sold control to Zhuhai Rongcheng, and the company pivoted into children's early-education franchising as 'My Gym' (美吉姆). He remained a major shareholder (about 3.8%).
interesting_fact: The company he co-founded made one of China's stranger listed-company pivots: from industrial plastic-pipe machinery (Sanlei) to licensing the US kids' gym brand My Gym in China.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of the 15 individual founding promoters when Dalian Sanlei Machinery Co. converted into a joint-stock company in 2008, before its September 2011 IPO at RMB 24 a share.
notes: The listed company (*ST My Gym, 002621) has been delisted, and I found no current company contact. Don't confuse him with Yu Yang, the general manager of Huaxin Co. (600621), who is a different person. Low profile.

name: Li Mingyan
current_role: Chairman, Zhejiang Shouxiangu Pharmaceutical (寿仙谷, SH: 603896)
profile: Correct characters are 李明焱 (list shows 李明炎). From a family of traditional medicine practitioners in Wuyi, Zhejiang, he built Shouxiangu, a 'China Time-honored Brand', into a listed maker of reishi (lingzhi) mushroom and broken-wall spore powder products. His two sons now serve as vice chairman and general manager.
interesting_fact: He helped drive international standards for traditional Chinese medicine on lingzhi (2018) and on broken-wall Ganoderma spore powder (ISO, 2025).
deep_cut_fact: From 1993 he combed the mountains of Zhejiang, Fujian and Jiangxi, collecting 50+ wild reishi strains. He bred 'Xianzhi No.1' around 2001, then sent seeds aboard China's first crewed spacecraft Shenzhou-5 to breed the improved 'Xianzhi No.2' (2006).
notes: Scientist-entrepreneur profile; open to media about TCM standardisation. Contact via the company's SSE-listed IR/board secretary. Not an energy/data-center fit.

name: Lu Yuanjian
current_role: Co-actual controller of Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon (300174.SZ) with Wang Yan'an; no formal company post since Feb 2018
profile: Born 1950, a chemical engineer-manager from Nanping, Fujian, who led and chaired Yuanli Active Carbon, which grew from a ~500-tonne plant (1999) into China's largest wood-based activated-carbon maker. He left formal posts in 2018 but remains controlling shareholder and is subscribing shares in Yuanli's acquisition of silica maker Tongsheng.
interesting_fact: Yuanli's wood-based activated carbon output grew from about 500 tonnes when the plant was built in 1999 to nearly 100,000 tonnes, making it the largest such producer in China.
deep_cut_fact: Before Yuanli he was director of Nanping No. 2 Chemical Factory and GM/chief engineer of Nanping Jialian Chemical; he later chaired the Evonik Jialian precipitated-silica JV in Nanping and served as president of the Fujian Activated Carbon Industry Association.
notes: Hurun lists co-owner as 'Wang Yanan'; filings give 王延安 (Wang Yan'an), his wife and fellow actual controller. Activated carbon/silica has energy-storage angles (supercapacitor carbon). Private; route via board secretary IR email.

name: Wang Yanan
current_role: Co-actual controller (with husband Lu Yuanjian) of Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon Co. (SZSE: 300174); holds no current post at the company
profile: Wang Yan'an (王延安, b. 1949) co-built Fujian Yuanli Active Carbon in Nanping, Fujian, with her husband Lu Yuanjian; she was general manager of the predecessor company and later a director and deputy GM. Yuanli is one of China's largest wood-based activated carbon producers and has moved into silica and carbon materials for new energy uses. She has since stepped back from any role.
interesting_fact: Yuanli's activated carbon business has expanded beyond water and food purification into materials for the battery/new-energy supply chain, such as porous carbon used in silicon-carbon anodes.
deep_cut_fact: Before going into industry she was a schoolteacher, teaching in the Wangtai school district and at a vocational school in Nanping, Fujian, before becoming GM of Nanping Yuanli Active Carbon, the company's predecessor.
notes: Name in Chinese is 王延安 (Wang Yan'an). Retired from company roles per the 2025 annual report; very low profile. The energy-materials angle may suit the podcast; route via board office dm@yuanlicarbon.com.

current_role: Founder, Chairman and controlling shareholder, Shenzhen Yitoa Intelligent Control (英唐智控, SZSE: 300131)
profile: Hu Qingzhou (b. 1968) founded Yitoa Electronics in Shenzhen in July 2001 and built it into a ChiNext-listed electronic-components distributor. Since 2020 he has steered it toward semiconductor manufacturing (IDM), starting with the purchase of Pioneer Micro Technology from Japan's Pioneer Corp. He still chairs the company, holding about 8.5% as of April 2026.

deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he worked at the Huaibei (Anhui) tax bureau and at ICBC's Shenzhen branch. He studied at University of Science and Technology Beijing (BS 1991) and earned a management master's from Tianjin University in 2000, a year before founding Yitoa.
notes: Active chip-industry founder; the semiconductor localisation and IDM-pivot story could suit an entrepreneurship episode. Best route is the board-secretary/IR email from the 2026 interim report. His stake has shrunk through pledge-related transfers, so avoid that topic.

current_role: Retired. Former chairman of Kunming Department Store Group (昆百大, now 5i5j / 我爱我家, 000560.SZ) and former Executive President of the China Foundation for Poverty Alleviation

profile: Hilton Darren Nathanson is a Perth-raised, London-based hedge fund manager who founded Marble Bar Asset Management (MBAM) in 2002 (with Gilad Hayeem per one source). interesting_fact: In February 2001 he gained control of the relaunched Eden Group by leading a management buyout of the Kyte Group's remaining stake in Kyte Securities.
deep_cut_fact: He is a University of Western Australia commerce graduate (BCom '92) and featured on the UWA alumni podcast in an episode titled 'Find something you love doing'.
notes: Not connected to Marshall Wace. Search summaries also mention a family charitable trust named for Rosemarie Nathanson and later ventures (Firefly Capital 2013, Red Deer 2014) - unverified, not included. Route via Marble Bar Asset Management.

name: Tony Brotherton-Ratcliffe
current_role: Retired (2020) Non-Executive Chairman of Croudace Homes Group; family owners of Croudace
profile: Tony Brotherton-Ratcliffe is the son of Jack Brotherton-Ratcliffe, who co-founded South-East housebuilder Croudace in 1946 and owned it outright from 1957. Tony became non-executive chairman in 2001 when his father retired at 81, and retired in 2020, handing over to his nephew Caspar Brotherton. The family's wealth (shared with Diana Jones in the Rich List) comes from Croudace.
interesting_fact: Croudace's first private development (Haroldslea Close, Horley, 1951) bought land at £100 per house; two-bed homes sold for £1,690.
deep_cut_fact: Croudace began in 1946 repairing bomb-damaged properties after WWII, and its first new-build contract (1947) was 200 council houses in Bletchingley, Surrey; in 1962 it won consent for Vigo Village, an 800-home New Town-style scheme on a former army camp in Kent.
notes: Private family; retired from the board in 2020. Estates Gazette rich lists also cite the family via Croudace. Best route is via Croudace Homes Group head office.

name: Ayman Asfari
current_role: Co-founder, The Asfari Foundation (London); former CEO (2002-2020) of oilfield-services group Petrofac
profile: Syrian-born British engineer (b. 1958; Villanova, Penn, Wharton MBA) who joined Petrofac in 1991, bought it out in 2001 and floated it in London in 2005, building a major oil & gas engineering contractor. He stepped down as CEO at end-2020. Since Assad's fall he has become a prominent diaspora investor and philanthropist re-engaging with Syria.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 he returned to Syria via Idlib and laid the foundation stone for the Dr. Mohammad Adeeb Asfari Maternity and Children's Hospital, named after his father; in 2025 he met Syria's energy minister about oil and gas investment and was floated as a possible transitional PM.
deep_cut_fact: His first job was in Oman as a consulting engineer doing soil testing; when he joined Petrofac in 1991 it was essentially a single plant in Tyler, Texas. He won the UK EY Entrepreneur of the Year award in 2011.
notes: Sensitivities: he was questioned in the SFO's Unaoil-related inquiry (Petrofac itself pleaded guilty in 2021; he was not charged) and was a large Conservative donor - avoid. His personal site aymanasfari.com (listed on Wikipedia) did not load. Great angle: post-war Syrian energy reconstruction. Foundation is the cleanest route.

name: Bart Becht
current_role: Former CEO of Reckitt Benckiser (1995-2011) and former partner at JAB Holding (2012-2019); investor and philanthropist
profile: Dutch-born Bart Becht (b. 1956) joined Benckiser in 1988 after Procter & Gamble, became CEO in 1995 and led the 1999 Reckitt & Colman merger, roughly quintupling Reckitt Benckiser's value before retiring in 2011. He then became a partner at JAB Holding (Keurig Dr Pepper, Krispy Kreme, Pret) and chaired Coty, retiring from JAB in 2019.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Reckitt Benckiser was the fourth-best performing FTSE 100 stock over the ten years to 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He founded the Becht Family Charitable Trust in 2006 (humanitarian, education and environmental causes incl. Save the Children), sat on Save the Children UK's board 2013-14 and ranked second on the Sunday Times Giving List in 2011.
notes: Coty chairmanship appears to have ended in 2018 (Peter Harf chair 2018-2025) per search-result governance data; current board seats not verified. Education: Groningen BA, Chicago Booth MBA. Low public profile since 2019.

name: Brian P Friedman
current_role: President and Director, Jefferies Financial Group (NYSE: JEF); Director, Vitesse Energy (NYSE: VTS)
profile: Brian P. Friedman (70) has been President and a director of Jefferies Financial Group since 2013, after joining legacy Jefferies Group in 2005. A former Wachtell Lipton lawyer, he spent 17 years at Furman Selz (head of investment banking) and ran Jefferies Capital Partners. He sits on the board of Vitesse Energy, the oil and gas company Jefferies spun off in 2023.
interesting_fact: About 70% of his pay since joining Jefferies has come in equity; counting all earned and unearned deferred shares and options, he would own about 6.8 million Jefferies shares, roughly 3.2% of the firm.
deep_cut_fact: He is co-chairman of the board of Strive, a workforce-training nonprofit, and a board member of the HC Leukemia Foundation. He graduated summa cum laude in economics from Wharton, also took a Wharton M.S. in Accounting, and holds a Columbia Law J.D.

public_contacts.value: https://www.jefferies.com/contact-us/ (directs investor, media and general inquiries to Jefferies Investor Relations)

notes: Energy angle: Vitesse Energy (non-operated oil and gas interests, spun off by Jefferies in 2023). Jefferies' IR pages are behind a bot wall, so no published email was captured. Route via Jefferies IR/corporate communications.

profile: Founder and long-time chairman of Beijing-based LandOcean Energy Services (Hengtai Aipu), a ChiNext-listed provider of oil and gas exploration software, geophysical services and oilfield equipment, which put him on the Hurun China list in 2011-2014. profile: Zeng Zhijun (b. 1971), a PhD in management from Hong Kong PolyU, is co-controller with Yang Liangzhi of Richinfo, an industrial-internet tech and services firm (enterprise messaging, cloud). notes: Identity confirmed via Richinfo convertible-bond prospectus (2026). Low personal profile.

name: Chen Zhenbiao
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Petpal Pet Nutrition Technology Co. (SZSE: 300673), Pingyang, Wenzhou
profile: Chen Zhenbiao (陈振标), born 1961, is a senior economist with a master's degree. In 2002 he co-founded Wenzhou Peidi Pet Products with family members including Chen Zhenlu and Zheng Xianglan, and built it into Petpal, a leading Chinese maker of pet chews and pet food, much of it exported. It listed on ChiNext in 2017, and he still runs it as chairman and GM.
interesting_fact: Petpal is based in Shuitou town, Pingyang, historically China's leather-processing hub. He also chairs the Zhejiang Import & Export Pet Food and Supplies Association and is vice-president of the China Animal Agriculture Association's pet industry branch.
deep_cut_fact: Before pet food he spent a decade (1992 to 2002) as director of the Pingyang Peidi Leather Goods Factory (平阳县佩蒂皮件制品厂). The Peidi name and the leather know-how carried straight into the pet-chew business he founded in 2002.
notes: Hurun co-lists Zheng Chunlan; the company's co-founder in filings is Zheng Xianglan (郑香兰), possibly the same person under a different romanisation, which I could not verify. Web search quota ran out mid-lane; data comes from Sina Finance filings. Weak fit for the energy/data-centre theme.

current_role: Founder and former chairman/GM, Shenzhen Shengxunda Technology (盛讯达, 300518.SZ; now renamed Guangxi Xinxunda Technology); ceded control in Sept 2022
profile: Guangzhou-born (1984) MBA who founded Shengxunda in Dec 2006 and took it public on ChiNext in June 2016 while holding ~60%. The firm began making mobile-phone hardware, then pivoted fully to mobile games (standalone and cross-platform titles) by 2014; it now focuses on casual/social card games for Southeast Asia. Control passed to new owners in 2022.

profile: Hurun-listed (2017-2018) founder behind Xin Point, established in Huizhou in 2002 and listed in Hong Kong in 2017. Through Huizhou Keen Point Precision Plastics it supplies electroplated and painted plastic trim ('one-stop surface decoration') to global automakers, with ~4,700 staff and production in China, Malaysia and Mexico.

name: Guan Li
current_role: Former SF Holding (顺丰控股) supervisor and SF strategy/innovation executive; current role not confirmed
profile: Guan Li (官力, born 1979) is an SF Express insider. After strategy consulting in Singapore and Beijing, he joined SF's parent in 2007 and rose from senior strategic-planning manager to VP of strategy management and VP of innovation management. He later headed SF's change-management department. He sat on SF Holding's supervisory board from December 2016, which explains his place on the Hurun list (2017–2020) through SF shares.
interesting_fact: He was one of the strategy executives who joined SF in 2007, long before its 2017 backdoor listing in Shenzhen made Wang Wei and early managers very rich.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a master's in high-performance computation for engineered systems from the National University of Singapore. He began his career as a consultant at a Singapore decision-systems consultancy (2002–05) before moving into logistics strategy.
notes: Bio is from SF Holding's 2017 annual report (supervisor section). He no longer appears among directors or supervisors in the 2020 report, so the SF IR email is only an indirect route. Very low public profile.

He served as general manager from 1995 to 2020 and remains chairman; the company also has a Cambodian subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Anji's product range includes six main seasoning families - pork-rib, seafood, bone-broth, beef, chicken and restaurant-dish seasonings - plus natural extracts such as mushroom, scallop and abalone essences.
notes: Very low media profile. Web search budget ran out before a personal deep-cut fact could be sourced. Route via board secretary (published IR email).

notes: Highly relevant to a data-center podcast because of Eoptolink, but Hu has a very low profile and left the board in 2020 (board history: http://vip.stock.finance.sina.com.cn/corp/go.php/vCI_CorpManager/stockid/300502.phtml). profile: Sun Li (孙黎) leads Xiamen Amoytop Biotech, founded in 1996 and focused on long-acting recombinant protein drugs, especially peginterferon for chronic hepatitis B. HealthCor backed Heartflow, the AI-driven non-invasive coronary-artery imaging company, whose board he has sat on since 2011 and which IPO'd in August 2025.

name: Perry A Sook
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Nexstar Media Group, Inc. (NASDAQ: NXST)
profile: Perry Sook (b. c.1958, DuBois, PA) founded Nexstar in 1996 with a single TV station, WYOU in Scranton, after selling Superior Communication Group to Sinclair, and took it public in 2003. Through the Media General (2017) and Tribune (2019) deals it became the largest US local broadcaster: with partners ~265 stations in 132 markets, plus NewsNation, 81% of The CW and 31% of Food Network. He chaired the NAB Joint Board 2023-25.
interesting_fact: Named Broadcasting & Cable's 2009 Broadcaster of the Year and inducted into the B&C Hall of Fame in 2014; he has 45+ years in broadcasting and sits on the NAB and Broadcasters Foundation of America boards.
deep_cut_fact: His first sales job was at a small radio station in Kissimmee, Florida, which failed to pay his commission after he landed a big ad sale, prompting his move into TV sales. Early on he also did radio sales and on-air work at WPME AM/FM in Punxsutawney, PA, and was an adjunct professor at Edinboro State University.
notes: Punxsutawney/WPME detail confirmed by NY State Broadcasters Hall of Fame bio (https://halloffame.nysbroadcasters.org/post/perry-sook). Route via Nexstar corporate communications.

name: Tom Markusic
current_role: Co-founder of Firefly Aerospace (Nasdaq: FLY); former CEO, later chief technical advisor and board member; 10%+ holder per SEC filings
profile: Tom Markusic, a Princeton PhD in mechanical and aerospace engineering, co-founded Firefly in Texas in 2014 and relaunched it as Firefly Aerospace in 2017 with Noosphere backing. He was CEO until 2022, then became chief technical advisor and board member; his wealth stems from his Firefly stake after its 2025 IPO.
interesting_fact: He worked at three of the earliest New Space companies before Firefly: principal propulsion engineer at SpaceX, senior systems engineer at Blue Origin and VP of propulsion at Virgin Galactic, after starting as a NASA and US Air Force propulsion scientist.
deep_cut_fact: His original research specialty was electric (plasma) propulsion for spacecraft, from his time as a NASA/USAF research scientist, rather than the chemical rockets he later built at Firefly.
notes: Based in Austin area. No longer an operating exec (Jason Kim is CEO), so the Firefly press team may not route to him. Firefly signed Starcloud (space data centers) as a customer: good data-center hook. Avoid referencing past Virgin Galactic/shareholder disputes.

name: Tom Martin
current_role: Probable match: Thomas Henry Martin, chairman of Martin's Properties Holdings Ltd (Chelsea, London), per MarketScreener
profile: The Sunday Times Rich List 2020 lists a Tom Martin with a property fortune. The most plausible match is Tom Martin of Martin's Properties, a family-owned investor with a large Chelsea/King's Road portfolio. He was managing director after his father Peter Martin died in 2009 and has been listed as chairman of the holding company since 2023; Richard Bourne is CEO.
interesting_fact: Martin's Properties co-founded the King's Road Partnership Business Improvement District and still sits on its board; in 2025 it reported that 75% of its Chelsea residential portfolio was let to overseas customers.
notes: Identity match to the Rich List entry is inferred, not confirmed. MD quote and 2009 succession: https://www.constructionenquirer.com/?p=105933. Chairman role from MarketScreener (https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/THOMAS-HENRY-MARTIN-A2IP0J/, search summary). Private, low-profile family; approach via the company.

name: Vernon Hill
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Metro Bank (UK) and Commerce Bancorp (US); no current executive role confirmed (left Republic Bank in 2022)
profile: Vernon W. Hill II (b. 1945) is an American banker who founded Commerce Bank in New Jersey in 1973, grew it to about 470 branches and saw it sold to TD for $8.5bn in 2007, then co-founded Metro Bank, the first new UK high-street bank in over 100 years (2010), chairing it until 2019. He has also chaired pet insurer Fetch (Petplan US) and wrote 'Fans Not Customers' (2012).
interesting_fact: Forbes put him in its 2007 '20-20-20 Club' alongside Warren Buffett and Larry Ellison: CEOs with 20+ year tenures delivering 20%+ annual shareholder returns (Commerce compounded 23% a year).
deep_cut_fact: After Wharton he founded a real estate firm finding sites for McDonald's, which meant driving Ray Kroc on scouting trips; he credits McDonald's for his retail-style 'stores not branches' banking model. He also co-founded Galloway National Golf Club near Atlantic City (Tom Fazio design).
notes: Listed with wife Shirley Hill (InterArch founder). Big veterinary philanthropist (Hill Family Foundation; $10m Vernon and Shirley Hill Pavilion at Penn Vet). No published personal contact found; route via Hill Family Foundation or his publisher Profile Books.

name: Shirley Hill
current_role: Founder of InterArch, the architecture and branding firm behind Commerce Bank and Metro Bank's branch design (wife of Metro Bank founder Vernon Hill)
profile: Founder of InterArch, the design and branding firm responsible for the look of Commerce Bank (US) and Metro Bank (UK), both founded by her husband Vernon Hill. Listed jointly with him on the Sunday Times Rich List (finance). Metro Bank moved its design work to other suppliers by end-2020.
interesting_fact: InterArch created the branding for both Commerce Bank and Metro Bank, the 'retail-style' banks known for long hours and in-person 'stores'.
deep_cut_fact: The Hills gave $10 million for the Vernon and Shirley Hill Pavilion at the University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine; their foundation is one of the largest supporters of veterinary causes.
notes: No independent profile or published contact found; no recent source on her status, so alive marked unknown. Best route is likely via Vernon Hill's business offices. Avoid the InterArch/Metro related-party contract topic (governance controversy).

name: Shishir Bajaj
current_role: Former chairman & managing director, Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar (1986-2014); patriarch of the Kushagra Bajaj-led Bajaj Group (sugar, ethanol, power, FMCG incl. Bajaj Consumer Care / Bajaj Corp)
profile: Grandson of freedom fighter Jamnalal Bajaj and younger brother of the late Rahul Bajaj, Shishir Bajaj ran Bajaj Hindusthan, once described as Asia's largest sugar company, from 1986 until handing the chair to son Kushagra in Oct 2014. His branch of the family controls the sugar/ethanol/power group and the FMCG company Bajaj Corp (Bajaj Consumer Care).
interesting_fact: He said his grandfather Jamnalal Bajaj, busy with the Freedom Movement, set up the sugar business (1931, reportedly with Gandhi's blessing) and let Shishir's father run it.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership the family's foundation and Jamnalal Bajaj Trust ran a water programme that deepened 82 rivers and rejuvenated ~120 km of riverbeds around the group's sugar areas; he set a goal of covering 1,000 villages in five years.
notes: Press email is for Neeraj Jha, Group President & Chief Communication Officer (Bajaj Group, Mumbai), as published on the media contacts page. Energy angle: group cogeneration/power business (450 MW per 2014 article). Chairman tenure dates from MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/SHISHIR-KAMALNAYAN-BAJAJ-A040QN/experience/). Current status/alive not verified.

name: Rashesh Chandrakant Shah
current_role: Chairman, Edelweiss Group / Edelweiss Financial Services Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Indian financier (b. 1963) who co-founded Edelweiss with Venkat Ramaswamy in November 1995, after IIM Ahmedabad (MBA 1989), ICICI and Prime Securities. Unable to meet SEBI's Rs 5 crore capital requirement, Edelweiss started in PE syndication, M&A and advisory with three staff in a small Mumbai office and grew into a diversified financial group. In Feb 2026 he bought a further 2.1% of EFSL for Rs 236 crore.
interesting_fact: He was President of FICCI for 2017-18 and has served on the executive committees of the NSE and SEBI.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first in his family to attend an English-medium school; before his MBA he took a B.Sc. in statistics at KC College, Mumbai, and spent a year studying exports at the Indian Institute of Foreign Trade, Delhi.
notes: Feb 2026 'Group Chairman' title and stake purchase: https://www.motilaloswal.com/news/stocks/117704 . The IR email was seen only in a search snippet of the Edelweiss IR page (the site returned 403 to direct fetch), so re-check it. The EdelGive Foundation (Edelweiss's philanthropy arm) is another angle. Wikipedia carries COI/paid-editing tags. Avoid the 2020 ED/Capstone matter.

name: Rakesh Malhotra
current_role: Co-founder and head of SAR Group (Livguard, Livfast, Livpure, Lectrix EV, Ncubate), Gurugram
profile: Engineer-entrepreneur who founded Luminous Power Technologies in 1988 and built it into one of India's leading home inverter/UPS and battery brands before selling it to Schneider Electric (74% in 2011, the rest later). He then relaunched SAR Group around clean energy, founding Livguard (inverters, batteries, solar, storage) in 2014, plus EV and venture-incubation arms.
interesting_fact: He started Luminous at 26 with just Rs 40,000 in a 600 sq ft workshop in South Delhi; after the Schneider exit he built a second energy company, Livguard, reported to be worth about Rs 3,500 crore.
deep_cut_fact: Luminous's first big break was an order from Modi Xerox for 28 UPS units worth Rs 4.2 lakh; the company closed its first year with just Rs 8 lakh in revenue.
notes: SAR Group co-founded with Navneet Kapoor (per Livguard 'About us'). Good fit for an energy-storage / Indian power-backup episode. No personal social accounts verified; Livguard's published mailbox is marketing, so it is a fallback rather than a press desk.

name: Akshata Murty
current_role: Director, Catamaran Ventures (venture capital); Infosys shareholder (~0.9%)
profile: Akshata Murty, born 1980 in Hubballi, India, is the daughter of Infosys co-founder N. R. Narayana Murthy and holds roughly 0.9% of Infosys. Educated at Claremont McKenna, FIDM Los Angeles and Stanford (MBA), she ran a fashion label, became a director of Catamaran Ventures in 2013 and has stakes/board seats in businesses such as Digme Fitness and Soroco. She is married to former UK PM Rishi Sunak.
interesting_fact: She studied economics and French at Claremont McKenna, then took a diploma in clothes manufacturing at the Fashion Institute of Design and Merchandising before launching her own fashion label.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion and venture capital, she spent two years from 2007 as marketing director at Tendris, a Dutch cleantech firm - a neat link to an energy podcast.
notes: High-profile and media-cautious given former spouse-of-PM role; no personal official site/social listed on Wikipedia. Best route likely via Catamaran Ventures or a mutual introduction. Avoid property/tax topics.

name: Pradeep Kumar Jain
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, PNC Infratech Ltd (NSE: PNCINFRA)
profile: Pradeep Kumar Jain is the promoter, chairman and managing director of Agra-headquartered PNC Infratech, an Indian highway and infrastructure EPC/construction company. He ran PNC Construction Company as a sole proprietorship in Agra before it was folded into PNC Infratech (incorporated 1999), and oversees project administration, monitoring and government liaison.
interesting_fact: PNC Infratech grew out of his Agra sole proprietorship, PNC Construction Company, which the company acquired in exchange for equity shares; he has over 43 years in infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Bachelor of Arts degree, not an engineering degree, despite leading a major highway construction firm; he is also a director of PNC Cold Storage Pvt Ltd.
notes: IR handled by outside advisor Strategic Growth Advisors (per Q1 FY27 earnings call transcript). PNC Cold Storage directorship per MarketScreener. Emails cited from BSE filing letterheads as summarized by search; verify exact filing.

name: Prashant Mehta
current_role: Former managing director, Rajesh Exports Ltd. (MD from 1 Feb 1995; retired 3 Dec 2022)
profile: Prashant Mehta co-founded Bangalore gold jewellery maker Rajesh Exports with his brother Rajesh Mehta. They grew it from a small garage workshop into one of India's largest companies, and in 2015 it bought Swiss gold refiner Valcambi for $400m. He was MD from 1995 until he retired in December 2022; Rajesh Mehta remains executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2015 Rajesh Exports bought Valcambi, which Wikipedia calls the world's largest gold refiner, for $400 million; the company ranked 7th on the Fortune India 500 in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He and his brother started out making jewellery in a small garage workshop in Bangalore with about ten workers, and opened their first retail outlet by 1990.
notes: Retirement confirmed by the NSE filing RAJESHEXPO_03122022200300_RelIntimationMDresignation.pdf ('desired to retire'). No personal contacts found. In 2026 SEBI made fraud allegations against Rajesh Exports, per Wikipedia; this is a sensitive topic to keep in mind for outreach.

name: Ashok Kumar Goel
current_role: Non-executive, non-independent director of Hindustan Oil Exploration Co. (since 2018); former Chairman & MD of Essel Propack (now EPL Ltd)
profile: Long-time head of Mumbai-based Essel Propack, the world's largest maker of laminated tubes (toothpaste, pharma and cosmetics tubes), and a member of the Essel Group promoter family. In 2019 his family's Ashok Goel Trust sold a 51% stake to Blackstone at Rs 134 a share. He now holds board roles including at oil & gas producer Hindustan Oil Exploration.
interesting_fact: With about a third of the global oral-care tube market, Essel pivoted to pharma and cosmetics tubes, which Goel said fetch roughly 2x and 3-4x oral-care prices: 'So suddenly, our market size nearly tripled.'
notes: Described by Business Standard (2011) as reticent and media-shy. Energy angle: board seat at Hindustan Oil Exploration (per MarketScreener/Tofler, DIN 00025350). MarketScreener also lists an independent directorship at Nilkamal from 2023 (unverified). Blackstone deal: https://www.bloombergquint.com/business/blackstone-to-acquire-majority-stake-in-essel-propack

name: Chimanlal Khimchand Mehta
profile: Deceased: C.K. Mehta, founder and chairman emeritus of the Deepak Group (Deepak Nitrite, 1970; Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals, 1979), died on 3 July 2023 at age 91 in Vadodara.
notes: Died 3 July 2023 (sources: Business Today; Deepak Fertilisers BSE filing https://bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/695923ed-fd4a-490e-b542-8873a97405a4.pdf). His son Sailesh C. Mehta (P14423) chairs Deepak Fertilisers.

name: V K Mathews
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, IBS Software / The IBS Group; owner and chairman of Calicut FC
profile: Valayil Korath Mathews is a Kerala-born aeronautical engineer (IIT Kanpur) who worked at Air India and then as a general manager at Emirates (1983-1997). He founded IBS Software in 1997, and it grew into a SaaS provider for airline operations, loyalty, cargo, hospitality and cruise. Blackstone is a backer of IBS, and Mathews remains executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2024 he launched Calicut FC, which won the inaugural Super League Kerala title, beating Forca Kochi 2-1 in the final. The club has said it aims to reach the I-League and ISL.
deep_cut_fact: In 1980 he taught computer science at the Military College for the Indian Army, then joined Air India as a systems analyst (1981-83), before 14 years at Emirates. He grew up in the village of Kizhakkambalam in Ernakulam district.
notes: Visible in Kerala's IT and football scene and speaks often (Khaleej Times, Onmanorama). Wikipedia article is flagged as possibly autobiographical, so check the details. No press email found on the IBS site; use the IBS website/LinkedIn.

name: Forest Baskett
current_role: Partner (listed as Special Partner) at New Enterprise Associates (NEA)
profile: Forest Baskett (b. 1943) is a computer scientist turned venture capitalist: former Stanford EE professor, founder/director of DEC's Western Research Lab (1982-86), then CTO and SVP R&D at Silicon Graphics, before joining NEA in 1999 (general partner from 2004). His SEC 10%-owner filings (Trevi, Korro Bio, Senti, SpyGlass, BuzzFeed) reflect NEA fund holdings.
interesting_fact: At Stanford he was doctoral advisor to Andy Bechtolsheim and was involved in the founding of Sun Microsystems; he is a National Academy of Engineering member (1994) for high-performance workstation hardware/software.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he spent two years at Los Alamos National Laboratory, where he designed the operating system for the original Cray-1 supercomputer; he also co-introduced the BCMP queueing-network model.
notes: Alive inferred from 2026 SEC insider filings and UT Austin CS advisory council listing; no death notice seen. Strong fit for data-centre/compute themes (Cray-1, SGI, workstations). Computer History Museum has his oral history: https://www.computerhistory.org/collections/catalog/102717243. Route via NEA.

name: Shaji Mathew
current_role: EVP and Chief Human Resources Officer (Group Head of HR), Infosys
profile: Shaji Mathew has spent over 31 years at Infosys, rising from software engineer trainee to global head of delivery for Financial Services, Insurance, Healthcare and Life Sciences, and became Group Head of HR in March 2023, succeeding Krish Shankar. He is an Infosys executive officer leading its AI-first workforce and capability-based talent model.
interesting_fact: He moved from leading delivery for Infosys' financial services and healthcare businesses directly into the top HR job in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He began at Infosys as a software engineer trainee; he also serves on the board of IIIT Bangalore and the CII National Committee on Leadership and HR.
notes: IIIT-B board/CII roles per Infosys profile as shown in search results. Active speaker (WEF, SHRM, qwoted media source profile).

name: Richard Todd Schwartz
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI)
profile: Lawyer-turned-iGaming executive who co-founded Rush Street Interactive (BetRivers online casino and sportsbook) in 2012 with Neil Bluhm and Greg Carlin. He served as president and was promoted to CEO in August 2021; his RSI stake underpins his wealth. Previously he built the online gaming business at WMS Industries.
interesting_fact: Before RSI he founded and led WMS Industries' interactive business, which in 2010 launched the award-winning UK-facing online casino Jackpot Party.
deep_cut_fact: He started at WMS Gaming as Intellectual Property Counsel before moving into corporate development and online gaming; earlier he was VP of Technology Development & Legal Affairs at Telecom Italia Lab USA in San Francisco. Berkeley AB, UC Hastings JD.

public_contacts.value: lisa@lisajohnsoncommunications.com (Lisa Johnson Communications, RSI media contact)

notes: CEO title confirmed on RSI About page (Nov 2026). Deep-cut details (WMS IP counsel, Telecom Italia Lab) come from search snippets of Gambling Insider profile (page 403 to direct fetch) - verify before use. Milken page fetch did not render bio; WMS/Jackpot Party fact seen in search snippet.

name: Muhammad Raghib Hussain
current_role: CEO, Altera (Intel's FPGA business, majority-owned by Silver Lake) since May 2025; director, Cirrus Logic
profile: Pakistani-American chip executive who co-founded Cavium (networking/security processors) with Syed Ali in 2000, took it public in 2007 and sold it to Marvell for ~$6bn in 2018. He then ran Marvell's products and technology as president, helping build its data-center/custom AI silicon business, before being named Altera CEO when Silver Lake bought 51% of the FPGA maker from Intel.
interesting_fact: Intel picked him to lead Altera as part of the April 2025 deal valuing the FPGA pioneer at $8.75bn, making him the first CEO of Altera as a standalone, PE-backed company.
deep_cut_fact: A NED University (Karachi) computer-systems engineering grad, he began his career at Karachi firms Zelin (Pvt.) Ltd. and ITIM Associates before moving to Silicon Valley (Cisco, Cadence); he later earned an MS from San Jose State.
notes: Input lists him as Marvell president, but he moved to Altera in May 2025. Strong fit for data-center/AI theme (FPGAs, AI infrastructure). Altera media contact is Stephen Gabriel via the newsroom email. NED University awarded him a citation (neduet.edu.pk).

name: Keith Richards
current_role: Guitarist, secondary vocalist and co-principal songwriter, The Rolling Stones
profile: English musician and an original member of the Rolling Stones. His songwriting partnership with Mick Jagger is one of the most successful in history, and his career spans more than six decades. Wealth comes from music royalties and touring. He also has a solo career (latest solo album Crosseyed Heart, 2015) and wrote the bestselling memoir Life (2010).
interesting_fact: Dartford, his hometown, honoured him with a statue in 2023. In 2025 he was the first recipient of the Connecticut Governor's Award of Excellence.
deep_cut_fact: His grandfather Gus Dupree would only let him have the guitar on the shelf once he could reach it, which he called 'the prize of the century'. He turned the story into a 2014 children's book, Gus and Me. As a boy chorister he sang in a trio for Queen Elizabeth II at Westminster Abbey.
notes: Not an obvious fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Approaches go through Rolling Stones management/label. He also produced the 1997 Wingless Angels Rastafarian nyabinghi record on his own Mindless Records label.

name: Mike Clare
current_role: Head of Clare Family Office Ltd (formerly Stable Ventures), Beaconsfield; founder of The Clare Foundation; former founder, chairman and CEO of Dreams plc
profile: Dr Mike Clare founded UK bed retailer Dreams in 1987, opening a modest shop in Uxbridge, and grew it to 200+ superstores before selling in March 2008. He now runs the Clare Family Office, which invests and lends private capital (including short-term business loans and Bijou Living's office-to-residential conversions), and chairs his Buckinghamshire charity, The Clare Foundation.
interesting_fact: His charity, The Clare Foundation (set up 2009), has an overarching aim to make Buckinghamshire 'the happiest county in the UK', and runs CAN, a pro-bono Charity Advisors Network, plus a charity incubator for start-up philanthropists.
deep_cut_fact: To open the first Dreams shop in 1987, aged 30, he sold his car, maxed out his Barclaycard and put up his home as security; in the early years he sold beds by day, delivered them in the evening and did the bookkeeping on Sundays. He had risen from salesman to divisional director in furniture retail.
notes: Very approachable: his own site has a 'Send Mike a message' form and says he is 'not great on social media'. mgc@clarenco.org appears as a mailto link on his contact page (exact label not visible in scraped HTML). Deputy Lieutenant for Buckinghamshire; honorary doctorate from Bucks New University (2009); active speaker/mentor. His site mentions a recent health matter; do not reference it.

name: Olivia Harrison
current_role: Director, Apple Corps; trustee/director, The Material World Foundation; chair, Harrison Family Foundation; steward of George Harrison's estate and catalogue
profile: Born Olivia Trinidad Arias in Los Angeles in 1948, she worked at A&M Records and then George Harrison's Dark Horse label before marrying him in 1978. Since his 2001 death she has managed his legacy: reissues, books and films, and serves as one of Apple Corps' five directors. Her wealth (shared with son Dhani on the Sunday Times list) is inherited.
interesting_fact: She has won Emmys as a producer for Scorsese's 'George Harrison: Living in the Material World' (2011) and 'The Beatles: Get Back' (2021), plus Grammys for 'Concert for George' and the 'All Things Must Pass' reissue.
deep_cut_fact: In 1990 she founded the Romanian Angel Appeal for Romanian orphans, and in 2022 published 'Came the Lightening', a poetic memoir she said was inspired by Edna St. Vincent Millay.
notes: Not an energy/data-center figure; wealth is inherited (George Harrison estate). Best route is via the Material World Foundation email or the George Harrison official site/label. Trustee listing: https://register-of-charities.charitycommission.gov.uk/en/charity-search/-/charity-details/266746/trustees

name: Dhani Harrison
current_role: Musician, composer and singer-songwriter (solo artist; thenewno2)
profile: Dhani Harrison (b. 1978), son of George and Olivia Harrison, is an English-American musician and film/TV composer. He helped complete his father's final album Brainwashed (2002), formed thenewno2 in 2006, released solo albums In Parallel (2017) and Innerstanding, and scores films with partner Paul Hicks. Rich-list wealth is listed as inherited, shared with Olivia Harrison.
interesting_fact: He is named after the sixth and seventh notes of the Indian music scale, dha and ni; Dhani is also a North Indian raga.
deep_cut_fact: He studied industrial design and physics at Brown University and pursued a career as a car designer at McLaren Automotive before turning to music professionally.
notes: Musician, not an entrepreneur; wealth is inherited. Engineering/design background (Brown, McLaren) could be an angle.

name: Desmond Richard
profile: Likely a merged Rich List entry for the Maybury siblings Desmond and Richard Maybury (with Eleanor Maybury), founders of London's Big Bus Company. They started it in June 1991 with a handful of open-top buses, merged it with Paris's Les Cars Rouges in 2011 to form Big Bus Tours, and sold to Exponent Private Equity in Feb 2015.
interesting_fact: Big Bus began in London in 1991 with three or four buses and grew into a global sightseeing operator in cities such as Dubai, Hong Kong, Paris, New York and Sydney before the 2015 sale.
notes: No source uses the exact name 'Desmond Richard'. Travel Weekly lists 'Richard, Desmond and Eleanor Maybury' as Big Bus Tours founders on the 2016 Rich List, so this record probably merges two brothers; please check which one the journalist means. No current role or public contact found for either.

name: Sacha Mascolo-Tarbuck
current_role: Global Brand Director & Owner, TONI&GUY Global Group; majority/controlling shareholder (June 2026); sole owner of label.m
profile: Daughter of TONI&GUY co-founder Toni Mascolo. Long-time global creative director responsible for the brand's imagery and annual trend collections; in June 2026 took a majority controlling stake in TONI&GUY Global Group, with label.m wholly owned by her.
interesting_fact: Her grandfather Francesco was a barber from near Pompeii; her father and uncle opened the first TONI&GUY salon in Clapham, London.
deep_cut_fact: Started out assisting her uncle Anthony on brand-building, and helped session stylist Guido Paulo at London Fashion Week creating big 1980s hair for supermodels; says 'I'm a fashion follower rather than celebrity lover.'
notes: Ownership news: https://hji.co.uk/toniguy-global-group-enters-new-era (8 June 2026). Off-topic for energy podcast; entrepreneurship angle only.

name: The Walduck family
current_role: Owners of Imperial London Hotels (Bloomsbury, London); active directors of Imperial London Hotels Group Ltd include Stephen, Alexander and Jason Walduck
profile: The Walducks have run London hotels since Thomas Henry Walduck bought one in Warwick Court in 1837. Imperial London Hotels runs a cluster in Bloomsbury, including the Royal National (1,630 rooms), the Tavistock, the Bedford, the President, the Morton and the Imperial. The flagship Imperial reopened in August 2026 after renovation as the group's first lifestyle hotel.
interesting_fact: When the merged Royal National Hotel officially opened in 1998 with 1,630 rooms, it was billed as Western Europe's largest hotel; the Beatles stayed at the family's President Hotel in summer 1963.
deep_cut_fact: The family's post-war Tavistock Hotel was Britain's first post-war hotel: 77 rooms with ensuites and free-to-use TVs, on the site of Virginia Woolf's former home (it carries her English Heritage blue plaque).
notes: Family business, now led by the children of Richard, Thomas and Stephen Walduck. Directors from Companies House: Alexander H.E.P. Walduck, Jason A.G. Walduck, Stephen H. Walduck, Katharine T. Waller, Candida S. Walton. Rich List history: £205m (2013) to £310m (2017) per The Caterer. Corporate accounts, not personal ones. The site has a Contact Us page.

name: Stewart Bainum Jr
current_role: Chairman, Choice Hotels International (NYSE: CHH)
profile: Stewart W. Bainum Jr. (b. 1946, Takoma Park, Maryland) is chairman of Choice Hotels and son of its founder Stewart Bainum Sr. Since the 1980s he has led four public companies: Choice Hotels, HCR Manor Care, Vitalink Pharmacy Services and Sunburst Hospitality. He served as a Democrat in the Maryland House of Delegates (1979-82) and Senate (1983-86).
interesting_fact: He led Manor Care's 1980 acquisition of Quality Inns, the hotel business that became Choice Hotels; by 1983 Manor Care was the second-largest US nursing-home company.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he taught at Southern College in Tennessee and studied theology at Andrews University in Michigan for 18 months (1971-72); he began working in his father's business at age 12 during summer breaks.
notes: UCLA Anderson MBA (1970) and alumni-award recipient. Best route is via Choice Hotels corporate communications / IR (not captured here).

name: Michael D Farkas
current_role: Founder, CEO and Executive Chairman, NextNRG, Inc. (Nasdaq: NXXT), Miami Beach
profile: Michael D. Farkas founded EV-charging network Blink Charging and led it as chairman/CEO for nearly two decades. He now runs NextNRG, which combines AI-driven smart microgrids, wired and wireless EV charging, EzFill mobile fuel delivery and a utility operating system. He also founded the Farkas Group, a private investment firm.
interesting_fact: NextNRG grew out of problems he hit building Blink's charging network: interconnection delays, insufficient utility capacity and no unified way for customers to manage their energy.
deep_cut_fact: A Miami resident for about 30 years, he told Refresh Miami (2022): 'People used to ask me if I was a crackpot, and now they think I'm a prophet,' and argued Miami's sun should let it reach net zero faster than other cities.
notes: info@ is NextNRG's general company inbox (no dedicated press/IR email on site; IR site investors.nextnrg.com). Strong fit for energy/microgrid podcast. Exact CEO vs exec chair title varies by source.

name: Miao Liansheng
current_role: Founder and former chairman/CEO of Yingli Green Energy (Baoding); no current role confirmed after the 2020-21 court restructuring
profile: Miao Liansheng (苗连生), from Hebei, left the military, ran a cosmetics trading business in Baoding, and in 1998 founded Yingli, which became one of the world's largest solar module makers and listed on the NYSE in 2007. Heavy debts led to a 2020-21 court restructuring in which the Baoding government became the largest shareholder; his role since then is not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Under Miao, Yingli became the first Chinese company to sponsor the FIFA World Cup (2010, renewed for Brazil 2014), and by 2013 it was described as the world's largest PV module maker.
deep_cut_fact: Before solar he was in the military, then ran the 'Yingli' cosmetics trading company in Baoding. The solar business took the same Yingli name when it was founded in 1998.
notes: Yingli went through court restructuring in 2020-21 and is now controlled by Baoding state investors, so Yingli company channels are probably not a route to him.
