profile: Xie Xiaomei (谢小梅) and her husband, chairman/GM Xu Huan (徐缓), are the controlling shareholders and acting-in-concert actual controllers of Bomin Electronics, a maker of high-precision PCBs (HDI, high-frequency/high-speed, flex) and ceramic substrates. She held ~6.2% of the company in 2026 and was re-elected to the sixth board in October 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2024-25 she and Xu Huan led a share-buying plan alongside Bomin's executives, buying RMB 17.5m+ of stock to signal confidence in the company's long-term value.
notes: Low public profile; husband Xu Huan is the public face. Route via the board office (董事会办公室, BM@bominelec.com). Board composition confirmed in the Oct 2026 board resolution (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-10-30/1225644929.PDF). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Yang Xiang
current_role: Shareholder and concerted party of the controlling Yang family of Juli Sling Co. (SZSE: 002342), Baoding, Hebei
profile: The Chinese name on file, 姚香 (Yao Xiang), matches the wife of Yang Jianzhong, one of the controlling Yang siblings of Juli Sling (巨力索具), China's leading maker of slings and rigging for lifting, construction and energy projects, based in Xushui, Baoding. She holds shares directly and acts in concert with the family; Hurun listed the couple's wealth in 2015.
interesting_fact: Juli Sling describes itself as the leader of China's rigging industry, running a national-level enterprise technology center and the Hebei provincial sling and rigging engineering innovation center, with 247 valid patents as of 2021.
notes: Romanization 'Yang Xiang' looks wrong: the name is 姚香 (Yao Xiang), spouse of Yang Jianzhong per Juli's 2021 annual report, hence identity 'uncertain'. Not an operating executive; no public profile. IR emails are the board secretary and securities rep from the 2021 report (may be out of date). Juli came under a CSRC investigation in May 2026 (https://stock.10jqka.com.cn/20260519/c676796665.shtml).

name: Guo Jun
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2015) as owner of 辰祥投资 (Chenxiang Investment), Shanghai, solar; probably linked to Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center, an investor in GCL System Integration (unverified)
profile: Hurun's 2015 list gives Guo Jun (郭军) as owner of Shanghai-based 辰祥投资 (solar equipment). The likely vehicle, Shanghai Chenxiang Investment Center (LP), was one of nine investors in the 2014 bankruptcy restructuring of Chaori Solar. That left it with 300m shares (11.89%) of the renamed GCL System Integration (002506.SZ), the second-largest holding. No document found names Guo Jun as its partner.
interesting_fact: In 2014 Shanghai Chenxiang took about 11.9% of bankrupt solar maker Chaori in its court-led restructuring, which GCL led. This was China's first onshore corporate bond default case, and Chaori became GCL System Integration.
notes: The link to Chenxiang is inferred from the Hurun API (2015: 辰祥投资, Shanghai, 太阳能设备). The GCL SI restructuring report and 2016 annual report name the vehicle but not its partners. A 2014 China Securities Journal article says it raised capital from RMB169m to RMB469m in Aug 2014. Name is very common. Treat as unconfirmed.

name: Zhang Guoan
current_role: Controlling shareholder, Tong Petrotech / Tongyuan Petroleum Technology Group (通源石油, SZSE ChiNext: 300164), Xi'an
profile: Zhang Guoan (张国桉) is the controlling shareholder of Xi'an-based Tongyuan Petroleum (Tong Oil Tools), an oilfield-services firm founded in 1995 specialising in perforation technology, with fracturing, drilling/completion, coalbed-methane and enhanced-recovery services. It was among the first oilfield-services companies listed on ChiNext (2011). Day-to-day leadership is with chairman Ren Yanzhong.
interesting_fact: Tongyuan was one of the first oilfield-services companies to list on Shenzhen's ChiNext board in 2011 and positions itself as China's perforation-technology leader.
notes: Hurun-listed only in 2015 (~$310M). Confirmed as controlling shareholder in a May 2025 exchange filing (cninfo). No personal bio, interviews or published company IR email retrieved (company site unreachable); IR contact should be in Tongyuan's annual report on cninfo.com.cn. Low public profile.

name: Ding Yuxin
current_role: None public; former chairwoman of Beijing Boyou (Broad-union) Investment Management; sentenced in Dec 2014 to 20 years in prison
profile: Ding Yuxin (also Ding Shumiao), a Shanxi businesswoman, made her fortune in coal transportation and hotels and chaired Beijing Boyou Investment Management (Broad-union). In Dec 2014 a Beijing court sentenced her to 20 years and a 2.5bn yuan fine for bribery and illegal business tied to railway contracts under ex-minister Liu Zhijun.
interesting_fact: According to Caixin, she built her fortune in the coal transportation business before moving into hotels and investment management.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: she was convicted in the Liu Zhijun railway graft case (20-year sentence, Dec 2014) and is presumably still in prison. Listed only on Hurun China 2010. Recommend dropping from the guest list.

name: Yan Tangfeng
current_role: President, Sinolion Holdings Pte Ltd (Singapore investment firm); independent director, China Sunsine Chemical Holdings (SGX), appointed 2019
profile: Singapore-based financier (b. ~1970, Shandong). He was the ultimate controlling shareholder (about 60%, through BVI vehicle Aceplus) and non-executive chairman of Shengli Oil & Gas Pipe Holdings (HKEX:1080), a maker of spiral-welded oil and gas line pipe that listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2009. He now runs the investment firm Sinolion and sits on the board of an SGX-listed rubber-chemicals maker.
interesting_fact: In 2009, the year his pipe company listed in Hong Kong, it reported revenue of about RMB3.0bn, nearly triple the RMB1.07bn of 2008, and profit of RMB336m.
deep_cut_fact: He started out in academia, not business. After graduating in engineering from Shandong University of Technology in 1994, he worked there until 2003, including as Communist Youth League committee secretary. He then moved to Singapore's ICH Capital as a VP and rose to senior VP of investments.
notes: Identity confirmed via HKEX filings (2009 annual report: 閆唐鋒, non-exec chairman and 60.21% holder via Aceplus) and a 2019 SGX announcement that cites his Shengli chairmanship. He lives in Singapore. He is no longer on Shengli's board; its 2025 report names Wei Jun as chairman. No published personal contact was found. Possible routes are Sinolion Holdings (Singapore) or the China Sunsine company secretary. SGX bio: https://links.sgx.com/1.0.0/corporate-announcements/X0NGZVPH1N35T92M/f9db018c1a9524b7f6b46655c40a5b2ed4a7588d6d7e4e0d56f3b17f

name: Ma Xiaocui
profile: Listed by Hurun China (2016) jointly with Li Shifa as a source of wealth in China Logistics Property Holdings (中国物流资产, 1589.HK), the warehouse/logistics-park developer Li founded in 2000 (Shanghai Yupei group). No public source found describing Ma Xiaocui's role or relationship to Li or the company.
interesting_fact: China Logistics Property ran a network of logistics parks across 38 locations; in 2021 JD Logistics agreed to buy most of Li Shifa's stake and bid for more shares.
notes: Could not verify who Ma Xiaocui is (Chinese and English searches return nothing linking her to the company; Li Shifa's 2016 HKEX disclosure lists no spousal interest). The Hurun-listed wealth relates to the Li Shifa/Yupei stake. Recommend skipping or approaching via Li Shifa / Yupei group instead.

name: Liu Zhixiong
current_role: Founder and Chairman, 3NOD Group (Shenzhen; audio and consumer electronics)
profile: Liu Zhixiong (刘志雄), from Chaozhou, Guangdong, left school at 17 and came to Shenzhen in 1989. He worked his way up in mould factories, then in 1995 founded a mould-processing shop that became 3NOD, a maker of multimedia speakers and audio equipment. At one point 3NOD produced roughly a tenth of the world's PC speakers. He still chairs the group.
interesting_fact: On 17 August 2007, 3NOD listed on the Korea Exchange. It was reported as the first foreign (and first Chinese) company to list on the Korean market, and Liu was named a 2007 Korean securities market figure of the year.
deep_cut_fact: His first job in Shenzhen came from his calligraphy: neat handwriting got him a clerical post at a Japanese-Hong Kong joint venture. He then trained as an unpaid apprentice in a mould workshop and rose to manager before founding Xunhongda (迅鸿达), the predecessor of 3NOD, in August 1995.
notes: Founded the Shenzhen alumni association of Cheung Kong Graduate School of Business (CKGSB). The company site 3nod.com.cn returned an error when I checked, and I found no published press email. 36Kr lists a different legal representative (Liu Zhijian) for the operating entity, but the chairman role is confirmed (https://uk.marketscreener.com/insider/ZHIXIONG-LIU-A0ICG9/).

name: Han Fang
current_role: Chairman and actual controller, Nacity Property Service Group (南都物业, 603506.SH), Hangzhou
profile: Han Fang (韩芳, b. 1971) joined Zhejiang Nandu Real Estate in 1993 and rose to group vice president. She took over its property-management arm, turned it profitable, and in 2018 made Nacity the first property-services company listed on China's A-share market. She controls about 57% of Nacity and is pushing into smart services and robotics ('Nacity Robotics').
interesting_fact: Under her, Nacity became mainland China's first A-share-listed property-management company. She started at Nandu Real Estate as an ordinary employee and worked up to running the business.
deep_cut_fact: She was in the first graduating class of the Hong Kong Polytechnic University's International Real Estate (IRE) master's programme. She chairs the Zhejiang University-PolyU joint centre alumni association, and her personal motto is 'think carefully, discern clearly; move steadily, go far' (慎思明辨，行稳致远).
notes: Not to be confused with Seazen's 新城悦服务 (a similar English name; its chairman is Qi Xiaoming). She was named a Zhejiang Women Entrepreneur of the Year (12th edition). Best route is Nacity investor relations.

name: Lu Hualiang
current_role: Director and Deputy General Manager, Hangzhou Onechance Tech Corp. (壹网壹创, SZSE: 300792), per insider-data listings (since Feb 2016)
profile: Lu Hualiang (卢华亮) is listed as a director and deputy GM of Hangzhou Onechance Tech Corp., a Hangzhou e-commerce services firm founded in 2012 and controlled by chairman Lin Zhenyu. Onechance runs Tmall and other online stores for consumer brands. It listed on ChiNext in 2019, and Hurun (2020) put his stake at about US$310m.
interesting_fact: Onechance is an outsourced 'TP' (Tmall partner) operator. It runs the whole online chain for brands such as P&G, Pechoin (百雀羚), Elizabeth Arden, Shiseido and Amorepacific, from store design and big-data marketing to customer service and warehousing.
notes: Identity is only partly confirmed: insider aggregators (MarketScreener) list 'Hua Liang Lu' as director and deputy GM of Onechance, and his current board status was not verified in recent filings. He has no public profile. Contact him through the board secretary (Gao Fan) at the company IR email.

name: Pan Yejiang
current_role: Chairman and President, VATTI Corporation (SZSE: 002035)
profile: Pan Yejiang (b. 1977, master's degree) is the actual controller of VATTI, the Zhongshan, Guangdong kitchen-appliance maker (range hoods, gas hobs, water heaters). Formerly chairman/GM of Guangdong Baide Group, he has chaired VATTI since 2015 and runs it as chairman and president, holding ~87m shares directly.
interesting_fact: As official sponsor of France's team, VATTI promised full refunds on 'champion' packages bought June 1-July 3, 2018 if France won the World Cup; France did, costing an estimated RMB 79m (~$12m), which the company said was within its marketing budget.
deep_cut_fact: Before taking VATTI's chair he ran Guangdong Baide Group as chairman and general manager; he also chairs the investment firm Guangdong Deqian Investment Management.
notes: IR emails are the board secretary and securities representative contacts listed in VATTI's 2025 annual report summary. Wealth shared with Pan Quanzhi (relative). Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Ren Rui
current_role: Co-founder and major shareholder (~2.4%, end-2024) of Guangzhou Shiyuan Electronic Technology (CVTE, SZSE: 002841); formerly chairman of its supervisory board
profile: Ren Rui (任锐, b. 1977) is one of CVTE's five original founders and an engineer by background. He was chief engineer of the TV products division and chaired CVTE's supervisory board from 2011; CVTE (Seewo, MAXHUB brands) listed in Shenzhen in 2017. He no longer appears among current officers but remains a top-10 shareholder.
interesting_fact: CVTE began in Dec 2005 when five people, Ren Rui among them, each put in RMB 200,000 to form a company with RMB 1m registered capital; it is now a leading maker of LCD TV controller boards and interactive flat panels.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding CVTE he worked as an engineer at Amoi (Xiaxin Electronics), Guangzhou Lehua Electronics and Guangzhou Chixun, then joined CVTE at its founding as deputy chief engineer of the TV products division.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal media/social accounts found. Only route is via CVTE board office (shiyuan@cvte.com). Not to be confused with other people named Ren Rui.

name: Ye Dalin
current_role: Chairman and General Manager, Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering Co., Ltd. (SZSE ChiNext: 300813)
profile: Ye Dalin (叶大林, b. 1960) founded Hangzhou-based Tailin Bioengineering, which makes sterility-testing, microbial-detection, filtration and isolator equipment for pharma and biotech labs. He and his wife Ni Weiju are the controlling shareholders (~57%), and the company listed on ChiNext in 2020. In 2026 Tailin was pursuing a convertible-bond issue to fund high-performance filter and functional-membrane production.
interesting_fact: Tailin's core products are sterility-test pumps and microbial-limit testers used by drug makers, and its 2026 fundraising targets industrialising high-performance filters and functional membranes.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 13 years as a lab technician: at Zhejiang Hospital (1981-88) and the Hangzhou Central Blood Station (1988-94), then ran the Zhejiang Pan'an Kaixuan microporous filter factory (1994-99) before founding Hangzhou Tailin Industrial in 1999.
notes: Low media profile; best route is the company board-secretary office. Wealth shared with wife Ni Weiju.

name: Ni Weiju
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with husband Ye Dalin), Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering Co. (300813.SZ)
profile: Ni Weiju (倪卫菊) and her husband Ye Dalin are the controlling shareholders and actual controllers of Hangzhou-based Zhejiang Tailin Bioengineering, a Shenzhen ChiNext-listed maker of microbial testing, organic-matter analysis and contamination-control instruments for pharma labs. The couple control ~57% of the company; in 2025 Ye transferred a ~10% block to Ni (she now holds ~15%).
interesting_fact: In June 2025 Ye Dalin transferred 12.1m Tailin shares (~10% of the company) to Ni Weiju as an internal spousal adjustment, leaving their combined ~57% control unchanged.
notes: Low public profile; no executive title confirmed for her. Emails are the board-secretary / securities-affairs rep contacts published in Tailin's 2024 interim report (verify against latest report). Husband Ye Dalin is the public face.

name: Yin Fengshan
current_role: Chairman and controlling shareholder, Jiangsu Fengshan Group Co., Ltd. (SSE: 603810)
profile: Yin Fengshan (b. 1947) built Jiangsu Fengshan Group, a pesticide and agrochemical maker in Dafeng, Yancheng, from a county agrochemical plant he ran from 1988 into a Shanghai-listed company. He remains chairman and controlling shareholder; his daughter Yin Ping (co-listed on Hurun) is president and vice chair.
interesting_fact: Fengshan's predecessor was Dafeng County Agrochemical Plant No. 2, which Yin ran as factory director from 1988-1993 before restructuring it into Yancheng Fengshan Pesticide Co. and later a listed group.
deep_cut_fact: Before pesticides, Yin was deputy director of the Changcheng Electrical Equipment Factory in Caomiao Township, Dafeng County (1986-88); he is also a vice president of the China Pesticide Industry Association.
notes: Still chairing board meetings in 2025 per SSE filing (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2025-04-29/1223386457.PDF). Bio source is user-submitted (maigoo); cross-check with prospectus. Best route: company board secretary via SSE disclosures.

name: Zhou Yuqing
profile: Listed as deriving wealth from 'Top Alliance' (China). English-language searches did not surface a company or executive profile that could be confidently matched to this name, so no further details are given.
notes: Could not confirm identity; 'Top Alliance' is likely a translated name of a Chinese private group. Needs Chinese-language research (Hurun list entry in Chinese) before any outreach.

name: Vasyl Khmelnytsky
current_role: Founder, UFuture investment holding (Kyiv/Brussels) and K.FUND foundation
profile: Ukrainian entrepreneur and former MP (1998-2002, 2006-2014). Built wealth in real estate, infrastructure and steel (sold a Zaporizhstal stake in 2006 for ~$400m), then founded UFuture (2017), which holds UDP, Kyiv's Sikorsky (Zhuliany) airport, IT firms and stakes in Biopharma and UDP Renewables, plus the UNIT.City innovation park.
interesting_fact: He set out to build a 'Silicon Valley match' in Ukraine via UNIT.City in Kyiv; UFuture also backs UDP Renewables (wind/solar) and his K.FUND has run humanitarian aid since the 2022 invasion.
deep_cut_fact: Born 1966 in Bayanaul, Kazakhstan, to a tractor driver and a house-painter, he trained as a fitter-welder (vocational school in Vatutine, 1984) and worked as a gas-electric welder and foreman in Leningrad before business; he earned a law degree from Kyiv's Shevchenko University in 2002.
notes: Energy angle: UDP Renewables (wind/solar) and industrial parks. UN Global Compact ambassador (2021). Speaks at Kyiv International Economic Forum; best route is via UFuture/K.FUND press office.

name: Lady Smith
current_role: Co-founder figure behind the Paul Smith fashion label; wife of Sir Paul Smith
profile: Pauline, Lady Smith (née Denyer) is the wife of designer Sir Paul Smith and shares his Rich List entry (fashion). A Royal College of Art-trained fashion designer, she helped him launch his first Nottingham shop in 1970, which grew into a brand with ~130 stores in 60+ countries. Very low public profile.
interesting_fact: She was a Royal College of Art-trained fashion designer teaching at a Nottingham art school when she met Paul Smith; she married him when he was 21.
deep_cut_fact: Before the Paul Smith label existed, her RCA fashion training contributed to many of the pieces sold at the Nottingham boutique Paul managed for six years, and Paul has credited her with teaching him garment construction.
notes: Very private; no personal channels. Email is for Paul Smith's Foundation (Sir Paul's archive charity, Nottingham), the closest published route. Sources disagree on wedding date (1967 per Wikipedia vs 2000 per other profiles), so avoid citing it. No death reported, but status not confirmed.

name: Todd J. Kantor
current_role: Founder, Portfolio Manager and Managing Member, Encompass Capital Advisors LLC; Director of T1 Energy Inc. (NYSE: TE) since April 2024
profile: New York hedge-fund manager who launched Encompass Capital Advisors in 2012, an energy-focused fund investing across oil and gas, renewables and battery technology. Encompass is a 10%+ holder of T1 Energy (formerly FREYR Battery), the US solar-module and cell manufacturer, and Kantor sits on its board.
interesting_fact: Before starting Encompass he was a portfolio manager on Citadel's PioneerPath platform (2008-2012) and a senior analyst at Touradji Capital, a commodities-focused fund.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a senior research analyst and equity trader at Solstice Equity Management (2002-2005) after earning a BBA in finance from Emory University's Goizueta Business School.
notes: Low media profile; best route is Encompass's published office email. T1 Energy press releases also list an investor contact (EVP IR) and media contact (EVP Strategic Communications) - see ir.t1energy.com releases. Background from proxy-derived profile (fintool) and SEC 13D filings.

name: Robert Madison Murphy
current_role: Chairman, Murphy USA Inc. (NYSE: MUSA); Director, Murphy Oil Corp. (NYSE: MUR); President, The Murphy Foundation (El Dorado, Ark.)
profile: R. Madison Murphy is a scion of the El Dorado, Arkansas oil family; his father Charles H. Murphy Jr. built Murphy Oil. He is a longtime Murphy Oil director and has chaired fuel retailer Murphy USA since its 2013 spin-off. He also runs The Murphy Foundation and owns The Sumac Company, Arc Vineyards and Presqu'ile Winery.
interesting_fact: He has served as chairman of the Arkansas Highway Commission. He also bought ~$1.8M of Murphy USA stock in August 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His family's Santa Maria Valley (California) winery, Presqu'ile, is named after the Murphy family's longtime Gulf Coast gathering spot at Henderson Point near Pass Christian, Mississippi. 'Presqu'ile' is a Creole word meaning 'almost an island'.
notes: Still listed as Murphy USA Chairman in the 2026 proxy (https://s22.q4cdn.com/506259022/files/doc_financials/2025/ar/2026-Proxy-Statement.pdf). The IR email belongs to Murphy USA's VP of Investor Relations (company-published). Energy angle: Murphy Oil (E&P) plus Murphy USA (fuel retail).

name: Han Junliang
current_role: Unknown; former founder, chairman and president of Sinovel Wind Group (华锐风电) - left management in 2012-13
profile: Han Junliang (韩俊良) was deputy GM of a Dalian Heavy Industry equipment unit when he moved into wind power in 2004, licensing Fuhrländer's 1.5 MW turbine design and founding Sinovel (registered Feb 2006). Sinovel briefly became China's largest and the world's No.2 turbine maker and listed in Shanghai in 2011. He stepped down as president in 2012 and chairman in 2013; his current activity is not public.
interesting_fact: Sinovel went from incorporation in 2006 to the world's second-largest wind turbine maker in about four years, largely by localising a single licensed 1.5 MW German design at enormous scale.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Sinovel he was deputy general manager of Dalian Heavy Industry's mechanical & electrical equipment complete-sets company; his first move into wind (2004) was securing a production licence for Fuhrländer's FL1500 turbine series.
notes: Out of public life since ~2013. Sensitive history: CSRC penalised Sinovel and 15 individuals including Han over overstated 2011 revenue (https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c101928/c1042913/content.shtml); Sinovel (the company, not Han personally) was convicted in the US in 2018 over AMSC trade secrets. No public contact route found; likely unsuitable/unreachable.

name: Qu Naijie
current_role: Founder, Haichang Group / Haichang Ocean Park Holdings (HK: 2255); chairman and CEO as of March 2023 — current role unclear after Xiangyuan Holding became the largest shareholder
profile: Dalian entrepreneur who started in oil trading and marine shipping in 1992, set up Dalian Haichang Group in 1998, and from 1999 moved into ocean theme parks, building 11+ cultural-tourism projects across China (Dalian, Shanghai, Sanya, Zhengzhou etc.). Haichang Ocean Park listed in Hong Kong; a later share placement handed control (~38.6%) to Xiangyuan Holding.
interesting_fact: His fortune began in petrochemical trading and shipping in the early 1990s; property development then funded his theme parks, a model the company later moved away from in favour of 'asset-light' IP deals such as Ultraman-themed pavilions.
deep_cut_fact: In 2002 he led the construction of the Polar Aquarium at Dalian Laohutan Ocean Park, China's first polar aquarium, which became a national 5A attraction in 2007; in 2015 he received China's 'Feima Award' for outstanding contribution to tourism.
notes: Last on Hurun in 2019; Haichang has faced heavy debt and a control change, and press reports cite legal issues in France — handle with care. Alive status not verified by a recent source (aged 62 in the 2022 annual report). Weak fit for energy topic today (theme parks).

name: Wu Jialing
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2009-2012) with her sister Wu Jie (吴洁) under Yango/Yangguangcheng (阳光城), Fuzhou; role unverified
profile: Hurun lists Wu Jialing (吴家玲, b. 1968, Fujian) jointly with her sister Wu Jie, the co-founder of Fujian Yango Group, as holders of Yango (阳光城; real estate and power). In 2006 Wu Jie held 35.83% of Yango Group and was its chairman. No filing naming Wu Jialing was found.
notes: The sister relationship (姐妹) and birth year come from the Hurun rich-list API (2010 entry). Wu Jie's 35.83% stake is from a 2006 SZSE filing (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk01/finalpage/2006-04-14/05bfde3b-9248-4ad1-9961-bbd501219bb5.PDF), which does not mention Wu Jialing. Yango's listed arm was delisted after the property crisis. Not recommended for outreach.

name: Xu Ling
current_role: Actual controller of Geo-Jade Petroleum (洲际油气, Shanghai 600759) via Guangxi Zhenghe Industrial Group; also controls Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum B.V. (中科荷兰石油)
profile: Xu Ling (许玲, also written HUI LING in filings) indirectly owns 100% of Guangxi Zhenghe Industrial Group, controlling shareholder of Shanghai-listed Geo-Jade Petroleum, an oil producer with upstream assets in Central Asia. She also indirectly holds 70.04% of Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum ('Zhongke'), controlling holder of Sozak Oil & Gas LLP.
interesting_fact: Her 'Zhongke' vehicle, Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum B.V., is the controlling shareholder of Sozak Oil & Gas LLP, in which Geo-Jade was set to hold an indirect 17.859% stake after a 2025 share-for-debt swap between her two companies.
notes: Identity match via Hurun's 'Zhongke' + oil exploitation/trading = Sino-Science Netherlands Petroleum, which Geo-Jade filings say she controls. Very private, no interviews found. Heads-up: Geo-Jade got an adverse internal-control audit opinion for 2025, was renamed 'ST Zhouji' from April 2026, and has had exchange inquiries about guarantees. Off Hurun since 2019.

name: Zhong Baisheng
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Tempus Group / Tempus Global Business Service (腾邦国际, formerly SZSE: 300178), Shenzhen
profile: Zhong Baisheng (钟百胜) founded Shenzhen-based Tempus (腾邦), an air-ticketing and business-travel services group that listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext as 腾邦国际 and expanded into travel, logistics and supply-chain finance. After a 2019-20 debt crisis the listed company was delisted in June 2022; his current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Control of 腾邦国际 changed hands three times within a year around 2019-20, ultimately reverting to founder Zhong Baisheng.
notes: Hurun listing (2015-17) is stale: the listed company collapsed under debt, faced litigation and was delisted (摘牌 22 Jun 2022). No current published contact found. Sensitive subject; likely a poor podcast target.

name: Wu Mingting
current_role: Chairman (and founder/initiator), Ruiqi Holding Co. / KEN power tools (SZ ChiNext: 300126), Shanghai
profile: Born in 1966, Wu co-founded Shanghai-based Ken (Ruiqi) in 2000 to make professional-grade electric power tools for industry, shipbuilding, auto, aerospace and construction. He took it public on ChiNext and remains chairman (signing its April 2026 articles as chairman).
interesting_fact: KEN is one of the few Chinese brands positioned in high-end professional power tools, a field long dominated by Bosch, Makita and Hilti; the company offers 20+ product series and 100+ specifications for industrial and infrastructure users.
deep_cut_fact: A senior economist who studied at Shanghai Jiao Tong University and CEIBS's general-manager program, he has received the 'Shanghai Science & Technology Entrepreneur Innovation Award' and was named an 'Outstanding Chinese Private Science & Technology Entrepreneur'.
notes: Chairman role confirmed by company articles signed Apr 2026 (https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN202604221821456686_1.pdf). Hurun lists him in 'energy' focus but business is power tools - limited fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Bio details from a third-party brand site (CNPP).

name: Ruan Renyi
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2015-2016 (with Ruan Shouguo) with wealth from a rail-transit-systems business named 'Dinghan'. I could not confirm which company this is. Beijing Dinghan Technology (SZSE: 300011) is controlled by Gu Qingwei, and no Ruan family member appears among its main shareholders.
notes: Identity unresolved. Do not assume a link to Beijing Dinghan Technology (shareholders per https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1818824729022593). Needs Chinese corporate-registry research on 阮仁义 before any outreach.

name: Ruan Shouguo
current_role: Founder/former owner of Anhui Chaohu Haixing Cable Group; shareholder in Beijing Dinghan Technology (300011.SZ) since 2014 (current role not confirmed)
profile: Ruan Shouguo (阮寿国) and Ruan Renyi owned 100% of Anhui Chaohu Haixing Cable Group, which makes rail-vehicle and special cables. In 2014 they sold it to Beijing Dinghan Technology, a rail-transit electrical equipment maker, for about 91.6 million new Dinghan shares and also took part in its private placement. Dinghan is now controlled by Guangzhou state capital (Guangzhou Industrial Investment).
interesting_fact: Haixing Cable was folded into Dinghan's rail-transit group and continues as its cable arm (e.g. Wuhu Dinghan, making EU/GB-standard rail-vehicle cables). The 2014 share-swap made the Ruans among Dinghan's largest shareholders.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal web presence found. Hurun wealth is shared with Ruan Renyi. Dinghan founder Gu Qingwei is a different person. Dinghan also sells rail energy-storage and liquid-cooling thermal-management systems, which is the closest energy angle.

name: Xu Zhonggui
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder of Shenzhen SZZT Electronics Co., Ltd. (证通电子, SZSE: 002197); the chairman is her husband, Zeng Shengqiang
profile: Xu Zhonggui (许忠桂, b. 1963) and her husband Zeng Shengqiang control SZZT Electronics. Founded in Shenzhen in 1993, SZZT makes payment and financial self-service hardware (encrypted PIN pads, kiosks) and has expanded into IDC/cloud data-centre services. She has worked at the company since 1997, and it listed in Shenzhen in 2007.
interesting_fact: SZZT's ATM encrypted PIN pad was the first in Asia to win VISA certification. The company also helped write China's national technical specification for PIN-pad systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before she joined SZZT in 1997 she worked at the Ministry of Electronics Industry's Jiannan Machinery Factory (电子工业部建南机器厂), then at Shenzhen Kaifa Technology and Shenzhen Anke High-Tech.

public_contacts.value: ztbank@szzt.com.cn (company email in the 2007 IPO prospectus; may be outdated)

notes: Very private, with no media presence. Her husband Zeng Shengqiang is the public face, so approach through him or the board secretary. SZZT's IDC/data-centre business makes it relevant to the podcast. Her current shareholding was not re-verified.

name: Gao Xueming
current_role: Founder, Chairman and legal representative, Luoyang Northglass Technology Co. (SZSE: 002613)
profile: Gao Xueming (b. 1958), a senior engineer, founded Luoyang Northglass Technology in 1995. The company makes glass deep-processing equipment, notably tempering furnaces, and processed glass, and listed in Shenzhen in 2011. He remains chairman and controlling shareholder, acting in concert with Feng Jinjun and Gao Xuelin.
interesting_fact: Gao is an engineer-founder: he spent 12 years at state-owned Luoyang Glass, rising from technician to engineer, senior engineer and branch-factory head, before starting Northglass in 1995.
deep_cut_fact: Northglass began in 1995 as Luoyang Northglass Technology Co., Ltd., founded by Gao after his 1982-1994 stint at Luoyang Glass Factory, where he ended as a branch-factory director.
notes: Hurun listing (2015-17) is older. Still chairman per the 2025 annual report (April 2026). The IR mailbox is a 126.com address, as published by the company. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jin Minbo
current_role: Unclear; if this is Xu Minbo (徐岷波), he is a co-founder and ~4.6% shareholder of Shenzhen Kingdom Sci-Tech (金证股份, SSE: 600446) who left its board in Nov 2025
profile: No person named 金泯波 could be found linked to Kingdom. The Hurun entry most likely mis-renders Xu Minbo (徐岷波), a Tsinghua industrial-automation graduate who co-founded Kingdom, the Shenzhen financial-IT vendor (securities trading/asset-management systems), in 1998, served as acting president (2018) and director until resigning in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: (If Xu Minbo) Kingdom's FS2.5 core trading system and A8 investment-management platform are used widely by Chinese brokerages and fund managers.
notes: Identity unverified: name 金泯波 does not appear in Kingdom filings; probable Hurun data error for co-founder 徐岷波 (Xu Minbo). Verify before outreach. Contact listed is Kingdom's company email; Xu no longer holds any company role.

name: Wang Yaofang
current_role: Chairman and Party Secretary, Changzhou Qianhong Bio-Pharma (SZSE: 002550); controlling shareholder (~20%)
profile: Wang Yaofang (王耀方, b. 1953), a senior engineer and licensed pharmacist, rose from deputy director of the state-owned Changzhou Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory to lead its restructured successor, Qianhong Bio-Pharma, a heparin API and enzyme-drug maker he took public in Shenzhen in 2011. Qianhong is now pushing original drugs such as QHRD106 and QHRD107 through clinical trials.
interesting_fact: Qianhong is one of China's main exporters of heparin sodium API (made from pig intestinal mucosa) and also sells pancreatic kininogenase; at a May 2026 earnings call Wang said its novel drugs QHRD106 (Phase IIb) and QHRD107 (Phase IIa) were on schedule.
deep_cut_fact: He began at the state-run Changzhou Biochemical Pharmaceutical Factory, rising to deputy factory director, before leading its spin-out Changzhou Biochemical Qianhong Pharmaceutical as chairman and GM; he holds three professional titles: senior engineer, national licensed pharmacist and senior economist.
notes: Since the 2024 annual report the company's legal representative is Wang Ke (acts in concert with Wang Yaofang); confirm current chairman title before outreach. Best route: board secretary office.

name: Lu Sanping
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder (no executive role), Broad-Ocean Motor / Zhongshan Dayang Electric (002249.SZ)
profile: Lu Sanping (鲁三平) is one of the six founding promoters of Zhongshan Broad-Ocean Motor (大洋电机), the Guangdong maker of micro-motors, HVAC motors and EV drive systems chaired by his elder brother Lu Chuping. A passive shareholder holding no company post, he sold down his stake from above 5% in 2016-2018 and held ~1.4% by 2019.
interesting_fact: Broad-Ocean's articles of association list Lu Sanping among the company's six original promoters alongside his brother Lu Chuping, who has chaired the motor maker since 2000.
notes: Very low profile; 2016 filing states he holds no position at the company. Company IR emails (from 2020 interim report) are the only route; brother Lu Chuping is the public face. Not on Hurun since 2016.

name: Chen Haichang
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2015-2016 with wealth from 'Protruly' (electronic equipment), i.e. Shenzhen/Jiangsu Protruly (Baoqianli) vision-tech group, which listed via a 2015 reverse merger. Searches could not confirm Chen Haichang's role; chairmen on record are Zhuang Min (founder), Li Hongding and Peng Lu.
notes: Likely a shareholder in the 2015 Baoqianli/Protruly reverse merger, not an executive; not verified. Jiangsu Protruly was later delisted. Low priority; verify via 2015 restructuring filings before any outreach.

name: Kong Deyong
profile: Listed as deriving wealth from 'WHWH' (China). English-language searches did not identify the company behind the 'WHWH' abbreviation or a profile matching this name, so no further details are given.
notes: Identity unconfirmed; 'WHWH' is an unexplained abbreviation. Needs Chinese-language research before any outreach.

name: Duan Peizhang
current_role: Controlling shareholder and director, Shanghai Longyun Cultural Creation & Technology Group (ST Longyun, 603729.SH)
profile: Duan Peizhang co-founded Longyun, a Shanghai advertising/media-buying company, with Fang Xiaoqin in 2003 and took it public on the Shanghai exchange in 2015. He was chairman and GM 2008-2015 and has sat on the board since 2008; after a June 2026 internal transfer he holds ~30% and is sole actual controller.
interesting_fact: Longyun's business spans TV/media advertising agency, digital marketing and (more recently) liquor sales, and it has tried to expand into film/TV content via Yuheng Pictures.
notes: Low public profile; little biography published. Company is under ST (risk-warning) status since April 2026 and loss-making - avoid as an outreach hook. Reach via company board secretary office (see SSE filings).

name: Meng Xianming
current_role: Controlling shareholder and actual controller, Hengxin Oriental Culture Co., Ltd. (SZSE: 300081; formerly Hengxin Mobile Business)
profile: Meng Xianmin (孟宪民; Hurun romanises as Meng Xianming) built Hengxin Mobile Business, founded in Shijiazhuang in 2001 to sell and service mobile phones and mobile information products, and listed it on ChiNext in May 2010. The company pivoted into culture/VR content, renaming itself Hengxin Shambala Culture in 2017 and later Hengxin Oriental Culture. He still held ~10.3% in 2026.
interesting_fact: Hengxin was one of the early ChiNext listings (2010) and later reinvented itself from mobile retail into digital culture and VR content, acquiring Dongfang Dream Culture Industrial Investment.
notes: Low public profile; no published personal or IR contact verified. The company currently trades with an ST (special treatment) designation and has had board-level disputes, so a sensitive moment for outreach. Pinyin of 孟宪民 is Meng Xianmin; listed names differ by romanisation only.

name: Liu Dongliang
current_role: Director and controlling shareholder (~22.6%), Shanxi Yongdong Chemistry Industry (永东股份, SZSE: 002753)
profile: Founder (b. 1969) of Shanxi Yongdong, a Jishan County, Shanxi producer of carbon black and refined coal-tar products, which he grew from Jishan Yongdong Chemical Co. and took public in Shenzhen in 2015. He was GM and later chairman; his brother Liu Dongjie now chairs the company and Liu remains a director and, with Jin Caihong, actual controller.
interesting_fact: Yongdong runs an integrated coal-tar-to-carbon-black model: it refines coal tar into naphthalene, wash oil and other products, then blends the residue into feedstock oil for carbon black used in tyres.
deep_cut_fact: Outside chemicals, he has also served as general manager of a tea company, Wuzhishan Wuchuang Tea Co. (五指山五创茶业) in Hainan's Wuzhishan tea region.
notes: Input lists co-holder as 'Jing Caihong'; company filings spell it 靳彩红 (Jin Caihong), co-actual controller and director. Low media profile; only one Hurun appearance (2017). Route via securities office mailbox.

name: Jing Caihong
current_role: Co-actual controller and major shareholder, Shanxi Yongdong Chemistry Industry (SZSE: 002753), Jishan, Yuncheng, Shanxi
profile: Jing (Jin) Caihong (靳彩红) and her husband Liu Dongliang are the actual controllers of Shanxi Yongdong Chemistry, a coal-tar processor and carbon-black maker in Shanxi's Jishan county. She remains a top-10 shareholder per the 2025 annual report; the company has been squeezed by weak carbon-black prices.
interesting_fact: Yongdong runs a circular model: it distills coal tar into naphthalene and wash oil, turns the residue into carbon-black feedstock, and burns the carbon-black tail gas to generate power.
notes: Hurun romanises 靳 as 'Jing'; standard pinyin is Jin Caihong. Shared Hurun entry with husband Liu Dongliang. No executive role or public profile found; only route is the company securities office. Alive status inferred from her listing as a shareholder in the April 2026 annual report.

name: Sun Yang
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2019) under Zhongrong Xinda Group (coal/coking, Qingdao); exact role not verified
profile: Appears on the 2019 Hurun China Rich List (~$300m) under Zhongrong Xinda, a Qingdao-headquartered group (formerly Shandong Coking Group, founded 2003) with coking/coal, logistics (Shandong Logistics Group) and financial (Zhongrong Financial Holding) arms. No public biography linking a Sun Yang to the group was found; not the Olympic swimmer.
interesting_fact: Zhongrong Xinda began life as Shandong Coking Group before rebranding and expanding into logistics and financial holdings.
notes: Very common name; identity could not be confirmed against the company in English or Chinese searches. Verify via Hurun 2019 Chinese list and company registry (Qichacha) before outreach.

name: Hrishikesh A Mafatlal
current_role: Chairman and Promoter Director, Mafatlal Industries Ltd; Chairman and Promoter Director, NOCIL Ltd (Arvind Mafatlal Group)
profile: Hrishikesh A. Mafatlal, son of industrialist Arvind Mafatlal, heads the Arvind Mafatlal Group, whose holdings include Mafatlal Industries (textiles, founded 1913) and NOCIL (India's largest rubber-chemicals maker), and historically Navin Fluorine International. He chairs Mafatlal Industries and NOCIL, with his son Priyavrata as MD of Mafatlal Industries.
interesting_fact: He leads one of India's oldest business houses: Mafatlal Industries was incorporated in 1913 in Gujarat, and the group spans textiles, rubber chemicals (NOCIL) and, historically, fluorochemicals (Navin Fluorine).
deep_cut_fact: A 1975 commerce honours graduate of Mumbai's Sydenham College and a 1993 Harvard Business School AMP alumnus, he served 12 years on IIM Ahmedabad's Board of Governors and was vice-chairman of the Cotton Textiles Export Promotion Council (TEXPROCIL).
notes: Navin Fluorine is now chaired by cousin-branch member Vishad P. Mafatlal (Padmanabh Mafatlal Group); Hurun's link to Navin Fluorine reflects older group holdings. The best route is Mafatlal Industries' corporate contact (Mafatlal House, Mumbai). He is also on the board of BAIF (sustainable livelihoods), which could be an angle.

name: Vitaliy Haiduk
current_role: Businessman; co-founder of Industrial Union of Donbas (ISD); former Secretary of Ukraine's National Security and Defense Council (2006-07)
profile: Ukrainian businessman-politician (b. 1957) who co-founded the Industrial Union of Donbas steel group in 1995 with Serhiy Taruta and Oleh Mkrtchian, exiting c. 2009-10. He was Minister of Fuel and Energy (2001-02), Deputy PM (2002-03) and NSDC Secretary (2006-07); Ukrainian media link him to current security-contracting businesses.
interesting_fact: An energy-sector veteran: he was First Deputy Minister then Minister of Fuel and Energy of Ukraine and holds the title 'Honored Power Engineer of the CIS'.
deep_cut_fact: Before politics he ran the Zuyevskaya electromechanical plant (1988-94), and he wrote a PhD on the economics of leasing and co-authored the 2000 book 'Problems and prospects of development of leasing in Ukraine'.
notes: Politically exposed person; 2024-25 Ukrainian media (UNN) carry unproven allegations about his current business links - handle with care. No published personal or office contact found. Alive status inferred from recent media coverage (no death reported).

name: Lagbaja
current_role: Masked Afrobeat musician (stage name of Bisade Ologunde); founder of the Motherland live-music venue, Ikeja, Lagos
profile: Lagbaja is the stage persona of Nigerian saxophonist, singer and percussionist Bisade Ologunde (b. 1960, Lagos), who has performed behind a mask since the early 1990s, blending Afrobeat, highlife, jazz and Yoruba percussion. Debut album 1993; breakthrough 'We Before Me' (2000). His wealth comes from music and live events.
interesting_fact: The name Lagbaja is Yoruba for 'nobody in particular' (a John Doe); the mask is meant to represent the faceless common man in Africa, and he has said several people have played the role.
deep_cut_fact: Before music fame he studied Education/Biology at Obafemi Awolowo University, worked as a Kwara State civil servant, taught himself saxophone, and in March 1997 opened Motherland in Ikeja, modelled on a traditional African village square, for monthly concerts.
notes: The $300M figure comes from Wikidata and looks doubtful for a musician; treat it with caution. His official site (lagbaja.com) is listed as a dead link on Wikipedia, and I found no verified contact. Best route is probably the Motherland venue in Ikeja or his band management. Not an energy or data-center figure.

name: Valeriy Khoroshkovskyi
current_role: Private investor/businessman, based abroad since about 2014 (no confirmed current corporate title)
profile: Kyiv-born (1969) Ukrainian businessman and politician. He made money in metal trading and banking (sold his Ukrsotsbank stake to Victor Pinchuk in 2004), briefly ran Evraz in 2006, and controlled Inter Media Group until selling it to Dmytro Firtash in 2013. He was economy minister, head of the State Customs Service, SBU chief (2010-12), finance minister and First Deputy PM (2012), and has lived outside Ukraine since about 2014.
interesting_fact: In 2005 he bought 61% of Inter, Ukraine's most-watched TV channel, for about $250m and built it into U.A. Inter Media Group before selling to Firtash in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He became Ukraine's Minister of Economy and European Integration in December 2002 at about 33, after one term (1998-2002) as a Verkhovna Rada deputy.
notes: Politically sensitive figure (former SBU head under Yanukovych). Ukrainian media report that 2025 court orders froze some of his Ukrainian assets in a tax case. Lives abroad; no published contact channel found. Not a natural podcast guest; journalist discretion advised.

name: Oleksiy Martynov
current_role: Co-owner of Privat Group (Ukraine) and private investor; no current executive title published
profile: Oleksiy Martynov (b. 1966, Liudinovo, Russia) is a Dnipro-based businessman and long-time partner of Ihor Kolomoisky and Hennadiy Bogolyubov in Privat Group. He co-founded PrivatBank in 1992 and sat on its supervisory board from 2000 until the bank was nationalised. He has also run Solm Ltd, the group's ferroalloy business. NV ranked him 12th-richest in Ukraine in 2019 (about US$602m).
interesting_fact: He was one of the four co-founders of PrivatBank (1992), which became Ukraine's largest bank, after first co-founding the trading firm Sentoza with Kolomoisky and Bogolyubov in 1991.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer in automatic control systems (Dnipropetrovsk University, 1989). His first business job was at the late-Soviet 'Fianit' cooperative, before Sentoza and PrivatBank.
notes: Extremely private, with no website, social accounts or press office. Privat Group/PrivatBank shareholders are under heavy legal and political scrutiny in Ukraine since the 2016 nationalisation, which makes him a sensitive and probably unreachable guest. Alive status is inferred (no death reported in the 2021+ sources).

name: Marcos Marcelo Mindlin
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Pampa Energía (NYSE: PAM); co-founder of Grupo EMES; 2026 Chair of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance
profile: Argentine economist who co-founded investment firm Grupo EMES in 1989 and was IRSA's vice-chairman and CFO (1990-2003). He founded Pampa Energía in 2005: a top Vaca Muerta shale producer, Argentina's largest independent power producer, and co-controller of Transener and TGS. In 2025 EMES took over Intercement/Loma Negra.
interesting_fact: In 2026 he was appointed Chairman of the International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA), an intergovernmental body: an unusual role for a sitting energy CEO. He has received EY's CEO of the Year (2017) and the 2025 Apertura/PwC CEO Achievement Award.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2016 he has been president of the Holocaust Museum of Argentina (Buenos Aires), overseeing a US$7M full renovation of the building and exhibitions. His Pampa Energía Foundation has put about US$30M into education and employability over two decades.
notes: Gives long-form interviews to Argentine business press (e.g. El Cronista on Pampa's 20 years and the Loma Negra deal), so he is approachable on energy and Vaca Muerta topics. Best route is Pampa IR or corporate communications. 'Marcos Marcelo' is his formal SEC name; he goes by Marcelo Mindlin.

name: Talal Jassim Al-Bahar
current_role: Vice Chairman & CEO, Kuwait Real Estate Co. (AQARAT); Chairman & Group CEO, IFA Hotels & Resorts; Chairman, Arzan Financial Group; Independent Director, Miami International Holdings (MIAX)
profile: Kuwaiti investor and real-estate/hospitality executive with a Loyola Marymount business degree. He led International Financial Advisors and Kuwait Invest Holding, now runs AQARAT and IFA Hotels & Resorts, chairs Arzan Financial Group, and has long sat on the board of US options-exchange operator MIAX, where his stake is worth ~$300m.
interesting_fact: In January 2025 AQARAT and IFA Hotels & Resorts launched the $953m Al Tay Hills residential project in Sharjah, which reportedly sold about $572m in its first week; Forbes Middle East ranked him No. 42 among the region's most impactful real-estate leaders of 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He is credited as the driving force behind IFA Hotels & Resorts' global expansion, which tripled in size under him, and he is a certified Six Sigma Development Champion.
notes: The MIAX IR contact goes to a company where he is only a director. A more direct route is likely via AQARAT, Arzan or IFA Hotels & Resorts corporate offices in Kuwait. He also sits on the Boursa Kuwait board.

name: Victor Perlroth
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Kodiak Sciences Inc. (Nasdaq: KOD), Palo Alto
profile: Victor Perlroth, M.D. (Princeton A.B. molecular biology; Stanford M.D./M.B.A.) co-founded Kodiak Sciences in 2009 and leads it as chairman and CEO, developing long-acting retinal drugs for wet AMD and diabetic eye disease. He earlier co-founded Avidia, sold to Amgen for $450m, then worked in life-sciences venture capital.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Kodiak said its tarcocimab (Zenkuda) and tabirafusp-ted met primary endpoints in the pivotal DAYBREAK wet-AMD trial, with most Zenkuda patients on a 24-week dosing interval.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he was chief operating officer of Guzik Technical Enterprises, a maker of test equipment for the hard-disk-drive industry; he graduated summa cum laude from Princeton in molecular biology.
notes: Wealth is mostly KOD stock (volatile biotech). Kodiak IR site (ir.kodiak.com) blocks automated fetches, so IR/media contacts could not be read; company general email info@kodiak.com is published in the site footer.

name: Hugh Osmond
current_role: Founder, Sun Capital Partners (2001) and Osmond Capital (2017); Non-Executive Director, Coppa Collective plc (formerly Various Eateries, AIM)
profile: Hugh Osmond (b. 1962), an Oxford-educated former medic, co-led the 1993 PizzaExpress flotation with Luke Johnson, founded pub group Punch Taverns in 1997 and co-founded closed-life-fund consolidator Pearl Group (bought from Henderson for GBP1.1bn in 2005). He now invests via Sun Capital and Osmond Capital, bought Capital Physio in 2019, and founded Coppa Club operator Various Eateries in 2014.
interesting_fact: Read medicine at Merton College, Oxford, but went into hospitality; he spotted in early-1990s America how many places served a decent meal for $5-10, which convinced him and Luke Johnson that PizzaExpress could become a national chain.
deep_cut_fact: He started running clubs and bars while at university, ran clubs in America after graduating in 1983, and admits to a brief stint trying to run a computer company ('I don't know what possessed me') before working at a small Madrid investment bank.

public_contacts.value: Alma PR (Coppa Collective's PR adviser), 71-73 Carter Lane, London EC4V 5EQ

notes: Significant Conservative Party donor. No personal social accounts found; best route is via Coppa Collective's PR (Alma PR) or Osmond Capital.

name: Sir John Ritblat
current_role: Honorary President, The British Land Company PLC (former chairman & CEO)
profile: Sir John Ritblat (b. 1935, Hampstead) bought British Land from Jim Slater in 1970 for £1m and built it into one of the UK's largest REITs, chairing it until 2006. Now 91, he is honorary president of British Land and has chaired Colliers CRE and the advisory board of Delancey, the property investor founded by his son Jamie.
interesting_fact: He acquired British Land from financier Jim Slater in 1970 for just £1m and ran it for 36 years before retiring as chairman in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: The British Library's permanent treasures gallery (Magna Carta, Lindisfarne Gospels, Shakespeare First Folio) is the Sir John Ritblat Gallery, named for him after he gave £1m toward its display cases; he is also honorary president of the British Ski and Snowboard Federation.
notes: Aged 91, largely retired; no personal published contacts found. Possible indirect routes: British Land corporate/press office or Delancey (son's firm), but neither is his personal office. Wikipedia cites the BSSF role without a source; gallery fact is well documented.

name: Joseph V. Topper Jr.
current_role: Chairman, CrossAmerica Partners LP (NYSE: CAPL); CEO, Dunne Manning Holdings (Topper Group); director, CoastalSouth Bancshares
profile: Allentown, PA fuel-distribution entrepreneur who bought his family's retail fuel business in 1987 and founded what became Lehigh Gas Corp., later taken public as Lehigh Gas Partners/CrossAmerica Partners. He was CAPL's CEO 2012-15, retook control via the Topper Group in 2019 and is chairman; he also runs the Dunne Manning real-estate/investing group.
interesting_fact: A 1977 Villanova accounting graduate (and former CPA), he chaired Villanova University's Board of Trustees from 2017 to 2020 after serving as trustee since 2010.
deep_cut_fact: His fuel empire started with his family's gas business on MacArthur Road in Whitehall Township, PA, which he bought in 1987; five years later he started the company that became Lehigh Gas Corp. (now Dunne Manning Inc.).
notes: Energy/fuel-retail angle fits the podcast. Bio lists him on board of Patriot Acquisition Corp. since March 2026. Corporate main line published on CAPL site (610-625-8000, Allentown HQ).

name: Scott W. Hart
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and board member, StepStone Group Inc. (Nasdaq: STEP)
profile: Scott Hart joined private-markets firm StepStone in 2007 as a senior associate, became partner in 2013, co-CEO with Monte Brem in 2019 and sole CEO in January 2022; he has sat on the board since 2020. His wealth comes from his equity in StepStone, a global private markets investor and adviser with hundreds of billions in assets under advisement/management.
interesting_fact: He went from senior associate to CEO of the same firm in about 15 years, and still leads StepStone's global private equity activities with a focus on co-investments.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was an analyst in Morgan Stanley's Consumer & Retail group, and at StepStone he helped open the firm's London office around 2011.
notes: Frequent Milken/industry conference speaker; Edelman handles StepStone media in 2026 releases (earlier releases listed ICR). Pitch via the Edelman media address with a private-markets/infrastructure/data-center financing angle.

name: Kenneth T. Sim
current_role: Co-Founder and Executive Chairman, Astrana Health (NASDAQ: ASTH)
profile: Dr. Kenneth Sim is a general surgeon who co-founded Network Medical Management and built it, via a 2017 merger with Apollo Medical, into Astrana Health (formerly ApolloMed), a physician-centric, value-based care platform in Southern California and beyond. He is Executive Chairman; his son Brandon Sim is CEO. He also chairs Allied Pacific IPA (APC).
interesting_fact: He led development of 'Super Medical Centers' across Southern California, integrated sites combining surgery, lab, radiology and urgent care under one roof.
deep_cut_fact: He trained at Loma Linda and the Autonomous University of Guadalajara in Mexico, did his general surgery residency at LA County King/Drew Medical Center, and won the LA County Medical Association's Independent Physician Leadership Award in 2014.
notes: Healthcare, not energy. Also on governing boards of Alhambra Hospital Medical Center, Garfield Medical Center and AHMC Seton. Son Brandon Sim (CEO) is the more public-facing figure.

name: Peter Thomas
profile: Welsh businessman who, with brother Sir Stanley Thomas, built Peter's Pies (sold to Grand Metropolitan in 1988) and later property/transport interests; former Cardiff Rugby chairman and benefactor, CBE 2012. Died 29 March 2023, aged 79.
notes: Deceased: died 29 March 2023 aged 79 (Cardiff Rugby / Caerphilly Observer: https://caerphilly.observer/news/1018781/bedwas-based-peters-pies-pays-tribute-to-peter-thomas/). Surviving brother Sir Stanley Thomas shared the Rich List entry.

name: Ye Fang
current_role: Unconfirmed; listed by Hurun (2013-2020) against Landbridge Group (山东岚桥集团, Rizhao)
profile: Hurun listed a Ye Fang (叶芳) for Landbridge Group, the Rizhao-based petrochemicals, trading and ports group founded in 2001 by Ye Cheng (叶成), which holds the 99-year Port of Darwin lease. No filing or news source was found that states Ye Fang's role or her relationship to Ye Cheng.
notes: Chinese searches tried: 叶芳+岚桥集团, 叶芳+岚桥 董事/监事/股东, and bond-prospectus shareholder searches. English searches tried: Ye Fang Landbridge Hurun. Every 叶芳 found was an unrelated person (an AllBright lawyer, a Huaqiao Univ. professor). She may be a relative or co-owner of Ye Cheng, but this is unverified. A 2024 CSRC penalty notice (csrc.gov.cn) names Ye Cheng as actual controller and records Landbridge's missed bond disclosures. Low priority.

name: Zhao Zhaofeng
current_role: Early shareholder/member of founding team, Bitmain Technologies (current title not publicly disclosed)
profile: A low-profile member of Bitmain's early team. The September 2018 Hong Kong IPO filing showed him with 6.26% of the bitcoin-mining-chip maker, the third-largest individual stake after co-founders Micree Zhan (36%) and Jihan Wu (20.25%). That stake put him on the Hurun China list from 2018 to 2020. No public executive role or later stake has been disclosed.
interesting_fact: In Bitmain's 2018 HKEX application his 6.26% holding ranked third among individuals, ahead of fellow early team members Ge Yuesheng (葛越晟) and Hu Yishuo (胡一说), at 4.18% each.
notes: Identity confirmed via the 2018 Bitmain prospectus coverage (NBD/券商中国) and Blockmedia's Hurun report (https://www.blockmedia.co.kr/archives/49046). He has almost no web footprint in Chinese or English. MarketScreener's 'Zhao Feng Zhao' entry is probably him but is unsourced. No personal channels were found. The only route is Bitmain corporate.

name: Guo Yan
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2017-2019) under Zhongrong Xinda Group (中融新大集团), Qingdao (coking coal/coke); role unverified
profile: Hurun lists Guo Yan (郭岩) under Zhongrong Xinda Group (formerly Shandong Coking), a Qingdao-headquartered coking-coal and coke group that expanded into finance from 2015. Its chairman and controller is Wang Qingtao (王清涛). No filing or news source naming Guo Yan as a shareholder or executive was found.
notes: The company match (中融新大, Qingdao, 煤焦) was confirmed via the Hurun rich-list API, but the role was not. Searched 中融新大 with 郭岩, 总裁 and 股东, plus group bond filings on Eastmoney; no hit. The name is common. Zhongrong Xinda defaulted on several bonds in 2020 (https://www.digitaling.com/articles/390978.html), so outreach is not recommended.

name: Li Renchao
current_role: Former chairman and president of Huaxi Energy Industry Co. (华西能源, SZSE: 002630), Zigong, Sichuan; resigned May 2025
profile: Li Renchao (黎仁超), nicknamed the 'boiler king', built Zigong-based Huaxi Energy into a maker of power-station and waste-to-energy boilers and an EPC/energy investor. He chaired it from Nov 2007 and was also president from April 2024 until he stepped down in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Chinese media nicknamed him the 'boiler king' (锅炉大王) for building one of Sichuan's leading industrial-boiler groups, listed in Shenzhen in 2011.
notes: Not suitable for outreach: in May 2025 he resigned all Huaxi Energy posts, and the company disclosed a detention (liuzhi) and case-filing notice against him from a Suining district supervisory commission. No longer an active executive; current status unknown.

name: Lin Zhenggang
current_role: Former major shareholder of Yihua Healthcare (宜华健康, SZSE: 000150); chairman of its subsidiary 众安康后勤集团 (per 2019 filing)
profile: Lin Zhenggang (林正刚) became a 5%+ shareholder of Yihua Healthcare (宜华健康, the former Yihua real-estate arm of Shantou's Yihua group) around 2015 when it acquired his hospital-logistics business 众安康后勤集团, which he chaired. He and brother Lin Jianxin acted in concert; by 2022 he held ~8.45% but pledged shares were being forcibly sold.
interesting_fact: His wealth came from hospital back-office/logistics services (众安康), an unusual niche, which he folded into a listed healthcare platform in exchange for shares.
notes: Hurun's 'Yihua Timbar Stock' label refers to his Yihua Healthcare shareholding. Very low public profile, no personal bio found. 2022 filings show forced disposal of pledged shares - wealth likely much reduced. No published contact; weak podcast target.

name: Liu Lirong
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Gionee (Shenzhen Gionee Communication Equipment); no current public role
profile: Liu Lirong founded the Chinese phone maker Gionee in 2002 and built it into a major domestic handset brand. The company hit a cash-flow crisis in 2018, and in December 2018 a Shenzhen court accepted a bankruptcy application against it. He has kept a very low profile since. A 2026 IT Home report, unverified, said he may be selling furniture in Indonesia.
notes: Very low profile since Gionee's 2018 bankruptcy, and press coverage of him is mostly negative (debts, gambling). Not a good outreach target. I found no published contact. Where he is now is unverified (https://www.ithome.com/0/939/207.htm). Sources: https://www.ifanr.com/1148318 (Dec 2018 court news) and https://www.jiemian.com/article/2643335.html.

name: Liu Tongbo
current_role: CEO and Director, Sunlands Technology Group (NYSE: STG), Beijing
profile: Liu Tongbo (刘通博) joined Sunlands, the online adult-education company founded by Peng Ou, in 2009 straight out of Tsinghua University. He has been CEO since January 2015 and a director since August 2017, and led the company through its 2018 NYSE IPO. Sunlands offers online degree and diploma-prep and professional-certification courses in China.
interesting_fact: Sunlands listed on the NYSE in March 2018 as one of China's largest online post-secondary and professional education platforms. Liu became CEO about six years after joining as a new graduate.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a bachelor's degree in applied mathematics from Tsinghua University and joined Sunlands right after graduating in 2009, so he has spent his whole career at the company.
notes: The company founder and chairman is Peng Ou, not Liu, although some profiles call Liu a founder. Liu gave interviews to China Daily (2018). Best route is Sunlands IR, which also handles media.

name: Lyu Rengao
current_role: Former founder and chairman of Zhejiang Julong Pipe Industry (巨龙管业, 002619.SZ); current role unknown
profile: Lyu Rengao (吕仁高, b. Nov 1961, from Dongyang, Zhejiang) built Jinhua-based Zhejiang Julong Pipe, a maker of large concrete water-transmission pipes (PCCP) for water-diversion projects, and listed it in Shenzhen in 2011 holding about 54%. The listed company later did a reverse takeover with game developer Aigelasi and was renamed (艾格拉斯). His current activities are not public.
interesting_fact: Julong Pipe's listed shell later became Aigelasi (艾格拉斯), a mobile-game company, through a reverse takeover: a concrete-pipe maker turned into a games stock.
deep_cut_fact: Julong began in January 1996 as a small private cement-products works Lyu set up in Bailongqiao, Jinhua county (later the Jinhua County Cement Pipe Factory). He spent nearly 30 years in cement products and won Jinhua's 'Golden Bull' outstanding entrepreneur award in 2010.
notes: 'Dragon Pipe Manufacturing' = 巨龙管业 (Julong = 'giant dragon'). He was on Hurun only 2015-2018. After the 002619 reverse takeover the listed company is unrelated to him (IR ir@egls.cn belongs to the games company, not him), so there is no current published contact. Status after about 2018 is unknown.

name: Ren Sanming
profile: Hurun China (2017–2018) lists Ren Sanming (任三明) with wealth from Rizhao Steel, the large private steelmaker in Rizhao, Shandong, founded by Du Shuanghua. No public source found describes his role at Rizhao Steel; he may be a shareholder or executive there.
notes: Could not confirm identity or current role. English and Chinese web searches found no profile of a Ren Sanming at Rizhao Steel. He is not a public figure, so Rizhao Steel corporate channels are the only route. Low priority.

name: Shao Yutian
current_role: Founder of Zhejiang Nanyang Technology (now CASC Rainbow, 002389); private investor whose family backs capacitor-film maker Xingyang Technology and other firms
profile: Shao Yutian founded Zhejiang Nanyang Electronic Film Co. in Taizhou in 2001. It became Nanyang Technology, a maker of capacitor and optical films, and listed in Shenzhen in 2010. A 2016-17 restructuring merged in CASC's drone assets (now CASC Rainbow) and cut his stake to ~3%. His family has since backed Xingyang Technology's Beijing Stock Exchange IPO filing and invested across the solar supply chain.
interesting_fact: The capacitor-film company he started in 2001 became, via a 2016-17 asset restructuring, CASC Rainbow (Aerospace CH UAV), China's listed maker of Rainbow military drones.
notes: No published personal or office contact found. He no longer controls a listed company. Recent coverage (2024-25) concerns family investments in Xingyang Tech and Taifu Pump's 2025 related-party acquisition of Nanyang Huacheng. Hurun listing is old (2010-18). Activity was reported in 2024-25, but there is no explicit confirmation he is alive. Wealth is shared with son Shao Yixing.

name: Shao Yixing
current_role: Private investor; shareholder (~3.8% in 2022) of Aerospace CH UAV Co. (航天彩虹, SZSE: 002389, formerly Zhejiang Nanyang Technology); no company role since Dec 2022
profile: Shao Yixing (邵奕兴, b. 1987) is the son of Shao Yutian, founder of Zhejiang Nanyang Technology, a Wenling (Taizhou) maker of capacitor and optical films. Father and son jointly controlled ~42%; in 2016 the father sold 21% to a Taizhou state investor, and China Aerospace (CASC) later took control. Shao was executive VP until resigning in Dec 2022.
interesting_fact: The family's plastic-film company became the listed vehicle for China Aerospace's Rainbow (CH) drone business; renamed Aerospace CH UAV, it now makes the CH-3/CH-4 drones alongside film materials.
notes: No current executive role or public profile; on his Dec 2022 resignation the company thanked him for his contributions to Nanyang and CH UAV (https://disc.static.szse.cn/disc/disk03/finalpage/2023-01-02/d6ea13b9-8f28-41ea-a3cd-68b43d174368.PDF). No published contact route found.

name: Wang Jianhua
current_role: Director and Chief Technology Officer, Qingdao Topscomm Communication Inc. (SSE: 603421); chairman 2012-May 2025
profile: Wang Jianhua (王建华, b. 1966), a senior engineer with a postgraduate degree, co-founded Qingdao Topscomm with Zeng Fanyi in 2008. Topscomm makes power-line carrier communication chips and modules, smart-meter and grid-automation equipment sold largely to China's State Grid, and listed in Shanghai in 2016. He chaired the company until May 2025 (succeeded by Liu Min) and remains a director, CTO and a major shareholder (~91.6m shares).
interesting_fact: Topscomm is a grid-edge tech play: it designs its own power-line carrier (PLC) communication chips used in electricity-meter reading networks, and its business scope now spans energy storage, EV charging and PV equipment.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a founder-chairman, he doubled as the company's hands-on technologist: CTO since 2015 and, from 2019 to 2024, head of Topscomm's in-house Chip and Basic Theory Research Institute; he also runs its fire-safety subsidiary Dingxin Xiaofang.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/grid-tech episode (PLC chips for smart grid). Low media profile; route via Topscomm securities office.

name: Wang Panrong
current_role: Former co-controlling shareholder of SEC Electric Machinery (中电电机, 603988.SH); no current role confirmed
profile: Wang Panrong (王盘荣) was one of the actual controllers, with Wang Jianyu and Wang Jiankai, of Wuxi-based SEC Electric Machinery, a maker of large and medium AC/DC motors and generators listed in Shanghai in 2014. In 2024 the Wang family's holding vehicle sold 30% to Beijing Gaodi Resources, handing control to gold-mining entrepreneur Guo Wenjun (completed Dec 2024).
interesting_fact: In 2024 the founding Wang family sold control of SEC Electric Machinery to Beijing Gaodi Resources, making a gold-mine owner the motor maker's new actual controller; Wang Panrong was a party to the supplementary deal agreement.
notes: Very low profile; no longer tied to the company after the 2024 control change. IPO prospectus naming him as actual controller: https://pdf.dfcfw.com/pdf/H2_AN201409110006968502_1.PDF. No usable contact route found.

name: Xu Haijiang
current_role: Former CEO and major shareholder, Jilin Jinguan Electric Co. (Jinguan Shares, SZSE: 300510); current role not confirmed
profile: Xu Haijiang was CEO and an early, major shareholder of Jilin Jinguan Electric, a Changchun maker of power distribution/switchgear equipment founded in 2006 and listed on ChiNext in 2016. He cut his stake below 9% in 2020; control has since passed to state-backed Luoyang Gudu Asset Management and he is no longer on the listed executive roster.
interesting_fact: Jinguan Electric, where he was CEO, listed on Shenzhen's ChiNext board (300510) in 2016; in 2020 his holding fell from 9.10% to 7.22% as the company's control shifted.
deep_cut_fact: Before electrical equipment, he worked in Tanzania (1998-2001) and was deputy GM of Jilin Hengkun (2004-06) prior to joining Jinguan.
notes: Appears to have stepped back from Jinguan; current activities unknown. Profile details come from 36kr company database (possibly dated).

name: Xu Jianmin
current_role: Actual controller (~30.9%) of Xi'an Huaxin New Energy Co., Ltd. (西安华新新能源, ex-NEEQ 834368 '华新能源'), per exchange data; likely match
profile: Probable match: Xu Jianmin (许建民) is listed as actual/ultimate controller of Xi'an Huaxin New Energy, a Shaanxi firm doing engineering, EPC and energy-management contracts for industrial waste-heat/waste-pressure power plants and biomass power. It traded on China's NEEQ board (834368), consistent with Hurun's 2016-18 'HuaXin, new energy' entry; it has since been delisted.
interesting_fact: Xi'an Huaxin specialises in turning industrial waste heat (e.g. coke dry-quenching, ferroalloy and yellow-phosphorus furnaces) into electricity, and is a registered NDRC energy-service company.
notes: Tie to Hurun entry is inferred (name + 'Huaxin' new-energy company + NEEQ listing timing), not confirmed by a Hurun source. Chairman/legal rep is Wang Jihua, not Xu. Company delisted from NEEQ; 2019-21 broker/company notices cite court-enforcement (失信) issues for the company and Xu - treat outreach with caution. Chinese web search tools were weak; Baidu/cninfo unreachable.

name: Xu Liang
profile: Listed with source of wealth 'Yuhuan' (China). Yuhuan is a manufacturing county in Taizhou, Zhejiang, so this may refer to a company based there rather than a company name; no matching profile could be confirmed in English sources.
notes: Common name; identity not confirmed. Needs Chinese-language research (Hurun entry) to determine the company before any outreach.

name: Yan Dapeng
current_role: Vice Chairman and Chief Engineer, Wuhan Raycus Fiber Laser Technologies (300747.SZ)
profile: Dr. Yan Dapeng is a laser physicist who returned from the US in 2007 to co-found Wuhan Raycus with Huagong Laser, building China's leading domestic fiber-laser maker and challenging IPG Photonics' dominance. Raycus listed in Shenzhen in 2018; Yan remains vice chairman and chief engineer, recognised as a 'national outstanding engineer'.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Raycus unveiled a single-mode 10,000-watt fiber laser (10.1 kW, beam quality M2 as low as 1.13); Yan described the Raman effect as a 'traffic jam' of light energy in the fiber that limits power scaling.
deep_cut_fact: From 1996 to 2007 he worked in the US at the University of Illinois at Chicago, Wright State University and fiber-laser firms including Nufern, earning three US patents, after earlier working at Nanjing Polytechnic; he and Huagong Laser each put RMB30m into Raycus in 2007.
notes: Raycus is now majority-owned by state-backed China Aerospace Science & Industry (via Huagong lineage). Deep-cut source is a 2010 industry blog citing Raycus' website - verify before use. Technical person; lasers for battery/EV manufacturing link to energy theme.

name: Yan Rui
profile: Listed on the Hurun China Rich List (2017-2019) as Yan Rui (颜瑞) of real-estate group "Xingyao" (星耀). Searches in English and Chinese did not identify this person or confirm which Xingyao company is meant (e.g. Kunming-based Shining Star Group 星耀集团 is a possible but unconfirmed match).
notes: Could not confirm identity within budget; possible match is Shining Star Group (星耀集团, Kunming, founded 1993; https://beltandroad.hktdc.com/en/node/58976) but no source links Yan Rui to it. Needs Chinese business-registry (Qichacha/Tianyancha) check before outreach.
