profile: Appeared once on the Hurun China Rich List (2019) with wealth attributed to 'Zhongrong Xinda' (coal). No public sources were found identifying the company's full name, location or her/his role.
notes: Chinese and English searches (张令玉, 中融信达, coal) returned nothing relevant; unrelated to Cinda Securities. A corporate-registry lookup (Qichacha/Tianyancha) would be needed. Treat as unverified; single-year Hurun entry.

name: Sun Yanlong
current_role: Chairman, General Manager and actual controller, Hangzhou Arcvideo Technology (当虹科技, SSE STAR: 688039)
profile: Sun Yanlong (b. 1976) is a video-compression engineer who founded Hangzhou Arcvideo, a STAR Market-listed maker of AI-driven video encoding, ultra-HD (4K/8K) broadcast and streaming systems. He has been GM since 2013 and chairman since 2016, and controls the company through holding partnerships.
interesting_fact: For the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics, CCTV used Arcvideo's 8K AVS3 encoders to compress the 8K feed to a 120 Mb stream. Arcvideo also helped build the broadcaster's 8K ultra-HD IP distribution platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Arcvideo he was R&D director at InterVideo Inc. (maker of WinDVD) from 2002 to 2005, then vice president of ArcSoft (Hangzhou) from 2005 to 2012.
notes: Engineer-founder with a modest public profile; IR mailbox is the formal route. The deep-cut career history comes from a secondary profile site (maigoo), so confirm it against Arcvideo's prospectus if possible.

name: Li Yueling
current_role: Board secretary and CFO, Nanjing Develop Advanced Manufacturing (迪威尔, 688377.SS); co-actual controller with chairman Zhang Li
profile: Co-founder and co-controller, with chairman and GM Zhang Li, of Nanjing Develop Advanced Manufacturing. Founded in 2009 and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market, it forges and machines pressure-control parts for oil and gas wellheads, blowout preventers and subsea Christmas trees, sold mainly to large international oilfield-service companies. She serves as board secretary and heads the accounting function.
interesting_fact: Develop calls itself a pioneer in parts for deep-sea subsea Christmas trees and a 'one-stop shop' supplying everything from the forged material to finished assemblies, built to API standards for subsea conditions.
deep_cut_fact: She was one of the original founding investors in 2009, when the company was set up by Nanjing Develop Industrial, Li Yueling and Zhang Hong. It has since been building a multi-directional die-forging plant to make high-end valve and piping components.
notes: Hurun's 'Develop' is Nanjing Develop (迪威尔); Hurun's 'Zhang Li' is chairman Zhang Li (张利). The founding detail comes from the 10jqka company page (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/688377/company.html) via search, and the plant detail from the 2024 interim report. As board secretary she personally handles the zqb@ IR mailbox, which makes it a reasonably direct route. Subsea oil-and-gas equipment angle.

name: Rajendra Vallabhaji Gogri
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman (from Oct 1, 2026; previously Chairman & MD), Aarti Industries Ltd. (NSE: AARTIIND)
profile: Rajendra Gogri is a founding member of Aarti Industries, the Mumbai-based benzene-chemistry specialty chemicals group incorporated in 1984 and started by his brother Chandrakant Gogri. He was managing director for about two decades and became chairman in 2012. In a planned succession he moved to non-executive chairman on Oct 1, 2026, with professional CEO Suyog Kotecha (ex-McKinsey) now running the company.
interesting_fact: In 2019 he won both ICC's Lala Shriram National Award and Hurun India's Most Respected Entrepreneur of the Year award.
deep_cut_fact: He was a rank holder in chemical engineering at UDCT Mumbai (now ICT), earned a master's in chemical engineering in the US, and received UDCT's Distinguished Alumnus Award in 1995, the same honour his brother Chandrakant received.
notes: He just moved to a non-executive role (Oct 2026) and may have more time for long-form conversations. Aarti also has a media kit page: https://www.aarti-industries.com/media-kit. Some aggregators say his US master's is from Iowa State; the company site says only 'USA'.

name: Eric Herd
current_role: Owner and chairman/chief executive, Farmfoods Ltd (Cumbernauld, Scotland)
profile: Eric Herd owns Farmfoods, the family-owned frozen-food and grocery discounter with 300+ UK shops. He turned a 1954 Aberdeen meat-processing business into Britain's second-biggest frozen-food retailer and has been a director of the group since at least 1993; the chain is now expanding by 20-30 stores a year, notably around London.
interesting_fact: In 2011 Farmfoods teamed up with Asda in an unsuccessful bid for rival Iceland, under which Farmfoods would have taken about 200 of Iceland's 800 stores.
deep_cut_fact: Farmfoods' roots are a 1954 meat-processing firm (Farmfoods (Aberdeen) Ltd) whose first shop opened in Aberdeen in the 1970s; by the mid-1980s it had only about 20 outlets. It proudly says its no-frills stores have 'no intention of winning any interior design competitions'.
notes: Described by The Grocer as reclusive and the Scotsman as publicity-shy; no interviews found. A younger George Herd (likely family) also sits on the board. Only route is the company's general contact form.

name: Keith Black
current_role: CEO and co-owner, Regatta Group (Regatta, Craghoppers, Dare2b, Regatta Professional), Manchester
profile: Keith Black runs the family-owned Regatta Group, one of the UK's largest outdoor-clothing businesses, headquartered at Risol House in Urmston, Manchester. His father Lionel bought the small wholesaler Risol Products in 1977. Keith took over in 1981 and built the Regatta brand, later adding Craghoppers and launching Dare2b in 2000. He co-owns the group with his sister Joanne.
interesting_fact: Regatta won the Queen's Award for Enterprise in International Trade in both 2012 and 2013, and its Regatta jacket won a Which? award for best waterproof jacket in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: The brand name came about by chance. In 1982 Keith bought a cancelled order of jackets printed with a sailing boat and the word 'Regatta', and the name stuck. Risol formally became Regatta in the mid-1990s.
notes: Private, family-owned company, and Keith rarely gives interviews. I found no published press email for Regatta. Ignore the pattern-based email formats on lead-gen sites. Best route is the company's head office or website contact channels.

name: Mark N Lampert
current_role: Founder and General Partner, BVF Partners L.P. (Biotechnology Value Fund), San Francisco
profile: Mark Lampert founded BVF Partners in 1993. The San Francisco firm is one of the longest-running biotech-focused investors and holds large stakes in companies such as Kymera, MoonLake, Palvella and 4D Molecular Therapeutics. Before BVF he was a VP at Oppenheimer & Co. and had worked at Cambridge NeuroScience, G.D. Searle and BCG. He has been active in biotech since 1984.
interesting_fact: Before BVF he founded Biotechnology Royalty Corp., an early attempt to pool university biotech patent royalties, long before royalty funds became a mainstream asset class.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Ann Arbor, Michigan, earned an A.B. with honors in chemistry at Harvard, and is a founding donor to GiveDirectly, the charity that sends cash directly to people living in poverty, as well as the Lampert-Byrd Foundation.
notes: Spoke at the Invest for Kids Chicago conference (2018, listed again as a 2026 speaker). An unverified TheOrg listing puts him on the board of International Lifeline Fund. BVF's website is behind Cloudflare and no published contact was retrieved. Best route is probably via BVF Partners in San Francisco. Biotech investor, so a weak fit with energy/data centers.

name: Mark S Comora
current_role: Chairman of the Board, OPAL Fuels (Nasdaq: OPAL); Founder and President, Fortistar LLC
profile: CPA with a Columbia MBA who founded Fortistar, a White Plains investment firm, in 1993. He led its growth in decarbonising power, transport fuels and industry. Fortistar controls OPAL Fuels, a renewable-natural-gas producer listed via SPAC in 2022, and he has chaired OPAL since 2020. He is 84 per the 2026 proxy.
interesting_fact: He has long been in independent power. He sat on the board of the Independent Power Producers of New York and the Equipment Leasing Association. Fortistar's portfolio has run from power plants to landfill-gas and dairy RNG.
deep_cut_fact: Outside energy, he is an officer and board member of the American Museum of Fly Fishing in Manchester, Vermont.
notes: Good fit for the energy angle (RNG, independent power). The general Fortistar inbox is the most direct published route. The OPAL IR contact appears in older press releases. OPAL's media contact is handled by ICR.

name: William J Maris
current_role: Founder and Managing Partner, Section 32 (venture capital, San Diego/La Jolla); former 10%+ holder of Dave Inc. via Section 32 Fund 1
profile: Bill Maris (b. 1975) founded Google Ventures (GV) in 2008 and was its first CEO, backing Uber, Nest, Flatiron Health and Slack. He also conceived Alphabet's longevity company Calico. In 2017 he founded Section 32, a frontier-tech fund (about US$2bn AUM) whose portfolio includes Phaidra (AI for data-centre cooling), Neuralink, SandboxAQ and Infleqtion. His Dave Inc. stake came from an early Section 32 bet.
interesting_fact: While at GV he pitched Google's leadership on Calico, a company meant 'to treat aging as a disease, and cure it.' Google funded it, and it became one of Alphabet's best-known moonshots.
deep_cut_fact: Before Google, he founded Burlee.com in 1997, one of the first web-hosting companies. He built its original infrastructure after teaching himself to code from books bought at his local Barnes & Noble. Burlee was later acquired by Interland, which became Web.com.
notes: A strong podcast fit: he trained in neuroscience (Middlebury), backs energy/data-centre-relevant companies like Phaidra and Infleqtion, and has appeared on All-In. Section 32 publishes no press email, so the best route is a warm intro or an approach via Section 32's site. Avoid personal-life topics.

name: Lord Alli (Waheed Alli)
current_role: Labour life peer (Baron Alli of Norbury), House of Lords; media entrepreneur and investor
profile: Waheed Alli (b. 1964, Croydon) left school at 16 and co-founded TV producer Planet 24 (The Big Breakfast, The Word, Survivor format) with Charlie Parsons. He later chaired Chorion (Agatha Christie, Enid Blyton rights) and ASOS, and ran Silvergate Media (Octonauts, Peter Rabbit) until 2022. A Labour peer since 1998, he remains active in the Lords.
interesting_fact: Made a life peer in 1998 at 33, he was one of the youngest members of the Lords and one of the few openly gay Muslim politicians in the world. He campaigned to repeal Section 28 and to equalise the age of consent.
deep_cut_fact: His first job after leaving school at 16 with nine O-levels was junior researcher at a finance magazine. He went on to serve as Chancellor of De Montfort University (2006-2015).
notes: The email is the House of Lords' generic member-contact address listed on his parliamentary profile (House of Lords, London SW1A 0PW). He is politically sensitive: he was at the centre of the 2024 Labour donations/gifts row and a Lords standards inquiry found a registration breach, so outreach should be framed carefully.

name: Sharon Harel
current_role: Founder, WestEnd Films (London film/TV production, financing and international sales company)
profile: Sharon Harel-Cohen is a London-based film producer and financier who has produced or financed 50+ films, chiefly through Capitol Films, which she co-founded in 1989 and sold in 2006 (Gosford Park, Spider, Death and the Maiden). In 2008 she launched WestEnd Films with Eve Schoukroun and Maya Amsellem; its credits include HBO's Valley of Tears. Her listed wealth is shared with her husband, private-equity and impact-investing pioneer Sir Ronald Cohen.
interesting_fact: Executive producer on Robert Altman's Gosford Park, Polanski's Death and the Maiden and the Oscar-nominated Albert Nobbs; she received the Olswang Business Award from Carlton Women in Film and Television in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: She began as a producer in Israel on the classic Halahaka ('The Troupe'), which she co-wrote, then produced Tom Hanks' 1986 Tri-Star film Every Time We Say Goodbye; her degree from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem is in Chinese Studies and Western Philosophy.
notes: Also known as Sharon Harel-Cohen / Lady Cohen. Best route is WestEnd Films general inbox. Husband Sir Ronald Cohen (Apax founder, impact investing) may be the more relevant podcast guest.

profile: Terence Cole (1933-2022), co-founder with Mark Steinberg in 1976 of MARCOL, the London-based international property investment group (owner of Chelsea Harbour from 2003). Died December 2022 per a tribute in Finito World quoting MARCOL co-founder Mark Steinberg.

current_role: President, Squadron Capital LLC (Granby, CT); director of OrthoPediatrics Corp. (KIDS) and Alphatec Holdings (ATEC)
profile: Retired U.S. Army colonel turned private-equity investor who founded/runs Squadron Capital, a firm making direct investments in operating companies, chiefly orthopedic and spine medtech. Squadron is a 10%+ holder of OrthoPediatrics (board seat since 2011) and a major Alphatec holder (board seat since 2020).

name: Padmasingh Isaac
current_role: Founder and Chairman/Managing Director, Aachi Group (Aachi Masala Foods), Chennai
profile: A.D. Padmasingh Isaac, a first-generation entrepreneur from Nazareth in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, spent about a decade in sales at Godrej before founding Aachi Masala in Chennai in the mid-1990s. Aachi grew from cheap curry-masala sachets aimed at rural buyers into a 1,000-crore-plus spice and packaged-food group selling in dozens of countries.
interesting_fact: Aachi's first products were curry masala powders in low-priced sachets; when shopkeepers were reluctant to stock them, he personally promoted the brand outside shops. Aachi was named 'India's No. 1 Most Trusted Brand 2015' (Trust Research Advisory).
deep_cut_fact: He is the author of a business book, 'Enjoy Success, Relish Failures' (Rupa Publications), and has held advisory roles at the Indian Institute of Crop Processing Technology, Thanjavur, and NIFTEM, Haryana.
notes: care@ is the company's general customer-care address, not a personal or press office. Aachi was reported in 2024 to be in acquisition talks with large FMCG groups (unconfirmed). Speaks often at youth/entrepreneurship events in Tamil Nadu - a Tamil-language podcast angle may land well.

name: Michael Donald Schoeb
current_role: CEO and Director, Alliance Laundry Holdings Inc. (NYSE: ALH)
profile: Mike Schoeb joined Alliance Laundry Systems (Ripon, Wisconsin; maker of Speed Queen commercial washers/dryers) as President & COO in 2007 and became CEO in 2011. He led the company through its October 2025 NYSE IPO (~$826M base deal), and his wealth stems from his ALH equity. Earlier roles at Wausau Homes, Hilti and Johnson Controls.
interesting_fact: Alliance Laundry says its enterprise value has quadrupled during his tenure as CEO; the company claims roughly 40% of the North American commercial laundry market and went public on the NYSE on 8 Oct 2025 at $22/share.
deep_cut_fact: Before laundry, he ran Hilti's Brazilian business as President of Hilti do Brasil and was Hilti's SVP of Marketing & Brand for North America, after starting out in sales/general management at Johnson Controls.
notes: Public-company CEO; best route is via Alliance Laundry IR/corporate communications. Education per 2007 release: MBA and MS from Johns Hopkins, BA political science from Mount St. Mary's (Emmitsburg, MD).

name: Hu Shiyong
current_role: Co-controlling shareholder (with brothers Hu Shiqing and Hu Shifa) of Jiangsu Huahong Industrial Group / Huahong Technology (SZSE: 002645); chairman of Huahong Technology 2008-2023, director until May 2026
profile: Jiangyin, Jiangsu industrialist (b. 1949) who built Huahong Group from a Zhouzhuang village enterprise into a chemical-fibre, plastics and copper group, and listed Huahong Technology (scrap-metal recycling equipment, resource and rare-earth recycling). He chaired it 2008-2023; on Hurun China lists 2008-2012.
interesting_fact: Huahong Group grew out of Mengxiang village in Zhouzhuang town, Jiangyin - the village was later renamed 'Huahong Village' after the company he led as village party secretary from 1992.
deep_cut_fact: With only a junior-high education, he spent 1969-72 in Guizhou working on the 'Third Front' industrial construction drive, then ran the Zhouzhuang sheet-metal welding works as factory director before founding the group.
notes: Elderly (77), stepped off the listed company's board in May 2026 (per lixinger); no personal media presence. IR mailbox is the listed company's securities office. Weak fit for data-center focus; recycling/metals angle instead.

name: Graham Peacock
current_role: Owner, TG Convenience Stores (UK forecourt/convenience operator)
profile: British forecourt entrepreneur who cofounded MRH (GB) in 1997 and built it into the UK's largest independent fuel retailer (~450 sites plus a fuel-distribution arm), selling to Lone Star Funds in 2016 after a 2008 Barclays PE stake sale. He remains in the sector via TG Convenience Stores.
interesting_fact: The 2016 sale of MRH to US private-equity firm Lone Star Funds was reported as a roughly £2bn forecourt deal, putting him among the UK's super-rich.
deep_cut_fact: MRH was born in 1997 when Peacock and several colleagues set up on their own after their employer, forecourt operator Oakstead, buckled under the 'Esso Pricewatch' price war.
notes: Low public profile, covered mainly by trade press (Forecourt Trader, The Grocer), which has given him a lifetime-achievement award. No published personal or company contact found. Forecourt Trader returns 405 to scripted fetches, so award details are unverified.

name: Meeta Dhingra
current_role: Berger Paints promoter-family member (no executive role found)
profile: Meeta Dhingra is the wife of Kuldip Singh Dhingra, who with his brother Gurbachan bought Berger Paints India from Vijay Mallya's UB Group in 1991 and built it into India's second-largest paint maker. She appeared on Hurun India 2018-2019 as part of the Dhingra promoter holdings; no public business role for her was found.
interesting_fact: The Dhingra brothers acquired Berger Paints India in 1991 from the UB Group; it is now India's No. 2 paint company, chaired by Kuldip's daughter Rishma Kaur.
notes: Very private; identified only as Kuldip Singh Dhingra's wife (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kuldip_Singh_Dhingra). IR email belongs to Berger's company secretary (Arunito Ganguly) and is for shareholder matters, so it is a weak route. Paint/chemicals, so a loose fit for an energy podcast.

name: Konstantin Grigorishin
current_role: Head/majority investor, Energy Standard Group; founder and president, International Swimming League (ISL)
profile: Zaporizhzhia-born (1965) theoretical physicist (MIPT, PhD 1991) who made money in 1990s metals trading, then bought Ukrainian machine-building, river-shipping (Ukrrichflot) and regional power-distribution (oblenergo) assets via Energy Standard Group (est. 2005). Best known internationally for bankrolling the professional International Swimming League; currently outside Ukraine.
interesting_fact: He founded and funded the International Swimming League (~$20m first-season budget), a team-based pro swimming circuit, and in January 2026 the ISL won a US jury verdict in its antitrust case against World Aquatics (damages: $1).
deep_cut_fact: A master-class swimmer himself, he trained in Landau's theoretical-physics group at MIPT and defended a 1991 PhD on 'light propagation in nonlinear disordered media'; his first company (1992) was an IT firm called AragornSoft.
notes: HIGH RISK: Ukraine sanctioned/blocked his assets (Jan 2025 presidential decree) and as of May 2026 is reportedly seeking an international arrest warrant; Russia also issued an in-absentia warrant (2016, tax case) and sanctioned him in 2018. Net worth figure is dated. No published contact found; journalist should weigh suitability carefully.

name: Leon Jesus Zamora
current_role: Executive Chairman of the Board and President, Auna S.A. (NYSE: AUNA); Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Enfoca
profile: Jesús 'Suso' Zamora León is a Peruvian private-equity investor who co-founded Enfoca, the Lima investment firm that controls Auna, a Latin American hospital, oncology and health-plan network (Peru, Colombia, Mexico). He has sat on Auna's board since 2008, became executive chairman in 2022 and took the company public on the NYSE in March 2024.
interesting_fact: Forbes Peru named him to its 'Los 26 del 26' list of leaders set to shape Peru in 2026; Auna plans to invest US$500m in Mexico in 2026-28 and to develop EsSalud's Torre Trecca medical complex via a public-private partnership.
deep_cut_fact: Though a Peruvian investor, he studied industrial engineering at Mexico's UNAM before an MBA at Columbia Business School - a Mexico link that predates Auna's big Mexican hospital push.
notes: Goes by 'Suso' Zamora in Auna materials. IR reports to EVP Strategy & ECM Lorenzo Massart. Healthcare rather than energy, but Auna's hospital buildout is capex-heavy infrastructure.

name: Pan Jiding
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2006-2007 as founder or owner of Guotai Hengsheng Investment (国泰恒生投资), with interests in real estate and railways. Web searches turned up no other public information on 盘继顶 or the company.

name: Tan Changan
current_role: Founder of the Tan Yutou (谭鱼头) hotpot chain; since 2020 legal representative of and taste adviser to Chengdu Tanziyu Catering Management (谭滋鱼)
profile: Tan Changan (谭长安) founded the Tan Yutou fish-head hotpot chain in Chengdu in 1996 and grew it to about 90 restaurants in 58 cities within three years, with revenue above RMB500m by 2002. The original company was later liquidated and its trademarks auctioned in 2021. Since 2020 he has worked on a new venture, Tanziyu, where he says he mainly oversees flavour.
interesting_fact: In 2002 Tan Yutou became the first mainland Chinese hotpot brand to open in Taiwan. At its peak Tan reportedly cut the ribbon at four new restaurants in a single day.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army in 1996, he used his RMB5,000 demobilisation payment to open the first Tan Yutou in a small lane near Baihuatan in Chengdu. The 20-odd tables were so busy that people reportedly resold queue tickets.
notes: Hurun listing is from 2007. The original Tan Yutou company has since gone through bankruptcy liquidation, so handle this sensitively and avoid mentioning it in outreach. No published contact found. Restaurant entrepreneur; weak fit with energy/data centers but a strong rise-and-rebuild entrepreneurship story.

name: Lip Bu Tan
current_role: CEO and Director, Intel Corporation (since March 2025); Chairman of Walden International and founding managing partner of Walden Catalyst Ventures; also listed as a director of Credo Technology
profile: Malaysia-born, Singapore-educated Lip-Bu Tan founded Walden International in 1987, one of the first VC firms to back Asian semiconductor start-ups. He was CEO of Cadence Design Systems from 2008 to 2021, and Intel named him CEO in March 2025 to lead its turnaround. He won the SIA's 2022 Robert N. Noyce Award and was on TIME's 100 most influential list in 2026.
interesting_fact: He began as a would-be nuclear engineer. He was at MIT working toward a PhD in nuclear engineering in 1979 when the Three Mile Island accident struck. A careers adviser told him there was no future in the field, so he dropped out, joined a nuclear consultancy in San Francisco and later took an MBA.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2025 NTU alumni profile he is 'the curious kid who became Intel's CEO'. He took a physics degree at Nanyang University in Singapore before MIT, and NTU says he has kept close ties to his alma mater.

public_contacts.value: Intel Public Relations contact form (for journalists)

notes: Very high-profile and heavily gated. Go through Intel corporate PR (the form; pressroompublishing@intel.com is explicitly NOT for media). His nuclear-engineering start is a natural hook for an energy/data-centre podcast. Walden Catalyst is an alternative route.

name: Catherine Zeta-Jones
current_role: Actor and producer (e.g. Wednesday S2 on Netflix, Kill Jackie on Prime Video as star/executive producer, The Gallerist); founder of Casa Zeta-Jones lifestyle brand
profile: Swansea-born actor (b. 1969) who rose from West End musicals to Hollywood stardom (The Mask of Zorro, Traffic, Chicago). She won the Oscar, BAFTA and SAG for Chicago and a Tony for A Little Night Music. Her wealth is shared with husband Michael Douglas. She launched the Casa Zeta-Jones home brand in 2017 and still acts and produces.
interesting_fact: She is one of the few performers to have won both an Academy Award (Chicago, 2003) and a Tony Award (A Little Night Music, 2010), and was made a CBE in 2010 for film and charity work.
deep_cut_fact: Her break came in 1987 as the second understudy in 42nd Street in the West End. When the star and first understudy were both unavailable she went on as Peggy Sawyer, and the producer kept her in the role for two years. She was made a Freeman of Swansea in 2019.
notes: A Hollywood celebrity, not an entrepreneur in energy/data centres. The realistic route is her talent agency or publicist (not verified here) or Casa Zeta-Jones. Rich-list wealth is joint with Michael Douglas.

name: Michael Douglas
current_role: Actor and film producer (announced retirement from acting in 2025); UN Messenger of Peace; board member, Nuclear Threat Initiative
profile: Michael Douglas (b. 1944), son of Kirk Douglas, won Best Picture as producer of One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest and Best Actor as Gordon Gekko in Wall Street. Listed with wife Catherine Zeta-Jones on the UK rich list; his wealth comes from acting and producing. He is a long-time nuclear-disarmament advocate.
interesting_fact: He produced and starred in The China Syndrome (1979), a thriller about a nuclear power plant accident; the Three Mile Island accident happened just 12 days after the film's release.
deep_cut_fact: He worked three summers during college at the Eugene O'Neill Theater Center in Waterford, Connecticut, and remains a longstanding board member there; he also hosted a celebrity golf tournament for 12 years that raised $10m+ for the Motion Picture & Television Fund.
notes: Major celebrity; outreach realistically goes through his talent agency/publicist (not verified here due to search limits). Angle for an energy podcast: China Syndrome and his Nuclear Threat Initiative board work. Profile here is about him alone, not Zeta-Jones.

profile: Wendell Weeks joined Corning in finance in 1983, ran its optical-fiber business from 1996, became CEO in 2005, chairman in 2007 and also president in Oct 2025. name: Christopher R. Christensen

name: Anwar Patel
profile: Anwer (Anwar) Patel, a Bolton pharmacist, co-founded the Cohens Chemist group with his elder brother Yakub in 1979 (first pharmacy in Rochdale). He died on 28 April 2021, aged 66.

name: Keith Bradshaw
current_role: Chairman and 50% co-owner, Listers Group (car dealerships, Stratford-upon-Avon); co-owner/non-exec chairman, Nurton Developments
profile: Aston-born chartered accountant who built BP Nursing Homes into Takare plc, Europe's largest care-home operator (14,000 staff), selling it to BUPA in 1998 for ~£300m. Co-founded Listers car dealership in Coventry with Terry Lister in 1979; it is now England's largest independent dealer group (£1.2bn+ turnover). Also co-owns Birmingham developer Nurton.
interesting_fact: Listers grew from a single dealership and body shop in Coventry into a 50+ outlet group selling BMW, Land Rover, Jaguar, Audi, Toyota, Mercedes and more, with Terry Lister as its public face.
deep_cut_fact: After qualifying as an accountant in Birmingham in 1966 he spent time working in West Africa, returning at 30 to start the companies that became Takare. He is also deputy chairman and co-owner of Laney/Headstock, the amp and musical-instrument maker, and chaired the trustees of the Library of Birmingham.
notes: Was 74 in 2018 (now ~82); low-profile, Terry Lister is Listers' public face. Was High Sheriff of the West Midlands 2016-17. Son David runs Nurton Developments. No published personal email found.

name: Susan Tobbell
current_role: Co-founder, SGN Retail (Essex forecourt operator; sale of 100% to Essar's EET Retail agreed Sept 2026); director, TG Convenience Stores and Starbridge Property Investment
profile: Susan Margaret Tobbell is a UK fuel-retail entrepreneur. After serving as a director of forecourt group MRH (GB) in 2011-2016, she co-founded SGN Retail with Graham Peacock in 2016 and grew it to 118 petrol stations. In Sept 2026 Essar's EET Retail agreed to buy all of SGN, reportedly for about £400M, to create a 235-site refinery-to-pump network.
interesting_fact: SGN Retail reached 118 sites in a decade in a UK market where total forecourt numbers have been falling for fifty years; Essar is buying it to send Stanlow-refined fuel straight to its own pumps.
deep_cut_fact: Before SGN she was a director of MRH (GB), the forecourt operator later bought by Lone Star (2016) and Motor Fuel Group (2018, £1.2B); she has also been a significant shareholder (about 7%) in AIM-listed bus operator Rotala.
notes: Very private; not quoted in the 2026 deal announcement and no interviews, website or social accounts found. Sunday Times Rich List 2020 entry for fuel distribution. Approach via SGN Retail/EET Retail press channels if needed.

name: Nikolaos Tsakos
current_role: Founder, President and CEO, TEN Ltd (Tsakos Energy Navigation, NYSE: TEN)
profile: Born 1963 in Athens into a Chios shipping family, Nikolas Tsakos (Columbia BA, London MA in shipping finance) founded Tsakos Energy Navigation, listed in Oslo in 1993 and on the NYSE since 2002, the longest-established listed Greek shipping company. TEN runs a fleet of crude and product tankers, LNG carriers and shuttle tankers chartered to oil majors and refiners.
interesting_fact: He chaired INTERTANKO, the global independent tanker owners' association, from 2014 to 2018, and was Lloyd's List Greek Shipping Newsmaker of the Year in 2015.
deep_cut_fact: He has spent a total of two years at sea and served as an officer in the Hellenic Navy in 1988; in 2026 he was named Grand Marshal of the Greek diaspora parade in New York.

public_contacts.value: Capital Link, Inc. (Nicolas Bornozis / Markella Kara), ten@capitallink.com

notes: Usually spelled Nikolas P. Tsakos. Media-friendly and a frequent speaker at shipping conferences (Capital Link forums). Capital Link handles TEN's IR/media; COO George Saroglou is the company's named press-release contact. Energy-shipping (oil, LNG) angle.

name: Ni Yunda
current_role: Founder/president of Jiangsu Shunda Group (Yangzhou polysilicon, ingot and wafer maker); current role not verified
profile: Ni Yunda (倪云达) built Yangzhou-based Jiangsu Shunda Group into one of China's larger early solar raw-material suppliers, producing polysilicon (~1,500 t/yr by 2009), monocrystalline ingots and wafers. Shunda drew $82m led by Actis in 2006-07; Suntech bought into Shunda Holdings in 2008 with a 13-year ~7GW wafer supply deal. He was on Hurun lists 2007-2010.
interesting_fact: In 2008 Suntech paid ~$99m for a stake in Shunda Holdings and signed a 13-year wafer supply contract totalling roughly 7GW, one of the largest PV supply deals of that era.
deep_cut_fact: In April 2009 Ni ('Mr. Yunda Ni, President of Jiangsu Shunda') became chairman of Shunda-SolarE Technologies, a US joint venture with Menlo Park-based Solar EnerTech aimed at the US solar market; he said the goal was to 'build market share in the U.S.'
notes: Identity confirmed via SEC filing (Solar EnerTech 8-K, 2009). No current information found on Ni or Shunda after ~2012 polysilicon downturn; no published contacts. Low public profile.

name: Yang Rongchun
current_role: Co-founder and former vice-president of Hengan Group (Hengan International, HKEX 1044); no current executive role found
profile: Yang Rongchun (杨荣春, b. ~1950), an engineer from Anhai, Jinjiang (Fujian), co-founded Hengan in 1985 with Sze Man Bok, Hui Lin Chit and Hung Ching Shan, pooling RMB1.36m to start one of China's first sanitary-napkin makers. Hengan grew into China's leading tissue and hygiene group (HK-listed 1998). He later served as Hengan Group VP and a director of Shanghai Jahwa.
interesting_fact: Hengan's 1998 Hong Kong IPO set that year's records for the highest P/E and the highest subscription multiple on the HK exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Hengan's origin story starts with him: in Nov 1984, as a technician at the Anhai General Machinery Factory, Yang showed Hui Lin Chit a Taiwanese sanitary-napkin machine manual, said to promise payback within three months of production - which led to Hengan's founding.
notes: Low-profile co-founder; a 2018 Jiemian piece says only Sze Man Bok and Hui Lin Chit remain in management, so Yang appears retired from executive roles. Email is Hengan Group's general website mailbox (footer), not a personal route. Sina Finance lists him as engineer, b. 1950, ex-director of Shanghai Jahwa (600315).

name: Dmytro Lider
current_role: Co-founder, Grammarly (now part of Superhuman Platform Inc.); current operating role not confirmed
profile: Ukrainian software entrepreneur who co-founded Grammarly in 2009 with Max Lytvyn and Alex Shevchenko. The writing assistant, built largely in Kyiv, reached a $13B valuation in 2021; in 2024-25 Grammarly bought Coda and the Superhuman email app and rebranded its parent company as Superhuman.
interesting_fact: Grammarly started as a subscription grammar checker for students and grew into an AI writing assistant used as a browser extension and Google Docs add-on; the company keeps a major engineering office in Kyiv.
notes: Least public of the three Grammarly co-founders; no own website or verified social accounts found. Web search budget ran out before checking his current role or a Superhuman press contact. Alive status assumed, no reports otherwise.

name: David B Blundin
current_role: Managing Partner, Link Ventures (Kendall Square, Cambridge MA); Chairman, EverQuote (NASDAQ: EVER); co-host of the Moonshots podcast
profile: Dave Blundin is an MIT-trained serial entrepreneur and investor who has co-founded about 23 companies. They include DataSage (sold to Vignette), Vestmark (wealth-management software), the Cogo Labs incubator, and EverQuote, which he has chaired since 2008. He now runs Link Ventures, an AI-focused fund backing MIT and Harvard founders, and teaches MIT's 'AI for Impact: Venture Studio' course.
interesting_fact: He co-hosts Peter Diamandis's Moonshots podcast and is on the XPRIZE Innovation Board. He has said he had been waiting for today's AI platform shift since he was 14.
deep_cut_fact: He studied AI at MIT starting in 1984, researching neural networks at the AI lab. He says he was quantizing neural networks as early as 1992, long before today's low-bit LLM inference. He has also discussed meeting Jeff Bezos and building personalization at Amazon in DataSage's early days.
notes: Highly relevant for an AI, compute and entrepreneurship podcast: he is an active podcaster and AI investor and a strong guest candidate. Best route is the Link Ventures 'Get in touch' form or the Moonshots/Diamandis team. EverQuote IR (investors.everquote.com) is a formal fallback.

name: Stelleo Tolda
current_role: Co-founder and board director (Audit Committee chair), MercadoLibre Inc. (NASDAQ: MELI)
profile: Rio de Janeiro-born Stelleo Tolda co-founded MercadoLibre with Marcos Galperin in 1999 and ran its Brazilian operation (Mercado Livre) from the start. He later served as COO and then President of Commerce, building Latin America's largest e-commerce marketplace. He stepped back from executive duties and since September 2024 has sat on MELI's board, chairing the audit committee since April 2025.
interesting_fact: He met Marcos Galperin in the US while working in New York finance (Merrill Lynch, Lehman Brothers) and helped launch MercadoLibre in Argentina and Brazil the same year, 1999. In 2001 eBay took a stake and formed a five-year alliance with the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he trained as an engineer: he studied mechanical engineering at Stanford, began a master's there, and worked at Silicon Valley tech firms such as Proxim Wireless. He then moved to Banco Icatu and Pactual in Rio.
notes: Now a non-executive director (Ariel Szarfsztejn became CEO on 1 Jan 2026). The deep-cut source is a Brazilian broker blog that also wrongly calls him CEO, so verify the engineering details against MELI proxy bios before use. Best route is MELI IR or a LinkedIn message.

name: Alan Wells
current_role: Founder (former owner) of Sauflon Pharmaceuticals; private investor since its 2014 sale. No current title found.
profile: Alan Wells, an optician in south-west London, founded contact-lens maker Sauflon Pharmaceuticals in 1985. The company grew factories in London, Kent, Southampton and Hungary and sold in 50+ countries, and in 2014 the family (with Bradley and David Wells) sold it to CooperVision for about £700m. The Sunday Times Rich List has since tracked the Wells family fortune.
interesting_fact: Sauflon's Southampton plant produced more than 100 million contact lenses a year. It was one of only four companies worldwide making both lenses and aftercare solutions, and it supplied chains such as Specsavers.
deep_cut_fact: Sauflon started from scratch in Twickenham selling only contact-lens aftercare solution. Wells moved into making lenses as they took off, and after silicone hydrogel lenses were invented in 1998 he added those too.
notes: Very private, with no website, social media or family office found. Not to be confused with racing driver or other Alan Wells. The web-search budget ran out mid-lane, so his post-2014 activities and alive status were not verified. Low podcast fit.

name: Dame Janet de Botton
current_role: Chairman of the Board, The Wolfson Foundation
profile: Janet Wolfson de Botton, eldest daughter of Lord (Leonard) Wolfson and granddaughter of GUS founder Sir Isaac Wolfson, is a London art collector and philanthropist. She was a Tate trustee and chair of the Tate Modern council, and has chaired the Wolfson Foundation since 2010. Her wealth is inherited plus that of her late husband, financier Gilbert de Botton (Global Asset Management).
interesting_fact: In 1996 she gave Tate 60 contemporary works, including Warhol, Cindy Sherman and Richard Long, and in 2010 she donated a Cy Twombly ceiling painting to the Louvre's Salle des Bronzes. She was made a Dame (DBE) in 2013.
deep_cut_fact: She is a serious competitive bridge player whose record appears in World Bridge Federation and European Bridge League results.
notes: Very private philanthropist. Best route is the Wolfson Foundation communications team. Contacts belong to the foundation, not her personally. The web-search budget ran out here, so the bridge detail is general rather than a specific title.

name: David Crossland
current_role: Jersey-based private investor; founder and former chairman of Airtours/MyTravel Group
profile: David Crossland (b. 1946), from east Lancashire, founded Airtours in 1972 by buying two small travel shops in Nelson, then built it into MyTravel, a global package-holiday group with its own charter airline, which merged with Thomas Cook AG in 2007. He now lives in Jersey and invests privately (travel and investment per the rich list).
interesting_fact: Airtours' first two shops (Pendle Travel Services, Nelson) were bought from an elderly couple, with half the money borrowed from his brother-in-law; Airtours later launched its own airline in 1990 and offered £299 Caribbean charters.
deep_cut_fact: He left Burnley Grammar School with three O-levels and his first job, in August 1963, was at the travel agency inside the Colne Co-operative Society's Colne Hall offices on Albert Road, where he learnt the trade.
notes: Private; no published personal/office contact found (web search budget ran out mid-lane, so current business interests were not re-verified). Alive status assumed from no death record on Wikipedia.

This link could not be confirmed from the list itself, and the co-listed 'Gabriella di Nora' could not be identified.

notes: Family entry, not an individual; identity of the family unconfirmed (assumed Sir Donald Gosling's heirs, who are private individuals). No public contact route. Probably not a fit for outreach.

name: Geoffrey Kent
current_role: Founder and Chairman Emeritus, Abercrombie & Kent (luxury travel group)
profile: Born in 1942 while his parents were on safari in what is now Zambia and raised in Kenya, Kent co-founded Abercrombie & Kent with his parents in 1962 while still in the British Army, pioneering the photographic (not hunting) luxury safari. He grew it into a global luxury and expedition travel group and, now in his 80s, still personally hosts A&K's flagship private-jet journeys (2026, 2027).
interesting_fact: He pioneered private-jet luxury touring with 'The Royal Air Tour' in 1989 using Concorde with British Airways, and as a polo player captained teams that won the US Open and played alongside King Charles III.
deep_cut_fact: At 16, after being expelled from school, he made a solo ~5,000-mile, two-month motorbike ride from Nairobi to Cape Town, credited as the first by motorcycle; he recounts it in his 2015 memoir 'Safari: A Memoir of a Worldwide Travel Pioneer'.

notes: Very media-friendly founder (memoirs, TV series, hosts trips). Also Honorary Consul of Kenya to Monaco. Best route: A&K global comms.

name: Iqbal Ahmed
current_role: Chairman and Chief Executive, Seamark Group (Manchester seafood processor/exporter)
profile: Bangladesh-born British entrepreneur (b. 1956, Sylhet) who moved to the UK at 15, joined his family's Oldham business and, with brothers Kamal and Bilal, built Seamark/Ibco into a major frozen-seafood importer, processor and catering supplier with a processing plant in Chittagong. The family also has interests in hotels, property and hospitality in Manchester.
interesting_fact: Known in the British-Bangladeshi community as 'Mr Shrimp' or 'King Prawn'; his brands include Mr Prawn, Lily, Classic and Tiger, and he was made an OBE in 2001 for services to international trade.
deep_cut_fact: In 2007 George Osborne invited him onto the New Enterprise Council think tank, and in 2012 he won the international category of EY's North region Entrepreneur of the Year awards.
notes: Family business; profile largely from older UK press. Seamark site did not return a contact page when checked. Wealth is family-held (brothers Kamal and Bilal).

name: Chris Miller
current_role: Co-owner, Harris & Sheldon Group (Meriden, property/investment/sporting estates); co-founder and former executive vice-chairman of Melrose Industries (stood down March 2024)
profile: Christopher Miller worked for Lord Hanson and was chief executive of engineering group Wassall before co-founding Melrose Industries in 2003 with David Roper and Simon Peckham; Melrose's 'buy, improve, sell' model culminated in the GKN takeover. With brother Michael he owns family group Harris & Sheldon, now focused on investments, property and sporting lets.

current_role: Chairman and CEO, National Energy Services Reunited Corp. (NESR, Nasdaq), Houston
profile: Egyptian-born oilfield-services executive who spent ~25 years at Schlumberger (SLB), rising to President of the Production Group and senior advisor to the chairman. In 2017 he started NESR as a SPAC, rolling up MENA oilfield-service firms into the region's largest Nasdaq-listed energy services company; NESR recently signed with Aramco on the region's first direct lithium extraction project.

name: Carl Ledbetter
current_role: Independent director, Cloudflare (since Nov 2009; chair of compensation committee); Chairman, CEO and CTO of SimpleRose, Inc.
profile: Dr. Carl Ledbetter (76) is a mathematician-turned-tech executive and VC. As a Managing Director of Pelion Venture Partners (2003-2018) he joined Cloudflare's board in November 2009, and his long-held stake is the source of his SEC-listed wealth. He has sat on four other public-company boards and 30+ private boards, and since 2018-19 leads SimpleRose, an optimization/mathematical-programming software company.
interesting_fact: He has been on Cloudflare's board since November 2009, one of its longest-serving directors, and is designated an 'audit committee financial expert'.
deep_cut_fact: He is a career mathematician: B.S. in Mathematics from the University of Redlands, M.S. from Brandeis and a Ph.D. in Mathematics from Clark University. Fittingly, his current company SimpleRose sells optimization software for supply-chain, scheduling and even sports scheduling.
notes: Low public profile; best routes are via SimpleRose (his own company, website contact page) or Cloudflare's press office (company-level). Wealth figure is from SEC insider holdings of Cloudflare stock.

profile: Hurun India (2018-2019) listed Jyotsna Ramesh Shah (Mumbai) with INR 1,300-2,100 crore from Fine Organic Industries, the oleochemical-additives maker founded in 1970 by Mumbai chemical trader Ramesh Shah and ICT-trained technocrat Prakash Kamat. name: Ramprakash V Bubna
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Sharda Cropchem Ltd (NSE/BSE listed, Mumbai)
profile: IIT Bombay-trained chemical engineer who founded Sharda International in 1987, growing it into Sharda Cropchem, a global generic agrochemicals company. Its asset-light model centres on preparing dossiers and winning product registrations in high-barrier markets (Europe, US, LATAM), then selling formulations via distributors and its own sales forces.
interesting_fact: Sharda Cropchem does not need to own big factories: its core competence is regulatory, compiling registration dossiers for off-patent fungicides, herbicides and insecticides and sourcing from a global supplier network; it also sells conveyor belts and V-belts.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as two sole proprietorships, Sharda International (1987) and Bubna Enterprises (1989), exporting dyes, dye intermediates, pesticides and V-belts, before being rolled into Sharda Worldwide Exports in 2004 and renamed Sharda Cropchem in 2013 ahead of its IPO.
notes: Agrochemicals, not energy, so a weak fit for the podcast theme. Company secretary Jetkin Gudhka handles investor contact. Low media profile; no personal accounts found.

name: Song Dianquan
current_role: Founder & chairman, Coslight Technology International Group (光宇国际; ex-HKEX 1043) / Harbin Coslight group (batteries, power supplies)
profile: Song Dianquan (宋殿权), a Harbin Institute of Technology electrochemical engineer, founded the Coslight battery group in Harbin in 1994 (with Li Kexue), making lead-acid and lithium batteries and power products for telecom, power and EV markets. He chaired HK-listed Coslight Technology until its 2022 delisting; Hurun-listed 2001-2010.

He joined Diversified Energy's board as a director tied to EIG funds that received DEC shares when Diversified bought EIG-backed Maverick Natural Resources in 2025. name: Vincent D Foster
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Main Street Capital Corp (NYSE: MAIN), Houston; founding director of Quanta Services 1998-2025
profile: Vince Foster, a CPA and former Arthur Andersen partner who ran its Southwest corporate-finance/M&A practice, co-founded the Main Street predecessor funds in 1997; they co-founded Quanta Services, now the leading builder of grid and power infrastructure. He was Main Street's CEO 2007-2018 and has chaired its board since 2007, after 27 years on Quanta's board.
interesting_fact: Main Street's predecessor funds co-founded Quanta Services (NYSE: PWR), the specialty contractor that has become a key builder of transmission lines and power infrastructure for the AI data-center boom; Foster sat on its board from its 1998 IPO until 2025.
deep_cut_fact: At Arthur Andersen he specialised in 'roll-ups' - companies consolidating fragmented industries - the playbook behind Quanta; he was a founding director of the Texas TriCities chapter of the National Association of Corporate Directors and won EY Entrepreneur of the Year 2008 (Houston, financial services). He holds a JD from Wayne State.
notes: Main Street publishes his direct work email on its board page - the best route. Strong podcast angle: the origin story of Quanta Services, now central to US grid and data-center power build-out. Michigan State BBA.

name: Brian E. Lane
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX); Director, Main Street Capital (NYSE: MAIN)
profile: Brian Lane has been CEO of Houston-based Comfort Systems USA, a large US mechanical and electrical contractor, since December 2011, after joining in 2003 and rising through regional operations to COO. Under him the company became a major builder of data-center and semiconductor-fab HVAC/electrical systems, with technology work reaching ~45% of 2025 revenue and backlog near $12bn.
interesting_fact: Comfort Systems' technology segment (mostly data centers) grew from about a third of revenue in 2024 to roughly 45% in 2025, making it one of the biggest picks-and-shovels winners of the AI build-out.
deep_cut_fact: A chemistry graduate of Notre Dame, Lane spent 15 years at Halliburton (leaving as Regional Director, Europe & Africa) and was also a Regional Director at Capstone Turbine, the microturbine distributed-power maker - real on-site power experience now relevant to data centers.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast. Gave up the President title in Dec 2025 (remains CEO) - possible succession planning. Corporate general inbox is the published route; IR is handled by the CFO's office.

name: Martin Tuchman
current_role: CEO, The Tuchman Group / Kingstone Capital V; director of FTAI Aviation and Princeton Bancorp; chair of the Tuchman Foundation
profile: Martin 'Marty' Tuchman (NJIT '62, Seton Hall MBA '68) co-founded the container lessor Interpool in 1968 and later the chassis lessor Trac Lease. Interpool listed on the NYSE in 1993 and was sold to Fortress in 2007 for about $797M. He now runs the Tuchman Group (real estate, banking, shipping) and Kingstone Capital V, sits on the FTAI Aviation board and is a large Princeton Bancorp holder.
interesting_fact: NJIT's business school, the Martin Tuchman School of Management, is named after him. As an engineer at Railway Express Agency he helped create the intermodal container and chassis standard that lets boxes move between rail, truck and ship, and it is still in use.
deep_cut_fact: At 25 he was on the Railway Express Agency team that developed the container twist lock. He got the idea for Interpool while on vacation in Bermuda, seeing containers chained to chassis, and later said of the container business: 'This isn't rocket science, it's a hole.'

public_contacts.value: See FTAI Aviation investor relations (board-member page)

Central Jersey reports he long owned Princeton's PJ's Pancake House (https://archive.centraljersey.com/?p=684317). I could not open that article to verify it. Avoid opening with his Parkinson's philanthropy unless it is relevant. I found no direct email; best route is the Tuchman Group office or FTAI IR.

name: Carl M. Eschenbach
current_role: Former CEO of Workday (2022-2026; co-founder Aneel Bhusri is CEO again); director of Palo Alto Networks per SEC filings
profile: Carl Eschenbach is a veteran enterprise-software operator. After sales roles at 3Com, Lucent, Inktomi and EMC, he spent 14 years at VMware (2002-16), rising to President and COO. He then became a partner at Sequoia Capital, joined Workday's board in 2018, was named co-CEO in Dec 2022 and sole CEO in Feb 2024. name: Daniel S Shugar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nextpower Inc. (Nasdaq: NXT; formerly Nextracker)
profile: Solar pioneer who co-founded PowerLight (sold to SunPower for $332M in 2007; he became SunPower president), then co-founded Nextracker in 2013 as its CEO. It became the top utility-scale solar tracker maker, IPO'd in 2023 and rebranded as Nextpower in 2025, adding power conversion and battery storage.
interesting_fact: Under Shugar the company had shipped trackers for 100+ GW of solar capacity in 40 countries by 2024, and in Dec 2024 shipped the first US-made solar trackers with 100% domestic content after reshoring manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: An RPI electrical-engineering grad from New Jersey, he started in the late 1980s in PG&E's R&D department; in 2023 the American Solar Energy Society gave him its Hoyt Clarke Hottel Award, and S&P Global Platts named him Chief Trailblazer of the Year.
notes: Very media-friendly CEO and frequent conference speaker; excellent fit for an energy podcast. Pitch via media@nextpower.com (global media contact Brandy Lee).

name: Mark Allen McFarland
current_role: President and CEO, Talen Energy Corp. (NASDAQ: TLN) since May 2023; Director, California Resources Corp.
profile: Known as 'Mac', a veteran power-industry executive who has run Luminant (2013-16), GenOn Energy (2017-18) and California Resources Corp. (2020-23) before taking over Talen Energy. At Talen he pivoted the independent power producer toward data centers, selling the Cumulus campus beside the Susquehanna nuclear plant to AWS and signing a large nuclear power deal with Amazon.

deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer: a B.S. in Civil Engineering with an environmental concentration from Virginia Tech (plus an MBA from the University of Delaware), and spent 1999-2008 at Exelon, rising to SVP of Corporate Development.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast (nuclear + hyperscaler deals). Media contact is Talen's Director of Corporate Communications as listed in 2026 press releases.

current_role: Co-founder and Executive Deputy Chairman, The Raven Property Group (formerly Raven Russia); non-executive Chairman, Sabina Estates (Ibiza)
profile: Anton Bilton is a third-generation British property developer who co-founded Raven Russia (now The Raven Property Group), which built a large portfolio of Russian logistics warehouses, and has founded three other AIM-floated companies. Raven's Russian warehouse business is a sensitive topic post-2022; the Raven role on his site may be dated. Do not confuse with the unrelated US 'RAVEN Property Group' (Pacific Northwest).

profile: Charles Innes-Ker (b. 1981), the 11th Duke, succeeded his father Guy, the 10th Duke, in August 2019. Educated at Eton, Newcastle University and Sandhurst, he served as a captain in the Blues and Royals, including in Iraq, and now runs the family estate business.

Mehta, has run Deepak Fertilisers since the 2010s (chairman since 2012/13), steering it from commodity fertilisers and chemicals toward ammonia self-sufficiency (a new greenfield ammonia plant), technical ammonium nitrate for mining, and branded crop nutrition.
