current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Corporación Inmobiliaria Vesta (Vesta Real Estate Corp., BMV/NYSE: VTMX)
profile: Lorenzo Berho Corona co-founded Vesta in 1998, a Mexican developer and owner of industrial parks and build-to-suit logistics facilities. He chairs the board while his son Lorenzo Dominique Berho Carranza is CEO (since 2018). Vesta listed on the NYSE in 2023 and is riding nearshoring demand in Mexico.
interesting_fact: Vesta debuted on the New York Stock Exchange in 2023 and accelerated a US$1.1bn development pipeline to finish two years early because of nearshoring demand.
notes: Do not confuse with son Lorenzo Berho Carranza (Vesta CEO). Aggregator profiles say he led the Mexican industrial parks association AMPIP (2007-09) and chaired YPO's real estate network, but I did not verify these from primary sources. Best route: Vesta IR.

name: Travis Murdoch
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Braveheart Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: BRVE)
profile: Canadian physician-scientist and biotech founder. He co-founded and ran Human Immunology Biosciences (HI-Bio), sold to Biogen in 2024 for $1.15B upfront plus up to $650M in milestones. He now leads Braveheart Bio, a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy company that launched with a $185M Series A in Nov 2025 and listed on Nasdaq in 2026.
interesting_fact: Biogen acquired his first company, HI-Bio, for $1.15B in cash upfront (plus up to $650M in milestones) in 2024, mainly for the antibody felzartamab.
deep_cut_fact: At 16, as a high-school student in an AHFMR Heritage Youth Researcher summer program, he joined the University of Alberta's clinical islet transplantation team (the Edmonton Protocol group). He won the Governor General's medal in 2002 and a 2008 ASTech 'Leaders of Tomorrow' award as a Rhodes Scholar at Oxford.

public_contacts.value: FGS Global (media contact for Braveheart Bio)

notes: Biotech (cardiology), not energy. Best route is the company's media contact at FGS Global.

name: Mike F Chang
current_role: Founder, Chairman of the Board and EVP of Strategic Initiatives, Alpha and Omega Semiconductor (Nasdaq: AOSL)
profile: Mike F. Chang, Ph.D. (81) founded power-semiconductor maker Alpha and Omega Semiconductor in 2000 after a career at General Electric (1974-87) and Siliconix, where he rose to EVP. AOS designs power MOSFETs, IGBTs and power ICs and runs its own fabs; he led it as CEO through its 2010 Nasdaq IPO and in 2023 handed the CEO role to Stephen C. Chang, staying on as chairman. He is a 10%+ holder.
interesting_fact: Before founding AOS he spent 13 years in product R&D management at General Electric and then 13 years at Siliconix (a Vishay subsidiary), ending as Executive VP - over 25 years in power semiconductors before starting his own company at about 55.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his B.S. in electrical engineering at National Cheng Kung University in Taiwan, then an M.S. and Ph.D. in electrical engineering at the University of Missouri before joining GE's R&D ranks in 1974.

public_contacts.value: The Blueshirt Group (AOS investor relations) - Steven Pelayo, steven@blueshirtgroup.co

notes: Low media profile; the company's public face is now CEO Stephen C. Chang. Route via AOS IR (Blueshirt Group). Avoid family topics.

name: John F.W. Rogers
current_role: Executive Vice President and Secretary to the Board, Goldman Sachs; Management Committee member; chairman, Goldman Sachs Foundation
profile: Long-serving Goldman Sachs insider who joined in 1994 (partner 2000) and was chief of staff to CEOs Corzine, Paulson, Blankfein and Solomon. Earlier a Reagan White House aide, Assistant Treasury Secretary (1985-87) and Under Secretary of State for Management under George H.W. Bush. Wealth is from Goldman equity; he keeps a deliberately low public profile.
interesting_fact: Joined the Reagan White House staff at 27 and later followed James Baker to Treasury; he has been a life trustee and treasurer of the Ronald Reagan Presidential Foundation and chaired the Atlantic Council board.
deep_cut_fact: Before government he was a research assistant to David Gergen and to Fed chairman Arthur F. Burns; in 2020 he received the ICAA's Arthur Ross Award (patronage category) for supporting classical architecture and historic preservation.
notes: Famously private and dislikes being photographed (per NYT profile cited on Wikipedia); route via Goldman media relations. Strong interest in historic preservation (White House Historical Association vice chair, American Academy in Rome).

name: Michelangelo Volpi
current_role: General Partner, Hanabi Capital (co-founded 2025); director of Confluent, Aurora Innovation, Wealthfront and Ferrari N.V.
profile: Milan-born, Tokyo-raised Stanford engineer who became Cisco's chief strategy officer, leading 70+ acquisitions and running its $10B+ routing business. Briefly CEO of Joost, then built Index Ventures' San Francisco office (2009-2024), backing Confluent, Elastic, Scale AI, Aurora and Wealthfront. Now invests in AI/infra via Hanabi Capital.
interesting_fact: As Cisco's M&A chief in the late 1990s he did 70+ acquisitions in under five years; the NYT dubbed him 'The Cisco Whiz Kid' and MIT Technology Review named him an Innovator Under 35 in 1999.
deep_cut_fact: He moved to Japan at age 5-6, attended a Roman Catholic boys' school in Tokyo and is trilingual (Italian, Japanese, English); he started his career in HP's optoelectronics division in 1989 before his Stanford MBA.
notes: Hanabi deploys largely his own capital; AI/infrastructure focus and Aurora (autonomous trucking) board seat make him relevant to data-center/energy themes. Has done podcasts (Uncapped with Jack Altman #52, Microsoft Behind the Tech).

name: James R. Scott Jr
current_role: Director, First Interstate BancSystem (since May 2025); Managing General Partner, JS Investments LP
profile: James R. Scott Jr. (48) is a member of the Scott family that founded First Interstate Bank and remains a major holder under the Scott Family Stockholder Agreement. A career banker, he worked at Citywide Banks in Denver and then in First Interstate's commercial banking in Missoula, Ashland (OR) and Denver before rejoining the board in 2025 (he also served 2016-2022).
interesting_fact: First Interstate traces to 1968, when founder Homer Scott Sr. bought the Bank of Commerce in Sheridan, Wyoming; the company is now a multi-state regional bank still anchored by the Scott family.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than starting at the top, he worked through the family bank's commercial lending ranks: VP in Missoula (2014-17), Commercial Loan Manager in Ashland, Oregon (2017-19), and Commercial Group Manager in Denver from 2022. He also sits on the Padlock Ranch Company board.
notes: The email belongs to First Interstate's corporate secretary, Kirk D. Jensen, and is published in the 2026 proxy for shareholder questions. It is not a direct line to Scott. He is a low-profile director with no personal public channels found. Holds degrees from CU Boulder (Leeds) and the University of Denver (MBA and MS Finance). He is a director of the Homer and Mildred Scott Foundation.

name: Wallace Chiachang Kou
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Silicon Motion Technology (NASDAQ: SIMO)
profile: Taiwanese-American engineer who founded Silicon Motion in May 1995 after senior engineering roles at Western Digital (VP/Chief Architect, multimedia products). He built it into the world's largest merchant NAND flash controller maker (SSD, eMMC/UFS controllers), and still runs it, now pushing into AI/data-center SSD controllers.
interesting_fact: Silicon Motion describes itself as the world's largest NAND flash controller vendor; its controllers sit inside a large share of the world's SSDs and memory cards.
deep_cut_fact: Kou earned his MS in electrical & computer engineering at UC Santa Barbara (1983-85); despite a weak chip market he got 20+ job offers and credits a UCSB course where students fabricated and tested real silicon. His advice to young engineers: "Don't hesitate."
notes: Low public profile; best route via Silicon Motion corporate communications (Minnie Lin) or IR. Company is relevant to AI data-center storage angle.

name: Reed McGinley-Stempel
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Stytch (now a Twilio subsidiary)
profile: Co-founded passwordless authentication company Stytch in 2020 with Julianna Lamb after both worked at Plaid; Stytch became a unicorn and grew into a B2C/B2B identity platform for humans and AI agents. Twilio announced its acquisition of Stytch on Oct 30, 2025; the deal closed in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Twilio bought Stytch in late 2025 to build an 'intelligent identity layer' for agentic AI; Stytch's changelog confirms Twilio is now its parent company.
deep_cut_fact: He and Julianna Lamb met at Plaid working on bank-account authentication, where they saw how much engineering time went into auth flows that were never the product; Stytch launched with just email magic links.
notes: Hurun unicorn-founder identity (Stytch) is clear, but the SEC link to Omega Flex (OFLX) as director/10% owner could not be verified (EDGAR full-text search shows no filings under his name; Omega Flex's major holders are the Reed family). Likely a record-merge error; the net worth figure tied to OFLX may not be his.

name: John Fichthorn
current_role: Co-Founder & Managing Partner, Dialectic Capital Management (Norwalk, CT); Director, Quantum Corp (QMCO) since April 2025
profile: Investment manager with 25+ years as a public-equities analyst and activist investor; co-founded Dialectic Capital Management in 2003 and relaunched it in May 2020. In April 2025 Dialectic bought all $51M of Quantum's term debt from Blue Torch and Fichthorn rejoined Quantum's board (he previously served 2019-2021).
interesting_fact: Dialectic became Quantum's strategic lender by buying its entire $51M term loan; Fichthorn said 'providing capital to solve balance sheet constraints can unlock growth' and that Quantum had revamped its portfolio 'to address every stage of the data lifecycle'.
deep_cut_fact: This is his second stint on Quantum's board: he first served as a director from April 2019 to July 2021, before returning in April 2025 alongside the Dialectic debt purchase.
notes: Low public profile; little personal bio published. Don't confuse with Dialectic (Zug crypto firm of Ryan Zurrer). Best route is via Dialectic Capital's website; Quantum IR is a fallback for the director role. Quantum is a data-storage company (relevant to data-center angle).

name: Gregory Garrabrants
current_role: President and CEO, Axos Financial, Inc. (NYSE: AX) and Axos Bank
profile: Greg Garrabrants has run Axos Financial (formerly BofI Holding / Bank of Internet USA) since October 2007, turning a small online thrift into a diversified, digital-first bank and financial services group with consumer and commercial banking, brokerage and advisory arms. His wealth comes from his Axos equity.
interesting_fact: Axos says that under his leadership total bank assets grew to about $24.8 billion and market value rose more than 30-fold; he describes it as: 'We didn't transform traditional banking. We created something new, built for the future.'
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he trained as an engineer and lawyer: a USC industrial and systems engineering graduate with a Northwestern JD and Kellogg MBA, he clerked for a federal judge and is a CFA charterholder and member of the California Bar, with stints at Deloitte, Goldman Sachs and McKinsey.

public_contacts.value: jlai@axosfinancial.com (Johnny Lai, SVP Corporate Development & IR; also listed as media contact)

notes: Axos's exec bio links to his LinkedIn. Company press/IR route goes through Johnny Lai (some 2026 releases list jlai@axosbank.com instead). Gives regular CEO interviews to The Wall Street Transcript.

name: Kevin P Clark
current_role: Chair and CEO, Aptiv PLC; director of Versigent PLC and UPS
profile: Finance executive who joined Delphi as CFO in 2010, became COO in 2014 and CEO in March 2015, steering Delphi's 2017 split into Aptiv and Delphi Technologies; chair since 2022. In April 2026 he completed the spin-off of Aptiv's Electrical Distribution Systems unit as Versigent (NYSE: VGNT), refocusing Aptiv on software, sensing and electrification.
interesting_fact: Under Clark, Aptiv spun off its wiring-harness business as Versigent on April 1, 2026 (one VGNT share per three APTV shares), his second major break-up of the former Delphi after the 2017 Aptiv/Delphi Technologies split.
deep_cut_fact: Before Delphi he was Fisher Scientific's CFO from its 2001 IPO through the 2006 Thermo Electron merger, then a founding partner of middle-market private-equity firm Liberty Lane Partners; he began his career in Chrysler's finance organization and holds two Michigan State degrees.
notes: Sitting public-company CEO; route via Aptiv corporate communications. Aptiv's electrification/high-voltage and data-center-adjacent electronics are possible podcast angles.

name: William Heard
current_role: Founder, CEO & CIO of Heard Capital LLC (Chicago); independent director of Anterix Inc. (ATEX) since 2024
profile: William E. Heard founded Chicago hedge fund Heard Capital around 2010-11 while in his twenties, after working as a special situations analyst at Stark Investments. The fund runs a concentrated ~20-stock book in tech, media, telecom, financials and industrials and became a major Anterix shareholder (~9.4% in 2024), leading to his board seat at the 900 MHz utility private-LTE spectrum company.
interesting_fact: Named to Fortune's 2020 40 Under 40 in Finance: Heard Capital grew from $35M to over $250M in two years, backed by the Teacher Retirement System of Texas and Vista Equity founder Robert F. Smith.
deep_cut_fact: During the pandemic he told Fortune he had started tracking a new metric: video calls were generating 'a meaningful return on time.'
notes: Anterix is highly relevant to energy/grid podcast (private LTE for utilities). Also sits on City Year Chicago board. IR email is Anterix VP IR Natasha Vecchiarelli (company contact, not his). Heard Capital site is behind Cloudflare; no published direct contact found.

name: Kent P Dauten
current_role: Chairman and co-founder, Keystone Capital (Chicago); independent director, Iron Mountain (since 1997)
profile: Chicago private equity investor who began at First Chicago Venture Capital in 1979 and co-founded Madison Dearborn Partners. In 1994 he co-founded Keystone Capital; its first company, a medical records business he ran, was built via ~a dozen acquisitions and merged into Iron Mountain, where he has been a director since.
interesting_fact: He personally ran Keystone's first portfolio company, a healthcare records management firm (Record Masters), rolling up about a dozen acquisitions before merging it into Iron Mountain and briefly running its Health Care Division.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond finance he chaired the board of Chicago's Museum of Science and Industry, chaired Lutheran Social Services of Illinois, and served as an elected member and president of his local school district board.
notes: kdauten@ address was listed as media/contact in Keystone's own 2021 Fund II press release (Business Wire); could not re-fetch page (403) to reconfirm. Active Milken Institute participant (brain health).

name: Gary Hromadko
current_role: Independent Director, Equinix Inc. (since June 2003); private investor
profile: Silicon Valley investor (age 73) who has sat on the board of Equinix, the world's largest data-center/interconnection REIT, since June 2003. He was a venture partner at Crosslink Capital (2002-2017), has been a private investor since 1993, and formerly served on the board of Carbonite; his wealth comes largely from long-held Equinix stock.
interesting_fact: He is Equinix's longest-tenured current director, joining in 2003 when it was a post-dotcom recovery story; in 2025 he chaired both the Finance Committee and the Real Estate Committee overseeing data-center development capital spending.
deep_cut_fact: In March 2026 Equinix created a new board Technology and Strategy Committee to assess emerging technologies and digital-infrastructure trends, and Hromadko was named one of its four founding members.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Equinix's proxy says interested parties may write to the Board c/o the Corporate Secretary, Equinix Inc., One Lagoon Drive, Redwood City, CA 94065 (corporate address, not personal). Good fit for data-center episode as a 20+ year insider of the sector's bellwether.

name: Randall J Weisenburger
current_role: Managing Member, Mile 26 Capital LLC; Presiding Director and Senior Independent Director, Carnival Corp & plc; director of Valero Energy, MP Materials and Corsair Gaming
profile: Finance executive (age 67) who was EVP and CFO of advertising giant Omnicom Group from 1998 to 2014, after a decade (1988-98) as a founding member of boutique bank Wasserstein Perella, where he ran its merchant-banking arm Wasserstein & Co. Since 2014 he has run private investment firm Mile 26 Capital and serves on major public boards, including Valero (since 2011) and rare-earths producer MP Materials (since 2020).
interesting_fact: He has served on Carnival's boards since 2009 and is now its Presiding Director and chair of the compensation committee, while also sitting on the boards of refiner Valero Energy (since 2011) and rare-earths producer MP Materials (since 2020).
deep_cut_fact: In 1988 he was a founding member of Bruce Wasserstein and Joseph Perella's boutique investment bank Wasserstein Perella, serving as president and CEO of its merchant-banking subsidiary Wasserstein & Co. and as an executive of several of its portfolio companies before joining Omnicom.
notes: Very private board-level investor; no personal website, social accounts or Mile 26 Capital contact found. Only published route: letters to Carnival directors via Carnival Corporation & plc, Attention: Company Secretary, 3655 N.W. 87th Avenue, Miami, FL 33178 (per 2026 proxy). Valero/MP Materials board seats give energy/critical-minerals angle.

name: Padmakar Haribhau Mulay
current_role: Chairman, Ajeet Seeds Pvt. Ltd. (PM Group), Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (Aurangabad), Maharashtra
profile: Padmakar Mulay founded Ajeet Seeds in Aurangabad in 1986 and built it into a hybrid-seed company covering 22 crops. It is the flagship of the PM Group, which also includes construction (Gangamai Industries & Construction), sugar and other seed businesses. His son Sameer Mulay runs it day to day as managing director.
interesting_fact: Ajeet Seeds' first big hit was the Ajeet-11 cotton hybrid, launched in 1992. The company says it was the first private seed company in India to introduce a proprietary wheat variety, Ajeet-102.
deep_cut_fact: Ajeet Seeds set up its own Plant Biotechnology Research Center in Hanumantgaon (Gangapur taluka) in 2003. Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University recognises it as a research centre, and it launched three Bt cotton hybrids in kharif 2006.
notes: Elder founder. A Feb 2025 Lokmat obituary of his brother lists him (as Padmakarrao Mulay) among the surviving brothers. MD Sameer Mulay is the public face of the company. The email is the company's general address, and the X account belongs to the company, not to him personally.

name: Gautam N Mehra
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Savita Oil Technologies Ltd (re-appointed MD to Sept 2028)
profile: Chemical engineer with a UC Berkeley MBA, Gautam N. Mehra leads Savita Oil Technologies, the Mumbai petroleum-specialties firm his father N.K. Mehra co-founded in 1961. Savita leads India in transformer oils, white oils and waxes, sells in 75+ countries, owns wind farms, and now markets data-center immersion-cooling and BESS fluids.
interesting_fact: Savita says it set up India's first private-sector R&D centre in the petroleum industry, was the first Indian private petroleum company to earn ISO 9001, and commissioned its first windmill in Maharashtra around 1999-2002 - an early oil-company move into renewables.
deep_cut_fact: Savita began in 1961 at Sakinaka, Mumbai, making liquid paraffin as an import substitute; in his chairman's message Mehra says founder N.K. Mehra 'drew inspiration from the sun' and coined the company motto 'Bonds Build Businesses'.
notes: legal@savita.com is the published registered-office (Nariman Point) email, likely routed via company secretary. Good podcast angle: Savita now sells 'Data Center Fluids' (immersion cooling) and transformer oils for grid/BESS.

name: Vijay Sankeshwar
current_role: Founder & Chairman, VRL Logistics / VRL Group (Hubballi, Karnataka)
profile: Born 1950 in Gadag, Karnataka. He started a cargo business in 1976 with one truck and built VRL Logistics into one of India's largest commercial-vehicle fleet owners. He also founded the Kannada newspaper Vijaya Karnataka (sold to the Times Group in 2007) and later Vijaya Vani, and was a BJP MP for Dharwad North. He is chairman, and his son Anand runs VRL as MD.
interesting_fact: His life story, from a single truck to India's largest logistics fleet, became the 2022 multilingual biopic 'Vijayanand'. He received the Padma Shri in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1976 with one truck bought on a Rs 2 lakh loan and took heavy early losses from accidents and competition. In 1978 the family moved to Hubballi and added three more trucks. His father ran a printing press, B G Sankeshwar & Co., in Gadag.
notes: Both emails appear in VRL's FY2025-26 BRSR filing on NSE. The filing also lists the Company Secretary, Aniruddha Phadnavis (aniruddha@vrllogistics.com), as compliance contact. Better known in Karnataka media and politics. Family-owned Kannada media (Vijaya Vani, Digvijay 24x7) are another route.

name: KP Ramasamy
current_role: Founder and Chairman, KPR Mill Ltd and KPR Group (Coimbatore, India)
profile: Born into a farming family in Kalliampudur village, Erode district, he started as a power-loom cloth maker in 1971 and, with his brothers, built KPR Mill into one of India's largest vertically integrated apparel makers, with sugar, ethanol, power and education arms. He still chairs the group and appears on Forbes India's rich lists.
interesting_fact: KPR Mill runs an in-house higher-education program for its mostly rural women workers. The company says about 27,000 employees have earned degrees (computing, management, nursing, teaching) while working there, through tie-ups with Annamalai, Alagappa and Tamil Nadu Open universities.
deep_cut_fact: He started his first power-loom business in 1971 with a borrowed Rs 8,000, which some profiles say came from his mother's uncle.
notes: Also appears as Palanisamy Ramasamy Kalliampudur on data sites. The published email is the company's investor-grievance address, not a press line, so the corporate office in Coimbatore is the realistic route. The group also has an energy angle: windmill/solar and sugar-ethanol cogeneration.

name: KPD Sigamani
current_role: Managing Director and promoter, K.P.R. Mill Ltd (Coimbatore); heads the apparel division
profile: KPD Sigamani is a founding promoter of the KPR Group, the Coimbatore textile conglomerate begun by K.P. Ramasamy as a power-loom business in 1971. As MD of K.P.R. Mill he runs the export-focused apparel division of a yarn-to-garment maker that also has sugar, ethanol, wind and solar power. Re-appointed MD in 2025.
interesting_fact: KPR Mill runs a long-running in-factory education programme (since 1998) that lets its mostly women workers earn school-level, degree, vocational and nursing qualifications while employed; tens of thousands have completed courses.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mathematician: the group describes him as a postgraduate in mathematics, and he is credited with a major role in project execution for KPR's expansions.
notes: The published email is KPR Mill's investor grievance-redressal address (company secretary), not a personal contact. Chairman K.P. Ramasamy is the group's public face; Sigamani gives few interviews.

name: P Nataraj
current_role: Managing Director, K.P.R. Mill Limited (Coimbatore)
profile: Science graduate and Chartered Accountant, one of three brothers (with founder K.P. Ramasamy and K.P.D. Sigamani) behind KPR Mill, one of India's largest vertically integrated textile/apparel makers. As MD he oversees finance, cotton procurement and yarn marketing, and fronts the company's earnings calls.
interesting_fact: KPR began in 1984 as a small textile business, started exporting fashion apparel in 1989, and opened its first spinning unit at Sathyamangalam in 1995 with just 6,000 spindles.
deep_cut_fact: Despite being a CA, Nataraj's remit at KPR has long included the hands-on job of cotton procurement and yarn marketing, not just finance.
notes: Low public profile; route via company secretary/IR. Family also runs KPR Institute of Engineering and Technology trust.

name: Ajay Relan
current_role: Managing Director, Sharda Motor Industries Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Ajay Relan is Managing Director of Sharda Motor Industries, an Indian auto-components maker (exhaust/emission-control systems, suspension) founded by the Relan family. He oversees manufacturing, plants, R&D and product development; wealth is shared with family member Rohit Relan.
interesting_fact: Holds a B.Com (Hons.) and completed Harvard Business School's three-year Owner/President Management (OPM) programme.
notes: Family-run listed company; best route is via company IR/contact page. Auto-components angle rather than energy/data centers (emissions tech).

A chartered accountant, he has run engineering companies since 1986 and leads Bharat Seats, a seating-systems JV of Suzuki Motor Corp, Maruti Suzuki and the Relan family, which recently opened a Gujarat plant.
interesting_fact: Bharat Seats is a joint venture of Suzuki Motor Corporation Japan, Maruti Suzuki India and 'Rohit Relan and Associates', making seats for cars, two-wheelers and even railways.

name: Sanjeev Kumar Bijli
current_role: Executive Director, PVR INOX Limited (India's largest multiplex chain)
profile: Sanjeev Kumar Bijli co-founded PVR with his brother Ajay in 1995 as a joint venture between the family's Priya Cinemas and Australia's Village Roadshow, pioneering India's multiplex era. Long-time Joint MD, he oversees programming, Hollywood studio relationships and the PVR Pictures distribution arm; since the 2023 PVR-INOX merger he is Executive Director of PVR INOX.

name: Vidya Rashesh Shah
current_role: Executive Chairperson, EdelGive Foundation; Non-Executive Director, Edelweiss Financial Services
profile: Co-founding figure of India's Edelweiss financial group, where she was earlier CFO, after 11 years in investment banking (ICICI, Peregrine, NM Rothschild). In 2008 she founded EdelGive Foundation, Edelweiss's philanthropy arm, which she ran as CEO until 2021 and now chairs, building collaboratives in education, women's empowerment, climate and migration.

name: Bharat H Parajia
current_role: Co-promoter / significant shareholder of the IIFL group (IIFL Finance, IIFL Securities, 5paisa); Singapore-based
profile: Bharat Himatlal Parajia is a Singapore-based investor and part of the promoter group of India's IIFL (India Infoline) financial-services group, previously listed as a managing director of IIFL Asia. Third-party filings data show stakes of ~4.4% in IIFL Finance, ~3.6% in IIFL Securities and ~2% in 5paisa Capital (2023).
interesting_fact: Holds stakes across three listed IIFL-family companies (IIFL Finance, IIFL Securities and online broker 5paisa Capital).
notes: Low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Best route is likely via IIFL group corporate communications. Alive status not confirmed by a recent public source.

name: Rajvi H Mariwala
current_role: Director, Mariwala Health Initiative (mental-health grant-maker); member of the Marico promoter family
profile: Rajvi (Raj) Mariwala is the daughter of Marico founder-chairman Harsh Mariwala and part of the promoter family behind the Parachute/Saffola consumer-goods group. In 2015 she co-founded with her father the Mariwala Health Initiative, which funds rights-based, community-led mental-health work across India; she also advocates for animal rights.
interesting_fact: Under her leadership MHI shifted to a psychosocial, 'nothing about us, without us' funding model; per Fortune India it partnered with 33 NGOs on 37 projects in 20 states over seven years.
deep_cut_fact: She describes philanthropy as 'an exercise in redistribution of wealth' and says MHI blended her father's focus on service-delivery innovation with her own rights-and-agency approach; early partners included iCALL counselling and the Bapu Trust in Pune bastis.
notes: Goes by 'Raj Mariwala' professionally. Best route is via MHI comms. Her public focus is mental health/queer-affirmative and animal advocacy rather than business, so podcast fit is indirect.

name: Prava Ranjan Patnaik
current_role: Managing Director, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (per company-registry aggregators, DIN 00417793); also director of Falcon Holdings, Falcon Finance and Falcon Real Estate
profile: Prava Ranjan Patnaik is listed as managing director of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar, Odisha-based shrimp/seafood exporter, and of other Falcon Group companies. The group was founded in 1985 by Tara Ranjan Patnaik and grew into one of India's largest shrimp exporters, using thousands of contract farms. It later added real estate and other businesses.
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports' promoters (the Patnaik family) appeared in the 2024 Hurun India Rich List at about Rs 4,900 crore. The company won MPEDA's award as India's highest-value seafood exporter over 15 years (2017).
notes: Almost all press covers group founder Tara Ranjan Patnaik and his son Parthajeet; Prava's exact relationship to them (likely a family member) is not confirmed in sources found. Very low public profile. No official website or published contact found; outreach via Falcon Group HQ (Falcon House, Bhubaneswar) or the Tara/Parthajeet Patnaik side is likely the best route.

name: R Lakshmanan
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Shanthi Feeds (Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu)
profile: Founded Shanthi Feeds in 1988 as a small poultry farm in Pappampatti, near Coimbatore; it grew into an integrated broiler business (hatcheries, poultry and cattle feed mills, processing, soya/corn cultivation) with capacity of ~47 million birds a year, and also runs wind energy projects.
interesting_fact: Shanthi Feeds has set up more than 1,000 contract broiler farms over 30 years and in 2019 commissioned a Petersime single-stage hatchery able to hatch 14+ million eggs a year; the group also invests in wind energy.
deep_cut_fact: He started the business in Pappampatti, a rain-shadow area so dry that conventional farming was limited, and expanded with the explicit aim of creating paid work in the village.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Alive status not confirmed though a 'Lakshmanan, Shanthi Hatcheries' chaired a Poultry Farmers Regulatory Committee summit in Nov 2025 (businessminutes.in). Wind-energy angle may suit the energy podcast. Best route: company website/office in Coimbatore.

name: Nara Bhuvaneswari
current_role: Vice Chairperson & Managing Director, Heritage Foods Ltd; Managing Trustee, NTR Memorial Trust
profile: Runs Heritage Foods, the Hyderabad-based listed dairy company, which she joined in 1994 as a whole-time director before becoming Vice Chairperson & MD; she is its largest individual shareholder (~24%). She also leads the NTR Memorial Trust (healthcare, blood banks, education, clean water) and is the daughter of N. T. Rama Rao.
interesting_fact: In November 2025 she received the Institute of Directors (UK) Distinguished Fellowship in London for her social work through the NTR Trust, while Heritage Foods won the Golden Peacock Award for Excellence in Corporate Governance 2025.
deep_cut_fact: She took charge of NTR Trust Bhavan in June 2014; the trust she leads runs NABH-accredited blood centres in Hyderabad, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati, and its NTR Sujala scheme supplies clean drinking water to about 18 lakh people in AP and Telangana.
notes: Wife of Andhra Pradesh CM N. Chandrababu Naidu; politically high-profile family, so outreach is best via Heritage Foods corporate office or NTR Trust. Heritage's site blocks some automated fetches.

name: Nemish S Shah
current_role: Co-founder, ENAM Holdings (manages treasury and proprietary capital); Governing Body member, FLAME University
profile: Mumbai investor who co-founded ENAM with Vallabh Bhanshali in 1984. ENAM began as a broking firm, then grew into a leading IPO investment bank. ENAM's banking and broking businesses were merged into Axis Bank. Shah now runs ENAM Holdings' treasury and long-term proprietary investing in Indian equities, using bottom-up fundamental research.
interesting_fact: He is widely credited with pioneering equity investment research in India. ENAM's investment banking arm went on to top India's IPO league tables.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a B.Com from Lala Lajpat Rai College (Mumbai University) in 1977. He reads Jain scriptures, follows cricket and loves music, and peers say his spirituality balances his investing.
notes: Very low public profile and no personal social media found. ENAM founders also set up FLAME University in Pune, which may be a warmer route in. No published office email found.

name: B Umapathy Reddy
current_role: Founder director / head (listed as Managing Director in registry data), BGR Mining & Infra Ltd, Hyderabad
profile: Bathina Umapathy Reddy co-founded BGR (originally B Girijapathi Reddy & Co.) in 1988 with Girijapathy Reddy and I. Sudhakara Reddy. It is now a Hyderabad-based contract-mining and Mine Developer & Operator (MDO) group running coal and mineral projects for NTPC, CCL, Vedanta and Hindalco. He still leads the group alongside the second generation.
interesting_fact: BGR says it runs 900+ dump trucks and 8,000+ employees across 7 states. It has won a string of coal MDO contracts, including NTPC's Kerendari 'A' (2023) and Badam (2024) and Hindalco's Meenakshi (2025).
deep_cut_fact: BGR began in 1988 as a small partnership firm, B Girijapathi Reddy & Co., set up by three co-founders including Umapathy Reddy. It became a company only in 2011, and by FY2022-23 it was moving about 29 million tonnes of coal a year.
notes: Low personal media profile. The company publishes only a careers email (careers@bgrmining.com) and a Hyderabad office line, so the contact form or the corporate office is the best route. Relevant to the energy angle as a coal mining contractor.

name: Soshil Kumar Jain
profile: Founder and chairman of Panacea Biotec (founded 1984 as Panacea Drugs). Died 7 October 2022 at age 89.
notes: Deceased 7 Oct 2022 (sources: https://medicaldialogues.in/news/industry/pharma/panacea-biotec-chairman-soshil-kumar-passes-away-at-age-of-89-100381 ; https://biospectrumindia.com/news/66/22078/founder-chairman-of-panacea-biotec-passes-away.html). Company now led by his son Rajesh Jain as Chairman & MD.

name: Ghisulal Rathod
current_role: Founder, Cello group; former non-executive chairman of Wim Plast Ltd (1988-2020)
profile: Ghisulal Dhanraj Rathod founded the Mumbai-based Cello plastics group, starting with plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon before building the Cello brand of housewares, writing instruments and furniture; Wim Plast (Cello moulded furniture) was a listed group company. The business is now run by his sons Pradeep and Pankaj and grandson Gaurav via Cello World Ltd (listed 2023).
interesting_fact: Cello started in 1967 with seven machines and about sixty workers making plastic bangles and PVC footwear in Goregaon, Mumbai, and grew into one of India's best-known consumerware brands.
deep_cut_fact: After seeing American households store food in round plastic containers on a US trip, he launched insulated casseroles in India in the late 1980s, a product that became a Cello staple.
notes: Patriarch, likely elderly and not public-facing; sources differ on founding dates (1962/1967/1974). Day-to-day leadership is son Pradeep Rathod (CMD, Cello World), the more practical outreach target. Reports say Wim Plast was being merged into Cello Consumer Products (2026, unverified).

name: Mayur Mukundlal Desai
current_role: Shareholder (>1%), Infibeam Avenues Ltd (now AvenuesAI)
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018 (approx. US$144m) with wealth from Infibeam Avenues, the Ahmedabad fintech/e-commerce company behind the CCAvenue payment gateway. Infibeam's March 2019 shareholding filing lists 'Mayur Mukundlal Desai' as a public shareholder holding more than 1%. Not a director or executive of the company.
interesting_fact: Appears in Infibeam Avenues' official March 2019 shareholding pattern among public shareholders owning more than 1% of the company.
notes: Passive investor in Infibeam rather than founder (founders are Vishal Mehta and Vishwas Patel). No public profile found; identity beyond the shareholding filing unverified. Company was renamed AvenuesAI in 2025-26.

name: Uday J Desai
current_role: Founder director / managing director, Frost International Ltd (Mumbai commodity trader) per company registry listings
profile: Uday Jayant Desai is listed as founder director and managing director of Frost International Ltd, a Mumbai commodity-trading company (incorporated 1995, also with a Kanpur presence) that traded a large portfolio of agri and other commodities. Hurun ranked him in 2017-18. Registry sites show the company under insolvency resolution (CIRP) as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Frost International traded a broad commodity portfolio out of Mumbai's Bandra Kurla Complex and Kanpur; company material credits Uday J. Desai as founder director who grew its trade volumes.
notes: Thin, aggregator-only sourcing; identity only partly confirmed. Company reportedly in insolvency (CIRP) per IBBI listing https://ibbi.gov.in/claims/pub-process/U05001MH1995PLC243081 - likely no longer UHNW; low-priority outreach target. No published contacts found.

name: Ajay S Shriram
current_role: Chairman & Senior Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Indian industrialist who leads DCM Shriram, the diversified group spanning chloro-vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Shriram Farm Solutions and Bioseed. A B.Com graduate of Sydenham College, Bombay, he also attended Harvard Business School's Program for Management Development, and he was president of the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) in 2014-15.
interesting_fact: He chairs the Governing Body of Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), the Delhi college his family founded, and chairs the board of IIM Sirmaur.
deep_cut_fact: Before leading CII, he was President and Chairman of the Paris-based International Fertilizer Industry Association (2009-11), and earlier he chaired the Fertilizer Association of India (2000-02).
notes: The press email is DCM Shriram's published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). The group's chlor-alkali business is power-intensive and runs captive power plants, which could make a good energy angle.

name: Ajit S Shriram
current_role: Joint Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd.
profile: Ajit S. Shriram is the youngest of three brothers (with Ajay and Vikram Shriram) running DCM Shriram, the Delhi-based conglomerate spun out of the old DCM Group in 1990, spanning chlor-alkali chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, Bioseed, Fenesta windows and PVC. He has served on the board for about two decades.
interesting_fact: He is a past President of the Indian Sugar Mills Association (ISMA) and a member of the CII National Council on Agriculture.
deep_cut_fact: After a commerce degree from Osmania University, Hyderabad, he did his MBA at IMD Lausanne; his company bio lists his passions as travel, photography and theatre.
notes: Press email is the published Corporate Communication/CSR contact (Ms. Aman Pannu). Energy angle: DCM Shriram is a large captive power and chlor-alkali (energy-intensive) operator.

name: Vikram S Shriram
current_role: Vice Chairman & Managing Director, DCM Shriram Ltd (since Sept 2001)
profile: Member of the Shriram business family, Vikram S. Shriram co-runs DCM Shriram, a Delhi-based conglomerate in chlor-alkali/vinyl chemicals, sugar, fertilisers, agri-inputs and captive power, alongside elder brother and Chairman Ajay S. Shriram. A chartered accountant, he has been Vice Chairman & MD since 2001.
interesting_fact: He is a qualified chartered accountant (Associate Member, ICAI) with a B.Com (Hons) from Calcutta University, and the company bio notes his strong aptitude for finance.
deep_cut_fact: After training across SRF Group functions, he joined Shriram Bearings Ltd in Ranchi in 1981 as senior management (works, marketing, general management); he studied at Mayo College, Ajmer, and lists swimming and cooking as hobbies.
notes: response@dcmshriram.com is the general corporate email in 2022-24 annual reports; shares@ appears in a 2022 AGM notice (shareholder services). DCM Shriram has a large captive power business - an angle for an energy podcast. Not to be confused with DCM Shriram Industries (separate company).

name: Pravinbhai Patel
current_role: Whole-time Director (long-time Chairman) of Patel Infrastructure Ltd, Vadodara
profile: Pravinbhai Vithalbhai Patel is a second-generation leader of Patel Infrastructure, the Vadodara road, highway, bridge and irrigation contractor founded by his father Vitthalbhai Gobarbhai Patel in 1972. He long served as chairman alongside his brother, MD Arvind Patel; the company has filed for an IPO (Rs 400 cr fresh issue) with SEBI.
interesting_fact: Patel Infrastructure was among the contractors for the first phase of the Vadodara-Mumbai Expressway, and its highway arm won a Silver Award at India's National Highway Awards for Excellence 2018.
notes: Title conflict: older sources (Craft, MarketScreener, CEO Magazine) call him Chairman & Whole-time Director; the current patelinfra.com About page lists brother Arvindbhai as Chairman and Pravin V. Patel as Whole-time Director. A 2015 Volvo CE case study quotes the family on PIPL's 'humble beginnings as a small family business in the 1970s'. Low public profile.

name: Arvind Patel
current_role: Managing Director, Patel Infrastructure Ltd (Vadodara, Gujarat) — note one registry record shows his MD term ending Oct 2024; company is pursuing an IPO (DRHP filed)
profile: Arvindbhai Vithalbhai Patel runs Patel Infrastructure, the Vadodara road/highway EPC contractor founded in 1972 by his father Vithalbhai Patel as a builder of government buildings and hotels; his brother Pravinbhai Patel is chairman. The firm became a major NHAI contractor (Delhi–Vadodara, Ganga expressways) and has filed a draft prospectus for an IPO.
interesting_fact: In May 2025 Patel Infrastructure laid 34.24 lane-km (20,105 t) of bituminous concrete in 24 hours on UP's Ganga Expressway, a record recognised by Golden Book, India Book and Asia Book of Records; Patel called it a contribution to nation-building.
deep_cut_fact: Patel received Built India Magazine's 'Legendary award for outstanding work in road construction'; in an NBM&CW interview he argued technology 'will not replace employees, rather, it will alter the working pattern at construction sites.'
notes: Shares Hurun listing with brother Pravinbhai Patel. Company website (has Contact Us / Media Corner pages) blocks scripted access; check it manually for press/IR email, or the DRHP's compliance-officer contact. Confirm whether he is still MD given the Oct 2024 registry end date.

name: Ramesh Chauhan
current_role: Chairman, Bisleri International Pvt. Ltd. (Mumbai)
profile: Indian beverage entrepreneur (b. 1940) of the Parle family. Parle bought the Bisleri brand from an Italian entrepreneur in 1969 and he built it into India's dominant bottled-water brand; he also created Thums Up, Limca, Gold Spot and Maaza, sold to Coca-Cola in 1993. After talks to sell Bisleri to Tata Consumer ended in 2023, daughter Jayanti (Vice Chairperson) and CEO Angelo George run it.
interesting_fact: After Coca-Cola left India in 1977 he launched Thums Up and built it into India's leading cola; Coca-Cola later bought Parle's soft-drink brands (Thums Up, Limca, Gold Spot, Maaza, Citra) in 1993.
deep_cut_fact: Known as 'RJC' to friends, he holds a double major in mechanical engineering and business management from MIT, returned home at 22, and introduced bottled mineral water to India at 27. His 2013 biography 'Thunder Unbottled, From Thums Up to Bisleri' was written by friend and ex-Newsweek UN bureau chief Patricia J Sethi.

public_contacts.value: wecare@bisleri.co.in (Bisleri general customer contact, not personal)

notes: Private company; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Bisleri corporate communications. Biography source: https://www.afaqs.com/39024_ramesh-j-chauhan-unveils-his-biography

name: Khushboo Rajiv Poddar
current_role: Member of the Poddar promoter family of Balkrishna Industries (BKT); role at the company not confirmed in filings
profile: Khushboo Poddar is part of the promoter family behind Balkrishna Industries (BKT), Mumbai-based maker of off-highway tyres for agriculture, construction and mining, chaired by Arvind Poddar with Rajiv Poddar as Joint MD. Her listed wealth stems from the family's BKT shareholding. MarketScreener lists her as a former management-committee member; a media report calls her joint MD, unconfirmed by filings.
interesting_fact: BKT, the source of the family wealth, is a global off-highway tyre specialist serving customers in 163 countries and runs an extensive sports-sponsorship programme.
notes: Very private; almost no public footprint of her own. Board filings name Arvind and Rajiv Poddar, not her. Best route is via BKT corporate channels. Role claim (joint MD) comes only from a tabloid-style DNA India piece — treat as unverified.

name: Suresh Venkatachari
current_role: Chairman & CEO, SecureKloud Technologies Ltd (formerly 8K Miles Software Services), since Feb 2024
profile: Chennai/US-based serial IT entrepreneur who founded 8K Miles Software in 2008 (renamed SecureKloud Technologies), a cloud, security and healthcare-IT services firm; earlier founded SRM Technologies (1999). He also served as CEO of Nasdaq-listed spinoff Healthcare Triangle (2019-2023) and returned as SecureKloud chairman & CEO in 2024.
interesting_fact: Over 35 years in IT services, he has founded several technology companies, three of which went public.
deep_cut_fact: Back in 2011, when 8K Miles was a young cloud startup, he told YourStory that 'security in cloud is one of the biggest concerns' of customers, foreshadowing the company's later rebrand to SecureKloud.
notes: Also known as Suresh V. Chari. Company has had governance/audit controversies in the past; keep outreach focused on cloud/healthcare-IT and data infrastructure.

name: Vishnukant Bhutada
current_role: Managing Director, Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Raichur, Karnataka)
profile: Vishnukant C. Bhutada is a first-generation pharma entrepreneur who founded Shilpa Medicare in his hometown of Raichur in 1987, at age 22, right after his B.Pharm. The company started with antibiotics, moved into oncology APIs and generics around 2000, and now sells globally. He remains Managing Director; Omprakash Inani is chairman.
interesting_fact: He came from a cotton-trading family but chose to build a pharma company in Raichur rather than a metro city: "I wanted to develop the region where I grew up." He started with Rs 50 lakh and 20 staff, and took the company public in 1994.
deep_cut_fact: His early export push targeted Bangladesh, which other Indian pharma firms ignored ("Nobody was focusing on Bangladesh back then"). Before a USFDA inspection of one API line, he added two more lines so inspectors would review all three at once.
notes: Low media profile. info@vbshilpa.com is the general company email. cs@vbshilpa.com is the company secretary's address (Ritu Tiwary), so the best route is a general corporate enquiry. His son Keshav Bhutada runs the subsidiary Shilpa Pharma Life Sciences.

name: Vijay S Nair
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Visen Industries Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Vijay S. Nair (Vijayasankaran Sivaraman Nair) founded Visen Industries in Mumbai in 1985 to make water-based polymer emulsions, starting with a 500-tonne-a-year plant at Tarapur. Visen now supplies binders to the paint, textile, adhesive and construction industries from plants in Tarapur, Silvassa, Jammu and Chennai plus a UAE unit; he remains CMD, with family members Cherry and Rohnit Nair on the board.
interesting_fact: Visen started in 1985 with capacity of just 500 tonnes a year at Tarapur near Mumbai; by the late 2000s it was producing about 60,000 tonnes a year across two plants with turnover over US$50m.
deep_cut_fact: In his 'From the Director's Desk' note he writes: 'I began this company with nothing but a handful of dreams and a drive to make it big in the industry... It still takes me by surprise to see how far Visen has come.'

public_contacts.value: info@visen.net (Secretarial Dept., Ms. Binita Gosalia, Company Secretary)

notes: Unlisted public company (CIN U24100MH1985PLC037350). Website footer is dated 2018, so plant list and contacts may be stale. Corporate contacts only (no personal channel found). Director Cherry V. Nair has given trade-press interviews (Indian Chemical News, 2022) and may be a route in. LinkedIn/X are the company's accounts, not his.

name: Atit Agarwal
current_role: Former Non-Executive Chairman, Responsive Industries Ltd (Mumbai) - chairmanship ended 2018; current role not confirmed
profile: Atit Omprakash Agarwal is a member of the Agarwal family that owns and manages Responsive Industries, a BSE/NSE-listed Mumbai maker of PVC/vinyl, SPC and LVT flooring, synthetic leather and (via Axiom Cordages) ropes. He chaired the company until 2018; the family business has since been fronted by Rishabh Agarwal.
interesting_fact: Responsive Industries describes itself as India's No.1 LVP/SPC flooring maker, with plants in India, Vietnam and Thailand exporting to 70+ countries; the family moved from ropes into PVC flooring in the early 1990s.
notes: Low public profile; little press coverage of Atit personally. Insider profiles (MarketScreener) show chairmanship ending 2018-09-30. Company contacts are corporate, not personal. Best route probably via company office or Rishabh Agarwal.

name: Vijay Darda
current_role: Chairman, Lokmat Media Group (Lokmat newspapers, Nagpur/Mumbai); former Rajya Sabha MP (1998-2016)
profile: Vijay Jawaharlal Darda (b. 1950, Yavatmal) is the elder son of freedom fighter Jawaharlal Darda, who launched the Marathi daily Lokmat in 1971. He built Lokmat into a multi-language media group and served three Rajya Sabha terms for Maharashtra. He remains group chairman, writes columns and has published books such as 'Ringside' (2023) and 'The Churn' (2025).
interesting_fact: He won his first Rajya Sabha seat in 1998 as an independent, defeating the official Congress candidate, before Congress nominated him for the 2004 and 2010 terms.
deep_cut_fact: His long-running 'dream project' is the 284 km Wardha-Yavatmal-Nanded railway line serving his home district; by 2021 he said he had pursued it for 13 years and discussed it with eleven Railway Ministers.
notes: Active on social media and writes regularly, so reachable via his site/X. Be aware he and his son were defendants in a coal-block allocation case (2023 conviction reported, later acquittal reported by Lokmat Times); avoid the topic.

name: Nitin Raojibhai Desai
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Desai Brothers Ltd (Pune); Independent Director, Zydus Lifesciences
profile: Pune industrialist who heads Desai Brothers, a family group founded in Gujarat in 1901 that is one of India's largest bidi makers and diversified into food (Mother's Recipe pickles, acquired 2002), finance, hospitality and renewable energy. He has been an independent director of Zydus Lifesciences since 2011 and was on the Force Motors board 2014-2022.
interesting_fact: The Desai group traces back to 1901 in Gujarat, still makes about 70 million bidis a day, and bought the 'Mother's Recipe' pickle brand in 2002 for roughly Rs 6 crore before demerging food into Desai Foods in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: He is a civil engineer with a master's in environmental engineering from the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, and chairs The Poona Blind Men's Association; he was also President of Poona Club.
notes: Private family group; no published personal/office email found. Group's renewable-energy arm is a possible angle for the energy podcast. Route via Desai Brothers corporate office or Zydus company secretary.

name: Arpan Paul
current_role: Executive Chairman, SAJ Food Products Pvt Ltd (Bisk Farm), Kolkata
profile: Arpan Paul heads SAJ Food Products, the Kolkata-based maker of Bisk Farm biscuits founded in 2000 by his father Krishnadas Paul, who launched it at age 60. Arpan took over as executive chairman after his father's death in 2020; the company has been reported at roughly Rs 2,000+ crore turnover.
interesting_fact: His father Krishnadas Paul started SAJ Food at age 60 after suffering a Rs 15 crore business loss, and grew Bisk Farm into one of eastern India's leading biscuit brands.
deep_cut_fact: The company name SAJ comes from the initials of Krishnadas Paul's three children - Sharmistha, Arpan and Jayeeta - so Arpan's own initial is in the company name.
notes: Low media profile; few interviews found. Best route is via the company (Bisk Farm news/press section: https://www.biskfarm.com/news-media/press-release/).

name: Hemant Kamala Jalan
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Indigo Paints Ltd (NSE: INDIGOPNTS), Pune
profile: Founder of Indigo Paints (2000), which he grew from a small cement-paint maker into India's fifth-largest decorative paint company by revenue, with Sequoia Capital backing (2014, 2016). Indigo listed in Feb 2021 after an IPO oversubscribed ~117 times, and in 2023 moved into waterproofing/construction chemicals by buying 51% of Apple Chemie India.
interesting_fact: Indigo's January 2021 IPO was oversubscribed about 117 times, with anchor investors including the Government of Singapore, Fidelity and Goldman Sachs; MS Dhoni has been its brand ambassador since 2018, and actor Mohanlal fronts it in Kerala.
deep_cut_fact: Indigo began in 2000 making only low-end cement paints before moving into emulsions, and later unified its scattered product brands under the single 'INDIGO' name; it now runs factories in Jodhpur, Kochi and Pudukkottai.
notes: Paints/chemicals, not energy - weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast (dataset tags him as petrochemicals). Gives media interviews on growth (e.g. Economic Times). No personal channels verified.

name: Jehangir Nusli Wadia
current_role: Non-executive promoter director, Bombay Burmah Trading Corp. and Britannia Industries (rejoined Wadia Group boards Nov 2024; reported to be returning as MD of Bombay Dyeing)
profile: Jeh Wadia (b. 1973), younger son of Nusli Wadia, ran Wadia Group airline GoAir/Go First from its 2005 launch until 2021 and was MD of Bombay Dyeing, where he founded Bombay Realty in 2011. He left the group's boards in 2021 and moved to London; Go First ceased flying in 2023. He returned to the group in late 2024 in non-executive board roles.
interesting_fact: He is a great-grandson of Pakistan's founder Muhammad Ali Jinnah, and was named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Secretary of the Deendayal Research Institute under social reformer Nanaji Deshmukh; DRI adopted 500 villages in Chitrakoot to make them self-reliant. He also attended Millfield school in England and holds an MSc from Warwick.
notes: Go First's 2023 insolvency is a sensitive topic. No personal social accounts found. Best route is via Wadia Group company secretariat (Bombay Dyeing / Bombay Burmah). Not confirmed whether the Bombay Dyeing MD role has formally taken effect.

name: K R Nagarajan
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Ramraj Cotton (Tiruppur, Tamil Nadu)
profile: Tiruppur entrepreneur who founded Ramraj Khadi Traders in 1983 to sell dhotis and support local weavers; renamed Ramraj Cotton in 1987. Built it into India's leading dhoti/veshti and white-shirt ethnic-wear brand, with 250+ stores by its 40th anniversary in 2023 and exports to Sri Lanka, Singapore and Malaysia.
interesting_fact: The 'Ramraj' name combines letters from his own name (Nagarajan) and his father's (Ramaswamy); the business began with just a table and a chair in a small Tirupur office.
deep_cut_fact: He finished his SSLC in 1977 but couldn't afford college, so went straight to work, spending 18 months at a Tirupur dhoti maker learning production and marketing; being stopped by a hotel watchman for wearing a dhoti later inspired the brand's 'Salute Ramraj' pride-in-dhoti positioning.
notes: Company contact page lists only customer care/franchise/corporate-orders emails, no press contact. Tamil-language interview (Vikatan, 2020) says he started trading at age 13.

name: Mustak Hossain
current_role: Chairman, Pataka Group (MD, Pataka Industries Pvt Ltd), Kolkata
profile: Mustak Hossain leads Kolkata-based Pataka Group, founded in 1952 by Giasuddin Biswas as a single biri factory in Murshidabad. Joining in 1980, he diversified it into tobacco, packaged tea and biscuits, textiles (East End Silks), healthcare and real estate (Pataka Infracorp).
interesting_fact: By 1998 Pataka had become India's largest biri maker and marketer, selling over 100 million sticks a day; it entered packaged tea with Pataka Tea in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: The group's philanthropic arm, GD Charitable Society (set up 1989), named after founder Giasuddin Biswas, went on to establish the GD Hospitals and Diabetes Institute in Kolkata in 2007.

profile: Neil Subin is a New York special-situations and activist investor who founded Trendex Capital Management and later chaired Broadbill Investment Partners. He now runs MILFAM LLC, a single-family office, and has sat on NextNav's board since 2022; SEC filings show 10%+ stakes in Optimum Communications and Gulf Coast Ultra Deep Royalty Trust.
interesting_fact: He has repeatedly served on creditor or shareholder committees in bankruptcies and has been a director of Federal-Mogul, Primus Telecommunications, Komag and Centrus Energy, the US enriched-uranium fuel supplier.
deep_cut_fact: He sits on the board of Type One Energy, a fusion-power startup developing stellarator reactors, bringing his earlier nuclear-fuel board experience from Centrus Energy.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (fusion via Type One Energy, nuclear fuel via Centrus, ultra-deep gas royalties). Very private family-office investor; no personal channels found. Best route likely via Type One Energy or NextNav investor relations.

name: Jesse Feldman
current_role: General Partner, Battery Ventures (Boston); leads its industrial-technology practice
profile: Boston-based private-equity/VC investor who joined Battery Ventures in 2005 and became a General Partner in 2012. He appears as a 10% owner of Sprinklr and Braze in SEC filings as one of the Battery Ventures fund reporting persons (shared fund holdings, not personal stakes). He focuses on buyout and growth-equity deals in industrial tech and life-science tools.
interesting_fact: Battery's industrial-technology practice he leads has completed 60+ transactions in the US and Europe since 2003; his exits include Drillinginfo, HighJump, Qognify and Rogue Wave Software, plus 40+ add-on acquisitions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Battery he was a founding member of Ionian Ventures, a fund focused on transportation and logistics technology, after starting his career at GE Capital; he holds a BA from Wesleyan and an MBA from Harvard.
notes: SEC 'net worth' figure reflects Battery Ventures fund holdings reported jointly by GPs, not his personal wealth. Relevant for industrial-tech/robotics angle (Robotiq, LI-COR boards).

name: Patrick Fleury
current_role: CFO & Treasurer, TeraWulf Inc. (WULF); Director, Corvex, Inc.
profile: Patrick Fleury has been CFO of TeraWulf, the bitcoin-mining-turned-AI/HPC data-center developer, since May 2022, leading its capital raising for expansion. He spent ~24 years in finance: Banc of America energy & power banking, MD at Blackstone's GSO Capital Partners, and founding member of Platinum Equity's credit team.
interesting_fact: Began his career in the Global Energy & Power Investment Banking Group at Banc of America Securities before moving into credit investing at Blackstone/GSO.
deep_cut_fact: Graduated magna cum laude from Bowdoin College with a BA in Economics and Government & Legal Studies.
notes: Highly relevant for energy/data-center podcast (TeraWulf's Lake Mariner / AI hosting deals). Regular conference speaker (SALT, RBLT) - conference circuit is a natural route.

name: John Kristofer Galashan
current_role: Partner and Investment Committee member, Leonard Green & Partners; Director, Life Time Group Holdings and Mister Car Wash
profile: Kris Galashan is a Los Angeles private-equity investor who joined Leonard Green & Partners (LGP) as an associate in 2002 after investment banking at DLJ/Credit Suisse First Boston, and now sits on LGP's Investment Committee. His SEC-reported holdings reflect LGP fund stakes in Life Time (board since 2015) and Mister Car Wash (board since 2014), which LGP took private in a ~$3.1bn deal announced Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: He has overseen LGP's bet on Mister Car Wash since 2014; in 2026 LGP took the car-wash chain private at $7/share (~$3.1bn enterprise value) after taking it public in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Canadian-educated: he earned an Honors Business Administration (HBA) degree from the Ivey Business School at the University of Western Ontario before starting in DLJ's Los Angeles investment-banking office.
notes: Net worth figure largely reflects LGP fund holdings attributed via SEC filings, not personal stake. Mister Car Wash take-private reportedly closed May 2026 (verify); avoid referencing the related shareholder litigation. Low public profile; best route is LGP's office contact form.

name: James Charles Hays
current_role: Director (retiring in 2026), Skyward Specialty Insurance Group (NASDAQ: SKWD); founder of Hays Companies
profile: Jim Hays left Aon in Chicago to found Minneapolis-based Hays Companies in 1994, building it into the Upper Midwest's largest independent commercial insurance and benefits broker before selling its insurance operations to Brown & Brown in 2018 for about $705M. He has been a long-time backer and director of Skyward Group, which announced in April 2026 he would retire from its board.
interesting_fact: The 2018 Hays deal (about $705M) was the largest acquisition in Brown & Brown's 75-year history; Hays then had 700+ professionals in 32 offices across 21 states.
deep_cut_fact: Hays started Hays Companies in 1994 with five partners, each of whom put in $300,000 of their own money.

public_contacts.value: Skyward Specialty investor relations site (IR contacts listed there)

notes: Skyward said Peter Hearn would join the board Aug 1, 2026, succeeding Hays, who retires 'later this year' after nearly two decades with Skyward Group (https://investors.skywardinsurance.com/news-releases/news-release-details/industry-leader-peter-hearn-join-board-directors-jim-hays-retire). Low public profile; no personal channels found.

name: Christopher E Kubasik
current_role: Former Chair & CEO, L3Harris Technologies (removed Aug 2026); no new role announced
profile: CPA and former Ernst & Young partner who became CFO and then President/COO of Lockheed Martin. He joined L3 Technologies in 2015 and became CEO in 2017. He led the 2019 L3-Harris merger and was CEO of L3Harris from 2021 (Chair from 2022). His wealth comes from L3Harris equity. In Aug 2026 the board terminated him after a code-of-conduct investigation, and Sam Mehta succeeded him.
interesting_fact: He went from Ernst & Young partner to Lockheed Martin controller in 1999, then CFO in 2004 and President/COO in 2010. He also completed the Defense Acquisition University's Systems Acquisition Management course for flag officers (2004).
deep_cut_fact: University of Maryland Athletics runs a career-readiness program for student-athletes named for him, the 'Kubasik First Impact Program'. He is a 1983 magna cum laude accounting graduate of UMD's Smith School.
notes: SENSITIVE: L3Harris fired him on 16-17 Aug 2026 over conduct (https://fortune.com/2026/08/17/l3harris-ceo-ousted-chris-kubasik-sam-mehta/). In 2012 he also left Lockheed as CEO-elect over an ethics issue. The L3Harris press email no longer reaches him. No personal channel was found. Approach with care or deprioritise.

name: Matthew J. Missad
current_role: Executive Chairman, UFP Industries (Grand Rapids, MI); agreed to stay through 2026
profile: Career-long UFP Industries executive (wood/composite building, packaging and industrial products). He was EVP and general counsel from 1996, CEO from July 2011 to Dec 2024 and chairman from 2023. He became executive chairman when Will Schwartz took over as CEO at the start of fiscal 2025.
interesting_fact: Became UFP's fifth CEO in its history (July 2011) after more than 25 years at the company, much of it as its top lawyer.
deep_cut_fact: Started at UFP in 1978 as a high-school student working part-time on the maintenance crew. He paid his own way through college and law school, then joined full-time in 1985 as manager of legal compliance.
notes: Press contact (Lynn Afendoulis, Director of Corporate Communications) comes from a Feb 2023 release; check a recent UFP release to confirm it is current.

name: Surendralal Lanca (Lal) Karsanbhai
current_role: President & CEO, Emerson Electric Co. (EMR); Director, Merck & Co.
profile: Lal Karsanbhai joined Emerson in 1995 as an international planner after his Washington University MBA and rose through corporate planning and the Automation Solutions business, which he led from 2018. CEO since February 2021, he has reshaped Emerson into a pure-play industrial automation and software company (selling Climate Technologies, buying AspenTech and NI). He also sits on Merck's board.
interesting_fact: He was born outside the US, moved country to country with his father's job, and did not learn English until age 10, before coming to the US for an economics degree at the University of Michigan.
deep_cut_fact: He is a vinyl enthusiast who unwinds listening to LP records, and named Tower Grove's iNDO as a favourite St. Louis restaurant in a 2022 profile.
notes: Strong fit for energy/automation theme (Emerson serves power, LNG, data-centre controls). Media requests go through FleishmanHillard per Emerson's newsroom.

name: Gregg J Felton
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Altus Power (Stamford, CT; now owned by TPG Rise Climate)
profile: Gregg Felton co-founded Altus Power, a developer, owner and operator of commercial-scale and community solar, storage and EV-charging assets, and has been with it since 2013. Altus went public via SPAC in December 2021 (NYSE: AMPS) and has since been taken private by TPG Rise Climate. He previously was a Goldman Sachs partner and CIO of GSAM's Credit Alternatives platform.
interesting_fact: Altus Power energized its first solar system in Bridgeport, Connecticut in 2010, took an initial investment from Blackstone in 2014, and grew into one of the largest US commercial-scale solar owners before teaming up with TPG Rise Climate.
deep_cut_fact: A Tufts economics graduate with both a J.D. (Georgetown Law) and an MBA (Georgetown business school), Felton started at Chase Manhattan Bank and, before Altus, ran Goldman Sachs Asset Management's Credit Alternatives platform overseeing more than $5B in hedge-fund and private-credit vehicles.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (distributed solar + storage + EV charging). hello@ is Altus's general company inbox. Altus no longer files with the SEC after the TPG take-private.

name: Rakesh Wadhawan
current_role: Promoter and suspended director of Housing Development and Infrastructure Ltd (HDIL), which is in insolvency
profile: Mumbai real-estate promoter who built HDIL into one of Mumbai's largest developers, known for slum-rehabilitation and redevelopment projects, including near Mumbai airport. HDIL entered insolvency in 2019 and its assets are being sold through the NCLT process; he remains involved in disputes over the resolution.
interesting_fact: HDIL's slum-rehabilitation project around Mumbai airport was one of the largest such schemes in India and became central to the company's later financial strain.
notes: Not a suitable outreach target: arrested in 2019 in the PMC Bank case and facing ongoing criminal/insolvency proceedings (e.g. https://www.freepressjournal.in/amp/mumbai/hdil-promoter-rakesh-wadhawan-moves-eow-alleges-illegal-assignment-of-600-crore-yes-bank-loan-to-suraksha-arc). Wealth likely largely wiped out. No published contacts.

name: Yugandhar Reddy
current_role: Associated with Medha Servo Drives, Hyderabad (per Hurun India 2017-2019); current role unverified
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2017-2019 (~US$132m) for Medha Servo Drives, a Hyderabad-based maker of railway traction/propulsion electronics founded in 1984 that also makes solar inverters. Public searches did not surface a profile tying this name to the company; registry listings show other Reddy family members (e.g. Kasyap Reddy Yadavelli) as directors.
interesting_fact: Medha Servo Drives runs a joint venture with Austria's Traktionssysteme Austria (TSA) that has produced over 10,000 traction motors in Hyderabad.
notes: Very private family-owned company; identity could not be confirmed online. Searches mostly return an unrelated Hyderabad oncologist with a similar name. Medha's solar-inverter line may be relevant to an energy podcast.

name: Dendi Ram Reddy
current_role: Managing Director, Sneha Farms Pvt. Ltd. (Sneha Group), Hyderabad
profile: D. Ram Reddy founded what became Sneha Group, starting with a single chicken shop ('Ram Reddy Chicken Market') and building a vertically integrated Telangana poultry conglomerate spanning feed, breeder farms, hatcheries, processing, eggs and edible-oil refining. He remains MD while son Varun Reddy Dendi is CEO; Japan's Mitsui & Co. now has a director on the board.
interesting_fact: Sneha Group says it set up India's first fully automated chicken processing facility (12,000 birds/hour) and has supplied frozen chicken to Indian defence organisations since 2012.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial journey began in 1981 with one chicken retail outlet in Malakpet, Hyderabad - the 'Ram Reddy Chicken Market' that was later rebranded Sneha Fresh Chicken.
notes: Low public profile; company contacts are general corporate ones. Son Varun Reddy Dendi (CEO) is the more public-facing executive.

name: Venkat Ramaswamy
current_role: Vice Chairman, Edelweiss Group (Edelweiss Financial Services); heads the alternatives business (Edelweiss Alternatives / EAAA)
profile: Venkatchalam 'Venkat' Arakoni Ramaswamy co-founded Edelweiss with Rashesh Shah in 1995. The two had been colleagues at ICICI. Edelweiss grew into a diversified Indian financial-services group, and he is now vice chairman. He leads its alternatives arm, a major private-credit and infrastructure investor in India.
interesting_fact: The alternatives arm he leads raised INR 8,000 crore for its Infrastructure Yield Plus II fund, which buys operating roads and renewable-energy assets. A 2026 report said it was in talks for a third fund of about $1bn+. That is directly relevant to the energy/infrastructure theme.
deep_cut_fact: Edelweiss started in 1995 as a three-person startup that Rashesh Shah launched with his ICICI colleague Venkat Ramaswamy after both quit their jobs.
notes: Lower media profile than co-founder Rashesh Shah, but quoted in fund-raise announcements and speaks at CFA Society India events. Edelweiss's investor-services page lists the company secretary (Tarun Khurana) at Edelweiss House, Kalina, Mumbai. No press email was confirmed (site blocked automated fetch). Good energy-transition/infra-fund angle.

name: Vamanrai V Parekh
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Nilkamal Ltd (stepped down from the board in Aug 2020)
profile: First-generation entrepreneur who, with brother Sharad, left the family button business in 1981 to make plastic household goods in a rented shed in Powai, Mumbai. That became Nilkamal, the listed maker of moulded plastic furniture, material-handling crates/pallets, mattresses and @Home retail. He was Chairman 1990-2020 and is now Chairman Emeritus; sons Hiten and Manish are in the business.
interesting_fact: Nilkamal describes itself as the world's largest producer of moulded plastic furniture, selling in about 30 countries; it has been listed on NSE/BSE since 1991.
deep_cut_fact: The crate business that made Nilkamal began when the brothers noticed wooden crates carrying milk bottles at Worli Dairy and realised plastic crates would be lighter, more durable and cheaper. The family firm itself traces back to a one-machine metal-button shed their father Vrajlal Parekh started in 1934.
notes: Elderly (about 88 per data providers) and retired from the board in 2020; no recent public statements found, and no death reports found. Hurun wealth shared with brother Sharad V Parekh. Best route: via Nilkamal company secretary or investor relations. The 1934 button-shed detail comes from Nilkamal's 'Our Journey' page (https://nilkamal.com/?p=201).

name: Sharad V Parekh
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Nilkamal Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Co-founded Nilkamal in 1981 with elder brother Vamanrai Parekh, leaving the family's metal-button business to make plastic household goods in Powai, Mumbai. He led marketing and pioneered India's plastic material-handling (crate) business; Nilkamal is now a Rs 2,000+ cr furniture, materials-handling and retail (@home) group. He became chairman in 2020 after years as MD.
interesting_fact: Nilkamal's roots go back to a one-machine metal-button factory shed set up by the family in 1934; the brothers switched to plastics in 1981 and 'crate' became almost synonymous with the Nilkamal brand.
deep_cut_fact: Spotting that Operation Flood was spawning dairies, Sharad Parekh, then 37, followed a milk van all the way to Mumbai's Worli Dairy to pitch plastic crates; by 1983 Nilkamal won its first crate order, launching its material-handling business.
notes: Low-profile family business founder; company bio says he is active in several charitable trusts and educational institutions. Route via corporate office.

name: Jayendra H Kharawala
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Jay Chemical Industries Pvt Ltd (JCIL), India (listed as chairman on the company website)
profile: Founder of Jay Chemical Industries, started in 1967 as a small dye and dye-intermediate unit. JCIL is now one of the world's top reactive-dye producers, with more than 15% of India's market, sales in over 40 countries and revenue above $200M. It has expanded into digital textile inks, construction chemicals and garments.
interesting_fact: JCIL makes more than half of its own raw-material inputs (over 50% backward integration). That is a deliberate self-reliance strategy that Kharawala built into a dye business started when international firms dominated Indian dyes.
deep_cut_fact: Jay Chemicals marked its 50th anniversary on 9 March 2017. The company credits its founding to Kharawala's vision 'to do business that would not only provide for his family but would better society as well'.
notes: Private company with a low profile. Day-to-day operations are run by Managing Director Greeven Kharawala. Alive status is not independently confirmed (the company site still lists him as chairman). The links are corporate, not personal. Industry is textile dyes, so the fit with energy and data centers is weak.

name: Ramesh Vinayak Vaze
current_role: Not on the current board of S H Kelkar and Company (Keva); current status unconfirmed
profile: Member of the Vaze promoter family behind S H Kelkar and Company (now branded Keva), a Mumbai fragrance, flavour and aroma-ingredients maker that began as an industrial perfume manufacturer in British India and is now one of India's largest fragrance companies. The family's third generation, Kedar Vaze, is Group CEO; Prabha Vaze is a non-executive director.
interesting_fact: Keva started as S H Kelkar & Company, a maker of industrial perfumes in British India, and grew organically and via acquisitions into an Indian fragrance multinational.
notes: Hurun India 2018-2019 listing. He does not appear on Keva's current board/leadership page; his current role and whether he is alive could not be verified (web search budget exhausted). Contacts are company-level (Keva). Industry is fragrances/chemicals, weak fit for energy focus.

name: Arvind Domadia
current_role: Managing Director, Kunal Structure (India) Pvt Ltd, Ahmedabad (per company registry aggregators)
profile: Gujarat infrastructure contractor. Kunal Structure (India) Pvt Ltd was incorporated in 2006 and builds roads, canals and buildings. A registry aggregator reported operating revenue above INR 500 crore for FY2021. Registry listings name Arvindbhai Amrutlal Domadia as managing director, with his son Kunal A. Domadia as co-director.
interesting_fact: The company carries his son's name, Kunal, who sits on the board with him. Kunal Structure is privately held and was incorporated in April 2006 with registered offices in Bodakdev, Ahmedabad.
notes: Identity based on registry listings only (Arvindbhai Amrutlal Domadia, DIN 01608844). No press coverage, official website or published contacts found. Very private. Kunal Structure also appears in Gujarat tender records.

name: Kulanthaivel Vinayagam
current_role: Managing Director, SCM Group / The Chennai Silks; Group MD, Space Textiles Pvt Ltd
profile: K. Vinayagam (also spelled Vinayakam) is one of the brothers who run SCM Group, the family textile empire founded by A. Kulandaivel Mudaliar, best known for the South Indian retail chain The Chennai Silks. The group also spins yarn, exports hosiery and garments to brands such as Decathlon and Hanes, and runs precast-construction, school and hospital ventures.
interesting_fact: In 2007 The Chennai Silks set a Guinness record for the world's most expensive silk saree, worth about Rs 41 lakh. It reproduced 11 Raja Ravi Varma paintings and took around 4,760 hours to design.
deep_cut_fact: The business began as a Khadi shop, Kasthuribhai Khadi Vasthralayam in Madurai (1962). Today it is run jointly by eight brothers, four sisters and their children, about 130 family members, and spins roughly 130 tonnes of yarn a day on 170,000 spindles.
notes: Low individual media profile; family-run group led publicly by chairman T.K. Chandiran. His son V. Vikram Narayen is Executive Director. The best route is the corporate office via the official website. Spelling varies (Vinayagam/Vinayakam).

name: Shantaben P Jain
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, Kewal Kiran Clothing Ltd (Mumbai; 'Killer' jeans) - no executive role found
profile: Shantaben P. Jain is a member of the Jain promoter family of Kewal Kiran Clothing, the Mumbai apparel maker behind the Killer, Lawman Pg3 and Integriti brands run by the Pukhraj Jain brothers (CMD Kewalchand P.
