Jain). Exchange filings show the largest promoter block (~30.8m shares) held in her name jointly with Kewalchand and Hemant P. Jain.
interesting_fact: The promoter group reported no pledged or encumbered shares for FY26; her name heads the joint holding with Kewalchand and Hemant Jain.
notes: Private family shareholder with no public profile, interviews or biography found; relationship to the Pukhraj Jain brothers not stated in sources (name suggests family matriarch, unverified). Approach would realistically be via the company / CMD Kewalchand Jain.

name: Sonal Yatin Kakodkar
current_role: Listed shareholder/family member associated with Parle Products (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Appears on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$132m) with wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) founded in 1929 and controlled by the Chauhan family. No public biography, interviews or executive role were found; she appears to be a passive family shareholder.
interesting_fact: Parle Products, the source of her listed wealth, became India's first packaged-food company to pass US$2bn in annual revenue (FY22).
notes: Very private; family relationship to the Parle Products Chauhans not publicly documented. Not a public-facing figure; only route is via Parle Products corporate.

name: Rita Kishore Sinha
current_role: Non-Executive Director, SIS Limited (Security and Intelligence Services India)
profile: Rita Kishore Sinha is a long-time director and major shareholder (~16%) of SIS Ltd, the Patna-founded security, facility-management and cash-logistics group started by her husband, journalist-turned-politician RK Sinha. SIS is now one of India's largest private employers, with FY2026 revenue of about ₹15,982 crore; her son Rituraj Sinha is Group MD.
interesting_fact: SIS grew from a small Patna security agency into a multinational group; the company says revenue rose from ₹25 crore in 2002 to ₹15,982 crore in FY2026, with operations including Australia (MSS) and a cash-logistics JV with Prosegur.
deep_cut_fact: She is a lawyer by training: she holds a BA in Hindi and an LLB from Ranchi University, has around 32 years of legal experience and is enrolled with the Supreme Court Bar Association.
notes: Low personal media profile; the public face of SIS is son Rituraj Kishore Sinha (Group MD). Best route is SIS media relations.

name: Mahendra Nahata
current_role: Promoter & Managing Director, HFCL Ltd; director, Reliance Jio Infocomm
profile: Kolkata-raised B.Com (St. Xavier's) who co-promoted Himachal Futuristic Communications (HFCL) in 1987, building it from transmission equipment into a telecom gear, optical-fibre and defence-electronics maker. MD since 2005 and on the Jio Infocomm board; in 2026 he is pushing HFCL's record order book and calling for Indian data-centre and R&D expansion.
interesting_fact: Voice & Data named him 'Telecom Man of the Millennium' in 2003; he also has been president of the Telecom Equipment Manufacturers Association of India, and his family holds a stake in Jio Platforms.
deep_cut_fact: Before telecom, he began his business career dabbling in tea trading out of New Jalpaiguri, a small town in north Bengal.
notes: Strong podcast fit: publicly advocating data-centre and telecom-infrastructure build-out (Entrepreneur India 2026: https://india.entrepreneur.com/business-news/entrepreneur-2026-hfcls-mahendra-nahata-calls-for-infra-data-centre-expansion-and-rd-investment). Son Anant Nahata runs Exicom (EV chargers/telecom power). Route via HFCL company secretary/IR.

name: Hanwant Manbir Singh
current_role: Former director, Karamtara Engineering (Mumbai), appointed 2001 and ceased 22 June 2023 per MCA-derived records; still lists directorships in Karamtara Steel and Karamtara Fasteners
profile: Member of the Singh family behind Karamtara Engineering, a Mumbai-area maker of transmission-line towers, solar mounting and tracker structures, and fasteners. The company is run by promoters Tanveer Singh (CMD) and Rajiv Singh, and it received SEBI approval in 2025 for a Rs 1,750 crore IPO.
interesting_fact: Karamtara says in its DRHP that it is India's largest producer of solar mounting structures and tracker components, and it also builds lattice towers for power transmission lines.
notes: Very low public profile, and his exact relation to the current promoters isn't documented in sources I could verify. The role comes from MCA-aggregator data (tofler/qorpiq). Karamtara's grid and solar-structures business fits the energy theme, but the promoters Tanveer or Rajiv Singh are the more visible route.

name: Aroon Purie
current_role: Chairman & Editor-in-Chief, India Today Group; Chairman & MD, TV Today Network
profile: Aroon Purie (b. 1944) is the founder-publisher and editor-in-chief of India Today, launched in 1975, and built the India Today Group into a diversified media house (Aaj Tak, India Today TV, magazines, radio, printing via Thomson Press). In 2017 he passed day-to-day control to daughter Kalli Purie but remains editor-in-chief.
interesting_fact: Awarded the Padma Bhushan in 2001; in 2025 at FICCI Frames he warned AI poses an 'existential threat' to credible journalism.
deep_cut_fact: A chartered accountant and LSE economics graduate (1965), he began his career in 1970 as a production controller at the family's Thomson Press printing business; he was a Doon School contemporary of Rajiv Gandhi.
notes: No published personal or press email found; route via India Today Group corporate office/editorial. Media figure rather than energy; AI-in-media views may be a hook.

name: Chigurupati Krishna Prasad
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Granules India Ltd
profile: Dr. Krishna Prasad Chigurupati founded Triton Laboratories in Hyderabad in 1984 with Uma Chigurupati to make paracetamol API; it grew into Granules India, among the world's largest makers of paracetamol, metformin and ibuprofen and a pioneer of pharmaceutical formulation intermediates (PFIs). He still leads it as CMD, pushing green-chemistry projects and a 2025 move into peptides.
interesting_fact: Granules commissioned what it called the world's largest single-site PFI plant at Gagillapur in 2003; he received the Economic Times Lifetime Achievement Award (2022) and an IOD Distinguished Fellowship (2025).
deep_cut_fact: In 1987 his first company, Triton Laboratories, became only the second Indian pharma company to export to the United States; Triton also pioneered selling bulk 'direct compressible' granulated paracetamol (PFIs).
notes: Granules' 'Healthy People, Healthy Planet' green-molecules push (Granules CZRO subsidiary) is a good sustainability/energy hook. Family also active in company (Uma, Priyanka, Harsha Chigurupati are EDs).

name: Suresh G Kare
current_role: Chairman, Indoco Remedies Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Suresh Govind Kare is chairman of Indoco Remedies, the Mumbai pharma maker of formulations and APIs founded by his father Govind Ramnath Kare in 1947. He took over the family firm and built it into a profitable, listed drug maker with export plants in Goa; daughter Aditi Kare Panandikar is now MD while he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: Indoco was incorporated on 23 August 1947, eight days after Indian independence, by his father to make indigenous medicines, making it one of India's oldest pharma companies.
deep_cut_fact: A past President of the Indian Drug Manufacturers' Association (IDMA), he was felicitated by Amitabh Bachchan at IDMA's Golden Jubilee celebrations in Mumbai in January 2012 for decades of service to the industry.
notes: Sources differ on whether his chairmanship is executive or non-executive. In late 2025 Kare family trusts took over shares from family members. Low media profile; go through Indoco corporate communications.

name: Rajesh Patil
current_role: Chairman (and promoter), Kolte-Patil Developers Ltd, Pune — now jointly controlled with Blackstone (40% stake, Aug 2025)
profile: Rajesh Anirudha Patil, a University of Mysore civil engineer, co-founded Pune developer Kolte-Patil in 1989/1991 with his brother Naresh and the Kolte family, growing it into a listed residential developer across Pune, Mumbai and Bengaluru. In 2025 Blackstone bought a 40% stake (~Rs 1,160 cr), giving joint control alongside the promoters; Patil remains chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2010 he shocked India's real-estate industry by hiring 28-year-old ISB graduate Sujay Kalele, making him CEO within a couple of years, bringing in IBM for an 11-year business-transformation project, and paying to be mentored by CEO coach Ram Charan.
deep_cut_fact: When he set up the company in 1989 after his engineering degree, he promised his parents he would never associate with politicians and would avoid debt; he says he made only two trips to Mantralaya in his whole career, and peers eventually 'decided to stop inviting me altogether' to industry meets.
notes: Shares Hurun listing with brother Naresh Patil (vice-chairman). info.kpdl@ is the general company email listed on the investor-services page. Blackstone now co-controls the company, which may affect comms routing.

name: Naresh Patil
profile: Co-promoter and former Vice Chairman of Kolte-Patil Developers (Pune real estate). Kolte-Patil's own founders page now refers to him as 'Late Mr. Naresh Patil' and he no longer appears on the board page; date of death not found.
notes: Deceased per company website (https://www.koltepatil.com/about-us/founders). Brother Rajesh Patil (Chairman & MD) is the living co-holder of the Hurun entry; profile him instead if relevant.

name: Karthik Ganapathy
current_role: Co-founder and Vice President, BillDesk (IndiaIdeas.com Ltd), Mumbai
profile: IIT Bombay (EE '93) and IIM Bangalore (MBA '95) graduate who left Arthur Andersen's financial-services consulting practice to co-found BillDesk in 2000 with MN Srinivasu and Ajay Kaushal. BillDesk became India's leading bill-payment gateway; a $4.7bn sale to Prosus/PayU agreed in 2021 was later terminated (2022), and he remains co-founder and VP.
interesting_fact: BillDesk processed over Rs 12 trillion in digital transactions in 2023; when the Prosus deal was announced in 2021, the three co-founders were each expected to receive about $500m for their combined ~30% stake.
deep_cut_fact: Spent ~5 years at Arthur Andersen consulting for banks and brokers before BillDesk; lists tennis and reading as hobbies and his mantra as 'Be yourself, everybody else is already taken.' Fond of his IIT Bombay hostel-council and Mood Indigo days.
notes: Low-profile founder; rarely gives interviews. The Prosus/PayU acquisition was terminated in Oct 2022, so the founders retain their stake. Approach via BillDesk corporate or IIT Bombay / IIM Bangalore alumni networks. Bloomberg 2021 piece on the founders: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-09-02/three-men-pushing-50-reap-millions-selling-india-payments-firm

name: Sameer Padmakar Mulay
current_role: Managing Director, Ajeet Seeds Pvt Ltd (Aurangabad / Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar)
profile: Second-generation head of Ajeet Seeds, one of India's largest cotton-seed companies, founded by his father Padmakar Mulay. Joining when revenue was Rs 18 crore, he grew it to roughly Rs 700 crore by 2015, driven by the Bt cotton hybrid Ajeet 155, and diversified into bajra, corn, wheat, paddy and vegetable seeds.
interesting_fact: The Ajeet 155 Bt cotton hybrid (2006), developed with Mahyco-Monsanto technology, pulled the company back into profit by 2008 and became its breakout product.
deep_cut_fact: He originally aspired to be a civil engineer and join the family construction business, but a 1996 tea-time talk with his father steered him to the College of Agriculture, Pune (graduated 2001) and into seeds.
notes: Private company; corporate general email is the only published route. Agri focus, little energy/data-center angle.

name: N Srinivasan
current_role: Former VC & MD of India Cements (stepped down Dec 2024 after the UltraTech takeover). Promoter figure behind IPL team Chennai Super Kings.
profile: Narayanaswami Srinivasan (b. 1945, Tirunelveli) ran India Cements from 1989 and built it into a major South Indian cement producer. He was also a top cricket administrator: BCCI president and the ICC's first chairman. In December 2024 he sold the family's stake to UltraTech (Aditya Birla Group) and resigned as CEO & MD. He remains the figure most associated with Chennai Super Kings.
interesting_fact: After selling India Cements to UltraTech in 2024, he told staff the sale was driven by cost pressures, price wars and the inability to sell some land. The deal ended a family link to the company: his father, T.S. Narayanaswami, was one of India Cements' first employees.
deep_cut_fact: He has an MS in chemical engineering from the Illinois Institute of Technology in Chicago. He served two terms as Sheriff of Madras (1989–91), was president of the All India Chess Federation, and heads the Tamil Nadu Golf Federation.
notes: Well known in India because of cricket, and his cricket-administration years drew controversy, so outreach should stay on business and the industry. He has no personal website or social accounts that I could find. Best route is probably via Chennai Super Kings Cricket Ltd's corporate office. Source on his exit: https://www.dtnext.in/news/business/india-cements-promoter-n-srinivasan-steps-down-as-ultratech-completes-acquisition-816723

name: Sat Paul Singhla
current_role: Founder & Managing Director, S P Singla Constructions / SPS Construction India Pvt Ltd
profile: Sat Paul Singla (also spelled Singhla) is a civil engineer and first-generation entrepreneur who founded S P Singla Constructions in 1996 with no capital. The privately held firm specialises in river bridges, highways and metro work across ~15 Indian states and reported revenue of Rs 1,150 crore in FY2017, while remaining fully owned by him.
interesting_fact: His company built what it calls India's longest cable-stayed bridge, between Okha and Beyt Dwarka in Gujarat, plus an extradosed bridge across the Ganges between Aunta and Simaria in Bihar.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting out on his own he spent 12 years with small construction firms in Punjab and Haryana building river bridges in J&K, Punjab and Himachal; his first project as an entrepreneur was a small bridge over the Yamuna in 1996 worth just Rs 10 lakh.
notes: Private company, low media profile; Forbes India 'Built To Last' profile is the main press source. Registered office New Delhi, corporate office Panchkula (Haryana). Alive status not confirmed by a recent source.

name: Sheela Ashwin Chiniwalla
profile: Listed on the Hurun India Rich List (2018-2019) with about US$132m, wealth attributed to Parle Products, the Mumbai biscuit maker (Parle-G) owned by the Chauhan family. Presumably a Chauhan family member/shareholder; no public profile found and she is not among the listed directors of Parle Products.
notes: Private family shareholder with no public footprint found. Parle Products current directors are Vijay, Ajay, Arup and Samar Chauhan; any approach would realistically go via the company (parleproducts.com).

name: SV Balasubramaniam
current_role: Chairman, Bannari Amman Sugars Ltd and founder-chairman, Bannari Amman Group (Coimbatore)
profile: Dr. S.V. Balasubramaniam, a chartered accountant and company secretary from Sangampalayam village near Coimbatore, founded the Bannari Amman Group, which grew from sugar in the early 1980s into distilleries, granite, wind power and education. The board re-appointed him as chairman of listed Bannari Amman Sugars in 2025.
interesting_fact: Bannari Amman Group started Tamil Nadu's first biodiesel plant (2007) and runs wind power alongside its sugar, alcohol and granite businesses, using molasses from sugar production for its distilleries.
deep_cut_fact: He hails from Sangampalayam village near Coimbatore and trained as both a chartered accountant and a company secretary before building the group; he also founded the Bannari Amman Institute of Technology in Sathyamangalam.
notes: Elderly founder; son B. Saravanan is MD. Energy angle: wind power, cogeneration, ethanol/biodiesel. Company secretary C. Palaniswamy signs filings; secretary@bannari.com also published in BRSR report.

name: Bhupinder Singh Manhas
current_role: Founder, Harman Finochem Ltd (Mumbai/Aurangabad API manufacturer); not listed among current board directors
profile: Bhupinder Singh Minhas (also spelled Manhas) founded Harman Finochem in 1983, an Indian maker and exporter of active pharmaceutical ingredients and intermediates (45+ APIs, 75+ countries served). The company is now run by family directors Harpreet Singh Minhas and Dr. Gurpreet Singh Minhas; he is presented on the company site as founder.
interesting_fact: Harman Finochem, which he founded in 1983, makes 45+ APIs including 10+ WHO essential medicines and supplies 75+ nations, with approvals from regulators such as Health Canada and Mexico's COFEPRIS.
deep_cut_fact: The company website quotes him as founder: 'At Harman Finochem, our work is guided by a simple principle: to foster health, happiness, and harmony in every life we touch, while staying true to our responsibility towards humanity.'
notes: Name spelled 'Minhas' on company site. He does not appear among current registered directors (Inderjit Kaur, Harpreet, Gurpreet, Savreen Minhas), so he may have retired or passed away - status unverified. Very low public profile; approach via company.

name: Omprakash Inani
current_role: Chairman, Shilpa Medicare Ltd (Raichur, Karnataka); Managing Director, Inok Cottons Pvt Ltd
profile: Omprakash Tulsiram Inani is chairman and a promoter-shareholder of Shilpa Medicare, a Raichur-based maker of oncology APIs, formulations, biologics and CDMO services co-founded with MD Vishnukant Bhutada. With 35+ years in business, he oversees the company's plants and also runs a cotton business, Inok Cottons, in Raichur.
interesting_fact: Shilpa Medicare grew from Raichur, a cotton town in northern Karnataka, into one of India's leading suppliers of oncology active pharmaceutical ingredients; Inani still runs a cotton ginning business alongside it.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond pharma he is a Managing Committee member of the Karnataka State Cotton Association (Hubli), a council member of Raichur's Taranath Shikshana Samsthe (which runs a medical/dental/pharmacy academy), and a trustee of the Akhil Bhartiya Maheshwari Education Trust in Pune.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts or interviews found. Company website lists no press/IR email; route via company enquiry form or company secretary listed in BSE/NSE filings.

name: Vijaykumar Taparia
current_role: Executive (Whole-time) Director, The Supreme Industries Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: V.K. Taparia is a member of the Taparia family that controls The Supreme Industries, India's largest plastics processor (piping systems, moulded furniture, packaging films, industrial products). A B.Com graduate, he has been on Supreme's board since October 1984 and was re-appointed Executive Director at the 2026 AGM with his term running to Sept 2027.
interesting_fact: He has sat on Supreme Industries' board for over four decades (appointed 29 Oct 1984) and personally holds about 244,890 Supreme shares per the 2025-26 annual report.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Company is fronted by Chairman & MD M.P. Taparia, so outreach via the company (registered office Raheja Chambers, Nariman Point, Mumbai) is the realistic route.

name: Sudhir Dhingra
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Orient Craft Ltd (Gurugram)
profile: Sudhir Dhingra founded Orient Craft, one of India's largest garment exporters, supplying global fashion brands from factories around Gurugram. A law graduate from a Punjab cotton-farming family, he started exporting shirts in the 1970s and registered Orient Craft in 1978. The company has since rebuilt, declared itself debt-free and is expanding to Jharkhand.
interesting_fact: He told Outlook Business he wanted Orient Craft to be 'a 32-legged animal' that never depends on a single client; by 2014 it had revenue over Rs 1,151 crore and 30,000+ employees.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Fazilka near the Pakistan border, he studied law like his father and grandfather; after a 1972 US trip a London trader friend asked him for 1,000 'cheese cloth' shirts, made in Delhi at Rs 15 each - the Rs 15,000 he calls his 'seed capital'.
notes: Company site orientcraft.com was unreachable when checked; recent press releases (Newsvoir, May 2024+) cover the debt-free turnaround and Jharkhand/Ranchi expansion - a positive hook. Avoid the NPA/debt history.

name: Jimmy William Almeida
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, G.M. Breweries Ltd (BSE 507488 / NSE GMBREW)
profile: Jimmy William Almeida Kashyap founded G.M. Breweries in Mumbai in 1981 and took it public in 1993. It is now Maharashtra's largest country-liquor maker, best known for its orange-flavoured G.M. Santra brand. He is still chairman and MD; shareholders reappointed him as MD through March 2028, and he owns a majority stake.
interesting_fact: G.M. Breweries started out bottling 200 cases a day. Its fully automatic plant at Virar, near Mumbai, can now turn out about 50,000 cases a day, and the company says it has paid a dividend every year since its 1993 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Country liquor used to be sold only in 750 ml and 375 ml bottles. According to the company, Almeida introduced the 180 ml bottle to the industry and was also the first to use PET (plastic) bottles for it.
notes: Low media profile. Filings use several name forms: Jimmy Almeida, Jimmy William Almeida Kashyap. The company secretary, Sandeep Kutchhi, is the formal contact route (https://www.gmbreweries.com/overview.html).

name: Mridu Hari Dalmia
current_role: Former Joint President, OCL India; family-business investor (current directorships unclear; listed by MarketScreener at First Capital India Ltd)
profile: Mridu Hari Dalmia is a son of industrialist Jaidayal Dalmia. With his brothers he controlled OCL India (formerly Orissa Cement), the cement and refractories company, and served as its Joint President. In 2015 he and his family trust sold a combined ~26.6% of OCL to Dalmia Cement (Bharat), a deal worth about US$165m. Hurun lists him as UAE-based.
interesting_fact: OCL changed its name from Orissa Cement Ltd in 1996 to reflect its non-cement ventures. After Jaidayal Dalmia's death it was controlled by his sons Ajay, Mridu and Raghu Hari Dalmia. OCL later became part of Dalmia Bharat.
notes: Very low public profile; I found no interviews, website or social accounts. 'Alive' could not be confirmed from a recent source. His directorships are listed inconsistently across data aggregators, so check MCA filings (DIN 00009529) before approaching. 2015 stake-sale source: https://globalcement.com/news/8916-ocl-india-and-dalmia-bharat-merger-moves-ahead

name: Seema Suryavanshi
current_role: Promoter/shareholder of Dilip Buildcon Ltd (Bhopal); former executive director (2006-2010)
profile: Seema Suryavanshi is a promoter of Dilip Buildcon, the Bhopal road and infrastructure EPC contractor founded by her husband Dilip Suryavanshi, who is chairman. She was a director of the company from 2006 to 2010 and has sat on boards of group entities such as Suryavanshi Infrastructure and DBL toll-road SPVs.
interesting_fact: Dilip Buildcon grew from a small Bhopal contractor into one of India's largest road builders; she was on its board when it incorporated as a company in 2006.
notes: Low public profile. Best route is through the company (head of IR Gautam Jain is named on earnings calls) or via Dilip/Rohan Suryavanshi. Her current board status is unclear: sources conflict.

name: AVS Raju
current_role: Deceased (13 Oct 2026). He was Founder and Chairman Emeritus of NCC Limited (formerly Nagarjuna Construction Company), Hyderabad.
profile: Dr Alluri Venkata Satyanarayana Raju, founder of NCC Limited and a Padma Shri awardee, died in Hyderabad on 13 October 2026, aged 89.
notes: Died 13 Oct 2026 (Construction World, 14 Oct 2026). NCC also disclosed to the exchanges that he ceased to be a promoter. Per the instructions, I skipped the rest of his profile.

name: Sajan Kumar Bansal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Skipper Limited (Kolkata)
profile: Commerce graduate who in 1981 incorporated Skipper Investments Ltd, later Skipper Steels and then Skipper Ltd. Starting with steel poles for telecom, he built Skipper into a major Indian maker of power transmission & distribution towers, plus polymer pipes; he still runs it as CMD.
interesting_fact: Skipper began as a small maker of 'Hamilton' steel poles for telecom connectivity and became a leading supplier of telecom poles and masts in India in the 1980s-90s before pivoting to power transmission towers.
notes: Skipper's T&D tower business is directly relevant to grid/energy-infrastructure topics. mail@ is the company's general inbox, not personal. Also Managing Trustee of Skipper Foundation.

name: Bharat Naresh Oberoi
current_role: Joint Managing Director and Promoter, Powerica Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Bharat Oberoi is a promoter and Joint MD (since 2003) of Powerica, the Mumbai power-solutions firm his father Naresh Chander Oberoi founded in 1984. Powerica builds diesel generator sets and medium-speed large generators for standby/prime power (a key data-center backup market) and since 2008 has been a wind IPP and wind EPC/O&M contractor. He joined in 1994 and leads its marketing side.
interesting_fact: Powerica began as a diesel-generator business in 1984, added medium-speed large generators in 1996, and in 2008 moved into wind energy as an independent power producer, later adding wind EPC and O&M services.
notes: Low public profile; last on Hurun India in 2018. Backup-power gensets for Indian data centers plus wind IPP make a natural energy/data-center angle. Route via company. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so no sourced personal deep-cut.

name: Rajas R Doshi
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, The Indian Hume Pipe Company Ltd (since 14 April 1994)
profile: Rajas Ratanchand Doshi, a civil engineer from the Walchand-Hirachand business family, has run The Indian Hume Pipe Company (est. 1926), a Mumbai-listed maker of concrete/steel water pipes and builder of water-supply and irrigation projects. He has spent 49+ years at the company and also sits on the boards of family foundations and the IMC Chamber of Commerce.
interesting_fact: Indian Hume Pipe was established in 1926 to manufacture and popularise Hume pipes in India, and today executes large urban and rural water-supply pipeline projects; Doshi has been its chairman for over three decades.
deep_cut_fact: He started at the bottom: a B.E. in civil engineering, he joined Indian Hume Pipe in 1981 as a Senior Executive at its Wadala (Mumbai) factory, then rose via Chief Engineer and General Manager to Joint MD in 1988 and CMD in 1994.
notes: Company emails are corporate (general info / investor relations), not personal. Low media profile; a water-infrastructure angle fits better than energy/data centres.

name: Mohan Anand Chandavarkar
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, FDC Limited (Mumbai) since 1 April 2026
profile: Second-generation leader of FDC Limited, the Mumbai drugmaker his father Anand Chandavarkar started as Fairdeal Corporation (incorporated 1940) to import and distribute medicines and infant foods. FDC makes ~147 brands across anti-infectives, gastro, ophthalmology and more, and is best known for Electral oral rehydration salts. Long-time MD, he was re-designated Chairman & MD in April 2026.
interesting_fact: FDC began as an importer/distributor (Fairdeal Corporation) of drugs, infant foods and surgical appliances before turning manufacturer; its Electral ORS is one of India's best-known rehydration brands.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews or personal social accounts found. Route via company secretarial/investor desk (Mumbai, tel published on filings). Pharma, not energy/data-center.

name: Anupama Menda
current_role: Director, RMZ Corp Holdings Pvt Ltd (Menda family, RMZ Corp, Bengaluru) per company registry listing
profile: Anupama Manoj Menda is a member of the Bengaluru Menda family behind RMZ Corp, the commercial real-estate group founded in 2002 by Arjun Menda and his sons Raj and Manoj; registry data lists her as a director of RMZ Corp Holdings since Dec 2019. Hurun India listed her (2017-18) with RMZ wealth. RMZ now spans real estate, digital infrastructure and private capital.
interesting_fact: RMZ, the family's company, now runs a Digital Infrastructure business line alongside real estate and private capital, relevant to a data-center podcast.
notes: Very low public profile. Likely the same person as 'Anu Menda', described as founder/managing trustee of RMZ Foundation (public art, Sustainable Health Initiative) in a Yale profile and wiki drafts, but that link is NOT confirmed; RMZ's 2021 CSR policy lists only Arjun, Raj and Manoj Menda as trustees. Verify before referencing foundation work. Registry source: qorpiq.com (RMZ Corp Holdings).

name: Neetu Menda
current_role: Director, RMZ Corp Holdings Pvt Ltd and RMZ Realtors Pvt Ltd (Bengaluru)
profile: Neetu (Raj) Menda is a member of the Menda family behind RMZ Corp, the Bengaluru commercial real-estate and infrastructure group founded in 2002 by Arjun Menda and sons Raj and Manoj Menda. Corporate registry data lists her as a director of RMZ group holding entities; she has no public executive role.
interesting_fact: RMZ's governing Supervisory Board is made up entirely of Menda family members (Raj, Manoj, Sidharth, Mihir and Kunal Menda).
notes: Very private; virtually no public profile. Registry names her 'Neetu Raj Menda' (likely Raj Menda's family) - relationship not confirmed. Best route is via RMZ corporate (contact@rmz.com).

name: Ajitbhai Champaklal Mehta
current_role: Chairman Emeritus & Non-Executive Director, AvenuesAI Limited (formerly Infibeam Avenues Ltd), Gandhinagar, India
profile: Gujarat businessman (Ajit Mehta) who served as non-executive chairman of Infibeam Avenues, the e-commerce and payments group (CCAvenue) founded in 2007 by his son Vishal Mehta. He is now chairman emeritus as the renamed AvenuesAI moves into enterprise AI infrastructure alongside payments.
interesting_fact: Infibeam Avenues renamed itself AvenuesAI. It is based in GIFT City, Gujarat, and says it is building 'enterprise-grade AI infrastructure' alongside its CCAvenue payments business.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, he spent about 20 years in textiles, chemicals, building materials and construction, then more than 16 years in the automobile industry.
notes: Low public profile. Most interviews go to his son Vishal Mehta (Chairman & MD). Best route is the company's corporate communications. The Hurun 2018 wealth figure probably reflects family holdings.

name: Sudhir Mohanlal Jatia
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Safari Industries (India) Ltd
profile: Mumbai-based luggage industry veteran who previously ran VIP Industries as MD, then acquired control of Safari Industries in 2011 (MD since April 2012). He turned Safari into a fast-growing challenger brand by shifting to soft and polycarbonate luggage, backpacks (Genius, Genie) and online channels; his wealth is his Safari stake.
interesting_fact: After leaving VIP Industries, India's largest luggage maker, he built rival Safari from about Rs 67 crore revenue in FY12 to roughly INR 5.7bn by 2018, nearly a tenfold increase.
deep_cut_fact: Rather than build a new Rs 40-50 crore plant, he converted Safari's existing Halol factory to polycarbonate luggage, lifting capacity from 27,000 to 80,000 pieces a month for about Rs 22 crore; he also turned down a PE offer that would have made him a minority holder and relisted Safari on the NYSE.
notes: Studied commerce at Mumbai University and attended Harvard Business School's Owner/President Management program (per Safari site). Also a director of the Association for Development of Luggage and Accessories. Manufacturing-localisation angle (China sourcing to India) could suit the podcast.

name: Vasant Laxminarayan Rathi
current_role: Promoter and Non-Executive Director, Advanced Enzyme Technologies Ltd (NSE: ADVENZYMES); heads its US subsidiaries
profile: V. L. Rathi, a pharmacist turned enzyme entrepreneur, co-founded Rathi Papains (1978), set up Cal-India Foods in the US (1985) and has been with Advanced Enzyme Technologies since 1993. The Thane-based enzyme and probiotics maker listed in India in 2016; from the US he runs its American subsidiaries.
interesting_fact: Advanced Enzymes grew from a family papain business into one of India's largest enzyme makers, with US and European arms. It owns Germany's evoxx technologies in Monheim am Rhein.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Rathi Papains (1978), made enzymes from papain, the protein-digesting enzyme taken from papaya latex. He trained as a pharmacist (B.Pharm, Nagpur University) and earned an MS at the University of Hawaii.
notes: Categorized as Chemicals/Petrochemicals 'energy', but the business is industrial and nutritional enzymes, so the fit for an energy podcast is weak (enzymes are used in biofuel/biogas, which could be an angle). Low media profile; route via the US subsidiaries (Cal-India Foods / AST Enzymes in California) or the company's general email.

name: Satish Parakh
current_role: Managing Director, Ashoka Buildcon Ltd (Nashik, India)
profile: Civil engineer who joined the Ashoka Group in 1982 and rose to Managing Director of Ashoka Buildcon, one of India's largest highway developers (EPC plus 35+ PPP/BOT road projects). He led its diversification into power transmission/distribution EPC, railways and city gas distribution; his wealth stems from his shareholding in the listed company.
interesting_fact: Ashoka Buildcon was an early mover in India's build-operate-transfer (BOT) road model from the 1990s and has even built a road network for the Housing Development Corporation in the Maldives.
deep_cut_fact: His association with Ashoka began in 1982 and he has received the 'Industry Doyen' award from the Construction Industry Development Council; in interviews he credits the company's in-house highway research facility and its policy of avoiding 'ambitious bidding'.

public_contacts.value: Stellar IR Advisors (investor relations advisor) - vgaurang@stellar-ir.com

notes: Power T&D EPC business is the energy angle. Low public profile beyond trade-press interviews (NBM&CW, Construction World).

name: Manoj Kumar
current_role: Whole-time Director, RSPL Ltd (RSPL Group, Kanpur); oversees the group's dairy business
profile: Manoj (Kumar) Gyanchandani is the elder son of RSPL founder-chairman Murli Dhar Gyanchandani and a promoter/whole-time director of RSPL Ltd (since 2008), maker of Ghadi detergent. The Kanpur-based group has diversified into dairy (Namaste India), footwear (Red Chief), real estate and 50+ MW of wind/solar power; Manoj runs the dairy arm.
interesting_fact: RSPL operates wind and solar plants across India generating over 50.1 MW of renewable energy, alongside its FMCG business that employs 25,000+ people.
deep_cut_fact: Ghadi broke into a Nirma/Surf-dominated market by making its detergent white (rivals were yellow or blue), with the tagline 'Pehle istemaal karein phir vishwas karein' (First use it, then trust it).
notes: Hurun lists him as 'Manoj Kumar'; company registry (DIN 00049387) shows him as Manoj (Kumar) Gyanchandani, whole-time director of RSPL Ltd. Family is notably low-profile; only the general corporate inbox is published. RSPL renewable-energy arm is a possible energy-podcast angle.

name: Rahul Gyanchandani
current_role: Joint Managing Director, RSPL Group (Ghadi detergent), Kanpur
profile: Second-generation leader of Kanpur-based RSPL Group, founded in 1988 by Murli Dhar and Bimal Kumar Gyanchandani with Ghadi detergent, now one of India's largest detergent brands. As Joint MD he fronts Ghadi's marketing (e.g. the Madhuri Dixit 'Vishwas Ki Pariksha' campaign) and launches such as Ghadi Rapid Wash liquid detergent.
interesting_fact: Beyond detergent, RSPL has diversified into dairy (Namaste India), footwear, real estate and renewable energy, operating wind and solar plants across India generating over 50 MW.
deep_cut_fact: RSPL began as Rohit Surfactants Pvt. Ltd. in 1988; in 2006 four family detergent companies, including one named Rahul Detergents Pvt. Ltd., were merged into RSPL, and Ghadi Industries was folded in in 2008.
notes: Family is known as low-profile ('silent billionaire' coverage of Murli Dhar Gyanchandani). Forbes wealth likely listed for the family; Rahul appears as company spokesperson in campaign press releases. Only general company email published.

name: Rohit Gyanchandani
current_role: Director, RSPL Group (maker of Ghadi detergent), Kanpur, India
profile: Second-generation director of Kanpur-based RSPL Group, the family FMCG conglomerate behind Ghadi, one of India's best-selling detergent brands, founded in 1988 by his father's generation (Murli Dhar and Bimal Kumar Gyanchandani). Alongside brother Rahul he helps run the group, reportedly focusing on international markets and hygiene/personal-care brands.
interesting_fact: Energy angle: RSPL has 15 solar plants totalling about 50.1 MW and built a ₹40bn+ soda-ash plant in Devbhumi Dwarka, Gujarat (commissioned FY2019-20) to backward-integrate its detergent supply chain.
deep_cut_fact: The group was originally incorporated in Kanpur in 1988 as 'Rohit Surfactants Pvt. Ltd.' (later renamed RSPL Ltd.); a predecessor company merged in 2006 was named 'Rohit Soaps & Detergents Pvt. Ltd.'
notes: Family is famously low-profile ('silent billionaires'). He was quoted as Director in RSPL's 50-year anniversary release (https://www.outlookbusiness.com/spotlight/news-wire/from-kanpur-to-global-rspl-group-celebrates-50-years-contributing-to-india-s-growth-story). The division-of-responsibility detail comes from a Wikipedia mirror, so treat it as indicative. The deep-cut fact doesn't say the company was named after him, so don't present it that way.

name: Rishabh H Mariwala
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Sharrp Ventures (Mariwala family investment office); Non-Executive Director, Marico Ltd
profile: Son of Marico founder Harsh Mariwala. Worked at Marico's Kaya skin clinics (2007-10), then left to build his own soap brand before founding Sharrp Ventures (c.2014-15), the family's consumer-focused investment office. Early backer of Nykaa and Honasa (Mamaearth); the office has invested in ~40 companies and 18 funds.
interesting_fact: Sharrp Ventures was an early investor in both Nykaa and Honasa Consumer (Mamaearth), two of India's best-known consumer IPOs; he says the firm runs on 'long-term patient capital'.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial start was selling soaps out of a small shed in Sewri, Mumbai, building on his mother's soap-making hobby; he later launched the brand Pure Scents (2015) and sold it in 2020 to focus on investing. He has said of Marico: 'I sensed the organisation's culture, and I realised I did not fit in.'
notes: Accessible, podcast-friendly investor (has appeared on Dezerv and LetsVenture podcasts). Focus is consumer brands, not energy/data centers. Best route: Sharrp Ventures contact email.

name: Suresh Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Chairman, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Samrat flour brand), Parakh Group, Pune
profile: Younger son of Parakh Group founder Harakchand K. Parakh (1930-2015), Suresh Parakh is a flour-milling veteran who chairs Parakh Agro Industries, maker of Samrat atta, besan and oil. The family's Parakh Foods built the Gemini edible-oil brand, sold to Cargill in 2004-05; the Pune group now spans FMCG, flexible packaging, real estate (Gemini Housing) and wind power.
interesting_fact: Parakh Group's energy arm, Parakh Energy, runs 8.3 MW of wind turbines (4 Suzlon, 2 Vestas) in Dhule, Maharashtra, feeding the western regional grid.
deep_cut_fact: He drove the adoption of Swiss Bühler milling technology in the group's flour mills, which combine traditional stone chakkis with Bühler machinery, and personally heads the bulk flour sales business, with some customers loyal for 25+ years. B.Com, Maharashtra Mandal College, Pune.
notes: Primarily a food/FMCG businessman; the energy link is the family's wind assets and former edible-oil refining (Gemini sold to Cargill: https://www.foodnavigator.com/Article/2011/03/29/Acquisition-boosts-Cargill-brand-portfolio-in-India). Elder brother Prakash Parakh led group expansion. Low-fit for energy podcast.

name: AD Padmasingh Isaac
current_role: Founder and Chairman/Managing Director, Aachi Group (Aachi Masala Foods Pvt Ltd), Chennai
profile: A first-generation entrepreneur from Nazareth in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, Padmasingh Isaac worked in sales at Godrej in the early 1980s before founding Aachi Masala in 1995-96. Selling Rs 2 sachets of ready curry masala to rural and working households, he built Aachi into a South Indian spice and packaged-food group reported at Rs 1,000+ crore revenue with about 3,500 staff.
interesting_fact: Aachi was rated 'Asia's Fastest Growing FMCG Brand' (2014) and 'India's No 1 Most Trusted Brand 2015' (Trust Research Advisory); he won TiECon Chennai's 'Extreme Entrepreneur of the Year 2010'.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published author: his book 'Enjoy Success, Relish Failures' (Rupa Publications) draws on his early struggles, and he holds advisory roles at the Indian Institute of Crop Processing Technology, Thanjavur, and NIFTEM in Haryana.
notes: Alive status assumed (no death reports found), but no 2024-26 news coverage turned up. Only a general company/customer-care email is published; no press office. He is a motivational speaker at youth forums, so speaking invitations or his publisher (Rupa) could be routes in. Hurun data is old (2018-19).

name: Sureshbhai Jayantibhai Patel
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Bodal Chemicals Ltd (NSE: BODALCHEM), Ahmedabad.
profile: Suresh J. Patel founded Bodal Chemicals in Ahmedabad around 1989-90 as a small vinyl sulphone maker and built it into a vertically integrated producer of dye intermediates, textile/leather/paper dyestuffs and basic chemicals (sulphuric acid etc.), exporting to 40+ countries. He has been chairman & MD since 2006, the year the company went public.
interesting_fact: Bodal is one of very few dye makers integrated from basic chemicals through intermediates to finished dyestuffs; by 2015 it ran eight Gujarat plants with ~2,500 staff and sales above Rs 1,000 crore, exporting 80% of its dyestuff output.
deep_cut_fact: Bodal began in 1989 as 'JK Pharma', a two-man partnership of Suresh Patel and Ramesh Patel with capacity of just 60 tonnes a year of vinyl sulphone; it became Bodal Chemicals Pvt Ltd in 1994.
notes: Chemicals, not energy/data-center; modest wealth (Hurun India 2017 only). Director Bhavin Patel runs the dyestuff division. Best route: company secretarial/info email.

name: Madan Mohan Dhanuka
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, I G Petrochemicals Ltd (Dhanuka Group), Mumbai (per Simply Wall St/Investing.com; some sites list Nikunj Dhanuka as chairman)
profile: Senior figure of the Dhanuka Group and a director of I G Petrochemicals since its incorporation in October 1988. IGPL, set up in technical collaboration with Germany's Lurgi, is India's largest maker of phthalic anhydride (used in plasticisers, paints and resins), with plants at Taloja, Maharashtra; he also sits on the board of Mysore Petro Chemicals.
interesting_fact: He has served on IGPL's board for more than 35 years, since the company's founding in 1988, as it grew into India's largest phthalic anhydride producer.

public_contacts.value: ssingh@igpetro.com (Company Secretary Sudhir R Singh, published company contact)

notes: Chairman title conflicts across data sites; confirm in latest IGPL annual report. Day-to-day leadership by younger family members (Nikunj, Mayank Dhanuka). Low public profile.

name: Abhay Vithaldas Udeshi
current_role: Chairman, Jayant Agro-Organics Ltd (Mumbai; BSE/NSE listed)
profile: Mumbai industrialist who succeeded his father Vithaldas Udeshi as chairman of Jayant Agro-Organics, a castor-oil and castor-derivatives company with an estimated 35-40% share of the global castor oil market. The group runs JVs with France's Arkema and a Japanese partner, plus hybrid castor seed and pharma-grade oil operations.
interesting_fact: He notes India produces nearly 90% of the world's castor oil; Jayant says it was the first company in India to process castor seeds into oil, starting in 1952.
deep_cut_fact: He helped create the Sustainable Castor Association (with Arkema, BASF and NGO Solidaridad), which runs a sustainable castor farming code and certification for Indian farmers and had grown to 31 global members by 2024.
notes: University of Baroda graduate; director of the Sustainable Castor Association. Energy relevance is modest (company has a power-generation segment; castor-based bio-chemicals). Family-run board.

name: Brij Bhushan Agarwal
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Shyam Metalics and Energy Ltd (and subsidiary Shyam SEL and Power); President, Indian Chamber of Commerce
profile: Kolkata-based industrialist (B.Com, University of Calcutta) who has led Shyam Metalics since its inception in 2001, building it into an integrated metals producer (ferroalloys, iron and steel, aluminium foil) with captive power plants in West Bengal and Odisha; listed on NSE/BSE in 2021. He owns roughly 9.5% directly, with the promoter family holding the majority.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Shyam Metalics became India's largest producer of ferroalloys (per CRISIL, as of Feb 2021); its integrated plants run partly on captive power, hence 'Energy' in the name.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Indian Chamber of Commerce's National Expert Committee on Minerals and Metals in 2019 and that October won Zee Business's 'Inspirational Leader of the Year' award in the 'Dare to Dream' category, before rising to ICC Senior VP and then President.
notes: Hurun India figure ($132m, 2019) is stale; promoter-family stake is worth much more today. Head of IR Pankaj Harlalka appears on earnings calls; IR partner is EY (per call transcripts). ICC presidency gives a second route via Indian Chamber of Commerce, Kolkata.

name: Sridhar Vembu
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Zoho Corporation (stepped down as CEO in January 2025)
profile: Sridhar Vembu co-founded AdventNet with his brothers in 1996. It was renamed Zoho in 2009 and grew into a bootstrapped SaaS company with no outside investors. He has an IIT Madras degree and a Princeton PhD and started his career as a wireless engineer at Qualcomm. He handed the CEO role to Shailesh Davey in January 2025 to focus on R&D as Chief Scientist, and he runs Zoho's rural-development work from Tenkasi, Tamil Nadu.
interesting_fact: He moved from the Bay Area to the village of Mathalamparai in Tenkasi district in 2019, and Zoho set up offices there to bring product development to rural India. He received the Padma Shri in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004 he started Zoho Schools (originally Zoho University), which trains rural students in software as an alternative to college. Zoho says 15-20% of its engineers have no college degree.
notes: Very active on X (@svembu) and accessible to podcasters, especially on deep tech, rural R&D and Indian manufacturing; Zoho is also building chips and its own data-centre infrastructure. Hurun's figure is outdated: Forbes put Vembu and his siblings at about $6B in October 2025. Avoid personal topics, as his divorce litigation is public.

name: Sultan Ali
current_role: Founder & Chairman, IB Group (Abis Exports India Pvt Ltd), Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh
profile: Co-founded IB Group (Indian Broiler Group) in Rajnandgaon, Chhattisgarh, with his younger brother Bahadur Ali. It grew from a small poultry farm in the mid-1980s into one of India's largest integrated poultry, feed and protein groups. Abis Exports, incorporated in 1998, was the group's backward-integration arm. He chairs the group and oversees its CSR.
interesting_fact: IB Group says it began with a small poultry farm (500 chicks) in 1984, started on the advice of a veterinarian. Some company sources date it to 1985. It became an integrated protein group running contract farming with thousands of rural farmers.
deep_cut_fact: According to his brother's account on the IB Group site, Sultan Ali started the poultry venture in Rajnandgaon with 500 chicks in 1984 after a veterinarian suggested poultry. The company calls 1984-1996 its formative growth period.
notes: Low personal media profile. His brother Bahadur Ali (MD) is the group's public face and does more interviews. The IB Group site was unreachable (503) during research, so no published email was confirmed. Try the group's corporate site or investor-relations page.

name: Sumitra Agarwal
current_role: Director in the Delhi-branch Haldiram's companies (e.g. Haldiram Marketing Pvt Ltd), per company-registry aggregators; current status unclear
profile: A member of the Delhi-based Agarwal family behind Haldiram Snacks, who appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2019. Registry aggregators list her (DIN 00011417) as a director of Haldiram Marketing, Haldiram Ethnic Foods and Haldiram Snacks entities. No public biography or media profile was found.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's traces back to a sweets shop opened in Bikaner in 1937 by Ganga Bhishen 'Haldiram' Agarwal. Hurun has named Haldiram Snacks India's most valuable unlisted company (about Rs 63,000 crore, 2024).
notes: Very private, with no interviews or social accounts found. Her exact place in the family and her current directorships could not be confirmed: aggregators disagree, and one shows her Haldiram Marketing role ending in Jan 2026. Any contact would go through the Haldiram's corporate office. Low priority.

name: Umesh Agarwal
current_role: Director, Haldiram Snacks Pvt Ltd (Delhi branch of Haldiram's); also director of Haldi Ram Products and Haldiram's Marketing
profile: Umesh (Kumar) Agarwal is a member of the Delhi branch of the Agarwal family behind Haldiram's, the snack brand that grew from a 1937 Bikaner sweet shop. Company filings list him (DIN 00011472) as a director of Haldiram Snacks and related entities; the Delhi business has since merged into Haldiram Snacks Food, which took investment from Temasek in 2025.
interesting_fact: In an October 2026 interview he argued that 'consistency is not created by writing a standard' and that food safety at Haldiram's has to be a daily culture rather than something prepared for before inspections.
notes: Several Umesh Agarwals are linked to Haldiram's in press (Umesh Kumar Agarwal of Haldiram's Marketing; 'Umesh Madhu Agarwal', interviewed by Zomato's Deepinder Goyal in 2024). Filings tie DIN 00011472 to Haldiram Snacks; confirm which person Hurun means before outreach. Family is private; corporate channel is the realistic route.

name: Y Kasyap Reddy
current_role: Managing Director, Medha Group (Medha Servo Drives Pvt Ltd), Hyderabad
profile: Kasyap Reddy Yadavelli runs Medha, a privately held Hyderabad rail-technology group founded in 1984 that supplies propulsion electronics, traction motors and signalling systems to Indian Railways. Under him Medha has moved into full rolling stock (Vande Bharat propulsion, train sets) and opened a 100-acre coach factory near Hyderabad in 2023.
interesting_fact: Medha's Kondakal plant, inaugurated in June 2023, was billed as India's largest private rail coach factory, with planned capacity of 500 coaches and 50 locomotives a year; Medha also has a JV with Swiss maker Stadler Rail.
deep_cut_fact: Beyond rail, Medha has worked on solar inverters, battery-electric vehicle propulsion and canal automation, and signed an MoU to develop large propulsion motors for the Indian Navy.
notes: Private company, low-profile MD. marketing@ is the general sales/marketing address (no dedicated press address found). Relevant energy angle: electrification/propulsion, solar inverters.

name: Y Swetha
profile: Listed (~US$132m) with wealth from Medha Servo Drives, a privately held Hyderabad maker of rail propulsion/traction systems, signalling and, more recently, solar inverters and EV drives. No public source found identifying Y Swetha's role at the company; public director lists name other Yadavelli/Nookala family members.
interesting_fact: Medha Servo Drives (founded 1984, Hyderabad) supplies rail propulsion equipment to 50+ countries and has diversified into solar string inverters (250 kW unit launched at Intersolar India 2024).
notes: Identity/role could not be confirmed; likely a family shareholder of a private company with no public profile. Company itself is relevant (rail electrification, solar inverters). Approach via company only.

name: Mark D. McClain
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Director, SailPoint, Inc. (Nasdaq: SAIL), Austin, Texas
profile: Serial identity-security founder: started Waveset Technologies in 2000 (sold to Sun Microsystems in 2003) and co-founded SailPoint in 2005. He took SailPoint public in 2017, sold it to Thoma Bravo for $6.9bn in 2022, and led it back to public markets in February 2025; he remains CEO as SailPoint pushes into securing AI agent identities.
interesting_fact: He wrote a leadership book, 'Joy and Success at Work: Building Organizations that Don't Suck the Life Out of People' (ForbesBooks, 2020), critiquing perk-driven 'pseudo-cultures'.
deep_cut_fact: After selling Waveset to Sun Microsystems he served as Sun's VP of Software Marketing, then carried Waveset's 'Four I's' core values (integrity, innovation, impact, individuals) into SailPoint.
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder CEO who speaks often on culture and leadership (book, podcasts). The 'Four I's' values are also described in an Austin Technology Council post: https://www.austintechnologycouncil.org/?p=484

name: Matthew H. Peltz
current_role: Partner and Co-Head of Research, Trian Fund Management; Wendy's director (non-exec Vice Chairman since Nov 2021; verify current board status)
profile: Son of activist investor Nelson Peltz, Matt Peltz joined Trian's investment team in 2008 after two years as a Goldman Sachs investment-banking analyst, and is now a partner and co-head of research. He has sat on Wendy's board since December 2015 and served as non-executive Vice Chairman from 2021; Trian and the Peltzes hold a roughly 15% stake.
interesting_fact: He previously served on the board of ARG Holding Corporation, the former parent of Arby's, from 2012 to 2015, one of several restaurant brands in the Peltz family's orbit.
deep_cut_fact: Outside finance he is a trustee of the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York.
notes: MarketScreener lists his Wendy's director/vice-chair role as ending in 2025 while Wendy's bio page still shows him; check the latest proxy. Media route is via Trian or Wendy's corporate communications.

name: Darren M Rebelez
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Casey's General Stores (CASY)
profile: West Point graduate and former Army Ranger who built a career in fuel and convenience retail. He spent time at ExxonMobil and Thornton Oil, was COO of 7-Eleven, and served as president of IHOP. He became Casey's CEO in 2019 and Chair in 2023. Casey's is the third-largest US convenience-store chain and is known for its pizza, and it joined the S&P 500 in 2026.
interesting_fact: Before his civilian career he was an Army Ranger and Gulf War veteran. He is a San Diego native and earned a BS in Foreign Area Studies at West Point.
deep_cut_fact: Before oil and c-stores, his early civilian jobs were at Fuddruckers and PepsiCo. He told CSP Daily he spent his whole post-military career 'either in the restaurant business or the' convenience business.

public_contacts.value: Casey's media relations: Katie Petru, (515) 446-6772 (company line)
Casey's investor relations: Sam James, (515) 446-6506 (company line, Aug 2026 release)

notes: Casey's press releases list phone contacts but no email. Energy angle: Casey's is a large fuel retailer, roughly 2,900 stores across the Midwest/South.

name: Scott H. Baxter
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Kontoor Brands (Wrangler, Lee, Helly Hansen); director at Lowe's
profile: Has led Kontoor Brands since August 2018, when it was spun out of VF Corp as the home of Wrangler and Lee. He has been chairman since 2021. Before VF (2007-2018, including group president roles over The North Face and Vans) he spent about 20 years at Nestle, PepsiCo and Home Depot, where he was SVP running the services division.
interesting_fact: Spent the first half of his career in suits at consumer and retail companies. He now wears denim to work and says he often gives away Wrangler and Lee clothes when someone compliments them: 'It shocks people, but 99% of the time, they take it.'
deep_cut_fact: A history graduate, he turned down a job offer from the US Secret Service to start his career at Nestle.
notes: Kontoor is based in Greensboro, NC. The Brunswick Review interview (2023) is a good source of rapport material.

name: Glade M. Knight
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Apple Hospitality REIT, Inc. (APLE), Richmond, VA
profile: Utah-born, BYU-educated (BA, MBA) real estate entrepreneur who built the 'Apple' family of non-traded REITs and earlier ran Cornerstone Realty Income Trust (1993-2005). He founded Apple Hospitality, a lodging REIT owning Marriott- and Hilton-branded select-service hotels, was CEO until 2014 when his son Justin took over, and remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: He is the founding figure of Southern Virginia University, which he reorganised in the 1990s and chaired from 1996 to 2015; its stadium bears the Knight name.
deep_cut_fact: A competitive horseman with ranches in Virginia and Texas, he offered SVU students a yearly 'Cowboy Up' scholarship honouring his father 'Mac' Knight, whom he calls 'my champion and the real cowboy'; the campus knight statue bears Mac's likeness.
notes: Born 1944; low media profile. Wikipedia notes an LDS patriarch role and close friendship with Bill Marriott. Avoid referencing the 2014 SEC disclosure fines.

name: Michael Pompeo
current_role: Director, VEON Ltd. (since May 2024) and Kyivstar board member; founder, Pompeo Foundation; former US Secretary of State
profile: West Point graduate and Harvard Law alumnus who built and sold Wichita aerospace-parts maker Thayer Aerospace, ran oilfield-equipment firm Sentry International, then served as Kansas congressman, CIA director (2017-18) and US Secretary of State (2018-21). He now sits on the boards of VEON and its Ukrainian unit Kyivstar and runs the Pompeo Foundation.
interesting_fact: He graduated first in his class at West Point in 1986, majoring in engineering management.
deep_cut_fact: In 1996 he and West Point classmates bought three Wichita aircraft-parts shops and a St. Louis tool-and-die firm and named the company Thayer Aerospace after Sylvanus Thayer, the 'father of West Point'; he later ran Sentry International, an oilfield equipment manufacturer – relevant energy-industry roots.
notes: High-profile political figure; likely routed through a speakers bureau or his foundation. Kyivstar board role was framed as safeguarding US investors in Ukraine's largest mobile operator.

name: Mark A Goldsmith
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Revolution Medicines (Nasdaq: RVMD)
profile: Mark A. Goldsmith, MD, PhD (Princeton; UCSF) has led Redwood City-based Revolution Medicines since 2014, building it around RAS(ON) inhibitors for RAS-addicted cancers. Its lead drug daraxonrasib showed a major overall-survival benefit in the Phase 3 RASolute 302 trial in previously treated metastatic pancreatic cancer and was reported FDA-approved (as RASONQUE) in Aug 2026.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 Revolution reported daraxonrasib met all primary and key secondary endpoints, including overall survival, in a pivotal Phase 3 trial in metastatic pancreatic cancer, one of the hardest-to-treat cancers.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech management he was an academic HIV researcher: a UCSF School of Medicine faculty member who ran a research lab at the Gladstone Institute of Virology and Immunology; he later founded and led Cogentus Pharmaceuticals (2006-09) and ran Constellation Pharmaceuticals.
notes: Biotech, not energy; podcast angle would be entrepreneurship/company-building. Deep-cut source (The Org) is marked unverified; career history is corroborated by MarketScreener bio pages. Aug 2026 FDA approval taken from company release summarized in search results.

name: William D. Banfield
current_role: Chief Business Officer, Rocket Companies (RKT), Detroit
profile: Bill Banfield is a 25+-year Rocket Mortgage veteran who joined in 1999 and rose through capital markets, serving as Chief Risk Officer and EVP of Capital Markets before becoming Chief Business Officer in March 2024. He oversees capital markets, mortgage servicing and government affairs - a remit that grew with Rocket's acquisition of servicing giant Mr. Cooper.
interesting_fact: He sits on the Mortgage Bankers Association board of directors, giving him a voice in national housing-finance policy alongside his Rocket role.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Rocket (then Quicken Loans) in 1999, he worked at two smaller Michigan-area lenders, MCA Mortgage and Lambrecht Mortgage Company; he holds a finance degree from Western Michigan University.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; low personal public profile. IR email seen via search snippet of Rocket's IR page (site is bot-protected) - verify before use. Route media requests via Rocket's press room.

name: Russell Craig Ellwanger
current_role: CEO (since May 2005) and director, Tower Semiconductor Ltd (Nasdaq/TASE: TSEM), Migdal HaEmek, Israel
profile: An American-born semiconductor veteran, Ellwanger spent 1980–92 at Philips Semiconductors and 1992–96 at Novellus. He then held senior roles at Applied Materials from 1996 to 2005, including running its Metal CVD, CMP/electroplating and global services units. Since 2005 he has turned Tower into a profitable specialty foundry; it now has big silicon-photonics and SiGe contracts for AI data-centre optical modules, including work with NVIDIA.
interesting_fact: Tower reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $460m (+24%), and Ellwanger raised the 2028 target to $3.6bn revenue and $1.2bn net profit. Growth is driven by silicon photonics for data-centre optics; Tower signed customer contracts for about $1.3bn of 2027 silicon-photonics revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He started wrestling at 11 and his family picked a Las Vegas high school for its wrestling programme. While studying physics at BYU he joined Philips Semiconductors' Utah site, partly because it was one of the few companies offering students health insurance, and was later sent to Philips' main lab in the Netherlands.
notes: Articulate and quotable: Globes says he quotes management gurus, William Faulkner and Alice in Wonderland. A strong data-centre/AI-optics guest. The IR contact is Liat Avraham (+972-4-6506154). A media contact (oritsha@towersemi.com) appears in some releases but I didn't verify it. The $1.3bn photonics-contracts figure comes from a Finviz headline.

name: Aaron Cowen
current_role: Founder, CIO and Managing Partner, Suvretta Capital Management (New York); director of Veradermics and Benitec Biopharma
profile: Aaron Cowen is a hedge-fund manager who founded Suvretta Capital Management in 2011-12 after stints at Lehman Brothers, Baupost, Karsch Capital, SAC Capital (CIO) and Soros. Suvretta runs generalist and healthcare/biotech long-short funds (the Averill funds). He holds large stakes in and sits on the boards of several biotechs, including Veradermics, Benitec and ProKidney.
interesting_fact: By mid-2023 Suvretta's biotech/healthcare-focused Averill funds had grown to double the size of its flagship generalist funds.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Seth Klarman's Baupost Group in 1997 as an analyst for two years after starting as an associate at Lehman Brothers. He then spent 6+ years as a managing director at Karsch Capital before becoming SAC's CIO.
notes: Low-profile hedge-fund manager. No published press contact or personal social accounts found; Suvretta has no informative public website. Best route is likely via the IR/press contacts of portfolio companies where he is a director (e.g. Veradermics, Benitec). Biotech focus, so limited fit with an energy/data-center theme.

name: Dominic Frederico
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Assured Guaranty Ltd (NYSE: AGO)
profile: Has led bond insurer Assured Guaranty since December 2003, taking it public in 2004 and building the leading municipal bond insurer, notably by buying FSA in 2009 (now part of Assured Guaranty Inc.). Previously President/COO of ACE Limited and about 13 years at AIG. In Jan 2026 he took the company into annuity reinsurance (Assured Life Re).
interesting_fact: In January 2026 Assured Guaranty entered annuity reinsurance by acquiring a life and annuity reinsurer it renamed Assured Life Re; by mid-2026 he reported record per-share book value metrics.
deep_cut_fact: At ACE (1995-2003) he was the deal executive behind ACE's purchase of CIGNA's property-casualty business and the Capital Re acquisition. That Capital Re platform later became the core of Assured Guaranty, the company he has run since 2003.
notes: Media contact is Ashweeta Durani (Director, Media Relations, 212-408-6042) and IR contact is Robert Tucker; both are listed in the Q2 2026 earnings release. Little personal or public-profile information exists beyond earnings calls. Assured Guaranty insures infrastructure bonds such as JFK New Terminal One, which could be a relevant hook for energy and infrastructure topics.

name: Rocco A Ortenzio
current_role: Deceased (October 2024); was Chairman Emeritus & Co-Founder, Select Medical
profile: Healthcare entrepreneur who founded or co-founded four healthcare companies, including Continental Medical Systems (sold to Horizon Healthcare in 1995 for $502m) and Select Medical (co-founded 1996), now a Fortune 500 company. Died October 26, 2024.
notes: Deceased: died Oct 26, 2024 per Harrisburg University tribute (https://www.harrisburgu.edu/news/2024-10-28-remembering-rocco-ortenzio/) and APTA in-memoriam notice (https://apta.org/article/2024/11/20/rocco-ortenzio-in-memoriam). Rest skipped per instructions.

name: Zheng Dingping
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Guangdong Great Impression (Dayinxiang) Group, Shantou
profile: Shantou entrepreneur, born 1955 in Chaoyang, who founded Great Impression (大印象) in 1988 and has chaired the group since 1996. The company is best known for health and slimming teas and also makes health products, wine and medicine. It took over Shantou Brewery in 2003 to move into brewing.
interesting_fact: Great Impression expanded beyond health teas by merging with Shantou Brewery in 2003, entering beer brewing. Its range now runs to more than 100 product series.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics by correspondence at Jinan University (1976–77), and in 1994 the Ministry of Agriculture gave him a personal award for scientific and technological progress. He was named a Guangdong Model Worker in 2003.
notes: Bio details come from a user-submitted Chinese directory (maigoo), so verify before use. No official website or published contacts found. Probably best reached through the company in Shantou.

profile: Appeared on the Hurun China rich lists 2005-2008 with ~US$130M, attributed to Yinjiang Jinghong Investment in communications and property. No current online profile, company website or press coverage could be found to confirm his present role.
notes: Common name; nothing found linking 李建宏 to a Yinjiang/Jinghong entity. Unrelated to the listed smart-city firm Enjoyor (银江股份), whose leadership is different. He has been off the lists since 2008. A Chinese business-registry lookup would be needed; not a practical podcast target.

name: Hu Jishen
current_role: Chairman of the board, Xingyue Group (Yongkang, Zhejiang) per brand-profile site; date unverified
profile: Founder figure of Xingyue (Star Moon) Group in Yongkang, Zhejiang, which grew from a small workshop into a diversified manufacturer of power equipment/engines, doors and tools, reportedly with 4,000+ staff and a place among China's top 500 private firms. Hurun listed him (with Hu Jirong) in 2005-07. Current activity not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Xingyue grew from a factory with annual output under RMB 1 million into a group with over RMB 2 billion in assets, spanning engines, doors and hardware tools in Yongkang, China's 'hardware capital'.
deep_cut_fact: He served about 20 years as Party secretary of Gushan village in Gushan town, Yongkang, and reportedly put around RMB 30 million into the village's infrastructure; he was also vice-chair of the Jinhua federation of industry and commerce.
notes: Only source is a promotional brand-directory profile (CNPP); verify before use. Shares the Hurun listing with Hu Jirong (relationship not confirmed). No published contacts found.

name: Hu Jirong
current_role: President (总裁), Xingyue Group Co., Ltd. (星月集团), Yongkang, Zhejiang
profile: Co-founded Xingyue with his brother Hu Jishen in 1989 as a small aluminium-ingot workshop in Gushan, Yongkang. It grew into a group of more than 10 companies making motorcycle engines, security doors, tools, carpets and appliances. Under his leadership it has moved into agricultural machinery, pharmaceuticals and silk-based regenerative-medicine devices, and the group reports assets above RMB 8bn.
interesting_fact: In 1996 Xingyue produced China's first GY6-125 scooter engine, and its engines went on to power more than 500 Chinese motorcycle makers. The same year it formed a joint venture with an ordnance-industry plant in Luoyang, which the company calls the first such tie-up between a military enterprise and a private firm in China.
deep_cut_fact: Xingyue started on 6 August 1989 with RMB 750,000 and 12 workers in a 100 m2 workshop. Its first breakthrough came in 1993 with the 147FM motorcycle cylinder head, which won gold at the 1995 China high-tech new products expo. Hu Jirong was also a deputy to the 10th National People's Congress and is honorary principal of Gushan Primary School.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advised. The group publishes office phone lines but no group-level press email (subsidiary sales emails only). His 'President's message' is at http://www.xingyue.com/president.html.

current_role: Independent director, Tesla (since 2025, Audit Committee); also on boards of The Honest Company, Portillo's, Wonder Group and ZocDoc. Retired from Chipotle March 2026
