He delayed retirement after Brian Niccol left for Starbucks, retired as senior advisor in March 2026, and now sits on the boards of Tesla, Honest Company, Portillo's and others.
interesting_fact: He was persuaded to delay his retirement when CEO Brian Niccol made a surprise move to Starbucks in 2024; he has been named 'CFO of the Year' by the Orange County Business Journal and 'Best CFO' (restaurants) by Institutional Investor.
deep_cut_fact: Portillo's 2026 proxy lists his favorite menu item as the Italian Beef with Hot Peppers. He holds a B.S. in accounting and economics and an MBA from Illinois State University, and is a (non-practicing) CPA and CMA.
notes: Tesla board seat gives an energy/AI angle (Tesla Energy, Megapacks). Low social-media profile; route via board/IR channels or Chipotle alumni network.

name: Theodore Blegen
current_role: Retired EVP & CFO (Feb 2026), Monolithic Power Systems; remains with MPS in a transition role
profile: T. Bernie Blegen joined power-chip maker Monolithic Power Systems in 2011 as corporate controller and served as CFO from 2016 until retiring after the FY2025 10-K in Feb 2026, a decade in which MPS grew into a major supplier of power-management chips for AI servers and data centers. Earlier he held finance roles at Xilinx and Credence Systems; UC Santa Barbara graduate.
interesting_fact: CEO Michael Hsing credited him with helping MPS grow 'consistently at an above-market growth rate' during his ten years as CFO, after joining in 2011 'when MPS was relatively small and only beginning to strategically diversify'.
deep_cut_fact: Before semiconductors he worked in publishing and software finance, including at Times Mirror's higher-education group, Shutterfly and Micro Focus, per his executive profile; his 10-K bio cites 25+ years across the semiconductor, software and publishing industries.
notes: Goes by 'Bernie'. Now retired as CFO, so the company IR route is indirect; Rob Dean is interim CFO. Specific employers Times Mirror/Shutterfly/Micro Focus come from MarketScreener profiles (not the 10-K, which confirms only the publishing/software background).

name: Joseph W Gorder
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Valero Energy (CEO 2014-June 2023, Executive Chairman until 31 Dec 2024)
profile: Joe Gorder ran Valero, the largest US independent refiner, as CEO (May 2014-June 2023) and chairman (from end-2014), then executive chairman until retiring at end-2024. He rose through Diamond Shamrock/Ultramar Diamond Shamrock (sales, treasury, IT, business development) before Valero's 2001 acquisition of UDS.
interesting_fact: When he became CEO, UMSL noted he was one of only two undergraduate alumni of the University of Missouri-St. Louis running a Fortune 500 top-20 company (with Express Scripts' George Paz) - a distinction otherwise shared only by Cornell.
deep_cut_fact: A Pattonville High School (Maryland Heights, Mo.) grad, he chose UMSL because he could work 30-40 hours a week and still graduate on time (BSBA, marketing, 1979). His leadership line: 'I believe that a leader is one who serves... give them the latitude to do their jobs without micromanaging them.'
notes: Retired from Valero's board at end-2024, so Valero IR is only an indirect route; no personal social accounts found. SEC-derived wealth (~$125m). UMSL alumni network is a possible warm connection.

name: Hu Yuxing
profile: Listed on the 2006 Hurun China Rich List with wealth from 'CNPC & Tafo Petro Corp' (oil). No public source found tying a Hu Yuxing (胡玉兴) to an oil business or identifying 'Tafo Petro'.
notes: Not identified. Tried 胡玉兴 + 石油/董事长/塔佛/大佛/泰富, "胡玉兴" 企业家, and 'Hu Yuxing' + oil/Tafo/CNPC; only CNPC executives and namesakes returned. 'CNPC & Tafo' suggests a private partner/contractor to CNPC (possibly an oilfield-cooperation firm), but the Chinese name is unknown. SEC EDGAR full-text search not tried for this name pattern beyond web search.

name: William J McMorrow
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Kennedy Wilson (taken private in June 2026 by a consortium he led with Fairfax Financial)
profile: Bill McMorrow, a former banker, bought the small real-estate auction firm Kennedy-Wilson in 1988, when it had one office and 11 employees. He grew it into a global real estate investor with about $16B of assets under management across the US, UK, Ireland, Spain and Japan. In June 2026 he and Fairfax completed a take-private at $10.90 a share. He keeps operational control while Fairfax holds the majority economic interest.
interesting_fact: He has taken three companies public in three countries: Kennedy-Wilson on the NYSE, Kennedy Wilson Japan in Tokyo, and Kennedy Wilson Europe Real Estate in London. The London company's $1.7B IPO was the second-largest real-estate IPO in the London Stock Exchange's 200-year history.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 17 years in banking before buying Kennedy-Wilson. That included eight years as a Senior VP at Fidelity Bank in Pennsylvania, followed by EVP and chair of the Credit Policy Committee at Imperial Bank in Los Angeles. In 2011 Kennedy Wilson led the recapitalisation of Bank of Ireland, which was its entry into Europe.
notes: The company is now private, so the SEC-derived net worth is out of date: he cashed out or rolled over his stake in the take-private. The best route is Emily Heidt, MD Communications, the media contact on the June 2026 release; she is a company contact, not his personal one. His bio page also has an 'Open contact form' link. He has appeared on podcasts (ceointerviews.ai lists interviews).

name: James J Filler
current_role: Lead Independent Director, ServisFirst Bancshares (NYSE: SFBS), Birmingham, Alabama
profile: Birmingham businessman who spent 44 years in metals recycling with Jefferson Iron & Metal and its brokerage affiliate, then retired in 2006 to invest privately. He has been a director of ServisFirst Bank since its 2005 founding and of the holding company since 2007, and has been Lead Independent Director since 2019. His wealth is mostly early ServisFirst shares.
interesting_fact: He was an original director when ServisFirst Bank was founded in Birmingham in 2005 and has stayed on the board as it grew into a multi-state commercial bank with roughly US$17bn+ in assets.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he spent 44 years in scrap-metal recycling with Jefferson Iron & Metal, Inc. and its brokerage affiliate, which he led, before retiring in 2006. He attended Samford University.
notes: Private investor in his 80s with no personal media presence. The only published route is ServisFirst investor relations (Davis Mange). Proxy statements say board communications can go by mail to the corporate secretary.

name: Avishai Abrahami
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Wix.com Ltd (Nasdaq: WIX). Director, monday.com.
profile: A Jerusalem-born serial entrepreneur and IDF Unit 8200 veteran who co-founded Wix in 2006 with his brother Nadav and Giora Kaplan, after the founders were frustrated by how hard it was to build websites. He has grown Wix into a global website-building platform for tens of millions of users and is now pushing it into AI-built sites. He was also an early backer and board member of monday.com.
interesting_fact: Wix was monday.com's first customer, and Abrahami was an early investor who owned about 4% of monday.com at its 2021 IPO. Founder Roy Mann credits him with helping them 'identify the challenge of harnessing people at work.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Wix he founded the software company AIT in 1994 and sold it in 1997, then co-founded Sphera Corporation (1998), which was later acquired by SWsoft. Wikipedia also says he practices ninjutsu.
notes: Wix PR (pr@wix.com) is the best route. The ninjutsu detail rests on Wikipedia only, so treat it lightly. Strong entrepreneurship guest.

name: Lee Miller
current_role: Shareholder (~12%) of StartEngine Crowdfunding, Inc. via The Lee Miller Trust; no public operating role found
profile: An SEC Schedule 13G/A (Feb 2024) shows Lee Miller, a US citizen, beneficially owning about 4.2 million StartEngine shares (12.0%), mostly through The Lee Miller Trust, plus Series Seed preferred and stock options. StartEngine is the Burbank-based equity-crowdfunding platform co-founded by Howard Marks and chairman Ron Miller. No further public biography could be found.
interesting_fact: The holding includes Series Seed preferred shares, indicating a very early-stage investor in StartEngine.
notes: Not to be confused with StartEngine co-founder/chairman Ron Miller. Essentially no public profile; the 13G lists a c/o business address (FPG, Inc., Encino). Only realistic route is via StartEngine investor relations. Low priority.

name: Oleg Khaykin
current_role: President & CEO, VIAVI Solutions (NASDAQ: VIAV); director, Avnet
profile: Semiconductor and network-test executive who has led VIAVI since February 2016. Previously CEO of International Rectifier (2008 until its 2015 sale to Infineon) and a senior advisor at Silver Lake. VIAVI now pitches heavily into AI/data-center optical and high-speed Ethernet test (e.g. 1.6T validation, hollow-core fibre testing).
interesting_fact: He ran power-semiconductor maker International Rectifier from 2008 until Infineon acquired it in January 2015, then spent a year at Silver Lake before taking the VIAVI job.
deep_cut_fact: He started out as an engineer at Motorola and spent eight years at Boston Consulting Group before moving into operating roles; he holds a B.S. with honors in electrical and computer engineering from Carnegie Mellon and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Strong data-center fit: VIAVI sells test gear for AI-fabric/optical interconnects. Best route is VIAVI PR (Grand Bridges).

name: Mario A Harik
current_role: Chairman (since Dec 2025) and CEO, XPO, Inc.; Director, QXO, Inc.
profile: Mario Harik is chairman and CEO of XPO, the North American LTL trucking carrier. A founding executive of Brad Jacobs' XPO in 2011, he was CIO, built its tech platform, ran LTL from 2021 and became CEO in 2022 after the GXO/RXO spin-offs. He also sits on the board of Jacobs' QXO.
interesting_fact: As XPO's CIO he ran the technology integrations of 17 acquisitions in four years, then spent six years building digital tools for the Con-way LTL business he later took over.
deep_cut_fact: Engineer by training: computer & communications engineering from the American University of Beirut and an MIT master's in IT; early in his career he co-founded G3 Analyst as chief architect of web and voice applications, and was CTO of Tallan.
notes: Media contact Cole Horton listed on XPO press releases (mid-2026). Tech-heavy CEO (AI in freight ops) - good podcast angle; spoke at Northwestern in 2026.

name: Brent M Stevens
current_role: Founder/Manager of Peninsula Pacific and Chairman of Peninsula Pacific Entertainment (P2E); Director, Concrete Pumping Holdings
profile: Los Angeles investor and former Jefferies investment banker (1990-2010; EVP and Head of Capital Markets). He co-founded Peninsula Gaming (sold to Boyd Gaming for $1.45bn in 2012) and P2E, which sold most assets incl. Colonial Downs to Churchill Downs for ~$2.8bn in 2022. Peninsula Pacific also backed Brundage-Bone, now Concrete Pumping Holdings, where he is a ~10%+ holder and director.
interesting_fact: His gaming empire started in 1999 with a single Mississippi riverboat casino, the Diamond Jo in Dubuque, Iowa, bought for $77m; P2E's later assets sold to Churchill Downs for ~$2.8bn in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before gaming and concrete, he spent 20 years at Jefferies, rising to Head of Capital Markets and a seat on its Executive Committee; he holds a B.A. in Accounting from USC and a Wharton MBA.
notes: Low media profile. Avoid referencing a past Iowa campaign-contribution legal matter. P2E still pursuing Iowa casino development (Cedar Rapids).

name: Edward Smolyansky
current_role: Founder, Pure Culture Naturals (kefir brand); largest individual shareholder of Lifeway Foods (LWAY)
profile: Son of Lifeway Foods founders Michael and Ludmila Smolyansky, Edward worked at the family kefir company for two decades as controller, CFO, COO and director until 2022. He remains Lifeway's largest shareholder (~16%) and has led a public campaign for board change, and in 2025 launched his own kefir brand, Pure Culture.
interesting_fact: After leaving Lifeway he started a direct kefir competitor, Pure Culture, unveiled at Natural Products Expo West 2025.
deep_cut_fact: His family brought kefir to the American mainstream after emigrating from the Soviet Union; Lifeway was founded in Morton Grove, Illinois in 1986, and Edward grew up speaking Russian at home.
notes: Ongoing, contentious shareholder dispute with Lifeway's board (CEO is his sister Julie Smolyansky); avoid that topic in outreach. Best route is likely via Pure Culture or the press contacts on his shareholder-campaign press releases (e.g. https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2361215/).

name: Nicholas Little
current_role: Senior Vice President & Chief Operating Officer, DXP Enterprises (DXPE), Houston
profile: Nick Little is a long-time DXP Enterprises operator. DXP is a Houston-based distributor of pumps, rotating equipment, MRO and safety products, with large exposure to oil & gas and industrial customers. He rose from application engineer through outside sales, director of operations and regional VP of sales & operations, and became COO effective January 2022. His wealth is mainly DXP stock.
interesting_fact: Leadership changed in January 2022. Nick Little and Paz Maestas were appointed COO and Chief Marketing & Technology Officer together as part of DXP's next-generation management team.
deep_cut_fact: His career at DXP began about 18 years before his 2022 COO promotion, as an application engineer, a technical pump/equipment role, before he moved into outside sales.
notes: Low public profile. An aggregator says he is the son of DXP CEO David R. Little, but no primary filing confirming this was found, so don't rely on it. DXP serves the energy, water and industrial pump markets, which is a relevant podcast angle. No DXP press or IR email was found. A Baylor BBA (Finance) is reported only by aggregators and is unverified.

name: G. Zachary (Zack) Gund
current_role: Managing Partner, Coppermine Capital (Concord, MA)
profile: Member of the Cleveland Gund family, longtime major Kellogg shareholders. He founded the private-capital firm Coppermine Capital in 2002 and still runs it. He was a Kellogg/Kellanova director from Dec 2014 and later lead independent director of the WK Kellogg Co spin-off. Both board seats likely ended when Ferrero bought WK Kellogg (2025) and Mars bought Kellanova.
interesting_fact: The Gund family and the Kellogg Foundation Trust agreed to vote 21.7% of WK Kellogg's stock in favour of Ferrero's US$3.1bn takeover of the cereal maker.
deep_cut_fact: Coppermine's portfolio includes B2U, which builds grid storage from second-life EV batteries, and Little Leaf Farms, a controlled-environment lettuce grower. These are useful hooks for an energy-focused podcast.
notes: His firm's website publishes his direct work email. The Kellogg board status after the 2025 acquisitions is not confirmed from a primary source. University of Vermont BA and Kellogg (Northwestern) MBA, per third-party databases.

name: Bruce C. Bruckmann
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director, Bruckmann, Rosser, Sherrill & Co. (BRS), New York; Director, Mohawk Industries
profile: Harvard College and Harvard Law graduate who practised at Patterson Belknap, then spent 1983-94 at Citicorp Venture Capital before co-founding middle-market private equity firm BRS in 1995 with Harold Rosser and Stephen Sherrill. BRS backed consumer, retail and restaurant companies such as B&G Foods and AMF Bowling; he sits on Mohawk's board and was a long-time H&E Equipment director (H&E was acquired by Herc in 2025).
interesting_fact: The three BRS founders had worked together at Citicorp Venture Capital since as early as 1983 before spinning out their own firm in 1995 and putting their surnames on the door.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was a lawyer: an associate at New York firm Patterson, Belknap, Webb & Tyler after Harvard Law School.
notes: Very private PE investor; no published personal or press email found. Best route is via BRS's main office or Mohawk Industries' corporate secretary. Current BRS title not reconfirmed on brs.com (site blocked automated access).

name: Aaron Rosenberg
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, BeOne Medicines Ltd. (formerly BeiGene; Nasdaq: ONC) since July 2024
profile: Pharma finance executive who spent more than two decades at Merck, rising to Senior Vice President and Corporate Treasurer, before becoming CFO of oncology company BeiGene (renamed BeOne Medicines after redomiciling to Switzerland in 2025) in July 2024.
interesting_fact: He joined BeiGene just ahead of its transformation into BeOne Medicines, a Swiss-domiciled global oncology company known for the blood-cancer drug Brukinsa.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Merck in 2003 and, before becoming corporate treasurer, ran finance for Merck Animal Health (2015-18) and led Merck's corporate strategy and planning (2018-21). University of Florida finance BS, NYU Stern MBA.
notes: Corporate executive rather than founder; best route is BeOne investor relations.

name: Arthur G. Sulzberger
current_role: Chairman, The New York Times Company, and Publisher of The New York Times
profile: A.G. Sulzberger (b. 1980), fifth-generation member of the Ochs-Sulzberger family, became publisher of The New York Times in 2018 and company chairman in 2021. A former reporter (Providence Journal, The Oregonian, NYT Kansas City bureau), he led the 2014 Innovation Report and has steered the Times' shift to a subscriber-first digital business.
interesting_fact: He was lead author of the Times' 97-page 2014 Innovation Report, a blunt internal assessment of how the paper was losing ground to digital rivals that leaked to BuzzFeed and became a widely read industry document.
deep_cut_fact: The 2017 film 'Kodachrome' (Ed Harris, Jason Sudeikis, Elizabeth Olsen) was inspired by his 2010 NYT article on Parsons, Kansas, the last place in the world to develop Kodachrome film. As a Providence Journal intern he exposed a Narragansett Lions Club's men-only membership; it began admitting women months later.
notes: booking@nytimes.com is listed by NYTCo as the 'Press: Media Requests' address (for booking Times people on outside media), the natural route for a podcast invitation. Media-business rather than energy angle; he speaks publicly on press freedom and AI/copyright.

name: Megan Greuling
current_role: Reporting person on LendingTree (TREE) 10%-owner filings as co-executor of the estate of founder Doug Lebda and manager/co-trustee of related family holding entities; no public operating role found
profile: Megan Greuling appears in SEC filings (Form 3, Oct 2025; Schedule 13G amendments in 2026) as a deemed beneficial owner of LendingTree shares through Family Holdings LLC, a trust she co-trusts, and her role as co-executor of the estate of LendingTree founder Doug Lebda, who died in October 2025. She is not a LendingTree executive and has no public business profile.
notes: Private individual whose 'wealth' is a fiduciary/estate-related holding in LendingTree, not a self-made fortune; stakes in filings vary (deemed ownership changed Dec 2025). Recommend not pursuing outreach. Source: https://www.secform4.com/filings/1434621/0001683168-26-001257.htm

name: Aaron Jagdfeld
current_role: President and CEO, Generac Holdings (NYSE: GNRC), Waukesha, Wisconsin; director, Hillman Solutions
profile: Jagdfeld joined Generac in its finance department in the mid-1990s and became CFO in 2002. As CFO he helped sell the company to CCMP for about $2bn in 2006. He became CEO in 2008 at 36 and took Generac public in 2010. He has turned Generac into the leading US home-standby generator maker and now a fast-growing supplier of backup power for data centers.
interesting_fact: In Q3 2026 Generac signed a long-term supply deal for backup generators for Amazon data centers, with initial deliveries of about $2.4bn in 2027-28. Jagdfeld said the data-center backlog had reached about $4.5bn.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Deloitte & Touche auditor in Milwaukee when Generac, one of the manufacturers he audited, offered him a job. Years later he said of the business: 'We don't have a company jet.'
notes: Top fit for an energy/data-center podcast: Generac is pivoting hard into data-center backup power (Amazon deal, capacity expansion). He regularly does earnings calls and trade-press interviews. Route via Generac IR/communications.

name: Donald G Macpherson
current_role: Chairman & CEO, W.W. Grainger (NYSE: GWW); Director, DuPont de Nemours
profile: D.G. Macpherson has been CEO of industrial MRO distributor Grainger since 2016 and Chairman since 2017. He joined from BCG in 2008, where he was a partner, and ran supply chain and international before becoming COO. He has pushed Grainger's dual high-touch and 'endless assortment' (Zoro, MonotaRO) models and, lately, AI.
interesting_fact: Under his tenure Grainger has split into two models: 'High-Touch Solutions' for large customers, and an 'Endless Assortment' online business (Zoro in the US, MonotaRO in Japan). At the April 2026 AGM he highlighted the company's AI push.
deep_cut_fact: Before running a distributor he advised them: at BCG (2002-2008) he was on the firm's Industrial Goods leadership team. He holds a Stanford bachelor's degree and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Goes by 'D.G.'. IR head is Kyle Bland (VP Investor Relations). Data aggregators (MarketScreener) say he was earlier an operations manager at Rain Bird Sprinkler Manufacturing, but no primary source was found, so verify before using it. Grainger sells MRO supplies to data-center builders and utilities, which is a possible podcast angle.

name: Vincent Pilette
current_role: CEO, President & Chair of the Board, Gen Digital Inc. (Norton, Avast, LifeLock, MoneyLion)
profile: Belgian-born (1972) finance executive who was CFO of Electronics for Imaging (2011) and Logitech (2013-19) before joining Symantec as CFO in 2019. He led the sale of Symantec's enterprise business, became CEO of the consumer remainder, NortonLifeLock, merged it with Avast in 2022 to form Gen Digital, and added the Board chair role in 2025.
interesting_fact: Pilette says he arrived at Symantec as CFO on the very day its CEO was fired, then led the split and sale of half the company within a year and was named CEO months later, despite never having CEO aspirations.
deep_cut_fact: As a young financial analyst at a Fortune 500 IT company he told the CFO he wanted her job; when she laid out a 15-year succession plan he left ('I don't have that much time') and chased CFO roles through 'hundreds of nos', including an initial rejection from EFI, which later hired him as CFO.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Gen press office. Has spoken publicly about CFO-to-CEO path and consumer cyber safety/AI-era scams, good podcast angles.

name: Dan O Dinges
current_role: Former Chairman, President and CEO of Cabot Oil & Gas (2002-2021); Coterra Energy director until the May 2026 Devon-Coterra merger
profile: Dan Dinges ran Cabot Oil & Gas for about 20 years. He took over in 2002 after more than 20 years at Noble Energy/Samedan and built Cabot into a leading Marcellus Shale gas producer. He led the 2021 merger with Cimarex that created Coterra Energy and then served on Coterra's board. Coterra merged into Devon Energy in May 2026, and Dinges was not named to the combined board.
interesting_fact: He chaired the American Exploration & Production Council, the trade group of the largest US independent oil and gas producers, from 2015. He has also served on the boards of U.S. Steel and the American Petroleum Institute.
deep_cut_fact: Dinges started out as a Mobil Oil landman covering Louisiana, Arkansas and the central Gulf of Mexico. He holds a BBA in Petroleum Land Management from the University of Texas, a niche degree. He is a member of the All-American Wildcatters and served on the executive committee of UT Austin's Kay Bailey Hutchison Center for Energy, Law and Business.
notes: Retired from executive roles and Houston-based, with no personal website or social accounts found. Coterra no longer exists independently (merged into Devon, May 2026), so there is no current corporate press route. Industry associations (AXPC, All-American Wildcatters) or UT's KBH Energy Center are possible intro paths.

name: Emil D Kakkis
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Ultragenyx Pharmaceutical (NASDAQ: RARE); founder of the EveryLife Foundation for Rare Diseases
profile: Physician-scientist (MD/PhD, UCLA) who developed Aldurazyme, an enzyme replacement therapy for MPS I, at Harbor-UCLA. As BioMarin's CMO he steered further rare-disease drugs to approval. He founded the EveryLife Foundation in 2009 and Ultragenyx in 2010, and Ultragenyx has built a portfolio of rare and ultra-rare disease therapies.
interesting_fact: Drug companies turned down his MPS I therapy as too complex and too costly for so few patients. The family of a young patient, Ryan Dant, set up the Ryan Foundation and raised the money for the trial, and the drug went on to win FDA approval in 2003.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Montebello and Long Beach, graduated from Pomona College, and did his early MPS enzyme work with Dr. Elizabeth Neufeld. In 2019 he won BIO's Henri A. Termeer Biotechnology Visionary Award.
notes: A frequent public speaker on rare-disease policy, so the EveryLife Foundation is another route. Ultragenyx had an FDA complete response letter for UX111, so check recent company news before outreach. The latest release found (Sept 2025) still listed him as CEO.

name: Theresa E Wagler
current_role: EVP & CFO, Steel Dynamics (becomes President & CEO on 1 Jan 2027); Director, CF Industries
profile: Theresa Wagler is a former Ernst & Young CPA who joined steelmaker Steel Dynamics in 1998, when it was still a fast-growing startup. She became CFO in 2007 and built her wealth through the company's stock. In August 2026 SDI named her its next President & CEO, effective 1 January 2027, succeeding co-founder Mark Millett, who becomes Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: She will become CEO of one of the largest US steelmakers, an electric-arc-furnace producer that has expanded into aluminum (Aluminum Dynamics). That puts her squarely in industrial energy and decarbonisation themes.
deep_cut_fact: She is an avid rock climber who books several climbing trips at the start of each year and tells her team in advance. She nearly took a Chicago consulting job before a mentor steered her to Steel Dynamics to set up its financial reporting.
notes: Strong podcast fit (steel, energy-intensive industry, newly named CEO from Jan 2027). Taylor University accounting graduate; Trine University trustee and 2022 Woman of Distinction honoree. Route through SDI investor relations / corporate office, Fort Wayne (260-969-3500).

name: Michael C Morgan
current_role: Co-founding partner & Chairman, Triangle Peak Partners; Lead Director, Kinder Morgan Inc.
profile: Former president of Kinder Morgan (pipelines and energy infrastructure) who co-founded Triangle Peak Partners, a venture/growth investor in energy and technology, and runs the Portcullis Partners investment partnership. He is lead director at Kinder Morgan and has served on the boards of residential-solar firm Sunnova and AI-driven storage company Stem.
interesting_fact: He spans both ends of the energy transition: lead director of one of North America's largest natural-gas pipeline operators while backing solar, storage and clean-tech companies through Triangle Peak.
deep_cut_fact: A 2022 Stanford Distinguished Careers Institute fellow (billed as 'Energy & Technology Geek/Investor'), he co-chaired the Precourt Institute for Energy's advisory council, won the Stanford Associates Governors' Award, and once taught as an adjunct professor at Rice's Jones School.
notes: Kinder Morgan contacts are corporate routes, not personal. No working Triangle Peak website found. Sunnova filed for Chapter 11 in 2025, so avoid that topic. Education: Stanford BA econ & MA sociology, Harvard MBA. Stanford energy-network ties could make a warm intro.

name: Chinh Chu
current_role: Founder and Senior Managing Director, CC Capital (New York private equity); director of Getty Images and other portfolio companies
profile: Vietnamese-born American dealmaker who spent ~25 years at Blackstone (joined 1990), rising to senior managing director and co-chair of private equity. He left in 2015 to found CC Capital, which led deals including Dun & Bradstreet's take-private, Utz Brands' SPAC listing, E2open and Getty Images' listing.
interesting_fact: Chu summited Mount Everest on 17 May 2023, guided by record-holding Sherpa Kami Rita.
deep_cut_fact: To pay for college at the University at Buffalo he sold educational books door-to-door for Southwestern Co., building a sales team and becoming a top seller; he also worked as a telemarketer raising funds for UB. After a 1999 flood he co-founded Vietnam Relief Effort with his sister.
notes: Fled Saigon at age 8 in 1975 on one of the last US military refugee flights. Best route is CC Capital's published media contacts (Karv / Joele Frank).

name: Girish Saligram
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Weatherford International plc (NASDAQ: WFRD), Houston
profile: Engineer-turned-oilfield-services executive who has run Weatherford since October 2020, leading its post-bankruptcy turnaround and return to profitability. Previously COO of Exterran (from 2016) and spent about 20 years at GE, in GE Healthcare and later GE Oil & Gas. His wealth comes largely from Weatherford equity awards.
interesting_fact: He spent roughly 12 years at GE Healthcare in engineering, services and operations before moving into oil and gas, an unusual route into the CEO seat of a major oilfield services firm.
deep_cut_fact: Before Exterran he ran GE Oil & Gas's Contractual Services business from Florence, Italy; he holds an engineering degree from Bangalore University, an MS in computer science and a Kellogg MBA.
notes: Frequent energy-conference speaker (ADIPEC, CERAWeek-type events); writes occasionally for SPE's JPT. Good fit for an energy podcast; route via Weatherford corporate communications (media contact Kelley Hughes per releases).

name: Rene R. Joyce
current_role: Director, Targa Resources Corp. (NYSE: TRGP); founding CEO (2005-2011)
profile: Rene Joyce is the founding CEO of Targa Resources, the Houston midstream natural-gas and NGL company he led from its 2005 formation until 2011, then served as executive chairman (2012-2014) and remains a director. Earlier he ran Tejas Gas pipeline subsidiaries and Shell's Coral Energy units, and has sat on the boards of Apache and Core Labs.
interesting_fact: Targa, which he built from a 2005 private-equity-backed startup, is now one of North America's largest independent midstream companies; in 2026 it signed 20-year integrated midstream agreements with ExxonMobil in the Permian Delaware Basin.
deep_cut_fact: He is both an engineer and a lawyer: BS in mechanical engineering from LSU (1970) and a JD from Loyola University New Orleans (1974); he sits on the LSU Foundation National Board and is a member of LSU's Society for Engineering Excellence.
notes: Highly relevant to energy theme (natural gas midstream, Permian). Low personal media profile; route via Targa corporate/investor relations or LSU engineering network. A Targa proxy noted a planned board retirement at an annual meeting—confirm current board status in latest proxy.

name: Gerold Buettiker
