profile: Rahul C. Kirloskar is a fourth-generation member of India's Kirloskar engineering family with 34+ years in the group. He became MD of Kirloskar Pneumatic in 1993 and its chairman in 1998, ran exports for Kirloskar Oil Engines 2001-2012, and succeeded his brother Atul as KOEL chairman when Atul retired on 31 March 2026.
interesting_fact: He took over the KOEL chair from his brother Atul Kirloskar, who retired at 70 in March 2026, with Gauri Kirloskar becoming vice-chairperson alongside her MD role; KOEL makes gensets and engines widely used for backup power.
deep_cut_fact: He personally founded Kirloskar Chillers (HVAC/refrigeration) and has chaired both the CII Pune Council and the Maharashtra State CII Council; from 2001-2012 he led KOEL's push to expand exports for the whole Kirloskar Group.
notes: Good energy/data-center angle: KOEL gensets are used for data-center backup power. Kirloskar Pneumatic (where he is chairman) is a separate listed company with its own IR. Route via KOEL corporate inbox.

name: C Selvam
current_role: Whole-time Director, Asvini Fisheries Pvt. Ltd., Chennai, per company-registry aggregators (likely Chandrasekaran Selvam)
profile: C Selvam is linked to Asvini Fisheries, a Chennai seafood processor and exporter incorporated in 1986 that runs a raw-fish freezing unit at Tuticorin. Registry data lists Chandrasekaran Selvam as whole-time director since 1994. He is also a director of Asvini Hatcheries, Selvam Exports, Emerald Fishing and Meridian Fisheries, and is listed on the Seafood Exporters Association of India.
interesting_fact: His directorships cover much of the seafood chain: hatcheries (Asvini Hatcheries), fishing (Emerald Fishing Co.), processing and exports (Asvini Fisheries, Selvam Exports).
notes: Very low public profile. The identity rests only on registry aggregators (Tofler/Qorpiq) matching 'C Selvam' to Chandrasekaran Selvam at Asvini Fisheries; this is plausible but not confirmed by a primary source. I found no company website or published contact. The search budget ran out before a fuller check.

name: Arjun Juneja
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Mankind Pharma Ltd (New Delhi)
profile: Second-generation leader of Mankind Pharma, founded in 1995 by his father Ramesh C. Juneja and uncle Rajeev Juneja. He studied business at the University of Bradford, got an MBA from Strathclyde, and joined Mankind in 2008, starting in business development. As COO he helped lead its 2023 IPO and its expansion into one of India's largest pharma companies by domestic sales.
interesting_fact: He cold-called his way into Mankind's first big pharma partnership, a marketing deal with Belgium's UCB, which led to Mankind taking over UCB's India business. He also led the 2012 R&D push on fertility drug Dydroboon.
deep_cut_fact: He was a serious cricketer: a leg-spinner from grade 4 who played up to state level. Fortune India links that to Mankind's cricket-heavy marketing with Sourav Ganguly and Anil Kumble. His line on the UCB deal: 'Cold calling randomly got us the first break with UCB.'
notes: investor.relations@ is the institutional-IR desk (Head of IR). investors@ is the secretarial/shareholder address. Fortune India 40 Under 40 (2024) honoree. He has given interviews to Hurun, Business Today and Entrepreneur India, so he is reasonably media-accessible.

name: Vijay Biyani
current_role: Unclear. Formerly Managing Director of Future Retail (from May 2016) and a senior executive at Future Enterprises.
profile: Vijay Laxminarayan Biyani is a brother of Kishore Biyani and one of the Biyani family members who built the Mumbai-based Future Group (Big Bazaar, Pantaloons heritage), India's former retail giant. He served as Managing Director of Future Retail and on the boards of group companies, and appeared on the Hurun India Rich List in 2018-19.
interesting_fact: Future Retail redesignated Vijay Biyani as its Managing Director in May 2016, during the group restructuring in which Kishore Biyani became vice chairman.
notes: Future Retail and the group's listed companies went through insolvency proceedings from 2022, so there is no working corporate press channel. No personal public presence was found. Avoid the group's financial troubles in any outreach. Low priority.

name: Gundavaram Vanaja Devi
current_role: Whole-time Director and co-promoter, Kaveri Seed Company Ltd (Secunderabad); re-appointed for 2026-2031
profile: G. Vanaja Devi is a co-promoter of Kaveri Seed Company, the Hyderabad-area hybrid seed maker (cotton, maize, rice, vegetables) led by chairman and MD G.V. Bhaskar Rao. She has been on the board since the company was incorporated in 1986 and oversees CSR and community development while assisting the MD with administration; shareholders were asked in 2026 to extend her term to 2031.
interesting_fact: Kaveri Seed has been named six times by Forbes Asia among its 'Best Under a Billion' companies.
deep_cut_fact: She has been a director since the company's incorporation on 27 August 1986 and heads Kaveri's CSR and community-development work, which the board credits for its rural-empowerment programmes.
notes: Company contacts only (company secretary and general info). Very low media profile; chairman G.V. Bhaskar Rao is the public face.

name: Vrajmohan Shah
current_role: Founder, GSP Crop Science (Ahmedabad); no current directorships on MCA record
profile: Vrajmohan Ramanlal Shah founded GSP Crop Science in Ahmedabad in February 1985; it began in phosphate sales before moving into agrochemicals (crop-protection formulations and technicals). The company is now run by his son Bhavesh Shah (Chairman & MD) with the next generation (Executive Director Tirth Shah).
interesting_fact: GSP started out selling phosphates in 1985 before pivoting into agrochemicals around 1988, growing into one of India's larger privately held crop-protection makers.
notes: One aggregator profile refers to 'his demise', and the MCA register shows his DIN deactivated with zero current appointments, but no obituary was found, so alive status is unverified. If contacting, route via the company/Bhavesh or Tirth Shah (Tirth has given trade-press interviews, e.g. agribusinessglobal.com). Web-search budget ran out before contact research.

name: Mahabir Prasad Jalan
current_role: Chairman Emeritus (founder), Ramkrishna Forgings Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Mahabir Prasad Jalan founded Ramkrishna Forgings in Kolkata in 1981, initially making forged parts for Indian Railways; the firm moved into commercial-vehicle components around 2000 and is now a major listed forging/casting exporter. He chaired it until 2023 and is now Chairman Emeritus, with son Naresh Jalan as MD and grandson Chaitanya Jalan in management.
interesting_fact: RKFL began in 1981 as a railway forging supplier and only entered the automotive market around 2000, later becoming a key supplier of heavy-truck components globally.
deep_cut_fact: Has said: 'Honesty, dedication, and customer engagement are the three cardinal mantras that RKFL believes in' - and blamed India's early forging struggles on outdated techniques and low volumes.
notes: Now semi-retired (emeritus); for a podcast the active family leaders (Naresh / Chaitanya Jalan) may be more accessible. Alive status inferred from 2025-26 board listings naming him Chairman Emeritus.

name: Simran Lal
current_role: CEO, Good Earth (Eicher Goodearth) and co-founder/creative director, Nicobar; Eicher Motors promoter-family shareholder
profile: Daughter of Eicher Motors patriarch Vikram Lal and sister of Royal Enfield/Eicher chairman Siddhartha Lal; her Hurun wealth reflects family Eicher Motors holdings. Rather than join Eicher, she joined her mother Anita Lal's luxury design house Good Earth in 2002, became CEO, took it online in 2013, co-founded resortwear brand Nicobar (2016) with husband Raul Rai and later launched luxury label Paro.
interesting_fact: Nicobar is named after the Nicobar Islands in the Indian Ocean; the brand draws on the Spice Route and an island aesthetic, and fabric-hunting and factory visits are among her favourite parts of the job.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Good Earth she had a brief stint at a homewares label; after Good Earth and Nicobar she launched Paro, a luxury brand spanning apparel, jewellery, bed linen and a botanical range.
notes: Design/retail entrepreneur rather than auto executive; some 2024 sources call her 'former CEO' of Good Earth, so confirm current title. Podcast angle: building heritage luxury brands, D2C.

name: Tara Lal
profile: Listed by Hurun India (2018) with wealth from Eicher Motors, the Royal Enfield parent controlled by the Vikram Lal family. Authoritative Eicher sources do not name a Tara Lal; one data aggregator links a 'Tara Lal Vikram' to Eicher's promoter holding company, so she is likely a passive Lal-family shareholder.
notes: Could not confirm identity or role from reliable sources. Not a public figure; the operating family leader is Siddhartha Lal (Executive Chairman, Eicher Motors) https://eicher.in/about-us/siddhartha-lal

name: Gaurav Swarup
current_role: Co-Chairman, Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd (Kolkata); long-time Chairman, KSB Ltd (India)
profile: Third-generation leader, with brother Vikram Swarup (Chairman), of Paharpur Cooling Towers, India's market leader in industrial cooling towers and air-cooled heat exchangers for power, petrochemical and steel plants; MD from 1993. In July 2024 Paharpur bought control of thyssenkrupp Industries India, renamed TKIL Industries.
interesting_fact: Paharpur took control of thyssenkrupp's Indian engineering arm (cement, mining, energy and sugar equipment) in 2024. He and Vikram called TKIL 'a highly successful and well-regarded entity'.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2016 he became President of the All India Organisation of Employers (AIOE), the FICCI-allied employers' body, at its 82nd AGM. He has also chaired pump maker KSB Ltd's Indian board since 2009.
notes: Paharpur also makes dry/air-cooled systems (SPG Dry Cooling), which fit the data-center cooling theme. The contact page lists only general and regional company inboxes, none specific to him. The KSB chairmanship dates from 2009 (marketscreener) and should be rechecked before citing.

name: Vikram Swarup
current_role: Chairman, Paharpur Cooling Towers Ltd (Kolkata)
profile: Vikram Swarup chairs family-owned Paharpur Cooling Towers (est. 1949, Kolkata), a major global maker of wet, dry and adiabatic cooling towers for power plants, HVAC, oil & gas, chemicals and heavy industry, alongside co-chairman Gaurav Swarup. A director since 1993, he has expanded the group into engineering; in 2024 Paharpur took majority control of thyssenkrupp's Indian unit, renamed TKIL Industries.
interesting_fact: In 2024 Paharpur Cooling Towers became majority shareholder of thyssenkrupp Industries India, which was renamed TKIL Industries - a supplier of equipment for cement, mining, energy and sugar plants.
notes: Low public profile; no personal accounts or interviews found. Strong energy/data-center fit (industrial and power-plant cooling, dry/adiabatic coolers). Company HQ switchboard and support@paharpur.com are the published routes. Don't confuse with author/diplomat Vikas Swarup.

name: Sanjay Chandrakant Kirloskar
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Kirloskar Brothers Ltd (Pune)
profile: Born 1957 in Nagpur. He is a fourth-generation member of the Kirloskar industrial family and has led Kirloskar Brothers, India's largest pump maker, for decades. He took it global with acquisitions including SPP Pumps (UK, 2002), Braybar (South Africa), SyncroFlo (USA, 2014) and Rodelta (Netherlands, 2015). He studied mechanical engineering at Illinois Institute of Technology (1978).
interesting_fact: Under him, Kirloskar Brothers received the ASME N-Stamp in 2012. It was the first Indian rotating-equipment company to do so, which qualified it to make pumps for nuclear power plants.
deep_cut_fact: He set up KBL's all-women-run pump plant at Kaniyur near Coimbatore (c. 2010-11) to give rural women engineering jobs. Its team entered the Limca Book of Records by assembling a pump in 17.25 seconds.
notes: Energy/water angle: pumps for power plants, including nuclear, and irrigation. A 2025 interview at theworldfolio.com/interviews/engineering-leader-a/3889/ explains why he started the women's plant. Avoid the long-running Kirloskar family trademark dispute. The emails come from listing aggregators that cite exchange filings; check the latest BSE/NSE filing to confirm them.

name: Tulsi Tanti
profile: Founder and chairman of Suzlon Energy, India's wind-turbine pioneer (founded 1995). He died of cardiac arrest on 1 October 2022, aged 64.
notes: Deceased 1 Oct 2022 (per Suzlon's stock-exchange filing). Source: https://www.businesstoday.in/latest/corporate/story/suzlon-energy-founder-tulsi-tanti-passes-away-due-to-cardiac-arrest-348768-2022-10-02. Suzlon is now run by the Tanti family and professional management; if relevant, approach the company directly, not this profile.

name: Rupal Anant Bhat
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder of Asian Paints Ltd (India); no executive or board role found
profile: Member of the Asian Paints promoter group (the founding Choksi/Dani/Vakil families) who holds about 0.20% of Asian Paints directly and is listed as a significant beneficial owner through promoter investment companies Doli Trading and Investments and Elf Trading and Chemical Manufacturing. Asian Paints is India's largest paint maker. Appeared on Hurun India 2018-2019.
interesting_fact: Asian Paints' September 2026 filing lists her as holding 1,923,770 shares directly (0.20%), plus beneficial interests via Doli Trading & Investments (0.98%) and Elf Trading & Chemical Manufacturing (0.22%), recorded since February 2019.
notes: Private individual with no public profile; only appears in shareholding disclosures. Weak fit for energy/data-center podcast (paints/chemicals). Company contacts are indirect; low-priority target.

name: Vinod Vyas
current_role: Founder & Joint Managing Director, Standard Greases and Specialities Pvt Ltd (Mumbai); Director, Tide Water Oil Co. (India) Ltd (Veedol)
profile: Vinod S. Vyas, a science graduate with 48+ years in lubricants and greases, founded Mumbai-based Standard Greases & Specialities (est. ~1983), described as India's largest private-label grease manufacturer. Through Standard Greases he became a co-promoter and the largest shareholder of listed Tide Water Oil, maker of Veedol lubricants, and sits on its board.
interesting_fact: In 2015-16 his privately held Standard Greases ran an open offer for Tide Water Oil (Veedol) and overtook the state-owned Andrew Yule group as its largest shareholder, after which the board named it co-promoter.
deep_cut_fact: His directorships reach well beyond India: he sits on the boards of Granville Oil & Chemicals in the UK and Geotic Company in New Zealand, plus Tarapur Grease Industries and Royal Castor Products at home.
notes: Contact is Tide Water Oil (Veedol India) corporate office, where he is a director; no Standard Greases website found online. Business partner D.S. Chandavarkar is CMD of Standard Greases and chairman of Tide Water Oil. Low public profile.

name: Sajja Kishore Babu
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Managing Director, Power Mech Projects Ltd (Hyderabad; NSE/BSE-listed)
profile: Power-plant engineer who spent 14 years building and maintaining thermal power plants before founding Power Mech in 1999. The company grew into one of India's largest erection, testing and commissioning (ETC) and O&M contractors for power plants, and has expanded into civil works, mining (MDO), railways and the Middle East.
interesting_fact: Power Mech moved from maintenance into large builds within three years, doing its first ETC job on 1x63 TPH and 2x165 TPH fluidised-bed boilers for BHEL, then units at Raigarh, Chhattisgarh. It went on to commission generating units for every fuel type.
deep_cut_fact: Power Mech's very first contract in 1999 was the overhaul and maintenance of gas turbines for Tata Power at Trombay, Mumbai. His company bio also notes he is known for remembering employees by name.
notes: Hurun India 2018-19 listing; Power Mech's market value has risen sharply since, so his wealth is likely higher now. A good fit for India power-buildout themes. Route via corporate office or company secretary.

name: Rahul Sharma
current_role: Co-founder, Micromax Informatics; drives its AI/semiconductor pivot (MiPhi Semiconductors JV with Taiwan's Phison) and Bhagwati Products
profile: Co-founded Micromax in 2000 with Vikas Jain, Sumit Arora and Rajesh Agarwal. It began as an IT/telecom hardware firm and became one of India's top phone brands after 2008. He founded electric-motorcycle maker Revolt Intellicorp (2019), which RattanIndia fully acquired in 2023. He now focuses on electronics components, AI storage chips (MiPhi) and a Rs 250 crore deeptech family office.
interesting_fact: Micromax's MiPhi joint venture with Taiwan's Phison designs and makes AI-enabled storage chips in India. In 2026 the family set up a Rs 250 crore family office to back deeptech startups.
deep_cut_fact: Micromax's first big hit came from a trip to a village with no grid power, where a phone booth ran on a truck battery that its owner cycled to the next village each night to charge. Sharma came back and built the X1i, a phone with a 30-day battery.
notes: Many Indians share this name; this record is the Micromax co-founder. I found no published press or IR email (the only email on MiPhi's site is customer care). The truck-battery story appears in many outlets (CNN Money 2016, Business Standard 2010, YourStory), though accounts disagree on whether the village was in West Bengal or Bihar. It fits an energy angle well.

name: Rajesh Agarwal
current_role: Co-founder, Micromax Informatics Ltd (Gurugram, India)
profile: A mechanical engineer and former IT salesman (Pertech, Xerox), Rajesh Agarwal co-founded Micromax with Rahul Sharma, Sumit Arora and Vikas Jain, growing it from an IT/training business into India's top domestic phone brand in the late 2000s on cheap dual-SIM handsets. Micromax has since pivoted toward electronics manufacturing and memory chips (MiPhi JV with Phison) under Rahul Sharma.
interesting_fact: Micromax broke into handsets with dual-SIM phones when critics predicted it would 'end up losing big time'; Agarwal says 'We wouldn't be in business had we not created a category.'
deep_cut_fact: In 1991 he sold his Maruti 800 for Rs 80,000 to fund his first venture, a PC-assembly firm called Micromax Technologies; he later co-founded Micromax Informatics with Rahul Sharma, his neighbour of 35 years.
notes: Low public profile versus co-founder Rahul Sharma. No published personal/press email found; route via Micromax corporate. Current executive role not confirmed in 2026 sources.

name: Sumeet Kumar
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Micromax group; director of MiPhi Semiconductors, Micromax Biofuels, YU Televentures and Bhagwati Products
profile: Co-founded Micromax in 2000 (with Rahul Sharma, Rajesh Agarwal and Vikas Jain) as an embedded-systems startup and grew it into India's largest home-grown phone brand. The group now spans electronics manufacturing (Bhagwati Products), enterprise SSDs (MiPhi, a JV with Taiwan's Phison), solar modules (Startup Energy) and ethanol (Micromax Biofuels).
interesting_fact: MiPhi Semiconductors, the Micromax-Phison JV (55/45) on whose board he sits, became the first Indian brand to design and manufacture enterprise SSDs aimed at data centres and AI workloads.
deep_cut_fact: Besides chips, he is a director of Micromax Biofuels, which runs a 100 KLPD ethanol plant in Bihar supplying fuel-grade ethanol under India's Ethanol Blending Programme; the group also makes solar modules via Startup Energy.

public_contacts.value: https://micromaxinfo.com/micromax-biofuels (group 'Contact the group' form on site pages)

notes: Sometimes listed as Sumeet Kumar Arora. Strong energy/data-center angle (MiPhi SSDs, solar, ethanol). Low public profile; co-founder Rahul Sharma is the usual spokesperson. Studied B.Tech mechanical engineering at Jamia Millia Islamia per a Naukri company profile (https://companies.naukri.com/micromax-jobs/executive-team).

name: Vikas Jain
current_role: Co-founder, World of Play (PLAY wearables/audio brand); co-founder of Micromax Informatics
profile: Vikas Jain is one of the four co-founders (with Rahul Sharma, Rajesh Agarwal and Sumeet Kumar) of Micromax, the Gurgaon company that grew from an IT venture into one of India's largest budget phone brands. He later co-founded World of Play, which sells affordable smart wearables and audio products aimed at young Indian consumers.
interesting_fact: In a DNA interview he said the Micromax founders 'never thought we would sell 1.8 million handsets a month', a volume the company reached at its peak.
deep_cut_fact: He was the fourth partner to join Micromax Informatics in its pre-phone era as a computer-training/IT venture; co-founder Rajesh Agarwal recalled: 'Later on, Vikas too joined us, chipping in his share of capital.'
notes: Consumer electronics, not energy. Micromax's fortunes declined after ~2016; avoid that topic. Hurun appearances 2015-2018 only. No published press email found for World of Play.

name: Ashok Kumar Chaturvedi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, UFlex Ltd (Noida, India)
profile: First-generation entrepreneur Ashok Chaturvedi started a tiny manufacturing unit in 1985 that became UFlex, India's largest multinational flexible-packaging group (films, pouches, chemicals, holography, aseptic packaging, printing cylinders and packaging machines) with film plants in the US, Mexico, Poland, Egypt, UAE, Russia, Hungary and Nigeria and >US$1bn turnover. He was reappointed CMD from Feb 2024 for five years; son Anantshree is Vice Chairman/CEO of Flex Films.
interesting_fact: He is widely called the 'Father of Flexible Packaging' in India (title conferred at the Global Conference on Plastic & Packaging 2019) and also won the ET Polymers Lifetime Achievement Award 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He promises customers '3 Q's' - Quality, Quantity & Quickness - and is a cricket enthusiast who funds education and sports facilities for under-privileged children and youth.
notes: Best route is UFlex Global Corporate Communications (corpcomm@). UFlex's recycling/biodegradable packaging and energy-intensive film plants could be podcast angles.

name: Mukesh Chimanlal Gandhi
profile: Co-founder, Whole-time Director and CFO of MAS Financial Services (Ahmedabad NBFC founded 1995). Died January 19, 2021, according to the company's founders page.
notes: Deceased (Oct 20, 1957 - Jan 19, 2021), source: https://mas.co.in/about/#our-founders. The surviving founder is co-founder Kamlesh Gandhi (Chairman & MD); company contact mfsl@mas.co.in is published at https://www.mas.co.in/.

name: Jyoti Agarwal
current_role: Promoter-group shareholder, AU Small Finance Bank; co-founder, Sanjay & Jyoti Agarwal Foundation
profile: Wife of AU Small Finance Bank founder and MD/CEO Sanjay Agarwal. She holds about 3.2% of the Jaipur-based bank (roughly 3.8% in FY21) as part of the promoter group. She was an early director of the group (appointed 2003, since ceased). Her Hurun wealth comes from that stake. AU is moving toward universal bank status.
interesting_fact: AU grew from a Jaipur vehicle-finance NBFC into one of India's first small finance banks and has been asked by the RBI to move the promoter family's ~22% stake into a non-operative holding company before final approval as a universal bank.
deep_cut_fact: She co-founded the Sanjay and Jyoti Agarwal Foundation, which works on education for underprivileged children, road safety and digital empowerment.
notes: Private individual with almost no public profile of her own. Shareholding source: AU Bank MGT-9 FY2020-21 (https://www.au.bank.in/pdfs/other-reports/mgt-7---mgt-9/MGT-9-2020-21.pdf). Best route is via AU Bank corporate communications or the family foundation.

name: Shakuntala Agarwal
current_role: Promoter shareholder, AU Small Finance Bank Ltd (no executive or board role found)
profile: Listed by Hurun India for AU Small Finance Bank, the Jaipur-based lender founded by Sanjay Agarwal (AU Financiers, 1996) that converted to a small finance bank in 2017. AU's filings list her in the promoter group, holding ~1.86 crore shares (~2.5%) as of late 2025. No public profile, interviews or operating role found.
interesting_fact: AU's promoter group (Sanjay Agarwal, Jyoti Agarwal, Shakuntala Agarwal, MYS Holdings) built the bank from a Jaipur vehicle-finance NBFC into one of India's largest small finance banks, which has since sought RBI approval to become a universal bank.
notes: Very private passive promoter shareholder; relationship to founder Sanjay Agarwal not confirmed in sources found. Only realistic route is via AU Small Finance Bank corporate/IR office; consider approaching Sanjay Agarwal instead.

name: Madhu N Jain
current_role: Director, IIFL Foundation (CSR arm of IIFL Group); promoter shareholder in IIFL with husband Nirmal Jain
profile: Wife of IIFL founder Nirmal Jain. Together they are promoters of the IIFL financial-services group (IIFL Finance, IIFL Capital, 360 ONE), which Bloomberg has valued their stake in at over $1B. She leads IIFL Foundation, whose flagship Sakhiyon Ki Baadi programme teaches out-of-school girls in rural Rajasthan.
interesting_fact: IIFL Foundation's Sakhiyon Ki Baadi programme has brought about 36,000 out-of-school girls in rural Rajasthan into education, making it one of India's largest girl-literacy efforts. In December 2024 the Foundation adopted 102 government girls' high schools in the state.
deep_cut_fact: She personally received a 'CSR Leadership Award', and the Foundation's work has been recognised by the United Nations. In April 2026 the Foundation opened revitalised government schools in Rajasthan, inaugurated on Mahavir Jayanti.
notes: Her public profile is almost entirely philanthropic (girls' education in Rajasthan). The IIFL Foundation email is the most natural route. Not an operating business executive.

name: Archana H Mariwala
current_role: Director, Ascent India Foundation; Marico promoter-group shareholder
profile: Archana Mariwala is the wife of Harsh Mariwala, founder and chairman of Marico (Parachute, Saffola). Her wealth comes from her promoter-group stake in Marico. She has kept a low public profile and has sat on the board of ASCENT, the entrepreneur peer-learning foundation set up by Harsh Mariwala, since 2015.
interesting_fact: ASCENT Foundation, on whose board she sits, is funded by Harsh Mariwala and runs peer-learning groups for growth-stage Indian entrepreneurs. That ties directly to the podcast's entrepreneurship theme.
notes: Very private; no interviews found. Her board role comes from registry data (tofler). Don't confuse her with Archanna Das, ASCENT's CEO. Best route is via the ASCENT Foundation or Harsh Mariwala's office; Harsh is the far more natural podcast guest.

name: Prakash Harakchand Parakh
current_role: Managing Director, Parakh Agro Industries Ltd (Parakh Group, Pune); heads group real estate arm Gemini Housing
profile: Second-generation leader of Pune's Parakh Group, a Maharashtra trading house that moved into wheat flour, pulses and edible oil in the 1980s. He drove the edible-oil business, sold to Cargill in 2005, then refocused on atta/pulses, flexible packaging (Parakh Flexipacks), wind power and real estate; the group re-entered oil refining in 2017.
interesting_fact: Parakh pioneered flexible pouches for edible oil in India and claims the first 10 kg atta pack; Fortune India named it the fastest-growing mid-size FMCG company in 2017-18.
deep_cut_fact: Per the group's own site, he set up what it calls Asia's largest edible-oil refinery under one roof at Kurkumbh in 1999, and was appointed a non-executive director of Bank of Maharashtra on the recommendation of Maharashtra's Chief Minister.
notes: Privately held family group; MD listing per MCA-based directories (DIN 00337188). Brother Suresh Parakh and third-generation Harshal Parakh also active. Web search budget ran out mid-research; Cargill deal details from packaging trade press only.

name: Reena Kamalkumar Agrawal
current_role: Family shareholder associated with Haldiram's Nagpur business (per Hurun India 2018-2019); no public executive role found
profile: Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (about US$120m) with wealth from Haldiram Foods International, the Nagpur arm of the Haldiram's snacks group built by Shivkisan Agrawal. Her name suggests a link to executive director Kamalkumar Agrawal, but no public source confirms her role. The Nagpur and Delhi FMCG businesses merged in 2025 into Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd.
interesting_fact: Haldiram's began as a small sweet shop in Bikaner; the Nagpur and Delhi family branches completed a merger in 2025 to form Haldiram Snacks Food Pvt Ltd, one of India's largest packaged-snack companies.
notes: Very private, no public profile found; relationship to Kamal Agrawal inferred from the patronymic only and unconfirmed. Outreach would go via Haldiram's corporate; Kamal Agrawal is the more visible family member.

name: Rashmita Patnaik
current_role: Director/promoter, Falcon Marine Exports Ltd (Bhubaneswar, Odisha)
profile: Rashmita Patnaik is a long-serving director and promoter of Falcon Marine Exports, a Bhubaneswar-based seafood (mainly shrimp) processor and exporter founded in 1986 by Tara Ranjan and Prava Ranjan Patnaik. She also holds directorships in group companies such as Falcon Drinks, Falcon Real Estate and Falcon Holdings. Listed on Hurun India 2018-2019 (~US$120m).
interesting_fact: Falcon Marine Exports, set up in Odisha in 1986, grew into one of India's leading shrimp exporters and has been recognised in MPEDA's export awards (2018-19 awardee list).
notes: Non-executive, very private; company's public face is chairman Tara Ranjan Patnaik (Priyanka Mohanty named Joint MD in 2026). Board data from third-party MCA aggregators (qorpiq.com). No published company email found on falconmarine.in.

name: C Sathyan
current_role: Vice Chairman, Hatsun Agro Product Ltd (Chennai)
profile: Son of founder R.G. Chandramogan, C. (Chandramogan) Sathyan became executive director of Hatsun Agro in 2002, later MD and since 2024 (Executive) Vice Chairman, supporting the chairman on strategy. Hatsun is India's largest private dairy (Arun Ice Creams, Arokya milk, Hatsun curd, Ibaco), buying milk from 400,000+ farmers across South India.
interesting_fact: Hatsun began in 1970 as a single Arun ice-cream shed in Chennai started with Rs 13,000 and now procures millions of litres of milk a day; it famously earns more in minutes today than in its first decade.
notes: Signed filings as Vice Chairman in March 2026, so active. Little personal press; father R.G. Chandramogan is the public face. Best route is Hatsun's corporate office.

name: Karuturi Satyanarayana Murthy
current_role: Executive Chairman and co-promoter, Apex Frozen Foods Ltd (Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh; NSE/BSE: APEX)
profile: Andhra Pradesh aquaculture entrepreneur (born 1955) with more than 30 years in the shrimp business. He co-promoted Apex Frozen Foods, a vertically integrated exporter of farmed Pacific white shrimp to the US, EU and UK that listed in 2017. Long its chairman and MD, he was reappointed Executive Chairman from 1 December 2025, with K. Subrahmanya Chowdary as MD.
interesting_fact: Apex runs a Kakinada processing plant of about 9,240 MTPA and its own shrimp hatchery and farming operations, and supplies frozen and ready-to-cook shrimp to major Western retailers and distributors.
deep_cut_fact: Apex began in 1995 as a partnership firm exporting shrimp from a leased processing facility, and only built its own plant at Kakinada in 2004, almost a decade later.
notes: Low media profile. The company's IR agency, Stellar IR, is also listed on the contact page. This is a food business, so the fit with the energy/data-center theme is weak.

name: Jaya Bachchan
current_role: Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (Samajwadi Party, Uttar Pradesh), serving since 2004
profile: Jaya Bachchan (née Bhaduri, b. 1948) is a celebrated Hindi film actress (ten Filmfare Awards, Padma Shri) and a Samajwadi Party Rajya Sabha MP since 2004. Her listed wealth is held jointly with husband Amitabh Bachchan, largely via investments and film/real-estate assets.
interesting_fact: She made her screen debut at 14 in Satyajit Ray's Bengali film Mahanagar (1963), and her first adult lead was Hrishikesh Mukherjee's Guddi (1971).
deep_cut_fact: Inspired by working with Satyajit Ray, she enrolled at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), Pune, and graduated with a gold medal.
notes: Office email is her official Rajya Sabha (sansad.nic.in) address as carried in OpenSanctions' copy of the Rajya Sabha member dataset; verify on sansad.in. Known to be media-averse; poor fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Rup Chand Lohia
current_role: Senior patriarch/director of the Merino Group (Merino Industries / Merino Panel Products, Kolkata); reportedly redesignated Chairman Emeritus in 2024
profile: Rup Chand Lohia is a senior member of the Lohia family behind the Kolkata-based Merino Group, one of India's largest makers of high-pressure decorative laminates, plus plywood, panels and food processing. The family business dates to 1965 (Hapur, UP); day-to-day leadership now sits with family members such as MD Prakash Lohia and CEO Manoj Lohia.
interesting_fact: Merino set up its first high-pressure decorative laminate plant at Hapur in 1981 and now runs laminate plants in Hapur, Rohad, Dahej and Hosur, among India's largest capacities.
notes: Very low public profile; Merino Industries is unlisted (CIN U51909WB1965PLC026556). 'Chairman Emeritus' (2024) came from a search summary of an annual report not directly verified. Best route is via Merino corporate office in Kolkata or MD Prakash Lohia. Alive status not confirmed (no obituary found).

name: Sudarshan Kumar Saraf
current_role: Co-Chairman & Managing Director, Technocraft Industries (India) Ltd, Mumbai
profile: Sudarshan Kumar Saraf co-founded Technocraft with his elder brother Sharad in 1972 using borrowed capital. It became one of the world's largest makers of steel drum closures and also makes scaffolding, formwork and textiles, with affiliates in Canada, China and Poland. He holds roughly 28% of the listed company.
interesting_fact: Technocraft says it was the first company to break an American multinational's monopoly in drum closures, and became the world's second-largest drum-closure producer.
deep_cut_fact: An IIT Bombay mechanical engineering alumnus, he is a keen alumni organizer: during the class of 1969's silver jubilee in 1994 he helped raise Rs 12 lakh in alumni contributions for the institute.
notes: Engineer-founder. The company profile credits him with pioneering an interval thread-rolling process and building special-purpose machines. Sources differ on his title (Co-Chairman & MD vs Chairman); brother Sharad is generally listed as Chairman. Low media profile.

name: Sharad Kumar Saraf
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Technocraft Industries (India) Ltd, Mumbai
profile: IIT Bombay graduate (B.Tech, 1969) who co-founded Technocraft Industries around 1971–72 with his younger brother Sudarshan on a small MIDC plot in Mumbai; it grew into a leading exporter of steel drum closures, scaffolding/steel hardware and cotton yarn/garments. He has also been president of FIEO (Federation of Indian Export Organisations) and of the Council of EU Chambers of Commerce in India.
interesting_fact: He has chaired the boards of governors of IIT Bombay and IIT Jammu as well as the Bombay Textile Research Association.
deep_cut_fact: A self-described student of history and cultures who has visited 50+ countries, he has backed the rejuvenation of Powai Lake (next to his alma mater IIT Bombay) and projects to improve cotton cultivation in Vidarbha; he also writes for Fair Observer and appeared on its podcast in 2023.
notes: Shares Hurun listing with brother Sudarshan Kumar Saraf. Active in export-policy circles (FIEO) and writes op-eds — a thought-leadership/export-manufacturing angle may land well. technocraft@ is the general corporate email on the company site.

name: Nawal Kishore Singh
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director (CMD), Galpha Laboratories Ltd (Mumbai); Alkem Laboratories promoter-group shareholder
profile: Son of Alkem Laboratories founder Samprada Singh and part of Alkem's promoter family; he served on Alkem's board until 2015 and still holds a small promoter stake (~1% in 2024). He runs Galpha Laboratories, a pharma formulations maker that became independent of the Alkem group in 1986, with plants in Baddi and Ankleshwar and exports to 23 countries.
interesting_fact: Galpha says it exports more than 100 pharmaceutical brands to 23 countries; in his CMD message he calls the company 'an extended family of mine' built to provide quality medicines at an affordable price.
notes: Galpha site names him 'Shri N.K. Singh, CMD'; link of N.K. Singh = Nawal Kishore Singh = Samprada Singh's son comes from Wikipedia/aggregator sources (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samprada_Singh). Alkem shareholding: https://trendlyne.com/equity/holding-overtime/73719/nawal-kishore-singh/alkem-laboratories-ltd

name: M Sivakumaran
current_role: Retired; former Whole-time Director of Aurobindo Pharma (stepped down 24 Aug 2023); still listed as director of some Aurobindo group entities
profile: Dr Meenakshisunderam Sivakumaran is an organic chemist who spent about 34 years (1989-2023) as an executive director of Hyderabad-based Aurobindo Pharma, overseeing R&D, new-product development and quality as it grew into one of India's largest generic drugmakers. His wealth stems from his Aurobindo shareholding. He retired from the board in August 2023.
interesting_fact: In his 2023 resignation letter he wrote that 'after careful consideration spanning over several years' he had decided it was time to retire, despite already being past the typical retirement age.
deep_cut_fact: A University of Madras graduate with a doctorate in organic chemistry from Jadavpur University, he joined Aurobindo's board in 1989 — three years after its founding — and led its R&D and new-product development for over three decades.
notes: Retired and very low profile; no personal online presence found. Company IR is only an indirect route. Board change record: https://www.aurobindo.com/investors/corporate-governance/appointment-and-resignation-of-directors

name: Ashok Anand Chandavarkar
current_role: Executive Director, FDC Limited (Mumbai-listed pharmaceutical company)
profile: Member of the Chandavarkar family that controls FDC Ltd (formerly Fairdeal Corporation), the Mumbai drugmaker known for the oral rehydration brand Electral. A mechanical engineer, he joined FDC in 1987, became Executive Director in 1996 and oversees materials procurement, inventories and general management; still listed as an active ED in FDC's April 2026 governance filing.
interesting_fact: FDC traces back to 1936, when founder Anand Chandavarkar began importing infant foods, drugs and surgical appliances; it is today the 'custodian' of Electral, India's best-known oral rehydration salts brand.
deep_cut_fact: Though FDC is a pharma company, he trained as a mechanical engineer (B.E. Mechanical) and is actively involved in running FDC's CSR activities, sitting on its CSR committee.
notes: Born 1941 per NSE filing (age ~85). Low public profile; route via FDC company secretary/IR. Active-director status from NSE integrated governance filing Apr 2026: https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/ixbrl/INTEGRATED_FILING_GOVERNANCE_151745_21042026113420_iXBRL_WEB.html

name: Prakash Amrut Mody
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Unichem Laboratories Ltd (now an Ipca Laboratories subsidiary)
profile: Dr. Prakash A. Mody (b. 1952) is the son of Unichem founder Amrut Mody and joined the board in 1974. He led the Mumbai drugmaker for decades and expanded it into 80+ countries. In 2017 he sold the domestic branded business to Torrent, and in 2023 he sold a 33.38% stake to Ipca Laboratories. He stepped down as MD in August 2023 and remains non-executive chairman.
interesting_fact: In 2017 Unichem sold its India branded-formulations business to Torrent Pharma and pivoted to exports and generics abroad. In 2023 Mody sold control to Ipca for about Rs 1,034 crore (announced price).
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained scientist with a Ph.D. in organic chemistry (after a Mumbai University post-graduate degree), an alumnus of Harvard Business School, and a former president of the Indian Pharmaceutical Alliance, the body of research-based Indian drugmakers.
notes: Low public profile. shares@unichemlabs.com is the company's shareholder or secretarial inbox, not a personal one. Since the Ipca deal, Unichem is controlled by Ipca, so his role is now non-executive.

name: Samit Satish Mehta
current_role: Executive Director (Operations), Emcure Pharmaceuticals; Whole-Time Director & CEO, Gennova Biopharmaceuticals
profile: Samit Mehta is the son of Emcure founder Satish Mehta and a whole-time director of the Pune-based drugmaker, which listed on Indian exchanges in 2024. He built Emcure's business in regulated markets (US, EU, Canada) and in July 2026 was named to lead Gennova, its now wholly owned biologics/mRNA subsidiary.
interesting_fact: Gennova developed India's first mRNA COVID-19 vaccine (HGCO19), designed to be stable at 2-8 degrees C; Mehta argued emerging markets would not adopt a vaccine needing a sub-zero cold chain.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family business he worked as a strategy management consultant at Ernst & Young in India.
notes: Gennova also works on saRNA vaccines (e.g. Nipah) - good biotech/manufacturing angle. Emcure's site blocks automated fetches; IR email taken from earnings-call transcript.

name: Ashok Sarin
current_role: Deceased (was Executive Chairman and founder of Anant Raj Ltd)
profile: Founder (1969) of the Delhi real-estate group Anant Raj Ltd; served as Executive Chairman until his death on 22 August 2021. The company is now led by the next generation (Aman Sarin, CEO) alongside Anil Sarin.
notes: Died 22 Aug 2021 per Anant Raj's stock-exchange intimation: https://bseindia.com/xml-data/corpfiling/AttachHis/ac95e740-007e-4694-9b97-89aed63d7ce7.pdf . Wealth was shared with brother Anil Sarin; for Anant Raj (now pushing into data centres) approach Aman/Anil Sarin.

name: Anil Sarin
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, TARC Limited (formerly Anant Raj Global), New Delhi
profile: Anil Sarin is a co-founder of the Delhi-based Anant Raj real-estate group (with brother Ashok Sarin) and was its managing director until 2020. Since 2016 he has chaired TARC Ltd, the luxury residential developer demerged from Anant Raj; he was re-appointed chairman in May 2024. Anant Raj itself has pivoted into data centres, targeting ~307 MW by FY32.
interesting_fact: Anant Raj, the group he co-founded, plans to invest about US$2.1 billion to scale its data-centre capacity from 28 MW to ~307 MW by FY32, carving the business into Ashok Cloud Pvt Ltd.
notes: For data-center angle, Anant Raj MD Amit Sarin is the public face. TARC IR: Ankush Vijan (no email published). Data aggregators conflict on dates of his Anant Raj roles.

name: Saravana Selvarathinam
current_role: Managing Director, Saravana Selvarathnam Retail Pvt Ltd (Saravana Selvarathinam stores, Chennai) per company-registry data
profile: Part of the Nadar family behind Chennai's Saravana Stores retail empire (founded 1969 as 'Shanmugam Stores', a vessel shop, by brothers Yogarathinam, Selvarathinam and Rajarathinam). The 'Saravana Selvarathinam' branch, founded by S. Selvarathinam, runs large stores in T. Nagar and Pallavaram (Chennai), Tirunelveli and Madurai; registry data lists 'Selvarathinam Saravana' as MD of its retail company.
interesting_fact: Saravana Stores began as 'Shanmugam Stores', a small shop selling vessels, before opening its first big 'Saravana Stores' complex in T. Nagar in 1977; the family's founders came from Panika Nadar Kudiyiruppu village near Tuticorin.
notes: Identity uncertain: Hurun name may refer to the Selvarathinam branch/family or to the son listed in registries as 'Selvarathinam Saravana' (DIN 01835364). Company site saravanaonline.com was unreachable; no published contact found. Very low media profile.

name: Ashok Kumar Nedurumalli
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Vice Chairman, TeamLease Services (MD & CEO until Suparna Mitra took over effective Feb 2, 2026)
profile: Ashok Kumar Reddy Nedurumalli (SRCC, IIM Bangalore) co-founded India Life, a payroll and pension administration firm, with Manish Sabharwal and Mohit Gupta; Hewitt bought it in 2002. The pair then founded TeamLease, now one of India's largest staffing companies, listed in 2016. After about a decade as MD, he moved to Executive Vice Chairman in 2026.
interesting_fact: Before TeamLease, he and SRCC classmate Manish Sabharwal built India Life, a payroll and pension administration company that worked with 450-500 corporates within three years and was bought by Hewitt Associates in 2002. Its exit money went into TeamLease.
deep_cut_fact: Reddy and Sabharwal have been friends since their 1990 batch at Shri Ram College of Commerce. On why they started again after selling India Life, Reddy said: 'We still wanted to rule over our own kingdoms.'
notes: Publicly known as Ashok Reddy. He writes occasional columns for People Matters (https://www.peoplematters.in/author/ashok-reddy) and comments on India's jobs and labour market, which could make a good podcast angle. Beware namesakes (Digital.ai/Broadcom exec).

name: J Murugavel
current_role: Founder, Chairman & Managing Director, Matrimony.com Ltd (BharatMatrimony), Chennai
profile: Murugavel Janakiraman studied statistics at Presidency College Chennai and did an MCA at the University of Madras. While working as a software consultant in New Jersey he started a Tamil community portal in April 1997, which became TamilMatrimony and then BharatMatrimony (2000). He built Matrimony.com into India's largest matchmaking group, listed in 2017, and still runs it.
interesting_fact: The company's own board page says he found his wife through his own matchmaking site.
deep_cut_fact: Matrimony.com began as a hobby: a community portal for Tamil NRIs that he built in his spare time in New Jersey in 1997. The matrimonial listings on that portal took off and became TamilMatrimony. He is also Chairman Emeritus of IAMAI (Internet and Mobile Association of India).
notes: Full name Murugavel Janakiraman. Accessible founder who often speaks to the Indian business press; the corporate communications email is the best route. No verified personal social accounts were confirmed.

name: Rituraj Kishore Sinha
current_role: Group Managing Director, SIS Limited (Security and Intelligence Services India)
profile: Rituraj Kishore Sinha runs SIS, the security, facility-management and cash-logistics group founded by his father R.K. Sinha. After UK banking, he joined in 2002, led India's first private-equity deal in the security sector (2007), 12 acquisitions and the 2017 IPO, and became Group MD in 2017; revenue grew from Rs 25 crore to ~Rs 15,982 crore (FY2026).
interesting_fact: SIS was the first company in India's private-security sector to list on the stock exchanges (2017); under him it has expanded heavily abroad, notably in Australia.
deep_cut_fact: A Doon School alumnus with a Leeds BBA and LBS MBA, he chaired FICCI's Private Security Sector Committee (2014-22), sits on the board of the Swiss-based International Security Ligue and IIM Bodh Gaya, and lists a keen interest in wildlife.
notes: Also active in BJP politics (described as a BJP national secretary by Outlook India topic page) - same person. Data-center angle: SIS provides security/facility services to large campuses, a possible podcast hook.

name: Deep Kalra
current_role: Founder, Group Chairman & Chief Mentor, MakeMyTrip (NASDAQ: MMYT)
profile: Deep Kalra founded MakeMyTrip in 2000 after stints at ABN AMRO, AMF Bowling and GE Capital, and built it into India's largest online travel company, which listed on Nasdaq in 2010. He handed day-to-day leadership to Group CEO Rajesh Magow and in 2022 became group chairman and chief mentor. He also co-founded Ashoka University and chaired the WTTC India Initiative from 2024 to 2026.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for MakeMyTrip while trying to sell his wife's car online, which showed him what the internet could do for transactions in India.
deep_cut_fact: Before MakeMyTrip, after IIM Ahmedabad and three years at ABN AMRO, he worked with AMF Bowling setting up bowling alleys in India. He then joined GE Capital as VP of business development in 1999.
notes: The IR email is the company's published investor-relations contact (Vipul Garg, SVP IR), not Kalra's own. He speaks publicly a lot on travel, startups and philanthropy, including Ashoka University and the 'I am Gurgaon' NGO.

name: Chandra Prakash Madrecha
current_role: Co-founder/director, Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (Mumbai); listed director of Trimax Data Center Services
profile: Chandra Prakash Madrecha is one of the Udaipur-born Madrecha brothers behind Mumbai's Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (founded 1995). Trimax grew from a hardware assembler into a systems integrator and data-centre/e-governance firm, best known for electronic bus-ticketing systems. His brother Surya Prakash was the public face as CMD.
interesting_fact: In 2009 Trimax won the open tender to supply electronic ticket-issuing machines to Maharashtra's state bus corporation (MSRTC). It later built similar systems for BEST, Rajasthan, UP and Bangalore transport, and sold ~1.8m BEST smart cards.
deep_cut_fact: The company name Trimax comes from the founders' philosophy of 'try maximum'. The brothers came from a Udaipur family that ran a kirana store and a wholesale sugar business.
notes: Sources disagree on whether Chandra Prakash or his brother Surya Prakash is 'the founder'. Most press covers Surya Prakash, so check before outreach. There is no recent (2024-26) news on Trimax and no published contact. The data-centre background is relevant to the podcast theme.

name: Surya Prakash Madrecha
current_role: Co-founder and former Chairman & MD, Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (Mumbai); current role unknown
profile: Udaipur-born science graduate who moved to Bombay in 1991 and co-founded Trimax IT Infrastructure & Services (incorporated 1995), growing it from a PC assembler into a systems integrator known for e-ticketing for state bus corporations (MSRTC, BEST, Rajasthan, UP, BMTC). The company entered insolvency in 2018 and was taken over by EbixCash under a 2020 resolution plan.
interesting_fact: Trimax won Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation's 2009 tender for handheld electronic ticketing machines and depot-linked software, and later built BEST's smart card (about 1.8m sold).
deep_cut_fact: 'Trimax' stands for 'try maximum'. His first job was at Sanghvi Electronics for Rs 800 a month, and his old boss Suresh Sanghvi rented him his first Lamington Road office and handed him his first two clients, Dharamsi Morarji Chemical and Arthur Andersen.
notes: Sensitive: Trimax went through insolvency (2018-2020) and lenders filed personal-guarantee proceedings against family members. Hurun wealth figure (2017-18) is likely stale. No current published contact found.

name: Yamunadutt Amilal Agrawal
current_role: Founder and Chairman (non-executive), Jindal Worldwide Ltd (NSE: JINDWORLD), Ahmedabad
profile: Dr Yamunadutt Agrawal founded Jindal Worldwide, an Ahmedabad textile group that calls itself one of India's largest denim makers. It also makes bottom-weight, shirting and yarn-dyed fabrics and home textiles, and exports to the Americas, Europe, Africa and the Middle East. He has been non-executive chairman since 2011, and his son Amit Agrawal runs the company as vice chairman and MD.
interesting_fact: The company says its denim business made it India's largest denim manufacturer. It produces 400-500 fabric designs a month in a vertically integrated operation with about 3,000 staff.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a medical doctor (MD in medicine) before spending 40 years in textiles. He sits on the advisory board of Gujarat's Textile Committee, is vice chairman of the Agrasen Foundation and Maharaja Agrasen Vidhyalaya, and has represented the Gujarat government at summits in the UK, China, Italy, Hong Kong and Singapore.
notes: Not to be confused with the steel and power Jindal family (JSW/Jindal Steel); this is a separate Ahmedabad textile company. Day-to-day leadership sits with his son Amit Agrawal (MD). Only the generic company email is published.

name: Narendra Aggarwal
current_role: Chairman, Shivalik Group / Shivalik Prints Ltd (per 2017 reporting); registry data suggests he may have left the board
profile: Patriarch of the Aggarwal family behind Shivalik Prints, a Faridabad (Delhi NCR) knitwear and garment exporter founded in 1998 as a small family business; it now runs about nine factories supplying Walmart, GAP, H&M, Target and others. Sons/younger directors including Nishant Aggarwal (MD) now lead day-to-day operations.
interesting_fact: Shivalik's factories all sit within a 4-5 km radius so orders can be processed within six hours; in 2017 it produced ~200,000 knitted garments a day with a 99.8% on-time shipping record and zero air shipments.
deep_cut_fact: Shivalik runs 1.5 MW of solar generation with water recycling and set out to become the largest biologically zero-discharge apparel factory in Haryana.
notes: Hurun shares the wealth with Mukesh Aggarwal. The enquiry@ address is the company's general inbox. Next generation (Nishant Aggarwal, MD) may be the more active contact.

name: Mukesh Aggarwal
current_role: Director / export-side leader, Shivalik Prints Ltd (Faridabad garment & textile group)
profile: Mukesh Aggarwal is a son of Narendra Aggarwal, chairman & MD of Shivalik Prints, a vertically integrated knit/woven textile and garment exporter founded in 1998 in Faridabad. With his brother Nishant he has driven the export business, supplying US/EU retailers such as Walmart, Target, Kohl's, JCPenney and H&M from about nine factories.
interesting_fact: Shivalik started exporting only in 2008, in the middle of the global recession, and within five years was producing ~3.5 million garments a month with 6,000+ sewing machines and 10,000+ workers.
deep_cut_fact: Shivalik built a Rs 3.5 crore water-recycling plant around 2010 that recycles ~85% of its wastewater (over 2 million litres a day), and the group has won Target Sourcing's Vendor Partner Excellence Award.
notes: Wealth shared with father Narendra Aggarwal (Hurun). Little personal coverage; latest detailed profile is from 2013. Several unrelated 'Mukesh Aggarwal's exist in India's corporate registry - don't confuse. Company enquiry email is general, not personal.

name: Irshad Mirza
profile: Kanpur leather industrialist, founder/executive chairman of Mirza International (RedTape footwear) and Padma Shri recipient (2010). Died 4 December 2022 in Kanpur.
notes: Deceased (4 Dec 2022), confirmed by ETV Bharat and Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irshad_Mirza). Family business continues: RedTape chairman is Rashid Ahmed Mirza (https://redtape.com/pages/chairs-man-massage).

name: Rashid Ahmed Mirza
current_role: Chairman (non-executive), RedTape Ltd (Noida, India); co-founder of Mirza International / RedTape
profile: Rashid Ahmed Mirza co-founded, with Irshad Mirza, the Kanpur leather business that became Mirza International, a major Indian leather-footwear exporter, and launched the RedTape footwear/apparel brand in 1996. He was Chairman & MD/CEO of Mirza International until 2023, when RedTape was demerged into a separately listed company (NSE/BSE: REDTAPE), which he now chairs.
interesting_fact: RedTape began as a brand of a Kanpur tannery/footwear exporter and was spun off from Mirza International in 2023 into its own listed company focused on branded footwear and apparel in India.
notes: Low media profile; no personal social accounts found. Some sources say he holds a Diploma in Leather Technology from London and that the business began as Mirza Tanners in 1979, but neither could be verified from a primary source, so they were left out. Role details from MarketScreener (https://in.marketscreener.com/insider/RASHID-AHMED-MIRZA-A0JONH/).

name: Prahlad Rai Agarwal
current_role: Chairman (Executive Chairman & Whole-time Director), Rupa & Company Ltd, Kolkata
profile: Prahlad Rai Agarwala (b. 1938, Shekhawati) co-founded the Rupa knitwear brand in 1968 with brothers Ghanshyam Prasad and Kunj Bihari Agarwal; Rupa grew into one of India's largest innerwear and hosiery makers and exporters. He has chaired Rupa & Company since 1985; the family promoter group owns about 74%.
interesting_fact: He received the Padma Shri in 2022 for trade and industry, cited as a 'flag bearer of Make in India'.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Binod Hosiery, set up in 1962, failed before he co-founded Rupa six years later; he also trained in law (LLB, University of Calcutta) and is Honorary Consul of Colombia in Kolkata.
notes: Aged 88; missed the 41st AGM (Kunj Bihari Agarwal presided). Best route is company secretary / IR in Kolkata.

name: Siddhartha Roy Burman
current_role: Executive Chairman, Khadim India Ltd (Kolkata; NSE/BSE: KHADIM)
profile: Kolkata businessman who leads Khadim's, one of India's largest footwear retail chains, started as a single shop by his late father S.P. Roy Burman. He was managing director for years before becoming Executive Chairman; Rittick Roy Burman became Managing Director in April 2025.
interesting_fact: Khadim's grew from one shop into a footwear retailer with more than 800 exclusive outlets. Its founder's motto was 'More than being a manufacturer, I love to manufacture manufacturers': he backed many small shoemaking entrepreneurs as suppliers.
notes: Low media profile; no interviews found. Retail/footwear, not an obvious fit for energy or data centers. The only published route is the company's compliance/IR mailbox.

name: Jahangir Wadia
current_role: Vice Chairman (non-executive), Bombay Dyeing & Manufacturing Co.; director, Britannia Industries and Bombay Burmah Trading Corp (Wadia Group)
profile: Jeh Wadia, son of Nusli Wadia, founded low-cost airline GoAir (later Go First) in 2005 and ran it for 16 years, and was MD of Bombay Dyeing, where he launched real estate arm Bombay Realty in 2011. He left Wadia Group boards in 2021, then returned in late 2024 as a non-executive director and was named Bombay Dyeing vice-chairman in Aug 2025.
interesting_fact: He founded Bombay Realty in 2011 and oversaw two 60-floor residential towers in central Mumbai that were completed in 47 months; WEF named him a Young Global Leader in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He served as Secretary of the Deendayal Research Institute under the late Nanaji Deshmukh, which adopted 500 villages in Chitrakoot to build self-reliant models in health, education, entrepreneurship and agriculture. He was schooled at Lawrence School, Sanawar and Millfield, and holds an MSc from Warwick.
notes: Hurun listing was tied to Go Air; that airline entered insolvency in 2023, so lead with Bombay Realty/Wadia Group rather than the airline. Only published company contact found is Bombay Dyeing's shareholder grievance cell; no personal or PR contact found.

name: Mark Saldanha
current_role: Chairman & Managing Director, Marksans Pharma Ltd (Mumbai)
profile: Science graduate and son of Glenmark founder Gracias Saldanha who took the former Glenmark subsidiary private-label generics business independent and renamed it Marksans Pharma in 2005. He built it into a listed generic/OTC drug maker selling heavily into the US, UK and Australia via acquired subsidiaries; he holds a large controlling stake.
interesting_fact: Glenmark Pharmaceuticals, founded by his father in 1977, was named by combining the names of his two sons: Glenn and Mark. Mark later went his own way with Marksans, while brother Glenn runs Glenmark.
deep_cut_fact: Marksans' official bio describes him as a science graduate with hands-on experience across R&D, marketing, production and finance; the company was renamed Marksans Pharma on 10 Oct 2005 after spinning out of Glenmark.
notes: Low media profile; corporate channels are the realistic route. Not an energy/data-center figure.

name: Vishal Segal
current_role: Co-founder and Non-Executive Director, Lava International Ltd (Noida, India)
profile: Vishal Sehgal (listed as 'Segal' by Hurun) is one of four co-founders of Lava International, the Indian mobile-phone maker founded on 27 March 2009 with Hari Om Rai, Shailendra Nath Rai and Sunil Bhalla. Lava grew into one of India's top domestic handset brands. Sehgal remains on its board; a 2024 restructuring kept him as a director while independent directors were added.
interesting_fact: Lava designs its phones largely in India under Make in India. In FY2023 it held about 25% of India's feature-phone market, and it now sells in 30+ countries, including the UK since early 2026.
notes: Very low public profile: no interviews or personal channels found. The email is Lava's company-compliance address, the closest published corporate route; Lava publishes no press email. Aggregators also link him to Sojo Infotel and Ottomate International (unverified). The Hurun spelling 'Segal' is a variant of Sehgal.

name: Vijaykumar Gupta
