profile: Ludhiana-born (1993) ethical hacker turned entrepreneur. He founded TAC Security at 19 and built it into a vulnerability-management and AppSec platform company (ESOF) that listed in India in 2024, says it has over 10,000 clients, and has made acquisitions such as CyberScope. Hurun lists him among India's youngest self-made rich, at about $215M in 2025.
interesting_fact: He failed 8th standard and dropped out of school, then started TAC Security at 19. Investor Vijay Kedia backed the company's pre-Series A in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: At 19 he trained Ludhiana's station house officers and IPS officers on cybercrime (extracting data from smartphones, tracing IP addresses) at a session organised by Police Commissioner Paramjit Singh Gill. He had already trained Gujarat Police and Punjab DSPs.
notes: Media-friendly founder with frequent press, so likely receptive to podcast outreach. The cybersecurity angle fits the data-center theme. The Facebook page is linked from Wikipedia as 'Official'; X/LinkedIn handles not verified.

name: Daniel P. Harrington
current_role: President and CEO, HTV Industries, Inc. (private holding company, Cleveland area); independent director of Churchill Downs Inc since 1998
profile: Ohio-based private investor who runs HTV Industries, a private holding company with interests in manufacturing, distribution, technology and banking. He has sat on the Churchill Downs board since 1998 (longtime audit chair, compensation chair) and previously on the boards of First Guaranty Bank, First State Financial and Portec Rail Products; his listed wealth reflects CHDN holdings.
interesting_fact: He has been a Churchill Downs director for more than 25 years (since 1998), spanning its transformation from a racetrack operator into a large racing, online wagering and gaming company, and served for years as its Audit Committee chair.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trustee of The Veale Foundation, a Cleveland-area family foundation, alongside running HTV Industries.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal site or social accounts found. Only route is via Churchill Downs IR (contact is a named IR VP published in CDI press releases). Deep-cut fact is thin.

name: Aj Teague
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Enterprise Products Holdings LLC (general partner of Enterprise Products Partners, NYSE: EPD); announced retirement effective Jan 4, 2027
profile: A. James 'Jim' Teague, Louisiana-raised Navy veteran, spent 22 years at Dow Chemical rising to head of hydrocarbon feedstocks, then joined Enterprise in 1999 via its Tejas NGL acquisition. He became COO, then CEO in 2016 and co-CEO with Randy Fowler in 2020 of one of the largest US midstream pipeline/NGL/export companies. Wealth is from EPD units.
interesting_fact: The Greater Houston Port Bureau named him 2021 Maritime Leader of the Year for his advocacy and financial investment to widen and improve the Houston Ship Channel; he has called his work at Enterprise 'a calling'.
deep_cut_fact: After college (East Texas Baptist University) he served in Vietnam with a Navy attack helicopter squadron and as a naval intelligence officer, then joined Dow Chemical as a pharmaceutical sales rep before moving into its hydrocarbon division.
notes: Strong energy fit (NGLs, petrochemicals, LPG/ethane exports, Permian gas for data centers). Outspoken on energy policy in earnings calls. Retiring Jan 2027, may be more available afterwards. Sits on UH Energy advisory board.

name: Byron Allen Folks
current_role: Chairman & CEO, BuzzFeed (since May 2026); Founder, Chairman & CEO, Allen Media Group; ~10.7% holder of Starz
profile: Byron Allen (legal name Byron Allen Folks, born 1961 in Detroit) went from stand-up comic and co-host of NBC's Real People to building Allen Media Group (founded 1993), which owns the Weather Channel and many local TV stations. In May 2026 his family office closed a $120M majority investment in BuzzFeed, and he became its chairman and CEO. He has also bought a large stake in Starz and says he intends to take control of it.
interesting_fact: He made his Tonight Show stand-up debut at 18, then co-hosted NBC's Real People before building a media empire. In 2026 he took over BuzzFeed from founder Jonah Peretti, who moved to a new role heading BuzzFeed AI.
deep_cut_fact: As a boy he tagged along with his mother, an NBC publicist in Burbank, and would sneak onto the empty Tonight Show set to sit at Johnny Carson's desk and pretend to host. Years later he made his own debut on that show.
notes: High profile and media-friendly, and he hosts Comics Unleashed himself. BuzzFeed PR or Allen Media Group are the best routes. His interests now span broadcasting, the Weather Channel, BuzzFeed's AI and 'super app' plans, and a Starz takeover bid, so tech and infrastructure angles may appeal. The X and email contacts are corporate accounts (Allen Media Group / BuzzFeed), not his personal ones.

name: Kirsten M. Spears
current_role: Chief Financial Officer and Chief Accounting Officer, Broadcom Inc. (NASDAQ: AVGO)
profile: Broadcom's CFO since December 2020, promoted from VP, Corporate Controller and Principal Accounting Officer. A career semiconductor finance executive, she came to Broadcom (then Avago) in 2014 via its acquisition of LSI, and now oversees finance for one of the biggest beneficiaries of AI data-center spending (custom AI accelerators and Ethernet networking).
interesting_fact: She became CFO in December 2020 when predecessor Tom Krause moved over to lead the newly formed Broadcom Software Group, making her finance chief through Broadcom's AI-chip boom.
deep_cut_fact: She spent 17 years at LSI Logic/LSI Corp before Broadcom: she joined LSI in September 1997, held accounting and reporting management roles, and became its Corporate Controller in 2007; she holds an MBA from Santa Clara University (class of '93).
notes: Very low public profile beyond quarterly earnings calls; no personal social accounts found. Wealth (~$118M) is from Broadcom equity, well below UHNW thresholds. Approach via Broadcom IR (Ji Yoo).

name: Toby Z. Rice
current_role: President & CEO and Director, EQT Corporation (NYSE: EQT), largest US natural gas producer
profile: Co-founded Rice Energy with his siblings (family started 2007) and served as President/COO until EQT bought it for $6.7B in 2017. In 2019, at age 39, he won a proxy fight and became EQT's CEO, turning it into a vertically integrated gas producer (Equitrans acquisition) and a vocal advocate for US LNG exports and gas to power AI data centers.
interesting_fact: He became CEO of America's largest natural-gas producer in July 2019 after leading a shareholder proxy campaign to take control of the company that had acquired his family's firm.
deep_cut_fact: At Rollins College he captained the 2004 'Dirtbags' baseball team (48-12, first Sunshine State Conference title, DII College World Series semifinal) and was SSC Player of the Year batting .376. A lesson he draws: "You can't tell if you're winning if you're not keeping score."
notes: Very media-friendly; frequent podcast/conference guest on gas, LNG and AI power demand - strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Media route: EQT Strategic Communications (Amy Rogers, Head of Strategic Communications, listed in 2026 releases; email not captured).

name: Todd C Davis
current_role: CEO, Ligand Pharmaceuticals (NASDAQ: LGND); director of Pelthos Therapeutics and Palvella Therapeutics
profile: Healthcare royalty investor who co-founded Cowen Healthcare Royalty Partners (now HealthCare Royalty) in 2006 and later founded RoyaltyRx Capital (2018). A long-time Ligand board member, he became CEO in December 2022 and has refocused Ligand on its royalty-aggregator model of funding late-stage drugs in exchange for royalties.
interesting_fact: He helped pioneer pharmaceutical royalty investing as an asset class: he co-founded Cowen Healthcare Royalty Partners in 2006, then ran it as managing partner until 2018.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Navy veteran and US Naval Academy graduate who began his business career in sales and marketing at Abbott Laboratories before earning a Harvard MBA and moving to Apax Partners.
notes: Best route is Ligand investor relations. The navy detail comes from a board-news aggregator quoting Ligand's Dec 2022 press release.

name: John Ballantyne
current_role: Director and largest shareholder (10%+ owner), Glucotrack Inc (GCTK); biotech investor; retired co-founder/CSO of Aldevron
profile: New Zealand-born pharmaceutical scientist who co-founded Aldevron in Fargo, ND in 1998 with Michael Chambers and served 20+ years as Chief Science Officer; Danaher bought Aldevron for $9.6B in 2021. Now an investor and board member, he joined Glucotrack's board in Sept 2024 and funded its continuous blood glucose monitor first-in-human trial.
interesting_fact: Aldevron's $9.6 billion sale to Danaher was the largest acquisition in North Dakota history; the plasmid-DNA maker became a key supplier for mRNA COVID-19 vaccines.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a pharmacist in New Zealand (Central Institute of Technology and University of Otago) before a pharmaceutical sciences doctorate at NDSU, where he met co-founder Michael Chambers as a student; Aldevron began making plasmid DNA in a small lab on the NDSU campus.
notes: Great founder story (NDSU student startup to $9.6B exit). Low media profile personally; route via Glucotrack IR/ICR. The Aldevron 'largest acquisition in ND history' detail comes from secondary coverage of the deal.

name: David J. Snyderman
current_role: Managing Partner and Global Head of Alternative Credit & Fixed Income, Magnetar Capital; co-owner, Austin FC (MLS)
profile: Dave Snyderman joined Evanston, IL-based alternative asset manager Magnetar Capital in 2005 shortly after its launch and is now Managing Partner and chair of its investment committee. Magnetar was one of CoreWeave's earliest and largest backers - the source of his 10%-owner SEC filings - and invests across credit, energy and infrastructure. Previously head of global credit at Citadel.
interesting_fact: He is an owner of MLS club Austin FC; he played college football at Washington University in St. Louis and is described by the club as an avid sports fan.
deep_cut_fact: Before Citadel he spent five years at Koch Industries running convertible, merger-arb and special-situations portfolios in Houston, Wichita and Switzerland; he started at PricewaterhouseCoopers and sat the CPA exam. He is a founding board member of the Magnetar Capital Foundation's UChicago high-school financial-education program (26,000+ students).
notes: Strong data-center angle: Magnetar's early CoreWeave bet is one of the defining AI-infrastructure investments. Magnetar media email is the best route. Avoid the firm's 2000s CDO controversy.

name: Jeffrey R Immelt
current_role: Venture Partner, New Enterprise Associates (NEA); director of Bloom Energy, Twilio and NeueHealth (and Desktop Metal per SEC filings)
profile: Jeff Immelt was GE's CEO from 2001 to 2017, succeeding Jack Welch and pushing GE into energy, industrial software and the Baker Hughes deal. Since 2018 he has been an NEA venture partner backing healthcare, automation, clean-tech and IoT startups, and he sits on the board of Bloom Energy, a fast-growing supplier of on-site data-center power.
interesting_fact: His Bloom Energy board seat links him to the AI data-center power boom: Bloom's solid-oxide fuel cells are being deployed as on-site power for data centers. He also wrote a 2021 memoir about running GE, 'Hot Seat'.
deep_cut_fact: Fresh out of Dartmouth in 1978, he started at Procter & Gamble in Cincinnati, where he shared a cubicle with future Microsoft CEO Steve Ballmer, before going to Harvard Business School and joining GE in 1982.
notes: High-profile and media-accessible; best route is NEA (or Bloom Energy investor relations/press for an energy angle). The P&G cubicle detail is from Wikipedia (cited there), not independently confirmed in my search.

name: Hans Helmerich
current_role: Director (longtime Chairman) of Helmerich & Payne (NYSE: HP); independent director of Coterra Energy (NYSE: CTRA)
profile: Tulsa oilman and third-generation leader of drilling contractor Helmerich & Payne, founded in 1920 by his grandfather Walter Helmerich II and Bill Payne. He was H&P's president from 1987 and CEO 1989-2014, then chairman; he also sits on Coterra's board (previously Cimarex). The family is a major Tulsa philanthropic force via the Helmerich Trust and Foundation.
interesting_fact: He was inducted into Hart Energy's 50th-anniversary Hall of Fame (2023), which credits H&P's FlexRig, introduced under him in 2002, as a key tool that helped kick-start the US shale revolution.
deep_cut_fact: He pushed ahead with the FlexRig launch in 2002 in the middle of an industry downturn, reassuring customers by signing two-to-three-year contracts so they could count on a return. He studied government at Dartmouth.
notes: Full name Hans Christian Helmerich. Whether he still holds the H&P chair in 2026 not confirmed (Trey Adams became CEO Mar 2026). Hart Energy page could not be fetched directly; facts from search summary of it. Dartmouth detail from twst.com/insider bios.

name: Peter Yu
current_role: Managing Partner, Cartesian Capital Group; Chairman & CEO, Cartesian Growth Corp IV; board observer at Factorial Energy (NASDAQ: FAC) after its June 2026 SPAC merger with Cartesian Growth Corp III
profile: Private-equity investor who founded AIG Capital Partners (>$4.5bn committed capital) and then co-founded New York-based Cartesian Capital Group in 2006, leading 20+ investments across 30+ countries. Through his Cartesian Growth SPACs he took AlTi Global and solid-state battery maker Factorial Energy public; his sponsor entities hold a large Factorial stake.
interesting_fact: Before finance he was President of the Harvard Law Review, clerked on the U.S. Supreme Court, and served President Bill Clinton as a Director of the National Economic Council.
deep_cut_fact: Alongside his deals he sits on the board of The John Paul Stevens Fellowship Foundation and the advisory council of Princeton's School of Public & International Affairs (his alma mater), and his boards include Tims China and Argentine low-cost airline Flybondi.
notes: Not Factorial's operating CEO (Siyu Huang is CEO; SEC insider title reflects his SPAC role). Factorial S-1 (June 2026) says Factorial appointed him board Observer. Good angle: SPAC financing of next-gen battery tech.

name: Matthew B. Oppenheimer
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Remitly Global (Nasdaq: RELY); former CEO. Sebastian Gunningham is CEO as of 2026.
profile: Matt Oppenheimer co-founded Remitly in Seattle in 2011 with Josh Hug and Shivaas Gulati and ran it as CEO for more than a decade, through its 2021 IPO. Remitly is a mobile-first cross-border payments company with more than 9.6 million customers. By 2026 Sebastian Gunningham had taken over as CEO and Oppenheimer remained on the board.
interesting_fact: In 2025, while still CEO, he spoke at the Milken Institute Global Conference and the Philadelphia Fed fintech conference about widening access to financial services for immigrants who send money home.
deep_cut_fact: Remitly did not start under that name. It began in 2011 as BeamIt Mobile, a search engine for comparing remittance services, before it started moving money itself, and it was renamed Remitly in August 2012.
notes: I could not confirm the exact date of the CEO handover or his current title beyond director: the SEC data says Director, and Remitly's Sept 2026 release names Gunningham as CEO. Check the Remitly IR site (blocked to my fetcher) before outreach. The widely told founding story about his time at Barclays in Kenya is not verified here. He has a LinkedIn profile, but I did not verify the URL.

name: John P Rochon
current_role: Founder & Chairman, AIAI Holdings Corp (Nasdaq: AIAI), Dallas; founder of Richmont Holdings
profile: Dallas investor and former chairman/CEO of Mary Kay Inc. who founded the private-equity and holding firm Richmont Holdings in the late 1980s/1990. In May 2026 he took AIAI Holdings (Ai²), an 'AI-enabled diversified holding company', public via a Nasdaq direct listing. It licenses AI tech from his company M42, and his family has since bought about US$127m of extra shares.
interesting_fact: AIAI listed on Nasdaq in May 2026 through a direct listing, not an IPO, so it raised no new capital. The pitch is buying companies across industries and running them on 'Transformational AI' licensed from Rochon's M42.
deep_cut_fact: As CEO of privately held Mary Kay in the late 1980s, Rochon tried unsuccessfully to buy its much larger rival Avon. Decades later, as Richmont chairman, he was again reported to be preparing an Avon bid.

public_contacts.value: Matthew Selinger, Integrous Communications (AIAI IR) - mselinger@integcom.us

notes: AI and holding-company angle fits the podcast. The AIAI CEO is Todd Furniss, who could be a route in. Mary Kay tenure dates vary across aggregator sites. The deep-cut source page blocked automated fetch and was confirmed only through search snippets, so re-check it before use.

name: Michael O'Grady
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Northern Trust Corporation (Chicago). Director, Abbott Laboratories.
profile: Michael G. O'Grady (60) was a Bank of America Merrill Lynch investment banker who joined Northern Trust as CFO in 2011. He then ran its Corporate & Institutional Services arm, became President in 2017, CEO in 2018 and Chairman in 2019. He leads the bank's 'One Northern Trust' strategy, and it reported 2025 revenue of about $8.1bn.
interesting_fact: He moved from outsider to CEO in about seven years: hired from BofA Merrill's investment banking group as CFO in 2011, he was running the 130-plus-year-old Chicago custody and wealth bank by 2018.
notes: Best route is the Northern Trust media contacts listed on its 2026 press releases. Web search quota ran out during this lane, so no deep-cut fact was sourced.

name: Christopher William Degnan
current_role: Former Chief Revenue Officer, Snowflake; now a go-to-market adviser, fund investor and Stanford GSB lecturer (MEDDIC course)
profile: Chris Degnan was Snowflake's first sales hire and its CRO for 11 years, scaling revenue from zero to about $3.5B under four CEOs. Earlier he sold at Informatica and Covalent, spent ~8 years at EMC (rising to AVP West) and was VP West at Aveksa. He now advises founders and invests.
interesting_fact: He brought EMC's MEDDPICC sales-qualification discipline to Snowflake, and now teaches a MEDDIC course at Stanford Graduate School of Business.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he was told he would never be a VP of Sales, let alone a CRO. He began in EMC's mid-market commercial sales team and spent about eight years there learning under sales trainer John McMahon.
notes: Data-infrastructure fit (Snowflake). Has done several long-form podcasts (First Round, Operators), so receptive to interviews. Could not confirm exact date he left the CRO post (web-search budget exhausted); First Round now titles him 'Former CRO'.

name: Peter Dore Rawlinson
current_role: Former CEO & CTO, Lucid Group (step-down announced 25 Feb 2025); current role not confirmed
profile: Welsh-born automotive engineer (b. 1957) who held senior engineering roles at Jaguar and Lotus, was VP/chief vehicle engineer of the Tesla Model S (2009-2012), then joined Lucid as CTO in 2016 and became CEO in 2019, overseeing the Lucid Air and Gravity. He stepped down as CEO in 2025.
interesting_fact: A week after joining Tesla in 2009 he told Elon Musk the early Model S prototype was a 'false dawn' and restarted the car from a clean sheet; at Lucid he also oversaw the battery packs supplied to every Formula E team.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Bonvilston in the Vale of Glamorgan, attended Cowbridge Grammar School, and considered art school before choosing engineering at Imperial College (graduated 1979); in the 1980s his Jaguar team built the company's first intranet for moving engineering files.
notes: No longer Lucid CEO, so Lucid press office is not a good route; no personal site or verified social account found. Strong energy/battery angle (efficiency-focused EV powertrains).

name: Elizabeth P Bruno
current_role: Director, Brady Corporation (since 2003); President, Brady Education Foundation (Chapel Hill, NC)
profile: Dr. Elizabeth Pungello Bruno is a descendant of Brady Corp founder William H. Brady Jr. and a long-time Brady director, with the family holding control of the voting stock. A former developmental psychology researcher at UNC Chapel Hill, she leads the Brady Education Foundation, which funds research on closing educational opportunity gaps.
interesting_fact: Through the Brady Education Foundation she helped launch a roughly $3M initiative to rigorously study public Montessori education, with the Trust for Learning.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the family foundation she was a developmental psychology researcher/professor at UNC Chapel Hill; she is a University of Rochester alumna (1989).
notes: Sources differ on whether she is the founder's granddaughter (Brady IR site) or great-granddaughter (BizTimes). Philanthropy/education-research focused; foundation contact form is the best route. Brady IR contact Ann Thornton by phone only.

name: Amir Elstein
current_role: Chairman, Tower Semiconductor (NASDAQ/TASE: TSEM); Independent Director, Teva Pharmaceutical; Chairman, Israel Democracy Institute
profile: Israeli executive and physicist who held senior roles at Intel, latest as GM of Intel Electronics Ltd. (Israel), then joined Teva in 2004, rising to EVP Global Pharmaceutical Resources. He has chaired specialty foundry Tower Semiconductor since 2009 and the Israel Democracy Institute since 2012; he also chaired Israel Corporation (2010-13) and sits on Teva's board.
interesting_fact: Under his chairmanship Tower has become a key silicon-photonics foundry for AI data-center interconnects; in 2026 it announced customer contracts worth $1.3B of silicon photonics revenue for 2027.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a physicist: a B.Sc. in physics and mathematics and an M.Sc. in solid-state physics, both from the Hebrew University of Jerusalem. He also chaired the Board of Governors of the Jerusalem College of Engineering from 2009 to 2018.
notes: Emails are the Tower company contact (Orit Shahar) and IR contact (Liat Avraham) printed in Tower's 2026 press releases. Good data-center angle via silicon photonics/analog foundry. The Israel Democracy Institute is a possible alternative route.

name: Miles E. Everson
current_role: Former CFO (to Apr 2026) and director (Apr-Jul 2026) of Fermi Inc.; former CEO of MBO Partners. Current role not publicly stated
profile: Veteran consulting executive: 20+ years at PwC, rising to Global Advisory and Consulting Leader and Vice Chairman, then CEO of independent-workforce platform MBO Partners (2019-2025). He joined Fermi America, the Rick Perry co-founded Texas 'HyperGrid' nuclear/gas data-center power campus developer, as CFO around its Oct 2025 IPO, moved to the board in April 2026 and resigned in July 2026.
interesting_fact: He was finance chief of Fermi America, which IPO'd in 2025 to build a multi-gigawatt private power and AI data-center campus near Amarillo combining gas, solar and planned nuclear reactors.
deep_cut_fact: A Minnesota-educated accountant, he holds a B.S. in Accounting from St. Cloud State University's Herberger Business School, the base for a 25+ year PwC career that ended as global head of its advisory business.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast, but sensitive: he resigned from Fermi's board on 10 Jul 2026 citing a disagreement with the company (8-K), and he was a board designee of co-founder Toby Neugebauer amid litigation. Don't raise that. No published personal contact found; LinkedIn is the likely route (not verified).

name: Raffaele Zagari
current_role: CEO and Chairman, Augustea Group (Naples); Director, Star Bulk Carriers (NASDAQ: SBLK)
profile: Neapolitan shipowner from the Cafiero-Zagari family behind Augustea Group, which he has led since 2010 after running its chartering desk from 1997. In 2018 Augustea sold 16 dry-bulk ships to Star Bulk largely for shares, which brought him onto Star Bulk's board and created his SBLK stake.
interesting_fact: The 2018 sale of 16 Augustea bulkers to Star Bulk was paid mostly in Star Bulk stock, turning the Zagari family into major shareholders of one of the largest US-listed dry-bulk owners.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining the family firm he cut his teeth at Zodiac Maritime Agencies in London (1996-97) and earlier at Blenheim Shipping, where he gained hands-on experience at Japanese shipyards; he holds a diploma in commercial shipping operations from London Guildhall University.
notes: Dates for his Augustea CEO role vary by source (2010 per Star Bulk, 2015 per a third-party case study). Route via Augustea Group or Star Bulk IR.

name: Gregory A Heckman
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Bunge Global SA (BG), St. Louis
profile: Agribusiness and energy trader who has been CEO of Bunge since 2019 (board since 2018). He led its merger with Viterra and took it into the S&P 500 in 2023. Earlier he was CEO of The Gavilon Group (2008-15), where he grew its agriculture and energy arms before selling them to Marubeni and NGL Energy Partners. Before that he held COO roles at ConAgra.
interesting_fact: His Bunge bio cites food security and 'sustainable food, feed and renewable fuel production' as priorities. He also serves on the board of the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis and is a non-executive director of fertilizer maker OCI NV.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bunge he was a founding partner of Flatwater Partners. He holds a B.S. in agricultural economics and marketing from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.
notes: Strong energy angle: Gavilon had an energy arm, and Bunge is a big renewable diesel and SAF feedstock supplier. He speaks often at ag industry events such as the NGFA convention in 2026.

name: Joshua (Josh) Jergensen
current_role: President & Chief Operating Officer, PACS Group, Inc. (NYSE: PACS), Farmington, Utah
profile: Senior operator at PACS Group, a fast-growing US post-acute and skilled-nursing company (from 2 facilities in 2013 to 324). He has provided operational support across the PACS portfolio since 2014 and is now president and COO, driving acquisitions such as a 32-facility Florida deal. His wealth comes from PACS stock after the 2024 IPO.
interesting_fact: PACS grew from two facilities in 2013 to 324 within about a decade (roughly 16,000%), a story Jergensen presented at Utah Business's Forward event in 2026 under the theme 'healthcare is local'.
deep_cut_fact: He is a licensed nursing home administrator and approved preceptor (trainer of new administrators) in California. He holds a BYU Marriott business degree and a USC master's in healthcare administration, and is a keen golfer.
notes: Not a co-founder (Jason Murray and Mark Hancock founded PACS). Healthcare operator with little link to energy or data centres.

name: Jason Robins
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman & CEO, DraftKings Inc. (DKNG), Boston
profile: Former Vistaprint analytics executive who co-founded DraftKings in 2012 with colleagues Matt Kalish and Paul Liberman. He took it from daily fantasy sports to the largest US-based vertically integrated sports betting and iGaming operator, and in 2026 is pushing into prediction markets; DraftKings says 1.6M+ customers used its Predictions product year-to-date in Q3 2026.
interesting_fact: In April 2013 Major League Baseball invested in DraftKings, the first US pro league to invest in daily fantasy sports.
deep_cut_fact: DraftKings started out of co-founder Paul Liberman's house, and its very first product was a one-on-one fantasy baseball contest timed to launch on MLB Opening Day 2012.
notes: Active on LinkedIn and X personally (handles not verified here). Media-savvy; route via Media@draftkings.com. Avoid referencing the 2024 SEC Reg FD matter tied to his social posts.

name: Zachary Bradford
current_role: CEO and President, CleanSpark, Inc. (Nasdaq: CLSK) since October 2019
profile: Nevada CPA who joined CleanSpark as CFO in 2014 and became CEO in 2019, steering it from a microgrid/energy-software company into one of the largest US bitcoin miners. In 2026 CleanSpark is repositioning its power and land portfolio (e.g. its Sandersville, Georgia site) for AI/HPC data-center development.
interesting_fact: CleanSpark now pitches its bitcoin-mining sites and power capacity as AI/HPC data-center campuses – a September 2026 investor presentation focused on its Sandersville, GA site – squarely in the podcast's energy/data-center theme.
deep_cut_fact: Before CleanSpark he founded his own public accounting and consulting firm in Henderson, Nevada in June 2013 (still a non-active partner); he earned a bachelor's in accounting and a master of accountancy from Southern Utah University and sits on the board of the Digital Energy Council.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy/data-center podcast; frequent conference speaker (e.g. Bitcoin 2023). Route via pr@cleanspark.com.

name: Arie Kotler
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, ARKO Corp. (Nasdaq: ARKO), parent of GPM Investments
profile: Israeli-born Arie Kotler, in the U.S. since 1997, founded GPM Investments in 2003 by buying the Fas Mart and Shore Stop c-store chains, regained control in 2011 and built Richmond, Virginia-based ARKO into one of the largest U.S. convenience-store and fuel operators through serial acquisitions. ARKO went public on Nasdaq via a 2020 SPAC merger with Haymaker II.
interesting_fact: GPM had about 200 stores in seven states when Kotler took over as CEO in 2011; by 2022, after 21 acquisitions and some 5,000 stores vetted, it ran roughly 1,400 stores in 35 states. 'We're an acquisition company. We have it in our blood.'
deep_cut_fact: Before ARKO's Nasdaq listing he chaired and ran Arko Holdings Ltd., a Tel Aviv Stock Exchange-listed company that controlled GPM, so the U.S. c-store roll-up was originally financed through the Israeli capital market.
notes: Fuel retail/energy-adjacent (c-stores plus fuel wholesale), a good energy-podcast fit. Named to Virginia Business power lists 2025 and 2026. IR email is published on the ARKO homepage.

current_role: Listed as founder/owner of Xin Gaochao Group (China); current role not verified
profile: Tao Xinkang is listed among China's wealthy with Xin Gaochao Group as the source of wealth. No independent public sources could be retrieved to confirm his current role or the group's business in this pass.

name: Zhu Zhangjin
current_role: President (总裁) of Kasen Group / Kasen International Holdings (HKEX: 0496), Haining, Zhejiang; chairman of its Cambodian special economic zone
profile: Zhu Zhangjin built Kasen from a small tannery (1988) into a leather and sofa exporter, listed in Hong Kong in 2005. The group expanded into property and resorts in Hainan and Changbaishan. Since 2019 Kasen has repositioned as a Belt-and-Road special-economic-zone operator in Cambodia and an international power developer. It builds thermal, solar, hydro and wind projects in Mongolia, Cambodia and Zimbabwe.
interesting_fact: Kasen now develops power projects (coal, solar, hydro, wind, district heating) in Mongolia, Cambodia and Zimbabwe with Chinese state builders. It also runs the 15,000-mu Koh Kong Zhejiang Special Economic Zone in Cambodia, launched 2022-23.
deep_cut_fact: Kasen began in 1988 as the Qingyun Huafeng tannery, making pigskin and sheepskin garment leather. By 2001 its leather sofas were exported to Europe and the US and, per the company, 'placed in the White House'.
notes: Listed (Wikipedia) among Zhejiang delegates to the National People's Congress. He accompanied President Hu Jintao on a 2008 state visit to the Americas. Strong energy/infrastructure angle (overseas power plants). Chinese-language outreach advised; the HK email is the listed company's IR mailbox (via IMS).

name: Martin Lawrence
current_role: Actor and stand-up comedian; touring 'Y'all Still Know What It Is!' (2026)
profile: American comedian and actor (born 1965). He co-created and starred in Fox's 'Martin' (1992-97) and plays Marcus Burnett in the four 'Bad Boys' films with Will Smith, the latest being 2024's 'Ride or Die'. Other hits include 'Big Momma's House'. He is back on the road with a national stand-up tour through 2026 and starred in Tubi's sci-fi comedy series 'Demascus' (2025).
interesting_fact: He received a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame on April 20, 2023, and his 'Bad Boys' role spans nearly three decades, from 1995 to 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Frankfurt, West Germany, while his father served in the US Air Force, and was named after Martin Luther King Jr. and John F. Kennedy. As a teen in Maryland he was a Mid-Atlantic Golden Gloves boxing contender.
notes: Entertainer rather than a business founder, so a weaker fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast. Reach him through his talent agency or publicist; none was verified here. martinlawrence.com is an unrelated art gallery (Martin Lawrence Galleries), so do not use it. He owns a farm near Purcellville, VA. His net worth (~$110M) comes from Wikidata/press estimates.

name: Emilie Choi
current_role: President & COO, Coinbase Global; Director, Okta
profile: Johns Hopkins economics grad and Wharton MBA who started in investment banking, worked at Yahoo and on digital strategy at Warner Bros., then spent 8+ years leading M&A/corporate development at LinkedIn. Joined Coinbase in 2018 to run corporate development, became COO in 2019 and President in 2020, steering it through its 2021 listing and crypto cycles; on Okta's board since 2022.
interesting_fact: She joined Coinbase to run M&A and within a year her remit had expanded to business development, ventures, strategy, data, international and institutional coverage; she describes herself as 'not an engineer and I'm not a product person' but a partner to founders.
deep_cut_fact: She joined LinkedIn when it had about 400 employees and left when it had about 13,000; she started her tech career at Yahoo 'back when Yahoo was the epicenter of all the technology activity.'
notes: Has done several podcasts (Masters of Scale with Reid Hoffman, Grit, The Block's The Scoop), so podcast-friendly. Personal X handle not verified; LinkedIn reportedly linkedin.com/in/emiliechoi (unverified, from an aggregator).

name: Thomas S Bremner
current_role: Partner, Venture Growth, Adams Street Partners (Chicago); independent director, BillionToOne (NASDAQ: BLLN)
profile: Chicago growth-equity investor focused on healthcare technology. He joined Adams Street Partners in 2013 after roles at Summit Partners, The Edgewater Funds and JPMorgan Chase. He has served on the board of prenatal and cancer-diagnostics company BillionToOne since 2022, and his reported health-tech investments include DispatchHealth, Lyra Health and VillageMD.
interesting_fact: He has sat on BillionToOne's board since early 2022, before its 2025 Nasdaq IPO. BillionToOne makes molecular diagnostics such as single-molecule prenatal and oncology tests.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at the University of Dayton (BS) before earning an MBA with high honors from Chicago Booth. He is a CFA charterholder and sits on Adams Street's Impact Investment Committee.
notes: Probably on Forbes/SEC lists through Adams Street's BillionToOne stake rather than personal founder wealth. The best route is Adams Street's contact page.

name: D James Bidzos
current_role: Executive Chairman, President & CEO, VeriSign Inc.
profile: Jim Bidzos is a pioneer of commercial internet security. He ran RSA Data Security from 1986 to 1999, co-founded RSA Laboratories, created the RSA Conference in 1991 and founded VeriSign in 1995. He has chaired VeriSign since 2007 and been CEO since 2011. Verisign now runs the authoritative .com and .net registries and two of the internet's 13 root servers.
interesting_fact: He started the RSA Conference in 1991 as a small cryptography gathering; it grew into one of the world's largest cybersecurity events. In the mid-1990s he publicly led the industry campaign against the US government's Clipper chip.
deep_cut_fact: When he joined RSA Data Security on 1 Feb 1986, he later said the company was 'a complete failure'. A toolkit deal with Iris Associates (makers of Lotus Notes) helped turn it around, and by 1993 about 100 companies were using RSA's encryption toolkit.
notes: Rarely gives interviews these days. Strong fit for internet-infrastructure / data-center themes (DNS root operations). Route via Verisign media relations, using the contacts published in the Q3 2026 earnings release.

name: Jane Nind Fraser
current_role: Chair (since Oct 2025) and CEO (since 2021), Citigroup Inc.
profile: Scottish-born banker (b. 1967, St Andrews) who became the first woman to run a major US bank when she took over as Citigroup CEO in 2021, adding the chair role in October 2025. A former McKinsey partner, she joined Citi in 2004 and ran Citi Private Bank, CitiMortgage, US consumer banking and Latin America; she is leading Citi's multi-year simplification and restructuring.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her No. 1 on its 2026 Most Powerful Women list; she was made a Dame (DBE).
deep_cut_fact: Before banking leadership, she co-authored the 1999 book 'Race for the World: Strategies to Build a Great Global Firm' with three McKinsey colleagues, and early on worked as a brokerage associate at Asesores Bursátiles in Madrid (1990-92).
notes: Very high-profile CEO; requests go through Citi Corporate Communications (US media hotline 212-793-0710 published on the same page). Educated at Girton College, Cambridge and Harvard Business School.

name: David Hallal
current_role: Chairman (since 2017) and CEO (since April 2025), Scholar Rock Holding Corp (NASDAQ: SRRK); Executive Chairman, ElevateBio
profile: Biotech commercial executive who spent 2006-2016 at Alexion Pharmaceuticals, rising from Chief Commercial Officer to COO and CEO, then co-founded/led cell and gene therapy company ElevateBio. He chaired Scholar Rock's board from 2017 and took over as CEO in 2025 to bring its SMA drug apitegromab to market; his wealth comes largely from Scholar Rock equity.
interesting_fact: He built Alexion's commercial infrastructure for Soliris, one of the world's most expensive drugs for ultra-rare diseases, before becoming the company's CEO.
deep_cut_fact: A psychology graduate of the University of New Hampshire, he began his career in 1988 at The Upjohn Company, and as VP of Sales at OSI Eyetech led the US launch of Macugen; he still sits on the UNH Foundation board.
notes: Also chairs Kalaris Therapeutics; listed as iTeos director in SEC data. Biotech rather than energy, so a stretch for the podcast's theme; route via Scholar Rock media (Molly MacLeod per releases).

name: Jean-Marie Mognetti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, CoinShares PLC (Nasdaq: CSHR)
profile: French-born Jean-Marie Mognetti co-founded CoinShares, Europe's largest digital-asset manager, which launched the world's first regulated Bitcoin ETP in 2015 and holds ~34% EMEA crypto-ETP market share. A former quantitative commodity trader, he has led the Jersey-registered firm since 2014, including its 2024 acquisition of Valkyrie and its move to a US listing.
interesting_fact: CoinShares launched the world's first regulated Bitcoin exchange-traded product in 2015—roughly a decade before US spot Bitcoin ETFs were approved.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he was a quant commodity trader at Hermes Commodities Fund Managers, after a Master's in Mathematical Trading and Finance from Sir John Cass Business School; Blockworks reports oil-industry/JPMorgan veterans Danny Masters and Russell Newton brought him into what became CoinShares in 2012.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and media guest — good podcast fit (bitcoin mining/energy angle via CoinShares' mining research and ETPs). Background story: blockworks.co 'Gone Crypto: Mognetti and the Birth of CoinShares'.

name: Douglas Valenti
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, QuinStreet Inc. (Nasdaq: QNST), Foster City, CA
profile: Founded performance-marketing firm QuinStreet in 1999 (CEO since 1999, chairman since 2004) and took it public in 2010; it runs online customer-acquisition marketplaces for insurance, financial and home services. Georgia Tech industrial engineer, Stanford MBA, ex-Rosewood Capital partner and McKinsey consultant. Owns ~3.4% of QNST.
interesting_fact: Before founding QuinStreet he worked at McKinsey, Procter & Gamble and venture firm Rosewood Capital, and graduated from Georgia Tech in industrial engineering with highest honors.
deep_cut_fact: He spent five years as a U.S. Navy nuclear submarine officer before going into business school and consulting.
notes: IR contact (Robert Amparo) is the published route. Low personal media profile beyond earnings calls.

name: Bradley Bauer
current_role: Partner, Co-CEO and Co-CIO, Värde Partners (global alternative credit investor; Minneapolis/New York)
profile: Brad Bauer joined Värde in 2007, became a partner in 2013 and was named Co-CEO alongside Ilfryn Carstairs in October 2023. He also oversees private-markets investing as Co-CIO. He appears as a 10% owner of Nabors Industries (NBR) only because he is a reporting person on Värde funds' filings after Nabors bought Parker Wellbore in 2025, and he disclaims beneficial ownership beyond his pecuniary interest.
interesting_fact: Värde, founded in Minneapolis in 1993, has invested more than $100bn across credit markets. Bauer co-leads it under a deliberate US/Asia co-CEO structure with Singapore-based Carstairs, with whom he had worked for more than 16 years by 2023.
notes: The SEC 'TenPercentOwner' flag on Nabors reflects Värde fund holdings, not a personal stake. Route through Värde Communications & Public Affairs. He is a frequent speaker at private-credit conferences such as SuperReturn and the Milken Institute.

name: Daniel Masters
current_role: Co-founder and Non-executive Director (former Executive Chairman), CoinShares
profile: Daniel Masters (b. 1963) is a veteran energy trader turned crypto pioneer. After heading global energy trading at Morgan Guaranty Trust and working in Salomon's energy division, he founded Jersey-based commodities manager Global Advisors, launched the world's first regulated bitcoin fund (GABI) in 2014, and co-founded CoinShares, now a Nasdaq-listed digital-asset manager.
interesting_fact: He launched GABI, described as the world's first regulated bitcoin fund, out of Jersey in 2014 - years before institutional crypto ETPs.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he helped establish the UK's natural gas and electricity markets, completed some of the first forward contracts for electricity, and was among the earliest active traders in European Contracts for Difference.
notes: Excellent energy+crypto fit: physics graduate (Exeter), MSc OR (Imperial), 30+ years in energy trading. Route via CoinShares press office.

name: Thomas J. Healy
current_role: Founder & CEO, Hyliion Holdings Corp. (HYLN)
profile: Thomas Healy founded Hyliion in 2015 out of Carnegie Mellon to electrify long-haul trucks and took it public via SPAC in Oct 2020 at a $1B+ valuation. After exiting the EV powertrain business in 2023, he pivoted Hyliion to the KARNO generator - a 3D-printed, fuel-agnostic linear-heat generator (tech bought from GE for $37M) pitched for data centers, the US Navy and oilfield power.
interesting_fact: He argues 'every electron will end up in a data center' and that providers now start site planning with 'How do we secure power?' rather than 'Where do we put servers?' - a direct fit for an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: A Carnegie Mellon mechanical engineering & public policy grad (ENG 2014) with a passion for racing and motorsports, he founded two startups while still in college before starting Hyliion from his CMU dorm room; CMU featured him in its 'Tartans on the Rise' alumni honours.
notes: Top-priority guest for the podcast: young founder now selling on-site generators to data centers (Flexnode LOI for up to 10 KARNO units, US Navy and Air Force contracts). Does media readily (FreightWaves, Startup Junkie podcast). Forbes 30 Under 30 (2017).

name: Margot Golden
current_role: Director, The New York Times Company (since 2024); Chair, Ochs-Sulzberger Trust
profile: Margot Golden Tishler, about 49, is a fifth-generation member of the Ochs/Sulzberger family that controls The New York Times Company through its Class B shares. She chairs the family's Ochs-Sulzberger Trust and joined the NYT board in 2024, succeeding her relative Hays N. Golden. Her wealth comes from the family's inherited NYT stake.
interesting_fact: As chair of the Ochs-Sulzberger Trust she sits at the center of the dual-class structure that has kept one family in control of The New York Times since Adolph Ochs bought it in 1896.
deep_cut_fact: Outside the boardroom she is a freelance graphic designer with an associate degree in graphic design from Pratt Institute, and she manages a small company that sells accessories for children's clothing.
notes: Also listed as Margot Golden Tishler. Very private family member with no public media presence. The contacts are NYT's corporate press and IR contacts from the Feb 2024 nomination release and may have changed. Not an obvious fit for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Ryan P. Taylor
current_role: Managing Partner, Richmond Hill Investment Co. (NYC); Director, Reservoir Media, Inc. (Nasdaq: RSVR)
profile: New York investor who has run Richmond Hill Investments, a registered adviser managing opportunistic private partnerships, since founding it in 2008/2010, after a decade (1998–2008) at Greenhill & Co. rising to Principal. Richmond Hill-affiliated entities are among the largest holders of independent music company Reservoir Media, where he has been a director since 2019 (Reservoir Holdings) and of the public company since 2021.
interesting_fact: He sat on the Board of Managers of hip-hop label Tommy Boy Music from 2017 until Reservoir acquired it in June 2021, and serves on boards of several other private music-business companies.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a B.B.A. in Finance with Honors from the University of Texas at Austin in 1998 and went straight to Greenhill & Co., where he spent ten years before co-founding Richmond Hill.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts identified. Reservoir contacts are company-level; no published Richmond Hill contact found.

name: Andrew Gundlach
current_role: President & Co-CEO, Bleichroeder LP; Independent Director, Welltower (since July 2024)
profile: New York investor (b. ~1971) who spent nearly 30 years in investing; a long-time First Eagle Investment Management director (from 2004), he initiated the 2015 sale of majority control to Blackstone and Corsair and in 2019 spun out Bleichroeder LP, an RIA for ultra-high-net-worth families. Bleichroeder sponsored SPACs incl. the vehicle (BACQ) that merged with autonomous-flight firm Merlin.
interesting_fact: He is a trustee of the Guggenheim Museum, sits on the Columbia Business School board and the Council on Foreign Relations' investment committee.
deep_cut_fact: Since 2004 he has taught investing as an adjunct professor at Columbia Business School's Heilbrunn Center for Graham & Dodd Investing; he started out in corporate finance and M&A at Morgan Stanley and J.P. Morgan after Georgetown's School of Foreign Service.
notes: No published personal contacts found; bleichroeder.com returned an empty page. Best route: Bleichroeder LP (New York) or Columbia Business School Heilbrunn Center. Merlin/BACQ SPAC details were partly conflicting in sources.

name: Paul E Jacobs
current_role: CEO, Globalstar (since Aug 2023); director of Dropbox
profile: Berkeley EECS PhD who joined Qualcomm as an engineer in 1990 and led it as CEO (2005-2014) and executive chairman until 2018, steering the smartphone-chip era. He then founded wireless startup XCOM Labs (now Virewirx) and in 2023 became CEO of satellite operator Globalstar, Apple's partner for iPhone emergency satellite messaging.
interesting_fact: Named on 80+ U.S. patents (granted or pending) in wireless technology; elected to the National Academy of Engineering (2016) and a part-owner/vice chairman of the NBA's Sacramento Kings.
deep_cut_fact: After his 1989 PhD he spent a year as a postdoc at a French government lab in Toulouse, then at Qualcomm led the team that built the variable-rate 8 kbps CDMA speech codec — the source of one of his early patents. As a kid he wrote code to play the game Adventure with his dad.
notes: Speech-codec detail also in Berkeley EECS bio (https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/bears/2005/jacob-bio.shtml); Adventure anecdote from Cal alumni magazine (https://alumni.berkeley.edu/california-magazine/summer-2017-adaptation/life-and-career-design-qualcomm-exec-paul-jacobs). Strong fit for energy/data-center/telecom podcast; frequent conference speaker. Avoid the 2018 Qualcomm board exit.

name: Enrique Selva Bellvis
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Turbo Energy S.A. (Nasdaq: TURB); Chairman & CEO, Umbrella Global Energy S.A. (formerly Umbrella Solar Investment, BME Growth)
profile: Valencia-based solar entrepreneur who built IM2 Energía Solar (founded ~2003) into the Umbrella group of PV development, O&M and equipment businesses. Its subsidiary Turbo Energy, maker of the SunBox all-in-one solar-plus-storage system and AI-driven energy management, listed on Nasdaq in 2023; he moved from CEO to chairman at end-2023 and Turbo now focuses on C&I battery storage in Europe.
interesting_fact: Turbo Energy pitches itself as AI applied to renewables: its software optimises battery storage for industrial sites, and in 2026 it brought 62.5 MWh of intelligent storage online across three industrial sites.
deep_cut_fact: His first venture, Valencia's IM2 Energía Solar, had installed some 152,000 solar panels generating ~79 million kWh a year by 2018, when he regrouped its businesses (incl. Solar Rocket, Thunder Energy and Turbo Energy) into the Umbrella Capital holding.
notes: Small-cap (net worth figure derives from SEC insider holdings). Speaks Spanish; quoted regularly in Valencian business press (Valencia Plaza). Turbo's CEO is Mariano Soria; communications contacts have changed through 2026, so IR inbox is the stable route.

name: Seth Dallaire
current_role: EVP & Chief Growth Officer, Walmart Inc. (also a director of Shift4 Payments)
profile: Ad-tech and retail-media executive who runs Walmart's global enterprise platforms: Walmart Connect advertising, Walmart+, Walmart Data Ventures, VIZIO, Sam's Club MAP and Marketplace. Previously Walmart U.S. chief revenue officer (2021-24), Instacart CRO, and eight years leading Amazon's global ad sales; earlier at Yahoo and Microsoft. Wealth is from executive equity.
interesting_fact: At Instacart he built the advertising business from the ground up, partnering with more than 2,500 brands, before Walmart hired him to scale its retail-media arm.
deep_cut_fact: A liberal-arts product rather than a typical tech exec: he holds a BA from Vassar College, plus an MBA from NYU.
notes: Data/advertising angle (Walmart Data Ventures, VIZIO) is the strongest hook. Route via Walmart media relations or LinkedIn.

name: Earl H Nemser
current_role: Vice Chairman and Director, Interactive Brokers Group (IBKR)
profile: Earl H. Nemser is a securities and commodities lawyer (NYU economics; J.D. magna cum laude, Boston University) who has been a director or officer of Thomas Peterffy's IBKR companies since 1988 and Vice Chairman since 2006. He was a partner at Cadwalader and at Swidler Berlin, then special counsel at Dechert (2005–18), where he is now an independent advisor. His wealth comes from his long-held IBKR stake.
interesting_fact: He has been involved with Interactive Brokers' predecessor companies since 1988, nearly from the start of Peterffy's electronic-trading empire, and became Vice Chairman when the group prepared its 2007 IPO.
deep_cut_fact: He knew Thomas Peterffy before Interactive Brokers existed: in the 1970s he was outside counsel to Mocatta Metals, where Peterffy worked, and Institutional Investor quotes his recollections of that era. Institutional Investor calls him one of Peterffy's few close friends.
notes: Low-profile lawyer-director who rarely gives interviews. Best route is IBKR media relations (recent releases also list media@ibkr.com). His age is reported as late 70s.

name: Mark Newcomer
current_role: President, CEO & Co-founder, Paysign, Inc. (NASDAQ: PAYS), Henderson, Nevada
profile: Mark Newcomer co-founded Paysign (formerly 3PEA) in 2001 and has run it since, taking it from an early prepaid-card issuer processor to a NASDAQ-listed (2018) payments and software platform. It leads U.S. plasma-donor compensation cards and pharma co-pay programs, and in 2025 expanded into SaaS for the blood/plasma industry (Apherion).
interesting_fact: Under Newcomer, Paysign built a market-leading position paying U.S. plasma donors via prepaid cards, then bought software that became the Apherion donor-management ecosystem for blood and plasma centers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied bioscience at Cal Poly San Luis Obispo, a background he credits for his interest in platforms for complex, regulated healthcare markets.
notes: Stepped down as chairman in 2025 (Dan Henry became chair), remains CEO. Fintech/healthcare angle rather than energy. Press releases also list ir@paysign.com.

name: Philip R Gallagher
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Avnet Inc. (since Nov 2020); director, Dycom Industries
profile: Phil Gallagher is a Drexel graduate from South Jersey who joined Hamilton Avnet in 1982 and has spent almost his whole career at the Phoenix-based electronic components distributor, running Electronics Marketing Americas and Technology Solutions before a stint at TTI. He returned in 2017 to run Electronic Components and became CEO in 2020; his wealth is mainly Avnet equity.
interesting_fact: He joined Avnet in 1982 in a 100%-commission sales job with no electronics background after a lunch with an Avnet employee: 'I didn't know anything about electronics ... and I'm still learning after 40 years.'
deep_cut_fact: As a teen he pumped gas at a Hess station, and his first resume described the job as 'petroleum transferring agent'; he was also a college nose guard whom a coach once said was too small to make varsity.
notes: Press contact Liam Creighton is named in Avnet's 2026 press releases. Avnet is moving its HQ from Phoenix to Tempe in 2026. Relevant to the podcast via electronics/semiconductor supply chain for data centres.

name: Jeff Horing
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Insight Partners; Chair of monday.com board; director of nCino
profile: Jeff Horing co-founded Insight Partners (originally Insight Venture Partners) with Jerry Murdock in 1995 after stints at Warburg Pincus and Goldman Sachs; it became one of the largest software-focused growth/VC firms. He leads its investment team and sits on boards including monday.com (chair) and nCino.
interesting_fact: In Insight's early days, Horing and Murdock sourced every deal themselves by scanning software trade publications for companies that were hiring; he says 'Sourcing is everything' and calls analysts the 'lifeblood of Insight'.
deep_cut_fact: He has said Insight's bottom-up, data-driven sourcing model was inspired by Summit Partners and TA Associates; he likens investing to baseball - an investor's edge comes only from the pitches they actually see.
notes: Described by Fortune as low-profile. Route via Insight Partners press/communications team (insightpartners.com). He was a guest on Invest Like the Best EP.440 (https://podwise.ai/episodes/5210842) - useful prep.

name: Thomas E. Long
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Energy Transfer LP (set to become sole CEO when Mackie McCrea retires by end-2026); chairman, USA Compression Partners; director, Texas Capital Bancshares
profile: Dallas-based midstream finance executive. CFO of Regency Energy Partners (2010-15), joined Energy Transfer when it bought Regency, was ET's CFO 2016-2020 (overseeing the 2018 ETE/ETP merger), and co-CEO since Jan 2021. In June 2026 ET said he will become sole CEO on McCrea's retirement. Wealth reflects his ET equity per SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Long sits on the board of the new Texas Stock Exchange (since July 2024), and in Sept 2026 Energy Transfer announced it would move its listing from the NYSE to TXSE — the exchange's first primary listing transferred from the NYSE.
deep_cut_fact: Before Energy Transfer he spent 1998-2005 in executive roles at Duke Energy subsidiaries, then was CFO of DCP Midstream Partners and of Matrix Service Co.; he also serves on the Dallas Fed's Energy Advisory Council.
notes: Energy Transfer press releases list Media Relations (Vicki Granado) and Investor Relations contacts with phone numbers only, no email. Speaks at industry events (Hart Energy Super DUG). Strong energy/data-center-gas fit.

name: Kathy J Warden
current_role: Chair, CEO and President, Northrop Grumman; Director, Merck & Co.
profile: Kathy Warden has led Northrop Grumman as CEO since January 2019 and chair since July 2019, steering the defense giant behind the B-21 Raider and Sentinel ICBM programs. She began at General Electric, held executive roles at Veridian and General Dynamics, joined Northrop in 2008 and rose to president and COO before the top job.
interesting_fact: In 2022 Russia put her on its sanctions list; she told David Rubenstein the sanctions 'don't really accomplish anything, but - it's part of the job.'
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in Smithsburg, Maryland (near Hagerstown, pop. ~3,000) and joked 'I don't think we knew how to spell aerospace and defense in Smithsburg'; with no one to guide her, she researched colleges herself pre-internet and chose James Madison University for its teaching focus.
notes: Very high-profile Fortune 100 CEO; active on public speaking circuit (Economic Club, Brookings, KPMG). Best route is Northrop corporate communications. Energy/data-center angle: space and defense electronics.

name: Kevin J Jacobs
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, Hilton Worldwide; Director, Omega Healthcare Investors
profile: Kevin Jacobs (Cornell Hotel School '94) joined Hilton in 2008 as SVP corporate strategy, became treasurer, chief of staff and, in 2013, CFO, steering finances through Hilton's 2013 IPO era and asset-light shift. From 2020 to 2025 he also ran global development. Earlier he was at Fairmont Raffles, Host Hotels, PwC and Cushman & Wakefield; his wealth comes from Hilton equity compensation.
interesting_fact: He has spent essentially his whole career in hotel finance, from hospitality valuation at Cushman & Wakefield to running development for one of the world's largest hotel pipelines as Hilton's President, Global Development (2020-2025). He is a past chair of the American Hotel & Lodging Association.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the board of Goodwill of Greater Washington and is a trustee and executive committee member of the Federal City Council in Washington, D.C.
notes: Corporate executive (not a founder); wealth from Hilton stock. Regular presence on earnings calls and investor conferences; data-center/energy angle is weak, but hotel development/real-estate finance is a fit. Route via Hilton corporate communications.

name: Jamie Iannone
current_role: President & CEO, eBay Inc. (since April 2020)
profile: Princeton BS/Stanford MBA; started at Booz Allen and Epinions, led search and buyer experience at eBay (2001-09), ran NOOK at Barnes & Noble, then was CEO of SamsClub.com and COO of Walmart eCommerce. CEO of eBay since April 2020; in 2026 he closed the Depop deal and the board rejected GameStop's unsolicited bid.
interesting_fact: At Walmart eCommerce he was responsible for Store No. 8, Walmart's in-house incubation hub. At Barnes & Noble he ran everything NOOK, from devices and software to digital content.
deep_cut_fact: His favourite eBay experience was selling a Hammond B-3 organ he had owned since he was a teenager to a church. When it arrived, the pastor sent a video of the organist playing it, and Iannone joked it never sounded that good when he played it.
notes: Press releases name Sybille St. Arromand as media relations and John Egbert as IR. He is a high-profile CEO, so go through eBay media relations. Good podcast angles: recommerce, AI in marketplaces, small business.

name: Paul J. Schneider
current_role: President, Schneider Resources (Green Bay family investment/operating company); director nominee/director, Schneider National (2026)
profile: Paul J. Schneider, 52, is a grandson of Schneider National founder Al Schneider and son of longtime CEO Don Schneider; he is one of five family members whose interests make up the voting trust controlling the trucking giant. He runs Schneider Resources, whose portfolio makes precision parts for aerospace and energy, and rejoined Schneider National's board in 2026 after serving 2020-22.
interesting_fact: He co-founded SLK Finance, a business-lending group, in 2011, and Schneider Resources' portfolio companies (e.g. JR Machine, Lindquist Machine) focus on precision parts for the aerospace and energy sectors - a direct energy-industry hook.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an M&A analyst at Morgan Stanley, held truckload, logistics and engineering roles at Schneider National, and holds a Northwestern economics BA, a Kellogg MBA and a master's in information systems from UW-Oshkosh; he sits on Northwestern University's board.

public_contacts.value: BoardofDirectors@schneider.com (Schneider National board; forwarded by Corporate Secretary)

notes: Private family figure; best routes are via Schneider Resources (Green Bay) or the Schneider National board mailbox. Energy/aerospace manufacturing portfolio is the natural podcast angle.

name: Robert L. Goldstein
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, BlackRock, Inc.; oversees Aladdin and the firm's operating and technology platforms
profile: Rob Goldstein joined BlackRock in 1994 at age 20, straight out of Binghamton University (BS economics), and has spent his whole career there. He helped build BlackRock Solutions and the Aladdin risk and portfolio platform, ran the institutional client business from 2012, and became COO in 2014. He sits on the Global Executive Committee and leads the firm's technology and AI agenda.
interesting_fact: When he joined, BlackRock had about 55 employees. It now manages more than $10 trillion. In 2024 he said generative AI would be 'the most significant technology, innovation, evolution, revolution' of his 30-year career.
deep_cut_fact: He started in BlackRock's Portfolio Analytics Group and was part of the BlackRock Solutions technology unit from its early days. He worked under Charles Hallac, Aladdin's architect, and Institutional Investor repeatedly named him to its Tech 50 list (2013-2017).
notes: BlackRock media relations contact is Patrick Scanlan (212-810-3622), per the Q2 2026 earnings release (https://s24.q4cdn.com/856567660/files/doc_financials/2026/Q2/BLK-2Q26-Earnings-Release.pdf). Strong data-center angle: BlackRock's GIP/AIP AI infrastructure partnership, plus Aladdin and AI. Go through BlackRock corporate communications.

name: Mark Ein
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Venturehouse Group and Capitol Investment Corp; Chairman, Kastle Systems; owner, Washington Kastles & Washington City Paper; Chairman, DC Open
profile: Mark Ein (b. 1964, Chevy Chase MD; Wharton '87, HBS '92) worked at Goldman Sachs, Brentwood Associates and Carlyle before founding Venturehouse Group in 1999. He sponsors the Capitol-series SPACs, which produced public companies such as Custom Truck One Source, Lindblad and Two Harbors, and he chairs Kastle Systems. He is a Washington sports figure: Kastles founder, DC Open chair and a Commanders limited partner.
interesting_fact: He chaired President Biden's President's Export Council from 2023 and was part of Josh Harris's group that bought the Washington Commanders for $6.05bn. He and Harris have been friends since elementary school.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong tennis player, he played seven or eight pro doubles tournaments in his forties. The Daily Pennsylvanian called him the oldest person ever to receive an ATP doubles ranking. He traces his sports-owner ambitions to hearing 76ers owner Ed Snider speak at Wharton in 1982.
notes: Highly accessible and media-friendly. He owns a newspaper, speaks often at DC business and sports events, and is a WEF contributor. Kastle Systems (building security/access data) is a natural angle for an energy/data-centre podcast. I could not verify a personal X/LinkedIn handle.

name: Guilherme Marques Lago
current_role: Partner, Kaszek (venture capital); Special Advisor to Nubank (CFO 2021-July 2026)
profile: Brazilian finance executive who spent about 13 years at Credit Suisse (rising to managing director), with earlier stints at McKinsey and Advent, then joined Nubank in June 2019 and became CFO in Feb 2021, steering its 2021 NYSE IPO and growth in Mexico and Colombia. name: Eric H. L. So
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Helus Pharma Inc. (formerly Cybin Inc.; Nasdaq/Cboe CA: HELP). In Oct 2026 he moved from executive chair/interim CEO to a board-only seat.
profile: Eric So co-founded Cybin in 2019 with Paul Glavine. Cybin develops psychedelic-derived serotonin-pathway drugs for depression and anxiety and rebranded as Helus Pharma in 2026. He was executive chairman and president, and returned as interim CEO in April 2026. In October 2026 he stepped back to the board as Mark Lawson became independent chair, ahead of Phase 3 data for HLP003.
interesting_fact: Helus's lead program, HLP003, holds FDA Breakthrough Therapy Designation, and pivotal Phase 3 data is expected in Q4 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer (LLB), not a scientist. Before Cybin he was VP Strategy and General Counsel at Synergex Corp (2006-2010), and he co-founded the boutique merchant bank Trinity Venture Partners.
notes: Cybin's legal name became Helus Pharma Inc. on 1 Oct 2026. His step-back to the board comes from a secondary news site (Panabee, 27 Oct 2026); confirm on ir.helus.com, which blocked automated fetch. The deep-cut career details come from MarketScreener, an aggregator. Some company bios called him a chemist, which conflicts with his LLB.

name: William John Sibold
current_role: President and CEO, Madrigal Pharmaceuticals (since Sept 2023)
profile: Bill Sibold spent ~12 years at Sanofi, ending as EVP Specialty Care and President of Sanofi North America, after roles at Biogen and Avanir. He joined Madrigal in 2023 and led the launch of Rezdiffra (resmetirom), the first FDA-approved drug for MASH/NASH liver disease, approved in March 2024.
interesting_fact: At Sanofi he is credited with bringing Dupixent to market and building specialty care into Sanofi's largest global business unit; he called Dupixent 'a once-in-a-career type of product' in a 2020 interview.
deep_cut_fact: Marking the 30th anniversary of Sanofi's Rare Humanitarian Program in 2021, he highlighted that '95 percent of known rare diseases still lack an approved treatment.'
notes: Madrigal is based in West Conshohocken, PA. Media contact named in releases: Christopher Frates.

name: Jonathan A. Brudnick
current_role: Partner, Sachem Head Capital Management; Director, Six Flags Entertainment Corp. (since Oct 2025)
profile: Jonathan Brudnick is a partner at activist hedge fund Sachem Head (since 2017), after earlier roles at private equity and public-market investment firms. He joined the Six Flags board in October 2025 under a cooperation agreement after Sachem Head built a stake of nearly 10% in the theme-park operator formed from the 2024 Cedar Fair-Six Flags merger.
interesting_fact: On joining the board he said Sachem Head invested because 'numerous pathways exist to addressing the Company's current undervaluation', aiming for Six Flags to build on its legacy as 'the premier amusement park company in North America'.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BBA in finance from Emory University and an MBA from Wharton, and sits on Six Flags' Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee as a Class III director through 2027.

name: Luis A Gonzalez
current_role: Director and 10%+ shareholder, Mission Produce, Inc. (NASDAQ: AVO)
profile: Peruvian agribusiness entrepreneur who founded Camposol (Peru's leading agro-industrial company and once the world's largest asparagus exporter) and Austral Group, Peru's second-largest fishing/marine food producer. He co-founded avocado grower Grupo Arato in 2011, which Mission Produce acquired in 2018; he has sat on Mission's board since around 2011.

deep_cut_fact: Before avocados, he built businesses in two very different Peruvian sectors - asparagus (Camposol became the world's largest asparagus exporter) and fishing/marine foods (Austral Group).
