name: David E Flitman
current_role: Chair of the Board and CEO, US Foods Holding Corp.; director, Avery Dennison
profile: Dave Flitman has been CEO of US Foods since January 2023 and added the board chair role in May 2026. A Purdue chemical engineer, he spent ~20 years at DuPont, then ran Allegheny Power, held senior roles at Nalco and Univar, and was CEO of Performance Foodservice, BMC Stock Holdings and Builders FirstSource.
interesting_fact: He has run businesses in four different industries: chemicals (DuPont, Nalco, Univar), electric utilities (Allegheny Power), building products (BMC, Builders FirstSource) and foodservice distribution (Performance Foodservice, US Foods).
deep_cut_fact: Energy credentials: from February 2005 to July 2008 he was President of Allegheny Power, the electric utility, after nearly 20 years at DuPont where he started his career.
notes: Utility background (Allegheny Power) is a natural hook for an energy podcast. Route via US Foods media relations.

name: Rami Rahim
current_role: EVP, President & GM, HPE Networking (Hewlett Packard Enterprise); director, Autodesk
profile: Canadian engineer who rose from early engineer to CEO of Juniper Networks (2014-2025). After HPE's ~$14B acquisition of Juniper closed in 2025, he became head of HPE Networking. He now leads HPE's push into AI data-center and 'self-driving' networking, including the Juniper-Aruba integration.
interesting_fact: He argues networking is a 'force multiplier' for AI compute: in a typical data center it is only about 10-15% of total spend but determines how well the GPUs are used. Oracle agreed in 2026 to deploy HPE Juniper routing and switching across its data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Juniper in early 1997 as employee No. 32 and worked as an engineer on its first breakthrough product, the M40 core router. He holds 17 U.S. networking patents and has EE degrees from the University of Toronto (BS) and Stanford (MS).

public_contacts.value: ben.stricker@hpe.com (HPE networking media contact on releases)

notes: Excellent fit for a data-center podcast because he is a frequent speaker on AI networking (MWC, HPE Discover, Six Five Media). The best route is HPE corporate communications for networking. HPE media contacts change from release to release; others listed include victor.obrien@hpe.com (Oracle deal release, Sept 2026).

name: Curtis Drew Hodgson
current_role: Co-founder and ~17.5% shareholder, Legacy Housing Corp (NASDAQ: LEGH); retired as Executive Chairman in July 2026
profile: Texas manufactured-housing entrepreneur who co-founded Legacy Housing with Kenny Shipley in 2005 after decades owning manufactured-home retail lots and communities in Texas. He was co-CEO (2018-19) around the 2018 Nasdaq IPO, then chairman/executive chairman, and retired from the company in July 2026 while remaining its largest individual holder.
interesting_fact: An engineer-lawyer: he holds a B.S. in Engineering from the University of Michigan and a J.D. from the University of Texas, and took only a nominal $50,000 salary as executive chairman.
deep_cut_fact: Legacy's own site credits Hodgson and Shipley with innovating in floor-plan design and financing, and quotes him: 'If I were going to buy a mobile home for someone in my family, I would buy a Legacy manufactured home.'
notes: Retired from Legacy in July 2026 (per 2026 proxy), so company contacts may only forward. Contacts come from a syndicated copy of Legacy's Q1 2026 press release. Affordable-housing/factory-built homes angle; low public profile.

name: David Moreno
current_role: President, FTAI Aviation Ltd. (NASDAQ: FTAI), since Feb 2026
profile: Babson-trained finance executive who spent 2013-2021 on Fortress Investment Group's aviation investment team, then served as FTAI Aviation's COO (2021-2026) leading growth initiatives, acquisitions and partnerships. Named to the newly created President role in Feb 2026, running day-to-day performance as FTAI evolved from aircraft leasing into the leading CFM56/V2500 engine-maintenance platform.
interesting_fact: FTAI launched 'FTAI Power' in Dec 2025, converting CFM56 jet engines (the world's largest aircraft-engine fleet) into ~25 MW aeroderivative gas turbines for AI data centers, targeting 100+ units a year.
deep_cut_fact: CEO Joe Adams credited him as part of the team 'since FTAI's inception' and as key to transforming the company from a leasing platform into an engine-maintenance business; he holds both a B.A. in Business Administration and an M.S. in Accounting from Babson College.
notes: Excellent topical fit: FTAI Power (jet engines repurposed for data-center power). IR head is Alan Andreini per company press releases; route via FTAI IR (ir.ftaiaviation.com). Young executive (~mid-30s), low personal media profile.

name: Paul Glavine
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Helus Pharma Inc. (formerly Cybin Inc.; Nasdaq/Cboe CA: HELP)
profile: Paul Glavine co-founded Cybin, a Toronto-based clinical-stage company developing psychedelic-derived treatments for mental health, now renamed Helus Pharma. He was its COO, became Chief Growth Officer in 2021 and now sits on the board. The company says he has raised over US$600M and led deals that advanced its anxiety candidate (HLP004) into human trials.
interesting_fact: The company's lead program, HLP003 (a psilocybin analog for depression), received Breakthrough Therapy Designation from the US FDA under his co-founding leadership.
deep_cut_fact: He is a Milken Institute Young Leader and was named one of Canada's Top 40 under 40 in Life Sciences by Catalytic Health.
notes: Cybin rebranded as Helus Pharma. Use irteam@helus.com, which the company lists for 'Investor & Media Inquiries'. MarketScreener also lists him as a director of Adelia Therapeutics and founder of Truverra (unverified).

name: Jeffrey C Kunins
current_role: Chief Product Officer & Chief Technology Officer, Axon Enterprise (NASDAQ: AXON)
profile: Product/engineering executive who joined Axon (TASER, body cameras, evidence.com cloud) in September 2019 and now leads its global product, software and hardware engineering, AI, design and security teams. Previously VP of Kindle and head of Alexa Entertainment at Amazon, GM at Skype and Windows Live Messenger at Microsoft; CMU graduate.
interesting_fact: At Amazon he ran Alexa Entertainment, striking the partnerships that put Apple Music, Spotify, SiriusXM/Pandora, Netflix and YouTube on Alexa devices, after leading Kindle.
deep_cut_fact: He spent eight years at voice-recognition pioneer Tellme Networks (acquired by Microsoft in 2007) - an early bet on voice computing long before Alexa.
notes: Executive (SEC insider), not a founder. Good angle: AI in public safety (Draft One AI report writing). Route via Axon press office.

name: Arnaud Ajdler
current_role: Founder, Managing Partner & Portfolio Manager, Engine Capital (activist investment firm, New York); director, UniFirst
profile: Belgian-born activist investor who was a partner at Crescendo Partners before founding Engine Capital in 2013. Engine runs about $1.2-1.7bn and has pushed for change at companies such as Lyft, UniFirst and Avantor. Through Engine he has been a 10% holder of Civeo, which runs workforce accommodation for energy and mining sites, and of Orthofix.
interesting_fact: He trained as an aerospace engineer before becoming an activist investor: B.S. in mechanical engineering from the Free University of Brussels and an S.M. in aeronautics from MIT, then a Harvard MBA.
deep_cut_fact: While at Crescendo Partners he taught as an Adjunct Associate Professor of Business at Columbia Business School.
notes: Engine Capital's contact page lists the general-inquiries email (mdiagonale@) and the investor-inquiries email (apessolano@). Energy angle: Civeo stake (oil-sands and mining workforce lodging).

name: Fang Jin
current_role: Founder and Chairman/General Manager, Fujian Scud Co. (飞毛腿, Fuzhou) - per company-profile sources (undated)
profile: Fujian entrepreneur who founded Scud (飞毛腿) in Fuzhou's Mawei district in 1997, building one of China's best-known mobile-phone battery and power-bank brands and listing Scud Group in Hong Kong in late 2006. The group later spun its power-battery business into a separate unit (2016) and expanded into energy storage.
interesting_fact: Scud ('飞毛腿', literally 'fleet-footed') grew from phone batteries into a group of 10+ companies making mobile batteries, power banks and EV/storage power batteries, and appeared on Hurun's China Rich List in 2007 after its 2006 Hong Kong IPO.
deep_cut_fact: In 2010 Scud set up its own vocational school, the Fujian Scud Senior Technical School (福建省飞毛腿高级技工学校), which has since graduated nearly 10,000 skilled workers.
notes: Only appeared on Hurun in 2007; very little recent coverage, and no official company contact page could be verified (scudbattery.com is a parked domain). Alive status not confirmed by a dated source. Low-priority lead.

name: Tao Guoping
current_role: Founder and former controlling shareholder of Jiangsu Jiangnan High Polymer Fiber (Shanghai 600527); transferred control in 2023 (no current executive role found)
profile: Tao Guoping (陶国平) founded Jiangsu Jiangnan High Polymer Fiber in Suzhou's Xiangcheng district, listed in Shanghai in 2003, and remained controlling shareholder (22.57%) until July 2023, when he passed control to the next generation of the family. The company says it is China's largest maker of bicomponent (ES) staple fibre and polyester tops.
interesting_fact: Jiangnan High Polymer Fiber's ES bicomponent staple fibres (230,000 t/yr capacity) are a main raw material for nonwovens used in disposable hygiene products such as diapers, and its polyester tops are blended with wool for worsted fabrics.
notes: Hurun-listed only in 2007. Polyester fibres, not data centers/AI, so a weak fit for the podcast's focus. He stepped back in 2023 (control-transfer notice: https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2023-07/22/content_1798337.htm). 'Alive' is based on that 2023 transaction. Route via the IR mailbox.

name: Jagdeep Singh
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO/Chairman of QuantumScape; retired from the board at the end of 2024. I could not verify a current role.
profile: Jagdeep Singh is a serial deep-tech founder. He founded and ran optical-networking company Infinera as CEO from 2001 to 2009, then co-founded solid-state battery maker QuantumScape in 2010 with Tim Holme and Stanford professor Fritz Prinz. He was CEO until February 2024, when Siva Sivaram took over after a year-long succession plan, and he left the chairmanship and board at the end of 2024.
interesting_fact: He planned his own exit: QuantumScape's 8-K says Siva Sivaram's appointment as CEO in Feb 2024 was the culmination of a year-long succession plan that Singh started as chairman and outgoing CEO. Before that he had led the company since founding it in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He has three degrees from three schools: a B.S. in computer science from the University of Maryland, an M.S. in computer science from Stanford, and an MBA from UC Berkeley Haas. He also sat on the boards of the SPACs Khosla Ventures Acquisition Co. and Slam Corp. in 2021-22.
notes: A strong fit for the energy theme (batteries). He started the QuantumScape CEO succession himself, so it was not an ouster. The SEC net-worth figure dates from 2024, before his equity awards terminated when he retired. I found no personal site or published contact; LinkedIn is the likely route but I did not verify it.

name: Michael J. Farrell
current_role: Chairman & CEO, ResMed Inc. (NYSE: RMD), San Diego; 2026 Chair of AdvaMed
profile: Australian-American engineer ('Mick') who joined ResMed in 2000, ran its Americas and global sleep-apnea businesses, became CEO in 2013 and board chair in 2023. He has steered ResMed into cloud-connected CPAP devices and digital health. The company's 2030 strategy, unveiled in 2024, aims to help 500 million people. He also sits on the Zimmer Biomet board.
interesting_fact: Under Farrell, ResMed turned its CPAP machines into one of medtech's largest IoT fleets, with millions of cloud-connected devices sending nightly therapy data. It is central to the company's 2030 strategy.
deep_cut_fact: Before medtech he worked as a process engineer at BHP's steelmaking operations and in chemicals at Dow, then in biotech at Genzyme and consulting at Arthur D. Little. He holds a UNSW engineering degree and an MIT chemical-engineering master's plus MBA (MIT LGO '98).
notes: Media contact is Brad Lotterman (news@resmed.com). He speaks often at conferences and on LinkedIn about digital health and AI. The interesting fact is a summary of ResMed's connected-device strategy; check exact device counts in the latest 10-K before quoting.

name: Rehan Jaffer
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, H Partners Management LLC (New York investment firm). Director, Six Flags Entertainment Corp since May 2026.

He joined the Six Flags board after the 2026 annual meeting under a cooperation agreement with the company, replacing H Partners' previous representative Arik Ruchim, and sits on its Audit and Finance Committee.

name: J Scott Kirby
current_role: CEO, United Airlines Holdings; director, CVS Health
profile: Scott Kirby is CEO of United Airlines (since May 2020), after serving as United's president from 2016 and earlier as president of US Airways and American Airlines. He also chairs the Star Alliance chief executive board.

notes: High-profile, heavily handled by United corporate communications; route via United media relations newsroom.

profile: Operations executive who joined Bloom Energy in 2019 as SVP of global supply chain and became COO (around end-2023/April 2024), overseeing supply chain, manufacturing, installations and facilities as Bloom scales solid-oxide fuel-cell production to power AI data centers onsite. notes: Low public profile operator rather than founder; great for a 'how do you build fuel cells fast enough for AI' segment. Route via Bloom media relations (Katja Gagen, press@bloomenergy.com). Interesting_fact customer names from general Bloom news, not his bio page.

name: David D Dallas

profile: New Jersey industrialist and banker (age 71) who has been on Unity Bancorp's board since 1991 and is its Chairman and a 10%+ holder alongside his brother Robert H. Dallas II. deep_cut_fact: He and his brother Robert have both sat on Unity's board since 1991, more than three decades of continuous oversight of the community bank, which they combine with running a global specialty-chemicals business.

name: Clinton Bybee
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Director (listed by some sources as Emeritus), ARCH Venture Partners
profile: Clint Bybee co-founded ARCH Venture Partners, the early-stage firm spun out of the University of Chicago/Argonne tech-transfer effort, and has invested in advanced materials, semiconductors, photonics and infrastructure tech. name: Christopher Swift
current_role: Chairman & CEO, The Hartford (HIG); becomes Executive Chair on 1 Mar 2027, when Mo Tooker takes over as CEO
profile: CPA who began at KPMG, where he rose to head its Global Insurance Industry Practice, then held senior finance roles at AIG. He joined The Hartford as CFO in 2010, became CEO in 2014 and Chairman in 2015. He refocused it on P&C and group benefits, selling the Japanese annuity business and buying Aetna's group life/disability unit and Navigators. Succession to Mo Tooker was announced in Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: During his tenure The Hartford returned about $22bn to shareholders (2010-June 2026) and nearly doubled P&C written premium to $18bn in 2025. In 2017 it also helped pledge $50m to the City of Hartford.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 interview he summed up the business: 'An insurance company sells a promise.' He has also championed The Hartford's Junior Fire Marshal programme, created in 1947, whose red helmets have reached over 110 million children.
notes: Marquette University accounting graduate and trustee (2017-). He is in transition: Executive Chair from March 2027 and plans to leave in H2 2027, so he may have more time for a podcast in 2027.

name: Arnon Dinur
current_role: Partner, 83North (Israeli/European VC, formerly Greylock Israel); director, Via Transportation (NYSE: VIA)
profile: Israeli venture investor, partner at 83North, which led Via's US$110m round at a US$3.5bn valuation in 2023. He sits on Via's board, and his holding became public wealth after Via's IPO. Exits he was involved in include Wolt (DoorDash), Marqeta, SuperPlay (Playtika) and BlueVine. Current boards include Holidu, Podimo, Lendbuzz and Mixtiles.
interesting_fact: Before venture capital he worked at M-Systems, the Israeli company that invented the USB flash drive, and stayed on at SanDisk after its US$1.6bn acquisition of M-Systems.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs Lobby99, a crowd-funded Israeli non-profit that lobbies the Knesset on behalf of the public interest rather than corporate clients.
notes: 83North publishes his work email (assistant: stacey@83north.com on the same page). VCs tend to welcome podcast invitations. Education details (law background, MBA from Texas McCombs) appear only on aggregator sites and are unverified.

name: Chris Diorio, Ph.D.
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Vice Chair, Impinj, Inc. (PI), Seattle
profile: Caltech-trained electrical engineer (BA physics, Occidental) who co-founded Impinj in 2000 with his PhD adviser Carver Mead, commercialising their research. Impinj makes RAIN (UHF RFID) chips and readers that tag billions of retail and logistics items. CEO since 2014, he reported record endpoint IC revenue in Q3 2026 on its M800 chips; he remains an affiliate professor of CSE at the University of Washington.

deep_cut_fact: Before running Impinj he consulted for it (2000-04) and served as VP Engineering and CTO; he also chaired the RAIN Alliance industry group and sits on GS1's Innovation Board and the EPCglobal Board of Governors that set RFID standards.

ir@impinj.com (Andy Cobb, VP Corporate Finance & IR)

current_role: Chairman of the Board, Central Securities Corporation (NYSE American: CET)

name: John Kent Walker
current_role: President, Global Affairs and Chief Legal Officer, Google & Alphabet
profile: Kent Walker (Harvard BA 1983, Stanford JD) has been Google's top lawyer since 2006 and President of Global Affairs since 2021, overseeing legal, policy, government affairs and trust & safety. name: Anastasios Arima
current_role: Founder, Managing Director & CEO, IperionX (ASX: IPX / NASDAQ: IPX)
profile: Engineer and entrepreneur known as Taso. He founded Piedmont Lithium (NASDAQ: PLL), now merged into Elevra Lithium, and helped finance and list it on NASDAQ. He now runs IperionX, which makes low-carbon titanium metal from scrap using patented technologies at its Virginia plant and owns the Titan critical-minerals project in Tennessee. IperionX has U.S. Army and defense supply contracts.
interesting_fact: IperionX won its first U.S. Army titanium task order, which Arima called 'a decisive step toward reshoring the nation's titanium supply chain'. Its Virginia facility recycles titanium scrap into 100%-recyclable metal products.

current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Scorpio Tankers (Monaco); Vice Chairman, Cadeler A/S

He also co-founded Eneti (formerly Scorpio Bulkers), which pivoted into offshore-wind installation vessels and merged with Cadeler in December 2023.
interesting_fact: He steered Eneti from dry-bulk shipping into building offshore-wind turbine installation vessels. After its 2023 merger with Cadeler, the world's leading wind-installation vessel operator, he became Cadeler's Vice Chairman, a strong energy-transition angle.
deep_cut_fact: He studied international business at the European Business School, London. He is Vice President of the Monaco Chamber of Shipping and sits on Fordham University's London Advisory Council.
notes: Based in Monaco; brother Filippo Lauro is a Scorpio VP. Very good fit for the energy theme (oil-product shipping plus offshore wind via Cadeler). Route via Scorpio IR.

He took over Equifax after its 2017 breach, led a ~$3bn cloud rebuild and grew revenue from $3.4bn (2018) to about $6.1bn (2025).

deep_cut_fact: Outside Equifax he chairs the board of trustees of Dartmouth Health and is a trustee of the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Foundation; earlier he led GE's investor-relations function.
notes: Syracuse University BA, RPI MBA. Left the NCR Atleos board in May 2025 per Equifax bio. Route via Equifax media relations.

profile: Serial Atlanta healthcare entrepreneur who co-founded nuclear pharmacy business Central Pharmacy Services (1992-2001, sold to Cardinal Health) and then, in 2003-04, Guardian Pharmacy, which grew by partnering with local long-term-care pharmacies into a national network serving assisted-living and senior-care facilities. He then led the 2020 acquisition of Bayer Animal Health and the move to a new Indianapolis headquarters.

notes: Media-friendly CEO who does many interviews and podcasts (McKinsey, Semafor, ICE House, the University of Arkansas Be EPIC podcast) and talks often about food security and the human-animal bond. LinkedIn is the best direct route. His social accounts are linked from his official Elanco bio.

current_role: Chief Technology Officer, TOYO Co., Ltd / VSUN (Nasdaq: TOYO), a Japan-headquartered solar cell and module maker with factories in Vietnam
profile: Dr. Aihua Wang is a UNSW-trained photovoltaic scientist. With her husband Dr. Jianhua Zhao she co-founded China Sunergy / CEEG (Nanjing) PV-Tech in 2006, in which she held equity, and led its R&D as head of research and VP. She became CTO of VSUN/TOYO in 2024 and in 2026 presented on solar power in space to investors.
interesting_fact: In 2023 she, Jianhua Zhao, Martin Green and Andrew Blakers received the Queen Elizabeth Prize for Engineering for developing PERC solar cell technology, which now dominates global solar production.
deep_cut_fact: Working in Martin Green's UNSW lab, she and Zhao set several world records for silicon solar cell efficiency, including the 25.0% PERL cell. In 2013 she won the ACAA/IELTS Australia China Alumni Award for Research and Innovation.
notes: An excellent energy-podcast fit as a world-class PV scientist. The listed wealth source 'CEEG PV-Tech' refers to her early equity in China Sunergy (controlled by Lu Tingxiu's CEEG). Her husband Jianhua Zhao is VSUN group chief advisor. Best route is TOYO investor relations.

name: Cao Ruiying
current_role: Shareholder (7.18%) of Jinglong Industrial Group, Ningjin, Hebei; the original parent of JA Solar. No public executive title found
profile: Cao Ruiying (曹瑞英) owns 7.18% of Jinglong Group, alongside Jin Baofang (78.45%), Liu Binguo and Ren Bingyan. Jinglong began in 1996 as a county power-bureau silicon plant, became employee-owned in 2003 and co-founded JA Solar. After moving its PV assets into JA Solar, it now focuses on hotels, property and finance.
interesting_fact: Jinglong started in 1996 when the county power bureau chief Jin Baofang heard of a Hebei University of Technology process for making monocrystalline silicon by neutron-transmutation doping. The plant later became one of the world's largest monocrystalline-silicon producers and gave rise to JA Solar.
notes: Identity confirmed via Jinglong's registry shareholding (7.18%), reported by Beijing News (https://m.bjnews.com.cn/detail/160517055515260.html). No personal public profile, role or contact found, and she appears only on Hurun 2008. The Jin Baofang family fronts JA Solar and Jinglong; approach via Jinglong Group, in Chinese.

name: Chai Guosheng
current_role: Founder and long-time chairman of Guangdong Cnlight Co. (雪莱特光电, SZSE: 002076), Foshan; current role unclear
profile: Chai Guosheng (柴国生, b. 1953) is a lighting engineer who founded Nanhai Huaxing Optoelectronics in 1992. It became Guangdong Cnlight (雪莱特), a maker of energy-saving lamps and light sources that listed in Shenzhen in 2006 with him as controlling shareholder and chairman/president. Filings show his stake fell below 5% by 2023.
interesting_fact: At Cnlight's 2006 IPO he held 66.57% of the company. He was credited with 61 service inventions and a 2004 National Science and Technology Progress Award (second class).
deep_cut_fact: He studied electric light sources in Fudan University's optics department. From 1978 to 1992 he rose from technician to chief engineer at the Gejiu Light Bulb Factory in Yunnan, where in 1986 he co-developed an 'H-type single-ended rare-earth energy-saving fluorescent lamp'.
notes: Low profile and no English-language coverage. His holdings in Cnlight were reduced in 2019-2023 (see SZSE filings), so avoid wealth topics. The best approach is in Chinese via the Cnlight board secretary. His energy-efficient lighting background is relevant to the energy theme.

name: Feng Yajun
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2008 (US$100m) as founder/owner of 'Zhanda Group' (展大集团) in animal feed. No online source found for 封亚军 or a feed company called 展大集团, so neither identity nor current status could be confirmed.
notes: Unresolved; possibly a small private regional feed company. Check business registries (e.g. the national enterprise credit system) with the Chinese company name.

name: Hu Xiangen

notes: I could not identify him from English or Chinese (胡祥根 + 慈星) searches. Don't assume he is linked to Ningbo Cixing (300307), whose founder is a different person. This needs the original Chinese characters or a registry lookup.

current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chairman, Win Hanverky Holdings Ltd (永嘉集團, HKEX: 3322)

He has 45+ years in the apparel industry and remains chairman, holding his stake via Quinta Asia Ltd (70%).

name: Liu Huiqiang
current_role: Co-owner of Jinglong Group (BVI), a founding shareholder group of JA Solar (Ningjin, Hebei)
profile: Liu Huiqiang (柳辉强) is one of the ten Chinese individual co-owners of Jinglong Group, the Ningjin, Hebei silicon group led by Jin Baofang that founded JA Solar. He held 7.18% of Jinglong Group BVI, which kept a JA Solar stake through its 2007 Nasdaq IPO, 2018 take-private and 2019 Shenzhen relisting as JA Solar Technology (002459).
interesting_fact: JA Solar grew out of Jinglong's mono-silicon business in Ningjin county, Hebei; its predecessor, Jinglong Zhong'ao, was renamed JA Solar in December 2005 and went to Nasdaq barely 14 months later.
deep_cut_fact: JA Solar's SEC filings list 'Mr. Huiqiang Liu (7.18%)' among Jinglong Group BVI's owners, alongside Jicun Yan, Rongrui Liu and Ruiying Cao with equal 7.18% stakes.

name: Shen Dongyun
current_role: Founder/chairman (as of 2009) of Zhejiang Lantian Industrial Group (浙江蓝天实业集团), Keqiao, Shaoxing - if same person

profile: Xu Xinxi (徐新喜) is listed as deriving his wealth from Zhaoshan Xinxing Group, a Zhejiang building-materials/cement group that in 2005 began a 1.35bn-yuan cement plant in Liuyang, Hunan. name: Zhang Feiyue (张飞跃)
current_role: Unknown; formerly linked to FibreChem Technologies (SGX-listed Chinese microfibre leather / bi-component fibre maker)
profile: Listed on Hurun China 2007-2008 with wealth from FibreChem Technologies, a Fujian-based chemical-fibre and microfibre synthetic-leather maker listed in Singapore in 2004. name: Mehmet Öz
current_role: Administrator, Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS), US Dept. of Health and Human Services (since April 2025)
profile: Cardiothoracic surgeon and TV host ('The Dr. Oz Show') who co-founded digital-health company Sharecare with Jeff Arnold in 2010. After a 2022 US Senate run in Pennsylvania, he was confirmed 53-45 as CMS Administrator in April 2025, where he oversees Medicare/Medicaid and is pushing AI and anti-fraud efforts.
interesting_fact: Before TV fame he helped develop heart devices and procedures including the MitraClip and LVAD work, and held several heart-surgery patents.
deep_cut_fact: At Harvard he was a varsity water polo goalkeeper and played safety on the football team, winning the Captain's Athletic Award for leadership; he later earned an MD from Penn and an MBA from Wharton, and was student body president in med school.
notes: Sitting federal official: podcast requests must go through CMS Office of Communications (media inquiries form, media line 202-690-6145 per CMS press page). Ethics rules may limit discussion of Sharecare.

name: Caitlyn Jenner
current_role: Media personality, public speaker and political commentator; 1976 Olympic decathlon champion
profile: Won Olympic decathlon gold at Montreal 1976 with a world record and built a fortune from endorsements, motivational speaking, TV and reality TV (Keeping Up with the Kardashians, I Am Cait). She ran for California governor in the 2021 recall and is now a conservative commentator and speaker.
interesting_fact: While training for the 1976 Olympics she trained by day and sold insurance at night, earning about $9,000 a year, at a time when amateur athletes could not turn pro.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s she raced in the IMSA Camel GT series. Her first win was the 1986 12 Hours of Sebring GTO class, co-driving the 7-Eleven Roush Racing Ford Mustang with Scott Pruett (4th overall).

public_contacts.value: https://caitlynjenner.com/ (returned an error when checked Nov 2026)

notes: Celebrity athlete and media figure rather than an entrepreneur or energy figure, so a weak fit for the podcast. She is politically outspoken, so outreach should be handled carefully. No published management or press email found; booking normally goes through speaker agencies or talent representation.

name: Emilia Clarke
current_role: Actress and producer; star and executive producer of the 2026 series 'Ponies'; founder of the charity SameYou
profile: London-born, Oxfordshire-raised actress best known as Daenerys Targaryen in HBO's Game of Thrones (2011-19), with film roles in Solo: A Star Wars Story, Me Before You and Last Christmas. Her wealth comes from acting. She now increasingly produces as well as stars (Ponies, Next Life) and runs SameYou, which funds neurorehabilitation for young adults.
interesting_fact: She was appointed MBE in the 2024 New Year Honours for founding the charity SameYou, and was invested at Windsor Castle by the Prince of Wales in February 2024.
deep_cut_fact: She decided to act at age three after seeing the musical Show Boat (her father was a theatre sound engineer), and was turned down by RADA, LAMDA and Guildhall before graduating from Drama Centre London in 2009; her first credited TV role was a bit part in the BBC soap Doctors.
notes: Not an entrepreneur/energy figure (net worth from Wikidata, acting). Professional bookings go through her agency/publicist (not published publicly here); SameYou is the only published organisational contact found. Avoid leading with her aneurysm history.

name: Noel Edmonds
current_role: Broadcaster and entrepreneur; founder of Positivity Radio; based in New Zealand's South Island
profile: English broadcaster (b. 1948) who rose from Radio Luxembourg and the Radio 1 Breakfast Show to front Multi-Coloured Swap Shop, Noel's House Party (15M+ viewers, creator of Mr Blobby) and Channel 4's Deal or No Deal (2005-16). He built wealth via presenting fees and his Unique Group production/media businesses. Emigrated to New Zealand in 2019, where he launched the Positivity Radio network.
interesting_fact: He was one of the original presenters of BBC's Top Gear in the late 1970s, and later returned to road-test a Ford GT40 (he owned two) because 6ft 5in Jeremy Clarkson couldn't fit in the cockpit.
deep_cut_fact: A licensed helicopter pilot (an early aircraft was registered G-NOEL), he ferried stars to and from Wembley by helicopter during Live Aid in 1985 and flew Phil Collins to Heathrow so he could catch Concorde to play the Philadelphia concert the same day.
notes: Media personality rather than energy/tech founder. Avoid his Lloyds/HBOS dispute and health topics. Lives in New Zealand (Ngatimoti); recent ITV series 'Noel Edmonds' Kiwi Adventure' (2025). Official site lists no direct contact; go via agent/management.

name: George T. Haber
current_role: Serial semiconductor entrepreneur and investor; listed as Growth Partner at AnD Ventures (unverified aggregator listing)
profile: George T. Haber was born in Oradea, Romania, in 1954 and trained in electronics at the Technion. He worked at Daisy Systems, Sun and SGI, then founded CompCore Multimedia (sold to Zoran for about $80M), GigaPixel (sold to 3dfx for $180M in 2000), Mobilygen (sold in 2008) and CrestaTech, which made TV tuners. He has since invested through the Cresta Fund.
interesting_fact: He says CompCore's technology for playing films on PCs fed into DVD: 'I can say with my hand on my heart that the DVD was, in part, developed by us.'
deep_cut_fact: As an 11th-grader in Oradea he played in a rock band with future actor Adrian Pintea. When the band was short-handed one Friday, he brought a tape recorder and tapes and ran what is reputed to be the city's first disco, earning about 100 lei a night.
notes: His current role is unclear. TheOrg (unverified) lists him as Chairman and Chief AI Officer at TBRS, Chairman of Tailent and Growth Partner at AnD Ventures; MarketScreener lists him as CEO of Adimos Systems. Confirm before outreach. The LinkedIn link comes from his Romanian Wikipedia article. He has also advised Bitdefender and sat on the boards of Romanian tech companies Interakt and Avangate.

name: Bruce Campbell
current_role: Chief Revenue & Strategy Officer, Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD)
profile: Princeton- and Harvard Law-educated dealmaker who joined Discovery in 2007 from NBCUniversal and became its chief development, distribution and legal officer. He was lead negotiator on the WarnerMedia-Discovery merger and the Scripps, SBS Nordics and Eurosport deals, and now oversees WBD ad sales, distribution, licensing and strategy, including the 2026 sale agreement with Paramount Skydance.
interesting_fact: He announced the ~$110B Paramount Skydance deal for WBD to staff at a February 2026 town hall, after Netflix declined to match Paramount's offer.
deep_cut_fact: Before Discovery, as NBCUniversal's EVP of Business Development, he negotiated the online video joint venture with News Corp that became Hulu; he began his career at law firm O'Melveny & Myers.
notes: Common name (not the actor). WBD's sale to Paramount Skydance was expected to close in Q3 2026 - his role may change after closing; verify before outreach. Route via WBD corporate communications.

name: Campos Vicente Falconi
current_role: Chairman of the Board (independent), AXIA Energia S.A. (formerly Eletrobras); founding partner and board chairman, Falconi Consultores de Resultado
profile: Vicente Falconi Campos is a Brazilian engineer and management thinker who founded Falconi, one of Brazil's largest management consultancies, over 40 years ago. He spent 25 years on AmBev's board and also sat on Unibanco, Sadia, BRF, Cyrela and Qualicorp boards. He now chairs AXIA Energia (ex-Eletrobras), Latin America's largest power utility.
interesting_fact: Falconi introduced Japanese-style Total Quality Control to Brazilian industry in the 1980s-90s; his book 'TQC: Controle da Qualidade Total (no estilo japonês)' became a standard management text in Brazil.
deep_cut_fact: Before consulting he was an academic: he earned his Master's and PhD in engineering at the Colorado School of Mines and taught engineering for about three decades at UFMG in Belo Horizonte, which made him Professor Emeritus.
notes: Input name is inverted; he is known as Vicente Falconi. Board role confirmed on AXIA's IR governance page (https://ri.axia.com.br/en/?p=1043). Best route is the Falconi consultancy press page or AXIA IR. Individual AXIA IR staff emails are also listed on the IR page, but ri@ is the general inbox.

name: Gjorgi Popstefanov
current_role: Founder & CEO, PMG (Dallas/Fort Worth digital marketing agency); director, Soho House & Co (since Jan 2026)
profile: Known as George Popstefanov. The North Macedonia native founded digital ad agency PMG in 2010 at age 28 and grew it to 900+ employees and billions in media billings, adding acquisitions such as Camelot and RocketMill and an AI analytics product, Alli. In January 2026 his vehicle Momentum Solutions II put $100M into Soho House's take-private, and he joined its board.
interesting_fact: When Soho House went private in January 2026, his Momentum Solutions II funded $100M at $9/share, and he joined a reconstituted board alongside Ron Burkle, Richard Caring and Ashton Kutcher.
deep_cut_fact: He financed PMG's launch himself in 2010 at age 28. Under him the agency built its own AI-powered analytics tool, 'Alli', and moved into a 75,000-sq-ft headquarters.
notes: SEC filings use 'Gjorgi'; he goes by George. Best route is via PMG. A secondary source says he launched PMG with $960 after working at Fort Worth agency Range Online Media, but I couldn't verify that from a primary source.

name: Richard E Muncrief
current_role: Retired President & CEO of Devon Energy (to March 2025); Director, Williams Companies (since 2022) and OGE Energy (since Aug 2026)
profile: Rick Muncrief (Oklahoma State petroleum engineering, 1980) spent about 45 years in oil and gas, including at Continental Resources. He became CEO and chairman of WPX Energy in 2014, led its 2021 merger with Devon, and ran Devon as CEO until retiring in March 2025. He now sits on the boards of pipeline giant Williams and Oklahoma utility OGE Energy.
interesting_fact: In April 2026 he and former Noble Energy CEO Chuck Davidson received the Energy Workforce & Technology Council's Platinum Award, its highest honour, which is not given every year. He is also in Hart Energy's Hall of Fame (2023).
deep_cut_fact: Muncrief took his first oilfield job at 17. He grew up in the Texas and Oklahoma oil fields of the '60s and '70s listening to his father's and grandfather's stories, including his granddad's stint on a pulling unit in southern Oklahoma.

public_contacts.value: Williams board communications via the Corporate Secretary, The Williams Companies, Inc., One Williams Center, Tulsa, OK (details on the Investors page of williams.com)

notes: Retired from Devon, so outreach via Devon is no longer appropriate. Best published routes are the board-communication channels at Williams or OGE Energy. Age 68 per OGE's Jul 2026 8-K. Good podcast fit: he spans upstream gas, midstream pipelines and a utility facing data-center load growth in Oklahoma.

name: Pablo Manuel Vera Pinto
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Vista Energy S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE/BMV: VIST), since Aug 2017
profile: Argentine executive Pablo Vera Pinto (48) is a founding member of Vista Energy, the Vaca Muerta shale producer launched in 2017 by ex-YPF CEO Miguel Galuccio as a SPAC, and has been CFO since. Before that he ran business development at YPF (2012-2017), after restructuring work, McKinsey in Europe and Credit Suisse First Boston in New York.
interesting_fact: He has been involved with Vista since its incorporation on March 22, 2017 - the company was created as a Mexican-listed blank-check vehicle that bought Argentine oil assets and became one of Vaca Muerta's leading shale producers.
deep_cut_fact: At YPF he was Director of Transformation in 2012 and sat on the boards of fertilizer JV Profertil (with Agrium), power generator Central Dock Sud (with Enel) and gas distributor MetroGAS. He studied economics at Universidad Torcuato Di Tella and holds an INSEAD MBA.
notes: Listed name order 'Pinto Pablo Manuel Vera' is SEC-insider style; he goes by Pablo Vera Pinto. Regularly speaks on Vista earnings calls, so IR is a natural route. Wealth (~$98m) is from Vista insider holdings.

name: Marshall T Reynolds
current_role: Chairman, First Guaranty Bancshares (FGBI); Chairman, Champion Industries; Director, Energy Services of America (ESOA)
profile: Huntington, West Virginia businessman who built printing/office-products firm Champion Industries (Nasdaq IPO 1993) from Chapman Printing, bought in 1964; took control of First Huntington National Bank in the early 1980s and has chaired Louisiana's First Guaranty Bank since 1996. Also a director of utility contractor Energy Services of America.
interesting_fact: He remains an active buyer of his own bank's stock: he was chairman and proxy holder at First Guaranty's 2026 annual meeting and bought about $250k of FGBI shares in October 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Chapman Printing in Huntington as a 1950s clean-up boy, rose to delivery boy and top salesman, ran it when owner John Chapman fell ill, and in 1964 bought the company from his former boss; he attended Marshall University but never finished his degree.
notes: Born late 1930s; long-time Huntington power broker, featured repeatedly in Huntington Quarterly. Inducted into WVU Business Hall of Fame (business.wvu.edu). Energy angle: Energy Services of America (gas/water/electric utility contracting). Route via company IR/corporate secretary.

name: R. Lane Riggs
current_role: Chairman, CEO and President, Valero Energy Corporation (NYSE: VLO)
profile: Lane Riggs is a chemical engineer who has spent his whole career at Valero, joining in 1989 and rising through refining operations, crude supply and trading to President & COO. He became CEO in June 2023 and added chairman in Dec 2024, leading the largest independent US refiner, which also has major renewable diesel and ethanol businesses.
interesting_fact: A rare lifer CEO: 35+ years at one company, from process engineer to chairman. He holds a chemical engineering BS from the University of Oklahoma and an MBA from West Texas A&M.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Valero as a process engineer at the McKee refinery in the Texas Panhandle. He also writes bylined pieces for the San Antonio Report on Valero's giving culture, e.g. 'Valero's legacy of giving and culture of caring' (Oct 2026).

public_contacts.value: Media relations: Lillian Riojas, Executive Director - Media Relations and Communications, 210-345-5002 (no email published)

name: Nguyen Duc Tai
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Mobile World Investment Corporation (MWG; Thegioididong, Dien May Xanh, Bach Hoa Xanh)
profile: Nguyễn Đức Tài (born 1969, Nam Định) studied finance and accounting at the University of Economics HCMC and earned an MBA from the French-Vietnamese CFVG programme. In 2004 he and four partners founded Thegioididong, which grew into MWG, Vietnam's largest electronics and phone retailer, with the Bach Hoa Xanh grocery chain and the EraBlue venture in Indonesia. He was CEO until 2019 and remains chairman.

deep_cut_fact: Thegioididong had five co-founders, not one: Tài, Trần Lê Quân, Đinh Anh Huân, Điêu Chính Hải Triều and Trần Huy Thanh Tùng. Before founding it, Tài had trained in finance and accounting and earned a French-Vietnamese (CFVG) MBA.
notes: The $96M Wikidata net-worth figure probably understates his MWG holding. He is well known in Vietnam for blunt speeches at MWG shareholder meetings. Outreach in Vietnamese via MWG IR is the most practical route; I found no personal contact. The search budget ran out, so I could not find an English-language deep cut.

name: Liam M Mallon
current_role: Retired; former President, ExxonMobil Upstream Company (retired 1 Feb 2025)
profile: Irish-born petroleum engineer who spent about 35 years at Mobil/ExxonMobil, from 1990 in Aberdeen through postings in Nigeria, Australia, Canada (president, 2004), Malaysia and Africa. He led ExxonMobil Development Company on mega-projects and was president of the whole Upstream business from 2022 until retiring in February 2025, when Dan Ammann succeeded him.
interesting_fact: He ran ExxonMobil's entire upstream (oil and gas production) business from 2022 to 2025, a period that included the Pioneer Natural Resources acquisition and rapid Guyana and Permian growth. Before that he headed ExxonMobil Development Company, which builds its largest projects.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Drogheda, Ireland, he studied mechanical engineering at Trinity College Dublin and petroleum engineering at Heriot-Watt in Edinburgh. He joined Mobil in Aberdeen in 1990 and was operations manager in Nigeria by 1998.
notes: Retired, so ExxonMobil media relations is not an appropriate route. A self-described personal bio site (liam-bio-ertwb6gq.manus.space) mentions openness to speaking and board work, but it could not be verified as his and is not listed. Conference speaker pages (CERAWeek, ADIPEC) show he speaks at energy events. Strong fit for the energy theme.

name: Keith Stuart Liddell
current_role: Founder and Chair of the Board, Lifezone Metals Ltd (NYSE: LZM)
profile: A metallurgical engineer who has worked only in minerals and metals since 1981, taking nickel, copper and PGM projects from exploration through to production. He founded the Lifezone group, which listed on the NYSE via a SPAC in 2023. As chair he focuses on its Hydromet refining technology and the Kabanga Nickel Project in Tanzania. He and his family hold about 28% of Lifezone.
interesting_fact: Lifezone's pitch is its own hydrometallurgical ('Hydromet') process, offered as a lower-emission alternative to smelting, which it plans to use to refine nickel from the Kabanga project in Tanzania.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a minerals engineer, with an honours BSc in Minerals Engineering from the University of Birmingham and an MSc in Engineering from the University of the Witwatersrand. Lifezone also retains him as a consultant for hands-on metallurgical engineering.
notes: Good fit for an energy-transition and critical-minerals (battery nickel) episode. The company's general info@ address is the only published channel found.

name: H Andrew DeFerrari

Polo team/US Open detail from Wikipedia and polo press (eqliving.com/the-first-family-of-polo/).

name: Harel Moshe Beit-On
current_role: Founder & General Partner, Viola Growth; Chairman of the Board, Similarweb (since March 2026)

name: Yuen Wupen
current_role: President, Global Business Units (also described as President, Cloud and Networking Platform), Lumentum
profile: Wupen Yuen is a photonics engineer-executive with 25+ years in optical components. Stanford EE PhD, CTO of tunable-laser startup Bandwidth9, then ~17 years at NeoPhotonics (rising to Chief Product Officer). He joined Lumentum with its 2022 NeoPhotonics acquisition and now runs its business units, supplying lasers and optical transceivers for AI data-center networks.

name: R Brad Martin
current_role: Executive Chairman / Chairman of the Board, FedEx Corp (since June 2025); chairman, RBM Venture Company; director, Westrock Coffee

name: Chris Sugden
current_role: Managing Partner and Chair of the Investment Committee, Edison Partners (growth equity), based in Nashville
profile: Chris Sugden is a growth-equity investor who joined Edison Partners in 2002 and has been Managing Partner since 2011. He founded and leads its fintech team. He led Edison's investments in MoneyLion, including the 2018 $42M round, and sat on its board until Gen Digital acquired the company in April 2025. Before Edison he was CFO and division president of Princeton eCom.
interesting_fact: Over the last decade he has led exits of ten Edison portfolio companies with a combined enterprise value of over $15 billion. He has served as a director of 30+ companies.
deep_cut_fact: Away from venture capital, he serves on the Board of Commissioners of the Chattanooga Municipal Airport Authority and the board of the Michigan State University Research Foundation. He holds an honors accounting degree from Michigan State and credits his salesman father and grandfather with teaching him that "nothing happens without the first sale."

name: Patricia K Poppe
current_role: CEO, PG&E Corporation
profile: Patti Poppe, a Purdue industrial engineer, spent ~15 years at General Motors before moving to DTE Energy (2005) and Consumers Energy (2011), becoming its CEO. Since 2021 she has led PG&E, California's largest utility, through post-bankruptcy wildfire-safety work and grid buildout, including data-center load growth.

notes: Excellent fit for energy/data-center podcast (PG&E has a large data-center interconnection queue). Business Roundtable member; inducted into Automotive Hall of Fame. Media relations line published on PG&E pages: 415-973-5930. Approach via PG&E corporate communications.

name: Luther King Jr
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Luther King Capital Management (Fort Worth); independent director, TXO Partners L.P.
profile: J. Luther King Jr., CFA, born in Odessa, Texas, founded Fort Worth investment adviser Luther King Capital Management in 1979 (about $30.5bn AUM in late 2025). He is a director and roughly 8% unitholder of oil and gas producer TXO Partners, has served on five public boards (incl. Tyler Technologies) and chaired TCU's board of trustees.
interesting_fact: He started LKCM in 1979 after declining to relocate to New York when his employer, Lionel D. Edie & Company (where he ran the Dallas office), was sold. He was inducted into the Texas Business Hall of Fame in October 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1963 as a credit analyst at First National Bank of Fort Worth, and in 2002 established the LKCM Center for Financial Studies at TCU's Neeley School of Business, his alma mater (BSC and MBA).

public_contacts.value: https://www.lkcm.com/about/contact-lkcm/ (firm office contact page; Fort Worth office main line 817.332.3235)

notes: Not to be confused with Martin Luther King Jr. Energy angle: major TXO Partners (oil & gas) holder alongside his firm. Best route is via LKCM's Fort Worth office.

name: David J Lubar
current_role: President & CEO, Lubar & Co. (Milwaukee); director and 10%+ owner of Hallador Energy (HNRG)
profile: Milwaukee investor who has led Lubar & Co., a family office/private investment firm founded in 1977 that buys middle-market companies for long-term ownership; he joined in 1983 and led investments in 20+ companies. A Hallador Energy director since 2018; also on the Milwaukee Brewers and Baird Funds boards.
interesting_fact: Hallador, where he is a director and major holder, owns Indiana's ~1 GW Merom coal plant and signed a commitment agreement with a global data-center developer in 2025 as it repositions the plant to serve data-center demand.

notes: Strong energy and data-center angle through Hallador and Merom. He is a prominent Milwaukee civic leader (past chair of Froedtert-ThedaCare Health, the Greater Milwaukee Committee and United Way). No published email found; lubar.com blocks scripted access, so check its contact page manually.

name: Gregg C Sengstack
current_role: Retired Executive Chairperson, Franklin Electric (retired 2025); Director, Woodward Inc. and Allegion plc
profile: Gregg Sengstack spent ~37 years at Franklin Electric (pumps, water and fueling systems), joining in 1988 as assistant treasurer, becoming CFO in 1999, CEO 2014-2024 and chair from 2015; he expanded its energy systems, water-treatment and U.S. distribution businesses. He retired in 2025 and remains on the boards of Woodward (energy conversion/aerospace) and Allegion.
interesting_fact: He rose from assistant treasurer to CEO at the same company, leading Franklin Electric's push into fueling systems, water treatment and connected (IoT) pumping solutions.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Franklin Electric he headed its Franklin Fueling Systems and International Water businesses; he holds a bachelor's from Bucknell University and an MBA from the University of Chicago.
notes: Retired from Franklin Electric in 2025 (Retirement & Consulting Agreement in SEC filing). No personal channels found; reach via Woodward or Allegion corporate secretary. Relevant for energy/fueling/water infrastructure angle.

name: David J. Rosa
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Intuitive Surgical (since July 1, 2025)
profile: Dave Rosa has spent nearly all of Intuitive's history at the robotic-surgery pioneer, joining in 1996 as a mechanical engineer on the first da Vinci system. He later led engineering, regulatory, sales and marketing, served as chief business officer and president (2023), and succeeded Gary Guthart as CEO in July 2025.
interesting_fact: An engineer with multiple patents, he founded Intuitive's first clinical engineering and endoluminal groups, which led to the da Vinci single-port (SP) robot and the Ion bronchoscopy system.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Intuitive as a mechanical engineer working on the very first da Vinci system and has said he 'really loved' tackling its unique and complex engineering challenges; he is a Cal Poly San Luis Obispo mechanical engineering grad (B.S. 1989).
notes: Cal Poly degree per CSU alumni profile (https://calstate.edu/impact-of-the-csu/alumni/made-in-the-csu/san-luis-obispo/Pages/david-j-rosa.aspx). Speaks at DeviceTalks. Best route: Intuitive media relations.

name: W Randall Fowler
current_role: Co-CEO and director, Enterprise Products Partners (Houston); becomes sole CEO when Jim Teague retires on Jan 4, 2027
profile: Randy Fowler joined midstream giant Enterprise Products Partners in 1999, soon after its IPO. He was CFO in 2007-2015 and again in 2018-2024 and has been co-CEO since 2020. He has 48 years in energy finance and accounting, and his wealth is mainly Enterprise units. Under the July 2026 succession plan he takes sole command of the ~$120bn-enterprise-value pipeline, NGL and export business in January 2027.
interesting_fact: He is about to become sole CEO of one of the largest US energy infrastructure companies (pipelines, NGL fractionation, Gulf Coast export terminals). Chairman Randa Duncan credits outgoing co-CEO Teague with growing enterprise value from $1.8bn to almost $120bn over the period Fowler was there.
deep_cut_fact: A Louisiana Tech graduate (BS Accounting '78, MBA Finance), he was named the College of Business Distinguished Alumnus in 2012 and sits on its advisory board. He has also chaired the National Association of Publicly Traded Partnerships, the MLP industry group.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: natural gas/NGL infrastructure and power demand from data centers are live topics for Enterprise. No personal social accounts. Route via Enterprise investor relations or media relations (named in quarterly press releases). Sources disagree on his MBA year ('89 vs '91).

name: Eric B Stang
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Ooma Inc. (NYSE: OOMA); Director, Rambus
profile: Stanford economics AB and Harvard MBA who worked at McKinsey, Monitor Company and Raychem. As CEO of Lexar Media (2001-06) he grew it into a Silicon Valley public company with more than $850M in revenue, then ran medtech firm Reliant Technologies. He has led Ooma since 2009, taking it public on the NYSE. In 2026 the company is pushing Ooma AI with revenue growing about 25% a year.
interesting_fact: He grew flash-memory maker Lexar from a small private company into one of the 50 largest public tech companies in Silicon Valley before it became part of Micron.
deep_cut_fact: Outside work he lists sailing, skiing, backpacking and car racing among his hobbies. Before running companies he did stints at McKinsey, Monitor Company and Raychem.
notes: Also on the Avalanche Technology (MRAM) board, which is relevant to a data-center/memory angle. Ooma's published IR/press email could not be retrieved (Business Wire blocked), so use the Ooma investor relations site.

name: Jonathan M Jaffe
current_role: Retired Co-CEO & President of Lennar (retired 31 Dec 2025); board member, HomeAid America and other boards
profile: Jon Jaffe joined Lennar in 1983 and spent 42 years there, rising to COO (2004), President and Co-CEO; he led Lennar's 1995 expansion into California and the West and deals including CalAtlantic. He retired at the end of 2025 and left the board. An architect by training, he has served on boards incl. Five Point Holdings, Opendoor and True Anthem.
interesting_fact: He oversaw Lennar's acquisition and redevelopment of former military sites Mare Island, Hunters Point, El Toro and Treasure Island in California.
deep_cut_fact: Before homebuilding, he earned an undergraduate degree in architecture at the University of Florida and did graduate architecture studies at Georgia Tech.
notes: Retirement announced 14 Nov 2025 (https://investors.lennar.com/press-releases/2025/11-14-2025-222013161). Also listed on Millrose Properties insider filings. HomeAid (homeless-housing charity of the homebuilding industry) bio page is a warm, positive hook.

name: Richard M McVey
current_role: Founder and former CEO/Executive Chairman of MarketAxess (retired end of 2024); Miami University (OH) trustee; senior advisor to an AI data company
profile: Rick McVey incubated MarketAxess inside J.P. Morgan in 1999 while running North American fixed-income sales, and spun it out in 2000. He built it into the leading electronic corporate-bond trading platform and ran it as CEO until 2023. He was executive chairman through 2024 and then retired. He now focuses on philanthropy, board work and advising an AI firm that builds datasets for illiquid assets.
interesting_fact: When MarketAxess spun out of J.P. Morgan in January 2000, around 50 other electronic bond-trading startups were competing. McVey recalls that the hardest early hurdle was client onboarding, which was 'arduous and painfully slow with the legal reviews.'
deep_cut_fact: A Miami University class of 1981 alumnus, he gave $20 million for the 87,000 sq ft Richard M. McVey Data Science Building on Miami's Oxford, Ohio campus, one of the five largest single gifts in the school's history. He also funded the McVey Center for Computational and Data Sciences at Colby College.
notes: Retired from MarketAxess at the end of 2024, so the SEC 'Executive Chairman' tag is outdated. He has no public personal channels that I found. Possible routes are Miami University (as a trustee) or MarketAxess corporate communications. He is interested in AI and data science.

name: Emily M. Leproust
current_role: CEO, President & Co-founder, Twist Bioscience (Nasdaq: TWST); Director, GeneDx Holdings
profile: French-born chemist Emily Leproust (M.Sc. Lyon industrial chemistry 1995; PhD University of Houston 2001) was Director of Applications and Chemistry R&D in Genomics at Agilent. In 2013 she co-founded Twist Bioscience, which mass-produces synthetic DNA on silicon chips for genes, NGS target enrichment, antibody discovery and DNA data storage. She has led Twist through its 2018 IPO to today.
interesting_fact: She won BIO's Rosalind Franklin Award in 2020 and gave a 2021 TED talk on how synthetic biology can improve health, food and materials.
deep_cut_fact: She co-authored the landmark 2013 Nature paper with EMBL-EBI's Nick Goldman and Ewan Birney ('Towards practical, high-capacity, low-maintenance information storage in synthesized DNA'). It was an early demonstration of archiving digital files in DNA, made with DNA synthesized while she was at Agilent.
notes: A strong fit for a data-centre podcast because of DNA data storage, which Twist spun into a separate venture. She speaks often (TED, WEF, SynBioBeta). Route via Angela Bitting (corporate affairs). The Wikipedia article covers past litigation and a short report; avoid those topics.

name: Jennifer L Sherman
current_role: President & CEO, Federal Signal Corporation (Downers Grove, IL); Chair, Franklin Electric
profile: Jennifer Sherman began as a corporate attorney, joined Federal Signal in 1994 and rose through general counsel, chief administrative officer and COO before becoming CEO on Jan 1, 2016. She has built the maker of street sweepers, vacuum trucks, safety and signalling equipment into a serial acquirer of specialty vehicle businesses. She also chairs Franklin Electric's board.
interesting_fact: She won the 2024 EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Midwest Award, unusual for a CEO of a century-old industrial company.
deep_cut_fact: Before running the company she won Outstanding Corporate Counsel awards in 2005 and 2006 from Chicago's Center for Disability and Elder Law, which helps low-income people get legal help. She also chaired the executive board of The Community House.
notes: The IR contact listed is CFO Ian Hudson. Chicago business-community figure; University of Michigan BBA and JD.

name: Adam J Katz
current_role: Co-Founder and CIO, Irenic Capital Management LP (activist hedge fund, New York); CEO and director, Irenic Acquisition Corp. (SPAC)

Irenic's campaign at Barnes Group put him on its board in 2024, before Apollo bought Barnes for $3.6bn (closed Jan 2025). In 2026 he launched an aerospace and defense-focused SPAC and pushed for changes at Snap and Big Yellow.

The best route is likely the Irenic SPAC's SEC filings, or press contacts named in Irenic campaign releases.

name: Victor Gapare

profile: Victor Gapare is a Zimbabwean mining entrepreneur who led Bilboes Holdings, a gold miner near Bulawayo, after a 2003 management buyout from Anglo American Zimbabwe. When Caledonia Mining (owner of the Blanket gold mine) acquired Bilboes in January 2023, he received roughly 13% of Caledonia through his family trust's Toziyana Resources and joined its board as an executive director.

name: John D Idol
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Capri Holdings (Michael Kors, Jimmy Choo) - stepping down 4 Jan 2027, then senior adviser to 31 Mar 2027

He built it into Capri Holdings (adding Jimmy Choo and Versace, later sold to Prada in 2025). In Nov 2026 Capri named Justin Boxford to succeed him as CEO.

name: William B. Cyr
current_role: CEO, Freshpet, Inc. (since Sept 2016); director, Vital Farms
profile: Billy Cyr spent ~19 years at Procter & Gamble, then led the buyout of Sunny Delight from P&G with J.W. Childs and ran it as CEO for over a decade. Since 2016 he has run Freshpet, the refrigerated fresh pet-food maker, taking it from about $6 a share to a ~$1bn+ revenue business; it marked its 20th anniversary in October 2026.

notes: Princeton '85 (History/East Asian Studies). Freshpet runs 'Freshpet Kitchens' plants and has publicised renewable-energy sourcing - possible energy angle.

name: R Douglas Orr
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, FirstCash Holdings, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCFS), Fort Worth, TX

In that time it has grown into the largest pawn-store operator in the U.S. and Latin America, and later the UK, plus the American First Finance point-of-sale lending business. His wealth comes mainly from long-held FirstCash equity.
interesting_fact: He has been CFO for more than 23 years, very long for a public company, covering FirstCash's expansion from a regional Texas pawn chain into a multinational operator with $1B+ in quarterly revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Before pawn lending, he spent 14 years in senior executive and financial management roles at Ray & Berndtson, a global executive search firm, after four years at Price Waterhouse.

Gar Jackson, Global IR Group - gar@globalirgroup.com

name: Alexander R. Slusky
current_role: Founding Partner and Managing Director, Vector Capital; director, Rocket Lab (NASDAQ: RKLB)
profile: Alex Slusky founded San Francisco technology private-equity firm Vector Capital in 1997 after investing roles at Ziff Brothers Investments and NEA. Vector has backed or bought companies such as Corel, SafeNet, WatchGuard, Technicolor and LivePerson. His Vector Acquisition Corp SPAC took Rocket Lab public in 2021, and he remains on Rocket Lab's board.
