deep_cut_fact: Before finance he was a product manager at Microsoft and a McKinsey consultant; he graduated summa cum laude in economics from Harvard and was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School. Early board seats included NetGravity (sold to DoubleClick) and Savi Technology (sold to Lockheed Martin).
notes: Vector's contact page lists only investment-sourcing and investor-relations emails (no press contact). Space/Rocket Lab angle is the strongest hook for the podcast.

name: Eduardo S Elsztain
current_role: Chairman of IRSA, Cresud, BrasilAgro and Banco Hipotecario (Argentina)
profile: Buenos Aires-born (1960) businessman who, after a 1990 meeting persuaded George Soros to let him manage $10M, built IRSA into Argentina's largest real-estate group (malls, offices, Llao Llao Hotel) and took control of agribusiness Cresud in 1994. He also chairs Brazil's BrasilAgro and mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario, controlling them via his holding company IFISA.
interesting_fact: His career turned on one meeting: in 1990 he landed an hour with George Soros, said he could manage $10M, and Soros replied 'Okay, no problem!'; within four years he had raised $110M and bought Buenos Aires office towers and the Alto Palermo mall.
deep_cut_fact: He saw potential in Buenos Aires' derelict, mice-infested Abasto wholesale market and turned it into Abasto Shopping while keeping its historic facade; and the former Boca Juniors training ground IRSA bought in 1997 finally won approval in 2024 as the Ramblas del Plata waterfront project.
notes: Leading Argentine real estate/agribusiness figure; also active in Jewish community organisations. Spanish-language press covers him widely. Studied medicine and economics at UBA but left to pursue business.

name: Wajid Ali
current_role: EVP & Chief Financial Officer, Lumentum Holdings (NASDAQ: LITE); Director, TTM Technologies (NASDAQ: TTMI)
profile: Canadian-trained finance executive (York University BA/MA economics, Schulich MBA, CPA/CMA) who became Lumentum's CFO in February 2019 after serving as SVP & CFO of Synaptics, VP & Controller at Teledyne and CFO of DALSA, with earlier roles at AMD and ATI. Lumentum's optical lasers and transceivers are now a key supplier to AI data-center networks.
interesting_fact: Lumentum, where he is CFO, makes the optical components (lasers, transceivers, optical circuit switches) that link GPUs in AI data centers - one of the market's biggest AI-infrastructure winners.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley, he was CFO of DALSA, the Canadian image-sensor/semiconductor company Teledyne acquired in 2011, then stayed on as Teledyne's VP & Controller.
notes: Corporate executive, low personal profile. Strong data-center/AI optics angle. Route via Lumentum IR.

name: Balan Nair
current_role: President & CEO, Liberty Latin America (NASDAQ: LILA); director, Charter Communications and ADTRAN
profile: Telecom technologist who spent 12+ years at Qwest (rising to CIO/CTO), was CTO of AOL, then joined Liberty Global in 2007 as CTO, later becoming its Chief Technology & Innovation Officer. Since the 2017-18 spin-off he has led Liberty Latin America, the Denver-based cable, mobile and subsea-fiber operator serving the Caribbean and Latin America (brands such as Flow, Liberty and Cable & Wireless).
interesting_fact: He is an engineer-CEO: at Liberty Global he ran the worldwide network, IT, mobile, supply chain and venture investments before taking over the Latin America/Caribbean spin-off.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a patent in systems development, is a Licensed Professional Engineer in Colorado, and has been inducted into the Cable Hall of Fame.
notes: The LLA media page lists Michael Coakley (Corporate Communications) and Soomit Datta (IR). Relevant to the podcast's data-center angle: LLA operates subsea cable and data-center/network infrastructure across the Caribbean.

name: Robert E Switz
current_role: Retired; former Chairman of Micron Technology (2012-Jan 2025) and Marvell director (2016-June 2025)
profile: Bob Switz was CFO and then Chairman/President/CEO of ADC Telecommunications (CEO 2003-2010) until its sale to Tyco Electronics. He went on to chair Micron's board from 2012 and sat on the boards of Marvell, Broadcom (lead independent director), FireEye/Mandiant, Gigamon and GT Advanced. He left Micron in early 2025 and did not stand for re-election at Marvell in June 2025.
interesting_fact: He chaired Micron's board for over a decade (2012-2025), spanning its rise to become a key supplier of AI-data-center HBM memory.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he did finance roles at Olin (1971-79), AMF (1979-85), PepsiCo and Gulfstar, then was CFO of Tucson chipmaker Burr-Brown (now part of TI), where he oversaw five startup ventures. CFO magazine gave him its CFO Excellence Award in 1999.
notes: Retired from public boards in 2025 (Marvell announcement: https://investor.marvell.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/99/marvell-announces-changes-to-its-board-of-directors). No personal public contact found; Minnesota-based executive historically. Alive assumed (no obituary found, active through 2025).

name: Gregory M. Shepard
current_role: Private investor; ~6.2% shareholder of Atlas Energy Solutions (NYSE: AESI); former AESI director (appointed Sept 2023)
profile: Florida investor who chaired Union Insurance Group (1985-2004) and was a long-time activist investor in listed insurers. An early backer of Permian frac-sand supplier Atlas Sand (2017), he joined successor Atlas Energy Solutions' board in 2023 and holds ~7.65m shares; recent Form 4s list him as 'Other', not director.
interesting_fact: From 1996 to 2019 he ran activist campaigns at publicly traded subsidiaries of mutual insurers, including Meridian Insurance Group, State Auto Financial, Donegal Group and EMC Insurance Group.
deep_cut_fact: Before backing Atlas, he was sole owner and founder of Wisconsin Northern White Sands Holdings (2014-2019), which explored building frac-sand (proppant) mines in Illinois, Wisconsin, Oklahoma and Texas.
notes: No published contact; SEC filings list counsel Amundsen Davis LLC (Chicago) as authorized to receive notices - not an outreach channel. Dec 2025 he entered a UBS prepaid variable forward on 532,500 AESI shares. Atlas IR is the only corporate route.

name: Steven Sell
current_role: Former President and CEO of agilon health (2020 to Aug 2025); advisor to early-stage healthcare companies. I could not verify a current role.
profile: Steven J. Sell is a managed-care executive. He ran Health Net's Western Region from 2008 to 2016 and was President, CEO and Chairman of Health Net from 2016 to 2019, the period of its sale to Centene. He led value-based primary-care company agilon health from 2020 through its 2021 IPO, then stepped down as CEO and director in August 2025, when co-founder Ron Williams became Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: agilon health, which he led for five years, partners with independent primary-care physician groups to move them into full-risk Medicare Advantage contracts, a model built around doctors rather than insurers.
deep_cut_fact: He is a liberal-arts graduate (B.A. from Swarthmore College) who went on to a Stanford GSB MBA. While running agilon he also advised several early-stage healthcare startups.
notes: He is no longer at agilon, so the agilon press (media@agilonhealth.com) and IR contacts no longer reach him. The SEC net-worth figure reflects 2025 holdings and the stock has fallen sharply, so it is likely overstated. His exit came alongside withdrawn guidance, so avoid making that the angle. LinkedIn is the probable route, but I did not verify it. Not a natural fit for the energy/data-center theme.

name: Robert Regan Shannon
current_role: EVP & Chief Accounting Officer, Permian Resources Corp (NYSE: PR), Midland, Texas
profile: Texas oil-and-gas finance executive (born about 1989) who was VP and Chief Accounting Officer of Midland-based Colgate Energy from 2016. When Colgate merged with Centennial Resource Development in 2022 to form Permian Resources, he became EVP Corporate Services, then EVP & CAO in May 2024. His wealth comes largely from Colgate equity converted into PR shares.
interesting_fact: He was Chief Accounting Officer of Colgate Energy from 2016, when he was in his mid-20s. Colgate was a founder-led private Permian producer whose 2022 merger with Centennial created Permian Resources, one of the largest pure-play Delaware Basin producers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Colgate he was controller of Burnett Petroleum, an independent onshore E&P, and before that a KPMG auditor focused on upstream oil and gas companies. He came through UT Austin's Business Honors Program and its Master in Professional Accounting.
notes: Back-office finance executive with no public media profile. For an energy podcast, Permian Resources' co-CEOs (Will Hickey, James Walter) are the natural interviewees. Age (35 in 2024) is from the May 2024 8-K.

name: Morgado Horta Alessandro Monteiro
current_role: Founding partner, CEO and Director, Vinci Compass Investments Ltd (Nasdaq: VINP), Rio de Janeiro
profile: Alessandro Monteiro Morgado Horta (55) is a founding partner of Vinci Partners, which grew out of Banco Pactual's principal investment group and merged with Chile's Compass Group to form Vinci Compass, a Latin American alternative-asset manager. Before Vinci he was managing partner and COO at Banco Pactual, a VP at UBS Pactual, and a partner at Banco Icatu.
interesting_fact: Vinci Compass is consolidating Latin American asset management. In October 2025 it agreed to buy 50.1% of Verde Asset Management, Luis Stuhlberger's multi-strategy firm with about R$16bn in assets.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an electrical engineer at PUC-Rio, like co-founder Gilberto Sayao. At Banco Pactual (2001-06) he was managing partner and COO and also ran the Long-Term Investments division.
notes: Known publicly as Alessandro Horta. The SEC insider record lists him as 'Pres. of Finance & Operations', but the 2025 20-F names him CEO. Best route is the US PR agency (Prosek).

name: Lynn J Good
current_role: Retired Chair & CEO of Duke Energy (retired April 1, 2025); director of Morgan Stanley and Caterpillar
profile: Lynn Good, from Fairfield, Ohio, spent two decades at Arthur Andersen (one of its first female partners in the Midwest) before joining Cinergy/Duke, becoming Duke Energy CFO, then CEO in 2013 and chair in 2016. She steered Duke's coal-to-clean transition and grid and nuclear plans, retiring in April 2025 (succeeded by Harry Sideris).
interesting_fact: She has been a leading voice for the U.S. nuclear industry, serving on the board of the World Association of Nuclear Operators and as past chair of the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations; EEI gave her its Thomas A. Edison Legacy Award.
deep_cut_fact: Her math-teacher father sat with her over the college catalog and steered her to the equivalent of computer science; she told NPR she had 'never seen a computer' before college (she graduated from Miami University in systems analysis and accounting).
notes: Retired from Duke, so Duke corporate channels are no longer hers; no personal website/social accounts or published office contact found. Strong energy-transition/nuclear/load-growth guest; best route likely via board/industry networks (EEI, Morgan Stanley/Caterpillar corporate secretaries).

name: Lawrence Otto Klein
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Oruka Therapeutics (Nasdaq: ORKA)
profile: Lawrence Klein, PhD, is CEO of Oruka Therapeutics, which develops long-acting antibodies for psoriasis and other inflammatory skin diseases, aiming for clearance with one or two doses a year. He was previously CBO then COO at CRISPR Therapeutics (7 years), a partner at Versant Ventures, and a McKinsey associate partner.
interesting_fact: He was part of CRISPR Therapeutics' leadership for seven years, helping set its strategy and partnerships as it became one of the best-known gene-editing companies.
deep_cut_fact: Before business he was a scientist: his Stanford PhD in biophysics focused on T-cell immunology. Oruka's name blends words meaning 'skin' and 'restoration'.
notes: Biotech, not an energy/data-center fit. No direct email found; IR site blocks automated access, so check Oruka press releases manually for the IR/media contact.

name: Barry F Cohen
current_role: COO - Americas and Board Member, SS Innovations International (SSII); Chairman, Avra Medical Robotics
profile: Veteran industrial-company manager and securities professional (50+ years) who founded Avra Surgical (2006) and Avra Medical Robotics (2015), the US shell that became SS Innovations International, maker of Dr. Sudhir Srivastava's low-cost SSi Mantra surgical robot. He now runs the company's Americas operations and sits on its board.
interesting_fact: His medical-robotics vehicle Avra became the US listing for SS Innovations, the Indian company behind the SSi Mantra surgical robotic system.
deep_cut_fact: Long before robotics he was a director of pipe and specialty-chemicals maker Synalloy Corp. (c.1979-1989) and its president in 1984-85, and ran his own NASD broker-dealer, Barry F. Cohen & Co., from 1983 to 1999.
notes: info@ is a general company address (no dedicated press/IR address found on the leadership page).

name: Navdeep S Sooch
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Silicon Laboratories (Silicon Labs), Austin, TX
profile: Nav Sooch co-founded Austin chipmaker Silicon Labs in 1996 with fellow Crystal Semiconductor alumni Dave Welland and Jeff Scott, was CEO until 2003 (and interim CEO in 2005) and has chaired the board since inception. From 2011-2018 he was CEO of Ketra, a solid-state lighting startup. Earlier he was VP Engineering at Crystal Semiconductor/Cirrus Logic and a design engineer at AT&T Bell Labs.
interesting_fact: Silicon Labs' first product (1998), a cheaper, smaller silicon DAA modem chip, took sales from $5.6M in 1998 to nearly $47M in 1999; the company also built the first CMOS RF synthesizer for mobile phones.
deep_cut_fact: Holds a B.S. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Michigan-Dearborn and an M.S. from Stanford, and started out as a design engineer at AT&T Bell Labs before Crystal Semiconductor.
notes: Serial founder (Silicon Labs, Ketra lighting) - strong entrepreneurship angle. No published personal contact found; route via Silicon Labs corporate communications / IR.

name: Dennis Degner
current_role: President & CEO, Range Resources Corp (Fort Worth, TX); slated to join EQT's board when EQT's all-stock acquisition of Range closes (expected Q1 2027)
profile: Petroleum engineer who joined Range Resources in 2010 after roles at EnCana, Sierra Engineering and Halliburton, ran operations as COO and became CEO in May 2023. Range is a pioneer Marcellus shale gas producer; on 26 Oct 2026 it agreed to be acquired by EQT in an all-stock deal creating a >$50bn-EV natural gas giant pitched at AI/data-center power demand.
interesting_fact: The EQT-Range merger (0.987 EQT shares per Range share) creates America's largest vertically integrated natural gas producer, >9 Bcfe/d, explicitly positioned for demand-led growth; Degner will join EQT's board.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a gas CEO, his degree is in Agricultural Engineering (B.S., Texas A&M), and he has worked fields across Texas, Louisiana, Wyoming, Colorado and Pennsylvania and published SPE work on deploying new technologies.
notes: Timely guest for energy/data-center angle (Range has an 'Energy for the AI Revolution' section). Mid-merger with EQT, so expect quiet-period constraints until close in Q1 2027.

name: Samuel M Mencoff
current_role: Founding Partner and Senior Advisor, Madison Dearborn Partners; Lead Independent Director, Packaging Corporation of America; Chair, Brown University Health
profile: Sam Mencoff spent 11 years at First Chicago Venture Capital before co-founding Chicago private-equity firm Madison Dearborn Partners in 1992, later serving as co-CEO; MDP's 1999 buyout of Packaging Corporation of America put him on PCA's board, where he is lead independent director. He also founded industrial holding company Temple Hall Group.
interesting_fact: He served as Brown University's 21st chancellor (2016-2024) and in 2025 became board chair of Brown University Health, Rhode Island's largest integrated academic medical system.
deep_cut_fact: He studied anthropology at Brown (BA 1978), is a commissioner of the Smithsonian's National Portrait Gallery, and chairs the Art Institute of Chicago's Committee on American Art.
notes: Past boards include Great Lakes Dredge & Dock, Huntway Refining, Smurfit Kappa and Boise Cascade (industrial/energy-adjacent). Route via Madison Dearborn Partners.

name: Matthew Stumpf
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, AppLovin Corp (APP), Palo Alto
profile: Finance executive who joined AppLovin in February 2020 to lead FP&A, after years in PwC's transaction services group as a financial due-diligence director. He became CFO in January 2024, succeeding Herald Chen. He has led finance through AppLovin's AI-driven (AXON) ad-tech surge and its S&P 500 inclusion. His wealth is mainly AppLovin equity.
interesting_fact: He joined AppLovin about a year before its April 2021 IPO and rose from FP&A head to CFO in under four years. As CFO he oversees global finance, accounting, tax, treasury and investor relations.
deep_cut_fact: His first PwC role was a summer 2005 assurance internship. He later spent about five years (2015-2020) as a Financial Due Diligence Director in PwC Transaction Services before moving to AppLovin. He studied Business Management Economics at UC Santa Cruz.
notes: Low public profile outside earnings calls. Career dates come from aggregators (Clay, MarketScreener) and differ slightly. Possible AI angle: AppLovin's AXON ad engine is ML-driven.

name: Hilton H. Howell Jr.
current_role: Executive Chairman & CEO, Gray Media (NYSE: GTN), Atlanta; also Chairman/CEO of Atlantic American Corp
profile: Atlanta executive and lawyer who joined Gray's board in the 1990s after J. Mack Robinson's investor group took control. He became vice chairman in 2002 and CEO in 2008, when the stock had fallen to about 16 cents. He then led a run of acquisitions, including the US$3.65bn Raycom deal in 2018, that made Gray one of the largest US local-TV station owners.
interesting_fact: Under Howell, Gray bought the former GM Doraville assembly plant in 2021 to build 'Assembly Atlanta', a studio-city film and TV production campus, and also bought Third Rail Studios. It was an unusual move for a broadcaster.
deep_cut_fact: He took over as CEO in 2008, when Gray shares traded as low as 16 cents and the NYSE was warning about delisting. He then turned the over-leveraged regional group into the third-largest US TV station owner.
notes: The deep-cut fact touches on Gray's 2008 low point, so frame it as a turnaround story. Assembly Atlanta (studio campus on a former GM plant) is a good real-estate/infrastructure hook. Gray's press releases list executive contacts (CFO and an EVP) by phone; I found no published press email. Education per aggregators: Baylor, UT Austin MBA, Baylor Law (unverified). Web search budget ran out at this person, so contacts were not researched further.

name: Edwin A. Poston
current_role: Co-Founder & Senior Advisor, TrueBridge Capital Partners (Chapel Hill, NC); Director, Ridgepost Capital, Inc. (formerly P10, Inc.)
profile: Ed Poston co-founded TrueBridge Capital Partners, a venture capital fund-of-funds and co-investment manager, after serving as Managing Director and Head of Private Equity at The Rockefeller Foundation. TrueBridge was acquired by P10 in 2021, and Poston joined P10's board as TrueBridge's designee; P10 has since been renamed Ridgepost Capital.
interesting_fact: Before founding TrueBridge he ran private equity, including oversight of the venture portfolio, for The Rockefeller Foundation's endowment.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he was an investment banker at NationsBanc Montgomery Securities and an opportunistic real estate investor in Washington, D.C.; he holds a JD and MBA from Emory and a BA from UNC-Chapel Hill, near where TrueBridge is based.
notes: Now Senior Advisor (not day-to-day) at TrueBridge; Mel Williams is GP & CEO. Low public profile.

name: Neil Gagnon
current_role: Principal, Gagnon Securities LLC and Gagnon Advisors LLC (New York investment managers)
profile: New York small-cap investor whose firms, Gagnon Securities and Gagnon Advisors, take concentrated stakes in small public companies. He appears as an insider of engine and power-system maker Power Solutions International (PSIX) via a large shareholding, not as an operator; Gagnon Advisors still filed 13F reports in Nov 2026.
interesting_fact: His personal and firm holdings are frequently large enough to cross SEC 5-10% reporting thresholds; in 2025 he reported a ~5% stake in NYSE-listed Chinese lender CNFinance alongside his firms.
notes: Very private; almost no press profile. Only published contact found is the Gagnon Advisors office, 1370 Avenue of the Americas, New York (main line 212-554-5000 per its SEC 13F: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1599466/000101905626000153/primary_doc.xml). Firm sites did not load. Latest personal SEC filing: Mar 2025.

name: Nicolas Papadopoulo
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Arch Capital Group Ltd. (Nasdaq: ACGL) since October 2024
profile: French-trained actuary and underwriter who joined Arch Re in Bermuda in 2001 and rose through the specialty insurer/reinsurer to run Arch Reinsurance, then its Global Insurance Group, then serve as President and Chief Underwriting Officer before succeeding Marc Grandisson as group CEO in October 2024.
interesting_fact: He has spent his entire 25-year Arch career there since joining Arch Re Bermuda in 2001; in his first full year as CEO (2025), Arch's tangible book value per share grew at a 33.65% annualised rate over 2023-25 and the company bought back $1.9bn of stock.
deep_cut_fact: Before reinsurance, he worked as an insurance examiner at France's Ministry of Finance (Insurance Department); he is a graduate of École Polytechnique and ENSAE (master's in statistics) and a Fellow of the French Actuarial Society.

public_contacts.value: dwatson@archgroup.com (Donald Watson, Investor Relations, as listed on Arch earnings releases)

notes: Bermuda-based insurance CEO; low media profile. Possible energy/data-center angle: Arch underwrites property, energy and construction risks. Route via investor relations.

name: Srinivasan Sivaram
current_role: President and CEO, QuantumScape Corp (NYSE: QS)
profile: Dr. Siva Sivaram, a semiconductor-memory veteran (Intel, Matrix Semiconductor, SanDisk; Western Digital President of Technology and Strategy 2019-23), became CEO of solid-state battery developer QuantumScape in 2024. He has steered it toward a capital-light licensing model, including a 2024 deal with Volkswagen's PowerCo targeting up to 40 GWh/yr of production.
interesting_fact: QuantumScape's solid-state cell passed its first endurance test as independently confirmed by VW's battery unit PowerCo, and the company has also partnered with grid-storage firm Fluence, extending its batteries beyond EVs.
deep_cut_fact: Long before batteries he was a solar entrepreneur: in 2008 he founded Twin Creek Technologies, a U.S. maker of solar manufacturing equipment, and ran it as CEO for five years. He holds a mechanical-engineering BS from NIT Trichy (Distinguished Alumnus) and a materials-science PhD from RPI.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy/storage podcast; he has done many media interviews (Bloomberg, CNBC, 'E For Electric'). Commonly known as Siva Sivaram. info@ is a general company inbox.

name: Mary T Barra
current_role: Chair & CEO, General Motors; Director, The Walt Disney Company
profile: Mary Barra has run General Motors since January 2014 (chair since 2016), the first woman to lead a Detroit 'Big Three' automaker. A lifelong GM employee who started as an 18-year-old co-op student in 1980, she rose through engineering, plant management (Detroit-Hamtramck), HR and global product development; as CEO she has steered GM's push into EVs, batteries and autonomous driving.
interesting_fact: Her father was a tool-and-die maker at GM's Pontiac Motor Division for 39 years; she earned an electrical engineering degree from the General Motors Institute (now Kettering University) and a Stanford MBA on a GM fellowship.
deep_cut_fact: Her first GM job, at 18 in 1980, was as a co-op student checking fender panels and inspecting hoods at Pontiac - work she used to pay her college tuition.
notes: Extremely high-profile; requests should go through GM Global Communications (news.gm.com lists media contacts; IR site blocked automated access). Energy angle: GM's Ultium battery JV plants and EV-charging/energy (GM Energy) business.

name: Ryan Berry
current_role: Partner and Chief Marketing & Strategy Officer, Ares Management Corporation (NYSE: ARES), Los Angeles (in role since Jan 2018; 2026 proxy notes he was no longer an executive officer at end-2025)
profile: Ryan Berry joined Ares in 2005 as a private-equity investment professional after working as a UBS investment-banking analyst in Los Angeles. As Chief Marketing & Strategy Officer he led Ares' global expansion: asset-manager acquisitions, strategic partnerships, distribution and the 2014 IPO. He is one of the 'Holdco Members' who control Ares' general partner and holds a substantial stake in the firm.
interesting_fact: He is one of six 'Holdco Members', alongside Ares co-founders Arougheti, Kaplan, Ressler and Rosenthal plus Kipp deVeer, who control Ares Management's general partner.
deep_cut_fact: He has two degrees from Western University in Canada: a B.A. with distinction in Business Administration from the Ivey Business School and a B.A. in Cross Disciplinary Studies from Huron University College.

public_contacts.value: Carl Drake, Partner/Senior Advisor to Public Markets IR and Corporate Communications, cdrake@ares.com

notes: The 2026 proxy says he was an NEO for 2025 'despite not being an executive officer at the end of 2025', so his role may have changed; verify before outreach. Ares is a big infrastructure, digital-infrastructure and energy investor, so there is a podcast angle. Low personal media profile; route via Ares corporate communications.

name: Keh Shew Lu
current_role: Director, Diodes Inc (DIOD); retired as Chairman in May 2026 (CEO 2005-2025, Chairman 2020-2026)
profile: Taiwan-born engineer (Tainan; NCKU BSEE 1969; Texas Tech MS/PhD) who rose from junior engineer at Texas Instruments in 1974 to Senior VP running its IC and mixed-signal businesses. He joined the Diodes board in 2001 and as CEO from 2005 built the Plano, TX discrete and analog chipmaker into a multi-billion-dollar company. He handed the CEO role to Gary Yu in 2025 and retired as Chairman in May 2026.
interesting_fact: He was only the second Asian executive, after TSMC founder Morris Chang, to reach Senior Vice President at a major American firm, which he did at Texas Instruments.
deep_cut_fact: As an NCKU undergraduate he published two research papers in IEEE journals. He still funds NCKU scholarships and likes to hire NCKU grads, and NCKU gave him an honorary doctorate in 2021. On receiving it he said, 'Small steps are taken to achieve big goals.'
notes: Uncertain whether he remains a director after the May 2026 annual meeting, so treat the director role as unconfirmed. He founded the DFW Asian-American Citizens Council. Retirement is recent, which makes a reflective 'TI to Diodes' career episode plausible. Power semiconductors connect to data-center and energy topics.

name: Jeffrey Clay Sell
current_role: CEO, X-Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: XE), Rockville, MD - advanced small modular reactors (Xe-100) and TRISO-X fuel
profile: J. Clay Sell (b. 1967, Texas) was U.S. Deputy Secretary of Energy (2005-08), effectively DOE's COO, after years as an energy-policy staffer in Congress and the White House. After eight years running Hunt Energy Horizons, he became X-energy's CEO in 2019, leading it to a Dow SMR construction permit, an Amazon/AEP deal and a Nasdaq listing.
interesting_fact: X-energy's Xe-100 project with Dow on the Texas Gulf Coast won a construction permit for what X-energy calls a historic nuclear-powered industrial site; Sell credited the NRC for granting it earlier than expected.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career on the staff of Texas congressman Mac Thornberry (1995-99), led the Bush-Cheney transition's energy policy team, and holds an accounting BBA from Texas Tech and a JD from UT Austin; before X-energy he spent eight years building Hunt Energy Horizons' renewables portfolio.
notes: Excellent fit (nuclear SMRs powering data centers - Amazon is an investor/partner). Frequent conference speaker and policy voice; press releases name Robert McEntyre (Corporate Communications) as media contact via media@x-energy.com.

name: Brian Lian
current_role: President & CEO (founder), Viking Therapeutics (NASDAQ: VKTX), San Diego
profile: Organic chemist (Whitman College BA, University of Michigan PhD, Indiana University MBA) who worked in small-molecule drug discovery at Amgen, then became a biotech equity analyst at CIBC World Markets and SunTrust Robinson Humphrey. Founded Viking in 2012, which is now developing VK2735, a dual GLP-1/GIP agonist for obesity in Phase 3 trials, in both injectable and oral forms.
interesting_fact: Viking was launched in 2014 on a broad licensing deal for five metabolic and endocrine programs from Ligand Pharmaceuticals, rather than on its own discovery science; it has since become one of the most-watched obesity-drug challengers to Novo and Lilly.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Viking while still working as a sell-side biotech analyst: he spotted metabolic drug candidates Ligand wanted to out-license, negotiated rights to five programs and got Ligand to put up about $2.5m of initial funding.

public_contacts.value: Vida Strategic Partners, Tim Brons (media): tbrons@vidasp.com

notes: Deep-cut fact comes from an aggregator profile (Fintool), so treat it with some care. Viking's 2026 contact blocks also list the CFO's company email; PR contact names rotate, so check the latest release. Ligand has disputed Viking's license for the TR-beta program (2026); avoid this topic.

name: Francis James ONeill
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Underwriting Officer and director, Accelerant Holdings (NYSE: ARX)
profile: Irish-born reinsurance executive known as Frank, who co-founded Accelerant in 2018 with Jeff Radke and Christopher Lee-Smith. Accelerant is a data-driven risk exchange that connects specialty insurance underwriters (MGAs) with risk capital, and it listed on the NYSE in July 2025. He has been its Chief Underwriting Officer since 2018 and holds roughly 3% of the company.
interesting_fact: Before Accelerant he spent about 18 years at Swiss Re, ending as CEO of Swiss Re UK & Ireland (2016–2018) after running its Middle East & Africa business.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Swiss Re in 1998 as a Life & Health underwriter in London, then worked in strategy in Zurich. He led L&H for South-East Asia from 2006 and became a global client executive in the U.S. in 2008.
notes: London-based and low profile. One search summary claimed Accelerant agreed to be acquired by Thoma Bravo alongside its Q2 2026 results, but the release I checked did not mention it, so verify before outreach. Possible podcast angle: data/AI-driven insurance risk exchange.

name: Phillip A Sharp
current_role: Institute Professor (emeritus), MIT / Koch Institute; Director and SAB chair, Alnylam Pharmaceuticals
profile: Phillip Sharp is a molecular biologist who shared the 1993 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering split genes and RNA splicing. He co-founded Biogen (1978) and Alnylam Pharmaceuticals, the RNAi pioneer, and his wealth comes largely from his Alnylam stake. He remains an MIT Institute Professor and chairs the advisory board of MIT's Jameel Clinic for AI in health.
interesting_fact: He co-founded two of biotech's landmark companies, Biogen and Alnylam. He is the subject of the 2025 documentary 'Cracking the Code: Phil Sharp and the Biotech Revolution'.
deep_cut_fact: Raised on a family farm in a bend of the Licking River near McKinneysburg, Kentucky, he paid his own way to college by raising cattle and growing tobacco. He then attended small Union College in Barbourville, KY.

public_contacts.value: sharppa@mit.edu (MIT faculty email; assistant julialib@mit.edu also listed)

notes: Aged 82; very accessible academic who speaks often on science policy and AI in biology. The MIT faculty email is published on his MIT Biology profile, with an assistant (Julia Libe) listed, so going through the assistant is likely best.

name: Cameron Brown
profile: Input record mixes two unrelated sources: a Brown-Forman director (SEC insider data) and a Hurun 'gaming' unicorn founder. No 'Cameron Brown' appears among Brown-Forman's directors or Section 16 insiders in EDGAR or in its 2024-2026 proxy statements, so the person could not be identified.
notes: Likely a data-matching error. Brown-Forman's Brown-family directors are Campbell P. Brown (former chairman) and Elizabeth M. Brown (see https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/own-disp?action=getissuer&CIK=0000014693 and the 2026 DEF 14A). The Hurun gaming-unicorn founder named Cameron Brown was not researched (web-search limit reached). Re-check source data before outreach.

name: Jeffrey Stoops
current_role: Chair of the Board, SBA Communications Corp (NASDAQ: SBAC), since January 2024
profile: Florida corporate/M&A lawyer who joined wireless tower company SBA Communications in 1997, served as CFO, President (2000) and CEO (2002-2023), turning it into one of the world's largest independent tower owners across the Americas and beyond. He retired as CEO in December 2023 and now chairs SBA's board; he co-founded the Stoops Family Foundation (health and education).
interesting_fact: He was brought into SBA in 1997 specifically to transition it from a tower-site services firm into a tower owner, an asset-based model that became the core of the business.
deep_cut_fact: An FSU College of Law grad (1984), he spent 13 years as a corporate/M&A lawyer at Gunster Yoakley; his first big task at SBA was raising its initial US$30m private placement. His motto: 'To get rewards in life, you have to take some risks.'
notes: Good fit for a digital-infrastructure angle (towers, fiber, edge data centers). Based in Boca Raton area; FSU donor (law school, social work, Seminole Boosters). Route via SBA media relations.

name: Mattias Stetz
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Rush Street Interactive (NYSE: RSI)
profile: Swedish-born Mattias Stetz (46) has been COO of online casino and sportsbook operator Rush Street Interactive (BetRivers) since April 2016, overseeing operations and its Latin American business. He spent 2004-2016 at Kindred Group (Unibet), serving as Chief Commercial Officer from 2009, and joined RSI as it built out US online gaming after state legalisation.
interesting_fact: He oversees RSI's Latin American business, one of the earliest US-listed online gaming operators to build a major presence in Colombia and Mexico.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MSc in Marketing and Business Development from the Stockholm School of Economics and is a Harvard Business School alumnus (General Management Program, 2015)—completed the year before he left Kindred for RSI.
notes: Low media profile; gaming sector, weak fit for energy/data-center. IR email confirmed via SEC full-text search of RSI 8-K press releases.

name: Letitia G C Carlson
current_role: Director (non-independent), Telephone and Data Systems (NYSE: TDS); trustee, TDS Voting Trust; physician and clinical professor, George Washington University Medical Faculty Associates
profile: Member of the Carlson family that controls TDS (founded by her father LeRoy T. Carlson) through the TDS Voting Trust; she has sat on the TDS board since 1996 alongside her brothers Walter C.D. and LeRoy T. Carlson Jr. Her career is in medicine: Harvard-trained internist (MD, MPH, FACP) practising and teaching at GW in Washington, D.C.
interesting_fact: She combines a decades-long seat on the board of a family-controlled telecom/broadband group with an active clinical career as an internal-medicine physician and clinical professor at George Washington University.
notes: Not an operating executive; very low public profile. Bio details from aggregators (Fintool/MarketScreener) - confirm against TDS proxy. Approach only via TDS corporate/IR; no published personal contact.

name: Anthony F Markel
current_role: Chairman Emeritus, Markel Group Inc. (NYSE: MKL), Richmond/Glen Allen, VA; retired as Vice Chairman and director in May 2025
profile: Tony Markel joined the family insurance business in 1964 after graduating from UVA's McIntire School of Commerce. He became President & COO in 1992 and Vice Chairman in 2009, helping turn the specialty insurer his grandfather Sam founded in 1930 into today's diversified 'mini-Berkshire', Markel Group. He retired from the board in May 2025 and became Chairman Emeritus.
interesting_fact: He spent more than 60 years at Markel (joined 1964) and 47 years on its board (1978-2025). Insurance Business America inducted him into its Hall of Fame in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He was National Chairman of City of Hope's $1 billion Centennial 'Power of Hope' campaign, which hit its goal in January 2014. He also once joked that the insurance industry 'has provided me at least three square meals a day.'
notes: Retired in 2025. He is a major Richmond, VA philanthropist (UVA, Richmond SPCA, Special Olympics Virginia). The only published route is Markel Group IR.

name: Alexis P Michas
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Juniper Investment Company; Non-Executive Chair of Revvity and of BorgWarner
profile: Alexis P. Michas is a Harvard College/HBS-educated private-equity investor who founded Juniper Investment Company in 2008. He chairs the boards of Revvity (formerly PerkinElmer, on its board since 2001) and auto/e-mobility supplier BorgWarner, sits on Cenergy Holdings' board, and holds a 10%+ stake in Orthofix.
interesting_fact: He chairs BorgWarner, a major supplier pivoting to EV propulsion, and sits on the board of Cenergy Holdings, the Greek maker of power cables and steel pipes for energy grids and offshore wind.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the U.S. Board of Trustees of Athens College in Greece.
notes: Low public profile investor; no published personal/firm email found. Energy angle via Cenergy (cables for grid/offshore wind) and BorgWarner. Route via Juniper Investment Company or company corporate secretaries.

name: Charles Alan Williams
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Northpointe Bancshares, Inc. (NYSE: NPB) and CEO/director of Northpointe Bank, Grand Rapids, MI
profile: Charles 'Chuck' Williams founded Northpointe Bank in Grand Rapids in 1998-99 after a decade as SVP and senior lending officer at First National Bank of America. He built it into one of the only mortgage-focused banks in the US and one of the largest providers of mortgage warehouse financing, taking the holding company public on the NYSE in 2025.
interesting_fact: Northpointe operates nationally from a single Grand Rapids headquarters, describing itself as one of the largest mortgage warehouse lenders and one of the only mortgage-focused banks in the country.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Northpointe he spent 1988-1997 as SVP, senior lending officer and director at First National Bank of America (formerly First National Bank of Michigan), serving on its executive committee; he is a graduate of the University of Wisconsin's Graduate School of Banking.

name: Jamie Foxx
current_role: Actor, musician, comedian and producer; founder of Foxxhole Productions (multiyear first-look deal with Fox Entertainment Studios)
profile: Jamie Foxx (born Eric Marlon Bishop, 1967, Terrell, Texas) is an Oscar-winning actor (Ray) and Grammy-winning musician who started in stand-up and In Living Color. He has hosted and executive-produced Fox's Beat Shazam since 2017. In 2026 he returned to music with the single 'Somebody' and is producing and starring in new films, including Amazon MGM's 'Deadlocked'.

He was also the first quarterback at Terrell High to pass for more than 1,000 yards.

Outreach normally goes through his agency or publicist, and I did not verify their current contacts. Avoid his 2023 hospitalization. jamiefoxx.com was unreachable when I checked.

name: Ryan H. Saadi
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO, Tevogen Bio Holdings (NASDAQ: TVGN)
profile: Dr. Ryan Saadi, MD, MPH, spent nearly three decades in hospital administration, managed care and life-sciences leadership before founding Tevogen Bio in 2020, which went public via SPAC in 2024. Tevogen develops off-the-shelf allogeneic precision T-cell therapies (virology, oncology, neurology); he controls a majority of the voting stock.

deep_cut_fact: He was a 2019 PharmaVoice 'Red Jacket' honoree for challenging the status quo on equal access to healthcare; his motto for Tevogen is 'doing well by doing good.'
notes: Named to 2025 NJBIZ Power 100. Tevogen also runs an AI unit (Tevogen.AI) - possible data/AI angle. Social links are company accounts.

name: Giuseppina Albo
current_role: Group Chief Executive Officer, Hamilton Insurance Group, Ltd. (NYSE: HG, Bermuda) since January 2018
profile: Pina Albo is a Canadian-trained lawyer who spent about 25 years at Munich Re, rising from claims expert to its Board of Executive Management (P&C Europe and Latin America). She succeeded founder Brian Duperreault as CEO of Bermuda-based specialty insurer/reinsurer Hamilton in 2018 and took it public on the NYSE in 2023; her wealth is largely Hamilton equity.
interesting_fact: She began her career practising real estate, corporate finance and M&A law in Toronto before switching to insurance as a claims expert at Munich Re.
deep_cut_fact: Before law school at Osgoode Hall she earned a BA in Languages from the University of Winnipeg, and she also holds a Maitrise en Droit in international and European Community law from Universite d'Aix-Marseille III in Aix-en-Provence.
notes: Goes by 'Pina'. Media contact is Kelly Corday Ferris; IR is Darian Niforatos. Advocate for women in insurance (ambassador, Insurance Supper Club); NIC Canada keynote speaker.

name: Shai Yeshayahu Weil
current_role: Independent Director (Compensation Committee), Enlight Renewable Energy (NASDAQ/TASE: ENLT); chairman of Har Tuv Group, Lumen Capital, Essence Partners and Minrav Group
profile: Dr. Shai Weil, an Israeli investor and executive, has sat on Enlight Renewable Energy's board since November 2009. He is an executive/partner in companies across industry, tech, real estate and services (Milgam, Pango, AllCloud, Minrav, Israel Post) and chairs Har Tuv Group, Lumen Capital, Essence Partners and Minrav.
interesting_fact: He joined Enlight's board in November 2009, making him one of the longest-serving directors of what is now one of Israel's largest renewable-energy companies.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a doctorate (D.P.S.) in International Business and Management from Pace University in New York, plus an M.S. from Boston University, and sits on the board of JGIVE, a nonprofit dedicated to cultivating a culture of philanthropy in Israel.
notes: Net worth here is from SEC insider holdings (~$85M), not a billionaire. Not a public-facing figure; best route is Enlight's corporate contact form or via the companies he chairs. The 20-F's only listed contact is the General Counsel (not used here as a press route).

name: John Belizaire
current_role: CEO and Director, Soluna Holdings (NASDAQ: SLNH)
profile: Serial software entrepreneur (founded Theory Center, sold to BEA Systems, and FirstBest Systems, sold to Guidewire) and former Intel architect, Belizaire co-founded Soluna Computing, which builds data centers co-located with wind and solar farms to use curtailed renewable power. Soluna merged into Mechanical Technology Inc. in 2021 and he became CEO of Soluna Holdings in 2023, now pivoting to AI/HPC hosting.
interesting_fact: Soluna's flagship wind-powered West Texas campus, Project Dorothy, is named after Dorothy Vaughan, one of NASA's 'Human Computers', and soaks up curtailed power from a 150 MW wind farm.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding his first company he was lead architect for Intel's Digital Enterprise Group; he holds a BS and MEng in Computer Science from Cornell.

public_contacts.value: hello@soluna.io (listed for Investor Relations and Media, 2024)
West of Fairfax (PR agency named on Soluna press releases)

notes: Ideal guest for energy + data-center podcast; frequent podcast guest and speaker (e.g. Bigger Than Us #184, Through The Noise). Very approachable via Soluna PR.

name: A B Krongard
current_role: Director, Iridium Communications (since 2009) and Apollo Global Management; former Executive Director of the CIA
profile: Alvin B. 'Buzzy' Krongard (b. 1936) spent 29 years in finance, rising to chairman and CEO of Alex. Brown & Sons (the oldest US investment bank) and vice chairman of Bankers Trust after their merger. He then served at the CIA as counselor to the DCI and, from 2001-2004, as Executive Director (the agency's COO). He now sits on the boards of Iridium and Apollo.
interesting_fact: A former Marine Corps infantry officer, he went from running Wall Street's oldest investment bank to being the CIA's No. 3 official, effectively its chief operating officer, in 2001.
deep_cut_fact: A Princeton philosophy major (A.B. 1958, senior thesis 'The Nature and Meaning of Religious Propositions') and lacrosse player, he was inducted into the National Lacrosse Hall of Fame in 1980; its bio says he 'was captain of every team on which he ever played.'
notes: Turns 90 in Oct 2026; long-time Baltimore figure (Mount Washington Lacrosse Club). Very private; no personal channels. Iridium (satellite comms) angle may suit the podcast. Avoid 9/11-trading and Blackwater topics referenced on his Wikipedia page.

name: Robert Lawrence Seelig
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Counsel (also handles Investor Relations), White Mountains Insurance Group
profile: Rob Seelig joined Bermuda-domiciled, Hanover NH-based insurance holding company White Mountains in 2002 from law firm Cravath, Swaine & Moore. He is its EVP and General Counsel and also its investor-relations contact. His wealth comes from long-tenured equity compensation at a company whose shares trade above $1,500.
interesting_fact: He doubles as White Mountains' general counsel and its investor-relations voice, unusual for a large-cap insurer, and is the named contact on the company's earnings releases.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three degrees from different schools: an undergraduate degree from Duke, an MBA from Duke's Fuqua School of Business, and a law degree from the University of Chicago Law School. He practised at Cravath before going in-house in 2002.
notes: As IR lead he is directly reachable through White Mountains' investor-relations channel (named on earnings releases with an office phone). The email on the bio page is obfuscated and was not reconstructed. He is a lawyer/executive rather than an entrepreneur, so the podcast fit is weak.

name: Joshua Ian Weinstein
current_role: CEO, Carnival Corporation Ltd.; director, Chipotle Mexican Grill; Chairman, Cruise Lines International Association
profile: New York-born lawyer (Penn; NYU Law) who joined Carnival's legal department in 2002 and rose through treasurer (2007-17), president of Carnival UK (P&O Cruises, Cunard) and COO before becoming CEO in August 2022. He steered the post-COVID restart of a 90-plus-ship, eight-brand fleet carrying about 13.5M guests a year.

deep_cut_fact: Before Carnival he was a corporate associate at Skadden, Arps (1999-2001) and Greenberg Traurig (2001-02); he is also a trustee of the Perez Art Museum Miami.

name: Gilbert L. Baird Iii
current_role: Managing Partner, GreyLion (New York middle-market growth equity firm); former director of TheRealReal (2018 to Nov 2025)
profile: Gilbert 'Chip' Baird III is a private equity investor. He started in Merrill Lynch investment banking, then worked at The Beacon Group and was a partner at Weston Presidio. In 2012 he co-founded PWP Growth Equity at Perella Weinberg, which spun out as GreyLion in 2020 and which he co-leads with David Ferguson. He sat on TheRealReal's board from 2018 until November 2025.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Perella Weinberg's growth equity strategy and led its 2020 spin-out into an independent firm, GreyLion. He has served on the boards of more than 20 portfolio companies.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his private-equity career at The Beacon Group he focused on business and industrial services, energy and general manufacturing companies. He holds a BS in Finance and International Business from Penn State.
notes: Goes by 'Chip'. He resigned from TheRealReal's board on 17 Nov 2025 but consulted for the company through June 2026. GreyLion's general inbox is the best route.

name: Anirudh Devgan
current_role: President and CEO, Cadence Design Systems; director, Lam Research
profile: Anirudh Devgan has been CEO of Cadence, the chip-design (EDA) software leader, since December 2021, succeeding Lip-Bu Tan. An IIT Delhi and Carnegie Mellon PhD, he spent ~12 years at IBM Research and seven at Magma Design Automation before joining Cadence in 2012. He is pushing Cadence into AI-driven design, system simulation and data-center digital twins.
interesting_fact: He received the 2021 Phil Kaufman Award, EDA's top honor, and was elected to the US National Academy of Engineering in 2023; he has said 'almost any chip designed in the world is done so with Cadence software.'
deep_cut_fact: Born in New Delhi in 1969 to an IIT Delhi professor, he holds 27 US patents, won best-paper awards at DAC and ICCAD, became an IEEE Fellow (2007) for electrical analysis and simulation of ICs, and chaired the American Heart Association's 2023 Heart of the Bay campaign.
notes: Excellent data-center fit: Cadence's Reality Digital Twin platform models data-center power/cooling, and it partners with NVIDIA. Frequent conference speaker.

name: Jay J Jackson
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Abacus Global Management, Inc. (NYSE: ABX; formerly Abacus Life, Nasdaq: ABL), Orlando
profile: Jay Jackson is a life-settlements and longevity-finance specialist. He started at Franklin Templeton, co-founded Abacus Life Settlements in 2004, and ran the Fayerweather Street Life Fund and the Cambridge Life Management platform for Ken Froot's FDO Partners. He has led Abacus since 2016, took it public in 2023, and has expanded it into asset management, longevity data (Abacus Intel) and wealth advisory.
interesting_fact: According to Abacus, its life-settlements business has transacted more than $10 billion in face value of life insurance policies, buying policies from seniors and managing them as an alternative asset class tied to longevity.
deep_cut_fact: Outside work he sits on the Orlando Mayor's Committee on Livability and is an executive board member of the Senior Resource Alliance, an agency of the Florida Department of Elder Affairs.
notes: Media-friendly: he has spoken at Milken 2026 and on ICR's podcast. press@abacusgm.com is the best route.

name: D Bradley Childers
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Archrock, Inc. (NYSE: AROC), Houston
profile: Brad Childers (BA Claremont McKenna, JD USC) worked at Occidental Petroleum (1994-2002), then held senior roles at Universal Compression and Exterran. He has been CEO since 2011 of Archrock, the largest US provider of natural-gas contract compression, which was spun out of Exterran in 2015. He also chaired the Archrock Partners MLP until its 2018 merger into Archrock.

notes: Highly relevant to the energy theme (natural gas compression powering gas-fired generation for data centres). Low personal media profile; approach via Archrock IR/corporate communications. Age 61 per the 2026 proxy.

name: David Alan Kennedy

profile: David Kennedy (49) is a Dell lifer who joined in 1998 and rose through finance and sales operations: CFO of the Client Solutions Group (2017-20), COO of Global Sales (2020-23) and SVP Global Business Operations, Finance, before succeeding Yvonne McGill as CFO. notes: Low public profile outside earnings calls. Route via Dell media relations; same company contacts as Michael Dell's profile in lane 000.

He has run a 'buy-and-build' rollup of independent commercial laundry distributors (30+ acquisitions, including Girbau North America in 2025) aiming to build North America's largest such distributor.

name: Benjamin Wood

Cardinal Infrastructure Group bought ALGC for $245.5M in February 2026 to enter Georgia and South Carolina, and Wood became Cardinal's COO. Cardinal is a fast-growing Southeast civil and site-development contractor, a segment tied to the data-center and industrial build-out.

name: John F Rex
current_role: Strategic Advisor, UnitedHealth Group (since Sept 2, 2025); formerly President and CFO

deep_cut_fact: He is a certified public accountant with a dual bachelor's in accounting and economics from Brigham Young University and a Wharton MBA (finance), and also worked as a strategy and operations consultant.
notes: Role change confirmed in UNH 2026 proxy (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/731766/000110465926046125/tm261387-6_def14a.htm). UNH is under heavy media scrutiny; a strategic-advisor executive is unlikely to do press without corporate approval.

name: Daniel Patrick O'Day
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Gilead Sciences (since March 2019)
profile: Daniel O'Day runs Gilead Sciences, the HIV/antiviral and oncology biopharma, which he joined as chairman and CEO in 2019 after more than three decades at Roche, latest as CEO of Roche Pharmaceuticals (and earlier head of Roche Diagnostics). His wealth comes from Gilead equity compensation; he also serves on the boards of PhRMA and Georgetown University.
interesting_fact: Before Gilead he sat on the boards of Genentech, Flatiron Health and Foundation Medicine while at Roche, and he has served as board chair of the drug-industry trade group PhRMA.
deep_cut_fact: A Georgetown biology graduate, he started at Roche in 1987 in U.S. sales and marketing, earned his Columbia Business School MBA (class of '97) mid-career, and moved to Roche's Basel headquarters in 1998 before rising to run the pharma division.

name: Larry R Webb
current_role: Director, Cincinnati Financial Corporation (since 1979; Executive and Investment committees); retired president of Webb Insurance Agency Inc., Lima, Ohio

name: April S Arnzen

profile: April Arnzen (55) leads Micron's global people strategy and also oversees its global communications and marketing organisation and the Micron Foundation's philanthropy. profile: Houston energy lawyer and longtime lieutenant of Enterprise founder Dan Duncan. A former partner at Butler & Binion and Snell & Smith, he joined Enterprise as general counsel (c.1999), was President & CEO of Duncan Energy Partners (2006-10), and has served as Vice Chairman/director of the midstream giant's general partner.

profile: Argentine executive (b. 1958): IRSA financial director 1993-2001 and Darwin Inversiones partner before joining Pampa Energía, Argentina's largest integrated power company (generation, transmission, oil & gas, petrochemicals). name: Aman Joshi
current_role: Chief Commercial Officer, Bloom Energy (NYSE: BE), leading global sales and business development since Jan 2024
profile: Commercial chief at fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy, whose on-site solid-oxide power systems have become a go-to fast power source for AI data centers. He joined in 2024 after 20+ years at GE across GE Capital, Corporate, Aviation, Power and Vernova; his wealth figure reflects Bloom stock awards after the share price surge.
interesting_fact: From 2018 to 2024 he was global GM of GE's aeroderivative gas turbine business, working with utilities and policymakers; the same 'bring your own power' pitch now drives his fuel-cell sales to data-center developers.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an energy dealmaker he trained in finance and governance: he is a member of both the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India and the Institute of Company Secretaries of India, and held business-unit CFO roles at GE Vernova.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; strong fit for an energy/data-center podcast since he sells Bloom's data-center power deals. Route via Bloom media relations (Katja Gagen). Did not verify a personal LinkedIn (search budget exhausted).

name: Dawn E Hudson
current_role: Independent director, NVIDIA (since 2013; chairs Compensation Committee); former CMO of the NFL
profile: Marketing executive (b. ~1957) who spent 13 years at ad agencies (D'Arcy Masius Benton & Bowles, Omnicom), then ran Pepsi-Cola North America as President (2002) and CEO (2005-07), was Vice Chairman of The Parthenon Group (2009-14) and NFL Chief Marketing Officer (2014-18). Her wealth stems largely from NVIDIA stock earned as a director since 2013; she also sat on IPG's board until its Omnicom merger.

current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Oscar Health (NYSE: OSCR); Director and Audit Committee chair, SLM Corp (Sallie Mae)
profile: Scott Blackley is CFO of health insurer Oscar Health (since 2021, with a 2022-23 stint as Chief Transformation Officer), overseeing treasury, actuarial, capital management and IR. Previously he was CFO of Capital One (2016-2021) and its Controller/Principal Accounting Officer (2011-2016), after roles at Fannie Mae, the SEC and KPMG.
interesting_fact: He moved from CFO of Capital One, one of the largest US banks, to CFO of then-recently IPO'd tech-driven insurer Oscar Health in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Before corporate finance he worked at the US Securities and Exchange Commission (as well as Fannie Mae and KPMG); he holds a BS in Accounting from the University of Utah.
notes: Corporate finance executive, low personal media profile; health-insurance sector, weak fit for energy/data-center themes. Emails confirmed via SEC full-text search of Oscar press release filings.

name: S. Matthew Schultz
current_role: Co-founder, CEO & Chairman, CleanSpark Inc. (Nasdaq: CLSK)
profile: Utah-based financier turned energy entrepreneur who co-founded CleanSpark, steering it from biomass power and microgrid software into one of North America's largest bitcoin miners and now an AI data-center developer. CEO 2014-19, then executive chairman, he returned as CEO in August 2025; he says he has helped raise over $3.8bn in capital.
interesting_fact: CleanSpark began as an alternative-energy company converting biomass into power with a patented gasifier, then built microgrid software deployed notably at Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, before pivoting to bitcoin mining and AI data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before CleanSpark he chaired Pali Financial Group (1999-2003), helping early-stage public companies raise capital, and was a founding member and former vice president of the Utah Consumer Lending Association.
notes: Top podcast fit (energy + bitcoin mining + AI data centers). Frequent conference/podcast speaker (Blockworks events). Deep-cut sourced from aggregator bio (insidertrades) - cross-check with CleanSpark proxy. LinkedIn listed is the company page, not personal.

name: Theodore Xenohristos
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Concept Officer and director, CAVA Group, Inc. (NYSE: CAVA)
profile: Ted Xenohristos is a Greek-American restaurateur who co-founded the original CAVA Mezze full-service restaurant in Rockville, MD in 2006 with childhood friends. It evolved into the CAVA fast-casual Mediterranean chain, which has more than 400 locations and went public in 2023. As Chief Concept Officer he guards the menu and brand, which draw on his immigrant parents' Greek cooking.
interesting_fact: CAVA grew from one sit-down restaurant into a national chain of more than 400 fast-casual locations. Its 2023 IPO was one of the biggest restaurant debuts in years.
deep_cut_fact: The first CAVA opened in a former Russian bakery in Rockville, Maryland. The founders built it themselves with materials from discount and home-goods stores, and it ran with no marketing budget, signage or POS system, relying on free drinks, food and desserts to build word of mouth. 'We built that first restaurant with our bare hands.'
notes: He does guest podcasts readily (e.g. episode #340, 'CAVA, Mediterranean Food Defender'). The energy/data-center fit is weak, but he is a strong pure entrepreneurship story. Route via media@cava.com.

name: Shelley Simpson
current_role: President & CEO, J.B. Hunt Transport Services (since July 2024)
profile: Shelley Simpson joined J.B. Hunt in 1994 as an hourly customer service rep straight out of the University of Arkansas and rose through the ranks - creating its Integrated Capacity Solutions brokerage unit, becoming chief commercial officer (2017) and president (2022) - before succeeding John Roberts as CEO of the Fortune 500 freight carrier in 2024.
interesting_fact: She is one of the few Fortune 500 CEOs to have started at the company in an entry-level hourly job, climbing from customer service to CEO over 30 years.
deep_cut_fact: A Russellville, Arkansas native, she launched J.B. Hunt's ICS brokerage unit in 2007 with 18 employees; by 2014 it had 540 people and $535M+ revenue.
notes: Press contact is Brittnee Davie, VP Marketing, via press@jbhunt.com. Has done podcasts before (Be EPIC, FreightWaves events) - receptive to media. Guest on Walton College 'Be EPIC' podcast ep. 189: https://walton.uark.edu/be-epic-podcast/episodes/blooming-where-you-are-planted-with-shelley-simpson.php

name: Peter J Millones
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Counsel, Booking Holdings Inc. (BKNG)
profile: Peter Millones has been Booking Holdings' (formerly Priceline.com) top lawyer since January 2001 and an EVP since 2003, leading legal, compliance and privacy for the parent of Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, Kayak and OpenTable. He joined Priceline in March 2000 from Latham & Watkins as VP and Associate General Counsel, during the dot-com era.
interesting_fact: He has been general counsel of the same company for 25+ years - from Priceline.com in 2001 through its transformation into Booking Holdings - an unusually long tenure for a Fortune 500 GC; he is profiled by Chambers as an in-house leader.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Priceline.com in March 2000 - at the very peak of the dot-com bubble - leaving Latham & Watkins to become VP & Associate GC, and was promoted to General Counsel within ten months.
notes: Executive, not a founder; low public profile. Best route is Booking Holdings media relations (communications@). Weak fit for an entrepreneurship/energy podcast.

name: Eric Andersen
current_role: President & CEO, AIG (since June 1, 2026)
profile: Eric Andersen spent about three decades at Aon, as CEO of Aon Benfield (reinsurance), CEO of Aon Risk Solutions Americas and president of Aon from 2020 to 2025. He joined AIG as CEO-elect in February 2026 and succeeded Peter Zaffino as president and CEO on June 1, 2026, also joining AIG's board.
interesting_fact: He moved from the broker side (Aon) to run one of the world's largest insurers, an unusual crossover. Zaffino, his predecessor, had made a similar jump from Marsh/Guy Carpenter.
deep_cut_fact: A Colgate political-science graduate with a Fordham MBA, he serves on Colgate's Board of Trustees and on the board of Covenant House New Jersey, which serves young people facing homelessness.
notes: Newly installed CEO of a large insurer. Insuring data centers and energy transition risk is a possible podcast angle. Business Roundtable member. Route via AIG media relations.

name: Alejandro Chernacov
current_role: Strategic Planning and Investor Relations Officer, Vista Energy (NYSE/BMV: VIST) since Aug 2017
profile: Alejandro Cherñacov is a founding-team executive at Vista Energy, the Vaca Muerta shale oil producer launched in 2017 by ex-YPF CEO Miguel Galuccio. He was previously CFO of Jagercor Energy and IR officer at YPF. His wealth comes from Vista shares and options (~1.2M series A shares per the latest 20-F).
interesting_fact: He has been part of Vista since the SPAC-style vehicle was incorporated on 22 March 2017, helping take it from a blank-check company to one of Argentina's largest shale oil producers listed in New York and Mexico.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vista he spent years inside YPF's E&P department, ending up running upstream portfolio management across Argentina, Brazil and Bolivia; he holds an economics degree from Universidad de Buenos Aires, a finance master's from Di Tella, and a Stanford certificate in strategic decision and risk management.
notes: Name is spelled Cherñacov in filings. He personally runs Vista's IR function, so ir@vistaenergy.com reaches his team directly - a natural route. Accessible executive, regularly on earnings calls.

name: Daniel R Feehan
current_role: Chairman of the Board, FirstCash Holdings (Nasdaq: FCFS); director of Enova International (since 2011, chairs its compensation committee) and AZZ Inc. (AZZ chairman until Feb 2026)
profile: Fort Worth consumer-finance executive (age 75) who joined pawn lender Cash America in 1990 as CFO, then served as President/COO and CEO from 2000 to 2015, spinning off online lender Enova in 2014 and merging Cash America with First Cash in 2016. He now chairs FirstCash and sits on the boards of Enova and galvanizing/coil-coating firm AZZ.
interesting_fact: He served on AZZ's board since 2000 and chaired it until February 2026 — AZZ is a leading U.S. hot-dip galvanizer whose steel coatings go into power transmission and data-center/industrial infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: A Texas A&M accounting graduate (BBA), he has been recognised as a Distinguished Alumnus of Texas A&M University.
notes: Board-level director rather than operator now; low media profile. contact@enova.com is Enova's general company address, not personal. The 'AZZ since 2000' date is from a Cash America-era SEC proxy summary; AZZ's power-grid/infrastructure angle may interest the podcast.

name: Ching Hang Shen
current_role: 10% owner of CapsoVision, Inc. (Nasdaq: CV), per SEC filings
profile: Taiwan-based investor who filed a Form 3 (event date 17 Mar 2026) as a 10%+ owner of CapsoVision, the Saratoga, CA maker of the CapsoCam capsule endoscope; he holds ~6.4M shares (12.8%), partly via Star One Global Capital Ltd, making him reportedly its largest individual shareholder. No public biography found.
notes: Private investor; no published contacts. Do not confuse with Ching Hsing Shen (chairman of Asia Vital Components) - link unverified. 13G/A April 2026: https://www.secform4.com/13dg/2102304/0002102304-26-000002.html

name: Sarah London
current_role: CEO and Vice Chairman of the Board, Centene Corporation (CEO since March 2022)
profile: Healthcare-technology executive who leads Centene, the largest U.S. Medicaid managed-care insurer (~26m+ members). Harvard history & lit grad and Chicago Booth MBA; worked at health-analytics startup Humedica (acquired by Optum), became Optum Analytics' chief product officer and an Optum Ventures partner, then joined Centene in 2020 to run tech modernization before becoming CEO.
interesting_fact: Ranked No. 60 on Fortune's 2024 Most Powerful Women list; at Fortune Brainstorm Health in May 2024 she announced plans to help build nearly $1bn of affordable housing in low-income communities across eight states.
deep_cut_fact: She played Division I tennis at Harvard, and began her healthcare career at Health Leads, a social enterprise that connects patients with community resources like food and housing.
notes: Corporate media contact per Q1 2026 earnings release: Sara Garland, Chief Communications Officer (phone listed, no email) — https://app.edgar.tools/filing/1071739/0001071739-26-000099/a20260428ex991pressrelease.htm. Avoid: Centene's 2025 stock drop/guidance withdrawal. Business Roundtable member; frequent Milken/AHIP speaker.

name: Robert Piconi
current_role: Chairman, Co-Founder & CEO, Energy Vault Holdings (NYSE: NRGV)
profile: Piconi co-founded Energy Vault in 2017 at Bill Gross's Idealab with Swiss engineer Andrea Pedretti, first to store energy by crane-lifting heavy blocks. It went public via SPAC in Feb 2022 and now develops, owns and operates grid storage and power infrastructure, including for AI/data centers. Earlier roles: Amoco/BP, Bell Labs/Lucent/Alcatel, Danaher.
interesting_fact: Energy Vault's ~70 m test tower in Castione-Arbedo, Switzerland, used cranes to raise and lower 35-tonne blocks made with fly-ash cement, storing grid power as gravitational potential energy.
deep_cut_fact: Before energy storage he founded and ran several healthcare-service and diagnostic-imaging companies in Europe that were later acquired; in 2020 the World Economic Forum named him one of 15 global 'SDG Champions'. He holds a Kellogg MBA and Notre Dame BS/BBA degrees.
notes: Energy Vault now pitches an 'AI & Data Centers' offering, a direct fit for the podcast's energy + data-center theme. Public, media-friendly CEO.

name: Mark W. Jenkins
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Carvana Co. (since July 2014)
profile: Carvana's CFO since 2014, recruited by CEO Ernie Garcia III; besides finance he oversees strategic planning, Carvana's lending platform, marketing distribution and the data science behind vehicle acquisition and pricing. He helped steer Carvana's 2023-24 debt restructuring and turnaround to profitability. Wealth is from Carvana equity.
interesting_fact: He told Fortune Carvana's comeback rested on a three-step plan: drive operating efficiency, restore profitability, then return to growth.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining a startup as CFO, he was a Wharton finance professor (2009-14) researching consumer and corporate credit markets, with a Stanford economics PhD and a Duke B.S.E. in mathematics and civil engineering.
notes: Low personal media profile; best route is Carvana communications/IR.

name: Victor Nesi
current_role: Director, Stifel Financial Corp. (former Co-President and Head of the Institutional Group, 2014–2025)
profile: Victor J. Nesi is a veteran investment banker. He joined Stifel in 2009 and served as Co-President running the Institutional Group from 2014 until stepping back from operating duties on July 1, 2025, when he joined the board. He was previously Head of Americas Investment Banking at Merrill Lynch and global head of its TMT private equity group, and before that worked at Salomon Brothers and Goldman Sachs.
interesting_fact: Over a 35-year career he advised on strategic deals totalling more than $200 billion. He worked on the AT&T Wireless $10.6 billion tracking-stock carve-out, which was then the largest IPO in US history.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking, he practised corporate and securities law for four years at Shea & Gould, a once-prominent New York firm, after earning both his B.A. (1982) and J.D. (1985) at Georgetown.
notes: Now a non-executive director, so he may have more time for outside conversations. For press, Stifel's releases name Neil Shapiro as the media contact. He has a strong telecom and media banking background, which is relevant to data-center and infrastructure topics.

name: Robert C Pohlad
current_role: President & CEO, Pohlad Holdings (Dakota Holdings); independent director, PepsiCo
profile: Bob Pohlad, son of financier Carl Pohlad, has led the family's Pohlad Holdings since 1987 (real estate, automation/robotics, sports & entertainment) and was Chairman & CEO of PepsiAmericas until PepsiCo bought it in 2010. The family has owned the Minnesota Twins since 1984; he has been a PepsiCo director since 2015.
interesting_fact: PepsiAmericas, formed in 1998 from several independent bottlers, grew under his leadership into the second-largest bottler of PepsiCo products before PepsiCo bought it in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the University of Puget Sound Board of Trustees (signing its board reports as chair in 2018-2021), and was elected to Minnesota Public Radio's board of trustees in 2013.
notes: Arizona State grad (1976). Pohlad Holdings includes automation/robotics engineering businesses - possible industrial angle. Brothers Jim (Twins) and Bill (film producer) share equal ownership. No published personal contact; route via Pohlad Companies (Minneapolis) or PepsiCo corporate secretary.

name: Steven D Hovde
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Hovde Group (bank-focused investment bank); director and 10% owner, Coastal Financial Corp (CCB); chairman, Hovde Properties
profile: Steve Hovde co-founded Hovde Group in 1987, a boutique investment bank advising banks and thrifts on capital raising and M&A, and opened its Chicago office in 1988. He invests in banks alongside his brother Eric (controlling interest in Sunwest Bank; major holder of Seattle-area Coastal Financial, on whose board he has sat since 2011) and chairs Madison-based Hovde Properties.
interesting_fact: Before investment banking he was a CPA at Touche Ross in Chicago, then a real-estate lawyer at Rudnick & Wolfe (now DLA Piper), then regional general counsel of developer Vantage Companies.
deep_cut_fact: With his brother Eric he backs the Hovde Foundation, whose 'Hovde Homes' partner with children's homes in countries including Bolivia, Ghana, Malawi, Peru and Rwanda; it reports $19M+ granted to 170+ nonprofit partners.
notes: Law degree (cum laude) from Northwestern, BBA accounting from UW-Madison. Brother Eric Hovde is a political figure; keep outreach business-focused (bank M&A, fintech/BaaS via Coastal's CCBX).

name: Greg Warnock
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Mercato Partners (Salt Lake City); board member at MNTN (formerly SteelHouse)
profile: Utah venture investor who co-founded early-stage fund vSpring Capital and then growth-equity firm Mercato Partners (2007, with Alan Hall); his >10% MNTN stake comes via Mercato's early backing of SteelHouse, now ad-tech company MNTN. He also chaired the SPAC Mercato Partners Acquisition Corp and has sat on boards incl. Skullcandy, Fusion-io, Goal Zero and Domo.
interesting_fact: He holds a BS in Computer Science, an MBA and a PhD in Entrepreneurship and Venture Finance, all from the University of Utah's David Eccles School of Business.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Junto Partners, an education program that trains and mentors aspiring entrepreneurs, and has chaired the board of the Community Foundation of Utah.
notes: Active speaker/podcast guest in Utah startup scene. Mercato portfolio includes Goal Zero (portable solar power) - energy angle. Route via Mercato Partners.

name: Patrick Miles
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Alphatec Holdings / ATEC Spine (since Oct 2017)
profile: Pat Miles spent ~16 years at spine-surgery company NuVasive, rising to president, COO and vice chairman, and helped build its lateral-approach and nerve-monitoring franchise. In 2017 he took over near-insolvent Carlsbad rival Alphatec and has rebuilt it into a fast-growing 'approach-based' spine company (2026 revenue guidance ~US$880-890m), including buying EOS imaging.
interesting_fact: He took on Alphatec in 2017 when it had shrunk after selling its international business to Globus to stay solvent, betting he could rebuild the culture and innovation he had helped create at NuVasive - a turnaround now guiding to ~$890m revenue in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: As part of NuVasive's senior leadership with Alex Lukianov and Keith Valentine, he helped pick the cheetah as NuVasive's emblem to symbolize its commitment to innovation and customer responsiveness.
notes: Bought ~$1m of ATEC stock in Sept 2026 (Form 4). Earlier career: marketing director at ORATEC Interventions (2000-01). Route via ATEC IR.

name: Nicholas Dominic Cortezi
current_role: Director and Executive Committee member, Ryan Specialty Holdings (NYSE: RYAN)
profile: Nick Cortezi joined Baltimore wholesale insurance broker All Risks, Ltd. in 1987, became CEO in 1999, and grew it from about $1.7m to roughly $250m in revenue, making it the fourth-largest US wholesale broker. He sold it to Ryan Specialty in 2020 and has been on Ryan's board since 2021. He also sits on boards including Datacubed Health, Cintana Education and Vennpoint Real Estate.
interesting_fact: At the 2020 merger, All Risks was on track to place $2.6bn in premiums with 850+ staff across 27 locations, which he built from a small Baltimore brokerage.
deep_cut_fact: Trained in foreign policy rather than insurance: he earned a diploma at Johns Hopkins SAIS in Bologna (1987), a BA in International Relations from Johns Hopkins (1988), and later a Master's in International Public Policy from SAIS DC (2008). He is a Life Member of the Council on Foreign Relations and a member of Business Executives for National Security.
notes: Also a board observer at Accrete AI, a possible AI/data angle. Low public-media profile. He was President of the National Association of Professional Surplus Lines Offices in 2002-03.

name: Jason Zhang
current_role: President and Co-Founder, Applied Digital Corp. (NASDAQ: APLD) since Jan 2026; also President, Secretary and director of Base Electron
profile: Co-founder (2021) of Applied Digital, the Dallas-based builder of high-density AI/HPC data-center campuses, promoted from Chief Strategy Officer to President in Jan 2026. He also helps lead Base Electron, an affiliated independent power producer formed to build dedicated generation for AI data-center campuses. Harvard economics BA; earlier founded Valuefinder (2019), a tech advisory/investment firm.
interesting_fact: Base Electron, where he is president, was created in late 2025 to develop and operate dedicated power-generation infrastructure for high-density AI data center campuses - squarely at the energy/data-center intersection.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Applied Digital he was an investment analyst at Sequoia Capital (2017-19) covering AI, blockchain and digital infrastructure, and before that analyzed investments at MSD Capital, Michael Dell's family office (2015-17).

public_contacts.value: apld@gateway-grp.com (Gateway Group IR: Matt Glover, Ralf Esper)

notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast. Media route is JSA. The Hurun 'unicorn founder' tag in the input may refer to a different Jason Zhang - not verified.

name: Michael Torok
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, JEC Capital Partners; non-executive director, Amarin Corp (since April 2025)
profile: Boston College-trained finance professional (BS Accounting & Finance, MS Finance) who began at PricewaterhouseCoopers, then was CFO of semiconductor-equipment firm Integrated Dynamics Engineering until its sale to Aalberts. Since 2008 he has run JEC Capital Partners, a US/German investment firm. As an engaged shareholder he joined Amarin's board in April 2025 after pushing for a strategic review.
interesting_fact: He joined Amarin's board in April 2025, shortly after JEC and Bradley Radoff, together holding about 15 million shares, publicly urged the board to start a strategic review.
deep_cut_fact: Before investing full-time he was CFO (2006-09) of Integrated Dynamics Engineering, a semiconductor equipment technology company later acquired by Aalberts Industries. He has also sat on the board of Liberated Syndication (Libsyn), a podcast hosting and monetisation platform, since December 2022.
