notes: Low public profile, activist-style investor. The Libsyn board seat is a natural podcast hook (the Libsyn detail comes from secondary profiles such as fintool/MarketScreener). No published email was found for JEC Capital or Amarin IR.

name: Sachin Lawande
current_role: President and CEO, Visteon Corporation; independent director, Cognex
profile: Sachin Lawande has led Visteon, the Michigan-based automotive cockpit-electronics supplier, since June 2015, repositioning it around digital clusters, infotainment and in-vehicle compute (with NVIDIA and Qualcomm). Earlier he spent a decade at Harman International, rising to CTO and president of its infotainment division, after engineering roles at QNX, 3Com, U.S. Robotics and AT&T Bell Labs.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Visteon pushed beyond cars, launching D6Sigma, an edge-AI product line for industrial automation built with Qualcomm, and an edge-to-cloud AI platform for vehicles on NVIDIA technology.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he earned his bachelor's in electronics and telecommunications in India and a master's in electrical engineering at Southern Illinois University Edwardsville, and worked at AT&T Bell Labs and U.S. Robotics before moving into automotive software.
notes: Good AI-at-the-edge / compute angle. Undergrad institution given variously as Bombay University or Goa Engineering College - avoid naming it.

name: Michael N. Kennedy
current_role: CEO and President, Antero Resources (NYSE: AR) and Antero Midstream (NYSE: AM), Denver
profile: Michael Kennedy runs Antero Resources, one of the largest US natural gas and NGL producers in the Appalachian Basin, and its midstream affiliate. He joined Antero in 2013, was CFO of Antero Resources from 2021 to 2025, and then became CEO of both companies. Before Antero he was EVP and CFO of Forest Oil (2009-2013).
interesting_fact: Antero is a major Appalachian natural-gas supplier at a time when US gas demand is growing with LNG exports and power for AI data centers, which makes Kennedy a relevant voice on gas-for-data-center supply.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an Arthur Andersen auditor focused on the natural-resources industry, joined Forest Oil in 2001 in finance roles, and rose to its EVP and CFO by 2009. He holds an accounting degree from the University of Colorado Boulder.
notes: The IR email belongs to Dan Katzenberg, VP Investor Relations, as published on Antero's investor page. Strong fit for an energy and data-center podcast (Appalachian gas and data-center power demand). The SEC 'See Remarks' tag reflects his move from CFO to CEO.

name: Dean Phillips
current_role: Former U.S. Representative (D-MN-3, 2019-2025) and 2024 presidential candidate; entrepreneur/investor, Braver Angels advisory council
profile: Dean Phillips (b. 1969; Brown '91, Carlson MBA) ran family firm Phillips Distilling, where he helped build Belvedere Vodka (sold to LVMH) and launched Prairie Organic Vodka. He then chaired Talenti gelato (sold to Unilever in 2014). He served in Congress 2019-2025, challenged Biden in the 2024 primary, and now advocates political reform.
interesting_fact: He pioneered the organic vodka category with Prairie Organic Vodka. As chairman of Talenti gelato he oversaw its growth until Unilever bought it in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: In summer 1989, as a college student, he interned for Senator Patrick Leahy, playing on the intern softball team. Roll Call notes that path eventually led him to the Congressional Baseball Game. After Brown, his first job was two years at a bicycle-equipment startup, InMotion.
notes: Very media-accessible and does many podcasts. In 2025 he reportedly took a 'gap year' in Southern California and has said he will not run for Minnesota governor. I could not verify his current personal X/Substack handles; his campaign-era X account was widely used. His Wikidata net worth (~$77m, 2018) comes from congressional disclosures.

name: Ernest Scott Santi
current_role: Non-Executive Chairman, Illinois Tool Works; director, W.W. Grainger
profile: E. Scott Santi spent his whole career at Illinois Tool Works, rising to vice chairman (2008) and serving as CEO from 2012 through 2023. Under him ITW narrowed its portfolio and rolled out its 'ITW Business Model', lifting operating margins from about 16% to nearly 24% and more than tripling market value. He retired as an employee in March 2024 and remains non-executive chairman.
interesting_fact: He became CEO in November 2012 after the death of his predecessor David Speer, and went on to lead ITW for about 11 years.
deep_cut_fact: He began at ITW as a summer intern in 1982 and spent four decades there, eventually as CEO.
notes: Board chairs can be reached via ITW Corporate Secretary (ITWCorporateSecretary@itw.com per investor contacts page). Low-key, rarely gives interviews.

name: Hassane El-Khoury
current_role: President & CEO and Director, onsemi (ON Semiconductor, Nasdaq: ON)
profile: Hassane El-Khoury (46) has run onsemi since December 2020, refocusing it on intelligent power and sensing chips - silicon-carbide power devices for EVs, energy infrastructure and AI data centers. Before that he spent 13 years at Cypress Semiconductor, becoming CEO in 2016 and leading it until its sale to Infineon in 2020. His wealth is in onsemi equity.
interesting_fact: He joined Cypress Semiconductor in 2007 as a staff application engineer and was its president and CEO within nine years (2016); he led Cypress until its sale to Infineon in April 2020, then took the top job at onsemi that December.
deep_cut_fact: He immigrated to the US from Lebanon at 17, earned a BS in electrical engineering from Lawrence Technological University and a master's in engineering management from Oakland University (Michigan), started as a senior design engineer at Continental Automotive Systems, and chairs the board of 3D-display company Leia Inc.
notes: Accessible, media-active public-company CEO; strong fit for an energy/data-center episode (SiC power, AI data-center power). Route via onsemi media relations; his LinkedIn is linked from onsemi's own leadership page.

name: Anders Gustafsson
current_role: Chair of the Board, Zebra Technologies (ZBRA); director of NetApp (NTAP) and International Paper (IP), where he chairs the audit committee
profile: Swedish-born executive Anders Gustafsson was CEO of Zebra Technologies from 2007 to March 2023, turning the barcode-printer maker into an enterprise mobile-computing and data-capture company. He is now Zebra's chair. Before Zebra he was CEO of Spirent Communications (2004-07) and held executive roles at Tellabs and Motorola. He also sits on the NetApp and International Paper boards.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership, Zebra bought Motorola Solutions' Enterprise division (including Symbol Technologies and Psion) for $3.45 billion in 2014. The deal turned Zebra into a major player in rugged mobile computers.
deep_cut_fact: He is an engineer by training, with an MSc in electrical engineering from Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg, Sweden, plus a Harvard MBA. He is also a trustee of Chicago's Shedd Aquarium and on the Commercial Club of Chicago's Civic Committee.
notes: Chicago-based. His NetApp board seat ties in with the data-center and storage theme. The Zebra press contact (Therese Van Ryne, Sr Director External Communications) and IR email appear in the 2026 press releases; I saw them via search snippets, not a direct page fetch.

name: Ganesh Moorthy
current_role: Chair of the Board, Ralliant Corp. (NYSE: RAL); director of GlobalFoundries, SiTime, Celanese and Ayar Labs; retired President & CEO of Microchip Technology (2021-Nov 2024)
profile: Semiconductor executive who spent 23 years at Microchip Technology (2001-2024), rising to President & COO in 2016 and President & CEO in 2021 before retiring in November 2024. He now chairs Fortive spin-off Ralliant and sits on the boards of GlobalFoundries (since Jan 2026), SiTime (since Oct 2025), Celanese and optical-I/O startup Ayar Labs.
interesting_fact: He sits on the board of Ayar Labs, a private startup building optical (light-based) chip-to-chip I/O aimed at AI data-centre bottlenecks, alongside public boards spanning chip foundry (GlobalFoundries) and timing chips (SiTime).
deep_cut_fact: He holds two bachelor's degrees - a B.S. in Physics from the University of Bombay and a B.S. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Washington - plus a marketing MBA from National University.

public_contacts.value: Board of Directors of Ralliant Corporation (attn: Chair), c/o Corporate Secretary, 4114 Center at North Hills Street, Suite 400, Raleigh, NC 27609

notes: Input lists him as Microchip CEO, but he retired from that role in Nov 2024 (Steve Sanghi succeeded). Strong data-centre/AI-hardware angle via GlobalFoundries and Ayar Labs boards. No personal social accounts verified.

name: Philip Andrew Smith
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, StoneX Group Inc. (since December 2024)
profile: UK-based financial-services executive who joined FX payments firm Global Currencies in 1996; after StoneX (then INTL) bought it in 2004 he ran INTL Global Currencies, then led the group's EMEA (and from 2015 Asia) operations as CEO of StoneX Financial Ltd. He became Group CEO of StoneX, the Nasdaq-listed commodities, FX and securities broker, in December 2024.
interesting_fact: He came into StoneX through an acquisition: Global Currencies, a UK foreign-exchange payments company he joined in 1996, was bought by the group in 2004 - two decades later he was running the whole company.
deep_cut_fact: He was elected to Global Currencies' board in 1999, just three years after joining the small UK FX payments firm.

public_contacts.value: kevin.murphy@stonex.com (Kevin Murphy, investor inquiries, as published in StoneX earnings releases)
Linked from his official StoneX leadership bio

notes: StoneX is a major commodities/energy-markets broker - relevant to energy topics. Based in London.

name: Scott C Donnelly
current_role: Executive Chairman, Textron Inc. (since Jan 4, 2026); Director, Medtronic plc
profile: Scott Donnelly (b. 1961) was CEO of Textron, maker of Bell helicopters, Cessna and Beechcraft aircraft and Textron Systems, from Dec 2009 to Jan 2026, and chairman since 2010; Lisa Atherton succeeded him as CEO and he became Executive Chairman. Before Textron he spent ~19 years at GE, rising to CEO of GE Aviation and head of GE Global Research.
interesting_fact: Before running a jet-engine business he ran one of the world's biggest industrial labs: he was senior VP and director of GE Global Research before becoming president & CEO of GE Aviation, then joined Textron as COO in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He is an electronics engineer by training: his first GE job (1989) was manager of Electronics Design Engineering for GE's Ocean Systems Division in Syracuse, NY, followed by engineering roles in Australia and the US; he has also served on Cornell and Stanford engineering advisory committees.

public_contacts.value: Textron media contact Michael Maynard (phone published, no email)

notes: Good fit for aerospace/eVTOL/engineering topics (Bell, Pipistrel electric aircraft). Route via Textron corporate communications; general enquiries inbox is generic.

name: William L Meaney
current_role: President & CEO, Iron Mountain (NYSE: IRM); director, State Street Corp.
profile: New Hampshire-born engineer (RPI) and Carnegie Mellon Tepper MSIA (1986) who did turnarounds at South African Airways and Swiss International Air Lines, then tripled sales at Hong Kong's Zuellig Group as its first non-family CEO. Since 2013 he has transformed Iron Mountain from records storage into a fast-growing data-center, digital and asset-lifecycle business.
interesting_fact: Under Meaney, Iron Mountain's data-center, digital and asset-lifecycle businesses collectively grew more than 40% in 2025, and the company entered 2026 on the back of strong data-center leasing.
deep_cut_fact: As a teenager he worked summer jobs for the Morrell family at Story Land, the New Hampshire theme park - an experience he lists among the four that shaped him. He tells his team to 'become comfortable being uncomfortable' and likens international business to 'three-dimensional versus two-dimensional chess'.
notes: Top-priority fit for a data-center podcast (Iron Mountain Data Centers is a major colocation/hyperscale developer). Route via media@ironmountain.com.

name: Scott Dietzen
current_role: CEO, Augment Code (AI coding); director (former chairman/CEO), Everpure (formerly Pure Storage)
profile: Carnegie Mellon PhD in computer science who co-founded or helped build Transarc, WebLogic (CTO of BEA after its acquisition) and Zimbra (sold to Yahoo). As CEO of Pure Storage 2010-2017 he took the all-flash storage company through its 2015 IPO, then served as chairman. Since 2023 he has led Augment Code, an enterprise AI coding-agent company.
interesting_fact: He took Pure Storage (now Everpure), a key supplier of flash storage for data centers, from startup to its 2015 IPO as CEO.
deep_cut_fact: He did all three degrees at Carnegie Mellon (BS applied math/CS, MS and PhD in CS with a machine-learning emphasis) - decades before applying ML to code at Augment.

public_contacts.value: Frequent podcast guest, e.g. 'What the futr' ep. 2

notes: Very podcast-friendly (many recent appearances). Data-center angle via Pure/Everpure storage. One source calls him Augment executive chairman - confirm title. No published direct email found.

name: Frank Klein
current_role: Chief Operations Officer, Rocket Lab Corp (NASDAQ: RKLB), since Sept 2024
profile: German manufacturing executive with 30+ years in automotive: 27 years at Daimler/Mercedes-Benz (vehicle research, trucks, cars, VP of Mercedes-Benz Vans operations across 12 plants), president of contract manufacturer Magna Steyr, then COO of Rivian (2022-24). At Rocket Lab he scales Electron, Neutron and spacecraft/component production; wealth is from Rocket Lab equity awards.
interesting_fact: At Rivian he helped turn the EV start-up from low-volume production into a high-volume manufacturer with 9,000+ staff, before Peter Beck recruited him to bring automotive lean manufacturing to rockets and satellites.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in Germany's dual-study system, earning a master's in Electrical and Industrial Engineering from Baden-Wuerttemberg Cooperative State University Stuttgart plus a business degree from FernUniversitat in Hagen, and once ran Magna Steyr (13,000 staff on three continents).
notes: Good manufacturing-scaling story (cars to rockets). Education details partly from aggregator coverage of the Rocket Lab release. Low personal media profile.

name: Dirk Kersten
current_role: Managing Partner, Forbion (manages Forbion Growth Opportunities Fund); Director, Dyne Therapeutics (NASDAQ: DYN)
profile: Dutch life-sciences venture investor and physicist by training. Joined Forbion in 2018 after leading Gilde Healthcare's Boston office and running healthcare investing at INKEF Capital. He led investments in Dyne Therapeutics, Ascendis Pharma, Profibrix, Lanthio Pharma and Nightbalance, and sits on the boards of Dyne, SynOx and NorthSea Therapeutics.
interesting_fact: He led Forbion's investment in Dyne Therapeutics' $50M Series A in 2019 alongside Atlas Venture and MPM, and has stayed on Dyne's board through its Nasdaq listing.
deep_cut_fact: A physicist by training, he led the investment in Nightbalance, a Dutch sleep-positioning device startup later acquired by Philips.
notes: Appears in SEC data as Dyne director (Forbion fund holdings), likely not personally UHNW. Biotech VC - limited fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Roger Fradin
current_role: Independent director, Vertiv Holdings (Compensation Committee chair), L3Harris and Janus International (Vice Chairman); consultant to The Carlyle Group
profile: Veteran industrial executive (age 72) who ran Honeywell's Automation and Control Solutions business as CEO from 2004 to 2014 and was Honeywell Vice Chairman until retiring in 2017. He helped bring data-center power/cooling leader Vertiv public as a director of SPAC GS Acquisition Holdings (2018-2020) and has sat on Vertiv's board since 2020.
interesting_fact: He arrived at Honeywell in 2000 through its acquisition of Pittway Corporation; he has since chaired Carlyle-owned Victory Innovation and served on the boards of Resideo, MSC Industrial, Pitney Bowes and SPAC Juniper II.
deep_cut_fact: He earned both his B.S. and MBA at the Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, where he has also served as a member of the faculty.
notes: No personal or office contact published. As a board member rather than executive, the only formal route is via the corporate secretary of Vertiv/L3Harris/Janus. Strong data-center angle via Vertiv. Wealth estimate (~$75M) from SEC insider holdings.

name: Matthew C. Bonner
current_role: Director of DCM International IV and IX (general-partner entities of DCM Ventures funds), Menlo Park; DCM's Section 16 filer/attorney-in-fact
profile: Matthew C. Bonner appears in SEC filings as one of two directors (with DCM co-founder Frank Hurst Lin, a GigaCloud board member) of the ultimate general partners of venture firm DCM's Fund IV and IX entities. Those funds own more than 10% of GigaCloud Technology (Nasdaq: GCT), a B2B e-commerce marketplace for large-parcel goods. The ~$74M figure reflects fund holdings he may be deemed to share voting power over, not personal wealth.
interesting_fact: In the GigaCloud filings he signs as attorney-in-fact for every DCM entity and for Frank Hurst Lin, suggesting a finance/operations or legal role at DCM rather than an investing partner.
notes: Not a UHNW founder: he is an SEC 'ten percent owner' only via DCM fund entities and disclaims beneficial ownership beyond his pecuniary interest. Not listed on DCM's public team page. GigaCloud is not a data-center company despite the tag. Low priority for the podcast; Frank Hurst Lin (DCM co-founder) is the more relevant figure.

name: Iv L P Dcm
current_role: Not a person. 'DCM IV, L.P.' is a venture fund managed by DCM (Menlo Park, CA) and was a >10% holder of GigaCloud Technology (NASDAQ: GCT).
profile: This record is the venture fund DCM IV, L.P. and its affiliate fund, not an individual; the name is a scrambled SEC filer name. DCM is a US-Asia venture firm headquartered on Sand Hill Road. DCM IV was GigaCloud's earliest institutional investor and has been selling down its stake since the 2022 IPO (13D/A amendments in 2024).
interesting_fact: DCM IV backed GigaCloud from the start. In September 2006 it and DT Ventures lent the startup $600,000 at 7.04%, then bought Series A preferred at $50/share for $6.1M in November 2006 and converted the loans into equity.

public_contacts.value: contact@dcm.com (DCM general enquiries; hello@dcm.com for pitches)

notes: This is a fund entity, not an individual, so exclude it from the people list or map it to DCM's partners. The SEC 13D contact person for DCM is Matthew C. Bonner (c/o DCM, 2420 Sand Hill Road). The relevant human at the portfolio company is GigaCloud founder Larry Wu.

name: Steven Vassallo
current_role: General Partner, Foundation Capital; Director, Cerebras Systems (Nasdaq: CBRS) since May 2016
profile: Foundation Capital general partner since 2007 and former product designer at IDEO, Immersion and Ning. He led Foundation's investments in Cerebras (the firm says it wrote Cerebras' first term sheet in 2016), Stripe, Sunrun, Control4 and Framer, co-leads its crypto practice, and was No. 17 on Forbes' 2026 Midas List. Cerebras IPO'd in May 2026.
interesting_fact: He sat on Sunrun's board from 2008 to 2019, backing the residential-solar company long before its IPO, and has served on the Cerebras board since its founding-era 2016 round; he wrote about 'a nineteen-year relationship' with the Cerebras founders.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup was 'Steve's Snowblowing Service', launched at age 13; as an IDEO design engineer he later developed products for Cisco, Nike, BMW and Caterpillar and his design work earned him 77+ patents and BusinessWeek's Design of the Decade award. He wrote the book 'The Way to Design'.
notes: Good fit for data-center/AI angle (Cerebras wafer-scale AI chips) and energy angle (early Sunrun investor). Writes publicly (Foundation Capital 'Perspectives' essays, e.g. 'A decade with Cerebras'). Email is linked from his official Foundation Capital profile.

name: Nicholas Sheridan Lewin
current_role: Chairman of the Board, Establishment Labs Holdings (Nasdaq: ESTA); private investor; director of Allurion Technologies
profile: Nicholas Lewin, 48, has been a private investor since 2000. He backs companies with innovative technology and strong IP, sometimes in activist situations where he works with management. He joined the board of Costa Rica-founded breast-implant maker Establishment Labs in 2015 and has chaired it since 2017. The company reported 34% revenue growth and its first positive free cash flow in Q3 2026.
interesting_fact: His board seats range well beyond medtech: from 2022 to 2025 he was a director of GameSquare Holdings, including its predecessor FaZe Holdings, the parent of esports and creator brand FaZe Clan. He also sat on the board of aesthetics-device maker Cutera.
deep_cut_fact: He studied political science at Johns Hopkins University, not finance or engineering, and has invested on his own account since 2000 rather than through a big fund.
notes: Low public profile with few interviews. The Establishment Labs investor/media contact (Malavika William) is the only published route; it belongs to the company, not to him. Not an energy or data-centre fit, but relevant as an activist-style tech investor.

name: Diane N Landen
current_role: Director, Murphy USA Inc. (NYSE: MUSA); Owner & President, Vantage Communications; Vice Chairman & EVP, Noalmark Broadcasting (El Dorado, Arkansas)
profile: El Dorado, Arkansas businesswoman who started her career at Murphy Oil in 1996. She has sat on the Murphy USA board since its 2013 spin-off, chairing nominating and governance. She owns Vantage Communications (investments, broadcast properties), is Vice Chairman of Noalmark Broadcasting (radio in Arkansas and New Mexico), and is a partner in oil and gas firm Munoco Company.
interesting_fact: She has been a director since Murphy USA was spun out of Murphy Oil in 2013, a period in which the El Dorado-based fuel retailer, which runs stations near Walmarts, grew into a Fortune 500 company.
deep_cut_fact: Besides fuel retail she has a radio business: she is Vice Chairman and EVP of Noalmark Broadcasting, which runs radio stations in Arkansas and New Mexico. She is also Secretary of Loutre Land and Timber Company.
notes: Private, low-profile director with no media presence found. The only published route is Murphy USA IR (Christian Pikul, VP IR; Ash Aulds also listed). The MUSA board page fetched may be partly out of date.

name: Viswas Raghavan
current_role: Head of Banking (investment, corporate and commercial banking) and Executive Vice Chair, Citigroup
profile: 'Vis' Raghavan is an India-raised investment banker who spent 24 years at J.P. Morgan, mostly in London, rising from equity-linked capital markets to global co-head of investment banking. CEO Jane Fraser recruited him to Citi in 2024 to run its combined banking businesses, and he has since brought over about 15 senior bankers to rebuild Citi's M&A franchise.
interesting_fact: Citi offered a reported $40m package to hire him from J.P. Morgan in 2024, and he is widely seen as a potential successor to Jane Fraser.
deep_cut_fact: He studied physics at the University of Bombay before earning a dual degree in electronic engineering and computer science at Aston University in Birmingham, UK, and started his banking career at Lehman Brothers. He is also a keen professional-cricket follower.
notes: Rarely gives interviews. Requests would go through Citi corporate communications (newsroom). No published press email was found in recent Citi 8-K releases.

name: Nello Mainolfi
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Kymera Therapeutics (Nasdaq: KYMR), Watertown, MA
profile: Nello Mainolfi, PhD, founded Kymera Therapeutics, a pioneer of targeted protein degradation making oral 'degrader' drugs for immunology. Kymera has raised close to $3B and partnered with big pharma; in Oct 2026 it reported positive Phase 1 data for KT-579. He trained at Imperial College and Scripps and began at Novartis.
interesting_fact: He has authored more than 100 publications and patents, and says his favourite part of the day is digging into emerging data.
deep_cut_fact: At Novartis he led cross-functional teams that identified several investigational medicines, including iptacopan, the first-in-class factor B inhibitor later approved by the FDA.
notes: Founder-entrepreneur story (built Kymera from scratch, 'Ten Years of Kymera' blog). Biotech rather than energy; best route is the Kymera contact form, Media option.

name: Snehal Patel
current_role: CEO, CFO and Director, Greenwich LifeSciences (NASDAQ: GLSI), Stamford CT
profile: Biotech executive and former healthcare investment banker (JP Morgan Chase, Sanders Morris Harris, Ferghana Partners) who runs Greenwich LifeSciences, a clinical-stage company developing GLSI-100 (GP2), a HER2 peptide immunotherapy aimed at preventing breast-cancer recurrence, now in the Phase III FLAMINGO-01 trial.
interesting_fact: He doubles as both CEO and CFO of the Nasdaq-listed company while it runs a global Phase III trial (FLAMINGO-01).
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer - BS in chemical engineering and MS in biochemical engineering from MIT - and early on worked in operations at Bayer and advised on disposable biotech manufacturing equipment and scale-up.
notes: Off-theme for energy/data centers; entrepreneurship angle only. No dedicated press/IR email published.

name: Brittany Bagley
current_role: Chief Operating Officer & Chief Financial Officer, Axon Enterprise (AXON); Director, Aurora Innovation (AUR)
profile: Brittany Bagley is COO and CFO of Axon (TASER, body cameras, evidence software), which she joined in 2022 from Sonos, where she was CFO from 2019. Before that she spent over a decade at KKR (Managing Director) after starting as a Goldman Sachs analyst. She chairs the audit committee of self-driving truck company Aurora Innovation.
interesting_fact: Sat on Sonos' board as a KKR investor (2017-2019) before switching sides to become Sonos' CFO in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Graduated magna cum laude in Economics from Brown University and began her career as a Goldman Sachs analyst before joining KKR in 2007.
notes: Operator-CFO with autonomy angle (Aurora board) - fits entrepreneurship/tech podcast. Route via Axon press office.

name: John T Stankey
current_role: Chairman and CEO, AT&T Inc.
profile: Lifer telecom executive who joined Pacific Bell in 1985 in an entry-level job and rose through SBC/AT&T (CIO, CEO of WarnerMedia 2018-20) to AT&T CEO in July 2020. He unwound AT&T's media bets (WarnerMedia, DirecTV) and refocused on fiber and 5G, buying Lumen's consumer fiber business ($5.75bn, closed Feb 2026) and ~$23bn of EchoStar spectrum.
interesting_fact: Under Stankey AT&T partnered with AST SpaceMobile on satellite-to-phone service and committed $3bn to closing the US digital divide after federal broadband subsidies lapsed in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: He and his wife Shari, both Loyola Marymount alumni (he is LMU '85, finance), endowed the John and Shari Stankey Fellowship, LMU's first faculty fellowship with an interdisciplinary requirement, linking journalism, media, computer science and business (up to $50k/yr).

public_contacts.value: https://about.att.com/ (AT&T corporate newsroom; media contacts page)

notes: Very high-profile Fortune 50 CEO; outreach via AT&T Corporate Communications. AT&T is a large data-center/fiber player, so it fits the podcast. The media-contacts page blocked automated fetch, so check it manually. LA native, son of an insurance underwriter.

name: Jason Chung
current_role: Chief Financial Officer (since March 1, 2026; formerly EVP, Head of Corporate Development & Strategy), Riot Platforms
profile: Former Nomura M&A managing director who joined bitcoin miner Riot Platforms in June 2022 to run corporate development, capital markets and IR, becoming EVP in 2023. Promoted to CFO effective March 2026 as Riot pushes to convert its large Texas power footprint into AI/HPC data-center capacity.
interesting_fact: His CFO promotion was framed around Riot's pivot to AI/high-performance computing, leveraging its large power-secured Texas sites (e.g. Corsicana) for data-center use.
deep_cut_fact: Before Riot he was a Managing Director in M&A at Nomura (2017-2022); he is a CFA charterholder with a Bachelor of Commerce from the University of Toronto.
notes: Highly relevant to energy/data-center podcast (bitcoin mining to AI/HPC conversion). Has spoken at Consensus Hong Kong. Media contact listed: Becca Rincon; IR: Joshua Kane.

name: Richard S. Swartz Jr.
current_role: President & CEO, MYR Group Inc. (MYRG), Henderson NV / Rolling Meadows IL
profile: Rick Swartz has spent his whole career at MYR Group. He started in 1982 as an apprentice electrician at Sturgeon Electric, rose through management to COO, and has been CEO since 2017. MYR builds transmission lines, substations and commercial/industrial electrical systems, and in 2026 it agreed to buy Valley Electric and Comet Electric for about $328m.
interesting_fact: MYR Group, which he runs, is a major US grid contractor building high-voltage transmission lines and substations. That puts it at the centre of the power build-out for data centers and renewables.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 1982 as an apprentice electrician for Sturgeon Electric, an MYR subsidiary, and worked his way up to CEO of the whole group about 35 years later.
notes: A strong energy and data-center guest: he came up from the tools and now runs a grid-construction contractor. The apprentice-electrician detail comes from a MYR executive quote in search snippets; the MYR IR page blocked direct fetch.

name: Richard William (Rick) Svetkoff
current_role: Former founder/CEO/Executive Chairman of Starfighters Space, Inc. (NYSE American: FJET); resigned 19 Feb 2026; remains ~19% holder
profile: Founder and long-time leader of Starfighters (Kennedy Space Center, Florida), which flies the world's only commercial fleet of flight-ready Lockheed F-104 supersonic jets and is developing the 'StarLaunch' air-launch system for small payloads. He resigned all company roles in Feb 2026 but holds about 10.6m shares (~19%), the basis of his listed wealth.
interesting_fact: Starfighters operates the world's only commercial fleet of flight-ready F-104s, the first production aircraft to sustain Mach 2 in level flight and one NASA used for high-speed research. The company plans to use them to air-launch small rockets.
notes: CAUTION: a contested situation. He resigned in Feb 2026, and the company's 10-K and Nov 2026 proxy disclose litigation between him and Starfighters and allegations from an internal investigation. Not a good outreach target via the company. I found no published personal contact, and I did not record the home address that appears in SEC filings.

name: Paul Gu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (since May 1, 2026), Upstart Holdings, Inc. (UPST), San Mateo/Burlingame, CA
profile: Paul Gu co-founded AI lending marketplace Upstart in 2012 with ex-Google executive Dave Girouard and Anna Counselman, and as CTO led the machine-learning underwriting models that price personal, auto and home-equity loans for partner banks and credit unions. He succeeded Girouard as CEO on May 1, 2026 and has sat on the board since 2015.
interesting_fact: He left Yale, where he studied economics and computer science, to join Peter Thiel's Thiel Fellowship, which pays young people to skip college and build companies.
deep_cut_fact: His first earnings quote as CEO (Q3 2026) was a one-liner: 'Macro comes and goes, but alpha compounds,' as Upstart posted record contribution profit.
notes: New CEO (2026) and data/AI technologist, good fit for a data-centric episode. Contacts from Upstart's Q3 2026 earnings release (8-K Ex. 99.1, Nov 2026).

name: Fran Horowitz
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and Director, Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (NYSE: ANF); Director, Jersey Mike's Subs
profile: Retail merchant who spent 13 years at Bloomingdale's plus stints at Express and Ann Taylor LOFT before joining Abercrombie & Fitch in 2014 to run Hollister. CEO since February 2017, she led A&F's turnaround from its exclusionary-era image into one of retail's strongest comebacks; she also sits on the board of Jersey Mike's (Conagra board 2021-25).
interesting_fact: In 2026 the National Retail Federation named her 'The Visionary 2026' for building authentic, customer-centric retail brands.
deep_cut_fact: She started out in buying jobs at Bergdorf Goodman and the long-gone New York department store Bonwit Teller, after a liberal-arts degree from Lafayette College (1985) and a Fordham MBA (1990); she grew up attending high school in Armonk, NY.
notes: Professional CEO rather than founder; turnaround story is a strong podcast hook. Route via A&F public relations. Also on Jersey Mike's board (JMKE).

name: Chen Peihong
current_role: Vice President, Human Resources, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC); files SEC Form 4 as 'Chen Pei-Hung' (P.H. Chen)
profile: TSMC lifer: joined in 1990, held fab production-management roles, ran Fab 14A (2015-20), then led the Program Office (2020-25). Promoted to VP in Feb 2025, he now heads Human Resources as TSMC hires for AI-chip fabs in Arizona, Japan and Germany. Held ~433,000 TSMC shares (Mar 2026).
interesting_fact: He has spent more than 35 years at TSMC, having joined in 1990, only three years after the foundry was founded, and rose from fab production management to the vice-president ranks.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming HR chief he ran a fab himself: he was Senior Fab Director of Fab 14A in Tainan from 2015 to 2020. He trained as a chemist, with an M.S. in Chemistry from National Sun Yat-sen University.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; the Hurun Unicorn 2020 tag in the input looks like a mis-merge. TSMC tightly controls executive media access; route via TSMC corporate communications/IR. Good angle: talent and workforce for AI-chip fabs.

name: Earl A Steinert Jr
current_role: Director, Great Southern Bancorp (Nasdaq: GSBC), Springfield, Missouri; owner, EAS Investment Enterprises Inc.
profile: Earl A. Steinert Jr. (89 per the 2026 proxy) is a Springfield, Missouri accountant and real-estate investor who practised as a CPA from 1962 until retiring in 2006. He owns EAS Investment Enterprises, which owns and operates hotels in Springfield, previously ran apartment owner Mid-American Real Estate Partners, and has been a Great Southern Bancorp director since 2004.
interesting_fact: He practised public accounting for 44 years (1962-2006) while building a hotel and apartment portfolio in Springfield, Missouri on the side.
notes: Low-profile regional businessman; listed in 2026 proxy (filed Mar 2026), so alive as of then. Hospitality/real-estate and community banking; weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Only formal route is via Great Southern Bancorp corporate secretary.

name: Matthew J Desch
current_role: CEO & Director, Iridium Communications (IRDM); Director, VeriSign and Unisys
profile: Matt Desch has led satellite operator Iridium since 2006 (predecessor Iridium Holdings, then the listed company from 2009), steering the $3bn Iridium NEXT constellation replacement and growth into IoT, PNT and aviation surveillance (Aireon, acquired 2026). Earlier he was CEO of Telcordia (2002-05) and spent 13 years at Nortel, including as president of its global wireless business. Iridium agreed in 2026 to be acquired by Rocket Lab.
interesting_fact: In October 2026 Iridium completed its acquisition of Aireon and won stockholder approval for its pending acquisition by Rocket Lab, which Desch called 'an important milestone in creating a next generation space powerhouse'.
deep_cut_fact: A computer-science graduate of Ohio State (MBA, University of Chicago), he sits on the President's National Security Telecommunications Advisory Committee (NSTAC).
notes: Role may change on closing of the Rocket Lab acquisition - check status before outreach. Desch is an active, accessible public speaker on space/telecom; strong podcast fit.

name: Matthew Richard Crocker
current_role: Vice President (corporate officer), Exxon Mobil Corporation, since May 1, 2025
profile: Matt R. Crocker (52 per the FY2025 10-K) is a long-time ExxonMobil executive. He ran Fuels & Lubricants (SVP, 2020-22), then served as SVP of Strategy, Product and New Assets in Low Carbon Solutions (2022-23). He led Global Business Solutions as President (2023-25) before being named a corporate Vice President in 2025.
interesting_fact: In 2022-23 he was SVP of Strategy, Product and New Assets at ExxonMobil Low Carbon Solutions, the unit behind its carbon-capture, hydrogen and lithium push.
notes: Corporate executive (not a founder), with low public profile. His current VP portfolio is not specified in filings. ExxonMobil Media Relations publishes a phone line (737-272-1452) in its press releases; that is the realistic route. Energy/low-carbon background fits the podcast. The web-search budget was exhausted, so there was no deeper bio research.

name: Brandon Sim
current_role: CEO and President, Astrana Health, Inc. (Nasdaq: ASTH)
profile: Harvard-trained (AB Statistics & Physics, MS CS&E) technologist, age 32 per the 2026 proxy. He was a Citadel Securities quant researcher (2015-19) before joining Astrana (formerly ApolloMed), the LA-based value-based care and physician-network company co-founded by his father Dr. Kenneth Sim. He rose from VP Engineering/CTO/COO to co-CEO in 2021 and sole CEO in 2024, and is leading its tech-driven expansion.
interesting_fact: He went from building trading models at Citadel Securities to running a multi-billion-dollar healthcare company at around 30, overseeing Astrana's 'strategy, growth, operations and technology innovation'.
deep_cut_fact: As a Harvard undergraduate (2012-15) he co-founded and was CTO of Theratech, a medical-device startup developing a low-cost, easy-to-use patch for automated drug delivery.
notes: His father, Dr. Kenneth Sim, is Executive Chairman. Young, technical CEO, which is a plausible guest for AI-in-healthcare and entrepreneurship themes. Personal social accounts were not verified because the search budget was exhausted.

name: Robert E Apple
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, MasTec Inc. (since Dec 2006)
profile: Naval Academy graduate and former Marine Corps lieutenant colonel who spent 1985-2004 at Hughes Electronics/DIRECTV (CEO of Hughes Electronics-Spain, COO of Telefonica's Via Digital satellite TV venture, SVP at DIRECTV). Joined MasTec in 2005 to run energy services and has been COO of the infrastructure contractor (pipelines, power delivery, communications, clean energy) since 2006; former chairman of Domtar.
interesting_fact: While on assignment from Hughes/DIRECTV Latin America he was COO and a board member of Via Digital, Telefonica's direct-broadcast satellite TV company in Spain (1997-2001).
deep_cut_fact: As a US Marine Corps aviator he graduated from the Naval Fighter Weapons School ('Top Gun') and was part of the team that rolled out the F/A-18 strike fighter.
notes: Public-company executive; no personal contact published. Route via MasTec corporate (Coral Gables, FL) or its investor relations site (investors.mastec.com). Couldn't confirm the IR/press email because the search budget ran out.

name: Anil K Singhal
current_role: Co-Founder, President, CEO and Chairman, NetScout Systems (NASDAQ: NTCT)
profile: Indian-born engineer, now 72, who co-founded NetScout in June 1984 and has been its CEO for more than four decades. He took the company public in 1999 and bought Danaher's communications business for $2.3B in 2015. NetScout now sells service-assurance, network-visibility and DDoS/cybersecurity tools to carriers and enterprises.
interesting_fact: He has run NetScout since its founding in 1984, one of the longest founder-CEO tenures among U.S. public tech companies, and was EY's New England Entrepreneur of the Year in 1997.
deep_cut_fact: He studied electrical engineering at BITS Pilani before an MS in computer science at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign. In 2013 he received TiE Boston's Lifetime Achievement award.
notes: Good fit for a data-center or network-infrastructure angle, since NetScout monitors carrier and data-center traffic. Active in the Boston Indian-American entrepreneur scene through TiE Boston. Search budget ran out, so this record is based on SEC filings.

name: Roy Zisapel
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Radware Ltd. (Nasdaq: RDWR)
profile: Roy Zisapel co-founded Israeli cybersecurity and application-delivery company Radware in May 1996 and has been its President & CEO ever since, building it into a global provider of DDoS protection and application security. A Tel Aviv University maths and CS graduate, he also sits on boards across the RAD-Bynet Group, the Israeli tech family of companies.
interesting_fact: He has run Radware as CEO continuously for 30 years, since its founding in 1996, making him one of the longest-serving founder-CEOs on Nasdaq.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Radware in his mid-20s, he worked as a software engineer (1994-96) and an R&D team leader at RND Networks. He is also a director of Bynet Data Centers, a data-center operator in the RAD-Bynet Group, a natural hook for a data-center podcast.
notes: Good fit (cybersecurity, data centers, AI-era app security). He does industry interviews fairly regularly. Route via Radware media relations. Web search budget ran out; facts are from Radware's 2025 20-F and Q3 2026 release.

name: Halit Coussin
current_role: Chief Legal Officer, Chief Compliance Officer and director, Pershing Square Inc. (NYSE: PS); director of Pershing Square Holdings
profile: Lawyer who joined Bill Ackman's Pershing Square in 2007 and has been its Chief Legal Officer and Chief Compliance Officer since 2015. She joined the management company's board in June 2024 and the PSH board in November 2024, and is a director/officer at the newly listed Pershing Square Inc.
interesting_fact: One of the longest-tenured members of Ackman's team, she has overseen legal and compliance through Pershing Square's SPAC (PSTH), SPARC and the 2026 public listing of the management company.
deep_cut_fact: She earned her LL.B. magna cum laude from Tel Aviv University in 1998 and an LL.M. from NYU in 2000, then advised hedge-fund managers on regulatory matters as an associate at Schulte Roth & Zabel before joining Pershing Square.
notes: Behind-the-scenes legal/compliance executive with essentially no media presence; route via Pershing Square media relations. Age 54 per 2026 prospectus.

name: Anat Ashkenazi
current_role: SVP and Chief Financial Officer, Alphabet Inc. and Google (since July 2024)
profile: Israeli-American finance executive who spent 23 years at Eli Lilly, rising to CFO (2021-2024) during the Mounjaro/Zepbound GLP-1 boom, before succeeding Ruth Porat as Alphabet's CFO in 2024. She now oversees one of tech's largest capital programs, with roughly US$91bn of 2025 capex aimed largely at AI infrastructure. Her wealth is mostly Alphabet stock awards.
interesting_fact: Fortune ranked her No. 48 on its 2026 Most Powerful Women list, citing Alphabet's AI capex program, one of the most aggressive capital deployments in tech history.
deep_cut_fact: Before moving to Lilly in 2001 she worked in Israel's financial sector, including at credit-rating agency Ma'alot Standard & Poor's and Bank Hapoalim; she studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem and earned an MBA from Tel Aviv University.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/energy theme (Alphabet AI capex, power procurement), but very hard to book; route only via Google corporate communications.

name: Braden Michael Leonard
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, BML Capital Management LLC (Zionsville, Indiana)
profile: Braden (Brad) Leonard founded BML Capital Management in 2004 and runs BML Investment Partners, a concentrated, value-oriented fund that takes large stakes in small caps—recently mostly healthcare/biotech names such as Adverum, AN2 Therapeutics and Outset Medical (hence his SEC 10%-owner filings). Before BML he was an equity trader at proprietary trading firm ETG (1995-2003).
interesting_fact: As representative of Build-A-Bear Workshop's largest stockholder, he sat on the toy retailer's board from 2011 to 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career straight out of Purdue (accounting degree) as a proprietary equity trader at ETG, LLC from 1995 to 2003, then launched his own fund from Zionsville, Indiana rather than New York.
notes: Private Midwest investor with no website or published contact found; reachable only via BML Capital Management's SEC-registered office. Weak fit for energy themes; possible entrepreneurship/investing angle.

name: Ramesh Srinivasan
current_role: President & CEO, Agilysys Inc. (Nasdaq: AGYS)
profile: Has led hospitality-software firm Agilysys since January 2017, shifting it to cloud/subscription products for hotels, resorts, casinos and cruise lines with a long run of record revenue quarters. Previously CEO of Bally Technologies (2012-14), Innotrac and Ooyala, and a warehouse-management software leader at Manhattan Associates.
interesting_fact: Under him Agilysys posted 17 consecutive record-revenue quarters through fiscal 2026, reaching record annual revenue of about $319m with subscription revenue growing ~30%.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer at IIT (Banaras Hindu University), Varanasi, took his MBA at IIM Bangalore, and spent 1998-2005 at Manhattan Associates, ending as EVP of Warehouse Management Systems, before running Bally's systems business.
notes: IR contact Jessica Hennessy (VP IR) named on releases. Regular earnings-call speaker; hospitality-tech rather than energy, so weaker podcast fit.

name: Benjamin J Tisch
current_role: President and CEO, Loews Corporation (NYSE: L), since January 2025
profile: Ben Tisch is the third generation of the Tisch family to run Loews, the conglomerate whose holdings include CNA Financial, Boardwalk Pipelines (natural-gas pipelines and storage), Loews Hotels and Altium Packaging. A Brown honors graduate, he spent his early career at Lehman Brothers and Fortress Investment Group before joining Loews' investment department in 2011. He rose to SVP of Corporate Development & Strategy and succeeded his father James Tisch as CEO.
interesting_fact: He sits on the board of Boardwalk Pipelines, Loews' wholly owned natural-gas pipeline and storage business, which is a direct link to gas-fired power demand from data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Loews he was a Managing Director at Fortress Investment Group, running international fixed income, international equities and US/European credit for its Global Macro Fund, after starting in Lehman Brothers' two-year investment-banking program. At Brown he studied Public and Private Sector Organizations and Political Science.
notes: Loews press releases name Chris Nugent (Investor and Public Relations) as the contact, with a published corporate phone number but no email. Boardwalk Pipelines gives a strong energy/data-center (gas-for-power) angle. Fortune profiled the Loews CEO transition in February 2025.

name: Richard Deal
current_role: Executive Vice President & Chief Human Resources Officer, FICO (Fair Isaac Corp.)
profile: Richard S. 'Rich' Deal is FICO's long-serving HR chief: he joined in 2001 as VP of Human Resources, became SVP & CHRO in 2007 and EVP & CHRO in 2015. His wealth stems from FICO equity accumulated as the analytics/credit-scoring company's share price soared. Earlier he held HR roles at Arcadia Financial and U.S. Bancorp.
interesting_fact: He has spent roughly 25 years at FICO, leading talent strategy and acquisition-integration work through its transformation into a high-margin scores and decisioning-software business.
deep_cut_fact: Before FICO he was VP of Human Resources at Arcadia Financial (1998-2001) and held HR consulting and line roles at U.S. Bancorp (1993-1998).
notes: Low public profile HR executive; limited relevance for energy/data-center themes. Route via FICO media relations.

name: Peter Nieh
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners
profile: Peter Nieh co-founded Lightspeed Venture Partners and has ~30 years in venture, mainly SaaS and infrastructure. His 10%-owner SEC filings for Rubrik and Netskope reflect Lightspeed fund holdings (Lightspeed led Rubrik's 2014 Series A and is its largest holder). Past investments include DoubleClick, Informatica, Blue Nile, Nest, QuantumScape and Eightfold.
interesting_fact: His portfolio spans energy and hardware as well as software - he is listed as an investor in solid-state battery maker QuantumScape and in Nest, the smart-thermostat company Google bought for $3.2B.
deep_cut_fact: He entered venture in 1995 after working in business development and product marketing at General Magic, the legendary Apple spin-off that built an early handheld communicator; outside work he plays competitive ultimate frisbee.
notes: Stanford BA and MBA. Good energy angle via QuantumScape and Nest; Lightspeed is a large AI/infra investor. VC so reachable via Lightspeed; X handle @peterlsvp.

name: Barry Eggers
current_role: Founding Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners (Menlo Park)
profile: Barry Eggers co-founded Lightspeed Venture Partners after six years at Cisco and focuses on enterprise infrastructure and cybersecurity. Lightspeed was an early lead investor in Rubrik (IPO 2024, ~24% stake) and Netskope (first backed with a $21M Series B in 2013, IPO 2025), and Eggers is reported as a 10% owner of both through Lightspeed vehicles. He also backed Nutanix early.
interesting_fact: Netskope's 2025 IPO followed Rubrik's in 2024. These were two rare cybersecurity IPOs, and Lightspeed was a top holder in both (about 19% of Netskope and about 24% of Rubrik at listing).
deep_cut_fact: At Cisco (1991-97), before co-founding Lightspeed, he built major sales channels and set up the company's first mergers-and-acquisitions process. He holds a UCLA BA in economics/business and a Stanford MBA.
notes: Strong fit for a data-center/infrastructure podcast (enterprise infra and storage investor). Advisory member of The Nature Conservancy's Investment Committee. He and his wife fund conservation, sustainability and mentoring initiatives. Best route is via Lightspeed's comms team.

name: Laura Louene Prieskorn
current_role: Advisor to Jackson Financial Inc. (NYSE: JXN) through Dec 31, 2026; was President & CEO until Don Cummings succeeded her on Oct 1, 2026
profile: Lifetime Jackson National Life insider who joined the Lansing, Michigan annuity giant in 1991 and rose through operations roles to Chief Administration Officer (2009–19), COO (2019–21) and CEO (2021–2026). She led Jackson through its 2021 demerger from Prudential plc and NYSE listing; in July 2026 she announced her retirement at year-end 2026.
interesting_fact: Calling the CEO role 'the highlight of my nearly 40 years with Jackson,' she is one of the few Fortune 500-scale financial CEOs to have spent her entire senior career at a single company, which she steered through its demerger from Prudential plc.
deep_cut_fact: She is a Central Michigan University business graduate (B.B.A.) and has sat on the board of the American Council of Life Insurers since 2021.
notes: Retiring at end of 2026 — after that, corporate channels may not reach her. 'Nearly 40 years' (company release) vs 'joined 1991' (proxy) differ slightly. Jackson press releases name rotating media contacts (e.g. Amanda Chaney) without emails in the sources checked. Limited energy/data-center relevance.

name: Ralph Alvarez
current_role: Chairman, First Watch Restaurant Group; Director, Eli Lilly (since 2009); Operating Partner, Advent International
profile: Cuban-born restaurant executive raised in Florida (University of Miami BBA, 1976). After roles at Burger King and Wendy's he rose through McDonald's (president of McDonald's Mexico, then McDonald's USA) to president and COO of McDonald's Corp. 2006-2009. He now chairs First Watch and sits on the boards of Eli Lilly and Lowe's, while serving as an operating partner at Advent.
interesting_fact: As McDonald's president and COO he is credited with expanding the menu and adding internet access to thousands of restaurants during the chain's late-2000s turnaround.
deep_cut_fact: Carnegie Corporation of New York named him one of its 'Great Immigrants' in 2013; he arrived in Florida from Cuba aged 5. He also chaired Skylark Co., the Japanese family-restaurant operator, and serves on the University of Miami President's Council.
notes: No personal channels found; route via First Watch investor relations or Advent International. Arrival-age detail from NRN profile: https://www.nrn.com/restaurant-segments/mcd-s-alvarez-works-to-keep-industry-s-biggest-chain-on-the-rise

name: Howard Feinglass
current_role: Founder and Senior Partner, Priam Capital; director of USCB Financial Holdings / U.S. Century Bank (Miami)
profile: Private-equity investor (Brown AB, UCLA MBA) who was a principal in Odyssey Partners' PE group, ran a $1bn+ family office for three years, then founded Priam Capital in 2003. Priam's fund is a 10%+ holder of Miami-based USCB Financial (U.S. Century Bank), where he has been a director since 2015; he also sits on boards of Centrix Aerospace and First National Bank of America.
interesting_fact: While running a $1bn+ family office he led its diversification from a real-estate core into alternative investments and public-company holdings, before launching Priam Capital in 2003.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of the Riverside Hawks, a non-profit youth basketball organization, alongside his bank and aerospace directorships.
notes: Low-profile PE investor; no Priam Capital website found. Only indirect route via USCB investor relations. Previously a director of Howard Bancorp (per its proxies).

name: Michael Alfred
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, Alpine Fox LP; independent director of IREN (since 2021), Bakkt (since 2025) and Opendoor (since Oct 2026)
profile: Michael Alfred is a serial fintech/data founder turned investor: he co-founded and ran BrightScope (401k ratings, sold to Strategic Insight in 2016) and Digital Assets Data (sold to NYDIG in 2020). Since 2023 he has run Alpine Fox LP, a value-equities-and-Bitcoin partnership, and sits on the board of IREN, the Bitcoin miner turned AI data-center developer, plus Bakkt and, from October 2026, Opendoor.
interesting_fact: He joined the board of IREN (then Iris Energy) in October 2021, before its Nasdaq IPO, and has overseen its pivot from Bitcoin mining to AI cloud/data-center infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: A Stanford history graduate, he chaired Crestone Group, a national artisan bakery company, from 2020 (board member 2015-July 2026) - an unusual sideline for a crypto/fintech board member.
notes: Contacts are IREN's company IR/media inboxes (he is a non-executive director). He is known to be active on X about value investing and Bitcoin, but no official source linking a handle was verified, so none listed. Opendoor appointment per 8-K filed 2026-10-29.

name: Jennifer A Parmentier
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Parker-Hannifin Corp (CEO since Jan 2023, chair since Jan 2024); director, Nordson
profile: Industrial executive leading Parker-Hannifin, the Cleveland-based motion and control technologies maker. She joined Parker in 2008, ran the Sporlan and Hose Products divisions and the Engineered Materials Group, then served as COO before becoming CEO. Earlier career at Ingersoll Rand/Trane Residential and Magna. Wealth is from executive equity.
interesting_fact: She rose from division general manager to COO overseeing all of Parker's operating groups (2021), then became CEO in Jan 2023 and added chair in Jan 2024, succeeding Tom Williams.
deep_cut_fact: One of her early Parker posts was general manager of the Sporlan Division, which makes refrigeration and air-conditioning flow-control valves, before she ran the Hose Products Division.
notes: Parker's aerospace and thermal/filtration lines give a possible energy/data-center angle. Route via Parker IR.

name: Daniel A Bergeron
current_role: Vice President and Chief Operating Officer, and Director, RBC Bearings Inc. (Oxford, Connecticut)
profile: Daniel A. Bergeron joined RBC Bearings in 2003 as VP Finance and became CFO the same year. He helped take the company public in 2005 and added the COO role in 2017. He gave up the CFO title in 2020 and now runs operations at the precision bearings and engineered components maker, which bought Dodge from ABB in 2021. He has been a director since 2013.
interesting_fact: He has spent more than two decades at RBC, first as CFO and then as COO, while the company grew into a large aerospace and industrial components supplier. His wealth comes mainly from long-held RBC stock.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in industrial finance: he spent 1987–1998 in financial reporting roles at Dorr-Oliver, a Connecticut maker of process equipment, and later was CFO of the telecom firm Paragon Networks International. He holds a finance B.S. from Northeastern and an MBA from the University of New Haven.
notes: A low-profile operating executive with very little media presence. I could not verify a current published IR or press email: the release pages returned 403. The best route is RBC's investor relations, via the contact block in its latest earnings release.

name: Serge Saxonov
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, 10x Genomics (NASDAQ: TXG)
profile: Serge Saxonov co-founded 10x Genomics in 2012 with Ben Hindson and Kevin Ness and has been CEO since inception, building it into a leader in single-cell and spatial biology instruments. Earlier he was 23andMe's first employee (founding architect, director of R&D) and VP of applications at droplet-digital-PCR startup QuantaLife, sold to Bio-Rad in 2011 for $162m.
interesting_fact: He was 23andMe's first employee, helping define the consumer genetics company's original product concept; Goldman Sachs named him one of its 100 Most Intriguing Entrepreneurs in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Born in the former Soviet Union, he emigrated to the US as a teenager, went to Bronx Science, then studied at Harvard under genomics pioneer and Nobel laureate Wally Gilbert before a Stanford PhD in biomedical informatics.
notes: Good fit for data/compute angle: 10x is pushing AI-scale biological datasets (e.g. Cancer Research Institute AI immuno-oncology initiative, 2026). Has appeared on GEN's 'Close to the Edge' podcast.

name: Richard Barry
current_role: President & CEO, Cassava Sciences (SAVA); independent director, Sarepta Therapeutics (since 2015)
profile: Rick Barry is a former hedge-fund manager: a portfolio manager and managing director at Robertson Stephens Investment Management, then a founding managing general partner of Eastbourne Capital Management (1999-2010), a large equity fund with healthcare exposure. He has sat on Sarepta's board since 2015 and moved from Cassava's board (2021) to executive chairman and then CEO, now steering it towards TSC-related epilepsy.
interesting_fact: He was a partner and advisory board member of Major League Baseball's San Diego Padres from 2009 to 2021.
deep_cut_fact: A Penn State BA, he previously served on the advisory board of Penn State's Schreyer Honors College.
notes: Goes by 'Rick'. Best business route is via Cassava Sciences (Austin, TX) investor relations; no published personal channels found. Biotech investor, not energy.

name: David Phillips
current_role: Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer & Treasurer, Publix Super Markets; director since 2016
profile: David P. Phillips has spent his whole executive career at employee-owned Publix, joining in 1984 as an internal auditor after auditing the company for its outside accounting firm. He became controller in 1990, CFO in 1999 and EVP & CFO in 2016, and is a trustee of Publix's ESOP. His wealth comes from Publix stock (company is employee-owned, not listed).
interesting_fact: While auditing Publix for its outside auditors he decided the company was 'much better than other companies' and pursued a job there; he personally knew founder George Jenkins, whom he calls a 'complete genius'.
deep_cut_fact: A Lakeland, Florida native, after college he and his two brothers cycled across the U.S. from Astoria, Oregon to Yorktown, Virginia - about 2.5 months; he studied engineering and pre-med before switching to accounting.
notes: Lane data tags him 'Hurun Unicorn founders / Data Analytics' - likely a name collision; the SEC wealth is Publix CFO. Low public profile; route via Publix corporate communications. Jan 2025 media advisory names Jared Glover, Media Relations Manager (https://www.insidetheisle.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Publix-Media-Advisory-1.3.25.pdf).

name: Lainie Goldstein
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Take-Two Interactive (since 2007); Director, Phreesia
profile: Lainie Goldstein has been CFO of Take-Two Interactive (Rockstar/GTA, 2K, Zynga) since 2007, after joining as SVP Finance in 2003; she oversees finance, accounting, tax, treasury, IR and corporate communications. A CPA, she previously was VP Finance & Business Development at Nautica and worked in audit and reorganization at Grant Thornton. She also sits on Phreesia's board.
interesting_fact: She has been CFO through nearly two decades of Grand Theft Auto releases - from GTA IV to the build-up to GTA VI - making her one of the longest-serving CFOs in video games; she stepped up (initially on an interim basis) in 2007.
deep_cut_fact: Before video games she worked in fashion: she rose through finance roles at apparel maker Nautica Enterprises to VP of Finance and Business Development; she earned her accounting degree at American University in Washington, D.C.
notes: Low personal media profile; communications routed via Take-Two IR/corporate comms (which report to her).

name: Roberto R Herencia
current_role: Executive Chairman & CEO, Byline Bancorp (Chicago); Chairman, First BanCorp / FirstBank Puerto Rico; Director, Banner Corp
profile: Banker Roberto Herencia spent 17 years at Popular Inc., including as president of Banco Popular North America, then ran Midwest Banc Holdings. In 2010 he founded community-bank investment fund BXM Holdings, which recapitalized Chicago's Metropolitan Bank Group and turned it into Byline Bank (IPO 2017). He has chaired Byline since 2013, has been CEO since 2021, and has chaired First BanCorp since 2011.
interesting_fact: He led a turnaround-by-recapitalization: through BXM Holdings he rebuilt failing Metropolitan Bank Group into Byline Bank, now a top Chicago commercial and SBA lender. At the same time he chaired First BanCorp through Puerto Rico's debt crisis.
deep_cut_fact: President Obama appointed him to the board of the Overseas Private Investment Corporation (OPIC), the US government's development finance agency, in 2011. He holds a Georgetown finance degree and a Kellogg MBA.

public_contacts.value: brennie@bylinebank.com (Brooks O. Rennie, Head of Investor Relations, Investors/Media)

notes: Byline's IR head doubles as its media contact. The bank-turnaround story could fit an entrepreneurship angle.

name: Lange Bob De
current_role: Group President, Services, Distribution & Digital, Caterpillar Inc.; Director, AGCO Corp (since Jan 2021)
profile: Bob De Lange is a Belgian-trained mechanical engineer who joined Caterpillar in 1993 and held product and leadership roles in Europe and Asia, including VP of the Excavation Division (Singapore, 2015). He ran Construction Industries, a roughly $20bn business, from 2017, and since 2018 has led Caterpillar's dealer network, services and Cat Digital. He also sits on AGCO's board.
interesting_fact: He is responsible for the Caterpillar brand, its global dealer network and Cat Digital, the unit behind connected-machine data across Caterpillar's fleet.
deep_cut_fact: He earned both a BS and an MS in Mechanical Engineering from the Catholic University of Leuven (KU Leuven) in Belgium in 1992, then an MBA from EDHEC in France in 1993, the year he joined Caterpillar.
notes: Name order in the source is reversed ('Lange Bob De'). Still listed as a Caterpillar group president per the officers page and a Jan 2026 Form 4. Caterpillar's power-generation and data-center gensets business sits in a different segment, but the services/digital angle is relevant. No published press email could be retrieved (site blocks bots); use Caterpillar media relations via caterpillar.com.

name: Richard A Hubbell
current_role: Executive Chairman, RPC, Inc. (oilfield services); formerly Executive Chairman, Marine Products Corp.
profile: Richard Hubbell is a longtime lieutenant of the Rollins family businesses in Atlanta. He was President of RPC, the oil-and-gas services company spun out of Rollins, from 1987 and CEO from 2003 until May 2022, when he became Executive Chairman; he also chaired boat maker Marine Products (Chaparral, Robalo).
interesting_fact: RPC (Cudd Pressure Control, Patterson Services and other units) provides pressure pumping, coiled tubing and other services to US oil and gas producers - a direct energy-industry link spanning nearly four decades of his leadership.
deep_cut_fact: He began with Rollins, Inc. in 1970 and was Executive Vice President of Rollins Communications, the family's media company, before moving to oilfield services; he holds an economics BA from Westminster College.
notes: Around 80 years old. RPC announced CEO Ben Palmer's retirement and a successor search in June 2026; Hubbell quoted as Executive Chairman. Input lists Marine Products Group as 'former' chairmanship (Marine Products appears to have changed ownership in 2026 - verify).

name: Heather M. Lovier
current_role: Chief Operating Officer, Rocket Companies (NYSE: RKT), Detroit; also COO of RKT Holdings, LLC
profile: Heather Lovier is a long-time Rocket insider who joined Rocket Mortgage in 2003 and worked her way up through operations. She was chief client experience officer (2021-2024) and in June 2024 succeeded Bill Emerson as COO. She now oversees banking, Rocket Pro, Rocket Close and client experience, and leads the rollout of the Rocket Logic AI platform.
interesting_fact: HousingWire named her a 2026 Woman of Influence, crediting her with deploying Rocket Logic and Rocket's agentic-AI tools and expanding AI-powered mortgage preapproval that borrowers can use around the clock.
notes: Unverified profile claims (fintool, MBA speaker bio) say she started as a loan analyst and later joined Rocket's internal 'Mousetrap' process-improvement team, but I could not confirm this from a primary source. She has appeared on podcasts such as 'The Way with Dino Katsiametis'. No published press email found; go through Rocket corporate communications.

name: Carrie Wheeler
current_role: Board director, APi Group (since 2019) and TKO Group Holdings (since 2023); former CEO & Chair of Opendoor (2022-Aug 2025)
profile: Carrie Wheeler (Queen's University BComm) spent 21 years at TPG, joining it early, rising to partner and head of consumer/retail, and leading deals worth over $20bn, with board seats at J.Crew, Neiman Marcus and Petco. She joined Opendoor as CFO in 2020 and became CEO in December 2022. She stepped down in August 2025 and now serves on corporate boards.
interesting_fact: She led Opendoor through the 2022-24 housing downturn as CEO. Opendoor reported its first adjusted-EBITDA-positive quarter since 2022 in the period just before she stepped down in August 2025.
deep_cut_fact: She was among TPG's earliest hires, part of the core team that scaled the firm into one of the world's largest private equity houses. Opendoor's announcement of her hiring notes she is a Canadian-educated Queen's University commerce graduate.
notes: Her Opendoor exit followed activist-investor pressure, so avoid that topic and lean on her TPG/consumer-investing experience. SignalFire lists her on its team page (https://www.signalfire.com/team/carrie-wheeler), which may be a route. No published personal contact.

name: Mark Samuel Hoplamazian
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Hyatt Hotels Corporation (chairman since Feb 2026); director, VF Corp
profile: Harvard BA and Chicago Booth MBA who started in M&A at First Boston, then spent years at The Pritzker Organization, the Pritzker family's investment office, rising to president. He was made interim CEO of Hyatt in 2006, took it public in 2009 and has moved it toward an asset-light, luxury and lifestyle-heavy brand portfolio. He became board chairman in Feb 2026 when Thomas Pritzker retired.
interesting_fact: When he joined Hyatt from the Pritzker family office he recalled: 'The Pritzker Organization was 10 people. Hyatt was around 80,000', and said he 'embraced my ignorance and learned as much as I could as quickly as I could.'
deep_cut_fact: He was a Boston Consulting Group summer associate in 1988 and went to Episcopal Academy in Pennsylvania (class of 1981). His favourite advice is to say 'I don't know that yet' when facing something unfamiliar.
notes: High-profile CEO, frequent conference speaker (Skift, Milken, Aspen). Route via Hyatt corporate communications (Investor Day 2026 media contact: Franziska Weber). Avoid the Pritzker/Epstein context of his chairmanship.

name: Michael W Koehnen
current_role: Vice Chairman and Corporate Secretary, TriCo Bancshares / Tri Counties Bank (Chico, CA); Owner and President, C.F. Koehnen & Sons (Ord Bend, CA)
profile: Michael Koehnen is a Northern California agribusiness owner. He runs C.F. Koehnen & Sons, a fourth-generation farming and beekeeping company, and the almond processor Riverwest Processing, along with related export companies in Glenn County. He has been a TriCo Bancshares director since 2002, vice chairman since 2010 and corporate secretary since 2021, and is a long-time significant shareholder.
interesting_fact: The Koehnen family has kept bees since 1907 and is one of the world's largest producers of honey bees and queen bees. Its colonies are around Glenn County in the Northern Sacramento Valley.
deep_cut_fact: Koehnen's Italian queens are all light-coloured 'Cordovan' bees, from a breeding project begun around 1975. The family has produced Italian queens since the 1930s, and they make up about two-thirds of its queen production.
notes: Private, rural agribusiness owner with no personal media presence. The Koehnen bee-business contact form is a commercial channel, so use it sparingly. TriCo's corporate secretary office is the formal route. He is not an energy or data-center figure; his wealth is agriculture plus TriCo stock.

name: James F Risoleo
current_role: President, CEO and Director (Chairman per some profiles), Host Hotels & Resorts (CEO since January 2017)
profile: Jim Risoleo, 70, runs Host Hotels & Resorts, the largest US lodging REIT. He joined Host in 1996 as SVP acquisitions, became CIO in 2000, led its European and later West Coast investment activities, and was named CEO in January 2017. Before Host he worked in hotel development at Interstate Hotels and commercial real estate at Westinghouse.
interesting_fact: He is a past chairman of NAREIT, the REIT industry's trade body, and sits on the executive committee of the American Hotel & Lodging Association and the US Travel Association CEO Roundtable.
deep_cut_fact: A Duquesne-trained lawyer, he is still a member of the Pennsylvania Bar; before hotels he was SVP of commercial real estate at Westinghouse Electric Corporation.
notes: Host is based in Bethesda, MD. Hotel Business ran a 2016-era career-journey piece saying Dick Marriott (Host chair) personally called him to come back as CEO (https://hotelbusiness.com/hb-on-the-scene-jim-risoleo-shares-career-journey/ - not directly verified, page blocked).

name: Brian H. Franke
current_role: Principal, Indigo Partners LLC; Chair of Volaris (Controladora Vuela); Director, Frontier Group Holdings
profile: Brian Franke has been a principal since 2004 at Indigo Partners, the Phoenix private-equity firm specialising in ultra-low-cost airlines founded by former America West CEO Bill Franke. He has served on Frontier Airlines' board since 2013, on Volaris' board since 2010 (chair since April 2020), and on boards of JetSMART (South America), Cebu Air (Philippines) and airline analytics firm APiJET.
interesting_fact: He sits on the boards of ultra-low-cost carriers on three continents - Frontier (US), Volaris (Mexico, which he chairs), JetSMART (South America) and Cebu Pacific (Philippines) - and earlier on Tiger Airways in Singapore and Australia.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Master of International Management from Thunderbird School of Global Management (plus a B.S. from the University of Arizona) and served on the University of Arizona Foundation board from 2016 to 2025.
notes: Indigo Partners keeps a minimal public footprint (no published press email found). Route via Frontier or Volaris investor relations. APiJET (real-time airline fuel/cost analytics) could be an energy-efficiency talking point.

name: James G Shiel
current_role: Executive Vice President - Investments, W. R. Berkley Corporation (Greenwich, CT)
profile: Long-serving investment chief at specialty insurer W. R. Berkley, which he joined in 1987 via its Berkley Dean & Company investment-advisory subsidiary (later its president). He was SVP Investments 1997-2015 and has been EVP Investments since June 2015, overseeing the insurer's investment portfolio. Educated at Colgate (BA) and NYU (MBA).
interesting_fact: He has spent nearly four decades at W. R. Berkley, starting in 1987 at Berkley Dean & Company, the group's in-house investment adviser founded in 1967.

public_contacts.value: No email published; company contact is Karen A. Horvath, VP External Financial Communications (phone listed on releases)

notes: Low-profile insurance investment executive; no interviews or social accounts found. Founder William R. Berkley died June 2026 (context only). Only route found: Berkley external financial communications.

name: Dustin Beck

profile: Blake Baird, 65, co-founded Terreno Realty and has run it since its 2010 IPO. The REIT owns infill industrial and logistics property in six major US coastal markets. Before that he was President of AMB Property Corporation (now part of Prologis) from 2000 to 2006, and he spent 15 years in real estate investment banking at Morgan Stanley and Dean Witter.
interesting_fact: He helped build AMB Property, now part of Prologis, the world's largest industrial REIT, serving as its CIO and then President from 1999 to 2006. He then started Terreno almost from scratch, through Terreno Capital Partners in 2007.

notes: A founder-CEO with a good angle for the podcast: infill industrial land in dense coastal markets competes with data-centre demand. The IR contact is Jaime Cannon via investors@terreno.com. No personal social accounts were verified.

name: Sharon Yeshaya
current_role: EVP & Chief Financial Officer, Morgan Stanley (NYSE: MS), New York
profile: A career-long Morgan Stanley banker who joined as a college intern and started in M&A after graduating from Penn/Wharton in 2001. She worked in the Fixed Income Division in New York and Hong Kong, became Head of Investor Relations and Chief of Staff to the Chairman and CEO, and has been CFO since June 2021. Her wealth is accumulated Morgan Stanley equity.

deep_cut_fact: She started as an M&A analyst right after graduating in 2001, just as 9/11 hit. She later moved to the fixed-income side in Hong Kong before running investor relations. She graduated summa cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa from Penn with dual finance (Wharton) and economics degrees.
notes: Route through Morgan Stanley Corporate Communications or Investor Relations. No published media email was confirmed because the web-search budget ran out and MS pages hide contacts behind scripts. Trustee of NewYork-Presbyterian and on Wharton's undergraduate board. The 9/11 timing detail comes from CFO Dive's 2021 interview coverage.

name: Marvin R Ellison
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Lowe's Companies (since 2018; Chairman since May 2021). Director, FedEx.
profile: A career retail operator who spent 15 years at Target and 12 at Home Depot (rising to EVP of U.S. Stores), then served as CEO and Chairman of J.C. Penney (2015-18). He joined Lowe's as CEO in 2018 and has focused on store operations, the Pro customer and digital and omnichannel growth.

deep_cut_fact: His path to the top ran through the back of the store: at Home Depot he was VP of Loss Prevention before moving to VP and then SVP of Logistics, after starting his career in operational roles at Target in 1987.
notes: High-profile CEO, so the route is Lowe's corporate communications via its newsroom. The media emails on older releases date from 2022 and may be stale, so they were omitted.

name: Kunal Kapoor
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Morningstar, Inc. (Chicago)
profile: Kunal Kapoor, CFA, has been CEO of Morningstar, the investment research and data firm, since 2017, succeeding founder Joe Mansueto (now executive chairman). current_role: Chief Financial Officer, DigitalOcean Holdings (NYSE: DOCN), since January 2023

He was previously CFO (2017-2022) and strategy EVP at fiber/data-center-connectivity company Zayo Group, and before that co-founded and ran video-intelligence SaaS company Envysion for a decade; earlier he worked at Level 3, ICG Communications and Bain.

deep_cut_fact: He co-founded Envysion (2006), a video-intelligence SaaS company he led as CEO until 2016 and which merged into Motorola Solutions in 2021; he studied civil engineering and operations research at Princeton.

current_role: Former EVP, Transformation and Chief Information & Digital Officer, T-Mobile US (not listed as an executive officer in T-Mobile's April 2026 proxy); current role unverified
profile: Nestor Cano is a Spanish-born telecom/IT operator who was T-Mobile's EVP Transformation and CIDO from 2023, after leading the Sprint integration as EVP Integration & Transformation (2020-2023).
