notes: Not among T-Mobile executive officers in the 2026 proxy, so he may have left or changed role - verify before outreach. No published contact found.

name: Eric Mark Green
current_role: Chair, President & CEO, West Pharmaceutical Services (since 2015); Director, Ecolab
profile: Life-sciences executive who spent 22 years at Sigma-Aldrich (1993-2015) running several of its major businesses before becoming CEO of West Pharmaceutical Services, the Exton, PA maker of drug-containment and injectable-delivery components (vial stoppers, syringe components, GLP-1 injector parts). He leads 10,000+ employees and also sits on Ecolab's board.
interesting_fact: West's elastomer stoppers and seals sit on a large share of the world's injectable drug vials, so West became a critical supplier during COVID-19 vaccine rollouts; under Green it has pushed into high-value components for GLP-1 and biologic drugs.
deep_cut_fact: He trained in science: his undergraduate degree is a B.A. in Chemistry from Bethel University, followed by an MBA from Washington University's Olin Business School in St. Louis, Sigma-Aldrich's home town.
notes: No current press email found (older releases list 2017-2019 contacts). The cited proxy confirms career, roles and education; the COVID/GLP-1 context in interesting_fact is general industry knowledge. Medtech rather than energy, so lower podcast fit.

name: Masi Niccolo De
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, IonQ (NYSE: IONQ); Director, Rush Street Interactive
profile: Niccolo de Masi is a Cambridge-trained physicist turned serial tech CEO (Glu Mobile, Monstermob, Resideo) and SPAC sponsor whose dMY Technology Group III took quantum-computing company IonQ public in 2021 (also Rush Street Interactive, Genius Sports, Planet). He joined IonQ's board in 2021, became CEO in February 2025 and chairman in August 2025, driving an acquisition-led expansion.

deep_cut_fact: He studied physics at Cambridge (BA and MSc), and one of his first jobs was at Siemens Solar, before Technicolor and his move into mobile gaming.
notes: High-profile, media-friendly CEO; good fit for tech/data-center angle (quantum + space division). Note the IR page lists investors@ionq.com while the release says investors@ionq.co.

name: David R Brooks
current_role: Director, SouthState Bank Corp (since Jan 2025); Chairman of the Board, Capital Southwest Corp (CSWC); former Chairman & CEO, Independent Bank Group
profile: Texas banker who founded Independent Bank in McKinney in 1988 and grew it into Independent Financial (Independent Bank Group, Nasdaq: IBTX), serving Texas and Colorado. He led it as Chairman/CEO until SouthState acquired it on 1 Jan 2025, then joined SouthState's board. He chairs BDC lender Capital Southwest and is on Baylor University's Board of Regents.

name: Randall W. (Randy) Edgar
current_role: CEO and Director, Suncrete, Inc. (Nasdaq: RMIX), Tulsa, Oklahoma
profile: Tulsa concrete entrepreneur, age 69. A former KPMG CPA, he was VP of Mid-Continent Concrete and then president under Mexican cement maker GCC after it bought the company (2006). He founded Eagle Redi-Mix Concrete in 2008, which grew into Suncrete, a ready-mix concrete platform across Oklahoma, Arkansas, Texas and Louisiana. Suncrete listed in 2026 through a SPAC merger led by Ned Fleming and Mark Matteson.

deep_cut_fact: He started as a CPA at KPMG before entering concrete. He holds an accounting degree from the University of Tulsa and founded his own company, Eagle Redi-Mix, in 2008 after running GCC's US ready-mix arm.

current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, PROG Holdings, Inc. (PRG), Salt Lake City
profile: Steve Michaels joined Aaron's in 2008 as VP Finance of its Sales & Lease Ownership division and rose through strategy and finance roles to CFO of Aaron's Inc. He became CEO of the Progressive Leasing segment in 2020 and of PROG Holdings when it separated from Aaron's that November, running lease-to-own provider Progressive Leasing and BNPL app Four; he is now also Chairman.
interesting_fact: In Q3 2026 PROG reported consolidated GMV growth of 59%, driven by its diversified platform including the Four buy-now-pay-later business.
deep_cut_fact: His whole senior career has been inside one corporate family: he joined Aaron's in 2008 as a division finance VP and held roughly seven roles (VP Strategic Planning, President, CFO and President of Strategic Operations) before becoming PROG's first CEO.

name: Eugene Sheridan
current_role: Co-founder and former President & CEO of Navitas Semiconductor (stepped down 31 Aug 2025); co-founder and Executive Chairman, Empower Semiconductor (per Crunchbase/2024 interview)
profile: Gene Sheridan co-founded Navitas Semiconductor in 2014 and led it as its only CEO through its 2021 SPAC listing, building GaN and SiC power chips for fast chargers, EVs and AI data-centre power; he handed over to Chris Allexandre in Sept 2025. He has 25+ years in power management semiconductors.
interesting_fact: Before Navitas he was CEO of BridgeCo, a wireless audio company sold to Standard Microsystems (SMSC), and earlier worked in management at International Rectifier; he holds a BSEE from Clarkson University.
deep_cut_fact: He also co-founded Empower Semiconductor (Milpitas) with Tim Phillips and Volterra co-founder David Lidsky, and serves as its chairman; Empower makes integrated voltage regulators aimed at the power-delivery bottleneck of AI/HPC processors in data centres.
notes: No longer at Navitas (resigned as CEO and director effective 31 Aug 2025 under a transition agreement: https://navitassemi.com/navitas-semiconductor-names-chris-allexandre-as-president-and-chief-executive-officer/). Good fit for data-centre power topics (GaN/SiC, IVRs). Empower route: info@empowersemi.com.

name: Kurt Sievers
current_role: Retired President & CEO of NXP Semiconductors (CEO 2020 to Oct 2025); board member of Booking Holdings (since Apr 2026), Capgemini SE and Daimler Truck
profile: German physicist-turned-chip executive who spent 30 years at Philips Semiconductors/NXP. He ran the automotive business, joined executive management in 2009, helped on NXP's 2010 Nasdaq IPO and the 2016 Freescale acquisition, became President in 2018 and CEO 2020-25. Retired Oct 2025 (succeeded by Rafael Sotomayor) and now holds board seats.
interesting_fact: He chaired the European Semiconductor Industry Association and has sat on the boards of Germany's electrical/electronics industry association (ZVEI) and the Global Semiconductor Alliance, a leading voice for Europe's chip industry.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Augsburg in 1969, he earned an MSc in Physics and Computer Science at the University of Augsburg and joined Philips in 1995, working in product definition and development before moving into marketing, strategy and general management.
notes: No longer at NXP (advisor to the CEO until 31 Dec 2025), so the SEC-listed titles are outdated. He is now a professional director, possibly more open to podcast invitations post-retirement. No verified personal site or social account found; approach via board-company corporate secretaries or a mutual industry contact.

name: David A Sumoski
current_role: Retired (June 2026) Executive Vice President and former Chief Operating Officer (2021-Jan 2026), Nucor Corporation
profile: Career Nucor steelman who joined as an electrical supervisor at Nucor Steel-Berkeley in 1995 and rose through maintenance and plant leadership (GM of Nucor Steel Marion and Nucor Steel Memphis) to EVP in 2014 and Chief Operating Officer of America's largest steelmaker in 2021. He stepped down as COO in January 2026 and retired in June 2026.

deep_cut_fact: He started at Nucor in 1995 as an electrical supervisor at the Nucor Steel-Berkeley mill in South Carolina, later its maintenance manager, before running the Marion (Ohio) and Memphis mills – a shop-floor-to-COO career.

public_contacts.value: katherine.miller@nucor.com (Nucor media inquiries, as published in Nucor press releases)

name: Bryan Leach
current_role: Founder, CEO & President, Ibotta, Inc. (NYSE: IBTA), Denver

Ibotta, which powers digital promotions for retailers such as Walmart, IPO'd on the NYSE in April 2024, the largest tech IPO in Colorado history.

deep_cut_fact: He and his wife funded the Leach Center for Performing Arts at Colorado Academy, opened in 2021; the gift also helped start the school's speech and debate program. He also clerked for Justice David Souter at the US Supreme Court.
notes: Media-friendly founder-CEO who talks often about entrepreneurship. Strong fit for the founder-story side of the podcast. Route via Ibotta corporate communications.

Treat the SEC net-worth figure as unrelated.

profile: Co-founder with husband Walt Woltosz of Simulations Plus (1996, Lancaster CA), a maker of modelling and simulation software for drug discovery and development, where she held director and secretary/treasurer roles. name: Walter S Woltosz
current_role: Co-founder and Director, Simulations Plus, Inc. (chairman 1996–Dec 2024; company being acquired by Altaris for about $375M, expected to close Q4 2026)
profile: Walt Woltosz is an Auburn-trained aerospace engineer who spent 13 years building simulation and optimization software for rocket motors and missiles (Space Shuttle, AMRAAM, Pegasus). He then founded Words+ (1981), maker of PC-based communication systems for people who cannot speak, and Simulations Plus (1996), a Nasdaq-listed developer of ADME/PBPK modeling software for drug development. He was chief product officer from 2016, president in 2020 and CEO from 2021, pushing Mastercard into data, cybersecurity, open banking and stablecoin/on-chain payments.
interesting_fact: Wikipedia describes him as the only German leading a major US corporation; as chief product officer he played a central role in Mastercard's 2016 acquisition of UK payments-infrastructure firm Vocalink.
deep_cut_fact: He comes from Obergünzburg in Bavaria's Allgäu region, studied at the University of Passau, and in his Barclays years sat on the boards of Barclays' banks in Egypt, Tanzania and Botswana.
notes: Seth Eisen is Mastercard Global Communications as listed in the June 2026 release. Also on the American Red Cross Board of Governors (2025) and a WEF regular.

name: Christopher P Kalnin
current_role: Founder, CEO and Director, BKV Corporation (NYSE: BKV), Denver
profile: Chris Kalnin is a former McKinsey consultant and Level 3 Communications executive who founded BKV in 2015 with Thailand's Banpu. The company became the dominant gas producer in Texas's Barnett Shale and also operates in Pennsylvania. BKV IPO'd in September 2024 and owns 1.5 GW of gas-fired power plants in Temple, Texas. It is pursuing carbon capture and power deals with AI data-center hyperscalers.
interesting_fact: He says a big institutional investor 'berated' him for about 30 minutes over his gas-to-power strategy. Buying the Temple, Texas power plants is now 'one of our best investments ever', and hyperscalers' requests 'now start with gigawatts'.
deep_cut_fact: BKV stands for 'Banpu Kalnin Ventures'. His thesis was contrarian: after other operators left the Barnett around 2010, he bought in cheaply and applied newer drilling and fracking techniques from other shale plays. He calls his McKinsey-honed approach following 'megatrends' — 'a glacier moving in a direction.'
notes: The strongest fit in this lane for an energy and data-center podcast: gas-to-power for AI, CCUS and a hyperscaler deal pipeline. He already talks openly to press (Fortune, Hart Energy). Best route is BKV media relations.

name: Sierk Poetting
current_role: Chief Operating Officer & Management Board member, BioNTech SE; Chairman of the Board, IQM (Finland)
profile: German physicist-turned-executive (b. 1973) who started at McKinsey, held finance roles at Novartis/Sandoz (CFO Sandoz North America 2012-14), then joined BioNTech in 2014 as CFO and later COO, helping scale the Mainz company through its COVID-19 vaccine with Pfizer. He also chairs IQM, a Finnish quantum-computer maker.
interesting_fact: He chairs the board of IQM Quantum Computers in Espoo, Finland - an unusual quantum-hardware role for a biotech COO.
deep_cut_fact: He did his physics PhD at the Max Planck Institute for Quantum Optics (thesis: 'Coherent momentum state manipulation of matter waves', 2004) after a University of Arizona MS thesis on 'Gap solitons in atomic Bose-Einstein condensates'.
notes: Strong compute angle via IQM quantum computing. BioNTech management board term listed as ending 2026 - check whether reappointed (BioNTech named a new CEO, Guido Oelkers, in 2026).

name: Aristeidis P Pittas
current_role: Vice Chairman, Euroseas Ltd. (ESEA) and EuroDry Ltd. (EDRY) and Euroholdings Ltd.; Vice President, Oceanbulk Maritime SA
profile: Aristides P. Pittas (b. ~1951) is a member of the Athens shipping family whose interests were consolidated into Nasdaq-listed Euroseas in 2005; he has been its vice chairman since 2005 and vice chairman of drybulk spin-off EuroDry since 2018. He is a cousin of chairman/CEO Aristides J. Pittas (not to be confused with him) and has been VP of ship manager Oceanbulk Maritime since 1989.
interesting_fact: According to EuroDry's filings he has been a shareholder in over 100 oceangoing vessels over the last 20 years.
deep_cut_fact: He started in 1979 in the operations and freight-collection department of Gourdomichalis Maritime, then worked four years as a sale-and-purchase ship broker at Trust Marine Enterprises and in the supply department of Drytank SA before joining Oceanbulk in 1989; he holds a BSc in Economics from the Athens School of Economics.
notes: Identity caution: the public face of Euroseas/EuroDry is his cousin Aristides J. Pittas (Chairman/CEO, Lloyd's List Greek Newsmaker 2021); most web bios refer to J., not P. Very low public profile; approach via the company.

name: Louis Tomlinson
current_role: Singer-songwriter (solo artist, formerly One Direction); founder of Away From Home Festival and clothing brand '28'
profile: Doncaster-born Louis Tomlinson rose to fame in One Direction after The X Factor (2010) and has since built a solo career; his third album 'How Did I Get Here?' (Jan 2026) debuted at #1 in the UK, backed by the 54-date 'How Did We Get Here?' world tour in 2026. He runs production company 78 Productions, the Away From Home indie festival and streetwear brand '28'.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he signed with hometown club Doncaster Rovers on non-contract terms, wearing squad number 28 for the reserves, and announced a (failed) crowdfunded takeover bid of the club with ex-chairman John Ryan.
deep_cut_fact: Before fame he worked at a Vue cinema and as a waiter in the hospitality suites at Doncaster Rovers' stadium, and was an extra on TV's 'Fat Friends' (2005), where he first met James Corden.
notes: Musician, not an energy/data-center figure; entrepreneurship angle = festival, 78 Productions, '28' brand. Management reported as Matt Vines & Mark Gillespie (Three Six Zero era; https://musicbusinessworldwide.com/louis-tomlinson-signs-with-matt-vines-and-mark-gillespie-for-management) - confirm current rep. Instagram handle not verified.

name: Paul Manning
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Sensient Technologies (Milwaukee); CEO since Feb 2014
profile: Paul Manning runs Sensient Technologies, the Milwaukee-based maker of colors, flavors and extracts for food, beverage, pharma and cosmetics. He joined in 2009 as GM of Food Colors North America, ran the Color Group from 2010, became president/COO in 2012 and CEO in 2014, steering the company toward natural colors as the food industry moves away from synthetic dyes.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Sensient has become a major beneficiary of the shift from synthetic to natural food colors; revenue grew 11.6% to $462m in Q2 2026 as food makers reformulated.
deep_cut_fact: He is a trained chemist - B.S. in chemistry from Stanford, then an MBA from Northwestern (Kellogg) - and his first job at Sensient was general manager of Food Colors North America, leading the Color Group to record operating profits before becoming CEO.
notes: Succeeded Kenneth Manning (long-time CEO) in 2014. Low personal media profile; route via Sensient IR.

name: Russell Stokes
current_role: Retired from GE Aerospace (July 2026) after leading Commercial Engines & Services; independent director, UPS
profile: Russell Stokes spent about 29 years at GE. He ran GE Transportation, then GE Energy Connections, and became president and CEO of GE Power in 2017 during its restructuring. He later ran GE Aviation Services and, from 2022, GE Aerospace's $27bn Commercial Engines & Services unit with about 12,000 people. Mohamed Ali succeeded him in January 2026, and he advised CEO Larry Culp until retiring in July 2026.
interesting_fact: He ran GE Power, GE's gas-turbine and power-plant business, through its 2017-2019 turnaround and then helped lead GE Aerospace's commercial engine business. That background spans both energy generation and jet engines, highly relevant to the gas-turbine supply crunch driven by data-center power demand.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in sales at a PC manufacturer before joining GE's Financial Management Program, and holds a finance degree from Cleveland State University. In Atlanta he served on the board of Usher's New Look, the youth-leadership nonprofit founded by the singer Usher, and on Junior Achievement of Atlanta's executive committee.
notes: Retired from GE in July 2026 (Jan 15, 2026 GE 8-K/press release: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/40545/000004054526000002/exhibit991pressrelease11526.htm), so GE channels no longer apply. Still listed as a UPS director; also listed on the Morehouse School of Medicine trustee page. No verified personal social accounts found. Strong guest fit for energy/power-equipment topics; reach via his board affiliations.

name: Brian G Robins
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Snowflake Inc. (since Sept 2025); previously CFO of GitLab (2020-25)
profile: Nashville-educated finance executive (BS Finance, Lipscomb; MBA, Vanderbilt Owen) and serial software CFO at VeriSign, AlienVault, Cylance and Sisense. As GitLab's CFO from 2020 he took it through its 2021 IPO and roughly 450% revenue growth. In September 2025 he succeeded Mike Scarpelli as CFO of Snowflake, the AI Data Cloud company.
interesting_fact: He has served as CFO of six technology companies (VeriSign, AlienVault, Cylance, Sisense, GitLab and Snowflake). At GitLab, revenue rose about 450% during his tenure while he built operating leverage.
deep_cut_fact: Much of his CFO career was in cybersecurity (VeriSign, AlienVault, Cylance). He still sits on the Advisory Council of ForgePoint Capital, a cybersecurity VC, and chairs the audit committee of identity-verification company ID.me.
notes: Also listed on Brighton Park Capital's team page (advisor network). Strong fit for data-center and AI infrastructure economics. Route via Snowflake PR (Eszter Szikora, Head of PR) or IR (Katherine McCracken).

name: Christopher A Wright
current_role: 17th U.S. Secretary of Energy (sworn in Feb 4, 2025); former founder, Chairman & CEO of Liberty Energy (LBRT)
profile: MIT-trained engineer who founded Pinnacle Technologies (1992-2006), which created the hydraulic-fracture-mapping industry, chaired early shale-gas producer Stroud Energy (sold to Range Resources, 2006), then founded Liberty Oilfield Services/Liberty Energy (2011), a top US frac company. He left Liberty and his boards (incl. nuclear startup Oklo) to become Energy Secretary in 2025.
interesting_fact: Pinnacle Technologies' fracture-mapping innovations helped launch commercial shale-gas production in the late 1990s; he has also worked on next-gen geothermal (applying shale tech) and helped launch small modular reactors.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he went to MIT to work on nuclear fusion; his MIT mechanical-engineering undergraduate thesis was on using semi-viscous materials to damp vibrations in spacecraft, and he interned at Honeywell while a student.
notes: Input's SEC role (Liberty chairman/CEO) is outdated: he resigned in Feb 2025 on becoming Energy Secretary. As a cabinet official, interview requests go through DOE Office of Public Affairs (DOENews@hq.doe.gov). He was a frequent podcast guest at Liberty, so a podcast fit is plausible. Self-described 'energy nerd'; skier, cyclist, climber.

name: Maryann T. Mannen
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, Marathon Petroleum Corp. (Findlay, OH) and Chairman/CEO of MPLX LP; director, Owens Corning
profile: Career finance executive. She spent about 35 years at FMC Technologies (joined 1986), rising to CFO of FMC Technologies and then TechnipFMC, before joining Marathon Petroleum as CFO in 2021. She became president in Jan 2024, CEO in Aug 2024 and later board chair, running the largest US refiner and its MPLX midstream arm. Her wealth is largely from MPC/MPLX equity awards.
interesting_fact: She is Marathon Petroleum's first female CFO and first female CEO, and was among the few women running a Fortune 20 company when she took over in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining FMC Technologies in 1986 she was finance manager at auto-parts maker Sheller-Globe. Outside work she has served as vice chairman of the board of the Cynthia Woods Mitchell Pavilion, the outdoor concert amphitheatre in The Woodlands, Texas.

public_contacts.value: No email published; MPC Media Contact line (419) 421-3577 (Jamal Kheiry, Communications Manager)
No email published; MPC Investor Relations line (419) 421-2071

notes: A professional executive rather than a founder: the ~$53M figure is from SEC insider holdings. Corporate sites block automated fetches. Route via MPC corporate communications. The Rice Business page describes her as a speaker or guest, so she does do public appearances.

name: William L. Williams Iii
current_role: Vice Chairman, director and co-founder, Live Oak Bancshares (Live Oak Bank), Wilmington NC
profile: Lee Williams III co-founded Live Oak Bank in 2007-08 with Chip Mahan; it grew into the nation's leading SBA 7(a) lender with a branchless, tech-driven model. Before that he spent 19 years in corporate banking at Wachovia and 14 years running SBA lending at Vine Street Financial (later part of BB&T). He remains vice chairman and a director.
interesting_fact: Live Oak Bank, which he co-founded, has led the nation in SBA 7(a) lending activity, serving small businesses through a branchless, cloud-based model.
deep_cut_fact: A 1973 UNC-Chapel Hill business graduate, he started at Wachovia that year, moved to Wilmington in 1987 to run its corporate lending for three southeastern NC counties, and serves on Elon University's Board of Trustees and the New Hanover County Airport Authority board.
notes: Goes by 'Lee Williams'. Low-key, Wilmington NC civic figure.

name: Daniel Rabinowitz
current_role: Secretary and Chief Legal Officer, Natera, Inc. (Nasdaq: NTRA), Austin TX
profile: Daniel Rabinowitz is a South African-trained corporate lawyer who joined cell-free DNA testing company Natera (then Gene Security Network) in its founding year, 2004. He served as general counsel before becoming chief legal officer in April 2021. Earlier he was a corporate lawyer at Davis Polk & Wardwell (1994-2001) and a corporate partner at McDermott Will & Emery (2001-2004). His wealth comes from Natera equity.
interesting_fact: Natera grew from a 2004 startup into a leader in prenatal (Panorama), cancer-recurrence (Signatera) and transplant (Prospera) cell-free DNA tests. Rabinowitz has been its top lawyer for that entire run, including its intellectual-property work.
deep_cut_fact: He earned both a BA and an LLB at the University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg before taking an LLM at NYU School of Law and starting his US career at Davis Polk.
notes: Low public profile, typical for a general counsel. Natera changed CEOs in November 2026: Solomon Moshkevich replaced Steve Chapman, and Matthew Rabinowitz is executive chairman and co-founder. Approach through Natera corporate communications.

name: Cynthia L Tregillis
current_role: EVP, Chief Legal Officer & Corporate Secretary, Western Digital (WD) (Nasdaq: WDC)
profile: Cynthia Tregillis (UC San Diego Revelle College; University of San Francisco School of Law) was an IP and civil litigator at McDermott Will & Emery, Oppenheimer Wolff & Donnelly and Orrick. She joined Western Digital in 2012 and became Chief Legal Officer in 2025, overseeing legal, compliance, risk and government relations for the hard-drive maker as AI data-centre demand drives its growth.
interesting_fact: She sits on the boards of the Silicon Valley Leadership Group, the U.S.-India Business Council and the International AntiCounterfeiting Coalition. World Trademark Review lists her on its WTR 300 and Global Leaders lists.
deep_cut_fact: She is a founding leader of the Los Angeles chapter of ChIPs, a network advancing women in technology, policy and law. Early in her career she was a judicial clerk at the Superior Court of the District of Columbia.
notes: Highly relevant to the data-centre theme, since WD's HDDs are core data-centre storage, but she is a legal executive rather than a founder and is rarely in the media. Route via WD corporate communications.

name: Ram R. Krishnan
current_role: EVP & Chief Operating Officer, Emerson; director, Autodesk (and formerly AspenTech)
profile: An IIT metallurgical engineer with a Rensselaer master's and Xavier MBA, Ram Krishnan joined Emerson in 1994 as a project engineer. He ran Climate Technologies Asia from Hong Kong and integrated the $3.15bn Pentair valves acquisition as group president of Final Control. Since 2021 he has been Emerson's COO, overseeing supply chain, IT, M&A and international operations as Emerson becomes a pure-play automation company.
interesting_fact: CEO Lal Karsanbhai said Krishnan 'has turned final control into a world-class business' when promoting him to COO in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Emerson in 1994 as a project engineer and in 2011 moved to Hong Kong to run Climate Technologies in Asia, returning in 2015 in an unusually titled role: VP of 'profit planning and perfect execution'.
notes: Relevant to energy and industrial automation themes (Emerson automates power, LNG and data-center infrastructure). Also listed on USISPF's team page. AspenTech directorship ended when Emerson took AspenTech private in 2025.

name: Kyle Beilman
current_role: Chief Financial Officer, Chief Operating Officer and Secretary, Dave Inc. (Nasdaq: DAVE)
profile: Kyle Beilman is the finance and operations chief of Dave, the Los Angeles neobank known for small cash advances. An early employee (around 2017) who became CFO in 2022, he was promoted to CFO & COO in July 2025; he and founder-CEO Jason Wilk were Dave's only executive officers in 2025, a year in which revenue grew 60% to $554m and GAAP net income reached $196m.
interesting_fact: Dave's 2025 turnaround was dramatic: GAAP revenue up 60% to $554.2m, net income up 238% to $195.9m and adjusted EBITDA up 162% - with Beilman as one of only two executive officers.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Dave he was Head of Corporate Strategy at Red Bull North America (2016-2017); he studied at USC's Marshall School of Business.
notes: Deep-cut source is a data aggregator (MarketScreener), not a primary filing - verify before use. Low personal media profile; founder Jason Wilk is Dave's public face.

name: De Lima Filho Pedro Batista
current_role: Board member, AXIA Energia (formerly Eletrobras); founding partner, Radar Gestora (3G Radar)
profile: Pedro Batista de Lima Filho co-founded Brazilian asset manager Radar (3G Radar) in 2013 and was a 3G Capital partner until 2024; earlier he co-founded Vinci Partners and ran Brazil equity research at UBS Pactual. Since Eletrobras' 2022 privatization he has held the preferred shareholders' board seat (re-elected 2025); the utility is now AXIA Energia.
interesting_fact: After Eletrobras - Latin America's largest power utility - was privatized in 2022, he won the board seat reserved for preferred shareholders in a separate vote, and was re-elected in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an investor he was a star sell-side analyst: a Banco Pactual partner (1997-2006) whose research won Institutional Investor and LatinFinance awards across several sectors. He graduated in production engineering from UFRJ in 1997.
notes: SEC-derived net worth reflects AXIA shares held via Radar-managed funds. Private investor with little media presence; no personal accounts found. Contacts are AXIA corporate channels only.

name: Lawrence S Coben
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, NRG Energy (NYSE: NRG)
profile: Larry Coben (b. 1958), a Harvard JD and Penn PhD, is a veteran energy entrepreneur: co-founder of early alternative-energy firm Catalyst Energy, founder/CEO of Tremisis Energy, and CEO of Bolivian Power Co. NRG's chair since 2017, he became interim CEO in Nov 2023 and permanent CEO in 2024, steering NRG's push into power for data centers and its growth in generation.
interesting_fact: He is also a working archaeologist: a consulting scholar at the Penn Museum who founded the Sustainable Preservation Initiative (now the Escala Initiative) to save heritage sites by funding local, often women-led, businesses in Peru, Mexico, Tanzania and Guatemala.
deep_cut_fact: He directed excavations at the monumental Inca site of Incallajta in Bolivia, wrote a 2012 Penn dissertation titled 'Theaters of Power: Inca Imperial Performance', and co-edited the book 'Archaeology of Performance' (2006). Catalyst Energy, which he co-founded, topped Inc.'s fastest-growing public companies list.
notes: Excellent fit for energy + data-center podcast (NRG is pursuing data-center power supply). He gave a TED talk 'Build Futures, Save Pasts'. Best route: NRG Corporate Affairs.

name: Elizabeth W Vanderslice
current_role: Independent Director, AMD (since Feb 2022); Partner, Trewstar Corporate Board Services (since 2019)
profile: Elizabeth 'Beth' Vanderslice is a veteran tech board director: she sat on Xilinx's board from December 2000 until AMD acquired it in 2022, then joined AMD's board. Earlier she was CEO of Wired Digital (Wired's online arm), led its sale to Lycos and became a Lycos GM. She is now a partner at Trewstar, which places women on corporate boards, and a Boston College trustee.
interesting_fact: Her board tenure spans the FPGA era to the AI-accelerator era: 21+ years at Xilinx, then AMD as it became Nvidia's main challenger in data-center GPUs. Women Inc. named her a 2018 Most Influential Board Director.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Wired Digital (home of HotWired) in 1996-99 she worked at IBM and as a San Francisco investment banker; she holds a Boston College computer-science BS and a Harvard MBA, and is an Aspen Institute Henry Crown Fellow.
notes: Goes by 'Beth'. Her Trewstar work email is published on the firm's team page - the most direct route. AMD media contact is from a Feb 2022 release (named PR lead); verify it is current. Good angle: board governance across AMD's data-center/AI push.

name: Bryan H. Lawrence
current_role: Founder and senior manager, Yorktown Partners LLC (energy private equity, New York); director of Riley Exploration Permian, Ramaco Resources, Hallador Energy and Star Group's general partner
profile: Has run the Yorktown Partners energy funds since 1983; they began inside Dillon, Read & Co., where he worked from 1966 and was a managing director until its 1997 merger with SBC Warburg. Yorktown backs oil and gas, coal and energy-transition companies, and he sits on several listed portfolio-company boards.
interesting_fact: Through his Hallador Energy board seat he is connected to one of the more closely watched coal-to-data-centre stories: Hallador's 1 GW Merom power station in Indiana signed (and later lost) a 2025 commitment with a global data-centre developer and keeps pursuing data-centre and utility capacity deals.
deep_cut_fact: He has been in energy finance for 60 years: a Hamilton College graduate with a Columbia MBA, he joined Dillon, Read in 1966, and the first Yorktown funds were started inside that firm before the founders took the business independent when Dillon Read merged with SBC Warburg in 1997.
notes: Do not confuse with Bryan Ross Lawrence (Oakcliff Capital, also a Yorktown partner). Net worth figure is SEC-insider-derived only. Low media profile; Yorktown's general inbox is the published route. Age 82 per April 2025 proxy.

name: C Clark Webb
current_role: Co-founder and Principal, 210 Capital (Dallas); former Co-CEO (2017-2023), Executive Vice Chairman and director (until Nov 2024) of P10, Inc. (NYSE: PX)
profile: Clark Webb is a Dallas investor who, with Robert Alpert, built P10 from a tax-asset shell into a listed private-markets asset manager. He was Co-CEO from 2017 to 2023, then Executive Vice Chairman, and left the board in November 2024 as the 210 Group sold down its stake. He earlier co-managed P10 Capital Management and the Lafayette Street Fund and was a partner at Select Equity Group. He has a 2003 BA from Princeton.
interesting_fact: P10 started life as Active Power, a power-equipment maker founded in Texas in 1992. In 2016 it sold its operations to Langley Holdings/Piller, kept about $235M of tax losses, and was renamed P10 Industries. Webb and Alpert then used it as a platform to acquire private-equity managers.
deep_cut_fact: He has chaired Elah Holdings, an investment holding company, and Collaborative Imaging, a healthcare technology and management services organisation. He also sat on the board of Globalscape, a maker of secure enterprise file-transfer software.
notes: The SEC holdings figure dates from 2024 and he has since sold much of his P10 stake (13D/A filings from Oct 2024 to Jan 2025). Podcast angle: P10's origin as a data-centre power company (Active Power) turned into an investment vehicle. I found no published personal or 210 Capital contact.

name: Charles M Royce
current_role: Founder and Senior Advisor, Royce Investment Partners (Royce & Associates), New York
profile: 'Chuck' Royce is a pioneer of small-cap investing. He started as an equity analyst and in 1972 founded what became Royce Investment Partners, managing the Pennsylvania Mutual Fund and later the Royce closed-end trusts (RMT, RGT, RVT). Royce later became part of Legg Mason and then Franklin Templeton. He stepped back from day-to-day portfolio management to Senior Advisor in 2024.
interesting_fact: He has run small-cap money for more than 50 years. Morningstar called him a 'small-cap investing legend' when he moved to Senior Advisor at the firm he founded in 1972.
deep_cut_fact: His firm says he did not initially see himself as a value investor or even as a risk manager. Early experience shaped his rule that long-term success comes from both preserving and growing capital, and that the approach works best in under-researched small caps that institutions ignore.
notes: Born around 1939. No obituary was found on the firm site, but the web-search budget ran out before a news check, so confirm 'alive' before outreach. His 2024 Barron's Q&A and his firm's media page are the best routes. He is also widely reported as owner of the Ocean House and Weekapaug Inn hotels in Rhode Island, but that was not verified here.

name: John Sculley
current_role: Investor and adviser; co-founder and, until his June 2025 retirement, board director of Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA); former Apple CEO
profile: Brown (architectural design) and Wharton MBA graduate who became PepsiCo's youngest president, creating the Pepsi Challenge, then ran Apple from 1983 to 1993 as sales grew from about $1B to $8B. He co-founded marketing-data company Zeta Global with David Steinberg in 2007 and backed health-tech (RxAdvance) and other startups; he retired from Zeta's board in June 2025.
interesting_fact: He has said moving the Mac to PowerPC instead of Intel was his greatest mistake at Apple; Zeta honoured him as 'co-founder and visionary board member' when he retired in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: A teenage electronics tinkerer, he built a color cathode-ray picture tube at about 14; his own speaker bio says that if someone hadn't beaten him to the patent, it would have been the prototype for Sony's Trinitron tube.
notes: Born 1939; lives in Palm Beach. Active on the speaking circuit, so the speaker-booking site is the most direct published route (it blocked automated fetch; the bio claim comes via search snippet and SiliconANGLE). Zeta Global IR is a secondary route. Avoid the Jobs ouster and Spectrum lawsuit; Obi Worldphone is also sensitive.

name: William George Iii
current_role: EVP and Chief Financial Officer (since 2005) and Regional Vice President, Comfort Systems USA (NYSE: FIX), Houston
profile: William George (61) was on the founding management team that formed Comfort Systems USA in 1997, a roll-up of mechanical and electrical contractors. He was its general counsel until 2005 and has been CFO since. The company now has $12bn+ in yearly revenue, with demand driven especially by the technology sector and data centers.
interesting_fact: Comfort Systems has become a major play on the AI and data-center buildout. Its 2025 10-K credits especially strong demand from the technology sector, 'particularly for data centers', for its revenue growth and it bought J&S, a data-center HVAC specialist.
deep_cut_fact: He is a lawyer turned CFO: a BYU economics graduate with a Harvard Law JD, he practised corporate and antitrust law at Ropes & Gray in Boston (1992-95) and was GC of American Medical Response before helping found Comfort Systems.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center podcast because Comfort Systems builds data-center mechanical and electrical systems. The IR inbox is the published route, since the CFO handles investor communications.

name: John T. Treace
current_role: Founder, Chief Executive Officer and Board Chair, Treace Medical Concepts (Nasdaq: TMCI), Ponte Vedra, FL
profile: John Treace founded Treace Medical Concepts in 2014 and has led it as CEO since inception (Board Chair since May 2025). The company makes the Lapiplasty 3D bunion-correction system. Before founding it he spent over a decade at Wright Medical Group, rising to SVP of U.S. Sales and Global Marketing, after earlier marketing roles at Xomed Surgical Products.
interesting_fact: Treace's patented Lapiplasty System for three-dimensional bunion correction has treated over 134,000 patients since late 2015; in 2025 he broadened the company into a full 'bunion solutions' business covering all four bunion classes.
deep_cut_fact: He studied finance, not medicine (BS in Finance, Seattle University), and started in med-tech as a senior product manager at Xomed Surgical Products in 1996.
notes: Med-tech founder; entrepreneurship angle but no energy/data-center link. No published press/IR email found in the proxy; check Treace's press releases for IR/media contacts.

name: Thomas J McInerney
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Genworth Financial (NYSE: GNW), since January 2013; director, Enact Holdings
profile: Career insurance executive who has led Genworth since 2013, steering it through long-term-care insurance restructuring and the 2021 IPO of its mortgage-insurance arm Enact. Previously COO of ING's global insurance and investment management business and a senior advisor at BCG, after a long career at Aetna.
interesting_fact: He began his career in June 1978 as an insurance underwriter at Aetna and rose to run one of America's largest long-term-care insurers.
deep_cut_fact: Outside insurance he serves as Vice Chair of United Way Worldwide and sits on the boards of the Irish Arts Council and the U.S. Ski and Snowboard Foundation; he is a Colgate economics graduate with a Tuck MBA.
notes: Off-theme for energy/data centers. No press email found; IR address is the published corporate route.

name: Joshua Horowitz
current_role: Portfolio Manager & MD, Palm Management (US) LLC; Chairman of Limbach Holdings and BK Technologies; Director, Barnwell Industries and Kingsway Financial
profile: Joshua Horowitz is a small-cap activist-style investor who manages the Palm Global Small Cap Master Fund (Palm entities since 2012) and chairs Limbach Holdings (building systems, since 2024) and BK Technologies (radios, since 2023). Earlier he was Director of Research at Berggruen Holdings and an analyst at Crossway Partners.
interesting_fact: Served as interim chairman of Birner Dental Management Services - then the only publicly traded U.S. dental service organization - through its 2019 sale, and helped lead NeuroMetrix's 2025 sale to electroCore.
deep_cut_fact: Magna cum laude B.S. in Management from Binghamton University, studied at the University of Bath School of Management, and holds an NACD/Carnegie Mellon cyber-risk oversight certificate.
notes: Limbach (mechanical/electrical building systems incl. data-center work) is a relevant angle. Best route is via Limbach or BK Technologies IR.

name: Andrew Miles Snyder
current_role: CEO, Cambridge Information Group (family investment firm, since 2003); Non-executive Chair, Clarivate plc
profile: Andrew Snyder runs Cambridge Information Group, a family-owned investment firm focused on real estate, education, technology and information services. current_role: CFO, Casey's General Stores (Nasdaq: CASY); director, Cracker Barrel Old Country Store
profile: Finance executive who has been CFO of Casey's, the Midwest convenience-store and fuel chain, since May 2020, overseeing finance, fuel, strategy, M&A and data/analytics. current_role: Executive Chairman and CEO, Spectrum Brands Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: SPB), Middleton, Wisconsin
profile: David Maura is a former distressed-debt analyst (Merrill Lynch, First Albany) who joined Philip Falcone's Harbinger Capital in 2006 and became EVP of Investments at Harbinger's HRG Group. name: Richard D Francis
current_role: President & CEO, Teva Pharmaceutical Industries (since January 2023)
profile: Richard Francis, a British pharma executive, became Teva's CEO in 2023 and launched its 'Pivot to Growth' strategy toward innovative and biosimilar medicines. profile: Sean Hennessy, a CPA and University of Akron graduate, was Sherwin-Williams' CFO from 2001 to 2016, then SVP Corporate Planning, Development & Administration, leading the Valspar integration until 2018. He now sits on the boards of TransDigm and Perimeter Solutions.

name: H Eric Bolton Jr

profile: Eric Bolton joined Memphis-based apartment REIT MAA in 1994 and was CEO from 2001 to March 2025, building it into a leading Sun Belt multifamily owner, including the 2016 Post Properties merger. Brad Hill succeeded him as CEO, and Bolton is executive chairman through 2026. He has been an EastGroup director since 2013.

profile: Italian-born photonics engineer and executive (BSEE Bari, PhD photonics Glasgow) who held roles at BT Labs, AT&T Bell Labs, Lucent and HP before becoming CEO of optical-components maker Avanex until its merger into Oclaro. current_role: Moderator/co-host of ABC's The View (since 2007); co-founder of All Women's Sports Network (AWSN)
profile: Born Caryn Elaine Johnson in New York in 1955. She is an EGOT-winning actor and comedian (Emmy, Grammy, Oscar for Ghost, Tony) who broke through with her one-woman show and The Color Purple. She has moderated ABC's The View since 2007 and has business ventures, including co-founding AWSN, an all-women's sports streaming network launched on Pluto TV in 2025.
interesting_fact: She is one of only about 28 people to have won an EGOT. In June 2025 she announced she had co-founded AWSN, a network dedicated entirely to women's sports, streaming on Pluto TV.
deep_cut_fact: Before fame, while living in Berkeley in the 1970s, she worked odd jobs as a bank teller, a bricklayer and a mortuary cosmetologist. Seeing Nichelle Nichols as Uhura on TV as a child sparked her lifelong Star Trek fandom, which later led to her role as Guinan.
notes: Best podcast angle is entrepreneurship: AWSN (women's sports media). Route via ABC/The View press or her talent representation; no published email was found. Couldn't confirm 2026 status on The View beyond late-2025 coverage.

name: Lionel Bonnot
current_role: Executive Vice President, Worldwide Sales and Business Development, SiTime Corp
profile: Lionel Bonnot is a French-born semiconductor sales and business-development executive who joined SiTime, the MEMS precision-timing chip company, in 2018 and now runs its worldwide sales. SiTime's timing devices are increasingly used in AI data-center and networking hardware. He previously held senior roles at Quantenna Communications and Ikanos Communications.
interesting_fact: SiTime is the third company where he has helped lead the journey from pre-revenue through IPO and beyond (after Ikanos and Quantenna).
deep_cut_fact: He holds a Master of Science in computer science from the Ecole Nationale Superieure d'Informatique in Paris, and at Ikanos served as vice president of Europe before running North America and EMEA sales.
notes: Strong data-center fit: SiTime's MEMS timing/clock chips target AI data-center and networking hardware. Sources differ on his 2007-17 employer (SiTime says Quantenna).

name: Barbara Weber
current_role: Executive Chair, Tango Therapeutics (Nasdaq: TNGX), stepping down per an Aug 2026 announcement; Director, Revolution Medicines
profile: Barbara Weber, M.D. (Yale residency, Dana-Farber fellowship) was a genetics professor at Michigan and Penn, then led oncology R&D at GSK and Novartis. At Third Rock Ventures she co-launched Tango Therapeutics and Relay Therapeutics, and she was Tango's founding CEO (2017 to Jan 2026). She then became Executive Chair; in Aug 2026 Tango said she would step down for other pursuits.
interesting_fact: Tango launched in March 2017 with a $55m Series A from Third Rock Ventures to find synthetic-lethal targets in cancer. At Third Rock she also helped found Relay Therapeutics and was interim CMO of Neon Therapeutics.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech she had a full academic career as a professor of genetics at both the University of Michigan and the University of Pennsylvania. She left academia for R&D leadership at GSK and then Novartis.
notes: She did a long-form interview on Luke Timmerman's 'The Long Run' podcast, so she is open to podcasts. She is in transition after leaving Tango ('other pursuits'), so her next role may be newsworthy. Off-theme for energy, but fits the entrepreneurship angle.

name: Noel R. Wallace
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Colgate-Palmolive; director, American Express
profile: Texas A&M finance graduate who joined Colgate-Palmolive in 1987 and spent his career there, running the global toothbrush division, North America and Latin America before becoming president/COO in 2018. He has been CEO since April 2019 and chairman since April 2020, focusing on premium oral care, Hill's pet nutrition and sustainability.
interesting_fact: He has spent his whole career, nearly 40 years, at Colgate-Palmolive, starting in 1987.
deep_cut_fact: He ran Colgate's Global Toothbrush Division (2002-2006) and later combined the North America presidency with responsibility for global sustainability.
notes: Business Roundtable member. High-profile consumer-goods CEO; any approach goes through Colgate corporate communications. Less natural fit for an energy/data-center theme beyond sustainability.

name: Kade Matthews
current_role: Director (since 1998), First Financial Bankshares (Abilene, TX); President, Ruth and Percy Jones Foundation and Dodge Jones Legacy Foundation; rancher
profile: Kade L. Matthews, 68, is a rancher and investor from Clarendon, Texas who has sat on the board of First Financial Bankshares and its bank since 1998, holding about 1.29m shares. He presides over two Texas private charitable foundations and has long been involved in Texas higher-education and health philanthropy.
interesting_fact: He is President of the Ruth and Percy Jones Foundation and the Dodge Jones Legacy Foundation, private Texas charitable foundations, and an Emeritus Trustee of his alma mater, Texas Christian University.
deep_cut_fact: A Panhandle rancher, he is a former regent of Clarendon College and former president of the Clarendon College Foundation, and sits on MD Anderson Cancer Center's board of visitors.
notes: Very private, low public profile; rural ranching/investments background. No published personal or foundation email found; FFIN corporate office in Abilene is the only formal route.

name: Steven J. Demetriou
current_role: Executive Chair of the Board, Amentum Holdings, Inc. (NYSE: AMTM); director of FirstEnergy and Arcosa
profile: Chemical engineer turned industrial CEO: Exxon/ExxonMobil and Cytec (1981-99), CEO of Noveon (2001-04) and Aleris (2004-15), then CEO (2015) and chair/CEO (2016-23) of Jacobs. After retiring as Jacobs CEO he became executive chair, then led the 2024 merger of Jacobs' government services unit with Amentum, a defense, space and nuclear engineering contractor. His Amentum agreement was extended open-ended in Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: Amentum, which he chairs, is engineering heavy in energy: e.g. a JV it leads won a $406m owner's-engineer contract for the UK's first small modular reactors, and it supports NASA Artemis ground systems.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in chemical engineering from Tufts University and began his career in 1981 in engineering and leadership roles at Exxon (later ExxonMobil) before moving to Cytec Industries.
notes: Net worth (~$44m in SEC-reported holdings) is far below UHNW; included via SEC insider data. Strong energy angle via FirstEnergy board seat and Amentum's nuclear/SMR work. Sept 2026 8-K confirms he continues as Executive Chair. Press contact varies by release; David Hylton listed on Oct 2026 release.

name: Nora Denzel
current_role: Lead Independent Director, AMD; board member of Sony Group, Gen Digital, SUSE and NACD
profile: Nora M. Denzel is a Silicon Valley technology executive turned full-time director. She started as an IBM engineer (13 years), then held senior roles at Legato Systems, HP and Intuit, where she retired in 2012 as SVP of Big Data. She was interim CEO of Redbox parent Outerwall in 2015 and has been AMD's Lead Independent Director since 2022 (on its board since 2014).
interesting_fact: She has been on AMD's board since 2014, through the company's turnaround under Lisa Su into a major data-center CPU and AI GPU supplier, and has been Lead Independent Director since Nov 2022.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 she stepped in as interim CEO of Outerwall, the parent of Redbox DVD kiosks and Coinstar coin machines. Earlier, at Intuit, she led big-data analytics across the TurboTax/Mint maker's roughly 50 million customers. She also spent 10 years on the board of AnitaB.org, which works to get more women into computing.
notes: Wealth is from director stock holdings, not founder equity. She speaks frequently (NACD, RSA Conference) and a speaker bureau lists her for bookings, so a podcast invitation via a speaker agency or NACD is plausible. AMD IR (ir.amd.com) handles board correspondence.

name: David Liu
current_role: Richard Merkin Professor and director of the Merkin Institute, Broad Institute; Thomas Dudley Cabot Professor at Harvard; HHMI Investigator; co-founder of Prime Medicine (PRME) and Beam Therapeutics
profile: David R. Liu (劉如謙, b. 1973, Riverside, CA) is a Harvard/Broad chemical biologist who invented base editing (2016) and prime editing (2019), two of the main gene-editing technologies after CRISPR nucleases. His wealth is equity in companies he co-founded, including Prime Medicine (a 10%+ holder), Beam Therapeutics, Editas and Pairwise. He won the 2025 Breakthrough Prize in Life Sciences.
interesting_fact: Liu gives away his entire salary to the students and researchers in his lab every Thanksgiving. As a high-schooler he placed second in the national 1990 Westinghouse Science Talent Search.
deep_cut_fact: Liu was a formidable Street Fighter II player and helped create Naughty Dog's 1994 fighting game 'Way of the Warrior', in which he also voiced the character Chin 'The Dragon' Liu. Naughty Dog co-founder Andy Gavin called him 'insanely good' at Street Fighter.
notes: Hurun's 'AI' tag is misleading: he is a gene-editing scientist, not AI or energy. The lab site directs general questions to Dr. Anahita Vieira (Manager of Communications & Outreach) or Emily Botelho (Chief of Staff). His own email is published for prospective postdocs and students, so media requests should go through the communications contact or the Broad press office.

name: Khozema Shipchandler
current_role: CEO and board member, Twilio Inc.; director, Ethos Technologies
profile: Twilio's CEO since January 2024, succeeding co-founder Jeff Lawson. He joined Twilio as CFO in 2018, then served as COO and President of Twilio Communications. Before Twilio he spent over two decades at GE in finance and operating roles across Industrial Internet (GE Digital), Corporate Audit and Aviation.
interesting_fact: He rose from CFO (2018) to COO (2021) to President of Twilio Communications (2023) and then CEO (Jan 2024), one of the few finance chiefs to take over from a founder-CEO at a major developer-platform company.
deep_cut_fact: His GE career took him abroad: he held operating and financial roles at GE in the U.S., the Middle East and Singapore, across Industrial Internet, Corporate Audit and Aviation. He is an Indiana University Bloomington graduate.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Twilio press office. Speaks at Twilio SIGNAL conferences.

name: Eric M Demarco
current_role: President, CEO and Director, Kratos Defense & Security Solutions (NASDAQ: KTOS)
profile: Eric DeMarco joined Wireless Facilities Inc. in 2003 as President/COO and became CEO in April 2004, transforming it into Kratos, a national-security technology firm in drones, hypersonics, space, propulsion and microwave electronics. Previously President/COO of Titan Corporation. His wealth comes from Kratos equity.
interesting_fact: He led Kratos' pivot from a commercial wireless-infrastructure services company to a defense-tech maker of jet-powered unmanned aircraft (e.g. the XQ-58 Valkyrie), hypersonic systems and satellite ground systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before defense, he started in public accounting; at Titan Corporation he helped grow annualized revenue from about $150M to $1.5B. He graduated summa cum laude from the University of New Hampshire (B.S. business administration & finance) and sits on the Aerospace Industries Association's Board of Governors.
notes: Press contact Claire Cantrell is listed on Kratos releases; IR phone 877-934-4687. Frequent CEO interviewee (TWST, earnings calls) on defense/drones.

name: Rollin L. Ford
current_role: Independent Director, Symbotic Inc. (since ~2022); retired Walmart EVP & Chief Administrative Officer
profile: Rollin Ford spent 33 years at Walmart, where he held several executive roles including Chief Logistics Officer, CIO (2006-2012) and finally EVP & Chief Administrative Officer, before retiring in 2016. He now sits on the board of warehouse-robotics firm Symbotic, in which Walmart is a major customer and shareholder.
interesting_fact: He ran IT for the world's largest retailer as Walmart's CIO from 2006 to 2012, after years running its logistics network as Chief Logistics Officer.
deep_cut_fact: He began at Walmart as an intern in 1983 and moved onto a distribution-center floor role in 1984 before rising to the C-suite; he holds a B.S. from Taylor University.
notes: Low public profile; board member, not executive. The Walmart careers article on his intern-to-exec path (deep-cut source) now returns 404 - verify via archive before quoting. Also reportedly on boards of Mercy Health and John Brown University (CB Insights). Strong fit for supply-chain automation angle.

name: Jeffrey Hessekiel
current_role: EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer, Cytokinetics (since Nov 2025)
profile: Biopharma lawyer who was EVP & General Counsel of Exelixis from 2014 to 2025, leading 100+ legal, IP, compliance, quality and government-affairs staff. Earlier he spent a decade at Gilead (ending as Chief Compliance & Quality Officer) and was Senior Counsel at Arnold & Porter. In November 2025 he joined Cytokinetics as EVP, Chief Legal & Administrative Officer.
interesting_fact: Before law school he worked with international nongovernmental organizations; he went on to hold legal roles at Wilson Sonsini and Heller Ehrman before moving in-house at Gilead in 2002.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of HairToStay, a nonprofit that helps cancer patients afford scalp cooling to preserve their hair during chemotherapy, as well as Biocom California and Life Sciences Cares. Duke political science BA; GWU Law JD.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; low public profile. Cytokinetics media/IR contact in 2026 releases is Diane Weiser, SVP Corporate Affairs (company line published in releases, e.g. https://ir.cytokinetics.com/press-releases/press-release-details/2026/Cytokinetics-to-Participate-in-June-Investor-Conferences/default.aspx).

name: John Christopher Sullivan
current_role: Executive Vice President, General Counsel & Corporate Secretary, Costco Wholesale Corp.
profile: John Sullivan is Costco's top lawyer. He has been Corporate Secretary since 2010 and General Counsel since 2016, and he became an executive officer in 2021. He leads the legal function at the Issaquah, WA-based warehouse retailer. His reported wealth comes from Costco equity disclosed in SEC insider filings.
interesting_fact: Costco's 10-K says he has been Corporate Secretary since 2010 and General Counsel since 2016. He was named an executive officer (EVP) in 2021. In a 2014 SEC letter he signed as VP, Associate General Counsel & Secretary.
notes: Low-profile in-house lawyer with almost no public interviews. A common name: several other lawyers called John Sullivan (TI China, Carlson Inc.) show up in searches, so don't mix them up. Best route is Costco corporate or IR.

name: Nancy Quan
current_role: EVP and Global Chief Technical & Innovation Officer, The Coca-Cola Company
profile: Purdue-trained food/nutrition scientist who spent years at Mars Inc. (R&D, business development, manufacturing) before joining Coca-Cola in 2007 as R&D GM for Europe/Eurasia in Brussels. Rose through Global R&D Officer and CTO roles; now EVP overseeing technical, innovation and supply chain for all Coca-Cola brands, reporting to CEO James Quincey.
interesting_fact: She led a redesign of Coca-Cola's plastic bottles in India that cut plastic use by 38% without sacrificing quality or carbonation.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Newton County, Indiana, was starting point guard and valedictorian at South Newton High; her first job out of Purdue (after a Mars internship) was on the Dove chocolate line, where she helped develop heat-stable chocolate for troops in the Middle East. Received Purdue HHS Distinguished Alumni Award (2025).
notes: Corporate executive (wealth from KO equity). Reach via Coca-Cola media relations. Reportedly also a non-exec director of Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (secondary source, unverified).

name: Satish Dhanasekaran
current_role: President and CEO, Keysight Technologies; director, Zebra Technologies
profile: Engineer-turned-executive who joined Agilent (Keysight's predecessor) in 2006 and rose through its communications business to COO before becoming Keysight's second-ever CEO on May 1, 2022. Wealth is from executive equity rather than founding. He now runs the ~$5B test-and-measurement company spanning 5G/6G, AI data-center interconnect, quantum and aerospace/defense.
interesting_fact: Before becoming CEO he led Keysight's multi-billion-dollar Communications Solutions Group and is credited with helping establish Keysight's leadership in 5G test; he also sponsors Keysight's seat on the FCC Technological Advisory Committee and the NextG Alliance.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a master's in electrical engineering from Florida State University and started at the company in 2006 as an engineer before moving into management.
notes: Hired executive, not a founder. Keysight's AI data-center interconnect (1.6T) test work is a natural podcast hook. Route via Keysight corporate communications (Andrea Mueller listed as worldwide editorial contact).

name: Lauren R Hobart
current_role: President & CEO, DICK'S Sporting Goods (incl. Foot Locker); independent director, Marriott International
profile: Penn and Stanford MBA graduate who worked at Wells Fargo, JPMorgan Chase and 14 years at PepsiCo (incl. CMO of carbonated soft drinks NA) before joining DICK'S as CMO in 2011. Became president in 2017 and in Feb 2021 succeeded Ed Stack as CEO, the first non-Stack-family CEO; she now also runs the acquired Foot Locker business.
interesting_fact: She is only the third CEO in DICK'S 75+-year history and the first from outside the founding Stack family.
deep_cut_fact: She personally initiated DICK'S 'Sports Matter' program in 2014, which funds grants, equipment and sponsorships for underserved youth sports teams; she is also president of The DICK'S Sporting Goods Foundation.
notes: Fortune (Mar 2022) profiled how her psychology interest shaped her leadership - useful hook. Best route is DICK'S corporate communications.

name: Ralph J Andretta
current_role: President and CEO and director, Bread Financial Holdings (NYSE: BFH), Columbus, Ohio
profile: Card-industry executive who became CEO of Alliance Data Systems in February 2020 and led its transformation into Bread Financial, a tech-forward consumer credit/payments company. Earlier he was Managing Director and Head of U.S. Cards at Citi, held affinity and international card roles at Bank of America, and spent 18 years at American Express. Wealth is from BFH equity.
interesting_fact: He steered Alliance Data's reinvention: spinning off its loyalty business and renaming the company Bread Financial in 2022, refocusing it on private-label/co-brand credit cards and the Bread Pay buy-now-pay-later platform.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career with an 18-year run at American Express before moving to Bank of America and Citi, and holds a bachelor's degree in accounting and finance from Siena College.
notes: Public-company CEO; route via Bread Financial media relations (Rachel Stultz). Fintech/consumer credit angle rather than energy.

name: Michael D Cordano
current_role: Executive Vice President, Worldwide Sales, Micron Technology (since Jan 2025), reporting to CEO Sanjay Mehrotra
profile: Mike Cordano is a storage/memory industry veteran: EVP of sales and marketing at Hitachi Global Storage Technologies (HGST), then 8+ years at Western Digital after it bought HGST, rising to President and COO. He later founded investment group Prime Impact Capital, and in January 2025 joined Micron to run global sales during the AI-driven boom in HBM and data-center memory.
interesting_fact: He succeeded Mike Bokan, a 28-year Micron veteran, as head of worldwide sales - an outside hire into Micron's top sales job just as AI data centers drove record demand for high-bandwidth memory.
deep_cut_fact: He is a University of Colorado graduate (B.S. in business administration and management) and sits on the board of advisors of CU Boulder's Leeds School of Business.
notes: Not to be confused with WD CEO David Goeckeler; Cordano was WD President/COO. Press/IR emails are Micron's named media and IR contacts in the Jan 2025 release (may have changed). Strong data-center/AI memory angle.

name: Fred E Cohen
current_role: Co-founder & Chairman, Monograph Capital; Co-founder & Senior Managing Director, Vida Ventures; director at Intellia, CareDx, Kyverna
profile: Physician-scientist (Yale BS, Oxford DPhil as a Rhodes Scholar, Stanford MD) who spent 1980-2014 at UCSF, including as Chief of Endocrinology and Metabolism. Co-founded TPG Biotech (2001-2016), then Vida Ventures (2017) and Monograph Capital; sits on several biotech boards.
interesting_fact: Has published 200+ peer-reviewed papers, is co-inventor on 10+ patents, and was elected to the National Academy of Medicine (2004) and American Academy of Arts and Sciences (2008).
deep_cut_fact: His UCSF research covered prion diseases and structure-based drug design, and he shared the LVMH 'Science pour l'art' prize with Nobel laureate Stanley Prusiner.
notes: Best route is via Monograph Capital's published media/info emails. Biotech investor; little energy/data-center overlap beyond computational biology.

name: Hao-Yuan Chuang
current_role: Chief Financial Officer & Director, Belite Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: BLTE)
profile: Hao-Yuan Chuang has been CFO of Belite Bio, a San Diego/Taiwan-linked clinical-stage biotech developing tinlarebant for Stargardt disease and geographic atrophy, since April 2020 and a director since Nov 2021. He previously was CFO of parent Lin BioScience (TPEx: 6696). His wealth is tied to Belite equity; Belite has submitted an NDA for tinlarebant in Stargardt disease.
interesting_fact: Belite Bio completed a rolling NDA submission to the US FDA for tinlarebant, an oral drug for Stargardt disease, a juvenile macular degeneration with no approved therapy.
deep_cut_fact: Before biotech he worked in institutional investing: Investment Director at Suning International and Portfolio Manager at The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China; he holds a triple MBA (Columbia, London Business School, HKU) plus CFA and FRM.
notes: Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Best route is Belite IR (Jennifer Wu, ir@belitebio.com). Biotech, not energy/data-center.

name: Hilary Shane
current_role: Private investor; >5% / 10% beneficial owner of FONAR Corp (FONR) via a revocable trust
profile: Hilary L. Shane is a private investor who has accumulated a large stake in MRI company FONAR Corp; a January 2026 Schedule 13G (filed as a passive investor) reported ~6.66% of FONAR's common stock, and Form 4s show continued open-market purchases in 2026. No public biography or operating role found.
interesting_fact: Her FONAR holdings are reported through the Hilary L. Shane Revocable Trust and filed on a passive basis, stating the shares are not held to influence control of the company.
notes: Very private individual investor; no public profile, website or social accounts found. Only public trace is SEC filings (EDGAR CIK filings for FONR). Identity beyond the filings could not be confirmed. Not a fit for outreach without a warm intro.

name: Andrew Fentress
current_role: Chairman of the Board and Managing Director, Capital Markets (principal executive officer), ACRES Commercial Realty Corp. (NYSE: ACR); co-founder, ACRES Capital
profile: Commercial real estate lender who co-founded ACRES Capital in 2012 and has chaired mortgage REIT ACRES Commercial Realty since July 2020. He started at Morgan Stanley in institutional equities in 1995, moved into private credit in 2004 and was a founding/managing partner of direct lender Medley before ACRES, which he says manages about $4B.
interesting_fact: He pivoted from corporate private credit to commercial real estate lending after the financial crisis, building ACRES on a loss-control philosophy: 'In credit, you're only as good as your losses.'
deep_cut_fact: He sailed four years on Boston College's varsity sailing team, competing in national championships, and right after college sold NordicTrack fitness equipment for an entrepreneur he had worked for as a student, before Morgan Stanley.
notes: Appeared on Dakota Rainmaker podcast (comfortable with podcast format). Internalization of ACR management closed Aug 2026 per secondary profile; title may be evolving.

name: Raymond T. White
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Director, Legion Partners Asset Management; director of NN Inc., Clear Channel Outdoor and Lifecore Biomedical
profile: Raymond T. 'Ted' White co-founded Legion Partners (2012), a Los Angeles long-only activist fund focused on North American small caps. Earlier he was Director of Corporate Governance at CalPERS and COO of European activist Knight Vinke. He joined Clear Channel Outdoor's board in Jan 2024 and NN Inc.'s in Jan 2026 via a Legion cooperation agreement.
interesting_fact: At CalPERS he ran the entire corporate-governance program, including $3 billion in active management, proxy voting and focused engagement, before switching sides to become an activist investor.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an Investment Officer / Deputy State Treasurer in the California State Treasurer's Office doing fixed-income trading, and later co-chaired the ICGN Executive Remuneration Committee (to Dec 2014) and sat on the PCAOB Standing Advisory Group.
notes: Goes by 'Ted White'. Board seats come via Legion Partners activism; firm's general email is the published route. NN appointment: https://www.nninc.com/?p=4834

name: Christopher S Kiper
current_role: Co-founder, Managing Director & Chief Investment Officer, Legion Partners Asset Management; director, Lifecore Biomedical (since 2023)
profile: Christopher Kiper co-founded Legion Partners (Los Angeles, 2012), a long-only activist fund targeting North American small caps with fewer than 15 concentrated positions. His wealth tracks Legion's activist stakes, including a 10%+ holding in Lifecore Biomedical, where he sits on the board as Legion's representative. He has also served on boards such as NN Inc.
interesting_fact: Legion describes its method as a 'private equity approach to investing in public equities', running a concentrated book of fewer than 15 small-cap positions and engaging boards directly.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Legion he worked at Shamrock Capital, the Disney family's investment firm. On the Beyond the Boardroom podcast he said 'most boards need upgrading' and that replacing directors is one of the biggest ways to change a company.
notes: Activist investor, not an operator, but a good fit for small-cap governance/value angles. Clear Channel Outdoor's 2024 Legion board seat went to co-founder Ted White, and I could not confirm Kiper sat on the CCO board, so the SEC-derived CCO directorship may be a data error. CCO was later taken private by Mubadala. Reach him through Legion's general inbox.

name: Bruce A Ogilvie Jr
current_role: Executive Chairman, Alliance Entertainment Holding Corp (Nasdaq: AENT)
profile: Veteran music/video wholesale distributor. Founded Abbey Road Distributors (sold to Alliance in the early 1990s), bought a one-third stake in one-stop Super D in 2001 as co-CEO, and in 2013 Super D acquired Alliance Entertainment, with Ogilvie as chairman. Alliance went public via SPAC (Adara) in 2023; he remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: Alliance is one of the world's largest distributors of physical media (CDs, vinyl, DVDs, games); Ogilvie has said 'We are long on physical — we want to be the last guy standing.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Super D, he founded Abbey Road Distributors, a music wholesaler known for aggressive pricing, which he sold to Alliance in the early '90s — so in 2013 he effectively bought back the company that had bought his first one.
notes: Low public profile; little personal biography online. IR handled by RedChip Companies (Dave Gentry). Has appeared on investor podcasts (Wall Street Resource, SPAC podcast).

name: Michael A Carusi
current_role: Managing Partner, Lightstone Ventures; General Partner, Advanced Technology Ventures; director, Shoulder Innovations (SI)
profile: Mike Carusi is a life-sciences venture capitalist who joined Advanced Technology Ventures in 1998 and co-founded Lightstone Ventures, investing in biopharma and medical devices. He joined the board of shoulder-implant maker Shoulder Innovations in 2020 with its Series C, and the company's IPO is the source of his listed SEC insider holdings.
interesting_fact: He has appeared on the Forbes Midas List, served on the National Venture Capital Association board and taught as an adjunct professor at Dartmouth's Tuck School of Business.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer (B.S., Lehigh). Before VC he was business-development director at Inhale Therapeutic Systems (now Nektar), and earlier at consultancy The Wilkerson Group he helped open its London and San Francisco offices.
notes: Investor-director, not a founder. The firm site gives no published email; contact goes through the Lightstone website. Aggregator sites disagree on whether his Shoulder Innovations board seat continues in 2026, so check the latest proxy.

name: Andrew R J Bonfield
current_role: CFO Emeritus / retired CFO, Caterpillar Inc. (advisory role May-Oct 2026); Senior Independent Non-Executive Director, Reckitt
profile: South African-trained chartered accountant who became one of the most experienced big-company CFOs: SmithKline Beecham, BG Group, Bristol-Myers Squibb (2002-08), National Grid (2010-18) and Caterpillar (2018-26), where he was the first CFO hired from outside. He handed over to Kyle Epley in May 2026 and retires Oct 1, 2026.
interesting_fact: Named 2025 CFO of the Year by the CFO Leadership Council and Chief Executive Group; he was Caterpillar's first externally hired CFO after a long insider tradition.
deep_cut_fact: After joining Caterpillar he trained at its Peoria demonstration and learning center, driving an articulated truck and operating an excavator: 'The best way to learn the iron is to get on it.' He earned his BCom at the University of Natal in Durban.
notes: Ex-National Grid CFO, so the energy/utility angle is relevant. Caterpillar press releases list enterprise media contacts, but the pages blocked fetching so I couldn't verify them; use the caterpillar.com newsroom. Now leaving executive life, so he may have more time.

name: Robert Frenzel
current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Xcel Energy (Minneapolis); director, Patterson Companies
profile: Bob Frenzel runs Xcel Energy, a major US electric and gas utility serving eight states. A former Navy nuclear engineering officer and Goldman Sachs banker, he was an Energy Future Holdings/Luminant executive before joining Xcel as CFO in 2016; CEO since Aug 2021 and chairman since Dec 2021, he is steering Xcel through a data-center load boom.
interesting_fact: On the Q4 2025 call Xcel said it had 2+ GW of contracted data-center capacity and doubled its target to ~6 GW of data-center contracts by end-2027, backed by alliances with NextEra and GE Vernova and large-load tariffs in four states.
deep_cut_fact: Before finance he served six years in the US Navy as a nuclear engineering officer and weapons officer, later rising to Lieutenant Commander in the Navy Reserve; Twin Cities Business named him a 2022 Notable Military Veteran Executive.
notes: Highly relevant for energy/data-center podcast: frequently speaks on AI load growth, nuclear and grid. Educated Georgia Tech (industrial engineering) and Chicago Booth MBA per proxy-derived profiles. Best route: Xcel Energy media relations / corporate communications.

name: Michael K Grimm
current_role: Independent director, Energy Transfer LP; President, Rising Star Petroleum, L.L.C.
profile: Michael K. Grimm is a Texas oil-and-gas landman turned wildcatter. He spent 13 years in Amoco's land and exploration departments, co-founded Rising Star Energy in 1995 and RSP Permian in 2010 (co-CEO to 2014, later chairman). He has sat on Energy Transfer-group boards since 2005 and joined the ET LP board in Oct 2018.
interesting_fact: He co-founded RSP Permian, a Midland-based Permian Basin producer, and was its chairman until its sale. He is also a member of the All American Wildcatters.
deep_cut_fact: He earned a BBA in Petroleum Land Management from UT Austin in 1977 and is in the Silver Spurs Hall of Fame. The Silver Spurs is the UT spirit group that looks after the Longhorns' live mascot, Bevo.

public_contacts.value: Energy Transfer media relations: Vicki Granado, 214-840-5820; IR 214-981-0795 (no email published)

notes: Private Texas oilman; no personal social media found. Route via Energy Transfer corporate secretary/media relations or Rising Star Petroleum. The ET bio page could not be fetched directly (access denied), so bio details come via search snippets of it and aggregator profiles. The Silver Spurs/Bevo explanation is general knowledge, not from that page.
