Previously an energy strategist/portfolio manager at Loews and head of global commodity strategy at Bank of America.
interesting_fact: He leads the long-term contracting that underwrites Cheniere's export expansions; in Feb 2026 Cheniere marked 10 years since its first Lower-48 LNG export cargo and signed a new long-term SPA with Taiwan's CPC.
deep_cut_fact: An electrical engineer by training (BS, Rutgers; MBA in finance, NYU Stern), he began his banking career at J.P. Morgan Securities as a senior analyst covering natural gas pipelines and distributors.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Gastech, World LNG Summit, Atlantic Council) - a good outreach hook. Cheniere media relations contacts on 2026 releases: Randy Bhatia and Bernardo Fallas (phone only in releases).

name: Jon A Olson
current_role: Independent director of AMD, Rocket Lab (audit committee chair) and Kulicke & Soffa; retired CFO of Xilinx
profile: Jon A. Olson spent 25+ years in finance at Intel (rising to Director of Finance), then was CFO of FPGA maker Xilinx from 2005 until retiring in 2016. He rejoined Xilinx's board in 2020 and moved onto AMD's board when AMD closed its ~$49B Xilinx deal in 2022; he also chairs Rocket Lab's audit committee and sits on Kulicke & Soffa's board.
interesting_fact: He joined AMD's board on Feb 14, 2022, the day AMD completed its acquisition of Xilinx, one of two Xilinx directors added as the board grew from eight to ten; he also sits on AMD's Audit and Finance Committee.
deep_cut_fact: The Silicon Valley Business Journal named him CFO of the Year in 2010; he holds a BS in accounting from Indiana University and an MBA from Santa Clara University.
notes: Board-level operator rather than founder; no public social presence or published contacts found. Formal route would be via company corporate secretaries (AMD/Rocket Lab). Good guest on semiconductor/AI-chip and space-economy finance.

name: Ellen Jamison Kullman
current_role: Chair of the Board, Carbon Inc. (former CEO); Lead Independent Director, Dell Technologies; director, Amgen
profile: Delaware-born mechanical engineer (Tufts, Kellogg MBA) who started at GE, joined DuPont in 1988 and rose to Chair and CEO (2009-2015). She later ran 3D-printing company Carbon as CEO from 2019 and now chairs its board, while serving as Dell's lead independent director and on Amgen's board. Her wealth is mainly executive and board compensation.
interesting_fact: She was the first woman, and 19th executive, to lead DuPont in its then 212-year history; Fortune ranked her among the five most powerful women in business in 2009 and 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She joined DuPont in 1988 as a marketing manager in its medical imaging business, after beginning her career at General Electric; in 2014 the Biotechnology Innovation Organization gave her its George Washington Carver Award for industrial biotech leadership.
notes: Net worth in input is small (~$41M SEC holdings); a corporate-governance figure rather than a founder. Best route is Carbon PR (pr@carbon3d.com) or Dell corporate communications given her Dell board role; Dell angle (AI servers) fits the podcast.

name: Howard Wenger
current_role: President and director, Nextpower Inc. (Nasdaq: NXT; formerly Nextracker), Fremont, CA
profile: Solar veteran (in the industry since 1984) and President of Nextracker/Nextpower since Feb 2022, director since 2024. Previously President of Solaria and, at SunPower (2007-17), President of Global Business Units and CEO of SunPower Corp. Systems, after being EVP of PowerLight. Nextpower, the top utility-scale solar-tracker maker, rebranded in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Nextracker rebranded as Nextpower on Nov 12, 2025 to reflect its move from solar trackers to a broader energy-technology platform for utility-scale and distributed solar plants; FY2025 revenue was ~$3.0B.
deep_cut_fact: He began his solar career in 1984 and early on held engineering and research roles at PG&E, AstroPower, Pacific Energy Group and Intersol Power; he has a BA in environmental studies from UC Santa Barbara and an MS in civil engineering from CU Boulder.
notes: 40+ years in solar - a great 'history of the industry' guest (PowerLight/SunPower era). Route via Nextpower media relations (media contact Brandy Lee per press releases). Nextpower's own site rate-limited automated access, so contacts come from SEC-filed press releases.

name: Illiya I. Pesic
current_role: Director (and 10%+ shareholder), Silvaco Group, Inc. (Nasdaq: SVCO)
profile: Iliya Pesic is the son of Ivan Pesic, who founded TCAD/EDA software maker Silvaco in 1984; the family remains a major shareholder. Iliya joined Silvaco's board in 2012, served as Chair (2012-14) and Executive Chair (2014-21), stepped off the board in 2023 and rejoined it in May 2025, after Silvaco's 2024 Nasdaq IPO.
interesting_fact: Silvaco makes TCAD (technology computer-aided design) software used to simulate semiconductor processes and devices, an unusual niche of chip-design tooling; Pesic led the board as Executive Chair for seven years before the company went public.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an M.S. in electronic engineering from Tohoku University in Sendai, Japan (after a B.S. EE from Santa Clara University), and before chairing Silvaco worked as a senior process engineer in a fabrication facility in the MEMS and biomedical industries.
notes: Spelled 'Iliya' in company materials (SEC lists 'Illiya'). Low public profile; no personal social accounts found. Route via Silvaco IR/press.

name: Ryan Pardo
current_role: Chief Legal Officer and Corporate Secretary, LifeStance Health Group (NASDAQ: LFST)
profile: Ryan Pardo has been Chief Legal Officer of LifeStance Health, one of the largest US outpatient mental-health providers, since 2017, and was part of the team through its 2021 IPO. Earlier he was General Counsel of Liberty Dialysis until its 2012 sale to Fresenius, and co-founded Liberty Health Partners (merged into Signify Health). Wealth stems from LifeStance equity.
interesting_fact: A healthcare-services dealmaker: he was GC at Liberty Dialysis through its acquisition by Fresenius Medical Care, then worked in M&A/business development for Fresenius before joining LifeStance.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he was Corporate Counsel at outdoor retailer Eddie Bauer, leading its securities reporting before the going-private deal, and earlier practiced corporate finance law at Dorsey & Whitney. He studied economics at Stanford and earned his J.D. at Harvard Law School.
notes: Legal executive, low public profile; 'See Remarks' insider title = CLO. Little relevance to energy/data centers. IR contact Monica Prokocki (VP Finance & IR); media contact Brooke Matthews (Sr. Director Communications) per releases.

name: Cynda Beauchamp
current_role: Private investor (Durham, NC area); former indirect ~34% owner of 8 Rivers Capital and SEC-reported 10% owner of NET Power (NPWR) via NPEH, LLC; sold those interests Nov 2, 2025
profile: Per SEC filings (Form 3, Aug 2025) she indirectly owned ~34.2% of 8 Rivers Capital, the Durham, NC clean-energy tech firm that manages and owns ~91% of NPEH, NET Power's largest holder. Her Form 4s show NPEH share sales in Oct 2025 and that on Nov 2, 2025 she sold 100% of 8RCH, LLC, her vehicle holding 8 Rivers interests.
interesting_fact: The fortune traces to NET Power, which now pitches 'Project Permian', a powered-land natural-gas generation project for fast-growing power demand, designed to be carbon-capture-ready in later phases.
notes: Not a public figure; no published personal or office contact. After the Nov 2025 sale she is likely no longer a NET Power insider, so NET Power IR (investors@netpower.com, ir.netpower.com) is not a route to her. Wealth figure (~$41M) is from SEC insider data only. Recommend low priority.

name: Terrance Lane Wilson
current_role: Senior Vice President & General Counsel, The Williams Companies (since April 2017)
profile: T. Lane Wilson is Williams' top lawyer, overseeing legal, government affairs, outreach and compliance at the Tulsa-based natural-gas pipeline giant. Before joining in 2017 he was a U.S. Magistrate Judge for the Northern District of Oklahoma, and earlier a partner at Tulsa firm Hall Estill; his wealth reflects Williams stock awards.
interesting_fact: He went from the federal bench straight to the C-suite: a sitting U.S. Magistrate Judge whom Chief Justice John Roberts had appointed to the Judicial Conference Committee on Criminal Law in 2016, he left to become Williams' general counsel in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: Before law, he was an engineer: he earned an electrical-engineering degree from the University of Tulsa (1989), where he played varsity tennis and won an individual conference championship, then worked for Exxon before law school.
notes: Goes by 'T. Lane Wilson'. In-house lawyer rather than entrepreneur; relevant for gas/power-for-data-centers angle (Williams has power JV work for data centers). Route via Williams media relations.

name: L Reade Fahs
current_role: Executive Chairman, National Vision Holdings (America's Best, Eyeglass World)
profile: Optical-retail veteran who led National Vision as CEO for 23 years (2002 to Aug 2025), building the discount eyewear chain behind America's Best and Eyeglass World and taking it public in 2017. Before that he spent a decade at LensCrafters and ran Vision Express in the UK. Since August 2025 he has been Executive Chairman, with Alex Wilkes as CEO.
interesting_fact: He chaired VisionSpring for a decade and has sat on RestoringVision's board for ~20 years; the company says the two nonprofits have provided eyeglasses to over 30 million low-income people worldwide during his tenure.
deep_cut_fact: Between LensCrafters/Vision Express and National Vision he was CEO of First Tuesday, the European dot-com era internet start-up/network. He started at LensCrafters in 1986 in advertising and new product development, and holds a Harvard BA in English and American Literature.
notes: Also on boards of PetVet Care Centers (KKR), Atlanta Committee for Progress and Alliance Theatre; active with the Coalition for Clear Vision. Emails taken from release boilerplate (could not re-fetch page directly).

name: Rahul Ghai
current_role: Senior Vice President & Chief Financial Officer, GE Aerospace (General Electric Co.)
profile: Rahul Ghai has been CFO of GE Aerospace since August 2022. He was also CFO of all of GE from September 2023 until the GE Vernova spin-off in April 2024. Before GE he was CFO of Otis, where he helped with its spin-off from UTC, and before that CFO of Harris Corp. for four years. He earlier held finance roles at Aetna, Carrier and UTC Fire & Security. His wealth comes from executive equity compensation.
interesting_fact: He has now helped steer three big corporate separations: Otis's spin-off from United Technologies, GE Vernova's spin-off from GE, and GE's own transformation into a standalone GE Aerospace.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in financial services in India. He earned an undergraduate degree in accounting and economics from Delhi University before getting an MBA from Purdue. GE credits his four years as CFO of Harris Corp. in Florida with tripling its stock price.
notes: Public-company CFO and a regular on earnings calls. As CFO he oversees investor relations, so the GE Aerospace IR team (Head of IR: Blaire Shoor) is the natural route. Directly relevant to the energy theme through the GE Vernova spin.

name: Alfred Lee Finley
current_role: Director, GBank Financial Holdings (Las Vegas); President/owner of BFX Fire (wildland fire trucks), Fort Worth
profile: Vancouver-born entrepreneur (UBC economics) who has worked in the utility-equipment business since 1969 and founded BFX Fire, a maker of wildland fire trucks, and heads Air Shelters USA. Holds real estate across 10 states, has lived in Fort Worth since 1990, and has been a director and 10%+ owner of Nevada-based GBank since 2013; joined Medalist Diversified REIT's board in 2024.
interesting_fact: Besides banking, he founded and owns BFX Fire, a manufacturer of wildland fire trucks, and heads Air Shelters USA; he also holds real estate across 10 states.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in the utility equipment business in Vancouver, B.C. back in 1969, decades before moving to Fort Worth in 1990.
notes: Private, low-profile businessman; no personal published contacts found. Was a 2026 GBank Class 1 director nominee (MarketBeat). Aggregators show Medalist board role ended early 2026 (unverified). Best route likely via GBank investor relations or BFX Fire Apparatus company channels. BFX Fire Apparatus (Weatherford, TX factory) supplies wildland engines to agencies such as the BLM and Texas A&M Forest Service (per firehouse.com / TFS purchase orders).

name: John M. Foraker
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chair, Once Upon a Farm, PBC (NYSE: OFRM)
profile: Packaged-food operator who spent 11 years as CEO of Annie's, taking it public in 2012 and selling it to General Mills in 2014, then ran the Annie's unit inside General Mills until 2017. He then co-founded organic kids' food brand Once Upon a Farm (with actress Jennifer Garner as co-founder/chief brand officer), which he now runs as a newly public benefit corporation.
interesting_fact: He has now led two natural-food brands to the public markets: Annie's (IPO 2012, sold to General Mills 2014) and Once Upon a Farm, which listed as OFRM; Jennifer Garner is his co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: Before food, he was a Bank of America vice president managing commercial banking relationships in its premium wine portfolio; he studied agricultural economics at UC Davis before a Berkeley MBA.
notes: Consumer-food founder rather than energy/data-center; good for an entrepreneurship/serial-operator angle. Media route is ICR. Some sources differ on exact Annie's CEO dates.

name: Anutthara Bharadwaj
current_role: Partner, ICONIQ (per TechCrunch/Toast bios); board director, Toast Inc.; former President of Atlassian (2023-Dec 2025)
profile: Known as Anu Bharadwaj; RV College of Engineering grad who spent ~11 years at Microsoft (Visual Studio ALM/TFS) before joining Atlassian in 2014 as head of product for Jira. Rose to COO (2021) and President (2023), then left Atlassian on 31 Dec 2025 after 12 years; joined Toast's board in Oct 2025 and is now listed as a partner at ICONIQ.
interesting_fact: In 2016 she took a year-long sabbatical for wildlife conservation fieldwork: rescuing lions from canned hunting in South Africa, GPS-collaring cheetahs in Namibia, monitoring penguin rookeries in Antarctica.
deep_cut_fact: Her first job at Microsoft was as a developer building 'Terrarium', a game; she said: 'As a gamer and a nerd, I couldn't believe they actually paid me for this job!'
notes: Departure from Atlassian announced Aug 2025, effective 31 Dec 2025. ICONIQ affiliation comes from TechCrunch contributor page and Toast bio; one site lists Operator Collective instead - confirm. Chaired Atlassian Foundation. Best route likely via ICONIQ or Toast board.

name: Michael George Rosenbaum
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Guidewire Software (NYSE: GWRE); director, DocuSign
profile: Mike Rosenbaum has been CEO of Guidewire, the property-and-casualty insurance core-systems software company, since August 2019, leading its shift to the Guidewire Cloud platform and AI tools for insurers. Before that he spent about 14 years at Salesforce, latterly as EVP of Product for its core CRM clouds. He also sits on DocuSign's board.
interesting_fact: Before tech, he was a US Navy submarine officer; he holds a B.S. in Systems Engineering from the US Naval Academy and an MBA from UC Berkeley's Haas School.
deep_cut_fact: At Salesforce he ran product management and go-to-market strategy for the core CRM products (EVP Product, 2016-2019) before being recruited to run Guidewire.
notes: Do not confuse with Michael Rosenbaum, founder of Catalyte/Arena Analytics (different person). Contacts read from Guidewire press-release media block via search tool (site blocked direct fetch); re-check before use. Media: Melissa Cobb, Director of PR.

name: David Livingstone
current_role: Chief Client Officer, Citigroup (since Sept 2023); member of Citi's Executive Management Team
profile: Australian-born investment banker who spent 16+ years in M&A at Goldman Sachs, then HSBC and Credit Suisse (CEO of Credit Suisse Australia 2010-13). Joined Citi in 2016 as Country Officer for Australia/NZ, ran Citi EMEA for nearly five years, and since 2023 leads Citi's global client coverage as Chief Client Officer.
interesting_fact: As Citi's EMEA CEO he steered the bank through Brexit and the pandemic in its largest region, and led Citi's global response to the war in Ukraine and resulting Russia sanctions.
deep_cut_fact: Before banking leadership he studied economics (BA Hons) at Macquarie University in Sydney and then took a law degree at Jesus College, Cambridge; he spent over 16 years in Goldman Sachs' M&A department.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; route via Citi media relations (press-release media contact). Common name - many unrelated David Livingstones online.

name: Martin Hoffmann
current_role: Former CEO (stepped down 1 May 2026), now advisor through March 2027 and shareholder, On Holding AG (NYSE: ONON)
profile: Martin Hoffmann joined Swiss running-shoe brand On as CFO in July 2013, became co-CEO in 2021 and sole CEO in July 2025, helping take On from startup to a NYSE-listed global brand (IPO 2021). He stepped down effective May 1, 2026 for a planned hiatus and philanthropic interests; co-founders David Allemann and Caspar Coppetti became co-CEOs.
interesting_fact: He spent 13 years as On's CFO and about five as co-/sole CEO; on leaving he said 'The timing to move on feels right' and planned to focus on philanthropy while staying an advisor until March 2027.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining a then-tiny On in 2013 he was CFO of Swiss kiosk/retail group Valora (2009-2013); he studied business management and computer science at TU Kaiserslautern.
notes: No longer CEO as of May 2026; reach via On press (press@on.com) while he remains advisor. No verified personal social accounts found. Swiss-based.

name: Lois K Zabrocky
current_role: President & CEO and Director, International Seaways, Inc. (NYSE: INSW); Director, Tidewater Inc.
profile: Lois Zabrocky has been the first and only CEO of International Seaways, one of the largest US-listed tanker owners, since its 2016 spin-off from Overseas Shipholding Group, where she spent ~25 years and ran the International Flag unit. She also sits on the boards of Tidewater, BIMCO and ITOPF.
interesting_fact: She is one of very few women leading a major listed tanker company, and her whole 30+ year career has been with INSW and its predecessor OSG.
deep_cut_fact: She began her career at sea: a graduate of the US Merchant Marine Academy holding a Third Mate's license, she sailed as third mate on a chemical tanker in the US Jones Act fleet before moving ashore.
notes: Frequent speaker at Capital Link and Marine Money shipping forums — conference circuit is a natural route. IR/media contact is Tom Trovato (Investor Relations & Media) per company press releases.

name: David S. Graziosi
current_role: Chair, President and CEO, Allison Transmission Holdings Inc. (NYSE: ALSN)
profile: Indianapolis-based industrial executive who has led Allison Transmission, the maker of commercial and defense vehicle automatic transmissions, as CEO since June 2018 and chair since about 2021. He joined in November 2007 as EVP, CFO and treasurer, just after GM sold Allison to Carlyle and Onex, and became president in 2016. Earlier he was CFO at Berry Plastics and Covalence Specialty Adhesives (per secondary profile).
interesting_fact: He joined Allison right after GM's 2007 carve-out sale to Carlyle and Onex, helped take it public in 2012, and as CEO has steered it into electrified propulsion and defense (e.g. 2026 deal to supply transmissions for BAE Systems Hagglunds CV90 MkIV vehicles).
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a tax auditor before moving into finance roles at multinational manufacturers.
notes: Low personal media profile; route via Allison media relations (Sjoerd Vos, Global Brand + External Communications, listed on 2026 releases). IPO 2012 detail is general company history.

name: Bernard Shek
current_role: Chief Legal Officer and Secretary, Sandisk Corporation
profile: Bernard Shek is Sandisk's Chief Legal Officer and Secretary (since the Feb 2025 spin-off from Western Digital), overseeing global legal, compliance, IP and government affairs. A litigator with ~30 years advising semiconductor and tech companies, he joined Sandisk in 2011 as a litigation leader and later served as a deputy general counsel at Western Digital after it acquired Sandisk.
interesting_fact: He has effectively come full circle: joined SanDisk in 2011 in litigation (Senior Director, then VP of Litigation), stayed through Western Digital's 2016 acquisition, and now runs legal for the re-spun-off, independently listed Sandisk.
deep_cut_fact: A Bay Area local product: BA from UC Berkeley (1994) and law degree from UC Hastings (now UC College of the Law, San Francisco, 1997).
notes: Low public profile in-house lawyer; no personal social presence found. Education/dates from aggregator + Justia lawyer directory, so treat deep-cut as moderately sourced. Best route is Sandisk media relations.

name: Gerhard Watzinger
current_role: Chairman of the Board, CrowdStrike (since April 2012)
profile: German-born security executive who has chaired CrowdStrike since its 2012 founding. He was CEO of encryption company SafeBoot until McAfee bought it in 2007 for about $350M, then became McAfee's Chief Strategy Officer and EVP. He also sits on the boards of KnowBe4, NinjaOne and Invicti.
interesting_fact: At McAfee he was the architect of the company's $7.7B sale to Intel, before teaming up with McAfee colleagues George Kurtz and Dmitri Alperovitch at CrowdStrike.
deep_cut_fact: He ran SafeBoot, a Dutch-based data-encryption company that McAfee bought for about $350M in 2007, then took over McAfee's new Data Protection business unit and reported to CEO Dave DeWalt. He has an advanced computer-science degree from the University of Applied Sciences in Munich.
notes: Low public profile: he gives few interviews and I found no personal social accounts. The only published route is CrowdStrike corporate communications.

name: Nikhil Behl
current_role: President, Software, FICO (Fair Isaac Corp, NYSE: FICO)
profile: Silicon Valley tech/e-commerce executive who joined FICO in 2014 as CMO, then ran software sales & marketing, and since July 2024 leads all technology and go-to-market for FICO's software business (FICO Platform), now titled President, Software. Earlier: 12 years at HP, COO of Mercantila, and e-commerce start-ups.
interesting_fact: He runs the software half of FICO, whose decisioning platform (AI/ML and analytics at scale) is used by businesses in 100+ countries, alongside the FICO Score used by 90% of top US lenders.
deep_cut_fact: Before FICO he spent 12 years at Hewlett-Packard, including as VP of sales and operations for HPShopping.com, and helped lead e-commerce start-up Zoostores.com, a retailer offering 2M+ home and fitness products.
notes: Corporate executive (not founder). Best route is FICO press office (press@fico.com). Serves on advisory boards of Silicon Valley start-ups.

name: Thomas Deitrich
current_role: President and CEO, Itron, Inc. (NASDAQ: ITRI); director, onsemi
profile: Tom Deitrich has led Itron, the smart-meter and grid-edge intelligence company serving utilities and cities, since August 2019, after joining as EVP and COO in 2015. A 25-year operations veteran of GE, Ericsson Mobile, Flextronics and Freescale Semiconductor, he has pushed Itron toward industrial IoT, grid-edge AI and utility data analytics.
interesting_fact: Under Deitrich, Itron positions its meters as distributed computing nodes ('grid edge intelligence') and has partnered with firms such as Snowflake on AI-powered grid planning, relevant as data centers strain utility grids.
deep_cut_fact: Before Itron he was SVP and general manager of Digital Networking at Freescale Semiconductor, and he sits on the GridWise Alliance's Grid Infrastructure Advisory Council.
notes: Good fit for an energy/grid podcast (smart grid, utilities, data-center load). Route via Itron Corporate Communications (pr@itron.com).

name: Gavin Turner
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Mainsail Partners; director, Brilliant Earth Group (BRLT)
profile: Gavin Turner co-founded Austin-based growth-equity firm Mainsail Partners in 2003. It invests in bootstrapped software companies and has nearly $4B in committed capital. Mainsail backed lab-grown and ethical jewelry retailer Brilliant Earth, where he has been a director since 2012 (LLC board) and through its 2021 IPO, so he is an SEC 10% owner as Mainsail's designee.
interesting_fact: Mainsail focuses on founder-owned, bootstrapped software companies that have never raised outside capital, which is unusual among growth-equity firms. It has partnered with 100+ such companies.
deep_cut_fact: He is originally from Cleveland. Before Mainsail he spent seven years at Summit Partners, then joined the senior management of Sirenza Microdevices, a deal he had sourced, which RF Micro Devices later bought for $900M. He skis in winter and sails in summer.
notes: Investor-director. Mainsail's bio page lists the firm's Austin and San Francisco office phone numbers; no published email was found. He serves on the board of the Boys & Girls Club of the Austin Area.

name: Joseph M Hogan
current_role: President and CEO, Align Technology (Invisalign, iTero), since June 2015
profile: Industrial and medtech executive who spent 25+ years at GE, including 8 years as CEO of GE Healthcare, then ran Swiss power and automation group ABB (2008-13) before taking over Align Technology, maker of Invisalign clear aligners and iTero scanners, in 2015. His wealth comes mainly from Align equity.
interesting_fact: Before dental aligners he ran ABB, a ~$40B power-grid and automation company, so he has led both a grid/electrification giant and a consumer-medical-device firm. Align says he grew GE Healthcare revenue from $7B to $16B.
deep_cut_fact: He didn't come from an elite school: his B.S. in business and economics is from Geneva College, a small Christian college in Beaver Falls, Pennsylvania, and his MBA is from Robert Morris University near Pittsburgh.
notes: His ABB years (power grids, electrification) are the natural angle for an energy podcast. Go through Align corporate communications.

name: Scott M Sperling
current_role: Co-CEO, THL (Thomas H. Lee Partners); Lead Independent Director, Thermo Fisher Scientific
profile: Boston private-equity investor who joined Thomas H. Lee Partners in 1994 and is now its co-CEO and co-chair of the management committee. Earlier he spent a decade running Harvard Private Capital, the endowment's private-investment arm, after a stint at Boston Consulting Group. Long-time Thermo Fisher director (lead independent director) and a Liberty Mutual board member.
interesting_fact: He has sat on the boards of iHeartMedia and The Madison Square Garden Company, and has chaired the Brigham & Women's/Faulkner Hospitals board.
deep_cut_fact: Before private equity he spent 10 years at Harvard Private Capital (formerly the Aeneas Group), the Harvard Management Company unit investing the endowment in private deals; the Harvard Crimson reported his move to Thomas H. Lee in August 1994.

public_contacts.value: Edelman Smithfield for THL - Nicole Hakimi, nicole.hakimi@edelmansmithfield.com (2023 release)
Guest on Bloomberg Masters in Business (May 2021)

notes: Gives long-form interviews (Bloomberg Masters in Business 2021, Semafor 2024, SALT Talks), so a podcast invite is plausible; route through THL's PR agency. PR contact is from 2023 and may have changed.

name: John A Cuomo
current_role: President, CEO and Director, VSE Corporation (Nasdaq: VSEC), since April 2019
profile: Aerospace-distribution executive who has run VSE since 2019, repositioning it as an aviation aftermarket distribution and MRO company. Before VSE he led Boeing Distribution Services (2018-19), KLX Aerospace Solutions (2014-18) and held senior roles at B/E Aerospace (2000-14). Also sits on the board of FDH Aero.
interesting_fact: He started his career as a commercial lawyer (M&A and litigation) at a multinational law firm before moving into aerospace in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a B.S. in International Business, a J.D. from the University of Miami and an MBA from the University of Florida, and completed Harvard Business School's Advanced Management Program.
notes: Named a top transportation/logistics leader by Virginia Business (2023). Best route is VSE investor relations.

name: Adam Joseph Lowe
current_role: Chief Product & Innovation Officer, CompoSecure, Inc. (NASDAQ: CMPO), Somerset, NJ; creator of the Arculus platform
profile: Dr. Adam Lowe is CompoSecure's Chief Product & Innovation Officer, leading R&D at the premium metal payment-card maker. After about six years in its R&D group he became the company's first Chief Innovation Officer in 2020, and he created Arculus, CompoSecure's crypto cold-storage wallet and passwordless authentication platform, launched in 2021.
interesting_fact: He named Arculus after the Roman god of safes and strongboxes. The product turns a metal card into a crypto cold-storage wallet and a tap-to-phone authenticator with three-factor protection.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he worked in government defense-department labs. He holds a BS in Microbiology from Salisbury University and a PhD and MBA from Cornell, where his doctoral research was in bio-nanotechnology. He is listed as an inventor on 200+ patents and patents pending.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Finovate, Consensus, Seamless, Singapore FinTech Festival), so a speaking or podcast invite is a natural angle. Patent counts in his bios range from a dozen to 500+, so don't quote a number.

name: John Caplan
current_role: CEO and Director, Payoneer Global Inc. (Nasdaq: PAYO)
profile: Serial internet/commerce executive who founded e-commerce platform OpenSky (2009), sold it to Alibaba in 2017 and then ran Alibaba.com for North America & Europe until 2021. He joined Payoneer as co-CEO in 2022 and became sole CEO in 2023, leading the cross-border payments platform for SMBs and freelancers worldwide.
interesting_fact: Before OpenSky he was CMO of About.com and later CEO of Ford Models; at Alibaba he turned OpenSky into Alibaba.com's North America B2B business.
deep_cut_fact: His family founded fine-jeweler Oscar Heyman & Brothers in New York in 1912 after emigrating from Latvia; he and his cousins still sit on its board.
notes: Frequent podcast/conference guest (e.g. Fintech Blueprint, NYSE IPO Edge) - receptive to media. Go via Payoneer PR.

name: Michael H. Train
current_role: Senior Vice President and Chief Sustainability Officer, Emerson (NYSE: EMR)
profile: Mike Train is a 35-year Emerson veteran. He joined in 1991 as an international planner, ran Process Management Asia-Pacific, the Rosemount business and global sales, then was president of Emerson from 2018 to 2021. In March 2021 he became Emerson's first Chief Sustainability Officer, steering its decarbonization and energy-transition automation strategy.
interesting_fact: Before becoming its first CSO he was President of Emerson (2018-2021), overseeing software and digital technology, major investments, international growth and global shared services.
deep_cut_fact: He is an electrical engineer from the General Motors Institute (now Kettering University), a 2008 Eisenhower Fellow, and chairs the board of trustees of Ranken Technical College in St. Louis. Early on he led Emerson's operations in Japan and Korea.

public_contacts.value: Joele Frank, Wilkinson Brimmer Katcher (Emerson media contact), (212) 355-4449

notes: Strong energy-transition and industrial-automation angle for the podcast. Corporate executive, not a founder; outreach should go through Emerson communications.

name: John M. Evans
current_role: Chief Executive Officer and director, Beam Therapeutics (since 2017)
profile: John Evans has led Beam Therapeutics, the Cambridge, MA base-editing gene-therapy company, since 2017, joining from ARCH Venture Partners as its launch CEO. Before that he was an early employee and SVP of corporate development and portfolio leadership at Agios, where he helped bring IDH inhibitors IDHIFA and TIBSOVO forward and co-led the Celgene alliance.
interesting_fact: Under Evans, Beam reported what it called the first-ever clinical genetic correction of a disease-causing mutation, with its in-vivo base editor BEAM-302 for alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency (2025).
deep_cut_fact: A gene-editing CEO with a humanities start: he earned a bachelor's in English with distinction from Yale before adding a Penn biotechnology master's and Wharton MBA; early career stops included MedImmune, McKinsey's pharma practice and Infinity Pharmaceuticals.
notes: Has said on podcasts 'I do not come from this field' — comfortable discussing the business side of biotech. Route via 1AB media contact.

name: Glenn H Hutchins
current_role: Executive chairman, North Island; co-founder and chairman, North Island Ventures; lead independent director, CoreWeave; co-founder of Silver Lake
profile: Glenn Hutchins (b. 1955) did private equity at Thomas H. Lee and Blackstone, advised the Clinton transition and White House on economic and health policy, then co-founded tech buyout firm Silver Lake in 1999. He now chairs North Island (2020), is lead independent director of AI cloud CoreWeave and a Santander director, and formerly sat on the boards of AT&T and the New York Fed.
interesting_fact: He co-chairs the Brookings Institution, chairs CARE and is vice chair of the Obama Foundation; his family foundation created the Hutchins Center on Fiscal and Monetary Policy at Brookings and the Hutchins Center for African & African American Research at Harvard.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from Harvard College in 1977 he started out as a credit analyst at Chemical Bank, then earned a joint JD/MBA from Harvard Law and Business schools simultaneously (1983); his foundation also funds the Hutchins Institute for Civics at his old prep school, Lawrenceville.
notes: AT&T directorship is now past per his North Island bio; CoreWeave (AI data-centre cloud) role is the podcast hook. X/LinkedIn are North Island Ventures firm accounts, not personal. Also minority owner of the Boston Celtics. No published press email found.

name: Denise C Johnson
current_role: Group President, Resource Industries, Caterpillar Inc. (retiring Feb 1, 2027; advisory role during transition)
profile: Denise Johnson is a Michigan State mechanical engineer and MIT LGO alumna who spent two decades at GM (product development, labor relations VP, head of GM Brazil) before joining Caterpillar in 2011. She has led Caterpillar's mining equipment group, Resource Industries, since 2016, returning it to profitability and making Cat a leader in mining autonomy. Caterpillar announced in Oct 2026 that she will retire Feb 1, 2027.
interesting_fact: She was the first woman in Caterpillar's history to lead one of its business groups, and oversaw the scale-up of Cat's autonomous mining truck fleet.
deep_cut_fact: Facing her first union negotiation as GM's labor-relations VP after the 2009 bankruptcy, she pulled out her old MIT LGO negotiations-class notes, including her written list of BATNAs.
notes: Retiring Feb 2027 (successor Derrick York from Nov 1, 2026) per Caterpillar release https://www.caterpillar.com/en/news/corporate-press-releases/h/caterpillar-announces-leadership-transition-in-resource-industries.html. Mining electrification/autonomy is a strong energy-podcast angle; post-retirement she may be more available. Route via Caterpillar corporate communications.

name: Barry Hytinen
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer, Iron Mountain Inc.; director, ABM Industries
profile: Barry Hytinen has been CFO of Iron Mountain since January 2020, helping steer the records-storage company's push into data centers. Before that he was CFO of Hanesbrands and spent 12 years at Tempur Sealy (including as CFO), after earlier finance roles at GE, Vignette and venture-backed Fogbreak Software.
interesting_fact: As CFO he is a key financial architect of Iron Mountain's pivot from paper-records storage into a fast-growing data-center business, highly relevant to a data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He is a 1997 political science graduate of Syracuse University's Maxwell School (later Harvard MBA), and early on was VP Finance at Fogbreak Software, a small venture-backed Milpitas software startup.
notes: Fogbreak detail comes from secondary bio aggregators (marketscreener/vectorshift); Syracuse/Harvard and Tempur/Hanes facts are from the Maxwell page. Route via Iron Mountain IR or media team.

name: David Scott Offer
current_role: Executive Vice President & General Counsel, Flex Ltd.
profile: Goes by Scott Offer. UK- and US-qualified lawyer (LSE law degree) who started at London firm Boodle Hatfield, spent years at Motorola (chief counsel of Motorola Mobility under Google), then was SVP & GC of Lenovo before joining Flex in 2016, where he leads legal, government relations, IP, compliance and security.
interesting_fact: Named by the Financial Times Innovative Lawyers programme (2025) as one of the Top 20 General Counsel of the last two decades; his team ran the separation of solar-tracker maker Nextracker from Flex, one of the largest US IPOs of 2023.
deep_cut_fact: He has written on Flex's blog about measuring corporate ethics with data, e.g. 'A scorecard approach to improve compliance and ethics across the enterprise' (Aug 2022) and 'Data-backed ethical culture' (Jan 2022).
notes: Known professionally as Scott Offer. Data-center angle: Flex is big in data-center power/liquid cooling and announced (May 2026) intent to spin off its Cloud & Power Infrastructure segment.

name: Matthew K Schatzman
current_role: Chairman & CEO, NextDecade Corporation (NASDAQ: NEXT)
profile: LNG executive with nearly four decades in energy. Former EVP of Global Energy Marketing & Shipping at BG Group and senior executive at Dynegy. Joined NextDecade in 2017, CEO since 2018 and Chairman since 2019, he led the financing and construction of the Rio Grande LNG export terminal in Brownsville, Texas.
interesting_fact: Under him NextDecade financed the multi-train Rio Grande LNG project (about 30 MTPA initially, site permitted/planned for up to ~60 MTPA with ten trains), one of the largest US LNG export developments.
deep_cut_fact: He began his energy career at Transco Pipeline, a Williams subsidiary, and holds a BA in political science from Yale; he also sits on the National Petroleum Council.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (US LNG exports). Appears linked to Baker Hughes annual meeting materials (possible board nominee) - not verified. Route via NextDecade media contact.

name: Shaun White
current_role: Founder/CEO, The Snow League; founder, WHITESPACE (snowboard/apparel brand)
profile: San Diego-born snowboarder and skateboarder, a three-time Olympic halfpipe gold medalist (2006, 2010, 2018) and winner of 10 ESPYs, who retired after the 2022 Games. Wealth came from prize money, sponsorships, video games and brand deals. He now runs WHITESPACE (launched 2022) and The Snow League, a pro halfpipe league backed by Ares, Will Ventures and David Blitzer that debuted in 2025.
interesting_fact: The Snow League raised $4.5M seed and a further $30M by Nov 2025; after a first season in Aspen, China and LAAX, its second season opens at Park City Mountain (Jan 21-23), with broadcasts reaching ~175 countries via NBC/Peacock and YouTube.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first guitar as first prize in a snowboarding competition; he later played guitar in the electronic-rock band Bad Things, which took a Saturday headline slot at Lollapalooza 2013 as a last-minute replacement for Death Grips. Tony Hawk befriended and mentored him at age 9 at the Encinitas YMCA skate park.
notes: Celebrity athlete-turned-founder; outreach best via Snow League press channels. Fits entrepreneurship angle (league building, sports-media business). Social handles are his verified accounts; check snowleague.com for a press contact.

name: Wendy Williams
current_role: Retired talk-show host and radio personality (former host, The Wendy Williams Show, 2008-2021)
profile: Wendy Williams built her fame as a New York hip-hop radio DJ (WQHT Hot 97, WBLS) before hosting the syndicated daytime 'The Wendy Williams Show' for 13 seasons, stepping away in 2021. Entry has no listed company; assumed to be the US TV host (Wikidata Q618233).
interesting_fact: Inducted into the National Radio Hall of Fame in 2009; her Asbury Park, NJ street was renamed 'Wendy Williams Way' on her 50th birthday, and she received a Hollywood Walk of Fame star in 2019.
deep_cut_fact: Her first radio job, right after graduating from Northeastern University in 1986, was as a DJ at WVIS, a small calypso/reggae station in Frederiksted, U.S. Virgin Islands; at Northeastern's WRBB, LL Cool J was her first celebrity interview.
notes: Identity marked uncertain only because the input has no source of wealth; Wikidata ID matches the TV host. Not a realistic podcast guest and not an energy/data-center fit; outreach not recommended.

name: Russell A. (Chip) Childs
current_role: President & CEO, SkyWest, Inc. (St. George, Utah)
profile: Russell 'Chip' Childs runs SkyWest, the largest U.S. regional airline group, which flies for United, Delta, American and Alaska. A former audit manager, he joined SkyWest in 2001 as VP-Controller, was President/COO of SkyWest Airlines 2007-2014, and became CEO of SkyWest, Inc. in January 2016.
interesting_fact: He chairs the U.S. DOT/FAA NextGen Advisory Committee and sits on the Salt Lake City branch board of the Federal Reserve Bank of San Francisco; under him SkyWest was named one of Fortune's Most Admired Companies.
deep_cut_fact: Before aviation he spent five and a half years in public accounting as an audit manager doing SEC reporting for large corporations; he holds a BYU economics BA and MAcc and has sat on BYU Marriott School's National Advisory Council since 2017.
notes: Low personal media profile; speaks mainly on pilot shortage / 1,500-hour rule and regional capacity. Go via SkyWest Corporate Communications.

name: Jeffrey Jacobowitz
current_role: Founder and Managing Member, Simcoe Capital Management, LLC (New York); former director of Donnelley Financial Solutions (DFIN)
profile: Jeffrey Jacobowitz founded New York hedge fund Simcoe Capital Management in 2003 to invest in undervalued U.S. public companies with a concentrated, 3-5 year horizon. Simcoe built a ~7.9% stake in DFIN and he joined its board in 2019 under a cooperation agreement; he does not appear on DFIN's 2026 director slate.
interesting_fact: He joined DFIN's board via a 2019 settlement with his fund, having earlier served on the boards of Exar Corporation, Telular Corporation and Alloy Inc. as an activist-style shareholder representative.
notes: Low-profile investor; no published personal or firm contact found. Third-party profiles (MarketScreener) say he started as a senior accountant at Deloitte & Touche and studied at UMBC, but these weren't confirmed in a primary source. Appears in 2024 DFIN proxy but not the 2026 nominee list.

name: Charles L. Treadway
current_role: President & CEO and Director, Vistance Networks (formerly CommScope); stepping down Feb 1, 2027; Director, AZZ Inc.
profile: Chuck Treadway has been CEO of CommScope (renamed Vistance Networks in Jan 2026) since October 2020. He led the sale of several divisions, including RUCKUS to Belden, leaving Vistance focused on Aurora Networks. Before that he was CEO of Accudyne Industries (2016-20) and Thomas & Betts (2012-16). He plans to step down on Feb 1, 2027.
interesting_fact: He has run businesses in the U.S., Mexico, Europe and Asia, including as CEO of a Schneider-Swire joint venture in China and president of Grupo Tesa Mexico (Yale Security).
deep_cut_fact: He started as an engineer at Square D. At the University of Louisiana at Lafayette (B.S.E.E. 1988) he was student government president for the College of Engineering and president of the Louisiana Engineering Society. He later earned an M.S.E.E. from Clemson and an MBA from Harvard.
notes: CEO departure announced (effective Feb 1, 2027), so he may soon be free to talk about the CommScope breakup. Some newer releases list Weiwei Tan as the media contact.

name: T Wilson Eglin
current_role: Chairman, CEO & President, LXP Industrial Trust (taken private by Brookfield/CPP Investments on Nov 2, 2026; post-close role unclear)
profile: T. Wilson (Will) Eglin has led LXP Industrial Trust (formerly Lexington Realty) as CEO since 2003, after joining as COO in 1993, and transformed it into a pure-play Sunbelt/Midwest industrial REIT. In July 2026 he agreed a $5.2B all-cash sale to Brookfield and CPP Investments, which closed on Nov 2, 2026.
interesting_fact: He steered LXP's multi-year pivot from a diversified net-lease REIT to a pure-play industrial owner (~53M sq ft in 12 markets), which culminated in the $5.2B take-private by Brookfield and CPP Investments in 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At Nareit REITweek in June 2026 he said 'The greatest opportunity for us is development in our land bank'; he has been with the company since 1993 and a trustee since 1994.
notes: LXP is now private (acquired by Brookfield & CPP Investments, closed Nov 2, 2026); LXP assets now managed by BGRE (bgre.com). IR email may lapse post-deal; Brookfield comms contact listed in the deal release. Unclear whether Eglin remains post-close.

name: Jonathan J Doyle
current_role: Vice Chairman, Senior Managing Principal & Head of Financial Services Group, Piper Sandler; director, nCino
profile: Veteran bank M&A and capital-raising banker. Was senior managing principal at Sandler O'Neill + Partners, which Piper Jaffray acquired in January 2020 to form Piper Sandler; now runs its financial services group and sits on its leadership team and board. Also a director of bank-software company nCino since around 2019-2020.
interesting_fact: Sits on the board of nCino, the cloud banking software company, while leading one of the largest bank M&A advisory franchises in the US.
deep_cut_fact: A William & Mary finance graduate, he is a trustee emeritus of the College of William & Mary Foundation and serves on the board of The Governor's Academy in Byfield, Massachusetts.
notes: Private-leaning banker; route via Piper Sandler media relations (Nick Lawler).

name: Scott Egan
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, SiriusPoint Ltd (NYSE: SPNT), Bermuda-based global insurer/reinsurer
profile: Scottish-born insurance executive and qualified management accountant (Cranfield MBA) who joined SiriusPoint as CEO in September 2022 and led its turnaround. Previously spent ~6 years on the RSA Group board as CFO and then CEO of RSA UK & International, after roles at Norwich Union/Aviva, Zurich, Brit and Towergate. In 2026 he is pushing growth in A&H and SiriusPoint's MGA ecosystem.
interesting_fact: He credits staff engagement scores, not underwriting metrics, as the 'secret sauce' behind SiriusPoint's record growth, including a 44% year-on-year jump in half-year net income.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Motherwell, Scotland, moved to London at 18 and trained as an accountant at British Rail before joining Norwich Union; he raced cars until his early twenties and is a self-described 'football nut' with a passion for Tottenham Hotspur.

public_contacts.value: https://investors.siriuspt.com (investor relations site; press-release contacts listed per release)
Guest appearances on The Voice of Insurance podcast (Ep297, April 2026)

notes: Frequent trade-press interviewee (Reinsurance News, Insurance Business, Voice of Insurance podcast) — media-friendly. SiriusPoint press releases list IR/media contacts (recently Liam Blackledge IR, Natalie King media), but I could not verify the addresses on an accessible page, so check the latest release on investors.siriuspt.com.

name: Carrie Lee Kirby
current_role: EVP & Chief Administrative Officer, Vistra Corp. (per SEC Form 4 filings through Feb 2026; no longer shown on Vistra's leadership page as of Nov 2026)
profile: Carrie Kirby is a long-time HR and corporate-services executive at Vistra, the Texas-based power generator and retail electricity company. She joined predecessor TXU in 2006 as an HR director, became EVP of HR at Energy Future Holdings, and has been Vistra's EVP & Chief Administrative Officer since 2016, overseeing HR, community affairs, supply chain and corporate functions.
interesting_fact: Her career has tracked the full arc of Texas power: from TXU through the Energy Future Holdings era to Vistra, now a Fortune 500 generator selling nuclear power to hyperscalers such as Meta.
deep_cut_fact: She holds both a bachelor's degree in marketing and an MBA from TCU, sits on the board of the Women's Business Council Southwest and is a member of United Way's Women of Tocqueville (per her former Vistra leadership bio).
notes: Her name no longer appears on vistracorp.com/about/leadership (Nov 2026 check), so she may have left or retired; verify before outreach. Deep-cut bio comes from an earlier version of that page. Low public profile.

name: David Barr
current_role: Managing Director, Bessemer Investors; Director (Compensation Committee chair), TransDigm Group
profile: David A. Barr is a private-equity veteran of 37+ years: 11 years at Butler Capital, 17 years at Warburg Pincus (co-head of Industrial & Business Services, 60+ deals), and since 2018 Managing Director at family-owned Bessemer Investors. He has sat on 40+ boards, including TransDigm (2003-2011 and again since 2017), Aramark and Builders FirstSource.
interesting_fact: He has served on more than 40 private and public company boards over his career, and currently also sits on the boards of Mas Restaurant Group, RotoCo and Xanitos.
deep_cut_fact: A Wesleyan alumnus and Wesleyan trustee, he chairs the Finance Committee of Good Shepherd Services, a New York City social-services agency; outside work he enjoys biking and paddleboarding.
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via TransDigm board + Bessemer Investors bio. Best route is via Bessemer Investors (firm site) rather than TransDigm IR.

name: Sara Wechter
current_role: Chief Human Resources Officer, Citigroup (since July 2018)
profile: Career Citi executive who joined as an investment-banking analyst in 2004, moved to Corporate M&A and Strategy, then served as chief of staff to chairmen Richard Parsons and Michael O'Neill and CEO Mike Corbat. She has led Citi's global HR since 2018 and sits on the bank's management committee; her wealth reflects Citi equity awards.
interesting_fact: Named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 list in 2020; she drove high-profile Citi workforce policies such as hybrid work and expanded benefits and mental-health resources.
deep_cut_fact: An Emory alumna (class of 2003) who originally planned to focus on health care, until a first-year internship at a start-up pulled her toward business; at Citi she later worked on the Smith Barney sale during the financial crisis.
notes: Also on the boards of Onex Corp, Citi Foundation and NYU Langone overseers. Low public profile; HR executive rather than founder, so a weak fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Route via Citi corporate communications.

name: Clayton M. Magouyrk
current_role: Chief Executive Officer (co-CEO with Mike Sicilia) and Director, Oracle Corporation (since Sept 2025)
profile: Clay Magouyrk (b. ~1986) spent 2008-2014 as a senior engineer at Amazon/AWS, then joined Oracle in 2014 as a founding member of its Seattle cloud engineering center that built Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). He led OCI engineering as EVP from 2019, became President of OCI in June 2025 and co-CEO in Sept 2025, as OCI scaled to 100+ public regions and huge AI data-center contracts.
interesting_fact: Oracle's 2026 proxy reports his fiscal-2026 total compensation as $627.5 million, versus $94,740 for the median Oracle employee.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BS in electrical engineering from the University of Memphis, and is described by Oracle as a founding member of Oracle's cloud engineering development center (the ex-AWS team that built OCI from scratch after he left Amazon in 2014).
notes: Prime data-center guest (OCI/Stargate-scale AI infrastructure, power procurement). Requests must go through Oracle global PR. SEC-insider wealth estimate ($39.9M) is likely far below his actual equity given his FY26 award.

name: Maciej Kurzymski
current_role: Chief Accounting Officer, Bloom Energy Corp (NYSE: BE), San Jose, CA
profile: Finance executive at fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy, whose solid-oxide fuel-cell systems are increasingly used for on-site power at AI data centers. He became a Section 16 officer on May 2, 2025 as Chief Accounting Officer and acting principal financial officer, and still files as CAO in 2026. His wealth estimate stems from Bloom equity.
interesting_fact: Bloom reported record Q3 2026 revenue of $1.24B, up 138% year on year, and raised full-year guidance - a direct play on behind-the-meter power for AI data centers.
notes: Not a UHNW founder - a corporate officer whose ~US$40M estimate comes from SEC insider holdings. Appointment per Form 3 (period 2025-05-02): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2067410/000095017025068362/ownership.xml. No public bio found; for a podcast, Bloom's CEO KR Sridhar is the natural guest. Route via Bloom media/IR.

name: William Chan
current_role: Chief Product & AI Officer, Waystar Holding Corp. (NASDAQ: WAY), since October 2025
profile: Serial healthcare-software founder who co-founded and ran Iodine Software (2010-2025), an AI clinical-intelligence company that Waystar bought for $1.26B (closed Oct 2025). He now leads product and AI at Waystar, a healthcare payments platform. Earlier he co-founded Crimson (sold to The Advisory Board Co. in 2008) and WhisperWire (acquired by Concentrix).
interesting_fact: Waystar paid about $638.9M in cash plus ~16.6M shares for Iodine, whose AI flags clinical-documentation gaps and prevents revenue leakage before billing; Chan holds multiple healthcare-technology patents.
deep_cut_fact: A Cornell computer-science grad with an HBS MBA (with honors), he sits on the board of American Mission Hospital in Bahrain, one of the oldest hospitals in the Gulf, and advises health-tech startup Revival Health.
notes: Healthcare AI rather than energy/data centers; better fit for an entrepreneurship episode (three exits). Press contact is Waystar's named media contact Kristin Lee as published in its earnings release. Common name: confirm via Iodine/Waystar context.

name: John W Ketchum
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, NextEra Energy (NEE); Chairman, Florida Power & Light and XPLR Infrastructure
profile: Tax lawyer turned utility executive who joined NextEra in 2002, served as CFO of NextEra and FPL and CEO of NextEra Energy Resources (largest US renewables developer), then became NextEra CEO in March 2022 and chairman in July 2022. He is positioning NextEra as a power supplier to AI data centers via deals with Google and others.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2025 NextEra and Google agreed to restart Iowa's shuttered Duane Arnold nuclear plant (615 MW) with Google buying its power for 25 years to run cloud/AI infrastructure; DOE closed a loan of up to $1.9B for the restart in Sept 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a JD and an LL.M. in taxation from the University of Missouri-Kansas City School of Law, where he was managing editor of the Law Review, and graduated magna cum laude in economics and finance from the University of Arizona.
notes: Highly relevant to energy + data-center theme (nuclear restarts, Google Cloud partnership, data-center campus projects). Wealth (~$40M) is executive equity. Route via NextEra media relations.

name: Nitin Agrawal
current_role: Chief Financial Officer (since March 2024) and Treasurer (since June 2025), CoreWeave, Inc. (Nasdaq: CRWV)
profile: Cloud-finance executive (age 46 per 2026 proxy) who has run finance at three hyperscale-era compute businesses: Finance Director of AWS's Compute Services division (2015-19), CFO of Mapbox (2019-21) and VP Finance of Google Cloud (2021-24). As CoreWeave's CFO he took the AI-cloud provider public in 2025 and manages its large debt-funded GPU data-center buildout; his wealth (~$39M) is CoreWeave equity.
interesting_fact: He has been a finance chief at AWS compute, Google Cloud and now CoreWeave, a rare seat on three sides of the cloud/GPU-capacity race.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training: he holds a B.Tech in engineering from the National Institute of Technology, Kurukshetra (India) before his Duke Fuqua MBA, and was CFO of mapping startup Mapbox before Google Cloud.
notes: Not a UHNW founder (SEC-holdings estimate ~$39M), but a top-tier source on AI data-center financing (GPU-backed debt, capex, power). Route via CoreWeave press or IR. Personal social accounts not verified (search quota exhausted).

name: Edward Sonnenschein
current_role: Director, X-Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: XE; board member since Dec 2021); Vice Chairman, IBX, LLC
profile: Ed Sonnenschein (~71) spent 1979-2021 at Latham & Watkins, rising to Global Chair of the Corporate Department. He is now vice chairman of IBX, LLC (governance, deals, legal) and sits on the boards of advanced-nuclear developer X-energy (IPO April 2026), Quantum Space and Axiom Space.
interesting_fact: His board seats span next-gen nuclear and private space: X-energy (high-temperature gas-cooled small modular reactors), Quantum Space (since 2022) and Axiom Space (since March 2026), private commercial space-station developer.
deep_cut_fact: While a Latham partner he also dabbled in biotech investing as a member of Coastview Capital LLC, a biotechnology venture-capital firm, from 2001 to 2003. He holds an A.B. in Social Studies and a JD, both from Harvard.
notes: Lawyer/dealmaker, not a founder; insider wealth stems from X-energy stock. Board ties to Kam Ghaffarian's network (X-energy chairman; IBX). No published personal or X-energy press contact retrieved (x-energy.com blocked automated access); try X-energy's media page manually.

name: Troy Rudd
current_role: Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, AECOM (NYSE: ACM)
profile: Troy Rudd has led global infrastructure consultancy AECOM as CEO since August 2020 (now also Chairman), refocusing it on professional services, advisory and program management in water, energy, transportation and buildings. He joined AECOM in 2009 and was previously its CFO; before that he was a KPMG partner for 10 years.
interesting_fact: AECOM credits his tenure with a near tripling of its market capitalization since he became CEO; the firm posted $16.1B of revenue in fiscal 2025 and works on energy and data-center-adjacent infrastructure.
deep_cut_fact: A tax specialist by training, he holds a Master of Science in Taxation from Golden Gate University and a B.S. from the University of British Columbia; he sits on the Executive Board of SMU's Lyle School of Engineering and on the Sustainable Markets Initiative board.
notes: Strong fit for energy/data-center infrastructure topics. Press contact is AECOM's head of global communications as listed on 2025 releases; confirm current before use.

name: Julian Forrest Barnwell Jr.
current_role: President & CEO, Design and Production Inc. (Lorton, VA); Director, Burke & Herbert Financial Services Corp. (NASDAQ: BHRB) since 2001
profile: J. Forrest Barnwell Jr. has led Design and Production Inc. (D&P), one of the largest US museum-exhibit fabricators, since 1991, and has been a director of Northern Virginia lender Burke & Herbert since 2001. His insider holdings are in Burke & Herbert stock (several hundred thousand shares, partly held in family trusts).
interesting_fact: His firm D&P, founded in 1949 and celebrating 75 years in 2024, builds exhibits for presidential, military, natural-history and state museums; in 2018 alone it opened the Bell Museum, Tennessee State Museum and National Law Enforcement Museum.
deep_cut_fact: D&P, the company he runs, helped create the 1970s 'Treasures of Tutankhamen' (King Tut) blockbuster exhibition, and in the 1960s invented the 'Sho Coach', a customizable tractor-trailer traveling museum that toured the country.
notes: Bank director role is via Form 4/proxy (Burke & Herbert 10-K 2023: director since 2001, age 68 then). Contact email is D&P's general marketing inbox, not personal. Private, low public profile; relevance to podcast is as a family-business/manufacturing owner.

name: Bradley Lee Soultz
current_role: Director, WillScot Holdings (CEO 2017-Dec 2025); Non-Executive Director, Constellium SE (special advisor from Sept 2024)
profile: Brad Soultz led modular-space and portable-storage leasing company WillScot as President & CEO from 2017, steering its 2020 merger with Mobile Mini; the company says revenue grew over 5x during his tenure. He handed the CEO role to Tim Boswell on Jan 1, 2026. Earlier he spent nine years at aluminium maker Novelis, ending as Chief Commercial & Strategy Officer, and now sits on aluminium producer Constellium's board.
interesting_fact: WillScot credits him with growing revenue more than fivefold and free cash flow to over $500 million as CEO, turning a Williams Scotsman spin-out into a Nasdaq-listed leasing leader.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an agricultural engineer, earning his bachelor's in agricultural engineering from Purdue University, before a career in aluminium and leasing.
notes: Recently stepped down as WillScot CEO (effective Dec 31, 2025) - avoid framing around the exit; current WillScot board status not confirmed from the 2026 proxy. Constellium (aluminium) board link may suit energy/materials angle.

name: Richard Scott Struthers
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Crinetics Pharmaceuticals (acquired by Vertex, Sept 2026); Chairman, Radionetics Oncology
profile: Endocrinologist-turned-founder (PhD, UC San Diego) who co-founded Crinetics in 2008 after a decade at Neurocrine, and built it into the maker of Palsonify (paltusotine), an FDA-approved oral acromegaly drug. Vertex agreed to buy Crinetics for ~$10B ($85/share) in July 2026, its largest-ever deal, closing Sept 1, 2026. His post-close role was not found.
interesting_fact: The Vertex deal (about $10B, roughly a 100% premium) was the largest acquisition in Vertex's history, and paid out a company Struthers co-founded with three fellow scientists in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Crinetics he co-founded ScienceMedia, an e-learning company for the life sciences and higher-ed markets, and did his doctoral research at the Salk Institute. At Neurocrine he launched the oral non-peptide GnRH antagonist program that produced elagolix. He was elected to the BIO board in March 2026.
notes: Crinetics is now a Vertex company; corporate press routes likely via Vertex media relations. Also co-founded the San Diego Entrepreneurs Exchange (nonprofit for early-stage startups) - good angle for an entrepreneurship podcast. Post-acquisition title unconfirmed.

name: Ryan Greenawalt
current_role: Chairman & CEO, Alta Equipment Group Inc. (NYSE: ALTG)
profile: Ryan Greenawalt is the second-generation leader of Alta Equipment. His father Steve founded it in 1984 as a single Yale forklift dealership in Detroit. Ryan rejoined in 2008 after several years in wealth management, led the move into construction equipment and many acquisitions, bought out the family in 2017, and took Alta public in February 2020. He still runs it as Chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: In 2009, in the middle of Michigan's auto-industry crisis, he led Alta's purchase of a Volvo construction-equipment dealership directly from the factory. That deal took the forklift dealer into construction equipment.

profile: William H. Lamb is a founding partner of West Chester, PA law firm Lamb McErlane and a former Justice of the Supreme Court of Pennsylvania (2003-04). He has been an independent director of fintech-focused bank The Bancorp since around 2004 and now serves Of Counsel in the firm's appellate group, running a mock-argument service for lawyers preparing appeals.
interesting_fact: Appointed to the Pennsylvania Supreme Court by Gov. Mark Schweiker in 2003, he was the first justice from Chester County in 147 years, and was named Chester County Citizen of the Year for it.
deep_cut_fact: As a Chester County special prosecutor (1981-84) he won two Awards of Merit from the Pennsylvania State Police; he served as Chester County DA 1972-80, holds a Duke BA in English and a Penn Law JD cum laude, and sat on the President's Advisory Committee on the Arts.
notes: Addressed as 'Justice Lamb'. Law-firm bio publishes his work email. Recipient of The Legal Intelligencer's 2014 Lifetime Achievement Award. Long-time Bancorp director (since ~2003/04; start year varies by source).

name: Paul Elliot Mann
current_role: Executive Chairman & CEO, ASP Isotopes Inc. (returned as CEO Jan 2026); Chairman, Quantum Leap Energy (planned nuclear-fuel spin-out)
profile: Paul E. Mann co-founded ASP Isotopes in 2021. The company enriches isotopes in Pretoria, South Africa, and is developing HALEU nuclear fuel through Quantum Leap Energy, a unit it plans to spin out. Before ASPI he was CFO of PolarityTE and a healthcare and chemicals investor at Soros Fund Management, Highbridge and DSAM, after 11 years as a sell-side analyst at Morgan Stanley and Deutsche Bank.
interesting_fact: He has pitched enriched carbon-14 at about $24,000 per gram, which he said is more than 400 times the price of gold. He got involved when ASPI's South African scientists were running out of money while building their enrichment plant.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a research scientist at Procter & Gamble and is named as the inventor of numerous skin creams in the Oil of Olay range. At Morgan Stanley he was corporate broker to over half of the UK's pharmaceutical companies.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast (nuclear fuel/HALEU, isotopes); he often does investor interviews. Took a medical leave Oct 2025 to Jan 2026, so avoid health topics. The IR contact is Jason Assad; some releases list Jacob Rowe instead.

name: Aaron A. Robertson
current_role: Director, Commercial Bancgroup, Inc. (NASDAQ: CBK) and Commercial Bank, Harrogate, Tennessee
profile: Aaron A. Robertson is a director (since Jan 2023) and major shareholder of Commercial Bancgroup, the Harrogate, Tennessee bank holding company controlled by the Robertson family and founded by E. Oscar Robertson in 1976; the company IPO'd on Nasdaq in 2025. Outside the bank he runs a cattle/farming business, works with Harrogate Insurance Agency and is a partner in Harrogate Restaurant Group.
interesting_fact: Commercial Bank was founded in Harrogate, Tennessee in 1976 by the late E. Oscar Robertson and remained Robertson-family controlled until its 2025 Nasdaq IPO.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong Claiborne County, Tennessee resident, he studied Diesel Technology at Southeast Kentucky Community & Technical College and has been self-employed in farming and cattle since 2009.
notes: Low public profile; family bank insider rather than an operator/entrepreneur in the podcast's sectors. Only route found is company IR.

name: Cosmo Feilding-Mellen
current_role: Co-Founder and Director, AtaiBeckley Inc. (formerly Co-Founder & CEO, Beckley Psytech)
profile: British biotech entrepreneur, son of psychedelic-research pioneer Amanda Feilding. Co-founded Beckley Research & Innovations (2016), Beckley Canopy Therapeutics and, in 2019, Beckley Psytech to develop psychedelic medicines (e.g. BPL-003 5-MeO-DMT nasal spray). atai took a stake and later merged with Beckley Psytech to form AtaiBeckley, where he is a director.
interesting_fact: Beckley Psytech's 5-MeO-DMT nasal spray (BPL-003) for depression reached a successful FDA end-of-Phase 2 meeting, with Phase 3 planned for 2026 at AtaiBeckley.
deep_cut_fact: Says that at a school drug-education workshop aged about 13-14, his classmates' answers to a question about drugs all named his mother - an upbringing he says took the 'exciting act of rebellion' out of drugs and made him more sensible about them.
notes: A July 2026 SEC filing mentions a pending transaction involving Lilly and Nualtis, so company contacts may change. Has done podcasts (e.g. Power to the Patients).

name: Eric P Hansotia
current_role: Chairman, President and CEO, AGCO Corporation; Director, The Toro Company
profile: Wisconsin native Eric Hansotia spent ~20 years at John Deere before joining AGCO in 2013, rising to COO and becoming Chairman, President & CEO in January 2021. He leads the Massey Ferguson/Fendt/Valtra maker's push into precision ag (PTx) and smart, digitally connected farm machinery. Holds UW-Madison BS/MS in mechanical engineering and a University of Iowa MBA.
interesting_fact: A trained mechanical engineer, he has steered AGCO toward precision agriculture and AI, saying 'Young farmers are thirsty for digital interaction with smart machines.'
deep_cut_fact: His ag roots go back to working on a local dairy farm as a youth and being active in 4-H and FFA: 'I've had farming in my blood for most of my life.'

public_contacts.value: rachel.potts@agcocorp.com (Rachel Potts, Chief Communications Officer, published media contact)

notes: Accessible, frequently interviewed at farm shows (e.g., Farm Progress 2026). Route via AGCO corporate communications.

name: Matt Mills
current_role: President, SailPoint (identity security; NASDAQ: SAIL)
profile: Enterprise-software sales leader who spent 20+ years at Oracle, rising to SVP North America sales, then served as CEO of big-data firm MapR Technologies until 2018. He joined SailPoint as Chief Revenue Officer in 2019 and was promoted to President in August 2024, helping lead the company through its Thoma Bravo ownership and 2025 return to public markets.
interesting_fact: Before SailPoint he was CEO of MapR Technologies, a Hadoop/big-data platform company, after two decades selling at Oracle.
deep_cut_fact: On Thoma Bravo's 'Beyond the Deal' podcast he described his energy with 'I get up every day, and I'm on fire' and called himself 'actually a ham.'
notes: Common name; identity confirmed via SailPoint filings/press. Comfortable on podcasts and video interviews (ISMG, Thoma Bravo), so a podcast invite via SailPoint PR is plausible.

name: Brett T. Agee
current_role: President and CEO, Bayou Wells Holdings Company, LLC (since 2011); former director of Ranger Energy Services (resigned Sept 19, 2025)
profile: Texas oilfield-services entrepreneur who founded Bayou Well Services in 2009 and ran it until it was acquired by Ranger Energy Services in 2016. He then served as CEO of Ranger Services (2016-2017) and as an independent director of Ranger Energy Services (NYSE: RNGR) from 2017 until resigning in September 2025; his wealth largely reflects Ranger stock received in that deal.
interesting_fact: His company Bayou Well Services became one of the building blocks of Ranger Energy Services, a well-services provider that went public in 2017; he was Ranger's operating CEO in its first year.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for an oilfield-services CEO, his degree is a Bachelor of Science in Geography from Texas A&M University's College of Geosciences.
notes: No longer a Ranger insider (left board Sept 2025 per 2026 proxy: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1699039/000162828026023149/rngr-20260401.htm). No published personal, Bayou Wells Holdings or social contacts found. Low public profile; modest wealth relative to the list.

name: Ryan Fukushima
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Data, Tempus AI (Nasdaq: TEM), since February 2026; board member and advisor, Pathos AI
profile: Ryan Fukushima (40) was a founding-era executive at Tempus AI, Eric Lefkofsky's Chicago precision-medicine company that pairs clinical/molecular data with AI. He served as COO from 2015 to February 2026, when he became CEO of Tempus's Data business (data licensing and AI applications, which grew revenue 33% in Q3 2026). Before Tempus he was an entrepreneur-in-residence and VP at Lefkofsky's Lightbank.
interesting_fact: While COO of Tempus he simultaneously served as CEO of Pathos AI (2021-2025), an AI-driven oncology drug-development company, and remains on its board.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Tempus in September 2015 from venture firm Lightbank, where he had been an entrepreneur-in-residence; he holds a B.S. from Cal Poly and an MBA from Michigan's Ross School of Business.
notes: Healthcare-AI/data rather than energy or data centers; angle would be AI data licensing at scale. Press contact is Tempus media relations (Kelli Manalli) per Q3 2026 earnings release. Personal LinkedIn/X not verified.

name: John P Surma
current_role: Independent Lead Director, Marathon Petroleum (director since 2011; also MPLX GP board); director, Trane Technologies; former Chairman & CEO, U.S. Steel
profile: Pittsburgh-born accountant (Penn State '76, PwC partner) who joined Marathon Oil in 1997, ran Speedway SuperAmerica, then became CFO, CEO (2004-13) and chairman of U.S. Steel. Now lead independent director of refiner Marathon Petroleum (since Aug 2024) and a director of HVAC/data-center-cooling maker Trane Technologies.
interesting_fact: He was a minority owner of the NHL's Pittsburgh Penguins (as of 2012), served as vice chairman of President Obama's Advisory Committee for Trade Policy and Negotiations, and chaired the National Safety Council (2015-2017).
deep_cut_fact: In 1983, as a young Price Waterhouse accountant, he was picked for Ronald Reagan's Executive Exchange Program and spent time in Washington working with the Federal Reserve Board; in 2006 he received AISI's Elbert Gary Medal.
notes: non-managedirectors@ is MPC's published channel for communications to the independent (non-management) directors, which he leads as Lead Director - formal but legitimate. Trane board seat is relevant to data-center cooling. Avoid the Penn State trustee episode (2011-12) in outreach.

name: Victor K Lee
current_role: Independent director (audit committee financial expert), Monolithic Power Systems (Nasdaq: MPWR), since Sept 2006
profile: Victor K. Lee (69) is a veteran semiconductor finance executive with 40+ years in the industry. He was CFO of video-chip maker Ambarella (2007-2011), served on the MoSys board (2012-2016), and has sat on the board of power-chip maker MPS since 2006; his wealth comes largely from MPS stock, whose power ICs are now key in AI data-center servers.
interesting_fact: He has been on MPS's board for ~20 years, through its growth into a major supplier of power-management chips for AI/data-center hardware; he was re-nominated in 2026 for a term to 2029.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining Ambarella as CFO (Aug 2007-Mar 2011), he had already been CFO at several public and private companies; he holds both a B.S. in Industrial Engineering & Operations Research and an MBA from UC Berkeley.
notes: The corporate-secretary email is MPS's published channel for writing to any director. Low public profile; board member rather than operator.

name: Matthew C. Lucey
current_role: President & CEO and director, PBF Energy Inc. (NYSE: PBF)
profile: Energy executive (age 52) who has led PBF Energy - one of the largest US independent refiners, with six refineries - as CEO since July 2023 and President since 2015. An early PBF hire (VP Finance, 2008), he was CFO 2010-2014 as the company grew via refinery acquisitions; before PBF he spent 2001-08 at energy private-equity firm M.E. Zukerman & Co. after six years in banking.
interesting_fact: PBF's 2025 'Refining Business Improvement' initiative targeted at least $200M of annualized cash savings across its six-refinery system, a turnaround push after a Feb 2025 fire curtailed its Martinez, California refinery.
deep_cut_fact: At M.E. Zukerman & Co. he sat on the management committees of Cortez Pipeline Company, a 500-mile CO2 pipeline, Penreco (specialty petroleum products) and Venture Coke Company, a merchant petroleum-coke calciner.
notes: Public-company CEO; regularly on earnings calls and at industry conferences. Media requests likely via PBF corporate communications; IR email is the published route found.

name: Peter W Carter
current_role: President, Delta Air Lines (since April 1, 2026); SEC filings also list him as a director of Xcel Energy
profile: Peter Carter became Delta's President on April 1, 2026, succeeding Glen Hauenstein, after serving from 2015 as Chief Legal Officer, Corporate Secretary and Chief External Affairs Officer. He leads enterprise strategy, legal, regulatory, government affairs, real estate and sustainability, and works closely with partners such as Virgin Atlantic and Aeromexico.
interesting_fact: Besides Delta, he sits on the boards of Virgin Atlantic, Aeromexico, the SkyTeam alliance and the anti-poverty group Global Citizen.
deep_cut_fact: He chaired the Georgia Chamber of Commerce in 2020, served on the State of Georgia Judicial Selection Commission, and sits on the boards of the Westside Future Fund (Atlanta's Westside revitalisation) and the Minnesota Business Partnership.
notes: Energy angle is his Xcel Energy directorship (from SEC insider data; not shown in Xcel's April 2026 proxy, so likely appointed later in 2026 - verify). Route via Delta corporate communications.

name: Peter Trizzino
current_role: President, Global Sales, Dell Technologies (since January 2026)
profile: Career enterprise-tech sales leader (age 53 per Dell's FY26 10-K) who joined EMC in 2000 and stayed through the 2016 Dell-EMC merger, later running Dell's 'DT Select' strategic accounts and North America sales. He now oversees Dell's worldwide sales, presales and partner ecosystem as Dell sells AI servers and infrastructure at scale.
interesting_fact: Before taking over global sales he ran a 'Global Sales Modernization & GTM' role (Aug 2025-Jan 2026), simplifying, standardising and automating Dell's end-to-end sales motions.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career at Xerox before joining EMC in 2000, where he held sales and leadership roles for years before the Dell merger.
notes: Corporate executive, not a founder; wealth is Dell equity compensation. Best route is Dell media relations. Relevant to data-centre theme as head of sales for Dell's AI server business.

name: Ellen R Patterson
current_role: Senior EVP and General Counsel, Wells Fargo & Company; member of the Operating Committee
profile: Ellen Patterson has been Wells Fargo's General Counsel since March 2020, leading global legal affairs, litigation and regulatory matters and advising on corporate governance during the bank's long regulatory remediation. She was previously Group Head and General Counsel of TD Bank Group and, before that, a Simpson Thacher & Bartlett partner focused on M&A for financial institutions.
interesting_fact: American Banker profiled her as a 'Most Powerful Woman to Watch' for her role in steering Wells Fargo's legal and regulatory clean-up after the fake-accounts era.
