notes: Bank GC, not an entrepreneur; low media profile and limited fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Route via Wells Fargo corporate communications (newsroom media contacts page).

name: Vinay S. Kumar
current_role: Chief Product & Technology Officer, DigitalOcean (NYSE: DOCN), since January 2026
profile: Vinay Kumar joined DigitalOcean as CPTO in January 2026 to lead product, engineering, cloud infrastructure and security as the company pushes into AI inference cloud. He spent a decade-plus at Oracle (from 2015), helping build Oracle Cloud Infrastructure from its earliest days into a hyperscale platform, after earlier roles at AWS, Akamai and Dell/EMC.
interesting_fact: He was an early/founding leader of Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, helping grow it from inception into a global hyperscale cloud before moving to DigitalOcean to build its AI inference platform.
deep_cut_fact: Before Oracle he led product management for AWS core storage services, including Elastic Block Store (EBS) and S3. He trained as an electronics & communication engineer at Bangalore University and later earned an MBA at Babson College.
notes: Highly relevant to data-center/AI-cloud theme (OCI hyperscale buildout, DigitalOcean AI inference cloud). Oracle exec page may be stale/removed after his departure; deep-cut details are from it (fetched via search summary, page 403s to curl).

name: Vito S Pantilione
current_role: President, CEO & Director, Parke Bancorp / Parke Bank (Sewell, NJ)
profile: Vito Pantilione co-founded Parke Bank, which opened in January 1999, and has run it as President & CEO ever since (and its holding company Parke Bancorp since 2005). He grew the South Jersey community bank to over $2 billion in assets; earlier he owned mortgage firms Eagle Valley and Interstate Mortgage Management and was President of First Commercial Bank of Philadelphia (1991-94).
interesting_fact: Parke Bank turned a profit in only its 13th month of operation and, per the bank, has been profitable every quarter since; it has repeatedly ranked among the top-performing community banks in the U.S.
deep_cut_fact: He received an honorary doctorate from Philadelphia University for his work in finance and banking, and served on the Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia's Community Depository Institution Advisory Council.
notes: Small-cap community banker; only generic bank inbox found, no dedicated IR/press email. Bank emphasizes community work (veterans, feeding the poor, Boys & Girls Clubs). Weak fit for energy/data-center theme.

name: Alexandre Weinstein Manieu
current_role: Chairman of the Board and ~30% shareholder, Pluri Inc. (Nasdaq/TASE: PLUR); President, Sofgen Pharma (formerly Procaps Group)
profile: Chilean pharma entrepreneur (usually spelled Alejandro Esteban Weinstein Manieu) who ran CFR Pharmaceuticals as CEO from 2000 to 2014, expanding it to 26 countries before its US$3.3B sale to Abbott. Now Switzerland-based, he invests in health/biotech: he put US$6.5M into Israeli cell-technology firm Pluri in 2025 and became its chairman in Dec 2025, and regained control of Procaps (now Sofgen Pharma) in 2024.

He also helped set up Chilean stem-cell banks Vidacel and Banco de Vida.

profile: Career asset-management executive who spent 32 years at JPMorgan (CFO of its Investment Management & Private Banking unit, then a decade as global head of Fixed Income & Currency) before becoming AllianceBernstein CEO in 2017. current_role: Director, Vir Biotechnology (founding CEO 2017-2023) and director, Agilent Technologies
profile: Biotech veteran from Lynn, Massachusetts: Johns Hopkins biology professor, then Bayer Biotechnology, CEO of Exelixis (1996-2010, took it public), CEO of Biogen (2010-2016, refocused it on neurology), and founding CEO of Vir Biotechnology (2017-2023). profile: Robert Weyers (61) is a Wisconsin real-estate developer and private-equity investor and a founding director of Nicolet (board member since 2000). current_role: Chairman, President & CEO, Comstock Resources Inc. (Frisco, Texas)

name: Trevor Fetter
current_role: Senior Lecturer & Henry B. Arthur Fellow, Harvard Business School; Lead Director, The Hartford; Director, Omada Health
profile: Trevor Fetter was Chairman and CEO of Tenet Healthcare, a ~$20B hospital/healthcare services company, retiring in late 2017; earlier he was Tenet's CFO, CFO of MGM, and founder/CEO of hospital supply-chain firm Broadlane. profile: Bruce Kiefer is a long-serving Hershey Company chemist (since 1984) who joined the board of Pennsylvania bank holding company Mid Penn Bancorp in March 2023. name: Patrick Wendell
current_role: Co-founder, Databricks; leads the company's AI efforts (Genie, Unity Gateway, model-provider partnerships)
profile: Patrick Wendell is one of the UC Berkeley AMPLab researchers behind Apache Spark who co-founded Databricks in 2013, now one of the world's most valuable private data/AI companies. Long its VP of Engineering, he now leads Databricks' AI efforts, including Genie, Unity Gateway and partnerships with OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.
interesting_fact: He was a founding committer and PMC member of Apache Spark and served as release manager for several Spark releases, including Spark 1.0.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated summa cum laude with a B.S.E. in computer science from Princeton, and his Berkeley M.S. research focused on optimizing large-scale analytics workloads; in 2022 he returned to Princeton to talk founding Databricks with CS chair Jen Rexford.
notes: Low public profile compared with co-founders Ghodsi/Zaharia; strong AI/data-center infrastructure fit. Route via Databricks press team. Spark 1.0 release-manager detail is from the Princeton alumni event page; Rexford event from same page.

name: Reynold Xin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect, Databricks
profile: Computer scientist (U of Toronto EngSci; PhD UC Berkeley AMPLab under Michael Franklin and Ion Stoica) and one of the original creators of Apache Spark. Co-founded Databricks in 2013 with Matei Zaharia, Ali Ghodsi and others; it has become a data/AI platform giant valued around $134B. He designed Spark's GraphX, Project Tungsten and Structured Streaming and co-designed DataFrames.
interesting_fact: In 2014 he led a Databricks team that won the Daytona GraySort world record using Spark, crunching 100 TB of data in 23 minutes and dethroning the previous Hadoop-based record holder.
deep_cut_fact: His first Berkeley research project, Shark (SQL on Spark), won the Best Demo Award at SIGMOD 2012; he also served as release manager for Apache Spark 2.0.
notes: Strong data-center/AI-infrastructure fit. Active on X (@rxin); his social links are published on his official Databricks author page.

name: Zhu Guang
current_role: CEO, Du Xiaoman Financial (as of its 2018 spin-off from Baidu; current 2026 status not verified)
profile: Chinese internet executive (朱光) who was Baidu Senior Vice President and General Manager of its Financial Services Group. When Baidu divested a majority stake in the unit to investors led by TPG and Carlyle in 2018 (raising ~US$1.9bn), it was renamed Du Xiaoman Financial and he became its CEO, leading the AI-driven consumer-credit and wealth-management fintech.
interesting_fact: Du Xiaoman grew out of Baidu's financial services unit founded in December 2015; at the 2018 spin-off Baidu kept about 42% and Zhu said it would use Baidu AI to deliver 'technology-driven, trustworthy financial services'.
notes: Hurun lists him as a 'founder' but he was the Baidu executive who led the spin-off rather than a classic founder. Could not verify his 2026 role or find a published Du Xiaoman press contact (web search budget exhausted; Wikipedia rate-limited). Approach via Du Xiaoman corporate communications.

name: Ryan Petersen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Flexport (San Francisco); venture partner, Founders Fund
profile: Bethesda-raised Berkeley economics grad who ran an import-export business in China, co-founded trade-data firm ImportGenius (2007), then founded tech-driven freight forwarder Flexport in 2013 (Y Combinator 2014). Flexport hit an $8B valuation in 2022; Petersen handed the CEO role to Amazon's Dave Clark, then returned as CEO in Sept 2023 and bought Convoy's assets.
interesting_fact: In Oct 2021 his Twitter thread proposing fixes for the LA/Long Beach port backlog (e.g. relaxing container-stacking limits) went viral and reached Gov. Gavin Newsom; local authorities adopted some of his suggestions.
deep_cut_fact: At 17 he and his brother David started an import-export business buying goods from China and selling them on eBay; he moved to China in 2005 to run it, before an MBA at Columbia (2008).
notes: Very accessible and media-friendly; active on X (@typesfast) and does many podcasts/TV hits on tariffs, Hormuz and supply-chain risk. Good energy/logistics angle. No published press email found on Flexport's newsroom.

name: Doug Hirsch
current_role: Co-founder and Board Member, GoodRx Holdings (NASDAQ: GDRX)
profile: Doug Hirsch co-founded GoodRx in 2011 to make prescription drug prices transparent and was co-CEO until April 2023, then Chief Mission Officer until October 2024; he remains on the board. GoodRx went public in 2020. Earlier he held senior product roles at Yahoo! and Facebook (VP of product around 2005) and ran DailyStrength.
interesting_fact: He co-founded GoodRx with fellow ex-Facebook executive Scott Marlette and Trevor Bezdek; Hirsch was Facebook's VP of product in 2005, working closely with Mark Zuckerberg.
deep_cut_fact: Before GoodRx he was CEO of DailyStrength (2005-2008), a health-focused network of online support groups - an early bet on social health communities; he holds a B.A. in Political Science from Tufts.
notes: No longer an operating executive at GoodRx (board only since Oct 2024). No published press/personal email found (search budget exhausted); LinkedIn or GoodRx corporate communications are likely routes. Limited energy/data-center relevance; good founder story.

name: Scott Marlette
current_role: Co-founder, GoodRx; former partner at Slow Ventures (stepped back from venture capital); no current operating role found
profile: Early Facebook engineer and product manager (c. 2005-2010) who co-founded GoodRx, the prescription-drug price comparison and coupon platform, in Santa Monica in 2011 with Doug Hirsch and Trevor Bezdek. He joined Facebook-alumni seed fund Slow Ventures as a partner in 2016, then stepped back from VC; GoodRx went public in 2020.
interesting_fact: At Facebook he started as an engineer and is credited with building Facebook Photos, later overseeing Groups, Events and Inbox as a product manager.
deep_cut_fact: Slow Ventures was nicknamed the 'Facebook Alumni Fund', backed by five early Facebook friends. When he stepped back, managing director Kevin Colleran said he was taking time off from VC and 'may eventually start another company of his own like he did previously with GoodRx.'
notes: Very low public profile; no verified personal site or social accounts found. Facebook Photos credit comes from Crunchbase (aggregator); verify before citing. Possible warm routes: Slow Ventures (slow.co) or GoodRx co-founder Doug Hirsch.

name: Jesse Levinson
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Zoox (Amazon subsidiary)
profile: Princeton summa cum laude graduate who did his CS PhD and postdoc under Sebastian Thrun at Stanford, helping build Stanford's 2007 DARPA Urban Challenge car and later leading its self-driving research. He co-founded Zoox in 2014 to build a purpose-built electric robotaxi; Amazon acquired it in 2020 and he remains CTO, overseeing software, AI, compute and sensing.
interesting_fact: Rather than retrofitting existing cars, Zoox designed a purpose-built robotaxi from scratch; Amazon bought the company in 2020 and Levinson stayed on as CTO to scale it.
deep_cut_fact: As a high-schooler he won a 2000 Intel ISEF Grand Award (psychology) for 'Computer Simulated Evolution of Behavior'; he also co-created the iPhone photography app Pro HDR, bought by more than a million people.
notes: ISEF award source: https://www.societyforscience.org/alumni/notable/jesse-levinson/. Press requests likely routed through Amazon/Zoox comms; no dedicated press email found. Frequent conference speaker (WEF, TechCrunch, EmTech).

name: Tim Kentley-Klay
current_role: Founder of HYPR (AI robotics/autonomous mobility startup); founder of Melbourne animation studio XYZ Studios. Current status of HYPR not confirmed
profile: Australian designer-turned-tech founder who co-founded self-driving company Zoox with Jesse Levinson in 2014 and was its CEO until the board removed him in August 2018; Amazon bought Zoox in 2020 for a reported ~$1.2bn. He then founded HYPR, an AI robotics company that raised a US$10m seed (Andrew 'Twiggy' Forrest and R7 Partners) at a reported US$200m valuation.
interesting_fact: He describes himself as a 'painter, designer, animator, film-maker, trouble-maker and thinker', and won the 2020 Advance Global Australian Award.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zoox he founded XYZ Studios, a commercial-animation studio, in Melbourne in 2003 despite having no animation training and, by the studio's account, not knowing a single person in advertising; it grew to offices in Melbourne and New York.
notes: No verified published contact found (HYPR and XYZ sites blocked automated access). Avoid dwelling on the 2018 Zoox exit. Hurun lists him as a Zoox founder (2019-20); personal wealth from the Amazon deal is undisclosed. Autonomy/robotics angle rather than energy.

name: Zia Chishti
current_role: Investor; co-founder of Align Technology, The Resource Group (TRG) and Afiniti (left Afiniti as chairman/CEO in 2021) - current operating role unclear
profile: Columbia CS/econ grad and ex-Morgan Stanley/McKinsey banker who invented Invisalign while at Stanford GSB and co-founded Align Technology (1997, IPO 2001). He then co-founded Pakistan-based investor TRG and AI call-center routing firm Afiniti, which reached unicorn status; he resigned from Afiniti in 2021.
interesting_fact: Named inventor on around 150 patents and co-founder of three unicorns; TRG's first deal was buying Align's abandoned Lahore operation and rehiring laid-off staff, growing into one of Pakistan's largest tech employers.
deep_cut_fact: The Invisalign idea came from his own orthodontic treatment in his early twenties - he envisioned computer-designed clear plastic aligners instead of metal braces while an MBA student at Stanford. He received Pakistan's Sitara-e-Imtiaz for IT in 2018.
notes: Caution: resigned from Afiniti in 2021 after sexual misconduct allegations were made public (he won a 2025 libel settlement against the Daily Telegraph); reputational risk for a podcast guest. No published personal/office contact found; Afiniti no longer represents him.

name: J. Andrew Bagnell
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Aurora Innovation (NASDAQ: AUR); Consulting Professor, CMU Robotics Institute and Machine Learning Dept.
profile: Drew Bagnell is a machine-learning and robotics researcher who co-founded self-driving company Aurora in 2016 with Chris Urmson and Sterling Anderson, serving as CTO until 2020 and now Chief Scientist. Earlier he was a CMU professor (2004-2018) and head of perception/autonomy architect at Uber ATG. Aurora now runs driverless trucks commercially in Texas.
interesting_fact: His research group has won best-paper awards at ICML, RSS and NeurIPS, and he co-authored DAgger, a widely used imitation-learning algorithm for teaching robots from expert demonstrations.
deep_cut_fact: He was the founding director of CMU's Robotics Institute Summer Scholars program, which has brought hundreds of undergraduates from around the world into robotics research, and won CMU's 2016 Ryan Award for Meritorious Teaching. His BS is in electrical engineering from the University of Florida.
notes: Goes by Drew Bagnell. DAgger attribution (Ross, Gordon & Bagnell, AISTATS 2011) is from general knowledge of the literature, not the cited page. Academic and podcast-friendly (NeurIPS invited talks). Fit for AI angle; less so energy/data centers. Route via Aurora press.

name: Dave Palmer
current_role: General Partner, Ten Eleven Ventures (leads its European office in Cheltenham, UK)
profile: Former UK intelligence technologist (GCHQ and MI5) who co-founded Cambridge AI-cybersecurity firm Darktrace in 2013 and, as Director of Technology and later Chief Product Officer, helped scale it to a 2021 London IPO and an eventual $5.3B take-private by Thoma Bravo. He now invests in cybersecurity startups as a General Partner at Ten Eleven Ventures, an early Darktrace backer.
interesting_fact: He says what most excites and worries him in cyber is the same thing: AI coding agents that will soon find huge numbers of vulnerabilities, forcing the world to fix decades of software risk at once.
deep_cut_fact: He names Gaven Smith, who later became GCHQ's CTO, as the biggest influence on his career - teaching him to study why things succeed, not just how. His hardest Darktrace lesson: stop describing how clever the product/team was and tell stories of customer success.
notes: Accessible and media-friendly; regular conference speaker (RSA Conference, GBx). Ten Eleven opened its UK office with him as GP (PR Newswire, 2022). Good guest for AI-security angle.

name: Emily Orton
current_role: Co-founder and former CMO of Darktrace (stepped down July 2022); reportedly Non-Executive Director at ThreatSpike (from May 2025, per Crunchbase)
profile: Emily Orton was a founding team member of Cambridge, UK-born AI cybersecurity firm Darktrace (2013) and its Chief Marketing Officer through the 2021 London IPO, building its global marketing engine. She stepped down as CMO in July 2022; Darktrace was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2024 for ~$5.3B.
interesting_fact: She built Darktrace's marketing from founding to IPO, helping turn a Cambridge mathematics/AI startup into a London-listed company used by thousands of organisations worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: She is a linguist by training, with an MA in Modern Languages from the University of Cambridge, rather than a technical background.
notes: Low public profile since leaving Darktrace in 2022; no verified personal website or social account found (Crunchbase lists a ThreatSpike NED role - unverified). Hurun 'unicorn founder' listing (2019-2020) only. LinkedIn likely the best route but URL not verified.

name: Jack Stockdale
current_role: Founding Chief Technology Officer, Darktrace (Cambridge, UK; taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2024)
profile: Jack Stockdale OBE FREng is Darktrace's founding CTO (2013) and leads the Bayesian and self-learning AI behind its cyber-defence products. He was previously a technical director at Autonomy, worked at blinkx and was chief architect at Invoke Capital, Darktrace's seed investor. Thoma Bravo took Darktrace private for about $5.3B in 2024.
interesting_fact: He and Darktrace's then-CEO were both appointed OBE in 2019 for services to cyber security; he is also a Fellow of the Royal Academy of Engineering.
deep_cut_fact: He and his Cambridge development team were recognised by the Royal Academy of Engineering's MacRobert Award committee twice, in 2017 and again in 2019, for outstanding contribution to engineering. He studied computer science at Lancaster University.
notes: Low public profile but does speak at events (e.g. MIT Technology Review cybersecurity events). Best route is Darktrace media relations. Wealth figure unclear since Darktrace went private.

name: Nicole Eagan
current_role: Co-founder and Strategic Advisor, Darktrace (owned by Thoma Bravo since 2024)
profile: Tech executive with ~30 years at Oracle, HP, startups and VC who co-founded Cambridge, UK AI-cybersecurity firm Darktrace in 2013. She was CEO from 2014, then Chief Strategy and AI Officer from 2020; Darktrace listed in London in 2021 and was taken private by Thoma Bravo in 2024. She now advises on strategy.
interesting_fact: Darktrace grew out of a team of Cambridge mathematicians and ex-intelligence specialists applying self-learning AI to detect cyber threats; it now protects close to 10,000 organisations across cloud, email, network and OT.
deep_cut_fact: She was named 'AI Leader of the Year' and took the No. 1 spot on The Software Report's 'Top 25 Women Leaders in Cybersecurity' in 2020.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (CNBC TEC, Fortune Brainstorm AI, Economist Impact); speaker-bureau route likely receptive. Input lists company value $2B; Thoma Bravo deal valued Darktrace at ~$5.3B.

name: Poppy Gustafsson
current_role: Labour life peer (Baroness Gustafsson of Chesterton, House of Lords); trustee of RUSI (from Jan 2026); former co-founder and CEO of Darktrace
profile: British accountant-turned-tech founder (b. 1982, Huntingdon) who co-founded Cambridge AI cybersecurity company Darktrace in 2013 as CFO, became co-CEO in 2016 and sole CEO in 2020, leading its 2021 London IPO before its 2024 sale to Thoma Bravo. She served as UK Minister for Investment (Oct 2024-Sep 2025) and joined the RUSI board in 2026.
interesting_fact: She was named Tech Businesswoman of the Year at the 2019 UK Tech Awards, received an OBE (2019) and CBE (2025) for services to cybersecurity, and was made a life peer in 2024 so she could serve as investment minister.
deep_cut_fact: Before Darktrace she started out at Cambridge venture firm Amadeus Capital Partners, then joined Autonomy in 2009 as a corporate controller until its acquisition by HP; the University of Sheffield, her alma mater, gave her an honorary DSc in 2022.
notes: Hurun listed her as Darktrace founder (company now private under Thoma Bravo). Parliament's published route is the House of Lords member contact service (forwards to members). Frequent speaker (London Tech Week) - podcast-friendly.

name: Jeff Kinsey
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Dataminr (per company/third-party profiles; not confirmed by a dated primary source)
profile: Yale computer-science graduate who co-founded Dataminr in New York in 2009 with Ted Bailey and Sam Hendel. Dataminr's AI platform detects breaking events from public data (originally Twitter) in real time for corporations, newsrooms and governments; Hurun lists it at a ~$4B valuation. In 2025 it agreed to buy cyber-threat-intelligence firm ThreatConnect for $290M.
interesting_fact: Dataminr first drew wide notice when its system flagged the death of Osama bin Laden 23 minutes before major news organizations reported it.
deep_cut_fact: Dataminr's three founders (Kinsey, Ted Bailey and Sam Hendel) were Yale undergraduate roommates.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Ted Bailey is the company's public face. No published press email verified (dataminr.com was bot-blocked on direct fetch). Net worth not quantified; Hurun unicorn-founder listing only.

name: Theodore Bailey
current_role: Founder, CEO & Chairman, Dataminr (New York)
profile: Ted Bailey founded Dataminr in 2009 with Yale roommates Sam Hendel and Jeff Kinsey to detect breaking events from Twitter and other public data in real time. It grew into an AI real-time event-detection and risk platform for corporations, newsrooms and governments (valued ~$4bn), and in 2025-26 expanded into cyber defense (ThreatConnect) and large defense contracts.
interesting_fact: In August 2026 the Pentagon awarded Dataminr a $318m, five-year contract (through 2031) for AI-powered alerting from publicly available information across all US military branches and combatant commands.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his Yale BA in American Studies with a concentration on technology's impact on society, and says that academic interest was the direct inspiration for Dataminr; before founding it he worked in social-media-analytics strategy/product roles for public-sector agencies and NYC start-ups.
notes: Legal first name appears as Edward/Theodore in some databases; goes by Ted. Speaks at AI and journalism conferences (HumanX, ONA, Imagination in Action, WEF) - conference circuit is a natural route. Press email cited across 2025-26 Dataminr releases.

name: Yet-Ming Chiang
current_role: Kyocera Professor of Materials Science and Engineering, MIT; co-founder and Chief Scientist of 24M Technologies and Form Energy
profile: Taiwan-born MIT materials scientist (b. 1958), serial climate-tech founder with 100+ patents. Co-founded American Superconductor, A123 Systems (LFP batteries), 24M (semi-solid Li-ion), Form Energy (iron-air long-duration storage), Sublime Systems (electrochemical cement) and Desktop Metal; since 2023 has started more, incl. Propel Aero (electric aviation).
interesting_fact: LFP, the cathode chemistry his lab and A123 helped commercialize, has become the dominant battery chemistry in EVs and grid storage worldwide; the Boston Globe has named him a Tech Power Player in energy three times.
deep_cut_fact: He arrived at MIT as a freshman in 1976 and 'never left' (SB 1980, ScD 1985, faculty since). As a junior professor he was told to keep his startup work quiet because academic entrepreneurship wasn't well regarded. Of his work he says: 'Climate is the biggest problem that I could think of tackling with the skill set that I have.'
notes: Excellent podcast fit (batteries, long-duration storage for grid/data centers via Form Energy). Accessible academic who gives interviews (Cipher, MIT Tech Review ClimateTech). No published email confirmed; best via MIT DMSE or Form Energy/24M press teams.

name: Jason Citron
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Discord (CEO 2015-April 2025; now director/adviser)
profile: Jason Citron co-founded Discord, the chat platform that grew from gamer voice chat into a mass-market community app valued around $15B. He previously founded mobile social-gaming network OpenFeint (sold to GREE for ~$104M in 2011). He stepped down as CEO in April 2025, handing over to Humam Sakhnini ahead of a planned IPO, and remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Discord began as an internal chat tool at his game studio Hammer & Chisel while it was building the mobile MOBA 'Fates Forever'; frustration with existing gamer voice apps led the team to pivot to communication software.
deep_cut_fact: He learned to code in QBasic at 13, and his first program was a text-based role-playing game; he calls Final Fantasy VI his favorite game and has said 'I was a Squaresoft fanboy, and I still am.' He was inducted into Full Sail University's Hall of Fame in 2025.
notes: Post-CEO, said he planned to catch up on a backlog of video games; more available than when CEO. Discord press inquiries via the newsroom address. Avoid child-safety hearing topics.

name: André Schwämmlein
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Flix SE (FlixBus, FlixTrain, Greyhound, Kâmil Koç), Munich
profile: André Schwämmlein co-founded FlixBus in Munich in 2011 with Daniel Krauss and Jochen Engert, launching its first routes in Bavaria in 2013 as Germany deregulated intercity buses. As CEO he has built Flix into a global long-distance travel platform, expanding into the US (buying Greyhound in 2021), Brazil, India, Mexico, Australia and Peru.
interesting_fact: Flix runs an asset-light model: it mostly handles network planning, pricing, booking and marketing while local partner firms operate the buses; in 2021 it acquired America's Greyhound Lines.
deep_cut_fact: The FlixBus idea took shape in 2009 while he was a consultant at Boston Consulting Group, discussing Germany's planned bus-market deregulation with his future co-founders. He also sits on the supervisory boards of Scout24 SE and the digital association Bitkom.
notes: Executive communications handled by Iris Brand (Flix Corporate Communications) via globalpress@flix.com. Electrified buses/trains are an energy angle for the podcast.

name: Daniel Krauss
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Information Officer & Chief HR Officer, Flix SE (FlixBus/FlixTrain/Greyhound), Munich
profile: Daniel Krauss co-founded FlixBus in Munich in 2011 with Jochen Engert and Andre Schwammlein, betting on Germany's planned deregulation of long-distance buses. As CIO and CHRO he oversees Flix's technology and people as it grew into an international mobility group spanning FlixBus, FlixTrain, Greyhound and Kamil Koc. He also invests in and advises startups.
interesting_fact: The three co-founders met at university and began sketching the FlixBus idea in 2009, when Germany announced plans to deregulate intercity buses; Flix later bought America's Greyhound Lines (2021) and says it has carried 500+ million passengers.
deep_cut_fact: He is a committed backer of entrepreneurship education: an active shareholder in STARTUP TEENS, Germany's largest NGO for entrepreneurial education, a co-shareholder and trustee of Berlin's CODE University, and a frequent lecturer at Friedrich-Alexander University Erlangen.
notes: Not to be confused with German actor Daniel Krauss (de.wikipedia). Flix is tech-heavy (in-house routing/pricing platform) - good entrepreneurship/mobility angle.

name: Jochen Engert
current_role: Co-founder and Deputy Chairman of the Supervisory Board, Flix SE (FlixBus/FlixTrain); business angel
profile: German entrepreneur (b. 1977) who co-founded FlixBus in 2011 with Daniel Krauss and André Schwämmlein when Germany liberalised long-distance bus travel. He was co-CEO of FlixMobility from founding until March 2022, drove its US expansion from 2017 (incl. Greyhound), and since April 2022 has been deputy chair of Flix SE's supervisory board while angel-investing in tech start-ups.
interesting_fact: The founders spotted FlixBus in 2011 when the government planned to end Deutsche Bahn's 75-year monopoly on domestic long-distance travel; they initially held back, assuming 'Deutsche Bahn will surely do it itself.'
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Goßmannsdorf am Main, a ~1,000-person village near Ochsenfurt in Lower Franconia, played in the local football club, studied technical business administration in Stuttgart (with two semesters at the University of Ottawa) and was on a BCG sabbatical writing a PhD on 'Industrial Service Pricing' at WHU when FlixBus began.
notes: Mentors young founders via Startup Teens and is a jury member for BCG's Business@School initiative - good entrepreneurship-podcast angle. No longer operational at Flix; Flix press office is the best documented route. US press: press@FlixBus.com (https://www.flixbus.com/company/press-room).

name: Girish Mathrubootham
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Together Fund (AI/SaaS venture fund); founder of Freshworks
profile: Girish Mathrubootham is a former Zoho executive. In 2010 he co-founded Freshdesk, later Freshworks, in Chennai with Shan Krishnasamy, and took it public on Nasdaq in 2021 as one of India's flagship SaaS companies. He handed the CEO role to Dennis Woodside in 2024 and then became executive chairman. He is no longer listed on Freshworks' board and now invests in AI-first software founders through Together Fund, which he co-founded with Manav Garg.
interesting_fact: In his 2021 IPO founder letter he listed the doubts he had heard: '600 help desks in the market', 'you can't find talent in Chennai', and 'you can't build a global SaaS company from India'. He chose to stay in Chennai anyway.
deep_cut_fact: His IPO founder letter opens with 'I feel really good today', the text of an artwork on the wall of Freshworks' Chennai office. He says he showed a picture of it at almost every company meeting to remind staff they choose how they approach their work.
notes: Together Fund lists him as US-based. Very active in the Indian SaaS community (SaaSBoomi) and generally approachable for founder-focused podcasts. The Zoho litigation (settled 2021) is a topic to avoid.

name: Shan Krishnasamy
profile: Former Zoho employee who co-founded Freshdesk with Girish Mathrubootham in Chennai in 2010; it became Freshworks (2017), moved HQ to San Mateo (2018) and listed on Nasdaq in 2021. Current role not verified.
interesting_fact: Freshworks was one of the first Indian-born SaaS companies to IPO on Nasdaq (2021), having started as Freshdesk in Chennai.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Freshdesk he worked at Zoho, the Chennai SaaS company, alongside co-founder Girish Mathrubootham.
notes: Web search budget ran out mid-lane; record built only from direct page fetches, kept minimal — re-research recommended.

name: Dave Waiser
current_role: Founder of Gett (GetTaxi); current role not verified
profile: Dave (Shahar) Waiser is the Israeli entrepreneur who founded GetTaxi (later Gett) with Roi More, a ride-hailing and corporate ground-transport platform that reached a ~$1B+ valuation. Gett's Israeli and international business was sold to Pango (deal announced May 2024 for $175M) and Lyft agreed in April 2026 to buy Gett's UK operations for GBP 40M.
interesting_fact: Gett's UK operations are being folded into Lyft's European platform Freenow after Lyft agreed in April 2026 to buy them for GBP 40 million.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for GetTaxi came to him in summer 2009 while he waited about 30 minutes for a taxi to the airport in Palo Alto, California.
notes: Wikipedia's History section calls him Shahar Waiser; the infobox says Dave Waiser - same person. Web search budget ran out mid-lane, so his current venture and any published contact could not be verified; check his LinkedIn/X before outreach.

name: Roi More
profile: Israeli entrepreneur credited as co-founder (with Shahar/Dave Waiser) of GetTaxi, launched in Tel Aviv in 2011 and later rebranded Gett, the corporate ground-transport app. Gett's Israeli business was sold to Pango (deal announced May 2024, $175M) and its UK operations to Lyft/Freenow (April 2026, GBP 40M). His current activities could not be established.
interesting_fact: GetTaxi was conceived in 2009 when co-founder Shahar Waiser was waiting for a taxi in Palo Alto; it launched in Tel Aviv and London in 2011.
notes: Name spelling varies (Roi More / Roi Mora / possibly Roi Man in Hebrew sources), so identity details are uncertain. Web-search quota ran out mid-lane; only Wikipedia (en/he) could be checked. No indication of death found. Needs a follow-up search.

name: Nigel Toon
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, BlankPage Capital (deep-tech VC); stepped down as Graphcore Executive Chair on 31 Jul 2026
profile: British semiconductor entrepreneur who co-founded AI-processor maker Graphcore with Simon Knowles in 2016 (idea born 2012), raised over $600m and sold it to SoftBank in 2024; Graphcore now has ~1,000 staff. Earlier he was a founder/CEO of Icera (bought by Nvidia) and a long-time Altera executive. He now co-runs BlankPage Capital to back European deep-tech chip and AI firms.
interesting_fact: Graphcore's first chip, the Colossus MK1 - named after Bletchley Park's wartime Colossus computer - shipped to Microsoft in 2018 and, with 1,200+ cores and 23.6bn transistors, was then the world's most complex CMOS chip. His 2024 book 'How AI Thinks' (Penguin/Torva) became a Times bestseller.
deep_cut_fact: Graphcore was conceived not in a garage but over lunch at the Marlborough Tavern pub in Bath in January 2012; he and Knowles then spent 2012-14 touring the world meeting AI pioneers, many of whom became friends-and-family investors.

public_contacts.value: press@graphcore.ai (Graphcore press office; he remains a supporter 'from the sidelines')

notes: Very media-friendly and a published author - strong podcast candidate (AI chips, UK/EU sovereign compute, energy efficiency of AI). BlankPage Capital (co-founded with Ekaterina Almasque) had no verifiable website found; publisher publicity or LinkedIn are likely better routes than Graphcore now.

name: Simon Knowles
current_role: Co-founder, CTO and EVP Engineering, Graphcore (Bristol, UK; acquired by SoftBank in 2024)
profile: Simon Knowles is a Cambridge-trained British chip architect who has designed processors for over 30 years. He co-founded Element-14 (DSL chips, sold to Broadcom), Icera (cellular basebands, sold to Nvidia in 2011) and, with Nigel Toon, Graphcore, whose Colossus IPU he architected for AI workloads. name: Louay Eldada

profile: Louay Eldada, a Columbia electrical-engineering PhD, is a photonics and solar technologist. He built telecom photonics at Honeywell/AlliedSignal, founded Telephotonics (bought by DuPont), was CTO at thin-film solar maker HelioVolt and chief science officer at SunEdison, then co-founded lidar company Quanergy in 2012, which was valued around $2B. name: Bradley Keywell
current_role: Founder and Executive Chairman, Gigawatt AI (AI-native operating system for energy and water utilities); director, TKO Group

name: Eugenio Pace

profile: Argentine-born Eugenio Pace co-founded developer-focused identity platform Auth0 in 2013 with Matías Woloski, after more than a decade at Microsoft. He became CEO in 2017, made Auth0 an Argentine-rooted unicorn, and sold it to Okta for about $6.5B in 2021. He then served as Okta's President, Business Operations, and retired in March 2025.

current_role: Co-founder and former CTO, Auth0; product advisor via Shipit Partners (e.g. OpenZeppelin, 2023); angel investor
profile: Argentine engineer who co-founded identity platform Auth0 in 2013 with Eugenio Pace and served as CTO. profile: Nevada Sanchez co-founded Butterfly Network with Jonathan Rothberg in 2011 and helped develop its ultrasound-on-a-chip, the basis of the handheld Butterfly iQ whole-body scanner. deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author of 'Elements of Programming Interviews' (with Adnan Aziz and Tsung-Hsien Lee), the cult coding-interview prep book used by thousands of software engineers.

public_contacts.value: https://intro.co/AmitPrakash (paid advisory calls he lists himself)

notes: No published personal net worth; on Hurun unicorn-founder list via ThoughtSpot. Accessible founder: active on LinkedIn and offers paid intro.co calls. Good AI/data angle.

name: Priyendra Deshwal
current_role: Software engineer at Snowflake (reported, since Aug 2025); co-founder of ThoughtSpot and NetSpring
profile: IIT Kanpur (B.Tech) and Stanford (MS CS) engineer who worked on search and ads technology at Google before co-founding search-driven analytics company ThoughtSpot in 2012 (valued ~$4B). In 2019 he and fellow ThoughtSpot founders started warehouse-native analytics firm NetSpring as CTO; Optimizely bought it in 2024, and he has reportedly since joined Snowflake.
interesting_fact: He co-founded two analytics companies with the same core team: ThoughtSpot (2012) and NetSpring (2019), which Optimizely acquired in late 2024 to power analytics across its marketing platform.
notes: Low public profile, engineer rather than spokesperson; no personally published contacts found. Current Snowflake role comes from TheOrg (aggregator), so unconfirmed. Google and education details come from MarketScreener/TheOrg profiles. ThoughtSpot no longer his main affiliation.

name: Sanjay Agrawal
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Revefi (AI data-operations / data observability startup, founded 2021)
profile: Database researcher-turned-founder: after a decade-plus at Microsoft (incl. Research work on self-tuning databases) he co-founded ThoughtSpot in 2012 (AI/search analytics, ~$4bn valuation), leading engineering. In 2021 he co-founded Revefi, which raised a $20m Series A and was a 2025 Gartner Cool Vendor.
interesting_fact: At ThoughtSpot he pushed the decision to build a specialised in-memory database for analytics and a push-based data-recommendation system, foundations of its 'search your data' product.
deep_cut_fact: At Microsoft Research he co-authored the VLDB 2000 paper 'Automated Selection of Materialized Views and Indexes in SQL Databases' with Surajit Chaudhuri and Vivek Narasayya - the AutoAdmin work behind SQL Server 2000's index/view tuning tool; Revefi says he earned two 'Test of Time' awards at Microsoft.
notes: Hurun unicorn-founder listing (ThoughtSpot); personal wealth not confirmed as $1bn+. Technical founder - deep database/AI-for-data angle. Name is common: confirm via ThoughtSpot/Revefi context. Best route is Revefi's website/contact.

name: Shashank Gupta
current_role: Cofounder and CTO, Revefi (AI/data FinOps and observability); cofounder of ThoughtSpot
profile: IIT Delhi / UT Austin-educated engineer who cofounded search-driven analytics firm ThoughtSpot in 2012, building its search engine and leading engineering for three years. After leading data quality for Meta's exabyte-scale warehouse, he cofounded Revefi in 2021 with ThoughtSpot cofounder Sanjay Agrawal to cut AI and cloud-data spend.
interesting_fact: Revefi's RADEN agent targets AI/data cost control across Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery and LLM apps; in Nov 2026 it launched closed-loop 'AI FinOps' to budget and enforce enterprise AI spend.
deep_cut_fact: While working on an EdTech startup venture, he went back to school for a master's degree in education to understand learners from the inside; earlier he worked on distributed systems and search at Amazon and Yahoo.
notes: Revefi media contact is Girish Bhat (published on press releases). Revefi runs its own 'Deep Dive' podcast. Good AI-cost/compute-efficiency angle.

name: Vijay Ganesan
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of NetSpring (acquired by Optimizely, 2024); now leads NetSpring analytics within Optimizely (exact current title unverified)
profile: Vijay Ganesan, an IIT Madras graduate, co-founded AI-search analytics firm ThoughtSpot (2012; valued at about $4.2bn) and led product there until 2019. He then co-founded NetSpring, a warehouse-native analytics platform, which Optimizely acquired in late 2024. He now works on bringing that analytics across Optimizely One.
interesting_fact: Before founding companies he spent eight years at Oracle as technical lead for its flagship business-intelligence product. He has now built two analytics startups on that foundation: ThoughtSpot and NetSpring.
deep_cut_fact: NetSpring was built on his thesis that 'event data' from sensors, devices, phones and product instrumentation was outgrowing traditional reporting tools. Its answer was analytics that sit directly on the customer's data warehouse rather than copying data out. Dell Technologies Capital backed it at seed and led its Series A.
notes: The press contact is Optimizely's VP of Global Communications as listed on the 2024 NetSpring acquisition release, so it may be outdated. He appears on marketing and analytics podcasts (e.g. Agile Brand), so he is open to podcast appearances. Not a billionaire; the Hurun unicorn-founder listing relates to ThoughtSpot.

name: Hao Jianan
current_role: Co-founder, COO & Director, CreateAI Holdings (formerly TuSimple; OTC: TSPH); legal representative of Beijing TuSimple
profile: NTU PhD in parallel/distributed systems and ex-Temasek Labs researcher who cofounded autonomous-trucking firm TuSimple in 2015 as COO, running its China engineering. After TuSimple froze US operations and delisted, it rebranded in Dec 2024 as CreateAI, pivoting to generative AI for games and animation.
interesting_fact: CreateAI open-sourced its 'Ruyi' image-to-video model (Ruyi-Mini-7B, a DiT model trained on ~200M clips) on Hugging Face and licensed Jin Yong's martial-arts IP and The Three-Body Problem for AI-made games and animation.
deep_cut_fact: Before TuSimple he was a supercomputing researcher: in 2007 he designed a parallel pi-calculation system that broke the world record for computing digits of pi.
notes: Sensitive context: TuSimple co-founder disputes and a 2025 report on data transfers to China (TechCrunch); avoid. COO/director role per https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/tsph/company. No working CreateAI/TuSimple press or IR email found (ir.tusimple.com returns 403; createai.com unreachable from here). The pi record claim comes from the company's own 36Kr team bio.

name: Sebastian Thrun
current_role: Co-founder, Cresta (AI for contact centers); founder, Sage AI Labs; adjunct professor, Stanford University
profile: Sebastian Thrun (b. 1967, Solingen) led Stanford's Stanley to win the 2005 DARPA Grand Challenge, led Google's self-driving project (now Waymo) and co-founded Google X. He co-founded Udacity, ran eVTOL firm Kitty Hawk, co-founded $2bn AI contact-center unicorn Cresta (2017) and recently founded agentic-AI start-up Sage AI Labs.
interesting_fact: Larry Page reportedly disguised himself to watch a driverless-car race in order to scout and recruit Thrun to Google, where he went on to found the moonshot lab Google X.
deep_cut_fact: Long before self-driving cars he built museum tour-guide robots: Rhino at the University of Bonn (1994) and Minerva, which guided thousands of visitors at the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History in 1998 - the same museum that now houses his DARPA-winning car Stanley.
notes: Hurun lists him for Cresta. Very accessible public speaker and podcast guest (recent appearances on AI, flying cars, education). Active on X (posted 2025 about hiring for an agentic-AI start-up) but handle not verified here.

name: Liang Jia'en
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CTO, Unisound AI Technology (HKEX: 9678)
profile: Liang Jia'en (梁家恩), a USTC graduate with a CAS Institute of Automation PhD, led speech-recognition R&D at CAS before co-founding Unisound in 2012. Unisound makes voice AI, AI chips and its 'Shanhai' large model for IoT and healthcare, and listed in Hong Kong on 30 June 2025.
interesting_fact: Unisound's work on what it called the world's first AI chip for IoT voice interaction won the Wu Wenjun AI Science & Technology Progress Award; its medical knowledge-graph work won a Beijing Science & Technology Progress first prize.
deep_cut_fact: At CAS in 2008-2010 his biggest project put machine scoring into the English oral middle-school entrance exams for all of Jiangsu province and Wenzhou, reaching millions of students. He calls it China's first large-scale AI scoring deployment; it was hard to commercialise inside CAS, which pushed him toward entrepreneurship.
notes: Self-described 'engineer at heart': all four Unisound founders are AI PhDs, and he is the one who stayed on R&D. Quote: tech founders must not 'succeed by technology and then fail by technology', since tech is only a third of the business chain. CEO Huang Wei is the commercial face. Mostly Chinese-language media.

name: Paul Nguyen
current_role: Unknown; co-founder of View, Inc. (formerly eChromics/Soladigm), no longer with the company
profile: Paul Nguyen co-founded electrochromic smart-glass maker eChromics with Mike Scobey in April 2007 in Santa Rosa, California; it became Soladigm and in 2012 View, Inc., whose dynamic glass tints to cut building heat and glare. Rao Mulpuri took over as CEO in 2008. View reached a $1B+ valuation, listed on Nasdaq via SPAC (2021) and went private again in 2024. No public record of Nguyen's current role was found.
interesting_fact: The company he co-founded makes 'dynamic' electrochromic windows that tint electronically to control sunlight and heat, an energy-efficiency play for buildings; it was valued above $1 billion in 2017.
notes: Common name — don't conflate with other Paul Nguyens. His exit from the company led to a 2010 lawsuit/arbitration (ruled in his favour in 2015); avoid the topic. View itself had financial trouble and went private in 2024. Current whereabouts unknown; very low profile.

name: Craig Ramsey
current_role: Co-founder and former chairman/board member of Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce in 2020); former Salesforce director (to 2014)
profile: Craig D. Ramsey is a veteran enterprise-software sales executive. He worked at Oracle (1986-94), nCUBE and Siebel Systems, where he became SVP Worldwide Operations in 1996, and sat on Salesforce's board until 2014. In 2014 he co-founded Vlocity, an industry-specific cloud CRM built on Salesforce, which Salesforce bought for about $1.33B in 2020.
interesting_fact: He was part of the Oracle-to-Siebel-to-Salesforce sales lineage that built the enterprise CRM industry. He sat on Salesforce's board in its early public years, then co-founded Vlocity, which Salesforce later acquired.
deep_cut_fact: Siebel's 1996 IPO filing shows he joined from parallel-computing pioneer nCUBE, where he was SVP of worldwide sales, marketing and support. Before that he spent eight years at Oracle, rising to VP of US Commercial Sales. He holds a BA in economics from Denison University.
notes: Low public profile, with no published contact or social accounts found. MarketScreener lists a Glide Foundation (San Francisco) directorship. He has been out of the news since the 2020 Vlocity sale; alive status not confirmed. Fit with the podcast theme is weak (cloud CRM, not infrastructure).

name: David Schmaier
current_role: President & Chief Strategy Officer, Salesforce (per Salesforce media bio, June 2025)
profile: Founding executive and EVP at Siebel Systems, then co-founder/CEO of Vlocity (industry cloud apps on Salesforce), sold to Salesforce for $1.33B in 2020. At Salesforce he ran Salesforce Industries, then was Chief Product Officer driving agentic AI, and now oversees strategy, M&A, Salesforce Ventures and philanthropy.
interesting_fact: Salesforce acquired Vlocity for about $1.33B in 2020 and immediately made Schmaier CEO of the new Salesforce Industries division.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a mechanical engineer (B.S., Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute) before his Harvard MBA, and today sits on the cabinet board of Harvard's Paulson School of Engineering and Applied Sciences and on Genstar Capital's strategic advisory board.
notes: Title has shifted several times (CEO Industries -> President & CPO -> President & Chief Strategy Officer); confirm current title before outreach. Also oversees Salesforce's Office of Ethical and Humane Use of technology.

name: James Ramsey
current_role: Co-founder & former board member, Vlocity (acquired by Salesforce 2020); LP at Stage 2 Capital; private investor
profile: James (Burr) Ramsey co-founded Vlocity in 2014 with Craig Ramsey, David Schmaier, Mark Armenante and Young Sohn to build industry-specific cloud CRM apps on Salesforce. Salesforce bought Vlocity in 2020 for about $1.33bn in cash. A long-time enterprise-software sales executive, he sat on SPS Commerce's board 2014-May 2025 and is now an LP with go-to-market VC Stage 2 Capital.
interesting_fact: Vlocity was built entirely on top of Salesforce's own platform, and Salesforce ended up acquiring it for ~$1.33bn in 2020, folding it into Salesforce Industries.
deep_cut_fact: Before Vlocity he was SVP of Worldwide Sales & Distribution at NetSuite, after starting out at Oracle, and he served about 11 years as an independent director of supply-chain software firm SPS Commerce, leaving in May 2025.

name: Young Sohn
current_role: Founding Managing Partner, Walden Catalyst Ventures; Chairman, HARMAN International; Chairman, Samsung Semiconductor Advisory Board
profile: Seoul-born, Maryland-raised Silicon Valley executive (Penn EE, MIT Sloan). Intel, Quantum, Agilent Semiconductor and Oak Technology, then took Inphi public in 2010 as CEO. As Samsung President/CSO (2012 on) he drove the $8B HARMAN deal and created the Samsung Catalyst Fund. He now invests in deep tech, AI and semis at Walden Catalyst (with Lip-Bu Tan).

He also co-founded the Extreme Tech Challenge, a startup competition tied to the UN SDGs.
notes: Identity is clear (well-known executive), but Hurun's label 'Vlocity founder' could not be verified. Vlocity's known founders are other people, so he may have been an early investor or board member; avoid calling him its founder. Strong fit for an AI/semis/data-center podcast and a frequent conference speaker (CES, Web Summit).

name: David A. Steinberg
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & CEO, Zeta Global (NYSE: ZETA)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who spent ~17 years in wireless (Sterling Cellular, then InPhonic) before co-founding XL Marketing - now Zeta Global - with former Apple CEO John Sculley in 2007. Zeta, an AI/data-driven marketing cloud, listed on the NYSE in 2021; he now pushes its 'Athena' AI agent, including a partnership with OpenAI.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Zeta Global (originally XL Marketing) with former Apple CEO John Sculley shortly after leaving InPhonic.
deep_cut_fact: His first real company, at 16 or 17, was a nightclub production business in New York City and the Hamptons; after college (1990) Goldman and Morgan Stanley turned him down, so he worked on telecom issues on Capitol Hill before entering wireless.
notes: Very media-friendly; does many podcasts/interviews (Adam Mendler, ICE House, Alejandro Cremades). Best route: press@zetaglobal.com. Zeta's valuation is now well above the $1B in the source field.

name: Wang Xiaogang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director, CTO and EVP, SenseTime (HKEX: 0020); Chairman, ACE Robotics (since Dec 2025)
profile: Computer-vision scientist who co-founded SenseTime in 2014 from Tang Xiaoou's CUHK lab, whose DeepID face recognition beat human accuracy. SenseTime became one of China's largest AI firms and runs big AI compute (SenseCore). Since Dec 2025 he has also chaired ACE Robotics, a SenseTime embodied-AI spinout behind the open 'Kairos' world model.

deep_cut_fact: He studied in USTC's famous 'Special Class for the Gifted Young' (BEng 2001), took an MPhil at CUHK under Tang Xiaoou, and on Tang's recommendation did his PhD at MIT (2009). He returned that year to teach electronic engineering at CUHK.

He speaks often to media (Yicai, CnTechPost); in 2026 he predicted robotics' 'ChatGPT moment' is about two years away. SenseTime is on the US Entity List.

name: Tang Wenbin

profile: Zhejiang-born member of Tsinghua's elite Yao Class who co-founded Beijing computer-vision company Megvii (Face++) in 2011 with classmates Yin Qi and Yang Mu, serving as CTO through ~14 years of the 'AI 1.0' wave. In March 2025 he launched Yuanli Lingji, focused on embodied intelligence, deliberately keeping its scope narrow.

name: Yang Mu
current_role: Co-founder and executive director, Megvii Technology (旷视科技, Beijing); earlier titled co-founder and senior vice president
profile: Yang Mu (杨沐) is one of Megvii's three co-founders, with Yin Qi and Tang Wenbin, all classmates in Tsinghua University's elite 'Yao Class' computer-science programme (2006 intake). They founded Megvii in 2011, building the Face++ computer-vision platform into one of China's 'AI four little dragons'. He remains on the company's board.

deep_cut_fact: Yang, Yin Qi and Tang Wenbin were all in the Yao Class's 2006 cohort. They started Megvii in 2011, the same year Yin Qi left for a PhD at Columbia University in New York.

Executive-director title comes from a 10jqka company profile (https://basic.10jqka.com.cn/A04701/company.html) and the date is unverified. Chinese-language outreach recommended.

CloudWalk, set up in 2015, grew into one of China's 'AI four dragons' in face recognition and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2022. He is not a director or senior officer in its 2025 annual report.

Very low public profile (no interviews found; search hits for 温浩 are mostly an unrelated artist). Route via CloudWalk IR.

name: Yao Zhiqiang
current_role: Co-founder and head of strategic planning, CloudWalk Technology (SSE STAR: 688327) (role as of 2022 interviews)
profile: Yao Zhiqiang co-founded CloudWalk in 2015 with Zhou Xi, spinning the team out of a Chinese Academy of Sciences lab in Chongqing; it became one of China's 'AI Four Dragons' in computer vision (face recognition for banks, airports, cities). CloudWalk listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in May 2022; Yao champions its 'human-machine collaboration' operating system strategy.
interesting_fact: Yao describes the ideal AI system as like Iron Man's J.A.R.V.I.S.: it lays out options, but the human makes the final call - the thinking behind CloudWalk's human-machine collaboration OS (CWOS).
deep_cut_fact: Early on, the team camped at a bank client in Guangzhou for 1-2 weeks and proudly submitted a few-dozen-page PPT bid - only to be told vendors normally submitted at least 300 pages. He earned bachelor's, master's and PhD at USTC, where he was Zhou Xi's senior.

name: Huang Chang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chief Technology Officer, Horizon Robotics (地平线, 9660.HK)
profile: Dr. Huang Chang (黄畅, Chang Huang) co-founded Beijing-based Horizon Robotics with Kai Yu in July 2015 after both worked at Baidu's deep-learning effort. As CTO he leads R&D on Horizon's 'Journey' automotive AI chips and its BPU architecture; Horizon listed in Hong Kong in October 2024 and supplies assisted-driving chips/software to most major Chinese automakers.
interesting_fact: Horizon's founding team came out of NEC Labs America and Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning; the company's investors include SAIC, FAW, VW's CARIAD, BYD, Dongfeng and CATL.
deep_cut_fact: He took all three degrees in computer science at Tsinghua (BS 2003, MS 2005, PhD 2007), did a postdoc in the US, was a research staff member at NEC Laboratories America (2010-12) and principal architect at Baidu before co-founding Horizon; there he led in-house research on its BPU chip architecture.
notes: Horizon is now a listed company (~$9bn unicorn valuation is outdated). Huang is technical and less media-facing than CEO Kai Yu; English-language international PR team exists. horizon.auto was unreachable from our network, contacts taken from search-indexed company pages.

name: Yang Ming
current_role: Reportedly Head of Multi-Modality Cognition, Ant Group (since 2023, per an unverified profile); co-founder and former VP of Software, Horizon Robotics
profile: Computer-vision researcher (Tsinghua; PhD Northwestern), ex-NEC Labs and a founding member of Facebook AI Research, who co-founded Horizon Robotics with Kai Yu and Chang Huang in 2015 and was VP of software until ~2019. Profiles then place him at xForwardAI and, since 2023, Ant Group.
interesting_fact: He was a founding member of Facebook AI Research (FAIR) before leaving Silicon Valley to co-found Horizon Robotics, now one of China's leading makers of AI chips for driver-assistance systems.
deep_cut_fact: He is the second author of Facebook's landmark 2014 'DeepFace' paper (with Taigman, Ranzato and Wolf), which hit 97.35% accuracy on the Labeled Faces in the Wild benchmark - closely approaching human-level face verification.
notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because the Hurun record is name-only; Ming Yang is the Horizon co-founder per MarketScreener/Crunchbase, so the match is likely. Current role is from aggregator profiles (alphaXiv/Village), not confirmed by Ant Group. No published contact; he appears to have left Horizon.

name: Tao Feiwen
current_role: Co-founder, Horizon Robotics (HKEX: 9660); former COO and executive director (left the board Aug 27, 2025)
profile: Feiwen 'Annie' Tao (陶斐雯) co-founded Horizon Robotics in 2015 with ex-Baidu colleagues Yu Kai and Huang Chang. The company makes AI chips and driver-assistance software for Chinese automakers and listed in Hong Kong in Oct 2024. As COO and executive director she ran operations; she held ~7% of the company as of 2024 and stepped off the board in Aug 2025.
interesting_fact: Horizon's Journey chips and software power driver-assistance in many Chinese EVs, making it one of China's most valuable AI-chip companies after its 2024 Hong Kong IPO.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Horizon she spent nearly four years at Baidu, after an undergraduate degree from Nanjing University (2007) and a graduate degree from Northwestern University (2008).
notes: Resigned as executive director effective 27 Aug 2025 (HKEX announcement 2025082701309); it gave a personal reason, which should not be raised. Unclear whether she keeps an operating role. Low-profile; route via Horizon IR/PR. The Baidu tenure is from TheOrg/MarketScreener, a secondary source.

name: Feng Shicong
current_role: Founder and CEO, Bailian Intelligence (百炼智能, AI-driven B2B marketing/lead generation); co-founder and former President/CTO of Mininglamp (明略)
profile: Feng Shicong (冯是聪) earned a Peking University computer science PhD (2003) under Prof. Li Xiaoming, worked at Lucent and HP Labs China, then joined Wu Minghui's AdMaster/Miaozhen as tech director and VP and co-founded Mininglamp Data as CTO. In 2018 he left to found Bailian Intelligence, which raised a 100M+ RMB Pre-B in 2022; Mininglamp listed in Hong Kong in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: He was a core developer of 'Peking University Tianwang', one of China's first general web search engines; teammates from that project went on to co-found Baidu with Robin Li, while he chose Lucent instead, which he called 'following the crowd'.
deep_cut_fact: Before leaving HP Labs China he did a formal SWOT analysis to decide whether to start a company; he introduced his PKU junior Yao Conglei to HP Labs, and Yao later became Bailian's CTO. He holds 50+ patents and studied at Hundun and Cheung Kong business schools to go from CTO to CEO.
notes: Hurun lists him as a Mininglamp unicorn founder, but his current company is Bailian Intelligence; in May 2026 he spoke publicly about AI shifting B2B SaaS from 'selling tools' to 'selling results' (https://cj.sina.com.cn/articles/view/2311077472/89c03e6002002khka). No published contact found; route via Bailian Intelligence.

name: Kunle Olukotun
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technologist, SambaNova Systems; Cadence Design Systems Professor of EE and CS, Stanford University
profile: London-born Nigerian computer architect known as the 'father of the multi-core processor' for Stanford's Hydra chip-multiprocessor project. His startup Afara Websystems (2000) was bought by Sun in 2002 and became the Niagara/UltraSPARC T1 line. In 2017 he co-founded AI-chip company SambaNova (dataflow RDU chips for inference), which raised $1B at an $11B valuation in July 2026.

current_role: Investor/advisor, Lightweight Ventures (former co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Dutchie)
profile: Serial entrepreneur who co-founded Dutchie in 2017 with his younger brother Ross; as chief product officer he helped build it into the leading cannabis e-commerce/point-of-sale platform (valued ~$3.75B in 2021). The brothers left Dutchie in early 2023; he has since invested in and advised early-stage startups.
interesting_fact: Dutchie started in Bend, Oregon; within two years it served 450 dispensaries in 18 states and was pitched as 'a Shopify of the cannabis space maybe meets DoorDash'. Ross described Zach as the methodical one: 'Zach is the one who wants to make sure that we're doing everything right.'
notes: No longer at Dutchie (left Feb 2023; the founders later filed suit against company leadership, so avoid framing outreach around Dutchie's current management). Low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route. Appeared on the 'To Be Blunt' cannabis podcast (ep. 020).

name: Felix Ohswald
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, GoStudent (Vienna)
profile: Austrian mathematician-turned-founder who co-founded GoStudent with Gregor Müller in 2016, building a one-to-one online tutoring platform that became Europe's first edtech unicorn (valued ~$3.5B in 2022). After a post-boom restructuring, GoStudent reported full-year operational profitability in 2025.
interesting_fact: Studied maths in Vienna and at Cambridge (BA Hons 2014), then a master's in quantitative finance at ETH Zurich, before quitting a finance path to start GoStudent.
deep_cut_fact: GoStudent began in 2015 when Ohswald, then 20 and at ETH Zurich, ran an online group answering schoolchildren's homework questions after helping his younger brother's friends with their schoolwork.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (ASU+GSV, 4GameChangers). Best route is the GoStudent press team.

name: Ferdinand von Hagen
profile: Listed by Hurun as a GoStudent founder, but public sources name Felix Ohswald and Gregor Müller as GoStudent's founders (Vienna, 2016). A CB Insights entry lists a Ferdinand von Hagen as former CTO of Studienkreis (a German tutoring firm acquired by GoStudent), with GoStudent, Deloitte, ETH Zurich and Airbus in his work history.
notes: Founder attribution looks wrong: he appears to be a tech executive (ex-CTO at Studienkreis, a GoStudent group company), not a co-founder. His current role isn't confirmed. Source: https://www.cbinsights.com/company/studienkreis/people. For GoStudent, the founders are Felix Ohswald (CEO) and Gregor Müller.

name: Gregor Muller
current_role: Co-founder & COO, GoStudent (Vienna)
profile: Austrian entrepreneur who co-founded online/hybrid tutoring platform GoStudent in Vienna in 2016 with CEO Felix Ohswald. GoStudent has raised over EUR 675m (Prosus, SoftBank Vision Fund 2, Left Lane) at a peak valuation around EUR 3bn, and has expanded via acquisitions (Seneca Learning, Tus Media, Studienkreis, Berlitz Germany sites).
interesting_fact: GoStudent Group reported its first full year of operational profitability in 2025, after a period of rapid post-pandemic expansion and restructuring.
deep_cut_fact: Before it was a platform, GoStudent began in 2016 as a WhatsApp chat through which pupils could go over their homework with tutors.
notes: Common name: a different Gregor Mueller (health economist, Thieme RECOM) exists - don't confuse. Lower public profile than CEO Felix Ohswald; GoStudent press office is best route.

name: Cliff Click
current_role: CTO, CRATUS Technology (lidar machine perception / industrial IoT automation), since Feb 2019; co-founder of H2O.ai
profile: Compiler engineer Cliff Click (Texas A&M BS/MS, Rice PhD 1995) was primary architect of Sun's HotSpot JVM server compiler (C2), co-founded Azul Systems (2002), and co-founded H2O.ai (2012), designing its distributed in-memory math engine. He later was CTO of fintech Neurensic and since 2019 CTO of CRATUS; he also hosts the open 'Coffee Compiler Club'.
interesting_fact: His Rice PhD work produced the 'sea of nodes' intermediate representation, which became the basis of HotSpot's C2 JIT - code that still optimizes much of the world's Java.
deep_cut_fact: He describes himself as having been 'writing compilers since age 15', holds 20+ patents, and runs a weekly 'Coffee Compiler Club' video call open to anyone interested in language design.
notes: Hacker/engineer personality, approachable in the compiler/PL community; technical deep-dives (JIT, GC, sea of nodes, ML infra) would land well. Coffee Compiler Club recordings are on YouTube (link via https://lists.puremagic.com/pipermail/digitalmars-d-announce/2021-December/058199.html).

name: Sri Satish Ambati
current_role: Founder and CEO, H2O.ai (Mountain View, CA)
profile: Sri Ambati co-founded H2O.ai in 2012 (originally 0xdata, with Java veteran Cliff Click) to build the open-source H2O ML platform, later adding Driverless AI and enterprise GenAI/agent products. He earlier co-founded Platfora and led engineering at DataStax. In 2026 H2O launched the tabH2O tabular foundation model and expanded an AI lab in Singapore.
interesting_fact: H2O.ai's open-source ML platform is used by tens of thousands of organizations; in July 2026 its 'H2O AI Super Agent' ranked #2 on the FutureX overall leaderboard.
deep_cut_fact: Before H2O he was a partner and performance engineer at Java multi-core startup Azul Systems, built a NoSQL trie-based index for semi-structured data at in-memory startup RightOrder, pursued theoretical neuroscience at Berkeley, and worked on scaling R over big data with Purdue and Stanford researchers.
notes: Very accessible, prolific speaker and poster (handle @srisatish). Press contact is the named contact in H2O's site metadata. Company is private; 'unicorn' valuation dates from 2021 funding.

name: Rishi Singh
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Harness; founder & CEO, SapientAI / BaseRock.ai (AI software testing)
profile: IIT Delhi-trained engineer who spent five years at Apple leading its deployment-automation platform, then co-founded Harness (AI software delivery platform) with Jyoti Bansal and served as CTO until 2021. He remains on Harness's board and now runs an AI test-generation startup (SapientAI, launched May 2023 with $5M seed from 8VC; BaseRock.ai).
interesting_fact: SapientAI emerged from stealth in May 2023 with a $5M seed led by 8VC to build an 'AI Test Coder' that writes unit tests automatically.
deep_cut_fact: Before Harness he spent five years at Apple leading development of its internal deployment automation platform, and says he learned from Steve Jobs the importance of constantly talking about what you believe in.
notes: Not the founder-CEO of Harness (that is Jyoti Bansal); he is the technical co-founder. Best route likely via his current AI-testing startup.

name: Andy Katz-Mayfield
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Mammoth Brands (formerly Harry's Inc.; owns Harry's, Flamingo, Lume, Mando)
profile: Duke and Stanford GSB (MBA 2011) alum who worked at Bain & Company and Charlesbank Capital before co-founding Harry's with Jeff Raider in 2012. Harry's grew into a ~$750M-revenue DTC/retail razor business; in April 2025 the parent was renamed Mammoth Brands, which he still co-leads with Raider.
interesting_fact: In January 2014, barely a year after launch, Harry's bought the century-old German blade maker Feintechnik (Eisfeld, founded 1920) for $100M so it could control manufacturing; in 2019 Edgewell agreed to buy Harry's for $1.4B before the FTC sued to block it.
deep_cut_fact: His first paying job was as a banquet waiter at a country club, which taught him that great service 'isn't that hard'; he has every Harry's employee spend a day each quarter working in customer experience, and says he wants to build a brand that lasts 100 years.
notes: Co-CEO with Jeff Raider (also Warby Parker co-founder). Best route is Mammoth Brands press email. LinkedIn listed is the company page, not his personal profile.

name: Israel David
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, HiBob (Tel Aviv / New York / London)
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded HiBob with CEO Ronni Zehavi in 2015; HiBob makes 'Bob', a cloud HR/people platform for mid-sized companies, and has been valued at about $2.7B+ (Hurun lists $3B). Before HiBob he held senior technology roles at companies including Kenshoo and VMware (per third-party profiles). He continues to lead HiBob's technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: HiBob was founded in 2015 by Ronni Zehavi and Israel David on the idea that 'the employee experience and role of HR needed to evolve'; it opened its first US HQ in New York in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining as co-founder, David was Ronni Zehavi's neighbor in Silicon Valley; Bessemer's account of HiBob's rise notes Zehavi brought on 'his former Silicon Valley neighbor, Israel David.'
notes: Low public profile compared with CEO Ronni Zehavi, who does most media. Earlier career details (Kenshoo, VMware, 48Upper) come from third-party profiles; verify before citing. HiBob's US PR has been handled by 5W Public Relations (5wpr.com/practice/hibob.cfm) but no verified press email was found.

name: Ronni Zehavi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, HiBob (HR software, London/Tel Aviv/New York)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur who co-founded HiBob in Tel Aviv in 2015, maker of the 'Bob' cloud HR/HCM platform for mid-sized, distributed companies. HiBob has raised several $150M rounds (valued ~$2.7B in 2023) and has added payroll (Pento, 2024) and FP&A (Mosaic, 2025) via acquisitions. He remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Before HiBob he co-founded content-delivery startup Cotendo in January 2008 (backed by Sequoia and Benchmark), which Akamai bought in March 2012 for over $300M - he calls HiBob his third company.
deep_cut_fact: Cotendo was founded by three former Commtouch (later Cyren) colleagues - Zehavi, Udi Trugman and David Drai - with R&D in Netanya, Israel and HQ in Sunnyvale; it set out to challenge Akamai and ended up being acquired by it.
notes: No published press email found on hibob.com; press page and general Contact Us form are the official routes. Frequent podcast guest on HR/future-of-work topics (Josh Bersin, Digital HR Leaders, DealMakers).

name: Arseniy Vershinin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Architect (formerly CTO), Personio
profile: Russian-born software engineer who co-founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 with Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher and Ignaz Forstmeier, serving as CTO as it grew into Europe's leading SMB HR platform (valued up to $8.5B). In a 2024 leadership change he moved from CTO to Chief Architect, leading technology projects.
interesting_fact: He met his three Personio co-founders in 2014 at Munich's Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), a one-year startup program for TUM/LMU students.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Ulan-Ude and raised in the small Siberian town of Ust-Ilimsk, he spent a year in the US as a teen on the FLEX exchange program, then studied at MIPT ('Phystech') and did iOS development for Moscow startups before moving to Munich for 'an international atmosphere'.
notes: Low public profile; listed as a Founders Pledge member (https://www.founderspledge.com/members/2681). Best route is Personio press office. Could not directly re-verify the press email in the PDF (download blocked); also seen as press@personio.de on older releases.

name: Hanno Renner
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Personio (Munich)
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded HR-software company Personio in Munich in 2015 with fellow CDTM classmates. Personio grew into one of Europe's most valuable startups (valued ~$8B in 2022), serving SMEs with HR and payroll software; Renner continues to lead it as CEO.
interesting_fact: Personio started with about $200 in the bank and reached a $6.3B valuation within six years, making Renner one of Europe's youngest unicorn CEOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Personio he trained as a sailing skipper and spent semester breaks taking tourists out on sailing boats; he studied industrial engineering at HTWG Konstanz and Management & Technology at TUM.
notes: Press releases also list press@personio.de; best route is Personio's comms team.

name: Ignaz Forstmeier
current_role: Co-founder and former CMO, Personio; now with 3VC (Vienna software VC) and an angel investor
profile: One of four TU Munich/CDTM alumni who founded Munich HR-software company Personio in 2015 (with Hanno Renner, Roman Schumacher and Arseniy Vershinin); he served as CMO as it grew to an $8B valuation. Having left Personio's operations, he is based in Vienna, works with Series A fund 3VC and has angel-invested in 25+ startups.
interesting_fact: Personio grew out of the Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM) programme in Munich, which all four founders attended; Forstmeier was there 2013-2015.
deep_cut_fact: In Personio's early days, while hunting for their EUR 2.1M seed round, the founders went unpaid for a while; Forstmeier said fundraising is usually a full-time job for at least one founder. In 2016 customers grew from ~20 to 100+ purely through referrals, with no marketing budget.
notes: No longer operational at Personio; LinkedIn shows current affiliation with 3VC, Vienna. Low public profile.

name: Roman Schumacher
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Personio (former Chief Product Officer; moved to a strategic role in late 2022)
profile: Co-founded Munich HR-software firm Personio in 2015 with Hanno Renner and others and led product as CPO for about seven years. Personio grew into one of Europe's top SaaS startups (valued at about $8.5B). In Nov 2022 he handed product to ex-Meta exec Maria Angelidou-Smith, taking a strategic role and staying on the board.
interesting_fact: Personio grew out of the founders' time at Munich's Center for Digital Technology and Management (CDTM), where Schumacher met CEO Hanno Renner.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of his studies to build Personio and had no prior work experience. On handing over product leadership as the company scaled, he told t3n: 'Die Zügel aus der Hand zu geben, war schon hart für mich' ('Handing over the reins was really hard for me').
notes: Low public profile since leaving the CPO role (Nov 2022, per Munich Startup). Reach him through Personio press. One unverified profile says he later started a venture called Studio Sonntag; not confirmed.

name: Anastasia Zamyshlyaeva
current_role: VP Engineering, GitKraken (per 2025/26 speaker bio); co-founder and former Chief Architect of Reltio
profile: Russian-born software architect who co-founded master-data-management company Reltio with CEO Manish Sood in 2011, serving as technical co-founder, Chief Architect and VP Platform Product Management. She has since held engineering leadership roles at Redpanda Data and is now VP Engineering at developer-tools company GitKraken.
interesting_fact: Won the 2018 Aragon Research Women in Technology Award (CIO category) as Reltio's Chief Architect.
deep_cut_fact: Before Reltio she designed core components of the Informatica MDM tool; she holds an MS in CS from Chelyabinsk State University (research in distributed graph computing), and Reltio's earliest brainstorms took place in Mountain View coffee shops.
notes: Appears to have left Reltio; current role at GitKraken per SF Engineering Leadership Community speaker page (https://sfelc.com/speaker/anastasia-zamyshlyaeva-2). Low public profile; no published contacts found. Best route likely via conference speaking circuits (LeadDev/SFELC).

name: Manish Sood
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Reltio (sources differ; has also been listed as CTO & Chairman 2020-2022)
profile: Indian-born engineer who founded Reltio in 2011 (with Anastasia Zamyshlyaeva) after leading MDM product strategy at Siperian and Informatica. Reltio sells a cloud master-data-management / 'data unification' platform, valued around $1.7-2B, and now pitches it as the data foundation for enterprise AI.
interesting_fact: Before enterprise software, Sood was educated as a mechanical engineer (Andhra University, graduated 1995) in India.
deep_cut_fact: He told interviewer Adam Mendler that he began his career working on the automation of large-scale power plants, a natural hook for an energy/data-center podcast.

public_contacts.value: reltio@allisonpr.com (Allison + Partners, media and analyst inquiries)

notes: Press contacts per Reltio press releases (Kevin Keenan, VP Communications, listed in 2026 release); verify current contact on latest release. Frequent podcast guest (Modern CTO, DataVersity).

name: Drew Durbin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Wave Mobile Money (Dakar, Senegal)
profile: American entrepreneur who co-founded remittance app Sendwave (YC, sold to WorldRemit for ~$500M in 2020) and then Wave, a low-fee mobile money network that launched in Senegal and became Francophone Africa's first unicorn after a $200M Series A in 2021. He continues to run Wave as it expands across West Africa.
interesting_fact: Wave's flat 1% transfer fee undercut incumbents by roughly 70%, forcing Orange Money and others to slash their prices; Wave reached about 70% of Senegal's mobile-money users.
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Sendwave came from his own frustration with fees and unreliable transfers when sending money to an NGO he ran in Tanzania; he and co-founder Lincoln Quirk met as freshman hallmates at Brown University.
notes: Low public profile; no published press email found on wave.com. Best route is via Wave corporate channels.

name: Lincoln Quirk
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Product, Wave Mobile Money
profile: Co-founded Sendwave (low-fee US/UK-to-Africa remittances, sold to WorldRemit in 2020) and then Wave, a mobile money company that has grown into one of francophone West Africa's largest fintechs, starting in Senegal and valued around $1.7-2B.
