He met CEO Drew Durbin as a freshman hallmate at Brown and still leads product at Wave.
interesting_fact: Says he and his co-founders build Wave 'primarily for EA reasons'; he attended his first effective altruism gathering in 2013 (about 50 people in an Oakland house) and says he has had more impact through direct work at Wave than through donations.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2020 EA Forum AMA with CTO Ben Kuhn he said he personally wrote much of the original code for both Sendwave and Wave; Sendwave's pitch was sending money by phone number at a 3% fee vs the typical 8-12%.
notes: Low-profile; active in effective altruism circles (EA Forum). Best route likely via Wave or EA community. No published personal email found.

name: Peng Yi
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of YBM (药帮忙 / Xiaoyaoyao, Wuhan-based B2B pharmaceutical e-commerce platform connecting drugmakers with pharmacies and clinics; valued ~$2B). Could not confirm in public sources that Peng Yi is a founder; business registration lists Li Meng as legal representative of Wuhan Xiaoyaoyao.
notes: Identity unverified; English and Chinese searches did not link Peng Yi to YBM/Xiaoyaoyao. Verify via company registry (shareholders) or Hurun list before outreach.

name: Huang Tingting
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of YBM (Yaobangmang/药帮忙), the B2B pharmaceutical procurement platform run by Wuhan Xiaoyaoyao Pharmaceutical Technology (founded Dec 2015). Public sources found name Peng Yi (彭裔) as founder and Li Meng (李萌) as founder/CEO; no source tying a Huang Tingting to the company was found.
notes: Could not confirm identity. Searches for 'Huang Tingting' mostly return an unrelated SNH48 idol singer. Company sources: https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1679729594749704 and https://finance.ifeng.com/c/87KuE7F91Ne. Verify via Hurun or company registry before outreach.

name: JC Glancy
current_role: Co-founder, ZenBusiness; Venture Partner, Fluent Ventures
profile: JC (James) Glancy co-founded ZenBusiness, the Austin-based all-in-one platform that helps small businesses form, run and grow (LLC formation, compliance, banking, accounting), valued around $1.7B in 2021. He brought in HomeAway founding CTO Ross Buhrdorf as investor and later CEO. He is now a venture partner at Fluent Ventures and an angel/advisor.
interesting_fact: ZenBusiness took roughly a 10-year journey to become an 'overnight success'; Glancy says his drive came from wanting to make life easier for small-business owners like his father.
deep_cut_fact: Glancy deliberately hired his own boss, bringing in Ross Buhrdorf as CEO, summing up the trade-off as: "You can either be rich or be king." He also noted ZenBusiness customers who use its banking churn at half the rate of those who don't.
notes: Low public profile; Ross Buhrdorf is ZenBusiness's public face. Fluent Ventures (Alex Lazarow) is a warm route - Glancy is a venture partner there.

name: Rafael Lopez
current_role: Listed as a ZenBusiness founder/'Product Director' on an insider-data aggregator; not named on ZenBusiness's current leadership page
profile: Rafael Lopez is named as one of several ZenBusiness co-founders (alongside Ross Buhrdorf, Shanaz Hemmati, JC Glancy and Art Flores) in a secondary source and as a founder/Product Director on MarketScreener. ZenBusiness, an Austin-based small-business formation and compliance platform founded in 2015, was valued around $1.7B. No independent biography was found.
interesting_fact: ZenBusiness is a public benefit corporation (ZenBusiness PBC) in Austin that helps small-business owners form LLCs, stay compliant and manage finances; a 2025 CNBC piece described it as a $1.7 billion startup.
notes: Very low public profile; company's official founder list (website, Wikipedia) names only Buhrdorf and Hemmati. 'Rafael Lopez' is a common name - verify identity (e.g. via the Forbes listing) before outreach. Best route is via ZenBusiness press.

name: Ross Buhrdorf
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, ZenBusiness (Austin, Texas)
profile: Nebraska-born technologist who was founding CTO of HomeAway (vacation rentals), acquired by Expedia for $3.9B in 2015. That year he co-founded ZenBusiness with Shanaz Hemmati, a public-benefit SaaS platform for business formation and compliance that has served 1M+ entrepreneurs and reached a ~$1.7-2B valuation.
interesting_fact: He met his ZenBusiness co-founder Shanaz Hemmati when both worked at Excite.com, one of the internet's earliest web portals; EY named him Entrepreneur of the Year (Gulf South) in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: His personal motto, published on ZenBusiness's site: "Fear is a liar that holds us back... Don't let fear dictate your actions - go for it."
notes: Best route is ZenBusiness press team. Company is a PBC; Hemmati is also co-founder.

name: Ryan Pitylak
current_role: Executive Vice President of Growth, NinjaTrader (since May 2024); co-founder of ZenBusiness
profile: Austin-based marketer and entrepreneur (b. 1982) who co-founded ZenBusiness in 2015, a public-benefit corporation helping micro-businesses form and run companies, and served as its CMO; ZenBusiness reached a ~$1.7B valuation. In May 2024 he joined futures-trading platform NinjaTrader as EVP of Growth.
interesting_fact: Before ZenBusiness he co-founded and ran Unique Influence, a digital marketing firm acquired in 2015 by MDC Partners' media agency network Assembly.
deep_cut_fact: He earned undergraduate degrees in both economics and philosophy at the University of Texas.

public_contacts.value: https://ninjatrader.com/contact-us/ (has a Media & Communication Inquiries section)

notes: Wikipedia notes a 2004-06 spam-email history settled with Texas and Microsoft; avoid that topic. Now at NinjaTrader, so the ZenBusiness angle is past tense.

name: Shanaz Hemmati
current_role: Co-Founder & Executive Advisor, ZenBusiness (formerly COO)
profile: Iranian-born, UT Austin-trained engineer who co-founded Austin-based ZenBusiness with Ross Buhrdorf (2015 per company); the small-business formation/AI platform has helped 700,000+ entrepreneurs and was valued at ~$1.7B after a $205M Series C. Long-time COO, she is now Co-Founder & Executive Advisor; earlier led tech at Excite.com and HomeAway.
interesting_fact: She left Iran as a child to study in the U.S.; at ZenBusiness she led a DEI strategy reaching nearly 50% female representation across staff and management, and was named to Inc.'s 2025 Female Founders list.
deep_cut_fact: She was inducted as a 2026 Distinguished Alumna of UT Austin's Electrical & Computer Engineering department; she met co-founder Ross Buhrdorf years earlier when both worked at Excite.com.
notes: Founding year given as 2015 (company) vs 2017 (Entrepreneur). She is a Capital Factory mentor in Austin; also appeared on Startergirlz podcast. Route via ZenBusiness press.

name: Charles Gorintin
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Alan (Paris health insurer); co-founding advisor, Mistral AI
profile: French engineer who co-founded Alan in 2016 with Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve, building a digital health-insurance 'super-app' for companies in France, Spain and Belgium; Alan has raised over €500m and is valued in the billions. Before Alan he led data-science work at Facebook, Instagram and Twitter. Since 2023 he has also been a co-founding advisor to Mistral AI.
interesting_fact: Alan was the first new health insurance company licensed in France since 1986.
deep_cut_fact: At Facebook, Instagram and Twitter he worked on fighting fake accounts, growth and social psychology; he holds three master's degrees (Ponts ParisTech, ML at ENS Paris-Saclay, Financial Engineering at Berkeley Haas). He co-writes the French Substack 'Intelligence Humaine' on AI for HR.
notes: French-American Foundation Young Leader 2022. Mistral AI link is a strong angle for an AI/data-center podcast.

name: Jean Charles Samuelian
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Alan (French digital health insurer)
profile: Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve co-founded Paris-based health insurer Alan in 2016 and has led it since. Alan sells digital-first health insurance and prevention services in France, Belgium, Spain and Canada; a €480M Series G valued it at about €5.5B. He is also an early backer and board member of Mistral AI.
interesting_fact: Alan's 2026 Series G raised €480M (~$550M) at a ~€5.5B valuation to expand into Canada's group-benefits market; the company reported >€800M ARR and >1.1M members.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alan he co-founded Expliseat, maker of the 'Titanium Seat' economy airline seat that cut seat weight by about two-thirds; it earned him the French Industry Medal and two Montgolfier prizes. He is also a Founders Pledge member.
notes: Also appears as Jean-Charles Samuelian-Werve. Alan press room is the best formal route; he speaks often at French tech events (VivaTech, Paris Fintech Forum).

name: Andreas Bittner
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder of Solaris (formerly solarisBank), Berlin; left the management board in February 2020 - current executive role not confirmed
profile: Co-founded Berlin banking-as-a-service platform solarisBank (now Solaris) in 2015 and, as COO and board member, built its operations. He left the board in Feb 2020. Solaris became a fintech unicorn before a 2025 rescue by Japan's SBI Holdings, whose takeover he and other ex-shareholders have challenged in a Berlin court.
interesting_fact: As founding COO he built solarisBank's banking and back-office processes from scratch - a fully licensed bank designed to be plugged into other companies' apps via APIs; by 2020 it had nearly 300 staff and had raised over EUR100m.
notes: Hurun tags him 'energy' but Solaris is a fintech (banking-as-a-service), not solar - weak fit for an energy/data-centre podcast. He is in active litigation against Solaris/SBI (2025), so Solaris's press office is not an appropriate route. An insider-data site links him to finCraft AG (unconfirmed). No published personal contact found.

name: Marko Wenthin
current_role: Co-founder of Solaris (formerly solarisBank, Berlin); current role unconfirmed (former CCO of solarisBank, CEO of Penta Fintech 2019-2021)
profile: German banker-turned-fintech founder who co-founded Berlin banking-as-a-service platform solarisBank (Solaris) with Andreas Bittner in 2015-16, serving as co-managing director/Chief Commercial Officer. He later ran Solaris-owned SME neobank Penta (2019-21). Solaris reached unicorn status (~$2B) before a 2025 SBI-led rescue round. His Hurun listing comes from that founder stake.
interesting_fact: Solaris pioneered 'banking-as-a-service' in Europe, giving fintechs and brands such as Vivid, Tomorrow and ADAC the regulated bank licence underneath their apps.
deep_cut_fact: Before solarisBank he founded GroupPlatina and created Sofort Bank, the banking sister of Sofortüberweisung, Germany's big online-payment brand. Earlier he was COO and board member of Deutsche Bank PBC in Poland and worked for Deutsche Bank in Argentina.
notes: Fintech, not energy; weak fit for the podcast's focus. Current activity unclear after Penta (2021). Solaris valuation collapsed and co-founder Bittner is litigating against SBI, so avoid. I found no verified personal site or social account; LinkedIn is the likely route but unverified.

name: Lori Stacy
current_role: Chair of the Board, Trader Interactive (retired as CEO Dec 2023)
profile: Lori Stacy is the long-time leader of Trader Interactive (Norfolk, VA), the marketplace business behind vertical listing sites such as RV Trader, Cycle Trader and Equipment Trader. She joined Auto Trader in 1997 as a sales manager, became CEO in 2017, steered the company through its 2021-22 sale to Australia's carsales.com, and retired as CEO in Dec 2023, staying on as board chair.
interesting_fact: carsales.com bought 49% of Trader Interactive in 2021 and agreed to buy the remaining 51% in 2022; carsales CEO Cameron McIntyre said 'Lori is a strong, capable leader who built a world-class business'.
deep_cut_fact: She started at Auto Trader in 1997 as a sales manager and rose through the ranks by building up the non-automotive brands (RVs, motorcycles, equipment) before taking the CEO job in 2017 -- a 25-year career at one company.
notes: Hurun lists her as 'founder' but she was a career executive/CEO, not a founder (Trader Interactive spun out of Dominion Enterprises). Company site blocks bots; no published press email found. Best route: Trader Interactive corporate communications.

name: Xu Hui
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and CEO, AInnovation Technology Group (创新奇智, HKEX: 2121)
profile: Xu Hui (徐辉), a former Microsoft Greater China vice president with earlier enterprise-software roles at SAP, co-founded AInnovation in April 2018 with Kai-Fu Lee's Sinovation Ventures (Lee is non-executive chairman). The company builds industrial AI and large-model applications, mainly for manufacturing; it listed in Hong Kong and in FY2025 grew revenue 23.8% to RMB 1.51bn, with manufacturing over 80%.
interesting_fact: Under his 'One Model, One Body, Two Wings' strategy AInnovation pivoted almost entirely to AI-for-manufacturing: manufacturing revenue reached RMB 1.22bn (80.9% of the total) in 2025 and he described operations as at a 'historically optimal level'.
notes: Strong fit for the AI/industrial angle. The published inbox is for business cooperation; IR contact via HKEX filings. Third-party profiles also mention IBM, Wanda Network and a Honma Golf INED seat, which could not be verified from primary sources here.

name: Gustavo Sapoznik
current_role: Founder of ASAPP (CEO 2014-2024, now reportedly founder/advisor); per Crunchbase, founder & CEO of Conquest Labs (Bozeman, MT) - unverified by primary source
profile: University of Chicago math graduate who founded New York-based ASAPP in 2014 to build AI that makes contact-center agents 'radically' more productive rather than replacing them; backers included John Doerr and John Chambers and it reached unicorn status. He stepped back as ASAPP CEO in 2024 (Katie Stein is now CEO) and has reportedly started a new venture, Conquest.
interesting_fact: ASAPP built its pitch on augmenting rather than replacing humans: 'If we can automate half of this thing away, we can get to the same place by making people twice as productive.' Its speech tech came from a team led by a founding member of Apple's Siri speech group.
deep_cut_fact: He is a licensed pilot with a fondness for classical music, and before ASAPP he first applied his coding skills to his family's real-estate and financial business in Miami, building machine-learning systems to trade markets - which he found unfulfilling.
notes: Facts source is a repost of Alan Ohnsman's 2020 Forbes AI 50 profile (original on forbes.com). Conquest Labs info only from aggregators (https://crunchbase.com/person/gustavo-sapoznik). ASAPP PR may not reach him now that he's not CEO; LinkedIn likely the best direct route (not verified).

name: Marcus Westin
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of ASAPP; later co-founder/CTO of Aldyn (closed 2022); current role unclear (profiles say he now builds software for writers)
profile: Marcus Westin is a software engineer who co-founded New York AI customer-experience company ASAPP with Gustavo Sapoznik in 2014 and served as its founding CTO; ASAPP was valued at about $2bn per Hurun. Earlier he was a senior engineer at Meebo (2008), a founding engineer at Clover (2011) and founder of Flutterby Labs (2012). He no longer appears on ASAPP's leadership roster.
interesting_fact: ASAPP, which he co-founded, builds AI systems for large enterprise contact centres and was one of New York's early AI unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote WebViewJavascriptBridge, a widely used open-source iOS/OSX library for passing messages between Objective-C and JavaScript in web views; its README lists Facebook Messenger and Facebook Paper among apps that used it.
notes: Engineer-founder, low media profile; his GitHub is the most reliable self-published presence (search results also indicate @marcuswestin on X, not verified here). Not involved in ASAPP's current management (CEO is Gustavo Sapoznik), so ASAPP press is not a good route.

name: Andy Byrne
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Clari (merged with Salesloft in Dec 2025; Steve Cox named CEO of combined company). Current post-merger role not publicly confirmed.
profile: Silicon Valley sales/product executive who co-founded revenue-forecasting SaaS company Clari in 2013 with Venkat Rangan and led it as CEO to a ~$3B valuation. Earlier founded Timestock and was on the founding exec team at Clearwell Systems (acquired by Symantec). Clari merged with Vista-backed Salesloft, a deal announced Aug 2025 and closed Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Clari and Salesloft announced a 'merger of equals' in August 2025 to create an AI revenue platform; Byrne was originally slated to lead the combined company.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up around Mountain View, where his father leased office space to tech startups; he says dinner-table stories about companies like Fairchild Semiconductor made him love 'the idea that you could create something from nothing.' He practices Qi Gong and has a family motto 'DPA' (Dream. Plan. Act.).
notes: Post-merger role unclear (Steve Cox became CEO at close per Business Wire). No published press email found on Salesloft/Clari newsrooms; best route likely LinkedIn or via Sequoia network. TechCrunch 2014 quoted him: Clari was his 'company number-four with Sequoia.'

name: Venkat Rangan
current_role: Co-founder and founding CTO, Clari (now merged with Salesloft; combined company operates under the Salesloft brand)
profile: Indian-born engineer (IIT Madras; MS computer science, University of Miami) who co-founded revenue-forecasting SaaS Clari with Andy Byrne in 2012-13 and served as CTO. Earlier co-founded e-discovery firm Clearwell Systems (acquired by Symantec in 2011). Clari merged with Salesloft in 2025; his current operating title post-merger was not confirmed.
interesting_fact: Before Clari he co-founded and was CTO of e-discovery company Clearwell Systems, which Symantec acquired in 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He first met his Clari co-founder Andy Byrne in the late 1990s at VitalSigns Software, a network-diagnostics startup where Rangan was an engineer and Byrne got his first product management job (1997).
notes: Low public profile; Clari now operates as Salesloft (Steve Cox CEO). Best route likely via LinkedIn or Salesloft/Clari press team. No personal published email found.

name: Jack Newton
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Clio (legal practice management / legal AI software, Vancouver)
profile: Canadian software entrepreneur who co-founded Clio in 2008 with Rian Gauvreau, pioneering cloud-based practice management for lawyers. In Nov 2025 Clio closed the US$1B acquisition of vLex (largest legal-tech M&A ever) alongside a US$500M Series G at a US$5B valuation; Newton is pushing Clio into AI-powered legal research and workflows.
interesting_fact: The vLex deal was described as the largest M&A transaction ever in legal technology, and was announced together with a US$500M Series G at a US$5B valuation.
deep_cut_fact: Before Clio, he was the first software developer at Chenomx, a University of Alberta spinoff building an NMR-based medical diagnostic tool, and took a sabbatical from it to do an MSc in machine learning under Russ Greiner; he started programming around age eight on an IBM 8086.
notes: Very public CEO; author of 'The Client-Centered Law Firm'; frequent conference keynoter (ClioCon). Press route via Clio media team.

name: Rian Gauvreau
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Clio; Founder & CEO, Aeon Health (Vancouver)
profile: Vancouver entrepreneur who co-founded legal-practice-management SaaS Clio with Jack Newton in 2008; served as COO until 2017, then chief people officer until stepping back in 2021, staying on the board. In 2023 he founded Aeon Health, an AI-focused health-tech company, aiming to do for health care what Clio did for law.
interesting_fact: Before Clio he worked as a legal technologist at a Vancouver law firm, where he and Newton concluded that existing practice software was clunky and expensive; Clio became the first-to-market cloud practice-management product.
deep_cut_fact: He and Clio co-founder Jack Newton are lifelong friends whose first joint 'venture' dates back to Grade 3. He also earned his UBC Sauder MBA ('11) while growing Clio, and in 2025 became the first Sauder grad to win UBC's Alumni Achievement Award for Entrepreneurship.
notes: Aeon Health site lists only support@/work@ inboxes; best route likely via Aeon Health or Clio comms. Departure dates from Clio ops differ by source (2019 vs 2021).

name: Fredrik Anfinsen
current_role: Co-founder & Senior Principal Architect, Cognite (Norway)
profile: Norwegian software engineer and co-founder of Cognite, the Oslo-founded (2016) industrial DataOps/AI company behind Cognite Data Fusion, backed by Aker and used by BP, Aramco and Aker BP. Previously founded and ran 3D file-sharing startup ShareMy3D. Still at Cognite in a senior technical (architect) role rather than an executive one.
interesting_fact: Cognite's platform contextualises raw industrial sensor/OT data for heavy-asset sectors (oil & gas, power, renewables); customers include BP, Aker BP, Saudi Aramco and Statnett.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cognite he co-founded ShareMy3D in Oslo (with Kaye Hope), a browser-based service pitched as making sharing 3D models (up to 5 GB) as easy as sharing a YouTube video.
notes: Low public profile; technical co-founder (not CEO). Founder attribution for Cognite is often given to John Markus Lervik et al.; Anfinsen listed as co-founder by Cognite job pages/MarketScreener. Best route: Cognite media relations.

name: Geir Engdahl
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, AI, Cognite (Oslo)
profile: Norwegian technologist who co-founded industrial-data/AI software company Cognite in 2016 with John Markus Lervik and others. Previously founded ML classifieds startup Snapsale (acquired by Schibsted in 2017) and was a senior software engineer at Google. Served as Cognite CTO, then Chief Product Officer (2024), and was named CTO, AI in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Before Cognite he founded Snapsale (2011), a machine-learning classifieds startup he ran as CEO/CTO until Schibsted acquired it in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He won a silver medal at the International Olympiad in Informatics, and holds a master's in computational science from the University of Oslo.
notes: Press contact is Cognite's VP Global PR (Michelle Holford) as listed in 2024 release; may have changed. Role update: https://itbrief.co.uk/story/cognite-appoints-ai-leaders-to-drive-innovation-push

name: John Markus Lervik
current_role: Founder, Cognite (Oslo industrial data/AI software); CEO until April 2022, then Chief Strategy & Development Officer
profile: Norwegian tech entrepreneur (b. 1969) with an NTNU PhD. He was CEO of Fast Search & Transfer until Microsoft bought it in 2008, founded ad/analytics firm Cxense in 2010, and in 2016 co-founded Cognite, the Aker-backed industrial DataOps company described as Norway's first unicorn. Girish Rishi took over as CEO in 2022; Cognite now lists Lervik as Founder.
interesting_fact: When he handed over the CEO role in 2022, Cognite's announcement credited him with building Cognite into 'Norway's first unicorn'.
deep_cut_fact: He was the first person hired at Fast Search & Transfer, and he won an Esso academic award for his NTNU PhD work in 1996. He is a fellow of the Norwegian Academy of Technological Sciences.

public_contacts.value: michelle.holford@cognite.com (Michelle Holford, Global PR Lead, Cognite)

notes: Strong fit for the energy/data angle: Cognite does industrial data for oil and gas and utilities. Avoid the 2014 FAST accounting conviction. Cognite now lists him only as 'Founder', so his day-to-day role may be smaller. The PR email was in the media-contact box on a Cognite newsroom page.

name: Stein Danielsen
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Solutions Officer, Cognite (per conference bio)
profile: Stein Hardy Danielsen co-founded Norwegian industrial data/AI software company Cognite in 2016 with John Markus Lervik and Geir Engdahl. Cognite's Cognite Data Fusion platform contextualizes industrial (oil & gas, energy, manufacturing) data; he has overseen applications and solutions built on it.
interesting_fact: Before Cognite he was Chief Architect at Cxense, and earlier CEO of Kopek; his background spans search, real-time systems, 3D graphics and large-scale data/transaction systems.
deep_cut_fact: He worked in product development at FAST (Fast Search & Transfer), the Norwegian enterprise-search company, and is also listed as a principal at Microsoft; he holds an MSc in Computer Science from NTNU.
notes: Low public profile; rarely interviewed. media@cognite.com seen in Dec 2025 Cognite HQ release (page blocked direct fetch; seen via search). Cognite is industrial/energy-data focused, a good podcast fit. Some sources spell his name 'Danielson'.

name: Joe Moss
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Extend (San Francisco)
profile: Joe Moss co-founded Extend, a San Francisco company that sells product-protection plans (extended warranties) and shipping protection through online merchants. CEO Woody Levin leads the company. Extend began selling in 2019 and raised a $260M Series C at a valuation of over $1.6B in May 2021. Moss leads product.
interesting_fact: Extend became a unicorn in about 27 months of operation. CEO Woody Levin pitched it as the 'Apple Care' for everything that isn't an Apple product.
notes: Low public profile. Moss's prior roles (reportedly DocuSign product and an earlier startup) appear only on aggregator sites and could not be verified, so they are left out. No published press email was found on extend.com. The best route is the company contact form, or via CEO Woody Levin.

name: Michael Darmousseh
current_role: Co-founder, Extend (product-protection/warranty platform, San Francisco); listed variously as SVP Engineering / CTO
profile: Co-founder of Extend, the San Francisco post-purchase platform offering product protection, shipping protection and returns for merchants. He started the company in February 2019 with Woodrow Levin, Joe Moss and Rohan Shah; Extend raised a $260M SoftBank-led round in 2021 at a valuation of over $1B.
interesting_fact: Extend was co-founded in February 2019 and within ten months of its Series A closed a $40M Series B, signing merchants such as Peloton, iRobot and Harman/JBL.
notes: Low public profile; engineering-side co-founder. Exact current title unverified (sources say SVP Engineering, CTO or Distinguished Engineer). Best route likely via Extend (extend.com) or CEO Woodrow Levin. No published press email found.

name: Rohan Shah
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer, Extend (product protection / extended warranty platform, San Francisco)
profile: Stanford 2014 graduate who co-founded Extend in 2019 with Woody Levin and others; the company lets merchants offer extended warranties and protection plans and handles claims, with customers such as Peloton, iRobot and Logitech. He is listed as Founder & CRO / head of partnerships. Not to be confused with Extend (paywithextend, virtual cards, CEO Andrew Jamison).
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2020 for co-founding Extend, which grew to 100+ full-time employees in under two years.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup after Stanford, which sold to startups, didn't work out; he then became a product lead in BCG's Digital Ventures group to build skills before co-founding Extend. His parents are both entrepreneurs who started a company together in 1987. Quote: 'I was always the best at learning by doing.'
notes: Hurun's 'Extend' here is the warranty company (extend.com), not the fintech paywithextend.com. NYSE TV lists him as 'Extend Founder & CRO' (https://tv.nyse.com/ceos-leaders/videos/extend-founder-cro-rohan-shah). No published personal contact found.

name: Woodrow H. Levin
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Extend (product-protection / extended-warranty platform for merchants)
profile: Serial founder Woody Levin co-founded Extend, a San Francisco platform that lets merchants sell product-protection plans online; it raised a $260M SoftBank-led Series C in 2021 at a $1.6B+ valuation. Earlier he founded gaming company BringIt (sold to IGT in 2012), stadium-ad firm InStadium and Estate Assist.
interesting_fact: He pitched Extend directly to SoftBank's Masayoshi Son, who he said 'immediately understood what we were doing'; his stated goal is to be the 'AppleCare' for everything that isn't an Apple product.
deep_cut_fact: Before Extend he founded InStadium, the NFL advertising company behind the ads in stadium bathrooms ('his idea'), and started Estate Assist (digital-asset estate planning) after watching his family of lawyers scramble for his grandmother's information after she died.

public_contacts.value: Danielle Vaknin, ASTRSK PR - extend@astrskpr.com (Extend media contact, Jan 2022 release)

notes: PR contact is from a 2022 release and may be stale. Search results also say he sits on the DraftKings board, but I could not open the DraftKings IR page to confirm it.

name: BC Broussard
profile: Listed as a co-founder of HomeLight (San Francisco real-estate agent-matching platform founded 2012; valued ~$1.6B in 2021) alongside Drew Uher and Jason Zhang in MarketScreener/Zippia listings. HomeLight's own materials and Wikipedia credit only Drew Uher as founder/CEO; no biography of Broussard was found.
notes: Thin public footprint: only aggregator listings (marketscreener.com Drew Uher relations page, zippia.com/homelight-careers-1415353) name BC Broussard as HomeLight co-founder; current role unknown. Wikipedia credits Drew Uher alone. Verify via HomeLight before outreach.

name: Drew Uher
current_role: Founder & CEO, HomeLight
profile: Drew Uher founded HomeLight in San Francisco in 2012 after he and his wife struggled to find a well-matched agent when buying a home. HomeLight matches consumers with real estate agents using transaction data and has added direct home buying and financing; it was valued at $1.6B in 2021 and is now headquartered in Scottsdale, Arizona.
interesting_fact: Uher says his one non-negotiable habit is not working on planes: 'It's the only time I really have to myself.' He now leads HomeLight's AI efforts including an AI-powered 'Buy Before You Sell' bridge loan.
deep_cut_fact: Before HomeLight he co-founded Gameyola, a distribution and monetization platform for casual Flash games that reached 250,000 daily active users; earlier he covered real estate and mortgage stocks in Morgan Stanley's New York research division. He is also a licensed California real estate broker.
notes: Texas A&M (MIS) and Stanford MBA. Best route is HomeLight press team.

name: Ma Zheren
current_role: Founder and CEO, Inceptio Technology (Shanghai autonomous heavy-truck developer)
profile: Julian Ma (Ma Zheren), a veteran of Motorola, Tencent (corporate VP) and fleet-IoT firm G7 (president), founded Inceptio Technology in Shanghai in 2018. It builds full-stack L3 autonomous driving for heavy trucks, put series-production L3 trucks on the road with OEMs in 2021, and opened a German office in 2024.
interesting_fact: Inceptio's autonomous trucking system has logged over 500 million km in commercial operation on Chinese freight routes; in Feb 2026 Ma joined the China-Germany Economic Advisory Committee symposium with the Chinese premier and German chancellor.
deep_cut_fact: He started Inceptio at about 47 after three decades spanning China and the US in tech, consulting and strategy; he told IMD: 'The essence of entrepreneurship is to do what no one else has done in the past, whether it is technological innovation or business model innovation.'
notes: Goes by Julian Ma in English. Company also lists partner@inceptio.ai for business partnerships. Hurun unicorn founder (company ~$2bn); personal wealth not disclosed.

name: Immad Akhund
current_role: Founder & CEO, Mercury (Mercury Technologies Inc.)
profile: Cambridge-educated immigrant founder; Mercury (founded 2017 with Max Tagher and Jason Zhang in San Francisco) is his fourth company and provides banking services to startups and small businesses via partner banks; valued at about $5.2B (May 2026). Previously built and sold Heyzap, a developer tool/ad network for app publishers.
interesting_fact: The Mercury idea came from frustration running Heyzap: 'I'd go to send a wire and it wasn't enabled in my account.' Mercury reportedly gained many customers and deposits after the March 2023 Silicon Valley Bank failure.
deep_cut_fact: Before starting Mercury in 2017 he was a part-time Partner at Y Combinator; meeting Kai Stinchcombe of True Link (debit cards for seniors via a bank partner) at YC's 2013 Demo Day gave him early confidence the bank-partnership model could work.
notes: Very active on X (@immad); also an angel investor (Mercury hosts an investor-database profile for him).

name: Max Tagher
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Mercury (Mercury Technologies Inc.)
profile: Max Tagher co-founded San Francisco fintech Mercury in 2017 with Immad Akhund and Jason Zhang and serves as its CTO. Mercury offers banking services to startups and small businesses through partner banks and was valued at about $5.2B as of 2026.
interesting_fact: Mercury's entire backend is written in Haskell, an unusual choice for a startup; Tagher says Haskell's correctness suited building the core features of a bank, and that backend Haskell engineer is the company's 'easiest role to hire for'.
deep_cut_fact: Tagher credits Michael Snoyman's open-source Yesod and Persistent libraries, saying Mercury 'would have never used Haskell if not for his work'; he personally tries to sponsor the OSS authors of the ~194 packages Mercury depends on.
notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile compared with CEO Immad Akhund; Haskell/engineering angle is the natural hook.

name: Asish Mohapatra
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, OfBusiness (OFB Tech), Gurugram
profile: IIT Kharagpur B.Tech and ISB MBA who worked at ITC, McKinsey and Matrix Partners India before co-founding OfBusiness in 2015, a tech platform combining raw-material procurement with credit for SMEs. OfBusiness became a SoftBank-backed unicorn; its lending arm Oxyzo is run by his wife and co-founder Ruchi Kalra.
interesting_fact: OfBusiness started by supplying steel for guardrail manufacturing; Mohapatra has said the founders faced 73 investor rejections in 2016 before the company went on to become a unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Born while his parents were researchers at IIT Kharagpur, he grew up in Cuttack, Odisha (and says he loves Cuttack's thunka puri); he traces his entrepreneurial spark to a Class 3 school essay he researched on Walt Disney.

public_contacts.value: https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/news (Press & Media page with media kit)

notes: No published press email; only a general support address (getsupport@ofbusiness.in) on the company site. Team page links his LinkedIn. Has done podcasts (e.g. KPMG Startup Speakeasy).

name: Bhuvan Gupta
current_role: Co-Founder and CTO, OfBusiness (OFB Tech)
profile: Bhuvan Gupta is co-founder and CTO of OfBusiness, an Indian B2B platform that supplies raw materials and credit to small and medium businesses. He holds a B.E. from BITS Pilani and an MBA from FMS, University of Delhi, and worked at Snapdeal, Bharti SoftBank and Exponential before co-founding OfBusiness.
interesting_fact: Before OfBusiness he worked at three tech companies: Snapdeal, Bharti SoftBank (BSB) and Exponential, according to the company's own team page.
deep_cut_fact: He combines an engineering degree from BITS Pilani with an MBA from the Faculty of Management Studies (FMS), University of Delhi, and worked at Bharti SoftBank (BSB) before OfBusiness.
notes: The team page lists no press email (only getsupport@ofbusiness.in for customer support); its Press & Media section has a media kit. Aggregator sites call him ex-VP Engineering at Snapdeal, but that title is not on an official source.

name: Chandranshu Sinha
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, EkAnek Networks (Foxy beauty-shopping app); co-founder of OfBusiness
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded B2B commerce and lending unicorn OfBusiness (OFB Tech), where he headed products. In 2018 he co-founded EkAnek Networks, which runs Foxy, an artist-led online shopping platform for beauty, grooming and personal care, where he serves as CTO.
interesting_fact: After helping build OfBusiness, he left to co-found Foxy (EkAnek Networks, founded 2018) alongside Kartik Sheth, Nikhil Gilani and Sachin Singhal.
notes: No longer listed on OfBusiness's current team page (https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/team?tab=team); best route is via Foxy/EkAnek. Background reportedly IIT Kharagpur, DevFactory and Trilogy, but that comes from a single weak source (CrazyEngineers), so it is not used as a fact. Low public profile.

name: Nitin Jain
current_role: Former co-founder & Chief Business Officer, OfBusiness (left Dec 2025; new venture announced as upcoming)
profile: IIT Delhi graduate who spent seven years at Royal Bank of Scotland in London (VP, structured solutions trading) before co-founding OfBusiness in 2016, a B2B raw-material procurement and credit platform for Indian SMEs with lending arm Oxyzo. He left in Dec 2025, saying 'Something big is upcoming', hinting at manufacturing.
interesting_fact: In his Dec 2025 LinkedIn farewell from IPO-bound OfBusiness he said 'Something big is upcoming' and, asked about manufacturing, replied his next move would be 'around these lines'.
deep_cut_fact: He was a silver medalist at IIT Delhi and worked in investment banking in London, where he faced a culture shock and even unexpected layoffs, before returning to India as a founding team member of OfBusiness.

public_contacts.value: Interview: The Desi VC podcast E112 (Nitin Jain, Co-founder & CBO, OfBusiness)

notes: Left OfBusiness Dec 2025; new venture not yet named in sources found. He announced the move on LinkedIn, so LinkedIn is the likely best route. Hurun lists the $5B valuation, which belongs to OfBusiness, not his own stake. The podcast entry is a past interview he gave, not a channel he runs.

name: Srinath Ramakkrushnan
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Operating Officer, Zetwerk
profile: IIT Madras mechanical engineer who co-founded Zetwerk, an Indian contract-manufacturing platform, in 2018 with IIT classmates incl. CEO Amrit Acharya. As COO he leads strategy/execution and directly drives growth of Zetwerk's energy and capital-goods businesses across India, the U.S. and Europe.
interesting_fact: He personally runs Zetwerk's energy and capital-goods businesses across India, the U.S. and Europe - a direct fit for an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he was a manager in ITC Limited's crop development and buying division, then co-founder/head of supply at OfBusiness (OFB Tech) and head of supply sales at BlackBuck (Zinka Logistics). Named to Fortune India 40 under 40 (2023) and ET 40 under 40 (2024).
notes: Some directories mislabel him as CEO; Amrit Acharya is CEO. Only a general company contact email is published (no dedicated press email found).

name: Vasant Sridhar
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Strategy Officer, OfBusiness (OFB Tech), Gurugram
profile: Vasant Sridhar co-founded OfBusiness in 2015 with Asish Mohapatra, Ruchi Kalra and others. The Gurugram company runs B2B commerce for raw materials and SME financing (through its lending arm Oxyzo) and is valued at about $5B. He serves as Co-Founder and CSO.
interesting_fact: OfBusiness's team page lists him as a B.Tech graduate of IIT Madras who came to OfBusiness from ITC.
deep_cut_fact: Before OfBusiness he worked at the FMCG conglomerates ITC and Unilever, per his company and org-chart profiles.

public_contacts.value: https://www.ofbusiness.com/about/news (Press & Media page; PR lead Akansha Verma, VP PR & Corporate Communications, listed without email)

notes: Low public profile. Sources disagree on whether CSO means Chief Strategy or Chief Sales Officer. Best route is via OfBusiness's PR/corporate communications team.

name: Qiu Yujing
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SemiDrive (芯驰科技), Nanjing
profile: Qiu Yujing (Maggie Qiu, 仇雨菁) co-founded Nanjing-based automotive chip designer SemiDrive in June 2018 with chairman Zhang Qiang, after leading automotive-grade chip R&D in China for NXP (and earlier Freescale). SemiDrive makes cockpit, ADAS, gateway and MCU chips for Chinese and overseas carmakers and is valued at about $2B as a Hurun unicorn.
interesting_fact: SemiDrive taped out China's first 16nm automotive-grade chip and broke into a cockpit-chip market where domestic firms had almost zero share; it has since won cockpit-chip supply deals with a European carmaker.
deep_cut_fact: SemiDrive was effectively a team spin-out: when rumours of Qualcomm's planned takeover of NXP threatened to break up her automotive-chip R&D team in 2018, Qiu and dozens of veteran colleagues walked out together and founded the company that June.
notes: English name Maggie Qiu. No published press/IR email found (private company). Possible route via SemiDrive's website or its investors. Automotive semiconductor angle; tangential to AI/data centers.

name: Jens Grede
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SKIMS
profile: Swedish-born entrepreneur (b. 1978) who co-founded ad agencies Saturday Group and Wednesday (majority sold to BBDO in 2016), fashion label Frame (2012), and in 2019 SKIMS with Kim Kardashian and his wife Emma Grede. As CEO he and Kardashian hold a majority stake; SKIMS was valued at over $5B as of 2025.
interesting_fact: He left school in 1997 to become managing editor of the Stockholm magazine Stockholm New, before Tyler Brule recruited him to his London agency Winkreative in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: At Winkreative he worked on the rebrand of Swiss International Air Lines and helped design the fashion identity and logo for Stella McCartney's eponymous label; he also met future partner Erik Torstensson there.
notes: No published press email found on skims.com; company contact page is customer-service oriented. Son of Swedish film director Kjell Grede.

name: Kensuke Naito
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of SmartHR (Japanese cloud HR/labor-management SaaS, launched 2015, valued ~$2B). SmartHR's own site and press credit Shoji Miyata as founder; current CEO is ex-CTO Masato Serizawa. Naito's specific role could not be verified from a primary source in this session.
interesting_fact: SmartHR was inspired by founder Shoji Miyata's personal experience dealing with paperwork; the service launched in 2015 and is used by tens of thousands of Japanese companies.
notes: Only CB Insights lists Naito as founder; SmartHR's official pages name Shoji Miyata. Could not confirm Naito's role or whether he is still at the company; verify before outreach (likely route via SmartHR corporate PR).

name: Shoji Miyata
current_role: Founder & CEO, Nstock Inc. (Tokyo); founder of SmartHR (stepped down as CEO 2022, left board 2025)
profile: Japanese entrepreneur who founded KUFU (now SmartHR) in 2013 and launched SmartHR, a cloud HR/labor-management SaaS, in 2015; it became a unicorn after a JPY15.6bn raise in 2021. He handed the CEO role to Masato Serizawa in 2022 and founded Nstock, an equity-compensation SaaS now building a secondary market for private shares.
interesting_fact: Nstock, his second startup, began in 2022 as a wholly owned SmartHR subsidiary and later became independent from the SmartHR Group; it is building a market for trading unlisted startup shares.
deep_cut_fact: Before SmartHR worked, he started a business with a friend in 2013 and racked up more than 10 failed ideas over two years before launching SmartHR in 2015.
notes: Japanese name: 宮田昇始. Best route is via Nstock; the X link is the company account, not his personal one.

name: Gong Jian
profile: Listed by Hurun as founder of 'The Little Bear' (valued ~$2B). The Little Bear (Xiaopangxiong, 小胖熊) is a Shanghai B2B home-renovation building-materials platform; Chinese press (Jiemian) names Niu Dalong as founder and controller, and does not mention Gong Jian. Could not verify Gong Jian's link to the company.
interesting_fact: The Little Bear (Xiaopangxiong) raised nearly $400M in its C and C+ rounds, the C+ led by SoftBank Vision Fund 2.
notes: Identity unresolved: Jiemian names Niu Dalong (牛大龙) as founder of 小胖熊; a CB Insights listing reportedly names 'Jian Gong' but could not be opened (403). Hurun's 'SaaS' label also doesn't match the B2B materials business. Verify before outreach.

name: Aly Orady
current_role: Founder of Tonal (CEO 2015-2023, then CTO; one profile lists him as founder/board member & advisor since Jan 2025)
profile: Engineer (McMaster computer engineering; Samsung, Sun, HP and enterprise startups) who founded Tonal, the electromagnetic-resistance smart home gym, in 2015. He led it as CEO until 2023, when it raised $130M and he moved to CTO; Tonal later appointed new CEOs (Todd Bartee named CEO in 2026).
interesting_fact: Tonal was born of his own health turnaround: after developing type 2 diabetes and sleep apnea he lost 70 pounds in nine months in 2014, then in March 2015 looked at a gym cable machine and wondered if electricity could replace its weight plates.
deep_cut_fact: He built the first Tonal prototypes himself on a wooden workbench at home with parts ordered online; the first version used a single magnet and gave only 25-40 lb of usable resistance, and he had studied electromagnetics at university but never built such a device in his jobs.
notes: Current exact title unclear (Tonal site: Founder & CTO; Village.ai: board member & advisor from 2025). Press route: media@tonal.com.

name: Nate Bosshard
current_role: Co-founder & partner, Offline Ventures (VC firm); co-founder of Tonal
profile: Nate Bosshard is a consumer-brand builder who co-founded Tonal, the connected strength-training machine company valued around $2B, leading brand and marketing. Earlier he worked at Burton Snowboards, The North Face, GoPro and was a partner at Khosla Ventures. He now invests via Offline Ventures, which he started in 2020 with Dave and Brit Morin and James Higa.
interesting_fact: Offline Ventures, which he co-founded with Dave and Brit Morin and James Higa, closed a $100M debut fund with Apple reported as an anchor investor.
deep_cut_fact: He has been promoting an idea he calls 'algorithmic immunity' - reclaiming personal taste and identity from AI-driven feeds - and cites his time at Burton Snowboards as a model of brands that create a 'world' customers step into (Getting2Alpha podcast, June 2025).
notes: Tonal's founder/CEO was Aly Orady; Bosshard was a co-founder on the brand/marketing side. Best route is via Offline Ventures. Has done podcasts (Fitt Insider, Getting2Alpha) - receptive to brand/taste topics.

name: Sid Viswanathan
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, Alchemy (in-house pharmacies for 340B safety-net clinics)
profile: Co-founded digital pharmacy/health-infrastructure company Truepill in 2016 with pharmacist Umar Afridi; served as President, then CEO from 2022 (Series D valued it at $1.6B). Now co-CEO of Alchemy, which builds in-house pharmacies for safety-net clinics serving people with HIV and Hepatitis C; it raised a $31M a16z-led seed in Oct 2024.
interesting_fact: Alchemy's $31M seed round was led by a16z Bio + Health, with Magic Johnson among the investors.
deep_cut_fact: Started his career in Johnson & Johnson's Global Operations Leadership Development program, then founded CardMunch, a business-card scanning app acquired by LinkedIn, where he became a product manager.
notes: Left Truepill in 2023; best angle is Alchemy / 340B pharmacy. Co-CEO with Peter Park (ex-Truepill).

name: Yu Liang
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2021-2024) as the person behind CASICloud / 航天云网 (Casicloud Technology Development Co., Beijing); role not independently confirmed
profile: Hurun names 於亮 (Yu Liang) as founder of CASICloud (航天云网), the industrial-internet company set up in June 2015 by state aerospace group CASIC and affiliates to run the INDICS platform (INDICS 2.0 launched June 2021). As a CASIC subsidiary, its leaders are state-appointed executives, not private founders.
interesting_fact: CASICloud's INDICS platform is billed as one of China's leading national industrial-internet platforms and underpins CASIC's 'Digital Aerospace' strategy; INDICS 2.0 was unveiled at the International Industrial Internet Conference on 15 June 2021.
notes: Chinese name 於亮 per Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2021 and 2024 (hurun.net list data). Searches in Chinese (於亮/于亮 + 航天云网/航天科工 + 董事长/总经理) and English (Yu Liang + CASICloud) found no news or filing confirming his title; casicloud.com was unreachable from this session. Many unrelated 'Yu Liang's exist (Guilin Fuda, Guangzhou Finance Holdings, etc.), so don't conflate. Treat as unverified.

name: Pedro Castillo
current_role: Founder of Onum, now Falcon Onum inside CrowdStrike (deal announced Aug 2025, reported ~$290M); co-founder of Devo
profile: Spanish engineer Pedro (del) Castillo co-founded Devo (originally Logtrust) in Madrid in 2011, a cloud-native security data analytics platform that became Spain's first cybersecurity unicorn; he served as CEO and then about 11 years as CTO. In 2022-23 he founded Onum, a real-time security data pipeline company, which CrowdStrike agreed to buy in 2025 to feed its Falcon Next-Gen SIEM.
interesting_fact: CrowdStrike's 2025 purchase of Onum (reported at $290M) gave Castillo a second security exit after Devo; he said pipelines should 'transform data into real-time intelligence', not just move it.
deep_cut_fact: Before Devo he was security tech director, then CTO and head of tech innovation at Bankinter, where back in 2001 his team built an on-prem system to collect all the data the bank generated, the seed of the Devo idea. Devo spent two years building product before launching and came within days of running out of cash.

public_contacts.value: https://www.crowdstrike.com (onum.com now redirects to CrowdStrike's Falcon Onum page)

notes: Also appears as Pedro del Castillo / Pedro Muros Castillo. Since the CrowdStrike deal, CrowdStrike press relations is likely the route; his post-acquisition title not verified. MWC Barcelona speaker. Do not confuse with Peru's former president Pedro Castillo.

name: Sammy Krikler
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Insurance Officer and board member, Earnix
profile: Israeli statistician and co-founder (2001) of Earnix, whose AI-driven pricing and rating software is used by insurers and banks to price policies and loans. He is the only one of the three co-founders still at the company, which became a unicorn in 2021 after a $75M round led by Insight Partners.
interesting_fact: Earnix's CEO Udi Ziv has called Krikler 'the brains of the product'; of the three 2001 co-founders (with Yoni Cheifetz and Shai Fogel) he is the one who stayed for two decades-plus.
notes: Very low media profile. Aggregator profiles say he studied statistics at the Hebrew University and was R&D manager at Eventus Software before Earnix (unverified primary source). Route via Earnix press/marketing or LinkedIn.

name: Yoni Cheifetz
current_role: Partner, Lightspeed Venture Partners (heads Israel investment team); co-founder of Earnix
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur who co-founded insurance/banking pricing-analytics firm Earnix in 2001 with Sammy Krikler (valued ~$1B after Insight Partners' 2021 investment). Also co-founded or chaired Demantra (sold to Oracle), Agentics and Traiana; since 2006 he has led Lightspeed's Israel investing across AI, enterprise, fintech, climate and deep tech.
interesting_fact: A serial founder of nearly a dozen software companies before VC, including Demantra (acquired by Oracle), Agentics (acquired by Mercado) and Traiana (acquired by ICAP).
deep_cut_fact: Holds an MSc in applied mathematics and computer science from the Weizmann Institute, ran product management at ClickSoftware, and unwinds by kayaking and rowing: 'Somehow that makes me a better, or at least calmer, person.'
notes: Also listed as Jonathan Cheifetz in some filings. Says he tries to meet as many entrepreneurs as possible. Work email is the 'Get in Touch' link on his Lightspeed bio.

name: Chen Yuqi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Hai Robotics (Shenzhen)
profile: Chen Yuqi (Richie Chen) co-founded Hai Robotics in Shenzhen in 2016. The company makes autonomous case-handling robots (ACRs) for warehouse automation and was later valued at about $2B. He still runs it as CEO. Its HAIPICK and HaiClimber systems are deployed worldwide for customers such as DHL and Philips.
interesting_fact: Hai Robotics launched HAIPICK, billed as the world's first autonomous case-handling robot. The company says it raises warehouse storage density by 80-130%. Chen was named to Fortune China's 40 Under 40 in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Chen earned a BEng in Electronic and Information Engineering from Hong Kong PolyU in 2012. PolyU calls Hai Robotics the first unicorn nurtured under its entrepreneurship ecosystem.
notes: Known in English as Richie Chen. The company PR inbox is the best route.

name: Ben Christensen
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Handshake
profile: Michigan Tech alum ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college-to-career recruiting network, with Garrett Lord and Scott Ringwelski in Houghton, Michigan. Handshake now connects ~20M students and alumni with 1M+ employers (valued ~$3.5bn) and has pushed into supplying expert talent for AI training work.
interesting_fact: Christensen nearly took a cybersecurity job at a Michigan company instead; the founders gave themselves three years to sign five schools or give up.
deep_cut_fact: He met Garrett Lord in a Michigan Tech outdoor adventure group; on early sales trips they often slept in a Ford Focus in McDonald's parking lots and once drove to Virginia and back for a single school visit.
notes: Low-profile co-founder (Crunchbase lists Denver base; previously Arbor Networks ASERT security research). Press office or Michigan Tech alumni connection are natural routes.

name: Garrett Lord
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Handshake
profile: Michigan native who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, in 2014 with Michigan Tech classmates Ben Christensen and Scott Ringwelski, leaving school a few credits short to raise capital. Handshake was valued at $3.5B (Series F, 2022). Since late 2024 he has pushed a 'refounding' via Handshake AI, which recruits domain experts to train AI models.
interesting_fact: He conceived Handshake AI at the company's 2024 Christmas party; the unit was projected to hit about $100M in annual recurring revenue, and he calls the pivot the 'refounding of Handshake'.
deep_cut_fact: At Michigan Tech he worked as a ski patroller at Mont Ripley, played broomball, and scavenged campus dumpsters for parts for his IT side business; he also cold-emailed recruiters to land a Palantir internship and won its summer hackathon.

public_contacts.value: Notion 'First Block' interview with Garrett Lord

notes: Very accessible founder with lots of interviews; Handshake AI (data-for-AI) angle relevant to a data-center/AI podcast.

name: Scott Ringwelski
current_role: Co-founder, Handshake (former CTO; current operating title not publicly stated)
profile: Traverse City, Michigan native and Michigan Tech software-engineering grad ('14) who co-founded Handshake, the college career network, with Garrett Lord and Ben Christensen in 2014 and served as its CTO. Handshake was valued at $3.5B in 2022; Ringwelski keeps a low public profile and is listed today simply as co-founder.
interesting_fact: Handshake was born at a small engineering school in Houghton, Michigan: the founders saw the opportunity gap versus Ivy League students; the platform grew to 18M students and 1,200 schools by 2021.
deep_cut_fact: While Lord and Christensen pitched colleges on the road, he stayed in Houghton building the product; he took the call from Wabash College that became Handshake's first client ('my first and only sales call'), and the first HQ was a rental house with a hole where a basement window should be.
notes: Very low public profile; co-founders call him 'the smartest person in all our CS classes'. Current role unclear (Handshake now lists a different CTO). Route via Handshake press or Michigan Tech alumni network.

name: Blake Hall
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, ID.me (McLean, Virginia)
profile: Former US Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me in 2010 (originally TroopSwap, a military deals site) with fellow Ranger Matt Thompson; renamed ID.me in 2013, it became a leading digital identity-verification network used by federal and state agencies and companies, valued around $2B. He remains CEO and a frequent voice on identity fraud policy.
interesting_fact: As a battalion reconnaissance platoon leader in Iraq he led some 450 combat patrols with no casualties in his platoon and received two Bronze Star medals before leaving the Army in 2008.
deep_cut_fact: He applied to Harvard Business School on his battalion commander's push; Hall recalled deciding to 'apply to the best of the best if I'm going to do this.' ID.me began life as TroopSwap, a Groupon-style deals site for service members.

public_contacts.value: ID.mePR@rhstrategic.com (Raffetto Herman Strategic Communications, listed in 2022 release)

notes: Comfortable with media and podcasts (veteran-entrepreneur story). PR agency contact is from a 2022 release and may be outdated; check ID.me's newsroom for current press contact.

name: Matthew Thompson
current_role: President & Chief Commercial Officer, Socure (identity verification), since Dec 2025
profile: Former Army Ranger and Harvard MBA who co-founded ID.me (begun 2010 as TroopSwap, a military deals site) with HBS classmate Blake Hall and served as its COO/president; left in 2015. Later ran IDEMIA's North America identity business and held an identity role at Capital One, then joined Socure, building its public-sector business before becoming CRO and, in Dec 2025, President & CCO.
interesting_fact: ID.me began as an HBS project: Hall and Thompson, both Army veterans, struggled to claim veteran discounts online. Thompson had gone to Goldman Sachs in Los Angeles after his MBA but came back when Hall opened shop near D.C. in early 2011.
deep_cut_fact: He holds three patents spanning mobile biometric liveness detection and tiered and third-party authentication, and was Socure's first public-sector leader, launching its government business.
notes: No longer at ID.me (left 2015 per Wikipedia https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ID.me); best route is via Socure's PR agency (Highwire). Common name - confirm via ID.me/Socure context.

name: Tanel Suurhans
current_role: Co-founder and Distinguished Engineer, ID.me (CTO 2014-2024)
profile: Estonian engineer who joined veterans' discount startup TroopSwap as co-founder in 2013 and helped rebuild it as ID.me, the digital identity wallet used by US federal and state agencies (valued ~$2B in 2021). He was CTO from 2014 until September 2024, when Scott Meyer succeeded him and he moved to Distinguished Engineer.
interesting_fact: Tallinn's city government celebrated ID.me as 'yet another unicorn co-founded by an Estonian', citing it as proof of Estonia's world-leading unicorn-per-capita record.
deep_cut_fact: ID.me began in 2010 as TroopSwap, a service founded by two former Army Rangers to verify veterans for discounts; Suurhans was brought on in 2013 as the Estonian technical co-founder who helped turn that log-in flow into a general identity network.
notes: Very low public profile; no published personal or press email found for ID.me (media seems routed through staff contacts). CTO transition source: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/idme-appoints-scott-meyer-as-chief-technology-officer-302242142.html

name: Lisa Riolo
current_role: Co-founder and advisor, impact.com (Santa Barbara)
profile: Affiliate-marketing veteran who was SVP of Business Development at Commission Junction before co-founding Impact Radius (now impact.com) in Santa Barbara in 2008. impact.com became a leading partnership-automation platform valued at ~$2B+; Riolo is described as co-founder and advisor and remains an industry speaker.
interesting_fact: She has 25+ years in affiliate/partnership marketing and was among impact.com's 2008 founding team alongside Per Pettersen, Roger Kjensrud, Todd Crawford and Wade Crang.
deep_cut_fact: Mixergy's Andrew Warner titled his interview with her 'The woman who paid me $1 million in affiliate revenue' from her Commission Junction days; she also co-founded workzones, a Santa Barbara co-working business.
notes: Low public profile; current operating role at impact.com unclear (listed as co-founder/advisor). Workzones detail is from Crunchbase bio.

name: Per Pettersen
current_role: Co-Founder, Chief Strategy Officer and Board Director, impact.com
profile: Serial ad-tech entrepreneur who co-founded Commission Junction (an early affiliate network, sold to ValueClick), then Leadpoint and Savings.com. In 2008 he co-founded Santa Barbara-based Impact Radius (now impact.com), a partnership-automation platform later valued at ~$2B. He was CEO until 2017, when he became executive chairman and CSO; impact.com now lists him as CSO.
interesting_fact: Impact Radius was founded by a group of Commission Junction alumni: Pettersen, Wade Crang, Todd Crawford, Lisa Riolo and Roger Kjensrud (now impact.com's CTO). In effect, the team that built one of the first affiliate networks rebuilt the category a decade later.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he holds a BS in electrical engineering and an MS in computer engineering from UC Santa Barbara. impact.com's own bio says he 'was building partnership businesses before the industry had a name for what he was doing.'
notes: Santa Barbara-based. No personal channels or published press email found; the impact.com contact page or press-releases section is the route in. The UCSB degrees appear in aggregated bios (e.g. a 2026 impact.com release, per search snippets); the full bio text could not be fetched directly.

name: Roger Kjensrud
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, impact.com (Santa Barbara, CA)
profile: Norwegian-born engineer who co-founded partnership-marketing platform impact.com (founded 2008 as Impact Radius) and has led its engineering and product teams as CTO ever since; the company was valued at about $2B+. Earlier he was Director of Engineering at affiliate pioneer Commission Junction and co-founded Savings.com and Leadpoint.
interesting_fact: At Commission Junction he led the move of the original affiliate network onto a scalable Java-based infrastructure, before co-founding impact.com with fellow CJ alumni.
deep_cut_fact: His Dark Reading author bio notes that he is a former Norwegian ice fishing champion.
notes: Very low public profile and a technical (non-CEO) founder. Ice-fishing fact comes from the Dark Reading bio as shown in search snippets (page is bot-blocked, so I couldn't read it directly). Media contact is from a 2024 release and may be stale. Also linked to the Estalea venture vehicle with co-founder Per Pettersen.

name: Todd Crawford
current_role: Co-Founder and VP Strategic Initiatives, impact.com
profile: Affiliate-marketing pioneer who was on the founding team of Commission Junction (CJ) in 1998, later guided strategy for Digital River's OneNetworkDirect, and in 2008 co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com), the Santa Barbara partnership-automation platform. He remains VP of Strategic Initiatives and co-hosts the company's Partnership Economy podcast.
interesting_fact: Industry peers call him the 'Godfather of Affiliate'; he was named to PartnerCentric/Hello Partner's Hero100 2025 as 'The OG Hero'.
deep_cut_fact: He was an original board member of the Performance Marketing Association, the US affiliate-industry trade group, and has offered paid one-on-one advice calls on Clarity.fm.
notes: Very approachable, conference-circuit regular; his Clarity.fm paid-call profile is a direct route. Some sources describe him as CJ's first employee rather than co-founder.

name: Wade Crang
current_role: Co-founder, impact.com (listed as Co-Founder & Growth Technologist / VP Strategic Operations)
profile: Cal Poly graduate and ad-tech data specialist who co-founded Impact Radius (now impact.com) in Santa Barbara in 2008 with Todd Crawford, Per Pettersen, Roger Kjensrud and Lisa Riolo. The partnership-automation platform reached a ~$1.5-2B valuation; Crang remains with the company in a strategic/technology role.
interesting_fact: impact.com was founded by a group of former Commission Junction (CJ) affiliate-marketing veterans; Crang had been CJ's VP of Business Intelligence & Product.
deep_cut_fact: Before impact.com he was on the founding team at LeadPoint, where he built the business-intelligence architecture credited with lifting revenue per lead.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal accounts verified. Best route is via impact.com communications (contact block on latest press release; EMEA releases have listed impact@mww.com agency address).

name: Wu Shufan
current_role: Co-founder/board member, LandSpace; founder and chairman, MinoSpace; Chair Professor and Executive Dean, School of Aeronautics and Astronautics, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
profile: Chinese aerospace engineer who co-founded LandSpace in 2015 with Zhang Changwu (CEO) and Wang Jianmeng; LandSpace builds the Zhuque methane-fuelled rockets and is pursuing a Shanghai IPO. He also founded small-satellite maker MinoSpace in 2017 and leads SJTU's aerospace school.
interesting_fact: Wu spent about 17 years in European aerospace research, including 2002-2013 at the European Space Agency's ESTEC centre in the Netherlands, before returning to China.
deep_cut_fact: Before going commercial he was chief engineer of the China-French SVOM gamma-ray-burst science satellite and the STU-2 CubeSat mission at the Shanghai Engineering Centre for Microsatellites (2013-2017); he was also a Humboldt Foundation fellow at TU Braunschweig.
notes: Not the founder/CEO of LandSpace (that is Zhang Changwu); he is a co-founder. Academic route via SJTU School of Aeronautics and Astronautics may be most accessible.

name: Shu Congxuan
current_role: Founder of Laoxiangji (Home Original Chicken), Hefei, Anhui (chairman in 2020; current formal title not confirmed)
profile: Former soldier who began raising chickens in Feixi, Anhui in 1982 and became one of the province's largest free-range chicken farmers. After a 1999 franchising course he opened the 'Feixi Old Hen' fast-food restaurant in Hefei in 2003, renamed Laoxiangji in 2012. The chain now has about 1,400 stores and has repeatedly attempted an IPO; his children hold most of the stake.
interesting_fact: In February 2020 he posted a video tearing up a letter in which employees offered to work without pay during COVID, saying he would sell houses and cars to keep about 16,000 staff fed and employed; it went viral and earned him the nickname 'China's best boss'.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army at 20 in autumn 1982, he spent his 1,800-yuan wedding money on about 1,000 chickens and reportedly ate and slept in the chicken shed for seven years while learning the trade.
notes: Chinese-language media only; reach via Laoxiangji corporate (Hefei). Reported to have transferred his direct shareholding to his children; daughter Shu Wen is an executive director.

name: Eric Larchevêque
current_role: Manager (gérant) and largest shareholder of TBSO (listed AI/fintech group); co-founder and former CEO/chairman of Ledger
profile: French serial entrepreneur since 1996 (Montorgueil, Prixing). Founded La Maison du Bitcoin in Paris, which merged with BTChip and Chronocoin in 2014 to form Ledger, the hardware crypto-wallet maker he led as CEO until 2019. Now an angel investor, TV investor on M6, and head of TBSO, which in 2026 dropped a bitcoin-treasury plan to build an AI/fintech group.
interesting_fact: Ledger was born in Vierzon (Cher), and in 2019 he co-founded ALGOSUP, a five-year software-development school, in the same town with Franck Jeanin.
deep_cut_fact: As an investor on M6's 'Qui veut être mon associé ?' he committed €590,000 in season 1, the third-largest total of the panel; he trained as an engineer at ESIEE Paris (MSc in information-processing architecture).
notes: Very public in French media and podcasts; best route is likely via TBSO investor relations or the M6 show/press. No published personal contact found in this pass. Recent interview: https://www.toutsurmesfinances.com/actualites/?p=799

name: Joel Pobeda
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (former COO); no current public title confirmed
profile: French entrepreneur and one of four co-founders of Ledger, the Paris-based crypto hardware-wallet maker, alongside Eric Larchevêque, Thomas France and Nicolas Bacca. He served as COO in Ledger's early years, helping build its operations. His current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Ledger was formed in 2014 by merging his startup Chronocoin with BTChip and Eric Larchevêque's La Maison du Bitcoin.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ledger he founded Chronocoin, which let people buy Bitcoin with 3D-Secure credit/debit cards; its purchasing service was later rebranded Coinhouse, now one of France's main crypto brokerages.
notes: Very low public profile; sources are mostly profile aggregators. Alive status assumed (no death reports found). Best route likely via Ledger press/comms or LinkedIn.

name: Nicolas Bacca
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, ZKNox (hardware security & zero-knowledge cryptography); angel investor
profile: French hardware-security engineer who co-founded Ledger (2014), the Paris crypto hardware-wallet unicorn, serving as CTO and from 2019 chief innovation officer until leaving in 2023. After briefly launching smart-wallet project Smoo.th, he co-founded ZKNox in 2025 with cryptographers from Ledger and Thales, and angel-invests in French crypto startups (Bitstack, Spiko, Bubblemaps, Hyli).
interesting_fact: He read the Bitcoin whitepaper in 2012 while holding a smart-card design that could store secrets but had no business model: 'Bitcoin gave me that. So I'm very grateful for Satoshi.'
deep_cut_fact: As a child he printed his own fake banknotes and 'paid' his parents with them ('I was kind of my own central bank'); today he's invested in a champagne house that pays dividends in bottles, and says he's famous for bringing champagne to every party.
notes: Long known in crypto by the handle 'btchip' (on Devcon profile) - personal X not independently verified here. Speaks regularly at Paris Blockchain Week, EthCC, Devcon; conference circuit is a natural route. Ledger's Recover controversy preceded his exit - avoid.

name: Thomas France
current_role: Co-founder of Ledger (board advisor per profile aggregators); founder/managing partner of Cygni Capital (crypto/trust-tech VC)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Ledger, the Paris-based maker of crypto hardware wallets, in 2014 (Ledger later raised $380M in 2021 at unicorn valuation). Earlier he co-founded the shopping app Prixing. After stepping back from operations around 2019 he co-founded Cygni Capital, investing in blockchain, privacy and AI, and is an active angel investor.
interesting_fact: Ledger, which he co-founded in 2014, became one of France's best-known crypto unicorns, building secure hardware wallets for digital assets and raising $380M in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2014, with Eric Larcheveque, he opened La Maison du Bitcoin on rue du Caire in Paris, a physical venue for training in and buying cryptocurrencies, often described as Europe's first bitcoin space and a precursor to Ledger.
notes: Ledger press email is for the company, where he is no longer an operator. Cygni Capital has no confirmed official website; dates from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener, Dealroom) are inconsistent. Low media profile; appeared on the 'Can't Be Done' podcast (ep. 58).

name: Assaf Eisenstein
current_role: Co-Founder & President, Lusha
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Lusha, a B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform, with developer Yoni Tserruya in 2016. Lusha bootstrapped to profitability before raising a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation; Eisenstein oversees business operations (legal, finance, investment strategy) as president.
interesting_fact: Lusha began as a side project aimed at recruiters, but salespeople quickly became its main users; it grew from a Chrome extension into a data platform with 515M+ data entries and now an MCP/API layer for AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before Lusha he was an HR-tech founder (Lusha's own site calls him 'an HR tech creator'), having built employee-referral software in Tel Aviv - which is why Lusha was first pitched as a recruiting tool.
notes: Low public profile compared to CEO Yoni Tserruya. No published press email found; LinkedIn (linked from Lusha's About page) is best route. Lusha's name comes from a family nickname (avoid in outreach per rules).

name: Yoni Tserruya
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Lusha (Tel Aviv / New York)
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded Lusha with Assaf Eisenstein in 2016; the B2B contact-data and sales-intelligence platform grew largely bootstrapped before a $205M Series B in 2021 at a $1.5B valuation. He still leads it as CEO, now pitching Lusha as a GTM data layer for AI agents via API and MCP.
interesting_fact: Lusha reached unicorn status in 2021 with a $205M Series B led by PSG at a $1.5B valuation after years of near-bootstrapped growth.
deep_cut_fact: Lusha began as a side project he built while working his first job as an iOS developer at AT&T, after studying computer science; he calls himself 'a builder at heart' who was 'more into tinkering than following plans'.
notes: Recent interview talks about AI agents and data infrastructure (MCP), a natural data/AI podcast angle.

name: Ed Thompson
current_role: CTO and co-founder, Matillion
profile: British software engineer who co-founded Manchester-born data-integration company Matillion with CEO Matthew Scullion in 2011. He led the team that launched Matillion ETL in 2014; the cloud data pipeline company (now pushing its 'Maia' agentic data team) raised $150M Series E at a $1.5B valuation in 2021 and reached ~$2B in later rankings.
interesting_fact: Matillion is one of the few UK tech unicorns founded in Manchester; it later built a major second hub in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: Before Matillion he spent 11 years as an IBM software consultant to UK blue-chip companies; Matillion ran for three years before he and his team shipped the flagship ETL product in 2014.
notes: Common name; identity tied to Matillion CTO. Writes bylines for DBTA, DevOps.com, Solutions Review; appeared on 'Data Sharks' podcast. Route via Matillion press.

name: Matthew Scullion
current_role: Co-founder and board member, Matillion (stepped down as CEO Aug 2026); lay member of the University of Manchester Board of Governors
profile: Altrincham-born entrepreneur who co-founded Matillion in Manchester in 2011 after 15 years in UK/European IT systems integration (incl. software division director at Imtech ICT). He built Matillion into a cloud data-integration unicorn and led its pivot to 'Maia' AI data automation; in Aug 2026 Girish Pancha became CEO and Scullion stayed on the board.

current_role: Founder and Executive Chair, Justworks (CEO 2012-Oct 2022)
profile: Former Amazon engineer/product manager and Army officer who founded ad startup Adtuitive (sold to Etsy in 2009), then founded Justworks in 2012 to fix the payroll/HR pain he had at small companies. He handed the CEO role to Michael Seckler in Nov 2022 and, as Executive Chair, leads the board and focuses on Justworks Labs, Justworks.org and its Leaders' Fellowship.
interesting_fact: He enlisted in the Army Reserve at 17 with a parent's note and served 12 years, doing counterterrorism analysis on weekends while working full time; he even took a six-month leave from Amazon for officer training.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Adtuitive, was a five-person ad platform he founded after leaving Amazon in 2008; Etsy acquired it in 2009, and the HR/payroll headaches he saw there inspired Justworks.
