name: John Gedmark
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Astranis Space Technologies
profile: John Gedmark is an aerospace engineer (BS Purdue, MS Stanford, rocket propulsion) who co-founded Astranis in 2015 with Ryan McLinko to build small geostationary communications satellites using software-defined radios. Astranis (YC W16) launched its first commercial satellite, Arcturus, in 2023 for Alaska and has customers in the Philippines, Mexico, Thailand, Taiwan and the U.S. government.
interesting_fact: Astranis' first commercial MicroGEO satellite (for Pacific Dataport, serving Alaska) rode to orbit in April 2023 as part of a multi-satellite payload on the ViaSat-3 launch.
deep_cut_fact: Before Astranis he was Director of Rocket Flight Operations at the X Prize Foundation and co-founded and led the Commercial Spaceflight Federation, advocating for commercial crew policies.
notes: Highly relevant for a space/connectivity angle; Astranis HQ in San Francisco. X handle listed on an event speaker page, not independently verified on X.

name: Allon Bloch
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, K Health (AI-powered primary care); independent director, Wix.com
profile: Israeli-American serial entrepreneur who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Ran Shaul. It uses AI models trained on large clinical datasets to power virtual primary care and has partnerships with health systems such as Northwell, Cedars-Sinai and Penn Medicine. Earlier he was co-CEO and president of Wix.com (2008-2010) and CEO of online car retailer Vroom (2014-2016).
interesting_fact: He has built companies in three very different sectors (website building at Wix, used cars at Vroom, AI medicine at K Health), and before that was a venture partner at Greylock and a general partner at JVP.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he trained in science: per his bios he holds a B.Sc. in biology from Tel Aviv University, then took an MBA at Columbia Business School (class of '97) and started at McKinsey; he now sits on the Columbia Business School board.
notes: The PR emails come from K Health press releases (2022 and 2025), seen via search; khealth.com/press hides its address behind Cloudflare. The biology B.Sc. comes from secondary profiles. Media-accessible; frequent health-tech conference speaker.

name: Israel Roth
current_role: Co-founder (former CTO) of K Health; reported in 2023 to have stepped back from the CTO role to work as a chef
profile: Israeli software entrepreneur and ex-Scitex manager who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Allon Bloch, Ran Shaul and Taboola CEO Adam Singolda and served as its CTO. K Health builds AI-driven primary care (symptom checking and virtual clinicians) and was valued as a unicorn. Earlier he co-founded print-personalisation software firm XMPie and Labgoo.
interesting_fact: According to a 2023 report on K Health's funding, Roth left the CTO post a few months earlier to become a chef.
deep_cut_fact: He was chief software architect and a co-founder of XMPie, a Scitex spin-off (with Jacob Aizikowitz and Reuven Sherwin) that pioneered variable-data/personalised printing and was bought by Xerox for $54M in 2006.
notes: Low public profile; no published personal or office contact found. Company route would be K Health press (khealth.com), but he may no longer be operational there. Name is common: confirm the right Israel Roth before outreach.

name: Ran Shaul
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, K Health (New York / Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur (Tel Aviv University) who co-founded K Health in 2016 with Allon Bloch, Israel Roth and Adam Singolda. K Health uses AI trained on millions of anonymised medical records to power a symptom checker and virtual primary care, partnering with health systems such as Cedars-Sinai; it reached unicorn status. Shaul leads product.
interesting_fact: K Health's pitch is 'a doctor in your pocket': its AI compares a user's symptoms against millions of patient records to show how doctors diagnosed similar people, before routing them to a clinician - Shaul has explained the approach on podcasts such as The MAML Podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In 2005 he co-founded Pursway, an audience-targeting startup that mapped real-life relationships among 150m+ North American consumers using machine-learning and techniques borrowed from anti-terrorism link analysis; it was acquired by Interpublic (IPG) in 2015.
notes: Has done podcast interviews before (MAML podcast) - receptive to podcast format. Route via K Health press team.

name: Augusto Marietti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kong Inc. (API and AI connectivity platform, San Francisco)
profile: Rome-born entrepreneur who started Mashape with schoolmate Marco Palladino in a rented Milan garage in 2009, moved to San Francisco after failing to raise money in Italy, and pivoted to an API marketplace. Mashape became Kong, whose open-source API gateway grew into an enterprise API/AI-gateway platform; Kong reached unicorn status (~$2B valuation).
interesting_fact: He and his co-founders lived on about $1,000 a month in Silicon Valley, gave themselves '90 days to make it or break it', and got their first break after cold-emailing hundreds of contacts from a Stanford entrepreneurship event list.
deep_cut_fact: Travis Kalanick let him stay at his San Francisco 'JamPad' for a few weeks on one condition: Marietti had to cook carbonara for Kalanick's partner once a week. He told the story on the a16z podcast with Martin Casado.
notes: Goes by 'Aghi'. Open, story-friendly founder who appears on podcasts (a16z) and in Business Insider. Kong now positions itself around AI-agent/API connectivity, which fits AI infrastructure. Best route: press@konghq.com.

name: Marco Palladino
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Kong Inc. (San Francisco)
profile: Italian-born, self-taught engineer who co-founded API marketplace Mashape in Milan (2009-10) with Augusto Marietti, moved to San Francisco in 2011, and pivoted it into Kong, the open-source API gateway (2015) that became a cloud-native API and AI-connectivity platform. Kong passed $100m ARR and raised at a ~$2bn valuation in 2024; as CTO he now focuses on APIs for AI agents.
interesting_fact: Kong began in a garage in Milan: Marietti and Palladino struggled to raise money because few Italian investors understood APIs, so in 2011 they moved to San Francisco and slept on friends' couches while building Mashape.
deep_cut_fact: He has been a self-taught programmer since about age 13 and still recalls coding on Windows 3.1 on a 486 PC 'with a Turbo button' - an early fascination with networking software that led him to RPC/HTTP APIs in the SOA/Web Services era.
notes: Active technical voice: frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (e.g. Software Engineering Daily, The Business of Open Source). Natural fit for an AI-infrastructure episode (API gateways for LLM/agent traffic). Personal social handles not verified from an official source.

name: Michele Zonca
current_role: Unclear — former co-founder/Chief Architect of Mashape (now Kong); listed as partner at Italian startup studio The Liquid Factory (Crunchbase) and CTO of Tok.tv since 2019 (MarketScreener)
profile: Italian software engineer (MSc computer science) who co-founded Mashape with Augusto Marietti and Marco Palladino in July 2009; Mashape pivoted into Kong, the API-gateway/cloud-connectivity company valued at $1bn+. He served as Chief Architect until ~2012-2013, then returned to Italy, later working in startups including sports-fan app Tok.tv.

deep_cut_fact: After raising a $1.5M seed round, the Mashape founders lived and worked in a green house-office at 433 Bryant Street in San Francisco, trading lower salaries for room and board — and threw away and rewrote at least 100,000 lines of code within months.
notes: Left Kong operations around 2012; current role unconfirmed and he has a low public profile. Wealth tied to his Kong founder equity. Best fit is an origin-story conversation about Kong.

name: Brad Goldoor
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Employee Experience Officer, Phenom (Ambler, PA) - most recent reported title (formerly Chief People Officer)
profile: Pittsburgh-educated (BA, University of Pittsburgh) sales and recruiting-tech veteran who co-founded Phenom around 2010-11 with Mahe Bayireddi and Hari Bayireddy. Phenom became an applied-AI talent-experience platform (recruiting automation, AI agents for HR, internal mobility) valued at over $1bn. He led business development, then people/HR, then employee experience.
interesting_fact: Phenom's stated mission is 'helping a billion people find the right work'; Goldoor, its people chief for years, has written publicly about running a 'not normal' candidate and employee experience, including an ERE piece 'Put Employees First, Work Second During a Crisis' (May 2020).
deep_cut_fact: Before Phenom he spent his early career selling for CareerBuilder and Gannett - i.e. he came to HR-tech from the job-board/newspaper-classifieds world that AI recruiting platforms like Phenom later disrupted.

public_contacts.value: jennifer.lyons@phenompeople.com (Phenom Director of PR, media inquiries)

notes: Not a data-center/energy figure - Phenom is HR/AI software; fit for the podcast is weak. Exact current title not confirmed by a dated official source. Also reportedly an angel investor and earlier VP BD at coupon app SnipSnap (directory sources only).

profile: Hari Bayireddy co-founded Phenom in 2010 (originally iMomentus) with Mahe Bayireddi (CEO) and Brad Goldoor. name: Mahe Bayireddi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Phenom (Phenom People), Ambler/Philadelphia
profile: Co-founded Phenom around 2010-11 with Hari Bayireddy and Brad Goldoor to build an AI-powered talent-experience platform for hiring, employee development and retention. A $100m Series D in 2021 valued Phenom at about $1.4bn; the company runs the IAMPHENOM conference and has been acquiring AI firms (e.g. Included AI, Be Applied in 2026) while selling AI hiring agents to large enterprises.

deep_cut_fact: Phenom wasn't his first startup: his earlier company, iMomentous, failed, and he has said the lessons from it - especially seeing talent from the candidate, HR and manager perspectives at once - shaped how he built Phenom.
notes: Media-friendly; frequent podcast guest on AI and HR tech. Press contact is Phenom's Director of PR, Jennifer Lyons (published on the newsroom). Topic fit is AI rather than energy/data centers.

name: Liu Yong
current_role: Founder, Chairman & President, DAS Solar (一道新能源), Quzhou, Zhejiang
profile: Solar-industry veteran who founded DAS Solar in Quzhou in August 2018, betting early on N-type TOPCon cells; it reached ~9th in global module shipments in 2024 (InfoLink). A planned ChiNext IPO was withdrawn in 2024, and in 2025 Quzhou's state-owned Quzhou Industrial Holding took control by buying a 17.46% stake plus Liu's voting proxy; he remains chairman.
interesting_fact: DAS Solar positions itself as an N-type TOPCon pioneer (lab cell efficiency >26%) and runs flagship 'scenario' projects such as desert ecological restoration in Gansu and fishery-PV integration in Hainan.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding DAS Solar he was a senior executive at two other leading PV makers, JA Solar and Jolywood (中来股份); company filings list his name in passport form as 'LIUYONG'.
notes: Common name - confirm via DAS Solar. Active on the conference circuit (Boao Forum 2024, Global Green Energy Leaders Dialogue) with English-language PR, so reachable via DAS Solar's international PR. Company now state-controlled (Quzhou Industrial Holding); unicorn valuation dates from Hurun 2021-25.

name: Alexandre Yazdi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Voodoo (Paris)
profile: Alexandre Yazdi, an engineering graduate (Polytech Nancy), co-founded Paris-based Voodoo with Laurent Ritter around 2012-13. Voodoo became one of the world's largest mobile game publishers through hyper-casual hits, backed by Goldman Sachs and Tencent at a ~$2B valuation, and has since expanded into consumer apps, including the social apps Wizz and BeReal.

profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris mobile-game publisher Voodoo with Alexandre Yazdi in 2013. Voodoo became a hyper-casual gaming giant (Goldman Sachs and Tencent invested) and was valued around $2B. Ritter is also an active angel investor in European startups.
interesting_fact: Voodoo, which he co-founded in 2013, grew from a small Paris studio into one of the world's most-downloaded mobile game publishers, popularising 'hyper-casual' games.

name: Omri Cohen
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Yotpo

Yotpo grew into an e-commerce retention platform (reviews, loyalty, SMS) used by Shopify brands and reached a $1.4B valuation in 2021; Cohen remains co-founder and COO as the company refocuses on reviews, loyalty and AI.

deep_cut_fact: Before Yotpo, Cohen worked on the ASIC team at Essence Security developing a future wireless MAC protocol, and earlier as a software engineer on a radio software team.

name: Tomer Tagrin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Yotpo
profile: Israeli entrepreneur Tomer Tagrin co-founded Yotpo with Omri Cohen in 2011. Yotpo is an e-commerce retention marketing platform for reviews, loyalty and, formerly, SMS/email, and reached a $1.4B valuation in 2021. He still runs it as CEO. In 2025 he refocused the company on Reviews, Loyalty and AI and bought CDP startup Coho AI.

name: Charles Hearn
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Alloy (New York)

As CTO he built the platform on AWS and still leads engineering.

Alloy provides identity verification, KYC/AML and fraud-prevention tooling to 900+ banks, credit unions and fintechs and was valued at about $1.55B in 2021. She serves as President and leads go-to-market and partnerships.

name: Tommy Nicholas

Alloy hit unicorn status in 2021 ($1.55B by 2022) and was on the 2025 Forbes Fintech 50; he still leads it as CEO.

His first startup, The City Swig (2011), offered real-time nightlife deals in Charlottesville.
notes: Coffitivity link supported by a Richmond Times-Dispatch reprint (names 'Nicholas', UVA grad at Shockoe.com) and his Wikipedia page; mention lightly. Alloy is a fintech, not energy; frequent podcast guest on fraud/AI in banking.

name: Etai Hochman
current_role: Co-founder of At-Bay (former CTO); co-founder and CTO of Mirato, acquired by Sayari in July 2025 (current title post-acquisition unconfirmed)
profile: Israeli engineer who co-founded cyber insurer At-Bay in 2016 with Rotem Iram and Roman Itskovich, serving as its first CTO; At-Bay pairs insurance with active security monitoring and reached unicorn status. He then co-founded Mirato (2018), an AI third-party risk management platform, with Aki Eldar; Mirato raised a $9M seed in 2021 and was bought by US risk-intelligence firm Sayari in 2025.
interesting_fact: He has built two companies in adjacent risk markets: At-Bay (cyber insurance + security monitoring) and Mirato, whose 'Risk Hunter' tool models how risk propagates across a company's supply chain; Mirato was acquired by Sayari in July 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Mirato's $9M 2021 seed round was led by Dov Moran's Grove Ventures (Moran invented the USB flash drive) with American Express Ventures participating, and Hochman was named CTO alongside CEO Aki Eldar, ex-CEO of Microsoft-acquired Secure Islands.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal social/website found. No longer operational at At-Bay (board observer/advisor per profiles). Current role at Sayari after the Mirato acquisition not confirmed. Education details (Bar-Ilan math, TAU MBA) only from aggregator profiles.

name: Roman Itskovich
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Risk Officer, At-Bay (cyber insurance, Mountain View/Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli-born co-founder of At-Bay (2016, with CEO Rotem Iram), a cyber insurer that pairs policies with active security monitoring ('insure-sec'). At-Bay has raised ~$295M from backers including Khosla, Lightspeed and M12 and reached unicorn status. As Chief Risk Officer he runs underwriting/risk and speaks publicly on cyber-market pricing discipline.

deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was VP of Financial Products at FX fintech Ebury, on Bain Capital's investment team, and a McKinsey consultant; he holds a BA in Economics and Accounting from Tel Aviv University and an HBS MBA.
notes: Has appeared on insurance podcasts (Behind the Growth, Making Risk Flow) - receptive to talking about cyber risk. Route via press@at-bay.com.

name: Rotem Iram
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, At-Bay (acquired by Munich Re, Aug 2026)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded cyber-insurance company At-Bay in 2016 with former McKinsey colleague Roman Itskovich; it pioneered 'InsurSec', pairing insurance with security scanning and monitoring, and hit a $1.35B valuation in 2021. Munich Re bought At-Bay for $575M in August 2026; Iram is based in Tel Aviv again after a decade in Palo Alto.
interesting_fact: He first ran into the cyber-insurance problem while at risk consultancy K2 Integrity after the Target data breach, which led to At-Bay's model of underwriting using external scans of client systems.
deep_cut_fact: Before McKinsey he was an officer in IDF Unit 8200 and a software engineer at RAD Data Communications, holds a computer-engineering BSc from the Hebrew University, and grew up in Herzliya after a childhood stint at Kibbutz Lehavot HaBashan.

She spent about 10 years as a partner at Greylock IL (now 83North) backing European and Israeli startups and now co-leads Pinegrove, a ~$10B multi-strategy venture platform spun out of SVB Capital.

He was interim CEO, then became CPO when ex-Comcast exec Daniel Herscovici was hired as CEO in April 2025.

profile: Wireless-systems engineer who co-founded Plume Design (2014), the cloud-managed home Wi-Fi platform used by ISPs and valued at about $2.6–3B. current_role: Co-founder (and longtime CEO) of Plume Design; Executive Chairman of Aliro (quantum networking) since June 2026
profile: Telecom entrepreneur who founded optical-networking firm Qtera, sold to Nortel in 2000 for $3.25B, then became a VC (Applied Materials Ventures, Sigma Partners). He co-founded Plume in 2014-15, building a cloud SaaS platform for smart home Wi-Fi sold through broadband providers, and in 2026 became executive chairman of quantum-networking startup Aliro.

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Signifyd
profile: Payments-risk veteran who co-founded Signifyd with Michael Liberty in 2011 after leading emerging-markets risk at PayPal. Signifyd sells guaranteed-fraud-protection and commerce-protection software to online retailers and reached unicorn status; Ramanand still leads it as CEO.
