name: Evan Doll
current_role: Rejoined Apple in 2016 as Director of Health Software Engineering (current role not confirmed by recent sources)
profile: Stanford 2003 grad who joined Apple as an engineer and worked on the original iPhone software (2003-2009). In 2010 he co-founded Flipboard, the magazine-style news app, with Mike McCue and led engineering/product; he left in 2015 for an EIR stint at Redpoint Ventures and returned to Apple in 2016 to direct health software engineering.
interesting_fact: Helped build the original iPhone's software as a senior iPhone engineer at Apple before leaving to co-found Flipboard, one of the breakout iPad apps of 2010.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Healdsburg, California (Healdsburg High class of 1999, senior class president). While at Apple he taught an iPhone app programming class on the side and persuaded management to let him keep teaching: 'Teaching is a way to gain mastery.'
notes: Low public profile since returning to Apple; no recent interviews or published contacts. Apple employees rarely do outside media without Apple PR approval.

name: Mike McCue
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Flipboard
profile: American tech entrepreneur who never attended college: founded Paper Software (sold to Netscape for $20M in 1996), co-founded voice-browser Tellme Networks (acquired by Microsoft in 2007), then co-founded the Flipboard news-magazine app in 2010, which he still leads and has pushed into the open social web/fediverse.
interesting_fact: He gave up a congressional nomination to the US Air Force Academy to support his family after his father died, joined IBM on a six-month temp contract in 1986 and stayed three and a half years.
deep_cut_fact: His Netscape project to turn Navigator into a web-based desktop OS was codenamed 'Constellation' after a boat his father helped restore; he later bought a 48-foot classic wooden sailboat and named it Constellation too. His first app was a space-shuttle flight simulator written in TI-BASIC in 1981.
notes: Media-friendly; frequent podcast guest on the open social web. Press contact is the 'Contact Us' link on Flipboard's press page.

name: Martin Tolar
current_role: Founder, President & CEO, Alzheon Inc. (Framingham, MA)
profile: Czech-born neurologist and neuroscientist who founded Alzheon in 2013 to develop ALZ-801, an oral tramiprosate-prodrug anti-amyloid Alzheimer's drug licensed from Bellus Health. Before that he was Yale neurology faculty, worked in business development at Pfizer, and ran CoMentis, NormOxys and Knome. He also founded Tolion Health, an AI brain-health company.
interesting_fact: He received his M.D. from Charles University in Prague, did a Ph.D. on apolipoprotein E in Alzheimer's, and was on The Medicine Maker's Power List 2016-2019.
deep_cut_fact: As a medical student in Prague he helped organize and lead the November 1989 Velvet Revolution that ended communist rule in Czechoslovakia; he later received the Czech Laurels Award (2021).
notes: Company email is a general corporate inbox, not a personal one. He sits on the CERGE-EI Foundation board, another possible warm route.

name: Eli Broverman
current_role: Co-founder, Treasury (early-stage fintech venture fund); co-founder of Betterment
profile: Securities lawyer who co-founded robo-advisor Betterment with Jon Stein in 2008, serving as President/COO and building its legal/regulatory structure, broker-dealer and 401(k) business. He stepped back from day-to-day operations in 2017 (staying on the board/advisory) and co-founded Treasury, an early-stage fintech fund with Acorns founders, which led Betterment's 2021 $60M Series F.
interesting_fact: Betterment's founders needed a lawyer willing to take risk: Stein realised automated advice needed a regulatory structure built from scratch, and Broverman, a lawyer who 'had been wanting to start something', built it at Stein's kitchen table.
deep_cut_fact: He first met Betterment co-founder Jon Stein at a poker table around 2003 - 'Little did I know that we would soon be working together at his kitchen table building a company...' He calls himself a masochist who loves a company's 'formative period'.
notes: Low public profile; no longer operational at Betterment so company press is an indirect route. Treasury fund (with Jeff Cruttenden/Acorns) is a better angle; Milken Institute speaker profile exists.

name: Jon Stein
current_role: Founder and chairman, Betterment (CEO 2008–Dec 2020); angel investor/advisor
profile: American fintech entrepreneur (Harvard BA, Columbia MBA) who founded Betterment, the pioneering robo-advisor, in 2008 after ~4 years at First Manhattan Consulting Group. He was CEO until December 2020, when ex-Viacom COO Sarah Levy succeeded him; he remains founder/chairman and advises and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: He launched Betterment on stage at TechCrunch's 2008 Startup Battlefield in the middle of the financial crisis, betting big banks would be distracted by lost trust; he was named to Fortune's 40 Under 40 in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: For the TechCrunch launch pitch he memorized his speech and practiced it about 50 times (he says he never memorized a speech again), overdressed, and got teased by Michael Arrington about his tie; Betterment's servers went live for the first time that day.
notes: Current day-to-day activities after stepping down as CEO are not well documented; a profile site mentions a new venture called 'Warmer' but this is unverified. In 2020 he said his next startup would not be in finance.

name: Eric Cheng
current_role: Co-Founder, Chairman & Group CEO, CARSOME (Kuala Lumpur)
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur who co-founded CARSOME in 2015 with Innity colleague Teoh Jiun Ee. It grew into Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform (Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore) and Malaysia's first tech unicorn, valued around $1.7B in 2021. He leads group strategy and sits on Endeavor Malaysia's board.
interesting_fact: An accounting-degree dropout, Cheng says he 'wasn't the smartest kid in the family'; Carsome was his third company after two short-lived ventures. He was EY Emerging Entrepreneur of the Year Malaysia 2019.
deep_cut_fact: In 2011 he started Clicks Communications, an ad network and creative agency, but sold his stake back to his co-founders within a year because he felt he had left Innity too soon - and went back to lead Innity's digital ad team before founding Carsome. His first venture (2008) was a print magazine with college friends.
notes: Active in SEA startup community and Endeavor Malaysia; Endeavor is a possible warm route.

name: Jiun Ee Teoh
current_role: Co-founder, CARSOME; CEO of CARSOME Academy
profile: Malaysian entrepreneur (known as 'JT') who co-founded CARSOME with Eric Cheng in 2015; it became Southeast Asia's largest integrated used-car e-commerce platform and Malaysia's first tech unicorn. A former COO and Chief Business Development Officer, he now runs CARSOME Academy, its accredited automotive training institution across Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand.
interesting_fact: CARSOME started in 2015 as an advertising platform and pivoted through trial and error to a used-car marketplace; the founders now preach that 'growth at all costs isn't a good mindset' after steering it to profitability.
deep_cut_fact: As CEO of CARSOME Academy he has spearheaded training partnerships with Sunway University, UniMAP, Beijing Business School, IUKL and Malaysia's MCMC; the academy has trained 1,500+ students and 6,500 corporate employees as automotive technicians.
notes: Eric Cheng is the public face of CARSOME; Teoh's background before CARSOME was in digital media.

name: Yin Jing
current_role: Founder and CEO, Cloudwise (云智慧, Beijing) - AIOps / IT operations and observability software
profile: Listed by Hurun as 'Yin Jing', the Cloudwise founder is Yin Jin (殷晋, 'Andy Yin'), CEO since 2010. Cloudwise began with the Jiankongbao (监控宝) website-monitoring SaaS for small businesses and grew into an AI-driven IT-operations platform for large enterprises; Sequoia China led its US$150m Series E in 2021, valuing it at about US$1bn.
interesting_fact: Cloudwise now pitches itself as 'Reliability for AI Infrastructure', selling AI agents for alert triage and autonomous incident resolution to 2,000+ enterprises.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cloudwise became an enterprise AIOps vendor, Yin co-founded and ran Jiankongbao (监控宝), one of China's early SaaS tools for monitoring small-business websites.
notes: Name discrepancy: Hurun 'Yin Jing' vs filings/press 'Yin Jin' (殷晋) / Andy Yin; same Cloudwise founder. The marketing mailbox is the international (Singapore) arm's published address; the Chinese site cloudwise.com was unreachable from here.

name: Lv Shijie
current_role: Founder, Cloudwise (云智慧), Beijing-based AIOps/observability software company
profile: Lv Shijie (吕士杰, Shijie Lyu) founded Cloudwise in Beijing in 2009, starting in application performance monitoring and growing into an AI operations platform (observability, incident resolution, ITSM/CMDB) used by 2,000+ enterprises. Hurun counted him among unicorn founders in 2021 when Cloudwise was valued at ~$1bn; the company now markets itself as 'reliability for AI infrastructure'.
interesting_fact: Cloudwise has repositioned from classic APM to AIOps for AI infrastructure, pitching AI agents that find root causes of IT incidents in seconds, a direct play on data-center reliability.
notes: Founder identity per CB Insights (lists Shijie Lyu as founder); some databases give other founder names (Yin Jin co-founder). Little English-language coverage of him personally; current title not confirmed. Company contact form is the published route.

name: Philip Kaplan
current_role: Founder, DistroKid; also makes small-batch headphones (Pud's Small Batch Headphones)
profile: Philip 'Pud' Kaplan (b. 1975) is a serial internet entrepreneur: dot-com-era satirist (Fucked Company, 2000), founder of ad network AdBrite (2004), creator of TinyLetter (sold to Mailchimp 2011) and of Fandalism, which became DistroKid in 2013. DistroKid, the flat-fee music distributor he calls the biggest in the world, was valued around $1.3B after a 2021 Insight Partners investment.
interesting_fact: Since 2024 he has gone viral on Reddit building wild novelty headphones (Helmholtz resonators, wine-cork damping, a built-in CD player, a water-pump 'rain' pair) that he sells in tiny batches from pud.com.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote a children's picture book about audio, 'Music Production ABCs', published by DistroKid, and is a drummer in the death-metal side project Butchers of the Final Frontier.
notes: Very online and approachable via X (@pud) and his headphone site; Syracuse iSchool '97, gave its 2014 convocation address. DistroKid valuation detail per press reports (Insight Partners 2021).

name: Oren Zaslansky
current_role: Founder & CEO, Flock Freight (San Diego-area shared-truckload freight company)
profile: San Diego native who grew up around the freight business, started a truckload carrier at 21, then ran a brokerage before founding Flock Freight in 2014-15. Flock pools LTL-sized shipments into 'shared truckloads' using software, avoiding hub-and-spoke terminals; it became a $1B+ unicorn and raised a $60M Series E led by O'Neil Strategic Capital in May 2025.
interesting_fact: Flock Freight describes itself as the largest shared-truckload (STL) freight brokerage in the U.S., moving pooled freight on one truck without terminal transfers to cut damage and emissions.
deep_cut_fact: He told Heavy Duty Trucking 'I was born into freight' - his childhood dinner-table talk was freight bills and flatbeds - and he started his own truckload company at age 21.
notes: One listing calls him Founder & Executive Chairman; most 2025-26 sources say Founder & CEO - confirm title. Frequent logistics-podcast guest (Logistics of Logistics, Alejandro Cremades).

name: Zhang Shijie
current_role: Chief Scientist, GalaxySpace (银河航天), per Chinese press; not the company's founder/CEO
profile: Hurun lists Zhang Shijie (张世杰) as a GalaxySpace founder, but public reporting names Xu Ming (ex-Cheetah Mobile CTO/president) as GalaxySpace's founder, chairman and CEO (22% stake, ~73% voting control). Zhang is quoted as GalaxySpace's chief scientist, describing its stackable flat-panel satellites and ~1mm-thick flexible solar wings. GalaxySpace began A-share IPO tutoring in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Zhang has explained that GalaxySpace builds stackable flat-panel satellites with foldable solar wings over 2.5m wide but only ~1mm thick, so dozens of satellites can be stacked and launched at once to cut per-satellite launch cost.
notes: Hurun attribution looks off: GalaxySpace's founder is Xu Ming (徐鸣). A Harbin Institute of Technology satellite professor named Zhang Shijie (b.1979) exists, but no source links him to GalaxySpace - same-name risk, so not used. Company IPO prep reported by cls.cn (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2330307).

name: Shen Ronghua
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of GalaxySpace (银河航天), the Beijing satellite-internet/LEO constellation company. Public sources name Xu Ming (ex-Cheetah Mobile co-founder/CTO) as GalaxySpace's founder, chairman and CEO, with Gao Qianfeng and Liu Chang as co-founders; no public record links a 'Shen Ronghua' to the company.
notes: Identity could not be confirmed -- possibly a Hurun romanisation error or a minor shareholder. GalaxySpace founder is Xu Ming (徐鸣); the company filed for A-share IPO tutoring in March 2026 (https://www.cls.cn/detail/2330307). Verify Chinese name before any outreach.

name: Elia Wallen
current_role: Founder and CEO, Engine (formerly Hotel Engine), Denver, Colorado
profile: Denver entrepreneur who founded corporate-housing firm Travelers Haven in 2008, then spun its hotel-booking side into Hotel Engine (independent in 2018). Rebranded Engine in 2024 after a Series C (~$140M), it now books hotels, flights and cars for businesses and is valued around $2B. Wallen left the Travelers Haven CEO role in 2020 to run Engine full time.
interesting_fact: Engine grew out of Travelers Haven customers asking for help booking hotels; Wallen was named ColoradoBiz Magazine's CEO of the Year in December 2024.
deep_cut_fact: In June 2017, long before the unicorn round, EY named Wallen an Entrepreneur Of The Year award winner (hospitality, Mountain Desert region) at a gala at the Denver Center for the Performing Arts; Travelers Haven had placed 20,000+ traveling professionals in 2016 alone.
notes: Writes occasional Inc. columns (e.g., Nov 2025) on company-building lessons. Engine press room is the best route.

name: Abhinav Shashank
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Innovaccer
profile: IIT Kharagpur graduate who co-founded Innovaccer (with Kanav Hasija and Sandeep Gupta) as a data analytics startup and pivoted it to healthcare around 2016. Innovaccer, based in San Francisco, became India-origin's first healthtech unicorn and now sells an AI/data platform and agents for US health systems.
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2017 (Enterprise Tech) and has published 300+ articles in international media outlets.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Kanav Hasija were IIT Kharagpur batchmates who graduated in 2010; Abhinav then spent about three years at Ingersoll (Rand) working alongside future co-founder Sandeep Gupta before starting the company.
notes: Active on LinkedIn and frequent media contributor; press team handles interview requests.

name: Kanav Hasija
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Customer Officer (previously Chief Product Officer), Innovaccer (San Francisco)
profile: IIT Kharagpur graduate who co-founded healthcare data/AI company Innovaccer with Abhinav Shashank and Sandeep Gupta. He built the company's Data Activation Platform underlying its Health Cloud. Innovaccer raised a US$275M Series F in Jan 2025 (backers incl. B Capital, Kaiser Permanente, M12), with press estimates above US$3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Innovaccer's Series F in January 2025 drew strategic health-system investors such as Kaiser Permanente and Banner Health alongside Microsoft's M12 and Danaher Ventures.
deep_cut_fact: An engineer by training, he went to the US after IIT Kharagpur to earn a master's in patent law at the University of New Hampshire; as an undergrad he interned at General Electric and was a principal consultant at the student-run Kharagpur Consulting Group.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Abhinav Shashank. Press email is the named press contact on Innovaccer's Jan 2025 release; may change.

name: Sandeep K Gupta
current_role: Co-founder & President (formerly COO), Innovaccer
profile: Co-founder of Innovaccer, the San Francisco-based healthcare data platform (India's first health-tech unicorn, valued ~$3-4B). An engineer with an MBA in finance from IIM Ahmedabad, he ran operations and is credited with helping drive ~100% revenue CAGR; he now serves as President.
interesting_fact: Innovaccer grew out of a Wharton/Harvard data-analytics research project on combining distributed datasets; Gupta met co-founder Abhinav Shashank while both worked at Ingersoll Rand.
notes: Common name; identified via Innovaccer leadership page. Low personal public profile.

name: Ren Yuancheng
current_role: Executive director (formerly chairman and CEO), Xinmai Semiconductor Technology (Hangzhou) Co. (芯迈半导体), which is seeking a Hong Kong IPO
profile: Ren Yuancheng (任远程), about 50, a power-electronics engineer, founded Xinmai Semiconductor in Hangzhou in 2019-20: a 'virtual IDM' power-chip firm backed by CATL and Xiaomi and valued around RMB 20bn (~$3bn). He was chairman/CEO until June 2025 (now executive director); the firm filed for a Hong Kong IPO a third time in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Xinmai's valuation went from a RMB 100m pre-money in August 2020 to RMB 5bn less than a month later, and reached about RMB 20bn within roughly three years, with CATL and Xiaomi among its investors.
deep_cut_fact: He holds bachelor's and master's degrees in engineering from Zhejiang University and a 2005 Virginia Tech PhD in electrical engineering. He ran a China subsidiary of Monolithic Power Systems (2006-13), then was VP at JoulWatt, and was named a provincial 'leading talent' by Hangzhou's Binjiang high-tech zone in 2014.
notes: Identity match is inferred: Hurun lists 'Jupiter' as a $3B semiconductor unicorn. Ren Yuancheng = 任远程, founder of Xinmai Semiconductor (valued about RMB 20bn, roughly $3B). I could not confirm 'Jupiter' as Xinmai's English name, so verify before outreach. No published contact found; the HKEX prospectus would list company contacts.

name: David Arana
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Konfío (Mexico City)
profile: Mexican fintech founder who left a VP role structuring Latin American credit derivatives at Deutsche Bank (NY) in March 2013 to co-found Konfío with Francisco Padilla. Konfío provides data-driven loans, corporate cards and SaaS tools to Mexican SMEs and reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021; it has pursued a banking licence.
interesting_fact: MIT mathematics graduate; Konfío's early model was to lend to small firms that micro-finance (group lending) and banks both ignored, using alternative data for underwriting.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2016 LAVCA interview he said he and Padilla first 'started building something basic' to lend to tiny companies just to see 'if we would get the money back' - Konfío began as a viability test, not a grand plan.
notes: Konfío press releases route media via named staff and the agency 'another'; no general press inbox found. Speaker at AS/COA and IFC podcasts.

name: Francisco Padilla
current_role: Co-founder of Konfío (Mexico City SME lender); described as growth director / formerly CTO
profile: Mexican technologist who co-founded Konfío in 2013 with David Arana, building its AI-driven self-service SME credit platform; Konfío became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.3B valuation) and has since obtained a banking licence. Padilla has held CTO/CIO and growth-director titles; Arana is CEO.
interesting_fact: Konfío's very first loan, for 10,000 pesos, was made in January 2014; by 2024-25 the company was disbursing more than 17 billion pesos and had backed ~80,000 businesses.
deep_cut_fact: A 2007 Tec de Monterrey computer-technologies grad, he met co-founder David Arana while both worked at MicroStrategy in New York (Citibank was its biggest client) during the 2008 crisis; his parents, both systems engineers, advised him not to quit.
notes: Low public profile compared with CEO David Arana; current exact title unclear (El CEO interview calls him cofundador y director de crecimiento: https://elceo.com/negocios/konfio-del-unicornio-fintech-al-reto-de-convertirse-en-banco/). Best route via Konfío corporate comms.

name: Alexander Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder of Marshmallow (London car-insurance insurtech); per 2021 coverage he leads internal culture and product while his twin Oliver handles external matters
profile: British entrepreneur from south-west London who co-founded Marshmallow with his identical twin Oliver and engineer David Goaté. Marshmallow is a licensed UK car insurer that uses data to price cover for people traditional insurers turn away, such as recent migrants and drivers with thin credit files. It became a unicorn in 2021 with an $85M Series B at a $1.25B valuation.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow was only the second UK start-up with Black founders to be valued at more than $1 billion, after WorldRemit.
deep_cut_fact: Marshmallow was first incorporated in 2016 under the name 'Twin Thinking'. For its first 10 months the team worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym on an £80 membership ('a desk plus a sauna and a steam room').
notes: His twin Oliver is the usual press voice, so Alexander gives few interviews. I found no published press email for Marshmallow; the gym anecdote is quoted from Oliver in the Evening Standard (syndicated on Yahoo). I could not verify his current title.

name: David Goate
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Marshmallow (UK insurtech)
profile: Software engineer David Goate co-founded London car insurer Marshmallow in 2017 with twins Alexander and Oliver Kent-Braham and is its CTO. It began by insuring migrants and expats who were overcharged by traditional insurers. It became a unicorn in 2021 with an $85M round at a $1.25B valuation, and later raised at a higher valuation.
interesting_fact: In 2018 the startup won a trademark battle against S&P 500 giant Marsh McLennan over the name 'Marshmallow', which the British press cast as David vs. Goliath. The FT ranked it Europe's 2nd-fastest-growing company in 2023 (660% CAGR).
deep_cut_fact: Goate and the Kent-Braham twins all previously worked at digital-identity company Yoti. The company was first incorporated in 2016 as 'Twin Thinking' and was renamed Marshmallow Technology in 2017, when the team went full time working from a gym (a Virgin Active lobby).
notes: Co-CEO twins are the public faces; Goate keeps a low profile. No published press email found (press page is JS-rendered). Sources for the gym and Twin Thinking details: Wikipedia and Yahoo Finance UK (au.finance.yahoo.com/news/entrepreneurs-tech-twins-behind-marshmallow-113830484.html).

name: Oliver Kent-Braham
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (also described as co-CEO), Marshmallow (UK car and home insurer for newcomers)
profile: Oliver Kent-Braham is a south-west Londoner and briefly a banker at Investec. In 2017 he co-founded Marshmallow with his twin Alexander and engineer David Goate to make car insurance fairer for people who have moved to the UK. Marshmallow became a licensed insurer in 2021. Its April 2025 $90M raise valued it at about $2B, with roughly 1M customers and a ~$500M revenue run rate.
interesting_fact: Marshmallow insures roughly one million people, up from about 100,000 in 2021, and says it is profitable on a ~$500M annual revenue run rate. Kent-Braham calls migration 'a huge opportunity'.
deep_cut_fact: In the early days the founders worked from the lobby of a Virgin Active gym. Kent-Braham paid for an £80 membership, which got the team a desk plus sauna and steam room access: 'the cheapest office space'. The idea came from a Canadian friend who kept getting sky-high car insurance quotes.
notes: His twin Alexander is the other co-founder (internal/product side); Oliver handles external matters and fundraising. No press email was found on marshmallow.com. Sources vary on the founding year (2016 or 2017).

name: Ilan Atias
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Melio (B2B payments; acquired by Xero in 2025) - current status post-acquisition unverified
profile: Israeli engineer who co-founded Melio in 2018 with Matan Bar and others, serving as CTO and running its Tel Aviv R&D centre. Melio, a bill-pay platform for US small businesses, was acquired by New Zealand's Xero for about $2.5B, completing in October 2025.
interesting_fact: When Melio hired an R&D chief in 2022, Atias said platform processing volume was 'surging to tens of billions of dollars annually'; Xero later bought Melio for about $2.5B.
notes: Search snippets suggest he may have left Melio after the Xero deal (unverified). Prior role reportedly VP R&D at maritime-AI firm Windward (aggregator sources only, not verified).

name: Matan Bar
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Melio; leads the combined Xero/Melio US business after Xero's acquisition (completed Oct 2025)
profile: Haifa-born Israeli founder who studied computer science at Tel Aviv University, co-founded The Gifts Project (sold to eBay), then spent six years at PayPal leading global consumer P2P payments. He co-founded Melio, a US SMB bill-pay platform, with Ilan Atias and Ziv Paz; Xero bought it for $2.5B upfront in 2025, its largest-ever deal.
interesting_fact: Xero agreed to buy Melio for US$2.5B upfront in June 2025 (up to ~$3B with earn-outs); Bar was slated to lead the combined US business reporting to Xero CEO Sukhinder Singh Cassidy.
deep_cut_fact: Melio's original idea was called 'Payper' (pay per check) - the team would mail paper checks for businesses. His first startup, The Gifts Project, was started in his last university semester at 24 with Ron Gura and sold to eBay when he was 26.
notes: Has appeared on many podcasts (Aleph 'Invested', Fintech Leaders, Founder Real Talk) - podcast-friendly.

name: Ziv Paz
current_role: Co-founder (non-operational) of Melio (former COO); current venture not verified
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Melio, a B2B payments platform for small businesses, in 2018 with Matan Bar and Ilan Atias. As COO and the company's number two he led operations and go-to-market. He gave up his operational role in 2021. Xero agreed in 2025 to buy Melio for up to $3B, and CTech reported that each co-founder holds about 9%.
interesting_fact: He was the only Melio founder without a technology background. He studied law and accounting after long service in the IDF naval commando unit Shayetet 13.
deep_cut_fact: He spent 2.5 years as a VP at FIMI Opportunity Funds and was on track to run a portfolio company and return as a partner. He left instead to start Melio with Matan Bar, his childhood school friend from Haifa.
notes: Left his operational role at Melio in 2021 (https://www.calcalistech.com/ctech/articles/0,7340,L-3923561,00.html). Melio is now part of Xero. An aggregator says he started a new company in 2024; I could not verify this. No published contact found; LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Alex Buttle
current_role: Co-founder, Motorway (UK online used-car selling platform)
profile: UK serial entrepreneur who co-founded Motorway in July 2017 with Tom Leathes and Harry Jones, a team that had already built several startups together including the UK's biggest broadband price-comparison site (acquired by uSwitch). Motorway connects car sellers with 8,000+ verified dealers and passed a $1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Motorway's founding trio has worked together since meeting in 2002; Motorway is their fifth startup together, after ventures including a broadband comparison site, a travel accommodation curation site and an office-space search site.
deep_cut_fact: Writing as a Motorway director in a City AM debate column, Buttle argued that 2035 was too soon for the UK to ban new petrol and diesel car sales.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Tom Leathes is the company's usual spokesperson. Exact current title not listed on motorway.co.uk/about (an earlier version listed him as Co-founder & VP Growth per search snippet).

name: Harry Jones
current_role: Co-founder, Motorway (former Chief Product Officer; current operating role not confirmed)
profile: Harry Jones co-founded Motorway, the London-based online used-car marketplace connecting private sellers with dealers, with Tom Leathes (CEO) and Alex Buttle; it reached a ~$1B valuation. Motorway was the trio's fifth startup together. TechCrunch notes Jones is no longer Motorway's CPO; no new venture was confirmed.
interesting_fact: Motorway began as a simple instant car-valuation price-comparison site; the team then cold-called dealers to find buyers before pivoting to its dealer marketplace model. Jones: 'That pivot was really critical in how we kind of evolved the company.'
deep_cut_fact: Jones, Leathes and Buttle met in 2002 and have built five startups together (two acquired), with earlier ideas including a travel-accommodation curation service and an office-space search site; their method is to ship cheap one-page websites fast and double down on whatever gets traction.
notes: Common name; ensure outreach targets the Motorway co-founder. Tom Leathes is Motorway's public face; Jones has stepped back from CPO role.

name: Tom Leathes
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Motorway (UK used-car marketplace)
profile: British serial entrepreneur who co-founded Motorway with long-time partners Harry Jones and Alex Buttle; Motorway lets consumers sell cars to a network of dealers and reached a ~$1B valuation. Motorway is the trio's fifth startup after Acre (recruitment), LoanCube, Official Space and Top10 (a hotel recommendation app closed in 2015).
interesting_fact: He and his co-founders have worked together for about 20 years; three of their earlier startups had 'moderately successful' exits, and he calls Motorway's success the product of '20 years of building start-ups, making mistakes and learning from them.'
deep_cut_fact: Motorway began after the founders spent about six months in an office deciding what to build; they launched an instant car-valuation website, then phoned sellers and cold-called dealers themselves to place cars. Leathes joked he's 'glad they're not recorded.'
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Secret Leaders, Riding Unicorns); Motorway press office is the published route.

name: Amir Nathoo
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Outschool (stepped back as CEO in Feb 2026; Brian Co named CEO Sept 2026)
profile: UK-raised, Cambridge-educated engineer who worked at IBM, co-founded mobile dev platform Trigger.io (acquired by Square in 2013), then co-founded Outschool in 2015, a marketplace for live online classes for kids valued at $3B in 2021. In Feb 2026 he stepped back from leading Outschool to start 'a new personal journey'.
interesting_fact: Outschool says it has offered 100,000+ live online classes to over 1 million learners in 196 countries, and Nathoo set aside equity in the company for teachers' benefit.
deep_cut_fact: After Square acquired his startup Trigger.io in 2013, Nathoo spent about 15 months there as a product manager and founded a new product line, Square Payroll, before leaving in 2015 to start Outschool.
notes: Now between roles after leaving the CEO job; may be more open to podcast invites. No published personal/press email found.

name: Mikhail Seregine
current_role: Co-founder, Outschool (current operating role not confirmed)
profile: Former Google employee who co-founded Outschool in 2015 with CEO Amir Nathoo and ex-Airbnb engineer Nick Grandy. The Y Combinator-backed San Francisco platform offers live small-group online classes for kids; it boomed in the pandemic, reaching unicorn status in April 2021 and a $3B valuation after a $110M Tiger Global-led Series D in Oct 2021.
interesting_fact: Outschool went from first class in 2017 to a $3 billion valuation in October 2021, after pandemic school closures drove a surge in demand; Lightspeed invested at the Series B in 2020.
notes: Very low public profile: no interviews, personal site or verified social accounts found. Aggregator profiles mention Google product/engineering roles (unverified detail). No published press email found on outschool.com; route via Outschool company channels.

name: Nick Grandy
current_role: Co-founder, Outschool (listed elsewhere as Head of Product; current title not confirmed)
profile: Nick Grandy co-founded Outschool, the San Francisco online marketplace for live small-group children's classes, in 2015 with Amir Nathoo and Mikhail Seregine. He came from Airbnb's engineering team. Outschool grew sharply during COVID and reached a $3B valuation in its October 2021 Series D. In February 2026 Nathoo stepped down as CEO and the COO and CTO took over as co-leaders.
interesting_fact: During COVID Outschool's business grew about 15x, and it went from 1,000 to 6,000 teachers in six months, Grandy said in a 2021 interview.
deep_cut_fact: Grandy was a high school teacher early in his career and then joined Airbnb's early team. He says Airbnb gave him his appreciation for peer-to-peer marketplaces, the model Outschool uses for education.
notes: Low public profile. Nathoo's February 2026 leadership-transition letter thanks Grandy as a co-founder but does not give his current role. Aggregator education details (Harvard/Oxford) were not verified and are left out.

name: Chaitanya Kanojia
current_role: Co-founder of Starry (fixed-wireless broadband); stepped down as CEO in June 2023 and was reported to stay on the board
profile: Chaitanya 'Chet' Kanojia is a Boston-area serial telecom/media entrepreneur. He ran Navic Networks, an advanced TV advertising firm Microsoft acquired in 2008. He then founded Aereo, a cloud-antenna TV service, followed by Starry, a fixed-wireless home internet provider founded around 2014 that listed via SPAC in 2022. He handed Starry's CEO role to COO Alex Moulle-Berteaux in June 2023.
interesting_fact: His earlier startup Aereo, which put an over-the-air TV antenna and DVR in the cloud, took its fight with broadcasters all the way to the US Supreme Court. He then built Starry as his next attempt to disrupt incumbent networks.
deep_cut_fact: Some of his investors at FirstMark have known him for about 20 years. He told TechCrunch he wanted backers who had 'seen that movie', meaning stayed with a company from seed stage all the way to IPO.
notes: Starry went through Chapter 11 in 2023 and was taken private; avoid this topic in outreach. In the 2023 transition post he said he wanted to dedicate more time to his family. His current activity is unclear. Highly relevant to a telecom/infrastructure podcast.

name: Austin Woodward
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, TaxBit (CEO until June 2023)
profile: Accountant-turned-founder who co-founded Utah-based TaxBit in 2017 with his brother Justin, a tax attorney, to automate tax reporting for crypto/digital assets. As CEO he raised about $230M (Paradigm, Tiger Global, IVP, Insight) and built enterprise and government businesses; in June 2023 he handed the CEO role to COO Lindsey Argalas and became chairman.
interesting_fact: TaxBit's $100M Series A in 2021, led by Paradigm and Tiger Global, was reported as the largest Series A in Utah history.
deep_cut_fact: He prefers the term 'digital assets' over 'cryptocurrency' because it covers more, and has said running a business is 'brutally transparent and honest'.
notes: The press email comes from a June 2023 TaxBit release. Secondary sources (podcast notes and directories) say he was a CPA and an early Qualtrics hire, but no primary source confirmed it, so it is not used above. His involvement has been chairman-level since 2023.

name: Bobby Clayson
current_role: Founder, Crofter Market (former co-founder/founding engineer, TaxBit)
profile: Utah entrepreneur and self-taught software engineer (V School coding bootcamp) who co-founded crypto tax/compliance software company TaxBit in 2018 with CPA Austin Woodward; TaxBit later pivoted to enterprise and government customers and passed a $1B valuation. He has since left TaxBit and founded Crofter Market, an online marketplace linking consumers with local regenerative farmers.
interesting_fact: Austin Woodward recruited him after hearing his talks on blockchain and smart contracts at a Utah cryptocurrency investment meetup.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he worked as a wildland firefighter and in sales; he was the eighth employee (a B2B sales rep) at Utah startup SpinGo, where watching engineers inspired him to learn to code.
notes: No longer at TaxBit; now runs Crofter Market (profiled on MountainWest Capital Network's Winners' Circle podcast, Feb 2026: https://www.mwcn.org/?p=15719). No published contact found; best route likely via Crofter Market.

name: Brandon Woodward
current_role: Co-founder, TaxBit (Taxbit); current day-to-day role not confirmed
profile: Brandon Woodward co-founded TaxBit in Utah in 2017 with his cousins Austin Woodward (CEO) and Justin Woodward. TaxBit started as crypto tax software and now provides tax compliance and information-reporting software for digital assets and the gig economy. It raised $130M at a $1.33B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: TechCrunch reported that brothers Austin and Justin Woodward founded TaxBit with their cousin Brandon in 2017. The family team paired CPAs and tax attorneys with software developers from day one.
notes: Very low public profile; secondary sources describe his background as front-end development and design, but I couldn't confirm that from a primary source. Releases carry media contacts (media@/press@taxbit.com, agency Wachsman), but none could be confirmed on a fetched page, so none are listed. Best route is via the company or CEO Austin Woodward.

name: Justin Woodward
current_role: Co-founder (tax attorney), Taxbit, Salt Lake City
profile: Utah tax attorney who co-founded Taxbit, the crypto/digital-asset tax and information-reporting software company, with his brother Austin Woodward (CPA, ex-Qualtrics) and cousin Brandon Woodward. Taxbit raised a $100M Series A in 2021 and became a unicorn, serving exchanges, enterprises and government agencies.
interesting_fact: His brother Austin calls him 'one of the youngest law grads at University of Chicago ever' and says Justin was already working on cryptocurrency tax issues for Fortune 500 companies in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Before Taxbit he was a judicial law clerk for U.S. District Judge Dale Kimball (handling matters incl. cryptocurrency civil forfeiture) and earlier a 'Cyber Currencies Project Leader' at Kirkland & Ellis.
notes: media@taxbit.com is from a 2021 release; current press page only links a contact form. Has appeared on the Wharton FinTech podcast with Austin (2021).

name: Li Zhan
current_role: Founder & CEO, Tungee (探迹科技), Guangzhou
profile: Li Zhan (黎展) is a serial entrepreneur who studied software engineering and business administration at Sun Yat-sen University and worked on personalized-recommendation research in Tencent's cloud platform division. He founded Tungee in Guangzhou in 2016; it sells AI-driven B2B sales software (lead mining, outreach, CRM) and raised from backers including Sequoia China and Qiming.
interesting_fact: Tungee's sales search engine claims coverage of 300M+ Chinese market entities, 9M+ factories and 300M+ tender notices, and now markets a 'Sales Agent' AI product.
deep_cut_fact: Before Tungee he was CEO of an earlier startup, Jiaxue (佳学); he placed second nationally in the Microsoft Elite Challenge, was a Microsoft outstanding MSP (student partner), and was the youngest member of the Great Wall Club.
notes: No published press email; company site lists only a sales hotline and a recruitment email. Chinese-language outreach likely best; WeChat official account is the main company channel.

name: Chen Kairan
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Tungee (探迹科技), Guangzhou
profile: Chen Kairan (陈开冉) holds a software-engineering master's from Sun Yat-sen University and was CTO of Jiaxue before co-founding Tungee with CEO Li Zhan in 2016. Tungee sells AI-driven B2B sales SaaS built on a knowledge graph of 100M+ companies and says it has served over 50,000 businesses. He leads its industrial-AI push.
interesting_fact: He built Tungee's two data foundations: the 'Kuanghu' cloud of external industry data (factories, tenders, customs, supply chains) and the 'Taiqing' platform for clients' internal data. Tungee also built ShopGLM, its own e-commerce large model.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Tungee, he did AI research at a university national laboratory and was a researcher on a Ministry of Education-funded data-mining project, specializing in boosting and neural-network algorithms. In 2026 he said: 'Technology itself has no warmth; the warmth lies in the direction of its application.'
notes: Sources call him CTO/co-founder; Li Zhan (黎展) is CEO and the company's public face. The 2026 interview argues for measuring AI by 'token efficiency'. The site lists a general sales hotline and only a recruitment email.

name: Michael Wolff Jensen
current_role: EVP & Chief Legal Officer, Ascendis Pharma; Chairman, VISEN Pharmaceuticals and Vicore Pharma (per Ascendis bio)
profile: Danish lawyer and biotech executive, a long-time leader at Ascendis Pharma (board chairman 2008-2021, acting CFO 2008-2013, CLO since 2013, EVP since 2023). He chairs VISEN Pharmaceuticals, the China joint venture Ascendis set up to bring its TransCon endocrine drugs to Greater China, which Hurun counts as a $1B unicorn. Earlier he was CFO of Genmab and LifeCycle Pharma.
interesting_fact: Before Ascendis's rise he was CFO of Genmab (2000-2003) and of LifeCycle Pharma (2003-2008), and chaired the Ascendis board for 13 years.
deep_cut_fact: An energy-sector detour: from 2010 to 2013 he was Senior Legal Advisor and Head of Partnerships (France) in the renewable-energy division of Orsted (formerly DONG Energy), alongside his Ascendis work.
notes: Hurun lists him as VISEN 'founder'; he is its chairman (joined at Series B). An aggregator noted VISEN directorate changes effective 27 June 2025, so confirm he is still chairman. VISEN's site no longer names him.

name: Kannan Muthukkaruppan
current_role: Co-founder and President of Yugabyte (distributed PostgreSQL database); some profiles list him as co-CEO with Karthik Ranganathan
profile: Database engineer. He spent 13 years on Oracle's PL/SQL compiler, then at Facebook built the HBase storage behind Messages, then worked on distributed storage at Nutanix. In 2016 he co-founded Yugabyte, maker of the open-source distributed SQL database YugabyteDB, with ex-Facebook colleagues Karthik Ranganathan and Mikhail Bautin, and was its founding CEO.
interesting_fact: He was the founding CEO of Yugabyte. In 2020 he handed the CEO role to Pivotal's ex-president Bill Cook and moved to President, Product Development. Before Yugabyte he spent about 13 years on Oracle's PL/SQL compiler and virtual machine team.
deep_cut_fact: He wrote Facebook's 2010 engineering post 'The Underlying Technology of Messages'. It explained why the team picked HBase over MySQL and Cassandra after weeks of benchmarking, to serve 350M users sending 15B+ messages a month.
notes: A technical founder who speaks at developer conferences (QCon, AsiaTechX). Sources conflict on his title (President vs co-CEO) and on whether Karthik Ranganathan is now sole CEO (May 2026 release), so confirm before outreach. The PR address was found through search excerpts of Business Wire releases; the pages themselves were blocked.

name: Karthik Ranganathan
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Yugabyte (previously CTO)
profile: Karthik Ranganathan (BS IIT Madras, MS UT Austin) was one of Facebook's early database engineers from 2007, working on Cassandra and as an Apache HBase committer. In 2016 he co-founded Yugabyte with ex-Facebook colleagues Kannan Muthukkaruppan and Mikhail Bautin to build YugabyteDB, an open-source, Postgres-compatible distributed SQL database for cloud-native and AI workloads.
interesting_fact: When he joined Facebook in 2007 it had roughly 30-40 million monthly users; by the time he left about six years later it had passed one billion, an experience that shaped YugabyteDB's focus on scale.
deep_cut_fact: He worked on Facebook's inbox-search store before it was open-sourced and is credited with naming it 'Cassandra'; he has been quoted saying he was 'fortunate enough to have given it its name'.
notes: Very accessible technical founder; frequent conference speaker (QCon, PGConf, Postgres Conference) and podcast guest (Last Week in AWS). Cassandra-naming claim comes from secondary profiles, so verify or soften before quoting it to him. Good data-infrastructure fit.

name: Mikhail Bautin
current_role: Engineer at Google Cloud (Cloud SQL), reportedly since Nov 2024; co-founder and former software architect of Yugabyte
profile: Stony Brook CS PhD and Apache HBase committer at Facebook (ran HBase for Facebook Messages and search indexing). Co-founded Yugabyte in Feb 2016 with Kannan Muthukkaruppan and Karthik Ranganathan; YugabyteDB is an open-source, PostgreSQL-compatible distributed SQL database (unicorn in 2021). After ~8 years building it he reportedly joined Google Cloud to work on Cloud SQL in Nov 2024.
interesting_fact: Called the quietest of Yugabyte's three ex-Facebook founders, he was the architecture-focused one who understood at code level where HBase and Cassandra diverged and broke under load, knowledge that shaped YugabyteDB.
deep_cut_fact: Before databases he worked on NLP: as a Stony Brook PhD student he co-authored 'International Sentiment Analysis for News and Blogs' (ICWSM 2008, with Lohit Vijayarenu and Steven Skiena), machine-translating news in nine languages and scoring entity sentiment with the Lydia text-analysis system.
notes: Low public profile; per a 2025/26 origin-story article he left Yugabyte in Nov 2024 for Google Cloud (Cloud SQL) via a LinkedIn update only (not independently confirmed). Yugabyte's PR agency (Inkhouse) is listed but is unlikely to route to him now. Hurun lists no net worth for him.

name: Vishal Chaudhary
current_role: Co-founder and MD, Aerospace & Defence vertical, Zetwerk (IPO-bound, filed with SEBI in 2026)
profile: IIT Kharagpur dual-degree chemical engineer who worked at ITC and logistics startup Rivigo before co-founding Zetwerk in 2018, the Bengaluru-based manufacturing/contract-manufacturing platform. He long ran its industrial vertical and, in Zetwerk's 2026 pre-IPO reorganisation, now heads aerospace & defence.
interesting_fact: He helped Zetwerk win an order to supply 10,000 MT of fabricated steel girders for India's bullet-train project; Fortune India named him and co-founder Srinath Ramakkrushnan to its 40 Under 40 in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Zetwerk's co-founders keep Saturday mornings reserved for brainstorming about the company's future, and he and Srinath share the motto 'What is good for the company trumps all views.'
notes: Role per Zetwerk UDRHP coverage (https://inc42.com/buzz/zetwerk-udrhp-a-look-at-shareholding-pattern-key-executives/). Company is in IPO quiet period, which may limit media availability.

name: Mike Murchison
current_role: Co-founder of Ada; becoming Chief AI Officer of the combined Dialpad-Ada company (deal announced Nov 4, 2026, expected to close ~Nov 12, 2026)
profile: Toronto serial entrepreneur (U of T cognitive science/HCI) who co-founded Ada with David Hariri in 2016 after their previous startup, Volley, was swamped by support requests. As CEO he built Ada into a $1bn+ AI customer-service agent platform (clients incl. Pinterest, Square, monday.com). In Nov 2026 Ada agreed to combine with Dialpad; Craig Walker becomes CEO and Murchison Chief AI Officer.
interesting_fact: Before building Ada, he and co-founder David Hariri worked as customer-service reps at several fast-growing tech companies to understand the problem first-hand; Ada then went through the AI stream of the Creative Destruction Lab at U of T's Rotman School.
deep_cut_fact: As a U of T cognitive-science and human-computer-interaction student he was regularly inspired by Geoffrey Hinton's research and by Steve Mann's wearable-computing lab; he was also in an early cohort of The Next 36 entrepreneurship program and is a Forbes 30 Under 30 alum.
notes: Role change: as of mid-Nov 2026 Ada is merging into Dialpad; use 'co-founder of Ada, Chief AI Officer at Dialpad' once closed. pr@ada.cx and PAN agency contact came via search of Ada's media center (site blocks scripted fetch); pr@dialpad.com verified on the deal release. Articulate, podcast-friendly AI-agents founder.

name: Aaron Kalb
current_role: Co-founder, Alation (data catalog / data intelligence); recent profiles list him as Chief Strategy Officer (title unconfirmed for 2026)
profile: Aaron Kalb co-founded Alation in 2012 with Satyen Sangani, Venky Ganti and Feng Niu, bringing design and linguistics to a team of database/ML researchers. The company pioneered the modern enterprise data catalog and reached unicorn status. Kalb has been Alation's head of product, its first Chief Data Officer (2019) and Chief Data & Analytics/Innovation Officer.
interesting_fact: In 2019 Kalb became Alation's first Chief Data Officer, a co-founder 'drinking his own champagne' by running the company's internal data governance and analytics, and he went on a global tour to collect best practices from other CDOs.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alation, Kalb was a designer and researcher in Apple's Siri Advanced Development Group. He studied Symbolic Systems (BS and MS) at Stanford, and Alation's own history describes him as the 'designer and linguist' of its founding team.
notes: Current title is inconsistent across sources (CSO vs CDAO vs Chief Innovation Officer; one profile says the CDAO role ended Aug 2023), so confirm on LinkedIn before outreach. Also linked to Alchemist Accelerator as a partner/mentor. Alation's media center lists marketingwebrequest@ for marketing/media requests.

name: Feng Niu
current_role: Co-founder of Alation (2012) and Lattice Data (acquired by Apple); current role not confirmed from a primary source
profile: Feng Niu is a database and machine-learning researcher (Tsinghua CS; UW-Madison PhD) who co-founded data-catalog company Alation in 2012 with Satyen Sangani, Venky Ganti and Aaron Kalb. Alation reached about a $1.7-2B valuation. He also co-founded Lattice Data (DeepDive-based dark-data extraction) with Chris Ré, which Apple acquired in 2017; profiles say he then worked at Apple.
interesting_fact: Niu is a co-author, with Ben Recht, Chris Ré and Stephen Wright, of 'Hogwild!' (2011), the lock-free parallel SGD paper that won the NeurIPS 2020 Test of Time Award and shaped how large ML models are trained.
deep_cut_fact: Hogwild! was written while Niu was a UW-Madison PhD student in the optimization group of the Wisconsin Institute for Discovery, which was in its first months of operation at the time. Alation's founding story credits him and Ganti with seeing data-discovery problems first-hand in research and at Google.
notes: Low public profile, with no verified personal site or social accounts. Secondary profiles claim Apple Research Scientist (2017-2020) and later CEO of a startup called Evidently, but neither is verified. The Alation founding-team description is at https://www.alation.com/about. Good AI-infrastructure/data angle for the podcast.

name: Satyen Sangani
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Alation, Inc. (Redwood City, CA)
profile: Satyen Sangani, an economist by training and former Oracle VP for financial-services analytical applications, co-founded Alation in 2012 with Aaron Kalb (ex-Apple Siri), Feng Niu and Venky Ganti. Alation pioneered the enterprise data catalog and was valued around $1.7-2B; in 2026 it relaunched its platform as AIOS, aimed at governing data and AI agents.
interesting_fact: Alation's founding idea combined Sangani's economics/Oracle view that big-company users can't find or trust data with Kalb's Siri-era natural-language work; its first 2015 product let employees query enterprise data in plain English.
deep_cut_fact: He has hosted Alation's podcast since 2022: launched as 'Data Radicals', it was relaunched in July 2026 as 'AI Radicals' for its fourth season, with biweekly interviews of data and AI leaders.
notes: A fellow podcast host, so a podcast-swap or guest invitation could land well. Fit: data/AI infrastructure rather than energy. ashley.womack@alation.com is Alation's named media contact (Sr. Director, Corporate Marketing).

name: Venky Ganti
current_role: Snowflake (Head of Migrations, per Snowflake blog author page, 2026); co-founder of Alation
profile: Venky Ganti co-founded data-catalog company Alation and served as CTO, helping define the 'data catalog' category. He later co-founded Mesh Dynamics, worked at Google, and was SVP Product & Engineering at AI startup Numbers Station (acquired by Alation in 2025). He now works on data migrations at Snowflake.
interesting_fact: Before Alation he worked on Google's Dynamic Search Ads, building web-scale ML/data-enrichment pipelines, and at Microsoft Research he initiated and productized several projects.
deep_cut_fact: He holds more than 35 granted patents from his Microsoft Research years and earned his PhD in machine learning and databases at the University of Wisconsin-Madison after a BTech from IIT Madras.
notes: Hands-on technical founder; good fit for a data-infrastructure/AI episode. Current Snowflake title taken from search snippet of snowflake.com blog author page (could not fetch directly). No net-worth figure; Hurun lists him via Alation's valuation.

name: Alex Cornell
current_role: Director of Design, Generative AI, Meta (per his own website)
profile: Alex Cornell is a San Francisco interface designer, filmmaker and musician. In 2011 he co-founded Firespotter Labs, which built UberConference and became Dialpad; he was creative director and design lead there. He later founded Cocoon (acquired by Substack in 2021), designed the Substack and Linear mobile apps, and now leads generative-AI design at Meta.
interesting_fact: Firespotter won TechCrunch Disrupt in 2012. Outside product design, his music has over 25M plays on Spotify/YouTube, and his best-known photos are of a flipped iceberg in Antarctica.
deep_cut_fact: Before startups he spent three years as an apprentice to Scott Hansen (ISO50 / Tycho), writing for the ISO50 blog and running the studio. In 2012 he published a book with Princeton Architectural Press.
notes: A designer-cofounder, not a typical UHNW profile; Hurun lists him as a Dialpad founder. Very approachable: he publishes a personal email. Angle: designing generative-AI products at Meta and the UberConference/Dialpad origin story.

name: Brian Peterson
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Dialpad
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Dialpad (originally UberConference) in 2011 with CEO Craig Walker, after both worked on Google Voice. He led engineering as SVP and in April 2021 became Dialpad's first CTO, overseeing its AI-powered calling, meetings and contact-center platform. In November 2026 Dialpad agreed to combine with the AI customer-service firm Ada in an all-share deal.
interesting_fact: Dialpad has pushed AI into its own engineering: in a 2026 HumanX interview he described a company-wide AI mandate, including that engineers should not write code without AI assistance.
deep_cut_fact: Before Dialpad he was a senior software engineer at Google and built the front end of Google Voice, the product that grew out of Craig Walker's startup GrandCentral, which Google acquired.
notes: Hurun lists him as a Dialpad unicorn co-founder. The Dialpad-Ada merger was announced on 4 Nov 2026 (https://www.dialpad.com/press/dialpad-and-ada/), so his title may change. The HumanX page now returns 404; the AI-mandate detail is from search snippets. Common name: be sure to reference Dialpad. A good engineering-leader guest on AI adoption.

name: Craig Walker
current_role: Founder and CEO, Dialpad (AI-powered business communications / contact center)
profile: Craig Walker is a former M&A lawyer turned three-time founder. He ran the first Dialpad Communications (sold to Yahoo) and co-founded GrandCentral, which Google bought in 2007 and relaunched as Google Voice. After leaving Google he founded today's Dialpad in 2011, an AI-native communications and contact-center platform valued at about $2B with roughly 1,500 staff. It is now pushing agentic AI with Google Gemini integrations.
interesting_fact: He co-founded GrandCentral, the startup Google acquired in 2007 that became Google Voice.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in door-to-door dictation-equipment sales, which he credits for his grit. He then worked at Apple, went to law school, and did M&A at Wilson Sonsini before becoming a founder.
notes: A frequent podcast guest and open about founder lessons, so likely receptive. A June 2026 Dialpad release also lists pr@dialpad.com. His LinkedIn is linked from his official Dialpad author page.

name: John Rector
current_role: Unclear. Former co-founder, VP Engineering and board director, Dialpad; aggregator profiles disagree on his current role (VP Engineering at Warp vs. Sr Director of Engineering at Reddit).
profile: Listed as a technical co-founder of Dialpad (founded around 2011 as UberConference/Switch, with Craig Walker and Brian Peterson), where he was VP Engineering (telephony) and a board director. Dialpad became an AI cloud-communications company valued at about $2B. He reportedly studied CS at Stanford and is named on several Dialpad patents.
notes: Low public profile, and all biographical data comes from aggregator sites (theorg, zerogtalent, patentleaderboard). Treat the details as unverified. Some profiles also claim earlier GrandCentral/Yahoo work, which I could not verify. dialpad.com was unreachable from this environment. The likely route is a professional network or Dialpad press.

name: Matt Vincett
current_role: Longtime CEO of LifeMiles / Avianca Chief Loyalty Officer (2010 to at least late 2023); current role unverified after Avianca named new LifeMiles leadership in 2025
profile: Matt Vincett built LifeMiles, the Avianca-TACA frequent-flyer programme, as its CEO from 2010, launching it in March 2011 and leading its 2015 carve-out and partial sale to Advent International at a valuation of about $1B+. Avianca bought the whole business back in 2020. LifeMiles had more than 11 million members in 2023 and earns most of its money selling miles to banks and retailers.
interesting_fact: He describes LifeMiles as a business that sells miles to banks, partners and retailers more than an airline perk; by 2023 it had 11M+ members and co-branded cards in 10 countries.
deep_cut_fact: Before LifeMiles he was an airline man at TACA, serving as Commercial VP, VP of TACA's regional airlines and Director of Strategy & Business Development (per Avianca IR management bio).
notes: In Feb 2025 Avianca named Valeria Yglesias SVP Loyalty & managing director of LifeMiles, and later Jaime Manso to lead LifeMiles, so Vincett has probably moved on; his bio is gone from Avianca's current IR page (the TACA background came from an earlier version). Very low public profile; LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Felipe Delgado
current_role: Co-founder (CFO/President), Merama; partner and board member, Beetmann Energy
profile: Mexican finance executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Mexico City/São Paulo group that acquires and scales leading Latin American e-commerce brands; its 2022 Series B valued it at $1.2B. Before that he was CEO/CFO of Beetmann, a Mexican wholesale-electricity supplier and renewable-energy developer using AI/IoT to optimise energy use.
interesting_fact: He has an energy background unusual for an e-commerce founder: he ran Beetmann Energy, a qualified supplier in Mexico's wholesale electricity market that develops renewable plants, and remains a partner and board member there.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in J.P. Morgan's US Oil & Gas investment-banking group, holds a UT Austin BBA (Walter B. Smith Scholar) and a Harvard MBA, and is a keen runner who has completed two marathons; Quién named him a 'Titan of Business' among its 50 people transforming Mexico (2022).
notes: Strong energy-podcast angle via Beetmann. Titles vary by source (CFO vs President). Low media profile; LinkedIn or Merama is the route.

name: Guilherme Nosralla
current_role: Co-founder, Merama (São Paulo / Mexico City)
profile: Brazilian growth/marketing executive who co-founded Merama in 2020, a Latin American e-commerce group that takes majority stakes in leading online consumer brands and scales them across marketplaces. Merama became a unicorn about a year after founding, valued at ~$1.2B after a $60M Series B extension led by Advent and SoftBank in Dec 2021.
interesting_fact: Merama hit a US$1.2B valuation roughly one year after launch, one of the fastest unicorn runs in Latin America; the round also funded Merama Labs, an in-house unit for building new businesses.
notes: Low public profile; founding-team lists vary (Sujay Tyle is CEO; Renato Andrade, Felipe Delgado, Olivier Scialom also cited). A Web Summit Rio 2025 speaker page (now 404) said he was previously Growth Strategy Director at mobile-game maker Wildlife Studios; unverified. No published press email found; reach via Merama website/LinkedIn.

name: Olivier Scialom
current_role: Co-founder, Merama (role since 2021 not confirmed)
profile: French entrepreneur Olivier Scialom co-founded Merama in December 2020 with Sujay Tyle, Felipe Delgado, Renato Andrade and Guilherme Nosralla. Merama is a Latin American e-commerce roll-up that buys majority stakes in leading online brands while their founders keep running them. It raised a $60M Series A and a $225M Series B in 2021 and became a unicorn.
interesting_fact: Merama raised its $225M Series B only about five months after its first round, becoming one of Latin America's fastest e-commerce unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: Before Merama, Scialom co-founded Petsy, a Mexican pet-focused e-commerce site that was sold to Maskota.
notes: Very low public profile and his current role isn't confirmed. Sujay Tyle is the company's public face. No published contact was found. Merama's website (merama.io) returned almost no content.

name: Renato Andrade
current_role: Co-founder, Merama; reportedly CEO of Omniteca since 2025 (directory listing only, unverified)
profile: Brazilian ex-McKinsey consultant (USP business degree, INSEAD MBA) who co-founded Merama in Dec 2020 with Guilherme Nosralla and others. Merama buys majority stakes in independent brands selling on Amazon/Mercado Libre across Latin America and became a unicorn in Dec 2021 at a $1.2bn valuation after Advent and SoftBank-backed rounds.
interesting_fact: Merama reached unicorn status less than a year after founding, with a $60m Series B extension valuing it at US$1.2bn.
deep_cut_fact: He and Nosralla met at McKinsey (Renato spent 5+ years there serving retail/consumer clients); the Merama idea came after they read about a funding round for US brand aggregator Perch and found nothing similar in Latin America.

name: Sujay Tyle

profile: US-born serial founder who entered Harvard at 15, left as a 2011 Thiel Fellow, and worked at Scopely before moving to Berlin to co-found Frontier Car Group (emerging-market used-car marketplaces), acquired by OLX/Naspers in 2019. He then co-founded Merama, which acquires and scales consumer brands selling on Mercado Libre and Amazon across Latin America, reaching unicorn status.

profile: IIT Bombay computer-science grad (2008) who started as a machine-learning/platform engineer at ad-tech startup PubMatic, then co-founded Mindtickle in Pune in 2011-12 with Krishna Depura, Nishant Mungali and Mohit Garg. Mindtickle became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.2B) selling sales-readiness and revenue-enablement software; he runs technology and operations as COO.

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mindtickle (San Francisco / Pune)
profile: Indian-born engineer and ISB MBA (Class of 2006) who co-founded Mindtickle in 2011 with former PubMatic colleagues Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali. Mindtickle grew from a gamified employee-learning tool into a revenue-enablement and sales-readiness platform, valued at over $1B; he leads it as CEO, now pushing AI coaching and role-play products.

name: Mohit Garg
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, OLOID (passwordless workforce identity, Sunnyvale CA); co-founder of Mindtickle
profile: One of four co-founders (with Krishna Depura, Deepak Diwakar and Nishant Mungali) of Pune-born Mindtickle, which pivoted from gamification to onboarding to sales enablement and became a unicorn in Aug 2021. In 2018 he co-founded OLOID, a passwordless/physical-identity platform for frontline workers, which has raised ~$23M Series A/A1 from Dell Technologies Capital, Honeywell, Okta Ventures and Yaletown.

name: Nishant Mungali
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Mindtickle
profile: Indian product designer-turned-founder who co-founded Mindtickle (Pune/San Francisco) in 2011 with Krishna Depura, Mohit Garg and Deepak Diwakar. The company grew from gamified onboarding into a sales-readiness and revenue-enablement platform, reaching unicorn status in 2021 (~$1.2B); he leads product.

name: Darpan Sanghvi
current_role: Founder, CoFounder Circle (AI-native startup acceleration/venture studio platform, India)
profile: Mumbai-based entrepreneur who founded MyGlamm in 2015 and built it into the Good Glamm Group, a content-to-commerce beauty conglomerate valued at $1.2B in 2021 (backers incl. Warburg Pincus, L'Occitane, Amazon). After the group was broken up by lenders in 2025, he launched CoFounder Circle, an AI-native accelerator for startups and MSMEs, and judges on JioHotstar's 'Pitch To Get Rich'.
interesting_fact: He is credited with pioneering the 'content-to-commerce' model in India's beauty industry, buying media/influencer platforms POPxo, Plixxo and ScoopWhoop to sell MyGlamm products; the group later launched Wyn Beauty with Serena Williams.
deep_cut_fact: While studying engineering at MIT Pune he worked at Baazee.com, the Indian auction site later bought by eBay; he later did a dual MBA at ESADE (Barcelona) and UT Austin.

name: Priyanka Gill
current_role: Founder & CEO, COLUXE (lab-grown diamond jewellery brand, launched 2025); co-founder, Good Glamm Group (MyGlamm)
profile: A former London-based journalist, Gill turned her blog eStylista into POPxo, a digital community for Indian women, after moving back to India in 2014. POPxo/Plixxo merged with MyGlamm in 2020 and became part of the Good Glamm Group in 2021, where she ran the media and content arm. She was later a venture partner at Kalaari Capital, then left in early 2025 to found COLUXE.
interesting_fact: COLUXE pitches AI-powered personalisation, virtual try-ons and modular jewellery, and has backers including Ajai Chowdhry (HCL co-founder) and Startup Sherpas.
deep_cut_fact: Born in a village in Punjab and an English Literature graduate of Lady Shri Ram College, she wrote for The Guardian, The Independent and Vogue India in London. She co-chaired the Pratham Gala (2009-10), which raised over GBP 3M. Her early collection of modern Indian art later sold at Christie's first auction in India.
notes: Media-friendly and active on social media. Her current focus is COLUXE (consumer/luxury), not the Good Glamm Group, so lead with COLUXE or her founder journey rather than Good Glamm's recent difficulties.

name: Michael Dombowsky
current_role: Co-founder, co-inventor and (per TheOrg) SVP Building Technology, Nexii Building Solutions; current status after Nexii's 2024 restructuring unclear
profile: Saskatchewan-born builder and inventor who co-founded Vancouver green-construction company Nexii (2017/18) with Ben Dombowsky and Stephen Sidwell. He invented its 'Nexiite' panelised low-carbon building system, which carried a unicorn valuation in 2021. Profiles credit him with 40+ years of designing and building residential, commercial and institutional projects.
interesting_fact: He is described as the inventor behind Nexii's whole-building system: prefabricated panels made of 'Nexiite', a concrete alternative pitched as cutting building emissions and construction time.
notes: Sensitive: Nexii entered CCAA creditor protection in Jan 2024 and was sold and relaunched under interim CEO Bill Tucker (SBIZ, Aug 2024); his role since then is unconfirmed. The 'unicorn' valuation is historical. A profile claim that he designed the Tunnels of Moose Jaw could not be verified, so I left it out. Very low public profile.

name: Ed Felten
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Scientist, Offchain Labs (developer of Arbitrum); Robert E. Kahn Professor of CS and Public Affairs emeritus, Princeton
profile: Princeton computer scientist and security researcher who was the FTC's first Chief Technologist (2011) and Deputy US CTO in the Obama White House (2015-17). In 2018 he co-founded Offchain Labs with former Princeton students Steven Goldfeder and Harry Kalodner; its Arbitrum rollup became the largest Ethereum layer-2. He served on the Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board until January 2025 and still keynotes events like EthCC 2026.
interesting_fact: As the US government's witness in United States v. Microsoft, he demonstrated in court a tool built with two students that removed Internet Explorer access from Windows 98, rebutting Microsoft's claim that it couldn't be done.
deep_cut_fact: He began as a physicist: after a Caltech BS in physics (1985) he spent three years as a staff programmer on a Caltech parallel-supercomputer project before his CS PhD at the University of Washington, where his thesis was on communication protocols between parallel processors.

public_contacts.value: Freedom to Tinker (blog he founded/writes for): https://freedom-to-tinker.com

notes: Princeton email is from his (older) self-published faculty homepage, written as 'felten at cs dot princeton dot edu'; may be less monitored now. Frequent podcast guest and conference speaker, so a podcast invitation fits him well. Also a NAE member and former EFF board member.

name: Harry Kalodner
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Offchain Labs (Arbitrum)
profile: Princeton computer-science PhD researcher who co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Steven Goldfeder to commercialise their Arbitrum research. Arbitrum became the most widely used Ethereum layer-2 rollup; Kalodner leads Offchain's engineering and technical vision.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic project: the three founders developed the technology at Princeton and published it as a 2018 paper before forming the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student he was lead author of BlockSci, an open-source blockchain analysis platform (2017 paper 'BlockSci: Design and applications of a blockchain analysis platform').
notes: Technical founder; appears on crypto podcasts (e.g. Masters of Web3).

name: Steven Goldfeder
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Offchain Labs (now branded Offchain), developer of Arbitrum
profile: Computer scientist who earned a Princeton PhD in cryptocurrency security and, after a Cornell Tech/IC3 postdoc, co-founded Offchain Labs in 2018 with Ed Felten and Harry Kalodner to commercialise the Arbitrum research project. Arbitrum became the largest Ethereum layer-2 rollup; he continues to lead the company as CEO.
interesting_fact: Arbitrum began as an academic research project at Princeton before being spun out as Offchain Labs, which raised at a $1.2B valuation in 2021.
deep_cut_fact: As a Princeton PhD student advised by Arvind Narayanan, he co-authored the widely used textbook 'Bitcoin and Cryptocurrency Technologies' (Princeton University Press) alongside Narayanan, Bonneau, Felten and Miller.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (Bankless, Castle Island, Fintech Blueprint) - receptive to long-form interviews.

name: Avi Shua
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Orca Security

Co-founded Orca Security in 2019 and was CEO until March 2023, building its agentless 'SideScanning' cloud security platform to a ~$1.8B valuation; he now leads innovation (SideScanning, Unified Data Model) as CIO.
interesting_fact: Orca's core idea, 'SideScanning', reads cloud workloads' block storage via the cloud provider's APIs instead of installing agents, giving full-stack visibility without touching running workloads.
deep_cut_fact: On CyberWire's 'Career Notes' he said he has been excited about cybersecurity since age 13, when he started probing his high school's network, and advised 'try to do things by yourself'.
notes: info@orca.security is Orca's general company email, not personal. Frequent conference speaker/podcast guest on cloud security, so a podcast invite fits his pattern.

current_role: Co-founder, Orca Security (listed on org charts as Head of SRE)
profile: Israeli engineer and one of eight co-founders of Orca Security, the agentless cloud-security platform founded in 2019 (largely by ex-Check Point colleagues) and valued at about $1.8B in 2021.
