interesting_fact: He is credited with inventing 18 patented technologies. At Corensic he brought what was billed as the world's first thin-hypervisor-based product to market.
deep_cut_fact: When he left Qumulo after nearly seven years, CEO Bill Richter called him 'a visionary, an inspiration and a good friend' and wished him 'a well deserved break, time with his family and his next adventure.'
notes: No public reporting on his activities since leaving Qumulo in 2018 was found, so alive is marked unknown (no death reports found either). Very low public profile; no verified personal site or social accounts found. Relevant to the data-center angle as a storage and file-system veteran.

name: Marek Sacha
current_role: Co-founder of Cera (UK home care); later head of XOM Materials (Klöckner-backed materials e-commerce platform) - current title unverified
profile: Czech-British entrepreneur (b. 1987), ex-McKinsey consultant, who was the first CEO of Czech online grocer Rohlik.cz and in 2015 co-founded Cera Care, the London tech-enabled home-care company, with Ben Maruthappu and Martin Ocenas, leading it until 2018. He then joined XOM Materials, a digital materials-trading platform initiated by Klöckner.
interesting_fact: Before Cera he was the first CEO of Rohlik.cz, the Czech online supermarket founded by Tomáš Čupr in 2014; Forbes Czech named him to its 30 Under 30 in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: He was formerly a competitive basketball player, and describes his focus as 'overlooked opportunities in boring or complicated industries from healthcare to groceries' (Aspen Young Leaders Program 2017 bio).
notes: Left Cera's leadership in 2018; Cera is now led by Ben Maruthappu. Aspen bio (2017) also lists him as CEO of Benefio, a family VC firm. No published personal contact found.

name: Tomas Cupr
current_role: Founder and CEO, Rohlik Group; also heads AI-agent startup Duvo AI (founded 2025)
profile: Czech serial entrepreneur (Tomáš Čupr) who founded deals site Slevomat and food-delivery app Dáme jídlo (later sold to Delivery Hero) before launching online grocer Rohlik in 2014, now a pan-European group (Knuspr, Gurkerl, Kifli, Sezamo). He also founded the investment firm TCF Capital and in 2026 Duvo AI raised a $32M Series A led by Balderton.
interesting_fact: His AI startup Duvo AI, founded in 2025, builds agents that learn company workflows and automate them inside existing systems like SAP; clients include Morrisons and Allegro, and in Oct 2026 it was raising $32M led by Balderton Capital.
deep_cut_fact: A Brno University of Technology IT student, he ended up in Sheffield, England in summer 2004 with three friends, lived there about five years doing web development, internet marketing and car financing, and started building Slevomat from Sheffield. He says 'Great service wins' is a lesson he learned in Britain.
notes: Frequent guest in Czech media/podcasts (CzechCrunch, Forbes CZ). Aspen Institute CE profile exists.

name: Malte Horeyseck
current_role: Co-founder, SellerX (former co-CEO); current operating role unclear
profile: German entrepreneur who co-founded SellerX, a Berlin-based Amazon-brand aggregator, with Harvard Business School friend Philipp Triebel in summer 2020. It raised a then-record €100M seed round and reached a $1B valuation. Press reports say both founders stepped down as co-CEOs in mid-2024. Since then SellerX has gone through a recapitalisation and CEO changes.
interesting_fact: After HBS he moved to Brazil and, in SellerX's words, 'built Latin America's leading ecommerce platform from scratch'; Crunchbase lists him as a Dafiti co-founder.
deep_cut_fact: He and Philipp Triebel met at HBS in Boston, then lived on opposite sides of the world (Brazil and London) and kept discussing a joint business for years before founding SellerX in summer 2020.
notes: Search results said he and Triebel stepped down as co-CEOs in June 2024, citing Sifted (https://sifted.eu/articles/sellerx-ceos-depart-share-sale-news), but I could not open that article. The company has been under financial strain since. Use a neutral approach, and LinkedIn is likely the best route. He was interviewed on the Tech.eu podcast: https://podcast.tech.eu/episodes/malte-horeyseck-co-founder-of-sellerx-interview-special

name: Philipp Triebel
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO of SellerX (Berlin Amazon-brand aggregator); stepped down June 2024. Current venture not publicly confirmed.
profile: German entrepreneur and Harvard Business School 2010 graduate who co-founded SellerX in Berlin in 2020 with Malte Horeyseck; the Amazon-seller aggregator raised heavily (incl. a $500M round in Nov 2021) and hit unicorn status. Both co-CEOs left in June 2024. Earlier he co-founded IVY, a New York 'social university' events community, and worked in investing (Accrete Capital, Praxi Partners per listings).
interesting_fact: Before SellerX he co-founded IVY, a 'social university' that by 2017 had 150,000+ subscribers and ran 1,000+ events a year across seven US cities; he and co-founder Beri Meric first toyed with a members-only dating network.
deep_cut_fact: On IVY's group trips he said: 'I made good friends in business school by traveling with them' - and that members 'all come back best friends.'
notes: Left SellerX June 2024 (per Sifted/OMR: https://omr.com/de/daily/thrasio-klone-scheitern-sellerx-bbg-razor-group). A self-maintained profile lists a stealth startup from April 2025 (unverified). Aggregator business model has struggled - avoid that topic. No published contact found; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Zheng Jie
current_role: Founder, chairman & president, Shulan Medical Group (树兰医疗), Hangzhou
profile: Zheng Jie (郑杰) co-founded Shulan Medical in Hangzhou in 2013, building a private hospital group around Shulan (Hangzhou), Anji and Quzhou hospitals; backers include Sequoia China and Qiming, at an ~8B yuan valuation, and the group has filed for a Hong Kong IPO. A serial entrepreneur in health IT, he is pushing Shulan's 2025 'All in Technology' strategy around computational medicine.
interesting_fact: Zheng frames his vision as moving medicine from 'seeing a doctor' to 'counting diseases', via a 'self-developed system - data driven - AI enabled' model built on computational medicine and high-performance computing.
deep_cut_fact: He took part in China's national 863 Program researching digital-healthcare and medical-information standards, launched the OMAHA (Open Medical and Health Alliance) in 2015, founded what is described as China's first non-profit digital-healthcare research institute, and introduced a 'Computational Medicine' course at Shulan.
notes: Common Chinese name; identity confirmed via Shulan founder references. The name Shulan combines characters from the names of academicians Zheng Shusen and Li Lanjuan (source: news.pedaily.cn/202308/520963.shtml). No published contact found; Chinese-language outreach via Shulan Medical corporate channels / HK IPO sponsors likely needed. Data-driven medicine angle fits a data-center podcast.

name: Jia Jiaya
current_role: Founder and Board Chairman, SmartMore (思谋科技); Chair Professor, HKUST and Dean of its von Neumann Institute
profile: Hunan-born computer-vision scientist (b. 1978; PhD HKUST 2004), ex-CUHK tenured professor and head of Tencent YouTu X-Lab, who founded SmartMore in 2019. SmartMore sells AI vision 'industrial agents' for inspection in EV batteries, autos, rail and electronics; a unicorn within two years, it filed for a Hong Kong IPO in March 2026.
interesting_fact: His lab produced LongLoRA (2023), a widely used technique for extending LLM context length, and the open-source multimodal model DreamOmni2 (2025); he has 200+ papers and over 100,000 citations.
deep_cut_fact: A keen photographer, in 2002 as an HKUST student he spent scholarship money on one of the early digital cameras; frustrated by the image quality, he wondered if algorithms could dehaze, deblur and denoise photos - the question that launched his computer-vision career.
notes: Accessible academic-founder; day-to-day SmartMore CEO is co-founder Shen Xiaoyong. SmartMore is in an HKEX IPO process (filed Mar 2026) - may limit what he can say. global@smartmore.com is a general company inbox; academic route via HKUST also possible.

name: Shen Xiaoyong
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, SmartMore (思谋科技)
profile: Chinese AI entrepreneur and CEO of SmartMore, an industrial machine-vision and AI company founded in 2019 with his former CUHK doctoral supervisor, Prof. Jia Jiaya, and a core team from Tencent's YouTu Lab. SmartMore sells AI inspection and smart-manufacturing systems to clients such as Bosch, Canon and P&G. It raised about US$200M in 2021 and reached a ~$1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: SmartMore's founding team largely came from Tencent YouTu Lab, which Jia Jiaya joined from CUHK in 2017; Shen was one of Jia's CUHK students before becoming CEO of the spin-out.
notes: global@smartmore.com appears on the company's international site and is a general company inbox, not his personal one; sales@ and product@ are on smartmore.com/contact. Sources differ on whether Jia Jiaya or Shen is called 'founder'. Mostly covered in Chinese media (36Kr, QbitAI).

name: Liu Shu
current_role: Co-founder and technology lead (CTO), SmartMore (思谋科技)
profile: Liu Shu (刘枢) co-founded Shenzhen/Hong Kong industrial-AI company SmartMore with CUHK professor Jia Jiaya and Shen Xiaoyong, and leads its R&D, including the IndustryGPT multimodal industrial model and AI visual-inspection equipment for manufacturing. SmartMore became a unicorn after large early funding rounds; he was named to Hurun's Under-30 entrepreneurs lists in 2020 and 2021.
interesting_fact: His R&D team at SmartMore has an average age under 30 and builds industrial-model-powered AI inspection machines that the company says reach 99.99% accuracy.
deep_cut_fact: Colleagues nickname him 'Co哥' ('Brother Co') because, as a PhD student, he won five MS COCO competition titles; his PANet paper (CVPR 2018, with Jiaya Jia) took 1st place in the COCO 2017 instance-segmentation challenge.
notes: 'Co哥' nickname and 5-title claim from Shenzhen Special Zone Daily (sznews, May 2025; page not directly fetchable here, quoted via search). PANet authorship/COCO 1st place verified on arXiv. global@smartmore.com is a general company inbox on the site, not specifically press. Chinese outreach preferred.

name: Li Ruiyu
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of SmartMore (思谋科技); a company directory lists a 'Ruiyu Li' as co-founder & head of product - not confirmed by an official source
profile: Hurun names Li Ruiyu among the founders of SmartMore, the Hong Kong/Shenzhen industrial-AI unicorn founded in 2019 by CUHK professor Jia Jiaya with former students including CEO Shen Xiaoyong, which sells machine-vision and AI inspection systems to manufacturers. No official bio of Li was found on SmartMore's site or in press coverage.
interesting_fact: SmartMore was founded in 2019 by CUHK computer-vision professor (and ex-Tencent YouTu X-Lab head) Jia Jiaya and his former PhD students, and has been dubbed Hong Kong's new hi-tech poster child.
notes: Could not confirm Chinese name or role from an official source; possibly the CUHK PhD 'Ruiyu Li' who co-authored with Jia Jiaya, but unverified - do not use in outreach without confirming. global@smartmore.com is SmartMore's general company inbox.

name: Kazuhide Sekiyama
current_role: Co-founder & Representative Executive Officer, Spiber Inc. (Tsuruoka, Yamagata, Japan)
profile: Japanese biotech entrepreneur who began researching artificial spider silk as a Keio University biotechnology student and founded Spiber (spider + fiber) during his doctoral studies. Spiber engineers microbes to ferment protein materials; it has shifted from replicating spider silk ('Qmonos') to Brewed Protein fibers for apparel, sold to fashion partners.
interesting_fact: Sekiyama and co-founder Junichi Sugahara were named to the Vogue Business 2025 100 Innovators list (Entrepreneurs and Founders category).
deep_cut_fact: Spiber grew out of a seminar at Keio's Institute for Advanced Biosciences in Tsuruoka under Prof. Masaru Tomita; in 2007 Sekiyama (then a 4th-year student) and Sugahara, joined by his high-school classmate and CPA Hideya Mizutani, made their first batch of synthetic protein fiber before incorporating.
notes: Japanese name 関山和秀. Company is based in rural Tsuruoka rather than Tokyo; contact form is the published route (no press email found).

name: Sugawara Junichi
current_role: Co-founder, Director and Representative Executive Officer, Spiber Inc.
profile: Junichi Sugahara (Sugawara in the source list) co-founded Spiber in 2007 in Tsuruoka, Yamagata, with Kazuhide Sekiyama out of Keio University's Institute for Advanced Biosciences. Spiber develops fermentation-made 'Brewed Protein' fibres and materials for fashion and other industries; he became Representative Executive Officer in 2023.
interesting_fact: Sugahara and Sekiyama were named to the Vogue Business 2025 100 Innovators list (Entrepreneurs and Founders category) for Spiber's protein-based materials.
deep_cut_fact: Spiber started in 2007 as student research at Keio's Tsuruoka biosciences lab under Prof. Masaru Tomita: Sugahara (then a second-year student) and Sekiyama analysed silk from several spider species to decode its amino-acid sequences.
notes: Name usually romanised 'Junichi Sugahara' (菅原潤一). Co-founder Sekiyama is the more public face; Sugahara holds a Keio PhD and has also led Spiber investee Synplogen (per MarketScreener, unverified on primary source).

name: Anu Sudarsan
current_role: Manager, Engineering at Starburst (listed among the company's founders)
profile: Software engineer listed among Starburst's founders, alongside CEO Justin Borgman and the Trino co-creators. She previously worked with Starburst's founding engineers at Hadapt (acquired by Teradata in 2014). At Starburst, the Trino-based data lakehouse/query-engine company, she has led Starburst Galaxy engineering and now serves as an engineering manager.
interesting_fact: She led the projects that brought Starburst to the Google Cloud Marketplace and Azure Cloud Marketplace, and was team lead for Starburst Galaxy, its fully managed cloud offering.
deep_cut_fact: Before Starburst she worked at Hadapt (later acquired by Teradata) alongside the engineers who would later found Starburst; in 2021 she said what she liked best was getting 'to experiment with cutting-edge technologies.'
notes: Engineering-focused, low public profile; no personal social accounts verified. Starburst leadership page lists her under 'Founders' as Manager, Engineering. Older releases list Beth Winkowski (Winkowski PR) as media contact.

name: Dain Sundstrom
current_role: Co-founder, IceGuard (stealth data-security startup); formerly co-founder and CTO of Starburst
profile: Dain Sundstrom is one of the four engineers who created the Presto distributed SQL engine at Facebook, starting in 2012. In 2018 they left and forked it as PrestoSQL, renamed Trino in 2020, and he co-founded Starburst, the commercial Trino company valued at $3B. In early 2025 he and David Phillips left Starburst to co-found IceGuard, a stealth data-security company.
interesting_fact: The four Presto creators left Facebook in 2018 after disagreements over Facebook's influence on Presto's governance, forked the code as PrestoSQL (now Trino), and reunited as Starburst's technical leadership.
deep_cut_fact: Before Presto he was in the Java open-source world: he is listed as an Apache committer in the Apache incubator proposal for OpenEJB, the EJB container used by the Apache Geronimo application server.
notes: Left Starburst in early 2025 (Blocks and Files, April 2025). IceGuard is in stealth, and no IceGuard website or contact was found. Active in the Trino open-source community, which is a possible route. Good fit for a data-infrastructure episode.

name: Grzegorz Kokosiński
current_role: Listed in the Founders section of Starburst's leadership page as Senior Manager, Engineering; Trino open-source maintainer
profile: Polish software engineer in the Warsaw-based founding engineering team of Starburst, the commercial company behind the Trino (formerly PrestoSQL) distributed SQL query engine. The team grew out of Hadapt/Teradata's Presto work. Starburst lists him among its founders as Senior Manager, Engineering.
interesting_fact: Starburst's own leadership page groups him with co-founders Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski, Matt Fuller and Piotr Findeisen in its 'Founders' section, part of the Warsaw engineering team behind Starburst.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the official maintainers of the open-source Trino SQL engine, listed under the GitHub handle 'kokosing' on Trino's project roles page.
notes: Low-profile engineer, not an executive. One search summary claimed his LinkedIn says his Starburst role was eliminated; this was not verified, and Starburst's leadership page still lists him. Starburst has no press email on its leadership page, only a general /contact/ form. The LinkedIn URL comes from search results and was not opened.

name: Justin Borgman
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, Starburst (Trino-based data platform)
profile: Former software engineer who, while at business school, co-founded Hadapt (2010) to commercialize Yale's HadoopDB research and sold it to Teradata in 2014, where he became VP/GM of Hadoop products. He then co-founded Starburst with the Trino (Presto) creators. Starburst now sells an open-lakehouse/AI data platform, including a GPU-native engine launched in 2026.
interesting_fact: In 2026 Starburst named 2025 F1 world champion Lando Norris as its brand ambassador; Borgman likened enterprise AI to an F1 driver's split-second, data-driven decisions.
deep_cut_fact: While in business school he read the HadoopDB paper by Yale researchers Daniel Abadi and Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski, walked over to the CS department to recruit them, and started Hadapt. He calls it 'basically like getting a Ph.D. in entrepreneurship.' Bajda-Pawlikowski later co-founded Starburst with him.
notes: A frequent speaker and podcast guest on data/AI infrastructure, which makes him a strong fit for a data-center/AI podcast. The best route is through Starburst's PR agency, AirCover.

name: Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski
current_role: Co-founder, Starburst (formerly CTO); no longer on the executive team per Starburst's leadership page
profile: Polish-born database engineer and Yale computer-science researcher who co-founded Hadapt (first SQL-on-Hadoop company, acquired by Teradata in 2014), then was Chief Architect at Teradata's Center for Hadoop working on Presto, before co-founding Starburst (enterprise Trino/Presto data platform) as CTO. Starburst now lists him as co-founder; Martin Traverso is CTO.
interesting_fact: Hadapt, the company he co-founded and served as chief software architect, was the first SQL-on-Hadoop company and was acquired by Teradata in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: As a Yale CS grad student he co-authored the 2009 VLDB paper 'HadoopDB: An Architectural Hybrid of MapReduce and DBMS Technologies for Analytical Workloads' with Daniel Abadi and Avi Silberschatz - the research that became Hadapt.
notes: Current operating role unclear; Starburst leadership page (starburst.io/about/leadership) lists him only as 'Co-founder' under Founders. PR contact is Starburst's agency (AirCover PR).

name: Karol Sobczak
current_role: Co-founder, Starburst Data; Trino open-source maintainer (current Starburst role unconfirmed)
profile: Karol Sobczak is a Warsaw-based database engineer and a co-founder of Starburst. Starburst commercialises the Trino (formerly PrestoSQL) distributed SQL query engine and is valued at about $3B. The company grew out of the Hadapt team, which Teradata acquired, and its engineering was rooted in Warsaw, Poland.
interesting_fact: Starburst's founding engineering team was based in Warsaw, Poland. It came from the Hadapt startup, which Teradata acquired, and had worked on developing Presto, the precursor to Trino.
deep_cut_fact: He is one of the officially listed Trino project maintainers, under GitHub handle 'sopel39', alongside Presto/Trino creators Dain Sundstrom, David Phillips and Martin Traverso.
notes: Engineer-founder with a low media profile. A third-party profile (Stackforce) says his Starburst tenure ran Nov 2017 to Jul 2024, but this is unverified, so check whether he is still at Starburst. Possible warm route is the Trino community (Slack/GitHub).

name: Martin Traverso
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Starburst; co-founder, Trino Software Foundation
profile: Software engineer who co-created the Presto distributed SQL engine at Facebook with Dain Sundstrom, David Phillips and Eric Hwang after joining its data-infrastructure team in 2012. He co-founded Starburst, which commercialises Presto/Trino for querying data lakes and federated sources, and leads the open-source Trino project.
interesting_fact: Presto was built because Facebook's data scientists needed fast, accurate interactive queries over more than 300 petabytes of data spread across multiple databases.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2019 he, Sundstrom and Phillips forked Presto as 'PrestoSQL' and set up the not-for-profit Presto Software Foundation; in December 2020 the fork was rebranded Trino. Trino now underpins products like Amazon Athena.
notes: Technical founder, active in the Trino community (trino.io, Trino Slack). LinkedIn URL is what DataStax's podcast-guest page redirects to; not otherwise verified.

name: Matt Fuller
current_role: Co-founder; Vice President, AI/ML Products and board member, Starburst
profile: Database engineer who was an early Vertica engineer, then a principal engineer at SQL-on-Hadoop startup Hadapt, which Teradata acquired in 2014; at Teradata he led Presto (now Trino) engineering in Boston. That team spun out as Starburst in 2017, the commercial Trino/lakehouse company; Fuller remains on its board and leads AI/ML products.
interesting_fact: He co-authored O'Reilly's 'Trino: The Definitive Guide' with Trino co-creator Martin Traverso and Manfred Moser.
deep_cut_fact: He says he got into databases via the C-Store research paper, which led him to join Vertica (the columnar database that grew out of it), where he co-built the query optimizer.
notes: Engineer-founder, low public profile; CEO Justin Borgman is the main public face. Vertica optimizer detail is from Strata speaker bio/Crunchbase summary in search; C-Store origin from podcast notes.

name: Piotr Findeisen
current_role: Co-founder of Starburst; Trino maintainer and Apache DataFusion committer (current employer not confirmed)
profile: Warsaw-based software engineer and founding team member of Starburst, the company behind enterprise Trino (formerly PrestoSQL). He worked on Presto's cost-based optimizer, spill-to-disk and correlated subqueries. He is listed as a Trino maintainer and, more recently, as a committer on the Rust-based Apache DataFusion query engine.
interesting_fact: Before Starburst, he worked at Teradata, where he was the top external committer to Facebook's Presto project, and he was a team leader at the supply-chain SaaS firm Syncron.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MS in computer science and a BSc in mathematics from the University of Warsaw. Besides Trino, he is now a committer on Apache DataFusion (GitHub: findepi).
notes: Engineer-founder with a low media profile; the open-source communities (Trino Slack/GitHub) are his main public presence. Kasia Findeisen is also a Trino maintainer. I could not confirm whether he still works at Starburst.

name: Wojciech Biela
current_role: Co-founder, Starburst (Senior Director of Engineering as of 2022 company blog)
profile: Polish engineer who co-founded Starburst, the data-lakehouse/query company built on the open-source Trino (formerly Presto) engine. He came from the Hadapt team acquired by Teradata in 2014, where he worked on Presto, and built Starburst's core engineering team in Warsaw.
interesting_fact: The Hadapt/Teradata team that founded Starburst kept working on Presto, which was later renamed Trino after a trademark dispute; Starburst's engineering core stayed in Warsaw.
deep_cut_fact: He was recruited to build the Warsaw engineering team by his college friend and fellow co-founder Kamil Bajda-Pawlikowski, and personally worked on closing Starburst's first EMEA customer, Zalando; he called Starburst 'not my first startup, but by far the most special.'
notes: Low public profile; the company blog is the main source. Current title could not be confirmed beyond the 2022 post.

name: Wu Gansha
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman and CEO, UISEE Technology (驭势科技; listed in Hong Kong, 2026)
profile: Wu Gansha (吴甘沙), born 1976 in Nantong, Jiangsu, holds a Fudan CS master's and spent 16 years at Intel, ending as head of Intel Labs China, before co-founding UISEE in 2016. UISEE skipped robotaxis to focus on L4 autonomy in closed sites like airports, factories and mines, and listed in Hong Kong in 2026 at ~RMB 10B.
interesting_fact: UISEE's contrarian bet on commercial vehicles in closed scenarios paid off: H1 2026 revenue was about RMB 163M (+64.9% YoY) with a ~53% gross margin; Wu says his main daily question is simply how to 'stay alive'.
deep_cut_fact: He likes to argue autonomy in unit economics: how expensive a driver is in Europe and how many drivers one unmanned vehicle replaces, pitching the near-zero marginal cost of an 'AI driver' sold like software.
notes: Articulate, media-friendly founder who speaks at conferences (World Robot Conference etc.); good fit for AI/autonomy angle. UISEE's site lists pr@uisee.com for media and an IR site (ir.uisee.com).

name: Peng Jinzhan
current_role: Co-founder, deputy general manager and head of innovation business division, UISEE Technologies (驭势科技, HKEX: 1511)
profile: Peng Jinzhan (彭进展) is one of five co-founders of UISEE (驭势科技), a Beijing L4 autonomous-driving company focused on closed scenarios such as airports and factories. Ex-Intel engineer; co-founded UISEE in Feb 2016 with Wu Gansha. UISEE listed on HKEX (1511.HK) in May 2026; Peng is a controlling shareholder (~2% stake) and part of the acting-in-concert founder group.
interesting_fact: UISEE was started in February 2016 in a garage in Beijing's Fangshan district by ex-Intel colleagues Wu Gansha, Zhou Xin and Peng Jinzhan plus Zhao Yong and Jiang Yan; in 2019 it began the world's first routine driverless baggage-logistics operation at Hong Kong International Airport.
deep_cut_fact: Before UISEE, Peng was lead system architect for Intel's Edison chip platform, which won four awards at CES 2014, and directed the Robotics System Lab at Intel China Research Institute. He studied computer science at Huazhong University of Science and Technology (1999) and Beihang (master's, 2002).
notes: Chinese name 彭进展. Identity confirmed via HKEX prospectus (May 12, 2026), Directors and Senior Management section. Not a board director; low public profile. Spoke at TIC 2021 as co-founder/chief system architect. Business contact on site: winfuture@uisee.com.

name: Jiang Yan
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of UISEE (驭势科技, HKEX 01511); current role not verified - he is not named on UISEE's current board or management page
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists (2021-2025) name Jiang Yan as a founder of UISEE Technology, the Beijing autonomous-driving company led by co-founder, chairman and CEO Wu Gansha. UISEE focuses on driverless logistics in airports and factories (tractors, shuttles, delivery vehicles), passed 11.2M km of fully driverless operation by Oct 2026, and listed in Hong Kong in May 2026.
interesting_fact: UISEE says it was the first company to run commercial 'truly driverless' operations (no safety driver) at airports and factories, starting in 2019, and passed 11.2M km of such operations by October 2026.
notes: Common name; I could not confirm his current role from an official source (web-search quota exhausted), and UISEE's site now names only Wu Gansha as co-founder. Verify before outreach; route via UISEE media mailbox pr@uisee.com. Autonomous-logistics rather than energy/data-center fit.

name: Hitesh Sheth
current_role: President and CEO, Vectra AI (San Jose, CA)
profile: Networking veteran who leads AI threat-detection company Vectra AI (formerly Vectra Networks) as president and CEO, building it into a $1B+ unicorn. Previously COO of Aruba Networks, EVP/GM of switching at Juniper, and a senior switching executive at Cisco (metro Ethernet), after roles at Liberate Technologies and Oracle.
interesting_fact: Vectra bills itself as the team behind 'the world's first AI-based cybersecurity platform'; its threat labs showed in 2016 that consumer Wi-Fi webcams could be reprogrammed into persistent network backdoors.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a Unix programmer at the Santa Cruz Operation (SCO) after earning a BA in Computer Science from the University of Texas at Austin.
notes: Hurun lists him as founder; Vectra's own bio describes him as president & CEO (he joined early rather than being a day-one founder). Best route: Vectra media room / InkHouse PR. Security-for-AI and data-center network angle.

name: Marc Rogers
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, nbhd.ai (AI observability startup); Head of Security, DEF CON
profile: British security researcher and white-hat hacker who co-founded Bay Area security startup Vectra (now Vectra AI; formerly TraceVector/Vectra Networks). Career spans a decade at Vodafone, Lookout, Cloudflare (head of security) and Okta (VP cybersecurity strategy). Now co-founder/CTO of nbhd.ai and senior technical advisor at the Institute for Security and Technology.
interesting_fact: His research hacks include Apple's TouchID (iPhone 5 and 6), Google Glass and, with Kevin Mahaffey in 2015, the Tesla Model S; in 2020 he co-founded the COVID-19 CTI League of volunteer hackers protecting hospitals, and received a President's Volunteer Service Award in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: Most of the DEF CON community knows him simply as 'CJ'. He has been hacking since the 1980s, was once a CISO in South Korea, and as technical advisor helped create the on-screen hacks for USA's 'Mr. Robot' and the BBC's 'The Real Hustle'.
notes: Vectra co-founder status confirmed by his own bio (marcrogers.org) and Wikipedia's Vectra AI infobox; one career profile shows him as Vectra VP Security/CISO 2013-2014. He is no longer at Vectra (CEO is Hitesh Sheth). His site invites people to reach out via social media. Beware confusion with Purdue professor Marcus K. Rogers.

name: Chris Lynch
current_role: Co-founder and Managing Partner, Arsenal Collective (defense-hardware venture fund); co-founder and former CEO, Rebellion Defense
profile: Seattle serial entrepreneur hired by Defense Secretary Ash Carter in 2015 to found the Pentagon's Defense Digital Service. Left DDS in April 2019 and co-founded AI/software firm Rebellion Defense with Oliver Lewis and Nicole Camarillo; it hit a $1B valuation in 2021. Now runs Arsenal Collective, a VC fund for weapons, munitions and defense manufacturing startups, with Capital Factory's Joshua Baer.
interesting_fact: At DDS he created Hack the Pentagon, the first federal bug bounty program, and helped launch the JEDI cloud program; Ash Carter called him the Pentagon's resident hoodie-wearer.
deep_cut_fact: Arsenal's bio credits him with building and fielding the first man-packable counter-drone hardware for CENTCOM and INDOPACOM. In 2019 he said: 'If the nerds don't show up and work on the mission of national defense...then I'm not sure who will.'
notes: Arsenal fund launched at Capital Factory's FSN 2026 event. He did a Nov 2025 interview on 'The Briefing Room' podcast about DDS, Rebellion and Arsenal. Common name, so make sure you have the defense-tech Chris Lynch (LinkedIn handle lynchseattle). Rebellion's later troubles (reported by Forbes, 2023) are best avoided in outreach.

name: Nicole Camarillo
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Rebellion Defense (Washington, DC defense-AI software); current role not verified
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder list (2021-2024) names Nicole Camarillo as a founder of Rebellion Defense, a defense-tech software company started in 2019 by former Pentagon Defense Digital Service people that builds AI and cybersecurity software for the U.S. and UK militaries, valued at ~$1B in 2021. Her current position could not be verified.
notes: Thin record: the web-search quota ran out and Rebellion's site has no team page, so her role and background could not be sourced. Company-level inquiries email only (she may no longer be with the company). Verify her current role before outreach.

name: Xie Xiaoliang
current_role: Listed by Hurun (2021-2025) as a co-founder of CalmCar (天瞳威视, Suzhou); not on CalmCar's current management team
profile: Hurun's Global Unicorn Index 2021-2025 named Xie Xiaoliang (谢晓靓) alongside Wang Xi and Li Hao as founders of CalmCar, a Suzhou-based (est. 2016) software-centric ADAS/autonomous-driving company valued at ~US$1.1B. CalmCar supplies L2-L2+ driving/parking and cockpit-monitoring solutions to 23 car brands and runs L4 Robobus/Robotaxi pilots. Hurun's 2026 list dropped her name.
interesting_fact: CalmCar says it was China's second-largest software-centric provider of combined highway-driving and parking ADAS in 2024, serving 23 car brands and nearly 200 models, and launched ConnectOne, billed as the first L4 robotaxi on Horizon Robotics' Journey 6 chip.
notes: Her role could not be verified: CalmCar's management page lists Wang Xi (chairman/CEO), Wang Ruoyu, Yuan Jin, Xu Jie, Tao Zhiheng and others, but not Xie; Hurun 2026 replaced her with Wang Ruoyu. Company appears to be preparing a listing (IR pages 'coming soon'). Contacts are the company's. Auto-ADAS, weak data-center fit.

name: Jochen Ziervogel
current_role: Co-founder of Enpal (Berlin); Crunchbase lists him as Co-Founder and Head of Partner Management (Mario Kohle is CEO)
profile: WHU alumnus and one of three co-founders (with Mario Kohle and Viktor Wingert) of Enpal, the Berlin solar company founded in 2017 that sells and rents rooftop PV, batteries and heat pumps to households. Enpal became Germany's first greentech unicorn in 2021, reached about EUR 960M revenue in 2023 and has installed ~115,000 solar systems; the company says it is still founder-led.
interesting_fact: Enpal was founded in 2017 under the name 'Evergreen' and drew early backing from Princeville's climate fund, which is supported by Leonardo DiCaprio; in 2021 it became Germany's first greentech unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: In May 2021, as Enpal was scaling, he was the guest on Tech.eu Podcast #219, 'The photovoltaic expansion', discussing solar panels and the future of green energy in Europe.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Mario Kohle; reach via Enpal press office. Prior career (per Crunchbase) included banking and BMW roles, not independently verified. Enpal restructured in 2026 (layoffs, Hamburg site closure); avoid that topic.

name: Viktor Wingert
current_role: Co-founder and managing director (board member), Enpal B.V., Berlin
profile: Co-founded Berlin solar company Enpal in 2017 with Mario Kohle and Jochen Ziervogel. Enpal sells/rents rooftop solar, batteries, wallboxes and heat pumps to German households, reached ~EUR 960M revenue in 2023, and is building what it calls Europe's largest virtual power plant by trading customers' flexible demand on the power exchange.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Enpal became Germany's first green-tech 'unicorn'; an early backer was Princeville's climate fund supported by Leonardo DiCaprio - its first-ever investment in a German company.
deep_cut_fact: Enpal was founded in 2017 under the name 'Evergreen Energy'; the founders started small, installing their first solar systems themselves before scaling into a heat-pump and virtual-power-plant business.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Mario Kohle; route via Enpal press office. Virtual power plant / grid flexibility angle fits the energy podcast. Personal social accounts not verified this pass (search budget exhausted).

name: Avi Baum
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Hailo (Tel Aviv-based edge-AI processor company)
profile: Israeli chip architect who co-founded Hailo in 2017 after serving as CTO for Wireless Connectivity at Texas Instruments and in senior architecture roles in the Israel Defense Forces. Hailo designs low-power AI accelerators and vision processors (Hailo-8, Hailo-10H with on-device generative AI, Hailo-15) used in cameras, cars, PCs and the Raspberry Pi AI HAT; it reached a ~$1B unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Hailo's chips power the official Raspberry Pi AI Kit/AI HAT add-ons, putting dedicated neural-network accelerators in the hands of hobbyists, and its Hailo-10H brings LLMs/VLMs onto edge devices.
deep_cut_fact: He argues TOPS is no longer the right yardstick for edge AI: for generative models, memory bandwidth matters more, and each product needs its own 'power-cost-latency working point' (Unite.AI interview, Aug 2025). He also writes on the DRAM shortage's effect on edge AI.
notes: Accessible technical leader who regularly blogs and gives interviews (hailo.ai/blog). LinkedIn is linked from Hailo's own leadership page. Edge-AI counterpoint to data-center AI; good on power-efficiency and memory-bandwidth topics.

name: Hadar Zeitlin
current_role: Listed as a co-founder of Hailo (Tel Aviv edge-AI chipmaker); not on Hailo's current leadership team page
profile: Hurun (2021-2024) lists Hadar Zeitlin as a founder of Hailo, the Israeli maker of edge AI processors (Hailo-8, Hailo-10 and vision processors), founded in 2017 and valued at about $1B. Hailo's current leadership team (CEO Orr Danon, CTO Avi Baum) does not include him; his current role could not be verified.
interesting_fact: Hailo says it was founded in 2017 to bring deep-learning compute, then largely confined to costly, power-hungry data centers, onto small edge devices - the opposite of the data-center build-out trend.
notes: Personal bio not verified (web search quota exhausted; no Hailo page names him). Company contacts reach Hailo, not necessarily him - he may have left the company. Check LinkedIn manually before outreach.

name: Orr Danon
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Hailo Technologies (Tel Aviv edge-AI chipmaker; acquired by Microchip Technology, completed Sept 2026)
profile: Orr Danon co-founded Hailo in Tel Aviv in February 2017 with Avi Baum, Hadar Zeitlin and Rami Feig, and became CEO after Feig's passing. Hailo designs low-power AI processors for edge devices - the Hailo-8 accelerator, Hailo-15 vision processors and Hailo-10H generative-AI module - and became a unicorn with its $136M Series C in 2021. Microchip Technology agreed to buy Hailo in July 2026 and closed the deal on 21 Sept 2026.
interesting_fact: Hailo went from a $3.5M seed round in 2017 to a $1B valuation in 2021, and its Hailo-10H powers what ASUS billed as the world's first USB edge-AI accelerator.
deep_cut_fact: At Calcalist's AI Conference in Sept 2025 he argued AI's next frontier is embodied systems: 'What's really big in AI today is undoubtedly the cloud, but the issue of AI entering the physical world is a revolution no less significant,' adding that China's robot competitions 'feel like the moments before ChatGPT.'
notes: Hailo's site still lists him as CEO, but his role post-Microchip acquisition (Sept 2026) should be checked. Strong fit for an edge-vs-datacenter AI compute conversation; regular conference speaker (CES, Calcalist). info@ is a general company inbox.

name: Jeffrey Spector
current_role: Co-founder and President, Karat (technical-interviewing and workforce-intelligence company, Seattle)
profile: Co-founded Karat in 2014 with Mo Bhende (now CEO) to re-engineer the technical interview for software engineers, outsourcing structured interviews to professional 'Interview Engineers'. Karat, valued around $1B, now pitches AI-native simulations and workforce intelligence for engineering leaders in the 'human + AI era'; Spector serves as President.
interesting_fact: Karat says it works with 7 of the 25 largest public companies in the world, 4 of the 7 largest payment companies and all 4 of the largest UK banks, having run hundreds of thousands of technical interviews.
deep_cut_fact: Spector and Bhende were friends who founded Karat around a shared belief that access to career growth is too often limited by where a person went to school, who their friends and family are, or past work experience - so they set out to make the technical interview itself more objective.
notes: Fit for data-center/AI podcast is indirect (hiring/talent in the AI era). Route via press@karat.com.

name: Mohit Bhende
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Karat (Seattle technical-interviewing / Human+AI hiring platform)
profile: Mohit 'Mo' Bhende co-founded Karat in 2014 with Jeffrey Spector to re-engineer how software engineers are interviewed; Karat runs technical interviews for large enterprises and reached unicorn valuation in 2021. Before Karat he was a senior director at Microsoft working on Xbox product strategy (including in China), and a strategy consultant at Oliver Wyman.
interesting_fact: Karat built a professional class of 'Interview Engineers' who conduct technical interviews on behalf of client companies, and in 2025 it pushed into AI-era hiring with products such as Partner Talent Solution for grading contractor engineers.
deep_cut_fact: He was in the very first cohort of Gates Cambridge Scholars (2001), doing an MPhil in Economics at Trinity Hall. In 2024 he spoke at a Gates Cambridge/Cambridge in America event in Seattle about purposeful leadership.
notes: Press contact in Karat releases: Gordie Hanrahan, Sr. Director Communications (press@karat.com). He also co-founded Seattle-based Topic Magazine (per secondary profiles, not verified). Gates Cambridge annual report 2024 lists him as a 2001 first-cohort scholar. Don't confuse Karat with Karat Packaging or Karat Financial.

name: Oleg Rogynskyy
current_role: Founder and Board Member, Backstory (formerly People.ai); Jason Ambrose is now CEO
profile: Oleg Rogynskyy founded People.ai in 2016, an AI platform that automatically captures sales activity (emails, meetings, calls) into CRM data and turns it into revenue insights; it reached unicorn status (~$1B valuation per Hurun). The company has since rebranded as Backstory, an 'AI answers platform for sales teams'; Rogynskyy remains founder and board member while Jason Ambrose runs it as CEO.
interesting_fact: People.ai, now Backstory, says it has spent more than a decade training AI models on billions of sales interactions, and was named a Challenger in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant for Revenue Action Orchestration.
notes: No longer CEO, so company PR may not route to him; his own domain olegrogynskyy.com redirects to his LinkedIn, the best direct route. Current new ventures not verified (web-search quota exhausted mid-lane). Fit: AI/sales data, not energy.

name: Jonathan Webb
current_role: Co-founder of Pharmapacks (later renamed Packable); co-founder and CEO of Packable per directory profiles; current activity unverified
profile: Jonathan Webb is one of five co-founders of Pharmapacks (2010, New York), which grew from a Bronx pharmacy operation into one of Amazon's largest US third-party sellers of health and beauty products and was valued at about $1B. It was renamed Packable, an e-commerce enablement company, and he is listed as its co-founder and CEO. His background is in spirits and luxury marketing and sales.
interesting_fact: Pharmapacks went from a Bronx retail pharmacy to one of the biggest sellers on Amazon in the US, built by a small group of friends.
deep_cut_fact: Before e-commerce, he co-founded LeSutra, a sparkling liqueur launched in 2012 with music producer Timbaland and Grey Goose co-founder Tom Bruno, with fellow future Pharmapacks co-founder Adam Berkowitz.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Packable (ex-Pharmapacks) went through Chapter 11 in 2022 after a planned SPAC deal fell through, so avoid framing outreach around the company's valuation. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Jordan Feldman
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Rightway (New York)
profile: Harvard-educated former Goldman Sachs banker who co-founded Rightway (c.2017), a New York healthcare-navigation and pharmacy-benefits company combining clinician-led support with an app to help members find high-quality, cost-efficient care. Rightway reached a unicorn valuation and Feldman remains CEO.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Rightway with his father, physician Dr. Theodore Feldman (its chief medical officer); his father's experience as a doctor inspired the clinician-led model.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare he worked on Goldman Sachs' Mortgage Trading and Investment Banking teams, then left to help found RedBird Capital Partners, Gerry Cardinale's private-equity firm; he holds an A.B. in Government and Economics from Harvard.
notes: Speaks at Conference Board events; reachable via Rightway's press/marketing team or LinkedIn.

name: Theodore Feldman
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Medical Officer, Rightway (New York)
profile: Dr. Ted Feldman is a Miami cardiologist who co-founded Rightway in 2017 with his son, CEO Jordan Feldman, to give employees physician-backed help navigating healthcare. Rightway has since become a transparent pharmacy-benefits (PBM) alternative valued at over $1B, and was reported in Sept 2026 to be eyeing an IPO after new funding.
interesting_fact: Rightway's founding story is a family one: Jordan Feldman grew up with a cardiologist father at his side and saw how transformative expert clinical guidance could be, so the two set out to give every member that access.
deep_cut_fact: A Harvard College and Albert Einstein College of Medicine graduate, he trained in cardiology at the University of Miami/Jackson Memorial and has served as medical director of the South Miami Heart Center and Baptist Health South Florida's Center for Healthy Living.
notes: Practising physician with low media profile; son Jordan Feldman (CEO) is the public face. Rightway's about page says media inquiries go to info@rightwayhealthcare.com; press page also lists press@. Deep-cut bio is from a CME faculty page (Miami cardiologist Theodore Feldman) - matches but not explicitly linked to Rightway there.

name: David Cummings
current_role: Founder, Atlanta Tech Village; founder/CEO, Atlanta Ventures
profile: Atlanta serial entrepreneur David Cummings co-founded marketing-automation firm Pardot, which was sold to ExactTarget (later Salesforce) for $95M in 2012. He then co-founded SalesLoft with Kyle Porter. Salesloft reached a $1B+ valuation before Vista Equity bought it. He now runs the Atlanta Tech Village startup hub and the Atlanta Ventures fund.
interesting_fact: Atlanta Tech Village, which he founded, is billed as the Southeast's largest tech entrepreneur center. Its alumni include SalesLoft, Calendly and Terminus. He was an early investor in Calendly.
deep_cut_fact: A Tallahassee, Florida native with an economics degree from Duke, he has founded 10+ companies. Besides software, they include Intown Golf Club, an Atlanta indoor golf venture.
notes: Very accessible. He has blogged on davidcummings.org for years and is active on X. Atlanta Tech Village and Atlanta Ventures are natural routes in.

name: Kyle Porter
current_role: Founder and board member/former chairman, Salesloft (now merged with Clari); LP at Stage 2 Capital
profile: Atlanta entrepreneur who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft in 2011 out of Georgia Tech's ATDC and led it as CEO through Vista Equity's ~$2.3bn acquisition (2021). He stepped down as CEO in 2023 (David Obrand succeeded him) and stayed on the board; Salesloft agreed to merge with Clari in 2025.
interesting_fact: Porter insisted Salesloft stay an 'Atlanta unicorn', refusing investor pressure to relocate; early culture perks included rotating a Porsche 911 to the top sales rep each month.
deep_cut_fact: Salesloft killed its original, most profitable product, the lead-scraping tool Prospector, because customers were using it for spam, betting the company on Cadence, then a tiny ~$75k business, which became the flagship.
notes: Active in Atlanta startup ecosystem (Endeavor Atlanta board per directories) and appears on podcasts; LinkedIn is the most direct published route.

name: Rob Forman
current_role: CEO coach (listed with Scalebound); independent board member (e.g., Grayscale); co-founder & former President, Salesloft
profile: Atlanta software engineer-turned-founder who co-founded Salesloft, the sales engagement platform, serving as head of technology and later President & Chief Strategy Officer. Vista Equity Partners acquired Salesloft in December 2021 for $2.3B. He now coaches CEOs on organizational health and execution and sits on company boards.
interesting_fact: Salesloft, which he co-founded and served as President, was acquired by Vista Equity Partners in December 2021 for $2.3B.
deep_cut_fact: Before Salesloft he co-founded HireIQ, a call-center hiring and machine-learning analytics company, serving as its CTO; it was later acquired by Verint Systems.
notes: Faith-driven entrepreneur active in the Praxis network; LinkedIn is the best published route. Board roles (Grayscale, Hubstaff) per aggregators, unverified on primary sources.

name: Tim Dorr
current_role: Co-founder of Salesloft; Atlanta startup investor/engineer (Techstars Atlanta MD 2022-24, later co-chair; current employer reported inconsistently)
profile: Georgia Tech-rooted Atlanta engineer who co-founded sales-engagement platform Salesloft (2011, with Kyle Porter and Rob Forman) and served as its original technical architect/CTO; Salesloft reached unicorn status and was sold to Vista Equity in 2021. In March 2022 he became Managing Director of Techstars Atlanta (with Cox Enterprises), backing local founders.
interesting_fact: On taking the Techstars Atlanta job he said he wanted to 'pay back into the ecosystem that has gotten me this far' and that he looks for 'the less-than-perfect founder, that 95% founder.'
deep_cut_fact: He is a long-time open-source maintainer of Redux, the JavaScript state-management library used by millions of web apps; his npm handle 'timdorr' sits on the Redux package maintainer list alongside creator Dan Abramov (gaearon) and Mark Erikson.
notes: Current day job unclear: aggregator profiles mention a principal-engineer role at 8th Light (2025) and Techstars Atlanta co-chair; verify before outreach. Very approachable in Atlanta tech circles (ATDC EIR, Atlanta Tech Village advisor). No published email found.

name: Jacob Boudreau
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Stord (Atlanta)
profile: Co-founded Atlanta-based Stord in 2015 with CEO Sean Henry out of Georgia Tech's CREATE-X student incubator; Stord started as a peer-to-peer storage idea and pivoted into an on-demand warehousing network and now a 'cloud supply chain' (fulfillment, OMS, software) for consumer brands. A 2025 Series F valued it around $3B. Boudreau leads technology as CTO.
interesting_fact: Stord came out of Georgia Tech's CREATE-X student startup program, and Atlanta security entrepreneur Chris Klaus (ISS founder), who backs CREATE-X, became one of Stord's early investors; Henry met him at Georgia Tech.
deep_cut_fact: Boudreau and Henry were named to Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2018, then picked as 'All-Star Alumni' on the 2020 Manufacturing & Industry list, which recognizes those 'creating the products, methods and materials of tomorrow.'
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Sean Henry is the public face. Recent Stord releases (2025-26) list David Packman as media contact.

name: Sean Henry
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Stord (commerce enablement / fulfillment, Atlanta)
profile: Atlanta native who co-founded Stord with Jacob Boudreau in 2015 as a Georgia Tech freshman, dropping out at 19. Stord provides warehousing, fulfillment and software that give independent brands Amazon-like shipping; a $250M Series F reportedly valued it around $3B. Thiel Fellow, Forbes 30 Under 30 (2019) and named by Forbes in 2021 the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company.
interesting_fact: Forbes recognized him in 2021 as the youngest CEO of a $1B+ company; he founded Stord at 18.
deep_cut_fact: The Stord idea crystallized days before his first Georgia Tech classes, while telling his family about his summer job at a manufacturer in Germany. He also dropped out before learning he'd won the Thiel Fellowship: 'I jumped two feet in and hoped they said yes later.'
notes: Accessible, media-friendly founder (Entrepreneur bylines, Not Another CEO interview). Logistics/supply-chain angle fits the podcast.

name: Arad Levertov
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Sunbit
profile: Israeli-born fintech founder who co-founded Sunbit in 2016 (with Tal Riesenfeld, Ornit Dweck-Maizel and Prof. Tamir Hazan) after serving as COO/EVP at online lender Enova and earlier at Intel. Sunbit offers point-of-sale 'pay-over-time' financing at dentists, auto-service shops and other everyday merchants; it was valued at $1.1B in 2021 and completed its first $200M ABS deal in 2025.
interesting_fact: Named an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2025 Greater Los Angeles award winner.
deep_cut_fact: He has said a personal experience of being rejected for a credit card - which he found humiliating - was a major reason he started Sunbit, whose pitch is approving people with thin credit files.
notes: Has done many podcasts (Mixergy, DealMakers, Fintech Business Weekly) - receptive to founder-story interviews. Reported military background varies between sources; not used.

name: Ornit Dweck-Maizel
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Sunbit (Los Angeles / Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli-born fintech engineer who co-founded buy-now-pay-later company Sunbit in 2016 with Arad Levertov and Tal Riesenfeld. As CTO she built the technology that lets dental offices, auto service departments and retailers offer instant point-of-sale financing; Sunbit was valued at ~$1.1B in 2021. Earlier she worked at Intel, SuperDerivatives and as VP R&D at Whipclip.
interesting_fact: Sunbit's financing is offered in roughly one in six US auto dealership service departments.
deep_cut_fact: With no offices at the start, she held Sunbit's first engineering team meeting in her in-laws' backyard garage at the end of a dirt road; after working late the team walked out by phone flashlight over rain-soaked mud.
notes: Also known as Ornit Maizel. Degrees: BSc Information Systems Engineering (Ben-Gurion Univ.), MBA in Finance (Tel Aviv Univ.). Mentors startups.

name: Tal Riesenfeld
current_role: Co-founder, Sunbit (Los Angeles-based point-of-sale financing); listed as Chief Revenue Officer/Head of Sales
profile: Israeli-born co-founder of Sunbit, a buy-now-pay-later platform for in-person purchases such as auto repair, dental and optical care, founded in 2016 with Arad Levertov, Ornit Dweck-Maizel and Prof. Tamir Hazan and valued at ~$1B+. He leads Sunbit's revenue/sales effort. Before Sunbit he co-founded video-ad company Eyeview (2008) and worked at HP and Google.
interesting_fact: Sunbit CEO Arad Levertov recruited Riesenfeld because they had known each other since childhood. Each of them put in $100,000 of his own money to start the company.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunbit, he co-founded the video-advertising startup Eyeview in 2008, where he was VP of Sales, so Sunbit is his second venture-backed company.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Arad Levertov is Sunbit's public face. Riesenfeld's background (HBS MBA, HP, Google, Eyeview) comes from aggregator profiles such as TheOrg and Crunchbase. Route via Sunbit media@sunbit.com.

name: Tamir Hazan
current_role: Co-founder & Head of AI/ML, Sunbit; faculty member at Technion
profile: Machine-learning academic who co-founded Sunbit, the buy-now-pay-later/point-of-sale financing fintech valued at about $1.1B, and leads its AI/ML. Sunbit's site calls him 'Published author. Professor. Tech-leader.' He heads an ML data lab at Technion and has held posts at UChicago and the University of Haifa. Arad Levertov is CEO.
interesting_fact: He keeps a dual career: he runs Sunbit's AI/ML while heading a machine-learning lab at Technion, and has written more than 35 publications.
deep_cut_fact: Before Sunbit his academic path ran through the University of Chicago and the University of Haifa as well as Technion, where Sunbit's bio says he now heads a machine-learning data lab.
notes: Academic and technical co-founder; CEO Arad Levertov is Sunbit's public face. An academic angle (ML research, credit-underwriting AI) is probably the best hook. I couldn't load his Technion and TTIC pages (bot-blocked), so I couldn't confirm specific research details.

name: Harry Franks
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Zego (stepped away from day-to-day role; Zego says he still provides 'ongoing support')
profile: London entrepreneur who co-founded Zego in 2016 with fellow Deliveroo alumnus Sten Saar after seeing how hard it was for couriers to get flexible insurance. Zego's pay-as-you-go and fleet insurance for gig-economy drivers made it a UK insurtech unicorn. Franks later left the company; no new venture has been publicly announced.
interesting_fact: Zego was born at Deliveroo: Franks saw first-hand that the company's couriers struggled to buy insurance that matched their part-time, on-demand work.
deep_cut_fact: He had no insurance background: before Zego he was Deliveroo's global head of procurement and earlier worked at luxury home-rental startup onefinestay.
notes: Left Zego (reported by Insurance Post / Insurance Times, citing personal reasons); keep outreach light. Low public profile since; no published personal contact found. LinkedIn is the likely route.

name: Sten Saar
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Zego
profile: Estonian entrepreneur who moved to London, worked in operations at onefinestay and Deliveroo, and in 2016 co-founded Zego with Harry Franks and Stuart Kelly to sell flexible insurance to gig-economy delivery drivers. Zego hit a $1B+ valuation in 2021, expanded into fleet and telematics car insurance, and reported monthly profitability in Q4 2024.
interesting_fact: Zego was born from a gap Saar spotted at Deliveroo: couriers had no flexible, pay-as-you-work insurance.
deep_cut_fact: At 17 in Estonia he launched a business selling notepads to students that earned about $1 million across four countries while he studied business and management.
notes: Has appeared on The F in Tech podcast. No generic press email confirmed; Zego newsroom pages list an obfuscated contact address.

name: Stuart Kelly
current_role: Co-founder of Zego (technical co-founder, formerly CTO); current title not confirmed
profile: London software engineer who co-founded insurtech Zego in 2016 with Harry Franks and Sten Saar, all ex-onefinestay. As technical co-founder he built the platform that prices pay-as-you-go insurance for gig-economy drivers by the hour; Zego reached a $1.1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Zego's first-ever sale was a £2.30 policy, sold after Kelly finished the mobile app in under four months.
deep_cut_fact: He created Zego's proprietary software that uses algorithms to assess a new driver's risk and spin up fresh policies by the hour - the 'secret sauce' behind its gig-worker cover.
notes: Very low public profile; engineer rather than public-facing exec. Some listings say he moved from CTO to a principal/staff engineer role. Co-founders Franks/Saar are more media-facing.

name: Andrew Farah
current_role: CEO and co-founder, Density (workplace occupancy analytics)
profile: Andrew Farah co-founded Density, which builds privacy-first people-counting sensors (designed and assembled in the US) and analytics showing how offices are used. Density has raised $225M+, serves clients such as Uber, Shopify and Pinterest in 30+ countries, and Farah is a frequent voice on return-to-office data.
interesting_fact: Density's sensors deliberately avoid cameras to protect privacy, and the company keeps sensor design and assembly in the United States to protect IP and quality control.
notes: X and LinkedIn listed are the company's accounts, not his personal ones. Media-friendly CEO (many RTO interviews in 2025), so press@density.io is a realistic route. Data-center angle is indirect (physical-space sensing/AI analytics).

name: Ben Redfield
current_role: Co-founder of Density; reportedly now managing partner at Bread, a software product firm (per podcast listing)
profile: Ben Redfield (Syracuse iSchool '12) co-founded Density in 2014 at Syracuse's Tech Garden incubator with fellow alumni including CEO Andrew Farah. Density makes privacy-preserving people-counting sensors for workplaces and reached a ~$1B valuation. He later moved on to lead Bread, which helps companies design and deploy software systems.
interesting_fact: Density started in 2014 in the Tech Garden incubator in downtown Syracuse with six co-founders, five of them Syracuse University alumni, and grew to offices in San Francisco and New York.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded Density straight out of Syracuse University's School of Information Studies (iSchool, class of 2012), launching it two years after graduating from the Tech Garden incubator in downtown Syracuse.
notes: No longer listed on Density's site; press@density.io reaches Density, not him. Current role (Bread) is from a podcast listing: https://chartable.com/podcasts/the-louis-and-kyle-show/episodes/148306219-benjamin-redfield-managing-partner-at-bread-and-founder-of-density

name: Brian Weinreich
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Density (San Francisco); not on Density's current leadership page - current role unverified
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder list (2021-2024) names him as a founder of Density, the San Francisco maker of privacy-preserving people-counting sensors and occupancy analytics for workplaces (raised $225M+; clients occupy ~1B sq ft). Density's current leadership page lists Andrew Farah as CEO/founder and does not mention Weinreich, so his present involvement could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: Density began as a weekend project to answer whether a favorite coffee shop was busy; it now designs and assembles its sensors in the US and pitches building-utilization data as a climate lever, noting buildings account for 39% of global CO2 emissions.
notes: Could not verify his biography or current role (web-search budget exhausted; Density site does not list him). Company press email is the only published route and he may no longer be at Density. Low priority for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Jordan Messina
current_role: Working on AI at Chainalysis (after Chainalysis acquired his startups Nash and Once Upon in 2025)
profile: Jordan Messina co-founded Density in 2013 (YC S13), the Syracuse-born people-counting sensor company that has raised $225M+. He then moved into crypto - first employee at OpenSea via acquisition, then founder of Nash and Once Upon, both acquired by Chainalysis in 2025 - and now works on AI at Chainalysis. He is no longer in Density's leadership.
interesting_fact: Density began as a weekend project to answer one question - is our favorite coffee shop busy right now? - and became a privacy-preserving people-counting sensor company whose devices are designed and assembled in the US.
deep_cut_fact: In 2018 OpenSea acquired his NFT bartering marketplace Atomic Bazaar; he and partner Dan Viau had also built KittyHats, an early 'layer two' add-on game for CryptoKitties, and KittyExplorer, a popular CryptoKitties analytics tool.
notes: Hurun lists him as Density founder; Density is now led by co-founder/CEO Andrew Farah. His personal site is the best direct route; Density press email only reaches the company he co-founded.

profile: Listed by Hurun's Unicorn Index (2021-2024) as a founder of Density, a U.S. maker of privacy-preserving people-counting/occupancy sensors and workplace analytics (valued around $1B). Density's current leadership page lists Andrew Farah as CEO/founder and does not list Grazioli, so his present role could not be confirmed.

name: Steven VonDeak
profile: Listed by Hurun's unicorn-founder ranking (2021-2024) as a founder of Density, the Syracuse-born (founded 2014) maker of privacy-preserving people-counting sensors and workplace-occupancy analytics, valued around $1B. His current role could not be confirmed: Density's current leadership page lists Andrew Farah as CEO/founder and does not mention VonDeak.
