name: Suhail Doshi
current_role: Founder and CEO, Playground (AI graphic design/image model company)
profile: Self-taught programmer who left Arizona State to co-found product-analytics company Mixpanel with Tim Trefren (YC Summer 2009), serving as CEO until 2018. He then built Mighty (a browser streamed from a data center) before pivoting to Playground, an AI-first graphics editor that trains its own image models.
interesting_fact: Mixpanel's idea came from his 2008 internship at Max Levchin's Slide, where he saw the company spending over $1M to build its own internal analytics, as Zynga and others were doing too.
deep_cut_fact: He landed the Slide internship via an offer over IRC while a computer systems engineering student at ASU; Levchin tried to hire him full-time after three months, but he went back to school and then left to start Mixpanel.
notes: Very active on X (@Suhail) and a frequent podcast guest (Latent Space, YC Lightcone) - X is the most natural public route. Data-center angle: Mighty streamed Chrome from cloud servers; Playground trains large diffusion models.

name: Tim Trefren
current_role: Working on climate at Recheck (identity/compliance platform for US residential solar; reported as co-founder & CEO)
profile: Co-founded product-analytics company Mixpanel with Suhail Doshi in Y Combinator's Summer 2009 batch and worked there 2009-2019 (latterly VP of Customer Success); Mixpanel hit a $1.05B valuation in 2021. He now works on climate through Recheck, a Hanover, NH-based identity, compliance and reputation layer for the residential solar industry.
interesting_fact: Recheck says it has 50,000+ verified solar sales reps and that partners account for 90%+ of US residential solar financing - a natural fit for an energy-focused podcast.
deep_cut_fact: Recheck's founding team is drawn from Mixpanel, HipChat, Notarize and Ohm Analytics, and the company is based in Hanover, New Hampshire rather than Silicon Valley.
notes: YC's Mixpanel page says he is 'now working on climate change at Recheck'; his exact title (CEO) comes from aggregator sites, so confirm. Strong energy-podcast angle (residential solar trust/compliance).

name: Brandon Y Jeon
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (San Mateo, CA / Seoul)
profile: Korean co-founder of Sendbird, the in-app chat, voice and AI-agent API company founded in 2013 with John S. Kim, Harry Kim and Forest Lee; it became a Korean-founded unicorn in 2021 (~$1B+ valuation). Profiles list him in developer-experience/quality-engineering and trust-and-safety roles at the company.
interesting_fact: Sendbird was named among Korea's new unicorns after its 2021 raise, with Jeon listed as one of its four co-founders.
notes: Very low public profile; titles differ across aggregators. Sendbird reportedly grew out of an earlier Korean community app (SmileMom) but only aggregator sources say so. Best route is via Sendbird or CEO John Kim.

name: Forest Lee
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (formerly Head of Design; aggregator profiles list an 'AI Agent Workforce Manager' role since 2025)
profile: Forest Lee is one of the four co-founders of Sendbird (2013, Korea; now San Mateo), the chat/messaging API company valued at $1.05B in 2021 that has pivoted to AI customer-service agents (Delight.ai). He led Sendbird's product design for over a decade; CEO John S. Kim is the company's public face.
interesting_fact: Sendbird began in Seoul in 2013 as a community app for mothers; the team pulled out its messaging engine and turned it into a B2B chat API, becoming only the second Korean company backed by Y Combinator (W16).
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Current role per aggregator profiles (Crunchbase/Humantic) only - verify on LinkedIn. Founder rosters vary by source; MarketScreener lists him as co-founder. Origin story detail also at https://koreatechdesk.com/?p=1370. Route via CEO John Kim/company.

name: Harry Kim
current_role: Co-founder, Sendbird (listed as Founder/CTO on Y Combinator; some profiles say Chief Architect)
profile: Korean-born engineer who co-founded Sendbird with CEO John S. Kim, Brandon Jeon and Forest Lee; it went through Y Combinator (W16), moved HQ to San Mateo and became a chat/messaging API unicorn (~$1B+ valuation in 2021). Sendbird is now pivoting to AI customer-service agents (Delight.ai). Per profiles he was earlier technical director at Paprika Lab (acquired by GREE).
interesting_fact: Sendbird began as a pivot: the team was building 'Smile Mom', an app to connect nearby mothers, couldn't find a good off-the-shelf chat tool, built their own, and friends kept asking to use it - so they turned the chat engine into the company.
notes: Very low public profile; no interviews found. Not to be confused with John S. Kim (CEO). Earlier career details (Paprika Lab, GREE Korea, Wisenut, Monash University) come only from aggregator profiles. No verified Sendbird press email found; a past release listed Moore Communications as PR contact.

name: Peter Meusel
current_role: Co-Founder, Agile Robots SE (Munich); role beyond co-founder not confirmed (TheOrg lists Co-CEO/Managing Director)
profile: German robotics engineer from the German Aerospace Center (DLR) who co-founded Agile Robots in 2018 with Dr. Zhaopeng Chen and eight other DLR experts. The Munich-based DLR spin-off builds force-sensitive robot arms, hands and AI-driven automation systems and has become one of Europe's most valuable robotics companies, backed by Sequoia China, Hillhouse and others.
interesting_fact: Agile Robots' first robot, the seven-axis lightweight arm 'Diana 7', debuted in 2019, only a year after founding; the company has since moved into humanoids and 'physical AI'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agile Robots, Meusel and Chen co-founded an earlier DLR spin-off, Wessling Robotics, built on the humanoid robot hand Chen developed at DLR; Meusel is also credited as a key member of the team behind the DLR/KUKA Light-Weight Robot (LWR).
notes: Low public profile; CEO Zhaopeng Chen is the company's public face. LWR credit comes from his Crunchbase profile (https://www.crunchbase.com/person/peter-meusel). No published press email found on the JS-rendered site.

name: Zhaopeng Chen
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Agile Robots SE (Munich)
profile: Chinese-born roboticist who completed his doctorate at the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and was deputy director of its Modular Dexterous Robotics Lab before co-founding Agile Robots with DLR scientist Peter Meusel in 2018. The Munich company makes force-sensitive AI-driven robot arms and systems and now the Agile ONE humanoid; it became a unicorn in 2021.
interesting_fact: At DLR he worked on the team that developed a widely acclaimed humanoid robotic hand, which became the basis of his first spin-off with Peter Meusel, Wessling Robotics, before Agile Robots.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong science-fiction fan, he says getting into his Chinese university's robotics institute 'was not easy'; from his third year he built robot hands and arms end-to-end, and at DLR spent years on robotic systems for outer space.
notes: No published press email found (site is JS-heavy); use the company website or DLR spin-off page (https://www.dlr.de/en/rm/transfer/spin-offs/agile-robots) for context. Space-robotics and humanoid angle fits a deep-tech podcast.

name: Leng Jing (冷静)
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Mengxiang Technology (梦饷科技, formerly Aikucun / 爱库存); Vice President, China Association of Trade in Services
profile: Shanghai e-commerce executive who co-founded Aikucun in 2017 with founder/chairman Wang Min; the inventory-clearance social-commerce platform rebranded as Mengxiang Group in 2020 and raised a C round that made it a unicorn. Its B2R2C model lets millions of mostly female 'shopkeepers' resell brand stock via mini-stores; she now pitches it as a 'dual SaaS' channel for China's industrial-belt brands.
interesting_fact: By 2021 Mengxiang said it had helped 2M+ shopkeepers, 95.5% of them women (many stay-at-home mothers), earn nearly RMB 5B in income; she frames the business as creating flexible jobs for women.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Aikucun she was VP and partner at the Chinese e-commerce consultancy Zhengwang Consulting (正望咨询) and VP of Tmall service partner Ruijinlin's e-commerce and Yunxiang Digital units.
notes: Hurun lists her as founder; company records name Wang Min as founder/chairman and Leng Jing as co-founder/CEO. Gave a keynote at the June 2026 Cross-Border E-commerce Development Conference (yzwb.net). No published press email found; approach via Mengxiang corporate PR.

name: Jonathan Anguelov
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder of Aircall (left operations Sept 2023); co-founder of real-estate investor Aguesseau Capital; investor-juror on M6's 'Qui veut être mon associé ?'
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded cloud-telephony company Aircall in 2014 with Olivier Pailhès, Pierre-Baptiste Béchu and Xavier Durand; he built its sales organisation and US expansion from New York as Aircall became a $1B+ unicorn. Since leaving operations in 2023 he invests in real estate via Aguesseau Capital, angel-invests and appears as a TV investor.
interesting_fact: Raised in foster care in Sucy-en-Brie, he told his rags-to-unicorn story in the autobiography 'Rien à perdre' (Éditions Alisio / Albin Michel, March 2025).
deep_cut_fact: He sold pizzas at 17 and began investing in real estate at 18 with savings from student jobs; those rental investments were his main income during Aircall's early, unpaid years.
notes: Very public in France (TV, book, podcasts). Aircall went through 500 Startups in San Francisco and raised $2.75M seed. contact@aircall.io is a general company inbox; he is no longer operational there, so outreach via his book publisher or Aguesseau Capital may be better.

name: Olivier Pailhès
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Aircall (returned as CEO on 29 Oct 2026, succeeding Scott Chancellor)
profile: HEC Paris MBA and ex-BCG/ArcelorMittal staffer who co-founded Paris-based cloud phone company Aircall in 2014 with three partners and ran it until 2023, then stayed on the board. He returned as CEO in October 2026 to push Aircall, now at $250M ARR and 24,000+ customers, into AI voice agents.
interesting_fact: On returning as CEO he framed the bet as: 'AI has handed us a rare opportunity; to bring voice back to the center of customer conversations.' Aircall was valued at about $1B+ in its 2021 round.
deep_cut_fact: He is an accomplished pianist - Aircall's own announcement says the Paris team knows that an unscheduled jazz performance usually means the founder is in the building.
notes: Very timely: just returned as CEO (Oct 2026) with an AI-voice-agent agenda. Press contact is Aircall's published media contact on that release.

name: Pierre-Baptiste Béchu
current_role: Co-founder, Aircall; leads the communications-platform (VoIP/WebRTC) engineering team
profile: French engineer and one of Aircall's four co-founders (with Olivier Pailhès, Xavier Durand and Jonathan Anguelov). Joining in 2014, he built the first version of Aircall's backend and infrastructure; the cloud phone system for sales and support teams reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021. He now runs the engineering team behind Aircall's global voice platform and has served as interim CTPO.
interesting_fact: Unusual dual training: a Master of Engineering from École Centrale de Lyon plus a master's in industrial and organizational psychology from Université Lumière Lyon 2.
deep_cut_fact: He personally wrote the first version of Aircall's backend and infrastructure in 2014, and today leads 20+ engineers keeping its worldwide voice services reliable -- voice quality and security are his core focus.
notes: Technical, low-profile co-founder (no CEO role); Aircall's press room lists no email. Also an angel investor (50 Partners, per aggregator profiles -- unverified). A data/infra-focused podcast angle fits him.

name: Thibaud Elziere
current_role: Co-founder of Hexa (formerly eFounders) startup studio; CEO of Folk (CRM built within Hexa)
profile: French serial entrepreneur (b. 1979, Aix-en-Provence) who co-founded stock-photo site Fotolia in 2004 (sold to Adobe in 2014 for ~EUR800M), then in 2011 co-founded startup studio eFounders (Hexa since 2022), which launched ~40 startups including unicorns Spendesk, Front and Aircall. He has run Folk since 2019 and has angel-invested in ~100 startups (Algolia, Notion, Hugging Face).
interesting_fact: Hexa's studio model hands founders a ready idea, seed funding and support; its startups (Spendesk, Front, Aircall) reached a combined ~$5B valuation and ~2,800 jobs.
deep_cut_fact: He started Fotolia while still a student at Ecole Centrale de Lyon, and his side ventures include Gama Space, a solar-sail space project, and Kate, a microcar maker.
notes: Spendesk's operating co-founder/CEO is Rodolphe Ardant; Elziere is co-founder via the eFounders studio. Based in Brussels. Gama Space solar sail could be a good energy/space hook.

name: Xavier Durand
current_role: Co-founder of Aircall (left the company in late 2020); current role not found
profile: French engineer with front-end development expertise who co-founded cloud phone-system company Aircall in 2014 at the eFounders startup studio in Paris, alongside Olivier Pailhes, Jonathan Anguelov and Pierre-Baptiste Bechu. Aircall became eFounders' first unicorn in 2020; Durand left in late 2020.
interesting_fact: Aircall's founders went through the 500 Startups 2015 batch in San Francisco, then raised $2.75M; within five months the team grew from 5 to 15 and turnover tripled.
deep_cut_fact: When Aircall struggled with hiring and fundraising, Durand moved to New York with CEO Olivier Pailhes while the technical team stayed in Paris -- a split that became a blueprint for French founders building in the US.
notes: Very low public profile and no longer at Aircall; contact@aircall.io is a company address, not his. LinkedIn is likely the only route.

name: Anderson Sumarli
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Ajaib Group (Indonesian investment app; also President Commissioner of Ajaib Sekuritas)
profile: Indonesian fintech founder who started Ajaib with Stanford GSB classmate Yada Piyajomkwan; it went through Y Combinator (S18) and became Southeast Asia's first investment-fintech unicorn, offering stocks, mutual funds and crypto. Ajaib also controls Bank Bumi Artha (BNBA). In Aug 2026 it raised a US$270M Series C led by SBI Group at a valuation above its prior ~US$1B mark.
interesting_fact: Ajaib's US$270M Series C (Aug 2026), led by Japan's SBI Group, was reported as Indonesia's biggest tech funding round since 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Ajaib he studied Applied Economics & Management at Cornell (summa cum laude), worked in IBM's Chief Analytics Office (2014-16) and was a BCG consultant (2016-18), then did his MBA at Stanford GSB.
notes: No published press email found on Ajaib's site. Stanford GSB has a case study on Ajaib (useful conversation hook). EY Indonesia 2022 Young Entrepreneur Award; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.

name: Yada Piyajomkwan
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Ajaib (Indonesia)
profile: Thai-born co-founder of Jakarta online brokerage Ajaib, started in 2019 with Stanford GSB classmate Anderson Sumarli; it became a unicorn in 2021 and passed one million investors. Ex-McKinsey and Unilever, Stanford MBA '19; Forbes 30 Under 30 Asia 2020.
interesting_fact: Ajaib went through Y Combinator and hit a $1B valuation in 2021 only about two years after founding; Stanford GSB later wrote a teaching case on it.
deep_cut_fact: She mentors women through UNHCR's Leading Women Fund and She Loves Tech, and was profiled by UNHCR Thailand for that work.
notes: Some older sources list her as COO; recent ones say CPO.

name: Derek Slager
current_role: Co-founder & co-CEO (also CTO), Amperity (Seattle)
profile: Seattle engineer who co-founded customer data platform Amperity (2016) with Kabir Shahani after both were on the founding team of Appature (acquired by IMS Health). He built Amperity's patented ML-based identity resolution; the company hit a $1B valuation in 2020. Now co-CEO leading its AI-first transformation.
interesting_fact: Amperity uses machine learning rather than hand-written rules to resolve customer identity, stitching together billions of records across a brand's systems; the patented identity resolution was built under Slager.
deep_cut_fact: Before Amperity and Appature he was a software developer at Seattle-era companies Activate, Loudeye (an early digital-music/streaming firm) and Blue Dot, then ran engineering at IMS Health after Appature's acquisition.
notes: Frequent podcast guest (NVIDIA AI Podcast 2025, Databricks Data+AI Summit speaker). Amperity site titles vary (CTO vs co-CEO).

name: Kabir Shahani
current_role: Founder, Amp It Up Ventures; co-founder and former CEO of Amperity; Affiliate Assistant Professor, UW Information School
profile: Seattle entrepreneur (b. 1982, Kansas City) who co-founded health-marketing software firm Appature (sold to IMS Health in 2013) and then customer-data platform Amperity (2016) with Derek Slager, leading it to unicorn status before stepping down as CEO in 2022. He now incubates and backs software startups through Amp It Up Ventures and teaches at UW.
interesting_fact: Holds more than 10 US patents spanning databases, entity resolution and machine learning; Amperity worked with UW's Dan Suciu on a probabilistic customer database.
deep_cut_fact: He founded his first company at 24 and was named the U.S. Small Business Administration's Young Entrepreneur of the Year in 2012; he earned a BS in Informatics from UW in 2004.
notes: Email is his UW iSchool affiliate-faculty address published by the university. 2024 GeekWire piece on his new venture: https://www.geekwire.com/2024/ex-amperity-ceo-kabir-shahani-is-amped-about-building-startups-with-his-latest-venture/

name: Amir Jerbi
current_role: Co-founder of Aqua Security; strategic advisor since stepping down as CTO in November 2025
profile: Israeli security engineer who served about four years in an IDF IT unit and later became a chief architect at a large security software company (CA Technologies). In 2015 he co-founded Aqua Security with Dror Davidoff; the cloud-native and container security company reached a $1B valuation in 2021. In November 2025 both founders stepped back to advisory roles, Mike Dube became CEO and Nir Makowski became chief product and technology officer.
interesting_fact: Aqua grew out of a weekly meetup. Jerbi saw an early Docker demo, went home, 'fell in love' with containers within days, and then quit his chief-architect job to work on container security full time.
deep_cut_fact: He has said he decided that 'leveraging containers for better security was my destiny'. He first worked on it as a 'new hobby' before founding Aqua with friends a year later; the original idea was to make containerised apps 'secured anywhere' as well as 'run anywhere'.
notes: The leadership change is dated 5 Nov 2025 (Calcalist). As of 2025, Aqua's press releases appear to route media through an agency (Look Left Marketing), but I could not open the release to verify the address, so it is not recorded. Note that Aqua cut staff after the 2025 reorganisation. He is a technical voice on cloud and container security and appeared on 'The IaC Podcast'.

name: Dror Davidoff
current_role: Co-founder and strategic advisor, Aqua Security (stepped down as CEO in Nov 2025)
profile: Dror Davidoff co-founded cloud-native security company Aqua Security in Ramat Gan in 2015 with CTO Amir Jerbi and was its CEO for a decade, growing it to about 450 staff, roughly $235M raised and a peak valuation of about $1B. In November 2025 he stepped back to strategic advisor, and President/CRO Mike Dube became CEO.
interesting_fact: Aqua was founded as 'Scalock' and rebranded in 2016. Jerbi said the original name 'ended up not fitting what we aim to do.'
deep_cut_fact: Before Aqua, Davidoff was EVP Sales & Business Development at database-security startup Sentrigo (joined 2008), which McAfee acquired in 2011. He then headed global sales of database security products at McAfee (Intel Security).

public_contacts.value: Look Left Marketing (Aqua's media contact on 2025 releases, e.g. Geena Pickering / Jennifer Tanner)

notes: Now an advisor, no longer running Aqua day to day, so he may have more time for a podcast. He has author pages on Dark Reading and Cloud Native Now. The PR agency was seen via a search snippet (page blocked direct fetch).

name: Adam Crawshaw
current_role: Unverified; co-founder and former President of Assembly (e-commerce software group behind Helium 10, Refersion and Pacvue)
profile: Adam Crawshaw is listed as a co-founder of Assembly, an e-commerce software roll-up formed around 2018. Assembly bought Refersion and Amazon-seller tool Helium 10 in 2020, then the ad platform Pacvue in 2021, and later unified its products under the Pacvue brand. In July 2020 he was quoted as President of Assembly. His current role could not be verified from official sources.
interesting_fact: Assembly assembled Helium 10, the Amazon-seller toolkit, and Pacvue, the commerce-advertising platform, into one software group serving brands that sell on online marketplaces.
notes: Identity marked uncertain: the only official mention found is a 2020 Assembly press release naming him 'President of Assembly'. Co-founder status and later roles (Refersion GM, Helium 10 GM) come only from aggregator profiles. Don't confuse this Assembly with the ad agency Assembly Global. No published contact found.

name: Sandeep Kella
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman of the Board, Pacvue (since Sept 2024; previously CEO)
profile: Co-founder and former CEO of Assembly, an e-commerce software roll-up that bought Amazon-seller tool Helium 10 (2020) and enterprise retail-media platform Pacvue (2021), then took the Pacvue name. In September 2024 he handed the CEO role to Rahul Choraria and became executive chairman, overseeing strategy.
interesting_fact: He bought Pacvue just one month after an Advent International-led round pushed Assembly's valuation above $1B; Pacvue says revenue quadrupled in four years and it has been 'highly profitable since inception'.
deep_cut_fact: When he stepped up to executive chairman in 2024 he brought onto Pacvue's board Harry Shum, the computer scientist who led Microsoft's AI and Research group.
notes: Acquirer/operator rather than original Pacvue founder (Pacvue was founded by Melissa Burdick and others; Kella co-founded Assembly). Low media profile.

name: Criag Iley
current_role: Founder of Business Finance Market (UK SME lending platform), per 2022 interview; current role not verified
profile: UK banker (name is Craig Iley; input has a typo) who joined Atom Bank from Santander as commercial/business banking director and is described as a co-founder of Atom Bank and of Bank North. He later founded Business Finance Market, a platform matching lenders with SMEs. Atom's commonly cited founders are Anthony Thomson and Mark Mullen, so 'founder' attribution is loose.
interesting_fact: He argues the UK has room for about ten more SME lenders in a ~£200bn market, and that a new bank needs 6-10 years to build a £5bn lending book; he points to Germany's tiered banking system as a model.
notes: Hurun listing 'Atom Bank founder' is a stretch; he was an early senior exec (Finextra: 'Atom names Santander's Craig Iley as commercial director', https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/55176/atom-names-santanders-craig-iley-as-commercial-director). Low profile; likely not UHNW. Alive status not specifically confirmed.

name: Gal Shaul
current_role: Co-founder, Augury Inc. (industrial AI / machine health, New York & Israel); current title not verified
profile: Gal Shaul co-founded Augury in 2011 (with CEO Saar Yoskovitz). Augury uses AI on vibration, temperature and magnetic sensor data to predict machine failures in factories. It launched its Machine Health product in 2017, became one of the first industrial-AI unicorns in 2021 and closed a Series F in 2025. It now pitches an 'Industrial AI Workforce' of monitoring and AI agents for manufacturers in 10+ industries.
interesting_fact: Augury's own timeline marks 2019 as the year its system first helped a manufacturer avoid a production loss, two years after Machine Health launched; in 2021 it became one of the first industrial-AI unicorns.
notes: Augury's leadership page is JS-rendered and the web-search budget was exhausted, so his current title (formerly CTO, per general knowledge, unverified here) and personal background were not confirmed. Co-founder Saar Yoskovitz is the public face. Good fit for an energy-efficiency and industrial-AI angle. Best route: Panblast PR.

name: Saar Yoskovitz
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Augury (machine-health AI; Haifa/Tel Aviv and New York)
profile: Saar Yoskovitz, a Technion graduate in electrical engineering and physics, co-founded Augury in 2012 with CTO Gal Shaul. Augury combines IoT sensors and AI to monitor industrial machines and predict failures before they happen, for customers such as PepsiCo, Nestlé and Colgate-Palmolive. It became a unicorn with a $180M round in October 2021 and raised $75M at a >$1B valuation in February 2025.
interesting_fact: Augury's sensors 'listen' to machines, continuously capturing sound, temperature and electromagnetic signals so AI can detect faults early. Its customers include utilities such as Israel Electric Corporation and the national water company Mekorot.
deep_cut_fact: Augury started small: its first seed round, in October 2014, raised just $2M, well before the later $55M and $180M rounds. In 2019 it acquired the US startup Alluvium. In 2021 it won Israel's Atlas Award.
notes: He is a strong fit for an industrial-AI/energy-efficiency episode and is a frequent speaker. augury.com blocked automated access (403), so I could not retrieve a press email or contact form. The web-search budget was exhausted before I could verify his social accounts. Try Augury's newsroom page manually.

name: Hari Ravichandran
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aura (digital safety; ASX: AXQ after the 2026 Qoria merger)
profile: Indian-born American serial founder. He started BizLand, which grew into Endurance International Group (Bluehost, HostGator), and ran it until 2017. He has been CEO of Aura, a consumer identity-theft and online-safety company, since 2019. In 2026 Aura completed its acquisition of Australia's Qoria, creating a group with more than $300M ARR that trades on the ASX as AXQ.
interesting_fact: He started BizLand with most of his $8,000 savings. After the dot-com crash he cut staff to 14 and made customers pay subscriptions; only about 2% converted, yet the company broke even the next year on $2M revenue.
deep_cut_fact: Instead of spending on marketing, Endurance grew by buying small hosting firms with 2,000-5,000 customers each, often with seller financing. His lesson from the crash: 'If you don't focus on profitability, things can go bad.'
notes: Aura's bio says he has an MBA from Wharton, a computer engineering degree from Mississippi State and studied electrical engineering at Stanford. He founded the Ravichandran Foundation (Boston area and India; source: latinpost). Aura is now ASX-listed, so ASX investor-relations channels apply.

name: Kam Ghaffarian
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Axiom Space; founder of X-energy; co-founder of Intuitive Machines and Quantum Space
profile: Iranian-born American engineer-entrepreneur who moved to the US at 17. Co-founded NASA contractor Stinger Ghaffarian Technologies (sold to KBR for $355M in 2018), then built a space-and-energy portfolio: X-energy (high-temperature gas-cooled nuclear reactors, 2009), Intuitive Machines (Moon lander, public via SPAC 2023), Axiom Space (private space station, 2016) and Quantum Space (2020).
interesting_fact: Watching the 1969 Apollo 11 landing on TV in Iran sparked his interest in space; decades later his Intuitive Machines lander touched down on the Moon on Feb 22, 2024. His X-energy nuclear reactor company makes him directly relevant to energy/data-center power.
deep_cut_fact: As keynote speaker at Capitol Technology University's May 2, 2026 commencement (his alma mater: BS 1983, PhD 2022), he surprised every graduate crossing the stage with $1,500 in a gold envelope.
notes: Also founded nonprofit Limitless Space Institute (2019). X-energy (nuclear SMRs) is the strongest angle for an energy/data-center podcast; X-energy's press office is an alternative route.

name: Michael Suffredini
current_role: Co-founder, board member and advisor, Axiom Space (CEO until Aug 2024)
profile: Mike Suffredini spent decades at NASA, including as International Space Station program manager (2005-2015), overseeing completion of ISS assembly. In 2016 he co-founded Houston-based Axiom Space with Kam Ghaffarian to build the first commercial space station, and led it as president/CEO; he stepped down as CEO in August 2024 and remains a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: His honors include the NASA Distinguished Service Medal, Presidential Meritorious and Distinguished Executive ranks, the National Air and Space Museum Trophy and the Yuri Gagarin Medal.
deep_cut_fact: After watching Neil Armstrong land on the Moon as a child he wanted to be a 'space guy'; at UT Austin (aerospace engineering, 1983) he originally aimed at high-performance aircraft until studying orbital dynamics under Victor Szebehely pulled him toward space. He also created NASA's ISS Research Office.
notes: Stepped back from CEO 'for personal reasons' (Axiom release Aug 2024) - avoid probing. Axiom now markets orbital data centers, a strong hook for an energy/data-center podcast. Current Axiom CEO is Tejpaul Bhatia (since Apr 2025).

name: Jaswinder Chadha
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Axtria Inc. (life-sciences data/analytics software, New Jersey)
profile: Jaswinder 'Jassi' Chadha co-founded Axtria in 2010, building it into a cloud software and analytics provider for pharma commercial operations (sales, marketing, data management) valued around $1B. An IIT Delhi mechanical engineer with operations-research graduate training (UTEP, Texas A&M), he has worked with 100+ global companies.
interesting_fact: Twice named E&Y Entrepreneur of the Year; also received the Pharmaceutical Management Science Association Lifetime Achievement Award and IIT Delhi's Distinguished Alumni Award (2022).
deep_cut_fact: He endowed a Chair in Operations Research at IIT Delhi (2008) and a Chair in Data Analytics (2021) named after himself and his mother, who in 1968 became the first woman to earn a maths PhD from IIT Delhi - making them IIT Delhi's first parent-child graduates.
notes: Goes by 'Jassi'. Co-founder Navdeep Chadha is CTO. A 2022 press release listed an individual Axtria media contact; the general connect@ inbox is the stable published route.

name: Navdeep (Navi) Chadha
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Axtria
profile: Navi Chadha co-founded Axtria in 2010 with his brother Jassi Chadha (CEO); the company provides AI-powered data analytics and cloud software to the life sciences industry. He previously co-founded pharma analytics firm marketRx, acquired by Cognizant in 2007, and has 20+ years in pharma analytics.
interesting_fact: He has been recognised as an EY Entrepreneur of the Year and a Top Industry Leader by Life Sciences Voice; his mantra for pharma AI is 'start with the data foundation, not with the AI.'
deep_cut_fact: Outside work he runs Spartan obstacle races, rides both a bicycle and his Harley, plays golf and skis; the family dog is an Australian Labradoodle named Bear (pharmaphorum '12 Questions', May 2026).
notes: connect@axtria.com is Axtria's general contact address. Pharmaphorum interview invites readers to connect with him on LinkedIn.

name: Peter Chaljawski
current_role: Founder of Berlin Brands Group (formerly Chal-Tec); stepped down as CEO in January 2024
profile: Berlin entrepreneur who founded Chal-Tec in 2005 at 19, selling affordable DJ and event gear on eBay, then expanded into audio and household appliances (Klarstein, auna, blumfeldt). Renamed Berlin Brands Group in 2019, it became a D2C/Amazon-marketplace unicorn backed by Ardian. He handed the CEO role to ex-eBay manager Eben Sermon in Jan 2024 after 18 years.
interesting_fact: He skipped university: he postponed his studies, never started them, and used his savings to found Chal-Tec, saying 'we basically democratized DJ equipment' by offering affordable alternatives to premium brands.
deep_cut_fact: The company began because at 18 he wanted DJ equipment and found only expensive premium gear or cheap junk; he asked why there was no 'Zara' of DJ gear. Its first eBay sale came in 2007, and he personally oversaw construction of the company's central warehouse.
notes: Left CEO role Jan 2024 (Börsen-Zeitung, https://www.boersen-zeitung.de/personen/berlin-brands-group-holt-ebay-veteranen-an-die-spitze). A deutsche-startups.de headline links him to 'D11Z.Ventures' investments (not verified). Named to Capital's Top 40 under 40 (2021). BBG website was unreachable this session; no contact verified.

name: Chanakya Hridaya
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and COO, BlackBuck Limited (formerly Zinka Logistics Solutions), a listed company
profile: Chanakya Hridaya co-founded BlackBuck in Bengaluru in 2015 with Rajesh Yabaji and B. Ramasubramaniam. BlackBuck is a digital platform for India's truck operators, covering payments, telematics, freight marketplace and vehicle finance. It listed in India in 2024 and has since renamed itself from Zinka Logistics Solutions to BlackBuck Limited. Hridaya is an executive director and promoter.
interesting_fact: BlackBuck, which he co-founded, listed on Indian exchanges in 2024. Its investor-relations page publishes his employment agreement among the IPO material documents, and he is named as a promoter and executive director.
deep_cut_fact: Before BlackBuck he worked in ITC Limited's supply-chain division. He holds a B.Tech in mechanical engineering and a master's in manufacturing science and engineering from IIT Kharagpur (per his company bio as quoted).

public_contacts.value: cs@blackbuck.com (Company Secretary and Compliance Officer, shareholder queries)

notes: The deep-cut source is an aggregator that quotes his official bio. MarketScreener lists a different title (Chief Sales Officer), so check the role before outreach. Do not confuse him with a different Chanakya Hridaya linked to AlmaBetter. He appeared on The Desi VC podcast (episode 89, October 2022).

name: Rajesh Yabaji
current_role: Chairman, Managing Director & CEO, BlackBuck Ltd (formerly Zinka Logistics Solutions; listed on NSE/BSE)
profile: IIT Kharagpur alumnus and former ITC supply-chain manager who co-founded BlackBuck in 2015 with ITC colleague Chanakya Hridaya and Ramasubramaniam B. The company began as a B2B full-truckload freight marketplace and grew into India's largest digital platform for truck operators, covering FASTag/fuel payments, telematics, loads and vehicle financing. It is now a listed company with Yabaji as chairman, MD and CEO.
interesting_fact: BlackBuck's growth exploded after India mandated FASTags for toll payments in 2019. Yabaji told Fortune India that '99% of the growth in business happened after 2019.'
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from his ITC project to modernise a 100-year-old supply chain. He could improve planning and warehousing, but transportation stayed out of reach because it was in the hands of fragmented truck owners.
notes: The deep-cut fact is from a search summary of the 2016 YourStory piece, which I did not open directly. Its ITC origin story matches Fortune India's account. BlackBuck runs regular investor calls, so the IR route is the most reliable.

name: Ramasubramaniam B
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Head - New Initiatives, BlackBuck (Zinka Logistics Solutions)
profile: Ramasubramaniam (Ramasubramanian) Balasubramaniam is a logistics veteran with about 27 years of experience, associated with supply-chain advisory Miebach Consulting India. In 2015 he co-founded BlackBuck, India's largest digital trucking platform, with Rajesh Yabaji and Chanakya Hridaya, and holds a roughly 10.7% stake per the 2024 DRHP.
interesting_fact: In BlackBuck's 2024 IPO filing the three co-founders held almost identical stakes: Ramasubramaniam and Yabaji 10.67% each, Hridaya 10.68%.
deep_cut_fact: Unlike his two IIT Kharagpur co-founders, he came from the consulting side: he holds a PGDBM from the Institute of Integrated Learning in Management (IILM) and remains a director of Miebach Consulting India alongside his BlackBuck role.
notes: Very low public profile; CEO Rajesh Yabaji is BlackBuck's public face. His name is also spelled Ramasubramanian Balasubramaniam. Accounts differ on how he met Yabaji (an ITC project vs. Miebach).

name: Fayez Mohamood
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Bluecore (acquired by Insider One, announced May 13, 2026; post-deal role not confirmed)
profile: Georgia Tech-trained engineer who co-founded New York retail-marketing software company Bluecore (originally TriggerMail, founded 2013) with Mahmoud Arram and Max Bennett and led it as CEO to unicorn status, serving 400+ brands such as Sephora, J.Crew and Ralph Lauren. In May 2026 Insider One announced it was acquiring Bluecore.
interesting_fact: Bluecore was sold to agentic customer-engagement platform Insider One in May 2026; at the time Bluecore served 400+ US enterprise brands including ALO Yoga, Sephora, Bloomingdale's and The North Face.
deep_cut_fact: He met co-founder Mahmoud Arram in freshman calculus class; the founders spent about four years on several failed consumer products before Bluecore grew out of a technical insight from one of them, and he was in Arram's wedding, held the day after their first seed round closed.
notes: After the Insider One acquisition (May 2026), check whether he remains in an operating role. No published press email found; Bluecore press page: https://www.bluecore.com/press/.

name: Mahmoud Arram
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Bluecore (acquired by Insider One, May 2026); post-acquisition role unconfirmed
profile: Mahmoud Arram co-founded Bluecore in New York in 2013 with CEO Fayez Mohamood and Max Bennett, and serves as its CTO. Bluecore built AI-driven retail marketing and customer-identity technology for large retailers and reached a valuation of about $1B. Insider One acquired the company in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Bluecore came after four years of failed consumer products by the founders and grew out of a technical insight from one of their earlier projects. Arram first met CEO Fayez Mohamood in a freshman calculus class.
deep_cut_fact: He has said cooking gives him the same satisfaction as coding. He has also said Bluecore stuck with Python 'because it's what we were familiar with in the early days.'

public_contacts.value: christopher.baldwin@useinsider.com (Insider One VP Marketing, media contact for the Bluecore acquisition)

notes: Bluecore was acquired by Insider One (announced May 13, 2026), and Arram's current role there is not public. The acquisition is a good timely hook.

name: Max Bennett
current_role: Researcher (neural memory, cortical microcircuits) at Columbia University and the Astera Institute; author
profile: Former Goldman Sachs trader who in 2013 co-founded Bluecore (AI marketing personalisation for retailers, valued at $1B+) and served as its Chief Product Officer, then co-founded AI shopping-assistant company Alby; both were acquired. He wrote 'A Brief History of Intelligence' (Mariner, 2023) and now does neuroscience/AI research at Columbia and the Astera Institute.
interesting_fact: His book 'A Brief History of Intelligence' was called 'amazing' by Nobel laureate Daniel Kahneman; he gave a keynote at Cosyne 2025 and appeared on Armchair Expert with Dax Shepard.
deep_cut_fact: Despite no academic post at the time, he published peer-reviewed neuroscience papers, e.g. 'An Attempt at a Unified Theory of the Neocortical Microcircuit in Sensory Cortex' (Frontiers in Neural Circuits, 2020); he sits on the board of the Thousand Brains Project and is writing a sci-fi novel about the origins of life.
notes: Very approachable for an AI/brains podcast angle; frequent podcast guest. Lavin lists him as Forbes 30 Under 30.

name: Blake Scholl
current_role: Founder & CEO, Boom Supersonic (Denver)
profile: Cincinnati-born Carnegie Mellon computer scientist who worked at early Amazon, then co-founded mobile startup Kima Labs (acquired by Groupon in 2012). He founded Boom in 2014 to build the Overture supersonic airliner; its XB-1 demonstrator went supersonic in 2025. In Dec 2025 Boom launched 'Superpower', a 42 MW natural-gas turbine for AI data centers, with a 1.21 GW launch order from Crusoe plus a $300M raise.
interesting_fact: Boom's Superpower turbine shares the core of its Symphony jet engine, needs no water, and Crusoe ordered 29 units (1.21 GW, >$1.25B backlog); Scholl says turbine revenue will help fund Overture. Highly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He left high school early on a scholarship for early entry to Carnegie Mellon, earned his private pilot license in 2007, and before founding Boom took aircraft-design classes and built his own aerodynamics model in early 2014; he put half his Kima sale proceeds into Boom.
notes: Very media-friendly and active on X (company account x.com/boomsupersonic linked from Boom site; personal handle not verified this session). Data-center power pivot makes him a strong podcast fit.

name: Joe Wilding
current_role: Co-founder and (per AIAA) Chief Technology Officer, Boom Technology (Boom Supersonic); current title not confirmed
profile: Aerospace engineer who co-founded Boom Supersonic in Denver in 2014 with Blake Scholl and Josh Krall to build the Overture supersonic airliner. He brought decades of certification experience from Hawker Beechcraft, Adam Aircraft, Eclipse Aviation and ICON Aircraft, and has led several passenger aircraft from clean-sheet design through FAA certification.
interesting_fact: He is one of only three Boom co-founders. He has led development of several passenger aircraft from clean-sheet design through FAA certification, the experience Boom needed to certify a new supersonic airliner.
deep_cut_fact: Before Boom, he was Chief Engineer of the Adam A700, a twin-engine very light jet from Adam Aircraft Industries. He was also an early employee at three aerospace startups and worked on experimental and military aircraft projects.
notes: Very low public profile and I found no recent news. I could not confirm whether he is still an active Boom executive; CEO Blake Scholl is the company's public face.

name: Joshua Krall
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Puck (per TheOrg; unverified by primary source)
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Boom Technology (Boom Supersonic) with Blake Scholl and Joe Wilding in Denver in September 2014; Boom is developing the Overture supersonic airliner. He led Boom's technology/software side (described as CTO) and later moved on; aggregator profiles list him as co-founder and CTO of a startup called Puck since 2020.
interesting_fact: Wikipedia lists Josh Krall as one of Boom Technology's three founders, alongside Blake Scholl and Joe Wilding, with the company founded September 26, 2014 in Denver.
deep_cut_fact: As Boom's CTO he went on the Big Compute podcast to explain how Boom used cloud-based high-performance computing to design a supersonic airliner as a startup.
notes: No longer at Boom (Contrary Research names a different current CTO). Current role (Puck, ex-OpenAtlas partner) comes only from TheOrg. Earlier Groupon/FeeFighters links are from aggregators and unverified. No published contact found; Boom is not a route to him.

name: Martin Mao
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Chronosphere (observability platform; acquisition by Palo Alto Networks announced Nov 2025)
profile: Martin Mao co-founded Chronosphere, a cloud-native observability platform built to handle very large metrics and telemetry volumes at lower cost. It became a Gartner Magic Quadrant leader for observability and in Nov 2025 agreed to be acquired by Palo Alto Networks for $3.35B, which plans to pair it with its AgentiX AI agents for automated fixes.
interesting_fact: At the time of the deal Chronosphere reported over $160M in annual recurring revenue, growing triple digits year over year, and counted two of the leading LLM developers among its customers; Palo Alto's Nikesh Arora called observability a foundational requirement for every modern AI data center.
notes: Strong AI-infrastructure angle (observability for AI workloads). He may now hold a Palo Alto Networks role; the deal was expected to close in PANW's second half of fiscal 2026 - verify. chronosphere.io blocked automated fetches and search budget ran out, so no press email or verified social account captured.

name: Rob Skillington
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Chronosphere (observability platform), acquired by Palo Alto Networks for $3.35B (announced Nov 2025, completed by early 2026); post-deal title not confirmed
profile: Ex-Uber observability tech lead who co-created M3, Uber's open-source Prometheus-compatible metrics engine. In 2019 he and Martin Mao co-founded Chronosphere for cloud-native observability; it passed $160M ARR before Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy it for $3.35B.
interesting_fact: Palo Alto Networks bought Chronosphere, pitched as 'next-generation observability for the data center era', for $3.35B; Chronosphere reported over $160M ARR growing triple digits year over year at signing.
deep_cut_fact: He designed M3DB's inverted index at Uber, explaining: 'When querying millions or billions of metrics, you want something flexible and sublinear in speed... This led us to the creation of M3DB's inverted index.' M3 now handles 3B+ datapoints queried per second and is used by companies such as Walmart.

public_contacts.value: nhockin@paloaltonetworks.com (Nicole Hockin, VP Global Communications, Palo Alto Networks; media contact on Chronosphere deal release)

notes: Deeply technical founder with an open-source following; strong fit for data-center/AI-infrastructure observability. chronosphere.io blocked our fetches (403), and the web search budget ran out, so his post-acquisition role and personal social accounts were not verified.

name: Jiang Yi
current_role: Founder, CEO and legal representative, CityCloud Technology (城云科技（中国）有限公司), Hangzhou
profile: Jiang Yi (蒋忆) founded CityCloud (城云科技) in Hangzhou in 2012, a smart-city / urban big-data company that helped build city-brain style digital-governance platforms for local governments. CityCloud raised a RMB500m Pre-D round led by Zhejiang's state-reform fund (late 2020) and a RMB1bn D round (July 2021), reaching unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: CityCloud coined the concept 'Internet of City' (IoC, 城市互联网), combining IoT, big data, AI and 'service networking'; in Jan 2021 it won a RMB590m EPC contract for phase two of Huaining county's smart-city project in Anhui.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding CityCloud, Jiang Yi was executive president of Insigma Technology (浙大网新科技股份有限公司), the Zhejiang University-linked listed IT group.
notes: English romanization 'Jiang Yi' maps to 蒋忆 (not 蒋毅), per 36Kr company profile listing 蒋忆 as founder/CEO and legal rep. Gender not confirmed in sources. Very low public profile; no recent (2024-26) interviews found. Company site www.onecc.me was unreachable; no published press email found. Company is private (not listed on A-share or HKEX as far as found).

name: Adrian Brock
profile: Hurun's Global Unicorn Index (2021-2024) lists Adrian Brock as a founder of CloudBees, the San Jose enterprise software-delivery/CI-CD company (Jenkins) valued at $1B in 2021. Public company sources name Sacha Labourey and Francois Dechery as CloudBees' co-founders, and Brock's role could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity is uncertain: Wikipedia and CloudBees name only Labourey and Dechery as founders. Brock may have been an early team member (an Adrian Brock was a known JBoss developer, which would fit CloudBees' ex-JBoss roots) or Hurun may be wrong. Moritz Plassnig became CEO in June 2026. The contact is the company press inbox. Verify before outreach.

name: François Déchery
current_role: Co-Founder and CloudBees Unify Executive Sponsor, CloudBees
profile: French software executive who co-founded CloudBees (the enterprise company behind Jenkins-based CI/CD and DevOps tooling) with Sacha Labourey in 2010. Earlier he held roles at KPMG, Sun Microsystems and Mapics (now Infor) before joining JBoss in 2005. He now sponsors CloudBees' unified DevOps platform.
interesting_fact: He met CloudBees co-founder Sacha Labourey at JBoss/Red Hat, where after the 2006 acquisition he ran worldwide JBoss support and launched Red Hat's global partner support program for Linux and JBoss.
deep_cut_fact: He joined JBoss in 2005 specifically to launch its services and support business in Europe; academically he holds an M.Sc. in business administration and information systems from ESC Clermont and a postgraduate degree in MIS from the Institut Francais de Gestion in Paris.
notes: Low personal media profile; route via CloudBees press. Cloud/DevOps infrastructure angle rather than data-center hardware.

name: Kohsuke Kawaguchi
current_role: Creator of Jenkins; co-founder of Launchable (acquired by CloudBees, Aug 2024); former CTO of CloudBees
profile: Tokyo-born programmer (b. 1977) who created Hudson at Sun Microsystems in 2004, which became Jenkins, the dominant open-source CI/CD automation server, after a 2011 fork from Oracle. His start-up InfraDNA merged into CloudBees (2010), where he became CTO (2014); in 2020 he left to co-found Launchable (ML-driven test selection), which CloudBees acquired in 2024.
interesting_fact: Jenkins exists because of a trademark fight: when Oracle claimed the 'Hudson' name after buying Sun, the community voted in January 2011 to rename the project Jenkins, and both sides still call the other the fork. He won the 2011 Google-O'Reilly Open Source Award.
deep_cut_fact: A keen long-distance cyclist who blogs his rides: in 2026 he and an old friend pedalled ~519 km over five days along the Shinano, Japan's longest river, to the Sea of Japan and up the coast, after riding Japan's historic eastern highway together the year before.
notes: Hurun's $1B figure is CloudBees' valuation, not his wealth. Approachable, frequent conference speaker, active blogger in English and Japanese (cycling, cooking, coffee, AI). His site's About page still says CloudBees CTO (outdated). Best route: LinkedIn or X.

name: Michael Neale
current_role: Principal Engineer, Block (works on goose, Block's open-source AI agent); co-founder of CloudBees
profile: Mic Neale, an Australian engineer (UNSW) and former Red Hat open-source architect, co-founded CloudBees, the Jenkins CI/CD company valued at more than $1B. At Block he led engineering at its TBD unit. He now works on goose, Block's open-source on-machine AI agent, which is now under the Agentic AI Foundation.
interesting_fact: At AI Engineer Melbourne 2026 he spoke on 'What If You Never Needed an API Key Again? Building a Mesh LLM From Spare Compute', which pools idle machines into a shared LLM inference mesh.
deep_cut_fact: Long before CloudBees he built the early versions of the Drools rules/inference engine (later JBoss Rules) while an open-source architect at Red Hat. The AI-agent work he does today is a return to his roots in reasoning engines.
notes: Goes by 'Mic Neale'. Active conference speaker in Australia (Web Directions / AI Engineer), so the best route is via conference organisers or Block's goose community (https://block.github.io/goose). I could not verify his personal X or GitHub handles because the fetches failed. Strong fit for AI-compute episodes (mesh LLM from spare compute).

name: Ryan Campbell
current_role: Most recently VP of Customer Success, Liquibase (Austin, TX); CloudBees co-founder. Current role unverified (no longer on Liquibase leadership page, Nov 2026)
profile: Software engineer and co-founding engineer of CloudBees, the enterprise Jenkins/CI-CD company Sacha Labourey started in 2010 after JBoss/Red Hat. At CloudBees he launched the CloudBees Jenkins Enterprise offering and built the customer-success organisation. He later joined Liquibase (formerly Datical), the database change-management/DevOps company, as VP of Customer Success.
interesting_fact: Sacha Labourey names him among the small founding group that created CloudBees with him (with François Déchery, Laurence Poussot, Michael Neale and Vivek Pandey), before Jenkins creator Kohsuke Kawaguchi joined.
deep_cut_fact: In CloudBees' early platform-as-a-service days he went on Chariot Solutions' TechCast (#67) to explain its Dev@Cloud and Run@Cloud services, years before the company pivoted fully to Jenkins and CI/CD.
notes: Hurun lists him as a CloudBees founder; confirmed by Sacha Labourey's Jenkins contributor profile and his G2 author bio (learn.g2.com/author/ryan-campbell). Common name, so make sure you have the Austin-based CloudBees/Liquibase Ryan Campbell. No personal contact published; LinkedIn is the likely route but no verified URL found. He was likely a minority co-founder, so 'unicorn founder' wealth is probably modest.

name: Sacha Labourey
current_role: Co-founder and board member, CloudBees (stepped back from day-to-day role as Chief Strategy Officer in Feb 2025).
profile: Swiss software entrepreneur (b. Neuchâtel 1975, EPFL) who was CTO of open-source middleware firm JBoss through its 2006 sale to Red Hat, then GM of Red Hat middleware. In 2010 he founded CloudBees (enterprise Jenkins CI/CD, DevOps), serving as CEO then CSO; since 2025 he is a board member and advisor.
interesting_fact: CloudBees became the main commercial company behind Jenkins, the open-source CI/CD automation server, and appointed Jenkins creator Kohsuke Kawaguchi as its Chief Technology Officer.
deep_cut_fact: Before JBoss he founded Cogito Informatique, a Swiss consultancy specialising in application servers and middleware; at JBoss he wrote the first implementation of load-balancing/fail-over (clustering) for the JBoss application server and ran JBoss Europe before becoming CTO.
notes: Based in Neuchâtel, Switzerland; frequent conference speaker and blogger. Now off day-to-day CloudBees duties (new CEO Moritz Plassnig, June 2026), so reach him personally via LinkedIn rather than company PR. Cloud/DevOps rather than energy.

name: Vivek Pandey
current_role: Engineering executive; reportedly at Mirantis since Dec 2022 (unverified); previously VP Engineering at Shipa.io
profile: Software engineer who was one of CloudBees' founding team in 2010 (with Sacha Labourey, Francois Dechery and others), the Jenkins-based CI/CD company that reached unicorn status with a $150m raise in Dec 2021. Earlier he held engineering roles at Sun Microsystems and VMware; after CloudBees he was VP Engineering at cloud-native app platform Shipa.io.
interesting_fact: CloudBees, which he helped found, became a unicorn in Dec 2021 after raising $150m from Goldman Sachs Asset Management, Morgan Stanley, Bridgepoint, HSBC and others.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding CloudBees he was an engineer at Sun Microsystems and VMware, then later took his DevOps experience to Shipa.io, an 'application-as-code' platform for Kubernetes.
notes: Hurun 'founder' wealth figure is likely overstated: CloudBees' own pages name only Labourey and Dechery as co-founders; third-party profiles list Pandey among the 2010 founders. Common name; no verified personal channels found. Not a public-facing executive.

name: Guang Zhou
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeepRoute.ai (Shenzhen)
profile: Guang 'Maxwell' Zhou (周光) is a Tsinghua-educated AI researcher with a PhD from UT Dallas who worked on autonomous driving at Baidu USA before founding Shenzhen-based DeepRoute.ai in 2019, his second self-driving startup. DeepRoute builds map-free assisted/autonomous driving software for Chinese automakers (backed by Great Wall Motor and others) and pitches itself as 'AI infrastructure of the physical world'.
interesting_fact: He argues general-purpose AI models will let one self-driving system work in any city without HD maps: 'Waymo can only drive in a few places like Phoenix or San Francisco... The power of the new AI technologies... gives us the potential to drive everywhere.'
deep_cut_fact: He studied in Tsinghua University's 'Talent Class' undergraduate program, and before autonomous driving worked on IoT projects at Texas Instruments in Dallas while doing his AI PhD at UT Dallas.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: China EVs & More, Episode 3 (not his own show)

notes: Goes by Maxwell Zhou in English. Avoid his first startup Roadstar.ai (ended in a 2019 founder dispute). Gives English-language interviews; no published press email found (site is JS-rendered).

name: Hillel Kobrinsky
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)
profile: Former IDF brigadier general who founded Interwise (sold to AT&T in 2007), then co-founded DriveNets with Ido Susan in 2015 to replace proprietary routers with disaggregated white-box networking. DriveNets now sells Ethernet AI fabric for GPU clusters and raised a $410m Series D in June 2026.
interesting_fact: DriveNets, built to displace Cisco in telcos like AT&T, has pivoted into AI data-center networking as an Ethernet alternative to Nvidia's fabrics - it reports $1bn+ in secured business and has been cash-flow positive since 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech he was a brigadier general in the IDF Armored Corps; after selling Interwise he built and ran AT&T's Israeli R&D center, and from 2013-2015 was a senior adviser to Israel's Minister of Finance.
notes: Globes notes both founders 'recoil from media interviews' - expect a hard get. Also a co-founder and early secretary-general of Yair Lapid's Yesh Atid party (Globes). Press releases list agency contacts (Crystal Monahan, Martin Perlin) but emails are obfuscated. Strong AI data-center networking angle.

name: Ido Susan
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, DriveNets (Ra'anana, Israel)
profile: Serial Israeli founder Ido Susan co-founded Intucell, which invented self-optimising network (SON) software, and sold it to Cisco in 2013 for $475m after raising only $6m. He then spent about two years at Cisco. In 2015 he co-founded DriveNets with Hillel Kobrinsky to replace carrier routers with disaggregated, cloud-native software. DriveNets now also sells Ethernet fabrics for AI clusters and raised a $410m Series D in 2026.
interesting_fact: DriveNets, started to take on Cisco and Juniper at telecom operators, now competes with Nvidia in AI-factory networking. Globes reported a roughly $1bn five-year order book in 2025, and in 2026 it announced the first commercial long-distance 'scale-across' AI supercluster deployment.
deep_cut_fact: He never earned a university degree. He founded Intucell at about 24 and sold it to Cisco at 26, then founded a company to compete with his acquirer.
notes: Globes says both founders 'recoil from media interviews', so pitch through the PR agency with a data-centre and AI-networking angle. He has spoken at Calcalist's Tech TLV and on the DealMakers podcast (Alejandro Cremades).

name: Eli Harris
current_role: Co-founder & Partner, One Dream Ventures (venture studio for SaaS/AI tools for real estate & construction); co-founder of EcoFlow and R-Zero
profile: Eli Harris, a former DJI strategic-partnerships lead, co-founded portable power-station maker EcoFlow with DJI battery engineer Lei 'Bruce' Wang (co-founder/CEO c.2016-2020). He then co-founded R-Zero (disinfection/building air quality) and Honor Pet, and now runs venture studio One Dream Ventures.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for EcoFlow at DJI, where disaster-relief and emergency projects showed him how critical portable batteries were; EcoFlow's pitch was to 'replace fuel generators and provide clean personal energy storage.'

deep_cut_fact: His first businesses straight out of college were an Ultimate Frisbee tournament and a league; a caterer for the event needed a website, which is how he drifted into web design -- the agency that later spawned FreshBooks.
notes: Press contact is Chloe Matcham, Senior Manager, Communications (named on FreshBooks press releases). FreshBooks recently launched an Anthropic MCP connector -- AI/small-business angle. CEO seat has turned over several times since 2021; McDerment's own status beyond 'chair' not confirmed for 2026.

name: Zheng Yong
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Geek+ (Beijing Geekplus Technology; HKEX: 2590)
profile: Tsinghua graduate who spent ~5 years at ABB and ~3 years as a plant manager at a Saint-Gobain subsidiary, then was a senior investment manager at New Horizon Capital before founding warehouse-robotics company Geek+ in Beijing in 2015. Geek+ listed in Hong Kong in July 2025 as the first global AMR warehouse-robot stock; he held ~38% pre-IPO.
interesting_fact: Geek+'s July 2025 HK IPO was the largest robotics H-share IPO to date; the retail tranche was ~134x oversubscribed and 2024 revenue was ~RMB2.4B, the largest of any HK-listed B2B robot maker.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came in 2014 while he was a VC at New Horizon Capital touring an Amazon warehouse full of Kiva robots; he couldn't find a Chinese team to back, so he founded one, starting with just himself and CTO Li Hongbo in a basement of Tsinghua's FIT building, and shipping its first goods-to-person product for Tmall's Singles' Day in under three months.
notes: Chinese name 郑勇. Public company, so IR/PR routes are formal and responsive. Quote: 'We enter each market not asking whether we can win, only how long until we're No.1 locally.'

name: Li Hongbo
current_role: Co-founder, executive Director, CTO and Vice President, Geek+ (Geekplus Technology, HKEX-listed)
profile: Beijing robotics engineer (PhD Tsinghua University, 2009) who was a postdoc and associate researcher in Tsinghua's computer science department before co-founding warehouse-robot maker Geek+ with CEO Zheng Yong in February 2015. Geek+ builds autonomous mobile robots for logistics and listed in Hong Kong in 2025; he leads its technology and R&D.
interesting_fact: Before co-founding Geek+ he was a postdoctoral researcher and associate researcher in Tsinghua University's Department of Computer Science and Technology.
deep_cut_fact: Recognised as a professor-level senior engineer by Beijing's senior professional qualification committee (May 2019) and receives a special government allowance from China's State Council (since June 2024); also named an Outstanding Young Member of the China Federation of Logistics & Purchasing.
notes: Chinese-language outreach likely more effective; company IR/PR are the published routes. Li Hongbo is a common name - this is the Geek+ CTO (李洪波).

name: Henrik Müller-Hansen
current_role: Founder & CEO, Gelato (on-demand print/production software, Oslo/Fornebu); board member, Patricia Industries (since Jan 2025)
profile: Norwegian-based entrepreneur, former CEO of Tele2 Norway, who launched Optimalprint around 2007 and then Gelato in 2012. Gelato's software and network route print-on-demand orders to local production hubs in 30+ countries, cutting transport distance and waste; it also sells GelatoConnect, a production OS for print factories. Gelato reached a US$1B+ valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Gelato's model is a 'local on-demand production' network: orders are produced in partner factories near the end customer across 30+ countries rather than shipped from a central plant.
deep_cut_fact: Before studying at the Stockholm School of Economics he served as a team leader in a military Underwater Demolition Team; as CEO of Tele2 Norway (2003-06) he roughly doubled revenue from NOK 1.5bn to 3.2bn.
notes: Gelato press releases name a VP PR & Communications (Julie Ryland, 2025) but email addresses are obfuscated on the pages; route via gelato.com news/press section. Tele2 revenue figure is from Gelato's leadership page (https://www.gelato.com/leadership).

name: Joel Hyatt
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman, Globality (stepped down as CEO in late 2026, per Procurement Magazine)
profile: Serial entrepreneur. He co-founded Hyatt Legal Services (1977), which brought affordable legal services to middle-income families, and Hyatt Legal Plans (later sold to MetLife). With Al Gore he co-founded Current TV (2004; sold to Al Jazeera in 2013). In 2015 he co-founded Globality, an AI platform for enterprise procurement and sourcing backed by SoftBank, and led it as CEO until 2026.
interesting_fact: He was the face of his own firm's nationwide TV ads, which always ended with the line: 'I'm Joel Hyatt and you have my word on it.'
deep_cut_fact: He co-authored the 2000 book 'The Long Boom' with futurists Peter Schwartz and Peter Leyden. He taught entrepreneurship at Stanford GSB from 1998 to 2003 and was founding chairman of VideoSurf, a computer-vision video search engine that Microsoft acquired in 2011.
notes: An experienced public figure: 1994 Democratic Senate nominee in Ohio, 2000 DNC national finance chair, former HP director, RAND trustee. He does podcasts readily. His personal site links to his X and LinkedIn, and he is reachable through Globality. The CEO handover is reported only by procurementmag.com, so confirm his current title.

name: Lior Delgo
current_role: Co-founder, Globality (AI platform for enterprise services procurement, Menlo Park/Palo Alto); listed as co-founder & president
profile: Israeli-American serial entrepreneur. Co-founded travel meta-search engine FareChase (acquired by Yahoo, 2004) and computer-vision video search company VideoSurf (acquired by Microsoft in 2011, reportedly ~$70M, for Xbox LIVE), then worked on Xbox at Microsoft. In 2015 he co-founded Globality with Joel Hyatt; the AI-driven sourcing platform for services spend reached unicorn status (~$1B).
interesting_fact: His VideoSurf technology used computer vision to 'see' frames inside videos, identifying people and moments rather than relying on text tags; Microsoft bought it in 2011 to power video search and Kinect voice search on Xbox LIVE.
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded VideoSurf with applied mathematician Prof. Achi Brandt (a pioneer of multigrid methods), Dr. Eitan Sharon and Shai Deljo; its computer-vision engine analyzed video about 10x faster than playback speed.

public_contacts.value: slafferty@roundearthconsulting.com (Sarah Lafferty, Round Earth Consulting; Globality media contact)

notes: Jared Hyatt succeeded Joel Hyatt as Globality CEO; Delgo remains co-founder. PR contact is from a Mar 2026 Business Wire release seen via search (page not directly fetchable; verify). FareChase/Yahoo link per Globality's own bio. Low personal media profile.

name: Ran Harpaz
current_role: Founder and CEO, Lettuce Financial (AI operating system for solopreneurs)
profile: Israeli-born tech executive who was founding CTO of procurement-AI unicorn Globality (2015-2019), then CTO/COO of Hippo Insurance and COO of Noname Security, after strategy roles at PayPal. In 2023 he founded Lettuce Financial, an AI platform handling accounting, tax, payroll and benefits for solopreneurs; it has raised $28M+ and bought Besolo and Carry's retirement platform.
interesting_fact: He has helped scale three unicorns (Globality, Hippo, Noname Security) and now says Lettuce aims to put at least $50 billion back into solopreneurs' businesses through smarter tax and accounting.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he was CIO of Israeli ISP Netvision/Cellcom and worked at security firms Skybox Security and Sanctum; he holds an MBA, a BA in economics and an LLB in law, all from Tel Aviv University.
notes: Active founder who gives press interviews; LinkedIn is linked from his official Lettuce author page. The X account is the company's (@joinlettuce), not his personal account. Unit 8200 veteran per aggregator profiles (unverified).

name: Andrew Barnes
current_role: Co-founder & director, Go1 (stepped down as co-CEO Aug 2024)
profile: Brisbane entrepreneur who co-founded workplace-learning platform Go1 with high-school friends Vu Tran, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; it went through Y Combinator and reached a ~$3B valuation. He led it as CEO for about a decade before handing the top job to Eigeland in 2024.
interesting_fact: Go1 started in a Brisbane suburban garage as a web-development shop he ran with Vu Tran; it now serves 10,000+ organisations and 50M+ users.
deep_cut_fact: A 2013 Rhodes Scholar, he did an Oxford MSc in Education (Learning and Technology) and a UQ PhD in business management, after UQ degrees in economics (2009) and business management honours (2011).
notes: Common name - distinguish from the NZ 4-day-week Andrew Barnes. Holds a doctorate (Dr Andrew Barnes).

name: Chris Eigeland
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Go1 (Brisbane)
profile: Australian co-founder of Go1, the Brisbane-born (2015, Y Combinator S15) corporate learning-content aggregator, started by four school friends. Former CRO and co-CEO, he became sole CEO in August 2024. Go1 was valued at $2B+ in 2022.
interesting_fact: Go1 went through Y Combinator's Summer 2015 batch and became one of Australia's first edtech unicorns, aggregating training content into whatever LMS a company already uses.
deep_cut_fact: A Griffith law graduate and trained international lawyer, he was Australia's Youth Representative to the United Nations in 2016 and gave a TEDx talk in 2015.

name: Chris Hood
current_role: Co-founder, Go1 (Brisbane-born workplace learning platform)
profile: Australian software engineer and one of Go1's four co-founders (with Andrew Barnes, Vu Tran and Chris Eigeland). Go1 grew from a Logan/Brisbane garage web-dev business into a corporate e-learning content aggregator valued at about $2B, Brisbane's first unicorn. Hood is the technical co-founder who built the platform's software.
interesting_fact: Go1 began as a web development business started in a garage by school friends; it became Brisbane's first tech unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Andrew Barnes met Hood at a tech conference; in Go1's early days, when salespeople promised features that didn't exist yet, Hood had to build them fast - 'It's how we learnt what people wanted.'
notes: Very low public profile; current title not confirmed. Griffith University alumnus and ex-Intellidesign software engineer per Crunchbase (unverified). Route via Go1 (go1.com/about-us).

name: Vu Tran
current_role: Co-founder, Black Sky Industries (Logan, Qld solid-rocket-motor and defence manufacturer); co-founder and former Chief Growth Officer of Go1
profile: Dr Vu Tran is a Brisbane GP who grew up in Logan as a migrant. He co-founded workplace e-learning marketplace Go1 with school friends Andrew Barnes, Chris Eigeland and Chris Hood; Go1 raised $272M in 2021 and was valued at about $3B when it bought Blinkist in 2023. He has since stepped back from Go1's day-to-day running and co-founded Black Sky Industries, which makes solid rocket propellant and rocket motors for Australian defence.
interesting_fact: Black Sky Industries describes itself as Australia's only sovereign supplier of solid rocket propellant and motors, and it produces ammonium perchlorate locally. Tran argues Australia has only one local firm in the top 100 defence suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: In high school, instead of stacking shelves at Coles, he and Andrew Barnes started a software business that 'made a dollar an hour'. Around 2006 it was building websites for ANZ and News Corp, which did not realise they were dealing with students. He did not pay off his last credit-card debts until early 2020.

public_contacts.value: Long-form interview: 'Meet the Founder - Vu Tran (Go1)', The Exchange by EW Private Wealth, Sept 2024

notes: Practising GP (MBBS Bond, per profiles). Speaks readily on podcasts about sovereign manufacturing and defence, which suits an energy and industry angle. Also a non-executive director of ASX-listed PeopleIN (per marketindex; not re-verified). Black Sky's site has only a contact section, no published email.

name: Jörg Kattner
current_role: Former co-founder of Gorillas (left Feb 2021). Current role not verified; an aggregator lists him as CEO of Berlin-based JoeKa UG.
profile: Jörg Kattner co-founded Berlin quick-commerce grocery startup Gorillas with CEO Kağan Sümer in 2020, joining early that year to help it scale. He left in early 2021 holding about 10%. Gorillas later reached a ~$3B valuation and was acquired by Getir in December 2022.
interesting_fact: Announcing his exit after about a year, he wrote that he was leaving 'this rocket in good hands' and looked forward to new adventures, building another company from scratch.
deep_cut_fact: He started in marketing at Rocket Internet in 2014, then ran HelloFresh's Swiss market from 2017. In 2018 he helped build HelloFreshGO, HelloFresh's in-office lunch-fridge business, and was its COO for a year.
notes: Very low profile since 2021, with no verified current venture or public channels. WikiFX article reproduces a Gründerszene report (Feb 2021). JoeKa UG and angel-investor mentions come from aggregators (siliconvalleyinvestclub, pipeseed) and are unverified.

name: Kağan Sümer
current_role: Former founder and CEO of Gorillas (Berlin). Reported since 2023 to be building a new health-tech startup, Mirror, with Gorillas co-founder Uğur Samut (current status unverified).
profile: Istanbul-born Kağan Sümer worked at Rocket Internet's B2B food group in Berlin, then in May 2020 founded Gorillas, a 10-minute grocery delivery service using bike couriers. It became a unicorn in about nine months, reportedly Germany's fastest. Rival Getir bought Gorillas in December 2022 for about $1.2B, and Sümer left. German press reported in 2023 that he was starting a health-tech company.
interesting_fact: Gorillas went from founding in May 2020 to a $1B+ valuation in about nine months, which Wikipedia describes as the fastest any German company had done so.
deep_cut_fact: Rocket Internet ignored six of his job applications in one month before later hiring him. He once cycled from Istanbul to China, captained Turkey's youth water polo team, and spent 88 of his 100 euros on a bike when he arrived in Berlin. Gorillas began as 'Get Goodies' in his living room.
notes: Gorillas no longer exists (Getir wound it down in 2024), so there is no company press channel. Mirror was reported by deutsche-startups.de (May 2023): https://www.deutsche-startups.de/2023/05/02/gorillas-gruender-klonen-aware/. Aggregator listings of newer ventures (Sugar, Nutz) are unverified. A strong fit for the entrepreneurship angle (bikes, logistics, blitzscaling).

name: James Carter
current_role: Co-founder, Gousto (UK recipe-box company); current role at the company not verified
profile: British entrepreneur who co-founded Gousto, the London meal-kit/recipe-box business, with Timo Boldt in 2012. Gousto reached unicorn status in 2021. Carter keeps a low public profile and Boldt has been the public face as CEO.
interesting_fact: Carter and Boldt pitched Gousto on BBC's Dragons' Den in 2013 and left without a deal, yet Gousto went on to become a unicorn in 2021.

notes: Common name - use 'Gousto co-founder' to disambiguate. No public contact found for him; route via Gousto press office. Note Startups.co.uk misnames Boldt as 'Timo Schmidt'. Whether Carter is still at Gousto is unverified.

name: Timo Boldt
current_role: Founder and CEO of Gousto (announced Sept 2026 he will step down to become a board director once a successor is appointed, expected H1 2027)
profile: German-born former banker and Cambridge Judge EMBA (2014) alumnus who founded UK meal-kit company Gousto in 2012, initially packing and delivering kits himself. Gousto became a unicorn in 2022, delivers 80M+ meals a year and posted 2025 revenue of £342m with record £45m adjusted EBITDA. He also founded Bento (2021) to license Gousto's tech.
interesting_fact: Named EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year Class of 2023 (UK); about 95% of Gousto staff are shareholders.
deep_cut_fact: Long banking hours and takeaway dinners inspired Gousto; at 26 he quit, moved into university housing to fund it, packed every meal by hand, delivered them himself and took no salary for three years. His advice: 'You will be rejected a thousand times...'
notes: Leadership transition news: https://www.grocerygazette.co.uk/2026/09/17/gousto-founder-step-down/ . Frequent conference speaker (London Tech Week, Sifted Summit).

name: Jonathan Ross
current_role: Founder of Groq; since Dec 2025 at NVIDIA (reported as Chief Software Architect) under Nvidia's ~$20bn non-exclusive Groq inference-technology licensing deal
profile: Chip architect who started Google's TPU as a '20% project', left in 2016 with much of the TPU team and founded Groq (LPU inference chips, GroqCloud; $6.9bn valuation in 2025). In Dec 2025 Nvidia licensed Groq's tech (~$20bn) and Ross and president Sunny Madra joined Nvidia; Groq continues under CEO Simon Edwards.
interesting_fact: Groq's tech is credited as one of the few credible challengers to Nvidia in inference - so much so that Nvidia ultimately paid ~$20bn to license it and bring Ross and his team in-house.
deep_cut_fact: He dropped out of high school because he 'was bored', taught himself programming, did a stint at Hunter College, then got into NYU where he took PhD classes (incl. under Yann LeCun) as an undergrad before dropping out again: 'I didn't want to cap my earning opportunity by graduating from something.'
notes: Very podcast-friendly historically (Chamath, 20VC etc.), but now an Nvidia employee, so requests likely route through Nvidia PR. 'Chief Software Architect' title comes from reports quoting his LinkedIn; not confirmed on nvidia.com. LeCun detail per Groq's former leadership bio (via search). Hurun $7bn valuation figure is outdated.

name: Li Xuelin
current_role: Founder & Chairman, Hefu Laomian (和府捞面) noodle restaurant chain
profile: Li Xuelin (李学林) founded Hefu Laomian in 2012. The premium Chinese noodle chain is known for its 'noodles in a study room' store concept and central-kitchen supply chain. It raised more than RMB1.6B in six rounds from 2016 to 2022 and reached roughly $1B valuation. Since late 2023 it has pursued expansion through franchising/joint operation, lower-tier cities and overseas markets.

notes: Based in mainland China and media-light. Chinese-language outreach through Hefu Laomian corporate channels is likely the best route. I found no published contact email.

name: Adam R. Gerchen
current_role: CEO, Gerchen Capital Partners (Chicago); co-founder of Heyday and Keller Postman
profile: Chicago-based investor and litigation-finance pioneer (Brown, Harvard Law; ex-Goldman Sachs and Alyeska). Co-founded Gerchen Keller Capital in 2013, which raised $2B+ before its 2016 sale to Burford Capital, where he became President; co-founded law firm Keller Postman. In 2020 he co-founded Heyday, an Amazon-brand aggregator that raised $175M Series A and a $555M Series C.
interesting_fact: Gerchen Keller Capital became the largest private investment firm focused exclusively on legal and regulatory risk within about three years of launch, raising over $2B in institutional capital before Burford acquired it.
