notes: Heyday co-founded Aug 2020 with CEO Sebastian Rymarz (https://prnewswire.com/news-releases/heyday-emerges-from-stealth-with-175m-series-a-funding-to-accelerate-marketplace-native-brands-301175394.html); aggregators list Gerchen as executive chairman 2020-2024. Not to be confused with Heyday skincare. Firm website is JS-only; no published email found.

name: Sebastian Rymarz
current_role: President, Essor (formed 2024 when Branded acquired Heyday); co-founder & CEO of Heyday
profile: Sebastian Rymarz co-founded San Francisco-based Heyday with Adam Gerchen in August 2020 to acquire and scale marketplace-native (mainly Amazon) consumer brands; it raised about $800M including a $555M Series C in 2021, reportedly at a $1B+ valuation. In September 2024 Branded acquired Heyday to form Essor, a ~$400M-revenue consumer products group where Rymarz became president.
interesting_fact: Heyday emerged from stealth with a $175M Series A just three months after founding; Rymarz called it 'the early days of a tectonic shift toward marketplace commerce.' Unlike rivals, he said Heyday would buy only one or two brands a month to focus on growing each.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 Heyday bought ZitSticka, the direct-to-consumer acne-patch brand, as part of its push into personal care.

name: Dror Shimoni
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, HoneyBook (runs its Israel R&D center) - per Calcalist profile; current title not re-confirmed on HoneyBook's site
profile: Israeli software engineer who co-founded HoneyBook in 2013 with Oz and Naama Alon. HoneyBook is a San Francisco-based clientflow/business-management platform (CRM, contracts, invoicing, payments) for freelancers and small service businesses, valued at $2.2B in 2021. Shimoni leads engineering from the Tel Aviv R&D office.

name: Naama Alon

profile: Israeli designer who co-founded HoneyBook with Oz Alon (CEO) and Dror Shimoni; it makes client-management and payments software for US freelancers and small creative businesses, and was valued at about $2.4B in 2021. Alon leads product and creative and is based between the Bay Area and Tel Aviv.

profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded HoneyBook in 2013 with Naama Alon and Dror Shimoni after a Tel Aviv accelerator, then moved the team to Silicon Valley via a Palo Alto accelerator. HoneyBook is a clientflow, payments and AI-powered business-management platform for independent business owners; as CEO he led its 2026 expansion to the UK and Australia.

current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kinside (child-care benefits marketplace); co-founder, HoneyBook
profile: Shadiah Sigala moved from Mexico to southern California at age 7 and later studied at Pomona College and the Harvard Kennedy School. In 2013 she co-founded HoneyBook, the small-business client and finance management platform valued at more than $2B in 2021, with three Israeli entrepreneurs. In 2018 she co-founded Kinside, an employer child-care benefit marketplace, which acquired LegUp in 2022.

name: Paul Sawaya
current_role: Founder & CEO, Elsewhere (multiplayer roguelike game startup, SF); co-founder and former CTO of Human Interest
profile: San Francisco engineer who co-founded Human Interest in 2015 with Roger Lee. The YC S15 digital 401(k) provider automated retirement plans for small businesses, and Sawaya was its founding CTO for about five years and sat on its board. He is now an angel investor and founder/CEO of Elsewhere, an a16z Speedrun gaming/AI-agents startup.

name: Izabel Jelenic
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Infobip
profile: Croatian engineer who co-founded Infobip with CEO Silvio Kutić in 2006 in Vodnjan, a town of about 6,000 on the Istrian peninsula, starting with a €25,000 loan. Infobip grew into a global cloud communications (CPaaS) platform and Croatia's first unicorn. As CTO he leads 800+ engineers across continents.

name: Roberto Kutic
current_role: CEO, Festina.ai (AI venture studio); co-founder and co-owner of Infobip
profile: Croatian mechanical engineer (University of Zagreb) who co-founded Infobip with brother Silvio Kutic and Izabel Jelenic and served as COO, helping grow it from zero to $1B revenue in 14 years without outside capital; it became Croatia's first unicorn in 2020. He left Infobip in mid-2025 (remaining a co-owner) and launched Festina.ai, building domain-specific AI agents.

name: Silvio Kutic

profile: Silvio Kutić co-founded Infobip in 2006 in Vodnjan, Croatia, with Izabel Jelenić (CTO) and his brother Roberto (COO), and is its CEO. Infobip is a global cloud communications (CPaaS) platform that handles SMS, WhatsApp, RCS and voice messaging for businesses. Infobip stayed bootstrapped for almost a decade. He fits a data-center/infrastructure angle via telecom APIs. Route through the Infobip global PR team (contacts from the Infobip media kit).

name: Albert Chon
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Injective Labs (per available profiles; current status not confirmed)
profile: Stanford-trained computer scientist (BS in CS/AI, MS in CS/systems) and ex-Amazon engineer who co-founded Injective Labs with Eric Chen in 2018; Injective came out of Binance Labs' first incubation program. Injective is a Cosmos-SDK layer-1 blockchain for decentralised spot and derivatives trading, backed by Pantera, Jump Crypto and Mark Cuban.
interesting_fact: Injective Labs was part of the very first incubation program hosted by Binance Labs in 2018.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto, he was valedictorian at Gretchen Whitney High School, studied biotechnology at Penn's Summer Academy in Applied Science & Technology, and worked as an analytical chemist; he later did research at Stanford's Parallel Distributed Processing Lab (2016).
notes: Deep-cut details come from IQ.wiki (crypto encyclopedia citing his profile), not a primary source. No published press email found for Injective; Eric Chen is the public face of the company. No verified personal social accounts confirmed.

name: Eric Chen
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Injective Labs (also leads the Injective Foundation)
profile: Chinese-American entrepreneur (b. 1998) who studied business and computer science at NYU, was involved with NYU's blockchain lab, then took leave in 2018 to co-found Injective with Albert Chon. Injective, incubated by Binance Labs, is a finance-focused Layer-1 blockchain backed by Pantera, Jump Crypto and Mark Cuban; he was on Forbes 30 Under 30 Finance (2024).
interesting_fact: Injective received $500,000 from Binance Labs' first incubation program in 2018, later raising from Pantera (2020), a token sale including Mark Cuban (2021) and a $40M round led by Jump Crypto (2022).
deep_cut_fact: In 2026 he co-authored a peer-reviewed paper in the journal Mathematics (MDPI) simulating an EIP-1559-style dynamic fee market for Injective's 600 ms blocks, finding proper tuning cut peak fees by 31% under variable demand.
notes: Common name - confirm it's the Injective CEO. Frequent podcast guest (CryptoNews Podcast, CNBC Crypto World). institutions@ is Injective's institutional inquiry address, not press. Wikipedia article flagged for source reliability.

name: Tian Dihong
current_role: Cofounder and former director of Intellif (Shenzhen Intellifusion, SSE STAR: 688343); sole owner of NaitMind, Inc. (current active role not published)
profile: Tian Dihong (田第鸿) cofounded Shenzhen Intellifusion (Intellif), an AI vision and AI-inference chip company, with Chen Ning in August 2014, holding 30% at founding. He later left the board for personal reasons and sold part of his stake in 2019; his company NaitMind, Inc. provided technical consulting to Intellif. Intellif listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023.
interesting_fact: Intellif's founding capital was largely intellectual property: Chen and Tian contributed a non-patent technology package for 'extracting crowd feature values through video analysis', valued at RMB 4.7M, in 70/30 proportion.
notes: Very low profile; no interviews or bio found. Possibly US-based (owns US-registered NaitMind, Inc.) but unconfirmed. Not to be confused with Intellif CEO Chen Ning. Intellif IR is the only published channel and he is no longer a director there.

name: Jennifer Bisceglie
current_role: Founder & Executive Vice Chair, Interos (CEO until April 2024)
profile: Supply-chain strategist who founded Interos in 2005 to help federal agencies manage supply-chain risk, then turned it into an AI-driven supply-chain risk and resilience platform valued at about $1B. In April 2024 she handed the CEO role to Ted Krantz and became Founder & Executive Vice Chair. She advises Congress on supply-chain security.
interesting_fact: She was selected as the U.S. delegate to the Women's 20 (W20), the G20 engagement group on gender inequality, and chaired Women Impacting Public Policy (WIPP) from 2010 to 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Her supply-chain career started in retail and footwear: before Interos she worked at Nine West Shoes, American Eagle Outfitters and the logistics software firm Manhattan Associates.
notes: Frequent speaker in national-security and supply-chain circles and media-friendly (Bloomberg, FT, CNBC). She fits an energy/data-center podcast angle on critical-infrastructure supply chains.

name: Roey Izkovsky
profile: Co-founder and CTO of Simply (formerly JoyTunes), the Tel Aviv music-learning app company he co-founded in 2011 with the Kaminka brothers. He died unexpectedly in March 2024 at age 44, per Calcalist (CTech).
notes: Deceased: Calcalist/CTech reported on 25 Mar 2024 that he 'passed away unexpectedly' at 44 (https://www.calcalistech.com/ctechnews/article/h1iwkhrap). Do not contact; profile skipped per instructions.

name: Alex Dulin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Morning Consult (Washington, DC)
profile: Alex Dulin co-founded Morning Consult in 2014 with Michael Ramlet and Kyle Dropp and has been CTO since. The firm grew from online political polling into a $1bn+ 'decision intelligence' company. Dulin leads engineering and product technology, from daily survey data collection to the AI systems built on top of it.
interesting_fact: Morning Consult started in political polling, where forecasts are tested against election results. Its tracking data is now used by Federal Reserve researchers, and the company says it ranked first for accuracy among alternative datasets in forecasting public-company earnings.
deep_cut_fact: Unusually for a CTO, Dulin's degree is not in computer science: he holds a bachelor's in political science from the University of Rochester. He built the tech stack of a billion-dollar data company from a polling and politics background.
notes: Behind-the-scenes technical co-founder; CEO Michael Ramlet is the usual spokesperson. Go through press@morningconsult.com. The AI-native data pipeline is a good podcast angle.

name: Kyle Dropp
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Research Officer (formerly President), Morning Consult, Washington DC
profile: Milwaukee-born political scientist (UW-Madison; Stanford PhD 2013) who worked in the Washington Post's polling unit, then cofounded Morning Consult in 2014 with Michael Ramlet and Alex Dulin. The firm became a $1B+ global data-intelligence company tracking public and consumer opinion in real time and increasingly AI-driven. He also taught at Dartmouth (2016-18).
interesting_fact: While building Morning Consult he was also an assistant professor in Dartmouth's Department of Government, leading its Washington program (2016-18) and teaching persuasion and applied data science; he was on Ad Age's 40 Under 40 (2020).
deep_cut_fact: He co-wrote the viral April 2014 Monkey Cage study (with Joshua Kertzer and Thomas Zeitzoff) that asked Americans to find Ukraine on a map: only about 1 in 6 could, and the farther off their guess, the more they backed US military intervention.
notes: Title has varied across sources (President vs Chief Research Officer); the IDFA bio says Chief Research Officer. Active in DC civic/business networks (Economic Club of Washington, Aspen Vanguard, Public Affairs Council board). No published press email found on the Morning Consult site.

name: Michael Ramlet
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Morning Consult (Washington, DC)
profile: Michael Ramlet (University of Minnesota Carlson School, BSB 2009) co-founded Morning Consult around 2013-14 with Kyle Dropp and Alex Dulin. It grew from a healthcare-policy newsletter into a global survey-based business-intelligence firm polling tens of thousands of people daily, valued at ~$1bn, and is now repositioning as an 'AI-native' intelligence company.
interesting_fact: Morning Consult's daily consumer-confidence tracking became a real-time economic indicator during the 2020 pandemic, with data shared with the Federal Reserve and Germany's central bank; he co-founded the firm before he was old enough to rent a car.
deep_cut_fact: Morning Consult started as a daily healthcare newsletter he launched while still a Carlson student; its very first poll asked whether young, uninsured people would sign up for insurance on the new ACA marketplaces. He was named UMN Entrepreneur of the Year in 2024.
notes: Grew up outside Madison, Wisconsin; worked at Purple Strategies before Morning Consult. Frequent conference speaker (Adweek, Cannes). AI angle: company pitching 'AI-native' market intelligence.

name: Matthew Strongin
current_role: Co-founder, CFO and director of The Fynder Group (Nature's Fynd), Chicago
profile: Matthew Strongin is one of six founders of Nature's Fynd (The Fynder Group, formerly Sustainable Bioproducts, 2012) and its long-time CFO; he came from venture capital and banking. The Chicago company makes 'Fy' protein by fermenting a fungus from Yellowstone's hot springs and raised money from Breakthrough Energy Ventures, SoftBank, ADM and Danone at a valuation above $1B.
interesting_fact: The company's 'Fy' protein comes from a fungus (Fusarium strain flavolapis) found in Yellowstone's geothermal springs during a NASA-funded study of life in extreme environments; NASA later funded work on growing it for astronauts.
deep_cut_fact: Nature's Fynd started life in 2012 as Sustainable Bioproducts, trying to turn the Yellowstone microbe into biodiesel before pivoting to food, and it pays Yellowstone a share of profits for the right to harvest from the park.
notes: Behind-the-scenes finance co-founder; no interviews found. CEO Thomas Jonas is the public face. The deep-cut fact is about the company, not him personally. Also listed as founder of Lotic Labs (per aggregators, unverified).

name: Thomas Jonas
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nature's Fynd (now The Fynder Group), Chicago
profile: French-born HEC graduate and former packaging-industry executive (MeadWestvaco beauty & personal care, Alcan Beauty Solutions) who co-founded Nature's Fynd around 2014. The Chicago company grows 'Fy', a protein from a fungus first studied in NASA-funded Yellowstone extremophile research, via fermentation; it raised ~$500M from backers including Bill Gates' Breakthrough Energy and was valued at ~$1B.
interesting_fact: The company's microbe comes from Yellowstone's volcanic hot springs, discovered by co-founder Mark Kozubal during NASA-funded research into how life might survive on other planets.
deep_cut_fact: After HEC (class of 1993) he served as a French Air Force officer and then ran a European-food distribution business in Hong Kong; his pivot to sustainability came in 2012 when a family holiday on Kaua'i stretched to a year and he saw plastic bottles piling up on the beaches. HEC named him 'HEC of the Year' 2022.
notes: Company rebranded from Nature's Fynd to The Fynder Group (food, pharma, materials). Has done climate podcasts before (My Climate Journey ep.169) - receptive to podcast format. Quote: 'It is not by lecturing and making people feel guilty that we will have an impact on the world.'

name: Wang Yongfeng
current_role: Chairman and CEO, Neusoft Reach (东软睿驰), automotive software and AI-vehicle platforms
profile: Wang Yongfeng is a long-time Neusoft Group executive (former VP, president and rotating CEO of Neusoft, 600718.SH) who now chairs and runs Neusoft Reach, Neusoft's intelligent-vehicle spin-off and a Hurun-listed unicorn. Neusoft Reach supplies automotive base software (NeuSAR OS), AI computing platforms, driver-assistance stacks and EV power electronics (BMS) to carmakers.
interesting_fact: Neusoft Reach's NeuSAR automotive OS has been adapted to more than 100 mainstream domestic and international chips; Wang calls the car OS 'the strategic commanding height' of intelligent vehicles (Beijing Auto Show 2026).
deep_cut_fact: He trained in AI long before the current boom: he holds a master's in computer applications (artificial intelligence) from Jilin University, and was named an outstanding young talent of China's software industry.
notes: He stepped down as Neusoft Group rotating CEO in 2025 and appears as Neusoft Reach chairman/CEO in April 2026 coverage. Gives interviews at auto shows (Chinese-language media). Data-center/AI angle: car-cloud AI computing platform. 'Founder' label in input is loose; Neusoft Reach was founded by Neusoft Group.

name: Jeff Zheng
current_role: Founder and CEO, NewsBreak (Particle Media), Mountain View, CA
profile: Search and recommendation engineer who led Yahoo Labs in Beijing, then left in 2011 to launch Chinese news app Yidian Zixun before founding NewsBreak in Silicon Valley in 2015. NewsBreak became one of the most-downloaded local-news apps in the US, raising $115M in 2021 at a $1B+ valuation; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: Former Microsoft AI and Bing chief Harry Shum became NewsBreak's board chairman in 2020.
deep_cut_fact: At Yahoo he headed Yahoo Labs Beijing, overseeing algorithm work across search, media, advertising and mobile, before leaving to build Yidian Zixun, the main rival to ByteDance's Toutiao.
notes: No published press email found (search budget ran out before confirming). Company has faced press scrutiny (2024 Reuters report on AI-generated stories and Chinese origins) - tread carefully. Approach via NewsBreak corporate site/LinkedIn.

name: Xuyang Ren
current_role: Co-founder, NewsBreak (Particle Media) and Yidian Zixun; angel investor (founded Tianshan Capital in 2015)
profile: Ren Xuyang (任旭阳) was an early Baidu executive and its VP of marketing and business development. He co-founded Chinese news aggregator Yidian Zixun and, with Jeff Zheng, the US local-news app NewsBreak (Particle Media), which reached a $1B+ valuation. Zheng runs NewsBreak as CEO, while Ren is mainly a serial founder and angel investor.
interesting_fact: NewsBreak became one of the most-downloaded news apps in the US. It started out applying the 'interest engine' recommendation approach behind Yidian Zixun's success in China to the American market.
deep_cut_fact: Ren was part of Baidu's early founding-era team. Chinese media also credit him with leading the creation of iQiyi, now one of China's biggest video-streaming platforms, as well as Yidian Zixun.
notes: China-based and low profile in English-language media. Jeff Zheng is NewsBreak's public face. Ren briefly served as Yidian Zixun CEO in early 2019. No personal contact was found.

name: Dan Cogan-Drew
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Academic Officer, Newsela
profile: Former teacher and charter-school digital-learning director who co-founded Newsela with Matthew Gross in 2013. Newsela began by rewriting news articles at multiple reading levels for classrooms and grew into a K-12 content platform (later adding Formative) used by millions of educators; he leads its academic work on student outcomes.
interesting_fact: Newsela 'started with news content, differentiated for students' - the same article published at several reading levels so a whole class could read it together.
deep_cut_fact: He began his education career in Teach For America and went on to teach in public and private schools - and in the U.S. Navy; he holds degrees from Wesleyan, Brown and Tufts.
notes: Educator-first founder; frequent speaker (ASU+GSV, ASCD). Newsela press office is the published route.

name: Matthew Gross
current_role: Founder & Executive Chair, Newsela (title per recent profiles; verify)
profile: Former Teach for America music teacher and New York education-policy leader who founded Newsela in 2013, an edtech platform that adapts news and instructional texts to each student's reading level. Newsela raised $100M in 2021 at a $1B valuation and later combined with Formative; Gross moved from CEO to executive chair.
interesting_fact: He started Newsela after a meeting with his struggling-reader son's assistant principal left him feeling the school had given up on his son.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a Teach for America corps member teaching music at C.S. 50 in the South Bronx, and before Newsela ran the Regents Research Fund, which helped implement New York's Race to the Top reforms. His favorite school subject: U.S. History.
notes: Exact current title unclear (sources differ between executive chair and co-founder after CEO change). Also on New Classrooms board.

name: Michael Bermingham
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Business Officer, Nium (Singapore cross-border payments; also listed as Global Relationship Officer on some 2025 event pages)
profile: Compliance and FX-industry veteran (Monmouth University BSBA) who spent years at forex broker GAIN Capital, latterly as director of its Australian business, before co-founding remittance startup InstaReM with Prajit Nanu in Singapore in 2014. InstaReM became Nium in 2019, a B2B cross-border payments and card-issuing platform valued at $2B+ in 2021; he drives strategy, partnerships and operations.
interesting_fact: Nium builds all its payments technology in-house and grew from a licensed money-transfer service into a full-stack payments infrastructure provider; in 2020 he said volumes were doubling year on year to about $6B.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech he spent about a decade at GAIN Capital, leading its operations and compliance teams in both the UK and US before running its Australian arm; that regulatory background was the compliance backbone InstaReM was built on.
notes: Goes by 'Mike' on Nium event pages. Low-profile co-founder; Prajit Nanu is the public face. Deep-cut source is an org-chart profile (moderate reliability).

name: Prajit Nanu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Nium (leads the company from its San Francisco office)
profile: Co-founded Instarem in 2014 with Michael Bermingham as a Singapore remittance app; rebranded Nium in 2019 and became a B2B cross-border payments infrastructure unicorn (~$2B valuation in 2022). Nium says it holds licenses in 40+ markets and processes $60B+ a year; Nanu is pushing stablecoin settlement and a planned US IPO.
interesting_fact: He started the company after personally experiencing the friction of sending money across borders; Nium now connects 190+ countries and issues 41M+ card tokens a year, and recently added USDC stablecoin funding and settlement via a Circle partnership.
deep_cut_fact: In September 2026 Nanu was named to Skift's 2026 Power Rankings of travel-industry leaders (travel is one of Nium's biggest verticals), and he has been an EY Entrepreneur Of The Year finalist.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who speaks regularly on payments, stablecoins and AI; press@nium.com is the published PR route. Relocated leadership to San Francisco ahead of US IPO plans (IPO target slipped to end-2026 per 2024 reports).

name: Akhil Gupta
current_role: Co-founder, NoBroker Technologies (Bengaluru proptech) - widely described as its CTO; not independently confirmed here
profile: IIT alumnus who co-founded NoBroker in 2013 with Amit Kumar Agarwal and Saurabh Garg as a broker-free portal connecting flat owners and tenants. It expanded into resale, home services, the NoBrokerHood society-management app and the CallZen.AI conversational-intelligence tool, raised ~$361M (Tiger Global, General Atlantic, Google) and became a unicorn in Nov 2021.
interesting_fact: NoBroker runs a consumer-to-consumer real-estate model; by 2022 it handled 500,000+ transactions a year with over 7.5 million properties registered, and its NoBrokerHood app became part of India's ONDC network.
notes: Co-founder Amit Agarwal is the public face/CEO; Akhil Gupta is lower-profile. Web-search quota ran out, so no sourced deep-cut fact. Common name - check NoBroker context.

name: Saurabh Garg
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Business Officer, NoBroker.com
profile: IIT and IIM Ahmedabad (PGP 2004) alumnus who co-founded Bengaluru-based NoBroker in 2014 with Amit Kumar Agarwal and Akhil Gupta to let Indians rent and buy property without paying broker commissions. NoBroker became India's first proptech unicorn (~$1B, 2021) and has expanded into home services and society-management (NoBrokerHood); Garg is also an angel investor in 30+ startups.
interesting_fact: He has said he first felt the problem in 2007, when he struggled to find accommodation in Mumbai without paying a large broker fee.
deep_cut_fact: He attempted startups while at IIT during the dot-com boom, then turned down master's-in-finance offers from LSE and Columbia to attend IIM Ahmedabad to learn 'how companies are built'; IIMA later gave him its Young Alumni Achievers' Award (YAAA 2022).
notes: Regular speaker at IITs/IIMs/incubators - open to talks. No verified press email found (only a redacted address on YourStory). Sources differ on whether his IIT was Bombay or Delhi; omitted.

name: Benjamin Eldridge
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Nutcracker Therapeutics (Emeryville, CA)
profile: Engineer-inventor who co-founded Nutcracker Therapeutics in 2018 with former FormFactor CEO Igor Khandros, applying semiconductor-style biochip manufacturing to RNA therapeutics. Previously a longtime FormFactor executive (incl. CTO) after starting at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center. Nutcracker has repositioned as an RNA contract research/development/manufacturing (CRDMO) business.
interesting_fact: Nutcracker's ACORN/NMU systems make nanoparticle-encapsulated RNA therapeutics on single-use biochips, essentially an RNA factory 'in a box' borrowed from chip-industry thinking.
deep_cut_fact: He is a named inventor on more than 200 US patents, and began his career doing engineering at IBM's T.J. Watson Research Center; he holds an M.S. in Physics from Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.
notes: Company status unclear: CEO Khandros retired March 2025 (Cynthia Collins interim CEO); PitchBook lists company out of business as of Nov 2025, while GEN covered it in Dec 2025. Verify his current role before outreach. No published press contact found.

name: Ishay Green
current_role: Co-founder, OpenWeb (formerly Spot.IM); current operating role unclear (LinkedIn shows MGK Labs, Tel Aviv)
profile: Israeli software architect who co-founded Spot.IM with Nadav Shoval. Spot.IM was renamed OpenWeb in 2020 and builds hosted comment sections, community tools and ad products for publishers. OpenWeb passed a $1B valuation in its 2021 Series E and was valued at $1.5B+ in its 2022 Series F. Green keeps a low profile; his LinkedIn now describes him as an entrepreneur, investor and systems architect.
interesting_fact: OpenWeb's 2021 $150M round included The New York Times Company and NYU professor Scott Galloway among its investors, an unusual cap table for an ad-tech company.
notes: The LinkedIn profile (Tel Aviv; 'entrepreneur, investor, software & system architect'; MGK Labs; open-source HumanitarianGenome.org project) very likely belongs to him, but the fetched view did not show OpenWeb, so confirm before using it. Avoid OpenWeb's 2024 CEO dispute involving co-founder Nadav Shoval. No OpenWeb press email found.

name: Nadav Shoval
current_role: Co-founder & board member, Project Omega (spent-nuclear-fuel recycling); CEO of FlowMode; senior advisor to OpenWeb
profile: Israeli-American entrepreneur (b. 1990) who co-founded Spot.IM in 2015, later renamed OpenWeb, the publisher comments/engagement platform valued above $1.5B in 2022. He was CEO until he left in 2024. In 2025 he co-founded Project Omega with CEO Staff Sheehan. It recycles used nuclear fuel into long-duration power sources and reactor fuel and emerged from stealth in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: Project Omega calls used nuclear fuel 'the crude oil of the future'. It uses pyroprocessing to refine it into long-life power isotopes, next-gen reactor fuel and medical/scientific isotopes, and announced an $80M raise in Nov 2026.
deep_cut_fact: At 24 he wrote in VentureBeat that he had been building startups since age 11, that Spot.IM was his fifth venture, and that 'I have had the tremendous opportunity to accrue a great many failures.'
notes: Strong fit for the energy angle via Project Omega (nuclear waste to power). Sensitive: he was ousted as OpenWeb CEO in Sept 2024 after a board dispute (an Israeli court rejected his petition), and per Wikipedia OpenWeb sought insolvency protection in Sept 2026. Avoid both topics. Project Omega's team page lists Staff Sheehan as CEO, and Johanna Spangenberg Jones as Head of Communications.

name: Roee Goldberg
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Atmospheric AI (London; raw-material supply-chain modeling)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who joined Spot.IM (now OpenWeb) as co-founder and COO in 2014, helping build the publisher comment/conversation platform into a unicorn before leaving the COO role around January 2022. In 2025 he founded London-based Atmospheric AI, which builds digital twins of raw-material supply chains (cost, resilience, emissions) and raised a $10M seed led by DBL Partners in November 2026.
interesting_fact: Atmospheric AI models tens of thousands of industrial plants 'between the well and your factory gate' so manufacturers can see the true cost and carbon of what they buy; the seed will extend models from plastics into chemicals, paper and metals.
deep_cut_fact: Before OpenWeb he was co-founder and CEO of a startup called Servito.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/climate podcast: just raised a seed for a climate/industrial supply-chain AI company (Axios exclusive, Nov 2026). Some sources say he advises Tech Nation's Climate Growth Programme (unverified). Wikipedia credits OpenWeb's founding to Nadav Shoval and Ishay Green only.

name: Ivan Dimov
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO (2016-May 2025), Orca Bio
profile: Engineer-turned-biotech founder (PhD applied biophysics, Dublin City University; postdocs at UC Berkeley and in Irv Weissman's Stanford lab) who co-founded Orca Bio in 2016 with Nate Fernhoff and Jeroen Bekaert. Orca develops high-precision allogeneic cell therapies (lead product Orca-T for blood cancers); Fernhoff succeeded him as CEO in May 2025 ahead of the BLA filing.
interesting_fact: He also co-founded Lucira Health, spun out of his Berkeley microfluidics work, which won FDA authorization for the first at-home COVID-19 self-test and was later acquired by Pfizer.
deep_cut_fact: His background is in electronics and bio-MEMS; he has said working with Stanford physicians changed his approach from 'building technology first' to starting from a clearly defined medical problem.
notes: CEO transition reported May 2025 (https://trial.medpath.com/news/902ccabbc6efd8da/orca-bio-appoints-co-founder-nate-fernhoff-as-ceo-ahead-of-2025-bla-submission-for-orca-t); his current exact title not confirmed. Also earlier co-founded Blobcode Technologies.

name: Jeroen Bekaert
current_role: Co-founder and President, Orca Bio (since May 2025; previously COO)
profile: Belgian-born engineer (Ghent PhD in computer science engineering, Stanford GSB master's) who co-founded cell-therapy company Orca Bio in 2016 with Ivan Dimov and Nate Fernhoff. Orca's high-precision cell therapy Orca-T won FDA approval as Tregzi in June 2026 for blood-cancer patients undergoing stem-cell transplants; Bekaert oversees company operations as President.
interesting_fact: Orca-T (Tregzi), approved by the FDA on 30 June 2026, is described as the first regulatory T-cell therapy approved for blood-cancer patients undergoing allogeneic stem-cell transplant.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as a researcher at Los Alamos National Laboratory, later ran J&J supply-chain engineering for EMEA and Merck KGaA's Silicon Valley innovation center, and was a Gustave Boel-Sofina Fellow.
notes: Operations-focused executive with a low media profile; Nate Fernhoff is CEO since 2025. Corporate comms contact listed on press releases.

name: Nathaniel Fernhoff
current_role: Co-founder and CEO (since May 2025), Orca Bio
profile: Scientist-founder (Stanford BS in biology and math, UC Berkeley PhD) who co-founded Menlo Park cell-therapy company Orca Bio in 2016 with Ivan Dimov and Jeroen Bekaert, serving as CSO before becoming CEO in 2025. Orca builds high-precision donor-cell therapies for blood cancers; its lead product Orca-T won FDA approval as Tregzi on June 30, 2026.
interesting_fact: Tregzi (Orca-T), approved by the FDA in June 2026, is described as the first approved therapy built on highly purified regulatory T cells, aimed at improving chronic-GVHD-free survival after matched-donor stem cell transplants.
deep_cut_fact: Before Orca he was an NIH Ruth L. Kirschstein NRSA postdoctoral scholar in Irving Weissman's stem-cell lab at Stanford, and he holds two Stanford bachelor's degrees, in biological sciences and in mathematics.
notes: Goes by Nate Fernhoff. Biotech rather than energy/data-center fit; timely hook is the 2026 Tregzi approval and commercial launch. Route via Orca Bio corporate communications.

name: Ronald Martell
profile: Listed by Hurun as a founder of Orca Bio (Menlo Park/Sacramento cell-therapy company founded 2016, developer of Orca-T for blood cancers; valued ~$2B). Orca Bio's current leadership page names co-founders Nate Fernhoff (CEO) and Jeroen Bekaert (President) and does not mention a Ronald Martell, so his link to the company could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity unverified; not on Orca Bio's leadership page (https://orcabio.com/our-company/). Possibly an early executive/board member or a Hurun data error - verify before outreach. Search budget ran out before further checks.

name: Court Cunningham
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Orchard (real estate tech, New York)
profile: Serial operator who ran local-marketing firm Yodle as CEO from 2007, growing it to $200M+ revenue before its 2016 sale to Web.com for $342M. In 2017 he co-founded Orchard, which lets homeowners buy a new home before selling the old one, and has expanded it across multiple US states. Former DoubleClick VP and Harvard MBA.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Yodle went from about $1M to over $200M in revenue and sold to Web.com for $342M.
deep_cut_fact: In high school he spent about three years building an 18th-century-style mahogany desk; when his woodworking teacher said the dividers were too loose, he made him start over ('You're better than good enough'). His mom's mantra was 'Action TNT' (today, not tomorrow).
notes: Regular Inman speaker; approachable via Orchard press.

name: Phil DeGisi
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product & Marketing Officer, Orchard (as of 2022; current title not re-verified)
profile: Phil DeGisi co-founded Orchard, the 'buy before you sell' real-estate tech company that lets homeowners purchase a new home before selling their old one, which reached a $1B+ valuation within about four years. He leads Orchard's product and marketing teams, growing marketing from one person to a 30-person department.
interesting_fact: Named a HousingWire 2022 Marketing Leader; in Orchard's early days he personally met with hundreds of homeowners to understand the pain of buying and selling a home.
notes: Low public profile. Web-search budget exhausted mid-lane, so background/deep-cut research was limited to direct page fetches.

name: Gilles Wainrib
current_role: Co-founder of Owkin (Chief Scientific Officer since 2016 per profiles; current title unconfirmed)
profile: French applied mathematician and machine-learning researcher who co-founded Owkin in Paris in 2016 with haematologist Thomas Clozel. Owkin uses AI and privacy-preserving (federated) learning on hospital data for drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a Sanofi investment, and now builds agentic AI for biology (K Navigator, K Pro). He came from academia (Stanford postdoc, assistant professor).
interesting_fact: Owkin's founding idea was to unlock insights from vast amounts of patient data held in hospitals and research centers 'in a privacy-preserving and secure way' - Owkin describes Wainrib as a pioneer of machine learning in biology.
deep_cut_fact: Before Owkin he was a mathematical neuroscientist: with Jonathan Touboul (Collège de France team) he co-authored work on bifurcations of stochastic differential equations and macroscopic limits of large stochastic neural networks.

public_contacts.value: alistair.jennings@owkin.com (international media; page's mailto link points to michelle.shearly@owkin.com)

notes: Low-profile scientist co-founder; Thomas Clozel is Owkin's public face. Press contacts on Owkin's press kit change often - check the latest release. Education (Ecole Polytechnique) per TheOrg, not independently verified.

name: Thomas Clozel
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Owkin (Paris / New York)
profile: French oncologist-hematologist (MD) and former clinical assistant professor at Hopital Henri-Mondor who co-founded Owkin in 2016 with ML professor Gilles Wainrib. Owkin applies AI and federated learning to drug discovery and diagnostics, became a unicorn in 2021 after a $180M Sanofi investment, and now pitches 'biological artificial superintelligence' via its K Pro AI-scientist agent.
interesting_fact: Owkin has raised 300M+ dollars and signed AI deals with Sanofi, BMS, Servier, MSD and AstraZeneca; it released K Pro, an agentic 'AI scientist' for biology, in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Before medicine he flirted with moving to LA 'to crack Hollywood'. He landed his Weill Cornell lab spot by meeting Ari Melnick in a Deauville hotel lobby: his phone had died, so he scanned the room until he spotted a man sipping a Diet Coke while reading a cell-biology paper.
notes: Son of Actelion founders Jean-Paul and Martine Clozel. Frequent conference speaker on AI in biology; Owkin press team is the clear route.

name: Austin Allison
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Pacaso
profile: Cincinnati-raised entrepreneur who founded real-estate transaction software dotloop in 2009, sold it to Zillow in 2015 (reported ~$108-120M) and ran it inside Zillow until 2018. He then co-founded Pacaso (2020), which sells co-owned second homes via property-specific LLCs; it hit a $1B valuation within five months, then a record for a US startup.
interesting_fact: Pacaso reached unicorn status in about five months after launch in 2020, among the fastest ever for a US startup.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in a small town north of Cincinnati, the son of a carpenter, and says he was 'swinging a hammer starting at age three or four'; watching his father show up every day to provide shaped his work ethic.
notes: Frequent podcast guest and speaker; receptive to founder-story interviews.

name: Spencer Rascoff
current_role: CEO, Match Group (since Feb 2025; also directly ran Tinder from July 2025); co-founder of Pacaso
profile: Serial founder (b. 1975) who co-founded Hotwire at 24 (sold to IAC for $685M), then co-founded Zillow and ran it as CEO 2010-2019 through its IPO and 15 acquisitions. Afterwards he co-founded dot.LA, co-ownership home platform Pacaso (unicorn) and AI firm Replify via family office 75 & Sunny, before being named Match Group CEO in 2025 to turn around Tinder/Hinge.
interesting_fact: He co-founded Hotwire.com in 1999 at age 24 after stints at Goldman Sachs and TPG; it sold to IAC a few years later for $685M.
deep_cut_fact: As a Visiting Executive Professor at Harvard Business School (2020) he co-created and co-taught the 'Managing Tech Ventures' course; he also co-wrote the NYT bestseller 'Zillow Talk' (2015).
notes: Highly visible public-company CEO; previously hosted the 'Office Hours' podcast and writes open letters on LinkedIn. Pacaso is the Hurun-listed source but Match Group is his day job; route via Match Group PR or 75 & Sunny.

name: Mikita Mikado
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PandaDoc (San Francisco / Minsk-origin document automation and e-signature company)
profile: Minsk-born entrepreneur (BSUIR graduate) who, with co-founder Sergey Barysiuk, built Quote Roller in 2011 to automate sales proposals; it became PandaDoc in 2013, raised funding from Kima Ventures, Microsoft Ventures, HubSpot and others, and hit a $1B valuation in 2021. He has run the company from San Francisco since 2013.
interesting_fact: He was featured in Yury Dud's 2020 documentary on Russian-speaking founders in Silicon Valley, which made him a role model for young people pursuing IT careers.
deep_cut_fact: At 19 he first went to the U.S. on a Work and Travel student program, working part-time jobs while teaching himself web design and software development - years before returning to Minsk to build Quote Roller, PandaDoc's predecessor.
notes: PandaDoc about page lists him as CEO; Keith Rabkin also appears (some third-party sites call Rabkin CEO) - confirm current title. Avoid politics: he was outspoken during Belarus 2020 protests (Protect Belarus initiative). Has told a 'berry seller' origin story in podcasts (Mixergy, SaaS Club).

name: Sergey Barysiuk
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, PandaDoc
profile: Belarusian-born engineer (also spelled Siarhei Barysiuk / Sergey Borisyuk) who, with Mikita Mikado, turned their Minsk software-outsourcing shop's sales-quote tool Quote Roller (c.2011) into PandaDoc, a document automation and e-signature platform. PandaDoc reached a $1B valuation in 2021 and is now headquartered in San Francisco with large teams in Europe.
interesting_fact: PandaDoc began life as Quote Roller, a set of proposal templates sent as a link, before broadening into all business documents and e-signatures and becoming one of the first Belarus-founded unicorns.
deep_cut_fact: He says the idea came on 'a warm June evening' at their outsourcing firm, when he was about to go home and got buried in contracts and proposals to write - as 'a true developer' who disliked paperwork, he decided the process had to be automated.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; Mikado is the public face. Company relocated staff out of Belarus after 2020 (sensitive political context - avoid in outreach). PandaDoc site blocked automated fetch; no press email confirmed.

name: Eynat Guez
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Papaya Global
profile: French-born Israeli entrepreneur (raised in Netanya) who co-founded Papaya Global in 2016 with Ofer Herman and Ruben Drong. The payroll and workforce-payments platform hit a $3.7B valuation in 2021, making it Israel's first woman-led unicorn; it now processes tens of billions in annual payments and is pushing agentic-AI compliance products (Papaya One, Papaya Talent in 2026).
interesting_fact: Papaya is her third company: she earlier founded Relocation Source (2009, corporate relocation) and Expert Source (helping firms expand into East Asia), after seven years as COO of LR Group, a holding company running infrastructure projects in Africa.
deep_cut_fact: Before business she worked as a youth journalist (Channel 2, Israeli Educational TV, Ma'ariv La'noar), served in the IDF as an F-16 squadron adjutant, and was a competitive swimmer; she sits on the board of Hagal Shely, an NGO that uses the sea (surfing) as therapy.
notes: Media-friendly CEO; frequent podcast guest (e.g. Fintech Leaders). Press contact on 2026 releases is Naomi Fletcher. Reports (Finance Magnates) say Papaya has explored a sale at up to $4.5B.

name: Ofer Herman
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Papaya Global (2016-2023); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded global payroll and workforce-payments platform Papaya Global in 2016 with Eynat Guez and Ruben Drong, serving as CTO as it grew to a $3.7B valuation in its 2021 Series D. He announced in June 2023 that he was leaving Papaya after seven-plus years. Earlier he co-founded AASL and co-founded/led MRD-IT Solutions and SafelyGuard.
interesting_fact: Papaya Global went from a $1.5M seed in 2016 to a $3.7B valuation in Sept 2021 (Series D led by Insight Partners and Tiger Global), and later bought UK payments firm Azimo.
notes: Very low public profile; no current venture found after leaving Papaya in June 2023 (per aggregator citing his LinkedIn post). Earlier ventures (AASL, MRD-IT Solutions, SafelyGuard) from Welcome to the Jungle profile only. Best route likely LinkedIn.

name: Ruben Drong
current_role: Co-founder, Papaya Global (named Chief Innovation Officer in 2022)
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur and software engineer who co-founded global payroll and workforce-payments platform Papaya Global in 2016 with Eynat Guez and Ofer Herman. He was Papaya's first Chief Product Officer, charting its technology vision, before moving in 2022 to Chief Innovation Officer focused on long-term strategy.
interesting_fact: As Papaya Global's first Chief Product Officer he set the technology vision for a platform that now runs payroll and payments in 160+ countries; in 2022 he shifted to Chief Innovation Officer.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Eynat Guez is the company's public face. Earlier ventures (AASL, SafelyGuard, MRD-IT) appear only on aggregator profiles, so not used. Best route LinkedIn or Papaya PR.

name: Artavazd Mehrabyan
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Picsart (creative/AI photo-video editing platform, Armenia/US)
profile: Armenian software engineer who co-founded Picsart with Hovhannes Avoyan and Mikayel Vardanyan (c.2011), serving first as COO and later as CTO. Picsart grew to ~150M monthly active users and 1B+ downloads and became Armenia's first unicorn (2021). He now leads Picsart's push into generative AI, including a commercially safe image model built with Getty Images.
interesting_fact: Picsart reached about 150 million monthly active users and over one billion downloads, and partnered with Getty Images in 2024 on a commercially safe text-to-image model.
deep_cut_fact: Before Picsart he was a chief software architect (incl. at Lycos Europe, Sourcio and Virtual Solutions); he holds two master's degrees: Industrial Engineering from the Armenian National Agrarian University and Computer Science from the American University of Armenia.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Hovhannes Avoyan is the public face. Good angle: Picsart's AI/GPU infrastructure and Armenia's tech ecosystem. Prior-employer list from a job-board company profile; degrees from conference speaker bio.

name: Hovhannes Avoyan
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Picsart
profile: Armenian-American serial entrepreneur (b. 1965, Yerevan) who co-founded photo/video editor Picsart in 2011 and built it into a 150M+ MAU creative platform. Earlier companies (CEDIT, Sourcio, Monitis and others) were sold to buyers including Lycos, GFI/TeamViewer and HelpSystems.
interesting_fact: Five of his startups before Picsart were acquired by global companies, and he was founding president of Armenia's Union of IT Enterprises (2000-2015).
deep_cut_fact: Besides a 1987 computer science degree, he holds a master's in political science and international affairs from the American University of Armenia (1995), which gave him its Distinguished Alumni Award in 2016; he also sits on AUA's board of trustees.
notes: Active speaker/writer on AI; has a TechCrunch contributor page.

name: Ben Kinney
current_role: Co-founder, PLACE Inc.; founder, Ben Kinney Companies (BKCO)
profile: Washington-state real estate agent turned proptech entrepreneur. Founded BKCO (Brivity, ActiveRain, Kwkly, Blueroof360) and in 2019 co-founded PLACE with Chris Suarez, a platform/services company for top real-estate teams that raised $100M led by Goldman Sachs at a $1B valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: He was the top-ranked agent in Washington state by transaction volume from 2012 to 2021 and appeared on the WSJ/REAL Trends top-1,000 agents lists 2011-2022.
deep_cut_fact: While studying at Western Washington University he worked as a cable-TV installer, then sold cable, phone and internet door-to-door before starting in real estate in 2004.
notes: Active speaker and author (Inman, RISMedia). PLACE reportedly eyeing an IPO.

name: Chris Suarez
current_role: Co-founder, PLACE, Inc. (real estate team platform); leads Xperience Brokerage Network and Xperience Growth Coaching
profile: Portland-area real estate entrepreneur who founded Xperience, a top Keller Williams expansion organisation, then in 2020 co-founded PLACE with Ben Kinney, a platform providing tech, back-office and services to top agent teams across 100+ US/Canada markets; PLACE reached unicorn valuation. He also owns brokerage offices and runs coaching/mastermind programmes.
interesting_fact: PLACE launched in early 2020 already carrying $1.5B in sales and $40M revenue from its founders' existing businesses, just as COVID-19 hit.
deep_cut_fact: He and Ben Kinney shared the 2023 EY Entrepreneur Of The Year Mountain West Award; he hosts the podcast 'Xperience Growth with Chris Suarez'.

public_contacts.value: Xperience Growth with Chris Suarez (Apple Podcasts)

notes: Active speaker/coach with his own site and podcast - accessible. Team page: https://place.com/team/

name: Justin Waldron
current_role: Co-founder and President, Playco (Tokyo instant-play web games company), per 2020 coverage; current title not re-confirmed
profile: American game developer and angel investor who co-founded Zynga at 19 and was lead engineer/designer on its first game, Texas Hold'em Poker (later Zynga Poker). He rose to SVP Product before leaving in October 2013. He then co-founded Playco in Tokyo with Game Closure's Michael Carter; it raised a $100M Series A in September 2020 at just over $1B, making it a unicorn.
interesting_fact: He was only 19 when he built Zynga Poker, Zynga's first game. On leaving in 2013 he wrote that it had been 'six and a half years since we pushed the button to launch our first game, and each moment since has been magic'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Playco he had invested in more than 50 startups, including Snackpass and Substack. He relocated to Tokyo to run Playco as President.

public_contacts.value: Colossus episode 'Waldron: The Future of Social Gaming'

notes: Lower profile than Zynga co-founder Mark Pincus. Playco's site is still live (games: Everwing, Heads Up!, Buruburu Do Butsu), but I found no post-2021 news on the company's status or his current title. The Colossus podcast page blocked automated access, so I confirmed it only from search results. Several sources say he dropped out of UConn to co-found Zynga.

name: Michael Carter
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Playco (Tokyo-based instant-games company)
profile: Michael Maxwell Carter co-founded instant-games company Playco in 2020 with Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and game producers Takeshi Otsuka and Teddy Cross. It launched with a $100M Series A (led by Josh Buckley and Sequoia) at a valuation just over $1B. Earlier he founded Game Closure, a StartX-backed HTML5 instant-games startup that raised $12M in 2012.
interesting_fact: Playco makes games that launch instantly from a link, with no download, across Facebook Instant Games, Snapchat Minis, iOS App Clips and similar platforms. Carter predicted that for mobile gaming, 'At some point, people will hit a switch.'
deep_cut_fact: Carter helped create WebSocket: in June 2008 he led the discussions that produced the first version of the protocol, and he and Ian Hickson coined the name 'WebSocket'.
notes: He met Waldron when Waldron was advising Game Closure. He works remotely (Playco execs are spread across Tokyo, Seoul, SF and LA). No published press email or verified personal accounts found. Hurun lists Playco at a $1B valuation.

name: Takeshi Otsuka
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Producer & SVP, Playco (instant-play gaming, HQ Tokyo)
profile: Takeshi Otsuka is a Japanese game producer who led DeNA's Mobage mobile social gaming platform (2005-2015), which Playco says generated over $1B in revenue. He moved to the US in 2011 for roles at DeNA West and N3TWORK. In 2020 he co-founded Playco with Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron, WebSocket co-inventor Michael Carter and Teddy Cross. Playco builds games playable instantly inside social and messaging apps and was valued at $1B in its Series A.
interesting_fact: Playco's co-founders include Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and Michael Carter, co-inventor of HTML5 WebSockets. The company is headquartered in Tokyo but distributed-first, with founders split across Seoul, Tokyo, San Francisco and LA.
deep_cut_fact: He produced 'Kaito Royale' (2009), a mobile social game whose success helped spark Japan's mobile social gaming boom (over a thousand such games were released in 2010) and which also became a TV show. N3TWORK CEO Neil Young called him a '10x-er'.
notes: Second source for the Kaito Royale TV show and the '10x-er' quote: https://www.pocketgamer.biz/n3twork-hires-takeshi-otsuka/. No published press email was found on play.co. Low English-language media profile.

name: Teddy Cross
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Playco (Tokyo-based instant-play games company)
profile: American game producer and engineer and early HTML5 gaming pioneer who worked with Michael Carter at Game Closure from 2011 and led software development at tech companies in Korea. In 2020 he co-founded Playco with Carter, Zynga co-founder Justin Waldron and ex-DeNA executive Takeshi Otsuka; it debuted as a unicorn with a $100M Series A.
interesting_fact: Playco launched in Sept 2020 already a unicorn: a $100M Series A at just over $1B valuation, co-led by Josh Buckley and Sequoia Capital Global Equities, with backers including Keisuke Honda's KSK Angel Fund.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career in 2011 at age 15 as a software intern in gaming, building HTML5 puzzle games that quickly gained thousands of users, and later became a well-known figure in the Korean tech scene.
notes: website@play.co is Playco's published general-inquiry address (not personal). Very young founder (born c.1996 per Playco bio age).

name: Philipp Nieland
current_role: Co-founder of PPRO (cross-border payments infrastructure, London/Munich); current role not verified
profile: German co-founder of PPRO, which provides local/alternative payment-method acquiring and processing to PSPs such as PayPal and Stripe. Crunchbase says he studied economics and computer science and founded PPRO in 2006; MarketScreener credits Nieland and Tobias Schreyer as founders. PPRO's backers include PayPal, Citi Ventures and HPE Growth.
interesting_fact: PPRO raised a $50M round led by PayPal, with Citi Ventures participating and HPE Growth reinvesting.
notes: Very low public profile; founder attribution rests on Crunchbase (https://crunchbase.com/person/philipp-nieland) and MarketScreener. Not to be confused with co-founder Philipp Bock. No published press email found on ppro.com.

name: Tobias Schreyer
current_role: Co-founder of PPRO (former Chief Commercial Officer); not on PPRO's current leadership page
profile: German payments entrepreneur who co-founded PPRO, the London-based local-payments infrastructure provider, with Philipp Nieland in 2006. PPRO was later valued at about $1B. As CCO he helped secure PPRO's UK FCA e-money licence in 2012 and launch its VIABUY prepaid card. As an undergraduate he started a Munich internet service provider.
interesting_fact: His interest in payments started in childhood: he collected prepaid calling cards and traded them at exchanges.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 PYMNTS interview he said he commuted 50 miles to work by bike, using the ride to plan his day. He also said: 'you need to have failed at some point in your career; otherwise you don't know the essentials.'
notes: He is not listed on PPRO's current leadership page (CEO is Motie Bring), so his current role is unverified. Low public profile; LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Davis Siksnans
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Printful; Senior Advisor at Draugiem Group (since June 2022) and angel investor
profile: Latvian entrepreneur who co-founded print-on-demand company Printful with Lauris Liberts in 2013 out of Latvia's Draugiem Group, and was CEO from 2015 to June 2022. Printful became Latvia's first unicorn in 2021 after a $130M investment from Bregal Sagemount, and in late 2024 agreed to merge with rival Printify (combined group named Fyul).
interesting_fact: Printful was spun out of Startup Vitamins, the team's online store selling motivational-quote posters for startups; frustration with third-party printers led them to build their own printing operation.
deep_cut_fact: Printful launched on July 16, 2013 with a three-person team printing t-shirts in co-founder Lauris Liberts's garage; Siksnans's motto: 'A good time to start is anytime, because a better one will never come.'
notes: Stepped down as CEO June 29, 2022 (https://www.printful.com/news/printful-management-team-change). Frequent podcast guest (Mixergy, Hack the Entrepreneur, Wix 'Now What'). No published direct email found; LinkedIn is likely best route.

name: Lauris Liberts
current_role: Founder and co-owner, Draugiem Group; co-founder and board chair of Printful
profile: Latvian tech entrepreneur Lauris Liberts founded the social network draugiem.lv and created Draugiem Group in 2004. In 2013 the group incubated Printful, a print-on-demand and drop-shipping fulfilment service he co-founded with Davis Siksnans; it became Latvia's first unicorn after a $130M investment from Bregal Sagemount in 2021.
interesting_fact: Printful grew out of the team's own side businesses Startup Vitamins and Behappy.me, which sold motivational quote posters and prints; needing a reliable print-and-ship partner, they built their own and launched Printful on July 16, 2013.
deep_cut_fact: He studied economics at the University of Latvia and earned a master's in e-business and innovation from Lancaster University in the UK.
notes: Chair/board role at Printful per MarketScreener aggregator. Draugiem Group (draugiemgroup.com) and Printful press page (printful.com/press) are JS-rendered; no published email extracted. Route via Draugiem Group or Printful press team.

name: Meng Jiange
current_role: Executive Director & Chairman, GenScript Biotech Corp. (HKEX: 1548), parent of Probio; also a director of Legend Biotech
profile: Most likely Robin (Jiange) Meng, chairman of GenScript, whose CDMO subsidiary Probio provides biologics and cell/gene-therapy manufacturing services; GenScript announced plans in Sept 2026 to spin off Probio on the HKEX. A finance executive with 30+ years' experience, he joined GenScript as CFO (c. 2010-2017) and became chairman around 2020.
interesting_fact: Before GenScript he was CFO of Quay Magnesium (2008-2010), Asia finance controller at Saint-Gobain's Grains and Powder division, and held finance roles at Schering-Plough China and Guangdong Whirlpool.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer - a Bachelor of Engineering from Changsha Communications Institute (now Changsha University of Science & Technology) - before earning a Master's in finance from Queen's University at Kingston, Canada.
notes: Identity match is probable but not confirmed: Hurun lists him as a Probio 'founder', while GenScript names Frank Zhang, Sally Wang and Larry Wang as co-founders and Meng as chairman. Also known as Robin Meng / Jian Ge Meng.

name: Joel Gottsegen
current_role: Co-founder, Qualia (current operating role not confirmed; Nate Baker is CEO)
profile: Joel Gottsegen co-founded Qualia in 2015 with Nate Baker and Lucas Hansen; the company runs a cloud platform connecting homebuyers, sellers, lenders, title/escrow and real-estate agents to digitise the US home-closing process, and was valued around $2B. The co-founders were Forbes 30 Under 30 honorees.
interesting_fact: Qualia was the first technology company to join the Coalition to Stop Real Estate Wire Fraud, and all three co-founders were Forbes 30 Under 30 award recipients.
notes: Very low public profile; aggregator sites suggest a Stanford CS degree and a later venture ('Petty Karma'), but these were not verified from primary sources. Best route is via Qualia press or CEO Nate Baker.

name: Lucas Hansen
current_role: Co-founder, CivAI (Civic AI Security Program); co-founder and board member, Qualia
profile: Co-founded Qualia in 2015 with Nate Baker and Joel Gottsegen; Qualia is a real-estate closing/title software platform (unicorn). In 2023 he co-founded CivAI, a Berkeley nonprofit that uses live software demos (deepfakes, phishing, AI biosecurity risks) to educate lawmakers and the public about AI capabilities and dangers.
interesting_fact: CivAI, which he co-founded in response to ChatGPT's launch, gives private AI-risk demos to lawmakers and national-security officials, and is a member of the NIST AI Safety Institute Consortium; its tools were used at the 2025 AI Action Summit.
deep_cut_fact: In October 2025 he wrote a Wall Street Journal op-ed, 'I Need a Chatbot That Won't Drive Me Crazy,' arguing AI firms should be liable for harms like chatbot-induced psychosis if they don't take adequate precautions. He met his CivAI co-founder Siddharth Hiregowdara while working together at Qualia.
notes: Now focused on AI safety (very relevant for an AI/data-center podcast angle); frequently quoted in media (NYT, S&P Global). CivAI site blocked automated fetches this session, so no CivAI contact verified; it has a press section (civai.org/press). LinkedIn: linkedin.com/in/llucash (per search result, not independently verified).

name: Nate Baker
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Qualia (real-estate closing / title software)
profile: Nate Baker is co-founder and CEO of Qualia, a San Francisco software platform that title, escrow and real-estate companies use to run home closings (valued at about $2B per Hurun). He had started a small company in college and then worked at the venture fund 8VC before Qualia. Qualia has since grown past $100M ARR.
interesting_fact: Qualia was chosen by spreadsheet. Baker drew up 10 'selection heuristics' for an enduring B2B software market (platform not feature, network effects, multiple paths to revenue). The finalists were life-insurance broker software, P&C claims-adjusting software and title software.
deep_cut_fact: Qualia's first customer, Massachusetts state senator and real-estate lawyer Barry Feingold, was met at a conference thanks to a Stanford sweatshirt. Baker and Qualia's first 25 employees took turns living in Feingold's Andover basement to learn the title business, and new hires also tutored his kids in math.

public_contacts.value: Guest on The SaaS Podcast (SaaS Club) episode 467

notes: He speaks at industry events (ALTA) and on podcasts, so he is fairly accessible. No published press email was verified. Education (UPenn mechanical engineering) appears only on aggregator sites and is not verified here.

name: Mario Ciabarra
current_role: Founder & CEO, Quantum Metric (digital analytics, Colorado)
profile: Penn State-educated serial founder and son of an immigrant family, the youngest of six, from Montgomery County, PA. He sold his app-performance-monitoring startup DevStream to Compuware, built iPhone app businesses Intelliborn and Rock Your Phone, and in 2015 co-founded Quantum Metric with hacker David Wang. Quantum Metric became Colorado's first tech unicorn after a $200M Insight-led round in 2021.
interesting_fact: Quantum Metric passed $100M in annual recurring revenue in December 2022 and says it captures insights from about 45% of the world's internet users. Penn State's podcast called him the first unicorn founder to start a business in Colorado.
deep_cut_fact: At Penn State he started YourNotes.com, which paid students to take class notes and published them free for other students, funded by sponsors, as a challenge to paid service Nittany Notes. He says he still hates taking notes.
notes: As a teen he resold arcade tokens and sold candy and donuts (Insight Partners profile: https://www.insightpartners.com/ideas/how-mario-ciabarra-is-reimagining-customer-experiences-for-the-fortune-100-with-quantum-metric/). He was a guest on Penn State's 'Dare to Disrupt' podcast.

name: Yang Wei
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Quicktron Robotics (Shanghai Quicktron Intelligent Technology)
profile: Yang Wei (杨威) founded Shanghai-based Quicktron in 2014. It makes autonomous mobile robots and warehouse-automation software, and its backers include Alibaba's Cainiao, BEST Inc., KION Group and Aramco's Prosperity7. By 2021 Quicktron served 500+ customers in 30+ industries and was expanding to Europe, the Americas and Asia.
interesting_fact: In 2021 he set the goal of expanding Quicktron from 15 markets to more than 100 countries and shipping one hundred thousand robots, and said: 'Within five years, we hope to achieve tens of billions in revenue.'
deep_cut_fact: At 36Kr's 2017 summit he gave a talk titled 'Intelligent Robots: Giving Warehouses a Soul' (智能机器人——赋予仓库灵魂), arguing that robot clusters could save about 50% of warehouse labor.
notes: A common Chinese name; identity is tied to Quicktron via 36Kr and The Wire China (which says he is in his early 40s). Education (Peking University master's) appears only in third-party summaries and was not verified. Low English-language profile; best route is via the company.

name: Ni Fei
current_role: Co-founder, Quicktron Robotics (Shanghai Quicktron Intelligent Technology); current title not verified
profile: Shanghai Jiao Tong University PhD in mechatronic engineering and port-automation engineer who co-founded warehouse-robotics company Quicktron (Shanghai, est. 2014) with CEO Yang Wei. Quicktron builds AMRs and intralogistics automation; investors include Cainiao, KION and Aramco's Prosperity7. Company registry data shows him as a ~10.35% shareholder.
interesting_fact: Quicktron's 2020 C+ round of over $100M was co-led by forklift/supply-chain group KION and Saudi Aramco's Prosperity7 Ventures; Cainiao (Alibaba's logistics arm) is also a major shareholder.
deep_cut_fact: Before Quicktron he was director of the R&D center at ZPMC (Shanghai Zhenhua Heavy Industries) electrical company, where he led development of China's first generation of automated rail-mounted gantry cranes and port AGVs.
notes: Very low public profile; Chinese name 倪菲. Bio sourced from 36Kr PitchHub company profile (third-party compiled). Alive status not independently confirmed; no indication otherwise.

name: Christoph F. Gamon
current_role: Co-founder, Razor Group (Berlin), formerly CFO; current role unconfirmed
profile: Christoph Felix Gamon is listed as a co-founder (and former CFO) of Razor Group, founded in Berlin in 2020. Razor buys and scales Amazon marketplace (FBA) brands and was valued at $1.7B after merging with Perch in 2024. It merged with Infinite Commerce in August 2025. By then Max Biller was CEO and Jörg Meiner was CFO.
interesting_fact: Razor merged with US rival Perch in 2024, raising $100M at a $1.7B valuation. It then merged with Infinite Commerce in 2025 to form a Berlin- and Boston-headquartered FBA consolidator.

public_contacts.value: Gaffney Bennett PR (Avery Gerber), media contact on the Aug 2025 Razor/Infinite Commerce merger release (email obfuscated on page)

notes: Very low public profile. His founder/CFO role comes only from MarketScreener insider data (https://www.marketscreener.com/insider/CHRISTOPH-FELIX-GAMON-A1R4OS/), which also links him to Flash Ventures (Rocket Internet) and ConCloud GmbH. The 2025 releases do not name him, and CFO is now Jörg Meiner. Razor's own site was unreachable.

name: Jonas Diezun
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Beam AI (Berlin)
profile: German serial founder (TU Munich business/electrical engineering, CDTM) who was an early team member helping scale rail-tech firm Konux, then in 2020 co-founded Berlin e-commerce aggregator Razor Group, which hit unicorn status in 2021. Since 2022 he runs Beam AI, which builds self-learning AI agents for enterprise workflows.
interesting_fact: Razor Group, which buys and scales Amazon marketplace brands, reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021, only about a year after he co-founded it.
deep_cut_fact: He studied behavioural economics and neuroscience at TU Munich and, by his own account, became a 'semi-professional pizza maker' during the pandemic; his Beam bio invites people to ask him about the best coffee spots in Munich.
notes: Now focused on AI agents (relevant to AI/data-center angle). Writes regularly on the Beam blog; LinkedIn is the most active channel.

name: Oliver Dlugosch
current_role: Co-founder & CCO, GeneralMind (Berlin AI supply-chain startup); co-founder of Razor Group
profile: Dr. Oliver Dlugosch trained as a physicist, moved into consulting and operating roles, and in 2020 co-founded Berlin e-commerce aggregator Razor Group (COO), which acquired and integrated 300+ Amazon/e-commerce brands. In 2025 the Razor founding team launched GeneralMind, an 'AI system of action' that automates email/spreadsheet-heavy supply-chain operations; it raised $12M in Jan 2026.
interesting_fact: GeneralMind's $12M round was led by Lakestar, Leo Capital and others; the startup is based in Berlin with a second site in Bangalore.
deep_cut_fact: His career started in physics, not e-commerce; he says he joined Razor in 2020 after his schoolmate Tushar Ahluwalia pitched him the idea.
notes: Now focused on GeneralMind rather than Razor. Appeared on the 'Behind the Click' podcast (E-commerce Germany, Sept 2026). Company emails are general inboxes (hello@/info@).

name: Shrestha Chowdhury
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Razor Group (Berlin); current status not confirmed
profile: Co-founder and CTO of Razor Group, a Berlin e-commerce aggregator founded in 2020 that buys and scales Amazon marketplace brands. Razor became a unicorn with a $125M Series B in November 2021. Chowdhury built its data platform for sourcing acquisitions.
interesting_fact: Chowdhury built Razor's 'M&A 2.0' platform, which screened about 1 million companies a week using thousands of data points to flag acquisition targets. Razor said this let it source 99% of its deal pipeline without brokers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Razor, Chowdhury and CEO Tushar Ahluwalia worked on Stalkbuylove, an Indian social-shopping site in the mold of Wanelo.
notes: Very low public profile. TechCrunch (2021) refers to Chowdhury as 'she'. I found no recent coverage, and Razor's leadership has changed since 2024, so confirm the current role before outreach. I found no published press email.

name: Tushar Ahluwalia
current_role: Co-founder and (at least until recently) CEO, Razor Group, Berlin
profile: German-raised entrepreneur of Indian heritage who co-founded Berlin-based Razor Group in 2020 to acquire and scale Amazon Marketplace merchants into multichannel consumer brands. Razor raised $400M in May 2021 and $125M in October 2021, passing a $1B valuation. He previously built e-commerce businesses in Asia and Europe after starting at Rocket Internet.
interesting_fact: Razor Group reached unicorn status within about 18 months of founding, after raising $400M (May 2021) and $125M (Oct 2021).
deep_cut_fact: After finishing a Masters in Management at London Business School in 2011 (bachelor's at EBS in Germany), he joined Rocket Internet, which sent him to India to build e-commerce businesses; he describes himself as from a third-generation Indian family raised in Germany.
notes: One aggregator (village.ai) suggests he left the Razor co-CEO role in Oct 2025 for a stealth company. Not confirmed; check before outreach. Has appeared on podcasts about Razor's ~300 acquisitions.

name: He Dongdong
current_role: Co-founder, Vice Chairman and General Manager/CEO, Rootcloud (树根互联 / 树根科技), Guangzhou
profile: He Dongdong (b. 1967; SJTU industrial-management engineering, CEIBS EMBA) spent 2003-2017 at construction-equipment giant SANY, rising to senior VP and head of process IT. In 2016 he launched SANY's spin-out Rootcloud, an industrial-internet (IIoT) platform connecting factory and machinery data; it filed for a STAR Market IPO in 2022 and in 2026 was on Hurun's Global Unicorn list for the sixth year running.
interesting_fact: Rootcloud grew out of SANY's own effort to connect its excavators and cranes worldwide and became one of China's flagship industrial-internet platforms, recognised as a Hurun global unicorn six years in a row (2026).
deep_cut_fact: At SANY he ran businesses abroad, serving as general manager of SANY India and chairman of SANY Germany before becoming SANY's CIO-style process-IT chief; he is also vice president of the Chinese Society of Vocational and Technical Education.
notes: Company now brands itself 树根科技 (Rootcloud Technology); still unlisted as of 2026. Frequent speaker on industrial internet/AI in manufacturing. No press email found (site lists only a partner@ address).

name: Andrew Reiter
current_role: Co-founder and former CTO of Shield AI (left 2022; remains an adviser). Contrary Research reports he moved to ThorCon US (molten-salt nuclear) in 2023; I could not confirm his title there.
profile: Andrew Reiter (Northwestern '10, Harvard MS robotics '12) is a perception and sensor-fusion engineer. He co-founded San Diego defense-autonomy company Shield AI in 2015 with Ryan and Brandon Tseng and was its first CTO; Shield AI makes the Hivemind AI pilot and the V-BAT drone. He left in fall 2022 to pursue decarbonization, and Contrary Research says he joined nuclear developer ThorCon US in 2023.
interesting_fact: Shield AI was born when ex-Navy SEAL Brandon Tseng and his brother Ryan flew from San Diego to Boston to meet him at Draper. 'After eight hours, we had the loose strings of Shield AI in place,' Reiter recalled. The company grew from three people in a garage to more than 500 staff.
deep_cut_fact: He started at Northwestern as a chemical engineering major, but robotics hooked him when he won the 2009 McCormick Autonomous Robot Design Competition with classmates Andrew Dai and Eric West. At Draper he led teams building a handheld 3D-scanning system and a fully autonomous exploration quadrotor.
notes: Strong fit for an energy podcast: in 2023 he said his next move targeted decarbonization via nuclear energy or energy storage ('The climate emergency waits for no one'). He has no published email or verified social handle; try LinkedIn or Northwestern Engineering alumni channels. Shield AI's press office is not a good route since he left.

name: Brandon Tseng
current_role: Co-founder and President, Shield AI
profile: Former Navy SEAL officer and surface warfare officer (7 years; deployed to Afghanistan and the Pacific) who co-founded Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Ryan Tseng and Andrew Reiter. Shield AI builds the Hivemind AI-pilot software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft and (via Aechelon) simulation tech; it was valued at ~$12.7B in 2026 and is a leading US defense-autonomy startup.
interesting_fact: His thesis is that the AI pilot matters more than the airframe; in 2026 he said he now expects autonomous defense systems to be ubiquitous by 2040-45, not his original 2035 forecast, because procurement moved slower than he expected.
deep_cut_fact: In August 2015 he and his co-founders pitched 30 Silicon Valley investors and all said no; the next year they met 25 more and two said yes. a16z's Peter Levine, a board member, likened defense tech then to Uber or Airbnb: 'ideas that look dumb until they don't.'
notes: Frequent podcast/op-ed guest (Masters of Scale, War on the Rocks), so receptive to media. AI/autonomy plus defense angle; adjacent rather than core to energy/data centers. Shield AI's own site blocked automated fetch; personal social handles not verified.

name: Ryan Tseng
current_role: Co-founder & President (strategic growth), Shield AI; CEO 2015-May 2025
profile: Ryan Tseng co-founded San Diego-based Shield AI in 2015 with his brother Brandon (an ex-Navy SEAL) and Andrew Reiter to build AI pilots for military aircraft and drones (Hivemind software, V-BAT drone). He was CEO until former Splunk chief Gary Steele took over in May 2025; Ryan now focuses on senior government and industry engagement as president. Shield AI raised a $1.5bn Series G at a $12.7bn valuation in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Shield AI's founding idea came from Brandon Tseng's SEAL deployments: small autonomous drones that could clear buildings ahead of troops; it grew into Hivemind, an AI pilot for aircraft from quadcopters to F-16s.
deep_cut_fact: Before defense tech he was a wireless-power entrepreneur: as founder/CEO/CTO of WiPower he developed wireless charging technology and sold the company to Qualcomm in 2010. He studied electrical engineering at the University of Florida and earned an MBA at MIT.
notes: Leadership change confirmed by Shield AI release (12 Mar 2025). Titles vary (President / President & Chief Strategy Officer / President, Strategic Growth). Defense-AI focus rather than data centers. Frequent speaker (CSIS, Sedona Forum, AIAA), so open to media; route via Shield AI communications (shield.ai blocked from this session, so no press email captured).

name: David Durrleman
current_role: Co-founder, Shift Technology (Paris); former CTO (current title unconfirmed)
profile: Co-founded Shift Technology in Paris in 2014 with Jeremy Jawish and Eric Sibony. Shift sells AI for insurance (claims-fraud detection, claims automation) and became a $1B+ unicorn in 2021. As CTO he built a 100+ engineer tech organisation. Marc Jones has been CTO since Oct 2022, and Durrleman remains a co-founder.
interesting_fact: Shift Technology is one of France's AI unicorns, selling AI for insurance fraud detection and claims decisions to insurers worldwide.
notes: Low public profile; his pre-Shift background and education could not be verified. Shift lists marketing@ as its 'Press & Media' contact. CEO Jeremy Jawish is the company's main spokesperson.

name: Eric Sibony
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Science Officer, Shift Technology (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique-trained mathematician who co-founded Shift Technology in 2013 with Jeremy Jawish and David Durrleman. Shift sells AI for insurance claims fraud detection, underwriting and claims automation; it became a unicorn in 2021 with a $220M Series D led by Advent. He leads its data science and now its agentic-AI push for insurers.
interesting_fact: Shift Technology raised $220M in May 2021 at a $1B+ valuation, becoming one of France's insurtech unicorns; its AI scores insurance claims for fraud for insurers worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: While building Shift as CSO, he completed a PhD at Telecom ParisTech (2016) titled 'Multi-resolution analysis of ranking data', on machine learning over permutations and rankings, co-authoring work on ranking aggregation with Stephan Clemencon.
notes: marketing@shift-technology.com is listed under 'Press & Media' on Shift's contact page. He appears in Shift content ('Four questions with Eric Sibony') and trade press commentary on AI in insurance. Less direct energy/data-center fit; AI/entrepreneurship angle.

name: Jeremy Jawish
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shift Technology (Paris)
profile: Polytechnique-trained French entrepreneur who co-founded Shift Technology in 2014 with Eric Sibony and David Durrleman.
