Shift sells AI for insurers, starting with fraud detection and now claims and underwriting decision automation and AI agents. It became a unicorn after a $220m Series D (2021) and earns about half its revenue in the US.
interesting_fact: Shift says its fraud-detection AI saves insurers over EUR 5bn a year. By late 2021 it had analysed nearly two billion claims for 100+ insurers in 25 countries.
deep_cut_fact: He met cofounder Eric Sibony at Ecole Polytechnique, and their first calling was 'more mathematical'. The idea for Shift came during his internship at a big insurer, where experts reviewed claims by hand despite all the maths that could be applied. He says he became an entrepreneur mainly 'to work with Eric on something that was ours.'

public_contacts.value: Safia Danger, Public Relations Europe (in-house): safia.danger@shift-technology.com

notes: An approachable, media-friendly French Tech CEO who writes bylines for American Banker and similar outlets. He is an AI-applications person rather than energy or data-center. The PR contact is Shift's in-house European PR lead, as named on its press releases.

name: Cui Dong
current_role: Founder, chairman & CEO of SJ Semiconductor (盛合晶微, formerly SMIC-Changdian / 中芯长电), Jiangyin
profile: Born 1971, Cui Dong worked in government and then as a senior executive at Hua Hong and SMIC, rising to SMIC executive VP for investment and strategy. In 2014 he led the founding of SMIC-Changdian, a JV incubated by SMIC and JCET, which became SJSemi - a leader in bumping, wafer-level and 2.5D/3D advanced packaging for AI chips. SJSemi has cleared review for a STAR Market IPO.
interesting_fact: SJSemi has no controlling shareholder (top holder under 11%), but Cui controls the votes of all 11 employee shareholding platforms; revenue grew from about RMB1.6bn to RMB6.5bn on AI-chip packaging demand, fastest among the global top-10 packaging/test firms.
deep_cut_fact: Before entering the chip industry he worked as a secretary in the General Office of China's Ministry of Electronics Industry, which commentators credit for his feel for national industrial policy.
notes: Strong AI/data-center angle (advanced packaging for AI accelerators; heavy customer concentration in a large domestic AI-chip client). Media differ on his title (chairman vs CEO); profile details are from media reports, not the prospectus.

name: Abraham Bachrach
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Skydio (autonomous drones, San Mateo, CA)
profile: Abe Bachrach (BS UC Berkeley; MS/PhD MIT) led MIT's autonomous-flight research from 2007 in Nick Roy's Robust Robotics Group, then joined Google's Project Wing drone effort. In 2014 he co-founded Skydio with Adam Bry and Matt Donahoe; it builds AI-driven autonomous drones and docks for enterprise, utilities/infrastructure inspection, public safety and defense.
interesting_fact: Skydio grew out of MIT research on drones that fly themselves without GPS; Bachrach and Bry built a fixed-wing drone with a laser rangefinder that autonomously navigated around a parking lot.
deep_cut_fact: As an MIT grad student he led the Robust Robotics Group team whose GPS-denied quadrotor won the 2009 International Aerial Robotics Competition: it entered an unknown building through a window, explored without GPS and found a target. It was the first time a new IARC mission was solved in its first year.
notes: Technical founder with a low media profile (CEO Adam Bry is the usual spokesperson). Energy angle: Skydio drones and docks are used for utility and energy-infrastructure inspection. Press route: press@skydio.com.

name: Adam Bry
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Skydio (largest US drone maker, San Mateo, CA)
profile: MIT CSAIL roboticist (SM '12) who helped lead research on autonomous high-speed flight, then co-founded Google X's Project Wing delivery-drone effort. Co-founded Skydio in 2014; it pivoted from consumer selfie drones to autonomous drones and docks for public safety, infrastructure inspection and defence, has delivered over 60,000 drones to 3,800+ organisations, and raised at a ~$4.4B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: Skydio is the largest drone manufacturer in the US, with more than 60,000 autonomous drones flying thousands of daily missions in public safety, critical-infrastructure inspection and national security.
deep_cut_fact: He started building things that fly at age five and had won two US national championships in radio-controlled airplane aerobatics by 18. At MIT he co-captained the cycling team and led it to a 2012 national title.
notes: Experienced public speaker (congressional testimony, MIT fireside chats, FAA Drone Advisory Committee). Energy angle: drones for grid and utility infrastructure inspection. Best route is press@skydio.com.

name: Matt Donahoe
current_role: Cofounder, Skydio (autonomous drones), San Mateo, CA - current exec title not confirmed
profile: Matt Donahoe (MIT Media Lab SM '11) cofounded Skydio in 2014 with MIT roboticists Adam Bry and Abe Bachrach. Skydio began with the R1 'selfie drone' (13 cameras, full autonomy) and became the largest US drone maker, selling to the military, police and utilities; it raised a Series F at a $4.4B valuation in 2026 and plans $3.5B of US manufacturing.
interesting_fact: Skydio's first product, the 2018 R1 'selfie drone', used 13 cameras and deep neural networks to follow and film a person while dodging obstacles with no pilot - which CEO Adam Bry likened to a driverless car with level-four autonomy.
deep_cut_fact: For Skydio's first year the three cofounders worked out of Abe Bachrach's dad's basement, getting free rent in exchange for yard work; their first prototype was a quadcopter with a media-center PC and USB camera held together with duct tape - yet it won a $3M seed round.
notes: Lowest-profile of the three cofounders (CEO Adam Bry is the public face). Third-party sites give conflicting titles (COO / CRO / chief experience officer); verify before addressing him. Skydio is on China's sanctions list (relevant to supply chain stories, not to outreach).

name: Li Yang
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Guangzhou Smarter Microelectronics (Smarter Micro / 慧智微, SSE STAR: 688512)
profile: Li Yang (b. ~1974) is an RF engineer who spent years in the US chip industry before founding Smarter Micro in Guangzhou in November 2011. The company designs RF front-end modules (power amplifiers etc.) for 4G/5G phones and IoT using a reconfigurable RF front-end architecture, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2023; he holds ~9.5% directly.
interesting_fact: Smarter Micro bet on a 'reconfigurable' RF front-end architecture - one adaptable PA design covering many frequency bands - as China's answer to the Skyworks/Qorvo-dominated discrete-module approach.
deep_cut_fact: Before returning to China he worked in US RF/semiconductor firms: Principal Engineer at Millennial Net (2004-06), Staff Engineer at Peregrine Semiconductor (2006-08) and Principal Engineer at Skyworks (2008-11), founding Smarter Micro three months after leaving Skyworks.
notes: Common name - identity confirmed via Smarter Micro annual report. Fit is semiconductors (RF for handsets), not data-center power directly.

name: Mike Pittaro
current_role: SnapLogic co-founder; last publicly listed as Distinguished Engineer, Cloud and Big Data Solutions, Dell EMC (current role unverified)
profile: Mike (Michael) Pittaro co-founded SnapLogic in 2006 with Informatica co-founder Gaurav Dhillon, serving as chief community officer while it ran as an open-source data-integration project; SnapLogic later became an iPaaS unicorn. He came from Informatica (customer services/strategic support) and later worked as a principal engineer at La Honda Research Center and a distinguished engineer at Dell EMC.
interesting_fact: SnapLogic launched in 2007 as open-source data-integration software under a GPL-style licence, with Pittaro as chief community officer building the developer community, long before it became a commercial AI-integration platform.
deep_cut_fact: In 2008 he was an active member of BayPIGgies, the San Francisco Bay Area Python users' group, answering members' data-pipeline questions and signing off as 'Co-Founder, Snaplogic, Inc.'; SnapLogic's early engine was built in Python.
notes: Founder status per Golden wiki, MarketScreener and a 2009 Sramana Mitra profile; current role from Crunchbase (may be outdated). Low public profile; no current published contact found. Old snaplogic.org address in 2008 list posts is obsolete and should not be used. He left SnapLogic around 2010, so his stake in the unicorn is probably small.

name: Alexander Ratner
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Snorkel AI (Redwood City/SF); Affiliate Assistant Professor of Computer Science, University of Washington
profile: Stanford CS PhD (advisor Christopher Re) who started and led the open-source Snorkel project for programmatic data labelling, then spun it out as Snorkel AI in 2019. The unicorn now focuses on expert data, evaluations and benchmarks for frontier AI labs and enterprises. He is also affiliate faculty at the University of Washington.
interesting_fact: Snorkel grew from his 2016 NeurIPS paper 'Data Programming: Creating Large Training Sets, Quickly', which showed models could be trained without hand-labelled data by writing noisy 'labeling functions' and modelling their accuracies - the weak-supervision idea behind the company.
deep_cut_fact: As a PhD student he co-authored AMELIE, a Stanford tool that speeds diagnosis of patients with rare Mendelian genetic diseases by mining the primary medical literature directly (with Gill Bejerano's lab).

public_contacts.value: ajratner at gmail.com (self-published on his academic homepage, last updated ~2020)

notes: Accessible, academically minded founder who speaks often at AI events (Snorkel hosts its own Frontier Data Summit). For a business/podcast request, media@snorkel.ai is the most appropriate route; the gmail address is from his older academic page.

name: Braden Hancock
current_role: Research Partner, Laude Ventures and Laude Institute (since Jul 2025); co-founder and advisor, Snorkel AI
profile: BYU mechanical-engineering valedictorian turned Stanford CS PhD (under Chris Ré) who co-founded Snorkel AI from Stanford weak-supervision research; it reached a $1.3B valuation (Series D, May 2025). He then founded Meta's GenAI Evaluations org for Llama (2024-25), and since mid-2025 is a Research Partner at Laude.
interesting_fact: At Meta he founded the centralized evaluation org responsible for all eval work on Llama 3, 3.1 and 3.2, the most-downloaded open LLM family.
deep_cut_fact: Before AI he was a mechanical engineer: in summer 2011 he worked in the Air Force Research Laboratory's Turbine Engine Division on evolutionary algorithms for turbine-engine simulation, and he graduated BYU (2015) as valedictorian.
notes: Very accessible: maintains a personal site, posts on X/LinkedIn and does podcasts (e.g. The SaaS CFO, Aug 2025; Practical AI #117). Good guest for AI data/evals and research-to-startup topics. No published email; X or LinkedIn is the best route.

name: Chris Re
current_role: Professor of Computer Science, Stanford (Stanford AI Lab / Hazy Research); co-founder of Together AI
profile: Christopher Re is a Stanford CS professor and MacArthur Fellow whose machine-learning systems research has spun out multiple companies: Lattice (DeepDive) and Inductiv (HoloClean), both acquired by Apple, plus Snorkel AI, SambaNova Systems and Together AI, the AI-cloud/open-model infrastructure company co-founded in 2022. His lab now focuses on AI kernels (ThunderKittens) and AI efficiency.
interesting_fact: He has co-founded companies straight out of his research, including SambaNova and Snorkel, and his lab says over a dozen of its members have gone on to become professors; his students also run the MLSys podcast.
deep_cut_fact: In Nov 2025 he co-authored 'Intelligence Per Watt' with John Hennessy, arguing that, as with mainframes to PCs, efficiency gains could shift AI inference from power-constrained data centers to local devices; they found local LMs could answer 88.7% of single-turn chat and reasoning queries.
notes: Excellent fit for a data-center/energy podcast given his 'intelligence per watt' work. The email is his Stanford work address, published on his own homepage. The X account is the lab's (Hazy Research), not personal.

name: Henry Ehrenberg
current_role: Co-founder, Snorkel AI (technical strategy and engineering)
profile: Yale applied-math grad with a Stanford MS who was a core member of the Snorkel project in the Stanford AI Lab, then tech lead of Facebook Applied AI's representation-learning team. He co-founded Snorkel AI (spun out 2019 with Alex Ratner, Chris Ré and others), which sells programmatic data-labeling and expert-data tooling for enterprise and frontier AI.
interesting_fact: Snorkel's core idea, 'programmatic labeling' or weak supervision, lets teams write labeling functions instead of hand-labeling data; it began as an open-source Stanford research library he helped build.
deep_cut_fact: He is a co-author of the original 2017 paper 'Snorkel: Rapid Training Data Creation with Weak Supervision' and of 'Learning to Compose Domain-Specific Transformations for Data Augmentation' (2017), the research that seeded the company.
notes: Lower profile than CEO Alex Ratner but does public talks (theCUBE + NYSE Wired 'Robotics & AI Infrastructure Leaders' 2025: https://snorkel.ai/press/henry-kiss-ehrenberg-snorkel-ai-robotics-ai-infrastructure-leaders/). Snorkel press list mentions a 2026 RIF - avoid as an angle.

name: Paroma Varma
current_role: Co-founder and Head of Research, Snorkel AI
profile: Paroma Varma earned an EE PhD at Stanford, where her weak-supervision research in the Stanford AI Lab became Snorkel, spun out as Snorkel AI (valued ~ $1bn). Snorkel has pivoted toward expert-curated datasets, benchmarks and evaluation for frontier AI labs, and she leads its research (e.g. 2026 work on rubric-based LLM evaluation).
interesting_fact: Snorkel started as a Stanford AI Lab research project in 2015 to give ML a 'higher-level interface' through training data; she describes Snorkel Flow as the first data-centric platform built on programmatic labelling.
deep_cut_fact: Her first exposure to machine learning was as a UC Berkeley undergrad working in a neuroscience lab, and during her PhD she collaborated with radiologists, applying weak supervision to medical imaging.
notes: Researcher-founder; accessible via Snorkel media. Some third-party profiles list her as Head of Solutions, but Snorkel's own author page says Head of Research.

name: Idit Levine
current_role: Founder and CEO, Solo.io (cloud-native application networking / agentic AI infrastructure)
profile: Israeli-born engineer who held roles at Verizon, CloudSwitch, DynamicOps and VMware before serving as CTO of EMC's Cloud Management Division (2014-17). She left in 2017 to found Solo.io, which built the Gloo API gateway and Istio/Ambient-mesh products, raised a $135m Series C at a $1bn+ valuation, and now ships agentic-AI infrastructure such as kagent and agentgateway.
interesting_fact: Before tech she played professional basketball in Israel for about seven years (Elitzur Holon), juggling up to six hours of practice a day with mandatory military service.
deep_cut_fact: She left Dell EMC in 2017 to start a company without yet knowing what she would build; she credits basketball for her style: 'Basketball is a small team, no politics whatsoever, that's going to the same goal.'
notes: Very podcast-friendly (InfoQ, The New Stack, Spot.io 'Cloud Control' appearances). Agentic-AI/cloud infra angle fits data-center/AI theme. Some 2026 releases also list media@solo.io via a third-party republisher - unverified.

name: Brandon Ogle
current_role: Co-founder of Standard AI (formerly Standard Cognition), San Francisco; listed as Head of Machine Learning
profile: Brandon Ogle is one of seven co-founders of Standard AI (Standard Cognition), a Y Combinator company founded in 2017 to build camera-based, cashierless checkout for retailers using computer vision, which reached a ~$1-2B valuation. He is listed as the company's machine-learning lead. Standard AI later pivoted toward retail computer-vision analytics.
interesting_fact: Standard's system tracked shoppers with overhead cameras that identify people by shape and movement rather than facial recognition, pitching itself as a privacy-friendlier rival to Amazon Go.
notes: Very low public profile: role known only from aggregator profiles (MarketScreener: Head of Machine Learning since 2017). Current status at the company unverified. No published personal or press email found.

name: Daniel Fischetti
current_role: Believed to be at DoorDash (joined March 2024 with ex-Standard AI CEO Jordan Fisher to work on AI voice ordering); co-founder of Standard AI
profile: Co-founder and former Director of Research of Standard AI (Standard Cognition), the San Francisco computer-vision startup that came out of Y Combinator's Summer 2017 batch to build camera-based autonomous checkout for retailers and reached a ~$1B+ valuation. In March 2024 he, Jordan Fisher and co-founder Brandon Ogle joined DoorDash with part of Standard's engineering team to build an AI phone-ordering product for restaurants.
interesting_fact: Standard Cognition (YC S17) set out to let shoppers 'grab what they want' and walk out without a cashier, using ceiling cameras and machine learning rather than shelf sensors - a rival approach to Amazon Go.
notes: Low public profile; technical co-founder rather than public face (Jordan Fisher was CEO). Move to DoorDash reported by Bloomberg/PYMNTS (https://www.pymnts.com/artificial-intelligence-2/2024/report-doordash-boosts-voice-ai-with-standard-ai-hires/); current role after 2024 not confirmed. No published contacts found.

name: David Valdman
current_role: Co-founder of Standard AI (formerly Standard Cognition); listed by Y Combinator among 'Former Founders' - current role not confirmed (some profiles say board member)
profile: David Valdman (PhD) co-founded San Francisco-based Standard Cognition in 2017 (Y Combinator S17) with Jordan Fisher, Michael Suswal, John Novak and others to build camera-based, cashierless 'autonomous checkout' for retail; it reached unicorn status (~$1B+; Hurun lists $2B) and later rebranded as Standard AI, pivoting toward AI/edge vision analytics for stores.
interesting_fact: Standard Cognition was part of Y Combinator's Summer 2017 batch and pitched a store where shoppers simply grab items and walk out, with ceiling cameras and computer vision replacing cashiers - a direct challenger to Amazon Go.
notes: YC now lists him as a former founder; unclear what he is doing now (one profile mentions a sabbatical). Earlier roles reported as Chief Architect at Famo.us and graphics lead at Mapzen, but only in low-quality profiles, so not used as a deep-cut fact. X/LinkedIn via YC founder page are the best routes.

name: John Novak
current_role: Co-founder and former Head of Hardware Engineering, Standard AI (formerly Standard Cognition); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: John Novak is one of the co-founders of Standard AI (Standard Cognition), the San Francisco computer-vision company founded in 2017 (YC Summer 2017) that builds camera-based autonomous checkout and retail analytics. He led hardware engineering; Standard reached a reported ~$1B+ valuation around 2019-2021. Y Combinator now lists him among its former founders.
interesting_fact: Standard AI was one of the first startups to retrofit existing stores with ceiling-camera, AI-only checkout (no shelf sensors), positioning itself as an alternative to Amazon Go.
deep_cut_fact: He came to retail AI from physics: he earned a PhD in nuclear physics from Michigan State University in 2013 before co-founding Standard Cognition.
notes: Common name; identity anchored via YC's Standard Cognition page. Low public profile; no published personal contact found. Hurun counts him as a unicorn founder; his personal wealth is uncertain. A directory mentions a 2025 acquisition of Standard AI, which I did not verify.

name: Jordan Fisher
current_role: Co-founder and chairman of Standard AI (CEO until Mar 2024); reportedly leads an AI alignment research team at Anthropic (per YC podcast listing, 2025)
profile: Co-founded Standard Cognition (Standard AI) via Y Combinator in 2017 to build camera-based autonomous checkout; it raised $260M+ and hit ~$1B valuation in 2021. notes: Co-founder Samir Vasavada is the more public face of Vise. No published press email found. Mehrotra's title has varied (CTO in 2019, later CIO, Co-CEO in 2025).

name: Samir Vasavada
current_role: Co-founder and Co-Head of Vise (New York)
profile: Co-founded Vise in 2016 with Runik Mehrotra while both were teenagers; Vise is an SEC-registered AI investment platform that builds, manages and explains personalised portfolios (direct indexing, models, tax-loss harvesting) for financial advisers. It reached a $1B valuation in 2021; Vasavada now co-heads the company from NYC.
interesting_fact: Flatiron Health founders Nat Turner and Zach Weinberg wrote Vise's first $100K check, and Founders Fund co-led its $2M seed.
deep_cut_fact: Vise's origin story: when Runik went to UPenn, Samir moved onto his dorm floor and refused to leave until Runik dropped out; Runik's parents agreed only if they first raised $1M - which they did.
notes: Team page lists him as 'Co-Head of Vise' alongside co-founder Runik Mehrotra. No published press email found; vise.com/press page is the media entry point.

name: John Schwarz
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman (former CEO), Visier Inc.
profile: Canadian-born software veteran (b. 1950) who spent ~25 years at IBM, was president/COO of Symantec, then CEO of Business Objects, which he sold to SAP in 2008, joining SAP's executive board. In 2010 he co-founded people-analytics company Visier in Vancouver with Ryan Wong and his sons Jan and Brett. Has sat on boards including Synopsys and Teradata.
interesting_fact: As CEO of Business Objects he doubled revenue to over $1.5B, made seven acquisitions and negotiated its sale to SAP.
deep_cut_fact: He holds both a BA in political science and a BSc in computer science from the University of Manitoba, plus an executive MBA from the University of Toronto; Dalhousie gave him an honorary law doctorate in 2004.
notes: Ryan Wong is now Visier CEO; Schwarz's title is variously given as chairman/founder. Visier co-founded with his sons - do not contact family.

name: Ryan Wong
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Visier (Vancouver)
profile: Vancouver-based business-intelligence veteran who co-founded Visier (2010), the people-analytics / 'Workforce AI' software company valued at $1B+. Before Visier he spent 20+ years in BI at Crystal Decisions, Business Objects and SAP, ending as VP Engineering for SAP BusinessObjects. Visier now pitches AI talent agents built on enterprise workforce data.
interesting_fact: Visier's leadership grew out of the Crystal Reports lineage: Wong rode Crystal Decisions through its acquisition by Business Objects and then SAP, before co-founding Visier to apply analytics to HR/workforce data.
deep_cut_fact: Wong was the original author and Chief Software Architect of the Crystal Enterprise platform, the server product behind Crystal Reports' enterprise reporting business.
notes: Technical founder; data/AI angle fits the podcast. Common name - target Visier's Ryan Wong (Vancouver).

name: Alexander Zosel
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (eVTOL air-taxi pioneer, Bruchsal); current role unconfirmed after Volocopter's 2025 acquisition by Diamond Aircraft
profile: German serial entrepreneur (civil-engineering studies) who co-founded e-volo/Volocopter in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Stephan Wolf, pioneering electric multicopter air taxis and serving in roles including managing director and technical/marketing lead. Volocopter raised hundreds of millions, then filed for insolvency in Dec 2024; its assets were bought by Wanfeng's Diamond Aircraft in March 2025.
interesting_fact: On 30 March 2016 Zosel personally piloted the first manned flight of the 18-rotor Volocopter VC200, saying: 'It is definitely a sublime feeling to lift off, fly the first few meters.'
deep_cut_fact: In 1981, aged 15, he and friends built one of Germany's first skateboard halfpipes; he developed his first patent while still a civil-engineering student.
notes: Current activities after the Volocopter insolvency/Diamond takeover are undocumented; avoid dwelling on the insolvency. Has given interviews (tech.eu, dronebelow, re:publica 2018 speaker). No published personal or office contact found.

name: Stephan Wolf
current_role: Co-founder of Volocopter (Bruchsal, Germany); current role not publicly documented
profile: German industrial-automation software specialist who co-founded Volocopter (originally e-volo) in Karlsruhe in 2011 with Alexander Zosel and Thomas Senkel. Volocopter pioneered electric multicopter air taxis and reached a ~$2B valuation, but filed for insolvency in December 2024 and was acquired in 2025 by Diamond Aircraft (owned by China's Wanfeng).
interesting_fact: Volocopter's first prototype, the VC1, was essentially a seat on a yoga ball with 16 electric rotors; its 90-second flight on 21 Oct 2011 is credited as the world's first crewed all-electric multicopter flight.
deep_cut_fact: The Volocopter idea was Wolf's: in 2010, after being struck by how stable a small consumer quadcopter was, he did his own calculations on scaling it up to carry people and then pitched the project to his childhood friend Alex Zosel, a hobby pilot and paragliding instructor.
notes: Very low public profile; no current role, personal site or social accounts found. Alive status not confirmed by any recent source (no reports of death). Volocopter no longer independent, so the company press office is not a reliable route to him.

name: Wang Anquan
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Webull Corporation (Nasdaq: BULL)
profile: Chinese software engineer (Hunan University CS) who spent 2006-2012 at Alibaba's finance arm, then worked at Hengfeng Bank and as GM of Xiaomi Finance before founding Fumi Technology in 2016, parent of the Webull commission-free trading app. Webull listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in April 2025; he controls the majority of its voting power.
interesting_fact: Xiaomi, where he ran the finance business in 2015-16, was one of Fumi/Webull's early investors.
deep_cut_fact: Webull's first MVP was built in 2013 while he was still at Alibaba: he and an Ali colleague developed it as a market-intelligence tool, years before it became a brokerage.
notes: Very low Western media profile; Webull's US face is Anthony Denier. Best route is Webull IR/communications. Ownership/voting figures should be checked against 20-F.

name: Chris Van Pelt
current_role: Co-founder (and CIO / CISO-type roles), Weights & Biases, now part of CoreWeave
profile: Chris Van Pelt co-founded CrowdFlower (later Figure Eight, sold to Appen for $300m in 2019) with Lukas Biewald, then Weights & Biases in 2017 with Biewald and Shawn Lewis. W&B's experiment-tracking platform is used by OpenAI, NVIDIA and others; CoreWeave acquired it for about $1.7B in 2025, and he remains as co-founder.
interesting_fact: Weights & Biases became the standard experiment-tracking tool at frontier AI labs, and its 2025 sale to GPU cloud provider CoreWeave tied ML developer tooling directly to data-centre compute.
deep_cut_fact: He built OpenUI as a side project: an open-source tool that lets you describe a UI in plain English and watch it render live, then convert it to React, Svelte or Web Components. Its README jokingly calls it 'like v0 but open source and not as polished', and it passed about 20k GitHub stars.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearances: Learning from Machine Learning #9 (2024), ThursdAI (May 2024), Software Engineering Daily (2023)

notes: Approachable, engineer-minded founder who does podcasts often; X @vanpelt is the most direct public channel. He says: 'My title is co-founder really at the end of the day.' Since the acquisition, press for W&B goes through CoreWeave (press@coreweave.com). Strong data-centre/AI angle.

name: Lukas Biewald
current_role: SVP of AI Initiatives at CoreWeave and General Manager/co-founder of Weights & Biases (acquired by CoreWeave, May 2025); Xometry board member
profile: Two-time AI founder. After Stanford and Yahoo search, he co-founded data-labeling firm CrowdFlower in 2007 (later Figure Eight, sold to Appen in 2019). In 2017 he co-founded ML experiment-tracking platform Weights & Biases. CoreWeave acquired W&B in 2025, and he now leads AI initiatives at the GPU cloud.
interesting_fact: His companies tackled two successive bottlenecks of practical ML: getting labelled training data (CrowdFlower/Figure Eight) and making model development reproducible (W&B). W&B now sits inside one of the largest AI data-center operators, CoreWeave.
deep_cut_fact: W&B's first product began as an experiment-tracking tool built to help train models at OpenAI. Biewald had gone back to hands-on deep learning and spent time at OpenAI before starting the company.
notes: Very accessible: he hosts his own AI interview podcast, Gradient Dissent, so a podcast-swap or guest invite is a natural angle. Now at CoreWeave, which is directly relevant to a data-center podcast. No personal email published; reach him via W&B/CoreWeave or the podcast.

name: Shawn Lewis
current_role: Co-founder (CTO / distinguished engineer), Weights & Biases, now part of CoreWeave
profile: Shawn Lewis, a former Google engineer, co-founded Weights & Biases in 2017 with Lukas Biewald and Chris Van Pelt to build developer tools for machine learning, starting with experiment tracking used at OpenAI. W&B grew into a leading MLOps platform and was acquired by AI cloud provider CoreWeave (deal closed May 2025, reportedly ~$1.7B); he remains with the company.
interesting_fact: W&B's first product was an experiment-tracking tool developed to help build models at OpenAI; it grew into an end-to-end platform used by millions of ML practitioners and now sits inside CoreWeave's AI cloud.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in 2006 on Google's platforms team, which built Google's data-center infrastructure and the software that ran it, and he built internal tools to let colleagues analyze that data (Gradient Dissent podcast).
notes: Great data-center angle (Google platforms team -> CoreWeave AI cloud). Lower public profile than CEO Lukas Biewald; exact current title varies by source (CTO vs distinguished engineer). Best route likely via CoreWeave/W&B press; no personal channels verified.

name: Ali Javid
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Wrapbook
profile: Co-founder and CEO of Wrapbook (founded March 2018), a payroll, accounting and AP platform for film, TV and commercial productions that hit a ~$1B valuation after a $100M Series B in Nov 2021. He is now repositioning it as an AI platform that reads invoices, updates the general ledger and answers finance questions in plain English. Previously VP of Business Development at Body Labs (acquired by Amazon in 2017).
interesting_fact: The company is named after the physical binder of onboarding, payroll documents and receipts that gets assembled at the end of every production - the 'wrap book' - which Wrapbook set out to replace.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he was VP of Business Development at Body Labs, a 3D body-modelling AI startup bought by Amazon in 2017; he holds a BBA from the University of Washington and an MBA from NYU Stern.
notes: Speaker at 2026 AICP Week (commercial production industry). Co-founders: Naysawn Naji, Hesham El-Nahhas, Cameron Woodward. No published press email found.

name: Cameron Woodward
current_role: Co-founder (and CMO per 2022 trade press) of Wrapbook, the production payroll/finance platform for film and TV; current title not confirmed
profile: Former owner of the boutique commercial production house Sprinkle Lab who experienced production-payroll pain first-hand, then co-founded Wrapbook in 2018 with CEO Ali Javid, Hesham El-Nahhas and Naysawn Naji. Wrapbook, backed by investors including Jeffrey Katzenberg's WndrCo, handles payroll, insurance and accounting for productions and reached a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: He described Wrapbook as 'built as a tech company that offers a payroll service rather than a payroll service' with software bolted on, with 100+ features for crews and productions.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he ran the boutique commercial production house Sprinkle Lab, where he learned the 'prickly problems' of paying crews that inspired the company.
notes: Ali Javid is Wrapbook's CEO; Woodward is lower-profile. A third-party profile (standout.work) says he directed the KONY2012 marketing campaign - unverified, use cautiously. No published press email; LinkedIn likely best route.

name: Hesham El Nahhas
current_role: Co-founder, Wrapbook (listed as Co-Founder & Chief People Officer as of the 2021 Series B; current title unconfirmed)
profile: Hesham El-Nahhas is one of four co-founders (with Ali Javid, Cameron Woodward and Naysawn Naji) of Wrapbook, founded in 2018 to digitise payroll, onboarding and insurance for film, TV and commercial productions. Wrapbook raised a $27M Series A led by a16z and a $100M Series B led by Tiger Global in Nov 2021 at a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Wrapbook's backers include Hollywood figures Jeffrey Katzenberg (WndrCo) and CAA co-founder Michael Ovitz; a16z said at its Series A the company was growing revenue about 7x year-over-year.
notes: Spelled El-Nahhas in company materials. Very low individual public profile; CEO Ali Javid is the company's public face. Wrapbook press center (https://www.wrapbook.com/press) lists no press email.

name: Naysawn Naji
current_role: Co-founder and former CPO of Wrapbook (left 2022); reportedly founded Buildpal, a scheduling tool for general contractors
profile: Product-focused fintech founder who co-founded Wrapbook in 2018 with Hesham El-Nahhas, Ali Javid (CEO) and Cameron Woodward. Wrapbook, a payroll and onboarding platform for film/TV/commercial productions, raised a $100M Series B at a $1B valuation in 2021 (Tiger Global, a16z). Naji left in 2022 and moved on to construction software (Buildpal).
interesting_fact: The Wrapbook idea started at a New York tech open-mic, where an actor demoed an app she had built to help actors book gigs; he was unimpressed until he learned it had 4,000 paying users, convincing him media production was ripe for better software.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wrapbook he was co-founder and CPO of Arcus, a Latin America-focused bill-payment API, where he and future co-founder Hesham El-Nahhas had lunch together 'every day for four years'; one early Wrapbook check came blind from a friend of his at Google.
notes: Low public profile; no published contact found. Buildpal role comes from Contrary Research (2024) and could not be independently confirmed. Wrapbook's later 2024 round was at $750M.

name: Bo Chen
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Xendit (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure)
profile: UC Berkeley EECS graduate (2014) who briefly worked at Brandcast and Ripple before co-founding Xendit in 2015 with fellow Berkeley alum Moses Lo (plus Tessa Wijaya and Juan Gonzalez). Xendit builds payment rails across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and was valued at ~$3B after its 2022 Series D.
interesting_fact: Xendit was the first Indonesian tech startup accepted into Y Combinator (S15 batch) and the first B2B payments company in Indonesia to reach unicorn status; Chen founded it at 23.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated early from Berkeley to get into startups faster, and his official festival bio notes he likes creating original rap performances for Xendit company offsites; he spoke at Singapore FinTech Festival 2023 on 'Become a Cockroach: Survive to Thrive.'
notes: CEO Moses Lo is the main public face. Xendit press releases list PR staff contacts (e.g., Ami Windarti, PR & Communications; a 2022 Series D release listed ami@xendit.co) - not independently re-verified, check newest release on xendit.co newsroom.

name: Juan Gonzalez
current_role: Co-founder, Xendit (listed by Y Combinator as Founder/Principal Software Engineer)
profile: Software engineer who co-founded Jakarta-based payments infrastructure company Xendit in 2015 with Moses Lo, Tessa Wijaya and Bo Chen; the company went through Y Combinator (Summer 2015). Xendit started as a consumer fintech app before pivoting to payment APIs for businesses across Southeast Asia, reaching unicorn status in 2021.
interesting_fact: Xendit was part of Y Combinator's Summer 2015 batch and became a unicorn in 2021 after a $150M round led by Tiger Global.
deep_cut_fact: Xendit was originally launched in 2015 as a consumer-focused fintech before the founders pivoted to B2B payment infrastructure.
notes: Very low public profile and common name - verify any LinkedIn match against Xendit. CEO Moses Lo is the public face.

name: Moses Lo
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Xendit Group (Southeast Asian payments infrastructure, Jakarta)
profile: Australian-born founder (UNSW, UC Berkeley MBA; ex-BCG and Amazon) who co-founded Xendit in 2015; it went through Y Combinator S15 and became the first YC unicorn from Indonesia. Xendit provides payment APIs across Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Thailand and Vietnam, and in Nov 2025 launched a Global Account product at the Singapore FinTech Festival.
interesting_fact: Xendit was among the first five Southeast Asian companies accepted into Y Combinator, and became Indonesia's first YC unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: At Radford College in Canberra (Class of 2005) he won debating tournaments and represented Australia at Model United Nations; his advice to students is that 'marks are less important than soft skills.'
notes: Accessible, frequent podcast/conference speaker (Money20/20 Asia). Press email is the named PR & Communications contact on Xendit's Nov 2025 release; based in Jakarta.

name: Tessa Wijaya
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Xendit (also reported as CEO of Xendit Thailand)
profile: Indonesian co-founder and COO of Xendit, the Jakarta-based payments infrastructure company (Y Combinator alum, valued ~$3B). A former private-equity analyst, she oversees operations, partnerships, compliance and government relations, and is often cited as Indonesia's first female unicorn founder.
interesting_fact: She joined Xendit in 2016 after being introduced via Y Combinator to the UC Berkeley founders working on payments, having spotted the missing payment rails while working with early-stage startups in private equity.
deep_cut_fact: She grew up in a small Indonesian town raised by her grandmother, who ran a small food business, and landed her first PE analyst job in Jakarta with no finance background, teaching herself finance on her own time.
notes: Frequent podcast/conference speaker. Xendit press releases have named Ami Windarti (PR & Comms) as media contact; I could not verify the address directly.

name: Wu Yun
current_role: Founder & CEO, XforcePlus (Shanghai Yunli Information Technology / 票易通)
profile: Chinese enterprise-software founder (吴云, 'Will Woo') who set up XforcePlus in 2015 to digitise VAT invoices and supply-chain/finance/tax collaboration for large enterprises. Backed by Temasek (2019 Series C ~$100M) and a 2021 round at ~$1B valuation. Company filings show him holding the large majority of the operating entity.
interesting_fact: Described as a China supply-chain/finance/tax IT expert who led construction of what was billed as China's largest cloud-deployed financial shared-services platform before founding XforcePlus.
deep_cut_fact: Named to Fortune China's 2020 '40 Under 40' business list and is a member of Tsinghua SEM's entrepreneur-scholar DBA programme.
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable; no press email found.

name: Shen Xiangyang
current_role: Chairman of the HKUST Council (reappointed for 2026-2029); founder of IDEA (International Digital Economy Academy, Shenzhen); co-founder/chair of Xiaoice
profile: Harry Shum (沈向洋, b. 1966, Nanjing) earned a CMU robotics PhD (1996), co-founded Microsoft Research Asia and rose to Microsoft EVP of AI & Research, overseeing Bing and Cortana. He left in 2020 as Microsoft spun its Xiaoice chatbot into an independent company he co-founded, then founded the IDEA institute in Shenzhen and has chaired HKUST's Council since 2023.
interesting_fact: HKUST's Chancellor reappointed him Council Chairman for a second three-year term from March 6, 2026. He is also a foreign member of the US National Academy of Engineering and an IEEE Fellow, ACM Fellow and FREng.
deep_cut_fact: Before running Microsoft's AI empire he was a computer-vision researcher: with Richard Szeliski he wrote the SIGGRAPH 1997 paper 'Creating full view panoramic image mosaics and environment maps', showing how to seamlessly stitch handheld-camera photos into 360-degree panoramas.
notes: Hurun lists him under Xiaoice (valued ~$2B); Xiaoice's current status/leadership is unclear in 2025-26 coverage. No personal published contact found. Best routes are institutional: HKUST (Council Chair's office via HKUST communications) or the IDEA institute in Shenzhen. Very high-profile AI figure.

name: Bao Chunjian
current_role: Founder and CEO, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通), Shenzhen
profile: Chinese engineer (USTC computer science graduate) who spent ~9 years at Tencent, rising to data-centre director in its data platform department, before founding Xiaoe-tech, a SaaS platform that lets creators, educators and brands sell paid knowledge content, courses and live streams. Tencent is a major shareholder (~16.8%); the company has been preparing a Hong Kong listing.
interesting_fact: At Tencent he reached the rare 'T4 expert engineer' technical rank before leaving in 2015 to start his own business.
deep_cut_fact: Xiaoe-tech's prototype was a one-month rebuild of the paid-audio and membership system for finance writer Wu Xiaobo's 'Wu Xiaobo Channel' in 2016; Wu then invested. His first venture, a blue-collar hiring app called 工作帮, shut after about seven months.
notes: Known internally as 'Lao Bao'; hosts Xiaoe-tech's live interview series 老鲍对话标杆客户. Chinese-language outreach via Xiaoe-tech (xiaoe-tech.com) recommended. Education details vary across sources.

name: Yu Qianli
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen private-domain operations / creator-commerce SaaS)
profile: One of the ex-Tencent co-founders of Xiaoe-tech, the Shenzhen SaaS company led by founder-CEO Bao Chunjian (鲍春健). Its tools help merchants, educators and creators run e-commerce, marketing and CRM in their own channels. Investors include Tencent, Hillhouse, IDG and Qiming. Its 2021 Series D valued it at about HK$5.1B. It filed for a Hong Kong IPO in August 2025, and 36Kr reported a new attempt in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech's whole founding team came from Tencent. Founder Bao Chunjian left as a rare T4-level expert engineer with ¥5M of savings and burned through it in seven months before the business took off.
deep_cut_fact: 36Kr reports that this co-founder was previously responsible for product development on Tencent's QQ Zone (QQ空间). The article spells the name 喻干里, likely a misprint of 喻千里 (Yu Qianli).
notes: Very low public profile. The only mention I found is in 36Kr, which spells the name 喻干里 rather than 喻千里, so identity is marked uncertain until checked against the HKEX prospectus. Bao Chunjian is the public face and controlling shareholder (about 44.9% pre-IPO). Chinese-language outreach via the company's public-affairs email is the best route.

name: Wang Lianghu
current_role: Co-founder and VP of Product & R&D (产研副总裁), Xiaoe-tech / 小鹅通 (Shenzhen)
profile: Wang Lianghu (王良虎) co-founded Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通), a Shenzhen SaaS platform for selling online courses and digital content and running private-domain customer operations. It was founded by ex-Tencent data-center director Bao Chunjian, is backed by Tencent, Hillhouse and IDG, and refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in May 2026.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech is a 'Tencent alumni' startup: all four co-founders came from Tencent, and co-founder Yu Ganli once handled QQ Zone product development. Revenue grew from RMB 298M (2022) to RMB 521M (2024).
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding Xiaoe-tech, Wang Lianghu was a T3-level senior R&D engineer at Tencent, as was fellow co-founder Zeng Yongjun.
notes: Very low public profile, with few media appearances; CEO Bao Chunjian is the face of the company. Hong Kong IPO filing (lapsed Aug 2025, refiled 2026) is the best source for an official bio. VP title per Chinese press (sfccn.com, 2025). Company site: xiaoe-tech.com (not fetched).

name: Ze Yongjun
current_role: Co-founder, Xiaoe-tech (小鹅通, Shenzhen knowledge-commerce / private-domain SaaS); current title not found
profile: Xiaoe-tech's 2026 Hong Kong IPO filing coverage names co-founders Wang Lianghu and Zeng Yongjun (曾勇军), both former Tencent T3 senior R&D engineers, alongside founder-chairman-CEO Bao Chunjian (ex-Tencent data-centre director). Founded in 2015, Xiaoe-tech sells SaaS tools for online courses and private-domain e-commerce. Tencent invested in its 2020 Series C. It reported 2025 revenue of about RMB 608M and is pursuing an HKEX listing.
interesting_fact: Xiaoe-tech's founding team is heavily ex-Tencent. Founder Bao Chunjian ran Tencent's data centre business, two co-founders were Tencent T3 senior engineers, and another co-founder (Yu Ganli) worked on QQ Zone product development.
notes: 'Ze Yongjun' appears to be a romanization of 曾勇军 (Zeng Yongjun), a co-founder named in 36Kr's May 2026 IPO coverage. The match is likely but not confirmed. He is not among the listed executive directors (Bao Chunjian, Wang Tiebo, Hu Yabei, Zhou Shikun). Very low public profile; the best route is via the company once IR contacts appear in the HKEX prospectus.

name: Deng Guobiao
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, XTransfer (Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments platform for SMEs)
profile: Deng Guobiao ('Bill Deng') spent over a decade in payments, first at Visa and then at Ant Financial's Alipay (joined 2010), before co-founding XTransfer in May 2017 with five former Alibaba/Ant colleagues as a 'B2B version of Alipay'. XTransfer serves 800,000+ enterprises and holds payment licences in multiple markets; he now speaks widely on stablecoins for trade.
interesting_fact: Deng says he jumped to found XTransfer after watching colleagues leave to start businesses including ride-hailing giant Didi; he argues stablecoins suit cross-border B2B trade because 'when it comes to money, there's no 24/7 infrastructure'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Alipay he worked at Visa; Alibaba's eWTP fund led XTransfer's $15M Series B1, and Deng has said 'Our background from Alibaba indeed offers a good start'.
notes: Goes by Bill Deng in English media; active conference speaker (Singapore FinTech Festival, Forum Ekonomi Malaysia). No dedicated press email found; contact page offers general inquiry form.

name: Zheng Kai
current_role: Listed as co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer of XTransfer (single aggregator source; unverified)
profile: One of six co-founders of XTransfer, a Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments platform for SME exporters founded in 2017 by Bill (Guobiao) Deng with former Ant Group colleagues. Only one aggregator profile names 'Kai Zheng (Co-founder and CSO)'; no official XTransfer source found confirming his role.
interesting_fact: XTransfer was founded in 2017 by Bill Deng and five other co-founders, largely former Ant Group employees, to serve Chinese small exporters.
notes: Identity weakly sourced (https://yespress.io/xtransfer.md). The public face of XTransfer is founder/CEO Bill Deng; route via company.

name: Deng Xianliang
current_role: (If same person) Founder & CEO, XTransfer (Shanghai-based B2B cross-border payments)
profile: XTransfer's founder and CEO is Bill Deng (邓国标, Deng Guobiao), who launched it in May 2017 with five former Ant Group colleagues as a 'B2B Alipay' for Chinese SME exporters. He previously spent more than a decade in payments at Visa and Ant Financial. Fortune reported in 2026 that XTransfer serves over 800,000 businesses and processes over $12B a month.
interesting_fact: Fortune reported in 2026 that XTransfer handles more than 2% of China's exports. 'Global South' countries now make up 70% of its payments, while the US share fell from 22% to 9%.
deep_cut_fact: Deng says seven years at Alipay showed him that consumer payment rails were mature while B2B cross-border payments were still badly served. Former colleagues leaving to found companies such as Didi pushed him to start his own.
notes: Name mismatch: Hurun lists 'Deng Xianliang', but every source I found names XTransfer's founder and CEO as Bill Deng / 邓国标 (Deng Guobiao). Confirm this is the same person before outreach. He speaks often at fintech conferences such as Money20/20 and the Singapore FinTech Festival.

name: Liu Yanfang
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Chief Technology Officer, XTransfer (Shanghai)
profile: Chinese technologist (刘艳芳) who co-founded XTransfer in 2017 with CEO Bill (Guobiao) Deng and other ex-Alibaba/Ant Group colleagues; she leads engineering as CTO. XTransfer is a B2B cross-border payments platform for Chinese SME exporters, valued at $3.02B after its March 2026 Series E, and filed for a Hong Kong main-board IPO in April 2026.
interesting_fact: XTransfer says it is the world's largest B2B cross-border trade payment platform by volume, with 2025 payment volume of ~$60.5B, ~897,000 registered clients and over 98.5% of transactions reviewed automatically by AI.
deep_cut_fact: Before XTransfer she was a senior technical expert in Alibaba's B2B business unit, where she built Alibaba B2B's financial product management framework and its payment solutions from scratch.
notes: Very low English-language profile; CEO Bill Deng is the public face. Company site lists only customer helpdesk/complaints emails, no press email. Chinese-language outreach via the company is the likely route; HK IPO prospectus (2026) has her official bio.

name: Yao Wenchun
current_role: Co-founder, executive director & Chief Risk Officer, XTransfer (listed in the 2026 HKEX prospectus coverage as 姚伟春 / Yao Weichun)
profile: XTransfer, a Shanghai-founded B2B cross-border trade payments platform for small exporters, was started in 2017 by Bill Deng (邓国标) and fellow ex-Ant Group/Alibaba staff. Its co-founder and CRO 姚伟春 previously ran risk at Ant Group. XTransfer reached a $3.02B valuation after a Series E in March 2026 and filed for a Hong Kong main-board IPO in April 2026.
interesting_fact: XTransfer's 2017 seed round was just $2.95M at a $12M post-money valuation (from Yunqi Partners and Gaorong); its 2026 Series E valued it at $3.02B.

name: David Kirtley
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Michigan-trained nuclear, plasma and aerospace engineer who co-founded fusion company Helion in 2013. Helion holds the first fusion power-purchase agreement (with Microsoft) and began building its 50 MW Orion plant in Malaga, WA in July 2025, targeting 2028. In February 2026 its Polaris prototype showed the first private D-T fusion.
interesting_fact: Helion's Orion plant is meant to sell fusion electricity to Microsoft, a direct link between fusion and AI data-center power demand. On Lex Fridman's podcast, Kirtley described wanting a 'gigafactory' that turns out 50 MW fusion generators.
deep_cut_fact: He started in space propulsion, not power plants. Early in his career he studied beamed-microwave rocket concepts, in which a spacecraft needs no onboard fuel. Before spinning out Helion, his team worked on fusion rockets and advanced materials. He says they reused circuit topologies from space hardware for fusion.
notes: Very podcast-friendly. He has appeared on Lex Fridman #485, GeekWire's Positive Charge and Slush 2026, and is an ideal guest for the energy/data-center theme. Use Helion's press form. Company X account: @helion_energy. I found no verified personal handle.

name: George Votroubek
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Scientist, Helion Energy (Everett, WA)
profile: Plasma physicist (MS, PhD University of Washington) who co-founded fusion company Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and John Slough, colleagues from MSNW in Redmond. Helion pursues pulsed field-reversed-configuration fusion, is building its Polaris prototype and Orion plant, and has raised ~$1.5B.
interesting_fact: Helion signed the world's first fusion power purchase agreement with Microsoft (plus a deal with steelmaker Nucor) - a direct link between fusion and powering data centers.
deep_cut_fact: He was Principal Investigator for the program that demonstrated Helion's 'Fusion Engine' technology at one-third scale, work that grew out of the Inductive Plasmoid Accelerator experiments the founders ran before Helion existed.
notes: Low-profile scientist; CEO David Kirtley is Helion's public voice. Helion's contact form has a 'Press' inquiry option. Excellent fit for energy + data-center theme. Deep-cut sourced to Crunchbase bio (not a primary document).

name: John Slough
current_role: Cofounder (former) of Helion Energy; plasma physicist, MSNW LLC (Redmond, WA)
profile: Plasma physicist who cofounded Helion Energy in 2013 with David Kirtley, Chris Pihl and George Votroubek; Helion's pulsed fusion approach builds on his FRC plasmoid merging-and-compression research. He left Helion in 2018 to refocus on his research firm MSNW. His wealth reflects his Helion stake (company valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: He is an inventor on Helion's foundational patents, including a 2011 patent on generating, heating and compressing plasmoids and recovering energy from them, and the 'Advanced D–3He fuel cycle for a pulsed fusion reactor'.
deep_cut_fact: NASA's Innovative Advanced Concepts (NIAC) program funded his 'Fusion Driven Rocket' (2012 Phase II): magnetically driven metal liners crush a plasmoid to fusion and become the propellant, a concept meant to make crewed interplanetary travel 'common place'.
notes: No longer with Helion (left 2018), so Helion PR is not a route to him; reports cite disagreement over fuel choice, so avoid that topic. Very low public profile; MSNW's website was unreachable. Best approached as a fusion-science expert via academic or plasma-physics channels.

WTW completed its acquisition of Newfront in January 2026 for up to $1.3B. In May 2026 WTW named Lipkin Chief AI Officer and Wintrob Head of AI Acceleration, helping colleagues embed AI tools into daily work.
interesting_fact: A year after graduating from MIT he founded StackLead (2013), which aggregated sales-lead data from across the web and was quickly acquired by LinkedIn. He then worked at LinkedIn for about three years. He met Lipkin through a friend who said: 'You're the only two people I know interested in insurance.'
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Los Angeles he was 'basically an IT support guy' for his neighbors, setting up Wi-Fi and installing software. As an MIT undergrad he worked on a money-transfer system for developing countries, and his team was the only undergraduate team to reach the final round of the MIT $100K Entrepreneurship Competition.
notes: Appears on podcasts (Software Engineering Daily; 'The Blind Ambition' with Jack Kelly), so he is receptive to podcast formats. Now inside WTW, so outreach may go through WTW media relations (wtwco.com). Role source: riskandinsurance.com, May 1, 2026.

name: Spike Lipkin
current_role: Co-founder and CEO of Newfront, now part of WTW after WTW completed the acquisition in January 2026. At WTW he focuses on integration, client development, talent acquisition and technology.
profile: Spike Lipkin was a Blackstone investor on the startup team behind Invitation Homes, then one of Opendoor's first employees. In 2017 he co-founded Newfront, a San Francisco insurance brokerage built on its own technology covering business insurance and employee benefits. WTW agreed to buy Newfront in December 2025 and completed the roughly $1.3bn acquisition in January 2026; Lipkin joined WTW.
interesting_fact: WTW's acquisition of Newfront was reported at about $1.3bn including contingent consideration. Lipkin built the tech-enabled broker from a 2017 start into one of the largest venture-backed deals in insurance brokerage.
deep_cut_fact: Before insurance he was on Blackstone's startup team that built Invitation Homes into the largest US owner of single-family rental homes. He then joined Opendoor when it had five people. Both jobs exposed him firsthand to how painful buying insurance was.
notes: Now inside WTW, a public company, so media requests likely route through WTW media relations (contact not verified this session). He has appeared on podcasts (Category Visionaries, June 2023). Insurance Business named him a 2019 Young Gun at age 31.

name: Chen Zhongguo
current_role: Listed legal representative of GTA Semiconductor (上海积塔半导体) and its parent Huada Semiconductor (per 36Kr company profiles)
profile: Chen Zhongguo (陈忠国) appears in Chinese company records as legal representative of Shanghai GTA Semiconductor, a Lingang-based maker of analog ICs and power devices founded in 2017, and of its parent Huada Semiconductor, a wholly owned unit of state-owned China Electronics Corp (CEC).
