name: Dileep Thazhmon
current_role: Founder and CEO, Jeeves (global corporate card, spend management and cross-border business finance platform)
profile: Serial entrepreneur and Stanford GSB graduate who co-founded and ran ad-tech firm PowerInbox (later Jeeng) as COO before founding Jeeves (Y Combinator S20). Jeeves offers multi-currency corporate cards, payments and credit to companies across Latin America, Europe and North America; it raised $180M led by Tencent at a $2.1B valuation in March 2022.
interesting_fact: Jeeves hit a $2.1B valuation only about seven months after its $57M Series B, in a Tencent-led $180M Series C that included Stanford University and GIC as investors.
deep_cut_fact: At PowerInbox, an email ad server used by 600+ brands including CNN and Disney, he grew the team from 3 to 50+ while keeping it profitable at $35M+ ARR; it ranked #3 on Deloitte's Fast50. He also worked in venture capital earlier.
notes: Featured on HubSpot for Startups 'Spiraling Up: The Journey to Become a Unicorn' (S1 ep3), where he calls Jeeves his 'legacy project' - good podcast hook. No published press email found for Jeeves.

name: Sherwin Gandhi
current_role: Co-founder and director of Jeeves (cross-border corporate cards and spend management for Latin America and beyond); also an angel investor
profile: Co-founder of Jeeves, a fintech offering multi-currency corporate cards, payments and expense management to startups in Latin America, Canada and Europe, led by CEO Dileep Thazhmon. Aggregator profiles list Gandhi as founder, executive officer and director, with an RPI undergraduate degree and around eight angel investments.
notes: Very thin public footprint; role sourced only from aggregators (https://www.pipeseed.com/investor/sherwin-gandhi-936507, https://seedtable.com/person/Sherwin_Gandhi-39W6XNJ, https://ch.marketscreener.com/insider/SHERWIN-GANDHI-A39CHL/erfahrung). Public face of Jeeves is CEO Dileep Thazhmon. No published press email found on tryjeeves.com.

name: Firmin Zocchetto
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PayFit (Paris-based payroll & HR software)
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded PayFit in 2015 with Ghislain de Fontenay and Florian Fournier while studying at ESCP, then dropped out to run it. PayFit automates payroll and HR for SMEs in Europe and became a unicorn in 2022. In 2024 he said PayFit would be profitable in 2026, and for its tenth anniversary he said an IPO was not planned for the next three years.
interesting_fact: He caught the 'startup bug' in high school in Laval. His first venture, built with classmate and future PayFit co-founder Ghislain de Fontenay, was a social network for learning languages.
deep_cut_fact: His family has Italian roots and worked as builders and construction entrepreneurs. On leaving ESCP he said: 'For me, it was an obvious choice; for my family, a little less so.' He was mentored early by Capgemini chair Paul Hermelin.
notes: Gives interviews often in French media (JDN, Maddyness). Good podcast candidate on the European SaaS scale-up story.

name: Florian Fournier
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Orasio (European AI video-analysis/defence-tech startup); co-founder and board member, PayFit
profile: French entrepreneur who co-founded Paris payroll/HR SaaS PayFit in 2015 with Firmin Zocchetto and Ghislain de Fontenay and spent nine years building it into a ~$2B company. He left his operational role in January 2024 and in 2025 launched Orasio, which raised a EUR16M seed led by Frst to build sovereign European AI that analyses video feeds for police, cities, critical sites and the military.
interesting_fact: Orasio's name comes from the Greek 'orasi' ('vision'); its AI detects fires, falls, crowd movements and weapons in real time, and France's defence ministry AI agency (Amiad) has taken up its image-analysis tools.
deep_cut_fact: A Polytechnique alumnus who also attended a military school, he met both Orasio co-founders (Arnaud Delaunay and Fabio Gennari) back in preparatory school; he says 'J'ai toujours eu une sensibilité forte pour les enjeux de défense.'
notes: Media-friendly: Orasio's press page lists his interviews with BFM Business, Europe 1, BFMTV etc. French-language outreach likely best. LinkedIn link is the company page, not personal.

name: Ghislain de Fontenay
current_role: Co-founder and Director of the Innovation Lab ('Delta Team'), PayFit (former CTO)
profile: Ghislain de Fontenay co-founded Paris-based PayFit in 2015 with Firmin Zocchetto and Florian Fournier to automate payroll and HR for European SMEs, serving as its first CTO. PayFit became a unicorn after raising EUR 254M in late 2021. He now leads PayFit's innovation lab.
interesting_fact: To tame French payroll rules, PayFit's founders created their own programming language, JetLang, to encode labour regulations and collective agreements, later extended to other countries.
deep_cut_fact: He and Firmin Zocchetto built their first company together as high-school students: a social network for learning foreign languages, which they dropped because it became too time-consuming.
notes: Current Innovation Lab title comes from an aggregator profile (me.sh); low public profile, technical founder. PayFit press contact published as mailto on its press page.

name: Gaston Taratuta
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aleph Group (formerly Aleph Holding), Miami
profile: Argentine entrepreneur (b. 1972) whose Aleph Group acts as commercial/advertising partner for platforms such as X, TikTok and Spotify in markets where they don't operate directly. It grew from IMS Internet Media Services (2005); CVC's 2021 minority investment valued Aleph at about $2B. Aleph has since expanded into payments (Aleph Payments, Localpayment).
interesting_fact: He was named EY World Entrepreneur Of The Year 2022 - the first Argentine to win the global award.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding IMS he spent six years at Brazilian internet company UOL's Miami office, leaving in 2004 as head of international operations; by his own account he started IMS in 2005 with about US$5,000, and from 2011 it represented Twitter commercially abroad.
notes: Full name Christian Gastón Taratuta. No press email published on the company site; the company X account is @itsalephdigital.

name: Mathieu Alengrin
current_role: Co-founder, Ankorstore (listed by Crunchbase as Co-founder and Principal Engineer; not verified on primary source)
profile: French software engineer who was Head of Engineering at Vestiaire Collective before co-founding Ankorstore in Paris in 2019 with Pierre-Louis Lacoste, Nicolas d'Audiffret and Nicolas Cohen. Ankorstore is a European B2B wholesale marketplace connecting independent brands with retailers; it raised a EUR250M Series C in 2022 and reached unicorn status in about two years.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore went from founding in 2019 to unicorn in roughly two years, raising EUR6M seed (2019), EUR25M Series A (2020), EUR84M Series B (2021) and EUR250M Series C (2022).
deep_cut_fact: Ankorstore's founding team paired Alengrin, the engineering lead from luxury resale marketplace Vestiaire Collective, with the founders of the handmade marketplace A Little Market (Nicolas d'Audiffret and Nicolas Cohen) and ex-Etsy Wholesale manager Pierre-Louis Lacoste.
notes: Technical, behind-the-scenes co-founder with almost no press presence; CEO Pierre-Louis Lacoste is the public face. No published press email found on ankorstore.com.

name: Nicolas Cohen
current_role: Co-founder of Ankorstore (co-CEO since 2019; current title not confirmed for 2025-26)
profile: French e-commerce entrepreneur who co-founded ALittleMarket, a leading French handmade-goods marketplace sold to Etsy in 2014, then worked at Etsy before co-founding Paris-based B2B wholesale marketplace Ankorstore in 2019. Ankorstore became a unicorn in Jan 2022 with a EUR 250M Series C (BOND, Tiger Global) at a EUR 1.75B valuation.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore hit unicorn status only about two years after launch, by which time it connected 200,000 independent retailers with 15,000 brands; Cohen said the mission was 'to swing the balance in favor of independents.'
deep_cut_fact: The idea for Ankorstore came from conversations, while he and Nicolas d'Audiffret were at Etsy after it bought their ALittleMarket, about how hard it was for Etsy sellers to grow from B2C storefronts into wholesale businesses.
notes: Common name - be careful with disambiguation. Aggregator profiles conflict on whether he is still co-CEO (one says 2019-2024). No published press email found for Ankorstore this session.

name: Nicolas d'Audiffret
current_role: Co-founder, Ankorstore (co-led the company until 2025; Grégoire de Tilly named CEO in 2026)
profile: Nicolas d'Audiffret is a French serial marketplace founder. With Nicolas Cohen he co-founded ALittleMarket (2012), France's top handmade-goods marketplace, which Etsy bought in 2014. In 2019 he co-founded Ankorstore, a European B2B wholesale marketplace linking independent brands and shops, which raised over €365M and was valued at more than €1.7B in early 2022. He co-ran it until 2025.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore was born at Etsy. He and Nicolas Cohen worked there after the ALittleMarket sale, noticed Etsy sellers wanted to wholesale to shops, and after staying France-only with their first company, launched Ankorstore internationally from day one.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent 2003-2011 as a consultant at Bain & Company in Paris and San Francisco. In 2026 Ankorstore's CEO role passed to another Bain alumnus, Grégoire de Tilly.

public_contacts.value: Guest episode: 'How To Build A $2 Billion Unicorn In Under 3 Years with Ankorstore's Nicolas d'Audiffret'

notes: No longer CEO. Consultor (2026) says he co-led Ankorstore until 2025, and his new activity was not found. Do not confuse him with co-founder Nicolas Cohen. He has done English-language podcasts and interviews. The podcast entry was taken from a search listing and was not opened.

name: Pierre Louis Lacoste
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Brand Officer, Ankorstore (Paris B2B wholesale marketplace); current title per MarketScreener, not confirmed on Ankorstore's own site
profile: French e-commerce entrepreneur who co-founded Ankorstore in 2019 with Nicolas d'Audiffret, Nicolas Cohen and Mathieu Alengrin. Ankorstore is a wholesale marketplace connecting independent brands with independent shops across Europe. Before that he was a VP at activewear brand Lolë and Etsy's Country Manager for France. Ankorstore raised a €250M Series C in 2022 at unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Ankorstore is partly a second attempt at an idea Etsy dropped: at Etsy he worked on Etsy Wholesale, which was cancelled when Etsy refocused on consumers. 'I always thought it was a missed opportunity, but also that I would do a few things differently.'
deep_cut_fact: Before building a platform for independent retailers he ran one himself: he owned a multi-brand retail store for several years, and says this taught him how hard it is for shops to find brands and agree terms.
notes: Nicolas d'Audiffret, not Lacoste, is Ankorstore's CEO. The PR agency contact is from a March 2024 release and may be dated. No recent (2025-26) coverage of Lacoste found.

name: Itai Lahan
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Tal Lev-Ami (CTO) and Nadav Soferman (CPO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Its API-based image/video management platform grew for years without VC before Bessemer invested; Hurun values it at ~$2bn, and it now ships AI agents for visual media.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary had paying customers within months of formation and grew organically for years without venture capital, before Bessemer Venture Partners invested to fund expansion.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cloudinary he was an executive at Israeli anti-spam startup Blue Security and at Collactive, founded news aggregator Newsodrome, and in 2009 co-founded Ndivi, a tech consultancy for start-up founders - the gap he noticed there sparked the Cloudinary idea.
notes: Press contact on Cloudinary newsroom: Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications. Has done developer-podcast interviews (Software Engineering Daily, 'Bootstrapping a SaaS for Developers') - receptive to podcast format.

name: Nadav Soferman
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli engineer Nadav Soferman co-founded Cloudinary in early 2012 with Itai Lahan (CEO) and Tal Lev-Ami (CTO), whom he met in the IDF's 8200 unit. Cloudinary's API-first platform optimises, transforms and delivers images and video for the web; it bootstrapped for years before taking growth capital (~$2B valuation). As CPO he leads product.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary was a rare bootstrapped Israeli startup: five years in (2017) it had raised no venture capital, yet had 220,000 developers on its free tier and 5,000 paying customers including eBay and Sky News.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary's first version took just four months to build and launched quietly in mid-2012; the idea came from the founders' consulting firm Ndivi, where every new social-network client struggled to render images well on every device and resolution.
notes: Low-profile product-side founder (CEO Itai Lahan is the usual spokesperson). Press contact is Cloudinary's Senior Director of Global Communications (Juli Greenwood) as listed on the newsroom page. He has written for Smashing Magazine on responsive images.

name: Tal Lev-Ami
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cloudinary
profile: Israeli developer who co-founded Cloudinary in 2012 with Itai Lahan and Nadav Soferman to fix the tedious work of uploading, transforming and delivering images and video online. The API-first media platform grew profitably without venture funding; a 2022 Blackstone-led secondary deal valued it at $2B. He remains CTO, focusing on AI-powered visual media at scale.
interesting_fact: Cloudinary bootstrapped its way to a $100M annual revenue run rate (2021) without venture capital, before Blackstone's $100M+ secondary investment valued it at $2B.
deep_cut_fact: Cloudinary worked with Google researchers to create the JPEG XL image format, and has since championed JPEG XL support across browsers and Apple devices.
notes: Press contact is Juli Greenwood, Senior Director Global Communications, as listed on the Cloudinary newsroom. He gives technical interviews (e.g. TechDogs Dec 2025). Deep-cut fact is about the company he co-founded, not him personally. Fit is CDN/media infrastructure rather than energy.

name: Renaud Heitz
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Exotec (warehouse robotics, France)
profile: French robotics engineer (Mines Paris-PSL 2006) who worked in robotics software at BA Systèmes and GE Healthcare, then co-founded Exotec in 2015 with CEO Romain Moulin, a longtime colleague. Exotec's Skypod robots climb racks to move in 3D; after first customer Cdiscount it signed clients including Carrefour, Uniqlo and Gap, becoming France's first industrial unicorn.
interesting_fact: In Feb 2026 Exotec opened 'Imaginarium', a 25,000 m² global HQ and production site in Wasquehal, Northern France, with 700+ staff from 60+ nationalities. Heitz said it 'reflects our commitment to build in Europe and our decision to invest for the long term.'
deep_cut_fact: He experienced both Mines Paris-PSL and MIT, calling them two excellent programs with very different academic models, and says his Mines diploma is 'une vraie carte de visite', even with American investors like Goldman Sachs.
notes: No current published press email found. A 2024 release named PR agency Hopscotch for Exotec, but that is dated. CEO Romain Moulin is the more public founder. Pre-Exotec employers come from company job listings and profiles.

name: Romain Moulin
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Exotec
profile: French robotics engineer who co-founded Exotec (Croix/Lille, launched 2015) with longtime friend and GE colleague Renaud Heitz. Exotec's Skypod system uses climbing robots for warehouse automation; a $335M Series D led by Goldman Sachs in Jan 2022 valued it at $2B. Moulin remains CEO, leading global expansion and next-gen Skypod launches.
interesting_fact: Exotec's $335M Series D (Jan 2022, led by Goldman Sachs Asset Management with Bpifrance and 83North) at a $2B valuation made it France's first industrial unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a sales engineer at a small French automated-forklift company, rising to technical manager, then worked on advanced robotic imagers at GE Healthcare, where he says he 'really learned what it takes to build a hardware product.' He has known co-founder Renaud Heitz for 20+ years.
notes: PR agency email (Hopscotch, France) is from an April 2024 joint release and may be outdated; UK releases (2025) list agency Spreckley. Exotec press page: https://www.exotec.com/press/.

name: William Addy
current_role: Founder and board member, ISN Software Corporation (Dallas, TX)
profile: Bill Addy founded Dallas-based ISN Software in 2001. ISN runs the ISNetworld platform, which energy, steel, pharma and other enterprises use to manage contractor and supplier compliance; it served 75,000+ customers in 85+ countries including 170 Fortune 500 firms. He was CEO until about 2015 and then executive chairman. ISN now lists him as Founder, with Brian Callahan as CEO. He is a Dallas philanthropist (The Addy Foundation).
interesting_fact: He and his wife Lydia gave the gift behind Addy Hall, a dormitory in Princeton's new residential colleges. Addy is a Princeton '82 chemical engineering graduate.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012 the Addys created the Addy/ISN North American Low Carbon Emission Energy Self-Sufficiency Fund at Princeton for research on cutting carbon and achieving North American energy self-sufficiency. His senior thesis was 'one part chemical engineering and nine parts economics' on ExxonMobil in western Colorado.
notes: A strong fit for an energy podcast: his clients are heavily energy-sector and he funds low-carbon energy research. Blackstone is an ISN investor with a board seat. He also does North Texas philanthropy (search results tie him to KERA public broadcasting, unverified). No published personal email.

name: Alvin Tamsir
current_role: Scientific Fellow and Co-Founder, Pivot Bio (Berkeley, CA)
profile: Synthetic biologist (BA Molecular & Cell Biology, UC Berkeley; PhD UCSF under Christopher Voigt) who co-founded Pivot Bio in 2011 with lab mate Karsten Temme. Pivot Bio makes nitrogen-fixing microbes that replace part of farmers' synthetic fertiliser; Tamsir led its first commercial corn product, co-authored foundational patents and grew research from under 10 to 200+ scientists.
interesting_fact: Pivot Bio grew out of a 2011 paper by Temme and Dehua Zhao in Voigt's lab on engineering nitrogen fixation - an idea Berkeley dean Paul Ludden suggested to Voigt after a photosynthesis grant proposal was heavily criticised.
deep_cut_fact: As a PhD student he was first author of a 2010 Nature paper, 'Robust multicellular computing using genetically encoded NOR gates and chemical wires', building logic circuits out of communicating E. coli colonies.
notes: Scientist, low media profile; route via Pivot Bio media team. The source page renders the address as 'media@www.pivotbio.com' (CMS artifact); recent Business Wire releases reportedly use media@pivotbio.com.

name: Karsten Temme
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Innovation Officer and board member, Pivot Bio (Berkeley, CA)
profile: Bioengineer (Iowa BS/MS; UC Berkeley-UCSF PhD) who in Chris Voigt's lab tried to rebuild microbial nitrogen fixation from scratch. In 2011 he co-founded Pivot Bio with Alvin Tamsir to replace synthetic nitrogen fertilizer with nitrogen-fixing soil microbes, serving as CEO until 2023; he now leads innovation focused on 'the Future Acre' (agriculture in 2050).
interesting_fact: He holds over 200 patents or patent applications (90+ granted) and spoke at the TED Countdown Summit in Nairobi in 2025.
deep_cut_fact: Originally from Casper, Wyoming, he played trumpet in the University of Iowa's Hawkeye Marching Band, helped design parts for a Mars rover, and as an undergrad founded Xwires Communications to bring internet service to remote farmland.
notes: Chris Abbott replaced him as CEO in Aug 2023. Experienced TED speaker; climate/ag-emissions angle (synthetic fertilizer is energy-intensive).

name: Anurag Arjun
current_role: Co-founder, Avail (modular blockchain data-availability network); co-founder of Polygon (formerly Matic Network)
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded Matic Network (now Polygon) in 2017 with Jaynti Kanani and Sandeep Nailwal and served as its Chief Product Officer. In 2023 he spun Avail, a data-availability project, out of Polygon Labs and became its 'sole steward'. Avail raised a $27M seed round led by Founders Fund and Dragonfly.
interesting_fact: Avail started inside Polygon in late 2020. In March 2023 Polygon spun it off, and Arjun left Polygon Labs to run it as an independent company with co-founder Prabal Banerjee.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto, he spent years in health-tech product management. At Dexter Consultancy he co-created HealthTrac, a platform that monitored vital signs remotely through wearables, and HealthOne, a free SaaS clinic-management tool for doctors. His first job was programmer analyst at Cognizant in 2006.
notes: Active on X and a regular on crypto podcasts. The deep-cut source is a crowd-edited wiki, so double-check before using it. Hurun lists the wealth source as Polygon Labs.

name: Jaynti Kanani
current_role: Founder, Morphic (AI creative/video studio); Polygon co-founder (stepped back 2023)
profile: Indian engineer from Ahmedabad who co-founded Matic Network in 2017 with Sandeep Nailwal and Anurag Arjun; it became Polygon, a leading Ethereum scaling network. He stepped back from Polygon leadership in 2023 and now builds Morphic, an AI studio for consistent, controllable images, video and stories, launched as Morphic Studio in July 2024.
interesting_fact: On Product Hunt he introduces himself as 'JD here, Founder of Morphic', pitching an all-in-one AI creative studio for cinematic images, videos and stories.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto he was a senior software engineer at Persistent Systems (from 2011) and then a data scientist at real-estate startup Housing.com (from Dec 2014), freelancing before co-founding Matic in 2017.
notes: He announced on X (4 Oct 2023) that he had stepped back from Polygon about six months earlier. Best route is likely X (@jdkanani) or Morphic. Indian media profiles focus heavily on his family's finances; avoid that angle.

name: Ouyang Jian
current_role: CEO, Kunlunxin (昆仑芯, Beijing) - Baidu's AI-chip spin-off (CEO since June 2021; 2026 status per company news, not independently re-verified)
profile: Ouyang Jian (欧阳剑) was Baidu's chief chip architect and led its Kunlun AI-chip program. When Baidu spun Kunlun out in June 2021 (valued ~CNY 13B after a CPE-led round), he became CEO and legal representative. Kunlunxin sells AI accelerator cards and 'supernode' clusters for data centers and large models.

deep_cut_fact: At the 2021 launch he said compute and semiconductor technology faced 'an unprecedented opportunity for change', and Kunlun's team presented at chip-design's top conference ISSCC 2021 just before the spin-off.
notes: Strong data-center/AI-chip fit. Company publishes only a business/cooperation mailbox (marketing@kunlunxin.com); no personal social accounts found. Speaks at Baidu/WAIC events; interviews mostly in Chinese. Web-search quota ran out, so his current title rests on the company's own news pages.

name: Jeff Elton
current_role: Vice Chairman and Founding CEO, ConcertAI (oncology real-world data and AI)
profile: Dr. Jeff Elton was founding CEO of ConcertAI, backed by founder/executive chairman Romesh Wadhwani, which combines oncology real-world data, clinical expertise and applied AI for pharma and providers (CancerLinQ, TeraRecon). After an April 2025 leadership transition Eron Kelly became CEO and Elton moved to vice chairman.
interesting_fact: ConcertAI now runs ASCO's CancerLinQ oncology quality platform and in 2025 launched a generative and agentic AI 'Precision Suite' that automates ASCO guidelines and clinical-trial matching.
notes: No longer CEO (vice chairman since 2025). Frequent podcast/interview guest (e.g. 'Cracking the Clinical Trial Code', AITech interview) so open to media; route via Treble PR. No sourced deep-cut found (web-search budget exhausted). Healthcare-AI angle rather than energy/data centers.

name: Chase Lochmiller
current_role: Co-founder, CEO and Chairman, Crusoe
profile: Co-founded Crusoe with Cully Cavness in 2018 to turn flared, otherwise-wasted natural gas into power for on-site computing. Crusoe has since become a vertically integrated AI-infrastructure company (energy, data centers, cloud) building campuses in Texas, Wyoming and beyond; in 2026 it raised a $3.9B Series F at a $30.9B valuation.
interesting_fact: Crusoe's origin was its patented 'Digital Flare Mitigation' technology: putting modular data centers at oil fields to burn stranded gas for computing instead of flaring it. It now reports 6GW+ of contracted capacity.
deep_cut_fact: On the Series F he framed Crusoe's strategy as 'controlling the infrastructure from electrons to tokens', saying AI 'will usher in an era of abundance'.
notes: Top-priority fit for an energy + data-center podcast. The Hurun '$10B valuation' is stale (now $30.9B). No published press email found; use the contact form or company socials. Web search budget ran out before personal background (education, earlier career) could be sourced.

name: Cully Cavness
current_role: Co-Founder, President and Chief Strategy Officer, Crusoe (AI data-centre / 'AI factory' developer and cloud), Denver
profile: Cully Cavness co-founded Crusoe with CEO Chase Lochmiller after leadership roles in upstream oil and gas, geothermal energy and energy investment banking (Middlebury and Oxford alum). Crusoe began by using stranded, flared natural gas to power bitcoin mining in oilfields, then pivoted to energy-first AI data centres, including the flagship campus for OpenAI's Stargate project.
interesting_fact: Crusoe's origin pitch: pay oil producers for gas they would otherwise flare for zero, and burn it in on-site generators to power computing; Cavness told Insider it was one of North America's biggest bitcoin miners, with units in North Dakota, Colorado and Montana.
deep_cut_fact: Before Crusoe he worked in the geothermal energy industry as well as upstream oil and gas, an early clean-energy thread that shows up in Crusoe's internal rule to pick projects only if they are net reducers of greenhouse gases.
notes: Perfect fit for an energy + data-centre podcast; frequent conference speaker (e.g., FII Riyadh). Title changed over time (President, COO, now President & Chief Strategy Officer per crusoe.ai). Route via media@crusoe.ai.

name: John Street
current_role: Founder and Chairman of the Board, Pax8 (Greenwood Village, Colorado); former CEO
profile: Denver native John Street is a serial Colorado founder who started Pax8 in 2012 as a cloud-commerce marketplace that lets managed service providers buy and bill Microsoft and other cloud/security products. Pax8 grew to ~2,000 employees and a multi-billion valuation; Street handed the CEO role to Scott Chasin and now chairs the board as Pax8 pushes into 'managed intelligence' AI agents.
interesting_fact: He received the 2023 Colorado Governor's Citizenship Medal for Growth and Innovation from Gov. Jared Polis and CTA's Bob Newman Lifetime Achievement Award in 2025, after being named CTA CEO of the Year in 2024.
deep_cut_fact: Pax8 is his fourth Colorado start-up: before it he launched Telephone Express, USA.Net (an early web-based email provider) and MX Logic (email security).
notes: Accessible, community-minded Colorado founder who does podcasts and local tech events (e.g. FirstMile Ventures 'Four Minute Founder', Colorado Voices on Tech). Route via Pax8 media relations. interesting_fact: Upside's model gets fuel stations, grocers and restaurants to fund personalised cash-back offers only on incremental profit, and users have earned hundreds of millions of dollars in cash back.

notes: Very low individual profile; common name - identity anchored only via company co-founder lists. No published press email found on Upside newsroom; CEO Alex Kinnier is the company's public face.

name: Wayne Lin
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Product Officer, Upside (Washington, DC); COO 2016-2023
profile: Wayne Lin co-founded Upside (formerly GetUpside) with CEO Alex Kinnier and others after both were product executives at Opower, the utility-energy-savings software firm that IPO'd in 2014 and was bought by Oracle. Upside's app gives consumers personalized cash back at gas stations, grocers and restaurants, paid from merchants' incremental profit; it reached a $1B+ valuation in 2021.
interesting_fact: Upside's model is pay-for-performance: 'Only when they make more profit than they made today do we make money,' Lin said in 2017, when the app was live at 650 D.C.-area gas stations and had paid out $300K in cash back. Google chief economist Hal Varian advised the startup.
deep_cut_fact: The Upside idea came from his Opower years, watching how consumers responded to personalized nudges to save on utility bills; the 2017 app even had a #GasForGood option letting users donate cash back to local charities like the Capital Area Food Bank.
notes: Energy angle: ex-Opower product/analytics VP. Don't confuse with a different Wayne Lin (Berkeley/Amazon, Mooncat/Nostos Health). No published press email on Upside newsroom.

name: Christina Cacioppo
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Vanta (security compliance automation)
profile: Midwest-raised founder who began her career in venture at Union Square Ventures, quit to teach herself to code, helped build Dropbox Paper, then founded Vanta in 2017 to automate SOC 2 and other security compliance. Vanta scaled to $10M ARR before raising a Series A and was valued around $4B by 2025.
interesting_fact: Vanta famously reached $10M ARR before raising a Series A; she has said she worked through many failed ideas ('I failed 22 times') before landing on compliance automation.
deep_cut_fact: Her personal site says her internet life began in the 90s on Beanie Baby forums and eBay, she 'still bleeds scarlet and gray,' loves 80s-90s gymnastics and Magritte's L'Empire des lumieres, and she angel-invested in Nigerian ISP Tizeti in 2017.
notes: Publishes her own email on her personal site - best direct route. Frequent podcast guest (Masters of Scale, My First Million, Invest Like the Best).

name: Erik Goldman
current_role: Co-founder of Vanta (left the company in 2020); current role not found
profile: Software engineer (reportedly ex-Dropbox, Stanford) who co-founded compliance-automation company Vanta with CEO Christina Cacioppo, working on the initial SOC 2 automation product; Vanta went through Y Combinator and is now valued at about $4B. He left Vanta in 2020.
interesting_fact: Co-founded Vanta, which pioneered automated SOC 2 / security compliance for startups and grew into a multibillion-dollar company.
notes: Very low public profile and a common name (several other Erik Goldmans in tech, e.g. Limelight Labs and Sfara founders) - verify identity before outreach. No published contact found.

name: Aidan Corbett
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Wayflyer (revenue-based financing for e-commerce/SMEs, Dublin)
profile: Irish serial entrepreneur (UCC engineering, London Business School MBA) who founded Kubicle and analytics firm Conjura before launching Wayflyer with Jack Pierse in 2019. Wayflyer, which became a unicorn about 20 months after launch, has deployed over €5B to 6,000+ businesses and in 2026 added large credit facilities (e.g. US$250M with ATLAS SP Partners).
interesting_fact: Wayflyer reached unicorn status roughly 20 months after launching; Corbett credits the Netflix culture book 'No Rules Rules', which he says he and Pierse 'swallowed whole'.
deep_cut_fact: He started his career as a civil servant in Ireland's Department of Communications, Marine and Natural Resources, and his first venture was Kubicle (2013), an online training business teaching professionals Excel and PowerPoint.
notes: Active on podcasts and Web Summit stages. Press contact is Head of Communications Lewis Jones via press@wayflyer.com (2025-26 releases).

name: Jack Pierse
current_role: Co-founder & former CFO, Wayflyer; angel investor
profile: Irish chartered accountant who co-founded Dublin e-commerce revenue-based financing company Wayflyer with Aidan Corbett in 2019 and served as CFO; it hit unicorn status in ~29 months. He stepped away in 2023 to pursue new ventures and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: Aidan Corbett credits Pierse with coming up with the original idea for Wayflyer in 2019; he saw the working-capital squeeze first-hand while working at an e-commerce accelerator.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 he joined the $20M Series A of US fintech startup Arc as an angel investor.
notes: No public contact found; post-Wayflyer venture not confirmed.

name: Arthur Macedo
current_role: Listed as CloudWalk co-founder (chief commercial officer 2013-2018 per MarketScreener); current role unknown
profile: Arthur Macedo is listed by MarketScreener as one of five 2013 co-founders of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech behind InfinitePay (with Luis Silva, Behzad Malek, Bruno Freitas and Eliezer Pimentel), serving as chief commercial officer from 2013 to 2018. No independent press, company or filing source confirming his role or background was found.
interesting_fact: CloudWalk, which he is listed as co-founding, became a unicorn in Nov 2021 when a $150M round valued it at $2.15B, more than incumbents Cielo and Getnet combined according to Brazilian press.
notes: Only source tying him to CloudWalk is MarketScreener's insider profile (marketscreener.com/insider/ARTHUR-MACEDO-A2AI8G), which also mentions a University of Notre Dame undergraduate link. Tried: English/Portuguese web searches, CloudWalk SEC Form D filings (2019, 2021; list only Luis Silva, James Aviles, Everson Lopes, Bruno Freitas), Wikipedia (en/pt credit only Luis Silva), Brazilian fintech press. Common name; don't use without checking his LinkedIn first.

name: Behzad Malek
current_role: Listed by Hurun as a founder of CloudWalk (São Paulo fintech); current role not verified
profile: Hurun's unicorn-founder lists (2022-2024) name Behzad Malek as a founder of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech founded in May 2013 and valued at about $2B, known for InfinitePay. CloudWalk now runs AI agents for small sellers (JIM, also in the US) and the Pierre finance app. His role could not be confirmed.
interesting_fact: CloudWalk pitches its products as AI agents: millions of Brazilian sellers use InfinitePay alongside JIM, an autonomous agent that handles payments, credit, storefronts and marketing, which CloudWalk calls one of the largest agentic deployments in commerce.
notes: Company facts verified; his founder role and bio not verified (web search quota exhausted; his name does not appear on CloudWalk's pages). Press email reaches CloudWalk, not necessarily him. Check LinkedIn manually.

name: Eliezer Pimentel
current_role: Co-founder, Quero 2 Pay (Franca, SP; payment terminals rebranded Monetix in 2024); co-founder and former executive director of CloudWalk. Current title unverified
profile: Eliézer Pimentel is a co-founder and former executive director of CloudWalk, the Brazilian payments fintech behind InfinitePay (valued at $2.15B in Nov 2021). After leaving, he backed and co-founded Quero 2 Pay with Gabriel Andrade in 2020, turning a pandemic-hit Franca ticketing startup into a card-machine fintech that processed R$1.5B in 18 months.
interesting_fact: Quero 2 Pay grew out of Quero 2 Ingressos, a ticketing startup whose revenue fell to zero when Covid hit. With Pimentel's backing it pivoted to payment terminals ('Queridona Smart') for small merchants, launching in April 2020 and reaching R$100m a month in volume within eight months.
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 he told Finsiders Brasil that Quero 2 Pay was 'designing a payment machine for the Metaverse' and planned to launch its own Q2 Bank, a striking ambition for a fintech from Franca, the interior São Paulo shoe-making city.
notes: CloudWalk co-founder status per startups.com.br ('cofundador e ex-diretor executivo da CloudWalk') and the MarketScreener founder list (Luis Silva, Arthur Macedo, Behzad Malek, Bruno Freitas, Eliezer Pimentel, 2013). Not on CloudWalk SEC Form D filings (2019/2021), and CloudWalk's own materials credit only Luis Silva as founder. No published personal contact found. Quero 2 Pay brand now Monetix (iDinheiro, 2025).

name: Luis Silva
current_role: Founder and CEO, CloudWalk (Brazilian fintech; owner of InfinitePay and JIM)
profile: Brazilian founder of CloudWalk, the AI- and blockchain-heavy payments company behind InfinitePay, which serves 4M+ small merchants in Brazil. CloudWalk reported US$497M revenue for 2024 with tripled net income, and says it passed US$1M revenue per employee thanks to 40+ in-house AI agents. Silva headlined Web Summit Rio 2025 on AI agents and AGI ethics.
interesting_fact: In 2025 CloudWalk raised its internal 'minimum wage' for analysts to R$7,000/month, crediting AI productivity gains; Silva said 'It's only fair that this gain is used to reward CloudWalk's employees.'
deep_cut_fact: CloudWalk's support team built an in-house AI agent named 'Claudio Walker' that handles about 90% of InfinitePay customer interactions with satisfaction comparable to human analysts.
notes: Very AI-forward and publicly vocal (Web Summit, Bloomberg Linea 100 Most Innovative 2024) - strong podcast candidate on AI-native operations. No press email found on CloudWalk's site; route via newsroom or his public talks.

name: John Lafleur
current_role: Co-founder & COO, Airbyte (San Francisco)
profile: French serial entrepreneur who co-founded Airbyte (2020, YC) with CEO Michel Tricot; the open-source data-integration/ELT platform reached a ~$1.5B valuation in 2021. Earlier ventures: As-App, StreamNation (acquired by SmugMug), CodinGame (COO/CEO) and Anaxi.
interesting_fact: Airbyte started in YC as Daxtarity, a marketing-data tool, and pivoted during COVID after customer interviews revealed teams were hand-building data pipelines.
deep_cut_fact: His entrepreneurial career began in 2008 with As-App, a ski-resort app later acquired by Lumiplan.

public_contacts.value: Joe Eckert, Eckert Communications - jeckert@eckertcomms.com (Airbyte media contact)

notes: Writes about developer marketing/open source; dev.to profile is his own blog, labelled substack type for lack of a better field.

name: Michel Tricot
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Airbyte (San Francisco)
profile: French data engineer who co-founded open-source data-integration company Airbyte in 2020 with John Lafleur (YC W20); Airbyte's connector platform became one of the most widely used ELT tools and was valued around $1.5B in 2021. Before that he was Head of Integrations/Director of Engineering at LiveRamp and a founding engineering leader at rideOS (later acquired by Gopuff).
interesting_fact: At LiveRamp he spent about seven years building and scaling more than 1,000 data connectors - the pain point that inspired Airbyte's open-source connector model.
deep_cut_fact: His data career began around 2008 as an R&D engineer handling financial data at FactSet in Paris; on YC's profile he says he has 'been working in data since 2007'.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (Airflow Summit, Percona Live, RAISE). Also a venture partner at Flex Capital (per profiles, unverified). Route via Airbyte.

name: Collin Chin
current_role: Co-founder, Aleo (zero-knowledge privacy L1 blockchain); led teams building developer tooling such as the Leo language and Aleo SDK
profile: Collin Chin co-founded Aleo in 2019 with Howard Wu, Raymond Chu and others. Aleo is a programmable privacy blockchain built on zero-knowledge proofs; a16z led its 2021 Series A. At Aleo, Chin worked on the developer stack, especially the Leo programming language for private applications.
interesting_fact: Leo, first released in 2020, was one of the first programming languages built specifically for zero-knowledge applications.
deep_cut_fact: He is first author of the 2021 IACR paper 'Leo: A Programming Language for Formally Verified, Zero-Knowledge Applications' (ePrint 2021/651), co-written with Howard Wu, Raymond Chu and formal-methods researchers Alessandro Coglio, Eric McCarthy and Eric Smith.
notes: Low public profile; Howard Wu is Aleo's main public voice. Aleo's author page for him now returns 404, so his current role is unclear. A good angle is the technical depth of the Leo language. I found no personal contact.

name: Howard Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Provable (an Aleo Labs company); co-founder of Aleo
profile: Cryptographer Howard Wu co-founded Aleo, a privacy-focused, zero-knowledge layer-1 blockchain, after research at UC Berkeley under Alessandro Chiesa and Dawn Song. He now leads Provable, which builds products for compliant, confidential payments and developer tools for deploying applications on Aleo.
interesting_fact: His Berkeley research, including the Zexe (Zero-Knowledge Executions) and DIZK papers, has been adopted by protocols such as Ethereum and Zcash.
deep_cut_fact: After Zexe was published, Vitalik Buterin asked him to launch it on Ethereum, and DeFi protocols such as Uniswap and Kyber wanted it for decentralized dark pools. That interest led him to take 'a leap of faith' and commercialize the research as Aleo. He calls cryptography 'a fundamental desire to define what trust means.'
notes: Frequent conference speaker (CoinDesk Consensus 2025 Hong Kong and Toronto). Aggregators differ on whether he is still Aleo CEO; Provable is his verified current role. Social links are company accounts, not personal.

name: Raymond Chu
current_role: Co-founder, Aleo (zero-knowledge privacy blockchain); described as an engineer on Aleo's core node software (snarkVM/snarkOS). Exact current title not verified.
profile: Raymond Chu co-founded Aleo Systems in December 2019 with Howard Wu, Michael Beller and Collin Chin. Aleo builds a layer-1 blockchain for private applications using zero-knowledge proofs, rooted in the Berkeley Zexe research, and is backed by investors including a16z. Mainnet launched in September 2024. Chu is an engineering co-founder rather than a public face.
interesting_fact: Aleo was created as 'the first platform for fully private applications', and its name stands for Autonomous Ledger Executions Off-chain. The design grew out of the Zexe zero-knowledge research at UC Berkeley.
deep_cut_fact: He is a hands-on engineer: GitHub shows Raymond Chu (handle raychu86) committing code to Aleo's trusted-setup ceremony software (AleoNet/aleo-setup) in November 2020, ahead of the network's launch.
notes: Very low media profile; Howard Wu (now CEO of Provable) is Aleo's public spokesperson. His commit email appears in git metadata, but it was not published as a contact and is deliberately excluded.

name: Deepika Bodapati
current_role: Co-founder of Athelas; COO of Commure (Athelas merged with Commure in Oct 2023)
profile: Co-founded Athelas with Tanay Tandon (Y Combinator), building the Athelas One, an FDA-cleared, internet-connected finger-prick device that measures white blood cell and neutrophil counts at home, and expanding into remote patient monitoring and revenue-cycle software. After Athelas merged with healthcare infrastructure firm Commure in 2023 she became COO of the combined company.
interesting_fact: Athelas One became key for schizophrenia patients on clozapine, who need regular white-cell monitoring; the work led to a partnership with clozapine maker HLS Therapeutics and deployments in California state hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Even as Athelas neared unicorn status she personally read every customer support ticket; persistent emails from Dr. Deanna Kelly of the Maryland Psychiatric Research Center led Bodapati to call her, opening the clozapine use case.
notes: Route via Commure/Athelas. No published press email found in this session.

name: Tanay Tandon
current_role: CEO, Commure (healthcare technology; merged with Athelas in Oct 2023)
profile: Silicon Valley founder with a machine-learning background who co-founded Athelas with Deepika Bodapati (YC S16), starting with an in-home blood-testing device and expanding into remote patient monitoring and revenue-cycle software. After Athelas merged with Commure in October 2023 he became CEO of the combined company, with Bodapati as COO; Commure now focuses on AI tools for health systems.
interesting_fact: During Athelas's first clinical trial in 2016 at a hospital in Juárez, Mexico, Tandon spotted a white blood cell count above 40,000 with immature cells - the patient was later confirmed to have leukemia.
deep_cut_fact: He and co-founder Deepika Bodapati met on the high-school science-fair circuit, first bonding on a flight to a competition; Athelas's first Mountain View office was 'a barely refurbished liquor store.'
notes: Speaks publicly (e.g. Slush 2024 with Initialized: https://blog.initialized.com/2024/11/supercharging-healthcare-with-tanay-tandon-at-slush-2024/). Hurun lists Athelas; the company now operates as Commure. No published press email found on commure.com.

name: Alan Chiu
current_role: Founder & CEO, Boba Network / Enya Labs (per 2022 sources; current status not re-verified)
profile: Alan Chiu co-founded Enya, a startup that took over the OMG Network project, an early Ethereum scaling effort. Under contract with the OMG Foundation, Enya's team built Boba Network, an Ethereum Layer-2 optimistic rollup with 'hybrid compute' (optional off-chain computation). Hurun lists Boba at a $2B peak valuation.
interesting_fact: He said Boba came from his frustration that early DeFi users profited while others were priced out by high gas fees: 'Seeing this inequality made me uneasy, and I was angry.'
notes: Aggregator profiles say he holds a Stanford MS in Management, was co-president of Stanford Angels & Entrepreneurs and is a partner at XSeed Capital. I could not verify these from primary pages. The crypto-industry profile and 2022 interview (crypto @ Stanford) are the best context. I did not verify his current activity in 2026.

name: Diogo Frenkel
current_role: Co-founder and CFO, Dock (Brazilian payments/banking-infrastructure company, formerly Conductor) - title as of 2021; current status not confirmed
profile: Brazilian fintech executive listed as co-founder and CFO of Dock, the Sao Paulo-area payments and banking-as-a-service provider that grew out of card processor Conductor (founded 1999). In 2021 Conductor, Dock and Muxi were unified under the Dock brand; Dock reached unicorn status in 2022 (~$1.5B) and serves 400+ companies in 11 Latin American countries.
interesting_fact: Dock started as an in-house project inside card processor Conductor in 2018; it became the name for the whole company in 2021 because it was the only pillar built entirely in-house, and in 2023 Dock became a Central Bank of Brazil-regulated institution.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal bio or post-2021 coverage found. CEO Antonio Soares is Dock's spokesperson. Sources conflict on founding history (Conductor 1999 vs Dock 2014/2018). Portuguese-language outreach via Dock press room recommended.

name: Frederico Amaral
current_role: Founder & CEO, Lerian (São Paulo); co-founder and former Chief Product & Technology Officer of Dock
profile: Fred Amaral co-founded Brazilian payments and banking-as-a-service infrastructure firm Dock, which became a unicorn, and served as its Chief Product & Technology Officer. He left to found Lerian with his own capital in 2023; it builds Midaz, a source-available core-banking ledger, and raised an R$18M seed led by Maya Capital in 2024 plus a further round reported in 2026.
interesting_fact: With Lerian he is betting that core banking goes open: Midaz's code is public and Lerian plans to earn mainly from hosting and add-on features, building a developer community through developer advocacy and workshops.
deep_cut_fact: He personally pitched Midaz to Brazil's developer community on TabNews, the Brazilian dev forum, in posts like 'Midaz: open source banking ledger com múltiplos conectores'.
notes: Goes by 'Fred Amaral'. Lerian email is the company's general contact, not personal. Aggregator profiles mention earlier stints at Uber, Deutsche Bank, BTG Pactual and Movile (unverified).

name: Marcelo Jacques
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer, Dock (Brazilian payments & banking-as-a-service platform, formerly Conductor) - title as of 2020-2021; not re-confirmed for 2026
profile: Brazilian fintech executive and former investment banker (TMT coverage) who serves as Chief Strategy Officer of Dock, the São Paulo paytech formed when Conductor unified Conductor, Dock and Muxi under one brand in 2021. Dock provides card processing, digital accounts and BaaS infrastructure to 200+ companies across Latin America.
interesting_fact: In 2020 Conductor said it processed more than R$10B in monthly transactions across 100M customer accounts while staying profitable; Jacques: 'we always look for the correct balance between growth and profitability.'
notes: Low public profile; CEO Antonio Soares is Dock's main public face. Press room lists both an in-house inbox and an agency inbox.

name: Brad Siegler
current_role: Co-founder and shareholder, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT); current operating role not confirmed
profile: Missouri-based co-founder of EquipmentShare, the Columbia, Missouri construction-equipment rental and fleet-technology company started by brothers Willy and Jabbok Schlacks with Siegler, Jeff Lowe and Matthew McDonald. Backed early by Y Combinator (2015), EquipmentShare went public on Nasdaq in January 2026; Siegler was listed as a shareholder in the IPO prospectus.
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare grew out of a 2014 Startup Weekend in Columbia, Missouri, where the Schlacks brothers won first place and $2,000; by 2021 it had about 3,000 employees and 90+ locations.
deep_cut_fact: When EquipmentShare went through Y Combinator in 2015, TechCrunch pitched it as 'Airbnb for construction equipment', a peer-to-peer marketplace letting contractors rent idle gear from one another; Siegler was one of three Missouri-area co-founders who joined the Schlacks brothers.
notes: Low public profile. Shareholding confirmed in the 424B4 prospectus (Jan 2026): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1693736/000162828026003334/eqpt-424b4.htm . Wellfound describes him as a UI/UX/web designer and Univ. of Missouri '13 grad (unverified primary).

name: Jeff Lowe
current_role: Co-founder of EquipmentShare (no longer in an active role, per Contrary Research)
profile: Jeffrey Lowe is one of five co-founders of EquipmentShare, founded in Columbia, Missouri in 2015 with brothers Willy and Jabbok Schlacks, Brad Siegler and Matthew McDonald. EquipmentShare grew from a Startup Weekend-winning contractor equipment-sharing idea into a national construction equipment rental and telematics (T3) platform that filed to go public (S-1/A, Jan 2026, ticker EQPT).
interesting_fact: EquipmentShare's idea won first place and $2,000 at a 2014 Startup Weekend in Columbia, Missouri; the company now has thousands of employees and files with the SEC as EquipmentShare.com Inc (EQPT).
notes: Very low public profile; Contrary Research says the Schlacks brothers are the only founders still active at the company, and Lowe is not named in the Jan 2026 S-1/A. Common name (do not confuse with the 'Tiger King' Jeff Lowe). An aggregator claims prior work as a freelance web designer and partner at Lowe Constructing (unverified). No contact found. Source: https://research.contrary.com/company/equipmentshare

name: Matthew McDonald
current_role: Co-founder and founding CTO, EquipmentShare (Nasdaq: EQPT). He stepped back from the CTO seat to an engineering role by 2019; current title not confirmed.
profile: Matthew McDonald is EquipmentShare's technology co-founder. At a Columbia, Missouri Startup Weekend he met the contractors behind the idea, built a prototype and booked a skid-loader rental the same weekend. The team went through Y Combinator, and EquipmentShare grew into a national construction-equipment rental and telematics company that IPO'd on Nasdaq in January 2026 at about a $6B valuation.
interesting_fact: Former co-worker Wade Foster, who went on to co-found Zapier, talked the team into applying to Y Combinator. McDonald admits he first dismissed YC as 'something for Silicon Valley people'.
deep_cut_fact: As founding CTO he grew the engineering team to 11, then with a mentor's help realised he did not enjoy the leadership seat and handed it over. His engineering team was remote from day one because his wife had just taken a job in Maine.
notes: The SEC filing names only the Schlacks brothers as co-founders, while Startland News lists McDonald among the co-founders (with Brad Siegler and Jeff Lowe). Low profile; his current role at EquipmentShare is unknown. IPO details (23 Jan 2026, $24.50/share, about $6B) come from search snippets of RER/IPOScoop.

name: Wang Shunbo
current_role: Founder, Chairman and General Manager, Forehope Electronic (Ningbo) Co., Ltd (688362.SH)
profile: Chip-packaging veteran (b. 1978) who founded Forehope Electronic in Yuyao, Ningbo in November 2017 and has chaired it since, adding the general-manager role in 2019. Forehope does integrated-circuit packaging and testing, and listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in November 2022, about five years after its founding.
interesting_fact: Forehope went from incorporation (Nov 2017) to a STAR Market IPO (Nov 2022) in five years, after Hurun had already valued it at $2bn as a unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: He spent a decade (2001-2011) as an engineer at ASE's Shanghai packaging-and-test plant, then ran the integrated-circuit business centre at JCET (Jiangsu Changjiang Electronics Technology) before leaving in 2017 to start Forehope - so he learned the trade at two of the world's largest chip packaging-and-test (OSAT) groups.
notes: Advanced packaging is a hot AI/data-center supply-chain topic, so a good fit. IR email is the securities-department mailbox. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Xi Gang
current_role: Chairman, New Hope Dairy (新乳业, SZSE 002946); President of Caogen Zhiben (草根知本); Chairman of Xianshenghuo cold chain (Fresh-SCM)
profile: Xi Gang (席刚) is a New Hope Group veteran of 25+ years who has led New Hope Dairy since joining it in 2004. He built it through acquisitions into a 'fleet' of regional fresh-milk brands focused on low-temperature milk, and in 2026 the company was preparing a Hong Kong H-share listing. As president of New Hope's consumer investment platform Caogen Zhiben, he chairs Chengdu cold-chain logistics firm Xianshenghuo (Fresh-SCM). It was founded in 2016 and reportedly valued at RMB 10B after its 2022 Series B.
interesting_fact: New Hope Dairy deliberately chose fresh low-temperature milk to avoid Yili and Mengniu's strength in shelf-stable milk. Its flagship '24-hour' fresh milk is sold only on the day it ships, with no more than 24 hours on the shelf.
deep_cut_fact: He jokes that he is New Hope Group's 'dingzihu' (holdout): of the 20-plus university graduates who joined with him, he was the only one who stayed. He also says he had never worked in dairy and called himself a dairy 'outsider' when he took over New Hope Dairy in 2004.

public_contacts.value: nhdzqb@newhope.cn (New Hope Dairy board office / securities dept)

notes: Identity 'uncertain' only because the input calls him 'founder' of Fresh-SCM. Sources (36Kr) list Xi Gang (席刚) as chairman of Xianshenghuo/Fresh-SCM, which was incubated by New Hope's Caogen Zhiben, and its legal rep is Sun Xiaoyu. This is very likely the right person. Chairman role confirmed in New Hope Dairy's March 2026 board notice (https://static.cninfo.com.cn/finalpage/2026-03-12/1225005444.PDF). Relevant to a cold-chain/logistics angle.

name: Cheng Haotian
current_role: Founder and CEO, Gausium (formerly Gaussian Robotics / 高仙机器人), Shanghai
profile: Cheng Haotian (程昊天, known in English as Edward Cheng) is a Cambridge-educated (2009) robotics engineer who founded Gaussian Robotics in 2013, now Gausium. It makes SLAM-based autonomous commercial cleaning robots used in 70+ countries. Gausium, described as China's first profitable cleaning-robot maker, said in 2025 it was planning a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: IDC's 2025 tracker ranked Gausium the world's No.1 commercial cleaning-robot supplier by both shipments and revenue; in 2025 Cheng targeted selling 20,000 cleaning robots, up 40-50% year on year.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Gaussian, he worked at the Shanghai World Expo Coordination Bureau, where he led the project approval, technical planning and implementation of the 2010 Shanghai Expo's 'Haibao' robot and its full performance and exhibition program.
notes: Goes by Edward Cheng in English media, e.g. The Standard (HK), May 2025, on the IPO plan. Hurun lists the company as 'Gaussian'. No published press email found.

name: Ilana Harkavi
current_role: Original founder of Il Makiage (1972); no current role found
profile: New York-based makeup artist who founded the Il Makiage cosmetics brand in 1972; it was known mainly among professional makeup artists. The brand was later bought by siblings Oran Holtzman and Shiran Holtzman-Erel, who relaunched it in 2018 as a digital-first, AI-driven brand under parent ODDITY (Nasdaq IPO 2023). No evidence found that she holds equity or a role in today's ODDITY.
interesting_fact: The brand name is an intentionally simplified spelling of the French word 'maquillage' (makeup).
deep_cut_fact: Under her, Il Makiage was known in professional circles for innovations such as windowed eyeshadow packaging.
notes: Likely a list mis-attribution: the $1-2B valuation reflects the post-2018 Holtzman relaunch (ODDITY), not the original founder. Almost no public information on her; alive status unknown. Consider Oran Holtzman (ODDITY CEO) instead if the goal is the unicorn's founder.

name: Shiran Holtzman Erel
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Product Officer and board member, ODDITY Tech (NASDAQ: ODD; IL MAKIAGE, SpoiledChild)
profile: Shiran Holtzman Erel co-founded ODDITY with her brother, CEO Oran Holtzman. ODDITY is an Israeli-American, AI- and data-driven beauty and wellness company that owns IL MAKIAGE and SpoiledChild and listed on Nasdaq in 2023. She has been Chief Product Officer since inception and joined the board in November 2022.
interesting_fact: In 2013 she and her brother bought the struggling IL MAKIAGE brand out of receivership for NIS 12M plus NIS 80M of assumed debt, and turned it into a billion-dollar online beauty brand.
deep_cut_fact: She told Calcalist in 2020: 'In Israel, we're a proud retail player; in the U.S., we're 100% online.' This describes IL MAKIAGE's dual model of physical stores at home and a pure-online US business.
notes: Her brother Oran is the public face; she rarely gives interviews. ODDITY runs a biotech lab in Boston (ODDITY LABS) and an R&D centre in Tel Aviv, which could be an AI/data angle. Route through press@oddity.com.

name: Aron Schwarzkopf
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Kushki (Latin American payments infrastructure)
profile: Ecuadorian entrepreneur raised in Quito, educated at Babson College (also Singularity University and CUHK), now Miami-based. deep_cut_fact: As a child she loved numbers so much she memorized license plates and phone numbers, and her favourite game was Monopoly; she became a Citi country manager by age 29.
notes: No longer at Kushki (2016-2022). No published email or verified own website found; LinkedIn (ec.linkedin.com/in/daespinosa) appears in search but was not verified as hers. Speaks at South Summit Madrid; Spanish-language outreach likely best.

name: Aaron Matos
current_role: Founder of Paradox (conversational-AI recruiting, Scottsdale, AZ); handed CEO role to Adam Godson in March 2024; Paradox now part of Workday
profile: Aaron Matos launched Paradox in 2016 in Scottsdale, AZ, building 'Olivia', a conversational AI assistant that screens and schedules candidates by text for employers like Chipotle, 7-Eleven, GM and Nestle. name: Doron Myersdorf
current_role: CEO and Co-Founder, StoreDot (Herzliya, Israel)
profile: Israeli engineer (DSc, Technion) who co-founded StoreDot in 2012 to develop extreme-fast-charging (XFC) lithium-ion batteries; backers include Daimler, BP, Samsung, TDK, VinFast and Polestar. Its silicon-dominant XFC cells have been validated by seven OEMs; in 2026 the company is pivoting to licensing deals and says it is preparing for the public markets. It also pitches XFC to data-center operators.
interesting_fact: StoreDot's earliest tech grew out of peptide 'nano-dot' research linked to Alzheimer's studies (Prof. Ehud Gazit's peptide nanocrystals) - the 'dots' still in the company's name - and it demonstrated a 30-second full phone charge in 2014.
deep_cut_fact: Before StoreDot he founded and led SanDisk's SSD business unit, growing it to $100M+ in under three years, and earlier was VP Flash & Operations at Israeli flash pioneer M-Systems; his motto: 'everything is possible, if you approach it with pure credulity.'
notes: Talkative founder, good energy-storage guest; company now markets XFC to data-center operators too. Some press (per Wikipedia, Feb 2026) questions StoreDot's runway and long commercialization timeline - handle tactfully.

name: Gil Rosenman
current_role: Co-founder, StoreDot (Herzliya, Israel); current operational role not verified
profile: Gil Rosenman co-founded StoreDot in 2012 with Doron Myersdorf and Simon Litsyn. It began with peptide-based displays and storage built on Tel Aviv University research by Ehud Gazit, then pivoted to extreme-fast-charging EV batteries, backed by BP, Daimler, Samsung, TDK, Polestar and VinFast; it was valued at $1.5B in 2022.
interesting_fact: StoreDot started out not in batteries but in bio-organic 'peptide' nanocrystals for phone displays and memory, before becoming known for EV cells designed to add about 100 miles of range in 5 minutes of charging.
notes: Low public profile; StoreDot is fronted by CEO Doron Myersdorf. Sensitive timing: per 2026 press, StoreDot's SPAC deal was cancelled and it is seeking new funding - avoid raising this. Rosenman is widely described as a Tel Aviv University physics/engineering academic, but that was not verified here (web-search budget exhausted).

name: Simon Litsyn
current_role: Co-founder, Chief Strategy Officer and director, StoreDot (Herzliya); Professor Emeritus of Electrical Engineering, Tel Aviv University
profile: Soviet-trained electrical engineer (PhD, LETI Leningrad 1982) and Tel Aviv University professor since 1991 who was chief scientist at M-Systems/SanDisk (1999-2012). In 2012 he co-founded StoreDot, developer of extreme-fast-charging silicon-based EV batteries backed by BP, Daimler, Samsung and Polestar. He also consults on second-life battery storage (Sparkion).
interesting_fact: At M-Systems his signal-processing techniques raised flash storage density and helped make the DiskOnKey - the original USB flash drive - possible; his x4 NAND technology was a key reason SanDisk bought M-Systems for $1.6B in 2006.
deep_cut_fact: In 2015 he shared the IEEE Reynold B. Johnson Storage Systems Award and Medal with Dov Moran and Amir Ban for pioneering flash-memory storage; he was SanDisk's Engineering Fellow (its top technical title) and holds 60+ patents.
notes: Email is his Tel Aviv University faculty address as published by the university (academic, not company). Per Wikipedia, financial journalists reported in Feb 2026 that StoreDot had limited runway and needed more development time, so be tactful about the company's status. Strong energy-storage podcast guest given his flash-memory and battery background.

name: Ham Serunjogi
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Chipper Cash (Critical Ideas, Inc.), San Francisco / Africa
profile: Ugandan entrepreneur (b. 1993) who studied economics at Grinnell College on scholarship, worked at Facebook/Meta in Dublin, then in 2018 co-founded Chipper Cash with Grinnell classmate Maijid Moujaled. Chipper offers cross-border payments across Africa and the US; it raised $300M+ from Ribbit, Bezos Expeditions, SVB Capital and others, reaching unicorn status in 2021. He was named to Biden's Advisory Council on African Diaspora Engagement in 2023.

deep_cut_fact: Before tech he was a competitive swimmer: he represented Uganda in swimming at the 2010 Youth Olympic Games in Singapore and later swam for Grinnell College. At Grinnell he also co-built an app for sending short, encrypted voice recordings.

profile: Maijid Moujaled co-founded Chipper Cash with CEO Ham Serunjogi. Chipper Cash is a fintech app for cross-border payments across Africa, with operations in markets including Nigeria, Ghana, Rwanda, Uganda and the US. It was valued at over $1B, and he serves as its president.

He previously co-founded Fluidic Energy (now NantEnergy), which built rechargeable zinc-air batteries for off-grid power and raised over $150M.

deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Arizona, and the Lemelson-MIT profile credits the state's farmland and desert, including irrigation canals built by Native Americans, with sparking his early interest in science and environmental technology.
notes: Strong fit for an energy/water-tech podcast: deep background in batteries and off-grid power. Henry Crown Fellow (Aspen Institute). ASU faculty channels and SOURCE's website are the routes; no published press email found. 2025-26 status not checked because the search budget ran out.

interesting_fact: RIDI first tried producing comics with dozens of hired artists, then pivoted to e-books because text only needed digitizing; despite skeptical publishers, he had deals with about 200 publishers by 2011.

notes: RIDI was selected for the Tokyo Stock Exchange Asia Startup Hub in 2024 and 2025 (https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2025092908590212822). No published press email found.

name: Mike Moreno
current_role: Co-founder, Route (Lehi, Utah post-purchase / package-protection platform); listed as VP
profile: Mike Moreno co-founded Route with Evan Walker. The Utah company launched in January 2019 and sells package protection, visual order tracking and post-purchase tools to e-commerce merchants. Forbes listed it among the 'next billion-dollar startups', and it later raised a Series C at a reported $1.4B valuation. Data providers list Moreno as co-founder/VP.
interesting_fact: Forbes's list of startups most likely to become unicorns named Mike Moreno and Evan Walker as Route's founders, citing $91M raised and estimated 2020 revenue of $34M.
notes: Very low public profile. Most press coverage features co-founder Evan Walker. A 2025 profile says Eric Kobe is now CEO (not verified). LinkedIn is likely the best route.

name: Brian Denker
current_role: Cofounder and longtime COO, Tackle.io (Boise), acquired by AppDirect (announced Dec 2025); current post-deal role unconfirmed
profile: Idaho-rooted cloud entrepreneur who cofounded Tackle.io in 2016 with longtime friend Dillon Woods after years working in cloud computing since AWS's 2006 launch. Tackle helps software vendors sell through AWS, Microsoft and Google Cloud marketplaces, became a $1B+ unicorn, and agreed to be acquired by AppDirect in December 2025.
interesting_fact: Tackle's platform supports over $20 billion in cloud hyperscaler marketplace transactions, per AppDirect.
deep_cut_fact: Tackle began with just him and Dillon Woods 'hacking away in a shared office above Goldy's in downtown Boise'; New Relic became their 'lighthouse customer'. He splits his time between Boise, Riggins (Idaho) and Boston.
notes: Outdoorsy, Idaho-proud founder; friends with cofounder Dillon Woods since the early 2000s. Riggins/Boston detail is from Tackle's company page (via search). No published personal or press email found; post-acquisition role unclear.

name: Dillon Woods
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Tackle.io (Boise, ID) - acquired by AppDirect in Dec 2025; post-acquisition role not confirmed
profile: Idaho native and Boise State CS grad (2005) who spent a decade at California data companies (CTO at zData and Alpine Data) before co-founding Tackle.io in Boise in 2016. Tackle helps software vendors sell through AWS/Azure/Google Cloud marketplaces; it raised ~$148m and was acquired by AppDirect in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: Tackle turned cloud-hyperscaler marketplaces into a sales channel for SaaS vendors and became a Boise-born unicorn; AppDirect bought it in Dec 2025 to add native hyperscaler-marketplace integration to its B2B subscription-commerce platform.
deep_cut_fact: He minored in philosophy at Boise State and was already 'playing around with starting companies' as a student; Tackle's official HQ sits in downtown Boise above Goldy's, about 50 feet from Boise State's computer-science department at City Central Plaza. His advice: 'solve a problem that you actually have.'
notes: Hurun lists him as founder; John Jahnke was Tackle's CEO. Since the AppDirect acquisition, press goes through AppDirect's PR agency (Bospar). Cloud-marketplace angle rather than energy/data-center hardware.

name: Avi Meir
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Perk (formerly TravelPerk)
profile: Serial founder who co-founded Hotel Ninjas (sold to Booking.com in 2014) and then founded TravelPerk in Barcelona in 2015 to bring consumer-grade tech to business travel. Rebranded Perk in Nov 2025 as an AI-native travel and spend platform, it passed $300M annualized revenue with 10,000+ customer companies and moved to dual HQs in London and Boston.
interesting_fact: When COVID made business travel effectively illegal in early 2020, Meir cut costs without layoffs, kept hiring engineers and bought two competitors cheaply; ARR went from ~$20M pre-pandemic to over $300M.
deep_cut_fact: He likens his pandemic playbook to a hibernating bear ('preserve the core, lose the fat'), and says the lesson he took from Booking.com after selling Hotel Ninjas was that 'winning globally means building locally.'
notes: Rebrand announced Nov 4, 2025 (https://www.perk.com/press-release/travelperk-rebrands-to-perk-the-intelligent-platform-powering-real-work/). Talkative, candid interviewee; IPO talk in recent coverage.

name: Javier Suarez
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Oliva (workplace mental health platform); co-founder and former CPO of TravelPerk (now Perk)
profile: Javier Suarez co-founded Barcelona-based business travel platform TravelPerk in 2015 with Avi Meir and Ron Levin, serving as chief product officer; it later reached a multi-billion-dollar valuation. In 2020 he co-founded Oliva with Sancar Sahin, an employee wellbeing platform offering therapy and workshops used in 27+ countries and 14 languages, backed by Molten Ventures and Stride VC.
interesting_fact: TravelPerk was born from an observation at Booking.com: the founders, both ex-Booking employees, saw that the company focused on leisure travel while business travel was a poorly served market.
deep_cut_fact: Before TravelPerk he worked at Booking.com in business development; his co-founder Avi Meir had joined Booking when it acquired Meir's startup Hotel Ninjas in 2014.
notes: Now focused on Oliva (CEO). He has spoken publicly about founder burnout as Oliva's origin; let him lead on that topic. Sources differ on his Booking.com role (product performance & innovation vs business development). No published press email found.

name: Ron Levin
current_role: Co-founder of Perk (formerly TravelPerk); originally its CTO - current position not confirmed by a primary source
profile: Technologist who co-founded TravelPerk in 2015 with Avi Meir and Javier Suarez, leading engineering as CTO. The company, now called Perk, is a travel and spend-management platform with dual HQ in Boston and London and a large Barcelona hub; a 2025 Series E ($200M) valued it at about $2.7B.
interesting_fact: Perk raised $409M through its 2022 Series D to reach unicorn status; in January 2025 it raised a $200M Series E led by Atomico (valuing it at $2.7B) and acquired Zurich-based spend-management platform Yokoy.
notes: Very low public profile. A 2025 Perk press release reportedly names Robin Smith as CTO, so Levin may have stepped back from the role; an aggregator claims he is now at a VC firm but this is unverified. Perk press office is the published route.

name: Tian Ye
profile: Could not identify a 'Tian Ye' (田野?) who founded a semiconductor company called 'Xinxin'. The most plausible company is Xinxin Semiconductor (鑫芯半导体, Xuzhou), a 12-inch silicon-wafer maker founded 2017 that raised RMB1.79bn in a July 2022 Series B (fits a one-year 2022 Hurun listing). TCL Zhonghuan's Zhonghuan Leading acquired it in 2023 for RMB7.757bn in equity. Its legal rep is Wang Yanjun (王彦君); no link to Tian Ye was found.
