name: Lyu Shijie
profile: Could not tie anyone named Lyu Shijie (吕仕杰/吕世杰?) to Cloudwise (云智慧), the Beijing AIOps/IT-operations software company founded in 2009. It raised a $150M Series E led by Sequoia China in July 2021. Public sources name Yin Jin (殷晋) as founder and CEO; he holds about 92% of the onshore operating entity.
notes: Tried: Chinese searches (云智慧 + 吕仕杰/吕世杰/吕 + 创始人/CTO/总裁), exact-name search for 吕仕杰, English Cloudwise founder searches, 36Kr company profile (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/1678266129003528: team lists only 殷晋; legal rep 夏婧雯), cloudwise.com (unreachable). Overseas databases name founders 'Andy Yin and Bin Tan'; a 2021 release names David Liu as president. Hurun's name may be wrong; Yin Jin is the better-documented founder.

name: Ricardo Amper
current_role: Founder and CEO, Incode Technologies
profile: Mexico City-born serial entrepreneur who founded and sold two earlier companies (one in food, one in chemicals) before moving to the Bay Area in 2015 to start Incode. Incode began as a face-recognition photo-sharing app and pivoted to AI-based identity verification and fraud prevention for banks, fintechs and governments; it was valued at about $1.25B in 2021.
interesting_fact: Incode's origins are in consumer photos: its first app automatically shared pictures with whoever face recognition detected in them, and wrestling with bad, low-light phone photos shaped its later identity-verification tech for low-end phones in Latin America.
deep_cut_fact: Apple took Incode's early photo-sharing app on a roadshow as one of three companies showcasing its on-device machine-learning framework, but the app 'couldn't get traction', prompting the pivot into identity verification.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (e.g. Money20/20) and interviewee; contact@incode.com is the company's general address. Has an active media presence, so a podcast pitch on AI/deepfake fraud is plausible.

name: Brian Barlow
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (SIP)
profile: Infrastructure investor with three decades in private markets who led infrastructure investing for Alphabet's urban-innovation arm (Sidewalk Labs), then co-founded SIP, spun out of Alphabet in 2020 with about $400M. SIP builds energy and digital infrastructure businesses, including Verrus (flexible, grid-friendly data centers) and Everyday Electric (residential virtual power plants).
interesting_fact: SIP's portfolio sits right at the AI-power nexus: Verrus builds next-generation flexible data centers, and Everyday Electric (formerly Renew Home) aggregates millions of homes into virtual power plants and acquired Smartcar to add EVs to its VPP.
deep_cut_fact: Earlier in his career he was a senior member of Scion Capital, Michael Burry's hedge fund made famous by 'The Big Short', and he was a managing director at American Infrastructure Funds before joining Alphabet.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy/data-center podcast. Did a GrowthCap podcast interview (June 2026) on AI infrastructure. Co-founded SIP with Jonathan Winer (Fortune, 2020: https://fortune.com/2020/05/07/alphabet-vets-infrastructure-funding-400-million/). Best route: press@sidewalkinfra.com.

name: Jonathan Winer
current_role: Co-founder and former co-CEO, Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (no longer on SIP's team page, which lists Brian Barlow as Co-Founder and CEO). Current role unknown.
profile: Jonathan Winer is a former Alphabet/Sidewalk Labs executive who co-founded Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners (SIP) with Brian Barlow. SIP spun out of Alphabet in 2020 with a $400M Series A from Alphabet and Ontario Teachers'. It builds tech-enabled infrastructure platforms, and its current companies include Verrus (flexible, grid-friendly data centers) and Everyday Electric (residential virtual power plants).
interesting_fact: SIP's portfolio sits squarely in the energy and data-center space: Verrus builds next-generation data centers designed for flexibility, and Everyday Electric aggregates millions of households into virtual power plants.
deep_cut_fact: In SIP's first-ever interview (Fortune, May 2020) Winer pitched it as building 'unglamorous but sorely needed' infrastructure such as recycling sorting plants, consulting mayors rather than lobbying: 'We're not trying to sell our widgets.'

public_contacts.value: Guest on HASI 'Climate Positive' podcast E43 (March 2023)

notes: Highly relevant to energy and data-center themes (Verrus, VPPs). As of this check he is NOT listed on SIP's team page, so he has likely left SIP, and his new activity was not found; verify before outreach. Aggregators say he founded Nereus Capital, a private-equity firm, in 2010 (not verified here).

name: Michael Delucia
current_role: Partner, Montauk Capital (NY 'Electron Economy' venture capital and venture studio); adjunct faculty, NYU School of Professional Studies
profile: Infrastructure investor (Brown; JPMorgan banking) with 18+ years in project finance: early wind/solar IPP lending at HSH Nordbank, Nereus Capital, and power-project financing at Macquarie Energy. He joined Alphabet's Sidewalk Labs, then the founding team of spin-out Sidewalk Infrastructure Partners, which Hurun counts as a $1B unicorn. Later at Wellington's Climate Innovation Fund, now at Montauk.
interesting_fact: Montauk Capital, where he is a partner, backs the 'Electron Economy'. Its portfolio includes a home energy storage and power retailer, an enhanced-geothermal developer, an off-grid data-center development platform, AI-powered ERP for industrials and data centers, and AI tools for large-load grid interconnection.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career at HSH Nordbank he was an early investor and financier in some of the first wind and solar independent power producers in North America. At Wellington's Climate Innovation Fund he led investments in grid-enhancing technologies.
notes: The 'founder' label is loose: SIP's co-founders are Jonathan Winer and Brian Barlow, and DeLucia was on the founding team (Principal 2019-21, Partner 2021-22). He is not a UHNW founder and has no meaningful personal SIP valuation. Still a highly relevant energy/data-center infrastructure guest and likely approachable.

name: David Leiberman
current_role: Co-founder of Triller, Mibblio and Console; co-founder of The Lorca (hospitality retreats, self-described). Current day-to-day role unclear.
profile: New York musician, teacher and app builder. He co-founded children's music-app maker Mibblio and then, with his cousin Sammy Rubin, Triller, the AI-powered music-video app (founded around 2015) that later attracted celebrity investors and a reported $1B+ valuation. He later co-founded Console, a Web3 Discord-style community platform, with Chris Castig.
interesting_fact: Triller started as a family project: he co-founded it with his cousin Sammy Rubin, after the two had built Mibblio, a music-making app for toddlers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Triller he helped create the Disney Frozen Karaoke app. He describes himself as a teacher and musician, and also co-founded The Lorca, a contemporary retreat in the Catskills plus a midcentury motel in the Adirondacks.
notes: No longer prominent at Triller. Avoid Triller's later corporate/financial troubles in outreach. Facts come mostly from his self-written Product Hunt profile. The Lorca's site appears to be thelorca.com, but I could not confirm his link to it independently.

name: Sammy Rubin
current_role: Co-founder of Triller (current role not found)
profile: New York app developer who, with collaborator David Leiberman, created the kids' music platform Mibblio and the chart-topping 'Disney Frozen: Karaoke' app, then launched Triller in July 2015 with music-video director Colin Tilley. Triller began as an AI auto-editing music-video app and later became a TikTok rival under new owners. His current activities are not publicly documented.
interesting_fact: Triller launched in July 2015 as a collaboration with director Colin Tilley (known for videos for Kendrick Lamar, Justin Bieber and Nicki Minaj). Its auto-editing tech assembled several takes into a finished music video.
deep_cut_fact: Before Triller, he and Leiberman built Mibblio, a children's music-book app platform, and the chart-topping 'Disney Frozen: Karaoke' app.
notes: Do not confuse him with UK insurtech founder Sammy Rubin (YuLife, PruProtect), who is a different person; aggregators such as MarketScreener conflate the two. The Triller co-founder keeps a very low profile. Triller (later TrillerNet) went through ownership changes and turmoil, so avoid that topic. No published contact found.

name: Jenn Knight
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, AgentSync (per company/podcast materials; latest title not re-verified in 2026)
profile: Salesforce-ecosystem engineer who co-founded Denver-based insurtech AgentSync in 2018 with Niji Sabharwal after building back-office systems at LinkedIn, Dropbox and Stripe. AgentSync automates producer licensing and compliance for insurers; it bootstrapped before raising from Craft Ventures and others and reached a $1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: AgentSync bootstrapped to early product-market fit and only began pitching VCs in March 2020; investors initially said insurance's $1.3 trillion market was 'not cool enough.'
deep_cut_fact: Without a CS degree, she began her tech career as LinkedIn's first Salesforce engineer, building its Salesforce engineering and solutions-architecture team; at Dropbox she migrated the company's ERP before its IPO, and earlier did consulting at Bluewolf.
notes: Has done many podcasts (FNO InsureTech ep. 275, The SaaS Podcast #426) - receptive to podcast appearances. No dedicated press email published; company newsroom at agentsync.io/newsroom.

name: Niranjan Sabharwal
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Board Chair, AgentSync (Denver)
profile: Niranjan 'Niji' Sabharwal co-founded AgentSync in 2018 with his wife Jenn Knight, the company's CTO. AgentSync makes insurance producer licensing and compliance software for carriers, agencies, MGAs and insurtechs and became a unicorn in 2021. He was previously CEO and now serves as executive board chair.
interesting_fact: AgentSync grew out of his job fixing Zenefits' agent-licensing compliance crisis. After Zenefits exited insurance, it licensed the intellectual property to him, and that became AgentSync.
deep_cut_fact: Before Zenefits he led sales strategy and operations at LinkedIn. At Zenefits he led the producer licensing and broker compliance response team.
notes: The AgentSync site publishes only sales@ and support@ emails, with no press address. Use the contact form or newsroom (https://agentsync.io/newsroom). Goes by 'Niji'.

name: Assaf Resnick
current_role: Co-Founder and CEO, BigPanda (agentic AI for IT operations / AIOps)
profile: UC Berkeley Haas graduate who started at Moody's on Wall Street, then invested for Sequoia Capital (Israel) before co-founding BigPanda in 2012 with Elik Eizenberg. BigPanda, a unicorn, correlates IT monitoring alerts and automates incident response; in 2025-26 it repositioned around 'agentic ITOps' and an IT knowledge graph.
interesting_fact: He got the idea for BigPanda while at Sequoia, where he saw that as companies moved to the cloud, IT Ops teams were overwhelmed by alert noise from fragmented monitoring tools.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he began his career on Wall Street at Moody's. He says he left to 'marry my passion for tech with my background in investments', and that the 'courage and conviction' of Sequoia's founders inspired him to start BigPanda.

public_contacts.value: jbarbour@bigpanda.io (Jenne Barbour, Head of Corporate Marketing, listed as BigPanda contact on July 2026 release)

notes: Active speaker in 2026 (Emerj AI in Business podcast, July 2026; BigPanda 26 keynote, Atlanta, April 2026). Earlier 2026 releases list Adam Blau (VP Product Marketing) as media contact. bigpanda.io blocked automated fetches (403), so the leadership-page URL is from search results. Data-center angle: IT ops reliability and incident automation.

name: Elik Eizenberg
current_role: Founder and CEO, Scroll AI (AI 'mentor' for employees); co-founder and former CTO, BigPanda
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded BigPanda (AIOps / IT incident intelligence, backed by Sequoia) in 2012 with Assaf Resnick and served as CTO as it reached unicorn status. He has since founded Scroll AI, focused on reliable, ethical AI that acts as a trusted partner to human leaders.
interesting_fact: He describes 25 years of deploying mission-critical AI across finance, operations and security, and frames his mission around 'the humanist side of technology'.
deep_cut_fact: Before BigPanda he led development of highly scalable data pipelines in the Israeli intelligence service, then designed autonomous trading algorithms for a hedge fund - experiences that made him sceptical of ML vendor hype.
notes: Name sometimes spelled 'Eisenberg'. No published contact email found for Scroll AI; LinkedIn or Scroll's site are likely routes.

name: Conway Teng
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, CaptivateIQ (San Francisco)
profile: Former McKinsey consultant who held finance and go-to-market roles at Gusto and OrderAhead (acquired by Square), where he managed sales commissions. In 2017 he co-founded CaptivateIQ with college friends Mark Schopmeyer and Hubert Wong (YC 2018) to replace commission spreadsheets with no-code incentive-compensation software; it has raised $164.6M from Sequoia, Accel, ICONIQ and others, and he is now listed as CEO.
interesting_fact: CaptivateIQ says it runs about 8 trillion real-time commission calculations per month for 1,000+ customers.
deep_cut_fact: CaptivateIQ was born when co-founder Mark Schopmeyer, nearly ready to quit over building commission spreadsheets, caught up with college friends Conway and Hubert and found they shared the same frustration; the three quit their jobs to start the company.
notes: Previously co-CEO with Schopmeyer; company About page now lists Teng as CEO and Schopmeyer as President. A Comparably profile says he co-founded loyalty company Fivestars, but this was not verified.

name: Hubert Wong
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, CaptivateIQ (San Francisco)
profile: Software engineer who co-founded CaptivateIQ in 2017 with Mark Schopmeyer and Conway Teng. The no-code platform designs and calculates sales commissions; it went through Y Combinator (Winter 2018) and reached a $1.25B valuation with a $100M raise in January 2022. Wong leads engineering as CTO.
interesting_fact: CaptivateIQ's backers include Sequoia, Accel and Y Combinator. Its January 2022 round valued the commission-software startup at $1.25B less than five years after launch.
notes: Low-profile technical founder; co-CEOs Schopmeyer and Teng are the public faces. Profiles say he was previously a senior software engineer at Vungle, and Comparably adds Amazon and founding engineer at Copilot (acquired by OpenTable), but I could not open those pages to verify.

name: Wang Donglin
current_role: Founder and Chief Scientist, Smartlogic Technology (思朗科技), Beijing/Shanghai; STAR Market IPO application accepted July 2026
profile: Chip architect and former director of the CAS Institute of Automation. In 2016 he founded Smartlogic to commercialise his reconfigurable MaPU processor architecture, used in 5G small-cell, edge-AI and energy-management chips. Backed by CATL Capital, Smartlogic filed for a roughly RMB 4.4bn STAR Market IPO in 2026.
interesting_fact: CATL, the world's largest battery maker, led Smartlogic's D round. Investors cited MaPU's efficiency for AI inference and smart battery and energy-storage management, a link between AI chips and the energy sector.
deep_cut_fact: He invented the MaPU (Mathematics Processing Unit) architecture, described as the world's first reconfigurable chip architecture built on 'software-defined hardware'. It won a first-class Technology Invention Award from the Chinese Institute of Electronics, and he is a recipient of China's National Science Fund for Distinguished Young Scholars.
notes: The Hurun 'Smart Logic' entry maps to 思朗科技 (Smartlogic). The founder is written 王东琳 in Chinese media. He is described as founder and chief scientist; Zha Hao has been chairman and CEO since 2019. Wang directly holds about 19% and controls about 34%. Sources give different dates for his CAS posts. No public contact found; the company's IR office will open once the IPO proceeds.

name: Doron Somech
current_role: Co-founder of Unit (embedded-banking infrastructure, NYC/Tel Aviv); apparently now building Submilli, a secure runtime for AI code agents
profile: Doron Somech is a Tel Aviv engineer listed as a co-founder of Unit, the embedded-banking platform (founded 2019 with CEO Itai Damti) valued at about $1B. He is no longer on Unit's leadership page; his GitHub now points to Submilli, an open-source WebAssembly sandbox runtime for 'code-mode' AI agents.
interesting_fact: His newest project, Submilli, runs code written by AI agents in isolated WebAssembly sandboxes with no network or file access by default, enforcing permissions on each call with an audit trail.
notes: GitHub user somdoron (Doron Somech, Tel Aviv, ZeroMQ org member, site submilli.ai) is very likely him; he is known in open source as a ZeroMQ/NetMQ maintainer, but that link and his Unit role were not confirmed from a primary page (search budget ran out). Unit's about page lists only Itai Damti as founder.

name: Itai Damti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Unit (New York)
profile: Israeli fintech operator who co-founded brokerage-tech provider Leverate (grew to ~160 staff without VC money) and later ran its Asia-Pacific business from Hong Kong. In 2019 he and Doron Somech founded Unit, an embedded-finance/banking-as-a-service platform letting companies launch accounts, cards and lending 'in weeks, not years'; it became a unicorn in 2022 ($100M Series C led by Insight).
interesting_fact: He and CTO Doron Somech had both left Leverate in 2015-16 and reunited about three years later to start Unit, which hit a $1.2B valuation within roughly three years.
deep_cut_fact: Before Unit he was a Fintech Entrepreneur in Residence at 500 Startups and EIR at hardware accelerator HAX, and is a special advisor to Hong Kong investment bank Ion Pacific; he has written guest columns for TechCrunch.
notes: Active writer/speaker on embedded finance. Route via Unit marketing/press or LinkedIn.

name: Chris Mansi
current_role: CEO and co-founder, Viz.ai (AI disease detection and care coordination, San Francisco)
profile: Newcastle-raised, Cambridge-trained neurosurgeon who operated at Queen Square and King's College hospitals in London before moving to the US for a Stanford MBA. In 2016 he co-founded Viz.ai with ML postdoc David Golan; it won the first FDA clearance for an AI triage platform (stroke) and by its 10th anniversary (July 2026) was in 2,000 hospitals covering ~230M patients with 50+ AI care pathways.
interesting_fact: Viz.ai's software now 'helps one patient every six seconds'; Mansi calls it 'an AI safety net that works consistently across hospital settings'. The idea came from seeing surgeries go well yet patients die or end up disabled because getting them to the OR took too long.
deep_cut_fact: In 2012, while still a neurosurgeon, he started Edusurg, an online exam-prep business for junior surgeons; at Stanford he tinkered with 'every technology I could find', including 3D-printing brains for surgical practice and a cranial-nerve stimulation device.
notes: Frequent conference speaker and WEF contributor; accessible via PR agency. Healthcare AI rather than energy; angle could be AI deployment at scale in hospitals.

name: David Golan
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Viz.ai (former CTO); current operating role not found
profile: Israeli machine-learning researcher (PhD in statistics & ML, Tel Aviv University) who, as a Fulbright postdoc at Stanford applying deep learning to medical imaging and genetics, co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and served as CTO. Viz.ai built the first FDA-cleared AI triage system for stroke (2018), now installed in 800+ hospitals in the US and Europe; he remains on the board.
interesting_fact: Viz.ai's software was the first AI-powered automatic stroke-triage system cleared by the FDA, alerting specialists directly so patients can be treated faster; it runs in 800+ hospitals.
deep_cut_fact: Before academia he founded the machine-learning team at Israeli startup b-hive Networks, acquired by VMware in 2008, and later co-authored 20+ scientific papers including three in the journal Science.
notes: Podcast entry is a past guest appearance (Brains Behind AI episode on building Viz.ai), not his own show; useful as prep. Left day-to-day role at Viz.ai; member of TechAviv founders club. No published personal/press email found; Viz.ai media inquiries via company site.

name: Manoj Ramachandran
current_role: Co-founder of Viz.ai; Consultant Orthopaedic & Trauma Surgeon (and reported Director of Innovation) at Barts Health NHS Trust, London; CEO & co-founder of halfloop (per profiles)
profile: London paediatric/young-adult orthopaedic surgeon who co-founded Viz.ai in 2016 with Chris Mansi and David Golan; its FDA-cleared AI care-coordination tools (stroke first, now cardio, vascular, oncology) made it a ~$1bn+ unicorn. He combines NHS practice at Barts with ventures, most recently halfloop (patient data for implant recipients).
interesting_fact: Viz.ai was his fourth business venture; in 2016 he described operating on children on Mondays and 'switching on in the evenings when Silicon Valley wakes up on the West Coast' to build the company.
deep_cut_fact: He became an orthopaedic consultant at a very young age (his self-described career highlight), has a keen interest in medical history - arguing most health solutions 'have been explored at some point in history but now we are adding a technological layer' - and is lead author of a Hodder Arnold basic orthopaedic sciences guide for fellowship exam candidates.
notes: Not a Viz.ai executive (CEO is Chris Mansi), so Viz.ai is an indirect route; halfloop or Barts Health innovation channels may be better. Titles (Professor, Director of Innovation, halfloop CEO) come from aggregator profiles - verify. Textbook detail via search results, not read directly. Personal wealth unconfirmed.

name: Rujul Zaparde
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Zip (procurement software, San Francisco)
profile: Two-time YC founder who co-founded Zip in 2020 with Lu Cheng and Felix Meng to fix slow enterprise purchasing with an AI 'intake-to-pay' procurement platform. Zip raised $190M at a $2.2B valuation and says its agentic platform processed $355B in spend in 2025; he remains CEO.
interesting_fact: His first company, FlightCar (YC Winter 2013), was pitched as 'the Airbnb of car rentals at airports', letting travellers rent out their parked cars; it operated at 12 US airports with backers including Brian Chesky.
deep_cut_fact: Between FlightCar and Zip he worked at Y Combinator as a Visiting Partner.
notes: Media-friendly (YC talks with Dalton Caldwell on enterprise sales). Route via press@ziphq.com.

name: Lyu Shiwen
current_role: CEO & CTO, Jenscare Scientific (健世科技, HKEX: 9877)

deep_cut_fact: At 2017's T-EDGE he quipped that if Nxin is an internet company, it must be one 'full of the smell of soil - or even pig manure' (充满泥土味/猪粪味道的互联网企业).
notes: Chinese-language outreach advisable. Hurun lists him as founder; he is chairman/president (Nxin was incubated by Dabeinong).

name: Zhang Jihui (Jeffrey Tiong)
current_role: Founder and CEO, PatSnap (Singapore/Beijing)
profile: 'Zhang Jihui' appears to be the Mandarin rendering of Jeffrey Tiong Jee Hui, NUS bioengineering graduate who founded PatSnap in 2007 with Dian Guan. PatSnap is an AI-driven patent and R&D intelligence platform (Eureka, Analytics) serving 10,000+ customers, valued above $1B after a 2021 SoftBank Vision Fund 2-led round.
interesting_fact: PatSnap started in Singapore with a SGD 50,000 grant from NUS Enterprise; Vertex Ventures was its first investor.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from an internship at a medical-device startup in Philadelphia (via NUS Overseas College), where his supervisor asked him to research patents - his first encounter with IP search.
notes: Name match inferred: Tiong = Zhang (张) in Hokkien and 'Jee Hui' = Jihui; MarketScreener lists 'Jeffrey Jee Hui Tiong'. Confirm before outreach. Route via PatSnap comms.

name: Guan Dian
current_role: Co-founder, CMO and APAC General Manager, Patsnap (Singapore-founded AI patent and R&D intelligence platform), per Vertex Ventures, Feb 2024
profile: Guan Dian studied management information systems at the National University of Singapore. In 2007 she co-founded Patsnap with fellow NUS student Jeffrey Tiong, starting with a S$50,000 NUS Enterprise grant. Patsnap became a unicorn after a $300M round led by SoftBank and Tencent, and it serves more than 10,000 customers in over 50 countries with AI-powered patent and innovation analytics. She runs marketing and the Asia-Pacific business.
interesting_fact: Patsnap began with a S$50,000 (about US$37,700) grant from NUS Enterprise, and the founders spent two years building their data capabilities before expanding globally.
deep_cut_fact: As an NUS undergraduate she interned in Silicon Valley at a video-streaming company. NUS later gave her its Outstanding Young Alumni Award in 2019.

public_contacts.value: Hard Truths by Vertex, Series 2 Ep 8 (Feb 2024): 'How Guan Dian built a Tech Unicorn from Ground up'

notes: Female co-founder, featured in Vertex's women-founder series. The Vertex episode covers why she left a 'cushy job' to join the startup, a good conversation hook. CEO Jeffrey Tiong is the main press voice. I found no published press email. Her Stanford education appears in some bios but was not verified.

name: Manish Taneja
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Purplle (Indian beauty e-commerce and brands, Mumbai)
profile: IIT Delhi electrical engineer Manish Taneja, who passed the CFA exam in 2010, left an investments job at Fidelity to start beauty e-tailer Purplle around 2011-12 with ex-flatmate Rahul Dash; Suyash Katyayani joined soon after. Backed by Blume, Verlinvest, Goldman Sachs, Kedaara and Premji Invest, it has built its own brands since 2017.
interesting_fact: The founders chose beauty over furniture because it needed less capital and offered high gross margins and repeat purchases. They started with about $100,000 in combined savings.
deep_cut_fact: Growing up in Faridabad he wanted to be a cricketer. At IIT he was inspired by a talk from Sunil Bharti Mittal on how Airtel stayed focused on telecom, and he counts Rajiv Vij's 'Inside Out Leadership' among his favorite books. His motto: 'Being nice to other people is a superpower.'
notes: Podcast-friendly: he has appeared on Blume's X-Unicorns and Z47's Unstarted. The only published Purplle email found is customercare@purplle.com (customer service, not press). Blume transcript is AI-generated, but details are consistent with other sources.

name: Rahul Dash
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Purplle (Indian online beauty retailer and brand house, Mumbai); role as reported in 2023
profile: Rahul Dash is an IIT Kharagpur graduate who then went to IIM Ahmedabad and worked at Tata, where the Purplle idea took shape. He co-founded Purplle with Manish Taneja (CEO) and Suyash Katyayani (CTO). The trio pooled about Rs 40 lakh of savings to start it. Purplle sells beauty products online and through its own brands, and became a unicorn valued at about $1B.
interesting_fact: Purplle's three co-founders started the company by pooling just Rs 40 lakh (about $50k) of their own savings. It later became a ~$1B (about Rs 8,200 crore) beauty unicorn competing with Nykaa.
notes: Sources conflict on his pre-Purplle employer: DNA says Tata (aggregators say Tata Power strategy and business development), while indiacsr.in says McKinsey. Left out of the deep-cut for that reason. If Tata Power is confirmed, it is a natural energy-podcast hook. CEO Manish Taneja is the public face. Current role not re-verified after 2023.

name: Frank Wolf
current_role: Co-founder, Staffbase (Chemnitz-based employee communications platform); listed as President & Co-Founder on recruiter profiles - current title unverified
profile: German entrepreneur who spent years as a consultant building enterprise intranets before co-founding Staffbase in Chemnitz in 2014 with Martin Böhringer and Lutz Gerlach. Staffbase launched what it calls the world's first employee app and now serves 1,500 customers and 16.5M users; it is still founder-led and was valued at over €1B (OMR, 2022).
interesting_fact: Staffbase's founding idea came from Wolf's frustration that the big enterprise intranets he built as a consultant were complex, expensive and used by only a fraction of the workforce - so they designed for 'the hardest-to-reach employee'.
deep_cut_fact: Wolf championed Dresden as Staffbase's 'kind of second headquarters', moving there largely to recruit software talent from TU Dresden; by end-2020 the Dresden office had 62 staff.
notes: Staffbase is headquartered in Chemnitz, East Germany - a notable non-Berlin unicorn story. CEO is Martin Böhringer; Wolf is lower-profile.

name: Lutz Gerlach
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Staffbase (employee communications platform, Chemnitz, Germany)
profile: German former academic (doctorate in business/managerial economics, senior researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology) who co-founded productivity app Hojoki in 2011 and then Staffbase in 2014 with Martin Böhringer and Frank Wolf. Staffbase grew into a leading employee-app and intranet platform, reaching unicorn valuation with Series D (2021) and E (2022) rounds.
interesting_fact: Staffbase is headquartered in Chemnitz, eastern Germany, a rare unicorn outside Berlin/Munich, and grew out of the same founding team as the earlier Hojoki startup.
deep_cut_fact: Before Staffbase he was a senior researcher at Chemnitz University of Technology (doctorate in business/managerial economics), then co-founded and served as COO of productivity-app startup Hojoki, founded in Chemnitz in March 2011.
notes: Role sourced from Staffbase recruiting pages and MarketScreener; CEO Martin Böhringer is the more public face.

name: Balaji Srinivasan
current_role: Founder, The Network School; founder, Balaji Fund; author of 'The Network State'
profile: Balaji S. Srinivasan (b. 1980; Stanford EE PhD) co-founded Counsyl (sold to Myriad for $375m), was an a16z general partner, co-founded 21 Inc/Earn.com (sold to Coinbase in 2018, where he became first CTO) and relocation start-up Teleport (2014, sold to Topia). He now runs the Network School (now in Kazakhstan) and the Balaji Fund.
interesting_fact: His self-published 2022 book 'The Network State: How To Start a New Country' hit No. 2 on the Wall Street Journal's e-book bestseller list, and in 2017 the Trump administration considered him for FDA Commissioner.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he taught Stanford's 'Startup Engineering' online course, which Business Insider ranked in 2014 as the sixth most popular free online course for professionals; his genomics papers have 5,000+ citations.
notes: IDENTITY CAVEAT: Hurun lists him as founder of a $1bn cloud unicorn 'Teleport' - that is almost certainly Gravitational/Teleport (founders Ev Kontsevoy et al.), not Balaji's 2014 relocation start-up teleport.org (sold to Topia). Treat the Hurun attribution as an error. Very active on X; reachable publicly. Renounced US citizenship in 2023.

name: Silver Keskküla
current_role: CEO, ScamGuardian.AI (deepfake-scam defence); also runs trackAIanswers.com; CDL-Estonia associate
profile: Estonian engineer-entrepreneur Silver Keskküla was the first researcher on Skype's core team, then co-founded Teleport (2014, with Sten Tamkivi and Balaji Srinivasan), a data-driven relocation search engine for 'digital nomads' later acquired by MOVE Guides/Topia (2017). He then founded AI startup Supervaisor and now builds AI-safety and LLM-brand-monitoring tools.
interesting_fact: Teleport, which he co-founded with ex-Skype executive Sten Tamkivi and Balaji Srinivasan, began as a search engine to help people pick cities to live and work in, and was acquired by global-mobility firm MOVE Guides (now Topia).
deep_cut_fact: At Skype he used machine learning to optimise the peer-to-peer network topology, shipping neural networks to hundreds of millions of computers years before the deep-learning boom; he says he is most inspired by bio-mimetic algorithms, from evolutionary computation to neural nets.
notes: Identity confirmed as Teleport co-founder, but the input's claim that Teleport was a $1B 'unicorn' is doubtful: it was a modest exit to MOVE Guides/Topia, so the Hurun listing may be an error. Not a UHNW profile. Approachable startup founder; also raised what was described as Estonia's largest solo-founder angel round for Supervaisor.

name: Sten Tamkivi
current_role: Partner, Plural (European founder-led VC platform); Founding Partner, Creative Destruction Lab Estonia
profile: Estonian entrepreneur and investor who spent 8+ years as an early Skype executive through its $8.5B sale to Microsoft. As an EIR at Andreessen Horowitz he co-founded Teleport, a tool for remote workers and digital nomads that pivoted to B2B and was acquired by Topia in 2017; he stayed as Topia's CPO through a $48M Series C. He now invests as a partner at Plural.
interesting_fact: Teleport was co-founded while he was an entrepreneur-in-residence at Andreessen Horowitz, after his Skype years spanning startup to the $8.5B Microsoft exit.
deep_cut_fact: He started his entrepreneurial career in 1996, aged 18, by founding the first digital media agency in Estonia.
notes: Very accessible and public: active on X and LinkedIn, gives interviews (ERR, Estonian World, Seedcamp). Founders Pledge member. Hurun lists him via Teleport, but his wealth is mainly from Skype/Teleport exits. Good podcast guest candidate.

name: Anthony Watson
current_role: Founder of The Bank of London (CEO until September 2024); current executive role not confirmed
profile: London-born technology executive (CBE, 2023) who was CIO of Barclays' retail bank (launching the Pingit app) and Nike's CIO in 2014, then co-founded crypto platform Uphold in 2015. He conceived The Bank of London in 2016 and launched it in November 2021 as a UK clearing, correspondent and wholesale bank, serving as CEO until September 2024.
interesting_fact: The Bank of London launched on 30 November 2021 as the UK's sixth clearing bank; Watson is also a prominent LGBT advocate - GLAAD board member since 2013, Stonewall ambassador and founder of The Watson Pride Foundation.
deep_cut_fact: He studied theology and considered becoming a minister, but a part-time job at AOL Ireland during his degree hooked him on technology; he then joined First-e, billed as Europe's first internet bank.
notes: Left Bank of London CEO role Sept 2024; the bank has had difficult press since - avoid that topic. anthonywatson.com is a parked domain (not his). No published contact found; LinkedIn or GLAAD/Stonewall networks are possible routes. Also an art collector (18th-19th c. portraits, contemporary works).

name: Jonathan Siddharth
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Turing (Palo Alto)
profile: Jonathan Siddharth co-founded Turing in 2018 (incubated at Foundation Capital) to source, vet and manage remote software developers with AI. Turing has since pivoted to supplying coding and reasoning data and talent to frontier AI labs such as OpenAI, raising a $111M Series E led by Khazanah Nasional in March 2025 at a $2.2B valuation, with a ~$300M revenue run rate.
interesting_fact: In 2012, needing mobile engineers for his first startup, he hired developers from Ukraine, Serbia and China; their app was recognized by Apple as one of the best in the App Store, an experience that seeded Turing's 'Talent Cloud' idea.
deep_cut_fact: His career began with an internship on Yahoo's search relevance team, then ranking work at natural-language search startup Powerset (acquired by Microsoft); in 2008 he co-founded content-discovery app Rover, acquired by Revcontent in 2016. He has also served on Quora's board and advised through Stanford's StartX.
notes: Strong fit for AI/data-center angle: Turing is a key training-data/coding provider for LLM labs. Stanford MS in CS (ML and search). Active writer (Unite.AI author page).

name: Jose Gustavo Fuentes Cabrera
profile: Could not identify. The best-known 'Turing' unicorn (the Palo Alto AI/talent company valued at ~$4B) was founded by Jonathan Siddharth and Vijay Krishnan; no source found linking a José Gustavo Fuentes Cabrera to Turing or any other company named Turing.
notes: Likely a mismatch or data error in the Hurun founder list; exact-name searches returned nothing. Kept minimal - verify the source listing before any outreach.

name: Vijay Krishnan
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Turing
profile: Vijay Krishnan co-founded Palo Alto-based Turing in 2018 with CEO Jonathan Siddharth; Turing started as an AI-vetted remote software-talent cloud and now focuses on supplying data, training and engineering for frontier AI labs and enterprise AI. He has 20+ years in ML/AI and previously founded content-recommendation startup Rover (acquired by Revcontent).
interesting_fact: An IIT Bombay alumnus, he was chosen for IIT Bombay's Young Alumni Achiever Award (announced Feb 2024); the awards are conferred each year on March 10, IIT Bombay's Foundation Day.
deep_cut_fact: Before Turing he was founder and CTO of Rover, a personalized content-recommendation company later acquired by Revcontent, and he has authored highly cited papers on web search, semantic search and entity extraction.
notes: Has appeared on podcasts (e.g. The Neon Show) talking about AI startups, so open to media. Name is common - confirm it is the Turing CTO.

name: Gu Jing
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Viewtrix Technology Co., Ltd (云英谷科技 / Yunyinggu, HKEX: 3310)
profile: Dr. Gu Jing founded Shenzhen-based fabless chip designer Viewtrix (Yunyinggu) in 2012. It is China's leading AMOLED display-driver IC supplier for smartphones and, per Frost & Sullivan, No. 2 globally in micro-OLED backplanes for AR/VR, with a ~40.7% share. Viewtrix listed on the Hong Kong Main Board on 27 May 2026, and in September 2026 it began preparing an A-share listing.
interesting_fact: Viewtrix shipped 51.4 million AMOLED driver ICs in 2024, up from 14.1 million in 2022, with revenue near $130M. Its micro-OLED backplanes go into the near-eye displays used in AR/VR headsets.
deep_cut_fact: Gu is personally the named inventor on a string of Yunyinggu patents covering subpixel rendering and display-driving methods, the image-processing tricks that let OLED panels look sharper with fewer physical subpixels.
notes: 'Viewtrix' is 云英谷 (Yunyinggu), not the similarly named Hefei micro-OLED maker SeeYA (视涯, founder Gu Tie). A Harvard engineering PhD is claimed only by Dealroom (unverified). I found no published IR email; check the forthcoming 2026 interim report on HKEXnews for the IR contact. A good fit for AI-hardware and AR themes.

name: Xue Wenxiang
profile: No link found between a 'Xue Wenxiang' and Viewtrix (云英谷科技, HKEX: 3310), the Beijing/Shenzhen fabless maker of AMOLED display-driver chips and Micro-OLED backplanes. It was founded in 2012 by Harvard PhD Dr. Gu Jing (顾晶) and listed in Hong Kong on May 27, 2026. Xue does not appear among its directors, senior management or controlling shareholders in the prospectus.
notes: Tried: Viewtrix HKEX prospectus dated 2026-05-18 (https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/0518/2026051800021.pdf), searched for Xue/Wenxiang (no match); allotment results; Chinese exact-name search for 薛文翔 (no relevant hits); English searches. Hurun's founder attribution may be wrong. Chairman/founder Gu Jing is the documented founder (~17% post-IPO control).

name: Adam de la Zerda
current_role: Founder & CEO, Visby Medical; Associate Professor, Stanford University School of Medicine
profile: Israeli-born, Technion- and Stanford-trained (PhD) engineer who incorporated Click Diagnostics in Dec 2012 after an EIR stint at Artiman Ventures; renamed Visby Medical in March 2020. Visby makes palm-sized, instrument-free single-use PCR tests: the first such FDA-cleared, CLIA-waived STI test (2021) plus COVID and flu tests.
interesting_fact: In 2012 he became the youngest tenure-track faculty member at Stanford Medical School, and he still holds an Associate Professor post there while running Visby.
deep_cut_fact: He came to Stanford for an EE PhD drawn by its quantum-computing groups and never expected to work in medicine; radiology chair Sam Gambhir introduced him to the field. In March 2020, the month Visby pivoted to COVID testing, it was hiring about 20 people a week.
notes: Academic plus founder; likely reachable via Stanford faculty profile or Visby press. Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree per company bio.

name: Hiroki Takeuchi
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, GoCardless, which now operates as 'GoCardless, a Mollie company' after Mollie completed its acquisition on 1 September 2026
profile: Hiroki Takeuchi co-founded London-based GoCardless, a bank-payments (direct debit / Pay by Bank) company, which went through Y Combinator and was valued at £1.55bn in 2022. GoCardless grew revenue 22% in FY25 and posted its first EBITDA-positive quarter. In September 2026 Dutch payments firm Mollie completed its acquisition of GoCardless, which keeps its brand under Takeuchi.
interesting_fact: After Mollie's acquisition, GoCardless keeps running as its own brand ('GoCardless, a Mollie company') under Takeuchi. The combined group serves 350,000+ businesses across 30+ markets, and GoCardless brings presence in the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
deep_cut_fact: A line from Y Combinator stuck with him: Sam Altman described building a startup as 'riding a wave on a surfboard', where if you stay on the board you will eventually succeed and if you fall you can choose to get back on.
notes: GoCardless was acquired by Mollie (completed 1 Sep 2026), and Koen Köppen leads the group. Takeuchi is a regular speaker (London Tech Week, Paris Fintech Forum). Background details on aggregators (Oxford maths, McKinsey, co-founded 2011 with Tom Blomfield and Matt Robinson) were not verified on a primary source here.

name: Matt Robinson
current_role: Partner, Accel (London), investing in AI, inference, security and software; co-founder and board member of GoCardless
profile: Oxford graduate and ex-McKinsey consultant who co-founded London payments company GoCardless with Hiroki Takeuchi and Tom Blomfield, leading business, marketing and sales. He then founded and ran Nested, a proptech start-up that tackled the cash-buyer disadvantage in UK house sales. He joined Accel as an investor in 2024 and has angel-invested in Cleo, Gamma, n8n and Wayve.
interesting_fact: GoCardless was started by three Oxford students, Robinson, Hiroki Takeuchi and Tom Blomfield. Blomfield later founded Monzo, making the trio an unusually prolific UK fintech founding team.
deep_cut_fact: His Accel profile lists his favourite works as Jez Butterworth's play 'Jerusalem' and Tom Stoppard's 'Arcadia'.
notes: As an active VC focused on AI inference, he is a natural fit for a data-center themed podcast. Easiest to reach via Accel or X. He has said the early GoCardless team 'literally made every mistake you could' (https://smallbusiness.co.uk/gocardless-founder-matt-robinson-now-shaking-property-industry-2534362/).

name: Zhao Qian
current_role: Legal representative and largest individual shareholder (~17.8%), Wuhan ABclonal Biotechnology (爱博泰克) per business registry
profile: Zhao Qian (赵骞) is listed in ABclonal's business registration (via 36Kr) as legal representative and largest shareholder of Wuhan ABclonal Biotechnology, founded in June 2011. ABclonal makes research antibodies, molecular enzymes and NGS kits and has a US arm in Woburn, Massachusetts. It raised a RMB1.2bn Series D in 2021 led by Sequoia China.
interesting_fact: ABclonal's RMB1.2bn Series D (Dec 2021) was co-led by Sequoia China, Luxin Venture Capital and CMB International. At its RMB600m Series C in 2020, overseas sales were about 40% of revenue.
notes: The registry spells the name 赵骞 (Zhao Qian). 36Kr's funding coverage calls 吴知才 (Wu Zhicai) 'founder and CEO', so Zhao is better described as a co-founder/major shareholder. No personal biography found, and a common name; confirm the role before outreach.

name: Wu Zhicai
current_role: Founder & CEO, ABclonal (Wuhan ABclonal Biotechnology / 爱博泰克); also listed as President of ABclonal Technology (Woburn, MA)
profile: Founder (吴知才, often 'Zack Wu') of ABclonal, a Wuhan-based life-science tools maker (antibodies, enzymes, NGS library kits) founded in 2011 with a US arm in Woburn, MA. The company raised RMB 1.2B in a Dec 2021 Series D co-led by Sequoia China, Luxin Venture Capital and CMB International, after a RMB 600M Series C in 2020.
interesting_fact: ABclonal set up a US subsidiary as early as 2013 and later built a US R&D center and national sales network; by 2020 overseas sales were about 40% of revenue.
deep_cut_fact: He and his co-founders started ABclonal in 2011 with just RMB 50,000 in start-up funds; within a year it was selected for Wuhan Optics Valley's 5th '3551 Talent Program', and within three years it had over RMB 100M in assets.
notes: Chinese name 吴知才 (not 武). English press releases quote 'Zack Wu, CEO'; BBB lists 'Zhicai Wu, President' for the Woburn entity - very likely the same person. The listed email is a general China marketing inbox.

name: Lin Yuanqing
current_role: Founder & CEO, Aibee (爱笔智能), Beijing
profile: Lin Yuanqing (Yuanqing Lin) is a computer-vision researcher who led media analytics at NEC Labs America, then directed Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning (2015-2017) under Andrew Ng. He left in late 2017 to found Aibee, raising $25m within a month; Aibee sells AI 'total solutions' (footfall analytics, navigation, parking, face access) for malls, retailers, banks and airports and was valued at ~$1bn.
interesting_fact: He was featured as one of the 'Heroes of Deep Learning' interviewees in Andrew Ng's deeplearning.ai course, reflecting his time running Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning.
deep_cut_fact: He is first-listed on the NEC-UIUC team that won the very first ImageNet Large Scale Visual Recognition Challenge in 2010, two years before AlexNet made the contest famous.
notes: Baidu appointment source: https://sg.news.yahoo.com/finance/news/baidu-appoints-yuanqing-lin-computer-010000604.html ; Aibee founding/funding: https://syncedreview.com/2018/01/19/life-after-baidu-yuanqing-lins-ai-startup-moves-fast-on-funding-and-b2b-opportunities/. Aibee website footer dated 2019, so confirm company's current status. Technical founder; good for an AI-infrastructure conversation.

name: Baskar Subramanian
current_role: Co-founder, Managing Director & CEO, Amagi Media Labs Ltd (NSE/BSE-listed, Bengaluru)
profile: Baskar Subramanian co-founded Amagi in 2008 with Srividhya Srinivasan and Arunachalam Srinivasan Karapattu. Amagi makes cloud software that TV networks and streamers (Fox, Lionsgate, Roku, DirecTV and others) use to distribute and monetise video, and about 73% of its revenue comes from the US. It listed in India in January 2026, raising about $196M.
interesting_fact: At the January 2026 IPO he called the listing 'a pit stop in a long journey' and said the founders sold no shares. He argues that fewer than 10% of broadcasters have moved from 'big iron' hardware and satellite workflows to the cloud.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, Impulsesoft (founded 1999), made wireless multimedia headsets and watches. Amagi's first service, in Hyderabad, offered localised TV ads by splicing broadcast signals.
notes: A strong fit for a data-center/cloud-infrastructure theme: Amagi plans about ₹5.5B of IPO proceeds for tech and cloud infrastructure. He has appeared on several founder podcasts (100x Entrepreneur, Accel) and is described as an IIT dropout and ex-Texas Instruments engineer (secondary sources).

name: John de Souza
current_role: Co-founder and President, Ample (modular EV battery swapping; San Francisco)
profile: Serial entrepreneur (MIT SB/SM in EECS) who co-founded Smartleaf, Flash Communications and MedHelp before co-founding Ample with MedHelp's CTO, Khaled Hassounah. Ample's robotic stations swap modular EV batteries in about five minutes. It raised $330M+ and ran pilots with Uber drivers, Stellantis/Fiat in Madrid and Mitsubishi Fuso/Yamato in Tokyo.
interesting_fact: Ample's stations swap an EV's modular battery in about five minutes. Investors had been scared off by the failure of Better Place, but the founders still raised over $275M by 2021.
deep_cut_fact: Born and raised in Ethiopia, he moved with his family to Dubai in the 1970s, then came to the US at 16 on a full university scholarship. He later co-founded Flash Communications, a real-time two-way messaging startup acquired by Microsoft.
notes: Ample filed for Chapter 11 in Dec 2025 (Electrek, CCJ), so its unicorn status is stale; be tactful. No press email was found (ample.com contact/press pages return 404). The podcast entry is a past guest spot, not his own show. The Microsoft acquisition of Flash comes from profile summaries; TechCrunch confirms only that he co-founded Flash.

name: Khaled Hassounah
current_role: Co-Founder & CEO, Ample (San Francisco EV battery-swapping company)
profile: Jordan-trained electrical engineer (University of Jordan, 1998) who co-founded Ample with John de Souza in 2014 to build robotic, modular EV battery-swapping stations. Ample has run stations for Uber drivers in the Bay Area, expanded to Japan with ENEOS and partnered with Stellantis; its newest stations swap a battery in about five minutes.
interesting_fact: TIME named Ample to its TIME100 Most Influential Companies list in 2023 (Disrupters); Hassounah argues Ample's real competitor is gasoline, not charging.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ample he was co-founder and CTO of MedHelp, an online health community, and sat on the board of KarmSolar, Egypt's first private off-grid solar power company.
notes: Strong energy fit (EV infrastructure, solar background). Has appeared on climate podcasts (MCJ 'Inevitable' - https://mcj.vc/inevitable-podcast/ample), so podcast-friendly. No published press email found on ample.com (contact page is JS-only); LinkedIn link is the company page, not personal. Deep-cut source is a third-party bio aggregator; KarmSolar board role may be past.

name: Michael I. Jordan
current_role: Directeur de Recherche, Inria and ENS Paris; Pehong Chen Distinguished Professor Emeritus, UC Berkeley; co-founder of Anyscale and Arena Intelligence
profile: Among the most influential figures in machine learning and statistics, he was an MIT professor (1988-98) and then at Berkeley, where his RISELab students created Ray and spun out Anyscale, the distributed-AI-compute company he co-founded. He went emeritus in 2024, now researches at Inria Paris, and won the 2025 BBVA Frontiers of Knowledge Award.
interesting_fact: In 2016 an article in Science, using Semantic Scholar rankings, named him the 'most influential computer scientist' in the world.
deep_cut_fact: His degrees are not in computer science: a master's in mathematics from Arizona State and a 1985 PhD in cognitive science from UC San Diego. Beyond AI startups, he sits on the board of UnitedMasters, the independent-music distribution company.
notes: This is the Berkeley ML professor, not the basketball player. The email is his academic address, published on his own homepage; he is now based mostly in Paris (Inria). He is an outspoken critic of 'AI' hype who favours framing it as economics plus ML. Strong guest for AI-infrastructure topics: Ray and Anyscale underpin large-scale AI compute.

name: Philipp Moritz
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Anyscale (Ray) - being acquired by AI cloud/data-center operator Nscale (deal signed July 2026)
profile: Computer scientist who did his PhD at UC Berkeley's RISELab, where he co-created the open-source distributed computing framework Ray with Robert Nishihara and Ion Stoica. The trio founded Anyscale in 2019 to commercialize Ray, now a standard for scaling AI training/inference (used by OpenAI among others). In July 2026 London-based Nscale agreed to buy Anyscale to add orchestration software to its power-data-center-GPU stack.
interesting_fact: Nscale's acquisition makes Anyscale the software layer of a vertically integrated AI cloud spanning power, data centers and compute; Anyscale's ~200 staff will join Nscale while keeping the Anyscale brand.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ray, he co-authored the landmark 2015 reinforcement-learning paper 'Trust Region Policy Optimization' (TRPO) with John Schulman, Sergey Levine, Michael I. Jordan and Pieter Abbeel - a precursor to PPO.
