He led search and AI for Glean's enterprise search / work-AI assistant, which was valued at $7.2B in 2025. He left around 2023 to start a new company.
interesting_fact: Glean was born from Arvind Jain's frustration at Rubrik, where a survey found that finding information was employees' 'single biggest' workplace problem across 300+ SaaS apps.
deep_cut_fact: At Google (2005-2017) he was a technical/engineering lead on the Google Maps and Search Quality Ranking teams, the background that shaped Glean's ranking engine for enterprise search.
notes: Post-Glean venture unclear: one aggregator says a stealth work-management startup, another names it Aida (AI chief of staff for sales). No verified personal site or contact found. Glean's earlier Uber work (Uber Transit, shared bikes) is per startupintros.com aggregator only.

name: Tony Gentilcore
current_role: Co-founder and Product Engineering lead, Glean (enterprise 'Work AI' search and assistant platform, Palo Alto)
profile: Tony Gentilcore co-founded Glean in 2019 with Arvind Jain, T.R. Vishwanath and Piyush Prahladka after a decade at Google. Glean builds AI search and agents over a company's internal data and was valued at about $7bn; he leads product engineering.
interesting_fact: At Google he helped move the search results page from the static 'ten blue links' era into the JavaScript era, then founded and led the Chrome Speed Team, which contributed to HTML5 and helped form the W3C Web Performance Working Group.
deep_cut_fact: Away from work he is on a quest to photograph every bird species in the world, per his Glean bio. He studied electrical engineering (BS) at Saint Louis University.
notes: Engineering co-founder with a lower public profile than CEO Arvind Jain; the birding hobby is a natural, friendly opener. Route via Glean press.

name: TR Vishwanath
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Glean (enterprise AI search and agents platform)
profile: IIT Delhi/UT Austin engineer who worked on web services and developer platforms at Microsoft, then ~2010-19 at Facebook on developer platform, News Feed ranking and Ads. In 2019 he co-founded Glean with Arvind Jain and others; the enterprise AI company was valued at ~$7bn and he oversees its 275+ data connectors.
interesting_fact: Glean's enterprise search/assistant became prominent enough that Business Insider reported Sam Altman viewed it as a competitive threat to OpenAI in the enterprise.
deep_cut_fact: He got his first taste of startup life in the early 2000s at a Bay Area storage startup, long before Glean; his Glean bio jokes that he 'likes to subject his family to terrible dad jokes and listen to podcasts to appear knowledgeable.'
notes: Self-described podcast listener; spoke at Databricks Data + AI Summit 2026 on the AI-native stack. Technical co-founder rather than public face (CEO Arvind Jain). Good fit for AI infrastructure/data angle.

name: Carlos Paniagua
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Glia (based in Tartu, Estonia)
profile: Guatemala-born software engineer who co-founded Glia with Dan Michaeli and Justin DiPietro; Glia's digital customer-service platform (voice, chat, video, co-browsing and AI) is used mainly by banks and credit unions. He built its engineering hub in Tartu, and Glia became Estonia's tenth unicorn in 2021.
interesting_fact: Although Glia is headquartered in New York, Paniagua proposed moving the developer team to Tartu, recruiting engineers he had studied with, making Glia counted as an Estonian unicorn.
deep_cut_fact: Originally from Guatemala, he moved to Estonia in 2010 on a scholarship to study a master's in software engineering at the University of Tartu; he advises foreign founders there to learn Estonian ('It's very powerful').
notes: Active in Estonian startup community (LIFT99, Startup Day). CEO Dan Michaeli is Glia's public face in the US. No published press email found.

name: Daniel Michaeli
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Glia (formerly SaleMove), New York
profile: Penn graduate and ex-Accenture analyst who co-founded SaleMove in 2012, later renamed Glia; the company sells AI-driven digital customer-service and contact-center software to banks and credit unions (700+ institutions) and became a unicorn in 2021 (~$1.2B valuation). He remains CEO, pushing 'banking AI' agents and interactions.
interesting_fact: Born in New York, he grew up in Guatemala from birth to 18; he tells how his grandfather, after fleeing Czechoslovakia, built a Guatemalan plastics business that began with selling plastic combs from a bicycle.
deep_cut_fact: He swears by a 'Rhythm of Business' (ROB) system - a fixed annual cadence of board meetings and planning events used as forcing functions - which he calls the single practice he would repeat as CEO of any future company.
notes: Glia has Estonian roots (strong presence in Tallinn/Tartu). Aggregators say he studied Economics, Engineering Entrepreneurship and Film at Penn and was Forbes 30 Under 30 Europe 2017 (unverified). Glia's recent releases used agency Words@Work for media; no glia.com press email found.

name: Justin DiPietro
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Strategy Officer, Glia (New York; banking AI / digital customer service platform)
profile: Co-founded Glia (originally SaleMove) in 2012 with CEO Dan Michaeli after working with him as a strategy consultant to large enterprises; previously COO. Glia sells AI-powered contact-center and digital customer-service software to banks and credit unions, was valued at about $1B, and in Nov 2026 announced it had passed $100M ARR with positive cash flow.
interesting_fact: Glia announced in November 2026 that it had surpassed $100M in annual recurring revenue while cash-flow positive, driven by 'banking AI' adoption among community banks and credit unions.
deep_cut_fact: A Penn State graduate, he was a consultant working alongside Dan Michaeli on customer and technology strategy before they co-founded the company as SaleMove in 2012.
notes: Low public profile; Dan Michaeli is Glia's public face. No published press email found on glia.com; LinkedIn likely best route. Earlier title was COO; Glia's site now lists him as Chief Strategy Officer & Co-Founder.

name: Advait Shinde
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, GoGuardian (CEO until April 2024)
profile: UCLA computer-science grad and former Google software engineer who co-founded El Segundo-based edtech company GoGuardian in 2014 with Aza Steel and Todd Mackey, becoming CEO in 2018. GoGuardian's classroom-management, filtering and student-safety tools serve thousands of school districts; it was valued above $1B after Tiger Global's 2021 investment. In 2024 he handed the CEO role to Rich Preece and moved to Executive Chairman focused on technology and innovation.
interesting_fact: GoGuardian was originally born out of a Chromebook extension built by co-founder Aza Steel to track down stolen laptops, before pivoting to school internet filtering.
deep_cut_fact: He has said that as a first-time founder he probably would have hesitated had he known how hard it would be, and credits executive coaches with rewriting the internal 'narratives' that made him doubt he could grow from engineer into CEO.
notes: Now non-CEO (Executive Chairman since April 2024) so may have more time for podcasts; engineer-founder angle.

name: Aza Steel
current_role: Co-founder, GoGuardian (Los Angeles edtech); current position not publicly confirmed
profile: UCLA sociology graduate who taught himself to code and founded GoGuardian in 2014 with fellow Bruin Advait Shinde (later CEO). GoGuardian grew from a Chrome-extension laptop tracker into classroom-management and student-safety software used by thousands of US schools; it reached a $1B+ valuation and took investment from Thoma Bravo in 2021.
interesting_fact: GoGuardian began as his dorm-room Chrome extension to track his own laptop if it was stolen -- a 'flawed plan' since it relied on the thief using Chrome -- until school districts flooded him with requests to use it.
deep_cut_fact: When GoGuardian scaled so fast its servers were 'literally melting', he called AWS support daily as 'an emotional and technological crutch' and kept getting Australian agents: 'that accent was just really soothing.' He and Shinde made Forbes 30 Under 30 in 2016.
notes: Very low public profile since ~2018; no current role or published contact found. Name sometimes misspelled 'Steele'. Best route may be via GoGuardian corporate communications.

name: Todd Mackey
current_role: Co-founder, President & COO, MightyByte (maker of the ClassCalc math calculator app)
profile: Southern California entrepreneur and angel investor (R. Todd Mackey) who co-founded web-filtering/classroom-management EdTech company GoGuardian, serving as President & COO 2014-2016 after leading its Series A; GoGuardian was acquired by Sumeru Equity Partners in 2018 and later valued ~$1B. He has since co-founded MightyByte, which builds the free ClassCalc calculator app for students.
interesting_fact: He says he has co-founded and/or scaled six companies across manufacturing, industrial products and education, with experience spanning investment banking to operations.
deep_cut_fact: On ClassCalc's team page he describes himself as a beach-loving volleyball player, world explorer and 'lover of dark chocolate and BF The Cookie,' and says education should be made cheap and accessible for all.
notes: Moved to advisory role at GoGuardian in Aug 2016 (self-reported). team@classcalc.com is a general company inbox. Social links are from his self-written (unverified) Wellfound profile.

name: Aaron Feaver
current_role: Director, Joint Center for Deployment and Research in Earth Abundant Materials (JCDREAM), Washington State University; co-founder of Group14 Technologies
profile: Aaron Feaver is a materials scientist who co-founded EnerG2 (carbon materials for energy storage, CTO; acquired by BASF) and then Group14 Technologies, the Woodinville, WA maker of silicon-carbon anode materials that boost lithium-ion battery capacity, valued around $3B. Since 2019 he has directed WSU's JCDREAM, a state-backed program commercialising earth-abundant clean-energy materials.
interesting_fact: He and his team grew EnerG2 from a small venture-backed start-up into a 100-person manufacturer with sites in Seattle and Oregon before BASF bought it, then spun the silicon-anode work into Group14.
deep_cut_fact: Before batteries he was an aerospace engineer: a project manager and engineer in Liaison and Value Engineering at Boeing. His path runs from a BA in physics (North Central College) and a BS in civil engineering (Illinois) to a materials-science PhD at the University of Washington.
notes: Strong energy-storage fit. No published personal/press email found for him or Group14; best routes are the Group14 website or WSU JCDREAM (WSU Everett). Serves on the UW Materials Science & Engineering advisory board. JCDREAM role dates from 2019; confirm it is still current.

name: Rick Costantino
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Technology Officer, Group14 Technologies (Woodinville, Washington)
profile: Chemical engineer (BS/MS Johns Hopkins, PhD MIT) who co-founded Group14 in 2015 with CEO Rick Luebbe as a spin-out of carbon-materials firm EnerG2, where he was VP of R&D. Group14 makes silicon-carbon anode material (SCC55) that boosts lithium-ion energy density by up to 50%, has factories in Washington state and Sangju, South Korea (EV-scale production from 2026), and closed a EUR 150M Series D extension in Oct 2026.
interesting_fact: Group14's silicon-carbon anode material promises up to 50% more energy density in any lithium-ion battery, and it is supplied at commercial scale to EV, consumer-electronics and aviation customers.
deep_cut_fact: He came to batteries from biotech: he spent the early part of a 30-year career stabilising molecules for drug makers Genentech, Alkermes and Nastech, with work ending up in marketed therapeutics, before applying the same molecular-level skills to ultracapacitor and battery electrode materials. He reports 50+ US patents.
notes: Technical co-founder; CEO Rick Luebbe is the main public face. Frequent industry-conference speaker (Benchmark Week). Group14's site blocks scripted access, so no press email was verified - check its press page manually. Strong energy-storage angle.

name: Rick Luebbe
current_role: CEO and Co-founder, Group14 Technologies (silicon-carbon battery materials, Woodinville/Bothell, WA)
profile: Rick Luebbe co-founded EnerG2 in 2003 (engineered carbon materials), led it to its 2016 acquisition by BASF, then spun out Group14 Technologies to commercialise silicon-carbon composite anode material (SCC55) that boosts lithium-ion battery energy density. Group14 has raised well over $1B (valued ~$5B per Hurun) and is building US and Korean manufacturing; he remains CEO in 2026.
interesting_fact: Group14's silicon-carbon anode material lets lithium-ion cells store substantially more energy and charge faster, and the company has partnered with cell makers such as Enovix and Forge Nano on US-made high-performance batteries.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career as an Army aviation officer: he led an aeroscout platoon in Desert Storm, earning the Bronze Star and two Air Medals, and later flew Apaches as commander of an attack helicopter company. He also co-founded B2B integrator Hubspan and worked at Booz Allen.

public_contacts.value: group14@missionc2.com (Mission Control, PR agency for Group14 - as listed in Jan 2024 release)

notes: Strong energy-storage angle; Group14 is a prominent US battery-materials unicorn. PR agency address is from a 2024 release and may be out of date. Group14 website blocks automated access, so no direct press email confirmed. Veteran background is a natural rapport point.

name: Michael Cassau
current_role: Founder and CEO, SKROL (Miami); founder and former CEO of Grover
profile: German entrepreneur, ex-Goldman Sachs investment professional and Rocket Internet executive, who founded Berlin tech-rental/subscription platform Grover in 2015 and grew it into a unicorn that raised about $2B. He stepped back from Grover at the end of 2023 and in 2024 launched SKROL in Miami, an AI-driven platform to acquire and grow small and medium-sized businesses.
interesting_fact: Grover pioneered renting rather than buying consumer electronics (phones, laptops, consoles) on monthly subscriptions and entered the US market via Miami.
deep_cut_fact: For SKROL he brought former Grover CTO Christopher Silva and finance lead Mitja Sadar with him; SKROL targets mainly brick-and-mortar SMBs and explicitly avoids restaurants, Amazon FBA and Shopify stores.
notes: Now Miami-based; no longer runs Grover (CEO Rob Straathof). No published personal contact found; LinkedIn or SKROL likely best.

name: Brynne Rojas
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Habi (proptech / iBuyer, Bogotá; operates in Colombia and Mexico)
profile: Brynne McNulty Rojas, a Miami-born, Harvard MBA, ex-Goldman Sachs real estate investor and ex-McKinsey consultant, co-founded Habi in Bogotá in 2019 with Merqueo co-founder Sebastián Noguera. Habi uses algorithmic pricing to buy, renovate and resell used homes and became Colombia's second unicorn (2022, US$200M round); in March 2026 it acquired Mexican broker-tech startup Pulppo.
interesting_fact: Habi prices tens of thousands of homes a month (30,000+ per month in 2021) and makes most of its offers automatically; its sales team rings a cowbell whenever a transaction is signed.
deep_cut_fact: She and Sebastián Noguera were selected as Endeavor's 100th and 101st entrepreneurs in Colombia (Habi was Endeavor Colombia's 54th company); before Habi she was VP of Global Corporate Strategy at hospitality startup Selina.
notes: Publicly known as Brynne McNulty Rojas. Habi's site lists only a general customer address (contacto@habi.co), no press email found. Habi founded in Bogotá; idea came from her own struggle to find a home remotely when moving to Colombia.

name: Sebastián Noguera Escallón
current_role: Co-founder & President, Habi (Colombia)
profile: Colombian entrepreneur who co-founded Bogota proptech Habi with CEO Brynne McNulty around 2019; it buys and sells homes for Latin America's middle class and became Colombia's second unicorn. Earlier he was Chief Digital Officer at Banco de Bogota and co-founded online grocer Merqueo.
interesting_fact: Habi uses data to give quick offers on middle-class apartments in Colombia and Mexico; he argues Latin Americans invest in apartments rather than the stock market.
deep_cut_fact: Before Habi he led the digital transformation of Banco de Bogota as its Chief Digital Officer, and he co-founded Merqueo, which became Colombia's largest digital supermarket.

name: Young-il Lee
current_role: Founder & CEO, HAEGIN (Seoul)
profile: Korean mobile-games veteran and co-founder of Com2uS who founded HAEGIN in Sept 2017. Its social game Play Together (2021) became a global hit with 200M+ downloads; HAEGIN raised a $110M Series B in 2022 from Kakao Games, Netmarble, SK Square and others.
interesting_fact: 'Haegin' means 'living long and happily' in old Korean; over 90% of the company's traffic and revenue comes from outside Korea.
deep_cut_fact: Lee co-founded Com2uS, one of Korea's pioneering mobile game makers, and later served as its EVP for Far East business before starting HAEGIN.
notes: $8B figure in source list looks inflated; public reports suggest ~$1B+ unicorn status.

name: Zhang Kai
current_role: Chairman (reported in June 2025 to have resigned), Haomo.AI (毫末智行), the Great Wall Motor-incubated autonomous-driving company
profile: Zhang Kai headed Great Wall Motor's intelligent-driving efforts and became chairman of Haomo.AI when that unit was spun out in 2019 to build its HPilot driver-assistance system and other autonomous-driving products. Haomo reached unicorn status and planned a Hong Kong IPO, but in June 2025 36Kr reported he had resigned, and the company halted operations in November 2025.
interesting_fact: Haomo built one of China's earliest automaker-affiliated AI computing centers for autonomous-driving training (announced 2022-23, the MANA OASIS 'intelligent computing center'), and its HPilot system was fitted to about 20 Great Wall models.
notes: Sensitive timing: Haomo effectively stopped operating in Nov 2025 (staff furloughed, unpaid-wage reports), and Zhang's resignation was reported in June 2025. Very common name; identity rests on the Haomo link. No published contact. Low priority.

name: Gu Weihao
current_role: Former CEO of Haomo.AI (Great Wall Motor-backed autonomous-driving firm); reported in Jan 2026 to be founding a new service-robot startup (hotel service robots)
profile: Chinese autonomous-driving executive (顾维灏) who led mass-production work on Baidu Apollo, then became founding CEO of Haomo.AI (Dec 2019), building driver-assistance and last-mile autonomous delivery for Great Wall Motor and others. He left in 2025 and reportedly started a robotics company in 2026.
interesting_fact: Under him Haomo delivered 11 products in its first 22 months; at the 2021 Zhongguancun connected-car forum he summed up its strategy as 'product is king, scale wins'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Haomo he led the mass-production effort for Baidu's Apollo autonomous-driving program; his 2026 robotics venture recruits largely from former Baidu and Momenta engineers and targets hotel service robots.
notes: Haomo reportedly halted operations in Nov 2025 (unconfirmed press reports), so the '$1B company' founder status is dated. No published contacts for him or the new robot company found.

name: Rajoshi Ghosh
current_role: Co-founder of Hasura; listed as Co-founder & Chief Ecosystem Officer at PromptQL (Hasura's AI spin-out/rebrand)
profile: Co-founded Hasura with Tanmai Gopal; its open-source GraphQL engine let developers spin up real-time APIs on databases and passed 100M+ downloads, with the company valued at $1B in 2022. She served as COO, and the founders have since launched PromptQL, an AI data-agent platform. She studied computational biology at NUS (per profiles).
interesting_fact: Hasura's open-source GraphQL engine reached more than 100 million downloads within about two years of launch.
deep_cut_fact: Hasura began as her idea for a healthy home-cooked food delivery company in Chennai; the founders pivoted when local developers wanted to use Tanmai's backend platform 'procrust.es', which evolved into Hasura - and she admits they were reluctant to drop the food idea.
notes: Current PromptQL title from a conference speaker page (https://www.ai-infra-summit.com/speakers/rajoshi-ghosh); verify. Route via Hasura/PromptQL.

name: Tanmai Gopal
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, PromptQL (AI data-agent/AI-native workspace spun out of Hasura); co-founder of Hasura
profile: IIT Madras computer-science graduate who co-founded Hasura with Rajoshi Ghosh. He started as CTO and later became CEO; Hasura's open-source GraphQL Engine has passed 600M downloads and reportedly runs under half the Fortune 500. In 2025 he steered the company into PromptQL, an enterprise AI analyst that raised a $25M Series B and a $100M Series C at a valuation above $1B, and it is now pitched as an AI-native workspace to replace Slack.
interesting_fact: After ChatGPT he concluded his own company was an existential risk and took it through 'three lives in eighteen months': GraphQL engine, AI analyst, then AI workspace. That included moving his team off Slack and living through what he calls three weeks of 'AI psychosis'.
deep_cut_fact: Hasura began as an internal tool. While building a food-delivery venture in Chennai with Rajoshi Ghosh, he wrote a database platform called procrust.es. He also helped create and teach IIT Madras's 'Introduction to Modern Application Development' course.
notes: Very accessible: a frequent conference speaker and podcast guest (The Ken's Zero Shot, July 2026). His X and LinkedIn links come from his AI Engineer speaker page. A strong fit for AI and data-infrastructure conversations.

name: Glenn Luk
current_role: Co-founder and board member, HealthCare.com (HealthCare Inc.); investor and writer on China's economy
profile: Glenn Luk co-founded HealthCare.com in 2014, an online marketplace that makes individual health and Medicare insurance easier for consumers to understand and buy, and sits on its board. He previously spent about a decade in Investcorp's technology investment group in New York. He has since been involved with blockchain, edtech and internet companies.
interesting_fact: He is a widely followed analyst of the Chinese economy, U.S.-China competition and China's high-speed rail. Steve Hsu's Manifold podcast (ep. 58, April 2024) featured his work on China's GDP and HSR.
deep_cut_fact: After college he joined Deutsche Bank in Hong Kong for about three years, doing M&A for Chinese state-owned oil & gas and power companies, before returning to New York in 2004 to join Investcorp. He grew up in suburban New Jersey with Taiwanese, Hong Kong and mainland Chinese heritage.
notes: Highly active on X (@GlennLuk) and Substack, making him one of the most reachable people in this lane. His power and energy background plus China infrastructure commentary make him a strong podcast fit. X bio also mentions he was previously at Catalyte.

name: Howard Yeh
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Revenue Officer, HealthCare.com (New York). His roles there went Co-Founder, then CEO, then COO, then CRO.
profile: Howard Yeh is a Penn graduate who started as a Merrill Lynch media investment banker and was a VC at VantagePoint. He co-founded BrokersWeb, an insurance ad network that made the Inc. 500 twice and was acquired by Vantage Media in 2011. He then co-founded HealthCare.com, a health-insurance marketplace that has raised $200M+ across Series A to C, and he still blogs on ACA, Medicare Advantage and insurtech.
interesting_fact: BrokersWeb, his first insurance company, grew revenue from $16M in 2010 to $55M in 2011 before Vantage Media acquired it. It was twice on the Inc. 500.
deep_cut_fact: Between BrokersWeb and HealthCare.com he co-founded ContactUs.com (2012-2015), a SaaS tool for better website contact forms and lead capture. He describes its sale to WorkWave in 2015 as a 'bite-sized acquisition'. He also writes on his blog about Asian American leadership and entrepreneurship.
notes: Very accessible: he runs an active personal blog (posts through March 2026) on healthcare markets, AI and founder stories, which is a natural hook for outreach. NYC-based. Don Loonam became HealthCare.com CEO in March 2021.

name: Jeff Smedsrud
current_role: Founder & CEO, Pivot Health (short-term/supplemental health insurance products, now part of HealthCare.com); co-founder of HealthCare.com
profile: Health-insurance marketing veteran who co-founded HealthCare.com, the health-coverage shopping and lead-generation company (Hurun lists it at a $1B valuation), and founded Pivot Health, an Arizona-based designer and marketer of short-term and supplemental health plans that HealthCare.com later acquired. Pivot Health products are sold through HealthCare.com sites such as Healthcare Insider.
interesting_fact: HealthCare.com both publishes consumer guides (e.g. Healthcare Insider) and manufactures its own short-term and supplemental health insurance products under the Pivot Health brand that Smedsrud founded.
notes: Low public profile; ThinkAdvisor ran a 2022 profile 'The View From HealthCare.com: Jeff Smedsrud' (paywalled/blocked, not read). pivothealth.com now redirects to healthcare.com/about-company. No press email found.

name: Jose Vargas
current_role: Co-founder and President, HealthCare.com (Miami/New York insurtech)
profile: Miami-based serial internet entrepreneur who has built online companies in Miami for about two decades and co-founded investment firm PeopleFund. In 2014 he co-founded HealthCare.com with Howard Yeh and Jeff Smedsrud - a marketplace to compare and enroll in health insurance and Medicare plans plus its own Pivot Health products. It reached a $1B+ valuation with a $180M Oaktree-led round in 2021.
interesting_fact: HealthCare.com's $180M round (led by Oaktree) made it one of Miami's unicorns; staff grew from ~100 to 425 in a year, and its CEO quipped 'it doesn't hurt that we have the world's greatest url.'
deep_cut_fact: He co-founded PeopleFund, which backed HealthCare.com, and earlier founded, grew and sold other online platform businesses; on the #MiamiTech Pod (Ep 53, Feb 2022) he discussed two decades of building online companies and M&A in Miami.
notes: Not to be confused with journalist Jose Antonio Vargas. No published press email found on healthcare.com.

name: Matias de Tezanos
current_role: Founder and CEO, PeopleFund (multi-family office / global tech investor); co-founder, HealthCare.com
profile: Costa Rican-born serial internet entrepreneur who founded Hoteles.com at about 20 (later acquired by Expedia), co-founded ad network ClickDiario (sold to Fox International Channels in 2006), led US insurance marketplace BrokersWeb (2008-2011) and co-founded health-insurance platform HealthCare.com (Inc. 500's #1 insurance company in 2019). He now invests globally via PeopleFund, founded 2012.
interesting_fact: Named a World Economic Forum Young Global Leader in 2009; his PeopleFund portfolio reportedly includes stakes in 12 unicorns among 30+ companies, and he was building an agri-tech venture turning plastic into biodegradable products (2023).
deep_cut_fact: He first went online in 1994 while on holiday in Punta del Este, Uruguay (Costa Rica had no access for him yet) - and publicly thanked Uruguay for it at the Punta Tech Meetup; website-building began as a hobby before Hoteles.com.
notes: Lives in Costa Rica (per El Observador 2023). matiasdetezanos.com is a parked domain, not his. PeopleFund site contact form is the only published route found. Spanish-language outreach may help.

name: João Pedro Resende
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Hotmart (Hotmart Company)
profile: Belo Horizonte-born computer scientist João Pedro Resende co-founded Hotmart in 2011 with university classmate Mateus Bicalho, building a platform that bundles payments, hosting and delivery for creators selling courses, ebooks and other digital products. Hotmart Company, which also owns Teachable and eNotas, sells into ~190 countries; global HQ moved to the Netherlands in 2016. He still leads it, now pushing AI tools.
interesting_fact: Resende and Bicalho were early figures in 'San Pedro Valley', the Belo Horizonte tech hub that grew from startups clustering in the São Pedro neighborhood.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, MobWorks (2004, with Bicalho), tried to build mobile apps and failed; at the same time he ran an online gaming forum, where he learned traffic, site optimization and monetization, lessons that fed into Hotmart.
notes: Known as 'JP Resende'. Hosts the annual Hotmart FIRE creator conference in Belo Horizonte (11th edition in 2026). Portuguese-language outreach recommended.

name: Mateus Bicalho
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Hotmart (Belo Horizonte, Brazil) - per company/press profiles
profile: Brazilian computer scientist (PUC-MG) who co-founded Hotmart in 2011 with university friend João Pedro Resende. Hotmart is a creator-economy platform handling hosting, delivery, payments and affiliate sales for digital products such as online courses, selling in 188+ countries; it became a unicorn and hosts the annual Hotmart FIRE event in Belo Horizonte.
interesting_fact: He was involved from the start in creating San Pedro Valley (SPV), the tech hub/startup community in Belo Horizonte's São Pedro neighborhood.
deep_cut_fact: Years before Hotmart, he and Resende founded MobWorks (2004-2006), a mobile-app developer that arrived before the technology was mature; Hotmart's alpha in 2010 was an affiliate-based platform for selling e-books.
notes: Co-founder JP Resende (CEO) is the company's main public voice; Bicalho is lower profile. Name sometimes spelled 'Matheus'.

name: Elizabeth Hunker
profile: Could not verify any Elizabeth Hunker as a founder of Human Longevity Inc. The company's own site credits co-founder Dr. J. Craig Venter (founded 2013, San Diego); no web source beyond a single funding-data aggregator links the name to the company, and no other public profile for an Elizabeth/Liz Hunker was found.
notes: Likely a data error in the source list. Human Longevity founder info: https://www.humanlongevity.com/about/ . Do not use for outreach without independent confirmation.

name: Dan Littman
current_role: Helen L. and Martin S. Kimmel Professor of Molecular Immunology, NYU Grossman School of Medicine; HHMI Investigator; Pfizer board member; scientific co-founder of Immunai
profile: Dan R. Littman is a leading immunologist best known for cloning the CD4 and CD8 T-cell genes. He has been at NYU since 1995 and an HHMI investigator since 1987, and is a member of the National Academy of Sciences and National Academy of Medicine. He is a scientific co-founder and advisory board member of Immunai (AI and single-cell immune profiling) and Vedanta Biosciences, and sits on Pfizer's board.
interesting_fact: As a postdoc in Richard Axel's Columbia lab he cloned CD8 and, within months, CD4, the genes that define the two main types of T cells. CD4 later turned out to be HIV's receptor, and his lab's HIV work contributed to identifying CCR5 as a drug target, which Pfizer's maraviroc now blocks.
deep_cut_fact: He was born in Bucharest in 1952. His family waited years to emigrate, finally leaving Romania in 1962, and spent six months in Rome while his father passed the US medical licensing exam before they came to the US with help from HIAS.
notes: Primarily an academic scientist; Immunai is one of several company affiliations. The best route is his NYU lab. 'Pfizer's maraviroc' is my identification: the transcript says only 'Pfizer makes a drug' targeting CCR5.

name: Noam Solomon
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Immunai
profile: Israeli mathematician and computer scientist (two PhDs, MIT math postdoc) who co-founded Immunai in 2018 with MIT alum Luis Voloch. Immunai maps the human immune system with single-cell multi-omics and AI (its AMICA database) to improve drug development, raising a $215M Series B and signing deals with pharma partners such as AstraZeneca.
interesting_fact: He entered Tel Aviv University at 14 and had a CS bachelor's by 19, then earned two PhDs (computer science and mathematics) before coming to MIT as a postdoc in 2017.
deep_cut_fact: As a second-grader who disliked school, he'd visit his family doctor for notes - and she would give him a riddle each visit, which he spent hours or days cracking; he credits this with his comfort being 'outside my comfort zone.' He also told an investor 'No' when asked if he knew how to map the immune system - and still got the investment.
notes: Frames Immunai's mission around reversing 'Eroom's Law' (drug development costs doubling every ~9 years) - a good podcast hook. Writes op-eds (Calcalist/CTech).

name: Steven Touw
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Immuta
profile: Steve Touw co-founded Immuta in 2015 with CEO Matthew Carroll and Mike Schiller, all veterans of U.S. intelligence-community data programs. Immuta sells data security and policy-based access-control software for cloud data platforms and became a unicorn. He was previously CTO of 42Six Solutions, which Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) acquired.
interesting_fact: He designed large-scale geo-temporal analytics for the U.S. intelligence community and Special Operations Command, including some of the very first Hadoop analytics and frameworks for multi-tenant data-policy controls, the ideas behind Immuta.
notes: Writes bylined articles on data security (RTInsights, Solutions Review). Some profiles say he studied geography (University of Maryland) and was a geospatial analyst, but I could not verify this, so it is left out. I found no published press email.

name: Chen Kuan
current_role: Founder and CEO (later reported as chairman), Infervision (推想医疗科技), Beijing
profile: Shenzhen-born founder of Infervision, a Beijing medical-imaging AI company started in 2016 whose deep-learning tools help radiologists screen CT scans for lung cancer, stroke and other conditions across hospitals in China, Europe, Japan and the US. Hurun lists Infervision as a $1bn unicorn; he was named to Fortune China's 40 Under 40 in 2024.
interesting_fact: Before university in the US he attended Singapore's Raffles Institution - alma mater of Lee Kuan Yew and Goh Chok Tong - on the way to studying at the University of Chicago.
deep_cut_fact: He left a joint economics-and-finance PhD at the University of Chicago, where he studied under Nobel laureate James Heckman, to start Infervision in 2015-16; he has said modelling markets from massive data felt 'basically no different from computational science'.
notes: Goes by 'CK' / Kuan Chen in English. Contacts are Infervision's general company addresses (global and China sites); no dedicated press email found.

name: Abhinai Srivastava
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Mashgin (AI computer-vision self-checkout, Palo Alto)
profile: IIT Delhi CS graduate who co-founded Mashgin (founded 2013; YC W15) with dorm-mate Mukul Dhankhar. Its barcode-free computer-vision kiosks let customers pay in about 10 seconds in stadiums, cafeterias and convenience stores. A 2022 $62.5M Series B led by NEA valued Mashgin at $1.5B.
interesting_fact: Mashgin says its system rings up multiple items in half a second with 99.9% identification accuracy, making checkout four times faster than cashiers.
deep_cut_fact: Mashgin began with a lunch line: co-founder Mukul Dhankhar, then working on Toyota computer-vision research, kept losing 30-40 minutes a day in a corporate cafeteria queue. He flew to California, reconnected with Srivastava (his dorm-mate at IIT Delhi), and his early demo convinced Srivastava to join.
notes: contact@mashgin.com is Mashgin's general company inbox (not personal). Prior employers (Yahoo/Microsoft/Facebook) come only from aggregator profiles and are unverified. Edge-AI/computer-vision angle rather than data center.

name: Mukul Dhankhar
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, Mashgin (computer-vision self-checkout, Palo Alto/San Francisco)
profile: IIT Delhi-trained computer-vision engineer who worked on camera-based perception for Toyota before co-founding Mashgin in 2013 with his IIT dorm-mate Abhinai Srivastava (YC W15). Mashgin's kiosks recognise multiple items without barcodes in about half a second; its 2022 NEA-led Series B valued it at $1.5bn, with kiosks in stadiums, airports, convenience stores and corporate cafeterias.
interesting_fact: Mashgin's kiosks ring up multiple items in roughly half a second with ~99.9% identification accuracy and no barcodes, and are installed at venues such as Madison Square Garden, Citi Field and Arrowhead Stadium.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from his own lunch break: while working on computer vision for Toyota in the early 2010s, he spent 30-40 minutes a day queuing in the corporate cafeteria, built a camera-based checkout demo, flew to California to pitch it, and won over his former IIT Delhi dorm-mate Abhinai.
notes: Surname also spelled 'Dhankar' in Mashgin's own press release. CEO Abhinai Srivastava is the more public co-founder. help@ is a general/support inbox; no dedicated press email found.

name: Anand Babu (AB) Periasamy
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO (with Garima Kapoor), MinIO, Inc. (Redwood City, CA)
profile: Free-software developer (Annamalai University CS) who co-founded Gluster (open-source distributed file system, sold to Red Hat in 2011 for a reported ~$136m), then MinIO in 2014 with Garima Kapoor and Harshavardhana. MinIO's S3-compatible object storage (AIStor) is a common data layer for AI and private-cloud infrastructure.
interesting_fact: He says he built Gluster 'accidentally' while trying to solve storage for supercomputing clusters; Red Hat's acquisition made Gluster the basis of Red Hat Storage.
deep_cut_fact: In 2004, as CTO of California Digital Corp., he led development of Lawrence Livermore's 'Thunder', then the world's second-fastest supercomputer; he also wrote GNU FreeIPMI and GNU FreeTalk and sat on the board of Free Software Foundation India.
notes: Very accessible and podcast-friendly: has guested on Last Week in AWS 'Screaming in the Cloud' and speaks at open-source conferences. Strong data-center/AI-storage fit. MinIO's site offers only a generic contact form; X handle is self-published in his SCALE speaker bio.

name: Frederick Kautz
current_role: Cloud-native security / zero-trust architect and open-source leader; SPIFFE Steering Committee member (current employer not confirmed; TheOrg lists HumanForm Technologies)
profile: Software engineer named among MinIO's co-founders in 2015 coverage (Nov 2014 founding, after he was a senior principal engineer at Red Hat and CTO of GridX); MinIO's own site now credits three other founders. He went on to co-found Network Service Mesh, co-create OmniBOR and ProtoBOM, lead architecture at Elevance Health and co-chair KubeCon + CloudNativeCon.
interesting_fact: He co-authored NIST SP 800-204D on integrating software-supply-chain security into DevSecOps CI/CD pipelines, which shaped the US DoD's Enterprise DevSecOps Fundamentals v2.5, and co-wrote the SPIFFE/SPIRE book 'Solving the Bottom Turtle'.
deep_cut_fact: He defined the term 'CNF: Cloud Native Network Function', the idea of running telecom network functions on Kubernetes-style cloud infrastructure, and in 2019 built one of the first federated-learning platforms for healthcare research that kept patient data private.
notes: MinIO founder status is disputed: 2015 sources (StorageNewsletter, YourStory) list him, but MinIO's About page names only Periasamy, Kapoor and Harshavardhana - mention MinIO carefully. Frequent conference speaker/podcast guest, so approachable; best route is LinkedIn or his site zt.dev.

name: Garima Kapoor
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, MinIO (Silicon Valley; co-CEO since early 2024, previously CFO/COO)
profile: Garima Kapoor, an economist with a PhD in accounting and finance from Nirma University, co-founded MinIO in 2014. MinIO's high-performance, S3-compatible object storage (open-source roots, now the commercial AIStor) is widely used for AI and data-lake workloads. She is also an active angel investor and adviser to Silicon Valley startups.
interesting_fact: MinIO is squarely in the AI data-center build-out: its AIStor was named Databricks' ISV Storage Partner of the Year and provides the object data store for NVIDIA's STX reference architecture.
deep_cut_fact: Before tech she planned an academic life: she told The Founder Formula podcast (Oct 2025) that she loved economics and set out to be a college economics professor, which is why she did a PhD. She still says 'I love teaching' and jokes that in the Valley 'everyone has to be a technologist no matter what.'
notes: Strong fit for the data-center/AI-infrastructure theme (AI storage) and an accessible guest: she does podcasts and conference talks (Founder Formula, techstrong.tv, WomenTech). LinkedIn is linked from her official MinIO author page.

name: Harshavardhana .
current_role: Co-founder of MinIO, Inc. (long-time CTO/lead engineer); not listed on MinIO's current leadership page (co-CEOs Garima Kapoor and AB Periasamy) - present title unclear
profile: Harshavardhana (he uses a single name; 'Harsha') co-founded MinIO in Nov 2014 with Anand Babu 'AB' Periasamy and Garima Kapoor after working at Gluster (acquired by Red Hat). MinIO built the most widely used open-source, S3-compatible object store, reached a ~$1bn valuation, and now sells AIStor, a commercial object-storage 'data engine' for AI factories and enterprise AI.
interesting_fact: MinIO's founding principle, as he describes it, was simplicity: software anyone can run on a laptop, marketed to developers first, then monetised with a Red Hat-style commercial model.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career around 2006 as a research engineer at Gluster, the distributed file-system startup co-founded by AB Periasamy and later acquired by Red Hat - the partnership that led to MinIO.
notes: Mononymous - the trailing '.' in the input name is a placeholder. Engineer with low media profile; he was still committing to MinIO's repo in Dec 2025. MinIO's shift of the open-source project to maintenance mode (2025-26) is a sore point with the community - handle tactfully. Strong AI-storage/data-center fit.

name: Arik Faingold
current_role: Listed as a founder of Pentera (formerly Pcysys), Israeli automated security-validation company; current role unknown
profile: Arik Faingold is listed as a founder of Pentera, the Tel Aviv/Boston company founded in 2015 (as Pcysys) that sells an autonomous penetration-testing / exposure-validation platform and was valued at about $1B in its 2022 round. Pentera's current site names only Dr. Arik Liberzon as founder and Amitai Ratzon as CEO, and does not mention Faingold.
interesting_fact: Pentera now sells AI agents that run attack simulations against live production web apps within customer-set guardrails; this is the 'automated pentesting' category it helped create in 2015.

public_contacts.value: https://pentera.io/newsroom/ (press contact obfuscated; company Contact Us page)

notes: Identity not confirmed from a primary source: Pentera's about page credits only Arik Liberzon as founder. Faingold was probably an early co-founder or executive at Pcysys who has since left. Kept minimal (search budget exhausted).

name: Arik Liberzon
current_role: Founder and board member, Pentera (formerly co-founder & CTO)
profile: Israeli cyber-warfare veteran (Dr. Arik Liberzon) who co-founded Pcysys, now Pentera, in 2015 to turn offensive-security expertise into software. Pentera's automated penetration-testing / security-validation platform became a unicorn in 2022 (backers include Insight, Blackstone, K1, Evolution). Amitai Ratzon is CEO; Liberzon served as CTO and now sits on the board as founder.
interesting_fact: Pentera's platform automates what human 'ethical hackers' do, safely running real attack techniques against a company's own network to validate which exposures are actually exploitable; CEO Amitai Ratzon joined Liberzon while the company was still in stealth mode.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Pentera he headed the Cyber Warfare group in the Israeli military's Computer Service Directorate, a unit with experience in both defensive and offensive cyber.

name: Debasish Chakraborty

profile: Debasish Chakraborty co-founded Perfios in 2008 with V.R. Govindarajan. Perfios is a Bengaluru B2B fintech whose bank-statement analysis, KYC and credit-decisioning software is used by Indian and international lenders. It became a unicorn in 2024 and operates across South and Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Africa. He sits on its board, and Nitin Chugh is group CEO.
interesting_fact: Perfios says it started in 2008 to 'transform the financial landscape of the nation'. Its tools now underpin digital lending decisions for many Indian banks and NBFCs, with operations across 15+ countries.
notes: Low public profile, and the company sometimes spells his name 'Debashish'. Co-founder V.R. Govindarajan is the more public face. The web search budget was exhausted, so no deep-cut fact was found.

name: V.R. Govindarajan
current_role: Co-founder & Executive Chairman, Perfios Software Solutions (Bengaluru)
profile: Indian software entrepreneur (IISc Bangalore engineering; MS in CS in the US; database work at DEC and IBM) who co-founded IT product-engineering firm Aztecsoft, sold to MindTree in 2008. With Debasish Chakraborty he then founded Perfios, which pivoted from consumer personal-finance software to B2B credit-underwriting and financial-data analytics for banks and became a unicorn after a 2022 Warburg Pincus-led round.
interesting_fact: Perfios started as a web-based personal finance management tool for retail consumers before pivoting to serve lenders; today its software can read data from 250+ financial institutions and returns credit decisions in under a minute.
deep_cut_fact: He became a founder back in the 1980s, when it was unusual for trained engineers in India to enter the start-up space; years later Perfios was fielding unexpected enquiries from recruitment portals, healthcare firms and even matrimony services.
notes: Perfios CEO is now Sabyasachi Goswami; Govindarajan is executive chairman. Only a general company inbox is published.

name: Amit Bareket
current_role: Co-founder & former CEO, Perimeter 81 (acquired by Check Point); reportedly VP of SASE at Check Point Software (verify)
profile: Israeli cybersecurity entrepreneur and IDF Unit 81 veteran who, after engineering stints at IBM XIV Storage and BigBand Networks, co-founded consumer VPN SaferVPN with Sagi Gidali (sold to J2 Global) and then Perimeter 81, a cloud network-security/SASE platform. Check Point agreed to acquire Perimeter 81 for about $490M in August 2023, after it had been valued at $1B in 2022.
interesting_fact: Perimeter 81 is named after IDF Unit 81, the elite technology intelligence unit Bareket served in; co-founder Sagi Gidali came from Unit 9900.
deep_cut_fact: He holds eight patents covering storage, mobile applications and UI, graduated cum laude in Computer Science and Economics from Tel Aviv University, and his company bio jokes he has 'a poker face that's great for keeping secrets or for deadpan humor.'
notes: Contributor to SC World and Forbes Technology Council. No published press email; route via Check Point media relations.

name: Sagi Gidali
current_role: Co-founder of Perimeter 81 (acquired by Check Point in 2023, now 'Harmony SASE'); current role not confirmed
profile: Israeli serial entrepreneur who with Amit Bareket first built consumer VPN SaferVPN (sold to J2 Global), then reused its six-year-old network infrastructure to found zero-trust network-security company Perimeter 81 in Tel Aviv in 2018. Perimeter 81 hit a $1B valuation in a 2022 Series C led by B Capital and was bought by Check Point for $490M in 2023.
interesting_fact: Perimeter 81 went from a $100M valuation to unicorn status in about two years (2020-2022), with 2,500+ customers including Fortune 500 firms; Check Point rebranded it Harmony SASE after buying it.
deep_cut_fact: Perimeter 81 was not built from scratch: its first product ran on the global network that Gidali and Bareket had spent about six years building for their earlier consumer company, SaferVPN.
notes: Long-time partner of Amit Bareket. I could not confirm his post-acquisition role (Check Point or a new venture), and found no published contact; LinkedIn is likely the best route. The deep-cut is company history, not a personal detail.

name: James Edwards
current_role: Co-founder, Pet Circle (Sydney); current title not verified
profile: Australian co-founder, with CEO Mike Frizell, of Pet Circle, the Sydney-based online pet supplies retailer founded in 2011 as 'Paws for Life' and renamed in 2014. Pet Circle raised a A$125M Series C in December 2021 at a valuation above $1B, added a further $75M in 2023, and has expanded into pet insurance and vet services.

profile: Mike Frizell co-founded Australian online pet-supplies retailer Pet Circle with James Edwards in mid-2011. It grew 300%+ between 2013 and 2015, raised A$125M Series C in Dec 2021 at a valuation above $1B, added pet insurance in 2023 and secured a further $75M that year to fund expansion.

name: Noam Ben-Zvi
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Placer.ai (location/foot-traffic analytics), Los Altos, CA / Tel Aviv
profile: Israeli founder who leads Placer.ai, which uses anonymised mobile-location data to show foot traffic and visitor patterns for any physical place; it counts 4,000+ customers across retail, commercial real estate, CPG, hedge funds and municipalities and has been valued at $1.5-2B. He co-founded it with Zohar Bar-Yehuda, Oded Fossfeld and Ofir Lemel.
interesting_fact: He sums up the product as letting you 'research anything you can draw a polygon around' - a geofence around a mall, store or stadium - and argues it is a more current alternative to once-a-decade Census data.
deep_cut_fact: The founders had earlier built data startup BlueTail, which was sold to Salesforce; when they started Placer in 2016 they were, in his words, 'a bunch of technology guys' who 'didn't even know who CBRE or Cushman' were - commercial real estate became their first big market.
notes: Media-friendly CEO who gives trade-press interviews (Bisnow, Trademark Property). X account is the company's, not personal. Data/AI angle rather than data-centre infrastructure.

name: Oded Fossfeld
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Placer.ai (Los Altos, CA / Israel) - location analytics
profile: Oded Fossfeld, a Ben-Gurion University alumnus, co-founded Placer.ai around 2014 with CEO Noam Ben-Zvi and serves as CTO. Placer uses anonymized, privacy-compliant mobile location data to measure foot traffic at stores, malls and properties, and became a ~$2bn unicorn; it is now adding AI capabilities and data partnerships such as Bloomberg.
interesting_fact: Placer.ai turns aggregated smartphone location signals into foot-traffic analytics used by retailers, landlords and investors; in 2026 it deepened a data-entitlements collaboration with Bloomberg.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2022 CTech book review he championed Andrea Wulf's 'Chasing Venus', about 18th-century expeditions to time the transit of Venus, saying it made him 'feel humble' about the origins of the geographic calculations that are Placer's 'bread and butter'.
notes: Low-profile technical co-founder; CEO Noam Ben-Zvi is the public face. Title also appears as Chief Data Scientist / VP R&D on some databases. Press route: press@placer.ai (media contact Jesse Kent, Oct 2026 release).

Placer.ai turns anonymised mobile-location data into foot-traffic analytics for retailers, real-estate owners and investors; it became a unicorn (~$1.5-2bn valuation) and Hurun has listed him among unicorn founders since 2022.

deep_cut_fact: A former lieutenant in the IDF's Unit 8200, he was a serial founder before Placer: he co-founded Juntos! (2011-12) and was co-founder, CEO and developer of Roamie (2012-13).
notes: Low personal media profile; CEO Noam Ben-Zvi is Placer's usual spokesperson. Deep-cut source is a people-profile aggregator (also echoed in a Placer job listing on Welcome to the Jungle) - verify on his LinkedIn before using.

profile: Zohar Bar-Yehuda is an Israeli data scientist who co-founded Placer.ai with Noam Ben-Zvi (CEO), Oded Fossfeld (CTO) and Ofir Lemel (CPO). Placer's location-analytics platform estimates foot traffic to stores, malls and venues from anonymised mobile data, serves 4,000+ customers in real estate, retail, CPG and the public sector, and was valued around $2B as a Hurun unicorn.
interesting_fact: Placer.ai turns anonymised location data into near-real-time foot-traffic estimates for almost any US venue, and has become a go-to source for retailers, landlords, investors and journalists tracking consumer activity.
deep_cut_fact: Before Placer he was a senior algorithm developer at OrCam, the Jerusalem company making AI-powered wearable cameras that read text aloud for blind and visually impaired people. Before that he was a system architect at Verint. He studied engineering at Ben-Gurion University of the Negev.
