current_role: Founder, Rad Power Bikes (CEO until 2022); current role not publicly confirmed
profile: Mike Radenbaugh built his first e-bike as a teenager in Humboldt County, California, and turned custom conversions into Rad Power Bikes, launched with Ty Collins in 2015 via a ~300-bike Indiegogo pre-sale. The Seattle direct-to-consumer brand became North America's biggest e-bike seller during the pandemic boom (valued ~$1.65B+ in 2021). He handed the CEO role to Phil Molyneux in 2022.
interesting_fact: At 15 he rigged a battery and motor onto an old mountain bike to handle a 34-mile round-trip commute to high school; a local Redwood Times story led neighbours to order conversions from him.
deep_cut_fact: He paid his way through Humboldt State and grad school at UC Davis with money from building custom e-bike conversions, years before Rad sold its first production bike.
notes: Contact listed is his own Medium blog (type 'substack' used as nearest category). Rad Power Bikes went through Chapter 11 and was sold to Life Electric Vehicles in early 2026, after he had left as CEO; avoid that framing. Good energy/EV angle via his founding story and battery-electric micromobility.

name: Tyler Collins
current_role: Unknown; co-founder and former Chief Marketing Officer of Rad Power Bikes
profile: Ty Collins co-founded Seattle-based Rad Power Bikes with Mike Radenbaugh and Marimar White-Espin; relaunched in 2015 with the RadRover, it became North America's largest direct-to-consumer e-bike brand (Hurun: ~$2B). He led marketing and sales (VP, then CMO). Rad Power was sold out of bankruptcy to Life EV in March 2026; his current role is not public.
interesting_fact: Rad Power skipped the traditional dealer channel and sold direct to riders, letting it offer premium e-bikes at roughly half the price of comparable models. Collins and his co-founders were on Forbes' 2017 30 Under 30 list (Manufacturing & Industry).
deep_cut_fact: Collins is a 2010 journalism graduate of Humboldt State (now Cal Poly Humboldt). The idea began with co-founder Mike Radenbaugh's home-built 'frankenbikes' in small-town Humboldt County in 2007; Collins helped turn it into a business.
notes: Goes by 'Ty Collins'. Low public profile compared with Radenbaugh; Rad Power's 2025 bankruptcy and 2026 sale to Life EV make company channels unhelpful. No published personal contact found.

name: Iddo Gino
current_role: Founder of RapidAPI (now Nokia-owned); per his own site, working on new ideas and advising dev-tools/API companies
profile: Israeli-born, Bay Area-based founder who started RapidAPI as a teenager and spent about a decade building it into what he calls the world's largest API marketplace, used by over 5 million developers and valued at about $1B. RapidAPI is now part of Nokia; he says he is working on new ideas and advising dev-tools and API companies.
interesting_fact: He is a 2017 Thiel Fellow (Peter Thiel's program that pays young people to skip or leave college to build companies) and a Forbes 30 Under 30 honoree.
deep_cut_fact: He keeps a personal Posthaven blog ('Random thoughts') with hands-on tinkering posts, e.g. a Mac Finder automation to right-click any file and copy it as Markdown for AI prompts with Microsoft's markitdown, and fixing Cloudflare 'too many redirects' on Posthaven.
notes: He published the email himself as 'iddo [at] gino.email' on his About page, which makes it the best direct route. Nokia ownership is inferred from Nokia's DPO address on RapidAPI's site; the web-search budget ran out before deal terms could be confirmed.

name: Mickey Hasalvsky
profile: Listed by Hurun as a co-founder of RapidAPI (Tel Aviv/San Francisco API marketplace, valued ~$1B; its technology and team were later acquired by Nokia, per a November 2024 Nokia release). The name is usually spelled Mickey Haslavsky; his current role could not be confirmed in this pass.
notes: Name in input likely misspelled (Haslavsky). Search budget ran out and Wikipedia/Nokia pages were blocked, so nothing verified beyond the Hurun listing. Nokia acquisition release: https://www.nokia.com/about-us/news/releases/2024/11/18/nokia-to-acquire-rapid-technology-and-team-to-boost-network-api-ecosystem/

name: Brian Murphy
current_role: Founder & CEO, ReliaQuest (Tampa, FL)
profile: Florida State accounting/finance graduate and former PwC consultant who founded cybersecurity firm ReliaQuest in Tampa in 2007. It grew into an AI-driven security-operations (GreyMatter) company valued at about $3.4B. He is also an FSU trustee and active in Tampa's startup scene.
interesting_fact: He bootstrapped ReliaQuest with a second mortgage and credit cards and taught himself programming despite having no tech background.
deep_cut_fact: He chairs the board of Embarc Collective, the Tampa nonprofit startup hub, giving back to the local founder ecosystem.
notes: Strong Florida/FSU ties (trustee). Possible warm routes via Embarc Collective or FSU.

name: Magnus Wanberg
current_role: Founder, reMarkable (Oslo); exact current executive title not re-verified
profile: Norwegian entrepreneur who founded reMarkable in 2013 and spent three-plus years developing the original E Ink 'paper tablet', launched in 2017. The distraction-free tablets (reMarkable 2, Paper Pro, Paper Pro Move) passed one million users by 2022 and lifted the Oslo company to a $1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: At Harvard he left his laptop and phone at home to work only on paper; by graduation he had four overflowing boxes of notebooks, and standing over them he conceived a device merging paper with digital.
deep_cut_fact: As a child he wore the keys off his family's IBM PC and Game Boy, and by 18 he was building and selling computers out of his father's garage.
notes: Check whether he is still CEO (company has had leadership changes) before addressing him by title.

name: Rahul Singhvi
current_role: Co-founder and former CEO of Resilience (National Resilience Inc.); Resilience is now led by President & CEO William S. Marth - Singhvi's current role unconfirmed
profile: Biopharma manufacturing executive who co-founded Resilience in 2020 to broaden access to complex medicines and safeguard supply chains, building a biologics CDMO with more than one million square feet of North American operations. The company raised billions in its early years and has since been restructured around sites in Ohio and Toronto under new leadership.
interesting_fact: Resilience was founded in 2020, in the midst of the pandemic, with two goals: broaden access to complex medicines and safeguard the supply chains that carry them.
notes: Research cut short by a web-search quota: his prior career (widely reported as ex-Novavax/Takeda Vaccines/Flagship Pioneering) and current activity were not verified here. No longer appears on Resilience's leadership page.

name: Roth Martin
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Creative and Innovation Officer, Rothy's (San Francisco) - since Jan 2024, previously President
profile: San Francisco native and former gallery owner who co-founded Rothy's with ex-investment banker Stephen Hawthornthwaite. Rothy's makes washable 3D-knit shoes and bags from recycled plastic bottles in its own factory on a make-to-demand model, and reached a ~$1B valuation. In Jan 2024 he moved from president to chief creative and innovation officer.
interesting_fact: Rothy's debuted its recycled-bottle flats in the vegetable aisle of San Francisco's Ferry Plaza Farmers Market, between eggplants and Brussels sprouts, after four years of development that nearly sank the company.
deep_cut_fact: He came to shoes as a former San Francisco gallery owner, not a footwear person. On Rothy's early struggles: 'We had no idea how complicated shoes were... We almost didn't have a company because we couldn't make the product' - development started in a factory in Maine.
notes: Aggregator profiles say he started as a Glencore commodities trader and co-founded Hedge Gallery (2003); not verified on a primary source. No published press email found on rothys.com.

name: Stephen Hawthornthwaite
current_role: Co-founder and Chair of the Board, Rothy's (CEO until Jan 2024)
profile: Former tech M&A banker (GCA Savvian, InfoSpace corporate development) who co-founded San Francisco shoe brand Rothy's with Roth Martin in 2012 (launched 2016), known for flats knit from recycled plastic bottles. He was CEO until January 2024, when Jenny Ming took over and he became board chair; Brazil's Alpargatas bought a 49.9% stake at a $1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Rothy's built its own vertically integrated factory in Dongguan, China, the world's first shoe manufacturer to earn both LEED and TRUE Platinum certification, and has diverted 166M+ plastic bottles from landfill.
deep_cut_fact: On a 2020 Talks at GS episode he said the founding bet was that 'fashionable products aren't always comfortable... and sustainable products historically haven't been made with the quality and attention to detail they deserve', so Rothy's set out to do all three at once.

public_contacts.value: adore@rothys.com (Anna Doré, Senior Director of Communications, as of Jan 2024)

notes: Spent ~20 years in M&A/investment banking before Rothy's (directory profiles also list Duke undergrad and Wake Forest law degree; unverified). Press contact is from a Jan 2024 release; may be stale.

name: Jiang Hua (蒋华)
current_role: Executive Director & CEO, Ruqi Mobility (如祺出行 / Chenqi Technology, HKEX: 9680), Guangzhou
profile: Career GAC Group executive (joined 1997) who has led Ruqi Mobility as CEO since June 2019, when GAC and Tencent launched it as a Guangzhou ride-hailing platform. Ruqi raised a ~$153M Series A, then listed in Hong Kong in July 2024 positioning itself as a robotaxi operator, with Pony.ai as a strategic shareholder and partner.
interesting_fact: Ruqi was co-founded by carmaker GAC and Tencent and marketed its Hong Kong IPO as an autonomous-driving operations story, running robotaxi services in the Greater Bay Area.
deep_cut_fact: Before Ruqi he spent two decades inside GAC: general manager of GAC Business/Trading (广汽商贸) 2008-2018, then head of GAC's mobility project team (2018-19) that spawned Ruqi; he holds a business-management BA from Beijing Technology and Business University (1994) and a Sun Yat-sen University MBA (2003).
notes: Hurun lists him as founder; he is better described as founding CEO of a GAC/Tencent-backed venture (corporate, not founder-owned). No published IR/press email found; HK-listed so IR route via company site / HKEX filings.

name: Johnny Mitrevski
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Scalapay (Milan-based buy-now-pay-later fintech)
profile: Shellharbour-born engineer (UOW telecoms engineering, 2000) who spent over a decade at Nortel Networks in Wollongong and later was a technology manager at Commonwealth Bank. In 2019 he co-founded Scalapay with CEO Simone Mancini after spotting a lack of BNPL options in Italy; it became Italy's first fintech unicorn in Jan 2022 and in 2025 secured €70M from the EIB.
interesting_fact: Scalapay hit unicorn status in January 2022, under three years after founding, and was dubbed the 'Wollongong-founded' unicorn because its tech team was built in the Illawarra while the business runs from Milan.
deep_cut_fact: He calls himself 'a child of the public education system' and spent over a decade commuting by local train to Nortel Networks' office on the University of Wollongong campus - where he met future Scalapay engineering colleagues.
notes: Splits time between Wollongong and Milan. No published press email found; Simone Mancini is the public face. University of Wollongong alumni relations has profiled him and could be a warm route.

name: Simone Mancini
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Scalapay (Milan/Dublin buy-now-pay-later fintech)
profile: Tuscan-born, raised in Darwin, Australia, Mancini co-founded Scalapay in 2019 with CTO Johnny Mitrevski after earlier startups and product roles in Sydney. Scalapay became an Italian-founded BNPL unicorn after a $497M Series B in 2022 (Tencent, Tiger Global) and now serves 13M+ users and 12,000+ brands; it reported monthly break-even in 2025, took a €70M EIB venture loan and expanded via Stripe to 30+ countries in 2026.
interesting_fact: Mancini said Scalapay reached monthly break-even during 2025 and expected to finish 2026 in profit, after the EIB granted it a €70M Scale Up Debt loan.
deep_cut_fact: Before Scalapay he took a sewing course and launched his own online fashion brand, then in 2015 co-founded with Mitrevski EatTonight (a Sydney marketplace for home-cooked meals) and Sweetly (a platform for cake-decorating artists). His parents were lay Catholic missionaries sent from Empoli to Darwin.
notes: Speaks Italian with a Tuscan accent; gives interviews to Italian business press (EconomyUp, Milano Finanza, Fortune Italia 40 Under 40). No published press email found on scalapay.com.

name: Christian Floerkemeier
current_role: Co-founder, CTO and VP Product, Scandit (Zurich)
profile: Cambridge-trained electrical engineer with an ETH Zurich computer-science PhD who was Associate Director of MIT's Auto-ID Lab, part of the team behind RFID tech now used in major supply chains. In 2009 he co-founded Scandit with fellow ETH PhDs Samuel Mueller and Christof Roduner; its smartphone computer-vision barcode/'smart data capture' software made it a $1B unicorn in 2022.
interesting_fact: Scandit was bootstrapped for three and a half years, only raising its first round in 2013; he did all the early product, algorithm and computer-vision work himself and jokes that he once did the jobs of everyone who now reports to him.
deep_cut_fact: Within his first week as a PhD student he joined a Walmart-MIT research collaboration on the 'next-generation barcode'; he also co-founded Fosstrak, the leading open-source RFID software platform.
notes: Technical co-founder, comfortable with media (writes bylines, speaks at NRF). Fosstrak detail confirmed on Scandit management page.

name: Christof Roduner
current_role: Co-founder, CIO and VP Engineering, Scandit (Zurich)
profile: Swiss computer scientist and co-founder (2009, with Samuel Mueller and Christian Floerkemeier) of Scandit, the Zurich-based smart data capture company whose smartphone-camera barcode scanning and computer vision is used in retail and logistics; it reached unicorn status in 2022. He leads Scandit's software engineering and research organisation.
interesting_fact: Scandit grew out of ETH Zurich/MIT Internet-of-Things research, aiming to bridge physical objects and digital information just as smartphone cameras became capable enough.
deep_cut_fact: Before research he founded a company that built and sold a CRM system and ran the internet business at a Zurich IT firm; as an ETH/MIT researcher he co-founded Fosstrak, the leading open-source RFID platform implementing the EPC Network spec, used by SAP and Orange.
notes: Studied CS and business at University of Zurich and Uppsala. Appeared on Swisspreneur podcast ep. 249 (2022). Samuel Mueller (CEO) is the main public face.

name: Samuel Mueller
current_role: CEO and Co-founder, Scandit
profile: Swiss computer scientist (PhD ETH Zurich; MSc CS and MA financial economics, University of Zurich) who co-founded Zurich-based Scandit in 2009 with Christian Floerkemeier and Christof Roduner. Scandit sells smartphone-based barcode, ID and label scanning plus store-intelligence software powered by computer vision and AI to retailers, logistics and airlines.
interesting_fact: Scandit started from the idea of bridging physical objects and digital information, using barcodes as the entry point just as phone cameras were becoming ubiquitous.
deep_cut_fact: Before Scandit he was a corporate researcher at IBM Zurich Research Lab, earning three IBM Invention Achievement Awards and an IBM Research Division Award; his ETH PhD was in computer science and temporal logics.
notes: Regular conference speaker and podcast guest; press email is the best route.

name: Sachin Nayyar
current_role: Founder, CEO & Chairman, Saviynt (identity security, El Segundo, CA)
profile: Serial identity-security entrepreneur who founded Vaau (acquired by Sun Microsystems, where he became Chief Identity Strategist), then Securonix (SIEM; US$1B+ Vista-led growth investment in 2022) and Saviynt. He stepped back to executive chairman at Saviynt in 2018 and returned as CEO in 2023; in Dec 2025 Saviynt raised US$700M led by KKR at about a US$3B valuation.
interesting_fact: Saviynt's US$700M Series B (Dec 2025), led by KKR with Sixth Street Growth, TenEleven and Carrick Capital, valued the identity-security company at roughly US$3B and was pitched as making identity 'the foundation for the AI era'.
deep_cut_fact: He served five years as Board Chair of the Health Information Sharing & Analysis Center (H-ISAC), the healthcare sector's cyber-threat-sharing body; per CEO Magazine he sold his first company, Vaau, to Sun Microsystems at age 28.
notes: Founded both Saviynt and Securonix. PR handled by agency Inkhouse. Vaau-at-28 detail from https://digitalmag.theceomagazine.com/sachin-nayyar/ (page blocked to fetch; seen in search summary).

name: Tanuj Gulati
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Securonix; part of Austin FC ownership group
profile: Cybersecurity entrepreneur and investor. A founding member of identity-governance firm Vaau (sold to Sun Microsystems), he co-founded SIEM company Securonix with Sachin Nayyar and served as CTO, growing ARR past $100M. Nayyar also founded Saviynt; I found no primary source naming Gulati as a Saviynt co-founder.
interesting_fact: He is part of the ownership group of MLS club Austin FC; a lifelong soccer fan, he played varsity soccer at school and still plays.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a BS in computer applications and an MBA from Oklahoma State University, and serves on the boards of the Miracle Foundation and Austin Speech Labs.
notes: Hurun lists him under Saviynt; documented roles are Vaau, Oracle/Sun, Securonix. Verify the Saviynt link before outreach.

name: Michael Gilbert
current_role: Founder, Semios (Vancouver); CEO until Amie Thesingh's appointment in late 2025 - current title unconfirmed
profile: Canadian chemist (PhD, UBC) who founded Semios in 2010 to bring pheromone-based mating disruption and wireless orchard sensors to growers, reducing pesticide use. Semios grew into an ag-data platform covering 100M+ acres.
interesting_fact: Semios pairs aerosol pheromone dispensers with a wireless sensor network, confusing pests like codling moth so they can't mate instead of killing them with sprays.
deep_cut_fact: He told the Georgia Straight that pheromones, though well understood, were used on 'less than one per cent of the farms that could be using them' - and that 'farmers are always environmentalists'.
notes: Common name; confirmed via Semios coverage. The Semios Group named Amie Thesingh CEO (Sept/Oct 2025).

name: Laura Behrens Wu
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Shippo (San Francisco)
profile: German-born entrepreneur who left her University of St. Gallen master's to co-found Shippo in San Francisco (2013-14) with Simon Kreuz; the multi-carrier shipping API/platform serves 100,000+ e-commerce merchants and was valued at $1B in 2021. In 2026 she is still CEO, pushing AI-driven shipping analytics ('Shippo Intelligence').
interesting_fact: Shippo was born after she and Simon Kreuz ran an online shop as students and found shipping was the problem they couldn't solve; she was named to Forbes 30 Under 30 and Inc.'s Female Founders 100.
deep_cut_fact: She came to the US for a compulsory master's internship intending to stay just three months ('Ich hatte die Absicht, nur drei Monate zu bleiben'); she was named HSG (St. Gallen) Founder of the Year in 2015.
notes: Media contact listed on Shippo's Oct 2026 press release. Speaks German; featured in the German government's 'Makers of Tomorrow' series.

name: Max M. Diez
current_role: Chairman & Co-Founder, Assaia (Zurich AI/computer-vision platform for aircraft turnarounds); co-founder of Shippo
profile: Zurich-based serial B2B software entrepreneur, listed with Laura Behrens Wu and Simon Kreuz as a 2013 co-founder of Shippo, the San Francisco multi-carrier shipping API later valued at over $1B. He then co-founded Assaia, whose ApronAI uses existing apron cameras to manage aircraft turnarounds in real time for customers such as Alaska Airlines, Southwest and Fraport. He was CEO until January 2024, when he became chairman.
interesting_fact: On handing over Assaia's CEO role in 2024, he predicted that around 80% of airlines and airports would buy turnaround-optimisation technology within a few years, a category Assaia says it created.
deep_cut_fact: Assaia began as computer-vision technology without a use case. Diez and co-founder Nikolay Kobyshev ran workshops to find one, and Swissport's head of innovation saw a demo and said, in effect, 'if this actually worked' it would change apron operations.
notes: Rarely in the press about Shippo, where Laura Behrens Wu is the public face; his early Shippo CTO title appears only in aggregator profiles. Assaia also pitches sustainability benefits (cutting APU use and taxi time), which could interest an energy podcast.

name: Simon Kreuz
current_role: Co-founder and President, Shippo (multi-carrier shipping API/platform, San Francisco). Title per 2020 Shippo Q&A; current status not re-verified.
profile: German-born Simon Kreuz co-founded Shippo with CEO Laura Behrens Wu, whom he met at business school in Switzerland. Shippo gives e-commerce merchants and platforms a single API and app to compare carriers, buy labels and handle customs, an 'abstraction layer for the shipping network' in his words. It reached a ~$1B valuation.
interesting_fact: Shippo started when he and Behrens Wu ran a side-project online store and found that importing products in bulk from South Africa and shipping them around Europe was the hard part. The company sold its first label on February 14, 2014.
deep_cut_fact: He chose the name because hippos are herd animals that protect their group and can travel on land and water. He's bugged when people call the company 'Goshippo', and Shippo still didn't own shippo.com, so he offered a bonus to anyone who could help get it. Favorite reads include Cixin Liu's 'Remembrance of Earth's Past' trilogy.
notes: Self-described as preferring to work outside the spotlight, and very few interviews exist. No 2025-26 mentions found, so confirm he is still active at Shippo. Fun icebreaker: he'd rather chat over a German beer and would most like to meet Arnold Schwarzenegger.

name: Gaurab Chakrabarti
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Solugen (Houston chemicals-from-biology company)
profile: Gaurab Chakrabarti is a physician-scientist (Forbes 30 Under 30; author on 20+ publications and patents). In 2016 he co-founded Solugen with MIT chemical engineer Sean Hunt. Solugen's 'Bioforge' plants combine enzymes and metal catalysts to turn corn sugar into chemicals such as hydrogen peroxide and organic acids that normally come from petroleum. It is building a second Bioforge in Marshall, Minnesota.
interesting_fact: In June 2024 Solugen got a conditional commitment for a $213.6M DOE Loan Programs Office loan guarantee for Bioforge Marshall. It is a ~500,000 sq ft plant next to an ADM corn facility, which DOE called its largest single bioindustrial manufacturing investment since the 2022 biotech executive order.
deep_cut_fact: Solugen started on a $10,000 MIT grant meant to cover salaries, rent and equipment, in a $150/month space near the Houston airport. Chakrabarti jokingly called himself 'the Heisenberg of hydrogen peroxide'. Seed investor Seth Bannon of Fifty Years called it one of the 'sketchiest' labs he had seen.
notes: Strong fit for the energy and decarbonization angle. Secondary sources (search results only) say he and Hunt met at a poker game in Texas while Hunt was visiting from MIT. Whether the DOE loan guarantee has closed was not verified.

name: Sean Hunt
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Solugen (Houston chemicals company using enzymes + metal catalysis - 'Bioforge' plants)
profile: MIT chemical engineer (SM '13, PhD '16) who co-founded Solugen in 2016 with physician-scientist Gaurab Chakrabarti. Solugen makes hydrogen peroxide and other commodity chemicals from sugar using engineered enzymes and metal catalysts instead of petrochemicals; Hunt leads the chemienzymatic process technology behind its Bioforge plants. Forbes 30 Under 30.
interesting_fact: Solugen's first lab was leased for $150/month near the Houston airport in a facility TechCrunch said made it possibly 'the first legitimate multi-million-dollar company to start out in a meth lab'; Chakrabarti calls himself 'the Heisenberg of hydrogen peroxide'.
deep_cut_fact: Their first customers were float-spa owners: one saw the MIT $100K pitch video and shared it in a Facebook group of ~400 US float spas. Hunt then spent $7,000 at Home Depot building a pilot reactor - 'this little PVC bubble column' - and fed it 55-gallon drums of sugar. He calls himself a 'recovering biotech skeptic'.
notes: Great fit for energy/industrial podcast: Solugen now pitches its Forges as dual-use for energy systems and defense. Hunt has appeared on podcasts (e.g. MCJ 'Inevitable' ep.175 with Chakrabarti, The Chemical Show).

name: Mark Frank
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, SonderMind (Denver behavioral-health platform)
profile: West Point graduate and former Army officer, Kellogg MMM ('07) and ex-Morgan Stanley investment banker turned serial healthcare entrepreneur. He co-founded SonderMind in 2014 with clinician Sean Boyd to make in-network therapy accessible, partly after struggling to find a therapist that fit his needs and insurance; it raised a $150M Series C in 2021.
interesting_fact: As an Army officer he led three platoons between ages 22 and 24 before serving as a company executive officer.
deep_cut_fact: In 2009 he founded Denver Cyberknife (later Anova Cancer Care), personally guaranteeing over $6M of bank debt - 'the alternative to success was personal insolvency' - and sold it, returning 12x to his outside investor.

public_contacts.value: MedCity News author page (his contributed columns)

notes: Frequent podcast guest (HLTH 'The Beat', others); veteran-focused - featured by NVCA: https://nvca.org/startup-story/the-denver-unicorn-making-in-network-mental-healthcare-actually-work-for-patients-therapists-and-veterans/

name: Jacques Fu
current_role: Founder, PETE (PETE Learning, per Crunchbase); former co-founder and CTO of Stax Payments (formerly Fattmerchant)
profile: Orlando technologist and University of Central Florida alum who was co-founder and founding CTO of Stax (originally Fattmerchant), the subscription-pricing payments processor started in 2014 with Suneera Madhani and Sal Rehmetullah. Stax passed $100M in recurring revenue and was valued at $1B+ after a $245M Series D in 2021, becoming Orlando's first unicorn. He has since founded PETE and invests in startups.
interesting_fact: Stax was Orlando's first startup to reach unicorn status; its model - flat monthly subscription instead of per-transaction payment fees - grew out of Madhani selling payment terminals from her VW Beetle.
notes: Co-founded the Orlando Devs developer meetup community (per search snippets of SpeakerHub/Crunchbase; pages returned 503, so unverified). A podcast lists him as author of a book 'Time Hacks' (unverified). Profile pages: https://drupal.speakerhub.com/speaker/jacques-fu, https://crunchbase.com/person/jacques-fu. No published email found.

name: Salman Rehmetullah
current_role: Co-founder, Worth (Worth AI), Orlando, Florida
profile: Sal Rehmetullah co-founded Orlando-based payments company Stax with his sister Suneera Madhani in 2014; after nearly 10 years it had over $140M recurring revenue, $245M raised and a $1.1B+ valuation, and the siblings exited in 2023. They now run Worth, an AI platform that automates SMB underwriting, onboarding and verification for banks and fintechs; it raised a $20M seed led by TTV Capital in 2025.
interesting_fact: On Worth's edge: 'We have the full 360 financial data of a small business, which has been nonexistent.' Worth pre-fills applications and automates KYB, ownership identity, fraud, bank-account and real-time financial statement checks.
deep_cut_fact: Stax and its sibling co-founders were EY Entrepreneur Of The Year 2021 Florida finalists.
notes: Goes by 'Sal'. Has a Qwoted expert-source page (app.qwoted.com/sources/sal-rehmetullah), a possible journalist-facing route. Avoid the 2023 Stax exit circumstances. EY finalist fact is from the press-release title (page body was blocked).

name: Li Hangwen
current_role: Co-founder of Stemirna Therapeutics (斯微生物); removed as chairman and CEO by the board on 7 May 2024, a decision he has challenged in court
profile: Li Hangwen (李航文) co-founded Shanghai mRNA company Stemirna Therapeutics in 2016 with Shen Haifa and led it as chairman and CEO; it was a lead mRNA developer in China's COVID vaccine programme and became a unicorn. In 2024 the board replaced him with Shen Haifa; Li told Jiemian he was in the US and looking for new investors.
interesting_fact: Stemirna's COVID mRNA vaccine received emergency use authorisation in Laos; in a 2023 interview on the Nobel Prize for mRNA, Li predicted therapeutic cancer mRNA vaccines would see major success within 3-4 years.
deep_cut_fact: Commenting on Karikó and Weissman's 2023 Nobel, Li noted that before COVID the focus of mRNA vaccines had 'always been cancer treatment', and called a Nobel for a technology within five years of its breakthrough rare in biomedicine.
notes: Sensitive: ongoing control dispute with Stemirna (board removal, lawsuit, travel restrictions reported in 2023) and he is reportedly in the US. Avoid company-related outreach angles. Sources: https://m.jiemian.com/article/11669588.html , https://m.jiemian.com/article/11597777.html . No public contact found.

name: Kevin Jones
current_role: Co-founder, Tarana Wireless (Milpitas, CA). MarketScreener lists him as VP Product Innovation 2009-2020; current role unknown.
profile: Kevin Jones is listed by financial-data aggregators as one of the 2009 founders of Tarana Wireless, a next-generation fixed-wireless broadband equipment maker, and as its VP of Product Innovation until 2020. Tarana's radios deliver high-speed non-line-of-sight broadband and cancel interference. The company has spent more than $400M in private R&D and is valued at about $1B+.
interesting_fact: Tarana's CEO told Congress in 2024 that the company was founded in 2009 by a wireless-industry veteran and three immigrant PhD students whose thesis was about bringing internet access to villagers in Ghana. Its radios adapt to channel conditions 5,000 times a second.
notes: Very little public information. His founder status comes only from aggregators (MarketScreener: founder and VP Product Innovation 2009-2020), and no official Tarana page naming him could be loaded (site returns 403). Common name, so take care not to confuse him with other Kevin Joneses (e.g. KORE Wireless). Low priority.

name: Miri Ratner
current_role: Co-Founder and VP R&D, Vayyar Imaging (Yehud, Israel)
profile: Israeli R&D executive with 20+ years in wireless and telecom engineering who co-founded Vayyar Imaging in 2011 with Raviv Melamed and Naftali Chayat. Vayyar builds single-chip 4D mmWave imaging radar used in automotive in-cabin sensing, eldercare fall detection, smart home and industrial applications, and raised $108m in a Koch-led Series E in 2021, reaching unicorn valuation.

name: Iman Abuzeid
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Incredible Health (San Francisco nurse-hiring and career platform)
profile: Sudanese-American physician (MD, University College London) and Wharton MBA who worked in healthcare consulting and McKinsey, then health-tech product roles, before co-founding Incredible Health in 2017 with CTO Rome Portlock. The platform matches nurses with hospitals and offers career tools; it reached a $1.65B valuation in 2022, making her one of very few Black women to lead a $1B+ company.
interesting_fact: Forbes named her one of America's Richest Self-Made Women in 2024 (est. ~$350M), and Inc. put her on its 2020 Female Founders 100.

notes: Frequent podcast guest (TechCrunch 'Found' ep.1, Masters of Scale, a16z, Wharton Pulse). Trained as a doctor - healthcare workforce/AI angles work well.

name: Rome Portlock
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Incredible Health (San Francisco)
profile: MIT-trained software engineer who was a principal platform engineer at mobile-health company AliveCor, where he met Iman Abuzeid; together they founded Incredible Health in 2017 (after pivoting during the NFX accelerator). Its marketplace flips nurse hiring so hospitals apply to nurses; customers include Kaiser Permanente and Johns Hopkins, and it was valued at $1.65B in 2022. He has led engineering and data since day one.
interesting_fact: CEO Iman Abuzeid calls Portlock 'the best engineer I've ever worked with'; the founders abandoned their first idea six weeks before NFX demo day and pivoted to what became Incredible Health.
deep_cut_fact: The idea came from a mismatch the founders noticed: doctors around Abuzeid complained of understaffing, while nurses in Portlock's own family said they applied to many jobs and often heard nothing back.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Iman Abuzeid is the public face. Mention the family-of-nurses origin only in general terms.

name: Ross Andrew Paquette
current_role: Founder, CEO and Chairman, Maropost (Toronto)
profile: Toronto entrepreneur who founded Maropost in 2011 after working in SaaS and email marketing, spotting a gap for an email provider with strong deliverability and service. Maropost has grown into a 'unified commerce' platform (ecommerce, POS, marketing automation, service, AI analytics) used by 5,000+ brands such as UNTUCKit and Luxottica, reaching a ~$2B valuation; he also runs Maropost Ventures.
interesting_fact: Maropost was meant to be a small 'lifestyle business' he ran on the side for a few clients; word-of-mouth referrals grew it so fast that by 2017 it was ~$30M in revenue and billed as Toronto's fastest-growing company.
deep_cut_fact: Asked for the best advice he ever got, he said: 'Secret to success is to never stop understanding your own business'; he described his work style in one word -- 'Tirelessly' -- and in 2017 was re-reading Ashlee Vance's Elon Musk biography.
notes: Bootstrapped founder; also backs startups via Maropost Ventures and environmental/wildlife causes via MaropostCARES. Maropost site lists sales/success emails but no press email.

current_role: Founder and CEO, Redesign Health (New York healthcare venture studio)
profile: Former Lone Pine Capital partner and lead healthcare analyst (earlier Carlyle, Goldman Sachs, Google and BCG) who founded Redesign Health in 2018, a venture studio that co-founds, staffs and funds new healthcare companies from scratch. Redesign raised $175M in Dec 2024 and has been valued around $2B.

notes: Search results indicate a press office address press@redesignhealth.com and named comms contacts on Business Wire releases (e.g., Dec 2024 $175M release), but I could not re-verify them on-page; check redesignhealth.com/press.

name: Hayden Adams
current_role: Founder and CEO, Uniswap Labs
profile: Former Siemens mechanical engineer (Stony Brook grad) who taught himself Solidity in 2017 and launched Uniswap, the automated-market-maker decentralized exchange on Ethereum, in November 2018. As CEO of Uniswap Labs he leads development of the Uniswap protocol, wallet and the Unichain layer-2 network.
interesting_fact: Uniswap was inspired by a Vitalik Buterin blog post on automated market makers; it launched on Ethereum mainnet on November 2, 2018 and became the largest decentralized exchange.
deep_cut_fact: Karl Floersch showcased Adams' early Uniswap demo in a Devcon 3 talk; an attendee, Pascal Van Hecke, then reached out and gave him a grant to fund his next month of research, kick-starting weekly calls that kept the project going.
notes: Very active on X (@haydenzadams); that is the most direct public route. Media inquiries via media@uniswap.org.

name: Jonathan Ellis
current_role: Founder & CEO, Brokk (AI coding tools; product now marketed as SlopCop at slopcop.com)
profile: Co-founder and former CTO of DataStax and first chair of the Apache Cassandra project. He and Matt Pfeil left Rackspace in 2010 to found Riptano in Austin (renamed DataStax), the commercial Cassandra company later pivoted to real-time data for AI and acquired by IBM in 2025. He now runs Brokk, building static-analysis and review tooling for AI coding agents.
interesting_fact: He became the first chair of Apache Cassandra when it graduated from the Apache incubator, and directed the project from 2010 until stepping down in 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Before Cassandra, around 2005 he built a multi-petabyte storage system for backup service Mozy using Reed-Solomon encoding; a PyCon talk about it led Rackspace to hire him, where evaluating NoSQL databases drew him to Cassandra.
notes: Highly technical; writes the company blog himself (e.g. Nov 2026 post on cost-efficient coding with expensive models). brokk.ai now redirects to slopcop.com; company has a public Discord linked from the site. Strong data-infrastructure angle for the podcast.

deep_cut_fact: A Virginia Tech CS grad, he started in infrastructure at Blacksburg email-hosting startup Webmail.us, then built and ran Rackspace's Email and Apps infrastructure development group.

Magic Eden became the leading Solana NFT marketplace, expanded to Bitcoin Ordinals and other chains, hit a $1.6B valuation in 2022 and launched its ME token in Dec 2024.

In 2021 he co-founded Magic Eden with Jack Lu, Sidney Zhang and Zhuoxun Yin; it became Solana's dominant NFT marketplace and a unicorn within months. We didn't know how long the revenue was going to last.' The first six people all worked from six different addresses with no office.

Within a year, Southchip shipped the SC8801, billed as the industry's first buck-boost charging chip supporting USB Type-C Power Delivery. Lei Jun's Shunwei Capital led its 2018 Series A, its first-ever chip-design investment.

name: Dave Rogenmoser
current_role: Co-founder and Chairman of the Board, Jasper (AI marketing platform), Austin TX
profile: Kansas-raised serial founder who co-founded Jasper, a generative-AI writing/marketing platform, in 2021; it hit unicorn status within ~18 months (valued $1.5B in 2022). He was CEO for its first two years, handed the CEO role to ex-Dropbox president Timothy Young in Sept 2023, and remains chairman.

profile: John Philip 'JP' Morgan co-founded Jasper (launched Feb 2021 as Conversion.ai, then Jarvis) with Dave Rogenmoser and Chris Hull, and built its technical architecture as CTO. Jasper raised $125M at a $1.7B valuation in Oct 2022. The trio previously co-founded YC-backed Proof (W18). Reports say he and Rogenmoser stepped back from day-to-day roles in Sept 2023.

name: Lin Xiuhua
current_role: Shareholder associated with HiTHIUM (Xiamen Hithium Energy Storage); spouse of founder/chairman Jeff Wu (Wu Zude)
profile: Lin Xiuhua (林秀華) is listed by Hurun as a founder of HiTHIUM, the Xiamen battery energy-storage maker founded in 2019. HiTHIUM's Hong Kong IPO filing describes her as the spouse of founder Jeff Wu; she held 82% of predecessor entity Zhuhai Haiheng at its 2019 formation before transferring her stake to Wu in 2021. She has no public operating role.
interesting_fact: HiTHIUM, founded only in 2019, says it has passed 200 GWh of cumulative battery shipments and ranks among the world's top two energy-storage cell suppliers.
deep_cut_fact: Per HiTHIUM's HKEX listing application, Lin Xiuhua held 82% of Zhuhai Haiheng (the original HiTHIUM vehicle) when it was set up in June 2019, with co-founder Jason Wang holding 18%.
notes: Very low profile and not an operating executive. The Hurun 'founder' label seems to reflect her shareholding as Jeff Wu's spouse. Best route is HiTHIUM media relations (China: Naoki Chen chenlq@; North America: Ivy Xu xuyf01@; Europe: jiangm@; RoW: liuy15@hithium.com, per Jan 2026 release), aimed at Jeff Wu.

name: Xu Xiaohua
current_role: Founder, Chairman and CEO, Anhui Huasun Energy Co. (Huasun)
profile: Xu Xiaohua (Jimmy Xu) is a former vice president and executive director of Hanergy Thin Film Power Group who founded Huasun Energy in Xuancheng, Anhui in 2020. He bet the company on heterojunction (HJT) solar cells; within about three years Huasun raised over RMB 5bn in 2023 and became the world's youngest PV unicorn and a leading HJT maker.
interesting_fact: Chinese media nicknamed him the 'HJT madman' (异质结狂人) for staking Huasun entirely on heterojunction technology while most of the industry chose TOPCon; Huasun ranked 12th on TIME's World's Top GreenTech Companies of 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He studied in the physics department of Beijing Normal University before entering solar at Hanergy, where he was named executive director of Hanergy Thin Film in 2016 after Li Hejun stepped down.
notes: Uses English name Jimmy Xu in Huasun press releases. Only general company inboxes found; no dedicated press email. Huasun is preparing an IPO.

name: Huang Yuqing
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, MegaRobo Technologies (镁伽科技 / Mega Robotics), Beijing
profile: Huang Yuqing co-founded MegaRobo in 2016 with Qiao Zhixin and Zhang Yan to build lab-automation 'robot scientists' for life sciences plus precision inspection/cutting systems for semiconductor and battery manufacturing. Backed by Bosch, WuXi AppTec, Goldman Sachs and Sinovation, it was valued at ~10.5bn yuan and filed for a Hong Kong IPO in June 2025.
interesting_fact: Explaining why he targeted labs, Huang said life-science experimental methods are 'almost the same as they were 100 years ago', with practitioners spending over 80% of their time on basic work; during COVID MegaRobo delivered its first sample-dispensing prototypes 25 days after project start.
deep_cut_fact: The three MegaRobo co-founders were old colleagues at measurement-instrument maker Rigol Technologies; around 2010 Huang concluded from rising labour costs that robots replacing human labour was a major trend. He studied Information Engineering at Xi'an Jiaotong University and holds a Tsinghua MBA.
notes: Company email is a general business/customer-service inbox, not a press desk. Crunchbase/Caproasia list him as 'Daniel Huang'. HK IPO status after the June 2025 filing not confirmed.

name: Pei Feng
current_role: President, Greater Bay Technology (GBT, 广州巨湾技研), Guangzhou
profile: Pei Feng (裴锋), a South China University of Technology PhD, led GAC Group's ultra-fast-charging research team from 2014 and became president of Greater Bay Technology, the GAC-incubated battery maker founded in Sept 2020. GBT makes extreme-fast-charging (XFC) EV batteries; it opened a 4 GWh XFC plant in Guangzhou in 2023 and is building a Chongqing base.
interesting_fact: Pei says GBT's batteries reached a 7.5-minute fast-charge level in 2022, three years ahead of the US Department of Energy's goal; its 'Phoenix' battery was marketed as charging for ~600 miles in about eight minutes.
deep_cut_fact: Before GBT existed, Pei had been leading a GAC R&D center team on ultra-fast charging systems since 2014, six years before the company was spun out with private investors taking control.
notes: Hurun lists him as founder; press usually titles him president. Some English outlets (Just Auto) misspell his name 'Gong Feng'. No published personal or press contact found; route via GBT corporate PR.

name: Shen Ziyu
current_role: Chairman & CEO, ECARX Holdings (Nasdaq: ECX); Chairman, SiEngine Technology
profile: Shen Ziyu (Ziyu Shen) co-founded automotive-tech firm ECARX with Geely founder Li Shufu in 2017 and chairs SiEngine, the ECARX/Arm China-backed auto-grade chip designer (7nm cockpit SoCs) valued at ~$1B. He leads ECARX, which supplies smart-cockpit computing to Geely brands and others, and listed on Nasdaq via SPAC in 2022.
interesting_fact: SiEngine, founded in 2018 as a joint venture of ECARX and Arm China, is one of China's homegrown automotive chip makers; its 2022 ~$148M round was led by Sequoia.
deep_cut_fact: Before ECARX he was an engineer then senior manager at Shanghai General Motors (2006-08), senior manager at Shanghai OnStar Telematics (2009-11), and GM of Shanghai Pateo (2012-16); he holds a master's in information security from Shanghai Jiao Tong University.
notes: Hurun lists him as SiEngine founder; SiEngine's day-to-day founder/CEO is Wang Kai, while Shen is chairman. Best route is via ECARX IR/media contacts.

name: Zhang Xinbo
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Tongdun Technology (同盾科技), Hangzhou
profile: Zhang Xinbo (张新波) co-founded Hangzhou-based Tongdun Technology in 2013 with CEO Jiang Tao and others, and serves as its CTO. Tongdun started in big-data anti-fraud/risk control for lenders and expanded into AI 'intelligent decision' products for finance, government and internet firms; Hurun lists it as a ~$1B unicorn.
interesting_fact: Tongdun began in 2013 as a big-data anti-fraud and credit risk-control provider and is now one of China's best-known fintech risk-control unicorns, serving banks, government and internet clients.
deep_cut_fact: In a Feb 2022 TMTPost 'Tanlu 2022' interview he summed up Tongdun's 2021 in three keywords - compliant development, digital transformation and supporting small and micro businesses - and argued intelligent decision-making will become infrastructure of the digital economy.
notes: Low public profile; few personal details published (aggregators list him as Tongdun co-founder/CTO, Nankai University alumnus - unverified). mkt@xiaodun.com is the 'business cooperation' inbox shown on tongdun.cn (Xiaodun is a Tongdun brand). Best route is via Tongdun corporate/marketing.

name: li Zexiang
current_role: Founder & Chairman, CiDi Inc. (希迪智驾, HKEX: 3881); Professor, HKUST; also chairman of Googol Technology and founder of XbotPark
profile: Li Zexiang (李泽湘) is an HKUST robotics professor and serial hard-tech founder. He co-founded motion-control maker Googol Technology (ChiNext 2023), mentored DJI founder Frank Wang and chaired DJI, and founded Changsha-based CiDi in 2017, which makes autonomous mining trucks and V2X gear and listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: CiDi's Dec 2025 debut made it Hong Kong's first listed company focused on commercial-vehicle autonomous driving; its retail tranche was ~22x oversubscribed. Li also runs the XbotPark incubator network, which has spawned dozens of robotics startups.
deep_cut_fact: One of the first students in Li's HKUST Robocon training class was Frank Wang, who went on to found DJI; the team lost in 2004, won Hong Kong in 2005. Li studied EE and economics at Carnegie Mellon before a Berkeley PhD, and in 2019 shared the IEEE Robotics and Automation Award for civilian-drone contributions.
notes: Hurun spells him 'li Zexiang'; company is CiDi (希迪智驾), HQ Changsha. CiDi site lists cidipublicaffairs@cidi.ai for ecosystem cooperation; IR page at cidi.ai/cn/investor/. Also reachable via HKUST ECE faculty page. Award source: https://ec.hkust.edu.hk/node/7828

name: Ma Wei
current_role: Co-founder, Executive Director and Executive Vice Chairman, CiDi Inc. (希迪智驾, HKEX: 3881), Changsha
profile: Dr. Wei Ma (马潍), a Bay Area chip veteran, co-founded CiDi in 2017 with HKUST professor Li Zexiang (of DJI fame). CiDi makes autonomous mining and logistics trucks and C-V2X road systems, and listed in Hong Kong in Dec 2025. Ma is executive vice chairman; Albert Sibo Hu is CEO.
interesting_fact: CiDi was the first company focused on commercial-vehicle autonomous driving to list on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange (Dec 2025); its driverless mining-truck fleets now run mixed coal-mining and stripping operations in China's northwest Gobi.
deep_cut_fact: Before Silicon Valley he was a lecturer at Xidian University (1985-89), then earned a PhD in signal processing at the UK's University of Surrey (1994); he spent a decade at National Semiconductor (2002-12) and five years at Texas Instruments (2012-17) before co-founding CiDi.
notes: Name in Chinese filings is 马潍 (not 马伟). Hurun label 'Cidi' = CiDi Inc./希迪智驾. cidi.ai lists info@cidi.ai as media contact; cidipublicaffairs@ is for ecosystem cooperation. Deep-cut career data comes from HKEX-listing executive bios (via lixinger), single source.

name: Junwei Bao
current_role: Co-founder, Chairman, President and CEO, Seyond Holdings Ltd. (formerly Innovusion; HKEX: 2665)
profile: Peking University physics grad with a Berkeley EECS PhD who co-founded lidar maker Innovusion in Silicon Valley in 2016 with Yimin Li; renamed Seyond in 2023, it supplies Falcon lidar to NIO and others. Seyond listed in Hong Kong via a de-SPAC in December 2025, and Bao remains chairman and CEO.
interesting_fact: Before founding Innovusion, Bao worked at Baidu USA (2014-2016) as head of the Autonomous Driving hardware & sensors team and also head of HPC, developing hardware acceleration and high-performance networking for data centers.
deep_cut_fact: Bao co-founded Timbre Technologies (semiconductor metrology), acquired by Tokyo Electron in Feb 2001, then spent 13 years at Tokyo Electron America rising to VP of Engineering; in 2001 he won the IEEE Transactions on Semiconductor Manufacturing Best Paper Award. Berkeley professor Costas Spanos now sits on Seyond's board.
notes: info@seyond.com is the general/ESG feedback address published by the company (no dedicated IR email found). Data-center angle: led Baidu USA's HPC/data-center hardware acceleration work. Seyond still loss-making (FY2025 revenue US$154m).

name: Yimin Li
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Seyond (formerly Innovusion), lidar maker headquartered in Sunnyvale, CA
profile: Optical/laser engineer who co-founded Innovusion with ex-Baidu hardware head Junwei Bao in Silicon Valley in 2016 to build image-grade 1550nm lidar. Renamed Seyond in Dec 2023, the company supplies NIO's Falcon lidar and went public on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange in Dec 2025 via a de-SPAC merger with TechStar Acquisition (agreed valuation HK$11.7B).
interesting_fact: Innovusion's Falcon 1550nm lidar is standard equipment on almost all NIO models; Li said in 2023 that it ranked No.1 globally in passenger-vehicle lidar volume and revenue in 2022.
deep_cut_fact: Li trained in quantum electronics and, before Innovusion, worked at Velodyne, Baidu, Agilent, GE Healthcare and AOSense (a quantum-sensing/atom-interferometry firm), building 20+ years in electronic, optical and laser tech.
notes: Low public profile; CEO Junwei Bao is the usual spokesperson. A Seyond media contact appears in a Dec 2024 de-SPAC press release (AccessWire) but could not be verified directly, so not listed. Best route: Seyond corporate/press channels.

name: Chen Zuochuan
current_role: General manager & vice chairman (and legal representative), Hebei Kuntian New Energy Co. (河北坤天新能源)
profile: Chen Zuochuan (陈佐川) is listed as GM, vice chairman and legal representative of Hebei Kuntian New Energy, a lithium-battery anode-material maker in Yuanshi county, Shijiazhuang, that grew out of graphitization processing. Kuntian raised 3B+ yuan in 2022-23 from Sinopec Capital, SK China, Fosun and others (peak valuation ~12.9B yuan). In Sept 2026 Xuetian Salt announced a plan to buy 100% of it.
interesting_fact: Kuntian traces back to the Huaiyang carbon works founded in 2000 and became a 'county-town unicorn'; its 2026 deal to be acquired by a Hunan state-owned salt company is part of a wave of anode-maker takeovers.
deep_cut_fact: In Dec 2024 Kuntian unveiled what it called an industry-first continuous graphitization furnace process at its Yuxi, Yunnan base (phase one: 40,000 t/yr, 1.1B yuan).
notes: Hurun's 'Chen Zuochuan' matches 陈佐川 (GM/vice chairman/legal rep per 36Kr and registry data); chairman and controlling shareholder is Song Zhitao (宋志涛, ~20.4%), so 'founder' label is uncertain. Very low public profile, no published contacts found; company site ktxny.com.cn unreachable.

name: Robert Duva
current_role: Co-founder of Invoca (formerly RingRevenue); co-founder of Fin & Field, Santa Barbara
profile: Rob Duva co-founded Santa Barbara-based RingRevenue in 2008 with Jason Spievak and Colin Kelley; it became Invoca, an AI-powered call-tracking and conversation-intelligence platform valued at $1B+. He served as COO and a board member. The founding team came from VoIP firm CallWave. He is now also listed as co-founder of Fin & Field, a marketplace for hunting and fishing trips.
interesting_fact: RingRevenue's pitch was letting advertisers track phone calls the way they track clicks; within 18 months of founding the eight-person team had raised $3.5M and signed the biggest customer in its target (affiliate marketing) market.
deep_cut_fact: Before Invoca he was at CallWave (VoIP firm, $40M IPO in 2004) and is a named inventor on CallWave call-processing patents filed in 2004, e.g. US8750469B1 'Methods and systems for call processing'.
notes: Low public profile; no personal contact published. Fin & Field (finandfield.com) appears to be a side venture. Third-party profiles (Crunchbase) describe him as Invoca co-founder/COO; current day-to-day Invoca role unclear (CEO is Gregg Johnson). Hunting/fishing interest is a possible rapport angle.

name: Jeff Flowers
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Wasabi Technologies (Boston hot cloud object storage)
profile: Serial infrastructure entrepreneur who co-founded Boston-based Wasabi Technologies (cloud object storage, valued ~$2B) with David Friend in 2015 and serves as its CTO. The pair previously co-founded online-backup company Carbonite, where Flowers was CTO; Wasabi grew out of their vision for a cheaper, faster next-generation storage architecture.
interesting_fact: Flowers and David Friend have together started, built and sold five technology companies; Carbonite's backup technology, built by their team, backs up hundreds of millions of new files a day.
deep_cut_fact: He holds both a B.S. and an M.S. in information and computer science from Georgia Tech, and sits on the Board of Trustees of Walnut Hill School, a Massachusetts arts high school that feeds Juilliard, the New England Conservatory and Boston Ballet.
notes: Wasabi newsroom lists Lindsay Daly (Sr. Director, Corporate Communications) as press contact via press@wasabi.com. Good fit for data-center/storage topics. Sometimes spelled 'Jeffry Flowers' in filings.

name: David Friend
current_role: Co-founder, President & CEO, Wasabi Technologies (hot cloud storage, Boston)
profile: Serial Boston entrepreneur who has co-founded about seven companies, including Computer Pictures, Pilot Software, Faxnet, Sonexis and cloud-backup firm Carbonite (co-founded 2005, public 2011). In 2015 he co-founded Wasabi with Carbonite co-founder Jeff Flowers; the low-cost S3-compatible cloud storage provider is now valued around $2B and is pitched at AI/data-heavy workloads.
interesting_fact: Before computing, Friend worked on synthesizers at ARP Instruments in the 1970s (including later versions of the ARP Odyssey) and has said the lesson he carried into Wasabi is simplicity.
deep_cut_fact: An avid mineral and gem collector, he donated the Friend Gem and Mineral Hall at the Yale Peabody Museum; he also has a concert hall named for him at Berklee College of Music, chairs the board of Boston Baroque, and was a David Sarnoff Fellow at Princeton's engineering graduate school.
notes: Very accessible, media-friendly CEO (frequent bylines in TechRadar, VentureBeat, theCUBE). Wasabi press team: Lindsay Daly, Sr. Director of Corporate Communications, via press@wasabi.com. Good fit for data-center/storage-cost angle.

name: Qi Ruifeng
current_role: Co-founder of Aibee (爱笔智能), Beijing AI solutions company (joined Nov 2019 to lead sales and marketing)
profile: Qi Ruifeng (祁瑞峰, 'Ken Qi') is a veteran enterprise-IT sales executive who joined Lin Yuanqing's Aibee in November 2019 as co-founder in charge of sales expansion and marketing. Aibee digitizes offline spaces (malls, airports, stores) with AI and became a unicorn after a 2022 Xiaomi-led round. Chinese media in 2026 describe him as an 'AI serial entrepreneur'.
interesting_fact: Hurun lists Aibee's founders as Lin Yuanqing (ex-head of Baidu's Institute of Deep Learning), Qi Ruifeng and Silvio Savarese; Qi was brought in to take Aibee 'from 10 to 100' in large-scale commercialization.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aibee he was SVP at B2B fresh-produce platform Meicai (in charge of ecosystem and new-business incubation), and earlier VP of SAP China and GM of North China; he also served as a divisional sales GM at Microsoft China and Oracle China.
notes: Low public profile; Hurun lists him as an Aibee co-founder (not the CEO, who is Lin Yuanqing). contact@aibee.com is Aibee's general company contact, not personal. Current status at Aibee in 2026 not independently confirmed.

name: Silvio Savarese
current_role: EVP & Chief Scientist, Salesforce AI Research; adjunct professor of computer science, Stanford
profile: Italian-American computer-vision and robotics researcher (Caltech PhD under Pietro Perona; Univ. of Michigan, then Stanford). In 2017-18 he joined ex-Baidu Research head Lin Yuanqing as co-founder/chief scientist of Aibee, a Beijing AI firm digitising offline retail spaces. Since 2021 he has led Salesforce AI Research, architecting its agentic AI work (Agentforce, CodeGen).
interesting_fact: Named to TIME's 100 Most Influential People in AI (2024) and appointed in 2026 to the UN Independent International Scientific Panel on AI. At Stanford he built JackRabbot/JR-2, a socially aware robot that reads human intentions.
deep_cut_fact: Long before AI agents, he and his father Gey built a point-and-click PC adventure game, 'A Quiet Weekend in Capri' (Italy 2003, North America 2004), followed by the sequel 'AnaCapri: The Dream' (2007).
notes: Hurun lists him as an Aibee founder; Aibee's founder/CEO is Lin Yuanqing, and a 2018 interview (36kr) has Lin announcing Savarese joining as the Stanford vision professor, so his Aibee stake is likely co-founder equity. Active writer on LinkedIn and the Salesforce blog about enterprise AI agents; an ideal podcast guest on agentic AI.

name: Abakar Saidov
current_role: Co-founder and Executive Chairman, Beamery (London AI workforce/talent platform); stepped down as CEO April 2025
profile: Russian-born British entrepreneur who co-founded Beamery in a London garage in 2013 (as Seed.Jobs) with brother Sultan Saidov and Michael Paterson, after finance roles incl. Goldman Sachs. As CEO he built it into an AI talent/skills platform; a 2022 Series D led by Ontario Teachers' valued it at $1B. Since April 2025 he is executive chairman, focused on external/partner relationships.
interesting_fact: His family emigrated from Moscow/Dagestan to the UK in the mid-1990s; his mother, a neuropathologist, became a shopkeeper and his theoretical-physicist father took a desk job. Beamery's mission of matching people to work by skills rather than credentials or passport came from watching that.
deep_cut_fact: At 18 he went to Beijing to study Mandarin and, among part-time jobs, taught golf to Chinese children despite never having played; he also tried (and failed) to export cheap Chinese cement to Europe by ship. He speaks Russian, Mandarin, English, Spanish and French.
notes: Leadership is in flux: Beamery's April 2025 release named Sultan Saidov CEO and Abakar executive chairman; Wikipedia (2026) lists Has Dosanjh as CEO from Sept 2025. No published press email found; route via Beamery contact form or Boardwave (he is a Boardwave mentor). Studied maths & economics at Warwick (RAF-sponsored).

name: Sultan Murad Saidov
current_role: Co-founder, Beamery (London); named CEO in April 2025, but Has Dosanjh was CEO by late 2025, so Saidov's current title is unclear
profile: London-based co-founder of Beamery, an AI talent and workforce-intelligence platform he started in 2013 (first called Seed.Jobs) with his brother Abakar and Michael Paterson after working in finance. Beamery became a $1B unicorn with a $50M Series D in Dec 2022. Sultan led product as President, then was named CEO in April 2025.
interesting_fact: Beamery began life as Seed.Jobs, went through the AngelPad accelerator, and reached unicorn status in December 2022 with a $50M Series D led by Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan's venture arm.
deep_cut_fact: Beamery was founded in a London garage in 2013. The company says the Saidov brothers, as children of immigrants, saw that jobs were handed out by experience or education rather than skills or potential, and that this shaped its mission of equal access to work.
notes: Wikipedia and UK filings show Has Dosanjh as Beamery CEO from Sept 2025, only months after Sultan was announced as CEO (Apr 2025). Check his current title before reaching out. He has written bylines for VentureBeat. No published press email was found; Beamery's general contact form is the only official route.

name: Noam Shazeer
current_role: Technical co-lead of Gemini at Google DeepMind (returned Aug 2024); co-founder of Character.AI
profile: AI researcher who joined Google in 2000, co-authored the 2017 'Attention Is All You Need' Transformer paper and pioneered mixture-of-experts scaling. Left Google in 2021 to co-found Character.AI (valued ~$1B+). In Aug 2024 Google paid ~$2.7B to license Character.AI's tech and rehire him; he now co-leads Gemini with Jeff Dean and Oriol Vinyals.
interesting_fact: Google reportedly paid about $2.7B in a licensing deal largely to bring Shazeer back, after he had quit in 2021 when Google declined to release the chatbot (Meena/LaMDA) he built with Daniel De Freitas.
deep_cut_fact: As a high-schooler from Swampscott, Massachusetts, he scored a perfect 42/42 at the 1994 International Mathematical Olympiad, on the US team that became the first in the IMO's 35-year history to achieve a perfect team score.
notes: Now a Google employee; press via Google DeepMind communications. Private, rarely does interviews (notable exception: Dwarkesh Patel podcast with Jeff Dean, 2025). Hurun-listed wealth from Character.AI stake.

name: Daniel De Freitas
current_role: Research scientist at Google DeepMind (rejoined Google in Aug 2024 via its licensing/talent deal with Character.AI)
profile: Brazilian-born engineer who led Google's experimental chatbot Meena, which became LaMDA. He co-founded Character.AI with Noam Shazeer in 2021; the chatbot startup reached a $1B valuation in 2023. In August 2024 Google licensed Character.AI's technology and rehired both co-founders into Google DeepMind.
interesting_fact: He started Meena, the chatbot that became Google's LaMDA, as a '20% time' side project while working on YouTube at Google.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a computer engineering degree from the Escola Politécnica of the University of São Paulo (USP), and first got interested in conversational AI as a software engineer on Microsoft's Bing search engine.
notes: Low public profile; rarely gives interviews. Google did not disclose his exact DeepMind title; 'research scientist' is per press reports. Any outreach would go via Google DeepMind press (no personal channel found).

name: Jaroslaw Kutylowski
current_role: Founder and CEO, DeepL SE (Cologne, Germany)
profile: Polish-born computer scientist (PhD, Paderborn) who joined Linguee as CTO in 2012 and led the team that built the neural DeepL Translator, launched in August 2017. CEO since 2019, he turned DeepL into Germany's best-known AI unicorn ($2B valuation after a $300M Series C in 2024), expanding into DeepL Write, DeepL Voice and enterprise language AI.
interesting_fact: DeepL Translator launched on 28 Aug 2017 with just seven languages and claimed to beat Google and Microsoft in blind tests; it grew out of Linguee, the online dictionary, whose company was renamed DeepL GmbH.
deep_cut_fact: Born in Poland, he moved to Germany in sixth grade without speaking German. He has joked that his school teachers would 'roll their eyes' that he now works in languages, since it 'was never my strong subject' - he'd rather sit at a computer for days building things.
notes: Goes by 'Jarek'. Described by NZZ as a low-profile 'grounded visionary'; frequent conference speaker (re:publica, Slush, London Tech Week). Studied in Wroclaw before his Paderborn PhD. Route: DeepL press team.

name: Li Jingpeng
current_role: Listed as founder of Desano (Shanghai Desano Pharmaceuticals / 上海迪赛诺医药集团); current title not verified
profile: Li Jingpeng is listed as founder of Desano, a Shanghai drugmaker founded in 1996 that makes HIV and antimalarial APIs and finished drugs plus CDMO services. It holds WHO/FDA/EMA approvals, is a major global HIV-API supplier and was valued at about $1B. Desano's website does not name its founder.
interesting_fact: Since 2003 Desano has supplied drugs to China's national HIV/AIDS treatment programme every year (23 consecutive years), and several of its anti-HIV APIs carry WHO, FDA and EMA approvals for global public-health supply.
notes: Identity unconfirmed: Desano's Chinese name is 迪赛诺 and the founder's Chinese name was not verified (search budget exhausted). Private and Chinese-language; the company inbox is the only published route.

name: Pierre-François Thaler
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, EcoVadis (Paris)
profile: French engineer (CentraleSupélec MSc, INSEAD MBA) who co-founded EcoVadis in 2007 with Frédéric Trinel, pioneering business sustainability ratings for global supply chains. EcoVadis now rates well over 100,000 companies and is backed by General Atlantic and CVC. As co-CEO he leads customers, marketing, solutions and impact.
interesting_fact: EcoVadis invented the idea of a standardised 'sustainability scorecard' that big buyers require from their suppliers, making its medals a de facto credential in global procurement (including for carbon and energy management).
deep_cut_fact: Before EcoVadis he was CEO of B2Build, the first B2B online marketplace for the European construction industry, and later ran Ariba's procurement managed-services/BPO business in EMEA.
notes: Energy/sustainability angle fits the podcast; EcoVadis offers energy-management and carbon solutions. Frequent conference speaker (BSR, Sustainable Purchasing Leadership Council).

name: Frédéric Trinel
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, EcoVadis (Paris)
profile: French serial entrepreneur who co-founded EcoVadis in 2007 with Pierre-François Thaler; it became the leading provider of business sustainability (ESG) ratings for global supply chains and a unicorn. As Co-CEO he runs People, Finance, Evaluations and Technology and co-steers strategy.
interesting_fact: EcoVadis ratings have become a de facto supplier sustainability passport in global procurement, assessing companies' environmental, labour, ethics and sourcing practices.
deep_cut_fact: Before EcoVadis he was COO running technology and operations at HR-software firm MrTed (now part of Cornerstone), and he has founded four other companies in global trade, software and HR, all still active; he studied international business at ICAD in Paris.
notes: No press email published; EcoVadis news page points to a media kit and general contact form. ESG/supply-chain angle fits an energy podcast.

name: Bobby Balachandran
current_role: Founder and CEO, Exterro
profile: Bobby Balachandran founded Exterro, a Portland, Oregon legal-GRC software company, and runs it as CEO. Exterro sells eDiscovery, privacy and data governance, digital forensics (it bought AccessData, maker of FTK) and cybersecurity-compliance software. It has about 820 employees in 11 countries and says half the Fortune 100 use it.
interesting_fact: Exterro says half of the Fortune 100 use its software and that it has managed about 800,000 legal holds.
deep_cut_fact: Under his leadership, Exterro double-matches employee donations to causes such as World Central Kitchen, Black Girls Code and the Ukrainian Red Cross. Employees also volunteer with the Oregon Food Bank and Habitat for Humanity.
notes: Exterro is private and PE-backed (Leeds Equity). No press email is published; the newsroom is at https://www.exterro.com/news-press. The web search budget was exhausted, so his personal background wasn't researched.

name: Jordi Romero
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Factorial (HR software, Barcelona)
profile: Barcelona-based entrepreneur who co-founded and leads Factorial, an all-in-one HR, payroll and expense software platform for small and mid-sized companies used by 17,000+ companies. Factorial became a unicorn in 2022, expanded into North America with a Miami hub, and in June 2026 raised funds at a reported $2.5bn valuation.
interesting_fact: Factorial raised new funding at a reported $2.5 billion valuation in June 2026, more than doubling its unicorn valuation.
notes: Web search budget ran out before a sourced personal deep-cut fact could be found (worth checking his pre-Factorial career and Barcelona startup-community roles). Factorial communications team is the published route.

name: Bernat Farrero
current_role: Co-founder of Factorial (HR software; listed as CRO/executive); Co-CEO & founder of Itnig (Barcelona startup ecosystem and fund)
profile: Barcelona engineer (UPC, PoliTo) who founded Itnig in 2010 as a development consultancy and turned it into a startup studio that spawned about a dozen companies, including Camaloon, Quipu (exited to Providence) and Parkimeter. In 2016 he co-founded Factorial with Jordi Romero and Pau Ramon; the HR software company became a unicorn in 2022.
