deep_cut_fact: In August 2024 Cui Qiu signed a new framework agreement on PingCAP's behalf with the China Computer Federation's (CCF) database committee for a joint program to cultivate top open-source database talent; he was also elected an executive member of that committee.

public_contacts.value: len@firecrackerpr.com (Len Fernandes, Firecracker PR, PingCAP media contact)

notes: Low-profile, engineering-focused co-founder; public face of PingCAP is CEO Max Liu and CTO Ed Huang. Wellfound lists 'Dylan Cui' as co-founder and co-author/core committer of TiDB. Best route is via PingCAP PR (Firecracker PR in 2026 releases).

name: Brandon Millman
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Phantom (self-custody crypto wallet), San Francisco
profile: Former Twitter engineer who moved into crypto in 2017, helping build the 0x protocol and the Matcha DEX aggregator before co-founding Phantom in 2021 with Chris Kalani and Francesco Agosti. Phantom became the dominant Solana wallet, expanded to Ethereum, Bitcoin, Base and Sui, acquired Bitski, and was valued at $3B in a $150M Series C (Jan 2025).
interesting_fact: Phantom grew to 3M+ users within about six months of launch; Millman's thesis was that a wallet is most people's first crypto experience, so 'a great wallet can 100x how many people we onboard'.
deep_cut_fact: He says he left Twitter after becoming 'disillusioned with the typical web2 growth loops (A/B tests, time spent, etc)' and started diving into Ethereum in 2017, which led to building 0x and Matcha with his future Phantom co-founders.
notes: Active on X and frequent crypto-podcast guest (CoinGecko, Solfate, Lightspeed). Note Phantom warns of impersonation scams - use only official channels. Sometimes misspelled 'Brandon Miller'.

name: Wang Shaolan
current_role: Co-founder, President & Vice General Manager, Beijing Zhipu Huazhang Technology (Zhipu AI / Z.ai, HKEX: 2513)
profile: Wang Shaolan (王绍兰, male, b. ~1972) co-founded Zhipu AI in 2019 as a spin-out of Tsinghua University's knowledge-engineering lab. Zhipu makes the GLM family of large language models. He runs business development, fundraising and day-to-day operations. Zhipu listed in Hong Kong on 8 Jan 2026; Wang was an early public face of the company and once held the CEO title.
interesting_fact: Zhipu bills itself as the world's first listed company whose core business is AGI foundation models. It debuted on HKEX in January 2026, ahead of every US frontier lab.
deep_cut_fact: Wang is an electrical engineer by training, with a 1999 master's in power electronics and electric drives from Anhui University of Technology. He spent 2001-2012 at Beijing chip firm 北京凹凸微系电子开发, then served as CEO of Wankang Century Technology (2013-17). He worked at Tsinghua University in 2018-19 before Zhipu spun out.
notes: HKEX-derived executive listing: male, age 53, Masters. No personal social accounts found; best route is Zhipu's PR mailbox, ideally with Chinese-language outreach. His power-electronics background is a natural hook for an energy/data-center podcast.

name: Jason Warner
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Poolside (frontier AI lab for software engineering; co-leads with Eiso Kant)
profile: American technologist, ex-CTO of GitHub (through the Microsoft acquisition) and earlier engineering leader at Heroku and Canonical. After a stint as a VC at Redpoint he co-founded Poolside with Eiso Kant in 2023 to build foundation models for coding and, ultimately, AGI; Poolside has raised billions and was reported valued around $12B.
interesting_fact: Poolside went full-stack into energy and compute: in Oct 2025 it announced Project Horizon, a self-powered 2-gigawatt AI campus on ~568 acres in West Texas's Permian Basin, fuelled by on-site natural gas and planned in eight 250MW phases.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Thomaston and Southbury, Connecticut, he got into tech via a high-school co-op at IBM's Southbury office, carrying printers and hooking up Token Ring networks, while also working at McDonald's; he only started programming at ~17 and first planned to study mechanical/aerospace engineering at Penn State.
notes: Penn State CS alumnus; very active publicly on AI/compute. Strong fit for data-center/energy angle (Project Horizon). Some 2026 reports say the CoreWeave anchor-lease arrangement for Horizon changed - check current status before referencing. Media route: press@poolside.ai.

name: Eiso Kant
current_role: Co-founder and co-CEO, Poolside (AI foundation models for coding); earlier described as CTO
profile: Dutch-born software entrepreneur who co-founded Poolside in 2023 with ex-GitHub CTO Jason Warner. Poolside trains its own foundation models for agentic coding and was valued at about $12B after Nvidia agreed in Oct 2025 to invest up to $1B. He previously co-founded Tyba (a talent marketplace), source{d} (ML on source code) and Athenian.
interesting_fact: Poolside is building Project Horizon, a 2-gigawatt AI data-center campus in Pecos County, Texas, with CoreWeave. Phase one began in Oct 2025. Kant argues energy and compute will decide the AGI race.
deep_cut_fact: In a 2015 op-ed for El Adelantado de Segovia, Kant wrote that he had been programming since age 12. He said he was one of three friends from around Europe (he came from the Netherlands) who went to IE University in Segovia in 2009 and started Tyba while they were still students.
notes: Very relevant for an energy/data-center show: Poolside's 2GW Texas campus, plus his podcast appearance 'Intelligence Isn't Enough: Why Energy & Compute Decide the AGI Race' (The MAD Podcast with Matt Turck). Active on X. Warner and Kant first met in 2017 when GitHub tried to acquire source{d}. No published press email was found.

name: Keone Hon
current_role: Co-founder of Monad; co-founder & general manager, Monad Foundation (formerly co-founder & CEO of Monad Labs, now Category Labs)
profile: Former high-frequency trader (quant at GETCO, then ~8 years leading a futures trading team at Jump Trading, then Jump Crypto) who in early 2022 co-founded Monad Labs with James Hunsaker and Eunice Giarta to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-execution EVM layer-1. The company (renamed Category Labs) raised ~$244M+ incl. a $225M Paradigm-led round; Monad mainnet launched 24 Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: Monad's MON public sale in Nov 2025 was the first-ever token sale run through Coinbase's Token Sales platform, ahead of mainnet on 24 Nov 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He earned three MIT degrees by 2011 - a B.S. in Computer Science and Math, a Master of Finance and an M.Eng in Computer Science - before building ultra-low-latency trading systems at GETCO and Jump.
notes: Very active on X and crypto podcasts (Edge Podcast, Unlayered, CryptoNews); X handle widely cited as @keoneHD but not verified here. HFT-systems-to-blockchain-infrastructure angle fits a data-center/compute podcast. Title per IQ.wiki (Dec 2024 move to Foundation) - confirm.

name: James Hunsaker
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Category Labs (formerly Monad Labs, developer of the Monad blockchain)
profile: University of Iowa CS/maths graduate who worked at Goldman Sachs and J.P. Morgan, then spent eight years at Jump Trading building ultra-low-latency HFT systems and working on crypto trading and Pyth. In 2022 he co-founded Monad Labs with Keone Hon and Eunice Giarta to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-EVM Layer 1; the team rebranded to Category Labs in Dec 2024 and Monad mainnet launched in 2025.
interesting_fact: Monad applies HFT-style low-latency engineering to Ethereum compatibility - a parallel-execution EVM chain aiming for ~10,000 transactions per second while remaining portable for Ethereum apps.
deep_cut_fact: He started programming in elementary school by typing code printed in magazines into Apple II computers at school, as he recalled on Munjal Shah's Unfiltered Podcast (2023).
notes: Category Labs' team page lists him as CEO (older sources say CTO). Active in crypto podcasts/X; no published press email found.

name: Eunice Giarta
current_role: Co-founder of Monad (Monad Labs, renamed Category Labs in Dec 2024); now with the Monad Foundation (co-founder/general manager per profiles)
profile: MIT computer-science graduate who co-founded Monad Labs in 2022 with Keone Hon and James Hunsaker to build Monad, a high-performance parallel-EVM layer-1 blockchain. As COO she ran business development and ecosystem; when Monad Labs became Category Labs in Dec 2024 (valued ~$3B), she moved with Keone Hon to the new Monad Foundation, which handles ecosystem, governance and developer relations.
interesting_fact: She took a famously non-linear route into crypto: MIT (CS, minor in finance), a rates-derivatives trading internship at Bank of America Merrill Lynch, product/business-development roles at Broadway Technology and senior PM at Shutterstock, before co-founding Monad.
deep_cut_fact: Between Shutterstock and Monad she reportedly worked as a chef de partie in Jean-Georges Vongerichten's restaurant group (2019-2020), and she ran her own design studio, Euna Creative; at MIT she was a Media Lab research assistant, which is where she met co-founder Keone Hon.
notes: Career details come from IQ.wiki (crowd-sourced, LinkedIn-derived) -- the Jean-Georges chef detail is not independently confirmed; verify before using in outreach. Active conference speaker (ETHDenver, TOKEN2049) and podcast guest. Category Labs CEO is James Hunsaker.

name: Yotam Segev
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Cyera (AI-native data security)
profile: Israeli Talpiot and Unit 8200 veteran who, with CTO Tamar Bar-Ilan, built and ran the cloud security division of Unit 8200 before co-founding data-security platform Cyera in 2021. Cyera discovers, classifies and protects data across cloud, SaaS and on-prem; backed by Sequoia, Accel, Coatue and others, it raised at a $6B+ valuation in 2025 and ~$9B later, among the fastest-growing cyber companies ever.
interesting_fact: Cyera went from founding in 2021 to a $3B valuation (Series D, $300M) in 2024 and over $6B in 2025, a trajectory Calcalist compared only to Wiz; it also acquired Trail Security for $162M.
deep_cut_fact: He met co-founder Tamar Bar-Ilan in the IDF's Talpiot program, where he later served as a Senior Class Commander; on Cyera's Cyber Inspiration podcast he said 'We wanted to build something that will outlast us.'
notes: Frequent podcast/conference speaker (RSAC, SC World, Dark Reading contributor). Route via Cyera press office.

name: Tamar Bar-Ilan
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Cyera
profile: Israeli engineer (BSc physics and computer science, Hebrew University) and Talpiot graduate who co-founded AI-native data security company Cyera in 2021 with CEO Yotam Segev. Cyera, based in New York and Tel Aviv, discovers and classifies sensitive data across clouds and has become one of the fastest-growing cybersecurity unicorns; she leads product and engineering.
interesting_fact: She and Yotam Segev met in the IDF's elite Talpiot program and together founded, built and ran the cloud security division of Unit 8200.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving the army in early 2020 she and Segev spent most of that year as 'independent entrepreneurs in our living rooms, learning how to set up a company' - Cyera is her first job after military service.
notes: Rare example of a female cybersecurity unicorn co-founder/CTO; press route via press@cyera.io.

name: Don Burnette
current_role: Founder, CEO & Director, Kodiak AI (Kodiak Robotics; autonomous trucking, Mountain View; Nasdaq: KDK)
profile: Autonomous-vehicle engineer (UF electrical engineering, CMU robotics master's) who was a software tech lead on Google's self-driving project (now Waymo), co-founded self-driving truck startup Otto (bought by Uber in 2016), and founded Kodiak in 2018. Kodiak went public via SPAC in 2025 and runs customer-owned driverless trucks hauling frac sand in the Permian Basin for Atlas Energy Solutions.
interesting_fact: Kodiak's trucks run fully driverless for Atlas Energy Solutions in the Permian Basin, hauling frac sand to wellsites around the clock; Atlas plans to grow the driverless fleet to 100 trucks by mid-2027.
deep_cut_fact: Before Kodiak he co-founded Otto, described in Kodiak's investor materials as the first self-driving truck startup, after starting as a software tech lead on Google's self-driving car project; he holds a robotics master's from Carnegie Mellon.
notes: Excellent energy-podcast fit: driverless trucking in oilfield logistics (Permian frac sand). Frequent speaker at CES, FreightWaves and SAE events. First Kodiak/Atlas driverless delivery: Jan 2025 (https://techcrunch.com/2025/01/24/kodiak-has-made-its-first-driverless-truck-deliveries-to-customer-atlas-energy).

name: He Jian
current_role: President, Dongchedi (DCar), ByteDance's auto platform (as of 2020)
profile: Likely He Jian (He Jian, Chinese 何戬), president of Dongchedi (DCar), the car-information and auto-commerce app spun out of Toutiao's auto channel in 2017. ByteDance reportedly sought ~$700-800M for DCar at a ~$3B valuation in 2024. Little public biography exists.
interesting_fact: At DCar's 2020 creator conference he said the platform became China's largest auto livestreaming platform just 10 months after launching livestreams in October 2019.
notes: Name in list may refer to 何戬 (DCar president); 'founder' label unverified - DCar is a ByteDance product. Keep outreach minimal; route via ByteDance/DCar PR.

name: Nan Cewen
current_role: Chief scientist and co-founder, Qingtao Energy (清陶能源, Kunshan); professor and CAS academician, Tsinghua University School of Materials Science and Engineering
profile: Nan Cewen (南策文) is a Tsinghua materials scientist and Chinese Academy of Sciences academician (2011) whose team's solid-state lithium battery research spun out as Jiangsu Qingtao Energy in Kunshan in 2016. Qingtao makes solid-state/semi-solid batteries (partnered with SAIC/BAIC) and filed for a Hong Kong IPO in April 2026; chairman Feng Yuchuan is the controlling holder, with Nan part of the acting-in-concert group.
interesting_fact: Qingtao was created in 2016 when Kunshan's development zone recruited Nan's Tsinghua team to industrialise its solid-state lithium battery ceramic-separator research; at the time his team was already running pilot tests with BAIC for EV battery components.
deep_cut_fact: He started as a lecturer at Wuhan University of Technology in 1985 and earned his PhD there in 1992 as an on-the-job graduate student, being promoted to full professor the same year, before moving to Tsinghua in December 1999.
notes: Academic founder; operational leader is chairman Feng Yuchuan. Best route is likely via Qingtao (HKEX IPO filing April 2026 will list company secretary/IR contacts) or Tsinghua MSE. Valuation reports vary (~RMB 24-28B).

name: He Xianming
profile: Hurun's 2025 Global Unicorn Index listed 'He Xianming' (何向明) with Nan Cewen and Li Zheng as founders of Qingtao Energy (清陶能源), a Kunshan/Suzhou solid-state battery maker. Hurun's 2026 list and Qingtao's 2026 Hong Kong IPO filing name only Feng Yuchuan, Li Zheng, Nan Cewen and Yang Fan as founders, so the attribution looks doubtful.
notes: Identity unresolved. Hurun Chinese name is 何向明; the best-known person of that name is a Tsinghua INET lithium-ion battery researcher (https://www.imem.tsinghua.edu.cn/info/1334/2272.htm), but no source links him to Qingtao. Qingtao's prospectus founders (jiemian.com/article/14257975.html) exclude him; Hurun dropped him in 2026. Possible Hurun error; verify before outreach.

name: Kavitha Subramanian
current_role: Co-founder, Upstox (growth, strategy, finance and customer experience)
profile: Indian fintech co-founder who, with Ravi Kumar and Shrini Viswanath, built Upstox (RKSV), a Mumbai discount broker backed by Tiger Global and Ratan Tata that became a unicorn in 2021 with 10M+ users. IIT Bombay electrical engineer and Wharton MBA, formerly at McKinsey and private-equity firms Actis and LeapFrog.
interesting_fact: She is one of relatively few women co-founders of an Indian fintech unicorn; Upstox scaled past 10 million users during the 2020-21 retail investing boom.
deep_cut_fact: Before Upstox she was an associate director at impact investor LeapFrog Investments and an investment principal at emerging-markets PE firm Actis.
notes: Frequently quoted on women investors and financial literacy (Zee Business).

name: Shrini Viswanath
current_role: Co-founder, Upstox (RKSV Securities), Mumbai; former CTO, now in a strategic role
profile: Co-founded RKSV Securities in 2009 with Ravi Kumar and Raghu Kumar; it moved into flat-fee online retail broking in 2012 and launched the Upstox trading platform in 2016. Upstox, backed by Tiger Global, grew into one of India's largest discount brokers with 10M+ users and a ~$3.5B valuation (2021). Viswanath led technology until an external CTO was hired in 2021.
interesting_fact: More than 80% of Upstox's new customers come from India's tier 2 and tier 3 cities, per Viswanath.
deep_cut_fact: RKSV was set up in 2009 purely as a proprietary trading firm; only in 2012 did it pivot to retail broking with an online-only, flat-fee unlimited trading plan.
notes: Lower profile than CEO Ravi Kumar. Undergraduate degree from University of Illinois per MarketScreener (aggregator, unverified). Route via Upstox corporate comms.

name: Lu Haoan
current_role: President & CEO, Mattson Technology; President, CEO and director of parent Beijing E-Town Semiconductor Technology (屹唐股份, SSE STAR: 688729)
profile: Hao Allen Lu (陆郝安), ~70, is a semiconductor-equipment veteran (Applied Materials, Intel, SEMI China president) who became CEO of Fremont-based Mattson Technology in Oct 2016 after its acquisition by Beijing E-Town. He runs the dry-strip/etch/rapid-thermal-processing toolmaker, whose Chinese parent listed on Shanghai's STAR Market in 2025.
interesting_fact: He holds a PhD in solid-state physics from the University of Virginia and a BSc from the University of Science and Technology of China, and began his career in chip equipment at Applied Materials before Intel.
deep_cut_fact: At Intel he started the company's public-affairs organisation in China (serving as its director for four years) and later managed the China Fab Program that developed suppliers for Intel's first Asian fab in Dalian, before being named president of SEMI China.
notes: Hurun labels him 'founder', but Mattson was founded by Brad Mattson in 1988; Lu is the post-2016 CEO and was the top-paid exec at 屹唐股份 (2025 pay ~RMB10.6M). Only general corporate contact published: info@mattson.com (https://mattson.com/contact-us/). Low public profile.

name: Xie Tianwei
current_role: Listed by Hurun as founder of Shougang Zhixin (首钢智新电磁材料(迁安)股份有限公司), Shougang's electrical-steel unicorn; his title could not be verified
profile: Hurun names Xie Tianwei as founder of Shougang Zhixin, the Qian'an (Hebei) electrical-steel subsidiary of state-owned Shougang (listed parent: Shougang Co., 000959). Shougang began its electrical-steel project in 2008. Zhixin's thin silicon-steel sheets go into EV motor cores, and Beijing Daily reports that about one in three Chinese new-energy vehicles uses a 'Shougang core'. It joined Hurun's Global Unicorn list in 2025.
interesting_fact: Shougang Zhixin mass-produces EV electrical steel only 0.1mm thick ('as thin as A4 paper') on what it calls the world's first six-stand tandem cold mill for this product. It has 160+ electrical-steel products, 16 of them world firsts.
notes: I could not confirm the person: Chinese searches for 谢天伟 with Shougang returned nothing, and the Chinese characters are unknown. Zhixin is a state-owned-enterprise subsidiary, so 'founder' probably means a senior Shougang manager rather than an independent entrepreneur. Check Shougang Co. (000959) announcements for the executive list. The company is highly relevant to energy (EV motors, transformers).

name: Shiv Rao
current_role: Founder and CEO, Abridge (generative-AI clinical documentation); practicing cardiologist at UPMC
profile: Cardiologist Dr. Shiv Rao, a Pittsburgh native, ran UPMC Enterprises' health-tech investments (2013-19). In 2018 he founded Abridge with CMU professor Zachary Lipton to end doctors' nightly note dictation. Its ambient AI scribe turns clinical conversations into notes. Fortune valued it at $2.75B in Feb 2025; Hurun lists $5B.
interesting_fact: Rao still practices cardiology while running a multibillion-dollar AI company: he is on call Thursdays and takes one weekend shift a month. Emory Healthcare CEO Joon Lee calls him 'a doctor first.'
deep_cut_fact: He was a high-school skateboarder into Fugazi and Minor Threat. At Carnegie Mellon he deejayed in art museums and made avant-garde electronic music with virtual synths (he admires Aphex Twin and Autechre). One of his 'side quests' was tracking down Rick Rubin, whom he persuaded to give an interview at an Abridge event.
notes: Very media-friendly; has appeared on Masters of Scale, the Voicebot podcast and HLTH. He says 'Pittsburgh is a part of our founding DNA' (Axios, March 2025). Music is a great rapport topic.

name: Wang Jianmeng
current_role: Co-founder of LandSpace (蓝箭航天, Chinese commercial rocket company). Described as LandSpace chairman in earlier interviews; current title not verified (Zhang Changwu is founder-CEO and controlling shareholder).
profile: Wang Jianmeng (王建蒙) is a Chinese space-industry veteran who spent most of his career in satellite launch and international space cooperation, including as a senior space-systems engineer in China's satellite launch and TT&C system. In 2015, at about 60, he co-founded LandSpace with Zhang Changwu and Wu Shufan. LandSpace builds methane-LOX rockets (Zhuque-2, reusable Zhuque-3) and filed for a RMB 7.5B Shanghai STAR Market IPO in December 2025.
interesting_fact: LandSpace's STAR Market IPO filing (accepted December 31, 2025) seeks RMB 7.5B, largely for reusable rockets. Zhuque-3's first flight on December 3, 2025 reached orbit, though the first-stage landing attempt failed.
deep_cut_fact: LandSpace was conceived at a meeting in a hotel near Beijing's Drum Tower between a 31-year-old Zhang Changwu, 60-year-old Wang Jianmeng and 50-year-old Wu Shufan, who decided to start a market-driven commercial rocket company. 36Kr calls Wang a space veteran who spent most of his life on satellite launches and international space cooperation.
notes: Born around 1955 per the age given in 36Kr's account. Alive marked unknown because no recent mention was found. The Hurun $11B valuation reflects LandSpace's pre-IPO value. Very low international profile; outreach would go through LandSpace's corporate channels (not verified). Strong space and energy-adjacent angle (methane rocket propulsion).

name: Nathaniel Bennett
current_role: Co-founder, Xaira Therapeutics (AI drug discovery; South San Francisco/Seattle) - employed there per 2025 Nature paper disclosures
profile: Protein-design scientist (Nate Bennett, PhD) trained at the University of Washington's Institute for Protein Design under Nobel laureate David Baker, where he worked on generative deep-learning models for designing binding proteins, including RFdiffusion. He co-founded Xaira Therapeutics with Baker and Joseph Watson; Xaira launched in 2024 with over $1B in funding and licenses IPD technology.
interesting_fact: He was co-lead author of the 2025 Nature paper 'Atomically accurate de novo design of antibodies with RFdiffusion' - AI-designed antibodies created from scratch - technology Xaira has licensed.
deep_cut_fact: Explaining why de novo antibodies matter, he noted that many diseases have no approved medicines because they are driven by molecules with vulnerable sites that small-molecule drugs can't reach - 'Computer-generated antibodies could target these sites directly.' The RFantibody code was released openly on GitHub.
notes: Scientist-founder rather than the business lead (Xaira launched with ex-Genentech executives in leadership, per BioSpace headline). info@xaira.com is the company's general contact.

name: Justas Dauparas
current_role: Protein-design scientist; Hurun lists him as a Xaira Therapeutics founder, but no Xaira source confirms his current role
profile: Machine-learning protein-design researcher, formerly a project scientist in David Baker's lab at the UW Institute for Protein Design, who led ProteinMPNN (Science 2022) and LigandMPNN (Nature Methods 2025). Xaira, launched in 2024 with $1B+ under CEO Marc Tessier-Lavigne, was founded to build on IPD models including RFdiffusion and ProteinMPNN.
interesting_fact: ProteinMPNN, the sequence-design model he led at the Baker lab, runs in about one second - over 200x faster than the previous best software - and its designs were more likely to fold as intended in lab tests.
deep_cut_fact: On building ProteinMPNN he said: 'Neural networks are easy to train if you have a ton of data... We had to go in and identify which features in these molecules are the most important.'
notes: GeekWire (2024) describes him as one of the scientists behind ProteinMPNN in its Xaira coverage (https://www.geekwire.com/2024/inside-the-seattle-labs-of-xaira-the-ai-powered-startup-launched-with-1b-from-investors/); I couldn't open the article to confirm his Xaira title. An academic, not a typical founder-CEO; route via Xaira.

name: Philip Leung
current_role: Scientist on the molecule-design team at Xaira Therapeutics (Seattle); self-described co-founder per profile aggregators
profile: Protein-design scientist (Philip J. Y. Leung) trained in David Baker's lab at the University of Washington Institute for Protein Design (NSF Graduate Fellow, then postdoc) who joined AI drug-discovery company Xaira Therapeutics, launched in 2024 with $1B+ from ARCH, Foresite and others. IPD names Baker, Watson and Bennett as Xaira co-founders; Leung's founder status is only claimed on aggregator profiles.
interesting_fact: He is a co-author of the 2025 Nature RFantibody study - AI that designs antibodies from scratch - whose technology Xaira licensed; IPD notes Leung is employed by Xaira.
deep_cut_fact: He co-led (with Susana Vazquez-Torres and Preetham Venkatesh) the 2023 Baker Lab project in which AI-designed proteins bound helical peptide hormones such as glucagon with the highest affinity ever reported for a computer-generated protein without experimental optimization.
notes: Founder claim uncertain: Xaira launch releases and IPD don't list him as a co-founder; aggregator village.ai does. GeekWire 2024 calls him a former IPD postdoc on Xaira's design team. Baker lab alumni page may list a different venture (search snippet: 'Co-Founder, Sealth Biotech') - unverified. Early-career scientist; outreach via Xaira or academic channels.

name: David Baker
current_role: Director, Institute for Protein Design, University of Washington; co-founder of Xaira Therapeutics
profile: Biochemist David Baker shared the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry for computational protein design. He directs UW's Institute for Protein Design, whose Rosetta software, Rosetta@home and Foldit pioneered protein modelling, and has co-founded more than a dozen biotechs including Icosavax (acquired by AstraZeneca), Sana, Lyell and AI drug-discovery company Xaira Therapeutics, which launched with $1B+.
interesting_fact: His lab turned protein folding into crowd science: Rosetta@home lets volunteers donate computer time, and Foldit is a video game in which players solve protein structures.
deep_cut_fact: A Seattle native and Garfield High School graduate, his lab designed Top7, the first artificial protein with a fold not seen in nature; he also gave a 2019 TED talk, '5 challenges we could solve by designing new proteins'.
notes: Nobel laureate; heavy media demand, so go via IPD communications. AI-for-science and compute angle (protein design models) fits a data-center podcast. Not to be confused with other David Bakers.

name: Greg Keller
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Technology Officer, JumpCloud (Louisville, Colorado)
profile: Co-founded JumpCloud with CEO Rajat Bhargava in late 2013/early 2014 as a cloud-based alternative to Microsoft Active Directory; it grew into an identity, access and device-management platform valued around $3B. Keller was its founding product/technology leader, later chief strategy officer, and is now CTO. Career spans ~30 years of startups, incl. COO of LinkSmart.
interesting_fact: Named an Endeavor Entrepreneur via Endeavor Colorado in 2023 and later appointed to Endeavor Colorado's board of directors, where he mentors high-growth founders.
deep_cut_fact: In 2013, before any code was deployed, he and Bhargava wrote down JumpCloud's thesis as 'an alternative to Microsoft's Active Directory from the cloud', and gave the product away as freeware for distribution before 'product-led growth' was a common term; he calls a neutral identity layer JumpCloud's 'hood ornament'.
notes: Titles shifted over time (CPO -> CSO in 2023 -> CTO now per JumpCloud's cofounders page). Frequent podcast/interview guest on identity and AI-era IT; reachable via JumpCloud press.

name: Tomasz Greber
current_role: Co-founder, Bending Spoons (Nasdaq: BSP); no current executive role listed in the 2026 IPO prospectus
profile: One of five co-founders of Bending Spoons, started in Copenhagen in 2013 and based in Milan since 2014. The company acquires and rebuilds digital products (Evernote, WeTransfer, Vimeo, AOL, Eventbrite and more), reported $1.31B revenue for 2025 and listed on Nasdaq in July 2026. Greber, previously an art director at predecessor startup Evertale, keeps a very low profile.
interesting_fact: Bending Spoons was seeded with the $40,000 left over after the founders liquidated their failed startup Evertale; the name comes from a scene in The Matrix.
deep_cut_fact: The founders' IPO letter says that after liquidating Evertale they used the leftover $40,000 to start a new company 'alongside Luca Querella and Tomasz Greber, two Evertale standouts', vowing product-market fit would never again be their Achilles' heel.
notes: Extremely private; Crunchbase lists him as Berlin-based and a former Evertale art director (not verified from primary source). Best route is via Bending Spoons; CEO Luca Ferrari is the public face.

name: Chris Simair

In 2024 she co-founded World Labs to build 'spatial intelligence' world models; on 28 Sep 2026 AMD agreed to buy it for ~$8.2B in stock, with Li to become AMD EVP and chief scientist.

deep_cut_fact: Before computer vision she worked on hearing: her 1999 Princeton physics senior thesis built a computational model of 'Huggins dichotic pitch' (an auditory illusion), supervised by EE professor Bradley Dickinson - while she went home most weekends to help run her family's dry-cleaning shop in Parsippany, NJ.
notes: AMD deal announced 28 Sep 2026, expected to close by end-2026 - after close, AMD corporate comms becomes the PR route. Hurun lists her via World Labs ($5B valuation, pre-AMD). Highly sought-after speaker; her memoir 'The Worlds I See' (2023) is a natural outreach hook. Dry-cleaning detail is from Wired 2018 per Wikipedia.

name: Justin Johnson
current_role: Co-founder, World Labs (spatial-intelligence / world-model AI company, San Francisco)
profile: Computer-vision researcher who did his Stanford PhD under Fei-Fei Li, worked at Meta/FAIR and became an assistant professor at the University of Michigan. In 2024 he co-founded World Labs with Li, Christoph Lassner and Ben Mildenhall; its first product, Marble, generates explorable 3D worlds and became generally available in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: On launching World Labs' first product he said: 'Marble is a brand-new category of model - one that generates 3D worlds.' Before World Labs he was a Meta/FAIR researcher and a University of Michigan professor, and Fei-Fei Li's former PhD student.
deep_cut_fact: The CS231n 'Python Numpy Tutorial' that has taught a generation of ML students their first numpy was originally written by Justin Johnson; the course site still credits him.

public_contacts.value: justincj at umich dot edu (academic address he publishes)

notes: Common name - make sure outreach references World Labs/CS231n. No published World Labs press email found (site only lists support@ and legal@). Appeared on the a16z and TWIML podcasts, so receptive to podcast format. Also known for fast neural style transfer (Perceptual Losses, ECCV 2016) and the CLEVR dataset.

name: Christoph Lassner
current_role: Co-founder of World Labs (spatial-intelligence AI); stepped away from his operating role in 2026 and remains an advisor
profile: German computer-vision/graphics researcher (PhD at Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems, Tubingen) who led research teams at Meta Reality Labs and Epic Games before co-founding World Labs with Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson and Ben Mildenhall in 2024. World Labs (Marble, Atlas world models) raised $1B in Feb 2026 and in Sept 2026 agreed to join AMD.
interesting_fact: Before World Labs he worked at Body Labs (acquired by Amazon) and created the human pose estimation system for Amazon Halo, which builds a 3D model of your body from a smartphone.
deep_cut_fact: In 2021 he single-handedly wrote the Pulsar differentiable renderer, now the sphere-based rendering backend of Meta's PyTorch3D; he also won an Honorable Mention at the ACM Multimedia Open-Source Software Competition 2016 for his decision-forest library.
notes: Researcher persona; his site invites collaboration outreach ('please reach out'). Reportedly stepped back from World Labs in 2026 (advisor now); World Labs announced it is joining AMD on Sept 28, 2026 (worldlabs.ai/blog). GitHub: github.com/classner.

name: Ben Mildenhall
current_role: Cofounder, World Labs (spatial intelligence / world-model AI startup)
profile: Ben Mildenhall is a cofounder of World Labs, the spatial-intelligence AI company started with Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson and Christoph Lassner in 2024. He is first author of the 2020 Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) paper, which spawned a whole subfield of 3D reconstruction. Stanford undergrad, UC Berkeley PhD (2020, advised by Ren Ng), then research scientist at Google Research 2021-2023.
interesting_fact: His NeRF work earned the 2025 ACM Grace Murray Hopper Award and the 2025 SIGGRAPH Significant New Researcher Award.
deep_cut_fact: As a Stanford undergrad he spent summer 2014 at Pixar Research; he later interned in Marc Levoy's computational-photography group at Google (2017) and did his PhD on a Hertz Fellowship.
notes: Academic-style researcher; publishes his own email on his homepage. Approach via research/technical angle (NeRF, 3D world models).

name: Connor Zwick
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Speak (Speakeasy Labs), San Francisco
profile: Connor Zwick left Harvard as a 2012 Thiel Fellow and co-founded Speak in 2016 with fellow Thiel Fellow Andrew Hsu. Speak is a conversational-AI language tutor that launched first in South Korea; the OpenAI Startup Fund led its 2022 Series B and Accel led a $78M Series C at a $1B valuation in Dec 2024. Forbes reported Speak passed $100M in annualized revenue in 2025.
interesting_fact: Speak deliberately launched in South Korea before the US, betting on intense demand for spoken-English practice; it was one of the first startups backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund.
deep_cut_fact: He traces his whole founder career to a chance encounter at the Milwaukee airport that got him building apps as a teenager, and says Speak grew out of a 2015 thesis that deep learning would eventually be able to teach people a language.
notes: No published press email found (only customer support addresses). Some profiles say he built the study app Flashcards+ (later part of Chegg) while at Harvard; not independently verified. Podcast-friendly founder - has done Accel 'Spotlight On' and other podcasts.

name: Andrew Hsu
current_role: Co-founder and CTO, Speak (AI language-learning app, San Francisco)
profile: Andrew Hsu co-founded Speak in 2016 with fellow Thiel Fellow Connor Zwick and serves as CTO. Speak uses speech and language models to replace human tutors for spoken practice; backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund, it became an AI-native unicorn (~$1B). In Sept 2026 he announced Live Tutor Lessons powered by OpenAI's GPT-Live-1.
interesting_fact: Hsu frames Speak as the 'third generation' of language-learning software, after Rosetta Stone (gen 1) and Duolingo (gen 2), with AI now doing what previously only human tutors could.
deep_cut_fact: A Seattle prodigy, he entered the University of Washington at 12, began a Stanford neuroscience PhD at 16 and left in 2011 as a fourth-year candidate to become a Thiel Fellow building ed-games startup Airy Labs, which is where he met Speak co-founder Connor Zwick.
notes: Has appeared on the Latent Space podcast (Jul 2025), so open to tech-podcast appearances. No published Speak press email found (support address only). Not to be confused with Andrew T. Hsu, College of Charleston president.

name: Evan Smith
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Altana (AI-powered global supply-chain network, New York)
profile: Yale economics graduate who co-founded Altana in December 2018 with Panjiva colleagues Peter Swartz and Raphael Tehranian plus former CBP commissioner Alan Bersin. Altana builds an AI map of global supply chains used by customs agencies, enterprises and banks for compliance, tariffs and forced-labor screening; a $200M Series C in 2024 made it a ~$1B unicorn.
interesting_fact: Altana co-founder Alan Bersin is a former Commissioner of U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and the platform tracks shipments for compliance with the U.S. import ban on forced-labor goods (e.g. via a Maersk partnership).
deep_cut_fact: Before Altana he was CEO of IMBU Technologies, a textile supply-chain automation software firm owned by a family-office PE partnership he co-managed, then led enterprise solutions at trade-data firm Panjiva through its 2018 sale to S&P Global; Altana's site says he earlier worked in clean tech and renewable energy.
notes: Common name: identify him as 'Evan Smith, Altana CEO'. Regular conference speaker (Milken 2025, HumanX). Renewable-energy/clean-tech past is a good hook for an energy podcast. Clean-tech background is from Altana's own leadership bio.

name: Peter Swartz
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Science Officer, Altana (Altana AI), New York
profile: Peter Swartz co-founded Altana, an AI company that maps global supply chains and trade networks for governments and companies, and leads its application of modern AI as Chief Science Officer. Before Altana he was Head of Data Science at trade-data firm Panjiva, later sold to S&P Global. Hurun lists Altana as a ~$1B unicorn.
interesting_fact: He has spoken on global trade and machine learning at the World Trade Organization, the World Customs Organization and the US Court of International Trade, and holds a number of patents in machine learning and global trade.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Yale, MIT and EPFL (Lausanne), focusing on engineering, statistical methods and global trade, and has high-level proficiency in both French and Chinese.
notes: Technical co-founder; CEO of Altana is Evan Smith. Frequent conference speaker (World Trade Week NYC, HumanX, Yale Innovation Summit) - speaker programs are a natural outreach angle.

name: Raphael Tehranian
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Operating Officer, Altana (Altana Technologies / Altana AI), New York
profile: Raphael 'Raph' Tehranian (Hurun spells it 'Tegranian') co-founded Altana in December 2018 with CEO Evan Smith and Peter Swartz; all three came from trade-data firm Panjiva, sold to S&P Global in 2018. Altana builds an AI-powered global supply-chain knowledge graph for governments (e.g., customs agencies) and companies. It hit a $1B valuation after a $200M Series C in 2024. Tehranian runs operations across the business.
interesting_fact: Altana's seed round was led by Amadeus Capital's Anne Glover, and its executive chairman is Alan Bersin, a former commissioner of US Customs and Border Protection. Border agencies use the platform to 'pick the needles out of the haystack' of illicit shipments.
deep_cut_fact: His own Altana bio says he co-founded the company 'after failing and succeeding to build several clean technology, market intelligence, and supply chain businesses.' It cites investing, advising and operating experience across energy, agriculture, transportation and financial services, which makes him a natural energy-angle guest.
notes: Name is correctly spelled 'Tehranian' (input has 'Tegranian'). He keeps a low profile; CEO Evan Smith does most of the public speaking. Best route is press@altana.ai or LinkedIn. A third-party profile mentions earlier roles at JP Morgan, Cleantech Group and Suncor Energy, but we could not verify these on a primary source.

name: Arvind Bansal
current_role: Founder, Whole-time Director and CEO, Continuum Green Energy Ltd (India); director of Singapore parent Continuum Green Energy Holdings
profile: Indian renewable-energy entrepreneur (b. 1970) who co-founded Continuum with Vikash Saraf in 2009-10 after investment-banking work at SBI Capital Markets and SSKI Corporate Finance and a stint at Mission NewEnergy. Continuum builds wind-solar hybrid projects selling green power to commercial & industrial customers; it filed for a Rs 3,650 crore IPO (SEBI approval April 2025).
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Continuum grew from a single 16.5 MW project in 2010 to 3.52 GWp of capacity by late 2024, supplying 170+ commercial and industrial customers - largely via wind-solar hybrid plants.
deep_cut_fact: He is a civil engineer by training (B.Tech, IIT Delhi) with a PGDM from IIM Ahmedabad; Continuum's founding team were close friends from their IIM Ahmedabad days who left firms like IDFC-SSKI, Suzlon, Wipro and HSBC to start 'Continuum Wind Energy'.
notes: Low public profile; few interviews. ir_email is the Company Secretary/Compliance Officer address from the DRHP (Mahendra Malviya). Group majority-backed by Morgan Stanley Infrastructure (North Haven). Deep-cut source for 'IIM Ahmedabad friends' detail is Continuum Wind's Crunchbase description (https://www.crunchbase.com/organization/continuum-wind-energy); education from DRHP.

name: Vikash Saraf
current_role: Co-founder, promoter and director, Continuum Green Energy Ltd (India); also reported as an Essar Group executive (CEO of Essar Teleholdings per MarketScreener, not independently verified)
profile: Co-founded Continuum (first Continuum Wind Energy) in 2009 with Arvind Bansal, who runs it as CEO. The company builds large wind and wind-solar hybrid projects in India, with about 2.2 GWp operating and 1.3 GWp under construction as of its Dec 2024 IPO filing. Saraf is a named promoter and a board director, and has a long background in Essar Group's telecom and strategy roles.
interesting_fact: Continuum filed for a Rs 3,650-crore IPO in Dec 2024. In 2024 it took a primary equity investment from an affiliate of Just Climate, the climate-investment firm set up by Al Gore's Generation Investment Management.
notes: Very low public profile: no interviews, personal accounts or bio found. Continuum's site (continuumenergy.in) could not be reached from this environment, so no IR/press email was checked. The SEBI DRHP should have his official bio and the company-secretary contact. Arvind Bansal (CEO) is the company's public face. Sources disagree on the founding year (2007 incorporation vs 2009 founding).

name: Li Kaifu (Kai-Fu Lee)
current_role: Founder and CEO, 01.AI (零一万物); chairman, Sinovation Ventures
profile: Taiwan-born AI pioneer (CMU PhD) who held senior roles at Apple, SGI and Microsoft (founding Microsoft Research Asia) and ran Google China before launching VC firm Sinovation Ventures in 2009. He founded LLM startup 01.AI in 2023, which hit a $1B valuation within eight months; in 2025 it pivoted from frontier pre-training to enterprise 'Boss AI' and is targeting a 2027 Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: 01.AI reached a $1B valuation about eight months after founding, and its open-source Yi-34B model topped Hugging Face leaderboards in Nov 2023; Lee now pitches the company as 'the Palantir of China'.
deep_cut_fact: As a CMU grad student in 1986 he co-built (with Sanjoy Mahajan) 'Bill', a Bayesian-learning Othello program that won the 1989 US national computer Othello tournament; his 1988 PhD thesis was the Sphinx speaker-independent speech recognizer. He went to high school in Oak Ridge, Tennessee.
notes: Very media-friendly (frequent Bloomberg/CNBC interviews, TED speaker, author of 'AI Superpowers' and 'AI 2041'); approachable via 01.AI or Sinovation Ventures PR. Avoid his 2013 lymphoma as a topic in outreach.

name: Xiao Guowei
current_role: Chairman of Guangdong Ascen Power (芯粤能, SiC chip foundry) and its sister firm Xinjuneng (芯聚能); chairman and chief strategy officer of HK-listed APT Electronics (2551.HK)
profile: 肖国伟, an HKUST-trained semiconductor engineer, co-founded LED-chip maker APT Electronics (晶科电子) in Guangzhou, later pivoting it to smart car lighting with Geely-linked backers and listing it in Hong Kong in 2024. He chairs Ascen Power, a Guangzhou Nansha automotive-grade silicon-carbide wafer fab rated a $1B unicorn by Hurun, which raised a RMB700M+ round with Xinjuneng in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Ascen Power positions itself as a SiC foundry for China's chip designers: by mid-2026 it reported 250+ foundry customer products in engineering runs, with chips used in EV traction inverters, PV inverters, chargers and AI data-center power.
deep_cut_fact: Before becoming an entrepreneur he spent seven years (1990-1997) teaching in Xi'an Jiaotong University's electronic engineering department, then did a PhD at HKUST and in Feb 2003 co-founded Hong Kong LED-chip startup Advanced Photoelectronic (微晶) with HKUST professors.
notes: Hurun romanizes 芯粤能 as 'Ascen Power'. Geely Holding president An Conghui is vice-chairman of Ascen Power. Best outreach route likely via APT Electronics (listed company) or Ascen Power corporate channels; no personal channels found.

name: Vik Bajaj
current_role: Co-CEO (with Jeff Bezos), Project Prometheus; co-founder of Foresite Labs and Xaira
profile: Vikram 'Vik' Bajaj is a physicist/chemist who worked at Google X (on projects incl. Wing and what became Waymo), co-founded Alphabet's Verily as CSO, then was CSO of GRAIL and ran AI incubator Foresite Labs for ~7 years. In Nov 2025 he became co-CEO alongside Jeff Bezos of Project Prometheus, an AI-for-physical-engineering startup launched with ~$6.2B.
interesting_fact: Project Prometheus marked Jeff Bezos's first formal operating role since leaving Amazon's CEO post; Bajaj shares the co-CEO title with him at a company building AI that learns from the physical world for engineering and manufacturing.
deep_cut_fact: As a Berkeley researcher in Alex Pines's lab he was lead author of a 2010 Science paper, 'Zooming In on Microscopic Flow by Remotely Detected MRI', which imaged fluid flow in microfluidic chips ~a million times faster than conventional MRI on the same hardware.
notes: Also adjunct associate professor at Stanford and co-founder/director of AI drug-discovery company Xaira (per Foresite Capital bio). No published press email found for Project Prometheus; company is secretive. Possible route: Foresite Capital contact page (https://www.foresitecapital.com).

name: John Schulman
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist, Thinking Machines Lab
profile: American AI researcher and OpenAI co-founder (Dec 2015) who led the reinforcement-learning team behind ChatGPT and invented TRPO and PPO, the RL algorithms used in RLHF. Left OpenAI for Anthropic in Aug 2024 to focus on alignment, then in Feb 2025 joined Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab as co-founder and chief scientist.
interesting_fact: Often called the 'architect' of ChatGPT: his Trust Region Policy Optimization and Proximal Policy Optimization algorithms were core components of the RLHF training that produced it.
deep_cut_fact: As a seventh-grader he became obsessed with TV's BattleBots and self-studied to design a better combat robot (it was never built); he went on to make the 2005 US Physics Olympiad team from Great Neck South High School before studying physics at Caltech.
notes: Personal X is reportedly @johnschulman2 (bio mentions RL, alignment, birds, jazz) but I could only confirm via third-party aggregators, not his own site. No published press email found for Thinking Machines; company is research-focused and media-light.

name: Liu Huaiyu
current_role: Co-founder and COO, Bambu Lab (Shenzhen consumer 3D-printer maker)
profile: Liu Huaiyu (UESTC class of 1999) was a DJI product manager for DJI Goggles, the digital FPV system and FPV drones before co-founding Bambu Lab in 2020 with fellow DJI engineers led by CEO Tao Ye. Bambu Lab became a global leader in consumer 3D printers (X1, P1, A1, H2 series); he serves as COO.
interesting_fact: Bambu Lab's founding team came out of DJI's core R&D groups and set out to build 3D printers 'to the same standards DJI applied to drones'; its X1 launched via Kickstarter, raising about US$7M.
deep_cut_fact: In January 2026 Liu personally visited his alma mater UESTC to make the first donation under Bambu Lab's 100M-yuan 'Alma Mater Fund', funding a Bambu Lab Scholarship and Teaching Award plus 3D printers for student robotics and model-aircraft clubs.
notes: Low public profile; Bambu Lab's media/influencer channel (contact@bambulab.com, select 'Influencer & Media' category) is the published route. No personal social accounts found.

name: Chen Zihan
current_role: Co-founder and chief engineer, Bambu Lab (Shenzhen)
profile: Chen Zihan is one of the former DJI engineers who co-founded Bambu Lab in November 2020; at DJI he was reported to have run the gimbal department (motion-control/stabilisation). Bambu Lab now makes some of the world's best-selling consumer 3D printers (X1, P1, A1, H2 lines) and was valued around $6B.
interesting_fact: Bambu Lab's founders deliberately applied DJI's precision machinery, motion control and machine-vision know-how to desktop 3D printing; the X1 used lidar-based bed levelling and first-layer inspection.
deep_cut_fact: Before Bambu Lab, Chen was responsible for gimbal systems at DJI, the camera-stabilisation tech at the heart of DJI's drones and handhelds.
notes: Name also appears as 陈子涵/陈子寒 in Chinese press; very low public profile, no personal accounts found. Route via Bambu Lab media channel.

name: Max Junestrand
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Legora (legal AI platform, Stockholm/New York)
profile: Swedish founder who studied computer engineering at KTH and business at the Stockholm School of Economics in parallel while working as a programmer. In 2023 he joined Sigge Labor and August Erséus to build Leya (renamed Legora in 2025), a collaborative AI workspace for lawyers that went through YC W24, reached ~$100M ARR within about 18 months and was valued at ~$5.55B.
interesting_fact: Legora is used by 140,000+ legal professionals at 2,600+ firms and in-house teams across 80+ markets, despite its CEO having no legal background.
deep_cut_fact: He initially missed admission to SSE on a technicality - after retaking courses to raise his grades he forgot to upload the updated transcripts - and got in a year later as one of the final reserve candidates. Legora's internal motto LFG stands for 'Lean in. Fight for excellence. Grow together.'
notes: Highly visible on podcasts (YC, Pigment Perspectives, 20VC-style shows); comfortable with media. Legora press office is the published route.

name: August Erséus
current_role: Co-founder of Legora (listed as CPO on Crunchbase; current involvement unclear)
profile: Swedish co-founder of legal-AI company Legora (formerly Leya). With Sigge Labor he began experimenting with AI for legal text in 2020, revived the idea in 2023 once LLMs could handle it, and brought in Max Junestrand as CEO. Legora went through YC W24 and has been valued at ~$5.5B+, serving 2,600+ legal customers.
interesting_fact: Legora's origin was a 2020 attempt by Erséus and Labor to use Google's BERT for legal tech; pre-LLM models couldn't handle nuanced legal text (especially non-English), so they shelved it until GPT-3-era models made a prototype work 'flawlessly'.
notes: Some aggregator sources (aiwiki.ai) claim he parted ways with the company in Nov 2024; Contrary (2026) still lists him as co-founder. Verify current status before outreach. Very low public profile. Unverified: LinkedIn snippet says he previously did data science at Conmigo and R&D at KTH. He is not listed among active founders on Legora's YC page.

name: Sigge Labor
current_role: Co-founder and President (formerly CTO), Legora
profile: Swedish developer and Hyper Island graduate who worked as a full-stack engineer at startups before co-founding legal-AI company Leya (now Legora). He and August Erséus began building legal AI in 2020, revived it in 2023 with LLMs and recruited Max Junestrand as CEO; Legora went through YC W24 and has been valued at ~$5.5B+.
interesting_fact: Legora started as a 2020 experiment using Google's BERT on legal text; it was shelved because pre-LLM models couldn't handle nuanced (especially non-English) legal language, then revived in 2023.
deep_cut_fact: His own YC bio says he 'founded the first-ever Mexican hops company' and jokingly lists his skills as family tech support - resetting grandparents' forgotten email passwords.
notes: Lower public profile than CEO Max Junestrand; route via Legora press office.

name: Jeff Cardenas
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Apptronik (Austin, TX humanoid robotics)
profile: UT Austin BBA '08 / MSTC '13 who co-founded Apptronik in 2016 as a spin-out of UT's Human Centered Robotics Lab with Luis Sentis, Nick Paine and Bill Helmsing. Apptronik builds the Apollo humanoid, partners with Google DeepMind, and closed a $935M+ Series A in Feb 2026 (valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: When Apptronik started, he says, 'everyone told us not to do humanoids'; he framed humanoids as a 'PC moment for robotics' and Apptronik later partnered with Google DeepMind on AI-powered humanoids.
deep_cut_fact: Son of an Air Force colonel, he grew up playing with Transformers; after his BBA he first tried a mobile-app startup (market was oversaturated), then spent four years at Deloitte and worked at UT's IC2 Institute, where he met mentor Gen. Bill Welch and the robotics team.
notes: Frequent podcast/conference guest (TechFirst, Automated podcast, SiliconANGLE theCUBE) - receptive to media. Head of Communications Liz Clinkenbeard is the named media contact on press releases.

name: Luis Sentis
current_role: Professor of Aerospace Engineering, UT Austin (directs Human Centered Robotics Lab); co-founder & scientific advisor, Apptronik
profile: Catalan-trained roboticist (telecom engineering, UPC) who went to Stanford in 1997, did a PhD on humanoids and worked with Honda and NASA. As a UT Austin professor he led UT's DARPA Robotics Challenge effort with NASA JSC, and in 2016 co-founded Apptronik, spun out of his lab; it builds the Apollo humanoid and is valued ~$5B.
interesting_fact: His whole-body control theory for humanoid robots is described as now used in humanoid robots worldwide.
deep_cut_fact: He went to Stanford in 1997 on a 'la Caixa' Foundation fellowship (he says humanoid robots 'might not exist' without it); the day after arriving he was already discussing robotics with physicist Edward Teller, and he later lived the dot-com boom/bust at a Motorola spin-off.
notes: Academic and approachable; speaks Spanish. University email is the most direct published route.

name: Nicholas Paine
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Apptronik
profile: Robotics researcher from UT Austin's Human Centered Robotics Lab (Luis Sentis's lab) who co-founded Apptronik in 2016; the company's first project was work on NASA's Valkyrie humanoid. As CTO he leads hardware/controls for the Apollo general-purpose humanoid; Apptronik has raised $935M+ and is valued ~$5B.
interesting_fact: For Apollo, the team tested about 30 actuators to find the right one; Paine says he co-founded a general-purpose humanoid company partly because 'I was sick of seeing robots just dancing all the time.'
deep_cut_fact: Apptronik's first project was NASA's 300-pound Valkyrie humanoid; Paine explained in 2018 that robots must sense force and detect human contact to work safely near people, and that 'we try to be unconventional in the way we design things.'
notes: Technical co-founder; lower profile than CEO Jeff Cardenas. Route via Apptronik press.

name: Bill Helmsing
current_role: Co-founder, Apptronik (current title not confirmed)
profile: UT Austin alumnus and one of the 2016 co-founders of Apptronik (with Jeff Cardenas, Nick Paine, Luis Sentis and Gen. Bill Welch), the humanoid-robot spin-out of UT's Human Centered Robotics Lab now valued ~$5B. Little else about him is public.
interesting_fact: Apptronik, which he co-founded, ran without outside investors through at least 2018, building its own actuators and controllers in-house for clients including NASA and Lockheed Martin.
notes: Very low public profile; not quoted in Apptronik press. Web search budget exhausted before a fuller check.

name: Matt Huang
current_role: Co-founder & Managing Partner, Paradigm; founder & project lead, Tempo (payments blockchain incubated by Stripe and Paradigm)
profile: MIT math grad and former Sequoia partner (early in ByteDance, Instacart, Benchling) who co-founded crypto/frontier-tech investor Paradigm in 2018. He sits on the boards of Stripe and Kalshi and leads Tempo, a payments-first Layer 1 for stablecoins co-founded by Paradigm and Stripe (valued ~$5B).
interesting_fact: Stripe CEO Patrick Collison says Tempo is now Stripe's default blockchain for new features.
deep_cut_fact: Before venture capital he founded Hotspots, a Y Combinator company that Twitter acquired in 2012.
notes: Paradigm lists an executive assistant (Anita Wong) on his profile, with no published email; Paradigm contact page is the formal route. Tempo press email is best for a payments/stablecoin angle.

name: Chen Zhuo
current_role: Chairman-designate (previously President/CEO) of Avatr Technology; Vice President of Changan Automobile
profile: Chongqing-born Changan Automobile veteran (joined 2006) who ran brand PR and was company spokesperson before moving to Changan/Huawei/CATL-backed EV maker Avatr in Feb 2023, becoming president that December. Named a Changan VP in June 2026; Sept 2026 reports say he is moving up to Avatr chairman as it pursues a Hong Kong IPO.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Avatr launched the 11, 12, 07 and 06 models plus the 06T and 07L, and refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in June 2026.
deep_cut_fact: He joined Changan straight out of an engineering degree in 2006 and rose through brand PR to become Changan's company spokesperson, and was CEO of its Qiyuan product line before leading Avatr.
notes: Corporate executive of state-owned Changan's EV subsidiary rather than a classic founder-owner; Hurun lists him as founder. Title in flux (president -> chairman reported Sept 2026, based on unnamed sources). Avatr site also lists oversea@avatr.com for overseas inquiries.

name: Florian Seibel
current_role: Co-founder and Co-CEO, Quantum Systems (Gilching, Germany); BDLI board startup representative
profile: Former Bundeswehr officer (1999-2016) and helicopter pilot who studied aerospace engineering at the Bundeswehr University Munich, left a PhD unfinished and co-founded drone maker Quantum Systems in January 2015 with Michael Kriegel, Tobias Kloss and Armin Busse. The firm builds eVTOL surveillance/mapping drones (Trinity, Vector) used heavily by Ukraine and has grown to 1,000+ staff with multibillion-euro valuations.
interesting_fact: After Russia's 2022 invasion he committed Quantum Systems to support Ukraine's armed forces with a 'whatever it takes' approach; the company opened service and production sites in Ukraine.
deep_cut_fact: He is a passionate glider pilot, flight instructor and paraglider as well as a helicopter pilot, and he never finished the drone-focused PhD he started at the Bundeswehr University in 2010 because he chose to found Quantum Systems instead.
notes: Quantum Systems site is behind Cloudflare and could not be read for a press email; check its press page manually. Seibel is a frequent conference speaker (Unternehmertag, Project A Knowledge Conference) and the defence-tech angle is strong.

name: Michael Kriegel
current_role: Co-founder, Quantum Systems (Gilching, Germany) — current title not confirmed
profile: Dr. Michael Kriegel met Florian Seibel at the Bundeswehr University Munich and co-founded drone maker Quantum Systems with Seibel, Tobias Kloss and Armin Busse in January 2015. The company builds eVTOL fixed-wing reconnaissance drones (Trinity, Vector) widely used in Ukraine, has grown past 1,000 staff and is valued in the billions.
interesting_fact: Quantum Systems' Vector drones were first sold to Ukraine in April 2022 for reconnaissance; by Aug 2024 about 288 had been delivered, and the Bundeswehr bought units for its own stocks.
deep_cut_fact: Together with Seibel he filed a 2012 German patent (DE102012104783) for the precursor of the company's first production drone — three years before Quantum Systems was incorporated. Its first product, the 'Tron' eVTOL, carried a 2 kg payload.
notes: Very low public profile; no personal channels found. Quantum Systems site is behind Cloudflare; press contact should be taken from its press page. Web-search budget ran out during this lane, so research was limited to directly fetched pages.

After an early detour into mobile vending, Neolix pivoted to courier logistics, raised a $600M+ Series D and (Oct 2026) a ~$400M Series E, and says it has deployed 13,000+ vehicles in 300+ cities across 15 countries.
interesting_fact: In 2021 Neolix obtained China's first public-road licence for an autonomous delivery vehicle; in 2026 Yu said the industry's real 'blue ocean' is nighttime delivery.
deep_cut_fact: Yu graduated from Chongqing University in automation in 1996, invented a parcel locker and built China's first dedicated courier handheld scanner (PDA). Neolix's first vans used the chassis and Changzhou production lines of Li Xiang's shelved SEV mini-car; Li Auto became its angel investor.
notes: contacts@neolix.cn is Neolix's general company contact (no separate press address found). Yu speaks often at Chinese mobility conferences; Gasgoo has English coverage of his talks.

name: Li Ziyi
current_role: Probably 李子夷 (Li Ziyi), CFO of Neolix (新石器) - unconfirmed
profile: Hurun lists Li Ziyi as a founder of Neolix (新石器慧通), the Beijing maker of L4 driverless delivery vans (13,000+ deployed in 15 countries; ~US$400M Series E in Oct 2026). Neolix's founder and CEO is Yu Enyuan (余恩源); the closest match found is 李子夷, listed as Neolix CFO and legal representative of a Quanzhou subsidiary. No bio found.
interesting_fact: Neolix says it has deployed more than 13,000 driverless delivery vehicles in 300+ cities across 15 countries, with 60M+ km of autonomous driving, and closed a nearly US$400M Series E in October 2026.
notes: Identity uncertain: no source ties the romanised name 'Li Ziyi' to Neolix; 36Kr pitchhub lists 李子夷 as CFO (https://pitchhub.36kr.com/project/2011455065982216). If the journalist wants Neolix's founder, that is Yu Enyuan (余恩源). Low public profile.

name: Yang Zhe
current_role: Co-founder and Chief Designer (总设计师), Neolix (新石器慧通科技股份有限公司), Beijing
profile: Yang Zhe (杨哲) co-founded Neolix in 2018 with CEO Yu Enyuan and Li Ziyi; the Beijing company builds L4 driverless delivery vans used for parcel, fresh-food and retail logistics across Chinese cities. Hurun's 2026 unicorn index valued Neolix at about US$2B, and in Oct 2026 it reported a ~US$400M Series E. Yang leads vehicle design and speaks for the company at industry events.
interesting_fact: At the 2026 World Intelligent Connected Vehicles Conference Yang unveiled Neolix's X6T self-loading van, which keeps L4 autonomy while loading and unloading its own cargo - up to three standard roll cages of ~400 kg each.
deep_cut_fact: Yang is a designer by background: in December 2020 he was nominated for the 16th Guanghua Longteng Award as one of China's Top Ten Outstanding Young Designers (光华龙腾奖·中国设计业十大杰出青年提名奖).
notes: Common Chinese name - reference Neolix/新石器 and his chief-designer role. Deep-cut source is a Baike encyclopedia entry (secondary). He has said Neolix's real-world logistics data is valuable for embodied-AI training, which fits the AI/data angle. Investors include Li Auto and Tencent.

name: Parag Agrawal
current_role: Founder and CEO, Parallel Web Systems (web search/research APIs for AI agents)
profile: IIT Bombay and Stanford PhD computer scientist who rose from engineer to CTO and then CEO of Twitter (Nov 2021) until Elon Musk's takeover in Oct 2022. He then founded Parallel Web Systems, which builds infrastructure for AI agents to use the open web; it raised a $100M Series B led by Sequoia at a $2B valuation in April 2026.
interesting_fact: Parallel's $2B Series B (April 2026) came only about five months after a $100M Series A at a reported $740M valuation, roughly a 2.7x step-up.
deep_cut_fact: As a 17-year-old in 2001 he won a gold medal for India at the International Physics Olympiad in Antalya, Turkey; his Stanford PhD (advisor Jennifer Widom, 2012) was on incorporating uncertainty in databases.
notes: Highly relevant to AI/data-center theme (agent web infrastructure). Generally keeps a low media profile since Twitter; posts about Parallel on X @paraga.

name: Travers Nisbet
current_role: Co-founder, Parallel Web Systems (leads product, GTM and operations)
profile: Travers Nisbet co-founded Parallel Web Systems with ex-Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal in 2023; he runs product, go-to-market and operations. Parallel builds search and deep-research APIs designed for AI agents rather than humans, and hit a $2B valuation in April 2026. Before Parallel he was a GM at Chime and spent four years at McKinsey in San Francisco.
interesting_fact: Parallel's pitch is that AIs are the web's 'second user': it launched Index in May 2026, a model for paying publishers when AI agents use their content.
deep_cut_fact: At Chime he was a GM leading bank strategy and operations during hypergrowth, and at McKinsey he worked on research around AI governance.
notes: Low-profile co-founder (Agrawal is the public face). hello@parallel.ai is the general contact listed on Parallel's press page. He spoke at RAISE Summit 2026 and on a Terrain Capital video (May 2026).

name: Xu Gao
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Plaud (Plaud.ai), San Francisco/Shenzhen
profile: Xu Gao (Nathan Xu), a Wuhan University graduate and ex-VC at China Growth Capital, co-founded Plaud in 2021 with Shenzhen factory owner Charles Liu. Plaud's AI voice recorders (Note, NotePin) with ChatGPT-powered transcription have sold 1M+ units; it was bootstrapped, profitable and targeting ~$250M annualized revenue in 2025. He is based in San Francisco.
interesting_fact: Plaud was bootstrapped with the founders' savings and a Kickstarter that raised over $1M in pre-orders; it sells only outside China to avoid Shenzhen copycats and price wars, and about half its revenue comes from AI subscriptions.
deep_cut_fact: His first startup, inspired by a university class on innovation, was a website to help Chinese students choose and apply to colleges abroad; later, as an investor at Beijing-based China Growth Capital, he backed Indonesian digital bank Akulaku.
notes: Uses the English name Nathan Xu (sometimes Nathan Hsu) - search under that name. Media-friendly (Forbes, NYSE spotlight, Z Potentials interviews). media@plaud.ai is the published channel for interviews.

name: Pedro Mac Dowell
current_role: Founder and CEO, QI Tech (São Paulo, Brazil)
profile: Brazilian fintech founder. After 11 years as co-founder/CEO of credit fund manager Quatá Investimentos, he founded QI Tech in 2018 as banking/credit-as-a-service infrastructure; it became a unicorn in 2024 and in 2025 ANBIMA ranked it Brazil's largest FIDC administrator and custodian.
interesting_fact: QI Tech was the first Sociedade de Crédito Direto (SCD) licensed by Brazil's Central Bank (Dec 2018), and its 2021 R$270M round from GIC was billed as LatAm's largest fintech Series A.
deep_cut_fact: Before fintech, he spent five years at Standard & Poor's in Transaction Services for Latin America, managed funds at Link Corretora and co-founded Sorse Asset Management; he studied Business Administration at Ibmec.
notes: Company press inbox is comunicacao@qitech.com.br. QI Tech has publicly discussed an eventual IPO.

name: Marcelo Bentivoglio
current_role: Co-founder and CFO, QI Tech (Brazil)
profile: Co-founder and CFO of QI Tech, the Brazilian financial-infrastructure (banking/credit-as-a-service) unicorn, which he joined as CFO around its 2018 founding (one Insper report says 2021). He leads fundraising, including rounds from GIC and General Atlantic.
interesting_fact: On IPO plans (South Summit Brazil, Apr 2025): 'Hoje, eu não tenho nada a fazer com o dinheiro... Seria um IPO por ego' - he views an IPO purely as a financial transaction.
deep_cut_fact: His fundraising philosophy, from a 2025 interview: 'Muita gente olha para a captação como um prêmio, eu olho como um compromisso' (many see a raise as a prize; I see it as a commitment).
notes: Not listed among founders on QI Tech's own About page (which lists Mac Dowell, Buosi, Emilio Moreira), though press calls him co-founder.

name: Marcelo Buosi
current_role: Co-founder and COO, QI Tech (Brazil)
profile: Co-founder and COO of QI Tech, the Brazilian banking/credit-as-a-service infrastructure unicorn founded in 2018. Before that he worked with Pedro Mac Dowell at credit fund manager Quatá Investimentos in operations and fund management; QI Tech grew out of Quatá's own infrastructure needs.
interesting_fact: QI Tech reports R$494B in Pix transactions, R$107B+ in credit issued and R$190B+ under management.
deep_cut_fact: An economist from USP's FEA, he started out in the economics department of Barclays Bank before joining Quatá Investimentos.

name: Alex Bradford
current_role: CEO and Founder, Rain (earned wage access platform, rainapp.com)
profile: Founded Rain in 2019 to offer earned wage access and financial-wellness tools integrated with employers' payroll (Workday, etc.). Rain raised a $75M Series B led by Prosus (2025) and $300M in financing from Clear Haven. Stanford undergrad and HBS MBA, with brief stints at Goldman Sachs and McKinsey.
interesting_fact: Rain is his third fintech company; he got the idea in late 2018 after learning of a European employer-integrated finance company.
deep_cut_fact: At Stanford he was a teaching assistant for a Social Entrepreneurship course focused heavily on microcredit.
notes: Check Hurun's $2B valuation: it may conflate with Rain (rain.xyz), a separate stablecoin-card company. No press email found on rainapp.com.

name: George Brooks

profile: Hurun lists him as a founder of Rain (valued $2B). Rain's own press materials name Alex Bradford as CEO and founder and do not mention George Brooks; I could not confirm his role.

name: Guo Lifu
current_role: Co-president and co-founder, UniVista (合见工软, Shanghai Hejian Industrial Software Group), Chinese EDA chip-design software maker
profile: Guo Lifu (郭立阜) is a former Synopsys Fellow and R&D vice president who in 2020 co-founded Shanghai-based EDA firm UniVista with investor Pan Jianyue and ex-Cadence China head Xu Yun; he is co-president. UniVista, which builds domestic chip-verification and design tools, raised ~RMB 3B, was valued around RMB 13B and began A-share IPO tutoring in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: UniVista deliberately chose chip verification as its entry point because verification was the weakest link among Chinese EDA tools; within about a year of founding it had grown to 300 staff, 220+ in R&D.
deep_cut_fact: Before co-founding UniVista he held the title of Fellow at Synopsys, one of the most senior technical ranks at the US EDA giant, alongside a role as R&D vice president; UniVista's CTO Pei-Hsin Ho is also an ex-Synopsys Fellow.
notes: Listed jointly on Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026 with Pan Jianyue and Xu Yun (Chinese name 郭立阜 confirmed via Hurun data). Low public profile; no personal channels found. Relevant for AI-chip/data-center supply chain angle.

name: Xu Yun
current_role: General Manager (总经理), Shanghai UniVista Industrial Software Group (合见工软), Chinese EDA chip-design software maker
profile: Xu Yun (徐昀), a woman executive, co-founded UniVista in Shanghai in 2020 with chairman Pan Jianyue (ex-Synopsys China president) and co-president Guo Lifu; Hurun's 2026 Global Unicorn Index values it at ~$2B. UniVista builds electronic design automation (EDA) tools for domestic chips; she leads it as GM (earlier titled group president) and it filed for IPO tutoring in Dec 2025.
interesting_fact: UniVista is seen as the only Chinese vendor covering the full digital-chip verification flow, complete DFT and high-speed interconnect IP, challenging Synopsys, Cadence and Siemens, which hold ~74% of the global EDA market; it filed for IPO guidance on 26 Dec 2025.
notes: Identity confirmed via Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026 (Univista / 合见工软, founders 潘建岳、郭立阜、徐昀, Shanghai, semiconductors, $2B). Little English-language material on her personal background; she speaks at ICCAD and China electronics forums. AI super-node/compute angle relevant to data-center podcast. Approach via pr@univista-isg.com, ideally in Chinese.

name: Isaiah Taylor
current_role: Founder and CEO, Valar Atomics (El Segundo, CA; small modular / micro nuclear reactors)
profile: Isaiah Taylor, 27, dropped out of high school at 16, ran an auto-repair shop in northern Idaho and a software company, then founded Valar Atomics in 2023 to build small, passively safe nuclear reactors on a factory line. Valar raised a $130M Series A in late 2025 and is bringing its first reactor online at a site in Orangeville, Emery County, Utah.
interesting_fact: His great-grandfather, Ward Schaap, was a Manhattan Project nuclear physicist at Oak Ridge, Tennessee; Taylor's grandmother was born in the Army field hospital there.
deep_cut_fact: He learned to code at about age 10 after a software engineer at his church introduced him to a kids' programming language; by 16 he had decided to start Valar, but chose to build other companies first to gain experience. In Feb 2026 Valar's 5 MW reactor was airlifted to Utah aboard three Air Force cargo planes.
notes: Very media-accessible (TBPN, Limitless and other podcasts; active on X). Note that some outlets wrongly call Ward Schaap his grandfather - he is his great-grandfather. Some critical press exists about the company's investors; avoid. Good fit for energy/data-center podcast.

name: Bar Winkler
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Wonderful (enterprise AI agent platform)
profile: Israeli entrepreneur who co-founded Wonderful in early 2025 with CTO Roey Lalazar to build AI agents for enterprise customer service, especially in non-English markets. Previously founded procurement startup Approve.com (sold to Tipalti, 2021). Wonderful raised $150M at a $2B valuation (2026 Series B) and then $550M at ~$5B (Sept 2026).
interesting_fact: Wonderful went from founding in early 2025 to a ~$5B valuation in under two years and ~650 employees across 35+ markets, deploying local teams alongside its AI agents.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Approve.com, Winkler was an early employee at ironSource, the Israeli app-monetization company that later went public at an ~$11B valuation.
notes: Hurun lists the industry as Agriculture, but this is Wonderful the Israeli AI company (wonderful.ai), not The Wonderful Company. Valuation is now ~$5B, not $2B. No personal press email found; use company channels.

name: Roey Lalazar
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Wonderful (enterprise AI agent platform)
profile: Israeli technologist who co-founded Wonderful in early 2025 with CEO Bar Winkler. Wonderful builds AI agents and an 'AI operating system' for enterprise customer service and back-office workflows, focusing on non-English markets. It raised $150M at a $2B valuation (Series B, 2026), then $550M at ~$5B in September 2026, and has ~650 staff.
interesting_fact: Wonderful planned to grow from 350 to ~900 employees in a single year to serve enterprises in 30+ countries across Europe, the Middle East, APAC and Latin America, pairing its AI agents with local deployment teams.
deep_cut_fact: Before Wonderful, Lalazar founded Kaps, an AI-based localization platform. That language work foreshadows Wonderful's focus on non-English-speaking markets.
notes: Low personal media profile; CEO Bar Winkler does most of the press. Hurun's $2B valuation is outdated (now ~$5B). Some outlets misspell his name as 'Lalzar'/'Royel'.

name: Michael Grinich
current_role: Founder & CEO, WorkOS (San Francisco)
profile: Software founder who previously co-founded email-API company Nylas, then launched WorkOS in March 2020 to give developers plug-in enterprise features (SSO, SCIM directory sync, audit logs, permissions). In March 2026 WorkOS raised a $100M Series C at a $2B valuation led by Meritech and Sapphire. Customers include OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Cursor and Perplexity, and it is pushing into auth for AI agents.
interesting_fact: WorkOS sells 'enterprise readiness' to AI labs: OpenAI, Anthropic, xAI, Cursor, Perplexity and Replit all use it. Grinich argues that as software becomes autonomous, 'trust becomes the constraint.'
deep_cut_fact: In 2022 WorkOS bought Modulz, maker of the popular open-source Radix UI framework. Angels in that $80M Series B included Hollywood super-agent Michael Ovitz, Guillermo Rauch and Jack Altman.

public_contacts.value: Crossing the Enterprise Chasm (WorkOS podcast featuring Grinich): https://workos.com/podcast

notes: Very reachable founder: active on X (@grinich, ~15.7K followers, and grinich.com redirects there) and runs a B2B podcast, so it is a natural fit for a podcast invite. The Nylas background is from general knowledge; no fetched source was re-checked because web-search quota ran out.

profile: Hurun lists Wang Haibin as a founder of BioRay Biopharmaceutical, the biologics company that grew out of Hisun Pharma (Taizhou, est. 1956). No company source we could access names Wang Haibin.
