name: Yang Yufeng
current_role: Party Secretary & Chairman, SPIC Hydrogen Energy Technology (国氢科技, 'Spiche'); also Chairman of SPIC Green Energy (电投绿能, formerly Jilin Electric Power, SZ:000875)
profile: Yang Yufeng (杨玉峰, b. 1976) is a career executive at State Power Investment Corp (SPIC), not a founder in the entrepreneurial sense. In January 2026 SPIC put him in charge of its hydrogen unicorn 国氢科技 (Hurun: ~$1.9B) on top of chairing listed SPIC Green Energy, which renamed itself from Jilin Electric Power in Feb 2026.
interesting_fact: 国氢科技's self-developed 'Qingteng' (氢腾) fuel-cell systems powered about 150 hydrogen buses that handled transport during the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics. The company has built an in-house supply chain covering catalysts, proton-exchange membranes, carbon paper and full stack/system integration.
deep_cut_fact: Yang came up through HR and power marketing rather than engineering. He headed human resources at China Power International, ran the Pingdingshan Yaomeng coal-fired power plants in Henan, then directed SPIC's electricity-market marketing centre before taking over Jilin Electric. He holds a master's degree and is a senior economist.
notes: Hurun lists him as 'founder' of Spiche (SPIC Hydrogen), but he is a state-appointed SOE chairman, not an owner-founder; the company is controlled by SPIC. The email is the board-office mailbox of listed sister company SPIC Green Energy (2024 annual report). Contact through official channels in Chinese is likely to be slow, and SOE executives rarely do foreign podcasts.

name: Chen Yilun
current_role: Founder & CEO, TARS (它石智航), Shanghai embodied-AI/robotics company
profile: Chen Yilun co-founded TARS in Feb 2025 with ex-Baidu IDG president Li Zhenyu and ex-Huawei 'Genius Youth' Ding Wenchao. He was previously CTO of autonomous driving and chief scientist of Huawei's automotive BU, then chief robotics scientist at Tsinghua AIR. TARS builds industrial general-purpose robots (AWE foundation model, DexHand) and raised a record ~$455M Pre-A in April 2026.
interesting_fact: TARS's 2026 Pre-A round of about $455M (3.1bn yuan) was described as the largest single financing round in China's embodied-intelligence sector.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his bachelor's and master's in electronic engineering at Tsinghua and a PhD in EE from the University of Michigan (2011), and before Huawei was chief machine-vision engineer at DJI.
notes: Company press contact is published on TARS's PR Newswire releases. Chen has argued embodied AI today resembles intelligent driving around 2019; good podcast angle (autonomy to robotics).

name: Li Zhenyu
current_role: Co-founder & Chairman, TARS (它石智航), Shanghai embodied-AI/robotics company
profile: Li Zhenyu spent 16 years at Baidu (from 2007), rising to senior VP and president of the Intelligent Driving Group, where he led the Apollo autonomous-driving platform and the Apollo Go (Luobo Kuaipao) robotaxi service. He stepped back from IDG in late 2023 and in 2025 co-founded TARS with ex-Huawei executives Chen Yilun and Ding Wenchao; TARS raised a record ~$455M Pre-A in 2026.
interesting_fact: He built Apollo Go (Luobo Kuaipao), described as the world's largest robotaxi platform, before turning to embodied AI.
deep_cut_fact: A Beihang University (BUAA) master's graduate, he began his career doing network-technology R&D at Huawei, where he received Huawei's top honour, before Baidu recruited him in 2007; inside Baidu he was known as the 'firefighting captain' (救火队长).
notes: Only company-level contact found (TARS PR). Low personal public profile outside Chinese media.

name: Ding Wenchao
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Scientist, TARS (它石智航), Shanghai embodied-AI/robotics company
profile: Ding Wenchao joined Huawei in 2020 as one of its 'Genius Youth' recruits and worked on the decision-making network for its ADS 1.0 intelligent-driving system. In 2023 he became a researcher at Fudan University, then co-founded TARS in 2025 with Chen Yilun and Li Zhenyu. As chief scientist he leads TARS's AWE foundation model and DexHand dexterous hand.
interesting_fact: MIT Technology Review named him to its 2025 Innovators Under 35 China list (Inventor category), and he gave a plenary keynote at ICRA 2026 in Vienna.
deep_cut_fact: He studied at Huazhong University of Science and Technology and did his graduate degree at HKUST; at Fudan he developed the university's first humanoid robot.
notes: The Fudan humanoid-robot detail is from Gasgoo (https://autonews.gasgoo.com/articles/news/seeds-former-huawei-and-baidu-executives-team-up-secure-over-3-billion-yuan-in-financing-2044746801104470017); education is from cnyes. Most technical and English-friendly of the TARS founders, so a good podcast guest.

name: Jonathan Hurst
current_role: Co-Founder & Chief Robot Officer, Agility (formerly Agility Robotics); Professor of Robotics, Oregon State University
profile: Carnegie Mellon-trained roboticist (BS, MS, PhD) who joined Oregon State in 2008 and ran its Dynamic Robotics Lab. In 2015 he co-founded Agility Robotics with Damion Shelton and Mikhail Jones to commercialise his legged-locomotion research; its humanoid Digit targets logistics/warehouses. Agility has raised 640M+ USD and is valued around 2.5B USD; renamed Agility in March 2026.
interesting_fact: Agility's robots descend from his lab's spring-mass biped ATRIAS (modelled on how a pogo stick works) and the ostrich-like Cassie, unveiled in 2017 and sold to university research groups, before the humanoid Digit.
deep_cut_fact: He was Oregon State University's first robotics professor (2008); the legged-locomotion program he built grew into an OSU robotics MS/PhD program, which he says was only the third such program in the US.
notes: Frequent conference speaker (RoboBusiness, AI Infra Summit, CMU Yata lecture) and podcast guest - receptive to media. Press contact Tim Smith (Element PR) via media@ address. Title variously listed as CTO in older sources; current is Chief Robot Officer.

name: Damion Shelton
current_role: Co-Founder & Chairman of the Board, Agility (Agility Robotics); AVP & Executive Director, Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, Carnegie Mellon University
profile: Carnegie Mellon robotics PhD who co-founded Agility Robotics in 2015 as a spinout of Jonathan Hurst's OSU legged-locomotion lab and served as CEO until 2024 (Peggy Johnson succeeded him; he then served as president). He now chairs Agility's board and runs CMU's Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, mentoring founders.
interesting_fact: His founder advice: 'build something that's useful to someone rapidly, as opposed to having it be an indefinite science project' - the approach he used to take Agility from research robots to warehouse humanoids.
deep_cut_fact: Before Agility he co-founded threeRivers 3D, where as CTO he designed a low-cost, high-volume laser scanner for novice users in healthcare; he describes himself as a 'jack-of-all-trades roboticist' who left academia to build products.
notes: Now based at CMU (Pittsburgh); CMU Swartz Center may be a better route than Agility. Has written for TechCrunch (author page exists) and spoken at TC Disrupt. Exact end dates of CEO/president roles vary across sources.

name: Mikhail Jones
current_role: Co-Founder, Agility (Agility Robotics); last listed as VP of Software (unverified profile)
profile: One of three co-founders of Agility Robotics (2015, with Jonathan Hurst and Damion Shelton), spun out of Oregon State University's Dynamic Robotics Lab where he had been a research engineer. Agility builds the Cassie biped and the Digit humanoid for logistics and manufacturing and is valued around 2.5B USD.
interesting_fact: Agility grew out of OSU research on spring-mass bipedal walking (ATRIAS), leading to the ostrich-like Cassie in 2017 and the humanoid Digit.
notes: Very low public profile; not listed on Agility's current leadership page, so his current role is unclear (theorg.com, unverified, lists VP of Software and prior OSU Faculty Research Assistant). Best route is via Agility press or co-founders. Research cut short by web-search quota.

name: Yang Ye
current_role: Co-founder and vice-chairman, Aulton New Energy (奥动新能源), Shanghai/Guangzhou EV battery-swapping operator
profile: Yang Ye (杨烨) is a co-founder of Aulton New Energy, the battery-swap network backed by Alpha Group's Cai Dongqing (creator of 'Pleasant Goat') with tech lead Zhang Jianping; Hurun's 2026 unicorn list credits Cai, Zhang and Yang. Aulton runs swap stations for taxi/ride-hailing fleets, has been valued ~RMB 11.9bn, and refiled for a Hong Kong IPO in July 2026.
interesting_fact: Aulton's latest stations can swap batteries for multiple car brands in about 20 seconds, and the company pitches 'vehicle-to-station-to-grid' - using swap stations as distributed storage that can feed power back to the grid. name: Jacob Kimmel

deep_cut_fact: At Calico (Alphabet's aging company) his PI lab developed methods to engineer cell identity and reprogram cell age, the work that became NewLimit's core thesis.

profile: Founded Garner Health, which analyses large medical-claims datasets to rank doctors on quality and cost, then steers employees of self-insured employers to top performers and reimburses their out-of-pocket costs. He was earlier on Oscar Health's leadership team (analytics, provider networks) and a partner at Bridgewater Associates. Hurun values Garner at ~$1B+.
interesting_fact: Garner applies hedge-fund-style data analysis to healthcare: its leadership includes several Bridgewater alumni, and it scores physicians on outcomes to cut employer spend.
deep_cut_fact: Before healthcare, Reber was a partner at Bridgewater Associates, where he co-headed Research Analytics. At Oscar Health he then helped oversee growth to over $2B in revenue.
notes: Low-key founder with few personal social accounts found; the best route is Garner's PR email. Garner also runs a podcast and webinars (Resources section).

name: James Hawkins
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, PostHog
profile: British co-founder, with Tim Glaser, of PostHog, the open-source product-analytics and 'product OS' platform born in Y Combinator's W20 batch. PostHog has grown into session replay, feature flags, experiments, a data warehouse and AI tools, and claims 100,000+ customers. It has been cash-flow positive since Dec 2024, raised a Stripe-led $70M Series D (2025) and a $75M Series E (Oct 2025), and is valued at $1B+.
interesting_fact: PostHog says 54% of YC's first 2024 batch adopted it, making it one of the top three products used by YC companies. It is famous for an entirely public company handbook and a quirky hedgehog brand.
deep_cut_fact: PostHog's famous public handbook began as a hack. Before launching on Hacker News, Hawkins and Glaser wanted to 'look as mature as possible' with big footers like big, boring companies, so they wrote up how they wanted to work to fill the links.
notes: Very public, writes openly about running PostHog (handbook, newsletter, X), so a strong podcast candidate. The founders' first idea (Aug 2019) was a tool for managing technical debt, which failed before PostHog.

name: Tim Glaser
current_role: Co-founder & Co-CEO, PostHog
profile: Engineer who co-founded PostHog with James Hawkins on 23 January 2020 in Y Combinator's W20 batch. PostHog grew from open-source product analytics into a full product/data platform (session replay, feature flags, experiments, data warehouse, AI) with 100,000+ customers. It has been cash-flow positive since Dec 2024 and raised a $70M Stripe-led Series D and a $75M Series E in 2025; valued $1B+.
interesting_fact: PostHog launched its MVP on Hacker News just four weeks after the founders started writing code. Later it moved from PostgreSQL to ClickHouse to support billions of events.
deep_cut_fact: PostHog was not Glaser and Hawkins's first idea. Their first startup together (Aug 2019) aimed to help engineers manage technical debt; it didn't work, but it convinced them to treat 'growth as an engineering problem.'
notes: More engineering-focused and lower profile than co-CEO James Hawkins, who handles most public comms. No personal social handle was confirmed on PostHog pages (profiles are client-rendered); use press@posthog.com or go via Hawkins.

name: Victor Cardenas
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Slash (San Francisco vertical-banking fintech)
profile: Venezuelan-born Thiel Fellow who dropped out of Stanford to co-found Slash with Kevin Bai. Slash began offering cards and banking to sneaker resellers, then pivoted to industry-specific ('vertical') banking for ad buyers, e-commerce, web3 and more; it raised a $100M Series C from Khosla and Ribbit at a $1.4B valuation.
interesting_fact: After the 2022 Kanye West/Adidas fallout hit the sneaker-resale market, Slash's revenue reportedly fell about 80% almost overnight, prompting the pivot to vertical banking; Cardenas later said over 1% of all Facebook ads were bought with a Slash card.
deep_cut_fact: Raised in Caracas during the onset of hyperinflation, he built his first 'fintech' for his school cantina, which was forced to sell food without cash; at 19, as a Stanford sophomore, he co-founded Tabtab, an app for splitting subscriptions and rent.
notes: No published press email on slash.com (only support@slash.com, customer support). He says he reads mostly biographies (Napoleon, Hamilton, Juan Vicente Gomez) and is 'bullish on Venezuela' (Fintech Leaders interview).

name: Kevin Bai
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Slash (San Francisco vertical-banking fintech)
profile: Kevin Bai co-founded Slash with Victor Cardenas around 2021 after dropping out of the University of Waterloo. As CTO he runs the technology behind Slash's industry-specific banking, cards and stablecoin payments platform, built on Column bank; Slash raised a $100M Series C at a $1.4B valuation in 2026.
interesting_fact: Slash scaled to about $150M annualized revenue with only 15 engineers, which Bai wrote about on the company blog.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Thunder Bay, Ontario, and immigrated to the US after dropping out of UWaterloo to work on Slash full time; he also wrote a Slash engineering post on designing a data-correctness verification system.
notes: Don't confuse with other Kevin Bais (e.g. at Anthropic or Rippling). No published personal or press email; Slash lists only support@slash.com.

name: Robert Krayn
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Talkiatry (New York telepsychiatry company)
profile: Robert Krayn left a finance career in 2019 to co-found Talkiatry with psychiatrist Dr. Georgia Gaveras. It is an in-network virtual psychiatry and therapy practice that employs its clinicians as salaried staff. Talkiatry went fully virtual during COVID and grew to 800+ psychiatrists; it raised a $210M Series D in Feb 2026, bringing total funding past $400M.
interesting_fact: Talkiatry planned to see patients in person, with its first appointment set for April 2020 in New York, but lockdown forced it to go fully virtual, which became the basis of its growth.
deep_cut_fact: A Rutgers alum who worked in finance, Krayn made Business Insider's 2023 '30 leaders under 40 changing healthcare' list at age 35, recognized for running Talkiatry as a better workplace for psychiatrists.
notes: He has spoken publicly about struggling to find in-network psychiatric care himself; that is the founding story, but handle it with care and don't use it as an outreach hook. Talkiatry's press page also has a downloadable press kit.

name: Georgia Gaveras
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Medical Officer, Talkiatry
profile: Dr. Georgia Gaveras, DO, is a triple-board-certified psychiatrist (adult, child & adolescent, addiction medicine) who co-founded Talkiatry in 2019 with Robert Krayn. The New York telepsychiatry practice now has 800+ psychiatrists and raised a $210M Series D in 2026. As CMO she sets clinical standards and co-authors Talkiatry's outcomes research.
interesting_fact: In 2025 she was named to Modern Healthcare's 50 Most Influential Clinical Executives and to Inc.'s Female Founders 500.
deep_cut_fact: Before Talkiatry she directed the Comprehensive Psychiatric Emergency Program (CPEP) at Kings County Hospital in Brooklyn. She studied at NYU, earned her DO at the University of New England in Biddeford, Maine, and trained at SUNY Downstate.
notes: Her clinical focus has been adolescents and young adults with co-occurring substance-use disorders. She is a co-author of a 2023 JMIR telepsychiatry outcomes study. Route via Talkiatry press.

name: Roman Axelrod
current_role: Founder & Managing Partner, XPANCEO (Dubai smart-contact-lens deep-tech company)
profile: Roman Axelrod founded XPANCEO in Dubai with nanophotonics scientist Dr. Valentyn Volkov. The company is building an invisible, weightless smart contact lens as an AI-era computing platform. He has 17+ years building companies across Europe, the US and the Middle East, and at XPANCEO runs strategy, product, marketing and operations. The company raised what it calls MENA's largest Series A.
interesting_fact: XPANCEO says the Nature Index ranks it the world's No. 1 private startup by research output in natural sciences (June 2025-May 2026), and it has applied for 50+ patents.
deep_cut_fact: He holds a master's-level Diploma in Strategy and Finance from Oxford's Saïd Business School and has an academic background in international private law. In 2024 he was named to MIT Technology Review Arabia's Innovators Under 35.
notes: Writes thought-leadership pieces (Fast Company, TechCrunch, Crunchbase News on fundraising and investor trust), so pitching a conversation about deep-tech fundraising may resonate. The newsroom offers a press kit.

name: Valentyn S. Volkov
current_role: Co-Founder & Scientific Partner, XPANCEO (Dubai)
profile: Physicist specialising in nanophotonics and 2D materials who co-founded XPANCEO in 2021 with entrepreneur Roman Axelrod to build an all-in-one smart contact lens (XR display, health monitoring, night vision, zoom). He leads its R&D team; in July 2025 XPANCEO raised a 250M USD Series A at a 1.35B USD valuation.
interesting_fact: XPANCEO's scientific advisory board is chaired by Nobel laureate Sir Konstantin Novoselov, co-discoverer of graphene.
deep_cut_fact: Before XPANCEO he directed MIPT's Center for Photonics and 2D Materials, and co-authored a 2020 Laser & Photonics Reviews study proposing quantum dots above graphene to convert light into surface waves with a calculated efficiency of up to ~90% (vs. under 10% for prior schemes).
notes: Regular AWE XR conference speaker. hello@ is a general company inbox. Founding year given as 2018 in one article; most sources say 2021.

name: Steven Hunter
current_role: CEO & Co-Founder, 9fin (London)
profile: British former leveraged-finance professional (J.P. Morgan LevFin in London; investment executive at Babson Capital covering European high yield and leveraged loans) who co-founded 9fin in 2016 with Huss El-Sheikh. 9fin is an AI-native data, news and analytics platform for debt capital markets used by 350+ institutions; it has raised 250M+ USD and was valued around 1.3B USD at its Series C.
interesting_fact: 9fin has become a go-to voice on financing of the AI/data-center buildout (e.g. neocloud and CoreWeave debt); Hunter discussed 'Who's funding the AI buildout?' on Bloomberg Radio in Sept 2026 - directly relevant to an energy/data-center podcast.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a lawyer, graduating from the University of Bristol with a first-class honours law degree; his co-founder Huss El-Sheikh is also a Bristol graduate (MEng aerospace engineering).
notes: Media-friendly (Bloomberg Radio, NYSE Wired). team@9fin.com is a general company inbox linked in the site header. Some profiles mention Credit Suisse in his history; the official bio lists only J.P. Morgan and Babson.

name: Huss El-Sheikh
current_role: CTO & Co-Founder, 9fin (London)
profile: Hussam 'Huss' El-Sheikh co-founded 9fin in 2016 with Steven Hunter after a career in investment-bank technology at Deutsche Bank. As CTO he built 9fin's AI-native debt-market intelligence platform (news, data, analytics for leveraged finance, distressed, CLOs, private credit), used by 350+ institutions; the company has raised 250M+ USD and reached unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: 9fin describes itself as having been 'deploying AI for debt markets' for nine years - long before the generative-AI wave - and now offers an MCP connector so AI agents can query its credit data.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an aerospace engineer (MEng, University of Bristol) and joined Deutsche Bank as a graduate analyst, rising to Associate Vice President in Prime Finance, Equities and Derivatives Technology before co-founding 9fin.
notes: team@9fin.com is a general inbox. 9fin's reporters actively cover data-center/neocloud debt financing - a natural podcast angle.

name: Chris Taylor
current_role: Listed as founder of Aalyria (Google spinout; ~1B USD valuation); CEO title not re-verified this session
profile: Aalyria, the company he is listed as founding, was spun out of Google to commercialise the network-orchestration software ('Spacetime', formerly codenamed 'Minkowski' / the Loon SDN) that ran Google's Loon stratospheric-balloon internet network in production for three years, plus laser-communication technology. It targets satellite, aerospace and 5G non-terrestrial networks, including US defence customers.
interesting_fact: Aalyria's Spacetime software orchestrated Loon's balloon mesh network for three years, serving hundreds of thousands of users - a network Aalyria says was in many ways more complex than the largest LEO satellite constellations because balloons move far less predictably than satellites.
notes: Common name; Aalyria's site has no leadership page and web-search quota ran out, so his title/background could not be verified in this session. Company press inbox is the best route.

name: Brian Barritt
current_role: Co-Founder & CTO, Aalyria
profile: Network engineer behind the temporospatial software-defined networking (TS-SDN) that orchestrated Google's Loon balloon internet network; he co-founded Aalyria, the Google spinout commercialising that software ('Spacetime') for satellite, aerospace, 5G-NTN and defence networks. Aalyria is valued around 1B USD.
interesting_fact: Spacetime ran Loon's stratospheric mesh network in production for three years, serving hundreds of thousands of users across multiple continents, over E-band links highly vulnerable to rain and weather.
deep_cut_fact: Inside Google the software was codenamed 'Minkowski' (after the spacetime mathematician); Barritt co-authored with Wesley Eddy the 2016 AIAA paper 'SDN Enhancements for LEO Satellite Networks', which Aalyria still cites as a foundation of Spacetime.
notes: CTO title from theorg.com (another CTO also listed there, so title may have changed). Technical, publication-oriented; good for an episode on space/aerospace networking.

name: Nathan Wolfe
current_role: Co-founder, EVP & CTO (as of 2022 reporting), Aalyria Technologies
profile: Former Google engineer who developed the free-space laser communications technology that became Aalyria's Tightbeam product. Aalyria spun out of Alphabet in 2022 with Tightbeam (laser links) and Spacetime (network orchestration software from the Loon project), led at launch by CEO Chris Taylor; co-founder Brian Barritt became CEO in 2026.
interesting_fact: Aalyria's Tightbeam grew out of Google's 'Project Sonora' and Loon-era work on steerable laser beams; Wolfe said the tech was designed for 'backhauling these large Google-scale volumes of data'.
deep_cut_fact: Before Aalyria, Wolfe worked at Google developing the technology that became Tightbeam; Tightbeam itself grew out of Google's internal Project Sonora.
notes: NAME COLLISION: not the virologist Nathan Wolfe (Metabiota/Global Viral, Stanford), who dominates search results and has a 2026 Epstein-correspondence controversy - do not confuse. Aalyria's Wolfe has a very low profile; current title after the 2026 CEO change not confirmed.

name: Geoffrey Chaiken
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Blink Health (BlinkRx)
profile: Yale (2004) and Harvard MBA (2009) graduate who co-founded Blink Health with his brother Matthew; it launched publicly in Feb 2016 letting patients prepay for discounted prescriptions regardless of insurance. The company has since pivoted to BlinkRx, a pharma-partnered platform for home delivery of branded medicines. Earlier he was one of three investors at Brave Warrior Advisors (~$3B AUM).
interesting_fact: Blink Health let uninsured and insured patients alike pay for lower-priced prescriptions online and pick them up at their preferred pharmacy; it now operates as BlinkRx delivering branded drugs in all 50 states.
deep_cut_fact: Early in his career he founded Marinus Pharmaceuticals (epilepsy treatments), licensed its lead product and closed its $30M financing - billed as the largest financing of its kind in Connecticut history.
notes: No published press email found (search budget ran out before a press-release media contact could be located; check recent BlinkRx press releases). Co-founded with brother Matthew Chaiken (also in wave 12, lane 082).

name: Matthew Chaiken
current_role: Co-founder & President, Blink Health (BlinkRx)
profile: Co-founded Blink Health with his brother Geoffrey; as President he oversees product, engineering, data science and analytics and manages key accounts. Blink launched in 2016 as a prescription-discount service and has since become BlinkRx, a pharma-partnered home-delivery platform for branded drugs. Previously an investor at Marble Arch Investments and Merchants' Gate Capital.
interesting_fact: BlinkRx now partners with drug makers to get branded medicines delivered free in all 50 states, claiming 40% more fills covered by insurance.
deep_cut_fact: He graduated from Yale with a BA in Biology and started out as a Citigroup investment banker before moving into investing at Merchants' Gate Capital and Marble Arch Investments.
notes: Low public profile; brother Geoffrey (CEO, lane 081) is the public face. Bio source is an org-chart site (marked unverified there) - double-check before quoting. No press email found.

name: Fred Turner
current_role: CEO & Co-founder, Curative Inc. (Austin, Texas)
profile: British-born biotech entrepreneur (from Brighouse) who dropped out of Oxford biochemistry, moved to San Francisco and founded Thiel-backed TL BioLabs (cattle genetic tests), later Shield Bio (sepsis/gonorrhea diagnostics, a16z/YC). He co-founded Curative in 2020; it became a leading COVID-19 tester, then pivoted to a $0-copay, $0-deductible employer health plan.
interesting_fact: Under Turner, Curative went from the leading COVID-19 testing provider to a $0-copay, $0-deductible health plan; the company says its model achieves a 98% member engagement rate.
deep_cut_fact: As a 17-year-old he built a home DNA lab/PCR device in his bedroom, winning the UK's Young Engineer of the Year and ranking #1 at the 2013 EU Contest for Young Scientists; he was named one of the UK's 100 leading practising scientists.
notes: Lane's industry tag 'FinTech' is a Hurun label; Curative is a health insurer. Co-founded with Isaac Turner (CTO, lane 084). Turner writes op-eds on price transparency - healthcare-cost angle likely appealing. No published press email found.

name: Isaac Turner
current_role: CTO & Co-founder, Curative Inc. (Austin, Texas)
profile: Computational biologist (PhD in Bioinformatics, Oxford) who co-founded Curative in 2020 with Fred Turner and Vlad Slepnev. After running mass COVID-19 testing, Curative pivoted to a vertically integrated $0 out-of-pocket health plan; Isaac leads its technology, including a proprietary 'first principles' insurance stack, the Curative Cash Card and AI-driven care navigation.
interesting_fact: Curative describes itself as the nation's first vertically integrated, $0 out-of-pocket health insurance plan, built on its own insurance software stack.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as a computational biologist with a PhD in Bioinformatics from Oxford before turning to building health-insurance software, and spoke with Cell Systems in 2020 about COVID testing at scale.
notes: Co-founder with Fred Turner (CEO, lane 083). Cell Systems interview: https://www.cell.com/action/showPdf?pii=S2405-4712(20)30367-7 (via Wikipedia citation). No press email found.

name: Vlad Slepnev
current_role: Co-founder, Curative (listed as Chief Scientific Officer / Chief Scientific Advisor; sources differ)
profile: Vladimir 'Vlad' Slepnev is a molecular biologist who co-founded Curative in January 2020 with Fred Turner and Isaac Turner, originally to build sepsis diagnostics. Curative pivoted to COVID-19 testing in March 2020, became one of the largest US testing providers, and later reinvented itself as a health insurer with no co-pays or deductibles.
interesting_fact: Curative started as a sepsis-diagnostics company and abruptly pivoted to COVID-19 testing in March 2020 amid national shortages of test kits and lab capacity, before winding testing down in 2022 to focus on health insurance.
deep_cut_fact: Long before Curative, Slepnev founded diagnostics company PrimeraDx in 2004 (serving as its CTO), and earlier was Director of Molecular Biology at Sention and a faculty member at Yale University.
notes: Very low public profile scientist-founder; Crunchbase says PrimeraDx raised $50M+ and was sold to Qiagen (single source, unverified). Best route is Curative media relations (press@curative.com). Also previously VP R&D at Shield Bio (Oct 2018-Jan 2020) per aggregator profiles.

name: Alice Bentinck
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Entrepreneurs First (EF), talent investor / company builder (lives in San Francisco)
profile: British entrepreneur (b. 1986) who left McKinsey to co-found Entrepreneurs First with Matt Clifford in 2011, a programme that backs exceptional individuals before they have a co-founder or idea. She became CEO in December 2023; in March 2026 EF raised $200M at a $1.3B valuation and is pivoting to act as a bridge between Europe and the US. She also co-founded Code First Girls.
interesting_fact: Code First Girls, which she co-founded in 2012 after noticing most EF applicants were male, has taught over 250,000 women to code for free; she received an MBE in 2016 and co-wrote the award-winning book 'How to be a Founder' (Bloomsbury, 2022) with Clifford.
deep_cut_fact: Her first business was at school: at Godolphin School in Salisbury she joined Young Enterprise and created a business model for handmade purses. Before McKinsey she also interned in Tony Blair's office, assisting the Africa Governance Initiative.
notes: Very accessible, frequent podcast guest and speaker; EF is highly media-friendly. Relevant angles: EF's 2026 US-centric strategy and $200M raise. No published press email found on joinef.com (web search budget ran out before a deeper check).

name: Matt Clifford
current_role: Head of International Affairs at Anthropic; co-founder and non-executive Chair, Entrepreneurs First; Chair of ARIA (UK)
profile: British entrepreneur (b. 1985) who left McKinsey to co-found Entrepreneurs First with Alice Bentinck in 2011; EF raised $200M at a $1.3B valuation in 2026. He chairs the UK's Advanced Research and Invention Agency, led preparations for the 2023 Bletchley Park AI Safety Summit, wrote the UK AI Opportunities Action Plan and was the PM's AI Adviser until summer 2025. In September 2026 he joined Anthropic.
interesting_fact: He was named to the TIME AI100, awarded an MBE (2016) and CBE for services to AI (2024), and an October 2025 speech on how to 'Make the UK Rich Again' was viewed well over a million times.
deep_cut_fact: For fun he writes immersive murder-mystery games, some downloadable from his website; he also published annual reviews of every book he read 2015-2019 and wrote the weekly 'Thoughts in Between' newsletter (2018-22). He was a Kennedy Scholar at MIT.
notes: His site says 'You can message me on Twitter' (preferred route) and lists matt@joinef.com. Note: he now works at Anthropic (since Sept 2026; Register reported MPs raised conflict-of-interest concerns) - outreach may route through Anthropic comms for AI topics. Strong fit for energy/data-centre/AI policy themes.

name: Jake Loosararian
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Gecko Robotics (wall-climbing inspection robots + AI for critical infrastructure, Pittsburgh)
profile: Jake Loosararian started Gecko Robotics as a Grove City College engineering student after visiting a power plant losing millions per month to boiler downtime, and co-founded the company with his college roommate Troy Demmer in 2013. Gecko's robots and Cantilever AI software inspect boilers, tanks, pipelines and Navy ships; it raised a $125M Series D in June 2025 at a $1.25B valuation.
interesting_fact: Gecko was in Y Combinator's Winter 2016 batch, one of the first robotics companies YC backed, and now works with Fortune 100 energy, oil & gas and manufacturing firms as well as the US Air Force and US Navy.
deep_cut_fact: He built the first Gecko prototype in his college dorm room - a robot that could climb walls carrying ultrasonic sensors and cameras - then spent weeks on site in a dirty power-plant boiler adapting it until it found the plant's recurring failure.
notes: Excellent fit for an energy podcast (power-plant origin story, grid/energy infrastructure). Media-friendly: CNBC and Fortune founder-story pieces linked from Gecko's About page. Contact form has a 'Media/Press' option.

name: Orion Correa
current_role: Unknown (listed by Hurun as a founder of 'Gecko')
profile: Listed as a founder of 'Gecko' (valued $1B) on the Hurun unicorn-founders list. Gecko Robotics' own About page names only Jake Loosararian and Troy Demmer as co-founders and no page on geckorobotics.com mentions Orion Correa, so the link to Gecko Robotics could not be confirmed.
notes: Identity unconfirmed: possibly a Hurun data error (Gecko Robotics' co-founder is Troy Demmer) or a different company named Gecko. Searched all 78 pages in Gecko Robotics' sitemap with no mention. Web search budget ran out before further checks. Verify before any outreach.

name: Troy Demmer
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Gecko Robotics (Pittsburgh)
profile: Co-founder of Gecko Robotics, which builds wall-climbing inspection robots and the Cantilever data/AI platform to monitor power plants, refineries, Navy ships and other critical infrastructure. He leads product across robotics and software; Gecko reached unicorn status in 2024 and works heavily with the US Air Force and Navy.
interesting_fact: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 (Energy) in 2019; he and CEO Jake Loosararian were roommates at Grove City College, Pennsylvania.
deep_cut_fact: A 2011 Grove City College finance/economics graduate, he worked as a financial analyst at UPMC (and attended Carnegie Mellon) before joining Gecko; he has credited the UPMC job with teaching him many of the skills he needed to build the company.
notes: Highly relevant to an energy podcast: Gecko inspects boilers/power-plant assets and speaks at CERAWeek. Frequent podcast guest (e.g. 5 Year Frontier), so likely receptive to interviews.

name: Jonathan Ng
current_role: Founder & CEO, Iterative Health (formerly Iterative Scopes), AI for gastroenterology
profile: Singapore-trained physician (MBBS, NUS) who founded Iterative Health in 2017 while studying at MIT/Harvard. The Cambridge, MA company applies computer vision and AI to GI endoscopy, IBD clinical-trial recruitment and research, and is valued at ~$1B. He is based in New York.
interesting_fact: He says that at an early business-school competition, judges were 'mistaking AI for artificial insemination'.
deep_cut_fact: His path to entrepreneurship began when he broke his wrist in a car accident in his third year of medical practice in Singapore; the pause made him look at the whole health system. He admits he 'had no idea what an MBA was' when he applied, and the Iterative idea came 3-4 months after arriving at MIT.
notes: Physician-founder; has done several podcasts (Physician-Executive Series, Third Spacing), so open to interviews. No published press email found.

name: Karri Saarinen
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Linear (Linear Orbit, Inc., San Francisco)
profile: Finnish designer-founder who left his Principal Designer role at Airbnb in 2019 to start Linear with Jori Lallo and Tuomas Artman. Linear's issue-tracking/product-development tool became a favourite of startups, was cash-flow positive by 2021, and an Aug 2026 tender valued it at $2.5B. He writes widely on design, quality and AI-era software.
interesting_fact: Linear began from a Chrome extension he wrote at Airbnb to tame JIRA's visual noise; about 100 Airbnb colleagues ended up using it.
deep_cut_fact: As Design Lead on Airbnb's Design Language System team he helped roll out the Airbnb Cereal typeface (made with Dalton Maag) in 2018, and earlier designed at Coinbase. Before Linear, he and Jori Lallo built a startup in Y Combinator's Summer 2012 batch. He's a fan of 'Jiro Dreams of Sushi' as a lesson in taste.
notes: Very accessible publicly: personal blog plus a long interviews list (YC, First Round, TBPN, Figma Config) at karrisaarinen.com/interviews. Good podcast candidate.

name: Jori Lallo
current_role: Co-founder & Chief Product Officer, Linear
profile: Finnish engineer/designer who co-founded Linear in 2019 with Karri Saarinen and Tuomas Artman after working at Coinbase, where he hit the same project-tracking frustrations. Linear's product-development platform, now pushing into AI coding agents, was valued at $2.5B in an Aug 2026 tender. He splits time between Brooklyn and Helsinki.
interesting_fact: He and Karri Saarinen were YC founders together years before Linear: they built a company in Y Combinator's Summer 2012 batch.
deep_cut_fact: Before Linear he worked at Coinbase, where he saw the same issue-tracker pain Saarinen saw at Airbnb and Artman at Uber; he and Saarinen first teamed up in YC's Summer 2012 batch.
notes: Active on X (~14.6K followers); recently posts about hacking Home Assistant smart-home setups with AI coding tools, which could be an easy conversation opener.

name: Tuomas Artman
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Linear
profile: Finnish engineer who co-founded Linear in 2019 with Karri Saarinen and Jori Lallo and leads its engineering as CTO. He built Linear's local-first sync engine, a big reason the app feels instant, and the company was valued at $2.5B in an Aug 2026 tender. Before Linear he was at Uber, and earlier Groupon.
interesting_fact: He had already been building sync engines for over a decade, at companies like Groupon and Uber, before making one the core of Linear's architecture.
deep_cut_fact: A well-known voice in the 'local-first' software movement: he spoke at Local-First Conf ('Unexpected benefits of going local-first') and argues the startup MVP should be rethought around quality. Linear's founders say the idea came partly from his frustration with issue trackers at Uber.
notes: Comfortable with podcasts (localfirst.fm #15, devtools.fm #61). A good technical guest on sync/infra topics.

name: Kay Zhu
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, MainFunc Inc. (Genspark), Palo Alto
profile: Kay Zhu (Zhu Kaihua) is a search engineer who worked on Google's search ranking. He then spent about a decade at Baidu as a chief architect and, from 2020, as CTO of its Xiaodu smart-device unit. He left in 2023 with Eric Jing to co-found MainFunc, maker of the Genspark AI agent/workspace. Genspark passed $200M annual run-rate in 2026 at a valuation near $1.6B.
interesting_fact: The company name MainFunc comes from the 'main function', the entry point of a computer program. Genspark raised a $60M seed at a $260M valuation and became a unicorn about 18 months after the founders left Baidu.
deep_cut_fact: Zhu pioneered AI-driven search ranking technology at Google back in 2011, before deep learning went mainstream. He and Eric Jing then worked side by side at Baidu for about 11 years, ending as CTO and CEO of Xiaodu, before starting Genspark together.
notes: 'Main Func' = MainFunc Inc., the parent of Genspark. CEO Eric Jing is the public face; Zhu is the technical cofounder and occasionally interviewed (e.g. VentureBeat). Route via press@genspark.ai or the PR firm VSC.

name: Carl Pei
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Nothing (London consumer-tech company)
profile: Beijing-born, Sweden-raised entrepreneur (b. 1989) who co-founded OnePlus with Pete Lau in 2013 and ran its global brand until 2020. In 2021 he founded London-based Nothing, backed by Tony Fadell, Casey Neistat and Steve Huffman among others; it makes the Nothing Phone and Ear lines plus lower-priced CMF sub-brand and is valued at over $1B.
interesting_fact: The OnePlus One sold close to a million units in 2014 against an initial target of 50,000.

name: Ezra Feilden
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Starcloud (formerly Lumen Orbit), Redmond, WA - orbital AI data centers

notes: Sports Business Journal Forty Under 40 honoree; appears on sports-business podcasts. Best route: Teamworks PR.
